evt-01-01-1773-hymn.scenario: It's New Year's Day 1773, and you sit among the congregation in Olney, England, as curate John Newton, a former slave ship captain turned clergyman, introduces a new hymn written for the occasion.
evt-01-01-1773-hymn.prompt: What hymn does Newton likely introduce at this service?

choices.text: "Rock of Ages"
"Abide with Me"
"How Great Thou Art"
"Amazing Grace"

evt-01-01-1773-hymn.butterflyEffect: The hymn was "Amazing Grace," drawing on Newton's own journey from slave trader to preacher. It went on to become one of the most recorded songs in history, later embraced as an anthem of abolition, civil rights, and personal redemption across the world.

evt-01-01-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is New Year's Day 1776, and you live in Norfolk, Virginia, one of the busiest ports in the colonies. Royal Navy ships under Lord Dunmore lie anchored offshore after weeks of siege and skirmishing with Patriot militia.
evt-01-01-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What happens to Norfolk on this day?

choices.text: A British garrison is welcomed without resistance
The town is spared and becomes a Loyalist stronghold for the war
Norfolk peacefully surrenders to Continental forces
British ships bombard the town and it burns to the ground

evt-01-01-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: British warships bombarded the town and landing parties set fires that, combined with later Patriot burning to deny its use to the British, destroyed most of Norfolk. The devastation of one of the colonies' largest ports became powerful propaganda, cited in the Declaration of Independence's list of grievances against George III.

evt-01-01-1801-giuseppe-piazzi.scenario: It is the night of 1 January 1801, and you are Giuseppe Piazzi at your telescope in Palermo, cataloguing faint stars for a new star chart. A tiny point of light you charted the night before has shifted position against the background, and you must decide whether this is a mapping error or something new.
evt-01-01-1801-giuseppe-piazzi.prompt: What did Piazzi conclude he had found?

choices.text: A moon orbiting Jupiter
A new celestial body, later recognized as the first-discovered dwarf planet, Ceres
A previously uncatalogued fixed star
A new comet on a highly elliptical orbit

evt-01-01-1801-giuseppe-piazzi.butterflyEffect: Piazzi had discovered Ceres, initially classified as a full planet, filling the suspicious gap between Mars and Jupiter predicted by the Titius-Bode law. The find opened the door to the discovery of the wider asteroid belt, reshaping astronomers' picture of the solar system's structure.

evt-01-01-1808-abolitionism.scenario: It is January 1, 1808, and you are a shipowner in an American port as a new federal law takes effect, ending decades of legal transatlantic human trafficking into the United States.
evt-01-01-1808-abolitionism.prompt: What actually changes for the slave trade in the United States on this date?

choices.text: Slavery is abolished throughout the United States
Only the New England states ban importing enslaved people
Importing enslaved Africans becomes illegal, but slavery itself continues
The trade remains fully legal for another decade under a compromise clause

evt-01-01-1808-abolitionism.butterflyEffect: The Act Prohibiting Importation of Slaves made it illegal to bring captives from Africa into the U.S., but it did not free a single enslaved person already in bondage. Smuggling persisted and the domestic slave trade between states expanded rapidly to meet demand, deepening slavery's hold on the American South for decades.

evt-01-01-1810-lachlan-macquarie.scenario: It is January 1810, and Sydney's docks are crowded as the colony's new governor, Lachlan Macquarie, steps ashore into a settlement still shaken by the Rum Rebellion and torn between convicts, emancipists, and free settlers.
evt-01-01-1810-lachlan-macquarie.prompt: What approach does Macquarie take toward emancipated convicts in the colony?

choices.text: He grants emancipists civil rights and appoints some to official positions
He orders emancipists deported back to Britain once their sentences end
He bars all former convicts from holding any position of trust
He declares martial law and suspends civil governance entirely

evt-01-01-1810-lachlan-macquarie.butterflyEffect: Macquarie appointed emancipists to public office and courts, insisting they be treated as equals to free settlers, while pushing major building and road projects across New South Wales. His policies enraged the colony's exclusive elite but accelerated its transformation from penal outpost into a self-sustaining free society.

evt-01-01-1863-emancipation-proclamation.scenario: It is January 1, 1863, and you are an enslaved man on a Louisiana plantation that lies within Union-occupied territory, exempted from President Lincoln's new proclamation. Word has spread that slaves elsewhere in the Confederacy are now declared free the moment they reach Union lines.
evt-01-01-1863-emancipation-proclamation.prompt: What does the Emancipation Proclamation actually change for slaves in rebel territory?

choices.text: They remain enslaved until the war ends, regardless of Union advances
They are legally free the instant they reach Union lines or Union troops advance
They are freed but forbidden from serving in the Union military
They are freed only if their enslaver personally signs a release

evt-01-01-1863-emancipation-proclamation.butterflyEffect: The proclamation freed slaves only in Confederate-held areas still in rebellion, not in Union-loyal border states, but it let escaped and liberated slaves join the U.S. armed forces. Nearly 200,000 Black soldiers and sailors ultimately served, turning the war into an explicit fight against slavery and paving the way for the 13th Amendment in 1865.

evt-01-01-1892-ellis-island.scenario: It is January 1, 1892. You are a young immigrant stepping off a steamship in New York Harbor, funneled with hundreds of others toward a new federal inspection station on a small island that has just opened its doors.
evt-01-01-1892-ellis-island.prompt: What awaits you and the other new arrivals at this newly opened immigration station?

choices.text: Medical inspection and legal screening before you are admitted into the United States
A mandatory return voyage unless you already have a job offer
Automatic citizenship papers handed out on arrival
Direct transport to designated farmland in the Midwest

evt-01-01-1892-ellis-island.butterflyEffect: Ellis Island became the busiest immigrant processing station in the country, screening around 12 million people for health and legal admissibility between 1892 and 1954. So many Americans trace their ancestry through its gates that historians estimate two-fifths of the U.S. population may descend from immigrants who passed through it.

evt-01-01-1914-st-petersburg-tampa-airbo.scenario: It's January 1914, and you've bought a ticket for what's billed as the world's first scheduled airline flight, a flying boat crossing Tampa Bay between St. Petersburg and Tampa. Pilot Tony Jannus is strapping into the open cockpit as a curious crowd gathers on the dock.
evt-01-01-1914-st-petersburg-tampa-airbo.prompt: What made this short hop across Tampa Bay historically significant?

choices.text: It carried the first transcontinental airmail
It launched the first scheduled fixed-wing airline service in the United States
It was the first transatlantic passenger flight
It introduced the first in-flight meal service

evt-01-01-1914-st-petersburg-tampa-airbo.butterflyEffect: The airline folded after only about four months once its subsidy ran out, but it had proven that paying passengers would fly a fixed schedule between two cities. That proof of concept planted an early seed for the scheduled commercial airline industry that would later transform American travel.

evt-01-01-1915-sayfo.scenario: It is early 1915 in Persia's Azerbaijan province. You are an elder in an Assyrian Christian village, and word arrives that the Russian troops who had shielded the region are pulling back under Ottoman pressure.
evt-01-01-1915-sayfo.prompt: With Russian protection gone, what is the safest course for your community?

choices.text: Flee toward Russian-held territory in the Caucasus while there is still time
Remain in place and rely on existing Ottoman law for safety
Petition Ottoman authorities and trust in their promises of protection
Appeal to the Persian government to send troops for defense

evt-01-01-1915-sayfo.butterflyEffect: Russia's withdrawal stripped Assyrian and Armenian Christians of their main protector, leaving them exposed to Ottoman forces and allied Kurdish tribes. The resulting massacres and forced displacements, part of the wider Sayfo alongside the Armenian Genocide, shattered ancient Christian communities across the region and drove survivors into permanent exile.

evt-01-01-1928-joseph-stalin.scenario: It is 1 January 1928, and you are Boris Bazhanov, Joseph Stalin's own personal secretary, standing near the Soviet border with Persia. You know too much about the inner workings of the Politburo, and you have decided tonight is the night to disappear.

choices.text: He defected, becoming one of the first insiders to expose Stalin's regime from the West
He joined the Trotskyist opposition and was jailed
He was captured and executed by Soviet border guards
He had a change of heart and returned quietly to Moscow

evt-01-01-1928-joseph-stalin.butterflyEffect: Bazhanov successfully fled across the border, becoming one of the earliest Soviet officials to defect to the West. His later memoirs gave outsiders a rare insider's account of Stalin's rise and the Communist Party's inner machinery, becoming a key early source for later histories of Soviet totalitarianism.

evt-01-01-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is January 1, 1945, in the shattered Belgian village of Chenogne. Word of the Malmedy massacre has spread through your unit, and a group of German soldiers now surrenders to your company during the fighting of the Bulge.
evt-01-01-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What do the American soldiers do with these German prisoners?

choices.text: They process them normally through standard POW channels
They hand them to Belgian resistance fighters for judgment
They execute dozens of the prisoners in reprisal for Malmedy
They arrange an immediate prisoner exchange with German command

evt-01-01-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: American troops shot roughly sixty German prisoners at Chenogne in reprisal for Malmedy, an atrocity that US Army investigators examined but never prosecuted, unlike the German perpetrators of Malmedy who faced war crimes trials. The episode is a sober reminder that wartime reprisals occurred on both sides, complicating simple postwar narratives of the conflict.

evt-01-01-1948-british-rail.scenario: It's New Year's Day 1948, and you're a railway clerk watching workers repaint locomotives overnight as ownership of Britain's entire rail network changes hands.
evt-01-01-1948-british-rail.prompt: What happens to Britain's "Big Four" railway companies today?

choices.text: They are nationalized into a single state-owned British Railways
They are dissolved and replaced by regional bus networks
They are sold off to American investors
They merge voluntarily into one private conglomerate

evt-01-01-1948-british-rail.butterflyEffect: The LMS, LNER, GWR, and Southern Railway passed into public ownership under the new British Transport Commission, forming British Railways. This began nearly five decades of state control over Britain's railways, a system that lasted until privatisation swept through the network in the 1990s.

evt-01-01-1959-cuban-revolution.scenario: It is early January 1959. Fulgencio Batista has just fled Havana, and Fidel Castro's rebel column is marching toward the capital after years of guerrilla war from the Sierra Maestra. You are a Cuban journalist trying to gauge what kind of government is coming.
evt-01-01-1959-cuban-revolution.prompt: What had allowed Castro's small guerrilla band to grow into a force capable of toppling Batista?

choices.text: The United States armed and trained Castro's forces directly
Batista's army defected en masse after a single battle in 1957
Years of guerrilla warfare, urban sabotage, and covert recruitment gradually built a cohesive rebel army
The Cuban Congress voted to hand power to Castro before any fighting began

evt-01-01-1959-cuban-revolution.butterflyEffect: Castro's 26th of July Movement absorbed support that had once gone to the Popular Socialist Party and built a broad anti-Batista coalition through sabotage, recruitment, and battlefield successes in the Sierra Maestra. Within two years Castro consolidated power, aligned with the Soviet Union, and set Cuba on a collision course with the United States that produced the Bay of Pigs and the Cuban Missile Crisis.

evt-01-01-1965-people-s-democratic-party.scenario: It is 1 January 1965 in Kabul, and you're one of the founding delegates gathered in a private home to launch a new Marxist-Leninist party to challenge Afghanistan's monarchy. Rival factions in the room are already arguing over leadership and strategy.
evt-01-01-1965-people-s-democratic-party.prompt: What internal split would come to define this new party in the years ahead?

choices.text: A conflict between rural agrarian and urban labor factions
A divide between Pashtun and Tajik nationalist wings
A split between monarchists and republicans within the party
The rivalry between the hardline Khalq and moderate Parcham factions

evt-01-01-1965-people-s-democratic-party.butterflyEffect: The rivalry between the hardline Khalq and moderate Parcham factions fractured the PDPA for over a decade. After the party seized power in the 1978 Saur Revolution, that same infighting fueled purges and instability that helped draw in Soviet military intervention in 1979, setting the stage for decades of war in Afghanistan.

evt-01-01-1978-air-india-flight-855.scenario: It is the early morning of 1 January 1978, and you are the captain of Air India Flight 855, climbing away from Bombay into a dark, moonless sky over the Arabian Sea. One of your primary flight instruments has just begun feeding you false information.
evt-01-01-1978-air-india-flight-855.prompt: What did investigators later conclude went wrong in the cockpit?

choices.text: Both engines failed from fuel contamination
The crew deployed the landing gear too early after takeoff
The captain became spatially disoriented after a flight instrument failed
A bomb exploded in the cargo hold

evt-01-01-1978-air-india-flight-855.butterflyEffect: Investigators determined the captain most likely became spatially disoriented after a faulty attitude indicator gave misleading readings in the dark, and he lost control of the aircraft, killing all 213 aboard. It remained India's deadliest air disaster for nearly two decades and pushed for greater scrutiny of instrument reliability and crew training.

evt-01-01-1995-world-trade-organization.scenario: It is January 1, 1995, in Geneva. You are a delegate watching the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, which has governed world commerce since 1948, formally give way to a new permanent body created by the Marrakesh Agreement.
evt-01-01-1995-world-trade-organization.prompt: What replaces GATT as the organization overseeing global trade rules starting today?

choices.text: The International Monetary Fund, expanding its mandate to cover trade
The United Nations Trade Council, a new UN subsidiary body
The World Trade Organization, with a permanent structure and binding dispute settlement
A revived League of Nations economic committee

evt-01-01-1995-world-trade-organization.butterflyEffect: The World Trade Organization took over from GATT with a permanent institutional structure and binding dispute-resolution powers that GATT had lacked. It grew to include 166 members representing over 98% of global trade, becoming the central forum for trade negotiations and disputes for decades to come.

evt-01-01-1998-juan-maldacena.scenario: It's late 1997, and you're a graduate student scanning the newest physics preprints. Argentine physicist Juan Maldacena has just posted a paper proposing an exact correspondence between a gravity theory in curved spacetime and a quantum field theory on its boundary, and you must decide whether it's worth restructuring your thesis around.
evt-01-01-1998-juan-maldacena.prompt: What did Maldacena's paper go on to establish for physics?

choices.text: A unification of general relativity with Newtonian mechanics
Experimental proof that string theory describes our universe
The AdS/CFT correspondence, linking gravity in curved space to a boundary quantum field theory
Direct detection of extra dimensions in a particle accelerator

evt-01-01-1998-juan-maldacena.butterflyEffect: The paper became one of the most cited in theoretical physics history, launching the AdS/CFT correspondence and the broader field of holography. It gave physicists a mathematical bridge between quantum gravity and more tractable field theories, reshaping string theory, black hole research, and even parts of condensed matter physics.

evt-01-01-2007-adam-air-flight-574.scenario: It is January 1, 2007, and you are a flight controller tracking Adam Air Flight 574 as it flies through stormy weather over the Makassar Strait toward Manado. The crew reports trouble with the aircraft's inertial navigation system.
evt-01-01-2007-adam-air-flight-574.prompt: What did investigators later conclude went wrong in the cockpit that led to the crash?

choices.text: They focused on fixing the navigation system and didn't notice the autopilot had disconnected
A mid-air collision with another aircraft brought it down
A bomb planted before departure detonated mid-flight
The aircraft ran out of fuel over the strait

evt-01-01-2007-adam-air-flight-574.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the pilots became so absorbed in troubleshooting the navigation system that they failed to notice the autopilot had disconnected, and the Boeing 737 rolled and dived into the sea, killing all 102 aboard. The disaster, following a string of Adam Air safety lapses, intensified scrutiny of Indonesian aviation oversight and contributed to the airline's closure the following year.

evt-01-01-2019-nasa.scenario: It's New Year's Day 2019, and you're monitoring telemetry from a spacecraft more than four billion miles from Earth as it closes in on a tiny, ancient world deep in the Kuiper Belt.
evt-01-01-2019-nasa.prompt: What does New Horizons reveal about the object Arrokoth?

choices.text: It possesses a faint ring system
It turns out to be an interstellar visitor passing through
It is a contact binary of two lobes gently joined together
It has a hidden subsurface ocean like Europa

evt-01-01-2019-nasa.butterflyEffect: Images beamed back showed Arrokoth as a flattened, snowman-shaped "contact binary" of two lobes gently fused together, the most pristine, unaltered object ever explored by a spacecraft. It gave scientists a direct window into how planetesimals formed billions of years ago, cementing New Horizons' extended mission as a landmark of outer solar system exploration.

evt-01-02-1680-trunajaya-rebellion.scenario: It is early January 1680 in the Mataram court camp. Trunajaya, the rebel leader who once sacked the Mataram capital, surrendered to Dutch VOC forces a week ago under an understanding that his life would be spared. Now King Amangkurat II arrives to see the captive himself.
evt-01-02-1680-trunajaya-rebellion.prompt: What happens to Trunajaya despite his surrender to the VOC?

choices.text: He is exiled to Ceylon under VOC guard
He is pardoned and given a minor court title
Amangkurat II personally stabs him to death
He escapes custody and resumes the rebellion

evt-01-02-1680-trunajaya-rebellion.butterflyEffect: Amangkurat II personally stabbed Trunajaya to death with his own kris, disregarding the terms of surrender arranged with the Dutch. The killing strained trust between the Mataram court and the VOC even as it crushed the last organized resistance, and the Company used the ensuing weakness to extract ever greater concessions, deepening its grip over Java's politics for generations.

evt-01-02-1920-a-mitchell-palmer.scenario: It is January 2, 1920, and as a federal agent under Attorney General A. Mitchell Palmer, you take part in coordinated raids across dozens of American cities targeting suspected radicals and anarchists.
evt-01-02-1920-a-mitchell-palmer.prompt: What do the Palmer Raids actually involve, and with what result?

choices.text: Only individuals with prior warrants for violent crimes are detained
Thousands are arrested without warrants, and some are later deported
Nearly all those arrested are convicted in court within weeks
Congress halts the raids before any arrests are made

evt-01-02-1920-a-mitchell-palmer.butterflyEffect: Agents arrested thousands, often without warrants, holding many in poor conditions before deporting some, including anarchist Emma Goldman. Public backlash over the raids' abuses damaged Palmer's presidential ambitions and helped end the Red Scare, while also spurring the growth of civil liberties advocacy in America.

evt-01-02-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It's January 2, 1944, and you're an infantryman crammed into a landing craft nearing the beach at Saidor, New Guinea, part of a surprise amphibious assault meant to leapfrog past heavily defended Japanese positions to the east.
evt-01-02-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What is the strategic goal of this landing?

choices.text: Cut off the Japanese 18th Army's coastal retreat route
Establish a submarine refueling base for the Pacific Fleet
Relieve besieged Australian troops still fighting at Buna
Capture the major Japanese airbase at Rabaul

evt-01-02-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The Saidor landing (Operation Michaelmas) cut the coastal escape route of the Japanese 18th Army, forcing thousands of survivors to abandon vehicles and heavy weapons and trek overland through mountainous jungle to Madang. Starvation and disease during that retreat crippled the force long before it could fight again, a major early demonstration of MacArthur's island-hopping strategy.

evt-01-02-1959-luna-1.scenario: It is January 2, 1959, and you monitor telemetry from Luna 1 as it races toward the Moon, the Soviet Union's first attempt to strike the lunar surface.
evt-01-02-1959-luna-1.prompt: What actually happens to Luna 1 as it nears the Moon?

choices.text: It loses contact shortly after launch and falls back to Earth
It enters a stable orbit around the Moon, becoming the first lunar satellite
It misses the Moon and becomes the first spacecraft in orbit around the Sun
It strikes the Moon exactly as planned, the first successful lunar impact

evt-01-02-1959-luna-1.butterflyEffect: A timing error in the launch caused Luna 1 to miss the Moon by thousands of kilometers, flying past it into orbit around the Sun and becoming the first artificial object to escape Earth's gravity. Soviet engineers corrected the guidance error, and Luna 2 successfully struck the Moon later that same year.

evt-01-02-1967-ronald-reagan.scenario: It is January 2, 1967, and you watch Ronald Reagan take the oath as California's new governor, having unseated incumbent Pat Brown on a promise to rein in state spending and confront campus unrest.
evt-01-02-1967-ronald-reagan.prompt: As one of his first acts in office, what does Governor Reagan do about the state budget?

choices.text: He proposes a large new state income tax to fund welfare expansion
He freezes government hiring and orders sweeping budget cuts
He borrows heavily through state bonds to avoid any cuts
He leaves the budget untouched and focuses only on crime policy

evt-01-02-1967-ronald-reagan.butterflyEffect: Reagan froze state hiring and pushed deep spending cuts to close a budget shortfall, clashing sharply with the University of California over funding and student protests. His fiscally conservative, anti-establishment image built during his governorship propelled him to the presidency in 1981.

evt-01-02-1971-1971-ibrox-disaster.scenario: It's the final minutes of the Old Firm match at Ibrox Park on 2 January 1971. As fans already descending stairway 13 hear a last-minute goal roar behind them, the crowd suddenly reverses and compresses around you on the narrow steps.
evt-01-02-1971-1971-ibrox-disaster.prompt: What fatal chain of events is unfolding on the stairway?

choices.text: Fans rushed the pitch after a disputed refereeing decision
A fire broke out in the stand, triggering a stampede to one exit
Fans surging back after a late goal collided with those still descending
A barrier gave way under fans climbing over a locked turnstile

evt-01-02-1971-1971-ibrox-disaster.butterflyEffect: Sixty-six spectators, including many teenagers, were crushed to death on Stairway 13 that day. The tragedy led to the Wheatley Report and the Safety of Sports Grounds Act 1975, tightening stadium regulations, though crowd-safety failures would tragically recur less than two decades later at Hillsborough.

evt-01-02-1981-united-kingdom.scenario: It is early January 1981 and you are a West Yorkshire detective, five years into Britain's largest police manhunt for a serial killer who has terrorized women across the north of England.
evt-01-02-1981-united-kingdom.prompt: What breakthrough finally leads to the arrest of the man responsible?

choices.text: A routine stop of a car with false plates leads officers to arrest him
He confesses after calling a police hotline anonymously
A coworker tips off police after noticing suspicious behavior
Fingerprints from a crime scene finally match a suspect on file

evt-01-02-1981-united-kingdom.butterflyEffect: On 2 January 1981, a routine police check on a car in Sheffield led to the arrest of Peter Sutcliffe, later confirmed as the Yorkshire Ripper. His capture ended a five-year hunt that had killed thirteen women and exposed serious failures in how police investigated crimes against sex workers, prompting lasting reforms in British policing.

evt-01-02-2004-stardust-spacecraft.scenario: It's January 2, 2004, and NASA's Stardust probe has one chance to pass within 236 kilometers of comet Wild 2's nucleus, extending an aerogel collector to snag particles streaming from its coma before racing on toward Earth.
evt-01-02-2004-stardust-spacecraft.prompt: What must the probe do with its precious cargo after the flyby?

choices.text: Vaporize the captured dust for immediate onboard spectral analysis
Seal and stow the sample capsule for a scheduled return to Earth
Transmit high-resolution images instead of physical samples
Release the capsule into a parking orbit around Mars for later pickup

evt-01-02-2004-stardust-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: Stardust's aerogel captured thousands of cometary grains, and its sample capsule parachuted safely into the Utah desert on 15 January 2006. Analysis revealed minerals that could only have formed near the sun, overturning assumptions that comets were purely icy relics from the solar system's frigid outer edge.

evt-01-02-2009-sri-lankan-civil-war.scenario: It is January 2, 2009, and you march with Sri Lankan army units into Kilinochchi, the town that has served as the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam's de facto administrative capital for years.
evt-01-02-2009-sri-lankan-civil-war.prompt: What follows the army's capture of the LTTE's capital?

choices.text: Foreign peacekeepers intervene and partition the island
A negotiated ceasefire is signed, freezing the front lines indefinitely
The LTTE recaptures the town within weeks, prolonging the war for years
The LTTE's territorial hold collapses, and the war ends within months

evt-01-02-2009-sri-lankan-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The fall of Kilinochchi broke the back of LTTE territorial control and triggered a rapid military collapse of the insurgency. Within five months the war ended with the death of LTTE leader Velupillai Prabhakaran, closing 26 years of civil war.

evt-01-02-2022-2022-kazakh-unrest.scenario: It is January 2, 2022, and you are among the crowds in Zhanaozen after the government lifted its cap on liquefied petroleum gas, doubling prices overnight. The protest is spreading toward Almaty as anger mounts.
evt-01-02-2022-2022-kazakh-unrest.prompt: As unrest spreads nationwide within days, how does President Tokayev respond?

choices.text: He flees to Russia and hands power to the military
He reinstates the fuel price cap and the protests end peacefully within a day
He resigns immediately and calls for new elections
He declares a state of emergency and calls in CSTO troops to help crush the unrest

evt-01-02-2022-2022-kazakh-unrest.butterflyEffect: Tokayev declared a nationwide state of emergency and invited Russian-led CSTO troops into the country while ordering security forces to shoot without warning. Over 227 people died in the crackdown, and the unrest let Tokayev purge remaining allies of former president Nazarbayev, consolidating his own power.

evt-01-02-2024-haneda-airport.scenario: It is the evening of 2 January 2024, and you are aboard Japan Airlines Flight 516 as it touches down at Haneda Airport, moments before colliding with another aircraft on the runway and bursting into flames.
evt-01-02-2024-haneda-airport.prompt: What happens next that allows everyone aboard the JAL jet to survive?

choices.text: Passengers wait inside for rescue crews to manually open the doors
The aircraft skids safely off the runway without further incident
Onboard fire suppression systems extinguish the flames before landing
Crew execute a rapid evacuation and everyone escapes before the fire spreads

evt-01-02-2024-haneda-airport.butterflyEffect: All 379 passengers and crew aboard the JAL Airbus evacuated safely down slides despite the fire, a result widely praised as a triumph of crew training and aircraft design. Five of the six crew aboard the Japan Coast Guard plane it struck were killed, prompting reviews of runway clearance procedures at one of the world's busiest airports.

evt-01-02-2024-2024-haneda-airport-runwa.scenario: It's January 2, 2024, aboard Japan Airlines Flight 516, moments after your Airbus A350 collides with a Japan Coast Guard aircraft on the runway at Haneda and flames begin spreading through the cabin.
evt-01-02-2024-2024-haneda-airport-runwa.prompt: As cabin crew, what's the priority in these chaotic first seconds?

choices.text: Evacuate everyone immediately, leaving carry-on baggage behind
Let passengers retrieve belongings for an orderly exit
Attempt to restart engines and taxi the burning aircraft clear
Wait for explicit instructions from ground control before opening doors

evt-01-02-2024-2024-haneda-airport-runwa.butterflyEffect: Despite the aircraft being engulfed in fire, all 379 passengers and crew aboard Flight 516 escaped alive through a fast, disciplined evacuation. All five crew of the Coast Guard plane, which had been delivering earthquake relief supplies, were killed, and the crash intensified scrutiny of runway-incursion safety at one of the world's busiest airports.

evt-01-03-250-decius.scenario: It's 250 AD, and as a provincial magistrate you must enforce Emperor Decius's new decree requiring every free person to publicly sacrifice to the Roman gods and obtain a certificate as proof.
evt-01-03-250-decius.prompt: What happens to those who refuse to perform the sacrifice, many of them Christians?

choices.text: Roman citizens are automatically exempt from the requirement
A simple promise to sacrifice later satisfies the magistrate
They face imprisonment, torture or execution as apostates
They may pay a fine instead of sacrificing

evt-01-03-250-decius.butterflyEffect: Refusal was treated as defiance of the state and punished with imprisonment, torture, or death, triggering the first empire-wide persecution of Christians. Pope Fabian was among those martyred, and the crisis over Christians who lapsed and later sought readmission shaped Church debates for decades.

evt-01-03-1521-pope-leo-x.scenario: It's January 1521, and you serve in the papal curia in Rome as Pope Leo X finalizes a bull against a defiant Augustinian friar who has refused to recant his teachings.
evt-01-03-1521-pope-leo-x.prompt: What does the bull Decet Romanum Pontificem actually do to Martin Luther?

choices.text: It orders his immediate arrest and execution
It excommunicates him from the Catholic Church
It condemns only his writings while leaving him in communion
It grants him one final year to recant without penalty

evt-01-03-1521-pope-leo-x.butterflyEffect: The bull formally excommunicated Luther after he refused to withdraw the propositions condemned in Exsurge Domine. Declared an outlaw months later at the Diet of Worms, Luther's break with Rome was now final, a rupture that grew into the Protestant Reformation.

evt-01-03-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is the night of 2 January 1777 near Trenton. Cornwallis's larger British force is closing in, and a losing battle seems certain by morning. Campfires are ordered kept burning in camp while Washington quietly prepares his exhausted men to move.
evt-01-03-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What move does Washington make instead of standing to fight at Trenton?

choices.text: A direct frontal assault on Cornwallis's main force
A full retreat back across the Delaware River
An attempt to negotiate a truce with the British command
A secret night march around the British flank to strike Princeton

evt-01-03-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Washington slipped his army around the British flank in a secret night march and struck the lightly defended garrison at Princeton at dawn, routing it. The victory, following Trenton days earlier, restored American morale after a string of defeats around New York, secured winter quarters in New Jersey, and persuaded many soldiers to re-enlist.

evt-01-03-1911-1911-kebin-earthquake.scenario: It is January 1911 in Verny, Russian Turkestan. The earthquake has just levelled hundreds of masonry buildings, yet you notice the timber-framed houses nearby are still standing.
evt-01-03-1911-1911-kebin-earthquake.prompt: As the town's rebuilding engineer, what do you recommend for new construction?

choices.text: Traditional mud-brick construction unchanged from before
Reinforced brick and stone towers for durability
Taller stone buildings to project imperial authority
Lightweight timber-frame houses that flex rather than crack

evt-01-03-1911-1911-kebin-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Authorities doubled down on wooden and timber-frame construction, a policy already favored after an 1887 quake, since such structures flexed rather than collapsed. This preference shaped Almaty's architecture for decades and reduced casualties in later regional tremors.

evt-01-03-1911-siege-of-sidney-street.scenario: It is January 1911 in Stepney, East London. Two armed Latvian revolutionaries who murdered several policemage during a botched robbery are now barricaded in a house, exchanging gunfire with your unarmed constables.
evt-01-03-1911-siege-of-sidney-street.prompt: As the commanding officer on scene, what do you do?

choices.text: Send in unarmed constables to negotiate a surrender
Withdraw entirely and let the men escape under cover of night
Call in the Army with rifles to reinforce the police cordon
Storm the house immediately with only police revolvers

evt-01-03-1911-siege-of-sidney-street.butterflyEffect: Home Secretary Winston Churchill personally travelled to the scene and authorised the Scots Guards to bring rifles against the gunmen. The house caught fire during the siege and both revolutionaries died inside; Churchill's hands-on conduct drew sharp criticism in Parliament from Balfour, an early sign of the combative public image that would follow him for decades.

evt-01-03-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It is dawn on 3 January 1941 in the Libyan desert. You are an Australian infantryman with the 6th Division, waiting for the barrage to lift before your assault on the fortified Italian garrison at Bardia.
evt-01-03-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: What was the outcome of the Allied assault on Bardia?

choices.text: A negotiated truce left the Italian garrison in place
German reinforcements arrived first and drove the attackers back
The garrison collapsed, surrendering tens of thousands of prisoners to the advancing Allies
The assault was repulsed and the Allied force withdrew into Egypt

evt-01-03-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Bardia fell within days, with tens of thousands of Italian troops taken prisoner for comparatively light Allied casualties. The victory, part of Operation Compass, shattered Italian resistance in eastern Libya and pushed the offensive on toward Tobruk, forcing Germany to send the Afrika Korps to shore up its ally.

evt-01-03-1961-aero-flight-311.scenario: You are an air safety investigator in Finland in January 1961, called to the crash site near Kvevlax where an Aero O/Y Douglas DC-3 flying from Kronoby to Vaasa has gone down, killing everyone aboard.
evt-01-03-1961-aero-flight-311.prompt: What did the investigation conclude was the cause of the crash?

choices.text: A mechanical failure in the landing gear
A navigational error caused by faulty instruments
Both pilots were intoxicated and unfit to fly
Severe icing conditions on the wings

evt-01-03-1961-aero-flight-311.butterflyEffect: Investigators found that both pilots were intoxicated and should never have been cleared to fly, making this the deadliest civilian air disaster in Finnish history. The scandal forced tighter scrutiny of crew fitness and alcohol regulation within Finnish aviation, reshaping how airlines screened pilots before flights.

evt-01-03-1973-cbs.scenario: You're a baseball insider in January 1973 reading that CBS, owner of the New York Yankees since 1964, has finally agreed to sell the struggling franchise.
evt-01-03-1973-cbs.prompt: Who leads the group that buys the Yankees from CBS?

choices.text: Entertainment mogul Charles Bronfman
Broadcasting executive William Paley
Shipbuilding executive George Steinbrenner
Team owner Walter O'Malley

evt-01-03-1973-cbs.butterflyEffect: Steinbrenner's group bought the Yankees for about $10 million, a deal he later called the best investment he ever made. Under his ownership the team embraced the new free-agency era, rebuilding into a dynasty that won World Series titles in 1977 and 1978.

evt-01-03-1977-apple-inc.scenario: It is 3 January 1977 in Cupertino, and you are Ronald Wayne, the third co-founder of the newly incorporated Apple Computer, worried that Jobs and Wozniak's spending could leave you personally liable for company debts.
evt-01-03-1977-apple-inc.prompt: What did you decide to do with your 10% stake in the new company?

choices.text: Keep the stake and become an active company executive
Sell the stake back to Jobs and Wozniak for a few hundred dollars
Donate the stake to a local university
Trade the stake to an outside investor for a large cash sum

evt-01-03-1977-apple-inc.butterflyEffect: Wayne sold his stake back for $800 within weeks, wary of the fledgling company's debts. Had he kept it, that share would later have been worth billions of dollars as Apple grew into one of the world's most valuable corporations.

evt-01-03-1987-varig-flight-797.scenario: It is 3 January 1987, and you are the captain of Varig Flight 797, climbing out of Abidjan toward Rio de Janeiro, when an engine fails and you must decide how to handle the return.
evt-01-03-1987-varig-flight-797.prompt: What happened during the attempted emergency return to Abidjan airport?

choices.text: The crew ditched successfully in a nearby lagoon
The aircraft landed safely on three engines with no injuries
The approach was misjudged, the aircraft stalled, and it crashed short of the runway
A second engine failure forced a mid-air explosion before landing

evt-01-03-1987-varig-flight-797.butterflyEffect: You misjudged the approach, stalled the aircraft, and it crashed into a rubber plantation 18 kilometres from the runway, killing all but one of the 50 aboard. The disaster fed a run of fatal Varig 707 incidents that pushed the airline to retire its aging fleet in favor of newer jets.

evt-01-03-1990-united-states-invasion-of.scenario: It is 3 January 1990, and you are General Manuel Noriega, holed up for days inside the Vatican's Panama City embassy while US troops blast loud rock music outside and American forces occupy the country.
evt-01-03-1990-united-states-invasion-of.prompt: What did Noriega do after days sheltering in the Vatican embassy?

choices.text: He escaped through a tunnel to rally loyalist troops
He surrendered to the waiting American forces outside
He negotiated safe exile in a third country
He was extracted by Panamanian military allies

evt-01-03-1990-united-states-invasion-of.butterflyEffect: Noriega walked out and surrendered to US forces, who flew him to Miami to face drug trafficking charges. His capture ended Operation Just Cause, cemented Guillermo Endara's presidency, and became a template for later US interventions justified by pursuing individual foreign leaders.

evt-01-03-1993-george-h-w-bush.scenario: It is 3 January 1993 in Moscow. In the final weeks of his presidency, you are advising George H. W. Bush as he and Boris Yeltsin sit down to sign a new arms control treaty going beyond START I.
evt-01-03-1993-george-h-w-bush.prompt: What key restriction does the new treaty impose?

choices.text: Cap warhead numbers at existing START I levels only
Ban all nuclear-armed submarines from both navies
Eliminate all land-based missiles carrying multiple warheads
Allow unlimited land-based missile deployment for both sides

evt-01-03-1993-george-h-w-bush.butterflyEffect: START II committed both sides to eliminate all land-based multiple-warhead (MIRVed) ICBMs, the weapons seen as most destabilizing. Russia never ratified it amid disputes over NATO expansion and US missile defense plans, and it was ultimately abandoned in 2002 — but it laid groundwork for the New START treaty signed in 2010.

evt-01-03-1999-mars-polar-lander.scenario: It is 3 January 1999 at Cape Canaveral, and NASA engineers watch the Mars Polar Lander lift off, bound for the icy terrain near the Martian south pole to study soil and climate.
evt-01-03-1999-mars-polar-lander.prompt: What happened when the lander attempted to touch down on Mars eleven months later?

choices.text: It burned up while still in the Martian atmosphere
It landed safely and transmitted years of climate data
It missed Mars entirely and drifted into deep space
It lost contact and was destroyed after its descent engine cut off too early

evt-01-03-1999-mars-polar-lander.butterflyEffect: On 3 December 1999 the lander fell silent during descent and was never heard from again. Investigators later concluded its engine likely shut off prematurely, causing it to slam into the surface, a failure that led NASA to overhaul testing and communication procedures for future Mars missions.

evt-01-03-2002-second-intifada.scenario: It is early January 2002 in the Red Sea. You command an Israeli naval unit shadowing the freighter MV Karine A, which intelligence claims is smuggling Iranian weapons toward the Palestinian Authority, though it sails in international waters.

choices.text: Sink the vessel with all hands to destroy the evidence
Let the freighter pass to avoid an international incident
Wait for UN Security Council authorization before acting
Board and seize the ship despite it being in international waters

evt-01-03-2002-second-intifada.butterflyEffect: Israeli commandos stormed and seized the ship, finding roughly 50 tons of weapons below decks. Israel used the seizure to accuse Yasser Arafat of violating his commitments to non-violence, which the Bush administration cited in sidelining Arafat from further peace negotiations.

evt-01-03-2002-israeli-palestinian-confl.scenario: It's January 2002, and you're part of an Israeli naval commando team boarding a flagless freighter, the Karine A, intercepted far out in the Red Sea.
evt-01-03-2002-israeli-palestinian-confl.prompt: What does the search of the ship's hold uncover?

choices.text: Barrels of smuggled oil evading international sanctions
A shipment of counterfeit currency
A large hidden cache of rockets, mines and other weapons
Crates of humanitarian food aid bound for Gaza

evt-01-03-2002-israeli-palestinian-confl.butterflyEffect: Israeli forces found roughly 50 tons of weapons, including rockets and mortars, which Israel said were destined for the Palestinian Authority. Arafat denied any knowledge, but the affair deepened American and Israeli distrust of him and hardened positions just as ceasefire efforts during the Second Intifada were unraveling.

evt-01-03-2004-flash-airlines-flight-604.scenario: It is just after midnight on 3 January 2004. You are the captain of a Boeing 737 climbing away from Sharm El Sheikh over the dark Red Sea, with no visible horizon to orient yourself.
evt-01-03-2004-flash-airlines-flight-604.prompt: What ultimately caused the fatal loss of control after takeoff?

choices.text: Air traffic control ordered an unnecessary emergency descent
A bomb planted in the cargo hold detonated minutes after takeoff
The aircraft was struck by a sudden, violent thunderstorm cell
The pilot became spatially disoriented over the black, moonless sea and lost control of the aircraft

evt-01-03-2004-flash-airlines-flight-604.butterflyEffect: The 737 rolled and dived into the sea, killing all 148 aboard, mostly French tourists. French investigators blamed spatial disorientation and pilot error; Egyptian investigators disputed this and suspected a mechanical fault, and the two nations never reached agreement, leaving the cause officially contested to this day.

evt-01-03-2015-boko-haram.scenario: It's early January 2015 in Baga, a lakeside garrison town in north-east Nigeria, and word spreads that Boko Haram fighters are advancing on the multinational military base meant to protect it.
evt-01-03-2015-boko-haram.prompt: What happens to the force defending the town as the attack unfolds?

choices.text: The defenders repel the assault and hold the town
Nigerian air support destroys the attacking column before it arrives
The defenders are overrun and retreat, leaving the town to be destroyed
Foreign peacekeepers arrive within hours to relieve the base

evt-01-03-2015-boko-haram.butterflyEffect: The multinational force was overwhelmed and withdrew, and Baga was largely destroyed in the assault. The disaster exposed how outmatched the regional coalition was, pushing Chad, Niger, Cameroon and Nigeria to reinforce the joint task force and becoming a major factor in Nigeria's tense 2015 election.

evt-01-03-2019-chang-e-4.scenario: It's 3 January 2019, and you're a controller in Beijing watching Chang'e 4 drop toward the Moon's far side, a hemisphere that never faces Earth and blocks any direct radio signal.
evt-01-03-2019-chang-e-4.prompt: How does the mission keep contact with the lander during its historic touchdown?

choices.text: The landing site is chosen so Earth stays barely visible on the horizon
A dedicated relay satellite parked beyond the Moon bounces signals to Earth
Ground stations bounce signals off the Moon's near side using lasers
The lander stores data and transmits it once it drifts into view of Earth

evt-01-03-2019-chang-e-4.butterflyEffect: China had launched the Queqiao relay satellite to the Earth-Moon L2 point months earlier, bouncing signals between the far side and mission control. The successful landing let rover Yutu-2 explore Von Kármán crater and set the stage for China's later sample-return and planned lunar-base missions.

evt-01-03-2020-qasem-soleimani.scenario: It is 3 January 2020, hours after a US airstrike near Baghdad airport has killed Iranian General Qasem Soleimani. You are a US military planner in the region bracing for Iran's response.
evt-01-03-2020-qasem-soleimani.prompt: What does Iran actually do in retaliation days later?

choices.text: Iran formally declares war on the United States
Iran launches ballistic missiles at US bases in Iraq
Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz to all shipping
Iran strikes Saudi oil facilities in direct retaliation

evt-01-03-2020-qasem-soleimani.butterflyEffect: Iran launched ballistic missiles at US forces stationed at Ain al-Asad airbase in Iraq, causing no fatalities but numerous traumatic brain injuries among troops. In the chaos of heightened alert that followed, Iranian air defenses mistakenly shot down a Ukrainian passenger jet, killing all 176 aboard.

evt-01-03-2024-2024-kerman-bombings.scenario: You are a security coordinator in Kerman on 3 January 2024, tasked with protecting the enormous crowd gathered at Qasem Soleimani's grave for the anniversary of his death, in a country where such commemorations are treated as high-security state occasions.
evt-01-03-2024-2024-kerman-bombings.prompt: Which group claimed responsibility for the twin bombings the following day?

choices.text: A rival Iranian political faction
Al-Qaeda's regional affiliate
An Iranian ethnic separatist group
The Islamic State (ISIS-Khorasan Province)

evt-01-03-2024-2024-kerman-bombings.butterflyEffect: The Islamic State's Khorasan Province branch claimed the attack, which killed at least 95 people and became Iran's deadliest terrorist incident since the 1978 Cinema Rex fire. The bombings sharpened Iran's security posture at public gatherings and added another flashpoint to the already tense Iran–ISIS-K conflict playing out across the region.

evt-01-04-1698-palace-of-whitehall.scenario: It is January 1698, and you are a servant at the sprawling Palace of Whitehall when flames suddenly rip through the timber buildings on a freezing night.
evt-01-04-1698-palace-of-whitehall.prompt: What happens to the palace as the fire rages through it?

choices.text: The palace is rebuilt within the same year
The fire is contained to a single kitchen wing
The blaze spreads across the river to Westminster Abbey
Nearly the whole palace burns except the Banqueting House

evt-01-04-1698-palace-of-whitehall.butterflyEffect: Most of the palace's roughly 1,500 rooms burned to ruin, but Inigo Jones's Banqueting House of 1622 survived. The monarchy never rebuilt Whitehall as a residence, shifting to St James's Palace instead, while the site's name endured as shorthand for the British government itself.

evt-01-04-1853-solomon-northup.scenario: You are Solomon Northup, a free Black musician from New York drugged and sold into slavery in 1841. After nearly twelve years in Louisiana, a sympathetic Canadian laborer on the plantation offers to help.
evt-01-04-1853-solomon-northup.prompt: How does word of your captivity finally reach your family in New York?

choices.text: He escapes at night and travels the Underground Railroad alone
A sympathetic laborer secretly sends letters north to alert his family
A New York lawyer discovers him by chance while visiting Louisiana
His enslaver agrees to sell him back his own freedom

evt-01-04-1853-solomon-northup.butterflyEffect: Samuel Bass secretly mailed letters north, alerting Northup's family and New York's governor, who invoked a state law protecting free citizens kidnapped into slavery. Northup was freed on January 3, 1853, and his memoir Twelve Years a Slave became a powerful abolitionist document, later adapted into an Oscar-winning 2013 film.

evt-01-04-1951-korean-war.scenario: It is 4 January 1951. You are a UN officer watching Seoul fall for the second time as Chinese and North Korean troops pour across the Han River, and your battered division has no orders to hold the line.
evt-01-04-1951-korean-war.prompt: What does UN command decide to do next?

choices.text: Counterattack immediately to retake Seoul within days
Withdraw further south to reorganize and build new defensive lines
Evacuate all UN forces from the Korean Peninsula entirely
Negotiate an immediate ceasefire with Chinese commanders

evt-01-04-1951-korean-war.butterflyEffect: Eighth Army, now under General Matthew Ridgway, withdrew to new defensive lines well south of Seoul rather than making a costly stand. Ridgway used the pause to regroup and resupply, then launched counteroffensives that retook Seoul in March 1951, stabilizing a front near the 38th parallel that would define the war's final two years.

evt-01-04-1970-1970-tonghai-earthquake.scenario: You are a geologist studying the Red River Fault in Yunnan province, a fault line that has stayed quiet since a major quake in 1700. In the early hours of January 5, 1970, the ground beneath Tonghai suddenly ruptures.
evt-01-04-1970-1970-tonghai-earthquake.prompt: What does the earthquake reveal about the fault's long silence?

choices.text: The fault had become permanently inactive after 1700
The quake was unrelated to the fault and came from a separate source
The fault only produces harmless minor tremors
Centuries of stress had been quietly accumulating before the sudden rupture

evt-01-04-1970-1970-tonghai-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The 1970 rupture showed that centuries of apparent quiet had masked slow-building tectonic stress along the Red River Fault rather than true inactivity. The disaster pushed Chinese seismologists to intensify monitoring of intraplate faults across Yunnan, a region since recognized as one of China's most earthquake-prone.

evt-01-04-1972-rose-heilbron.scenario: It is 4 January 1972 and you are a young barrister watching Rose Heilbron take her seat as the first woman judge ever to sit at London's Central Criminal Court, the Old Bailey.
evt-01-04-1972-rose-heilbron.prompt: What earlier legal 'first' had Heilbron already achieved before this appointment?

choices.text: First woman to serve on a criminal jury in England
First woman to win a scholarship to Gray's Inn and take silk as King's Counsel
First woman appointed Lord Chancellor
First woman elected to the House of Commons

evt-01-04-1972-rose-heilbron.butterflyEffect: Heilbron had already become one of the first two women appointed King's Counsel and the first woman to lead a murder defence. Her Old Bailey appointment reinforced her role as a trailblazer, and later that decade she became only the second woman ever appointed to the High Court, after Elizabeth Lane.

evt-01-04-1976-the-troubles.scenario: It is the night of 4 January 1976 in rural County Armagh. UVF gunmen have just shot dead six Catholic civilians in the Reavey and O'Dowd family homes, and you are an RUC officer taking the first reports of the attack.
evt-01-04-1976-the-troubles.prompt: What should you warn your commanders was likely to follow within the next 24 hours?

choices.text: The arrest and conviction of the gunmen within days
An immediate IRA ceasefire declaration
A sectarian reprisal attack against Protestant civilians
A formal peace conference between paramilitary groups

evt-01-04-1976-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The following evening, 5 January, republican gunmen stopped a minibus at Kingsmill and shot the Protestant workmen aboard in direct retaliation, killing ten. The two attacks became one of the grimmest examples of the tit-for-tat sectarian killing cycle that defined the mid-1970s Troubles.

evt-01-04-1987-1987-maryland-train-colli.scenario: It is January 4, 1987, and you are a dispatcher on Amtrak's Northeast Corridor as Conrail locomotives sit fouling the mainline near Chase, Maryland while the Colonial speeds north from Washington.
evt-01-04-1987-1987-maryland-train-colli.prompt: What allows the Conrail engines to be on the mainline as Amtrak's train bears down on them?

choices.text: A track switch mechanically failed to reset
Heavy fog obscured the signal lights
The Conrail crew, impaired by drug use, missed the warning signals
A dispatcher's radio malfunctioned during the handoff

evt-01-04-1987-1987-maryland-train-colli.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the Conrail crew had missed multiple warning signals after smoking marijuana on duty. The disaster's revelations helped push Congress toward the 1991 Omnibus Transportation Employee Testing Act, mandating drug and alcohol testing across the rail industry.

evt-01-04-1989-1989-air-battle-near-tobr.scenario: It is 4 January 1989 over the Mediterranean north of Tobruk. You are flying an F-14 Tomcat on combat air patrol when two Libyan MiG-23 Floggers turn and close on your formation despite repeated defensive maneuvers.
evt-01-04-1989-1989-air-battle-near-tobr.prompt: Under your rules of engagement, what should you do once the Libyan jets continue closing after multiple evasive turns?

choices.text: Fire air-to-air missiles to down the approaching jets
Hold fire until the Libyan jets fire first
Break off patrol and return immediately to the carrier
Radio Tripoli directly to request clarification

evt-01-04-1989-1989-air-battle-near-tobr.butterflyEffect: The American pilots fired AIM-7 Sparrow missiles and downed both MiG-23s, the second such Gulf of Sidra clash after a nearly identical 1981 incident. The engagement deepened the confrontation between Washington and Tripoli over Libya's disputed claim to the Gulf of Sidra as territorial waters.

evt-01-04-1998-january-1998-north-americ.scenario: It is January 1998, and freezing rain has coated Quebec and eastern Ontario in inches of ice. Power pylons are collapsing under the weight, and millions face a Montreal winter with no heat or light.
evt-01-04-1998-january-1998-north-americ.prompt: What do Canadian authorities do to respond to the collapsing power grid?

choices.text: Request emergency aid exclusively from the United States military
Deploy Canadian Forces personnel to assist utility crews and maintain order
Leave restoration entirely to provincial utility companies
Evacuate Montreal and Ottawa entirely until power is restored

evt-01-04-1998-january-1998-north-americ.butterflyEffect: Ottawa deployed over 16,000 Canadian Forces personnel, the largest domestic military mobilization since the Korean War, to clear debris and support utility crews. The crisis exposed how vulnerable overhead lines were to ice, spurring utilities to bury more cable and rebuild transmission towers to tougher standards.

evt-01-04-1999-jesse-ventura.scenario: It is 4 January 1999 in St. Paul, Minnesota, and you watch former professional wrestler Jesse Ventura take the oath of office as governor, having stunned both major parties in the election.
evt-01-04-1999-jesse-ventura.prompt: What third-party ticket carried Ventura to his upset victory over the Democratic and Republican nominees?

choices.text: The Green Party
The Reform Party
An independent write-in campaign
The Libertarian Party

evt-01-04-1999-jesse-ventura.butterflyEffect: Ventura won as the Reform Party candidate, becoming the only Reform Party politician ever elected to major office in the United States. His victory briefly energized third-party politics nationally, though he later left the party and served his term as an independent.

evt-01-04-2004-spirit-rover.scenario: It is January 4, 2004, and you are a JPL engineer watching telemetry as NASA's Spirit rover plunges toward Gusev Crater on Mars, three weeks ahead of its twin Opportunity.
evt-01-04-2004-spirit-rover.prompt: How does Spirit actually touch down safely on the Martian surface?

choices.text: A sky-crane lowers the rover gently onto the surface on cables
Wheels absorb the impact directly without any parachute or airbags
Retrorockets alone bring the rover to a soft, airbag-free stop
Airbags cushion the rover's bouncing landing after a parachute and retrorocket descent

evt-01-04-2004-spirit-rover.butterflyEffect: Spirit landed using a parachute and retrorockets followed by airbags that cushioned its bounce across Gusev Crater's floor. Designed for a 90-day mission, it operated for over six years until getting stuck in soft sand in 2009, and its success helped validate landing techniques later refined for Curiosity's sky-crane descent.

evt-01-04-2004-mikheil-saakashvili.scenario: It is January 4, 2004, and you are a Georgian voter heading to the polls weeks after the peaceful Rose Revolution swept aside President Shevardnadze.
evt-01-04-2004-mikheil-saakashvili.prompt: What is the result of this presidential election?

choices.text: Saakashvili wins in an overwhelming landslide
Shevardnadze narrowly retains power
Opposition parties boycott and the vote is annulled
The election forces a runoff between two candidates

evt-01-04-2004-mikheil-saakashvili.butterflyEffect: Saakashvili won in a landslide with roughly 96 percent of the vote, becoming Europe's youngest head of state at the time. His pro-Western, anti-corruption drive reshaped Georgian politics but also fueled tensions with Russia that erupted into the 2008 war over South Ossetia.

evt-01-04-2006-ehud-olmert.scenario: It is 4 January 2006 in Jerusalem. Word reaches the cabinet that Prime Minister Ariel Sharon has suffered a massive stroke and is unconscious, leaving Israel without an active head of government.
evt-01-04-2006-ehud-olmert.prompt: Who steps in to lead the country in this moment?

choices.text: Deputy Prime Minister Ehud Olmert becomes acting prime minister
President Moshe Katsav takes direct control of the government
Opposition leader Benjamin Netanyahu is recalled to lead
The Knesset immediately dissolves and calls snap elections

evt-01-04-2006-ehud-olmert.butterflyEffect: Deputy Prime Minister Ehud Olmert assumed the duties of acting prime minister, then led Sharon's new Kadima party to victory in the March 2006 election, becoming prime minister outright. His tenure was soon consumed by the 2006 Lebanon War and later corruption scandals that forced his resignation in 2009.

evt-01-04-2007-nancy-pelosi.scenario: It is January 4, 2007, and you are a newly sworn-in Democratic representative on the House floor, about to cast your vote for Speaker after your party's sweep of the 2006 midterms.
evt-01-04-2007-nancy-pelosi.prompt: Who does the Democratic majority elect as Speaker of the House?

choices.text: John Boehner
Nancy Pelosi
Harry Reid
Steny Hoyer

evt-01-04-2007-nancy-pelosi.butterflyEffect: Nancy Pelosi became the first woman elected Speaker of the House, a role she held from 2007-2011 and again from 2019-2023. Her speakership would later be pivotal in passing the Affordable Care Act and shaped two decades of Democratic strategy in Congress.

evt-01-04-2007-110th-united-states-congr.scenario: It is 4 January 2007 on the floor of the House of Representatives. The newly sworn-in 110th Congress, with Democrats holding the majority for the first time in over a decade, is about to elect its presiding officer.
evt-01-04-2007-110th-united-states-congr.prompt: Who did this Congress elect as the first woman ever to serve as Speaker of the House?

choices.text: Steny Hoyer
Nancy Pelosi
John Boehner
Dennis Hastert

evt-01-04-2007-110th-united-states-congr.butterflyEffect: Nancy Pelosi became Speaker, placing her third in the presidential line of succession, the highest position ever held by a woman in American government at that time. She would go on to lead House Democrats for years and later reclaim the speakership in 2019.

evt-01-04-2010-burj-khalifa.scenario: It is January 4, 2010, and you stand among dignitaries in Dubai as fireworks erupt around a needle-thin tower rising higher than any structure ever built.
evt-01-04-2010-burj-khalifa.prompt: What record does the tower claim at its grand opening, and what is it renamed?

choices.text: It sets only a record for most floors, keeping its original name
It becomes the world's tallest structure and is renamed Burj Khalifa
It ties with Taipei 101 and is renamed Burj Dubai Tower
It is declared the tallest hotel but not the tallest building

evt-01-04-2010-burj-khalifa.butterflyEffect: Originally called Burj Dubai, the tower was renamed Burj Khalifa at its opening in honor of Sheikh Khalifa of Abu Dhabi, whose financial backing had helped Dubai through its debt crisis. It remains the world's tallest structure and spurred a global race among cities to build ever-taller supertalls.

evt-01-04-2018-hennenman-kroonstad-train.scenario: It is January 4, 2018, and you are aboard a Shosholoza Meyl passenger train approaching Geneva Station between Hennenman and Kroonstad in South Africa's Free State.
evt-01-04-2018-hennenman-kroonstad-train.prompt: What causes the train to derail and catch fire?

choices.text: A sudden brake failure on a downhill grade
A collision with a truck at an unguarded level crossing
A collision with livestock that had strayed onto the line
Deliberate sabotage of the track

evt-01-04-2018-hennenman-kroonstad-train.butterflyEffect: The train collided with a truck at an unguarded level crossing, derailing several carriages that then caught fire. The disaster intensified scrutiny of South Africa's poorly maintained level crossings and rail safety standards under operator PRASA.

evt-01-05-1675-franco-dutch-war.scenario: It is January 1675 in Alsace. You march with Marshal Turenne's army through winter snow, seeking to strike a combined Austrian and Brandenburg force before it can consolidate near Turckheim.
evt-01-05-1675-franco-dutch-war.prompt: What tactic does Turenne use to gain the advantage?

choices.text: A rapid winter march to outflank and surprise the enemy
A single massed cavalry charge against the center
A naval blockade of the Rhine to cut off supplies
A prolonged siege of the nearest fortified town

evt-01-05-1675-franco-dutch-war.butterflyEffect: Turenne's forced winter march allowed him to outmaneuver and surprise the Imperial coalition, driving them back across the Rhine and securing Alsace for France. The victory cemented his reputation as one of Europe's finest generals, only months before his death at Sasbach later that year.

evt-01-05-1757-louis-xv.scenario: It is a bitterly cold evening at Versailles in January 1757. King Louis XV is stepping into his carriage when a man in the crowd suddenly lunges forward, a blade hidden in his palm.
evt-01-05-1757-louis-xv.prompt: What happens to the king in the attack?

choices.text: Guards intercept the attacker before any contact is made
He suffers a shallow knife wound and survives
He is unharmed but the shock causes him to collapse
He is killed instantly by the blade

evt-01-05-1757-louis-xv.butterflyEffect: Robert-François Damiens's knife left only a shallow wound between two ribs, and Louis XV recovered within weeks. Damiens was tortured and executed by drawing and quartering, one of the last such executions in France, and its horrific spectacle later became a touchstone for Enlightenment critiques of judicial cruelty.

evt-01-05-1869-te-kooti-s-war.scenario: It is January 1869 at the pā of Ngātapa. After five days under siege, government forces are about to overrun the position, and only a sheer cliff behind the pā offers any chance of escape.
evt-01-05-1869-te-kooti-s-war.prompt: What does Te Kooti do as the pā falls?

choices.text: Surrender the pā to negotiate terms
Set fire to the pā and fight to the last man
Descend the cliff face to escape capture
Launch a final counterattack against the besieging force

evt-01-05-1869-te-kooti-s-war.butterflyEffect: Te Kooti and a small band descended the cliff and slipped away, and he continued leading resistance for several more years. Many followers who could not escape were captured, and their treatment afterward remained a bitter grievance among Māori for generations.

evt-01-05-1919-german-workers-party.scenario: It is 5 January 1919 in a Munich beer hall. Locksmith Anton Drexler and journalist Karl Harrer have gathered a small circle of disillusioned workers and ex-soldiers to launch a new political party.
evt-01-05-1919-german-workers-party.prompt: What kind of program does this new German Workers' Party champion?

choices.text: Internationalist and communist, aligned with the Spartacists
Catholic centrist, focused on church-state relations
Nationalist and antisemitic, opposed to the Versailles Treaty
Monarchist, seeking restoration of Kaiser Wilhelm II

evt-01-05-1919-german-workers-party.butterflyEffect: The DAP preached German nationalism, antisemitism, and rejection of the Versailles settlement, but remained tiny and obscure. In September 1919 an army veteran named Adolf Hitler joined as its 55th member, and by 1920 he had transformed it into the National Socialist German Workers' Party.

evt-01-05-1922-ernest-shackleton.scenario: It is early January 1922, and you are a crew member aboard the Quest, anchored off South Georgia Island for Shackleton's fourth Antarctic expedition. Before dawn, 'the Boss' suffers a sudden heart attack in his cabin.
evt-01-05-1922-ernest-shackleton.prompt: What happens to Shackleton's body once the expedition decides on his final resting place?

choices.text: He is buried in the Antarctic ice near his old base camp
He is cremated at sea by the crew
His body is shipped back to England for burial
He is buried at Grytviken cemetery on South Georgia

evt-01-05-1922-ernest-shackleton.butterflyEffect: Shackleton died on 5 January 1922. His wife Emily asked that he be buried where he fell rather than returned to England, and he was interred at Grytviken, South Georgia. The grave became a pilgrimage site for polar explorers, and the expedition continued under Frank Wild.

evt-01-05-1925-nellie-tayloe-ross.scenario: You are Nellie Tayloe Ross, taking the oath of office in Cheyenne on 5 January 1925 after winning a special election to succeed your late husband, becoming the first woman ever to serve as a U.S. state governor.
evt-01-05-1925-nellie-tayloe-ross.prompt: As you begin your term, what course do you set for your administration?

choices.text: Reverse his policies entirely to build an independent legacy
Continue her late husband's reform program, including Prohibition enforcement
Campaign immediately for a U.S. Senate seat
Leave all policymaking to the state legislature

evt-01-05-1925-nellie-tayloe-ross.butterflyEffect: Ross largely continued her late husband's reform agenda, including support for Prohibition, but narrowly lost re-election in 1926. She later became the first woman to direct the U.S. Mint in 1933, a post she held for two decades, overseeing coin production through the Depression and the Second World War.

evt-01-05-1933-golden-gate-bridge.scenario: It is 5 January 1933 and you are chief engineer Joseph Strauss, breaking ground on a suspension bridge across the treacherous, fog-choked Golden Gate that many experts still call impossible to build safely.
evt-01-05-1933-golden-gate-bridge.prompt: What unusual safety measure do you insist on for the ironworkers?

choices.text: String a large net beneath the entire span to catch falling workers
Station lifeboats in the water as the only safety measure
Forbid harnesses, since they were thought to slow the men down
Require only hard hats, following standard practice of the day

evt-01-05-1933-golden-gate-bridge.butterflyEffect: Strauss required a safety net slung beneath the roadway, which caught nineteen falling workers who survived and became known as the "Halfway to Hell Club." The bridge's pioneering safety-first approach, rare for its era, influenced construction standards on major infrastructure projects for decades afterward.

evt-01-05-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It is dawn on 3 January 1941, and you are an Australian infantryman crouched before the heavily wired perimeter of Bardia, the fortified Libyan port held by General Bergonzoli's Italian garrison. Engineers signal that the outer defenses must be breached before the advance can continue.
evt-01-05-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: What tactic does the assault rely on to break through the Italian perimeter?

choices.text: A naval bombardment alone forces the garrison to surrender
A mounted cavalry charge overruns the forward trenches
Airborne troops are dropped behind the garrison to force capitulation
Engineers blast a gap in the defenses for tanks and infantry to exploit

evt-01-05-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Australian engineers blasted a gap through the anti-tank ditch and wire under artillery cover, letting British Matilda tanks and infantry pour through to roll up the defenses from within. Bardia fell within days with roughly 40,000 Italian prisoners taken, a stunning early Allied success that carried straight into the capture of Tobruk weeks later.

evt-01-05-1949-state-of-the-union.scenario: It is 5 January 1949, and you sit in the House chamber as a newly reelected President Truman, having stunned pollsters months earlier, rises to deliver his State of the Union address and lay out his domestic agenda.
evt-01-05-1949-state-of-the-union.prompt: What name does Truman give to the ambitious domestic program he outlines?

choices.text: The Fair Deal
The New Frontier
The New Deal
The Square Deal

evt-01-05-1949-state-of-the-union.butterflyEffect: Truman branded his agenda the 'Fair Deal,' promising civil rights measures, national health insurance, and an expanded welfare state building on the New Deal. Congress blocked much of it, but pieces like the minimum wage increase and public housing expansion passed, and the label shaped later liberal reform efforts.

evt-01-05-1970-1970-tonghai-earthquake.scenario: It is just past 1 a.m. on 5 January 1970 in Tonghai, Yunnan, and the ground has torn itself apart, burying whole villages. You are a local Party cadre who must decide how to report the disaster to Beijing during the height of the Cultural Revolution.
evt-01-05-1970-1970-tonghai-earthquake.prompt: How should you handle reporting the true scale of the disaster to the central government?

choices.text: Refuse to file any report and let local officials manage it independently
Report the estimated toll honestly and request outside assistance
Broadcast the disaster internationally to appeal for foreign aid
Downplay the casualty figures and keep the disaster largely out of the press

evt-01-05-1970-1970-tonghai-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Chinese authorities suppressed the true death toll for over a decade, treating open acknowledgment of disaster losses as politically embarrassing during the Cultural Revolution. The real figures only became public in the 1980s, and the quake's near-total secrecy became a case study in how Maoist-era politics distorted disaster response and delayed seismic research on the Red River Fault.

evt-01-05-1976-the-troubles.scenario: It is the night of 5 January 1976 in rural South Armagh. A minibus carrying twelve textile workers home from a factory is flagged down at what looks like an army checkpoint, one night after six local Catholics were shot dead nearby.
evt-01-05-1976-the-troubles.prompt: What do the armed men at the checkpoint do to the workers?

choices.text: Open fire on all twelve without asking anything
Separate the sole Catholic worker, send him away, then shoot the rest
Search the bus and let all twelve go unharmed
Take the whole group hostage for ransom

evt-01-05-1976-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The gunmen asked the workers their religion, sent the one Catholic man away, and then opened fire on the eleven Protestants, killing ten in what became known as the Kingsmill massacre. Though no group ever officially claimed it, the killings were widely attributed to the IRA and hardened sectarian divisions, fuelling further tit-for-tat violence across the border region for years afterward.

evt-01-05-1991-embassy-of-the-united-sta.scenario: It is January 1991 and Somalia's government has collapsed into civil war around you. As a Marine helicopter pilot, you are ordered to pull embassy staff out of Mogadishu before the fighting reaches the compound.
evt-01-05-1991-embassy-of-the-united-sta.prompt: How do you extract the diplomats safely?

choices.text: Charter a commercial airliner to fly staff out
Organize an armored convoy to the international airport
Wait inside the compound for a negotiated ceasefire
Fly evacuees by helicopter to US Navy ships waiting offshore

evt-01-05-1991-embassy-of-the-united-sta.butterflyEffect: In Operation Eastern Exit, CH-53 helicopters flew from amphibious ships offshore and lifted out over 260 people without loss, closing the embassy after three decades. The US then had no diplomatic presence as Somalia descended into famine and warlordism, a vacuum that led to the 1992 humanitarian intervention and the 1993 Battle of Mogadishu.

evt-01-05-2005-dwarf-planet.scenario: You are part of a team scanning archival images from the Samuel Oschin Telescope at Palomar Observatory in January 2005, searching for faint, slow-moving objects far beyond Neptune's orbit.
evt-01-05-2005-dwarf-planet.prompt: You spot an object that appears larger and more distant than Pluto — what should you do before going public?

choices.text: File it quietly as an already-catalogued asteroid
Carry out further observations to confirm its orbit and size before announcing
Dismiss it as a distant background star
Announce it immediately as the tenth planet

evt-01-05-2005-dwarf-planet.butterflyEffect: The object, later named Eris, was confirmed to rival Pluto in size, forcing astronomers to confront how loosely "planet" had been defined. The controversy led the IAU to adopt a formal definition in 2006, reclassifying both Eris and Pluto as dwarf planets and reshaping how the solar system is taught ever since.

evt-01-05-2005-eris-dwarf-planet.scenario: It is early January 2005, and at Palomar Observatory you are reviewing images of a faint, slow-moving object far beyond Neptune that appears bright enough to rival Pluto in size. Before announcing anything, you must decide how to proceed.
evt-01-05-2005-eris-dwarf-planet.prompt: What did the confirmation of this object ultimately force astronomers to do the following year?

choices.text: Officially declare Eris the tenth planet without further debate
Dismiss the object as ordinary trans-Neptunian debris
Keep the discovery classified pending further study
Formally define what a "planet" is, reclassifying Pluto as a dwarf planet

evt-01-05-2005-eris-dwarf-planet.butterflyEffect: The discovery of an object apparently as large as or larger than Pluto forced the International Astronomical Union to formally define "planet" for the first time in 2006. Under the new definition, Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet alongside Eris, whose name—the goddess of strife—proved fitting given the discord the debate caused among astronomers and the public.

evt-01-05-2007-taiwan-high-speed-rail.scenario: It is 5 January 2007, and you board the inaugural high-speed train from Taipei to Kaohsiung, a journey that once took over four hours by conventional rail. The line was built not by the state directly but through a private consortium under an unusual financing arrangement.
evt-01-05-2007-taiwan-high-speed-rail.prompt: What financing model funded this high-speed railway?

choices.text: Full state ownership and operation from the outset
A joint venture wholly owned by the Japanese state railway
A Build-Operate-Transfer model with a private consortium
Direct foreign aid grants from Japan's government

evt-01-05-2007-taiwan-high-speed-rail.butterflyEffect: Taiwan High Speed Rail Corporation built and initially operated the line under a Build-Operate-Transfer arrangement, using Japanese Shinkansen technology. The service cut the Taipei-Kaohsiung journey to about ninety minutes and reshaped commuting and business patterns across western Taiwan, though the private consortium later required a government-led financial restructuring to survive.
