evt-01-05-2008-mikheil-saakashvili.scenario: It is 5 January 2008, and you are a Georgian voter heading to the polls in a snap presidential election called after months of opposition protests forced Mikheil Saakashvili to briefly step aside.
evt-01-05-2008-mikheil-saakashvili.prompt: What is the outcome of this election?

choices.text: No candidate receives enough votes and a runoff is scheduled
The election is annulled after mass fraud allegations
An opposition candidate wins the presidency
Saakashvili wins outright in the first round

evt-01-05-2008-mikheil-saakashvili.butterflyEffect: Saakashvili won decisively enough to avoid a runoff, though opposition figures alleged fraud and continued to contest the result in the streets. The unresolved tension between Saakashvili's government and Russia over separatist regions would erupt into open war just eight months later, in August 2008.

evt-01-05-2022-kassym-jomart-tokayev.scenario: It is 5 January 2022. Fuel-price riots have spread from Zhanaozen to Almaty, government buildings are burning, and you are advising President Tokayev on how to respond before the unrest spirals further out of control.
evt-01-05-2022-kassym-jomart-tokayev.prompt: What does Tokayev do to try to regain control that day?

choices.text: Dismiss the government and declare a state of emergency
Negotiate fuel-price concessions directly with protest leaders
Order the immediate release of all political prisoners
Publicly resign and call for new elections

evt-01-05-2022-kassym-jomart-tokayev.butterflyEffect: Tokayev sacked Prime Minister Mamin and declared a nationwide state of emergency. Within a day he requested and received CSTO troops, a crackdown followed in which hundreds died, and Tokayev used the crisis to sideline the influence of former president Nazarbayev.

evt-01-05-2024-alaska-airlines-flight-12.scenario: It is 5 January 2024, minutes after takeoff from Portland. A section of the fuselage has just torn away with a bang, the cabin has depressurized, and you are the flight crew of the Boeing 737 MAX 9.
evt-01-05-2024-alaska-airlines-flight-12.prompt: What is the crew's immediate response to the depressurization?

choices.text: Shut down both engines to reduce pressure buildup
Divert to the farthest coastal airport with a longer runway
Initiate an emergency descent and don oxygen masks
Continue climbing to reach a higher, calmer altitude

evt-01-05-2024-alaska-airlines-flight-12.butterflyEffect: The crew declared an emergency, descended rapidly, and returned safely to Portland with no fatalities. Investigators found the door plug's bolts had never been properly installed, prompting the FAA to ground all 737 MAX 9 aircraft with the same panel and intensify scrutiny of Boeing's manufacturing quality.

evt-01-06-1066-harold-godwinson.scenario: It's 6 January 1066, hours after Edward the Confessor's death. You stand in Westminster Abbey as the Witan offers the crown to Harold Godwinson, bypassing the young Edgar Ætheling.
evt-01-06-1066-harold-godwinson.prompt: What does Harold do when offered the throne?

choices.text: Splits the realm with his brother Tostig
Declines, insisting Edgar Ætheling should rule instead
Accepts and is crowned king that same day
Demands a delay until Norman claims are resolved

evt-01-06-1066-harold-godwinson.butterflyEffect: Harold accepted and was crowned that same day, but his swift rise enraged both William of Normandy and Harald Hardrada of Norway, who each invaded England within the year. Harold crushed Hardrada at Stamford Bridge but was killed by William at Hastings on 14 October, ending Anglo-Saxon rule and opening England to Norman law, language, and aristocracy.

evt-01-06-1322-stefan-decanski.scenario: It is January 1322, and Serbia's throne is contested after King Milutin's death. You stand among the nobles as Stefan Dečanski moves against two rival claimants, his half-brother Constantine and his cousin Vladislav, for the crown.
evt-01-06-1322-stefan-decanski.prompt: What does Dečanski do to secure the Serbian throne?

choices.text: Defeats his rivals in battle and is crowned king
Flees to Hungary to avoid the succession fight
Agrees to divide the kingdom among the claimants
Cedes the throne peacefully to Constantine

evt-01-06-1322-stefan-decanski.butterflyEffect: Dečanski defeated both rivals in battle and was crowned king, later building the great monastery of Visoki Dečani that gave him his name. His victory secured the succession for his son, Stefan Dušan, who became Serbia's greatest medieval ruler and was crowned emperor in 1346.

evt-01-06-1540-henry-viii.scenario: It is 6 January 1540 at Greenwich. You watch King Henry VIII marry Anne of Cleves, a match Thomas Cromwell arranged to secure a Protestant alliance, though Henry has already voiced dismay at his bride's appearance.
evt-01-06-1540-henry-viii.prompt: What became of this marriage in the months that followed?

choices.text: Henry had the marriage annulled and Anne lived on comfortably as his 'sister'
Henry remained married to Anne for the rest of his reign
Anne was imprisoned in the Tower of London until her death
Anne was executed for treason soon after the wedding

evt-01-06-1540-henry-viii.butterflyEffect: Henry had the marriage annulled within six months, on grounds it was never consummated, and Anne accepted a generous settlement to live on as the 'King's Beloved Sister.' Cromwell, blamed for the disastrous match, was arrested and executed within weeks of the annulment.

evt-01-06-1912-alfred-wegener.scenario: It is 6 January 1912 in Frankfurt. You are a geologist in the audience as Alfred Wegener unveils a startling new idea: that the continents were once joined and have since drifted apart.
evt-01-06-1912-alfred-wegener.prompt: What evidence does Wegener point to for continents having once fit together?

choices.text: Matching coastlines, shared fossils, and continuous rock strata across separated continents
Radioactive dating showing continents formed at different ages
Reversals in Earth's magnetic field recorded in the ocean floor
Sonar surveys mapping mid-ocean ridges

evt-01-06-1912-alfred-wegener.butterflyEffect: Wegener cited the jigsaw-like match of coastlines like Africa and South America, along with matching fossils and rock strata across oceans. Lacking a mechanism for how continents could move, his idea was largely dismissed until seafloor spreading evidence in the 1960s finally confirmed plate tectonics.

evt-01-06-1941-state-of-the-union.scenario: It is 6 January 1941. You sit in the House chamber as President Roosevelt addresses Congress, with Britain standing alone against Nazi Germany and America still officially neutral.
evt-01-06-1941-state-of-the-union.prompt: What core idea did Roosevelt use to frame America's stake in the war?

choices.text: A call to end all foreign aid and focus on hemispheric defense
A renewed pledge to expand New Deal relief programs
The 'Four Freedoms' that all people everywhere ought to enjoy
An immediate declaration of war against Germany

evt-01-06-1941-state-of-the-union.butterflyEffect: Roosevelt articulated the 'Four Freedoms'—of speech and worship, from want and fear—as universal human rights worth defending. The phrase became the moral case for Lend-Lease and later the Atlantic Charter, and inspired Norman Rockwell's famous wartime paintings.

evt-01-06-1960-national-airlines-flight-.scenario: It is the night of 6 January 1960, and as a Civil Aeronautics Board investigator you are picking through wreckage scattered across a North Carolina farm field after a National Airlines DC-6 exploded in midair over Bolivia, North Carolina.
evt-01-06-1960-national-airlines-flight-.prompt: What do investigators conclude caused the explosion?

choices.text: Structural metal fatigue in the fuselage
A lightning strike during a storm
A dynamite bomb hidden aboard the aircraft
A catastrophic engine fire

evt-01-06-1960-national-airlines-flight-.butterflyEffect: The CAB determined a dynamite bomb had been planted aboard, but no one was ever charged, and suspicion centered on a possible suicide bombing by a passenger with recent insurance policies. The case remains one of the oldest unresolved airliner bombings in U.S. aviation history.

evt-01-06-1993-border-security-force.scenario: It's 6 January 1993 in Sopore, Kashmir. Militants have just ambushed a Border Security Force patrol, and you watch as enraged BSF personnel move into the crowded market in response.
evt-01-06-1993-border-security-force.prompt: What does the BSF do in the market, and what did it set off?

choices.text: They negotiate with local elders to identify the attackers
They withdraw from the town to avoid further violence
They set fire to the market and open fire on civilians
They cordon the area and wait quietly for reinforcements

evt-01-06-1993-border-security-force.butterflyEffect: BSF personnel set fire to large parts of the market and opened fire, killing dozens of civilians in what became known as the Sopore massacre. The episode was widely condemned as a case of security-force retaliation against civilians and became one of the most cited incidents fueling international criticism of India's counterinsurgency conduct in Kashmir.

evt-01-06-1994-nancy-kerrigan.scenario: It's January 6, 1994, at the U.S. Figure Skating Championships in Detroit. Backstage, an assailant strikes Nancy Kerrigan's knee with a metal baton, leaving her doubled over and unable to skate.
evt-01-06-1994-nancy-kerrigan.prompt: What happens to Kerrigan's Olympic chances after the attack?

choices.text: She retires from competitive skating immediately
She is named to the Olympic team and later wins silver
She competes at nationals despite the injury and wins gold
She misses the Olympics entirely due to her injury

evt-01-06-1994-nancy-kerrigan.butterflyEffect: Kerrigan was added to the Olympic team by special committee decision despite withdrawing from nationals. The attack was soon traced to rival skater Tonya Harding's ex-husband and bodyguard, turning the case into a global scandal; Harding pleaded guilty to conspiracy and was banned for life, while Kerrigan won Olympic silver in Lillehammer.

evt-01-06-2017-fort-lauderdale-airport-s.scenario: It is 6 January 2017, and you are a Broward County Sheriff's deputy on duty near baggage claim in Terminal 2 when a man retrieves a pistol from his checked luggage and opens fire on travelers.

choices.text: Officers wait for a SWAT team before approaching
He is shot dead by airport security
A deputy rushes in and disarms him within roughly 90 seconds
He is talked into surrendering after a lengthy negotiation

evt-01-06-2017-fort-lauderdale-airport-s.butterflyEffect: A deputy moved in and disarmed Esteban Santiago within about 85 seconds of the first shots. Santiago, a former National Guardsman later diagnosed with schizophrenia, had legally checked the firearm on his flight, and the case intensified debate over airline checked-firearm rules and mental-health reporting for gun purchases.

evt-01-06-2019-muhammad-v-of-kelantan.scenario: It is January 2019 in Kuala Lumpur. King Muhammad V has just abdicated the Malaysian throne partway through his term, the first such abdication in the country's history, amid swirling rumours about his personal life.
evt-01-06-2019-muhammad-v-of-kelantan.prompt: How was his successor as King of Malaysia chosen?

choices.text: Muhammad V returned to the throne months later after the scandal faded
The Conference of Rulers elected Sultan Abdullah of Pahang as the new king
Malaysia suspended the monarchy and appointed a regent indefinitely
Muhammad V's young son was crowned king in his place

evt-01-06-2019-muhammad-v-of-kelantan.butterflyEffect: The Conference of Rulers elected Sultan Abdullah of Pahang to complete the rotating five-year term. Abdullah would go on to play a decisive role in the 2020 political crisis, personally interviewing MPs to determine who commanded majority support to become prime minister.

evt-01-06-2021-january-6-united-states-c.scenario: It is the afternoon of 6 January 2021, and as Vice President you are presiding over the joint session of Congress counting electoral votes when a mob breaches the Capitol, forcing lawmakers to evacuate.
evt-01-06-2021-january-6-united-states-c.prompt: Under pressure from Trump to block the count, what does the Vice President ultimately do?

choices.text: Invokes the 25th Amendment to remove Trump
Rejects electoral votes from several contested states
Certifies the results as constitutionally required
Delays the certification indefinitely

evt-01-06-2021-january-6-united-states-c.butterflyEffect: Pence refused to reject or delay the count, insisting he had no constitutional authority to do so. Congress reconvened that night and certified Joe Biden's victory in the early hours of 7 January, and the attack led to Trump's second impeachment and later criminal charges over election interference.

evt-01-06-2025-justin-trudeau.scenario: It is early January 2025. You are a Liberal MP watching caucus revolt after Chrystia Freeland's shock resignation, with the party's polling in freefall ahead of an election year.
evt-01-06-2025-justin-trudeau.prompt: What did Trudeau announce alongside his resignation as party leader?

choices.text: He dissolved the Liberal Party and formed a new movement
He prorogued Parliament and stayed on as caretaker PM until a new leader was chosen
He called an immediate general election
He resigned his Papineau seat in Parliament effective immediately

evt-01-06-2025-justin-trudeau.butterflyEffect: Trudeau prorogued Parliament until late March 2025, buying time for a leadership race while staying on as caretaker PM. Mark Carney won that race and became prime minister, then quickly called a snap election.

evt-01-07-1327-parliament-of-1327.scenario: You sit among the lords and bishops crowded into Westminster in January 1327. Isabella and Mortimer have seized power, young Edward is at their side, and King Edward II sits captive and friendless in Kenilworth Castle.
evt-01-07-1327-parliament-of-1327.prompt: What does Parliament decide to do with the captive king?

choices.text: Exile him to France to live under Isabella's family's protection
Restore him to the throne under strict new conditions
Depose him and proclaim his son Edward III king in his place
Execute him immediately for treason against the realm

evt-01-07-1327-parliament-of-1327.butterflyEffect: Parliament declared Edward II had forfeited the throne and proclaimed his fourteen-year-old son Edward III king, with Isabella and Mortimer ruling as regents. Edward II was murdered at Berkeley Castle later that year. Edward III eventually overthrew Mortimer in 1330 and went on to launch the Hundred Years' War with France.

evt-01-07-1610-galileo-galilei.scenario: It is a clear night in early January 1610, and you are Galileo Galilei, eye pressed to your improved telescope, noticing three small unfamiliar points of light lined up beside the planet Jupiter.
evt-01-07-1610-galileo-galilei.prompt: What should Galileo do to find out what these lights really are?

choices.text: Report them immediately as newly discovered fixed stars
Dismiss them as flaws in the telescope's lens
Assume they are comets passing near Jupiter
Record their positions each night to see if they move with the planet

evt-01-07-1610-galileo-galilei.butterflyEffect: Galileo tracked the points over several nights and saw them move together with Jupiter, revealing four moons orbiting the planet. Published in Sidereus Nuncius, the discovery shattered the assumption that only Earth had orbiting bodies, becoming powerful evidence for the Copernican, Sun-centered universe.

evt-01-07-1797-flag-of-italy.scenario: You are a delegate at the assembly of the newly formed Cispadane Republic in January 1797, debating what banner should represent this French-inspired sister republic in northern Italy.
evt-01-07-1797-flag-of-italy.prompt: Which color scheme do the delegates adopt as the republic's official flag?

choices.text: Yellow and black, the colors of Austrian Lombardy
Green, white, and red vertical stripes modeled on the French tricolour
A plain white banner like the Papal States
Red, white, and blue horizontal stripes like Naples

evt-01-07-1797-flag-of-italy.butterflyEffect: Delegates chose green, white, and red vertical stripes, echoing the French tricolour that had inspired the republic's revolutionary ideals. That same design was later carried forward by Napoleon's Italian Republic and, after unification in 1861, became the national flag of Italy still flown today.

evt-01-07-1955-marian-anderson.scenario: You sit in the audience at New York's Metropolitan Opera House on the evening of 7 January 1955, watching contralto Marian Anderson step onto the stage as Ulrica in Verdi's Un ballo in maschera.
evt-01-07-1955-marian-anderson.prompt: What historic first does Anderson's performance mark for the Met?

choices.text: The first African American board member of the Met
The first African American composer commissioned by the Met
The first African American to conduct a Met orchestra
The first African American to sing a leading role for the company

evt-01-07-1955-marian-anderson.butterflyEffect: Anderson became the first African American to sing a principal role with the Metropolitan Opera, breaking a color line just sixteen years after being barred from Constitution Hall by the DAR. Her debut opened the door for later Black singers like Leontyne Price and Grace Bumbry to reach the Met stage.

evt-01-07-1979-people-s-army-of-vietnam.scenario: It is early January 1979. Vietnamese tanks and infantry are closing on Phnom Penh, brushing aside the crumbling defenses of Democratic Kampuchea, while Khmer Rouge leaders scramble to abandon the capital.
evt-01-07-1979-people-s-army-of-vietnam.prompt: What happens when Vietnamese forces take the city?

choices.text: They hand the city over to United Nations peacekeepers
They negotiate a ceasefire allowing the Khmer Rouge to remain in power
They overthrow the Khmer Rouge government and end its rule of Cambodia
They withdraw after a symbolic show of force at the city's edge

evt-01-07-1979-people-s-army-of-vietnam.butterflyEffect: Phnom Penh fell on 7 January 1979, ending nearly four years of Khmer Rouge rule and the Cambodian genocide. Vietnam installed the People's Republic of Kampuchea, but Khmer Rouge remnants fled to the border and continued fighting for over a decade with Chinese and Thai support, drawing Vietnam into a costly occupation and a brief border war with China.

evt-01-07-1984-brunei.scenario: It is early January 1984 in Bandar Seri Begawan. Brunei has just become fully independent from Britain, and its leaders must decide which regional bloc to join first as they step onto the world stage.
evt-01-07-1984-brunei.prompt: What alliance did Brunei join within days of independence, becoming its sixth member?

choices.text: Joined the Commonwealth of Nations
Joined the Non-Aligned Movement
Joined ASEAN as its sixth member
Joined the United Nations

evt-01-07-1984-brunei.butterflyEffect: Brunei's swift ASEAN membership tied its oil-rich economy to regional diplomacy, giving the tiny sultanate a seat in Southeast Asian trade and security talks. It would later join the UN and the Commonwealth that same year, cementing its place among both regional and global institutions.

evt-01-07-1985-jaxa.scenario: You are an engineer at Japan's Kagoshima Space Center on 7 January 1985, watching the countdown for the Mu-3S-II rocket that will send Japan's first probe beyond Earth orbit.
evt-01-07-1985-jaxa.prompt: What is Sakigake's primary mission target once it leaves Earth?

choices.text: Fly past Halley's Comet as part of an international observation campaign
Test technology for a future Mars sample return
Orbit Venus to study its thick atmosphere
Land a rover on the Moon's surface

evt-01-07-1985-jaxa.butterflyEffect: Sakigake was launched to fly past Halley's Comet as part of an international observation fleet alongside Europe's Giotto and the Soviet Vega probes. Its success made Japan the third nation to reach interplanetary space, laying groundwork for later JAXA deep-space missions such as Hayabusa.

evt-01-07-1989-ruhollah-khomeini.scenario: It is January 1989 and you are part of an Iranian delegation standing before Mikhail Gorbachev in Moscow, carrying a personal letter from Ayatollah Khomeini meant to shape the future of a crumbling Soviet Union.
evt-01-07-1989-ruhollah-khomeini.prompt: What does Khomeini's letter urge Gorbachev to do?

choices.text: Join Iran's war effort against Iraq
Withdraw Soviet troops from Afghanistan at once
Abandon communism and turn to Islam as the true path forward
Support Iran's nuclear energy program

evt-01-07-1989-ruhollah-khomeini.butterflyEffect: The letter urged Gorbachev to abandon Marxism and study Islam as the answer to the USSR's ideological crisis. Gorbachev politely acknowledged it but did not convert; the exchange nonetheless signaled how deeply the Soviet system's legitimacy was already unraveling, less than two years before its collapse.

evt-01-07-1999-impeachment-of-bill-clint.scenario: You are a senator entering the chamber on 7 January 1999 to be sworn in as a juror in only the second presidential impeachment trial in American history. President Clinton faces charges of perjury and obstruction of justice stemming from the Lewinsky affair.
evt-01-07-1999-impeachment-of-bill-clint.prompt: What is the eventual outcome of the Senate trial?

choices.text: Clinton resigns before the trial concludes
The trial ends in a mistrial and charges are dropped
The Senate convicts him and he is removed from office
The Senate acquits him and he remains in office

evt-01-07-1999-impeachment-of-bill-clint.butterflyEffect: On 12 February 1999 the Senate acquitted Clinton on both articles, falling well short of the two-thirds majority needed to convict and remove him from office. He served out the remainder of his term, and the episode became a lasting touchstone in later debates over presidential accountability and impeachment.

evt-01-07-2015-charlie-hebdo-shooting.scenario: It is January 9, 2015, north of Paris. The Kouachi brothers, who murdered twelve people at Charlie Hebdo two days earlier, are barricaded in a printing warehouse, while a separate gunman holds hostages at a kosher supermarket in the capital.
evt-01-07-2015-charlie-hebdo-shooting.prompt: How did French police end both standoffs that day?

choices.text: French forces waited out a prolonged siege lasting several more days
Negotiators convinced the attackers to surrender peacefully
The hostages overpowered the gunmen before police arrived
GIGN and RAID commandos stormed both sites almost simultaneously, killing all three attackers

evt-01-07-2015-charlie-hebdo-shooting.butterflyEffect: GIGN and RAID commandos stormed both sites within minutes of each other, killing the Kouachi brothers and the supermarket gunman, Amedy Coulibaly. The attacks triggered France's largest security crackdown in decades and sparked the global 'Je suis Charlie' movement, reigniting debate over satire, free speech, and religious offense that still shapes French politics.

evt-01-07-2020-2019-2020-spanish-governm.scenario: You are a deputy in Spain's Congress on 7 January 2020, casting a vote that will finally end 253 days of caretaker government after two inconclusive elections.
evt-01-07-2020-2019-2020-spanish-governm.prompt: What is needed in this second round of voting to confirm a new Prime Minister?

choices.text: An immediate call for fresh elections
Only a simple majority, achievable through abstentions from smaller parties
An absolute majority in the first round alone
Direct appointment by the King without a vote

evt-01-07-2020-2019-2020-spanish-governm.butterflyEffect: Pedro Sánchez won confirmation by a razor-thin margin in the second round, where only a simple majority was needed, secured through crucial abstentions from parties including Esquerra Republicana. It produced Spain's first coalition government since democracy returned in the 1970s, with Podemos as junior partner.

evt-01-07-2020-2019-20-puerto-rico-earth.scenario: It is just before dawn on January 7, 2020, in Ponce, Puerto Rico. A magnitude 6.4 earthquake, the strongest in a weeks-long swarm, has just toppled buildings and cut power across the island's southwest.
evt-01-07-2020-2019-20-puerto-rico-earth.prompt: What did officials urge residents to do in the earthquake's immediate aftermath?

choices.text: Gather in the tallest downtown buildings for safety
Sleep outdoors and avoid entering damaged buildings until inspections were complete
Return indoors immediately once the shaking stopped
Evacuate the island entirely by ferry

evt-01-07-2020-2019-20-puerto-rico-earth.butterflyEffect: Thousands of Puerto Ricans camped outdoors for weeks, too afraid of aftershocks to re-enter their homes. The quake strained an electrical grid still fragile from Hurricane Maria, and the governor's emergency declaration brought federal disaster aid and renewed scrutiny of the island's building codes.

evt-01-08-1198-1198-papal-election.scenario: You are a cardinal in Rome in January 1198, gathered with the Sacred College after the death of Pope Celestine III to choose his successor, this time by formal secret ballot rather than open acclamation.
evt-01-08-1198-1198-papal-election.prompt: Which cardinal does the College elect as pope?

choices.text: Cencio Savelli, later elected as Honorius III
Lotario dei Conti di Segni, who becomes Innocent III
Giovanni Colonna, a leading Roman noble cardinal
Octavian of Ostia, a rival claimant from decades earlier

evt-01-08-1198-1198-papal-election.butterflyEffect: The cardinals chose Lotario dei Conti di Segni, who took the name Innocent III. He became one of the most powerful medieval popes, launching the Fourth Crusade, convening the Fourth Lateran Council of 1215, and asserting papal authority over kings across Christendom.

evt-01-08-1735-george-frideric-handel.scenario: It is opening night at Covent Garden Theatre in 1735, and you watch George Frideric Handel unveil his new opera Ariodante, hoping to outshine the rival Opera of the Nobility across town.
evt-01-08-1735-george-frideric-handel.prompt: What innovation did Handel add to Ariodante to draw audiences from his rivals?

choices.text: Replaced the Italian libretto entirely with spoken English dialogue
Removed all instrumental interludes to shorten the running time
Cast only Italian castrati and cut all female roles
Incorporated ballet sequences performed by Marie Sallé's dance company

evt-01-08-1735-george-frideric-handel.butterflyEffect: Handel enriched the opera with elaborate French-style ballet sequences danced by Marie Sallé's troupe, a novelty for London opera seria. Despite the effort, Italian opera's popularity kept fading against cheaper English entertainments, nudging Handel over the following years toward the English oratorios that would define his later career.

evt-01-08-1790-george-washington.scenario: You sit among the senators and representatives crowded into Federal Hall in New York City as President Washington rises to deliver his first annual message to Congress, a new republic's first attempt at reporting on the state of the union.
evt-01-08-1790-george-washington.prompt: What does Washington urge Congress to prioritize for the young nation's security?

choices.text: Building domestic capacity to manufacture arms and military supplies
Drafting a Bill of Rights for ratification
Negotiating the purchase of Louisiana from France
Chartering a national bank to stabilize currency

evt-01-08-1790-george-washington.butterflyEffect: Washington called for domestic manufacture of arms and ammunition so the republic would not depend on foreign powers for its defense. His address established the enduring tradition of an annual presidential report to Congress, which evolved into the modern State of the Union.

evt-01-08-1889-herman-hollerith.scenario: You work in the U.S. Census Office where a young statistician named Herman Hollerith has spent years building a machine to read punched cards, hoping it will save the office from the decade-long slog of hand-tallying the coming 1890 census.
evt-01-08-1889-herman-hollerith.prompt: What problem does Hollerith's patented tabulating machine solve for the census?

choices.text: Predicting future population growth from past trends
Digitizing photographs of census takers in the field
Automatically printing final census reports for Congress
Mechanically sorting and tallying population data from punched cards

evt-01-08-1889-herman-hollerith.butterflyEffect: His machine used electrical sensing of punched holes to sort and count population data mechanically, cutting the 1890 census tabulation from years to months. Hollerith's Tabulating Machine Company later merged with others in 1911 to form what became IBM, seeding the modern data-processing industry.

evt-01-08-1918-woodrow-wilson.scenario: It is January 8, 1918, and President Woodrow Wilson rises before a joint session of Congress to lay out his vision for ending the Great War and building a lasting peace afterward.
evt-01-08-1918-woodrow-wilson.prompt: What principle did Wilson present as the foundation for the postwar peace?

choices.text: A system of secret alliances among the victorious powers
Harsh reparations to punish Germany for starting the war
Restoration of prewar colonial empires without change
Open diplomacy, self-determination for peoples, and a league of nations

evt-01-08-1918-woodrow-wilson.butterflyEffect: Germany later cited the Fourteen Points when seeking an armistice, but the eventual Treaty of Versailles diverged sharply, imposing harsh reparations on Germany. Wilson's proposed League of Nations was created, yet the U.S. Senate refused to ratify American membership, weakening the very body he had championed.

evt-01-08-1936-reza-shah.scenario: You are a Tehran schoolteacher in January 1936, watching Reza Shah appear at a public ceremony with his wife and daughters unveiled, enforcing his new Kashf-e hijab decree as part of his drive to modernize Iran along Western lines.
evt-01-08-1936-reza-shah.prompt: What does the decree actually require women to do in public?

choices.text: Wear only Western-style hats instead of headscarves
Register for a government permit to keep wearing a veil
Remove their veils and chadors when appearing in public
Wear the veil only inside religious buildings

evt-01-08-1936-reza-shah.butterflyEffect: Police were empowered to forcibly remove veils and chadors from women in the street, and many devout women stayed indoors rather than comply. The policy was relaxed after Reza Shah's forced abdication in 1941, but state control over women's dress remained a flashpoint in Iranian politics for decades, reversing dramatically after the 1979 revolution.

evt-01-08-1981-trans-en-provence.scenario: You are farmer Renato Nicolai in Trans-en-Provence on 8 January 1981, when a strange whistling sound draws your attention to a domed object settling in your field before it lifts off, leaving scorch marks and crushed earth behind.
evt-01-08-1981-trans-en-provence.prompt: What does he do about the strange marks left in the field?

choices.text: He keeps it secret to avoid being ridiculed by neighbors
He sells the story directly to a tabloid newspaper
He plows over the marks and says nothing
He reports it to police, who bring in France's official UFO investigators

evt-01-08-1981-trans-en-provence.butterflyEffect: He reported it to the gendarmerie, who brought in GEPAN, the French government's official UFO study group. Soil analysis found genuine physical and biochemical changes at the site, making it one of the most rigorously documented "trace" UFO cases on record, still cited and debated by ufologists and skeptics alike.

evt-01-08-2002-george-w-bush.scenario: It is January 8, 2002, and President George W. Bush stands before lawmakers from both parties at a high school signing ceremony, putting his pen to a sweeping new education law.
evt-01-08-2002-george-w-bush.prompt: What did the new law require of public schools in exchange for federal funding?

choices.text: Adoption of a single national curriculum for all states
Guaranteed free tuition at public universities
Regular standardized testing with results tied to funding
Elimination of locally elected school boards

evt-01-08-2002-george-w-bush.butterflyEffect: No Child Left Behind tied federal education funding to student performance on standardized tests, reshaping classroom priorities nationwide. Critics argued it narrowed teaching to test preparation, and the backlash eventually led Congress to replace it with the Every Student Succeeds Act in 2015.

evt-01-08-2003-air-midwest-flight-5481.scenario: You are a mechanic who just finished maintenance on a commuter turboprop at Charlotte-Douglas, unaware the elevator control cables have been rigged too tightly, restricting how far the plane's nose can pitch down once airborne.
evt-01-08-2003-air-midwest-flight-5481.prompt: What combination of factors sends the plane into an unrecoverable climb after takeoff?

choices.text: Mis-rigged elevator controls plus an aft-loaded aircraft
Contaminated fuel starving the engines
A bird strike disabling the left engine
Sudden wind shear during a rain squall

evt-01-08-2003-air-midwest-flight-5481.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the improperly rigged elevator system, combined with the aircraft being loaded past its rear weight limit, left pilots unable to push the nose down after takeoff. The crash killed all 21 aboard and led the NTSB to push for revised passenger weight standards and stricter maintenance rigging checks across the industry.

evt-01-08-2005-uss-san-francisco-ssn-711.scenario: It is 8 January 2005, and you command USS San Francisco, submerged and running at flank speed south of Guam. Without warning, the hull slams into an uncharted seamount, hurling crewmen through the boat.
evt-01-08-2005-uss-san-francisco-ssn-711.prompt: What is the immediate action to save the submarine after the collision?

choices.text: Blow ballast and drive the boat to the surface at once
Radio for a rescue submarine before attempting to move
Dive deeper to assess the extent of hull damage
Maintain course and speed until damage control reports arrive

evt-01-08-2005-uss-san-francisco-ssn-711.butterflyEffect: The crew blew ballast and surfaced immediately, saving the boat despite a crushed bow; one sailor died and dozens were injured. The accident, blamed on outdated navigation charts, triggered Navy-wide reviews of undersea chart accuracy and submarine navigation training.

evt-01-08-2010-front-for-the-liberation-.scenario: You are aboard the Togo national football team's bus, crossing into Cabinda for the Africa Cup of Nations, when gunmen from a FLEC splinter group open fire on the convoy, killing the assistant coach and the bus driver.
evt-01-08-2010-front-for-the-liberation-.prompt: What does the shaken Togo squad decide to do about the tournament?

choices.text: Withdraw from the tournament and return home
Play their opening match as scheduled the next day
Demand the tournament be moved to another country
Refuse to leave until FLEC issued a public apology

evt-01-08-2010-front-for-the-liberation-.butterflyEffect: Togo withdrew from the tournament and flew home to mourn. CAF then controversially banned Togo from the next two Cups of Nations for withdrawing, sparking outrage that a team attacked by gunmen was being punished for leaving.

evt-01-08-2011-jared-lee-loughner.scenario: You are standing in a Safeway parking lot in Tucson at a 'Congress on Your Corner' event when a gunman opens fire on Representative Gabby Giffords and the crowd around her, emptying his magazine before it runs dry.
evt-01-08-2011-jared-lee-loughner.prompt: What do bystanders do the instant the shooter's gun empties?

choices.text: Wait for armed security to intervene
Throw store merchandise at him to distract him
Retreat to safety and call 911
Tackle him and wrestle away his spare ammunition

evt-01-08-2011-jared-lee-loughner.butterflyEffect: Bystanders including Patricia Maisch wrestled away his spare magazine and helped pin him to the ground until police arrived. Giffords survived a devastating head wound but resigned from Congress in 2012 and became a prominent national advocate for gun violence prevention.

evt-01-08-2011-gabby-giffords.scenario: It is January 8, 2011, and Congresswoman Gabby Giffords is greeting constituents at a 'Congress on Your Corner' event outside a Tucson supermarket when a gunman suddenly opens fire on the crowd.
evt-01-08-2011-gabby-giffords.prompt: In the aftermath, what became the most visible response to the shooting?

choices.text: A nationwide suspension of congressional town hall events
Immediate passage of sweeping new federal gun control laws
A formal declaration of a national state of emergency
Heightened security for members of Congress and debate over political rhetoric

evt-01-08-2011-gabby-giffords.butterflyEffect: Giffords survived a severe brain injury and resigned from Congress in January 2012, later becoming, with husband Mark Kelly, a leading national voice for gun violence prevention. The attack intensified debate over political rhetoric and security for public officials, though comprehensive federal gun legislation did not follow immediately.

evt-01-08-2016-el-chapo.scenario: It is before dawn on 8 January 2016 in Los Mochis, Mexico. You are among the Mexican Marines closing in on a safe house where intelligence says Joaquín "El Chapo" Guzmán is hiding, months after his tunnel escape from a maximum-security prison.
evt-01-08-2016-el-chapo.prompt: What actually happens when the Marines storm the house?

choices.text: He is captured after fleeing through a drainage tunnel and a shootout
He surrenders peacefully at the front door
He is killed by Marine gunfire during the raid
He escapes entirely and is never located again

evt-01-08-2016-el-chapo.butterflyEffect: Guzmán fled through a storm drain, stole a car and reached a motel, but was cornered and captured after a brief shootout. He was extradited to the United States in January 2017, convicted in a New York court in 2019, and sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years, effectively ending the Sinaloa Cartel's leadership under him.

evt-01-08-2020-ukraine-international-air.scenario: You board Flight 752 in Tehran just hours after Iran fired missiles at US bases in Iraq in retaliation for a killing days earlier, as air defense crews across the city remain on edge for possible American reprisal strikes.
evt-01-08-2020-ukraine-international-air.prompt: What causes an Iranian air defense crew to fire on the departing airliner?

choices.text: A crew misidentifies the airliner as an incoming missile
A mechanical failure in the aircraft's engine
A drone operated by a separate militia group
A deliberate strike ordered from Tehran's command center

evt-01-08-2020-ukraine-international-air.butterflyEffect: An IRGC air defense operator misidentified the climbing airliner as an incoming cruise missile and fired two missiles, killing all 176 aboard. Iran initially denied responsibility before admitting the shootdown under mounting evidence, badly straining relations with Ukraine, Canada, and other nations who lost citizens.

evt-01-08-2021-la-vega-raid.scenario: It is January 8, 2021, and units of Venezuela's National Police, FAES, and National Guard push into La Vega Parish in Caracas to break the grip of drug lord Leonardo 'El Loco Leo' Polanco Angulo. Gunfire echoes through the barrio as security forces advance street by street.
evt-01-08-2021-la-vega-raid.prompt: In the days after the raid, how did the Maduro government respond to reports of the deaths?

choices.text: Maduro ordered an immediate independent judicial investigation
Security forces publicly named and disciplined the officers involved
The government issued a formal public apology to residents
Officials stayed silent and offered no official death toll for days

evt-01-08-2021-la-vega-raid.butterflyEffect: By January 11, no member of the Maduro administration had commented on the raid or confirmed a death toll, even as journalists and human rights groups put the number of dead at 23. The silence fueled accusations of a cover-up and sharpened international scrutiny of FAES tactics in poor urban neighborhoods.

evt-01-08-2023-jair-bolsonaro.scenario: You are a security officer outside Brazil's Congress in Brasília on 8 January 2023, as thousands of Jair Bolsonaro's supporters break through barricades and pour into Congress, the Supreme Court, and the presidential palace, refusing to accept his election defeat.
evt-01-08-2023-jair-bolsonaro.prompt: What actually happens as authorities respond to the breach?

choices.text: Federal forces are called in and the buildings are retaken
Local police let the crowd occupy the buildings for days
The army seizes the moment to install Bolsonaro by force
Officials negotiate a peaceful withdrawal with rioters' leaders

evt-01-08-2023-jair-bolsonaro.butterflyEffect: Federal reinforcements retook the buildings within hours, and more than a thousand people were eventually arrested. The riot led to a federal security intervention in Brasília, inquiries into Bolsonaro's own conduct, and lasting comparisons to the 6 January 2021 US Capitol attack.

evt-01-09-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It is dusk on 9 January 1917 near Rafa in the Sinai. You lead Anzac Mounted Division troopers who have fought the Ottoman garrison all day, ammunition running low, with word that Ottoman reinforcements may be marching to relieve the defenders.
evt-01-09-1917-world-war-i.prompt: With darkness closing in, what should you order for the final push on the garrison?

choices.text: Pull back immediately to conserve the exhausted force
Halt and wait for heavier artillery to arrive
Launch a final mounted charge before darkness forces a withdrawal
Send envoys to negotiate the garrison's surrender

evt-01-09-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The mounted troops pressed one last assault before nightfall and overran the position, capturing over 1,600 Ottoman soldiers and clearing the Sinai Peninsula of Ottoman forces entirely. The victory opened the road into Palestine, setting up the string of battles at Gaza later that year.

evt-01-09-1972-rms-queen-elizabeth.scenario: It is January 1972 in Hong Kong harbor. The former Cunard flagship RMS Queen Elizabeth, renamed Seawise University under new owner Tung Chao Yung, sits mid-refit, destined to become a floating university.
evt-01-09-1972-rms-queen-elizabeth.prompt: What happened to the ship before her conversion could be finished?

choices.text: She sank in a storm while under tow to Hong Kong
She was purchased by the US Navy and used for target practice
She was destroyed by fires, suspected arson, and later scrapped
She completed conversion and sailed for decades as a floating university

evt-01-09-1972-rms-queen-elizabeth.butterflyEffect: Mysterious fires, widely suspected to be arson, broke out aboard on 9 January 1972 and capsized the ship in Hong Kong harbor. The wreck blocked shipping lanes for years before being scrapped, ending the career of Cunard's grandest liner in disaster rather than as a seagoing campus.

evt-01-09-1975-great-storm-of-1975.scenario: You are a farmer in the rural Midwest on January 10, 1975, as a monstrous panhandle-hook storm bears down, dropping temperatures and whipping up blinding snow.
evt-01-09-1975-great-storm-of-1975.prompt: What is the safest response as the blizzard intensifies around your farm?

choices.text: Stay indoors and avoid all travel until the storm passes
Drive into town immediately for extra supplies
Move livestock out into open pasture right away
Wait outside near the road for a passing rescue vehicle

evt-01-09-1975-great-storm-of-1975.butterflyEffect: The Great Storm of 1975 spawned dozens of tornadoes in the Southeast and buried the Midwest under blizzard conditions, killing dozens across the region. Its severity spurred improvements in severe-weather forecasting and blizzard warning systems in the years that followed.

evt-01-09-1981-raymond-lederer.scenario: It is 1981 in Washington. You are Congressman Raymond Lederer of Pennsylvania, already convicted of bribery and conspiracy after undercover FBI agents caught you on tape during the Abscam sting. The House Ethics Committee has recommended your expulsion and a full floor vote looms.
evt-01-09-1981-raymond-lederer.prompt: What did Lederer do as the expulsion vote approached?

choices.text: Fought the vote and was formally expelled by his colleagues
Switched parties in hopes of avoiding expulsion
Resigned from Congress before the full House vote could take place
Appealed to the Supreme Court and remained seated in Congress

evt-01-09-1981-raymond-lederer.butterflyEffect: Lederer resigned his House seat on 10 May 1981, just before the full chamber could vote to expel him, joining other Abscam-implicated members who left office rather than face formal removal. The scandal deepened public distrust of Congress and prompted lasting debate over the FBI's use of undercover stings against elected officials.

evt-01-09-1991-iraq.scenario: It is 9 January 1991, and you are US Secretary of State James Baker, sitting across from Iraqi Foreign Minister Tariq Aziz in a Geneva hotel, six days before the UN deadline for Iraq to leave Kuwait.
evt-01-09-1991-iraq.prompt: What outcome must you press Aziz to accept in this last diplomatic session?

choices.text: Complete, unconditional Iraqi withdrawal from Kuwait
A UN-supervised transition to Kuwaiti autonomy under Iraqi oversight
A negotiated partition granting Iraq disputed oil fields
An immediate ceasefire that leaves Iraqi troops in place

evt-01-09-1991-iraq.butterflyEffect: Baker demanded unconditional Iraqi withdrawal from Kuwait, but Aziz refused even to accept a letter from President Bush addressed to Saddam Hussein. The talks collapsed, and when the 15 January deadline passed without withdrawal, the US-led coalition launched Operation Desert Storm on 17 January.

evt-01-09-1992-aleksander-wolszczan.scenario: You are an astronomer reviewing pulsar timing data from Arecibo, puzzling over tiny, regular irregularities in the radio pulses from PSR B1257+12.
evt-01-09-1992-aleksander-wolszczan.prompt: What did these timing anomalies reveal about the pulsar?

choices.text: It was being orbited by planets whose gravity tugged on it
It was part of a close binary star system
It had developed an unusually powerful magnetic field
It was gradually slowing down due to age

evt-01-09-1992-aleksander-wolszczan.butterflyEffect: Wolszczan and Frail confirmed the anomalies were caused by orbiting planets, marking the first confirmed discovery of worlds beyond our solar system. The find launched modern exoplanet science years before the first planet around a Sun-like star was detected in 1995.

evt-01-09-1992-national-assembly-republi.scenario: It is 9 January 1992 in Bosnia and Herzegovina. As Yugoslavia breaks apart and Bosnian Muslim and Croat leaders push toward independence, you sit among Serb delegates debating whether to proclaim a separate republic of your own.
evt-01-09-1992-national-assembly-republi.prompt: What did the Assembly of the Serb People vote to do?

choices.text: Proclaimed a separate Serb republic within Bosnia and Herzegovina
Dissolved itself and merged with the Croatian assembly
Voted to accept Bosnian independence without conditions
Declared independence from both Yugoslavia and Bosnia entirely

evt-01-09-1992-national-assembly-republi.butterflyEffect: The Assembly proclaimed what would become Republika Srpska, rejecting a future independent Bosnia and Herzegovina outside Yugoslavia. Within months war engulfed Bosnia, and Republika Srpska survived the conflict to be recognized as one of the country's two entities under the 1995 Dayton Accords.

evt-01-09-1992-exoplanet.scenario: You are a radio astronomer at Arecibo Observatory in early 1992, studying tiny periodic timing irregularities in the pulses from the millisecond pulsar PSR B1257+12.
evt-01-09-1992-exoplanet.prompt: What should you conclude is causing the pulsar's regular timing wobbles?

choices.text: A fault in the observatory's radio receiver
The pulsar's own rotation gradually slowing down
Small planets orbiting the pulsar and tugging on its signal
Interstellar dust scattering the radio waves

evt-01-09-1992-exoplanet.butterflyEffect: Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail announced that the wobbles were caused by orbiting planets, the first confirmed exoplanets ever detected. The discovery proved planets could survive or form even around the shattered remnants of dead stars, and it launched the modern search that has since found thousands of worlds, including Earth-sized ones circling ordinary stars.

evt-01-09-1996-first-chechen-war.scenario: It is 9 January 1996 in Kizlyar, Dagestan. Chechen fighters under Salman Raduyev have just stormed the town, seizing hostages including patients from a local hospital, with Russian troops closing in from every direction.
evt-01-09-1996-first-chechen-war.prompt: What did the raiders do after seizing hostages in Kizlyar?

choices.text: Surrendered to Russian forces immediately after taking the hospital
Negotiated safe passage out of Russia entirely
Held the town indefinitely without any Russian response
Retreated toward Chechnya and became besieged by Russian troops in Pervomayskoye

evt-01-09-1996-first-chechen-war.butterflyEffect: The raiders retreated toward Chechnya with their hostages but were surrounded by Russian forces in the village of Pervomayskoye, sparking a bloody multi-day siege. The standoff ended in a violent Russian assault with heavy casualties on all sides, exposing how vulnerable federal forces remained to guerrilla raids deep inside Russian territory.

evt-01-09-1997-comair-flight-3272.scenario: You are the first officer of Comair Flight 3272, holding in freezing cloud near Detroit on the afternoon of January 9, 1997, as ice steadily builds on the wings.
evt-01-09-1997-comair-flight-3272.prompt: What should the crew do as icing conditions persist during the hold?

choices.text: Climb to a higher altitude to escape the icing layer
Exit the holding pattern promptly and ensure anti-ice systems are fully engaged
Continue holding as instructed and wait for further clearance
Reduce airspeed to conserve fuel during the delay

evt-01-09-1997-comair-flight-3272.butterflyEffect: The crew held too long in icing conditions, and ice accumulation caused the aircraft to roll uncontrollably during approach, killing all 29 aboard. The NTSB investigation that followed led to stricter icing certification standards and clearer procedures for exiting holding patterns in icing conditions.

evt-01-09-2005-mahmoud-abbas.scenario: You are a voter in the West Bank on January 9, 2005, casting a ballot in the first Palestinian presidential election since Yasser Arafat's death.
evt-01-09-2005-mahmoud-abbas.prompt: Who did Palestinian voters choose to succeed Arafat as president?

choices.text: Marwan Barghouti
Mahmoud Abbas
Ahmed Qurei
Mustafa Barghouti

evt-01-09-2005-mahmoud-abbas.butterflyEffect: Mahmoud Abbas won decisively, cementing Fatah's hold on the presidency. But rivalry with Hamas deepened, and after Hamas's 2006 election victory the Palestinian territories split, with Abbas's Fatah governing the West Bank and Hamas controlling Gaza.

evt-01-09-2005-sudan-people-s-liberation.scenario: You are an SPLA negotiator in Nairobi in January 2005, watching decades of civil war between north and south Sudan finally come to an end at the signing table.
evt-01-09-2005-sudan-people-s-liberation.prompt: What did the Comprehensive Peace Agreement establish for southern Sudan?

choices.text: An indefinite extension of the existing ceasefire only
A single unified national army under Khartoum's command
Immediate full independence for the south
A period of autonomy leading to a future referendum on independence

evt-01-09-2005-sudan-people-s-liberation.butterflyEffect: The CPA granted southern Sudan a period of autonomy followed by a referendum on independence. In 2011 southerners voted overwhelmingly to secede, creating South Sudan—but unresolved disputes over oil, borders and power soon dragged the new nation into its own civil war by 2013.

evt-01-09-2007-apple-inc.scenario: It is January 2007 and you are Steve Jobs pacing backstage at Macworld in San Francisco, about to walk onstage and reveal a device you have called a combination of an iPod, a phone, and an internet communicator.
evt-01-09-2007-apple-inc.prompt: What single device does Jobs unveil to the crowd?

choices.text: The iPhone, a touchscreen smartphone
A keypad phone with an iPod built in
A successor to the Newton handheld
A tablet computer with a stylus

evt-01-09-2007-apple-inc.butterflyEffect: Jobs revealed the original iPhone, with a multitouch glass screen and no physical keypad, and Apple Computer, Inc. formally shortened its name to Apple Inc. that same year. The device reshaped the phone industry, ended the dominance of keypad smartphones like BlackBerry, and created the app-store economy that followed.

evt-01-09-2015-hypercacher-kosher-superm.scenario: It is early afternoon on 9 January 2015. You command the French police unit surrounding the Hypercacher supermarket in Porte de Vincennes, where a gunman is holding hostages and demanding that the Charlie Hebdo attackers, cornered elsewhere, not be harmed.
evt-01-09-2015-hypercacher-kosher-superm.prompt: When word comes that police are about to storm the gunmen's other hideout, what should your unit do at the supermarket?

choices.text: Cut power and water and wait him out for days
Storm the supermarket immediately to prevent reprisal killings
Wait for lengthy negotiations to run their course first
Withdraw officers and let the gunman leave with hostages

evt-01-09-2015-hypercacher-kosher-superm.butterflyEffect: French police stormed the Hypercacher almost simultaneously with the raid on the Kouachi brothers' hideout, fearing the gunman would kill remaining hostages once he learned of it. Four hostages had already been murdered before the assault. The coordinated sieges hardened French security policy and led to a lasting increase in armed protection for synagogues and Jewish institutions across Europe.

evt-01-09-2015-charlie-hebdo-shooting.scenario: It is the afternoon of 9 January 2015. You command the GIGN team surrounding a printing warehouse in Dammartin-en-Goële, where the Kouachi brothers are holding a hostage, while a second siege unfolds simultaneously at a Paris supermarket.
evt-01-09-2015-charlie-hebdo-shooting.prompt: What must the assault team do the moment the brothers emerge firing from the building?

choices.text: Call in an airstrike on the building
Withdraw the perimeter and wait for them to surrender
Return fire immediately to neutralize the threat
Offer safe passage in exchange for releasing the hostage

evt-01-09-2015-charlie-hebdo-shooting.butterflyEffect: As the brothers burst out shooting, GIGN officers engaged and killed both, ending the manhunt as police simultaneously stormed the Hypercacher supermarket siege. The coordinated attacks shocked France into the mass "Je suis Charlie" solidarity marches and led to sweeping expansions of French counterterrorism and surveillance law.

evt-01-10-236-pope-fabian.scenario: You are a Roman deacon in 236, gathered with the clergy to choose a new bishop of Rome, when a dove suddenly descends and lands on the head of Fabian, an obscure layman visiting from the countryside.
evt-01-10-236-pope-fabian.prompt: How do the assembled clergy respond to this unexpected sign?

choices.text: They arrest Fabian, suspicious of the strange occurrence
They acclaim Fabian pope at once, taking it as a divine sign
They ask Fabian to serve merely as a bishop's assistant
They dismiss it as coincidence and proceed with the usual vote

evt-01-10-236-pope-fabian.butterflyEffect: Taking the dove as a mark of the Holy Spirit, the clergy acclaimed Fabian pope on the spot despite his obscurity. He went on to organize Rome's clergy into administrative districts and aid persecuted Christians, before being martyred under Emperor Decius in 250, later venerated as a saint.

evt-01-10-1430-philip-the-good.scenario: You stand in the great hall at Bruges on 10 January 1430, amid the wedding feast of Philip the Good and Isabella of Portugal, as the duke announces the founding of a new chivalric order.
evt-01-10-1430-philip-the-good.prompt: What does Philip declare as the guiding purpose of this new Order of the Golden Fleece?

choices.text: To create a merchants' guild protecting the wool trade
To honor God and the Virgin, binding Burgundy's noblemen in loyalty to him
To organize an immediate crusade against the Ottomans
To fund the construction of new Burgundian cathedrals

evt-01-10-1430-philip-the-good.butterflyEffect: Philip bound Burgundy's greatest noblemen to his person through the order, reinforcing loyalty and prestige rather than any single military campaign. The order outlived Burgundy itself, passing to the Habsburgs and later the Spanish and Austrian crowns, and it is still awarded by European royal houses today.

evt-01-10-1475-moldavian-ottoman-wars.scenario: It is January 1475, and you serve under Stephen the Great as a vastly larger Ottoman army under Hadım Suleiman Pasha advances into Moldavia through the frozen marshland near Vaslui.
evt-01-10-1475-moldavian-ottoman-wars.prompt: What does Stephen order to counter the Ottomans' numerical advantage?

choices.text: Meet the Ottomans head-on in open cavalry battle
Retreat immediately and abandon the field to save his men
Offer tribute to the Sultan to avoid the confrontation
Lure the Ottoman army into the boggy terrain and ambush it

evt-01-10-1475-moldavian-ottoman-wars.butterflyEffect: Stephen drew the Ottomans into the marshy, fog-covered terrain near Vaslui and crushed them in a stunning victory. Pope Sixtus IV hailed him as the 'Athlete of Christ,' and the win briefly checked Ottoman expansion, though Sultan Mehmed II returned in force the following year at Valea Albă.

evt-01-10-1812-new-orleans-steamboat.scenario: You are aboard the steamboat New Orleans in December 1811, churning down the Mississippi under Captain Nicholas Roosevelt's command, when violent tremors from the New Madrid earthquakes begin reshaping the riverbed beneath you overnight.
evt-01-10-1812-new-orleans-steamboat.prompt: What must the captain do to keep the pioneering voyage alive?

choices.text: Turn back upriver to Pittsburgh and abandon the voyage
Have the boat portaged overland around the affected stretch
Wait months for spring floods before continuing downriver
Navigate cautiously past new sandbars and altered currents caused by the earthquakes

evt-01-10-1812-new-orleans-steamboat.butterflyEffect: Roosevelt pressed on cautiously through shifting sandbars, new islands, and even a stretch of river running briefly backward, and the New Orleans reached its namesake city safely in January 1812. The voyage proved steam power could conquer river currents, launching the steamboat era that reshaped American commerce for decades before railroads took over.

evt-01-10-1863-metropolitan-railway.scenario: It is dawn on 10 January 1863, and you join the crowds at Paddington waiting to ride the world's first underground passenger railway to Farringdon Street.
evt-01-10-1863-metropolitan-railway.prompt: What must you brace yourself for during the journey through the tunnels?

choices.text: Automatic ticket barriers at each station
Dense smoke and steam filling the enclosed tunnels
Bright electric lighting in every carriage
Air conditioning to cool the carriages

evt-01-10-1863-metropolitan-railway.butterflyEffect: Despite thick smoke and steam trapped underground, the Metropolitan Railway's opening day drew huge curious crowds and proved underground rail travel could work. Its success sparked the growth of London's Underground network and inspired subway systems built in cities worldwide.

evt-01-10-1901-blowout-well-drilling.scenario: You stand near the Lucas well outside Beaumont, Texas, on 10 January 1901, as mud, then gas, then a roaring column of oil suddenly erupts from the drilling rig.
evt-01-10-1901-blowout-well-drilling.prompt: What actually follows over the next several days at this well?

choices.text: The well settles into a steady, modest daily output immediately
The U.S. Army seizes the field to control the oil supply
The well collapses within hours and produces nothing
Crews struggle for days before finally capping the wild gusher

evt-01-10-1901-blowout-well-drilling.butterflyEffect: The gusher, later called the Lucas Geyser, sprayed oil roughly 150 feet into the air for nine days before crews managed to cap it with a hastily built valve. Spindletop's output dwarfed every well then known, triggering the Texas oil boom, birthing companies like Texaco and Gulf Oil, and helping shift the world's economy from coal toward oil.

evt-01-10-1917-imperial-trans-antarctic-.scenario: It is 10 January 1917. You are one of seven surviving members of Shackleton's Ross Sea Party, marooned at Cape Evans for nearly two years, when the rescue ship Aurora finally appears offshore.
evt-01-10-1917-imperial-trans-antarctic-.prompt: What should you and the other survivors do as the ship arrives?

choices.text: Refuse to leave until the ice thaws in spring
Signal at once and prepare to evacuate with all records
Hide the remaining supplies for a future expedition
Row out toward the ship in a makeshift boat immediately

evt-01-10-1917-imperial-trans-antarctic-.butterflyEffect: The Aurora, with Shackleton himself aboard, rescued the seven survivors that day; three of their companions had already died from scurvy and misadventure during the ordeal. Their story of endurance became overshadowed by Shackleton's own Endurance saga, but the depots they laid had been intended to support a trans-continental crossing that never happened.

evt-01-10-1923-klaipeda-region.scenario: It is January 1923 and you slip across the border into the Klaipėda Region to join Lithuanian-backed insurgents rising against the French-led administration governing the territory for the League of Nations.
evt-01-10-1923-klaipeda-region.prompt: What outcome are the revolt's organizers aiming to secure?

choices.text: Establish an independent free city-state
Force the region's union with Lithuania
Rejoin the territory to Weimar Germany
Petition for the region to become part of Poland

evt-01-10-1923-klaipeda-region.butterflyEffect: The uprising succeeded within days, and the Entente powers allowed Lithuania to annex the Klaipėda Region, formalized the following year in the Klaipėda Convention. The territory later became a flashpoint when Nazi Germany pressured Lithuania to cede it in 1939.

evt-01-10-1927-science-fiction.scenario: You attend the lavish Berlin premiere of Fritz Lang's Metropolis in January 1927, dazzled by its towering futuristic skyline and the army of extras staging a workers' uprising below.
evt-01-10-1927-science-fiction.prompt: What actually happens to Metropolis in the years right after this premiere?

choices.text: It wins the first Academy Award for Best Picture
It is a costly commercial flop, cut down and altered before rerelease
German authorities ban it outright for radical content
It becomes an instant box-office hit that launches a franchise

evt-01-10-1927-science-fiction.butterflyEffect: Metropolis was so costly that it lost UFA studio a fortune, and distributors cut and re-edited it repeatedly for different markets, scattering footage worldwide. Decades later restorers pieced together lost reels, and the film was recognized as a foundational work of science-fiction cinema, its visual style echoing forward into Blade Runner and countless later dystopian films.

evt-01-10-1941-greco-italian-war.scenario: It is January 1941 and you lead a Greek infantry platoon climbing icy slopes toward the Italian-held Klisura Pass, a key gateway on the road to Tepelenë in Albania.
evt-01-10-1941-greco-italian-war.prompt: How should your unit break the entrenched Italian defenses in the pass?

choices.text: Wait through winter for spring reinforcements
Charge straight up the main road under fire
Send troops over the surrounding heights to flank the defenders
Withdraw to a defensive line inside Greece

evt-01-10-1941-greco-italian-war.butterflyEffect: Greek forces flanked the Italian positions over the mountains rather than charging the road directly, and captured Klisura Pass on 10 January 1941. The victory embarrassed Mussolini and pushed toward Tepelenë, prompting Hitler to commit German troops to the Balkans that spring.

evt-01-10-1946-first-session-of-the-unit.scenario: You are a delegate filing into Methodist Central Hall in London on January 10, 1946, representing one of fifty-one founding member states as the fledgling United Nations meets for the very first time.
evt-01-10-1946-first-session-of-the-unit.prompt: What is the first major decision the assembled delegates must make?

choices.text: Admit the defeated Axis powers as founding members
Elect a President to preside over the General Assembly
Dissolve the wartime alliance structure entirely
Vote immediately on the permanent UN headquarters city

evt-01-10-1946-first-session-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: Delegates elected Belgian statesman Paul-Henri Spaak as the Assembly's first President. Weeks later the same session chose Norway's Trygve Lie as the UN's first Secretary-General, setting precedents for UN leadership that continue to shape the organization today.

evt-01-10-1985-clive-sinclair.scenario: It is January 10, 1985, and Clive Sinclair has just unveiled the C5, a battery-powered tricycle he promises will revolutionize urban commuting. You're weighing whether to place an early order.
evt-01-10-1985-clive-sinclair.prompt: What happens to the Sinclair C5 in the months following its launch?

choices.text: It becomes a runaway commercial success across Britain
The government bans it outright as a road hazard
It is exported successfully to the United States market
Production is halted within months amid poor sales and safety criticism

evt-01-10-1985-clive-sinclair.butterflyEffect: Reviewers and safety experts quickly attacked the C5 for its low seating position, lack of weather protection, and vulnerability in traffic, and sales collapsed. Production was halted before the year was out, the losses badly damaging Sinclair's business empire and computing ventures.

evt-01-10-1985-sandinista-national-liber.scenario: It is January 10, 1985, and you stand among the crowd in Managua as Daniel Ortega takes the presidential oath, the first elected Sandinista leader since the 1979 revolution. Washington has already armed and funded rebel forces against his government.
evt-01-10-1985-sandinista-national-liber.prompt: How does the Reagan administration respond to Ortega's inauguration?

choices.text: It opens immediate talks to normalize diplomatic relations
It formally recognizes the government and lifts all sanctions
It intensifies covert funding to the Contra rebels despite congressional restrictions
It sends U.S. Marines to occupy Managua directly

evt-01-10-1985-sandinista-national-liber.butterflyEffect: Reagan deepened covert funding to the Contra rebels despite congressional limits and imposed a full U.S. trade embargo on Nicaragua that May. The secret arms-funding scheme later exploded into the Iran-Contra scandal, badly damaging Reagan's second term.

evt-01-10-1990-warnermedia.scenario: It is early January 1990, and you sit on the board of Time Inc., which faces a hostile takeover bid from Paramount Communications. Warner Communications has offered a friendly merger instead, promising to create the world's largest media company.
evt-01-10-1990-warnermedia.prompt: Do you approve the friendly merger with Warner to fend off Paramount's hostile bid?

choices.text: Approve the merger with Warner Communications
Sue Paramount to block its takeover bid in court
Reject both offers and remain fully independent
Accept Paramount's higher cash offer instead

evt-01-10-1990-warnermedia.butterflyEffect: The board approved the merger, creating Time Warner and blocking Paramount's takeover. The company later absorbed Turner Broadcasting in 1996, then merged with AOL in 2001—a deal widely seen as one of the worst mergers in corporate history, destroying billions in shareholder value.

evt-01-10-2003-north-korea.scenario: It is 10 January 2003. You advise the U.S. State Department after Pyongyang announces it is withdrawing from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and restarting its Yongbyon reactor.
evt-01-10-2003-north-korea.prompt: What approach should Washington push for in response to North Korea's withdrawal?

choices.text: Launch immediate unilateral airstrikes on Yongbyon
Press for multilateral negotiations with regional powers
Ignore the announcement and maintain the status quo
Impose instant UN Security Council sanctions with no talks

evt-01-10-2003-north-korea.butterflyEffect: North Korea's withdrawal escalated the standoff over its nuclear program and led to the Six-Party Talks beginning later in 2003, involving the US, China, Russia, Japan and both Koreas. Negotiations repeatedly broke down, and North Korea tested its first nuclear weapon in 2006.

evt-01-10-2007-2007-guinean-general-stri.scenario: You are a union organizer in Conakry on 10 January 2007, as workers across Guinea walk off the job demanding President Lansana Conté answer for corruption and economic collapse.
evt-01-10-2007-2007-guinean-general-stri.prompt: What concession does the strike eventually force from Conté's government?

choices.text: Guinea's withdrawal from the ECOWAS regional bloc
Immediate resignation of Conté and snap elections
Nationalization of Guinea's entire mining industry
Appointment of a prime minister with genuine governing power

evt-01-10-2007-2007-guinean-general-stri.butterflyEffect: After weeks of unrest and a violent crackdown that killed dozens, Conté agreed in February 1907 to appoint Lansana Kouyaté as prime minister with real executive powers, a rare check on his authority. The instability set in motion continued political crisis that culminated in a military coup shortly after Conté's death in 2008.

evt-01-11-1055-theodora-porphyrogenita.scenario: You are a court official in Constantinople in 1055, watching the aging Theodora Porphyrogenita take the Byzantine throne alone after Emperor Constantine IX's death. Senators press her to remarry quickly to secure a male heir and steady the succession.
evt-01-11-1055-theodora-porphyrogenita.prompt: How does Theodora respond to pressure to remarry?

choices.text: She marries a prominent general to secure the throne
She shares power with a co-emperor chosen by the Senate
She refuses marriage and rules as sole empress
She abdicates in favor of a distant nephew

evt-01-11-1055-theodora-porphyrogenita.butterflyEffect: Theodora refused to remarry and ruled alone as the last of the Macedonian dynasty. On her deathbed in 1056 she named the elderly official Michael VI as her successor, a choice that satisfied no faction and triggered the succession crises that destabilized the empire in the following years.

evt-01-11-1787-william-herschel.scenario: You are William Herschel peering through your reflecting telescope at Slough on the night of 11 January 1787, six years after you discovered Uranus itself. Two faint points of light hover near the planet, moving in step with it night after night.
evt-01-11-1787-william-herschel.prompt: What do you conclude these two faint objects are?

choices.text: Distant background stars that happen to align with the planet
An optical flaw in his telescope's mirror
Moons orbiting Uranus
Fragments of a comet passing near Uranus

evt-01-11-1787-william-herschel.butterflyEffect: Herschel correctly identified them as satellites of Uranus, the third and fourth moons ever discovered in the solar system after those of Jupiter and Saturn. They went unnamed for decades until his son John Herschel christened them Titania and Oberon in 1852, and both remain the largest moons of Uranus known today.

evt-01-11-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It is January 1863 on the Arkansas River. You serve under Union General John McClernand and Admiral David Porter, facing Fort Hindman at Arkansas Post, a Confederate stronghold raiding Union supply boats bound for Vicksburg.
evt-01-11-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: What do the Union commanders decide to do about the fort?

choices.text: Negotiate a truce allowing the garrison to withdraw
Blockade the river and starve out the garrison
Bypass the fort and press on toward Vicksburg
Launch a combined army-navy assault on Fort Hindman

evt-01-11-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: McClernand and Porter combined army assault with naval bombardment and forced the fort's surrender, capturing nearly 5,000 Confederate troops. The victory secured the Arkansas River for Union shipping and removed a threat to the supply lines feeding the ongoing Vicksburg campaign.

evt-01-11-1914-karluk-ship.scenario: It is January 1914. Your ship Karluk has been crushed and is sinking in the Arctic pack ice, and Captain Robert Bartlett must decide how the twenty-five people aboard will try to survive.
evt-01-11-1914-karluk-ship.prompt: What does Bartlett order the survivors to do after the ship goes down?

choices.text: Split into small groups and abandon the supplies
Turn back toward Herschel Island immediately
March across the ice toward Wrangel Island
Wait beside the wreckage for a passing rescue ship

evt-01-11-1914-karluk-ship.butterflyEffect: Bartlett led the survivors on a brutal march across the ice to Wrangel Island, where several died before he set off alone across the frozen sea to Siberia to summon help. Months later a rescue ship reached the remaining survivors, but eleven of the original twenty-five had perished, a heavy toll that reshaped how the Canadian Arctic Expedition was remembered.

evt-01-11-1923-occupation-of-the-ruhr.scenario: It is January 1923, and French and Belgian troops have just marched into Germany's industrial Ruhr Valley after Berlin fell behind on war reparations payments. You are a German factory manager watching foreign soldiers take control of the coalfields and railways your workers depend on.
evt-01-11-1923-occupation-of-the-ruhr.prompt: How did the German government respond to the occupation?

choices.text: It immediately declared war on France and Belgium
It called for passive resistance and a general strike by German workers
It ordered full cooperation with the occupying forces to speed withdrawal
It agreed to pay reparations in gold within a week to end the occupation

evt-01-11-1923-occupation-of-the-ruhr.butterflyEffect: Germany called for passive resistance, and workers went on strike rather than cooperate with the occupiers, causing the German economy to collapse into hyperinflation. The crisis discredited the Weimar government, fueled nationalist resentment, and was later exploited by Hitler and other extremists as proof that Germany had been humiliated by the Treaty of Versailles.

evt-01-11-1946-people-s-socialist-republ.scenario: You are a delegate in Tirana on 11 January 1946, about to cast your vote in the Communist-dominated constituent assembly that will decide Albania's future form of government under Enver Hoxha's Democratic Front.
evt-01-11-1946-people-s-socialist-republ.prompt: What does the assembly vote to establish?

choices.text: A People's Republic under one-party Communist rule
Federation with Yugoslavia
A multi-party parliamentary republic
A constitutional monarchy under King Zog

evt-01-11-1946-people-s-socialist-republ.butterflyEffect: The assembly proclaimed the People's Republic of Albania, entrenching the Party of Labour's monopoly on power. Enver Hoxha's Stalinist regime would rule for over four decades, isolating Albania from both the West and eventually the Soviet bloc, until the system collapsed in 1991.

evt-01-11-1961-university-of-georgia.scenario: It is January 11, 1961, on the University of Georgia campus. A mob of white students hurls bricks and bottles at the dormitory sheltering Hamilton Holmes and Charlayne Hunter, the university's first Black students, and administrators must respond immediately.
evt-01-11-1961-university-of-georgia.prompt: What do university officials do to end the crisis that night?

choices.text: Call in the National Guard to guard the students and let them remain
Suspend Hunter and Holmes "for their own safety"
Shut down the university indefinitely
Expel the students permanently

evt-01-11-1961-university-of-georgia.butterflyEffect: Officials suspended Hunter and Holmes, citing concern for their safety, effectively caving to the mob. A federal judge ordered them reinstated within days, and both returned to campus under protection, completing their degrees and becoming pioneers of desegregation across Southern universities.

evt-01-11-1964-smoking-and-health.scenario: You are a public health official in January 1964, and the Surgeon General's advisory committee has just released its report linking cigarette smoking to serious disease. Millions of Americans light up daily, and the tobacco industry is powerful and well-funded.
evt-01-11-1964-smoking-and-health.prompt: What did this landmark report call for as its central conclusion?

choices.text: A recommendation that cigarette taxes be eliminated to help smokers quit gradually
A declaration that smoking is a serious health hazard requiring government action
A finding that smoking posed no proven risk but should be studied further
An immediate nationwide ban on the sale of all tobacco products

evt-01-11-1964-smoking-and-health.butterflyEffect: The report concluded that smoking was a definite health hazard, particularly linked to lung cancer, setting off decades of regulation. It led to mandatory warning labels on cigarette packs, a ban on broadcast advertising, and a steady decline in American smoking rates over the following decades.

evt-01-11-1994-republic-of-ireland.scenario: It is January 1994, and as an Irish government minister you must decide whether to lift the 15-year broadcasting ban that has kept Sinn Féin and IRA spokespeople off Irish radio and television.
evt-01-11-1994-republic-of-ireland.prompt: What does the government decide about the broadcasting restrictions?

choices.text: Keep the ban but allow only written statements
Lift the ban on broadcasting Sinn Féin and IRA statements
Extend the ban for another decade
Ban all political party broadcasts entirely

evt-01-11-1994-republic-of-ireland.butterflyEffect: The government lifted the ban, allowing Sinn Féin's voice to be heard directly on Irish airwaves for the first time in over a decade. The move was part of a wider peace push that helped pave the way for the IRA's ceasefire later that August and, eventually, the 1998 Good Friday Agreement.

evt-01-11-1996-space-shuttle-program.scenario: It is January 1996. You are a mission specialist aboard Space Shuttle Endeavour on STS-72, chasing down a Japanese satellite that has been drifting in orbit for ten months.
evt-01-11-1996-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What is the primary objective of the STS-72 mission?

choices.text: Dock with the Mir space station
Repair the Hubble Space Telescope
Retrieve Japan's Space Flyer Unit satellite
Deploy the Chandra X-ray Observatory
