evt-01-11-1996-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: Endeavour's crew used the shuttle's robotic arm to capture and retrieve Japan's Space Flyer Unit, also deploying and recovering a second small satellite during the same flight. The mission proved the shuttle could reliably chase, grapple, and return free-flying spacecraft, a skill soon reused for Hubble servicing missions.

evt-01-11-2013-bulo-marer-hostage-rescue.scenario: You are a French commando advancing on a compound in Bulo Marer before dawn on 11 January 2013, tasked with pulling DGSE agent Denis Allex out alive. Gunfire erupts from the huts ahead and your team's approach has already been compromised.
evt-01-11-2013-bulo-marer-hostage-rescue.prompt: What does the French assault team do next?

choices.text: Call in an airstrike on the compound
Withdraw immediately and wait for reinforcements
Press forward and force the assault despite being spotted
Attempt to negotiate a ceasefire with the militants

evt-01-11-2013-bulo-marer-hostage-rescue.butterflyEffect: The commandos pressed the assault despite the compromised approach, but the raid failed to reach Allex. Al-Shabaab executed him in retaliation, and the firefight killed two French soldiers along with at least seventeen militants and eight civilians, hardening France's caution over future hostage raids in Somalia.

evt-01-12-475-basiliscus.scenario: It is 468, and you command the East Roman fleet anchored off Cape Bon, sent to crush the Vandal kingdom. Vandal King Gaiseric, badly outnumbered, sends envoys asking for a few days' truce to arrange terms of surrender.
evt-01-12-475-basiliscus.prompt: Do you grant Gaiseric's request for a truce, or press the attack now?

choices.text: Grant the truce and wait for surrender terms
Withdraw the fleet to Sicily to resupply
Demand hostages before agreeing to any truce
Attack immediately while the Vandals are outnumbered

evt-01-12-475-basiliscus.butterflyEffect: Basiliscus granted the truce, and Gaiseric used the delay to load ships with combustibles, sending fireships into the anchored Roman fleet under favorable winds. The disaster cost the Eastern Empire 130,000 pounds of gold and left it near bankruptcy for thirty years, a failure that dogged Basiliscus's reputation even after he seized the throne in 475.

evt-01-12-1777-mission-santa-clara-de-as.scenario: You are a Franciscan friar in January 1777, standing on a stretch of land along a California river where you are about to found the eighth mission in the chain stretching up the coast. It will be the first mission named for a woman.
evt-01-12-1777-mission-santa-clara-de-as.prompt: In whose honor was this new mission named?

choices.text: Saint Barbara, patron saint of soldiers and miners
Saint Clare of Assisi, founder of the Poor Clares
Saint Teresa of Ávila, the Spanish mystic and reformer
The Virgin of Guadalupe, patroness of the Americas

evt-01-12-1777-mission-santa-clara-de-as.butterflyEffect: The mission was dedicated to Saint Clare of Assisi, founder of the Poor Clares, making it the first California mission honoring a woman. The settlement that grew around it eventually became the city of Santa Clara, and the mission site itself later formed the founding core of Santa Clara University.

evt-01-12-1808-john-rennie-the-elder.scenario: It is 1808, and the parish of Reculver in Kent is weighing a costly scheme by engineer John Rennie to shore up the crumbling cliffs threatening St Mary's Church against the encroaching sea.
evt-01-12-1808-john-rennie-the-elder.prompt: Facing Rennie's expensive proposal, what does the parish decide?

choices.text: Fund Rennie's sea defense scheme in full
Reject the plan and accept the loss of the church
Petition the government to pay for coastal engineering
Dismantle and rebuild the church further inland

evt-01-12-1808-john-rennie-the-elder.butterflyEffect: The parish rejected Rennie's scheme, and most of the church was demolished the following year. Trinity House paid to preserve the twin Norman towers as a landmark for sailors, and Reculver Towers still stand today as one of Kent's best-known coastal landmarks.

evt-01-12-1916-oswald-boelcke.scenario: It is January 1916, and you are a fellow pilot in the German air service, watching Oswald Boelcke pin on a decoration no German aviator has ever worn before.
evt-01-12-1916-oswald-boelcke.prompt: What honor did Boelcke and fellow ace Max Immelmann receive that day?

choices.text: The Iron Cross First Class, already common among frontline officers
A personal knighthood conferred by Kaiser Wilhelm II
Command of the entire German air service
The Pour le Mérite, becoming the first aviators awarded Prussia's highest military honor

evt-01-12-1916-oswald-boelcke.butterflyEffect: The Pour le Mérite, nicknamed "the Blue Max" by airmen, became the ultimate symbol of fighter-pilot prestige in Germany. Boelcke went on to codify air combat tactics in his "Dicta Boelcke" and personally mentored a young Manfred von Richthofen, the future Red Baron.

evt-01-12-1918-minnie-pit-disaster.scenario: It is January 1918, and you are among the inspectors called to Halmer End, Staffordshire, to determine what ignited the firedamp explosion that tore through the Minnie Pit, the worst disaster in the North Staffordshire Coalfield's history.
evt-01-12-1918-minnie-pit-disaster.prompt: What did the official investigation ultimately conclude about the cause of the explosion?

choices.text: An open flame carried by a foreman was blamed
A faulty electrical lamp was proven responsible
Deliberate sabotage by a disgruntled miner was confirmed
The exact ignition source was never established

evt-01-12-1918-minnie-pit-disaster.butterflyEffect: Despite a thorough inquiry, investigators could never pinpoint exactly what ignited the flammable gas underground. The unresolved cause underscored how difficult firedamp remained to control even with existing safety measures, and the disaster stands as a grim benchmark cited in later pushes for stricter mine ventilation and gas-detection standards in Britain.

evt-01-12-1964-jamshid-bin-abdullah.scenario: It is the night of January 11 into 12, 1964, in Zanzibar Town. John Okello's revolutionaries have seized armories and the radio station, and the Sultan's own police are melting away. You advise Sultan Jamshid bin Abdullah on his next move.
evt-01-12-1964-jamshid-bin-abdullah.prompt: With the palace surrounded, what should the Sultan do?

choices.text: Negotiate a power-sharing government with Okello
Call on British troops to restore his authority
Order his palace guard to counterattack at dawn
Flee into exile aboard a waiting yacht

evt-01-12-1964-jamshid-bin-abdullah.butterflyEffect: Jamshid fled by yacht into exile rather than fight, and a revolutionary government took power. Within months Zanzibar merged with Tanganyika to form Tanzania, ending centuries of Omani Arab sultanate rule on the island.

evt-01-12-1986-space-shuttle-program.scenario: It is January 12, 1986, and you are Congressman Bill Nelson, strapped into Space Shuttle Columbia as it lifts off from Kennedy Space Center on mission STS-61-C, part of a program now regularly flying non-astronaut passengers.
evt-01-12-1986-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What happened just sixteen days later that would change the shuttle program for years to come?

choices.text: Space Shuttle Challenger disintegrated shortly after launch
Congress voted to end the shuttle program entirely
Columbia suffered a similar fatal accident
NASA announced a new fleet of shuttles

evt-01-12-1986-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: On January 28, 1986, Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch, killing all seven crew members, including teacher Christa McAuliffe. The disaster grounded the shuttle fleet for 32 months, ended the practice of flying civilians and politicians aboard shuttles, and forced sweeping safety redesigns before flights resumed.

evt-01-12-1991-gulf-war.scenario: It is January 12, 1991, on the floor of the U.S. Capitol. Iraq has ignored the UN deadline to withdraw from Kuwait, and you are a member of Congress about to cast a defining vote.
evt-01-12-1991-gulf-war.prompt: How do you vote on authorizing military force against Iraq?

choices.text: Vote no and press for continued sanctions instead
Propose relying solely on a future UN resolution
Delay the vote pending further diplomatic talks
Vote yes to authorize the use of military force

evt-01-12-1991-gulf-war.butterflyEffect: Congress narrowly passed the authorization, and five days later Operation Desert Storm began. The swift coalition air and ground campaign expelled Iraqi forces from Kuwait by February 28, cementing U.S. military dominance in the post-Cold War order.

evt-01-12-1997-space-shuttle-atlantis.scenario: It is January 12, 1997, and Space Shuttle Atlantis lifts off on mission STS-81, bound for a docking with the Russian space station Mir as part of the ongoing Shuttle-Mir partnership.
evt-01-12-1997-space-shuttle-atlantis.prompt: What was the primary purpose of this docking with Mir?

choices.text: Test a new reusable booster design
Deploy a new communications satellite
Deliver supplies and exchange a crew member with Mir
Conduct repairs on the Hubble Space Telescope

evt-01-12-1997-space-shuttle-atlantis.butterflyEffect: Atlantis delivered supplies and science hardware to Mir and swapped out a long-duration crew member, bringing astronaut Jerry Linenger up and returning John Blaha to Earth. These repeated Shuttle-Mir exchanges built the operational trust and procedures that let NASA and Russia become core partners in assembling the International Space Station just a few years later.

evt-01-12-1998-human-cloning.scenario: It is January 12, 1998, and you are a diplomat at the Council of Europe, drafting an additional protocol to the Convention on Human Rights and Biomedicine in the wake of the Dolly the sheep cloning breakthrough.
evt-01-12-1998-human-cloning.prompt: What did the nineteen participating European nations agree to do?

choices.text: Permit therapeutic cloning while banning reproductive cloning
Leave regulation entirely to individual member states
Forbid the cloning of human beings outright
Fund a joint European cloning research program

evt-01-12-1998-human-cloning.butterflyEffect: They signed a protocol forbidding any intervention seeking to create a human being genetically identical to another, whether living or dead. It became one of the first binding international legal instruments banning human cloning outright, setting a template later echoed in national laws and United Nations declarations on the subject.

evt-01-12-2005-deep-impact-spacecraft.scenario: It is July 4, 2005, and mission control watches as the Deep Impact probe's copper impactor closes in on comet Tempel 1 at over 23,000 miles per hour, designed to blast open the nucleus so cameras can see what's inside.
evt-01-12-2005-deep-impact-spacecraft.prompt: What happened in the moments right after the impactor struck the comet?

choices.text: The impactor bounced off without leaving a mark
An unexpectedly huge, bright dust cloud obscured the crater
The crater was immediately visible in perfect detail
The comet's nucleus split cleanly in two

evt-01-12-2005-deep-impact-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: The collision kicked up a dust cloud far larger and brighter than scientists expected, briefly obscuring the crater it had just carved. The excess fine, fluffy debris showed Tempel 1 was more porous and dusty than predicted, reshaping models of comets as loosely packed rubble piles and informing the design of later missions like Rosetta.

evt-01-12-2006-incidents-during-the-hajj.scenario: You are a pilgrim caught in the dense crowd at Mina during the Stoning of the Devil ritual on the final day of the 2006 Hajj, moving slowly toward the Jamarat pillars alongside millions of others.
evt-01-12-2006-incidents-during-the-hajj.prompt: What change did Saudi authorities make afterward to prevent future crowd disasters at this site?

choices.text: They restricted the Hajj to only Saudi residents
They allowed pilgrims to perform the ritual by proxy from home
They banned the stoning ritual from the Hajj entirely
They redesigned the Jamarat area into a multi-level bridge with one-way pedestrian routes

evt-01-12-2006-incidents-during-the-hajj.butterflyEffect: Saudi authorities rebuilt the Jamarat area as a multi-level bridge with separated one-way entry and exit routes and stricter crowd scheduling. The redesign reduced but did not eliminate the risk, as later Hajj seasons, notably 2015, still saw deadly crushes elsewhere along the pilgrimage route.

evt-01-12-2010-2010-haiti-earthquake.scenario: It is January 12, 2010, hours after a magnitude 7.0 earthquake has leveled much of Port-au-Prince. You are helping coordinate the flood of incoming international aid before it collapses into chaos.
evt-01-12-2010-2010-haiti-earthquake.prompt: What should be the most urgent priority to prevent a second catastrophe?

choices.text: Focus solely on reopening the airport for more aid flights
Prioritize distributing building materials for reconstruction
Push for immediate national elections to restore stability
Secure clean water and sanitation before disease spreads through camps

evt-01-12-2010-2010-haiti-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Sanitation infrastructure never recovered in time, and later that year UN peacekeepers introduced cholera through contaminated waste, sparking an epidemic that killed thousands more and led to lawsuits against the United Nations.

evt-01-12-2012-2012-romanian-protests.scenario: It is 12 January 2012, and you stand in a swelling crowd in Bucharest's University Square, furious after President Traian Băsescu publicly humiliated the widely respected health official Raed Arafat on live television.
evt-01-12-2012-2012-romanian-protests.prompt: What did the escalating protests ultimately force from Romania's government?

choices.text: President Băsescu's resignation from office
Declaration of martial law across Bucharest
Withdrawal of the health reform bill and Prime Minister Emil Boc's resignation weeks later
Immediate dissolution of parliament and snap elections

evt-01-12-2012-2012-romanian-protests.butterflyEffect: Facing days of clashes with the Gendarmerie, the government withdrew the controversial health reform bill, and in February 2012 Prime Minister Emil Boc resigned amid the continuing unrest. It was a rare instance of Romanian street protest directly toppling a sitting government.

evt-01-12-2016-january-2016-istanbul-bom.scenario: It is mid-morning on 12 January 2016, and you are one of hundreds of tourists gathered near Istanbul's Blue Mosque, cameras raised toward the minarets, unaware of the man moving through the crowd toward Sultanahmet Square.
evt-01-12-2016-january-2016-istanbul-bom.prompt: What followed the suicide bombing that struck the tourist crowd that morning?

choices.text: Turkey closed the Bosphorus Strait to all shipping traffic
Turkey severed all diplomatic ties with every Western embassy in Ankara
Turkey blamed Kurdish militants and launched raids on the PKK
Turkey identified the bomber as a Syrian ISIL member and tightened border and visa controls

evt-01-12-2016-january-2016-istanbul-bom.butterflyEffect: The bomber was identified as Nabil Fadli, a Syrian member of ISIL, and Turkey responded by tightening border and visa controls and intensifying strikes on ISIL positions in Syria. Coming amid a string of 2016 attacks, the bombing also badly damaged Turkey's tourism industry for years afterward.

evt-01-13-1435-pope-eugene-iv.scenario: It is 1435, and word has reached Rome that Portuguese and Castilian sailors are enslaving native inhabitants of the newly reached Canary Islands. Pope Eugene IV is drafting a response.
evt-01-13-1435-pope-eugene-iv.prompt: What does the bull Sicut dudum command?

choices.text: Free all enslaved Canary Islanders or face excommunication
Permit enslavement of any non-Christian peoples encountered
Take no position, leaving the matter to secular rulers
Grant Portugal exclusive rights to the slave trade

evt-01-13-1435-pope-eugene-iv.butterflyEffect: Sicut dudum ordered that enslaved Canary Islanders be freed within fifteen days on pain of excommunication, one of the earliest papal condemnations of enslaving a colonized people. The stance proved short-lived: later fifteenth-century bulls like Dum Diversas reversed course to sanction the Atlantic slave trade, making Eugene's ruling a contested footnote later cited in abolitionist debates.

evt-01-13-1815-battle-of-fort-peter.scenario: It is 13 January 1815 and you command the small American garrison at Fort Point Peter near St. Marys, Georgia. A much larger British force is landing to seize the river crossing, and no word has yet reached you that a peace treaty was signed at Ghent weeks ago.
evt-01-13-1815-battle-of-fort-peter.prompt: Facing an overwhelming British assault, what should you do with your garrison?

choices.text: Surrender immediately without any resistance
Hold the fort to the last man regardless of the odds
Counterattack the landing party before it can regroup
Order a withdrawal to save the men rather than fight a losing battle

evt-01-13-1815-battle-of-fort-peter.butterflyEffect: American defenders withdrew rather than be overrun, and British troops occupied St. Marys and Cumberland Island, blockading the Intracoastal Waterway for weeks. The fighting continued because the Treaty of Ghent, though signed, had not yet been ratified by the US Senate, a reminder that peace on paper took time to reach the front lines.

evt-01-13-1842-first-anglo-afghan-war.scenario: It is January 1842. You are part of the roughly 16,000-strong British and Indian column retreating from Kabul through snow-choked mountain passes, harried at every turn by Afghan tribesmen.
evt-01-13-1842-first-anglo-afghan-war.prompt: What ultimately happens to the retreating column?

choices.text: Afghan forces negotiate safe passage for the entire column
The column fights through and reaches Jalalabad largely intact
British reinforcements arrive and rout the tribesmen
Almost all are killed or captured; only a few survivors reach Jalalabad

evt-01-13-1842-first-anglo-afghan-war.butterflyEffect: Nearly the entire column was killed or captured; only a handful, most famously assistant surgeon William Brydon, reached the British garrison at Jalalabad alive. The disaster shocked Britain into launching a punitive 'Army of Retribution' later in 1842, and the retreat became a lasting cautionary tale about the perils of occupying Afghanistan.

evt-01-13-1847-treaty-of-cahuenga.scenario: It is 13 January 1847 at Campo de Cahuenga. You command the Californio forces under Andrés Pico, worn down by months of fighting against advancing American troops under John C. Frémont.
evt-01-13-1847-treaty-of-cahuenga.prompt: What do you decide to do?

choices.text: Launch one final assault on Los Angeles
Retreat south to continue guerrilla resistance
Surrender unconditionally without negotiation
Sign a capitulation ending the fighting in California

evt-01-13-1847-treaty-of-cahuenga.butterflyEffect: Pico and Frémont signed an informal truce ending the fighting of the Mexican–American War in Alta California. It paved the way for the formal cession of California to the United States under the 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.

evt-01-13-1884-william-price-physician.scenario: It is January 1884 on a Welsh hillside near Llantrisant. You are a constable who has just interrupted Dr. William Price attempting to burn the body of his infant son, Jesus Christ Price, in the open air.
evt-01-13-1884-william-price-physician.prompt: What did the court decide when Price was tried for the act?

choices.text: He was fined but the child's body was ordered buried instead
He was acquitted, establishing that cremation was not illegal in England
He was convicted of desecrating a corpse and imprisoned
The case was dismissed on a technicality without any ruling on cremation

evt-01-13-1884-william-price-physician.butterflyEffect: Price was acquitted, since the judge ruled that cremation was not illegal under English law provided it caused no public nuisance. His case cleared the legal path for the Cremation Society, and Parliament formalized the practice with the Cremation Act 1902, transforming British funerary custom.

evt-01-13-1915-1915-avezzano-earthquake.scenario: It is the morning of 13 January 1915 and a violent earthquake has just leveled Avezzano and surrounding towns in central Italy. As word reaches Rome of the scale of destruction, the government must decide how to respond.
evt-01-13-1915-1915-avezzano-earthquake.prompt: What should Italian authorities do to address the disaster?

choices.text: Evacuate the entire province before attempting any rescue
Mobilize the army and royal government to lead rescue and relief operations
Leave relief entirely to local town councils and churches
Impose a strict quarantine on the region before sending aid

evt-01-13-1915-1915-avezzano-earthquake.butterflyEffect: King Victor Emmanuel III personally traveled to the disaster zone and the army was mobilized for rescue and relief, though the response was hampered by the region's poor infrastructure. The earthquake struck just months before Italy entered the First World War, straining resources that might otherwise have gone to reconstruction and building safety reforms.

evt-01-13-1916-first-feminist-congress-o.scenario: It is 13 January 1916 at the Peón Contreras Theater in Mérida. You are one of 620 delegates, mostly teachers, gathered to debate reforms to women's legal and educational rights.
evt-01-13-1916-first-feminist-congress-o.prompt: Which proposal sparks the fiercest debate among delegates?

choices.text: Whether women should be granted the right to vote
Whether divorce should be outlawed entirely
Whether women should be banned from teaching
Whether convent education should be made mandatory

evt-01-13-1916-first-feminist-congress-o.butterflyEffect: The most contentious issue was extending voting rights to women, which many delegates saw as too radical even within a feminist gathering. The congress's momentum helped Yucatán's Governor Salvador Alvarado grant women limited local voting rights soon after, decades before Mexican women won national suffrage in 1953.

evt-01-13-1963-sylvanus-olympio.scenario: It is 13 January 1963 in Lomé. You are a Togolese soldier among a group of disgruntled veterans and officers moving against President Sylvanus Olympio, who has resisted expanding the army.
evt-01-13-1963-sylvanus-olympio.prompt: What happened to Olympio and Togo's government in the aftermath?

choices.text: He negotiated a peaceful power-sharing deal with the soldiers
The coup failed and Olympio remained president until 1970
He fled into exile and later returned to reclaim the presidency
He was killed, and the coup opened an era of military-driven politics in Togo

evt-01-13-1963-sylvanus-olympio.butterflyEffect: Olympio was shot dead near the U.S. embassy, becoming one of the first African heads of state killed in a coup after independence. Nicolas Grunitzky was installed as president, but instability continued until Gnassingbé Eyadéma, one of the coup's soldiers, seized power himself in 1967 and ruled for decades.

evt-01-13-1968-johnny-cash.scenario: It is 13 January 1968 and you are producing Johnny Cash's live recording session inside Folsom State Prison, microphones capturing both the band and the roaring inmate audience.
evt-01-13-1968-johnny-cash.prompt: What should you do with the raw prisoner reactions caught on tape?

choices.text: Re-record the vocals later in a studio without an audience
Keep the live prisoner reactions in the final mix for authenticity
Cut the performance of "Folsom Prison Blues" from the album
Strip out all crowd noise for a cleaner studio sound

evt-01-13-1968-johnny-cash.butterflyEffect: The rowdy, authentic crowd noise stayed in the final mix, giving At Folsom Prison its raw, electric feel and reviving Cash's career at a low point. The album's success led to a follow-up live record at San Quentin and cemented Cash's image as a voice for the incarcerated and forgotten.

evt-01-13-1972-bernice-gera.scenario: You are Bernice Gera in June 1972, stepping onto the field as the first woman ever to umpire a professional baseball game after years of fighting a sex-discrimination case to get there.
evt-01-13-1972-bernice-gera.prompt: What happens to her umpiring career after this historic first game?

choices.text: She umpires for another decade without incident
She is banned from baseball entirely by the commissioner
She resigns after just one game due to resentment from other umpires
She is promoted to umpire major league games the following season

evt-01-13-1972-bernice-gera.butterflyEffect: Gera resigned immediately after that single game, citing open hostility and lack of support from her fellow umpires and league officials. Her brief tenure nonetheless opened the door for later generations of women pursuing officiating roles in professional sports.

evt-01-13-1998-alfredo-ormando.scenario: You are a journalist in St. Peter's Square on 13 January 1998, moments after a man has set himself on fire, and witnesses say he shouted about the Church's condemnation of homosexuality before collapsing.
evt-01-13-1998-alfredo-ormando.prompt: How should you report the story to reflect what he was trying to say?

choices.text: As a publicity stunt for his writing career
As an accident involving religious pilgrims
As a random act of violence unrelated to any cause
As a deliberate protest against the Church's teaching on homosexuality

evt-01-13-1998-alfredo-ormando.butterflyEffect: Much of the Italian press at the time framed Ormando's death as the act of a disturbed individual rather than a political protest, and the Church made no public comment on his message. It took over a decade of activism before LGBT groups reclaimed his death as a deliberate act of protest, and a plaque honouring him was finally placed near the square in 2015.

evt-01-13-2000-steve-ballmer.scenario: It is 13 January 2000 and you are a Microsoft shareholder watching the announcement: Bill Gates is stepping aside as CEO, handing the role to his longtime lieutenant Steve Ballmer.
evt-01-13-2000-steve-ballmer.prompt: What followed for Microsoft under Ballmer's fourteen-year tenure?

choices.text: He merged Microsoft with Apple to end their rivalry
Microsoft's stock price tripled within two years under his leadership
He immediately sold off the Windows division to focus on hardware
He led Microsoft into gaming and enterprise growth but missed the smartphone shift, with stock stagnating

evt-01-13-2000-steve-ballmer.butterflyEffect: Ballmer grew Microsoft's revenue and pushed into Xbox and enterprise cloud services, but the company largely missed the smartphone revolution, and its stock stagnated for most of the 2000s. He stepped down in 2014, succeeded by Satya Nadella, who pivoted the company toward cloud computing and revived its valuation.

evt-01-13-2001-january-2001-el-salvador-.scenario: It is the afternoon of 13 January 2001. A powerful earthquake off El Salvador's coast has just triggered a massive landslide that buried part of the Las Colinas neighborhood in Santa Tecla. You are coordinating the emergency response.
evt-01-13-2001-january-2001-el-salvador-.prompt: Where do you direct rescue teams first?

choices.text: The buried Las Colinas neighborhood where houses were swept away
Government buildings for structural inspection
Coastal towns at risk of a tsunami
Rural farmland unaffected by the landslide

evt-01-13-2001-january-2001-el-salvador-.butterflyEffect: The Las Colinas landslide buried an entire hillside neighborhood built on unstable, deforested slopes, becoming one of the disaster's deadliest single events. The tragedy exposed the dangers of unregulated hillside development and pushed El Salvador toward stricter land-use zoning and disaster-preparedness reforms.

evt-01-13-2003-208996-achlys.scenario: It is January 2003 and you are part of Chad Trujillo and Michael Brown's survey team at Palomar Observatory, tracking a faint, slow-moving point of light far beyond Neptune's orbit.
evt-01-13-2003-208996-achlys.prompt: Before announcing the discovery, what should you do with the observation?

choices.text: Announce it immediately as a new dwarf planet
Dismiss the signal as a camera artifact and move on
Classify it as a comet without checking its orbit
Track the object over multiple nights to confirm its orbit before announcing it

evt-01-13-2003-208996-achlys.butterflyEffect: The object, later named 208996 Achlys, was confirmed as one of the largest known plutinos, third only to Pluto and Orcus, with an elongated shape caused by its rapid 6.8-hour rotation. Careful confirmation of objects like this helped astronomers map the Kuiper belt's population and fueled the debate that led to Pluto's later reclassification.

evt-01-13-2012-costa-concordia.scenario: It is the night of 13 January 2012. The cruise ship Costa Concordia has struck rocks off Isola del Giglio and is listing badly as passengers scramble for lifeboats. You are Captain Francesco Schettino, responsible for the evacuation.
evt-01-13-2012-costa-concordia.prompt: What does the captain actually do as the ship capsizes?

choices.text: Radios nearby ships to coordinate a joint rescue effort
Abandons the ship before the evacuation is finished
Steers the ship toward shallow water to prevent sinking
Remains aboard directing rescue until the last passenger is off

evt-01-13-2012-costa-concordia.butterflyEffect: Schettino left the ship before the evacuation was complete, later claiming he had accidentally 'fallen' into a lifeboat, while thousands of passengers remained aboard. The scandal led to his manslaughter conviction and reshaped international scrutiny of cruise captains' legal duty to stay until evacuation is finished.

evt-01-13-2012-cruise-ship.scenario: It's the night of 13 January 2012. You are an officer aboard the Costa Concordia as it grazes a reef near Giglio Island, tearing open the hull below the waterline, and the ship begins to list hard to one side.
evt-01-13-2012-cruise-ship.prompt: What is the safest immediate response to the growing list?

choices.text: Wait for the captain to finish assessing the damage before alerting passengers
Reassure passengers there is no danger and resume the cruise schedule
Sound the abandon-ship alarm and begin evacuation immediately
Continue toward the nearest port at full speed

evt-01-13-2012-cruise-ship.butterflyEffect: In reality Captain Schettino delayed sounding the abandon-ship order for nearly an hour and then left the sinking vessel before all passengers were evacuated. 32 people died, and he was later convicted of manslaughter and abandoning ship, prompting stricter international rules on evacuation timing and captains' conduct.

evt-01-13-2018-2018-hawaii-false-missile.scenario: It is 8:08 a.m. on 13 January 2018 in Honolulu. Your phone buzzes with an official alert: a ballistic missile is inbound and this is not a drill.
evt-01-13-2018-2018-hawaii-false-missile.prompt: What actually happened next across Hawaii?

choices.text: It was a hacking attack on the state's emergency system
It was a false alarm from a mistaken drill command, not corrected for 38 minutes
It was a scheduled civil defense test announced in advance
It was a genuine North Korean missile test gone astray

evt-01-13-2018-2018-hawaii-false-missile.butterflyEffect: The alert was a false alarm caused by an employee error during a shift-change drill, and no correction reached phones for 38 agonizing minutes. The panic exposed serious flaws in emergency broadcast protocols, leading Hawaii to require two-person sign-off for future alerts and prompting a nationwide review of missile-warning systems.

evt-01-13-2020-ministry-of-public-health.scenario: You are a Thai health official screening arrivals at Bangkok's airport on 13 January 2020, when a traveler from Wuhan is flagged with a fever and respiratory symptoms.
evt-01-13-2020-ministry-of-public-health.prompt: What should you do with this traveler?

choices.text: Quarantine the entire airport terminal indefinitely
Send them back to China immediately
Allow them to proceed after a temperature check only
Isolate and test the traveler for the novel virus

evt-01-13-2020-ministry-of-public-health.butterflyEffect: Thai officials isolated and tested the patient, confirming the first case of the new coronavirus outside China. The finding forced health agencies worldwide to begin urgent airport screening and border monitoring, though most governments still underestimated how fast the virus would spread into a global pandemic weeks later.

evt-01-13-2021-president-of-the-united-s.scenario: It is 13 January 2021, one week after the storming of the U.S. Capitol. You are a member of the House of Representatives about to vote on impeaching outgoing President Donald Trump.
evt-01-13-2021-president-of-the-united-s.prompt: What was Trump impeached for, and what happened next?

choices.text: Incitement of insurrection, over the Capitol riot; the Senate later acquitted him
Bribery charges connected to his 2020 campaign finances
Obstruction of justice regarding the Mueller investigation
Abuse of power over the Ukraine phone call, as in his first impeachment

evt-01-13-2021-president-of-the-united-s.butterflyEffect: The House impeached Trump for 'incitement of insurrection,' making him the only U.S. president impeached twice. He left office before trial, and the Senate later voted to acquit after most Republicans argued it lacked jurisdiction over a former president, leaving the episode a defining flashpoint in post-2020 American politics.

evt-01-14-1301-andrew-iii-of-hungary.scenario: It is 1301. King Andrew III has just died without a male heir, ending the Árpád dynasty that has ruled Hungary for centuries. As a powerful Hungarian noble, you must choose which foreign claimant to back for the vacant throne.

choices.text: Wenceslaus of Bohemia
Charles Robert of Anjou, backed by the Pope
Otto III of Bavaria
A native Hungarian baron elected by the nobility

evt-01-14-1301-andrew-iii-of-hungary.butterflyEffect: A prolonged succession struggle followed among Charles Robert of Anjou, Wenceslaus of Bohemia, and Otto of Bavaria. Charles Robert eventually prevailed in 1310, founding the Angevin dynasty in Hungary and introducing sweeping administrative and economic reforms.

evt-01-14-1641-dutch-portuguese-war.scenario: You are a Portuguese officer trapped inside Malacca in January 1641, food nearly gone after months of blockade by Dutch ships and Johor's allied forces outside the walls.
evt-01-14-1641-dutch-portuguese-war.prompt: What do the exhausted defenders finally do?

choices.text: Surrender the fortress to the besieging Dutch-Johor forces
Break out at night and retreat overland to Goa
Hold on until a relief fleet arrives from Macau
Negotiate to keep the city under nominal Portuguese rule

evt-01-14-1641-dutch-portuguese-war.butterflyEffect: On 14 January 1641 the Portuguese garrison surrendered, ending over 130 years of Portuguese rule in Malacca and handing the Dutch East India Company control of the vital Strait. Dutch dominance there would last until 1824, when Malacca passed to the British under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty.

evt-01-14-1724-philip-v-of-spain.scenario: It is January 1724, and King Philip V of Spain, worn down by illness and religious melancholy, confides in you that he can no longer bear the burdens of the crown he has held since 1700.
evt-01-14-1724-philip-v-of-spain.prompt: What does Philip V decide to do?

choices.text: Abdicate the throne in favor of his son Louis
Convene the Cortes to establish a regency council
Retreat to a monastery while formally keeping the crown
Hand power temporarily to his wife, Elisabeth Farnese

evt-01-14-1724-philip-v-of-spain.butterflyEffect: Philip abdicated in favor of his son, who reigned briefly as Louis I. Louis died of smallpox that August, forcing Philip to resume the throne until 1746, giving him the longest reign of any Spanish monarch.

evt-01-14-1814-denmark-norway.scenario: It is January 1814. As a Danish negotiator, you sit across the table from Swedish and British diplomats at Kiel, forced to accept harsh terms after your king's alliance with the defeated Napoleon.
evt-01-14-1814-denmark-norway.prompt: What must Denmark agree to under the treaty?

choices.text: Pay a war indemnity while keeping all its territories
Cede Iceland and the Faroe Islands to Sweden
Cede the Kingdom of Norway to the King of Sweden
Cede Schleswig and Holstein to Sweden

evt-01-14-1814-denmark-norway.butterflyEffect: Norway did not simply accept the transfer of its crown; its national assembly declared independence and adopted a constitution, leading to a brief war with Sweden before Norway entered a looser union under the Swedish king that lasted until 1905.

evt-01-14-1900-giacomo-puccini.scenario: It is the evening of 14 January 1900 at Teatro Costanzi in Rome. Rumors of a plot against the royal family have unsettled the city, and armed police gather outside as the curtain is about to rise on your new opera, Tosca.
evt-01-14-1900-giacomo-puccini.prompt: What precaution is taken before the premiere begins?

choices.text: The theatre is evacuated mid-overture
The premiere is postponed indefinitely
The royal box is left empty and the King stays home
Police search the theater and stand guard through the performance

evt-01-14-1900-giacomo-puccini.butterflyEffect: Despite the tense atmosphere, the premiere proceeded without incident and the opera was a triumph. Tosca went on to become one of the most frequently performed operas in the world, cementing Puccini's reputation as the leading voice of verismo opera.

evt-01-14-1907-1907-kingston-earthquake.scenario: It is the afternoon of 14 January 1907. Kingston lies in ruins after the quake, fires are spreading through the wreckage, and American naval vessels in the harbour have just signaled an offer of aid. You are the Governor of Jamaica.
evt-01-14-1907-1907-kingston-earthquake.prompt: How do you respond to the American offer of assistance?

choices.text: Publicly reject the offer as unwanted foreign interference
Accept the aid gratefully and welcome the American sailors ashore
Quietly accept but ask that no publicity be given to it
Refer the decision to London before responding

evt-01-14-1907-1907-kingston-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Governor Alexander Swettenham publicly and rudely rebuffed the American aid, insulting Rear Admiral Charles Davis in the process. The insult caused a transatlantic diplomatic row over British sensitivity to American influence in the Caribbean, and Swettenham was forced to resign soon after.

evt-01-14-1939-queen-maud-land.scenario: It is January 1939. A German Antarctic expedition has just been surveying the same stretch of East Antarctic coastline your explorers have long charted. You advise the Norwegian government on how to respond.
evt-01-14-1939-queen-maud-land.prompt: What does Norway do about the territory?

choices.text: Formally proclaim Norwegian sovereignty over the territory
Leave the area unclaimed to avoid provoking Germany
Wait and negotiate a joint claim with Germany
Cede the region to Britain's existing Antarctic claims

evt-01-14-1939-queen-maud-land.butterflyEffect: Norway formally proclaimed sovereignty over the region as Queen Maud Land, preempting any German territorial ambitions there. The claim endured through the Antarctic Treaty System established in 1959, which froze territorial disputes but left Norway's claim internationally recognized.

evt-01-14-1960-reserve-bank-of-australia.scenario: You are a Sydney bank clerk in January 1960, watching new signage go up as the Reserve Bank Act 1959 takes effect and the old Commonwealth Bank is split in two.
evt-01-14-1960-reserve-bank-of-australia.prompt: What function is carried away from the Commonwealth Bank to create the new Reserve Bank?

choices.text: Central banking, including currency issue and monetary policy
The printing of postage stamps
All commercial lending to farmers
Management of the national census

evt-01-14-1960-reserve-bank-of-australia.butterflyEffect: The Reserve Bank of Australia took over central banking duties—note issue and monetary policy—while the Commonwealth Bank continued as an ordinary trading and savings bank. That commercial arm was eventually fully privatised in the 1990s, while the RBA remains Australia's central bank and currency authority to this day.

evt-01-14-1966-vietnam-war.scenario: It is January 1966 near Cu Chi, South Vietnam. Intelligence has just revealed that the Viet Cong tunnel network beneath your unit's feet is far larger than anyone suspected.
evt-01-14-1966-vietnam-war.prompt: How do you clear the newly discovered tunnel complex?

choices.text: Flood the entire complex with river water and abandon the search
Withdraw and call in a full B-52 airstrike on the area
Send small volunteers armed with pistols and flashlights down into the tunnels to fight and map them
Collapse every tunnel entrance immediately with bulldozers and move on

evt-01-14-1966-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: Operation Crimp failed to destroy the Cu Chi tunnels, which proved to be part of a vast, multi-level network. The operation exposed how little the Allies understood the tunnels' scale, spurring the creation of specialized 'tunnel rat' units and the larger Operation Cedar Falls the following year.

evt-01-14-1969-1969-uss-enterprise-fire.scenario: It is 14 January 1969 aboard the USS Enterprise off Hawaii. A Zuni rocket has just overheated and detonated beneath a parked aircraft on the flight deck, and fire is spreading toward more armed planes.
evt-01-14-1969-1969-uss-enterprise-fire.prompt: What must the flight deck crew do to prevent the disaster from worsening?

choices.text: Seal off the area and wait for shore-based fire crews
Launch all remaining aircraft immediately regardless of readiness
Evacuate the flight deck and let the fire burn out on its own
Fight the fire and jettison live ordnance overboard

evt-01-14-1969-1969-uss-enterprise-fire.butterflyEffect: Sailors fought the blaze and jettisoned burning ordnance overboard, but 28 crew died and 15 aircraft were destroyed before the fires were controlled. Combined with the 1967 USS Forrestal fire, the disaster pushed the Navy to overhaul weapons-handling procedures and firefighting training fleet-wide.

evt-01-14-1970-biafra.scenario: It is January 1970. Ojukwu has fled into exile and Biafran forces are collapsing. As Chief of General Staff, the fate of what remains of the breakaway state rests on you.

choices.text: Surrender to the Nigerian federal military government
Continue the war as a guerrilla resistance from the bush
Flee into exile alongside Ojukwu
Appeal directly to the United Nations for emergency intervention

evt-01-14-1970-biafra.butterflyEffect: Effiong surrendered to Nigerian federal forces, formally ending the civil war. General Gowon declared a policy of 'no victor, no vanquished,' though the promised reconciliation and reintegration of the Igbo region remained contested for decades afterward.

evt-01-14-1972-margrethe-ii.scenario: You stand in the courtyard of Christiansborg Palace on January 14, 1972, hours after King Frederik IX's death, as officials prepare to formally recognize his daughter as the new monarch.
evt-01-14-1972-margrethe-ii.prompt: What ceremony confirms Margrethe's new role, since Denmark has no coronation?

choices.text: She is crowned with a jeweled crown inside a cathedral
Parliament holds a formal vote to confirm her accession
The Prime Minister proclaims her from the palace balcony
She must marry before assuming the throne

evt-01-14-1972-margrethe-ii.butterflyEffect: Prime Minister Jens Otto Krag proclaimed Margrethe II queen from the palace balcony, following Danish tradition of proclamation rather than coronation. She would go on to reign for 52 years, becoming known for modernizing the monarchy, before abdicating in favor of her son Frederik X on the same date in 2024.

evt-01-14-1973-elvis-presley.scenario: It is 14 January 1973, and you are producing Elvis Presley's live concert broadcast from Honolulu, set to reach television audiences across Asia and Europe by satellite that same night.
evt-01-14-1973-elvis-presley.prompt: What do you do about airing the special to viewers in the United States?

choices.text: Delay the US broadcast for months to avoid competing with the Super Bowl
Broadcast it live domestically alongside the international feed
Skip a US television broadcast and release only a concert film
Air it live in the US but only on radio

evt-01-14-1973-elvis-presley.butterflyEffect: The US broadcast was held back and did not air on NBC until April 1973, after being delayed to avoid clashing with Super Bowl VII. When it finally aired, it drew a massive American audience and became a defining moment of Elvis's later career.

evt-01-14-1978-logic.scenario: It is January 1978 in Princeton. You are the aging logician Kurt Gödel. Your wife Adele, who has always tasted your meals to reassure you they are not poisoned, has just been hospitalized and cannot eat with you.
evt-01-14-1978-logic.prompt: What do you do about eating while Adele is away?

choices.text: Refuse to eat anything until Adele can taste it again
Accept hospital-prepared meals brought by staff
Eat only sealed, factory-packaged food he opens himself
Ask a trusted colleague to taste his meals in her place

evt-01-14-1978-logic.butterflyEffect: Gödel refused all food he could not verify was safe and starved to death within days, weighing barely 65 pounds. His paranoia cut short a mind that had reshaped mathematics with the incompleteness theorems, leaving many of his philosophical notebooks unfinished and unpublished at his death.

evt-01-14-1993-sinking-of-the-ms-jan-hew.scenario: It is the early hours of 14 January 1993, and the ferry Jan Heweliusz is crossing the storm-tossed Baltic Sea from Świnoujście to Ystad, a route it has sailed many times despite known troubles with its stability in rough weather.
evt-01-14-1993-sinking-of-the-ms-jan-hew.prompt: What did this disaster prompt in its aftermath?

choices.text: The permanent closure of the Świnoujście–Ystad ferry route
Poland's withdrawal from international maritime treaties
A major overhaul of Polish ferry safety and inspection standards
A total ban on winter crossings of the Baltic Sea

evt-01-14-1993-sinking-of-the-ms-jan-hew.butterflyEffect: As Poland's worst peacetime maritime disaster, the sinking exposed serious flaws in the ferry's stability and in rescue coordination during the storm. It led to tighter Polish maritime safety regulations and renewed scrutiny of Baltic ferry operations across the region.

evt-01-14-2010-al-qaeda-insurgency-in-ye.scenario: You are a Yemeni official in January 2010, weeks after a young man trained by militants in your country nearly bombed a Detroit-bound airliner on Christmas Day.
evt-01-14-2010-al-qaeda-insurgency-in-ye.prompt: What does the Yemeni government announce in response to the growing pressure?

choices.text: An open war against al-Qaeda
A peace treaty with al-Qaeda's leadership
The expulsion of all foreign counterterrorism advisors
A nationwide closure of mosques

evt-01-14-2010-al-qaeda-insurgency-in-ye.butterflyEffect: On January 14, 2010, Yemen declared open war on al-Qaeda, formalizing a campaign that drew in intensified US drone strikes and counterterrorism support. The escalation failed to root out the group and instead fed years of instability that helped set the stage for Yemen's later civil war.

evt-01-14-2011-arab-spring.scenario: You are a protester in the streets of Tunis on 14 January 2011, celebrating as word spreads that President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali has fled the country after weeks of unrest sparked by Mohamed Bouazizi's death.
evt-01-14-2011-arab-spring.prompt: What follows Ben Ali's flight for Tunisia's political future?

choices.text: The military immediately seizes permanent control of the country
Civil war breaks out across Tunisia within days
The monarchy is restored under a new ruler
A transitional government leads to Tunisia's first free elections

evt-01-14-2011-arab-spring.butterflyEffect: A transitional government formed and Tunisia went on to hold free elections and draft a new constitution, becoming the Arab Spring's rare lasting democratic success. Its uprising also inspired similar protests across Egypt, Libya, Yemen and Syria, though most of those countries descended into prolonged conflict or authoritarian relapse rather than stable democracy.

evt-01-14-2018-minneapolis-miracle.scenario: It's January 14, 2018, ten seconds left in the NFC Divisional playoff, your Minnesota Vikings trail the New Orleans Saints 24-23, and you have the ball at your own 39-yard line.
evt-01-14-2018-minneapolis-miracle.prompt: As quarterback Case Keenum, what do you do with the final play?

choices.text: Call for a long field-goal attempt
Spike the ball to stop the clock
Run the ball himself up the middle
Throw a pass toward Stefon Diggs near the sideline

evt-01-14-2018-minneapolis-miracle.butterflyEffect: Keenum's pass found Stefon Diggs near the sideline, and Diggs shed a diving defender to sprint 61 yards for a walk-off touchdown as time expired—the first such finish in NFL playoff history. The play sent the Vikings to the NFC Championship and is still replayed as one of the sport's most dramatic endings.

evt-01-14-2024-abdication-of-margrethe-i.scenario: It is 14 January 2024, exactly 52 years since you ascended the Danish throne. At Christiansborg Palace you sign a declaration ending your reign, an act no reigning Danish monarch has chosen since 1146.
evt-01-14-2024-abdication-of-margrethe-i.prompt: Who becomes monarch immediately after your abdication?

choices.text: Princess Mary becomes queen regnant in her own right
The throne passes to Prince Joachim
Crown Prince Frederik becomes King Frederik X
Denmark holds a referendum on abolishing the monarchy

evt-01-14-2024-abdication-of-margrethe-i.butterflyEffect: Crown Prince Frederik was proclaimed King Frederik X within hours, with his Australian-born wife Mary becoming queen consort. Margrethe's voluntary abdication, the first since Eric III, modernized public expectations of when and how a Danish sovereign may step down.

evt-01-15-1865-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 15 January 1865, and you are a Union sailor in the fleet massed off Fort Fisher, North Carolina, the earthwork guarding Wilmington, the Confederacy's last major open port. Landing parties are forming for a final push against the fort's walls.
evt-01-15-1865-american-civil-war.prompt: How do Union forces finally break through the fort's defenses?

choices.text: A heavy naval bombardment followed by a combined infantry and naval assault
A naval bombardment alone, with no landing of troops
A prolonged siege to starve out the garrison without direct assault
A surprise cavalry charge along the beach at night

evt-01-15-1865-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: A massive naval bombardment softened the fort before Union sailors, marines, and soldiers stormed its land face in brutal hand-to-hand fighting. Fort Fisher's fall sealed off Wilmington, cutting the Confederacy's last blockade-running lifeline and hastening its collapse within months.

evt-01-15-1910-buffalo-bill-dam.scenario: You are an engineer overseeing the final concrete pour on the Shoshone River in Wyoming in January 1910. The canyon walls are narrow and steep, and you must choose a design that can reach record height without collapsing.
evt-01-15-1910-buffalo-bill-dam.prompt: What design lets the dam reach record-breaking height in this narrow canyon?

choices.text: A wide earthen embankment dam across the full canyon floor
A timber crib dam reinforced with river stone
A series of smaller check dams built in succession
A concrete arch-gravity dam that lets the canyon walls bear part of the load

evt-01-15-1910-buffalo-bill-dam.butterflyEffect: The concrete arch-gravity design let the dam rise to 325 feet, the tallest in the world at completion, using the canyon walls to share the load. It later irrigated the Bighorn Basin's farmland, was raised further in the 1990s, and was renamed for Buffalo Bill Cody in 1946.

evt-01-15-1943-united-states-department-.scenario: It is 15 January 1943, and you are a War Department clerk moving your desk into the newly completed Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia. The ring-shaped corridors stretch on for miles, built to house the entire wartime military bureaucracy under one roof.
evt-01-15-1943-united-states-department-.prompt: What made this new headquarters building so remarkable when it opened?

choices.text: It became the largest office building in the world by floor area
It was built entirely underground for bomb protection
It housed only the newly formed Central Intelligence Agency
It became the tallest skyscraper in Washington, D.C.

evt-01-15-1943-united-states-department-.butterflyEffect: The Pentagon became the world's largest office building by floor area, consolidating the sprawling War Department into a single structure. After the 1947 National Security Act created the Department of Defense, it remained the nerve center of American military power through the Cold War and beyond.

evt-01-15-1962-derveni-papyrus.scenario: It is 1962 near Derveni, outside Thessaloniki. Road workers have opened an ancient tomb, and charred scraps of papyrus lie exposed inside a burial pyre, already crumbling in the open air.
evt-01-15-1962-derveni-papyrus.prompt: What should be done with these fragile, burnt fragments?

choices.text: Sell them at once to private collectors
Rebury them with the rest of the grave goods
Carefully preserve and painstakingly document them for scholars
Discard them as unreadable ash

evt-01-15-1962-derveni-papyrus.butterflyEffect: Careful conservation preserved what became Europe's oldest surviving manuscript, an allegorical commentary on an Orphic theogony linked to the circle of Anaxagoras. Decades of painstaking work followed, and its full publication in 2006 reshaped scholarly understanding of early Greek philosophy and religion.

evt-01-15-1970-biafra.scenario: It is 15 January 1970. Ojukwu has fled into exile, and as his deputy Philip Effiong you face the remnants of a defeated Biafran army with Nigerian federal forces closing in on all sides.
evt-01-15-1970-biafra.prompt: What do you do to end the fighting?

choices.text: Appeal to the United Nations for armed intervention
Continue guerrilla resistance in the bush
Negotiate a partition of the Eastern Region
Formally surrender to end the fighting

evt-01-15-1970-biafra.butterflyEffect: Effiong formally surrendered, ending nearly three years of civil war and Biafra's secession attempt. Nigeria pursued a stated policy of reconciliation, 'no victor, no vanquished,' though the war's toll left a lasting imprint on Igbo political memory and Nigeria's federal structure for decades after.

evt-01-15-2009-us-airways-flight-1549.scenario: It is three minutes after takeoff from LaGuardia. Both engines have died after striking a flock of geese, and you are the captain gliding a full Airbus A320 with no power over Manhattan.
evt-01-15-2009-us-airways-flight-1549.prompt: Where do you put the plane down?

choices.text: Crash-land on a Manhattan street
Divert to Teterboro Airport
Ditch in the Hudson River
Attempt to return to LaGuardia Airport

evt-01-15-2009-us-airways-flight-1549.butterflyEffect: Sullenberger and Skiles ditched safely in the Hudson River; all 155 aboard survived, pulled from the wings by nearby ferries within minutes. The 'Miracle on the Hudson' became a landmark case study in crew resource management and split-second decision-making under pressure.

evt-01-15-2020-ministry-of-health-labour.scenario: You are a public health officer at Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare on 15 January 2020. A man in his thirties has just tested positive after returning from Wuhan, China, and you must decide how aggressively to respond.
evt-01-15-2020-ministry-of-health-labour.prompt: What is the appropriate immediate response to Japan's first confirmed case?

choices.text: Immediately close all Japanese borders to international travel
Treat it as an isolated travel case requiring no further tracing
Isolate the patient, trace recent contacts, and monitor for further cases
Publicly downplay the case to avoid economic disruption

evt-01-15-2020-ministry-of-health-labour.butterflyEffect: Japan isolated the patient and began contact tracing, but the virus was already spreading quietly. Within weeks the Diamond Princess cruise ship became one of the first major outbreaks outside China, forcing Japan into a much larger public health reckoning and shaping early global assumptions about COVID-19's spread.

evt-01-15-2022-2022-hunga-tonga-hunga-ha.scenario: It is 15 January 2022 on Tongatapu. A colossal eruption plume is rising from the sea to the north, and the ground is trembling from what will later be recorded as history's largest atmospheric explosion.
evt-01-15-2022-2022-hunga-tonga-hunga-ha.prompt: What is the correct life-saving action for coastal residents right now?

choices.text: Wait for official confirmation before moving
Head to the beach to watch the eruption
Move immediately to higher ground away from the shore
Shelter on the ground floor of a coastal building

evt-01-15-2022-2022-hunga-tonga-hunga-ha.butterflyEffect: The eruption triggered tsunami waves across the Pacific and severed Tonga's undersea cable, isolating the kingdom for weeks. It also injected an unprecedented amount of water vapor into the stratosphere, an effect scientists linked to measurable short-term atmospheric warming.

evt-01-16-bce27-augustus.scenario: It is 16 January 27 BC in Rome. You stand in the Senate as Octavian, having theatrically offered to lay down his extraordinary powers, watches senators react to his gesture.
evt-01-16-bce27-augustus.prompt: What does Octavian do to secure lasting power while appearing to restore the Republic?

choices.text: He accepts the new titles while keeping control of the army and key provinces
He orders the Senate to formally crown him king of Rome
He abdicates all power and retires from public life
He declares himself dictator for life in the style of Julius Caesar

evt-01-16-bce27-augustus.butterflyEffect: The Senate granted Octavian the titles Augustus and Princeps while he retained command of the legions and key provinces, creating the Principate — a system that preserved republican forms while concentrating real power in one man. This arrangement became the template for Roman imperial rule for centuries.

evt-01-16-1275-eleanor-of-provence.scenario: It is 1275, and as Queen Dowager Eleanor of Provence you hold several towns as dower lands. You have sought your son Edward I's permission to deal with the Jewish communities living within them.
evt-01-16-1275-eleanor-of-provence.prompt: What does Eleanor do with Edward's blessing?

choices.text: Expels the Jewish communities from her dower towns
Grants Jewish residents new royal charters of protection
Imposes heavier taxes on Jewish moneylenders instead
Invites more Jewish merchants to settle in her towns

evt-01-16-1275-eleanor-of-provence.butterflyEffect: Eleanor expelled Jewish residents from towns under her control, seizing their property in the process. Her local expulsions foreshadowed Edward I's Edict of Expulsion of 1290, which drove all Jews from England for the next three and a half centuries.

evt-01-16-1780-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is the night of 16 January 1780 off Cape St Vincent. You command a ship in Admiral Rodney's fleet, sailing toward a rocky Spanish coast, and lookouts have just sighted Admiral Lángara's squadron in the darkness.
evt-01-16-1780-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: Do you press the attack in darkness, or wait until dawn to engage?

choices.text: Anchor and wait for daylight before engaging
Signal for a formal line-of-battle approach at dawn
Retreat to open water to avoid the hazardous coastline
Attack immediately under cover of night despite the rocky coast

evt-01-16-1780-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Rodney's fleet fought through the night, capturing or destroying most of the Spanish squadron in what became known as the 'Moonlight Battle.' The victory relieved the besieged garrison at Gibraltar and gave Britain a rare naval triumph during the otherwise difficult American Revolutionary War.

evt-01-16-1809-peninsular-war.scenario: It is 16 January 1809 at Corunna, Spain. You serve under Sir John Moore as Marshal Soult's French troops press an attack while the Royal Navy waits offshore to evacuate your exhausted army.
evt-01-16-1809-peninsular-war.prompt: What does Moore's army do to escape annihilation?

choices.text: They launch a full attack on Soult's main army instead of evacuating
They abandon the coast and retreat further inland
They fight a rearguard battle to hold off the French while completing the evacuation
They surrender to Soult to avoid further casualties

evt-01-16-1809-peninsular-war.butterflyEffect: Moore's men fought a fierce rearguard action that repelled Soult's assault, though Moore himself was killed in the fighting. The battle bought enough time for the British army to complete a full evacuation by sea, preserving the force that would later return under Wellington to campaign across the Peninsula.

evt-01-16-1862-coal-mining.scenario: It's 16 January 1862 at New Hartley Colliery, Northumberland. The pit has only a single shaft, and you are among the officials rushing to the surface after the massive cast-iron beam of the pumping engine has snapped and crashed down that shaft, blocking the only way in or out.
evt-01-16-1862-coal-mining.prompt: What change did this disaster force upon British mining law?

choices.text: Parliament nationalized the coal industry
Parliament banned the use of steam pumping engines in mines
Parliament abolished child labor in mines for the first time
Parliament required every colliery to have at least two shafts

evt-01-16-1862-coal-mining.butterflyEffect: The blocked single shaft trapped the men and boys below with no means of escape or rescue. Public outcry led directly to the Coal Mines Regulation Act 1862, which mandated two independent shafts or outlets at every colliery in Britain, a reform that shaped mine safety law for generations.

evt-01-16-1883-pendleton-civil-service-r.scenario: It is 16 January 1883 in Washington. You watch President Chester Arthur, once a beneficiary of political patronage, sign a bill responding to public outrage after President Garfield's assassination by a rejected office-seeker.
evt-01-16-1883-pendleton-civil-service-r.prompt: What system does the new Act establish to replace patronage hiring?

choices.text: The existing spoils system is left fully intact and unregulated
Competitive examinations determine appointment to federal government jobs
Civil service posts become hereditary within families
Federal employees are directly elected by voters in their districts

evt-01-16-1883-pendleton-civil-service-r.butterflyEffect: The Pendleton Act created competitive examinations for many federal jobs, founding the modern U.S. Civil Service and curbing the old spoils system. Over the following decades, the merit-based system expanded to cover the vast majority of federal positions, reshaping how the American government hires its workforce.

evt-01-16-1905-ice-hockey.scenario: It's 16 January 1905 in Ottawa, and you're playing for the Silver Seven against the exhausted Dawson City Nuggets, who have just completed an epic weeks-long journey west to challenge for the Stanley Cup. Blind in one eye, you keep finding yourself with open ice.
evt-01-16-1905-ice-hockey.prompt: What did Frank McGee actually do in this Stanley Cup challenge match?

choices.text: He was ejected for rough play and missed the rest of the series
He scored a record 14 goals in a single game
He scored a hat-trick but Ottawa lost anyway
He suffered an injury and had to leave the ice

evt-01-16-1905-ice-hockey.butterflyEffect: McGee's 14 goals in one game remain a Stanley Cup record more than a century later. Ottawa swept the overmatched Dawson City club, and the lopsided series became legendary as a symbol of how far teams would travel—and how badly they could be beaten—chasing the Cup in hockey's early era.

evt-01-16-1920-league-of-nations.scenario: It is 16 January 1920 in Paris. You are a delegate at the League of Nations' first Council session, drafting the list of founding members while the treaty creating the League still awaits ratification in Washington.
evt-01-16-1920-league-of-nations.prompt: What early setback cripples the League's authority from the outset?

choices.text: Soviet Russia joins immediately as a founding member
The United States Senate refuses to ratify the treaty, keeping America out of the League
The League is granted its own standing army to enforce peace
Germany is admitted as a founding member alongside the Allied powers

evt-01-16-1920-league-of-nations.butterflyEffect: The US Senate refused to ratify the Treaty of Versailles, so the United States never joined the League it had helped conceive, leaving the organization without one of its strongest potential enforcers. This weakness contributed to the League's failure to stop aggression in the 1930s, and it was eventually dissolved and replaced by the United Nations in 1946.

evt-01-16-1942-twa-flight-3.scenario: It's January 16, 1942, in Las Vegas. You're traveling with Carole Lombard's group after a war bonds tour. Her press agent Otto Winkler wants to go home by train, but Lombard insists on flying to reach Clark Gable sooner, so the group flips a coin to settle it.
evt-01-16-1942-twa-flight-3.prompt: What does the coin toss decide?

choices.text: They drive back to California by car
They wait several days for a later, safer flight
They take the train home instead
They fly on TWA Flight 3 to Burbank

evt-01-16-1942-twa-flight-3.butterflyEffect: They fly. TWA Flight 3 crashes into Potosi Mountain fifteen minutes after leaving Las Vegas, killing all 22 aboard, including Lombard, her mother, and Winkler. Investigators blamed a navigation error by the captain. Grief-stricken, Clark Gable enlisted in the U.S. Army Air Forces, a move that boosted wartime morale and recruitment.

evt-01-16-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 16 January 1945 in Berlin. Soviet forces are grinding westward, and you are one of Hitler's staff ordered to move operations underground into the newly readied Führerbunker beneath the Reich Chancellery garden.
evt-01-16-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What followed after Hitler relocated his command into the Führerbunker?

choices.text: He used it only briefly before returning to open command posts
He evacuated to Bavaria shortly afterward and abandoned Berlin
He directed the collapsing war from underground for the war's final months
He ordered it demolished within weeks as unnecessary

evt-01-16-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Hitler remained in the Führerbunker for the war's final 105 days, issuing orders as Berlin fell around him. It was there that he married Eva Braun and took his own life on 30 April 1945, days before Germany's unconditional surrender ended the war in Europe.

evt-01-16-1964-hello-dolly-musical.scenario: You are in the audience at the St. James Theatre on Broadway on January 16, 1964, watching Carol Channing belt out the title number as Dolly Gallagher Levi for the first time.
evt-01-16-1964-hello-dolly-musical.prompt: What happened to the show in the years after this opening night?

choices.text: It played only a brief limited engagement before touring
It was overshadowed by a rival show and closed early
It closed within weeks after poor reviews
It became a smash hit that ran for years and won a record number of Tony Awards

evt-01-16-1964-hello-dolly-musical.butterflyEffect: Hello, Dolly! became one of Broadway's biggest hits, running for 2,844 performances and winning a then-record ten Tony Awards. Its success led to a lavish 1969 film adaptation starring Barbra Streisand.

evt-01-16-2003-space-shuttle-columbia.scenario: It's launch day, 16 January 2003, at Kennedy Space Center. Cameras capture a piece of foam insulation breaking off Columbia's external tank and striking the left wing during ascent, though the shuttle reaches orbit safely and the crew begins mission STS-107.
evt-01-16-2003-space-shuttle-columbia.prompt: What do engineers do after spotting the foam strike on launch film?

choices.text: They order the crew to abort the mission and return early
They dismiss the strike without any internal discussion
They immediately schedule a spacewalk to inspect the wing
They request extra imagery of the wing, but managers decide it's unnecessary

evt-01-16-2003-space-shuttle-columbia.butterflyEffect: Engineers on the Debris Assessment Team requested additional satellite imagery of the wing to assess damage, but NASA managers declined, judging the strike routine and any damage unfixable in orbit anyway. On 1 February 2003, Columbia broke apart during re-entry, killing all seven astronauts. The Columbia Accident Investigation Board cited both the foam strike and a flawed safety culture, leading to redesigned tank insulation and mandatory on-orbit inspections for future shuttle missions.

evt-01-16-2006-ellen-johnson-sirleaf.scenario: You stand among the crowds in Monrovia on January 16, 2006, watching Ellen Johnson Sirleaf take the oath of office as Liberia emerges from years of civil war.
evt-01-16-2006-ellen-johnson-sirleaf.prompt: What historic first does her inauguration mark?

choices.text: The first woman to chair the African Union
The first elected female head of state in Africa
The first female Secretary-General of the United Nations
The first female prime minister in West Africa

evt-01-16-2006-ellen-johnson-sirleaf.butterflyEffect: Sirleaf became Africa's first elected female head of state. She would go on to lead Liberia's postwar reconstruction and, in 2011, share the Nobel Peace Prize for her work on women's rights and peacebuilding.

evt-01-16-2012-mali-war.scenario: It is 16 January 2012 in northern Mali. You fight alongside the Tuareg MNLA as it launches attacks on army garrisons, and jihadist fighters from Ansar Dine offer to join your uprising against Bamako.
evt-01-16-2012-mali-war.prompt: What alliance shapes the rebellion's early trajectory?

choices.text: ECOWAS troops arrive within days to crush the uprising
The rebellion disbands after its first clash with government troops
The MNLA immediately allies with the Malian government against Islamist militants
The MNLA allies with the jihadist Ansar Dine despite their very different goals

evt-01-16-2012-mali-war.butterflyEffect: The MNLA's secular nationalists and the jihadist Ansar Dine fought together at first, but by mid-2012 Ansar Dine and allied al-Qaeda-linked groups seized control of northern towns and imposed harsh sharia rule, sidelining the MNLA. This collapse triggered France's 2013 military intervention, Operation Serval, drawing outside powers into a conflict still unresolved today.

evt-01-16-2016-2016-ouagadougou-attacks.scenario: It's the night of 15 January 2016 in downtown Ouagadougou. Gunmen have stormed the Cappuccino restaurant and the Splendid Hotel, and Burkinabe security forces, with foreign support, are moving to end the siege before dawn.
evt-01-16-2016-2016-ouagadougou-attacks.prompt: What ultimately happens to the hostages held inside the hotels?

choices.text: Most are freed after a government-led counter-attack overnight
All hostages are killed before help arrives
The gunmen negotiate safe passage out of the country
The siege ends only when the hostages escape on their own

evt-01-16-2016-2016-ouagadougou-attacks.butterflyEffect: After a night-long standoff, government forces launched a counter-attack that killed the remaining gunmen and freed the hostages by the next morning, though dozens of people had already been killed. Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb and Al-Mourabitoun claimed responsibility, and the attack signaled the spread of jihadist violence from the Sahel into Burkina Faso's capital.

evt-01-16-2017-turkish-airlines-flight-6.scenario: It's before dawn on 16 January 2017, and you're in the cockpit of a Boeing 747 cargo jet on final approach to Manas International Airport near Bishkek. Thick fog blankets the runway, and visibility is dropping fast.
evt-01-16-2017-turkish-airlines-flight-6.prompt: What happens as the aircraft continues its approach through the fog?

choices.text: Air traffic control orders an emergency landing at a military base instead
The crew executes a go-around and diverts safely to another airport
The plane lands safely using instrument guidance
The plane crashes into a residential neighborhood short of the runway

evt-01-16-2017-turkish-airlines-flight-6.butterflyEffect: The 747 crashed into a residential area short of the runway, killing all four crew and 35 people on the ground. It became Kyrgyzstan's deadliest air disaster since 2008, and investigators pointed to an unstabilized approach continued in near-zero visibility, prompting renewed scrutiny of cargo-airline safety practices and low-visibility landing procedures at Manas.

evt-01-16-2018-mrauk-u.scenario: It is January 16, 2018, and you stand with a crowd in Mrauk U defying a government ban on marking the anniversary of the fall of the old Arakan kingdom. Security forces have moved into position and are ordering you to disperse.
evt-01-16-2018-mrauk-u.prompt: What did security forces do when the crowd refused to disperse?

choices.text: Arrested the organizers without further incident
Used only tear gas to clear the street
Negotiated a compromise allowing a small ceremony
Fired live rounds directly into the crowd

evt-01-16-2018-mrauk-u.butterflyEffect: Police opened fire on the crowd, killing several demonstrators. The bloodshed inflamed Rakhine nationalist anger at the central government, deepening the region's political crisis already strained by the concurrent Rohingya emergency in Rakhine State.

evt-01-16-2020-first-impeachment-of-dona.scenario: It is 16 January 2020 in Washington. You are a senator sworn in as a juror as House impeachment managers formally deliver the articles against President Trump to open the Senate trial.
evt-01-16-2020-first-impeachment-of-dona.prompt: What is the eventual outcome of this impeachment trial?

choices.text: The House withdraws the articles before a vote is held
The Senate acquits Trump on both articles of impeachment
The Senate convicts Trump and removes him from office
The trial is declared a mistrial and articles are dismissed

evt-01-16-2020-first-impeachment-of-dona.butterflyEffect: On 5 February 2020 the Senate voted largely along party lines to acquit Trump on both articles, abuse of power and obstruction of Congress. He remained in office, and the acquittal set a precedent later tested again when he became the only U.S. president impeached twice, following a second trial in early 2021.

evt-01-16-2020-united-states-mexico-cana.scenario: It's 16 January 2020, and you're a U.S. senator facing a vote on the new United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement, the deal meant to replace NAFTA after years of renegotiation.
evt-01-16-2020-united-states-mexico-cana.prompt: How did the Senate actually vote on ratifying USMCA?

choices.text: A narrow party-line vote along partisan lines
Overwhelming bipartisan approval, 89–10
The Senate rejected the agreement, sending it back for more talks
The vote was postponed indefinitely amid disputes

evt-01-16-2020-united-states-mexico-cana.butterflyEffect: The Senate's lopsided approval sent USMCA to the president for signature, and it took effect on 1 July 2020, formally retiring NAFTA after 26 years. The agreement reshaped rules on autos, labor, and digital trade across one of the world's largest free-trade zones.

evt-01-17-1377-pope-gregory-xi.scenario: You are a cardinal in the procession as Pope Gregory XI finally rides into Rome on 17 January 1377, ending a four-month journey from Avignon and nearly seventy years of the papacy's exile in France.
evt-01-17-1377-pope-gregory-xi.prompt: What actually followed within a year of Gregory XI's return to Rome?

choices.text: A contested election triggers the Western Schism, with rival popes
He is crowned Holy Roman Emperor by the College of Cardinals
He immediately relocates the papacy back to Avignon
Christendom enjoys uninterrupted peace under one pope

evt-01-17-1377-pope-gregory-xi.butterflyEffect: Gregory XI died in March 1378, and the contested election that followed produced rival popes in Rome and Avignon, launching the Western Schism. The split, later widening to three competing claimants, lasted until 1417 and badly damaged papal authority, feeding later calls for church reform.

evt-01-17-1562-catherine-de-medici.scenario: You advise Catherine de' Medici's regency council in January 1562, as France edges toward open conflict between Catholics and the growing Huguenot minority.
evt-01-17-1562-catherine-de-medici.prompt: What edict does Catherine's regime issue in an attempt to preserve peace?

choices.text: The Edict of Saint-Germain, granting Huguenots limited freedom of worship
An edict banning all Protestant worship across France
An edict expelling all Huguenots from the kingdom
An edict merging Catholic and Protestant liturgies into one rite

evt-01-17-1562-catherine-de-medici.butterflyEffect: The Edict of Saint-Germain, or Edict of January, granted Huguenots limited freedom to worship outside town walls, the first royal recognition of Protestant rights in France. Catholic hardliners were enraged, and within two months the Massacre of Vassy ignited the first of the French Wars of Religion, which would recur intermittently for decades.

evt-01-17-1773-james-cook.scenario: It is January 17, 1773, and you stand on the deck of HMS Resolution as Captain Cook pushes south into increasingly icy waters on his second Pacific voyage, searching for the fabled southern continent.
evt-01-17-1773-james-cook.prompt: What does Cook decide as the ship nears the edge of the ice?

choices.text: Land a party on Antarctica to claim it for Britain
Press south, becoming the first ship to cross the Antarctic Circle
Abandon the southern search and sail for Tahiti
Turn back immediately, fearing the ice will trap the ship

evt-01-17-1773-james-cook.butterflyEffect: Cook pressed on and Resolution became the first ship recorded to cross the Antarctic Circle. Though he never sighted Antarctica itself, his voyage disproved the existence of a habitable temperate southern continent, reshaping European geographic theory for decades.

evt-01-17-1893-lorrin-a-thurston.scenario: It is 17 January 1893 in Honolulu. Lorrin Thurston's Committee of Safety, backed by armed U.S. Marines landed from the USS Boston, has demanded you surrender your throne.
evt-01-17-1893-lorrin-a-thurston.prompt: As Queen Liliʻuokalani, how do you respond to avoid bloodshed?

choices.text: Flee immediately into exile abroad
Order Hawaiian royal troops to fight the armed committee
Yield the throne under protest and appeal to the United States government for restoration
Sign a treaty voluntarily ceding Hawaii to the United States
