evt-01-17-1893-lorrin-a-thurston.butterflyEffect: The Queen yielded her authority under protest, not to the Committee but to the United States, trusting Washington to reverse the coup. President Cleveland later condemned the overthrow as illegal, but Congress refused to restore her, and the Republic of Hawaii led to annexation in 1898; in 1993 Congress formally apologized for the U.S. role.

evt-01-17-1912-robert-falcon-scott.scenario: It is 17 January 1912. You are one of Robert Falcon Scott's five-man polar party, hauling your own sledges across the ice after the ponies and dogs turned back weeks ago, closing in on the South Pole.
evt-01-17-1912-robert-falcon-scott.prompt: What do you find waiting for you when you finally reach the Pole?

choices.text: A Norwegian flag and tent left by Amundsen's team
An American expedition already camped there
An empty, unmarked stretch of ice, making you first to arrive
A marker left by an earlier British expedition

evt-01-17-1912-robert-falcon-scott.butterflyEffect: Scott's party found Amundsen's tent and flag, planted 33 days earlier. Devastated, they began the 800-mile return march but all five died, the last three just 11 miles from a supply depot. Scott's diary made him a tragic British hero; Amundsen's feat secured Norway's polar legacy.

evt-01-17-1920-volstead-act.scenario: It is January 17, 1920, and you run a small tavern in Chicago as the Volstead Act takes effect at midnight, outlawing the sale of intoxicating liquor across the United States.
evt-01-17-1920-volstead-act.prompt: What do most Americans turn to for alcohol once Prohibition begins?

choices.text: Giving up alcohol entirely and never returning to it
Emigrating to Canada to drink legally
Legally purchasing wine for medicinal use only
Speakeasies and bootleggers supplying illegal liquor

evt-01-17-1920-volstead-act.butterflyEffect: Legal drinking establishments closed, but speakeasies and bootlegging networks flourished nationwide. Organized crime figures like Al Capone built empires supplying illegal liquor, a problem so severe it contributed to Prohibition's repeal via the 21st Amendment in 1933.

evt-01-17-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is January 1945 and you command an Australian company pushing north along Bougainville. The Japanese garrison is already cut off from resupply and reinforcement by Allied naval and air control of the region.
evt-01-17-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What approach do Australian commanders take against the isolated Japanese forces on Bougainville?

choices.text: Negotiate a local ceasefire directly with the Japanese commander
Advance cautiously and methodically to contain and wear down the isolated garrison
Withdraw entirely and let the Japanese forces starve without further contact
Launch an immediate all-out assault to force a quick Japanese surrender

evt-01-17-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Australian command chose a deliberate, limited advance to squeeze the isolated garrison while minimizing Australian casualties, rather than a swift all-out assault. Back home the campaign drew criticism as an unnecessary expenditure of lives against an already-defeated enemy, a debate that shaped postwar arguments about the value of Australia's late-war Pacific campaigns.

evt-01-17-1945-raoul-wallenberg.scenario: You are an aide to Raoul Wallenberg in Budapest on 17 January 1945, as advancing Soviet officers summon him to accompany them to their headquarters for what they call a routine meeting.
evt-01-17-1945-raoul-wallenberg.prompt: What should Wallenberg do when the Soviets ask him to come with them?

choices.text: Flee at once toward the Swedish border
Refuse and go into hiding immediately
Seek protection from the remaining Hungarian fascist officials
Go with them, trusting his diplomatic status will protect him

evt-01-17-1945-raoul-wallenberg.butterflyEffect: Wallenberg went with the Soviets and vanished into their custody, never to be seen in public again. Moscow long denied knowledge of his fate before eventually claiming he died in Lubyanka prison in 1947, and his disappearance became a lasting symbol of Soviet secrecy even as he was honored as Righteous Among the Nations for saving thousands of Hungarian Jews.

evt-01-17-1961-patrice-lumumba.scenario: You are one of the guards holding Patrice Lumumba, Congo's ousted first prime minister, after his transfer into the custody of Katangese secessionists and their Belgian advisors on 17 January 1961.
evt-01-17-1961-patrice-lumumba.prompt: What happens to Lumumba after this transfer to Katanga?

choices.text: He is put on public trial before the Congolese parliament
He is released and restored to power in Léopoldville
He is executed by firing squad
He escapes across the border to Ghana

evt-01-17-1961-patrice-lumumba.butterflyEffect: Lumumba was executed by firing squad that same night, with Belgian officers present and the CIA aware of the plot against him. His death turned him into a martyr for African independence movements worldwide and deepened Cold War rivalry over the Congo, eventually helping clear the way for Mobutu Sese Seko's long dictatorship.

evt-01-17-1961-dwight-d-eisenhower.scenario: It is 17 January 1961, three days before leaving office. You are helping President Eisenhower finalize his televised farewell address to the American people, warning of a danger he believes threatens the nation's future.
evt-01-17-1961-dwight-d-eisenhower.prompt: What warning does Eisenhower deliver to the American public in this address?

choices.text: A warning about escalating federal deficits
A warning about domestic civil rights unrest
A warning about the rising Soviet nuclear arsenal
A warning about the growing military-industrial complex

evt-01-17-1961-dwight-d-eisenhower.butterflyEffect: Eisenhower warned of the growing power of what he called the "military-industrial complex," cautioning that the fusion of a permanent arms industry and a massive defense establishment could distort democratic government. The phrase entered the political vocabulary and fueled decades of debate over defense spending, especially during the Vietnam War and Cold War arms buildups that followed.

evt-01-17-1989-stockton-schoolyard-shoot.scenario: It is early 1989, and you are a California state legislator reeling from the attack on Cleveland Elementary School in Stockton, drafting a response to public outrage over the weapon used.
evt-01-17-1989-stockton-schoolyard-shoot.prompt: What legislative action followed the shooting in California?

choices.text: Congress immediately bans assault weapons nationwide
The state legislature takes no action on gun laws
California bans all handgun sales statewide
California passes the nation's first state assault weapons ban

evt-01-17-1989-stockton-schoolyard-shoot.butterflyEffect: California passed the Roberti-Roos Assault Weapons Control Act of 1989, becoming the first state to ban specific assault weapons by name. The law became a template later cited in debates leading to the 1994 federal assault weapons ban.

evt-01-17-1998-clinton-lewinsky-scandal.scenario: It is 17 January 1998. You run an online political gossip site and have just learned that Newsweek has spiked a bombshell story about President Clinton and a young White House intern, unwilling to publish without more confirmation.
evt-01-17-1998-clinton-lewinsky-scandal.prompt: What do you do with the story the mainstream press is sitting on?

choices.text: Quietly pass it to a rival newspaper without your name attached
Wait for the White House press office to confirm it officially
Sell the exclusive tip to a print tabloid for cash
Publish it immediately on your own website, breaking the story to the world

evt-01-17-1998-clinton-lewinsky-scandal.butterflyEffect: Matt Drudge posted the story on the Drudge Report that day, and it exploded across the world within hours, bypassing the traditional editorial gatekeepers who had hesitated. The episode became a landmark moment for internet journalism and set off the investigation that led to Clinton's impeachment later that year.

evt-01-17-1999-little-saigon-orange-coun.scenario: You live in Little Saigon, Orange County, and a local video store owner has just hung a communist flag and a portrait of Ho Chi Minh in his shop window. Neighbors are furious, and word is spreading fast through the Vietnamese American community.
evt-01-17-1999-little-saigon-orange-coun.prompt: What does the community do in response over the following weeks?

choices.text: Organize sustained daily protests demanding the display be removed
Ignore the display as protected free expression
Vandalize the store overnight to force it to close
Petition Congress to strip the owner's citizenship

evt-01-17-1999-little-saigon-orange-coun.butterflyEffect: Daily demonstrations outside the shop stretched on for about two months, at times drawing thousands, becoming one of the largest sustained protests in Vietnamese American history. The episode entrenched Little Saigon's identity as the political and cultural capital of the Vietnamese diaspora and sharpened debates over free speech versus anti-communist sentiment.

evt-01-17-2002-mount-nyiragongo.scenario: You are a resident of Goma on January 17, 2002, as molten lava from Mount Nyiragongo begins flowing down toward the city streets.
evt-01-17-2002-mount-nyiragongo.prompt: What do most residents of Goma do as the lava advances?

choices.text: Stay behind to defend their homes
Flee across the border into Rwanda
Dig trenches to try to divert the flow
Shelter in place and wait for the lava to stop

evt-01-17-2002-mount-nyiragongo.butterflyEffect: The eruption destroyed large parts of Goma and forced hundreds of thousands of people to flee across the border into Rwanda. The disaster exposed the region's volcanic hazards and pushed for closer monitoring of Nyiragongo's active lava lake in the years that followed.

evt-01-17-2008-british-airways-flight-38.scenario: You are an accident investigator examining the wreckage of British Airways Flight 38, which crash-landed short of the runway at Heathrow on January 17, 2008, after losing engine power on approach.
evt-01-17-2008-british-airways-flight-38.prompt: What did investigators determine had choked off fuel to the engines?

choices.text: Ice restricting flow through the fuel-oil heat exchangers
Sabotage of the aircraft's fuel system
Pilot error during the final approach
A bird strike that disabled both engines

evt-01-17-2008-british-airways-flight-38.butterflyEffect: Investigators traced the failure to ice, formed from cold fuel on the long flight from Beijing, that had restricted flow through the fuel-oil heat exchangers. The finding led Boeing and regulators to redesign 777 fuel system components and revise cold-weather fuel-flow guidance across the industry.

evt-01-17-2010-2010-jos-riots.scenario: It is 17 January 2010 in Jos, Nigeria. A dispute has exploded into gunfire between Muslim and Christian neighbors, and homes, churches, and mosques are already burning across the city.
evt-01-17-2010-2010-jos-riots.prompt: What followed in the months after this outbreak of violence in Jos?

choices.text: The Nigerian government banned all religious worship in Jos indefinitely
Federal troops restored lasting peace within days and violence did not recur
An African Union peacekeeping force was deployed to patrol Plateau State
Further deadly attacks struck nearby villages, including a massacre at Dogo Nahawa months later

evt-01-17-2010-2010-jos-riots.butterflyEffect: The January clashes did not end the cycle: in March 2010, hundreds were killed in a coordinated attack on the nearby village of Dogo Nahawa. The Jos violence became a recurring flashpoint in Nigeria's Middle Belt, entrenching a pattern of ethnic and religious reprisal killings that outside forces struggled to contain.

evt-01-17-2013-lance-armstrong.scenario: You are watching live as Lance Armstrong sits across from Oprah Winfrey on 17 January 2013, taping the interview the world has been waiting for since his seven Tour de France titles were stripped.
evt-01-17-2013-lance-armstrong.prompt: What does Armstrong finally admit during the interview?

choices.text: He denies ever using performance-enhancing drugs
He blames his former coach for secretly drugging him
He admits to using performance-enhancing drugs throughout his career
He accuses rival teams of fabricating the doping evidence

evt-01-17-2013-lance-armstrong.butterflyEffect: Armstrong confirmed he had used performance-enhancing drugs throughout his championship-winning career, ending years of public denial. The confession triggered lawsuits, sponsor exits, and a permanent shift in his public image from cancer-survivor hero to disgraced champion, while reinforcing the credibility of anti-doping investigations in cycling.

evt-01-17-2016-barack-obama.scenario: It is January 17, 2016, and you are a State Department official watching Implementation Day for the Iran nuclear deal unfold. Sanctions relief is being finalized, but American citizens are still detained in Tehran.
evt-01-17-2016-barack-obama.prompt: What move does the administration pair with the nuclear deal's implementation that day?

choices.text: Negotiate a prisoner swap to coincide with sanctions relief
Send additional troops to the Persian Gulf
Suspend all nuclear talks indefinitely
Impose a fresh round of sanctions on Iran

evt-01-17-2016-barack-obama.butterflyEffect: Alongside the JCPOA taking effect, the U.S. and Iran carried out a prisoner swap that freed Americans including journalist Jason Rezaian. Billions in frozen Iranian assets were unlocked, but the deal's fragile diplomacy collapsed when the U.S. withdrew from it in 2018.

evt-01-17-2017-search-for-malaysia-airli.scenario: It is January 17, 2017, and you are an Australian official overseeing the multinational search for Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, which has scoured a vast stretch of the southern Indian Ocean without finding the wreck.
evt-01-17-2017-search-for-malaysia-airli.prompt: What do the coordinating governments decide after years without success?

choices.text: Expand the search into new ocean zones immediately
Transfer the search entirely to the airline's insurers
Declare the wreck found and close the investigation
Suspend the official search despite finding no wreckage

evt-01-17-2017-search-for-malaysia-airli.butterflyEffect: Australia, Malaysia, and China suspended the official search despite the aircraft never being located. A private firm, Ocean Infinity, resumed searching in 2018 under a no-find-no-fee arrangement, but the fate of most of the plane remains unresolved beyond a few debris pieces washed ashore in Africa.

evt-01-18-474-leo-ii-emperor.scenario: You serve at the Byzantine court in Constantinople. The aged emperor Leo I has just died of dysentery, leaving his young grandson Leo II, already crowned co-emperor months earlier, alone on the throne.
evt-01-18-474-leo-ii-emperor.prompt: What happens within days of Leo II becoming sole emperor on 18 January 474?

choices.text: The Senate deposes him in favor of a general
His father Zeno is raised to co-emperor
His mother Ariadne is crowned empress regnant
He abdicates immediately in favor of Zeno

evt-01-18-474-leo-ii-emperor.butterflyEffect: On 29 January, the Senate elevated Leo II's father Zeno to co-emperor. The boy died later that year, leaving Zeno as sole ruler, whose turbulent, twice-interrupted reign steered the Eastern Empire through the very years the Western Empire finally collapsed.

evt-01-18-1535-francisco-pizarro.scenario: You stand beside Francisco Pizarro on Peru's coast in January 1535 as he chooses ground for a new city meant to anchor Spanish rule over the conquered Inca lands.
evt-01-18-1535-francisco-pizarro.prompt: What factor most shapes his choice of site for Ciudad de los Reyes?

choices.text: An inland site chosen to avoid contact with the sea
Proximity to the largest existing Inca temple complex
Coastal access for a port to ship treasure and supplies to Spain
A defensible mountain position modeled on Cuzco

evt-01-18-1535-francisco-pizarro.butterflyEffect: Pizarro sited the city near the Rímac River for its access to a port and fertile valley, naming it Ciudad de los Reyes. It grew into Lima, which became the capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru and the administrative center of Spanish power across much of South America for nearly three centuries.

evt-01-18-1788-ship-s-tender.scenario: It is January 1788. You are aboard HMS Supply, the tender that has raced ahead of the First Fleet and anchored first in Botany Bay, but the land here is sandy and short of fresh water.
evt-01-18-1788-ship-s-tender.prompt: What should the fleet's commander decide to do next?

choices.text: Settle permanently at Botany Bay as planned
Sail the whole fleet back to Cape Town for resupply
Send the fastest ship north to search for a better harbour
Push the convicts ashore immediately regardless of conditions

evt-01-18-1788-ship-s-tender.butterflyEffect: Governor Arthur Phillip explored north and found a deep, sheltered harbour he named Sydney Cove, in Port Jackson. The fleet relocated there on 26 January 1788, the date now marked as Australia's founding, and the cove grew into the city of Sydney.

evt-01-18-1871-german-empire.scenario: You stand among the assembled princes and generals in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles on 18 January 1871, watching King Wilhelm I of Prussia accept a new title from the gathered German rulers.
evt-01-18-1871-german-empire.prompt: What does this proclamation actually establish?

choices.text: A restored Holy Roman Empire under Austrian rule
A unified German Empire under Prussian leadership
The dissolution of Prussia into smaller states
French annexation of the Rhineland states

evt-01-18-1871-german-empire.butterflyEffect: The German states unified into an empire dominated by Prussia, whose king now also reigned as Emperor. That imbalance of power shaped German politics for decades and fed the rivalries that helped trigger the First World War, until the empire itself collapsed in the 1918 revolution.

evt-01-18-1915-okuma-shigenobu.scenario: You advise Chinese President Yuan Shikai in early 1915, as Japanese Prime Minister Ōkuma Shigenobu's government presents a secret ultimatum demanding sweeping rights across Manchuria, Shandong, and beyond.
evt-01-18-1915-okuma-shigenobu.prompt: How does Yuan Shikai's government ultimately respond to the Twenty-One Demands?

choices.text: Rejects all demands and mobilizes for war
Negotiates and accepts a reduced set of the demands
Requests British mediation and refuses to respond
Declares Manchuria independent to avoid compliance

evt-01-18-1915-okuma-shigenobu.butterflyEffect: After months of negotiation and a final Japanese ultimatum, China accepted a reduced set of demands in May 1915, excluding the most extreme provisions. The humiliation fueled Chinese nationalism and anti-Japanese sentiment, feeding directly into the May Fourth Movement and decades of hostility between the two nations.

evt-01-18-1932-alt-llobregat-insurrectio.scenario: It is January 1932 in Fígols, Catalonia. You and your fellow miners have walked out over starvation wages, disarmed the local police, and now control the town with no bloodshed so far.
evt-01-18-1932-alt-llobregat-insurrectio.prompt: What do the striking miners proclaim as they take control of the town?

choices.text: Loyalty to the Republican government in Madrid
A constitutional monarchy
Libertarian communism
A return to Catalan feudal rule

evt-01-18-1932-alt-llobregat-insurrectio.butterflyEffect: The miners declared libertarian communism, and the revolt spread across the region before the Spanish Army crushed it within a week. The crackdown split the CNT, with radicals seizing control and moderates breaking away to form the Syndicalist Party.

evt-01-18-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 18 January 1943, and you are a Soviet soldier pushing through German lines south of Lake Ladoga in Operation Iskra, trying to reach the besieged city of Leningrad.
evt-01-18-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What is achieved when Soviet forces link up near Workers' Settlement No. 1?

choices.text: The siege of Leningrad is completely lifted
Army Group North surrenders outright
A German naval blockade of the city is broken
A narrow land corridor to Leningrad is opened

evt-01-18-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: A narrow land corridor to Leningrad was opened, and engineers rushed to build the 'Road of Victory' rail line through it. The full siege would not be lifted until January 1944, but this corridor let vital supplies reach the starving city a year earlier than otherwise possible.

evt-01-18-1958-willie-o-ree.scenario: It's January 18, 1958, at the Montreal Forum. You lace up for the Boston Bruins, about to become the first Black player to skate in an NHL game, all while quietly managing a career-threatening injury few teammates know about.
evt-01-18-1958-willie-o-ree.prompt: How did Willie O'Ree manage to keep playing in the NHL despite being blind in one eye?

choices.text: Sued the Bruins for concealing his medical exam results
Retired from professional hockey shortly after being drafted
Publicly disclosed it and requested special accommodations from the league
Concealed the injury and adapted his positioning to compensate

evt-01-18-1958-willie-o-ree.butterflyEffect: O'Ree kept his blindness secret for years, compensating by favoring his good eye on the ice, and played 45 NHL games across two seasons. He was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2018, and the NHL now gives an annual Willie O'Ree Community Hero Award in his honor.

evt-01-18-1958-lumbee.scenario: It's January 18, 1958, near Maxton, North Carolina. You are a Lumbee man who has heard that Klan leader James "Catfish" Cole plans a rally at Hayes Pond to intimidate your community.
evt-01-18-1958-lumbee.prompt: What did the Lumbee do when Cole's Klan rally began that night?

choices.text: Petitioned the governor and waited for state troopers to intervene
Filed a federal lawsuit to have the rally permit revoked
Armed themselves and surrounded the rally, driving the Klan off
Organized a boycott of local white-owned businesses instead

evt-01-18-1958-lumbee.butterflyEffect: Hundreds of armed Lumbee surrounded the rally and opened fire into the air, shooting out the only light bulb and sending Klansmen fleeing in panic. Cole was later convicted of inciting a riot, and the event, remembered as the Battle of Hayes Pond, bolstered Lumbee pride and their decades-long push for full federal recognition.

evt-01-18-1983-international-olympic-com.scenario: It is 18 January 1983, thirty years after Jim Thorpe's death, and you watch IOC officials hand something to his surviving children in a ceremony meant to correct a seventy-year-old wrong.
evt-01-18-1983-international-olympic-com.prompt: What does the IOC formally present to Thorpe's family that day?

choices.text: Duplicate medals for his 1912 pentathlon and decathlon golds
An honorary Olympic Hall of Fame induction only
A written apology with no medals attached
A cash settlement in lieu of medals

evt-01-18-1983-international-olympic-com.butterflyEffect: Thorpe had been stripped of his 1912 golds after it emerged he'd once been paid to play minor-league baseball, breaching amateurism rules. The IOC issued replacement medals to his children in 1983, a landmark case that fed pressure to loosen the Olympics' strict amateur code in the decades that followed.

evt-01-18-1990-sting-operation.scenario: It's January 18, 1990, inside a Washington, D.C. hotel room rigged with hidden FBI cameras. You are Mayor Marion Barry, and a former companion cooperating with federal agents has just offered you crack cocaine.
evt-01-18-1990-sting-operation.prompt: What happened to Marion Barry after this FBI sting captured him on tape?

choices.text: He resigned before any arrest could be made
The charges were dismissed for entrapment
He was arrested and later convicted on a misdemeanor drug charge
He was acquitted at trial on all counts

evt-01-18-1990-sting-operation.butterflyEffect: Barry was arrested that night and later convicted of a single misdemeanor drug possession charge, serving six months in prison. Remarkably, he returned to politics and was reelected mayor of Washington, D.C. in 1994, illustrating both the reach of federal sting tactics and the resilience of his political base.

evt-01-18-2002-sierra-leone-civil-war.scenario: It's January 18, 2002, in Freetown. You watch President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah set fire to a pile of surrendered weapons, formally declaring Sierra Leone's brutal civil war at an end.
evt-01-18-2002-sierra-leone-civil-war.prompt: What did the peace process require former fighters to do to end the conflict for good?

choices.text: Receive blanket amnesty with no requirement to surrender weapons
Go into permanent exile in neighboring Liberia
Hold immediate elections before any disarmament occurred
Disarm and demobilize through a UN-backed reintegration program

evt-01-18-2002-sierra-leone-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Over 70,000 combatants went through the UN-backed disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration program. The RUF later reorganized as a political party, and the Special Court for Sierra Leone went on to prosecute war crimes, eventually convicting former Liberian president Charles Taylor for his role in fueling the conflict.

evt-01-18-2003-2003-canberra-bushfires.scenario: It is the afternoon of 18 January 2003 in outer Canberra. Bushfires that have burned in the hills for a week suddenly turn and race toward your suburb, with no formal evacuation order yet issued.
evt-01-18-2003-2003-canberra-bushfires.prompt: With flames closing in and no official alert given, what is the safest course of action?

choices.text: Stay put until an official evacuation order arrives
Drive toward the fire to warn firefighting crews
Remain to actively defend the house from the fire
Evacuate immediately rather than wait for a formal alert

evt-01-18-2003-2003-canberra-bushfires.butterflyEffect: Many residents evacuated on their own judgment as the fire front overwhelmed warning systems, while four people died and over 500 homes were destroyed in hours. A coronial inquiry into the disaster later drove major reforms to Australia's bushfire warning and emergency alert systems.

evt-01-18-2005-airbus-a380.scenario: You are an Airbus engineer in Toulouse on 18 January 2005, standing before dignitaries and cameras as the enormous double-deck A380 is rolled out for the world to see for the first time.
evt-01-18-2005-airbus-a380.prompt: What major milestone still lies ahead before passengers can fly on it?

choices.text: Nothing; it entered service directly from the rollout ceremony
Its first commercial passenger flight, scheduled for the following week
Certification, which had already been completed
Its maiden test flight, still months away

evt-01-18-2005-airbus-a380.butterflyEffect: The A380 did not fly for another three months, making its maiden flight on 27 April 1985... actually 2005, and entering commercial service with Singapore Airlines in October 2007. Despite the fanfare, high costs and shifting airline preferences led Airbus to end production in 2021.

evt-01-18-2008-euphronios-krater.scenario: You are an Italian cultural ministry official in Rome in January 2008, watching the ancient Euphronios Krater go on display after decades in the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.
evt-01-18-2008-euphronios-krater.prompt: What persuaded the Met to hand the vase back to Italy?

choices.text: A United Nations resolution ordered its return
Evidence that the vase had been illegally excavated and smuggled out of Italy
The Met simply offered it as a diplomatic gift
Italy paid the Met a large sum to buy it back

evt-01-18-2008-euphronios-krater.butterflyEffect: Italian investigators had traced the krater to an illicit 1971 excavation of an Etruscan tomb and its sale to the Met by dealer Robert Hecht. The case became a landmark in the fight against antiquities trafficking, pushing major museums worldwide to review provenance and return other looted objects to their countries of origin.

evt-01-18-2012-protests-against-sopa-and.scenario: It's January 18, 2012, and you run a small website. You log on to find Wikipedia's English site replaced by a black screen, and Reddit, Google, and thousands of other sites are joining a coordinated protest against two bills moving through Congress.
evt-01-18-2012-protests-against-sopa-and.prompt: What tactic did protesting websites use to pressure lawmakers on SOPA and PIPA?

choices.text: Blacken their homepages and urge visitors to flood Congress with calls and emails
File a coordinated class-action lawsuit against Congress
Quietly lobby only through paid Washington attorneys
Relocate their servers overseas to escape U.S. jurisdiction

evt-01-18-2012-protests-against-sopa-and.butterflyEffect: The blackout flooded congressional offices with calls and emails, and within days both SOPA and PIPA lost sponsors and were shelved. The protest became a landmark demonstration of coordinated online activism shaping legislation, influencing later fights over net neutrality and internet regulation.

evt-01-18-2023-2023-brovary-helicopter-c.scenario: It is the morning of 18 January 2023 in wartime Kyiv, and you watch a government helicopter carrying Ukraine's interior minister and senior officials descend low over the suburb of Brovary, heading toward a kindergarten.
evt-01-18-2023-2023-brovary-helicopter-c.prompt: What happens as the helicopter comes down?

choices.text: It crashes into a kindergarten, killing officials and people on the ground
It makes a safe emergency landing in a nearby field
It crashes in open countryside with no ground casualties
It is struck by a Russian missile before landing

evt-01-18-2023-2023-brovary-helicopter-c.butterflyEffect: The Super Puma crashed directly into the kindergarten, killing Interior Minister Monastyrsky, two other senior officials, and four people on the ground including a child, with dozens more injured. The loss of top security leadership mid-war strained Ukraine's governance and triggered reviews of officials flying near populated areas during the conflict.

evt-01-18-2026-2026-adamuz-rail-disaster.scenario: It is 18 January 2026, and you are part of the investigation team called to a stretch of the Madrid–Seville high-speed line near Adamuz, Córdoba, where two trains have collided with devastating losses.
evt-01-18-2026-2026-adamuz-rail-disaster.prompt: What does the investigation determine actually caused the derailment?

choices.text: Deliberate sabotage of the line
A failure of the track's signalling system
Excessive speed by the lead train's driver
A poorly executed weld from an improper repair kit on the rail

evt-01-18-2026-2026-adamuz-rail-disaster.butterflyEffect: Investigators traced the rupture to a poor weld from an improperly used repair kit, worsened by weak data records, inexperienced inspectors, and overly conservative alert programming. The line closed for a month of repairs and testing before reopening, and the disaster became Spain's worst rail accident since 2013, prompting scrutiny of maintenance contracting.

evt-01-19-1419-hundred-years-war.scenario: It is January 1419, and you are a citizen of Rouen who has endured a months-long siege by Henry V's army, food gone and disease spreading through the city.
evt-01-19-1419-hundred-years-war.prompt: What do Rouen's defenders finally decide to do?

choices.text: Hold out indefinitely for a Burgundian relief army
Break out and force a decisive pitched battle
Negotiate surrender terms and open the gates to English occupation
Burn the city rather than let it fall

evt-01-19-1419-hundred-years-war.butterflyEffect: The city surrendered on January 19, 1419, giving Henry V control of Normandy and cementing England's strongest position of the entire war. This success paved the way for the 1420 Treaty of Troyes, which made Henry heir to the French throne — a triumph later undone by Joan of Arc's campaigns.

evt-01-19-1511-war-of-the-league-of-camb.scenario: It is January 1511, and you serve in the personal army of Pope Julius II, who has ridden to the walls of Mirandola himself, armored and directing the bombardment in the freezing cold.
evt-01-19-1511-war-of-the-league-of-camb.prompt: What did the warrior-pope's presence at the siege achieve?

choices.text: The siege was abandoned after his capture
Venice intervened to save the city
The Emperor forced a truce before the walls fell
The fortress fell to the papal army under his direct command

evt-01-19-1511-war-of-the-league-of-camb.butterflyEffect: Mirandola surrendered on 20 January 1511, one of the rare moments a reigning pope personally led troops into battle. The victory boosted Julius's prestige, but the wider war ground on for years, later drawing England and Spain into the conflict against France.

evt-01-19-1795-batavian-republic.scenario: It's 19 January 1795 in Amsterdam. Stadtholder William V fled to England only yesterday, French revolutionary troops occupy the country, and Dutch Patriots are meeting to decide what should replace the old Republic.
evt-01-19-1795-batavian-republic.prompt: What form of state do the Patriots proclaim?

choices.text: A sister republic aligned with revolutionary France, the Batavian Republic
Immediate annexation as a province of France
A restored hereditary monarchy under a new prince
A neutral confederation independent of French influence

evt-01-19-1795-batavian-republic.butterflyEffect: The Batavian Republic became a client state of revolutionary France, supplying troops and money to Napoleon's wars. It lasted just over a decade before Napoleon replaced it with the Kingdom of Holland under his brother Louis in 1806, and later annexed the Netherlands outright into France in 1810.

evt-01-19-1915-world-war-i.scenario: It's the night of 19 January 1915, and you are a special constable patrolling the blacked-out streets of Great Yarmouth. Overhead, an unfamiliar engine drones — German airships have crossed the North Sea to bomb Britain for the first time.
evt-01-19-1915-world-war-i.prompt: What did this first Zeppelin raid change for British home defence?

choices.text: Britain immediately built a fleet of long-range bombers to retaliate
The Royal Navy abandoned all coastal patrols in response
Britain organized anti-aircraft guns, searchlights, and blackout rules for civilian towns
Britain evacuated every East Coast town within a week

evt-01-19-1915-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The raid on Great Yarmouth and King's Lynn killed several civilians and opened a sustained Zeppelin bombing campaign against Britain. It forced the country to build home air defences — anti-aircraft batteries, searchlights, and blackout rules — turning British civilians into wartime targets for the first time and shaping air-defense doctrine for decades after.

evt-01-19-1920-american-civil-liberties-.scenario: It's January 1920 in a small New York office, and you're one of the founders meeting to organize a new national body from the wartime National Civil Liberties Bureau. Anti-radical raids and wartime speech prosecutions have just filled American jails with dissenters.
evt-01-19-1920-american-civil-liberties-.prompt: What core mission did the founders choose for the new ACLU?

choices.text: Lobby Congress to write new criminal statutes
Defend free speech and conscientious objectors regardless of politics
Represent only labor unions during strikes
Focus exclusively on women's suffrage

evt-01-19-1920-american-civil-liberties-.butterflyEffect: Roger Baldwin and his colleagues built the ACLU on defending unpopular speech across the political spectrum, a stance tested repeatedly in cases like the Scopes trial. It grew into one of the most litigious civil-rights organizations in American history.

evt-01-19-1972-l-aurore-newspaper-founde.scenario: You are a reporter at L'Aurore in January 1972, holding evidence that the wartime Gestapo chief of Lyon, Klaus Barbie, is living openly in Bolivia under a false name. Your editor wants to run the story immediately.
evt-01-19-1972-l-aurore-newspaper-founde.prompt: What did publishing Barbie's location set in motion?

choices.text: No action for another generation
A decades-long extradition campaign that eventually brought him to trial in France
A swift Bolivian deportation that same year
His immediate arrest by French police within days

evt-01-19-1972-l-aurore-newspaper-founde.butterflyEffect: The exposure launched a campaign led by Serge and Beate Klarsfeld that finally succeeded when Bolivia extradited Barbie in 1983. He stood trial in Lyon in 1987 for crimes against humanity, was convicted, and died in prison in 1991.

evt-01-19-1977-iva-toguri-d-aquino.scenario: It is President Gerald Ford's final day in office. On his desk sits the case of Iva Toguri D'Aquino, convicted in 1949 of wartime treason for allegedly being the radio broadcaster 'Tokyo Rose,' though new evidence suggests key witnesses lied under pressure.
evt-01-19-1977-iva-toguri-d-aquino.prompt: What does Ford do with her case before leaving office?

choices.text: He grants her a full pardon
He orders a new trial before leaving office
He denies clemency and upholds her conviction
He commutes her sentence but leaves the conviction intact

evt-01-19-1977-iva-toguri-d-aquino.butterflyEffect: Ford granted her a full and unconditional pardon on January 19, 1977, his last day as president, after journalists uncovered that prosecution witnesses had been coerced by government agents into false testimony. The pardon restored her citizenship and is now cited as a landmark case of wartime hysteria producing a wrongful conviction.

evt-01-19-1978-volkswagen-beetle.scenario: It is 19 January 1978, and you work the line at Volkswagen's Emden plant in West Germany. The last Beetle built in Germany is rolling toward the door, and reporters gathered outside want to know if this is the end of the road for the car.
evt-01-19-1978-volkswagen-beetle.prompt: What actually happens to Beetle production after this day?

choices.text: VW shifts all remaining Beetle production to the United States
VW launches a limited-edition retro Beetle that same year
Production stops worldwide, ending the Beetle for good
Production continues at Volkswagen plants in Mexico and Brazil

evt-01-19-1978-volkswagen-beetle.butterflyEffect: German production of the original Beetle ended that day, but assembly continued at Volkswagen plants in Mexico and Brazil, keeping the classic design alive for another quarter century. The very last original Beetle rolled off the line in Puebla, Mexico, in 2003, and the shape returned once more in 1998 as VW's retro-styled New Beetle.

evt-01-19-1981-iran-hostage-crisis.scenario: It is January 19, 1981, and you are one of 52 Americans held inside the former U.S. embassy compound in Tehran for over 14 months. Word reaches your captors that negotiators have just signed an agreement in Algiers.
evt-01-19-1981-iran-hostage-crisis.prompt: What actually happens next for you and the other hostages?

choices.text: You are transferred to a UN facility in Geneva for further talks
You are put on trial in Iran before being freed
You are held for several more months while Congress debates ratification
You are released the next day, after 444 days in captivity

evt-01-19-1981-iran-hostage-crisis.butterflyEffect: You are released the next morning, January 20, 1981 — the very hour Ronald Reagan is sworn in as president, ending the crisis exactly as Carter's term expires. The Algiers Accords unfroze billions in Iranian assets but left deep U.S.-Iran hostility that shapes Middle East policy for decades.

evt-01-19-1990-exodus-of-kashmiri-hindus.scenario: It is January 1990 in Srinagar. Loudspeakers from mosques and militant groups warn Hindu families to leave the Kashmir Valley within days, and your neighbors are already loading trucks with whatever they can carry.
evt-01-19-1990-exodus-of-kashmiri-hindus.prompt: What did most Kashmiri Pandit families decide to do in these weeks?

choices.text: Negotiate directly with the militants to remain
Stay and join the militant groups
Flee to Jammu and other parts of India
Wait for immediate United Nations intervention

evt-01-19-1990-exodus-of-kashmiri-hindus.butterflyEffect: Tens of thousands fled within months, becoming refugees within their own country. Their displacement remains unresolved decades later, with most Pandits never returning permanently to the Valley, reshaping Kashmir's religious and political landscape ever since.

evt-01-19-1991-gulf-war.scenario: Sirens wail over Tel Aviv as a second Iraqi Scud missile streaks toward Israel. American and Israeli commanders must decide how to respond without shattering the fragile coalition against Saddam Hussein.
evt-01-19-1991-gulf-war.prompt: How do coalition forces respond to protect Israel from the Scud attacks?

choices.text: US Patriot missile batteries are deployed to intercept the Scuds
Israel launches immediate retaliatory airstrikes on Baghdad
All of Tel Aviv is ordered to evacuate
The Soviet Union is asked to mediate a ceasefire

evt-01-19-1991-gulf-war.butterflyEffect: The US rushed Patriot missile batteries and crews to Israel to intercept incoming Scuds, persuading Israel to hold back from retaliatory strikes on Iraq. That restraint kept Arab coalition members from having to choose between the US-led alliance and fellow Arab state Iraq, preserving the coalition through the war's end.

evt-01-19-1996-north-cape-oil-spill.scenario: It's 19 January 1996, and a nor'easter is battering the Rhode Island coast. The tug Scandia catches fire, and with its barge North Cape still in tow, both vessels run aground on Moonstone Beach, spilling home heating oil into Block Island Sound.
evt-01-19-1996-north-cape-oil-spill.prompt: What actually followed the spill for the sound's fisheries?

choices.text: Congress banned all oil barges from New England waters
Officials closed roughly 250 square miles of the sound to fishing
The Coast Guard reopened the sound to fishing within 24 hours
The spill had no measurable effect on local fishing

evt-01-19-1996-north-cape-oil-spill.butterflyEffect: The spilled oil killed hundreds of thousands of lobsters and other marine life and fouled the nearby Trustom Pond National Wildlife Refuge, prompting officials to close roughly 250 square miles of the sound to fishing. The disaster became a landmark case in U.S. natural resource damage law, shaping how spill responders later calculated compensation for ecological harm.

evt-01-19-1997-yasser-arafat.scenario: It is 19 January 1997, and you stand in the crowded streets of Hebron as Yasser Arafat's motorcade approaches. Israeli troops have just withdrawn from most of the city under a new accord, and thousands press forward to greet him for the first time in over three decades.
evt-01-19-1997-yasser-arafat.prompt: What agreement made Arafat's return to Hebron possible?

choices.text: The Wye River Memorandum
The original Oslo I Accords
The Camp David Accords
The Hebron Protocol

evt-01-19-1997-yasser-arafat.butterflyEffect: The Hebron Protocol, signed by Arafat and Netanyahu weeks earlier, divided the city into Palestinian-controlled H1 and Israeli-controlled H2 to protect Jewish settlers there. It was one of the last substantive implementations of the Oslo process, and the divided city remains a flashpoint symbolizing the unfinished peace effort.

evt-01-19-2007-henry-cookson.scenario: It's 19 January 2007, and after weeks hauling sledges behind kites across the Antarctic plateau, your four-man team spots something unexpected rising from the snow at the Pole of Inaccessibility.
evt-01-19-2007-henry-cookson.prompt: What Soviet-era marker did the team find waiting for them?

choices.text: A bust of Lenin atop an abandoned research station
An abandoned weather station still intact
A buried time capsule
A Soviet flag frozen upright in the ice

evt-01-19-2007-henry-cookson.butterflyEffect: The bust of Lenin was left by a 1958 Soviet expedition that first established the pole; the only later visit before 2007 was in 1965, by plane and tracked vehicle. Cookson's team became the first to reach the pole entirely under human and wind power.

evt-01-19-2024-jaxa.scenario: You are a flight controller at JAXA's mission control, watching telemetry from the SLIM lander as it attempts Japan's first-ever soft landing on the Moon, aiming for pinpoint accuracy within 100 meters of its target.
evt-01-19-2024-jaxa.prompt: What happens to the SLIM lander immediately after touchdown?

choices.text: It crashes on the surface and is destroyed
It becomes stranded in permanent lunar orbit
Its engines fail to fire and it misses the Moon entirely
It lands successfully but tips over, temporarily losing solar power

evt-01-19-2024-jaxa.butterflyEffect: SLIM touched down but tipped onto its side, leaving its solar panels facing the wrong way and cutting power almost immediately. Weeks later, as the sun's angle shifted, the panels caught light and SLIM revived, confirming it had landed within about 55 meters of its target—the most precise lunar landing achieved to date, proving pinpoint-landing technology for future missions.

evt-01-20-1265-simon-de-montfort-6th-ear.scenario: You are a knight summoned to the Palace of Westminster on 20 January 1265 by Simon de Montfort, joining burgesses from English towns and barons at a great council convened while King Henry III remains sidelined.
evt-01-20-1265-simon-de-montfort-6th-ear.prompt: What made this assembly historically significant?

choices.text: It voted to abolish the English monarchy entirely
It consisted only of bishops and abbots
It formally crowned Simon de Montfort as king
It was the first English parliament to include elected town representatives

evt-01-20-1265-simon-de-montfort-6th-ear.butterflyEffect: This gathering, remembered as "Montfort's Parliament," was the first to include elected representatives from towns alongside nobles and clergy. De Montfort was killed at Evesham later that year, but the practice of summoning knights and burgesses endured under Edward I, becoming a cornerstone of the developing English Parliament.

evt-01-20-1356-edward-balliol.scenario: You are a Scottish nobleman present at Roxburgh on 20 January 1356 as the aging Edward Balliol meets Edward III of England to settle his long-disputed claim to the Scottish crown.
evt-01-20-1356-edward-balliol.prompt: What does Balliol do with his claim to the Scottish throne?

choices.text: He renounces his claim directly to David II Bruce
He refuses to give up his claim and continues fighting
He passes his claim on to his nephew to continue the fight
He surrenders his claim to Edward III in return for an English pension

evt-01-20-1356-edward-balliol.butterflyEffect: Balliol resigned his claim to Edward III in exchange for an English pension, effectively ending his rival kingship. This left Edward III holding a symbolic claim to Scottish sovereignty that England would invoke in future conflicts, while David II Bruce remained the Scots' recognized king.

evt-01-20-1726-johann-sebastian-bach.scenario: It is Sunday, 20 January 1726, the second Sunday after Epiphany, and you are seated in a Leipzig church as Cantor Johann Sebastian Bach directs the choir and orchestra through a brand-new cantata he composed for this very service.
evt-01-20-1726-johann-sebastian-bach.prompt: What should you expect from Bach's cantata for today's service?

choices.text: A revival of a cantata Bach had written decades earlier in Weimar
An entirely instrumental concerto with no vocal parts
A performance of an opera commissioned by the Leipzig town council
A newly composed work tied to the Gospel reading for that Sunday

evt-01-20-1726-johann-sebastian-bach.butterflyEffect: The cantata, 'Meine Seufzer, meine Tränen' (BWV 13), was one of dozens Bach wrote to a strict weekly schedule for Leipzig's churches during his tenure as cantor. Largely unheard outside Leipzig in his lifetime, it survived to be rediscovered during the 19th-century Bach Revival that restored his reputation as a towering figure of Western music.

evt-01-20-1942-the-holocaust.scenario: It is 20 January 1942, and you are a state secretary summoned to a villa on the Wannsee outside Berlin, where Reinhard Heydrich has gathered senior officials from across the Nazi bureaucracy to discuss the fate of Europe's Jewish population.
evt-01-20-1942-the-holocaust.prompt: What is the meeting actually convened to coordinate?

choices.text: Rationing of food supplies for German civilians
A plan to resettle Jews on the island of Madagascar
Deportation logistics for moving Jews to killing centers in the East
The treatment of captured Soviet prisoners of war

evt-01-20-1942-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: The Wannsee Conference coordinated the machinery of different ministries and agencies behind the mass deportation of Jews to killing centers in occupied Poland, formalizing bureaucratic cooperation in what became the systematic murder of six million people. The minutes, discovered after the war, became key evidence at the Nuremberg trials of the deliberate, coordinated nature of the genocide.

evt-01-20-1968-houston-cougars-men-s-bas.scenario: It is January 20, 1968, inside the packed Astrodome, and you are on the court for the Houston Cougars in the final seconds against Lew Alcindor's top-ranked UCLA Bruins, the score razor-thin.
evt-01-20-1968-houston-cougars-men-s-bas.prompt: What does Elvin Hayes do in the closing seconds to seal Houston's win?

choices.text: Sinks two free throws to put Houston ahead for good
Blocks Alcindor's final shot at the buzzer
Fouls out trying to stop UCLA's last possession
Calls a timeout to set up a final play

evt-01-20-1968-houston-cougars-men-s-bas.butterflyEffect: Hayes sank two free throws to give Houston a 71-69 victory, ending UCLA's 47-game winning streak. The nationally televised 'Game of the Century' proved college basketball could draw huge arena and TV audiences, paving the way for the sport's modern broadcast era and the eventual expansion of the NCAA Tournament.

evt-01-20-1969-amanullah-asaduzzaman.scenario: It is 20 January 1969 in Dhaka, and you are a student marching in defiance of curfew against President Ayub Khan's government, as police move to break up the crowd by force.
evt-01-20-1969-amanullah-asaduzzaman.prompt: What effect did the killing of student activist Amanullah Asaduzzaman that day have on the movement?

choices.text: It was barely noticed outside Dhaka and had no lasting effect
It turned the protest into a mass uprising against the Ayub Khan regime
It led Ayub Khan to immediately grant the students' demands
It caused the student movement to collapse in fear of further violence

evt-01-20-1969-amanullah-asaduzzaman.butterflyEffect: His death, along with two other student martyrs, transformed a student demonstration into a broader mass upsurge against Ayub Khan across East Pakistan. That momentum helped topple Ayub Khan by March 1969 and fed directly into the political awakening that led to the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War; Bangladesh posthumously honored him in 2018.

evt-01-20-1981-ronald-reagan.scenario: It is January 20, 1981, and as Ronald Reagan raises his hand to take the presidential oath, word reaches the crowd of something happening simultaneously thousands of miles away in Tehran.
evt-01-20-1981-ronald-reagan.prompt: What happens roughly twenty minutes after Reagan is sworn in?

choices.text: The Iranian government formally apologizes to the United States
Sanctions on Iran are permanently lifted
A new US embassy opens in Tehran
The 52 American hostages held in Iran are released

evt-01-20-1981-ronald-reagan.butterflyEffect: The 52 American hostages held in Tehran for 444 days were released just after Reagan's inauguration, ending the crisis that had dominated and doomed much of Jimmy Carter's presidency. The timing let Reagan open his term on a note of national relief, shaping the confident, assertive tone of his early foreign policy.

evt-01-20-1986-leabua-jonathan.scenario: It is 20 January 1986 in Maseru, Lesotho. Radio reports say army units under Major General Justin Lekhanya have surrounded government buildings, and Prime Minister Leabua Jonathan's twenty-year rule is about to end.
evt-01-20-1986-leabua-jonathan.prompt: What actually followed the army's move against Jonathan?

choices.text: Jonathan was overthrown in a bloodless military coup
Jonathan fled into exile and formed a government-in-exile
South African troops intervened to restore Jonathan to power
Jonathan called snap elections and won a new term

evt-01-20-1986-leabua-jonathan.butterflyEffect: Lekhanya's junta suspended the constitution and ruled through a Military Council, with King Moshoeshoe II given expanded ceremonial powers. Jonathan's fall ended his two-decade domination of Lesotho politics and opened years of rivalry between the military and the monarchy before multiparty elections returned in the 1990s.

evt-01-20-1990-red-army.scenario: It is the night of 19 to 20 January 1990 in Baku, and word spreads that Soviet troops are moving on the city to crush the Azerbaijani independence movement. You and your neighbors have hours before the columns arrive.
evt-01-20-1990-red-army.prompt: What do many Baku residents do to try to slow the Soviet advance?

choices.text: Evacuate the entire city by sea overnight
Build barricades of buses and trucks across the main roads into the city
Declare a general strike but leave the roads open
Appeal directly to the United Nations Security Council for troops

evt-01-20-1990-red-army.butterflyEffect: Red Army troops stormed through barricades on what became known as Black January, killing scores of civilians. Rather than crushing the independence movement, the crackdown discredited Soviet rule in Azerbaijan and hardened popular support for the Azerbaijan Popular Front, feeding the momentum that led to Azerbaijani independence in 1991.

evt-01-20-1990-black-january.scenario: It is the night of 19–20 January 1990 in Baku. Soviet tanks and troops move into the city to crush anti-Soviet and anti-Armenian unrest, and a curfew has just been declared over the radio.
evt-01-20-1990-black-january.prompt: What did the Soviet crackdown in Baku set in motion?

choices.text: It led to immediate independence being granted to Azerbaijan
It shattered public trust in Moscow and accelerated Azerbaijan's independence movement
It permanently restored Communist Party control over Azerbaijan
It reunited Azerbaijan and Armenia under a single Soviet republic

evt-01-20-1990-black-january.butterflyEffect: Scores of civilians were killed as troops fired into crowds, and the massacre became known as Black January. Rather than crushing nationalist sentiment, it discredited the Communist Party in Azerbaijan and hardened support for independence, which Azerbaijan declared the following year.

evt-01-20-1991-sudan.scenario: You are a civil servant in Khartoum as the government announces that Islamic law will now govern the entire country, including the largely non-Muslim, non-Arab south already at war with the north.
evt-01-20-1991-sudan.prompt: What follows from imposing Islamic law across all of Sudan?

choices.text: The international community reacts with no response at all
It brings a swift end to peace negotiations in Sudan's favor
It intensifies the civil war between north and south Sudan
Southern provinces are granted immediate exemption

evt-01-20-1991-sudan.butterflyEffect: The move deepened the Second Sudanese Civil War by alienating southern Sudanese who were Christian, animist, and non-Arab, confirming their fears of forced Islamization and marginalization. The conflict dragged on for over a decade more, until a 2005 peace agreement eventually paved the way for South Sudan's independence in 2011.

evt-01-20-2001-president-of-the-philippi.scenario: You stand among the crowds massed at the EDSA shrine in Manila in January 2001, as prosecutors walk out of President Joseph Estrada's impeachment trial over a vote to block key evidence and the Supreme Court weighs in on who holds power.
evt-01-20-2001-president-of-the-philippi.prompt: What happened to end Estrada's presidency in the days that followed?

choices.text: The military restored Estrada to full power
Congress formally voted to impeach and remove him
Estrada won a snap election and retained the presidency
The Supreme Court declared the presidency vacant and swore in Vice President Arroyo

evt-01-20-2001-president-of-the-philippi.butterflyEffect: The Supreme Court declared the presidency vacant, and Vice President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo was sworn in as his successor. Estrada was later convicted of plunder in 2007 but was pardoned, and the episode, known as EDSA II, set a precedent for extra-constitutional removal of presidents through mass mobilization rather than formal impeachment.

evt-01-20-2009-2008-2011-icelandic-finan.scenario: It is January 2009 and you stand outside the Althingi in Reykjavík, banging a pot with a wooden spoon alongside thousands of furious Icelanders after the krona collapsed and the banks defaulted.
evt-01-20-2009-2008-2011-icelandic-finan.prompt: What is the protesters' central demand as the crowds return night after night?

choices.text: Iceland's withdrawal from NATO
Iceland's immediate adoption of the euro
A bailout package for the three failed banks
The resignation of the government and new elections

evt-01-20-2009-2008-2011-icelandic-finan.butterflyEffect: The 'Kitchenware Revolution' forced the resignation of Prime Minister Geir Haarde's government within weeks. Iceland held early elections that brought Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir to power as the country's first female prime minister, and Iceland pursued an unusual path of letting banks fail and prosecuting bankers rather than bailing out the financial sector.

evt-01-20-2009-first-inauguration-of-bar.scenario: It is January 20, 2009, and you stand packed among the record crowd on the National Mall as Chief Justice John Roberts steps forward to administer the oath of office to Barack Obama.
evt-01-20-2009-first-inauguration-of-bar.prompt: What actually happens as Roberts leads Obama through the oath?

choices.text: Roberts misorders the words, so the oath is retaken privately the next day
Obama forgets a line and has to be prompted
The oath is delayed by a security scare
The Bible used belongs to George Washington and is dropped

evt-01-20-2009-first-inauguration-of-bar.butterflyEffect: Roberts transposed a word in the oath, and out of an abundance of caution the two men repeated it privately in the White House the next evening. The moment became a minor footnote to a day otherwise remembered for record attendance and the historic inauguration of the first African-American president.

evt-01-20-2009-iceland.scenario: You stand outside Iceland's parliament in Reykjavik, banging a pot with a wooden spoon alongside thousands of others, furious after the banking collapse wiped out savings and jobs across the country.
evt-01-20-2009-iceland.prompt: What does the sustained pressure of these protests force the government to do?

choices.text: Prime Minister Geir Haarde's government resigns
The central bank governor is installed as president
The government declares martial law
Iceland immediately joins the European Union

evt-01-20-2009-iceland.butterflyEffect: Prime Minister Geir Haarde's coalition government collapsed and announced early elections, unable to withstand the 'Kitchenware Revolution.' The resulting leftist government, led by Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir, let failing banks go bankrupt rather than bailing them out and imposed capital controls, a path many economists later credited with Iceland's comparatively fast recovery.

evt-01-20-2018-taliban.scenario: It is the evening of 20 January 2018, and you are a guest at Kabul's Hotel Inter-Continental when gunfire erupts in the corridors. Taliban attackers have entered the building and are moving floor to floor, and you must decide how to survive the night.
evt-01-20-2018-taliban.prompt: What should you do as the siege unfolds around you?

choices.text: Run into the corridors immediately to find the nearest exit stairwell
Barricade the room, stay low, and wait for security forces to clear each floor
Signal to attackers that you are a civilian guest and unarmed
Climb to the roof and wait for a helicopter evacuation

evt-01-20-2018-taliban.butterflyEffect: The attackers held the hotel for hours, killing more than twenty people including several foreign nationals, before Afghan special forces backed by NATO cleared the building. The assault underscored the Taliban's ability to strike high-profile targets in the capital even as peace talks were being discussed, hardening skepticism about negotiating a settlement.

evt-01-20-2018-2018-inter-continental-ho.scenario: It is the night of 20 January 2018 and you are a security guard on duty at the Inter-Continental Hotel in Kabul when gunmen storm the building and the siege stretches into its ninth hour.
evt-01-20-2018-2018-inter-continental-ho.prompt: What finally brought the 12-hour siege to an end?

choices.text: The gunmen escaped through a service tunnel before troops arrived
Taliban negotiators secured a ceasefire and the gunmen surrendered
NATO airstrikes leveled the building to end the standoff
Afghan special forces stormed the hotel floor by floor and killed the gunmen

evt-01-20-2018-2018-inter-continental-ho.butterflyEffect: Afghan special forces methodically cleared the hotel floor by floor and killed the attackers; 40 people, including 14 foreigners, died. The Taliban claimed responsibility, and the attack became part of a wave of high-profile Kabul strikes in early 2018 that exposed how far insurgents could reach into the fortified capital, hardening security debates around the stalled peace process.

evt-01-20-2018-syrian-civil-war.scenario: It is 20 January 2018, and you command a unit of Kurdish YPG fighters holding positions around Afrin in northern Syria when word arrives that Turkey has just announced a cross-border military operation aimed directly at your enclave.
evt-01-20-2018-syrian-civil-war.prompt: What does Turkey's newly announced offensive actually target?

choices.text: Assad regime positions near Damascus
ISIS remnants along the Iraqi border
Kurdish YPG-held territory around Afrin in northern Syria
Rebel-held districts of eastern Aleppo

evt-01-20-2018-syrian-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The operation, later named Olive Branch, saw Turkish forces and allied Syrian factions push into Afrin against the Kurdish YPG, capturing the city by March 2018 and displacing large numbers of its Kurdish residents. Because the US had armed and partnered with the YPG against ISIS, the offensive strained relations between Washington and Ankara for years afterward.

evt-01-21-763-abbasid-caliphate.scenario: It's January 763. You march with the Abbasid army under Isa ibn Musa, closing in on the rebel force of Ibrahim ibn Abdullah at Bakhamra near Kufa, the last stand of the Alid revolt against Caliph al-Mansur.
evt-01-21-763-abbasid-caliphate.prompt: What happened to the rebel leader Ibrahim after the battle at Bakhamra?

choices.text: He escaped and continued the rebellion for another decade
He was captured alive and later pardoned by al-Mansur
He was mortally wounded in battle and died soon after, ending the revolt
He negotiated a truce making him governor of Basra

evt-01-21-763-abbasid-caliphate.butterflyEffect: Ibrahim was mortally wounded in the fighting and died soon after, ending the Alid revolt his brother Muhammad al-Nafs al-Zakiyya had launched in Medina the previous year. With the rebellion crushed, Caliph al-Mansur consolidated Abbasid control and pressed ahead with founding Baghdad as his new capital.

evt-01-21-1326-edward-ii.scenario: It's January 21, 1326, and you are Adam de Brome, King Edward II's almoner, seeking royal backing for a small house of scholars you've founded near Oxford's St Mary's church.
evt-01-21-1326-edward-ii.prompt: What does the king's charter grant you?

choices.text: Permission to found a hospital for the poor
A monopoly on Oxford's wool trade
A royal charter confirming your foundation as a house of scholars at Oxford
Land to build a new cathedral

evt-01-21-1326-edward-ii.butterflyEffect: Edward II's charter confirmed de Brome's foundation of a house of scholars dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary. It became the nucleus of Oriel College, chartered fully a few years later and still one of Oxford's oldest colleges today.

evt-01-21-1793-french-revolution.scenario: It is 21 January 1793 in Paris. The National Convention has just found Louis XVI guilty of high treason, and a crowd gathers at the Place de la Révolution awaiting the sentence to be carried out.
evt-01-21-1793-french-revolution.prompt: What did the Convention do with the condemned king that day?

choices.text: They exiled him to the French colonies
They executed him by guillotine
They pardoned him in exchange for his abdication
They imprisoned him for life in the Bastille

evt-01-21-1793-french-revolution.butterflyEffect: Louis XVI was executed by guillotine that same day, a shock that radicalized the Revolution and shattered any hope of reconciliation with Europe's monarchies. The killing hardened the resolve of the First Coalition against France and helped push the Convention toward the Terror that followed.

evt-01-21-1931-isaac-isaacs.scenario: It is 1930, and you are Prime Minister James Scullin, determined to break tradition by recommending an Australian-born jurist for the vice-regal post, even as King George V voices strong reservations about the choice.
evt-01-21-1931-isaac-isaacs.prompt: What did Scullin do about the King's objections to his nominee?

choices.text: He resigned rather than confront the Crown
He withdrew the nomination and proposed a British peer instead
He called a referendum to let voters decide
He insisted on his choice, forcing the King to relent

evt-01-21-1931-isaac-isaacs.butterflyEffect: Scullin held firm, and Isaac Isaacs was sworn in as the first Australian-born governor-general on 21 January 1931. The episode set a precedent for Australian self-determination in choosing its own representative, strengthening the path toward full Dominion equality later codified in the Statute of Westminster.

evt-01-21-1951-mount-lamington.scenario: It is mid-January 1951, and you administer the district around Higaturu, Papua New Guinea. For days the forested peak known locally as a mountain, not a volcano, has been rumbling and dusting the valley with ash.
evt-01-21-1951-mount-lamington.prompt: How did colonial administrators respond to the tremors and ash in the days before the eruption?

choices.text: They ordered engineers to vent the crater with explosives
They flew in Australian geologists who declared the mountain extinct
They judged it non-threatening and did not order evacuation
They evacuated the entire district immediately

evt-01-21-1951-mount-lamington.butterflyEffect: Officials judged the activity minor and did not order evacuation, since Lamington had no recorded history of eruption. On 21 January it exploded catastrophically, killing roughly 3,000 people with little warning, a disaster that led directly to the creation of a dedicated volcanological observatory to monitor Papua New Guinea's volcanoes.

evt-01-21-1968-boeing-b-52-stratofortres.scenario: It's January 21, 1968. You're aboard a B-52 bomber flying an airborne nuclear alert mission near Thule Air Base in Greenland, four hydrogen bombs in the bay, when a fire breaks out in the cabin and the crew scrambles to save the aircraft.
evt-01-21-1968-boeing-b-52-stratofortres.prompt: What happened when the burning B-52 came down near Thule?

choices.text: The crew jettisoned the bombs safely into the ocean before impact
The plane crashed onto sea ice, rupturing the weapons and scattering radioactive material
The crew safely landed the bomber at Thule Air Base
The aircraft exploded in midair, destroying the warheads completely

evt-01-21-1968-boeing-b-52-stratofortres.butterflyEffect: The bomber crashed onto sea ice, and the conventional explosives in the weapons detonated on impact, rupturing the bombs and scattering plutonium contamination across the ice without a nuclear explosion. The massive cleanup, Project Crested Ice, and lingering doubts about a missing weapon pushed the U.S. to end airborne nuclear alert flights entirely.

evt-01-21-1968-vietnam-war.scenario: It's January 21, 1968, and North Vietnamese artillery and infantry begin a massive assault on the U.S. Marine base at Khe Sanh, just south of the DMZ. You command the besieged garrison, cut off from ground resupply.
evt-01-21-1968-vietnam-war.prompt: How does the U.S. military respond to keep the base from falling?

choices.text: Launch a full counteroffensive northward into Laos
Immediately evacuate all Marines by helicopter
Negotiate a local ceasefire with North Vietnamese commanders
Hold the base and resupply it entirely by air under heavy bombardment

evt-01-21-1968-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: U.S. forces held Khe Sanh through a 77-day siege, resupplied by air and backed by history's heaviest tactical bombing campaign. The siege proved a diversion: while attention focused there, North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces launched the surprise Tet Offensive elsewhere, reshaping American public opinion on the war.

evt-01-21-1976-concorde.scenario: It's January 21, 1976, and you're boarding one of the first-ever commercial supersonic flights, as British Airways and Air France simultaneously launch scheduled Concorde service from London and Paris.
evt-01-21-1976-concorde.prompt: Where are these historic first commercial Concorde flights headed?

choices.text: New York and Washington
Bahrain and Rio de Janeiro
Tokyo and Sydney
Los Angeles and Mexico City

evt-01-21-1976-concorde.butterflyEffect: British Airways flew London–Bahrain while Air France flew Paris–Rio de Janeiro, launching 27 years of supersonic passenger service. Noise and sonic-boom restrictions later barred routes like New York until 1977, and the type was retired in 2003 after the 2000 Paris crash and rising costs.

evt-01-21-1986-shanty-town.scenario: It's before dawn on January 21, 1986, on the Dartmouth College Green. A cluster of shanties built by student anti-apartheid activists to pressure the college into divestment has stood for weeks — until a group of conservative students arrives with sledgehammers to tear them down before classes begin.
evt-01-21-1986-shanty-town.prompt: What followed the destruction of the shanty town by conservative students?

choices.text: The college immediately divested from South Africa
Local police charged the conservative students with hate crimes
The students involved faced disciplinary hearings and it became a national free-speech controversy
The shanty town was quietly rebuilt and the incident drew no attention

evt-01-21-1986-shanty-town.butterflyEffect: The students, several tied to the Dartmouth Review, faced college disciplinary hearings and suspensions, but the incident exploded into a national controversy over free speech, campus activism, and political correctness. It became a touchstone case cited for years in America's ongoing culture-war debates over college politics.

evt-01-21-1997-united-states-house-of-re.scenario: It's January 21, 1997, and you're a member of the U.S. House of Representatives voting on a bipartisan ethics committee's recommendation against Speaker Newt Gingrich, who admitted to using tax-exempt funds for political purposes and giving investigators inaccurate information.
evt-01-21-1997-united-states-house-of-re.prompt: How does the House vote on disciplining the Speaker?

choices.text: Reprimand him and require him to pay $300,000 in costs
Censure him and strip his committee assignments
Acquit him of all charges
Expel him from the House

evt-01-21-1997-united-states-house-of-re.butterflyEffect: The House voted 395–28 to reprimand Gingrich, the first Speaker disciplined this way, and he paid a $300,000 penalty. The episode weakened his standing, and after Republican losses in the 1998 midterms he resigned as Speaker.

evt-01-21-2000-ecuador.scenario: It's January 21, 2000, in Quito. Indigenous organizers from CONAIE, joined by disaffected army officers, have just stormed and occupied the National Congress building, demanding the removal of President Jamil Mahuad amid economic collapse.
evt-01-21-2000-ecuador.prompt: What happened next in Ecuador's political crisis?

choices.text: Mahuad was ousted, and military commanders installed Vice President Gustavo Noboa as president
The indigenous coalition's chosen leader ruled the country for years afterward
Mahuad was reinstated by the military the next day
Congress was dissolved and immediate new elections were called

evt-01-21-2000-ecuador.butterflyEffect: The rebels briefly installed a three-person junta, but Ecuador's military high command refused to back it and forced the plotters out within hours, installing Vice President Gustavo Noboa as president instead. The episode nonetheless proved indigenous political mobilization could topple a government, and junta member Lucio Gutiérrez was elected president himself two years later.

evt-01-21-2004-nasa.scenario: It's January 21, 2004, seventeen days after Spirit landed on Mars, and mission control at JPL suddenly loses coherent data — the rover is transmitting only garbled signals and skipping communication sessions.
evt-01-21-2004-nasa.prompt: What should JPL engineers do to recover Spirit's failing systems?

choices.text: Command an immediate full system reboot without diagnosis
Order Opportunity to alter its landing trajectory to assist
Declare the mission over and shut down all further contact
Put the rover into a low-power fault mode and analyze it via slow, low-gain transmissions

evt-01-21-2004-nasa.butterflyEffect: Engineers traced the fault to Spirit's flash memory being overloaded with files, causing repeated reboots. After days of careful diagnosis and a memory reformat, the rover was fully restored and went on to operate for six years — 25 times its planned 90-day mission.

evt-01-21-2009-gaza-strip.scenario: It's January 21, 2009. Three weeks of intense fighting between Israel and Hamas have devastated Gaza, and now Israeli tanks are rolling back across the border as a unilateral halt to operations takes hold.
evt-01-21-2009-gaza-strip.prompt: What was the immediate outcome as Israel completed its withdrawal from Gaza?

choices.text: A permanent peace treaty between Israel and Hamas was signed
The United Nations deployed peacekeeping troops to administer Gaza
Israel and Hamas each declared separate unilateral ceasefires without a formal truce
Egypt formally annexed the Gaza Strip to end the conflict

evt-01-21-2009-gaza-strip.butterflyEffect: Rather than a negotiated treaty, Israel and Hamas each declared separate unilateral ceasefires without direct talks or a formal truce. The underlying blockade and political disputes went unresolved, setting the stage for repeated escalations between Israel and Gaza in the years that followed.

evt-01-21-2017-2017-women-s-march.scenario: It is 21 January 2017, the day after Donald Trump's inauguration. You join hundreds of thousands filling the streets of Washington, D.C., signs raised, as sister marches unfold in cities around the world.
evt-01-21-2017-2017-women-s-march.prompt: What did the 2017 Women's March become known as afterward?

choices.text: A protest that led directly to a change in the inauguration date
A march that failed to draw significant international attention
The founding rally of the modern labor union movement
The largest single-day protest in U.S. history at the time

evt-01-21-2017-2017-women-s-march.butterflyEffect: The march drew millions worldwide and was, at the time, the largest single-day protest in U.S. history, later surpassed by the 2020 George Floyd protests. It launched annual Women's Marches and helped energize a wave of women running for and winning office in the 2018 midterms.

evt-01-21-2023-2023-monterey-park-shooti.scenario: It's the night of January 21, 2023, at the Lai Lai Ballroom in Alhambra, moments after a gunman who just attacked a nearby dance studio walks in armed and threatening more violence.
evt-01-21-2023-2023-monterey-park-shooti.prompt: What do the ballroom staff do to stop him?

choices.text: Evacuate through a back exit and leave him unchallenged
Attempt to negotiate with him to leave peacefully
Call police and hide, waiting for backup
Physically confront him and wrestle the weapon away before he can fire

evt-01-21-2023-2023-monterey-park-shooti.butterflyEffect: Staff at the Alhambra ballroom disarmed the gunman before he could kill again there, ending his rampage after eleven deaths at the Monterey Park studio. He fled and died by suicide during a police standoff the next day, making it the deadliest mass shooting in Los Angeles County's history.

evt-01-21-2025-2025-kartalkaya-hotel-fir.scenario: It is the early hours of 21 January 2025 at the Grand Kartal Hotel in Kartalkaya, Turkey. Smoke is spreading from the fourth-floor kitchen, but the building has no working smoke detectors or sprinklers, and most guests are still asleep.
evt-01-21-2025-2025-kartalkaya-hotel-fir.prompt: What did investigators identify as decisive in the fire's death toll?

choices.text: A bomb threat that delayed firefighters from entering
A gas explosion that instantly destroyed the building's structure
An overcrowded evacuation stairwell that had been welded shut
The absence of functioning fire alarms, sprinklers, and emergency exit lighting

evt-01-21-2025-2025-kartalkaya-hotel-fir.butterflyEffect: At least 78 people died, most from suffocation, as the fire spread unchecked and rescue efforts were slowed by freezing weather and the resort's remote location. The disaster triggered nationwide inspections of Turkish ski hotels and renewed calls for stricter enforcement of fire-safety codes.

evt-01-22-1689-convention-parliament-168.scenario: It is January 1689. James II has fled to France, and you sit among the members of an emergency Convention Parliament summoned to settle who should rule England after his flight.
evt-01-22-1689-convention-parliament-168.prompt: What did the Convention Parliament decide about the vacant throne?

choices.text: Declared the throne vacant and offered it jointly to William III and Mary II
Crowned Mary II alone as sole reigning monarch
Restored James II with new legal limits on his authority
Abolished the monarchy and declared a parliamentary republic

evt-01-22-1689-convention-parliament-168.butterflyEffect: The Convention declared that James had effectively abdicated and offered the crown jointly to William III and Mary II, rather than restoring James or declaring a republic. This compromise avoided further civil war and led directly to the Bill of Rights 1689, permanently limiting royal power and asserting parliamentary supremacy.

evt-01-22-1879-anglo-zulu-war.scenario: It is the afternoon of 22 January 1879 at Isandlwana. Your British camp, left lightly defended while much of the column scouts ahead, suddenly faces a vast Zulu impi advancing in its famous 'horns of the buffalo' formation.
evt-01-22-1879-anglo-zulu-war.prompt: What happened to the British force at Isandlwana?

choices.text: British reinforcements arrived in time to repel the attack
The garrison retreated safely to Rorke's Drift before the assault began
