Zulu forces overwhelmed the camp and destroyed most of the British force
A truce was negotiated before any fighting occurred

evt-01-22-1879-anglo-zulu-war.butterflyEffect: Zulu warriors overwhelmed the camp, killing over 1,300 British and colonial troops in the worst defeat ever inflicted on a modern army by pre-industrial forces. The shock forced Britain to pour reinforcements into Natal, leading to the eventual crushing of the Zulu Kingdom at Ulundi later that year.

evt-01-22-1906-ss-valencia.scenario: It is the night of 22 January 1906. Your steamer has torn open on a reef off Vancouver Island, and heavy surf is smashing the lifeboats to pieces as they hit the water.
evt-01-22-1906-ss-valencia.prompt: As a survivor still aboard the wreck, what gives you the best chance of rescue?

choices.text: Stay in your cabin and wait for the tide to recede
Swim directly for the cliffs through the breakers
Climb into the rigging and hold on above the waterline
Jump into a lifeboat and row for the rocky shore

evt-01-22-1906-ss-valencia.butterflyEffect: Many who leapt into lifeboats drowned when the boats swamped in the surf; those who climbed into the rigging and clung to the wreck had better odds, though rescuers on the cliffs above struggled for hours to reach them. About 100 died. Public fury over the disaster helped drive construction of a coastal lifesaving trail on Vancouver Island, ancestor of today's West Coast Trail.

evt-01-22-1924-ramsay-macdonald.scenario: You are a Liberal MP in the House of Commons in January 1924, weighing whether to help Ramsay MacDonald's Labour Party, which lacks a majority, take office for the first time.
evt-01-22-1924-ramsay-macdonald.prompt: Do you back Labour's minority government in the confidence vote?

choices.text: Vote with the Conservatives to block Labour
Abstain and force an immediate new election
Demand a formal coalition before offering any support
Vote to support Labour's minority government

evt-01-22-1924-ramsay-macdonald.butterflyEffect: The Liberals let MacDonald govern rather than side with the Conservatives, making him Britain's first Labour Prime Minister. His minority government lasted only nine months before the Campbell Case and the Zinoviev letter scandal brought it down, triggering an election that returned the Conservatives under Baldwin.

evt-01-22-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: You are an Australian infantry officer at Buna-Gona in January 1943, worn down by weeks of jungle combat against a Japanese garrison that keeps fighting from its bunkers even as its position collapses.
evt-01-22-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: With victory in sight, what do you order your exhausted men to do?

choices.text: Request a temporary truce to negotiate a Japanese withdrawal
Halt and offer the garrison surrender terms
Withdraw and wait for naval bombardment to finish the job
Continue the systematic assault to clear each fortified bunker

evt-01-22-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Allied troops methodically cleared the remaining Japanese bunkers rather than waiting for a surrender that never came, securing Buna-Gona on 22 January 1943. The victory gave the Allies their first foothold on New Guinea's north coast, opening the way for the slow, disease-ridden advance toward Salamaua and Lae that became the template for the wider Pacific island campaign.

evt-01-22-1957-new-york-city-police-depa.scenario: It is January 22, 1957, and NYPD detectives arrive at a house in Waterbury, Connecticut, to arrest George Metesky, the suspect behind sixteen years of bombs planted in movie theaters, train stations, and Grand Central Terminal.
evt-01-22-1957-new-york-city-police-depa.prompt: What clue actually led detectives to identify Metesky as the bomber?

choices.text: Psychiatric profiling matched with old company employee records
Surveillance footage caught him planting a device
Fingerprints lifted from bomb fragments matched his record
An anonymous tipster turned him in for a reward

evt-01-22-1957-new-york-city-police-depa.butterflyEffect: A psychiatric profile by Dr. James Brussel, combined with a Con Edison clerk matching Metesky's grievance letters to old employee disability records, cracked the case. The investigation became a landmark early example of criminal profiling, shaping methods later formalized by the FBI's behavioral science unit.

evt-01-22-1963-elysee-treaty.scenario: It is January 22, 1963, in the Élysée Palace, and you watch Charles de Gaulle and Konrad Adenauer sign a treaty meant to end centuries of French-German conflict for good.
evt-01-22-1963-elysee-treaty.prompt: What ongoing mechanism did the treaty establish between the two nations?

choices.text: A merger of the French and German armed forces
A single shared currency for both countries
Regular government summits and a youth exchange office between the nations
Complete removal of the shared border checkpoints

evt-01-22-1963-elysee-treaty.butterflyEffect: The treaty created regular summits between French and German leaders and founded the Franco-German Youth Office to promote exchanges between citizens. It became a cornerstone of postwar European integration, with the Franco-German partnership later driving the formation of the European Union.

evt-01-22-1968-apollo-5.scenario: It is January 22, 1968, at Cape Kennedy, and a Saturn IB rocket carries an uncrewed Apollo Lunar Module skyward for its first-ever test in space—the vehicle that will one day set astronauts down on the Moon.
evt-01-22-1968-apollo-5.prompt: What problem forced controllers to improvise a new plan mid-mission?

choices.text: The ascent engine failed to ignite during the entire mission
The module lost all radio contact with ground control
A computer error shut down the descent engine early, requiring a backup test plan
A fuel leak forced an immediate abort of the launch

evt-01-22-1968-apollo-5.butterflyEffect: A programming error triggered an early shutdown of the descent engine, so ground controllers switched to an alternate flight plan to still exercise the ascent and descent engines fully. The mission was ultimately judged a success, giving NASA confidence to proceed toward crewed Lunar Module testing on Apollo 9.

evt-01-22-1968-apollo-program.scenario: It is 22 January 1968 and you are a flight controller in Houston watching Apollo 5's uncrewed Lunar Module test, when its onboard computer cuts short a scheduled descent engine burn far earlier than planned.
evt-01-22-1968-apollo-program.prompt: What do you do to salvage the test?

choices.text: Abort the entire mission and command the module to return
Order the module to remain dormant until a fresh test could be scheduled
Do nothing and wait for the next automatic burn sequence
Switch to manual ground control to complete the engine firings

evt-01-22-1968-apollo-program.butterflyEffect: Ground controllers switched the Lunar Module to manual backup control and completed the descent and ascent engine firings themselves, proving the engines could restart, throttle, and separate as designed. The salvaged data was convincing enough that NASA skipped a second unmanned Lunar Module test entirely, keeping Apollo on schedule for crewed flights and, ultimately, a 1969 Moon landing.

evt-01-22-1969-leonid-brezhnev.scenario: It is January 22, 1969, and a Moscow motorcade is returning cosmonauts from their triumphant Soyuz mission through Red Square. A man in a stolen police uniform steps forward with a pair of pistols, aiming at what he believes is Brezhnev's car.
evt-01-22-1969-leonid-brezhnev.prompt: What actually happened when the gunman, Viktor Ilyin, opened fire?

choices.text: He killed a chauffeur in the wrong car, missing Brezhnev entirely
He successfully assassinated Brezhnev's chief bodyguard instead
His gun jammed and he was tackled before firing a shot
He wounded Brezhnev, who recovered within weeks

evt-01-22-1969-leonid-brezhnev.butterflyEffect: Ilyin had misidentified the vehicles and instead killed a motorcade driver, wounding several others, while Brezhnev's real car was elsewhere in the procession. Declared insane rather than tried publicly, Ilyin spent decades in psychiatric confinement, and Soviet leadership dramatically tightened motorcade security afterward.

evt-01-22-1970-boeing-747.scenario: It is 22 January 1970, and you are boarding Pan Am's first scheduled 747 flight from New York to London. Word spreads that the original aircraft has developed an overheating engine on the tarmac.
evt-01-22-1970-boeing-747.prompt: How does Pan Am handle the mechanical problem before departure?

choices.text: Force the flight to depart on schedule with the faulty engine
Replace the jumbo jet with a smaller Boeing 707
Cancel the flight and rebook passengers for the next day
Swap in the backup aircraft and delay departure

evt-01-22-1970-boeing-747.butterflyEffect: Pan Am swapped in its backup 747, delaying the historic flight by more than six hours, and the jumbo jet finally entered service. The 747 went on to slash per-seat costs on long-haul routes, making international air travel accessible to the middle class and reshaping global tourism for decades.

evt-01-22-1973-supreme-court-of-the-unit.scenario: It is 22 January 1973. You are one of nine justices about to hand down a ruling on a Texas woman's challenge to her state's near-total ban on abortion.
evt-01-22-1973-supreme-court-of-the-unit.prompt: What does the Supreme Court rule in Roe v. Wade?

choices.text: Dismiss the case for lack of standing
Send the matter to Congress for federal legislation
Uphold the Texas law as within the state's police powers
Strike down the state ban, citing a constitutional right to privacy

evt-01-22-1973-supreme-court-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: The Court ruled 7–2 that a constitutional right to privacy, rooted in the Fourteenth Amendment, protected a woman's decision to have an abortion, though it allowed states to regulate more as pregnancy progressed. The ruling reshaped American politics for a generation, fueling decades of legal and electoral battles, until it was overturned by Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization in 2022.

evt-01-22-1987-philippines.scenario: It is 22 January 1987. You march with thousands of farmers toward Malacañang Palace in Manila, demanding that President Corazon Aquino's new government deliver genuine land reform.
evt-01-22-1987-philippines.prompt: What happens when the march reaches the barricades near the palace?

choices.text: Security forces open fire on the marchers
The marchers are allowed through peacefully to petition Congress
Police escort the marchers home without incident
President Aquino comes out to personally negotiate

evt-01-22-1987-philippines.butterflyEffect: Government security forces opened fire on the crowd, killing over a dozen farmers in what became known as the Mendiola massacre. The killings became a rallying symbol for the land reform movement and hardened distrust between Aquino's government and rural activists, complicating the land reform law eventually passed later that year.

evt-01-22-1992-space-shuttle-program.scenario: It is 22 January 1992 and you are Roberta Bondar, strapped into Discovery for STS-42, about to become the first Canadian woman in space aboard a shuttle carrying the International Microgravity Laboratory.
evt-01-22-1992-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What is the mission's primary scientific task once you reach orbit?

choices.text: Run life sciences and materials experiments in the microgravity lab
Deploy a communications satellite from the payload bay
Conduct a spacewalk to service the Hubble Space Telescope
Test a prototype space station module for later assembly

evt-01-22-1992-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: STS-42's crew spent eight days running life-science and materials experiments inside the International Microgravity Laboratory-1, gathering data on how human physiology, plants, and materials behave in weightlessness. The results helped shape research protocols later used aboard the International Space Station, and Bondar's flight marked a milestone for Canada's human spaceflight program.

evt-01-22-1995-israeli-palestinian-confl.scenario: It is 22 January 1995, at a junction near Netanya where soldiers routinely gather at a bus stop and snack stand while the Oslo peace process continues amid deep public division.
evt-01-22-1995-israeli-palestinian-confl.prompt: What happened at Beit Lid, and who claimed responsibility?

choices.text: Security forces intercepted and defused the explosives before detonation
Hamas detonated a car bomb targeting a military convoy
Palestinian Islamic Jihad carried out a double suicide bombing, killing 21 people
A lone gunman opened fire on the crowd at the bus stop

evt-01-22-1995-israeli-palestinian-confl.butterflyEffect: Palestinian Islamic Jihad carried out a double suicide bombing that killed 21 people, mostly soldiers, in one of the deadliest attacks against Israel to that point. The group cited opposition to the Oslo Accords, and the attack deepened Israeli public doubt about the peace process, hardening security policy in the years that followed.

evt-01-22-1998-space-shuttle-endeavour.scenario: It is January 22, 1998, and you're in Houston mission control as Endeavour lifts off to rendezvous with the Russian space station Mir, carrying a fresh crew member for the outpost.
evt-01-22-1998-space-shuttle-endeavour.prompt: What was the main purpose of Endeavour's docking with Mir on this mission?

choices.text: Rescue two stranded Russian cosmonauts from the station
Deliver a new communications satellite into orbit
Test a brand-new docking mechanism never used before
Swap out the American astronaut living aboard Mir for a new one

evt-01-22-1998-space-shuttle-endeavour.butterflyEffect: STS-89 delivered astronaut Andy Thomas to Mir and brought home David Wolf, who had lived aboard since October. It was one of the final Shuttle-Mir crew swaps, a program that built the trust and procedures the US and Russia would soon rely on to jointly build the ISS.

evt-01-22-2006-evo-morales.scenario: You are a newly appointed minister as Evo Morales is sworn in on 22 January 2006 as Bolivia's first president from its indigenous majority, promising to break foreign control of the country's resources.
evt-01-22-2006-evo-morales.prompt: What major policy do you push through within his first year in office?

choices.text: Nationalize the hydrocarbons (natural gas) industry
Adopt the U.S. dollar as Bolivia's official currency
Sign a free trade agreement with the United States
Privatize the state-owned mining companies

evt-01-22-2006-evo-morales.butterflyEffect: In May 2006 Morales nationalized Bolivia's natural gas industry, forcing foreign energy companies to renegotiate contracts on terms far more favorable to the state. The move dramatically increased government revenue and became a defining example of Latin America's leftist "pink tide," reshaping Bolivia's economy for over a decade.

evt-01-22-2009-barack-obama.scenario: It is January 22, 2009, two days into your presidency, and you sit at the Oval Office desk signing an executive order that sets a firm one-year deadline to close the Guantanamo Bay detention facility.
evt-01-22-2009-barack-obama.prompt: What actually happened to that one-year closure deadline?

choices.text: The Supreme Court ordered immediate closure within weeks
Congress voted to close it even faster than planned
The facility closed exactly on schedule in January 2010
The deadline passed and the facility remained open for years afterward

evt-01-22-2009-barack-obama.butterflyEffect: The deadline passed unmet as Congress moved to block detainee transfers and legal challenges piled up, keeping the facility open throughout Obama's presidency and beyond. The episode became a recurring flashpoint over executive power, national security, and the limits of unilateral reform.

evt-01-22-2012-2012-croatian-european-un.scenario: It is 22 January 2012. You are a Croatian citizen at the polling booth, asked to decide whether your country should join the European Union after finishing years of accession talks.
evt-01-22-2012-2012-croatian-european-un.prompt: How does the Croatian electorate vote in this referendum?

choices.text: The vote ends in a tie requiring a second referendum
Turnout is too low to validate the result
They reject EU membership
They approve EU membership by a clear majority

evt-01-22-2012-2012-croatian-european-un.butterflyEffect: Croatians voted decisively in favour of joining the EU, though turnout was low at under half the electorate. The result set Croatia on course to become the bloc's 28th member state on 1 July 2013, the last country to join before more than a decade of enlargement pause.

evt-01-23-1264-louis-ix-of-france.scenario: It is 23 January 1264, and you stand among the English barons awaiting King Louis IX of France's arbitration on the quarrel between Henry III and Simon de Montfort's reformist council. Louis has just ruled entirely in the king's favour, annulling the Provisions of Oxford.
evt-01-23-1264-louis-ix-of-france.prompt: Faced with a verdict wholly against them, what should Montfort and the barons do?

choices.text: Appeal the decision to the Pope in Rome
Offer Henry III a new compromise settlement
Reject the verdict and prepare to fight the king
Accept the ruling and disband their reform council

evt-01-23-1264-louis-ix-of-france.butterflyEffect: The barons rejected the Mise of Amiens outright, and England plunged back into civil war. Within months Simon de Montfort defeated and captured Henry III at the Battle of Lewes, briefly making Montfort the effective ruler of England before his own defeat and death at Evesham in 1265.

evt-01-23-1368-hongwu-emperor.scenario: It is January 1368 in Nanjing, and you watch the peasant-turned-rebel Zhu Yuanzhang, having driven out the Mongol Yuan dynasty, prepare to formally take the throne of a new Chinese empire.
evt-01-23-1368-hongwu-emperor.prompt: What does Zhu Yuanzhang do to legitimize his new rule?

choices.text: Requests the title of Great Khan from Mongol nobles
Accepts vassal status under the remaining Yuan court
Restores the deposed Song dynasty's imperial line
Declares himself the Hongwu Emperor and founds the Ming dynasty

evt-01-23-1368-hongwu-emperor.butterflyEffect: He proclaimed himself the Hongwu Emperor and named his new dynasty Ming, ending nearly a century of Mongol rule. His reign centralized imperial power dramatically, including later abolishing the chancellorship, setting patterns of autocratic governance that shaped China for the next 276 years of Ming rule.

evt-01-23-1556-1556-shaanxi-earthquake.scenario: It is the early morning of 23 January 1556 in Huaxian, Shaanxi, and the ground beneath the dense loess plateau begins to shake violently, bringing down entire hillsides where families have carved their homes.
evt-01-23-1556-1556-shaanxi-earthquake.prompt: What made the death toll of this earthquake so catastrophic?

choices.text: A tsunami sweeping inland from the coast
The failure of a major irrigation dam
Collapse of loess cave dwellings and landslides across the plateau
A volcanic eruption triggering the tremor

evt-01-23-1556-1556-shaanxi-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The soft loess soil of the region collapsed and slid in massive landslides, burying the cave dwellings that many residents called home, contributing to what remains one of the deadliest earthquakes ever recorded. Detailed Ming-era accounts of the disaster became some of the earliest thorough earthquake records in Chinese history.

evt-01-23-1570-james-hamilton-assassin.scenario: It is January 1570 in Linlithgow. You are James Hamilton of Bothwellhaugh, standing at the steps of your uncle Archbishop John Hamilton's house with a loaded firearm, watching Regent Moray's procession approach.
evt-01-23-1570-james-hamilton-assassin.prompt: What do you do as the Regent's procession passes below?

choices.text: Join the procession and pledge loyalty to Moray
Lower your weapon and surrender to the guards
Send a warning so Moray can escape
Fire on Moray as he rides past

evt-01-23-1570-james-hamilton-assassin.butterflyEffect: Hamilton shot and killed the Earl of Moray, one of the first recorded political assassinations carried out with a firearm. The killing deepened the civil war between supporters of the exiled Mary, Queen of Scots and the party of the infant King James VI, and English forces later retaliated by demolishing Hamilton's own house.

evt-01-23-1870-american-indian-wars.scenario: It is dawn on 23 January 1870 along the Marias River in Montana Territory. Your cavalry column has located a Blackfeet Piegan camp, though scouts warn it may be the wrong band and that sickness has struck the people inside.
evt-01-23-1870-american-indian-wars.prompt: What did the army command decide to do upon locating the camp?

choices.text: Waited for reinforcements before taking any action
Ordered an attack despite doubts about the band's identity and the presence of disease
Escorted the band safely to a nearby reservation
Withdrew after negotiating a peace agreement with the camp's leaders

evt-01-23-1870-american-indian-wars.butterflyEffect: The soldiers attacked anyway, killing well over 170 Blackfeet, mostly women, children, and the elderly, many already suffering from smallpox. Public outrage over the massacre helped block a proposal to transfer Indian affairs to military control, though violent conflict with Native nations continued for decades afterward.

evt-01-23-1909-tottenham-outrage.scenario: It is 23 January 1909 in Tottenham. You are a constable who has just seen two armed men gun down a policeman after robbing a rubber factory's wages, and they are now fleeing on foot through the streets with a mob and other officers giving chase.
evt-01-23-1909-tottenham-outrage.prompt: With no motor transport available and the gunmen firing wildly, what should the pursuers do?

choices.text: Surround the factory instead of chasing the fleeing men
Commandeer any passing vehicle to keep up the chase
Halt the pursuit and wait for armed reinforcements
Let the robbers go to protect bystanders from crossfire

evt-01-23-1909-tottenham-outrage.butterflyEffect: Pursuers commandeered a tram, a milkman's cart and other passing vehicles to keep pace over six frantic miles, until the two robbers, cornered near a marsh, shot themselves rather than be taken. The chaos exposed how poorly armed and equipped London's police were against gunmen, feeding debates that shaped firearms policy ahead of the even bloodier Sidney Street Siege two years later.

evt-01-23-1915-john-chilembwe.scenario: It is dawn on 23 January 1915 near Magomero, Nyasaland. You are one of Reverend John Chilembwe's followers, armed and gathered outside the home of a plantation manager notorious for his brutal treatment of African labourers.
evt-01-23-1915-john-chilembwe.prompt: What does Chilembwe's plan call for the rebels to do right now?

choices.text: Abandon the plan and disperse quietly
Present him with a list of grievances and demand reforms
Storm the manager's house and kill him to launch the uprising
Wait for promised German weapons from nearby Tanganyika

evt-01-23-1915-john-chilembwe.butterflyEffect: Chilembwe's men killed the plantation manager and raised the revolt, but colonial forces crushed the uprising within weeks; Chilembwe himself was shot dead while fleeing on 3 February 1915. Decades later he was reclaimed as a founding hero of Malawian independence, and Malawi still marks his stand every 15 January.

evt-01-23-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 23 January 1942 at Rabaul on New Britain. You serve with the small, outnumbered Lark Force garrison as Japanese invasion troops storm ashore in overwhelming numbers, and the order comes down that the town cannot be held.
evt-01-23-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: With the garrison's command dissolving, what should you and your comrades do?

choices.text: Surrender as an organised unit under a white flag
Wait offshore for an Allied naval rescue convoy
Dig in at the harbour and fight to the last man
Disperse into the jungle in small groups and try to escape overland

evt-01-23-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Rabaul fell within hours, and with no coordinated evacuation, survivors scattered in small groups into the New Britain jungle. Many were later captured and some were massacred by Japanese troops at Tol Plantation, while others made an extraordinary trek to the south coast and were evacuated to Australia, becoming one of the war's grim early lessons in abandoning garrisons without an exit plan.

evt-01-23-1957-walter-frederick-morrison.scenario: It is January 1957, and you are Fred Morrison, sitting across from executives at the Wham-O toy company, holding your plastic flying disc, the Pluto Platter, ready to make a deal.
evt-01-23-1957-walter-frederick-morrison.prompt: What does Morrison do with his flying disc invention?

choices.text: Sells the rights to Mattel for mass production
Keeps the patent and manufactures it himself
Sells the rights to Wham-O, who rename it the Frisbee
Gives the design away for free to promote it

evt-01-23-1957-walter-frederick-morrison.butterflyEffect: Wham-O bought the rights and soon renamed the disc the Frisbee, turning it into one of the best-selling toys in history with over 200 million sold. The disc later spawned the competitive sport of Ultimate Frisbee and became a lasting symbol of American backyard culture.

evt-01-23-1968-uss-pueblo-ager-2.scenario: It is 23 January 1968 in international waters off North Korea. You are Commander Lloyd Bucher aboard the intelligence ship USS Pueblo, surrounded by North Korean gunboats and a MiG fighter, with your crew scrambling to deal with cabinets full of classified material.
evt-01-23-1968-uss-pueblo-ager-2.prompt: With no weapons readied and the ship boxed in, what should Bucher do?

choices.text: Surrender the ship to prevent his crew being killed
Radio for immediate US naval air support and hold position
Attempt to outrun the gunboats at full speed
Order the crew to man the deck guns and fight

evt-01-23-1968-uss-pueblo-ager-2.butterflyEffect: Bucher ordered what destruction of sensitive documents his crew could manage but ultimately surrendered rather than see his unarmed men slaughtered. The Pueblo's 82 surviving crew were held and tortured for eleven months before a US apology secured their release in December 1968, while the ship itself remains in North Korean hands to this day as a propaganda exhibit.

evt-01-23-1993-ncsa-mosaic.scenario: It is early 1993 at the National Center for Supercomputing Applications. You are part of Marc Andreessen and Eric Bina's small team, deciding how your new web browser should handle images.
evt-01-23-1993-ncsa-mosaic.prompt: What choice made Mosaic stand out from earlier web browsers?

choices.text: Restricting use to plain text only, with no graphics
Displaying images inline with the surrounding text
Limiting access to a single university network
Requiring a paid subscription to view any page

evt-01-23-1993-ncsa-mosaic.butterflyEffect: Mosaic displayed images inline with text rather than in a separate window, making the web feel visual and inviting for ordinary users for the first time. Its success led Andreessen to co-found Netscape, igniting the browser wars and the wider dot-com boom of the 1990s.

evt-01-23-1997-madeleine-albright.scenario: It is 23 January 1997 in Washington, D.C. You watch as Madeleine Albright is sworn in as the first woman to serve as United States Secretary of State under President Bill Clinton.
evt-01-23-1997-madeleine-albright.prompt: What policy push came to define Albright's tenure at the State Department?

choices.text: Championing NATO's expansion into Eastern Europe
Withdrawing the United States from NATO entirely
Focusing American diplomacy exclusively on Latin America
Reducing all U.S. involvement in European affairs

evt-01-23-1997-madeleine-albright.butterflyEffect: Albright championed the expansion of NATO into Eastern Europe, bringing Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic into the alliance in 1999, and she led American diplomacy during the Kosovo crisis that same year. Her tenure reshaped post-Cold War transatlantic security arrangements for decades to come.

evt-01-23-2003-nasa.scenario: It is January 2003. Pioneer 10, launched in 1972 and now more than 12 billion kilometers from Earth, has been sending back an ever-fainter signal to NASA's Deep Space Network as its power source slowly decays.
evt-01-23-2003-nasa.prompt: What happened to Pioneer 10's communication with Earth after this point?

choices.text: It collided with space debris and stopped transmitting
Mission controllers deliberately shut it down after 2003
It continued sending strong signals for another decade
Its signal grew too weak to detect, and contact was permanently lost

evt-01-23-2003-nasa.butterflyEffect: The signal received on 23 January 2003 was the last confirmed contact with Pioneer 10, whose radioisotope power had dropped below the level needed to transmit. The probe still drifts silently toward the constellation Taurus, carrying its famous plaque depicting humans and Earth's location as a message to any who might find it.

evt-01-23-2022-paul-henri-sandaogo-damib.scenario: It is the night of 23–24 January 2022 in Ouagadougou. You are a junior officer in the Burkinabè army, and mutinous soldiers led by Lieutenant-Colonel Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba are moving against President Roch Marc Christian Kaboré.
evt-01-23-2022-paul-henri-sandaogo-damib.prompt: What actually followed the mutiny against Kaboré?

choices.text: Kaboré is deposed and Damiba becomes interim president
The army splits into rival factions and fights a civil war
Regional forces intervene and immediately restore civilian rule
The mutiny collapses and Kaboré retains full power

evt-01-23-2022-paul-henri-sandaogo-damib.butterflyEffect: Kaboré was deposed and Damiba installed himself as interim president, promising to restore security against jihadist insurgents. His government lasted barely eight months before he too was overthrown, by Captain Ibrahim Traoré in September 2022, extending Burkina Faso's cycle of military rule.

evt-01-24-41-40s.scenario: It is 24 January, AD 41, in Rome. You are a Praetorian guardsman moments after Cassius Chaerea and fellow officers cut down Emperor Caligula in a palace corridor, and the Senate is debating restoring the old Republic.
evt-01-24-41-40s.prompt: What do you and your fellow Praetorians do when you find Caligula's uncle Claudius hiding in the palace?

choices.text: Execute him alongside Caligula to end the dynasty
Hand power to the Senate to restore the Republic
Install Caligula's infant daughter as ruler
Proclaim him emperor to secure the Guard's position

evt-01-24-41-40s.butterflyEffect: The Guard proclaimed Claudius emperor, securing their own influence and bypassing the Senate's push to restore republican rule. The precedent that the military, not the Senate, could make an emperor endured for centuries, and Claudius went on to launch the Roman conquest of Britain in AD 43.

evt-01-24-914-fatimid-caliphate.scenario: It is 914, and you march west with Fatimid forces into Egypt, sent to challenge Abbasid authority in the name of the new Isma'ili caliph based in Ifriqiya.
evt-01-24-914-fatimid-caliphate.prompt: What is the outcome of this first Fatimid attempt to conquer Egypt?

choices.text: It results in a negotiated partition of Egypt
It succeeds immediately, capturing all of Egypt
It fails, and the Fatimid forces retreat back to Ifriqiya
It triggers the instant collapse of Abbasid Baghdad

evt-01-24-914-fatimid-caliphate.butterflyEffect: The invasion failed, and Fatimid forces were pushed back to Ifriqiya, delaying their ambitions for over half a century. Egypt would not fall to the Fatimids until 969, when the general Jawhar succeeded where this expedition had not, allowing the founding of Cairo as the new heart of the caliphate.

evt-01-24-1458-estates-of-the-realm.scenario: It is January 1458, and you stand among the Hungarian nobles gathered on the frozen Danube outside Buda, debating whom to proclaim as the new king after the sudden death of Ladislaus V.
evt-01-24-1458-estates-of-the-realm.prompt: Whom do the assembled estates unanimously choose as King of Hungary?

choices.text: George of Poděbrady of Bohemia
Frederick III of Habsburg
Matthias Corvinus, the young son of John Hunyadi
Casimir IV of Poland

evt-01-24-1458-estates-of-the-realm.butterflyEffect: The estates chose the 14-year-old Matthias Corvinus, son of the famed general John Hunyadi. He grew into one of Hungary's greatest Renaissance monarchs, building the formidable mercenary Black Army and turning Buda into a center of humanist learning while holding off Ottoman expansion for decades.

evt-01-24-1848-james-w-marshall.scenario: It is January 24, 1848, and you are James Marshall, standing in the tailrace of John Sutter's new sawmill in Coloma, California, when a glint of metal in the water catches your eye.
evt-01-24-1848-james-w-marshall.prompt: What does Marshall do after realizing the metal is gold?

choices.text: He buries the flakes and tells no one
He shows it to Sutter, who tries to keep the discovery secret
He immediately sells the samples to traveling merchants
He reports the find to Mexican territorial authorities

evt-01-24-1848-james-w-marshall.butterflyEffect: Marshall showed Sutter the flakes, and Sutter tried to keep the find quiet to protect his land and mill business. The secret leaked within months anyway, and by 1849 hundreds of thousands of prospectors had flooded California, triggering the Gold Rush that reshaped the American West economically and politically, while leaving both Marshall and Sutter ruined.

evt-01-24-1913-michael-moutoussis.scenario: It is January 1913, during the Balkan Wars. You and observer Aristeidis Moraitinis are airborne over the Dardanelles in a fragile floatplane, the Ottoman fleet anchored below and no aircraft ever having done this in combat before.
evt-01-24-1913-michael-moutoussis.prompt: What do you do with this unprecedented reconnaissance flight over the enemy fleet?

choices.text: Reconnoiter the fleet and drop bombs on the Ottoman ships
Land on the water to negotiate with Ottoman officers
Observe and report the fleet's position, then return safely
Abort the mission due to engine trouble

evt-01-24-1913-michael-moutoussis.butterflyEffect: Moutoussis and Moraitinis completed the first naval air mission in history, scouting the Ottoman fleet and dropping bombs on it from the air. Their flight helped establish naval aviation as a legitimate branch of warfare, a lesson every major navy would rapidly expand upon within a decade.

evt-01-24-1961-boeing-b-52-stratofortres.scenario: It is January 24, 1961, near Goldsboro, North Carolina. You are a maintenance officer at Seymour Johnson Air Force Base after word arrives that a B-52 has broken apart mid-air, releasing two Mark 39 nuclear bombs toward the ground.
evt-01-24-1961-boeing-b-52-stratofortres.prompt: What ultimately stopped the more dangerous of the two bombs from detonating?

choices.text: A single arm/safe switch survived and prevented detonation
The bomb's self-destruct mechanism triggered automatically
The crew ejected and manually disarmed it in mid-air
Ground crews reached it and cut the firing wires before impact

evt-01-24-1961-boeing-b-52-stratofortres.butterflyEffect: Investigators found that of four safety mechanisms on the parachute-deployed bomb, three had failed during the fall, and only a single low-voltage arming switch prevented detonation. The near-miss, kept classified for decades, later drove redesigns of nuclear weapon safety systems and became a landmark case study in accidental nuclear risk.

evt-01-24-1966-air-india-flight-101.scenario: It is the morning of January 24, 1966. You are an air traffic controller in Geneva, tracking Air India Flight 101 as it descends toward the airport through cloud cover near Mont Blanc.
evt-01-24-1966-air-india-flight-101.prompt: What error leads the aircraft into the mountain?

choices.text: An engine failure forced an emergency uncontrolled descent
The crew began descending before passing over the mountain, misjudging their position
A hijacking attempt caused the crew to lose control
A sudden storm forced the pilots to deviate sharply off course

evt-01-24-1966-air-india-flight-101.butterflyEffect: The Boeing 707 began its descent before clearing Mont Blanc, misjudging its position in poor visibility, and struck the mountain, killing all 117 aboard, including nuclear physicist Homi Bhabha, founder of India's Atomic Energy Commission. The crash echoed an earlier 1950 disaster at the same peak and dealt a severe setback to India's early atomic energy program.

evt-01-24-1972-shoichi-yokoi.scenario: It is January 1972 in the jungles of Guam. You are a Japanese soldier who has hidden in the wilderness for nearly 28 years, unaware the war ended in 1945, convinced surrender would bring shame upon your family and emperor.
evt-01-24-1972-shoichi-yokoi.prompt: When local hunters finally corner you, what do you do?

choices.text: You take your own life rather than be found
You flee deeper into the jungle successfully
You attack the hunters to avoid capture
You surrender peacefully when discovered

evt-01-24-1972-shoichi-yokoi.butterflyEffect: Sergeant Shoichi Yokoi was captured alive and returned to Japan, famously apologizing for coming back rather than dying in service. His emergence, decades after the war's end, made him a symbol of the era's rigid wartime code of honor and reignited public fascination with the last holdouts still scattered across the Pacific.

evt-01-24-1977-spanish-transition-to-dem.scenario: It is the evening of 24 January 1977 in Madrid's Atocha district. You are a lawyer working late at a labor law office tied to the outlawed Communist trade union, as Spain's fragile transition to democracy strains against violence from the far right.
evt-01-24-1977-spanish-transition-to-dem.prompt: What happens when armed men burst into the office that night?

choices.text: They open fire, killing several people inside
They are chased off by police before entering
They plant a bomb that fails to detonate
They rob the office and leave without violence

evt-01-24-1977-spanish-transition-to-dem.butterflyEffect: Neo-fascist gunmen opened fire, killing five people, mostly labor lawyers, in what became known as the Atocha massacre. Rather than derailing the transition, the killings triggered a massive, peaceful demonstration in Madrid that strengthened public support for democratization and legalizing the Communist Party.

evt-01-24-1978-nuclear-power.scenario: It is late January 1978. You are a Canadian government scientist tracking reports that a failed Soviet reconnaissance satellite, Kosmos 954, has broken up over the Northwest Territories, scattering radioactive wreckage across the frozen wilderness.
evt-01-24-1978-nuclear-power.prompt: What joint mission is launched to find and recover the radioactive debris?

choices.text: Operation Paperclip
Operation Morning Light
Operation Ice Worm
Operation Deep Freeze

evt-01-24-1978-nuclear-power.butterflyEffect: The US and Canada mounted Operation Morning Light, a months-long search using aircraft and ground teams to recover irradiated fragments across the Arctic. Canada later billed the USSR roughly $6 million under the 1972 Liability Convention for Damage Caused by Space Objects, the only claim ever settled under that treaty.

evt-01-24-1978-soviet-union.scenario: It is January 1978, and you are a Canadian defense official racing to track a failing Soviet satellite carrying a nuclear reactor as it tumbles out of orbit toward Earth.
evt-01-24-1978-soviet-union.prompt: Where does the doomed Kosmos 954 satellite come down?

choices.text: The Norwegian Arctic
Siberia
The Australian outback
Northern Canada's Northwest Territories

evt-01-24-1978-soviet-union.butterflyEffect: Kosmos 954 scattered radioactive debris across a remote stretch of Canada's Northwest Territories, prompting the joint US-Canada cleanup effort known as Operation Morning Light. The incident intensified international debate over the safety of nuclear-powered satellites and spurred new guidelines on their use.

evt-01-24-1986-voyager-2.scenario: It is January 24, 1986, and you are a mission controller at JPL watching Voyager 2's instruments return the first close-up data ever gathered from Uranus, a planet no spacecraft has ever visited.
evt-01-24-1986-voyager-2.prompt: After this flyby, where does Voyager 2 travel next?

choices.text: Directly out of the Solar System, bypassing further planets
Back toward Saturn for a second pass
Pluto
Neptune

evt-01-24-1986-voyager-2.butterflyEffect: Voyager 2 used the encounter's gravity assist to head toward Neptune, which it reached in August 1989, becoming the only spacecraft ever to visit all four giant planets. Data from both ice giants reshaped scientific models of planetary magnetism and formation, and the probe continues transmitting from interstellar space today.

evt-01-24-1990-hiten-spacecraft.scenario: You are a JAXA engineer on 24 January 1990, watching the Hiten spacecraft lift off carrying a tiny companion probe, Hagoromo, meant to become Japan's first lunar orbiter.
evt-01-24-1990-hiten-spacecraft.prompt: What happens after Hagoromo separates and heads toward the Moon?

choices.text: Hagoromo's transmitter fails, so engineers repurpose Hiten for new tests
Hagoromo successfully orbits the Moon and transmits data for years
The mission is aborted before Hagoromo can separate
Hagoromo crashes into Hiten immediately after release

evt-01-24-1990-hiten-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: Hagoromo's radio transmitter failed shortly after release, so engineers instead used Hiten itself to test aerobraking and, in 1991, a pioneering low-energy 'ballistic capture' trajectory into lunar orbit. That fuel-saving technique, developed with mathematician Edward Belbruno, later influenced low-cost missions like ESA's SMART-1.

evt-01-24-2003-united-states-department-.scenario: It is 24 January 2003 in Washington. You work under Secretary Tom Ridge as the new Department of Homeland Security officially begins operating, absorbing agencies from across the federal government overnight.
evt-01-24-2003-united-states-department-.prompt: What organizational change actually underlies DHS's first day of operation?

choices.text: Twenty-two existing agencies are merged into one department
An entirely new agency is built with no existing staff
Homeland security duties are transferred to the Pentagon
The FBI's counterterrorism division is dissolved

evt-01-24-2003-united-states-department-.butterflyEffect: DHS folded 22 separate agencies—including the Coast Guard, Secret Service, and the old INS—into one department. That consolidation soon split immigration duties into ICE and CBP and placed the new TSA under DHS, permanently reshaping US border security and air travel.

evt-01-24-2009-cyclone-klaus.scenario: It is 24 January 2009 near Bordeaux. You manage pine plantations in the Landes forest as Cyclone Klaus roars in from the Atlantic with hurricane-force winds.
evt-01-24-2009-cyclone-klaus.prompt: What is the storm's major consequence for the region's forestry industry?

choices.text: It weakens before landfall and causes negligible damage
It disrupts Spanish energy production but leaves France untouched
It affects only offshore shipping, sparing the mainland
It devastates the Landes pine forest, destroying huge stocks of timber

evt-01-24-2009-cyclone-klaus.butterflyEffect: Klaus flattened vast stretches of the Landes pine forest, France's largest managed woodland, wiping out years of planned harvest in a single night. The scale of timber loss prompted emergency EU aid and a long, costly replanting effort that reshaped the regional economy for over a decade.

evt-01-24-2011-domodedovo-international-.scenario: It is the evening of 24 January 2011. You work security at Moscow's Domodedovo Airport, watching the crowded international arrivals hall where a man in a dark coat lingers near the barrier separating arriving passengers from greeters.
evt-01-24-2011-domodedovo-international-.prompt: What follows in the arrivals hall minutes later?

choices.text: He detonates a suicide bomb amid the crowd
He is stopped and arrested by airport police
He boards a departing flight without incident
He hijacks a baggage cart and flees the terminal

evt-01-24-2011-domodedovo-international-.butterflyEffect: A suicide bomber detonated an explosive device in the crowded arrivals hall, killing at least 35 people and wounding around 180. The attack, linked to the North Caucasus insurgency, exposed major gaps in Russian airport security and led to sweeping reforms in access control at the country's airports.

evt-01-24-2018-larry-nassar.scenario: It is January 2018 in a Michigan courtroom. For seven days you have listened as more than 150 survivors gave impact statements against the former USA Gymnastics doctor before you, the sentencing judge.
evt-01-24-2018-larry-nassar.prompt: What does Judge Rosemarie Aquilina do after hearing the survivors' statements?

choices.text: Grants him parole eligibility within five years
Orders a new trial due to procedural errors
Sentences him to up to 175 years in prison
Accepts a plea deal for a reduced sentence

evt-01-24-2018-larry-nassar.butterflyEffect: Aquilina handed Nassar a sentence of up to 175 years, on top of earlier federal charges. The public reckoning that followed forced resignations across USA Gymnastics and Michigan State's leadership and accelerated reforms in how sports institutions report and investigate abuse.

evt-01-25-1533-anne-boleyn.scenario: It is 25 January 1533. You are King Henry VIII, secretly wed to Anne Boleyn in a private ceremony even though your marriage to Catherine of Aragon has not yet been formally annulled by Rome. Anne is already pregnant, and you need the child declared legitimate before it is born.
evt-01-25-1533-anne-boleyn.prompt: How do you move to secure the legitimacy of your marriage to Anne?

choices.text: Have the newly appointed Archbishop of Canterbury declare your marriage to Catherine null
Ask the Holy Roman Emperor to mediate a settlement with Catherine
Wait quietly for the Pope in Rome to rule on the annulment first
Keep the marriage to Anne secret indefinitely to avoid scandal

evt-01-25-1533-anne-boleyn.butterflyEffect: Thomas Cranmer, newly installed as Archbishop of Canterbury, declared the marriage to Catherine void in May 1533, and Anne was crowned queen weeks later. The break with Rome that made this possible was cemented in law by the Act in Restraint of Appeals, launching the English Reformation and Henry's title as Supreme Head of the Church of England.

evt-01-25-1704-province-of-carolina.scenario: You are an Apalachee villager in Spanish Florida in January 1704, as English colonists from Carolina and their Creek allies, led by James Moore, sweep through the mission towns destroying settlements and taking captives.
evt-01-25-1704-province-of-carolina.prompt: What was the main purpose behind Carolina's raids on the Apalachee missions?

choices.text: To convert the Apalachee to the Church of England
To establish a new English colony on the ruins of the missions
To weaken Spanish Florida and capture people to sell into slavery during Queen Anne's War
To seize silver and treasure rumored to be stored in the missions

evt-01-25-1704-province-of-carolina.butterflyEffect: Moore's raids shattered the Apalachee mission system, killing and enslaving thousands and driving survivors from their homeland. The devastation crippled Spanish Florida's northern defenses and altered the regional balance of power well before Florida passed to Britain decades later.

evt-01-25-1765-port-egmont.scenario: January 1765: you command a Royal Navy expedition sent to plant Britain's flag in the Falkland Islands before France or Spain can claim them outright. You have just brought your ship to anchor off a small island on the western side of the archipelago.
evt-01-25-1765-port-egmont.prompt: What do you do to found Britain's claim on the spot?

choices.text: Sail on to chart the whole archipelago before landing anyone
Send word home and wait for reinforcements before disembarking
Seek out Spanish officials nearby to negotiate joint use of the islands
Build a fort, raise the flag, and establish a garrison immediately

evt-01-25-1765-port-egmont.butterflyEffect: MacBride's men built a fort and garrison, naming it Port Egmont after the First Lord of the Admiralty. Unknown to the British at first, the French had already settled the eastern islands, and Spain soon bought them out — rival claims that erupted into the near-war Falklands Crisis of 1770 and echoed all the way to the 1982 Falklands War.

evt-01-25-1890-nellie-bly.scenario: You are journalist Nellie Bly in January 1890, racing to beat both Jules Verne's fictional eighty days and rival reporter Elizabeth Bisland across America to finish your circumnavigation for the New York World.
evt-01-25-1890-nellie-bly.prompt: How does Bly cover the final stretch across the United States in record time?

choices.text: Aboard a naval vessel loaned by the government
By stagecoach across the plains
Aboard a special chartered train arranged by her newspaper
By taking ordinary scheduled passenger trains

evt-01-25-1890-nellie-bly.butterflyEffect: The World arranged a private special train that raced Bly from San Francisco to New Jersey, letting her complete the circuit in 72 days, 6 hours and 11 minutes, beating Bisland and Verne's fictional record. Her celebrity fueled the rise of 'stunt girl' journalism and cemented the idea that women reporters could headline major news events.

evt-01-25-1932-alt-llobregat-insurrectio.scenario: It's late January 1932 in Fígols, Catalonia. You're a coal miner who has just watched fellow workers disarm the local police and seize the town hall in a spontaneous general strike that is spreading through the region.
evt-01-25-1932-alt-llobregat-insurrectio.prompt: What system do the rebelling miners declare in the towns they now control?

choices.text: A workers' soviet aligned with Moscow
A restored monarchist administration
An independent Catalan nationalist republic
Libertarian communism

evt-01-25-1932-alt-llobregat-insurrectio.butterflyEffect: The miners proclaimed libertarian communism, but within a week the Spanish Army crushed the revolt and a similar rising in Aragon. The crackdown split the CNT, with the moderate faction breaking away to form the Syndicalist Party, and further anarchist insurrections followed in 1933.

evt-01-25-1971-idi-amin.scenario: It is 25 January 1971, and Kampala radio has just announced that General Idi Amin has seized control of Uganda while President Milton Obote is abroad at a Commonwealth summit. Soldiers across the capital are choosing which side to back.
evt-01-25-1971-idi-amin.prompt: What did Amin's seizure of power lead to over the next eight years?

choices.text: Uganda's peaceful admission to the East African Federation
A swift return to civilian rule under Obote
Mass killings and the expulsion of Uganda's Asian minority
A period of economic growth and improved international relations

evt-01-25-1971-idi-amin.butterflyEffect: Amin ruled Uganda as a brutal dictator until 1979, ordering the 1972 expulsion of the Asian community and presiding over killings estimated at 100,000 to 500,000 people. His regime wrecked Uganda's economy and international standing, and he was only removed after Tanzanian forces and Ugandan exiles invaded in the Uganda–Tanzania War.

evt-01-25-1990-avianca-flight-052.scenario: It's the night of January 25, 1990. You are the co-pilot of Avianca Flight 052, holding in a stack over New York after repeated diversions for fog, and the fuel gauges are dropping toward empty.
evt-01-25-1990-avianca-flight-052.prompt: What should you tell air traffic control right now?

choices.text: Ask for priority landing without mentioning fuel status
Formally declare a fuel emergency using the word "emergency"
Divert silently to Boston without notifying ATC of your fuel state
Keep reporting "low on fuel" without a formal declaration

evt-01-25-1990-avianca-flight-052.butterflyEffect: The crew reported being 'low on fuel' but never used the word 'emergency,' so controllers kept them in the normal sequence. The 707 ran dry and crashed in Cove Neck, killing 73. The NTSB's findings led the FAA and ICAO to mandate standardized fuel-emergency phrasing worldwide.

evt-01-25-1993-mir-aimal-kansi.scenario: It is early 1993. You lead the FBI task force hunting the gunman who opened fire on CIA employees outside Langley headquarters before vanishing across the border into Afghanistan.
evt-01-25-1993-mir-aimal-kansi.prompt: Four years into the manhunt, where should international investigators concentrate the search?

choices.text: Iran, assuming safe haven from a hostile government
Afghanistan, where he first fled
Saudi Arabia, tracing family connections
Pakistan, drawing on local police cooperation

evt-01-25-1993-mir-aimal-kansi.butterflyEffect: Kansi was eventually located hiding in Pakistan and captured in 1997 with the help of Pakistani police working alongside the FBI. He was extradited, convicted of capital murder, and executed by lethal injection in 2002, closing one of the CIA's most high-profile domestic security breaches.

evt-01-25-1995-black-brant-rocket.scenario: It is 25 January 1995, and Russian early-warning radar detects a large rocket rising from Norway on a trajectory resembling a submarine-launched ballistic missile aimed at Russian territory. You are the duty officer who must decide how to respond.
evt-01-25-1995-black-brant-rocket.prompt: What is the correct next step given the ambiguous radar track?

choices.text: Escalate to command authority while awaiting further tracking data
Dismiss the reading as a radar glitch
Scramble interceptor aircraft to destroy the rocket
Order immediate retaliatory missile launch

evt-01-25-1995-black-brant-rocket.butterflyEffect: The alert was passed up the chain to President Boris Yeltsin, who had his nuclear command "football" activated for the first and only time before the rocket's harmless scientific trajectory was confirmed. The episode, since called the Norwegian rocket incident, exposed how close a routine research launch had come to triggering a nuclear response and pushed for better prior notification between nations.

evt-01-25-2004-mars-exploration-rover.scenario: It is 25 January 2004, and images beam back from Mars showing your rover Opportunity has bounced to rest inside a small crater, its cameras staring straight at an exposed rock outcrop no one planned for.
evt-01-25-2004-mars-exploration-rover.prompt: What should the mission team prioritize with this unexpected outcrop?

choices.text: Drive away immediately toward flatter, safer terrain
Ignore it and head straight for the crater rim
Shut down instruments to conserve power for the journey ahead
Examine the outcrop's rock and chemistry before moving on

evt-01-25-2004-mars-exploration-rover.butterflyEffect: Scientists directed Opportunity to examine the outcrop first, and its instruments soon found hematite-rich "blueberries" and layered rock chemistry pointing to ancient standing water. The find launched more than a decade of roving evidence that Mars once had a wetter, potentially habitable past.

evt-01-25-2006-ogle-2005-blg-390lb.scenario: You are an astronomer with the PLANET/OGLE microlensing network in early 2006, watching the brightness of a distant background star as a foreground object drifts across your line of sight. A small, brief dip breaks the smooth lensing curve.
evt-01-25-2006-ogle-2005-blg-390lb.prompt: What does this anomaly in the light curve most likely reveal?

choices.text: A faulty telescope sensor
An unrelated variable background star
A low-mass planet orbiting the lensing star
Interstellar dust dimming the light briefly

evt-01-25-2006-ogle-2005-blg-390lb.butterflyEffect: The anomaly confirmed a low-mass, icy planet orbiting a faint star some 21,500 light-years away, announced jointly by three collaborations on 25 January 2006. It stood among the smallest and most distant exoplanets found at the time, proving gravitational microlensing could detect worlds far beyond the reach of other methods.

evt-01-25-2011-arab-spring.scenario: It's January 25, 2011, the "Day of Anger." You march with thousands of Egyptians toward Tahrir Square, chanting against police brutality, corruption, and decades of stagnant rule.
evt-01-25-2011-arab-spring.prompt: What becomes the movement's central demand in the days ahead?

choices.text: Immediate multiparty elections while Mubarak stays in office
Restoration of the pre-1952 monarchy
A military coup installing army rule
The resignation of President Hosni Mubarak

evt-01-25-2011-arab-spring.butterflyEffect: The chant "Erhal" ("Leave!") became the movement's rallying cry, and eighteen days of sustained occupation of Tahrir Square followed. On February 11, 1911, Hosni Mubarak resigned after 30 years in power, and the moment became a catalyst for uprisings across the wider Arab world.

evt-01-25-2015-mamasapano-clash.scenario: You are a Philippine senator on 25 January 2015, reading reports that a police raid in Mamasapano, Maguindanao has ended in a bloody firefight after the SAF killed wanted bomber Zulkifli bin Hir. The Bangsamoro peace deal you support is suddenly in jeopardy.
evt-01-25-2015-mamasapano-clash.prompt: What did the Mamasapano clash do to the pending Bangsamoro Basic Law?

choices.text: It sailed through Congress with new urgency
It had no effect on the legislative process
It stalled the bill amid public anger and mistrust of the MILF
It caused the bill's immediate passage into law

evt-01-25-2015-mamasapano-clash.butterflyEffect: The deaths of 44 SAF commandos, alongside Moro combatants and civilians, triggered public outrage that stalled the Bangsamoro Basic Law for over a year and deepened distrust between government and MILF negotiators. The peace process eventually resumed, and a revised law creating the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region was finally passed in 2018.

evt-01-25-2019-brumadinho-dam-disaster.scenario: It's the aftermath of January 25, 2019, in Minas Gerais, Brazil. You are a mining safety regulator surveying the wreckage of the Córrego do Feijão tailings dam, Vale's second catastrophic dam failure in under four years.
evt-01-25-2019-brumadinho-dam-disaster.prompt: What sweeping change does Brazil push for in the disaster's wake?

choices.text: Vale commits to decommissioning all upstream tailings dams nationwide
Brazil nationalizes Vale's entire mining operation
The government permanently bans iron ore mining
International sanctions are imposed on Brazilian mining exports

evt-01-25-2019-brumadinho-dam-disaster.butterflyEffect: Courts ordered Vale to decommission its remaining upstream tailings dams across Brazil, and the company faced billions in fines and criminal charges against executives. The disaster also helped drive the 2020 Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management, reshaping mine-safety rules worldwide.

evt-01-26-661-ali.scenario: It is dawn in the mosque of Kufa. You kneel nearby as Caliph Ali leads the morning prayer, unaware that a man named Ibn Muljim has concealed a poisoned sword beneath his cloak and is stepping forward.
evt-01-26-661-ali.prompt: What actually happened when Ibn Muljim struck during the prayer?

choices.text: He was poisoned through food served at a feast
He was shot with a poisoned arrow from a rooftop
He was struck with a poisoned sword during prayer
He drowned after being pushed into a well

evt-01-26-661-ali.butterflyEffect: Ali was struck with a poisoned sword and died two days later from his wound. His death ended the Rashidun Caliphate and opened the way for Muawiyah's Umayyad dynasty, while deepening the Sunni-Shia division that still shapes Islamic history; his tomb in Najaf remains one of Shia Islam's holiest sites.

evt-01-26-1564-livonian-war.scenario: It is 26 January 1564 near the Ula River in Lithuania. You ride with Hetman Mikołaj Radziwiłł's small Lithuanian force, shadowing a far larger Russian army marching toward Vilnius.
evt-01-26-1564-livonian-war.prompt: What should Radziwiłł's outnumbered force do to beat the larger Russian army?

choices.text: Split forces and strike toward Moscow, bypassing the army in the field
Launch a surprise ambush while the Russian column is strung out and unprepared
Negotiate a truce to delay the Russian advance
Retreat to fortified positions and wait for Polish reinforcements

evt-01-26-1564-livonian-war.butterflyEffect: Radziwiłł's surprise attack shattered the far larger Russian column at the Battle of Ula, one of the war's most lopsided Lithuanian victories. It slowed Russia's advance into Lithuania and lifted morale, though the wider Livonian War dragged on for nearly twenty more years before ending in Poland-Lithuania's favor.

evt-01-26-1700-1700-cascadia-earthquake.scenario: It is late January 1700, and you keep the chronicle for a fishing village on the coast of Japan. In the night, without any earthquake to explain it, seawater surges through the streets and recedes just as strangely.
evt-01-26-1700-1700-cascadia-earthquake.prompt: With no tremor felt locally, what cause do you record for the flooding?

choices.text: A distant undersea earthquake, cause unknown
An unusually strong lunar tide
A volcanic eruption beneath the sea
A typhoon churning far offshore

evt-01-26-1700-1700-cascadia-earthquake.butterflyEffect: No quake was ever felt in Japan because the true source lay across the Pacific: a massive rupture of the Cascadia subduction zone off North America. Centuries later, seismologists matched these Japanese 'orphan tsunami' records with tree-ring and tribal evidence in the Pacific Northwest to date the quake to 26 January 1700 with startling precision.

evt-01-26-1788-arthur-phillip.scenario: It is 26 January 1788. You are Captain Arthur Phillip, having led the First Fleet's eleven ships into Sydney Cove after finding Botany Bay unfit for settlement.
evt-01-26-1788-arthur-phillip.prompt: What is Phillip's first act upon landing at Sydney Cove?

choices.text: Raise the British flag and found a penal colony
Negotiate a formal treaty with local Aboriginal peoples
Search the coastline for gold deposits
Build a fort to repel expected French rivals

evt-01-26-1788-arthur-phillip.butterflyEffect: Phillip raised the British flag and founded the penal colony of New South Wales, beginning continuous British settlement of Australia. The date later became Australia Day, a national holiday now contested by many Indigenous Australians as marking invasion and dispossession.

evt-01-26-1808-william-bligh.scenario: It is 26 January 1808 in Sydney. As governor of New South Wales, you have clashed repeatedly with wealthy officer John Macarthur and the New South Wales Corps over trade in rum, and now armed soldiers are marching on Government House.
evt-01-26-1808-william-bligh.prompt: What do the New South Wales Corps do to Governor Bligh on this day?

choices.text: They arrest him and depose him as governor
They execute him immediately for treason
They persuade him to resign the governorship voluntarily
They escort him peacefully onto a ship home

evt-01-26-1808-william-bligh.butterflyEffect: The Corps arrested and deposed Bligh in what became known as the Rum Rebellion, the only successful armed takeover of government in Australian history. The officers involved were later court-martialled in London, and Lachlan Macquarie was sent as the new governor to restore order and reform the colony.

evt-01-26-1841-gordon-bremer.scenario: It's 26 January 1841 at a rocky harbor on the coast of China. You stand among Commodore Gordon Bremer's landing party as they raise the Union Jack over a sparsely populated island called Hong Kong.
evt-01-26-1841-gordon-bremer.prompt: What did Bremer's act formally begin for Britain?

choices.text: A full military occupation of Canton and the Pearl River Delta
A temporary naval base with no claim to sovereignty
British possession of Hong Kong Island, later confirmed by treaty
The immediate annexation of the entire Chinese mainland coast

evt-01-26-1841-gordon-bremer.butterflyEffect: Bremer's landing at what became known as Possession Point began British rule over Hong Kong, soon claimed under the Convention of Chuenpi and later formalized by the Treaty of Nanking in 1842. Hong Kong grew into a major trading colony and remained under British control until 1997.

evt-01-26-1885-mahdist-war.scenario: It is January 1885 and you are General Charles Gordon, besieged inside Khartoum for months as Mahdist forces tighten their grip on the city, with a British relief column still far away on the Nile.
evt-01-26-1885-mahdist-war.prompt: What does Gordon decide as the Mahdist forces close in on Khartoum?

choices.text: Negotiate a surrender with the Mahdist commanders
Hold the city and wait for the British relief force
Flee the city alone disguised as a merchant
Evacuate the garrison by boat down the Nile at night

evt-01-26-1885-mahdist-war.butterflyEffect: Gordon chose to hold the city and await British relief, but Khartoum fell and he was killed just two days before the relief expedition arrived. His death caused a public outcry in Britain, became a symbol of imperial martyrdom, and contributed to the political downfall of Gladstone's government.

evt-01-26-1918-red-guards-finland.scenario: It's the night of 26 January 1918 in Helsinki. You watch Red Guard fighters climb the tower of the Workers' House and hang a red lantern, the signal thousands of socialist workers have been waiting for.
evt-01-26-1918-red-guards-finland.prompt: What did the lantern signal to Red forces across Finland?

choices.text: A call to negotiate a peaceful transfer of power with the Senate
The beginning of a general strike, not an armed uprising
The start of the armed uprising that launched the Finnish Civil War
An order for Red forces to retreat from Helsinki to Tampere

evt-01-26-1918-red-guards-finland.butterflyEffect: The lantern launched the Finnish Civil War between the Red Guards, backed by revolutionary sentiment from Russia, and the White Guards under General Mannerheim. The brutal months-long conflict ended in a White victory, but the divisions it exposed over class and politics shaped Finnish society for decades.

evt-01-26-1926-oliver-hutchinson.scenario: It is January 1926 in a cramped attic laboratory in London's Soho. Your old friend John Logie Baird asks you to sit before his crude, whirring device so he can prove to onlookers that his invention can transmit a moving image.
evt-01-26-1926-oliver-hutchinson.prompt: What do you do when Baird asks you to be the subject of his demonstration?

choices.text: Suggest testing with a mannequin first for safety
Agree to sit as the subject of the demonstration
Refuse, fearing the untested device is dangerous
Insist a paid actor be used instead of himself

evt-01-26-1926-oliver-hutchinson.butterflyEffect: Hutchinson agreed, and his flickering image became one of the first ever seen on television in a successful public demonstration. His willingness to fund and publicise Baird's work helped launch the Baird Television Development Company, and Hutchinson later stood alongside Baird for the first trans-Atlantic television broadcast in 1928.

evt-01-26-1934-apollo-theater.scenario: It's January 1934. You are the new manager of the old burlesque house on 125th Street in Harlem, forced to close after New York banned burlesque. The neighbourhood around you is now overwhelmingly Black, but the theater's old policy barred Black patrons from its seats.
evt-01-26-1934-apollo-theater.prompt: What do you do to fill the house and reopen the theater?

choices.text: Revive burlesque shows under a new name to dodge the ban
Convert the building into a movie house exclusively
Keep the whites-only policy and hope for downtown crowds
Open the doors to Black audiences and showcase Black performers

evt-01-26-1934-apollo-theater.butterflyEffect: The theater reopened as the Apollo, threw open its doors to Black audiences, and launched Amateur Night, discovering talents like Ella Fitzgerald that same year. It became the premier stage of Black American music and comedy for the rest of the century, later giving its name to television's Showtime at the Apollo.

evt-01-26-1945-audie-murphy.scenario: It is 26 January 1945 near the Colmar Pocket in France. Your infantry company has been driven back by advancing German tanks and troops, and you alone remain forward, wounded, standing atop a burning tank destroyer.
evt-01-26-1945-audie-murphy.prompt: What do you do to hold the line?

choices.text: Surrender the position to save the men
Order an immediate retreat to safer ground
Man the vehicle's gun and call artillery onto your own position
Dig in silently and wait for reinforcements

evt-01-26-1945-audie-murphy.butterflyEffect: Murphy manned the tank destroyer's machine gun for almost an hour while directing artillery fire onto his own position by field telephone, then led a counterattack despite his wounds. The stand earned him the Medal of Honor and made him, by war's end, the most decorated American combat soldier of the conflict, later launching a Hollywood acting career.

evt-01-26-1949-hale-telescope.scenario: It's the late 1940s on Palomar Mountain. After years of delay through the Depression and the war, engineers are finishing the 200-inch Pyrex mirror for the world's largest telescope, and it must hold its shape precisely as it swings across the night sky without sagging under its own enormous weight.
evt-01-26-1949-hale-telescope.prompt: What design do the engineers use to keep the giant mirror light and rigid?

choices.text: A metal-backed mirror instead of glass entirely
A single solid disk of thick Pyrex glass
A ribbed honeycomb structure cast into the Pyrex blank
A mirror made of many small hexagonal segments

evt-01-26-1949-hale-telescope.butterflyEffect: The finished mirror used a ribbed honeycomb structure to cut weight while keeping it thermally stable, a solution that made the Hale Telescope's unprecedented resolving power possible when it began work in 1949. The design influenced large-telescope engineering for decades, until segmented-mirror designs like Keck Observatory's eventually surpassed it in the 1990s.

evt-01-26-1950-indian-independence-movem.scenario: It is 26 January 1950 in New Delhi. The British Raj ended nearly three years ago, and this morning a new constitution comes into force, transforming the dominion of India into a sovereign republic.
evt-01-26-1950-indian-independence-movem.prompt: Who becomes India's first president under the new constitution?

choices.text: Jawaharlal Nehru
Vallabhbhai Patel
Mahatma Gandhi
Rajendra Prasad

evt-01-26-1950-indian-independence-movem.butterflyEffect: Rajendra Prasad became India's first president, a largely ceremonial head of state, while Jawaharlal Nehru continued as prime minister leading the government. This split established the parliamentary republic model India still follows, and 26 January is celebrated annually as Republic Day.

evt-01-26-1952-cairo-fire.scenario: It is 26 January 1952. You own a shop in downtown Cairo, and rioters furious over the killing of Egyptian police at Ismailia are burning cinemas, hotels, and businesses associated with foreigners around you.
evt-01-26-1952-cairo-fire.prompt: What does King Farouk's government do in response that same day?

choices.text: Invite British troops into Cairo to restore order
Dismiss the government and declare martial law
Grant Ismailia's police force full independence from Britain
Immediately outlaw the Muslim Brotherhood

evt-01-26-1952-cairo-fire.butterflyEffect: Farouk dismissed Prime Minister Nahhas's government that day and declared martial law, but the unrest exposed how fragile his rule had become. Within six months, the Free Officers Movement led by Nasser and Naguib overthrew the monarchy in the July 1952 revolution.

evt-01-26-1972-jat-flight-367.scenario: It is the afternoon of 26 January 1972. You are a flight attendant aboard JAT Flight 367, cruising at altitude over Czechoslovakia en route from Stockholm to Belgrade, when a violent explosion tears through the cabin.
evt-01-26-1972-jat-flight-367.prompt: What did investigators conclude caused the aircraft to break apart in mid-air?

choices.text: Lightning struck the fuselage during a storm
A bomb concealed aboard the aircraft detonated
Metal fatigue caused the cabin to depressurise suddenly
A catastrophic engine failure caused structural collapse

evt-01-26-1972-jat-flight-367.butterflyEffect: Investigators determined a bomb, likely hidden in the cargo hold, tore the DC-9 apart at high altitude, killing 27 of the 28 aboard. Stewardess Vesna Vulović fell over 10,000 metres trapped in the tail section and miraculously survived, later becoming a national hero and the record holder for the highest fall survived without a parachute.

evt-01-26-1998-bill-clinton.scenario: It is 26 January 1998. You are President Bill Clinton, standing before television cameras in the White House as reporters press you about your relationship with a former intern.
evt-01-26-1998-bill-clinton.prompt: What do you say at the press conference?

choices.text: Admit to an affair and apologize immediately
Refuse to answer any questions on the matter
Firmly and flatly deny any sexual relationship
Announce his resignation on the spot

evt-01-26-1998-bill-clinton.butterflyEffect: Clinton firmly denied any sexual relationship, famously stating, 'I did not have sexual relations with that woman, Miss Lewinsky.' The statement later proved false, fueling the perjury and obstruction charges that led to his impeachment by the House later that year, though the Senate acquitted him in 1999.

evt-01-26-2001-2001-gujarat-earthquake.scenario: It is 26 January 2001, hours after a devastating earthquake has leveled towns across Kutch district in Gujarat. You sit on the emergency committee tasked with India's long-term response to disasters like this one.
evt-01-26-2001-2001-gujarat-earthquake.prompt: What lasting institutional change does India make in the aftermath?

choices.text: Relocate the national capital away from seismic zones
Establish a national disaster management authority
Withdraw from international earthquake monitoring treaties
Ban all multi-story construction nationwide

evt-01-26-2001-2001-gujarat-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The scale of destruction in Gujarat exposed how unprepared India was for disasters, prompting the government to overhaul its approach. This led to the Disaster Management Act of 2005 and the creation of the National Disaster Management Authority to coordinate future emergency response nationwide.

evt-01-26-2009-antananarivo.scenario: It is 26 January 2009 in Antananarivo. You run a small shop as opposition supporters loyal to Andry Rajoelina clash violently with President Ravalomanana's government in the streets around you.
evt-01-26-2009-antananarivo.prompt: What does this unrest ultimately lead to in the months that follow?

choices.text: Ravalomanana is forced to hand power to Rajoelina
Madagascar's monarchy is restored to end the unrest
The United Nations installs a temporary government
The crisis ends quietly with Ravalomanana's re-election

evt-01-26-2009-antananarivo.butterflyEffect: The riots marked the start of a political crisis that deepened over the following weeks. By March 2009, the military had turned against Ravalomanana, forcing him to hand power to Rajoelina in what was widely regarded internationally as a coup.

evt-01-26-2015-2015-los-llanos-air-base-.scenario: It's 26 January 2015 at Los Llanos Air Base in Albacete, Spain, where NATO's Tactical Leadership Programme has gathered pilots and ground crews from across Europe. You watch a Hellenic Air Force F-16D roar down the runway before it suddenly slams into a line of parked jets and personnel on the flight line.
evt-01-26-2015-2015-los-llanos-air-base-.prompt: What did the crash mean for the multinational training program at Albacete?

choices.text: The exercise was suspended and flight-line safety procedures were later reviewed
NATO grounded every F-16 in Europe indefinitely
The program was permanently disbanded and never reconvened
Spain expelled the Hellenic Air Force from all future exercises

evt-01-26-2015-2015-los-llanos-air-base-.butterflyEffect: The crash killed 11 people, most of them ground personnel struck on the flight line, making it the deadliest accident in the program's history. Training was suspended in its wake, Greece grounded its F-16 fleet pending investigation, and flight-line safety procedures at multinational exercises came under fresh scrutiny.

evt-01-27-945-stephen-lekapenos.scenario: It is December 944 in Constantinople. You and your brother Constantine have just forced your ailing father, Emperor Romanos I, into a monastery and seized the throne for yourselves, though your brother-in-law Constantine VII still shares the imperial title.
evt-01-27-945-stephen-lekapenos.prompt: What happens to you and your brother in the weeks that follow your coup?

choices.text: You rule jointly with Constantine VII for decades in peace
You are tried and executed for treason
You are overthrown and exiled by Constantine VII
You restore your father Romanos I to the throne

evt-01-27-945-stephen-lekapenos.butterflyEffect: Within weeks the legitimate emperor Constantine VII, backed by the populace and palace guard, turned the tables and had Stephen and Constantine seized and exiled. Stephen lived out his days on Lesbos, dying on Easter 963, while Constantine VII went on to preside over a celebrated revival of Byzantine scholarship and law.

evt-01-27-1785-university-of-georgia.scenario: It is January 1785 and you sit in the Georgia legislature debating a charter to create a new institution of higher learning for the young state.
evt-01-27-1785-university-of-georgia.prompt: What did the charter you approved establish?

choices.text: A vocational school for agricultural trades only
A military academy for state defense
The first state-chartered public university in the United States
A private seminary funded by church donations

evt-01-27-1785-university-of-georgia.butterflyEffect: The charter created the University of Georgia, the first state-chartered public university in the United States. It later grew into the flagship of the University System of Georgia and set a precedent for public higher education nationwide.

evt-01-27-1869-tokugawa-shogunate.scenario: It is January 1869 on the northern island of Ezo. Admiral Enomoto Takeaki and the last loyal remnants of the Tokugawa navy and samurai, having fled the fallen shogunate, have just declared a breakaway state and elected him its president.
evt-01-27-1869-tokugawa-shogunate.prompt: What is the ultimate fate of Enomoto's breakaway republic?

choices.text: Western powers recognize it as an independent nation
It expands southward to conquer Honshu
It is crushed by Imperial forces within months, ending organized resistance
It peacefully merges into the Meiji government by treaty

evt-01-27-1869-tokugawa-shogunate.butterflyEffect: Imperial forces crushed the Republic of Ezo at the Battle of Hakodate in June 1869, ending the Boshin War and cementing Meiji rule over all of Japan.
