Enomoto himself was later pardoned and went on to serve as a minister in the very government he had fought, symbolizing the reconciliation of former shogunate loyalists with the new order.

evt-01-27-1927-bundaberg-tragedy.scenario: It is January 1928 in Bundaberg, Queensland. Doctors are drawing doses from a multi-use vial of diphtheria vaccine that has been punctured repeatedly over several days without the antiseptic precautions later standard practice demands.
evt-01-27-1927-bundaberg-tragedy.prompt: What lasting change did the resulting inquiry force upon vaccine handling?

choices.text: Sterile single-dose vials and preservative use became mandatory
All childhood immunisation programs were suspended for a decade
Diphtheria vaccination was banned across Australia
The vaccine manufacturer was seized by the government

evt-01-27-1927-bundaberg-tragedy.butterflyEffect: A royal commission found the vial had become contaminated with Staphylococcus aureus after repeated unsterile puncturing, killing twelve children. The tragedy pushed Australia and other countries toward single-dose sterile ampoules and the routine addition of preservatives, reshaping vaccine safety standards internationally.

evt-01-27-1945-auschwitz-concentration-c.scenario: It is 27 January 1945. Soldiers of the Soviet Red Army approach the gates of Auschwitz and find the SS guards gone, leaving behind a small number of starving, ill survivors.
evt-01-27-1945-auschwitz-concentration-c.prompt: What do the liberating Soviet troops do upon entering the camp?

choices.text: Send survivors home before recording any evidence
Immediately demolish all camp structures
Hand the camp over to Polish civilian authorities at once
Document the camp's conditions and give aid to survivors

evt-01-27-1945-auschwitz-concentration-c.butterflyEffect: Soviet forces documented the camp's atrocities in photographs and testimony while giving aid to survivors. That evidence became central to postwar trials of Nazi perpetrators, and the anniversary is now observed worldwide as International Holocaust Remembrance Day.

evt-01-27-1965-tran-van-huong.scenario: It is January 1965 in Saigon, and Buddhist-led unrest has paralyzed the government of Prime Minister Trần Văn Hương. General Nguyễn Khánh's military junta meets to decide his fate.
evt-01-27-1965-tran-van-huong.prompt: What did the junta do to Prime Minister Trần Văn Hương?

choices.text: Had him executed for treason
Removed him from the premiership
Exiled him permanently from Vietnam
Reappointed him for another full term

evt-01-27-1965-tran-van-huong.butterflyEffect: The junta removed Hương from office after only three months, reflecting the instability plaguing South Vietnam's leadership. He would resurface as prime minister again in 1968–69 and briefly become president in the chaotic final week before Saigon's fall in 1975.

evt-01-27-1967-apollo-1.scenario: It is 27 January 1967 at Cape Kennedy. Astronauts Grissom, White, and Chaffee are sealed inside the Apollo 1 command module in a pure-oxygen atmosphere for a routine launch rehearsal when a spark ignites a fire they cannot escape in time.
evt-01-27-1967-apollo-1.prompt: What did NASA do to the Apollo program in the fire's aftermath?

choices.text: Switched cabin atmosphere without any hardware changes
Canceled the crewed lunar program entirely
Launched the next crewed mission on schedule with the same design
Grounded the program for a major command module redesign

evt-01-27-1967-apollo-1.butterflyEffect: NASA halted crewed flights for 21 months while redesigning the command module with an outward-opening quick-release hatch, non-flammable materials, and a safer ground-test atmosphere. Those changes underpinned the success of Apollo 7 and, ultimately, the 1969 Moon landing.

evt-01-27-1980-iran-hostage-crisis.scenario: It is late January 1980. Six American diplomats who evaded the embassy seizure have been sheltering secretly in Tehran for months, and a plan is finally in place to get them out of Iran.
evt-01-27-1980-iran-hostage-crisis.prompt: How do the six diplomats manage to escape Iran undetected?

choices.text: Posing as a Canadian film crew with forged passports
Being extracted by a covert US special forces raid
Bribing airport officials with smuggled gold
Walking overland across the border into Turkey

evt-01-27-1980-iran-hostage-crisis.butterflyEffect: Canadian ambassador Ken Taylor and the CIA arranged forged Canadian passports, letting the six pose as a film crew and fly out on a commercial flight. Dubbed the 'Canadian Caper,' it stood as a rare bright spot in the crisis and was later dramatized in the film Argo.

evt-01-27-1996-mahamane-ousmane.scenario: It is late January 1996 in Niamey. You are an aide to President Mahamane Ousmane, Niger's first democratically elected leader, as soldiers under Colonel Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara surround the presidential palace demanding his resignation.
evt-01-27-1996-mahamane-ousmane.prompt: What actually happened next to Ousmane's government?

choices.text: Foreign peacekeepers intervened to restore him within days
Parliament negotiated a power-sharing deal that kept Ousmane in office
He was deposed, and Baré Maïnassara seized power in a military takeover
Ousmane rallied loyal troops and crushed the coup attempt

evt-01-27-1996-mahamane-ousmane.butterflyEffect: Baré Maïnassara's coup succeeded, and he ruled Niger until soldiers assassinated him in 1999. A transitional government then restored elections, and Ousmane re-entered politics, repeatedly running for president in the years that followed.

evt-01-27-2010-porfirio-lobo-sosa.scenario: On 27 January 2010 you take the presidential oath in Tegucigalpa. Honduras is still reeling from the 2009 coup that ousted Manuel Zelaya, and several governments, including the United States, have yet to recognize your election as legitimate.
evt-01-27-2010-porfirio-lobo-sosa.prompt: What step did Lobo take to help end Honduras's diplomatic isolation?

choices.text: He annexed opposition strongholds and banned Zelaya's party outright
He formed a truth commission and pursued reconciliation with Zelaya's supporters
He nationalized foreign-owned industries to appease critics
He reinstated Zelaya as co-president to share power

evt-01-27-2010-porfirio-lobo-sosa.butterflyEffect: Lobo established a Truth and Reconciliation Commission to investigate the coup and its aftermath, easing tensions with Zelaya's allies. The move helped Honduras win readmission to the Organization of American States in 2011, restoring broader international recognition.

evt-01-27-2011-arab-spring.scenario: It is 27 January 2011 in Sana'a, Yemen. More than 16,000 protesters, inspired by Tunisia's uprising weeks earlier, fill the streets demanding change from a president who has ruled for over three decades.
evt-01-27-2011-arab-spring.prompt: What is the central demand of the protesters at this rally?

choices.text: Independence for South Yemen only
The resignation of President Ali Abdullah Saleh
Immediate war with Saudi Arabia
Restoration of the old monarchy

evt-01-27-2011-arab-spring.butterflyEffect: The demonstrations grew into the Yemeni Revolution, and President Ali Abdullah Saleh eventually resigned in 2012 after 33 years in power. The resulting power vacuum, however, contributed to the civil war that has devastated Yemen since 2014.

evt-01-27-2013-kiss-nightclub-fire.scenario: It is the early hours of 27 January 2013 in Santa Maria, Brazil. A band's pyrotechnic display ignites the acoustic foam lining the Kiss nightclub's ceiling, and smoke quickly fills the crowded room.
evt-01-27-2013-kiss-nightclub-fire.prompt: What structural failure most worsened the disaster that followed?

choices.text: Overcrowding caused by counterfeit tickets
A gas leak from the kitchen
Faulty electrical wiring in the DJ booth
Flammable soundproofing foam and only one usable exit

evt-01-27-2013-kiss-nightclub-fire.butterflyEffect: The flammable foam and the club's single, hard-to-find exit trapped hundreds inside as power failed, killing 242 people. The tragedy forced Brazil to overhaul fire-safety codes and licensing for nightclubs nationwide, and several owners and band members were later convicted of manslaughter.

evt-01-27-2023-tyre-nichols-protests.scenario: It is January 27, 2023, in Memphis, and police have just released body-camera footage showing officers beating Tyre Nichols, who died from his injuries days later. Crowds are gathering in the streets.
evt-01-27-2023-tyre-nichols-protests.prompt: What did protesters demand from city and police officials after the footage aired?

choices.text: Immediate deployment of the National Guard to patrol Memphis
A federal takeover of the Memphis Police Department
Accountability for the officers and broader police-reform measures
The resignation of the state governor

evt-01-27-2023-tyre-nichols-protests.butterflyEffect: The five officers involved were fired and charged with second-degree murder, and Memphis disbanded the specialized SCORPION unit they belonged to. The case reignited a national push for police accountability legislation and stricter use-of-force policies.

evt-01-27-2023-2023-neve-yaakov-shooting.scenario: It is the evening of January 27, 2023, in Neve Yaakov, East Jerusalem. A gunman opens fire on worshippers leaving a synagogue, and police officers race to confront him.
evt-01-27-2023-2023-neve-yaakov-shooting.prompt: How did the attack end for the gunman?

choices.text: He fled and was captured weeks later
He was arrested and later stood trial
He was shot and killed by police at the scene
He surrendered after negotiations

evt-01-27-2023-2023-neve-yaakov-shooting.butterflyEffect: He was shot dead by responding police after opening fire on officers. It was Israel's deadliest peacetime Palestinian attack since 2008, deepening tensions and prompting tightened security measures across East Jerusalem in the days that followed.

evt-01-28-1393-charles-vi-of-france.scenario: It's 28 January 1393 at a masked ball in Paris, and you are one of six young nobles disguised as wild men, costumes stitched with flax and pitch, dancing before King Charles VI and the court.
evt-01-28-1393-charles-vi-of-france.prompt: A courtier approaches with a torch to get a better look at the costumes—what should you do?

choices.text: Ask him to light more torches for the dance
Dance nearer the fireplace for warmth
Invite him closer so he can see the wild-man mask
Warn him to keep the flame far away from the costumes

evt-01-28-1393-charles-vi-of-france.butterflyEffect: A torch brushed one dancer's flammable costume, igniting a blaze that killed several of the 'wild men'; Charles VI himself narrowly escaped death when his aunt, the Duchess of Berry, smothered him under her skirts. The Bal des Ardents became a symbol of court recklessness and deepened doubts about the king's fitness to rule as his mental illness worsened.

evt-01-28-1521-charles-v-holy-roman-empe.scenario: It's April 1521 in the city of Worms. You watch as Martin Luther stands before Emperor Charles V and the assembled princes of the Holy Roman Empire, ordered to recant the writings that have challenged papal authority.
evt-01-28-1521-charles-v-holy-roman-empe.prompt: What does Luther do when commanded to renounce his teachings?

choices.text: He agrees to a compromise revising only minor points
He recants immediately to avoid punishment
He refuses, declaring he will not act against his conscience
He flees Worms before answering

evt-01-28-1521-charles-v-holy-roman-empe.butterflyEffect: Luther's refusal led Charles V to issue the Edict of Worms, declaring him an outlaw whose writings were to be destroyed. Elector Frederick the Wise instead hid Luther at Wartburg Castle, where he translated the New Testament into German, fueling the spread of the Reformation across the Empire.

evt-01-28-1547-edward-vi.scenario: It is 28 January 1547. Henry VIII has just died, and you sit on the Privy Council with his will naming a council of sixteen equals to govern for his nine-year-old son Edward.
evt-01-28-1547-edward-vi.prompt: What actually happened to the balance of power after Henry VIII's death was announced?

choices.text: Princess Mary was appointed regent until Edward came of age
Catherine Parr, Henry's widow, was declared regent for young Edward
Edward Seymour maneuvered to become sole Lord Protector, sidelining the equal council named in the will
The sixteen councillors ruled jointly with no single leader, as Henry had intended

evt-01-28-1547-edward-vi.butterflyEffect: Edward Seymour outmaneuvered his fellow councillors, had himself named Lord Protector, and ruled almost as a king in Edward's name. His overreach led to his own downfall in 1549, when John Dudley seized control of the regency in his place.

evt-01-28-1754-serendipity.scenario: It is 1754, and you are the English writer Horace Walpole, drafting a letter to a friend in Florence. You have just finished an old Persian fairy tale about three princes who kept stumbling onto marvelous things they were not even looking for, and you want a single word for that kind of lucky accident.
evt-01-28-1754-serendipity.prompt: What word do you coin in your letter to describe this fortunate accident?

choices.text: Providence
Serendipity
Fortuity
Windfall

evt-01-28-1754-serendipity.butterflyEffect: Walpole wrote 'serendipity' into a private letter, naming it after the princes of Serendip (old Persian for Sri Lanka). The word barely circulated for over a century, then took off in the 20th century among scientists describing accidental breakthroughs like penicillin and X-rays, and today it names a whole category of unplanned discovery.

evt-01-28-1922-knickerbocker-storm.scenario: It's the evening of 28 January 1922, and a record blizzard has buried Washington, D.C. You've bought a ticket for a film at the Knickerbocker Theatre, whose flat roof is groaning under two feet of snow.
evt-01-28-1922-knickerbocker-storm.prompt: Given the strained roof, what should you do before the film starts?

choices.text: Leave the theatre and find safer shelter
Move to seats near the projection booth
Stay for the show, it's just an old building settling
Ask the usher to shovel snow off the marquee

evt-01-28-1922-knickerbocker-storm.butterflyEffect: Shortly after 9 p.m. the flat roof collapsed under the weight of the snow, killing 98 people and injuring 133 in the deadliest disaster in Washington, D.C. history. The tragedy spurred reforms in building codes for flat roofs and snow-load standards across the country.

evt-01-28-1933-choudhry-rahmat-ali.scenario: It is 1933, and you are a Muslim student in Cambridge, England, drafting a pamphlet titled 'Now or Never.' You argue that Muslims in the northwest of British India need their own separate homeland, and you need a name to put on the cover that will stick.
evt-01-28-1933-choudhry-rahmat-ali.prompt: What name do you coin for this proposed Muslim homeland?

choices.text: Hindustan
Pakstan
Bengalistan
Islamabad

evt-01-28-1933-choudhry-rahmat-ali.butterflyEffect: Rahmat Ali's pamphlet introduced the acronym-name 'Pakstan,' built from Punjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh, and Baluchistan. The name evolved into 'Pakistan' and was later adopted by the Muslim League's independence movement, becoming the official name of the nation created in 1947.

evt-01-28-1958-the-lego-group.scenario: It is 28 January 1958 in Billund, Denmark. You work at the Lego Group as it files a patent to protect the exact shape of its plastic building bricks before rivals can copy the design.
evt-01-28-1958-the-lego-group.prompt: What feature of the brick did the patent lock in that made Lego's later success possible?

choices.text: The cardboard box packaging used to sell the bricks
The stud-and-tube clutch design that let bricks interlock and stay compatible across future sets
The specific red, yellow, and blue color palette used on the bricks
A wooden brick design that Lego planned to phase in later

evt-01-28-1958-the-lego-group.butterflyEffect: The patent covered the stud-and-tube coupling system, which let bricks clutch together firmly yet come apart easily. Because every Lego set since 1958 uses compatible studs, bricks bought decades apart still fit together, underpinning the company's entire business model.

evt-01-28-1961-muhanga.scenario: It's 28 January 1961 in Gitarama, and Hutu political leaders have gathered local mayors and officials to declare an end to the Tutsi monarchy that has ruled Rwanda for generations.
evt-01-28-1961-muhanga.prompt: What did the assembled officials declare that day?

choices.text: Rwanda unites with Burundi under one crown
The Tutsi monarchy is restored with expanded powers
Rwanda will remain a Belgian trust territory indefinitely
Rwanda is a republic, deposing the Mwami

evt-01-28-1961-muhanga.butterflyEffect: The Gitarama coup declared Rwanda a republic and stripped Tutsi King Kigeli V of authority, a move Belgian trust authorities tacitly allowed. It cleared the way for Hutu-led PARMEHUTU dominance ahead of full independence in 1962, entrenching an ethnic political divide that would shape Rwanda for decades.

evt-01-28-1981-ronald-reagan.scenario: It is 28 January 1981, just days into Ronald Reagan's presidency. Domestic oil prices are still tangled in federal controls left over from the 1970s energy crisis, and you advise him on what to do first.
evt-01-28-1981-ronald-reagan.prompt: What did Reagan do with the remaining federal controls on petroleum prices?

choices.text: He signed an executive order abolishing the remaining federal price and allocation controls on petroleum
He imposed new, tighter price caps on gasoline sold at the pump
He placed new tariffs on all imported crude oil
He nationalized major American oil companies to stabilize supply

evt-01-28-1981-ronald-reagan.butterflyEffect: Reagan signed an executive order immediately abolishing the last federal price and allocation controls on crude oil and refined products. Freed prices encouraged more domestic drilling and helped erode OPEC's pricing power, contributing to the oil price collapse of the mid-1980s.

evt-01-28-1982-united-states-army.scenario: It is 28 January 1982 in Padua, Italy. You are part of an Italian anti-terrorism unit closing in on an apartment where Red Brigades militants have held kidnapped US Army General James Dozier for 42 days.
evt-01-28-1982-united-states-army.prompt: How did the raid to free General Dozier actually conclude?

choices.text: A gun battle broke out, leaving several hostages and captors dead
Dozier was exchanged for imprisoned Red Brigades members
Italian authorities paid a ransom to secure Dozier's release
The commandos rescued Dozier unharmed, overpowering his captors without any shots fired

evt-01-28-1982-united-states-army.butterflyEffect: NOCS commandos stormed the flat, overpowered the captors without firing a shot, and freed Dozier unharmed. The successful rescue was a major blow to the Red Brigades and helped accelerate the group's decline in Italy through the 1980s.

evt-01-28-1986-space-shuttle-challenger-.scenario: It's the freezing morning of January 28, 1986, at Kennedy Space Center. You are a Morton Thiokol engineer who has just told managers that the rubber O-rings sealing the solid rocket boosters may not seal properly in this cold, and launch is only hours away.
evt-01-28-1986-space-shuttle-challenger-.prompt: What should be done about the O-ring risk before Challenger launches?

choices.text: Swap in a spare booster from a warmer storage bay
Delay the launch until temperatures rise
Proceed with launch as scheduled
Launch but instruct the crew to abort if boosters show strain

evt-01-28-1986-space-shuttle-challenger-.butterflyEffect: NASA managers overruled the engineers' warnings and launched. Cold-stiffened O-rings failed 73 seconds after liftoff, destroying Challenger and killing all seven crew, including teacher Christa McAuliffe. The disaster grounded the shuttle fleet for 32 months, and the Rogers Commission, aided by physicist Richard Feynman's O-ring demonstration, exposed a NASA culture that silenced engineering dissent.

evt-01-28-1988-r-v-morgentaler.scenario: It is January 1988, and you are arguing before the Supreme Court of Canada on behalf of Dr. Henry Morgentaler, who has been prosecuted for performing abortions outside the hospital-committee approval required by the Criminal Code.
evt-01-28-1988-r-v-morgentaler.prompt: What is the core Charter argument you make to strike the law down?

choices.text: The law infringes freedom of religion under Section 2
The law breaches equality rights under Section 15
The mandatory committee-approval process violates a woman's right to security of the person under Section 7
The law exceeds federal jurisdiction over health matters

evt-01-28-1988-r-v-morgentaler.butterflyEffect: The Court struck down the law 5–2, ruling that its procedural hurdles violated a woman's right to security of the person under Section 7 of the Charter by causing dangerous delays. Parliament never passed a replacement law, leaving Canada with no criminal statute regulating abortion to this day, a status unique among Western democracies.

evt-01-28-2006-katowice-international-fa.scenario: It's 28 January 2006, and you're browsing cages of prize pigeons inside a hall at the Katowice International Fair. Snow has been falling for days, and the metal roof high above creaks under its weight.
evt-01-28-2006-katowice-international-fa.prompt: What is the safest move given the groaning, snow-laden roof overhead?

choices.text: Move to the far end of the hall away from the entrance
Ask organizers to turn up the heating to melt the snow
Stay to finish viewing the pigeon show
Evacuate the hall immediately

evt-01-28-2006-katowice-international-fa.butterflyEffect: Minutes later the roof gave way under the accumulated snow, killing 65 people and injuring more than 170 in one of Poland's deadliest building disasters. The catastrophe triggered nationwide inspections of large-span roofs and tougher snow-load building codes across the country.

evt-01-28-2023-tyre-nichols-protests.scenario: It's January 27, 2023, in Memphis. The police department has just released body-camera footage showing officers beating Tyre Nichols during a traffic stop, and the city braces for the public reaction.
evt-01-28-2023-tyre-nichols-protests.prompt: What action had already been taken against the officers before the footage aired?

choices.text: They were placed on paid administrative leave
They were fired and charged with second-degree murder
They were reassigned to desk duty pending review
No disciplinary action had yet been taken

evt-01-28-2023-tyre-nichols-protests.butterflyEffect: The unusually swift firings and murder charges preceded nationwide protests demanding broader police reform. Memphis later disbanded the specialized SCORPION unit the officers belonged to, and the case renewed national debate over aggressive policing units.

evt-01-28-2026-2026-rubaya-mines-collaps.scenario: It's late January 2026 at the Rubaya mines in eastern DR Congo, where thousands of miners dig hand-dug tunnels for coltan and tin ore with little engineering oversight after years of unchecked expansion.
evt-01-28-2026-2026-rubaya-mines-collaps.prompt: What triggered the collapse that destroyed several of the mines?

choices.text: A landslide caused by years of poor mining practices and lack of maintenance
Flooding from a burst river channel
A sudden earthquake beneath the mining district
An underground explosion from mining equipment

evt-01-28-2026-2026-rubaya-mines-collaps.butterflyEffect: The collapse killed more than 400 miners, one of the deadliest mining disasters in DRC history. It intensified international scrutiny of artisanal mining conditions in a region whose mineral wealth, including coltan used in electronics, has long been extracted with minimal safety regulation.

evt-01-29-1814-war-of-the-sixth-coalitio.scenario: It's the evening of 29 January 1814 at Brienne-le-Château, the town where you attended military school as a boy. Prussian and Russian troops under Blücher storm the streets, and Cossack cavalry suddenly close in around your position.
evt-01-29-1814-war-of-the-sixth-coalitio.prompt: What does Napoleon do when Cossacks nearly capture him at Brienne?

choices.text: Draw his sword and personally fight through the attackers
Order a full retreat of the entire army from the town
Flee alone on horseback, abandoning his staff
Surrender immediately to prevent bloodshed

evt-01-29-1814-war-of-the-sixth-coalitio.butterflyEffect: Napoleon drew his sword and personally fought off the Cossacks until his escort rescued him, holding Brienne that night. The near-capture was an early sign of how desperate his position had become; within months, defeat in the Six Days' Campaign forced his abdication and exile to Elba.

evt-01-29-1845-edgar-allan-poe.scenario: It's 29 January 1845, and you edit the New York Evening Mirror, weighing whether to run an unusual new poem about a grieving man and a talking raven, submitted by a struggling writer named Edgar Allan Poe.
evt-01-29-1845-edgar-allan-poe.prompt: What did the Evening Mirror do with Poe's poem "The Raven"?

choices.text: Reject it as too morbid for readers
Delay publication for a special holiday edition
Publish it with a glowing editorial introduction
Print only a short excerpt to test reaction

evt-01-29-1845-edgar-allan-poe.butterflyEffect: The Mirror ran the poem with an enthusiastic editorial introduction, and it became an overnight sensation, reprinted across American newspapers within weeks. Poe was paid only a small sum for it, but the poem made him a household name and remains his most famous work.

evt-01-29-1891-lili-uokalani.scenario: On 29 January 1891 you serve in the Hawaiian legislature as Liliʻuokalani ascends the throne after her brother King Kalākaua's death. American sugar planters and businessmen already chafe at native Hawaiian rule.
evt-01-29-1891-lili-uokalani.prompt: What did Liliʻuokalani attempt within her first two years that provoked her downfall?

choices.text: Voluntarily abdicate in favor of a republic
Dissolve the legislature and rule by decree indefinitely
Attempt to promulgate a new constitution restoring royal power
Sign a treaty ceding Hawaii's sovereignty to the United States

evt-01-29-1891-lili-uokalani.butterflyEffect: In 1893 she moved to promulgate a new constitution restoring royal authority the monarchy had lost, alarming American and European business interests. The Committee of Safety, backed by US Marines, staged a coup that overthrew her government and ultimately led to Hawaii's annexation by the United States in 1898.

evt-01-29-1907-charles-curtis.scenario: It's January 29, 1907, and you watch the Kansas legislature cast its vote for a new United States Senator, settling on Charles Curtis, an enrolled citizen of the Kaw Nation.
evt-01-29-1907-charles-curtis.prompt: What historic first does Curtis's election represent?

choices.text: First Native American cabinet secretary
First Native American in the U.S. Senate
First Native American state governor
First Native American Supreme Court justice

evt-01-29-1907-charles-curtis.butterflyEffect: Curtis became the first Native American to serve in the U.S. Senate, having already broken ground in the House. He rose to Senate Majority Leader and, in 1929, became the first Native American vice president under Herbert Hoover, a distinction that stood as the highest federal office held by a Native American for nearly a century.

evt-01-29-1911-mexican-revolution.scenario: It's January 1911 in Baja California. You're a fighter in the Mexican Liberal Party's ragtag army, poised to strike at a government garrison near the U.S. border as revolt against Porfirio Díaz spreads across Mexico.
evt-01-29-1911-mexican-revolution.prompt: What border town do the Magonista rebels seize to open their Baja California campaign?

choices.text: Mexicali
Guadalajara
Mexico City
Ensenada

evt-01-29-1911-mexican-revolution.butterflyEffect: The rebels captured Mexicali on January 29, 1911, launching a short-lived anarchist campaign that drew American volunteers and mercenaries and international press coverage. The movement was crushed by federal and Maderista forces within months, overshadowed by Francisco Madero's larger revolt, and Ricardo Flores Magón's radical vision was marginalized within the Revolution's mainstream narrative.

evt-01-29-1967-mantra-rock-dance.scenario: It is January 29, 1967, and you are packed into the Avalon Ballroom in San Francisco expecting the usual psychedelic light show and rock bands. Instead, an elderly Indian swami in saffron robes climbs onto the stage between sets and begins to chant.
evt-01-29-1967-mantra-rock-dance.prompt: What does the crowd do when Swami Prabhupada leads the Hare Krishna chant?

choices.text: They walk out, unimpressed by the interruption
They demand the club refund their tickets
They join in, chanting and dancing along with him
They heckle him until the bands return

evt-01-29-1967-mantra-rock-dance.butterflyEffect: The crowd, including bands like the Grateful Dead and Big Brother and the Holding Company with Janis Joplin, joined the chanting for nearly two hours. The event's success helped fund ISKCON's first West Coast temple and is often credited with launching the Hare Krishna movement's spread across America.

evt-01-29-1991-battle-of-khafji.scenario: It's the night of 29 January 1991. Iraqi armor rolls across the Saudi border into the town of Khafji, trapping two US Marine reconnaissance teams hidden inside as tanks rumble past their position.
evt-01-29-1991-battle-of-khafji.prompt: What should the trapped Marine observers do as Iraqi tanks fill the streets?

choices.text: Surrender to avoid detection and casualties
Attempt an immediate retreat across the border
Engage the tanks directly with small arms
Stay hidden and radio coordinates for coalition airstrikes

evt-01-29-1991-battle-of-khafji.butterflyEffect: The Marines stayed concealed and radioed in coordinates for punishing coalition airstrikes on the Iraqi column. Saudi and Qatari ground forces then recaptured Khafji within about 36 hours, giving the coalition a badly needed morale boost and showcasing Arab forces' fighting ability just weeks before the main ground offensive.

evt-01-29-2008-religion-in-egypt.scenario: You are a Baha'i citizen in Cairo in early 2008, unable to obtain a national ID card because your faith isn't one of the three religions Egypt officially recognizes, blocking your access to schools, banking, and public services.
evt-01-29-2008-religion-in-egypt.prompt: What compromise does the Egyptian court grant to Baha'is like you?

choices.text: A dash may replace a religion on official documents
Baha'is must register as one of the three recognized faiths
Baha'i is formally added as a recognized state religion
Baha'is are exempted from carrying identification

evt-01-29-2008-religion-in-egypt.butterflyEffect: The court allowed Baha'is to receive ID cards with a dash instead of a listed religion, easing daily bureaucratic exclusion without granting Baha'ism formal legal recognition. The ruling, upheld on appeal in 2009, became a landmark in Egypt's ongoing struggle over minority religious rights, though full recognition for Baha'is remains denied.

evt-01-29-2009-governor-of-illinois.scenario: It's January 29, 2009, and you're an Illinois state senator sitting in judgment after an impeachment trial exposed recordings of Governor Rod Blagojevich scheming to sell Barack Obama's vacated U.S. Senate seat.
evt-01-29-2009-governor-of-illinois.prompt: What does the Illinois Senate do with Blagojevich after the trial concludes?

choices.text: Allow him to resign quietly with no penalty
Convict him and remove him from office
Acquit him for lack of evidence
Refer the matter to federal prosecutors without a vote

evt-01-29-2009-governor-of-illinois.butterflyEffect: The Senate voted unanimously to convict and remove Blagojevich, also barring him from holding future state office. Lieutenant Governor Pat Quinn was sworn in immediately, and Blagojevich was later convicted in federal court and sentenced to 14 years, becoming a lasting symbol of Illinois's pay-to-play political culture until his sentence was commuted in 2020.

evt-01-29-2022-truck-driver.scenario: It's January 29, 2022, and you're a resident of downtown Ottawa as hundreds of trucks and thousands of protesters converge on Parliament Hill, opposing COVID-19 vaccine mandates for cross-border truckers.
evt-01-29-2022-truck-driver.prompt: How do city police initially respond as the convoy rolls into the capital?

choices.text: They immediately declare a state of emergency and clear the streets
They call in the military to disperse the crowd
They let the trucks park and the protest continue
They negotiate an instant end to all vaccine mandates

evt-01-29-2022-truck-driver.butterflyEffect: Police largely allowed the trucks to park and the protest to proceed, and the occupation stretched on for three weeks. The federal government eventually invoked the Emergencies Act for the first time in Canadian history, freezing protesters' finances and towing vehicles to clear the streets, reshaping national debate over protest rights and pandemic policy.

evt-01-29-2025-american-eagle-airline-br.scenario: It is the night of January 29, 2025, in the airspace above the Potomac River near Reagan National Airport, where a military helicopter route crosses the path of the airport's busiest landing approach used by regional jets like American Eagle Flight 5342.
evt-01-29-2025-american-eagle-airline-br.prompt: What change did aviation authorities order in the immediate aftermath of the collision?

choices.text: They closed Reagan National Airport permanently
They grounded all Black Hawk helicopters nationwide indefinitely
They restricted helicopter traffic through the corridor where the routes had crossed
They banned regional jets from operating near Washington, D.C.

evt-01-29-2025-american-eagle-airline-br.butterflyEffect: Following the collision between the regional jet and an Army Black Hawk helicopter, which killed everyone aboard both aircraft, the FAA moved quickly to restrict helicopter traffic through the corridor where military and civilian routes had overlapped near the airport. The crash also intensified scrutiny of how shared airspace near major airports is managed nationwide.

evt-01-30-1607-1607-bristol-channel-floo.scenario: You are a farmer near the Somerset coast at dawn on 30 January 1607. The tide is rushing inland far faster and higher than any you have seen, already swallowing the fields where your sheep are grazing.

choices.text: Wait to see if the water recedes on its own
Flee immediately for higher ground
Stay behind to herd the livestock to safety first
Go to the church to ring the bells and wait it out

evt-01-30-1607-1607-bristol-channel-floo.butterflyEffect: The surge drowned an estimated 2,000 people and destroyed farmland and livestock across the Somerset and Gwent coasts. Debate over whether it was a storm surge or a tsunami continues among historians, and the disaster spurred later improvements to sea defences along the Bristol Channel.

evt-01-30-1649-charles-i-of-england.scenario: It is 30 January 1649. You stand in the crowd outside the Banqueting House at Whitehall as King Charles I, convicted of treason by a parliamentary court, is led onto the scaffold.
evt-01-30-1649-charles-i-of-england.prompt: What happens to the king in the next moments?

choices.text: He is pardoned at the last moment
He is beheaded on the scaffold
He escapes with help from loyalist guards
He is exiled to France instead of executed

evt-01-30-1649-charles-i-of-england.butterflyEffect: Charles I was beheaded before the crowd, the first English monarch executed by his own subjects. His death abolished the monarchy and ushered in Oliver Cromwell's Commonwealth, until the throne was restored to his son Charles II in 1660.

evt-01-30-1661-oliver-cromwell.scenario: You are a royal official in Restoration London on 30 January 1661, the twelfth anniversary of Charles I's execution. King Charles II has ordered the exhumed corpse of Oliver Cromwell brought from Westminster Abbey to answer, symbolically, for the regicide.
evt-01-30-1661-oliver-cromwell.prompt: What is done with Cromwell's disinterred remains?

choices.text: It is put on posthumous trial and formally pardoned
It is quietly reburied in an unmarked grave
It is publicly hanged, beheaded, and the head displayed on a spike
It is burned and the ashes scattered in the Thames

evt-01-30-1661-oliver-cromwell.butterflyEffect: Cromwell's body was hanged in chains at Tyburn, then beheaded, with his skull mounted on a spike above Westminster Hall as a warning against republicanism. It reportedly remained there for over two decades and passed through private collectors for centuries before being buried at Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, in 1960.

evt-01-30-1835-richard-lawrence-failed-a.scenario: You stand outside the United States Capitol on 30 January 1835 as President Andrew Jackson leaves a congressman's funeral. A disgruntled house painter named Richard Lawrence steps from the crowd, raises a pistol, and pulls the trigger at point-blank range.
evt-01-30-1835-richard-lawrence-failed-a.prompt: What happens in the moment after Lawrence fires at the President?

choices.text: The pistol fires and wounds Jackson in the shoulder
Both pistols misfire, and Jackson attacks Lawrence with his cane
Capitol guards shoot Lawrence before he can fire
Jackson calmly talks Lawrence into surrendering the weapon

evt-01-30-1835-richard-lawrence-failed-a.butterflyEffect: Both of Lawrence's pistols misfired in the damp air, and the 67-year-old Jackson immediately began beating him with his walking cane before bystanders wrestled Lawrence away. Lawrence was found not guilty by reason of insanity and institutionalized for life; the episode became the first attempted assassination of a sitting U.S. president, decades before the Secret Service existed to guard one.

evt-01-30-1862-united-states-navy.scenario: You are a Navy engineer watching the strange iron vessel slide into the water at Greenpoint, Brooklyn, on 30 January 1862. Built in barely 100 days on John Ericsson's radical turret design, many veteran officers still call her nothing but a 'cheesebox on a raft.'
evt-01-30-1862-united-states-navy.prompt: What happens when this untested ironclad meets her Confederate rival weeks later?

choices.text: A storm forces both ships to withdraw before firing a shot
Monitor is boarded and captured by Confederate sailors
Monitor sinks the Confederate ironclad outright
The two ironclads batter each other for hours but neither sinks the other

evt-01-30-1862-united-states-navy.butterflyEffect: On 9 March 1862, USS Monitor fought CSS Virginia to an inconclusive draw at Hampton Roads, the first battle between ironclad warships. Neither ship sank the other, but the clash instantly rendered wooden warships obsolete and triggered an international arms race in armored, turreted warships.

evt-01-30-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: You are a Ranger with the 6th Ranger Battalion, crouched in the tall grass outside a Japanese-run POW camp deep in Japanese-held Luzon on the night of January 30, 1945, waiting for the signal to move with Filipino guerrilla scouts.
evt-01-30-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What must your unit do to save the prisoners held inside before they can be harmed?

choices.text: Wait for an entire division to encircle the camp before attacking
Launch a swift coordinated night assault with Filipino guerrillas before reinforcements arrive
Call in an airstrike to level the camp's defenses first
Attempt to negotiate a prisoner exchange with the camp commander

evt-01-30-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The raid succeeded, freeing more than 500 emaciated survivors of the Bataan Death March and years of brutal captivity, achieved through close coordination with Filipino guerrillas who scouted the camp and covered the retreat. It became one of the most celebrated rescue missions of the war and spurred urgent Allied efforts to reach other POW camps before retreating Japanese forces could kill the prisoners inside.

evt-01-30-1964-nguyen-khanh.scenario: You are an ARVN colonel in Saigon before dawn on January 30, 1964, roused by orders to secure key government buildings as General Nguyễn Khánh moves against Dương Văn Minh's ruling junta.
evt-01-30-1964-nguyen-khanh.prompt: What do you do as troops converge on the junta's headquarters?

choices.text: Follow Khánh's orders and help depose Minh's junta without a shot fired
Refuse the orders outright and defect north
Defend Minh's junta and order your men to fire on the advancing troops
Declare loyalty to the exiled family of Ngô Đình Diệm

evt-01-30-1964-nguyen-khanh.butterflyEffect: The coup succeeded without bloodshed, installing Khánh as South Vietnam's new leader, but it opened a chaotic cycle of coups and countercoups that lasted through 1965, when Khánh himself was ousted and exiled. This relentless political instability in Saigon deeply worried Washington and fed the rationale for escalating direct American military involvement.

evt-01-30-1968-vietnam-war.scenario: It is the pre-dawn hours of January 30, 1968, the Lunar New Year truce, and you are a military policeman standing guard outside the U.S. Embassy in Saigon when Viet Cong sappers suddenly breach the compound wall.
evt-01-30-1968-vietnam-war.prompt: What follows the surprise Tet assaults across South Vietnam?

choices.text: Though a military defeat for the attackers, the offensive shatters U.S. public confidence in the war effort
The offensive leads the U.S. to withdraw all combat troops within weeks
The offensive successfully triggers a general uprising against the Saigon government
The offensive forces an immediate North Vietnamese surrender

evt-01-30-1968-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: Though the Viet Cong and North Vietnamese forces suffered heavy losses and failed to hold any major city, the shock of coordinated attacks on Saigon, the embassy, and dozens of towns during a supposed truce devastated American confidence in official claims that victory was near. The resulting collapse in public and political support is widely credited with pushing President Johnson toward ending his re-election bid and beginning peace negotiations.

evt-01-30-1972-the-troubles.scenario: You march with thousands of civil rights demonstrators through the Bogside in Derry on 30 January 1972, as British paratroopers take up positions along the barricades ahead. Shots suddenly ring out among the unarmed crowd.
evt-01-30-1972-the-troubles.prompt: What follows in the days and years after the shootings in Derry?

choices.text: Direct rule over Northern Ireland ends immediately afterward
Outrage over the killings fuels a surge in IRA recruitment and violence
The British government issues an immediate apology and inquiry within days
The march organizers are convicted of inciting the violence

evt-01-30-1972-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: Thirteen marchers were killed outright and a fourteenth died later; the initial Widgery Tribunal largely exonerated the soldiers, but this fueled outrage and a surge in recruitment for the Provisional IRA. Decades later, the 2010 Saville Inquiry found the victims unarmed and posed no threat, prompting a formal apology from Prime Minister David Cameron.

evt-01-30-1979-varig-flight-967.scenario: You are a dispatcher at Narita International Airport on 30 January 1979, watching Varig Flight 967's Boeing 707 climb away toward Los Angeles with six crew aboard. An hour later, radio contact is lost and never regained.
evt-01-30-1979-varig-flight-967.prompt: What do investigators eventually conclude happened to Flight 967?

choices.text: No trace of the plane or crew is ever found, and the case remains unsolved
Wreckage is found off the Japanese coast within weeks
The aircraft is confirmed hijacked and diverted to another country
The crew is rescued after an emergency landing at sea

evt-01-30-1979-varig-flight-967.butterflyEffect: Despite one of the largest search efforts conducted over the Pacific at the time, no wreckage, debris, or remains were ever recovered. The disappearance remains officially unsolved, joining a small list of aviation mysteries where the cause was never determined.

evt-01-30-1982-rich-skrenta.scenario: You are a ninth-grader in suburban Pittsburgh in 1982, swapping Apple II game disks with classmates, unaware one disk is quietly copying itself onto every other disk that touches that machine.
evt-01-30-1982-rich-skrenta.prompt: What happens the fiftieth time an infected disk boots?

choices.text: The disk drive locks and refuses to eject
All the files on the disk are permanently erased
A short poem about the program appears on screen
The screen displays a ransom demand for money

evt-01-30-1982-rich-skrenta.butterflyEffect: The program, written by teenager Rich Skrenta as a prank, was Elk Cloner, widely considered the first computer virus to spread in the wild outside a lab. It foreshadowed the boot-sector and floppy-disk malware epidemics of the 1980s and 90s.

evt-01-30-1989-embassy-of-the-united-sta.scenario: You are a staff member at the U.S. embassy in Kabul in late January 1989. Soviet troops have finished withdrawing from Afghanistan, mujahideen factions are closing on the capital, and Washington recognizes no government there.

choices.text: Remain open and negotiate directly with mujahideen commanders
Evacuate staff and close the embassy
Request Soviet troops stay to guard the compound
Request a U.S. Marine deployment to hold the embassy

evt-01-30-1989-embassy-of-the-united-sta.butterflyEffect: The United States closed its Kabul embassy on 30 January 1989 and withdrew all staff, unwilling to recognize any faction controlling the capital. The mission stayed shuttered for over a decade, through Taliban rule, and only reopened after the Taliban's fall in late 2001.

evt-01-30-1995-hydroxycarbamide.scenario: You are a hematologist in early 1995 treating a young adult with sickle cell disease who has endured repeated painful crises. Hydroxyurea has just been approved as the first drug shown to prevent these episodes.
evt-01-30-1995-hydroxycarbamide.prompt: What should you recommend as ongoing preventive therapy?

choices.text: Start a lifelong regular blood transfusion program
Begin daily hydroxyurea therapy
Continue treating each crisis only as it occurs
Refer immediately for a bone marrow transplant

evt-01-30-1995-hydroxycarbamide.butterflyEffect: The FDA approval was based on a landmark trial showing hydroxyurea significantly cut painful crises by raising fetal hemoglobin levels. It became the standard preventive treatment for sickle cell disease, later extended to children, and remained the primary therapy for decades before newer gene-based treatments emerged.

evt-01-30-2007-microsoft.scenario: You are a Microsoft product manager on January 30, 2007, watching Windows Vista go on sale to consumers worldwide after more than five years of delayed development.
evt-01-30-2007-microsoft.prompt: What happens to Vista's reputation in the months after its release?

choices.text: Vista faces widespread criticism over performance issues and hardware compatibility
Vista wins unanimous praise from corporate IT departments for its speed
Vista is pulled from sale within weeks over legal disputes
Vista becomes an instant hit, quickly outselling Windows XP

evt-01-30-2007-microsoft.butterflyEffect: Vista drew sustained criticism for driver incompatibilities, sluggish performance on existing hardware, and intrusive User Account Control prompts, leading many businesses to skip it entirely and stay on Windows XP. Microsoft answered with Windows 7 in 2009, which addressed those complaints and became one of the company's most successful and well-regarded releases.

evt-01-30-2020-world-health-organization.scenario: It is January 30, 2020. You sit on the WHO Emergency Committee in Geneva, reviewing reports of a fast-spreading new coronavirus in China and scattered cases already appearing abroad.
evt-01-30-2020-world-health-organization.prompt: What should the committee recommend to the Director-General?

choices.text: Immediately declare a global pandemic
Declare a Public Health Emergency of International Concern
Recommend a total international travel ban at once
Wait for more confirmed cases outside China before acting

evt-01-30-2020-world-health-organization.butterflyEffect: The WHO declared COVID-19 a Public Health Emergency of International Concern that day, its highest alert level short of pandemic. Six weeks later, on 11 March 2020, it upgraded the designation to a pandemic as the virus spread to every continent, triggering the lockdowns that reshaped the following two years.

evt-01-31-1208-sverker-the-younger.scenario: It is late January 1208. You fight in King Sverker the Younger's ranks near Lena, where his forces have clashed with the army of the rival claimant Erik Knutsson for control of Sweden.
evt-01-31-1208-sverker-the-younger.prompt: Your king's army is broken at Lena. What does Sverker do next?

choices.text: He abdicates immediately and retires to a monastery
He is captured on the battlefield and executed
He flees to Denmark to seek allies for a comeback
He negotiates a treaty splitting Sweden in two

evt-01-31-1208-sverker-the-younger.butterflyEffect: Sverker fled into exile in Denmark, where he secured the support of King Valdemar II. He returned in 1210 to challenge Erik again at the Battle of Gestilren, where he was killed, leaving Erik Knutsson's line in control of the Swedish throne but not ending the dynastic struggle between the houses of Sverker and Erik for decades.

evt-01-31-1578-eighty-years-war.scenario: It's January 31, 1578, near Gembloux in the Spanish Netherlands. Your rebel army is retreating across a narrow causeway when Spanish cavalry under Don John of Austria and the Duke of Parma suddenly move to strike your exposed column.
evt-01-31-1578-eighty-years-war.prompt: What happens when the Spanish cavalry hits the retreating rebel force?

choices.text: Both sides disengage after an inconclusive skirmish
The rebels repel the charge and reform their ranks safely
The rebels spring a prepared ambush on the Spanish cavalry
The rebels are routed with devastating losses while Spanish casualties stay light

evt-01-31-1578-eighty-years-war.butterflyEffect: The Spanish shattered the disorganized rebel column, inflicting heavy casualties for minimal losses of their own. The victory restored Spanish momentum in the Netherlands and helped elevate the Duke of Parma, who soon became governor-general and drove an effective reconquest of the southern provinces, even as the wider revolt ground on for decades toward eventual Dutch independence.

evt-01-31-1747-london-lock-hospital.scenario: It is 1747, and you are a physician helping open a new hospital in London meant for sufferers of venereal disease who have been turned away by every other charitable infirmary in the city.
evt-01-31-1747-london-lock-hospital.prompt: What was this new hospital's founding purpose?

choices.text: To quarantine plague victims arriving by ship
To serve solely as a maternity hospital for the poor
To house debtors awaiting trial in a secure infirmary
To openly treat syphilis and other venereal diseases refused elsewhere

evt-01-31-1747-london-lock-hospital.butterflyEffect: The London Lock Hospital became the first voluntary hospital dedicated to treating syphilis and other venereal diseases, filling a gap left by hospitals that refused such patients. Its model spread to other British cities, and the institution itself later expanded into maternity and gynaecological care before joining the NHS in 1948.

evt-01-31-1827-nacogdoches-texas.scenario: It is the end of January 1827, and you march with a combined force of Mexican soldiers and Stephen F. Austin's Texan militiamen toward Nacogdoches, where Haden Edwards has declared the breakaway 'Republic of Fredonia.'
evt-01-31-1827-nacogdoches-texas.prompt: What do you find when your force reaches the town?

choices.text: The rebels have already fled toward the Sabine River
A fierce battle rages through the streets
The town formally votes to join the United States
Edwards surrenders in a public ceremony

evt-01-31-1827-nacogdoches-texas.butterflyEffect: By the time troops arrived, Edwards and his followers had already fled toward the U.S. border, collapsing the short-lived Fredonian Rebellion without a major fight. The episode deepened Mexican distrust of Anglo-American settlers in Texas, hardening policies that helped spark the Texas Revolution less than a decade later.

evt-01-31-1919-battle-of-george-square.scenario: It is January 31, 1919, and you stand among thousands of striking workers packed into George Square, Glasgow, demanding a 40-hour week as police draw batons to disperse the crowd.
evt-01-31-1919-battle-of-george-square.prompt: How did the British government respond once the rioting was reported to London?

choices.text: It immediately granted the 40-hour week to end the unrest
It ordered the City of Glasgow Police force disbanded
It deployed troops and tanks to the city and arrested the strike leaders
It sent government ministers to negotiate directly in the square

evt-01-31-1919-battle-of-george-square.butterflyEffect: Fearing a Bolshevik-style uprising, the government rushed troops and six tanks into Glasgow and had strike leaders, including Willie Gallacher and Manny Shinwell, arrested for incitement to riot. The episode became a defining symbol of 'Red Clydeside' and fed decades of British anxiety about organised labour turning revolutionary.

evt-01-31-1961-nasa.scenario: It is January 31, 1961, and you are a NASA engineer at Cape Canaveral preparing to strap a young chimpanzee named Ham into the Mercury-Redstone capsule.
evt-01-31-1961-nasa.prompt: Why send a chimpanzee into space before any American astronaut?

choices.text: To begin training animals for a permanent orbital colony
To calibrate the rocket's guidance computer using biometric feedback
To measure cosmic radiation levels for future satellite design
To test life-support systems and whether a living creature could perform tasks in spaceflight

evt-01-31-1961-nasa.butterflyEffect: Ham survived the suborbital flight, correctly performing his trained lever-pulling tasks despite a rougher ride than planned, proving a living being could function and be recovered safely. His success cleared NASA to launch Alan Shepard, the first American in space, just three months later.

evt-01-31-1978-holy-crown-of-hungary.scenario: It is January 1978, and you are a Hungarian official awaiting the return of the Holy Crown of Saint Stephen, held by the US Army since the end of World War II to keep it out of Soviet hands.
evt-01-31-1978-holy-crown-of-hungary.prompt: What happens to the crown once it is back on Hungarian soil?

choices.text: It is melted down for its gold
It goes on public display
It is sent to the Vatican for safekeeping
It is kept secret indefinitely

evt-01-31-1978-holy-crown-of-hungary.butterflyEffect: The crown went on public exhibition in the Hungarian National Museum, becoming a powerful symbol of national continuity even under communist rule. In 2000 it was moved to the Hungarian Parliament Building, where it remains a central emblem of Hungarian statehood.

evt-01-31-1988-doug-williams-quarterback.scenario: It's Super Bowl XXII on January 31, 1988. You're Doug Williams, quarterback for Washington, and your team trails the Denver Broncos 10-0 early after you've thrown an interception on your first series.
evt-01-31-1988-doug-williams-quarterback.prompt: What happens next as Williams leads the offense back onto the field?

choices.text: Williams is benched in favor of the backup quarterback
The game ends in a rare Super Bowl tie
Williams throws four touchdown passes in the second quarter alone
Washington's defense wins the game without further offense from Williams

evt-01-31-1988-doug-williams-quarterback.butterflyEffect: Williams engineered a historic second-quarter comeback, throwing four touchdown passes in a single quarter to help Washington win 42-10. He became the first Black quarterback to start and win a Super Bowl, was named MVP, and his performance opened doors for future Black quarterbacks in the NFL's biggest game.

evt-01-31-2000-alaska-airlines-flight-26.scenario: It is January 31, 2000, and you are flying the MD-83 of Alaska Airlines Flight 261 over the Pacific when the horizontal stabilizer suddenly jams, sending the nose pitching uncontrollably.
evt-01-31-2000-alaska-airlines-flight-26.prompt: What did the crew do as they fought to keep the aircraft controllable?

choices.text: Continued on to Seattle as originally scheduled
Turned back to Puerto Vallarta to land
Attempted an immediate ditching in the ocean without diverting
Diverted toward Los Angeles International Airport for an emergency landing

evt-01-31-2000-alaska-airlines-flight-26.butterflyEffect: The pilots diverted toward Los Angeles for an emergency landing but lost all pitch control before reaching it, and the jet crashed into the Pacific, killing all 88 aboard. Investigators traced the failure to a worn jackscrew assembly caused by extended lubrication intervals, prompting the FAA to overhaul maintenance and inspection rules for that mechanism across the MD-80 fleet.

evt-01-31-2001-libya.scenario: It is January 2001, and you sit in a specially convened Scottish court at Camp Zeist in the Netherlands, weighing the fate of two Libyan intelligence officers accused of bombing Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie in 1988.
evt-01-31-2001-libya.prompt: What verdict does the court reach?

choices.text: Both men are acquitted
Al-Megrahi is convicted, Fhimah is acquitted
The trial ends without a verdict
Both men are convicted

evt-01-31-2001-libya.butterflyEffect: Abdelbaset al-Megrahi was found guilty and sentenced to life imprisonment, while co-defendant Lamin Khalifah Fhimah walked free. The verdict fueled decades of controversy over Megrahi's guilt, his 2009 compassionate release from a Scottish prison, and Libya's eventual acceptance of responsibility and compensation payments in 2003.

evt-01-31-2007-aqua-teen-hunger-force.scenario: It's late January 2007 and you're a Boston police officer responding to reports of a blinking electronic device wired to a bridge support, complete with exposed wires and a battery pack.
evt-01-31-2007-aqua-teen-hunger-force.prompt: What should authorities do when they find these mysterious blinking devices around the city?

choices.text: Ignore it since no citizen has reported concern
Assume it's harmless advertising and leave it in place
Treat it as a possible explosive device and call in the bomb squad
Remove it themselves without specialized training

evt-01-31-2007-aqua-teen-hunger-force.butterflyEffect: The devices turned out to be LED placards of a Mooninite character, part of a guerrilla marketing campaign for the Aqua Teen Hunger Force movie. The citywide bomb scare led to the arrest of two marketers, the resignation of a Turner Broadcasting executive, and a $2 million settlement paid to Boston to cover emergency response costs.

evt-01-31-2009-kenya.scenario: It is the morning of 31 January 2009 near Molo, Kenya. A fuel tanker has overturned on the roadside, and villagers are already wading in with buckets and jerry cans to scoop up the spilled petrol before it evaporates.
evt-01-31-2009-kenya.prompt: What is the safest decision you can make right now?

choices.text: Warn others away and keep well back from the spill
Join the crowd collecting free fuel
Try to help right the tanker yourself
Light a fire nearby to see the spill better

evt-01-31-2009-kenya.butterflyEffect: Sparks ignited the leaking petrol, engulfing the crowd of scavengers in flames and killing at least 113 people while injuring more than 200 others. The disaster, one of Kenya's deadliest, pushed authorities to tighten rules on tanker safety and emergency response to roadside fuel spills.

evt-01-31-2013-torre-ejecutiva-pemex.scenario: It is January 31, 2013, and you work in the lower floors of the Pemex Executive Tower in Mexico City when a sudden explosion tears through the building, trapping and injuring workers.
evt-01-31-2013-torre-ejecutiva-pemex.prompt: What did investigators conclude had caused the deadly blast?

choices.text: A car bomb detonated by drug cartel operatives
An accidental buildup of gas that ignited in the basement
An intentional act of sabotage by a foreign intelligence agency
A boiler explosion in the building's rooftop mechanical room

evt-01-31-2013-torre-ejecutiva-pemex.butterflyEffect: Mexican authorities determined the explosion was caused by an accidental buildup of gas in the basement rather than sabotage, though initial fears of a bomb attack briefly gripped the country. The disaster prompted scrutiny of safety and maintenance practices at Pemex, the state oil giant already under pressure over aging infrastructure.

evt-01-31-2019-abdullah-of-pahang.scenario: It is late January 2019. Malaysia's nine hereditary state rulers gather in the Conference of Rulers to choose a new Yang di-Pertuan Agong after the previous king's sudden resignation.
evt-01-31-2019-abdullah-of-pahang.prompt: How does the Conference of Rulers actually select the new king?

choices.text: The Prime Minister appoints the king directly
They vote by secret ballot among themselves, largely by rotation
Malaysian citizens elect the king in a national vote
The eldest living sultan automatically inherits the role

evt-01-31-2019-abdullah-of-pahang.butterflyEffect: The nine hereditary rulers voted by secret ballot, following an informal rotation among their states, and chose Sultan Abdullah of Pahang as the 16th Yang di-Pertuan Agong. He was sworn in on 31 January 2019 and reigned until 2024, when the rotation passed to Sultan Ibrahim of Johor.

evt-01-31-2020-united-kingdom.scenario: It is 31 January 2020, and Britain's decades-long EU membership has just formally ended. As an official in Whitehall, you must explain to the public what changes tomorrow morning.
evt-01-31-2020-united-kingdom.prompt: What actually happens to the UK immediately after leaving the EU?

choices.text: It enters a transition period still bound by EU rules
Northern Ireland becomes fully independent
It adopts a new national currency
It immediately leaves the single market and customs union

evt-01-31-2020-united-kingdom.butterflyEffect: Britain entered an 11-month transition period lasting until 31 December 2020, still following EU rules while negotiators hashed out a future trade deal. The eventual agreement reshaped British trade, immigration and Northern Ireland's status, effects still rippling through UK politics and the economy today.

evt-01-31-2023-boeing-747.scenario: It is 31 January 2023 at Boeing's Everett factory, and you watch the final Boeing 747 ever built roll toward delivery after 54 years of production.
evt-01-31-2023-boeing-747.prompt: Who takes delivery of this last jumbo jet?

choices.text: Atlas Air, as a cargo freighter
Lufthansa, for passenger service
Pan Am, the airline that launched the 747
The Smithsonian Institution

evt-01-31-2023-boeing-747.butterflyEffect: The final 747, a -8 Freighter, was delivered to Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings, closing out a production run that began in 1968 and once defined the 'Jumbo Jet' era. Its retirement marked the twilight of four-engine widebodies, as airlines increasingly turned to more fuel-efficient twin-engine jets like the 777 and 787.

evt-02-01-1327-edward-iii.scenario: You stand in Westminster Abbey in February 1327 watching a fourteen-year-old boy crowned Edward III, while his mother Queen Isabella and her ally Roger Mortimer look on with quiet satisfaction.
evt-02-01-1327-edward-iii.prompt: Who actually wields power behind the new boy king's throne?

choices.text: The deposed Edward II still rules from hiding
Parliament governs directly without a regent
Queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer control the regency
The Despenser family retains full control of the court

evt-02-01-1327-edward-iii.butterflyEffect: Isabella and Mortimer ran the regency government until 1330, when the now-adult Edward staged his own coup, had Mortimer executed, and took the throne for himself. He went on to reign for fifty years, transforming England into a formidable military power and launching the claims that led to the Hundred Years' War.

evt-02-01-1411-peace-of-thorn-1411.scenario: You advise King Władysław Jagiełło in Thorn, February 1411. The Teutonic Knights, crushed at Grunwald just months earlier, now sit across the table begging for terms.
evt-02-01-1411-peace-of-thorn-1411.prompt: What peace terms do you urge the king to accept?

choices.text: Refuse any treaty and continue the war until unconditional surrender
Demand the total dissolution of the Teutonic Order
Insist on permanent annexation of all of Prussia
Accept modest territorial gains and let the Knights keep their state intact

evt-02-01-1411-peace-of-thorn-1411.butterflyEffect: Poland-Lithuania settled for the return of Dobrzyń Land and only temporary Samogitian gains, a treaty historians call a diplomatic failure given the scale of the Grunwald victory. War reparations bled the Knights financially, but it took two more wars—the Hunger War and Gollub War—before the 1422 Treaty of Melno finally settled the borders.

evt-02-01-1662-sino-dutch-conflicts.scenario: It is early 1662 at Fort Zeelandia on Taiwan. For nine months your Dutch East India Company garrison has withstood siege by the forces of Koxinga, but supplies are dwindling and no relief fleet has arrived.
evt-02-01-1662-sino-dutch-conflicts.prompt: As the Dutch commander, what should you do?

choices.text: Appeal to the Chinese emperor directly for mercy
Launch a desperate breakout attack against the besiegers
Surrender the fort under negotiated terms
Burn the fort's supplies and retreat by sea at night

evt-02-01-1662-sino-dutch-conflicts.butterflyEffect: Commander Frederick Coyett surrendered the fort, ending 38 years of Dutch colonial presence on Taiwan. Koxinga established the Kingdom of Tungning, the first Han Chinese state on the island, which endured until the Qing dynasty conquered it in 1683.

evt-02-01-1814-mayon.scenario: It is 1 February 1814 in the town of Cagsawa, in the shadow of Mount Mayon. Ash and stones are falling from the sky, and the volcano's tremors are growing violent. Many neighbors are running toward the stone church for shelter.
evt-02-01-1814-mayon.prompt: As ash rains down, what is the safest course of action for the townspeople?

choices.text: Head toward the coast to escape by boat
Gather belongings first, then decide where to go
Shelter inside the stone church and wait out the eruption
Flee immediately away from the volcano's base to higher, distant ground

evt-02-01-1814-mayon.butterflyEffect: The eruption buried Cagsawa town under volcanic debris and pyroclastic flows, killing over 1,200 people, many of whom had sheltered in the church believing its stone walls would protect them. Only the church's belfry remained above the ash, and it still stands today as a haunting landmark near Legazpi, drawing visitors to the site of the Philippines' deadliest recorded eruption.

evt-02-01-1896-giacomo-puccini.scenario: It's 1 February 1896 in Turin, and you're seated at the Teatro Regio as a young, little-known conductor named Arturo Toscanini raises his baton for the premiere of Puccini's La bohème.
evt-02-01-1896-giacomo-puccini.prompt: How did critics and audiences first receive this new opera?

choices.text: Mixed reviews, with critics puzzled by its intimate style despite growing audience enthusiasm
It was cancelled after intermission due to a fire
Universal critical acclaim from the very first night
A near-riot broke out over its perceived immorality

evt-02-01-1896-giacomo-puccini.butterflyEffect: Despite tepid, puzzled reviews from critics who found its intimate style unconventional, La bohème's public popularity grew rapidly. It went on to become one of the most performed operas in history, securing Puccini's international fame and launching Toscanini's rise to prominence.

evt-02-01-1942-voice-of-america.scenario: It's late February 1942 in a New York studio. America has just entered the war, and you're drafting the opening words for a new government radio service meant to reach occupied Europe.
evt-02-01-1942-voice-of-america.prompt: What editorial promise do you decide to open the broadcast with?

choices.text: Broadcast direct calls for Europeans to assassinate Hitler
Fill airtime purely with music and entertainment
Only broadcast victories and morale-boosting propaganda
Tell listeners the truth, even when the war news is bad

evt-02-01-1942-voice-of-america.butterflyEffect: The first Voice of America broadcast on 24 February 1942 pledged that listeners would hear "the news may be good or bad—we shall tell you the truth." That commitment to credibility became VOA's founding creed, and the service grew into the largest U.S. international broadcaster, later beaming uncensored news behind the Iron Curtain throughout the Cold War.

evt-02-01-1957-felix-wankel.scenario: It is 1 February 1957 in a workshop at NSU Motorenwerke in Germany. Engineers gather around a strange new engine with no pistons, cylinders, or crankshaft as it is about to run for the first time.
evt-02-01-1957-felix-wankel.prompt: What made this radical new engine design so different from conventional car engines?

choices.text: It used steam turbines borrowed from ship engines
It eliminated the need for an ignition system entirely
It used a triangular rotor instead of pistons to convert pressure directly into rotary motion
It replaced gasoline with compressed air as fuel

evt-02-01-1957-felix-wankel.butterflyEffect: The DKM 54 prototype proved that a triangular rotor spinning inside an epitrochoid-shaped housing could replace pistons entirely, producing smooth rotary motion directly. The design later powered the NSU Ro80 and, most famously, Mazda's rotary sports cars, though its thirst for fuel and sealing problems kept it a niche technology rather than a mainstream replacement for the piston engine.

evt-02-01-1960-civil-rights-movement.scenario: It is 1 February 1960, and you and three fellow North Carolina A&T students take seats at the whites-only lunch counter at Woolworth's in Greensboro, ordering coffee you know staff won't serve you.
evt-02-01-1960-civil-rights-movement.prompt: What do you do when the staff refuses to serve you?

choices.text: Leave immediately to avoid confrontation
Damage the counter in protest
Remain seated peacefully until closing, returning each day to sit again
Demand police arrest the staff on the spot

evt-02-01-1960-civil-rights-movement.butterflyEffect: The four students returned day after day, and their peaceful sit-in ignited a wave of similar protests across the South, helping launch the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee and accelerating the desegregation of lunch counters nationwide.

evt-02-01-1972-kuala-lumpur.scenario: It is 1 February 1972. Kuala Lumpur, already the seat of Malaysia's federal government, is formally proclaimed a city, elevating its status within Selangor state.
evt-02-01-1972-kuala-lumpur.prompt: What major administrative change follows for Kuala Lumpur a couple of years later?

choices.text: It becomes an independent city-state outside Malaysia
It is carved out of Selangor to become a Federal Territory
It loses its status as Malaysia's capital
It is merged fully into Selangor's state government

evt-02-01-1972-kuala-lumpur.butterflyEffect: In 1974, Kuala Lumpur was separated from Selangor and made Malaysia's first Federal Territory, placing it under direct federal administration rather than state control. This restructuring supported its rapid growth into the country's commercial and cultural hub, even after many federal government offices later relocated to the purpose-built city of Putrajaya in 1999.

evt-02-01-1979-ruhollah-khomeini.scenario: It is 1 February 1979, and you stand among millions lining the streets of Tehran as an Air France jet carrying Ayatollah Khomeini home from fifteen years of exile touches down at Mehrabad Airport.
evt-02-01-1979-ruhollah-khomeini.prompt: What did Khomeini's return trigger within weeks?

choices.text: Khomeini's immediate arrest by the military
The collapse of the Shah's government and declaration of an Islamic Republic
A negotiated power-sharing government with the Shah's ministers
A ceasefire between the Shah and rebel forces without government change

evt-02-01-1979-ruhollah-khomeini.butterflyEffect: Within days the Shah's last government collapsed, and by April 1979 Iran was declared an Islamic Republic with Khomeini as supreme leader. The revolution reshaped Middle Eastern politics and set off decades of hostility between Iran and the United States.

evt-02-01-2001-timor-leste-defence-force.scenario: It is February 2001 in newly liberated Timor-Leste, still under UN transitional administration ahead of full independence. You spent years as a guerrilla fighter with FALINTIL, resisting Indonesian occupation from the mountains.
evt-02-01-2001-timor-leste-defence-force.prompt: As the territory prepares for statehood, what should former FALINTIL fighters do?

choices.text: Integrate into the newly formed national defense force, F-FDTL
Disband entirely now that occupation has ended
Remain an independent militia outside government control
Merge with the departing Indonesian military units

evt-02-01-2001-timor-leste-defence-force.butterflyEffect: FALINTIL fighters were formally integrated into the new Timor-Leste Defence Force (F-FDTL), transforming a guerrilla resistance movement into the national military of an independent state ahead of Timor-Leste's formal independence in May 2002. The young force later faced serious internal strife, including a 2006 crisis rooted in regional divisions among its ranks.

evt-02-01-2003-space-shuttle-columbia-di.scenario: It is mid-January 2003. As a NASA engineer reviewing launch footage, you've spotted a chunk of foam striking Columbia's left wing during ascent, and you cannot yet tell how much damage it caused.
evt-02-01-2003-space-shuttle-columbia-di.prompt: What do the concerned engineers push mission management to do?

choices.text: Request additional imagery of the wing from military assets
Order the crew to attempt an emergency early landing
Dismiss the strike as routine and take no further action
Send an astronaut on an immediate spacewalk to inspect the tiles

evt-02-01-2003-space-shuttle-columbia-di.butterflyEffect: The Debris Assessment Team requested Department of Defense imagery to inspect the wing, but mission managers, including chair Linda Ham, judged it unnecessary and declined the request. The true extent of the damage remained unknown, and on 1 February 2003 hot gases breached the wing during re-entry, destroying Columbia and killing all seven astronauts. NASA later grounded the shuttle fleet for over two years and mandated on-orbit inspections for every future mission.

evt-02-01-2007-national-weather-service.scenario: You're a National Weather Service meteorologist surveying tornado damage on 1 February 2007, the very first day a new intensity scale takes effect nationwide.
evt-02-01-2007-national-weather-service.prompt: Which scale do you now use to rate the tornado's strength?

choices.text: The Enhanced Fujita (EF) Scale
The TORRO tornado intensity scale
The Saffir–Simpson hurricane scale
The original 1971 Fujita Scale

evt-02-01-2007-national-weather-service.butterflyEffect: The NWS retired the original 1971 Fujita scale in favor of the Enhanced Fujita (EF) Scale, which used 28 damage indicators on real structures to give far more precise wind-speed estimates. The change improved the accuracy of tornado ratings across the United States and became the new national standard for classifying tornado intensity.

evt-02-01-2009-johanna-sigur-ardottir.scenario: It is early 2009 in Reykjavík. Iceland's banking system has collapsed, protesters are banging pots outside parliament, and the sitting government has just resigned under pressure. As a senior minister in the Social Democratic Alliance, you are asked to lead an interim government.
evt-02-01-2009-johanna-sigur-ardottir.prompt: What should you do to steady the country as Iceland's economy is in freefall?

choices.text: Form a coalition government and take over as interim prime minister
Call for immediate new elections and step back from leadership
Request Iceland be annexed by a neighboring Nordic country for stability
Dissolve parliament and rule by emergency decree alone

evt-02-01-2009-johanna-sigur-ardottir.butterflyEffect: Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir was sworn in as prime minister, becoming Iceland's first female head of government and the world's first openly LGBTQ head of government. She led a coalition through the painful aftermath of the financial crash, overseeing bank restructuring and the contentious Icesave debt dispute with Britain and the Netherlands.

evt-02-01-2009-first-cabinet-of-johanna-.scenario: It's 1 February 2009 in Reykjavík. Iceland's government has just collapsed under weeks of pot-and-pan protests over the banking crash, and parliament must pick someone to lead an interim coalition until elections.
evt-02-01-2009-first-cabinet-of-johanna-.prompt: Who do the Social Democrats and Left-Greens choose to lead the caretaker government?

choices.text: Ingibjörg Sólrún Gísladóttir
Geir Haarde
Steingrímur J. Sigfússon
Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir

evt-02-01-2009-first-cabinet-of-johanna-.butterflyEffect: Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir became prime minister, making her the world's first openly lesbian head of government. She steered Iceland through brutal IMF-backed austerity and bank restructuring, then won a full mandate in the 2009 election that followed.

evt-02-01-2012-egyptian-premier-league.scenario: It is 1 February 2012, and the final whistle blows at Port Said Stadium as Al-Masry stun Al-Ahly 3-1. Home fans surge onto the pitch, and chaos engulfs Al-Ahly's players and traveling supporters.
evt-02-01-2012-egyptian-premier-league.prompt: What did the violence that followed trigger in Egypt's fragile transition?

choices.text: Al-Masry and Al-Ahly fans reconciling within days
The government's immediate resignation and fresh elections
A permanent ban on all football in Egypt
Nationwide protests and clashes with police that deepened distrust of security forces

evt-02-01-2012-egyptian-premier-league.butterflyEffect: The disaster, which killed dozens, ignited nationwide protests against police inaction and deepened public distrust of security forces during Egypt's post-revolution transition. Several police and stadium officials later faced trial over the failure to prevent the violence.

evt-02-01-2013-the-shard.scenario: It's 1 February 2013, and you've queued for hours to ride the high-speed lifts to the viewing gallery of London's newly finished Shard, the tallest building in Western Europe.
evt-02-01-2013-the-shard.prompt: What became of the Shard's public viewing platform in the years that followed?

choices.text: It was requisitioned by the government for security operations
It was converted into office space for tech companies
It became one of London's most popular paid attractions, drawing over a million visitors a year
