It closed within a year due to lack of public interest

evt-02-01-2013-the-shard.butterflyEffect: The View from The Shard became one of London's top paid tourist attractions, drawing over a million visitors annually and cementing the tower as a defining symbol of the city's skyline, spurring further high-rise development around London Bridge.

evt-02-01-2021-tatmadaw.scenario: It is the early morning of 1 February 2021 in Naypyidaw. You are a National League for Democracy lawmaker, and soldiers have just sealed off the roads to parliament ahead of its scheduled opening session.
evt-02-01-2021-tatmadaw.prompt: What does the Tatmadaw do to the elected government that morning?

choices.text: Detains Aung San Suu Kyi and the president, declaring a state of emergency
Resigns its command and hands full control to parliament
Calls for immediate fresh elections within the week
Allows Aung San Suu Kyi to continue as caretaker leader

evt-02-01-2021-tatmadaw.butterflyEffect: The military detained Aung San Suu Kyi and President Win Myint, declared a year-long state of emergency, and handed power to commander-in-chief Min Aung Hlaing. The coup triggered a nationwide Civil Disobedience Movement, armed resistance across the country, and international sanctions that pushed Myanmar into prolonged civil conflict.

evt-02-01-2022-death-of-rayan-aourram.scenario: You are part of the Moroccan rescue team at Ighran village in early February 2022. A five-year-old boy has been trapped for days deep in a narrow 32-metre dry well, and diggers have carved a parallel shaft alongside it to try to reach him.
evt-02-01-2022-death-of-rayan-aourram.prompt: How do rescuers try to reach the boy without endangering him further?

choices.text: Widen the original well directly with heavy machinery
Flood the well to try to float him to the surface
Dig a parallel shaft and tunnel sideways to reach him safely
Lower a rope harness and pull him straight up immediately

evt-02-01-2022-death-of-rayan-aourram.butterflyEffect: Rescuers reached Rayan on 5 February after days of round-the-clock digging watched live by millions across Morocco and the Arab world, but he had already died from his injuries. His case pushed Moroccan authorities to promise tighter safety rules for unguarded rural wells.

evt-02-02-506-alaric-ii.scenario: It is 506, and you serve as legal advisor to Alaric II at Aire-sur-l'Adour. Your Visigothic king rules over a kingdom split between Gothic warriors, who live by their own tribal law, and a much larger population of Gallo-Roman subjects, who expect the law of Rome.
evt-02-02-506-alaric-ii.prompt: What does Alaric II do to govern his Roman subjects?

choices.text: Adopt the law code of the Byzantine emperor wholesale
Force all subjects, Goth and Roman alike, to live under Visigothic tribal law
Promulgate a written compilation of Roman law for his Roman subjects
Abolish written law and rule purely by royal decree

evt-02-02-506-alaric-ii.butterflyEffect: He promulgated the Breviarium Alaricianum (Lex Romana Visigothorum), a codified digest of Roman law drawn from the Theodosian Code and other sources, for use among his Roman population. Because much of the original Theodosian Code was later lost, this Breviary became one of the main surviving channels through which Roman law reached medieval Western Europe, used for centuries until eclipsed by the rediscovered Corpus of Justinian.

evt-02-02-1659-jan-van-riebeeck.scenario: You are Jan van Riebeeck at the young Cape Colony, standing over vats of grapes pressed from vines carried out from Europe, waiting to see whether the settlement's first attempt at wine has succeeded.
evt-02-02-1659-jan-van-riebeeck.prompt: What do you note in your journal about the result of this first pressing?

choices.text: Wine has been successfully pressed from Cape grapes for the first time
Frost destroyed the young vines before harvest
The pressed wine spoiled within days and was discarded
The grapes failed to ripen in the Cape climate

evt-02-02-1659-jan-van-riebeeck.butterflyEffect: Van Riebeeck recorded that wine had been pressed from Cape grapes for the first time, a modest entry that marked the birth of South African winemaking. That single harvest grew into one of the world's major wine-producing regions, still tied to the Cape's identity today.

evt-02-02-1709-alexander-selkirk.scenario: You are Alexander Selkirk, marooned alone for over four years on a remote South Pacific island. A ship's sails finally appear on the horizon, and you scramble to make sure its lookout notices you.
evt-02-02-1709-alexander-selkirk.prompt: What do you do to catch the approaching privateers' attention?

choices.text: Wait silently, assuming the ship will pass regardless
Hide inland, fearing the ship carries pirates
Build up signal fires and wave to draw the ship's eye
Swim out immediately toward the distant vessel

evt-02-02-1709-alexander-selkirk.butterflyEffect: Selkirk was spotted and taken aboard by Captain Woodes Rogers, ending his four-year, four-month ordeal. His survival story became one of the inspirations for Daniel Defoe's 1719 novel Robinson Crusoe, helping to establish the castaway as a lasting literary archetype.

evt-02-02-1913-grand-central-terminal.scenario: It's early 1913 and you're an engineer overseeing the grand reopening of Grand Central after a deadly 1902 collision, when smoke filled the Park Avenue tunnel and blinded a train crew, killing seventeen commuters.
evt-02-02-1913-grand-central-terminal.prompt: What change do planners make to prevent another such disaster?

choices.text: Electrify the trains and move the tracks underground
Reduce train speeds through the tunnel
Relocate the station further from the city center
Install brighter gas lanterns throughout the tunnel

evt-02-02-1913-grand-central-terminal.butterflyEffect: The switch to electric trains let engineers bury the tracks on multiple underground levels beneath the new terminal, eliminating the smoke hazard entirely. The freed-up land above became the foundation for Park Avenue's skyscraper corridor, reshaping Midtown Manhattan for the next century.

evt-02-02-1934-export-import-bank-of-the.scenario: It is early 1934, and you advise President Franklin D. Roosevelt during the depths of the Depression. The United States has just recognized the Soviet Union diplomatically, and American manufacturers want financing to sell goods abroad but private banks are wary of the risk.
evt-02-02-1934-export-import-bank-of-the.prompt: What new institution does Roosevelt create to finance this export trade?

choices.text: Organize a private banking consortium to underwrite the risk
Have the Treasury issue direct loans to foreign governments
Create a federal export credit agency to finance and guarantee export sales
Rely solely on lowering tariffs to encourage trade

evt-02-02-1934-export-import-bank-of-the.butterflyEffect: Roosevelt established the Export-Import Bank by executive order, initially to finance trade with the Soviet Union. The agency quickly expanded beyond that original purpose to back American exports worldwide, becoming a permanent tool of U.S. economic policy that later supported wartime trade and postwar reconstruction financing.

evt-02-02-1943-battle-of-stalingrad.scenario: It is 2 February 1943 amid the rubble of Stalingrad. Field Marshal Friedrich Paulus commands the last starving, ammunition-less pocket of the German Sixth Army, encircled by the Red Army, while Hitler's standing orders forbid retreat or surrender.
evt-02-02-1943-battle-of-stalingrad.prompt: What does Paulus ultimately decide to do?

choices.text: Surrender his remaining forces to the Red Army
Order one final breakout attempt to the west
Negotiate a local ceasefire to evacuate only the wounded
Fight to the last man as Hitler demanded

evt-02-02-1943-battle-of-stalingrad.butterflyEffect: Paulus surrendered along with the remnants of his army, becoming the first German field marshal ever taken prisoner. The collapse ended Germany's 1942 summer offensive and handed the Soviet Union the strategic initiative on the Eastern Front for the rest of the war.

evt-02-02-1972-the-troubles.scenario: It is 2 February 1972, three days after British paratroopers shot dead thirteen unarmed civilians in Derry. You stand with thousands of furious demonstrators outside the British Embassy in Dublin's Merrion Square as tempers boil over.
evt-02-02-1972-the-troubles.prompt: What does the enraged crowd actually do to the embassy that day?

choices.text: Embassy staff repel the crowd with tear gas
Irish troops disperse the crowd before any damage occurs
They burn the embassy building to the ground
The ambassador negotiates a peaceful withdrawal of protesters

evt-02-02-1972-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The crowd burned the British Embassy to the ground, the only time a British diplomatic mission has been destroyed by a mob on foreign soil. The act deepened Anglo-Irish tension, boosted IRA recruitment across Ireland, and kept international attention fixed on Bloody Sunday for decades to come.

evt-02-02-1974-general-dynamics-f-16-fig.scenario: It is January 1974 at Edwards Air Force Base. You are test pilot Phil Oestricher, running a high-speed taxi test of the new YF-16 prototype, when the aircraft suddenly lifts off the runway and begins rolling uncontrollably from side to side.
evt-02-02-1974-general-dynamics-f-16-fig.prompt: What do you do to keep the prototype from crashing?

choices.text: Throttle back immediately and let the aircraft settle onto the runway
Continue the takeoff and fly the aircraft rather than risk a low-speed crash
Eject at once and abandon the prototype
Slam the brakes and try to force the nose wheel down

evt-02-02-1974-general-dynamics-f-16-fig.butterflyEffect: Oestricher chose to fly rather than fight the roll on the ground, climbing away and circling for six minutes before landing safely. The unplanned flight was later recognized as the YF-16's actual first flight, and the incident exposed a control-system flaw that engineers quickly fixed, keeping the program on track to become the F-16, the most widely produced fourth-generation jet fighter in the world.

evt-02-02-1980-federal-bureau-of-investi.scenario: It's early February 1980, and news breaks that FBI agents posing as aides to a wealthy fictional Arab sheikh spent two years secretly filming members of Congress accepting cash bribes in the operation known as Abscam.
evt-02-02-1980-federal-bureau-of-investi.prompt: What happens to the politicians caught on tape?

choices.text: The Supreme Court rules the sting unconstitutional
Several are convicted of bribery despite entrapment defenses
They resign quietly with no criminal charges filed
All charges are dropped due to unlawful surveillance

evt-02-02-1980-federal-bureau-of-investi.butterflyEffect: Abscam led to the conviction of six U.S. Representatives and one Senator, among the first major FBI undercover stings against sitting members of Congress. The case triggered lasting debate over entrapment and the limits of government sting operations.

evt-02-02-1982-1982-hama-massacre.scenario: It is February 1982, and you serve in Hafez al-Assad's government as the Fighting Vanguard of the Muslim Brotherhood leads an uprising in the city of Hama, part of a Sunni Islamist insurgency that has simmered since 1976.
evt-02-02-1982-1982-hama-massacre.prompt: What does the Assad government decide to do to end the revolt?

choices.text: Launch a sustained military siege and crackdown on the city
Withdraw the army and let local authorities handle it
Negotiate a power-sharing agreement with the Muslim Brotherhood
Grant amnesty to the uprising's leaders in exchange for surrender

evt-02-02-1982-1982-hama-massacre.butterflyEffect: The regime ordered the Syrian Arab Army and Defense Companies militia, commanded by Rifaat al-Assad, to besiege Hama for nearly a month, crushing the uprising by force. The massacre broke the Muslim Brotherhood's armed insurgency for a generation and became a lasting symbol of the Assad family's willingness to use overwhelming force, a precedent invoked again when Bashar al-Assad's government faced uprising in 2011.

evt-02-02-1989-soviet-afghan-war.scenario: It is 2 February 1989, and you command the last Soviet armoured column rolling out of Kabul. Nine years of fighting have failed to pacify Afghanistan, and mujahideen fighters watch from the hills as your convoy heads for the border.
evt-02-02-1989-soviet-afghan-war.prompt: What happens to the Afghan communist government after the Soviets fully withdraw?

choices.text: Mujahideen leaders immediately form a stable coalition government
It collapses within months of the Soviet exit
It survives for three more years before falling in 1992
Soviet forces return within weeks to prop it up

evt-02-02-1989-soviet-afghan-war.butterflyEffect: Contrary to many predictions, President Najibullah's government survived on its own for three more years, finally collapsing in 1992. The resulting power vacuum triggered a brutal civil war among mujahideen factions, paving the way for the Taliban's rise in 1996 and, later, al-Qaeda's sanctuary there.

evt-02-02-2004-roger-federer.scenario: It is 2 February 2004. Fresh off winning the Australian Open, you are Roger Federer, about to be crowned the world's No. 1 ranked men's singles player for the first time in your career.
evt-02-02-2004-roger-federer.prompt: What follows Federer reaching the world No. 1 ranking?

choices.text: He loses the ranking within a month to Andre Agassi
He begins a record run of 237 consecutive weeks at No. 1
He immediately retires from ranking competition to focus on exhibitions
He loses in the first round of his next tournament and drops out of the top ten

evt-02-02-2004-roger-federer.butterflyEffect: Federer went on to hold the top ranking for a record 237 consecutive weeks, a run that redefined dominance in men's tennis and set the stage for his rivalries with Rafael Nadal and later Novak Djokovic. He would finish as year-end No. 1 five times and eventually amass 20 major singles titles.

evt-02-02-2009-omid.scenario: It is 2 February 2009 at Semnan Space Center. You watch the Iranian-built Safir rocket ignite, carrying Omid, Iran's first domestically made satellite, timed to mark the 30th anniversary of the Islamic Revolution.
evt-02-02-2009-omid.prompt: What follows the launch of Omid?

choices.text: The UN immediately imposes new sanctions specifically over this launch
The rocket explodes on the launch pad, destroying the satellite
Iran cancels its space program shortly afterward
NASA confirms the satellite reached orbit successfully

evt-02-02-2009-omid.butterflyEffect: NASA confirmed the next day that Omid had reached low Earth orbit, making Iran one of only a handful of nations capable of building and launching its own satellite. The achievement also sharpened Western concern that the same rocket technology could be adapted for long-range missiles, feeding into later sanctions debates over Iran's missile program.

evt-02-02-2021-tatmadaw.scenario: It is 2 February 2021 in Naypyidaw. Overnight, soldiers detained Aung San Suu Kyi and other elected leaders, and the military has just announced the State Administration Council will now run the country.
evt-02-02-2021-tatmadaw.prompt: How do millions of ordinary Burmese citizens respond in the weeks that follow?

choices.text: They petition ASEAN and wait quietly for its verdict
They accept the new council peacefully and return to work as normal
They flee the country en masse within days
They launch a nationwide Civil Disobedience Movement of strikes and protests

evt-02-02-2021-tatmadaw.butterflyEffect: A mass Civil Disobedience Movement erupted, with doctors, civil servants, and railway workers walking off the job to paralyze the junta's administration. Peaceful protest was met with lethal force, and over time resistance hardened into armed struggle by newly formed People's Defence Forces, plunging Myanmar into a still-unresolved civil war.

evt-02-02-2025-slovenia.scenario: It's 1 February 2025 and you're a Dallas Mavericks executive weighing a stunning offer for franchise superstar Luka Dončić, just days after he suffered a hamstring injury.
evt-02-02-2025-slovenia.prompt: What trade shocks the NBA world this day?

choices.text: Trading Dončić to the Los Angeles Lakers for Anthony Davis
Trading Dončić to the Boston Celtics for draft picks
Trading Dončić to the Miami Heat for Jimmy Butler
Signing Dončić to a new supermax contract extension

evt-02-02-2025-slovenia.butterflyEffect: General manager Nico Harrison sent the 25-year-old Dončić to the Los Angeles Lakers for Anthony Davis, Max Christie, and a first-round pick—one of the most stunning trades in NBA history. It sparked furious backlash from Mavericks fans and immediately reshaped both franchises' championship hopes.

evt-02-03-1047-henry-iii-holy-roman-empe.scenario: It is 1047, and you stand before Emperor Henry III's court in Italy as he formally recognizes a Norman adventurer's claim over rich lands in the south, lands the Normans have already been carving out by the sword.
evt-02-03-1047-henry-iii-holy-roman-empe.prompt: Whom does Henry III recognize as count of Apulia and Calabria?

choices.text: Robert Guiscard
Roger de Hauteville
William Iron Arm
Drogo of Hauteville

evt-02-03-1047-henry-iii-holy-roman-empe.butterflyEffect: Henry III's recognition of Drogo of Hauteville legitimized Norman rule in southern Italy. This set a precedent that helped the Hautevilles, and later Robert Guiscard and Roger II, build a Norman kingdom that would eventually unite Sicily and southern Italy.

evt-02-03-1266-mudejar-revolt-of-1264-12.scenario: You march with King James I of Aragon's army toward rebel-held Murcia in early 1266, sent to help Castile crush the Mudéjar uprising in the south.
evt-02-03-1266-mudejar-revolt-of-1264-12.prompt: What happens when the Aragonese force reaches Murcia?

choices.text: The city surrenders and the revolt collapses
Murcia holds out for another decade of siege
James I is repelled and forced to retreat
Aragon annexes Murcia outright for itself

evt-02-03-1266-mudejar-revolt-of-1264-12.butterflyEffect: Murcia surrendered and the revolt collapsed soon after. Castile expelled much of the region's Muslim population and resettled Christians in their place, while Granada became a tribute-paying vassal of Castile, a relationship that lasted until Granada's final conquest in 1492.

evt-02-03-1852-argentine-confederation.scenario: It is 3 February 1852, and you are one of Juan Manuel de Rosas's soldiers dug in at Caseros near Buenos Aires, watching Urquiza's army and its Brazilian and Uruguayan allies close in.
evt-02-03-1852-argentine-confederation.prompt: What happens to Rosas after this crushing defeat?

choices.text: He is captured and executed by Urquiza's men
He negotiates a power-sharing government with Urquiza
He flees into exile in England
Congress reinstates him as governor

evt-02-03-1852-argentine-confederation.butterflyEffect: Rosas fled the battlefield and sailed into exile in England, where he lived out his life near Southampton. Urquiza emerged as Argentina's dominant leader, paving the way for the 1853 constitution and the eventual reunification of the provinces into the modern Argentine Republic.

evt-02-03-1862-moldavia.scenario: It is 3 February 1862 in Bucharest. Alexandru Ioan Cuza, already ruling both Moldavia and Wallachia since his double election three years earlier, presides over the formal merging of their governments into one.
evt-02-03-1862-moldavia.prompt: What did this formal union create?

choices.text: The United Principalities, the political basis of modern Romania
An Austrian protectorate over both territories
A permanent Ottoman province governed directly from Istanbul
A Russian military occupation zone

evt-02-03-1862-moldavia.butterflyEffect: The fusion created the United Principalities, soon simply called Romania, with Cuza as its single ruling prince and a unified administration in Bucharest. This foundation led toward full independence from Ottoman suzerainty in 1877–78 and the establishment of the Kingdom of Romania in 1881.

evt-02-03-1870-reconstruction-era.scenario: It is February 1870, and you are a Republican senator watching the tally as states ratify a new constitutional amendment. Southern states are required to approve it before rejoining the Union in good standing.
evt-02-03-1870-reconstruction-era.prompt: What did the Fifteenth Amendment guarantee?

choices.text: Equal pay for freedmen working on former plantations
Federal land grants of forty acres to formerly enslaved families
The right to vote regardless of race, color, or previous condition of servitude
Automatic citizenship for children born to formerly enslaved parents

evt-02-03-1870-reconstruction-era.butterflyEffect: The Fifteenth Amendment barred states from denying the vote based on race, color, or previous servitude. Southern states soon undermined it through poll taxes, literacy tests, and violent intimidation, and it would take the Voting Rights Act of 1965 to enforce its promise nationwide.

evt-02-03-1933-adolf-hitler.scenario: It's February 3, 1933, days after being sworn in as chancellor. You are a senior German army officer summoned to a private dinner where Hitler outlines his ambitions for the nation's future to the assembled Reichswehr leadership.
evt-02-03-1933-adolf-hitler.prompt: What does Hitler tell the generals is his ultimate foreign policy goal?

choices.text: Peaceful economic expansion through new trade treaties
The conquest of "Lebensraum" in the East, to be ruthlessly Germanized
A purely defensive strategy to restore Germany's 1914 borders
An alliance with the Soviet Union to jointly divide Europe

evt-02-03-1933-adolf-hitler.butterflyEffect: This early private speech previewed the racial and territorial logic that would drive Nazi Germany's invasions of Poland and the Soviet Union. It foreshadowed the brutal occupation policies in Eastern Europe that enabled the Holocaust and the deaths of millions in the years that followed.

evt-02-03-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It's February 3, 1941, and you're a British Indian Army soldier scaling the steep, fortress-like heights above Keren, Eritrea, where dug-in Italian colonial troops hold a narrow gorge blocking the road to Asmara.
evt-02-03-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: What must Allied forces do to break through at Keren?

choices.text: Endure weeks of costly frontal assaults on the mountain passes before finally storming the position in late March
Retreat and abandon the East African campaign as too costly
Negotiate a surrender with the Italian garrison after a brief siege
Bypass the position entirely by sea, landing troops directly at Asmara

evt-02-03-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The Battle of Keren, one of the hardest-fought actions of the East African Campaign, finally fell to Allied forces in late March 1941 after nearly two months of fighting. Its capture opened the road to Asmara and the port of Massawa, effectively ending organized Italian resistance in Eritrea.

evt-02-03-1966-soviet-union.scenario: You are a Soviet engineer at mission control on 3 February 1966, watching the Luna 9 probe descend toward the Moon on the first attempted soft landing by any spacecraft.
evt-02-03-1966-soviet-union.prompt: What does Luna 9 do once it touches down intact?

choices.text: Bounces back into lunar orbit
Explodes on impact with the surface
Loses all contact with Earth immediately
Transmits the first photographs from the lunar surface

evt-02-03-1966-soviet-union.butterflyEffect: Luna 9 transmitted the first photographs ever taken from the lunar surface, proving the ground could bear a lander's weight rather than swallowing it in deep dust. The images reassured NASA's Apollo planners about the lunar module's design and sharpened the space race just three years before Apollo 11.

evt-02-03-1971-frank-serpico.scenario: It's February 3, 1971, and you're a plainclothes NYPD detective forcing open a heroin dealer's door in Brooklyn. A shot rings out, hitting you in the face — and the two officers meant to back you up are nowhere to be found.
evt-02-03-1971-frank-serpico.prompt: What follows for you and for the NYPD after this shooting?

choices.text: You are quietly promoted and the incident is forgotten
Suspicion the shooting was a setup spurs a Times exposé and the Knapp Commission investigation into police corruption
The NYPD immediately disbands its plainclothes narcotics unit
The two officers are decorated for their response

evt-02-03-1971-frank-serpico.butterflyEffect: Serpico survived, but many believed his partners deliberately failed to help him because he had exposed corruption. Combined with his earlier testimony, the incident pushed Mayor Lindsay to form the Knapp Commission, whose findings reshaped NYPD internal affairs and made "Serpico" a byword for the police whistleblower, later dramatized in the 1973 Al Pacino film.

evt-02-03-1972-1972-iran-blizzard.scenario: It is February 1972 in a snowbound village in northwestern Iran. Seven meters of snow have fallen after days of blizzard, and rescue teams outside are struggling to reach anyone still alive.
evt-02-03-1972-1972-iran-blizzard.prompt: What actually happened when help tried to reach the buried villages?

choices.text: International aid agencies had already evacuated the entire region in advance
The government declared the storm exaggerated and sent no assistance at all
Rescue teams could not reach many villages for days, and thousands died before help arrived
Army helicopters airlifted every survivor to safety within 24 hours

evt-02-03-1972-1972-iran-blizzard.butterflyEffect: Many villages were completely cut off for days, and rescue teams could not dig through in time; over 4,000 people died, making it the deadliest blizzard ever recorded. The disaster, following four years of drought, exposed how unprepared rural Iran was for extreme weather and pushed later governments toward better winter emergency planning.

evt-02-03-1984-john-buster.scenario: You are part of Dr. John Buster's team at Harbor-UCLA Medical Center in early 1984. An embryo conceived by artificial insemination in one woman must now be transferred, without surgery, into another woman who will carry it to term.
evt-02-03-1984-john-buster.prompt: What historic first did this procedure achieve?

choices.text: The first baby born through in vitro fertilization
The first successful human cloning experiment
The first embryo transfer between two women resulting in a live birth
The first use of frozen sperm in artificial insemination

evt-02-03-1984-john-buster.butterflyEffect: The transfer resulted in the first live birth from an embryo moved from one woman to another, announced on 3 February 1984. The technique demonstrated that a pregnancy could be established without the carrying mother's own egg, laying groundwork for later embryo donation and gestational surrogacy practices.

evt-02-03-1986-steve-jobs.scenario: It's 1986. You've just been ousted from Apple, the company you co-founded, and you're weighing whether to sink your money into a struggling computer-graphics division that George Lucas wants to sell.
evt-02-03-1986-steve-jobs.prompt: What does Jobs do with Lucasfilm's graphics division?

choices.text: He licenses its software but leaves ownership with Lucasfilm
He buys it for about $10 million and renames it Pixar, becoming its majority owner
He merges it into his new company NeXT as a hardware division
He turns down the offer and Disney buys it directly instead

evt-02-03-1986-steve-jobs.butterflyEffect: Pixar spent years selling hardware and software at a loss before pivoting fully to computer animation. Jobs's patient investment paid off when Toy Story (1995) became a landmark hit, and Disney's eventual $7.4 billion purchase of Pixar in 2006 made Jobs Disney's largest shareholder.

evt-02-03-1989-1989-paraguayan-coup-d-et.scenario: It is the night of 2–3 February 1989 in Asunción. General Andrés Rodríguez, related to Stroessner by marriage, has turned his garrison against the aging dictator amid a bitter power struggle inside the regime.

choices.text: Fled the country to avoid retaliation from loyalist forces
Quietly negotiated Stroessner's peaceful retirement abroad
Led an armed uprising that overthrew Stroessner after a night of street fighting
Joined Stroessner's guard to crush rival officers

evt-02-03-1989-1989-paraguayan-coup-d-et.butterflyEffect: Rodríguez led his troops in overnight street fighting that toppled Stroessner, ending 34 years of dictatorship known as El Stronato. Rodríguez then became president himself, dismantling many repressive laws and beginning Paraguay's uneven transition toward democracy in the 1990s.

evt-02-03-1994-space-shuttle-program.scenario: It's February 3, 1994, and you're strapped into Space Shuttle Discovery's flight deck for STS-60, sharing the cabin with a Russian cosmonaut who once held the record for longest single spaceflight after being stranded aboard Mir during the USSR's collapse.
evt-02-03-1994-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What historic first does this mission achieve?

choices.text: Krikalev becomes the first non-American to command a shuttle mission
The mission deploys the first component of the International Space Station
Sergei Krikalev becomes the first Russian cosmonaut to fly aboard an American Space Shuttle
The crew completes the first shuttle docking with the Mir space station

evt-02-03-1994-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: Krikalev's flight on STS-60 opened the Shuttle-Mir program, a series of joint US-Russian missions that built trust and technical cooperation between the former Cold War rivals' space agencies. That cooperation became the foundation for the International Space Station, launched in 1998 as a multinational project.

evt-02-03-1995-sts-63.scenario: You are guiding Space Shuttle Discovery toward its first close approach to the Russian station Mir on 6 February 1995 when sensors detect a small thruster fuel leak.
evt-02-03-1995-sts-63.prompt: What do you decide as Discovery nears Mir?

choices.text: Ignore the leak and continue as planned
Proceed with a full docking regardless
Abort the mission and return to Earth immediately
Halt the approach and hold at a safe distance

evt-02-03-1995-sts-63.butterflyEffect: Mission control held Discovery at a safe distance rather than closing all the way in, then completed the flyaround once the leak was assessed as no threat. The rehearsal validated the approach procedures used months later for STS-71, the first actual shuttle docking with Mir.

evt-02-03-1995-eileen-collins.scenario: It is February 1995, and you are strapped into the pilot's seat of Space Shuttle Discovery on mission STS-63, the countdown ticking toward launch. No woman has ever sat in this seat before.
evt-02-03-1995-eileen-collins.prompt: What historic first does this flight achieve?

choices.text: The first American woman to walk in space
The first shuttle mission to dock with Mir
The first civilian to fly on a Space Shuttle
The first woman to pilot a Space Shuttle

evt-02-03-1995-eileen-collins.butterflyEffect: Eileen Collins became the first woman to pilot a Space Shuttle, and the mission also achieved a close approach to the Russian space station Mir, rehearsing techniques for future dockings. Collins later went on to command a shuttle mission herself, opening the top seat of spaceflight command to women.

evt-02-03-2005-kam-air-flight-904.scenario: It is 3 February 2005, and your Boeing 737 is descending toward Kabul International Airport as a snowstorm cuts visibility to almost nothing over the surrounding Pamir foothills.
evt-02-03-2005-kam-air-flight-904.prompt: What ultimately caused Kam Air Flight 904 to crash?

choices.text: It was struck by ground fire during the descent
It descended into mountains hidden by the storm, a controlled flight into terrain
A hijacking attempt caused the crew to lose control
An engine failure occurred mid-flight over open terrain

evt-02-03-2005-kam-air-flight-904.butterflyEffect: The aircraft continued its descent into mountainous terrain hidden by the storm, a case of controlled flight into terrain, killing all 105 people aboard. The disaster drew scrutiny to Afghanistan's weak aviation infrastructure and Kam Air's safety practices in the years after the airline's founding.

evt-02-03-2006-al-qaeda-insurgency-in-ye.scenario: It is early February 2006, and you are a guard at a high-security prison in Sana'a. Overnight, a group of convicted militants has vanished through a tunnel dug from inside their cell block.
evt-02-03-2006-al-qaeda-insurgency-in-ye.prompt: What did this escape lead to?

choices.text: The withdrawal of all US forces from the region
A ceasefire between Yemen and Saudi Arabia
The immediate collapse of Yemen's government
The founding of al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula by an escaped militant

evt-02-03-2006-al-qaeda-insurgency-in-ye.butterflyEffect: Twenty-three al-Qaeda-linked prisoners tunneled out of the Sana'a facility, among them Nasir al-Wuhayshi, who became bin Laden's former aide. He went on to found al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP), which grew into one of the group's most dangerous branches and fueled Yemen's long insurgency.

evt-02-03-2014-2014-moscow-school-shooti.scenario: It is 3 February 2014 at School No. 263 in Moscow. Your teenage son is inside holding his classmates hostage after shooting his teacher and a police officer, and negotiators ask you to talk him into stopping.
evt-02-03-2014-2014-moscow-school-shooti.prompt: What do you do to try to end the standoff safely?

choices.text: Arrange a car so he can escape the building
Denounce him publicly on television
Refuse to get involved and wait for a SWAT assault
Go inside and negotiate his surrender

evt-02-03-2014-2014-moscow-school-shooti.butterflyEffect: The father entered the school and persuaded his son to release the hostages and surrender without further bloodshed. The case set off a national debate in Russia over school security, youth mental health support, and firearm licensing rules.

evt-02-03-2023-east-palestine-ohio-train.scenario: You are the incident commander at East Palestine, Ohio, days after the derailment, staring at damaged tank cars of vinyl chloride whose pressure and temperature keep climbing toward a possible catastrophic explosion.
evt-02-03-2023-east-palestine-ohio-train.prompt: What do you order to prevent a large-scale blast?

choices.text: Vent and burn the vinyl chloride in a controlled release
Demolish all the rail cars immediately with explosives
Evacuate and let the cars cool naturally over weeks
Flood the tank cars with water and wait

evt-02-03-2023-east-palestine-ohio-train.butterflyEffect: Officials vented and deliberately burned the vinyl chloride, sending a black plume over the town and releasing hydrogen chloride and phosgene. The decision avoided a feared explosion but triggered years of health complaints, lawsuits against Norfolk Southern, and congressional hearings on freight rail safety.

evt-02-04-960-emperor-taizu-of-song.scenario: It is 960, and you march with the Later Zhou army under general Zhao Kuangyin toward a reported northern invasion. At Chen Bridge Station, the troops halt and grow restless with their young, weak court back in the capital.
evt-02-04-960-emperor-taizu-of-song.prompt: What do the soldiers do to Zhao Kuangyin at Chen Bridge?

choices.text: They drape him in a yellow robe and proclaim him emperor
They mutiny and desert him for the enemy
They assassinate him for delaying the march
They force him to continue the campaign against the invaders

evt-02-04-960-emperor-taizu-of-song.butterflyEffect: The troops draped a yellow robe over Zhao Kuangyin and proclaimed him emperor, and he marched back to the capital where the Later Zhou's child ruler, Emperor Gong, was forced to abdicate. Zhao founded the Song dynasty, which went on to preside over one of China's most prosperous and culturally influential eras for over three centuries.

evt-02-04-1169-1169-sicily-earthquake.scenario: It is the morning of 4 February 1169, the eve of the feast of St. Agatha, and you are a fisherman in Catania. The ground has just heaved violently and the sea before you is strangely pulling back from the shore, exposing wet sand far out.
evt-02-04-1169-1169-sicily-earthquake.prompt: What should you do as the sea suddenly recedes after the tremor?

choices.text: Run inland to high ground immediately
Stay put and wait for the tide to return to normal
Rush down to the exposed sand to gather stranded fish
Row out to sea to check on your boat

evt-02-04-1169-1169-sicily-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The earthquake triggered a paleotsunami that struck the eastern Sicilian coast, adding to the devastation already inflicted on Catania, Lentini, and Modica. The disaster, remembered alongside the region's veneration of St. Agatha, remains one of the deadliest seismic events in Sicily's recorded history, killing an estimated 15,000 people.

evt-02-04-1488-bartolomeu-dias.scenario: You are part of Bartolomeu Dias's watering party, sent ashore at a bay on the southern African coast in February 1488 after storms blew your caravels far past the continent's tip. Local Khoikhoi herders, alarmed by your presence, begin hurling stones at your men.
evt-02-04-1488-bartolomeu-dias.prompt: What does Dias's crew do in response to the stone-throwing herders?

choices.text: They retreat and abandon the watering attempt entirely
They trade goods to calm the herders down
They request a local guide to negotiate safe passage
Dias uses a crossbow, killing one of the herders

evt-02-04-1488-bartolomeu-dias.butterflyEffect: Dias used a crossbow and killed one of the herders, the first recorded violent clash between Europeans and southern Africa's indigenous peoples. He named the bay for the incident, planted a stone padrão to claim it for Portugal, and his voyage's proof that Africa could be sailed around opened the route Vasco da Gama would later use to reach India.

evt-02-04-1555-english-reformation.scenario: It is 4 February 1555 at Smithfield, London. You are John Rogers, a Protestant clergyman condemned for heresy under Queen Mary I's restoration of Catholic authority, standing before the stake for his role in producing an English Bible.
evt-02-04-1555-english-reformation.prompt: What did Rogers's execution set in motion?

choices.text: It ended religious persecution in England
It caused Mary I to abandon the restoration of Catholicism
It led to Rogers being pardoned and released
It began a wave of Protestant burnings later chronicled in Foxe's Book of Martyrs

evt-02-04-1555-english-reformation.butterflyEffect: Rogers became the first of the Marian martyrs; roughly 280 Protestants would be burned under Mary I's reign in the years that followed, including Cranmer, Ridley, and Latimer. Their deaths were chronicled in John Foxe's Book of Martyrs, which shaped English Protestant identity for centuries and strengthened support for Elizabeth I's later religious settlement.

evt-02-04-1801-john-marshall.scenario: It is 4 February 1801, in the final weeks of John Adams's presidency, and you are a Federalist senator watching Adams's nominee take the oath as the new Chief Justice just before Thomas Jefferson's incoming administration takes power.
evt-02-04-1801-john-marshall.prompt: What did Adams accomplish by installing Marshall as Chief Justice before leaving office?

choices.text: He transferred the power of judicial appointments to Congress
He installed a caretaker justice who would resign once Jefferson took office
He entrenched Federalist judicial influence that would outlast his own party for decades
He weakened the judiciary to appease the incoming Jefferson administration

evt-02-04-1801-john-marshall.butterflyEffect: Marshall would serve as Chief Justice for 34 years, far outlasting the Federalist Party itself, and his 1803 opinion in Marbury v. Madison established the principle of judicial review. That single ruling gave the Supreme Court the power to strike down unconstitutional laws, reshaping the balance of American government for centuries.

evt-02-04-1820-chilean-war-of-independen.scenario: It is early February 1820. You serve under Lord Thomas Cochrane, commanding a small Chilean naval and marine force approaching the heavily fortified Spanish port of Valdivia under cover of darkness.
evt-02-04-1820-chilean-war-of-independen.prompt: How does Cochrane's force take the powerful Spanish fortifications?

choices.text: A surprise night assault by landing parties storming the forts directly
Bribing the Spanish garrison commander to open the gates
A negotiated surrender after a lengthy siege
A prolonged naval bombardment that flattens the forts

evt-02-04-1820-chilean-war-of-independen.butterflyEffect: Cochrane's men stormed the forts in a daring night assault, capturing Valdivia with minimal losses despite the town's formidable defenses. The victory secured southern Chile for the independence cause and cemented Cochrane's reputation as one of the era's boldest naval commanders.

evt-02-04-1859-constantin-von-tischendor.scenario: You are Constantin von Tischendorf, standing before the monks of Saint Catherine's Monastery at Mount Sinai in 1859. You have just laid eyes on an ancient parchment Bible far older and more complete than any you found here fifteen years earlier.
evt-02-04-1859-constantin-von-tischendor.prompt: What do you do to secure the manuscript for scholarly study?

choices.text: Copy it by hand over several months and leave the original behind
Buy it outright from the monks on the spot
Report it to the Ottoman authorities for confiscation
Persuade the monks to lend it to him to present to the Tsar of Russia

evt-02-04-1859-constantin-von-tischendor.butterflyEffect: Tischendorf persuaded the monks to lend him the manuscript, ostensibly to show it to the Russian Tsar, and it eventually became the Codex Sinaiticus, presented to Russia. In 1933 the Soviet government sold it to the British Library, where it remains one of the most important witnesses to the early Christian Bible.

evt-02-04-1899-philippine-american-war.scenario: It's the night of 4 February 1899. You are an American army private on picket duty near Manila when several armed Filipino soldiers approach your post and ignore your order to halt.
evt-02-04-1899-philippine-american-war.prompt: What do you do as the sentry facing the advancing men?

choices.text: Let them pass without engaging to avoid provoking a wider clash
Challenge them again, then fire when they keep advancing
Retreat quietly to report the sighting to headquarters
Fire a warning shot into the air and step aside

evt-02-04-1899-philippine-american-war.butterflyEffect: Private William Grayson opened fire, killing at least one Filipino soldier and triggering the Battle of Manila that night. The skirmish ignited the Philippine–American War, a brutal three-year conflict that entrenched decades of American colonial rule over the islands until World War II.

evt-02-04-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is early morning, 4 February 1945, and you are an American civilian who has spent nearly three years imprisoned at the Santo Tomas Internment Camp in Manila. Outside the gates, you can hear tanks of the U.S. 1st Cavalry Division smashing through the walls as gunfire echoes across the city.
evt-02-04-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What should the newly freed internees do as the tanks break through the gates?

choices.text: Take up arms alongside American soldiers in the city fighting
Flee the city on foot toward the countryside
Immediately walk out into the streets of Manila to celebrate
Stay inside the camp compound as fierce fighting continues in the surrounding city

evt-02-04-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Santo Tomas's roughly 3,700 internees were freed, but their liberation came just as the brutal Battle of Manila erupted around them, a month-long struggle that devastated the city and killed well over 100,000 Filipino civilians. The internees' rescue is remembered as a moment of relief overshadowed by the catastrophe still unfolding beyond the camp walls.

evt-02-04-1969-yasser-arafat.scenario: It's February 1969, and you sit as a delegate at the Palestinian National Council in Cairo, where guerrilla factions have gained influence since the 1967 Arab defeat and a new chairman must be chosen to lead the PLO.
evt-02-04-1969-yasser-arafat.prompt: Who do the delegates elect as the new chairman of the PLO?

choices.text: Ahmad Shukeiri
Nayef Hawatmeh
George Habash
Yasser Arafat

evt-02-04-1969-yasser-arafat.butterflyEffect: Yasser Arafat was elected chairman, a post he held until his death in 2004. Under him the PLO shifted from a loose umbrella body toward guerrilla struggle and later diplomacy, culminating in his 1974 UN address, the 1993 Oslo Accords, and a shared Nobel Peace Prize in 1994.

evt-02-04-1974-patty-hearst.scenario: It is the evening of 4 February 1974 in Berkeley, California. You are in the apartment when armed strangers calling themselves the Symbionese Liberation Army force nineteen-year-old newspaper heiress Patty Hearst into a car at gunpoint.
evt-02-04-1974-patty-hearst.prompt: What did the kidnappers initially demand as ransom for her release?

choices.text: Distribution of free food to California's poor
A $10 million cash payment
Publication of a political manifesto in national newspapers
Release of imprisoned radical activists

evt-02-04-1974-patty-hearst.butterflyEffect: The SLA demanded that the Hearst family distribute free food to California's poor, prompting the creation of the "People in Need" program. Weeks later Hearst herself joined the SLA, took the name "Tania," and participated in a bank robbery, a stunning turn that fueled national debate over coercion, brainwashing, and criminal responsibility that shadowed her later trial and conviction.

evt-02-04-1974-the-troubles.scenario: It's 4 February 1974. A coach carrying British soldiers and their families travels the M62 motorway in Yorkshire when a bomb concealed in the luggage hold explodes without warning.
evt-02-04-1974-the-troubles.prompt: What happened to the person controversially convicted of the bombing?

choices.text: She escaped custody before trial and was never recaptured
Her conviction was quashed in 1992 after the forensic evidence was discredited
Her conviction was upheld and she served a full life sentence
She was released early under the 1998 Good Friday Agreement

evt-02-04-1974-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: Judith Ward was convicted in 1974 largely on flawed forensic evidence and false confessions extracted under pressure. Her conviction was quashed in 1992 after the evidence was discredited, making the case one of the most notorious miscarriages of justice of the Troubles and fuelling wider reform of forensic and interrogation practices in the UK.

evt-02-04-1997-lebanon.scenario: It is the night of 4 February 1997, and you are an Israeli reservist waiting near the Lebanese border to be airlifted north for a routine rotation into the security zone. Two CH-53 Sea Stallion helicopters carrying your comrades lift off ahead of you into the dark sky.
evt-02-04-1997-lebanon.prompt: What followed the mid-air collision of the two troop-transport helicopters?

choices.text: Israel immediately doubled its troop presence in the security zone
The incident was kept secret from the Israeli public for years
The disaster sparked the Four Mothers protest movement demanding withdrawal from Lebanon
The defense minister resigned within days and a ceasefire was signed

evt-02-04-1997-lebanon.butterflyEffect: All 73 soldiers aboard the two helicopters were killed in the collision over northern Israel, one of the worst disasters in IDF history. Public grief turned into the grassroots Four Mothers movement, which campaigned relentlessly for withdrawal from Lebanon and helped push Israel toward its unilateral pullout from the security zone in 2000.

evt-02-04-1999-new-york-city-police-depa.scenario: It is just after midnight on 4 February 1999 in the Soundview section of the Bronx. Four plainclothes NYPD officers approach Amadou Diallo, an unarmed West African immigrant, believing he matches the description of a serial rapist.
evt-02-04-1999-new-york-city-police-depa.prompt: What happened when Diallo reached into his jacket for his wallet?

choices.text: Officers, believing he was drawing a gun, opened fire
Officers called for backup and waited before approaching further
Officers recognized the wallet and immediately stood down
Officers ordered him to freeze and he complied without incident

evt-02-04-1999-new-york-city-police-depa.butterflyEffect: Believing he was drawing a weapon, the officers fired 41 shots, hitting him 19 times; he died in the vestibule of his own building. All four were charged with second-degree murder but acquitted in 2000, and the case became a national flashpoint against NYPD's Street Crimes Unit, fueling years of protest and reform debates over stop-and-frisk policing.

evt-02-04-1999-new-carissa.scenario: It is 4 February 1999, and you are part of the Coast Guard response team watching the freighter New Carissa break apart on the storm-battered beach near Coos Bay, Oregon. Hundreds of thousands of gallons of fuel oil sit in her tanks, and the surf is rising fast.
evt-02-04-1999-new-carissa.prompt: What method is used to try to keep the ship's fuel oil from fouling the coastline?

choices.text: Abandon the ship entirely and let the oil disperse naturally
Set explosive charges to burn the oil off the ship before it can spill
Pump all the oil onto barges before attempting any tow
Wait for the storm to pass before touching the wreck

evt-02-04-1999-new-carissa.butterflyEffect: Crews set explosive charges to ignite the oil aboard the wreck, burning off a large portion of it, though a damaging slick still reached local beaches. The bow was later towed out to sea and sunk by a Navy submarine's torpedoes, while the stern lingered on the sand for nine more years before it was finally dismantled in 2008.

evt-02-04-2008-colombia.scenario: It is February 4, 2008, and you join a river of people flowing through the streets of Bogotá, joined by marchers in cities across Colombia and abroad, all demanding an end to a decades-old armed conflict.
evt-02-04-2008-colombia.prompt: Who are these marches directed against?

choices.text: FARC, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia
Drug cartels in Medellín
Paramilitary groups aligned with landowners
The Colombian government itself

evt-02-04-2008-colombia.butterflyEffect: Millions marched worldwide against FARC in the largest anti-terrorism demonstration in Colombian history, driven by outrage over hostage-taking and kidnappings. The mobilization pressured the government and international opinion, feeding into years of pressure that eventually helped bring FARC to the negotiating table.

evt-02-04-2015-songshan-airport.scenario: You are aboard TransAsia Flight 235, seconds after it lifts off from Taipei's Songshan Airport on 4 February 2015. An engine has just lost power, and the crew has only moments to respond.
evt-02-04-2015-songshan-airport.prompt: What fatal error did the flight crew make while trying to save the aircraft?

choices.text: They increased throttle too sharply, causing an aerodynamic stall
They attempted an emergency water landing before losing altitude
They ignored the cockpit warning system entirely
They shut down the only working engine, leaving the plane powerless

evt-02-04-2015-songshan-airport.butterflyEffect: The pilots mistakenly shut down the still-functioning engine instead of the failing one, leaving the ATR 72 with no power. It clipped an elevated freeway and a taxi before crashing into the Keelung River; 43 of 58 aboard died. The disaster led to overhauled ATR 72 crew training worldwide on correctly identifying engine failures.

evt-02-04-2015-transasia-airways-flight-.scenario: It's 4 February 2015. You are the co-pilot of an ATR 72 climbing out of Taipei's Songshan Airport when the right engine's power readout drops sharply just seconds after takeoff.
evt-02-04-2015-transasia-airways-flight-.prompt: With one engine faltering, what is the correct emergency action?

choices.text: Ignore the warning and continue the climb on both engines
Shut down the engine that is actually losing power and feather its propeller
Shut down the healthy engine to conserve fuel on the good one
Immediately attempt a full restart of both engines simultaneously

evt-02-04-2015-transasia-airways-flight-.butterflyEffect: The captain mistakenly shut down the still-functioning left engine instead of the failing right one, leaving the aircraft with no power at all. It clipped a highway overpass and plunged into the Keelung River, killing 43 of the 58 aboard, and the crash's exposure of crew training failures contributed to TransAsia Airways collapsing entirely by 2016.

evt-02-04-2020-covid-19-pandemic.scenario: It's early February 2020. You oversee gaming operations in Macau as reports of a new coronavirus spreading from mainland China grow more alarming by the day, and casino floors remain packed with visitors.
evt-02-04-2020-covid-19-pandemic.prompt: What decisive step do Macau's authorities take on 4 February 2020?

choices.text: Evacuate foreign tourists while keeping gaming floors running
Close every casino in the territory for 15 days
Keep casinos open but require temperature checks at the door
Close casinos for just 48 hours before reopening

evt-02-04-2020-covid-19-pandemic.butterflyEffect: Macau ordered every casino shut for a full 15 days, an unprecedented halt to the world's largest gambling hub. The closure foreshadowed the global economic shutdowns to come and devastated Macau's casino-dependent economy for years, as the territory recorded historic revenue collapses through 2020 and beyond.

evt-02-04-2025-orebro-school-shooting.scenario: It is February 4, 2025, at Campus Risbergska in Örebro, an adult education center where students of many ages and backgrounds study together. A gunman who once attended classes here has returned.
evt-02-04-2025-orebro-school-shooting.prompt: What did investigators conclude motivated the attacker?

choices.text: A political grievance against the Swedish government
Primarily his own suicidal intentions
A workplace dispute with school staff
Involvement with an organized extremist group

evt-02-04-2025-orebro-school-shooting.butterflyEffect: Swedish police concluded the attacker, a former student at the center, was primarily driven by suicidal despair rather than any political or ideological cause. The attack became the deadliest mass shooting in Swedish history, prompting national debate over gun laws and support for people in crisis.

evt-02-05-1597-toyotomi-hideyoshi.scenario: It is early 1597 in Kyoto. Following the seizure of the Spanish ship San Felipe, Toyotomi Hideyoshi has ordered the arrest of missionaries and Japanese converts as part of his crackdown on Christianity, and the prisoners are being marched south.
evt-02-05-1597-toyotomi-hideyoshi.prompt: What happens to the arrested Christians when they reach Nagasaki?

choices.text: They are pardoned after paying heavy fines
They are executed by crucifixion at Nishizaka Hill
They are forced into Buddhist monastic life
They are deported to Portuguese Macau

evt-02-05-1597-toyotomi-hideyoshi.butterflyEffect: On 5 February 1597, the twenty-six prisoners were crucified on Nishizaka Hill in Nagasaki, becoming known as the Twenty-Six Martyrs. Canonized as saints in 1862, their deaths became a defining memory for Japan's underground 'Hidden Christians,' who preserved their faith in secret for over two centuries until religious tolerance returned in the 1800s.

evt-02-05-1818-charles-xiv-john.scenario: It is 5 February 1818, and you are Charles XIV John, the former French Marshal Bernadotte, ascending the thrones of Sweden and Norway after the death of Charles XIII. Sweden has been battered by decades of war with Russia and France, and you must set the kingdom's course.
evt-02-05-1818-charles-xiv-john.prompt: What foreign policy do you establish as the founding principle of your reign?

choices.text: A formal military alliance with Russia against Denmark
Renewed war to reclaim Finland from Russia
Strict neutrality, avoiding alliances and foreign wars
Active participation in restoring Napoleon's allies to power

evt-02-05-1818-charles-xiv-john.butterflyEffect: Charles XIV John committed Sweden-Norway to a policy of neutrality and non-alignment, avoiding foreign entanglements after centuries of costly wars. This choice became the foundation of Sweden's long tradition of neutrality, a stance the country largely maintained for the next two centuries.

evt-02-05-1869-moliagul.scenario: You are prospector John Deason, digging near a tree root outside Moliagul, Victoria in February 1869, when your shovel strikes something unexpectedly heavy just below the surface.
evt-02-05-1869-moliagul.prompt: What do you and your partner Richard Oates do with the find?

choices.text: Bury it again and keep its location secret forever
Break it apart themselves and sell the pieces privately
Donate it immediately to the Victorian colonial government
Take it into town to be weighed and sold, breaking it up when no scale is large enough

evt-02-05-1869-moliagul.butterflyEffect: Deason and Oates had unearthed the Welcome Stranger, the largest alluvial gold nugget ever found, weighing over 70 kilograms. It was too large for any scale in town and had to be broken into pieces to be weighed, and its sale made the pair wealthy and cemented Moliagul's place in goldfields lore.

evt-02-05-1909-leo-baekeland.scenario: You are Leo Baekeland, addressing the New York section of the American Chemical Society on 5 February 1909. Chemists in the room are used to celluloid and shellac, and you must convince them your new synthetic resin is something genuinely different.
evt-02-05-1909-leo-baekeland.prompt: What do you claim as Bakelite's decisive advantage over existing materials?

choices.text: It is cheaper to produce than paper
It is derived purely from natural tree resins, making it biodegradable
It can be dissolved and reused indefinitely like celluloid
It is entirely synthetic, and once molded it sets permanently and will not soften or burn easily

evt-02-05-1909-leo-baekeland.butterflyEffect: Baekeland announced Bakelite as the first fully synthetic plastic, moldable when heated but permanently hard once set, and an excellent electrical insulator. It launched the modern plastics industry, soon appearing in telephones, radios, and countless manufactured goods that had previously relied on wood, metal, or natural resins.

evt-02-05-1917-united-states-congress.scenario: It is early February 1917, and you are a member of the House of Representatives voting on whether to override President Wilson's veto of the Immigration Act, which imposes a literacy test and bars immigration from most of Asia.
evt-02-05-1917-united-states-congress.prompt: What does Congress do with Wilson's veto?

choices.text: Sustains the veto, killing the bill
Delays the vote indefinitely amid war preparations
Sends the bill back to committee for revision
Overrides the veto, enacting the law over Wilson's objection

evt-02-05-1917-united-states-congress.butterflyEffect: Congress overrode the veto by a wide margin, enacting the literacy test and the Asiatic Barred Zone into law. The act marked a major escalation in restrictive immigration policy, foreshadowing the even tighter national quota laws of the 1920s.

evt-02-05-1923-cricket.scenario: You are Bill Ponsford, batting for Victoria against Tasmania at the MCG. You have already passed 400 runs and the world first-class record of 424, held by England's A.C. MacLaren since 1895, is now within reach.
evt-02-05-1923-cricket.prompt: As captain, do you keep Ponsford batting to chase the record or declare the innings?

choices.text: Declare early to leave more time to bowl Tasmania out
Keep Ponsford batting until he is out, chasing the record
Send in a new batsman to protect Ponsford from injury
Ask Ponsford to retire voluntarily once past 400

evt-02-05-1923-cricket.butterflyEffect: Victoria kept batting and Ponsford was eventually dismissed for 429, breaking MacLaren's 27-year-old world record for the highest individual first-class score. Ponsford would break his own record again in 1927 with 437, part of a chain of record-breaking innings that led to Bradman's 452 and, decades later, Lara's 501.

evt-02-05-1958-1958-tybee-island-mid-air.scenario: It is the night of 5 February 1958, and your B-47 bomber has just collided with an F-86 fighter during a practice exercise off the coast of Georgia. Your aircraft is damaged and carrying a live Mark 15 nuclear bomb, and you must make an emergency landing.
evt-02-05-1958-1958-tybee-island-mid-air.prompt: What do you do with the bomb before attempting to land the crippled aircraft?

choices.text: Attempt to arm and detonate it safely over open water
Jettison it into the ocean before attempting to land
Order the crew to bail out and let the aircraft crash with the bomb aboard
Land with the bomb still secured in the bay

evt-02-05-1958-1958-tybee-island-mid-air.butterflyEffect: The crew jettisoned the bomb into the shallow waters off Tybee Island to avoid detonation risk during landing. Despite extensive Air Force searches at the time and periodic renewed interest since, the weapon was never recovered and remains lost somewhere in Wassaw Sound, a lingering Cold War mystery and environmental question.

evt-02-05-1985-carthage-municipality.scenario: It is 5 February 1985, and you are the mayor of Rome, meeting your counterpart from Carthage for a ceremonial gesture more than two thousand years after the Punic Wars ended in the city's destruction.
evt-02-05-1985-carthage-municipality.prompt: What symbolic act do the two mayors perform to close the ancient rivalry?

choices.text: Sign a symbolic treaty of peace and friendship between the two cities
Formally merge the two municipalities into one
Issue a joint currency commemorating the reconciliation
Exchange territorial claims over the ancient battle sites

evt-02-05-1985-carthage-municipality.butterflyEffect: The mayors of Rome and Carthage signed a symbolic peace treaty formally ending the Punic Wars, which had concluded in reality with Carthage's destruction in 146 BC. The gesture was largely ceremonial but drew global attention to Mediterranean reconciliation and helped cement cultural and sister-city ties between modern Rome and Tunis.

evt-02-05-1994-markale-massacres.scenario: It is 5 February 1994. A mortar shell has just torn through the crowded Markale marketplace in besieged Sarajevo, killing dozens. As international investigators and NATO commanders review the disputed evidence of who fired it, pressure mounts for a response.
evt-02-05-1994-markale-massacres.prompt: What does NATO do in response to the marketplace bombardment?

choices.text: NATO immediately launches full-scale airstrikes on Sarajevo
NATO issues an ultimatum demanding heavy weapons be withdrawn from around the city
The UN orders a complete evacuation of Sarajevo's population
NATO withdraws all peacekeepers from Bosnia in protest

evt-02-05-1994-markale-massacres.butterflyEffect: NATO issued an ultimatum demanding Bosnian Serb forces withdraw heavy weapons from around Sarajevo, its first major coercive move in the war. This set a precedent that, after the second Markale massacre in 1995, escalated into full NATO airstrikes on Bosnian Serb positions, helping force the negotiations that produced the Dayton Peace Accords.

evt-02-05-2004-common-cockle.scenario: It is dusk on Morecambe Bay, and dozens of migrant workers are wading far out across the sands gathering cockles as the light fades. The tide here is famous for turning fast and cutting off the flats without warning.
evt-02-05-2004-common-cockle.prompt: What should the cockle-pickers have relied on to avoid being cut off by the tide?

choices.text: A local guide with detailed knowledge of the tide tables and safe routes
Mobile phone signal strength to judge distance from shore
Instructions shouted from workers already back on the shore
The position of the sun to estimate remaining daylight

evt-02-05-2004-common-cockle.butterflyEffect: At least 21 cockle-pickers, mostly undocumented Chinese migrants working for an unlicensed gangmaster, drowned when the tide swept in faster than they could reach shore. The disaster exposed the exploitation of migrant labour in Britain and led directly to the Gangmasters (Licensing) Act 2004, creating regulation for labour providers in agriculture and fishing.

evt-02-05-2008-2008-super-tuesday-tornad.scenario: It is the afternoon of 5 February 2008, Super Tuesday. You manage a polling station in the rural South as radar shows a dangerous supercell bearing down while voters are still lining up to cast primary ballots.
evt-02-05-2008-2008-super-tuesday-tornad.prompt: What should officials do as tornado warnings intensify during voting?

choices.text: Move the voting line outdoors away from the building
Close the polling station early and move voters to shelter
Keep the polls open regardless of the warnings
Cancel the primary in that county entirely

evt-02-05-2008-2008-super-tuesday-tornad.butterflyEffect: Several polling places across the South closed early or moved voters to shelter as the outbreak's 87 tornadoes tore through the region during the primaries, ultimately killing 57 people. It remains one of the deadliest tornado outbreaks to strike on a U.S. election day, prompting later reviews of emergency procedures for voting during severe weather.

evt-02-05-2009-united-states-navy.scenario: It is the night of 5 February 2009, and you are on the bridge of the guided-missile cruiser Port Royal off Honolulu. The ship's navigation system has just lost power and rebooted, and the plotted position no longer matches what your lookouts are reporting.
evt-02-05-2009-united-states-navy.prompt: What should the bridge team do before trusting the reset navigation system's position?

choices.text: Independently verify the ship's position using radar fixes, soundings, and visual landmarks
Immediately increase speed to clear the area faster
Radio headquarters and continue on the plotted course while awaiting a reply
Wait for a full system reboot before making any course corrections

evt-02-05-2009-united-states-navy.butterflyEffect: The Port Royal ran hard aground on a coral reef near Honolulu's reef runway after crew relied on the faulty reset navigation data instead of independently verifying position. The grounding caused extensive damage to both the ship and the reef, cost tens of millions to repair, and led the Navy to fund coral restoration and review its navigation procedures.

evt-02-05-2016-steven-joyce.scenario: It is Waitangi Day, 5 February 2016, at the treaty grounds. As Economic Development Minister Steven Joyce steps forward amid protests over the Trans-Pacific Partnership trade deal, a pink object suddenly sails through the air toward him.
evt-02-05-2016-steven-joyce.prompt: What has just been thrown at Minister Steven Joyce?

choices.text: A rubber dildo, thrown in protest of the TPPA
A tomato, thrown by a farming protester
A flag, thrown by a Māori sovereignty activist
A shoe, thrown in protest of tax policy

evt-02-05-2016-steven-joyce.butterflyEffect: Activist Josie Butler had thrown a pink rubber dildo at Joyce in protest of the TPPA, striking him as cameras rolled. Footage of the moment went viral worldwide, turning it into an unlikely international symbol of anti-TPP protest and a lasting piece of New Zealand political pop culture.

evt-02-05-2016-bangladesh-bank-robbery.scenario: It is early February 2016, and you work at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, processing a flood of SWIFT transfer instructions from Bangladesh Bank's account, several of them for suspiciously large sums to private accounts in the Philippines.
evt-02-05-2016-bangladesh-bank-robbery.prompt: What tips you off to stop most of the fraudulent transfers?

choices.text: A misspelling in one of the transfer instructions
A phone call from Bangladesh Bank warning of fraud
A tip from Philippine banking regulators
An automatic fraud algorithm flagging the accounts

evt-02-05-2016-bangladesh-bank-robbery.butterflyEffect: A misspelled instruction referencing the Shalika Foundation as 'fandation' raised red flags, prompting the Fed to block thirty of thirty-five transfer requests worth $850 million. Still, hackers had already siphoned $101 million through the SWIFT network, exposing severe vulnerabilities in global interbank messaging security.

evt-02-05-2020-pegasus-airlines-flight-2.scenario: It is 5 February 2020, and heavy snow and poor visibility blanket Istanbul's Sabiha Gökçen Airport as your Boeing 737 comes in to land after the short hop from İzmir.
evt-02-05-2020-pegasus-airlines-flight-2.prompt: What happened as the aircraft touched down in these conditions?

choices.text: It overshot the runway and broke apart on an embankment
It landed safely despite the poor visibility
It overran the runway, split apart, and slid down an embankment killing three people
It aborted the landing and diverted to another airport

evt-02-05-2020-pegasus-airlines-flight-2.butterflyEffect: The aircraft overran the runway, broke apart, and slid down an embankment, killing three passengers and injuring 179 more. The disaster, the airline's first fatal accident, followed a similar runway excursion at the same airport weeks earlier and intensified scrutiny of landing procedures in adverse weather.

evt-02-06-1778-treaty-of-amity-and-comme.scenario: You are Benjamin Franklin in Paris, February 1778. After the American victory at Saratoga convinced the French court that the rebellion might succeed, you sit down with French ministers to finalize agreements that will bind France to the American cause.
evt-02-06-1778-treaty-of-amity-and-comme.prompt: What did Franklin and the French ministers formally agree to alongside the commercial treaty?

choices.text: An agreement for France to mediate peace talks with Britain
A treaty of alliance committing France to support American independence
A pact requiring the United States to declare war on Spain
A promise of French territory in North America to the United States

evt-02-06-1778-treaty-of-amity-and-comme.butterflyEffect: France signed both the Treaty of Amity and Commerce and a Treaty of Alliance, openly committing to support American independence against Britain. French money, troops, and especially its navy proved decisive at Yorktown in 1781, and France's overt involvement soon widened the war into a global conflict against Britain.

evt-02-06-1788-massachusetts.scenario: You are a delegate at the Massachusetts ratifying convention, where support for the new Constitution is stalled because many fear it lacks protections for individual liberties.
evt-02-06-1788-massachusetts.prompt: What compromise do Federalist leaders offer to win over wavering delegates?

choices.text: Ratify only if Massachusetts is allowed to secede later
Postpone the vote until all thirteen states agree on wording
Ratify now while recommending amendments for later consideration
Reject the Constitution until a bill of rights is added first

evt-02-06-1788-massachusetts.butterflyEffect: Massachusetts ratified while recommending a list of amendments to be added afterward rather than demanding changes first. This ratify-then-amend approach became the template other closely divided states followed, and it led directly to the Bill of Rights being adopted in 1791.

evt-02-06-1806-napoleonic-wars.scenario: It is 6 February 1806, and you command a British ship of the line off Santo Domingo. A French squadron under Admiral Leissègues lies ahead, some ships still unprepared for battle.
evt-02-06-1806-napoleonic-wars.prompt: Do you close in and attack the French warships despite their heavier guns?

choices.text: Blockade the port and wait for the French to run out of supplies
Attack immediately, using surprise before the French can form a battle line
Offer terms of surrender before engaging
Withdraw and wait for reinforcements from the main fleet

evt-02-06-1806-napoleonic-wars.butterflyEffect: Admiral Duckworth's squadron pressed the attack, capturing or destroying five French ships of the line at the Battle of San Domingo. The victory eliminated one of France's last battle-worthy squadrons after Trafalgar, cementing British naval dominance for the rest of the war.

evt-02-06-1819-stamford-raffles.scenario: It is 6 February 1819 and you stand on the muddy bank of the Singapore River with Stamford Raffles, negotiating with Sultan Hussein Shah of Johor over a swampy fishing village at the tip of the Malay Peninsula.
evt-02-06-1819-stamford-raffles.prompt: What does Raffles offer the Sultan to secure rights to a British trading post here?

choices.text: An exclusive monopoly on the spice trade
Territory in British India in exchange
Recognition as Sultan and annual payments to him and the Temenggong
A military alliance to invade Dutch Java

evt-02-06-1819-stamford-raffles.butterflyEffect: Raffles recognized Hussein as the rightful Sultan of Johor over a Dutch-backed rival and promised annual payments to him and the local Temenggong in exchange for founding a settlement. That post grew into the free port of Singapore, which became one of the world's great trading cities and a cornerstone of British power in Southeast Asia.

evt-02-06-1820-american-colonization-soc.scenario: It is February 1820 and you board the ship Elizabeth in New York harbor with dozens of free Black settlers, bound for the Grain Coast of West Africa to found a colony under the American Colonization Society.
evt-02-06-1820-american-colonization-soc.prompt: What actually follows once the ship reaches the West African coast?

choices.text: They found Monrovia immediately upon arrival
They merge into the existing British colony of Sierra Leone
They abandon the voyage and sail back to New York
They land at Sherbro Island, suffer heavy losses to disease, then later found Monrovia

evt-02-06-1820-american-colonization-soc.butterflyEffect: The settlers first landed on disease-ridden Sherbro Island, where many died of fever before survivors relocated in 1822 to Cape Mesurado. That settlement became Monrovia, the seed of the colony that declared independence as Liberia in 1847.

evt-02-06-1862-union-american-civil-war.scenario: It is February 6, 1862, on the Tennessee River. You serve under General Ulysses S. Grant as Union gunboats commanded by Andrew Foote bombard a Confederate fort guarding the river approach into the heart of Tennessee.
evt-02-06-1862-union-american-civil-war.prompt: Which Confederate stronghold fell to this combined Union army-navy assault?

choices.text: Fort Pillow
Fort Donelson
Fort Sumter
Fort Henry

evt-02-06-1862-union-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Fort Henry surrendered after a brief bombardment, opening the Tennessee River to Union gunboats and forcing the Confederates to abandon nearby Fort Donelson soon after. The twin victories gave Grant his first major fame of the war and cracked open the Confederate defensive line across Kentucky and Tennessee.

evt-02-06-1919-world-war-i.scenario: It is February 1919 and you are a shipyard worker in Seattle, walking off the job alongside tens of thousands of others after wartime wage controls end and employers refuse raises.
evt-02-06-1919-world-war-i.prompt: What does the strike committee do to keep public sympathy during the shutdown?

choices.text: Organize strikers to keep essential services like food delivery running
Shut down all public services to force quick surrender
Ally openly with the Communist Party for support
Call on federal troops to seize the city's factories

evt-02-06-1919-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The committee organized union crews to keep milk, bread, and hospital services running so the city would not turn against the strikers. Even so, Mayor Ole Hanson denounced it as a Bolshevik plot, the strike collapsed after five days without wage gains, and the episode fed the nationwide Red Scare of 1919–1920.

evt-02-06-1922-washington-naval-treaty.scenario: You are a naval delegate at the Washington Conference, negotiating how to cap the world's most powerful navies without triggering a costly new arms race.
evt-02-06-1922-washington-naval-treaty.prompt: What tonnage ratio for capital ships do the US, Britain, and Japan agree to?

choices.text: 10:10:5 with no cap on Japan's cruisers
5:5:3 for the US, Britain, and Japan
3:3:1 favoring smaller, faster fleets
5:5:5 equal tonnage for all three powers

evt-02-06-1922-washington-naval-treaty.butterflyEffect: The treaty set a 5:5:3 ratio for the US, Britain, and Japan, with lower allowances for France and Italy. Japanese naval officers resented being ranked below the Western powers, and that grievance fed the nationalist push that led Japan to abandon the treaty's limits in the 1930s.

evt-02-06-1951-woodbridge-train-derailme.scenario: It is the evening of February 6, 1951. You are aboard a Pennsylvania Railroad commuter train approaching Woodbridge, New Jersey, where trains have been rerouted onto a temporary wooden trestle while a new overpass is built.
evt-02-06-1951-woodbridge-train-derailme.prompt: What factor investigators later identified as central to the disaster that followed?

choices.text: A signal failure let two trains occupy the same track
The train was traveling well above the speed limit posted for the temporary trestle
A bridge support had been sabotaged
Ice on the rails caused the wheels to lose traction

evt-02-06-1951-woodbridge-train-derailme.butterflyEffect: The train derailed on the temporary trestle, killing 85 people in what remains New Jersey's deadliest train wreck and the deadliest U.S. rail disaster in peacetime. Investigators found the train had been traveling far above the posted speed limit for the temporary track, prompting tighter federal scrutiny of speed enforcement on railroads.

evt-02-06-1976-lockheed-corporation.scenario: You are a Senate investigator in early 1976. Lockheed's president, Carl Kotchian, has just admitted under questioning that the company funneled millions of dollars to foreign officials to secure aircraft sales.
evt-02-06-1976-lockheed-corporation.prompt: What did Kotchian admit Lockheed had done to win contracts overseas?

choices.text: Paid bribes to foreign government officials to secure aircraft sales
Overcharged the Pentagon for defense contracts
Sold restricted military technology to a hostile government
Falsified safety tests on its commercial airliners

evt-02-06-1976-lockheed-corporation.butterflyEffect: The admission exposed bribery of officials in Japan, Italy, and elsewhere, toppling political careers and embarrassing Lockheed. The scandal directly spurred the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act of 1977, the first law criminalizing bribery of foreign officials by American companies.

evt-02-06-1987-mary-gaudron.scenario: It is February 1987 and Prime Minister Bob Hawke's government announces its choice for the newest justice of the High Court of Australia, a position unbroken by one demographic since Federation.
evt-02-06-1987-mary-gaudron.prompt: What barrier does this appointment break for the High Court?

choices.text: She is the first solicitor appointed without prior judicial experience
She is the first woman appointed to the High Court of Australia
