She is the youngest justice ever appointed
She is the first justice from New South Wales

evt-02-06-1987-mary-gaudron.butterflyEffect: Mary Gaudron became the first woman appointed to the High Court of Australia, serving until 2003 and shaping rulings on native title and industrial law. Her appointment opened the path for later female justices, culminating in Susan Kiefel becoming the Court's first female Chief Justice in 2017.

evt-02-06-1998-ronald-reagan-washington-.scenario: It is February 1998 and Congress, pushed by Senator Jesse Helms, quickly passes legislation renaming Washington National Airport after former President Ronald Reagan.
evt-02-06-1998-ronald-reagan-washington-.prompt: What logistical problem does the sudden renaming create for the region's transit system?

choices.text: The airport must physically relocate across the Potomac
WMATA must undertake a costly, years-long process to rename the Metro station
All airlines must repaint their aircraft immediately
International air treaties require renegotiation

evt-02-06-1998-ronald-reagan-washington-.butterflyEffect: The Washington Metro's "National Airport" station could not simply be relabeled overnight; cost and bureaucratic wrangling delayed its official renaming to "Reagan National Airport" until 2001. The episode became an early example of the increasingly partisan practice of attaching presidential names to federal infrastructure.

evt-02-06-2000-second-chechen-war.scenario: It is early February 2000, and Russian federal forces have surrounded Grozny after weeks of siege. Chechen separatist fighters still hold pockets of the ruined city while the rebel government prepares to flee toward the mountains.
evt-02-06-2000-second-chechen-war.prompt: What followed the Russian capture of Grozny?

choices.text: Russia withdrew its troops within weeks of the capture
The Chechen government accepted a peace treaty and disbanded its forces
The Chechen separatist government went into exile, and the insurgency shifted to guerrilla warfare
The United Nations imposed a no-fly zone over Chechnya

evt-02-06-2000-second-chechen-war.butterflyEffect: With Grozny in ruins and the separatist government pushed into exile, the war shifted from conventional battles to a prolonged insurgency that lasted until 2009. Russia installed a pro-Moscow administration in Chechnya, laying the groundwork for the Kadyrov government that rules the republic today.

evt-02-06-2006-stephen-harper.scenario: It is February 2006 in Ottawa. After years of Liberal dominance and a bruising sponsorship-scandal, your minority Conservative government is about to be sworn in, with Stephen Harper as the new prime minister.
evt-02-06-2006-stephen-harper.prompt: What allowed Harper's Conservatives to defeat the long-governing Liberals in this election?

choices.text: A constitutional crisis forcing an emergency change of government
A sudden Liberal endorsement of Quebec separatism
Public anger over the Liberal sponsorship scandal and corruption allegations
Canada's entry into a new war that discredited the Liberal government

evt-02-06-2006-stephen-harper.butterflyEffect: Harper led a minority government from 2006 to 2015, later winning a majority in 2011. His nearly decade-long tenure reshaped Canadian conservatism, and he remains the only PM produced by the merged modern Conservative Party.

evt-02-06-2016-2016-southern-taiwan-eart.scenario: You are a structural engineer picking through the rubble of the collapsed Weiguan Jinlong complex in Yongkang, hours after the quake has flattened it while other buildings nearby still stand.
evt-02-06-2016-2016-southern-taiwan-eart.prompt: What do investigators find inside the collapsed building's pillars that explains why it failed?

choices.text: Empty tin cans used as filler instead of solid concrete
Steel reinforcement bars corroded by decades of seawater exposure
Termite-damaged wooden support beams
Cracks from a previous, undocumented earthquake

evt-02-06-2016-2016-southern-taiwan-eart.butterflyEffect: Empty tin cans and other debris were found packed into the concrete of the building's support columns, exposing shoddy, corner-cutting construction. The developer was later convicted of manslaughter, and the scandal pushed Taiwan to tighten enforcement of earthquake-resistant building codes.

evt-02-06-2018-spacex.scenario: It is February 6, 2018, at Kennedy Space Center. You watch as SpaceX's newest rocket, the Falcon Heavy, lifts off for the first time, carrying an unusual payload strapped into the nose cone.
evt-02-06-2018-spacex.prompt: What unconventional payload did SpaceX launch aboard the Falcon Heavy's debut flight?

choices.text: A time capsule of messages from SpaceX employees
A block of cheese as a tribute to an earlier rocket test
An empty mockup satellite for weight testing only
A Tesla Roadster with a mannequin dubbed 'Starman' in the driver's seat

evt-02-06-2018-spacex.butterflyEffect: The rocket carried Elon Musk's own Tesla Roadster with a mannequin nicknamed 'Starman' at the wheel, sent toward an orbit near Mars. The launch demonstrated the Falcon Heavy's capability as the most powerful operational rocket at the time, with two of its three boosters landing successfully back on Earth.

evt-02-06-2021-antony-blinken.scenario: It is February 2021 and newly sworn-in Secretary of State Antony Blinken reviews the Trump-era "safe third country" agreements that required asylum seekers to first seek protection in Guatemala.
evt-02-06-2021-antony-blinken.prompt: What does Blinken decide to do with these agreements?

choices.text: Leave the agreements fully in force
Expand the agreements to include Mexico
Transfer their enforcement entirely to Guatemala's government
Suspend the agreements as part of dismantling Trump-era asylum policy

evt-02-06-2021-antony-blinken.butterflyEffect: Blinken suspended the asylum cooperative agreements with Guatemala as part of the Biden administration's broader effort to reverse Trump-era immigration restrictions. The move aimed to restore access to the U.S. asylum system for Central American migrants, though rising migration through the region remained a persistent political challenge for Biden.

evt-02-06-2023-2023-turkey-syria-earthqu.scenario: You coordinate an aid convoy trying to reach earthquake-shattered towns in rebel-held northern Syria, where the ground has stopped shaking but the roads into the region remain a bottleneck.
evt-02-06-2023-2023-turkey-syria-earthqu.prompt: What is the biggest obstacle keeping international aid from reaching devastated areas in northern Syria?

choices.text: A lack of any international awareness of the disaster
A total absence of any damage on the Syrian side of the border
The ongoing civil war restricting which border crossings could be used
Syrian authorities refusing all foreign aid outright

evt-02-06-2023-2023-turkey-syria-earthqu.butterflyEffect: Syria's ongoing civil war meant only one UN-approved crossing, Bab al-Hawa, was initially open to move aid into the opposition-held northwest. International pressure soon forced Damascus to authorize additional crossings, and the disaster briefly drew regional governments back into contact with the Assad government.

evt-02-07-1497-dominican-order.scenario: It is Shrove Tuesday 1497 in Florence. Bands of boys and friars loyal to the preacher Girolamo Savonarola move door to door, urging citizens to surrender mirrors, cosmetics, playing cards, and paintings deemed sinful vanities.
evt-02-07-1497-dominican-order.prompt: What happens to the objects collected in Florence's main square?

choices.text: They are sold to fund Savonarola's church reforms
They are returned to their owners after a blessing
They are publicly burned in a great bonfire in the piazza
They are shipped to Rome for the Pope to judge

evt-02-07-1497-dominican-order.butterflyEffect: The confiscated goods were piled high in the Piazza della Signoria and set ablaze in the famous Bonfire of the Vanities. The spectacle deepened Florence's religious fervor but also hardened opposition to Savonarola, who was excommunicated within a year and executed in 1498 as political and papal patience ran out.

evt-02-07-1783-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: You are a clerk in the British Foreign Office in early February 1783. Word arrives that King George III is finally ready to act on the loss at Yorktown two years earlier.
evt-02-07-1783-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What official step does the Crown take to end the fighting in America?

choices.text: George III declares an official end to hostilities in America
The king dissolves Parliament over the war's cost
Parliament votes to send fresh reinforcements to New York
Britain annexes the Thirteen Colonies as crown territories

evt-02-07-1783-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Britain formally declared a cessation of hostilities, ending active fighting after three years and seven months of war. The Treaty of Paris that September made the peace permanent, recognizing the United States as an independent nation and reshaping the balance of power in North America and the Atlantic world.

evt-02-07-1795-eleventh-amendment-to-the.scenario: It is 1794. The Supreme Court's ruling in Chisholm v. Georgia has just allowed a citizen of one state to sue another state in federal court, and state legislatures are furious, fearing a flood of debt suits against them. You sit in Congress as this backlash builds.
evt-02-07-1795-eleventh-amendment-to-the.prompt: How does Congress respond to the outcry over Chisholm v. Georgia?

choices.text: Leave the ruling in place and let states pay their debts
Impeach the Supreme Court justices who decided the case
Expand the Supreme Court's jurisdiction to hear more such cases
Draft and pass a constitutional amendment restricting suits against states

evt-02-07-1795-eleventh-amendment-to-the.butterflyEffect: Congress passed the Eleventh Amendment, barring federal courts from hearing suits against a state by citizens of another state or country, and it was ratified in February 1795. It became the foundation of modern state sovereign immunity doctrine, still cited by courts to shield states from certain lawsuits over two centuries later.

evt-02-07-1813-napoleonic-wars.scenario: It is 7 February 1813 off the West African coast. You command HMS Amelia, and lookouts have spotted the French frigate Aréthuse, a ship of nearly matching size and firepower, closing to intercept you.
evt-02-07-1813-napoleonic-wars.prompt: As captain of Amelia, what do you do when the evenly matched French frigate approaches?

choices.text: Close and engage the Aréthuse in a ship-to-ship duel
Retreat to the nearest friendly port to avoid battle
Signal for reinforcements before making contact
Turn away and outrun the French frigate under full sail

evt-02-07-1813-napoleonic-wars.butterflyEffect: The two frigates fought a brutal close-range duel that left both ships shattered and suffering heavy casualties before Aréthuse broke off and limped home to Brest. The action became remembered as one of the bloodiest single-ship duels of the Napoleonic Wars, a grim testament to how costly even 'ordinary' frigate actions could be.

evt-02-07-1865-seattle.scenario: It is early February 1865, and you sit on Seattle's board of trustees as settlers debate the future of the young town's Native American residents living within its limits.
evt-02-07-1865-seattle.prompt: What did the trustees decide regarding Native Americans living in Seattle?

choices.text: They passed an ordinance expelling Native Americans from residing within the town
They required Native Americans to pay a residency tax but allowed them to stay
They granted Native Americans formal citizenship in the town
They set aside a reservation within the town limits for Native residents

evt-02-07-1865-seattle.butterflyEffect: The 1865 ordinance forced Native Americans, including many who had lived on the land long before Seattle's founding, out of the growing town. It set a precedent for decades of segregation and displacement that shaped the demographic and social geography of the Pacific Northwest's largest city.

evt-02-07-1900-bubonic-plague.scenario: You are a San Francisco health official in early 1900, called to a Chinatown lodging house where a Chinese immigrant lies dead, his lymph nodes grotesquely swollen and blackened.
evt-02-07-1900-bubonic-plague.prompt: How did city and business leaders respond once plague was suspected?

choices.text: They diagnosed it as tuberculosis and closed the matter for good
They evacuated the entire city as a precaution
They immediately alerted the federal government and the press
They quarantined Chinatown and publicly minimized the case to protect trade

evt-02-07-1900-bubonic-plague.butterflyEffect: Fearing damage to trade and the city's reputation, officials downplayed and denied the outbreak for years while imposing quarantines that targeted Chinese residents specifically. The bacteria nevertheless spread into local ground squirrel populations, permanently establishing plague in the wildlife of the American West, where isolated human cases still occur today.

evt-02-07-1900-second-boer-war.scenario: You are a British soldier under General Buller, crossing the Tugela River at Vaal Krantz on 7 February 1900, in the third attempt this month to break through Boer lines and reach the besieged garrison at Ladysmith.
evt-02-07-1900-second-boer-war.prompt: What happened after this third relief attempt at Vaal Krantz failed?

choices.text: The Boers negotiated a truce and lifted the siege voluntarily
Buller withdrew, later broke through elsewhere and relieved Ladysmith later that month
Buller abandoned the campaign entirely and returned to Cape Town
The garrison surrendered to the Boers before relief could arrive

evt-02-07-1900-second-boer-war.butterflyEffect: Buller withdrew from Vaal Krantz, his third failure to relieve Ladysmith after Colenso and Spion Kop. Weeks later he shifted tactics, broke through at the Battle of the Tugela Heights, and relieved Ladysmith on 28 February 1900, a turning point that restored British morale after the disasters of "Black Week."

evt-02-07-1914-kid-auto-races-at-venice.scenario: You are in a Los Angeles nickelodeon in early 1914, watching a cheap Keystone comedy about a children's soap-box derby. A shabby vagabond in an ill-fitting suit keeps wandering into the newsreel cameraman's shot, mugging for attention.
evt-02-07-1914-kid-auto-races-at-venice.prompt: Why does this unassuming short matter to film history?

choices.text: It marked the first public appearance of Chaplin's "Little Tramp" character
It was the first film shot with synchronized sound
It introduced pie-throwing slapstick to American cinema
It was the first American film shot entirely outdoors

evt-02-07-1914-kid-auto-races-at-venice.butterflyEffect: Though shot after Mabel's Strange Predicament, this film reached theaters first, making it the public debut of Chaplin's "Little Tramp." The character became the most recognizable figure in silent cinema, and its universal appeal helped make Chaplin the world's first global movie superstar.

evt-02-07-1940-walt-disney.scenario: You are a Disney studio executive in February 1940, watching the wide release of Pinocchio after its lavish and expensive production. War has just broken out in Europe, closing off a major market for the studio's films.
evt-02-07-1940-walt-disney.prompt: How does Pinocchio fare in its initial release and awards recognition?

choices.text: It receives only an honorary Academy Award, like Snow White before it
It is pulled from theaters after poor reviews and re-cut
It is an immediate box-office smash and sweeps every major Oscar category
It underperforms at the box office but wins competitive Oscars for its music

evt-02-07-1940-walt-disney.butterflyEffect: Wartime disruption to European distribution left Pinocchio a box-office disappointment on its first run, but it soon became the first animated feature to win competitive Academy Awards, taking honors for its score and for the song 'When You Wish Upon a Star.' Its reputation as a technical and artistic landmark grew steadily over the following decades.

evt-02-07-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: You are a US Navy patrol officer near Guadalcanal in early February 1943. For nights running, Japanese destroyers have been slipping in and out of the island under cover of darkness, and command wants an assessment of what they are doing.
evt-02-07-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What are the Japanese destroyers actually accomplishing on these night runs?

choices.text: Secretly evacuating Japanese troops from the island
Laying mines to blockade the harbor
Landing fresh reinforcements to hold the island
Shelling American positions before a final assault

evt-02-07-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The ships were carrying out Operation Ke, secretly evacuating over ten thousand starving Japanese troops before Allied forces realized the island was being abandoned rather than reinforced. It marked Japan's first major land campaign defeat of the Pacific War and a turning point that shifted momentum toward the Allies.

evt-02-07-1948-neil-harvey.scenario: It's February 1948 at the MCG. You are 19-year-old Neil Harvey, playing only your second Test match, facing a determined Indian bowling attack with Australia looking to press home their advantage.
evt-02-07-1948-neil-harvey.prompt: What did Harvey do to become the youngest Australian to score a Test century?

choices.text: He retired hurt just before reaching fifty
He batted cautiously all day to secure a draw
He attacked the bowling to race to a fluent 153
He was run out attempting a risky quick single

evt-02-07-1948-neil-harvey.butterflyEffect: Harvey attacked fluently to score 153, the fastest century by an Australian to that point and enough to make him the youngest Australian Test centurion. The innings announced him as a prodigy; he went on to play 79 Tests and became one of Australia's finest post-war batsmen.

evt-02-07-1984-space-shuttle-challenger.scenario: You are astronaut Bruce McCandless, floating freely outside Space Shuttle Challenger during mission STS-41-B, connected to nothing but a jet-propelled backpack, farther from the safety of the spacecraft than anyone before you.
evt-02-07-1984-space-shuttle-challenger.prompt: What historic first are you achieving on this spacewalk?

choices.text: The first docking of a shuttle with a space station
The first untethered spacewalk using a jet-propelled backpack
The first in-orbit repair of a damaged satellite
The first spacewalk performed by a woman

evt-02-07-1984-space-shuttle-challenger.butterflyEffect: McCandless's flight with the Manned Maneuvering Unit proved astronauts could operate freely and untethered in space. The mission also made the first shuttle landing at Kennedy Space Center, and the maneuvering technique later enabled satellite retrieval and repair missions.

evt-02-07-1986-jean-claude-duvalier.scenario: It is early February 1986 in Port-au-Prince. Weeks of riots and strikes against President Jean-Claude Duvalier have paralyzed Haiti, and even the army's loyalty is wavering.
evt-02-07-1986-jean-claude-duvalier.prompt: What does Duvalier do as the uprising against him peaks?

choices.text: He declares martial law and deploys the army against protesters
He resigns and hands power to an elected assembly
He negotiates a power-sharing deal with opposition leaders
He flees into exile aboard a US Air Force plane

evt-02-07-1986-jean-claude-duvalier.butterflyEffect: Duvalier boarded a US Air Force plane and fled into exile in France, ending 28 years of Duvalier family rule. His departure opened a turbulent period of military councils and contested elections in Haiti, and he would not return to the country until 2011.

evt-02-07-1991-the-troubles.scenario: You are a cabinet minister inside 10 Downing Street on 7 February 1991, meeting with Prime Minister John Major about the ongoing Gulf War, when a violent explosion suddenly rocks the garden just outside the window.
evt-02-07-1991-the-troubles.prompt: What had just struck near the Prime Minister's residence?

choices.text: An accidental military training explosion
Mortar shells fired by the IRA from a nearby parked van
A car bomb planted directly outside the building
A gas explosion in a neighboring building

evt-02-07-1991-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The mortar shells, fired from a parked van by the Provisional IRA, landed in the Downing Street garden but caused no serious injuries. The attack proved the IRA could strike at the heart of British government even amid the Gulf War, prompting a dramatic tightening of security around Whitehall.

evt-02-07-1992-maastricht-treaty.scenario: It is 7 February 1992, and you are a diplomat at Maastricht as the twelve members of the European Communities prepare to sign a treaty promising a shared currency, common foreign policy, and a new European citizenship.
evt-02-07-1992-maastricht-treaty.prompt: What was the direct long-term result of signing the Maastricht Treaty?

choices.text: The creation of a unified European army under a single command
The eventual introduction of the euro as a shared European currency
The abolition of border controls within days of signing
The immediate dissolution of all national parliaments in Europe

evt-02-07-1992-maastricht-treaty.butterflyEffect: The treaty's provisions for a single currency led directly to the launch of the euro in 1999, with notes and coins following in 2002, while its creation of European citizenship reshaped the continent's politics. The document also ignited lasting debates over national sovereignty that echo in disputes to this day, including Brexit.

evt-02-07-1994-michael-jordan.scenario: You are a sports reporter in February 1994, still stunned that basketball's dominant star walked away from the game months after his father's murder, and now hears he has signed a new contract entirely.
evt-02-07-1994-michael-jordan.prompt: What deal did Michael Jordan sign that day?

choices.text: A minor league baseball contract with the Chicago White Sox organization
A broadcasting contract with a major television network
A new multi-year deal to return to the Chicago Bulls
A contract to play professional basketball in Europe

evt-02-07-1994-michael-jordan.butterflyEffect: Jordan spent the 1994 season playing for the Double-A Birmingham Barons, batting a modest .202 in his unlikely baseball detour. He returned to the NBA in March 1995 and led the Bulls to three more championships, cementing his legacy as the game's greatest player.

evt-02-07-1995-ramzi-yousef.scenario: Islamabad, February 1995. You know the man renting a room in a nearby guesthouse is Ramzi Yousef, mastermind of the 1993 World Trade Center bombing, and you're aware Washington is offering a multi-million-dollar reward for information leading to his capture.
evt-02-07-1995-ramzi-yousef.prompt: What do you do with what you know about your guesthouse neighbor?

choices.text: Report him to authorities for the reward and capture operation
Warn him that his location may be known
Confront him yourself before contacting anyone
Say nothing and avoid any involvement

evt-02-07-1995-ramzi-yousef.butterflyEffect: An informant tipped off American and Pakistani authorities, who raided the guesthouse and captured Yousef without a shot fired. He was extradited to the United States, convicted for the WTC bombing and the Bojinka airline plot, and his case became an early model for international cooperation in counterterrorism investigations.

evt-02-07-1997-steve-jobs.scenario: You are an Apple engineer in early 1997, watching the fallout from the company's costly acquisition of NeXT. The man who co-founded Apple two decades ago and was pushed out in 1985 is suddenly back in the building.
evt-02-07-1997-steve-jobs.prompt: In what capacity does Steve Jobs return to Apple at this point?

choices.text: As chairman of Apple's board of directors
As head of a new hardware division only
As the newly appointed permanent chief executive
As an unpaid advisor consulting on strategy and products

evt-02-07-1997-steve-jobs.butterflyEffect: Jobs came back as an informal advisor to CEO Gil Amelio, not yet in charge. Within months Amelio was ousted, Jobs became interim CEO, and his subsequent overhaul of Apple's product line led to the iMac, iPod, and iPhone, transforming the company into one of the most valuable in the world.

evt-02-07-2014-report-of-the-commission-.scenario: It is 2013 and the newly formed UN Commission of Inquiry is gathering testimony on North Korea. You are a defector who witnessed conditions in a political prison camp, and investigators ask you to describe what you saw for the official record.
evt-02-07-2014-report-of-the-commission-.prompt: What should you do when asked to testify about what you witnessed?

choices.text: Testify in detail to help build the official record of abuses
Refuse to speak out of fear for family still in North Korea
Insist the investigation be abandoned entirely
Offer only a vague, unverifiable account

evt-02-07-2014-report-of-the-commission-.butterflyEffect: Testimony from defectors like this fed directly into the Commission's 2014 report, which documented systematic, wide-ranging violations and drew comparisons to crimes of the 20th century's worst regimes. The report pushed North Korea's human rights record onto the UN Security Council's agenda for the first time, though geopolitical vetoes have since blocked further formal action.

evt-02-07-2014-happisburgh-footprints.scenario: May 2013: a storm has stripped sand from a Norfolk beach at Happisburgh, exposing a strange rippled surface in ancient silt. You realise these are footprints left by early humans nearly a million years ago—and the incoming tide will erase them within hours.
evt-02-07-2014-happisburgh-footprints.prompt: What should your team do before the tide destroys the footprints forever?

choices.text: Try to cut the sediment block free and remove it whole
Wait for official permits before touching the site
Cover the prints with tarpaulin to shield them from the tide
Rapidly photograph and scan the surface in 3D before it is lost

evt-02-07-2014-happisburgh-footprints.butterflyEffect: The team rapidly recorded the surface with 3D photogrammetry before the sea washed it away days later. Analysis of the scans confirmed the prints were 850,000–950,000 years old, the oldest hominin footprints known outside Africa, proving early humans reached northern Europe far earlier than previously thought.

evt-02-08-421-honorius.scenario: It is February 421, and you serve at Emperor Honorius's court in Ravenna. The general Constantius has married Honorius's sister Galla Placidia and pressed hard for greater power within the crumbling Western Empire.
evt-02-08-421-honorius.prompt: What does Honorius do about Constantius's ambitions?

choices.text: Have Constantius executed for treason
Exile Constantius from Italy
Ignore Constantius's demands entirely
Elevate Constantius as co-emperor

evt-02-08-421-honorius.butterflyEffect: Honorius elevated Constantius as co-emperor, but Constantius died just months later, and the Eastern court in Constantinople never recognized him. The resulting succession chaos deepened instability in the Western Empire, feeding the power struggles that accelerated its collapse over the following decades.

evt-02-08-1250-seventh-crusade.scenario: It is April 1250, and you are a knight in King Louis IX's crusading army, trapped near Fariskur in the Nile Delta after the disastrous retreat from Mansura. Ayyubid forces surround what remains of the crusade, and plague and starvation have gutted your ranks.
evt-02-08-1250-seventh-crusade.prompt: What does the crusader army do?

choices.text: Fight to the last man rather than surrender
Escape by ship down the Nile to the coast
Break out and march overland to Jerusalem
Surrender to the Egyptians, hoping for ransom

evt-02-08-1250-seventh-crusade.butterflyEffect: Louis IX and most of his army surrendered and were taken captive. He was later ransomed for an enormous sum and the surrender of Damietta, and the failure ended serious crusading efforts against Egypt, hastening the Ayyubids' fall to the rising Mamluk dynasty within a decade.

evt-02-08-1587-mary-queen-of-scots.scenario: It is 8 February 1587 at Fotheringhay Castle. You are an English official who has just watched Mary, Queen of Scots kneel to the executioner, condemned after Elizabeth I's spymasters intercepted her secret correspondence.
evt-02-08-1587-mary-queen-of-scots.prompt: What evidence finally convinced Elizabeth's council to order Mary's execution?

choices.text: Testimony from the Duke of Norfolk about a planned invasion
Letters proving her approval of the Babington Plot to assassinate Elizabeth
Confessions extracted from her during the Ridolfi plot investigation
The so-called Casket Letters implicating her in her husband's murder

evt-02-08-1587-mary-queen-of-scots.butterflyEffect: Mary was convicted after intercepted letters in the Babington Plot showed she had approved a plan to assassinate Elizabeth I and seize the throne. Her death removed the last major Catholic claimant to the English crown, but it also cleared the way for her Protestant son, James VI of Scotland, to inherit England's throne in 1603, uniting the two kingdoms under one monarch.

evt-02-08-1837-richard-mentor-johnson.scenario: It is February 1837, and you are a U.S. senator facing an unprecedented situation: no vice-presidential candidate won a majority of electoral votes in 1836, so under the Twelfth Amendment the choice now falls to your chamber alone.
evt-02-08-1837-richard-mentor-johnson.prompt: Who does the Senate elect as vice president?

choices.text: John Tyler
William Rufus King
Richard Mentor Johnson
Francis Granger

evt-02-08-1837-richard-mentor-johnson.butterflyEffect: The Senate elected Richard Mentor Johnson, the only VP ever chosen this way. His controversial common-law marriage to a formerly enslaved woman had cost him support, and Van Buren later dropped him from the 1840 ticket, a sign of how personal scandal could unravel a national political career.

evt-02-08-1910-william-d-boyce.scenario: You are Chicago publisher William D. Boyce, lost in a thick London fog in 1909, when an unnamed boy in uniform guides you to your destination and then refuses any payment, saying he is simply doing his daily good turn as a Scout.
evt-02-08-1910-william-d-boyce.prompt: What did Boyce do after returning to the United States, inspired by this encounter?

choices.text: He founded the YMCA's youth division
He launched the American branch of the Boys' Brigade
He established the 4-H Club
He founded the Boy Scouts of America

evt-02-08-1910-william-d-boyce.butterflyEffect: Boyce incorporated the Boy Scouts of America on 8 February 1910, adapting Robert Baden-Powell's British scouting model for American youth. The organization grew into one of the largest youth movements in the country, while the boy who guided Boyce, later called the "Unknown Scout," was never identified.

evt-02-08-1924-gee-jon.scenario: It's February 1924 at Nevada State Prison. Nevada's new law mandates execution by lethal gas, but no government anywhere has ever actually built a gas chamber, and you must decide how to deliver the fatal dose to Gee Jon's cell.
evt-02-08-1924-gee-jon.prompt: What method do officials attempt first to administer the lethal gas?

choices.text: Release the gas into the prison yard during his exercise hour
Pump liquid cyanide gas directly into his sealed cell while he sleeps
Build a separate airtight chamber first and move him into it
Force a gas-filled mask over his face

evt-02-08-1924-gee-jon.butterflyEffect: The first attempt failed: officials tried to pump liquid cyanide gas directly into Gee Jon's cell while he slept, but the cell was not airtight and the gas leaked away. They then rushed to build a sealed chamber on site, which succeeded and became the prototype for the gas chambers later used by several U.S. states for decades.

evt-02-08-1968-orangeburg-south-carolina.scenario: It is the night of February 8, 1968, and you are a South Carolina Highway Patrol officer facing student protesters from South Carolina State University, who have gathered near campus over a segregated bowling alley. Tension is high, and someone hurls an object toward the officers' line.
evt-02-08-1968-orangeburg-south-carolina.prompt: What follows in the next moments outside the campus?

choices.text: Negotiators arrive and defuse the standoff
Officers withdraw without incident
Students are dispersed with tear gas only
Officers open fire on the crowd

evt-02-08-1968-orangeburg-south-carolina.butterflyEffect: Officers opened fire on the unarmed crowd, killing three young Black men and wounding around 27 others in what became known as the Orangeburg Massacre. Despite the deaths, the incident drew far less national attention than later campus shootings, but it remained a defining, painful marker in the civil rights struggle across the South.

evt-02-08-1971-army-of-the-republic-of-v.scenario: It is early February 1971, and you are an ARVN officer preparing to cross into Laos without American ground troops, ordered to sever the Ho Chi Minh Trail as North Vietnamese forces mass to meet you.
evt-02-08-1971-army-of-the-republic-of-v.prompt: How does the incursion into Laos ultimately unfold?

choices.text: ARVN cuts the trail and holds the ground
US ground troops join to reinforce the advance
ARVN suffers heavy losses and retreats in disarray
North Vietnam withdraws from the trail without resistance

evt-02-08-1971-army-of-the-republic-of-v.butterflyEffect: Operation Lam Son 719 collapsed into a costly rout, with ARVN units suffering heavy losses and some soldiers clinging to helicopter skids to escape. The debacle exposed the fragility of "Vietnamization" and deepened doubts, in Washington and Saigon alike, that South Vietnam could hold without direct American ground support.

evt-02-08-1974-skylab-4.scenario: It is January 1974, more than two months into an 84-day mission aboard Skylab. You are one of three exhausted astronauts whose schedule has been packed with back-to-back experiments by mission control on the ground.
evt-02-08-1974-skylab-4.prompt: What did the overworked Skylab 4 crew actually do in response?

choices.text: They took an unscheduled day off and reset their own pace of work
They demanded additional pay before continuing experiments
They radioed a formal resignation threat to Houston
They requested an emergency early return to Earth

evt-02-08-1974-skylab-4.butterflyEffect: The crew effectively staged a quiet one-day work stoppage, ignoring the timetable to rest and photograph Earth, before resuming duties on their own terms. NASA took the episode seriously, redesigning astronaut schedules on later Skylab operations and the Space Shuttle program to build in realistic workloads and rest time.

evt-02-08-1986-via-rail.scenario: It is 8 February 1986 near Hinton, Alberta. You are a rail safety investigator arriving at the wreckage of a VIA Rail passenger train that has collided head-on with a Canadian National freight train, killing 23 people.
evt-02-08-1986-via-rail.prompt: What did the investigation identify as the key failure behind the collision?

choices.text: Heavy snow obscured the signals from both crews
The freight crew failed to obey signals warning of the occupied track
A dispatcher error routed both trains onto the same schedule
A broken rail caused sudden derailment into the opposing track

evt-02-08-1986-via-rail.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the freight train's crew failed to stop at signals indicating an occupied track ahead, a lapse tied to crew fatigue and inadequate health screening. The disaster prompted Canadian regulators to tighten rules on crew alertness, medical fitness testing for engineers, and signal-compliance enforcement across the national rail network.

evt-02-08-1989-independent-air-flight-18.scenario: You are the flight crew of a Boeing 707 charter, descending through cloud toward Santa Maria Airport in the Azores on a non-precision instrument approach, with Pico Alto mountain hidden somewhere ahead in the murk.
evt-02-08-1989-independent-air-flight-18.prompt: What should the crew have done to avoid disaster on this approach?

choices.text: Descend early to break out of cloud sooner and proceed visually
Request a faster descent rate to save fuel on the approach
Trust a single distance reading without cross-checking their position
Maintain the published minimum safe altitude until confirming the correct approach fix

evt-02-08-1989-independent-air-flight-18.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew began descending before reaching the correct approach fix, flying into Pico Alto in low visibility. The crash, the deadliest in Portuguese aviation history, reinforced scrutiny of non-precision approaches and controlled-flight-into-terrain risks at mountainous airports worldwide.

evt-02-08-2013-february-2013-north-ameri.scenario: You are the governor of a New England state on 8 February 2013, watching forecasts predict two feet of snow and hurricane-force winds bearing down as Winter Storm Nemo approaches.
evt-02-08-2013-february-2013-north-ameri.prompt: What action did several governors take to protect residents before the storm hit?

choices.text: Declared states of emergency and banned non-emergency travel on roads
Closed only the region's airports and left roads open
Relied solely on the National Guard without any travel restrictions
Ordered mandatory evacuation of all coastal cities

evt-02-08-2013-february-2013-north-ameri.butterflyEffect: Governors in Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New York declared states of emergency and banned non-emergency travel on public roads. The bans were widely credited with keeping the death toll lower than feared, even as the storm killed at least 18 and left hundreds of thousands without power.

evt-02-08-2020-nakhon-ratchasima-shootin.scenario: It's the night of 8 February 2020 in Nakhon Ratchasima, Thailand. An army sergeant has already killed people at his military camp and is now holed up inside a crowded shopping centre, and you are among the security commanders deciding how to end the standoff.
evt-02-08-2020-nakhon-ratchasima-shootin.prompt: How do security forces ultimately end the gunman's rampage?

choices.text: He escapes through a service tunnel and is never found
He surrenders peacefully after negotiators talk him down
Police capture him alive and take him into custody
Security forces storm the mall and shoot him dead

evt-02-08-2020-nakhon-ratchasima-shootin.butterflyEffect: After an hours-long siege at the shopping centre, Thai security forces stormed the building and shot the gunman dead, ending a rampage that had begun at his army base and become the deadliest mass shooting in Thai history. The attack forced public scrutiny of grievances within the military's internal hierarchy and prompted debate over soldiers' access to weapons.

evt-02-09-1234-jin-dynasty-1115-1234.scenario: You are Emperor Aizong, trapped in the last Jin stronghold of Caizhou as combined Mongol and Song forces close in after months of siege. Food is gone, the walls are breached, and you must decide how the dynasty's story ends.
evt-02-09-1234-jin-dynasty-1115-1234.prompt: What does Aizong do as Caizhou falls to the Mongol-Song alliance?

choices.text: He leads a final cavalry charge and is captured alive
He surrenders personally to the Mongol commander
He abdicates to a relative and then takes his own life
He flees south to seek refuge with the Song

evt-02-09-1234-jin-dynasty-1115-1234.butterflyEffect: Aizong abdicated in favor of a relative, Wanyan Chenglin, then hanged himself rather than be captured; Chenglin was killed in street fighting hours later, ending the Jin dynasty after over a century of rule. The former Mongol-Song alliance immediately turned hostile, setting the stage for the Mongols' decades-long conquest of the Song dynasty itself.

evt-02-09-1799-quasi-war.scenario: It is 9 February 1799, and you command the American frigate USS Constellation off the island of Nevis in the Caribbean. A French frigate, L'Insurgente, comes into view, and your undeclared war with France gives you no formal orders to avoid a fight.
evt-02-09-1799-quasi-war.prompt: What do you do when L'Insurgente is sighted?

choices.text: Signal for a truce to negotiate on the spot
Avoid combat and report the sighting to Congress first
Engage and attempt to capture the French frigate
Retreat to protect American merchant convoys instead

evt-02-09-1799-quasi-war.butterflyEffect: Captain Thomas Truxtun closed and captured L'Insurgente in a hard-fought single-ship action, the US Navy's first major victory of the Quasi-War. The win boosted American naval prestige and confidence, encouraging further aggressive patrols that helped push France toward the 1800 Convention of Mortefontaine ending the conflict.

evt-02-09-1825-united-states-electoral-c.scenario: It's February 1825, and you sit in the House of Representatives choosing among John Quincy Adams, Andrew Jackson, and William Crawford after none secured an electoral majority. Henry Clay, eliminated from contention, has thrown his influence behind one candidate.
evt-02-09-1825-united-states-electoral-c.prompt: Which candidate does the House elect as president?

choices.text: William Crawford
John Quincy Adams
Andrew Jackson
Henry Clay himself

evt-02-09-1825-united-states-electoral-c.butterflyEffect: The House elected John Quincy Adams, who soon named Henry Clay his Secretary of State. Jackson's furious supporters branded it a "corrupt bargain," fueling the populist campaign that swept Jackson into the presidency in 1828 and reshaped American party politics.

evt-02-09-1855-devil-s-footprints.scenario: You wake in a Devon village after a night of heavy snow to find a single line of strange, cloven hoof-like prints running for miles, over walls, haystacks, and even rooftops, with no gaps or branching trail.
evt-02-09-1855-devil-s-footprints.prompt: As a worried villager, what is the most sensible next step?

choices.text: Note the pattern carefully and alert local naturalists or the press to investigate rationally
Follow the tracks alone at night to confront whatever made them
Assume it is proof of the Devil walking the earth and warn the parish priest immediately
Ignore it entirely as an ordinary animal trail not worth mentioning

evt-02-09-1855-devil-s-footprints.butterflyEffect: No definitive explanation was ever confirmed; theories ranged from an escaped kangaroo or donkey to owls, rope-makers' tools, or a hoax, while some insisted it was supernatural. The mystery was never solved and remains one of Victorian England's most enduring unexplained phenomena, still debated by researchers today.

evt-02-09-1861-jefferson-davis.scenario: You are a delegate at the Montgomery convention in Alabama, where seceded Southern states have gathered to form a new government. The delegates must choose who will lead the fledgling Confederacy before any war has even begun.
evt-02-09-1861-jefferson-davis.prompt: How did the convention select Jefferson Davis as provisional president?

choices.text: He seized power through a militia-backed coup
He was appointed by South Carolina's governor
He was elected unanimously by the convention delegates
He won a direct popular vote across the seceded states

evt-02-09-1861-jefferson-davis.butterflyEffect: Davis was chosen by unanimous vote of the convention delegates, not by popular election, and was inaugurated on February 18, 1861. His selection shaped Confederate strategy and diplomacy for the entire war, and he was later formally elected under the permanent Confederate constitution that November.

evt-02-09-1913-meteor-procession.scenario: On the night of 9 February 1913, you stand outside in Ontario watching a slow, silent chain of glowing fireballs cross the sky in near-perfect formation, moving from the northwest toward the Atlantic.
evt-02-09-1913-meteor-procession.prompt: As an observer, what should you do to help scientists later understand the event?

choices.text: Photograph only the brightest fragment and ignore the rest
Wait for official government confirmation before telling anyone
Assume it is an aircraft formation and disregard it
Record the exact time, direction, and duration, then report it to a newspaper or observatory

evt-02-09-1913-meteor-procession.butterflyEffect: Astronomer Clarence Chant gathered hundreds of eyewitness reports from Canada to Brazil and reconstructed the fragments' path, concluding they had likely orbited Earth briefly as a temporary natural satellite before burning up. The 1913 Great Meteor Procession remains one of the best-documented cases of this rare phenomenon.

evt-02-09-1920-svalbard-treaty.scenario: You are a delegate in Paris in 1920, finalizing a treaty that will hand sovereignty over the remote Arctic archipelago of Spitsbergen to Norway, but other nations insist on safeguards before signing.
evt-02-09-1920-svalbard-treaty.prompt: What unusual condition did the treaty impose alongside recognizing Norwegian sovereignty?

choices.text: Norway must cede half the archipelago to Russia within a decade
The League of Nations will administer the islands jointly with Norway
Norway is required to fully demilitarize and depopulate the archipelago
Signatory nations retain equal commercial and mining rights on the islands

evt-02-09-1920-svalbard-treaty.butterflyEffect: The treaty granted all signatory nations equal rights to mining and commercial activity on the islands and barred Norway from militarizing them. This unusual arrangement let the Soviet Union, and later Russia, maintain a permanent mining settlement on what is legally Norwegian territory, a source of friction that persists into the present day.

evt-02-09-1923-stanley-bruce.scenario: It is February 1923, and you lead the Nationalist Party after Prime Minister Billy Hughes has lost the confidence needed to govern alone. Country Party leader Earle Page refuses to serve under Hughes but signals he could work with you instead.
evt-02-09-1923-stanley-bruce.prompt: What do you do to secure a majority and the prime ministership?

choices.text: Offer the Country Party cabinet seats in a coalition government
Call an immediate new election to seek a majority
Try to govern alone as a minority government
Step aside and let Hughes continue as leader

evt-02-09-1923-stanley-bruce.butterflyEffect: Bruce formed a coalition with the Country Party, offering it cabinet posts including the treasury for Page, and became prime minister leading Australia's first coalition government. This Nationalist-Country arrangement became the template for the Liberal-National Coalition that still shapes Australian politics today.

evt-02-09-1942-imperial-japanese-army.scenario: You command Australian troops dug in along the Kranji shoreline on the night of 8-9 February 1942, watching Japanese assault boats cross the Johor Strait under cover of darkness and artillery fire.
evt-02-09-1942-imperial-japanese-army.prompt: With your defensive line under heavy pressure and gaps opening, what should you do?

choices.text: Abandon the beach immediately and retreat without engaging
Hold ground as long as possible while requesting reinforcements from the rear
Negotiate a local ceasefire with the advancing Japanese units
Launch an unsupported counter-landing across the strait at night

evt-02-09-1942-imperial-japanese-army.butterflyEffect: Despite fierce resistance, Japanese forces broke through the Kranji defenses and pushed rapidly toward Singapore city. Within a week the island fell, one of the British Empire's most devastating defeats, shattering colonial prestige across Southeast Asia and accelerating the end of European empire in the region.

evt-02-09-1964-beatlemania.scenario: It's February 9, 1964. You are a CBS producer backstage at The Ed Sullivan Show, about to send a little-known British band out in front of American television audiences for the first time.
evt-02-09-1964-beatlemania.prompt: What happens when the Beatles take the stage?

choices.text: Network censors pull the broadcast over the band's appearance
A record-breaking audience watches, igniting the British Invasion in America
The audience response is muted and the segment is cut short
Ratings are respectable but the band is dismissed as a novelty act

evt-02-09-1964-beatlemania.butterflyEffect: An estimated 73 million Americans watched, one of the largest audiences in television history at the time, and Beatlemania exploded across the United States overnight. The performance opened the door for the British Invasion, transforming American popular music for the rest of the decade.

evt-02-09-1971-1971-san-fernando-earthqu.scenario: It's the morning of February 9, 1971. You are a civil engineer sent to inspect the Van Norman Dam after a violent earthquake has cracked its earthen embankment, with a densely populated valley lying directly below it.
evt-02-09-1971-1971-san-fernando-earthqu.prompt: What is the responsible course of action given the dam's condition?

choices.text: Recommend reinforcing the dam overnight without evacuating anyone
Close only the streets directly beside the dam and reopen by morning
Declare the dam safe since it survived the initial shaking
Recommend immediate evacuation of everyone downstream of the dam

evt-02-09-1971-1971-san-fernando-earthqu.butterflyEffect: Officials ordered the evacuation of roughly 80,000 residents below the dam as engineers found it dangerously close to failure. The near-disaster led to California draining the reservoir permanently and passing the Alquist Hospital Seismic Safety Act, transforming how the state built dams and hospitals near fault lines.

evt-02-09-1975-soyuz-17.scenario: It is early February 1975, and you help direct the Soyuz 17 mission from Moscow. Cosmonauts Gubarev and Grechko have already spent longer aboard Salyut 4 than any Soviet crew before them, surpassing the ill-fated Soyuz 11 record.
evt-02-09-1975-soyuz-17.prompt: What does mission control decide about ending the flight?

choices.text: Abort the mission early over health concerns
Bring the crew home on schedule after 29 days
Send a second crew up to relieve them mid-flight
Extend the mission indefinitely to set an unbreakable record

evt-02-09-1975-soyuz-17.butterflyEffect: Ground controllers brought the crew home after 29 days as planned rather than pushing further. The record stood only months, as Soyuz 18's crew later logged 63 days aboard the same station, part of the steady Soviet push toward the multi-month stays needed for future space stations.

evt-02-09-1976-australian-defence-force.scenario: You are a defence planner in Canberra in 1976, tasked with ending decades of rivalry between the separately run Navy, Army, and Air Force departments by merging them into one unified command.
evt-02-09-1976-australian-defence-force.prompt: What structural change created the single Australian Defence Force?

choices.text: Merger of Australian forces directly into British Commonwealth command
Unification under one Chief of Defence Force Staff and department
Creation of separate joint chiefs while keeping independent departments
Introduction of compulsory national service across all services

evt-02-09-1976-australian-defence-force.butterflyEffect: The three services were unified under a single Chief of Defence Force Staff and one Department of Defence, replacing separate service departments. This centralization aimed to improve joint planning and efficiency, and it laid the groundwork for later reforms that created a fully integrated ADF headquarters for joint operations.

evt-02-09-1996-gsi-helmholtz-centre-for-.scenario: You are part of Sigurd Hofmann's team at the GSI accelerator in Darmstadt, firing a beam of zinc ions at a lead target for weeks, watching for the faint signature of a single new atom that decays in a fraction of a second.
evt-02-09-1996-gsi-helmholtz-centre-for-.prompt: What breakthrough does your detector finally confirm on this day?

choices.text: The discovery of a stable isotope of element 92
The creation of a new superheavy element, later named copernicium
The first artificial fusion of hydrogen isotopes
The successful splitting of a uranium nucleus for the first time

evt-02-09-1996-gsi-helmholtz-centre-for-.butterflyEffect: The team had created a single atom of element 112, later officially named copernicium after Nicolaus Copernicus. The discovery extended the periodic table into the superheavy elements and cemented GSI's heavy-ion fusion technique as the leading method for creating new elements in the decades that followed.

evt-02-09-1996-provisional-irish-republi.scenario: It's the evening of February 9, 1996. A massive explosion has just torn through London's Docklands, ending the IRA's seventeen-month ceasefire and killing two people. You advise the British government on how to respond to Sinn Féin the following morning.
evt-02-09-1996-provisional-irish-republi.prompt: What does the government do in response to the bombing?

choices.text: Exclude Sinn Féin from peace talks until a new ceasefire is declared
Launch British military operations across the Irish border
Immediately resume talks with Sinn Féin as though nothing happened
Arrest every known Sinn Féin political representative

evt-02-09-1996-provisional-irish-republi.butterflyEffect: The government excluded Sinn Féin from all-party talks until a new ceasefire was declared. The IRA campaign continued for another year until a fresh ceasefire in July 1997, clearing the way for Sinn Féin's return to negotiations and the Good Friday Agreement the following year.

evt-02-09-2001-uss-greeneville.scenario: You are the commanding officer of the nuclear submarine USS Greeneville off Pearl Harbor, with sixteen civilian guests aboard for a demonstration. You order the boat to perform a dramatic surfacing maneuver to impress them, without confirming the surface is clear.
evt-02-09-2001-uss-greeneville.prompt: What maneuver caused Greeneville to slam into the Japanese trawler Ehime Maru?

choices.text: A routine sonar calibration dive
A high-speed submerged transit at flank speed
A slow ascent to periscope depth for a torpedo drill
An emergency main ballast tank blow to surface rapidly

evt-02-09-2001-uss-greeneville.butterflyEffect: An emergency main ballast tank blow sent Greeneville rocketing upward directly beneath the Ehime Maru, sinking it and killing nine aboard, including four teenage students. Commander Scott Waddle was relieved of command and faced a court of inquiry rather than court-martial, and the incident forced new Navy rules restricting civilian VIP distractions during submarine drills.

evt-02-09-2016-bad-aibling-rail-accident.scenario: You are a dispatcher on the single-track Meridian line near Bad Aibling, responsible for making sure only one train occupies the section at a time. Two commuter trains are approaching each other on the same stretch of track.
evt-02-09-2016-bad-aibling-rail-accident.prompt: What error let both trains onto the same single track, causing the collision?

choices.text: Heavy fog made the warning lights invisible
The dispatcher, distracted by a phone game, misrouted the trains
A signal box mechanical failure went undetected
One driver deliberately ignored a red signal

evt-02-09-2016-bad-aibling-rail-accident.butterflyEffect: The dispatcher, distracted by a mobile phone game, gave a late and improperly overriding signal that put both trains on the same track; twelve people died. The dispatcher was convicted of negligent manslaughter, and German rail authorities accelerated rollout of automatic train protection systems on single-track regional lines.

evt-02-09-2020-nayib-bukele.scenario: It is 9 February 2020, and you are a Salvadoran lawmaker inside the Legislative Assembly. Armed soldiers loyal to President Bukele have entered the chamber and taken up positions, while Bukele himself sits down in the president's chair and bows his head in prayer before addressing you all.
evt-02-09-2020-nayib-bukele.prompt: What does Bukele do next after occupying the chamber with troops?

choices.text: Formally dissolve the Legislative Assembly on the spot
Give an ultimatum, then withdraw the troops without forcing a vote
Order the arrest of opposition lawmakers in the chamber
Force an immediate vote on the loan at gunpoint

evt-02-09-2020-nayib-bukele.butterflyEffect: Bukele gave lawmakers a 24-hour ultimatum to approve his security loan, then withdrew the troops without forcing an immediate vote after fierce domestic and international criticism of the show of force. The episode was an early sign of his willingness to sideline institutions, foreshadowing his 2021 removal of Supreme Court judges and the attorney general.

evt-02-09-2021-second-impeachment-trial-.scenario: It's February 9, 2021, opening day of Donald Trump's second impeachment trial. Before any evidence is heard, you must cast the Senate's first vote: whether the chamber even has jurisdiction to try a president who has already left office.
evt-02-09-2021-second-impeachment-trial-.prompt: How does the Senate vote on the constitutional question of jurisdiction?

choices.text: Refer the constitutional question to the Supreme Court
Vote that the trial is constitutional and proceed
Postpone the vote until Trump's team responds
Vote that the trial is unconstitutional and dismiss it

evt-02-09-2021-second-impeachment-trial-.butterflyEffect: The Senate voted 56–44 that the trial was constitutional, allowing proceedings to continue. Trump was ultimately acquitted on February 13 when the vote fell short of the two-thirds needed to convict, but the precedent that former officials can be tried left the door open for future impeachments of ex-presidents.

evt-02-10-1258-abbasid-caliphate.scenario: It's February 1258 in Baghdad. You are Caliph Al-Musta'sim, trapped inside the besieged city as Hulegu Khan's Mongol army breaches its defenses and famine spreads within the walls.
evt-02-10-1258-abbasid-caliphate.prompt: What do you decide to do about the city's fate?

choices.text: Surrender the city to Hulegu Khan
Continue resisting behind the city walls
Flee the city secretly by night
Seek an emergency alliance with the Mamluks

evt-02-10-1258-abbasid-caliphate.butterflyEffect: The caliph surrendered, but Hulegu's forces sacked Baghdad anyway, destroying its libraries and irrigation works and executing Al-Musta'sim. The fall ended five centuries of Abbasid rule in Baghdad and dealt a devastating blow to the Islamic world's intellectual and administrative center.

evt-02-10-1355-university-of-oxford.scenario: It is 10 February 1355, St Scholastica's Day, and you are a student drinking at the Swindlestock Tavern in Oxford. A quarrel over the quality of the wine has just turned ugly between your fellow students and the tavern keeper.
evt-02-10-1355-university-of-oxford.prompt: What does this tavern quarrel escalate into over the following days?

choices.text: Town officials intervene at once and the matter is quietly settled
It fizzles out once the tavern keeper is paid for the wine
The king orders the university dissolved to punish the students
It grows into a deadly three-day riot that ends with the Crown boosting the university's power over the town

evt-02-10-1355-university-of-oxford.butterflyEffect: The dispute exploded into a three-day town-versus-gown riot in which armed townspeople and countryfolk attacked scholars, leaving a significant number of students and townspeople dead. The Crown sided with the university afterward, granting it sweeping new privileges over the town, and Oxford's mayor and burgesses were made to perform an annual penance on the anniversary for centuries.

evt-02-10-1763-seven-years-war.scenario: It is February 1763 in Paris. You are a French diplomat finalizing peace terms after years of costly war, and Britain's negotiators are demanding territorial concessions to end the fighting.
evt-02-10-1763-seven-years-war.prompt: Which vast territory must France cede to Britain to secure the peace?

choices.text: Florida
Its Caribbean sugar islands
Louisiana west of the Mississippi
New France (Canada)

evt-02-10-1763-seven-years-war.butterflyEffect: France ceded New France (Canada) and its lands east of the Mississippi to Britain, having already secretly handed Louisiana west of the river to Spain. The loss ended France's mainland North American empire, cemented British dominance there, and left France with crushing debts that later fueled its support for American independence.

evt-02-10-1814-war-of-the-sixth-coalitio.scenario: You serve under General Olsufiev's isolated Russian corps near Champaubert on 10 February 1814, unaware that Napoleon has swung his main army directly toward your exposed position.
evt-02-10-1814-war-of-the-sixth-coalitio.prompt: What did Napoleon achieve by striking this isolated corps?

choices.text: He captures Marshal Blücher's headquarters
He retreats toward Paris without engaging
He negotiates a truce with the coalition
He destroys and captures the isolated Russian corps

evt-02-10-1814-war-of-the-sixth-coalitio.butterflyEffect: Napoleon's forces overwhelmed and largely destroyed Olsufiev's corps, capturing the general himself, in the opening blow of his celebrated Six Days' Campaign. The victory briefly revived French morale, but it could not reverse the strategic tide, and Napoleon abdicated just weeks later in April 1814.

evt-02-10-1840-prince-albert-of-saxe-cob.scenario: It is 10 February 1840 at the Chapel Royal, St James's Palace. Queen Victoria has just married her cousin Prince Albert, and courtiers are already whispering about what status Parliament will allow her new husband to hold.
evt-02-10-1840-prince-albert-of-saxe-cob.prompt: What does Parliament refuse to grant Albert despite his marriage to the queen?

choices.text: A private residence for the royal couple
The title of King Consort and formal precedence at court
British naturalization as a subject of the crown
An annual allowance from the royal purse

evt-02-10-1840-prince-albert-of-saxe-cob.butterflyEffect: Parliament denied Albert the title of King Consort and withheld formal precedence, leaving his role undefined for years. Victoria worked around this by issuing letters patent giving him precedence next to her, and finally secured him the title Prince Consort in 1857, cementing his influence over the crown.

evt-02-10-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: It's 10 February 1862 on the Pasquotank River, North Carolina. You command a Union gunboat bearing down on Confederate Flag Officer William Lynch's small, outgunned 'Mosquito Fleet' defending Elizabeth City.
evt-02-10-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: What is the outcome of this lopsided naval clash?

choices.text: Both fleets withdraw without engaging
The Confederates capture the Union gunboats instead
The Confederate fleet repels the Union attack
The Union destroys most of the Confederate fleet and takes the town

evt-02-10-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Union flotilla overwhelmed and destroyed nearly the entire Confederate fleet, and Elizabeth City fell. The victory tightened Union control over North Carolina's sounds, supporting Burnside's broader coastal campaign and further squeezing the Confederate blockade-running lifeline.

evt-02-10-1919-inter-allied-women-s-conf.scenario: It is 10 February 1919 in Paris, and you are a suffragist delegate at the Inter-Allied Women's Conference, meeting alongside the official Peace Conference. Your goal is to force women's issues onto the postwar settlement, but the peacemakers next door have shown little interest in hearing from you.
evt-02-10-1919-inter-allied-women-s-conf.prompt: What do the delegates eventually win from the peace process?

choices.text: A separate women's treaty signed alongside the Treaty of Versailles
The right to present a resolution to the League of Nations Commission
Automatic suffrage for women across all Allied nations
Formal voting seats for women at the Peace Conference itself

evt-02-10-1919-inter-allied-women-s-conf.butterflyEffect: On 10 April 1919 the women were finally permitted to present a resolution to the League of Nations Commission, addressing trafficking of women and children, women's political and suffrage status, and education reform. It was a narrow opening rather than a full victory, but it placed women's rights on record in the League's founding discussions for the first time.

evt-02-10-1930-viet-nam-quoc-dan-ang.scenario: It is the night of 9–10 February 1930 at the French garrison in Yên Bái. You are a Vietnamese sergeant in the colonial army, and VNQDĐ conspirators have quietly told you they plan to storm the barracks at midnight, kill the French officers, and ignite a nationwide uprising against colonial rule.
evt-02-10-1930-viet-nam-quoc-dan-ang.prompt: What happens when the mutineers make their move?

choices.text: They quietly abandon the plan for lack of support
French officers, tipped off in advance, arrest the conspirators before midnight
The mutiny triggers simultaneous uprisings across all of Tonkin's garrisons
They briefly seize the garrison and kill French officers before being crushed by reinforcements

evt-02-10-1930-viet-nam-quoc-dan-ang.butterflyEffect: The mutineers briefly seized the garrison and killed several French officers, but French reinforcements crushed the revolt within days and it failed to spread beyond Yên Bái. Nguyễn Thái Học and other leaders were captured and guillotined, but their deaths made them nationalist martyrs whose story fed later Vietnamese independence movements.

evt-02-10-1936-second-italo-ethiopian-wa.scenario: You command Ethiopian riflemen dug into the heights of Amba Aradam on 10 February 1936, watching Italian aircraft circle overhead as Ras Mulugeta's army braces for the assault.
evt-02-10-1936-second-italo-ethiopian-wa.prompt: What did the Italians use from the air to break the Ethiopian defenses?

choices.text: Leaflets urging surrender only
Naval bombardment from the coast
Armored cavalry charges
Mustard gas bombs

evt-02-10-1936-second-italo-ethiopian-wa.butterflyEffect: Italian forces employed mustard gas dropped from aircraft, a war crime under the Geneva Protocol, alongside heavy artillery and bombing to shatter the Ethiopian lines. The chemical attacks, combined with overwhelming firepower, doomed Ethiopian resistance and hastened Italy's brutal occupation later that year.

evt-02-10-1939-spanish-civil-war.scenario: It's early February 1939 in Catalonia. You are a Republican fighter as Nationalist troops overrun the last defenses and push toward the French frontier.
evt-02-10-1939-spanish-civil-war.prompt: What do you and hundreds of thousands of others do as the front collapses?

choices.text: Surrender immediately to Nationalist forces
Retreat south to make a final stand in Madrid
Flee across the border into France
Board ships bound for the Soviet Union

evt-02-10-1939-spanish-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Roughly half a million Republican soldiers and civilians fled across the Pyrenees into France in what became known as the Retirada, many interned in makeshift camps like Argelès-sur-Mer. The mass exodus signaled the war's approaching end and scattered a generation of Spanish exiles across Europe and Latin America.

evt-02-10-1941-operation-colossus.scenario: It is the night of 10 February 1941, and you are one of 38 paratroopers of X Troop dropping into the mountains of southern Italy. Your target is the Tragino Aqueduct, and Britain's airborne forces have never attempted an operation like this before.
evt-02-10-1941-operation-colossus.prompt: What happens to the team after they blow the aqueduct?

choices.text: They are all captured by Italian forces while trying to reach the coast
They are picked up by submarine off the coast as planned
They fight their way overland to Allied lines in North Africa
They are killed in a firefight with Italian carabinieri

evt-02-10-1941-operation-colossus.butterflyEffect: The aqueduct was successfully demolished, but the raiders were unable to reach the coast for evacuation by submarine and were captured by Italian troops. Despite the capture, the raid proved airborne assault was viable, spurring the rapid growth of British parachute forces used later at Bruneval, Sicily, and Arnhem.

evt-02-10-1962-rudolf-abel.scenario: It is dawn, 10 February 1962, on the Glienicke Bridge between West Berlin and Potsdam. You watch as convicted Soviet spy Rudolf Abel is walked toward the checkpoint to be traded for captured U-2 pilot Francis Gary Powers.
evt-02-10-1962-rudolf-abel.prompt: What happens to Abel once he crosses back into Soviet-controlled territory?

choices.text: He is welcomed home and honored for his service to Soviet intelligence
He is put on trial in Moscow for compromising his network
He is quietly exiled to a labor camp for having been caught
He defects back to the West soon after crossing

evt-02-10-1962-rudolf-abel.butterflyEffect: Abel returned to the Soviet Union and was celebrated as a loyal intelligence officer, later working as a KGB consultant and mentor to younger agents. The exchange also established the Glienicke Bridge as a recurring Cold War site for prisoner swaps, and decades later inspired the film Bridge of Spies.

evt-02-10-1962-roy-lichtenstein.scenario: You step into Leo Castelli's New York gallery on 10 February 1962 and find yourself facing a huge canvas of a comic-book panel, Look Mickey, blown up with visible dots and thick outlines.
evt-02-10-1962-roy-lichtenstein.prompt: How do most critics initially react to Lichtenstein's comic-strip paintings?

choices.text: They ignore the exhibition entirely
They hail him as the greatest painter of his generation
They dismiss the paintings as vulgar copying, not real art
They mistake his work for Abstract Expressionism

evt-02-10-1962-roy-lichtenstein.butterflyEffect: Critics largely mocked the work as a crude, mechanical copy of comic strips rather than serious art, questioning whether it was even painting at all. Yet the show sold out, and within a few years Lichtenstein and Pop Art were recognized as major forces, with Look Mickey now held by the National Gallery of Art as a founding image of the movement.

evt-02-10-1996-deep-blue-chess-computer.scenario: It is 10 February 1996 in Philadelphia, and you are world chess champion Garry Kasparov sitting down for game one of a six-game match against IBM's Deep Blue. The machine has just beaten you for the first time under standard tournament conditions.
evt-02-10-1996-deep-blue-chess-computer.prompt: What was the final result of the six-game 1996 match after this shock loss?

choices.text: Kasparov withdraws in protest before it concludes
The match ends in an overall draw
Deep Blue wins the match outright
Kasparov recovers to win the match overall

evt-02-10-1996-deep-blue-chess-computer.butterflyEffect: Kasparov steadied himself and won the 1996 match overall, four points to two. IBM upgraded the machine and brought it back in 1997, when Deep Blue won the rematch, becoming the first computer to defeat a reigning world champion in a full match and a landmark moment for artificial intelligence.

evt-02-10-2008-namdaemun.scenario: It is the night of 10 February 2008, and flames are climbing the wooden pavilions of Namdaemun, Seoul's ancient south gate and its first National Treasure. Firefighters below argue over how to save the structure without collapsing it.
evt-02-10-2008-namdaemun.prompt: What actually happened to Namdaemun that night?

choices.text: The gate is demolished as a safety precaution
The wooden upper structure burns down and collapses
Firefighters extinguish the blaze quickly with minimal damage
The fire is contained to the stone base only

evt-02-10-2008-namdaemun.butterflyEffect: The upper wooden structure of the 610-year-old gate collapsed and burned almost completely; the fire was later traced to a man enraged over a land compensation dispute. The loss shocked the nation and triggered a five-year, painstaking traditional-methods restoration completed in 2013.

evt-02-10-2009-iridium-33.scenario: It's 10 February 2009. You track orbital debris for U.S. Space Command and note a routine conjunction alert: the active Iridium 33 satellite will pass near the defunct Russian satellite Kosmos 2251 over Siberia.
evt-02-10-2009-iridium-33.prompt: What actually happens minutes later, given the tracking limits of the time?

choices.text: The satellites collide, destroying both instantly
Ground control cancels Iridium's orbit entirely in time
Iridium fires thrusters and dodges the collision
Kosmos 2251 unexpectedly reactivates and moves away

evt-02-10-2009-iridium-33.butterflyEffect: Neither operator maneuvered, and the two satellites collided at over 26,000 mph, destroying both instantly and scattering thousands of debris fragments into low Earth orbit. It was the first known accidental hypervelocity collision between two intact satellites, and it forced a lasting overhaul of how agencies track and avoid orbital debris.

evt-02-10-2016-south-korea.scenario: It is 10 February 2016, days after North Korea launched a long-range rocket widely seen as a disguised missile test. You are a South Korean Unification Ministry official deciding the fate of the Kaesong Industrial Complex, the last major joint economic project with the North.
evt-02-10-2016-south-korea.prompt: What does South Korea decide to do with the Kaesong complex?

choices.text: Increase investment to keep economic ties open
Suspend operations and withdraw all South Korean personnel
Hand control of the complex over to the United Nations
Expand the complex as leverage in future talks

evt-02-10-2016-south-korea.butterflyEffect: Seoul suspended all operations, ordered South Korean personnel and companies to withdraw, and froze remaining assets, ending the complex's twelve years of operation. Its closure severed the last major channel of inter-Korean economic cooperation, and the site remained shuttered for years despite later attempts to revive dialogue.

evt-02-10-2018-kowloon-motor-bus.scenario: It's evening rush hour on 10 February 2018 and you board a crowded Kowloon Motor Bus double-decker in Tai Po, unaware the driver behind the wheel has just taken over the route at short notice.
evt-02-10-2018-kowloon-motor-bus.prompt: What was later found to have caused the bus to overturn?

choices.text: A drunk driver behind the wheel
Sudden mechanical brake failure
A driver speeding after a rushed shift change
Flooding on the road surface

evt-02-10-2018-kowloon-motor-bus.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the driver had been speeding on a sharp bend after a last-minute shift change left him rushing to finish his route. The crash, which killed 19 and injured dozens, triggered public outrage, resignations at KMB, and new rules on driver scheduling and bus speed limiters across Hong Kong.

evt-02-10-2021-rio-carnival.scenario: It's February 2021 and you direct preparations for your samba school's parade, but instead of costumes and floats, officials are meeting to decide the fate of Carnival itself amid a raging pandemic.
evt-02-10-2021-rio-carnival.prompt: What decision did Rio's authorities make about Carnival that year?

choices.text: Carnival is moved entirely online with no cancellation
Carnival is cancelled outright for the first time in over 100 years
Carnival is postponed to July and held as normal
Carnival proceeds with a smaller in-person crowd

evt-02-10-2021-rio-carnival.butterflyEffect: For the first time in over a century, Rio cancelled its Carnival celebrations outright because of COVID-19, silencing the samba schools and emptying the streets. Samba schools lost crucial income and jobs, and the tradition would not fully return until 2022.

evt-02-10-2021-2021-texas-power-crisis.scenario: It's the night of 15 February 2021. You are a grid operator at ERCOT, watching frozen power plants trip offline one after another as demand for heat soars across Texas.
evt-02-10-2021-2021-texas-power-crisis.prompt: What must you order to keep the entire grid from collapsing for months?

choices.text: Immediately request a federal takeover of the grid
Keep all power flowing and hope demand falls on its own
Begin controlled rolling blackouts across the state
Shut down the entire grid at once as a precaution

evt-02-10-2021-2021-texas-power-crisis.butterflyEffect: ERCOT initiated emergency rotating outages, but the cuts were poorly rotated and left millions without power for days in freezing temperatures. The crisis exposed Texas's isolation from national grids and led to new (limited) state winterization mandates for power plants.

evt-02-11-1584-pedro-sarmiento-de-gamboa.scenario: It's 11 February 1584, and you are among the settlers Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa has landed at the mouth of the Strait of Magellan, tasked with building a fortress town to block English ships from reaching the Pacific.
evt-02-11-1584-pedro-sarmiento-de-gamboa.prompt: What fate awaits most of the colonists left at this remote outpost?

choices.text: They are evacuated safely back to Spain within months
They successfully repel every English raider who approaches
Most die of starvation before any rescue arrives
The colony grows into a thriving Spanish port city

evt-02-11-1584-pedro-sarmiento-de-gamboa.butterflyEffect: Promised supply ships never returned, and the colonists starved as the harsh strait cut them off from aid. Years later an English privateer, Thomas Cavendish, found only a handful of survivors and named the site "Puerto del Hambre"—Port Famine—a grim name that still marks the spot today.

evt-02-11-1823-carnival-tragedy-of-1823.scenario: It is the last day of Carnival, 11 February 1823, at the Convent of the Minori Osservanti in Valletta. You watch roughly a hundred boys crowd toward a single narrow stairwell after receiving bread from the friars.
evt-02-11-1823-carnival-tragedy-of-1823.prompt: What should be done to prevent a crush as the boys leave the convent?

choices.text: Let the boys push through the single stairwell as usual
Ignore the crowding since it seems manageable
Lock the doors until the crowd calms on its own
Open additional exits and stagger the boys' departure

evt-02-11-1823-carnival-tragedy-of-1823.butterflyEffect: No such precaution was taken, and the boys fell on the crowded stairs, crushing around 110 of them to death. It stands as one of the deadliest civilian disasters in Malta's history and is still remembered in Valletta as a somber warning about crowd control at charitable gatherings.

evt-02-11-1840-la-fille-du-regiment.scenario: You are Donizetti's librettist, finishing touches for tonight's premiere at the Paris Opéra-Comique, 11 February 1840. The tenor playing Tonio wants a moment that will make the audience adore him instantly.
evt-02-11-1840-la-fille-du-regiment.prompt: What showstopper does Donizetti give the tenor to win the crowd?

choices.text: A hushed love duet with no solo passage
A martial chorus sung by the full regiment
A shortened recitative to keep him offstage more
A rousing aria packed with high Cs

evt-02-11-1840-la-fille-du-regiment.butterflyEffect: Donizetti wrote "Ah! mes amis", an aria demanding nine high Cs from the tenor. It became one of opera's great tests of vocal daring, and Luciano Pavarotti's dazzling 1972 Metropolitan Opera performance of it revived the whole work's popularity and earned him the nickname "King of the High Cs".
