evt-02-11-1919-friedrich-ebert.scenario: It's 11 February 1919, and you sit among the delegates of the Weimar National Assembly, meeting in the shadow of revolution and defeat, tasked with choosing Germany's very first president.
evt-02-11-1919-friedrich-ebert.prompt: Who does the Assembly elect to lead the fragile new republic?

choices.text: Friedrich Ebert
Kaiser Wilhelm II, restored to the throne
Karl Liebknecht
Philipp Scheidemann

evt-02-11-1919-friedrich-ebert.butterflyEffect: The Assembly elected Friedrich Ebert, the Social Democrat who had helped steer Germany through the 1918 revolution. As president he relied heavily on Article 48's emergency powers to survive uprisings and crises, a precedent later exploited by Hitler to dismantle the very republic Ebert had helped found.

evt-02-11-1976-frente-de-liberacion-homo.scenario: It's February 1976 in Buenos Aires, and you lead Argentina's pioneering gay liberation group. Rumors of an imminent military coup are spreading, and repression against dissidents of all kinds is tightening.
evt-02-11-1976-frente-de-liberacion-homo.prompt: What does the group decide about its future as the political climate turns lethal?

choices.text: Dissolve and go underground to protect members
Relocate the entire organization to Uruguay overnight
Formally merge with a mainstream political party for cover
Publicly announce an expanded campaign of street protests

evt-02-11-1976-frente-de-liberacion-homo.butterflyEffect: The Frente de Liberación Homosexual made its final public appearance and dissolved that month rather than risk exposing its members to the dictatorship's coming terror. Organized LGBT activism in Argentina would not resurface openly until the return of democracy in the 1980s.

evt-02-11-1979-ruhollah-khomeini.scenario: It is 11 February 1979 in Tehran. The army has just declared neutrality and the Shah's government has collapsed. You are a young revolutionary in the streets, and word spreads about what has become of Prime Minister Shapour Bakhtiar, the monarchy's last appointed leader.
evt-02-11-1979-ruhollah-khomeini.prompt: What happens to Bakhtiar as Khomeini's revolution takes control of the government?

choices.text: He goes into hiding and later escapes into exile
He is publicly executed within days
He is invited to serve in Khomeini's new cabinet
He leads a counter-coup with army loyalists

evt-02-11-1979-ruhollah-khomeini.butterflyEffect: Bakhtiar went into hiding and later fled into exile in Paris, while Khomeini's supporters dismantled the imperial state and established the Islamic Republic through an April 1979 referendum. Bakhtiar continued to oppose the new regime from abroad until he was assassinated by Iranian agents in 1991.

evt-02-11-1990-nelson-mandela.scenario: It is 11 February 1990 outside Victor Verster Prison. After 27 years behind bars, you are among the crowd straining to see Nelson Mandela walk free, camera crews and supporters pressing in around the gates.
evt-02-11-1990-nelson-mandela.prompt: What does Mandela do within hours of walking out of prison?

choices.text: He immediately leaves South Africa for exile abroad
He calls for an armed uprising to begin at once
He delivers a speech in Cape Town committing to a negotiated end to apartheid
He announces his retirement from all political activity

evt-02-11-1990-nelson-mandela.butterflyEffect: Mandela addressed a huge crowd from the balcony of Cape Town City Hall, pledging that the struggle for democracy would continue through negotiation rather than renewed armed conflict. Within four years those negotiations led to South Africa's first fully democratic election and Mandela's presidency.

evt-02-11-2000-space-shuttle-endeavour.scenario: It is launch day for STS-99. You are a mission specialist aboard Endeavour, preparing to unfold a specialized radar mast that will scan almost the entire globe below.
evt-02-11-2000-space-shuttle-endeavour.prompt: What is the primary objective of this shuttle mission?

choices.text: Create a high-resolution topographic map of Earth's surface
Launch a new communications satellite
Test modules for the International Space Station
Deploy the Hubble Space Telescope

evt-02-11-2000-space-shuttle-endeavour.butterflyEffect: STS-99 carried out the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission, producing the most complete high-resolution digital elevation map of Earth to that date. The dataset became a foundational resource used for decades in cartography, disaster response planning, and flight simulation.

evt-02-11-2008-timor-leste.scenario: It is dawn on 11 February 2008 at President José Ramos-Horta's residence in Dili. Rebel soldiers loyal to fugitive leader Alfredo Reinado storm the compound, and gunfire erupts as the president is caught in the open.
evt-02-11-2008-timor-leste.prompt: What happens to rebel leader Alfredo Reinado during the attack?

choices.text: He is captured and put on trial
He is killed in the exchange of gunfire
He escapes and flees into exile
He negotiates a surrender and is granted amnesty

evt-02-11-2008-timor-leste.butterflyEffect: Reinado was shot dead during the assault, while Ramos-Horta was seriously wounded and evacuated to Australia for emergency treatment, surviving the attack. His recovery and return to office helped stabilize East Timor's fragile young democracy alongside Prime Minister Xanana Gusmão's government.

evt-02-11-2013-sultanate-of-sulu.scenario: It's February 2013, and you command Malaysian security forces surrounding armed followers of the Sultanate of Sulu who have landed at Lahad Datu, Sabah, demanding recognition of the sultanate's old territorial claim.
evt-02-11-2013-sultanate-of-sulu.prompt: After weeks of stalemate, what does the Malaysian government finally do?

choices.text: Launch a military operation to retake the area
Grant the sultanate's followers permanent settlement rights
Withdraw all forces and let the claim go to international arbitration
Deport the militants without any confrontation

evt-02-11-2013-sultanate-of-sulu.butterflyEffect: Malaysia launched combined air and ground operations to clear the militants, ending the standoff after several weeks of fighting that killed dozens on both sides. The crisis strained relations with the Philippines and hardened Malaysian security policy along the Sabah coast.

evt-02-11-2018-saratov-airlines-flight-7.scenario: It is 11 February 2018, minutes after takeoff from Moscow in freezing weather. Your airspeed indicator suddenly gives readings that contradict your instincts and the aircraft's attitude.
evt-02-11-2018-saratov-airlines-flight-7.prompt: What should the crew do when airspeed readings become unreliable in icing conditions?

choices.text: Push the nose down aggressively to regain speed
Rely on pitch and power settings rather than the erroneous airspeed indication
Continue the climb and ignore the discrepancy
Disengage the autopilot immediately without cross-checking instruments

evt-02-11-2018-saratov-airlines-flight-7.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew did not notice a malfunctioning airspeed sensor caused by inactive pitot heating, leading them to push the nose down in response to a false low-speed reading. The An-148 entered a steep dive and crashed, killing all 71 aboard, prompting renewed scrutiny of cold-weather pre-flight checks on the aircraft type.

evt-02-11-2020-covid-19-pandemic.scenario: It is 11 February 2020. You sit on the WHO naming committee, aware that calling the new illness by a place or ethnic group could fuel stigma and confusion for years to come.
evt-02-11-2020-covid-19-pandemic.prompt: What official name do you assign to the new coronavirus disease?

choices.text: 2019-nCoV Disease
Wuhan Flu
SARS-2
COVID-19

evt-02-11-2020-covid-19-pandemic.butterflyEffect: The WHO settled on 'COVID-19,' a neutral name with no geographic or animal reference, deliberately avoiding the stigma seen with past outbreaks. The name became the universal shorthand used by governments, media, and health agencies worldwide for the pandemic that followed.

evt-02-11-2024-2024-finnish-presidential.scenario: It is 11 February 2024. You join fellow Finns at the polls for the runoff vote, choosing between Alexander Stubb and Pekka Haavisto to succeed the term-limited Sauli Niinistö.
evt-02-11-2024-2024-finnish-presidential.prompt: Who wins the runoff to become Finland's 13th president?

choices.text: Sanna Marin
Pekka Haavisto
Alexander Stubb
Sauli Niinistö

evt-02-11-2024-2024-finnish-presidential.butterflyEffect: Alexander Stubb defeated Pekka Haavisto in the second round, becoming Finland's 13th president. His election came as Finland navigated its first year as a NATO member following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, reinforcing the country's pro-Western foreign policy course.

evt-02-12-1502-isabella-i-of-castile.scenario: You are a Muslim living under Castilian rule in February 1502, when Queen Isabella issues a new edict targeting your faith across the kingdom.
evt-02-12-1502-isabella-i-of-castile.prompt: What does Isabella's edict require you to do?

choices.text: Pay a special annual tax to continue practicing Islam openly
Register with local churches but face no other restrictions
Relocate to designated Muslim-only towns within Castile
Convert to Christianity or leave Castile

evt-02-12-1502-isabella-i-of-castile.butterflyEffect: Muslims in Castile were forced to convert to Christianity or leave the kingdom, creating a population of nominal converts known as Moriscos who often kept practicing Islam in secret. Suspicion of their true loyalties persisted for over a century, culminating in the mass expulsion of the Moriscos from Spain between 1609 and 1614.

evt-02-12-1691-1691-conclave.scenario: You are a cardinal locked inside the Vatican conclave in the summer of 1691, now in its fifth month. The heat is unbearable, colleagues are falling ill, and the Catholic monarchs have blocked your preferred candidate, Gregorio Barbarigo.
evt-02-12-1691-1691-conclave.prompt: What finally breaks the five-month deadlock and produces a new pope?

choices.text: The conclave is dissolved and a new one called in Avignon
French cardinals agree to vote for Pignatelli despite his Spanish-controlled homeland
The Holy Roman Emperor sends troops to force a decision
Barbarigo is elected once his opponents fall ill

evt-02-12-1691-1691-conclave.butterflyEffect: French cardinals, despite political rivalry with Spain, agreed to back Cardinal Antonio Pignatelli, who was elected as Pope Innocent XII on 12 July 1691. He went on to ban nepotism in the papacy outright, ending a long era of popes enriching their own families with church offices.

evt-02-12-1894-ere-des-attentats.scenario: It is the evening of 12 February 1894 in the crowded Café Terminus near Paris's Gare Saint-Lazare. Ordinary diners fill the tables when a young anarchist named Émile Henry hurls a bomb into the room, part of France's wave of anarchist "propaganda by the deed" attacks.
evt-02-12-1894-ere-des-attentats.prompt: What did Émile Henry do immediately after throwing the bomb?

choices.text: He detonated a second, larger bomb outside the café
He drew a pistol and fired at bystanders and pursuers while trying to escape
He escaped the scene and was never identified
He surrendered on the spot and confessed to police

evt-02-12-1894-ere-des-attentats.butterflyEffect: Henry drew a revolver and fired at the crowd and pursuing police as he tried to flee, before being overpowered and arrested. He was guillotined that May, and the attack pushed France's government to pass the repressive "lois scélérates," curbing anarchist press and organizing.

evt-02-12-1909-ss-penguin.scenario: It is the night of 12 February 1909, and you are aboard the inter-island ferry SS Penguin as it nears the entrance to Wellington Harbour in a violent storm, with dangerous rocks known to lie near Sinclair Head.
evt-02-12-1909-ss-penguin.prompt: What did the crew attempt after Penguin struck the rock and began sinking?

choices.text: They deliberately beached the ship on the nearest shore
They stayed aboard and waited for a rescue ship without launching boats
They launched lifeboats into the rough seas, though many were swamped
They continued toward Wellington, believing the damage was minor

evt-02-12-1909-ss-penguin.butterflyEffect: Crew launched lifeboats into the same storm-lashed seas that had doomed the ship, and several boats capsized or were swamped before reaching shore. The disaster, New Zealand's worst maritime tragedy of the 20th century, led to an official inquiry into ferry safety and calls for better warning systems along the Cook Strait approach.

evt-02-12-1924-george-gershwin.scenario: It is the afternoon of 12 February 1924 in New York's Aeolian Hall. You sit in an audience gathered for Paul Whiteman's concert billed as "An Experiment in Modern Music," meant to prove jazz can stand beside the classics, as a young composer named George Gershwin takes the piano for his hastily written new piece.
evt-02-12-1924-george-gershwin.prompt: What happened when Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue premiered that afternoon?

choices.text: The audience booed and walked out before it ended
It was an instant hit, blending jazz and classical music to wide acclaim
It flopped commercially and was shelved for a decade
Critics dismissed it as a derivative novelty and it was quickly forgotten

evt-02-12-1924-george-gershwin.butterflyEffect: The piece, opening with a now-famous clarinet glissando, was an instant sensation that fused jazz idioms with concert-hall form. It launched the genre of symphonic jazz and Gershwin's career, leading directly to his Piano Concerto in F and An American in Paris.

evt-02-12-1935-uss-macon-zrs-5.scenario: It is 12 February 1935 off Big Sur. A storm has torn away part of your airship's tail fin, and USS Macon is losing helium and altitude fast. You are one of the crew awaiting orders.
evt-02-12-1935-uss-macon-zrs-5.prompt: What does the crew do that saves nearly everyone aboard?

choices.text: Don life jackets and wait for a controlled water landing
Bail out with parachutes immediately over the ocean
Abandon the airship's aircraft to lighten the load
Dump all fuel and attempt to fly to the nearest airfield

evt-02-12-1935-uss-macon-zrs-5.butterflyEffect: Remembering the heavy loss of life when USS Akron crashed in 1933 without life jackets, the Navy had since equipped crews with vests and rafts. Only two of 83 men died in the Macon crash, but the disaster still ended the Navy's brief experiment with rigid airships as flying aircraft carriers.

evt-02-12-1942-imperial-japanese-army.scenario: It is dawn on 12 February 1942 at Bukit Chandu, Singapore. You command a company of the Malay Regiment as the Japanese Imperial Guards Division storms Pasir Panjang Ridge, and headquarters signals a withdrawal.
evt-02-12-1942-imperial-japanese-army.prompt: What did Lieutenant Adnan Saidi's company do when ordered to fall back?

choices.text: They held their ground and fought almost to the last man
They opened negotiations for a local surrender
They retreated in good order to regroup at the harbour
They launched a counterattack that drove the Japanese back off the ridge

evt-02-12-1942-imperial-japanese-army.butterflyEffect: They refused to retreat and fought on in brutal hand-to-hand combat until overrun; Adnan Saidi was captured and killed by the Japanese. The stand became a lasting symbol of resistance, commemorated today at Reflections at Bukit Chandu, even as Singapore fell to Japan three days later.

evt-02-12-1945-tornado-outbreak-of-febru.scenario: It is the evening of 12 February 1945 in Montgomery, Alabama. The sky has gone a sickly green and the wind is rising fast as a powerful tornado bears down on your neighborhood.
evt-02-12-1945-tornado-outbreak-of-febru.prompt: What is the safest action to take as the tornado approaches your home?

choices.text: Open all the windows to equalize the pressure
Go outside to watch which direction it is moving
Move immediately to a basement or small interior room away from windows
Drive away from the storm in your car

evt-02-12-1945-tornado-outbreak-of-febru.butterflyEffect: The Montgomery tornado, tracked closely by the Weather Bureau's own office just five miles away, tore through roughly 100 houses, two warehouses, and a freight train, killing 26 people. It remains the deadliest tornado ever to strike the city, and the outbreak became a case study for how closely a storm could be observed while still causing catastrophic loss.

evt-02-12-1994-edvard-munch.scenario: It is before dawn on February 12, 1994, during the Lillehammer Winter Olympics. Thieves have just used a ladder to break through a window of Oslo's National Gallery and lifted Edvard Munch's The Scream straight off the wall.
evt-02-12-1994-edvard-munch.prompt: What ultimately happens to the stolen masterpiece?

choices.text: It is recovered undamaged in a later police operation
It is returned to the gallery the very next morning
It is destroyed by the thieves to avoid capture
It vanishes permanently onto the black market

evt-02-12-1994-edvard-munch.butterflyEffect: The painting was recovered undamaged three months later in a Norwegian police sting, with no ransom paid. The brazen theft, timed to the Olympics' media spotlight, forced a lasting overhaul of security at Norway's national museums.

evt-02-12-2001-nasa.scenario: It is 12 February 2001. Your NEAR Shoemaker probe, never designed to land, has finished a year orbiting the asteroid Eros and mission controllers are deciding its fate as fuel runs low.
evt-02-12-2001-nasa.prompt: What does the team choose to do with the spacecraft at mission's end?

choices.text: Attempt a slow, controlled descent onto the asteroid's surface
Leave it in a stable orbit indefinitely
Deliberately destroy it with a final engine burn
Redirect it toward a second asteroid flyby

evt-02-12-2001-nasa.butterflyEffect: Controllers guided NEAR Shoemaker down for a slow, controlled touchdown on Eros, and the probe kept transmitting data from the surface, making it the first spacecraft ever to land on an asteroid. The unplanned success proved that soft landings on small bodies were possible, influencing later sample-return missions like Hayabusa and OSIRIS-REx.

evt-02-12-2002-trial-of-slobodan-milosev.scenario: You are a judge at the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in The Hague on 12 February 2002, as the trial of former Yugoslav president Slobodan Milošević opens on 66 counts including genocide.
evt-02-12-2002-trial-of-slobodan-milosev.prompt: What does Milošević do as his trial begins?

choices.text: He escapes custody before proceedings can begin
He accepts a court-appointed defense team without objection
He represents himself and disputes the tribunal's authority to try him
He pleads guilty in exchange for a reduced sentence

evt-02-12-2002-trial-of-slobodan-milosev.butterflyEffect: Milošević refused defense counsel and conducted his own defense, using the courtroom as a political platform to challenge the tribunal's legitimacy. The trial dragged on for over four years without a verdict until his death in custody in 2006, denying victims a formal conviction and fueling debate over whether international tribunals could effectively try sitting or former heads of state.

evt-02-12-2002-iran-airtour.scenario: It is February 12, 2002. You are in the cockpit of an Iran Airtour Tupolev Tu-154 descending toward Khorramabad as low cloud and poor visibility close in around the surrounding mountains.
evt-02-12-2002-iran-airtour.prompt: With the weather deteriorating over mountainous terrain, what should the crew do?

choices.text: Circle at low altitude until the weather clears
Request an emergency landing at the nearest military airfield
Continue the visual descent through the cloud layer
Abort the approach and divert to an alternate airport

evt-02-12-2002-iran-airtour.butterflyEffect: The crew continued the approach through cloud and struck a mountainside outside Khorramabad, with no survivors. The disaster renewed scrutiny of Iran's aging Tupolev fleet and pushed for wider adoption of terrain-awareness warning systems on its airliners.

evt-02-12-2003-la-paz.scenario: It is February 2003 in La Paz. Police, furious over a new IMF-backed income tax and unpaid wages, have mutinied and are exchanging gunfire with soldiers outside the Presidential Palace. You advise President Sánchez de Lozada.
evt-02-12-2003-la-paz.prompt: What does the government do to end the violence in the streets?

choices.text: Withdraw the proposed income tax hike
Resign the presidency immediately
Declare martial law across the country
Deploy the army to disarm the mutinous police

evt-02-12-2003-la-paz.butterflyEffect: The government withdrew the IMF-backed tax proposal, ending 'Black February,' but the unrest was a preview of deeper unrest. Later that year, the Bolivian Gas War forced Sánchez de Lozada's resignation and flight from the country.

evt-02-12-2004-san-francisco.scenario: It is 12 February 2004. Mayor Gavin Newsom has ordered the county clerk to start issuing marriage licenses to same-sex couples, defying state law. You and your partner are near the front of the line at City Hall.
evt-02-12-2004-san-francisco.prompt: What happens to the thousands of licenses issued during this 'Winter of Love'?

choices.text: They remain valid and unchallenged indefinitely
The California Supreme Court later voids them as unauthorized
The federal government recognizes them under full faith and credit
The state legislature immediately legalizes them retroactively

evt-02-12-2004-san-francisco.butterflyEffect: The California Supreme Court voided roughly 4,000 licenses in August 2004 as issued without legal authority, but the defiant act galvanized the national marriage equality movement. California legalized same-sex marriage years later, and the fight culminated in the 2015 Obergefell v. Hodges Supreme Court ruling nationwide.

evt-02-12-2009-buffalo-niagara-internati.scenario: It is the night of 12 February 2009. Your Bombardier Dash 8 is on approach to Buffalo Niagara International Airport in icy conditions when the stick shaker activates, warning of an impending stall.
evt-02-12-2009-buffalo-niagara-internati.prompt: What is the correct pilot response to a stall warning that the crew failed to perform?

choices.text: Push the nose down and add power to break the stall
Cut engine power to reduce speed
Pull back on the controls to climb away from terrain
Deploy flaps fully and hold altitude

evt-02-12-2009-buffalo-niagara-internati.butterflyEffect: The captain pulled back on the controls instead of pushing forward, deepening the stall; the aircraft plunged into a house, killing all 49 aboard and one person on the ground. The crash of Colgan Air Flight 3407 led Congress to mandate stricter pilot rest rules and raise minimum flight-hour requirements for airline co-pilots.

evt-02-12-2009-colgan-air-flight-3407.scenario: It is 10:17 pm on February 12, 2009. You are the captain of Colgan Air Flight 3407, on approach to Buffalo through icy air, when the stick shaker suddenly warns you the plane is about to stall.
evt-02-12-2009-colgan-air-flight-3407.prompt: What is the correct stall-recovery response to the stick shaker warning?

choices.text: Pull back on the controls to raise the nose and climb away
Push forward on the controls and add engine power to break the stall
Disengage the autopilot and let the aircraft self-correct
Extend the flaps further to generate more lift

evt-02-12-2009-colgan-air-flight-3407.butterflyEffect: The captain instead pulled back on the controls, deepening the stall, and the Q400 plunged into a house in Clarence Center, killing all 49 aboard and one person on the ground. The disaster led Congress to pass the 2010 airline safety act, raising minimum pilot experience to 1,500 flight hours and tightening fatigue rules.

evt-02-12-2016-catholic-church.scenario: You are an aide inside a Havana airport lounge on 12 February 2016, watching Pope Francis and Russian Orthodox Patriarch Kirill embrace for the first meeting between their two churches' leaders since the Great Schism of 1054.
evt-02-12-2016-catholic-church.prompt: What do the two leaders actually do at this historic meeting?

choices.text: They announce the full reunification of the Catholic and Orthodox churches
They sign a joint declaration on persecution and peace, without reuniting the churches
They agree to a shared liturgical calendar for both churches
Kirill formally submits the Russian Orthodox Church to papal authority

evt-02-12-2016-catholic-church.butterflyEffect: Francis and Kirill signed a joint declaration condemning the persecution of Christians in the Middle East and calling for peace in Ukraine, but stopped far short of reunifying the churches. Relations between Rome and Moscow later cooled further after Kirill publicly backed Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

evt-02-12-2016-pope-francis.scenario: It is February 12, 2016, on the tarmac of Havana's airport. Pope Francis and Russian Orthodox Patriarch Kirill are about to meet face to face for the first time between the heads of their churches since the Great Schism.
evt-02-12-2016-pope-francis.prompt: What do the two leaders do at this unprecedented meeting?

choices.text: Sign a treaty transferring Vatican properties to the Moscow Patriarchate
Formally reunite the Catholic and Russian Orthodox churches
Sign a joint declaration on Christian unity and persecuted believers
Issue mutual excommunications to settle old disputes

evt-02-12-2016-pope-francis.butterflyEffect: They signed a joint declaration calling for unity against the persecution of Christians in the Middle East and addressing the crisis in Ukraine, without resolving centuries of doctrinal division. The meeting was widely seen as a diplomatic thaw between Rome and Moscow, though full reconciliation between the churches remained distant.

evt-02-12-2019-coffin-of-nedjemankh.scenario: It is 2019 and you are a curator at New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art, whose gilded coffin of the priest Nedjemankh has just anchored a major exhibition, when new evidence reveals it was looted from Egypt during the 2011 unrest and sold with forged ownership papers.
evt-02-12-2019-coffin-of-nedjemankh.prompt: What did the Met do once it learned the coffin had been looted?

choices.text: It repatriated the coffin to Egypt and closed the exhibit ahead of schedule
It kept the coffin on display pending a lengthy legal review
It asserted legal title and refused to return the piece
It quietly sold the coffin to another museum

evt-02-12-2019-coffin-of-nedjemankh.butterflyEffect: The museum voluntarily returned Nedjemankh's coffin to Egypt in September 2019, closing its exhibition early and cooperating with the Manhattan DA's Antiquities Trafficking Unit. The case exposed gaps in museum provenance checks and pushed institutions worldwide toward stricter due diligence on acquisitions.

evt-02-12-2019-north-macedonia.scenario: It is 12 February 2019 in Skopje. Your parliament has just ratified the Prespa Agreement, and your country is about to shed the name it held since independence.
evt-02-12-2019-north-macedonia.prompt: What does adopting the name 'North Macedonia' unlock for the country?

choices.text: Independence from Yugoslavia
NATO membership and EU accession talks, previously blocked by Greece
A merger with Bulgaria
Immediate admission to the Eurozone

evt-02-12-2019-north-macedonia.butterflyEffect: The renaming ended a 27-year dispute with Greece, which had blocked Macedonia's path into Western institutions over the name. Greece lifted its veto, and North Macedonia joined NATO in 2020 and formally opened EU accession talks soon after.

evt-02-13-1660-charles-xi-of-sweden.scenario: It is 1660 in Stockholm. King Charles X Gustav has just died, leaving the throne to his four-year-old son, and you are a member of the Riksråd deciding how Sweden will be governed until the boy comes of age.
evt-02-13-1660-charles-xi-of-sweden.prompt: How does the council arrange government for the child king?

choices.text: A regency council of high nobles nominally led by the queen dowager
The queen dowager ruling alone as sole regent
Sweden's leading general appointed as sole regent
The Riksdag of the Estates assuming direct government

evt-02-13-1660-charles-xi-of-sweden.butterflyEffect: The nobles set up a regency council of five leading magnates, nominally headed by the queen dowager Hedwig Eleonora, to rule in the young king's name. The council's mismanagement and giveaways of crown land later pushed the adult Charles XI toward absolutism and his sweeping reduktion, reclaiming estates from the aristocracy.

evt-02-13-1692-clan-macdonald-of-glencoe.scenario: You are a government soldier who has spent two peaceful weeks billeted with the MacDonalds of Glencoe, when before dawn on 13 February 1692 written orders arrive commanding you to kill your hosts in their beds.
evt-02-13-1692-clan-macdonald-of-glencoe.prompt: What do you do when the order to slaughter your hosts arrives?

choices.text: Carry out the order against your hosts
Warn the family quietly and let them escape
Refuse and report the order to a magistrate
Desert your post rather than take any action

evt-02-13-1692-clan-macdonald-of-glencoe.butterflyEffect: Most soldiers obeyed, and around 38 MacDonalds were killed, with others dying of exposure fleeing into the winter hills. The massacre became a lasting symbol of government treachery, fueling Jacobite sympathy and Highland resentment toward Clan Campbell for generations.

evt-02-13-1867-covering-of-the-senne.scenario: You are a Brussels city engineer in 1867, tasked with solving the chronic flooding, stench, and disease caused by the polluted Senne running through the heart of the city.
evt-02-13-1867-covering-of-the-senne.prompt: What large-scale solution do you propose to fix the fouled river running through the city center?

choices.text: Build a network of open-air canals to replace it
Cover and divert the river, building boulevards above it
Relocate the entire city center to higher ground
Leave the river open but dredge it more frequently

evt-02-13-1867-covering-of-the-senne.butterflyEffect: Brussels covered and diverted the Senne underground between 1867 and 1871, building grand boulevards over it in a project inspired by Haussmann's Paris. The transformation created the city's modern central avenues, though the buried river still occasionally causes flooding today.

evt-02-13-1891-whitechapel-murders.scenario: You are Constable Ernest Thompson, alone on patrol in Whitechapel's Swallow Gardens before dawn, when you find a woman dying with her throat cut and hear footsteps running off into the dark.
evt-02-13-1891-whitechapel-murders.prompt: What should you do, alone and unarmed, with the attacker still fleeing?

choices.text: Stay with the victim and blow your whistle to summon help
Chase the fleeing figure alone through the dark streets
Wake nearby residents to form a search party yourself
Leave the scene to report at the station in person

evt-02-13-1891-whitechapel-murders.butterflyEffect: Thompson stayed with the dying Frances Coles and blew his whistle for backup rather than chase alone, and other constables soon arrived. A suspect, sailor James Sadler, was arrested but later released for lack of evidence, leaving the murder officially unsolved and closing the list of Whitechapel killings.

evt-02-13-1960-nashville-sit-ins.scenario: You are a Black college student sitting at a whites-only Nashville lunch counter on 13 February 1960, as hostile onlookers jeer and threaten the protesters around you.
evt-02-13-1960-nashville-sit-ins.prompt: What should you do to keep the protest effective?

choices.text: Physically block anyone who tries to remove you
Remain seated calmly and refuse to retaliate, no matter the provocation
Leave immediately once confronted to avoid arrest
Argue loudly with hecklers to draw press attention

evt-02-13-1960-nashville-sit-ins.butterflyEffect: Trained through workshops led by activists like James Lawson, the students held firm to nonviolent discipline even as they faced arrest and abuse. The sustained campaign helped desegregate Nashville's downtown lunch counters by May 1960 and produced leaders such as Diane Nash and John Lewis who carried these tactics into the wider civil rights movement.

evt-02-13-1960-nuclear-weapons-testing.scenario: You are a French military engineer at the Reggane test site deep in the Algerian Sahara, watching final checks on a device codenamed Gerboise Bleue.
evt-02-13-1960-nuclear-weapons-testing.prompt: What did the successful detonation make France on 13 February 1960?

choices.text: The first nuclear power in the southern hemisphere
The world's fourth nuclear-armed state
A signatory to a new global test-ban treaty
The first nation to test a hydrogen bomb

evt-02-13-1960-nuclear-weapons-testing.butterflyEffect: The test made France the world's fourth nuclear power after the US, USSR and UK. It underpinned President de Gaulle's push for an independent French nuclear deterrent, the force de frappe, which shaped France's later withdrawal from NATO's integrated military command in 1966.

evt-02-13-1961-coso-artifact.scenario: You are prospecting for geodes near Olancha, California, and crack open a stone to find what looks like a hard white core wrapped in porcelain and metal.
evt-02-13-1961-coso-artifact.prompt: What is the object actually revealed to be, despite claims of ancient origin?

choices.text: A Native American ceremonial object
A prehistoric tool made of an unknown alloy
A fossilized meteorite fragment
A 1920s automobile spark plug encased in a mineral concretion

evt-02-13-1961-coso-artifact.butterflyEffect: Later examination identified the object as a 1920s Champion spark plug encased in a natural mineral concretion, not a genuinely ancient artifact. Despite this, it became a favorite example among fringe theorists claiming "out-of-place artifacts" prove lost advanced civilizations, a claim mainstream science has consistently rejected.

evt-02-13-1967-codex-madrid-leonardo.scenario: You are an American language professor combing through uncatalogued manuscripts in Madrid's national library when you realize the handwriting and mirror-script sketches match no ordinary scribe.
evt-02-13-1967-codex-madrid-leonardo.prompt: What should you do next after suspecting these notebooks are Leonardo da Vinci's own?

choices.text: Assume it's a later copyist's forgery and move on
Quietly remove the pages to study them privately at home
Publish sensational claims immediately without outside review
Alert the library and arrange for expert verification of the manuscripts

evt-02-13-1967-codex-madrid-leonardo.butterflyEffect: Jules Piccus had indeed found two lost Leonardo notebooks, later called the Madrid Codices, filled with studies on mechanics, hydraulics, and horse anatomy from the 1490s–1500s. Their authentication added major new material to the known Leonardo corpus and reshaped scholarly understanding of his engineering work.

evt-02-13-1975-world-trade-center-1973-2.scenario: It is the night of February 13, 1975. You are a New York City firefighter arriving at the North Tower of the World Trade Center, where flames are racing upward through cable shafts spanning nine floors.
evt-02-13-1975-world-trade-center-1973-2.prompt: Why is the fire spreading so effectively despite firefighters' efforts?

choices.text: Faulty wiring throughout the tower fed the flames
Many floors had not yet been fitted with sprinkler systems
A partial structural collapse spread burning debris
The building's furniture was unusually flammable

evt-02-13-1975-world-trade-center-1973-2.butterflyEffect: Many floors of the newly opened tower still lacked sprinkler systems, letting fire and smoke travel unchecked through vertical shafts before crews contained it, with no fatalities. The Port Authority responded by accelerating the retrofit of sprinklers throughout the complex in the years that followed.

evt-02-13-1978-sydney-hilton-hotel-bombi.scenario: It is 13 February 1978, and a bomb hidden in a garbage truck has just exploded outside Sydney's Hilton Hotel, where Commonwealth leaders are gathered for a regional summit.
evt-02-13-1978-sydney-hilton-hotel-bombi.prompt: How did the Australian government respond in the bombing's immediate aftermath?

choices.text: He handed control of the investigation to Interpol
He ordered the immediate closure of Sydney's international borders
He declared a state of emergency and deployed troops to protect the summit
He cancelled the Commonwealth meeting and sent delegates home

evt-02-13-1978-sydney-hilton-hotel-bombi.butterflyEffect: Prime Minister Malcolm Fraser declared a state of emergency and deployed the army to guard the summit, the first domestic military deployment of its kind since federation. The bombing triggered the Hope Royal Commission into security and intelligence, reshaping Australia's federal counter-terrorism arrangements, though the case against convicted Ananda Marga members remained highly disputed for years afterward.

evt-02-13-1984-konstantin-chernenko.scenario: It is February 1984. Yuri Andropov has just died, and you sit on the Soviet Politburo deciding who will lead the Party next.
evt-02-13-1984-konstantin-chernenko.prompt: Whom does the Politburo select as the new general secretary?

choices.text: Mikhail Gorbachev, the youngest and most reform-minded candidate
Konstantin Chernenko, an elderly loyalist seen as a safe caretaker
Grigory Romanov, the Leningrad party chief
Viktor Grishin, the powerful Moscow party boss

evt-02-13-1984-konstantin-chernenko.butterflyEffect: The Politburo chose the ailing Konstantin Chernenko as a safe, transitional figure over younger reformers. He died just thirteen months later, and his short, weak tenure cleared the way for Mikhail Gorbachev's 1985 succession and the reforms of glasnost and perestroika.

evt-02-13-1991-gulf-war.scenario: Before dawn on 13 February 1991, you are a U.S. Air Force pilot over Baghdad, cleared to drop two laser-guided bombs on the fortified Amiriyah bunker your intelligence briefing identifies as an Iraqi command center.
evt-02-13-1991-gulf-war.prompt: What happens when the bombs strike the bunker?

choices.text: The bunker turns out to be empty and abandoned
The bombs miss and strike a nearby empty field
Hundreds of civilians sheltering inside are killed
The bunker is destroyed with no casualties, as intended

evt-02-13-1991-gulf-war.butterflyEffect: The bunker was sheltering hundreds of civilian families overnight, and the strike killed over 400 of them, an event later known as the Amiriyah shelter bombing. Televised images of the aftermath sparked global outrage and led the coalition to curb strikes on targets inside central Baghdad for the rest of the air campaign.

evt-02-13-1996-nepalese-civil-war.scenario: You are a cadre of the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) in February 1996, ordered to help launch the long-planned 'People's War' against the monarchy and its rural police posts.
evt-02-13-1996-nepalese-civil-war.prompt: What action do the Maoists take to begin the insurgency?

choices.text: Negotiate directly with the king for land reform
Request United Nations mediation before any violence
Launch coordinated attacks on rural police posts
Contest the attacks through parliamentary elections only

evt-02-13-1996-nepalese-civil-war.butterflyEffect: On 13 February 1996, Maoist fighters launched coordinated attacks on police posts in several districts, opening a decade-long civil war. The conflict killed roughly 17,000 people before the 2006 peace accord, and ultimately helped end Nepal's monarchy in 2008.

evt-02-13-2007-taiwan.scenario: It is February 13, 2007. You are a Kuomintang strategist as party chairman Ma Ying-jeou faces indictment over his use of a mayoral 'special allowance fund,' just as he prepares a bid for Taiwan's presidency.
evt-02-13-2007-taiwan.prompt: What does Ma decide to do about his party leadership role?

choices.text: Refuse to step down and fight the charges from within party leadership
Leave Taiwan until the legal case is resolved
Resign from politics entirely to avoid further scrutiny
Resign as KMT chairman to clear his name and keep running for president

evt-02-13-2007-taiwan.butterflyEffect: Ma resigned as KMT chairman to fight the corruption charges while continuing his presidential campaign. He was acquitted later that year and went on to win the 2008 election, serving two terms as President of Taiwan.

evt-02-13-2008-kevin-rudd.scenario: You are seated in the gallery of Australia's House of Representatives on 13 February 2008 as newly elected Prime Minister Kevin Rudd rises to deliver a long-awaited formal apology.
evt-02-13-2008-kevin-rudd.prompt: What does Rudd's apology specifically address?

choices.text: The transportation of convicts to penal colonies
The forced removal of Indigenous children, the Stolen Generations
The 19th-century Frontier Wars against Indigenous peoples
The outcome of the 1967 referendum on citizenship

evt-02-13-2008-kevin-rudd.butterflyEffect: Rudd apologized for the forced removal of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children from their families, known as the Stolen Generations, a policy that ran for much of the 20th century. The motion passed parliament with bipartisan support but included no compensation scheme, fueling later state-level reparations programs.

evt-02-13-2011-confederated-tribes-of-th.scenario: It's 13 February 2011, and you are a member of the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation, preparing to hunt and harvest a bison just outside Yellowstone National Park for the first time in over a century.
evt-02-13-2011-confederated-tribes-of-th.prompt: What legal basis allows the tribe to exercise this off-reservation hunting right?

choices.text: The Indian Reorganization Act of 1934
A state of Montana hunting permit program
A new federal grant issued specifically for 2011
The 1855 treaty reserving off-reservation hunting rights

evt-02-13-2011-confederated-tribes-of-th.butterflyEffect: The hunt relied on treaty rights reserved in the 1855 Treaty with the Walla Walla, Cayuse, and Umatilla, which preserved tribal access to traditional hunting grounds off the reservation. The event reinforced treaty-based hunting rights and encouraged other tribes to pursue similar bison hunts near Yellowstone in subsequent years.

evt-02-13-2012-vega-rocket.scenario: It's 13 February 2012 at the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou, and you are an ESA engineer watching the maiden flight of the new Vega rocket, carrying a small science satellite and several CubeSats into orbit.
evt-02-13-2012-vega-rocket.prompt: What is the outcome of this qualification flight?

choices.text: It successfully reaches orbit, qualifying the launcher
It reaches orbit but fails to release its payloads
The rocket explodes shortly after liftoff
The launch is scrubbed and rescheduled for later that year

evt-02-13-2012-vega-rocket.butterflyEffect: Vega's debut flight succeeded, delivering the LARES satellite and companion payloads into their target orbits and qualifying the vehicle for operational use. It opened a new era of affordable small-satellite launches for ESA and Italy's Avio, complementing the larger Ariane rockets.

evt-02-13-2012-european-space-agency.scenario: You are a mission controller at Europe's Kourou spaceport in French Guiana, watching the countdown for a brand-new rocket designed to fill the gap below the mighty Ariane 5.
evt-02-13-2012-european-space-agency.prompt: What was the outcome of Vega's maiden flight on 13 February 2012?

choices.text: It explodes shortly after liftoff, destroying its payloads
It successfully reaches orbit and deploys its satellite payloads
The launch is scrubbed due to a fuelling fault
It reaches orbit but fails to release its satellites

evt-02-13-2012-european-space-agency.butterflyEffect: Vega's first launch succeeded, deploying nine satellites and giving ESA a dedicated small-launcher capability. This opened affordable access to orbit for smaller scientific and Earth-observation missions that couldn't justify a full Ariane launch, and Vega became a workhorse for Europe's independent space access over the following decade.

evt-02-13-2021-donald-trump.scenario: It's February 13, 2021, and you are a U.S. Senator sitting in judgment on former President Trump's second impeachment trial, charged with 'incitement of insurrection' after the Capitol riot.
evt-02-13-2021-donald-trump.prompt: How does the Senate vote on conviction?

choices.text: The Senate declines to hold a final vote
The trial is dismissed for lack of jurisdiction over a former president
Convicted by the required two-thirds majority
Acquitted after falling short of the two-thirds threshold

evt-02-13-2021-donald-trump.butterflyEffect: The Senate voted 57-43 to convict, ten votes short of the two-thirds majority required, and Trump was acquitted. The trial set a template for post-presidency impeachment and became a touchstone in the fight over his eligibility to run again in 2024.

evt-02-13-2021-february-13-17-2021-north.scenario: It is February 2021, and you operate Texas's power grid as an unprecedented arctic blast freezes gas wells and power plants, sending demand soaring past supply just as generation collapses.
evt-02-13-2021-february-13-17-2021-north.prompt: What must you order to keep the entire grid from suffering a total, prolonged collapse?

choices.text: Import unlimited power from neighboring grids instantly
Order controlled rolling blackouts to reduce load
Shut down the entire grid preemptively for a full week
Keep all power flowing and hope demand drops on its own

evt-02-13-2021-february-13-17-2021-north.butterflyEffect: ERCOT initiated rolling blackouts across Texas, but outages stretched far longer than planned, leaving millions without power or water for days and killing dozens. The disaster triggered federal investigations and new state laws mandating winterization of power plants and gas infrastructure.

evt-02-14-1779-death-of-james-cook.scenario: You are a marine with Captain Cook's landing party at Kealakekua Bay on February 14, 1779. A cutter has been stolen from your ships, and Cook orders you ashore to seize the Hawaiian chief Kalaniʻōpuʻu as leverage for its return.
evt-02-14-1779-death-of-james-cook.prompt: What does Cook's party attempt that triggers the fatal confrontation on the beach?

choices.text: Kidnap the chief and hold him hostage until the stolen boat is returned
Arrest a local priest accused of theft
Negotiate a formal treaty of alliance with the chief
Trade muskets for fresh food supplies

evt-02-14-1779-death-of-james-cook.butterflyEffect: The kidnapping attempt collapsed as a crowd of Hawaiians surrounded the party; Cook, four marines, and seventeen Hawaiians were killed in the ensuing fight. His death shocked Europe, ending the age of largely peaceful Pacific voyages and turning Hawaii into a cautionary symbol in exploration lore.

evt-02-14-1779-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 14 February 1779 in the Georgia backcountry. You command Patriot militia and have just learned that a large body of Loyalist recruits under Colonel Boyd is marching to reinforce the British at Augusta.
evt-02-14-1779-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What do you decide to do with your militia?

choices.text: Disband the militia and return home for the winter
Send word to the Loyalists offering a truce
Attack the Loyalist column immediately before it can join the British
Retreat and avoid engagement until reinforcements arrive

evt-02-14-1779-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Andrew Pickens' Patriot militia struck Boyd's column at Kettle Creek and scattered it, killing Boyd and dispersing most of his recruits before they could reach Augusta. The victory revived Patriot morale in Georgia and showed that Loyalist manpower there could not be relied upon, though the British still held Augusta for a time afterward.

evt-02-14-1804-kara-or-e.scenario: It's February 1804 in Šumadija, and Ottoman-appointed janissaries have just massacred Serbian village leaders. Chieftains gather at Orašac to choose a commander for an uprising against Ottoman rule.
evt-02-14-1804-kara-or-e.prompt: Whom do the assembled chieftains choose to lead the revolt?

choices.text: Prince Alexander of Serbia
Miloš Obrenović
Đorđe Petrović, known as Karađorđe
Vuk Karadžić

evt-02-14-1804-kara-or-e.butterflyEffect: The chieftains chose Đorđe Petrović, known as Karađorđe, a former Habsburg soldier and pig trader, launching the First Serbian Uprising. Though crushed by 1813, the revolt planted the seeds of modern Serbian statehood, and his dynasty would rival the Obrenović family for the Serbian throne for the next century.

evt-02-14-1852-great-ormond-street-hospi.scenario: It's 1852, and you are among the physicians opening Great Ormond Street Hospital, the first hospital in England offering in-patient beds solely for sick children. Convincing London's wealthy patrons to fund such a novel institution is your greatest obstacle.
evt-02-14-1852-great-ormond-street-hospi.prompt: How do the founders secure the money to keep the ten-bed hospital running?

choices.text: Profits from selling patent medicines
Tithes collected by the Church of England
Through voluntary subscriptions and philanthropic donations from wealthy patrons
A direct grant from Parliament

evt-02-14-1852-great-ormond-street-hospi.butterflyEffect: The hospital survived through voluntary subscriptions and philanthropic donations, the standard model for Victorian charity hospitals. It later became famous for celebrity fundraising, including Charles Dickens's benefit readings, and eventually received J.M. Barrie's gift of the Peter Pan royalties in 1929, funding it for generations.

evt-02-14-1895-oscar-wilde.scenario: It's Valentine's Day, 1895, hours before the premiere of The Importance of Being Earnest at London's St James's Theatre. You are the theatre manager, and you've just learned that the Marquess of Queensberry intends to force his way in and disrupt the show.
evt-02-14-1895-oscar-wilde.prompt: As the manager, what do you do about Queensberry's plan?

choices.text: Have Scotland Yard arrest him on the spot
Quietly cancel and reschedule the premiere
Refuse to sell him a ticket and turn him away at the door
Confront him publicly in front of the audience before curtain

evt-02-14-1895-oscar-wilde.butterflyEffect: Manager George Alexander had Queensberry's ticket money refunded and barred him from entering, so the premiere went off as a triumph. Months later, though, Wilde's own libel suit against Queensberry collapsed and exposed evidence that led to Wilde's prosecution and conviction for gross indecency, ending his career.

evt-02-14-1914-gertie-the-dinosaur.scenario: It is 1914, and you are cartoonist Winsor McCay standing before a theater screen with a whip, performing your vaudeville act as animated frames of Gertie the Dinosaur play behind you.
evt-02-14-1914-gertie-the-dinosaur.prompt: How do you make Gertie appear to respond to your live commands on stage?

choices.text: A hidden stagehand in a dinosaur costume mimicked Gertie's moves
He used a phonograph to play pre-recorded dinosaur sounds cued to the film
He timed his live commands to match Gertie's pre-drawn animated actions
He animated Gertie using stop-motion puppetry rather than drawings

evt-02-14-1914-gertie-the-dinosaur.butterflyEffect: McCay carefully timed his spoken cues and whip gestures to match pre-drawn animated actions, making Gertie seem to obey him live before astonished audiences. The film's illusion of personality and continuity helped establish character animation as an art form, influencing later studios like Disney, though McCay's own touring act ended when his employer curtailed his vaudeville work.

evt-02-14-1916-world-war-i.scenario: You serve in the Belgian government-in-exile, based at the seaside town of Sainte-Adresse in France since German troops overran your homeland. Today, February 14, 1916, you sit down with British, French and Russian representatives to sign a joint declaration.
evt-02-14-1916-world-war-i.prompt: What do Britain, France and Russia commit to in the Declaration of Sainte-Adresse?

choices.text: Negotiate a separate peace with Germany on Belgium's behalf
Transfer the Belgian Congo to French administration
Send immediate reinforcements to liberate Belgian territory
Guarantee Belgium's independence and postwar restoration

evt-02-14-1916-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The declaration formally guaranteed the restoration of Belgian independence and recognized Belgium's colonial interests after the war, bolstering Belgian resolve to keep fighting under occupation. This Allied commitment later shaped the harsh reparations and territorial terms imposed on Germany at Versailles.

evt-02-14-1919-battle-of-bereza-kartuska.scenario: It's February 1919 in the shattered borderlands of the former Russian Empire. You command a Polish unit pushing east near Bereza Kartuska, testing the strength of the fledgling Red Army for the first time.
evt-02-14-1919-battle-of-bereza-kartuska.prompt: What happens when Polish and Soviet troops clash here?

choices.text: Polish forces defeat the Bolshevik unit, opening the Polish–Soviet War
German troops intervene to separate the combatants
Both sides sign a truce ending hostilities
Soviet forces capture Warsaw outright

evt-02-14-1919-battle-of-bereza-kartuska.butterflyEffect: The clash at Bereza Kartuska marked the first serious engagement of the Polish–Soviet War, as advancing Polish forces met Bolshevik troops for the first time. The war ground on for nearly two years, climaxing in Poland's decisive victory at the Battle of Warsaw in 1920, which halted the westward spread of Soviet power.

evt-02-14-1924-computing-tabulating-reco.scenario: It's February 1924, and you sit on the board of the Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company, a sprawling firm making scales, time clocks, and punch-card tabulators. President Thomas Watson wants a name that matches bigger ambitions.
evt-02-14-1924-computing-tabulating-reco.prompt: What new name does the board adopt for the company?

choices.text: National Cash Register Company
International Business Machines Corporation
American Tabulating Corporation
Computing Machines International

evt-02-14-1924-computing-tabulating-reco.butterflyEffect: The board renamed CTR as International Business Machines Corporation, signaling Watson's ambition to dominate global business equipment, not just tabulators. Over the following decades IBM grew into the dominant force in computing hardware, shaping the technology industry long before mainframes and personal computers made it a household name.

evt-02-14-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It's dawn on 14 February 1943 near Sidi Bou Zid, Tunisia. You command inexperienced American armor as German Panzers under General von Arnim's 5th Panzer Army strike your line in the first major clash between US and German forces in North Africa.
evt-02-14-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What actually followed this opening German assault?

choices.text: American forces suffered a costly defeat and were forced to retreat
Allied forces abandoned Tunisia entirely to the Axis
Local commanders negotiated a temporary ceasefire
American forces repelled the attack decisively at first contact

evt-02-14-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The green American units were routed, and the defeat spiraled into the broader Battle of Kasserine Pass. The disaster led Eisenhower to sack General Fredendall and hand II Corps to George Patton, driving reforms in leadership and tactics that toughened US forces for the rest of the Tunisian campaign and beyond.

evt-02-14-1989-ruhollah-khomeini.scenario: You are Salman Rushdie in London on February 14, 1989. News breaks that Ayatollah Khomeini has issued a fatwa condemning your novel The Satanic Verses as blasphemous and calling for your death.
evt-02-14-1989-ruhollah-khomeini.prompt: What must Rushdie do in the immediate aftermath of the fatwa?

choices.text: Go into hiding under police protection
Ignore the fatwa as a symbolic gesture
Publicly renounce the novel immediately
Travel to Iran to negotiate directly with Khomeini

evt-02-14-1989-ruhollah-khomeini.butterflyEffect: Rushdie spent years living under British police protection, moving between safe houses. The fatwa provoked violent protests and killings linked to the book worldwide, strained UK-Iran diplomatic relations for years, and became a defining case in global debates over free expression versus religious offense.

evt-02-14-1990-indian-airlines-flight-60.scenario: It's the afternoon of 14 February 1990, and you are the co-pilot on an Airbus A320 descending toward Bangalore. The autothrottle has quietly stayed in idle 'open descent' mode as the runway draws near.
evt-02-14-1990-indian-airlines-flight-60.prompt: What critical error in the cockpit leads to the crash moments later?

choices.text: The captain suffers a sudden medical emergency at the controls
The aircraft runs out of fuel on approach
The crew ignores an engine fire warning
The crew leaves the autothrottle in idle 'open descent' mode too long, letting airspeed drop dangerously

evt-02-14-1990-indian-airlines-flight-60.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew failed to notice the aircraft had remained in idle open-descent mode, letting speed and altitude bleed away until it struck a golf course short of the runway, killing 92 of 146 aboard. As one of the first fatal A320 accidents, it intensified global scrutiny of pilot confusion around fly-by-wire automation and reshaped crew training on flight-mode awareness.

evt-02-14-1990-nasa.scenario: It is February 1990, and Voyager 1 has just crossed beyond Neptune's orbit. Carl Sagan is urging mission controllers at JPL to turn the probe's camera back toward the inner solar system before it is shut off for good.
evt-02-14-1990-nasa.prompt: Do you command Voyager 1 to turn and photograph the distant planets, including Earth?

choices.text: Keep the camera pointed outward to save power for future instruments
Turn the camera and photograph the planets, including Earth
Shut down the imaging system immediately without further photos
Photograph only the outer planets, skipping Earth

evt-02-14-1990-nasa.butterflyEffect: Engineers carried out the request, and Voyager 1 captured the 'Family Portrait' series, including the tiny speck later named the Pale Blue Dot. Sagan used the image to argue for humility and stewardship of Earth, and shortly after the cameras were permanently switched off to conserve power for the probe's interstellar journey.

evt-02-14-2005-youtube.scenario: It's early 2005, and you're one of three former PayPal employees sketching plans for a website called 'Tune In Hook Up.' You need to decide what kind of content the site should actually host.
evt-02-14-2005-youtube.prompt: What do the founders originally build the site to do?

choices.text: A streaming service for licensed television reruns
A video-based clone of the social network MySpace
A tool for businesses to host product demonstration videos
A video-dating site where users upload clips describing who they're looking for

evt-02-14-2005-youtube.butterflyEffect: The dating-video concept flopped, so the founders opened uploads to any video content. The general-purpose platform exploded, and within eighteen months Google bought YouTube for $1.65 billion, reshaping media, advertising, and giving rise to the modern influencer economy.

evt-02-14-2008-2008-northern-illinois-un.scenario: It is February 14, 2008, and gunfire has just erupted in a crowded lecture hall at Northern Illinois University. As a campus safety official, phones are ringing off the hook as students and faculty scramble for information.
evt-02-14-2008-2008-northern-illinois-un.prompt: What emergency communication reform does this shooting, following Virginia Tech in 2007, push universities to adopt?

choices.text: Armed teacher training programs required by law
Mandatory locker searches before each semester
Campus-wide text and email alert systems for real-time emergencies
Extended winter breaks to reduce campus population

evt-02-14-2008-2008-northern-illinois-un.butterflyEffect: Coming less than a year after Virginia Tech, the NIU shooting accelerated nationwide adoption of instant mass-notification systems—text, email, and outdoor sirens—so campuses could warn students in real time. Emergency communication policy became a standard part of university safety planning across the United States.

evt-02-14-2011-arab-spring.scenario: It is 14 February 2011 in Manama. Inspired by Tunisia and Egypt, you and thousands of other Bahrainis are gathering for a planned 'Day of Rage' against the ruling monarchy.
evt-02-14-2011-arab-spring.prompt: What do the demonstrators demand as they take to the streets that day?

choices.text: Immediate abolition of the monarchy and a republic
Political union with Saudi Arabia
Constitutional reform and greater political freedoms under the monarchy
A change in the line of royal succession only

evt-02-14-2011-arab-spring.butterflyEffect: Protesters called for constitutional reform, an elected government, and the release of political prisoners rather than the monarchy's overthrow. Days later security forces cleared the Pearl Roundabout camp by force, and in March Gulf Cooperation Council troops entered Bahrain to help crush the uprising, making it one of the few Arab Spring movements that failed to unseat its ruler.

evt-02-14-2018-jacob-zuma.scenario: You are a senior ANC official at Luthuli House on the night of February 14, 2018, delivering the party's final ultimatum to President Jacob Zuma, who faces mounting corruption allegations and demands he step down.
evt-02-14-2018-jacob-zuma.prompt: How does Zuma respond to the ANC's pressure to resign?

choices.text: Resigns as president that evening on national television
Declares a state of emergency to remain in office
Dissolves parliament to avoid a no-confidence vote
Refuses and calls a snap general election

evt-02-14-2018-jacob-zuma.butterflyEffect: Zuma resigned that night, clearing the way for Cyril Ramaphosa's swift inauguration as president. The transition opened the door to renewed investigations into state capture and corruption from Zuma's presidency, reshaping South African politics for years afterward.

evt-02-14-2018-parkland-high-school-shoo.scenario: In the weeks after the shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School, surviving students decide they will not let the tragedy fade into another news cycle. You are one of them, weighing what to do next.
evt-02-14-2018-parkland-high-school-shoo.prompt: What nationwide effort did the Parkland students go on to organize?

choices.text: A national walkout demanding new immigration legislation
A campaign focused solely on raising teacher salaries nationwide
March for Our Lives, a national protest demanding stricter gun laws
A student-led effort to reform college admissions testing

evt-02-14-2018-parkland-high-school-shoo.butterflyEffect: Students formed the group Never Again MSD and organized March for Our Lives, drawing hundreds of thousands of demonstrators to Washington and sister marches worldwide on March 24, 2018. The movement helped push Florida and several other states to raise the minimum age for buying firearms and tightened background-check laws.

evt-02-15-438-codex-theodosianus.scenario: You are a jurist in Constantinople in 438, part of the imperial commission tasked with untangling over a century of scattered, sometimes contradictory imperial edicts into one usable code.
evt-02-15-438-codex-theodosianus.prompt: What body of law do you decide to compile into the new code?

choices.text: Every law issued since the founding of Rome, pagan and Christian alike
Private legal opinions of famous jurists rather than imperial edicts
Only local municipal ordinances from Italy
Only general laws issued by Christian emperors since Constantine

evt-02-15-438-codex-theodosianus.butterflyEffect: The commission gathered only the general laws (constitutions) issued by Christian emperors from Constantine onward, creating the Codex Theodosianus, which took force empire-wide on 1 January 439. It became the model for later Roman law collections, including Justinian's Code, and a quarter of its text survived in the Visigothic Breviary of Alaric after Rome's western fall.

evt-02-15-1113-pope-paschal-ii.scenario: It's 15 February 1113 in Rome. As Pope Paschal II, you review a petition from Gerard, founder of a hospital for pilgrims near the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, whose brotherhood cares for the sick and wounded arriving from across Christendom.
evt-02-15-1113-pope-paschal-ii.prompt: What status do you grant this brotherhood?

choices.text: Refusal, and an order to disband the brotherhood
Absorption into the Knights Templar
Papal recognition as an independent order, free of local episcopal control
A temporary charter subject to the Patriarch of Jerusalem

evt-02-15-1113-pope-paschal-ii.butterflyEffect: The bull Pie postulatio voluntatis placed the Hospitallers of St John under papal protection alone, freeing them from the authority of local bishops. This recognition gave the order the legal independence it needed to grow into the Knights Hospitaller, one of the great military-religious orders of the Crusading era.

evt-02-15-1493-christopher-columbus.scenario: It is mid-February 1493. Your storm-battered caravel has just limped into the Tagus at Lisbon, and the captain is drafting an account of islands he insists lie across the Ocean Sea.
evt-02-15-1493-christopher-columbus.prompt: What does Columbus do with his account to spread the news fastest?

choices.text: He keeps the discovery secret to protect the route
He sends a single handwritten note only to the Spanish monarchs
He has it printed and copies circulated across European courts and cities
He returns to Spain immediately without recording anything

evt-02-15-1493-christopher-columbus.butterflyEffect: Columbus's letter, addressed to a Spanish patron, was quickly set in print and translated across Europe within months of his return. It became a sensation, shaping the continent's first (largely inaccurate) picture of the 'New World' before any official Spanish verification and helping trigger the age of transatlantic exploration.

evt-02-15-1796-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: You are Johan van Angelbeek, Dutch governor of Ceylon, in February 1796. Britain and the French-dominated Netherlands are at war, and British troops now stand before Colombo with the colony's defenses crumbling.
evt-02-15-1796-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What does van Angelbeek do to settle the colony's fate?

choices.text: Surrender the colony to the British
Flee with the colonial treasury to Batavia
Fight on until the last garrison falls
Appeal to France for reinforcements

evt-02-15-1796-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: Van Angelbeek surrendered Colombo, ending nearly 150 years of Dutch rule on the island. Ceylon passed into British hands and remained a British possession until independence in 1948.

evt-02-15-1823-australian-gold-rushes.scenario: You are surveyor James McBrien, mapping the Fish River in New South Wales in 1823, when you notice specks of gold glinting in the riverbed and sediment.
evt-02-15-1823-australian-gold-rushes.prompt: What do you do with this discovery?

choices.text: Quietly mine the gold himself before anyone else notices
Publish the find immediately to attract diggers from Britain
Sell the information to private speculators in Sydney
Report the discovery to the colonial government

evt-02-15-1823-australian-gold-rushes.butterflyEffect: McBrien reported the find to the colonial government, which suppressed the news out of fear that a gold rush would drain labour from farms and destabilise the young colony's economy. Gold discoveries kept surfacing over the following decades until the government finally embraced them in 1851, triggering the mass immigration and economic transformation of the Australian gold rushes.

evt-02-15-1898-united-states-navy.scenario: It's the night of 15 February 1898. You serve aboard USS Maine, anchored in Havana harbor amid rising tension between the United States and Spain over Cuba's rebellion, when a sudden explosion tears through the ship.
evt-02-15-1898-united-states-navy.prompt: What does the American public demand in the disaster's aftermath?

choices.text: Immediate withdrawal of all US ships from the Caribbean
War with Spain over Cuba
Extended negotiations with Spain for a lasting peace
Annexation of Cuba without any military action

evt-02-15-1898-united-states-navy.butterflyEffect: Sensational newspaper coverage blamed a Spanish mine for the blast, and the rallying cry "Remember the Maine!" helped push the United States into declaring war on Spain two months later. The resulting Spanish-American War brought the US control of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines, and a later inquiry left the true cause of the explosion unresolved.

evt-02-15-1900-second-boer-war.scenario: It is 15 February 1900. You ride with General John French's cavalry division, racing to break the Boer siege that has choked the diamond town of Kimberley for months.
evt-02-15-1900-second-boer-war.prompt: How does French's force break through to relieve the town?

choices.text: A massed frontal infantry assault on the Boer trenches
Negotiating a ceasefire with the besieging commander
A wide, fast cavalry charge through gaps in the Boer lines
Weeks of continuous artillery bombardment

evt-02-15-1900-second-boer-war.butterflyEffect: French's cavalry executed a bold charge that scattered the Boer lines and relieved Kimberley that day. Combined with the capture of General Cronjé's army at Paardeberg soon after, it marked a major turning point that boosted British morale, though the war dragged on for two more grinding years.

evt-02-15-1906-ernesto-schiaparelli.scenario: You are digging alongside Ernesto Schiaparelli's team at Deir el-Medina in 1906 when you break into a sealed chamber that shows no sign robbers ever reached it.
evt-02-15-1906-ernesto-schiaparelli.prompt: What does the untouched tomb turn out to contain?

choices.text: Mummies of a non-royal couple surrounded by household goods and furniture
Only religious papyri with no burial goods
A royal pharaoh's sarcophagus and crown jewels
An empty chamber long since looted

evt-02-15-1906-ernesto-schiaparelli.butterflyEffect: The team had found the intact burial of the architect Kha and his wife Merit, packed with furniture, clothing, food, and cosmetics untouched for over 3,000 years. It became one of the richest non-royal Egyptian finds ever made, offering an unmatched window into everyday elite life and forming a centerpiece of Turin's Museo Egizio.

evt-02-15-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: You are Lieutenant General Arthur Percival, commanding British and Commonwealth forces in Singapore on 15 February 1942. Water and ammunition are nearly exhausted, and General Yamashita's forces control most of the island.
evt-02-15-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What does Percival decide to do?

choices.text: Surrender Singapore to Japanese forces
Hold his lines and wait for reinforcements
Order one final counterattack at dawn
Evacuate his command to Sumatra to regroup

evt-02-15-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Percival surrendered roughly 80,000 troops, the largest capitulation in British military history. The fall of Singapore shattered imperial prestige across Asia and helped fuel independence movements that reshaped the postwar region.

evt-02-15-1949-gerald-lankester-harding.scenario: You are Gerald Lankester Harding, director of Jordan's Department of Antiquities, arriving at Cave 1 near the Dead Sea in February 1949 after Bedouin traders had already sold some scrolls found there.
evt-02-15-1949-gerald-lankester-harding.prompt: What do you and archaeologist Roland de Vaux do about the site?

choices.text: Sell excavation rights to foreign private collectors
Conduct a controlled excavation to recover remaining fragments and document the site
Seal the cave permanently to prevent any further study
Leave further recovery entirely to the Bedouin traders

evt-02-15-1949-gerald-lankester-harding.butterflyEffect: Harding and de Vaux launched a formal excavation of Cave 1, recovering additional scroll fragments and pottery and establishing the archaeological context the earlier Bedouin finds had lacked. Their work helped keep many fragments in institutional hands rather than scattering permanently into private collections, securing the Dead Sea Scrolls as a scholarly resource.

evt-02-15-1961-sabena-flight-548.scenario: You are an official with the U.S. Figure Skating Association in February 1961, awaiting the arrival of the national team in Brussels ahead of the World Championships in Prague, when word comes that their Boeing 707 has crashed on approach.
evt-02-15-1961-sabena-flight-548.prompt: What do the World Championships organizers decide to do that year?

choices.text: Relocate the event to New York in tribute
Cancel the World Championships for the year entirely
Postpone the competition by a few weeks and proceed
Hold the championships without any American entrants

evt-02-15-1961-sabena-flight-548.butterflyEffect: The 1961 World Figure Skating Championships were cancelled outright—the only time in the event's history. The loss of an entire generation of American skaters led to the creation of a memorial fund that still supports U.S. figure skating development today.

evt-02-15-1965-flag-of-canada.scenario: You sit in the House of Commons in Ottawa on 15 February 1965, watching the new flag rise over Parliament Hill for the first time as Canada's official national flag, ending a bitter years-long debate championed by Prime Minister Lester Pearson.
evt-02-15-1965-flag-of-canada.prompt: Which design does Parliament ultimately adopt in place of the Red Ensign?

choices.text: The Red Ensign with a small maple leaf added in the corner
A single red maple leaf on white, flanked by red bars
Pearson's original three-leaf design on a blue and white field
The Union Jack retained as the sole official flag

evt-02-15-1965-flag-of-canada.butterflyEffect: Parliament settled on the single stylized red maple leaf on a white square flanked by red bars, rejecting Pearson's earlier three-leaf 'Pearson Pennant' design. The Maple Leaf flag quickly became Canada's most recognizable national symbol, marking a deliberate step away from British imperial imagery toward a distinct Canadian identity.

evt-02-15-1976-constitution-of-cuba.scenario: It's 15 February 1976, and you queue at a polling station in Havana. Cuban voters are being asked to approve a new constitution to replace the provisional Fundamental Law that has governed the revolution since 1959.
evt-02-15-1976-constitution-of-cuba.prompt: What system does the new constitution formally establish?

choices.text: A one-party socialist state led by the Communist Party
A multiparty parliamentary democracy
A return to the 1940 constitution
A federal system with autonomous provinces

evt-02-15-1976-constitution-of-cuba.butterflyEffect: Approved overwhelmingly in the referendum, the 1976 constitution formalized Cuba as a one-party socialist state with the Communist Party as the leading force, and created the National Assembly of People's Power. It remained the country's governing charter, with amendments, until a full revision was enacted in 2019.

evt-02-15-1979-don-dunstan.scenario: It's February 1979 in Adelaide. As South Australia's reforming Labor premier, you've spent twelve years transforming the state's laws and culture, but months after losing your partner Adele Koh to illness, exhaustion has overwhelmed you.
evt-02-15-1979-don-dunstan.prompt: What do you announce to your party colleagues?

choices.text: Hand day-to-day power to a deputy while remaining party leader
Call an early election while staying on as premier
Take extended leave but keep the premiership
Resign as premier immediately

evt-02-15-1979-don-dunstan.butterflyEffect: Dunstan resigned as premier on 15 February 1979, citing ill health after a decade of sweeping reforms including decriminalising homosexuality and expanding Aboriginal land rights. His successor Des Corcoran called an early election within months and lost to the Liberals, ending Labor's long grip on the state.

evt-02-15-1995-kevin-mitnick.scenario: You are an FBI agent in February 1995, working alongside security expert Tsutomu Shimomura, and you've just traced the signal of the nation's most-wanted hacker, Kevin Mitnick, to an apartment in Raleigh, North Carolina.
evt-02-15-1995-kevin-mitnick.prompt: What happens next in the pursuit of Kevin Mitnick?

choices.text: He is caught weeks later in California instead
Agents move in and arrest him at the apartment
He slips away and flees across the border to Mexico
His lawyer negotiates a surrender in a federal courthouse

evt-02-15-1995-kevin-mitnick.butterflyEffect: Agents arrested Mitnick at the apartment, ending a two-year manhunt. His case became a landmark in cybercrime law and public debate over disproportionate punishment for hackers; after five years in prison he reinvented himself as a security consultant.

evt-02-15-1996-long-march-3b.scenario: It is 15 February 1996 at the Xichang Satellite Launch Center. You watch the new Long March 3B lift off carrying the Intelsat 708 satellite, and within seconds it begins tipping away from its planned trajectory.
evt-02-15-1996-long-march-3b.prompt: What happens to the rocket moments after this loss of control?

choices.text: Ground controllers trigger a clean self-destruct over open desert
It veers off course and crashes into a populated village nearby
It corrects course and reaches orbit successfully
It explodes harmlessly over the launch pad

evt-02-15-1996-long-march-3b.butterflyEffect: The rocket crashed into a nearby village shortly after liftoff, destroying homes and killing people on the ground. The disaster pushed China toward stricter launch-safety protocols and eventually greater openness about failures, though details of casualties remained disputed for years afterward.

evt-02-15-1999-abdullah-ocalan.scenario: It is 15 February 1999 in Nairobi. You are part of a Turkish intelligence team watching as Abdullah Öcalan leaves the Greek ambassador's compound for a vehicle bound for the airport.
evt-02-15-1999-abdullah-ocalan.prompt: How do the agents seize him?

choices.text: They bribe embassy staff to hand him over quietly
They intercept him during the transfer, once he leaves diplomatic cover
They storm the Greek embassy compound directly
They wait for a formal extradition request to be approved

evt-02-15-1999-abdullah-ocalan.butterflyEffect: Turkish operatives, aided by foreign intelligence cooperation, intercepted Öcalan the moment he stepped outside diplomatic protection and flew him to Turkey. His capture and subsequent life sentence on İmralı Island reshaped PKK strategy, triggered mass Kurdish protests across Europe, and opened decades of on-and-off peace efforts.

evt-02-15-2003-anti-war-movement.scenario: It's 15 February 2003. You join millions marching through London, Rome, New York, and dozens of other cities in coordinated demonstrations against the looming US-led invasion of Iraq.
evt-02-15-2003-anti-war-movement.prompt: What is the immediate political effect of these worldwide protests?
