choices.text: The UN Security Council votes to block the war outright
The US postpones the invasion by a full year
The UK withdraws its support for the war
Governments proceed with invasion plans despite the protests

evt-02-15-2003-anti-war-movement.butterflyEffect: Despite being among the largest coordinated protests in history, with estimated turnout of six to ten million people worldwide, the demonstrations did not stop the United States, United Kingdom, and their allies from invading Iraq the following month. The scale of the marches fueled lasting debate over the limits of public protest in shaping foreign policy.

evt-02-15-2013-chelyabinsk-meteor.scenario: It's 9:20 a.m. on 15 February 2013 in Chelyabinsk, Russia. A flash brighter than the sun streaks overhead, you feel a wave of heat through the window, and you know a shockwave is coming.
evt-02-15-2013-chelyabinsk-meteor.prompt: What should you do in the seconds before the blast wave hits?

choices.text: Call emergency services before doing anything else
Move away from windows and take cover behind something solid
Stay by the window and film it on your phone
Run outside to get a better view of the fireball

evt-02-15-2013-chelyabinsk-meteor.butterflyEffect: The shockwave shattered windows across the city, injuring roughly 1,500 people—mostly from flying glass, not the meteor itself. The event, caught on countless dashcams, spurred renewed international investment in asteroid detection and planetary defense programs.

evt-02-15-2018-2014-2016-oromo-protests.scenario: It is February 2018 in Addis Ababa. Years of Oromo and Amhara protests over land seizures and political repression have paralyzed the government, and you sit among the ruling coalition's leadership as Prime Minister Hailemariam Desalegn weighs his next move.
evt-02-15-2018-2014-2016-oromo-protests.prompt: What does Hailemariam Desalegn do to try to end the crisis?

choices.text: Declare martial law and remain in office
Resign as prime minister
Appoint a military council to take over security
Dissolve parliament and call snap elections

evt-02-15-2018-2014-2016-oromo-protests.butterflyEffect: Hailemariam resigned, becoming the first Ethiopian prime minister to step down voluntarily. His exit opened the way for Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopia's first Oromo prime minister, whose early reforms won global praise before ethnic tensions later escalated into civil conflict.

evt-02-16-1249-louis-ix-of-france.scenario: You are King Louis IX, encamped in Cyprus during the Seventh Crusade in 1249. Mongol envoys have arrived claiming their commander wishes to join you against the Muslim powers, and you must decide how to respond to this unexpected offer.

choices.text: Ally immediately with the Mamluks instead
Send a return embassy under André de Longjumeau to seek an alliance
Reject the Mongol envoys outright as untrustworthy
Refer the offer to the Pope for negotiation

evt-02-16-1249-louis-ix-of-france.butterflyEffect: Louis sent André de Longjumeau on the return embassy to the Mongol court at Karakorum. But by the time he arrived, a new regent ruled in the Great Khan's name and treated the mission as a submission rather than an alliance, demanding tribute instead — a misunderstanding that delayed any real Christian-Mongol cooperation against the Muslim world for years.

evt-02-16-1270-livonian-crusade.scenario: It is 16 February 1270, and you ride with the Livonian Order's knights along the frozen Baltic coast near Cape Karuse. Samogitian raiders are crossing the ice ahead, weighed down with plunder from a raid on Courland.
evt-02-16-1270-livonian-crusade.prompt: Do you charge across the ice to strike the raiders now?

choices.text: Attack immediately across the ice before they escape
Wait for reinforcements from Riga before engaging
Withdraw and let the raiders pass unchallenged
Offer to ransom the captives instead of fighting

evt-02-16-1270-livonian-crusade.butterflyEffect: The Order attacked but was routed on the ice; Grand Master Otto von Lutterberg was mortally wounded and died soon after. The defeat weakened the Order's grip on the region and showed the limits of crusading force against the still-pagan Samogitians.

evt-02-16-1804-first-barbary-war.scenario: It is 16 February 1804. You are Lieutenant Stephen Decatur, guiding a captured Tripolitan vessel disguised as a merchant ship into Tripoli harbor, where the captured USS Philadelphia sits under the guns of the fortress.

choices.text: Attempt to sail the Philadelphia out of the harbor intact
Board the Philadelphia, overpower the guards, and burn the ship
Open negotiations to ransom the ship back
Bombard the harbor from a safe distance

evt-02-16-1804-first-barbary-war.butterflyEffect: Decatur's men boarded the Philadelphia, overpowered its guards, and set it ablaze without losing a single American. The raid denied Tripoli a captured warship, made Decatur a national hero, and was reportedly praised by Lord Nelson as one of the boldest acts of the age.

evt-02-16-1900-southern-cross-expedition.scenario: You are with Carsten Borchgrevink's sledging party on the Great Ice Barrier in February 1900, having just pushed further south than anyone before. Rations are thinning and the Antarctic season is turning against you.

choices.text: Wait on the ice for resupply from the ship
Turn back immediately to secure the record and the men's safety
Push on further south despite dwindling supplies
Build a permanent depot before retreating

evt-02-16-1900-southern-cross-expedition.butterflyEffect: They turned back and reached their ship safely, preserving the new farthest-south record. Their route onto the Barrier and their use of dogs and sledges gave Scott and Shackleton a proven template that shaped the following decade of Antarctic expeditions.

evt-02-16-1918-council-of-lithuania.scenario: It is 16 February 1918 in German-occupied Vilnius. You are one of twenty men on the Council of Lithuania, and you must decide whether to formally proclaim independence while enemy troops still patrol the streets outside.

choices.text: Sign the Act of Independence, declaring Lithuania a sovereign democratic state
Propose a permanent union with Poland instead of independence
Wait for German approval before making any declaration
Postpone any declaration until the World War ends

evt-02-16-1918-council-of-lithuania.butterflyEffect: The Council signed the Act despite the German occupation, and though German forces remained until autumn 1918, the declaration became the legal foundation of the modern Lithuanian state. It is still marked annually as State Restoration Day, and the Council's work led directly to the Constituent Assembly of 1920.

evt-02-16-1922-byblos.scenario: It is 1922 near Byblos. A landslide has just torn open the hillside, exposing a hidden underground tomb that archaeologists soon rush to examine.
evt-02-16-1922-byblos.prompt: What makes the sarcophagus found inside so significant?

choices.text: It holds a gold funerary mask of an Egyptian pharaoh
It bears one of the earliest known Phoenician alphabetic inscriptions
It is an empty decoy tomb meant to mislead robbers
It contains Roman legionary armor and weapons

evt-02-16-1922-byblos.butterflyEffect: The tomb held the sarcophagus of King Ahiram, bearing one of the earliest substantial inscriptions in the Phoenician alphabet. The find gave scholars crucial evidence for reconstructing the script that would go on to influence the Greek and, eventually, Latin alphabets.

evt-02-16-1936-popular-front-spain.scenario: It's election day, February 16, 1936, in Spain. You are a campaign organizer for the Popular Front, the alliance of left-wing parties led by Manuel Azaña, watching the votes come in against a divided right.
evt-02-16-1936-popular-front-spain.prompt: What follows the Popular Front's narrow victory in this election?

choices.text: The military immediately seizes power without resistance
A stable coalition governs peacefully for a decade
The monarchy is restored within the year
Rising tensions lead to civil war by that summer

evt-02-16-1936-popular-front-spain.butterflyEffect: Azaña's government took power, but the victory deepened polarization between left and right. Months of unrest, land seizures, and political violence followed, culminating in the military uprising of July 1936 that plunged Spain into civil war.

evt-02-16-1961-dusable-black-history-mus.scenario: It's 1961 on Chicago's South Side. You are Margaret Burroughs, opening the doors of your own home to the public as a new museum dedicated to preserving African American history, culture, and art.
evt-02-16-1961-dusable-black-history-mus.prompt: What do you and your husband Charles name this pioneering museum at its founding?

choices.text: DuSable Museum of African American History
Ebony Museum of Negro History and Art
South Side Museum of Black Culture
Chicago African American Heritage Museum

evt-02-16-1961-dusable-black-history-mus.butterflyEffect: The museum opened as the Ebony Museum of Negro History and Art before being renamed the DuSable Museum of African American History in 1968, honoring Jean Baptiste Point du Sable, Chicago's first non-Indigenous permanent settler. It grew into one of the oldest independent Black history museums in the United States.

evt-02-16-1991-nicaragua.scenario: It's February 16, 1991, in Managua. You are a former Contra fighter who learns that Enrique Bermúdez, the movement's longtime military commander, has just been shot dead outside a hotel less than a year after the war against the Sandinistas ended.
evt-02-16-1991-nicaragua.prompt: What actually follows the investigation into Bermúdez's killing?

choices.text: The United States extradites a named suspect from Honduras
Contra factions reunite and resume armed struggle
The case remains officially unsolved amid competing theories
Sandinista officials are swiftly tried and convicted

evt-02-16-1991-nicaragua.butterflyEffect: No one was ever definitively convicted; theories pointed variously to Sandinista sympathizers, disgruntled former Contras, or unresolved wartime grudges. The unsolved murder became a symbol of how fragile Nicaragua's postwar reconciliation remained even after peace accords ended the fighting.

evt-02-16-1996-amtrak.scenario: It's rush hour on February 16, 1996, in Silver Spring, Maryland. You are a federal investigator arriving at the wreckage where a MARC commuter train has just collided head-on with the Chicago-bound Amtrak Capitol Limited, killing eleven people aboard the commuter train.
evt-02-16-1996-amtrak.prompt: What safety reform does the investigation into this collision help drive nationwide?

choices.text: Mandatory installation of Positive Train Control systems
A federal ban on diesel locomotives near cities
Nationwide electrification of commuter rail lines
Elimination of all shared freight-passenger tracks

evt-02-16-1996-amtrak.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the MARC train had passed a red signal before the crash. The disaster added urgency to calls for automatic braking systems, feeding into the push for Positive Train Control, which Congress eventually mandated nationwide under the Rail Safety Improvement Act of 2008.

evt-02-16-1998-taoyuan-international-air.scenario: It is the evening of 16 February 1998. You are the captain of a China Airlines Airbus on final approach to Taipei in heavy rain, and the aircraft is unstable — too high, too fast, and drifting off the glideslope as the runway nears.

choices.text: Request an emergency diversion to Kaohsiung
Circle the airport until visibility improves
Continue the approach and correct on final
Abort the landing and execute a go-around

evt-02-16-1998-taoyuan-international-air.butterflyEffect: The crew continued the unstable approach rather than aborting, and the aircraft stalled and crashed into a residential area near the airport, killing everyone aboard along with several people on the ground. The disaster intensified international scrutiny of China Airlines' safety culture and spurred wider industry emphasis on go-around discipline during unstable approaches.

evt-02-16-1998-china-airlines-flight-676.scenario: It's the evening of February 16, 1998, near Chiang Kai-shek International Airport. You are an air traffic controller watching China Airlines Flight 676 abort its landing in poor visibility and attempt to climb away in a go-around.
evt-02-16-1998-china-airlines-flight-676.prompt: What does the crash investigation ultimately determine caused the disaster?

choices.text: A bomb detonated in the cargo hold
The aircraft collided with another plane on approach
The crew mismanaged the go-around and stalled the aircraft
An engine failure caused sudden loss of thrust

evt-02-16-1998-china-airlines-flight-676.butterflyEffect: Investigators concluded the crew mishandled the go-around, allowing the Airbus A300 to stall and plunge into a road and homes, killing all 196 aboard and six on the ground. The crash intensified scrutiny of China Airlines' safety culture and pilot training after a string of earlier accidents.

evt-02-16-2000-emery-worldwide-airlines-.scenario: You are an NTSB investigator sifting through the wreckage of the DC-8 cargo plane that went down in a Rancho Cordova salvage yard moments after the crew reported losing pitch control on takeoff.
evt-02-16-2000-emery-worldwide-airlines-.prompt: What does the investigation find caused the crew to lose control?

choices.text: An improperly maintained elevator control system
Pilot error in reading takeoff instruments
Sudden engine failure on both engines
Severe crosswinds at the airport

evt-02-16-2000-emery-worldwide-airlines-.butterflyEffect: Investigators traced the crash to an improperly maintained elevator control system that had been incorrectly rigged during earlier maintenance, robbing the crew of pitch control on takeoff. The findings intensified scrutiny of maintenance practices at aging cargo carriers and contributed to Emery Worldwide's decline before it ceased operations the following year.

evt-02-17-1621-myles-standish.scenario: It's February 17, 1621, in the struggling Plymouth Colony; the Pilgrims, having survived a devastating first winter, gather to choose someone to organize the settlement's defense against unknown dangers ahead.
evt-02-17-1621-myles-standish.prompt: Who should the colonists elect as commander of their militia?

choices.text: Myles Standish
William Bradford
Edward Winslow
John Carver

evt-02-17-1621-myles-standish.butterflyEffect: The colonists chose Myles Standish, who was re-elected to the post for the rest of his life. He went on to lead the colony's defense, including a controversial 1623 preemptive strike against a Massachusett plot, setting an early precedent for how New England colonies would organize military self-defense.

evt-02-17-1815-treaty-of-ghent.scenario: It is 17 February 1815 in Washington. A courier has just delivered the signed Treaty of Ghent, negotiated months earlier in the Low Countries, ending the war with Britain. The Senate must decide how quickly to act on it.
evt-02-17-1815-treaty-of-ghent.prompt: What did the treaty do regarding the territory each side held before the war?

choices.text: It restored the pre-war borders of June 1812 with no territorial changes
It ceded parts of Canada to the United States
It redrew the Great Lakes boundary in Britain's favor
It transferred Spanish Florida to American control

evt-02-17-1815-treaty-of-ghent.butterflyEffect: The Senate ratified the treaty unanimously and immediately, restoring all pre-war borders with no territorial changes on either side. News had already been outpaced by the Battle of New Orleans, fought weeks after signing, which let Americans celebrate the peace as a triumph and cemented a long era of Anglo-American accommodation.

evt-02-17-1838-great-trek.scenario: It is mid-February 1838, and you are camped with a Voortrekker party along the Bloukrans River in Zulu territory, having just heard that Piet Retief's negotiating party was killed by Dingane's warriors. Rumors say Zulu impis are massing nearby.
evt-02-17-1838-great-trek.prompt: What defensive step could have protected the scattered trekker camps from the coming night attack?

choices.text: Requesting British troops from Port Natal that same night
Drawing wagons into a defensive laager circle
Retreating immediately back to the Cape Colony
Sending unarmed scouts to negotiate at Dingane's kraal

evt-02-17-1838-great-trek.butterflyEffect: The Bloukrans and Weenen attacks, following Dingane's killing of Retief, became a foundational trauma in Afrikaner memory and spurred a Boer revenge campaign that culminated in the Battle of Blood River later in 1838. The bloodshed hardened Boer-Zulu hostility for a generation and helped justify the founding of the Boer republic of Natalia.

evt-02-17-1859-cochinchina-campaign.scenario: It's February 1859, and you serve aboard a French warship anchored on the Saigon River as combined French and Spanish forces storm the sprawling Vietnamese citadel defending the city.
evt-02-17-1859-cochinchina-campaign.prompt: What happened to the massive citadel shortly after its capture?

choices.text: It was rebuilt as the new French colonial headquarters
The French demolished it because they lacked troops to hold it
It was handed back to Vietnamese authorities under treaty
It became a joint French-Spanish garrison for the rest of the war

evt-02-17-1859-cochinchina-campaign.butterflyEffect: With too few troops to hold the sprawling citadel against Vietnamese counterattacks, French forces demolished it in 1859 and dug in around a smaller fortified enclave. Saigon nonetheless became the anchor of France's expanding colony, formally ceded in 1862 and developed into the capital of French Cochinchina.

evt-02-17-1894-rudolf-diesel.scenario: It's early 1894 in Augsburg, Germany, and you watch anxiously as engineer Rudolf Diesel starts up his experimental compression-ignition engine for a public test, hoping it will finally run under its own power.
evt-02-17-1894-rudolf-diesel.prompt: What happened when Diesel's engine started running that day?

choices.text: It exploded, destroying the workshop
It refused to start at all
It ran flawlessly for eight hours straight
It ran under its own power for about one minute before failing

evt-02-17-1894-rudolf-diesel.butterflyEffect: That brief run proved Diesel's compression-ignition principle was viable, though years of refinement followed before a reliable commercial engine appeared in 1897. The diesel engine's efficiency later transformed shipping, rail, and heavy industry worldwide.

evt-02-17-1904-giacomo-puccini.scenario: It's opening night, February 17, 1904, at La Scala in Milan, and you're watching Puccini's new opera Madama Butterfly unfold when jeers, catcalls, and animal noises suddenly erupt from parts of the audience.
evt-02-17-1904-giacomo-puccini.prompt: How should Puccini respond to this disastrous premiere?

choices.text: Replace the lead soprano and continue the run
Cancel the opera permanently
Withdraw the opera and revise it before restaging
Ignore the audience and keep performing it unchanged

evt-02-17-1904-giacomo-puccini.butterflyEffect: Puccini withdrew the opera after its single disastrous performance and revised it, splitting the long second act and adjusting the score. The reworked version premiered in Brescia three months later to great acclaim, and Madama Butterfly went on to become one of the most performed operas in the world.

evt-02-17-1913-armory-show.scenario: It's February 1913, and you stand inside the vast 69th Regiment Armory in New York City, staring at a jumble of overlapping angles the catalog calls 'Nude Descending a Staircase.' Newspapers outside are already mocking it mercilessly.
evt-02-17-1913-armory-show.prompt: What derisive nickname did American critics give this scandalous Cubist painting?

choices.text: An explosion in a shingle factory
A pile of kindling
A drunk man's nightmare
A broken stained-glass window

evt-02-17-1913-armory-show.butterflyEffect: The Armory Show introduced European modernism—Cubism, Fauvism, Post-Impressionism—to American audiences en masse, scandalizing critics and the public. Duchamp's painting became the most notorious image of the exhibition, and the show is credited with reshaping American art collecting and pushing US artists toward modernism.

evt-02-17-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is dawn on 17 February 1944. You stand on the flight deck of a U.S. carrier as pilots scramble to strike Truk Lagoon, the heavily fortified base Japan calls its 'Gibraltar of the Pacific.'
evt-02-17-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What was the outcome of the two-day carrier strike on Truk?

choices.text: U.S. Marines stormed and captured the atoll immediately after
The strike caused only minor damage and was called off early
Japanese defenses repelled the raid with heavy American losses
American carrier strikes devastated the fleet and aircraft based there

evt-02-17-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Operation Hailstone destroyed dozens of Japanese ships and aircraft, gutting Truk as a naval stronghold without a single American amphibious landing. Its neutralization let the Allies bypass the base entirely and push the island-hopping campaign faster toward the Mariana Islands.

evt-02-17-1959-vanguard-2.scenario: It is 17 February 1959 at Cape Canaveral. Engineers watch the Vanguard SLV-4 rocket lift the small spherical satellite meant to photograph cloud cover from orbit, a first for any spacecraft.
evt-02-17-1959-vanguard-2.prompt: What problem limited the quality of Vanguard 2's cloud-cover observations?

choices.text: The satellite began tumbling in orbit, degrading its readings
It collected perfect cloud data for its full nineteen-day mission
The satellite burned up on re-entry within hours of launch
The rocket failed to reach orbit at all

evt-02-17-1959-vanguard-2.butterflyEffect: An uneven separation left the satellite tumbling and wobbling in orbit, so its photocells rarely pointed steadily at Earth and much of the data was unusable. Despite the flaw, the mission proved satellites could observe weather from space, paving the way for TIROS-1's success the following year.

evt-02-17-1964-1964-gabonese-coup-d-etat.scenario: It is 17 February 1964 in Libreville. You are among the 150 officers who have just arrested President Léon M'ba and installed his rival Aubame as president. Gabon seems calm, but France has a garrison nearby and deep interests in this former colony.
evt-02-17-1964-1964-gabonese-coup-d-etat.prompt: What did French forces do in response to the coup against M'ba?

choices.text: France recognized Aubame's new government and sent economic aid
France evacuated its citizens and severed all ties with Gabon
French troops in Gabon remained neutral and did not intervene
French forces intervened militarily and restored M'ba to power

evt-02-17-1964-1964-gabonese-coup-d-etat.butterflyEffect: French paratroopers intervened within two days, crushed the coup, and restored M'ba to power, arresting the plotters. The episode became a textbook case of France's willingness to use force to protect friendly African leaders, a pattern repeated across Françafrique for decades.

evt-02-17-1974-bell-uh-1-iroquois.scenario: It's the early hours of February 17, 1974, and Army Private Robert Preston has just stolen a Bell UH-1 helicopter from Fort Meade and is buzzing low over Washington, D.C., circling toward the White House.
evt-02-17-1974-bell-uh-1-iroquois.prompt: How did Secret Service agents respond as the stolen helicopter hovered near the White House?

choices.text: They ordered anti-aircraft guns onto the roof
They evacuated the President by helicopter
They opened fire on the helicopter with shotguns
They scrambled fighter jets to intercept it

evt-02-17-1974-bell-uh-1-iroquois.butterflyEffect: Secret Service gunfire wounded Preston as he tried to land, and he was arrested minutes later on the South Lawn; no one else was hurt. The incident exposed serious gaps in White House airspace security and prompted reviews of grounds defense that shaped later security measures.

evt-02-17-1978-the-troubles.scenario: It's the evening of February 17, 1978, and you are the IRA member tasked with phoning in a warning about the incendiary device your unit has just planted at the packed La Mon House Hotel near Belfast.
evt-02-17-1978-the-troubles.prompt: How much warning time does the call actually give before the device detonates?

choices.text: No warning is given at all
A warning is phoned in for the wrong location entirely
A full hour, giving time for a complete evacuation
Only a few minutes, far too little to clear the building

evt-02-17-1978-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The warning came only minutes before the device exploded, giving almost no time to evacuate, and twelve people at a social gathering were killed in the resulting fireball. Public revulsion, including from within nationalist communities, was so intense that it pushed the Provisional IRA to reconsider its use of this type of indiscriminate incendiary device in crowded civilian venues.

evt-02-17-1980-mount-everest.scenario: It's February 17, 1980, and you're roped to your partner high on Everest, the wind screaming at nearly -40°C after weeks of siege climbing through the brutal Himalayan winter, the summit finally within reach.
evt-02-17-1980-mount-everest.prompt: What should the climbers do this close to the top in such extreme cold?

choices.text: Turn back and wait for warmer weather
Retreat immediately to base camp
Push for the summit despite the extreme cold
Signal for a helicopter evacuation

evt-02-17-1980-mount-everest.butterflyEffect: Krzysztof Wielicki and Leszek Cichy pushed on and reached the summit, achieving the first winter ascent of Everest. Their success proved winter Himalayan climbing was possible and launched a new era dominated by Polish mountaineers, later nicknamed the 'Ice Warriors' for their string of winter first ascents on 8,000-meter peaks.

evt-02-17-1995-cenepa-war.scenario: It's February 1995, and you're an Ecuadorian soldier holding a jungle outpost in the Cenepa River valley after weeks of fighting with Peruvian troops over this remote, disputed stretch of border.
evt-02-17-1995-cenepa-war.prompt: What finally brings the fighting to a halt?

choices.text: Peru withdraws all forces unilaterally
The conflict escalates into a full-scale invasion
A ceasefire is negotiated with international mediation
Ecuador surrenders the disputed territory outright

evt-02-17-1995-cenepa-war.butterflyEffect: A ceasefire was arranged with the help of Argentina, Brazil, Chile, and the United States—guarantors of the 1942 peace treaty—leading to a demilitarized buffer zone. That process eventually produced a comprehensive 1998 peace treaty that finally settled the decades-old border dispute between Ecuador and Peru.

evt-02-17-1996-philadelphia.scenario: It is February 1996 in Philadelphia, and you are world chess champion Garry Kasparov, seated across from IBM's Deep Blue supercomputer at the start of a six-game match.

choices.text: Deep Blue wins the match outright
Kasparov withdraws before the match is completed
The match ends in a tied score with no winner declared
Kasparov wins the six-game match overall

evt-02-17-1996-philadelphia.butterflyEffect: Kasparov won the 1996 match 4-2, despite losing the very first game to a computer for the first time. The result set up a rematch in 1997, which an upgraded Deep Blue won, making Kasparov the first world champion defeated by a machine and a defining moment in the history of artificial intelligence.

evt-02-17-1996-nasa.scenario: It is 17 February 1996 at Kennedy Space Center. You watch the first mission of NASA's new low-cost Discovery Program lift off atop a Delta II rocket, bound for a distant asteroid named Eros.
evt-02-17-1996-nasa.prompt: What made the NEAR Shoemaker mission historic?

choices.text: It became the first spacecraft to orbit and later land on an asteroid
It performed only a brief flyby without entering orbit
It was the first spacecraft to fly past and photograph a comet
It became the first spacecraft to orbit the planet Mars

evt-02-17-1996-nasa.butterflyEffect: NEAR Shoemaker became the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid, and in 2001 it made the first successful landing on one as well. Its success proved that small, cheaper Discovery-class missions could achieve major planetary science, opening the door to later missions like Dawn and Stardust.

evt-02-17-2006-2006-southern-leyte-mudsl.scenario: It's February 17, 2006, in the village of Guinsaugon, Southern Leyte, after ten days of relentless rain have soaked the mountainside looming over your community, and you suddenly hear a deep rumbling from the slope above.
evt-02-17-2006-2006-southern-leyte-mudsl.prompt: What should residents do the moment they hear the mountainside begin to move?

choices.text: Go outside to check on neighbors' houses first
Wait to see if the rumbling stops before acting
Shelter indoors and wait it out
Evacuate immediately to higher, stable ground

evt-02-17-2006-2006-southern-leyte-mudsl.butterflyEffect: The mountainside collapsed, burying most of Guinsaugon including an elementary school and killing over a thousand people. The disaster pushed the Philippine government to invest in geological hazard mapping and early-warning systems for landslide-prone communities.

evt-02-17-2008-kosovo.scenario: It is 17 February 2008, and you sit among the delegates of the Kosovo Assembly in Pristina as they prepare to cast a historic vote on the territory's status.

choices.text: Vote to unify with neighboring Albania
Vote to accept broad autonomy within Serbia
Declare independence from Serbia unilaterally
Reject the UN's proposed status settlement entirely

evt-02-17-2008-kosovo.butterflyEffect: The Assembly unilaterally declared independence from Serbia. The United States and most EU members recognized Kosovo, but Serbia, Russia, and China did not, leaving the country partially recognized and the status of its Serb-majority north disputed for years afterward.

evt-02-17-2011-arab-spring.scenario: It is the dark early hours of 17 February 2011 at Pearl Roundabout in Manama. You are camped with hundreds of protesters demanding reform when riot police suddenly advance on the sleeping crowd.
evt-02-17-2011-arab-spring.prompt: What did Bahraini security forces do in this pre-dawn raid?

choices.text: They raided the camp, killing four protesters and injuring dozens
They allowed the sit-in to continue undisturbed
They negotiated a peaceful withdrawal with protest leaders
They opened immediate political dialogue with the opposition

evt-02-17-2011-arab-spring.butterflyEffect: Police stormed the camp, killing four protesters and injuring many more in what became known as 'Bloody Thursday.' The crackdown inflamed the uprising rather than ending it, and by March Saudi-led Gulf troops entered Bahrain to help the monarchy suppress the movement entirely.

evt-02-17-2011-bahrain.scenario: It is before dawn on 17 February 2011, and you are camped with hundreds of pro-democracy demonstrators at Manama's Pearl Roundabout, asleep in tents after days of protest.
evt-02-17-2011-bahrain.prompt: What do Bahraini riot police do at this hour?

choices.text: Escort the protesters peacefully back to their homes
Open a dialogue tent to negotiate with organizers
Storm the camp in a violent pre-dawn raid
Distribute food and blankets to the campers

evt-02-17-2011-bahrain.butterflyEffect: Security forces stormed the camp in what became known as 'Bloody Thursday,' killing several sleeping protesters and injuring dozens. The crackdown hardened the opposition and led, weeks later, to Gulf Cooperation Council troops entering Bahrain to help suppress the uprising.

evt-02-17-2016-february-2016-ankara-bomb.scenario: It is evening rush hour on 17 February 2016, and you are riding in a convoy of military vehicles stopped at traffic lights on İsmet İnönü Boulevard in Ankara, close to the parliament and army headquarters.
evt-02-17-2016-february-2016-ankara-bomb.prompt: What happens to the convoy moments later?

choices.text: A gunman opens fire from a nearby rooftop
A car bomb detonates among the stopped vehicles
The convoy passes through without incident
Protesters block the road and the convoy turns back

evt-02-17-2016-february-2016-ankara-bomb.butterflyEffect: A car bomb tore through the convoy, killing at least 30 people, mostly military and civilian personnel. The Kurdistan Freedom Hawks (TAK) claimed responsibility, and the attack deepened the security crackdown and conflict between Ankara and Kurdish militant groups in the months that followed.

evt-02-18-1814-war-of-the-sixth-coalitio.scenario: It is 18 February 1814 at Montereau, and you command Napoleon's forces as the retreating Army of Bohemia tries to hold the bridges over the Seine and Yonne during his rapid Six Days' Campaign against the advancing coalition armies.
evt-02-18-1814-war-of-the-sixth-coalitio.prompt: What should you do to press your advantage at Montereau?

choices.text: Attack across the bridges to force the coalition back
Negotiate an immediate armistice with Schwarzenberg
Abandon the campaign and march south toward Italy
Withdraw and consolidate defenses around Paris

evt-02-18-1814-war-of-the-sixth-coalitio.butterflyEffect: Napoleon's troops stormed the bridges and drove Schwarzenberg's Army of Bohemia back with heavy losses, one of several sharp tactical victories in the campaign. But the coalition armies simply regrouped and kept advancing on multiple fronts; within two months Paris fell and Napoleon was forced to abdicate and depart for Elba.

evt-02-18-1873-vasil-levski.scenario: It is early 1873 and you are Vasil Levski, riding between secret revolutionary committees across Ottoman-ruled Bulgaria, aware that the network you built is fragile and that informers may already be watching your routes.
evt-02-18-1873-vasil-levski.prompt: What ultimately happens to you after your capture by Ottoman authorities?

choices.text: You are tried and hanged by Ottoman authorities
You are pardoned in exchange for revealing the committee network
You are exiled to a remote Ottoman province
You escape across the border into Serbia

evt-02-18-1873-vasil-levski.butterflyEffect: Levski was captured near Lovech after a committee member's letters were intercepted, and he was executed by hanging shortly afterward. His death, before any uprising could be launched, left the revolutionary network leaderless, but his writings and organizational model directly shaped the April Uprising of 1876 and his memory became central to Bulgaria's national identity.

evt-02-18-1878-lincoln-county-new-mexico.scenario: It is 18 February 1878 in Lincoln County, New Mexico Territory. You ride alongside merchant John Tunstall when a sheriff's posse aligned with his rival, the Murphy-Dolan faction, stops your party on the road.
evt-02-18-1878-lincoln-county-new-mexico.prompt: What happens to Tunstall in this encounter?

choices.text: He is shot dead, sparking the Lincoln County War
He escapes the encounter unharmed
He negotiates a truce between the rival merchants
He is arrested and jailed without incident

evt-02-18-1878-lincoln-county-new-mexico.butterflyEffect: The posse shot Tunstall dead, and his murder ignited the Lincoln County War as his young allies, including Billy the Kid, formed the "Regulators" to avenge him. The ensuing gunfights and manhunts turned Billy the Kid into one of the most enduring outlaw legends of the American West.

evt-02-18-1943-white-rose.scenario: It is February 1943 at Ludwig Maximilian University in Munich. You are Sophie Scholl, and you have just scattered the last leaflets of your sixth White Rose pamphlet from the top-floor gallery down into the atrium below.
evt-02-18-1943-white-rose.prompt: A university caretaker spots you. What happens next?

choices.text: He confronts you directly and tears up the leaflets himself
He reports you to university officials, who summon the Gestapo
He helps you gather the leaflets and lets you leave
He warns you quietly and pretends not to have seen anything

evt-02-18-1943-white-rose.butterflyEffect: The caretaker, Jakob Schmid, reported the Scholls to the Gestapo. Hans and Sophie Scholl were arrested that day, and within four days they and Christoph Probst were tried and executed by guillotine. The group's leaflets, smuggled abroad, were later cited by Allied propaganda and made the White Rose a lasting symbol of German civilian resistance to Nazism.

evt-02-18-1965-the-gambia.scenario: It is 18 February 1965 in Bathurst, and you are a Gambian official watching the Union Jack lowered as your small West African nation, surrounded almost entirely by Senegal, formally gains independence from Britain.
evt-02-18-1965-the-gambia.prompt: What form of government does the Gambia adopt at the moment of independence?

choices.text: A federation with Senegal
A one-party socialist state
A constitutional monarchy under the British queen
An immediate republic with an elected president

evt-02-18-1965-the-gambia.butterflyEffect: The Gambia initially became a constitutional monarchy, retaining Queen Elizabeth II as head of state represented by a governor-general, much like other newly independent Commonwealth states. It became a republic in 1970 after a national referendum, with Dawda Jawara as its first president.

evt-02-18-1970-chicago-seven.scenario: It is 18 February 1970 in a Chicago federal courtroom. You are one of seven defendants who have spent months on trial before Judge Julius Hoffman, accused of conspiring to incite riots at the 1968 Democratic National Convention.
evt-02-18-1970-chicago-seven.prompt: What does the jury ultimately decide about the conspiracy charge?

choices.text: They acquit on conspiracy but convict five on lesser charges
All seven are convicted of conspiracy
All seven are acquitted of every charge
The judge declares a mistrial for the whole case

evt-02-18-1970-chicago-seven.butterflyEffect: The jury acquitted all seven of conspiracy but convicted five of them on individual counts of crossing state lines to incite a riot. Those convictions, along with contempt citations against the defendants and their lawyers, were later overturned on appeal after the Seventh Circuit cited Judge Hoffman's open bias and errors, making the case a lasting symbol of 1960s courtroom political theater.

evt-02-18-1979-richard-petty.scenario: You are watching the 1979 Daytona 500 live on television as Donnie Allison and Cale Yarborough, locked together for the lead, crash into the wall on the final lap, opening the door for the pack behind them.
evt-02-18-1979-richard-petty.prompt: What actually happens to Allison and Yarborough right after the crash?

choices.text: They restart their cars and continue racing for the win
They get out and fight each other on the infield grass
They shake hands and wave the field past
They are both immediately disqualified from the race

evt-02-18-1979-richard-petty.butterflyEffect: With the two leaders wrecked, Richard Petty swept past to win his record sixth Daytona 500, but the real story was Allison and Yarborough brawling on the infield grass as cameras rolled. It was the first Daytona 500 broadcast live flag-to-flag on network television, and the fight's national exposure is widely credited with helping launch NASCAR into the American mainstream.

evt-02-18-1991-provisional-irish-republi.scenario: It is the early morning of 18 February 1991. You are a British Transport Police officer at Victoria station when a coded warning call reports a device has been left in the concourse.
evt-02-18-1991-provisional-irish-republi.prompt: What should you do immediately after receiving the warning?

choices.text: Evacuate the station and surrounding area at once
Wait for the bomb squad before clearing anyone
Assume it is a hoax and continue normal operations
Search the station yourself before deciding whether to evacuate

evt-02-18-1991-provisional-irish-republi.butterflyEffect: The Victoria station device detonated, killing one person and injuring dozens, while the Paddington bomb was found and dealt with after a partial evacuation. The attack was part of the IRA's mainland bombing campaign, which hardened British security policy and public anger even as it fed the slow diplomatic track that eventually produced the Good Friday Agreement.

evt-02-18-2003-daegu-subway-fire.scenario: You are the driver of the second train pulling into Jungangno station in Daegu on 18 February 2003, moments after fire breaks out in the train ahead of you, and smoke is already pouring across the platform.
evt-02-18-2003-daegu-subway-fire.prompt: What should you do as smoke fills the station around your train?

choices.text: Continue on to the next station before opening the doors
Shut off the ventilation system and keep the doors closed
Wait for authorization from the control room before acting
Open the doors and get passengers off the train immediately

evt-02-18-2003-daegu-subway-fire.butterflyEffect: The actual driver waited on instructions from the control room rather than acting on his own, then left the train while taking the master key, leaving the doors sealed as smoke filled the carriages. Most of the 192 deaths occurred in that second train, and the disaster forced sweeping reforms to South Korea's subway safety rules, including fire-resistant train materials and clearer emergency authority for drivers.

evt-02-18-2004-nishapur.scenario: On 18 February 2004, a runaway freight train carrying sulfur, petrol, and fertilizer derails near Nishapur, Iran. Villagers and emergency crews rush toward the wreckage, unaware of what the cargo could do.
evt-02-18-2004-nishapur.prompt: What should the gathering rescue workers do at the derailment site?

choices.text: Evacuate the surrounding area and wait for specialized hazmat teams
Search the wagons for survivors right away
Begin dousing the wreckage with water immediately
Start unloading cargo to prevent it from being lost

evt-02-18-2004-nishapur.butterflyEffect: The volatile cargo ignited hours later in a massive explosion that killed as many as 295 people, including 182 rescue workers who had gathered at the scene believing it safe. The disaster exposed gaps in hazardous-material handling and pushed Iran to tighten regulations on transporting dangerous chemicals by rail.

evt-02-18-2013-brussels-airport-diamond-.scenario: It is just before 8pm on 18 February 2013. You are part of a masked crew in two cars marked as police, driving onto the tarmac at Brussels Airport toward a Zurich-bound jet loaded with diamonds.
evt-02-18-2013-brussels-airport-diamond-.prompt: How do you get the gems without a single shot being fired?

choices.text: Storm the checkpoint with weapons drawn and force entry
Disguise the team and vehicles as police/security to bluff past ground staff
Hijack the aircraft mid-flight and demand the cargo
Bribe the airline's ground crew in advance to look away

evt-02-18-2013-brussels-airport-diamond-.butterflyEffect: The gang cut through a perimeter fence, drove up in police-marked vehicles, and threatened ground crew into handing over the diamond shipment worth roughly $50 million before vanishing in minutes. It became one of the largest diamond heists in history; most suspects were later arrested internationally but only a fraction of the diamonds were ever recovered.

evt-02-18-2014-revolution-of-dignity.scenario: It is 18 February 2014 in Kyiv. Riot police backed by armored vehicles push into Independence Square as street battles rage between security forces and Euromaidan demonstrators.
evt-02-18-2014-revolution-of-dignity.prompt: What follows over the next two days as the standoff escalates?

choices.text: Yanukovych immediately agrees to a full ceasefire and resigns peacefully
Security forces escalate further, killing dozens more protesters and collapsing support for Yanukovych
The Ukrainian army intervenes on the side of the demonstrators
The protesters disperse and the square is cleared without further violence

evt-02-18-2014-revolution-of-dignity.butterflyEffect: Within 48 hours, dozens more protesters were shot dead by security forces in what became the deadliest days of the crisis, shattering support for President Viktor Yanukovych. Parliament voted him out and restored the 2004 constitution, and within weeks Russia occupied Crimea, starting the Russo-Ukrainian war that continues today.

evt-02-18-2021-perseverance-rover.scenario: It is 18 February 2021 and you are a flight controller at JPL, watching telemetry as the Perseverance rover begins its descent through the Martian atmosphere toward Jezero Crater, minutes away from the moment engineers call the 'seven minutes of terror.'
evt-02-18-2021-perseverance-rover.prompt: What system does Perseverance rely on to set down gently in the crater?

choices.text: A parachute alone, landing on airbags
A crash-landing cushioned by a crushable frame
Retro-rockets that set it directly on wheeled legs
A sky crane that lowered it on cables from a hovering descent stage

evt-02-18-2021-perseverance-rover.butterflyEffect: Perseverance used a rocket-powered 'sky crane' to lower itself on cables and touch down safely, becoming the most sophisticated rover ever landed on Mars. It went on to collect rock samples for eventual return to Earth and carried the Ingenuity helicopter, which made the first powered flight on another planet weeks later.

evt-02-19-1903-venezuelan-crisis-of-1902.scenario: It is early 1903, and your fleet has spent weeks blockading Venezuelan ports, seizing gunboats and starving the treasury, all because President Cipriano Castro refuses to pay foreign debts.
evt-02-19-1903-venezuelan-crisis-of-1902.prompt: What did Castro ultimately agree to in order to end the crisis?

choices.text: Ceding Venezuelan territory to the blockading powers
Immediate full repayment of all debts
Submitting the disputed claims to international arbitration
Resigning the presidency

evt-02-19-1903-venezuelan-crisis-of-1902.butterflyEffect: Castro's agreement to arbitration ended the blockade, but the episode alarmed Washington. Fearing repeated European intervention in Latin America, Theodore Roosevelt issued the Roosevelt Corollary in 1904, asserting America's own right to intervene in the hemisphere first.

evt-02-19-1910-old-trafford.scenario: It is 19 February 1910, and you're among the first fans filing into Manchester United's brand-new Old Trafford stadium for its inaugural league match against Liverpool.
evt-02-19-1910-old-trafford.prompt: What was the result of Old Trafford's opening match?

choices.text: The match was abandoned due to weather
The match ended in a 1-1 draw
Manchester United won 3-0
Manchester United lost 3-4 to Liverpool

evt-02-19-1910-old-trafford.butterflyEffect: United lost their new stadium's debut 3–4 to Liverpool, a deflating start for such an ambitious new ground. Old Trafford nonetheless grew into the largest club football stadium in the UK, later nicknamed the 'Theatre of Dreams' and hosting decades of United's greatest triumphs.

evt-02-19-1931-socialist-soviet-republic.scenario: It is 19 February 1931, and Moscow has decreed that the Socialist Soviet Republic of Abkhazia — a nominally independent 'treaty republic' — is being dissolved and reorganised.
evt-02-19-1931-socialist-soviet-republic.prompt: What new status did Abkhazia receive after the dissolution?

choices.text: An autonomous Soviet socialist republic within the Georgian SSR
Independent statehood outside the Soviet Union
Direct incorporation into the Russian SFSR
Full union republic status equal to Georgia

evt-02-19-1931-socialist-soviet-republic.butterflyEffect: Abkhazia became the Abkhaz ASSR, subordinate to Georgia rather than an equal partner. The downgrade deepened Abkhaz grievances over Georgian dominance, resentment that erupted into full-scale war between Georgia and Abkhazia after the Soviet Union's collapse in the 1990s.

evt-02-19-1937-yekatit-12.scenario: You are a resident of Addis Ababa on 19 February 1937, hours after an attempt to assassinate Marshal Graziani, the Italian viceroy. Occupation troops are moving through the streets.
evt-02-19-1937-yekatit-12.prompt: What do the occupying Italian forces do in the hours that follow?

choices.text: Offer a general amnesty to calm the population
Negotiate quietly with Ethiopian nobles to restore order
Launch a mass killing and imprisonment of Ethiopian civilians
Withdraw troops from the city fearing an uprising

evt-02-19-1937-yekatit-12.butterflyEffect: Italian forces launched days of mass killing and imprisonment of Ethiopian civilians, an atrocity later described as the worst massacre in Ethiopian history. Rather than crushing resistance, the brutality hardened opposition and helped sustain the Ethiopian Patriots' guerrilla campaign until liberation in 1941.

evt-02-19-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: You are an aide in the Oval Office in February 1942. Advisors, citing fears after Pearl Harbor, have placed a sweeping order authorizing military exclusion zones on the West Coast in front of President Roosevelt for his signature.
evt-02-19-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What does Roosevelt do with the order before him?

choices.text: Signs Executive Order 9066, authorizing removal from military zones
Vetoes the order on constitutional grounds
Sends the order to the Supreme Court for review first
Delays signing until Congress debates it

evt-02-19-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: On 19 February 1942 Roosevelt signed Executive Order 9066, authorizing the forced removal of anyone deemed a threat from designated military zones. It led to the incarceration of roughly 120,000 Japanese Americans, two-thirds of them citizens, for the duration of the war. The order stood until 1976, when it was formally rescinded, and in 1988 the U.S. government issued reparations and a formal apology.

evt-02-19-1942-winnipeg.scenario: It is dawn on 19 February 1942 in Winnipeg. Nazi soldiers march down Portage Avenue, swastika flags fly over the legislature, and the mayor is dragged off by fake Gestapo agents — all staged to shock the city awake.
evt-02-19-1942-winnipeg.prompt: What was the real purpose of this elaborate staged 'invasion'?

choices.text: To recruit soldiers for overseas service
To test the city's civil defense readiness
To sell Victory Bonds by showing citizens what Nazi occupation would look like
To protest wartime rationing policies

evt-02-19-1942-winnipeg.butterflyEffect: If Day, organised by Winnipeg's Victory Loan committee, dramatized a fictional Nazi occupation complete with a mock book-burning and staged arrests of officials. The shock tactic worked: Manitoba's war bond sales far exceeded their targets, and similar theatrical fundraising stunts spread to other Canadian cities for the rest of the war.

evt-02-19-1959-cyprus.scenario: It is 19 February 1959 in London. As a Cypriot delegate, you sit across from British, Greek, and Turkish representatives, trying to end years of colonial rule and armed struggle on the island.
evt-02-19-1959-cyprus.prompt: What settlement do the parties sign to chart Cyprus's future?

choices.text: A formal partition of the island into separate Greek and Turkish states
A plan for full union (Enosis) of Cyprus with Greece
An agreement establishing an independent, power-sharing Republic of Cyprus
An extension of British Crown Colony rule with local autonomy

evt-02-19-1959-cyprus.butterflyEffect: The London Agreement, following the Zurich Agreement, created a framework for an independent Republic of Cyprus with power-sharing between Greek and Turkish Cypriots. Independence followed on 16 August 1960, but the fragile constitutional arrangement collapsed by 1963, setting the stage for the 1974 crisis and the island's lasting division.

evt-02-19-1965-pham-ngoc-thao.scenario: It is 19 February 1965 in Saigon, and you are Colonel Phạm Ngọc Thảo, leading tanks and loyal troops in a coup against General Nguyễn Khánh's government.
evt-02-19-1965-pham-ngoc-thao.prompt: What happened to Thảo's coup attempt within days?

choices.text: It succeeded and Thảo took power
The United States intervened militarily to restore Khánh
Khánh joined the coup and shared power with Thảo
It collapsed, forcing Thảo into hiding until his capture and death

evt-02-19-1965-pham-ngoc-thao.butterflyEffect: The coup failed, but it fatally weakened Khánh, who was ousted by rival generals days later. After Thảo's death in 1965, revelations that he had long been a Việt Minh sleeper agent embedded at the top of the ARVN stunned Saigon's officer corps and deepened American distrust of their South Vietnamese allies.

evt-02-19-1976-executive-order-9066.scenario: You are advising President Gerald Ford in February 1976 as growing public pressure calls for formally addressing the wartime order that had authorized the internment of Japanese Americans decades earlier.
evt-02-19-1976-executive-order-9066.prompt: What action does Ford take regarding Executive Order 9066?

choices.text: Refers the matter to Congress to repeal by statute
Issues an apology but leaves the order technically in force
Issues a proclamation formally terminating the order
Lets the order lapse quietly without public comment

evt-02-19-1976-executive-order-9066.butterflyEffect: On 19 February 1976 Ford issued Proclamation 4417, formally terminating Executive Order 9066 and acknowledging that the World War II internment had been a national mistake. The proclamation strengthened the redress movement, which culminated in the 1988 Civil Liberties Act granting reparations and a formal apology to survivors.

evt-02-19-1985-china-airlines-flight-006.scenario: You are the flight engineer aboard China Airlines Flight 006, cruising at 41,000 feet over the Pacific, when engine No. 4 fails and the autopilot's compensation sends the 747SP rolling onto its back.
evt-02-19-1985-china-airlines-flight-006.prompt: What must the captain do to pull the aircraft out of its plunge?

choices.text: Feather all engines and prepare for a water landing
Deploy speed brakes while leaving autopilot engaged
Disengage the autopilot and manually recover from the dive
Order the cabin crew to begin evacuation procedures over open ocean

evt-02-19-1985-china-airlines-flight-006.butterflyEffect: Captain Min Yuan-fong disengaged the autopilot and manually recovered the jet after it fell nearly 30,000 feet, inverted at times, before leveling out barely above the ocean and diverting to San Francisco. The near-catastrophe, caused by over-reliance on autopilot during asymmetric thrust, led airlines to revise training on manual upset recovery.

evt-02-19-1989-flying-tiger-line-flight-.scenario: It is before dawn on 19 February 1989, and you are in the cockpit of a FedEx-owned Boeing 747 cargo jet descending toward Kuala Lumpur. Outside there is no visible horizon, only blackness over the hills below.
evt-02-19-1989-flying-tiger-line-flight-.prompt: With no visual reference and altitude cues in doubt, what should the crew do before descending further?

choices.text: Descend early based on the timing of previous approaches into the airport
Cross-check instruments against the charted minimum safe altitude before continuing descent
Level off indefinitely and wait for enough daylight to see the ground
Judge height by eye despite the total darkness over the terrain

evt-02-19-1989-flying-tiger-line-flight-.butterflyEffect: The aircraft continued descending below a safe altitude and struck a hillside 12 km short of the runway, killing all four aboard. The crash became a textbook case of controlled flight into terrain at night, reinforcing the aviation industry's push for stricter altitude cross-checks and terrain-awareness warning systems on cargo aircraft.

evt-02-19-2002-nasa.scenario: It is February 2002, and after months spent aerobraking into a lower orbit, Mars Odyssey is finally ready to begin its primary science mission mapping the red planet's surface.
evt-02-19-2002-nasa.prompt: What did Odyssey's thermal-imaging instrument go on to reveal beneath the Martian surface?

choices.text: Vast deposits of subsurface water ice
Active volcanic vents
Fossilized microbial life
Liquid oceans beneath the poles

evt-02-19-2002-nasa.butterflyEffect: Odyssey's THEMIS and gamma-ray data revealed hydrogen-rich soil consistent with buried water ice across much of Mars. This discovery directly shaped NASA's choice of a northern landing site for the 2008 Phoenix lander, which confirmed the ice by digging it up.

evt-02-19-2006-methane.scenario: It is days after a methane explosion has trapped 65 miners deep inside the Pasta de Conchos coal mine near Nueva Rosita. You are coordinating the rescue as toxic gas readings keep climbing.
evt-02-19-2006-methane.prompt: What decision does the mining company ultimately make?

choices.text: Evacuate the surrounding town as a precaution
Halt rescue operations, citing lethal underground gas levels
Keep drilling regardless of explosion risk until every body is found
Flood the mine shafts to extinguish underground fires

evt-02-19-2006-methane.butterflyEffect: Grupo México suspended rescue operations after roughly a week, citing lethal gas concentrations underground. Only two of the 65 miners' bodies were ever recovered; the rest remain sealed in the mine. The disaster became a national symbol of lax mine safety enforcement and fueled a lasting movement for labor and safety reform among Mexican miners.

evt-02-19-2011-belitung-shipwreck.scenario: You are a curator preparing the 2011 Smithsonian exhibition of treasures from the Belitung shipwreck, a 9th-century Arabian dhow whose cargo was recovered by a commercial salvage company rather than trained archaeologists.
evt-02-19-2011-belitung-shipwreck.prompt: How do many archaeologists respond to the exhibition going forward?

choices.text: They protest and some scientists boycott, citing commercial salvage over rigorous excavation
They demand the artifacts be immediately returned to Indonesia
They offer to co-curate the show with the salvage company
They praise the find as a model of marine archaeology

evt-02-19-2011-belitung-shipwreck.butterflyEffect: Scholars objected that commercial salvage, done for profit rather than careful excavation, had destroyed valuable archaeological context, and some Smithsonian-affiliated researchers distanced themselves from the show. The controversy intensified a long-running debate over treasure hunting versus scientific excavation of underwater heritage sites worldwide.

evt-02-19-2012-mexican-drug-war.scenario: It is before dawn on 19 February 2012 inside Apodaca prison in Nuevo León. You are a guard on duty as tension boils between rival Zetas and Gulf Cartel inmates housed in the same cellblock.
evt-02-19-2012-mexican-drug-war.prompt: What actually unfolded during the riot that followed?

choices.text: Federal troops storm the prison at first sign of unrest
Corrupt guards unlock cells, letting Zetas attack rival inmates while dozens escape
Inmates negotiate a peaceful surrender with the warden
An accidental fire, not gang violence, causes the deaths

evt-02-19-2012-mexican-drug-war.butterflyEffect: Investigators found that corrupt guards had unlocked cell doors, letting Zetas inmates attack Gulf Cartel-affiliated prisoners while roughly 30 Zetas slipped out the back gate during the chaos. Forty-four inmates died in the staged violence. The scandal exposed deep corruption inside Mexico's prison system and triggered a wave of firings and reform efforts in state penitentiaries.

evt-02-20-1685-french-colonization-of-te.scenario: It is 1685, and you sail with Robert de La Salle's expedition. Navigational errors have stranded your ships 400 miles west of the Mississippi's mouth, on the unfamiliar coast of Texas.
evt-02-20-1685-french-colonization-of-te.prompt: What should La Salle do now that the fleet has missed its target?

choices.text: Abandon the mission and sail the fleet back to France
Establish a fort on the Texas coast and search overland for the river
Continue sailing west along the coast toward Spanish California
Ask local tribes to guide the ships directly to the Mississippi's mouth

evt-02-20-1685-french-colonization-of-te.butterflyEffect: La Salle built Fort Saint Louis near present-day Inez and led fruitless expeditions searching for the Mississippi, exploring the Rio Grande and East Texas instead. Disease, Native American raids, and La Salle's own murder by mutineers doomed the colony by 1688, but its brief existence alarmed Spain into accelerating its own settlement of Texas.

evt-02-20-1816-the-barber-of-seville.scenario: It is the evening of 20 February 1816 at the Teatro Argentina in Rome, and you sit in the audience for the premiere of Rossini's new opera buffa, unaware that supporters of the older composer Giovanni Paisiello are scattered through the crowd.
evt-02-20-1816-the-barber-of-seville.prompt: What happens during the chaotic opening night?

choices.text: The audience cheers wildly and demands an immediate encore
The audience jeers and sabotages the performance amid onstage accidents
Rossini is carried through the streets in triumph that same night
The performance is cancelled after the first act due to weather

evt-02-20-1816-the-barber-of-seville.butterflyEffect: The premiere was a near-disaster: onstage mishaps combined with hissing from Paisiello loyalists, who resented anyone retelling the same Beaumarchais story their favorite had already set. Rossini refused to attend the second performance out of caution, but that night succeeded, and the opera went on to become one of the most beloved comic operas ever written.

evt-02-20-1835-1835-concepcion-earthquak.scenario: It is 20 February 1835, and you are among the residents of Talcahuano on the Chilean coast. The ground has just stopped shaking violently, and you notice the sea beginning to pull back unusually far from the shore.
evt-02-20-1835-1835-concepcion-earthquak.prompt: As the sea recedes strangely after the earthquake, what should you do?

choices.text: Return home to check on belongings and structural damage
Wait for a formal warning from local authorities before moving
Walk down to inspect the exposed seabed before anyone else
Flee immediately to higher ground, anticipating a wave will follow

evt-02-20-1835-1835-concepcion-earthquak.butterflyEffect: The retreating water was the warning sign of a tsunami that soon struck and destroyed Talcahuano, killing dozens along the coast. Charles Darwin, then anchored nearby aboard HMS Beagle, examined the raised beaches and dead shellfish left stranded afterward, evidence he later cited to support his theory that land could rise gradually over time.

evt-02-20-1846-free-city-of-cracow.scenario: It is 20 February 1846, and you are among Polish insurgents who have seized control of the Free City of Kraków, hoping to spark a wider uprising against the partitioning powers before Austrian troops arrive.
evt-02-20-1846-free-city-of-cracow.prompt: What should the insurgents do to legitimize and rally support for the uprising?

choices.text: Disband quietly and wait for a better opportunity
Appeal to Russia to mediate between the insurgents and Austria
Surrender to Austrian authorities immediately
Proclaim a national government and issue a manifesto to rally support

evt-02-20-1846-free-city-of-cracow.butterflyEffect: The insurgents proclaimed a national government and issued a manifesto promising to abolish feudal obligations, but Austrian forces crushed the rising within days. Austria then incited Galician peasants against the rebelling nobility in a brutal backlash, and Kraków itself was annexed by Austria later that year, ending its status as a free city.

evt-02-20-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: It is dawn on 20 February 1864, and you march with Union General Truman Seymour's column through the Florida pine barrens near Olustee Station, where Confederate troops under Joseph Finegan wait behind hastily built defenses.
evt-02-20-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What does the Union command do when it meets the entrenched Confederate line?

choices.text: Order repeated frontal assaults against the entrenched Confederate line
Withdraw immediately without engaging
Wait for reinforcements before attacking
Attempt a wide flanking march around the Confederate position

evt-02-20-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Seymour ordered repeated frontal assaults into the Confederate position, and Union forces, including the 54th Massachusetts and other Black regiments, suffered roughly one-in-three casualties before retreating to Jacksonville. The defeat ended the Union's Florida expedition and became a defining moment proving the combat record of United States Colored Troops.

evt-02-20-1872-metropolitan-museum-of-ar.scenario: You are a patron in New York City on February 20, 1872, filing into a modest building on Fifth Avenue for the opening day of a new institution called the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
evt-02-20-1872-metropolitan-museum-of-ar.prompt: What did the museum's founders declare as its core purpose in opening to the public?

choices.text: To house only European royal collections
To compete directly with the Louvre for tourists
To bring art and education to the American public
To serve as a private club for wealthy collectors

evt-02-20-1872-metropolitan-museum-of-ar.butterflyEffect: The Met's founders framed it as a civic institution to bring art and education to the American public, not just the wealthy. From that small rented space it grew, moving to Central Park in 1880, eventually becoming the largest art museum in the Americas and one of the most visited museums on Earth.

evt-02-20-1943-fissure-vent.scenario: It's 20 February 1943, and you are farmer Dionisio Pulido, plowing your cornfield near Paricutin, Mexico, when the ground suddenly hisses, cracks, and begins spewing smoke and ash beneath your feet.
evt-02-20-1943-fissure-vent.prompt: What should you do as the fissure opens in your field?

choices.text: Keep plowing and ignore the disturbance
Dig into the crack to investigate its source
Flee the field immediately and report what you've seen
Try to smother the fissure with dirt to stop it

evt-02-20-1943-fissure-vent.butterflyEffect: Pulido fled and alerted his family and local authorities, and within a day a small cone was building where his cornfield had been. Parícutin grew into a full volcano over the next nine years, becoming one of the only volcanoes in history whose entire birth-to-dormancy life cycle was scientifically documented, transforming modern volcanology.

evt-02-20-1943-the-saturday-evening-post.scenario: It is February 20, 1943. You pick up your copy of The Saturday Evening Post and see a striking new Norman Rockwell painting titled 'Freedom of Speech,' the first of a planned series.
evt-02-20-1943-the-saturday-evening-post.prompt: What campaign will the government soon use these Four Freedoms paintings to promote?

choices.text: Food rationing
Victory gardens
Military enlistment
War bonds

evt-02-20-1943-the-saturday-evening-post.butterflyEffect: The four Rockwell paintings toured the country as the centerpiece of a war bond drive, raising over $130 million for the war effort. They became among the most reproduced artworks in American history and were adapted into Office of War Information posters seen nationwide.

evt-02-20-1959-john-diefenbaker.scenario: It is 20 February 1959, and you sit in the House of Commons as Prime Minister John Diefenbaker's government prepares to announce the fate of the Avro CF-105 Arrow, Canada's advanced supersonic interceptor program.
evt-02-20-1959-john-diefenbaker.prompt: What does Diefenbaker's government decide about the Arrow program?

choices.text: Continue funding development despite rising costs
Cancel the program entirely and order the aircraft destroyed
Sell the Arrow program and designs to Britain
Transfer production of the Arrow to the United States

evt-02-20-1959-john-diefenbaker.butterflyEffect: The government cancelled the Arrow outright on what became known as "Black Friday," grounding the fleet and ordering existing airframes, tooling, and blueprints destroyed. Nearly 14,000 Avro workers lost their jobs overnight, and many of Canada's top aerospace engineers emigrated to American firms and NASA, where some later contributed to the Apollo program.

evt-02-20-1962-project-mercury.scenario: It is 20 February 1962, and you are astronaut John Glenn aboard Friendship 7, about to become the first American to orbit the Earth. Ground control has just warned of a possible loose heat shield.
evt-02-20-1962-project-mercury.prompt: What precaution should you take before reentry to guard against a failed heat shield?

choices.text: Attempt an emergency splashdown before completing the orbits
Jettison the retrorocket package immediately to reduce weight
Manually override the capsule to land at a different site
Leave the retrorocket package attached to help hold the heat shield in place

evt-02-20-1962-project-mercury.butterflyEffect: On ground control's instruction, Glenn kept the retrorocket package strapped over the heat shield during reentry, in case the shield truly was loose. The warning proved to be a faulty sensor reading, and Glenn splashed down safely after three orbits, a triumph that boosted American morale in the Space Race and paved the way for Gemini and Apollo.

evt-02-20-1965-ranger-8.scenario: It's 20 February 1965, and you're monitoring telemetry at JPL as Ranger 8 hurtles toward the lunar surface, its six cameras finally awake and streaming images back to Earth.
evt-02-20-1965-ranger-8.prompt: What should mission control do as Ranger 8 closes in on impact?

choices.text: Command the probe to fire retro-rockets and attempt a soft landing
Shut down the cameras early to preserve the spacecraft's power
Redirect Ranger 8 into a stable lunar orbit instead
Keep the cameras transmitting continuously right up until impact

evt-02-20-1965-ranger-8.butterflyEffect: Ranger 8 transmitted 7,137 images before crashing into the Sea of Tranquility as planned, its cameras running to the very last second. The photographs helped NASA scientists evaluate potential landing sites, and Apollo 11 would touch down in that very region four years later.

evt-02-20-1988-nagorno-karabakh-autonomo.scenario: You sit among the delegates of the regional assembly in Nagorno-Karabakh on February 20, 1988, as a historic vote on the oblast's future is called.
evt-02-20-1988-nagorno-karabakh-autonomo.prompt: What did the assembly vote to do that day?

choices.text: Declare full independence from the USSR
Remain part of Azerbaijan with expanded autonomy
Dissolve the autonomous oblast entirely
Secede from Azerbaijan and join Armenia

evt-02-20-1988-nagorno-karabakh-autonomo.butterflyEffect: The assembly voted to secede from Azerbaijan and join Armenia, a demand Moscow refused to grant. The vote ignited the Karabakh movement and escalating ethnic tensions that, after the Soviet collapse, erupted into full-scale war between Armenia and Azerbaijan.

evt-02-20-1998-figure-skating.scenario: It is 20 February 1998 in Nagano, and you are 15-year-old Tara Lipinski, stepping onto the ice for the free skate trailing Michelle Kwan after the short program at the Winter Olympics.
evt-02-20-1998-figure-skating.prompt: To overtake Kwan and win gold, what must Lipinski do in her free skate?

choices.text: Simplify her program and rely purely on artistry for high marks
Cut the hardest jumps to guarantee a fall-free skate
Land her full set of difficult triple jump combinations cleanly
Focus mainly on spins to win over the judges on presentation

evt-02-20-1998-figure-skating.butterflyEffect: Lipinski skated a technically loaded program, cleanly landing seven triple jumps including a triple loop-triple loop combination, and edged out Kwan for gold. At 15, she became the youngest woman to win an Olympic figure skating title at the time, a result that pushed the ladies' discipline toward ever greater technical difficulty.

evt-02-20-1998-tara-lipinski.scenario: It's 20 February 1998 in Nagano, and you are fifteen-year-old Tara Lipinski, stepping onto the ice for the free skate trailing rival Michelle Kwan in the Olympic standings.
evt-02-20-1998-tara-lipinski.prompt: What should you attempt to overtake Kwan and win gold?

choices.text: Ask officials to delay her performance to later in the event
Skip jumps entirely and focus purely on artistic presentation
Attempt the difficult triple loop–triple loop combination
Simplify the program to minimize any risk of falling

evt-02-20-1998-tara-lipinski.butterflyEffect: Lipinski landed a triple loop–triple loop combination, her signature move, skating a clean, technically demanding program that overtook Kwan for the gold. At fifteen, she became the youngest women's singles figure skating Olympic champion in history, then turned professional soon after, reshaping debates over age and difficulty in the sport.

evt-02-20-2003-great-white.scenario: It is the night of 20 February 2003 inside a packed nightclub in West Warwick, Rhode Island, where the band Great White is about to take the stage and a tour manager readies a pyrotechnic display for the opening song.
evt-02-20-2003-great-white.prompt: What fatal decision sets the tragedy in motion?

choices.text: A cigarette left burning backstage ignites stage curtains
Pyrotechnics are set off indoors near flammable foam insulation
A kitchen grease fire spreads unnoticed into the main room
Faulty wiring in the DJ booth sparks the blaze

evt-02-20-2003-great-white.butterflyEffect: The tour manager ignited indoor pyrotechnics that ignited flammable soundproofing foam lining the club's walls, and the fire spread within minutes, killing 100 people. The disaster led to sweeping reforms in fire codes, pyrotechnic regulation, and crowd-safety enforcement in entertainment venues across the United States.

evt-02-20-2005-2005-spanish-european-con.scenario: It is 20 February 2005, and you stand in a polling booth in Madrid holding a ballot asking whether Spain should approve the Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe.
evt-02-20-2005-2005-spanish-european-con.prompt: What do Spanish voters overwhelmingly decide?

choices.text: Split almost evenly for and against
Reject the treaty narrowly
Approve the treaty by an overwhelming margin
Boycott the vote in large numbers, invalidating it

evt-02-20-2005-2005-spanish-european-con.butterflyEffect: Spain approved the Constitution with 81.8% support, though turnout was a low 41.8%. The celebration proved premature: French and Dutch voters rejected the treaty later that year, killing it outright, and the EU had to negotiate the scaled-back Lisbon Treaty in 2007 instead.

evt-02-20-2009-2009-suicide-air-raid-on-.scenario: You are a Sri Lankan air force officer on February 20, 2009, scrambling as two light aircraft laden with explosives approach Colombo in an apparent suicide raid.
evt-02-20-2009-2009-suicide-air-raid-on-.prompt: What must you do to stop the attackers from reaching their targets?

choices.text: Ground all military aircraft to avoid escalation
Open the runway to negotiate with the pilots
Intercept and shoot down the aircraft
Wait until the aircraft land to respond

evt-02-20-2009-2009-suicide-air-raid-on-.butterflyEffect: The air force shot down both aircraft before they could strike their intended military targets, though one crashed into a government building, killing two people, with over 50 injured overall. The failed raid was among the Tamil Tigers' last major operations before their military defeat just months later in May 2009.

evt-02-20-2010-2010-madeira-floods-and-m.scenario: It is the morning of February 20, 2010, and torrential rain is triggering flash floods and mudslides across the island of Madeira. You are a local official watching hillside neighborhoods and roads begin to give way.
evt-02-20-2010-2010-madeira-floods-and-m.prompt: What should authorities prioritize immediately to limit further loss of life?

choices.text: Wait until the rain stops before responding
Keep all roads open to avoid disrupting traffic
Delay warnings until damage is confirmed
Evacuate low-lying and hillside areas at once

evt-02-20-2010-2010-madeira-floods-and-m.butterflyEffect: The floods and mudslides killed 51 people and left around 600 homeless before the day was over. The disaster pushed Portuguese authorities to invest in stronger flood defenses and early-warning systems for its outlying Atlantic territories.

evt-02-20-2014-euromaidan.scenario: It is 20 February 2014, and you are standing with thousands of demonstrators on Kyiv's Maidan square as gunfire suddenly erupts from surrounding rooftops, cutting down protesters around you.
evt-02-20-2014-euromaidan.prompt: As security forces open fire on the crowd, what do the protesters do?

choices.text: Storm the presidential administration building in retaliation
Call for Russian troops to intervene and restore order
Disperse entirely from the square to avoid more casualties
Hold their ground on the square while documenting the violence for the world to see

evt-02-20-2014-euromaidan.butterflyEffect: Despite the killings, protesters held Maidan and images of the violence spread worldwide, intensifying condemnation of President Yanukovych's government. Within days he fled to Russia, parliament voted to remove him, and the ensuing Revolution of Dignity set in motion Russia's annexation of Crimea and the war in the Donbas.

evt-02-21-1437-james-i-of-scotland.scenario: You are inside Blackfriars monastery in Perth on the night of 21 February 1437, attending King James I of Scotland. Armed men led by his own uncle, Walter Stewart, Earl of Atholl, have broken into the building, and the king is desperately looking for somewhere to hide.
evt-02-21-1437-james-i-of-scotland.prompt: Where does James I try to conceal himself from the assassins?

choices.text: In the monastery's bell tower
Disguised among the monks in the chapel
In a drain beneath the floor, whose outlet he had ordered blocked days earlier
Aboard a boat moored on the River Tay

evt-02-21-1437-james-i-of-scotland.butterflyEffect: The drain's outlet had been blocked only days earlier because tennis balls kept vanishing into it, trapping the king inside where his attackers found and stabbed him to death. The conspirators were later captured and gruesomely executed, and the crown passed to his six-year-old son James II, beginning decades of minority rule and noble faction-fighting in Scotland.

evt-02-21-1746-jacobite-rising-of-1745.scenario: It is February 1746. The Jacobite army has surrounded Inverness, held by a small garrison loyal to King George II. Your commander weighs whether to hold the town or give it up before the rebels storm the walls.
evt-02-21-1746-jacobite-rising-of-1745.prompt: What happens to the government garrison holding Inverness?

choices.text: The garrison surrenders the town to the Jacobites
The garrison fights to the last man rather than yield
The garrison abandons the town without a fight before the Jacobites arrive
Government reinforcements arrive and relieve the siege

evt-02-21-1746-jacobite-rising-of-1745.butterflyEffect: The garrison surrendered and the Jacobites briefly held Inverness, their last significant success of the rising. Barely two months later, the government army crushed the Jacobites at Culloden in April 1746, ending the rebellion and the Stuart cause as a serious threat to the British throne.
