evt-02-21-1866-lucy-hobbs-taylor.scenario: It is February 1866. You have practiced dentistry for years despite being turned away from dental schools because you are a woman, and the Ohio College of Dental Surgery has finally agreed to examine your qualifications for a degree.
evt-02-21-1866-lucy-hobbs-taylor.prompt: What happens when the college reviews your case?

choices.text: She is told to complete another unpaid apprenticeship first
Her application is rejected a second time
She is granted a formal dental degree, becoming the first woman to earn one
She is offered an honorary certificate but no real degree

evt-02-21-1866-lucy-hobbs-taylor.butterflyEffect: Lucy Hobbs Taylor became the first woman to earn a doctorate from a dental college, receiving her degree from the Ohio College of Dental Surgery. Her breakthrough opened dental education to women, and she went on to practice and mentor other aspiring female dentists in Chicago and Kansas.

evt-02-21-1919-bavaria.scenario: It is 21 February 1919 in Munich. You watch Bavarian Minister-President Kurt Eisner, who led the revolution that toppled the Wittelsbach monarchy months earlier, walk toward the state parliament to announce his resignation after a crushing election defeat.
evt-02-21-1919-bavaria.prompt: What happens to Eisner on his way to deliver his resignation speech?

choices.text: He is assassinated by a right-wing nationalist army officer
He is arrested by conservative deputies before reaching the chamber
He flees to Berlin rather than face parliament
He delivers his resignation speech safely and retires from politics

evt-02-21-1919-bavaria.butterflyEffect: A young nationalist officer, Anton Graf von Arco auf Valley, shot Eisner dead in the street. The killing plunged Bavaria into chaos, radicalized the revolutionary left, and within weeks helped trigger the short-lived Bavarian Soviet Republic, whose bloody suppression by Freikorps troops later fed the far-right politics that took root in Munich.

evt-02-21-1947-edwin-h-land.scenario: You're seated among scientists at the Optical Society of America meeting in New York, 1947, as Edwin Land holds up a camera and, minutes later, a finished photograph.
evt-02-21-1947-edwin-h-land.prompt: What did Land's instant camera go on to do in the following years?

choices.text: It still required a full darkroom visit to finish developing
Kodak's existing patents blocked it from ever reaching the market
It flopped commercially and was quietly discontinued within a year
It went on sale in 1948 as the Polaroid camera, launching instant photography

evt-02-21-1947-edwin-h-land.butterflyEffect: The Polaroid Land Camera went on sale to the public in 1948, letting anyone develop a photo in under a minute without a darkroom. It launched an instant-photography industry that Polaroid would dominate for decades, and later triggered a landmark patent battle with Kodak in the 1980s.

evt-02-21-1952-bengali-language-movement.scenario: You are a student marching toward the University of Dhaka on 21 February 1952, defying a government ban on gatherings, to demand that Bengali be recognized as a state language of Pakistan.
evt-02-21-1952-bengali-language-movement.prompt: What happens as the march reaches the area near the university and assembly?

choices.text: Authorities allow the students to disperse without incident
The government immediately grants Bengali official status
Police open fire on the crowd, killing several protesting students
The march is called off before it reaches the campus

evt-02-21-1952-bengali-language-movement.butterflyEffect: Police opened fire on the demonstrators, killing several students. The deaths galvanized Bengali nationalism across East Pakistan, Bengali was made an official language in 1956, and the date is now observed worldwide as International Mother Language Day.

evt-02-21-1971-convention-on-psychotropi.scenario: You're a delegate in Vienna in 1971, where nations are negotiating whether international drug law, until now focused on opium, coca, and cannabis, should also cover the amphetamines, barbiturates, and psychedelics now spreading worldwide.
evt-02-21-1971-convention-on-psychotropi.prompt: What do the delegates agree to bring under international control?

choices.text: Alcohol and tobacco alongside existing narcotics
Psychotropic drugs such as amphetamines, barbiturates, and LSD
Only cannabis, extending the 1961 treaty's scope
Caffeine and nicotine as newly regulated stimulants

evt-02-21-1971-convention-on-psychotropi.butterflyEffect: The convention extended UN drug regulation to synthetic stimulants, sedatives, and hallucinogens like LSD, closing a gap left by the 1961 Single Convention. It became a foundation for national drug-scheduling laws still in use today, shaping decades of policy on prescription and recreational psychoactive substances.

evt-02-21-1973-sinai-peninsula.scenario: You are the pilot of Libyan Arab Airlines Flight 114, a Boeing 727 blown off course by a sandstorm on 21 February 1973. Israeli fighter jets have intercepted you over the Israeli-occupied Sinai Peninsula and are firing warning shots, signaling you to land at a nearby airbase.
evt-02-21-1973-sinai-peninsula.prompt: How does the crew respond to the Israeli fighters' warning shots?

choices.text: He lands immediately at the Israeli airbase as signaled
He ejects flares and continues straight ahead toward the Suez Canal
He turns the aircraft away and attempts to fly back toward Egyptian airspace
He radios Cairo tower and waits for instructions before moving

evt-02-21-1973-sinai-peninsula.butterflyEffect: The pilot banked away and tried to climb back toward Egyptian airspace rather than land; the Israeli jets then fired on the fuselage, and the plane crashed, killing 108 of the 113 aboard. The shootdown, one of the deadliest civilian aviation incidents of its time, drew international condemnation and deepened Arab-Israeli hostility just months before the Yom Kippur War.

evt-02-21-1974-suez-canal.scenario: You are an Israeli soldier holding a position on the west bank of the Suez Canal, weeks after the Yom Kippur War, as UN observers move in to enforce a new disengagement agreement.
evt-02-21-1974-suez-canal.prompt: What follows as Israeli forces complete their withdrawal from the canal's west bank?

choices.text: Israel formally annexes the west bank of the canal
Egypt regains the canal zone and works toward reopening it to shipping
Egypt cedes all claims to the Sinai Peninsula outright
Fighting resumes within days along the ceasefire line

evt-02-21-1974-suez-canal.butterflyEffect: This was the first Sinai disengagement, brokered by Henry Kissinger's shuttle diplomacy after the 1973 war. Egypt reasserted control of the canal zone, cleared it of wreckage, and reopened the Suez Canal to shipping in 1975 for the first time since 1967, a step on the road to the 1979 Egypt-Israel peace treaty.

evt-02-21-1975-watergate-scandal.scenario: You sit in Judge John Sirica's Washington courtroom as he prepares to pronounce sentence on former Attorney General John Mitchell and Nixon's top aides, convicted for their roles in the Watergate cover-up.
evt-02-21-1975-watergate-scandal.prompt: What sentence does Sirica hand down to Mitchell and his co-defendants?

choices.text: They receive fines but no prison time
Prison terms of several years for the men convicted in the cover-up
President Ford pardons them before sentencing can occur
They are acquitted after the jury finds insufficient evidence

evt-02-21-1975-watergate-scandal.butterflyEffect: Mitchell, H.R. Haldeman, and John Ehrlichman received prison sentences of roughly two and a half to eight years, though terms were later reduced on appeal. Nixon himself avoided trial after Gerald Ford's September 1974 pardon, leaving his top aides to bear the legal consequences of the cover-up he had directed.

evt-02-21-1994-aldrich-ames.scenario: It is February 21, 1994. You are an FBI counterintelligence officer who has spent nearly a decade quietly building a case against a CIA officer suspected of selling secrets to Moscow. Today you finally have enough evidence to act.
evt-02-21-1994-aldrich-ames.prompt: What do you do with your suspect, Aldrich Ames?

choices.text: Arrest him near his home in Arlington County
Quietly transfer him to a desk with no classified access instead of arresting him
Confront him openly inside CIA headquarters
Delay the arrest to gather more evidence first

evt-02-21-1994-aldrich-ames.butterflyEffect: Ames was arrested near his Arlington home and later pleaded guilty to espionage, receiving a life sentence without parole. His betrayal had exposed numerous US assets to the Soviets and Russians, and the case pushed the CIA and FBI to overhaul counterintelligence cooperation and internal security screening.

evt-02-21-1995-steve-fossett.scenario: You are Steve Fossett, alone in a helium balloon's gondola, having drifted across the entire Pacific Ocean, as the flat expanse of the Canadian prairie finally comes into view below.
evt-02-21-1995-steve-fossett.prompt: What record does Fossett complete when he sets down near Leader, Saskatchewan?

choices.text: The first solo nonstop flight around the world in a fixed-wing plane
The first solo nonstop balloon crossing of the Pacific Ocean
The first solo nonstop balloon crossing of the Atlantic
The first solo balloon circumnavigation of the entire globe

evt-02-21-1995-steve-fossett.butterflyEffect: Fossett became the first person to fly a balloon solo nonstop across the Pacific Ocean. The flight was one of several endurance records he chased before finally achieving the first solo balloon circumnavigation of the globe in 2002.

evt-02-21-2013-2013-hyderabad-blasts.scenario: You are a shopkeeper in Hyderabad's crowded Dilsukhnagar market on the evening of 21 February 2013, moments after two bombs explode within a hundred metres of each other, killing and injuring dozens of shoppers and diners.
evt-02-21-2013-2013-hyderabad-blasts.prompt: Which group is later held responsible for the Dilsukhnagar bombings?

choices.text: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam
The Indian Mujahideen
Naxalite insurgents
Lashkar-e-Taiba

evt-02-21-2013-2013-hyderabad-blasts.butterflyEffect: Investigators traced the attack to the Indian Mujahideen network. In December 2016 five men, including co-founder Yasin Bhatkal, were sentenced to death for the bombings, a sentence the Telangana High Court upheld in 2025, and the case intensified India's crackdown on homegrown jihadist cells in the years that followed.

evt-02-21-2022-prelude-to-the-2022-russi.scenario: It is the evening of 21 February 2022 in Moscow. You watch a lengthy televised address by President Vladimir Putin, delivered as tens of thousands of Russian troops sit massed along Ukraine's borders, in which he questions Ukraine's very legitimacy as a nation.
evt-02-21-2022-prelude-to-the-2022-russi.prompt: What announcement does Putin make at the close of this address?

choices.text: He calls for UN-mediated negotiations over Crimea
He declares an immediate ceasefire and opens talks with Kyiv
He recognizes the independence of the Donetsk and Luhansk 'people's republics'
He announces a full withdrawal of troops from the border

evt-02-21-2022-prelude-to-the-2022-russi.butterflyEffect: Putin recognized the independence of the self-declared Donetsk and Luhansk 'people's republics' and ordered Russian troops into eastern Ukraine as 'peacekeepers.' Three days later, on 24 February, Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

evt-02-22-1371-robert-ii-of-scotland.scenario: It is 22 February 1371 in Scotland. Your uncle, King David II, has died childless, and as the son of Marjorie, daughter of Robert the Bruce, you are next in line for the throne.
evt-02-22-1371-robert-ii-of-scotland.prompt: What happens to the Scottish crown?

choices.text: The nobles choose an English claimant instead
You are crowned Robert II, founding the House of Stewart
Civil war breaks out over the succession
The throne passes to a distant Bruce cousin

evt-02-22-1371-robert-ii-of-scotland.butterflyEffect: Robert Stewart was crowned Robert II, becoming the first monarch of the House of Stewart. His dynasty would go on to rule Scotland, and later England and Scotland together, for more than three centuries until Queen Anne's death in 1714.

evt-02-22-1744-war-of-the-austrian-succe.scenario: It is 22 February 1744 off the coast of Toulon. You serve aboard a British warship as Admiral Mathews signals an attack on the trailing ships of a combined French-Spanish fleet, but the British line of battle is falling into confusion.
evt-02-22-1744-war-of-the-austrian-succe.prompt: What followed this disorganized British attack at the Battle of Toulon?

choices.text: A decisive British victory that captured the entire enemy fleet
Courts-martial of senior British officers over the botched engagement
An immediate French surrender that ended the war
A mutiny among British sailors that sank several ships

evt-02-22-1744-war-of-the-austrian-succe.butterflyEffect: The muddled, uncoordinated assault let much of the enemy fleet escape, and the scandal triggered bitter courts-martial of British admirals Mathews and Lestock over their conduct. The controversy exposed weaknesses in Royal Navy signaling and discipline, driving reforms to fleet tactics later in the century.

evt-02-22-1979-saint-lucia.scenario: It is February 22, 1979, and you stand in a crowd in Castries as the Union Jack is lowered for the last time and Saint Lucia's new flag rises over the island for the first time.
evt-02-22-1979-saint-lucia.prompt: What constitutional arrangement does newly independent Saint Lucia adopt?

choices.text: It joins a new federation with neighbouring islands
It becomes a full republic with an elected president
It remains a British overseas territory with limited self-rule
It becomes independent within the Commonwealth, keeping the British monarch as head of state

evt-02-22-1979-saint-lucia.butterflyEffect: Saint Lucia became an independent Commonwealth realm, keeping the British monarch as ceremonial head of state while John Compton served as its first prime minister. The island remains a Commonwealth realm to this day, one of several small Caribbean nations to take this path to independence.

evt-02-22-1980-miracle-on-ice.scenario: It is February 22, 1980, in Lake Placid, and you are one of Herb Brooks's young amateur players facing the mighty, heavily favored Soviet squad in the Olympic medal round, the score locked at 3-3 entering the third period.
evt-02-22-1980-miracle-on-ice.prompt: What does Team USA do to complete the historic upset?

choices.text: Force overtime and win it in a shootout
Settle for a tie against the Soviets
Fall behind again and lose a close game
Score the go-ahead goal early in the third and hold on for a 4-3 win

evt-02-22-1980-miracle-on-ice.butterflyEffect: Mike Eruzione scored the go-ahead goal early in the third period, and the Americans held on to win 4-3, one of the greatest upsets in sports history. The U.S. clinched Olympic gold two days later, and the game became an enduring symbol of Cold War-era American morale.

evt-02-22-1983-broadway-theatre.scenario: You take your seat at a Broadway theatre on the evening of 22 February 1983 for the opening of a new comedy, Moose Murders. By intermission, walkouts have already begun.
evt-02-22-1983-broadway-theatre.prompt: What happened to Moose Murders after its disastrous opening night?

choices.text: It closed permanently after its one and only performance
It was rewritten and reopened successfully weeks later
It ran for a modest run before folding quietly
It transferred to a smaller off-Broadway venue

evt-02-22-1983-broadway-theatre.butterflyEffect: The producers closed Moose Murders after just that single performance, and it became legendary as the gold standard for Broadway flops. For decades afterward, critics and insiders invoked 'Have you seen Moose Murders?' as shorthand for a catastrophically bad production.

evt-02-22-1994-aldrich-ames.scenario: You are a Justice Department prosecutor in early 1994, having just charged CIA officer Aldrich Ames and his wife Rosario with espionage after years of investigation into a devastating mole inside the agency.
evt-02-22-1994-aldrich-ames.prompt: How does the Ames case actually conclude in court?

choices.text: He is quietly exchanged for an American held in Moscow
He is acquitted after a lengthy jury trial
He pleads guilty and is sentenced to life in prison without parole
He is convicted and sentenced to death

evt-02-22-1994-aldrich-ames.butterflyEffect: Ames pleaded guilty and received life imprisonment without parole, while Rosario received a reduced sentence for cooperating. His betrayal had exposed dozens of U.S. assets in the USSR, several of whom were executed, prompting sweeping reforms to CIA counterintelligence and internal security procedures.

evt-02-22-1995-corona-satellite.scenario: You are a CIA technician awaiting the return of a Discoverer satellite's film capsule from orbit over the Pacific in the early 1960s. The capsule is falling toward the ocean and must be secured before it sinks or is spotted by Soviet ships.
evt-02-22-1995-corona-satellite.prompt: How is the returning film capsule actually recovered?

choices.text: Its data is beamed down by laser before the capsule is abandoned
An aircraft catches the parachute in mid-air before it reaches the water
A Navy ship locates it by radio beacon and hauls it aboard after splashdown
It parachutes onto a marked recovery zone in the Colorado desert

evt-02-22-1995-corona-satellite.butterflyEffect: A specially modified C-119 'Flying Boxcar' aircraft snagged the capsule's parachute in mid-air, a method that became standard for CORONA missions. Reliable mid-air recovery let the CIA repeatedly retrieve high-resolution film of Soviet military sites, giving the U.S. its first systematic satellite intelligence on the USSR's missile and bomber forces.

evt-02-22-1997-roslin-institute.scenario: You are a lab technician at the Roslin Institute in 1997, watching journalists scribble down the name of the world's most famous sheep. Someone asks why she was called 'Dolly' rather than a lab code number.
evt-02-22-1997-roslin-institute.prompt: Why did researchers choose the name Dolly for the cloned lamb?

choices.text: As an acronym for the cloning technique used
After the institute director's pet sheep
After a popular 1990s cartoon character
After Dolly Parton, since the donor cell came from a mammary gland

evt-02-22-1997-roslin-institute.butterflyEffect: Dolly was named after Dolly Parton because she was cloned from a mammary gland cell — a playful nod that became instantly iconic. The Institute's fame from this single sheep drew global funding and scrutiny to Edinburgh, cementing Scotland's role in the ensuing biotech and stem-cell research boom.

evt-02-22-1997-roslin-midlothian.scenario: It is 22 February 1997, and you are a reporter crowding into a press conference near this quiet Scottish village. Scientists are about to reveal something that will change biology forever: a sheep cloned from an adult cell.
evt-02-22-1997-roslin-midlothian.prompt: What breakthrough did the scientists announce that day?

choices.text: The invention of a new in-vitro fertilization technique for livestock
The discovery of a new sheep breed resistant to disease
The first successful sheep-to-human organ transplant
The successful cloning of an adult mammal from a single somatic cell

evt-02-22-1997-roslin-midlothian.butterflyEffect: The announcement revealed Dolly the sheep, cloned from an adult mammary cell rather than an embryo, proving adult cells could be reprogrammed. It ignited worldwide ethical debates on cloning, prompted many nations to ban human cloning research, and helped launch the field of regenerative stem cell science.

evt-02-22-1998-cherry-throated-tanager.scenario: It is February 1998, and you are exploring a private fazenda in Brazil's Espírito Santo state when you glimpse a small songbird with a distinctive cherry-red throat — a pattern matching a species not confirmed alive since 1870.
evt-02-22-1998-cherry-throated-tanager.prompt: What should you do with this extraordinary sighting?

choices.text: Document it carefully and report it to ornithologists for verification
Capture the bird for a private collection as proof
Announce the rediscovery publicly without any verification
Assume it is a common tanager and continue on your way

evt-02-22-1998-cherry-throated-tanager.butterflyEffect: The sighting was documented and confirmed by ornithologists, rediscovering the cherry-throated tanager after more than a century presumed extinct. It sparked targeted conservation efforts, though by 2023 fewer than 50 individuals were known to survive, threatened by continued destruction of Atlantic Forest habitat.

evt-02-22-2002-angola.scenario: It is February 22, 2002, in the remote bush of Moxico province, Angola. Government troops have finally cornered the convoy of UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi after decades of guerrilla war, and gunfire erupts around his vehicle.
evt-02-22-2002-angola.prompt: What happens to Savimbi in this ambush?

choices.text: He negotiates an immediate ceasefire with the soldiers
He is killed in the firefight
He escapes across the border into Zambia
He is captured alive and put on trial in Luanda

evt-02-22-2002-angola.butterflyEffect: Savimbi was killed in the firefight, ending his 27-year insurgency. Within weeks UNITA's remaining commanders signed the Luena Memorandum of Understanding, finally ending Angola's brutal civil war after nearly three decades.

evt-02-22-2006-securitas-depot-robbery.scenario: It is the early hours of 22 February 2006 at a Securitas depot in Tonbridge, England. You and six accomplices, having kidnapped the depot manager's family the night before to force his cooperation, now stand before far more cash than your vehicles can hold.
evt-02-22-2006-securitas-depot-robbery.prompt: What do you do with the money you cannot carry away?

choices.text: Force staff to help load a second convoy
Burn it to destroy evidence
Leave it behind and escape with what you can carry
Return the next night with more vehicles

evt-02-22-2006-securitas-depot-robbery.butterflyEffect: The gang left roughly £154 million behind, escaping with almost £53 million — still Britain's largest cash robbery. Most of the crew were later caught and convicted, only a fraction of the stolen cash was ever recovered, and cash-handling depots across the UK tightened security procedures afterward.

evt-02-22-2011-2011-christchurch-earthqu.scenario: It is 12:51 p.m. on February 22, 2011, and you are working in an office in downtown Christchurch when the ground lurches violently — far more destructive than the larger quake that struck the region the previous September.
evt-02-22-2011-2011-christchurch-earthqu.prompt: Why did this smaller-magnitude quake devastate the city so much more severely?

choices.text: It triggered a tsunami that flooded the central city
It registered a much higher magnitude than the September 2010 quake
Its epicentre was far closer to, and shallower beneath, the city centre
It struck late at night when buildings were structurally weaker

evt-02-22-2011-2011-christchurch-earthqu.butterflyEffect: The quake's epicentre was only a few kilometres from the CBD and unusually shallow, concentrating its force directly beneath the city. The devastation led to the demolition of much of central Christchurch and a decade-long, still-ongoing rebuild with stricter seismic building codes.

evt-02-22-2012-2012-buenos-aires-rail-di.scenario: It is the morning rush hour of 22 February 2012, and you stand packed among commuters on a train approaching Once Station in Buenos Aires as it fails to slow for the final stop.
evt-02-22-2012-2012-buenos-aires-rail-di.prompt: What caused the train to crash through the buffer stop at Once Station?

choices.text: A brake failure caused by long-neglected mechanical maintenance
A signal malfunction sent the train onto the wrong track
The driver fell asleep at the controls
Sabotage by striking rail workers

evt-02-22-2012-2012-buenos-aires-rail-di.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the train's brakes had failed due to years of poor maintenance on Argentina's state-subsidized rail network. The tragedy exposed chronic underinvestment in the system, led to criminal prosecutions of transport officials and rail operators, and pushed the government toward long-delayed infrastructure modernization.

evt-02-22-2014-viktor-yanukovych.scenario: It is February 22, 2014, in Kyiv. The Verkhovna Rada votes overwhelmingly to remove President Viktor Yanukovych from office after months of Euromaidan protests and deadly clashes in the capital.
evt-02-22-2014-viktor-yanukovych.prompt: What does Yanukovych do as the Rada moves to strip him of power?

choices.text: He appeals the vote before Ukraine's Constitutional Court
He flees the country and takes refuge in Russia
He orders the military to suppress the Rada's vote
He resigns voluntarily and remains in Ukraine

evt-02-22-2014-viktor-yanukovych.butterflyEffect: Yanukovych fled Kyiv and ultimately took refuge in Russia, where he has lived in exile ever since. His fall, known as the Revolution of Dignity, was quickly followed by Russia's annexation of Crimea and the outbreak of conflict in eastern Ukraine.

evt-02-22-2015-sinking-of-ml-mostofa-3.scenario: It is the evening of 22 February 2015, and you are aboard a crowded two-deck ferry making its way along the Padma River toward Dhaka as darkness falls over the water.
evt-02-22-2015-sinking-of-ml-mostofa-3.prompt: What caused the ferry to capsize that night?

choices.text: An onboard fire forced passengers to abandon ship
It ran aground on a sandbar during low tide
A sudden storm overturned the vessel
It collided with a trawler on the river and capsized

evt-02-22-2015-sinking-of-ml-mostofa-3.butterflyEffect: The ferry collided with a trawler on the river and capsized, killing around 70 people. The disaster renewed criticism of overcrowding and lax safety enforcement on Bangladesh's crowded inland waterways, though similar accidents continued in the years after.

evt-02-22-2018-2018-united-states-embass.scenario: It is just before midnight on 22 February 2018 outside the closed U.S. embassy in Podgorica, Montenegro. You are a Serbian-born man who has just hurled a grenade into the embassy compound, and you now stand alone in the dark holding a second explosive device.
evt-02-22-2018-2018-united-states-embass.prompt: What does the attacker do next?

choices.text: Flees into the night and evades capture
Detonates the second explosive on himself
Surrenders to embassy security
Storms the embassy building

evt-02-22-2018-2018-united-states-embass.butterflyEffect: He detonated the second device on himself, killing only himself; the embassy was empty and no one else was hurt. Montenegro, a new NATO member deeply at odds with Russia over the alliance, treated the attack as a serious security threat, though Russian authorities denied any involvement.

evt-02-22-2019-north-korean-embassy-in-m.scenario: It is February 22, 2019, weeks before the planned Hanoi summit between Kim Jong Un and Donald Trump. You are part of a group with ties to North Korean dissidents who have just gained entry to the North Korean embassy in Madrid.
evt-02-22-2019-north-korean-embassy-in-m.prompt: What do you do once inside the embassy?

choices.text: Wait calmly for Spanish police to arrive and mediate
Destroy the embassy's paper records before leaving
Take electronic devices and documents to hand over to the FBI
Publicly announce a high-level defection to the press

evt-02-22-2019-north-korean-embassy-in-m.butterflyEffect: The group, later identified as Free Joseon, took phones, USB drives and a hard drive and handed them to the FBI in the United States. Spanish prosecutors accused several participants of assault and issued international arrest warrants, and the episode stirred diplomatic friction just before the Hanoi summit collapsed.

evt-02-23-1778-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: You are a Continental Army soldier shivering through the winter of 1778 at Valley Forge, when a Prussian officer named Friedrich Wilhelm von Steuben arrives, unable to speak much English but determined to reshape how you fight.
evt-02-23-1778-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What does von Steuben introduce that transforms the army over this winter?

choices.text: Heavy cavalry tactics modeled on Prussian dragoons
Standardized drill, weapons handling, and camp sanitation practices
A diplomatic plan to secure French recognition of independence
A new naval blockade strategy against British supply ships

evt-02-23-1778-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Von Steuben drilled the troops in standardized formations, weapons handling, and camp sanitation, writing a training manual used long after the war. The newly disciplined Continental Army that emerged from Valley Forge performed far better against British regulars, helping set up the eventual victory at Yorktown in 1781.

evt-02-23-1847-mexican-american-war.scenario: It's 23 February 1847, and you command an artillery battery under General Zachary Taylor at Buena Vista, watching Santa Anna's much larger Mexican army advance through the mountain pass.
evt-02-23-1847-mexican-american-war.prompt: How do you hold this position against overwhelming numbers?

choices.text: Withdraw the artillery and retreat to a defensible town
Mass your guns and fire canister shot into the advancing lines at close range
Order a full cavalry charge to break the enemy formation
Send an officer to negotiate a truce with Santa Anna

evt-02-23-1847-mexican-american-war.butterflyEffect: Taylor's artillery, firing canister at close range, shattered repeated Mexican assaults and won the battle despite being badly outnumbered. The victory made Taylor a national hero, propelling him to the U.S. presidency in 1848, while the defeat weakened Santa Anna's standing in Mexico.

evt-02-23-1886-charles-martin-hall.scenario: You are a 22-year-old chemist working in a homemade woodshed laboratory in Ohio, dissolving aluminum oxide in molten cryolite and passing an electric current through it, chasing a cheap way to produce a metal that currently costs more than silver.
evt-02-23-1886-charles-martin-hall.prompt: What method do you perfect to make aluminum affordable for the first time?

choices.text: Electrolysis of alumina dissolved in molten cryolite
Chemical reduction of alumina using sodium metal
Refining bauxite into alumina with caustic soda
Distilling bauxite ore at high temperature

evt-02-23-1886-charles-martin-hall.butterflyEffect: Hall's electrolytic process—dissolving alumina in molten cryolite and running current through it—became the Hall–Héroult process, still the basis of aluminum production today. It turned aluminum from a precious novelty into a cheap industrial metal, funded the company that became Alcoa, and reshaped aviation, packaging, and construction for the next century.

evt-02-23-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: You are a navigator aboard an RAF Lancaster on the night of 23 February 1945, part of a force converging on the German town of Pforzheim using a tightly concentrated marking and bombing pattern designed to overwhelm the town in minutes.
evt-02-23-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What tactic does Bomber Command use against Pforzheim that night?

choices.text: A concentrated incendiary raid packed into a short time window
A daylight precision strike on rail yards only
A slow, spread-out campaign over several nights
A diversionary raid meant to draw fighters from Berlin

evt-02-23-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The raid compressed hundreds of bombers into a narrow window, igniting a firestorm that killed a very high proportion of the town's population in a single night. Coming so soon after Dresden, it became one of the events most cited in the postwar debate over the morality and necessity of area bombing German cities late in the war.

evt-02-23-1945-joe-rosenthal.scenario: It is 23 February 1945, and you are AP photographer Joe Rosenthal climbing Mount Suribachi on Iwo Jima. You round the summit just as a group of Marines swings a larger flag up onto a makeshift pole to replace the first one already raised.
evt-02-23-1945-joe-rosenthal.prompt: With only seconds to react, what do you do to capture the shot?

choices.text: Snap the shot instantly without framing it perfectly
Wait for better afternoon light before shooting
Set up a tripod for a steadier long exposure
Ask the Marines to pause and pose formally

evt-02-23-1945-joe-rosenthal.butterflyEffect: Rosenthal swung his camera up and fired without even looking through the viewfinder, catching six Marines heaving the pole upright in one fluid motion. The image, published within days, won the Pulitzer Prize, became the most reproduced photograph in history, fueled a war bond drive, and was later cast in bronze as the Marine Corps War Memorial in Arlington.

evt-02-23-1971-vietnam-war.scenario: You are a staff officer at III Corps headquarters in South Vietnam, awaiting the arrival of General Đỗ Cao Trí, the aggressive commander overseeing ARVN operations pushing into Cambodia. His helicopter is due to land near Tây Ninh.
evt-02-23-1971-vietnam-war.prompt: What happens to General Trí's helicopter on this flight?

choices.text: It crashes, killing the general
It is diverted due to enemy anti-aircraft fire
It is grounded by mechanical trouble before takeoff
It lands safely and the inspection proceeds as planned

evt-02-23-1971-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: Trí's helicopter crashed near Tây Ninh, killing him instantly. He had been one of South Vietnam's most capable and aggressive field commanders, and his death was widely seen as a serious loss of leadership for ARVN's offensive operations into Cambodia at a critical stage of the war.

evt-02-23-1987-sn-1987a.scenario: It's the night of 23 February 1987, and you are an astronomer at Las Campanas Observatory in Chile, scanning photographic plates of the Large Magellanic Cloud.
evt-02-23-1987-sn-1987a.prompt: What do you spot that becomes the astronomical event of the decade?

choices.text: A previously unknown comet entering the inner solar system
A new star blazing where none had been before—a supernova
A nova flaring up within the Milky Way itself
An artificial satellite reflecting sunlight unusually brightly

evt-02-23-1987-sn-1987a.butterflyEffect: Ian Shelton's naked-eye discovery was the closest supernova seen since 1604. Hours earlier, detectors in Japan, the US, and the USSR had already caught a burst of neutrinos from the same explosion, confirming theories of core-collapse supernovae and launching the era of neutrino astronomy.

evt-02-23-1998-1998-central-florida-torn.scenario: You are an emergency manager on duty overnight in Central Florida on February 22–23, 1998, watching radar as a violent storm complex races along the I-4 corridor while most residents are asleep in their homes.
evt-02-23-1998-1998-central-florida-torn.prompt: What is the most urgent step you take to protect people before the tornadoes strike?

choices.text: Delay action until the National Weather Service issues a formal report
Rely solely on outdoor sirens to alert residents
Wait until daylight to confirm the tornadoes visually
Push out immediate warnings through broadcast and weather radio

evt-02-23-1998-1998-central-florida-torn.butterflyEffect: Because the tornadoes struck after midnight, many residents had no warning before their homes were destroyed, and the outbreak became the deadliest in Florida history. The disaster pushed forecasters and emergency agencies to expand NOAA Weather Radio alerting and rethink how nighttime tornado warnings reach sleeping households.

evt-02-23-1999-avalanche.scenario: It is 23 February 1999. Heavy snowfall has already cut off every road into the Tyrolean village of Galtür, and now an enormous avalanche has just buried its centre. Thousands of stranded tourists and locals need to be moved to safety before another slide hits.
evt-02-23-1999-avalanche.prompt: As rescue coordinator, how do you get everyone out of the snow-locked valley?

choices.text: Wait for the snow to melt before moving anyone
Send snowplows to clear the mountain roads first
Call in military helicopters to airlift people out
Have everyone ski out over the passes together

evt-02-23-1999-avalanche.butterflyEffect: The Austrian military mounted a massive helicopter airlift, ferrying thousands of stranded tourists and residents out of Galtür and nearby Valzur because roads remained impassable. The disaster, part of a deadly run of Alpine avalanches that winter, pushed Austria to overhaul its hazard-zoning laws and build new protective barriers above mountain villages.

evt-02-23-2007-grayrigg-derailment.scenario: It's the evening of 23 February 2007, and an express train barrels along the West Coast Main Line toward Grayrigg, Cumbria, over points that missed their scheduled inspection five days earlier.
evt-02-23-2007-grayrigg-derailment.prompt: What did investigators later determine caused this train to derail at speed?

choices.text: A signalling error that put two trains on the same line
A faulty set of points that had missed its scheduled inspection
A landslide that had shifted the track bed
Deliberate sabotage of the track by vandals

evt-02-23-2007-grayrigg-derailment.butterflyEffect: Investigators found a faulty, unmaintained set of points at Lambrigg ground frame had failed catastrophically. One passenger was killed and dozens injured; the disaster exposed lapses in Network Rail's maintenance regime and led to tighter inspection and accountability rules across the network.

evt-02-23-2008-united-states-air-force.scenario: You are one of two pilots at the controls of a B-2 Spirit stealth bomber, 'Spirit of Kansas,' lifting off from Andersen Air Force Base on Guam. Moisture has corrupted your air data sensors, and the nose suddenly pitches up uncontrollably just after takeoff.
evt-02-23-2008-united-states-air-force.prompt: With the bomber stalling seconds after liftoff, what is the correct action?

choices.text: Eject immediately once the aircraft becomes unrecoverable
Try to level the aircraft and land it despite the stall
Radio the tower and attempt a controlled belly landing
Shut down the engines to stop the pitch-up

evt-02-23-2008-united-states-air-force.butterflyEffect: Both pilots ejected safely and the $1.4 billion aircraft was destroyed—the first B-2 ever lost. Investigators traced the crash to moisture trapped in Port Transducer Units, which fed bad airspeed data to the flight computer; the Air Force overhauled ground-handling procedures for the entire fleet to keep the sensors dry.

evt-02-23-2017-syrian-civil-war.scenario: You are a fighter with Turkish-backed Free Syrian Army factions, part of Operation Euphrates Shield, closing in on the ISIL-held town of al-Bab in Aleppo province after weeks of grinding urban combat.
evt-02-23-2017-syrian-civil-war.prompt: What is the outcome of the final assault on al-Bab?

choices.text: ISIL retains control and the assault is called off
The Turkish-led coalition captures the town
Kurdish YPG forces take the town instead
Syrian government forces seize it first

evt-02-23-2017-syrian-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Al-Bab fell to the Turkish-led coalition, marking the culmination of Operation Euphrates Shield and pushing ISIL out of a key stronghold in northern Aleppo province. The victory expanded Turkey's buffer zone in northern Syria and hardened the line separating its forces from Kurdish-led YPG territory further east.

evt-02-23-2018-2018-djiboutian-parliamen.scenario: It is February 2018, and you lead a party within Djibouti's opposition Union for National Salvation coalition. Parliamentary elections are days away, and President Guelleh's ruling coalition dominates state media and resources.
evt-02-23-2018-2018-djiboutian-parliamen.prompt: What does your coalition decide to do about the vote?

choices.text: Boycott the election in protest
Ask the African Union to postpone the vote
Merge permanently with the ruling party
Field candidates in every constituency

evt-02-23-2018-2018-djiboutian-parliamen.butterflyEffect: Most opposition parties boycotted the election, arguing conditions were unfair, leaving the ruling coalition to sweep nearly all seats unopposed. The lopsided result deepened Djibouti's one-party dominance and left the opposition with even less institutional leverage going forward.

evt-02-23-2019-atlas-air-flight-3591.scenario: You are the first officer on Atlas Air Flight 3591, descending toward Houston through cloud on 23 February 2019, when the autothrottle disengages and the aircraft suddenly pitches into an unexpected attitude.
evt-02-23-2019-atlas-air-flight-3591.prompt: What ultimately caused this Boeing 767 to crash into Trinity Bay?

choices.text: Spatial disorientation caused the first officer to push the plane into a fatal dive
Severe wind shear flipped the aircraft inverted
Both engines failed simultaneously during descent
The aircraft ran out of fuel short of the runway

evt-02-23-2019-atlas-air-flight-3591.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the first officer became spatially disoriented and mistakenly pushed the aircraft into a steep dive it never recovered from, killing all three aboard. The crash renewed scrutiny of how airlines share pilots' training-failure histories, since the first officer had a record of performance problems at prior employers.

evt-02-23-2025-2025-german-federal-elect.scenario: It's 23 February 2025, and voters across Germany head to the polls in a snap Bundestag election called seven months early after Chancellor Scholz's coalition collapsed.
evt-02-23-2025-2025-german-federal-elect.prompt: What did this snap election actually produce for Germany's government?

choices.text: The SPD retained the chancellorship under Olaf Scholz
The AfD won a plurality and led the new government
The Greens formed a coalition government without the CDU
CDU/CSU became the largest party and Friedrich Merz became chancellor

evt-02-23-2025-2025-german-federal-elect.butterflyEffect: CDU/CSU emerged as the largest party, and Friedrich Merz negotiated a coalition that made him chancellor by May 2025, ending Scholz's tenure. The election also saw the AfD post its strongest ever federal result, becoming the second-largest party and reshaping Germany's political landscape.

evt-02-24-303-diocletianic-persecution.scenario: It is 303 AD in Nicomedia. Soldiers have just torn down the great church across from the imperial palace, and a new edict from Diocletian is nailed up, stripping Christians of legal standing.
evt-02-24-303-diocletianic-persecution.prompt: What does this first edict actually demand of Christians?

choices.text: Surrender scriptures to be burned and forfeit legal rights and rank
Convert or be exiled from the empire at once
Pay a special tax to continue worshipping privately
Sacrifice to the Roman gods immediately or be executed

evt-02-24-303-diocletianic-persecution.butterflyEffect: The initial edict ordered churches destroyed, scriptures burned, and Christians stripped of legal privileges and protections—universal sacrifice was only demanded in a later edict. Enforcement varied sharply across the empire, weakest in Gaul and Britain, until Constantine's rise and the 313 Edict of Milan brought the persecution to an end.

evt-02-24-1607-claudio-monteverdi.scenario: You are a courtier at the Mantuan court on 24 February 1607, gathered with the nobility at the Accademia degli Invaghiti for the debut of Claudio Monteverdi's daring new musical drama.
evt-02-24-1607-claudio-monteverdi.prompt: What groundbreaking work is being premiered for the court tonight?

choices.text: L'incoronazione di Poppea
L'Orfeo
Dafne
Euridice

evt-02-24-1607-claudio-monteverdi.butterflyEffect: The work was L'Orfeo. Its expressive recitative and rich orchestration helped establish opera as a serious art form at court, and it survives today as the earliest opera still regularly performed.

evt-02-24-1711-george-frideric-handel.scenario: It is 24 February 1711 and you sit in the Queen's Theatre, Haymarket, for the premiere of Handel's Rinaldo, London's first Italian opera written for the English stage.
evt-02-24-1711-george-frideric-handel.prompt: What stage spectacle became famous from this premiere?

choices.text: Live birds were released to fly loose over the stage
A real cannon was fired inside the theatre
Elephants were paraded across the stage
Fireworks accidentally set the scenery ablaze

evt-02-24-1711-george-frideric-handel.butterflyEffect: Live sparrows were released to flutter over the stage during Armida's enchanted garden scene, a stunt satirists like Joseph Addison later mocked. Rinaldo's success nonetheless launched Handel's London career and opened the door for Italian opera seria to dominate the city's stages for decades.

evt-02-24-1720-war-of-the-quadruple-alli.scenario: It is dawn on 24 February 1720, and you stand watch in the small British fort at Nassau in the Bahamas as Spanish warships close in, intent on seizing the colony during the War of the Quadruple Alliance.
evt-02-24-1720-war-of-the-quadruple-alli.prompt: What should the outnumbered garrison do to hold the fort?

choices.text: Abandon the fort and retreat inland
Sail out to attack the Spanish fleet directly
Man the fort's cannon and fire on the landing boats
Surrender immediately to avoid bloodshed

evt-02-24-1720-war-of-the-quadruple-alli.butterflyEffect: The defenders held their ground and drove off the Spanish landing force. Nassau remained under British control, letting the young colony continue developing into a key naval and trading outpost in the Caribbean.

evt-02-24-1809-theatre-royal-drury-lane.scenario: It is the night of 24 February 1809. You are Richard Brinsley Sheridan, playwright and MP, watching from a nearby coffeehouse as the Theatre Royal, Drury Lane—the building you own—goes up in flames.
evt-02-24-1809-theatre-royal-drury-lane.prompt: How does Sheridan reportedly react as he watches his theatre burn?

choices.text: He flees the scene before the fire takes hold
He calmly drinks wine, joking a man may enjoy a glass by his own fireside
He collapses in despair and refuses to watch
He organizes a bucket brigade to save the building

evt-02-24-1809-theatre-royal-drury-lane.butterflyEffect: Sheridan is said to have calmly sipped wine, remarking that a man may surely take a glass by his own fireside. The fire destroyed the theatre after only fifteen years and left Sheridan financially ruined, but a new Drury Lane opened in 1812 and still stands today as London's oldest continuously used theatre site.

evt-02-24-1809-napoleonic-wars.scenario: It is February 1809 and you serve under General George Beckwith as British forces besiege Fort Desaix, the last French stronghold on Martinique.
evt-02-24-1809-napoleonic-wars.prompt: What did the French garrison finally do after the siege?

choices.text: Negotiated a truce allowing joint Anglo-French control
Surrendered unconditionally to the British
Broke out and escaped by sea under cover of night
Received Spanish reinforcements and held the fort

evt-02-24-1809-napoleonic-wars.butterflyEffect: The French garrison surrendered unconditionally, and Britain occupied Martinique until 1814. The capture severed a key French Caribbean base and tightened the Royal Navy's grip on the region for the rest of the Napoleonic Wars.

evt-02-24-1868-andrew-johnson.scenario: You sit in the House of Representatives in early 1868, furious that President Andrew Johnson fired Secretary of War Edwin Stanton in apparent defiance of the Tenure of Office Act.
evt-02-24-1868-andrew-johnson.prompt: What did the House vote to do to President Johnson on this day?

choices.text: Refer the matter to the Supreme Court
Table the articles of impeachment indefinitely
Impeach him for violating the Tenure of Office Act
Formally censure him without impeachment

evt-02-24-1868-andrew-johnson.butterflyEffect: The House impeached Johnson, the first U.S. president to face that process. The Senate trial that followed ended in acquittal by a single vote in May 1868, but the episode set a lasting precedent invoked in every later presidential impeachment.

evt-02-24-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: You are an American tank commander in the Tunisian hills as Rommel's Afrika Korps smashes through the inexperienced U.S. II Corps at Kasserine Pass, forcing a chaotic retreat.
evt-02-24-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What command change followed this bruising early defeat for U.S. forces?

choices.text: The U.S. ceded the North African campaign entirely to the British
Eisenhower withdrew all U.S. forces from North Africa
Eisenhower replaced Fredendall with George S. Patton
Roosevelt recalled Eisenhower to Washington

evt-02-24-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Eisenhower relieved Major General Lloyd Fredendall and replaced him with George S. Patton, who tightened discipline and training. The humiliation at Kasserine spurred reforms that helped American forces perform far better weeks later at El Guettar, contributing to the Allied victory in Tunisia by May 1943.

evt-02-24-1968-vietnam-war.scenario: You are an ARVN officer under General Ngô Quang Trưởng, clearing the last defenders from the ruins of Hue's Imperial Citadel after weeks of house-to-house fighting during the Tet Offensive.
evt-02-24-1968-vietnam-war.prompt: What did South Vietnamese forces achieve inside the Citadel on this day?

choices.text: They retreated south to reinforce Da Nang
They recaptured the Citadel from communist forces
They withdrew and ceded the Citadel to the NVA
They negotiated a local ceasefire with the VC

evt-02-24-1968-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: ARVN troops recaptured the Citadel, ending the 26-day Battle of Hue. The devastation and discovery of mass executions by communist forces shocked the world, but graphic television coverage of the battle's destruction also deepened American public doubt about the war's winnability.

evt-02-24-1979-uganda-tanzania-war.scenario: You march with the Tanzania People's Defence Force as Ugandan government troops abandon the city of Masaka without a fight, opening the road deeper into Uganda.
evt-02-24-1979-uganda-tanzania-war.prompt: What did the fall of Masaka signal for Idi Amin's grip on power?

choices.text: It confirmed a decisive Ugandan victory over Tanzania
It triggered a United Nations peacekeeping intervention
It marked the beginning of the collapse that ended Amin's rule
It led to an immediate ceasefire agreement

evt-02-24-1979-uganda-tanzania-war.butterflyEffect: The collapse at Masaka marked the start of a rapid Ugandan army disintegration. Tanzanian and rebel forces pushed on to Kampala, and Amin fled into exile weeks later in April 1979, ending eight years of brutal rule but leaving Uganda in political turmoil for years afterward.

evt-02-24-1989-united-airlines-flight-81.scenario: You are the captain of United Airlines Flight 811, a Boeing 747 that has just left Honolulu on 24 February 1989, when a cargo door blows open, tearing away several rows of seats in an explosive decompression.
evt-02-24-1989-united-airlines-flight-81.prompt: What do you do as captain?

choices.text: Attempt to ditch the aircraft in the Pacific
Declare an emergency and return immediately to Honolulu
Continue on to Auckland as scheduled
Divert to the nearest small island airstrip

evt-02-24-1989-united-airlines-flight-81.butterflyEffect: The crew declared an emergency and turned the crippled 747 back to Honolulu, landing safely despite the deaths of nine passengers swept from the cabin. The investigation exposed a faulty cargo-door latch design, forcing FAA-mandated modifications across the Boeing 747 fleet.

evt-02-24-2000-pope-john-paul-ii.scenario: You are a Vatican aide as Pope John Paul II lands in Cairo on 24 February 2000, the opening stop of a Jubilee Year pilgrimage retracing the footsteps of Abraham and Moses.
evt-02-24-2000-pope-john-paul-ii.prompt: Which sacred site is next on the Pope's itinerary in Egypt?

choices.text: The Library of Alexandria
Mount Sinai
The Nile Delta wetlands
The Great Pyramid of Giza

evt-02-24-2000-pope-john-paul-ii.butterflyEffect: He traveled on to Mount Sinai, praying at the traditional site of Moses receiving the Ten Commandments. The visit, part of a wider Jubilee pilgrimage to biblical lands, strengthened ties with Egypt's Coptic Christians and advanced Catholic-Orthodox dialogue.

evt-02-24-2006-president-of-the-philippi.scenario: It is 24 February 2006, the 20th anniversary of the EDSA uprising. You are a Manila reporter as President Arroyo suddenly declares a state of national emergency, citing an alleged coup plot.
evt-02-24-2006-president-of-the-philippi.prompt: How did authorities enforce Proclamation 1017 that day?

choices.text: They raided a major newspaper's offices and broke up the anniversary rally
They formally declared martial law nationwide
They dissolved the Philippine Congress
They deployed the army to occupy Mindanao

evt-02-24-2006-president-of-the-philippi.butterflyEffect: Police dispersed the EDSA anniversary rally and raided the offices of the Daily Tribune newspaper, seizing copies over an alleged coup story. Arroyo lifted the proclamation within a week amid public and international criticism, and the Supreme Court later ruled parts of it unconstitutional.

evt-02-24-2007-reconnaissance-satellite.scenario: It is 24 February 2007 and you watch from the control room as Japan's space agency launches its fourth Information Gathering Satellite, aimed at watching North Korea and other regional threats.
evt-02-24-2007-reconnaissance-satellite.prompt: What did this fourth launch achieve for Japan's surveillance program?

choices.text: China's protests forced Japan to halt the reconnaissance program
It was repurposed as a civilian weather satellite
It failed on launch and had to be scrapped
It completed a four-satellite network giving round-the-clock optical and radar coverage

evt-02-24-2007-reconnaissance-satellite.butterflyEffect: The launch completed Japan's first full four-satellite reconnaissance constellation, combining optical and radar imaging for continuous day, night, and all-weather coverage. The program expanded further in later years as North Korean missile and nuclear tests deepened Tokyo's reliance on independent satellite intelligence.

evt-02-24-2008-fidel-castro.scenario: You sit in Cuba's National Assembly on 24 February 2008, called to formalize the transfer of power after Fidel Castro's resignation ends his 32-year hold on the presidency.
evt-02-24-2008-fidel-castro.prompt: Whom does the Assembly elect as Cuba's new president?

choices.text: Felipe Pérez Roque
Carlos Lage
Raúl Castro
Ricardo Alarcón

evt-02-24-2008-fidel-castro.butterflyEffect: The Assembly elected Raúl Castro, Fidel's brother and longtime defense minister. Raúl introduced limited economic reforms, set presidential term limits, and stepped down in 2018, ending direct Castro family rule even as the Communist Party retained control.

evt-02-24-2011-space-shuttle-discovery.scenario: You watch from the firing room at Kennedy Space Center as Discovery thunders off the pad for the final time on mission STS-133, bound for the International Space Station.
evt-02-24-2011-space-shuttle-discovery.prompt: What notable cargo did Discovery deliver to the ISS on this final flight?

choices.text: The Permanent Multipurpose Module and Robonaut 2
A new docking module for the Mir station
The Hubble Space Telescope
The first American astronaut to fly in space

evt-02-24-2011-space-shuttle-discovery.butterflyEffect: Discovery carried the Permanent Multipurpose Module and Robonaut 2, humanoid robot, to the station before returning to Earth for retirement. Having flown 39 missions over 27 years, more than any other orbiter, it was later put on permanent public display at the Smithsonian.

evt-02-24-2020-mahathir-mohamad.scenario: It is 24 February 2020. Secret meetings at a Kuala Lumpur hotel have triggered mass defections threatening to collapse your Pakatan Harapan government, and you must respond as Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
evt-02-24-2020-mahathir-mohamad.prompt: What does Mahathir do amid the unfolding political crisis?

choices.text: Resign as Prime Minister without naming a successor
Dissolve parliament and call snap elections
Resign and immediately endorse Anwar Ibrahim as successor
Refuse to resign and dismiss the defecting MPs

evt-02-24-2020-mahathir-mohamad.butterflyEffect: Mahathir abruptly resigned without naming a successor, throwing Malaysia into a power vacuum. Days later the King appointed Muhyiddin Yassin as prime minister, ending the Pakatan Harapan government and delaying Anwar Ibrahim's long-anticipated succession.

evt-02-24-2022-russian-invasion-of-ukrai.scenario: It is the early hours of 24 February 2022. Missiles are falling on Kyiv, tanks are rolling in from Belarus, Crimea and the Donbas, and Western allies have offered you a route out of the capital.
evt-02-24-2022-russian-invasion-of-ukrai.prompt: As President Zelensky, what do you decide to do?

choices.text: Accept evacuation and lead a government-in-exile
Refuse to leave and remain in Kyiv
Flee quietly to Lviv near the Polish border
Open immediate surrender talks with Moscow

evt-02-24-2022-russian-invasion-of-ukrai.butterflyEffect: Zelensky refused evacuation, reportedly telling allies "I need ammunition, not a ride," and stayed in Kyiv to lead the defense. His visible presence rallied Ukrainian resistance and helped unlock a surge of Western military and financial support that shaped the war's early course.

evt-02-25-628-khosrow-ii.scenario: You are a Sasanian noble in Ctesiphon in February 628. Decades of ruinous war against Byzantium have bled the empire dry, and the army has just turned on King Khosrow II, backing his son Kavad II instead. The captive king now awaits his fate at your hands.
evt-02-25-628-khosrow-ii.prompt: What does the new regime decide to do with the deposed Khosrow II?

choices.text: He is executed on Kavad II's orders
He is handed over to the Byzantines as a hostage
He is exiled to India for the rest of his life
He is restored to the throne after negotiations

evt-02-25-628-khosrow-ii.butterflyEffect: Kavad II had his father executed within days of seizing the throne. Kavad himself died of plague only months later, plunging the Sasanian court into a chaotic succession crisis that weakened the empire fatally just as Arab Muslim armies began their conquests in the following decade.

evt-02-25-1843-royal-navy.scenario: You are King Kamehameha III of Hawaii, facing a British warship in Honolulu harbor whose captain, Lord George Paulet, threatens to bombard the city unless you cede the islands to Britain.
evt-02-25-1843-royal-navy.prompt: What do you do to avoid bloodshed?

choices.text: Appeal immediately to the United States for annexation
Cede provisional sovereignty to Britain under protest
Order Hawaiian forces to fight the British ships
Flee inland and abandon Honolulu

evt-02-25-1843-royal-navy.butterflyEffect: Kamehameha III ceded sovereignty under protest, and Paulet occupied Hawaii for five months. When British Admiral Richard Thomas arrived and repudiated Paulet's actions, restoring full Hawaiian sovereignty, the king declared "Ua Mau ke Ea o ka ʻĀina i ka Pono" — words that remain Hawaii's state motto today.

evt-02-25-1866-calaveras-county-californ.scenario: You are a miner in Calaveras County who has just pulled a human skull from deep within ancient gold-bearing gravel, gravel said to date back to a time before recorded human history.
evt-02-25-1866-calaveras-county-californ.prompt: What do you do with the skull?

choices.text: Rebury it undisturbed out of respect
Sell it to a traveling collector for cash
Discard it as worthless mining debris
Hand it to State Geologist Josiah Whitney as scientific evidence

evt-02-25-1866-calaveras-county-californ.butterflyEffect: The skull was handed to State Geologist Josiah Whitney, who presented it as proof that humans had lived in California for a million years or more. Scientists later exposed it as a hoax planted by miners to fool Whitney, and the "Calaveras Skull" became a textbook warning about the dangers of unverified fossil evidence.

evt-02-25-1870-united-states-senate.scenario: It is 25 February 1870 on the Senate floor. As a senator, you must vote on seating Hiram Revels of Mississippi, whose opponents argue that under the Dred Scott decision he cannot have been a citizen long enough to meet the constitutional requirement.
evt-02-25-1870-united-states-senate.prompt: What did the Senate ultimately decide about seating Revels?

choices.text: It postpones the vote indefinitely without resolution
It seats him only after a constitutional amendment passes
It rejects him and orders a new Mississippi election
It votes to seat him despite the objections

evt-02-25-1870-united-states-senate.butterflyEffect: The Senate voted 48–8 to seat Revels, making him the first African American to serve in Congress. His swearing-in was a landmark of Reconstruction, though it would be nearly a century before another Black senator was elected.

evt-02-25-1932-adolf-hitler.scenario: You are an official in the German state of Brunswick in 1932, asked by the state's Nazi interior minister to grant a minor civil-service appointment to a stateless Austrian-born political agitator named Adolf Hitler.
evt-02-25-1932-adolf-hitler.prompt: What administrative step is taken to solve Hitler's statelessness?

choices.text: Naturalize him through marriage to a German citizen
Restore his original Austrian citizenship instead
Appoint him to a minor civil-service post that confers automatic citizenship
Grant him citizenship through a special act of parliament

evt-02-25-1932-adolf-hitler.butterflyEffect: Hitler was appointed to a low-level government post in Brunswick, which automatically granted him German citizenship after seven years of statelessness. That citizenship let him run for president later in 1932 and, within a year, be appointed Chancellor of Germany, opening the path to Nazi dictatorship.

evt-02-25-1933-uss-ranger-cv-4.scenario: It is launch day, 25 February 1933, at Newport News shipyard. As a naval architect on the USS Ranger project, you must defend an unusual design choice: building America's first carrier planned from the keel up without a permanent island superstructure.
evt-02-25-1933-uss-ranger-cv-4.prompt: Why was Ranger initially designed without an island?

choices.text: Because the Navy had not yet decided if it would carry aircraft
To reduce the ship's radar signature
To maximize flight-deck space for launching and landing aircraft
Because treaty tonnage limits forbade any superstructure

evt-02-25-1933-uss-ranger-cv-4.butterflyEffect: Naval planners believed a flat, unobstructed flight deck would maximize aircraft operations, so an island was omitted from the original design and only added after completion once its navigational drawbacks became clear. The lesson shaped every carrier built afterward, all of which received a proper island from the outset.

evt-02-25-1939-air-raid-precautions.scenario: You are a suburban Londoner in February 1939. A council delivery crew drops curved steel panels in your back garden, the very first of what will become 2.5 million such kits distributed under Britain's air raid precautions.
evt-02-25-1939-air-raid-precautions.prompt: What must you do with the panels to make them useful against bombing?

choices.text: Install them under the staircase inside the house
Bolt them together in the attic as a loft shelter
Sink them partway into the garden soil and cover them with earth
Store them flat in the garage until an air raid warning sounds

evt-02-25-1939-air-raid-precautions.butterflyEffect: The panels were bolted together and half-buried in gardens, covered with earth, to form the Anderson shelter. Issued free to lower-income households, millions of these shelters sheltered families through the Blitz and became one of the most recognisable symbols of Britain's Home Front.

evt-02-25-1941-communist-party-of-the-ne.scenario: You are a tram worker in Amsterdam in February 1941. Leaflets from the outlawed Communist Party urge you and your colleagues to walk off the job in protest at the German occupiers' escalating persecution of the city's Jewish population.
evt-02-25-1941-communist-party-of-the-ne.prompt: What had just happened to provoke this call for a general strike?

choices.text: Announcement of forced conscription into the German army
Nazi raids and violence against Jewish residents in Amsterdam
A wage freeze imposed on all Dutch industries
New rationing cuts to bread and dairy

evt-02-25-1941-communist-party-of-the-ne.butterflyEffect: The strike followed brutal Nazi raids and street violence targeting Amsterdam's Jewish quarter, including mass arrests. It became the first large-scale public protest against anti-Jewish persecution in occupied Europe, but the Germans crushed it swiftly, executing several organizers and imposing harsh reprisals on the city.

evt-02-25-1947-nkvd.scenario: It is 25 February 1947 and you are a Smallholders' Party colleague in Budapest when Soviet NKVD agents seize Béla Kovács from his home, disregarding his parliamentary immunity.
evt-02-25-1947-nkvd.prompt: What charge did the Soviets use to justify seizing Kovács?

choices.text: War crimes committed under the wartime regime
Voluntary defection to the West
Espionage and conspiracy against Soviet occupation forces
Collaboration with Nazi Germany during the occupation

evt-02-25-1947-nkvd.butterflyEffect: He was accused of running an espionage and conspiracy network against Soviet occupation forces, then deported to a Soviet labor camp for years. His removal gutted the Smallholders' leadership, clearing the way for the Communists to dominate Hungary's coalition and impose one-party rule by 1949.

evt-02-25-1948-edvard-benes.scenario: You are President Edvard Beneš in Prague, February 1948. Non-communist ministers have resigned in protest, Klement Gottwald's Communists have mobilised armed militias in the streets, and you fear that resistance could trigger civil war or a Soviet intervention like the one you witnessed a decade earlier.
evt-02-25-1948-edvard-benes.prompt: What decision does Beneš make under this pressure?

choices.text: He appeals to Britain and France for military support
He calls immediate new elections to resolve the crisis
He declares martial law and dissolves parliament
He accepts the resignations and approves a communist-dominated government

evt-02-25-1948-edvard-benes.butterflyEffect: Beneš accepted the ministers' resignations and approved a new government dominated by Communists, effectively completing their takeover of the state. He resigned the presidency months later in June 1948, and Czechoslovakia became a one-party communist state locked firmly into the Soviet bloc for four decades.

evt-02-25-1951-1951-pan-american-games.scenario: You are an athlete stepping off a ship in Buenos Aires in February 1951, for a continental games that officials first tried to launch nine years earlier before global events intervened.
evt-02-25-1951-1951-pan-american-games.prompt: What forced the postponement of these inaugural Pan American Games?

choices.text: Political instability within Argentina
World War II disrupted preparations and travel
A scheduling clash with the Olympic Games
A polio outbreak across South America

evt-02-25-1951-1951-pan-american-games.butterflyEffect: The Games, originally planned for 1942, were delayed by the outbreak of World War II. Their eventual 1951 debut in Buenos Aires launched a quadrennial tradition that continues today, becoming the largest regional multi-sport event in the Americas alongside the Olympics.

evt-02-25-1951-pan-american-games.scenario: You are an athlete standing in a packed Buenos Aires stadium as Argentine officials prepare to declare a brand-new continental sporting event open for the very first time.
evt-02-25-1951-pan-american-games.prompt: What historic first is being launched at this ceremony?

choices.text: The first FIFA World Cup hosted in the Americas
The first Winter Pan American Games
The first Pan American Games
The first Summer Olympics held in South America

evt-02-25-1951-pan-american-games.butterflyEffect: This was the inaugural Pan American Games, opened in Buenos Aires in 1951. It went on to become a quadrennial tradition held the year before each Summer Olympics, growing into the second-oldest continental multi-sport games in the world.

evt-02-25-1980-henck-arron.scenario: It is 25 February 1980 in Paramaribo. As Prime Minister Henck Arron, you learn that a group of sixteen non-commissioned officers, angry over pay and unionization, has seized the radio station and army barracks.
evt-02-25-1980-henck-arron.prompt: What actually happened to Arron's government that day?

choices.text: He orders the army to crush the mutiny within hours
He flees to the Netherlands before the coup begins
He is overthrown and detained by the military coup plotters
He negotiates a power-sharing deal that keeps him in office

evt-02-25-1980-henck-arron.butterflyEffect: The coup, led by Sergeant Major Dési Bouterse, toppled Arron and installed a military regime. Bouterse would dominate Suriname's politics for decades, and Arron himself was later jailed on corruption charges before being released and returning to banking and eventually the vice presidency.

evt-02-25-1980-suriname.scenario: It is 25 February 1980 and you are stationed with the National Army in Paramaribo as a group of sergeants led by Dési Bouterse storm government buildings, overthrowing Prime Minister Henck Arron's civilian government.
evt-02-25-1980-suriname.prompt: What followed the sergeants' seizure of power?

choices.text: The Netherlands reasserted colonial control
Arron was swiftly restored to power
Bouterse became the country's de facto military ruler
Suriname immediately held free elections

evt-02-25-1980-suriname.butterflyEffect: Bouterse emerged as Suriname's military strongman, ruling through a National Military Council for years. His dominance culminated in the 1982 December murders of opposition figures, for which he was later convicted, even after being elected president decades on.

evt-02-25-1986-ferdinand-marcos.scenario: It is 25 February 1986 outside Malacañang Palace. As a soldier ordered to defend President Marcos, you watch crowds and defecting units gather along EDSA while a U.S. Air Force helicopter idles nearby.
evt-02-25-1986-ferdinand-marcos.prompt: What happened to Marcos in the hours that followed?

choices.text: He is captured by rebel soldiers inside the palace
He is airlifted by the U.S. military into exile in Hawaii
He is handed over to Corazon Aquino's government for trial
He negotiates a ceasefire and remains as a figurehead president

evt-02-25-1986-ferdinand-marcos.butterflyEffect: Marcos and his family were flown by U.S. military helicopters to Clark Air Base and then into exile in Hawaii, ending 20 years of rule. Corazon Aquino, widow of the assassinated opposition leader Ninoy Aquino, was sworn in as president, and the People Power Revolution became a model for later nonviolent uprisings.

evt-02-25-1991-warsaw-pact.scenario: It is 25 February 1991 in Budapest. As a delegate representing one of the Eastern Bloc states, you sit down with counterparts to formally end the military structures of the Warsaw Pact, six years after Gorbachev's reforms began unraveling Soviet control.
evt-02-25-1991-warsaw-pact.prompt: What did the Budapest meeting actually accomplish?

choices.text: They renew the treaty for another decade with reforms
They vote to expand membership to include NATO states
They agree to transform the Pact into a purely economic bloc
They dissolve the Pact's military command structures

evt-02-25-1991-warsaw-pact.butterflyEffect: The member states agreed to dissolve the Pact's military structures, and the alliance was formally abolished later that year. The Soviet Union itself would collapse within months, and several former Warsaw Pact states eventually joined NATO, reshaping European security for decades.

evt-02-25-1999-minerva-airlines-flight-1.scenario: You are a passenger aboard the Dornier 328 turboprop flying Cagliari to Genoa, buckled in as the aircraft lines up for final approach to Genoa's runway, which ends abruptly near the sea wall.
evt-02-25-1999-minerva-airlines-flight-1.prompt: What actually happens as the aircraft touches down at Genoa?

choices.text: It lands safely despite difficult conditions
It aborts the landing and diverts safely to Milan
It circles and lands without incident on a second attempt
It overruns the runway and is destroyed, with fatal casualties

evt-02-25-1999-minerva-airlines-flight-1.butterflyEffect: The aircraft lost control on landing and overran the runway, killing three people at the scene and a fourth later in hospital; the plane was destroyed. The crash prompted a review of Dornier 328 operations and runway safety margins at short coastal airports like Genoa.

evt-02-25-2009-border-guard-bangladesh.scenario: It is 25 February 2009 and you are an army officer seconded to lead Bangladesh Rifles headquarters in Pilkhana, Dhaka. Mutinous border guards, furious over pay and unequal privileges with the army, have seized the armoury and begun rounding up officers.
evt-02-25-2009-border-guard-bangladesh.prompt: What ultimately followed the mutiny at Pilkhana?

choices.text: Army officers are massacred and buried in mass graves within the compound
Indian troops cross the border to help put down the mutiny
The mutiny is suppressed within hours with no casualties
The government grants all demands and the mutiny ends peacefully by nightfall

evt-02-25-2009-border-guard-bangladesh.butterflyEffect: Dozens of army officers were murdered by mutineers and buried in mass graves within the compound. The scandal led to the dissolution of the Bangladesh Rifles and its reconstitution in 2010 as Border Guard Bangladesh under tighter army control, with lengthy trials and executions of mutineers following in later years.

evt-02-25-2009-turkish-airlines-flight-1.scenario: You are the first officer aboard Turkish Airlines Flight 1951 on final approach to Amsterdam Schiphol on 25 February 2009, when the autothrottle suddenly retards engine power far earlier than it should on a normal descent.
evt-02-25-2009-turkish-airlines-flight-1.prompt: What faulty reading triggered this dangerous early power reduction?

choices.text: Severe wing icing caused loss of lift
A faulty radio altimeter caused the autothrottle to cut power too early
The aircraft ran out of fuel on approach
A bird strike disabled one engine

evt-02-25-2009-turkish-airlines-flight-1.butterflyEffect: A defective radio altimeter fed the aircraft's automated systems a false low-altitude reading, causing the autothrottle to cut power prematurely and the aircraft to stall and crash short of the runway, killing nine of those aboard, including all three pilots. The accident prompted renewed scrutiny of automation reliance and altimeter fault tolerance across the 737 fleet.

evt-02-26-1914-hmhs-britannic.scenario: You stand in the Belfast shipyard on 26 February 1914 as White Star Line's newest liner, sister to the ill-fated Titanic, slides into the water for the first time. Company officials point out the changes made in direct response to the 1912 disaster.
evt-02-26-1914-hmhs-britannic.prompt: What safety improvement most distinguishes this new ship from Titanic?

choices.text: Raised watertight bulkheads and lifeboat davits designed for a listing ship
A reduced passenger capacity to leave room for extra lifeboats only
A fully welded hull instead of riveted steel plates
Radar equipment to detect icebergs at night

evt-02-26-1914-hmhs-britannic.butterflyEffect: Britannic was fitted with a double hull along her engine rooms, raised watertight bulkheads, and davits capable of launching lifeboats even if the ship listed heavily. Yet when she struck a mine in the Aegean in 1916 while serving as a hospital ship, open portholes let water flood in far faster than designers anticipated, and she sank in under an hour, a lesson that further shaped maritime safety rules.

evt-02-26-1917-original-dixieland-jass-b.scenario: You are a recording engineer at the Victor studio in New York on 26 February 1917. A white New Orleans band wants to cut a rowdy, syncopated number full of barnyard imitations, and you must decide how to present it to the public.
evt-02-26-1917-original-dixieland-jass-b.prompt: How should the record be marketed to capture what this new sound is?

choices.text: Market it as a novelty ragtime comedy sketch
Label it plainly as a jazz record, a new type of music
Withhold release until a classically trained arranger cleans it up
Bury it as a B-side and promote a waltz instead

evt-02-26-1917-original-dixieland-jass-b.butterflyEffect: "Livery Stable Blues" became the first jazz record ever commercially released, and it was an immediate sensation, selling over a million copies. Its success launched the national jazz craze, though it also meant a white group got commercial credit ahead of the Black New Orleans musicians who had shaped the music for years.

evt-02-26-1935-adolf-hitler.scenario: You are a diplomat in London in late February 1935, reading dispatches that Hitler has publicly confirmed the Luftwaffe's existence, a direct breach of the Versailles Treaty's ban on German military aviation.
evt-02-26-1935-adolf-hitler.prompt: How do Britain and France respond to this open treaty violation?

choices.text: They immediately mobilize troops to occupy the Rhineland
They form a new military alliance with the Soviet Union to counter Germany
They issue diplomatic protests but take no enforcement action
They impose League of Nations economic sanctions on Germany

evt-02-26-1935-adolf-hitler.butterflyEffect: London and Paris lodged formal protests but took no concrete action to stop the rearmament. Emboldened, Hitler pressed on, securing the Anglo-German Naval Agreement later that year and reintroducing conscription, steps that steadily dismantled Versailles' restraints and set the course toward the Second World War.

evt-02-26-1935-daventry.scenario: It is 26 February 1935 near the BBC transmitter at Daventry. You are part of Robert Watson-Watt's team, watching a van bristling with receiving antennae as a Royal Air Force bomber is asked to fly slowly through the transmitter's radio beam.
evt-02-26-1935-daventry.prompt: What result would prove that aircraft can be detected by reflected radio waves?

choices.text: The bomber's radio communications are jammed by the transmitter
The transmitter causes visible interference on nearby home radios
A detectable echo appears on the receiver each time the bomber crosses the beam
The bomber's engine noise is picked up by the antennae array

evt-02-26-1935-daventry.butterflyEffect: The team detected a clear reflected signal each time the bomber crossed the beam, proving radio waves could locate aircraft at a distance. The demonstration led directly to funding for what became the Chain Home radar network, which gave Britain crucial early warning during the Battle of Britain five years later.
