evt-02-26-1936-imperial-japanese-army.scenario: It is 26 February 1936 and you command loyal troops in Tokyo. Rebel officers of the Imperial Japanese Army have seized government buildings and assassinated several senior officials, demanding a new military-led order.
evt-02-26-1936-imperial-japanese-army.prompt: What should the Army high command do about the uprising?

choices.text: Declare amnesty for the rebels immediately to avoid bloodshed
Await the Emperor's order and move troops to suppress the rebels
Withdraw all government officials from Tokyo until the rebels stand down
Negotiate a power-sharing arrangement with the rebel officers

evt-02-26-1936-imperial-japanese-army.butterflyEffect: Emperor Hirohito personally intervened and ordered the rebellion crushed; loyal troops surrounded the mutineers, who surrendered within days, and their leaders were court-martialed and executed. The failed coup nonetheless strengthened the military's grip on politics, as the government moved further toward the hardline factions the rebels had championed.

evt-02-26-1966-apollo-program.scenario: You are a NASA engineer at Cape Kennedy on 26 February 1966, watching the first Saturn IB rocket rise off the pad carrying an uncrewed Apollo command module on a suborbital test flight.
evt-02-26-1966-apollo-program.prompt: What is this AS-201 mission chiefly designed to test?

choices.text: Docking maneuvers between the command module and lunar module
A week-long crewed stay in low Earth orbit
The launch escape tower's ability to save a crew during liftoff
The Saturn IB rocket's performance and the capsule's reentry heat shield

evt-02-26-1966-apollo-program.butterflyEffect: AS-201 verified the Saturn IB's performance and put the Apollo command module's heat shield through a high-speed reentry, both essential proofs before astronauts could fly aboard. The successful test cleared the way for crewed Apollo missions later in the decade, ultimately leading to the first Moon landing in 1969.

evt-02-26-1979-superliner-railcar.scenario: You are an Amtrak planner in the late 1970s tasked with replacing worn-out single-level cars on the railroad's long-distance Western routes, drawing on an old Santa Fe design for inspiration.
evt-02-26-1979-superliner-railcar.prompt: What design approach do you adopt to boost capacity and comfort?

choices.text: Stick with traditional single-level cars but add more seats
Build articulated cars linked permanently in pairs
Adopt a bilevel, double-deck car design
Design streamlined cars with no upper-level windows to cut weight

evt-02-26-1979-superliner-railcar.butterflyEffect: Amtrak commissioned the Superliner, a bilevel car based on the Santa Fe's Hi-Level design, and it entered revenue service in February 1979. The design proved so durable that a second generation was built in the 1990s, and Superliners still form the backbone of Amtrak's long-distance Western fleet decades later.

evt-02-26-1980-egypt-israel-relations.scenario: It is 26 February 1980 in Cairo, and you watch Eliyahu Ben-Elissar present his credentials as ambassador, exactly one month after Egypt and Israel formally established diplomatic ties under the Camp David framework.
evt-02-26-1980-egypt-israel-relations.prompt: What historic first does this ceremony mark for Israel's diplomacy?

choices.text: The full return of the Sinai Peninsula to Egypt
The first Israeli ambassador ever accredited to an Arab state
The opening of the Suez Canal to Israeli shipping for the first time
The first joint Egyptian-Israeli military exercise

evt-02-26-1980-egypt-israel-relations.butterflyEffect: Ben-Elissar became the first Israeli ambassador ever posted to an Arab capital, while Saad Mortada took up the matching post in Tel Aviv. The exchange cemented the 1979 peace treaty into working diplomacy, embassies and border crossings that endure to this day, though the relationship has often remained a cold peace between governments rather than peoples.

evt-02-26-1987-iran-contra-affair.scenario: It is 26 February 1987 and the Tower Commission has just released its report, finding you, President Reagan, responsible for failing to control a secret operation that traded arms to Iran and funneled proceeds to Nicaraguan rebels.
evt-02-26-1987-iran-contra-affair.prompt: How should Reagan respond publicly to the Commission's rebuke?

choices.text: Resign the presidency immediately
Deny any knowledge of the affair entirely
Publicly accept responsibility for the operation's mismanagement
Blame Congress for the Boland Amendment restrictions

evt-02-26-1987-iran-contra-affair.butterflyEffect: Reagan went on national television and accepted responsibility for the affair's mismanagement, while insisting he had not known about the diversion of funds to the Contras. The admission salvaged his presidency's credibility somewhat, but the scandal permanently damaged his administration's reputation and led to convictions of aides like Oliver North.

evt-02-26-1993-1993-world-trade-center-b.scenario: It is midday on February 26, 1993, and a massive blast has just torn through the parking garage beneath the North Tower of the World Trade Center. As an FBI investigator arriving amid the smoke and chaos, you begin tracing who rented the van that carried the bomb.
evt-02-26-1993-1993-world-trade-center-b.prompt: How does the investigation ultimately catch the attack's mastermind, Ramzi Yousef?

choices.text: He is killed resisting arrest in New Jersey within days
He is captured in Pakistan two years later and extradited to the US
He surrenders voluntarily to New York police a week later
He is never identified and the case remains unsolved

evt-02-26-1993-1993-world-trade-center-b.butterflyEffect: Yousef fled the country immediately after the bombing, but investigators traced the rental van's VIN and followed a trail of evidence to his network. He was captured in Islamabad, Pakistan, in February 1995 and extradited to the U.S., where his conviction exposed a wider jihadist network later linked to the 9/11 plotters.

evt-02-26-2008-new-york-philharmonic.scenario: It is 26 February 2008 and you are a musician with the New York Philharmonic, about to perform in Pyongyang, North Korea, the first such visit by a major American orchestra. The concert hall is packed with officials and cameras broadcasting nationwide.
evt-02-26-2008-new-york-philharmonic.prompt: What should the orchestra play as a closing gesture of goodwill?

choices.text: A second full performance of the American national anthem
The Korean folk song "Arirang" as an encore
Nothing extra, ending strictly with the printed program
An entirely new commissioned piece with no Korean elements

evt-02-26-2008-new-york-philharmonic.butterflyEffect: The Philharmonic closed with the Korean folk song "Arirang," a piece beloved on both sides of the peninsula, moving many in the audience to tears. The broadcast concert was hailed as a rare moment of cultural opening, though it produced no lasting diplomatic breakthrough between Washington and Pyongyang.

evt-02-26-2013-2013-luxor-hot-air-balloo.scenario: It is the morning of 26 February 2013 near Luxor, Egypt, and you are part of the ground crew preparing a tourist hot air balloon for launch. You notice a faint smell and hissing sound near the fuel line before passengers board.
evt-02-26-2013-2013-luxor-hot-air-balloo.prompt: What should the crew do about the suspected gas leak before takeoff?

choices.text: Ignore the smell since the tanks were checked the previous day
Vent excess gas mid-flight to reduce risk
Ground the balloon and inspect the fuel system before flight
Proceed with launch but fly at a lower altitude

evt-02-26-2013-2013-luxor-hot-air-balloo.butterflyEffect: A leak in the balloon's fuel system was later found to have caused a fire that made the balloon deflate and crash, killing 19 of the 21 people aboard. The disaster prompted Egypt to tighten hot air balloon safety regulations and inspection requirements for its Luxor tourist flights.

evt-02-26-2013-hot-air-balloon.scenario: You are piloting a hot air balloon carrying tourists over Luxor's West Bank at dawn when flames suddenly flare from a fuel line just as you begin your final descent toward the landing field.
evt-02-26-2013-hot-air-balloon.prompt: With the balloon on fire during descent, what does the pilot do?

choices.text: Jump clear of the basket, hoping to escape the fire
Vent the envelope immediately to force a rapid landing
Use an onboard extinguisher to smother the flames before landing
Order all passengers to jump one by one while still airborne

evt-02-26-2013-hot-air-balloon.butterflyEffect: The pilot leapt from the basket to escape the flames; freed of his weight, the balloon shot upward before the envelope lost its lift and it plunged to the ground, killing nineteen of the twenty-one aboard. It became the deadliest hot air balloon disaster on record and prompted Egypt to tighten oversight of its Luxor ballooning industry, a major tourist draw.

evt-02-27-1560-treaty-of-berwick-1560.scenario: You're a Scottish Lord of the Congregation meeting England's Duke of Norfolk at Berwick-upon-Tweed in February 1560, weighing whether to accept English help against the French troops defending Regent Mary of Guise.
evt-02-27-1560-treaty-of-berwick-1560.prompt: What do the Scottish lords agree to in the treaty?

choices.text: Depose Mary of Guise immediately by force alone
Refuse all foreign intervention and negotiate directly with the French
Accept English troops and ships to help expel the French from Scotland
Ally with France against England

evt-02-27-1560-treaty-of-berwick-1560.butterflyEffect: The lords accepted English troops and ships, leading to a joint siege of the French garrison at Leith. The resulting Treaty of Edinburgh months later forced a French withdrawal, clearing the way for the Scottish Reformation Parliament to establish Protestantism as the national religion.

evt-02-27-1617-treaty-of-stolbovo.scenario: You are a Russian negotiator in February 1617, weary from the chaos of the Time of Troubles. Swedish envoys demand the Ingrian coastlands and the fortress of Kexholm as the price for ending years of war and finally withdrawing from Russian soil.
evt-02-27-1617-treaty-of-stolbovo.prompt: What do the Russians agree to in order to end the Ingrian War?

choices.text: Russia cedes Ingria and Kexholm, losing its Baltic coastline
Russia agrees to pay Sweden an annual tribute instead of ceding land
Both sides agree to a permanent joint administration of Ingria
Sweden withdraws entirely with no territorial concessions

evt-02-27-1617-treaty-of-stolbovo.butterflyEffect: Russia ceded Ingria and Kexholm to Sweden, buying peace but losing its only outlet to the Baltic Sea for nearly a century. That loss became a central grievance behind Peter the Great's Great Northern War, which reclaimed the coast and led directly to the founding of St. Petersburg.

evt-02-27-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is dawn on 27 February 1776 near Wilmington, North Carolina. You command Patriot militia across Moore's Creek Bridge as Loyalist Highlanders, swords drawn, charge toward you across the partially dismantled span.
evt-02-27-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What tactic breaks the Loyalist charge at the bridge?

choices.text: Remove the bridge's planks and grease the girders, then fire as Loyalists try to cross
Retreat inland to avoid direct engagement
Negotiate a truce with the Loyalist commander
Call in a naval bombardment from the Cape Fear River

evt-02-27-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: The Patriots had stripped the bridge's planks and greased its girders, then opened musket and cannon fire as the Loyalists tried to cross, routing them in minutes. The victory crushed the Loyalist uprising in North Carolina and helped push the colony to become the first to instruct its delegates to vote for independence.

evt-02-27-1814-peninsular-war.scenario: It is 27 February 1814, and you serve in Wellington's Anglo-Portuguese-Spanish army as it fords the Gave de Pau near Orthez in southern France, facing Marshal Soult's entrenched French line.
evt-02-27-1814-peninsular-war.prompt: What move helps Wellington break Soult's defensive position at Orthez?

choices.text: A single massed frontal charge straight into the French center
A full withdrawal to await reinforcements from Spain
A wide flanking movement around the French right that threatens Soult's line of retreat
A prolonged artillery bombardment with no infantry advance

evt-02-27-1814-peninsular-war.butterflyEffect: Wellington's flanking maneuver shattered Soult's line, forcing a costly French retreat toward Toulouse. The defeat further weakened Napoleon's position in the south, and just weeks later, in April 1814, he abdicated, ending the Peninsular War.

evt-02-27-1870-flag-of-japan.scenario: It is 1870, and Meiji officials are standardizing symbols for Japan's modernizing merchant fleet so its ships can be identified in foreign ports.
evt-02-27-1870-flag-of-japan.prompt: What flag design do officials mandate for merchant ships?

choices.text: A white field with sixteen red rays radiating outward
A white field bearing a single red disc at its center
A red field bearing a white disc at its center
A blue field bearing a red disc at its center

evt-02-27-1870-flag-of-japan.butterflyEffect: The white field with a red disc, the Hinomaru, became Japan's enduring national symbol through the Imperial era and beyond. It was only formally codified as the official national flag by law in 1999, over a century after this maritime decree.

evt-02-27-1900-fc-bayern-munich.scenario: It is late February 1900 in Munich. You are one of eleven footballers inside the gymnastics club MTV Jahn München, and its leadership has just refused to let your football section join the new national football association.
evt-02-27-1900-fc-bayern-munich.prompt: What do you and your teammates decide to do?

choices.text: Break away and found an independent club, FC Bayern Munich
Accept the gymnastics club's ruling and disband the football section
Merge quietly with a rival Munich sports club
Petition the Bavarian royal court to intervene

evt-02-27-1900-fc-bayern-munich.butterflyEffect: The frustrated players broke away and founded their own independent club, FC Bayern Munich, on 27 February 1900. That split eventually grew into Germany's most decorated football club, with a record haul of Bundesliga titles and DFB-Pokal wins.

evt-02-27-1933-reichstag-fire.scenario: It is the night of 27 February 1933, just four weeks after Hitler became chancellor. You are a Berlin police officer arriving at the blazing Reichstag, where you find a lone Dutchman, Marinus van der Lubbe, inside the building.
evt-02-27-1933-reichstag-fire.prompt: What does Hitler's government do with the fire in the days that follow?

choices.text: Form a coalition government with the Communist Party to calm tensions
Issue the Reichstag Fire Decree, suspending civil liberties and enabling mass arrests of Communists
Call new elections while leaving all existing civil liberties untouched
Declare war on the Soviet Union in retaliation

evt-02-27-1933-reichstag-fire.butterflyEffect: Hindenburg signed the Reichstag Fire Decree, suspending civil liberties and letting the Nazi-controlled police arrest Communist deputies en masse before the 5 March election. Crippled by the crackdown, the KPD's absence let the Nazis expand their plurality in the Reichstag, clearing the path toward the Enabling Act and one-party rule.

evt-02-27-1962-south-vietnam-air-force.scenario: On 27 February 1962, you're piloting one of two Republic of Vietnam Air Force Skyraiders on what looks like a routine mission, but you and your wingman have secretly decided to break formation and dive on President Ngo Dinh Diem's Independence Palace.
evt-02-27-1962-south-vietnam-air-force.prompt: What is the outcome of the attack on Independence Palace?

choices.text: The pilots are intercepted and shot down before reaching the target
The palace is bombed and damaged, but Diem survives
Diem is killed instantly in the blast
The bombs miss the palace entirely, hitting a nearby market

evt-02-27-1962-south-vietnam-air-force.butterflyEffect: Diem survived, though the palace was badly damaged and later demolished and rebuilt. Pilot Pham Phu Quoc was shot down and captured while Nguyen Van Cu escaped to Cambodia; the attack deepened Diem's paranoia and reliance on family for security, foreshadowing the coup that would kill him the following year.

evt-02-27-1963-dominican-republic.scenario: It is 27 February 1963, and you watch Juan Bosch sworn in as the Dominican Republic's first democratically elected president, following decades under the Trujillo dictatorship.
evt-02-27-1963-dominican-republic.prompt: What happens to Bosch's presidency within the year?

choices.text: He serves out a full, peaceful term uninterrupted
He is overthrown by a military coup later that year
He wins re-election the following year
He voluntarily resigns for health reasons within months

evt-02-27-1963-dominican-republic.butterflyEffect: Bosch was overthrown in a military coup in September 1963, just seven months into office. The instability that followed led to the 1965 civil war and a US Marine intervention, eventually paving the way for Joaquín Balaguer's long dominance of Dominican politics.

evt-02-27-1964-government-of-italy.scenario: It is 1964, and new measurements show the Leaning Tower of Pisa is tilting further each year, alarming officials who fear it could one day collapse.
evt-02-27-1964-government-of-italy.prompt: What does the Italian government do to address the worsening lean?

choices.text: Permanently close the surrounding piazza to all visitors and residents
Encase the entire tower in concrete within the year
Convene an international commission of engineers to study solutions
Immediately demolish the tower's upper floors to reduce weight

evt-02-27-1964-government-of-italy.butterflyEffect: The appeal launched decades of international study into stabilizing the tower. Real intervention came only in the 1990s, when lead counterweights and soil extraction from the north side reduced the lean by about 40 centimeters, letting the tower reopen safely to visitors in 2001.

evt-02-27-1973-american-indian-movement.scenario: On 27 February 1973, you're among roughly 200 Oglala Lakota and American Indian Movement activists who have just driven into the village of Wounded Knee, South Dakota, taking up positions and demanding federal action against reservation corruption.
evt-02-27-1973-american-indian-movement.prompt: What confrontation follows over the next several weeks?

choices.text: A prolonged armed siege with federal marshals and FBI agents surrounding the town
The U.S. Army bombs the occupied buildings
A peaceful negotiated withdrawal within 48 hours
Local police storm the town within days

evt-02-27-1973-american-indian-movement.butterflyEffect: The occupation became a 71-day armed siege, with federal marshals and FBI agents surrounding the town until a negotiated withdrawal ended it after two Native Americans were killed. The standoff drew international attention to Native rights, energizing AIM's activism through the rest of the decade even as promised treaty negotiations stalled.

evt-02-27-1976-western-sahara.scenario: It is 27 February 1976 in the desert of the former Spanish Sahara, one day after Spain formally ended its colonial administration and Moroccan and Mauritanian forces are moving into the territory.
evt-02-27-1976-western-sahara.prompt: What do Polisario Front leaders proclaim from exile in Algeria?

choices.text: Full union of the territory with Mauritania
The independent Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR)
Acceptance of the Moroccan-Mauritanian partition
A restored Spanish protectorate over the territory

evt-02-27-1976-western-sahara.butterflyEffect: Polisario declared the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR), rejecting the Moroccan-Mauritanian partition of the territory. The declaration launched a guerrilla war with Morocco that lasted until a 1991 ceasefire, and the sovereignty dispute remains unresolved at the UN and African Union today.

evt-02-27-1982-d-oyly-carte-opera-compan.scenario: You are a longtime singer with the D'Oyly Carte Opera Company in early 1982. After more than a century of touring Gilbert and Sullivan's Savoy operas almost without a break, the board tells the cast that funding has run dry and the company must close its doors.
evt-02-27-1982-d-oyly-carte-opera-compan.prompt: What happens to the D'Oyly Carte Opera Company after this closure?

choices.text: It relocates entirely to the United States to survive
It is nationalised and folded into the Royal Opera House
It disbands permanently with no future revival
It closes but is later revived for tours between 1988 and 2003

evt-02-27-1982-d-oyly-carte-opera-compan.butterflyEffect: The company folded in 1982, ending its unbroken run since the 1870s of touring the Savoy operas across Britain and abroad. It was not gone for good: a revived D'Oyly Carte returned for short seasons and tours between 1988 and 2003, keeping Gilbert and Sullivan's works alive on stage for a new generation before finally disbanding again.

evt-02-27-1988-sumgait.scenario: It is 27 February 1988, and you are an Armenian resident of Sumgait as ethnic tensions over Nagorno-Karabakh erupt into violent attacks on Armenian homes and families across the city.
evt-02-27-1988-sumgait.prompt: How did Soviet authorities respond as the violence continued over several days?

choices.text: The army arrived within hours and fully restored order immediately
Moscow declared martial law and evacuated the entire city that same night
Troops were slow to deploy, arriving only after days of unchecked violence
Local police alone stopped the violence before it spread

evt-02-27-1988-sumgait.butterflyEffect: Soviet Internal Troops were widely criticized for arriving only after the violence had raged for days, killing at least 26 people. The Sumgait pogrom became one of the opening atrocities of the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict, accelerating population exchanges between Armenia and Azerbaijan and foreshadowing the war that followed the Soviet collapse.

evt-02-27-1991-gulf-war.scenario: You are an advisor to President George H. W. Bush on 27 February 1991. Coalition forces have routed the Iraqi army and retaken Kuwait City, and Bush must decide whether to press the attack into Iraq itself or declare the war's objective achieved.
evt-02-27-1991-gulf-war.prompt: What does Bush decide to do once Kuwait is liberated?

choices.text: He orders a full advance on Baghdad to remove Saddam Hussein
He annexes southern Iraq as a buffer zone for Kuwait
He hands control of the campaign to the United Nations for further action
He declares a ceasefire, ending offensive operations with Kuwait liberated

evt-02-27-1991-gulf-war.butterflyEffect: Bush announced a ceasefire the next day, halting the coalition at Iraq's border and leaving Saddam Hussein in power. The decision avoided a costly occupation but left Saddam free to crush uprisings and remain a persistent threat, setting the stage for continued confrontation and the 2003 Iraq War.

evt-02-27-1996-pokemon.scenario: It's February 1996 in Nintendo's Kyoto offices. Game Freak has just finished Pocket Monsters Red and Green for the aging Game Boy, built around linking two cartridges together with a cable.
evt-02-27-1996-pokemon.prompt: What unusual design choice became the franchise's core hook?

choices.text: An always-online subscription service for battling strangers
Split into two paired versions, Red and Green, designed to be traded via link cable
A single cartridge bundled with a plastic toy pet
One fixed starter Pokémon to keep the game simple

evt-02-27-1996-pokemon.butterflyEffect: The games were split into two nearly identical versions so players had to trade to complete their collection, turning socializing into the core gameplay loop. That trading mechanic became the engine behind the card game, anime, and merchandise empire that grew into the world's highest-grossing media franchise.

evt-02-27-2002-2002-gujarat-violence.scenario: On 27 February 2002, news breaks that a train carrying Hindu pilgrims returning from Ayodhya has been set alight at Godhra station. You are a Gujarat state official facing the immediate aftermath.
evt-02-27-2002-2002-gujarat-violence.prompt: What widespread consequence follows in the days after the fire?

choices.text: The state government declares martial law and prevents any unrest
Communal riots erupt across Gujarat, lasting for months
The unrest is resolved within 24 hours through mediation
The violence remains contained to Godhra alone

evt-02-27-2002-2002-gujarat-violence.butterflyEffect: Communal riots swept across Gujarat for months, killing over a thousand people, mostly Muslims, amid accusations that the state government failed to act to stop the violence. The events became a defining, contested chapter in Indian politics, shaping the career of then chief minister Narendra Modi and prompting years of Supreme Court-monitored inquiries.

evt-02-27-2004-mv-superferry-14.scenario: It is 27 February 2004, hours after a bomb concealed inside a television set explodes aboard SuperFerry 14 in Manila Bay, and rescuers search the dark water for survivors.
evt-02-27-2004-mv-superferry-14.prompt: What does the Philippine government do in the wake of the country's deadliest terrorist attack?

choices.text: Treat the sinking as an accidental engine explosion
Overhaul maritime and port security screening procedures nationwide
Disband the national coast guard entirely
Negotiate a ransom directly with Abu Sayyaf

evt-02-27-2004-mv-superferry-14.butterflyEffect: Investigators confirmed Abu Sayyaf had planted the bomb, prompting sweeping reforms to Philippine port and ferry security screening. The attack also deepened US-Philippine counterterrorism cooperation and reinforced Abu Sayyaf's international designation as a terrorist organization.

evt-02-27-2010-2010-chile-earthquake.scenario: It's 3:34am on 27 February 2010. You're the duty officer at Chile's naval hydrographic service moments after a magnitude 8.8 earthquake rips through the coast, and the government is waiting on your call about a tsunami.
evt-02-27-2010-2010-chile-earthquake.prompt: What does the duty officer actually tell the government?

choices.text: Wait 24 hours for satellite confirmation before advising anything
Declare a state of emergency and order full coastal evacuation immediately
Recommend evacuating only the capital, Santiago
There's no significant tsunami risk, based on preliminary data

evt-02-27-2010-2010-chile-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The service mistakenly ruled out a major tsunami and the warning was cancelled; waves over ten meters high struck towns like Dichato and the Juan Fernández Islands with no alert, adding hundreds of preventable deaths. The failure led to SHOA losing its warning authority and the creation of a new national tsunami monitoring system.

evt-02-27-2015-boris-nemtsov.scenario: It is the night of 27 February 2015. You are walking across a bridge within sight of the Kremlin with a prominent Putin critic who has just spoken out against Russia's role in Ukraine, when gunfire suddenly rings out behind you.
evt-02-27-2015-boris-nemtsov.prompt: What follows in Moscow after this assassination becomes public?

choices.text: A binding no-confidence vote in the State Duma
Mass memorial marches in Moscow demanding a real investigation
An immediate resignation by Vladimir Putin
NATO intervention inside Russian territory

evt-02-27-2015-boris-nemtsov.butterflyEffect: Boris Nemtsov's killing on the bridge drew tens of thousands into memorial marches in Moscow, the largest opposition gathering in years. Investigators convicted low-level Chechen gunmen, but who ordered the killing was never conclusively established, and the case became a lasting symbol of the risks facing Kremlin critics.

evt-02-27-2019-pakistan-air-force.scenario: You are Indian Wing Commander Abhinandan Varthaman on 27 February 1991... you eject over Pakistani-controlled territory after your MiG-21 is shot down by a Pakistani JF-17 during a dogfight, and armed villagers and soldiers close in around you.
evt-02-27-2019-pakistan-air-force.prompt: What ultimately happens to the captured Indian pilot?

choices.text: He is put on trial for airspace violation
He is held indefinitely as a prisoner of war
He is exchanged for a captured Pakistani officer
He is returned to India within days as a goodwill gesture

evt-02-27-2019-pakistan-air-force.butterflyEffect: Pakistan captured Abhinandan and, after days of high tension between the nuclear-armed rivals, returned him to India as a peace gesture. The release helped de-escalate the crisis that followed the Balakot airstrikes, though the standoff left lasting mistrust between the two air forces.

evt-02-28-bce202-emperor-gaozu-of-han.scenario: It is 202 BCE at Sishui, days after Xiang Yu's defeat at Gaixia. You stand among the generals and nobles who followed Liu Bang through years of civil war, and they now press him to accept a new title.
evt-02-28-bce202-emperor-gaozu-of-han.prompt: What title do Liu Bang's followers urge him to accept?

choices.text: Chief Overlord under a puppet king
Regent for a Qin heir
King of Chu, reviving the old state
Emperor, founding a new dynasty

evt-02-28-bce202-emperor-gaozu-of-han.butterflyEffect: Liu Bang initially demurred but accepted the title of Emperor, founding the Han dynasty. Han rule lasted over four centuries, and its name became the ethnonym for the majority of the Chinese people to this day.

evt-02-28-1638-national-covenant.scenario: It is 28 February 1638 in Greyfriars Kirkyard, Edinburgh. A great parchment lies spread before you, condemning King Charles I's changes to Scottish worship, and ministers and nobles are lining up to add their names in blood and ink.
evt-02-28-1638-national-covenant.prompt: As a Scottish minister watching the crowd sign, what do you do?

choices.text: Refuse and publicly declare loyalty to the king's prayer book
Flee south to England to avoid taking a side
Sign the Covenant, joining the resistance to royal church reform
Write directly to Charles I asking him to withdraw the reforms quietly

evt-02-28-1638-national-covenant.butterflyEffect: Thousands signed the National Covenant across Scotland that year, binding Covenanters to resist the king's church reforms. The movement hardened into armed resistance in the Bishops' Wars, which drained Charles I's treasury and helped trigger the English Civil War a few years later.

evt-02-28-1874-tichborne-case.scenario: It's 28 February 1874, and after months of testimony you sit among the jury weighing the claim of the man known only as 'the Claimant' to be the long-lost heir to the Tichborne baronetcy.
evt-02-28-1874-tichborne-case.prompt: What did the court ultimately decide about the Claimant?

choices.text: He was confirmed as Sir Roger Tichborne and inherited the estate
The case ended in a hung jury with no verdict
He was acquitted but stripped of any claim to the estate
He was guilty of perjury and imprisoned for 14 years

evt-02-28-1874-tichborne-case.butterflyEffect: The Claimant, later identified as Arthur Orton, was convicted of perjury and served 14 years in prison. The case's twin trials—one civil, one criminal—became among the longest in English legal history to that date and fed lasting public fascination with mistaken identity and class pretension in Victorian Britain.

evt-02-28-1897-ranavalona-iii.scenario: You are Queen Ranavalona III in the royal palace at Antananarivo as French troops close in on the capital in 1895. Years of diplomacy have failed to keep Madagascar out of France's colonial grasp, and the palace itself is now under assault.
evt-02-28-1897-ranavalona-iii.prompt: What becomes of Queen Ranavalona III after the French seize her capital?

choices.text: She negotiates a power-sharing agreement and remains as ceremonial queen
She is deposed and exiled abroad, ending the Madagascar monarchy
She leads a successful counterattack that expels the French
She abdicates in favor of her prime minister, who continues resistance

evt-02-28-1897-ranavalona-iii.butterflyEffect: The French captured the palace in 1895 and formally ended the monarchy's sovereignty in 1897, exiling Ranavalona first to Réunion and later to Algeria, where she died never returning home. Her fall marked the end of centuries of Malagasy self-rule and the start of full French colonial administration of Madagascar.

evt-02-28-1914-balkan-wars.scenario: It is 28 February 1914 in Gjirokastër, a Greek-majority town the Great Powers have just assigned to the newly created state of Albania. You lead the local Greek community and must decide how to respond to this decision.
evt-02-28-1914-balkan-wars.prompt: What do you and fellow Epirote leaders proclaim in response?

choices.text: Proclaim an autonomous Republic of Northern Epirus
Petition quietly for Ottoman restoration of the region
Request immediate annexation and Greek military occupation
Accept incorporation into Albania without protest

evt-02-28-1914-balkan-wars.butterflyEffect: Georgios Christakis-Zografos declared the Autonomous Republic of Northern Epirus, briefly recognized under the Protocol of Corfu. The outbreak of World War I ended the arrangement, and the region was absorbed into Albania, leaving Greek-Albanian tensions over Epirus that lingered for decades.

evt-02-28-1928-c-v-raman.scenario: It is 28 February 1928 in a Calcutta laboratory. You are working alongside C. V. Raman, watching sunlight pass through a purified liquid, and you notice that some of the scattered light comes out at a different color than it went in.
evt-02-28-1928-c-v-raman.prompt: How do you interpret this unexpected change in the scattered light?

choices.text: Dismiss it as ordinary fluorescence and move on
Conclude it is a genuinely new type of scattering with a shifted wavelength
Attribute it to the Doppler effect from a moving source
Assume it is an instrument calibration error

evt-02-28-1928-c-v-raman.butterflyEffect: Raman and his student K. S. Krishnan correctly identified this as a new phenomenon, later named the Raman effect, in which scattered light shifts wavelength by interacting with a molecule's vibrations. It won Raman the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics, made him the first Asian laureate in the field, and gave science Raman spectroscopy, now vital across chemistry and materials analysis; India marks the discovery date as National Science Day.

evt-02-28-1947-nationalist-government.scenario: It is 28 February 1947 in Taipei. Anger over the beating of a widow selling untaxed cigarettes has spread into mass protest, and Nationalist government troops have opened fire on the crowds gathered outside the Governor-General's office.
evt-02-28-1947-nationalist-government.prompt: What followed this crackdown across the island in the years after?

choices.text: A negotiated power-sharing democracy established within months
Martial law and decades of authoritarian suppression known as the White Terror
Transfer of Taiwan back to Japanese administration
Immediate withdrawal of all Nationalist forces from Taiwan

evt-02-28-1947-nationalist-government.butterflyEffect: The killings sparked an island-wide uprising that was violently suppressed, and the Kuomintang government imposed martial law that lasted until 1987, ushering in the decades-long White Terror. The event, long suppressed from official memory, later became a founding grievance of Taiwan's democracy movement, and 28 February is now a national memorial day.

evt-02-28-1966-charles-bassett.scenario: It is 28 February 1966 over Lambert Field, St. Louis. You are flying a T-38 trainer toward McDonnell Aircraft's plant, where your Gemini 9 spacecraft awaits, but thick fog and low cloud have swallowed the runway ahead.
evt-02-28-1966-charles-bassett.prompt: As the pilot in poor visibility near the factory, what should you do?

choices.text: Break off and divert to an airport with clearer weather
Attempt a steep visual turn to land directly at the plant despite the fog
Request a full instrument approach and go-around procedure
Circle at altitude until ground control confirms the runway is visible

evt-02-28-1966-charles-bassett.butterflyEffect: Command pilot Elliot See attempted a tight visual approach through the fog and the T-38 struck the roof of the McDonnell building, killing both See and Charles Bassett instantly. Their backup crew, Tom Stafford and Gene Cernan, were promoted to fly Gemini 9 in their place, a routine reshuffle that placed Cernan on the path to later fly Apollo 10 and command Apollo 17.

evt-02-28-1972-law-enforcement-in-japan.scenario: It's 28 February 1972, day ten of a standoff at a snowbound mountain lodge near Karuizawa. Inside, United Red Army members hold a hostage; outside, you command the assembled riot police preparing for a final assault.
evt-02-28-1972-law-enforcement-in-japan.prompt: What did police actually do to end the siege?

choices.text: Called in the Self-Defense Forces to shell the building
Waited out the radicals until food and heat ran out
Negotiated a peaceful surrender after new terms were agreed
Stormed the lodge in a televised assault, freeing the hostage

evt-02-28-1972-law-enforcement-in-japan.butterflyEffect: Police stormed the Asama-Sansō lodge live on national television, rescuing the hostage after a costly assault that killed two officers. The operation, along with revelations of brutal internal purges within the United Red Army, discredited the armed New Left and hastened the decline of radical student militancy in Japan.

evt-02-28-1974-february-1974-united-king.scenario: It is the morning after the 28 February 1974 election. You are Prime Minister Edward Heath, and the results show Labour with more seats than you but no party holding a majority. The Liberals hold the balance.
evt-02-28-1974-february-1974-united-king.prompt: As Heath, what do you do to try to stay in office?

choices.text: Resign immediately without seeking any coalition
Form an emergency pact with Ulster Unionist MPs alone
Call an immediate second election within days
Negotiate a coalition with the Liberal Party to remain in government

evt-02-28-1974-february-1974-united-king.butterflyEffect: Heath opened talks with Liberal leader Jeremy Thorpe about a coalition, but the two sides could not agree on terms, particularly over electoral reform. Heath resigned days later, and Harold Wilson formed a minority Labour government, calling a fresh election that October to secure a working majority.

evt-02-28-1975-london-underground.scenario: It is the morning of 28 February 1975 at Moorgate station. A southbound Northern City Line train is approaching the dead-end terminal platform, but it fails to slow down as it nears the buffers.
evt-02-28-1975-london-underground.prompt: What safety change did London Underground introduce at dead-end platforms after this crash?

choices.text: Mandatory alcohol testing for all drivers before every shift
Removal of all dead-end terminal platforms from the network
An automatic system that enforces braking on approach to dead-end platforms
Installation of platform screen doors at every station

evt-02-28-1975-london-underground.butterflyEffect: The train ploughed into the tunnel end wall at speed, killing 43 people in the worst peacetime disaster on the Underground. In response, engineers developed the 'Moorgate control' system, an automatic device that forces trains to slow as they approach dead-end platforms, now standard across the network.

evt-02-28-1985-the-troubles.scenario: It's the evening of 28 February 1985 at the RUC base in Newry, County Down. You are an officer on break in the station's portable canteen, unaware that a homemade mortar has just been fired from a hijacked lorry outside.
evt-02-28-1985-the-troubles.prompt: What changed in RUC station security after this mortar attack?

choices.text: British troops replaced all RUC officers in border areas
All RUC bases were rebuilt with blast-resistant fortifications
The RUC disbanded rural border stations entirely
The RUC adopted a policy of unarmed patrols

evt-02-28-1985-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The attack killed nine RUC officers, the force's worst single loss of the Troubles. In response, the RUC and British government invested heavily in reinforced, blast-proof police stations across Northern Ireland, permanently changing the look and character of policing along the border for the rest of the conflict.

evt-02-28-1997-grb-970228.scenario: It's 28 February 1997, and the Italian-Dutch BeppoSAX satellite has just detected an intense 80-second flash of gamma rays. As the responsible astronomer, you must decide whether it's worth swinging ground telescopes toward the fading source to search for an afterglow no one has ever definitively captured before.
evt-02-28-1997-grb-970228.prompt: What did the follow-up observations of GRB 970228 actually reveal?

choices.text: A nearby supernova within our own galaxy
A previously unknown pulsar in the Milky Way's disk
An afterglow that proved gamma-ray bursts originate in distant galaxies
Evidence that gamma-ray bursts were solar flares

evt-02-28-1997-grb-970228.butterflyEffect: The detected afterglow, and the faint host galaxy later imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope, proved GRBs occur at cosmological distances rather than within the Milky Way. This ended a decades-long debate over the distance scale of gamma-ray bursts and opened the field of GRB afterglow astronomy that continues today.

evt-02-28-1997-north-hollywood-shootout.scenario: It is 28 February 1997 in North Hollywood. Two robbers in body armor are firing automatic rifles at you and your fellow officers, and your service pistols are useless against their gear.
evt-02-28-1997-north-hollywood-shootout.prompt: As an LAPD officer pinned down by rifle fire, what do you do?

choices.text: Continue firing handguns and hope for a lucky hit
Run to a local gun store to borrow rifles for the officers on scene
Call in an armored vehicle to ram the robbers' car immediately
Retreat and wait for a SWAT team to arrive with heavier weapons

evt-02-28-1997-north-hollywood-shootout.butterflyEffect: Officers ran to a nearby gun shop and borrowed rifles and ammunition to match the robbers' firepower, eventually killing both men. The shootout exposed how outgunned patrol officers were and pushed police departments nationwide to arm patrol cars with rifles.

evt-02-28-2002-2002-gujarat-violence.scenario: It is 1 March 2002, and reports reach New Delhi that rioting has spread across Ahmedabad following the Godhra train fire the day before. As a Union Home Ministry official, you must decide how to respond to the escalating violence.
evt-02-28-2002-2002-gujarat-violence.prompt: What did the central government actually do to try to stop the violence?

choices.text: Rely solely on state police to restore order
Impose President's Rule and dissolve the state government
Call in only the paramilitary Rapid Action Force
Deploy the Indian Army to restore order

evt-02-28-2002-2002-gujarat-violence.butterflyEffect: The Indian Army was deployed on 1 March, but by then extensive damage had already occurred, and critics said the response came too late. The unrest continued sporadically for months and left a lasting political controversy, with years of court cases and a Supreme Court-ordered investigation into the Godhra fire and subsequent killings.

evt-02-28-2023-tempi-train-crash.scenario: It is the night of 28 February 2023 near the Tempe Valley, Greece. A passenger train and a freight train are approaching each other on what should be separate tracks, but the automated signaling and traffic control systems along this line have been non-functional for years.
evt-02-28-2023-tempi-train-crash.prompt: What ultimately allowed both trains onto the same section of track?

choices.text: A manual signaling decision by a station manager, unchecked by any working automatic system
A deliberate act of sabotage on the line
A driver ignoring a functioning red signal
A software glitch in a fully automated modern control system

evt-02-28-2023-tempi-train-crash.butterflyEffect: A station manager manually directed the intercity passenger train onto the same line as an oncoming freight train, an error the broken automatic block system would normally have prevented. The head-on collision and resulting fire killed 57 people, triggering nationwide protests over decades of underinvestment in Greek rail safety and the resignation of the transport minister.

evt-02-29-1704-queen-anne-s-war.scenario: It is before dawn on 29 February 1704 in the frontier town of Deerfield, Massachusetts. Snow has drifted high against the wooden palisade, and a French and Native American war party is creeping toward the wall under cover of darkness.
evt-02-29-1704-queen-anne-s-war.prompt: What actually let the attackers get inside the town's defenses?

choices.text: The palisade held firm and the raid was repelled
Snowdrifts let the attackers climb over the wall undetected
The town bell sounded early enough for everyone to flee
A resident secretly opened the town gate for them

evt-02-29-1704-queen-anne-s-war.butterflyEffect: The snowbanks let raiders climb over the palisade before sentries could raise a full alarm. Dozens of settlers were killed and more than 100 were marched north as captives to New France; several, like young Eunice Williams, chose to remain and were assimilated into Mohawk communities, becoming enduring symbols of the era's brutal, blurred frontier.

evt-02-29-1960-1960-agadir-earthquake.scenario: It is early March 1960. You are a Moroccan official surveying Agadir's ruins after a shallow, violent quake leveled the Kasbah, Founty, and Talborjt, killing thousands in seconds.
evt-02-29-1960-1960-agadir-earthquake.prompt: What does King Mohammed V decide about the shattered city?

choices.text: Move the regional capital inland permanently
Rebuild immediately on the same foundations
Abandon the site and disperse the population nationwide
Evacuate the ruins and rebuild the city under new safety codes

evt-02-29-1960-1960-agadir-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The king ordered survivors evacuated and forbade rebuilding on the most dangerous ground, commissioning a new city built to modern seismic standards. The rebuilt Agadir became a model for earthquake-resistant urban planning in Morocco.

evt-02-29-1972-south-vietnam.scenario: It is early 1972 and you are a South Korean staff officer in Saigon, reviewing new orders from Seoul as Washington pushes allies to reduce their footprint in Vietnam.
evt-02-29-1972-south-vietnam.prompt: What does Seoul order regarding its 48,000 troops in South Vietnam?

choices.text: Withdraw 11,000 troops as a partial drawdown
Rotate troops into training-only roles with no reduction
Send additional reinforcements
Withdraw the entire force at once

evt-02-29-1972-south-vietnam.butterflyEffect: South Korea withdrew 11,000 troops as a first step, mirroring the American 'Vietnamization' policy of shifting the war onto South Vietnamese forces. Korean forces continued drawing down and were fully withdrawn by 1973, shortly before the Paris Peace Accords ended direct US involvement.

evt-02-29-1984-pierre-trudeau.scenario: It is 29 February 1984, and after a solitary walk in a snowstorm the night before, you decide the time has come to step down as Liberal leader and Prime Minister of Canada.
evt-02-29-1984-pierre-trudeau.prompt: What happens within the Liberal Party after Trudeau's announcement?

choices.text: John Turner wins the leadership and becomes Prime Minister
Parliament is dissolved before a new leader is chosen
Trudeau reverses his decision days later
Jean Chrétien immediately succeeds Trudeau unopposed

evt-02-29-1984-pierre-trudeau.butterflyEffect: John Turner won the ensuing leadership race and became Prime Minister, but he called a snap election that summer. Brian Mulroney's Progressive Conservatives won a landslide, ending sixteen years of near-continuous Liberal government.

evt-02-29-1988-desmond-tutu.scenario: It's 29 February 1988 in Cape Town. You are one of over 100 clergy marching toward Parliament to demand the release of anti-apartheid detainees, with Archbishop Desmond Tutu at the front as police form a line to block you.
evt-02-29-1988-desmond-tutu.prompt: What do you do as the police order the march to disperse?

choices.text: Kneel in prayer and continue the demonstration
Disperse immediately to avoid confrontation
Retreat and reroute the march quietly
Throw stones at the police line

evt-02-29-1988-desmond-tutu.butterflyEffect: Tutu and the other clergy held their ground and were arrested en masse, an image that traveled worldwide and underscored the moral bankruptcy of apartheid's crackdown on peaceful dissent. The arrests added to mounting international pressure that, within two years, helped push the government toward negotiations and Nelson Mandela's release.

evt-02-29-1992-socialist-republic-of-bos.scenario: It's 29 February 1992 in Sarajevo. Ballots are open for a referendum on independence from Yugoslavia, but Bosnian Serb leaders have called for a boycott and warned of grave consequences if it passes.
evt-02-29-1992-socialist-republic-of-bos.prompt: As a non-Serb resident, what do you do at the polling station?

choices.text: Boycott the vote alongside Bosnian Serb leaders
Vote against independence to preserve Yugoslavia
Stay home out of fear of violence
Cast a ballot in favor of independence

evt-02-29-1992-socialist-republic-of-bos.butterflyEffect: Turnout reached about 64%, with over 99% of those voting choosing independence, since most Bosnian Serbs stayed away as urged. Bosnia and Herzegovina declared independence weeks later, and Serb forces began mobilizing almost immediately, tipping the region into the Bosnian War.

evt-02-29-2000-second-chechen-war.scenario: It is 29 February 2000, and you command a company of Russian paratroopers holding a narrow pass near Ulus Kert as a much larger force of Chechen fighters attempts to break through your position.
evt-02-29-2000-second-chechen-war.prompt: What do you decide to do when retreat would save your men but let the rebels through?

choices.text: Negotiate a local truce with the fighters
Withdraw the company to preserve the men
Split the company to flank the rebels covertly
Hold the pass and call in artillery support

evt-02-29-2000-second-chechen-war.butterflyEffect: The paratroopers refused to withdraw and called artillery fire onto their own position in the battle's final hours, and nearly all of the roughly ninety men were killed. The stand blocked the rebel breakout and became a celebrated symbol of sacrifice in Russia, with many of the dead posthumously awarded Hero of Russia.

evt-02-29-2004-jean-bertrand-aristide.scenario: It is 29 February 2004. Armed rebels control much of Haiti, foreign governments are urging you to go, and you must decide how to respond to the collapsing situation as President.
evt-02-29-2004-jean-bertrand-aristide.prompt: What does Aristide do as the rebellion closes in?

choices.text: He resigns and leaves the country into exile
He calls on US troops to crush the rebellion
He arms loyalist militias and fights on
He appeals directly to the UN Security Council for troops to defend him

evt-02-29-2004-jean-bertrand-aristide.butterflyEffect: Aristide resigned and was flown out of Haiti to the Central African Republic, later relocating to exile in South Africa; he claimed the US and France had forced him out. An interim government took power backed by a UN peacekeeping mission, and Aristide did not return to Haiti until 2011.

evt-02-29-2012-tokyo-skytree.scenario: You're a structural engineer working on Tokyo Skytree in the years before its 2012 completion, aware that Japan's earthquakes could devastate a tower this tall.
evt-02-29-2012-tokyo-skytree.prompt: What earthquake-damping design do you build into the tower's core?

choices.text: A rigid steel exoskeleton with no separate core
Deep foundation piles alone, with a stiff uniform frame above
A central pendulum-like concrete cylinder inspired by pagoda design
A fully flexible outer frame with no internal support core

evt-02-29-2012-tokyo-skytree.butterflyEffect: Engineers built a central concrete cylinder that moves independently of the outer steel lattice, inspired by the shinbashira pillar found in centuries-old five-story pagodas. The system reportedly cut vibration by up to half, letting the still-unfinished tower ride out the massive 2011 Tōhoku earthquake undamaged and influencing seismic design in other supertall structures.

evt-02-29-2020-united-states.scenario: It is February 29, 2020, in Doha. You are part of the American delegation finalizing an agreement with Taliban negotiators after months of talks aimed at ending America's longest war.
evt-02-29-2020-united-states.prompt: What does the US commit to in exchange for Taliban counterterrorism guarantees?

choices.text: Withdrawal only after nationwide Afghan elections
A phased withdrawal of all US troops within 14 months
Immediate withdrawal within 30 days
A permanent reduction to 5,000 troops with no further drawdown

evt-02-29-2020-united-states.butterflyEffect: The Doha Agreement set a 14-month timeline for full US withdrawal, contingent on Taliban commitments to deny sanctuary to al-Qaeda and negotiate with the Afghan government. Withdrawal proceeded through 2021, ending with the Taliban's swift return to power in Kabul that August.

evt-02-29-2020-muhyiddin-yassin.scenario: It is 29 February 2020. Malaysia's government has just collapsed amid mass defections, and as King you must decide who commands the confidence of Parliament to become the next Prime Minister.
evt-02-29-2020-muhyiddin-yassin.prompt: How does the King resolve the deadlock?

choices.text: He appoints Anwar Ibrahim as the opposition leader
He appoints Muhyiddin Yassin after gauging MPs' support individually
He dissolves Parliament for an immediate snap election
He reinstates the outgoing Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad

evt-02-29-2020-muhyiddin-yassin.butterflyEffect: The King interviewed MPs individually and determined Muhyiddin Yassin held majority support, appointing him without a parliamentary vote. Muhyiddin's fragile coalition collapsed within eighteen months amid pandemic missteps, ushering in a period of unstable, rapidly changing governments in Malaysia.

evt-02-29-2020-luxembourg.scenario: You're Luxembourg's transport minister in the late 2010s. Your tiny country has the highest car-ownership rate in Europe and rush-hour gridlock chokes the capital every morning.
evt-02-29-2020-luxembourg.prompt: What bold policy do you push through to get cars off the road?

choices.text: Raise fuel taxes and leave transit fares unchanged
Build more highway lanes into the city centre
Make all public transport free of charge
Ban private cars from the capital outright

evt-02-29-2020-luxembourg.butterflyEffect: On 29 February 2020 Luxembourg abolished fares on all buses, trams and trains nationwide, becoming the first country to make public transport entirely free. The move drew global attention as a model for tackling congestion and emissions, and other cities studied it as a test case for fare-free transit.

evt-02-29-2024-flour-massacre.scenario: It is 29 February 2024, and you are among the international observers watching reports emerge from al-Rashid Street in Gaza City, where gunfire scattered a crowd gathered around aid trucks, killing and wounding hundreds.
evt-02-29-2024-flour-massacre.prompt: What major shift in humanitarian aid delivery follows this tragedy?

choices.text: The UN takes over all aid distribution in Gaza
The US begins airdropping aid into Gaza
A full ceasefire is declared within days
Israel immediately opens all land crossings unconditionally

evt-02-29-2024-flour-massacre.butterflyEffect: In the following days, the United States and allies began airdropping food into Gaza and started building a temporary sea pier to increase the flow of supplies. The killings intensified international criticism of aid access restrictions and added pressure toward ceasefire talks.

evt-03-01-1562-francois-duke-of-guise.scenario: It's March 1, 1562, in the town of Wassy, and you ride with the retinue of François, Duke of Guise, as he comes upon hundreds of Huguenots gathered for a forbidden church service nearby.
evt-03-01-1562-francois-duke-of-guise.prompt: What did the Duke's confrontation with the worshippers set in motion?

choices.text: The Duke's own arrest for disturbing the peace
The opening violence of the French Wars of Religion
A royal decree granting Huguenots full toleration
A negotiated truce that preserved religious peace

evt-03-01-1562-francois-duke-of-guise.butterflyEffect: The clash, remembered as the Massacre of Wassy, left dozens of Huguenots dead and is traditionally regarded as the spark that ignited the French Wars of Religion. The conflict between Catholics and Protestants would tear France apart for decades, ending only with the Edict of Nantes in 1598.

evt-03-01-1805-samuel-chase.scenario: It's March 1, 1805, and you are a United States Senator sitting in judgment of Supreme Court Justice Samuel Chase, who stands accused of letting his fierce Federalist politics corrupt his rulings from the bench.
evt-03-01-1805-samuel-chase.prompt: How does the Senate ultimately rule on Chase's impeachment?

choices.text: Censure him publicly but let the trial continue for years
Acquit him, allowing him to remain a sitting Justice
Convict him, removing him from the Supreme Court
Refer the matter to a federal court for a criminal trial

evt-03-01-1805-samuel-chase.butterflyEffect: The Senate failed to reach the two-thirds majority needed on any article, and Chase was acquitted, keeping his seat until his death in 1811. The outcome established that judges could not be removed simply for unpopular or partisan rulings, cementing the principle of judicial independence in the young republic.

evt-03-01-1869-dmitri-mendeleev.scenario: It is 1869 in St Petersburg. You watch chemist Dmitri Mendeleev arrange cards of the known elements by atomic weight again and again, hunting for a pattern no one else has found.
evt-03-01-1869-dmitri-mendeleev.prompt: What bold choice does Mendeleev make that other chemists hadn't dared?

choices.text: He leaves blank spaces for elements not yet discovered, predicting their properties
He orders elements strictly by their date of discovery
He groups elements only by color and physical appearance
He rejects atomic weight as unreliable and removes it from the table

evt-03-01-1869-dmitri-mendeleev.butterflyEffect: He left blank spaces in his table for elements not yet discovered, predicting their properties in advance. Within his lifetime, gallium, scandium, and germanium were found matching his predictions almost exactly, cementing the periodic law as chemistry's organizing framework and guiding the later search for new elements, including mendelevium.

evt-03-01-1870-paraguayan-war.scenario: It is 1 March 1870 in the forests of Cerro Corá. You stand with the last remnants of Paraguay's army beside Marshal Francisco Solano López as Brazilian cavalry close in on the camp.
evt-03-01-1870-paraguayan-war.prompt: What happens to López as the Brazilian troops close in?

choices.text: He is captured alive and exiled to Europe
He escapes across the border into Argentina
He refuses to surrender and is killed in the fighting
He negotiates a truce and keeps partial power

evt-03-01-1870-paraguayan-war.butterflyEffect: López refused to surrender and was killed in the fighting at Cerro Corá, ending organized Paraguayan resistance and the war itself. Paraguay, having lost a staggering share of its population, was forced to cede territory to Brazil and Argentina and spent generations rebuilding.

evt-03-01-1872-yellowstone-national-park.scenario: You're a member of Congress in early 1872, weighing a bill to protect the geysers and hot springs of the Yellowstone region from railroad speculators eager to fence and sell the land.
evt-03-01-1872-yellowstone-national-park.prompt: What does Congress ultimately decide to do with the Yellowstone region?

choices.text: Leave management entirely to the Wyoming Territory
Sell the land to a railroad company for development
Open the region to homesteading claims
Set the land aside as the first national park

evt-03-01-1872-yellowstone-national-park.butterflyEffect: On 1 March 1872 Congress set the land aside as Yellowstone National Park, the first national park in the world, placing it beyond private sale or settlement. The idea spread rapidly, inspiring the founding of the National Park Service in 1916 and similar protected parks in dozens of other countries.

evt-03-01-1896-battle-of-adwa.scenario: It's March 1, 1896, near the town of Adwa, and you stand in Emperor Menelik II's army as it clashes with the invading Italian colonial force of General Oreste Baratieri.
evt-03-01-1896-battle-of-adwa.prompt: What did the Ethiopian victory secure for the empire?

choices.text: A partition of Ethiopian territory between Italy and Britain
Status as an Italian protectorate with local autonomy
Recognition as an independent empire free of Italian colonial rule
Full annexation into Italian East Africa

evt-03-01-1896-battle-of-adwa.butterflyEffect: Italy was forced to recognize Ethiopian sovereignty in the Treaty of Addis Ababa, making Ethiopia one of the only African states to defeat a European power and preserve its independence during the Scramble for Africa. The humiliation lingered in Italian memory and was a factor Mussolini cited decades later when he invaded Ethiopia in 1935.

evt-03-01-1896-henri-becquerel.scenario: It's February 1896 in Paris. You're testing whether uranium salts glow after sunlight exposure, but overcast skies keep ruining the experiment, so you shut the wrapped photographic plates with a uranium sample in a dark drawer for days.
evt-03-01-1896-henri-becquerel.prompt: With no sunlight to trigger phosphorescence, what do you do with the plates?

choices.text: Develop them anyway, out of curiosity
Wait for a sunny day and start over
Switch to a different phosphorescent mineral
Discard them, assuming the experiment has failed

evt-03-01-1896-henri-becquerel.butterflyEffect: Becquerel developed the plates anyway and found them strongly fogged, proving the uranium emitted radiation with no external energy source. This accidental discovery of radioactivity launched Marie and Pierre Curie's research and, ultimately, the nuclear age.

evt-03-01-1921-kronstadt-rebellion.scenario: It's early March 1921, and you're a sailor manning the ice-bound fortress of Kronstadt, having just voted with your comrades for free elections to the soviets and an end to Bolshevik grain requisitioning.
evt-03-01-1921-kronstadt-rebellion.prompt: What happens when Trotsky sends the Red Army across the frozen gulf to retake the fortress?

choices.text: The assault crushes the rebellion within days
The uprising spreads and topples the Bolshevik government
The sailors successfully defect to White Russian forces
Lenin negotiates a lasting peace with the sailors

evt-03-01-1921-kronstadt-rebellion.butterflyEffect: Red Army troops stormed Kronstadt on 17-18 March 1921, crushing the rebellion at heavy cost to both sides, with survivors executed or sent to labor camps. The revolt shook Lenin badly enough that he abandoned War Communism days later for the New Economic Policy, allowing limited private trade.

evt-03-01-1936-hoover-dam.scenario: You're an engineer on the Hoover Dam project in the Black Canyon, watching crews pour a mass of concrete so vast that ordinary curing would take a century and could crack the structure apart.
evt-03-01-1936-hoover-dam.prompt: What method do engineers use to cool and cure the enormous concrete pour safely?

choices.text: Pack the concrete with ice blocks hauled in by rail
Embed cooling pipes and circulate river water through the concrete
Let the concrete cure naturally over many decades
Pour the entire dam as one continuous uninterrupted mass

evt-03-01-1936-hoover-dam.butterflyEffect: Workers embedded nearly 600 miles of steel pipe throughout the concrete and circulated cold river water through it to draw out curing heat block by block. The technique let the dam cure in about two years instead of a century, and it became the standard method for building large concrete dams worldwide.

evt-03-01-1950-klaus-fuchs.scenario: It is late February 1950 at the Old Bailey in London. You watch the trial of physicist Klaus Fuchs, who once calculated blast yields at Los Alamos, reach a verdict in under 90 minutes.
evt-03-01-1950-klaus-fuchs.prompt: What sentence does the court hand down to Fuchs?

choices.text: Death by execution for treason
Fourteen years in prison, the maximum under the Official Secrets Act
Deportation to the Soviet Union
Life imprisonment without parole

evt-03-01-1950-klaus-fuchs.butterflyEffect: Fuchs received fourteen years, the maximum under the Official Secrets Act, but served only nine before release and resettlement in East Germany, where he resumed his physics career. His espionage had already accelerated Soviet development of atomic and hydrogen weapons, intensifying the arms race and fueling Western fears that drove the spy scandals of the early Cold War.

evt-03-01-1973-pink-floyd.scenario: It's March 1, 1973, and you're a sound engineer at Abbey Road Studios watching the band mix the final cut of an album built from tape loops, synthesizers, and spliced interview tapes.
evt-03-01-1973-pink-floyd.prompt: What happened to this album on the record charts in the decades that followed?

choices.text: It flopped commercially and was quickly forgotten
It set a record for the longest run on the Billboard 200 chart
It only became popular decades later after the band's breakup
It was banned from radio play across Europe

evt-03-01-1973-pink-floyd.butterflyEffect: The Dark Side of the Moon became one of the best-selling albums in history and set a record for chart longevity, remaining on the Billboard 200 for over 700 weeks. Its layered production and thematic ambition helped define progressive rock and influenced how entire albums could be conceived as unified artistic statements.

evt-03-01-1992-serbs-of-bosnia-and-herze.scenario: It's March 1, 1992, in Sarajevo's old town, and gunfire suddenly erupts as a Bosnian Serb wedding procession carrying a Serbian flag moves through the city during the independence referendum.
evt-03-01-1992-serbs-of-bosnia-and-herze.prompt: What did this shooting come to be seen as in the years that followed?

choices.text: An isolated crime with no political consequences
A minor dispute settled quickly by city police
The event that triggered immediate NATO airstrikes
An incident later seen as an early spark of the Bosnian War

evt-03-01-1992-serbs-of-bosnia-and-herze.butterflyEffect: The groom's father was killed in the attack, and Bosnian Serb nationalists cited it as justification when barricades went up across Sarajevo days later. The incident is widely remembered as one of the first violent flashpoints leading directly into the Siege of Sarajevo and the wider Bosnian War.

evt-03-01-1992-bosnia-and-herzegovina.scenario: It's March 1, 1992, and you stand in line at a polling station in Sarajevo for the independence referendum, while Bosnian Serb leaders call for a boycott and paramilitary checkpoints spring up around the city.
evt-03-01-1992-bosnia-and-herzegovina.prompt: What do Bosnia's leaders do once the referendum passes with overwhelming support?

choices.text: Petition to join Croatia outright
Immediately partition the republic into three separate states
Agree to remain in a reformed Yugoslav federation
Declare full independence from Yugoslavia

evt-03-01-1992-bosnia-and-herzegovina.butterflyEffect: On 3 March 1992 Bosnia and Herzegovina declared independence from Yugoslavia, and the European Community and United States recognized it that April. Bosnian Serb forces, rejecting the vote, besieged Sarajevo within weeks, igniting a war that would last until 1995.

evt-03-01-2002-war-in-afghanistan-2001-2.scenario: It is early morning on 2 March 2002 in Afghanistan's Shahikot Valley. You are among the U.S. and allied troops helicoptering in, briefed to expect a quick sweep against a few hundred fleeing fighters.
evt-03-01-2002-war-in-afghanistan-2001-2.prompt: What actually followed as your forces hit the valley floor?

choices.text: A sudden sandstorm forced withdrawal before any contact was made
The valley was found empty, the fighters having fled overnight
Local Afghan militia surrendered the position without a fight
Entrenched al-Qaeda and Taliban fighters pinned troops down with heavy mortar and machine-gun fire

evt-03-01-2002-war-in-afghanistan-2001-2.butterflyEffect: Entrenched al-Qaeda and Taliban fighters pinned troops down with mortar and machine-gun fire, turning Operation Anaconda into days of hard fighting rather than a quick raid. Many fighters escaped into Pakistan's tribal areas, exposing coordination gaps between air, ground, and Afghan allied forces that foreshadowed the long insurgency to come.

evt-03-01-2002-envisat.scenario: It is 1 March 2002 at the Guiana Space Centre. You watch Envisat, the largest civilian Earth-observation satellite ever built, lift off atop an Ariane 5 rocket into polar orbit.
evt-03-01-2002-envisat.prompt: What happens to Envisat a decade later, abruptly ending its mission?

choices.text: A solar panel malfunction causes it to explode
It loses contact with ground control and becomes derelict
It is retrieved by a Space Shuttle for repairs
It is safely deorbited into the Pacific Ocean

evt-03-01-2002-envisat.butterflyEffect: In April 2012, ESA suddenly and permanently lost contact with Envisat. Still orbiting at nearly 800 km, it became one of the largest pieces of space debris, spurring research into active debris-removal missions to prevent collisions in Earth orbit.

evt-03-01-2002-space-shuttle-columbia.scenario: You're a spacewalking astronaut aboard Columbia on STS-109 in March 2002, floating beside the Hubble Space Telescope with a fresh set of hardware waiting to be bolted into place.
evt-03-01-2002-space-shuttle-columbia.prompt: Which major upgrade do you and your crewmates install on Hubble during this servicing mission?

choices.text: New rigid solar arrays and the Advanced Camera for Surveys
The telescope's original primary mirror
Its first-ever set of gyroscopes
The wide-field camera flown on its maiden launch

evt-03-01-2002-space-shuttle-columbia.butterflyEffect: The STS-109 crew fitted Hubble with new rigid solar arrays and the Advanced Camera for Surveys, dramatically boosting its power and image quality for years of discoveries to come. It was Columbia's last successful mission before the orbiter was lost on STS-107 in February 2003.

evt-03-01-2006-english-wikipedia.scenario: It's 2006 and you're an English Wikipedia editor watching the article counter climb toward a symbolic milestone: one million articles, all written by volunteers.
evt-03-01-2006-english-wikipedia.prompt: Which unglamorous topic actually became the millionth article?

choices.text: A biography of Albert Einstein
Jordanhill railway station, a Scottish commuter stop
A page about a popular video game character
An article on the Great Wall of China

evt-03-01-2006-english-wikipedia.butterflyEffect: The honor went to Jordanhill railway station, a minor Scottish stop — a fittingly mundane symbol of Wikipedia's exhaustive, crowd-built scope. The encyclopedia kept growing exponentially, passing six million English articles within two decades.

evt-03-01-2014-2014-kunming-attack.scenario: You're an armed police officer rushing into the ticket hall of Kunming Railway Station, where knife-wielding attackers are moving through the crowd on the evening of 1 March 2014.
evt-03-01-2014-2014-kunming-attack.prompt: What immediate action by police brings the attack to an end?

choices.text: Negotiators persuade the attackers to surrender peacefully
The station is fully evacuated before the attackers arrive
Station staff subdue the attackers with fire extinguishers
Officers open fire, killing four attackers at the scene

evt-03-01-2014-2014-kunming-attack.butterflyEffect: Police shot four of the attackers dead at the scene and wounded and captured a fifth; the remaining members of the group were arrested within days. Beijing labeled the assault a terrorist act tied to Xinjiang separatism, and it became a turning point that hardened China's security crackdown across Xinjiang in the years that followed.

evt-03-02-1444-league-of-lezhe.scenario: It is March 2, 1444, in the town of Lezhë. You are one of the Albanian nobles Skanderbeg has summoned, and your rival princedoms must choose whether to keep feuding or stand together against the advancing Ottoman Empire.
evt-03-02-1444-league-of-lezhe.prompt: What did the assembled chieftains agree to do?

choices.text: Agree to pay tribute directly to the Ottoman sultan
Unite in a military alliance under Skanderbeg's leadership
Divide the region into smaller independent fiefs
Submit their lands to Venetian protection

evt-03-02-1444-league-of-lezhe.butterflyEffect: The nobles formed a military and diplomatic alliance under Skanderbeg, the League of Lezhë, the first unified Albanian political entity of the Middle Ages. It sustained Albanian resistance to Ottoman conquest for over two decades and became a foundational symbol later invoked during Albania's 20th-century independence movement.

evt-03-02-1484-college-of-arms.scenario: You are a herald in London on 2 March 1484. King Richard III has summoned the officers of arms to grant them formal royal recognition and a shared headquarters at Coldharbour.
evt-03-02-1484-college-of-arms.prompt: What does the king's charter actually do for the heralds?

choices.text: It grants them full independence from the Crown
It abolishes the granting of new coats of arms
It merges them with Scotland's Court of the Lord Lyon
It incorporates them as a royal corporation overseeing heraldry

evt-03-02-1484-college-of-arms.butterflyEffect: Richard III's charter incorporated the heralds as a permanent royal body with its own common seal, creating the College of Arms. Despite surviving fires, civil war, and centuries of change, it still grants coats of arms, traces pedigrees, and organizes state ceremonies today.

evt-03-02-1791-claude-chappe.scenario: You stand between two hilltop towers in France in 1791, watching Claude Chappe and his brothers test a new device of pivoting wooden arms meant to send messages across the countryside.
evt-03-02-1791-claude-chappe.prompt: What advantage does this semaphore system offer over existing methods of sending messages?

choices.text: It allows written letters to be carried faster by mounted couriers
It sends messages instantly using wireless radio waves
It transmits messages through underwater cables between coastal towns
Operators relay visual signals tower to tower for rapid long-distance messaging

evt-03-02-1791-claude-chappe.butterflyEffect: Chappe's semaphore was adopted by the French government and expanded into a nationwide network of relay towers, becoming the first practical telecommunications system of the industrial age. It remained in use for carrying official messages until electric telegraphs replaced it in the 1850s.

evt-03-02-1836-texas-revolution.scenario: It is March 2, 1836, in the crude hall at Washington-on-the-Brazos. You are one of fifty-nine delegates gathered while Santa Anna's army marches toward the Alamo, and the convention must decide Texas's fate before it is too late.
evt-03-02-1836-texas-revolution.prompt: What did the convention vote to do?

choices.text: Negotiate surrender terms with Santa Anna
Request immediate annexation by the United States
Declare independence from Mexico
Petition for greater autonomy within Mexico

evt-03-02-1836-texas-revolution.butterflyEffect: The delegates adopted the Texas Declaration of Independence, creating the Republic of Texas. Days later the Alamo fell, but Sam Houston's army crushed Santa Anna at San Jacinto that April, securing the republic's independence and setting up its annexation by the United States nine years later, a move that helped trigger the Mexican-American War.

evt-03-02-1859-great-slave-auction.scenario: You stand under a leaden sky at Ten Broeck Race Course near Savannah as auctioneers begin selling nearly 436 men, women, and children to settle Pierce Butler's gambling debts. Rain falls without pause through both days of the sale.
evt-03-02-1859-great-slave-auction.prompt: What name did witnesses and history give to these two days of sale?

choices.text: The Weeping Time
The Dark Days
The Broken Ground
The Long Sorrow

evt-03-02-1859-great-slave-auction.butterflyEffect: It became known as "The Weeping Time," for the unrelenting rain and the grief of families torn apart forever. Journalist Mortimer Thomson's eyewitness account of the sale was published widely and became a powerful piece of abolitionist testimony in the years before the Civil War.

evt-03-02-1865-new-zealand-wars.scenario: It is 2 March 1865 at Opotiki. You stand among Pai Marire (Hauhau) followers who have just brought ashore the missionary Carl Völkner, accused of passing intelligence to the colonial government.
evt-03-02-1865-new-zealand-wars.prompt: What do the Hauhau leaders decide to do with Völkner?

choices.text: Hold a tribal council and release him unharmed
Send him to Auckland to face a colonial trial
Hold him for ransom in exchange for imprisoned chiefs
Hang him from a tree near his own mission church

evt-03-02-1865-new-zealand-wars.butterflyEffect: Völkner was hanged from a willow tree near his own church. The killing shocked the colonial press and government, who used it to justify a military campaign into the Bay of Plenty and the large-scale confiscation of Māori land there, deepening the wars for years afterward.

evt-03-02-1877-electoral-commission-unit.scenario: You are a congressman in early 1877, weeks before inauguration day, watching the Electoral Commission award Rutherford B. Hayes twenty disputed electoral votes while Southern Democrats threaten to block the count entirely.
evt-03-02-1877-electoral-commission-unit.prompt: What backroom bargain accompanied the Commission's ruling to secure Hayes the presidency?

choices.text: A new nationwide presidential election
Withdrawal of federal troops from the South
Supreme Court annulment of the results
Tilden's appointment as Treasury Secretary

evt-03-02-1877-electoral-commission-unit.butterflyEffect: The Compromise of 1877 saw Democrats accept Hayes's victory in exchange for the withdrawal of federal troops from the last occupied Southern states. This effectively ended Reconstruction, allowing Redeemer governments to rise and paving the way for decades of Jim Crow segregation.

evt-03-02-1901-u-s-steel.scenario: You are J.P. Morgan in early 1901, weighing whether to bankroll a merger of Carnegie Steel, Federal Steel, and National Tube into one giant firm.
evt-03-02-1901-u-s-steel.prompt: What did Morgan's financing create, making it the world's first billion-dollar company?

choices.text: The Bethlehem Steel Trust
United States Steel Corporation
A government-run steel monopoly
The American Iron Combine
