evt-03-02-1901-u-s-steel.butterflyEffect: The merger formed United States Steel, controlling roughly two-thirds of American steel production overnight. Its sheer scale made it a flashpoint for the trust-busting politics of the Progressive Era, drawing antitrust suits and setting the template for modern corporate consolidation.

evt-03-02-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: You fly an Australian Beaufighter over the Bismarck Sea on 2-3 March 1943, tracking a Japanese convoy racing troops and supplies toward besieged Lae in New Guinea.
evt-03-02-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What tactic do Allied pilots use to devastate the convoy?

choices.text: High-altitude carpet bombing
Naval gunfire bombardment
Kamikaze-style ramming attacks
Low-level skip bombing

evt-03-02-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Allied airmen used low-level skip bombing, skimming bombs across the water into ship hulls, alongside torpedo and strafing runs. The convoy was annihilated, ending Japan's ability to reinforce New Guinea by large ship convoy and forcing a costly reliance on small barges for the rest of the campaign.

evt-03-02-1949-boeing-b-50-superfortress.scenario: You are the pilot of the B-50 Superfortress Lucky Lady II, six days into an attempt to circle the globe without ever touching down, relying on tanker aircraft to keep your engines fed as you close in on Fort Worth, Texas.
evt-03-02-1949-boeing-b-50-superfortress.prompt: What technique let this bomber fly around the world without landing?

choices.text: Flying at reduced speed to stretch a single fuel load
Oversized auxiliary fuel tanks bolted under the wings
Repeated in-flight refueling from tanker aircraft
A series of scheduled fuel drops by parachute

evt-03-02-1949-boeing-b-50-superfortress.butterflyEffect: Lucky Lady II completed the first nonstop round-the-world flight using aerial refueling from KB-29 tankers, covering roughly 23,000 miles in about 94 hours. The feat proved Strategic Air Command could strike any target on Earth without foreign bases, cementing in-flight refueling as a permanent pillar of US nuclear deterrence strategy.

evt-03-02-1962-ne-win.scenario: It is the early hours of 2 March 1962 in Rangoon. You are a government minister woken by the sound of army trucks surrounding the ministries and soldiers cutting the telephone lines across the capital.
evt-03-02-1962-ne-win.prompt: What does General Ne Win's Revolutionary Council do in the days that follow the coup?

choices.text: Dissolve parliament, suspend the constitution, and rule by Revolutionary Council decree
Call snap elections within the year to restore civilian rule
Hand administration of the country to the United Nations
Negotiate a power-sharing deal and return U Nu to office

evt-03-02-1962-ne-win.butterflyEffect: Ne Win abolished the 1947 constitution, arrested U Nu and other civilian leaders, and installed a one-party socialist military government. He would rule Burma for the next 26 years, driving the country into isolation and economic decline that culminated in the 1988 popular uprising.

evt-03-02-1965-vietnam-war.scenario: It is March 2, 1965. You are a U.S. Air Force pilot flying one of the first missions of a new sustained bombing campaign against North Vietnam.
evt-03-02-1965-vietnam-war.prompt: What is the stated goal of this bombing campaign as it begins?

choices.text: Invade and permanently occupy North Vietnamese territory
Support an immediate coup against Ho Chi Minh's government
Cut off Chinese supply lines into North Vietnam
Pressure North Vietnam into halting support for the insurgency and negotiate

evt-03-02-1965-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: Operation Rolling Thunder continued for three years, dropping vast tonnages of bombs on North Vietnam without breaking Hanoi's resolve or its support for the Viet Cong. Instead it escalated U.S. troop commitments in Vietnam and fueled growing antiwar protest at home.

evt-03-02-1965-the-sound-of-music-film.scenario: It is March 2, 1965, and you are among the first audiences watching The Sound of Music in an American theatre, following Julie Andrews as Maria von Trapp.
evt-03-02-1965-the-sound-of-music-film.prompt: What happens to this film in the years that follow its release?

choices.text: It performs poorly at the box office and fades from memory
It is quickly withdrawn and remade as a stage-only production
It is banned in several countries for its wartime content
It becomes the year's top-grossing film and wins the Best Picture Oscar

evt-03-02-1965-the-sound-of-music-film.butterflyEffect: The Sound of Music went on to win five Academy Awards, including Best Picture, and became the highest-grossing film of 1965. Its songs, from "My Favorite Things" to the title number, became enduring staples of musical theatre and family entertainment for generations.

evt-03-02-1969-concorde.scenario: You are test pilot André Turcat at Toulouse-Blagnac on 2 March 1969, about to lift the delta-winged Concorde 001 off the ground for the first time before a watching world press.
evt-03-02-1969-concorde.prompt: How did Turcat fly the aircraft during this cautious maiden flight?

choices.text: Subsonic only, with the landing gear left down
Supersonic for the full test flight
At full hypersonic test speed
Briefly supersonic over the Atlantic

evt-03-02-1969-concorde.butterflyEffect: Turcat kept the 27-minute flight entirely subsonic, gear down, to prove basic controllability before pushing the envelope. Concorde would not exceed the speed of sound until October that year, and though it entered service in 1976, high costs and the 2000 Air France crash led to its retirement in 2003.

evt-03-02-1970-queen-of-rhodesia.scenario: It is March 1970 in Salisbury. The Ian Smith government has just declared Rhodesia a republic, formally abolishing the fiction that Elizabeth II remains its head of state.
evt-03-02-1970-queen-of-rhodesia.prompt: What is the immediate international consequence of Rhodesia declaring itself a republic?

choices.text: Britain officially recognizes Rhodesian independence
The Commonwealth admits Rhodesia as a full member
The United Nations grants Rhodesia formal membership
Almost no country recognizes the new republic

evt-03-02-1970-queen-of-rhodesia.butterflyEffect: Almost no country recognized the new republic, and Rhodesia's isolation deepened alongside existing UN sanctions over its 1965 unilateral declaration of independence. This unrecognized status persisted until the 1979 Lancaster House Agreement finally produced internationally recognized independence as Zimbabwe in 1980.

evt-03-02-1978-astronaut.scenario: You are Czechoslovak air force pilot Vladimír Remek, strapped into Soyuz 28 on 2 March 1978 as part of the Soviet Intercosmos program, about to launch toward the Salyut 6 space station.
evt-03-02-1978-astronaut.prompt: What historic first did Remek's flight achieve?

choices.text: First person in space from a country other than the USSR or US
First person to complete a spacewalk
First woman to fly in space
First civilian ever launched into orbit

evt-03-02-1978-astronaut.butterflyEffect: Remek became the first person to reach space who was neither Soviet nor American, flying as an Intercosmos guest cosmonaut. His flight opened the door for cosmonauts from Poland, East Germany, and beyond, turning spaceflight into a tool of Cold War diplomacy for the Eastern Bloc.

evt-03-02-1995-fermi-national-accelerato.scenario: It's early 1995 at Fermilab outside Chicago. You're part of the CDF and D0 teams sifting through years of Tevatron collision data, chasing the one quark the Standard Model predicts but no one has yet caught.
evt-03-02-1995-fermi-national-accelerato.prompt: What particle did the Fermilab teams announce discovering?

choices.text: The top quark
The bottom quark
The tau neutrino
The Higgs boson

evt-03-02-1995-fermi-national-accelerato.butterflyEffect: The teams confirmed the top quark, the heaviest known elementary particle and the last of the six quarks predicted by the Standard Model. Its surprisingly large mass later fed into theoretical calculations that helped point physicists toward the Higgs boson, finally discovered at CERN in 2012.

evt-03-02-2012-tornado-outbreak-of-march.scenario: It is the morning of March 2, 2012. Forecasters have just upgraded the risk to "high" across Middle Tennessee and central Kentucky, and a Particularly Dangerous Situation tornado watch has been issued for your area.
evt-03-02-2012-tornado-outbreak-of-march.prompt: Given this warning, what should residents in the watch area do right away?

choices.text: Drive out of the area to get ahead of the storm system
Move immediately to a sturdy, low-lying shelter and stay alert for warnings
Ignore the watch since most such alerts don't produce tornadoes
Wait until sirens actually sound before taking any action

evt-03-02-2012-tornado-outbreak-of-march.butterflyEffect: The outbreak went on to produce dozens of tornadoes, including long-track violent tornadoes across Kentucky, Indiana, and Ohio. The advance high-risk forecast gave residents crucial lead time, and the event became a widely studied case in improving warning communication for fast-moving, high-shear tornado outbreaks.

evt-03-02-2022-battle-of-kherson.scenario: It's March 1, 2022, and you're a territorial defense volunteer in Kherson as Russian armored columns push into the city, meeting only scattered resistance from lightly armed locals.
evt-03-02-2022-battle-of-kherson.prompt: What became of Kherson after Russian forces overran the city?

choices.text: Local defenders forced a Russian retreat by nightfall
It was formally annexed into Russia within days
Ukrainian forces repelled the assault within hours
It became the first Ukrainian regional capital captured and occupied

evt-03-02-2022-battle-of-kherson.butterflyEffect: Kherson fell that day, becoming the first Ukrainian regional capital seized in the invasion and placed under Russian occupation, giving Moscow a foothold on the Dnipro's west bank. Ukraine's autumn 2022 counteroffensive recaptured the city that November, forcing a Russian withdrawal across the river in one of the war's most significant reversals.

evt-03-03-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: You serve under Captain Samuel Nicholas as his newly formed Continental Marines land on New Providence Island in the Bahamas on March 3, 1776, sent to strike at British military stores far from the mainland fighting.
evt-03-03-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What was the outcome of this Marine landing against the British forts?

choices.text: They destroyed the British fleet anchored in Nassau harbor
They captured the British governor and held him for ransom
They captured the forts and seized badly needed gunpowder and cannon
They failed to take the forts and withdrew empty-handed

evt-03-03-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: The Marines captured Forts Montagu and Nassau, seizing cannon and gunpowder that were shipped back to reinforce the Continental Army, though much powder had already been removed before their arrival. This first amphibious raid by U.S. Marines became a founding legend of the Marine Corps.

evt-03-03-1820-united-states-congress.scenario: You are a member of Congress in early 1820, watching the House and Senate wrestle with Missouri's request for statehood, a decision that threatens to upend the fragile balance between free and slave states in the Union.
evt-03-03-1820-united-states-congress.prompt: What compromise did Congress pass to resolve the Missouri statehood crisis?

choices.text: Split Missouri into two separate states, one free and one slave
Delay Missouri's statehood indefinitely until slavery was resolved nationally
Admit Missouri as a slave state and Maine as a free state, banning slavery north of 36°30′
Admit Missouri as a free state and abolish slavery in all territories immediately

evt-03-03-1820-united-states-congress.butterflyEffect: The Missouri Compromise admitted Missouri as a slave state and Maine as a free state while banning slavery north of the 36°30′ line in the remaining Louisiana Purchase territory. It held sectional tensions in check for over thirty years until the Kansas-Nebraska Act of 1854 effectively repealed it, reigniting the slavery debate and pushing the nation toward civil war.

evt-03-03-1875-first-indoor-ice-hockey-g.scenario: You are watching from the stands of Montreal's Victoria Skating Rink on March 3, 1875, as two teams of nine players skate out onto an artificial indoor rink carrying sticks and a flat rubber disc instead of the ball you're used to seeing outdoors.
evt-03-03-1875-first-indoor-ice-hockey-g.prompt: What made this match different from the outdoor shinny games players had grown up with?

choices.text: It was played indoors with a rubber puck under organized rules
It introduced the forward pass to the sport
It used a wooden puck for the first time
It was the first game played with ten players per side

evt-03-03-1875-first-indoor-ice-hockey-g.butterflyEffect: James Creighton's match introduced a rubber puck in place of a ball, partly to protect spectators from wild shots, along with early organized rules for indoor play. This codified version spread to universities and clubs across Canada, eventually evolving into the modern sport and the NHL.

evt-03-03-1878-treaty-of-san-stefano.scenario: It is 3 March 1878 near Constantinople. As a Russian diplomat, you have just signed a treaty ending the war with the Ottomans and carving out a large autonomous Bulgaria stretching to the Aegean.
evt-03-03-1878-treaty-of-san-stefano.prompt: What happens to this Russian-drawn settlement in the months that follow?

choices.text: The Ottoman Empire regains all the ceded territory outright
It stands unchanged and Bulgaria keeps its full borders
France annexes Bulgaria as a protectorate
Britain and Austria-Hungary force a renegotiation that shrinks Bulgaria

evt-03-03-1878-treaty-of-san-stefano.butterflyEffect: Alarmed by the size of the new Bulgaria, Britain and Austria-Hungary forced a renegotiation at the Congress of Berlin three months later, which shrank Bulgaria drastically and split off Eastern Rumelia. The perceived injustice fed Bulgarian nationalism for decades and helped set the stage for later Balkan conflicts.

evt-03-03-1891-shoshone-national-forest.scenario: It is 3 March 1891 in Washington, and you watch President Benjamin Harrison sign a bill setting aside forested land in Wyoming as the Yellowstone Timberland Reserve.
evt-03-03-1891-shoshone-national-forest.prompt: What precedent does this reservation set for American land policy?

choices.text: It transfers the land permanently to the state of Wyoming
It establishes the first federally protected national forest
It creates the first national park in the United States
It opens the land immediately for homesteading

evt-03-03-1891-shoshone-national-forest.butterflyEffect: The reservation became Shoshone National Forest, the first federally protected national forest in the country. The model of setting aside forestland by presidential and congressional action spread rapidly, eventually leading to the creation of the U.S. Forest Service in 1905 under Gifford Pinchot.

evt-03-03-1913-woman-suffrage-procession.scenario: You are one of thousands of suffragists marching down Pennsylvania Avenue on March 3, 1913, the day before Wilson's inauguration. Hostile crowds press in against the ropes as Alice Paul's parade advances toward the Capitol.
evt-03-03-1913-woman-suffrage-procession.prompt: What happened to the marchers as they proceeded along the parade route?

choices.text: Police escorted them smoothly and the parade concluded without incident
The parade was cancelled before it began due to snowfall
President-elect Wilson joined the marchers in solidarity
Hostile male spectators attacked and harassed the marchers, forcing troops to restore order

evt-03-03-1913-woman-suffrage-procession.butterflyEffect: Mobs of men jeered, shoved, and assaulted marchers while police largely failed to intervene, until cavalry from Fort Myer was called in to restore order. The near-riot generated national outrage and congressional hearings, giving fresh momentum to the suffrage movement that culminated in the 19th Amendment in 1920.

evt-03-03-1933-nohra-concentration-camp.scenario: It is 3 March 1933 near Weimar. As a Thuringian official, you are ordered to open a makeshift camp in a schoolhouse at the Nohra airfield to hold communist politicians arrested after the Reichstag Fire Decree.
evt-03-03-1933-nohra-concentration-camp.prompt: What is the immediate purpose of this new camp at Nohra?

choices.text: To train new SS camp guards
To hold communist prisoners amid mass arrests after the Reichstag Fire Decree
To intern Jewish business owners from Weimar
To detain foreign nationals awaiting deportation

evt-03-03-1933-nohra-concentration-camp.butterflyEffect: Nohra held arrested communists, including half the Communist party's delegation in the Thuringian parliament, without formal charge. Opened within days of the Reichstag Fire Decree, it was among the first of many improvised local camps that year, a pattern that expanded rapidly into the much larger and more brutal Nazi concentration camp system.

evt-03-03-1972-jethro-tull-band.scenario: You drop the needle on Jethro Tull's new record on March 3, 1972, expecting a set of separate songs, but instead find one continuous piece of music running across both sides of the LP, packaged with a mock newspaper.
evt-03-03-1972-jethro-tull-band.prompt: What was the satirical conceit behind the album's lyrics?

choices.text: The lyrics were credited to a fictional schoolboy poet, satirizing concept albums
The album was presented as a soundtrack to a nonexistent film
The lyrics were credited to a Victorian poet found in an attic
The band claimed the album was recorded live at Stonehenge

evt-03-03-1972-jethro-tull-band.butterflyEffect: Ian Anderson credited the sprawling lyrics to a fictional precocious schoolboy, Gerald Bostock, mocking critics who had called the band's previous record a pretentious 'concept album.' Despite the joke, the album's ambition helped define progressive rock and became Jethro Tull's only album to reach number one on the US Billboard chart.

evt-03-03-1974-turkish-airlines-flight-9.scenario: It's 1972, and you're an aircraft engineer who has just seen test data proving the DC-10's rear cargo door latch can fail under pressure, much as it nearly did on an American Airlines flight over Windsor, Ontario. You draft a memo urging McDonnell Douglas management to act before more planes fly with the flaw.
evt-03-03-1974-turkish-airlines-flight-9.prompt: What does your memo recommend the manufacturer do?

choices.text: A complete redesign of the cargo door's latching system
No action, since the earlier incident had already been resolved
A warning placard instructing baggage handlers to double-check the door
Grounding the entire DC-10 fleet for one week only

evt-03-03-1974-turkish-airlines-flight-9.butterflyEffect: Management rejected the costly redesign and instead added a warning placard and a minor adjustment. Two years later, on 3 March 1974, the same door failure caused Flight 981 to break apart over Ermenonville, France, killing everyone aboard, and the disaster became a case study that pushed the FAA toward mandatory rather than voluntary safety fixes.

evt-03-03-1985-1985-algarrobo-earthquake.scenario: It is the evening of 3 March 1985 in central Chile. After ten days of small foreshocks, the ground beneath Valparaíso and Santiago begins to shake violently as an 8.0 magnitude earthquake strikes.
evt-03-03-1985-1985-algarrobo-earthquake.prompt: What does the widespread damage prompt Chilean authorities to address afterward?

choices.text: Relocate the national capital away from the coast
Ban further scientific study of the region's earthquakes
Ignore building standards since most damage was considered minor
Review and tighten enforcement of seismic-resistant building codes

evt-03-03-1985-1985-algarrobo-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The earthquake exposed weaknesses in older construction across the Valparaíso and Santiago region, prompting a review and stricter enforcement of Chile's seismic building codes. Chile's continued attention to earthquake-resistant construction is often cited when comparing its performance in later major quakes.

evt-03-03-1986-metallica.scenario: It's early 1986 in San Francisco, and Metallica has just released a new album to blistering reviews. You're the band, booking a long tour across Europe and the US to capitalize on the momentum.
evt-03-03-1986-metallica.prompt: What tragedy struck the band later that year on this album's tour?

choices.text: James Hetfield broke his arm in a skateboarding accident
The band canceled the European leg due to visa issues
Cliff Burton died when the tour bus overturned in Sweden
Dave Mustaine rejoined the band as a second guitarist

evt-03-03-1986-metallica.butterflyEffect: On 27 September 1986, the band's tour bus overturned near Ljungby, Sweden, killing bassist Cliff Burton. Jason Newsted joined within weeks, and the album went on to be regarded as a landmark of thrash metal despite the shadow cast over its tour.

evt-03-03-1986-australia-act-1986.scenario: It's 3 March 1986, and you sit in the Australian Parliament as the Australia Act formally commences, severing the last legal threads tying Australian law to Westminster and the Privy Council.
evt-03-03-1986-australia-act-1986.prompt: What immediate legal change follows from the Act's commencement?

choices.text: Australia adopts a new written constitution
The Australian monarchy is immediately abolished
State governments lose power to legislate independently of the Commonwealth
Australian courts can no longer be overruled by British courts

evt-03-03-1986-australia-act-1986.butterflyEffect: The Act ended appeals to the Privy Council and any British power to legislate for Australia, completing the country's legal independence from the United Kingdom. It sharpened later debates over the monarchy's role, feeding directly into the 1999 Australian republic referendum.

evt-03-03-1991-united-airlines-flight-58.scenario: You're an NTSB investigator in the days after 3 March 1991, examining wreckage of a United 737 that rolled over and dove into the ground on approach to Colorado Springs. Witnesses describe a sudden gust just before impact, but the flight recorders offer few clues.
evt-03-03-1991-united-airlines-flight-58.prompt: What ultimately explains the crash, confirmed only after two more 737s went down the same way?

choices.text: A jammed rudder power control unit forced the rudder to reverse
A rotor gust from mountain wave turbulence overwhelmed the aircraft
The captain suffered a sudden medical incapacitation
A bird strike disabled both engines simultaneously

evt-03-03-1991-united-airlines-flight-58.butterflyEffect: Investigators couldn't pin down a cause at the time, but after Eastwind Flight 517 and USAir Flight 427 suffered eerily similar upsets, the NTSB traced all three to a flaw in the Boeing 737's rudder power control unit that could jam and reverse. The finding forced a fleet-wide retrofit and changed how regulators treat recurring failures without a definitive black box answer.

evt-03-03-2012-szczekociny-rail-crash.scenario: It's the evening of 3 March 2012, and you're a dispatcher on the Polish rail line near Szczekociny. Signals show two passenger trains converging onto the same stretch of track, and the window to stop them is closing fast.
evt-03-03-2012-szczekociny-rail-crash.prompt: What should happen to prevent the collision?

choices.text: Immediately halt both trains before they enter the shared track section
Reroute one train onto a freight-only siding without notifying the driver
Let both continue, since the schedule allows a safe passing point
Increase both trains' speed to clear the junction faster

evt-03-03-2012-szczekociny-rail-crash.butterflyEffect: The warning was not acted on in time, and the two trains collided head-on, killing sixteen people and injuring dozens more. The disaster exposed gaps in Poland's signalling and dispatcher training, accelerating the national rollout of automatic train protection systems on regional lines.

evt-03-04-1461-wars-of-the-roses.scenario: It is 4 March 1461 in London. Henry VI has fled north after the Yorkist victory at Mortimer's Cross, and crowds gather as Yorkist lords decide how to fill the vacant throne.
evt-03-04-1461-wars-of-the-roses.prompt: What did the Yorkist leadership do in London that day?

choices.text: Opened peace talks to restore Henry VI
Proclaimed Edward, Earl of March, as King Edward IV
Crowned Henry VI's young son as king instead
Established a regency council under Warwick

evt-03-04-1461-wars-of-the-roses.butterflyEffect: They proclaimed Edward, Earl of March, as King Edward IV. His claim was made good weeks later at the bloody Battle of Towton, securing the throne for the House of York until Lancastrian forces briefly restored Henry VI in 1470.

evt-03-04-1675-john-flamsteed.scenario: You are John Flamsteed in 1675, freshly named England's first Astronomer Royal by Charles II, given rooms at the new observatory rising at Greenwich and told the Crown expects practical results, not just stargazing for its own sake.
evt-03-04-1675-john-flamsteed.prompt: What is the primary task the King has set for you as Astronomer Royal?

choices.text: Search for new planets beyond Saturn
Predict the return dates of comets for the Royal Society
Reform the English calendar to match the continent
Compile precise star positions to help sailors navigate by longitude

evt-03-04-1675-john-flamsteed.butterflyEffect: Flamsteed spent decades compiling the star catalogue Catalogus Britannicus, precise enough to help sailors calculate longitude by the stars. His work at Greenwich helped make the observatory the reference point that later became the Prime Meridian.

evt-03-04-1681-charles-ii-of-england.scenario: It is 4 March 1681. You are King Charles II, and you owe a substantial debt to the late Admiral Sir William Penn. His Quaker son, persecuted for his faith in England, now asks you to settle that debt with land in America instead of coin.
evt-03-04-1681-charles-ii-of-england.prompt: How does Charles II settle the Penn family debt?

choices.text: He pays Penn the full debt in gold from the treasury
He grants Penn a proprietary charter to a large American colony
He imprisons Penn for his Quaker beliefs instead
He exiles the Penn family to the Caribbean colonies

evt-03-04-1681-charles-ii-of-england.butterflyEffect: Charles II granted William Penn a vast royal charter, making him proprietor of what became Pennsylvania. Penn founded it as a haven of religious tolerance, and Philadelphia's design and Quaker principles later influenced American ideas about liberty and government.

evt-03-04-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is the night of March 4, 1776, and you are a Continental soldier hauling cannon that Henry Knox dragged from Fort Ticonderoga up the slopes of Dorchester Heights overlooking British-held Boston.
evt-03-04-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What does the Continental Army do with these guns once they reach the heights?

choices.text: Bury them as a decoy to mislead British scouts
Fortify the heights to threaten the British fleet and garrison
Ship them south to reinforce New York immediately
Haul them into Boston for a direct assault

evt-03-04-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Washington's men fortified Dorchester Heights overnight, placing the cannon within range of the British fleet and army in Boston. Facing an untenable position, General Howe evacuated the city on March 17, 1776, handing the Continental Army its first major strategic victory of the war.

evt-03-04-1804-convicts-in-australia.scenario: It is 4 March 1804 at Castle Hill, New South Wales. You are among the Irish convicts who have risen up under Philip Cunningham, planning to seize arms and march toward Parramatta before Major George Johnston's troops can catch you.
evt-03-04-1804-convicts-in-australia.prompt: What happens when Johnston's forces intercept the rebels at Rouse Hill?

choices.text: Both sides negotiate a peaceful pardon on the spot
The rebels overwhelm the troops and seize the colony's armory
The rebels are decisively defeated and their leaders captured
The rebels escape by ship before troops arrive

evt-03-04-1804-convicts-in-australia.butterflyEffect: The convicts were routed at what became known as the Australian Battle of Vinegar Hill, with several killed and ringleaders later hanged or flogged. The colony's authorities responded with martial law and tighter surveillance of Irish convicts, shaping decades of harsher penal policy in New South Wales.

evt-03-04-1837-chicago.scenario: It is early March 1837, and you are a shopkeeper in the muddy lakeside town of Chicago, population barely 4,000. The Illinois legislature has just granted a city charter, and townsfolk are deciding whether to accept it.
evt-03-04-1837-chicago.prompt: What did Chicago's residents do with the new state charter?

choices.text: Rejected it and remained an unincorporated town
Asked to be annexed by the state of Wisconsin
Accepted it and incorporated as a city
Petitioned to merge with a neighboring settlement instead

evt-03-04-1837-chicago.butterflyEffect: Chicago accepted the charter and incorporated as a city on March 4, 1837, electing William B. Ogden as its first mayor. The move gave the town a formal government just as canal and rail investment poured in, launching its explosive growth into the Midwest's dominant metropolis.

evt-03-04-1848-charles-albert-of-sardini.scenario: It is 4 March 1848 in Turin. Revolutions are erupting across Europe, and crowds outside your palace demand you follow France's example. As King of Sardinia, you must decide how to answer the unrest.
evt-03-04-1848-charles-albert-of-sardini.prompt: What does Charles Albert do to answer the pressure for reform?

choices.text: He dissolves the government and rules by decree
He abdicates immediately in favor of his son
He grants a constitution, the Statuto Albertino, establishing a limited parliament
He declares war on Austria before any reform

evt-03-04-1848-charles-albert-of-sardini.butterflyEffect: He granted the Statuto Albertino, creating an elected chamber alongside royal power while the king retained control of the executive and army. The document outlasted his 1849 abdication and became the constitutional backbone of the future unified Kingdom of Italy until 1948.

evt-03-04-1890-forth-bridge.scenario: You are an engineer standing on the newly completed Forth Bridge on 4 March 1890, waiting for the Prince of Wales to perform the ceremony that will formally open Fowler and Baker's giant cantilever span to rail traffic.
evt-03-04-1890-forth-bridge.prompt: What did the Prince of Wales do to mark the bridge's opening?

choices.text: Cut a ribbon stretched across the tracks
Fired a signal cannon from the middle span
Unveiled a bronze plaque at the north tower
Drove home a ceremonial golden rivet

evt-03-04-1890-forth-bridge.butterflyEffect: He drove home a specially prepared golden rivet, formally completing the structure. The bridge's success helped restore public confidence in large-scale railway engineering after the Tay Bridge disaster a decade earlier, and it remains a working rail link and UNESCO World Heritage Site.

evt-03-04-1899-cyclone-mahina.scenario: It is 4 March 1899. You captain a pearling lugger anchored with dozens of others in the sheltered waters of Bathurst Bay, Cape York, as the barometer plunges and the sky turns strange ahead of an approaching cyclone.
evt-03-04-1899-cyclone-mahina.prompt: Given what unfolds, what is the wiser course as the storm bears down?

choices.text: Shelter deep in the bay as most of the fleet does
Anchor tight against the nearest coral reef
Push out to open sea, away from the enclosed bay
Beach the lugger on the nearest shoreline

evt-03-04-1899-cyclone-mahina.butterflyEffect: Most of the fleet stayed anchored in the bay believing it offered safety, but an extraordinary storm surge, among the highest ever recorded, drove boats onto land and reef, killing over 300 people, mostly pearl divers. The disaster remains Australia's deadliest cyclone and reshaped understanding of storm surge danger in enclosed bays.

evt-03-04-1918-united-states-navy.scenario: It is early March 1918. You are a stoker aboard the USS Cyclops, a Navy collier loaded with a cargo of manganese ore, steaming from Barbados toward Baltimore through waters where German U-boats are rumored to prowl.
evt-03-04-1918-united-states-navy.prompt: What ultimately happens to the Cyclops and her 300-plus crew after this voyage?

choices.text: She is torpedoed by a U-boat within sight of other vessels
She vanishes without a trace, never found again
She is found drifting and abandoned off the Carolinas
She limps into Baltimore badly damaged but afloat

evt-03-04-1918-united-states-navy.butterflyEffect: The Cyclops vanished completely — no wreckage, debris, or distress call was ever found. It remains the U.S. Navy's largest single loss of life not directly caused by combat, and the unsolved disappearance later fed Bermuda Triangle legend.

evt-03-04-1918-camp-funston.scenario: It's 4 March 1918, and you're the camp doctor at Camp Funston, Fort Riley, when a soldier reports to sick call with fever, headache, and sore throat — one of the first documented cases of what will become a devastating pandemic.
evt-03-04-1918-camp-funston.prompt: What happens in the weeks that follow, as thousands of recruits pass through the crowded camp?

choices.text: The case is fully isolated and no further spread occurs
The army shuts the camp down permanently
The illness spreads rapidly, sickening hundreds within weeks
Only civilian visitors to the camp are affected

evt-03-04-1918-camp-funston.butterflyEffect: Within weeks over a thousand soldiers at Camp Funston had fallen ill, and wartime troop movements carried the virus to other camps and onward to Europe. This early outbreak is considered one of the possible starting points of the 1918 influenza pandemic, which went on to kill tens of millions worldwide.

evt-03-04-1933-frances-perkins.scenario: It's Inauguration Day, 4 March 1933, and you're among President Franklin D. Roosevelt's advisers as the Depression deepens. Roosevelt is filling out his cabinet and weighs who should run the Department of Labor.
evt-03-04-1933-frances-perkins.prompt: Whom does Roosevelt choose to lead Labor, breaking a historic barrier?

choices.text: Mary McLeod Bethune
Frances Perkins
Frances Willard
Eleanor Roosevelt

evt-03-04-1933-frances-perkins.butterflyEffect: Frances Perkins became the first woman to serve in a U.S. presidential cabinet, holding the post for Roosevelt's entire presidency. She helped draft the Social Security Act and the Fair Labor Standards Act, embedding labor protections at the heart of the New Deal.

evt-03-04-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It's dawn on 4 March 1941, and you're a Commando landing at Stamsund in Norway's Lofoten Islands during Operation Claymore, tasked with torching German-run fish-oil factories. A boarding party has just climbed aboard the armed German trawler Krebs.
evt-03-04-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: What should the boarding party grab before the ship goes down?

choices.text: Barrels of fuel stored below deck
The ship's fishing nets and gear
Crates of small arms in the hold
Any documents and cipher equipment on board

evt-03-04-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The men recovered a naval Enigma machine and its rotor settings from the Krebs. This intelligence windfall gave Bletchley Park's codebreakers a crucial boost in cracking German naval ciphers, aiding the Allied fight against U-boats in the Battle of the Atlantic.

evt-03-04-1943-the-holocaust.scenario: It is March 1943 in Bulgarian-occupied Western Thrace, and Jewish families are being ordered from their homes and marched toward assembly points under Bulgarian guard, told only that they are being relocated.
evt-03-04-1943-the-holocaust.prompt: What ultimately became of nearly all the Jews rounded up in Western Thrace that month?

choices.text: Conscripted into Bulgarian forced-labor battalions
Permitted to emigrate to neutral Turkey
Deported and murdered at the Treblinka extermination camp
Interned in local labor camps for the war's duration

evt-03-04-1943-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: They were handed to German authorities and deported to the Treblinka extermination camp, where almost all were murdered. This starkly contrasted with Bulgaria's own pre-war Jewish citizens, most of whom survived after public and church pressure halted their planned deportation, revealing how occupied territories bore the harshest brunt of collaboration.

evt-03-04-1966-john-lennon.scenario: You are a London journalist sitting with John Lennon in his Weybridge home in early March 1966, notebook open, as he muses aloud about religion's fading grip on modern Britain compared to the Beatles' own fame.
evt-03-04-1966-john-lennon.prompt: What is the line Lennon actually says that will later ignite controversy in America?

choices.text: "We're bigger than Elvis ever was"
"Rock and roll will outlast the Church"
"God is dead, and we proved it"
"Christianity will go... we're more popular than Jesus now"

evt-03-04-1966-john-lennon.butterflyEffect: The remark drew little notice in Britain, but when reprinted in a US teen magazine that July, it triggered record burnings, radio boycotts, and death threats across the American South. The furor was one factor pushing the Beatles to abandon touring after that year.

evt-03-04-1979-voyager-1.scenario: It is March 1979, and you're a JPL imaging scientist scanning fresh photographs beamed back from Voyager 1's flyby of Jupiter. A faint, unexpected band of light shows up where the team expected empty space.
evt-03-04-1979-voyager-1.prompt: What does this newly spotted feature around Jupiter turn out to be?

choices.text: A shadow cast by one of Jupiter's known moons
A previously unknown large moon
A faint ring system encircling the planet
An asteroid belt trapped in Jupiter's orbit

evt-03-04-1979-voyager-1.butterflyEffect: Voyager 1's images confirmed Jupiter has its own faint ring system, making it the second planet known to have one after Saturn. The find reshaped models of gas-giant formation and helped justify later dedicated study by the Galileo orbiter in the 1990s.

evt-03-04-1987-ronald-reagan.scenario: It is 4 March 1987. You are drafting talking points for President Reagan's first televised address since the Tower Commission's report on secret arms sales to Iran and funds diverted to Contra rebels.
evt-03-04-1987-ronald-reagan.prompt: What stance does Reagan take toward the American public in this address?

choices.text: He denies any wrongdoing occurred in his administration
He blames the entire affair publicly on Congress
He accepts responsibility for the policy while denying knowledge of the diversion
He announces his resignation effective immediately

evt-03-04-1987-ronald-reagan.butterflyEffect: Reagan admitted the policy had become a mistake while insisting he had not known funds were diverted to the Contras. The partial admission calmed the immediate crisis but Iran-Contra continued to shadow his final two years, feeding congressional hearings and prosecutions of aides.

evt-03-04-1990-college-basketball.scenario: It is March 4, 1990, and you are courtside as Loyola Marymount's Hank Gathers slams down a dunk in the West Coast Conference tournament, then suddenly collapses near midcourt. He had been diagnosed months earlier with a heart arrhythmia.
evt-03-04-1990-college-basketball.prompt: What had Gathers done about his heart medication before this game?

choices.text: Stopped playing basketball entirely for the season
Had recently undergone corrective heart surgery
Switched to an experimental unapproved drug
Reduced his dosage because of side effects on his play

evt-03-04-1990-college-basketball.butterflyEffect: Gathers had reduced his prescribed beta-blocker dosage because it made him feel sluggish on the court; he collapsed and died shortly after from cardiac arrest. His death prompted closer scrutiny of cardiac screening and medical clearance for college athletes with heart conditions.

evt-03-04-2000-playstation-2.scenario: It's 4 March 2000, and you're a gamer lined up outside a Tokyo electronics store as Sony's new console finally goes on sale, weighing it against Sega's Dreamcast already on shelves.
evt-03-04-2000-playstation-2.prompt: What feature tips your decision toward the PlayStation 2?

choices.text: A lower launch price than rival consoles
An exclusive built-in online multiplayer service
Superior graphics with no other advantages
Its built-in DVD playback and backward compatibility

evt-03-04-2000-playstation-2.butterflyEffect: The PS2's built-in DVD playback and backward compatibility with original PlayStation games made it an easy household upgrade, not just a game machine. It went on to sell over 155 million units, becoming the best-selling console in history and cementing Sony's dominance through the 2000s.

evt-03-04-2009-omar-al-bashir.scenario: It is 4 March 2009. The International Criminal Court has just issued an arrest warrant against you, the sitting President of Sudan, for war crimes and crimes against humanity linked to the conflict in Darfur. You must decide how your government responds.
evt-03-04-2009-omar-al-bashir.prompt: How does Bashir's government react to the ICC warrant?

choices.text: Sudan requests immediate UN peacekeepers to detain him
Bashir voluntarily surrenders himself to The Hague
Sudan's military arrests Bashir to comply with the warrant
Sudan expels foreign aid agencies and refuses to recognize the ICC's authority

evt-03-04-2009-omar-al-bashir.butterflyEffect: Sudan rejected the court's jurisdiction and expelled numerous foreign aid organizations working in Darfur in retaliation. Bashir remained in power for another decade, traveling to allied states that declined to arrest him, exposing the ICC's dependence on state cooperation to enforce its rulings.

evt-03-05-1279-livonian-order.scenario: It is 5 March 1279. You ride with the Livonian Order's heavy cavalry as Grand Duke Traidenis of Lithuania springs a devastating ambush near Aizkraukle, encircling the Order's advancing knights.
evt-03-05-1279-livonian-order.prompt: What happens to the Order's Master, Ernst von Rassburg, in the fighting?

choices.text: He surrenders the nearest fortress to spare his remaining men
He escapes and organizes an immediate counterattack
He is killed in the battle along with 71 of his knights
He is captured and later ransomed back to the Order

evt-03-05-1279-livonian-order.butterflyEffect: Rassburg was killed alongside 71 of his knights, crippling the Order's fighting strength for years. The disaster emboldened Lithuanian and Semigallian resistance and delayed German conquest of Semigallia by decades.

evt-03-05-1770-boston-massacre.scenario: It is March 1770 in Boston, and you are the young lawyer John Adams. British soldiers who fired into a crowd on King Street now need a defense counsel, but no one in town wants to touch the case.
evt-03-05-1770-boston-massacre.prompt: Does Adams take on the defense of the soldiers accused in the King Street shooting?

choices.text: He flees Boston rather than get involved
He takes the case, insisting the soldiers deserve a fair trial
He refuses, fearing damage to his reputation
He takes the case but sabotages the defense to please the crowd

evt-03-05-1770-boston-massacre.butterflyEffect: Adams accepted the case, arguing that even unpopular defendants deserved a fair trial. Six soldiers were acquitted and two convicted only of manslaughter, while Patriot propaganda like Paul Revere's engraving still used the killings to inflame anger that helped push the colonies toward revolution.

evt-03-05-1811-peninsular-war.scenario: It is 5 March 1811 near Cádiz. You command the Anglo-Spanish column marching to relieve the besieged city, but French troops under Marshal Victor have seized the high ground of the Barrosa ridge behind you.
evt-03-05-1811-peninsular-war.prompt: With the enemy suddenly astride your line of march, what do you order?

choices.text: Turn back and attack the French on the ridge before they can consolidate
Retreat to the coast and re-embark the troops
Continue the march to Cádiz and ignore the threat to the rear
Send envoys to negotiate a truce with Marshal Victor

evt-03-05-1811-peninsular-war.butterflyEffect: General Thomas Graham turned his outnumbered force about and stormed the ridge, routing Victor's divisions and capturing a French Imperial Eagle — the first taken in the Peninsular War. The tactical victory boosted Allied morale, though Spanish reluctance to follow up meant the siege of Cádiz dragged on for another two years.

evt-03-05-1824-first-anglo-burmese-war.scenario: It is early 1824, and you advise the British East India Company as Burmese forces under General Maha Bandula push into Assam and Cachar, territories bordering British India. Diplomatic protests have achieved nothing.
evt-03-05-1824-first-anglo-burmese-war.prompt: What does the Company decide to do in response to Burmese expansion toward its Indian frontier?

choices.text: Refer the dispute to arbitration by the Qing court
Withdraw all British garrisons from the disputed border regions
Offer Burma a formal alliance against Siam
Declare war on the Konbaung dynasty of Burma

evt-03-05-1824-first-anglo-burmese-war.butterflyEffect: The Company declared war, opening the costly First Anglo-Burmese War. Despite heavy losses to disease, Britain won decisively, forcing Burma to cede Assam, Arakan and Tenasserim and pay a huge indemnity — the first step toward Britain's eventual full annexation of Burma later in the century.

evt-03-05-1825-roberto-cofresi.scenario: You are a young Puerto Rican sailor in the early 1820s. Years at sea have taught you the region's coasts and hidden coves, but your wages remain meager and the island's economy is in turmoil under Spanish rule.
evt-03-05-1825-roberto-cofresi.prompt: What path does Cofresí choose to escape a life of poverty at sea?

choices.text: Petition for a commission in the Spanish royal navy
Abandon the sailor's life and turn to piracy
Sign on as a merchant ship captain trading with the United States
Retire to his family's estate and live off its remaining wealth

evt-03-05-1825-roberto-cofresi.butterflyEffect: Cofresí abandoned honest seafaring to become a pirate, raiding merchant shipping across the Caribbean for years. Spanish and American forces finally cornered him near Isla de Mona; he was captured and executed by firing squad on 29 March 1825, an event still remembered as marking the end of the Caribbean's age of piracy.

evt-03-05-1960-alberto-korda.scenario: It is 5 March 1960 in Havana, and you are photographer Alberto Korda covering a funeral rally for victims of the La Coubre explosion. For one instant, Che Guevara steps to the edge of the platform, his face turned toward the crowd, before he vanishes back among the dignitaries.
evt-03-05-1960-alberto-korda.prompt: What do you do to capture the moment?

choices.text: Instantly raise your camera and shoot before he turns away
Wait for the speeches to end and ask him to pose
Focus on Fidel Castro, the day's main speaker, instead
Set up a formal studio portrait for later that week

evt-03-05-1960-alberto-korda.butterflyEffect: Korda fired off two frames in seconds; the paper he worked for never even ran the shot. Years later it was cropped and printed as "Guerrillero Heroico," becoming one of the most reproduced photographs in history, adorning protest banners, T-shirts, and album covers worldwide.

evt-03-05-1978-landsat-3.scenario: It is March 1978 at Vandenberg Air Force Base, and you are part of the NASA team preparing Landsat 3 for launch, tasked with defining the satellite's core mission before it leaves the ground.
evt-03-05-1978-landsat-3.prompt: What is Landsat 3 designed primarily to do once in orbit?

choices.text: Provide a continuous global archive of Earth imagery for resource and ecological monitoring
Test experimental rocket propulsion for future missions
Track Soviet military installations for intelligence purposes
Relay communications for deep-space probes

evt-03-05-1978-landsat-3.butterflyEffect: Landsat 3 built a global archive of Earth imagery, far outlasting its one-year design life by operating until 1983. Thirty-one countries drew on its data for resource surveys and ecological monitoring, proving the lasting value of continuous satellite observation for nations without space programs of their own.

evt-03-05-1979-venera-11.scenario: It is 5 March 1979. Instruments aboard the Soviet Venera 11 and Venera 12 probes and the German-American Helios 2 satellite suddenly saturate with an intense, unexplained burst of gamma radiation sweeping through the solar system.
evt-03-05-1979-venera-11.prompt: What do scientists eventually conclude triggered this record gamma-ray flash?

choices.text: A large solar flare from the Sun
A magnetar flare from a supernova remnant in the Large Magellanic Cloud
A simultaneous instrument malfunction across all three probes
Radiation from a nearby comet's tail

evt-03-05-1979-venera-11.butterflyEffect: By comparing arrival times across the widely separated spacecraft, astronomers triangulated the source to the supernova remnant N49 in the Large Magellanic Cloud. The event provided the first solid evidence for soft gamma repeaters, later understood as flares from magnetars—ultra-magnetized neutron stars—reshaping high-energy astrophysics.

evt-03-05-1981-zx81.scenario: It is early 1981 and you work for Sinclair Research in Cambridge, finalizing the launch strategy for the ZX81, successor to the ZX80. The team must decide what kind of machine this is meant to be.
evt-03-05-1981-zx81.prompt: What is the core design goal you set for the ZX81?

choices.text: An educational clone built to compete directly with the Apple II
A low-cost, mass-market introduction to home computing
A dedicated arcade-style games console
A high-end workstation aimed at engineers and businesses

evt-03-05-1981-zx81.butterflyEffect: Sinclair aimed the ZX81 squarely at ordinary households, and the gamble paid off spectacularly: over 1.5 million units sold, with Timex licensing it in the US as the Timex Sinclair 1000. Its success helped ignite Britain's home-computer boom and cleared the path for the far more popular ZX Spectrum.

evt-03-05-1982-venera-14.scenario: It is 5 March 1982, and you are a Soviet engineer monitoring Venera 14 as it touches down on the scorching Venusian surface. The lander's mechanical arm is about to swing out to test how firm the ground is, while a lens cap ejects from one of its cameras nearby.
evt-03-05-1982-venera-14.prompt: What happens to the compressibility test when the lens cap falls?

choices.text: It is blown safely away by Venus's high winds
The cap burns up instantly in the dense atmosphere
It lands right under the arm, skewing the soil-hardness reading
The arm fails to deploy at all because of the fallen cap

evt-03-05-1982-venera-14.butterflyEffect: The ejected lens cap landed directly beneath the surface-compressibility probe, so instead of measuring soil the instrument tested the cap itself, returning a misleadingly "hard" reading. The mishap became a cautionary tale in planetary mission design about anticipating where discarded hardware might fall.

evt-03-05-2002-2002-mindanao-earthquake.scenario: It is just after 5 a.m. on 5 March 2002 in Mindanao, and a powerful magnitude 7.5 earthquake begins shaking your house. Furniture is toppling and the roof beams are groaning overhead.
evt-03-05-2002-2002-mindanao-earthquake.prompt: What is the safest immediate action to take as the shaking continues?

choices.text: Grab valuables from shelves before leaving the building
Drop to the floor, take cover under sturdy furniture, and hold on until the shaking stops
Run immediately for the nearest doorway and stand in the frame
Rush outside past falling debris to reach open ground

evt-03-05-2002-2002-mindanao-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The megathrust quake, centered near the Cotabato Trench, killed 15 people and injured over 100 across the southern Philippines. It renewed scrutiny of building codes and disaster preparedness in a region long exposed to the collision of the Philippine Sea and Sunda plates.

evt-03-05-2021-pope-francis.scenario: It is 5 March 2021. You are part of Pope Francis's advance team in Baghdad, and despite pandemic warnings and lingering security fears from the ISIS occupation, he insists on a meeting that no pope has ever attempted before.
evt-03-05-2021-pope-francis.prompt: Which historic meeting does Pope Francis insist on holding in Najaf?

choices.text: A private audience with Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani
A public concert in Baghdad's Green Zone
A ceremonial Mass inside a former ISIS command post in Fallujah
A closed meeting with only the Iraqi president, skipping clerics

evt-03-05-2021-pope-francis.butterflyEffect: He met Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani, the first-ever meeting between a pope and the top Shia religious authority. The encounter was hailed as a landmark in Sunni-Shia-Christian relations and a call to protect Iraq's dwindling Christian minority after years of ISIS persecution.

evt-03-05-2023-2023-estonian-parliamenta.scenario: It is election night, 5 March 2023, in Tallinn. Ballots are being counted after a campaign dominated by support for Ukraine, inflation, and Estonia's security posture toward Russia.
evt-03-05-2023-2023-estonian-parliamenta.prompt: Which party emerges on top, positioning its leader to form the next government?

choices.text: Estonia 200
The Reform Party
The Centre Party
The Conservative People's Party (EKRE)

evt-03-05-2023-2023-estonian-parliamenta.butterflyEffect: Kaja Kallas's Reform Party won decisively with 37 seats, while the far-right EKRE came second. Kallas went on to form a coalition with Estonia 200 and the Social Democrats, continuing Estonia's strongly pro-Ukraine, pro-NATO foreign policy.

evt-03-06-845-abbasid-caliphate.scenario: You are one of 42 Byzantine officials held captive in Samarra since the sack of Amorium seven years ago. Your Abbasid captors now offer you freedom and rank if you renounce Christianity and embrace Islam.
evt-03-06-845-abbasid-caliphate.prompt: What do you choose, knowing refusal means execution?

choices.text: Refuse and accept execution
Offer ransom in exchange for freedom
Convert to secure release
Attempt a mass escape

evt-03-06-845-abbasid-caliphate.butterflyEffect: The prisoners refused conversion and were executed on the banks of the Tigris. The Eastern Orthodox Church canonized them as the Forty-Two Martyrs of Amorium, and their feast became a lasting symbol of steadfast faith under Muslim captivity.

evt-03-06-1836-texas-revolution.scenario: It is before dawn on 6 March 1836, and you are inside the Alamo mission in San Antonio. Santa Anna's Mexican army, numbering in the thousands, is storming the walls, and your commander William Travis has already refused to surrender.
evt-03-06-1836-texas-revolution.prompt: As the walls are breached, what do the Texian defenders do?

choices.text: Negotiate a prisoner exchange with Santa Anna's officers
Escape through a hidden tunnel beneath the mission
Surrender immediately to secure safe passage out
Fight to the death rather than surrender

evt-03-06-1836-texas-revolution.butterflyEffect: Nearly all the Alamo's defenders, including Travis, Bowie, and Crockett, were killed in the final assault. Their deaths became the rallying cry "Remember the Alamo," galvanizing Texian forces who defeated Santa Anna weeks later at San Jacinto, securing Texas independence.

evt-03-06-1853-giuseppe-verdi.scenario: It is the night of 6 March 1853 at La Fenice in Venice. Your new opera, La traviata, is being jeered by an audience who find the soprano cast as the consumptive heroine Violetta too old and too robust for the role.
evt-03-06-1853-giuseppe-verdi.prompt: What do you do after the disastrous premiere?

choices.text: Withdraw the opera permanently
Revise the opera for a future production
Publicly blame the audience and refuse changes
Rewrite it as a spoken drama instead of an opera

evt-03-06-1853-giuseppe-verdi.butterflyEffect: Verdi revised the opera, and a reworked version premiered successfully in Venice the following year. La traviata went on to become one of the most frequently performed operas in the world, proving the original failure was one of casting, not composition.

evt-03-06-1904-scottish-national-antarct.scenario: It is 1903, and your ship Scotia is anchored off the South Orkney Islands as part of William Speirs Bruce's Scottish expedition. Robert Falcon Scott's rival Discovery Expedition is getting all the press attention back home, but you have a choice to make about how to spend your limited resources here.
evt-03-06-1904-scottish-national-antarct.prompt: What should Bruce's expedition do to leave a lasting scientific legacy in Antarctica?

choices.text: Focus solely on mapping coastlines and skip weather observation entirely
Establish a staffed meteorological station to gather continuous weather data
Sail home early since Scott's expedition already has government backing
Abandon the scientific programme and race Scott toward the South Pole

evt-03-06-1904-scottish-national-antarct.butterflyEffect: Bruce's team built and staffed a meteorological station in the South Orkneys, the first permanently manned station in Antarctic territory. Later handed to Argentina, it became Orcadas Base, which remains in continuous operation today, the oldest such station in Antarctica.

evt-03-06-1913-first-balkan-war.scenario: It is 6 March 1913 and you command Greek infantry advancing on the fortified heights of Bizani, the last major obstacle before Ioannina, the historic capital of Epirus still held by Ottoman forces.
evt-03-06-1913-first-balkan-war.prompt: Do you press the assault on Bizani's defenses?

choices.text: Yes, press the assault until the fortress falls
Negotiate a truce with the Ottoman garrison
Bypass Bizani entirely and march directly on Ioannina
No, withdraw and wait for reinforcements from Athens

evt-03-06-1913-first-balkan-war.butterflyEffect: Greek forces stormed and captured the Bizani fortress, and Ioannina fell days later, ending centuries of Ottoman rule over Epirus. The victory boosted Crown Prince Constantine's prestige and helped secure Epirus for Greece in the postwar settlement.

evt-03-06-1930-communist-international.scenario: It is 6 March 1930, International Unemployment Day, called by the Communist International. You are a labor organizer in New York's Union Square, rallying jobless workers as police lines form around the crowd.
evt-03-06-1930-communist-international.prompt: What happens when the demonstration reaches its peak?

choices.text: Police and demonstrators clash violently
Employers agree on the spot to a jobs program
The rally is cancelled due to rain
The mayor personally addresses the crowd and disperses them peacefully

evt-03-06-1930-communist-international.butterflyEffect: The Union Square rally erupted into violent clashes with police, one of many such confrontations in cities worldwide that day. The unrest sharpened American fears of communist agitation even as it spotlighted Depression-era unemployment, a grievance the New Deal would later try to address.

evt-03-06-1953-joseph-stalin.scenario: It is 6 March 1953 and the Kremlin has just announced Stalin's death. You sit among the Presidium, aware that whoever fills the vacuum will steer the Soviet Union's future.
evt-03-06-1953-joseph-stalin.prompt: Who is named Premier of the Soviet Union in the immediate succession?

choices.text: Vyacheslav Molotov
Georgy Malenkov
Lavrentiy Beria
Nikita Khrushchev

evt-03-06-1953-joseph-stalin.butterflyEffect: Georgy Malenkov became Premier, but he was soon outmaneuvered by Nikita Khrushchev, who consolidated power through the Party apparatus. Khrushchev's eventual rise led to de-Stalinization and the 1956 denunciation of Stalin's crimes.

evt-03-06-1975-1975-algiers-agreement.scenario: It is March 1975 in Algiers, and you are part of the Iraqi delegation negotiating with Iran after a costly border conflict over the Shatt al-Arab waterway. Algeria is mediating, and Iraq badly wants Iran to stop backing Kurdish rebels inside its territory.
evt-03-06-1975-1975-algiers-agreement.prompt: What concession does Iraq accept to reach the settlement?

choices.text: Demand Iran cede all of Khuzestan Province outright
Accept the thalweg line as the border in exchange for Iran halting aid to Kurdish rebels
Propose joint international administration of the waterway indefinitely
Insist on keeping the entire Shatt al-Arab under Iraqi control

evt-03-06-1975-1975-algiers-agreement.butterflyEffect: Iraq agreed to the thalweg line as the official border on the Shatt al-Arab, in exchange for Iran ending support for the Kurdish insurgency. The agreement held only until 1980, when Iraq abrogated it and invaded Iran, igniting the eight-year Iran–Iraq War.

evt-03-06-1988-the-troubles.scenario: It is 6 March 1988 in Gibraltar. You are part of an SAS team tracking an IRA active service unit believed to be preparing a car bomb attack on a military ceremony, and you must decide how to intervene.
evt-03-06-1988-the-troubles.prompt: What action does the SAS team take against the suspected IRA unit?

choices.text: They arrest the suspects without incident
They detonate the bomb remotely to prove intent
They open fire, killing all three suspects
They call off the operation and let the unit leave Gibraltar

evt-03-06-1988-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The SAS shot dead all three IRA members, later ruled lawful killing by an inquest despite no bomb being found on them at that moment. The deaths triggered the Milltown Cemetery attack on mourners by a loyalist gunman, which in turn provoked the killing of two British soldiers at a subsequent funeral, deepening the cycle of violence.

evt-03-06-1988-operation-flavius.scenario: It is 6 March 1988, and you are part of a British surveillance team in Gibraltar, watching three IRA members you believe are planning a car bomb attack on a military band ceremony. They have just parked a car and are now walking away on foot.
evt-03-06-1988-operation-flavius.prompt: What actually followed when the SAS team moved to intercept them?

choices.text: The SAS shot them dead, though no bomb or weapons were found on them or in the car
Gibraltar police intervened first and defused the situation
The trio surrendered peacefully and were arrested without incident
The car bomb detonated before soldiers could reach it

evt-03-06-1988-operation-flavius.butterflyEffect: The SAS shot all three dead, but no weapons were found on them and no bomb was ever found in the car, fuelling accusations of a shoot-to-kill policy. The killings triggered a violent fortnight: gunmen attacked the funeral days later, and two British soldiers were then killed after driving into another IRA funeral procession, deepening the cycle of Troubles-era violence.

evt-03-07-321-constantine-the-great.scenario: You are a Roman magistrate in 321 AD, unrolling a fresh edict from Emperor Constantine that names the 'venerable day of the Sun' as a day set apart from ordinary business across the empire.
evt-03-07-321-constantine-the-great.prompt: What does Constantine's new decree actually require on that day?

choices.text: All pagan temples in the empire must be permanently shut
Courts are closed and city workshops must halt business, except for farm labor
Every citizen must attend a Christian church service
Christianity is declared the sole official religion of Rome

evt-03-07-321-constantine-the-great.butterflyEffect: The edict closed law courts and suspended urban labor on Sunday, though it explicitly permitted farmers to keep working their fields. It was not yet a Christian holy law but a civic one, and it laid the groundwork for Sunday becoming the standard weekly day of rest across Christian Europe for centuries.

evt-03-07-1573-ottoman-venetian-war-1570.scenario: It is March 1573, and you are a Venetian envoy negotiating with the Sublime Porte. Your fleet is exhausted, the Holy League has abandoned further campaigns, and Constantinople demands harsh terms to end the war.
evt-03-07-1573-ottoman-venetian-war-1570.prompt: What do you concede to secure peace with the Ottomans?

choices.text: Refuse all terms and continue the war alone
Retain Cyprus but pay annual tribute
Cede Crete instead of Cyprus
Cede Cyprus and pay a large indemnity

evt-03-07-1573-ottoman-venetian-war-1570.butterflyEffect: Venice formally ceded Cyprus and agreed to pay a large indemnity of 300,000 ducats. Despite the Christian victory at Lepanto two years earlier, the treaty confirmed Ottoman dominance in the eastern Mediterranean and marked the start of Venice's long naval and commercial decline.

evt-03-07-1850-daniel-webster.scenario: It's 7 March 1850 and you sit in the packed Senate gallery as Daniel Webster of Massachusetts rises to speak on the crisis over slavery in the territories won from Mexico.
evt-03-07-1850-daniel-webster.prompt: What position did Webster take, angering many back home in Massachusetts?

choices.text: He called for immediate abolition of slavery in all territories
He urged Northern acceptance of a stronger fugitive slave law as part of a broad compromise
He demanded Massachusetts secede from the Union
He proposed nationwide compensated emancipation

evt-03-07-1850-daniel-webster.butterflyEffect: Webster's 'Seventh of March' speech backed the Compromise of 1850, including a tougher fugitive slave law, and helped secure its passage, preserving the Union for another decade. It cost him dearly among Massachusetts abolitionists, who denounced him as a traitor; poet John Greenleaf Whittier branded him 'Ichabod.'

evt-03-07-1871-jose-paranhos-viscount-of.scenario: It's 1871, and you sit among conservative landowners in Brazil's General Assembly as the new Prime Minister, the Viscount of Rio Branco, brings his boldest reform to a vote despite fierce opposition from slaveholding interests.
evt-03-07-1871-jose-paranhos-viscount-of.prompt: What does Rio Branco's landmark law actually establish?

choices.text: It frees all enslaved people over the age of sixty
It grants freeborn status to children born to enslaved women
It bans the importation of new slaves but leaves existing bondage untouched
It abolishes slavery throughout the Brazilian Empire immediately

evt-03-07-1871-jose-paranhos-viscount-of.butterflyEffect: The Law of Free Birth (Lei do Ventre Livre) declared that children born to enslaved women from that point on would be free, marking the first major legislative step toward ending slavery in Brazil. It set a course that culminated seventeen years later in the 1888 Golden Law, which abolished slavery entirely.

evt-03-07-1936-remilitarisation-of-the-r.scenario: It's 7 March 1936 and you serve in the French high command as reports arrive that German troops have marched, unopposed, into the demilitarized Rhineland in flagrant breach of Versailles and Locarno.
evt-03-07-1936-remilitarisation-of-the-r.prompt: What did France and Britain actually do in response?

choices.text: France mobilized its army and crossed into the Rhineland
The League of Nations imposed immediate sanctions
They protested diplomatically but took no military action
Britain launched airstrikes on German positions

evt-03-07-1936-remilitarisation-of-the-r.butterflyEffect: France and Britain limited their response to diplomatic protest, lacking both the political will and the military readiness for confrontation. Hitler later admitted the gamble had been his most nerve-wracking, and the unopposed move emboldened him toward further treaty violations that led step by step toward war.

evt-03-07-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It's 7 March 1945 and you lead an American column approaching the Rhine at Remagen, astonished to find the Ludendorff Bridge still standing while German engineers scramble to wire it for demolition.
evt-03-07-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What did American commanders decide to do upon finding the bridge intact?

choices.text: Rush troops across before German engineers could destroy it
Detonate the bridge themselves to deny German reinforcements
Negotiate a local ceasefire with the bridge's guards
Withdraw and wait for pontoon bridges downstream

evt-03-07-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: US troops charged across the Ludendorff Bridge before it could be destroyed, seizing the Allies' first bridgehead across the Rhine into Germany's interior. The damaged bridge collapsed ten days later, but the crossing had already accelerated the Allied advance into the German heartland, hastening the war's end in Europe.

evt-03-07-1965-selma-to-montgomery-march.scenario: You are one of roughly 600 marchers crossing the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma on 7 March 1965, and ahead of you state troopers and mounted possemen block the road with orders to turn back.
evt-03-07-1965-selma-to-montgomery-march.prompt: What did the marchers do when ordered to disperse?

choices.text: They continued advancing peacefully and were beaten and tear-gassed
They fought back against the troopers with weapons
They turned back at once and the march ended quietly
They dispersed and abandoned the voting rights campaign

evt-03-07-1965-selma-to-montgomery-march.butterflyEffect: The marchers knelt to pray and continued forward, and troopers responded with tear gas and clubs, an assault broadcast nationwide as 'Bloody Sunday.' The televised violence shocked the country, spurred federal intervention, and helped push Congress to pass the Voting Rights Act later that year.

evt-03-07-1971-sheikh-mujibur-rahman.scenario: It is 7 March 1971, and you stand among hundreds of thousands crowding Dhaka's Racecourse Ground as Sheikh Mujibur Rahman rises to speak, with tensions against West Pakistan's military government at breaking point.
evt-03-07-1971-sheikh-mujibur-rahman.prompt: What does Mujib urge the crowd to do?

choices.text: Accept the military government's compromise offer
Prepare for a full independence struggle, turning every home into a fortress
Request United Nations mediation before taking any action
Call for a ceasefire and return to normal life

evt-03-07-1971-sheikh-mujibur-rahman.butterflyEffect: His speech, closing with the cry "Joy Bangla," called on Bengalis to turn every home into a fortress and prepare for struggle. It became the rhetorical foundation of the Bangladesh Liberation War, which erupted weeks later after Pakistan's Operation Searchlight and ended in Bangladesh's independence that December.

evt-03-07-1986-space-shuttle-challenger-.scenario: You are a launch engineer at Kennedy Space Center on a freezing January morning in 1986, reviewing overnight temperature data before Challenger's scheduled liftoff.
evt-03-07-1986-space-shuttle-challenger-.prompt: What component failure, worsened by the cold, ultimately doomed the shuttle 73 seconds into flight?

choices.text: An O-ring seal in a solid rocket booster failed in the cold
A damaged heat shield tile on the orbiter's wing
Insulating foam breaking away from the external fuel tank
A rupture in the main engine's fuel feed line

evt-03-07-1986-space-shuttle-challenger-.butterflyEffect: An O-ring seal in the right solid rocket booster failed to seat properly in the cold, letting hot gas burn through and trigger the breakup. The Rogers Commission's findings exposed flawed NASA safety culture and grounded the shuttle program for over two years while sweeping engineering and management reforms were put in place.

evt-03-07-1989-iran.scenario: It's early March 1989, weeks after Ayatollah Khomeini issued a fatwa calling for Salman Rushdie's death over 'The Satanic Verses.' You work in the British Foreign Office, and Iran has refused to disavow the fatwa or guarantee Rushdie's safety.
evt-03-07-1989-iran.prompt: What step does Britain take in response?

choices.text: Imposes trade sanctions but keeps its embassy open
Expels the Iranian ambassador while keeping ties intact
Refers the dispute to the United Nations Security Council
Breaks diplomatic relations with Iran

evt-03-07-1989-iran.butterflyEffect: The United Kingdom broke diplomatic relations with Iran, and Tehran severed ties in return, leaving no formal embassies for years. Relations were only gradually restored through the early 1990s, and the Rushdie affair remained a defining strain on Iran-Western relations for decades.

evt-03-07-2007-reform-of-the-house-of-lo.scenario: It's 7 March 2007 and you are an MP in the House of Commons, facing a series of free votes on the future composition of the House of Lords: fully elected, fully appointed, or various hybrid mixes.
evt-03-07-2007-reform-of-the-house-of-lo.prompt: Which option did the Commons ultimately back in these votes?

choices.text: A 50/50 hybrid of elected and appointed members
A wholly appointed House of Lords
Outright abolition of the House of Lords
A wholly elected House of Lords

evt-03-07-2007-reform-of-the-house-of-lo.butterflyEffect: MPs voted decisively for a wholly elected upper chamber, but the House of Lords itself voted for a wholly appointed one days later, leaving Parliament deadlocked. The impasse stalled substantial Lords reform for years, with only incremental change like the 2014 Act allowing peers to retire.

evt-03-07-2007-garuda-indonesia-flight-2.scenario: You are the co-pilot of Garuda Flight 200 on final approach to Yogyakarta on 7 March 2007. The aircraft is coming in far too fast and too steep for a safe landing.
evt-03-07-2007-garuda-indonesia-flight-2.prompt: What should the crew do to avoid disaster?

choices.text: Continue the landing and brake harder on touchdown
Shut down one engine to reduce speed on approach
Divert immediately to Jakarta without informing the tower
Execute a go-around and attempt the approach again

evt-03-07-2007-garuda-indonesia-flight-2.butterflyEffect: Instead of aborting, the pilots continued the unstabilized approach, and the 737 overran the runway into a rice field and burst into flames, killing 21 people. Both pilots were fired, and the crash added to a wave of scrutiny that saw the EU temporarily ban Indonesian carriers from its airspace over safety concerns.

evt-03-07-2009-kepler-space-telescope.scenario: You are a NASA engineer at Cape Canaveral on the night of the Kepler launch, watching the Delta II rocket carry a telescope designed to stare unblinking at over a hundred thousand distant stars.
evt-03-07-2009-kepler-space-telescope.prompt: How was Kepler designed to actually detect a planet around a distant star?

choices.text: By directly photographing planets against the glare of their star
By detecting gravitational lensing as a planet passes in front of a background star
By tracking a star's wobble caused by a planet's gravitational tug
By measuring the periodic dimming of a star's light as a planet transits in front of it

evt-03-07-2009-kepler-space-telescope.butterflyEffect: Kepler watched for the tiny, periodic dimming of starlight as a planet crossed in front of its star. Over nine years it confirmed thousands of exoplanets and revealed that small, rocky, Earth-sized worlds are common throughout the galaxy, reshaping the search for habitable planets and directly inspiring the follow-up TESS mission.

evt-03-07-2009-dissident-irish-republica.scenario: It's the evening of 7 March 2009 outside Massereene Barracks in County Antrim. Off-duty soldiers step out to the gate to collect a pizza delivery, unaware gunmen are waiting in the shadows nearby.
evt-03-07-2009-dissident-irish-republica.prompt: What followed this ambush by dissident republicans?

choices.text: The Provisional IRA claimed responsibility, ending its ceasefire
The Ulster Defence Association retaliated within hours
Two soldiers were killed, claimed by the Real IRA, the first such killing since 1997
An undercover patrol foiled the attack before shots were fired

evt-03-07-2009-dissident-irish-republica.butterflyEffect: The Massereene Barracks shooting, claimed by the Real IRA, killed two soldiers and was the first killing of British soldiers in Northern Ireland since 1997. It shocked a decade-old peace process, triggered heightened security alerts and arrests, and drew condemnation from both unionist and nationalist leaders, though dissident political support remained marginal.

evt-03-07-2009-massereene-barracks-shoot.scenario: You are a pizza delivery driver pulling up to the gates of Massereene Barracks in Antrim on the evening of 7 March 2009, where soldiers from the 38 Engineer Regiment are waiting to collect an order before deploying to Afghanistan.
evt-03-07-2009-massereene-barracks-shoot.prompt: Which paramilitary group claimed responsibility for the shooting that followed?

choices.text: The Provisional IRA
The Real IRA
The Continuity IRA
The Ulster Volunteer Force

evt-03-07-2009-massereene-barracks-shoot.butterflyEffect: The Real IRA claimed the attack, the first killing of British soldiers in Northern Ireland since the 1998 Good Friday Agreement. Political and community leaders from all sides condemned it, and it triggered intensified security operations against dissident republican groups without derailing the wider peace process.

evt-03-07-2024-sweden.scenario: It's March 2024, and you're a Swedish diplomat in Brussels watching your country prepare to abandon two centuries of military non-alignment in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
evt-03-07-2024-sweden.prompt: What does Sweden formally do this week?

choices.text: Joins NATO as its 32nd member
Signs a bilateral defense pact with the United States only
Joins the European Union's defense arm exclusively
Applies to join the Collective Security Treaty Organisation

evt-03-07-2024-sweden.butterflyEffect: Sweden becomes NATO's 32nd member, ending over 200 years of neutrality and following Finland's own accession the previous year. The move completes a historic realignment of Nordic security policy triggered directly by Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

evt-03-08-1655-northampton-county-virgin.scenario: You sit on the Northampton County court in March 1655, hearing indentured servant John Casor's claim that his term of service has expired, against Anthony Johnson's insistence that Casor belongs to him for life.
evt-03-08-1655-northampton-county-virgin.prompt: How does the court rule on Casor's claim?

choices.text: Casor's indenture has expired; he is freed
Casor is ordered transferred to another master
Casor is Johnson's servant for life
The case is dismissed for lack of evidence

evt-03-08-1655-northampton-county-virgin.butterflyEffect: The court sided with Johnson, declaring Casor his servant for life. The ruling is one of the earliest legal recognitions of lifetime, hereditary bondage in the Virginia colony, a precedent that helped pave the way toward the codification of race-based chattel slavery in later decades.

evt-03-08-1702-anne-queen-of-great-brita.scenario: It is 8 March 1702, and word has just reached Parliament that King William III has died. As a member of the Privy Council, you now serve the new sovereign, Queen Anne, the last Stuart to inherit the crown.
