evt-03-08-1702-anne-queen-of-great-brita.prompt: What major constitutional change unites two of Anne's kingdoms during her reign?

choices.text: The Act of Settlement securing the Hanoverian line
The Acts of Union 1707, merging England and Scotland
The Glorious Revolution restoring Protestant succession
The Toleration Act extending freedom to Dissenters

evt-03-08-1702-anne-queen-of-great-brita.butterflyEffect: In 1707 the Acts of Union merged England and Scotland into the single Kingdom of Great Britain, with Anne as its first monarch and one shared Parliament at Westminster. She died in 1714 without a surviving heir, triggering the Hanoverian succession under George I and reshaping British politics for centuries.

evt-03-08-1736-nader-shah.scenario: It is early 1736 on the plain of Dasht-e Moghan by the Aras River. You are a tribal khan summoned by the victorious general Nader, alongside thousands of nobles and clergy, to settle who will rule Persia now that the Safavid line has faltered.
evt-03-08-1736-nader-shah.prompt: What does the assembled gathering ultimately decide?

choices.text: Crown Nader as Shah, founding a new dynasty
Restore the young Safavid prince to the throne
Elect a council of regents to govern jointly
Invite the Ottoman Sultan to rule as overlord

evt-03-08-1736-nader-shah.butterflyEffect: The assembly crowned Nader as Shah, ending over two centuries of Safavid rule and founding the Afsharid dynasty. He went on to campaign as far as Delhi in 1739, seizing the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond, though his empire splintered quickly after his assassination in 1747.

evt-03-08-1910-raymonde-de-laroche.scenario: It is 8 March 1910 in France, and you are Raymonde de Laroche, waiting before officials of the Aéro-Club de France after completing your qualifying flights for a pilot's licence, a certificate no woman has ever held.
evt-03-08-1910-raymonde-de-laroche.prompt: What does the Aéro-Club decide after her qualifying flights?

choices.text: She receives only an honorary, non-flying certificate
She is granted a full pilot's licence, a first for a woman
She is asked to repeat the qualifying flights
She is denied a licence because of her sex

evt-03-08-1910-raymonde-de-laroche.butterflyEffect: The club granted her pilot's licence No. 36, making her the world's first licensed female pilot. Her achievement opened aviation to women, though she died in 1919 in a crash while attempting to set a new speed record, and she is remembered as a pioneer of women's flight.

evt-03-08-1919-1919-egyptian-revolution.scenario: It is March 1919 and word spreads through Cairo's streets: British authorities have arrested Wafd Party leader Saad Zaghloul and exiled him to Malta. You are a nationalist sympathizer weighing how Egyptians should respond.
evt-03-08-1919-1919-egyptian-revolution.prompt: What follows Zaghloul's arrest and exile from Egypt?

choices.text: The Wafd Party dissolves itself in protest
Nationalist leaders quietly accept the exile and disband
Nationwide protests and strikes erupt across the country
Egyptians petition the Ottoman Sultan for intervention

evt-03-08-1919-1919-egyptian-revolution.butterflyEffect: Nationwide strikes, demonstrations, and clashes with British forces erupted across Egypt for months. The unrest forced Britain to unilaterally declare Egyptian independence in 1922, though it retained control over defense, foreign affairs, and the Suez Canal, and Zaghloul later returned to lead Egypt as prime minister.

evt-03-08-1924-castle-gate-mine-disaster.scenario: It is 8 March 1924 near Castle Gate, Utah. Three explosions have torn through the coal mine, and you lead the volunteer rescue crew standing at the entrance, knowing the shafts below are filled with deadly carbon monoxide.
evt-03-08-1924-castle-gate-mine-disaster.prompt: As rescue leader, what do you do to try to reach any survivors?

choices.text: Send only a caged canary down first and wait several days
Enter the mine immediately to search for survivors despite the toxic gas
Evacuate the surrounding town before attempting any rescue
Refuse to enter until ventilation fans clear the shafts completely

evt-03-08-1924-castle-gate-mine-disaster.butterflyEffect: The rescue leader entered the gas-filled mine to search for survivors and was overcome by carbon monoxide, dying alongside the 171 miners already lost. The disaster, one of Utah's worst, spurred wider adoption of self-contained breathing apparatus and stricter gas-testing procedures for mine rescue teams nationwide.

evt-03-08-1963-ba-ath-party.scenario: It is before dawn on 8 March 1963 in Damascus. You are an army officer among a clique of Ba'athist and allied officers moving to seize radio stations, army barracks, and government buildings before the city wakes.
evt-03-08-1963-ba-ath-party.prompt: Once key installations are secured, what do the plotters announce?

choices.text: The restoration of the old Syrian parliament and constitution
The formation of a National Council of the Revolutionary Command under Ba'ath control
A request for United Nations peacekeepers to oversee elections
Immediate union of Syria with Gamal Abdel Nasser's Egypt

evt-03-08-1963-ba-ath-party.butterflyEffect: The coup installed a National Council of the Revolutionary Command and brought the Ba'ath Party to power in Syria for the first time. That seizure of the state set the stage for decades of Ba'athist rule, including Hafez al-Assad's 1970 takeover and the Assad family's grip on Syria that followed.

evt-03-08-1966-nelson-s-pillar.scenario: It is just after 1:30am on 8 March 1966. You are one of a small group of former IRA men who have wired explosives to the base of Nelson's Pillar on Dublin's O'Connell Street, timed to fall on the eve of the Easter Rising's 50th anniversary.
evt-03-08-1966-nelson-s-pillar.prompt: What actually happens when the charge detonates?

choices.text: The charge fails and the pillar remains untouched
The top half of the column, statue and all, is destroyed, leaving a jagged stump
The whole column instantly collapses into rubble
Dublin fire brigade cuts the fuse before it detonates

evt-03-08-1966-nelson-s-pillar.butterflyEffect: The blast destroyed the upper section of the column, toppling Nelson's statue, but left an unstable stump standing. Days later the Irish Army dynamited the remainder themselves—ironically shattering more shopfront windows than the original bomb had. The empty plinth stood for decades until the Spire of Dublin was erected there in 2003.

evt-03-08-1978-bbc-radio-4.scenario: You are a BBC Radio 4 producer in early 1978, holding Douglas Adams's script full of Vogons, towels, and a supercomputer called Deep Thought. Nothing like it has aired on the network before, and you must decide how to schedule it.
evt-03-08-1978-bbc-radio-4.prompt: What do you do with this untested science-fiction comedy?

choices.text: Broadcast it as planned in its scheduled slot
Hand it to Radio 3 for a more literary audience
Shelve it indefinitely as too strange for listeners
Cut it down to a single stand-alone episode

evt-03-08-1978-bbc-radio-4.butterflyEffect: Radio 4 broadcast the series as scheduled on 8 March 1978. It became a cult sensation, spawning five novels, a TV series, a 2005 film, and phrases like "42" and "Don't Panic" that entered popular culture, launching Douglas Adams's career.

evt-03-08-1979-voyager-1.scenario: You are an imaging scientist at JPL in March 1979, scanning through raw Voyager 1 photographs of Jupiter's moon Io. One frame shows a strange umbrella-shaped feature bulging off the moon's dark edge, unlike anything on the calibration charts.
evt-03-08-1979-voyager-1.prompt: What do you do with this odd crescent-shaped feature on Io's limb?

choices.text: Log it as a newly discovered small moon of Jupiter
Recalibrate the camera and discard the image as faulty
Flag it as a possible active volcanic plume erupting from the surface
Dismiss it as a camera lens flare and move to the next frame

evt-03-08-1979-voyager-1.butterflyEffect: Navigation engineer Linda Morabito identified it as an active volcanic plume rising hundreds of kilometers above Io's surface. It made Io the first body beyond Earth confirmed to have ongoing volcanic eruptions, forcing planetary scientists to rethink how tidal heating could power geology on small, icy-looking moons.

evt-03-08-1979-philips.scenario: It is 8 March 1979 and you are a Philips engineer in Eindhoven, unveiling a shining silver disc that plays music by laser instead of a needle. Journalists are impressed, but rival electronics firms are already sketching their own competing formats.
evt-03-08-1979-philips.prompt: What should Philips do next to keep this format from splintering the market?

choices.text: Merge the disc technology into the existing cassette format
Partner with Sony to agree a single worldwide CD standard
Patent the format exclusively and license it to no one
Wait for a government body to mandate a standard

evt-03-08-1979-philips.butterflyEffect: Philips joined forces with Sony to hammer out the shared Red Book standard, and the Compact Disc reached shops worldwide in 1982. The single agreed format let CDs sweep aside vinyl and cassette within a decade, and its data-storage cousin, the CD-ROM, later reshaped computing too.

evt-03-08-1983-cold-war.scenario: It is 8 March 1983, and you are addressing the National Association of Evangelicals in Orlando, weighing how bluntly to characterize the Soviet Union while arms-control talks with Moscow remain fragile.
evt-03-08-1983-cold-war.prompt: What phrase do you use to brand the Soviet Union before the assembled evangelicals?

choices.text: "An empire of tyranny"
"An evil empire"
"A totalitarian menace"
"A godless dictatorship"

evt-03-08-1983-cold-war.butterflyEffect: Reagan called the USSR "an evil empire," a phrase that became shorthand for his hardline Cold War stance. It energized conservative supporters, alarmed detente advocates, and set the rhetorical stage for his later Berlin Wall challenge and eventual negotiations with Gorbachev.

evt-03-08-1988-aeroflot-flight-3739-1988.scenario: You are the captain of Aeroflot Flight 3739 on 8 March 1988 when the Ovechkin family, desperate to defect from the Soviet Union, threatens the cockpit crew and demands you fly toward the West.
evt-03-08-1988-aeroflot-flight-3739-1988.prompt: How does the crew respond to the hijackers' demands?

choices.text: Negotiate for the hostages' release mid-flight
Refuse outright and attempt an immediate emergency landing
Pretend to comply while secretly diverting to a Soviet military airfield
Comply and fly directly toward Finland as demanded

evt-03-08-1988-aeroflot-flight-3739-1988.butterflyEffect: The pilots quietly diverted the aircraft to a military airfield at Veshchevo instead of the West, buying time for Soviet special forces to storm the plane. The assault ended in a violent shootout that killed several family members and a flight attendant, becoming one of the last high-profile hijackings before the Soviet Union's collapse.

evt-03-08-2001-space-shuttle-discovery.scenario: It is 8 March 2001, and you are a mission specialist aboard Space Shuttle Discovery, closing in on the International Space Station. In the cargo bay sits the Leonardo module, and the station's first residents are waiting to go home.
evt-03-08-2001-space-shuttle-discovery.prompt: What is the primary task once Discovery docks with the station?

choices.text: Repair the Hubble Space Telescope's optics
Deploy the Chandra X-ray Observatory into orbit
Attach the Zarya control module to the station
Deliver the Leonardo module and rotate the station's Expedition One crew for Expedition Two

evt-03-08-2001-space-shuttle-discovery.butterflyEffect: STS-102 delivered the Leonardo Multi-Purpose Logistics Module and swapped crews, sending the Expedition One astronauts home after 141 days and installing Expedition Two. It was the first crew rotation flight, proving the ISS could be kept permanently staffed — a model followed for the next two decades.

evt-03-08-2017-azure-window.scenario: It is 8 March 2017, and a fierce storm is battering Dwejra Bay on Gozo. You run boat tours beneath the Azure Window, the limestone arch that drew tourists and film crews, including the makers of Game of Thrones, to this stretch of coast.
evt-03-08-2017-azure-window.prompt: What happens to the arch as the storm hits?

choices.text: Divers manage to brace it with underwater supports
It survives with only minor surface cracking
Engineers deliberately dismantle it for public safety
It collapses completely into the sea and disappears

evt-03-08-2017-azure-window.butterflyEffect: The arch collapsed entirely into the sea within moments, vanishing after millennia of erosion finally gave way. The sudden loss of one of Malta's best-known landmarks and filming sites led authorities to tighten safety limits on boats near the eroding Gozo cliffs and step up monitoring of other natural formations nearby.

evt-03-08-2018-aurat-march.scenario: It's 8 March 2018, and you're one of a small group of organizers preparing to lead Pakistan's first-ever Aurat March through the streets of Karachi, unsure how the public and authorities will react.
evt-03-08-2018-aurat-march.prompt: What follows in the years after this first march?

choices.text: It becomes an annual tradition despite recurring backlash and legal petitions
It merges into existing labour day marches and loses its identity
The government bans all future women's rights demonstrations
It is quietly discontinued after one year for lack of interest

evt-03-08-2018-aurat-march.butterflyEffect: The Aurat March returned every 8 March in cities across Pakistan, drawing larger crowds and steady controversy over banners addressing domestic violence, harassment, and bodily autonomy. Despite lawsuits seeking to ban it, courts repeatedly upheld organizers' right to assemble, and the march became a fixture of Pakistan's women's rights movement.

evt-03-09-1009-name-of-lithuania.scenario: You are a monk keeping the Annals of Quedlinburg in 1009, recording news from missionary Bishop Bruno of Querfurt, who has journeyed into the pagan Baltic lands to preach and has met a violent end.
evt-03-09-1009-name-of-lithuania.prompt: How do you record the land where Bruno met his death?

choices.text: As Livonia, a coastal trading region
As Rus, a Slavic principality
As Prussia, a Baltic tribal confederation
As Litua, the pagan land where he was martyred

evt-03-09-1009-name-of-lithuania.butterflyEffect: The Annals recorded the name in the form 'Litua' — the earliest known written record of the name of Lithuania. The land remained pagan for centuries, becoming the last officially pagan state in Europe until its rulers converted to Christianity in 1387.

evt-03-09-1776-adam-smith.scenario: It is March 1776, and a new book by an Edinburgh professor is unsettling coffeehouse debates across Britain. Merchants and ministers alike are arguing over whether the nation's wealth truly depends on hoarding gold and guarding trade monopolies.
evt-03-09-1776-adam-smith.prompt: According to Adam Smith's new book, what should governments do to make a nation prosperous?

choices.text: Stockpile gold and silver through strict mercantilist controls
Loosen trade restrictions and let self-interested markets allocate resources
Nationalize major industries under royal charter
Ban foreign imports to protect domestic manufacturers entirely

evt-03-09-1776-adam-smith.butterflyEffect: The Wealth of Nations argued that free markets, competition, and the division of labor—not gold reserves or state monopolies—generate national wealth. It became the foundational text of classical economics, influencing policy debates on free trade and capitalism for centuries afterward.

evt-03-09-1842-rancho-san-francisco.scenario: It's 9 March 1842, and you're resting near a stream at Rancho San Francisco with rancher Francisco López, who has just woken from a nap under an oak tree and pulls up some wild onions for his midday meal.
evt-03-09-1842-rancho-san-francisco.prompt: What does López notice clinging to the onion roots that changes California's history?

choices.text: Nothing unusual; he simply cooks and eats them
Traces of oil
Flecks of gold
Fragments of silver ore

evt-03-09-1842-rancho-san-francisco.butterflyEffect: López had discovered gold in what is now Placerita Canyon, six years before the famous 1848 find at Sutter's Mill that triggered the California Gold Rush. His discovery drew a small, earlier wave of prospectors to the area, and the site is still commemorated today as the 'Oak of the Golden Dream.'

evt-03-09-1842-nabucco.scenario: It's the evening of 9 March 1842 at La Scala in Milan. You watch an obscure 28-year-old composer's new opera about the Babylonian exile of the Israelites unfold, and the chorus of enslaved Hebrews swells through the hall.
evt-03-09-1842-nabucco.prompt: What happens next for the young composer, Giuseppe Verdi?

choices.text: The premiere flops and Verdi spends another decade in provincial theaters
Nabucco becomes an instant sensation, making Verdi's name overnight
Verdi abandons opera altogether to write only sacred choral music
Austrian censors ban the opera after one night for its political overtones

evt-03-09-1842-nabucco.butterflyEffect: Nabucco's triumph launched Verdi as Italy's leading opera composer for the next half-century. The chorus "Va, pensiero" became entwined with Risorgimento nationalist sentiment and was later sung at Verdi's own funeral as a symbol of Italian unity.

evt-03-09-1847-mexican-american-war.scenario: It's March 9, 1847. You are packed into a small boat off the coast near Veracruz with thousands of other soldiers under General Winfield Scott, about to land on an open beach within range of a Mexican fortress.
evt-03-09-1847-mexican-american-war.prompt: What tactic does Scott use to take Veracruz?

choices.text: A naval blockade alone, without landing any troops
A night assault straight against the fortress walls
A massive amphibious landing followed by a prolonged siege and bombardment
A negotiated surrender before any troops came ashore

evt-03-09-1847-mexican-american-war.butterflyEffect: The landing of over 10,000 men went unopposed, the largest U.S. amphibious operation to that date. After weeks of siege and bombardment, Veracruz surrendered, opening the road Scott's army would take inland to capture Mexico City later that year.

evt-03-09-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: It's March 9, 1862. You stand on the cramped deck of the ironclad USS Monitor in Hampton Roads, facing the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia a day after it devastated the Union's wooden fleet.
evt-03-09-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: How does this first clash between ironclad warships end?

choices.text: Virginia rams and sinks Monitor
Both ships withdraw without firing a single shot
An inconclusive hours-long duel that neither side can win outright
Monitor sinks Virginia within the first hour

evt-03-09-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The hours-long duel ended in a tactical draw, but it proved that cannonballs could no longer sink armored ships. Navies worldwide took notice, and a global race to build ironclad fleets began, ending the age of wooden warships.

evt-03-09-1891-ka-iulani.scenario: It is 1891, and you are a Hawaiian legislator watching young Princess Kaʻiulani, still studying abroad, formally named heir apparent after her uncle King Kalākaua's death. Two years later, the monarchy itself will be overthrown by American-backed businessmen.
evt-03-09-1891-ka-iulani.prompt: After the 1893 overthrow, what does the teenage Kaʻiulani do to defend her kingdom's cause?

choices.text: Leads an armed uprising against the provisional government
Remains silent in Europe and renounces her claim publicly
Joins the Committee of Safety to negotiate her own coronation
Travels to Washington to plead her kingdom's case before President Cleveland

evt-03-09-1891-ka-iulani.butterflyEffect: Kaʻiulani sailed to Washington to meet President Grover Cleveland, winning sympathy that fed into the Blount Report condemning the overthrow. Congress nonetheless refused restoration, and the United States annexed Hawaii in 1898; she died the following year, never having reigned.

evt-03-09-1932-eamon-de-valera.scenario: It's March 9, 1932. Your party, Fianna Fáil, has just won the general election on a promise to dismantle the remaining ties of the Anglo-Irish Treaty, and you are about to take office as head of the Irish Free State's government for the first time.
evt-03-09-1932-eamon-de-valera.prompt: What is your first major move as the new head of government?

choices.text: Immediately declare a republic and leave the Commonwealth
Begin dismantling the Oath of Allegiance to the British Crown
Reinstate the monarchy's full authority over Irish affairs
Call for a fresh election within the year

evt-03-09-1932-eamon-de-valera.butterflyEffect: De Valera's peaceful transfer of power, the first in the young state's history, stabilized Irish democracy. His systematic unwinding of the Treaty's provisions, beginning with the Oath, culminated in the 1937 Constitution and set Ireland on the path to full republic status.

evt-03-09-1933-franklin-d-roosevelt.scenario: It's March 9, 1933, five days into your presidency. Banks nationwide sit shuttered under the four-day "holiday" you declared, and you have just sent Congress a bill to reopen them under federal oversight.
evt-03-09-1933-franklin-d-roosevelt.prompt: What does Congress do with the Emergency Banking Act?

choices.text: Congress rejects it, forcing an indefinite extension of the bank holiday
Congress sends it to committee for weeks of hearings before voting
Congress passes it within hours, with almost no debate, that very day
Congress amends it to nationalize every bank outright

evt-03-09-1933-franklin-d-roosevelt.butterflyEffect: Congress passed the act unanimously and Roosevelt signed it into law that same night. Public confidence was restored as banks reopened in stages with deposits exceeding withdrawals, setting the rapid pace for the rest of the New Deal's "Hundred Days."

evt-03-09-1956-tbilisi.scenario: It's early March 1956 in Tbilisi, and thousands of Georgians have filled the streets after Khrushchev's speech denouncing Stalin, a native son, becomes known. Soviet authorities must decide how to answer the swelling crowds.
evt-03-09-1956-tbilisi.prompt: How does the Soviet government respond to the demonstrations?

choices.text: It sends troops to forcibly disperse the crowds, resulting in bloodshed
It ignores the demonstrations, letting them fizzle out
It grants Georgia expanded autonomy within the Soviet Union
It negotiates with protest leaders and restores Stalin's monuments

evt-03-09-1956-tbilisi.butterflyEffect: Soviet troops and armored vehicles were sent in to forcibly disperse the crowds, opening fire and causing many casualties in one of the first violent crackdowns on dissent after Stalin's death. The episode fed a lasting current of Georgian grievance against Moscow that resurfaced in later Soviet-era protests and in Georgia's independence movement decades on.

evt-03-09-1957-1957-andreanof-islands-ea.scenario: It's the early hours of 9 March 1957, and Hawaii's civil defense sirens are sounding after a massive earthquake near Alaska's Andreanof Islands sends a tsunami racing across the Pacific.
evt-03-09-1957-1957-andreanof-islands-ea.prompt: What should coastal residents in Hawaii do as the warning sounds?

choices.text: Head to the beach to watch the wave arrive
Evacuate low-lying coastal areas immediately for higher ground
Ignore the warning since Alaska quakes rarely reach Hawaii
Secure boats in the harbor and wait it out at home

evt-03-09-1957-1957-andreanof-islands-ea.butterflyEffect: The tsunami caused significant damage across the Hawaiian Islands, especially in Hilo, but the Pacific warning system built after the deadly 1946 tsunami let most residents evacuate in time, sparing many lives. The event reinforced the value of the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center and spurred further improvements to Pacific-wide detection.

evt-03-09-1959-barbie.scenario: It is March 9, 1959, and you are watching Ruth Handler unveil her new doll at the American International Toy Fair in New York. Unlike the baby dolls filling the other booths, this one has an adult woman's figure and a wardrobe of tiny fashionable outfits.
evt-03-09-1959-barbie.prompt: What makes Handler's new doll different from the baby dolls dominating the market?

choices.text: She is modeled as an adult woman with changeable fashion outfits
She is sold only through a mail-order catalog
She is designed to be an educational science teaching tool
She is marketed exclusively to adult collectors, not children

evt-03-09-1959-barbie.butterflyEffect: Barbie was marketed as a grown, fashionable adult woman rather than an infant, letting girls imagine careers and lifestyles through her. The doll became Mattel's most profitable line, with over a billion sold, and expanded into films, games, and decades of ongoing debate over body image.

evt-03-09-1967-svetlana-alliluyeva.scenario: You are Svetlana Alliluyeva, Stalin's daughter, standing in New Delhi in March 1967 after scattering your late husband's ashes in the Ganges, weighing whether to fly home to Moscow as your visa requires.
evt-03-09-1967-svetlana-alliluyeva.prompt: What do you do instead of returning to the Soviet Union?

choices.text: Seek asylum at the British embassy instead
Walk into the U.S. embassy and request political asylum
Board her scheduled flight back to Moscow as planned
Contact the Soviet embassy to request an extended visa

evt-03-09-1967-svetlana-alliluyeva.butterflyEffect: She walked into the U.S. embassy in Delhi and requested asylum, defecting to the West in a major Cold War embarrassment for Moscow. She later settled in America as Lana Peters, published memoirs critical of her father's regime, and died in the United States in 2011.

evt-03-09-1977-washington-d-c.scenario: You are a hostage negotiator in Washington, D.C., as twelve armed men led by Hamaas Abdul Khaalis seize three buildings, including the District Building, where councilman Marion Barry has just been shot.
evt-03-09-1977-washington-d-c.prompt: What condition finally persuades the gunmen to surrender after 39 tense hours?

choices.text: National television agrees to air their full demands live
The gunmen receive a large ransom payment
Diplomats from Muslim nations broker a religiously grounded surrender
Police storm the buildings and overpower them

evt-03-09-1977-washington-d-c.butterflyEffect: Ambassadors from Egypt, Pakistan, and Iran negotiated an end by invoking the Quran and agreeing to let Khaalis face trial for the earlier murder of his family, whose killers he blamed on a film about Islam. All hostages were freed; Marion Barry survived his wound and went on to become mayor of Washington, D.C.

evt-03-09-2000-nupedia.scenario: It is March 2000, and you have just volunteered to write an entry for Nupedia, the new online encyclopedia. Your draft must pass through seven stages of expert review before anyone will ever read it, and after a year the site has only about twenty articles.
evt-03-09-2000-nupedia.prompt: Frustrated by the slow pace, what do founders Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger create in January 2001?

choices.text: A paid subscription encyclopedia service
An open wiki-based encyclopedia anyone can edit instantly
A partnership with Encyclopædia Britannica to merge content
A print edition to distribute the reviewed articles faster

evt-03-09-2000-nupedia.butterflyEffect: They launched Wikipedia as a fast, open, wiki-based companion to Nupedia, letting anyone edit instantly instead of waiting for expert review. Wikipedia's article count exploded past Nupedia's within months, and by 2003 Nupedia shut down while Wikipedia grew into the world's largest encyclopedia.

evt-03-09-2011-space-shuttle-discovery.scenario: It is March 9, 2011, and you are a flight controller at Kennedy Space Center watching Space Shuttle Discovery glide in for touchdown after its 39th and final mission. Ground crews are already preparing for what comes next in its long career.
evt-03-09-2011-space-shuttle-discovery.prompt: What happens to Discovery after this final landing?

choices.text: It is converted into a test vehicle for future rocket designs
It is refurbished immediately for another orbital mission
It is retired and prepared for museum display at the Smithsonian
It is dismantled entirely for spare parts

evt-03-09-2011-space-shuttle-discovery.butterflyEffect: Discovery was retired and later transferred to the Smithsonian's Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center for permanent display. Its retirement marked the winding down of the entire Space Shuttle program, which ended in 2012, pushing NASA toward reliance on commercial spacecraft for crew launches.

evt-03-09-2012-2012-2014-salvadoran-gang.scenario: It is March 2012 in San Salvador. As Minister of Public Security, you sit down with mediators and a bishop to negotiate directly with imprisoned leaders of MS-13 and Barrio 18, hoping to halt the country's soaring homicide rate.
evt-03-09-2012-2012-2014-salvadoran-gang.prompt: What concession do you offer the gang leaders to secure the truce?

choices.text: Abolish the death penalty as a goodwill gesture
Grant full amnesty for all past crimes
Transfer top gang leaders to lower-security prisons with improved conditions
Pay gang leaders directly from the national budget

evt-03-09-2012-2012-2014-salvadoran-gang.butterflyEffect: The government transferred top gang leaders from a maximum-security prison to lower-security facilities with looser visitation rules, and homicides fell sharply for over a year. The truce unraveled by 2014 amid mistrust and political backlash, and violence later returned even worse, paving the way for President Bukele's mass-incarceration crackdown.

evt-03-09-2020-giuseppe-conte.scenario: It is the evening of 9 March 2020. As Italy's cases of a new virus surge past the north, you sit before television cameras as Prime Minister, holding an order that will change how forty million Italians live tomorrow.
evt-03-09-2020-giuseppe-conte.prompt: What do you announce to the nation?

choices.text: A full nationwide lockdown confining Italians to their homes
A lockdown limited only to the Lombardy region
Voluntary guidelines with no legal restrictions
Closure of Italy's borders only, with domestic life unchanged

evt-03-09-2020-giuseppe-conte.butterflyEffect: Conte announced a nationwide lockdown, making Italy the first country outside China to confine its entire population to control COVID-19. The move became a template studied and soon copied by governments across Europe and beyond within weeks.

evt-03-09-2023-2023-hamburg-shooting.scenario: In the days after the attack on the Kingdom Hall in Hamburg's Alsterdorf quarter, investigators dig into how the gunman, Philipp Fusz, obtained the firearms he used.
evt-03-09-2023-2023-hamburg-shooting.prompt: What does the investigation reveal about his access to weapons?

choices.text: He stole them from a police armory
He manufactured them himself using a 3D printer
He bought them illegally on the black market
He legally owned the guns as a licensed sport shooter

evt-03-09-2023-2023-hamburg-shooting.butterflyEffect: Authorities confirmed Fusz was a licensed sport shooter who legally owned the firearms used in the attack, reigniting debate in Germany over background checks tied to mental health. The tragedy also led Jehovah's Witnesses congregations worldwide to review security at their meeting halls.

evt-03-10-bce241-roman-republic.scenario: It is 10 March 241 BC. You captain a Carthaginian quinquereme laden with grain and reinforcements, sailing to relieve the besieged garrison at Lilybaeum when Rome's battle-ready fleet appears off the Aegates Islands.
evt-03-10-bce241-roman-republic.prompt: What follows the clash between the two fleets?

choices.text: The Carthaginian relief fleet breaks through and resupplies Lilybaeum
Both fleets withdraw without engaging
The Carthaginians ambush and rout the Roman fleet
The Roman fleet decisively defeats the undermanned Carthaginian ships

evt-03-10-bce241-roman-republic.butterflyEffect: The lighter, better-crewed Roman ships smashed the overloaded Carthaginian fleet, cutting off Sicily's last hope of resupply. Carthage sued for peace, ceding Sicily as Rome's first overseas province under the Treaty of Lutatius, ending the First Punic War and setting the two powers on course for the far bloodier Second Punic War a generation later.

evt-03-10-1876-alexander-graham-bell.scenario: It is March 10, 1876, in a Boston workshop. You are Thomas Watson, sitting in the next room with a receiver pressed to your ear, waiting to see if Alexander Graham Bell's device can carry a human voice through wire.
evt-03-10-1876-alexander-graham-bell.prompt: What words come through the receiver, becoming the first sentence ever transmitted by telephone?

choices.text: Hello, hello, is anyone there?
Watson, come and see this remarkable device.
Watson, come quickly, I need your assistance.
Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.

evt-03-10-1876-alexander-graham-bell.butterflyEffect: Bell's words to Watson, "Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you," confirmed the first working telephone just days after Bell filed his patent, narrowly ahead of rival inventor Elisha Gray. The device transformed long-distance communication and led Bell to co-found AT&T in 1885, building the telecommunications backbone still in use today.

evt-03-10-1915-battle-of-neuve-chapelle.scenario: It is 10 March 1915 near Neuve-Chapelle. Your battalion has just smashed through the German front line, but the telephone wires to headquarters have been cut by your own artillery barrage, and no fresh orders are coming.
evt-03-10-1915-battle-of-neuve-chapelle.prompt: With the gap open and no orders arriving, what should you do to keep the breakthrough alive?

choices.text: Wait for a runner to bring confirmed orders from headquarters
Dig in on the captured trench line and hold position
Push your men forward immediately to exploit the gap before the Germans recover
Request another artillery bombardment before advancing further

evt-03-10-1915-battle-of-neuve-chapelle.butterflyEffect: British reserves were held back awaiting confirmation through the broken communication chain, giving German defenders time to rush reinforcements and seal the gap. The stalled follow-through became a textbook lesson in the danger of rigid command structures without flexible communication, shaping how the British Army planned later offensives like the Somme.

evt-03-10-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 9–10 March 1945. You command a B-29 squadron ordered to abandon high-altitude daylight bombing and instead strike Tokyo at low altitude, after dark, loaded with incendiaries.
evt-03-10-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What tactical change do you adopt for this raid on Tokyo's wooden districts?

choices.text: Drop leaflets warning civilians before any bombing begins
Fly low at night with incendiary bombs to spread fire through wooden buildings
Switch to a naval blockade instead of further air raids
Maintain high-altitude daylight precision bombing on military targets only

evt-03-10-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Operation Meetinghouse became the single most destructive bombing raid of the war, killing roughly 100,000 people and burning out much of the city in one night. Its firestorm convinced US commanders that incendiary raids on Japan's wooden cities were devastatingly effective, and similar attacks followed on dozens more cities that spring.

evt-03-10-1949-mildred-gillars.scenario: It's March 1949 in a Washington, D.C. courtroom. You are on the jury weighing the treason case against Mildred Gillars, the American-born broadcaster known as "Axis Sally," accused of broadcasting Nazi propaganda aimed at demoralizing Allied troops.
evt-03-10-1949-mildred-gillars.prompt: What verdict does the jury reach on the treason charge?

choices.text: Guilty of a lesser charge of disloyalty
Guilty of treason
Acquitted on grounds of duress from her Nazi employers
Not guilty due to insufficient evidence of intent

evt-03-10-1949-mildred-gillars.butterflyEffect: Gillars was convicted on one count of treason and sentenced to ten to thirty years, becoming the first woman convicted of treason against the United States. She served over a decade before parole in 1961, and her case, alongside "Tokyo Rose" Iva Toguri's, set precedent for prosecuting American wartime propagandists.

evt-03-10-1959-1959-tibetan-uprising.scenario: It is 10 March 1959 in Lhasa. Thousands of Tibetans have surrounded the summer palace to protect the Dalai Lama from feared arrest, and Chinese artillery is moving into position as tensions escalate by the hour.
evt-03-10-1959-1959-tibetan-uprising.prompt: As the crisis deepens over the following days, what does the Dalai Lama decide to do?

choices.text: Flee north toward Chinese-controlled territory to seek protection
Remain in the palace to negotiate directly with Chinese authorities
Take up arms and join the resistance fighters in the streets
Escape secretly toward India before the situation grows more dangerous

evt-03-10-1959-1959-tibetan-uprising.butterflyEffect: The Dalai Lama slipped out of Lhasa in disguise and made a grueling journey over the Himalayas to India, where he was granted asylum. He established a Tibetan government-in-exile in Dharamsala that continues to this day, keeping the Tibetan cause before the world for over six decades.

evt-03-10-1966-nguyen-cao-ky.scenario: It's March 1966 in Saigon. You are Prime Minister Nguyễn Cao Kỳ, uneasy about the popular General Nguyễn Chánh Thi, whose independent command of I Corps in central Vietnam has built him a power base that rivals your own.
evt-03-10-1966-nguyen-cao-ky.prompt: What do you do about General Thi?

choices.text: Arrest him on corruption charges
Negotiate a power-sharing arrangement with him
Promote him to a ceremonial post in Saigon
Dismiss him from his command

evt-03-10-1966-nguyen-cao-ky.butterflyEffect: Kỳ dismissed Thi from his command, and the move ignited the Buddhist Uprising, months of civil unrest and armed confrontation in Hue and Da Nang between government troops and dissident forces. The crisis deepened political instability in South Vietnam and further shook American confidence in the reliability of its ally's government during the war.

evt-03-10-1975-1975-spring-offensive.scenario: It is March 1975. As a North Vietnamese Army planner, you have troops massed in the Central Highlands and must choose where to strike first to shatter South Vietnam's weakest defenses.
evt-03-10-1975-1975-spring-offensive.prompt: Which Central Highlands city do you target to open the general offensive?

choices.text: Pleiku
Da Nang
Buôn Ma Thuột
Hue

evt-03-10-1975-1975-spring-offensive.butterflyEffect: PAVN struck Buôn Ma Thuột on 10 March, and it fell within two days. The shock led President Thieu to order a disastrous, poorly organized retreat from the Highlands that turned into a rout, accelerating the collapse that ended with Saigon's fall on 30 April 1975.

evt-03-10-1989-air-ontario-flight-1363.scenario: It's the morning of 10 March 1989 in Dryden, Ontario. You are the captain of Air Ontario Flight 1363, sitting on the runway as snow falls and ice clings visibly to the wings — but the plane's auxiliary power unit is broken, so shutting down the engines to de-ice properly would strand you with no way to restart them.
evt-03-10-1989-air-ontario-flight-1363.prompt: What does the captain ultimately decide to do?

choices.text: Return to the gate and shut the engines down for full de-icing
Delay on the runway and call for a de-icing truck with engines running
Take off without de-icing, accepting the risk
Divert to a nearby airport equipped for de-icing

evt-03-10-1989-air-ontario-flight-1363.butterflyEffect: The captain took off without de-icing the wings, and the plane failed to gain altitude, crashing into trees beyond the runway. The Moshansky Commission's investigation exposed systemic failures at Air Ontario and Transport Canada, reshaping Canadian aviation rules on de-icing, holdover times, and a captain's authority to refuse an unsafe departure.

evt-03-10-1991-1991-salvadoran-legislati.scenario: It is 10 March 1991 in San Salvador. Civil war between the government and FMLN guerrillas is still raging as citizens line up to vote for a new Legislative Assembly.
evt-03-10-1991-1991-salvadoran-legislati.prompt: Which party emerges with the most seats, though short of an outright majority?

choices.text: The Christian Democratic Party (PDC)
The Nationalist Republican Alliance (ARENA)
A legally registered FMLN party
The National Conciliation Party (PCN)

evt-03-10-1991-1991-salvadoran-legislati.butterflyEffect: ARENA took 39 of 84 seats, enough to dominate but not to govern alone, forcing coalition bargaining in the Assembly. That fractured legislature helped push both sides toward the negotiations that produced the 1992 Chapultepec Peace Accords ending the civil war.

evt-03-10-2000-dot-com-bubble.scenario: It is mid-morning on 10 March 2000. Your tech-heavy portfolio has quintupled in eighteen months and the NASDAQ ticker just flashed a fresh all-time high of 5,048.
evt-03-10-2000-dot-com-bubble.prompt: With euphoria at its peak, what should you do with your stock gains?

choices.text: Move all your cash into new IPOs launching that week
Sell into the rally and lock in your gains
Hold everything, since growth stocks never correct
Buy more shares on margin to maximize returns

evt-03-10-2000-dot-com-bubble.butterflyEffect: That day marked the top; the NASDAQ fell 78% over the next two and a half years and most dot-com startups vanished. Investors who cashed out that week preserved fortunes, while survivors like Amazon and eBay had to prove real profitability before the market trusted internet companies again.

evt-03-10-2006-nasa.scenario: It is 10 March 2006 at mission control. NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter is about to fire its engines for orbit insertion, then pass behind Mars, cutting off radio contact with Earth for the most critical minutes of the mission.
evt-03-10-2006-nasa.prompt: During the communication blackout behind Mars, what keeps the spacecraft on course to enter orbit safely?

choices.text: It enters a low-power safe mode and drifts until contact resumes
It waits in place until Earth regains radio contact before firing engines
It deploys solar sails to slow its approach
It carries out the pre-programmed engine burn using its own onboard computer

evt-03-10-2006-nasa.butterflyEffect: The orbiter executed its pre-programmed burn entirely on its own computer, successfully entering Mars orbit without any real-time human guidance. MRO went on to map the planet in unprecedented detail, identifying landing sites for later rovers including Curiosity and Perseverance.

evt-03-10-2006-mars-reconnaissance-orbit.scenario: It's March 10, 2006, and you're a flight controller at JPL watching telemetry as the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter fires its engines to slow down and be captured by Martian gravity after a seven-month journey from Earth.
evt-03-10-2006-mars-reconnaissance-orbit.prompt: What must the spacecraft do next before it can begin its science mission?

choices.text: Deploy a rover before entering orbit around Mars
Begin high-resolution imaging immediately from its arrival orbit
Land instrument packages directly on the Martian surface
Spend months aerobraking to settle into its final circular orbit

evt-03-10-2006-mars-reconnaissance-orbit.butterflyEffect: MRO spent six months aerobraking, skimming the thin Martian atmosphere to gradually shrink its orbit into a low, circular path. By late 2006 it began its primary science phase, later helping map water ice and select landing sites for rovers, and it remains a vital data relay for Mars surface missions today.

evt-03-10-2019-ethiopian-airlines-flight.scenario: It's March 10, 2019, hours after Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 goes down near Bishoftu just six minutes after leaving Addis Ababa. Investigators quickly note unsettling similarities to Lion Air Flight 610, which crashed five months earlier flying the same aircraft type.
evt-03-10-2019-ethiopian-airlines-flight.prompt: What do aviation regulators around the world do in the days that follow?

choices.text: Ground the entire Boeing 737 MAX fleet worldwide
Wait for the final investigation report before taking any action
Order extra pilot training while keeping the planes flying
Restrict 737 MAX flights to routes over water only

evt-03-10-2019-ethiopian-airlines-flight.butterflyEffect: Countries began grounding the Boeing 737 MAX one by one, and within days the FAA joined them, grounding the entire fleet worldwide for roughly twenty months. Investigations centered on the MCAS flight-control system, forcing Boeing into costly software redesigns, congressional hearings, and lasting reputational damage.

evt-03-10-2023-silicon-valley-bank.scenario: It's March 10, 2023. Your fast-growing tech startup holds millions in uninsured deposits at Silicon Valley Bank, which has just disclosed a huge loss on bond sales, sending its stock plunging and triggering a panicked wave of withdrawal requests.
evt-03-10-2023-silicon-valley-bank.prompt: What do federal regulators do over the following weekend to contain the crisis?

choices.text: Merge SVB immediately with a larger bank without federal backing
Freeze all deposits indefinitely pending review
Guarantee all deposits, including those above the insured limit
Let uninsured depositors absorb losses to avoid moral hazard

evt-03-10-2023-silicon-valley-bank.butterflyEffect: The FDIC seized SVB on Friday, and regulators invoked a systemic risk exception to guarantee all deposits, even those above the $250,000 insured limit. The Fed launched a new emergency lending facility as fears spread to other regional banks, and SVB's assets were later sold to First Citizens BancShares.

evt-03-10-2026-bam-adebayo.scenario: It is the fourth quarter on 10 March 2026. Bam Adebayo has already poured in an astonishing scoring total against the Wizards, and the Heat have the win comfortably in hand.
evt-03-10-2026-bam-adebayo.prompt: Do you leave Adebayo on the floor to chase a historic scoring night?

choices.text: Keep him in to chase the scoring record
Rest him for the entire fourth quarter to prepare for the next game
Switch him to point guard duties for the rest of the game
Pull him immediately to avoid injury risk in a decided game

evt-03-10-2026-bam-adebayo.butterflyEffect: Adebayo stayed in and finished with 83 points, the second-highest single-game total in NBA history, trailing only Wilt Chamberlain's 100-point game from 1962 and surpassing Kobe Bryant's famous 81-point night from 2006.

evt-03-11-1669-mount-etna.scenario: It is March 1669, and a wall of molten lava creeps toward Catania's ancient walls. You join a crew led by Diego di Pappalardo, wrapped in wet cowhides, planning to hack open the lava's cooled crust with iron bars to steer the flow away from the city.
evt-03-11-1669-mount-etna.prompt: What happens when the crew tries to divert the lava away from Catania?

choices.text: The crew abandons the attempt, overcome by the intense heat before finishing
Armed villagers from Paternò, fearing the lava will now strike their own town, drive off the crew and the diversion fails
The diversion succeeds and the lava is guided harmlessly into the sea
The Spanish viceroy halts the plan, declaring it an affront to divine will

evt-03-11-1669-mount-etna.butterflyEffect: Armed men from nearby Paternò, whose own land now lay in the diverted flow's path, drove the crew off and the attempt collapsed. Lava went on to breach Catania's walls and fill part of its harbor, but the episode is remembered as one of the earliest recorded attempts at engineered lava diversion, a technique successfully revived during Etna eruptions in the 1990s and 2000s to protect towns with barriers and channels.

evt-03-11-1708-anne-queen-of-great-brita.scenario: It's 1708, a French fleet has just tried and failed to land a Jacobite pretender in Scotland, and Parliament now wants to arm the Scottish militia. You must advise the Queen on the bill sitting before her.
evt-03-11-1708-anne-queen-of-great-brita.prompt: What did Queen Anne do with the Scottish Militia Bill?

choices.text: She signed it into law immediately
She withheld royal assent, blocking the bill
She referred it to the Privy Council for amendment
She dissolved Parliament instead of deciding

evt-03-11-1708-anne-queen-of-great-brita.butterflyEffect: Fearing armed Scots so soon after the invasion scare, Anne withheld royal assent — the last time any British monarch has vetoed an act of Parliament. Her refusal cemented a constitutional convention: the veto power technically remains but has never been used again in over three centuries.

evt-03-11-1843-eta-carinae.scenario: It's March 1843, and from the Cape of Good Hope Observatory, astronomer John Herschel watches Eta Carinae flare until it outshines every star in the sky but Sirius.
evt-03-11-1843-eta-carinae.prompt: What should Herschel do with this extraordinary observation?

choices.text: Report it as a brief nova expected to fade within days
Assume it is a new comet and calculate its orbit
Dismiss the change as an artifact of atmospheric distortion
Carefully record its brightness and position for future comparison

evt-03-11-1843-eta-carinae.butterflyEffect: Herschel's careful records of the star's brightening during this "Great Eruption" gave later astronomers a rare baseline for studying a star's violent mass loss in real time. The ejected material formed the Homunculus Nebula, and Eta Carinae is now studied as a strong candidate to one day end its life as a supernova.

evt-03-11-1845-maori-people.scenario: It is dawn on 11 March 1845 in Kororāreka. Hōne Heke's warriors have just cut down the British flagstaff again and, with Te Ruki Kawiti, are storming the town as gunfire and explosions erupt near the magazine.
evt-03-11-1845-maori-people.prompt: What should the British garrison and settlers do as the attack overwhelms the town?

choices.text: Wait for reinforcements from Auckland before responding
Surrender the town immediately and negotiate terms on land
Evacuate residents to ships in the harbour and abandon the town
Hold the flagstaff position at all costs

evt-03-11-1845-maori-people.butterflyEffect: The magazine exploded, the garrison could not hold, and settlers evacuated to ships in the bay while Kororāreka was looted and burned. The sacking opened the Flagstaff War, the first major armed conflict between Māori and the Crown, foreshadowing decades of land wars across New Zealand.

evt-03-11-1851-rigoletto.scenario: It's the night of March 11, 1851, backstage at La Fenice in Venice, and Verdi has waited until the very last rehearsal to hand the tenor his showstopping aria.
evt-03-11-1851-rigoletto.prompt: Why did Verdi withhold 'La donna è mobile' until the final rehearsal?

choices.text: To surprise the orchestra during the performance
Because he hadn't finished composing it
To satisfy the Austrian censors' demands
To stop it leaking into the streets before opening night

evt-03-11-1851-rigoletto.butterflyEffect: Verdi's caution worked too well: the tune became so instantly infectious that gondoliers were reportedly singing it around Venice within days of the premiere. 'La donna è mobile' remains one of opera's most recognizable melodies, and Rigoletto's success helped cement Verdi's dominance of Italian opera.

evt-03-11-1888-great-blizzard-of-1888.scenario: It's the morning of 12 March 1888 in Manhattan. Snowdrifts already top ten feet, the elevated trains sit frozen on their tracks, and broken telegraph wires dangle over the streets.
evt-03-11-1888-great-blizzard-of-1888.prompt: What's the wisest way to try to get to work today?

choices.text: Walk along the elevated train tracks to bypass the street drifts
Stay home; the city is effectively shut down for days
Take a ferry across the Hudson to avoid the worst streets
Hire a horse-drawn sleigh, since the roads remain passable

evt-03-11-1888-great-blizzard-of-1888.butterflyEffect: Most New Yorkers simply stayed put, since the city was effectively paralyzed for nearly a week. The chaos of tangled, storm-felled telegraph and power lines convinced city leaders that above-ground infrastructure was too fragile, helping push forward the enclosed, underground subway system that finally opened in New York in 1904.

evt-03-11-1978-coastal-road-massacre.scenario: It's the days after the March 11, 1978 hijacking and killings on Israel's coastal highway, and the Israeli cabinet is weighing how to respond to the cross-border raid by Fatah militants.
evt-03-11-1978-coastal-road-massacre.prompt: What military response did Israel launch in the days that followed?

choices.text: Operation Litani into southern Lebanon
Airstrikes on Damascus
A ground invasion of the Sinai
A naval blockade of Beirut

evt-03-11-1978-coastal-road-massacre.butterflyEffect: On March 14, 1978, Israel launched Operation Litani, sending forces into southern Lebanon to push PLO fighters back from the border. The operation deepened Israel's entanglement in Lebanon's civil war and helped set the stage for the far larger 1982 invasion.

evt-03-11-1984-anime.scenario: It is March 1984 in Tokyo, and you are producing Hayao Miyazaki's new film about a princess fighting to protect a poisoned, insect-ruled world. Early screenings of Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind are drawing strong audience reactions.
evt-03-11-1984-anime.prompt: With the film proving a success, what should Miyazaki and his collaborators do next?

choices.text: License the story only for a live-action adaptation
Sell the story rights to a Hollywood studio for wider release
Use the film's success to found their own animation studio
Retire from animation, content with one acclaimed film

evt-03-11-1984-anime.butterflyEffect: Buoyed by Nausicaä's acclaim, Miyazaki and producer Isao Takahata used the momentum to found Studio Ghibli in 1985. The studio went on to produce landmark films like My Neighbor Totoro and Spirited Away, reshaping animation worldwide.

evt-03-11-1993-united-states-senate.scenario: It is 11 March 1993, and you are a U.S. senator considering Bill Clinton's third nominee for Attorney General after two earlier choices withdrew over controversies involving undocumented household staff.
evt-03-11-1993-united-states-senate.prompt: How should the Senate handle the vote on confirming Janet Reno?

choices.text: Delay the vote pending further background investigation
Reject her nomination over her Florida prosecutorial record
Confirm her narrowly along strict party lines
Confirm her unanimously as the first female Attorney General

evt-03-11-1993-united-states-senate.butterflyEffect: The Senate confirmed Reno unanimously, making her the first woman to serve as U.S. Attorney General. She went on to serve the longest tenure of any Attorney General in the 20th century, overseeing major controversies including the Waco siege and the Elián González case.

evt-03-11-2004-2004-madrid-train-bombing.scenario: It's the morning of 11 March 2004, three days before Spain's general election, and coordinated bombs have just torn through packed commuter trains in Madrid. You are a government spokesperson facing reporters within the hour.
evt-03-11-2004-2004-madrid-train-bombing.prompt: Who does the outgoing government publicly blame for the attack in the hours that follow?

choices.text: Al-Qaeda-linked cells, matching the findings later confirmed by investigators
A rogue faction within the Spanish military
ETA, the Basque separatist group, despite emerging evidence of Islamist involvement
Anarchist extremists opposed to Spain's NATO membership

evt-03-11-2004-2004-madrid-train-bombing.butterflyEffect: The government's insistence on ETA, contradicted within days by evidence pointing to a Madrid-based Islamist cell avenging Spain's role in the Iraq War, fueled public anger over perceived manipulation of the tragedy. Three days later voters ousted the ruling Popular Party, and the incoming Socialist government withdrew Spanish troops from Iraq.

evt-03-11-2006-michelle-bachelet.scenario: It's March 11, 2006, in Santiago, and Michelle Bachelet has just been sworn in as Chile's first female president, with her cabinet appointments about to make headlines of their own.
evt-03-11-2006-michelle-bachelet.prompt: What did Bachelet do differently when she named her first cabinet?

choices.text: She excluded all members of her own Socialist Party
She appointed equal numbers of men and women
She retained every minister from the previous government
She appointed only military officers to security posts

evt-03-11-2006-michelle-bachelet.butterflyEffect: Bachelet's gender-parity cabinet was a first for Chile and drew international attention to her presidency. She later became the founding head of UN Women in 2010, carrying her advocacy for gender equality onto the global stage.

evt-03-11-2007-2007-georgia-helicopter-i.scenario: It is 11 March 2007 and you are a Georgian government spokesperson. Three unmarked military helicopters have just struck Chkhalta in the Kodori Gorge, the last pocket of Abkhazia still under Tbilisi's control, damaging a school and the exiled Abkhaz government's headquarters.
evt-03-11-2007-2007-georgia-helicopter-i.prompt: How should Georgia respond to the attack on the Kodori Gorge?

choices.text: Launch an immediate retaliatory strike on Abkhaz separatist positions
Stay silent to avoid provoking Moscow further
Ask Russian investigators to jointly examine the wreckage
Publicly accuse Russia and raise the incident in international forums

evt-03-11-2007-2007-georgia-helicopter-i.butterflyEffect: Georgia publicly accused Russia of orchestrating the strike, while Moscow denied it and claimed its aircraft had been grounded that weekend. The unresolved incident deepened mutual suspicion between the two states, one of many frictions that built toward the outright Russo-Georgian War of August 2008.

evt-03-11-2008-space-shuttle-endeavour.scenario: It's March 11, 2008, and Space Shuttle Endeavour has just cleared the tower on mission STS-123, carrying a new robotic helper bound for the International Space Station.
evt-03-11-2008-space-shuttle-endeavour.prompt: What piece of hardware does Endeavour deliver to the ISS on this flight?

choices.text: A replacement mirror for the Hubble Space Telescope
Dextre, the two-armed robotic handyman
The first module of the ISS
Components for a Mars rover

evt-03-11-2008-space-shuttle-endeavour.butterflyEffect: Endeavour delivered Dextre, the Special Purpose Dexterous Manipulator, along with the first section of Japan's Kibo laboratory. Dextre went on to perform routine external maintenance and repairs on the ISS without requiring spacewalks, saving astronauts countless hours outside the station.

evt-03-11-2009-2009-winnenden-shootings.scenario: It is the week after 11 March 2009, and you sit in the Baden-Württemberg state legislature. A 17-year-old former student has just killed fifteen people at his old school and a nearby car dealership using a pistol legally registered to his father.
evt-03-11-2009-2009-winnenden-shootings.prompt: What reform should lawmakers pursue in response to the shooting?

choices.text: Focus reform entirely on video game content instead of firearms
Require stricter, inspected storage for privately owned firearms
Ban all civilian firearm ownership nationwide
Leave gun laws unchanged as an isolated tragedy

evt-03-11-2009-2009-winnenden-shootings.butterflyEffect: Germany tightened its firearms law, requiring stricter, checked storage of legally owned weapons and random home inspections for gun licence holders. The Winnenden shooting remains one of the deadliest school attacks in German history and reshaped national debate on gun safety.

evt-03-11-2010-sebastian-pinera.scenario: It's March 11, 2010, at Congress in Valparaíso, and Chile is still reeling from a massive earthquake two weeks earlier as Sebastián Piñera takes the presidential oath.
evt-03-11-2010-sebastian-pinera.prompt: What marred the ceremonial flypast during Piñera's inauguration?

choices.text: A helicopter was forced to land due to high winds
The flypast was cancelled after an earthquake aftershock
One aircraft ran out of fuel over the crowd
Two Air Force helicopters collided in midair

evt-03-11-2010-sebastian-pinera.butterflyEffect: Two military helicopters collided during the flypast display, and the crash killed members of the crew, casting a somber note over a ceremony already shadowed by the earthquake's devastation. The tragedy underscored how much recovery work still lay ahead for Piñera's new government.

evt-03-11-2011-2011-tohoku-earthquake-an.scenario: It is the afternoon of 11 March 2011 at the Fukushima Daiichi plant. The earthquake has already cut external power, and you watch the tsunami surge over the seawall toward the emergency diesel generators.
evt-03-11-2011-2011-tohoku-earthquake-an.prompt: What critical failure follows the loss of backup power to the reactors?

choices.text: Automatic shutdown safely contains all three reactors
Backup batteries maintain cooling for weeks without issue
Portable diesel generators restart cooling in time to avert meltdown
Cooling systems fail, leading to reactor meltdowns

evt-03-11-2011-2011-tohoku-earthquake-an.butterflyEffect: Without power, cooling systems failed and heat built inside the reactors, leading to meltdowns in three units and a hydrogen explosion that blew out a refueling hall. The disaster forced mass evacuations around Fukushima and triggered a global reassessment of nuclear safety, with Germany accelerating its planned reactor phase-out and Japan idling its entire nuclear fleet for review.

evt-03-11-2012-united-states-army.scenario: It is the morning of 11 March 2012 at a base in Kandahar Province. Staff Sergeant Robert Bales has returned from a night patrol during which he walked to nearby villages and killed sixteen Afghan civilians in their homes.
evt-03-11-2012-united-states-army.prompt: What should U.S. military command do upon learning of the killings?

choices.text: Discipline his unit informally and keep him on active duty
Hand him over to Afghan authorities for local prosecution
Arrest him, remove him from Afghanistan, and refer him to court-martial
Record the deaths as combat casualties and close the matter

evt-03-11-2012-united-states-army.butterflyEffect: Bales was arrested, flown out of Afghanistan, and later court-martialed, pleading guilty in 2013 to avoid the death penalty and receiving life without parole. The massacre badly strained U.S.-Afghan relations under President Hamid Karzai and intensified pressure to accelerate the withdrawal of American troops.

evt-03-11-2012-kandahar-massacre.scenario: It is the early hours of 11 March 2012 in Panjwayi District, Kandahar Province. Staff Sergeant Robert Bales has just walked back onto the base after leaving his post without authorization overnight.
evt-03-11-2012-kandahar-massacre.prompt: What happens when fellow soldiers confront Bales about where he has been?

choices.text: He tells them "I did it" and is immediately taken into custody
He slips away and evades capture for several weeks
He resists arrest and is shot by military police
He claims he was on an authorized patrol and is released pending review

evt-03-11-2012-kandahar-massacre.butterflyEffect: Bales told authorities "I did it" and was taken into custody that morning. He later pleaded guilty to avoid the death penalty and was sentenced to life without parole, while the killings inflamed Afghan public anger and became a rallying point for critics of the long American military presence in the country.

evt-03-11-2020-covid-19-pandemic.scenario: It is 11 March 2020 in Geneva. You sit among WHO officials reviewing case counts from over 110 countries, debating how to formally characterize the outbreak that began in Wuhan months earlier.
evt-03-11-2020-covid-19-pandemic.prompt: What announcement does the WHO Director-General make that day?

choices.text: WHO declares its first-ever public health emergency of international concern
WHO downgrades the outbreak to a regional epidemic
WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic
WHO recommends against any travel restrictions

evt-03-11-2020-covid-19-pandemic.butterflyEffect: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus declared COVID-19 a pandemic, a step beyond the public health emergency already declared in January. Within days, governments worldwide moved to lockdowns, border closures, and emergency economic measures, kicking off the deepest global recession since the Great Depression and an unprecedented rush to develop vaccines.

evt-03-11-2021-president-of-the-united-s.scenario: It's March 11, 2021, and you're standing behind President Biden in the Oval Office as he signs a $1.9 trillion pandemic relief bill that passed Congress without a single Republican vote.
evt-03-11-2021-president-of-the-united-s.prompt: What did the American Rescue Plan primarily deliver to most American households?

choices.text: Direct $1,400 stimulus checks
Free public college tuition
Automatic mortgage forgiveness
A permanent universal basic income

evt-03-11-2021-president-of-the-united-s.butterflyEffect: The law sent most adults a $1,400 stimulus check, extended unemployment aid, and temporarily expanded the child tax credit, which cut child poverty nearly in half for a year. Passed through budget reconciliation, it became a flashpoint in later debates over whether the spending fueled the inflation surge of 2021-2022.

evt-03-12-538-ostrogoths.scenario: It's March 538, outside the walls of Rome. You serve in King Vitiges' Ostrogothic army, encamped in the ruined suburbs after nearly a year of blockade, as supplies dwindle while Belisarius's garrison inside receives fresh reinforcements from Ravenna.
evt-03-12-538-ostrogoths.prompt: What does King Vitiges decide to do?

choices.text: Wait through another winter for Rome to starve
Break the siege and withdraw the army north to Ravenna
Negotiate a truce splitting control of the city
Launch one final all-out assault on the Aurelian Walls

evt-03-12-538-ostrogoths.butterflyEffect: After roughly a year of failed assaults and mounting losses, Vitiges lifted the siege and withdrew north, having failed to dislodge Belisarius. The Byzantine hold on Rome marked a turning point in Justinian's Gothic War, which would drag on for nearly two more decades before Ostrogothic power in Italy finally collapsed.

evt-03-12-1088-pope-urban-ii.scenario: You are a cardinal gathered at Terracina in March 1088, choosing a successor to the reform-minded Pope Gregory VII. The candidate before you, Odo of Châtillon, is a former prior of Cluny with a reputation for discipline and diplomacy.
evt-03-12-1088-pope-urban-ii.prompt: What should the cardinals do about the papal vacancy?

choices.text: Recall the exiled antipope Clement III instead
Elect Odo of Châtillon as pope
Delay the election and negotiate with the Holy Roman Emperor first
Ask the Byzantine Emperor to arbitrate the choice

evt-03-12-1088-pope-urban-ii.butterflyEffect: The cardinals elected Odo, who took the name Urban II. Seven years later he preached at the Council of Clermont, calling for the First Crusade, which reshaped relations between Christendom and the Islamic world for centuries.

evt-03-12-1622-ignatius-of-loyola.scenario: You kneel in St Peter's Basilica in March 1622 as Pope Gregory XV formally proclaims Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Society of Jesus, and his companion Francis Xavier as saints of the Catholic Church.
evt-03-12-1622-ignatius-of-loyola.prompt: What does this canonization confirm about the Jesuit order's standing?

choices.text: That the Jesuits are barred from missionary work outside Europe
That the Society of Jesus is fully sanctioned by Rome as a model of Catholic renewal
That Ignatius is condemned posthumously for heresy
That the Jesuit order is being dissolved and absorbed into the Dominicans

evt-03-12-1622-ignatius-of-loyola.butterflyEffect: The joint canonization affirmed the Jesuits as a central force in the Counter-Reformation, boosting their global missionary and educational efforts. Ignatius became patron of retreats and spiritual exercises, while Xavier became patron of missionaries, and Jesuit schools and missions expanded across Europe, Asia, and the Americas in the following century.

evt-03-12-1913-capital-hill-australian-c.scenario: You stand on Kurrajong Hill on 12 March 1913 beside Lady Denman, wife of the governor-general, as she prepares to reveal the name chosen for Australia's new federal capital city.
evt-03-12-1913-capital-hill-australian-c.prompt: What name does Lady Denman announce for the new capital?

choices.text: Denman City
Canberra
Kurrajong
Federation City

evt-03-12-1913-capital-hill-australian-c.butterflyEffect: Lady Denman announced the name 'Canberra,' derived from an Aboriginal word believed to mean 'meeting place.' The site atop Capital Hill would later host Australia's new Parliament House, cementing Canberra's role as the nation's political heart.

evt-03-12-1928-st-francis-dam.scenario: It's dusk on 12 March 1928, hours before the St. Francis Dam will fail. As dam keeper, you spot muddy water seeping from the base and fresh cracks along the face, but your supervisor insists it's normal for a new structure.
evt-03-12-1928-st-francis-dam.prompt: What should you do about this warning sign?

choices.text: Patch the leak with concrete at first light
Log it and continue routine monitoring
Sound the alarm and evacuate the canyon below immediately
Slowly lower the reservoir level over the coming days

evt-03-12-1928-st-francis-dam.butterflyEffect: The leak was dismissed as ordinary seepage; hours later, just before midnight, the dam collapsed catastrophically, sending a wall of water down San Francisquito Canyon that killed over 400 people. The disaster ended chief engineer William Mulholland's career and led to sweeping reforms in dam safety oversight and engineering licensing across California.

evt-03-12-1930-salt-march.scenario: It's dawn at Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930. You are one of 78 volunteers Gandhi has chosen to walk 240 miles to the sea and break a hated colonial law.
evt-03-12-1930-salt-march.prompt: What law was the march to Dandi designed to defy?

choices.text: Restrictions on public assembly
The British monopoly and tax on salt
The ban on wearing homespun cloth
The land revenue tax on farmers

evt-03-12-1930-salt-march.butterflyEffect: On 6 April, Gandhi scooped seawater and evaporated it into salt, openly breaking the British monopoly and tax on salt. The act ignited mass civil disobedience across India, drew worldwide press attention, and eventually forced the British to negotiate with Gandhi at the Second Round Table Conference.

evt-03-12-1952-hastings-ismay-1st-baron-.scenario: You are Lord Ismay in March 1952, stepping into the newly created post of NATO Secretary General. The alliance is barely three years old, and member states are still arguing over how much authority the post should hold.
evt-03-12-1952-hastings-ismay-1st-baron-.prompt: How does Ismay define his mission as NATO's first Secretary General?

choices.text: Act as a coordinator building consensus among member states, not a supreme commander
Push for a single unified NATO army under his direct command
Focus mainly on economic aid rather than defense coordination
Remain a ceremonial figurehead with no policy role

evt-03-12-1952-hastings-ismay-1st-baron-.butterflyEffect: Ismay famously summed up NATO's purpose as being 'to keep Russia out, America in, and Germany down.' His pragmatic, coordinating style set the template for the office, helping NATO survive its early Cold War growing pains and remain the West's central military alliance.

evt-03-12-1967-suharto.scenario: You are a delegate at the Provisional People's Consultative Assembly session in March 1967, where General Suharto, already holding executive power since the failed 1965 coup and its bloody aftermath, awaits formal confirmation as president.
evt-03-12-1967-suharto.prompt: What does the Assembly do regarding Suharto's status as head of state?

choices.text: Call for new nationwide elections before naming any leader
Reaffirm Sukarno as president with Suharto as a subordinate minister
Dissolve the presidency entirely in favor of a military junta
Formally strip Sukarno of presidential power and name Suharto acting president

evt-03-12-1967-suharto.butterflyEffect: The Assembly formally named Suharto acting president, sidelining Sukarno for good; a year later he became full president. His 'New Order' regime would rule Indonesia for three decades, combining anti-communist purges, economic development, and authoritarian control until his fall in 1998.

evt-03-12-2003-world-health-organization.scenario: It's 12 March 2003 at WHO headquarters in Geneva. Reports are arriving of a mysterious severe respiratory illness spreading rapidly among hospital staff and travelers linked to Hong Kong, Hanoi, and Guangdong.
evt-03-12-2003-world-health-organization.prompt: What does the WHO do in response?

choices.text: Issue a global alert warning of the atypical pneumonia outbreak
Wait for confirmed lab identification of the pathogen before any statement
Recommend closing all international airports in Asia
Quietly notify only the affected national governments

evt-03-12-2003-world-health-organization.butterflyEffect: The WHO issued a rare global alert naming the illness Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome and urged heightened surveillance worldwide. The outbreak that followed infected over 8,000 people across dozens of countries and became a template for the international health regulations reformed in its aftermath.

evt-03-12-2004-president-of-south-korea.scenario: It is March 2004 and you are a lawmaker in South Korea's National Assembly. President Roh Moo-hyun has publicly urged voters to back his party ahead of elections, which opposition members say violates election law neutrality rules.
evt-03-12-2004-president-of-south-korea.prompt: What does the National Assembly do in response to Roh's remarks?

choices.text: Vote to impeach and suspend President Roh
Issue a formal censure but take no further action
Refer the matter directly to the Supreme Court for a criminal trial
Call for Roh's voluntary resignation without a vote

evt-03-12-2004-president-of-south-korea.butterflyEffect: The Assembly voted to impeach Roh and suspend his powers, but the Constitutional Court overturned the impeachment in May 2004, ruling the violation too minor to warrant removal. Roh returned to office strengthened, and his party won a landslide in the interim elections.

evt-03-12-2009-bernie-madoff.scenario: It's 12 March 2009 in a federal courtroom in Manhattan. You are Bernie Madoff, standing before Judge Denny Chin on eleven federal felony charges after decades running your investment advisory business.
evt-03-12-2009-bernie-madoff.prompt: What does Madoff do when asked to enter a plea?

choices.text: Plead guilty to all charges without a plea deal
Negotiate a plea bargain for reduced charges
Name accomplices in exchange for leniency
Plead not guilty and demand a jury trial

evt-03-12-2009-bernie-madoff.butterflyEffect: Madoff pleaded guilty to all eleven counts, admitting his Ponzi scheme had defrauded investors of tens of billions of dollars over decades. He was sentenced to 150 years in prison, and the case triggered SEC reforms and lawsuits against feeder funds and regulators who had missed repeated warnings.

evt-03-12-2014-2014-east-harlem-gas-expl.scenario: It's the morning of 12 March 2014 in East Harlem. Neighbors have smelled gas for days and phoned it in, but no one has acted before two apartment buildings go up.
evt-03-12-2014-2014-east-harlem-gas-expl.prompt: What did investigators later find had made the explosion possible?

choices.text: Failures by the gas utility and city to act on leak reports
A boiler malfunction inside one building
An unrelated subway construction accident
A deliberate act of arson

evt-03-12-2014-2014-east-harlem-gas-expl.butterflyEffect: The blast killed eight people and displaced 100 families. In 2015 the NTSB concluded that failures by Consolidated Edison and city agencies to respond to leak reports had let the hazard fester, spurring renewed scrutiny of New York's aging gas pipe network.

evt-03-12-2018-us-bangla-airlines-flight.scenario: It's 12 March 2018 and you're aboard the Q400 on final approach into Kathmandu's Tribhuvan airport, sensing the cockpit crew is arguing with air traffic control over which runway to use.
evt-03-12-2018-us-bangla-airlines-flight.prompt: What went wrong on the flight's final approach that investigators pointed to?

choices.text: A bird strike that disabled both engines
An onboard bomb detonation
A lightning strike during final approach
Pilot confusion and disregard of air traffic control's runway instructions

evt-03-12-2018-us-bangla-airlines-flight.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the pilot became disoriented, contradicted air traffic control's runway instructions, and the aircraft crashed and burst into flames, killing 51 of 71 aboard. It remains the deadliest crash involving a Bangladeshi airline and prompted a review of procedures at Kathmandu's notoriously difficult, mountain-ringed airport.

evt-03-12-2019-european-union-withdrawal.scenario: It's the evening of 12 March 2019 in the House of Commons. You are Prime Minister Theresa May, returned from Strasbourg with last-minute legal assurances on the Northern Ireland backstop, hoping to win over rebellious MPs before the vote on your Brexit deal.
evt-03-12-2019-european-union-withdrawal.prompt: What happens when the vote is called?

choices.text: The deal passes narrowly, securing Brexit on schedule
The vote is postponed indefinitely by the Speaker
The deal is defeated again, this time by 149 votes
MPs approve the deal with a second referendum amendment attached

evt-03-12-2019-european-union-withdrawal.butterflyEffect: May's revised deal was rejected 391 to 242, the second crushing defeat for her Brexit agreement. The result forced Parliament to vote on ruling out no-deal and delaying Article 50, deepening the political crisis that led to May's resignation months later.

evt-03-12-2020-united-states.scenario: It's the evening of 11 March 2020 and you're watching President Trump address the nation from the Oval Office as European coronavirus cases climb sharply.
evt-03-12-2020-united-states.prompt: Which travelers did Trump's newly announced 30-day ban actually target?

choices.text: Travelers from the 26 Schengen Area countries, excluding the UK and Ireland
Only travelers arriving directly from Italy
All travelers arriving from anywhere in Europe including Britain
Every foreign national regardless of origin

evt-03-12-2020-united-states.butterflyEffect: The ban covered the 26 Schengen countries but pointedly excluded the UK and Ireland, a gap later criticized as incoherent. Its announcement triggered chaotic rushes at US airports as travelers scrambled home before the 13 March deadline, and markets fell further as the scale of the crisis became clear.
