evt-03-13-1567-battle-of-oosterweel.scenario: It's 13 March 1567, and you march with several hundred Calvinist rebels near the village of Oosterweel outside Antwerp, expecting reinforcements from sympathizers within the city as a Spanish mercenary force closes in.
evt-03-13-1567-battle-of-oosterweel.prompt: What happens when the Spanish force under Filips van Lannoy attacks the rebel camp?

choices.text: The rebels retreat safely into Antwerp
The rebels are routed, with most killed or captured
The rebels win a decisive victory
Both sides agree to a truce

evt-03-13-1567-battle-of-oosterweel.butterflyEffect: The rebels were caught by surprise and almost entirely killed or captured. The crushing defeat ended the early wave of Calvinist unrest and is traditionally seen as the opening clash of the Eighty Years' War, hardening Habsburg resolve that led to the Duke of Alba's harsh repression in the years that followed.

evt-03-13-1697-nojpeten.scenario: It is 13 March 1697. You serve under Martín de Ursúa, commander of a Spanish force facing the fortified island capital of the last independent Maya kingdom across Lake Petén Itzá.
evt-03-13-1697-nojpeten.prompt: How does the Spanish force finally break the Itza defenses?

choices.text: A naval assault using an armed galley (galeota) across the lake
Missionaries negotiating a peaceful surrender
Bribing rival Maya chiefs to open the gates
A prolonged land siege cutting off food supplies

evt-03-13-1697-nojpeten.butterflyEffect: Ursúa's forces stormed the island by boat and overwhelmed the Itza warriors, capturing Nojpetén and forcing King Kan Ek' to flee before his eventual capture. This ended the last independent Maya kingdom, completing the Spanish conquest of Yucatán nearly two centuries after Cortés first landed, and the island became the town of Flores.

evt-03-13-1741-war-of-jenkins-ear.scenario: It's March 1741, and you sail with Admiral Edward Vernon's massive fleet approaching the fortified Spanish port of Cartagena de Indias, tasked with seizing Spain's key stronghold in the Caribbean.
evt-03-13-1741-war-of-jenkins-ear.prompt: What ultimately happens to the British assault on Cartagena de Indias?

choices.text: Blas de Lezo's defenders repel the British with heavy losses
French forces intervene to save the Spanish port
The British capture the city with little resistance
The Spanish garrison surrenders without a fight

evt-03-13-1741-war-of-jenkins-ear.butterflyEffect: Admiral Blas de Lezo's outnumbered Spanish garrison repelled the huge British expedition, inflicting catastrophic losses from both combat and tropical disease. The failure crushed British hopes of seizing Spanish America and helped push the war toward stalemate ahead of the 1748 peace settlement.

evt-03-13-1781-william-herschel.scenario: It's the night of 13 March 1781, and you are peering through your homemade telescope in the garden of your house in Bath, tracking a faint object you first took for a star or comet.
evt-03-13-1781-william-herschel.prompt: What does careful observation over following nights reveal this object to be?

choices.text: An asteroid orbiting near Mars
A previously unknown planet
A newly appeared comet
A distant fixed star

evt-03-13-1781-william-herschel.butterflyEffect: Herschel had discovered Uranus, the first planet found using a telescope, doubling the known size of the solar system overnight. The discovery made Herschel famous, won him royal patronage as astronomer to King George III, and opened a new era of systematic sky surveys.

evt-03-13-1811-napoleonic-wars.scenario: Dawn, 13 March 1811, off the island of Lissa in the Adriatic. You serve aboard HMS Amphion under Captain William Hoste, whose three frigates face a Franco-Venetian squadron nearly twice their number.
evt-03-13-1811-napoleonic-wars.prompt: What signal does Hoste hoist to steady his outnumbered crews before battle?

choices.text: "Remember Nelson"
"Steady, lads, steady"
"Don't give up the ship"
"England expects every man to do his duty"

evt-03-13-1811-napoleonic-wars.butterflyEffect: Hoste's signal "Remember Nelson" inspired his ships to a decisive victory, killing the French commander Dubourdieu and scattering his squadron. The win secured British control of the Adriatic for the rest of the war, protecting trade and denying Napoleon a base to threaten British shipping.

evt-03-13-1845-felix-mendelssohn.scenario: It is 13 March 1845 at the Leipzig Gewandhaus. Felix Mendelssohn is too ill to attend the premiere of his own Violin Concerto, and the orchestra still needs someone to lead it.
evt-03-13-1845-felix-mendelssohn.prompt: Who steps in to conduct the premiere in Mendelssohn's place?

choices.text: Robert Schumann
Franz Liszt
Niels Gade
Ignaz Moscheles

evt-03-13-1845-felix-mendelssohn.butterflyEffect: Danish composer Niels Gade conducted while violinist Ferdinand David, who had advised Mendelssohn on the solo part for years, played the demanding solo line. The concerto went on to become one of the most performed violin concertos in the repertoire, and David's fingerings and bowings still shape how soloists play it today.

evt-03-13-1848-klemens-von-metternich.scenario: March 1848, Vienna. Crowds of students and workers fill the streets demanding reform, and as Chancellor Metternich's decades-long grip on Austrian politics finally gives way, the emperor's court must decide his fate.
evt-03-13-1848-klemens-von-metternich.prompt: What does Metternich do as the revolutionary crowds demand his removal?

choices.text: He negotiates a constitution and remains in office
He resigns but retires quietly to his Austrian estate
He orders the army to crush the protests immediately
He resigns and flees into exile abroad

evt-03-13-1848-klemens-von-metternich.butterflyEffect: Metternich resigned and fled into exile, eventually reaching London before settling in Brussels. His fall shattered the conservative order he had built across Europe since 1815, emboldening revolutionaries from Berlin to Budapest in the wave of 1848 uprisings.

evt-03-13-1920-kapp-putsch.scenario: It's 13 March 1920, and Freikorps units under Walther von Lüttwitz have just marched into Berlin, installing Wolfgang Kapp as chancellor while the legitimate government flees. As a Berlin trade unionist, you must decide how to resist.
evt-03-13-1920-kapp-putsch.prompt: What action by workers brings down the putsch within days?

choices.text: Negotiations granting Kapp a coalition government
An armed uprising storming the chancellery
Passive acceptance of the new regime
A nationwide general strike by workers and civil servants

evt-03-13-1920-kapp-putsch.butterflyEffect: A general strike by German workers paralyzed the country, and the putsch collapsed after just four days. Yet the crushing of a related workers' uprising in the Ruhr that followed showed how fragile the Weimar Republic remained, radicalizing both left and right ahead of later political crises.

evt-03-13-1943-the-holocaust.scenario: It is 13 March 1943 in the Kraków Ghetto. SS officers order everyone to an assembly point as the final liquidation begins, dividing the crowd into two lines.
evt-03-13-1943-the-holocaust.prompt: What determines which line — and which fate — a person is assigned to?

choices.text: The size of their family
Their neighborhood of residence within the ghetto
A random lottery drawn by the guards
Whether they were deemed capable of forced labor

evt-03-13-1943-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: Those judged fit for labor were marched to the nearby Płaszów forced-labor camp, while most others were deported to Auschwitz-Birkenau or killed on the spot; some, aided by Oskar Schindler, would later be transferred to his factory. The liquidation became one of the most documented ghetto clearances of the Holocaust, later portrayed in Schindler's List.

evt-03-13-1964-murder-of-kitty-genovese.scenario: It is past 3 a.m. on 13 March 1964 in Kew Gardens, Queens. You wake to screams from the street below as a woman is attacked outside her apartment building, and you go to your window to look.
evt-03-13-1964-murder-of-kitty-genovese.prompt: What is the responsible thing to do right now?

choices.text: Assume with so many windows lit, someone else has already called
Close the window and go back to sleep, since it's not your business
Go outside alone to confront the attacker
Call the police immediately and report what you're hearing

evt-03-13-1964-murder-of-kitty-genovese.butterflyEffect: Some neighbors did hear Kitty Genovese's cries, but few grasped the attack's severity, and no one intervened in time. A later New York Times story exaggerated the number of indifferent witnesses to 37, but the case still launched decades of psychological research into the 'bystander effect,' reshaping how emergency response and 911 systems were designed.

evt-03-13-1988-seikan-tunnel.scenario: You are a railway engineer riding in the first train to pass beneath the Tsugaru Strait, deep under the seabed connecting Honshu and Hokkaido, after decades of planning and construction.
evt-03-13-1988-seikan-tunnel.prompt: What historic milestone does this crossing mark for the world's railways?

choices.text: It becomes the first tunnel built with a bored service shaft
It becomes the world's longest railway tunnel
It becomes the deepest transportation tunnel on Earth
It becomes the fastest transit line in Japan

evt-03-13-1988-seikan-tunnel.butterflyEffect: The Seikan Tunnel became the world's longest railway tunnel, a title it held for 28 years until Switzerland's Gotthard Base Tunnel opened in 2016. It also gave Japan its first reliable, weather-proof link between the main islands, ending dependence on ferries that had long been vulnerable to storms.

evt-03-13-2012-sierre-coach-crash.scenario: You are a school administrator in Belgium awaiting the return of two coaches carrying children home from a ski trip in Switzerland, when word arrives that one of the buses has struck a wall inside the Sierre Tunnel.
evt-03-13-2012-sierre-coach-crash.prompt: How do the Belgian authorities respond in the days that follow?

choices.text: Revoke the coach company's operating licence within days
Permanently ban school ski trips abroad
Declare a national day of mourning
Lower the national highway speed limit

evt-03-13-2012-sierre-coach-crash.butterflyEffect: Belgium declared a national day of mourning, with King Albert II and Queen Paola attending memorial services for the victims. Investigators were never able to establish a definitive cause for the crash, and the tragedy fuelled a wider European debate about seatbelt use and safety standards on coaches carrying schoolchildren.

evt-03-13-2013-2013-conclave.scenario: You are a cardinal elector sealed inside the Sistine Chapel on 13 March 2013, black smoke already having drifted from earlier votes. The fifth ballot is being tallied and one name is pulling ahead of the rest.
evt-03-13-2013-2013-conclave.prompt: Which cardinal do the electors choose as the new pope?

choices.text: Jorge Mario Bergoglio of Buenos Aires
Odilo Scherer of São Paulo
Marc Ouellet of Quebec
Angelo Scola of Milan

evt-03-13-2013-2013-conclave.butterflyEffect: The conclave elected Jorge Mario Bergoglio, who took the name Francis, becoming the first pope from the Americas and the first Jesuit pope. His papacy pushed reform of the Vatican bureaucracy, emphasized care for the poor and the environment (Laudato Si'), and reshaped global Catholic priorities for over a decade.

evt-03-13-2015-2015-belgrade-helicopter-.scenario: You are the pilot of a Serbian Army Mi-17, carrying a critically ill five-day-old infant to Belgrade after a landslide blocked the ambulance route from Novi Pazar. Storm clouds close in as you approach Nikola Tesla Airport, and your first landing attempt is aborted.
evt-03-13-2015-2015-belgrade-helicopter-.prompt: With fuel running low and weather worsening, what does the crew do next?

choices.text: Enter a holding pattern and wait for the storm to pass
Divert immediately to an alternate airport further away
Request a ground ambulance meet the helicopter mid-route
Attempt a second landing at Nikola Tesla Airport

evt-03-13-2015-2015-belgrade-helicopter-.butterflyEffect: The crew attempted a second landing, but the helicopter crashed short of the runway, killing all seven aboard, including the infant, two medics and four crew. The disaster prompted scrutiny in Serbia of emergency medevac protocols in poor weather and renewed calls to improve ground transport links to isolated regions like Novi Pazar.

evt-03-13-2016-march-2016-ankara-bombing.scenario: It is the evening of 13 March 2016, and a car bomb has just torn through a crowded transit hub in central Ankara. As a Turkish security official, you must determine who is responsible and how the state should respond.
evt-03-13-2016-march-2016-ankara-bombing.prompt: Which group did investigators conclude was behind the bombing?

choices.text: The Revolutionary People's Liberation Party (DHKP-C)
The Kurdistan Freedom Hawks (TAK)
The PKK's central leadership directly
The Islamic State (ISIS)

evt-03-13-2016-march-2016-ankara-bombing.butterflyEffect: The attack was attributed to the Kurdistan Freedom Hawks (TAK), an offshoot of the PKK. Turkish authorities intensified military operations against Kurdish militants in the southeast, further hardening the collapse of the earlier PKK peace process and deepening years of renewed conflict.

evt-03-13-2016-grand-bassam-shootings.scenario: You are staying at a beachfront hotel in Grand-Bassam, Ivory Coast, when gunfire erupts along the shore and Ivorian security forces rush to confront the attackers.
evt-03-13-2016-grand-bassam-shootings.prompt: Which group claimed responsibility for the Grand-Bassam attack in the days that followed?

choices.text: Islamic State West Africa Province
Boko Haram
Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM)
Al-Shabaab

evt-03-13-2016-grand-bassam-shootings.butterflyEffect: Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM) claimed the assault, part of a wider jihadist push from the Sahel toward West Africa's coast after earlier attacks in Bamako and Ouagadougou. The attack pushed Ivorian and regional governments to expand counterterrorism cooperation and tourist-site security.

evt-03-13-2020-donald-trump.scenario: It's the afternoon of March 13, 2020. You're a reporter in the White House Rose Garden as President Trump steps to the podium to address the escalating coronavirus outbreak.
evt-03-13-2020-donald-trump.prompt: What did Trump's national emergency declaration actually unlock?

choices.text: A federal mandate requiring masks in all public spaces
Federal disaster relief funds and emergency powers under the Stafford Act
Closure of all US borders to every foreign traveler
An immediate nationwide stay-at-home lockdown order

evt-03-13-2020-donald-trump.butterflyEffect: Invoking the Stafford Act freed up roughly $50 billion in federal disaster relief and gave agencies emergency powers to expand testing and hospital capacity. State-by-state lockdowns, travel bans, and stimulus packages followed within weeks as the pandemic reshaped American life for years.

evt-03-13-2020-katerina-sakellaropoulou.scenario: You are a member of the Hellenic Parliament attending the swearing-in ceremony inside the chamber, as new health precautions are enforced against a spreading virus across Europe.
evt-03-13-2020-katerina-sakellaropoulou.prompt: What historic first does today's ceremony mark for Greece?

choices.text: The first president to be directly elected by public vote
The first president to serve two consecutive terms
The first president born outside Greece
The country's first female president

evt-03-13-2020-katerina-sakellaropoulou.butterflyEffect: Katerina Sakellaropoulou became Greece's first female president, succeeding Prokopis Pavlopoulos. Her presidency, running from 2020 to 2025, coincided almost immediately with the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in Greece, shaping much of her early time in office.

evt-03-14-1489-catherine-cornaro.scenario: It is February 1489 in Nicosia. Venetian officials stand before you, their queen, insisting that for the good of the republic you must give up your throne and sail away from the island you have ruled for fifteen years.
evt-03-14-1489-catherine-cornaro.prompt: What does Catherine Cornaro do when pressed to abdicate?

choices.text: She abdicates and sails to Venice, later ruling a small court at Asolo
She flees to the Ottoman court for protection
She remarries a Genoese lord to keep her throne
She refuses and rallies Cypriot nobles to resist Venice

evt-03-14-1489-catherine-cornaro.butterflyEffect: Catherine Cornaro abdicated on 26 February 1489, sailed to Venice, and was granted the town of Asolo as a consolation fief where she held a celebrated small court. Cyprus passed directly under Venetian rule, remaining so until the Ottomans conquered the island in 1570–71.

evt-03-14-1593-imjin-war.scenario: You stand with General Gwon Yul inside the earthen walls of Haengju fortress. Roughly 3,000 Korean defenders face a Japanese force many times their size, and your stockpile of arrows and gunpowder is running low.
evt-03-14-1593-imjin-war.prompt: How do the defenders hold the fortress against repeated Japanese assaults?

choices.text: Massed hwacha rocket-fire and stones hurled by every able hand, including women
Tunnelling gunpowder mines beneath the enemy camp
A cavalry charge that broke the Japanese siege lines
A surprise naval bombardment from turtle ships offshore

evt-03-14-1593-imjin-war.butterflyEffect: The defenders repelled wave after wave of attacks using hwacha rocket-launchers, stones, and even boiling water, with local women reportedly ferrying stones in their aprons to keep the defense supplied. The victory at Haengju became one of the three great Korean triumphs of the war and boosted morale as Ming and Korean pressure eventually forced a Japanese withdrawal from much of the peninsula.

evt-03-14-1757-royal-navy.scenario: It's 14 March 1757 aboard HMS Monarch at Portsmouth. You are Admiral John Byng, condemned by court-martial for failing to 'do his utmost' to relieve the besieged British garrison at Minorca the previous year.
evt-03-14-1757-royal-navy.prompt: What is Byng's fate as the sentence is carried out?

choices.text: He is merely stripped of rank and discharged
He is exiled to the American colonies
He is executed by firing squad on his own ship
He is pardoned by King George II at the last moment

evt-03-14-1757-royal-navy.butterflyEffect: Byng was shot by firing squad on his own quarterdeck, despite widespread sympathy for his defense. His death became a byword for harsh military justice, mocked by Voltaire in Candide, and it hardened an unforgiving Royal Navy culture in which any commander who hesitated to engage the enemy risked execution.

evt-03-14-1864-petite-messe-solennelle.scenario: It is 14 March 1864 in Paris. Gioachino Rossini, long retired from opera, has invited a small private audience to hear a sacred work he calls one of his 'sins of old age,' scored for a handful of singers and modest accompaniment.
evt-03-14-1864-petite-messe-solennelle.prompt: What instrumentation does Rossini use for this first, intimate performance?

choices.text: Twelve voices with two pianos and harmonium
A string quartet with no keyboard
Solo organ accompanying a quartet
Full orchestra and large choir

evt-03-14-1864-petite-messe-solennelle.butterflyEffect: Rossini originally scored the Petite messe solennelle for twelve singers, two pianos, and harmonium, deliberately avoiding orchestra for its private premiere. He later orchestrated a fuller version fearing others would do it after his death; that version premiered posthumously in 1869 and the work entered the standard choral repertoire.

evt-03-14-1945-royal-air-force.scenario: It's 14 March 1945. You are a Lancaster pilot with No. 617 Squadron, tasked with testing a massive new 22,000 lb bomb against the Bielefeld railway viaduct in Germany.
evt-03-14-1945-royal-air-force.prompt: What is this new 'earthquake bomb' designed to do to the target?

choices.text: Disperse chemical agents to disable the garrison nearby
Detonate on impact to demolish the viaduct's surface directly
Release incendiary submunitions across the rail yard
Burrow underground before exploding, collapsing the structure through shockwave

evt-03-14-1945-royal-air-force.butterflyEffect: The Grand Slam's ground shock brought down a section of the viaduct without needing a direct hit, proving the earthquake-bomb concept in combat. It became the RAF's most powerful conventional weapon of the war, later used against hardened U-boat pens and bridges, and its design philosophy influenced postwar bunker-busting munitions.

evt-03-14-1972-giangiacomo-feltrinelli.scenario: It is 14 March 1972 near a high-voltage pylon outside Segrate, Italy. Giangiacomo Feltrinelli, the publisher who brought Doctor Zhivago and The Leopard to the world, is found dead beside a partially assembled explosive device.
evt-03-14-1972-giangiacomo-feltrinelli.prompt: What did investigators conclude had happened to Feltrinelli?

choices.text: He suffered a fatal heart attack while hiking
He died in an ordinary car accident nearby
He was assassinated by neofascist gunmen
He died while apparently planting a bomb at the pylon

evt-03-14-1972-giangiacomo-feltrinelli.butterflyEffect: Authorities concluded Feltrinelli died while attempting to plant a bomb intended to sabotage the pylon, an act tied to his radical leftist sympathies during Italy's turbulent Years of Lead, though doubts and conspiracy theories about his death persist. His publishing house continued under family control, but his death became a symbol of the era's political violence.

evt-03-14-1973-vietnam-war.scenario: It is March 1973 at Gia Lam Airport, Hanoi. After five and a half years as a prisoner of war, your name is finally called for release under the terms of the Paris Peace Accords.
evt-03-14-1973-vietnam-war.prompt: What happens next as you board the aircraft home?

choices.text: Flown directly to Andrews Air Force Base with no stops
Held in Hanoi for further negotiations before release
Transferred to Soviet custody as part of a wider prisoner exchange
Flown to Clark Air Base in the Philippines for medical checks before going home

evt-03-14-1973-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: Under Operation Homecoming, released POWs were flown first to Clark Air Base in the Philippines for medical evaluation and debriefing before returning to the United States. Their emotional reunions became a defining media moment of the war's end, though many struggled for years afterward with the psychological toll of captivity.

evt-03-14-1979-alia-royal-jordanian-flig.scenario: It's the night of 13 March 1979 at Doha International Airport. You are aboard Alia Royal Jordanian Flight 600, executing a missed approach on Runway 34 when a sudden downburst strikes the aircraft.
evt-03-14-1979-alia-royal-jordanian-flig.prompt: What happens to the Boeing 727 as it struggles through the downburst?

choices.text: It climbs safely away and diverts to an alternate airport
It lands successfully on a second approach attempt
It aborts the approach entirely and returns to Amman
It crashes onto the runway, flips over, and slides into a fire station

evt-03-14-1979-alia-royal-jordanian-flig.butterflyEffect: The aircraft crashed onto the runway, flipped, and slid tail-first into a fire station, killing 45 of those aboard, though 19 survived. It remains Qatar's deadliest aviation accident and added to growing evidence of the dangers of downbursts during missed approaches, spurring later adoption of windshear detection systems.

evt-03-14-1988-johnson-south-reef-skirmi.scenario: It is 14 March 1988 near Johnson South Reef in the Spratly Islands. You command a Vietnamese naval detachment trying to plant a flag on the reef, but Chinese warships have moved to block you and tensions are rising fast.
evt-03-14-1988-johnson-south-reef-skirmi.prompt: What happens next in this standoff over the disputed reef?

choices.text: The United Nations intervenes and the reef is declared neutral territory
Chinese ships open fire, sinking Vietnamese vessels in a lopsided battle
Vietnamese forces successfully repel the Chinese ships and hold the reef
Both sides withdraw peacefully after a tense diplomatic exchange

evt-03-14-1988-johnson-south-reef-skirmi.butterflyEffect: Chinese forces opened fire, sinking several Vietnamese vessels and killing dozens of sailors in a decisive one-sided battle. China secured control of Johnson South Reef, strengthening its foothold in the Spratlys and hardening the ongoing South China Sea territorial disputes that persist among China, Vietnam, and other claimants today.

evt-03-14-1995-norman-thagard.scenario: It is 14 March 1995 at the Baikonur Cosmodrome. You are an American astronaut strapped into a Soyuz capsule, about to become the first American ever launched into space on a Russian rocket.
evt-03-14-1995-norman-thagard.prompt: Which space station is this historic Russian-launched mission bound for?

choices.text: The International Space Station
Salyut 7
Skylab
Mir

evt-03-14-1995-norman-thagard.butterflyEffect: Thagard's Soyuz TM-21 flight carried him to Mir for the Mir-18 mission, a landmark of post-Cold War cooperation. The mission helped build the trust and technical groundwork that led to the Shuttle-Mir program and eventually the International Space Station partnership.

evt-03-14-2007-nandigram-violence.scenario: It is early 2007 in Nandigram, West Bengal. Government surveyors have marked your village land for a proposed chemical hub, and neighbors are organizing to block officials from entering.
evt-03-14-2007-nandigram-violence.prompt: What follows as the standoff between villagers and the state government escalates?

choices.text: Villagers receive immediate compensation and withdraw objections
The project proceeds peacefully after negotiation
Police open fire on the blockade, killing 14 protesters
The state government quietly cancels the hub without incident

evt-03-14-2007-nandigram-violence.butterflyEffect: On 14 March 2007, police opened fire on protesters blocking the land acquisition, killing 14 people and drawing national outrage. The backlash badly damaged the ruling Left Front's standing in West Bengal and the chemical hub project was ultimately abandoned, contributing to the Front's historic defeat in the 2011 state election.

evt-03-14-2008-2008-tibetan-unrest.scenario: It is 14 March 2008 in Lhasa. Protests that began among monks days earlier have spread into wider unrest across the city as the anniversary of the 1959 uprising approaches.
evt-03-14-2008-2008-tibetan-unrest.prompt: How does the Chinese government respond to the escalating unrest?

choices.text: Opens direct negotiations with the Dalai Lama's representatives
Holds a public referendum on Tibet's political status
Deploys security forces and imposes martial law to suppress the protests
Grants Tibet expanded autonomy to defuse tensions

evt-03-14-2008-2008-tibetan-unrest.butterflyEffect: Beijing imposed martial law, flooded Lhasa with security forces, and cut off media and internet access to the region. The crackdown drew international condemnation just months before the Beijing Olympics, sparking pro-Tibet protests along the Olympic torch relay route across several continents.

evt-03-14-2019-cyclone-idai.scenario: It's 14 March 2019 in Beira, Mozambique, and Cyclone Idai's eyewall is closing in with winds over 170 km/h as floodwaters rise around your neighborhood.
evt-03-14-2019-cyclone-idai.prompt: What is the safest action as the cyclone makes landfall?

choices.text: Seek higher ground and sturdy shelter immediately
Wait at home for official evacuation buses to arrive
Drive inland along the coastal highway during the storm
Stay in your home to guard it against looters

evt-03-14-2019-cyclone-idai.butterflyEffect: Idai's landfall triggered catastrophic flooding across Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Malawi, killing more than 1,500 people and becoming the deadliest cyclone ever recorded in the South-West Indian Ocean. The disaster drew a major UN humanitarian response and exposed the region's vulnerability to intensifying storms.

evt-03-14-2021-tatmadaw.scenario: It's 14 March 2021 in Yangon's Hlaing Thar Yar township. You are among crowds protesting the military's February coup as security forces move to crush the demonstration.
evt-03-14-2021-tatmadaw.prompt: How does the junta escalate its response in the township that day?

choices.text: Opens negotiations with protest leaders on the spot
Imposes only a curfew without further violence
Withdraws troops from the area after early casualties
Declares martial law in the township and continues using lethal force

evt-03-14-2021-tatmadaw.butterflyEffect: The military declared martial law over Hlaing Thar Yar and continued using lethal force, killing at least 65 civilians in one of the deadliest single days since the coup. The massacre hardened resistance, pushing many urban protesters toward armed struggle and swelling the ranks of newly formed People's Defence Forces.

evt-03-15-bce44-assassination-of-julius-.scenario: It is the Ides of March, 44 BC. You are a senator inside the Curia of Pompey, and Julius Caesar has just entered for the Senate session, surrounded by men you know are conspirators against him.
evt-03-15-bce44-assassination-of-julius-.prompt: What happens to Caesar in the chamber that day?

choices.text: The senators surround Caesar and stab him to death
Caesar's bodyguards cut down the conspirators before they can strike
Caesar is arrested and exiled rather than killed
The plot is exposed beforehand and the session is cancelled

evt-03-15-bce44-assassination-of-julius-.butterflyEffect: The conspirators, led by Brutus and Cassius, stabbed Caesar roughly 23 times, killing him on the Senate floor. Rather than restoring the Republic, the murder triggered the Liberators' civil war and ultimately cleared the path for Caesar's heir Octavian to become Rome's first emperor, ending the Republic for good.

evt-03-15-856-michael-iii.scenario: You are a courtier in Constantinople in March 856. The teenage emperor Michael III chafes under the regency his mother Theodora still holds, and confides his plan to end it.
evt-03-15-856-michael-iii.prompt: What does Michael III do to seize real power?

choices.text: Ally with Theodora against his own advisors
Have Theodora quietly assassinated
Overthrow the regency and send Theodora into a convent
Abdicate the throne in Theodora's favor

evt-03-15-856-michael-iii.butterflyEffect: Michael overthrew Theodora's regency and began his sole reign, a period modern historians credit with reviving Byzantine strength. He was assassinated in 867 by his co-emperor Basil I, who founded the Macedonian dynasty.

evt-03-15-1147-reconquista.scenario: It is before dawn on 15 March 1147. You are among King Afonso I's Portuguese soldiers scaling the walls of the Moorish-held town of Santarém under cover of darkness.
evt-03-15-1147-reconquista.prompt: What tactic secures the town for the Portuguese crown?

choices.text: Portuguese forces bribe the garrison commander to open the gates
A surprise night assault with scaling ladders catches the garrison off guard
A naval bombardment from the Tagus River breaches the walls
A prolonged siege starves the defenders into surrender

evt-03-15-1147-reconquista.butterflyEffect: The surprise capture of Santarém gave Afonso I a crucial forward base and momentum that carried into the successful siege of Lisbon later that same year, aided by passing crusaders. Together these victories marked major turning points in establishing the independent Kingdom of Portugal.

evt-03-15-1311-battle-of-halmyros.scenario: It is 15 March 1311 near the Cephissus river in Greece. You serve Duke Walter of Brienne, whose feudal army of knights faces the battle-hardened mercenaries of the Catalan Company on marshy ground.
evt-03-15-1311-battle-of-halmyros.prompt: What happens as the Frankish knights charge into the wetland?

choices.text: Both sides withdraw after an inconclusive skirmish
The knights outflank the mercenaries and rout them decisively
Walter negotiates a truce before battle is joined
Their heavy cavalry bogs down and the Catalans cut them apart, killing Walter

evt-03-15-1311-battle-of-halmyros.butterflyEffect: Walter of Brienne died on the field along with much of the Frankish nobility of the Duchy of Athens, and the victorious Catalan Company simply took the duchy for themselves. Catalan rule endured in central Greece for decades, an unusual episode of mercenary conquest in the crusader states.

evt-03-15-1783-george-washington.scenario: It is 15 March 1783 in Newburgh, New York. You are an officer of the Continental Army, unpaid for months, gathered with fellow officers debating whether to defy Congress by force. General Washington rises to speak.
evt-03-15-1783-george-washington.prompt: What does Washington do that turns the officers back from mutiny?

choices.text: He promises to march the army on Philadelphia to force payment
He orders the ringleaders arrested on the spot
He reads a letter from Congress and fumbles for his reading glasses, moving the room to tears
He resigns his commission and departs the hall

evt-03-15-1783-george-washington.butterflyEffect: Washington's halting search for his spectacles and quiet remark that he had 'grown gray... in service to my country' broke the officers' anger and ended what became known as the Newburgh Conspiracy. His voluntary submission of military power to civilian Congress set an enduring precedent for civilian control of the military in the new republic.

evt-03-15-1916-pancho-villa.scenario: It is March 15, 1916, six days after Pancho Villa's raiders killed Americans in Columbus, New Mexico. You advise President Wilson on how to respond to the cross-border attack.
evt-03-15-1916-pancho-villa.prompt: What do you recommend the U.S. do?

choices.text: Appeal to European powers to mediate the dispute
Order a punitive military expedition into Mexico to capture Villa
Formally declare war on Mexico
Treat it as an internal Mexican matter and take no action

evt-03-15-1916-pancho-villa.butterflyEffect: Wilson sent General Pershing's Punitive Expedition into Mexico to hunt Villa. It never caught him, but the campaign tested new tools—trucks, aircraft, radios—that the U.S. Army carried into World War I the following year.

evt-03-15-1918-finnish-civil-war.scenario: It is 15 March 1918 outside Tampere. You serve under General Mannerheim as the White Guards begin their assault on this key industrial city held by the Red Guards.
evt-03-15-1918-finnish-civil-war.prompt: What follows as the battle for Tampere unfolds?

choices.text: The Whites take the city after fierce street-by-street fighting
Russian Bolshevik troops intervene directly to save the Reds
Both sides agree to a ceasefire before major fighting starts
The Reds hold the city and force a White retreat

evt-03-15-1918-finnish-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Whites captured Tampere after brutal urban fighting, breaking the back of Red resistance in western Finland. The victory, aided by German-trained Jäger officers, paved the way for the broader White triumph in the civil war and cemented Mannerheim's role in shaping independent Finland's future.

evt-03-15-1931-sing-song-girl-red-peony.scenario: It is 1931 at the Mingxing studio in Shanghai. You are directing China's first sound film, and your actors keep fumbling dialogue while the primitive recording equipment struggles to keep up.
evt-03-15-1931-sing-song-girl-red-peony.prompt: How do you push the production through its technical troubles?

choices.text: Bring in American engineers to run the whole production
Shelve the project indefinitely until better equipment arrives
Abandon sound and release the film silent instead
Hire language coaches and spend months refining the sound technique

evt-03-15-1931-sing-song-girl-red-peony.butterflyEffect: After six months of painstaking work with language coaches and crew, the film became a popular hit, proving talkies were commercially viable in China and accelerating the industry's shift to sound. The original print is now considered lost.

evt-03-15-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is March 1943. Field Marshal von Manstein's counteroffensive after Stalingrad is closing in on Kharkov, and you command a German panzer spearhead fighting street by street.
evt-03-15-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What armor spearheads the final push to retake the city?

choices.text: Horse-mounted cavalry regiments
Obsolete Panzer I light tanks
Captured Soviet T-34 tanks
Newly arrived Tiger tanks with elite SS panzer divisions

evt-03-15-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The Third Battle of Kharkov became the last major German victory on the Eastern Front, stabilizing the line after the Stalingrad disaster. It set the stage for the massive Battle of Kursk that summer, after which German initiative in the east never recovered.

evt-03-15-1943-the-holocaust-in-greece.scenario: It is 15 March 1943 in Thessaloniki. You are a member of the city's ancient Sephardic Jewish community as German occupation authorities order families to assemble with only what they can carry.
evt-03-15-1943-the-holocaust-in-greece.prompt: What pretext do the Nazi authorities give the community for the roundup?

choices.text: They offer transit to neutral Turkey for a fee
They announce a temporary curfew with no mention of travel
They state the community will be relocated within the city
They claim the deportees are being resettled to work in Poland

evt-03-15-1943-the-holocaust-in-greece.butterflyEffect: Told they were being resettled for labor, the Jews of Thessaloniki were instead sent by rail to Auschwitz, where the vast majority were murdered. The deportations destroyed one of the oldest and largest Sephardic communities in Europe, ending nearly five centuries of Jewish life in the city.

evt-03-15-1951-nationalization-of-the-ir.scenario: It is 15 March 1951. You sit in Iran's Majlis, about to cast your vote on a bill to seize control of the country's oil industry from Britain's Anglo-Iranian Oil Company.
evt-03-15-1951-nationalization-of-the-ir.prompt: What does the legislation you are voting on actually do?

choices.text: Nationalize the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company and form the National Iranian Oil Company
Sell Iran's oil rights outright to American firms
Nationalize only the refineries while leaving extraction to AIOC
Grant AIOC a fresh 50-year concession

evt-03-15-1951-nationalization-of-the-ir.butterflyEffect: The vote nationalized AIOC and created the National Iranian Oil Company, propelling Mosaddegh to prime minister. The move triggered a Western oil boycott and, in 1953, a CIA- and MI6-backed coup that toppled him, cementing the Shah's autocratic rule for decades.

evt-03-15-2019-2019-2020-hong-kong-prote.scenario: It is mid-March 2019 in Hong Kong. You join growing crowds opposing a new extradition bill that would allow suspects to be sent to mainland China for trial.
evt-03-15-2019-2019-2020-hong-kong-prote.prompt: What broader demand do the protests soon grow to include?

choices.text: Immediate independence from China
Abolition of the Hong Kong police force entirely
Reinstatement of British colonial administration
Full withdrawal of the bill and greater democratic accountability for the government

evt-03-15-2019-2019-2020-hong-kong-prote.butterflyEffect: The extradition bill was eventually withdrawn, but the protests had already expanded into the largest and most sustained pro-democracy movement in Hong Kong's history, lasting into 2020. Beijing's response came in mid-2020 with a sweeping National Security Law that curtailed the freedoms the protesters had sought to protect.

evt-03-15-2022-2022-sri-lankan-protests.scenario: It is March 2022. Fuel queues stretch for miles, blackouts darken Colombo, and you join the crowds gathering at Galle Face Green as Sri Lanka's economy collapses.
evt-03-15-2022-2022-sri-lankan-protests.prompt: What is the protest's central demand?

choices.text: Fresh parliamentary elections only
The release of unrelated political prisoners
The resignation of Gotabaya Rajapaksa and the Rajapaksa family from power
An immediate IMF bailout with no political demands

evt-03-15-2022-2022-sri-lankan-protests.butterflyEffect: The Aragalaya's pressure eventually forced President Gotabaya Rajapaksa to flee the country and resign in July 2022, the first time street protest alone had ousted a sitting Sri Lankan leader. The economic crisis, however, persisted under his successor.

evt-03-16-bce597-590s-bc.scenario: It is 597 BC, and you are an adviser to young King Jehoiachin as Nebuchadnezzar II's Babylonian army surrounds Jerusalem's walls, punishing Judah for rebelling against Babylonian rule.
evt-03-16-bce597-590s-bc.prompt: What choice ends the siege of Jerusalem?

choices.text: Ally openly with Egypt against Babylon
Fight to the last man rather than surrender
Surrender and accept exile of the king and nobles
Flee to Egypt and seek Pharaoh's protection

evt-03-16-bce597-590s-bc.butterflyEffect: Jehoiachin surrendered, and Nebuchadnezzar deported him along with much of Judah's elite and treasure to Babylon in the first great exile. The king then installed Jehoiachin's uncle Zedekiah as a puppet ruler, whose later revolt would bring Nebuchadnezzar back to destroy Jerusalem entirely within the decade.

evt-03-16-1190-york-castle.scenario: It is 16 March 1190. A mob inflamed by crusading fervour and unpaid debts has driven York's Jewish community into the wooden keep of the castle, and the siege will end in mass death by nightfall.
evt-03-16-1190-york-castle.prompt: What does the Crown do afterward to safeguard its financial interests in the Jewish community?

choices.text: It establishes a registry system recording Jewish debts to protect royal revenue
It publicly executes the ringleaders within the week
It immediately expels all Jews from England
It grants York exemption from royal taxation as compensation

evt-03-16-1190-york-castle.butterflyEffect: Rioters had destroyed the bonds recording debts owed to Jewish moneylenders, so the government created a national system of duplicate chirograph archives to record Jewish loans, held partly by the crown. This bureaucratic innovation (the Exchequer of the Jews) tightened royal control over Jewish moneylending, fuelling resentment that culminated a century later in Edward I's 1290 Edict of Expulsion.

evt-03-16-1322-despenser-war.scenario: It is 16 March 1322 near Boroughbridge in Yorkshire. You lead rebel forces loyal to Thomas, Earl of Lancaster, but a royalist army under Andrew Harclay now blocks the bridge ahead.
evt-03-16-1322-despenser-war.prompt: What happens when your force tries to force the crossing?

choices.text: You break through and rout the royalist army
Both armies withdraw without engaging
You negotiate a truce and withdraw unharmed
Your force is routed and you are captured, later executed for treason

evt-03-16-1322-despenser-war.butterflyEffect: The rebel army was routed at Boroughbridge, and Lancaster was captured and executed for treason days later. Edward II's victory ushered in a period of harsh, vindictive rule under the Despensers that alienated the nobility and helped trigger the 1326 invasion by Isabella and Mortimer that ended his reign.

evt-03-16-1621-samoset.scenario: It is March 16, 1621, and you are a Pilgrim standing watch at Plymouth. A lone Native man strides into the settlement and calls out in plain English, "Welcome, Englishmen."
evt-03-16-1621-samoset.prompt: How do you respond to this unexpected greeting?

choices.text: Treat him as a threat and reach for weapons
Order him to leave the settlement at once
Offer him food and drink and hear him out
Flee into the woods to avoid contact

evt-03-16-1621-samoset.butterflyEffect: Samoset, an Abenaki sagamore who had learned English from fishermen, stayed the night, ate with the colonists, and returned days later with Squanto, who spoke even better English. Their introductions led directly to Plymouth's peace treaty with Massasoit and the Wampanoag, the alliance that let the fragile colony survive its first year.

evt-03-16-1660-long-parliament.scenario: You are a member of the Long Parliament on 16 March 1660, sitting in a chamber that has endured coups, purges, and civil war for nearly twenty years, about to vote on dissolving itself at last.
evt-03-16-1660-long-parliament.prompt: What happens once the Long Parliament finally dissolves itself?

choices.text: Power passes directly to Richard Cromwell as Lord Protector
England is formally declared a permanent republic
New elections produce a Convention Parliament that invites Charles II to return
No new Parliament convenes for the next decade

evt-03-16-1660-long-parliament.butterflyEffect: New elections produced the Convention Parliament, which negotiated terms for the monarchy's return. In May 1660 Charles II landed in England, ending the eleven-year Commonwealth and Interregnum and restoring the crown.

evt-03-16-1689-royal-welch-fusiliers.scenario: It is March 1689, days after William III has secured the English throne. You are helping raise a new regiment in North Wales meant to defend the new Protestant regime against forces still loyal to the deposed James II.
evt-03-16-1689-royal-welch-fusiliers.prompt: What is this newly raised regiment primarily sent to fight?

choices.text: Jacobite forces in Ireland
Louis XIV's army in Flanders
Covenanter rebels in Scotland
Barbary pirates in the Mediterranean

evt-03-16-1689-royal-welch-fusiliers.butterflyEffect: The regiment, raised by Lord Herbert of Cherbury, was sent to fight in the Williamite War in Ireland against Jacobite forces. It went on to serve in nearly every major British conflict for the next three centuries, later gaining literary fame when war poets Siegfried Sassoon and Robert Graves served in its ranks during the First World War.

evt-03-16-1802-united-states-congress.scenario: You are a congressman in 1802 debating how to shrink the young republic's costly standing army while still preparing officers for future wars.
evt-03-16-1802-united-states-congress.prompt: What lasting institution does the Military Peace Establishment Act create alongside the troop cuts?

choices.text: The United States Military Academy at West Point
The Army War College for senior officers
The National Guard as a reserve militia force
The United States Naval Academy at Annapolis

evt-03-16-1802-united-states-congress.butterflyEffect: The act founded the United States Military Academy at West Point, the nation's first engineering school and its primary source of trained officers. Generations of American military leaders, including many opposing generals in the Civil War, would be shaped by its curriculum.

evt-03-16-1872-1872-fa-cup-final.scenario: It is 16 March 1872 at Kennington Oval, and you are packed into the crowd watching the very first FA Cup final between Wanderers and Royal Engineers.
evt-03-16-1872-1872-fa-cup-final.prompt: What is the final score of this inaugural showpiece?

choices.text: Wanderers win 3-0
Wanderers win 1-0
Royal Engineers win 2-1
The match ends 0-0

evt-03-16-1872-1872-fa-cup-final.butterflyEffect: Wanderers won 1-0, with the only goal credited to Morton Betts. The match launched the FA Cup as the oldest football competition in the world, a tradition that still shapes English club football and the global cup format today.

evt-03-16-1935-conscription.scenario: It is 16 March 1935 in Berlin. Adolf Hitler has just announced he is reintroducing military conscription and rebuilding the German army to 36 divisions, openly tearing up the Treaty of Versailles.
evt-03-16-1935-conscription.prompt: How do Britain and France respond to this open violation?

choices.text: They immediately invade the Rhineland to enforce the treaty
They issue formal diplomatic protests but take no concrete action
They impose a joint naval blockade on German ports
They call for immediate joint military mobilization against Germany

evt-03-16-1935-conscription.butterflyEffect: Britain and France lodged formal protests but took no concrete action to stop the buildup. The lack of a firm response emboldened Hitler, encouraging further violations such as the 1936 remilitarization of the Rhineland and ultimately paving the way toward the Second World War.

evt-03-16-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It is mid-March 1941, and you are part of a British Empire naval and land force closing in on Berbera, the capital of British Somaliland, seized by Italy the previous year. Intelligence suggests Italian garrisons are demoralized and thinly spread across the coast.
evt-03-16-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: How should the force approach retaking the colony?

choices.text: Bypass Berbera entirely and march overland from Kenya
Negotiate a prolonged truce with Italian commanders before any landing
Launch an unopposed amphibious landing backed by naval bombardment to seize the port quickly
Wait for a full armored division from Egypt before attempting any landing

evt-03-16-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Operation Appearance succeeded with minimal fighting as British and Commonwealth forces landed and reoccupied British Somaliland by 16 March 1941, the Italian garrison largely withdrawing inland. The recapture secured the southern approaches to the Red Sea and Suez shipping lanes and freed troops for the wider East African Campaign, which crushed Italian East Africa within months.

evt-03-16-1962-flying-tiger-line-flight-.scenario: It is 16 March 1962. You are a search coordinator scanning the empty Pacific after a chartered Super Constellation carrying 96 soldiers to Saigon vanished somewhere between Guam and the Philippines.
evt-03-16-1962-flying-tiger-line-flight-.prompt: What do investigators ultimately conclude about the flight's disappearance?

choices.text: The flight recorder confirmed pilot error in a storm
Salvaged debris proved an engine fire caused the crash
Wreckage confirmed the aircraft was shot down by a Soviet fighter
No wreckage was ever found and the cause remains officially undetermined

evt-03-16-1962-flying-tiger-line-flight-.butterflyEffect: Despite an extensive search, no wreckage or bodies were ever recovered, and the cause was never officially determined. The mystery, occurring as America deepened its involvement in Vietnam, fed lasting speculation about sabotage or foul play and remains one of the largest unsolved losses in civil aviation history.

evt-03-16-1968-vietnam-war.scenario: It is 16 March 1968 over the hamlet of Sơn Mỹ. You are a US Army helicopter pilot circling low and see American soldiers gunning down unarmed villagers in a ditch below.

choices.text: Report the incident quietly through normal channels once you return to base
Land the helicopter and order your crew to stop the killing, even if it means confronting fellow US soldiers
Radio for artillery support to secure the area
Continue the reconnaissance mission without interfering in ground operations

evt-03-16-1968-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: Pilot Hugh Thompson landed his helicopter between the soldiers and survivors, ordering his crew to fire on fellow Americans if the killing continued, and airlifted villagers to safety. The massacre was covered up for over a year until journalist Seymour Hersh exposed it in 1969, turning American public opinion sharply against the war and leading to the court-martial of Lieutenant William Calley.

evt-03-16-1978-aldo-moro.scenario: It is March 16, 1978, and you sit in an emergency cabinet meeting in Rome. The Red Brigades have just gunned down Aldo Moro's bodyguards and dragged the former prime minister away, demanding the release of jailed comrades in exchange for his life.
evt-03-16-1978-aldo-moro.prompt: What does the Italian government decide to do?

choices.text: Pay a secret ransom through intermediaries
Refuse to negotiate with the terrorists
Negotiate a prisoner exchange to save Moro
Launch an immediate military raid on suspected hideouts

evt-03-16-1978-aldo-moro.butterflyEffect: The Christian Democrats, backed by the Communist Party, adopted the "line of firmness" and refused all negotiation. Fifty-five days later Moro's body was found in the trunk of a car in Rome, and his death hardened Italy's anti-terrorism laws while ending his effort to bring the Communists into government.

evt-03-16-1984-william-francis-buckley.scenario: It is March 1984 in Beirut, and you are William Buckley, the CIA's station chief, walking to your car outside your apartment. Armed men linked to Hezbollah force you into a vehicle before you can react.
evt-03-16-1984-william-francis-buckley.prompt: What ultimately becomes of Buckley after this abduction?

choices.text: He is traded for Lebanese prisoners within the year
He escapes his captors on his own
He dies in captivity after prolonged torture
He is ransomed and quietly released within weeks

evt-03-16-1984-william-francis-buckley.butterflyEffect: Buckley was held, tortured, and died in captivity in 1985; a videotape of his suffering later reached Washington. His abduction became a key reason the Reagan administration pursued secret arms sales to Iran in hopes of freeing American hostages, a scheme that unraveled as the Iran-Contra scandal.

evt-03-16-2015-teddy-sinclair.scenario: It is early 2015, and you are a judge on the second series of The X Factor New Zealand. A contestant, Joe Irvine, has just performed a tearful tribute to his late father, and the cameras are on you for your feedback.
evt-03-16-2015-teddy-sinclair.prompt: What should you avoid doing when critiquing an emotionally vulnerable contestant on live television?

choices.text: Personally mock the contestant's appearance and character on air
Give measured, specific feedback focused on the performance itself
Praise the performance regardless of its actual quality
Refuse to comment and pass judgment to another panelist

evt-03-16-2015-teddy-sinclair.butterflyEffect: Judges Natalia Kills (then performing as Natalia Kills, later known as Teddy Sinclair) and Willy Moon instead mocked Irvine's appearance, likening him to Willy Moon in personal and derisive terms. The backlash was immediate, and on 16 March 2015 the network fired both judges, ending their run on the show and drawing wide media criticism of their conduct.

evt-03-16-2022-2022-fukushima-earthquake.scenario: It is 11:36 PM on 16 March 2022, and you live in a coastal town near Fukushima. The ground has just shaken violently for nearly a minute, and Japanese broadcasters are issuing a tsunami advisory for your stretch of coast.
evt-03-16-2022-2022-fukushima-earthquake.prompt: What should you do immediately after the shaking stops?

choices.text: Move immediately to higher ground away from the coastline
Head toward the shoreline to check on boats and property
Call family members before taking any other action
Stay indoors and wait for official confirmation before moving

evt-03-16-2022-2022-fukushima-earthquake.butterflyEffect: A 30-centimeter tsunami reached the coast and the magnitude-7.4 quake caused widespread damage, killing four people and injuring 247. The quake also derailed a Tohoku Shinkansen train and knocked out power plants, triggering rolling blackout warnings across the Tokyo region during an already strained energy period.

evt-03-16-2022-mariupol-theatre-airstrik.scenario: It is 16 March 2022, and you are sheltering with hundreds of other civilians inside the Mariupol Drama Theatre as Russian aircraft continue strikes across the besieged city. Someone suggests marking the building so pilots overhead cannot mistake it for a military target.
evt-03-16-2022-mariupol-theatre-airstrik.prompt: What should the civilians do to signal that the building shelters non-combatants?

choices.text: Broadcast a radio appeal to Russian forces asking for a ceasefire
Hang white flags from every window facing the street
Paint the word for "CHILDREN" in giant letters on the pavement outside
Move everyone into the theatre's basement without any outside marking

evt-03-16-2022-mariupol-theatre-airstrik.butterflyEffect: Civilians had painted the Russian word for "CHILDREN" in huge white letters on the ground outside the theatre, visible from the air. Despite this, the building was bombed, killing an unknown but substantial number of the hundreds sheltering inside, and the strike became one of the most widely documented alleged war crimes of the siege, cited in international investigations.

evt-03-16-2025-kocani-nightclub-fire.scenario: You are inside the packed Pulse nightclub in Kočani as sparks from an indoor pyrotechnic display catch the ceiling, and the crowd surges toward exits that were never built to handle a fire.
evt-03-16-2025-kocani-nightclub-fire.prompt: What underlying failure turned this fire into a mass-casualty disaster?

choices.text: A lightning strike outside started an electrical fire
Overcrowding alone caused the tragedy, with all safety codes met
The venue was unlicensed and lacked sprinklers or sufficient emergency exits
A faulty gas line beneath the building ignited the blaze

evt-03-16-2025-kocani-nightclub-fire.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the club had operated without a license, lacked sprinklers, and had only one fire extinguisher and too few exits for its capacity. The disaster led to arrests of owners and officials accused of enabling the venue to operate unsafely, and prompted nationwide safety inspections of nightclubs across North Macedonia.

evt-03-17-455-valentinian-iii.scenario: It is March 455 in Rome. Word spreads through the Forum that Emperor Valentinian III has just been cut down by two soldiers loyal to the murdered general Aetius, reportedly urged on by the senator Petronius Maximus.
evt-03-17-455-valentinian-iii.prompt: What happens next in the scramble for the Western throne?

choices.text: The general Ricimer is proclaimed emperor immediately
Aetius's son avenges his father and becomes emperor
Petronius Maximus seizes the throne
The Senate abolishes the imperial office and restores the Republic

evt-03-17-455-valentinian-iii.butterflyEffect: Petronius Maximus seized the purple within days, but his reign lasted barely two months. As the Vandal king Geiseric approached, Rome descended into panic, Maximus was killed by a mob, and Geiseric's forces sacked the city—accelerating the Western Empire's collapse.

evt-03-17-1337-edward-the-black-prince.scenario: You stand in Westminster as King Edward III prepares to elevate his teenage son above every earl in the realm, inventing a rank that has never existed in England before.
evt-03-17-1337-edward-the-black-prince.prompt: What title does Edward III create for his heir, Edward of Woodstock?

choices.text: Duke of Cornwall
Earl of Chester
Prince of Wales
Duke of Lancaster

evt-03-17-1337-edward-the-black-prince.butterflyEffect: Edward III created the title Duke of Cornwall, England's first dukedom, making his son the model of chivalric kingship later remembered as the Black Prince. The dukedom became permanently attached to the heir apparent of the English throne and is still held today by the eldest son of the reigning monarch.

evt-03-17-1452-reconquista.scenario: It is March 1452 near Lorca, in Murcia. You ride with a combined force of Castilian knights and Murcian militia, tracking a Nasrid raiding column returning toward Granada laden with captives and plunder.
evt-03-17-1452-reconquista.prompt: What should the Christian force do as the raiders near the border?

choices.text: Ambush and engage the raiders before they reach safety
Send envoys to negotiate a truce
Retreat and fortify the walls of Lorca instead
Let them pass to avoid provoking further retaliation

evt-03-17-1452-reconquista.butterflyEffect: The Castilian-Murcian force caught and destroyed the raiding column at what became known as the Battle of Los Alporchones, one of the heaviest blows dealt to Granada in decades. It boosted Christian confidence along the frontier, though the emirate itself would survive another forty years until its final surrender in 1492.

evt-03-17-1677-franco-dutch-war.scenario: You are a French engineer under Marshal Vauban in the trenches outside Valenciennes, March 1677. The town's garrison is strained, and Vauban proposes breaking with custom by storming the breach in broad daylight rather than waiting for the usual night assault.
evt-03-17-1677-franco-dutch-war.prompt: What should you urge Vauban's officers to do to take Valenciennes?

choices.text: Press for an immediate daylight assault on the breach
Withdraw and wait for reinforcements from Paris
Continue the slow, methodical trench approach
Open negotiations for a conditional surrender

evt-03-17-1677-franco-dutch-war.butterflyEffect: Vauban's unconventional daylight assault succeeded, and Valenciennes fell on 17 March 1677. The victory strengthened France's grip on the Spanish Netherlands and Vauban's siegecraft became a model for European engineers for a century afterward.

evt-03-17-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It's March 1776 and you serve under General William Howe aboard a ship in Boston Harbor. Overnight, Continental Army cannons dragged from Fort Ticonderoga by Henry Knox have appeared on Dorchester Heights, now able to pound your fleet and the city below.
evt-03-17-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What must Howe's besieged garrison do?

choices.text: Storm Dorchester Heights to retake the guns
Negotiate a truce to hold Boston through summer
Burn the city and retreat overland to New York
Evacuate Boston by sea to Halifax

evt-03-17-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Howe evacuated roughly 9,000 troops and 1,000 Loyalists by sea to Halifax on March 17, ending the eleven-month siege without a major battle. It was the first significant American victory of the war, and Knox's feat proved artillery could decide sieges, shaping how Washington fought for years afterward.

evt-03-17-1864-second-schleswig-war.scenario: You stand on the deck of an Austrian frigate off the island of Rügen as the combined Austro-Prussian squadron closes on the Danish ships blockading Prussia's Baltic ports.
evt-03-17-1864-second-schleswig-war.prompt: What must the Austro-Prussian fleet do to break the Danish blockade?

choices.text: Wait for winter ice to force a Danish withdrawal
Engage the Danish squadron directly in battle off Jasmund
Seek British mediation for an immediate armistice
Land troops on the Danish island of Falster

evt-03-17-1864-second-schleswig-war.butterflyEffect: The two fleets clashed in the Battle of Jasmund, an inconclusive but fierce engagement that nonetheless forced the Danish squadron to withdraw toward Copenhagen. The retreat eased pressure on German Baltic shipping and coastal towns, even as the war on land continued to turn decisively against Denmark.

evt-03-17-1891-ss-utopia.scenario: You are a passenger aboard the crowded steamship Utopia, entering Gibraltar Bay at night among hundreds of Italian emigrants bound for America, when the ironclad HMS Anson suddenly looms out of the darkness ahead.
evt-03-17-1891-ss-utopia.prompt: What does Utopia's captain attempt after the collision tears open her hull?

choices.text: Continue on to Gibraltar harbour for emergency repairs
Turn and ram HMS Anson to prevent a second collision
Steer the sinking ship toward the breakwater to run her aground
Order immediate abandonment into lifeboats mid-bay

evt-03-17-1891-ss-utopia.butterflyEffect: The captain tried to beach the crippled ship on the breakwater, but Utopia sank within minutes, trapping hundreds of emigrants below deck and killing over 500 people. The disaster exposed the dangers of overcrowded steerage compartments and spurred calls for better emergency access and lifeboat provision on immigrant steamships.

evt-03-17-1917-world-war-i.scenario: You ride with the Duke of Westminster's column of armoured cars racing across the Western Desert. Somewhere ahead, Senussi captors are holding 92 survivors of torpedoed British ships, and you must reach them before they are moved or killed.
evt-03-17-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What must the rescue column do to save the captives in time?

choices.text: Drive through the night in armoured cars to reach the camp before the captors relocate it
Open ransom negotiations through neutral intermediaries
Besiege the coastal town of Sollum first to cut off supply
Wait for camel-mounted cavalry reinforcements before advancing

evt-03-17-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The Duke of Westminster's motorized force reached the camp and freed all 92 prisoners, survivors of the torpedoed SS Tara and other vessels. The raid became one of the first successful long-range operations using armoured cars, proving the desert could be crossed by motor vehicle rather than camel, a lesson later applied throughout the North African campaigns.

evt-03-17-1950-lawrence-berkeley-nationa.scenario: It's March 1950 in Ernest Lawrence's Berkeley Radiation Laboratory. You've spent weeks bombarding curium with alpha particles in the 60-inch cyclotron, chasing a new, heavier element to name after the state that funds your work.
evt-03-17-1950-lawrence-berkeley-nationa.prompt: What element did the Berkeley team announce discovering on March 17, 1950?

choices.text: Californium, element 98
Einsteinium, element 99
Berkelium, element 97
Plutonium, element 94

evt-03-17-1950-lawrence-berkeley-nationa.butterflyEffect: The team of Ghiorso, Thompson, Street and Seaborg identified californium, element 98, named for the state and university behind the discovery. It later proved vital to neutron sources used in cancer therapy and oil-well logging, and cemented Berkeley's central role in synthesizing new transuranium elements throughout the Cold War.

evt-03-17-1955-ice-hockey.scenario: It's March 17, 1955, inside the Montreal Forum. Word spreads through the crowd that NHL president Clarence Campbell has suspended Canadiens star Maurice "Rocket" Richard for the rest of the season and playoffs — and Campbell has just taken his seat among the furious fans.
evt-03-17-1955-ice-hockey.prompt: What do the enraged fans do next?

choices.text: Riot in the streets of Montreal, causing extensive damage
Peacefully petition the NHL to reverse the suspension
Boycott Canadiens games for the rest of the season
Demand Richard retire in protest

evt-03-17-1955-ice-hockey.butterflyEffect: Fans hurled objects at Campbell, a tear-gas canister went off, and mobs smashed storefronts along Rue Sainte-Catherine in what became known as the Richard Riot, causing roughly $100,000 in damage. Historians often point to it as an early spark of Québécois nationalist frustration with English-Canadian institutions, a current that would swell into the Quiet Revolution.

evt-03-17-1957-1957-cebu-douglas-c-47-cr.scenario: You are Nestor Mata, a Philippine Herald reporter aboard the presidential aircraft as it flies home over Cebu. The plane goes down on the slopes of Mount Manunggal, and you alone walk away from the wreckage.
evt-03-17-1957-1957-cebu-douglas-c-47-cr.prompt: Who is sworn in as president following Magsaysay's death in the crash?

choices.text: Carlos P. Garcia
Elpidio Quirino
Diosdado Macapagal
Manuel Roxas

evt-03-17-1957-1957-cebu-douglas-c-47-cr.butterflyEffect: Vice President Carlos P. Garcia was sworn in immediately, completing Magsaysay's term and later winning election in his own right that same year. Garcia continued the 'Filipino First' economic policy, while the sudden loss of the widely popular Magsaysay reshaped Philippine politics for the following administration.

evt-03-17-1963-mount-agung.scenario: It is March 1963, and you are a Balinese official near Mount Agung. The sacred volcano has been rumbling for weeks, yet the once-a-century Eka Dasa Rudra ceremony at Besakih temple is drawing thousands of pilgrims to its slopes.
evt-03-17-1963-mount-agung.prompt: With tremors increasing, what should local authorities urge?

choices.text: Let the ceremony proceed and delay any evacuation
Evacuate nearby villages despite the ceremony's importance
Ignore the tremors as ordinary volcanic activity
Move pilgrims closer to the crater to witness the ritual

evt-03-17-1963-mount-agung.butterflyEffect: Despite mounting warning signs, many villagers remained near the mountain out of religious devotion, and on March 17 Agung erupted violently, sending pyroclastic flows and lahars down its slopes and killing well over a thousand people. The disaster spurred the Indonesian government's transmigration program, resettling thousands of Balinese survivors onto other islands.

evt-03-17-1968-dugway-proving-ground.scenario: It is March 1968 in Skull Valley, Utah. You are a rancher watching thousands of sheep on the range near Dugway Proving Ground suddenly stagger, convulse, and die within hours of each other.
evt-03-17-1968-dugway-proving-ground.prompt: What did investigators eventually determine had caused the mass sheep deaths?

choices.text: Nerve agent drifted from an aerial test at Dugway
The sheep drank from a contaminated irrigation canal
A contagious disease swept through the flock
Local farmers had oversprayed pesticide

evt-03-17-1968-dugway-proving-ground.butterflyEffect: Investigators traced the deaths to nerve agent VX that had drifted from an aerial test at Dugway. The Army never formally admitted fault but paid ranchers compensation, and the public outcry helped push President Nixon toward restricting open-air chemical weapons testing the following year.

evt-03-17-1973-pulitzer-prize-for-featur.scenario: It is 17 March 1973 at Travis Air Force Base, California. You raise your camera as a family sprints across the tarmac toward a newly released prisoner of war stepping off the plane from Vietnam.
evt-03-17-1973-pulitzer-prize-for-featur.prompt: What made this photograph, later titled 'Burst of Joy', a Pulitzer-winning image?

choices.text: It captured a returning POW's family reuniting after years apart
It captured a prisoner's release ceremony in Hanoi
It showed the last American combat troops leaving Vietnam
It depicted the fall of Saigon two years later

evt-03-17-1973-pulitzer-prize-for-featur.butterflyEffect: Slava Veder's photo of Lt. Col. Robert Stirm's family reunion became one of the most reproduced images of the Vietnam War's end. Its joy masked a private heartbreak: Stirm's wife had already told him by letter that their marriage was over, and she filed for divorce within weeks, a detail that later complicated the photo's legacy.

evt-03-17-1988-eritrean-war-of-independe.scenario: It is March 1988 near Afabet, Eritrea. You serve with Ethiopia's Nadew Command, one of the army's most battle-hardened forces, as EPLF fighters close in from several directions at once, cutting the roads behind your armored columns.
evt-03-17-1988-eritrean-war-of-independe.prompt: What was the outcome of the EPLF's encirclement at Afabet?

choices.text: A negotiated ceasefire ends the fighting on the spot
The Ethiopian Nadew Command is destroyed, a major turning point
The EPLF is repelled with heavy losses
Ethiopian reinforcements arrive and break the siege

evt-03-17-1988-eritrean-war-of-independe.butterflyEffect: The Nadew Command was overwhelmed and destroyed, one of Ethiopia's worst defeats of the war, with the EPLF capturing huge stores of Soviet-supplied tanks and artillery. The victory shifted momentum decisively toward the rebels, paving the way for Eritrean independence after the Derg's fall in 1991.

evt-03-17-1992-1992-buenos-aires-israeli.scenario: It is 17 March 1992 in Buenos Aires. You are an investigator sent to the smoking ruins of the Israeli embassy after a car bomb has torn through the building, and you must determine who was behind the attack.
evt-03-17-1992-1992-buenos-aires-israeli.prompt: What did the investigation conclude about who carried out the bombing?

choices.text: Islamic Jihad Organization, linked to Hezbollah, claimed responsibility
A rival diplomatic mission was responsible
A gas leak caused an accidental explosion
Argentine far-right militants carried out the attack

evt-03-17-1992-1992-buenos-aires-israeli.butterflyEffect: The Islamic Jihad Organization, linked to Hezbollah, claimed responsibility, and the attack was widely seen as retaliation for Israeli military actions against the group's leadership. It strained Argentina-Iran relations for years and foreshadowed the even deadlier 1994 AMIA Jewish community center bombing in the same city.

evt-03-17-2000-uganda.scenario: It is March 17, 2000, in Kanungu, Uganda. Hundreds of followers of the Movement for the Restoration of the Ten Commandments of God have gathered inside a locked, boarded church for what their leaders call a final gathering.
evt-03-17-2000-uganda.prompt: What did investigators later determine caused thefire that killed the congregation?

choices.text: A government raid gone wrong
Premeditated murder by leaders to silence the group
A voluntary mass suicide over a failed prophecy
An accidental fire during a religious ritual

evt-03-17-2000-uganda.butterflyEffect: Early reports assumed a mass suicide driven by a failed doomsday prophecy, but investigators found the doors nailed shut and windows boarded from outside, pointing to premeditated murder by the group's leaders amid financial collapse and rising dissent. Subsequent digs uncovered many more victims buried at the cult's properties, revealing one of the deadliest cult-linked mass killings in modern history.

evt-03-17-2004-2004-unrest-in-kosovo.scenario: It's 17 March 2004 in the divided town of Mitrovica. Unverified reports that Serbs chased three Albanian boys into the Ibar River have spread through local media, and crowds are surging toward Serb neighborhoods as gunfire breaks out along the partition line.
evt-03-17-2004-2004-unrest-in-kosovo.prompt: What must NATO's KFOR peacekeepers urgently do?

choices.text: Declare martial law and suspend the provisional government
Deploy reinforcements to contain the violence and protect Serb enclaves
Arm Kosovo Serb militias for self-defense
Withdraw entirely to avoid taking sides

evt-03-17-2004-2004-unrest-in-kosovo.butterflyEffect: Despite reinforcements, two days of rioting left at least 19 dead, displaced thousands of Kosovo Serbs, and destroyed dozens of Orthodox churches and homes. The violence exposed how fragile the postwar peace remained and added pressure toward negotiations over Kosovo's final status, which led to its 2008 declaration of independence.

evt-03-17-2011-libyan-civil-war-2011.scenario: You sit among the ambassadors in the UN Security Council chamber as Gaddafi's forces advance on Benghazi. A resolution is on the table to stop the looming assault on civilians.
evt-03-17-2011-libyan-civil-war-2011.prompt: What does Resolution 1973 authorize member states to do?

choices.text: Deploy UN ground troops to capture Tripoli
Establish a no-fly zone and use 'all necessary measures' to protect civilians
Impose economic sanctions only, with no military action
Send unarmed peacekeepers to monitor a ceasefire

evt-03-17-2011-libyan-civil-war-2011.butterflyEffect: The Council authorized a no-fly zone and 'all necessary measures' short of occupation to protect civilians, opening the door to NATO airstrikes against Gaddafi's forces. The intervention tipped the civil war toward the rebels and led to Gaddafi's fall months later, though it also left Libya fractured by years of subsequent conflict.

evt-03-17-2016-rojava-revolution.scenario: You are a delegate at the conference in Rmelan on 17 March 2016, representing Kurdish, Arab, and Assyrian councils asked to decide the political future of the territories they control across northern Syria.
evt-03-17-2016-rojava-revolution.prompt: What should the assembly declare for the region's governance?

choices.text: Request formal annexation by Turkey
Declare a federal system of self-governance for the region
Dissolve the local councils and disband the movement
Pledge full allegiance to the Assad government in Damascus

evt-03-17-2016-rojava-revolution.butterflyEffect: Delegates declared the Federation of Northern Syria, formalizing autonomous self-rule across mixed Kurdish, Arab, and Assyrian cantons. Both Damascus and Ankara rejected the declaration, and it became a lasting flashpoint behind years of Turkish military operations against the region.

evt-03-18-1241-first-mongol-invasion-of-.scenario: It is 18 March 1241. You stand with the Polish forces of Sandomierz and Kraków near Chmielnik as a Mongol army, advancing ahead of its main invasion of Hungary, closes in.
evt-03-18-1241-first-mongol-invasion-of-.prompt: What followed the Mongol victory over the Polish forces at Chmielnik?

choices.text: The Mongols retreated back across the border
The Mongols advanced and sacked Kraków
Polish forces regrouped and defeated the Mongols soon after
The Mongols made peace and withdrew from Poland

evt-03-18-1241-first-mongol-invasion-of-.butterflyEffect: With the Polish defenders broken, the Mongols advanced and burned Kraków within days. They then pressed on to crush a larger Polish-German coalition at the Battle of Legnica in April, leaving southern Poland devastated and fragmented for years.

evt-03-18-1277-charles-i-of-anjou.scenario: It is 1277, and as an advisor to Charles I, King of Sicily and Count of Provence, you are weighing whether he should pay Maria of Antioch for her contested claim to the throne of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.
evt-03-18-1277-charles-i-of-anjou.prompt: Should Charles purchase Maria of Antioch's claim to Jerusalem?

choices.text: No, renounce all claims outside France
Yes, purchase it to strengthen his claims across the Mediterranean
No, ally with the Mamluk Sultan Baibars instead
No, focus resources solely on governing Sicily

evt-03-18-1277-charles-i-of-anjou.butterflyEffect: Charles bought the claim and began styling himself King of Jerusalem, adding another crown to his sprawling Mediterranean holdings alongside Sicily, Albania, and soon Achaea. His mounting ambitions and heavy taxation provoked deep resentment in Sicily, helping trigger the 1282 uprising known as the Sicilian Vespers that shattered his empire.

evt-03-18-1892-frederick-stanley-16th-ea.scenario: You are a guest at Rideau Hall in Ottawa in March 1892 as the Governor General, Lord Stanley of Preston, announces he wishes to donate a trophy to reward the finest hockey club in the Dominion of Canada.
evt-03-18-1892-frederick-stanley-16th-ea.prompt: What did Lord Stanley's proposed donation eventually become?

choices.text: The Stanley Cup, ice hockey's championship trophy
The Vanier Cup, Canadian university football's trophy
The Grey Cup, Canadian football's championship trophy
The Memorial Cup, junior hockey's championship trophy

evt-03-18-1892-frederick-stanley-16th-ea.butterflyEffect: Stanley's gift became the Stanley Cup, first awarded in 1893, and it grew into the oldest trophy competed for by professional athletes in North America. Since 1926 it has been the championship prize of the National Hockey League, and Lord Stanley himself never saw a game played for it before returning to England.

evt-03-18-1906-traian-vuia.scenario: It is 18 March 1906, and you are Romanian inventor Traian Vuia, standing beside your self-built tractor monoplane on a country road near Paris, determined to prove it can leave the ground under its own power alone.
evt-03-18-1906-traian-vuia.prompt: How should Vuia's machine get airborne without any external launching aid?

choices.text: Fit it with ski-like runners for an ice launch
