Launch it from a steam-powered catapult ramp
Let its own engine drive the wheels to accelerate and lift off
Have it towed to speed by a motorcar

evt-03-18-1906-traian-vuia.butterflyEffect: Vuia's aircraft rolled forward on its own wheels and briefly lifted about 11 meters into the air, proving a wheeled, self-propelled takeoff was possible without rails or catapults. His design influenced later monoplane builders, including Louis Blériot, who would cross the English Channel by air just three years later.

evt-03-18-1915-world-war-i.scenario: It is 18 March 1915. You stand on the deck of an Allied battleship pushing through the Dardanelles Strait toward Constantinople, and three warships have just struck mines and gone down.
evt-03-18-1915-world-war-i.prompt: What do Allied commanders decide after losing three battleships to mines?

choices.text: Send in more battleships immediately to force through
Request Russian naval reinforcements to continue the attack
Call off the naval assault and plan a land invasion
Retreat back to the Mediterranean permanently

evt-03-18-1915-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The naval attempt was abandoned, and commanders opted to force the straits by land instead. This decision led directly to the Gallipoli landings of 25 April 1915, a brutal campaign that failed at enormous cost and became a defining national memory for Australia, New Zealand, and Turkey.

evt-03-18-1921-russian-civil-war.scenario: It is 18 March 1921. You are a Red Army soldier crossing the ice of the Gulf of Finland to retake the fortress of Kronstadt, where sailors and civilians have risen up demanding reforms.
evt-03-18-1921-russian-civil-war.prompt: What did the Bolshevik government do once the Kronstadt rebellion was crushed?

choices.text: Introduced the New Economic Policy to ease economic hardship
Restored the old Provisional Government
Disbanded the Red Army units that took part
Granted the sailors' demands for free elections

evt-03-18-1921-russian-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The suppression of sailors who had once been heroes of the revolution shocked socialists at home and abroad. Lenin responded by abandoning War Communism and introducing the New Economic Policy, allowing limited private trade to revive the ruined Soviet economy.

evt-03-18-1925-1925-tri-state-tornado.scenario: It is midday on 18 March 1925. You are a farmer in southern Illinois watching a dark, fast-moving storm bear down, with no siren, radio bulletin, or official warning to tell you what it is.
evt-03-18-1925-1925-tri-state-tornado.prompt: What left communities across Missouri, Illinois, and Indiana so unprepared that day?

choices.text: Poor roads that slowed any evacuation
The absence of any organized tornado warning system
A lack of sturdy building materials in the region
Too few local weather observers

evt-03-18-1925-1925-tri-state-tornado.butterflyEffect: At the time, the U.S. Weather Bureau avoided even using the word 'tornado' in forecasts, fearing it would cause panic, so no organized warning system existed. The catastrophic toll from this storm helped push meteorologists toward developing real tornado forecasting and public warning systems in the decades that followed.

evt-03-18-1959-1959-tibetan-uprising.scenario: It is March 1959, and you serve in the Dalai Lama's inner circle at Sera Monastery in Lhasa, as Chinese artillery begins shelling the summer palace and street fighting spreads through the city.
evt-03-18-1959-1959-tibetan-uprising.prompt: What should the Dalai Lama's party do as the situation collapses around them?

choices.text: Slip away secretly and flee toward India
Appeal directly to the United Nations from Lhasa
Surrender to negotiate greater autonomy for Tibet
Remain and personally direct the uprising's defense

evt-03-18-1959-1959-tibetan-uprising.butterflyEffect: The Dalai Lama and his entourage fled secretly across the Himalayas into India, where he was granted asylum and later established the Tibetan government-in-exile in Dharamshala. That exile government became the enduring center of the Tibetan independence movement and international advocacy for Tibetan rights for decades afterward.

evt-03-18-1965-alexei-leonov.scenario: You are Alexei Leonov, floating outside Voskhod 2 in March 1965, the first human ever to walk in space. After twelve extraordinary minutes, it is time to return, but your spacesuit has stiffened and swollen far beyond its normal size in the vacuum.
evt-03-18-1965-alexei-leonov.prompt: What must Leonov do to squeeze back through the narrow airlock?

choices.text: Use a reserve oxygen tank to blast the hatch open wider
Wait in orbit for a second spacecraft to retrieve him
Partially deflate his suit to squeeze through the airlock
Cut his tether and float free until pressure normalized

evt-03-18-1965-alexei-leonov.butterflyEffect: Leonov partially depressurized his suit, risking decompression sickness, in order to bend his limbs enough to re-enter the airlock headfirst rather than feet-first as trained. The near-disaster, kept secret for decades, pushed Soviet engineers to redesign spacesuits and airlocks, and Leonov's feat opened the door to all future spacewalks, including the Apollo missions.

evt-03-18-1969-vietnam-war.scenario: It is 18 March 1969, and you are a B-52 pilot briefed to strike suspected North Vietnamese supply routes inside neutral Cambodia, part of a bombing campaign your superiors have ordered kept hidden from Congress and the public.
evt-03-18-1969-vietnam-war.prompt: As the pilot, what do you do with these secret orders?

choices.text: Refuse to fly, citing Cambodia's neutral status
Divert the strike to targets inside Laos instead
Carry out the mission as ordered through the chain of command
Leak the mission's existence to a journalist before takeoff

evt-03-18-1969-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: The bombing, part of Operation Menu, proceeded and expanded over the following years, destabilizing Prince Sihanouk's neutral government and fueling the growth of the Khmer Rouge. When the secret campaign was later exposed, it deepened public distrust of the Nixon administration and intensified opposition to the war.

evt-03-18-1970-1970-united-states-postal.scenario: You are a postal clerk in New York City in March 1970. Congress has just approved a pay raise so small that many of your colleagues are furious, and word is spreading of a walkout, even though strikes by federal employees are illegal.
evt-03-18-1970-1970-united-states-postal.prompt: What do postal workers across the country do in response?

choices.text: Request arbitration through the Postmaster General's office
Accept the raise and pursue grievances through union channels
Launch a nationwide wildcat strike despite its illegality
Seek an immediate court injunction against Congress

evt-03-18-1970-1970-united-states-postal.butterflyEffect: Workers launched an eight-day wildcat strike, the largest in U.S. history, that spread from New York to cities nationwide and forced President Nixon to call in the National Guard to sort mail. The crisis led directly to the Postal Reorganization Act of 1970, which replaced the old Post Office Department with the independent U.S. Postal Service and granted postal workers collective bargaining rights.

evt-03-18-1985-soap-opera.scenario: It is 18 March 1985. You switch on the Seven Network to watch the debut episode of a new suburban soap opera called Neighbours, set on a quiet Melbourne street.
evt-03-18-1985-soap-opera.prompt: What happened to Neighbours after its rocky start on Seven?

choices.text: It moved to the ABC network
It became an instant hit and stayed on Seven for decades
It was cancelled by Seven and revived by Network Ten
It was cancelled outright with no further broadcast

evt-03-18-1985-soap-opera.butterflyEffect: Struggling with poor ratings, Neighbours was cancelled by Seven after only eight months but was quickly picked up by Network Ten in 1986. There it thrived for decades, became a major export to Britain, and launched the careers of Kylie Minogue and Jason Donovan.

evt-03-18-1990-isabella-stewart-gardner-.scenario: It is just after midnight on 18 March 1990 at the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston. Two men dressed as police officers buzz the side door, claiming they're responding to a disturbance call, and ask you, the night guard, to let them in.
evt-03-18-1990-isabella-stewart-gardner-.prompt: What should you do when the men in police uniforms ask to be let inside?

choices.text: Call the real police department to confirm first
Refuse entry and trigger a lockdown
Buzz them in without verifying their identity
Wake your supervisor before responding

evt-03-18-1990-isabella-stewart-gardner-.butterflyEffect: The guard let the impostors in, and they handcuffed both night watchmen before spending over an hour looting the museum of thirteen works, including a Vermeer and three Rembrandts worth hundreds of millions of dollars. The case remains unsolved decades later, and the empty frames still hang on the museum's walls awaiting the paintings' return.

evt-03-18-1996-ozone-disco-fire.scenario: It is the night of 18 March 1996, and hundreds of young people are packed into the Ozone Disco in Quezon City for an anniversary celebration when fire breaks out and smoke fills the club.
evt-03-18-1996-ozone-disco-fire.prompt: What turned this fire into the deadliest in Philippine history?

choices.text: A faulty sprinkler system sprayed flammable chemicals
The disco had no windows or ventilation of any kind
The building's fire alarm system failed to sound at all
Emergency exits had been locked or blocked, trapping patrons inside

evt-03-18-1996-ozone-disco-fire.butterflyEffect: Investigators found that emergency exits at the Ozone Disco had been locked or blocked, reportedly to stop people from entering without paying, trapping patrons inside as flames spread through flammable decorations. The tragedy, which killed 162 people, forced the Philippine government to tighten fire-safety enforcement and inspection of entertainment venues nationwide.

evt-03-18-2014-crimea.scenario: You sit in the Russian State Duma on 18 March 2014, summoned as Vladimir Putin and Crimean officials arrive to present a treaty absorbing Crimea into Russia, just days after a disputed referendum on the peninsula.
evt-03-18-2014-crimea.prompt: What should the Duma do with the accession treaty placed before it?

choices.text: Refer the matter to international arbitration
Reject the treaty outright
Ratify the treaty swiftly
Demand a UN-supervised revote first

evt-03-18-2014-crimea.butterflyEffect: The Duma ratified the treaty, formally annexing Crimea. Ukraine, the United States, and the European Union refused to recognize the move and imposed sweeping sanctions on Russia, setting the stage for years of tension that erupted into full-scale war in 2022.

evt-03-18-2015-bardo-national-museum-att.scenario: It is midday on 18 March 2015, and you are a Tunisian police commander responding to reports of gunfire and hostage-taking inside the Bardo National Museum in Tunis, where a busload of foreign cruise tourists has just arrived.
evt-03-18-2015-bardo-national-museum-att.prompt: What must your forces do to end the siege and save the hostages?

choices.text: Wait for military reinforcements from outside the capital
Open ransom negotiations through diplomatic channels
Evacuate hostages only through the museum's rooftop exit
Storm the building and neutralize the gunmen directly

evt-03-18-2015-bardo-national-museum-att.butterflyEffect: Tunisian security forces stormed the museum and killed both gunmen, Yassine Labidi and Saber Khachnaoui, ending the siege. The Islamic State claimed responsibility, and the attack devastated Tunisia's tourism-dependent economy, prompting European governments to issue travel warnings that lasted for years.

evt-03-18-2015-bardo-national-museum-tun.scenario: It is 18 March 2015. You are inside the Bardo National Museum in Tunis as gunmen open fire on tourists who have just stepped off buses from a cruise ship.
evt-03-18-2015-bardo-national-museum-tun.prompt: How did Tunisian forces end the siege that followed?

choices.text: Called in a foreign counterterrorism unit to lead the assault
Negotiated a ceasefire with the gunmen
Stormed the museum and killed the attackers
Waited days before any confrontation

evt-03-18-2015-bardo-national-museum-tun.butterflyEffect: Tunisian special forces stormed the museum and killed the two attackers, ending the siege. Claimed by the Islamic State, the attack devastated Tunisia's vital tourism industry and pushed the government into a nationwide state of emergency and crackdown on militant networks.

evt-03-19-1279-mongol-conquest-of-the-so.scenario: You stand on the imperial fleet at Yamen, hemmed into a bay by Mongol warships under Zhang Hongfan. The Song lines are broken, and Chancellor Lu Xiufu holds the eight-year-old Emperor Zhao Bing close as defeat becomes certain.
evt-03-19-1279-mongol-conquest-of-the-so.prompt: What does Lu Xiufu do to keep the boy emperor from Mongol hands?

choices.text: Surrenders the emperor in exchange for lenient terms
Carries the emperor into the sea and drowns with him rather than surrender
Hands the emperor to Zhang Hongfan to negotiate peace
Attempts to flee with the emperor's ship toward Vietnam

evt-03-19-1279-mongol-conquest-of-the-so.butterflyEffect: Lu Xiufu carried the young emperor into the sea and drowned with him rather than surrender, and thousands of loyal officials and soldiers followed by drowning themselves too. Their deaths ended Song resistance for good, completing the Mongol conquest of China and confirming Kublai Khan's Yuan dynasty as ruler of all China.

evt-03-19-1563-edict-of-amboise.scenario: You are a Huguenot nobleman in France in March 1563, as Catherine de' Medici's regency government ends the first war of religion with a new royal edict.
evt-03-19-1563-edict-of-amboise.prompt: What does the Edict of Amboise grant to Huguenots like you?

choices.text: Exile for all Huguenot nobles
Limited freedom of worship in specific towns and noble households
Full legal equality with Catholics nationwide
Conversion to Catholicism required for all officeholders

evt-03-19-1563-edict-of-amboise.butterflyEffect: The edict allowed Protestant worship only in limited places—nobles' households and certain towns—far short of full toleration. The compromise pleased no one fully, and religious violence resumed within a few years, dragging France through further wars of religion until the Edict of Nantes in 1598.

evt-03-19-1808-charles-iv-of-spain.scenario: It's March 19, 1808, at the palace of Aranjuez. Riots stirred by hatred of your favorite minister Godoy have spiraled out of control, and your son Ferdinand's supporters are demanding you step aside.
evt-03-19-1808-charles-iv-of-spain.prompt: As King Charles IV, what do you do?

choices.text: Flee immediately to Portugal with your court
Appeal to Napoleon to crush the uprising by force
Abdicate the throne in favor of Ferdinand VII
Have Ferdinand arrested for treason

evt-03-19-1808-charles-iv-of-spain.butterflyEffect: Charles abdicated in favor of Ferdinand VII, but Napoleon then summoned both men to Bayonne and pressured them to renounce the crown in favor of his own brother Joseph. This betrayal ignited the Peninsular War and years of fierce Spanish resistance to French rule.

evt-03-19-1865-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 19 March 1865 in North Carolina, and you serve under General Joseph E. Johnston, who has gathered his scattered forces to strike an isolated wing of Sherman's advancing army near Bentonville.
evt-03-19-1865-american-civil-war.prompt: What is Johnston's plan for this attack?

choices.text: Retreat and avoid all contact with Sherman
Crush Sherman's left wing before his forces can reunite
Encircle and capture the city of Raleigh
Wait for reinforcements from Robert E. Lee

evt-03-19-1865-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Johnston struck Sherman's left wing before it could unite with the rest of his army, achieving early success but ultimately failing to stop the Union advance. It was the last major Confederate offensive against Sherman; weeks later Johnston surrendered his army, effectively ending the war in the Carolinas.

evt-03-19-1911-clara-zetkin.scenario: It's March 19, 1911. You join over a million people across Europe rallying for the first International Women's Day, an idea championed by German socialist Clara Zetkin.
evt-03-19-1911-clara-zetkin.prompt: What were you and fellow marchers primarily demanding?

choices.text: Women's suffrage and the right to work
An end to the ongoing world war
Universal male suffrage
The abolition of child labor alone

evt-03-19-1911-clara-zetkin.butterflyEffect: The demands for suffrage and workplace rights echoed for decades. International Women's Day spread worldwide, was later fixed on March 8, and became a globally recognized day for advancing women's political and economic rights.

evt-03-19-1962-bob-dylan.scenario: You are a Columbia Records executive in early 1962, reviewing the tracklist for an unknown 20-year-old folk singer's first album. Most of the songs are traditional blues and folk covers, with only two originals.
evt-03-19-1962-bob-dylan.prompt: What should the label do with this cautious, mostly-covers debut?

choices.text: Release it as planned to establish the artist
Re-record it with a full studio orchestra
Shelve it and wait for an all-original album
Market it exclusively as a blues record

evt-03-19-1962-bob-dylan.butterflyEffect: The self-titled album sold modestly and some at Columbia nicknamed Dylan "Hammond's Folly." Within a year his second album, filled with original songs like "Blowin' in the Wind," made him the voice of the folk revival and reshaped songwriting for a generation.

evt-03-19-1964-march-of-the-family-with-.scenario: It's March 19, 1964, in São Paulo. You march with hundreds of thousands of fellow Brazilians, alarmed by President Goulart's recent rally promising land reform and warning of foreign 'exploiters.'
evt-03-19-1964-march-of-the-family-with-.prompt: What effect did this massive conservative show of force have on Brazil's crisis?

choices.text: It emboldened military leaders to depose Goulart weeks later
It sparked a larger counter-march that strengthened Goulart's position
It led to a peaceful compromise on land reform
It persuaded Goulart to resign immediately

evt-03-19-1964-march-of-the-family-with-.butterflyEffect: The march signaled broad civilian backing for removing Goulart, helping legitimize the military coup that followed on March 31–April 1, 1964. That coup installed a military dictatorship that would rule Brazil for the next 21 years.

evt-03-19-1979-cable-television.scenario: You are helping launch a new cable channel in March 1979, built on the promise of unedited access to government. Congress has just agreed to let cameras into the House chamber.
evt-03-19-1979-cable-television.prompt: What should the channel's very first broadcast show?

choices.text: Coverage of a state governors' conference
Live floor proceedings of the U.S. House of Representatives
A taped documentary about Congress
An interview with the President

evt-03-19-1979-cable-television.butterflyEffect: C-SPAN's debut broadcast was live proceedings of the U.S. House of Representatives, including a speech by then-Congressman Al Gore. The channel's gavel-to-gavel coverage became a fixture of American civic life, later expanding to the Senate and countless public affairs programming.

evt-03-19-1979-united-states-house-of-re.scenario: It's 19 March 1979, and you're a producer for a brand-new, unproven television venture, readying cameras trained for the first time on the floor of the U.S. House as debate begins.
evt-03-19-1979-united-states-house-of-re.prompt: What new television network is born from carrying this first broadcast gavel to gavel?

choices.text: PBS's Congressional Report
NBC's political affairs desk
C-SPAN
CNN's Capitol Hill bureau

evt-03-19-1979-united-states-house-of-re.butterflyEffect: The House's decision to allow cameras onto the floor let the fledgling network air unedited proceedings from day one, establishing an unbroken record of congressional debate. It reshaped how Americans watched their government and helped push the Senate to allow similar broadcasts in 1986.

evt-03-19-1987-televangelism.scenario: It's March 19, 1987. You're a longtime PTL Club donor watching televangelist Jim Bakker resign on air, amid swirling allegations of a hush-money payment to a former church secretary.
evt-03-19-1987-televangelism.prompt: What was the ultimate legal fallout from Bakker's resignation?

choices.text: He became a federal regulator overseeing religious broadcasting
PTL quietly folded with no further scandal or investigation
He was cleared of all wrongdoing and returned to broadcasting immediately
He was later convicted of fraud for misusing PTL donations

evt-03-19-1987-televangelism.butterflyEffect: Bakker was convicted in 1989 on fraud and conspiracy charges for overselling PTL 'lifetime partnerships' and diverting donor funds, and he served years in federal prison. The scandal became a landmark moment eroding public trust in televangelism and prompted lasting scrutiny of religious broadcasters' finances.

evt-03-19-1989-egypt.scenario: It's 19 March 1989. You stand on the small beach at Taba, watching Egyptian soldiers ready the flag they are about to raise after years of Israeli control over this last sliver of Sinai.
evt-03-19-1989-egypt.prompt: What actually resolved the dispute and returned Taba to Egypt?

choices.text: A ruling by an international arbitration tribunal
An Egyptian military operation to retake the town
Direct negotiation at the original Camp David Accords
A United Nations General Assembly resolution

evt-03-19-1989-egypt.butterflyEffect: An international arbitration tribunal ruled in 1988 that Taba lay on the Egyptian side of the old 1906 Ottoman-era border, forcing Israel's final withdrawal. The handover completed the territorial provisions of the 1979 Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty, closing the last unresolved piece of the Sinai return.

evt-03-19-2003-president-of-the-united-s.scenario: You are watching from the Oval Office broadcast on the evening of 19 March 2003, hours after President Bush's 48-hour ultimatum for Saddam Hussein to leave Iraq has expired.
evt-03-19-2003-president-of-the-united-s.prompt: What does Bush announce in this address to the nation?

choices.text: A last-minute diplomatic deal averting war
The withdrawal of US troops already massed in the Gulf
The launch of military operations to disarm Iraq and remove Saddam Hussein
A new UN Security Council resolution authorizing force

evt-03-19-2003-president-of-the-united-s.butterflyEffect: Within hours, US and coalition forces launched Operation Iraqi Freedom with strikes on Baghdad, beginning the Iraq War. The invasion toppled Saddam Hussein's government within weeks but led to a prolonged insurgency and years of instability that reshaped Middle East politics for a generation.

evt-03-19-2004-konginkangas-bus-disaster.scenario: It's just after 2am on 19 March 2004. You are one of 38 teenagers aboard a bus speeding north along route E75 toward a ski resort when the headlights of an oncoming truck suddenly swing across the centre line.
evt-03-19-2004-konginkangas-bus-disaster.prompt: What causes so many deaths in the moments after the two vehicles collide?

choices.text: A collapsing roof crushes passengers under snow load
The bus catches fire and burns before anyone can escape
The bus skids off an icy bridge into a river
The truck's unsecured paper rolls smash through the bus on impact

evt-03-19-2004-konginkangas-bus-disaster.butterflyEffect: The truck was hauling roughly 61.5 tonnes of paper rolls, which broke loose on impact and were hurled straight through the bus, killing most victims instantly. The disaster, one of Finland's deadliest road accidents, pushed authorities to tighten regulations on securing heavy cargo loads on trucks nationwide.

evt-03-19-2008-grb-080319b.scenario: At 06:12 UTC on 19 March 2008, you're monitoring data from the Swift satellite when it flags a gamma-ray burst in the constellation Boötes so bright it will briefly be visible to the naked eye.
evt-03-19-2008-grb-080319b.prompt: What should observing teams do the instant Swift flags this burst?

choices.text: Ground telescopes worldwide rapidly slew to catch the fading afterglow
Rely only on Swift's onboard camera without further observation
Wait a decade to analyze archived data at leisure
Use only radio telescopes since gamma-rays can't be seen optically

evt-03-19-2008-grb-080319b.butterflyEffect: Telescopes around the world swiftly slewed to catch the fading optical afterglow, confirming it as the most distant object ever seen without a telescope and one of the most luminous events ever recorded. The rapid response became a model for how astronomers coordinate follow-up on rare, brief cosmic flashes.

evt-03-19-2011-libyan-civil-war-2011.scenario: It is 19 March 2011, and you are a French Air Force pilot scrambled under a fresh UN Security Council resolution. Gaddafi's forces are closing in on the rebel stronghold of Benghazi.
evt-03-19-2011-libyan-civil-war-2011.prompt: What is your mission as the first strikes of Opération Harmattan begin?

choices.text: Bomb Tripoli's government ministries
Escort a rebel convoy to the capital
Halt Gaddafi's forces threatening Benghazi's civilians
Evacuate foreign nationals from Libya

evt-03-19-2011-libyan-civil-war-2011.butterflyEffect: French jets struck Gaddafi's armored columns advancing on Benghazi, opening a NATO-led air campaign to enforce the no-fly zone and protect civilians. The intervention tipped the civil war against Gaddafi, who was captured and killed that October, but Libya then spiraled into years of factional conflict.

evt-03-19-2016-flydubai-flight-981.scenario: You are the captain of Flydubai Flight 981, circling above Rostov-on-Don for nearly two hours as thunderstorms and gusting crosswinds have already forced you to abandon two landing attempts. Fuel is running low and the weather shows no sign of easing.
evt-03-19-2016-flydubai-flight-981.prompt: On the third approach, buffeted by wind shear near the runway, what does the crew do?

choices.text: Lands anyway despite the crosswind limits
Executes a go-around, pulling into a steep climb to try again
Diverts immediately to Krasnodar with remaining fuel
Declares an emergency and requests a straight-in landing at Rostov

evt-03-19-2016-flydubai-flight-981.butterflyEffect: The crew executed a go-around, but during the climb the aircraft entered a steep dive from which it never recovered, killing all 62 aboard. Investigators cited pilot fatigue, prolonged manual flying in turbulence, and spatial disorientation, prompting industry-wide reviews of go-around training and rest rules for long-haul crews.

evt-03-19-2016-march-2016-istanbul-bombi.scenario: It's mid-morning on 19 March 2016 and you're walking along İstiklal Avenue, Istanbul's crowded pedestrian shopping street, when a suicide bomber detonates near the district governor's office just ahead of you.
evt-03-19-2016-march-2016-istanbul-bombi.prompt: What did Turkish officials later say about the group behind the bombing?

choices.text: A leftist militant group claimed responsibility
An Armenian nationalist cell was blamed
PKK Kurdish militants carried out the attack
The bomber had links to ISIL

evt-03-19-2016-march-2016-istanbul-bombi.butterflyEffect: Turkey's interior minister confirmed days later that the bomber had links to ISIL. The attack, part of a wave of bombings that year, deepened Turkey's crackdown on ISIL cells and further battered a tourism industry already reeling from repeated attacks.

evt-03-19-2019-president-of-kazakhstan.scenario: You are watching Kazakh state television on the evening of 19 March 2019, when Nursultan Nazarbayev — the only president Kazakhstan has known since independence in 1991 — appears for a sudden, unscheduled address to the nation.

choices.text: His intention to run for a further term in a snap referendum
The appointment of his daughter as his direct successor
His resignation as president, handing power to the Senate speaker
The dissolution of parliament and new elections

evt-03-19-2019-president-of-kazakhstan.butterflyEffect: Nazarbayev resigned the presidency, and under the constitution Senate speaker Kassym-Jomart Tokayev became interim president. The capital Astana was soon renamed Nur-Sultan in his honour, but the arrangement unravelled in 2022 when unrest let Tokayev strip Nazarbayev of his remaining influence and restore the old capital's name.

evt-03-20-1602-dutch-east-india-company.scenario: It's March 20, 1602, in Amsterdam, and you're a merchant deciding whether to put your savings into shares of the newly chartered United East India Company, a merger of rival Dutch trading firms with a 21-year monopoly on Asian trade.
evt-03-20-1602-dutch-east-india-company.prompt: What do you do with your money?

choices.text: Refuse, since Dutch law forbids reselling shares
Wait until the company's charter expires before investing
Invest privately with a Portuguese trading house instead
Buy shares in the world's first publicly tradable joint-stock company

evt-03-20-1602-dutch-east-india-company.butterflyEffect: Investors who bought in gained shares tradable on an open secondary market, which grew into the Amsterdam Stock Exchange. The VOC's model of pooled capital, tradable stock, and quasi-governmental power became the template for the modern multinational corporation.

evt-03-20-1724-pope-innocent-xiii.scenario: It is March 1724, and you are a cardinal locked in conclave in the Sistine Chapel following the death of Pope Innocent XIII. Rival factions favoring French and Habsburg interests have deadlocked the vote for weeks.
evt-03-20-1724-pope-innocent-xiii.prompt: How should the conclave break the deadlock between the great power factions?

choices.text: Formally ask the King of France to select the next pope
Hand the decision to the Holy Roman Emperor's ambassador
Elect a compromise candidate acceptable to neither dominant faction outright
Dissolve the conclave and leave the papacy vacant indefinitely

evt-03-20-1724-pope-innocent-xiii.butterflyEffect: The cardinals eventually settled on a compromise: the reluctant Cardinal Vincenzo Maria Orsini, Archbishop of Benevento, who became Pope Benedict XIII. Devoted to personal piety but weak in governance, he delegated Church finances to his corrupt favorite Cardinal Niccolò Coscia, whose schemes caused scandals that outlasted the pontificate.

evt-03-20-1760-great-boston-fire-of-1760.scenario: It is the night of 20 March 1760, and flames are racing through Boston's crowded wooden buildings toward the harbor. You are a townsman called out to help stop the blaze before it consumes the whole waterfront district.
evt-03-20-1760-great-boston-fire-of-1760.prompt: What should the townspeople do to try to halt the fire's spread?

choices.text: Form bucket brigades and tear down buildings ahead of the fire to create a firebreak
Wait for a change in wind direction before taking any action
Evacuate the town entirely and abandon efforts to fight the fire
Request troops from a neighboring colony to fight the blaze

evt-03-20-1760-great-boston-fire-of-1760.butterflyEffect: Bostonians organized bucket brigades and tore down buildings in the fire's path to create firebreaks, but the flames still destroyed 349 buildings and left over a thousand people homeless. The disaster pushed the town toward stricter building codes favoring brick over wood and spurred the growth of fire insurance in colonial Boston.

evt-03-20-1852-harriet-beecher-stowe.scenario: It is March 1852 and you edit a small anti-slavery newspaper in Boston. An advance copy of a new novel about slavery, written by a minister's daughter from Connecticut, has just landed on your desk.
evt-03-20-1852-harriet-beecher-stowe.prompt: What do you do with Harriet Beecher Stowe's new novel?

choices.text: Bury it in a brief notice, fearing it is too sentimental to matter
Refuse to review it, worried it will alienate moderate readers
Publish only excerpts favorable to Southern planters to avoid controversy
Serialize and champion it in your pages to reach the widest possible audience

evt-03-20-1852-harriet-beecher-stowe.butterflyEffect: Uncle Tom's Cabin became the best-selling novel of the 19th century, selling millions of copies in the US and Britain, hardening Northern abolitionist sentiment while enraging the South. Its emotional depiction of slavery's cruelty is widely credited with reshaping public opinion in the decade before the Civil War.

evt-03-20-1861-1861-mendoza-earthquake.scenario: It is 11:30 at night on 20 March 1861, and the ground beneath Mendoza city suddenly convulses. Your family's adobe house groans around you as walls begin to crack.
evt-03-20-1861-1861-mendoza-earthquake.prompt: What is the safest thing to do right now?

choices.text: Get outside to open ground, away from walls and roofs
Stay inside and brace the doorway until the shaking passes
Climb to the roof to escape falling walls
Shelter under the heaviest furniture in the house

evt-03-20-1861-1861-mendoza-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The quake, one of Argentina's deadliest, leveled most of Mendoza's adobe buildings and killed a large share of the city's population. In the rebuilding that followed, Mendoza was redesigned with wide streets, plazas, and irrigation-fed tree cover to reduce future earthquake and fire risk—a layout the city still keeps today.

evt-03-20-1890-wilhelm-ii.scenario: It is March 1890 in Berlin, and you are a close advisor to the young Kaiser Wilhelm II. The Emperor has clashed repeatedly with his aging chancellor over foreign policy and how to handle the growing socialist movement.
evt-03-20-1890-wilhelm-ii.prompt: What does Wilhelm II decide to do with Chancellor Otto von Bismarck?

choices.text: Send Bismarck abroad as ambassador to Russia
Promote Bismarck to a ceremonial role commanding the army
Force Bismarck's resignation and dismiss him as chancellor
Keep Bismarck in office but strip him of foreign policy duties

evt-03-20-1890-wilhelm-ii.butterflyEffect: Wilhelm II forced Bismarck's resignation, ending nearly three decades of dominance over German policy. Without Bismarck's careful balancing act, Germany's alliance system unraveled—particularly its secret understanding with Russia—setting the stage for the more rigid, confrontational diplomacy that helped push Europe toward the First World War.

evt-03-20-1922-united-states-navy.scenario: It is 20 March 1922, and you stand on the deck of the newly commissioned USS Langley, a converted coal collier now fitted with a flat wooden flight deck. The Navy still isn't sure what role this odd-looking ship should play.
evt-03-20-1922-united-states-navy.prompt: What was USS Langley's intended purpose as the Navy's first carrier?

choices.text: To serve as an experimental and training ship for developing carrier aviation techniques
To be scrapped for parts after a brief ceremonial commissioning
To immediately join the battle fleet as a front-line combat carrier
To transport aircraft to allied nations under a lend-lease style program

evt-03-20-1922-united-states-navy.butterflyEffect: Langley served as an experimental and training platform, nicknamed the "Covered Wagon," where pilots and engineers worked out catapults, arresting gear, and flight-deck operations. Those lessons directly shaped the design of the fleet carriers Lexington and Saratoga, laying the groundwork for American carrier aviation in World War II.

evt-03-20-1923-arts-club-of-chicago.scenario: It's March 20, 1923. You step into the Arts Club of Chicago for the opening of Pablo Picasso's first solo exhibition in the United States, uncertain what to make of his cubist canvases.
evt-03-20-1923-arts-club-of-chicago.prompt: How did this exhibition shape the Arts Club's standing in American art?

choices.text: It was largely ignored by critics and the public
It caused the club to ban future modernist exhibitions
It led the Art Institute to remove all modern works from display
It cemented the club's reputation as a champion of modern art in America

evt-03-20-1923-arts-club-of-chicago.butterflyEffect: The show helped cement Chicago, alongside New York, as a serious venue for European modernism. The Arts Club went on to champion avant-garde artists for decades, shaping American taste for cubism and abstraction long after this single opening night.

evt-03-20-1939-1939-german-ultimatum-to-.scenario: It's March 20, 1939, and as Lithuania's foreign minister you sit across from Joachim von Ribbentrop, who warns that the Wehrmacht will bomb Kaunas unless you hand over the Klaipėda Region within days.
evt-03-20-1939-1939-german-ultimatum-to-.prompt: What do you recommend Lithuania's government do in response to the German ultimatum?

choices.text: Request immediate Soviet military support
Appeal to the League of Nations for armed intervention
Accept the ultimatum to avoid war
Reject the demand and mobilize the Lithuanian army

evt-03-20-1939-1939-german-ultimatum-to-.butterflyEffect: Lithuania accepted the ultimatum on 23 March 1939, becoming the last territorial gain Germany secured before World War II began. The episode, following closely on the occupation of Czechoslovakia, showed the failure of Western appeasement and previewed the pressure tactics Germany would soon use against Poland.

evt-03-20-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 20 March 1944 and you command a Marine landing force preparing to hit Emirau Island in the Bismarcks. Scouting reports suggest the Japanese have abandoned the island entirely, but headquarters still expects a fight.
evt-03-20-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What do you do with your landing plan?

choices.text: Call off the operation and divert forces to reinforce Bougainville
Order a full naval bombardment before any troops go ashore
Land as planned but skip the preliminary bombardment since the island appears undefended
Delay the landing until Rabaul itself is directly assaulted

evt-03-20-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The landing met no resistance, and Marines quickly built an airstrip that helped seal off the huge Japanese base at Rabaul without ever having to assault it directly. Emirau became a textbook example of the 'leapfrogging' strategy that let Allied forces bypass strongpoints and shorten the war in the Pacific.

evt-03-20-1987-antiviral-drug.scenario: It's March 1987, and as a physician treating patients dying of AIDS, you learn the FDA has just approved zidovudine (AZT), the first antiretroviral drug, after unusually fast, limited trials.
evt-03-20-1987-antiviral-drug.prompt: What happens to AIDS treatment in the years that follow this approval?

choices.text: AIDS is declared effectively cured within a year
No further antiretroviral drugs emerge for a decade
The drug is withdrawn immediately after approval
AZT becomes standard care despite toxicity and cost, driving further drug development

evt-03-20-1987-antiviral-drug.butterflyEffect: AZT became standard therapy despite severe side effects and a price tag near $10,000 a year, fueling activism from groups like ACT UP over cost and access. That pressure helped accelerate FDA approval pathways, and by the mid-1990s combination antiretroviral therapy transformed HIV from a near-certain death sentence into a manageable chronic condition.

evt-03-20-1993-the-troubles.scenario: It is 20 March 1993 on Bridge Street in Warrington. A coded IRA warning about bombs hidden in litter bins has just been phoned in, but shoppers, including children, are still crowded along the busy street when the devices explode.
evt-03-20-1993-the-troubles.prompt: What actually followed the deaths of the two children killed in this attack?

choices.text: It had little lasting effect on public opinion or politics
It led directly to an immediate, permanent IRA ceasefire
It caused the British government to withdraw from Northern Ireland talks entirely
The victims' families founded a peace organisation that still works with terrorism victims

evt-03-20-1993-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: Jonathan Ball, aged 3, and Tim Parry, aged 12, died from the blast, and the killings provoked widespread public revulsion on both sides of the Irish Sea. Tim's parents, Colin and Wendy Parry, co-founded the Warrington Peace Centre (later the Foundation for Peace), which still supports victims of terrorism, and the outrage added pressure toward the peace process that led to the 1998 Good Friday Agreement.

evt-03-20-1999-legoland-california.scenario: It's March 20, 1999, in Carlsbad, California, and you're a Lego executive watching the gates swing open on the company's biggest gamble yet: its first theme park built outside Europe.
evt-03-20-1999-legoland-california.prompt: What milestone does today's opening actually represent for the Lego brand?

choices.text: It's the first Legoland owned by Merlin Entertainments
It's the first Legoland to include an aquarium
It's the first Legoland park built outside Europe
It's the largest Legoland park ever built

evt-03-20-1999-legoland-california.butterflyEffect: Legoland California proved the brand could travel, and its success paved the way for Legoland Florida in 2011 and Legoland New York in 2021, cementing theme parks as a permanent arm of the Lego business rather than a one-off European experiment.

evt-03-20-2000-black-panther-party.scenario: It's March 20, 2000, in Atlanta's West End, and you are a Fulton County sheriff's deputy trying to serve a routine warrant on Jamil Al-Amin, the store owner once known as H. Rap Brown during his years as a Black Panther and radical activist.
evt-03-20-2000-black-panther-party.prompt: What happens when Al-Amin responds to the warrant with gunfire?

choices.text: He is arrested peacefully after a brief standoff
He turns the gun on himself before deputies can react
He opens fire, killing one deputy and wounding the other
He surrenders immediately without incident

evt-03-20-2000-black-panther-party.butterflyEffect: Al-Amin killed one deputy and wounded another before fleeing, and was captured days later in Alabama. Convicted of murder in 2002, he was sentenced to life without parole, closing the final chapter on one of the Black Power era's most notorious figures.

evt-03-20-2003-2003-invasion-of-iraq.scenario: It's March 20, 2003. As part of the US-led coalition crossing into Iraq, you've been told the mission is to disarm Saddam Hussein of weapons of mass destruction before he can use them.
evt-03-20-2003-2003-invasion-of-iraq.prompt: What did coalition forces ultimately conclude about Iraq's WMD program?

choices.text: Biological weapons were discovered in Saddam's palaces
A massive chemical weapons stockpile was uncovered near Baghdad
Nuclear warheads were found hidden in the desert
No weapons of mass destruction were ever found

evt-03-20-2003-2003-invasion-of-iraq.butterflyEffect: No weapons of mass destruction were ever found, discrediting the invasion's central justification. The fallout fueled a prolonged insurgency and sectarian violence in Iraq and left a lasting legacy of distrust in the intelligence used to justify the war.

evt-03-20-2010-eyjafjallajokull.scenario: It is 20 March 2010 and a fissure has opened on the Fimmvörðuháls ridge near Eyjafjallajökull, throwing up lava fountains but no ash. Icelandic authorities must decide how to handle the crowds already driving toward the glow.
evt-03-20-2010-eyjafjallajokull.prompt: How do officials respond to this first, non-explosive eruption?

choices.text: Evacuate the entire region immediately as if for a major explosive eruption
Restrict access to a safe viewing perimeter but allow controlled tourism
Ignore the eruption since it poses no threat to aviation
Close all Icelandic airspace as a precaution

evt-03-20-2010-eyjafjallajokull.butterflyEffect: This effusive opening phase drew sightseers and became known as a 'tourist eruption,' with little disruption beyond local road closures. Weeks later, though, the eruption shifted beneath the ice cap itself, turning explosive and sending an ash plume that grounded flights across Europe for days.

evt-03-20-2014-taliban.scenario: It's the evening of 20 March 2014, days before Afghanistan's presidential election, and you are a security guard at Kabul's Serena Hotel as four well-dressed young men walk in for a Nowruz gathering, guns hidden in their clothing.
evt-03-20-2014-taliban.prompt: What happens once the men pull out their weapons and open fire on the guests?

choices.text: Hotel guards fight back and kill all four attackers
International troops storm the hotel to end a hostage standoff
Afghan police negotiate their peaceful surrender
The gunmen escape into the night undetected

evt-03-20-2014-taliban.butterflyEffect: Hotel guards eventually killed all four gunmen in the ensuing gunfight, but not before nine people died, including AFP journalist Sardar Ahmad, his wife, and two of their children. The Taliban claimed the attack as a warning against the coming vote, prompting tightened security around the election and renewed international alarm over violence against journalists in Afghanistan.

evt-03-20-2015-syrian-civil-war.scenario: It is early 2015 and you fight with the YPG defending Kobanî, a Kurdish city besieged for months by Islamic State fighters. Coalition warplanes now circle overhead, waiting for targets your ground reports can supply.
evt-03-20-2015-syrian-civil-war.prompt: How do you finally break the siege?

choices.text: Coordinate ground positions with coalition airstrikes to grind down ISIS lines
Wait for Assad's army to relieve the siege from the south
Abandon the city and regroup across the Turkish border
Negotiate a local truce with ISIS commanders to spare civilians

evt-03-20-2015-syrian-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Kurdish fighters, guided by US-led coalition airstrikes, drove ISIS out of Kobanî by late March 1915— becoming the war's first major setback for the group. The victory cemented the US-YPG partnership that would anchor the later Syrian Democratic Forces campaign against ISIS.

evt-03-20-2019-kassym-jomart-tokayev.scenario: It is 20 March 2019. Nursultan Nazarbayev shocked the nation by resigning as president after nearly three decades in power, and as Senate chairman, you are next in the constitutional line. You are sworn in as acting president of Kazakhstan.
evt-03-20-2019-kassym-jomart-tokayev.prompt: What was one of Tokayev's first notable acts as acting president?

choices.text: He announced Kazakhstan would leave the Eurasian Economic Union
He ordered Nazarbayev's arrest on corruption charges
He called for the immediate dissolution of parliament
He proposed renaming the capital city in Nazarbayev's honor

evt-03-20-2019-kassym-jomart-tokayev.butterflyEffect: Tokayev proposed renaming the capital, Astana, to Nur-Sultan in honor of Nazarbayev, a move parliament quickly approved. The name stuck until January 2022, when, after deadly unrest weakened Nazarbayev's continuing influence, Tokayev consolidated his own authority and the capital was renamed back to Astana.

evt-03-21-1556-thomas-cranmer.scenario: It is March 21, 1556, in Oxford. You stand among the crowd as Thomas Cranmer, having already signed several recantations of his Protestant faith to save his life, is led out to the stake to be burned.
evt-03-21-1556-thomas-cranmer.prompt: What did Cranmer do at the stake that stunned onlookers?

choices.text: He begged Queen Mary for a last-minute pardon
He converted sincerely to Catholicism and prayed to the Virgin Mary
He publicly renounced his recantations and reaffirmed his Protestant faith before the flames
He remained completely silent throughout the execution

evt-03-21-1556-thomas-cranmer.butterflyEffect: Rather than dying as a repentant Catholic, Cranmer publicly renounced his recantations and reaffirmed his Protestant beliefs, reportedly thrusting the hand that had signed them into the flames first. His defiant end turned him into a Protestant martyr, later immortalized in Foxe's Book of Martyrs and helping cement Protestant identity in England for centuries.

evt-03-21-1788-great-new-orleans-fire-17.scenario: You watch from a doorway on Good Friday, 1788, as flames tear through the wooden buildings of Spanish-controlled New Orleans, consuming block after block of the Vieux Carré.
evt-03-21-1788-great-new-orleans-fire-17.prompt: How did colonial authorities change building rules after the devastation?

choices.text: Required new buildings to use masonry and tile roofs
Banned any new construction near the river
Relocated the entire settlement to higher ground
Rebuilt the city exactly as it had been, in wood

evt-03-21-1788-great-new-orleans-fire-17.butterflyEffect: Spanish officials mandated brick or stucco construction with tile or slate roofs to prevent future infernos. This building code, reinforced after a second major fire in 1794, gave the French Quarter its enduring Spanish colonial architecture, despite its French name.

evt-03-21-1861-alexander-h-stephens.scenario: It is March 21, 1861, in Savannah, Georgia. You stand in the crowd as newly sworn Confederate Vice President Alexander Stephens rises to explain, in plain terms, what truly separates the new Confederacy from the Union.
evt-03-21-1861-alexander-h-stephens.prompt: What did Stephens declare as the "cornerstone" of the Confederate government?

choices.text: Agricultural self-sufficiency free from Northern industry
The need for a strong, centralized Confederate government
The states' right to nullify unfair federal tariffs
The doctrine that Black people were inherently unequal and slavery was their natural, permanent condition

evt-03-21-1861-alexander-h-stephens.butterflyEffect: Stephens stated bluntly that the Confederacy rested on the principle that Black people were not equal to white people and that slavery was their natural condition, rejecting the Declaration of Independence's ideal of equality. The speech became one of the most quoted pieces of evidence for the Confederacy's founding purpose, cited for generations in debates over the Civil War's causes.

evt-03-21-1913-great-dayton-flood.scenario: You are a Dayton, Ohio business leader in the weeks after the March 1913 flood devastated the city, surveying ruined streets and knowing the Great Miami River could flood again without lasting protection.
evt-03-21-1913-great-dayton-flood.prompt: What long-term measure do you push the city to adopt?

choices.text: Rebuild exactly as before and rely on future luck
Relocate the entire city to higher ground
Raise levees only around the downtown business district
Build a system of upstream dry dams and floodways

evt-03-21-1913-great-dayton-flood.butterflyEffect: Engineer Arthur Morgan helped local leaders raise private funds to create the Miami Conservancy District, building a system of dry dams, levees, and floodways completed by 1922. It became one of the first major flood-control districts in the country and a model later studied in designing the Tennessee Valley Authority.

evt-03-21-1918-world-war-i.scenario: It is dawn on 21 March 1918, and you are a German stormtrooper crouched behind a rolling artillery barrage on the Western Front, ordered to break through British lines at the opening of Operation Michael.
evt-03-21-1918-world-war-i.prompt: What tactic do you use to exploit the breakthrough?

choices.text: Wait behind the lines for tank support to arrive
Advance in tight, disciplined waves across open ground
Infiltrate through gaps and bypass enemy strongpoints
Attempt to negotiate a local ceasefire with British troops

evt-03-21-1918-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: German infiltration tactics achieved the war's first major breakthrough since 1914, pushing Allied lines back nearly 40 miles. But overstretched supply lines and exhausted troops stalled the advance within weeks, and the offensive's failure left Germany spent, opening the door to the Allied Hundred Days Offensive that ended the war that November.

evt-03-21-1937-blanton-winship.scenario: It is Palm Sunday, March 21, 1937, in Ponce, Puerto Rico. You are marching with the Nationalist Party parade when police, acting under Governor Blanton Winship's orders, move to block your unpermitted march.
evt-03-21-1937-blanton-winship.prompt: What followed as the police confronted the unarmed marchers?

choices.text: Marchers were peacefully arrested and released the same day
Police opened fire on the crowd
The parade was allowed to continue without incident
The governor personally intervened to negotiate a truce

evt-03-21-1937-blanton-winship.butterflyEffect: Police opened fire on the crowd of marchers and bystanders, killing and wounding dozens in what became known as the Ponce massacre. A later U.S. Commission on Civil Rights investigation held Winship responsible, and the massacre became a rallying point for Puerto Rican independence movements for decades afterward.

evt-03-21-1952-moondog-coronation-ball.scenario: You've bought a ticket for Alan Freed's rock and roll show at Cleveland Arena on March 21, 1952, but thousands more people than the arena can hold are pushing through the doors with you.
evt-03-21-1952-moondog-coronation-ball.prompt: What happened to the show almost as soon as it began?

choices.text: It was cancelled beforehand due to a snowstorm
It was shut down by police due to overcrowding
The headliner refused to take the stage
It ran successfully through the entire night as planned

evt-03-21-1952-moondog-coronation-ball.butterflyEffect: Massive overselling caused dangerous overcrowding, and police shut the concert down after only one song. Despite its abrupt end, the Moondog Coronation Ball is remembered as the first major rock and roll concert, cementing disc jockey Alan Freed's role in bringing the genre to a wider audience.

evt-03-21-1963-federal-bureau-of-prisons.scenario: You are a guard on Alcatraz Island on March 21, 1963, watching the last inmates being ferried off to the mainland as the Federal Bureau of Prisons shuts the facility down for good.
evt-03-21-1963-federal-bureau-of-prisons.prompt: Why did the Bureau close the notorious Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary?

choices.text: The prison's population had dropped to zero inmates
A major fire destroyed most of the cellblocks
The deteriorating, isolated facility had become too expensive to keep running
A successful escape proved the island wasn't truly escape-proof, forcing closure

evt-03-21-1963-federal-bureau-of-prisons.butterflyEffect: The isolated island facility had grown far too costly to operate and maintain compared to newer federal prisons, and its crumbling infrastructure made continued use impractical. Decommissioned, Alcatraz was later opened to the public and became one of America's most visited historic sites, its legend fueling books and films for decades.

evt-03-21-1968-war-of-attrition.scenario: You are dug in at the Karameh refugee camp in Jordan on March 21, 1968, as Israeli tanks and paratroopers cross the border to strike Fatah bases in retaliation for cross-border attacks.
evt-03-21-1968-war-of-attrition.prompt: What was the immediate political outcome as Fatah and Jordanian forces resisted the Israeli assault?

choices.text: Despite heavy losses, the stand at Karameh became hailed as a moral victory, boosting Palestinian nationalism and Fatah's recruitment
The camp surrendered immediately without any fighting
Israeli forces were fully repelled without suffering any losses
Jordan formally declared full-scale war on Israel afterward

evt-03-21-1968-war-of-attrition.butterflyEffect: Though Israeli forces inflicted heavy losses and largely destroyed the camp, the fierce resistance turned Karameh into a symbolic moral victory for Palestinian nationalism. Recruitment to Fatah surged afterward, and Yasser Arafat's stature grew dramatically, reshaping leadership within the PLO in the years that followed.

evt-03-21-1980-cold-war.scenario: It is March 1980, three months after Soviet tanks rolled into Afghanistan. You are part of President Carter's team weighing how to respond as the Moscow Summer Olympics approach.
evt-03-21-1980-cold-war.prompt: What does Carter announce regarding U.S. participation in the Moscow Olympics?

choices.text: Boycotting only the opening ceremony while athletes compete
A full U.S. boycott of the Moscow Olympics
Quiet diplomatic protests while still attending fully
Sending only a small symbolic delegation without athletes

evt-03-21-1980-cold-war.butterflyEffect: Carter announced a full U.S. boycott of the 1980 Moscow Games, eventually joined by roughly 65 other nations. The Soviet Union retaliated by leading an Eastern Bloc boycott of the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, deepening Cold War divisions and politicizing the Games for years afterward.

evt-03-21-1990-namibia.scenario: You stand in a stadium in Windhoek on 21 March 1990 as the South African flag comes down after 75 years of rule and a new Namibian flag is raised before a cheering crowd and international dignitaries.
evt-03-21-1990-namibia.prompt: Who is sworn in as Namibia's first president at this ceremony?

choices.text: Robert Mugabe
Sam Nujoma
Hendrik Verwoerd
P.W. Botha

evt-03-21-1990-namibia.butterflyEffect: Sam Nujoma, longtime leader of SWAPO's liberation struggle, took office as Namibia's first president. His government pursued national reconciliation rather than reprisals against former rulers, and Namibia went on to become one of postcolonial Africa's more stable democracies, though land reform and inequality remained long-term challenges.

evt-03-21-1994-united-nations-framework-.scenario: You are a UN treaty official in early 1994, tracking ratifications of the new climate convention signed at the 1992 Earth Summit. Nations are slowly depositing their instruments of ratification.
evt-03-21-1994-united-nations-framework-.prompt: What triggers the treaty's formal entry into force under its own rules?

choices.text: The UN Security Council votes unanimously to approve it
The UN Secretary-General personally signs it into force
The 50th state deposits its ratification, starting a 90-day countdown
Only the G7 industrialized nations need to ratify it

evt-03-21-1994-united-nations-framework-.butterflyEffect: The convention entered into force 90 days after the 50th state ratified it, in March 1994. This created the legal foundation for the annual Conference of the Parties (COP) meetings, which later produced the 1997 Kyoto Protocol and the 2015 Paris Agreement.

evt-03-21-1999-bertrand-piccard.scenario: It is 21 March 1999, and you are piloting the Breitling Orbiter 3 over the Egyptian desert after nearly three weeks aloft, propane reserves dangerously low, needing to bring the first non-stop round-the-world balloon flight to a safe end.
evt-03-21-1999-bertrand-piccard.prompt: What do you do to complete the flight successfully?

choices.text: Push on toward Switzerland despite the shortage
Divert south toward Saudi Arabia for more fuel
Ditch the gondola into the Nile River
Land the balloon in the Egyptian desert

evt-03-21-1999-bertrand-piccard.butterflyEffect: Piccard and Jones landed in the Egyptian desert near Mut after 19 days aloft, completing the first non-stop circumnavigation of the globe by balloon. The achievement helped inspire Piccard's later Solar Impulse project, which in 2016 completed the first round-the-world flight by a solar-powered aircraft.

evt-03-21-2000-pope-john-paul-ii.scenario: You stand among the crowd at the Western Wall in Jerusalem, March 2000, as Pope John Paul II approaches the ancient stones on his historic first papal visit to Israel.
evt-03-21-2000-pope-john-paul-ii.prompt: What did the Pope do at the Western Wall that became a lasting symbol?

choices.text: He declined to approach the wall for security reasons
He inserted a written prayer into a crack in the wall
He requested a private audience away from cameras
He delivered a formal speech condemning Israeli policy

evt-03-21-2000-pope-john-paul-ii.butterflyEffect: He tucked a handwritten prayer into a crack in the wall, asking God's forgiveness for the sins of Christians against Jews throughout history. The gesture, following his earlier visit to Yad Vashem, became one of the most powerful images of Catholic-Jewish reconciliation and reshaped the Church's relationship with Israel and the Jewish people.

evt-03-21-2006-phra-phrom.scenario: You are a vendor near Bangkok's Erawan Shrine on the evening of 21 March 2006 when a man suddenly grabs a hammer and begins smashing the golden statue of Phra Phrom, the revered deity of fortune, in front of stunned worshippers.
evt-03-21-2006-phra-phrom.prompt: What happens to the attacker in the chaotic moments that follow?

choices.text: Furious bystanders beat him to death on the spot
Shrine guards restrain him until officials arrive unharmed
He escapes into the crowded street and vanishes
Police calmly arrest him and lead him away

evt-03-21-2006-phra-phrom.butterflyEffect: Enraged bystanders, many of them daily worshippers at the shrine, beat the man to death within minutes. Thai authorities commissioned a replacement statue that was installed within weeks, and the incident sparked national debate about mental illness, religious devotion, and mob justice in Thailand.

evt-03-21-2006-jack-dorsey.scenario: You're at Odeo's San Francisco office on March 21, 2006, watching co-founder Jack Dorsey type out the very first message on a new platform he calls Twitter.
evt-03-21-2006-jack-dorsey.prompt: What did Dorsey's first-ever tweet actually say?

choices.text: "What are you doing?"
"just setting up my twttr"
"Twitter is live!"
"Hello world"

evt-03-21-2006-jack-dorsey.butterflyEffect: Dorsey's message read simply "just setting up my twttr," marking the birth of microblogging as a format. Twitter would grow into a dominant platform reshaping journalism, politics, and activism worldwide, though Dorsey's plain founding message remains one of the most quoted lines in internet history.

evt-03-21-2006-social-media.scenario: It is March 2006 inside the Odeo offices in San Francisco. You are part of a small team, including Jack Dorsey, brainstorming a new way for people to share quick updates with friends.
evt-03-21-2006-social-media.prompt: What core feature do the founders settle on for their new service?

choices.text: An anonymous discussion forum for local news
Short 140-character text updates modeled on SMS messages
An email newsletter service for group updates
A video-sharing platform for short clips

evt-03-21-2006-social-media.butterflyEffect: The team built short, public status updates limited to 140 characters, mirroring the constraints of SMS text messages, and launched it as Twttr. That simple format grew into Twitter, reshaping journalism, political discourse, and real-time public communication worldwide.

evt-03-21-2022-china-eastern-airlines-fl.scenario: It is 21 March 2022, hours after China Eastern Flight 5735 has gone down in Guangxi. You are an aviation safety regulator in Beijing deciding how to respond while the cause remains unknown.
evt-03-21-2022-china-eastern-airlines-fl.prompt: What immediate step do Chinese aviation authorities take with the airline's fleet?

choices.text: Continue all flights while awaiting the final report
Immediately blame the flight crew before any investigation
Temporarily ground the airline's entire 737-800 fleet
Ground only the specific aircraft involved, nothing else

evt-03-21-2022-china-eastern-airlines-fl.butterflyEffect: China Eastern voluntarily grounded its entire fleet of Boeing 737-800 aircraft as a precaution while investigators examined the wreckage and flight recorders. The crash drew intense international scrutiny over data-sharing during the investigation and renewed global attention to 737-800 safety records.

evt-03-22-1638-anne-hutchinson.scenario: It is 1637, and you stand before Massachusetts Bay's magistrates, including Governor John Winthrop, accused of holding home meetings that challenge the colony's Puritan ministers on salvation and grace.
evt-03-22-1638-anne-hutchinson.prompt: When pressed to recant your teachings to avoid banishment, what do you do?

choices.text: Defend your views, insisting on direct revelation from God
Apologize and recant to remain in the colony
Flee immediately to Rhode Island before the verdict
Appeal directly to the King of England for protection

evt-03-22-1638-anne-hutchinson.butterflyEffect: Hutchinson refused to recant, was convicted, and was banished from the colony with many of her followers in 1638. She resettled first in Rhode Island and later New Netherland, where she was killed in 1643, but her defiant stand became an early landmark in colonial disputes over religious liberty and women's authority to interpret scripture publicly.

evt-03-22-1765-parliament-of-great-brita.scenario: You run a print shop in Boston in the spring of 1765. Parliament has just passed the Stamp Act, requiring a tax stamp on newspapers, legal documents, and even playing cards throughout the American colonies.
evt-03-22-1765-parliament-of-great-brita.prompt: How do many colonists respond to the new tax?

choices.text: Petition the king through official channels alone and take no other action
Quietly pay the tax to avoid confrontation with London
Organize boycotts of British goods and send delegates to a Stamp Act Congress
Immediately declare independence from Britain

evt-03-22-1765-parliament-of-great-brita.butterflyEffect: Widespread boycotts, the Stamp Act Congress, and Sons of Liberty protests forced Parliament to repeal the act in 1766. But Parliament simultaneously passed the Declaratory Act asserting its full authority over the colonies, setting the two sides on a collision course toward revolution.

evt-03-22-1784-emerald-buddha.scenario: It's 1784, and you are a courtier attending King Rama I's newly founded capital of Bangkok, where a small emerald-green Buddha image is about to be installed in a purpose-built royal temple.
evt-03-22-1784-emerald-buddha.prompt: What is King Rama I doing by enshrining this image at the new capital?

choices.text: Melting it down to fund the new capital's construction
Hiding it from Burmese forces before a planned relocation
Establishing the Emerald Buddha as Thailand's sacred palladium in the Grand Palace's temple
Sending it as a diplomatic gift to a neighboring kingdom

evt-03-22-1784-emerald-buddha.butterflyEffect: The Emerald Buddha's installation at Wat Phra Kaew tied the legitimacy of the new Chakri dynasty to possession of the sacred image, a role it retains today as the kingdom's most revered object. Thai monarchs have since ceremonially changed its robes each season, a ritual that continues to reinforce royal spiritual authority.

evt-03-22-1794-slave-trade-act-of-1794.scenario: It is March 1794, and you inspect ships at a busy American port. One vessel being fitted with shackles and extra water casks is rumored to be bound for the West African coast to load a cargo of enslaved people.
evt-03-22-1794-slave-trade-act-of-1794.prompt: Under the law President Washington just signed, what must you do?

choices.text: Allow departure as long as it doesn't dock again in a Southern state
Let it sail, since the ban only applies to ships flying foreign flags
Seize the ship and report it, since outfitting a vessel for the slave trade is now illegal
Do nothing unless enslaved people are already loaded aboard

evt-03-22-1794-slave-trade-act-of-1794.butterflyEffect: The Slave Trade Act of 1794 was the first federal law restricting the trade, banning the building or outfitting of ships for slave trafficking from U.S. ports, though it stopped short of banning the trade itself. It laid groundwork for a stronger 1800 act and the eventual 1808 constitutional ban on the international slave trade.

evt-03-22-1871-william-woods-holden.scenario: You are a North Carolina state senator in March 1871, sitting in judgment of Governor William Holden, who declared martial law and sent militia against Klan violence in Alamance and Caswell counties without following ordinary legal channels.
evt-03-22-1871-william-woods-holden.prompt: How does the impeachment trial conclude?

choices.text: He resigns before a vote can be taken
The trial is postponed indefinitely for lack of evidence
He is acquitted for acting out of necessity against the Klan
The senate convicts him and removes him from office

evt-03-22-1871-william-woods-holden.butterflyEffect: Holden was convicted and removed from office on March 22, 1871, becoming the first U.S. governor ever ousted by impeachment. His removal was a major setback for Reconstruction-era efforts to suppress Klan terrorism, emboldening white supremacist violence across the South in the years that followed.

evt-03-22-1896-charilaos-vasilakos.scenario: It is March 1896, days before the first modern Olympics open in Athens. You are one of the Greek runners chosen for a trial race over the roughly 40km route from Marathon to Athens, staged to prove the untested distance can even be survived.
evt-03-22-1896-charilaos-vasilakos.prompt: What happens after you and your fellow competitor Charilaos Vasilakos finish the trial run?

choices.text: Organizers shorten the Olympic race to half the trial's distance
The trial's success convinces organizers to include a marathon in the Olympic Games
The distance is judged too dangerous and the event is dropped entirely
Vasilakos is disqualified from the real Olympics for having run the trial

evt-03-22-1896-charilaos-vasilakos.butterflyEffect: Vasilakos's successful finish reassured organizers that the marathon distance was survivable, so it was added to the Olympic program. Weeks later Spyridon Louis won the real Olympic marathon before a jubilant Athens crowd, and the race became the most celebrated event of the Games, cementing the marathon's place in Olympic and modern running culture worldwide.

evt-03-22-1913-phan-xich-long.scenario: It's March 1913, and you are one of Phan Xích Long's followers in Saigon, clutching a bottle of a potion he promised would make you invisible before you plant a bomb outside a colonial building.
evt-03-22-1913-phan-xich-long.prompt: What happens when you carry out the attack?

choices.text: French troops mutiny and join the uprising
The bomb fails to detonate and French police arrest you
The bomb destroys the building and sparks a citywide uprising
The potion works and you escape undetected

evt-03-22-1913-phan-xich-long.butterflyEffect: None of the bombs planted that night exploded, and French authorities quickly rounded up the plotters, including Phan Xích Long himself. He remained imprisoned until his execution in 1916, but his millenarian uprising fed into a broader tradition of secret anti-colonial societies in Cochinchina.

evt-03-22-1934-golf.scenario: You're one of the golfers teeing off at Bobby Jones's new invitational tournament at his Augusta National Golf Club in Georgia, in the spring of 1934.
evt-03-22-1934-golf.prompt: Who wins this inaugural tournament, later renamed the Masters?

choices.text: Bobby Jones
Gene Sarazen
Craig Wood
Horton Smith

evt-03-22-1934-golf.butterflyEffect: Horton Smith won the first Augusta National Invitation Tournament in 1934. It was officially renamed the Masters Tournament in 1939 and grew into one of golf's four major championships, with Augusta National becoming synonymous with the sport's most storied event.

evt-03-22-1943-deutscher-kurzwellensende.scenario: It's 1943 and you're a U-boat radio operator on patrol in the mid-Atlantic, catching a strong signal playing German dance hits mixed with startlingly detailed war news.
evt-03-22-1943-deutscher-kurzwellensende.prompt: What should you suspect about this broadcast?

choices.text: It's an official Kriegsmarine morale broadcast
It's a British black propaganda station posing as a legitimate German broadcaster
It's American Armed Forces Radio testing new frequencies
It's a neutral Swiss relay station

evt-03-22-1943-deutscher-kurzwellensende.butterflyEffect: The station was in fact Deutscher Kurzwellensender Atlantik, run by Sefton Delmer's Political Warfare Executive from Britain, designed to erode U-boat crews' morale by convincing them the Allies already knew their operations. Its success helped establish a template for later black propaganda broadcasting aimed at closed societies.

evt-03-22-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It's March 22, 1943, and you are a villager in Khatyn as German security forces, having lost men to a nearby partisan ambush, surround the settlement and order everyone into a large barn.
evt-03-22-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What did such German reprisal operations typically do to villages suspected of aiding partisans?

choices.text: Deport the residents to labor camps but spare the buildings
Negotiate with partisans for the village's safety
Burn the village and kill nearly its entire population
Fine the village and confiscate livestock

evt-03-22-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Khatyn was one of thousands of Belarusian villages destroyed in Nazi reprisals, and its near-total destruction came to symbolize the fate of rural Belarus under occupation. In 1969 the Soviet Union built the Khatyn Memorial Complex on the site, dedicating it to all Belarusian villages annihilated during the war.

evt-03-22-1992-usair-flight-405.scenario: It is a snowy night at LaGuardia on March 22, 1992. You are part of the flight crew of USAir 405, sitting through a long ground delay before your turn to depart for Cleveland, snow still settling on the wings.
evt-03-22-1992-usair-flight-405.prompt: What decision before takeoff proves fatal for Flight 405?

choices.text: They request a heavier aircraft with more powerful engines
They take off without re-deicing despite the lengthy delay in snow
They delay takeoff another hour for a full second deicing
They divert to a different, drier airport

evt-03-22-1992-usair-flight-405.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew took off without a second deicing after a long snowy ground delay, leaving ice on the wings that robbed the aircraft of lift on rotation. The crash led to reforms in holdover-time guidance, requiring airlines to re-deice aircraft after lengthy delays in icing conditions.

evt-03-22-1995-astronaut.scenario: It's March 22, 1995, and you are part of the Mir ground control team preparing to receive cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov, who has just spent over a year continuously in orbit.
evt-03-22-1995-astronaut.prompt: What record does Polyakov's flight set upon landing?

choices.text: Longest single human spaceflight in history, at nearly 438 days
First spacewalk lasting over eight hours
First crewed flight to dock with an American shuttle
Longest cumulative time in space across multiple missions

evt-03-22-1995-astronaut.butterflyEffect: Polyakov's roughly 437-day mission aboard Mir remains the longest continuous human spaceflight ever recorded, demonstrating that astronauts could endure the physiological demands of a multi-year deep-space mission. His medical data became a key reference point for later long-duration planning on the International Space Station and for future Mars mission concepts.

evt-03-22-2014-2014-oso-landslide.scenario: It is late morning on March 22, 2014. You are a firefighter arriving at a debris field east of Oso, Washington, where a hillside has just collapsed onto a rural neighborhood along the Stillaguamish River.
evt-03-22-2014-2014-oso-landslide.prompt: What is the immediate priority for responders at the scene?

choices.text: Search the debris field for survivors trapped in mud and wreckage
Wait for structural engineers to certify the hillside is fully stable before entering
Begin cataloguing destroyed properties for insurance purposes
Focus solely on evacuating homes farther downstream

evt-03-22-2014-2014-oso-landslide.butterflyEffect: Rescuers faced days of unstable, waterlogged debris that hampered search efforts, and 43 people ultimately died, making it the deadliest landslide in U.S. history. The disaster pushed Washington State to expand lidar-based landslide-hazard mapping and tighten disclosure rules for building near known slide zones.

evt-03-22-2017-2017-westminster-attack.scenario: You are an unarmed police officer on duty at the gates of the Palace of Westminster on March 22, 2017, when a car smashes through the perimeter fence and a knife-wielding man runs straight at you.
evt-03-22-2017-2017-westminster-attack.prompt: What happens in the confrontation that follows at the gates?

choices.text: You retreat, allowing him to flee into Parliament unchecked
He fatally stabs you before being shot dead by an armed officer
He surrenders as soon as he sees armed police
You subdue him with a baton before he can strike

evt-03-22-2017-2017-westminster-attack.butterflyEffect: PC Keith Palmer was fatally stabbed defending the unfortified pedestrian entrance before an armed officer shot the attacker dead. His death triggered a major review of Parliament's security, new barriers around the grounds, and renewed debate over routinely arming officers who guard the building.

evt-03-22-2019-mueller-special-counsel-i.scenario: It is March 22, 2019. You are Attorney General William Barr, and Special Counsel Robert Mueller has just delivered his confidential final report on Russian interference in the 2016 election to your office.
evt-03-22-2019-mueller-special-counsel-i.prompt: What do you do before the public sees any part of Mueller's findings?

choices.text: Seal the report indefinitely under executive privilege
Write your own summary letter characterizing the findings before releasing the report
Release the full report to the public immediately, unedited
Forward it directly to Congress without review

evt-03-22-2019-mueller-special-counsel-i.butterflyEffect: Barr issued a four-page letter summarizing what he called Mueller's 'principal conclusions' days before the redacted report itself was released. Critics argued the letter mischaracterized Mueller's more cautious findings on obstruction of justice, fueling years of political dispute over how the investigation's results were first presented to the public.

evt-03-22-2020-kyriakos-mitsotakis.scenario: It is late March 2020 in Athens. Coronavirus cases are climbing across Europe, and Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis is about to address the nation on television.
evt-03-22-2020-kyriakos-mitsotakis.prompt: What does Mitsotakis announce for Greece?

choices.text: A total closure of Greece's borders with no domestic restrictions
The closure of schools only, with businesses remaining open
A voluntary curfew with no legal enforcement
A nationwide lockdown restricting movement and closing nonessential businesses

evt-03-22-2020-kyriakos-mitsotakis.butterflyEffect: Mitsotakis ordered a strict nationwide lockdown, one of the earliest and firmest in Europe, restricting movement and closing nonessential businesses. The swift action helped Greece keep its initial COVID-19 death toll among the lowest in Europe, though the shutdown devastated its tourism-dependent economy.

evt-03-22-2021-2021-boulder-shooting.scenario: You are a Boulder police officer racing to a King Soopers supermarket on March 22, 2021, after reports of gunfire. Officers converge and manage to wound and arrest the shooter, a 21-year-old local man.
evt-03-22-2021-2021-boulder-shooting.prompt: What happens to the shooter in the years after his arrest?
