choices.text: He is found mentally incompetent for years before eventually standing trial
He is executed within months of the shooting
He escapes custody during a hospital transfer
He is acquitted due to lack of evidence

evt-03-22-2021-2021-boulder-shooting.butterflyEffect: Ahmad Al-Issa was repeatedly ruled mentally incompetent to stand trial in 2021 and 2022, delaying the case for years. He was finally found competent in 2023, convicted in September 2024, and sentenced to life without parole, one of the longest gaps between a mass shooting and conviction in recent U.S. history.

evt-03-22-2024-crocus-city-hall-attack.scenario: You are a Moscow-area emergency responder arriving at Crocus City Hall on the night of March 22, 2024, as smoke pours from the venue where gunmen have opened fire and set the building alight.
evt-03-22-2024-crocus-city-hall-attack.prompt: Despite ISIS-Khorasan Province publicly claiming the attack, what did Russian officials suggest instead?

choices.text: That Ukraine and its intelligence services were involved
That a domestic anti-government militia was responsible
That no organized group was behind it at all
That a private security contractor staged the attack

evt-03-22-2024-crocus-city-hall-attack.butterflyEffect: President Putin and other officials pointed toward a Ukrainian connection without presenting evidence, a claim Kyiv firmly denied even as ISIS-K's claim stood. The attack deepened Russian rhetoric tying the Ukraine war to terrorism and led to tightened security screening at concert venues and public gathering spaces across the country.

evt-03-23-1400-tran-dynasty.scenario: You are a minister at the Đại Việt court in 1400, watching the powerful regent Hồ Quý Ly force the abdication of the child emperor he installed only two years before.
evt-03-23-1400-tran-dynasty.prompt: What does Hồ Quý Ly do once the last Trần emperor abdicates?

choices.text: Flees south to seek refuge in Champa
Restores a surviving Trần prince to the throne
Proclaims himself emperor, founding a new dynasty
Submits Đại Việt as a tributary province to Ming China

evt-03-23-1400-tran-dynasty.butterflyEffect: Hồ Quý Ly founded the short-lived Hồ dynasty, ending 175 years of Trần rule. His usurpation and sweeping reforms alienated the old nobility, weakening Đại Việt's defenses just as Ming China invaded in 1406, leading to a two-decade Ming occupation until Lê Lợi's rebellion restored independence.

evt-03-23-1775-american-revolution.scenario: It is March 23, 1775, and you sit among the delegates at Virginia's revolutionary convention in Richmond, listening to Patrick Henry's fiery closing words demanding action against the Crown.
evt-03-23-1775-american-revolution.prompt: What does the Virginia convention resolve to do after Henry's speech?

choices.text: Apologize to Parliament for prior unrest
Arm and organize Virginia's militia for defense
Send a formal petition seeking reconciliation with the King
Disband the convention to avoid provoking Britain

evt-03-23-1775-american-revolution.butterflyEffect: The convention voted to arm and train Virginia's militia for defense, a decision that put the colony on a war footing just weeks before fighting erupted at Lexington and Concord. Henry's speech became one of the Revolution's most enduring rallying cries, quoted for generations as a symbol of colonial defiance.

evt-03-23-1839-1839-ava-earthquake.scenario: You are a courtier in the royal city of Ava in March 1839 as the ground heaves violently, toppling pagodas and palace walls across the Burmese capital.
evt-03-23-1839-1839-ava-earthquake.prompt: What does the Burmese court ultimately decide about the capital after the earthquake's devastation?

choices.text: Relocate the royal capital to Amarapura
Divide the court between two temporary capitals
Rebuild the palace on the same site immediately
Move the capital north to Mandalay

evt-03-23-1839-1839-ava-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The destruction of Ava proved so severe that the Burmese court abandoned it as the royal seat, relocating the capital to nearby Amarapura by 1841. It marked the end of Ava's long history as a center of Burmese power and reshaped the kingdom's political geography in the decades before British annexation.

evt-03-23-1848-flag-of-italy.scenario: It is March 1848 in Turin. King Charles Albert of Sardinia has just declared war on Austria to support uprisings across northern Italy, and he needs a banner that unites Italians rather than just his own Piedmontese subjects.
evt-03-23-1848-flag-of-italy.prompt: What flag did Charles Albert adopt for his army marching into Lombardy?

choices.text: The green-white-red tricolour bearing the Savoy coat of arms
The red flag of Republican Rome
The Bourbon flag of the Two Sicilies
The plain blue flag of the House of Savoy

evt-03-23-1848-flag-of-italy.butterflyEffect: Charles Albert's adoption of the tricolour tied the flag permanently to the cause of Italian unification. When Italy was unified in 1861, this same tricolour, later without the Savoy shield, became the national flag still flown today.

evt-03-23-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: You serve under Stonewall Jackson near Kernstown, Virginia, on 23 March 1862. Jackson orders an attack believing the Union force ahead is only a small detachment, not the larger army actually deployed there.
evt-03-23-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: What happens when Jackson attacks on this faulty intelligence?

choices.text: Jackson suffers his only tactical defeat, but it draws Union troops away from Richmond
Jackson wins a decisive victory over the Union force
The battle ends in a stalemate with no strategic consequence
Jackson withdraws without ever engaging the Union troops

evt-03-23-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Jackson suffered his only tactical defeat of the war at First Kernstown, but the battle alarmed Washington, convincing Lincoln to keep reinforcements in the Shenandoah Valley rather than send them to McClellan's Peninsula Campaign. The tactical loss thus became a strategic gain for the Confederacy.

evt-03-23-1868-henry-huntly-haight.scenario: It is March 23, 1868. As governor of California, you sign the Organic Act, merging the private College of California with a proposed state agricultural college into a single new institution.

choices.text: The University of California
The University of Southern California
Stanford University
The California State University system

evt-03-23-1868-henry-huntly-haight.butterflyEffect: The Organic Act founded the University of California, which opened its first campus at Berkeley in 1869. It grew into one of the most influential public university systems in the world, spawning ten campuses and numerous Nobel laureates.

evt-03-23-1889-mirza-ghulam-ahmad.scenario: It is March 1889 in Ludhiana, Punjab. Mirza Ghulam Ahmad has announced his claim to be a divinely appointed reformer, and a small group of followers gathers to formally pledge allegiance to him.
evt-03-23-1889-mirza-ghulam-ahmad.prompt: What did this pledge of allegiance (bai'at) establish?

choices.text: A new Hindu reform sect
The Deobandi school of Islamic jurisprudence
The Sikh Singh Sabha movement
The Ahmadiyya movement within Islam

evt-03-23-1889-mirza-ghulam-ahmad.butterflyEffect: That initiation ceremony marked the formal founding of the Ahmadiyya movement, which grew into a global community with millions of adherents. Ahmad's later claims to messiahship made the movement controversial among mainstream Muslims, and Ahmadis still face persecution and are officially declared non-Muslim in some countries today.

evt-03-23-1905-crete.scenario: It is March 1905 in the mountain village of Theriso on Crete. You are among roughly 1,500 armed rebels gathered under the lawyer Eleftherios Venizelos to challenge the rule of High Commissioner Prince George.
evt-03-23-1905-crete.prompt: What demand do you and your fellow rebels proclaim from Theriso?

choices.text: Union (enosis) with the Kingdom of Greece
Continued autonomy under Ottoman suzerainty
Immediate independence as a separate Cretan state
A return to direct Ottoman rule

evt-03-23-1905-crete.butterflyEffect: The Theriso revolt did not achieve immediate union, but it forced Prince George's resignation as High Commissioner in 1906 and thrust Venizelos onto the national stage. He later became Greece's prime minister and helped steer Crete's actual union with Greece during the Balkan Wars of 1913.

evt-03-23-1919-benito-mussolini.scenario: It is March 1919 in a rented hall on Via Paolo da Cannobio, Milan. You are a disillusioned war veteran listening to Benito Mussolini call for a new movement blending nationalism with revolutionary syndicalism, and he asks you to sign the founding manifesto.
evt-03-23-1919-benito-mussolini.prompt: What actually became of this small gathering in the years that followed?

choices.text: It evolved into the National Fascist Party, which seized power in Italy by 1922
It merged with the Italian Socialist Party soon after
It was outlawed by the Italian government within months
It fizzled out within a year, unable to attract any following

evt-03-23-1919-benito-mussolini.butterflyEffect: The Fasci Italiani di Combattimento grew into the National Fascist Party by 1921, and after the March on Rome in October 1922, Mussolini became Prime Minister and built a totalitarian dictatorship that ruled Italy until 1943.

evt-03-23-1931-bhagat-singh.scenario: You stand outside Lahore Central Jail on the evening of 23 March 1931, having heard that British authorities moved Bhagat Singh's hanging forward by a day to avoid the crowds gathering to protest his execution.
evt-03-23-1931-bhagat-singh.prompt: What actually followed Bhagat Singh's execution that night?

choices.text: The execution passed largely unnoticed outside Punjab
The British granted clemency at the last moment
Congress leaders immediately abandoned nonviolent methods in response
Bhagat Singh became a martyr whose death intensified revolutionary sentiment across India

evt-03-23-1931-bhagat-singh.butterflyEffect: His death at 23 turned him into a martyr and folk hero across northern India, intensifying revolutionary sentiment and creating friction with Gandhi's nonviolent strategy within the Congress. His example continued to inspire militant nationalists through the remaining years of the independence struggle.

evt-03-23-1933-nazi-party.scenario: It is March 23, 1933, and you are a Reichstag deputy summoned to the Kroll Opera House under the watch of armed SA men to vote on the Enabling Act.
evt-03-23-1933-nazi-party.prompt: How does the Reichstag vote on the Enabling Act granting Hitler power to rule by decree?

choices.text: Most deputies abstain, leaving no quorum
The Reichstag unanimously rejects the bill
An overwhelming majority votes to grant the powers
The vote is postponed indefinitely

evt-03-23-1933-nazi-party.butterflyEffect: The Act passed 444 to 94, with only the Social Democrats voting against it, giving Hitler's cabinet the legal power to enact laws without parliament. Combined with the earlier Reichstag Fire Decree, it let the Nazis outlaw rival parties and dismantle Germany's federal states within months, completing the Gleichschaltung of the state.

evt-03-23-1977-david-frost.scenario: It is March 23, 1977, in California. You are producing a series of televised interviews between British broadcaster David Frost and former president Richard Nixon, who resigned amid the Watergate scandal three years earlier.
evt-03-23-1977-david-frost.prompt: What did Frost extract from Nixon during these interviews?

choices.text: A rare admission that he had let the American people down over Watergate
A full legal confession leading to criminal prosecution
Nixon's resignation from public life entirely
An apology broadcast live to Congress

evt-03-23-1977-david-frost.butterflyEffect: Nixon's admission, though short of a full confession, became the closest thing to public contrition he ever offered, and the interviews drew a huge television audience. They later inspired the play and film 'Frost/Nixon,' cementing the encounter as a landmark moment in political journalism.

evt-03-23-1982-fernando-romeo-lucas-garc.scenario: You are a junior officer in the Guatemalan army on 23 March 1982, days after a widely condemned fraudulent election, when senior officers ask you to back a coup against President Fernando Romeo Lucas García.
evt-03-23-1982-fernando-romeo-lucas-garc.prompt: What actually followed the coup that toppled Lucas García?

choices.text: Civilian opposition leader Vinicio Cerezo took power immediately
The coup failed and Lucas García retained the presidency
The military junta installed General Efraín Ríos Montt, who intensified the counterinsurgency campaign
The United States sent troops to restore Lucas García to power

evt-03-23-1982-fernando-romeo-lucas-garc.butterflyEffect: The junta installed General Efraín Ríos Montt, whose government intensified the scorched-earth counterinsurgency campaign against rural and Indigenous Mayan communities. Decades later, Guatemalan courts found that army operations under his rule constituted genocide.

evt-03-23-1989-cold-fusion.scenario: You are a reporter crammed into a press conference at the University of Utah on 23 March 1989, where chemists Stanley Pons and Martin Fleischmann announce they have achieved nuclear fusion at room temperature in a simple electrochemical cell.
evt-03-23-1989-cold-fusion.prompt: What actually followed this stunning announcement of 'cold fusion'?

choices.text: Independent labs quickly replicated the results, confirming cold fusion was real
The U.S. government immediately funded commercial cold fusion power plants
Within months, failed replication attempts and scientific scrutiny largely discredited the claim
Pons and Fleischmann were awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry that same year

evt-03-23-1989-cold-fusion.butterflyEffect: Labs worldwide rushed to replicate the experiment before it had been peer-reviewed, but within months most attempts failed and flaws in the original methodology emerged. The episode became a textbook case of premature science-by-press-conference, and 'cold fusion' remains synonymous with pathological science today.

evt-03-23-1991-sierra-leone-civil-war.scenario: It is March 1991, and Revolutionary United Front fighters have crossed from Liberia into eastern Sierra Leone, seizing villages and diamond fields. You serve in President Joseph Momoh's government, watching the insurgency spread faster than your forces can contain it.
evt-03-23-1991-sierra-leone-civil-war.prompt: What did this RUF invasion trigger over the following decade?

choices.text: A nearly 11-year civil war marked by mass displacement and atrocities
Sierra Leone's peaceful partition into two states
An immediate UN peacekeeping victory ending the conflict in 1992
A swift ceasefire negotiated within months

evt-03-23-1991-sierra-leone-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The war ground on until 2002, killing tens of thousands and displacing 2.5 million people, becoming infamous for RUF's use of child soldiers and mutilations funded by 'blood diamonds.' It eventually drew British military intervention and UN peacekeepers, and helped shape later global rules on conflict diamonds and war-crimes tribunals.

evt-03-23-1993-kowloon-walled-city.scenario: It is early 1993, and you are a longtime resident of Kowloon Walled City. The government has announced the maze of unlicensed towers you call home will be torn down within the year.
evt-03-23-1993-kowloon-walled-city.prompt: What does the Hong Kong government offer residents facing eviction from the Walled City?

choices.text: Cash compensation and resettlement into public housing
Forced eviction with no compensation offered
Relocation to a rebuilt tower on the same site
Permission to stay if they rebuild to code

evt-03-23-1993-kowloon-walled-city.butterflyEffect: Demolition ran from 1993 to 1994, ending one of the densest urban settlements on Earth after decades of ungoverned growth. Kowloon Walled City Park opened on the site in December 1995, and the vanished labyrinth went on to inspire cyberpunk films, novels, and video games worldwide.

evt-03-23-2001-roscosmos.scenario: It is March 23, 2001. Mission controllers at Roscosmos fire Mir's engines for the final time, sending the 15-year-old space station on a controlled descent toward the South Pacific.
evt-03-23-2001-roscosmos.prompt: What happened to Mir as it re-entered the atmosphere?

choices.text: It was captured and returned to Earth intact by a space shuttle
It boosted into a permanent higher orbit as a museum piece
It collided with the International Space Station during descent
It broke apart and burned up, with debris falling into the Pacific Ocean

evt-03-23-2001-roscosmos.butterflyEffect: Mir's fiery reentry ended 15 years of continuous Russian space station operations and closed out a program that had hosted astronauts from many nations, including record-setting cosmonaut stays. Its retirement let Russia focus its space resources on the International Space Station.

evt-03-23-2005-texas-city-refinery-explo.scenario: It is March 23, 2005, and you are a safety supervisor at the BP refinery in Texas City. The isomerization unit is being restarted, and contractors are working out of trailers positioned close by.
evt-03-23-2005-texas-city-refinery-explo.prompt: As the unit restarts, what should you do about the occupied trailers nearby?

choices.text: Evacuate all personnel from trailers near the unit
Continue the scheduled turnaround work without changes
Wait until the next shift change to reassess
Leave them in place since procedures don't require evacuation

evt-03-23-2005-texas-city-refinery-explo.butterflyEffect: The trailers were not evacuated, and a hydrocarbon vapor cloud ignited, killing 15 contractors and injuring 180. The disaster, later ruled the costliest refinery accident in history, exposed years of cost-cutting on safety and led to record OSHA fines and sweeping reforms in U.S. process-safety regulation.

evt-03-23-2021-2021-suez-canal-obstructi.scenario: It is the morning of March 23, 2021. You are piloting the 400-meter container ship Ever Given through the Suez Canal as a sudden sandstorm sends powerful winds tearing across the narrow waterway.
evt-03-23-2021-2021-suez-canal-obstructi.prompt: What happens as the massive ship loses control in the channel?

choices.text: It collides head-on with another vessel in the channel
It runs aground, wedging across the canal and blocking all traffic
It turns back toward open water before entering the canal
It docks safely at a nearby port to wait out the storm

evt-03-23-2021-2021-suez-canal-obstructi.butterflyEffect: The Ever Given ran aground diagonally, wedging its bow and stern into opposite banks and completely blocking the canal for six days. Hundreds of ships queued as roughly $9.6 billion in daily trade was delayed, pushing some shippers to consider rerouting around Africa and prompting a major review of canal navigation and salvage procedures.

evt-03-24-1882-robert-koch.scenario: You are a physician in the audience at the Berlin Physiological Society on 24 March 1882, where Robert Koch is about to reveal what actually causes the disease that kills one in seven Europeans.
evt-03-24-1882-robert-koch.prompt: What does Koch identify as the true cause of tuberculosis?

choices.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, a specific bacterium
An inherited weakness of the lungs
Bad air and miasma rising from swamps
Spontaneous generation within diseased tissue

evt-03-24-1882-robert-koch.butterflyEffect: Koch demonstrated that a specific bacterium, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, caused the disease, cementing germ theory as the foundation of modern medicine. His methods for identifying pathogens became the standard 'Koch's postulates,' and decades later his work paved the way for the BCG vaccine and antibiotic treatments like streptomycin.

evt-03-24-1900-robert-anderson-van-wyck.scenario: You stand among the crowd in Manhattan on 24 March 1900 as Mayor Robert Van Wyck lifts the ceremonial shovel to break ground on a project meant to solve the city's crippling street congestion.
evt-03-24-1900-robert-anderson-van-wyck.prompt: What is Van Wyck breaking ground for on this day?

choices.text: A new suspension bridge across the East River
A canal extension into New York Harbor
An underground rapid transit railroad linking Manhattan and Brooklyn
An elevated steam railway along Broadway

evt-03-24-1900-robert-anderson-van-wyck.butterflyEffect: This groundbreaking launched construction of New York's first underground rapid transit line, which opened in 1904 as the Interborough Rapid Transit subway. The IRT transformed the city, opening Upper Manhattan and the Bronx to development and setting the template for one of the world's largest subway systems.

evt-03-24-1939-german-national-movement-.scenario: You are a member of the pro-Nazi German National Movement in Vaduz on 24 March 1939, moving to seize government buildings and push Liechtenstein toward union with Hitler's Reich.
evt-03-24-1939-german-national-movement-.prompt: What happens to this attempt to seize power in Liechtenstein?

choices.text: It collapses within hours and the prince retains control
It succeeds and a pro-Nazi government is installed
Swiss soldiers occupy Vaduz to restore order
German troops cross the border to complete the annexation

evt-03-24-1939-german-national-movement-.butterflyEffect: The putsch collapsed within hours as loyal citizens and authorities rallied behind Prince Franz Josef II before Berlin could react or intervene. Its failure allowed Liechtenstein to remain formally independent and neutral throughout the Second World War, avoiding the fate of Austria's Anschluss the previous year.

evt-03-24-1980-revolutionary-government-.scenario: You are in the chapel of a small hospital in San Salvador on 24 March 1980, one day after Archbishop Óscar Romero publicly begged soldiers to stop obeying orders to kill their fellow citizens.
evt-03-24-1980-revolutionary-government-.prompt: What follows Romero's plea to the army the previous day?

choices.text: He resigns as archbishop under government pressure
He is arrested and imprisoned by the military
He is assassinated while celebrating Mass
He is quietly exiled to Rome by the junta

evt-03-24-1980-revolutionary-government-.butterflyEffect: Romero was shot dead while celebrating Mass, an assassination widely attributed to a death squad linked to the ruling junta. His killing is often cited as the spark that ignited El Salvador's twelve-year civil war, and in 2018 he was canonized by Pope Francis as a martyr and saint.

evt-03-24-2015-germanwings-flight-9525.scenario: It is 24 March 2015. You are the air traffic controller handling Germanwings Flight 9525 over the French Alps when the Airbus begins an unexplained descent and stops responding to your calls.
evt-03-24-2015-germanwings-flight-9525.prompt: What should you do as contact with the aircraft is lost?

choices.text: Assume a routine communications equipment failure and wait for the crew to re-establish contact
Immediately scramble fighter jets to intercept the airliner
Declare the flight hijacked and notify only military air defense
Keep attempting radio contact while alerting search-and-rescue services of the aircraft's last known position

evt-03-24-2015-germanwings-flight-9525.butterflyEffect: The co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, had locked the captain out of the cockpit and deliberately flown the plane into the mountainside, killing all 150 aboard. The investigation into his concealed mental health history led European regulators to mandate that two authorised crew members must always be present in the cockpit.

evt-03-24-2023-2023-rolling-fork-tornado.scenario: It is Friday evening, 24 March 2023, and you live in Rolling Fork, Mississippi. Sirens wail as a massive, multi-vortex tornado bears down on the town, and you have only minutes to act.
evt-03-24-2023-2023-rolling-fork-tornado.prompt: What is the safest action to take right now?

choices.text: Get in your car and try to drive away from the storm's path
Stay near a window to watch and film the funnel's approach
Shelter inside your mobile home, bracing against an outer wall
Move to a small interior room or hallway on the lowest floor, away from windows

evt-03-24-2023-2023-rolling-fork-tornado.butterflyEffect: The EF4 tornado, with winds near 195 mph, tore through Rolling Fork and Silver City, killing 17 and injuring at least 165, making it the deadliest twister of that outbreak. The devastation renewed national debate over tornado warning times and the vulnerability of mobile and manufactured homes in the rural Mississippi Delta.

evt-03-24-2024-2024-senegalese-president.scenario: You are a voter in Dakar on 24 March 2024, casting your ballot after weeks of unrest when outgoing president Macky Sall tried to postpone this very election.
evt-03-24-2024-2024-senegalese-president.prompt: Who wins this election, reshaping Senegal's political future?

choices.text: Idrissa Seck, a veteran opposition figure
Karim Wade, son of a former president
Amadou Ba, the ruling party's candidate
Bassirou Diomaye Faye

evt-03-24-2024-2024-senegalese-president.butterflyEffect: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a little-known former tax inspector and protégé of jailed opposition leader Ousmane Sonko, won outright in the first round. At 44, he became Senegal's youngest president and quickly named Sonko as his prime minister, signaling a sharp anti-establishment turn in West African politics.

evt-03-25-717-byzantine-empire.scenario: It is 717 AD. You are Theodosius III, raised to the Byzantine throne by mutinous soldiers, but now the ambitious general Leo the Isaurian marches on Constantinople with a rival army at his back.
evt-03-25-717-byzantine-empire.prompt: What do you do to avoid a ruinous civil war?

choices.text: Appeal to the Umayyad Caliphate for military aid
Fight Leo's forces to keep the throne
Flee west to Italy and rule in exile
Abdicate and retire to a monastery

evt-03-25-717-byzantine-empire.butterflyEffect: Theodosius abdicated peacefully and retired into monastic life, letting Leo III take the throne unopposed. Leo went on to repel the great Arab siege of Constantinople in 717–718 and later launched the Iconoclasm controversy that convulsed Byzantine religious life for over a century.

evt-03-25-1410-yongle-emperor.scenario: It is 1410 and you march north from Beijing with the Yongle Emperor himself at the head of the army, the first time a Ming emperor has personally led troops against the Mongols after Tatar leader Bunyashiri killed Ming envoys.
evt-03-25-1410-yongle-emperor.prompt: What is the campaign's objective as the army advances?

choices.text: Defeat the Tatar leader Bunyashiri and his forces
Conquer the kingdom of Korea
Strike first at the rival Oirat Mongols
Negotiate a tribute agreement with Tibet

evt-03-25-1410-yongle-emperor.butterflyEffect: The Ming forces crushed Bunyashiri's Tatars at the Onon River, forcing him to flee westward. It was the first of five personal northern campaigns the Yongle Emperor would lead, entrenching a costly policy of direct military confrontation with the Mongols that strained Ming finances for decades.

evt-03-25-1655-christiaan-huygens.scenario: It is 25 March 1655, and you are peering through Christiaan Huygens's improved telescope, trained on Saturn, when you notice a faint point of light steadily circling the planet.
evt-03-25-1655-christiaan-huygens.prompt: What has Huygens just discovered orbiting Saturn?

choices.text: A second, smaller planet beyond Saturn
A large moon, later named Titan
The rings of Saturn
A comet passing near Saturn

evt-03-25-1655-christiaan-huygens.butterflyEffect: Huygens had found Titan, Saturn's largest moon, using a telescope of his own design. The discovery cemented his reputation in the young science of astronomy, and centuries later NASA and ESA named their joint Saturn mission and its lander, Cassini-Huygens, after him when it touched down on Titan itself in 2005.

evt-03-25-1708-jacobitism.scenario: It is 25 March 1708 off Fife Ness. You are a French naval officer escorting James Francis Edward Stuart toward Scotland to spark a Jacobite rising, when an English fleet under Admiral Byng is sighted approaching fast.
evt-03-25-1708-jacobitism.prompt: What do you do with the invasion fleet and its royal passenger?

choices.text: Put James ashore alone and sail away
Land the troops and fight the English fleet
Surrender the fleet to the English navy
Retreat to France without landing any troops

evt-03-25-1708-jacobitism.butterflyEffect: The French commander chose to withdraw without landing troops, and the fleet sailed back to Dunkirk, aborting the invasion entirely. The failed attempt exposed weaknesses in Jacobite planning and left English authorities on high alert, foreshadowing the larger, equally unsuccessful rising of 1715.

evt-03-25-1799-war-of-the-second-coaliti.scenario: It is 25 March 1799 and you serve in Jourdan's French Army of the Danube. Five days after a bloody defeat at Ostrach, Archduke Charles's Austrians confront you again near Stockach, and the line is breaking.
evt-03-25-1799-war-of-the-second-coaliti.prompt: After this second defeat in a week, what does the French army do?

choices.text: Surrender the entire army to Archduke Charles
Push deeper into Austrian territory
Immediately counterattack the same day
Retreat back across the Rhine

evt-03-25-1799-war-of-the-second-coaliti.butterflyEffect: Jourdan's shattered army retreated across the Rhine and he soon resigned command, handing it to Masséna. The collapse of the southern German offensive let the Allies seize the initiative until Napoleon's return from Egypt reversed the war's course at Marengo in 1800.

evt-03-25-1807-slave-trade-act-1807.scenario: It is May 1807, days after the Slave Trade Act takes effect. You captain a British ship still loaded with enslaved Africans off the West African coast, and a Royal Navy patrol vessel is closing in.
evt-03-25-1807-slave-trade-act-1807.prompt: What penalty do you now risk if the navy stops your ship?

choices.text: Confiscation of all British colonial property
Seizure of the ship and fines for each enslaved person carried
Immediate execution of the entire crew
Automatic freedom granted to all enslaved people in British colonies

evt-03-25-1807-slave-trade-act-1807.butterflyEffect: The 1807 Act made the trade illegal and subjected captains to seizure of their ship and fines per enslaved person aboard, though slavery itself remained legal in the colonies until 1833. Britain used its navy to pressure other nations into abolishing the trade too, gradually turning suppression of the Atlantic slave trade into an international cause.

evt-03-25-1911-triangle-shirtwaist-facto.scenario: It is the week after the Triangle Shirtwaist fire, and you sit on New York's newly formed Factory Investigating Commission, tasked with responding to the deaths of 146 garment workers trapped behind locked doors.
evt-03-25-1911-triangle-shirtwaist-facto.prompt: What did the commission's investigation actually produce for New York's workers?

choices.text: A wave of New York State factory safety and fire-code laws
A national eight-hour workday statute
A federal minimum wage law
A permanent federal labor relations board

evt-03-25-1911-triangle-shirtwaist-facto.butterflyEffect: The Factory Investigating Commission's work led to dozens of new state laws on fire safety, building exits, and factory conditions within a few years. It also strengthened the International Ladies' Garment Workers' Union and made Frances Perkins, who witnessed the fire, a lifelong advocate who later shaped New Deal labor policy.

evt-03-25-1917-nicholas-ii.scenario: It is March 1917 in Petrograd. As a minister in the new Provisional Government, you must decide the fate of the just-abdicated Tsar Nicholas II and his family, still living at the Alexander Palace.
evt-03-25-1917-nicholas-ii.prompt: What does the Provisional Government decide to do with the former tsar's family?

choices.text: Send them into exile in Britain immediately
Place them under house arrest at Tsarskoye Selo
Execute the family without delay
Allow Nicholas to reverse his abdication

evt-03-25-1917-nicholas-ii.butterflyEffect: The government placed the Romanovs under house arrest at Tsarskoye Selo, later moving them to Tobolsk in Siberia after Britain's King George V withdrew an earlier offer of asylum. The family was eventually handed to Bolshevik authorities and executed in Yekaterinburg in July 1918, ending the Romanov dynasty for good.

evt-03-25-1934-enrico-fermi.scenario: It is 1934 in Fermi's Rome laboratory. You have just bombarded uranium with slow neutrons and detected new radioactivity where none should exist.
evt-03-25-1934-enrico-fermi.prompt: What does Fermi believe he has created from the uranium?

choices.text: Proof that atoms cannot be split
A stable new isotope of hydrogen
New elements heavier than uranium
A previously unknown noble gas

evt-03-25-1934-enrico-fermi.butterflyEffect: Fermi concluded he had produced new transuranium elements, a claim that helped win him the 1938 Nobel Prize. Years later, Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann showed the real process was nuclear fission, a discovery that redirected physics toward the chain reactions Fermi himself would soon harness in the Manhattan Project.

evt-03-25-1949-operation-priboi.scenario: It is before dawn on 25 March 1949 in a Latvian farming village. As the local Party official, you knock on doors with a list of names, ordering families onto trucks bound for Siberia.
evt-03-25-1949-operation-priboi.prompt: What official reason do you give villagers for the deportations?

choices.text: They owe unpaid war reparations to Moscow
They are urban intellectuals opposing socialism
They are kulaks and supporters of anti-Soviet nationalist bandits
They are being resettled for religious reasons

evt-03-25-1949-operation-priboi.butterflyEffect: Operation Priboi targeted families labeled kulaks or relatives of anti-Soviet partisans, clearing the way for forced collectivization and crushing support for the Forest Brothers resistance. The trauma of the March deportation became a defining memory in Baltic national identity and later fueled independence movements after 1989.

evt-03-25-1957-treaty-of-rome.scenario: It is 25 March 1957 in Rome, and you are a delegate from one of six nations about to sign a treaty binding your country's economy to its neighbours for the first time since the war.
evt-03-25-1957-treaty-of-rome.prompt: What core economic mechanism does the treaty commit these six nations to build?

choices.text: A shared single currency replacing national money
A joint European military command
A single European parliament with binding lawmaking power over all policy
A customs union and common market for goods, labour, services and capital

evt-03-25-1957-treaty-of-rome.butterflyEffect: The treaty created the European Economic Community, phasing out internal tariffs and building a customs union with a common external tariff. That single market became the economic backbone later renamed the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, underpinning today's EU.

evt-03-25-1975-faisal-of-saudi-arabia.scenario: It is 25 March 1975 in Riyadh. You are a royal guard at King Faisal's majlis when his nephew, Faisal bin Musaid, steps forward and fires point-blank at the king during a public reception.
evt-03-25-1975-faisal-of-saudi-arabia.prompt: Who becomes King of Saudi Arabia after Faisal's assassination?

choices.text: Crown Prince Fahd is crowned king that day
A military council seizes power
His son immediately inherits the throne
His half-brother Khalid becomes king

evt-03-25-1975-faisal-of-saudi-arabia.butterflyEffect: Faisal's half-brother Khalid became king, with Fahd as crown prince, continuing the pattern of succession among Abdulaziz's sons. The assassin, later declared mentally unfit by some but tried anyway, was publicly executed, and Saudi security around the royal family tightened significantly afterward.

evt-03-25-2006-2006-belarusian-president.scenario: It is 25 March 2006 and you are camped with fellow demonstrators on October Square in Minsk, days after Alexander Lukashenko claimed a third term. Riot police are massing at the edges of the square as night falls.
evt-03-25-2006-2006-belarusian-president.prompt: What do the protesters do as police move to clear the square?

choices.text: Hold their ground in a peaceful sit-in
Call for foreign troops to intervene
Disperse quietly before police arrive
Storm the presidential administration building

evt-03-25-2006-2006-belarusian-president.butterflyEffect: Riot police violently dispersed the crowd that night, arresting hundreds, including opposition candidate Alyaksandr Kazulin, who was later jailed. The crackdown, dubbed the response to the 'Denim Revolution', deepened Belarus's isolation from the West and hardened Lukashenko's grip on power for years.

evt-03-26-1169-saladin.scenario: It is 1169 in Cairo. Your uncle Shirkuh, commander of Syrian forces in Egypt, has just died, and the Fatimid caliph al-Adid has summoned you, a young officer, to take his place at the head of the army and government.
evt-03-26-1169-saladin.prompt: What do you do with your sudden appointment as vizier?

choices.text: Begin quietly consolidating personal control over the army and administration
Immediately depose the caliph and declare himself sultan
Offer an alliance to the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem
Return to Syria and abandon the position

evt-03-26-1169-saladin.butterflyEffect: Saladin used his new position to steadily consolidate real power in Egypt, sidelining the Fatimid court while officially serving the caliph. Within two years he abolished the Fatimid caliphate outright, founding the Ayyubid dynasty that would soon confront the Crusader states.

evt-03-26-1344-reconquista.scenario: It's late March 1344, and you are a soldier in King Alfonso XI's Castilian camp outside Algeciras, where the siege of this Nasrid port city has dragged on for twenty-one grinding months.
evt-03-26-1344-reconquista.prompt: What finally happens after this long siege?

choices.text: Algeciras surrenders to Alfonso XI after the prolonged siege
Plague forces both sides to abandon the siege unresolved
The city is destroyed and left uninhabited for a century
The Nasrid army breaks the siege and drives the Castilians back

evt-03-26-1344-reconquista.butterflyEffect: Algeciras surrendered to Alfonso XI, a major Christian gain in the Reconquista. The siege is also notable as one of the earliest documented uses of gunpowder cannon in European warfare, employed by the city's Muslim defenders against the besiegers.

evt-03-26-1484-william-caxton.scenario: It is 1484, and you work in William Caxton's print shop in Westminster, setting type for his new English translation of Aesop's Fables, one of the first popular secular works to come off his press.
evt-03-26-1484-william-caxton.prompt: What effect did printing works like this have on English readers?

choices.text: It was condemned by the Church and suppressed
It helped spread standardized English and wider literacy
It failed commercially and was quickly forgotten
It remained accessible only to Latin-trained scholars

evt-03-26-1484-william-caxton.butterflyEffect: Caxton's press made vernacular English texts widely available for the first time, helping standardize spelling and grammar and expanding literacy beyond Latin-reading clergy and scholars. His printed editions of works like Aesop's Fables laid groundwork for English becoming a serious literary language.

evt-03-26-1812-gerrymandering.scenario: It is early 1812 and you sit in the Massachusetts State Senate. Allies of Governor Elbridge Gerry have drawn a bizarre, salamander-shaped Essex County district built to favor his Democratic-Republican party in the coming election.
evt-03-26-1812-gerrymandering.prompt: As a legislator, what do you do when the redistricting bill comes to a vote?

choices.text: You vote for the bill, and it passes into law
You vote against it and the bill fails
You propose a nonpartisan redistricting commission instead
You resign rather than take part in the vote

evt-03-26-1812-gerrymandering.butterflyEffect: The bill passed, and the Boston Gazette soon printed a cartoon depicting the twisted district as a monstrous creature, dubbing it a "Gerry-mander." The word outlived Gerry's own political career and is still the global term for manipulating electoral boundaries.

evt-03-26-1873-first-aceh-expedition.scenario: It is April 1873, and you are Dutch Major General Köhler, leading Netherlands East Indies troops toward the Great Mosque of Banda Aceh after landing your invasion force on the Sumatran coast.
evt-03-26-1873-first-aceh-expedition.prompt: What happens as you press the assault on the mosque complex?

choices.text: You capture the Sultan of Aceh and end the war in a single day
The mosque's defenders surrender without a fight
You negotiate a peace treaty on the spot
You are struck down by a sniper, forcing a Dutch withdrawal

evt-03-26-1873-first-aceh-expedition.butterflyEffect: Köhler was shot dead by a sniper near the mosque, and the shaken Dutch force withdrew from Aceh entirely within days. The humiliation forced the Netherlands to mount a much larger Second Aceh Expedition later in 1873, dragging the two sides into a brutal war that lasted for decades.

evt-03-26-1885-metis.scenario: It's 26 March 1885, and you ride with a North-West Mounted Police column near Duck Lake, sent to secure supplies after Louis Riel's Métis provisional government asserts control nearby, with Gabriel Dumont's armed riders closing in on the trail ahead.
evt-03-26-1885-metis.prompt: What happens when your column meets Dumont's fighters?

choices.text: The police capture Riel and Dumont on the spot, collapsing the uprising
Both sides reach a peaceful truce and Ottawa addresses Métis grievances
The Métis surrender at once, ending the rebellion before it starts
Talks break down and gunfire erupts, starting the North-West Rebellion

evt-03-26-1885-metis.butterflyEffect: Negotiations collapsed into gunfire at the Battle of Duck Lake, opening the North-West Rebellion. Canadian militia crushed the rebellion by May at Batoche, and Louis Riel was captured and executed for treason that November, an event still central to Métis relations with Canada.

evt-03-26-1896-brunner-mine-disaster.scenario: It's the morning of 26 March 1896, and you are among the rescuers descending into the Brunner Mine in New Zealand after a violent explosion tore through the workings overnight, trapping dozens of men below.
evt-03-26-1896-brunner-mine-disaster.prompt: What do the rescue parties ultimately find when they reach the men underground?

choices.text: Most miners escaped through a second shaft before the gas spread
Only the men nearest the entrance were killed; the rest survived
The explosion caused no deaths, only damage to the mine's equipment
All 65 miners below ground have died, largely from toxic gas after the blast

evt-03-26-1896-brunner-mine-disaster.butterflyEffect: All 65 men working that shift were killed, most by the poisonous afterdamp that followed the blast rather than the explosion itself. It remains New Zealand's deadliest mining disaster and led to lasting changes in mine ventilation and safety inspection practices.

evt-03-26-1913-first-balkan-war.scenario: It is 26 March 1913. You are a Bulgarian artillery officer outside the fortress city of Adrianople, where a five-month siege against Ottoman defenders is finally reaching its end.
evt-03-26-1913-first-balkan-war.prompt: What happened when the siege of Adrianople concluded?

choices.text: The Ottoman garrison surrendered the city
The besieging forces withdrew due to disease
An Ottoman relief army broke the siege
The city was abandoned and burned before capture

evt-03-26-1913-first-balkan-war.butterflyEffect: The Ottoman garrison surrendered, and the fall of Adrianople pushed the Ottoman Empire toward the Treaty of London, ending the First Balkan War. Disputes among the victorious Balkan allies over the spoils, including Adrianople's fate, helped trigger the Second Balkan War just months later.

evt-03-26-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It is 26 March 1917. You serve with the Egyptian Expeditionary Force as it pushes toward Gaza, and by afternoon your cavalry has nearly encircled the town, but water is scarce and daylight is fading.
evt-03-26-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What does the British command decide to do as night falls near Gaza?

choices.text: Press the attack and seize Gaza before Ottoman reinforcements arrive
Dig in and wait several days for fresh supplies
Retreat all the way back to the Egyptian border
Withdraw the advancing troops, judging the position untenable

evt-03-26-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Despite being on the verge of taking Gaza, British commanders withdrew over fears of water shortages and Ottoman reinforcements, turning near-victory into the First Battle of Gaza's failure. The defeat led to General Murray's replacement by Edmund Allenby, whose more aggressive leadership eventually captured Jerusalem by year's end.

evt-03-26-1939-francoist-spain.scenario: It is 26 March 1939. You are a Republican militiaman holding the last defensive lines around Madrid as Franco's Nationalist armies launch a massive final push after nearly three years of civil war.
evt-03-26-1939-francoist-spain.prompt: What happened in the days that followed this final Nationalist offensive?

choices.text: Republican defenses collapsed and Madrid surrendered soon after
The offensive stalled for months, prolonging the war into 1940
The Republican government negotiated a lasting ceasefire with autonomy for Madrid
International forces intervened to halt the offensive

evt-03-26-1939-francoist-spain.butterflyEffect: Madrid fell within days, and Franco declared the war over on 1 April 1939. Nearly four decades of dictatorship followed, shaping Spain's politics, culture, and relationship with the rest of Europe until Franco's death in 1975.

evt-03-26-1942-ss-dixie-arrow.scenario: It is 26 March 1942 off Cape Hatteras. A German torpedo has just struck your tanker, the Dixie Arrow, and flames are racing toward the lifeboats where your shipmates are gathered.
evt-03-26-1942-ss-dixie-arrow.prompt: As helmsman, what do you do at the wheel while the ship burns?

choices.text: Head straight for the nearest shore at full speed
Radio for help and wait below deck
Abandon the wheel and jump overboard immediately
Steer the ship to keep the flames away from the crew, even at personal risk

evt-03-26-1942-ss-dixie-arrow.butterflyEffect: Helmsman Oscar Chappell steered the blazing tanker so the wind carried the flames away from his crewmates, saving many lives before he himself was killed. His sacrifice became one of the most cited acts of heroism from the brutal U-boat campaign that struck American shipping along the East Coast in early 1942.

evt-03-26-1953-jonas-salk.scenario: It is 26 March 1953. You are listening to a radio broadcast as Dr. Jonas Salk announces that his experimental polio vaccine has successfully immunized a small group of children and adults, including his own family.
evt-03-26-1953-jonas-salk.prompt: What happened next to test the vaccine on a larger scale?

choices.text: The FDA rejected further testing pending more research
Testing was halted due to lack of funding
The vaccine was immediately withdrawn over safety concerns
A massive field trial involving over a million children was launched

evt-03-26-1953-jonas-salk.butterflyEffect: In 1954, Salk's vaccine was tested in the largest clinical trial in history, involving over a million American schoolchildren. Its success led to licensing in 1955 and a nationwide vaccination campaign that dramatically reduced polio cases within just a few years.

evt-03-26-1974-chamoli-district.scenario: It is March 1974 in the village of Reni, Chamoli district. Contractors have arrived to fell trees while the men are away, and you and the other women in the village are the only ones present to stop them.
evt-03-26-1974-chamoli-district.prompt: How do the women of Reni respond to the loggers?

choices.text: Write a petition and wait for a reply from officials
Leave the village until the men return
Burn the loggers' equipment overnight
Hug the trees to physically block the loggers

evt-03-26-1974-chamoli-district.butterflyEffect: Led by Gaura Devi, the women embraced the trees to physically block the axes, coining the tactic that gave the Chipko movement its name. The successful stand spread across the Himalayas, eventually pressuring the Indian government into a fifteen-year ban on commercial logging in the region and inspiring grassroots environmental movements worldwide.

evt-03-26-1975-biological-weapons-conven.scenario: It's 26 March 1975 in Geneva, and you are a diplomat present as the Biological Weapons Convention officially enters into force, the first treaty to outlaw an entire category of weapons of mass destruction.
evt-03-26-1975-biological-weapons-conven.prompt: What does the convention actually commit signatory states to doing?

choices.text: Banning the development, production, and stockpiling of biological weapons
Outlawing the wartime use of chemical agents like mustard gas
Prohibiting atmospheric and underwater nuclear weapons testing
Banning landmines and cluster munitions in populated areas

evt-03-26-1975-biological-weapons-conven.butterflyEffect: The BWC banned developing, producing, stockpiling, or acquiring biological and toxin weapons, but included no verification mechanism. This gap let the Soviet Union secretly run its Biopreparat bioweapons program for years undetected, exposing weaknesses later treaties tried to address.

evt-03-26-1991-singapore-airlines-flight.scenario: It is 26 March 1991 at Paya Lebar Airport. You are part of Singapore's Special Operations Force facing a hijacked Airbus A310 whose four armed captors are demanding the release of Asif Ali Zardari from a Pakistani jail.
evt-03-26-1991-singapore-airlines-flight.prompt: How does the SOF team end the standoff on the tarmac?

choices.text: Negotiate a prisoner exchange for the hostages
Allow the plane to refuel and depart Singapore
Wait out the hijackers over several days
Launch a rapid armed assault on the aircraft

evt-03-26-1991-singapore-airlines-flight.butterflyEffect: Commandos stormed the aircraft in under 30 minutes, killing all four hijackers while every one of the 129 passengers and crew survived unharmed. The raid became a textbook case of successful counter-hijacking and cemented the SOF's international reputation for precision operations.

evt-03-26-1997-rancho-santa-fe-californi.scenario: It is late March 1997 in Rancho Santa Fe, California. Acting on a tip, you are among the sheriff's deputies entering a quiet mansion where dozens of members of a religious group have been found dead, timed with the passing of the Hale-Bopp comet.
evt-03-26-1997-rancho-santa-fe-californi.prompt: What belief had driven the group to this act?

choices.text: That the comet's approach was a signal a spacecraft would take their souls to a higher level
That a natural disaster was about to destroy the region
That their leader had been declared a fugitive and they faced arrest
That government agents were about to raid their compound

evt-03-26-1997-rancho-santa-fe-californi.butterflyEffect: The Heaven's Gate members believed the comet Hale-Bopp was accompanied by a spacecraft that would carry their souls to a higher existence once they left their bodies. The tragedy, amplified by the group's early use of the internet to recruit and spread its teachings, became a defining case study in how online communities could feed into cult dynamics.

evt-03-26-1999-jack-kevorkian.scenario: It is 26 March 1999 in a Michigan courtroom. You are a juror who has just watched footage, aired months earlier on 60 Minutes, of Dr. Jack Kevorkian administering a lethal injection to Thomas Youk, and deliberations are about to begin.
evt-03-26-1999-jack-kevorkian.prompt: What verdict does the jury reach on Kevorkian's charges?

choices.text: Convict him only of a minor manslaughter charge
Deadlock, forcing a mistrial
Convict him of second-degree murder
Acquit him on all charges

evt-03-26-1999-jack-kevorkian.butterflyEffect: The jury convicted Kevorkian of second-degree murder, and he was sentenced to 10 to 25 years in prison. His conviction and eventual parole in 2007 kept physician-assisted suicide at the center of American legal and ethical debate, feeding into later right-to-die legislation in several states.

evt-03-26-2009-tesla-model-s.scenario: It's March 26, 2009, and journalists gather in a California hangar as Tesla pulls the cover off a sleek four-door prototype. Elon Musk promises this car will prove an electric vehicle can be fast, luxurious, and desirable, not just practical.
evt-03-26-2009-tesla-model-s.prompt: What happens to this prototype in the years after its reveal?

choices.text: General Motors buys the design to mass-produce it as a Chevrolet
Tesla scraps the sedan to focus only on the Roadster
It becomes the Model S, entering production in 2012 and reshaping the EV industry
The prototype enters mass production immediately later that same year

evt-03-26-2009-tesla-model-s.butterflyEffect: The design became the Tesla Model S, entering production in 2012. It won Motor Trend's Car of the Year in 2013 and is widely credited with proving electric cars could outperform gasoline rivals, accelerating the entire auto industry's shift toward EVs.

evt-03-26-2010-torpedo.scenario: It is the night of 26 March 2010. You are a sailor aboard the South Korean corvette Cheonan, on routine patrol near Baengnyeong Island, when a sudden explosion tears the hull in two.
evt-03-26-2010-torpedo.prompt: What did the international investigation later conclude caused the explosion?

choices.text: A stray mine left over from the Korean War
An accidental collision with a submarine
An internal engine malfunction
A North Korean torpedo strike

evt-03-26-2010-torpedo.butterflyEffect: A multinational investigation concluded the ship had been struck by a North Korean torpedo, killing 46 sailors. South Korea responded with the 'May 24 measures,' cutting most trade and exchange with the North and sharply escalating inter-Korean tensions for years afterward.

evt-03-26-2024-francis-scott-key-bridge-.scenario: It's just before 1:30 a.m. on March 26, 2024. You're part of a construction crew patching potholes on the Francis Scott Key Bridge when the massive container ship MV Dali suddenly loses power and drifts toward a support pier beneath you.
evt-03-26-2024-francis-scott-key-bridge-.prompt: What happens in the seconds that follow?

choices.text: The pier absorbs the impact and the bridge holds firm
The Dali regains power just in time and steers safely away
The ship strikes the pier and the bridge's span collapses within seconds
A tugboat intercepts and pushes the Dali clear of the bridge

evt-03-26-2024-francis-scott-key-bridge-.butterflyEffect: The Dali struck a main support pier and the bridge's central span collapsed almost instantly, killing six construction workers. The disaster shut the Port of Baltimore for months, disrupted shipping and supply chains, and triggered a nationwide review of bridge protections against ship strikes.

evt-03-27-1625-charles-i-of-england.scenario: It's 27 March 1625. Your father, James I, has just died, and you ascend to the thrones of England, Scotland and Ireland believing firmly in the divine right of kings.
evt-03-27-1625-charles-i-of-england.prompt: What conflict would come to define your reign in the years ahead?

choices.text: An escalating struggle with Parliament over taxation and authority
Decades of peaceful cooperation with Parliament
A war of succession with a rival brother
A purely religious schism with the Church of Rome

evt-03-27-1625-charles-i-of-england.butterflyEffect: Charles's insistence on royal prerogative led to repeated clashes with Parliament, his Personal Rule without it, and eventually civil war. He was tried and executed in 1649, and England briefly became a republic under Cromwell.

evt-03-27-1836-republic-of-texas.scenario: You are among Colonel James Fannin's Texian volunteers who surrendered after the Battle of Coleto, promised humane treatment as prisoners of war. On the morning of March 27, 1836, Mexican soldiers march your column out of Goliad.
evt-03-27-1836-republic-of-texas.prompt: What happens next to the surrendered Texian prisoners?

choices.text: They are exchanged for captured Mexican soldiers
They are conscripted into the Mexican army
They are released after swearing loyalty to Mexico
They are marched out and executed on Santa Anna's orders

evt-03-27-1836-republic-of-texas.butterflyEffect: On Santa Anna's direct orders, the prisoners were marched out and shot, with survivors bayoneted; at least 425 died in what became known as the Goliad massacre. News of the killings, alongside the Alamo, fueled the Texian cry 'Remember Goliad!' at the decisive Battle of San Jacinto weeks later.

evt-03-27-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: You are a B-29 crewman in late March 1945, briefed on a new mission over Japan's Shimonoseki Strait that involves no bombs meant to explode on impact.
evt-03-27-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What are you ordered to drop into Japan's harbors and shipping lanes?

choices.text: Leaflets calling for surrender
Naval mines to block shipping lanes
Depth charges aimed at submarines
Incendiary bombs targeting port warehouses

evt-03-27-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Operation Starvation seeded Japanese waters with thousands of naval mines, sinking or damaging ships and choking off the food and raw materials the home islands needed. The campaign helped tighten the blockade of Japan in the war's final months.

evt-03-27-1958-nikita-khrushchev.scenario: It's 27 March 1958 in Moscow. Having already outmaneuvered rivals in the so-called Anti-Party Group the previous year, you watch Khrushchev take the additional post of Chairman of the Council of Ministers.
evt-03-27-1958-nikita-khrushchev.prompt: What did this move complete for Khrushchev's grip on power?

choices.text: Full concentration of party and government power in his hands
A formal alliance with Stalin's old loyalists
His removal from the Communist Party leadership
A return to collective leadership with the Politburo

evt-03-27-1958-nikita-khrushchev.butterflyEffect: By combining the premiership with his party leadership, Khrushchev now controlled both state and party machinery, a concentration of authority that let him push de-Stalinization and reform largely unopposed until his own removal in 1964.

evt-03-27-1976-washington-metro.scenario: It is 27 March 1976, and you are among the first passengers riding the newly opened Washington Metro from Rhode Island Avenue toward Farragut North. You step off the escalator into a cavernous station unlike any subway you have seen before.
evt-03-27-1976-washington-metro.prompt: What defines the striking look of these new Metro stations?

choices.text: Narrow tiled tunnels modeled directly on the New York subway
Wooden platforms modeled on old streetcar depots
Entirely elevated tracks running above city streets
Vaulted coffered concrete ceilings designed by Harry Weese

evt-03-27-1976-washington-metro.butterflyEffect: Architect Harry Weese's vaulted, coffered concrete ceilings became Metro's signature look, distinguishing it from older, cramped subway systems in New York or Boston. The design won lasting acclaim, helped Metro grow into one of the busiest US transit systems, and influenced later American transit architecture even as the network later faced serious maintenance challenges.

evt-03-27-1993-jiang-zemin.scenario: It's 27 March 1993 in Beijing. The National People's Congress has just voted, and you watch as Jiang Zemin is formally installed as President of China, adding the state presidency to his party and military titles.
evt-03-27-1993-jiang-zemin.prompt: What did Jiang's consolidation of these top posts signal for China's direction?

choices.text: A return to Maoist central planning
Direct military rule replacing civilian leadership
An imminent shift toward multiparty democracy
Continuity and stability for Deng Xiaoping's market reforms

evt-03-27-1993-jiang-zemin.butterflyEffect: Jiang's decade as president oversaw rapid economic growth, negotiations for WTO entry, and Hong Kong's 1997 handover, cementing China's turn toward market-driven reform while keeping one-party political control firmly intact.

evt-03-27-1998-food-and-drug-administrat.scenario: You are a Pfizer researcher in the mid-1990s, watching a compound called sildenafil fail its original clinical goal of treating angina. Trial volunteers keep reporting one unexpected, very noticeable side effect instead.
evt-03-27-1998-food-and-drug-administrat.prompt: What does Pfizer decide to do with this failed heart drug?

choices.text: Abandon the compound entirely as a failed drug
Shelve it for internal veterinary research only
Market it only as an experimental blood pressure medication
Seek FDA approval for it as a treatment for erectile dysfunction

evt-03-27-1998-food-and-drug-administrat.butterflyEffect: On 27 March 1998 the FDA approved sildenafil under the brand name Viagra as the first oral treatment for erectile dysfunction. It became an instant commercial phenomenon, reshaped public conversation about male sexual health, and opened a lucrative new pharmaceutical category that rivals quickly entered.

evt-03-27-1999-nato-bombing-of-yugoslavi.scenario: You command a Yugoslav SA-3 surface-to-air missile battery near Belgrade on the night of March 27, 1999, radar briefly catching a shape NATO calls invisible to detection.
evt-03-27-1999-nato-bombing-of-yugoslavi.prompt: What happens when your battery fires on the American stealth jet?

choices.text: The missiles destroy the stealth jet, its only combat loss
Your radar cannot lock onto the stealth aircraft at all
The jet evades using onboard electronic countermeasures
Yugoslav fighter jets intercept and force it to land

evt-03-27-1999-nato-bombing-of-yugoslavi.butterflyEffect: The missiles brought down an F-117 Nighthawk, the only combat loss of the type in its history. The wreckage, later displayed in Belgrade's Museum of Aviation, became a lasting symbol that stealth technology was not invincible against older Soviet-designed defenses.

evt-03-27-2002-second-intifada.scenario: It is 28 March 2002, the day after a suicide bomber killed roughly 30 Israeli civilians at a Passover seder in Netanya. You sit in an emergency Israeli cabinet session where ministers debate how to respond to the deadliest attack of the uprising so far.
evt-03-27-2002-second-intifada.prompt: What large-scale military response does Israel decide to launch?

choices.text: Operation Cast Lead in the Gaza Strip
A unilateral withdrawal from all West Bank settlements
Operation Defensive Shield, reoccupying major West Bank cities
Operation Peace for Galilee in Lebanon

evt-03-27-2002-second-intifada.butterflyEffect: Israel launched Operation Defensive Shield, its biggest West Bank military operation since 1967, reoccupying Ramallah, Bethlehem, Nablus and other cities to root out militant networks. The operation, and the barrier construction it accelerated, marked a turning point after which intifada violence gradually declined toward the 2005 Sharm el-Sheikh Summit.

evt-03-27-2002-passover-massacre.scenario: It is the evening of 27 March 2002, and you are the security guard on duty at the Park Hotel in Netanya, where families have gathered for a Passover seder. A man in a wig, sunglasses and women's clothing approaches the entrance, and something about him unsettles you.
evt-03-27-2002-passover-massacre.prompt: As the disguised bomber nears the seder hall, what happens next?

choices.text: He flees when confronted and is later arrested outside
He is tackled and disarmed before reaching the hall
He detonates his explosives as you approach to question him
He shows a fake ID and is waved through without incident

evt-03-27-2002-passover-massacre.butterflyEffect: You move to check his identity, and he detonates his explosives before you can stop him, killing 30 people, including you. The attack, the deadliest against Israeli civilians in the Second Intifada, led Israel to launch Operation Defensive Shield days later, its largest West Bank military operation since 1967.

evt-03-27-2004-hms-scylla-f71.scenario: It's 27 March 2004 off Whitsand Bay, Cornwall. You watch as HMS Scylla, the Royal Navy's last Leander-class frigate, is deliberately flooded and sent to the seabed.
evt-03-27-2004-hms-scylla-f71.prompt: Why is the Navy sinking its own decommissioned frigate?

choices.text: To simulate a wartime sinking for training exercises
To test new underwater weapons systems
To create Britain's first artificial reef for scuba divers
To safely dispose of unstable stored ammunition

evt-03-27-2004-hms-scylla-f71.butterflyEffect: HMS Scylla became the UK's first vessel deliberately sunk to create an artificial reef for recreational divers. The wreck quickly attracted marine life and diving tourism, encouraging further Royal Navy ship-to-reef conversions around Britain's coast.

evt-03-27-2009-situ-gintung.scenario: It is before dawn on 27 March 2009 in Cirendeu, near Tangerang, Indonesia. You live just below the earthen dam built by Dutch colonial engineers in 1933 that holds back the Situ Gintung reservoir, and in the darkness you hear a strange roaring sound from its direction.
evt-03-27-2009-situ-gintung.prompt: With the old dam suddenly failing above your sleeping neighborhood, what should you do?

choices.text: Go check the dam yourself to see how bad the leak is
Wait for an official siren or announcement before moving
Flee uphill away from the reservoir immediately
Assume it is normal seasonal runoff and go back to sleep

evt-03-27-2009-situ-gintung.butterflyEffect: The 76-year-old dam collapsed suddenly that morning, sending a wall of water through Cirendeu and killing more than 100 people who had no warning. The disaster pushed Indonesian authorities to inspect other aging colonial-era dams and invest in early flood-warning systems for reservoirs near dense settlements.

evt-03-27-2014-government-of-the-philipp.scenario: It is 27 March 2014 in Manila. After nearly two decades of conflict and failed ceasefires in Mindanao, you watch government negotiators and rebel representatives prepare to sign a landmark accord.
evt-03-27-2014-government-of-the-philipp.prompt: What does this agreement establish for the country's largest Muslim rebel group?

choices.text: Full independence for Mindanao as a separate nation
A United Nations peacekeeping mission in the south
Abolition of the Philippine Congress
An autonomous Bangsamoro region within the Philippines

evt-03-27-2014-government-of-the-philipp.butterflyEffect: The Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro paved the way for the 2018 Bangsamoro Organic Law and the 2019 creation of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, giving Moro Filipinos greater self-governance, though violence from splinter factions continued in following years.

evt-03-27-2015-himeji-castle.scenario: You join the crowds gathering outside Himeji Castle in late March 2015 as its gates reopen to the public for the first time in years, its walls gleaming brighter than anyone remembers.
evt-03-27-2015-himeji-castle.prompt: What project has just been finished before the castle reopens to visitors?

choices.text: A restoration of the main keep's white plaster walls
Demolition of unsafe wooden turrets
Addition of a modern visitor museum on the grounds
Construction of a new outer moat

evt-03-27-2015-himeji-castle.butterflyEffect: A multi-year restoration recoated the main keep's plaster walls, restoring the brilliant white finish that earns the castle its nickname, Shirasagi-jō, 'White Heron Castle.' The refreshed landmark drew a surge of visitors and reinforced its standing as one of Japan's most celebrated UNESCO World Heritage sites.

evt-03-27-2015-al-shabaab-militant-group.scenario: It is 27 March 2015, and you are a Somali security officer as al-Shabaab gunmen detonate a car bomb at the gate of Mogadishu's Makka al-Mukarama Hotel, a popular meeting place for officials and MPs, then storm inside and begin a siege.
evt-03-27-2015-al-shabaab-militant-group.prompt: What do Somali security forces do to end the siege?

choices.text: They negotiate the militants' safe passage out of the city
They storm the hotel and kill the attackers after a lengthy siege
They evacuate the hotel and abandon it to al-Shabaab
They call in African Union airstrikes on the hotel itself

evt-03-27-2015-al-shabaab-militant-group.butterflyEffect: Government forces stormed the hotel and killed the attackers after an hours-long gun battle, but not before at least 20 people, including a member of parliament, were killed. The attack exposed how deeply al-Shabaab could still strike the heart of Mogadishu, prompting a tightening of security around the capital's hotels.

evt-03-27-2016-2016-lahore-suicide-bombi.scenario: It is the morning after Easter Sunday, 27 March 2016, and you are a Pakistani counter-terrorism official reviewing the aftermath of the bombing at Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park in Lahore, where Christian families had gathered to celebrate.
evt-03-27-2016-2016-lahore-suicide-bombi.prompt: What does the Pakistani government do in the attack's immediate aftermath?

choices.text: It declares the attack an isolated criminal incident and takes no further action
It withdraws Pakistani forces from the region entirely
It launches a widespread counter-terrorism crackdown in South Punjab
It opens negotiations with Jamaat-ul-Ahrar

evt-03-27-2016-2016-lahore-suicide-bombi.butterflyEffect: Pakistan launched a sweeping counter-terrorism operation across South Punjab, arresting more than 200 people with suspected links to the attack. The bombing, claimed by a Pakistani Taliban faction, drew worldwide condemnation and days of national mourning.

evt-03-27-2020-north-macedonia-nato-rela.scenario: You are a diplomat from Skopje in the late 2010s, watching your country's NATO bid stall year after year because of Greece's veto over a decades-old naming dispute.
evt-03-27-2020-north-macedonia-nato-rela.prompt: What must your country do to finally unlock NATO membership?

choices.text: Withdraw from the Partnership for Peace program
Hold a national referendum on leaving the EU accession process
Sign a bilateral defense pact with Greece instead of joining NATO
Rename the country to resolve the dispute with Greece

evt-03-27-2020-north-macedonia-nato-rela.butterflyEffect: Under the 2018 Prespa Agreement, Macedonia formally renamed itself North Macedonia, resolving the dispute with Greece and clearing the way for accession. On March 27, 2020, it became NATO's 30th member, extending the alliance further into the Balkans.

evt-03-27-2020-north-macedonia.scenario: It is 2018, and you are a Macedonian diplomat tasked with ending your country's decades-long dispute with Greece over its name, a dispute that has blocked your nation's path into NATO and the European Union.
evt-03-27-2020-north-macedonia.prompt: What do you do to break the deadlock?

choices.text: You seek EU membership without pursuing NATO at all
You agree to rename the country to the Republic of North Macedonia
You refuse any name change and abandon NATO membership talks
You appeal to the United Nations to force Greece to drop its objection unconditionally

evt-03-27-2020-north-macedonia.butterflyEffect: Under the Prespa Agreement, the country accepted the name "Republic of North Macedonia," satisfying Greek objections and unlocking the NATO accession process. Two years later, on 27 March 2020, North Macedonia formally became NATO's 30th member.

evt-03-27-2023-2023-nashville-school-sho.scenario: You are one of the first Metro Nashville officers through the door of The Covenant School on the morning of March 27, 2023, after dispatch reports an active shooter inside.
evt-03-27-2023-2023-nashville-school-sho.prompt: What do you and the other responding officers do once inside?

choices.text: Attempt to open a phone line to negotiate with the shooter
Begin evacuating classrooms before searching for the shooter
Establish a perimeter outside and wait for a SWAT team
Move directly toward the sound of gunfire to confront the shooter

evt-03-27-2023-2023-nashville-school-sho.butterflyEffect: Officers Rex Engelbert and Michael Collazo moved directly toward the gunfire and shot the perpetrator within minutes of arriving, a response credited with limiting further loss of life. The attack renewed intense national debate over school security and gun policy.

evt-03-28-193-praetorian-guard.scenario: It is March 28, 193 AD, and you are a Praetorian guardsman in Rome, resentful that Emperor Pertinax has imposed strict discipline and refused to pay the donative he promised the Guard on taking the throne.
evt-03-28-193-praetorian-guard.prompt: What do you and your fellow guardsmen do about Pertinax?

choices.text: Petition the Senate to remove Pertinax through legal means
Proclaim a rival emperor from the legions stationed in Rome
Desert en masse and disband the Guard
Storm the palace, kill Pertinax, and sell the throne to the highest bidder

evt-03-28-193-praetorian-guard.butterflyEffect: The Guard stormed the palace, killed Pertinax after just 87 days as emperor, and then auctioned the throne to the highest bidder, Didius Julianus. This mockery of imperial authority disgusted the provincial legions, triggering the chaotic Year of the Five Emperors and Septimius Severus's march on Rome to seize power.

evt-03-28-1802-heinrich-wilhelm-matthias.scenario: It is the night of March 28, 1802, and you are astronomer Heinrich Olbers in Bremen, tracking a faint point of light moving slowly against the fixed stars, one that matches no charted planet or comet.
evt-03-28-1802-heinrich-wilhelm-matthias.prompt: What does Olbers conclude this newly spotted object actually is?

choices.text: A previously undiscovered short-period comet
An uncatalogued variable star
A fragment ejected from the planet Uranus
A new minor planet, later named Pallas

evt-03-28-1802-heinrich-wilhelm-matthias.butterflyEffect: Olbers had found Pallas, only the second asteroid ever identified after Ceres. His careful orbit calculations helped astronomers recognize a whole population of small bodies between Mars and Jupiter, fueling decades of searches that eventually catalogued thousands of minor planets.

evt-03-28-1918-world-war-i.scenario: It is dawn on 28 March 1918 near Dernancourt, France. You are an Australian infantryman dug in along a railway embankment as waves of German storm troops advance, part of the great Spring Offensive threatening to break the Allied line.
evt-03-28-1918-world-war-i.prompt: How should the defenders respond to the numerically superior German assault?

choices.text: Withdraw immediately to consolidate a new line at Amiens
Launch an immediate cavalry counter-charge against the German columns
Abandon the position and demolish the nearby railway bridge
Hold the railway embankment and pour concentrated rifle and machine-gun fire into the advancing waves

evt-03-28-1918-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The Australians held their embankment positions, pouring fire into the advancing German waves and inflicting heavy losses at First Dernancourt. It became one of the few clear-cut defensive successes against the Spring Offensive, and helped build the reputation of Australian troops as formidable defenders who would soon spearhead the Allied counteroffensives that ended the war that year.

evt-03-28-1935-propaganda-in-nazi-german.scenario: It's 1935 and you sit in a German cinema watching Leni Riefenstahl's newly released film of the 1934 Nuremberg rally — sweeping crowds, torchlight, and adoring salutes to Hitler filling the screen.
evt-03-28-1935-propaganda-in-nazi-german.prompt: What was the film's real purpose beyond simply documenting the rally?

choices.text: To advertise German cinema technology abroad
To recruit foreign tourists to visit Germany
To present Hitler and the Nazi movement as an unstoppable, unified force
To record the rally purely as a historical archive

evt-03-28-1935-propaganda-in-nazi-german.butterflyEffect: Triumph of the Will became one of the most effective propaganda films ever made, pioneering techniques for manufacturing an illusion of total national unity that are still studied today. It helped normalize the Nazi state ahead of its most aggressive years, and its imagery continues to shape how mass dictatorship is depicted on screen.

evt-03-28-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 28 March 1942. You are aboard the obsolete destroyer HMS Campbeltown, packed with hidden delayed-action explosives, racing under German fire toward the dry dock gates of Saint-Nazaire on the French Atlantic coast.
evt-03-28-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What is the raiders' primary objective in ramming Campbeltown into the dock gates?

choices.text: Blow up the local U-boat pens to sink docked submarines
Capture the German harbourmaster for intelligence purposes
Destroy the only dry dock on the Atlantic coast large enough to service the battleship Tirpitz
Block the harbour entrance to trap French Resistance saboteurs inside

evt-03-28-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The ship's hidden charges detonated hours later as planned, destroying the Normandie dock, which stayed unusable until 1947. Denied the only Atlantic dry dock able to service it, the battleship Tirpitz was effectively confined to threatening Arctic convoys from Norway, easing pressure on Britain's Atlantic lifeline. The daring raid, later called 'The Greatest Raid of All', also gave Allied morale a lift after a string of setbacks.

evt-03-28-1979-james-callaghan.scenario: It's the evening of 28 March 1979 in the House of Commons. Prime Minister James Callaghan's government hangs on a knife-edge no-confidence motion, and you are an MP about to cast the deciding vote.
evt-03-28-1979-james-callaghan.prompt: What happens after MPs vote 311 to 310 against Callaghan's government?

choices.text: Callaghan forms an emergency coalition to avoid an election
Callaghan resigns immediately without calling an election
Callaghan is forced to call a general election, which Labour goes on to lose
The vote is annulled on a technicality and Callaghan stays in office

evt-03-28-1979-james-callaghan.butterflyEffect: Callaghan became the last British PM forced from office by a Commons no-confidence vote. The general election that followed in May 1979 brought Margaret Thatcher to power, launching eighteen years of Conservative government.

evt-03-28-1979-three-mile-island-nuclear.scenario: It's the early hours of 28 March 1979 in the control room of TMI Unit 2. A relief valve has stuck open and coolant is draining away, yet your gauges show misleadingly high water levels in the reactor.
evt-03-28-1979-three-mile-island-nuclear.prompt: What do operators do based on the misleading water-level readings?

choices.text: They cut back emergency cooling water flow, worsening the core damage
They shut down the whole plant safely without incident
They flood the reactor with extra coolant right away
They order full evacuation of Harrisburg immediately
