evt-03-28-1979-three-mile-island-nuclear.butterflyEffect: The reduced cooling flow let the core partially melt, becoming the worst commercial nuclear accident in US history. Though no one died from radiation exposure, the crisis froze new US nuclear plant construction for decades and reshaped reactor safety and control-room design worldwide.

evt-03-28-1990-george-h-w-bush.scenario: It's 28 March 1990 in the White House, a decade after Jesse Owens's death, and President George H. W. Bush stands ready to honor the sprinter's legacy before Owens's family and dignitaries.
evt-03-28-1990-george-h-w-bush.prompt: What honor does Bush bestow on Owens that day?

choices.text: The Congressional Gold Medal
The National Medal of Arts
The Olympic Order
The Presidential Medal of Freedom

evt-03-28-1990-george-h-w-bush.butterflyEffect: The Congressional Gold Medal recognized Owens's four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics, won in defiance of Hitler's racial ideology. The award cemented Owens's status as an enduring symbol of athletic excellence over prejudice, reinforced by later tributes including a US postage stamp.

evt-03-28-1994-african-national-congress.scenario: It is March 28, 1994, weeks before South Africa's first democratic election. You stand near Shell House, the ANC's Johannesburg headquarters, as thousands of Inkatha Freedom Party supporters march toward the building.
evt-03-28-1994-african-national-congress.prompt: What do ANC security guards do as the IFP marchers approach Shell House?

choices.text: Negotiate with IFP leaders to allow safe passage past the building
Send ANC leadership out to address the crowd peacefully
Retreat inside and lock down the building until police arrive
Open fire on the marchers, killing dozens

evt-03-28-1994-african-national-congress.butterflyEffect: Guards opened fire on the marchers, killing at least 53 people in one of the bloodiest single incidents of the transition era. Nelson Mandela publicly defended the shooting as self-defense, straining ANC-IFP relations just before the April election, and the killings remained a source of legal and political controversy for years afterward.

evt-03-28-1997-tragedy-of-otranto.scenario: It is 28 March 1997 in the Strait of Otranto. You command the Italian Navy corvette Sibilla, ordered to stop the overloaded Albanian vessel Kateri i Radës, crowded with families fleeing civil unrest, from reaching Italian shores.
evt-03-28-1997-tragedy-of-otranto.prompt: Following the Italian Navy's blockade policy, what does the Sibilla attempt as it closes on the fleeing ferry?

choices.text: Let the ferry pass unimpeded into open water
Escort the ferry safely into an Italian port for processing
Radio nearby fishing boats to tow the ferry back to Albania
Manoeuvre to block and turn the overcrowded ferry back toward Albania

evt-03-28-1997-tragedy-of-otranto.butterflyEffect: The manoeuvre to turn the ferry back ended in a collision that sank the Kateri i Radës, killing at least 84 people, including children. The tragedy provoked public outrage in both countries, led to the prosecution of the Sibilla's commander, and pushed Italy and Albania toward replacing unilateral naval blockades with joint patrol agreements.

evt-03-28-2001-athens-international-airp.scenario: It is 28 March 2001 in Athens. You are an aviation official overseeing the final handover as decades of flights shift from the old Ellinikon Airport to the brand-new Eleftherios Venizelos Airport outside the city.
evt-03-28-2001-athens-international-airp.prompt: What happens to Athens' old airport, Ellinikon, once the new one opens?

choices.text: It is converted into a permanent Greek Air Force base
It closes and its site is later redeveloped for major public and commercial use
It continues operating as Athens' dedicated domestic airport indefinitely
It is expanded and kept running alongside the new airport

evt-03-28-2001-athens-international-airp.butterflyEffect: Ellinikon closed for good and its vast coastal site was mothballed, later hosting venues for the 2004 Athens Olympics. Decades on, the former airport became the centrepiece of Hellinikon, one of Europe's largest urban redevelopment projects, transforming the old runways into parks, housing and business districts.

evt-03-28-2005-2005-nias-simeulue-earthq.scenario: It's just after 11pm on 28 March 2005 on the coast of Sumatra, and the ground is still trembling from a massive earthquake — barely three months after the region's devastating tsunami. The shaking eases and you must decide what to do next.
evt-03-28-2005-2005-nias-simeulue-earthq.prompt: What is the safest immediate action as the shaking stops?

choices.text: Call relatives before deciding what to do
Return home first to check on belongings
Move quickly to higher ground in case a tsunami follows
Wait on the beach to see if the sea recedes

evt-03-28-2005-2005-nias-simeulue-earthq.butterflyEffect: Thousands fled inland across Sumatra, and even as far as Sri Lanka, fearing a repeat of December's tsunami, though this quake produced only a modest, localized wave. The scare highlighted the urgent need for a working Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System, which began operating later that year.

evt-03-28-2006-2006-youth-protests-in-fr.scenario: It is March 28, 2006, and you march through Paris with over a million students, union members and unemployed workers, protesting a new law that would let employers fire under-26 workers without cause during their first two years on the job.
evt-03-28-2006-2006-youth-protests-in-fr.prompt: What ultimately happens to the disputed CPE labor law after weeks of nationwide protest?

choices.text: Chirac dissolves parliament and calls new elections
The government withdraws the CPE clause and replaces it with a milder scheme
The Senate blocks the bill indefinitely without any formal repeal
Police crack down and the law is enforced unchanged

evt-03-28-2006-2006-youth-protests-in-fr.butterflyEffect: Facing sustained pressure, President Chirac's government withdrew the CPE clause and replaced it with a milder youth employment scheme. The episode became a landmark victory for French student and union mobilization and left the government politically weakened heading into the 2007 elections.

evt-03-28-2015-2015-makka-al-mukarama-ho.scenario: It is the morning of 28 March 2015. You lead an elite Gaashaan unit soldier stacked outside the besieged Makka al-Mukarama hotel in Mogadishu, where Al-Shabaab gunmen have been holding guests through the night.
evt-03-28-2015-2015-makka-al-mukarama-ho.prompt: What did the security forces do to end the siege and free the trapped guests?

choices.text: Storm the building directly to kill the attackers and rescue hostages
Call in an airstrike on the hotel itself
Surround the building and wait for the militants to surrender on their own
Negotiate a ceasefire and let the militants leave freely

evt-03-28-2015-2015-makka-al-mukarama-ho.butterflyEffect: Gaashaan commandos stormed the hotel, killed all five attackers, and rescued more than 50 guests, though around 20 people died overall including security personnel and civilians. The government ordered an investigation and pledged new laws against illicit firearms, and the hotel reopened after renovations that May.

evt-03-28-2025-2025-myanmar-earthquake.scenario: It is just after 1 pm on 28 March 2025. The ground beneath Mandalay, Myanmar's second-largest city, is still shuddering after a massive earthquake, and you are trying to gauge just how historic this rupture really is.
evt-03-28-2025-2025-myanmar-earthquake.prompt: What made this earthquake so significant in Myanmar's modern history?

choices.text: It triggered a major tsunami across the Bay of Bengal
It was the first earthquake ever recorded in Myanmar
It was the most powerful earthquake to hit Myanmar since 1912
It was centered in Yangon, Myanmar's largest city

evt-03-28-2025-2025-myanmar-earthquake.butterflyEffect: At magnitude 7.7–7.9, it was the most powerful earthquake to strike Myanmar since 1912 and the second deadliest in the country's modern era, killing more than 5,000 people. Damage extended far beyond Myanmar's borders, cracking buildings in Bangkok, Yunnan, and Ho Chi Minh City, exposing how a single fault rupture could ripple across mainland Southeast Asia.

evt-03-29-845-viking-expansion.scenario: It is Easter 845, and you stand beside King Charles the Bald as a Viking fleet, said to be led by Ragnar Lodbrok, besieges Paris and threatens to sack the city.
evt-03-29-845-viking-expansion.prompt: How did Charles the Bald secure the Vikings' withdrawal?

choices.text: He persuaded the Viking leader to convert to Christianity on the spot
He paid a huge tribute of silver for the raiders to leave
He called on his brother Louis the German to send reinforcements
He led his army to a decisive victory outside the walls

evt-03-29-845-viking-expansion.butterflyEffect: Charles's payment of roughly 7,000 pounds of silver, an early Danegeld, bought Paris a temporary reprieve but signaled to Norse raiders across the Frankish lands that tribute was easier than fighting. Similar payoffs became routine through the ninth century, encouraging repeated Viking raids deep into Francia.

evt-03-29-1430-siege-of-thessalonica-142.scenario: Dawn breaks over Thessalonica's walls in 1430. Sultan Murad II's forces, after eight grinding years of siege, finally breach the defenses and pour into the city.
evt-03-29-1430-siege-of-thessalonica-142.prompt: What actually followed the fall of Thessalonica to the Ottomans?

choices.text: Venice recaptured the city the following year
The city stayed under Ottoman control for nearly 500 years
The city was abandoned and left in ruins
Thessalonica was returned to Byzantine rule within a decade

evt-03-29-1430-siege-of-thessalonica-142.butterflyEffect: The city remained under Ottoman rule for nearly five centuries, only becoming part of the Kingdom of Greece in 1912. Its fall marked one of the last major Byzantine cities to be lost before Constantinople itself fell in 1453.

evt-03-29-1461-wars-of-the-roses.scenario: It is dawn on 29 March 1461, and a blinding snowstorm sweeps across Towton field as you stand among Lord Fauconberg's Yorkist archers, facing the massed Lancastrian ranks.
evt-03-29-1461-wars-of-the-roses.prompt: What tactic did the Yorkist archers use to exploit the storm?

choices.text: They charged the enemy line with pikes before archers could fire
They advanced, loosed a volley, then fell back to let the wind carry Lancastrian arrows short
They set fire to the frozen moor to blind the Lancastrians
They retreated entirely, luring the enemy into an ambush downhill

evt-03-29-1461-wars-of-the-roses.butterflyEffect: The trick emptied Lancastrian arrow supplies while Yorkist bowmen still had ammunition, and the ensuing slaughter became the bloodiest battle fought on English soil. The Lancastrian defeat drove Henry VI into exile and secured Edward IV's claim to the throne, though the Wars of the Roses would grind on for decades.

evt-03-29-1800-william-matthews-priest.scenario: It's 1800 in Maryland, and you are about to be ordained by Bishop John Carroll, becoming the first Catholic priest born in British America.
evt-03-29-1800-william-matthews-priest.prompt: What role did Matthews go on to take up after his ordination?

choices.text: Missionary priest in the Louisiana Territory
Pastor of St. Patrick's Church and president of Georgetown College
Returned to England for further study
First Catholic bishop of Boston

evt-03-29-1800-william-matthews-priest.butterflyEffect: Matthews became pastor of St. Patrick's Church in Washington, D.C., and later served as president of Georgetown College. His career helped establish American-born clergy as leaders within the young U.S. Catholic Church.

evt-03-29-1807-heinrich-wilhelm-matthias.scenario: It's March 1807 in Bremen, and through your telescope you've spotted an unfamiliar point of light drifting slowly against the fixed stars. You need to determine what it is.
evt-03-29-1807-heinrich-wilhelm-matthias.prompt: What should you do to confirm this is a new asteroid rather than a star or comet?

choices.text: Wait for a lunar eclipse before checking again
Assume it is a fixed star and ignore it
Publish a discovery announcement immediately without further observation
Track its motion against the background stars over several nights

evt-03-29-1807-heinrich-wilhelm-matthias.butterflyEffect: Olbers confirmed it as a new asteroid, the fourth ever found, and mathematician Carl Friedrich Gauss suggested naming it Vesta after the Roman goddess. Vesta remains one of the brightest asteroids visible from Earth and a key target of later spacecraft study.

evt-03-29-1823-joaquin-de-oreamuno.scenario: It's late March 1823 in Costa Rica. Joaquín de Oreamuno has just seized power in a coup, aiming to bind the province to the First Mexican Empire, and republican leaders must decide how to respond.
evt-03-29-1823-joaquin-de-oreamuno.prompt: What should opposing republican leaders do to counter the coup?

choices.text: Petition Spain to restore colonial rule
Rally republican militia under Gregorio José Ramírez
Flee north to Guatemala
Submit to the new imperialist government

evt-03-29-1823-joaquin-de-oreamuno.butterflyEffect: Republican forces under Gregorio José Ramírez defeated the imperialists days later at the Battle of Ochomogo. The victory ended the push to annex Costa Rica to Mexico and set the country on its path toward independent republican government.

evt-03-29-1865-american-civil-war.scenario: It is March 29, 1865, near Petersburg, Virginia. You march with Warren's Union V Corps along the Quaker Road, probing Confederate lines to extend the siege and cut Lee's last supply routes.
evt-03-29-1865-american-civil-war.prompt: What did this opening battle of the Appomattox campaign set in motion?

choices.text: It ended in a Confederate victory that prolonged the war for months
It began the final Union offensive that led to Lee's retreat and surrender at Appomattox
It forced Grant to abandon the siege of Petersburg
It allowed Lee to break through and retake Richmond

evt-03-29-1865-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Battle of Lewis's Farm opened Grant's final offensive. Within days Union victory at Five Forks forced Lee to abandon Petersburg and Richmond, leading straight to his surrender at Appomattox Court House on April 9, 1865, effectively ending the Civil War.

evt-03-29-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 28-29 March 1941 off Cape Matapan, and you serve aboard a radar-equipped British battleship closing silently on unsuspecting Italian cruisers in the darkness.
evt-03-29-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: What let the British fleet strike the Italian ships so decisively at night?

choices.text: Aerial flares dropped by carrier aircraft lit up the targets
Sonar detected the Italian ships' engine noise underwater
Coded radio intercepts revealed the exact firing positions
Radar allowed British ships to track and target the enemy in total darkness

evt-03-29-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The surprise night action sank three Italian heavy cruisers and two destroyers for minimal British loss, crippling the Regia Marina's willingness to risk major surface engagements. British naval dominance in the Mediterranean was reinforced just as the evacuation of Allied troops from Greece was becoming urgent.

evt-03-29-1968-funeral-of-yuri-gagarin-a.scenario: It is 30 March 1968 in Moscow, and you stand among the crowds lining Red Square as the Soviet state prepares to honor Yuri Gagarin, killed days earlier alongside instructor Vladimir Seryogin in a training jet crash.
evt-03-29-1968-funeral-of-yuri-gagarin-a.prompt: What does the Soviet government do with Gagarin's remains after the state funeral?

choices.text: Bury him in his hometown of Klushino
Place him in a mausoleum beside Lenin
Launch his remains into orbit as a memorial
Inter his ashes in the Kremlin Wall Necropolis

evt-03-29-1968-funeral-of-yuri-gagarin-a.butterflyEffect: Gagarin's ashes were placed in the Kremlin Wall Necropolis on Red Square, among the Soviet Union's most honored figures, cementing his status as a state icon. His unexplained crash also fueled decades of investigation and speculation about Soviet aviation safety and secrecy.

evt-03-29-1974-nasa.scenario: It is 29 March 1974, and you are a NASA engineer in mission control as Mariner 10 makes its historic close approach to Mercury, the first spacecraft ever to reach the planet.
evt-03-29-1974-nasa.prompt: What surprising discovery did Mariner 10 make about Mercury?

choices.text: The planet has its own weak but genuine magnetic field
A thick, cloud-covered atmosphere like Venus's
Active volcanic plumes erupting from its surface
A faint ring system encircling the planet

evt-03-29-1974-nasa.butterflyEffect: Mariner 10's detection of an intrinsic magnetic field around such a small, slowly rotating planet baffled scientists and forced a rethink of how planetary cores generate magnetism. The mission also pioneered the gravity-assist trajectory, using Venus to reach Mercury, a technique now standard for deep-space missions.

evt-03-29-1974-shaanxi.scenario: It's March 1974 near Xi'an, and you're digging a well with fellow farmers when your shovel strikes something hard. Brushing away the soil, a life-sized clay face stares back at you.
evt-03-29-1974-shaanxi.prompt: What should you do with this strange discovery?

choices.text: Smash it, believing it a bad omen
Sell the pieces to a passing collector
Report the find to local authorities
Rebury it and keep digging elsewhere

evt-03-29-1974-shaanxi.butterflyEffect: The farmers' report led archaeologists to the Terracotta Army, thousands of life-sized clay soldiers built to guard the tomb of China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang. It became one of the 20th century's greatest archaeological finds and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

evt-03-29-1975-jeff-beck.scenario: It's 1975, and you're a rock guitarist watching Jeff Beck's career take a sharp turn — after years fronting bands with singers, he's releasing an album with no vocals at all, produced by a Beatles veteran.
evt-03-29-1975-jeff-beck.prompt: What move did Beck make with Blow by Blow that reshaped his career?

choices.text: He recorded a full album of acoustic blues covers
He retired from music to focus on car racing
He abandoned vocal-led rock for an instrumental jazz-fusion sound produced by George Martin
He reunited with the Yardbirds for one final album

evt-03-29-1975-jeff-beck.butterflyEffect: Blow by Blow, produced by George Martin, became Beck's best-selling US album and one of the most successful instrumental rock records ever made, cementing him as a guitarist's guitarist rather than a frontman. It opened the door to a run of jazz-fusion work that influenced generations of instrumental guitarists.

evt-03-29-1981-dick-beardsley.scenario: You are Dick Beardsley, sprinting through the final mile of the inaugural London Marathon on 29 March 1981, matched stride for stride with Norway's Inge Simonsen, with no other runner in sight before the finish line.
evt-03-29-1981-dick-beardsley.prompt: What do you do as you and Simonsen approach the finish line together?

choices.text: Slow down and let him win outright
Stop to negotiate a split prize with officials
Grab his hand and cross the line together as joint winners
Sprint ahead for a solo victory

evt-03-29-1981-dick-beardsley.butterflyEffect: Beardsley and Simonsen linked arms and crossed the line together, sharing the first men's title in London Marathon history. The gesture became a beloved symbol of the race's spirit, though later rule changes required a single declared winner in future events.

evt-03-29-1982-elizabeth-ii.scenario: It's March 29, 1982, in London, and you watch Queen Elizabeth II give royal assent to a bill severing one of the last legal ties between Britain and Canada.
evt-03-29-1982-elizabeth-ii.prompt: What did the Canada Act 1982 actually accomplish?

choices.text: It patriated Canada's constitution, ending the UK Parliament's power to amend Canadian law
It abolished the Canadian Senate
It granted Quebec full independence from Canada
It made Canada a republic, replacing the monarchy with an elected president

evt-03-29-1982-elizabeth-ii.butterflyEffect: The Canada Act ended the last vestige of British legislative authority over Canada, and its companion Constitution Act 1982 added the Charter of Rights and Freedoms. Quebec never signed on to the new constitutional settlement, a rift that still shapes Canadian federal politics today.

evt-03-29-2004-bulgaria.scenario: It is March 29, 2004, and you watch flags raised outside NATO headquarters in Brussels as Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania and Slovakia complete a process years in the making.
evt-03-29-2004-bulgaria.prompt: What historic step do these former Eastern Bloc and Baltic states take today?

choices.text: They formally become full members of NATO
They sign treaties to join the European Union
They adopt the euro as their national currency
They ratify a successor treaty to the Warsaw Pact

evt-03-29-2004-bulgaria.butterflyEffect: These states, along with Slovenia, formally became full NATO members in the alliance's largest enlargement to date, extending Article 5 collective defense guarantees deep into former Soviet territory. Many of the same countries joined the European Union just weeks later in May 2004, reshaping Europe's post-Cold War security and political map.

evt-03-29-2010-caucasus-emirate.scenario: It is the morning of 29 March 2010, and you are a Kremlin security official learning that two female suicide bombers have just struck packed Moscow Metro trains during rush hour.
evt-03-29-2010-caucasus-emirate.prompt: How did the Russian government respond to the attack?

choices.text: It withdrew federal forces from Chechnya
It granted a general amnesty to separatist fighters
It launched an intensified security and counterinsurgency crackdown across the North Caucasus
It opened negotiations with Caucasus Emirate leaders

evt-03-29-2010-caucasus-emirate.butterflyEffect: Then-Prime Minister Vladimir Putin vowed to 'drag [the perpetrators] out of the sewers,' and Russian forces intensified operations against militants in Chechnya and Dagestan. Caucasus Emirate leader Dokka Umarov, who claimed responsibility, was eventually tracked down and killed in 2013.

evt-03-29-2010-2010-moscow-metro-bombing.scenario: It's the morning of 29 March 2010. Two bombs have just torn through Lubyanka and Park Kultury stations during Moscow's rush hour, and investigators are racing to identify who is responsible.
evt-03-29-2010-2010-moscow-metro-bombing.prompt: What did investigators determine had motivated the attack?

choices.text: A radical Islamist insurgency from the North Caucasus claimed responsibility
Chechen separatists publicly denied any connection
A far-right nationalist group sought to destabilize the government
The bombings were traced to a criminal gang dispute

evt-03-29-2010-2010-moscow-metro-bombing.butterflyEffect: Caucasus Emirate leader Doku Umarov claimed responsibility, framing the bombings as revenge for Russian security operations in the North Caucasus. The attack intensified Russian counterterrorism crackdowns in the region and was followed by further insurgent violence in the years after.

evt-03-29-2015-air-canada-flight-624.scenario: It's just after midnight on March 29, 2015, in blinding snow at Halifax airport, and you're a first responder rushing toward an Airbus A320 that has come down short of the runway, shearing off power lines and losing its landing gear.
evt-03-29-2015-air-canada-flight-624.prompt: What was the outcome for those aboard the aircraft?

choices.text: The aircraft caught fire on impact, killing several passengers
The plane overshot the runway into the harbor
Everyone escaped without any injuries at all
Everyone survived; 25 were injured, two seriously, in a rare survivable runway undershoot

evt-03-29-2015-air-canada-flight-624.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew had not properly monitored altitude during a non-precision approach in poor visibility, prompting a review of approach procedures and cockpit instrumentation at Halifax and similar snow-prone airports. The crash became a widely cited case study in aviation safety training on controlled-flight-into-terrain risk.

evt-03-29-2017-theresa-may.scenario: It is 29 March 2017, and you watch as Prime Minister Theresa May's letter formally invoking Article 50 is handed to European Council President Donald Tusk in Brussels.
evt-03-29-2017-theresa-may.prompt: What deadline did triggering Article 50 set in motion?

choices.text: An open-ended process with no fixed exit date
A two-year negotiating window for the UK's withdrawal, due to expire in March 2019
An immediate, same-day departure from the EU
A five-year transition period before any negotiations began

evt-03-29-2017-theresa-may.butterflyEffect: The original March 2019 deadline was missed as Parliament repeatedly rejected the negotiated withdrawal agreement, forcing multiple extensions and contributing to May's resignation. The UK finally left the EU on 31 January 2020 under her successor, Boris Johnson.

evt-03-29-2017-prime-minister-of-the-uni.scenario: It's March 29, 2017, in Westminster, and you watch Prime Minister Theresa May sign the letter formally starting Britain's departure from the European Union.
evt-03-29-2017-prime-minister-of-the-uni.prompt: What did invoking Article 50 set in motion?

choices.text: A second referendum on EU membership
A fixed two-year negotiating period for the UK's withdrawal from the EU
A formal request to join the European Economic Area instead
An immediate exit from the EU with no negotiation period

evt-03-29-2017-prime-minister-of-the-uni.butterflyEffect: Triggering Article 50 began formal Brexit negotiations that ran past the original deadline, through parliamentary deadlock, and outlasted two more prime ministers, before the UK finally left the EU on 31 January 2020. Those years reshaped UK trade policy, immigration rules, and its constitutional relationship with Northern Ireland and Scotland.

evt-03-29-2021-ever-given.scenario: It's March 29, 2021, and you're on the salvage team in the Suez Canal, watching tugboats strain against a grounded 400-meter container ship that has blocked one of the world's busiest trade routes for six days.
evt-03-29-2021-ever-given.prompt: What finally freed the Ever Given and reopened the canal?

choices.text: Engineers cut a new channel around the grounded ship
Dredging combined with tugboats and a high tide finally refloated the vessel
The ship's crew abandoned it and it was later demolished in place
The Egyptian navy towed it out using warships alone

evt-03-29-2021-ever-given.butterflyEffect: The Ever Given's grounding blocked roughly $9 billion in daily trade and exposed how fragile global supply chains had become, already strained by the pandemic. The incident pushed shipping firms to rethink ultra-large vessel routing and canal authorities to widen and deepen the waterway.

evt-03-30-1282-sicilian-vespers.scenario: It's Easter Monday, 1282, in Palermo, and a French sergeant's harassment of a Sicilian woman outside a church sparks a brawl. You watch the crowd's long-simmering anger at Charles of Anjou's occupying garrison boil over.
evt-03-30-1282-sicilian-vespers.prompt: What did the enraged Sicilians do next?

choices.text: Petitioned Charles I peacefully for lower taxes
Handed the woman over to French authorities to avoid punishment
Rose up in a citywide revolt against the French garrison
Fled the city to avoid confrontation

evt-03-30-1282-sicilian-vespers.butterflyEffect: The uprising spread rapidly across the island, ending Angevin rule within weeks and triggering the War of the Sicilian Vespers as Sicilians turned to the King of Aragon for a new crown. The resulting conflict dragged on for decades, permanently splitting southern Italy into rival Neapolitan and Sicilian kingdoms.

evt-03-30-1730-the-author-s-farce.scenario: London, 1730. The patent Theatre Royal has rejected your plays outright. You have taken a chance on the smaller, unlicensed Little Theatre in the Haymarket, free to break every rule of polite comedy.
evt-03-30-1730-the-author-s-farce.prompt: How does Fielding shape his new play to mock London's theatre world?

choices.text: He blends a play-within-a-play with a satirical puppet show mocking London's cultural fads
He stages a historical pageant celebrating the monarchy
He writes a solemn classical tragedy to win the Theatre Royal's favour
He composes an opera seria in the Italian style

evt-03-30-1730-the-author-s-farce.butterflyEffect: The Author's Farce mixed a rehearsal-comedy with a mock puppet-show satire of London's literary and theatrical fashions, and became Fielding's first real hit. Its success launched his career as a satirical playwright, culminating in works so pointed that the government's 1737 Licensing Act effectively shut down his stage career — pushing him toward the novels, including Tom Jones, for which he is now best remembered.

evt-03-30-1815-joachim-murat.scenario: It is March 1815, and you serve Joachim Murat, King of Naples, as Napoleon's dramatic return from Elba threatens to reignite war across Europe. Murat must decide whether to gamble his throne on a bold call to arms.
evt-03-30-1815-joachim-murat.prompt: What did Murat's Rimini Proclamation call on Italians to do?

choices.text: Rise up and unite in a single independent Italian nation
Ally with Britain against France
Support the restoration of the Bourbon king of Naples
Submit peacefully to Austrian rule

evt-03-30-1815-joachim-murat.butterflyEffect: Murat's appeal for Italian unity failed to rally enough support in time; Austria crushed his forces at Tolentino weeks later and he fled Naples. Captured in Calabria that October, he was executed by firing squad, but his proclamation is remembered as an early spark of the Italian unification movement that fed into the later Risorgimento.

evt-03-30-1822-east-florida.scenario: You are a territorial official in 1822, watching Congress act on the recently acquired Spanish province, deciding how to organize the former colonies of East and West Florida under American rule.
evt-03-30-1822-east-florida.prompt: What does the U.S. government do with the two former Spanish Floridas?

choices.text: Merge them into a single Florida Territory
Return administrative control to Spain
Keep them as separate territories indefinitely
Divide the land among neighboring states

evt-03-30-1822-east-florida.butterflyEffect: Congress merged East and West Florida into the single Florida Territory in 1822, with Andrew Jackson briefly serving as its first governor. This consolidation set the course toward Florida's eventual admission as a slave state in 1845, deepening its ties to the plantation South.

evt-03-30-1861-william-crookes.scenario: London, 1861. You are examining residues from a selenium extraction using flame spectroscopy, and a spectral line of an unfamiliar, brilliant green appears where none of the known elements should produce one.
evt-03-30-1861-william-crookes.prompt: What do you conclude from this unexplained green spectral line?

choices.text: It confirms the presence of ordinary tellurium
It is simply contamination from the laboratory glassware
It signals the discovery of a previously unknown element, thallium
It is an unusual allotrope of sulfur, not a new element

evt-03-30-1861-william-crookes.butterflyEffect: Crookes had discovered a new element, which he named thallium after the Greek word for a green shoot, thallos. The find helped establish flame spectroscopy as a reliable tool for identifying new elements, a method that would soon lead other chemists to further discoveries and cement Crookes's reputation before he went on to pioneer vacuum-tube research.

evt-03-30-1863-george-i-of-greece.scenario: You sit in the Greek National Assembly in 1863, months after King Otto's overthrow. The people favor Prince Alfred of Britain, but the Great Powers' old treaty forbids any of their royal houses from taking the Greek throne.
evt-03-30-1863-george-i-of-greece.prompt: Which foreign prince do you elect as the new King of the Hellenes?

choices.text: Alfred, Duke of Edinburgh
Leopold, Duke of Brabant
Prince William of Denmark
Prince Wilhelm of Prussia

evt-03-30-1863-george-i-of-greece.butterflyEffect: The assembly settled on Prince William of Denmark, who took the throne as George I. His fifty-year reign brought rare stability to Greece and founded a dynasty that endured, with interruptions, until the monarchy's abolition in 1973.

evt-03-30-1867-william-h-seward.scenario: It's late on March 30, 1867, and you're a State Department clerk watching Secretary William Seward finalize a treaty with Russian minister Eduard de Stoeckl in a hastily arranged midnight signing.
evt-03-30-1867-william-h-seward.prompt: What did Seward's treaty commit the United States to do?

choices.text: Trade California territory for Alaska
Lease Alaska from Russia for 99 years
Purchase only the Aleutian Islands, leaving the mainland to Russia
Purchase Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million

evt-03-30-1867-william-h-seward.butterflyEffect: Critics mocked the deal as "Seward's Folly," but the later discovery of gold and oil transformed Alaska into one of America's most valuable territories. Statehood followed in 1959, and the purchase pushed the U.S. border to the edge of the Bering Strait, a fact that gained new strategic weight during the Cold War.

evt-03-30-1912-abd-al-hafid-of-morocco.scenario: Fez, 1912. Tribal revolts are spreading, your treasury is empty, and French troops already occupy key positions across Morocco. French officials place a treaty before you, offering to prop up your throne in exchange for control of the state.
evt-03-30-1912-abd-al-hafid-of-morocco.prompt: What does Sultan Abd al-Hafid do?

choices.text: He allies with Spain to block French control entirely
He abdicates immediately and flees without signing anything
He signs the Treaty of Fes, accepting French protectorate status
He appeals directly to the Ottoman Sultan for military aid

evt-03-30-1912-abd-al-hafid-of-morocco.butterflyEffect: Abd al-Hafid signed the Treaty of Fes, making Morocco a French protectorate while leaving him a nominal sultan. The treaty triggered a violent uprising among Moroccan troops in Fez days later, and French colonial rule over Morocco endured — alongside a separate Spanish zone — until independence in 1956.

evt-03-30-1950-usmar-ismail.scenario: You are on set with director Usmar Ismail on 30 March 1950, rolling the first footage of Darah dan Doa, a film about soldiers fighting for the newborn Indonesian republic.
evt-03-30-1950-usmar-ismail.prompt: What makes this production historically distinct from earlier films made in Indonesia?

choices.text: It was the first Indonesian film entered at Cannes
It was the last Indonesian silent film produced
It was the first Indonesian film shot in color
It was made entirely by an Indonesian-owned production company

evt-03-30-1950-usmar-ismail.butterflyEffect: Darah dan Doa was produced by Perfini, a company owned and run by Indonesians rather than the Dutch- and Chinese-owned studios that had dominated the colonial-era film industry. The date of its first day of shooting is now marked annually in Indonesia as Hari Film Nasional, National Film Day.

evt-03-30-1972-vietnam-war.scenario: It is 30 March 1972, and North Vietnamese forces have launched a massive conventional assault across the DMZ into South Vietnam, catching Saigon and Washington largely by surprise.
evt-03-30-1972-vietnam-war.prompt: How does the United States respond to the Easter Offensive?

choices.text: Send large numbers of American ground troops back into combat
Resume heavy bombing campaigns against North Vietnam
Withdraw all remaining support from South Vietnam
Negotiate an immediate unconditional ceasefire

evt-03-30-1972-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: Nixon ordered intensified bombing, including Operation Linebacker, relying on air power since most American ground troops had already withdrawn. The offensive ultimately failed to topple South Vietnam but exposed the fragility of its army, shaping the terms of the Paris Peace Accords signed in January 1973.

evt-03-30-1979-airey-neave.scenario: You are Airey Neave's colleague at Westminster on 30 March 1979, walking with him through the House of Commons car park just weeks before the general election that would make Margaret Thatcher prime minister.
evt-03-30-1979-airey-neave.prompt: What happens as Neave starts his car?

choices.text: A car bomb planted by the INLA explodes
He is shot by an IRA gunman
He suffers a fatal heart attack
He is killed in a road traffic accident

evt-03-30-1979-airey-neave.butterflyEffect: A bomb planted by the Irish National Liberation Army detonated, killing Neave instantly. His death removed one of Thatcher's closest allies just before her election victory and heightened long-term security measures around the Palace of Westminster.

evt-03-30-1981-ronald-reagan.scenario: It's March 30, 1981, and you're a Secret Service agent walking beside President Reagan as he leaves a speech at the Washington Hilton. A young man in the crowd suddenly opens fire with a revolver.
evt-03-30-1981-ronald-reagan.prompt: What did the Secret Service do in the chaotic seconds after the shots?

choices.text: Shield Reagan and rush him into the limousine
Freeze and wait for local police backup
Evacuate through a different exit before helping the president
Return fire immediately into the crowd

evt-03-30-1981-ronald-reagan.butterflyEffect: Agent Jerry Parr pushed Reagan into the limousine and, noticing him coughing blood, diverted to George Washington University Hospital instead of the White House—a call credited with saving Reagan's life after a bullet punctured his lung. The attack reshaped presidential security protocols and reignited national debate over gun control, contributing to later legislation like the Brady Bill.

evt-03-30-1982-space-shuttle-program.scenario: It is 30 March 1982. Columbia is coming home after the STS-3 mission, but rain has flooded the planned runway at Edwards Air Force Base, forcing mission control to send the orbiter somewhere else entirely.
evt-03-30-1982-space-shuttle-program.prompt: Where does Columbia actually touch down?

choices.text: Vandenberg Air Force Base, California
White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico
Kennedy Space Center, Florida
It stayed in orbit an extra day and landed at Edwards anyway

evt-03-30-1982-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: Columbia landed at White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico, its gypsum sand runway kicking up fine dust that worked its way into the orbiter's systems and required extensive cleaning and refurbishment. The costly ordeal convinced NASA to treat White Sands strictly as a last-resort backup, reserving Edwards and Kennedy for nearly every other shuttle landing over the following decades.

evt-03-30-2002-queen-elizabeth-the-queen.scenario: It's March 30, 2002, and you're a member of the royal household at Windsor, informed that the 101-year-old Queen Mother has died peacefully in her sleep, just weeks after the death of her daughter Princess Margaret.
evt-03-30-2002-queen-elizabeth-the-queen.prompt: What followed the announcement of the Queen Mother's death?

choices.text: Hundreds of thousands queued to view her coffin lying in state at Westminster Hall
Public anger over the monarchy's cost forced its abolition
Her funeral was cancelled due to public indifference
She was buried immediately without any public ceremony

evt-03-30-2002-queen-elizabeth-the-queen.butterflyEffect: Her death, coming so soon after Princess Margaret's, marked the passing of a figure whose public life stretched back before World War I. The vast public turnout for her lying-in-state reaffirmed enduring affection for the monarchy at a moment of uncertainty, setting a warm tone ahead of the Queen's Golden Jubilee later that year.

evt-03-30-2006-cyclone-glenda.scenario: It is 30 March 2006, and Severe Tropical Cyclone Glenda, one of the most intense storms ever recorded in the Australian region, is bearing down on the Pilbara coast near Onslow, Western Australia.
evt-03-30-2006-cyclone-glenda.prompt: What happens to Glenda's intensity before it reaches the coast?

choices.text: It dissipates completely before reaching land
It weakens to a Category 3 storm before making landfall
It curves away and misses the coast entirely
It intensifies further and makes a record Category 5 landfall

evt-03-30-2006-cyclone-glenda.butterflyEffect: Glenda weakened from its peak strength and struck a sparsely populated stretch of coast near Onslow as a Category 3 system, sparing the region from catastrophic damage. It nonetheless remains one of the most intense cyclones ever recorded in the Australian basin, later cited as a benchmark in tropical cyclone forecasting.

evt-03-30-2009-lahore.scenario: It is the morning of 30 March 2009, and gunmen disguised as police have stormed the Manawan Police Training Academy in Lahore, taking cadets hostage inside the compound.
evt-03-30-2009-lahore.prompt: How do Pakistani security forces respond to end the siege?

choices.text: Withdraw and let the militants leave unopposed
Call in an airstrike on the academy
Launch a commando assault to storm the building
Negotiate a peaceful surrender with the attackers

evt-03-30-2009-lahore.butterflyEffect: Commandos stormed the academy after an hours-long standoff, killing most of the attackers, though cadets and officers died in the assault. The attack, one of several strikes on security institutions that year, hardened Pakistan's resolve to intensify military operations against militant networks in its tribal areas.

evt-03-30-2011-min-aung-hlaing.scenario: Myanmar, 2011. The military government is formally transferring power to a nominally civilian administration under President Thein Sein, and a new commander-in-chief of the armed forces must be named to lead the still-powerful Tatmadaw.
evt-03-30-2011-min-aung-hlaing.prompt: What did this appointment set in motion for Myanmar's future?

choices.text: The Tatmadaw was disbanded under his command
He later led the 2021 military coup against the elected civilian government
He retired quietly within a few years, ending his military career
He oversaw a peaceful, permanent transition to full civilian rule

evt-03-30-2011-min-aung-hlaing.butterflyEffect: Min Aung Hlaing held the post for a decade while the military retained deep influence even under civilian rule. In February 2021, he used that same command to seize power outright in a coup against Aung San Suu Kyi's elected government, plunging the country into prolonged conflict and eventually installing himself as president.

evt-03-30-2017-spacex.scenario: It's March 30, 2017, at Kennedy Space Center, and engineers watch a Falcon 9 first-stage booster—already flown once nine months earlier—prepare to launch again, this time carrying the SES-10 communications satellite.
evt-03-30-2017-spacex.prompt: What made this particular SpaceX launch historic?

choices.text: It was the first reflight of an orbital-class rocket booster
It was the first crewed SpaceX mission
It was the first rocket ever to land on a drone ship
It was the first satellite launched into geostationary orbit

evt-03-30-2017-spacex.butterflyEffect: The successful reflight proved that recovering and reusing an orbital-class rocket booster was commercially viable, slashing launch costs across the industry. Reused boosters soon became routine for SpaceX, helping enable megaconstellations like Starlink and accelerating the global pace of satellite deployment.

evt-03-30-2018-israel-defense-forces.scenario: It is Land Day, 30 March 2018, along the Gaza border fence. Thousands of Palestinians have gathered for what organizers call the start of a weekly 'Great March of Return,' and Israeli forces are stationed along the perimeter.
evt-03-30-2018-israel-defense-forces.prompt: What followed this day of mass protest and Israeli fire along the fence?

choices.text: An immediate ceasefire agreement ending all future border protests
Israel opened the Gaza border crossings in response
International condemnation and a UN commission of inquiry, with protests continuing for months
The events drew almost no international attention

evt-03-30-2018-israel-defense-forces.butterflyEffect: The deaths and mass casualties drew immediate international condemnation and calls for independent investigation, and the United Nations Human Rights Council established a commission of inquiry into the events. Far from ending there, the protests continued nearly every Friday for months, becoming one of the defining and most contested episodes of the Gaza-Israel conflict in the years that followed.

evt-03-30-2019-pope-francis.scenario: You are a Vatican aide in Rabat in March 2019, watching Pope Francis stand beside King Mohammed VI of Morocco, a Muslim-majority nation, ahead of a joint address to religious and civic leaders.
evt-03-30-2019-pope-francis.prompt: What central message does the pope deliver during this visit?

choices.text: He calls for interreligious dialogue and protection for migrants
He proposes establishing a new Catholic diocese boundary in North Africa
He announces a new Vatican trade agreement with Morocco
He urges Moroccan Christians to seek conversion of Muslims

evt-03-30-2019-pope-francis.butterflyEffect: Francis and the King issued a joint appeal on Jerusalem's status and urged protection for migrants, since Morocco is a major transit country. The visit built on the Abu Dhabi 'Human Fraternity' declaration signed weeks earlier, reinforcing Francis's push for closer Catholic-Muslim dialogue.

evt-03-30-2023-donald-trump.scenario: You are a reporter outside a Manhattan courthouse in March 2023 as word spreads that a grand jury has just voted on charges against former president Donald Trump.
evt-03-30-2023-donald-trump.prompt: What has the grand jury indicted Trump for?

choices.text: Falsifying business records over a hush-money payment
Tax evasion involving Trump Organization assets
Mishandling classified documents at Mar-a-Lago
Obstruction of the January 6th congressional investigation

evt-03-30-2023-donald-trump.butterflyEffect: The indictment centered on falsified business records tied to a hush-money payment to Stormy Daniels before the 2016 election. Trump was later convicted on 34 felony counts in May 2024, making him the first former or sitting U.S. president convicted of a felony, a fact that shaped the entire 2024 campaign.

evt-03-31-1146-abbot.scenario: It is 31 March 1146 at Vézelay, and you stand in the crowd as Bernard of Clairvaux, the most persuasive preacher in Christendom, rises before King Louis VII and the assembled nobles to call for a new holy war in the East.
evt-03-31-1146-abbot.prompt: What did Bernard's sermon at Vézelay actually launch?

choices.text: The Second Crusade to the Holy Land
The Reconquista campaign in Iberia
The First Crusade to capture Jerusalem
A crusade against the Cathar heretics

evt-03-31-1146-abbot.butterflyEffect: Bernard's oratory rallied Louis VII and thousands of knights to take the cross, formally launching the Second Crusade. The expedition ended in disastrous defeats in Anatolia and failure to retake Edessa, badly damaging Bernard's own reputation and European confidence in crusading for a generation.

evt-03-31-1174-pro-fatimid-conspiracy-ag.scenario: You are among the old Fatimid elite plotting in Cairo in early 1174, hoping to exploit Saladin's absence on campaign to restore the Isma'ili caliphate, with secret messages reportedly sent to the Crusaders and the Assassins.
evt-03-31-1174-pro-fatimid-conspiracy-ag.prompt: What actually follows for the conspirators?

choices.text: The conspirators successfully retake Cairo
Nur al-Din Zengi intervenes to restore the Fatimids himself
Crusader forces invade Egypt as planned
Saladin uncovers the plot and arrests the ringleaders

evt-03-31-1174-pro-fatimid-conspiracy-ag.butterflyEffect: The plot was betrayed to Saladin, who struck on March 31, 1174, arresting the ringleaders including the poet Umara al-Yamani. Executions followed at Cairo's Bayn al-Qasrayn square through the spring, and a pro-Fatimid revolt in Upper Egypt that autumn was crushed by Saladin's brother, al-Adil, cementing Ayyubid control of Egypt.

evt-03-31-1492-ferdinand-ii-of-aragon.scenario: It is March 31, 1492, in Spain. King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella have just signed a royal decree that gives you and every other Jewish resident of the kingdom a stark ultimatum.
evt-03-31-1492-ferdinand-ii-of-aragon.prompt: What did the Alhambra Decree order Jewish residents of Spain to do?

choices.text: Relocate permanently to segregated quarters within Spanish cities
Serve in the royal army in exchange for staying
Pay a special annual tax to remain in their homes
Convert to Catholicism or leave Spain within about four months

evt-03-31-1492-ferdinand-ii-of-aragon.butterflyEffect: Tens of thousands of Jews chose exile over conversion, fleeing to Portugal, North Africa, and the Ottoman Empire, seeding the Sephardic diaspora that preserved Judeo-Spanish language and culture for centuries. Those who converted became conversos, many later scrutinized by the Spanish Inquisition.

evt-03-31-1521-ferdinand-magellan.scenario: It is 31 March 1521 on the shore of Limasawa. Your fleet's chaplain, Pedro de Valderrama, prepares to celebrate Mass on the beach while the local rulers Kolambu and Siagu watch from among their people.
evt-03-31-1521-ferdinand-magellan.prompt: As Magellan, how do you mark the occasion and bind the islanders to your expedition?

choices.text: Trade for supplies but skip any religious ceremony ashore
Invite Kolambu and Siagu to the Mass and plant a cross on the highest hill
Demand the rulers convert on the spot or face the fleet's guns
Hold the service privately aboard ship, away from the islanders

evt-03-31-1521-ferdinand-magellan.butterflyEffect: Magellan invited the local rulers to the Mass and afterward had a large wooden cross planted on a nearby hilltop, claiming the land for Spain. The ceremony is now commemorated as the first Catholic Mass in the Philippines, and the alliance it sealed with local chieftains drew Magellan into island rivalries that led to his death at the Battle of Mactan weeks later.

evt-03-31-1854-united-states-navy.scenario: It is March 31, 1854, aboard an American warship anchored off Japan. Commodore Matthew Perry has returned with a larger fleet, pressing the Tokugawa shogunate to accept terms after more than two centuries of Japanese seclusion.
evt-03-31-1854-united-states-navy.prompt: What did Perry and the shogunate sign, ending Japan's sakoku policy?

choices.text: A trade treaty granting Japan full tariff control
A formal military alliance against Russia
A treaty ceding Okinawa to the United States
The Convention of Kanagawa, opening Japanese ports to American ships

evt-03-31-1854-united-states-navy.butterflyEffect: The Convention of Kanagawa opened the ports of Shimoda and Hakodate to American ships, ending over two hundred years of Japanese isolation. It set off further unequal treaties with Western powers and internal turmoil that eventually led to the Meiji Restoration in 1868.

evt-03-31-1899-philippine-american-war.scenario: It is 31 March 1899. You serve under General Emilio Aguinaldo as American troops under General Arthur MacArthur close in on Malolos, capital of the fledgling First Philippine Republic. The city cannot be held much longer.
evt-03-31-1899-philippine-american-war.prompt: What does the Filipino command do as the capital falls?

choices.text: Fortify Malolos and fight to the last man in the streets
Abandon the government entirely and disband the army
Negotiate an immediate surrender to save the city intact
Burn the city and retreat, denying the Americans a usable capital

evt-03-31-1899-philippine-american-war.butterflyEffect: Aguinaldo's forces set fire to Malolos and withdrew rather than make a final stand, denying the Americans an intact prize. The capital's fall forced the Republic's government into flight and pushed the Filipino army toward guerrilla warfare, prolonging the war until 1902.

evt-03-31-1913-arnold-schoenberg.scenario: It is 31 March 1913 in Vienna's Musikverein. You sit in a restless audience as Arnold Schoenberg conducts the Vienna Concert Society through works by himself, Zemlinsky, Webern, and Berg. Jeers and counter-cheers are already breaking out between rows.
evt-03-31-1913-arnold-schoenberg.prompt: As the disorder grows during Berg's Altenberg Lieder, what happens to the concert?

choices.text: The orchestra plays louder to drown out the crowd and finishes uninterrupted
Organizers cancel only Mahler's piece and the rest proceeds calmly
Police quietly remove a few hecklers and the concert finishes on schedule
The concert is halted mid-program amid shouting and a scuffle

evt-03-31-1913-arnold-schoenberg.butterflyEffect: The uproar escalated into shouting and at least one physical scuffle, forcing the performance to stop before the program's end. The event became known as the "Skandalkonzert" (or "Watschenkonzert," the slapping concert), a defining clash between Vienna's musical establishment and the emerging Second Viennese School.

evt-03-31-1921-royal-australian-air-forc.scenario: It is March 31, 1921, in Melbourne. Defence officials are finalising the charter that will replace the short-lived Australian Air Corps with a permanent, independent service.
evt-03-31-1921-royal-australian-air-forc.prompt: What new military branch was created on this day?

choices.text: The Australian Aviation Corps
The Royal Australian Naval Air Service
The Australian Flying Corps
The Royal Australian Air Force, as its own independent service

evt-03-31-1921-royal-australian-air-forc.butterflyEffect: The Royal Australian Air Force became the world's second-oldest independent air force after Britain's RAF. It would go on to fly combat missions across the Pacific and Europe in the Second World War and remains a core arm of the Australian Defence Force today.

evt-03-31-1930-cinema-of-the-united-stat.scenario: It is 1930 in Hollywood, and you are a studio executive facing threats of federal censorship over scandal and racy content, weighing whether to accept a strict new code of self-regulation instead.
evt-03-31-1930-cinema-of-the-united-stat.prompt: What did the studios do to head off government censorship?

choices.text: Adopted their own strict production code of self-censorship
Formed an independent review board run by clergy alone
Lobbied Congress to pass a federal censorship law themselves
Agreed to submit every script to state governors for approval

evt-03-31-1930-cinema-of-the-united-stat.butterflyEffect: The studios adopted the Motion Picture Production Code, later enforced rigorously from 1934 under the Hays Office, dictating what could and could not be shown on screen. It shaped American film content for over three decades until it was replaced by the modern ratings system in 1968.

evt-03-31-1964-brazilian-armed-forces.scenario: It is late March 1964 in Rio de Janeiro, and you are a junior officer watching your commanders openly discuss removing President João Goulart, whom they accuse of steering Brazil toward communism.
evt-03-31-1964-brazilian-armed-forces.prompt: What did the Brazilian military actually do to Goulart's government?

choices.text: Placed him under house arrest but kept him as figurehead president
Forced him to call new elections
Overthrew him in a swift military coup
Negotiated a coalition government with him

evt-03-31-1964-brazilian-armed-forces.butterflyEffect: The armed forces launched a coup that forced Goulart into exile within days, installing a military junta that would rule Brazil for the next 21 years. The regime suppressed dissent, censored the press, and used torture against opponents until democracy was restored in 1985.

evt-03-31-1992-uss-missouri-bb-63.scenario: It is March 31, 1992, and you stand at attention on the deck of USS Missouri as her colors are lowered for the last time, ending the era of the American battleship less than fifty years after her keel was laid.
evt-03-31-1992-uss-missouri-bb-63.prompt: What ultimately becomes of the Missouri after today?

choices.text: She is mothballed, then preserved as a museum ship at Pearl Harbor
She is sold to the Japanese Maritime Self-Defense Force
She is immediately scrapped for steel
She is kept in active combat service indefinitely

evt-03-31-1992-uss-missouri-bb-63.butterflyEffect: Missouri was placed in the reserve fleet before Congress and veterans' groups secured her future; in 1998 she opened as a museum ship at Pearl Harbor, moored near the sunken USS Arizona so that the ship marking the end of World War II now overlooks the wreck that marked its beginning.

evt-03-31-1993-macao-basic-law.scenario: It is 31 March 1993 in Beijing, and you sit among delegates of the National People's Congress as they vote to adopt a constitutional framework for a territory still six years away from returning to Chinese rule.
evt-03-31-1993-macao-basic-law.prompt: What did the delegates adopt that day?

choices.text: The Basic Law establishing the future Macau Special Administrative Region
A law granting Macau full independence
A treaty ending Portuguese sovereignty immediately
A trade agreement between Macau and mainland China

evt-03-31-1993-macao-basic-law.butterflyEffect: The Congress adopted the Macao Basic Law, the organic law that would govern the territory once Portugal handed it over. It came into force on 20 December 1999, guaranteeing Macau a high degree of autonomy under the "one country, two systems" model already used for Hong Kong.

evt-03-31-1995-selena.scenario: It is March 31, 1995, in Corpus Christi, Texas. News breaks of a shooting at a motel involving Tejano superstar Selena and the former president of her fan club and boutiques.
evt-03-31-1995-selena.prompt: What happened to Selena that day, cutting short her rising crossover career?

choices.text: She was shot and killed by Yolanda Saldívar
She collapsed on stage from a heart condition
She was killed in a car crash on tour
She died in a tour bus accident

evt-03-31-1995-selena.butterflyEffect: Selena was shot and killed by Yolanda Saldívar, sparking an outpouring of grief across Texas and the Latino community nationwide. Her posthumous English-language album Dreaming of You debuted at number one, and her life later inspired the 1997 film Selena, cementing her legacy in Latin pop.

evt-03-31-2004-anbar-campaign-2003-2011.scenario: It is March 31, 2004, and word reaches you as a U.S. commander in Anbar Province that American private security contractors have been ambushed and killed in Fallujah, their bodies publicly displayed in the city.
evt-03-31-2004-anbar-campaign-2003-2011.prompt: What does this incident set in motion?

choices.text: A lasting ceasefire is negotiated with local insurgents
Security is quietly handed over to Iraqi police alone
American forces withdraw entirely from Anbar Province
U.S. Marines launch the First Battle of Fallujah

evt-03-31-2004-anbar-campaign-2003-2011.butterflyEffect: The killings prompted the U.S. military to launch the First Battle of Fallujah in April 2004, a major escalation that failed to fully pacify the city and was followed by an even larger Second Battle of Fallujah that November. The Anbar campaign that followed became one of the bloodiest and longest of the Iraq War.

evt-03-31-2018-gyumri.scenario: It is March 31, 2018. You join opposition leader Nikol Pashinyan as he sets out on foot from Gyumri, vowing to march across Armenia to protest Serzh Sargsyan's bid to hold onto power as prime minister.
evt-03-31-2018-gyumri.prompt: What did Pashinyan's march grow into over the following weeks?

choices.text: A military-backed coup against the government
A small protest quickly dispersed by police
A parliamentary vote restoring the old constitution
A nationwide 'Velvet Revolution' that forced Sargsyan to resign

evt-03-31-2018-gyumri.butterflyEffect: The walk snowballed into mass street protests across Armenia. By late April, Sargsyan resigned, and Pashinyan became prime minister in May 2018, a peaceful transfer of power remembered as Armenia's Velvet Revolution.

evt-03-31-2018-2018-armenian-revolution.scenario: It is late March 1918... no, 2018, in Yerevan. Serzh Sargsyan, term-limited as president, is poised to take the more powerful post of prime minister. Opposition lawmaker Nikol Pashinyan calls on citizens to take to the streets.
evt-03-31-2018-2018-armenian-revolution.prompt: What tactic does the growing opposition movement use to pressure the government?

choices.text: A boycott of the next scheduled election only
Nonviolent civil disobedience, marching and blocking streets across the country
An armed uprising against government buildings
A quiet petition campaign submitted to parliament

evt-03-31-2018-2018-armenian-revolution.butterflyEffect: Pashinyan's supporters staged sustained nonviolent civil disobedience, blocking streets and squares across Armenia rather than resorting to arms. The pressure forced Sargsyan's resignation on 23 April, and Pashinyan became prime minister in May, ending nearly two decades of Republican Party dominance.

evt-03-31-2023-tornado-outbreak-of-march.scenario: It is the morning of March 31, 2023, and you are a forecaster at the Storm Prediction Center watching an extreme setup take shape over the Mississippi Valley, with the potential to put 28 million people under tornado watches by nightfall.
evt-03-31-2023-tornado-outbreak-of-march.prompt: What do you do with the outlook?

choices.text: Limit watches to a single state to avoid overreach
Downgrade the outlook to reduce public alarm
Wait until storms actually form before issuing any outlook
Issue a rare 'high risk' severe weather outlook

evt-03-31-2023-tornado-outbreak-of-march.butterflyEffect: Forecasters issued a rare 'high risk' outlook, the first since March 2021, and PDS tornado watches followed for cities including Little Rock, St. Louis and Memphis. The warning lead time helped save lives even as violent EF3 and EF4 tornadoes tore through Arkansas, Illinois and Iowa, including the collapse of the Apollo Theatre in Belvidere, Illinois.

evt-04-01-1234-richard-marshal-3rd-earl-.scenario: It is 1 April 1234 near the Curragh in Ireland, and you ride alongside Richard Marshal, Earl of Pembroke, believing you are heading into a parley with rival Irish lords loyal to King Henry III.
evt-04-01-1234-richard-marshal-3rd-earl-.prompt: What happens when the meeting turns out to be an ambush?

choices.text: Richard escapes unharmed and returns to England in triumph
Richard's men rout the ambushers decisively
Richard is mortally wounded and dies of his injuries soon after
Richard is captured unharmed and later ransomed

evt-04-01-1234-richard-marshal-3rd-earl-.butterflyEffect: Betrayed by rivals aligned with the king's justiciar, Richard Marshal was severely wounded in the fighting and died of his injuries within weeks. His death broke the Marshal family's rebellion and let Henry III reassert royal control over the earldom and Ireland.

evt-04-01-1346-hundred-years-war.scenario: It is April 1346, and you defend the walls of Aiguillon as Duke John of Normandy's vastly larger French army surrounds the town, cutting off supply and demanding submission.
evt-04-01-1346-hundred-years-war.prompt: Do you hold the walls and wait for relief, or seek terms?

choices.text: Hold the walls and await relief
Surrender to spare the garrison
Sally out to force a decisive battle
Abandon the town under cover of night

evt-04-01-1346-hundred-years-war.butterflyEffect: The garrison held for nearly five months, tying down Duke John's army so completely that when Edward III landed in Normandy, John could not break off in time to join the fight. His absence contributed to the campaign that ended in England's crushing victory at Crécy that August.

evt-04-01-1918-royal-air-force.scenario: It is 1 April 1918, and you are an airman watching two rival services, the Royal Flying Corps and the Royal Naval Air Service, merge into a single new force even as the war against Germany rages on.
evt-04-01-1918-royal-air-force.prompt: What new independent service did this merger create?

choices.text: The Royal Air Force
The Imperial Air Service
The British Aerial Corps
The Combined Flying Service

evt-04-01-1918-royal-air-force.butterflyEffect: The merger created the Royal Air Force, the world's first independent air arm, separate from army and navy control. Emerging from the war as the largest air force on earth, it would go on to defeat the Luftwaffe's bid for air superiority in the 1940 Battle of Britain.

evt-04-01-1933-wally-hammond.scenario: You are Wally Hammond, England's number three, unbeaten on well past 300 against New Zealand at Eden Park, with Bradman's world Test record of 334 now within reach.
evt-04-01-1933-wally-hammond.prompt: What do you do as you approach the world record score?

choices.text: Deliberately give your wicket away to let a teammate bat
Keep attacking to push past Bradman's record
Ask your captain to declare the innings immediately
Play cautiously to protect your wicket for the team total

evt-04-01-1933-wally-hammond.butterflyEffect: Hammond kept attacking and finished 336 not out, breaking Don Bradman's world Test record of 334 by two runs. The mark stood for 25 years until Garry Sobers scored 365 not out against Pakistan in 1958.

evt-04-01-1952-israeli-citizenship-law.scenario: You are a Palestinian Arab who stayed in your village after the 1948 war, and it is 1952: the new state is defining, for the first time, exactly who counts as its citizens.
evt-04-01-1952-israeli-citizenship-law.prompt: What must you do to be legally recognized as a citizen?

choices.text: Receive automatic citizenship under the Law of Return
Prove continuous residency and meet the law's residency conditions
Simply register as a resident at any government office
Apply through the old Ottoman-era land registry

evt-04-01-1952-israeli-citizenship-law.butterflyEffect: The 1952 Citizenship Law, paired with the 1950 Law of Return, granted Jewish immigrants automatic citizenship while requiring Arab residents to prove continuous residency and meet other conditions. This asymmetry left many Arab residents in prolonged legal limbo and remains a point of contention in Israeli society.

evt-04-01-1969-hawker-siddeley-harrier.scenario: It is 1969, and you are a Royal Air Force pilot converting onto the newly operational Hawker Siddeley Harrier, an aircraft that can climb straight up off the tarmac before flying forward like an ordinary jet.
evt-04-01-1969-hawker-siddeley-harrier.prompt: What must you do in the cockpit to make the Harrier hover and land vertically?

choices.text: Deploy a braking parachute at full throttle
Engage the afterburner to slow forward speed
Rotate the engine's thrust nozzles downward using a lever in the cockpit
Extend the flaps fully and cut the engine

evt-04-01-1969-hawker-siddeley-harrier.butterflyEffect: The Harrier entered squadron service with No. 1 Squadron RAF in 1969, giving the West its first true V/STOL combat jet by vectoring its engine thrust through swiveling nozzles. That flexibility proved decisive in 1982, when Sea Harriers operated from small Royal Navy carriers without long runways during the Falklands War.

evt-04-01-1970-richard-nixon.scenario: It is early 1970, and you sit on the Senate committee weighing a bill to strip cigarette advertisements from television and radio, even as broadcast networks warn of lost revenue.
evt-04-01-1970-richard-nixon.prompt: Do you push the bill through to the president despite industry pressure?

choices.text: Push for only stronger warning labels, no ad ban
Vote against it to preserve advertising freedom
Vote to send the ad ban to the president
Propose a voluntary industry advertising code instead

evt-04-01-1970-richard-nixon.butterflyEffect: Nixon signed the act, banning cigarette ads from TV and radio starting January 2, 1971, and mandating stronger health warnings on packs. Broadcasters lost a major revenue stream and tobacco companies shifted spending to print, sponsorships, and lobbying, a pattern later echoed in other advertising restrictions.

evt-04-01-1970-american-motors-corporati.scenario: It is 1 April 1970, and as an American Motors executive you unveil the Gremlin, a stubby hatchback rushed to market months ahead of Detroit's Big Three, aimed squarely at the Volkswagen Beetle and Japanese imports.
evt-04-01-1970-american-motors-corporati.prompt: What is AMC's strategy for beating GM and Ford to market with a subcompact?

choices.text: Import a rebadged European design
Chop down the larger Hornet platform into a shorter hatchback quickly and cheaply
Partner with a Japanese automaker to co-develop the car
Design an entirely new lightweight unibody from scratch

evt-04-01-1970-american-motors-corporati.butterflyEffect: AMC shortened its existing Hornet platform into the hatchback Gremlin, getting it to showrooms roughly six months ahead of the Ford Pinto and Chevrolet Vega. The gamble helped the small, cash-strapped automaker compete against the Big Three for another decade before it was absorbed by Chrysler in 1987.

evt-04-01-1974-mount-edgecumbe-alaska.scenario: It is the morning of April 1, 1974, and you are pilot Porky Bickar, hovering over the dormant crater of Mount Edgecumbe with a plan to convince nearby Sitka that the volcano has come back to life.
evt-04-01-1974-mount-edgecumbe-alaska.prompt: What do you drop into the crater to fake an eruption?

choices.text: Barrels of oil ignited with a flare gun
Dozens of burning, fuel-soaked tires
Smoke flares tied to balloons
Bags of black volcanic ash

evt-04-01-1974-mount-edgecumbe-alaska.butterflyEffect: Bickar dropped dozens of burning tires into the crater, sending up black smoke that panicked Sitka residents and flooded emergency lines. The hoax was revealed once flyovers spotted "April Fool" spelled out in tires in the snow nearby, and it became one of Alaska's most famous pranks.

evt-04-01-1976-steve-jobs.scenario: It is April 1976 in the Jobs family garage, and you and Steve Wozniak have just landed an order from the Byte Shop for fifty assembled computer boards, but you have no money for parts.
evt-04-01-1976-steve-jobs.prompt: How do you raise the capital to fill the order?

choices.text: Take out a bank loan against future sales
Sell personal possessions to fund the parts
License the design to an established electronics firm
Seek venture capital investment immediately

evt-04-01-1976-steve-jobs.butterflyEffect: Jobs sold his Volkswagen van and Wozniak sold his HP-65 calculator to buy components. They delivered the boards, used the proceeds to incorporate Apple Computer, Inc., and launched a company that would go on to redefine personal computing.

evt-04-01-2001-lockheed-ep-3.scenario: It is 1 April 2001. Your Navy EP-3 signals-intelligence aircraft has just collided with a Chinese fighter jet over the South China Sea and lost part of its propeller and nose cone. You have no permission to land in Chinese territory, but Hainan Island is the only runway within reach.
evt-04-01-2001-lockheed-ep-3.prompt: What should the crew do to save the aircraft and themselves?

choices.text: Make an emergency landing at the nearest airfield on Hainan Island
Attempt to fly the damaged plane back to Okinawa
Ditch the aircraft in the sea to avoid an international incident
Bail out and let the aircraft crash uncontrolled

evt-04-01-2001-lockheed-ep-3.butterflyEffect: The crew made an emergency landing on Hainan without clearance, and China detained all 24 crew members for eleven days while triggering a major diplomatic standoff. The incident strained early US-China relations under the new Bush administration and led to a formal US expression of regret rather than an apology, a compromise that shaped how both nations handled crises for years after.

evt-04-01-2006-serious-organised-crime-a.scenario: It is 1 April 2006, and you have just transferred from the National Crime Squad into a brand-new agency answerable to the Home Office, created to hit Britain's biggest criminal networks harder than ever.
evt-04-01-2006-serious-organised-crime-a.prompt: Which existing bodies have just been merged to form your new agency?

choices.text: Special Branch and the Serious Fraud Office
Regional Crime Squads and the Metropolitan Police Flying Squad
MI5 and MI6
The National Crime Squad, National Criminal Intelligence Service, and parts of Customs and Immigration

evt-04-01-2006-serious-organised-crime-a.butterflyEffect: SOCA combined the National Crime Squad, the National Criminal Intelligence Service, and parts of HM Customs and Excise and immigration enforcement into one body. It operated until 2013, when it was folded into the newly created National Crime Agency, further consolidating UK organised crime policing.

evt-04-01-2016-2016-nagorno-karabakh-con.scenario: It is early April 2016, and you are a soldier dug in along the Nagorno-Karabakh line of contact as artillery and tank fire suddenly erupt after years of an uneasy truce.
evt-04-01-2016-2016-nagorno-karabakh-con.prompt: What finally halts the fiercest fighting here since the 1990s war, after four days?

choices.text: NATO-brokered mediation
A Russian-mediated ceasefire agreement
Direct UN peacekeeping intervention
A decisive Armenian counteroffensive that ended hostilities

evt-04-01-2016-2016-nagorno-karabakh-con.butterflyEffect: A Russian-brokered ceasefire ended the so-called Four-Day War, but it left the underlying territorial dispute unresolved. The unresolved tensions would erupt again far more decisively in the 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war, which reshaped control of the region in Azerbaijan's favor.

evt-04-02-1513-conquistador.scenario: It is early April 1513, and you stand on the deck of Juan Ponce de León's ship as a green, flower-covered coastline rises on the horizon, land no Spanish expedition has charted before.
evt-04-02-1513-conquistador.prompt: What does Ponce de León do upon sighting this unknown coast?

choices.text: He declares the land already claimed by the French
He turns the fleet back toward Puerto Rico without landing
He immediately attacks the nearest native settlement
He names it La Florida and claims it for the Spanish crown

evt-04-02-1513-conquistador.butterflyEffect: He named the land La Florida, for its lush blooms and the Easter season, and claimed it for Spain, marking Europe's first documented contact with what is now the mainland United States. His voyage seeded both later Spanish colonization attempts and the enduring legend that he was searching for a Fountain of Youth.

evt-04-02-1979-spore.scenario: It is April 1979 in the closed Soviet city of Sverdlovsk. A ventilation filter was removed for maintenance at a secret military microbiology facility, and anthrax spores drifted over a nearby ceramics factory and residential district before anyone raised an alarm.
evt-04-02-1979-spore.prompt: How do Soviet authorities explain the sudden wave of anthrax deaths in the city?

choices.text: They accuse the United States of a covert biological attack
They openly admit a military lab accident and shut the facility
They blame tainted meat sold on the black market and quarantine the area
They evacuate the entire city and declare a nuclear-style exclusion zone

evt-04-02-1979-spore.butterflyEffect: Officials blamed contaminated black-market meat and quarantined the city under that cover story for over a decade. Not until 1992 did President Boris Yeltsin admit the true cause was a military accident, confirming the USSR had violated the 1972 Biological Weapons Convention and giving the West hard evidence of a hidden Soviet bioweapons program.

evt-04-02-1982-1982-invasion-of-the-falk.scenario: It's dawn on 2 April 1982, and you command the small Royal Marine garrison defending Government House in Stanley, Falkland Islands, as Argentine special forces land in overwhelming numbers on the surrounding beaches.
evt-04-02-1982-1982-invasion-of-the-falk.prompt: With no reinforcements possible and the odds hopeless, what do you decide?

choices.text: Fight to the last man rather than surrender
Call in an immediate Royal Navy bombardment of the beaches
Resist briefly, then surrender to avoid needless casualties
Retreat into the island's interior to wage guerrilla resistance

evt-04-02-1982-1982-invasion-of-the-falk.butterflyEffect: The garrison put up brief resistance before surrendering, and Argentina took control of the islands within hours. The invasion shocked Britain into dispatching a naval task force, igniting the 74-day Falklands War that ended in British victory, boosted Margaret Thatcher's political fortunes, and hastened the collapse of Argentina's military junta.

evt-04-02-1992-bosnian-war.scenario: It's dawn on 2 April 1992 in Bijeljina, and gunfire echoes from the town center. Arkan's Serb paramilitaries have moved in overnight, going door to door through Bosniak Muslim neighborhoods while local police stand aside.
evt-04-02-1992-bosnian-war.prompt: As a Bosniak resident hearing the paramilitaries approach, what is your best chance of survival?

choices.text: Attempt to escape toward government-held territory like Tuzla
Hide at home and wait for international peacekeepers to intervene
Gather with neighbors at the local mosque for collective protection
Report to the local Serb-controlled police station for safety

evt-04-02-1992-bosnian-war.butterflyEffect: The Bijeljina massacre killed dozens of Bosniak civilians and was one of the first major atrocities of the Bosnian War, carried out by Arkan's Tigers with little resistance from local authorities. It served as a grim template for the ethnic cleansing campaigns that would sweep across Bosnia over the following years, foreshadowing later, larger massacres.

evt-04-02-1992-john-gotti.scenario: It is April 2, 1992, in a federal courthouse in Brooklyn. You are among the reporters crowded outside as the jury in the racketeering and murder trial of Gambino boss John Gotti files back into the room to deliver its verdict.
evt-04-02-1992-john-gotti.prompt: What is the jury's verdict for John Gotti?

choices.text: Guilty only on minor tax charges
Acquitted for lack of sufficient evidence
Mistrial declared after juror tampering is discovered
Guilty on all counts, including murder and racketeering

evt-04-02-1992-john-gotti.butterflyEffect: Gotti was convicted on all charges, including the 1985 murder of Paul Castellano, and sentenced to life without parole. The verdict ended his image as the untouchable 'Teflon Don,' shattered the Gambino family's leadership, and marked a major victory for federal prosecutors using RICO statutes against organized crime.

evt-04-02-1992-new-york-state.scenario: It's April 2, 1992, in a federal courtroom in Brooklyn. You are a juror who has just heard closing arguments in the trial of Gambino crime family boss John Gotti, prosecuted for murder and racketeering after previous cases against him collapsed.
evt-04-02-1992-new-york-state.prompt: What is the jury's verdict on Gotti?

choices.text: Guilty only on minor racketeering charges
Guilty on all counts
Acquitted for lack of evidence
A hung jury forcing a retrial
