evt-04-08-1904-entente-cordiale.scenario: It is April 1904 in London. You are a diplomat finalizing an agreement between age-old rivals France and Britain, aiming to settle colonial disputes stretching from Egypt to Morocco before either nation drifts toward war with the other.
evt-04-08-1904-entente-cordiale.prompt: What do the Entente Cordiale agreements primarily settle?

choices.text: A currency union between the two empires
A formal military alliance against Germany
Terms for a joint invasion of the Ottoman Empire
Competing colonial claims, recognizing British control of Egypt and French influence in Morocco

evt-04-08-1904-entente-cordiale.butterflyEffect: The Entente Cordiale resolved decades of colonial friction without creating a binding military alliance, but it built the trust that let Britain and France cooperate closely as tensions with Germany grew. That relationship hardened into the core of the Allied coalition in the First World War.

evt-04-08-1911-winsor-mccay.scenario: It is 1911, and you're in the audience at a vaudeville theater where cartoonist Winsor McCay is about to debut something no one has seen before: drawings that move on their own, projected as part of his stage act.
evt-04-08-1911-winsor-mccay.prompt: What technique did McCay use to bring his Little Nemo characters to life onscreen?

choices.text: Mechanical puppets filmed frame by frame
Stop-motion photography of clay figures
Rear-projected live actors in costume
Hand-drawn frame-by-frame drawings, redrawn thousands of times

evt-04-08-1911-winsor-mccay.butterflyEffect: McCay's Little Nemo was one of the earliest American animated films, drawn frame by frame using his own comic-strip characters, with each background redrawn by hand. It helped establish animation as an art form and paved the way for his more influential Gertie the Dinosaur three years later.

evt-04-08-1933-western-australia.scenario: It is 8 April 1933 in Western Australia. Battered by the Great Depression and resentful of federal tariffs favoring the east, voters go to the polls in a referendum on leaving the Commonwealth of Australia.
evt-04-08-1933-western-australia.prompt: After voters back secession by a large margin, what does the state do next?

choices.text: Call a second referendum to confirm the result
Unilaterally declare independence
Send a delegation to petition the British Parliament for approval
Take the matter to the Australian High Court

evt-04-08-1933-western-australia.butterflyEffect: A WA delegation petitioned Westminster directly, bypassing Canberra. In 1935 the British Parliament ruled it could not act without the Australian Commonwealth's consent, effectively killing the bid. Western Australia remained part of the federation, though secessionist sentiment has resurfaced periodically since.

evt-04-08-1943-otto-and-elise-hampel.scenario: You are a working-class Berliner in the early 1940s, grieving a lost family member and furious at Hitler's regime. You have just finished writing another postcard denouncing the government and must decide how to spread it without being caught.
evt-04-08-1943-otto-and-elise-hampel.prompt: What should you do with the postcard you've written?

choices.text: Sign it with your real name so others know who is behind the resistance
Mail it directly to Gestapo headquarters to make a bold statement
Leave it anonymously in a stairwell or public place where a stranger will find it
Burn it out of fear and abandon the campaign entirely

evt-04-08-1943-otto-and-elise-hampel.butterflyEffect: Otto and Elise Hampel left dozens of such cards in stairwells and public places across Berlin for nearly two years before being betrayed and arrested; they were beheaded at Plötzensee Prison in April 1943. Their surviving Gestapo file inspired Hans Fallada's 1947 novel, later published in English as "Every Man Dies Alone" and filmed in 2016 as "Alone in Berlin," turning their quiet defiance into a lasting symbol of German resistance.

evt-04-08-1959-computer-science.scenario: It is April 1959, and you're among a group of computer scientists and industry representatives gathered to tackle a growing problem: every business computer speaks its own incompatible programming language.
evt-04-08-1959-computer-science.prompt: What common goal do you agree to pursue at this meeting?

choices.text: Agreeing on binary versus decimal number systems
Standardizing computer keyboard layouts
Building a single national computer network
Creating a shared, business-oriented programming language usable across machines

evt-04-08-1959-computer-science.butterflyEffect: The meeting set in motion the process that led to COBOL, formalized later that year by the CODASYL committee. COBOL became the dominant language for business data processing for decades, and its code still runs in banking and government systems today.

evt-04-08-1968-boac-flight-712.scenario: It is 8 April 1968, moments after takeoff from Heathrow. You are the captain of a Boeing 707 bound for Sydney when an engine bursts into flames and detaches from the wing.
evt-04-08-1968-boac-flight-712.prompt: What should you do with 127 people aboard?

choices.text: Continue toward the first scheduled stop in Zurich
Declare an emergency and turn back to land immediately at Heathrow
Divert to the nearest airport regardless of distance
Try to extinguish the fire in flight before deciding

evt-04-08-1968-boac-flight-712.butterflyEffect: The crew made a successful emergency landing back at Heathrow, but confusion over checklists and delays during evacuation meant five people died from fire and smoke rather than the crash itself. The disaster led to reforms in cockpit checklist discipline and cabin evacuation procedures across the airline industry.

evt-04-08-2002-space-shuttle-atlantis.scenario: You are part of the STS-110 crew aboard Atlantis in April 2002, tasked with attaching the massive S0 truss segment to the International Space Station's Destiny laboratory module.
evt-04-08-2002-space-shuttle-atlantis.prompt: How should the crew maneuver the truss into position for attachment?

choices.text: Use the station's Canadarm2 robotic arm to position the truss while spacewalkers bolt it in place
Manually carry the truss segment by hand during a spacewalk
Have the shuttle's own robotic arm handle the entire installation
Dock the truss directly using the shuttle's thrusters without any spacewalk

evt-04-08-2002-space-shuttle-atlantis.butterflyEffect: STS-110 became the first shuttle mission in which every spacewalk was based entirely on the station's own Canadarm2 robotic arm rather than the shuttle's arm, with astronauts riding the arm to install the S0 truss. That truss became the backbone of the station's structure, enabling later solar array segments to be added on future assembly missions.

evt-04-08-2008-soyuz-tma-12.scenario: It is early 2008 at Star City, Russia. You are the backup candidate for South Korea's first-ever astronaut seat, training alongside the chosen prime candidate ahead of an April launch to the ISS.
evt-04-08-2008-soyuz-tma-12.prompt: Days before liftoff, what happens that puts you in the seat instead?

choices.text: The prime candidate is removed for violating training center rules
Budget cuts limit the mission to one Korean seat
The prime candidate fails a medical exam
The prime candidate withdraws to focus on future missions

evt-04-08-2008-soyuz-tma-12.butterflyEffect: Ko San was disqualified for taking training manuals out of the facility against regulations, and backup Yi So-yeon flew instead, becoming the first Korean in space on 8 April 2008. She spent ten days aboard the ISS conducting experiments before returning to Earth on a separate Soyuz, an episode that fueled South Korea's growing space ambitions.

evt-04-08-2010-barack-obama.scenario: It is April 2010 in Prague. You are part of the American delegation as President Obama prepares to sign a landmark arms-control treaty with Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, capping months of negotiation over Cold War-era nuclear arsenals.
evt-04-08-2010-barack-obama.prompt: What does the New START treaty commit both nations to do?

choices.text: Cut deployed strategic nuclear warheads and launchers to agreed limits
Share missile defense technology
Ban intermediate-range missiles in Europe
Eliminate all nuclear weapons within a decade

evt-04-08-2010-barack-obama.butterflyEffect: The treaty limited each side to 1,550 deployed strategic warheads and 700 deployed delivery vehicles, backed by mutual verification. It remained the last major U.S.-Russia arms control pact in force in later years, extended in 2021, though its future grew uncertain after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

evt-04-08-2020-bernie-sanders.scenario: It is 8 April 2020. Trailing badly in delegates after a string of primary losses to Joe Biden, you are Bernie Sanders weighing whether to keep fighting for the Democratic nomination.
evt-04-08-2020-bernie-sanders.prompt: What does Sanders announce that day?

choices.text: He vows to fight on to the convention
He suspends his campaign without immediately endorsing a rival
He drops out and endorses Biden the same day
He announces a third-party run

evt-04-08-2020-bernie-sanders.butterflyEffect: Sanders suspended his campaign but held off endorsing Biden until 13 April, using the gap to extract policy commitments on healthcare and student debt. His delegates and progressive movement went on to shape the 2020 Democratic platform even without him at the top of the ticket.

evt-04-08-2024-solar-eclipse-of-april-8-.scenario: It is midday on April 8, 2024, and you are standing in a field in Texas as the sky darkens unnaturally. The Moon is sliding across the Sun and totality is only minutes away.
evt-04-08-2024-solar-eclipse-of-april-8-.prompt: What should you do as totality approaches to view the eclipse safely?

choices.text: Watch the whole event through ordinary sunglasses
Look through an unfiltered camera viewfinder for a clearer view
Stare directly at the Sun since the eclipse will only last a few seconds
Wear certified eclipse glasses, removing them only during totality to view the corona

evt-04-08-2024-solar-eclipse-of-april-8-.butterflyEffect: The Great North American Eclipse swept from Mexico through Texas and up to Maine before crossing into Canada, letting millions safely view the Sun's corona and prominences during totality. The next total eclipse to cross the contiguous United States will not occur until 2044.

evt-04-09-193-year-of-the-five-emperors.scenario: You stand among the legions at Carnuntum on 9 April 193, months after Rome burned through two emperors in succession, as your general Septimius Severus waits for the army's verdict.
evt-04-09-193-year-of-the-five-emperors.prompt: What do the legions do to back their commander's bid for the throne?

choices.text: Wait for the Senate's formal approval first
Stay neutral until a clear winner emerges
Acclaim Severus emperor and march on Rome
Declare loyalty to Pescennius Niger instead

evt-04-09-193-year-of-the-five-emperors.butterflyEffect: The troops proclaimed Severus emperor, and he marched swiftly on Rome, deposing and executing Didius Julianus. His victory launched the Severan dynasty, which held imperial power until 235.

evt-04-09-475-basiliscus.scenario: It is 475 in Constantinople. The newly enthroned Emperor Basiliscus has circulated his Enkyklikon, pressing bishops across the empire to reject the Council of Chalcedon and embrace a miaphysite creed. You are Patriarch Acacius of Constantinople.
evt-04-09-475-basiliscus.prompt: How does Acacius respond to the emperor's religious edict?

choices.text: Sign it immediately to secure imperial favor
Flee to Rome to seek the Pope's protection
Publicly oppose the edict and rally resistance against it
Remain silent and let regional bishops decide for themselves

evt-04-09-475-basiliscus.butterflyEffect: Acacius rallied monks, including the influential ascetic Daniel the Stylite, and stirred up popular resistance in the capital against the decree. The backlash forced Basiliscus to retreat, issuing the Antenkyklikon in 476 to rescind the edict, a humiliation that further eroded his shaky authority shortly before Zeno overthrew him.

evt-04-09-1388-old-swiss-confederacy.scenario: It is 9 April 1388, and you stand with the outnumbered men of Glarus as a large Habsburg Austrian force pushes up the narrow valley toward Näfels, intent on crushing the young Swiss confederacy.
evt-04-09-1388-old-swiss-confederacy.prompt: How should the vastly outnumbered defenders fight the advancing Austrian column?

choices.text: Meet the Austrians head-on in open formation on the valley floor
Ambush them from the high, narrow pass using the terrain against their numbers
Send envoys to negotiate tribute payments to avoid battle
Abandon the valley and retreat into fortified towns to wait them out

evt-04-09-1388-old-swiss-confederacy.butterflyEffect: The Glarners used the narrow terrain, rolling rocks and timber down onto the packed Austrian column before routing them, one of the confederacy's most celebrated victories. The win secured Glarus's place in the Swiss Confederacy, and the battle is still commemorated annually in the Näfelser Fahrt procession.

evt-04-09-1860-edouard-leon-scott-de-mar.scenario: You are a Parisian inventor in 1860, hunched over your phonautograph, a device built to trace the shape of sound waves onto smoked paper. You hum the melody of "Au clair de la lune" into its horn.
evt-04-09-1860-edouard-leon-scott-de-mar.prompt: What is your actual purpose in capturing this sound with the device?

choices.text: To study and visually analyze the physical shape of sound waves
To immediately play the recording back for an audience
To sell the recording as a novelty item to the public
To send the recording to inventors abroad for reproduction

evt-04-09-1860-edouard-leon-scott-de-mar.butterflyEffect: The phonautograph could only record visual traces of sound, not play them back, so the recording sat silent for nearly 150 years. In 2008, researchers used optical scanning technology to convert the tracing into audio, revealing it as the oldest known recording of a human voice, predating Edison's phonograph by 17 years.

evt-04-09-1865-battle-of-appomattox-cour.scenario: It is the morning of April 9, 1865, near Appomattox Court House, Virginia. You serve on General Robert E. Lee's staff, and Union infantry and cavalry have just closed the last escape route your exhausted, starving army had hoped to take south.
evt-04-09-1865-battle-of-appomattox-cour.prompt: With retreat cut off, what does Lee decide to do?

choices.text: Disperse the army into guerrilla bands to fight on
Retreat south to link up with Johnston in North Carolina
Order a full-scale breakout attack regardless of losses
Surrender the Army of Northern Virginia to Grant

evt-04-09-1865-battle-of-appomattox-cour.butterflyEffect: Lee met Grant that afternoon in Wilmer McLean's parlor and surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia on generous terms, paroling nearly 28,000 men. The formal stacking of arms on April 12 triggered a cascade of Confederate surrenders across the South, effectively ending the Civil War within weeks.

evt-04-09-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It's dawn, April 9, 1917, near Arras. You are a Canadian infantryman climbing out of the trenches behind a creeping artillery barrage, advancing toward the fortified height of Vimy Ridge.
evt-04-09-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What did the Canadian Corps achieve in this first wave of attacks?

choices.text: Were repelled with heavy losses
Captured the city of Arras itself
Captured Vimy Ridge from German forces
Breached only the first German trench line

evt-04-09-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The Canadian Corps seized Vimy Ridge from entrenched German defenders within days, a feat earlier Allied attacks had failed to achieve. The victory became a defining symbol of Canadian nationhood, strengthening the country's postwar claim to a distinct international identity apart from Britain.

evt-04-09-1939-dar-constitution-hall.scenario: It is early 1939 in Washington, D.C. The Daughters of the American Revolution have just refused to let celebrated contralto Marian Anderson perform at Constitution Hall because she is Black, and you are a DAR member, First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt.
evt-04-09-1939-dar-constitution-hall.prompt: How does Eleanor Roosevelt respond to the DAR's refusal?

choices.text: Ask Congress to pass a law banning such discrimination
Encourage Anderson to sue the DAR for damages
Publicly resign from the DAR in protest
Quietly lobby the DAR board to change the policy

evt-04-09-1939-dar-constitution-hall.butterflyEffect: Roosevelt resigned her DAR membership in protest and helped arrange for Anderson to sing instead from the steps of the Lincoln Memorial on Easter Sunday, 1939. Some 75,000 people attended, and the concert became an enduring symbol of the fight against segregation, inspiring later civil rights demonstrations at the same site.

evt-04-09-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It's April 9, 1942, on the Bataan Peninsula. You are an officer under General Edward King, commanding exhausted, starving troops as Japanese forces close in with no hope of resupply.
evt-04-09-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What did General King ultimately decide to do?

choices.text: Negotiate a ceasefire allowing safe withdrawal
Fight on until the last man fell
Evacuate all troops by boat to Corregidor
Surrender the Bataan garrison to Japanese forces

evt-04-09-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: King surrendered the Bataan garrison, the largest capitulation in US military history. The captured troops were forced on the brutal Bataan Death March, and the fall of Bataan hardened Allied resolve for the long Pacific campaign ahead.

evt-04-09-1947-journey-of-reconciliation.scenario: You are one of sixteen Black and white riders boarding a bus in Washington, D.C. on 9 April 1947, testing a Supreme Court ruling against segregation in interstate travel by sitting wherever you choose.
evt-04-09-1947-journey-of-reconciliation.prompt: When a Southern driver orders you to move seats by race, what do you do?

choices.text: Refuse to move, holding your seat to test the law
Get off the bus and walk instead
Demand the driver call the police yourself
Comply quietly to avoid arrest

evt-04-09-1947-journey-of-reconciliation.butterflyEffect: Riders who refused were arrested and some served on chain gangs in North Carolina. The journey's example of organized nonviolent resistance directly inspired the 1961 Freedom Rides led by the Congress of Racial Equality.

evt-04-09-1947-tornado-outbreak-of-april.scenario: It is the evening of April 9, 1947, in Woodward, Oklahoma. The sky has gone dark and greenish, but there is no siren and no official tornado warning, since the U.S. Weather Bureau still avoids the word 'tornado' in forecasts for fear of causing panic.
evt-04-09-1947-tornado-outbreak-of-april.prompt: With no warning issued but the sky clearly threatening, what should you do?

choices.text: Continue with your evening as usual since no warning was given
Take shelter immediately in a cellar or storm shelter
Drive toward open country to get a better view
Step outside to watch the storm's approach

evt-04-09-1947-tornado-outbreak-of-april.butterflyEffect: An enormous tornado, part of the Glazier–Higgins–Woodward family, tore through Texas, Oklahoma, and Kansas, killing 181 people and injuring 970, mostly in Woodward. The disaster intensified public pressure on forecasters to abandon their reluctance to name tornadoes directly, contributing to the eventual shift toward official public tornado warnings in the following decade.

evt-04-09-1948-1948-palestine-war.scenario: It is April 9, 1948, near Jerusalem. Word reaches Jewish Agency and Haganah leaders that Irgun and Lehi fighters have attacked the Palestinian village of Deir Yassin, acting outside official command.
evt-04-09-1948-1948-palestine-war.prompt: How do Jewish Agency and Haganah leaders respond once news of the attack spreads?

choices.text: Publicly condemn the attack and distance themselves from it
Endorse the attack as necessary military strategy
Suppress all news of the attack from spreading
Order Haganah to launch a retaliatory attack immediately

evt-04-09-1948-1948-palestine-war.butterflyEffect: The Jewish Agency publicly condemned the attack and Ben-Gurion sent an apology to King Abdullah of Transjordan, but the condemnation could not undo its impact. News of the killings spread fear through Palestinian towns and villages, accelerating the mass flight and expulsion of Palestinians that became central to the Nakba, and the name Deir Yassin remains a lasting flashpoint invoked by both sides in the conflict.

evt-04-09-1959-nasa.scenario: It's April 9, 1959, in a packed Washington press room. NASA is about to unveil seven men chosen from over 500 candidates to be America's first astronauts.
evt-04-09-1959-nasa.prompt: What background did NASA require every one of the seven to have?

choices.text: Experience as a military test pilot
Service as a decorated WWII infantry officer
A PhD in physics or engineering
Commercial airline piloting experience

evt-04-09-1959-nasa.butterflyEffect: All seven were military test pilots, a requirement that shaped the astronaut corps for a generation. Alan Shepard became the first American in space in 1961, and the test-pilot 'right stuff' mold persisted through Gemini and Apollo.

evt-04-09-1980-muhammad-baqir-al-sadr.scenario: It's April 1980 in Baghdad. You are a Shi'a cleric who has learned that Saddam Hussein's regime has seized the influential scholar Muhammad Baqir al-Sadr for his opposition writings.
evt-04-09-1980-muhammad-baqir-al-sadr.prompt: What fate did the regime impose on al-Sadr and his sister Amina?

choices.text: Forced public recantation on state television
Exile to Iran
Execution
Lifelong house arrest

evt-04-09-1980-muhammad-baqir-al-sadr.butterflyEffect: Both were executed by Saddam Hussein's government. Their deaths became a founding martyrdom narrative for the Islamic Dawa Party and Shi'a opposition movements, fueling decades of underground resistance that resurfaced openly after 2003.

evt-04-09-1993-morteza-avini.scenario: It is 1993 near Fakkeh, on ground still littered with unexploded mines from the Iran–Iraq War. You are part of documentary filmmaker Morteza Avini's crew, continuing his years-long project chronicling the war's aftermath.
evt-04-09-1993-morteza-avini.prompt: Before pushing further into the unmarked terrain to get the shot, what should the crew do?

choices.text: Rely on old wartime maps instead of asking local units
Push ahead quickly to capture the light before it fades
Send an assistant ahead alone to scout the ground
Confirm cleared paths with a military escort before advancing

evt-04-09-1993-morteza-avini.butterflyEffect: Avini stepped on a landmine while filming and was killed instantly. He was hailed as a martyr, with Ayatollah Khamenei calling him 'the master of martyred literati,' and his war documentary series Ravayat-e Fath became a foundational reference in Iranian sacred-defense cinema for decades after.

evt-04-09-2003-2003-invasion-of-iraq.scenario: You are a U.S. Marine in Baghdad's Firdos Square on 9 April 2003, watching a crowd struggle in vain to pull down a towering statue of Saddam Hussein with ropes and a sledgehammer.
evt-04-09-2003-2003-invasion-of-iraq.prompt: What do the Marines do to help finish toppling the statue?

choices.text: Fire tank shells to knock it over
Order the crowd to disperse immediately
Leave it standing to avoid provoking unrest
Bring in an armored vehicle to pull it down

evt-04-09-2003-2003-invasion-of-iraq.butterflyEffect: A Marine armored recovery vehicle hauled the statue down, and the image was broadcast worldwide as a symbol of the regime's collapse. Critics later argued the moment was staged for cameras and obscured the unresolved insurgency that would follow.

evt-04-09-2005-charles-iii.scenario: It is 9 April 2005 at the Windsor Guildhall. You are arranging the marriage of Charles, Prince of Wales, to Camilla Parker Bowles, both previously divorced, which complicates a traditional church wedding.
evt-04-09-2005-charles-iii.prompt: What kind of ceremony do they hold to accommodate their divorced status?

choices.text: A full Anglican wedding service in Westminster Abbey
A Catholic nuptial Mass held privately
An unofficial elopement ceremony held abroad
A civil ceremony followed by a church blessing

evt-04-09-2005-charles-iii.butterflyEffect: They married in a civil ceremony at the Guildhall, followed by a service of prayer and dedication with a blessing at St George's Chapel. The arrangement set a template for royal remarriage, and Camilla later became Queen consort when Charles ascended the throne in 2022.

evt-04-09-2021-myanmar-civil-war-2021-pr.scenario: You live in Bago on 9 April 2021, where residents have barricaded streets against security forces since the February military coup, and troops now move to clear the neighborhood.
evt-04-09-2021-myanmar-civil-war-2021-pr.prompt: What follows as the crackdown on Bago's barricades unfolds?

choices.text: The military withdraws after local negotiations
Residents successfully repel the troops unarmed
Security forces kill dozens of civilians in the assault
Foreign peacekeepers intervene to halt the raid

evt-04-09-2021-myanmar-civil-war-2021-pr.butterflyEffect: Security forces killed dozens of civilians that day in one of the deadliest single incidents of the post-coup crackdown. The massacre hardened resistance nationwide, pushing many opponents of the junta toward armed struggle and deepening the civil war.

evt-04-09-2021-prince-philip-duke-of-edi.scenario: It is April 2021 and you are helping plan Prince Philip's funeral at St George's Chapel, Windsor, while Britain remains under strict COVID-19 restrictions on gatherings.
evt-04-09-2021-prince-philip-duke-of-edi.prompt: How many guests were permitted to attend the funeral under pandemic rules?

choices.text: 30 guests, in line with pandemic limits on funerals
500 guests, with restrictions waived for the occasion
100 guests, given his status as a senior royal
An unlimited public ceremony open to mourners

evt-04-09-2021-prince-philip-duke-of-edi.butterflyEffect: Only 30 mourners attended, and the photograph of Queen Elizabeth II sitting alone in a face mask, separated by social distancing rules, became one of the defining images of the pandemic. It sparked widespread public sympathy and renewed debate about the personal costs of lockdown restrictions.

evt-04-09-2021-soyuz-ms-18.scenario: It's dawn at Baikonur, April 9, 2021. You are part of the crew boarding Soyuz MS-18 for a routine rotation to the International Space Station, expecting a standard six-month stay.
evt-04-09-2021-soyuz-ms-18.prompt: What unusual role would this same spacecraft play seven months later?

choices.text: Return a film director and actress to Earth after an orbital shoot
Be abandoned in orbit as space debris
Carry a paying space tourist back to Earth
Serve as an emergency lifeboat evacuating the whole station

evt-04-09-2021-soyuz-ms-18.butterflyEffect: In October 1921, MS-18 returned to Earth carrying director Klim Shipenko and actress Yulia Peresild, who had launched separately on MS-19 to film scenes for the movie Vyzov aboard the ISS. Crew and vehicle assignments were swapped, an unprecedented use of a Soyuz for a civilian film shoot.

evt-04-10-847-pope-leo-iv.scenario: It is 847, and Rome is still shaken from last year's Saracen raid that plundered St Peter's Basilica. The clergy and people have chosen you as pope, but word from Emperor Lothar confirming the election has not yet arrived.
evt-04-10-847-pope-leo-iv.prompt: Do you wait for imperial confirmation before your consecration, or proceed now?

choices.text: Seek the Byzantine emperor's approval instead
Delay until Lothar's legates formally ratify the election
Proceed with consecration immediately, citing the city's urgent need for leadership
Refuse the papacy until Carolingian troops arrive to secure Rome

evt-04-10-847-pope-leo-iv.butterflyEffect: Leo IV was consecrated without waiting for Lothar's imperial ratification, an urgent move given the ongoing Saracen threat. He went on to build the defensive Leonine Wall around the Vatican and organized the Italian league that crushed the Saracens at the Battle of Ostia in 849, and his precedent fed later disputes over whether emperors had any right to approve papal elections at all.

evt-04-10-1741-war-of-the-austrian-succe.scenario: It is 10 April 1741 at Mollwitz. Austrian cavalry has just routed your own Prussian horsemen, and King Frederick, fearing the battle is lost, has already ridden from the field. You command a line of Prussian infantry still standing in formation.
evt-04-10-1741-war-of-the-austrian-succe.prompt: What do you do to salvage the battle?

choices.text: Wait in place for reinforcements from Silesia before engaging
Hold formation and answer with disciplined volley fire
Retreat alongside the fleeing cavalry
Surrender the position to the advancing Austrians

evt-04-10-1741-war-of-the-austrian-succe.butterflyEffect: The Prussian infantry's disciplined volley fire broke the advancing Austrian ranks, turning apparent disaster into victory despite Frederick's early flight. The win secured Prussian control of Silesia and launched Frederick the Great's reputation as a commander, setting Prussia on course to become a major European power over the following decades.

evt-04-10-1809-napoleonic-wars.scenario: It is April 1809. You serve under Archduke Charles as the Austrian army masses to invade Bavaria, betting that Napoleon's forces tied down in Spain leave France exposed.
evt-04-10-1809-napoleonic-wars.prompt: What was Austria's strategic gamble in striking first this spring?

choices.text: Seize Italian territories while France was distracted by naval war with Britain
Prevent Prussia from mobilizing an army against Austria
Support a planned Russian invasion of the Grand Duchy of Warsaw
Exploit Napoleon's army being tied down fighting in the Peninsular War in Spain

evt-04-10-1809-napoleonic-wars.butterflyEffect: Napoleon rushed back from Spain, and after early Austrian gains the campaign turned at the bloody Battle of Wagram in July 1809. Austria was forced into the Treaty of Schönbrunn, losing territory and paying a huge indemnity, and the peace was sealed by Napoleon's marriage to Archduchess Marie Louise.

evt-04-10-1815-mount-tambora.scenario: It is April 1815, and you are a Dutch colonial official stationed near Sumbawa when Mount Tambora erupts with a roar heard hundreds of miles away, burying villages under ash and pumice.
evt-04-10-1815-mount-tambora.prompt: What global consequence follows the eruption in the year afterward?

choices.text: Global temperatures rise sharply, causing severe droughts worldwide
Volcanic ash fertilizes soil, producing a decade of record harvests
A 'Year Without a Summer' causes widespread crop failures and famine across Europe and North America
The eruption has no lasting effect on climate beyond Indonesia

evt-04-10-1815-mount-tambora.butterflyEffect: Tambora's ash veiled the sun worldwide, causing 1816 to become known as the 'Year Without a Summer,' with crop failures and famine across Europe and North America. The gloomy, colorful skies and confined weather inspired Mary Shelley to write Frankenstein and influenced painters like J.M.W. Turner.

evt-04-10-1858-big-ben.scenario: It is 10 April 1858 at the Whitechapel Bell Foundry in London. The first great bell cast for the new clock tower cracked during testing under too heavy a hammer, and you must cast its replacement without repeating the failure.
evt-04-10-1858-big-ben.prompt: What change does the foundry make for the new casting?

choices.text: Reproduce the first bell's exact specifications unchanged
Add iron reinforcing bands around the mold before casting
Switch from bronze to cast iron for greater strength
Cast a smaller, lighter bell than the original attempt

evt-04-10-1858-big-ben.butterflyEffect: George Mears cast a smaller, lighter bell than the failed original, and this is the bell still hanging in the tower today. It too cracked slightly after installation in 1859 from a hammer that was again too heavy, but rather than replace it, workers rotated the bell and fitted a lighter hammer, giving Big Ben the distinctive tone heard ever since.

evt-04-10-1919-mexican-revolution.scenario: It is 10 April 1919 near Ciudad Ayala, and Colonel Jesus Guajardo has invited you, revolutionary leader Emiliano Zapata, to Hacienda de Chinameca, claiming he wishes to defect with his troops to your cause.
evt-04-10-1919-mexican-revolution.prompt: What happens when Zapata rides through the hacienda gates to meet Guajardo?

choices.text: He demands Guajardo meet him on open ground instead
He senses a trap and turns back before reaching the gates
He enters trusting the invitation and is shot dead by soldiers hidden inside
He sends a lieutenant in his place to test Guajardo's loyalty

evt-04-10-1919-mexican-revolution.butterflyEffect: Guajardo's offer was a trap arranged with President Venustiano Carranza; as Zapata entered, hidden riflemen shot him dead. His death effectively broke the agrarian revolt in Morelos, but his image and cry of 'Tierra y Libertad' became a lasting symbol of Mexican land reform, later invoked by the Zapatista movement of the 1990s.

evt-04-10-1925-the-great-gatsby.scenario: You are an editor at Scribner's in April 1925, watching the first reviews and sales figures for F. Scott Fitzgerald's new novel about a mysterious Long Island millionaire come trickling in.
evt-04-10-1925-the-great-gatsby.prompt: How is the novel received in the months after its publication?

choices.text: It becomes an instant bestseller hailed as an American classic
It sells modestly and earns mixed reviews, seen as a disappointment
It is banned in several states for its content
Critics ignore it entirely upon release

evt-04-10-1925-the-great-gatsby.butterflyEffect: The Great Gatsby sold modestly and drew mixed reviews, and Fitzgerald died in 1940 believing it a failure. It was only revived through a wartime paperback giveaway to soldiers and later academic rediscovery, eventually becoming one of the most celebrated American novels and a fixture of school curricula.

evt-04-10-1944-the-holocaust.scenario: It is April 1944. You and a fellow prisoner have just slipped past the Auschwitz perimeter after three days hidden inside a woodpile while guards searched with dogs. You now stand on Slovak soil with details of the camp's machinery of murder in your memory.
evt-04-10-1944-the-holocaust.prompt: What do you do with what you know?

choices.text: Travel directly to the Vatican to appeal to the Pope
Dictate a detailed report to Jewish council leaders describing the camps and warning of planned mass deportations
Return secretly into Poland to organize an armed escape of other prisoners
Head immediately for Allied lines in Italy to enlist

evt-04-10-1944-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: Rudolf Vrba and Alfréd Wetzler dictated a detailed testimony to Jewish leaders in Slovakia, later called the Vrba-Wetzler report, part of the Auschwitz Protocols. It reached Allied governments and helped push Hungarian regent Miklós Horthy to halt deportations from Budapest in July 1944, saving tens of thousands of lives, though millions had already been murdered.

evt-04-10-1963-united-states-navy.scenario: It is 9:17 a.m. on 10 April 1963. You are aboard the support ship Skylark, tracking USS Thresher as it conducts a deep test dive off Cape Cod after months of overhaul, when garbled radio messages report trouble with the ballast system.
evt-04-10-1963-united-states-navy.prompt: What happens to Thresher moments after those final garbled messages?

choices.text: It surfaces safely after an emergency ballast blow
It implodes and sinks with all hands lost
The crew escapes through the escape trunk before it sinks
Skylark tows it back to Portsmouth for repairs

evt-04-10-1963-united-states-navy.butterflyEffect: Thresher imploded under crushing pressure, killing all 129 men aboard in the worst submarine disaster in history. The tragedy forced the Navy to create the rigorous SUBSAFE quality-control program, which has kept every SUBSAFE-certified submarine since from being lost to a similar non-combat casualty.

evt-04-10-1970-paul-mccartney.scenario: It is 10 April 1970. You are Paul McCartney, releasing your debut solo album alongside a self-written question-and-answer press release, while tension with Lennon over manager Allen Klein has festered for months.
evt-04-10-1970-paul-mccartney.prompt: What do you state in the release that becomes front-page news?

choices.text: That he is suing Allen Klein for control of Apple Records
That the Beatles will reunite for one final world tour
That he has no plans to write or record with John Lennon again
That the band will continue recording under a new manager

evt-04-10-1970-paul-mccartney.butterflyEffect: McCartney's answer that he had no plans to write or record with Lennon again was widely reported as him quitting the Beatles, even though Lennon had privately decided to leave the group months earlier. The statement made the split public and set in motion the legal dissolution of the band's partnership.

evt-04-10-1991-moby-prince-disaster.scenario: It is the night of 10 April 1991, and dense fog blankets the harbour of Livorno as your ferry, the Moby Prince, collides with an oil tanker and bursts into flame just outside the port.
evt-04-10-1991-moby-prince-disaster.prompt: What made the disaster's true cause bitterly disputed for decades afterward?

choices.text: Investigators found fog was the sole cause and no dispute ever followed
The ferry company admitted full responsibility immediately, ending all controversy
The tanker's captain was swiftly convicted and the case was closed within months
Persistent claims that an unidentified vessel or naval exercise in the fog was never officially acknowledged

evt-04-10-1991-moby-prince-disaster.butterflyEffect: The official inquiry initially blamed thick fog and errors by the ferry's crew, but families and later investigators argued a mysterious third vessel, possibly linked to a covert naval operation, was present and never acknowledged. The case was repeatedly reopened, and it remains one of Italy's most contested unsolved maritime tragedies.

evt-04-10-1998-the-troubles.scenario: It is Good Friday, 10 April 1998, in Belfast, and you are one of the negotiators racing against a self-imposed deadline to reach a settlement after decades of violence in Northern Ireland.
evt-04-10-1998-the-troubles.prompt: What key step follows the signing of the agreement to secure its legitimacy?

choices.text: All paramilitary groups disarm immediately and completely
Referendums are held in both Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland
Direct rule from London ends the very next day
A United Nations peacekeeping force is deployed to enforce the deal

evt-04-10-1998-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The Good Friday Agreement was put to referendums in both Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland, and voters in both approved it overwhelmingly. It established a power-sharing Northern Ireland Assembly and has remained the constitutional foundation of Northern Irish politics ever since, even as tensions periodically resurfaced.

evt-04-10-2009-josefa-iloilo.scenario: It is April 2009 in Suva. Fiji's Court of Appeal has just ruled that your 2006 dismissal of the elected government was unconstitutional and ordered the pre-coup administration restored. As president, the ruling threatens to unravel everything since 2006.
evt-04-10-2009-josefa-iloilo.prompt: What do you decide to do?

choices.text: Restore the pre-2006 elected government as the court ordered
Resign immediately and call fresh elections within weeks
Transfer all presidential authority directly to the military commander
Abrogate the constitution and reappoint Bainimarama as interim prime minister by decree

evt-04-10-2009-josefa-iloilo.butterflyEffect: Iloilo abrogated the constitution entirely, dismissed the judiciary, and reappointed Frank Bainimarama as interim prime minister under decree. Fiji was suspended from the Commonwealth and Pacific Islands Forum, and elections were delayed until 2014.

evt-04-10-2009-president-of-fiji.scenario: As Fiji's head of state, you hold reserve powers meant only for a genuine crisis. The Court of Appeal has just struck down the legal basis for the government you installed in 2006, and your ordinary ceremonial role offers no clear path forward.
evt-04-10-2009-president-of-fiji.prompt: How do you use your reserve powers to resolve the crisis?

choices.text: Convene Parliament to draft an entirely new constitution first
Abrogate the constitution by decree and reinstall the same government
Call in the United Nations to mediate a transition government
Ask the Great Council of Chiefs to select a new prime minister

evt-04-10-2009-president-of-fiji.butterflyEffect: Iloilo invoked his reserve powers to abrogate the 2007 constitution outright and reappointed Bainimarama's government by decree, an act critics called a second coup. It entrenched military-backed rule in Fiji for five more years and drew sustained international sanctions.

evt-04-10-2010-polish-air-force.scenario: You are the co-pilot of the Polish Air Force Tu-154 carrying President Lech Kaczyński and dozens of officials to the Katyn massacre commemoration. Approaching Smolensk North Airport in dense fog, the aircraft's warning system urges a go-around.
evt-04-10-2010-polish-air-force.prompt: What do the pilots do as the aircraft nears the ground in the fog?

choices.text: Request a full instrument landing system approach from air traffic control
Abort the approach and return to Warsaw
Continue descending below the safe decision altitude despite the warnings
Execute a go-around and divert to Moscow

evt-04-10-2010-polish-air-force.butterflyEffect: The crew continued the descent below a safe altitude and the aircraft struck trees short of the runway, killing all 96 aboard, including the president, the first lady, and much of Poland's military and civic leadership. The disaster triggered a snap presidential election, reshuffled the armed forces' command, and deepened years of dispute between Warsaw and Moscow over the crash's causes.

evt-04-10-2016-puttingal-temple-fire.scenario: It is the final night of a seven-day festival at Puttingal Temple in Paravur, Kerala, April 2016. You are part of the temple committee preparing a competitive fireworks display that local authorities had warned against.
evt-04-10-2016-puttingal-temple-fire.prompt: What did the temple committee do about the fireworks display despite the warnings?

choices.text: Requested additional police supervision before proceeding
Moved the display to an open field far from the crowd
Proceeded with the display despite the denial of official permission
Cancelled the display entirely after the warnings

evt-04-10-2016-puttingal-temple-fire.butterflyEffect: The organizers proceeded without proper permission, and sparks from the display ignited stored fireworks, causing an explosion that killed 111 people and injured hundreds more. The tragedy led Kerala authorities to tighten licensing and safety enforcement for fireworks at temple festivals across the state.

evt-04-10-2019-event-horizon-telescope.scenario: It is 10 April 2019, and you are part of the Event Horizon Telescope collaboration, about to unveil to the world an image built from years of combined data collected by radio telescopes spanning the globe.
evt-04-10-2019-event-horizon-telescope.prompt: What does the released image actually show?

choices.text: An image of a neutron star merger
An image of a newly discovered exoplanet
The first image of Sagittarius A* at the Milky Way's center
The first direct image of a black hole's shadow, at the center of galaxy M87

evt-04-10-2019-event-horizon-telescope.butterflyEffect: The image revealed the shadow of the supermassive black hole at the center of galaxy Messier 87, the first-ever direct visual evidence of a black hole, confirming predictions of general relativity. The EHT team followed up in 2022 with an image of Sagittarius A* at the Milky Way's core, opening a new era of directly observing black holes rather than inferring them.

evt-04-10-2023-2023-louisville-bank-shoo.scenario: It is the morning of 10 April 2023 at an Old National Bank branch in Louisville. Gunfire has erupted during a staff meeting, and in the chaos a phone camera keeps recording, streaming the attack in real time before anyone can stop it.
evt-04-10-2023-2023-louisville-bank-shoo.prompt: What did investigators later confirm the shooter had done during the attack?

choices.text: Posted a written manifesto to a news outlet beforehand
Called a local television station live during the attack
Livestreamed the shooting on Instagram
Broadcast the attack on a public radio scanner frequency

evt-04-10-2023-2023-louisville-bank-shoo.butterflyEffect: Connor Sturgeon livestreamed part of the shooting on Instagram before he was fatally shot by responding officers. The footage renewed national debate over how quickly social platforms detect and remove violent live content, and added fuel to Kentucky's ongoing gun-policy debates without producing new federal legislation.

evt-04-11-1713-peace-of-utrecht.scenario: You are a diplomat at Utrecht in 1713, working to end the long War of the Spanish Succession. Philip V wishes to keep the Spanish throne, but France and its enemies insist on guarantees that the French and Spanish crowns will never be united.
evt-04-11-1713-peace-of-utrecht.prompt: What concession must Philip V make to secure the peace?

choices.text: Cede all of Spain's American colonies to Britain
Formally renounce any right to inherit the French throne
Grant England direct rule over the Spanish Netherlands
Convert to the Anglican faith to satisfy British demands

evt-04-11-1713-peace-of-utrecht.butterflyEffect: Philip V formally renounced any claim to the French throne, and the treaties transferred Gibraltar and Minorca to Britain and the Spanish Netherlands and Italian territories to Austria. The resulting balance of power shaped European diplomacy for the rest of the century.

evt-04-11-1809-napoleonic-wars.scenario: It is the night of 11 April 1809, and you serve under Lord Cochrane in the Basque Roads. The French Atlantic fleet lies at anchor behind a boom and shoals, confident the Royal Navy cannot reach them.
evt-04-11-1809-napoleonic-wars.prompt: How does Cochrane's squadron attack the sheltered French fleet?

choices.text: Land marines to storm the coastal defenses first
Blockade the anchorage and wait for the French to run out of supplies
Send in fireships and explosion vessels under cover of darkness
Line up the fleet for a daylight broadside bombardment

evt-04-11-1809-napoleonic-wars.butterflyEffect: Cochrane sent in fireships and explosion vessels that panicked the French and drove most of their fleet aground. Admiral Gambier then refused to press the advantage with the main fleet, sparing the French from total destruction and igniting a bitter public feud between Cochrane and the Admiralty that damaged his naval career.

evt-04-11-1814-treaty-of-fontainebleau-1.scenario: It is April 1814 at Fontainebleau. Paris has fallen, your marshals have refused to fight on, and you must accept the Allied powers' terms for ending your reign as Emperor of the French.
evt-04-11-1814-treaty-of-fontainebleau-1.prompt: What terms do Austria, Russia, and Prussia offer Napoleon?

choices.text: Immediate execution for the wars he had caused across Europe
Restoration to the throne under a constitutional monarchy
Lifelong imprisonment in the Tower of London
Exile on the island of Elba with nominal sovereignty and a pension

evt-04-11-1814-treaty-of-fontainebleau-1.butterflyEffect: Napoleon accepted exile to Elba as a sovereign prince with a pension and a small guard. Within ten months he escaped, landed in France, and triggered the Hundred Days that ended at Waterloo, after which the Allies exiled him far more securely to remote Saint Helena.

evt-04-11-1908-sms-blucher.scenario: It's 1907, and you are a German naval designer finalizing plans for a new armored cruiser meant to counter Britain's latest ships, working from intelligence that may already be outdated.
evt-04-11-1908-sms-blucher.prompt: What armament did German planners commit to for the new cruiser Blücher?

choices.text: Twelve 21 cm guns, proceeding with the original design despite rumors of bigger British guns
Eight 30.5 cm guns to match the new British battlecruisers exactly
Delay construction entirely until better intelligence on British designs arrived
A mixed battery of large and small calibers to hedge against uncertainty

evt-04-11-1908-sms-blucher.butterflyEffect: Blücher was fitted with twelve 21 cm guns, but Britain had already leapt ahead with the Invincible-class battlecruisers' eight 30.5 cm guns, making Blücher obsolescent before she even entered service. She was sunk at the Battle of Dogger Bank in 1915, isolated and outgunned, a symbol of Germany falling behind in the pre-war naval arms race.

evt-04-11-1913-cricket-pavilion.scenario: It is the night of 11 April 1913, and you belong to the militant wing of the suffragette movement. The unguarded pavilion at the Nevill Ground cricket ground stands before you, a symbol of the male establishment you're fighting.
evt-04-11-1913-cricket-pavilion.prompt: What action do you take to draw attention to the suffrage cause?

choices.text: Organise a peaceful march past the ground
Set fire to the empty pavilion
Deliver a petition to the cricket club committee
Chain yourself to the pavilion gates

evt-04-11-1913-cricket-pavilion.butterflyEffect: The pavilion was burned down in an arson attack, one of dozens carried out by militant suffragettes that year targeting sporting and civic buildings. Such attacks kept the cause in the headlines but also hardened public opposition to militant tactics, a debate only interrupted when the outbreak of the First World War halted the campaign.

evt-04-11-1919-paris-peace-conference-19.scenario: You sit on the League of Nations commission at the Paris Peace Conference as Japan formally proposes a Racial Equality clause for the Covenant. Australia's delegation, backed by other British dominions, flatly refuses to accept it, and as chairman Woodrow Wilson must rule on the vote.
evt-04-11-1919-paris-peace-conference-19.prompt: How does Wilson rule on the racial equality clause?

choices.text: He refers the matter to the U.S. Senate for a binding vote
He rules that despite a majority in favor, unanimous consent is required, so the clause fails
He overrules the dominions and inserts the clause into the Covenant
He offers Japan a private immigration treaty instead of a Covenant clause

evt-04-11-1919-paris-peace-conference-19.butterflyEffect: Although the clause won a majority (11 of 17 votes), Wilson ruled that such a fundamental change required unanimous consent, so it failed. Japan's delegation left the conference feeling humiliated by Western racial hierarchy, a grievance that hardened nationalist and militarist sentiment in Japan through the interwar years.

evt-04-11-1921-abdullah-i-of-jordan.scenario: It is April 1921 and you are newly arrived in Amman as adviser to Emir Abdullah, tasked with organizing a functioning government over the tribal lands Britain has just carved out as Transjordan.
evt-04-11-1921-abdullah-i-of-jordan.prompt: What should Abdullah do to establish his authority?

choices.text: Reject the mandate outright and declare full independence at once
Leave authority scattered among rival tribal sheikhs with no central office
Abandon Transjordan and return to lead forces in the Hejaz
Build a centralized government administration loyal to him, working within the British mandate

evt-04-11-1921-abdullah-i-of-jordan.butterflyEffect: Abdullah set up a centralized administration under British oversight, laying the institutional foundation of the modern Jordanian state. He ruled for three decades, becoming king of an independent Jordan in 1946, and the Hashemite dynasty he founded there still reigns today.

evt-04-11-1930-jim-corbett.scenario: It is April 1930 in the Kumaon hills of northern India. You are Jim Corbett, tracking the second of the two Chowgarh man-eaters that have terrorized villagers for years, relying on fresh kills and local reports of the tiger's calls to find her.
evt-04-11-1930-jim-corbett.prompt: How do you finally close in on the man-eater?

choices.text: Lay out poisoned meat across several villages and wait
Set steel leg-hold traps along the forest paths
Organize hundreds of beaters to drive her into the open
Track her on foot through her territory, using villager sightings and her calls to close in

evt-04-11-1930-jim-corbett.butterflyEffect: Corbett stalked and shot the tigress, ending a killing spree that had claimed dozens of villagers across the region. His success cemented his reputation as India's foremost hunter of man-eaters, fueling the fame of his 1944 memoir Man-Eaters of Kumaon and his later turn to wildlife conservation, for which India's first national park was later named after him.

evt-04-11-1951-harry-s-truman.scenario: It is April 1951 and the Korean War has settled into a bloody stalemate. General Douglas MacArthur has publicly criticized your administration's limited-war strategy and pushed for widening the conflict against China without authorization.
evt-04-11-1951-harry-s-truman.prompt: What does President Truman decide to do about MacArthur's insubordination?

choices.text: Relieves MacArthur of all his commands for insubordination
Promotes MacArthur to Supreme Commander of all UN forces in Asia
Has MacArthur court-martialed and imprisoned
Sends MacArthur to negotiate directly with Chinese leaders

evt-04-11-1951-harry-s-truman.butterflyEffect: On April 11, 1951, Truman relieved MacArthur of all his commands, replacing him with General Matthew Ridgway. MacArthur returned home to a hero's welcome and testified before Congress, but the controversy ultimately reaffirmed the principle of civilian control over the military.

evt-04-11-1951-stone-of-scone.scenario: It is April 1951, four months after you and fellow Scottish students smuggled the Stone of Scone out of Westminster Abbey. Police are hunting for it, and you've just left it at Arbroath Abbey, wrapped in a Scottish flag.
evt-04-11-1951-stone-of-scone.prompt: What do you do with the stone now that its hiding place is about to be discovered?

choices.text: Leave it at Arbroath Abbey for the authorities to find and return it
Break it apart so it can never be used again
Smuggle it onto a ship bound for another country
Bury it permanently in the Scottish Highlands

evt-04-11-1951-stone-of-scone.butterflyEffect: Authorities recovered the stone at Arbroath and returned it to Westminster Abbey, where it continued to be used in coronations. In 1996 the British government formally returned it to Scotland, where it now sits in Edinburgh Castle except when required for a coronation.

evt-04-11-1963-pope-john-xxiii.scenario: It is 11 April 1963, and you are helping Pope John XXIII finalize a new encyclical. The world nearly slid into nuclear war during last year's Cuban Missile Crisis, and he wants this document to reach further than any before it.
evt-04-11-1963-pope-john-xxiii.prompt: Who should the encyclical Pacem in terris be addressed to?

choices.text: All people of good will, not just Catholics
Heads of Western governments only
Members of the Roman Curia
Catholic bishops alone

evt-04-11-1963-pope-john-xxiii.butterflyEffect: Pacem in terris became the first papal encyclical addressed to "all men of good will" rather than Catholics alone, arguing for human rights, disarmament, and peaceful coexistence amid Cold War tensions. It shaped later Vatican diplomacy and became a touchstone for the Church's modern engagement with global human rights.

evt-04-11-1965-midwestern-united-states.scenario: It is the afternoon of Palm Sunday, April 11, 1965, and the sky over Indiana, Ohio, and Michigan has turned an ominous green. As a local radio announcer, you receive word from the Weather Bureau that severe supercells are forming with almost no lead time before touchdown.
evt-04-11-1965-midwestern-united-states.prompt: What should you urge listeners to do as the warnings come in?

choices.text: Wait for a confirmed visual sighting before saying anything on air
Hold off on warnings until after church services end
Broadcast continuous warnings and urge immediate shelter despite the short lead time
Advise people to watch from their windows to track the storm's path

evt-04-11-1965-midwestern-united-states.butterflyEffect: Nearly 50 tornadoes tore through six states that day, killing 271 people in one of the deadliest outbreaks in American history. The tragedy exposed how little warning time communities had, spurring major investment in tornado detection, sirens, and what became NOAA Weather Radio.

evt-04-11-1968-rudi-dutschke.scenario: It is 11 April 1968, and you are Rudi Dutschke, walking to a Berlin pharmacy. A young stranger calls out your name and approaches on his bicycle, reaching into his jacket.
evt-04-11-1968-rudi-dutschke.prompt: What does the stranger do next?

choices.text: He warns him that police are watching
He shoots Dutschke at close range
He hands him a political pamphlet
He asks for his autograph

evt-04-11-1968-rudi-dutschke.butterflyEffect: Josef Bachmann, a young man influenced by far-right and anti-communist rhetoric, shot Dutschke three times, gravely wounding him. The attack, following inflammatory press coverage of student radicals, ignited the "Easter Riots" across West Germany and further radicalized parts of the student left in the years that followed.

evt-04-11-1970-apollo-13.scenario: It's April 13, 1970, two days after launch. An oxygen tank has just exploded, crippling your command module's power and life support, and the Moon landing is now impossible.
evt-04-11-1970-apollo-13.prompt: What should Lovell's crew do to survive the return to Earth?

choices.text: Jettison the service module and reenter the atmosphere immediately
Continue on to attempt the planned lunar landing as scheduled
Fire the service module engine immediately for a direct abort back to Earth
Shut down the command module and use the lunar module as a lifeboat around the Moon

evt-04-11-1970-apollo-13.butterflyEffect: The crew powered down the crippled command module and crowded into the lunar module as a makeshift lifeboat, looping around the Moon on a free-return trajectory before splashing down safely on April 17. Dubbed a 'successful failure,' the mission prompted a redesign of the oxygen tank and testing procedures and became a landmark case study in improvised crisis management.

evt-04-11-1979-uganda-tanzania-war.scenario: It is 11 April 1979. You command a column of Tanzanian troops and Ugandan exile fighters advancing on Kampala as Idi Amin's demoralized army collapses and flees the capital.
evt-04-11-1979-uganda-tanzania-war.prompt: What do you do as Amin's forces abandon the city?

choices.text: Halt outside the city and wait weeks for reinforcements before advancing
Withdraw to the Tanzanian border to consolidate gains already made
Push into the city immediately to secure key points and declare the capital taken
Open negotiations with Amin's remaining commanders for a ceasefire

evt-04-11-1979-uganda-tanzania-war.butterflyEffect: The allied forces seized Kampala that day, ending Amin's eight-year dictatorship; he fled first to Libya, later to Saudi Arabia. Uganda then cycled through unstable governments until Yoweri Museveni seized power in 1986, and Tanzania's intervention became a rare precedent for African states toppling a neighboring tyrant despite the OAU's non-interference norms.

evt-04-11-1993-southern-ohio-correctiona.scenario: You are a prison official at the Southern Ohio Correctional Facility on April 11, 1993, as inmates in L Block seize control and take hostages amid fury over a mandatory tuberculosis test that conflicts with some prisoners' religious beliefs.
evt-04-11-1993-southern-ohio-correctiona.prompt: How should officials respond as the standoff drags on?

choices.text: Immediately send in tactical teams to retake the block by force
Cut all power and water to force a surrender within hours
Open sustained negotiations with inmate leaders rather than storming the block
Grant every inmate demand at once to end the crisis quickly

evt-04-11-1993-southern-ohio-correctiona.butterflyEffect: The siege stretched to eleven days, the longest prison riot in U.S. history, and inmates killed correctional officer Robert Vallandingham during the standoff. The uprising led to reforms in Ohio's prison system and death sentences for several inmate leaders identified as ringleaders.

evt-04-11-2002-2002-venezuelan-coup-atte.scenario: It's April 11, 2002, in Caracas. Deadly shootings during opposition marches have thrown the capital into chaos, and dissident generals now press you, a senior military officer, to move against President Chávez.
evt-04-11-2002-2002-venezuelan-coup-atte.prompt: What did the dissident military leadership do that night?

choices.text: Deploy troops to defend the presidential palace against the protesters
Call for fresh elections while leaving Chávez in office
Detain Chávez and install opposition figure Pedro Carmona as interim president
Negotiate a power-sharing government with Chávez still as president

evt-04-11-2002-2002-venezuelan-coup-atte.butterflyEffect: Chávez was detained and businessman Pedro Carmona was sworn in as interim president, dissolving the National Assembly and Supreme Court. The move provoked mass protests and a backlash from loyalist troops, and within 47 hours Chávez was restored to power, emerging politically strengthened for years afterward.

evt-04-11-2011-2011-minsk-metro-bombing.scenario: It is April 2011, days after a bomb tore through Kastrychnitskaya station on the Minsk Metro. You are a Belarusian prosecutor under pressure from President Lukashenko's government to close the case swiftly.
evt-04-11-2011-2011-minsk-metro-bombing.prompt: What did Belarusian authorities ultimately do with the two men convicted of the bombing?

choices.text: Sentenced them to life imprisonment without parole
Executed them by shooting despite international appeals for clemency
Released them after evidence was ruled insufficient
Extradited them to Russia to face trial there

evt-04-11-2011-2011-minsk-metro-bombing.butterflyEffect: Dzmitry Kanavalau and Uladzislau Kavalyou were executed by shooting in 2012, carried out so quickly that their families were not properly notified and international appeals for clemency went unanswered. The rushed trial and secretive execution drew sharp condemnation from the EU and human rights groups, deepening Belarus's isolation as the last country in Europe still using capital punishment.

evt-04-11-2017-borussia-dortmund.scenario: It is the evening of 11 April 2017. Three explosions have just struck the Borussia Dortmund team bus as it leaves the hotel for a Champions League quarter-final against Monaco, injuring defender Marc Bartra.
evt-04-11-2017-borussia-dortmund.prompt: What do UEFA and the club decide about the match?

choices.text: Relocate the match to a neutral stadium in another country
Postpone the match by one day to allow investigation and player recovery
Play the match as scheduled just hours later
Cancel the fixture entirely and eliminate both clubs

evt-04-11-2017-borussia-dortmund.butterflyEffect: The tie was postponed and played the following evening. Investigators later found the attacker was not a terrorist but a German-Russian man who had bought stock options betting Dortmund's share price would fall, hoping to profit from the chaos; he was convicted and jailed. The case reshaped security protocols for team travel across European football.

evt-04-11-2023-myanmar-air-force.scenario: It's April 11, 2023, in Pazigyi village, Sagaing Region. Residents have gathered to mark the opening of a local administrative office when military aircraft appear overhead.
evt-04-11-2023-myanmar-air-force.prompt: What did the junta claim the airstrike on the village was targeting?

choices.text: A weapons depot belonging to an ethnic armed organization
A drug trafficking operation along the Sagaing border
A foreign-backed political rally against the military government
An alleged gathering of anti-junta People's Defence Force fighters

evt-04-11-2023-myanmar-air-force.butterflyEffect: The strike killed roughly 100 civilians, including many children attending the ceremony, drawing sharp international condemnation of the military junta. It intensified calls for an arms embargo on Myanmar and hardened resistance to the regime amid the ongoing civil war.

evt-04-12-1204-fourth-crusade.scenario: It is April 1204. You stand with the Venetian and crusader forces outside the walls of Constantinople, a campaign that set out for Jerusalem but has ended up besieging the Christian capital of Byzantium instead.
evt-04-12-1204-fourth-crusade.prompt: Once the city's defenses collapse, what do the crusade's leaders decide?

choices.text: Abandon the siege and continue on toward Jerusalem
Sack the city for days, plundering it and installing a Latin ruler
Withdraw entirely and return home without taking the city
Spare the city and restore the existing Byzantine emperor to power

evt-04-12-1204-fourth-crusade.butterflyEffect: The crusaders sacked Constantinople for three days, looting treasures and sacred relics and installing a Latin emperor in place of the Byzantine one. The empire was partitioned among the Crusaders and Venice, deepening the schism between Eastern and Western Christianity and leaving a permanently weakened Byzantium that never fully recovered before its final fall in 1453.

evt-04-12-1776-american-revolution.scenario: It's April 12, 1776, in Halifax, North Carolina. Delegates to the Provincial Congress are debating what instructions to give their representatives at the Continental Congress in Philadelphia.
evt-04-12-1776-american-revolution.prompt: What instruction does the North Carolina Provincial Congress adopt for its delegates?

choices.text: Demand a separate peace treaty with Britain for North Carolina alone
Order North Carolina's immediate withdrawal from the Congress
Instruct delegates to seek further reconciliation with the king
Authorize delegates to vote for independence from Britain

evt-04-12-1776-american-revolution.butterflyEffect: The Halifax Resolves authorized North Carolina's delegates to vote for independence, making it the first colony to explicitly do so. The resolution emboldened other colonies toward the same step, helping pave the way for the Lee Resolution and the Declaration of Independence just months later.

evt-04-12-1807-froberg-mutiny.scenario: It's April 1807 at Fort Ricasoli on British-held Malta. Albanian and Greek soldiers of the Froberg Regiment, angry over pay and rank, have seized the fort and are refusing to stand down.
evt-04-12-1807-froberg-mutiny.prompt: How does the British command respond to the mutiny after eight days of standoff?

choices.text: Quietly withdraw all British troops from Malta
Grant the mutineers' demands for higher pay and rank
Besiege the fort, suppress the mutiny, and execute the ringleaders
Disband the regiment peacefully with full pensions

evt-04-12-1807-froberg-mutiny.butterflyEffect: British forces besieged and retook the fort, and the mutiny's ringleaders were executed once the garrison surrendered. The affair became one of the most serious mutinies of the Napoleonic Wars and made British commanders far warier of hastily raising mercenary regiments from the Balkans and Ottoman lands.

evt-04-12-1822-greek-war-of-independence.scenario: It is April 1822 on the island of Chios, long known for its prosperity and peaceful relations under Ottoman rule, after a small band of Greek rebels briefly landed and stirred an uprising there.
evt-04-12-1822-greek-war-of-independence.prompt: How does the Ottoman government respond to the uprising on Chios?

choices.text: Dismiss the incident as too minor to warrant a response
Negotiate expanded local autonomy for Chios
Offer a general amnesty to defuse tensions
Send an overwhelming punitive force to make a brutal example of the island

evt-04-12-1822-greek-war-of-independence.butterflyEffect: Ottoman forces landed in overwhelming numbers and carried out a devastating reprisal against the island's population, killing or enslaving tens of thousands. News of the massacre shocked Europe, inspired Delacroix's painting 'The Massacre at Chios,' and swelled philhellenic sympathy that helped bring British, French, and Russian support to the Greek cause.

evt-04-12-1861-confederate-states-of-ame.scenario: It is before dawn on 12 April 1861. You are a Union soldier inside Fort Sumter as Confederate cannon around Charleston Harbor open fire on the fort under orders from General Beauregard.
evt-04-12-1861-confederate-states-of-ame.prompt: What does the fort's commander, Major Robert Anderson, do?

choices.text: Abandons the fort under cover of darkness before the attack
Surrenders the fort the moment the first shot is fired
Waits for Union reinforcements to arrive by sea before responding
Holds the fort and returns fire despite dwindling supplies

evt-04-12-1861-confederate-states-of-ame.butterflyEffect: Anderson held out and returned fire for 34 hours before surrendering when supplies and ammunition ran out; remarkably, no one was killed in the bombardment itself. The attack galvanized the North, Lincoln called for 75,000 volunteers, and four more states seceded—the American Civil War had begun.

evt-04-12-1955-polio-vaccine.scenario: It's April 12, 1955, and news bulletins interrupt regular programming: researchers have just confirmed a vaccine works against the disease that has crippled your children's generation.
evt-04-12-1955-polio-vaccine.prompt: What should a parent do now that Salk's vaccine trial has been announced a success?

choices.text: Rely on quarantine measures instead, since no vaccine exists yet
Avoid public swimming pools only, since that alone prevents infection
Get your child the new inactivated (injected) vaccine as soon as it's available
Wait for Sabin's oral vaccine, since it hasn't been invented yet

evt-04-12-1955-polio-vaccine.butterflyEffect: The announcement triggered a nationwide rush for the injectable Salk vaccine, and mass immunization campaigns began within weeks. Polio cases in the US fell from tens of thousands annually to near zero within a few years, and the vaccine effort became a model for global eradication campaigns still running today.

evt-04-12-1961-vostok-1.scenario: It's April 12, 1961, and you are Yuri Gagarin aboard Vostok 1, the first human ever to orbit the Earth. As your capsule plunges back through the atmosphere, you must follow procedure to survive the descent.
evt-04-12-1961-vostok-1.prompt: What must Gagarin do to land safely after re-entry?

choices.text: Fire retrorockets a second time to slow further before touchdown
Eject from the capsule and parachute to the ground separately
Remain strapped inside and ride the capsule down to a soft landing
Steer the capsule to splash down in the ocean for recovery

evt-04-12-1961-vostok-1.butterflyEffect: Gagarin ejected at about 7 km altitude and parachuted down separately from his capsule, a detail the Soviets initially concealed since spaceflight records required the pilot to land with the craft. His single orbit made him the first human in space, intensifying the Cold War space race and helping spur Kennedy's commitment to the Moon.

evt-04-12-1983-harold-washington.scenario: It is election night, 12 April 1983, in Chicago. You're a volunteer for Harold Washington, who has just won a bitterly racially polarized mayoral race against Republican Bernard Epton.
evt-04-12-1983-harold-washington.prompt: What political fight awaits Washington once he takes office?

choices.text: A bloc of white aldermen wages the 'Council Wars,' blocking his agenda for years
He resigns within a year under public pressure
The City Council unanimously welcomes him and passes his agenda at once
The Illinois legislature moves to impeach him within months

evt-04-12-1983-harold-washington.butterflyEffect: A bloc of 29 white aldermen led by Edward Vrdolyak blocked most of Washington's agenda for years in what became known as the 'Council Wars.' A 1986 court-ordered remap of wards finally gave Washington's allies a majority, letting him govern freely until his sudden death in office in 1987, and his rise reshaped Black political power in major American cities.

evt-04-12-1993-bosnian-war.scenario: You are a NATO pilot in April 1993, flying patrols over Bosnia and Herzegovina under a fresh United Nations mandate meant to keep warring factions' aircraft out of the skies.
evt-04-12-1993-bosnian-war.prompt: What is your mission under Operation Deny Flight authorized to do?

choices.text: Evacuate civilian refugees by helicopter exclusively
Intercept and prevent unauthorized military aircraft from flying over Bosnia
Escort humanitarian aid convoys on the ground only
Immediately bomb all Bosnian Serb army positions on sight

evt-04-12-1993-bosnian-war.butterflyEffect: NATO aircraft enforced the no-fly zone, intercepting unauthorized flights, and the mission gradually expanded into close air support and strikes against Bosnian Serb positions by 1994–95. This escalation helped pressure the warring parties toward the Dayton Accords of November 1995, which ended the war.

evt-04-12-1994-laurence-canter-and-marth.scenario: It is 12 April 1994 and you moderate several Usenet newsgroups. Overnight, an identical advertisement for a law firm's 'Green Card Lottery' services has been posted to thousands of unrelated groups at once, flooding your inbox and everyone else's.
evt-04-12-1994-laurence-canter-and-marth.prompt: How does the Usenet community respond to this unprecedented mass posting?

choices.text: The Usenet community praises the firm for innovative marketing
Users flame the firm, build cancel-bots, and the incident helps popularize the term 'spam'
Nothing changes and mass advertising on Usenet remains rare for years afterward
The firm is immediately criminally prosecuted under existing law

evt-04-12-1994-laurence-canter-and-marth.butterflyEffect: Canter and Siegel's flood of identical ads is now regarded as the first massive commercial Usenet spam. Furious users coined and popularized the term 'spamming', built early filtering and cancel-bot tools to fight it, and the backlash helped seed the anti-spam movement that eventually led to laws like the 2003 CAN-SPAM Act.

evt-04-12-2002-2002-mahane-yehuda-market.scenario: It's April 12, 2002, at the entrance to Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda Market, a crowded fruit and vegetable bazaar, during the height of the Second Intifada.
evt-04-12-2002-2002-mahane-yehuda-market.prompt: Which group claims responsibility for the bombing at the market entrance?

choices.text: Hamas
The al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades
Hezbollah
Palestinian Islamic Jihad

evt-04-12-2002-2002-mahane-yehuda-market.butterflyEffect: The al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades claimed the attack, one of many bombings that struck Israeli civilian life during this period. It added pressure on Israel's government, which had days earlier launched Operation Defensive Shield, deepening the cycle of raids and attacks that marked the intifada's bloodiest year.

evt-04-12-2007-2007-iraqi-parliament-bom.scenario: It's April 12, 2007, inside Baghdad's fortified Green Zone. The Iraqi Council of Representatives has just adjourned for lunch, and sniffer dogs swept the parliament building earlier that day as a precaution.
evt-04-12-2007-2007-iraqi-parliament-bom.prompt: What happens minutes after the parliament session breaks for lunch?

choices.text: A suicide bomber detonates inside the parliament's canteen
The session simply resumes without incident after the break
Delegates are evacuated by helicopter before anything happens
The dogs detect the threat and the attack is thwarted before lunch

evt-04-12-2007-2007-iraqi-parliament-bom.butterflyEffect: A suicide bomber detonated inside the parliament's own canteen despite the security sweep, killing lawmakers' staff and wounding dozens, with two more unexploded vests found nearby. The attack exposed how deeply insurgents had penetrated even the most secured zone in Iraq, prompting mobile network shutdowns and renewed doubts about internal security screening.

evt-04-12-2010-merano-derailment.scenario: It is the morning of 12 April 2010 near Merano, South Tyrol. Heavy spring rain has soaked the slopes above a regional rail line between Latsch and Kastelbell, and a train is approaching the stretch as usual.
evt-04-12-2010-merano-derailment.prompt: What actually causes the train to derail that morning?

choices.text: The train's brakes fail on a steep downhill grade
A landslide sweeps onto the tracks directly in the train's path
A bridge along the route collapses under the train's weight
It collides head-on with another train on the same track

evt-04-12-2010-merano-derailment.butterflyEffect: A landslide loosened by the rain swept onto the tracks and the train struck it, killing nine people and injuring dozens. The disaster pushed South Tyrol's rail authority to invest in slope-monitoring and rockfall-detection systems and rethink drainage along vulnerable Alpine lines.

evt-04-13-1204-sack-of-constantinople.scenario: It is April 1204 and you stand among the Crusader host outside the walls of Constantinople. Diverted from Jerusalem by debts to Venice and the promise of a Byzantine throne, your army has just broken through the city's defenses.
evt-04-13-1204-sack-of-constantinople.prompt: What do the Crusaders do once they are inside the city?

choices.text: They sack and pillage the city for days, seizing relics and treasure
They accept a tribute payment and depart without entering the walls
They burn only military targets and leave the churches untouched
They peacefully install the promised claimant and withdraw at once

evt-04-13-1204-sack-of-constantinople.butterflyEffect: The Crusaders sacked Constantinople for days, looting treasures such as the bronze horses later placed on St Mark's Basilica in Venice, and installed a Latin Empire in place of Byzantine rule. The sack poisoned Catholic-Orthodox relations for centuries and so weakened Byzantium that it never fully recovered before falling to the Ottomans in 1453.

evt-04-13-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is before dawn on 13 April 1777 near Bound Brook, New Jersey. British and Hessian columns under Cornwallis have slipped past your pickets undetected, and gunfire erupts around your headquarters while you are barely dressed.
evt-04-13-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: As General Benjamin Lincoln, roused mid-attack, what is your only real option?

choices.text: Flee out the back before the house is surrounded
Send a rider to Washington and wait for rescue
Negotiate a personal surrender to save his men
Charge out the front door at the attacking troops
