evt-04-13-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Lincoln escaped through a back exit half-dressed, losing his baggage, papers, and several cannon and men to the raiders. Cornwallis withdrew without pressing the advantage, and the raid became one of several British spoiling attacks that punctuated the otherwise quiet 1777 New Jersey campaign before Washington's main army moved north.

evt-04-13-1943-neoclassical-architecture.scenario: You stand among the crowd on 13 April 1943 as President Roosevelt dedicates the new Jefferson Memorial on the 200th anniversary of Jefferson's birth, even as the nation is fully absorbed in fighting a world war.
evt-04-13-1943-neoclassical-architecture.prompt: What theme did Roosevelt stress in his dedication speech?

choices.text: Jefferson's role in westward continental expansion
Jefferson's devotion to individual liberty and democracy as inspiration against tyranny
Detailed plans for the postwar reconstruction of Europe
The need to negotiate an early peace with the Axis powers

evt-04-13-1943-neoclassical-architecture.butterflyEffect: By tying Jefferson's ideals of liberty to the fight against fascism, the ceremony fixed the memorial's identity as a wartime shrine to democracy rather than a mere architectural monument. Alongside the Lincoln Memorial, it became a fixture for future generations of visitors, speeches, and protest movements in the capital.

evt-04-13-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 13 April 1943, and you serve on the staff of the Polish government-in-exile in London. German radio has just broadcast the discovery of mass graves in the Katyn Forest, claiming thousands of missing Polish officers were executed there by the Soviets in 1940.
evt-04-13-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: How does the Polish government-in-exile respond to the German announcement?

choices.text: Accept the German findings immediately without seeking verification
Ask Britain to sever ties with the Soviet Union at once
Publicly dismiss the German claims as pure propaganda and take no action
Call for an independent International Red Cross investigation into the graves

evt-04-13-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The Polish government's call for an investigation gave Moscow the pretext it wanted: on 25 April 1943 the Soviet Union severed diplomatic relations with the London Poles. Stalin then began building a rival, Soviet-backed Polish administration, a rift that shaped Poland's postwar communist government for decades.

evt-04-13-1946-nakam.scenario: It is April 1946. You are one of Abba Kovner's followers, having infiltrated the water system of Nuremberg with poison meant to avenge the six million murdered in the Holocaust, awaiting Kovner's final signal from Palestine.
evt-04-13-1946-nakam.prompt: What happens before the poisoning can go ahead?

choices.text: British engineers discover the poison first
Kovner calls it off out of moral doubt
Kovner is arrested and the poison is discarded
The poisoning proceeds exactly as planned

evt-04-13-1946-nakam.butterflyEffect: Kovner was arrested by British authorities crossing into occupied Germany and had to throw the poison overboard, aborting the Nuremberg water plan before it began. Nakam's separate attempt to poison bread at a POW bakery went ahead and sickened hundreds, but the group's larger campaign of mass revenge never materialized, and Kovner later emigrated to Israel, becoming a celebrated poet and Holocaust memorial advocate.

evt-04-13-1953-ian-fleming.scenario: It's early 1953 and you are Ian Fleming, a former naval intelligence officer finishing your first thriller. You need a plain, forgettable-sounding name for your ruthless secret agent hero.
evt-04-13-1953-ian-fleming.prompt: What name does Fleming settle on for his fictional British agent?

choices.text: Peter Fleming
James Bond
Duncan Grant
Hilary Bray

evt-04-13-1953-ian-fleming.butterflyEffect: Fleming borrowed the name from an American ornithologist whose bird guide sat on his shelf. Casino Royale launched a literary and later cinematic franchise that would run for decades, making James Bond one of the most recognizable fictional characters of the 20th century.

evt-04-13-1953-central-intelligence-agen.scenario: It is 13 April 1953, and CIA Director Allen Dulles has just authorized a new covert program to develop mind-control and interrogation techniques, testing chemicals like LSD to see how far the human mind can be manipulated.
evt-04-13-1953-central-intelligence-agen.prompt: How did MKUltra researchers test these techniques on their subjects?

choices.text: Testing exclusively on soldiers who volunteered for the program
Dosing unwitting subjects with LSD and other drugs without their knowledge or consent
Running voluntary clinical trials with full informed consent
Using placebo-controlled studies with complete disclosure to participants

evt-04-13-1953-central-intelligence-agen.butterflyEffect: Investigators dosed subjects, including unwitting American citizens, without consent, and the CIA destroyed most records before a 1975 Senate inquiry could examine them fully. The scandal, surfacing amid post-Watergate distrust, led to new oversight of intelligence agencies and lasting restrictions on human experimentation.

evt-04-13-1956-vietnamese-national-army.scenario: You are a Vietnamese National Army soldier in April 1956, closing in on Ba Cụt, the one-eyed Hoa Hảo warlord whose private militia has defied Saigon's authority in the Mekong Delta for years.
evt-04-13-1956-vietnamese-national-army.prompt: What happened to Ba Cụt after government forces captured him?

choices.text: He escaped custody and led guerrilla resistance for years afterward
He was tried and executed, ending Hoa Hảo armed resistance to Diệm's government
He was exiled to France under a negotiated settlement
He was pardoned and given a senior government post

evt-04-13-1956-vietnamese-national-army.butterflyEffect: Ba Cụt was tried and executed in July 1956, ending the last major armed sect resistance to Ngô Đình Diệm's consolidation of power in South Vietnam. But the harsh crackdown on Hoa Hảo militias left lasting resentment in the delta, resentment the Viet Cong would later exploit for recruitment.

evt-04-13-1958-cold-war.scenario: It is April 1958 in Moscow. You sit on the jury of the brand-new International Tchaikovsky Competition, and an unknown 23-year-old Texan pianist has just delivered a performance the crowd will not stop cheering for, in the heart of the Soviet Union.
evt-04-13-1958-cold-war.prompt: With Cold War pride on the line, what does the jury decide?

choices.text: Split the top prize between him and a Soviet pianist
Quietly disqualify him on a technicality
Award the top prize to Cliburn on merit
Award a Soviet pianist to avoid embarrassment

evt-04-13-1958-cold-war.butterflyEffect: The jury awarded the top prize to Van Cliburn, reportedly after Khrushchev personally approved it since he was simply the best. Cliburn returned to New York to a ticker-tape parade, the first ever given to a classical musician, and became an unlikely cultural bridge between the superpowers during the Cold War.

evt-04-13-1975-1975-beirut-bus-massacre.scenario: It's 13 April 1975 in the Ain el-Rammaneh district of Beirut. A bus carrying Palestinian passengers is ambushed by Phalangist gunmen, and the streets erupt into gunfire between rival militias.
evt-04-13-1975-1975-beirut-bus-massacre.prompt: What large-scale conflict does this clash come to be seen as igniting?

choices.text: The Yom Kippur War
Black September in Jordan
The Lebanese Civil War
The Six-Day War

evt-04-13-1975-1975-beirut-bus-massacre.butterflyEffect: The Ain el-Rammaneh clashes are widely regarded as the spark of the Lebanese Civil War, a conflict that would tear the country apart for fifteen years. It devastated Beirut, drew in regional powers, and reshaped Lebanon's sectarian political balance for generations.

evt-04-13-1976-united-states-department-.scenario: It is April 1976, and you're a bank teller as the Treasury Department reintroduces the two-dollar bill for the first time in a decade, timed to coincide with the nation's Bicentennial and Thomas Jefferson's birthday.
evt-04-13-1976-united-states-department-.prompt: Why did the Treasury choose this particular design and moment to relaunch the bill?

choices.text: To combat a wave of counterfeiting in small bills
To replace the one-dollar coin then in circulation
To phase out the one-dollar bill entirely
To honor the Bicentennial and Jefferson's birthday with a redesigned bill featuring the Declaration of Independence

evt-04-13-1976-united-states-department-.butterflyEffect: Despite the patriotic timing, Americans never warmed to the note—cash drawers and vending machines weren't built for it, and many banks simply stopped stocking it. Nearly fifty years later, the two-dollar bill remains the rarest denomination in everyday circulation, more collector's curiosity than working currency.

evt-04-13-1997-tiger-woods.scenario: You're a spectator at Augusta National on 13 April 1997, watching a 21-year-old golfer finish a final round that has left the field far behind him.
evt-04-13-1997-tiger-woods.prompt: What record does Tiger Woods set with this Masters victory?

choices.text: First left-handed winner of the Masters
Oldest player to win the Masters
Youngest player to win the Masters
First amateur to win the Masters

evt-04-13-1997-tiger-woods.butterflyEffect: Woods won by 12 strokes and became the youngest Masters champion ever, at age 21. His dominance signaled a new era of power and athleticism in golf, drawing record television audiences and reshaping the sport's global reach and commercial appeal.

evt-04-13-2013-lion-air-flight-904.scenario: It is 13 April 2013 and you are aboard Lion Air Flight 904 on final approach to Ngurah Rai International Airport in Bali. The Boeing 737 suddenly loses altitude and slams into the water short of the runway, its fuselage snapping in two.
evt-04-13-2013-lion-air-flight-904.prompt: What happens to the passengers and crew after the crash into the sea?

choices.text: Most passengers are killed on impact
The crew aborts the landing in time and diverts safely
All 108 people aboard survive the crash
The aircraft explodes, killing dozens instantly

evt-04-13-2013-lion-air-flight-904.butterflyEffect: Remarkably, all 108 people aboard survived, though 46 were injured. The crash added to mounting scrutiny of Lion Air's safety record following its earlier EU airspace ban and foreshadowed the intense investigations that followed the airline's later, fatal 2018 crash.

evt-04-13-2017-war-in-afghanistan-2001-2.scenario: It is 13 April 2017 in Achin district, Nangarhar Province. Reconnaissance has mapped an ISIS-Khorasan tunnel and bunker complex, and commanders on the ground are weighing how to strike a target too deep and dispersed for ordinary bombs.
evt-04-13-2017-war-in-afghanistan-2001-2.prompt: What weapon do US forces authorize to hit the tunnel complex?

choices.text: A single precision cruise missile
A ground assault by special operations troops
The GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb
A sustained B-52 carpet-bombing campaign

evt-04-13-2017-war-in-afghanistan-2001-2.butterflyEffect: The US dropped a GBU-43/B, the 21,600-pound "Mother of All Bombs," its first combat use ever, killing dozens of ISIS-K fighters and destroying the tunnel network. The strike drew global attention as a show of force against the group and sparked debate over the weapon's proportionality and environmental impact in a civilian-adjacent area.

evt-04-13-2024-bondi-junction-stabbings.scenario: You are shopping at Westfield Bondi Junction on 13 April 2024 when a man begins attacking bystanders with a knife, and panic spreads through the mall.
evt-04-13-2024-bondi-junction-stabbings.prompt: How is the attacker ultimately stopped?

choices.text: Security guards subdued him with pepper spray
A police inspector shot him after he charged at her
Bystanders tackled and restrained him
He was talked down by a negotiator

evt-04-13-2024-bondi-junction-stabbings.butterflyEffect: An NSW Police Inspector fatally shot the attacker after he charged at her with the knife. The attack prompted national conversations in Australia about mental health care access, public venue security, and led to widespread public recognition of the responding officer's actions.

evt-04-13-2025-rory-mcilroy.scenario: You're watching the final round of the 2025 Masters at Augusta, where Rory McIlroy needs this win to complete a rare career achievement in golf.
evt-04-13-2025-rory-mcilroy.prompt: Which title does McIlroy's Masters win complete?

choices.text: The Ryder Cup title
The FedEx Cup playoff title
The Triple Crown of horse racing
The career Grand Slam of all four majors

evt-04-13-2025-rory-mcilroy.butterflyEffect: McIlroy became only the sixth man in history, and the first European, to win the modern career Grand Slam of all four major championships. It placed him alongside legends like Nicklaus, Player, and Woods in golf's most exclusive club.

evt-04-14-1471-wars-of-the-roses.scenario: It is 14 April 1471 at Barnet. You command part of the Earl of Warwick's Lancastrian army, and thick fog has scattered the battle lines so badly that your own allied units can barely tell friend from foe.
evt-04-14-1471-wars-of-the-roses.prompt: What actually followed this fog-shrouded battle?

choices.text: Warwick negotiated a truce with Edward IV on the field
The Lancastrians won and restored Henry VI to full power
Warwick was killed and his Lancastrian force was routed
Warwick withdrew his men intact and regrouped in the north

evt-04-14-1471-wars-of-the-roses.butterflyEffect: In the confusion, some of Warwick's own men attacked each other, and his Lancastrian army collapsed; Warwick himself was killed fleeing the field. His death removed the Lancastrians' most powerful backer, clearing the way for Edward IV's decisive victory at Tewkesbury weeks later.

evt-04-14-1909-31-march-incident.scenario: It is early April 1909. You are a Committee of Union and Progress officer in Constantinople as reactionary soldiers and mobs turn the city against the constitutional government, and Sultan Abdul Hamid II's loyalty is in doubt.
evt-04-14-1909-31-march-incident.prompt: What move restores CUP control of the capital?

choices.text: Appeal to European powers to intervene militarily
Negotiate a power-sharing deal directly with the Sultan
Organize a military force from Macedonia and march it on the capital
Dissolve the Ottoman parliament and rule by decree

evt-04-14-1909-31-march-incident.butterflyEffect: Mahmud Shevket Pasha organized the Action Army from Macedonia and marched it into Constantinople on 24 April, crushing the uprising. Abdul Hamid II was deposed for Mehmed V, and Mahmud Shevket Pasha became the empire's dominant military figure until his assassination in 1913.

evt-04-14-1931-alfonso-xiii.scenario: It is 14 April 1931. Municipal elections have just swept republicans and socialists into power across Spain's cities, and your advisors warn that the army can no longer be trusted to defend the throne.
evt-04-14-1931-alfonso-xiii.prompt: What does King Alfonso XIII decide to do to avoid civil bloodshed?

choices.text: Leave the country quietly without formally abdicating
Dissolve the Cortes and call new elections
Sign a formal abdication in favor of his son
Order the army to crush the republican movement

evt-04-14-1931-alfonso-xiii.butterflyEffect: Alfonso left Spain for exile without ever formally signing an abdication, hoping the monarchy might one day be restored. The Second Spanish Republic was proclaimed that same day, a fragile experiment that collapsed into civil war just five years later.

evt-04-14-1935-dust-bowl.scenario: It is the afternoon of April 14, 1935, on your Oklahoma Panhandle farm. The sky ahead has gone black as a wall of dust a thousand feet high rolls toward your homestead.
evt-04-14-1935-dust-bowl.prompt: What should you do as the massive dust storm bears down on you?

choices.text: Keep working the fields until visibility drops completely
Try to outrun the storm by car
Get everyone indoors, seal windows and doors with wet cloth
Herd the livestock into the open pasture for safety

evt-04-14-1935-dust-bowl.butterflyEffect: This storm, later called Black Sunday, was the most devastating of the Dust Bowl. Photos and eyewitness accounts of it shocked the nation and helped push Congress and the Roosevelt administration to create the Soil Conservation Service that same year.

evt-04-14-1944-ss-fort-stikine.scenario: It is April 14, 1944, at Bombay's Victoria Docks. Fire has broken out aboard the freighter Fort Stikine, whose holds are packed with cotton bales, explosives, and gold bars. You lead the dockside firefighting crew.
evt-04-14-1944-ss-fort-stikine.prompt: What fatal decision is made in fighting the shipboard fire?

choices.text: Scuttle the ship at the dockside at once
Continue fighting the fire aboard the moored ship
Evacuate the crew and let the fire burn out unattended
Immediately tow the ship out to open water

evt-04-14-1944-ss-fort-stikine.butterflyEffect: Firefighters kept battling the blaze in place rather than scuttling or towing the ship clear, and the ammunition detonated in two catastrophic explosions. The blast devastated Bombay's docks, sank over a dozen surrounding ships, killed hundreds of people, and scattered gold bars across the city, some of which were still being recovered decades later.

evt-04-14-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is April 14, 1945, in northwest Germany. Your brigade commander has just been killed by a sniper as Canadian troops take the town of Friesoythe. As the division's commanding general, you must decide how to respond.
evt-04-14-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What does the Canadian commander order done to the town?

choices.text: Occupy the town without destroying it
Arrest only the suspected sniper and spare the rest
Order the town burned and razed
Bypass the town and push on toward Berlin

evt-04-14-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Major General Christopher Vokes ordered Friesoythe razed in reprisal for his brigade commander's death. The decision remains a controversial example of collective punishment against a civilian town during the closing weeks of the war in Europe.

evt-04-14-1970-apollo-13.scenario: It is 14 April 1970, two days into your mission toward the Moon, when an oxygen tank in the service module explodes, crippling your spacecraft's power and life support far from Earth.
evt-04-14-1970-apollo-13.prompt: What should the crew do to survive the trip home?

choices.text: Shelter in the Lunar Module and use it to loop around the Moon back to Earth
Continue to the Moon and attempt the scheduled landing anyway
Jettison the Lunar Module and rely solely on the command module's remaining power
Attempt an immediate landing using the damaged service module's engine

evt-04-14-1970-apollo-13.butterflyEffect: Lovell, Swigert, and Haise powered down the crippled command module and used the Lunar Module as a lifeboat, looping around the Moon before splashing down safely on 17 April. The near-disaster, later called a "successful failure," drove major reforms in NASA's spacecraft redundancy and mission-abort procedures.

evt-04-14-1994-iraqi-no-fly-zones-confli.scenario: It is 14 April 1994. You are an F-15 pilot patrolling the northern Iraqi no-fly zone under Operation Provide Comfort when your radar picks up two helicopters your onboard identification system flags as possible Iraqi Hinds.
evt-04-14-1994-iraqi-no-fly-zones-confli.prompt: What happened when the pilots acted on that identification?

choices.text: They fired warning shots that forced the helicopters to land
They held fire and radioed AWACS for a second confirmation first
They escorted the helicopters safely to the nearest coalition base
They shot down the helicopters, which turned out to be friendly Black Hawks

evt-04-14-1994-iraqi-no-fly-zones-confli.butterflyEffect: The F-15s shot down two US Army Black Hawk helicopters that were actually carrying UN and coalition personnel, killing all 26 aboard. The disaster exposed serious flaws in IFF coordination between AWACS controllers and fighter pilots, prompting sweeping reforms to communication and identification procedures in coalition air operations.

evt-04-14-2010-2010-eruptions-of-eyjafja.scenario: You are an airline dispatcher in mid-April 2010, watching radar images of a vast ash plume from Eyjafjallajökull drifting across Iceland toward mainland Europe.
evt-04-14-2010-2010-eruptions-of-eyjafja.prompt: What do aviation authorities decide to do with flights across Western Europe?

choices.text: Continue normal schedules and monitor conditions
Fly through the ash cloud at higher altitudes
Ground flights and close airspace across much of Western Europe
Reroute only flights departing from Iceland

evt-04-14-2010-2010-eruptions-of-eyjafja.butterflyEffect: European airspace was closed for nearly a week, the largest disruption to air travel since the Second World War, stranding around ten million passengers and costing airlines billions. The chaos led to new international protocols for testing and tolerating volcanic ash concentrations, easing future shutdowns.

evt-04-14-2010-2010-yushu-earthquake.scenario: It is the morning of 14 April 2010. You are a rescue worker who has just reached Yushu, a Tibetan plateau town at nearly 3,700 meters, where traditional mud-brick and rammed-earth homes have collapsed across the town.
evt-04-14-2010-2010-yushu-earthquake.prompt: What should rescuers prioritize given how these buildings failed?

choices.text: Evacuating the entire town before any search for survivors begins
Waiting for foreign engineering teams to arrive before starting search efforts
Setting up international press briefings to draw global attention
Digging by hand through collapsed adobe walls before heavy equipment can arrive

evt-04-14-2010-2010-yushu-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Most deaths came from the collapse of traditional adobe and rammed-earth homes never built to withstand strong shaking. The disaster pushed Chinese authorities to expand seismic retrofitting and stricter building standards for rural housing across Qinghai and other Tibetan plateau regions.

evt-04-14-2014-april-2014-nyanya-bombing.scenario: You command a security checkpoint near the crowded bus station in Nyanya, Abuja, in the pre-dawn hours of 14 April 2014, days after intelligence warned of possible attacks on the capital.
evt-04-14-2014-april-2014-nyanya-bombing.prompt: What follows this morning's twin bombings at the station?

choices.text: The government negotiates a ceasefire with Boko Haram
Boko Haram claims responsibility and attacks intensify near the capital
The bombers are captured at the scene
The attack is quickly forgotten amid other news

evt-04-14-2014-april-2014-nyanya-bombing.butterflyEffect: The blasts killed at least 88 people and wounded hundreds, striking fear into the capital just as the world's attention turned to Boko Haram's kidnapping of the Chibok schoolgirls days later. Together the attacks intensified Nigeria's state of emergency in the northeast and drew unprecedented international pressure on the government's counterterrorism response.

evt-04-14-2014-chibok-schoolgirls-kidnap.scenario: It is the night of 14 April 2014. Armed men have stormed your school dormitory in Chibok and are loading you and your classmates onto trucks bound for the forest.
evt-04-14-2014-chibok-schoolgirls-kidnap.prompt: As the convoy rattles through the bush, what do many girls attempt?

choices.text: Overpower the guards as a group
Wait quietly for a negotiated release
Signal a passing military patrol with phones
Jump from the moving trucks and run into the bush

evt-04-14-2014-chibok-schoolgirls-kidnap.butterflyEffect: Dozens of girls leapt from the trucks and fled into the forest that same night, escaping capture. The rest were held for years, sparking the global #BringBackOurGirls campaign and years of negotiations that eventually freed many, though some remain missing.

evt-04-14-2016-2016-kumamoto-earthquakes.scenario: It is the night of 14 April 2016 in Kumamoto, Japan. A sharp magnitude 6.2 earthquake has just shaken your neighborhood, cracking walls and knocking out power.
evt-04-14-2016-2016-kumamoto-earthquakes.prompt: With aftershocks likely, what should residents do rather than return to damaged homes?

choices.text: Gather in the school gymnasium's upper floor
Assume the danger has passed and resume normal activity
Return home immediately to check for gas leaks
Shelter outdoors or in vehicles away from damaged buildings

evt-04-14-2016-2016-kumamoto-earthquakes.butterflyEffect: Many families spent the night in cars or shelters rather than go back inside—a wise choice, since a far larger magnitude 7.0 mainshock struck the same area two days later, on 16 April, killing dozens more and destroying thousands of homes. The confusion over which quake was the 'main' one later prompted Japan to revise how it classifies foreshocks and warns the public.

evt-04-14-2022-2022-russian-invasion-of-.scenario: It is April 13-14, 2022, in the Black Sea. You serve aboard the Moskva, flagship of Russia's Black Sea Fleet, when reports come in that Ukrainian forces have fired anti-ship missiles at your vessel.
evt-04-14-2022-2022-russian-invasion-of-.prompt: What happens to the Moskva after being struck?

choices.text: It catches fire and sinks after ammunition explodes
It is boarded and captured by Ukrainian forces
It is towed safely back to Sevastopol for repairs
It survives with only minor damage

evt-04-14-2022-2022-russian-invasion-of-.butterflyEffect: The Moskva caught fire and sank after a major explosion, the largest Russian warship lost since World War II. Its loss was a severe blow to Russian prestige, boosted Ukrainian morale, and highlighted the vulnerability of large surface warships to modern anti-ship missiles.

evt-04-14-2023-jupiter-icy-moons-explore.scenario: It is April 14, 2023, at Europe's Spaceport in French Guiana. The ESA's JUICE probe sits atop its Ariane 5 rocket, about to begin an eight-year journey to Jupiter's icy moons.
evt-04-14-2023-jupiter-icy-moons-explore.prompt: What is JUICE's primary scientific goal once it reaches Jupiter's moons?

choices.text: Search for signs of habitability in oceans beneath the icy moons' surfaces
Study only Jupiter's Great Red Spot storm system
Establish a crewed research base near Jupiter
Land probes directly on Europa's surface

evt-04-14-2023-jupiter-icy-moons-explore.butterflyEffect: JUICE will study Ganymede, Callisto, and Europa for evidence of subsurface oceans that could support life, and in 2034 it is expected to become the first spacecraft ever to orbit a moon other than Earth's when it settles into orbit around Ganymede.

evt-04-14-2024-2024-persian-gulf-floods.scenario: It is April 14, 2024, in Dubai. Nearly a year's worth of rain has fallen in a single day, flooding streets, homes, and the airport. As a government official, you must decide how the city responds.
evt-04-14-2024-2024-persian-gulf-floods.prompt: What immediate step do UAE authorities take to protect residents?

choices.text: Order a full evacuation of the entire city
Open additional roads to ease the flooding
Take no special measures and continue normal operations
Close schools and move government work online

evt-04-14-2024-2024-persian-gulf-floods.butterflyEffect: Authorities across the UAE closed schools and shifted government work to remote arrangements as floodwaters overwhelmed drainage built for a desert climate. The disaster exposed how unprepared Gulf infrastructure was for extreme rainfall, prompting renewed scrutiny of urban drainage and weather-modification practices in the region.

evt-04-15-769-lateran-council-769.scenario: It is April 769, and you sit among the assembled clergy at the Lateran Council in Rome. The Church is still reeling from the violent, uncanonical elevation of the layman Constantine II to the papacy, and factional bloodshed nearly tore Rome apart.
evt-04-15-769-lateran-council-769.prompt: What does the council decree to prevent future usurpations of the papal throne?

choices.text: The Byzantine emperor must approve every future papal election
The Lombard king would thereafter appoint the pope directly
Only ordained clergy could be elected pope, with laity barred from voting
Every bishop in Italy must personally cast a vote in each conclave

evt-04-15-769-lateran-council-769.butterflyEffect: The council ruled that only ordained clergy of the diaconate or higher, chosen with proper procedure, could become pope, and it stripped the laity of any formal role in papal elections. This reform helped shape the papal election process for centuries and was cited by later reformers seeking to insulate the papacy from secular and factional interference.

evt-04-15-1071-byzantine-norman-wars.scenario: You are a Byzantine defender trapped inside Bari, the last imperial stronghold in Italy, as Robert Guiscard's Norman forces tighten their blockade after nearly three years of siege.
evt-04-15-1071-byzantine-norman-wars.prompt: What ultimately becomes of the city and Byzantine rule in Italy?

choices.text: The city is razed and its population deported
Bari is handed over to the Papal States as a compromise
A Byzantine relief fleet arrives and breaks the siege
Bari surrenders to the Normans, ending Byzantine rule in Italy

evt-04-15-1071-byzantine-norman-wars.butterflyEffect: Bari surrendered to Robert Guiscard in April 1071, ending over five centuries of Byzantine presence in southern Italy. The conquest secured Norman dominance over the region and laid the groundwork for the later Kingdom of Sicily.

evt-04-15-1632-thirty-years-war.scenario: It is April 1632, and you march with Gustavus Adolphus's Swedish-German army as it forces a crossing of the Lech River under heavy cannon fire from Count Tilly's entrenched Catholic League troops.
evt-04-15-1632-thirty-years-war.prompt: What happens to Tilly, the Catholic League's veteran commander, during this battle?

choices.text: Tilly negotiates a truce with Gustavus Adolphus on the riverbank
Tilly is mortally wounded and dies of his injuries soon after
Tilly withdraws unharmed to reorganize his forces
Tilly is captured and held for ransom by Swedish troops

evt-04-15-1632-thirty-years-war.butterflyEffect: Tilly was struck by cannon fire during the fighting and died of his wounds weeks later, depriving the Catholic League of its most experienced general. With Tilly gone, Gustavus Adolphus pushed into Bavaria and occupied Munich, dramatically shifting momentum in the war toward the Protestant coalition.

evt-04-15-1738-serse.scenario: You are in the audience at London's King's Theatre on 15 April 1738 for the premiere of Handel's new opera Serse. Instead of a rousing overture number, the curtain rises on the Persian king addressing a plane tree.
evt-04-15-1738-serse.prompt: What unconventional choice has Handel made for the opera's opening number?

choices.text: Opening with total silence before the first line is sung
Opening with an unaccompanied battle chorus
Opening with a slow, tender aria of devotion rather than a grand overture piece
Opening with a comic duet between servants

evt-04-15-1738-serse.butterflyEffect: Serse flopped commercially, closing after only five performances, and Handel's operatic fortunes in London continued to decline afterward. Yet the gentle opening aria, now known as Handel's "Largo" (Ombra mai fù), long outlived the opera itself to become one of the most recorded pieces in classical music.

evt-04-15-1755-a-dictionary-of-the-engli.scenario: It's April 15, 1755, in London, and you are among the first readers to open Samuel Johnson's newly published two-volume dictionary, the fruit of nearly nine years of solitary labor.
evt-04-15-1755-a-dictionary-of-the-engli.prompt: What set Johnson's dictionary apart from earlier English wordbooks?

choices.text: It was commissioned and funded entirely by King George II's royal court
It illustrated word meanings with literary quotations and pursued consistent, scholarly definitions
It included only scientific and technical vocabulary
It was compiled by a committee of forty scholars in under a year

evt-04-15-1755-a-dictionary-of-the-engli.butterflyEffect: Johnson's dictionary remained the standard reference for English for over a century, until the Oxford English Dictionary project, begun in 1857, gradually superseded it. His method of illustrating meanings with literary quotations shaped the practice of lexicography worldwide.

evt-04-15-1912-sinking-of-the-titanic.scenario: It is just past midnight on 15 April 1912. You are Second Officer Charles Lightoller, supervising the lowering of lifeboats on Titanic's port side as the ship lists further into the freezing Atlantic.
evt-04-15-1912-sinking-of-the-titanic.prompt: What rule do you strictly enforce while filling the lifeboats?

choices.text: Fill every boat to its full rated capacity before lowering, regardless of who is nearest
Load crew first so they can row back for more passengers
Women and children first, even if it means lowering boats before they are full
Hold all boats at the davits until a complete muster of every passenger is confirmed

evt-04-15-1912-sinking-of-the-titanic.butterflyEffect: Lightoller's strict "women and children first" policy meant several port-side boats were lowered only half full, unnecessarily costing lives. The disaster's lifeboat shortfall led directly to the 1914 SOLAS convention requiring ships to carry lifeboat capacity for everyone aboard.

evt-04-15-1936-1936-1939-arab-revolt-in-.scenario: It is mid-April 1936, and word spreads that Arab gunmen have killed Jewish travelers near Nablus, followed swiftly by reprisal killings. As a British Mandate official, you watch strikes and unrest spread through Palestine's towns.
evt-04-15-1936-1936-1939-arab-revolt-in-.prompt: How did the British administration respond to the escalating unrest that spring?

choices.text: They halted all Jewish immigration into Palestine overnight
They granted Palestine immediate independence to defuse the crisis
They declared emergency measures, deployed troops, and later sent a Royal Commission to investigate
They transferred control of security entirely to local Arab councils

evt-04-15-1936-1936-1939-arab-revolt-in-.butterflyEffect: The unrest grew into the three-year Arab Revolt against British rule and Zionist immigration. Britain's Peel Commission, convened in response, proposed in 1937 the first formal plan to partition Palestine into separate Jewish and Arab states, an idea that would resurface in the 1947 UN partition plan.

evt-04-15-1947-jackie-robinson.scenario: It's opening day, April 15, 1947, at Ebbets Field. You're a Brooklyn Dodgers teammate watching Jackie Robinson take the field at first base, breaking a color line that had held for over sixty years.
evt-04-15-1947-jackie-robinson.prompt: What did Robinson's debut set in motion for professional baseball?

choices.text: He won the first-ever MLB Rookie of the Year Award and paved the way for full integration of the majors
Rival National League teams boycotted games against Brooklyn
He was quietly returned to the Negro Leagues before the season ended
He was suspended mid-season for violating unwritten segregation rules

evt-04-15-1947-jackie-robinson.butterflyEffect: Robinson endured intense hostility but excelled, winning the inaugural MLB Rookie of the Year Award in 1947. His success accelerated the slow integration of every major league team over the following decade and made him a lasting symbol of the civil rights movement.

evt-04-15-1952-boeing-b-52-stratofortres.scenario: It is 15 April 1952 at Boeing Field in Seattle. You are the test pilot strapped into the prototype YB-52, about to take the untried eight-engine bomber into the sky for the first time.
evt-04-15-1952-boeing-b-52-stratofortres.prompt: What is the outcome of this first flight?

choices.text: The bomber completes a successful test flight, clearing the way toward USAF production orders
The Air Force grounds the design after the flight reveals a fatal wing flutter problem
The flight is cancelled due to a hydraulic failure discovered before takeoff
An engine fire forces an emergency landing minutes after takeoff

evt-04-15-1952-boeing-b-52-stratofortres.butterflyEffect: The YB-52 flew successfully, clearing the way for full USAF production and the B-52's entry into service with Strategic Air Command in 1955. More than seventy years later, upgraded B-52s remain in active US service, making it one of the longest-serving military aircraft ever built.

evt-04-15-1955-ray-kroc.scenario: It's April 15, 1955, in Des Plaines, Illinois. You watch Ray Kroc open his very first McDonald's restaurant, built on a licensing arrangement with the McDonald brothers rather than outright ownership of their chain.
evt-04-15-1955-ray-kroc.prompt: What arrangement did Kroc use to build this single restaurant into a national chain?

choices.text: He merged the restaurant with a national hotel chain to finance expansion
He inherited full ownership of McDonald's directly from its founders in 1955
He sold regional rights to independent investors and stepped away from the business
He operated as a franchising agent, opening licensed outlets before buying the brand outright in 1961

evt-04-15-1955-ray-kroc.butterflyEffect: Kroc's franchising system, refined through the late 1950s, became the blueprint for American fast food. In 1961 he bought out the McDonald brothers for 2.7 million dollars, and by his death in 1984 McDonald's had grown into the world's largest fast-food company.

evt-04-15-2002-air-china-flight-129.scenario: You are aboard Air China Flight 129 on its final approach to Gimhae International Airport near Busan on 15 April 2002, as thick fog and rain shroud the hills surrounding the runway.
evt-04-15-2002-air-china-flight-129.prompt: What happens to the aircraft during this fog-shrouded descent?

choices.text: It executes a safe go-around and lands on a second attempt
It lands but overruns the runway into a field
It crashes into a hillside near the airport, with heavy loss of life
It diverts successfully to an alternate airport

evt-04-15-2002-air-china-flight-129.butterflyEffect: The Boeing 767 struck Mount Dotdae short of the runway, killing 129 of the 166 people aboard in one of South Korea's deadliest air disasters. The crash prompted renewed scrutiny of approach procedures and terrain warning systems at airports with hazardous surrounding topography.

evt-04-15-2013-dzhokhar-tsarnaev.scenario: You are a Boston police officer in the chaos moments after two bombs tear through the crowd near the marathon finish line on 15 April 2013, with the perpetrators still unidentified and at large.
evt-04-15-2013-dzhokhar-tsarnaev.prompt: What follows in the days after the bombing, leading to the attackers' capture?

choices.text: Authorities quickly rule the explosions an accidental gas leak
A manhunt and lockdown culminate in Tamerlan's death and Dzhokhar's capture
Both brothers are apprehended immediately at the finish line
The brothers flee the country before investigators identify them

evt-04-15-2013-dzhokhar-tsarnaev.butterflyEffect: A massive manhunt and city-wide lockdown ended with Tamerlan Tsarnaev killed in a shootout with police and his younger brother Dzhokhar captured hiding in a Watertown backyard boat. Dzhokhar was later convicted and sentenced to death, and the attack led to lasting changes in event security and counterterrorism coordination in American cities.

evt-04-15-2013-boston-marathon-bombing.scenario: It is 18 April 2013, three days after two bombs tore through the crowd at the Boston Marathon finish line. You are an FBI investigator sifting through hundreds of hours of footage from race-day cameras and cell phones.
evt-04-15-2013-boston-marathon-bombing.prompt: What breakthrough finally lets investigators identify the bombing suspects?

choices.text: Intercepted phone calls between the suspects and a foreign handler
An anonymous tip from a marathon medical volunteer
A fingerprint lift from unexploded bomb fragments
Releasing surveillance photos of two suspects to the public for tips

evt-04-15-2013-boston-marathon-bombing.butterflyEffect: The FBI's release of photos showing two men in backpacks prompted a flood of public tips and a massive social-media identification effort that named Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev within a day. The brothers' subsequent flight led to the killing of an MIT officer, a Watertown shootout, and a citywide lockdown before Dzhokhar's capture.

evt-04-15-2019-notre-dame-fire.scenario: It's the evening of April 15, 2019, and you are a Paris firefighter arriving to find flames tearing through Notre-Dame's roof, threatening its twin bell towers.
evt-04-15-2019-notre-dame-fire.prompt: What critical decision did firefighters make to save the cathedral that night?

choices.text: They flooded the entire interior with water cannons from the very start
They concentrated on stopping the fire from reaching the bell towers, sacrificing the spire and roof
They evacuated all artwork before attempting to fight the blaze at all
They demolished the north tower to create a firebreak

evt-04-15-2019-notre-dame-fire.butterflyEffect: The spire and roof collapsed, but the stone towers, bells, and most relics survived. The fire triggered a global wave of restoration donations and a French-led rebuilding effort, with the cathedral reopening to worshippers in December 2024.

evt-04-16-69-ad-69.scenario: It is April 69 AD. Your emperor Otho has just been crushed by Vitellius' legions at Bedriacum, yet thousands of loyal troops still stand ready to fight on in his name.
evt-04-16-69-ad-69.prompt: What does Otho decide to do after the defeat at Bedriacum?

choices.text: Continue fighting with his remaining loyal troops
Flee east to rally more legions to his cause
Take his own life to spare further bloodshed
Negotiate a power-sharing arrangement with Vitellius

evt-04-16-69-ad-69.butterflyEffect: Otho took his own life rather than prolong the civil war, becoming the second emperor to die in the chaotic Year of the Four Emperors. His death cleared the way for Vitellius, who would himself be overthrown and killed by Vespasian's forces before the year was out.

evt-04-16-556-justinian-i.scenario: Rome, 556. Pope Vigilius has died under suspicious circumstances, and Justinian has already thrown his backing behind Pelagius as successor. Roman clergy and citizens whisper that Pelagius had a hand in Vigilius' death.
evt-04-16-556-justinian-i.prompt: How does Pelagius try to overcome suspicion and secure his legitimacy as pope?

choices.text: Ask the Byzantine army to arrest his critics
Excommunicate every clergyman who doubts him
Abdicate and return quietly to Constantinople
Publicly swear an oath of innocence over the Gospels in St Peter's

evt-04-16-556-justinian-i.butterflyEffect: Pelagius publicly swore his innocence in Vigilius' death while holding the Gospels in St Peter's Basilica, watched by witnesses. The gesture helped him hold the papacy, but his close ties to Justinian and support for condemning the Three Chapters left lasting resentment among Western bishops.

evt-04-16-1520-revolt-of-the-comuneros.scenario: Toledo, 1520. Charles I rules Castile through foreign-born advisors while draining the treasury for his imperial ambitions abroad, and the city council is meeting to decide how far its defiance should go.
evt-04-16-1520-revolt-of-the-comuneros.prompt: What do the citizens of Toledo do in response to Charles I's rule?

choices.text: Flee the city ahead of expected royal reprisals
Submit formal petitions but remain loyal to Charles
Rise in revolt and form their own comunero government
Quietly negotiate greater autonomy through royal envoys

evt-04-16-1520-revolt-of-the-comuneros.butterflyEffect: Toledo rose in open revolt, forming a comunero government that soon linked with Valladolid and other Castilian cities against royal authority. The rebellion was ultimately crushed at the Battle of Villalar in 1521, and its defeat cemented centralized Habsburg control over Castile for generations.

evt-04-16-1799-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: It is 16 April 1799 near Mount Tabor in Ottoman Syria. Your commander, General Kléber, has led roughly 2,000 French troops onto an open plain where a much larger Ottoman relief army has surrounded the division.
evt-04-16-1799-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What must the trapped French troops do to survive until help arrives?

choices.text: Form defensive squares and hold their ground until relief arrives
Retreat immediately toward Acre
Surrender to negotiate favorable terms
Break into small groups and flee into the desert

evt-04-16-1799-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: Kléber's men held their infantry squares long enough for Napoleon's flanking force to strike the Ottoman rear, routing the far larger army. The victory secured French control near Palestine, but the wider Syrian campaign still collapsed weeks later after the failed siege of Acre, forcing Napoleon back to Egypt and eventually to France.

evt-04-16-1862-washington-d-c.scenario: Washington, D.C., 16 April 1862. Congress has just passed a law on slavery in the capital, and enslaved residents are hearing the news for the first time.
evt-04-16-1862-washington-d-c.prompt: What does the new law do for the enslaved people of Washington, D.C.?

choices.text: It frees them only after a five-year waiting period
It requires them to purchase their own freedom
It frees only children born after the law's passage
It frees them immediately, compensating former owners

evt-04-16-1862-washington-d-c.butterflyEffect: The District of Columbia Compensated Emancipation Act freed roughly 3,000 enslaved people immediately while paying their former owners for their loss. It became the only instance of federally compensated emancipation in U.S. history, and the date is still marked today as D.C. Emancipation Day.

evt-04-16-1912-harriet-quimby.scenario: At dawn on 16 April 1912, you are Harriet Quimby, seated in your Blériot monoplane at Dover, preparing to become the first woman to fly across the English Channel. Thick fog blankets the water and you have only a compass to guide you.

choices.text: Fly a longer coastal route to avoid open water
Take off anyway, navigating by compass alone through the fog
Wait for clearer skies before attempting the crossing
Request a naval escort ship to guide your flight

evt-04-16-1912-harriet-quimby.butterflyEffect: Quimby flew blind through fog for much of the crossing, landing safely on a French beach near Calais fifty-nine minutes later. Her historic feat was overshadowed within days by news of the Titanic's sinking, and though she died in a flying accident just three months later, she remained a pioneering symbol for women entering aviation.

evt-04-16-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It is dawn on 16 April 1917 along the Aisne. General Nivelle has promised a breakthrough within 48 hours using massed artillery and fast-moving infantry against fortified German positions on the Chemin des Dames ridge.
evt-04-16-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What happens when French troops advance against the well-prepared German defenses?

choices.text: They achieve the promised rapid breakthrough
They suffer heavy casualties for minimal gains, discrediting Nivelle's plan
German forces retreat without a fight
The attack is called off before troops leave their trenches

evt-04-16-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The offensive's failure, with tens of thousands of casualties for little ground, shattered French troops' faith in their commanders and triggered widespread mutinies across the army in the following weeks. Nivelle was removed and replaced by Pétain, who restored discipline through reform rather than punishment alone.

evt-04-16-1919-polish-soviet-war.scenario: It is April 1919, and you ride with Polish cavalry under Piłsudski's command, racing toward Vilnius, a city Soviet forces hold but Poland, Lithuania, and local populations all claim.
evt-04-16-1919-polish-soviet-war.prompt: How did Polish forces seize Vilnius in this swift offensive?

choices.text: A rapid cavalry-led surprise attack overran the garrison before it could be reinforced
Polish forces allied with the Red Army against local Lithuanian militias
Polish and Soviet commanders negotiated a peaceful handover
A months-long siege starved the city into surrender

evt-04-16-1919-polish-soviet-war.butterflyEffect: A rapid cavalry-led surprise attack captured Vilnius on 19 April 1919 before Soviet reinforcements could arrive. The victory ignited a bitter, decades-long Polish–Lithuanian dispute over the city, since Lithuania also claimed it as its historic capital, souring relations between the two states throughout the interwar period.

evt-04-16-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is mid-April 1945, seven months after the failed airborne assault on Arnhem during Operation Market Garden. You advance with Canadian and British troops back into the ruined Dutch city, whose population has just endured a brutal winter of occupation and famine.
evt-04-16-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What do the Allied forces achieve by 16 April 1945?

choices.text: Force a final German surrender in the Netherlands
Capture the Nijmegen bridge intact
Complete the liberation of Arnhem from German occupation
Establish the first Allied bridgehead over the Rhine

evt-04-16-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The Canadian-led capture of Arnhem finally secured the objective that had eluded the Allies in September 1944's costly airborne battle. Coming just weeks before Germany's surrender, it ended the Dutch Hunger Winter and freed a population that had suffered severe starvation under occupation.

evt-04-16-1947-bernard-baruch.scenario: You are a reporter in the South Carolina legislature on 16 April 1947, listening as financier and presidential adviser Bernard Baruch warns lawmakers of a new kind of global struggle emerging between former allies.
evt-04-16-1947-bernard-baruch.prompt: What phrase did Baruch use in this speech that would come to define the era?

choices.text: "Cold War"
"Iron Curtain"
"Cold Peace"
"Containment"

evt-04-16-1947-bernard-baruch.butterflyEffect: Baruch's phrase "Cold War," reportedly suggested by journalist Herbert Bayard Swope, was picked up and popularized later that year by columnist Walter Lippmann's book of the same name. The term stuck, giving a lasting name to the decades of US-Soviet rivalry that followed.

evt-04-16-1948-oecd.scenario: It's 16 April 1948 in Paris, and delegates from sixteen Western European nations gather to sign the founding convention of a new organisation created to coordinate American economic aid to the continent.
evt-04-16-1948-oecd.prompt: What is this new organisation's primary task?

choices.text: Negotiate the independence of European colonies
Establish a common European currency
Distribute and coordinate American economic aid among member states
Form a joint European military command

evt-04-16-1948-oecd.butterflyEffect: The Organisation for European Economic Co-operation successfully administered Marshall Plan funds and fostered unprecedented cooperation among former rivals. In 1961 it was reconstituted as the OECD, expanding beyond Europe to include the United States, Canada, and eventually dozens of nations, becoming a leading forum for global economic policy and statistics.

evt-04-16-2001-2001-bangladesh-india-bor.scenario: April 2001, Pyrdiwah on the disputed India-Bangladesh border. Bangladesh Rifles troops have surrounded an isolated Indian Border Security Force post, and tempers on both sides are at breaking point.
evt-04-16-2001-2001-bangladesh-india-bor.prompt: What happens to the surrounded Indian BSF personnel at Pyrdiwah?

choices.text: They are released unharmed after quick negotiations
They retreat safely across the border unnoticed
They successfully repel the Bangladeshi advance
Several are captured and killed, sparking outrage in India

evt-04-16-2001-2001-bangladesh-india-bor.butterflyEffect: Several BSF personnel were captured and killed in the clash, provoking outrage in India and a diplomatic crisis between the two governments. The incident led to urgent talks between New Delhi and Dhaka and pushed both nations toward later efforts to formally demarcate their still-disputed border.

evt-04-16-2003-treaty-of-accession-2003.scenario: You are a diplomat in Athens on 16 April 2003, watching foreign ministers from ten prospective member states sign the Treaty of Accession alongside EU leaders.
evt-04-16-2003-treaty-of-accession-2003.prompt: What happens to these ten countries once the treaty takes effect?

choices.text: They gain EU membership immediately upon signing in Athens
They join a customs union but remain outside EU political institutions
They formally become full members of the European Union on 1 May 2004
They become associate members pending a second referendum

evt-04-16-2003-treaty-of-accession-2003.butterflyEffect: The treaty took effect on 1 May 2004, bringing in Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia — the largest single expansion in EU history. It shifted the Union's center of gravity eastward, reshaping its budget, labor markets, and politics for decades, and set the template for further enlargements into the Balkans.

evt-04-16-2007-virginia-tech-shooting.scenario: It's just after 7:15 a.m. on 16 April 2007 at Virginia Tech. Two students have been shot dead in a dormitory, and as a campus administrator you must decide how to warn the rest of the 26,000-student campus before classes begin.

choices.text: Notify only local police and wait for more details before alerting students
Close only the dormitory building where the shooting occurred
Assume it was an isolated domestic dispute and continue with the normal schedule
Immediately lock down the entire campus and alert every student and staff member

evt-04-16-2007-virginia-tech-shooting.butterflyEffect: University officials waited over two hours, sending a campus-wide alert only at 9:26 a.m. By then Seung-Hui Cho had entered Norris Hall and begun a second attack that killed 30 more people. The delayed response became the central controversy of the tragedy, prompting lawsuits, a state review panel, and reforms to U.S. campus emergency-notification laws, including amendments to the federal Clery Act requiring timely warnings.

evt-04-16-2012-trial-of-anders-behring-b.scenario: You are a judge in Oslo District Court in 2012, weighing two conflicting psychiatric evaluations of Anders Behring Breivik — one declaring him psychotic and criminally insane, the other finding him legally sane.
evt-04-16-2012-trial-of-anders-behring-b.prompt: How does the court rule on his mental state?

choices.text: Partially responsible, warranting a reduced sentence
Insane and unfit to stand trial, committed to psychiatric care indefinitely
Sane and criminally responsible, eligible for ordinary sentencing
Unable to determine sanity, requiring a third independent evaluation

evt-04-16-2012-trial-of-anders-behring-b.butterflyEffect: The court ruled Breivik sane, and on 24 August 2012 sentenced him to Norway's maximum penalty, 21 years of preventive detention, extendable indefinitely if he remains a danger. The verdict affirmed his acts as a calculated political act rather than psychotic delusion, shaping Norway's ongoing debate over sentencing for terrorism and mass violence.

evt-04-16-2012-2012-pulitzer-prize.scenario: You sit on the Pulitzer Prize Board in early 2012, reviewing the fiction jury's three recommended finalists, including David Foster Wallace's posthumous novel The Pale King. No candidate secures the majority vote needed to win.
evt-04-16-2012-2012-pulitzer-prize.prompt: What does the board ultimately decide about the Fiction Prize?

choices.text: The board overrules the jury and picks its own winner
The decision is delayed until the following year
The prize is shared between all three finalists
No Fiction Prize is awarded for the year

evt-04-16-2012-2012-pulitzer-prize.butterflyEffect: It marked only the eleventh time in Pulitzer history that no Fiction Prize was awarded, drawing sharp public criticism from publishers and authors about the selection process. The controversy pushed the board to expand the fiction jury for future years to help avoid future deadlocks.

evt-04-16-2014-mv-sewol.scenario: It's the morning of 16 April 2014, and the ferry Sewol is listing sharply off the coast of South Korea. Over the intercom, the crew addresses hundreds of students below deck as the ship begins to founder.
evt-04-16-2014-mv-sewol.prompt: What did the crew instruct the passengers to do?

choices.text: Abandon ship at once and jump into the water
Follow the crew to lifeboats being lowered on the port side
Immediately put on life jackets and move to the top deck
Stay in their cabins and wait, assuring them it was safer than moving

evt-04-16-2014-mv-sewol.butterflyEffect: The repeated order to 'stay put' kept most passengers trapped as the ship rolled over, while the captain and several crew were among the first to escape. Of the 476 aboard, 304 died, most of them students from Danwon High School. The disaster triggered nationwide grief and anger, led to criminal convictions of the captain and crew, and forced sweeping reforms of South Korea's maritime safety regulations.

evt-04-16-2014-south-korea.scenario: You are a crew member aboard the ferry Sewol as it lists sharply in the Yellow Sea near Jindo Island. Hundreds of passengers, many of them high school students on a field trip, wait below deck for instructions over the intercom.
evt-04-16-2014-south-korea.prompt: What does the crew tell passengers to do as the ship begins to capsize?

choices.text: Move to the upper deck and prepare life rafts
Immediately abandon ship and jump into the sea
Remain in their cabins and await further instructions
Evacuate to lifeboats in an orderly line

evt-04-16-2014-south-korea.butterflyEffect: The order to remain in cabins, combined with crew members abandoning ship early, trapped hundreds as the vessel rolled over, killing more than 300 people, mostly students. Public fury over the crew's conduct and lax safety oversight forced the prime minister's resignation and led to sweeping reforms of South Korea's maritime and disaster-response laws.

evt-04-16-2016-2016-ecuador-earthquake.scenario: It is the evening of 16 April 2016, and a magnitude 7.8 earthquake has just leveled much of Manta's commercial district. As a rescue coordinator, you have only hours before survivors trapped in the rubble run out of air.
evt-04-16-2016-2016-ecuador-earthquake.prompt: What immediate step does President Correa's government take to organize the response?

choices.text: Rely solely on local municipal governments to manage rescue
Postpone rescue operations until international teams arrive
Declare a state of emergency and deploy over 13,000 troops and police
Request the immediate suspension of international aid

evt-04-16-2016-2016-ecuador-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The mobilization of over 13,000 troops and police helped pull survivors from collapsed buildings in Manta and Pedernales during the critical first days. The disaster, Ecuador's deadliest in decades, exposed weak coastal building codes and pushed the government toward costly reconstruction and stricter seismic regulations.

evt-04-16-2024-b-rsen.scenario: Copenhagen, 16 April 2024. Flames tear through the 17th-century Børsen during renovation work, and the building's famous dragon-tail spire is starting to buckle above you.
evt-04-16-2024-b-rsen.prompt: What do staff and bystanders do as the fire spreads through the building?

choices.text: Evacuate immediately and leave everything to firefighters
Rush inside to carry paintings and artworks to safety
Try to put out the flames themselves with garden hoses
Focus only on shoring up the building's outer walls

evt-04-16-2024-b-rsen.butterflyEffect: Staff, firefighters and passersby formed chains to carry paintings and artworks out of the burning exchange before the dragon spire collapsed. The rescue saved much of the Danish Chamber of Commerce's collection, though the building itself suffered severe damage, reigniting European debate over funding for historic heritage protection after Notre-Dame's 2019 fire.

evt-04-17-1080-canute-iv-of-denmark.scenario: It is 1080, and your brother King Harald III has just died without an heir. As a Danish nobleman watching Canute take the throne, you sense his ambitions reach well beyond Denmark's borders.
evt-04-17-1080-canute-iv-of-denmark.prompt: What ambitious plan would come to define, and ultimately end, Canute's reign?

choices.text: He pursued a claim to invade and rule England
He abdicated the throne to become a monk
He negotiated a lasting peace treaty with Normandy
He focused solely on expanding Baltic trade routes

evt-04-17-1080-canute-iv-of-denmark.butterflyEffect: Canute pressed a claim to the English throne and enforced harsh new church tithes and levies to fund it, provoking a rebellion among his own nobles. In 1086 he was cornered and killed by rebels inside a church in Odense, and the Church later canonized him as Saint Canute, Denmark's patron saint.

evt-04-17-1362-lithuanian-crusade.scenario: It is 1362, and you are a Lithuanian defender trapped inside Kaunas Castle, which has withstood a month of battering by Teutonic Knights' siege engines along the Nemunas River.
evt-04-17-1362-lithuanian-crusade.prompt: What happened when the month-long siege of Kaunas Castle finally ended?

choices.text: A negotiated surrender let the defenders leave unharmed
The garrison successfully broke the siege and drove the knights off
A relieving Lithuanian army arrived just in time to save the castle
The castle fell and its defenders were killed or captured

evt-04-17-1362-lithuanian-crusade.butterflyEffect: The castle fell to the Teutonic Order, its garrison killed or captured and the stronghold largely destroyed. The loss of Kaunas was a serious blow to Lithuanian defenses along the frontier, and the fortress had to be rebuilt as the wider Lithuanian Crusade dragged on for decades more.

evt-04-17-1797-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: It is April 1797, and you serve under Lieutenant-General Ralph Abercromby as his British fleet and troops approach the heavily fortified Spanish port of San Juan, Puerto Rico.
evt-04-17-1797-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What was the outcome of Abercromby's attempt to seize San Juan?

choices.text: The assault failed and British forces withdrew after fierce resistance
Spanish defenders surrendered without a fight
Storms forced the British to cancel the attack before landing
The British captured and held the city until 1802

evt-04-17-1797-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: Fierce Spanish resistance forced Abercromby to abandon the siege and withdraw his forces by the end of April 1797. The failure preserved Spanish control of Puerto Rico for another century, and Abercromby went on to command later campaigns in the Caribbean and Egypt before his death in 1801.

evt-04-17-1907-brazilian-battleship-mina.scenario: It is April 1907, and you sit on the Brazilian naval commission deciding whether to press ahead with laying down Minas Geraes, a British-built dreadnought that would make Brazil only the third nation with such a ship under construction.
evt-04-17-1907-brazilian-battleship-mina.prompt: What is the main strategic calculation behind commissioning this dreadnought?

choices.text: To counter German colonial expansion in southern Brazil
To secure new rubber export routes down the Amazon
To prepare Brazil for early entry into the First World War
To project naval power and outpace rivals Argentina and Chile

evt-04-17-1907-brazilian-battleship-mina.butterflyEffect: The order for Minas Geraes triggered a South American naval arms race, as Argentina and Chile scrambled to order dreadnoughts of their own to avoid falling behind. Brazil's economic boom from rubber and coffee had funded the ambition, but by the time the ships were delivered the strategic landscape had shifted and the financial strain outweighed much of the prestige gained.

evt-04-17-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It's April 17, 1942, and you are French general Henri Giraud, held prisoner by the Germans in the fortress of Königstein. Months of careful planning finally give you a chance to slip past your guards and vanish into occupied Europe.
evt-04-17-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What did Giraud do after escaping German captivity?

choices.text: He made his way to unoccupied Vichy France and later became a rival Allied leader in North Africa
He was recaptured within days and executed
He surrendered to the British and was flown to London to join de Gaulle immediately
He joined the French Resistance in Paris under a false identity

evt-04-17-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Giraud's escape made him a hero in Vichy France, and after the Allied invasion of North Africa in November 1942 he was installed as a rival to Charles de Gaulle for leadership of Free French forces. The rivalry was resolved in 1943 when their movements merged into the French Committee of National Liberation, with de Gaulle emerging as sole leader.

evt-04-17-1951-peak-district.scenario: You sit on the planning committee in April 1951 tasked with implementing Britain's new National Parks Act, weighing whether the moors and dales of Derbyshire's Peak District should become the country's very first national park.
evt-04-17-1951-peak-district.prompt: Which landscape did the committee designate as Britain's first national park?

choices.text: Snowdonia
The Lake District
Dartmoor
The Peak District

evt-04-17-1951-peak-district.butterflyEffect: The Peak District's designation on 17 April 1951 opened the floodgates: the Lake District and Snowdonia followed within months that same year, and by the end of the decade ten national parks covered England and Wales, cementing a lasting framework for countryside protection and public access.

evt-04-17-1969-communist-party-of-czecho.scenario: It's April 17, 1969, eight months after Soviet tanks crushed the Prague Spring reforms. You sit in the Central Committee as Moscow's pressure finally forces Alexander Dubček from the party leadership.
evt-04-17-1969-communist-party-of-czecho.prompt: Who replaced Dubček as First Secretary, ushering in the era of 'normalization'?

choices.text: Gustáv Husák
Ludvík Svoboda
Klement Gottwald
Leonid Brezhnev

evt-04-17-1969-communist-party-of-czecho.butterflyEffect: Gustáv Husák purged reformers, rolled back Prague Spring liberalizations, and restored censorship and repression across Czechoslovakia. Dubček himself was expelled from the party and sent to work as a forestry official, only reemerging as a symbol of resistance during the 1989 Velvet Revolution.

evt-04-17-1969-sirhan-sirhan.scenario: It's April 17, 1969, and you sit on the Los Angeles jury weighing evidence in the trial of the man who shot Senator Robert F. Kennedy in a hotel pantry the previous June.
evt-04-17-1969-sirhan-sirhan.prompt: What verdict and sentence did Sirhan Sirhan receive?

choices.text: Guilty of first-degree murder, sentenced to death by gas chamber
Guilty of second-degree murder, sentenced to life with parole
Found not guilty by reason of insanity
Guilty of manslaughter, sentenced to twenty years in prison

evt-04-17-1969-sirhan-sirhan.butterflyEffect: Sirhan's death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment in 1972 after California briefly abolished capital punishment. He remains in prison today, and the case has fueled decades of conspiracy theories about a second gunman and possible political motives behind the killing.

evt-04-17-1973-george-lucas.scenario: It's 1973, fresh off the success of American Graffiti, and you're George Lucas sitting down to sketch out a 13-page treatment for a strange space fantasy film few studios understand yet.
evt-04-17-1973-george-lucas.prompt: What did that early treatment eventually grow into?

choices.text: Blade Runner, released in 1982
Star Wars, released in 1977, launching one of cinema's most enduring franchises
Close Encounters of the Third Kind, released in 1977
2001: A Space Odyssey, released in 1968

evt-04-17-1973-george-lucas.butterflyEffect: Lucas rewrote the treatment through several drastically different drafts before Star Wars finally reached theaters in 1977. Its unprecedented success reshaped Hollywood around blockbuster franchises and merchandising, and made Lucasfilm's effects division, Industrial Light & Magic, an industry powerhouse.

evt-04-17-1975-khmer-rouge.scenario: It is April 17, 1975, and you are a resident of Phnom Penh as Khmer Rouge soldiers march into the city after five years of civil war. Loudspeakers order every resident to abandon their home immediately, claiming American bombers are coming.
evt-04-17-1975-khmer-rouge.prompt: What is your safest course of action when cadres order the city emptied at once?

choices.text: Comply immediately and join the exodus out of the city
Organize neighbors to resist the soldiers at the roadblocks
Seek shelter inside a foreign embassy compound
Barricade yourself indoors and wait for the situation to calm

evt-04-17-1975-khmer-rouge.butterflyEffect: Residents who obeyed left within hours, joining columns marched into the countryside; those who resisted, or were identified as soldiers, officials, or educated professionals, were often killed on the spot. The forced evacuation of Phnom Penh was the opening act of Democratic Kampuchea's agrarian revolution, which over the next four years led to mass death from starvation, overwork, and execution across Cambodia.

evt-04-17-1984-metropolitan-police.scenario: It's April 17, 1984, and you're policing a small anti-Gaddafi demonstration outside the Libyan embassy in St James's Square, London. Suddenly automatic gunfire erupts from an upper window of the embassy itself, and your colleague Yvonne Fletcher falls.
evt-04-17-1984-metropolitan-police.prompt: What followed the shooting of WPC Yvonne Fletcher outside the embassy?

choices.text: Britain closed its own embassy in Tripoli but kept ties with Libya
The Libyan ambassador was tried for murder in a British court
Police besieged the embassy for eleven days, and Britain severed diplomatic relations with Libya
British troops immediately stormed the embassy and arrested everyone inside

evt-04-17-1984-metropolitan-police.butterflyEffect: Diplomatic staff inside the embassy left Britain unsearched under diplomatic immunity after an eleven-day siege, so no one was ever charged with Fletcher's murder. Britain severed diplomatic relations with Libya for over a decade, and the case remained unresolved until Gaddafi's government paid compensation in 1999.

evt-04-17-1986-isles-of-scilly.scenario: It is 17 April 1986, and a Dutch ambassador has traveled to the Isles of Scilly to formally end a conflict dating back to 1651, one in which not a single shot was ever fired.
evt-04-17-1986-isles-of-scilly.prompt: What is the ambassador here to formally declare?

choices.text: A twinning ceremony between Dutch and Scillonian towns
A new fishing rights agreement for Dutch trawlers
A trade treaty granting Dutch tax exemptions on the islands
A formal peace ending the centuries-old declared state of war

evt-04-17-1986-isles-of-scilly.butterflyEffect: The 'war' had begun in 1651 when a Dutch fleet, in England's Civil War, declared war on the Royalist-held Scilly Isles to press for compensation, then simply sailed away without ever fighting. In 1986 the two sides signed a peace treaty ending the technically 335-year-old conflict, which endures today as a favourite curiosity of diplomatic trivia.

evt-04-17-1998-space-shuttle-columbia.scenario: It is 17 April 1998, and you are a payload specialist strapped into Space Shuttle Columbia, preparing to launch on STS-90, the final flight of the Spacelab program.
evt-04-17-1998-space-shuttle-columbia.prompt: What was the primary scientific focus of this mission?

choices.text: Deploying a new communications satellite
Deployment of the Hubble Space Telescope
Neurolab research into how microgravity affects the nervous system
Testing a robotic arm for future ISS assembly

evt-04-17-1998-space-shuttle-columbia.butterflyEffect: STS-90 flew the Neurolab mission, studying how microgravity affects the brain, vestibular system, and sleep. As the sixteenth and last Spacelab flight, it closed out a program running since 1983, and its findings on human physiology later informed research protocols for long-duration stays aboard the International Space Station.

evt-04-17-2003-anneli-jaatteenmaki.scenario: It is June 2003, and you are a Finnish MP examining allegations that Prime Minister Anneli Jäätteenmäki used leaked confidential documents about President Bush's private talks with her predecessor over Iraq to win the spring election.
evt-04-17-2003-anneli-jaatteenmaki.prompt: What ultimately happens to Jäätteenmäki's premiership once the leak scandal breaks?

choices.text: She leads Finland to apply for NATO membership
She calls a snap election and is re-elected decisively
She resigns after just over two months as prime minister
She wins a confidence vote and serves a full term

evt-04-17-2003-anneli-jaatteenmaki.butterflyEffect: Jäätteenmäki resigned on 24 June 2003, after just 68 days in office, the shortest tenure of any Finnish prime minister. The affair badly damaged public trust in the leaking of classified diplomatic material, though she later rebuilt her political career as a member of the European Parliament from 2004 to 2019.

evt-04-17-2006-palestinian-suicide-attac.scenario: It is the evening of 17 April 2006, and a bomber has just detonated explosives inside a crowded Tel Aviv restaurant near the old central bus station. As an Israeli security official, you must decide how to respond in the hours that follow.
evt-04-17-2006-palestinian-suicide-attac.prompt: What did Israeli authorities do in the immediate aftermath of the bombing?

choices.text: Open immediate ceasefire talks with the attack's sponsors
Seal border crossings into Gaza and tighten security at cafes and restaurants
Launch a full-scale ground invasion of the West Bank that week
Request an emergency UN peacekeeping deployment to Tel Aviv

evt-04-17-2006-palestinian-suicide-attac.butterflyEffect: Palestinian Islamic Jihad claimed responsibility for the attack, which killed eleven people and wounded dozens more. Israel responded by tightening closures on crossings into Gaza and stepping up security at public venues, deepening a cycle of restrictions that shaped daily life in the Palestinian territories for years afterward.

evt-04-17-2013-west-fertilizer-company-e.scenario: It is 17 April 2013 in West, Texas, and volunteer firefighters are rushing toward a blaze at a fertilizer storage facility, unaware that tons of ammonium nitrate sit nearby.
evt-04-17-2013-west-fertilizer-company-e.prompt: What did investigators ultimately conclude about the cause of the fire that triggered the blast?

choices.text: A worker was convicted of industrial sabotage
A lightning strike was confirmed as the ignition source
Investigators found faulty electrical wiring caused an accidental fire
The ATF said the fire was deliberately set, though the finding remained disputed

evt-04-17-2013-west-fertilizer-company-e.butterflyEffect: Fifteen people, including several volunteer firefighters, died in the explosion that followed. In 2016 the ATF stated the fire had been deliberately set, but that finding remained disputed, and the disaster spurred renewed calls for stricter federal oversight of ammonium nitrate storage near populated areas.

evt-04-17-2013-death-and-funeral-of-marg.scenario: It is 17 April 2013, and you are standing among the crowds outside St Paul's Cathedral in London, watching a gun carriage bring Margaret Thatcher's coffin for her ceremonial funeral.
evt-04-17-2013-death-and-funeral-of-marg.prompt: What made this funeral for a former prime minister historically exceptional?

choices.text: Parliament was dissolved for a month of national mourning
Her coffin lay in state in Westminster Hall for a week
The reigning monarch personally attended, an honour last given to Churchill
She was buried in Westminster Abbey among past monarchs

evt-04-17-2013-death-and-funeral-of-marg.butterflyEffect: Queen Elizabeth II attended, making Thatcher only the second former prime minister after Winston Churchill to receive that honour. The funeral's scale and the mixed public reaction reflected how sharply divided opinion of her premiership remained, a division that continued to shape British political debate for years.

evt-04-17-2014-nasa.scenario: It's April 17, 2014, and you're part of the Kepler mission science team studying a faint red dwarf star 500 light-years away. Your data reveals a rocky world roughly Earth's size orbiting squarely within the star's habitable zone.
evt-04-17-2014-nasa.prompt: What did NASA announce about this newly confirmed planet, Kepler-186f?

choices.text: It was the first rogue planet discovered outside any star system
It was the first Earth-sized planet found orbiting within another star's habitable zone
It was confirmed to have liquid water oceans on its surface
It was the first exoplanet ever directly photographed

evt-04-17-2014-nasa.butterflyEffect: Kepler-186f became a landmark benchmark in the search for potentially habitable worlds, though orbiting a red dwarf means it may be tidally locked and hostile to life as we know it. The discovery intensified interest in exoplanet research and helped justify follow-up missions like TESS and the James Webb Space Telescope.

evt-04-17-2021-death-and-funeral-of-prin.scenario: It is April 2021, and you are among the royal household staff planning the funeral of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, at St George's Chapel while England remains under strict COVID-19 gathering limits.
evt-04-17-2021-death-and-funeral-of-prin.prompt: What rule most shapes how the funeral must be arranged?

choices.text: A strict 30-guest limit imposed by pandemic restrictions
A public procession through central London beforehand
A delay of several months until restrictions were lifted
A full state funeral with foreign heads of state attending

evt-04-17-2021-death-and-funeral-of-prin.butterflyEffect: Only 30 mourners were permitted inside St George's Chapel, and the image of the Queen sitting alone in a face mask became one of the defining photographs of the pandemic. The stripped-down, socially distanced service drew widespread sympathy and renewed public debate about the isolation many families endured during lockdown funerals.

evt-04-18-1689-glorious-revolution.scenario: It is 18 April 1689 in Boston. Word has reached the colony that James II has fled England and William of Orange has landed, and the town is boiling over against the hated royal governor Sir Edmund Andros.
evt-04-18-1689-glorious-revolution.prompt: As a Boston colonist, what do you do?

choices.text: Join the militia and citizens rising up to seize Andros
Wait quietly for royal instructions from London
Flee south to New York to avoid the unrest
Write a formal petition asking King James for redress

evt-04-18-1689-glorious-revolution.butterflyEffect: Militia and townspeople rose up, seized Andros, and imprisoned him, collapsing the unpopular Dominion of New England.
