The colonies quickly restored their earlier charters and assemblies, entrenching a tradition of colonial self-government that Britain would struggle to override for the next century.

evt-04-18-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: It's April 18, 1864, near Poison Spring, Arkansas. You serve with the 1st Kansas Colored Infantry, guarding a Union foraging train ambushed by Confederate cavalry during the Camden Expedition.
evt-04-18-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What happened to many Black Union soldiers who tried to surrender in the fighting?

choices.text: They were captured and later exchanged as prisoners of war
They were disarmed and released unharmed
They were massacred rather than taken as prisoners
They were forcibly recruited into Confederate units

evt-04-18-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Confederate troops massacred surrendering and wounded Black soldiers rather than taking them prisoner. News of the killings spread through the Union army, hardened Northern resolve, and fed into breakdowns over prisoner exchanges tied to the treatment of Black troops.

evt-04-18-1915-world-war-i.scenario: It is 18 April 1915. French aviator Roland Garros, whose plane carries a secret propeller deflector letting his machine gun fire straight ahead, is hit by ground fire over German lines and forced down before he can destroy the aircraft.
evt-04-18-1915-world-war-i.prompt: What happens to Garros's secret weapon after he goes down?

choices.text: French mechanics reach him first and destroy the evidence
British intelligence recovers it before the Germans arrive
The wreckage burns completely and the device is lost forever
Germans capture and reverse-engineer it into their own fighter design

evt-04-18-1915-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: German engineers recovered the wrecked plane and handed it to Anthony Fokker, who improved the idea into a true synchronization gear. The resulting Fokker Eindecker fighters gave Germany a brief but deadly edge known as the "Fokker Scourge" over the Western Front skies.

evt-04-18-1946-league-of-nations.scenario: It's April 18, 1946, in Geneva. You are a delegate at the League of Nations' final assembly, closing an organization that failed to stop a second world war.
evt-04-18-1946-league-of-nations.prompt: What did delegates decide to do with the League's remaining assets and functions?

choices.text: Dissolve everything with no successor organization
Transfer them to the newly formed United Nations
Divide them among the founding member states
Keep the League running as an advisory body

evt-04-18-1946-league-of-nations.butterflyEffect: The assembly voted to transfer the League's property, library, and several technical agencies to the newly created United Nations. The UN's founders studied the League's failures closely, building in a Security Council with veto power to try to avoid the paralysis that had doomed its predecessor.

evt-04-18-1949-the-republic-of-ireland-a.scenario: It's Easter Monday, 18 April 1949, in Dublin. You watch as the new Republic of Ireland Act takes effect, formally cutting the state's last constitutional ties to the British Crown.
evt-04-18-1949-the-republic-of-ireland-a.prompt: What did the Act formally end for Ireland?

choices.text: Ireland's use of the pound sterling as currency
The partition of Ireland into two states
Ireland's neutrality in international conflicts
Ireland's membership of the British Commonwealth

evt-04-18-1949-the-republic-of-ireland-a.butterflyEffect: Declaring Ireland a republic meant it left the British Commonwealth, closing decades of ambiguity over its status since 1937. The UK responded with its own Ireland Act 1949, guaranteeing that Northern Ireland would remain part of the United Kingdom unless its parliament chose otherwise.

evt-04-18-1954-gamal-abdel-nasser.scenario: It is 18 April 1954 in Cairo. Tensions between Colonel Nasser and President Mohamed Naguib have reached a breaking point after a failed assassination attempt is blamed on the Muslim Brotherhood.
evt-04-18-1954-gamal-abdel-nasser.prompt: What actually happens to the balance of power between the two men?

choices.text: The Muslim Brotherhood seizes power from both men
The army splits into open civil war between their supporters
Naguib crushes Nasser's faction and retains full control
Nasser becomes prime minister and Naguib is effectively sidelined

evt-04-18-1954-gamal-abdel-nasser.butterflyEffect: Nasser assumed the premiership and sidelined Naguib, who was placed under house arrest, cementing Nasser's control of the revolution. This consolidation paved the way for his formal presidency in 1956 and his later leadership of pan-Arab nationalism through the Suez Crisis.

evt-04-18-1980-robert-mugabe.scenario: It is 18 April 1980, and Zimbabwe has just gained independence. You are a white commercial farmer who fought against Mugabe's guerrillas during the war, and you have no idea what the new prime minister intends for people like you.
evt-04-18-1980-robert-mugabe.prompt: What does Mugabe actually do as Zimbabwe's first prime minister?

choices.text: He expels every white resident from the country within a year
He calls for reconciliation and urges white farmers to remain
He orders reprisals against former Rhodesian fighters and settlers
He nationalizes all white-owned farmland immediately

evt-04-18-1980-robert-mugabe.butterflyEffect: Mugabe publicly urged reconciliation, telling whites to stay and keep farming while promising majority rule without immediate mass land seizure. That uneasy peace held for two decades, until fast-track land reform in the 2000s reversed it and helped trigger economic collapse.

evt-04-18-1980-zimbabwe.scenario: It's April 18, 1980, in a stadium in Salisbury, soon to be renamed Harare. You watch as the Union Jack is lowered and Zimbabwe formally gains independence after years of guerrilla war and white minority rule under Rhodesia.
evt-04-18-1980-zimbabwe.prompt: Who was sworn in as Zimbabwe's first prime minister that day?

choices.text: Canaan Banana
Joshua Nkomo
Ian Smith
Robert Mugabe

evt-04-18-1980-zimbabwe.butterflyEffect: Robert Mugabe became prime minister, initially preaching reconciliation between Black and white Zimbabweans. His government later grew increasingly authoritarian, and decisions made in these early years shaped decades of land disputes and economic turmoil that followed.

evt-04-18-1980-elmore-city-oklahoma.scenario: It's early 1980 in Elmore City, Oklahoma, a town that has banned public dancing since 1898. You're a high schooler who has just convinced the town council to consider letting your class hold a dance.
evt-04-18-1980-elmore-city-oklahoma.prompt: What did the council decide about lifting the town's decades-old dance ban?

choices.text: They allowed dancing only for adults over 18
They upheld the ban permanently
They voted to lift the ban and allow the dance
They asked the state legislature to intervene instead

evt-04-18-1980-elmore-city-oklahoma.butterflyEffect: The council voted to lift the ban, and Elmore City held its first sanctioned dance that spring. The story of the campaign became the basis for the 1984 film Footloose, turning a small-town council vote into pop-culture legend.

evt-04-18-1988-operation-praying-mantis.scenario: It's 18 April 1988 in the Persian Gulf. Four days after the USS Samuel B. Roberts struck an Iranian mine, you command US Navy warships ordered to retaliate against Iranian military targets.
evt-04-18-1988-operation-praying-mantis.prompt: What did the US Navy strike during Operation Praying Mantis?

choices.text: Iranian oil platforms used for military surveillance, along with warships and gunboats
Oil tankers bound for the Soviet Union
Iranian nuclear facilities near Bushehr
The Iranian port city of Bandar Abbas

evt-04-18-1988-operation-praying-mantis.butterflyEffect: The one-day battle sank or crippled several Iranian frigates and gunboats and destroyed two oil platforms, the US Navy's largest surface engagement since World War II. It sharpened the American role in the 'Tanker War' and contributed to Iran's eventual acceptance of a ceasefire ending the Iran-Iraq War later that year.

evt-04-18-1996-operation-grapes-of-wrath.scenario: It's April 18, 1996, in southern Lebanon. Israeli shells have just struck a UN compound at Qana sheltering civilians who fled fighting between Israel and Hezbollah during Operation Grapes of Wrath.
evt-04-18-1996-operation-grapes-of-wrath.prompt: How did the international reaction to the shelling affect the operation?

choices.text: It had no effect and the operation continued unchanged
Israel was expelled from the United Nations
It fueled pressure that helped bring the operation to a ceasefire
The UN endorsed the strike as a justified military action

evt-04-18-1996-operation-grapes-of-wrath.butterflyEffect: Global condemnation of the civilian deaths at the UN compound put intense diplomatic pressure on Israel, helping push both sides toward a ceasefire understanding days later. That April Understanding set informal rules limiting attacks on civilians that shaped Israeli-Hezbollah conflict dynamics for the next decade.

evt-04-18-2018-protests-against-daniel-o.scenario: It's mid-April 2018 in Managua. President Daniel Ortega has just announced a plan to fix the social security system, and university students are pouring into the streets in anger.
evt-04-18-2018-protests-against-daniel-o.prompt: What sparked the nationwide protests against Ortega that began this week?

choices.text: Ortega's re-election with a court-approved third term
A reform cutting pensions and raising social security contributions
The cancellation of national elections
A currency devaluation announced by the central bank

evt-04-18-2018-protests-against-daniel-o.butterflyEffect: A reform cutting pensions and raising payroll contributions ignited protests that quickly merged with broader anger at Ortega's rule, met by a violent government crackdown. The unrest became the largest sustained challenge to his government, driving hundreds of deaths, mass emigration, and years of continued repression.

evt-04-18-2019-united-states-department-.scenario: It is 18 April 2019. You are a reporter in the room as Attorney General William Barr prepares to release a redacted version of Robert Mueller's report on Russian interference and possible obstruction of justice.
evt-04-18-2019-united-states-department-.prompt: What does the released report actually conclude about obstruction?

choices.text: It fully clears the president of any wrongdoing
It states it does not exonerate the president on obstruction
It recommends immediate criminal indictment of the president
It finds no evidence of any Russian interference at all

evt-04-18-2019-united-states-department-.butterflyEffect: The report explicitly stated it did not exonerate the president on obstruction, contradicting the more favorable summary Barr had issued weeks earlier. The clash over Barr's characterization deepened partisan mistrust of the DOJ and fueled congressional hearings into the investigation's conduct.

evt-04-18-2019-mueller-report.scenario: It's April 18, 2019, in Washington. Attorney General William Barr is about to release a redacted version of Robert Mueller's two-year investigation into Russian election interference and possible obstruction of justice.
evt-04-18-2019-mueller-report.prompt: What did the Mueller report conclude about charging Trump with obstruction?

choices.text: It explicitly cleared him of any wrongdoing
It formally recommended his indictment
It did not exonerate him but reached no prosecutorial conclusion
It recommended immediate impeachment proceedings

evt-04-18-2019-mueller-report.butterflyEffect: The report stated it did not exonerate Trump on obstruction but declined to reach a prosecutorial judgment. Barr's summary framing the findings favorably for Trump drew sharp criticism and became a flashpoint feeding later impeachment efforts.

evt-04-19-1506-lisbon-massacre.scenario: It is the week after Easter, 1506. Word reaches you, King Manuel I of Portugal, that a mob incited by two Dominican friars has spent days massacring hundreds of "New Christians" in the streets of Lisbon.
evt-04-19-1506-lisbon-massacre.prompt: As king, what do you order in response to the massacre?

choices.text: Take no action and let the matter be forgotten
Execute the instigating friars and let New Christians emigrate freely
Blame the New Christians themselves for provoking unrest
Pardon the mob to preserve religious unity in the capital

evt-04-19-1506-lisbon-massacre.butterflyEffect: Manuel I had the two friars who incited the mob burned, punished other ringleaders, and suspended Lisbon's civic privileges. He also granted New Christians temporary freedom to emigrate, and many fled to the Ottoman Empire and the Netherlands, seeding Sephardic communities that endured for centuries.

evt-04-19-1713-charles-vi-holy-roman-emp.scenario: It is 1713, and you advise Emperor Charles VI, who has no surviving son to inherit the vast Habsburg lands after his death. Foreign powers are watching closely for any sign of weakness in the succession.
evt-04-19-1713-charles-vi-holy-roman-emp.prompt: What does the emperor decree to secure the succession?

choices.text: A petition to the Pope to name a new male heir
An adoption of a distant male Habsburg cousin as heir
A division of the territories among the German princes
A decree allowing female inheritance of the Habsburg lands

evt-04-19-1713-charles-vi-holy-roman-emp.butterflyEffect: Charles VI issued the Pragmatic Sanction, allowing his daughter Maria Theresa to inherit the Habsburg territories undivided. When he died in 1740 without a son, rival powers contested her claim anyway, plunging Europe into the War of the Austrian Succession.

evt-04-19-1773-partition-sejm.scenario: It is 19 April 1773 in the Warsaw Sejm chamber. Russian, Prussian, and Austrian troops surround the city, and the assembled deputies are expected to rubber-stamp the partition of your homeland. Deputy Tadeusz Rejtan throws himself across the doorway to block anyone from leaving to form the fatal confederation.
evt-04-19-1773-partition-sejm.prompt: As a fellow deputy, what is the most consequential act of protest available to you now?

choices.text: Quietly sign the partition treaty to avoid bloodshed
Propose a compromise ceding only border fortresses
Physically block the chamber doorway like Rejtan to prevent a quorum
Flee the capital and rally foreign support before the vote

evt-04-19-1773-partition-sejm.butterflyEffect: Rejtan's dramatic gesture failed to stop the Sejm, which legalized the First Partition and stripped away nearly a third of the Commonwealth. His protest became a lasting symbol of doomed patriotic resistance, later immortalized in Jan Matejko's famous painting, and helped inspire the reforms of the 1791 Constitution as Poles sought to prevent further partitions.

evt-04-19-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is dawn, April 19, 1775, on Lexington Green. You are one of Captain John Parker's militiamen as a column of British regulars marches into view, sent to seize rebel arms at Concord.
evt-04-19-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What does Captain Parker order his outnumbered militia to do?

choices.text: Surrender the town's arms peacefully
Open fire on the British column immediately
Retreat to Concord before the British arrive
Stand your ground, but don't fire unless fired upon

evt-04-19-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: The militia stood firm but held their fire until a shot rang out from an unknown source, igniting a skirmish that killed several colonists. Word of the clash spread rapidly, and militiamen inflicted heavy casualties on the British column retreating from Concord, turning a local confrontation into the opening battle of the Revolutionary War.

evt-04-19-1782-states-general-of-the-net.scenario: You are John Adams in The Hague on April 19, 1782, seeking to convince the States General of the Dutch Republic to formally recognize the United States as an independent nation.
evt-04-19-1782-states-general-of-the-net.prompt: What does Adams do to secure Dutch recognition?

choices.text: Present formal credentials as U.S. minister to the States General
Negotiate a secret treaty with Britain instead
Request Spanish mediation with the Dutch
Threaten to blockade Dutch merchant shipping

evt-04-19-1782-states-general-of-the-net.butterflyEffect: The States General accepted Adams's credentials, making the Dutch Republic the second nation to recognize American independence after France. The recognition opened the door to a crucial Dutch loan that helped finance the final years of the Revolutionary War.

evt-04-19-1809-war-of-the-fifth-coalitio.scenario: It's April 19, 1809, near the Bavarian village of Teugen-Hausen. You command a division under Marshal Davout, cut off from Napoleon's main army and suddenly facing the bulk of Archduke Charles's Austrian forces.
evt-04-19-1809-war-of-the-fifth-coalitio.prompt: What should Davout's isolated corps do to avoid being overwhelmed?

choices.text: Fight through the wooded terrain and hold until reinforcements arrive
Wait motionless for Napoleon's personal orders
Retreat immediately to Regensburg
Surrender to preserve the corps

evt-04-19-1809-war-of-the-fifth-coalitio.butterflyEffect: Davout's troops fought through the wooded ravines around Teugen-Hausen, holding off repeated Austrian attacks until reinforcements arrived. This bought Napoleon time to concentrate his army, leading to French victories at Abensberg and Eckmühl days later and Archduke Charles's retreat across the Danube.

evt-04-19-1861-american-civil-war.scenario: It is April 19, 1861, and you march with the 6th Massachusetts Militia through the streets of Baltimore, changing trains en route to defend Washington. A mob of Confederate sympathizers blocks your path, hurling stones and then opening fire.
evt-04-19-1861-american-civil-war.prompt: What does the unit do when the mob turns violent?

choices.text: Fire back to break through the mob
Retreat back to the train station immediately
Wait silently for city police to intervene
Lay down arms and surrender to the crowd

evt-04-19-1861-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The soldiers fired back, and in the melee four soldiers and at least twelve civilians died—the war's first bloodshed. The riot pushed Maryland's divided loyalties into crisis, prompting Lincoln to impose martial law and occupy Baltimore to keep the strategically vital state in the Union.

evt-04-19-1875-the-minute-man.scenario: It is the early 1870s in your Concord studio. You are sculptor Daniel Chester French, commissioned to create a monument for the upcoming centennial of the Battles of Lexington and Concord, and you must decide what material will give the citizen-soldier lasting weight.
evt-04-19-1875-the-minute-man.prompt: What material do you ultimately choose for The Minute Man statue?

choices.text: Local New England granite
Carved marble imported from Italy
Bronze cast from surplus Civil War cannons
Cast iron from a Massachusetts foundry

evt-04-19-1875-the-minute-man.butterflyEffect: French cast the statue in bronze melted down from ten Civil War-era cannons donated by Congress, linking the Revolutionary militiaman to the recently ended Civil War. Unveiled on 19 April 1875 at the battle's centennial, the statue became one of America's most recognized images of the citizen-soldier and made French's early reputation.

evt-04-19-1903-kishinev-pogrom.scenario: It's Easter Day, 19 April 1903, in Kishinev. Rumors of a ritual murder have spread through the city, and mobs are moving through Jewish neighborhoods while police stand by.
evt-04-19-1903-kishinev-pogrom.prompt: What response did the pogrom provoke among Jewish communities abroad?

choices.text: Organized relief funds and support for emigration from Russia
A boycott of Russian goods by European governments
Immediate establishment of the state of Israel
A formal Russian government apology and compensation

evt-04-19-1903-kishinev-pogrom.butterflyEffect: News of the massacre shocked world opinion and spurred American Jews to organize large-scale financial relief and emigration assistance. It also pushed Theodor Herzl to propose the Uganda Scheme as a temporary refuge, and it accelerated Jewish emigration from the Russian Empire in the years that followed.

evt-04-19-1927-mae-west.scenario: It's April 1927 in a New York courtroom. You are Mae West, on trial for writing, producing, and starring in your play "Sex," which prosecutors say corrupts public morals.
evt-04-19-1927-mae-west.prompt: What sentence does the judge hand down?

choices.text: A year of probation with no jail time
Ten days in jail and a fine
Acquittal on all charges
A lifetime ban from the New York stage

evt-04-19-1927-mae-west.butterflyEffect: West was sentenced to ten days in jail, of which she served eight with good behavior, along with a fine. The scandal only heightened her notoriety, fueling ticket sales for her later plays and launching her into a lucrative Hollywood career, though it also drew ongoing censorship battles that culminated in Hays Code restrictions on her films.

evt-04-19-1956-grace-kelly.scenario: You stand among the crowd outside Saint Nicholas Cathedral in Monaco on April 19, 1956, watching Hollywood star Grace Kelly arrive to marry Prince Rainier III in a wedding broadcast to millions.
evt-04-19-1956-grace-kelly.prompt: What did this marriage actually deliver for tiny Monaco?

choices.text: A surge of global publicity and tourism for Monaco
A formal military alliance with the United States
The abolition of Monaco's casino economy
Monaco's admission to the United Nations

evt-04-19-1956-grace-kelly.butterflyEffect: The wedding turned Monaco into a global media sensation, drawing tourists, press, and prestige to the tiny principality almost overnight. Grace Kelly's fame helped secure Monaco's independence and economic future, cementing its identity as a glamorous destination for decades to come.

evt-04-19-1971-salyut-1.scenario: It is 19 April 1971 at Baikonur Cosmodrome. Your Proton rocket has just carried Salyut 1, the world's first space station, into low Earth orbit, and mission control now waits to see whether a crew can safely dock and occupy it.
evt-04-19-1971-salyut-1.prompt: What actually followed the successful launch of Salyut 1?

choices.text: The launch failed and Salyut 1 never reached orbit
A crew docked, set an endurance record, but died during their return to Earth
The station immediately malfunctioned and had to be abandoned unmanned
It was the first of many stations crewed without incident for a decade

evt-04-19-1971-salyut-1.butterflyEffect: The first crew failed to dock, but the Soyuz 11 crew later boarded successfully and set a new endurance record aboard Salyut 1—only to die during re-entry when their capsule depressurized. The tragedy forced a redesign of Soyuz spacecraft with pressure suits for descent, and the Salyut program continued, eventually leading to Mir and the ISS's Russian segment.

evt-04-19-1971-the-doors.scenario: It is early 1971 in a Los Angeles studio. You are producer Paul Rothchild, who has shepherded every Doors album so far, but the new sessions feel flat to you and you are losing patience with the direction the band wants to take.
evt-04-19-1971-the-doors.prompt: As the increasingly frustrated producer, what do you do?

choices.text: Demand the band scrap all the new songs and start over
Postpone the album indefinitely until Morrison improves
Quit the sessions and let the band self-produce with their engineer
Bring in an outside songwriter to rework the tracks

evt-04-19-1971-the-doors.butterflyEffect: Rothchild walked out, dismissing the new material as 'cocktail music,' so the band self-produced the album with engineer Bruce Botnick instead. The result, L.A. Woman, released on 19 April 1971, became one of the Doors' most acclaimed records and was the last released before Jim Morrison's death in Paris just three months later.

evt-04-19-1975-aryabhata-satellite.scenario: You are an ISRO engineer on April 19, 1975, watching a Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket lift off from Kapustin Yar carrying Aryabhata, India's first satellite, into orbit.
evt-04-19-1975-aryabhata-satellite.prompt: What did this launch actually mark for India's space program?

choices.text: The first satellite launched from Indian territory
The first satellite placed in geostationary orbit
India's first fully domestic rocket launch
India's entry into satellite technology, launched via Soviet rocket

evt-04-19-1975-aryabhata-satellite.butterflyEffect: Aryabhata proved India could design and operate its own satellites, even while relying on Soviet rockets for launch. The mission built expertise that led directly to India's first indigenous satellite launch vehicle, the SLV-3, in 1980, and the growth of ISRO into a major space agency.

evt-04-19-1984-advance-australia-fair.scenario: It's April 19, 1984. Prime Minister Bob Hawke's government must finally settle years of confusion since a 1977 plebiscite tested Australians' preference for a national song.
evt-04-19-1984-advance-australia-fair.prompt: What does the Hawke government proclaim as Australia's official national anthem?

choices.text: "Waltzing Matilda"
"Advance Australia Fair"
"Song of Australia"
"God Save the Queen"

evt-04-19-1984-advance-australia-fair.butterflyEffect: "Advance Australia Fair" was proclaimed the national anthem, ending a decade of switching between it and "God Save the Queen." The latter was retained only as the royal anthem for occasions involving the monarch, and Advance Australia Fair has remained Australia's anthem since, with its lyrics amended in 2021 to better reflect Indigenous Australians.

evt-04-19-1989-gun-turret.scenario: It is 19 April 1989 aboard USS Iowa during a gunnery exercise in the Atlantic. An explosion has just torn through gun turret two, killing 47 sailors, and you are the Navy investigator assigned to find out why.
evt-04-19-1989-gun-turret.prompt: What did the Navy's controversial initial investigation conclude caused the blast?

choices.text: Enemy sabotage during the exercise
A powder bag manufacturing defect ignited spontaneously
A lightning strike ignited the turret's magazine
A sailor deliberately caused the explosion

evt-04-19-1989-gun-turret.butterflyEffect: The Navy initially concluded that Gunner's Mate Clayton Hartwig deliberately caused the explosion, possibly to end his own life. His family and a CBS 60 Minutes report challenged the finding, and the Navy later revised its report to allow mechanical or procedural causes, making the case a lasting lesson in the limits of forensic certainty.

evt-04-19-1995-oklahoma-city-bombing.scenario: It is the afternoon of April 19, 1995, and you are a federal investigator combing through the wreckage of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building for any clue to who planted the truck bomb.
evt-04-19-1995-oklahoma-city-bombing.prompt: What physical evidence led investigators to identify the bomber within days?

choices.text: Security camera footage from inside the building
An anonymous tip from a militia informant
A recovered truck axle bearing a VIN traced to a rental agency
Fingerprints lifted from a nearby pay phone

evt-04-19-1995-oklahoma-city-bombing.butterflyEffect: A rear axle from the rental truck, recovered from the blast site, carried a VIN traced to a Ryder agency in Junction City, Kansas, where a composite sketch identified Timothy McVeigh, already in custody on an unrelated traffic stop. The bombing led Congress to pass the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996 and reshaped security around federal buildings nationwide.

evt-04-19-2000-air-philippines-flight-54.scenario: It is 19 April 2000. You are in the cockpit of Air Philippines Flight 541, descending toward Davao City through poor visibility, and as you reach minimum descent altitude the runway is still not in sight.
evt-04-19-2000-air-philippines-flight-54.prompt: What should the flight crew do at this point in the approach?

choices.text: Execute a go-around and attempt the approach again
Continue descending, trusting instruments to find the runway
Divert immediately to a distant alternate airport
Request a lower minimum descent altitude from air traffic control

evt-04-19-2000-air-philippines-flight-54.butterflyEffect: The crew continued descending without visual contact with the runway, and the Boeing 737 struck terrain south of Davao, killing all 131 aboard in the deadliest air disaster in Philippine history. The controlled-flight-into-terrain accident intensified calls for stricter approach discipline and better terrain-warning equipment on Philippine carriers.

evt-04-19-2005-2005-conclave.scenario: It's April 19, 2005, in the Sistine Chapel. You are a cardinal elector on the second day of the conclave to choose John Paul II's successor, watching the ballots being counted for the fourth time.
evt-04-19-2005-2005-conclave.prompt: Which cardinal does the conclave elect on the fourth ballot?

choices.text: Joseph Ratzinger
Carlo Maria Martini
Angelo Sodano
Jorge Bergoglio

evt-04-19-2005-2005-conclave.butterflyEffect: Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger was elected and took the name Benedict XVI, becoming the first German pope in centuries. He emphasized doctrinal orthodoxy through his papacy, and in 2013 became the first pope in nearly 600 years to resign, opening the conclave that elected Pope Francis.

evt-04-19-2013-boston-marathon-bombing.scenario: It's the early hours of 19 April 2013 in Watertown, Massachusetts. Police have cornered the Tsarnaev brothers after a car chase and firefight, and Tamerlan Tsarnaev lies dead in the street.
evt-04-19-2013-boston-marathon-bombing.prompt: What happened next in the search for his brother, Dzhokhar?

choices.text: He escaped the state and was captured weeks later
He was killed in the same shootout
He surrendered immediately at the scene
He fled and was found hours later hiding in a resident's boat

evt-04-19-2013-boston-marathon-bombing.butterflyEffect: Dzhokhar Tsarnaev evaded capture through an unprecedented lockdown of the Boston area, until a resident noticed blood on a tarp covering a backyard boat and alerted police. He was later tried, convicted, and sentenced to death, a sentence that has remained tied up in appeals for years.

evt-04-19-2020-2020-nova-scotia-attacks.scenario: It is the early hours of April 19, 2020, and you are an RCMP communications officer as reports come in that a gunman disguised as a police officer, driving a replica cruiser, is moving through rural Nova Scotia.
evt-04-19-2020-2020-nova-scotia-attacks.prompt: How does the RCMP actually choose to warn the public that morning?

choices.text: Going door-to-door to warn every household
Interrupting radio broadcasts across the province
Posting updates on Twitter instead of using the national alert system
Issuing an immediate province-wide Alert Ready warning

evt-04-19-2020-2020-nova-scotia-attacks.butterflyEffect: The RCMP relied on Twitter updates rather than the national Alert Ready emergency system, and the warnings reached many residents too late. The decision became a focal point of a public inquiry, which later recommended sweeping changes to how Canadian police issue emergency alerts during active-threat situations.

evt-04-19-2021-ingenuity-helicopter.scenario: It is 19 April 2021 on the floor of Jezero Crater. Your team at JPL has spent months preparing the small helicopter Ingenuity for a brief hop into Mars's thin atmosphere, knowing a single flight would prove whether powered flight is even possible there.
evt-04-19-2021-ingenuity-helicopter.prompt: What actually followed this first attempted flight on Mars?

choices.text: The flight was aborted before liftoff due to a software fault
It crashed immediately upon lifting off
It flew but lost contact with Earth for several days
It completed a brief hover and landed safely, proving powered flight was possible

evt-04-19-2021-ingenuity-helicopter.butterflyEffect: Ingenuity rose about three meters, hovered, and landed safely, becoming the first powered, controlled flight on another planet—a moment NASA compared to the Wright brothers' first flight. It went on to fly dozens more missions over three years, scouting terrain for the Perseverance rover before rotor damage ended its mission in 2024, proving aerial exploration's value for future planetary missions.

evt-04-20-1657-anglo-spanish-war-1654-16.scenario: It is 20 April 1657, and you command Admiral Robert Blake's English fleet off Tenerife. A Spanish treasure fleet lies at anchor in Santa Cruz harbour, sheltered by a stone fortress and shore batteries bristling with cannon.
evt-04-20-1657-anglo-spanish-war-1654-16.prompt: Do you sail in and attack the anchored fleet despite the fort's guns?

choices.text: Withdraw and wait for reinforcements from England
Attack the anchored fleet head-on under the fort's guns
Blockade the harbour and starve the Spanish out
Attempt to negotiate a ransom for the treasure fleet

evt-04-20-1657-anglo-spanish-war-1654-16.butterflyEffect: Blake pressed the attack and destroyed every Spanish ship in the harbour, but the silver had already been unloaded ashore, so no treasure was actually captured. The raid nonetheless became legendary as proof of Commonwealth naval daring, cementing England's reputation as a rising sea power under Cromwell.

evt-04-20-1809-war-of-the-fifth-coalitio.scenario: It is dawn on 20 April 1809 near the Danube. Napoleon has just arrived to personally take command, finding the Austrian army divided into separated corps under Archduke Louis and General Hiller.
evt-04-20-1809-war-of-the-fifth-coalitio.prompt: What does Napoleon do to exploit the Austrians' scattered position at Abensberg?

choices.text: Negotiate a truce to buy time
Attack the divided corps before they can unite
Withdraw westward to consolidate with reinforcements
Fortify his position and wait for the Austrians to attack

evt-04-20-1809-war-of-the-fifth-coalitio.butterflyEffect: Napoleon struck the separated Austrian corps before they could reunite, defeating Archduke Louis and Hiller's forces and shattering Austrian cohesion. The victory opened the road to Vienna, which French forces occupied within weeks, setting up the costly showdown at Wagram that July.

evt-04-20-1818-court-of-king-s-bench-eng.scenario: It is April 1818, and you are William Ashford, seeking to overturn the acquittal of Abraham Thornton for your sister Mary's murder. Thornton throws down his gauntlet before the Court of King's Bench, invoking an ancient right rarely used for centuries.
evt-04-20-1818-court-of-king-s-bench-eng.prompt: How does the Court of King's Bench rule on Thornton's demand for trial by combat?

choices.text: The court sentences Thornton immediately without further proceedings
The court rules he retains the ancient right to trial by battle
The court orders a new jury trial instead
The court dismisses the request as long obsolete

evt-04-20-1818-court-of-king-s-bench-eng.butterflyEffect: The court upheld Thornton's right to trial by battle, and when Ashford declined to fight, Thornton walked free. The case caused such public outrage that Parliament abolished trial by battle in England the following year, 1819, closing off the medieval practice for good.

evt-04-20-1828-rene-caillie.scenario: It is 1828, and disguised as a Muslim traveler, you have just become the first European to see Timbuktu and live to tell of it. The legendary city is smaller and poorer than European tales promised.
evt-04-20-1828-rene-caillie.prompt: How do you get back to France to claim the prize for reaching Timbuktu?

choices.text: Join a Berber caravan crossing the Sahara to Morocco
Travel east toward French-controlled Algeria
Wait in Timbuktu for a British rescue expedition
Sail down the Niger River to the West African coast

evt-04-20-1828-rene-caillie.butterflyEffect: Caillié joined a trans-Saharan caravan north to Fez, Morocco, then made his way to France, where the Paris Geographical Society awarded him its prize for reaching Timbuktu and returning alive. His account also punctured Europe's myth of a golden city, redirecting French colonial ambition toward the real resources of West Africa.

evt-04-20-1914-colorado-national-guard.scenario: It is 20 April 1914 at the Ludlow tent colony in southern Colorado. Gunfire has raged all day between the Colorado National Guard and striking coal miners, and flames are now consuming the camp where miners' families have been living for months.
evt-04-20-1914-colorado-national-guard.prompt: In the days that follow, how do the miners respond to the attack on their colony?

choices.text: They pursue the matter solely through federal courts
They take up arms and wage open warfare across the coalfields for ten days
Union leadership flees the state and abandons the strikers
They immediately disband the strike and return to the mines

evt-04-20-1914-colorado-national-guard.butterflyEffect: Enraged miners took up arms across the southern Colorado coalfields in what became known as the ten-day Colorado Coalfield War, attacking mine property until federal troops sent by President Wilson restored order. Ludlow became a defining symbol of labor struggle, later prompting reforms like John D. Rockefeller Jr.'s employee representation plan at the mines.

evt-04-20-1939-adolf-hitler-s-50th-birth.scenario: You stand among the crowds lining a Berlin avenue on April 20, 1939, as tens of thousands of troops and over a hundred aircraft parade past in a lavish four-hour spectacle for Hitler's 50th birthday.
evt-04-20-1939-adolf-hitler-s-50th-birth.prompt: What message is this enormous military display meant to send to the watching world?

choices.text: A tribute exclusively to German cultural achievements
A memorial ceremony for World War I veterans
A peace overture toward Britain and France
A warning to the Allied powers of Germany's military might

evt-04-20-1939-adolf-hitler-s-50th-birth.butterflyEffect: The parade was a calculated warning to Britain and France of Germany's military strength. Five months later, on 1 September 1939, Germany invaded Poland, plunging Europe into the war this show of force had foreshadowed.

evt-04-20-1939-billie-holiday.scenario: You sit in a New York recording studio on April 20, 1939, as Billie Holiday steps up to the microphone to record a haunting new song about lynching in the American South.
evt-04-20-1939-billie-holiday.prompt: What made this recording so significant in American culture?

choices.text: It became one of the first widely heard protest songs against lynching
It was banned for being an overly sentimental love song
It marked the final recording of Holiday's career
It topped the charts as a popular swing dance hit

evt-04-20-1939-billie-holiday.butterflyEffect: "Strange Fruit" became one of the earliest and most powerful protest songs against lynching, its stark imagery unsettling audiences and radio programmers alike. It later became an anthem of the civil rights movement and was named Song of the Century by Time magazine.

evt-04-20-1968-enoch-powell.scenario: It is 20 April 1968, and you are Enoch Powell, Conservative MP and Shadow Defence Secretary, about to address a Conservative Association meeting in Birmingham on the subject of Commonwealth immigration.
evt-04-20-1968-enoch-powell.prompt: What happens to Powell's political career in the immediate aftermath of the speech?

choices.text: He is dismissed from the Shadow Cabinet within a day
He resigns from Parliament in protest at party policy
He is expelled from the Conservative Party outright
He is promoted to Shadow Home Secretary for his stance

evt-04-20-1968-enoch-powell.butterflyEffect: Powell delivered his "Rivers of Blood" speech warning against mass immigration, and party leader Edward Heath sacked him from the Shadow Cabinet the very next day. The speech made Powell a lightning rod in British politics for decades and hardened national debate over race and immigration.

evt-04-20-1968-pierre-trudeau.scenario: It is April 1968, and you have just been sworn in as Canada's new prime minister. The press is calling it 'Trudeaumania,' and your party wants to turn that energy into a governing mandate before it fades.
evt-04-20-1968-pierre-trudeau.prompt: What do you do to consolidate your position as prime minister?

choices.text: Focus first on private negotiations with Quebec separatists
Call an immediate general election to capitalize on public enthusiasm
Form a coalition with the New Democratic Party
Delay any election for at least a full term

evt-04-20-1968-pierre-trudeau.butterflyEffect: Trudeau called a snap general election for June 1968, riding the wave of Trudeaumania to a strong majority government. That mandate let him pursue bilingualism reforms and later face the October Crisis and patriation of the Constitution during his long tenure.

evt-04-20-1968-south-african-airways-fli.scenario: It is dawn on 20 April 1968 at Windhoek airport. You are aboard a Boeing 707, only six weeks old, continuing its scheduled service from Johannesburg toward London after a brief stopover.
evt-04-20-1968-south-african-airways-fli.prompt: What investigators later determined caused the aircraft to fly into the ground after takeoff?

choices.text: Severe wind shear over the runway
An engine failure shortly after liftoff
Sabotage aboard the aircraft
Pilot error compounded by no ground-proximity warning system

evt-04-20-1968-south-african-airways-fli.butterflyEffect: Investigators attributed the crash largely to pilot error during the climb, worsened by the aircraft's lack of a ground-proximity warning system. Boeing acknowledged the gap in its aircraft, and the disaster remains the deadliest aviation accident in Namibia's history.

evt-04-20-1978-korean-air-lines-flight-9.scenario: It is 20 April 1978, and your Boeing 707 has strayed into Soviet airspace over the Kola Peninsula. Soviet interceptors have just fired on the aircraft, damaging it, and you must decide how to save your passengers.
evt-04-20-1978-korean-air-lines-flight-9.prompt: With the aircraft crippled over Soviet territory, what do you do?

choices.text: Try to outrun the fighters back toward Norwegian airspace
Attempt an emergency landing on a frozen lake below
Radio Washington and request a military rescue escort
Order passengers to prepare for a parachute evacuation

evt-04-20-1978-korean-air-lines-flight-9.butterflyEffect: The crew put the crippled jet down on the frozen Korpijärvi lake in Karelia; two passengers died from the missile strike but most survivors were rescued by Soviet forces. The incident exposed the risks of civilian jets straying near Soviet airspace, a warning tragically repeated with KAL 007 five years later.

evt-04-20-1985-animal-liberation-front.scenario: It is the night of 20 April 1985, and you are part of an Animal Liberation Front team that has just broken into a University of California research laboratory. Cages of animals used in experiments sit before you, along with filing cabinets of research records.
evt-04-20-1985-animal-liberation-front.prompt: What does the group do before slipping away?

choices.text: Set the building on fire to destroy all evidence
Destroy the animals' cages but leave the animals inside
Leave a note demanding funding cuts and depart empty-handed
Free the animals and take documents alleging abuse

evt-04-20-1985-animal-liberation-front.butterflyEffect: The activists freed research animals and removed documents they said exposed abusive conditions, then publicised the raid to the press. It became one of the first ALF actions to draw major American media attention, pushing research institutions to tighten security and fuelling a national debate over animal testing that shaped later legislation.

evt-04-20-1999-eric-harris-and-dylan-kle.scenario: News breaks on April 20, 1999, that two students have opened fire at Columbine High School in Colorado before turning the guns on themselves.
evt-04-20-1999-eric-harris-and-dylan-kle.prompt: What lasting change did this massacre prompt across American schools?

choices.text: An immediate nationwide ban on all firearm sales
Widespread adoption of active-shooter drills and school security measures
The closure of public high schools in favor of private schooling
A total media blackout on covering school violence

evt-04-20-1999-eric-harris-and-dylan-kle.butterflyEffect: Columbine became the byword for school shootings and prompted schools nationwide to adopt lockdown procedures, active-shooter drills, and increased security measures still in use today. It also intensified ongoing debates over gun control and media influence on youth violence.

evt-04-20-2004-nicoll-highway-mrt-statio.scenario: You are a site engineer on Singapore's Circle Line tunnel works beneath Nicoll Highway. Instruments show the excavation's retaining struts flexing more than expected, and cracks are spreading across the road surface above.
evt-04-20-2004-nicoll-highway-mrt-statio.prompt: With the ground visibly failing, what is the responsible course of action?

choices.text: Continue on schedule since minor cracking is normal
Halt work and evacuate the site immediately
Reinforce the struts overnight and resume work at dawn
Reduce excavation depth slightly but keep working

evt-04-20-2004-nicoll-highway-mrt-statio.butterflyEffect: The struts and diaphragm walls failed catastrophically, and the tunnel collapsed, killing four workers and swallowing part of the highway into a huge crater. A Committee of Inquiry found the retaining wall system had been under-designed, leading Singapore to tighten independent checks on geotechnical designs for all future underground works.

evt-04-20-2008-danica-patrick.scenario: It is 20 April 2008 at Twin Ring Motegi, and you are calling strategy for Danica Patrick late in the Indy Japan 300. Fuel is running low across the field and a final round of pit stops looms.
evt-04-20-2008-danica-patrick.prompt: Do you gamble on stretching her fuel to skip a final stop and leapfrog the leaders?

choices.text: Retire the car to preserve points standing
Pit early for fresh tires and fuel to be safe
Match every rival's pit strategy exactly
Stretch fuel mileage and skip the final pit stop

evt-04-20-2008-danica-patrick.butterflyEffect: Patrick's team stretched their fuel mileage and she took the lead during the final pit cycle, going on to win the race. It made her the first woman to win an IndyCar Series race, a milestone that reshaped her career and raised the profile of women in top-level motorsport.

evt-04-20-2010-deepwater-horizon-explosi.scenario: You are a crew member aboard the Deepwater Horizon rig on the night of April 20, 2010, when mud suddenly surges up the drill pipe from the Macondo well far below.
evt-04-20-2010-deepwater-horizon-explosi.prompt: What actually happens next aboard the rig?

choices.text: An explosion and fire erupt, and the rig later sinks
The blowout preventer activates instantly and the well is sealed
The crew safely evacuates before any damage occurs
The rig is towed to port for minor repairs

evt-04-20-2010-deepwater-horizon-explosi.butterflyEffect: A blowout triggered an explosion and fire that killed 11 workers and sank the rig two days later. The ruptured well gushed oil for 87 days, making it the largest accidental marine oil spill in history and reshaping US offshore drilling regulation.

evt-04-20-2021-derek-chauvin.scenario: It is 20 April 2021, and you are seated in a packed Minneapolis courtroom as the jury in the trial of former police officer Derek Chauvin returns after deliberating over the killing of George Floyd.
evt-04-20-2021-derek-chauvin.prompt: What is the jury's verdict on all three charges against Chauvin?

choices.text: Guilty only on the lesser manslaughter charge
A mistrial is declared due to a deadlocked jury
Guilty on all three charges
Acquitted on all charges

evt-04-20-2021-derek-chauvin.butterflyEffect: The jury convicted Chauvin on all three counts, including second-degree murder, one of the rare instances of a police officer being held criminally accountable for an on-duty killing. The verdict intensified national conversations about policing and use of force and was cited in subsequent police reform efforts across the country.

evt-04-20-2023-spacex.scenario: It is 20 April 2023, and you are watching telemetry from SpaceX's Starbase control room as the first fully stacked Starship lifts off. Minutes into flight, the booster fails to separate and the vehicle begins tumbling.
evt-04-20-2023-spacex.prompt: With stage separation failed and the rocket out of control, what should flight controllers do?

choices.text: Command the booster to attempt an emergency landing burn
Attempt a manual override to force stage separation
Trigger the flight termination system to destroy the vehicle
Continue the flight to gather more telemetry data

evt-04-20-2023-spacex.butterflyEffect: Controllers triggered the flight termination system, destroying the vehicle over the Gulf of Mexico about four minutes after liftoff. The explosion also damaged the launch pad, prompting an FAA-mandated investigation and leading SpaceX to add a water deluge system and other fixes before its next test flight.

evt-04-21-bce43-mark-antony.scenario: It is 21 April 43 BC near Mutina in northern Italy. You lead Mark Antony's legions besieging the city held by Decimus Brutus, one of Caesar's assassins, as consular armies march to break the siege.
evt-04-21-bce43-mark-antony.prompt: What happens when the consuls' forces clash with Antony's army?

choices.text: Antony's forces are defeated and he abandons the siege, retreating
Antony captures Mutina and executes Decimus Brutus
Antony and Brutus agree to divide Gaul between them
The consuls surrender and join Antony's cause

evt-04-21-bce43-mark-antony.butterflyEffect: Antony was defeated and forced to abandon the siege, and both consuls, Hirtius and Pansa, died as a result of the battle, leaving the Senate dependent on the young Octavian's army. Rather than side with the Senate, Octavian marched on Rome and forced an alliance with Antony and Lepidus, forming the Second Triumvirate that would proscribe its enemies and hasten the Republic's end.

evt-04-21-1526-ibrahim-khan-lodi.scenario: It is 21 April 1526 on the plain of Panipat. You command Sultan Ibrahim Khan Lodi's vast infantry and war-elephant army, facing Babur's far smaller force armed with cannons, matchlocks, and cavalry poised on the flanks.
evt-04-21-1526-ibrahim-khan-lodi.prompt: What happens when Babur's guns and flanking horsemen meet the Sultan's massed army?

choices.text: Both armies fight to a stalemate and negotiate a truce
Ibrahim Khan Lodi retreats to Delhi to regroup for a second battle
Babur's cannons and flanking cavalry rout the Sultanate's army and kill Ibrahim Khan Lodi
Ibrahim Khan Lodi's army breaks Babur's line and drives him from India

evt-04-21-1526-ibrahim-khan-lodi.butterflyEffect: Babur's artillery and his tulughma flanking maneuver shattered the Sultanate's army, and Ibrahim Khan Lodi was killed on the field, ending both his reign and the Lodi dynasty. Babur's victory opened the way for the Mughal Empire, which would dominate the Indian subcontinent for the next three centuries.

evt-04-21-1789-george-washington-s-recep.scenario: It is 21 April 1789. You are among the Ladies of Trenton, watching President-elect George Washington approach a triumphal arch built over the bridge at Assunpink Creek on his journey to his inauguration in New York.
evt-04-21-1789-george-washington-s-recep.prompt: What did the Trenton arch and reception commemorate?

choices.text: The signing of the Declaration of Independence
The British surrender at Yorktown
His victories at the Battle of Trenton and the Assunpink Creek
The ratification of the Constitution in New Jersey

evt-04-21-1789-george-washington-s-recep.butterflyEffect: The arch honored Washington's wartime victories at Trenton and the Assunpink Creek, part of a string of celebrations along his route north. These public displays helped cement Washington's image as a unifying national hero and set an early template for ceremonial presidential travel.

evt-04-21-1836-republic-of-texas.scenario: It's the afternoon of 21 April 1836 near the San Jacinto River. You serve under General Sam Houston, and scouts report that Santa Anna's larger Mexican force is resting, many soldiers asleep, after a long march.

choices.text: Dig in and wait for the Mexican army to attack first
Launch a surprise attack immediately while the enemy rests
Send envoys to negotiate a truce with Santa Anna
Retreat further east to gather more volunteers before engaging

evt-04-21-1836-republic-of-texas.butterflyEffect: Houston's men attacked during the Mexican army's siesta and routed them in about eighteen minutes, capturing Santa Anna the next day. The victory secured Texan independence through the Treaties of Velasco and set the stage for later U.S. annexation of Texas and the Mexican-American War.

evt-04-21-1958-united-air-lines-flight-7.scenario: It's 1958, weeks after a Douglas DC-7 airliner and an Air Force fighter jet collided over the Nevada desert, killing all 47 aboard the airliner. You sit on the panel tasked with fixing America's fractured airspace, where military and civilian flights share the sky with no shared radar picture.
evt-04-21-1958-united-air-lines-flight-7.prompt: What sweeping reform do you recommend to prevent another mid-air collision?

choices.text: Create a single federal agency controlling both civilian and military airspace
Leave military and civilian air traffic control separate but ask both to file paperwork
Ban military training flights near any commercial airport but change nothing else
Expand radar coverage for civilian routes only, leaving military flights unchanged

evt-04-21-1958-united-air-lines-flight-7.butterflyEffect: Congress passed the Federal Aviation Act of 1958, creating the FAA to unify control of civilian and military airspace under one authority. The reform followed a string of deadly 1950s mid-air collisions and reshaped American air traffic control for decades.

evt-04-21-1960-brasilia.scenario: It is 21 April 1960, and President Juscelino Kubitschek has just inaugurated Brasília, a brand-new city carved out of the Brazilian highlands, as the nation's capital. You work in a government ministry still based in Rio de Janeiro.
evt-04-21-1960-brasilia.prompt: What does the federal government do with its ministries and workers after this?

choices.text: Abandon the Brasília project entirely due to cost overruns
Split the capital equally between Rio de Janeiro and Brasília indefinitely
Relocate the ministries permanently to Brasília over the following years
Keep the federal government in Rio de Janeiro and use Brasília only for ceremonies

evt-04-21-1960-brasilia.butterflyEffect: Over the following years the federal government relocated its administration wholesale to Brasília, forcing civil servants to move to a city built almost overnight by Lúcio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer. The bold modernist capital later earned UNESCO World Heritage status and shifted Brazil's political center of gravity toward its interior.

evt-04-21-1962-century-21-exposition.scenario: It is opening day, 21 April 1962, at the Century 21 Exposition in Seattle. Crowds stream past futuristic pavilions, and a striking new tower dominates the skyline above the fairgrounds.
evt-04-21-1962-century-21-exposition.prompt: Which new structure, built for the fair, became Seattle's lasting symbol?

choices.text: An observation Ferris wheel
The Space Needle
A scale replica of the Eiffel Tower
A giant geodesic dome

evt-04-21-1962-century-21-exposition.butterflyEffect: The Space Needle, built for the exposition, became an enduring icon of Seattle long after the fair closed in October 1962. The fairgrounds themselves were repurposed into Seattle Center, and the monorail built to shuttle visitors still operates as public transit today.

evt-04-21-1975-south-vietnam.scenario: It's the night of 21 April 1975. Xuan Loc, the last defensive line before Saigon, has just fallen to North Vietnamese forces. You are President Nguyen Van Thieu, addressing the nation on television and blaming the United States for abandoning South Vietnam.
evt-04-21-1975-south-vietnam.prompt: What do you do next as your government's collapse becomes undeniable?

choices.text: Resign the presidency and transfer power to your vice president
Fly to Hanoi to negotiate a ceasefire directly with the North
Dissolve the government and call for immediate US ground troops
Declare martial law and personally lead the defense of Saigon

evt-04-21-1975-south-vietnam.butterflyEffect: Thieu resigned and handed power to Vice President Tran Van Huong, who himself gave way days later to Duong Van Minh. Minh surrendered Saigon to North Vietnamese forces on 30 April 1975, ending the war and leading to national reunification under communist rule in 1976.

evt-04-21-1975-vietnam-war.scenario: It's 21 April 1975. You are a South Vietnamese officer as Xuân Lộc, the last major defensive line before Saigon, collapses under a massive North Vietnamese assault. President Nguyễn Văn Thiệu prepares to address the nation.

choices.text: Declare martial law and remain in the presidential palace
Resign the presidency and flee into exile
Open direct ceasefire talks with Hanoi
Order a general mobilization and vow to defend Saigon to the last

evt-04-21-1975-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: Thiệu resigned that night, bitterly blaming the United States for abandoning South Vietnam, and soon fled into exile abroad. Saigon fell to North Vietnamese forces just nine days later, on 30 April 1975, ending the war and reunifying Vietnam under communist rule.

evt-04-21-1985-the-covenant-the-sword-an.scenario: It is April 1985 at the CSA's fortified Arkansas compound, 'the Farm.' FBI agents have surrounded the property after a lengthy investigation into the group's stockpiled weapons, and your leader must decide how to respond to the siege.
evt-04-21-1985-the-covenant-the-sword-an.prompt: How did the CSA standoff with federal agents end?

choices.text: The group escaped through a hidden tunnel overnight
The leader surrendered peacefully after negotiations
Members set the compound ablaze rather than surrender
Members opened fire, resulting in a fatal shootout

evt-04-21-1985-the-covenant-the-sword-an.butterflyEffect: Leader James Ellison surrendered peacefully after days of negotiation, avoiding the bloodshed many feared. The relatively bloodless outcome was later studied by federal negotiators, and Ellison's cooperation with prosecutors helped expose other far-right extremist networks in the years that followed.

evt-04-21-1989-1989-tiananmen-square-pro.scenario: It's 21 April 1989, two days before Hu Yaobang's state funeral. Tens of thousands of students have marched into Tiananmen Square, defying official warnings, to mourn the ousted reformist leader and demand political change.
evt-04-21-1989-1989-tiananmen-square-pro.prompt: What do the student organizers decide as the funeral approaches?

choices.text: Disperse quietly once the funeral service concludes
Accept the government's first offer of limited dialogue and go home
Remain in the square to press their demands after the funeral
Move the protest to Shanghai to avoid confrontation in Beijing

evt-04-21-1989-1989-tiananmen-square-pro.butterflyEffect: The students stayed, and the occupation grew for weeks, drawing workers and citizens from across Beijing and other cities. The government declared martial law in late May, and on the night of 3–4 June troops moved to clear the square by force, an event that shaped Chinese politics for a generation.

evt-04-21-1996-jokela-rail-accident.scenario: It's dawn on 21 April 1996 near Jokela, Finland. You are driving overnight express train P82 from Oulu to Helsinki through thick fog, approaching a junction with a low-speed turnout.
evt-04-21-1996-jokela-rail-accident.prompt: What must you do as you approach the turnout in the fog?

choices.text: Hold track speed and rely on the train's headlights in the fog
Disregard the speed restriction sign since fog makes it hard to see anyway
Reduce speed well before reaching the turnout
Speed up slightly to clear the junction before visibility worsens

evt-04-21-1996-jokela-rail-accident.butterflyEffect: The train failed to slow enough for the turnout and derailed, killing four people and injuring 75 of the 144 aboard. The investigation blamed overspeeding through the junction and led Finland's railways to strengthen automatic speed enforcement at similar low-speed turnouts.

evt-04-21-2010-kharkiv-pact.scenario: It is 21 April 2010 in Kharkiv, and you advise Ukrainian President Viktor Yanukovych as he negotiates with Russia over the Black Sea Fleet's lease on Crimean naval bases, due to expire in 2017.
evt-04-21-2010-kharkiv-pact.prompt: What deal does Yanukovych strike to secure cheaper energy for Ukraine?

choices.text: He proposes joint Ukrainian-Russian ownership of the fleet
He sells the naval bases outright to Russia
He rejects any extension and orders the fleet to leave by 2017
He agrees to extend the Russian lease to 2042 in exchange for discounted gas

evt-04-21-2010-kharkiv-pact.butterflyEffect: The Kharkiv Pact extended Russia's naval basing rights in Crimea to 2042 in exchange for discounted natural gas, provoking chaos in Ukraine's parliament as opposition lawmakers threw eggs and smoke bombs during ratification. The prolonged Russian military presence it secured later helped facilitate Russia's 2014 annexation of Crimea.

evt-04-21-2012-amsterdam-westerpark-trai.scenario: It is early evening on 21 April 2012 near Sloterdijk station in Amsterdam. You are the driver of an intercity train approaching a signal that investigators will later focus on, with another train on the same track ahead.
evt-04-21-2012-amsterdam-westerpark-trai.prompt: What caused the two trains to collide head-on near Sloterdijk?

choices.text: A driver passed a red stop signal
A signal box computer malfunctioned and showed green on both tracks
Brake failure prevented one train from stopping in time
Thick fog made the signals impossible to see

evt-04-21-2012-amsterdam-westerpark-trai.butterflyEffect: Investigators concluded a driver had passed a red signal, sending the trains into a head-on collision that injured around 117 people, one fatally. The crash intensified scrutiny of Dutch rail signalling safety and added pressure to accelerate automatic train protection upgrades on the national network.

evt-04-21-2014-flint-michigan.scenario: It's 21 April 2014. Flint's emergency manager has just switched the city's water supply from Detroit's system to the Flint River to cut costs while a new pipeline is built.
evt-04-21-2014-flint-michigan.prompt: What should city officials do to the new water supply to protect residents' health?

choices.text: Skip treatment for now to keep costs down during the transition
Add corrosion control treatment before distributing the water
Issue immediate boil-water advisories instead of treating the source
Test only businesses' water, not residential homes

evt-04-21-2014-flint-michigan.butterflyEffect: Officials failed to add proper corrosion control treatment, and the river water's chemistry corroded aging pipes, leaching lead into thousands of homes. The Flint water crisis became a national symbol of infrastructure neglect and environmental injustice, prompting lawsuits, criminal charges, and a costly pipe replacement program.

evt-04-21-2021-indonesian-navy.scenario: It is 21 April 2021, and you are part of the search coordination team scrambling as the Indonesian Navy submarine Nanggala fails to resurface after a torpedo drill in the Bali Sea, with oxygen reserves estimated at only about 72 hours.
evt-04-21-2021-indonesian-navy.prompt: What does the multinational search operation ultimately find?

choices.text: The crew escapes via emergency pods before oxygen runs out
The submarine is towed into Bali harbor for repairs
Wreckage is found split apart on the seabed, with all 53 crew lost
The submarine surfaces safely after an electrical fault is repaired

evt-04-21-2021-indonesian-navy.butterflyEffect: The Nanggala had broken apart at a depth beyond its crush limit, killing all 53 crew aboard. Indonesia declared national mourning, grounded its aging submarines for safety review, and accelerated stalled plans to modernize its undersea fleet with newer foreign-built boats.

evt-04-22-1073-pope-gregory-vii.scenario: Rome, April 1073: Pope Alexander II has just died, and before any formal conclave can convene, the crowd at his funeral begins acclaiming the archdeacon Hildebrand as the next pope.
evt-04-22-1073-pope-gregory-vii.prompt: As a cardinal present, what do you do about this irregular, crowd-driven acclamation?

choices.text: Declare an interregnum pending consultation with Byzantium
Send word to the Holy Roman Emperor for approval first
Accept and formally ratify the acclamation as valid
Reject it and demand a proper conclave vote

evt-04-22-1073-pope-gregory-vii.butterflyEffect: The cardinals ratified the acclamation, and Hildebrand became Pope Gregory VII. His aggressive reform agenda soon triggered the Investiture Controversy with Emperor Henry IV, culminating in the emperor's famous penance at Canossa in 1077 — a defining clash between papal and imperial authority.

evt-04-22-1500-pedro-alvares-cabral.scenario: It is 22 April 1500, and you are aboard Pedro Álvares Cabral's fleet, blown far off its intended route to India. An unfamiliar coastline appears on the horizon, unlike anything charted on your maps.
evt-04-22-1500-pedro-alvares-cabral.prompt: What does Cabral do upon sighting this unexpected land?

choices.text: Claims it for the Portuguese Crown
Sails past without landing, continuing on to India
Turns back immediately for Lisbon
Claims it for the Spanish Crown under the Treaty of Tordesillas

evt-04-22-1500-pedro-alvares-cabral.butterflyEffect: Cabral claimed the land for the Portuguese Crown, giving Portugal its foothold in South America and setting Brazil on course to become the continent's only Portuguese-speaking nation. The voyage also proved that a vast landmass separated Europe from Asia, reshaping European geography.

evt-04-22-1622-anglo-persian-capture-of-.scenario: It is April 1622, and you serve aboard an English East India Company ship anchored beside Safavid Persian forces, besieging the Portuguese fortress that has ruled Hormuz Island and its Gulf trade for over a century.
evt-04-22-1622-anglo-persian-capture-of-.prompt: What should the Anglo-Persian force do to break Portuguese control of the strait?

choices.text: Sail past Hormuz to avoid direct confrontation
Withdraw and wait for Portuguese reinforcements to arrive
Negotiate a trade treaty and leave the fortress untouched
Combine naval bombardment with a land siege to force surrender

evt-04-22-1622-anglo-persian-capture-of-.butterflyEffect: The combined assault succeeded, and the Portuguese garrison surrendered Hormuz. Portugal's century-old monopoly on Persian Gulf trade collapsed, and England gained new commercial footing in the region that helped it eclipse Portugal as the dominant European power in Persian trade.

evt-04-22-1864-coinage-act-of-1864.scenario: It is April 1864, and you sit on a U.S. Mint committee tasked with fixing a wartime cash crisis: copper cents have vanished from circulation, hoarded or replaced by private tokens.
evt-04-22-1864-coinage-act-of-1864.prompt: What alloy does the new Coinage Act mandate for the redesigned cent and new two-cent piece?

choices.text: Bronze — 95% copper, 5% tin and zinc
Pure copper, as before
Silver, to restore public confidence
A copper-nickel alloy

evt-04-22-1864-coinage-act-of-1864.butterflyEffect: Congress switched the cent (and the new two-cent coin) to a bronze alloy of 95% copper and 5% tin and zinc, and banned private one- and two-cent tokens outright. Bronze remained the standard for U.S. cents for over a century, and the ban quietly killed the vast wartime economy of Civil War store tokens.

evt-04-22-1918-transcaucasian-democratic.scenario: It is April 22, 1918, in Tiflis, and you sit among Georgian, Armenian, and Azerbaijani delegates proclaiming a joint Transcaucasian republic while Ottoman troops advance and old rivalries simmer beneath the new flag.
evt-04-22-1918-transcaucasian-democratic.prompt: What happens to this joint republic within a month of its founding?

choices.text: It splits apart as Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan each declare independence
It voluntarily rejoins Soviet Russia
It forms a lasting confederation recognized by the Ottomans
It becomes a permanent Ottoman protectorate

evt-04-22-1918-transcaucasian-democratic.butterflyEffect: Barely a month after its founding, Georgia declared independence on 26 May 1918, followed almost immediately by Armenia and Azerbaijan. The three nations went their separate ways, setting borders and rivalries in the South Caucasus that still shape the region today.

evt-04-22-1945-jasenovac-concentration-c.scenario: It is April 22, 1945, inside the Jasenovac camp, and roughly 600 remaining prisoners sense that Ustaše guards are preparing to liquidate the camp before Yugoslav Partisan forces can arrive.
evt-04-22-1945-jasenovac-concentration-c.prompt: What do the prisoners decide to do as liquidation appears imminent?

choices.text: Surrender peacefully and await liberation
Hide in the barracks until Partisans arrive
Stage a mass breakout attempt over the camp walls
Negotiate their release with the guards

evt-04-22-1945-jasenovac-concentration-c.butterflyEffect: The prisoners staged a desperate mass breakout, armed with little more than tools and stones. Most were killed in the attempt, but around a hundred escaped to tell what had happened inside the camp, making the uprising one of the rare acts of armed resistance recorded at a Holocaust-era camp.

evt-04-22-1948-1947-1948-civil-war-in-ma.scenario: Haifa, April 22, 1948: Haganah forces have broken through into the city's Arab quarters as British troops withdraw to the port, and loudspeakers announce terms for those still remaining.
evt-04-22-1948-1947-1948-civil-war-in-ma.prompt: Facing collapse of their neighborhoods, what did most of Haifa's Arab residents ultimately do?

choices.text: Seek indefinite protection from British forces at the port
Take up arms with local militias to hold their neighborhoods
Flee the city by sea and land despite calls to remain
Stay and negotiate surrender terms with Haganah commanders

evt-04-22-1948-1947-1948-civil-war-in-ma.butterflyEffect: Despite appeals from some British officials and Jewish leaders for residents to stay, the overwhelming majority fled by boat and road in the days that followed. Haifa's Arab population collapsed from roughly 70,000 to only a few thousand, a defining episode of the wider 1948 Palestinian exodus that reshaped the city permanently.

evt-04-22-1951-korean-war.scenario: Dawn, 22 April 1951: you command a company of the Gloucestershire Regiment dug in along the Imjin River as waves of Chinese troops open a massive spring offensive, aiming to smash through toward Seoul.
evt-04-22-1951-korean-war.prompt: With your battalion nearly surrounded, what does the commander order?

choices.text: Negotiate a local ceasefire with the Chinese commander
Withdraw immediately to avoid encirclement
Launch a full counterattack across the river
Hold the position at all costs to delay the Chinese advance

evt-04-22-1951-korean-war.butterflyEffect: The Glosters held their hill for three days against overwhelming numbers, buying critical time for UN forces to form a new defensive line before Seoul fell again. Most survivors were eventually overrun and captured, but the stand became legendary, earning a rare U.S. Presidential Unit Citation for a foreign unit.

evt-04-22-1970-earth-day.scenario: It's April 22, 1970, and you're a campus organizer working with Senator Gaylord Nelson's small staff, trying to turn public concern over pollution into a nationwide day of action almost overnight.
evt-04-22-1970-earth-day.prompt: What strategy do organizers use to mobilize millions across the country?

choices.text: Run a single national television campaign instead of events
Organize one large march on Washington, D.C.
Encourage decentralized local teach-ins and rallies nationwide
Focus entirely on closed-door lobbying of Congress

evt-04-22-1970-earth-day.butterflyEffect: Rather than a single centralized march, organizers let thousands of campuses, schools, and cities run their own teach-ins and rallies, and roughly 20 million Americans took part. The momentum helped push Congress to create the EPA and pass the Clean Air and Clean Water Acts within a few years, and Earth Day became an annual global event.

evt-04-22-1974-pan-am-flight-812.scenario: It is 22 April 1974, and you are aboard Pan Am's Clipper Climax, a Boeing 707 descending toward Denpasar's Ngurah Rai airport at night over Bali's mountainous terrain.
evt-04-22-1974-pan-am-flight-812.prompt: What causes the aircraft to crash short of the airport?

choices.text: A hijacking attempt leads to the crash
An engine fire forces an emergency water landing
The plane is struck by lightning and breaks apart mid-air
The aircraft descends into mountainous terrain in a controlled flight into terrain accident

evt-04-22-1974-pan-am-flight-812.butterflyEffect: The 707 struck mountainous terrain about 42 nautical miles from the airport in a controlled flight into terrain accident, killing all 107 aboard and making it Indonesia's deadliest air disaster until 1991. The crash intensified scrutiny of approach procedures at mountain-ringed airports and fed broader calls for better terrain-awareness warnings in cockpits.

evt-04-22-1977-optical-fiber.scenario: It is April 22, 1977, in Long Beach, California, and engineers are about to route live telephone calls through a new kind of cable: hair-thin glass strands carrying pulses of light instead of copper wires carrying electricity.
evt-04-22-1977-optical-fiber.prompt: What technology do engineers successfully use to carry live telephone traffic for the first time?

choices.text: Coaxial copper cable
Microwave relay towers
Satellite uplink
Optical fiber cable

evt-04-22-1977-optical-fiber.butterflyEffect: The test proved that light-based signals could reliably carry telephone traffic over glass fiber. Telecom companies began building fiber networks that eventually became the backbone of long-distance communication and, decades later, the modern internet.

evt-04-22-1992-gas-explosion.scenario: It's the morning of 22 April 1992 in the Analco neighborhood of Guadalajara. For weeks residents have complained of a strong gasoline smell rising from the sewers, but officials have brushed off the warnings.
evt-04-22-1992-gas-explosion.prompt: What triggers the disaster that follows the ignored warnings?

choices.text: A tanker truck collides with a gas station
Explosive gasoline fumes trapped in the sewer system ignite
Lightning strikes an above-ground fuel depot
A natural gas pipeline bursts at street level

evt-04-22-1992-gas-explosion.butterflyEffect: Gasoline that had leaked from a nearby Pemex pipeline into the sewer system ignited, tearing up kilometers of streets and killing over 200 people. The disaster exposed the danger of dismissing public warnings and led to tighter safety oversight of Mexico's state oil infrastructure.

evt-04-22-1993-black-british-people.scenario: It's the night of 22 April 1993 in Eltham, southeast London. Eighteen-year-old student Stephen Lawrence is waiting at a bus stop with a friend when a group of white youths attack him without warning.
evt-04-22-1993-black-british-people.prompt: What did the 1999 Macpherson Inquiry conclude about the police response?

choices.text: It cleared the police of any wrongdoing in the case
It recommended the Metropolitan Police be disbanded entirely
It found the investigation was thorough but hampered only by a lack of witnesses
It found the investigation was marred by institutional racism within the Metropolitan Police

evt-04-22-1993-black-british-people.butterflyEffect: The inquiry found the Metropolitan Police investigation was undermined by institutional racism, a verdict that reshaped British policing and led to the Race Relations Amendment Act 2000. Changes to double jeopardy law later allowed two of Lawrence's killers to be convicted in 2012, nearly two decades after the murder.

evt-04-22-1993-murder-of-stephen-lawrenc.scenario: It is April 1993 in southeast London. Eighteen-year-old Stephen Lawrence is stabbed to death by a gang of white youths as he waits for a bus in Eltham. The police investigation that follows will be scrutinized for years.
evt-04-22-1993-murder-of-stephen-lawrenc.prompt: What did the later public inquiry into the police's handling of the case conclude?

choices.text: That the case should be closed due to lack of evidence
That existing double jeopardy protections should remain untouched
That the Metropolitan Police was institutionally racist
That the investigation had been conducted flawlessly

evt-04-22-1993-murder-of-stephen-lawrenc.butterflyEffect: The 1999 Macpherson Report found the Metropolitan Police guilty of institutional racism, triggering reforms across British policing and equality law. It also helped bring about a partial revocation of the double jeopardy rule, allowing a retrial that finally convicted two of Lawrence's killers in 2012.

evt-04-22-2000-elian-gonzalez.scenario: It is before dawn on 22 April 2000 in Little Havana, Miami. You are inside the house with six-year-old Elián González when armed federal agents burst through the door to enforce a court order.
evt-04-22-2000-elian-gonzalez.prompt: What happens to Elián in the raid, and what follows?

choices.text: He is placed in foster care while the case goes to the Supreme Court
He is seized by agents and reunited with his father, who returns him to Cuba
He is granted political asylum and stays permanently with his Miami relatives
Congress intervenes and grants him instant U.S. citizenship

evt-04-22-2000-elian-gonzalez.butterflyEffect: Elián was seized and flown to reunite with his father, Juan Miguel González, who took him back to Cuba weeks later. The raid inflamed Cuban-American politics in Florida ahead of the 2000 presidential election, a race decided there by a razor-thin margin.

evt-04-22-2004-ryongchon-disaster.scenario: It is April 22, 2004, at the rail station in Ryongchon, North Korea, hours after leader Kim Jong-il's train has passed through, and workers are shunting freight cars loaded with ammonium nitrate fertilizer and fuel.
evt-04-22-2004-ryongchon-disaster.prompt: What causes the catastrophic explosion that levels the station and surrounding town?

choices.text: A bomb planted to target Kim Jong-il's train detonates late
Lightning strikes fuel tanks on the platform
A locomotive boiler explodes from overheating
A collision during shunting ignites the explosive cargo

evt-04-22-2004-ryongchon-disaster.butterflyEffect: A collision during shunting operations detonated the ammonium nitrate cargo, flattening buildings for a wide radius and killing at least 54 people. The disaster prompted a rare North Korean appeal for international humanitarian aid, briefly opening the isolated country to outside relief workers.
