evt-04-22-2005-junichiro-koizumi.scenario: It is April 22, 2005, at the Asian-African Summit in Jakarta, and Japanese Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi stands before regional leaders still wary of Japan's wartime conduct six decades earlier.
evt-04-22-2005-junichiro-koizumi.prompt: What does Koizumi do in his speech to address Japan's wartime past?

choices.text: He refuses to address Japan's wartime history
He denies that wartime atrocities occurred
He expresses deep remorse and apologizes for Japan's war record
He calls for revising history textbooks to remove war content

evt-04-22-2005-junichiro-koizumi.butterflyEffect: Koizumi expressed 'deep remorse' for the suffering Japan caused during its colonial rule and wartime aggression. Critics in China and South Korea noted it echoed earlier apologies, and tensions persisted as Koizumi continued visiting the Yasukuni Shrine, keeping the historical dispute unresolved.

evt-04-22-2013-royal-canadian-mounted-po.scenario: It's April 2013, and Canadian intelligence has been tracking two men suspected of plotting to attack a passenger train running between Toronto and New York City.
evt-04-22-2013-royal-canadian-mounted-po.prompt: What does the RCMP do as the plot nears its final stage?

choices.text: Allows the attack to proceed to gather evidence
Deports the suspects without charge
Negotiates a plea deal before making any arrests
Arrests the two suspects before they can carry out the attack

evt-04-22-2013-royal-canadian-mounted-po.butterflyEffect: The RCMP, working with the FBI and other agencies, arrested the two suspects and foiled the plot to derail a Via Rail train. The case became one of Canada's most prominent terrorism prosecutions and fueled debate over cross-border intelligence sharing.

evt-04-22-2016-paris-agreement.scenario: It is Earth Day, 22 April 2016, and world leaders gather at the United Nations in New York to sign the Paris Agreement, the product of months of negotiation outside Paris the previous December.
evt-04-22-2016-paris-agreement.prompt: What happens as leaders line up at the UN to sign the treaty that day?

choices.text: The agreement is rejected by most UN member states
Only a handful of nations agree to sign
A record number of countries sign a single treaty on its opening day
The United States refuses to attend the ceremony

evt-04-22-2016-paris-agreement.butterflyEffect: A record 175 countries signed the Paris Agreement on its opening day, an unprecedented show of unity that helped it enter into force within a year. It became the central framework for global climate action, though its binding force has since been tested by shifting commitments, including repeated US withdrawals and re-entries.

evt-04-22-2025-2025-pahalgam-attack.scenario: It is 22 April 2025 in the Baisaran Valley near Pahalgam, Kashmir. Armed militants emerge from the surrounding forest and begin separating and shooting tourists in the meadow.
evt-04-22-2025-2025-pahalgam-attack.prompt: How does the Indian government respond to the massacre in the following days?

choices.text: It opens immediate peace talks with Pakistan
It grants Kashmir full independence to end the violence
It treats the attack as a purely local law-and-order matter
It suspends the Indus Waters Treaty and downgrades relations with Pakistan

evt-04-22-2025-2025-pahalgam-attack.butterflyEffect: India accused Pakistan-based militants of orchestrating the attack, suspended the decades-old Indus Waters Treaty, expelled diplomats, and closed the main border crossing. The response sharply escalated tensions between the nuclear-armed neighbors and raised fears of broader military confrontation.

evt-04-23-1014-vikings.scenario: It is Good Friday, 23 April 1014, at Clontarf near Dublin. You serve in the army of the aging High King Brian Boru as his forces clash with a Norse-Leinster alliance.
evt-04-23-1014-vikings.prompt: What happens to Brian Boru during the battle?

choices.text: He leads the final charge personally and dies in the thick of combat
He is captured by the Vikings and later ransomed
He stays in his tent to pray and is killed by fleeing Norse warriors after the battle is won
He survives the battle and rules for another decade

evt-04-23-1014-vikings.butterflyEffect: Brian, too old to fight, prayed in his tent while his army won the field, but he was killed there by Norsemen fleeing the rout. His death fractured the unity he had built, and Ireland returned to rival kingdoms even as Viking military power on the island went into lasting decline.

evt-04-23-1016-edmund-ironside.scenario: It is April 1016 in London. King Æthelred has just died while Danish forces under Cnut hold much of England, and the city's nobles must decide who will lead the fight to keep the kingdom.
evt-04-23-1016-edmund-ironside.prompt: What did the nobles do about the succession?

choices.text: Proclaimed Edmund king to continue resisting Cnut
Submitted immediately to Cnut without a fight
Sent the royal family into exile in Normandy
Crowned a rival Saxon claimant instead of Edmund

evt-04-23-1016-edmund-ironside.butterflyEffect: Edmund was proclaimed king and fought on against Cnut, but was defeated at the Battle of Assandun that October. He agreed to divide England with Cnut, only to die weeks later, leaving Cnut as sole king and beginning Danish rule of England.

evt-04-23-1467-skanderbeg.scenario: It is April 1467 and you are inside the fortress of Krujë, where an Ottoman army has kept you under siege for ten months. Food is nearly gone, but word arrives that Skanderbeg's relief force is approaching.
evt-04-23-1467-skanderbeg.prompt: What happened when Skanderbeg's forces reached the besieged fortress?

choices.text: The defenders abandoned the fortress and fled to Venice
Skanderbeg negotiated a tribute payment instead of fighting
They broke the siege and forced the Ottoman army to retreat
The garrison surrendered before the relief force arrived

evt-04-23-1467-skanderbeg.butterflyEffect: Skanderbeg's relief force broke the siege and forced the Ottoman army to withdraw, saving Krujë's garrison. It stood as one of his final victories before his death the following year, after which sustained Ottoman conquest of Albania resumed.

evt-04-23-1685-charles-ii-of-england.scenario: It is 23 April 1685 and you stand in Westminster Abbey as James II is crowned king, the first openly Catholic monarch to take the English throne in over a century, in a country still deeply suspicious of Rome.
evt-04-23-1685-charles-ii-of-england.prompt: What followed in the years after James's coronation?

choices.text: Voluntary abdication in favor of his Protestant daughter within a year
Growing Protestant opposition that led to his overthrow in 1688
A long, uncontested reign lasting three decades
Immediate war with France over religious differences

evt-04-23-1685-charles-ii-of-england.butterflyEffect: James's Catholic faith and increasingly autocratic rule alienated Parliament and Protestant elites. Within three years he was deposed in the Glorious Revolution of 1688, replaced by William and Mary, which reshaped the balance of power between crown and Parliament for good.

evt-04-23-1891-chilean-civil-war-of-1891.scenario: It is before dawn on 23 April 1891 in Caldera Bay. You command one of President Balmaceda's small torpedo boats, facing the anchored Congressionalist ironclad Blanco Encalada, whose guns could shatter your vessel with a single hit.
evt-04-23-1891-chilean-civil-war-of-1891.prompt: How do you strike the powerful ironclad before she can respond?

choices.text: Launch torpedoes in a swift night attack while she lies at anchor
Wait for army artillery to bombard her from the shore
Challenge her to a daylight gunnery duel
Try to board her and seize control by force

evt-04-23-1891-chilean-civil-war-of-1891.butterflyEffect: The torpedo boats Almirante Lynch and Almirante Condell launched a night torpedo attack and sank the Blanco Encalada, one of history's earliest successful torpedo-boat strikes on an armored warship. The victory was a morale boost for Balmaceda's forces, but it did not reverse the war: Congress prevailed by September, and Balmaceda took his own life.

evt-04-23-1918-world-war-i.scenario: It is the night of 22-23 April 1918, and you are a sailor aboard HMS Vindictive off the Belgian coast. Your mission is to scuttle obsolete cruisers in the canal mouths at Zeebrugge and Ostend, sealing in German U-boats based there.
evt-04-23-1918-world-war-i.prompt: What was the actual outcome of the Zeebrugge and Ostend raids?

choices.text: The canal was permanently sealed, ending U-boat operations there
The blockships sank askew, leaving the canal passable again within days
The raid was aborted before the ships reached the coast
German forces captured the entire raiding party before it landed

evt-04-23-1918-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The blockships settled in the wrong position, and German engineers cleared a usable channel within days, so the raid failed strategically. Even so, Britain hailed it as a heroic success that boosted flagging wartime morale, and several participants were awarded the Victoria Cross.

evt-04-23-1920-grand-national-assembly-o.scenario: It is 23 April 1920 in Ankara. The Ottoman government in occupied Istanbul has dissolved parliament, and you are among the deputies gathering in open defiance to form a new national body.
evt-04-23-1920-grand-national-assembly-o.prompt: What did the assembly do to assert its authority over Turkey?

choices.text: Dissolved itself after a single symbolic session
Recognized the Ottoman Sultan as the country's rightful ruler
Voted to accept Allied occupation terms
Elected Mustafa Kemal as its speaker and claimed sole legislative authority

evt-04-23-1920-grand-national-assembly-o.butterflyEffect: The Grand National Assembly declared itself the sole legitimate representative of the Turkish people and elected Mustafa Kemal as its speaker. It became the political engine of the Turkish War of Independence and the direct forerunner of the Turkish Republic proclaimed in 1923.

evt-04-23-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is April 23, 1945. You are a soldier of the US Army's 90th Infantry Division advancing into Bavaria, and your unit reaches the gates of Flossenbürg concentration camp, partly abandoned by fleeing SS guards.
evt-04-23-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What do you and your fellow soldiers discover as you enter the camp?

choices.text: A camp already empty and abandoned for months
Starving survivors and evidence of mass killings, with many prisoners already sent on death marches
A fully staffed camp administration awaiting them peacefully
Only German soldiers who surrender immediately

evt-04-23-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The division found starving survivors and clear evidence of executions, including the site where resistance figures Dietrich Bonhoeffer and Wilhelm Canaris had been hanged just weeks earlier for their role in the plot against Hitler. Documentation and testimony gathered at Flossenbürg became part of the evidence later used to prosecute Nazi war crimes at Nuremberg.

evt-04-23-1971-the-rolling-stones.scenario: It's April 1971 and you've just bought the Rolling Stones' new LP, Sticky Fingers, the first release on their own label, featuring Andy Warhol's striking cover.
evt-04-23-1971-the-rolling-stones.prompt: What practical problem did Warhol's zipper cover design cause?

choices.text: The metal zipper scratched the vinyl records during shipping and storage
The cover was banned outright in several countries for indecency
The zipper jammed, making the sleeve impossible to open
Ink from the cover rubbed off onto buyers' hands

evt-04-23-1971-the-rolling-stones.butterflyEffect: The working metal zipper scratched the vinyl records during shipping and storage, forcing later pressings to be adjusted. Despite the flaw, the album topped charts on both sides of the Atlantic and its cover became one of the most iconic in rock history, while the new label gave the band full control over their output going forward.

evt-04-23-1976-ramones.scenario: It is April 1976, and you flip through record bins, coming across a stark black-and-white album cover from a scrappy New York band still mostly unknown outside CBGB.
evt-04-23-1976-ramones.prompt: What was the lasting impact of the Ramones' self-titled debut album?

choices.text: It was banned from radio play across the United States
It won the band a Grammy for Best New Artist
It topped the Billboard album chart within weeks
It became a foundational text of punk rock despite poor initial sales

evt-04-23-1976-ramones.butterflyEffect: Though a commercial disappointment on release, the album's stripped-down, fast, three-chord songs became a blueprint for punk rock worldwide. It influenced generations of bands from the Sex Pistols to Green Day, cementing the Ramones' status as pioneers of the genre.

evt-04-23-1979-death-of-blair-peach.scenario: It is 23 April 1979, and you march with thousands through Southall, London, protesting a National Front election meeting. Lines of Metropolitan Police Special Patrol Group officers face the crowd as tensions rise.
evt-04-23-1979-death-of-blair-peach.prompt: What happened during the police response to the Southall demonstration?

choices.text: The demonstration passed without any serious injuries
Peach was arrested and later cleared of all charges
Teacher Blair Peach was fatally struck, likely by an SPG officer, though no one was charged
Police instead arrested the National Front speakers for incitement

evt-04-23-1979-death-of-blair-peach.butterflyEffect: Blair Peach was struck fatally, likely by an SPG officer, and died in hospital that night. An inquest returned an open verdict and no officer was ever prosecuted, but the case fuelled sustained criticism of the Special Patrol Group, which was disbanded in 1987, and remains a touchstone in debates over policing and racism in Britain.

evt-04-23-1982-zx-spectrum.scenario: It is April 1982, and you're browsing a British electronics shop, eyeing Sinclair Research's new affordable colour home computer promising to bring programming into ordinary living rooms.
evt-04-23-1982-zx-spectrum.prompt: What made the ZX Spectrum a landmark success for Sinclair Research?

choices.text: It sold over five million units, becoming Britain's best-selling home computer
It required a separate monitor costing more than the computer itself
It was banned from export outside the United Kingdom
It flopped commercially due to its high price against rivals

evt-04-23-1982-zx-spectrum.butterflyEffect: The Spectrum's low price and colour graphics sparked a grassroots software boom, with bedroom coders across Britain writing games and selling them by mail order. It is widely credited with helping launch the UK's video game industry, whose studios still trace their roots back to it.

evt-04-23-1993-eritrea.scenario: It is April 1993, after Eritrea's thirty-year war for independence. You stand in line at a polling station in Asmara to cast your vote in the UN-supervised referendum on separating from Ethiopia.
evt-04-23-1993-eritrea.prompt: What does the referendum decide, and what follows immediately after?

choices.text: The referendum is annulled amid widespread fraud allegations
Voters opt for autonomy short of full independence
Voters overwhelmingly choose independence, and Eritrea becomes sovereign weeks later
Voters narrowly reject independence, remaining part of Ethiopia

evt-04-23-1993-eritrea.butterflyEffect: Voters chose independence by an overwhelming margin, and Eritrea formally became a sovereign state on 24 May 1993, quickly gaining international recognition. Relations with Ethiopia later soured over border disputes, erupting into the brutal Eritrean-Ethiopian War of 1998–2000.

evt-04-23-1999-nato.scenario: It is 23 April 1999, and you are a NATO planner reviewing a target list during the Kosovo air campaign. The Radio Television of Serbia headquarters in Belgrade is flagged as a legitimate target for broadcasting state propaganda.
evt-04-23-1999-nato.prompt: What happened when NATO struck the RTS headquarters in Belgrade?

choices.text: Serbian air defenses shot down the attacking aircraft
NATO called off the strike after diplomatic warnings
The building was evacuated in time with no casualties
NATO bombed the building, killing sixteen civilian staff and sparking international criticism

evt-04-23-1999-nato.butterflyEffect: The strike killed sixteen civilian technicians and journalists working the night shift, drawing condemnation from Amnesty International as a possible war crime. The bombing intensified debate over the legality of targeting media infrastructure and shaped later scrutiny of NATO's rules of engagement.

evt-04-23-2005-youtube.scenario: It is April 23, 2005, at the San Diego Zoo. YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim stands in front of the elephant enclosure, camera rolling, about to upload the very first video to the fledgling website he helped build.
evt-04-23-2005-youtube.prompt: What does Karim film to become YouTube's first-ever upload?

choices.text: A short clip of himself narrating the elephants
A music video parody he had made with friends
A slideshow of his recent vacation photos
A recorded clip from a television broadcast

evt-04-23-2005-youtube.butterflyEffect: The 19-second clip, "Me at the zoo," became the first video ever posted to YouTube. The site grew from that humble test into the world's dominant video platform, reshaping television, music, and news, and giving rise to an entire creator economy built on user-uploaded video.

evt-04-23-2010-jan-brewer.scenario: It is April 2010 and you are Governor of Arizona. A sweeping bill requiring police to check the immigration status of anyone they reasonably suspect is undocumented sits on your desk, backed by supporters and condemned by civil rights groups.
evt-04-23-2010-jan-brewer.prompt: What did Governor Jan Brewer decide to do with the bill, SB 1070?

choices.text: Put the measure to a statewide voter referendum
Vetoed it under pressure from business leaders
Sent it back to the legislature for softer language
Signed it into law

evt-04-23-2010-jan-brewer.butterflyEffect: Brewer signed SB 1070 into law, making it the toughest state-level immigration enforcement measure in the country at the time. It triggered nationwide boycotts of Arizona, a Supreme Court challenge, and became a template debated in statehouses across the US.

evt-04-23-2018-2018-toronto-van-attack.scenario: It is April 23, 2018, on Yonge Street in Toronto. Moments after a rented van has plowed through pedestrians, you are the officer who confronts the driver, who claims to have a gun and demands to be shot.
evt-04-23-2018-2018-toronto-van-attack.prompt: What does the responding officer do when the driver demands to be killed?

choices.text: Calmly talks him down and arrests him without firing
Opens fire immediately to neutralize the threat
Retreats to a safe distance and waits for backup
Uses a stun gun to subdue him from range

evt-04-23-2018-2018-toronto-van-attack.butterflyEffect: Constable Ken Lam calmly talked the driver down and arrested him without firing a shot, an act widely praised around the world as a model of restrained policing. The attacker, who cited online misogynist ideology as motivation, was later tried in a landmark case examining criminal responsibility and autism spectrum diagnoses, and the attack intensified debate over vehicle-ramming terrorism and radicalization.

evt-04-23-2024-2024-lumut-mid-air-collis.scenario: It is 23 April 2024, and you watch two Royal Malaysian Navy helicopters rehearsing a formation flypast near Lumut ahead of the navy's 90th anniversary parade.
evt-04-23-2024-2024-lumut-mid-air-collis.prompt: What did investigators determine caused the fatal collision between the two helicopters?

choices.text: A mechanical failure in one helicopter's rotor system
A collision with an unauthorized civilian aircraft
Poor weather conditions obscuring visibility
Pilot error during the formation manoeuvre

evt-04-23-2024-2024-lumut-mid-air-collis.butterflyEffect: The collision killed all ten personnel aboard the AW139 and Fennec helicopters. In its aftermath, the Royal Malaysian Navy suspended flypast rehearsals and launched a review of formation flying protocols to prevent similar accidents at future ceremonial events.

evt-04-24-1704-john-campbell-editor.scenario: You are Boston's postmaster in April 1704, about to release the first issue of a regular newspaper for the colonies. You know the royal governor can shut you down if your content displeases him.
evt-04-24-1704-john-campbell-editor.prompt: What editorial approach did Campbell take to keep his paper running under colonial authority?

choices.text: Print only paid advertisements with no news content
Fill it mostly with approved foreign news reprinted from London papers
Focus entirely on local Boston scandals and gossip
Publish anonymous attacks on the royal governor

evt-04-24-1704-john-campbell-editor.butterflyEffect: Campbell printed his News-Letter "published by authority," filling it mainly with reprinted London and European news rather than risky local commentary, which kept it in the governor's good graces. This cautious, authority-sanctioned model set the template colonial papers followed for decades, until bolder printers like Benjamin Franklin's brother James began pushing back against such controls.

evt-04-24-1800-library-of-congress.scenario: It is April 1800, and you are a congressman debating how the federal government, newly relocated to Washington, should equip itself with the books and reference materials it needs to legislate.
evt-04-24-1800-library-of-congress.prompt: What does Congress decide to do to establish a working library for itself?

choices.text: Postpone the matter until a permanent capital building is finished
Rely on private donations from wealthy citizens to stock a reading room
Borrow books indefinitely from state legislatures as needed
Appropriate $5,000 to purchase an initial collection of books for Congress's use

evt-04-24-1800-library-of-congress.butterflyEffect: Congress approved an act appropriating $5,000 to purchase books, housing the first collection inside the new Capitol building. After the British burned that collection in 1814, Congress bought Thomas Jefferson's personal library to rebuild it, permanently shaping the institution into the vast research library it is today.

evt-04-24-1837-1837-surat-fire.scenario: It is April 1837, and you are a cloth merchant in Surat. Smoke is rising over the crowded wooden bazaar near your shop, and the wind is picking up fast.
evt-04-24-1837-1837-surat-fire.prompt: What is the wisest immediate action as the fire spreads through the tightly packed city?

choices.text: Stay and try to protect your shop's stock with wet cloth
Flee immediately toward open ground away from the densely built quarters
Gather neighbors to form a bucket brigade using well water
Move goods into a nearby stone temple believed to be fireproof

evt-04-24-1837-1837-surat-fire.butterflyEffect: The blaze went on to destroy roughly three-quarters of Surat, killing over 500 people and levelling nearly 9,700 houses. In the aftermath, British administrators pushed through wider streets and stricter building codes, permanently reshaping the city's crowded medieval layout.

evt-04-24-1913-woolworth-building.scenario: It is the evening of 24 April 1913, and you are among the guests gathered at the base of the new Woolworth Building in Lower Manhattan, waiting for the ceremony that will mark its official opening.
evt-04-24-1913-woolworth-building.prompt: What happens when the building is switched on for the first time that night?

choices.text: President Wilson presses a button in Washington to light the entire building at once
Frank Woolworth personally throws a switch inside the lobby
A fireworks display over the Hudson River signals the opening
The building's lights are turned on gradually floor by floor over the evening

evt-04-24-1913-woolworth-building.butterflyEffect: President Woodrow Wilson, from the White House in Washington, pressed a button that simultaneously lit all 80,000 lightbulbs in the building. The Woolworth Building became the world's tallest building, a title it held until 1929, and its Gothic "Cathedral of Commerce" style influenced skyscraper design for a generation.

evt-04-24-1914-franck-hertz-experiment.scenario: It's April 1914, and you're recording the current through a tube of mercury vapor while slowly raising the voltage accelerating electrons through it. Instead of rising smoothly, the current climbs then abruptly drops at regular intervals of about 4.9 volts.
evt-04-24-1914-franck-hertz-experiment.prompt: What does this repeating pattern reveal about mercury atoms?

choices.text: Atoms can only absorb energy in fixed, discrete quantities
The mercury vapor is contaminated with impurities
The electrons are simply losing energy to friction in the tube
Atoms can absorb energy in any continuous amount

evt-04-24-1914-franck-hertz-experiment.butterflyEffect: Franck and Hertz had confirmed that atoms absorb energy only in fixed discrete amounts, offering the first direct experimental proof of the quantum energy levels Bohr's model had predicted. The pair won the 1925 Nobel Prize in Physics, and the effect became a standard classroom demonstration of quantum mechanics.

evt-04-24-1915-armenian-genocide.scenario: It is 24 April 1915 in Constantinople, and you are an Armenian community leader hearing that Ottoman authorities have begun rounding up prominent Armenian intellectuals, clergy, and professionals across the city.
evt-04-24-1915-armenian-genocide.prompt: What follows this wave of arrests in the following months?

choices.text: The arrests remain an isolated incident with no further action
The Ottoman government reverses the policy within weeks
The intellectuals are released after international protest
The arrests mark the beginning of mass deportations and killings across the empire

evt-04-24-1915-armenian-genocide.butterflyEffect: Most of those arrested that night were deported or killed, an act that marked the start of the systematic destruction of the Armenian population through massacre and forced death marches. April 24 is now marked worldwide as Armenian Genocide Remembrance Day, and the events remain a defining case study in the study of genocide and its recognition by nations today.

evt-04-24-1918-world-war-i.scenario: It is dawn on 24 April 1918 near Villers-Bretonneux, and you crew a British Mark IV tank when German A7V tanks emerge from the morning mist directly ahead.
evt-04-24-1918-world-war-i.prompt: What historic first is about to happen in this clash?

choices.text: The first tank-versus-tank battle in military history
The first aerial bombing raid on a European city
The first large-scale use of poison gas in the war
The first successful amphibious tank landing

evt-04-24-1918-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: This engagement was the first tank-versus-tank battle in history, a preview of the armored warfare that would dominate later 20th-century conflicts. Australian infantry recaptured the town itself in a daring night counterattack shortly after.

evt-04-24-1922-imperial-wireless-chain.scenario: You are a telegraph engineer in April 1922, present as the beam finally links Leafield in Oxfordshire to Cairo, the first working section of a chain long promised to bind the British Empire together by wireless.
evt-04-24-1922-imperial-wireless-chain.prompt: What was this Imperial Wireless Chain built to do?

choices.text: Transmit early television pictures between imperial capitals
Carry high-speed Morse code traffic linking Britain's colonies and dominions
Broadcast entertainment radio programs to colonial settlers
Replace ocean telegraph cables with floating radio buoys

evt-04-24-1922-imperial-wireless-chain.butterflyEffect: The Leafield–Cairo link was the first section of a planned network of long-range radiotelegraph stations meant to connect the British Empire independently of undersea cables. The chain grew slowly, with the final Australia–Canada link not opening until 1928, and it was soon overtaken by newer shortwave technology.

evt-04-24-1932-walking.scenario: You join roughly 400 ramblers on 24 April 1932, marching onto the private grouse moors of Kinder Scout in the Peak District in defiance of gamekeepers blocking the traditional footpaths.
evt-04-24-1932-walking.prompt: What long-term change did this mass trespass help set in motion?

choices.text: The immediate abolition of private land ownership across England
A royal decree opening all moorland to public hunting
A long campaign that eventually led to Britain's 'right to roam' access laws
The founding of the National Trust that same year

evt-04-24-1932-walking.butterflyEffect: Organizer Benny Rothman and several others were arrested and jailed, but the publicity galvanized Britain's access-to-countryside movement. Decades later it contributed to the 1949 National Parks Act and eventually the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000, which established a legal right to roam.

evt-04-24-1933-nazi-germany.scenario: In April 1933, you work at the Watch Tower Society's German branch office in Magdeburg when Nazi police arrive, seize the presses, and ban the literature of Jehovah's Witnesses nationwide.
evt-04-24-1933-nazi-germany.prompt: What followed for Jehovah's Witnesses in Germany over the next decade?

choices.text: The movement dissolved entirely and vanished from Germany
Many refused to recant and were imprisoned in concentration camps for their faith
The ban was quietly reversed within a year due to public pressure
Jehovah's Witnesses were granted special legal recognition as an official church

evt-04-24-1933-nazi-germany.butterflyEffect: Thousands of Jehovah's Witnesses refused to renounce their faith, salute Hitler, or serve in the military, and were imprisoned in concentration camps, where many died. They became one of the first religious groups systematically targeted by the Nazi state, years before the mass persecutions of the Holocaust intensified.

evt-04-24-1965-cold-war.scenario: It's late April 1965, and you're briefing President Lyndon Johnson on the chaos in Santo Domingo, where a military coup has toppled the government and rival factions battle in the streets. Washington fears Communists could seize control, as in Cuba.
evt-04-24-1965-cold-war.prompt: What does the Johnson administration decide to do?

choices.text: Quietly supply arms only to the anti-Communist faction
Send U.S. Marines and airborne troops into the Dominican Republic
Impose a naval blockade of the island
Refer the crisis to the United Nations Security Council

evt-04-24-1965-cold-war.butterflyEffect: Johnson ordered over 20,000 U.S. troops into the Dominican Republic in Operation Power Pack, the largest U.S. military intervention in Latin America since the 1920s. The move drew accusations of imperialism across the region and set a precedent for later Cold War interventions justified by fear of "another Cuba."

evt-04-24-1990-hubble-space-telescope.scenario: It's April 24, 1990, and you're aboard Space Shuttle Discovery, about to release NASA's most expensive telescope yet after years of delay and the Challenger tragedy. The world is waiting for the sharpest images of the cosmos ever taken.
evt-04-24-1990-hubble-space-telescope.prompt: What happens when Hubble sends back its first images from orbit?

choices.text: Dust contamination ruins the optics during deployment
Ground control loses contact with the telescope entirely
The images come back blurry because of a flawed mirror
The images are sharper than any ground telescope has ever produced

evt-04-24-1990-hubble-space-telescope.butterflyEffect: The primary mirror had been ground to the wrong shape, causing spherical aberration that blurred images and embarrassed NASA. In 1993 the STS-61 servicing mission installed corrective optics (COSTAR), transforming Hubble into the icon of modern astronomy it became known as.

evt-04-24-1993-provisional-irish-republi.scenario: It's Saturday morning, April 24, 1993, in the City of London. Police receive a coded warning about a bomb near Bishopsgate, in the heart of the financial district, just minutes before a truck packed with explosives detonates.
evt-04-24-1993-provisional-irish-republi.prompt: What is the immediate consequence of the Bishopsgate bombing?

choices.text: Only minor damage occurs thanks to the early warning
The explosion is contained within an empty warehouse
The bomb is defused before it can detonate
One person is killed and the blast causes catastrophic damage to nearby buildings

evt-04-24-1993-provisional-irish-republi.butterflyEffect: The blast killed photographer Ed Henty and caused roughly £350 million in damage, making it one of the costliest bombings on British soil. It pushed insurers to create dedicated terrorism cover, accelerated the City's "Ring of Steel" security cordon, and encouraged firms to relocate offices to the developing Canary Wharf district.

evt-04-24-2005-cardinal-catholic-church.scenario: You stand in St Peter's Square on 24 April 2005, watching as Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger, elected only days before, is formally inaugurated as pope before the world's cameras.
evt-04-24-2005-cardinal-catholic-church.prompt: What papal name does he take upon his inauguration?

choices.text: Pope Gregory XVII
Pope Benedict XVI
Pope John Paul III
Pope Pius XIII

evt-04-24-2005-cardinal-catholic-church.butterflyEffect: Ratzinger became Pope Benedict XVI, a former doctrinal enforcer known for theological conservatism. In 2013 he became the first pope in centuries to resign rather than die in office, an act that paved the way for his successor Francis and set a modern precedent for papal resignation.

evt-04-24-2006-2006-dahab-bombings.scenario: It is the evening of 24 April 2006, and Dahab's seafront promenade is crowded with tourists and Egyptian families marking the Sham el-Nessim holiday. Within minutes, three bombs tear through the crowded waterfront.
evt-04-24-2006-2006-dahab-bombings.prompt: Which Sinai-based militant group did Egyptian investigators link to the Dahab bombings?

choices.text: Core al-Qaeda operatives sent from Afghanistan
The Muslim Brotherhood's youth wing
A Sinai Bedouin group linked to earlier Taba and Sharm el-Sheikh attacks
The Palestinian militant faction Hamas

evt-04-24-2006-2006-dahab-bombings.butterflyEffect: Egyptian authorities blamed a Sinai Bedouin militant network already tied to the 2004 Taba and 2005 Sharm el-Sheikh attacks. The bombings triggered a heavy security crackdown across the Sinai Peninsula, including mass arrests, which deepened long-running tensions between the state and local Bedouin communities and fed grievances that resurfaced in later Sinai insurgencies.

evt-04-24-2013-savar-upazila.scenario: It is the morning of 24 April 2013, and you are a garment worker in Savar, near Dhaka, staring at deep cracks that appeared in the Rana Plaza building's walls the day before. Factory managers are telling everyone to report for their shift as usual.
evt-04-24-2013-savar-upazila.prompt: What should workers and managers have done given the visible structural damage?

choices.text: Continue working but keep exits propped open
Ask for a temporary bonus in exchange for continuing to work
Evacuate and refuse to enter the building until engineers certified it safe
Work only on the ground floor to reduce risk

evt-04-24-2013-savar-upazila.butterflyEffect: Workers were ordered back inside despite the cracks, and the eight-story building collapsed hours later, killing over 1,100 people in the deadliest garment-factory disaster in history. The catastrophe triggered international outrage and led to the Bangladesh Accord on Fire and Building Safety, forcing major Western retailers to fund safety inspections across the industry.

evt-04-24-2013-rana-plaza-collapse.scenario: It's early morning on April 24, 2013, in Savar, Bangladesh. Cracks appeared in Rana Plaza's walls the day before and engineers warned the building was unsafe, but garment factory managers order thousands of workers back inside to meet export deadlines.
evt-04-24-2013-rana-plaza-collapse.prompt: What happens after the workers are ordered back to their stations?

choices.text: Government inspectors arrive and shut the factories down first
Emergency reinforcements are installed overnight and the building holds
The workers refuse and the shift is called off
The building collapses minutes into the workday

evt-04-24-2013-rana-plaza-collapse.butterflyEffect: The nine-story building collapsed minutes into the shift, killing 1,134 people and injuring roughly 2,500 in the deadliest garment-factory disaster in history. The catastrophe forced international retailers to sign the Bangladesh Accord on Fire and Building Safety, reshaping labor safety standards across the global garment industry.

evt-04-25-775-abbasid-caliphate.scenario: It is 775 near Bagrevand, and you stand with the Mamikonian and allied Armenian nakharars in revolt against Abbasid rule, your forces vastly outnumbered by the caliphal army under Amir ibn Isma'il.
evt-04-25-775-abbasid-caliphate.prompt: What follows for Armenian noble power after the battle?

choices.text: The Armenian nobility secures full autonomy under a new treaty
The Mamikonian dynasty is crushed, opening the way for Bagratuni ascendancy
The Armenian princes force a full Abbasid withdrawal from the region
The Byzantine Empire seizes the region amid the chaos

evt-04-25-775-abbasid-caliphate.butterflyEffect: The crushing Abbasid victory at Bagrevand effectively destroyed the centuries-old Mamikonian dynasty's dominance in Armenia. Into the vacuum stepped the Bagratuni family, who within a century would found the medieval Kingdom of Armenia, reshaping the region's noble order for generations.

evt-04-25-799-pope-leo-iii.scenario: It is 25 April 799 during the St Mark's Day procession through Rome. Armed men loyal to your late predecessor's family suddenly drag you from your horse, intent on blinding you and cutting out your tongue to disqualify you from office.
evt-04-25-799-pope-leo-iii.prompt: To survive and reclaim your authority, where should you flee for protection?

choices.text: To Constantinople, seeking Byzantine protection
Submit quietly to the conspirators' demands
To Charlemagne's court in the Frankish kingdom
Resign the papacy at once to end the crisis

evt-04-25-799-pope-leo-iii.butterflyEffect: Leo escaped and sought refuge with Charlemagne, who restored him to Rome after investigating the attack. The episode deepened the alliance between papacy and Frankish crown, culminating in Leo crowning Charlemagne Holy Roman Emperor in December 800.

evt-04-25-1644-transition-from-ming-to-q.scenario: It's April 25, 1644, and you serve in the Ming palace guard in Beijing as rebel forces under Li Zicheng breach the city walls. The Chongzhen Emperor climbs Jingshan, the hill behind the Forbidden City, with only a handful of loyal attendants.
evt-04-25-1644-transition-from-ming-to-q.prompt: What does the last Ming emperor do as the rebels close in?

choices.text: He surrenders to Li Zicheng in exchange for his life
He flees south to rally loyalist forces in Nanjing
He appeals to Manchu leader Nurhaci for rescue
He hangs himself on Coal Hill rather than be captured

evt-04-25-1644-transition-from-ming-to-q.butterflyEffect: Chongzhen hanged himself on Coal Hill, ending nearly three centuries of Ming rule. Li Zicheng's rebel Shun dynasty proved short-lived, as Manchu forces soon swept in and founded the Qing dynasty, which would govern China until 1912.

evt-04-25-1792-claude-joseph-rouget-de-l.scenario: It's the night of 25 April 1792 in Strasbourg. France has just declared war on Austria, and the mayor has asked you, an army engineer known for writing verse, to compose a song to rally the volunteers marching to the front.
evt-04-25-1792-claude-joseph-rouget-de-l.prompt: What did Rouget de Lisle originally title this new marching song?

choices.text: Le Chant du Départ
Chant de guerre pour l'Armée du Rhin (War Song for the Army of the Rhine)
Ça Ira
La Marseillaise

evt-04-25-1792-claude-joseph-rouget-de-l.butterflyEffect: The song, carried to Paris by volunteers from Marseille, became known as La Marseillaise and was declared France's national anthem in 1795. Banned under Napoleon and the Bourbon Restoration, it was permanently restored in 1879 and became a global template for revolutionary and national anthems.

evt-04-25-1915-world-war-i.scenario: It is dawn, 25 April 1915, and your landing boat grounds not on the open beach you were briefed on, but beneath steep cliffs and ravines far north of the intended spot on the Gallipoli Peninsula.
evt-04-25-1915-world-war-i.prompt: What do the ANZAC troops do after landing in the wrong place under fire?

choices.text: Hold position on the sand and wait for naval bombardment
Retreat to the boats and search for the intended beach
Scramble up the cliffs and dig in on the high ground
Attempt to signal a truce with Ottoman defenders

evt-04-25-1915-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The troops scrambled up the ravines and dug in on the high ground, beginning a stalemate that would last for months and cost tens of thousands of lives on both sides. The Ottoman defense, led by Mustafa Kemal, helped launch his career toward becoming Atatürk, founder of the modern Turkish republic.

evt-04-25-1916-irish-war-news.scenario: It's 25 April 1916, the second day of the Easter Rising, and you're inside the rebel-held General Post Office in Dublin, where the Gaelic Press has been commandeered to spread word of the uprising.
evt-04-25-1916-irish-war-news.prompt: What do the rebel leaders decide to publish from the captured press?

choices.text: A bulletin, Irish War News, reporting the rising's opening hours
A satirical pamphlet mocking British rule
An open letter proposing negotiations with the Crown
A formal notice of surrender to the British authorities

evt-04-25-1916-irish-war-news.butterflyEffect: The bulletin, Irish War News, reported the rising's first 24 hours and became only the second printed document produced by the rebellion's leadership, alongside the Proclamation of the Irish Republic. A single further issue would not appear until eight years later, to mark the rising's anniversary.

evt-04-25-1920-san-remo-conference.scenario: You are a diplomat at Castle Devachan in Sanremo on 25 April 1920, where the Allied Supreme Council is dividing up the former Ottoman territories of the Middle East into League of Nations mandates.
evt-04-25-1920-san-remo-conference.prompt: Which power is awarded the mandate over Palestine, incorporating the Balfour Declaration?

choices.text: Britain
Italy
The United States
France

evt-04-25-1920-san-remo-conference.butterflyEffect: Britain received the Palestine mandate, France took Syria and Lebanon, and Britain also secured Mesopotamia (Iraq). Enshrining the Balfour Declaration in an international mandate gave legal weight to Zionist settlement claims, while the arbitrarily drawn borders of Syria, Iraq, and Palestine shaped decades of Middle Eastern conflict.

evt-04-25-1946-naperville-train-disaster.scenario: It's April 25, 1946, near Naperville, Illinois. The Advance Flyer has stopped without warning on the main line to check its running gear, and the Exposition Flyer is closing in on the same track at 80 mph.
evt-04-25-1946-naperville-train-disaster.prompt: What lasting change did this disaster bring to U.S. passenger railroading?

choices.text: Federal government takeover of all rail lines
Mandatory two-engineer crews on every train
A ban on unscheduled stops for mechanical checks
A nationwide 79 mph speed limit for passenger trains

evt-04-25-1946-naperville-train-disaster.butterflyEffect: The collision killed 45 people and injured about 125, exposing the danger of high-speed trains sharing track without adequate protection for stopped trains. It became a landmark case for rail safety, and it is a major reason most U.S. passenger trains still observe a 79 mph speed limit today.

evt-04-25-1960-united-states-navy.scenario: You are Captain Edward L. Beach Jr., commanding the nuclear submarine USS Triton on a secret submerged voyage around the globe, when a young sailor collapses with what looks like a ruptured appendix.
evt-04-25-1960-united-states-navy.prompt: What do you do to save the sailor without abandoning the mission?

choices.text: Surface briefly near a nearby Navy vessel to transfer the sailor, then resume submerged
Radio for a helicopter to winch the sailor off without surfacing
Abort the circumnavigation and head directly to the nearest port
Refuse to surface and treat the sailor with the ship's medic alone

evt-04-25-1960-united-states-navy.butterflyEffect: Beach surfaced briefly near a Navy cruiser off South America to transfer the ailing seaman, the only interruption in an otherwise fully submerged 60-day voyage. The Navy still credited Triton with the first submerged circumnavigation of the globe, a Cold War showcase of nuclear submarine endurance that echoed Magellan's original route.

evt-04-25-1974-carnation-revolution.scenario: It is 25 April 1974, and you are a young conscript soldier stationed with your unit near a Lisbon radio station as the coup unfolds. A restaurant worker pushes through the crowd and holds out a red carnation toward your rifle.
evt-04-25-1974-carnation-revolution.prompt: What do you do as the civilian offers the flower for your gun barrel?

choices.text: Arrest the civilian for interfering with a military operation
Fire a warning shot to disperse the civilians
Retreat immediately back to the barracks
Accept the carnation and hold your fire, letting the crowd pass

evt-04-25-1974-carnation-revolution.butterflyEffect: Soldiers across Lisbon accepted the carnations and refused to fire on the crowds, and civilians began slipping flowers into rifle muzzles and uniforms throughout the day. The nearly bloodless coup became known as the Carnation Revolution, toppling the Estado Novo dictatorship and triggering Portugal's rapid transition to democracy and decolonization of its African territories.

evt-04-25-1986-mswati-iii.scenario: It is April 1986 at the royal kraal in Swaziland, and you sit among the councillors choosing the nation's next king after years of regency following King Sobhuza II's death.
evt-04-25-1986-mswati-iii.prompt: Who ascends the throne, and what does his reign become?

choices.text: Prince Makhosetive is crowned Mswati III, later becoming Africa's last absolute monarch
Prince Sozisa Dlamini is crowned king in his place
Queen Regent Ntombi is confirmed as permanent monarch instead
The Liqoqo council abolishes the monarchy in favor of a republic

evt-04-25-1986-mswati-iii.butterflyEffect: At just eighteen, Prince Makhosetive was crowned Mswati III, then the world's youngest reigning head of state. He has ruled for decades as an absolute monarch over Eswatini (renamed from Swaziland in 2018), resisting calls for democratic reform and remaining one of the last true absolute monarchs on Earth.

evt-04-25-1990-violeta-chamorro.scenario: It is April 25, 1990, in Managua. Violeta Chamorro has just been sworn in as president after her UNO coalition defeated Daniel Ortega's Sandinistas at the ballot box, ending a decade of civil war and US-backed Contra fighting.
evt-04-25-1990-violeta-chamorro.prompt: What does her incoming government do to bring the civil war to an end?

choices.text: Exile Daniel Ortega and ban the Sandinista party
Negotiate a peace accord and demobilize the Contra rebels
Nationalize all private landholdings immediately
Continue military operations against the Sandinista army

evt-04-25-1990-violeta-chamorro.butterflyEffect: Chamorro negotiated the demobilization of the Contra rebels while keeping much of the Sandinista army intact under Humberto Ortega, a delicate balancing act that ended the fighting. Her presidency also saw the lifting of the US trade embargo and a painful transition toward a market economy.

evt-04-25-2005-obelisk-of-axum.scenario: It is April 2005, and you stand in the square at Axum as the final section of the ancient obelisk, looted by Italian troops under Mussolini in 1937, is lowered from a cargo plane onto Ethiopian soil after decades of diplomatic pressure.
evt-04-25-2005-obelisk-of-axum.prompt: What happens next to restore the stele to its original site?

choices.text: The pieces are stored indefinitely in an Addis Ababa warehouse
UNESCO funds a lengthy reconstruction, formally unveiling it in 2008
It is immediately re-erected within days using its original base
The government auctions the fragments to pay for other restoration work

evt-04-25-2005-obelisk-of-axum.butterflyEffect: The three-shipment return was hailed as a landmark act of cultural restitution, but disputes over funding delayed reassembly for years. UNESCO and Ethiopian engineers finally completed re-erection of the 1,700-year-old stele, unveiling it at its original site in 2008, sixty-eight years after it was taken.

evt-04-25-2007-death-and-state-funeral-o.scenario: You stand outside Christ the Saviour Cathedral in Moscow on 25 April 2007, watching Russia give its first president a state funeral blessed by the Orthodox Church, the first such church rite for a head of state in over a century.
evt-04-25-2007-death-and-state-funeral-o.prompt: Where does the funeral procession take Boris Yeltsin's body for burial?

choices.text: Novodevichy Cemetery, Moscow
A family plot in Yekaterinburg
The Kremlin Wall Necropolis
Cremation with ashes scattered over the Volga

evt-04-25-2007-death-and-state-funeral-o.butterflyEffect: Yeltsin was interred at Novodevichy Cemetery in Moscow, resting place of many notable Russians, rather than the Kremlin Wall reserved for Soviet leaders. The church-sanctioned ceremony, attended by President Putin and foreign dignitaries, symbolized the state's reconciliation with the Orthodox Church after Soviet-era secularism.

evt-04-25-2014-flint-water-crisis.scenario: It is April 25, 2014, in Flint, Michigan. City officials, under a state-appointed emergency manager trying to cut costs, are switching the municipal water supply away from Detroit's system.
evt-04-25-2014-flint-water-crisis.prompt: What source do officials switch Flint's water supply to, without adding proper corrosion controls?

choices.text: Bottled water trucked in from outside the county
The Flint River
A newly drilled municipal well system
Lake Huron via a new pipeline

evt-04-25-2014-flint-water-crisis.butterflyEffect: Flint began drawing water from the Flint River without the anti-corrosion treatment needed for its aging pipes, causing lead to leach into the water supply and poisoning thousands of children. The crisis triggered a federal emergency declaration, criminal charges against several officials, and became a national symbol of environmental injustice and infrastructure neglect.

evt-04-25-2015-april-2015-nepal-earthqua.scenario: It is 25 April 2015, hours after a massive earthquake struck central Nepal. You are coordinating relief flights into Kathmandu as reports come in of villages cut off high in the Himalayan foothills.
evt-04-25-2015-april-2015-nepal-earthqua.prompt: What obstacle most hampered getting aid to remote mountain communities in the days after the quake?

choices.text: Landslides and destroyed roads left many villages accessible only by air
A nationwide fuel shortage grounded every aircraft immediately
A diplomatic dispute delayed all foreign aid from entering the country
A tsunami had cut off the entire coastal region

evt-04-25-2015-april-2015-nepal-earthqua.butterflyEffect: Landslides and destroyed mountain roads left many villages reachable only by helicopter, slowing aid for days in the hardest-hit rural districts. The disaster also triggered a deadly avalanche on Mount Everest, and in its aftermath Nepal faced years of slow, politically contested reconstruction while pushing through stricter building codes.

evt-04-26-1478-pazzi-conspiracy.scenario: It is Easter Sunday, 26 April 1478, inside Florence's cathedral. As the priest raises the host during Mass, armed men lunge at you and your brother Giuliano, daggers drawn, in a plot to end Medici rule.
evt-04-26-1478-pazzi-conspiracy.prompt: What should Lorenzo do in the instant the attack begins?

choices.text: Flee toward the sacristy and bar the doors
Call on the congregation to seize the conspirators
Surrender and negotiate for his brother's safety
Draw a weapon and fight the attackers in the open nave

evt-04-26-1478-pazzi-conspiracy.butterflyEffect: Giuliano was stabbed to death at the altar, but Lorenzo fled into the sacristy and survived. The failed plot triggered brutal Medici reprisals, including the hanging of Archbishop Salviati from the walls of the Palazzo Vecchio, and left Lorenzo's grip on Florence stronger than before.

evt-04-26-1803-l-aigle-meteorite.scenario: It is spring 1803, and the French Academy of Sciences has sent you, physicist Jean-Baptiste Biot, to investigate reports that thousands of stone fragments rained down over L'Aigle, Normandy, during a meteor shower.
evt-04-26-1803-l-aigle-meteorite.prompt: What did your investigation conclude about the stones, and what did that achieve?

choices.text: Attributed the stones to volcanic ejecta from a nearby eruption
Confirmed the stones fell from the sky, of extraterrestrial origin
Concluded a lightning strike had shattered a local quarry
Dismissed the reports as exaggerated local superstition

evt-04-26-1803-l-aigle-meteorite.butterflyEffect: Biot's meticulous report convinced the skeptical scientific establishment that the stones had fallen from the sky, vindicating Ernst Chladni's earlier theory of extraterrestrial origin. The L'Aigle fall ended meteorites' dismissal as folk superstition and helped establish meteoritics as a legitimate field of astronomical study.

evt-04-26-1865-united-states-army.scenario: It is before dawn on 26 April 1865 at a Virginia tobacco barn. You are one of the soldiers who have cornered John Wilkes Booth, and your orders are to take him alive if possible, but he refuses to come out and the barn is now burning.
evt-04-26-1865-united-states-army.prompt: What happened as Booth stood inside the burning barn refusing to surrender?

choices.text: The soldiers waited him out and took him alive
A soldier shot Booth through the barn wall
Booth surrendered peacefully once the flames spread
Booth escaped through a rear door under cover of smoke

evt-04-26-1865-united-states-army.butterflyEffect: Sergeant Boston Corbett fired through the barn slats and mortally wounded Booth, who died a few hours later still refusing to confess. Because he was never captured alive, no trial ever tested the full scope of the conspiracy, leaving lasting questions about who else was involved in Lincoln's assassination.

evt-04-26-1915-world-war-i.scenario: It is late April 1915 in London. Italian negotiators sit across from British, French and Russian diplomats, weighing a secret offer to abandon their old alliance with Austria-Hungary and Germany.
evt-04-26-1915-world-war-i.prompt: What did Italy do in response to the Allies' secret territorial promises?

choices.text: Honor the Triple Alliance and fight alongside Germany and Austria-Hungary
Sign the secret treaty and join the Allies for promised territory
Demand a separate peace conference before choosing sides
Remain neutral for the rest of the war

evt-04-26-1915-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Italy signed the Treaty of London and entered the war on the Allied side a month later, drawn by promises of Trieste, South Tyrol, Istria and Dalmatia. Many of these promises were only partly honored at Versailles, feeding Italian resentment over a 'mutilated victory' that fascist propaganda later exploited.

evt-04-26-1933-gestapo.scenario: It is April 1933 in Prussia. As Hermann Göring's decree takes effect, you are among the officials tasked with organizing a new secret state police force answerable directly to the Nazi leadership.
evt-04-26-1933-gestapo.prompt: What is this new Gestapo initially built to do?

choices.text: Regulate traffic and public order at Nazi Party rallies
Oversee customs and border enforcement
Investigate ordinary street crime in major German cities
Suppress political opponents like communists and socialists

evt-04-26-1933-gestapo.butterflyEffect: The Gestapo was created to hunt down communists, socialists, and other political opponents of the new regime, operating outside normal judicial oversight. It was later absorbed into Heinrich Himmler's SS apparatus under Reinhard Heydrich, becoming a central instrument of surveillance, terror, and the machinery of the Holocaust.

evt-04-26-1937-spanish-civil-war.scenario: It is market day, 26 April 1937, in the Basque town of Guernica, and the drone of Condor Legion bombers grows louder over the crowded streets below.
evt-04-26-1937-spanish-civil-war.prompt: How did the bombing of Guernica affect international opinion on the war?

choices.text: It convinced other nations to formally intervene militarily
It led to an immediate ceasefire between Nationalists and Republicans
It went almost unnoticed outside Spain at the time
It galvanized international condemnation and became a symbol of civilian bombing's horrors

evt-04-26-1937-spanish-civil-war.butterflyEffect: News of the bombing, and the devastation of a civilian town far from the front lines, shocked the world and became a symbol of the horrors of aerial warfare against civilians. Pablo Picasso's painting 'Guernica,' created that same year, turned the attack into a lasting anti-war icon recognized long after the Spanish Civil War ended.

evt-04-26-1964-tanganyika-1961-1964.scenario: It is 26 April 1964 in Dar es Salaam. You stand beside President Julius Nyerere as he signs the Act of Union joining Tanganyika with the People's Republic of Zanzibar.
evt-04-26-1964-tanganyika-1961-1964.prompt: What happened to the newly merged state within the following year?

choices.text: Zanzibar withdrew from the union within months
It was renamed the United Republic of Tanzania
The union was dissolved by a military coup
It kept the name Tanganyika permanently

evt-04-26-1964-tanganyika-1961-1964.butterflyEffect: The union was first named the United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, but within a year it was renamed the United Republic of Tanzania, blending both territories' names into one. Nyerere became its first president, and the union has endured as one of Africa's few lasting post-independence mergers.

evt-04-26-1986-chernobyl-disaster.scenario: It is late April 1986 near Pripyat. Reactor 4 has just exploded during a botched safety test, and Soviet officials are deciding how much of the disaster to reveal to the public and the world.
evt-04-26-1986-chernobyl-disaster.prompt: What actually happened with the official response in the days after the explosion?

choices.text: The government evacuated Pripyat and informed the world within hours
Authorities stayed silent until Sweden detected the radiation two days later
Officials held the scheduled May Day parade nearby with no changes at all
The reactor was quickly repaired and the plant resumed normal operation

evt-04-26-1986-chernobyl-disaster.butterflyEffect: Soviet authorities stayed silent until elevated radiation was detected in Sweden two days later, forcing a belated admission. The cover-up attempt badly damaged public trust in Soviet institutions and fed the glasnost-era push for transparency that helped hasten the USSR's collapse.

evt-04-26-1994-nagoya-airfield.scenario: It is the night of 26 April 1994. You are the first officer of a China Airlines Airbus approaching Nagoya, and the autopilot has quietly slipped into go-around mode even as the captain tries to force the nose down for landing.
evt-04-26-1994-nagoya-airfield.prompt: What should the crew do as the aircraft fights the pilot's control inputs on final approach?

choices.text: Keep pushing the control column forward against the autopilot
Fully disengage the autopilot and hand-fly the recovery
Radio the tower to request a new runway assignment
Increase flap setting to compensate for the pitch-up

evt-04-26-1994-nagoya-airfield.butterflyEffect: The crew never fully disengaged the conflicting autopilot mode, and the aircraft pitched up, stalled and crashed short of the runway, killing 264 people. The disaster became a landmark case study in automation confusion, prompting airlines worldwide to retrain pilots on recognizing and overriding autopilot mode conflicts.

evt-04-26-1994-china-airlines-flight-140.scenario: It is the night of 26 April 1994 over Nagoya. In the cockpit of your Airbus A300, the autopilot has unexpectedly entered go-around mode as you descend, and the aircraft is fighting your control inputs on final approach.
evt-04-26-1994-china-airlines-flight-140.prompt: What should the crew do the moment they realize the autopilot is working against them?

choices.text: Radio the tower and request a new approach clearance
Increase back pressure on the controls to overpower the autopilot
Switch to a different autopilot mode without disconnecting it
Immediately disconnect the autopilot completely and fly manually

evt-04-26-1994-china-airlines-flight-140.butterflyEffect: The crew instead kept pulling against the autopilot's climb command without fully disengaging it, pitching the nose dangerously high until the aircraft stalled and crashed short of the runway, killing 264 of 271 aboard. The disaster prompted airlines and Airbus to overhaul training on autopilot mode confusion and mandatory full disconnection during unexpected control conflicts.

evt-04-26-2002-erfurt-school-massacre.scenario: It is 26 April 2002 at the Gutenberg-Gymnasium in Erfurt. An expelled 19-year-old student has entered the building armed, and lawmakers across Germany will soon be forced to confront how he obtained his weapons.
evt-04-26-2002-erfurt-school-massacre.prompt: What lasting change did Germany make to its firearms law in response to this attack?

choices.text: Mandated armed guards in every German school
Banned all handgun ownership nationwide
Raised the minimum age for large-caliber firearm ownership and tightened storage rules
Abolished the Gymnasium school-tracking system entirely

evt-04-26-2002-erfurt-school-massacre.butterflyEffect: The massacre prompted Germany's 2002 reform of its weapons law, raising the minimum age for owning large-caliber firearms to 21 and tightening storage and licensing rules. It also sparked lasting national debate over school security and the influence of violent media on young people.

evt-04-26-2005-cedar-revolution.scenario: It is spring 2005 in downtown Beirut. Weeks after Rafic Hariri's assassination, you stand among hundreds of thousands of Lebanese filling Martyrs' Square, waving flags and chanting for change.
evt-04-26-2005-cedar-revolution.prompt: What are the crowds primarily demanding from Damascus and Beirut?

choices.text: Immediate elections for a new Lebanese constitution
The resignation of the Lebanese army command
The withdrawal of Syrian troops and an independent investigation into Hariri's death
A merger of Lebanon and Syria into one state

evt-04-26-2005-cedar-revolution.butterflyEffect: Under this sustained, nonviolent pressure combined with international demands, Syria withdrew its troops from Lebanon in April 2005 after a 29-year military presence. The movement's success in achieving withdrawal without major bloodshed became a model, though Lebanon's sectarian divisions and Syrian influence resurfaced in the years that followed.

evt-04-26-2015-nursultan-nazarbayev.scenario: It is election day, April 2015, in Kazakhstan. You watch as state television announces Nursultan Nazarbayev has won with 97.7 percent of the vote against two token rivals, both from parties loyal to him.
evt-04-26-2015-nursultan-nazarbayev.prompt: What actually followed this landslide, virtually unopposed victory?

choices.text: He continued consolidating power, later engineering a controlled succession
International observers forced a recount that overturned the result
He dissolved the presidency and restored a parliamentary system
He immediately called for open multi-party elections

evt-04-26-2015-nursultan-nazarbayev.butterflyEffect: Nazarbayev governed for four more years before resigning in 2019, hand-picking Kassym-Jomart Tokayev as successor while retaining influence as Elbasy. That arrangement unraveled in January 2022, when deadly unrest forced Tokayev to strip Nazarbayev of remaining powers and the capital's name reverted from Nur-Sultan to Astana.

evt-04-26-2015-anti-monuments-in-mexico.scenario: It is April 2015 in Mexico City. You join activists installing a black, hand-shaped monument outside a government building to demand answers about the 43 students who vanished in Iguala the previous year.
evt-04-26-2015-anti-monuments-in-mexico.prompt: What is the antimonumento meant to force the government to do?

choices.text: Reopen the investigation and hold officials accountable for the students' disappearance
Rebuild the road where the students were last seen
Fund a new university scholarship program
Issue a public apology and close the case permanently

evt-04-26-2015-anti-monuments-in-mexico.butterflyEffect: The Antimonumento +43 became a permanent, unauthorized fixture the government could never quietly remove, and the tactic spread nationwide as families of femicide victims and the disappeared erected their own antimonumentos. The Ayotzinapa case itself remained largely unresolved, keeping public pressure alive for years.

evt-04-27-395-aelia-eudoxia.scenario: You are Eutropius, the powerful eunuch chamberlain of the Eastern court in 395. The praetorian prefect Rufinus expects his own daughter to marry the young emperor Arcadius, but you have other plans.
evt-04-27-395-aelia-eudoxia.prompt: What do you do to block Rufinus and expand your own influence?

choices.text: Propose a foreign princess as a compromise candidate
Urge Arcadius to remain unmarried
Openly support Rufinus's daughter as the bride
Secretly arrange for Arcadius to marry Aelia Eudoxia instead

evt-04-27-395-aelia-eudoxia.butterflyEffect: Eutropius secretly arranged Arcadius's marriage to Aelia Eudoxia, presenting Rufinus with a fait accompli. The humiliation deepened the rivalry between the two men, and Rufinus was assassinated by Gothic soldiers later that year, leaving Eutropius the dominant power behind the throne.

evt-04-27-630-shahrbaraz.scenario: It is April 630, and you are a Sasanian noble at Ctesiphon. The general Shahrbaraz has just marched his army into the capital and deposed the child-king Ardashir III to seize the throne himself.
evt-04-27-630-shahrbaraz.prompt: How do the Iranian nobility respond to Shahrbaraz's seizure of power?

choices.text: They crown him and his heirs permanently
They exile him to the eastern provinces
They accept him as the legitimate King of Kings
They assassinate him within weeks of his usurpation

evt-04-27-630-shahrbaraz.butterflyEffect: The nobles turned on Shahrbaraz and had him killed after only forty days on the throne. His brief, violent reign opened a chaotic succession of short-lived monarchs, including two reigning empresses, that fatally weakened the Sasanian state ahead of the Arab-Muslim conquests a few years later.

evt-04-27-1522-italian-war-of-1521-1526.scenario: You serve as a Swiss pikeman in French service near Bicocca, outside Milan, in April 1522. Imperial and Papal troops under Prospero Colonna hold a fortified position bristling with arquebusiers, and your comrades are impatient to attack head-on.
evt-04-27-1522-italian-war-of-1521-1526.prompt: What does the French commander Lautrec decide to do?

choices.text: Withdraw and besiege Milan instead
Attack the fortified line head-on as the Swiss demand
Negotiate a truce with Colonna
Wait for Venetian reinforcements before engaging

evt-04-27-1522-italian-war-of-1521-1526.butterflyEffect: Lautrec bowed to Swiss demands and ordered a frontal assault, which was shredded by entrenched arquebus fire before the pikemen could close. The slaughter shattered Swiss confidence in French service and demonstrated the growing killing power of firearms over massed pike formations, accelerating a shift in European battlefield tactics.

evt-04-27-1650-wars-of-the-three-kingdom.scenario: You are the Marquess of Montrose in April 1650, having landed in Scotland to raise an army for the exiled Charles II. At Carbisdale, Covenanter forces have caught your small, poorly equipped force by surprise.
evt-04-27-1650-wars-of-the-three-kingdom.prompt: With your army collapsing under attack, what do you do?

choices.text: Fight to the death alongside your men
Surrender immediately to negotiate terms
Order a full retreat back to the ships
Flee the battlefield to seek refuge

evt-04-27-1650-wars-of-the-three-kingdom.butterflyEffect: Montrose's force was routed and he fled the field, but he was soon captured, tried, and executed in Edinburgh. Charles II, negotiating with the Covenanters, publicly disavowed the man who had fought for him, then accepted Covenanter terms to be crowned King of Scots in 1651.

evt-04-27-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 27 April 1777, and you stand with hastily gathered Connecticut militia near Ridgefield, trying to block a British column retreating toward the coast after burning Patriot supplies at Danbury.
evt-04-27-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What happens in the fighting that follows?

choices.text: British commander Tryon is killed in the fighting
The militia let the column pass without engaging
British regulars break through and reach their ships despite militia resistance
The militia capture the entire British column

evt-04-27-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: British regulars broke through and reached their ships at Compo Beach, but General David Wooster was killed and Benedict Arnold's conspicuous bravery under fire drew wide praise. Congress, which had passed over Arnold for promotion months earlier and embittered him deeply, promoted him to major general soon after in recognition of his conduct at Ridgefield.

evt-04-27-1805-first-barbary-war.scenario: You are Marine Lieutenant Presley O'Bannon on 27 April 1805, having led a brutal 600-mile desert march across Libya with a small force of Marines and mercenaries to reach the fortified port of Derna.
evt-04-27-1805-first-barbary-war.prompt: How do you take the city's defenses?

choices.text: Negotiate a peaceful surrender first
Bypass Derna and march directly on Tripoli
Wait for reinforcements before attacking
Coordinate a naval bombardment with a ground assault on the fort

evt-04-27-1805-first-barbary-war.butterflyEffect: With naval guns bombarding the harbor forts, O'Bannon's men stormed and captured the city, raising the American flag over foreign soil for the first time. The victory later gave rise to the Marines' Hymn line 'to the shores of Tripoli.'

evt-04-27-1810-ludwig-van-beethoven.scenario: You are Ludwig van Beethoven in Vienna, 1810, finishing a tender little piano piece written for a woman you admire. It is charming, personal, and utterly unlike your grand symphonic works.
evt-04-27-1810-ludwig-van-beethoven.prompt: What do you do with the finished piece?

choices.text: Destroy the manuscript out of embarrassment
Keep it as a private gift, never publishing it
Rework it into a movement of a piano sonata
Send it to his publisher for immediate release

evt-04-27-1810-ludwig-van-beethoven.butterflyEffect: Beethoven never published the piece; it stayed in private hands after his death. In 1867 musicologist Ludwig Nohl discovered the manuscript, dedicated to a mysterious 'Elise,' and published it as Bagatelle No. 25 — now known worldwide as 'Für Elise,' one of the most recognized piano pieces ever written, despite its composer never releasing it himself.

evt-04-27-1848-national-assembly-france.scenario: You sit on the drafting commission of France's Second Republic, working under Victor Schœlcher's direction on the decree to end slavery in the colonies. The Revolution of 1848 has given abolitionists a rare political opening, and you must decide how freedom will actually be granted.
evt-04-27-1848-national-assembly-france.prompt: What does the decree of 27 April 1848 actually order?

choices.text: Freedom contingent on a colonial plebiscite
Immediate, unconditional freedom, with the state compensating slaveholders
A ten-year phased emancipation timetable
Abolition only in the Caribbean colonies, excluding the Indian Ocean territories

evt-04-27-1848-national-assembly-france.butterflyEffect: The decree granted immediate, unconditional freedom to roughly 250,000 enslaved people across France's colonies, while compensating former owners financially rather than the freed. It reshaped colonial labor systems, pushing many freedmen into restrictive wage contracts and prompting the later importation of indentured workers from Asia, and it made France the second major European power after Britain to abolish slavery outright.

evt-04-27-1904-chris-watson.scenario: You are Chris Watson, sworn in on 27 April 1904 as the world's first Labor prime minister, leading a minority government in Australia's young federal Parliament with no secure majority behind you.
evt-04-27-1904-chris-watson.prompt: What brought his government down just four months later?

choices.text: Watson's resignation due to ill health
Defeat on an amendment to the Conciliation and Arbitration Bill
A no-confidence vote over the federal budget
A snap election called by the Governor-General

evt-04-27-1904-chris-watson.butterflyEffect: Watson's government fell in August 1904 after losing a vote on an amendment to the Conciliation and Arbitration Bill concerning public servants. Though brief, his premiership proved a Labor government could actually hold office, paving the way for Andrew Fisher's stable majority Labor government within a decade.

evt-04-27-1911-second-guangzhou-uprising.scenario: You are a young revolutionary under Huang Xing in Guangzhou on 27 April 1911, poised to storm the Qing viceroy's residence as part of a planned uprising against imperial rule.
evt-04-27-1911-second-guangzhou-uprising.prompt: What happens when your assault on the viceroy's compound begins?

choices.text: Qing troops suppress the uprising and kill many rebels
The viceroy's guards defect to the revolutionaries
The rebels overwhelm the guards and capture the viceroy
Huang Xing calls off the attack before it starts

evt-04-27-1911-second-guangzhou-uprising.butterflyEffect: The uprising was crushed and many rebels were killed, their remains later honored as the '72 Martyrs of Huanghuagang.' Their sacrifice inspired revolutionary momentum across China, and just months later the Wuchang Uprising succeeded, triggering the collapse of the Qing dynasty and the founding of the Republic of China.

evt-04-27-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 27 April 1945, and you are among the Finnish troops reaching the remote cairn where Finland, Norway, and Sweden meet, the last German forces having just been driven from Finnish Lapland.
evt-04-27-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What do the soldiers do to mark reaching the border cairn?

choices.text: They raise a Soviet flag to mark the Red Army's arrival
They raise the Finnish flag, later photographed as a symbol of liberation
They raise a white flag to signal surrender to Germany
They demolish the cairn to erase the old border marker

evt-04-27-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: They raised the Finnish flag over the cairn, and the resulting photograph became one of Finland's most iconic wartime images, symbolizing the end of the Lapland War against its former ally Germany. As with other famous war photographs, historians have since debated exactly how and when the image was staged for the camera.

evt-04-27-1967-expo-67.scenario: You are a visitor at the sprawling Expo 67 fairgrounds in Montreal, with only a few hours before the gates close and dozens of national pavilions still to see.
evt-04-27-1967-expo-67.prompt: Which pavilion should you prioritize, knowing it will outlast the fair itself?

choices.text: The American geodesic dome pavilion
The temporary Cuban exhibit tent
The Expo 67 parking garage
The small souvenir kiosk near the entrance

evt-04-27-1967-expo-67.butterflyEffect: The American pavilion, Buckminster Fuller's giant geodesic dome, became one of the fair's most photographed structures. After a 1976 fire destroyed its acrylic skin, the steel frame survived and was later reopened as Montreal's Biosphère environmental museum.

evt-04-27-1985-1985-world-snooker-champi.scenario: It is past midnight on 28 April 1985, and you're among millions still watching as Dennis Taylor and Steve Davis, tied at 17-17, both eye the final black ball that will decide the World Championship.
evt-04-27-1985-1985-world-snooker-champi.prompt: Who pots that final black ball to win the title?

choices.text: Steve Davis pots it and defends his title
The frame is declared a draw and replayed
Dennis Taylor pots it, completing a stunning comeback
Officials postpone the deciding frame to the next day

evt-04-27-1985-1985-world-snooker-champi.butterflyEffect: Dennis Taylor sank the black to complete a comeback from 8-0 down, one of the greatest reversals in snooker history. The match drew over 18.5 million late-night viewers in Britain, a record that still stands for snooker and helped cement the sport's huge popularity boom of the 1980s.

evt-04-27-1993-zambia-national-football-.scenario: You are Kalusha Bwalya, Zambia's star forward, playing club football in Europe when you learn the shocking news: the plane carrying your national teammates has crashed off the coast of Gabon, killing everyone aboard.
evt-04-27-1993-zambia-national-football-.prompt: What do you do in the aftermath of the tragedy?

choices.text: Retire from international football out of grief
Switch allegiance to a European national team
Demand the tournament be cancelled entirely
Return home to help rebuild and captain the national team

evt-04-27-1993-zambia-national-football-.butterflyEffect: Bwalya became captain of a hastily rebuilt Zambian squad. Remarkably, this new team reached the final of the 1994 Africa Cup of Nations as an emotional tribute to the fallen, before Zambia finally won the tournament outright in 2012.

evt-04-27-1994-1994-south-african-genera.scenario: It is 27 April 1994, and you have waited half a day in a line stretching for miles outside a Soweto polling station. For the first time in your life, your race does not determine whether you may vote.
evt-04-27-1994-1994-south-african-genera.prompt: What follows once the ballots from this historic vote are counted?

choices.text: The results are annulled after widespread violence at the polls
The National Party retains power through a coalition majority
The Inkatha Freedom Party wins outright and moves to secede KwaZulu-Natal
The ANC wins a landslide and Nelson Mandela becomes South Africa's first Black president

evt-04-27-1994-1994-south-african-genera.butterflyEffect: The ANC won 62% of the vote, just short of a supermajority, and formed a Government of National Unity with the National Party and Inkatha Freedom Party. The new National Assembly's first act was electing Nelson Mandela as South Africa's first Black president, and 27 April became the national holiday Freedom Day.
