evt-04-27-2005-airbus-a380.scenario: It is 27 April 2005 at Toulouse-Blagnac Airport. You are aboard the maiden flight of the Airbus A380, the largest passenger airliner ever built, after years of delays and soaring costs threatened the program before a single wheel left the ground.
evt-04-27-2005-airbus-a380.prompt: What followed this successful first flight in the years ahead?

choices.text: It immediately replaced the Boeing 747 as the world's best-selling jet
It entered airline service two years later, starting with Singapore Airlines
Airbus cancelled the program before any airline placed an order
It was grounded permanently after the flight due to structural failure

evt-04-27-2005-airbus-a380.butterflyEffect: The A380 entered commercial service in October 2007 with Singapore Airlines, becoming an icon of long-haul travel for two decades. But airlines increasingly favored smaller, cheaper twin-engine jets over its four-engine bulk, and Airbus ended production in 2021 after just over 250 were built.

evt-04-27-2007-estonia.scenario: It is 27 April 2007 in Tallinn, and city workers have fenced off the Bronze Soldier monument to Soviet soldiers overnight, preparing to remove it as anger builds among the city's Russian-speaking minority.
evt-04-27-2007-estonia.prompt: What happens in the hours and days that follow the statue's removal?

choices.text: The European Union orders Estonia to restore the statue immediately
Riots erupt and Estonia is hit by unprecedented cyberattacks blamed on Russia
The statue is relocated quietly with no public reaction
Russian troops cross the border to protect the monument

evt-04-27-2007-estonia.butterflyEffect: The removal triggered the 'Bronze Night' riots among Russian-speaking Estonians and a massive, sustained wave of cyberattacks on Estonian government, bank, and media websites, widely attributed to Russia. It is often cited as the first major state-linked cyberwarfare campaign against a country, and it spurred NATO to later establish its Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre in Tallinn.

evt-04-27-2011-2011-super-outbreak.scenario: It is 27 April 2011, and meteorologists across Alabama and Mississippi are issuing tornado warning after tornado warning as an extraordinary number of storms fire up within hours of each other.
evt-04-27-2011-2011-super-outbreak.prompt: What made this single day historically unprecedented for tornado activity?

choices.text: The tornadoes were confined entirely to a single state
It was the first outbreak ever tracked using Doppler radar
No tornado that day was rated above EF2
A record 224 tornadoes struck in a single day, including four EF5s

evt-04-27-2011-2011-super-outbreak.butterflyEffect: A record 224 tornadoes touched down on 27 April alone, including four rated EF5, the highest possible rating. The outbreak's scale and the difficulty communicating its danger led the National Weather Service to overhaul its warning language soon after, introducing Impact-Based Warnings meant to convey urgency more clearly to the public.

evt-04-28-224-parthian-empire.scenario: It is 224 AD on the plain of Hormozdgan. You stand beside King Artabanus IV of Parthia as the rebel Persian vassal Ardashir advances his army, determined to overthrow four centuries of Arsacid rule.
evt-04-28-224-parthian-empire.prompt: What does Artabanus IV choose to do when Ardashir's forces close in?

choices.text: Offer Ardashir a peace settlement and tribute
Meet Ardashir's army head-on in a decisive battle
Delegate command entirely to regional satraps
Retreat into a fortress and wait for reinforcements

evt-04-28-224-parthian-empire.butterflyEffect: Artabanus met Ardashir in open battle and was killed, reportedly by Ardashir's own hand. Ardashir crowned himself Shahanshah, founding the Sasanian Empire, which revived Zoroastrianism as a state religion and became Rome's great rival in the East for the next four centuries.

evt-04-28-1253-nichiren.scenario: You are the monk Nichiren at Seichō-ji temple in 1253, convinced after years of study that only the Lotus Sutra offers salvation in this degenerate age, while rival schools promote other chants and rituals.
evt-04-28-1253-nichiren.prompt: What does Nichiren proclaim to begin his new teaching?

choices.text: Withdraw into silent meditation alone
Adopt esoteric Shingon rituals
Recite the Nembutsu prayer to Amida Buddha
Chant "Namu Myōhō Renge Kyō"

evt-04-28-1253-nichiren.butterflyEffect: Nichiren began chanting "Namu Myōhō Renge Kyō," founding what became Nichiren Buddhism. His sharp attacks on rival schools brought persecution and exile to Sado Island, yet his teachings endured and later inspired modern lay movements such as Soka Gakkai.

evt-04-28-1783-second-anglo-mysore-war.scenario: You are a British officer trapped inside the fortress of Bednore in early 1783, besieged by Tipu Sultan's army after your commander, General Mathews, seized the stronghold months earlier. Supplies are failing and no relief is in sight.
evt-04-28-1783-second-anglo-mysore-war.prompt: What does General Mathews decide to do?

choices.text: Wait indefinitely for reinforcements from Madras
Launch a desperate night sortie to break the siege
Negotiate surrender in exchange for safe passage for the garrison
Fight on to the last man rather than surrender

evt-04-28-1783-second-anglo-mysore-war.butterflyEffect: Mathews surrendered Bednore in exchange for promised safe passage, but Tipu Sultan broke the terms, seizing the garrison's treasure and imprisoning the men. Mathews and several officers reportedly died in captivity, and the episode hardened British resolve against Mysore in the wars that followed.

evt-04-28-1789-fletcher-christian.scenario: It is dawn on 28 April 1789 aboard HMS Bounty in the South Pacific. Fletcher Christian and armed sailors have just seized the ship and dragged Lieutenant William Bligh from his cabin.
evt-04-28-1789-fletcher-christian.prompt: What do the mutineers do with Bligh and the men who stay loyal to him?

choices.text: Lock them below deck as prisoners
Set them adrift in the ship's launch with minimal supplies
Maroon them on the nearest deserted island
Execute them immediately to prevent reprisal

evt-04-28-1789-fletcher-christian.butterflyEffect: Christian set Bligh and 18 loyal men adrift in a 23-foot open launch. Bligh then navigated over 3,600 nautical miles to Timor, one of history's great feats of seamanship, while Christian and the mutineers eventually settled Pitcairn Island, whose hidden colony wasn't discovered by outsiders until 1808.

evt-04-28-1910-louis-paulhan.scenario: You are Louis Paulhan in April 1910, racing rival Claude Grahame-White for the Daily Mail's £10,000 prize, pressing your biplane through headwinds and fatigue on the first attempted flight from London to Manchester.
evt-04-28-1910-louis-paulhan.prompt: What must Paulhan do to claim the prize?

choices.text: Land at Manchester within the required time
Abandon the race and land safely early
Switch to a different aircraft mid-route
Wait on the ground for calmer weather

evt-04-28-1910-louis-paulhan.butterflyEffect: Paulhan landed at Manchester ahead of Grahame-White, winning the first Daily Mail aviation prize and captivating the British public. The contest proved long-distance flight was practical, spurring rapid British investment in aviation just years before it became vital in the First World War.

evt-04-28-1923-1923-fa-cup-final.scenario: You are a mounted police constable at the brand-new Wembley Stadium on 28 April 1923, where a crowd far beyond the stadium's capacity has spilled onto the pitch just before the FA Cup final is due to kick off.
evt-04-28-1923-1923-fa-cup-final.prompt: How did police clear the pitch so the match between Bolton and West Ham could go ahead?

choices.text: Soldiers were brought in to forcibly clear the stadium
Fire brigades used hoses to drive spectators off the pitch
The match was cancelled and rescheduled for the following week
Mounted police, most memorably one on a white horse, pushed the crowd back

evt-04-28-1923-1923-fa-cup-final.butterflyEffect: Constable George Scorey on his white horse Billy gently pushed the crowd back to the touchlines, giving the match its enduring nickname, the "White Horse Final." Bolton Wanderers won 2-0, and the chaos led to lasting safety changes, including all-ticket sales for future finals to prevent such overcrowding.

evt-04-28-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 28 April 1945 in a village near Lake Como. Italian partisans have just stopped a column of retreating German trucks and discovered a disguised passenger: Benito Mussolini, trying to slip into Switzerland.
evt-04-28-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What did the partisans do with Mussolini once they confirmed his identity?

choices.text: Executed him without trial
Held him in custody awaiting an Italian court proceeding
Handed him over to Allied forces for a formal trial
Escorted him across the border into Switzerland as agreed

evt-04-28-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: He and his mistress Clara Petacci were shot the next day, and their bodies were strung up in Milan's Piazzale Loreto for public display. The images marked the symbolic collapse of Italian fascism and meant Mussolini, unlike the Nazi leadership at Nuremberg, never faced a war crimes tribunal.

evt-04-28-1952-treaty-of-taipei.scenario: You are a Republic of China diplomat in Taipei in April 1952, days after the San Francisco Peace Treaty took effect without China's participation, now negotiating Japan's separate peace with the Nationalist government instead of Beijing.
evt-04-28-1952-treaty-of-taipei.prompt: What must this treaty formally accomplish between Japan and the Republic of China?

choices.text: Form a military alliance against the People's Republic of China
Transfer former Japanese colonies to Chinese control
End the state of war and settle wartime claims
Formally reunify Taiwan with mainland China

evt-04-28-1952-treaty-of-taipei.butterflyEffect: The Treaty of Taipei formally ended the state of war from the Second Sino-Japanese War and settled claims, but left Taiwan's sovereignty status ambiguous. Japan later abrogated the treaty in 1972 when it normalized relations with the People's Republic of China, deepening the unresolved dispute over Taiwan's status.

evt-04-28-1972-jimmy-reid.scenario: You are a student packed into Glasgow University's Bute Hall in 1972, listening as newly installed Rector Jimmy Reid, the shipyard union leader, rises to deliver his inaugural address.
evt-04-28-1972-jimmy-reid.prompt: What does Reid urge the students to reject in his speech?

choices.text: The idea of Scottish independence
The alienation and cut-throat competition of the capitalist rat race
Studying subjects with no practical career use
Any involvement with trade unions

evt-04-28-1972-jimmy-reid.butterflyEffect: Reid attacked the "rat race," arguing capitalism turned people into aggressive, insecure ciphers and calling instead for solidarity and human dignity. The New York Times printed the speech in full, comparing it to Lincoln's Gettysburg Address, and it became one of the most celebrated rectorial addresses in British history.

evt-04-28-1978-president-of-afghanistan.scenario: It is 27–28 April 1978 in Kabul. Tanks loyal to pro-communist military officers surround the presidential palace where Mohammad Daoud Khan and his family have barricaded themselves.
evt-04-28-1978-president-of-afghanistan.prompt: What is the outcome of the coup against President Daoud Khan?

choices.text: Daoud is overthrown and killed, and communist officers seize power
Daoud negotiates a power-sharing government with the officers
Daoud successfully suppresses the coup and executes the plotters
Daoud flees into exile and rules from abroad

evt-04-28-1978-president-of-afghanistan.butterflyEffect: Daoud and much of his family were killed during the Saur Revolution, and PDPA leader Nur Muhammad Taraki took power, declaring a communist-aligned republic. The upheaval and factional infighting that followed helped draw in the Soviet Union, setting the stage for the 1979 invasion and decades of war in Afghanistan.

evt-04-28-1983-stern-magazine.scenario: You are an editor at Stern in April 1983, sitting on a sensational scoop: dozens of handwritten diaries attributed to Adolf Hitler, bought for millions of marks from a shadowy source who claims they survived a 1945 plane crash.
evt-04-28-1983-stern-magazine.prompt: Before publishing, what is the crucial step the magazine should take?

choices.text: Announce the find at a press conference without checking it
Rush the story to print to beat rival publications
Sell serialization rights abroad before verifying anything
Have the paper, ink, and handwriting forensically tested first

evt-04-28-1983-stern-magazine.butterflyEffect: The diaries were crude forgeries by Konrad Kujau; German federal archives proved the paper and ink post-dated the war within days of publication. The scandal humiliated Stern and the historian Hugh Trevor-Roper who had vouched for them, ending careers and becoming a lasting byword for journalistic gullibility.

evt-04-28-1986-chernobyl-disaster.scenario: You are a health physicist at Sweden's Forsmark nuclear plant on 28 April 1986. Radiation alarms are sounding on workers' clothing and on-site instruments, yet nothing is malfunctioning at Forsmark itself.
evt-04-28-1986-chernobyl-disaster.prompt: What do you do with this unexplained radiation reading?

choices.text: Alert Swedish authorities and trace the radiation to an external source
Wait for the next scheduled inspection before reporting anything
Dismiss the readings as instrument malfunction and continue routine operations
Classify the data internally without notifying the government

evt-04-28-1986-chernobyl-disaster.butterflyEffect: Swedish scientists traced the fallout to the Soviet Union and pressed Moscow for answers, forcing the USSR to publicly acknowledge the Chernobyl disaster two days after the explosion, far later than it occurred. The exposure embarrassed Soviet authorities internationally and became an early test of Gorbachev's glasnost policy of openness.

evt-04-28-1988-aloha-airlines-flight-243.scenario: You are a flight attendant aboard Aloha Airlines Flight 243, climbing over the Pacific between Hilo and Honolulu, when a roar tears through the cabin and 18 feet of the fuselage roof rips away above first class.
evt-04-28-1988-aloha-airlines-flight-243.prompt: What do the pilots decide to do with the crippled aircraft?

choices.text: Continue on to Honolulu as originally scheduled
Divert to the nearest suitable airport and land as quickly as possible
Turn back and attempt to return to Hilo
Climb to a higher altitude to reduce aerodynamic stress

evt-04-28-1988-aloha-airlines-flight-243.butterflyEffect: Captain Robert Schornstheimer diverted immediately and landed safely at Kahului Airport on Maui rather than pressing on to Honolulu. One flight attendant, Clarabelle Lansing, was swept overboard and died, but all others survived. The near-disaster exposed widespread metal fatigue in aging jets and led the FAA to launch the National Aging Aircraft program, tightening inspection rules across the industry.

evt-04-28-1988-maui.scenario: You are the captain of Aloha Airlines Flight 243, cruising at 24,000 feet over Hawaii, when a section of the upper fuselage suddenly tears away, ripping a hole above the passenger cabin.
evt-04-28-1988-maui.prompt: What did the crew do to bring the crippled aircraft down safely?

choices.text: Shut down both engines and attempted to glide toward the coast
Climbed to a higher altitude to relieve pressure on the fuselage
Began an emergency descent and diverted to the nearest airport
Continued on to the original destination of Honolulu

evt-04-28-1988-maui.butterflyEffect: Captain Robert Schornstheimer made a rapid emergency descent and landed the severely damaged Boeing 737 at Kahului Airport; flight attendant Clarabelle Lansing, who had been standing in the aisle, was swept out and did not survive. The incident exposed dangerous metal fatigue in aging aircraft and led to sweeping FAA inspection and maintenance reforms across the airline industry.

evt-04-28-1991-space-shuttle-discovery.scenario: You are part of the ground crew at Kennedy Space Center on 28 April 1991, watching Discovery roar off the pad on STS-39, a mission billed as unusually open for a flight tied to defense research.
evt-04-28-1991-space-shuttle-discovery.prompt: What is the primary purpose of this shuttle mission?

choices.text: Service the Hubble Space Telescope
Deploy a classified reconnaissance satellite
Deliver a module to the International Space Station
Conduct unclassified science experiments tied to defense-related sensor research

evt-04-28-1991-space-shuttle-discovery.butterflyEffect: STS-39 carried unclassified Department of Defense payloads, including spacecraft studying the upper atmosphere and phenomena relevant to missile defense sensors, making it the first Shuttle flight to conduct such research openly rather than in secrecy. It signaled a small but notable shift toward transparency in military-linked shuttle science as the Cold War wound down.

evt-04-28-1994-central-intelligence-agen.scenario: You are a federal prosecutor in a Virginia courtroom in April 1994, presenting evidence that CIA officer Aldrich Ames sold secrets to Moscow for nearly a decade in exchange for cash and a house.
evt-04-28-1994-central-intelligence-agen.prompt: What did Ames do when he appeared before the court?

choices.text: Refused to enter a plea and was held in contempt
Fled to Russia before the hearing could begin
Pleaded not guilty and demanded a full trial
Pleaded guilty to espionage

evt-04-28-1994-central-intelligence-agen.butterflyEffect: Ames pleaded guilty on 28 April 1994 in a deal that spared his wife Rosario from a lengthy prison term, and he was sentenced to life without parole. His betrayal had exposed at least ten CIA sources inside the Soviet Union, several of whom were executed, prompting a sweeping overhaul of CIA counterintelligence procedures.

evt-04-28-1996-whitewater-controversy.scenario: You are President Bill Clinton in April 1996, the first sitting president called to testify in a criminal trial, answering questions about your old land dealings with Jim and Susan McDougal from inside the White House.
evt-04-28-1996-whitewater-controversy.prompt: How does Clinton give his testimony for the Whitewater-related trial?

choices.text: Give videotaped testimony from the White House
Invoke the Fifth Amendment and decline to answer
Travel to Little Rock to testify in person
Refuse to testify by citing executive privilege

evt-04-28-1996-whitewater-controversy.butterflyEffect: Clinton gave a four-and-a-half-hour videotaped deposition rather than appearing in the Little Rock courtroom, an unprecedented arrangement for a sitting president. The McDougals were later convicted, but Clinton himself was never charged, though the episode kept independent-counsel scrutiny of the Clintons alive through his second term.

evt-04-28-1999-taber-alberta.scenario: It is 28 April 1999, just over a week after Columbine, and a 14-year-old former student walks into W.R. Myers High School in Taber, Alberta, carrying a sawed-off rifle.
evt-04-28-1999-taber-alberta.prompt: What did the shooting prompt Canadian schools and lawmakers to focus on afterward?

choices.text: Strengthening school security and anti-bullying programs
Closing all public schools in Alberta indefinitely
Treating the incident as unrelated to broader school safety policy
Immediately banning all firearm ownership nationwide

evt-04-28-1999-taber-alberta.butterflyEffect: One student, Jason Lang, was killed and another was wounded before the shooter was subdued and later tried as a youth. Coming so soon after Columbine, the attack intensified Canadian debate over youth violence, bullying, and school security, pushing many districts toward new threat-assessment and anti-bullying protocols.

evt-04-28-2004-cbs-news.scenario: You produce 60 Minutes II in April 2004, holding graphic photographs of American soldiers abusing detainees at Abu Ghraib prison. The Pentagon has asked you to hold the story, warning it could endanger U.S. troops in Iraq.
evt-04-28-2004-cbs-news.prompt: Knowing a journalist is about to publish similar material elsewhere, what should CBS do?

choices.text: Broadcast the photographs as planned
Delay the story indefinitely at the Pentagon's request
Air only a heavily censored version after government review
Hand the photographs over to the military exclusively

evt-04-28-2004-cbs-news.butterflyEffect: CBS broadcast the photographs, and the images ignited global outrage, congressional hearings, and courts-martial of several soldiers. The scandal became a defining, damaging image of the Iraq War and fueled lasting debate over detainee treatment and U.S. moral authority abroad.

evt-04-29-1760-seven-years-war.scenario: It is late April 1760, and you serve under the Chevalier de Lévis outside the walls of Quebec, fresh from routing the British garrison at Sainte-Foy. The city is battered but still held by the enemy, and everything now depends on whose ships reach the St. Lawrence first.
evt-04-29-1760-seven-years-war.prompt: What should the French force do while awaiting reinforcements?

choices.text: Storm the city walls immediately before the British can be resupplied
Abandon the campaign at once and withdraw all forces to France
Maintain the siege and wait for a French relief fleet to force the garrison's surrender
Negotiate an immediate surrender in exchange for safe passage to Montreal

evt-04-29-1760-seven-years-war.butterflyEffect: Lévis besieged Quebec and gambled on a French relief fleet arriving before the British. British ships reached the city first in May 1760, forcing the French to abandon the siege and retreat to Montreal, which fell later that year, sealing Britain's hold on Canada and its confirmation in the 1763 Treaty of Paris.

evt-04-29-1770-first-voyage-of-james-coo.scenario: It is 29 April 1770, and HMS Endeavour eases into an unfamiliar bay on the east coast of New Holland. You can see figures of the local Gweagal people watching from the shore as Cook prepares to bring a party ashore.
evt-04-29-1770-first-voyage-of-james-coo.prompt: What did Cook and his crew do upon making landfall here?

choices.text: Claimed the bay for the Dutch East India Company
Turned the ship around without attempting to land
Sailed past without recording the bay's location
Landed, made brief contact with local people, and collected botanical specimens

evt-04-29-1770-first-voyage-of-james-coo.butterflyEffect: Cook went ashore, encountered brief resistance from the Gweagal, and his naturalists Banks and Solander collected so many plant specimens that Cook named the site Botany Bay. Nearly two decades later, Britain chose Botany Bay as the destination for the First Fleet, founding its first penal colony in Australia in 1788.

evt-04-29-1826-parramatta.scenario: It is 1826, and you are surveying the southern sky from your observatory at Parramatta. Through your telescope you notice a faint, unusual smudge of light unlike any star cluster in your catalogues.
evt-04-29-1826-parramatta.prompt: What should you do with this puzzling nebulous object?

choices.text: Dismiss it as an optical flaw in the telescope lens
Record its position and appearance carefully for the catalogue
Assume it is a known comet and move on
Wait for a clearer night before noting it at all

evt-04-29-1826-parramatta.butterflyEffect: James Dunlop had spotted what is now known as Centaurus A, a peculiar galaxy later found to be one of the nearest active galactic nuclei to Earth. His careful recording of it in his catalogue of southern nebulae let later astronomers, armed with radio and X-ray telescopes, identify it as a landmark object for studying supermassive black holes.

evt-04-29-1863-grand-gulf-mississippi.scenario: It is April 29, 1863, and you are aboard one of Admiral David Porter's Union gunboats, hammering the Confederate batteries at Grand Gulf, Mississippi, to clear a crossing point for Grant's army.
evt-04-29-1863-grand-gulf-mississippi.prompt: After the bombardment fails to silence the forts, what does Grant decide to do?

choices.text: Order an immediate infantry assault on the Grand Gulf forts
March the army further south and cross the river unopposed at Bruinsburg
Withdraw the fleet north to Memphis to regroup
Wait at Grand Gulf for reinforcements from the navy

evt-04-29-1863-grand-gulf-mississippi.butterflyEffect: Grant abandoned the direct assault and marched his troops further south, crossing the Mississippi unopposed at Bruinsburg the next day. This bold flanking move launched the inland campaign that captured Vicksburg in July 1863, splitting the Confederacy along the river.

evt-04-29-1903-frank-slide.scenario: It is just after 4:10 a.m. on 29 April 1903 near Frank, Alberta. Tonnes of rock from Turtle Mountain have just buried the Canadian Pacific line, and you know a passenger train is due to pass this stretch within minutes.
evt-04-29-1903-frank-slide.prompt: As a railway brakeman on the scene, what should you do?

choices.text: Run down the tracks to flag down the train before it reaches the debris
Telegraph ahead and assume the message will arrive in time
Wait at the station for a supervisor's orders
Focus on evacuating the town instead of the railway

evt-04-29-1903-frank-slide.butterflyEffect: A quick-thinking brakeman ran down the line waving a lantern and managed to flag down the oncoming train just short of the debris, averting a second disaster. The slide itself remains Canada's deadliest landslide, and Turtle Mountain is still monitored for movement today.

evt-04-29-1910-parliament-of-the-united-.scenario: It is 29 April 1910, and you sit in the House of Lords. A year earlier you helped reject the radical People's Budget, triggering a constitutional crisis and a general election that returned the Liberal government to power.
evt-04-29-1910-parliament-of-the-united-.prompt: What does the House of Lords do when the budget is presented again?

choices.text: Amend it heavily before returning it to the Commons
Petition the King to dissolve Parliament instead
Reject it again and force another election
Pass the budget without further obstruction

evt-04-29-1910-parliament-of-the-united-.butterflyEffect: The Lords passed the People's Budget on 29 April 1910 without further resistance, introducing Britain's first taxes explicitly designed to fund old-age pensions and social welfare. The bruising standoff over the Lords' veto power led directly to the Parliament Act 1911, which stripped the unelected chamber of its ability to block money bills.

evt-04-29-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 29 April 1945. Your unit has just broken through the gates of Dachau and found boxcars packed with corpses and thousands of starving survivors. Armed SS guards stand nearby with their hands raised.
evt-04-29-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: As the liberating force arrives, what is the immediate priority?

choices.text: Secure the camp, disarm guards, and get medical aid to survivors
Immediately execute all captured guards without process
Focus solely on pursuing retreating German forces nearby
Withdraw and wait for specialized medical units to arrive first

evt-04-29-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: US troops liberated Dachau that day, uncovering horrors that hardened Allied resolve to prosecute Nazi crimes; some guards were killed by enraged soldiers in the camp's aftermath, an incident later investigated by the Army. Photographs and testimony from Dachau became key evidence at the Nuremberg trials and shaped postwar memory of the Holocaust.

evt-04-29-1968-broadway-theatre.scenario: It is April 29, 1968, and you are seated in the audience at the Biltmore Theatre for the Broadway opening of the rock musical "Hair."
evt-04-29-1968-broadway-theatre.prompt: What element of the show shocks and captivates the audience that night?

choices.text: A brief nude scene alongside frank depictions of drug use and antiwar sentiment
A traditional big-band orchestral score
A script rewritten to remove any political content
An all-star cast of established Hollywood film actors

evt-04-29-1968-broadway-theatre.butterflyEffect: "Hair" went on to run for 1,750 Broadway performances, and its rock score, nudity, and frank engagement with drugs and the Vietnam War helped open the door for later boundary-pushing musicals and brought countercultural politics into mainstream American theatre.

evt-04-29-1991-1991-bangladesh-cyclone.scenario: It is late April 1991, and radio warnings say a super cyclone is bearing down on Chittagong. You are a local official with hours left before landfall and coastal villages that have never emptied fast enough before.
evt-04-29-1991-1991-bangladesh-cyclone.prompt: What should you prioritize to save the most lives before the storm hits?

choices.text: Focus resources on protecting fishing boats in harbor
Wait for confirmation from national weather authorities before acting
Move coastal residents inland and to raised shelters immediately
Distribute sandbags to reinforce individual homes

evt-04-29-1991-1991-bangladesh-cyclone.butterflyEffect: The cyclone struck with roughly 250 km/h winds and a storm surge that overwhelmed the coast, becoming one of the deadliest tropical cyclones on record. The catastrophic toll pushed Bangladesh to build thousands of raised cyclone shelters and a community-based early warning network, dramatically reducing deaths in later storms of similar strength.

evt-04-29-1992-rodney-king.scenario: It is the evening of April 29, 1992, and you are a resident of South Central Los Angeles, watching the news announce that four LAPD officers have been acquitted in the videotaped beating of Rodney King.
evt-04-29-1992-rodney-king.prompt: What happens across Los Angeles in the hours and days that follow the verdict?

choices.text: The officers are re-arrested on state charges that same night
The National Guard restores full calm within a few hours
Widespread rioting and unrest break out across the city for days
Peaceful citywide vigils are held with no unrest

evt-04-29-1992-rodney-king.butterflyEffect: The acquittal ignited six days of rioting that left dozens dead and caused roughly a billion dollars in damage. The unrest pushed the Department of Justice to pursue federal civil rights charges against the officers and forced a long reckoning with LAPD practices.

evt-04-29-1992-1992-los-angeles-riots.scenario: It is the afternoon of 29 April 1992, and word has just spread through South Central Los Angeles that a jury has acquitted the four LAPD officers filmed beating Rodney King. You run a small shop nearby and can already hear crowds gathering in the streets.
evt-04-29-1992-1992-los-angeles-riots.prompt: What actually followed in Los Angeles over the next several days?

choices.text: Large-scale rioting and unrest spread across the city, lasting nearly a week
The protests remained calm and dispersed peacefully by evening
A state appeals court immediately overturned the acquittal
The city imposed a curfew and unrest ended within hours

evt-04-29-1992-1992-los-angeles-riots.butterflyEffect: Unrest spread across the city for five days, with widespread arson, looting, and violence before the National Guard and federal troops restored order. The riots intensified national debate over policing and race, and pressure for reform contributed to changes within the LAPD in the years that followed.

evt-04-29-1997-chemical-weapons-conventi.scenario: It is 29 April 1997, and your government's ratification of a new treaty has just brought it into force worldwide. Inspectors from a new international body are preparing to verify compliance at declared facilities.
evt-04-29-1997-chemical-weapons-conventi.prompt: What must your nation now do under the newly binding Chemical Weapons Convention?

choices.text: Continue production but cease testing on human subjects
Declare all chemical weapons stockpiles and begin verified destruction
Only restrict the export of chemical weapons to other states
Transfer existing stockpiles to allied nations for safekeeping

evt-04-29-1997-chemical-weapons-conventi.butterflyEffect: The CWC's entry into force created the OPCW to verify destruction of chemical arsenals worldwide, the first disarmament treaty banning an entire weapons category with intrusive inspections. Over the following decades it oversaw the elimination of declared stockpiles in the US, Russia, and elsewhere, though enforcement against non-signatory or covert use remained contentious.

evt-04-29-2004-oldsmobile.scenario: It is 29 April 2004, and you stand on the factory floor in Lansing, Michigan, as the last Oldsmobile ever built rolls off the assembly line after 107 years of production.
evt-04-29-2004-oldsmobile.prompt: What did General Motors do with the Oldsmobile brand after this final car was built?

choices.text: Relaunched it as a low-cost sub-brand of Saturn
Kept producing a single Oldsmobile model for fleet sales only
Discontinued the brand completely and shifted dealers to other GM lines
Sold the Oldsmobile name to a foreign automaker

evt-04-29-2004-oldsmobile.butterflyEffect: GM discontinued Oldsmobile entirely, ending America's oldest surviving car brand, and its dealers were folded into other GM lines. The closure foreshadowed the deeper consolidation GM underwent during its 2009 bankruptcy, when several more storied brands were shed.

evt-04-29-2006-cyclone-mala.scenario: It is 27 April 2006, and you are a village leader on Myanmar's Rakhine coast. Cyclone Mala is rapidly strengthening offshore, its winds climbing toward 185 km/h as it drifts slowly toward land.
evt-04-29-2006-cyclone-mala.prompt: What should you do for your coastal community as the storm intensifies?

choices.text: Assume the coast is safe since major cyclones rarely strike there
Stay behind to secure fishing boats and property
Wait for an official government warning before acting
Evacuate coastal villages inland well ahead of landfall

evt-04-29-2006-cyclone-mala.butterflyEffect: Mala made landfall near Thandwe on 29 April 2006 as the strongest storm of that cyclone season, killing 37 people and damaging thousands of homes. Its rapid, hard-to-predict intensification exposed gaps in Bay of Bengal storm forecasting that were tragically underscored two years later by the far deadlier Cyclone Nargis.

evt-04-29-2011-william-prince-of-wales.scenario: You are among the crowds lining The Mall in London on April 29, 2011, waiting for Prince William to arrive at Westminster Abbey to marry Catherine Middleton.
evt-04-29-2011-william-prince-of-wales.prompt: What title does the Queen grant William on the morning of his wedding?

choices.text: Duke of York
Prince of Wales
Duke of Edinburgh
Duke of Cambridge

evt-04-29-2011-william-prince-of-wales.butterflyEffect: William was created Duke of Cambridge (along with Earl of Strathearn and Baron Carrickfergus) on his wedding day. He held that title for over a decade until his father's accession in 2022, when he became Prince of Wales.

evt-04-29-2011-wedding-of-prince-william.scenario: It is 29 April 2011, and you stand among the crowds outside Westminster Abbey as Catherine Middleton arrives to marry Prince William, with millions more watching on screens around the world.
evt-04-29-2011-wedding-of-prince-william.prompt: What happened immediately after the couple left the Abbey that day?

choices.text: They traveled directly to Windsor Castle for a private reception only
They appeared on the Buckingham Palace balcony before a global broadcast audience
They held a formal press conference announcing future duties
They departed immediately for a private honeymoon abroad without public appearances

evt-04-29-2011-wedding-of-prince-william.butterflyEffect: The newlyweds appeared on the Buckingham Palace balcony before a vast crowd and a global television audience estimated in the hundreds of millions. Catherine became Duchess of Cambridge, and the couple's popularity helped bolster public support for the monarchy; in 2022 they became Prince and Princess of Wales upon Charles III's accession.

evt-04-29-2013-national-airlines-flight-.scenario: You are the loadmaster preparing five heavy armored vehicles as cargo aboard a Boeing 747 freighter departing Bagram Airfield, Afghanistan, on April 29, 2013.
evt-04-29-2013-national-airlines-flight-.prompt: What must you do to keep the vehicles from shifting once the aircraft climbs steeply?

choices.text: Rely on each vehicle's own parking brake to hold it in place
Chain and secure every vehicle according to weight-and-balance restraint procedures
Skip tie-downs since the vehicles are heavy enough to stay put
Secure only the two heaviest vehicles and leave the rest loose

evt-04-29-2013-national-airlines-flight-.butterflyEffect: Investigators found that at least one armored vehicle broke free of inadequate restraints during climb-out, shifting the center of gravity and causing an unrecoverable stall; all seven crew members died. The crash prompted tightened guidance on securing rolling cargo aboard freighter aircraft.

evt-04-30-311-ad-311.scenario: It is early 311, and you are a Christian in Nicomedia. Word spreads that the dying Emperor Galerius, wracked by illness, has issued a new edict concerning your faith.

choices.text: It ends persecution and grants Christians toleration
It exiles all Christian clergy to Egypt
It intensifies persecution across the empire
It orders all Christians to sacrifice to the Roman gods or face exile

evt-04-30-311-ad-311.butterflyEffect: The Edict of Toleration ended the Great Persecution in the eastern Roman Empire, letting Christians worship openly again. It foreshadowed Constantine's Edict of Milan two years later, which extended toleration empire-wide and set Christianity on its path to becoming Rome's dominant religion.

evt-04-30-313-civil-wars-of-the-tetrarch.scenario: It's 30 April 313, and you serve in Licinius's army near Adrianople in Thrace, badly outnumbered by Maximinus Daza's forces marching to seize control of the East.
evt-04-30-313-civil-wars-of-the-tetrarch.prompt: What does Licinius decide to do despite being outnumbered?

choices.text: Retreat and wait for reinforcements from Constantine
Fortify a camp and wait out a siege
Negotiate a truce dividing the eastern provinces
Attack immediately, trusting his veteran troops

evt-04-30-313-civil-wars-of-the-tetrarch.butterflyEffect: Licinius's smaller, disciplined army crushed Maximinus Daza's forces; Daza fled east and died within months, leaving Licinius master of the Roman East. This reduced the empire to two rulers, Licinius and Constantine, setting the stage for the final civil war that ended with Constantine's sole rule in 324.

evt-04-30-1789-george-washington.scenario: It is April 30, 1789, and you stand among the crowd outside Federal Hall in New York City as George Washington steps onto the balcony to take the oath as the nation's first president.
evt-04-30-1789-george-washington.prompt: What does Washington place his hand on as he swears the oath?

choices.text: No object; he simply raised his hand
The Declaration of Independence
A copy of the newly ratified Constitution
A Bible borrowed from a New York Masonic lodge

evt-04-30-1789-george-washington.butterflyEffect: Washington swore on a Bible borrowed from St. John's Masonic Lodge No. 1, since no official Bible had been prepared. The gesture became an enduring inaugural tradition, and his peaceful assumption of executive power set the precedent for the orderly transfer of authority that has defined the presidency since.

evt-04-30-1803-louisiana-purchase.scenario: It is early 1803 and you are part of the American delegation in Paris, sent to secure river access at New Orleans. Napoleon's ambitions in the Americas have just collapsed after disaster in Haiti.
evt-04-30-1803-louisiana-purchase.prompt: What deal do you strike with France?

choices.text: Buy only the port city of New Orleans
Agree to joint French-American control of the territory
Purchase the whole Louisiana Territory for roughly $15 million
Lease permanent navigation rights on the Mississippi

evt-04-30-1803-louisiana-purchase.butterflyEffect: The United States bought the entire Louisiana Territory for about $15 million, doubling the nation's size overnight. It opened the way for westward expansion, though most of the land was still held by Native nations, setting up decades of further conflict and treaty-making.

evt-04-30-1894-coxey-s-army.scenario: It is April 30, 1894, and you have walked hundreds of miles with Jacob Coxey's army of unemployed workers, finally approaching the U.S. Capitol to demand government relief from the depression.
evt-04-30-1894-coxey-s-army.prompt: What happens when Coxey tries to mount the Capitol steps to deliver his speech?

choices.text: Police open fire on the crowd
Congress immediately passes his relief bill
He is invited inside to address Congress
He is arrested for trespassing on the grass

evt-04-30-1894-coxey-s-army.butterflyEffect: Coxey was arrested for walking on the Capitol lawn before he could speak, and the march dispersed without winning its demands. Still, it became the first major protest march on Washington, setting a template later followed by the Bonus Army in 1932 and civil rights marches of the 1960s.

evt-04-30-1897-j-j-thomson.scenario: You are assisting J. J. Thomson at Cambridge's Cavendish Laboratory in 1897, bending a beam of cathode rays with electric and magnetic fields to settle whether they are particles or waves.
evt-04-30-1897-j-j-thomson.prompt: What do you conclude from the deflection data?

choices.text: Cathode rays are positively charged ions of hydrogen gas
Cathode rays are neutral particles with no charge
Cathode rays are streams of negatively charged particles smaller than atoms
Cathode rays are a form of electromagnetic radiation like light

evt-04-30-1897-j-j-thomson.butterflyEffect: Thomson identified the electron as a negatively charged particle far smaller than any atom, proving atoms were not indivisible after all. The discovery opened the door to subatomic physics and quantum theory, earning him the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physics.

evt-04-30-1927-douglas-fairbanks.scenario: You stand with your wife Mary Pickford outside Sid Grauman's new Chinese Theatre in Hollywood on 30 April 1927, invited to leave a permanent mark in the wet cement of the forecourt.
evt-04-30-1927-douglas-fairbanks.prompt: What do you do to make history?

choices.text: Plant a commemorative tree in the courtyard
Sign your names on a plaque above the theatre entrance
Unveil a bronze statue of yourselves
Press your hands and feet into the wet concrete forecourt

evt-04-30-1927-douglas-fairbanks.butterflyEffect: Fairbanks and Pickford pressed their hands and feet into the wet concrete, starting the famous forecourt tradition at what became Grauman's Chinese Theatre. A simple publicity stunt turned into one of Hollywood's most enduring rituals, imitated by hundreds of stars over the following century.

evt-04-30-1945-death-of-adolf-hitler.scenario: It is the afternoon of 30 April 1945 in the Führerbunker beneath Berlin. Soviet troops are only blocks away, and Hitler has just said goodbye to his remaining staff.
evt-04-30-1945-death-of-adolf-hitler.prompt: What does Hitler do in the bunker's final hour?

choices.text: He shoots himself while Eva Braun takes poison
He orders one final armored counterattack on the city
He flees through an escape tunnel south of Berlin
He surrenders personally to the advancing Red Army

evt-04-30-1945-death-of-adolf-hitler.butterflyEffect: Hitler shot himself while Eva Braun took cyanide; their bodies were burned in the Chancellery garden. Germany surrendered unconditionally within days, ending the war in Europe, while Soviet secrecy about the remains fueled decades of conspiracy theories about his fate.

evt-04-30-1963-bristol-omnibus-company.scenario: It's 30 April 1963 in Bristol, and you've just learned the Bristol Omnibus Company and the Transport and General Workers' Union have refused to hire Black or Asian bus crews. As a young West Indian community leader, you must decide how to fight the color bar.
evt-04-30-1963-bristol-omnibus-company.prompt: What tactic do you organize to challenge the bus company's color bar?

choices.text: Petition Parliament for new legislation and wait
Stage a sit-in aboard the buses themselves
File a lawsuit under existing race discrimination law
Organize a boycott of the bus company

evt-04-30-1963-bristol-omnibus-company.butterflyEffect: Led by Paul Stephenson and inspired by Montgomery, the Bristol Bus Boycott lasted four months until the company scrapped its color bar in August 1963. The campaign's success helped push Parliament toward the Race Relations Acts of 1965 and 1968, which outlawed racial discrimination in British public life.

evt-04-30-1975-fall-of-saigon.scenario: It is 29 April 1975 and North Vietnamese shells are falling on Tan Son Nhut Airbase. You are one of thousands of Americans and South Vietnamese civilians waiting desperately to leave Saigon before it falls.
evt-04-30-1975-fall-of-saigon.prompt: What operation gets you out of the city in time?

choices.text: An overland evacuation by train north to Da Nang
A fixed-wing airlift from Tan Son Nhut's main runway
A naval convoy sailing up the Mekong River
Operation Frequent Wind, a mass helicopter evacuation

evt-04-30-1975-fall-of-saigon.butterflyEffect: Operation Frequent Wind became the largest helicopter evacuation in history, lifting thousands from rooftops and the embassy compound. Saigon fell the next day, South Vietnam ceased to exist, and Vietnam was formally reunified under communist rule in 1976.

evt-04-30-1994-formula-one.scenario: It is Saturday, 30 April 1994, qualifying for the San Marino Grand Prix at Imola. You watch Roland Ratzenberger's Simtek lose its front wing at high speed and slam into the wall at the Villeneuve corner.
evt-04-30-1994-formula-one.prompt: What does this crash mark for the rest of the weekend?

choices.text: The first of two fatal crashes that weekend, the next being Ayrton Senna's
Ratzenberger walks away and races the next day
The race is cancelled outright and never rescheduled
It is ruled a minor incident with no lasting consequence

evt-04-30-1994-formula-one.butterflyEffect: Ratzenberger's death was F1's first fatality in over a decade, and Ayrton Senna was killed in a crash the very next day. The double tragedy forced sweeping safety reforms across circuits, cars, and cockpits that still shape modern motorsport.

evt-04-30-2000-faustina-kowalska.scenario: You stand in St. Peter's Square on 30 April 2000 as Pope John Paul II declares a Polish nun a saint before a vast crowd, invoking the visions of mercy she once described.
evt-04-30-2000-faustina-kowalska.prompt: What devotion does the Pope establish that day, tied to her visions?

choices.text: The Sacred Heart devotion
The Feast of the Immaculate Conception
Divine Mercy Sunday
The Feast of Christ the King

evt-04-30-2000-faustina-kowalska.butterflyEffect: John Paul II canonized Faustina and instituted Divine Mercy Sunday, the Sunday after Easter, elevating her once-obscure private revelations into official Church teaching. The devotion spread rapidly worldwide, becoming one of modern Catholicism's fastest-growing popular movements.

evt-04-30-2000-canonization.scenario: It's 30 April 2000, and you stand among 200,000 pilgrims in St. Peter's Square as Pope John Paul II canonizes the Polish nun Faustina Kowalska, once viewed with suspicion by Church authorities for her visions of divine mercy.
evt-04-30-2000-canonization.prompt: What does the Pope establish alongside this canonization?

choices.text: A new religious order dedicated to Faustina
Divine Mercy Sunday as a feast on the Church calendar
The Vatican's first televised Mass
A new basilica built that same day in Kraków

evt-04-30-2000-canonization.butterflyEffect: John Paul II declared the Sunday after Easter as Divine Mercy Sunday, elevating a once-controversial devotion into a universal feast of the Catholic Church. Faustina's diary and the Divine Mercy image spread rapidly worldwide, becoming especially central to Catholic devotion in Poland and among the diaspora.

evt-04-30-2004-abu-ghraib-torture-and-pr.scenario: It is late April 2004, and as a news editor you are holding a set of graphic photographs, obtained by CBS News, showing American soldiers abusing detainees at Abu Ghraib prison in Iraq.
evt-04-30-2004-abu-ghraib-torture-and-pr.prompt: What happened once these photographs became public?

choices.text: The photos were dismissed as fabricated and no action followed
Defense Secretary Rumsfeld resigned within days
The Iraq War ended shortly afterward
Several soldiers were court-martialed after investigations and hearings

evt-04-30-2004-abu-ghraib-torture-and-pr.butterflyEffect: The images sparked global outrage and congressional hearings, leading to courts-martial of several low-ranking soldiers including Lynndie England and Charles Graner. The scandal badly damaged U.S. credibility abroad and fueled lasting debate over interrogation policy and military oversight.

evt-04-30-2009-2009-attack-on-the-dutch-.scenario: You are in the crowd at Apeldoorn on Koninginnedag, 30 April 2009, watching an open-topped bus carrying Queen Beatrix and the royal family, when a car suddenly accelerates toward the parade route.

choices.text: Police intercept the car before it reaches the parade
The queen is struck and injured by the vehicle
The driver is arrested unharmed with no other casualties
The car misses the royal bus, kills bystanders, and crashes into a monument

evt-04-30-2009-2009-attack-on-the-dutch-.butterflyEffect: The car missed the royal bus but plowed through the crowd before smashing into a monument; the driver and several bystanders were killed, though the royal family was unharmed. The attack prompted the Netherlands to overhaul security arrangements for future royal public appearances.

evt-04-30-2009-chrysler.scenario: It is 30 April 2009, and Chrysler's executives face a midnight deadline set by the Obama administration to strike a restructuring deal with creditors and Fiat or face liquidation.
evt-04-30-2009-chrysler.prompt: What move does Chrysler make to survive?

choices.text: Finds a buyer among German automakers instead
Files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in a government-backed deal with Fiat
Merges outright with General Motors
Liquidates entirely and sells off its factories

evt-04-30-2009-chrysler.butterflyEffect: Chrysler filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy as part of a government-backed restructuring, emerging weeks later with Fiat as a major stakeholder. That alliance eventually grew into Fiat Chrysler Automobiles, which later merged into today's Stellantis.

evt-04-30-2014-april-2014-urumqi-attack.scenario: It is April 30, 2014, and you are passing through Ürümqi's South railway station just as explosions and a knife attack erupt, coinciding with the end of a high-profile visit by China's top leader to the region.
evt-04-30-2014-april-2014-urumqi-attack.prompt: How did Chinese authorities respond to the attack in the following days?

choices.text: They launched an intensified security and anti-terrorism campaign in Xinjiang
They disbanded local police forces in the region
They eased travel restrictions to calm tensions
They dismissed it as an isolated criminal incident with no policy change

evt-04-30-2014-april-2014-urumqi-attack.butterflyEffect: Authorities launched an intensified anti-terrorism campaign across Xinjiang, expanding surveillance and security checkpoints. This response was part of a broader escalation that, over the following years, developed into sweeping state security and re-education policies across the region.

evt-04-30-2021-2021-meron-crowd-crush.scenario: It is just after midnight on 30 April 2021 on Mount Meron. As a safety planner, you watch thousands of pilgrims funnel from an open gathering into a single narrow, sloping passageway toward a staircase.
evt-04-30-2021-2021-meron-crowd-crush.prompt: What change to the site could have prevented the crush that followed?

choices.text: Increasing the number of food and drink stalls nearby
Limiting how many people could enter the passage at once
Adding more musicians to keep the crowd calm
Extending the event's opening hours

evt-04-30-2021-2021-meron-crowd-crush.butterflyEffect: No such limits were in place, and the wet, narrow passage became fatally congested, causing Israel's deadliest civil disaster. A state commission of inquiry later found years of ignored safety warnings about the site, leading to reforms in how mass religious gatherings are managed.

evt-05-01-305-diocletian.scenario: It is 1 May 305 at Nicomedia. You stand among the assembled troops as the aging Emperor Diocletian, worn by illness and two decades of rule, prepares to lay down the imperial purple.
evt-05-01-305-diocletian.prompt: What unprecedented act does Diocletian perform that day?

choices.text: He names his son as sole heir
He declares himself a living god
He permanently splits the empire into East and West
He voluntarily abdicates the throne

evt-05-01-305-diocletian.butterflyEffect: Diocletian became the first Roman emperor to abdicate voluntarily, and forced co-emperor Maximian to do the same the same day under the Tetrarchy system he had designed. The orderly succession he envisioned collapsed within months into civil war among rival claimants, eventually clearing the path for Constantine's rise to power.

evt-05-01-1169-anglo-normans.scenario: It is May 1169, and your ships have just grounded on the sands of Bannow Bay. Diarmait Mac Murchada, the exiled King of Leinster, has hired your band of Cambro-Norman knights to help him reclaim his throne.
evt-05-01-1169-anglo-normans.prompt: What fortified town do you march on first to secure Mac Murchada's return?

choices.text: Waterford
Dublin
Cashel
Wexford

evt-05-01-1169-anglo-normans.butterflyEffect: Robert FitzStephen's mercenaries took Wexford within days, and the swift success drew more Norman lords to Ireland, including Strongbow in 1170. Their gains alarmed King Henry II, who landed himself in 1171 to assert royal control, beginning centuries of English lordship over Ireland.

evt-05-01-1576-stephen-bathory.scenario: It is 1576, and the Polish-Lithuanian throne stands vacant after Henry of Valois fled back to France. As a member of the szlachta gathered at the election sejm, you must cast your support for the next monarch, with rival factions backing different foreign candidates.
evt-05-01-1576-stephen-bathory.prompt: Which candidate do you back to marry Anna Jagiellon and take the throne?

choices.text: John III of Sweden
Ivan the Terrible of Muscovy
Stephen Báthory
Maximilian II of the Habsburgs

evt-05-01-1576-stephen-bathory.butterflyEffect: Enough nobles backed Stephen Báthory, Voivode of Transylvania, to override the senate's choice of the Habsburg Maximilian II, who died before the dispute could turn into open war. Báthory proved one of the Commonwealth's most capable rulers, reforming the army and defeating Ivan the Terrible in the Livonian War.

evt-05-01-1625-dutch-portuguese-war.scenario: You serve aboard a combined Spanish-Portuguese fleet in early 1625, sent across the Atlantic after news that Dutch forces have seized Salvador da Bahia, the capital of Portuguese Brazil.
evt-05-01-1625-dutch-portuguese-war.prompt: What does this large relief fleet achieve?

choices.text: It retakes Salvador da Bahia, ending the Dutch occupation of the city
It is destroyed by storms before reaching Brazil
It sails past Brazil to attack Dutch ports in Africa instead
It negotiates a permanent truce ceding Bahia to the Dutch

evt-05-01-1625-dutch-portuguese-war.butterflyEffect: The Spanish-Portuguese fleet under Fadrique de Toledo recaptured Salvador da Bahia from the Dutch West India Company, ending its brief occupation. The victory temporarily secured Portuguese Brazil, but Dutch ambitions in the Americas continued, leading to further conflict including the later Dutch conquest of Pernambuco.

evt-05-01-1794-war-of-the-pyrenees.scenario: You command French Revolutionary troops along the Pyrenees frontier in spring 1794, a year after Spanish forces pushed into French territory and seized ground along the border.
evt-05-01-1794-war-of-the-pyrenees.prompt: What does the French army accomplish in this campaign?

choices.text: They abandon the frontier entirely and retreat to Toulouse
They recover almost all the ground lost to Spain in 1793
They lose additional territory to a renewed Spanish offensive
They sign an immediate armistice with Spain

evt-05-01-1794-war-of-the-pyrenees.butterflyEffect: French forces regained nearly all the territory lost to Spain in the previous year's fighting, turning the momentum of the War of the Pyrenees firmly in France's favor. The campaign set up further French advances into Spanish Catalonia and the Basque country that would eventually force Spain to seek peace in 1795.

evt-05-01-1884-moses-fleetwood-walker.scenario: You are Moses Fleetwood Walker, catcher for the Toledo Blue Stockings, stepping onto the field for the 1884 American Association season. You already starred at Oberlin and Michigan, but no Black man has caught in a major league before.
evt-05-01-1884-moses-fleetwood-walker.prompt: What is the outcome of your season with Toledo?

choices.text: He plays the season as the first Black major leaguer, then the sport enforces an unwritten color line
He is drafted into military service midseason
He switches to pitching after being banned from catching
He is immediately welcomed and more Black players join him the same year

evt-05-01-1884-moses-fleetwood-walker.butterflyEffect: Walker became the first African American to play major league baseball, catching for Toledo in the American Association in 1884. Rising racial hostility, including from stars like Cap Anson, helped push an unwritten color line into place, and no Black player would appear in the majors again until Jackie Robinson in 1947.

evt-05-01-1897-ramakrishna-mission.scenario: It is May 1897 in Calcutta. You are a young monk under Swami Vivekananda, who insists the order cannot remain shut away in silent meditation while famine, disease, and poverty ravage the countryside.
evt-05-01-1897-ramakrishna-mission.prompt: What does Vivekananda establish to fuse spiritual discipline with organized public service?

choices.text: The Arya Samaj
The Theosophical Society
The Brahmo Samaj
The Ramakrishna Mission

evt-05-01-1897-ramakrishna-mission.butterflyEffect: Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897, grounding it in Karma Yoga—selfless service as spiritual practice. It grew into one of India's largest charitable organizations, running hospitals, schools, and disaster relief, and its model of monk-led humanitarian work shaped later Indian social reform movements.

evt-05-01-1931-empire-state-building.scenario: It's 1 May 1931, and you're among the crowd in Manhattan as workmen put the finishing touches on an Art Deco tower raised in barely over a year, rising higher than any building on Earth.
evt-05-01-1931-empire-state-building.prompt: What happens at the building's dedication ceremony that day?

choices.text: Aviators fly a plane through its unfinished mooring mast
President Hoover pushes a button in Washington to light it up
Construction workers strike, delaying the opening
The mayor cuts a ribbon at street level only

evt-05-01-1931-empire-state-building.butterflyEffect: The Empire State Building opened as the world's tallest building, a title it held for nearly forty years until 1970. Its rapid construction became a symbol of American ambition even amid the Great Depression, though empty floors for years earned it the nickname the "Empty State Building."

evt-05-01-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is dawn on 1 May 1945. You are a Gurkha paratrooper of the Indian 50th Parachute Brigade, dropping onto Elephant Point south of Rangoon to silence Japanese guns guarding the river approach.
evt-05-01-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What is the immediate objective of this airborne assault?

choices.text: Rescue Allied prisoners of war held in Rangoon
Destroy Japanese airfields near Rangoon
Clear the way for Allied forces to retake Rangoon by sea
Capture the Japanese commander of Burma

evt-05-01-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The drop at Elephant Point cleared coastal defenses just ahead of the monsoon, letting Allied amphibious forces enter Rangoon virtually unopposed on 3 May 1945, since Japanese troops had already withdrawn. The swift, low-cost capture secured Burma's capital and port, effectively breaking major Japanese resistance in the campaign.

evt-05-01-1950-gwendolyn-brooks.scenario: It is May 1, 1950, and you are a poet from Chicago's South Side whose second collection, Annie Allen, chronicles ordinary Black life with unusual formal skill. The Pulitzer board is about to announce this year's poetry prize.
evt-05-01-1950-gwendolyn-brooks.prompt: What happens next for this poet?

choices.text: She is awarded the National Book Award instead
She declines the nomination in protest of segregation
She wins the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry, a first for a Black writer
The prize goes unawarded that year due to a tie

evt-05-01-1950-gwendolyn-brooks.butterflyEffect: Gwendolyn Brooks won the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry for Annie Allen, becoming the first African American to win a Pulitzer Prize in any category. The award gave her national literary standing and helped open doors for later Black writers seeking recognition from mainstream American institutions.

evt-05-01-1991-major-league-baseball.scenario: It is 1 May 1991 at the Oakland Coliseum. You watch Rickey Henderson take his lead off first base, one steal away from a mark untouched since 1977.
evt-05-01-1991-major-league-baseball.prompt: What record does Henderson break with his 939th career stolen base?

choices.text: The career stolen base record
The career home run record
The single-season stolen base record
The career hits record

evt-05-01-1991-major-league-baseball.butterflyEffect: Henderson stole his 939th base, passing Lou Brock as baseball's all-time career stolen base leader, and famously declared himself 'the greatest of all time.' He finished his career with 1,406 steals, a mark still considered nearly unreachable in the modern power-hitting era.

evt-05-01-2002-horncastle-boar-s-head.scenario: You are sweeping a field near Horncastle, Lincolnshire with your metal detector in 2002 when a small, ornately worked bronze object turns up in the soil. It looks Anglo-Saxon, and possibly valuable.
evt-05-01-2002-horncastle-boar-s-head.prompt: What should you do with a find like this under UK treasure law?

choices.text: Sell it privately to a collector as soon as possible
Clean it yourself with metal polish before showing anyone
Rebury it and mark the spot for later without telling anyone
Report it to the local coroner or a Finds Liaison Officer as potential treasure

evt-05-01-2002-horncastle-boar-s-head.butterflyEffect: The finder reported the object as treasure, and it was identified as an early seventh-century boar's-head ornament, likely once part of a helmet crest. It was valued and acquired for £15,000 by what is now the Lincoln Museum, where it remains on permanent display, adding to the small corpus of Anglo-Saxon helmet fittings known to archaeologists.

evt-05-01-2016-2016-fort-mcmurray-wildfi.scenario: It's 3 May 2016, and you're a Fort McMurray resident watching smoke choke the sky as officials order the entire city to leave immediately, with only one highway leading out.
evt-05-01-2016-2016-fort-mcmurray-wildfi.prompt: What is the safest choice as the evacuation order comes?

choices.text: Wait until morning to see if the order is lifted
Take shelter in the downtown arena
Shelter in place and wait for the fire to pass
Join the mass convoy south along Highway 63 immediately

evt-05-01-2016-2016-fort-mcmurray-wildfi.butterflyEffect: Nearly 88,000 people evacuated safely in the largest wildfire evacuation in Alberta's history, aided by convoys, work camps, and the Canadian Red Cross. The fire caused roughly $9 billion in damage, becoming Canada's costliest disaster at the time and prompting nationwide reviews of wildfire preparedness.

evt-05-02-1194-richard-i-of-england.scenario: It is 2 May 1194. King Richard I, newly freed from captivity and planning further campaigns, considers how to strengthen a harbor town on England's south coast that could serve his fleets and trade.
evt-05-02-1194-richard-i-of-england.prompt: What does Richard grant to secure Portsmouth's future?

choices.text: He transfers all naval activity to Southampton instead
He orders the town demolished for supporting his rivals
He grants the charter to Dover rather than Portsmouth
He grants Portsmouth its first royal charter

evt-05-02-1194-richard-i-of-england.butterflyEffect: Richard's charter gave Portsmouth market rights and formal legal status as a town, and it went on to become a key royal dockyard and, for centuries, the home of the Royal Navy. Portsmouth still marks 2 May as its founding day in honor of the charter.

evt-05-02-1559-presbyterianism.scenario: It's May 2, 1559. You watch John Knox step ashore in Scotland after years of exile, determined to challenge the Catholic regency of Mary of Guise and push the Reformation forward.
evt-05-02-1559-presbyterianism.prompt: What does Knox do next to advance the Scottish Reformation?

choices.text: Return immediately to Geneva rather than risk confrontation
Quietly negotiate a private settlement with Mary of Guise
Preach openly to rally Protestant nobles against the Catholic regency
Seek asylum in England instead of remaining in Scotland

evt-05-02-1559-presbyterianism.butterflyEffect: Knox's fiery preaching rallied Protestant nobles into open resistance against the regent, helping trigger the Scottish Reformation Parliament of 1560, which abolished papal authority in Scotland. This established the Protestant Kirk and laid the foundation for Presbyterian church governance that would spread across the English-speaking world.

evt-05-02-1670-royal-charter.scenario: It is 2 May 1670 at the court of King Charles II. A group of English investors, including the king's cousin Prince Rupert, petition for exclusive rights to trade furs across the vast, largely uncharted watershed draining into Hudson Bay.
evt-05-02-1670-royal-charter.prompt: What does the king grant them?

choices.text: A shared monopoly to be split evenly with French traders
A royal charter granting a fur-trading monopoly over Rupert's Land
A charter limited strictly to fishing rights in the bay
A temporary five-year trading license only

evt-05-02-1670-royal-charter.butterflyEffect: The charter created the Hudson's Bay Company and handed it a trading monopoly over Rupert's Land, a territory covering much of modern Canada. The grant shaped centuries of exploration, fur trade rivalry with the French, and dealings with Indigenous nations, and the company still exists today as one of the world's oldest corporations.

evt-05-02-1878-great-mill-disaster.scenario: It is the days after 2 May 1878, and you sit on the board overseeing the rebuilding of the Washburn A Mill in Minneapolis after flour dust ignited and destroyed the world's largest mill, killing eighteen workers.
evt-05-02-1878-great-mill-disaster.prompt: What change do you order for the new mill's design?

choices.text: Move production outside city limits
Ban night-shift work entirely
Install dust-collection and ventilation systems
Replace stone grinding with hand milling

evt-05-02-1878-great-mill-disaster.butterflyEffect: Owner Cadwallader Washburn had engineer William de la Barre design the new mill with dust-collection and ventilation systems to prevent flour dust from accumulating to explosive levels. The improvements became a model for the milling industry, and the site's ruins are preserved today as part of the Mill City Museum.

evt-05-02-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 2 May 1945 in the ruins of Berlin. As General Helmuth Weidling, commander of the city's defense, you know Hitler is dead, Soviet troops have overrun most of the center, and no relief is coming.
evt-05-02-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What do you decide to do with your remaining garrison?

choices.text: Surrender the city and its garrison to Soviet forces
Disguise yourself and flee the city alone
Attempt a mass breakout westward to surrender to the Americans instead
Order the remaining troops to fight to the last man

evt-05-02-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Weidling surrendered Berlin's garrison to Soviet General Vasily Chuikov, ending the Battle of Berlin and organized German resistance in the capital. Germany's unconditional surrender to all Allied powers followed just six days later, on 8 May 1945.

evt-05-02-1964-vietnam-war.scenario: You are a US Navy sailor aboard the escort carrier USNS Card, moored in Saigon harbor on the night of 2 May 1964, unaware that Viet Cong divers have slipped into the water beneath the hull.
evt-05-02-1964-vietnam-war.prompt: What happens to the Card that night?

choices.text: She is struck by an artillery barrage from the shore
She runs aground during a storm and capsizes
She is sunk by explosive charges planted by Viet Cong divers
She is hit by a rocket fired from a passing sampan

evt-05-02-1964-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: Viet Cong commandos planted limpet mines that sank the Card at her moorings, though she was later raised, repaired, and returned to service. The attack exposed the vulnerability of American logistics ships in supposedly secure harbors, reinforcing Washington's sense that the war required greater direct involvement.

evt-05-02-1970-alm-flight-980.scenario: It is the night of 2 May 1970. You are the captain of ALM Flight 980, circling Sint Maarten in driving rain after three failed landing attempts, and your fuel gauges are nearing empty.
evt-05-02-1970-alm-flight-980.prompt: With no runway in reach and fuel almost gone, what should you do?

choices.text: Attempt a fourth landing through the storm
Ditch the aircraft in a controlled manner on the open sea
Divert to a farther airport and hope fuel lasts
Circle and wait for the weather to clear

evt-05-02-1970-alm-flight-980.butterflyEffect: Captain Balsey DeWitt ditched the DC-9 in a controlled water landing 48 km off St. Croix; the fuselage broke apart but 40 of 63 aboard survived. The crash spurred renewed scrutiny of Caribbean diversion-airport fuel planning and overwater ditching procedures.

evt-05-02-1972-sunshine-mine.scenario: It's May 2, 1972, deep in the Sunshine Mine near Kellogg, Idaho. Smoke is pouring through the tunnels from a fire far below, and you are one of the miners trying to stay alive as the air turns toxic.
evt-05-02-1972-sunshine-mine.prompt: What should you do to survive the spreading smoke underground?

choices.text: Barricade yourself in a sealed area with any available fresh air and wait for rescue
Try to blast or dig through rock toward a neighboring mine shaft
Run at full speed through the smoke toward the surface shaft
Crowd into the mine elevator cage immediately regardless of smoke conditions

evt-05-02-1972-sunshine-mine.butterflyEffect: Ninety-one miners died of carbon monoxide poisoning in one of the deadliest US mining disasters. Two men, Ron Flory and Tom Wilkinson, survived by sealing themselves behind a barricade with fresh air and waiting eight days for rescue. The disaster spurred tougher federal mine safety laws, including stronger requirements for self-rescue breathing devices.

evt-05-02-1986-chernobyl-disaster.scenario: It is 2 May 1986, six days after reactor 4 exploded, and you are a Soviet civil defense officer standing in the town of Chernobyl. Radiation readings are climbing, and residents are asking whether they should pack their belongings.
evt-05-02-1986-chernobyl-disaster.prompt: What order do you give the town's residents?

choices.text: Evacuate by bus without delay
Evacuate on foot toward Kyiv
Continue normal work while officials assess risk
Shelter in place and await further tests

evt-05-02-1986-chernobyl-disaster.butterflyEffect: Authorities evacuated the town by bus, adding to the roughly 115,000 people eventually removed from the expanding exclusion zone. The government's delay in admitting the scale of the disaster, only acknowledged publicly after Sweden detected fallout, deepened international distrust of Soviet secrecy and added pressure for the glasnost reforms already underway.

evt-05-02-1989-cold-war.scenario: You are a Hungarian border official in the spring of 1989, as reformist leaders in Budapest weigh how far to loosen the country's ties to Moscow's old order along the frontier with Austria.
evt-05-02-1989-cold-war.prompt: What does Hungary do at its Austrian border on 2 May 1989?

choices.text: Hold a national referendum before taking any action
Reinforce the fence with new minefields
Close the border entirely to all traffic
Begin dismantling the barbed-wire fence along the border

evt-05-02-1989-cold-war.butterflyEffect: Hungarian troops began cutting down the barbed-wire Iron Curtain fence, a symbolic first breach in the Cold War border system. Months later this opening enabled thousands of East Germans to cross into Austria during the Pan-European Picnic, a key step toward the fall of the Berlin Wall that November.

evt-05-02-1995-croatian-war-of-independe.scenario: It's May 2, 1995. Air raid sirens wail over Zagreb as rockets fall near the city center, days after Croatian forces recaptured territory in western Slavonia.
evt-05-02-1995-croatian-war-of-independe.prompt: What prompted Serb forces to launch this rocket attack on Zagreb?

choices.text: Retaliation for Croatia's recent Operation Flash offensive in western Slavonia
An opening move in a new Serb offensive to seize Zagreb outright
Retaliation for the fall of Srebrenica to Bosnian government forces
A response to NATO airstrikes against Bosnian Serb positions

evt-05-02-1995-croatian-war-of-independe.butterflyEffect: Krajina Serb leader Milan Martić ordered cluster-rocket strikes on Zagreb in retaliation for Croatia's Operation Flash, which had recaptured western Slavonia. Seven civilians were killed and roughly 200 wounded, deepening international condemnation of Serb forces and hardening Croatian resolve ahead of the larger Operation Storm offensive later that year.

evt-05-02-1998-european-central-bank.scenario: It's the night of May 2, 1998, in Brussels. EU leaders are locked in tense negotiations to finalize which countries will launch the euro and who will lead the new European Central Bank.
evt-05-02-1998-european-central-bank.prompt: What do EU leaders decide during this all-night Brussels summit?

choices.text: Move the ECB's headquarters from Frankfurt to Brussels
Admit the United Kingdom as a founding member of the euro
Delay the euro's launch by two years to allow more preparation
Confirm the eleven founding eurozone members and appoint Wim Duisenberg as ECB president

evt-05-02-1998-european-central-bank.butterflyEffect: Leaders confirmed eleven countries would launch the euro on January 1, 1999, and resolved a bitter dispute over the ECB presidency by installing Wim Duisenberg with an informal understanding he would step aside partway through his term for Jean-Claude Trichet. The compromise kept the euro project on schedule and set the stage for the eurozone's later expansion.

evt-05-02-1999-mireya-moscoso.scenario: It's May 2, 1999, and the votes are in: you have just become Panama's first female president, inheriting a nation on the verge of a historic transition.
evt-05-02-1999-mireya-moscoso.prompt: What major handover will you preside over before the year is out?

choices.text: The handover of the Panama Canal from the United States to Panama
The replacement of the balboa with a new national currency
Panama's admission into the North American Free Trade Agreement
Panama's first application to join the European Union

evt-05-02-1999-mireya-moscoso.butterflyEffect: On December 31, 1999, Moscoso presided over the transfer of the Panama Canal from the United States to Panama, fulfilling the 1977 Torrijos–Carter Treaties. The handover marked full Panamanian sovereignty over the waterway and became the defining achievement of her presidency.

evt-05-02-1999-1999-panamanian-general-e.scenario: It's May 2, 1999, election day in Panama. As a voter, you must choose between the widow of a beloved former president and the son of a former military strongman running for the top office.
evt-05-02-1999-1999-panamanian-general-e.prompt: Who wins Panama's presidency in this election?

choices.text: Incumbent Ernesto Pérez Balladares wins a second consecutive term
Mireya Moscoso defeats Martín Torrijos to win the presidency
Musician-turned-candidate Rubén Blades wins the presidency
Martín Torrijos wins outright in a landslide victory

evt-05-02-1999-1999-panamanian-general-e.butterflyEffect: Mireya Moscoso defeated Martín Torrijos, son of former ruler Omar Torrijos, to become Panama's first female president. The loss did not end Torrijos's career; he returned to win the presidency himself in 2004, continuing a long rivalry between Panama's leading political dynasties.

evt-05-02-2000-bill-clinton.scenario: It is May 2000. As President, you weigh the Cold War-era policy of Selective Availability, which deliberately degrades GPS accuracy for civilians, against booming demand from businesses and drivers for precise navigation.
evt-05-02-2000-bill-clinton.prompt: What do you decide about civilian GPS access?

choices.text: Turn off Selective Availability, giving civilians full-accuracy GPS
Restrict GPS use to the military only
Keep Selective Availability in place but ease it slightly
Sell exclusive rights to GPS technology to private companies

evt-05-02-2000-bill-clinton.butterflyEffect: Clinton ended Selective Availability, instantly improving civilian GPS accuracy roughly tenfold, from about 100 meters to about 10. The change helped ignite explosive growth in car navigation systems, and later smartphones and location-based apps, over the following decade.

evt-05-02-2008-cyclone-nargis.scenario: You coordinate international aid in the days after Cyclone Nargis strikes the Irrawaddy Delta on 2 May 2008, with hundreds of thousands left homeless and international relief teams ready to fly in.
evt-05-02-2008-cyclone-nargis.prompt: How did Myanmar's ruling military government respond to offers of foreign disaster aid?

choices.text: It declared the disaster a state secret and denied it occurred
It requested that only Chinese aid workers be allowed entry
It restricted and delayed access for foreign aid workers for weeks
It welcomed foreign relief workers immediately and without restriction

evt-05-02-2008-cyclone-nargis.butterflyEffect: The junta severely restricted visas and access for foreign aid workers for weeks, delaying relief to survivors and drawing international condemnation. The crisis eventually forced Myanmar to accept a compromise allowing ASEAN-coordinated aid, a rare crack in its isolationist policy.

evt-05-02-2011-killing-of-osama-bin-lade.scenario: It is shortly before 1 a.m. on 2 May 2011, and you are part of the SEAL Team Six assault force clearing the third floor of the Abbottabad compound. A man matching Osama bin Laden's description appears in a doorway ahead of you.
