evt-05-02-2011-killing-of-osama-bin-lade.prompt: What do you do in that instant?

choices.text: Order him to surrender and wait
Fire immediately
Attempt to capture him alive by force
Retreat and call in an airstrike

evt-05-02-2011-killing-of-osama-bin-lade.butterflyEffect: The SEALs fired, killing bin Laden along with several others in the compound; his body was flown to the Arabian Sea and buried at sea within 24 hours. Al-Qaeda confirmed his death days later and vowed revenge, while the raid became a defining moment of the post-9/11 war on terror and boosted President Obama's public standing.

evt-05-02-2012-pastel.scenario: It is 2 May 2012 at Sotheby's in New York. A pastel version of Edvard Munch's 'The Scream'—one of only four, and the sole one still in private hands—comes up for auction before a packed room of bidders.
evt-05-02-2012-pastel.prompt: What happens when the gavel falls?

choices.text: It sells for just under $120 million, a new record auction price for any artwork
It is donated to a museum just before the auction begins
It fails to meet its reserve and is withdrawn from sale
It sells well under its low estimate amid weak bidding

evt-05-02-2012-pastel.butterflyEffect: The pastel sold for $119.9 million, setting a new world auction record for any work of art at the time, surpassing Picasso's 'Nude, Green Leaves and Bust.' The sale underscored the surging market for trophy artworks among the world's wealthiest collectors in the years that followed.

evt-05-02-2014-russo-ukrainian-war.scenario: It is 2 May 2014 in Odessa. Marchers supporting Ukrainian unity and pro-Russian separatist sympathizers clash in the streets, and the violence spills into the Trade Unions House, which catches fire with people trapped inside.
evt-05-02-2014-russo-ukrainian-war.prompt: What did this violent day come to mean for the wider war?

choices.text: Odessa declared independence from Ukraine within days, as Crimea had
NATO forces intervened directly in Odessa to restore order
The clashes hardened positions on both sides and fed the separatist narrative used to justify the war in the Donbas
Ukraine's government negotiated an immediate ceasefire with Odessa's separatists

evt-05-02-2014-russo-ukrainian-war.butterflyEffect: The deaths in the Odessa fire became one of the most bitterly contested episodes of the conflict, repeatedly invoked by Russian state media to justify backing separatists in the Donbas. The bitterness it sowed helped harden the divide between Kyiv and Russian-speaking regions, a rift that widened into the full-scale invasion of 2022.

evt-05-02-2014-2014-badakhshan-mudslides.scenario: You are among villagers who rush to Argo District, Badakhshan, on 2 May 2014, digging by hand through the mud where homes stood only minutes before.
evt-05-02-2014-2014-badakhshan-mudslides.prompt: What happened to those who rushed in to help the buried survivors?

choices.text: They were evacuated safely before further danger arrived
The mud had already stabilized and posed no further risk
Government helicopters arrived in time to guide them clear
They were struck by a second mudslide that followed the first

evt-05-02-2014-2014-badakhshan-mudslides.butterflyEffect: A second mudslide struck the site while rescuers and villagers were still digging, killing many of them and burying still more victims. The disaster exposed how little warning infrastructure and heavy machinery existed in remote Afghan districts, hampering both the rescue and the eventual count of the dead.

evt-05-03-1491-kingdom-of-kongo.scenario: You are Nzinga a Nkuwu, ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo. Portuguese priests have sailed up the Congo River bearing gifts, sacred texts, and an offer of baptism and alliance with the Portuguese crown.
evt-05-03-1491-kingdom-of-kongo.prompt: What do you decide to do?

choices.text: Delay any decision indefinitely to weigh the risks
Expel the missionaries and reject their religion
Seek an alliance with a rival African kingdom instead
Accept baptism and ally with the Portuguese crown

evt-05-03-1491-kingdom-of-kongo.butterflyEffect: He accepted baptism, taking the name João I, and forged Kongo's first formal ties with a European power. His son Afonso I deepened this Christian, diplomatic relationship with Portugal, a bond that later became the channel through which the transatlantic slave trade reached Central Africa.

evt-05-03-1616-treaty-of-loudun.scenario: You advise Queen Mother Marie de Medici in the spring of 1616. Henry II de Condé's revolt, fueled by rebellious Huguenot princes, has dragged on, and the crown wants it ended without further bloodshed.
evt-05-03-1616-treaty-of-loudun.prompt: What terms does the crown offer Condé to end his rebellion?

choices.text: Execution as a warning to other rebellious princes
A marriage alliance binding him to the royal family
Money, titles, and a place on the royal council in exchange for peace
Exile from France and forfeiture of his estates

evt-05-03-1616-treaty-of-loudun.butterflyEffect: The Treaty of Loudun bought Condé off with money, offices, and a seat on the royal council rather than punishing him. The peace proved fragile: Concini had Condé arrested later that year, reigniting noble unrest until young Louis XIII seized personal power in 1617.

evt-05-03-1791-great-sejm.scenario: It is 3 May 1791 in Warsaw. As a delegate to the Great Sejm, you must decide whether to back a sweeping new constitution that would curb the nobility's veto power and strengthen the central government against foreign interference.
evt-05-03-1791-great-sejm.prompt: What followed the ratification of this constitution?

choices.text: Prussia and Austria praised the reforms and formed an alliance with Poland
Russia intervened militarily, leading to further partitions of Poland
The nobility unanimously embraced the loss of their veto power
The constitution was quietly adopted with no international reaction

evt-05-03-1791-great-sejm.butterflyEffect: The May 3rd Constitution, only the second codified national constitution in the world after the American one, alarmed conservative nobles and neighboring powers. Russia backed the Targowica Confederation against it, leading to war and ultimately the Second and Third Partitions of Poland, which erased the Commonwealth from the map by 1795.

evt-05-03-1855-mercenary.scenario: It is 3 May 1855, and you stand on a San Francisco dock about to board a ship bound for Central America. William Walker, a charismatic adventurer, has recruited you and dozens of other Americans for a private military expedition into Nicaragua.
evt-05-03-1855-mercenary.prompt: What did Walker's band of mercenaries go on to achieve in Nicaragua?

choices.text: They were captured immediately upon landing and imprisoned
They seized power, and Walker made himself president of Nicaragua
They joined the Nicaraguan army as advisors under the existing government
They negotiated a peaceful trade treaty and returned home

evt-05-03-1855-mercenary.butterflyEffect: Walker's filibusters seized control of Nicaragua, and in 1856 he declared himself president. His regime collapsed within a year under pressure from a Central American coalition, and he was eventually captured and executed by firing squad in Honduras in 1860. His exploits became a cautionary tale about American filibustering and stoked regional fears of US expansionism tied to slavery interests.

evt-05-03-1913-raja-harishchandra.scenario: You are director Dadasaheb Phalke in 1913, preparing India's first feature-length film. No respectable actress will accept film work due to the social stigma attached to it, and you still need someone for the female lead.
evt-05-03-1913-raja-harishchandra.prompt: How do you solve your casting problem?

choices.text: Bring in a foreign actress to play the part
Postpone the film until an actress agrees
Cast a man in the female role
Cut the female character from the story entirely

evt-05-03-1913-raja-harishchandra.butterflyEffect: Phalke cast a man, Anna Salunke, in the female role, a common workaround in early Indian cinema. Raja Harishchandra premiered successfully and is widely credited with launching India's feature film industry, the foundation of what would grow into Bollywood.

evt-05-03-1921-government-of-ireland-act.scenario: It's May 3, 1921, and you're a civil servant in Dublin Castle as the Government of Ireland Act 1920 formally comes into force, dividing the island along new administrative lines.
evt-05-03-1921-government-of-ireland-act.prompt: What does the Act actually create on this day?

choices.text: Two separate self-governing entities, Northern Ireland and Southern Ireland, within the UK
A single fully independent Irish state
The outright abolition of Irish Home Rule
A unified Irish Free State covering the whole island

evt-05-03-1921-government-of-ireland-act.butterflyEffect: The Act split the island into Northern Ireland and Southern Ireland, both nominally self-governing within the UK. Southern Ireland's parliament never functioned as intended amid the ongoing War of Independence, and within months the Anglo-Irish Treaty superseded it, leading to the Irish Free State in 1922 while Northern Ireland remained part of the UK, a partition whose consequences still shape Anglo-Irish relations.

evt-05-03-1939-subhas-chandra-bose.scenario: It is May 1939. You are a Congress delegate watching Subhas Chandra Bose, forced out as party president after clashing with Gandhi over strategy toward the British, launch a new political vehicle for the militant left.
evt-05-03-1939-subhas-chandra-bose.prompt: What is Bose's purpose in forming the All India Forward Bloc?

choices.text: To merge Congress with the Muslim League
To negotiate directly with the British for dominion status
To unite left-wing anti-British factions for more radical action
To form an alliance with the Communist Party of India

evt-05-03-1939-subhas-chandra-bose.butterflyEffect: Bose intended the Forward Bloc to unite radical, anti-imperialist factions frustrated with Congress's gradualism. The British interned him soon after war broke out; he escaped India in 1941 and eventually raised the Indian National Army with Axis backing, cementing his legacy as a militant alternative to Gandhian nonviolence.

evt-05-03-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 3 May 1945, days before Germany's surrender. Royal Air Force pilots spot the German liner Cap Arcona anchored in Lübeck Bay, but intelligence about its true cargo is incomplete and contradictory.
evt-05-03-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What should commanders have confirmed before ordering the strike?

choices.text: Whether the ship was registered as a hospital vessel
Whether the ship held retreating troops or evacuated camp prisoners
Whether the ship was carrying looted war matériel
Whether the ship was transporting German gold reserves

evt-05-03-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The RAF sank the Cap Arcona unaware it was crammed with evacuated concentration camp prisoners, killing thousands in one of the war's last and deadliest maritime disasters. It stands as a grim reminder of how fog-of-war intelligence gaps could turn liberation into catastrophe in the conflict's final hours.

evt-05-03-1947-constitution-of-japan.scenario: You sit in Japan's Diet in 1946, reviewing the new constitution drafted under General MacArthur's occupation authorities before it takes effect the following spring.
evt-05-03-1947-constitution-of-japan.prompt: Which sweeping renunciation does the new constitution commit Japan to?

choices.text: The recognition of state Shinto as an official religion
The right to wage war and maintain offensive armed forces
The practice of capital punishment
The granting of universal suffrage

evt-05-03-1947-constitution-of-japan.butterflyEffect: Article 9 renounced Japan's right to wage war and maintain offensive armed forces, a pacifist clause that reshaped postwar Japanese identity. Decades of debate followed over the Self-Defense Forces and whether Japan could ever revise this article to expand its military role.

evt-05-03-1960-off-broadway.scenario: It is 3 May 1960, and you're deciding whether to invest in a small, whimsical musical called The Fantasticks opening in a tiny Off-Broadway theater in Greenwich Village, far from the bright lights of Broadway.
evt-05-03-1960-off-broadway.prompt: What became of this modest little show over the following decades?

choices.text: It was cancelled after a single disastrous performance
It became the longest-running musical in American history
It closed within a month due to poor reviews
It transferred to Broadway and won multiple Tony Awards

evt-05-03-1960-off-broadway.butterflyEffect: The Fantasticks ran continuously for 42 years, closing in 2002 as the longest-running musical in American theater history. Its success proved that intimate, low-budget Off-Broadway productions could rival Broadway's staying power, helping cement Off-Broadway as a lasting home for experimental and enduring theater.

evt-05-03-1963-birmingham-alabama.scenario: It's May 3, 1963, and you're a teenage marcher in Birmingham's Children's Crusade. As you walk toward downtown, Commissioner Bull Connor orders police to turn fire hoses and dogs on you and your friends.
evt-05-03-1963-birmingham-alabama.prompt: What happens next that transforms this local clash into a national crisis?

choices.text: Birmingham's stores desegregate that same afternoon without further protest
The confrontation goes almost unnoticed by national media
Images of the violence broadcast nationwide spark outrage and pressure for civil rights legislation
President Kennedy immediately sends federal troops into the city

evt-05-03-1963-birmingham-alabama.butterflyEffect: Photographs and television footage of children blasted by hoses and bitten by dogs ran worldwide, shocking public opinion and embarrassing the Kennedy administration. Birmingham's business leaders negotiated a desegregation agreement within days, and the images helped push Kennedy to propose the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

evt-05-03-1971-erich-honecker.scenario: It is 3 May 1971 in East Berlin. Moscow has grown tired of Walter Ulbricht's independent streak, and the Socialist Unity Party's Central Committee has just voted to remove him as party leader.
evt-05-03-1971-erich-honecker.prompt: Who does the Committee install as First Secretary, with Brezhnev's backing?

choices.text: Egon Krenz
Erich Honecker
Willi Stoph
Erich Mielke

evt-05-03-1971-erich-honecker.butterflyEffect: Erich Honecker took power that day and led East Germany for the next 18 years, tightening Stasi surveillance and hewing closely to Soviet orthodoxy. His refusal to embrace reform left the GDR isolated as glasnost spread; mass protests forced his resignation in October 1989, weeks before the Berlin Wall fell.

evt-05-03-1999-doppler-on-wheels.scenario: It's May 3, 1999, and you're part of a Doppler on Wheels crew tracking a violent tornado tearing through the Oklahoma City suburbs. Your mobile radar locks onto the vortex as it rips through Bridge Creek and Moore.
evt-05-03-1999-doppler-on-wheels.prompt: What wind speed do you record that becomes the highest ever measured on Earth?

choices.text: 301 mph within the tornado's vortex
150 mph
220 mph
350 mph

evt-05-03-1999-doppler-on-wheels.butterflyEffect: The Doppler on Wheels team measured winds of roughly 301 mph inside the tornado, a figure that still stands as the highest wind speed ever recorded near Earth's surface. The event fed directly into research that helped develop the Enhanced Fujita Scale, adopted in 2007 to better link damage to wind speed.

evt-05-03-2015-2015-curtis-culwell-cente.scenario: It is 3 May 2015 outside the Curtis Culwell Center in Garland, Texas, where a contest featuring cartoons of Muhammad is underway. Two armed men pull up to the security checkpoint and open fire.
evt-05-03-2015-2015-curtis-culwell-cente.prompt: What does the off-duty police officer on scene do?

choices.text: Attempt to negotiate with the attackers first
Engage the gunmen with return fire at once
Wait for a SWAT team to arrive before acting
Evacuate attendees without confronting the gunmen

evt-05-03-2015-2015-curtis-culwell-cente.butterflyEffect: The officer returned fire immediately, killing both attackers before they could enter the building; only a security guard was wounded. The attack, later linked to ISIS-inspired radicalization, intensified American debate over free speech, security at controversial events, and the threat of homegrown lone-wolf terrorism.

evt-05-03-2016-fort-mcmurray.scenario: It's May 3, 2016, and you're a Fort McMurray resident watching wildfire smoke roll toward the city as officials issue a mandatory evacuation order. Flames have already reached the edges of the highway south toward Edmonton.
evt-05-03-2016-fort-mcmurray.prompt: With the southern route blocked by fire, what do most of the 88,000 evacuees actually do?

choices.text: All evacuees drive south to Edmonton immediately without delay
The entire city evacuates by rail
Flee north to oil sands work camps before being moved out days later
Residents are told to shelter in place until the fire passes

evt-05-03-2016-fort-mcmurray.butterflyEffect: With Highway 63 south impassable, tens of thousands fled north to oil sands work camps before being bused or flown out once the road reopened. It became the largest wildfire evacuation in Alberta's history, causing over $9 billion CAD in damage and reshaping Canadian wildfire emergency planning.

evt-05-04-1493-pope-alexander-vi.scenario: It is 1493 in Rome. Spain's monarchs have pressed you, an advisor to Pope Alexander VI, to settle their rival claim with Portugal over the lands Columbus has just reported finding across the Atlantic.
evt-05-04-1493-pope-alexander-vi.prompt: Where does the pope's bull Inter caetera draw the line dividing new lands between the crowns?

choices.text: No line was drawn; lands were shared jointly
Along the equator, splitting north from south
100 leagues west of the Azores and Cape Verde islands
At the Strait of Gibraltar

evt-05-04-1493-pope-alexander-vi.butterflyEffect: The bull set a line 100 leagues west of the Azores and Cape Verde islands, granting Spain rights west of it. Portugal objected and negotiated the Treaty of Tordesillas the next year, shifting the line further west—which is why Brazil ended up Portuguese while the rest of Latin America became Spanish.

evt-05-04-1677-trunajaya-rebellion.scenario: It is May 1677 on the coast near Surabaya. You serve under Cornelis Speelman as his Dutch East India Company fleet moves to break the port city held by Trunajaya's rebels and their Makassarese allies.
evt-05-04-1677-trunajaya-rebellion.prompt: What does Speelman offer Mataram's sultan in exchange for VOC military help against the rebels?

choices.text: Immediate Dutch annexation of the entire sultanate
A one-time cash payment with no lasting claims
Free military aid with no conditions attached
Territorial and trade concessions on Java's north coast

evt-05-04-1677-trunajaya-rebellion.butterflyEffect: The VOC won steep trade monopolies and territorial concessions along Java's coast as payment for its help. This debt bound the Mataram court to the Company for generations, becoming a key step toward full Dutch colonial control of Java in the following century.

evt-05-04-1776-american-revolution.scenario: You sit in the Rhode Island General Assembly on 4 May 1776. Two months before Philadelphia acts, colonists here are already impatient with royal rule and debating whether to break with the Crown on their own.
evt-05-04-1776-american-revolution.prompt: What does the Assembly vote to do?

choices.text: Wait for the Continental Congress to act first
Send a petition begging the King for reconciliation
Renounce allegiance to King George III
Reaffirm loyalty to the Crown

evt-05-04-1776-american-revolution.butterflyEffect: Rhode Island became the first of the Thirteen Colonies to formally renounce allegiance to King George III, doing so nearly two months before the Declaration of Independence. Its early break emboldened other colonies weighing the same step.

evt-05-04-1789-boydell-shakespeare-galle.scenario: It is 4 May 1789 in Pall Mall, London. You are engraver John Boydell, watching investors and critics file past your new gallery of Shakespeare paintings, wondering how you will turn this costly venture into profit.
evt-05-04-1789-boydell-shakespeare-galle.prompt: What is Boydell's plan for making the gallery pay for itself?

choices.text: Sell the paintings directly to King George III's royal collection
Tour the paintings as a travelling exhibition across Europe
Commission engraved prints of the paintings for a subscription series
Stage the paintings as backdrops for London theatre productions

evt-05-04-1789-boydell-shakespeare-galle.butterflyEffect: Boydell commissioned engravers to reproduce the paintings as a lavish subscription print series sold across Europe. The French Revolutionary Wars cut off his continental market, ruining him financially; by 1804 he was forced to sell the whole collection off by lottery, and he died in debt that same year.

evt-05-04-1919-may-fourth-movement.scenario: It's May 4, 1919, and you are a student at Peking University who has just learned that the Paris Peace Conference will let Japan keep Germany's former holdings in Shandong. Thousands of classmates are massing near Tiananmen.
evt-05-04-1919-may-fourth-movement.prompt: What do you and your fellow students do next?

choices.text: March through Beijing's streets in protest, refusing to stay silent
Wait quietly for the delegation in Paris to negotiate a reversal
Return to classes, trusting the government's response
Petition the Japanese embassy for direct talks

evt-05-04-1919-may-fourth-movement.butterflyEffect: The protests spread nationwide as merchants and workers joined strikes, forcing China's delegation to refuse to sign the Treaty of Versailles. The movement fused nationalism with new intellectual currents, boosting vernacular literature and helping seed the Chinese Communist Party two years later.

evt-05-04-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: You are an American carrier pilot over the Coral Sea, scrambling to intercept a Japanese task force screening an invasion fleet bound for Port Moresby, New Guinea.
evt-05-04-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What strategic result followed from this first carrier-versus-carrier battle in history?

choices.text: Japan secured an open path to invade Hawaii
Japan's invasion of Port Moresby was halted
The entire US Pacific Fleet was destroyed
Australia was captured by Japanese forces

evt-05-04-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The Battle of the Coral Sea forced Japan to call off its seaborne invasion of Port Moresby, the first major check on its advance in the Pacific. Damage to Japanese carriers also kept them out of the pivotal Battle of Midway a month later.

evt-05-04-1961-civil-rights-movement.scenario: It is 4 May 1961 in Washington, D.C. You board a Greyhound bus with a small interracial group organized by CORE, headed south to test whether the Supreme Court's ban on segregated interstate travel is actually being obeyed.
evt-05-04-1961-civil-rights-movement.prompt: When you reach segregated waiting rooms in the Deep South, what do the Freedom Riders do?

choices.text: Wait for a police escort before entering any facility
Sit in the back of the waiting room as usual
Avoid the segregated facilities entirely to prevent conflict
Sit together in the 'whites only' sections despite the risk

evt-05-04-1961-civil-rights-movement.butterflyEffect: The riders sat in whites-only areas anyway, and by mid-May mobs firebombed their bus near Anniston and beat riders in Birmingham. The resulting national outrage pushed the Kennedy administration and the Interstate Commerce Commission to finally enforce desegregation of bus terminals later that year.

evt-05-04-1970-vietnam-war.scenario: It is 4 May 1970 on the Kent State University campus. Ohio National Guard troops, deployed after protests over the Cambodian incursion, stand facing a crowd of student demonstrators across the commons.
evt-05-04-1970-vietnam-war.prompt: What did the shootings trigger across the country in the days that followed?

choices.text: The resignation of President Nixon
A new law banning National Guard deployment domestically
An immediate US withdrawal from Vietnam
A nationwide student strike closing hundreds of campuses

evt-05-04-1970-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: The Guard opened fire, killing four students and wounding nine others. The deaths ignited a nationwide student strike that shut down hundreds of college campuses and hardened public opposition to the Vietnam War and to using troops against civilian protesters.

evt-05-04-1973-willis-tower.scenario: It is 4 May 1973, and you're an ironworker watching the final beam hoisted onto the Sears Tower in Chicago, a building already being called the tallest in the world.
evt-05-04-1973-willis-tower.prompt: How long did the Sears Tower hold onto its title as the world's tallest building?

choices.text: Nearly 25 years, until the Petronas Towers surpassed it in 1998
It never actually held the title due to a measurement dispute
Only a few months before a taller building opened in New York
Over 50 years, until the 2010s

evt-05-04-1973-willis-tower.butterflyEffect: The Sears Tower held the title of world's tallest building for nearly 25 years until Malaysia's Petronas Towers surpassed it in 1998. It remained the tallest building in the United States until One World Trade Center overtook it in 2013, and it endures as one of Chicago's most recognizable landmarks, later renamed Willis Tower in 2009.

evt-05-04-1974-manaslu.scenario: You are a member of the Japanese Ladies' Climbing Club, high on Manaslu after years of fundraising and training for an all-female assault on an 8,000-metre peak. The route above camp looks climbable, but the team has never attempted anything this high before.
evt-05-04-1974-manaslu.prompt: What does the team decide to do?

choices.text: Send only male Sherpa support to the top
Abandon the attempt and switch to a lower peak
Push for the summit as a full team
Retreat to base camp and wait for spring

evt-05-04-1974-manaslu.butterflyEffect: On 4 May 1974 the team reached Manaslu's summit, becoming the first all-female expedition to climb an 8,000-metre peak. The achievement proved women could lead major Himalayan expeditions, encouraging a wave of female mountaineers in the decades that followed.

evt-05-04-1982-type-42-destroyer.scenario: It's 4 May 1982, and you are a lookout aboard HMS Sheffield on picket duty off the Falkland Islands when radar detects an incoming contact the ship's systems fail to identify in time.
evt-05-04-1982-type-42-destroyer.prompt: What struck the destroyer moments later?

choices.text: A bomb dropped by an Argentine Skyhawk
Naval gunfire from an Argentine cruiser
A torpedo fired from a submarine
An Argentine Exocet missile launched from a Super Étendard jet

evt-05-04-1982-type-42-destroyer.butterflyEffect: The Exocet strike killed twenty crew and set the ship ablaze, forcing its abandonment; Sheffield became the first Royal Navy ship lost in action since the Second World War. The disaster exposed the vulnerability of modern warships to sea-skimming missiles and reshaped naval air-defence doctrine.

evt-05-04-1988-pepcon-disaster.scenario: It is 4 May 1988 in Henderson, Nevada. Smoke is pouring from the PEPCON chemical plant, which stores tons of ammonium perchlorate rocket fuel oxidizer, and you are among the first responders arriving on scene.
evt-05-04-1988-pepcon-disaster.prompt: What is the safest response to a fire at a plant storing this much oxidizer?

choices.text: Evacuate a wide surrounding area before the fire can detonate the stockpile
Evacuate only the workers inside the plant building
Continue normal operations since the chemical is considered stable
Move in close with water hoses to douse the flames directly

evt-05-04-1988-pepcon-disaster.butterflyEffect: Minutes later, massive explosions leveled the plant, injured hundreds, and were felt as far as Las Vegas. Because PEPCON supplied much of the country's ammonium perchlorate for solid rocket boosters, the blast disrupted NASA's shuttle program and pushed new safety regulations for storing oxidizing chemicals.

evt-05-04-1989-iran-contra-affair.scenario: It is 4 May 1989 in a Washington, D.C. courtroom. You are Oliver North, former National Security Council aide, awaiting the jury's verdict after your trial over the Iran-Contra affair.
evt-05-04-1989-iran-contra-affair.prompt: What happens to North's felony convictions after this verdict?

choices.text: He is acquitted on retrial after a hung jury
They are overturned on appeal over his immunized testimony
President Reagan issues him a full pardon before sentencing
They are upheld and he serves a lengthy prison sentence

evt-05-04-1989-iran-contra-affair.butterflyEffect: North was convicted on three of twelve counts, but in 1990 a federal appeals court vacated the convictions, ruling his immunized congressional testimony may have tainted the trial evidence. Prosecutors dropped the remaining charges in 1991, and North never served prison time.

evt-05-04-1989-space-shuttle-atlantis.scenario: You are a mission specialist aboard Space Shuttle Atlantis moments before launch on STS-30, with the Magellan probe secured in the payload bay for a journey to Venus.
evt-05-04-1989-space-shuttle-atlantis.prompt: What is Magellan's mission once it is deployed and reaches Venus?

choices.text: Map Venus's surface using radar
Fly past Jupiter en route to the outer planets
Land and transmit images from the surface
Orbit the Sun measuring solar wind

evt-05-04-1989-space-shuttle-atlantis.butterflyEffect: Magellan became the first spacecraft to map Venus's surface in detail using synthetic aperture radar, piercing the planet's thick clouds to reveal volcanic plains, craters, and mountains. Its data reshaped scientific understanding of Venusian geology for decades.

evt-05-04-1990-latvia.scenario: It is 4 May 1990, and you sit among the deputies of Latvia's Supreme Council, casting a vote to declare the restoration of Latvian independence after decades of Soviet rule.
evt-05-04-1990-latvia.prompt: What happened in the months immediately following this declaration?

choices.text: The declaration was reversed by a popular vote later that year
The Soviet Union immediately granted full recognition without objection
Latvia was granted independence peacefully within weeks by treaty
The Soviet Union rejected it, leading to a tense standoff and troop confrontations in Riga

evt-05-04-1990-latvia.butterflyEffect: Moscow refused to recognize the declaration, and tensions escalated into the January 1991 crisis, when Soviet troops stormed key buildings in Riga and barricades went up across the city. Latvia's independence was finally recognized internationally after the failed Soviet coup in August 1991, restoring the statehood it had lost in 1940.

evt-05-04-1994-prime-minister.scenario: It's May 4, 1994, in Cairo, and you are an aide to PLO leader Yasser Arafat as he prepares to sign an agreement with Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin implementing the Oslo Accords.
evt-05-04-1994-prime-minister.prompt: What did the agreement actually hand over to the newly formed Palestinian Authority?

choices.text: Full sovereignty over the entire West Bank
Limited self-rule over Gaza and Jericho
Administration of all Israeli-occupied territories
Control of East Jerusalem

evt-05-04-1994-prime-minister.butterflyEffect: The Cairo Agreement gave the Palestinian Authority its first territorial foothold, launching a phased process of self-government. Rabin and Arafat's cooperation deepened over the next year, but the peace process fractured after Rabin's assassination in November 1995.

evt-05-04-2000-ken-livingstone.scenario: It's May 4, 2000, and you are a Londoner watching results come in from the city's first-ever mayoral election, where independent candidate Ken Livingstone—expelled from Labour for running against its official candidate—has just triumphed.
evt-05-04-2000-ken-livingstone.prompt: What happened as a result of Livingstone's independent win?

choices.text: He was readmitted to Labour before the vote
He was barred from taking office by the Labour Party
The election result was annulled and rerun
He took office as London's first directly elected mayor

evt-05-04-2000-ken-livingstone.butterflyEffect: Livingstone governed London as an independent before rejoining Labour in 2004, introducing the congestion charge and shaping the city's transport policy and Olympic bid. The mayoralty became a powerful platform later used by Boris Johnson to build a national profile.

evt-05-04-2007-greensburg-kansas.scenario: It is the evening of 4 May 2007. Sirens are wailing over Greensburg, Kansas, and radio warns of a massive tornado bearing down on the town. You have only minutes before it arrives.
evt-05-04-2007-greensburg-kansas.prompt: What should you do to survive the approaching tornado?

choices.text: Stand in an open field to watch its path
Shelter in a mobile home away from windows
Get into a basement or storm shelter below ground
Drive away from town to outrun the storm

evt-05-04-2007-greensburg-kansas.butterflyEffect: The EF5 tornado destroyed roughly 95% of Greensburg and killed 11 people that night. In the aftermath, the town chose to rebuild as one of the greenest communities in America, adopting LEED-platinum standards and wind power for its public buildings.

evt-05-04-2019-w-series-championship.scenario: It's May 4, 2019, at Hockenheim, and you are a young racing driver on the grid for the very first race of the all-female W Series, created to give women a dedicated path into single-seater motorsport.
evt-05-04-2019-w-series-championship.prompt: Who dominated the inaugural W Series season that followed?

choices.text: Beitske Visser
Susie Wolff
Jamie Chadwick
Alice Powell

evt-05-04-2019-w-series-championship.butterflyEffect: Jamie Chadwick won that first race and went on to claim all three W Series titles before the championship folded in 2022. Her success became a springboard into other categories, including Indy NXT, and W Series' rise and fall fuelled ongoing debate over how best to support women in top-level motorsport.

evt-05-05-1860-giuseppe-garibaldi.scenario: It is 5 May 1860, and you stand at the port of Quarto near Genoa. Giuseppe Garibaldi is assembling around a thousand volunteers to sail for Sicily and challenge the Bourbon Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
evt-05-05-1860-giuseppe-garibaldi.prompt: Do you board the ships with the Redshirts?

choices.text: Wait in Genoa for news before committing
Board the ships and join Garibaldi's expedition to Sicily
Petition Cavour to stop the expedition as reckless
Join the Bourbon forces defending Sicily instead

evt-05-05-1860-giuseppe-garibaldi.butterflyEffect: Those who joined became the famous Expedition of the Thousand, sailing to Sicily and sparking an uprising that toppled Bourbon rule across southern Italy within months. Garibaldi's conquest handed the south to King Victor Emmanuel II, decisively advancing the unification of Italy.

evt-05-05-1891-carnegie-hall.scenario: It is opening night, 5 May 1891, in Andrew Carnegie's new Manhattan concert hall. You are in the audience as a celebrated foreign guest takes the podium for part of the gala program.
evt-05-05-1891-carnegie-hall.prompt: Which composer conducts his own work as the gala's centerpiece?

choices.text: Antonín Dvořák
Giuseppe Verdi
Pyotr Tchaikovsky
Johannes Brahms

evt-05-05-1891-carnegie-hall.butterflyEffect: Tchaikovsky, on his only visit to the United States, conducted his Marche Solennelle that night. The visit gave the fledgling hall instant international prestige and helped cement New York's rise as a world center for classical music.

evt-05-05-1904-pitcher.scenario: It is 5 May 1904 at Boston's Huntington Avenue Grounds. You watch Cy Young take the mound for the Boston Americans against the Philadelphia Athletics, retiring batter after batter without a single one reaching base.
evt-05-05-1904-pitcher.prompt: What milestone does Young's performance mark in major league history?

choices.text: The first no-hitter in baseball history
The first game with electric lighting
The first game broadcast on radio
The first perfect game of the modern era

evt-05-05-1904-pitcher.butterflyEffect: It was the first perfect game of baseball's modern era, thrown after the mound distance and foul-strike rules were standardized. No pitcher threw another until Addie Joss in 1908, and Young's feat became a benchmark cited whenever a new perfect game is thrown.

evt-05-05-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 5 May 1945, and you are a German Wehrmacht officer inside Castle Itter in Austria. SS troops are closing in to execute the French VIP prisoners held here, and the only reinforcements nearby wear American uniforms.
evt-05-05-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What do you do as the SS assault begins?

choices.text: Refuse to fight, since Germany has not yet surrendered
Flee the castle before the SS arrive
Join the Americans and French prisoners in defending the castle against the SS
Surrender the prisoners to the SS to save your own unit

evt-05-05-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: German Wehrmacht soldiers and US troops fought together against the SS in the unusual Battle for Castle Itter, successfully defending French prisoners including two former prime ministers. It remains one of the war's few documented instances of American and German forces as allies in combat.

evt-05-05-1945-mauthausen-concentration-.scenario: It is 5 May 1945. Your American armored unit has just reached the gates of Mauthausen concentration camp above the Austrian town, and the SS guards have already fled into the surrounding hills.
evt-05-05-1945-mauthausen-concentration-.prompt: What is your unit's immediate priority upon entering the camp?

choices.text: Pursue the fleeing SS guards into the hills
Secure the camp and organize emergency medical care for survivors
Wait for higher command before entering the camp at all
Hand control of the camp to local Austrian authorities

evt-05-05-1945-mauthausen-concentration-.butterflyEffect: US troops liberated Mauthausen and its subcamps, uncovering the full scale of the suffering inflicted there since 1938. The liberation became key evidence in postwar war crimes trials and cemented Mauthausen's place among the sites central to Holocaust memory and education.

evt-05-05-1961-project-mercury.scenario: It is 5 May 1961 at Cape Canaveral. You are strapped into the Freedom 7 capsule atop a Redstone rocket, waiting for the countdown that will decide whether America answers the Soviet lead in the space race.
evt-05-05-1961-project-mercury.prompt: What does Alan Shepard's flight achieve that morning?

choices.text: First American to orbit Earth
First uncrewed Mercury test flight
First American spacewalk
First American in space

evt-05-05-1961-project-mercury.butterflyEffect: Shepard's fifteen-minute suborbital hop made him the first American in space, splashing down safely in the Atlantic. The success gave Kennedy the political confidence to commit, weeks later, to landing a man on the Moon by decade's end.

evt-05-05-1980-special-air-service.scenario: It is 5 May 1980, day six of the siege at the Iranian embassy in London. Gunmen have just killed a hostage and thrown his body outside, and you are watching live television as black-clad figures appear on the embassy balcony.
evt-05-05-1980-special-air-service.prompt: What does the SAS do next?

choices.text: Negotiate for the release of more hostages before acting
Storm the building in a rapid assault to end the siege
Wait for the gunmen to surrender peacefully
Withdraw and let police handle the situation

evt-05-05-1980-special-air-service.butterflyEffect: The SAS launched Operation Nimrod, storming the embassy and killing five of the six gunmen while rescuing the remaining hostages, all broadcast live on television. The operation made the previously secretive SAS a household name and set the template for modern hostage-rescue tactics worldwide.

evt-05-05-1980-iranian-embassy-siege.scenario: It is 5 May 1980, and you are part of the SAS assault team positioned on the roof of the Iranian embassy in South Kensington. Six days of siege have ended in a hostage's murder, and the order to go in has just been given.
evt-05-05-1980-iranian-embassy-siege.prompt: How does the SAS team enter the building to end the siege?

choices.text: They negotiate a peaceful surrender through the front door
They wait for the gunmen to run out of supplies
They tunnel in from the building next door
They abseil from the roof and blast through windows to storm the rooms

evt-05-05-1980-iranian-embassy-siege.butterflyEffect: Troopers abseiled from the roof and blasted through windows with explosives and stun grenades, storming the building live on television in under twenty minutes. The operation's success made the SAS internationally famous almost overnight and became a model for hostage-rescue units worldwide.

evt-05-05-1981-1981-irish-hunger-strike.scenario: It is 5 May 1981 in the H-Blocks of Long Kesh prison. Word spreads through the wings that Bobby Sands has died after 66 days without food, and you and the other blanket protesters must decide how to respond.
evt-05-05-1981-1981-irish-hunger-strike.prompt: What do the remaining republican hunger strikers do next?

choices.text: They end the strike immediately out of grief
They continue the strike, and more prisoners join it
They are all transferred to prisons in England
They accept an immediate British offer of full political status

evt-05-05-1981-1981-irish-hunger-strike.butterflyEffect: The protest continued, and nine more prisoners died before the strike was called off in October 1981. Sands's death, and his election as an MP weeks earlier, pushed Sinn Féin toward electoral politics, reshaping republican strategy for decades.

evt-05-05-1987-iran-contra-affair.scenario: It is 5 May 1987, and you are a member of Congress on the joint committee opening televised hearings into secret arms sales to Iran and funding for Nicaraguan Contras. Cameras fill the hearing room.
evt-05-05-1987-iran-contra-affair.prompt: How do you approach questioning the Reagan administration officials involved?

choices.text: Grant witnesses immunity to compel their testimony despite risks to prosecution
Close the hearings to the public and press entirely
Focus solely on Contra funding and ignore the Iran arms sales
Refuse to call any administration officials to testify

evt-05-05-1987-iran-contra-affair.butterflyEffect: The hearings culminated in Oliver North's dramatic testimony, given under a grant of limited immunity, which exposed the covert operation while complicating later prosecutions. The scandal damaged Reagan's final years in office and left lasting questions about executive power and congressional oversight of covert action.

evt-05-05-1992-twenty-seventh-amendment-.scenario: It is the early 1990s, and you are tracking a grassroots campaign that began with a college student's forgotten term paper on an amendment James Madison proposed back in 1789, still short of ratification after two centuries.
evt-05-05-1992-twenty-seventh-amendment-.prompt: What does the campaign achieve as state legislatures take up the old amendment?

choices.text: It gets the amendment ratified, completing the process after 202 years
It results in a brand-new amendment replacing the old proposal
It fails, and the amendment is formally withdrawn by Congress
It leads the Supreme Court to rule the old proposal void

evt-05-05-1992-twenty-seventh-amendment-.butterflyEffect: Enough states ratified the amendment on congressional pay by May 1992, making it the 27th Amendment more than 202 years after it was first proposed. Its success proved that amendments without a ratification deadline can still be adopted centuries later, prompting Congress afterward to routinely attach time limits to new proposals.

evt-05-05-1994-bishkek-protocol.scenario: It is May 1994 in Bishkek, and you are among the diplomats from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Artsakh, and Russia finalizing a document meant to stop years of fighting over Nagorno-Karabakh.
evt-05-05-1994-bishkek-protocol.prompt: What does the protocol achieve when it takes effect?

choices.text: It transfers Nagorno-Karabakh's control to a UN administration
It creates a ceasefire that freezes the conflict along existing lines
It ends in immediate renewed fighting within days
It establishes a lasting peace treaty with new permanent borders

evt-05-05-1994-bishkek-protocol.butterflyEffect: The Bishkek Protocol produced a ceasefire that halted large-scale fighting and froze the front lines roughly where they stood. That frozen conflict lasted over two decades, with only sporadic clashes, until full-scale war broke out again in 2020.

evt-05-05-2006-sudan.scenario: It is May 2006 in Abuja. You lead one faction of the fractured Sudan Liberation Army, weighing whether to sign a peace deal with Khartoum that the movement's other commanders are refusing to accept.
evt-05-05-2006-sudan.prompt: Which SLA faction breaks ranks and signs the Darfur Peace Agreement with the government?

choices.text: Abdul Wahid al-Nur's faction
The Justice and Equality Movement
All rebel factions signed together
Minni Minnawi's faction

evt-05-05-2006-sudan.butterflyEffect: Minni Minnawi's faction signed while rival commanders Abdul Wahid al-Nur and the Justice and Equality Movement rejected the deal. The split fractured the rebellion further and the agreement largely collapsed, prolonging the conflict in Darfur for years afterward.

evt-05-05-2023-world-health-organization.scenario: It is 5 May 2023, and you sit on the WHO's Emergency Committee reviewing over three years of pandemic data. Case numbers and deaths have fallen sharply, and the Director-General is weighing whether to lift the highest level of alert.
evt-05-05-2023-world-health-organization.prompt: What does the WHO announce about COVID-19's international emergency status?

choices.text: It declares the virus fully eradicated worldwide
It ends the Public Health Emergency of International Concern status
It downgrades the emergency to a regional-only concern
It extends the emergency for another two years

evt-05-05-2023-world-health-organization.butterflyEffect: The WHO ended the Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) designation, though it stressed the pandemic itself was not over. Countries began winding down emergency funding and surveillance programs, shifting COVID-19 management into routine long-term public health systems.

evt-05-06-1536-spanish-conquest-of-the-i.scenario: It is 6 May 1536 near Cuzco. You march with Sapa Inca Manco Inca Yupanqui's army, which has risen against the small Spanish garrison holding the former Inca capital.
evt-05-06-1536-spanish-conquest-of-the-i.prompt: What did Manco Inca's forces do next?

choices.text: Withdraw without engaging the garrison
Negotiate an immediate truce with Pizarro
Ally with the Spanish against rival Inca factions
Besiege the city for close to a year

evt-05-06-1536-spanish-conquest-of-the-i.butterflyEffect: Manco Inca's army besieged Cuzco for nearly a year, at times nearly overrunning the Spanish garrison, but ultimately failed to retake the city. He retreated to Vilcabamba and founded the Neo-Inca State, which held out against Spanish rule until 1572.

evt-05-06-1801-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: It is May 6, 1801, off Barcelona, and you command HMS Speedy, a tiny 14-gun brig facing the Spanish frigate El Gamo, which carries more than double your guns and crew.
evt-05-06-1801-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What daring tactic do you use to seize the much larger ship?

choices.text: Ram her broadside to disable her rudder
Sail hull-to-hull against her and storm aboard with almost the whole crew
Retreat and lure the frigate onto hidden rocks
Bombard from long range until she strikes her colors

evt-05-06-1801-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: Lord Thomas Cochrane closed alongside El Gamo so tightly that her heavier guns fired harmlessly overhead, then led nearly his entire crew aboard in a boarding assault, capturing the frigate. The victory made Cochrane's reputation as a brilliant, daring commander, later inspiring fictional naval heroes such as Jack Aubrey in Patrick O'Brian's novels.

evt-05-06-1882-thomas-henry-burke-civil-.scenario: You are walking through Phoenix Park in Dublin on the evening of 6 May 1882, alongside the newly arrived Chief Secretary for Ireland, Lord Frederick Cavendish, and the Permanent Under-Secretary, Thomas Henry Burke.
evt-05-06-1882-thomas-henry-burke-civil-.prompt: What happens to Cavendish and Burke moments later on this walk?

choices.text: They are arrested by British troops for corruption
They are shot by Fenian gunmen
They escape the park unharmed
They are stabbed to death by the Irish National Invincibles

evt-05-06-1882-thomas-henry-burke-civil-.butterflyEffect: Members of the Irish National Invincibles stabbed both men to death with surgical knives, shocking Gladstone's government. The killings ended the fragile Kilmainham conciliation with Parnell and led to a harsh new Crimes Act, while several Invincibles were later hanged for the murders.

evt-05-06-1882-chester-a-arthur.scenario: It is 6 May 1882 in Washington. A bill restricting Chinese immigration sits on your desk as president, backed by strong support from western states amid rising anti-Chinese sentiment.
evt-05-06-1882-chester-a-arthur.prompt: What did President Chester A. Arthur do with the bill?

choices.text: Veto it as unconstitutional
Send it back demanding it apply only to merchants
Sign it, suspending Chinese laborer immigration for ten years
Sign a version granting Chinese immigrants a path to citizenship

evt-05-06-1882-chester-a-arthur.butterflyEffect: Arthur signed the Chinese Exclusion Act, suspending immigration of Chinese laborers for ten years, the first U.S. law to bar immigration by nationality. It was repeatedly renewed and expanded, remaining in force until its repeal in 1943, and set a precedent for later racially restrictive immigration policy.

evt-05-06-1930-vita-sackville-west.scenario: You are touring a semi-ruined Elizabethan estate in the Kentish countryside in the spring of 1930 with your husband, looking past a crumbling brick tower toward overgrown fields choked with weeds.
evt-05-06-1930-vita-sackville-west.prompt: What do you decide to do with this derelict property?

choices.text: Walk away, judging it beyond repair
Purchase a cottage in Sussex instead
Lease the ruins to a local farmer
Buy it and begin restoring the estate and grounds

evt-05-06-1930-vita-sackville-west.butterflyEffect: Vita Sackville-West and Harold Nicolson bought Sissinghurst Castle that year, and over decades transformed its ruins into one of England's most celebrated gardens. It later passed to the National Trust and remains a major literary and horticultural pilgrimage site.

evt-05-06-1937-hindenburg-disaster.scenario: It is May 6, 1937, and you are a radio reporter at Naval Air Station Lakehurst, microphone in hand, describing the giant German airship as it glides toward its mooring mast before an audience of photographers and spectators.
evt-05-06-1937-hindenburg-disaster.prompt: What happens moments later as the Hindenburg tries to dock?

choices.text: It explodes mid-air far out over the Atlantic
A sudden storm forces it to abort and fly on
It lands safely and passengers disembark calmly
It catches fire and is destroyed within seconds

evt-05-06-1937-hindenburg-disaster.butterflyEffect: The hydrogen-filled airship caught fire and was destroyed in under a minute, killing 36 people. Herbert Morrison's emotional broadcast and newsreel footage shattered public trust in rigid airships almost overnight, effectively ending the era of passenger airship travel and clearing the way for airplanes to dominate long-distance transport.

evt-05-06-1941-bob-hope.scenario: It's May 6, 1941, and you're a serviceman at March Field, an Army airbase in California, watching a young radio comedian take the stage for a broadcast aimed at troops rather than his usual civilian audience.
evt-05-06-1941-bob-hope.prompt: Who is this comedian, about to begin his decades-long partnership with the USO?

choices.text: George Burns
Milton Berle
Bob Hope
Jack Benny

evt-05-06-1941-bob-hope.butterflyEffect: This broadcast marked Bob Hope's first USO performance, launching a partnership that would define his career. He went on to headline USO tours through WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and beyond, becoming the entertainment world's most enduring symbol of support for American troops overseas.

evt-05-06-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 6 May 1942 on Corregidor Island. Your American and Filipino troops have endured weeks of siege, are out of food and ammunition, and Japanese forces have just landed on the island in overwhelming numbers.
evt-05-06-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What did the American commander, Lt. Gen. Jonathan Wainwright, ultimately do?

choices.text: Surrender all remaining forces to Japan
Evacuate the entire garrison by submarine
Order a final counterattack to break the siege
Disperse the men into guerrilla units in the jungle

evt-05-06-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Wainwright surrendered all U.S. and Filipino forces in the Philippines, the largest American surrender in history. Tens of thousands of prisoners endured brutal captivity, and the fall of the Philippines marked the last major Allied defeat before the tide of the Pacific War began to turn.

evt-05-06-1954-oxford.scenario: It's May 6, 1954, on Oxford's Iffley Road track, and you watch a young medical student named Roger Bannister line up for a mile race that experts have long insisted cannot be run in under four minutes.
evt-05-06-1954-oxford.prompt: What time will Bannister clock, shattering a barrier once thought physically impossible?

choices.text: 4 minutes 0.9 seconds
4 minutes 2.1 seconds
3 minutes 59.4 seconds
3 minutes 58.8 seconds

evt-05-06-1954-oxford.butterflyEffect: Bannister finished in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds, becoming the first man to break the four-minute mile. Remarkably, his record lasted only 46 days before Australian John Landy ran faster, and the feat came to symbolize how quickly perceived human limits can fall once someone proves them wrong.

evt-05-06-1991-time-magazine.scenario: It is 6 May 1991. You are a reader opening the new issue of Time, whose cover investigation by Richard Behar promises to expose the inner workings of the Church of Scientology.
evt-05-06-1991-time-magazine.prompt: What did the article claim about Scientology?

choices.text: It focused on a celebrity divorce unrelated to the church
It exposed Scientology as a ruthless financial and legal machine preying on members
It examined Time's own corporate finances
It praised Scientology's charitable outreach programs

evt-05-06-1991-time-magazine.butterflyEffect: The article, titled "The Thriving Cult of Greed and Power," accused Scientology of financial fraud, harassment of critics, and predatory recruitment. Scientology sued Time for libel and lost, and the piece became a landmark in decades of scrutiny over the organization's tax-exempt status and tactics.

evt-05-06-1998-steve-jobs.scenario: You are a tech journalist seated in Apple's Cupertino auditorium on May 6, 1998, as Steve Jobs pulls a sheet off a strange, egg-shaped, translucent blue computer unlike anything on the market.
evt-05-06-1998-steve-jobs.prompt: What does this new machine signal for Apple's future?

choices.text: The launch of the iMac, sparking Apple's design-led revival
A costly flop that nearly bankrupts the company
A rebranding of NeXT's old hardware line
Apple's final desktop before exiting the computer business

evt-05-06-1998-steve-jobs.butterflyEffect: The iMac G3 became an instant commercial hit, praised for its bold design and simplicity, and is widely credited with rescuing Apple from near-collapse. It cemented Jobs's partnership with designer Jony Ive, setting the stylistic and strategic foundation that would later produce the iPod, iPhone, and iPad.

evt-05-06-1998-kerry-wood.scenario: It is 6 May 1998 at Wrigley Field. You are the Cubs' 20-year-old rookie pitcher, and the Houston Astros' lineup has been swinging through your fastball all afternoon.
evt-05-06-1998-kerry-wood.prompt: What did Kerry Wood accomplish by the final out?

choices.text: He threw a perfect game
He was pulled early with a sore arm
He struck out 20 batters, tying the MLB record
He lost the no-hitter in the ninth inning

evt-05-06-1998-kerry-wood.butterflyEffect: Wood struck out 20 batters in a one-hit shutout, tying the major-league single-game record and earning the nickname "Kid K." The performance launched his Rookie of the Year season, though injuries would plague much of his career afterward.

evt-05-06-1999-devolution.scenario: It's May 6, 1999, and you join long queues of voters across Scotland and Wales, casting your ballot for entirely new parliamentary bodies that haven't existed in centuries.
evt-05-06-1999-devolution.prompt: What voting system are you using to elect these new devolved bodies?

choices.text: The additional member system, combining constituency seats with proportional list seats
Pure first-past-the-post, identical to Westminster elections
Single transferable vote across multi-member constituencies
A closed party-list system with no constituency element

evt-05-06-1999-devolution.butterflyEffect: The additional member system delivered a mixed proportional result, denying Labour an outright majority in either body and forcing coalition governments from the start. This marked the revival of a Scottish Parliament for the first time since 1707 and Wales's first legislative assembly, setting in motion decades of expanding devolved powers and renewed debate over the future shape of the United Kingdom.

evt-05-06-2001-syria.scenario: You stand among Pope John Paul II's entourage in Damascus on May 6, 2001, waiting to step through the doors of the Umayyad Mosque, a shrine some believe holds relics of John the Baptist.
evt-05-06-2001-syria.prompt: What historic first does the Pope achieve by entering?

choices.text: First pope to deliver a sermon in Arabic
First pope to enter and pray inside a mosque
First pope to convert Muslim worshippers on the spot
First pope to ever set foot in the Middle East

evt-05-06-2001-syria.butterflyEffect: John Paul II became the first pope in history to set foot inside a mosque, removing his shoes as a sign of respect. The visit was hailed as a landmark in Catholic-Muslim dialogue and part of his broader interfaith outreach, though tensions between the West and the Islamic world would soon deepen sharply after the September 11 attacks later that year.

evt-05-06-2002-pim-fortuyn.scenario: You are a reporter outside a radio studio in Hilversum on 6 May 2002, watching the populist leader Pim Fortuyn walk to his car after an interview, just nine days before the Dutch general election.
evt-05-06-2002-pim-fortuyn.prompt: What happens to Fortuyn in the car park moments later?

choices.text: He wins a landslide re-election
He is arrested for incitement
He is assassinated by an animal rights activist
He flees the country in disgrace

evt-05-06-2002-pim-fortuyn.butterflyEffect: Animal rights activist Volkert van der Graaf shot Fortuyn dead, the first political assassination in the Netherlands in nearly four centuries. The shock vote propelled his Pim Fortuyn List to a stunning second-place finish in the election held days later, reshaping Dutch politics for years.

evt-05-06-2010-dow-jones-industrial-aver.scenario: It's 2:32pm on Wall Street, May 6, 2010, and you watch in disbelief as the Dow Jones plunges nearly 1,000 points in minutes, prices flickering wildly across every screen on the trading floor.
evt-05-06-2010-dow-jones-industrial-aver.prompt: What triggered this unprecedented intraday plunge, later dubbed the 'Flash Crash'?

choices.text: A rumored terrorist attack on the New York Stock Exchange
A large mutual fund's automated sell order interacting with high-frequency algorithms
An emergency Federal Reserve interest rate announcement
The sudden collapse of a major investment bank

evt-05-06-2010-dow-jones-industrial-aver.butterflyEffect: Investigators traced the crash to a massive automated sell order by a mutual fund, amplified by high-frequency trading algorithms that fed on each other's panic selling. The market recovered within minutes, but regulators introduced new circuit-breaker rules to automatically halt trading during extreme volatility, reshaping how modern markets guard against algorithmic chaos.

evt-05-06-2013-cleveland.scenario: It is May 6, 2013, and after nearly a decade held captive in a locked Cleveland house, you notice the front door left slightly open while your captor is away.
evt-05-06-2013-cleveland.prompt: What do you do to finally get free?

choices.text: Slip out through a back window unnoticed at night
Break through the storm door and call for help from neighbors
Signal to a passing mail carrier through a locked window
Wait quietly for the captor to release her voluntarily

evt-05-06-2013-cleveland.butterflyEffect: Amanda Berry broke through a locked storm door and, with a neighbor's help, called 911 from a nearby house. Police responded within minutes, rescuing Gina DeJesus and Michelle Knight from the same home that day. Ariel Castro was arrested and later pleaded guilty to hundreds of charges before taking his own life in prison.

evt-05-06-2023-charles-iii.scenario: You sit in the congregation at Westminster Abbey on 6 May 2023, coronation service booklet in hand, as the ceremony includes a moment inviting everyone watching, not just the assembled peers, to take part directly.
evt-05-06-2023-charles-iii.prompt: What new ritual element lets ordinary viewers participate in this coronation?

choices.text: A public referendum confirming the King beforehand
The entire service conducted in Welsh for inclusivity
The Homage of the People, inviting all watching to swear allegiance aloud
The crown being passed through the congregation to touch

evt-05-06-2023-charles-iii.butterflyEffect: The service introduced a 'Homage of the People,' inviting viewers at home to declare allegiance aloud alongside the peers, a first in British coronation history. The innovation drew criticism from republican campaigners as pressuring compulsory loyalty, fuelling fresh debate over the monarchy's modern role.

evt-05-07-1487-granada-war.scenario: It is the spring of 1487, and you are among the defenders of Málaga as Castilian and Aragonese forces tighten their siege around the city's walls, cutting off food and hope of relief.
evt-05-07-1487-granada-war.prompt: Do the defenders hold out or seek terms early?

choices.text: Negotiate a truce splitting the city into two zones
Hold out for months hoping for relief or better terms
Break out and abandon the city under cover of night
Surrender immediately to secure lenient terms

evt-05-07-1487-granada-war.butterflyEffect: Málaga held out for months before starving into surrender. Because the city had resisted so long, the Catholic Monarchs punished it harshly, enslaving much of the population rather than granting the lenient terms other conquered towns received.

evt-05-07-1544-rough-wooing.scenario: It is May 1544, and the Earl of Hertford's English fleet has landed at Leith. Edinburgh's town lies undefended below the castle, and Hertford's soldiers are already torching the streets, but the castle garrison still commands the high ground with its guns.
evt-05-07-1544-rough-wooing.prompt: As commander of Edinburgh Castle, what should you do as the English burn the town?

choices.text: Sally out with the garrison to meet Hertford in open battle
Surrender the castle to spare the burning town
Offer to hand over Mary, Queen of Scots, in exchange for peace
Hold the castle and let its guns keep the English at bay

evt-05-07-1544-rough-wooing.butterflyEffect: The garrison held the castle, and its cannon fire kept Hertford's men from ever taking it, though much of the town and Holyrood were burned. The failed raid did not force the marriage treaty England wanted; instead it pushed Scotland closer to France, a drift that eventually saw the young Mary, Queen of Scots betrothed to the French Dauphin and sent to France in 1548.

evt-05-07-1697-tre-kronor-castle.scenario: It's the night of 7 May 1697, and you're the royal librarian inside Stockholm's Tre Kronor castle as flames tear through the upper floors, threatening centuries of manuscripts and royal records.
evt-05-07-1697-tre-kronor-castle.prompt: With the fire spreading fast, what is your priority?

choices.text: Focus solely on rescuing the crown jewels
Try to extinguish the fire with the castle's own water supply first
Throw books and manuscripts from the library windows to save them
Evacuate only the royal family's portraits

evt-05-07-1697-tre-kronor-castle.butterflyEffect: Quick action by the library staff saved much of the royal collection, even as large parts of the castle's archives and art were lost forever. The disaster cleared the site for architect Nicodemus Tessin the Younger to design the Stockholm Palace that still stands there today, a project that took decades to finish.

evt-05-07-1794-french-revolution.scenario: It is 7 May 1794 in the National Convention. Robespierre has just proposed a decree replacing the state's official atheism with a new civic religion honoring a Supreme Being, and you must cast your vote as a deputy.
evt-05-07-1794-french-revolution.prompt: How do you vote on Robespierre's decree?

choices.text: Abstain and quietly plan to flee Paris
Vote against it, defending the Cult of Reason's atheism
Propose restoring the Catholic Church instead
Vote for it, embracing the new state-sanctioned deism

evt-05-07-1794-french-revolution.butterflyEffect: The Convention adopted the decree, and Robespierre staged a lavish Festival of the Supreme Being the following month. The spectacle struck many as self-glorifying and deepened suspicion of Robespierre's power, feeding the resentment that toppled him in the Thermidorian coup weeks later.

evt-05-07-1798-war-of-the-first-coalitio.scenario: It is 6 May 1798 off the Normandy coast. You row toward the Îles Saint-Marcouf in a flat-bottomed invasion barge as part of a French assault force, and British guns on the islands have opened fire on your approach.
evt-05-07-1798-war-of-the-first-coalitio.prompt: Do you press the attack against the fortified British position?

choices.text: Wait offshore for naval bombardment support first
Press forward and attempt to storm the islands
Signal for surrender terms before landing
Turn back immediately under fire

evt-05-07-1798-war-of-the-first-coalitio.butterflyEffect: The British garrison's fire devastated the French barges, inflicting heavy casualties for almost no loss of their own. The failed assault embarrassed French invasion planning and reinforced British confidence that the Channel coast could be defended against Napoleon's forces.

evt-05-07-1937-fleischer-studios.scenario: It is May 1937 outside Fleischer Studios in Manhattan. Fellow animators are walking a picket line demanding recognition of their union, and management has warned that anyone who joins the strike may lose their job.
evt-05-07-1937-fleischer-studios.prompt: Do you join the animators' strike?

choices.text: Join the picket line despite the risk of dismissal
Quit outright and take a job at Disney
Cross the line and keep working for Fleischer
Stay home and wait to see who wins before choosing a side

evt-05-07-1937-fleischer-studios.butterflyEffect: The five-week strike ended with Fleischer forced to recognize the animators' union, but the bitterness lingered. Max Fleischer later relocated the studio to Miami to escape unionized New York, losing key talent, and the weakened studio was absorbed by Paramount just a few years later.

evt-05-07-1940-norway-debate.scenario: It's early May 1940 and you're a backbench Conservative MP in the House of Commons. The bungled Norway campaign has just been debated for three days, and Chamberlain's government is visibly rattled as the division bell rings.
evt-05-07-1940-norway-debate.prompt: When the vote is called, what do you do?

choices.text: Vote against the government despite party loyalty
Support Chamberlain unanimously to preserve unity
Call publicly for an armistice with Germany
Demand an immediate general election instead

evt-05-07-1940-norway-debate.butterflyEffect: Chamberlain technically won the division, but roughly 40 Conservatives voted against him and dozens more abstained, revealing he had lost the confidence of the House. Within days he resigned, and Winston Churchill became prime minister on 10 May 1940—the very day Germany invaded France and the Low Countries.

evt-05-07-1946-masaru-ibuka.scenario: It is May 1946 in bombed-out Tokyo. You and Akio Morita have just founded Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo with a handful of engineers and almost no capital, working out of a damaged department store.
evt-05-07-1946-masaru-ibuka.prompt: What does the fledgling company do to survive its earliest months?

choices.text: Mass-produce rice cookers for households
Manufacture automobile parts for Toyota
Repair radios and tinker with new electronic devices
Import American electronics for resale

evt-05-07-1946-masaru-ibuka.butterflyEffect: The company began by repairing radios and building small electronic devices for a war-ravaged market, slowly building the technical reputation that let it develop Japan's first tape recorder in 1950. It was renamed Sony in 1958 and went on to pioneer the transistor radio and the Walkman.

evt-05-07-1992-michigan.scenario: You are a Michigan state legislator on 7 May 1992, casting a vote on an obscure 1789 constitutional amendment about congressional pay that a college student's grassroots letter-writing campaign has quietly revived after two centuries of neglect.
evt-05-07-1992-michigan.prompt: What does Michigan's ratification actually accomplish?

choices.text: It triggers a new constitutional convention
It becomes the first state to ratify the amendment
It formally rejects the proposed amendment
It becomes the 38th state, completing ratification of the 27th Amendment

evt-05-07-1992-michigan.butterflyEffect: Michigan became the 38th state to ratify, giving the amendment the three-quarters majority needed and making it the 27th Amendment—203 years after James Madison first proposed it, the longest ratification span in US history. It was largely the work of Texas student Gregory Watson's solo campaign.

evt-05-07-1992-space-shuttle-program.scenario: You are a NASA engineer at Kennedy Space Center on 7 May 1992, watching Endeavour lift off on its maiden flight with a crew tasked with rescuing a stranded Intelsat VI communications satellite stuck in the wrong orbit.
evt-05-07-1992-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What unprecedented feat does the crew perform to complete the rescue?

choices.text: A single astronaut retrieves it using only the robotic arm
The satellite is deliberately destroyed to avoid debris
The mission is aborted due to a docking failure
Three astronauts spacewalk together to grab the satellite by hand

evt-05-07-1992-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: Three astronauts performed the first-ever three-person spacewalk, manually capturing the satellite by hand before attaching a new booster to send it into proper orbit. Endeavour went on to fly 25 missions before the shuttle program ended in 2011.

evt-05-07-1994-edvard-munch.scenario: It is May 1994 and you are a Norwegian detective working the case of Edvard Munch's stolen masterpiece The Scream, taken from Oslo's National Gallery the day the Winter Olympics opened. A shadowy contact claims he can broker its return.
evt-05-07-1994-edvard-munch.prompt: How do the authorities recover the painting?

choices.text: They negotiate a public reward through the media
They wait for the painting to surface at auction
They stage a sting posing as buyers to trap the thieves
They quietly pay the demanded ransom

evt-05-07-1994-edvard-munch.butterflyEffect: Police ran a sting operation, posing as buyers from London's Getty Museum, and recovered The Scream undamaged without paying any ransom. The thieves were later convicted, and Norwegian museums overhauled their security in response.

evt-05-07-1998-mercedes-benz.scenario: It's May 7, 1998, and you're a Daimler-Benz executive standing beside Chrysler's chairman in Stuttgart, about to announce a $40 billion combination to a skeptical world press.
evt-05-07-1998-mercedes-benz.prompt: How do you publicly frame the deal to markets and employees?

choices.text: As a joint venture limited to European sales only
As a hostile takeover of Chrysler by Daimler
As a 'merger of equals' creating DaimlerChrysler
As Daimler simply licensing Chrysler's technology

evt-05-07-1998-mercedes-benz.butterflyEffect: Despite being marketed as a 'merger of equals,' Daimler executives soon dominated management and culture clashes plagued the new company. Profits sagged and American workers chafed under German corporate control, and by 2007 Daimler sold an 80.1% stake in Chrysler to private equity firm Cerberus for a fraction of the original price.

evt-05-07-1999-pope-john-paul-ii.scenario: It is May 1999, and Pope John Paul II has just landed in Bucharest, the first pope to set foot in a majority Orthodox nation since the Great Schism of 1054. Romanian Patriarch Teoctist stands waiting on the tarmac before the watching crowds and cameras.
evt-05-07-1999-pope-john-paul-ii.prompt: How does Patriarch Teoctist choose to receive the visiting pope?

choices.text: Boycott the visit and leave the capital
Refuse any public meeting with the pope
Meet him only in a closed-door private audience
Publicly embrace him as a gesture of Christian unity

evt-05-07-1999-pope-john-paul-ii.butterflyEffect: Teoctist publicly embraced John Paul II, and crowds chanted "Unitate!" (Unity!), a striking scene after nearly a millennium of division between Rome and Orthodoxy. The visit became a landmark in Catholic-Orthodox relations, encouraging further ecumenical outreach between the two churches in the following decades.

evt-05-07-1999-guinea-bissau.scenario: It is 7 May 1999 in Bissau. Rebel soldiers loyal to General Ansumane Mané have surrounded the presidential palace after months of civil war, and you are President João Bernardo Vieira, weighing how to respond before the walls are breached.
evt-05-07-1999-guinea-bissau.prompt: What does Vieira do as the junta closes in?

choices.text: Seek refuge in the Portuguese embassy and accept ouster
Flee immediately to Senegal to rally ECOMOG intervention forces
Order loyal troops to fight to the last to defend the palace
Negotiate a power-sharing deal to remain as ceremonial head of state

evt-05-07-1999-guinea-bissau.butterflyEffect: Vieira was ousted and took refuge in the Portuguese embassy before going into exile in Portugal. A transitional government held elections in 2000, but instability persisted; Vieira later returned to win the 2005 presidency, only to be assassinated in 2009.

evt-05-07-2000-vladimir-putin.scenario: It is 7 May 2000, and you watch Vladimir Putin take the oath of office in the Kremlin's Andreyevsky Hall, having risen from little-known prime minister to president in under a year, largely on the strength of his hard line in Chechnya.
evt-05-07-2000-vladimir-putin.prompt: What does Putin make his central priority upon taking office?

choices.text: Restore the market liberalization pace of the early Yeltsin years
Pursue rapid decentralization of power to Russia's regions
Seek immediate integration into NATO
Continue the Chechen war while centralizing state authority

evt-05-07-2000-vladimir-putin.butterflyEffect: Putin pressed on with the war in Chechnya and moved swiftly to reassert Kremlin authority over Russia's regions, oligarchs, and media, building what became known as the "power vertical." This consolidation of central control set the pattern for over two decades of increasingly centralized rule in Russia.

evt-05-07-2002-egyptair-flight-843.scenario: It's the early morning of 7 May 2002, and you're the pilot of EgyptAir Flight 843 on final approach to Tunis–Carthage Airport, with dense fog obscuring the runway ahead.
evt-05-07-2002-egyptair-flight-843.prompt: With visibility failing on final approach, what should you do?

choices.text: Execute a go-around and attempt another approach or divert
Increase speed to try to break through the fog layer
Continue descending below the minimum altitude on visual cues
Request clearance to switch runways mid-approach

evt-05-07-2002-egyptair-flight-843.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew continued descending below the minimum safe altitude in fog without adequate visual reference, and the aircraft struck a hill short of the runway, killing 14 of the 62 people aboard. The crash intensified scrutiny of low-visibility approach procedures and cockpit decision-making across the region's airlines.

evt-05-07-2002-china-northern-airlines-f.scenario: It is 7 May 2002. You are the captain of an MD-82 over Bohai Bay near Dalian when smoke suddenly fills the cabin and a fire breaks out behind the cockpit. Air traffic control is waiting for you to declare your next move.
evt-05-07-2002-china-northern-airlines-f.prompt: With fire spreading and the coast still miles away, what should you do?

choices.text: Order passengers to fight the fire themselves before informing ATC
Attempt an emergency diversion to the nearest airport
Climb to a higher altitude to starve the fire of oxygen
Continue on the original flight plan and hope the fire dies down

evt-05-07-2002-china-northern-airlines-f.butterflyEffect: The crew tried to divert toward Dalian, but the aircraft lost control and plunged into the bay, killing everyone aboard. Investigators later determined the fire had been deliberately set by a passenger, prompting Chinese airlines to tighten cabin security and passenger screening procedures in the years that followed.

evt-05-07-2009-napier-new-zealand.scenario: It's 7 May 2009 in the Napier suburb of Chaucer Road. You're a police officer serving a search warrant on a suspected drug house when gunfire erupts and a colleague falls wounded beside you.
evt-05-07-2009-napier-new-zealand.prompt: What do you do next as the situation turns violent?

choices.text: Call for backup and set up a perimeter around the house
Storm the house immediately regardless of casualties
Offer the gunman a cash payment to surrender
Withdraw entirely and abandon the operation

evt-05-07-2009-napier-new-zealand.butterflyEffect: Police pulled back and cordoned off the property, beginning a siege that stretched on for roughly 40 hours. When officers finally entered, they found gunman Jan Molenaar dead of a self-inflicted gunshot wound; Constable Len Snee, killed in the initial shooting, was posthumously honoured, and the siege prompted a review of police firearms policy.

evt-05-07-2010-neanderthal.scenario: It is 2010 in a genomics lab, and you are part of the team comparing the newly sequenced Neanderthal draft genome against DNA from living humans around the world, looking for shared genetic markers.
