evt-05-07-2010-neanderthal.prompt: What does the comparison reveal about Neanderthals and modern humans?

choices.text: They share no meaningful genetic overlap with any living humans
Neanderthals are genetically identical to modern chimpanzees
Neanderthal DNA is found equally in all human populations worldwide
Neanderthal DNA persists in modern humans outside Africa due to interbreeding

evt-05-07-2010-neanderthal.butterflyEffect: The genome revealed that Neanderthals interbred with early modern humans, leaving a lasting genetic trace of one to four percent in the DNA of people outside Africa today. The discovery upended the view of Neanderthals as a wholly separate dead-end species and reshaped understanding of human ancestry.

evt-05-08-1373-julian-of-norwich.scenario: It is May 1373 and you lie near death in your sickbed, a priest having already given you last rites, when sudden, vivid visions of Christ's suffering unfold before your eyes.
evt-05-08-1373-julian-of-norwich.prompt: Once you recover, what do you do with these visions?

choices.text: Confess them privately to a priest and never speak of them again
Have them recorded in Latin for the Church hierarchy only
Dismiss them as fevered dreams and move on
Write them down in English for others to read

evt-05-08-1373-julian-of-norwich.butterflyEffect: She recorded them as Revelations of Divine Love, becoming the earliest surviving English-language work known to be written by a woman. She later lived as an anchoress attached to a Norwich church, and her writings on God's love survived to become one of the most influential texts of Christian mysticism.

evt-05-08-1643-first-english-civil-war.scenario: It is May 1643 at Wardour Castle in Wiltshire. You are Blanche, Lady Arundell, holding the walls with a garrison of barely two dozen men and servants against a Parliamentarian force under Sir Edward Hungerford, and after six days your powder and water are nearly gone.
evt-05-08-1643-first-english-civil-war.prompt: What do you do to save your people?

choices.text: Order a desperate night-time breakout through enemy lines
Set the castle ablaze rather than let it be taken
Fight on until the last man and woman fell
Negotiate a surrender in exchange for safe treatment of the garrison

evt-05-08-1643-first-english-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Lady Arundell surrendered on terms promising safety for her household, though the victors plundered the castle regardless. Royalists retook and then deliberately blew up much of Wardour the following year to deny it to the enemy, leaving the picturesque ruin that still stands today.

evt-05-08-1821-greek-war-of-independence.scenario: It is 8 May 1821, and you are one of roughly 120 Greek fighters holed up in the inn at Gravia, facing thousands of Ottoman troops under Omer Vrioni as night falls and ammunition runs low.
evt-05-08-1821-greek-war-of-independence.prompt: What do the defenders do to survive?

choices.text: Surrender under terms
Wait for reinforcements that never came
Fight to the last man in the inn
Break out under cover of darkness

evt-05-08-1821-greek-war-of-independence.butterflyEffect: Odysseas Androutsos's men slipped through the Ottoman lines that night after a day of fierce resistance that had inflicted heavy losses on Vrioni's force. The stand became a celebrated early triumph of the revolution, boosting Greek morale and Androutsos's reputation as a guerrilla leader.

evt-05-08-1842-versailles-rail-accident.scenario: It is 8 May 1842 and you have boarded a train from Versailles to Paris, the carriage door locked behind you as is customary practice, when the lead locomotive suddenly breaks an axle ahead.
evt-05-08-1842-versailles-rail-accident.prompt: What happens to the passengers as the wrecked carriages catch fire?

choices.text: The carriages uncouple safely before the fire reaches them
Passengers break windows and escape without injury
Guards quickly unlock every door and all passengers escape
Many are trapped inside their locked carriages as fire spreads

evt-05-08-1842-versailles-rail-accident.butterflyEffect: Locked inside their carriages, many passengers could not escape the flames, and the disaster killed at least 52 people, including the explorer Jules Dumont d'Urville. The horror of trapped victims led French railways to abandon the practice of locking passengers into their compartments.

evt-05-08-1927-charles-nungesser.scenario: It is dawn on 8 May 1927 at Le Bourget airfield near Paris, and a crowd watches war ace Charles Nungesser and navigator François Coli climb into L'Oiseau Blanc for the first attempt at a nonstop flight from Paris to New York.
evt-05-08-1927-charles-nungesser.prompt: What follows their departure over the Atlantic?

choices.text: They land safely in New York to a hero's welcome
They vanish without a trace somewhere over the Atlantic
They crash shortly after takeoff and are rescued
Engine trouble forces them to turn back to France

evt-05-08-1927-charles-nungesser.butterflyEffect: The plane was last sighted over Ireland and then vanished without a trace; no confirmed wreckage was ever found despite extensive searches. Their disappearance intensified public fascination with transatlantic flight just two weeks before Charles Lindbergh's successful solo crossing, which claimed the fame and prize money Nungesser and Coli had been chasing.

evt-05-08-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 8 May 1942, and Manstein's 11th Army has just broken through your lines on the Kerch Peninsula, threatening to trap three Soviet armies against the sea.
evt-05-08-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What does the Soviet high command do as the front collapses?

choices.text: Wait for Stavka's approval before withdrawing
Order an immediate, unauthorized retreat to the coast
Evacuate command staff only
Launch a full counteroffensive

evt-05-08-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Front commander Kozlov and political officer Mehlis delayed seeking Moscow's permission to retreat, and by the time it came the escape routes were cut. The resulting encirclement destroyed much of three Soviet armies, and the German capture of the peninsula by late May freed troops for the final assault on Sevastopol weeks later.

evt-05-08-1945-victory-in-europe-day.scenario: It is the afternoon of 8 May 1945 and you are standing in a packed Trafalgar Square in London, having just heard that Germany's surrender is official.
evt-05-08-1945-victory-in-europe-day.prompt: What happens as the crowds surge toward Buckingham Palace?

choices.text: The king declares martial law to control the crowds
The government announces the immediate demobilisation of all troops
The royal family and Churchill appear together on the balcony
Parliament dissolves itself in celebration

evt-05-08-1945-victory-in-europe-day.butterflyEffect: Winston Churchill and the royal family appeared together on the palace balcony to the roar of celebrating crowds, a scene that became the defining image of VE Day. The war against Japan continued for another three months, so celebrations were tempered by the knowledge the conflict was not fully over.

evt-05-08-1950-tollund-man.scenario: It is 8 May 1950, and you and your brother are cutting peat in a bog near Silkeborg, Denmark, when your spade uncovers a face so lifelike you think you have found a murder victim.
evt-05-08-1950-tollund-man.prompt: What do you do after finding the body in the bog?

choices.text: Assume it's an old grave and ignore it
Rebury it quietly to avoid trouble
Sell the discovery to a local museum yourself
Report the discovery to the local police

evt-05-08-1950-tollund-man.butterflyEffect: Police were indeed called, fearing a recent murder, but the body turned out to be roughly 2,400 years old, preserved by the bog's acidic, oxygen-free peat. The Tollund Man, likely a ritual sacrifice who had been hanged, became the best-preserved Iron Age body ever found, reshaping understanding of prehistoric Scandinavian ritual and death.

evt-05-08-1957-south-vietnam.scenario: It is May 1957 and you are a US Congressman watching President Ngô Đình Diệm address a joint session of Congress during his state visit, with American officials eager to showcase him as a Cold War success story.
evt-05-08-1957-south-vietnam.prompt: What does Diệm's visit aim to secure from the United States?

choices.text: A formal NATO-style mutual defense treaty
Immediate United Nations membership for South Vietnam
Increased American economic and military aid
French troops to return and garrison the south

evt-05-08-1957-south-vietnam.butterflyEffect: Diệm returned home with pledges of continued American economic and military aid, and Washington publicly hailed him as a bulwark against communism in Southeast Asia. That deepening commitment helped lock the United States into supporting South Vietnam, a relationship that expanded into full military involvement over the following decade.

evt-05-08-1963-hue.scenario: It is Vesak, 8 May 1963, in Huế. You stand among a crowd of Buddhists gathered near the government radio station, angry that officials banned the traditional Buddhist flag while permitting Catholic banners for a recent celebration.
evt-05-08-1963-hue.prompt: What happens as the crowd's protest grows more tense outside the station?

choices.text: Soldiers open fire into the crowd
The crowd disperses peacefully after negotiations
Officials grant the Buddhist flag request on the spot
The protest ends with the Catholic banners being removed instead

evt-05-08-1963-hue.butterflyEffect: Government forces opened fire on the crowd, killing several people, an event that ignited the Buddhist crisis against President Ngô Đình Diệm's rule. The unrest culminated in Thích Quảng Đức's self-immolation months later and helped set the stage for the November 1963 coup that toppled Diệm.

evt-05-08-1970-hard-hat-riot.scenario: It is 8 May 1970 in Lower Manhattan. News of the Kent State shootings and the invasion of Cambodia has students staging an angry demonstration near Wall Street, and you are one of hundreds of construction workers watching from nearby scaffolding, hard hat in hand.
evt-05-08-1970-hard-hat-riot.prompt: What do many of the construction workers do as the student protest continues?

choices.text: March alongside the students in solidarity against the war
Organize a rival peace rally a block away
Charge into the crowd, attacking the anti-war demonstrators
Ignore the protest entirely and return to work

evt-05-08-1970-hard-hat-riot.butterflyEffect: Hundreds of construction and office workers charged the demonstrators, beating some students bloody while chanting pro-war, pro-America slogans. The 'Hard Hat Riot' made blue-collar support for the war a national symbol, and weeks later President Nixon publicly welcomed union leaders to the White House, courting the 'silent majority' that would help reshape American politics.

evt-05-08-1973-wounded-knee-occupation.scenario: It is late February 1973 and you are among roughly 200 Oglala Lakota and American Indian Movement members who have just seized the small town of Wounded Knee, South Dakota, as federal marshals and FBI agents begin surrounding the perimeter.
evt-05-08-1973-wounded-knee-occupation.prompt: What does the group decide to do as the siege begins?

choices.text: Hold the town and demand negotiations over treaty rights and tribal governance
Disperse quietly before federal forces arrive
Abandon Wounded Knee for a more defensible reservation town
Surrender immediately to avoid bloodshed

evt-05-08-1973-wounded-knee-occupation.butterflyEffect: The occupation held for 71 days before a negotiated end, becoming one of the most watched Native American protests of the era. It drew national attention to treaty rights and reservation governance, spurred federal reviews of Bureau of Indian Affairs policy, and cemented AIM's role in the wider Native rights movement.

evt-05-08-1976-the-great-american-revolu.scenario: It is opening day, 8 May 1976, at Six Flags Magic Mountain, and you are eyeing a new steel coaster with a loop unlike anything you've ridden before.
evt-05-08-1976-the-great-american-revolu.prompt: What makes this ride, the Great American Revolution, historic?

choices.text: It is the tallest coaster in the world
It is the first modern coaster with a vertical loop
It is the first roller coaster ever built
It is the first coaster with an onboard camera

evt-05-08-1976-the-great-american-revolu.butterflyEffect: The Revolution's smooth vertical loop, engineered by Werner Stengel, proved loops could be ridden comfortably, launching a wave of looping steel coasters across American and European parks through the late 1970s and 1980s. It kicked off the modern 'coaster wars' that still shape theme park competition today.

evt-05-08-1978-mount-everest.scenario: It is 8 May 1978, and you are gasping through thin air near the summit of Mount Everest alongside your climbing partner, having deliberately left the bottled oxygen behind to prove the mountain can be climbed on lungs alone.
evt-05-08-1978-mount-everest.prompt: What do you and your partner achieve on this attempt?

choices.text: They reach the summit without using bottled oxygen
They reach the summit but only after breaking out emergency oxygen
One climber dies before reaching the top
They turn back just short of the summit due to altitude sickness

evt-05-08-1978-mount-everest.butterflyEffect: Reinhold Messner and Peter Habeler became the first climbers to reach Everest's summit without supplemental oxygen, overturning assumptions about human limits at extreme altitude. The feat launched a new era of 'purist' high-altitude mountaineering, and Messner himself would go on to solo the mountain without oxygen just two years later.

evt-05-08-1980-smallpox.scenario: It is the 1970s and you are a WHO epidemiologist tasked with eradicating smallpox worldwide, but vaccine supplies and staff are far too limited to inoculate every person on Earth.
evt-05-08-1980-smallpox.prompt: What strategy do you adopt to stop the disease with the resources available?

choices.text: Let natural infection build herd immunity over time
Vaccinate entire national populations regardless of outbreaks
Track outbreaks and vaccinate everyone in contact with each case
Rely on quarantine alone without vaccination

evt-05-08-1980-smallpox.butterflyEffect: Teams used surveillance-containment, or 'ring vaccination': tracking every outbreak and vaccinating everyone around it rather than whole populations. The approach succeeded, smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980, and the same ring-vaccination technique was later adapted to fight Ebola and polio outbreaks.

evt-05-08-1984-1984-summer-olympics-boyc.scenario: It is 8 May 1984 and you sit on the Soviet Olympic Committee. Moscow cites 'security concerns' about the Los Angeles Games, and Washington shows no sign of backing down after the 1980 boycott.
evt-05-08-1984-1984-summer-olympics-boyc.prompt: What does the Soviet Union announce?

choices.text: Participation under a neutral Olympic flag
A full boycott of the Los Angeles Games
A partial team sent only in non-medal sports
Acceptance of US security guarantees and full attendance

evt-05-08-1984-1984-summer-olympics-boyc.butterflyEffect: The USSR led fourteen Eastern Bloc allies plus a few non-aligned states in boycotting Los Angeles, staging rival 'Friendship Games' instead. Despite the walkout, a record 140 nations still competed in LA, and the tit-for-tat boycotts of 1980 and 1984 hastened the end of Cold War Olympic politics by the Seoul Games of 1988.

evt-05-08-1984-soviet-union.scenario: It is 8 May 1984, four years after the United States boycotted the Moscow Olympics, and Soviet officials are deciding how to respond to the upcoming Los Angeles Games.
evt-05-08-1984-soviet-union.prompt: What does the Soviet government announce?

choices.text: Sending only unofficial athletes
Full participation to prove Soviet athletic superiority
A boycott of the Los Angeles Olympics
A joint Olympics compromise with the IOC

evt-05-08-1984-soviet-union.butterflyEffect: The USSR boycotted, citing security concerns, and thirteen more Eastern Bloc allies followed suit, mirroring the Western boycott of 1980. American athletes dominated the medal table, while the Soviets staged the alternative 'Friendship Games' for their bloc, deepening Cold War sporting rivalry.

evt-05-08-1984-thames-barrier.scenario: It is 1953, and a catastrophic North Sea storm surge has just drowned parts of eastern England and pushed dangerously up the Thames toward London. As a government engineer tasked with preventing a repeat disaster, you must recommend a permanent solution for the capital.
evt-05-08-1984-thames-barrier.prompt: What massive flood-defence project do you ultimately propose for the Thames?

choices.text: Permanent concrete walls raised along the entire riverbank
Compulsory relocation of all riverside communities
A movable barrier across the Thames that can be raised during storm surges
A new diversion channel to reroute the Thames around London

evt-05-08-1984-thames-barrier.butterflyEffect: The Thames Barrier, a retractable steel-gate system near Greenwich, opened in 1984 after over a decade of construction. It has since been raised hundreds of times to protect London from tidal surges, though rising sea levels have already sparked debate over whether it will need a successor by the 2070s.

evt-05-08-1987-special-air-service.scenario: It is the evening of 8 May 1987 near Loughgall, County Armagh. You are part of a Provisional IRA active service unit driving a stolen digger loaded with a bomb toward the small RUC police station, believing it to be lightly guarded.
evt-05-08-1987-special-air-service.prompt: What happens as the unit approaches the station?

choices.text: The RUC officers surrender the station without a fight
Local police intercept and arrest the unit peacefully
The bomb detonates successfully and the unit escapes unseen
A hidden SAS ambush opens fire, killing the entire unit

evt-05-08-1987-special-air-service.butterflyEffect: A concealed SAS unit opened fire, killing all eight IRA members involved, the single greatest loss the organisation suffered during the Troubles. The ambush intensified allegations of a British 'shoot-to-kill' policy while devastating the East Tyrone Brigade, hardening resolve on both sides of the conflict for years afterward.

evt-05-08-2019-phage-therapy.scenario: It is 2019, and your teenage patient's lungs are failing again after a transplant, this time from a Mycobacterium infection that shrugs off every antibiotic you try.
evt-05-08-2019-phage-therapy.prompt: What treatment do doctors turn to as a last resort?

choices.text: Palliative care only
A second lung transplant
An experimental cocktail of engineered bacteriophages
High-dose intravenous antibiotics alone

evt-05-08-2019-phage-therapy.butterflyEffect: Doctors at Great Ormond Street, working with a US lab, engineered bacteriophages specifically to attack Isabelle Holdaway's drug-resistant infection, and her recovery was reported in 2019 as one of the first documented successes of its kind. The case reignited global interest in phage therapy as a weapon against antibiotic-resistant bacteria, spurring new clinical trials.

evt-05-08-2025-2025-conclave.scenario: It is the evening of 8 May 2025, and you are a cardinal elector inside the Sistine Chapel. White smoke has just risen from the chimney after the fourth ballot, signaling that a new pope has been chosen to succeed Francis.
evt-05-08-2025-2025-conclave.prompt: Which cardinal emerges as the newly elected pope?

choices.text: Robert Francis Prevost, who takes the name Leo XIV
Peter Turkson of Ghana
Pietro Parolin, the Vatican's Secretary of State
Luis Antonio Tagle of the Philippines

evt-05-08-2025-2025-conclave.butterflyEffect: Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost was elected and took the name Leo XIV, becoming the first pope born in the United States. His election was seen as a signal of continuity with Francis's priorities while also reflecting the Church's deepening global reach beyond Europe.

evt-05-09-1761-exhibition-of-1761.scenario: You are a member of the newly formed Society of Artists of Great Britain, preparing to open Britain's first public art exhibition at Spring Gardens, Westminster, on 9 May 1761.
evt-05-09-1761-exhibition-of-1761.prompt: How do you decide to control access to the exhibition?

choices.text: Charge a shilling for the catalogue as a de facto entrance fee
Make the exhibition free and open to all without restriction
Sell numbered tickets weeks in advance
Restrict entry to invited patrons only

evt-05-09-1761-exhibition-of-1761.butterflyEffect: The Society charged visitors a shilling for the catalogue, effectively creating Britain's first paid public art exhibition, and it proved hugely popular. Internal disputes over control of these exhibitions later split the Society, leading Joshua Reynolds and others to found the rival Royal Academy of Arts in 1768.

evt-05-09-1864-second-schleswig-war.scenario: You command the Danish squadron off Heligoland on 9 May 1864, your frigates locked in a fierce duel with the Austrian-Prussian force. As the smoke clears, the enemy ships turn and flee toward the neutral waters around the British-held island.
evt-05-09-1864-second-schleswig-war.prompt: What do you do as the enemy squadron retreats into British neutral waters?

choices.text: Break off pursuit and respect British neutral waters
Chase the enemy ships into the harbor regardless
Retreat immediately to a Danish port
Open fire on the neutral port itself

evt-05-09-1864-second-schleswig-war.butterflyEffect: Suenson broke off pursuit rather than violate British neutrality, and the Austrian-Prussian ships escaped to safety. Though Denmark won the tactical naval engagement, it made no difference to the war's outcome: Denmark still lost Schleswig-Holstein on land, a defeat that cleared the path for Prussia's later unification of Germany.

evt-05-09-1918-world-war-i.scenario: It is the night of 9 May 1918. You are aboard HMS Vindictive, ordered to steam into Ostend harbour and scuttle your ship across the channel to trap German destroyers and U-boats inside, following the failed first attempt weeks earlier.
evt-05-09-1918-world-war-i.prompt: What happened to this second attempt to block Ostend harbour?

choices.text: Vindictive was scuttled in the wrong position, leaving the channel only partly blocked
The ship successfully sealed the harbour, trapping the German fleet
The raid was called off before any ship entered the harbour
German shore batteries sank Vindictive before she reached the harbour

evt-05-09-1918-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Vindictive was sunk in the wrong position due to shifting currents and lost navigational markers, leaving the channel only partially obstructed. German vessels continued to use the port, making the raid a tactical failure, though it was celebrated in Britain as a feat of daring that boosted wartime morale.

evt-05-09-1949-rainier-iii-of-monaco.scenario: It is 9 May 1949. You are the young new Prince of Monaco, inheriting a tiny principality whose finances depend almost entirely on casino revenue.
evt-05-09-1949-rainier-iii-of-monaco.prompt: What strategy do you pursue to secure Monaco's long-term future?

choices.text: Abdicate in favor of a regency council
Petition France to formally annex the principality
Diversify the economy and raise Monaco's global profile through marriage
Rely entirely on expanding the existing casino

evt-05-09-1949-rainier-iii-of-monaco.butterflyEffect: Rainier diversified Monaco's economy beyond gambling into banking, real estate, and tourism, and his glamorous 1956 marriage to Hollywood star Grace Kelly transformed the tiny principality into an internationally famous destination. The combination secured Monaco's finances and visibility for decades to come.

evt-05-09-1960-food-and-drug-administrat.scenario: You are a health reporter in Washington on 9 May 1960, waiting for the FDA's ruling on a small pink pill that a Chicago pharmaceutical company hopes to sell not for menstrual disorders, but for something far more controversial.
evt-05-09-1960-food-and-drug-administrat.prompt: What does the FDA approve today, changing millions of lives?

choices.text: A new over-the-counter tranquilizer
Enovid, the first oral contraceptive pill
The Salk polio vaccine
Thalidomide, a new sedative for morning sickness

evt-05-09-1960-food-and-drug-administrat.butterflyEffect: The FDA approved Enovid for use as an oral contraceptive, making it the world's first birth control pill. Within five years over six million American women were using it, reshaping family planning, workforce participation, and the sexual revolution for decades to come.

evt-05-09-1961-newton-n-minow.scenario: You are a network executive in the audience as FCC chairman Newton Minow addresses the National Association of Broadcasters on 9 May 1961, delivering a speech that will outlast every show on your schedule.
evt-05-09-1961-newton-n-minow.prompt: What does Minow dare broadcasters to do to prove him wrong?

choices.text: Watch a full day of their own network's programming
Replace all game shows with news programming
Double their advertising rates
Submit their schedules for FCC pre-approval

evt-05-09-1961-newton-n-minow.butterflyEffect: Minow challenged them to sit and watch their own programming for a full day without a break, promising they would find it a 'vast wasteland.' The phrase became a lasting indictment of television quality and helped fuel momentum toward public broadcasting, culminating in the 1967 Public Broadcasting Act that created PBS.

evt-05-09-1964-ngo-inh-can.scenario: You are a military tribunal officer in Saigon on 9 May 1964. Ngô Đình Cẩn, once the feared warlord of central Vietnam, now sits convicted before the new government that overthrew his brother Diệm months earlier.
evt-05-09-1964-ngo-inh-can.prompt: What happens to Ngô Đình Cẩn now that the new regime has judged him?

choices.text: He is exiled to France with his fortune intact
He is acquitted and returns to Huế
He is executed by firing squad
He is imprisoned for life on an island penal colony

evt-05-09-1964-ngo-inh-can.butterflyEffect: Cẩn was executed by firing squad, closing the chapter on the Ngô family's grip on power. His death came amid a wave of coups and countercoups that destabilized South Vietnam's government just as American involvement in the war was deepening.

evt-05-09-1979-iranian-jews.scenario: It's May 9, 1979. News spreads through Tehran's Jewish community that Habib Elghanian, a prominent businessman and community leader, has been executed by firing squad after a revolutionary tribunal convicted him of spying for Israel.
evt-05-09-1979-iranian-jews.prompt: What was the immediate response among Iran's Jewish community?

choices.text: Tens of thousands of Iranian Jews fled the country in the following months
The execution had little effect and emigration rates stayed steady
Iranian Jews were granted expanded religious autonomy as compensation
The community organized protests that forced a government apology

evt-05-09-1979-iranian-jews.butterflyEffect: Elghanian's execution, the first of a prominent Jew under the new government, convinced many that Iran's ancient Jewish community was no longer safe. Tens of thousands fled in the following months to Israel, the United States, and Europe, permanently reshaping a diaspora with roots stretching back to Cyrus the Great.

evt-05-09-1980-sunshine-skyway-bridge.scenario: At dawn on 9 May 1980, a sudden squall blinds the freighter Summit Venture as it steers through Tampa Bay, right beneath the towering piers of the Sunshine Skyway Bridge.
evt-05-09-1980-sunshine-skyway-bridge.prompt: What happens next as the ship loses sight of the channel?

choices.text: The ship's crew abandons ship before ever reaching the bridge
The ship strikes a support pier, collapsing a section of the bridge and sending vehicles into the bay
The ship runs aground on a sandbar well short of the bridge
The ship narrowly avoids the bridge and continues safely to port

evt-05-09-1980-sunshine-skyway-bridge.butterflyEffect: The Summit Venture struck a support pier, dropping a 1,200-foot section of the southbound span into the bay. Several vehicles, including a Greyhound bus, plunged in, killing 35 people. The disaster led to protective pier "dolphins" on bridges nationwide and inspired the cable-stayed replacement bridge that opened in 1987.

evt-05-09-1992-methane.scenario: It's May 9, 1992. An underground explosion rips through the Westray coal mine in Plymouth, Nova Scotia, killing 26 miners. Investigators soon uncover that repeated methane and safety warnings had gone unheeded by management.
evt-05-09-1992-methane.prompt: What major legal change followed the Westray mine disaster in Canada?

choices.text: Canada nationalized all coal mining operations
A national mine workers' union was formed with binding strike rights
Nova Scotia banned underground coal mining entirely
Canada passed the 'Westray Law,' making corporate executives criminally liable for workplace safety failures

evt-05-09-1992-methane.butterflyEffect: The Westray disaster exposed how corporate negligence in mine safety could go unpunished. It led to Canada's 2004 'Westray Law' (Bill C-45), amending the Criminal Code to make corporations and executives criminally liable for failing to ensure workplace safety.

evt-05-09-1992-armenia.scenario: It's May 9, 1992. You are with Armenian forces launching a final assault on the hilltop town of Shusha, a stronghold from which Azerbaijani artillery has been shelling the besieged city of Stepanakert below.
evt-05-09-1992-armenia.prompt: What did the fall of Shusha achieve for Armenian forces in the war?

choices.text: It forced Azerbaijan to surrender Baku
It broke the siege of Stepanakert and secured Armenian control of the region's former capital
It ended the war immediately with a negotiated ceasefire
It opened a direct land corridor to Russia

evt-05-09-1992-armenia.butterflyEffect: The capture of Shusha broke the Azerbaijani siege of Stepanakert and gave Armenian forces control of Nagorno-Karabakh's historic capital, cementing their dominance for nearly three decades. Shusha remained a symbol of the conflict until Azerbaijan recaptured it in the 2020 war.

evt-05-09-1999-mother-s-day-bus-crash.scenario: You are a safety investigator called to Interstate 610 in New Orleans on 9 May 1999, where a charter bus carrying Mother's Day travelers has veered off the road and struck an embankment, killing 22 people.
evt-05-09-1999-mother-s-day-bus-crash.prompt: What does the investigation determine caused the driver to lose control?

choices.text: A sudden brake failure
A blown front tire
The driver fell asleep due to undiagnosed sleep apnea
The driver was intoxicated

evt-05-09-1999-mother-s-day-bus-crash.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the driver had undiagnosed obstructive sleep apnea and fell asleep at the wheel. The tragedy pushed federal regulators toward stricter medical screening requirements for commercial drivers, reshaping how trucking and bus companies test for fatigue-related conditions.

evt-05-09-2001-accra-sports-stadium.scenario: You are a police officer inside Accra's Ohene Djan Stadium on 9 May 2001, watching fans hurl bottles and chairs onto the pitch during the Hearts of Oak–Asante Kotoko match as tension in the packed stands rises fast.
evt-05-09-2001-accra-sports-stadium.prompt: What do police do to control the unruly crowd, with tragic results?

choices.text: Halt the match and evacuate calmly over the loudspeakers
Call in the fire brigade to hose down the crowd
Fire tear gas directly into the crowded stands
Immediately open all stadium exits

evt-05-09-2001-accra-sports-stadium.butterflyEffect: Officers fired tear gas into the packed stands, and panicked fans stampeded toward exits that were locked shut, crushing 126 people to death in Ghana's worst sporting disaster. The catastrophe triggered a national inquiry, criminal charges against officials, and lasting reforms to stadium exits and crowd-control policy.

evt-05-09-2001-ghana.scenario: You are a police officer inside Accra Sports Stadium on 9 May 2001, as Asante Kotoko fans, furious at conceding two late goals to Accra Hearts of Oak, begin hurling bottles and plastic chairs onto the pitch.
evt-05-09-2001-ghana.prompt: What decision by police sets the disaster in motion?

choices.text: Open every stadium gate immediately to let fans leave calmly
Let the match continue without any police response
Order the players off the field without engaging the crowd
Fire tear gas into the packed stands, triggering a stampede toward locked exits

evt-05-09-2001-ghana.butterflyEffect: Police fired tear gas canisters into the packed terraces, and fans fleeing the fumes found many exit gates locked, causing a fatal crush. It became one of the worst stadium disasters in African football history and led to reforms in Ghanaian stadium safety and crowd-control policing.

evt-05-09-2002-siege-of-the-church-of-th.scenario: It is May 2002, and you are mediating the 38-day standoff between Israeli forces and Palestinian militants sheltering inside the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem.
evt-05-09-2002-siege-of-the-church-of-th.prompt: What arrangement finally brings the siege to an end?

choices.text: Israeli troops storm the church by force
The Vatican grants the church permanent diplomatic sanctuary
Wanted militants are exiled abroad while others are sent to Gaza
The militants surrender unconditionally to Israeli forces

evt-05-09-2002-siege-of-the-church-of-th.butterflyEffect: The siege ended with a negotiated deal: thirteen wanted militants were flown into exile in Europe while twenty-six others were relocated to Gaza, and the remaining occupants left freely. The peaceful resolution avoided a violent storming of one of Christianity's holiest sites, though it left lingering resentment on both sides over the leniency shown to the exiled men.

evt-05-09-2012-yakovlev-sj-100.scenario: It is 9 May 2012. You are piloting a new Sukhoi Superjet 100 on a demonstration flight over Mount Salak in West Java, Indonesia, showcasing the aircraft to airline buyers when the terrain warning system suddenly sounds in the cockpit.
evt-05-09-2012-yakovlev-sj-100.prompt: What do you do when the terrain alert sounds?

choices.text: Assume it is a database error and continue the descending turn
Immediately climb away from the terrain
Abort the flight and return to the airport at once
Radio air traffic control for a new heading

evt-05-09-2012-yakovlev-sj-100.butterflyEffect: The crew disregarded the alert, assuming the mountain database was outdated, and continued the descending turn directly into Mount Salak, killing all 45 people aboard. The disaster was traced to cockpit distraction and over-reliance on assumption over instruments, prompting stricter terrain-awareness protocols for demonstration flights across the industry.

evt-05-09-2018-barisan-nasional.scenario: You're a Malaysian voter heading to the polls on 9 May 2018, weighing the 1MDB corruption scandal against six decades of Barisan Nasional rule.
evt-05-09-2018-barisan-nasional.prompt: What happens when the election results come in?

choices.text: Barisan Nasional loses power for the first time since independence, to Pakatan Harapan
The election produces a hung parliament with no clear winner
Barisan Nasional wins but with a sharply reduced majority
Barisan Nasional wins another decisive majority

evt-05-09-2018-barisan-nasional.butterflyEffect: Pakatan Harapan's shock win, led by 92-year-old Mahathir Mohamad, ended Barisan Nasional's 61-year hold on power since independence and opened the door to corruption prosecutions against former PM Najib Razak over the 1MDB scandal. The result plunged Malaysian politics into a period of unstable shifting coalitions.

evt-05-09-2020-covid-19-recession.scenario: It's May 8, 2020. The U.S. Labor Department releases figures showing unemployment has surged to 14.9 percent, the worst since the Great Depression, as lockdowns shutter businesses across the country.
evt-05-09-2020-covid-19-recession.prompt: What relief measure had Congress already enacted to cushion this economic shock?

choices.text: A federal minimum wage increase to $15
A permanent universal basic income program
The CARES Act, providing stimulus checks and expanded unemployment benefits
Nationalization of the U.S. airline industry

evt-05-09-2020-covid-19-recession.butterflyEffect: Congress had passed the $2.2 trillion CARES Act in March 2020, sending stimulus checks and expanding unemployment benefits to millions. The scale of the crisis set a precedent for further rounds of federal relief, including the American Rescue Plan in 2021.

evt-05-09-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.scenario: On 9 May 2022, as Russia marks its own Victory Day parades, you watch President Biden sign a bill in Washington reviving a World War II-era program to speed weapons to an ally under invasion.
evt-05-09-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.prompt: What does the new law actually let the US do?

choices.text: Impose sweeping new sanctions on Russian oil exports
Establish a no-fly zone over Ukrainian airspace
Streamline the lending or leasing of military equipment to Ukraine, cutting delays
Deploy US troops directly to fight alongside Ukrainian forces

evt-05-09-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.butterflyEffect: The Ukraine Democracy Defense Lend-Lease Act, modeled on the 1941 program that armed Britain and the USSR, cut bureaucratic delays in lending or leasing US military equipment to Ukraine. It signaled a deepening, longer-term American military commitment beyond one-off aid packages as the war ground on.

evt-05-10-1627-pieter-nuyts.scenario: It is 1628 on Formosa. Japanese traders led by Hamada Yahei arrive demanding trade access you, as VOC governor, have restricted, and the standoff turns violent when they seize you and your son inside the fort.
evt-05-10-1627-pieter-nuyts.prompt: What must you decide to secure release from your captors?

choices.text: Order the garrison to storm the room and free yourself by force
Refuse all demands and wait for VOC reinforcements from Batavia
Attempt a secret escape from the fort at night
Agree to a hostage exchange and grant trade concessions

evt-05-10-1627-pieter-nuyts.butterflyEffect: Nuyts agreed to send his son to Japan as a hostage and grant trading concessions, but the affair so poisoned relations that the shogunate shut Dutch traders out of Hirado until Nuyts himself was extradited to Japan in 1636. The episode marked an early step in Japan's drift toward the isolationist sakoku policy.

evt-05-10-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is before dawn on 10 May 1775. You are one of the Green Mountain Boys crossing Lake Champlain with Ethan Allen and Benedict Arnold toward the sleeping British garrison at Fort Ticonderoga.
evt-05-10-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What do you do to seize the fort with your small, poorly equipped force?

choices.text: Storm the fort while the garrison sleeps, demanding surrender before they can resist
Negotiate to purchase the fort's cannons from the British commander
Lay siege and wait for reinforcements from Boston
Withdraw and wait for the Continental Congress to authorize a formal attack

evt-05-10-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Allen and Arnold stormed the fort and caught the garrison completely by surprise, capturing it without serious resistance and seizing more than 60 badly needed cannons. Those guns were later hauled to Boston by Henry Knox in the famous 'Noble Train of Artillery,' forcing the British to evacuate the city in March 1776.

evt-05-10-1833-siamese-vietnamese-wars.scenario: It is 1833 in the Saigon citadel. You are Lê Văn Khôi, a garrison officer facing arrest under Emperor Minh Mạng's crackdown on southern officials and Catholic converts, and you have just broken out of prison with fellow soldiers.
evt-05-10-1833-siamese-vietnamese-wars.prompt: What do you do next to strike back at the imperial court?

choices.text: Flee immediately across the border into Cambodia for asylum
Seize the citadel and openly declare revolt against Minh Mạng
Appeal only to French missionaries for protection and wait quietly
Surrender to imperial authorities and beg for clemency

evt-05-10-1833-siamese-vietnamese-wars.butterflyEffect: Khôi seized the Saigon citadel and held it for nearly three years, drawing in Siamese intervention and reigniting the Siamese–Vietnamese wars. Minh Mạng's forces finally retook the fortress in 1835, brutally crushing the revolt and hardening imperial persecution of Catholics, a policy France later cited as pretext for colonial intervention.

evt-05-10-1849-edwin-forrest.scenario: It is the evening of 10 May 1849 outside the Astor Place Opera House in New York City. A crowd loyal to American actor Edwin Forrest has gathered to protest a performance by his British rival, William Macready, and the mood is turning violent.
evt-05-10-1849-edwin-forrest.prompt: What does the militia called in to control the crowd ultimately do?

choices.text: They arrest Macready and cancel the show
They force Macready to publicly apologize to Forrest
They disperse the crowd peacefully with no casualties
They fire into the crowd, killing dozens

evt-05-10-1849-edwin-forrest.butterflyEffect: The militia fired directly into the crowd, killing at least twenty-two people in what became the deadliest riot New York had seen. The bloodshed exposed raw class and nationalist tensions between working-class Americans and the city's Anglophile elite, and it left a lasting mark on debates over crowd control and public order.

evt-05-10-1869-first-transcontinental-ra.scenario: It is 10 May 1869, and you stand among the dignitaries and laborers gathered at Promontory Summit, Utah, waiting for the two halves of America's first transcontinental railroad to finally meet.
evt-05-10-1869-first-transcontinental-ra.prompt: What symbolic act completes the railroad's construction?

choices.text: Blowing a locomotive whistle at both ends simultaneously
Driving a ceremonial golden spike into the final rail tie
Signing a treaty between the two railroad companies
Laying an entire rail segment made of gold

evt-05-10-1869-first-transcontinental-ra.butterflyEffect: Central Pacific President Leland Stanford drove the ceremonial 'Golden Spike,' joining the Central Pacific and Union Pacific lines into a continuous route from the Atlantic to the Pacific. The connection cut cross-country travel from months to about a week, accelerating westward migration and binding the American West into the national economy.

evt-05-10-1933-persecution-of-transgende.scenario: It is the night of 10 May 1933 in Berlin. You watch Nazi students haul books and case files from Magnus Hirschfeld's Institute for Sexual Research toward a bonfire in front of the university.
evt-05-10-1933-persecution-of-transgende.prompt: What happens to the Institute's decades of research on gender and sexuality?

choices.text: It is nationalized and continued under new Nazi-approved directors
It is smuggled to Switzerland and preserved intact
Staff hide it in the university's sewers until the war ends
It is burned in the square, destroying most of the records

evt-05-10-1933-persecution-of-transgende.butterflyEffect: The archive, including case records of early trans patients such as Dora Richter, was burned in the square that night. The destruction crippled one of the world's leading centers of sex and gender research, and Hirschfeld died in exile in France two years later, his life's work reduced to ashes.

evt-05-10-1940-neville-chamberlain.scenario: It is 10 May 1940. German forces have just invaded the Low Countries, and you are among the ministers gathered as Neville Chamberlain, his authority shattered by the Norway debate, prepares to resign as Prime Minister.
evt-05-10-1940-neville-chamberlain.prompt: Whom does Chamberlain formally recommend to the King as his successor?

choices.text: Winston Churchill
Lord Halifax
Clement Attlee
Anthony Eden

evt-05-10-1940-neville-chamberlain.butterflyEffect: Chamberlain recommended Winston Churchill, who formed an all-party coalition government that same evening. Churchill's leadership through the following months, including the fall of France and the Battle of Britain, reshaped the entire course of the war.

evt-05-10-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 10 May 1941. You are Rudolf Hess, Deputy Führer, flying a Messerschmitt Bf 110 alone toward Scotland, hoping to reach the Duke of Hamilton and broker peace with Britain.
evt-05-10-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: What happens after you bail out over the Scottish countryside?

choices.text: You are captured by a local farmer and held as a prisoner of war
You successfully meet the Duke and negotiate a ceasefire
You are shot down by RAF fighters before reaching Scotland
British officials welcome you and fly you to London for peace talks

evt-05-10-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Hess was quickly captured by a local farmer and held as a prisoner of war for the remainder of the conflict. Hitler publicly disowned him as mentally unstable, and Hess was later tried at Nuremberg, sentenced to life imprisonment, and died in Spandau Prison in 1987.

evt-05-10-1993-thailand.scenario: You work the cutting room floor at the Kader Industrial factory outside Bangkok when synthetic fabric scraps catch fire. Smoke rolls through the crowded building as workers scramble for the stairwells.
evt-05-10-1993-thailand.prompt: What fatal flaw trapped hundreds of workers inside as the fire spread?

choices.text: Exit doors were kept locked to prevent theft and unauthorized breaks
A power failure disabled the sprinkler system before the fire began
The building's only fire escape had collapsed years earlier
Local firefighters lacked ladders tall enough to reach the upper floors

evt-05-10-1993-thailand.butterflyEffect: Exit doors had been kept locked to stop theft and unauthorized breaks, and the building's cheap construction collapsed under the fire's heat, killing over 200 workers, most of them young women. The disaster became one of the deadliest factory fires in history and drew international scrutiny to safety conditions in export manufacturing across Southeast Asia.

evt-05-10-1994-john-wayne-gacy.scenario: It is 10 May 1994 at Stateville Correctional Center in Illinois. You are among the witnesses gathered as convicted killer John Wayne Gacy is prepared for execution for the murders of dozens of young men and boys.
evt-05-10-1994-john-wayne-gacy.prompt: What method does Illinois use to carry out Gacy's execution?

choices.text: Hanging
Lethal injection
The electric chair
The gas chamber

evt-05-10-1994-john-wayne-gacy.butterflyEffect: Gacy was executed by lethal injection, the method Illinois had adopted years earlier to replace the electric chair. His case remained a byword for hidden serial violence, and Illinois itself would abolish the death penalty entirely in 2011.

evt-05-10-2002-robert-hanssen.scenario: It is 10 May 2002 in a federal courtroom in Alexandria, Virginia. You are the judge about to sentence FBI agent Robert Hanssen, who pleaded guilty under a deal that spared him execution in exchange for full cooperation with investigators.
evt-05-10-2002-robert-hanssen.prompt: What sentence do you hand down, honoring the terms of his plea agreement?

choices.text: 25 years with eligibility for parole
Life imprisonment with parole possible after 20 years
Life imprisonment without parole
The death penalty

evt-05-10-2002-robert-hanssen.butterflyEffect: Hanssen was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. His required debriefings revealed the staggering scope of the damage he had caused Soviet and Russian intelligence, prompting sweeping reforms to FBI counterintelligence security.

evt-05-10-2005-grenade.scenario: It is 10 May 2005, and you stand in the crowd at Tbilisi's Freedom Square as U.S. President George W. Bush addresses tens of thousands of Georgians.
evt-05-10-2005-grenade.prompt: What happens to the grenade thrown toward the podium, landing about 20 meters from Bush?

choices.text: Secret Service agents intercept it in mid-air
It explodes, injuring several bystanders near the stage
It misses the crowd entirely and lands in an empty lot
It lands near the stage but fails to detonate, its pin still attached

evt-05-10-2005-grenade.butterflyEffect: The grenade, wrapped in a handkerchief, failed to detonate because its safety pin never fully released. The attacker, former Georgian police officer Vladimir Arutyunian, was later caught after killing a police officer during his escape and was convicted and sentenced to life in prison.

evt-05-10-2013-one-world-trade-center.scenario: It is 10 May 2013, and you are a construction worker atop One World Trade Center in Lower Manhattan, guiding the final section of the spire into place.
evt-05-10-2013-one-world-trade-center.prompt: What milestone does completing the spire achieve?

choices.text: It becomes the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere
It installs a broadcast antenna unrelated to the tower's height
It finishes the September 11 memorial museum below
It completes the public observation deck

evt-05-10-2013-one-world-trade-center.butterflyEffect: The finished spire brought the tower to its symbolic full height of 1,776 feet, making it the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere. The height, referencing the year of American independence, became a lasting symbol of Lower Manhattan's rebuilding after the September 11 attacks.

evt-05-10-2022-elizabeth-ii.scenario: It is 10 May 2022 at Buckingham Palace. Aides have just confirmed that the 96-year-old Queen, troubled by mobility problems, cannot attend the State Opening of Parliament for the first time in 59 years.
evt-05-10-2022-elizabeth-ii.prompt: Who does the Palace announce will read the Queen's Speech from the Throne in her place?

choices.text: The Duchess of Cornwall, Camilla
The Lord Chancellor reads it on the Queen's behalf
Prince Charles, the heir apparent
Prince Andrew, Duke of York

evt-05-10-2022-elizabeth-ii.butterflyEffect: Prince Charles delivered the Speech from the Throne alongside Prince William, the first time in decades a monarch's speech was read by someone else. It was widely seen as a rehearsal for his own reign, which began four months later when Elizabeth II died in September 1922... 2022.

evt-05-11-868-diamond-sutra.scenario: It is 868 in Tang-dynasty China. You are a devout craftsman overseeing the woodblock printing of a scroll of the Diamond Sutra, preparing its closing colophon before the copies are handed out.
evt-05-11-868-diamond-sutra.prompt: What does the colophon state as the purpose of printing this copy?

choices.text: To be buried alongside the dead as a funerary offering
For free distribution to earn religious merit for his parents
To be sold for profit in the marketplace
To serve as an official government legal record

evt-05-11-868-diamond-sutra.butterflyEffect: The colophon declared it was printed for free distribution as an act of merit dedicated to the printer's parents. Sealed away for centuries in the Dunhuang caves and rediscovered in 1900, it is recognized today as the world's oldest complete dated printed book, predating Gutenberg's press by nearly six centuries.

evt-05-11-1745-war-of-the-austrian-succe.scenario: It is 11 May 1745, and you march shoulder-to-shoulder in the Duke of Cumberland's great infantry column, pressing deep into the French lines at Fontenoy while cannon tear gaps in the ranks around you.
evt-05-11-1745-war-of-the-austrian-succe.prompt: What happens to the advancing allied column as it nears the French center?

choices.text: It is halted and driven back by French guns and the Irish Brigade's charge
It breaks through and seizes the French center outright
It withdraws before contact when Dutch allies refuse to advance
It outflanks the position and captures the village of Fontenoy

evt-05-11-1745-war-of-the-austrian-succe.butterflyEffect: French artillery and a devastating counterattack by the Irish Brigade shattered the column, forcing an allied retreat and securing a French victory. The win let Marshal Saxe overrun the Austrian Netherlands, while Britain's depleted forces at home helped embolden the Jacobite rising later that year.

evt-05-11-1812-spencer-perceval.scenario: You are standing in the lobby of the House of Commons on 11 May 1812 when a merchant named John Bellingham, nursing a long-standing grievance over unpaid compensation, steps toward Prime Minister Spencer Perceval.
evt-05-11-1812-spencer-perceval.prompt: What does Bellingham do as Perceval passes?

choices.text: He hands Perceval a written petition
He publicly denounces Perceval before the assembled members
He shoots Perceval with a pistol at close range
He attempts to seize Perceval and drag him outside

evt-05-11-1812-spencer-perceval.butterflyEffect: Bellingham shot Perceval point-blank, killing him instantly and making him the only British prime minister ever assassinated. Bellingham was tried and hanged within a week, and Lord Liverpool's succession kept Britain's war policy against Napoleon largely unchanged despite the shock.

evt-05-11-1813-william-lawson-explorer.scenario: You depart Sydney on 11 May 1813 with William Lawson and William Wentworth, determined to succeed where earlier expeditions failed at crossing the Blue Mountains into the colony's unknown interior.
evt-05-11-1813-william-lawson-explorer.prompt: What approach do you take to finally cross the mountains where others turned back?

choices.text: They follow the rivers upstream through the gorges
They keep to the ridge crests instead of descending into valleys
They sail around the range along the coast
They use convict labor to tunnel through the range

evt-05-11-1813-william-lawson-explorer.butterflyEffect: By following the ridgelines instead of the tangled river valleys that had defeated earlier explorers, the party reached the edge of the fertile Bathurst Plains. Their route was quickly turned into a road, triggering rapid pastoral expansion west of Sydney and easing the colony's land pressure.

evt-05-11-1820-hms-beagle.scenario: It is May 1820 at Woolwich Dockyard. HMS Beagle has just launched, but the Admiralty has no immediate mission for the new ten-gun brig, so she sits idle 'in ordinary,' stripped of masts and rigging.
evt-05-11-1820-hms-beagle.prompt: What does the Admiralty ultimately decide to do with the idle Beagle?

choices.text: Refit her as a hydrographic survey vessel
Sell her outright to a private trading company
Convert her permanently into a moored training hulk
Scrap her and sell the timber for parts

evt-05-11-1820-hms-beagle.butterflyEffect: Beagle was refitted as a survey vessel, and on her second voyage from 1831 to 1836 she carried a young naturalist, Charles Darwin, whose observations on that journey became the foundation of his theory of evolution.

evt-05-11-1858-minnesota.scenario: It is May 1858 and you are a delegate watching Minnesota enter the Union as the 32nd state, admitted free without a corresponding slave state joining alongside it.
evt-05-11-1858-minnesota.prompt: What does Minnesota's admission signal for the sectional balance in Congress?

choices.text: It triggers the simultaneous admission of a new slave state
It breaks the long-standing free/slave state pairing tradition
It delays statehood pending a new compromise bill
It grants slaveholders special transit rights through the territory

evt-05-11-1858-minnesota.butterflyEffect: Minnesota's free-state admission, followed by Oregon's in 1859, broke the old tradition of pairing free and slave states and tipped the Senate balance toward the North. The shift deepened Southern fears of political marginalization in the years leading to the 1860 election and secession.

evt-05-11-1880-southern-pacific-railroad.scenario: You have farmed this land near Hanford, California for years, believing the Southern Pacific Railroad promised you first right to buy it cheaply. Now a US marshal and railroad land agent ride up with eviction papers demanding you leave or pay the much higher market price.
evt-05-11-1880-southern-pacific-railroad.prompt: What happens when settlers confront the marshal's posse over the eviction?

choices.text: They peacefully vacate the land as ordered
A confrontation turns violent, leaving several dead on both sides
They win an injunction in federal court that day
They quietly resettle claims overnight before the marshal arrives

evt-05-11-1880-southern-pacific-railroad.butterflyEffect: The standoff erupted into gunfire, killing several settlers and members of the posse in what became known as the Mussel Slough Tragedy. The bloodshed turned public opinion against the railroad's land practices and inspired Frank Norris's novel The Octopus, fueling decades of populist anger at corporate power over farmers.

evt-05-11-1889-wham-paymaster-robbery.scenario: It is May 11, 1889, on a remote Arizona Territory road. You are one of the Buffalo Soldiers escorting Major Wham's wagon of gold and silver payroll when gunfire erupts from the rocks above, wounding several of your comrades.
evt-05-11-1889-wham-paymaster-robbery.prompt: With your escort outgunned and taking casualties, what do you do?

choices.text: Attempt to negotiate a surrender of the payroll for safe passage
Charge directly up the hillside at the ambushers
Abandon the wagon and ride for the nearest fort immediately
Retreat to cover and return fire as best you can

evt-05-11-1889-wham-paymaster-robbery.butterflyEffect: The soldiers were forced to retreat to cover as the bandits made off with over $28,000 in payroll, one of the largest such robberies in Army history. Despite strong evidence, local juries acquitted every suspect, while several of the wounded Buffalo Soldiers were later awarded Medals of Honor for their bravery under fire.

evt-05-11-1894-pullman-company.scenario: It is May 11, 1894, in the company town of Pullman, Illinois. Your wages have just been cut by 28 percent, yet the rent you owe the Pullman Company for your housing has not changed at all.
evt-05-11-1894-pullman-company.prompt: Alongside thousands of your fellow workers, what do you do?

choices.text: Petition only for a rent reduction while continuing to work
Accept the pay cut quietly to keep your job and housing
Walk out on strike alongside thousands of coworkers
Quit individually and seek work with a rival railroad company

evt-05-11-1894-pullman-company.butterflyEffect: The workers walked out, launching the Pullman Strike, which spread nationwide after the American Railway Union, led by Eugene Debs, boycotted trains hauling Pullman cars. Federal troops eventually broke the strike and Debs was jailed, but the unrest pushed Congress to swiftly establish Labor Day as a federal holiday that same year.

evt-05-11-1910-glacier-national-park-u-s.scenario: It's 11 May 1910 in Washington, D.C. President William Howard Taft has a bill on his desk that would set aside more than a million acres of Montana's Rocky Mountain wilderness, championed for years by conservationist George Bird Grinnell.
evt-05-11-1910-glacier-national-park-u-s.prompt: What does Taft do with the bill creating Glacier National Park?

choices.text: Send it back to Congress demanding more funding first
Sign it into law
Veto it under pressure from mining interests
Delay signing until railroads approved the boundaries

evt-05-11-1910-glacier-national-park-u-s.butterflyEffect: Taft signed the bill, making Glacier the United States' tenth national park and permanently protecting its glaciers, lakes, and peaks along the Canadian border. The park became a flagship of the growing conservation movement, helping build momentum toward the creation of the National Park Service in 1916.

evt-05-11-1970-lubbock-texas.scenario: It's the days after 11 May 1970 in Lubbock, Texas. A multi-vortex tornado has torn through downtown, and you are a severe-storms researcher standing in the wreckage, trying to figure out how fast the winds actually spun.
evt-05-11-1970-lubbock-texas.prompt: How do you determine the tornado's true wind speeds from the wreckage?

choices.text: Rely solely on eyewitness estimates of wind speed
Trace debris paths and damage patterns in photographs
Wait for anemometer readings from the storm's path
Use only the barometric pressure drop recorded nearby

evt-05-11-1970-lubbock-texas.butterflyEffect: Ted Fujita studied the Lubbock damage patterns and photographs to trace individual debris trajectories, discovering the tornado's multiple-vortex structure and using the data to refine his new Fujita scale. His findings reshaped how meteorologists estimate tornado intensity and issue warnings ever since.

evt-05-11-1981-andrew-lloyd-webber.scenario: It is May 11, 1981, and you are a skeptical West End producer watching the curtain rise on Cats at the New London Theatre, a plotless musical built from T.S. Eliot poems about dancing felines.
evt-05-11-1981-andrew-lloyd-webber.prompt: What ultimately happens to Cats after this uncertain opening night?

choices.text: It runs for over two decades, becoming one of the longest-running musicals ever
It is quickly adapted into a feature film that overshadows the stage show
It closes within weeks after poor reviews
It transfers to Broadway but is banned in London over rights disputes

evt-05-11-1981-andrew-lloyd-webber.butterflyEffect: Far from flopping, Cats became a phenomenon, running for 21 years in the West End and 18 on Broadway, winning Olivier and Tony Awards and becoming one of the longest-running musicals in theatre history. Its success helped cement Andrew Lloyd Webber as the dominant force in commercial musical theatre for decades.

evt-05-11-1997-deep-blue-chess-computer.scenario: It is 11 May 1997, Game 6 of your rematch against IBM's supercomputer in New York. You are Garry Kasparov, and the machine has just played an unnervingly clever knight sacrifice you cannot fully calculate.
evt-05-11-1997-deep-blue-chess-computer.prompt: Facing the sacrifice, do you fight on or resign the game?

choices.text: Demand an adjournment to analyze overnight
Play on, hoping the machine miscalculates
Offer a draw to end the match evenly
Resign, believing the position is lost

evt-05-11-1997-deep-blue-chess-computer.butterflyEffect: Kasparov resigned after just 19 moves, giving Deep Blue the match and making it the first computer to beat a reigning world champion under standard time controls. The result fueled decades of debate over AI's limits, accusations of hidden human help (later dismissed), and spurred research that eventually produced systems like AlphaGo.

evt-05-11-2011-2011-lorca-earthquake.scenario: It is the evening of 11 May 2011 in Lorca, Spain. At 17:05 a magnitude-4.4 foreshock has cracked walls and toppled part of the historic Espolón Tower, and you and your neighbours must decide what to do next.
evt-05-11-2011-2011-lorca-earthquake.prompt: What should residents do in the hour after the foreshock, before any stronger tremor?

choices.text: Stay outdoors, away from damaged buildings
Assume the tremor was a one-off and resume normal routines
Take shelter inside the historic tower for safety
Go back inside quickly to gather belongings

evt-05-11-2011-2011-lorca-earthquake.butterflyEffect: A far stronger 5.1 Mw quake struck barely two hours later, collapsing weakened facades and killing several people, some by falling cornices from damaged buildings. The disaster prompted Spain to review seismic building codes in a region long considered low-risk.

evt-05-11-2013-2013-reyhanl-car-bombings.scenario: It is May 11, 2013, in the Turkish border town of Reyhanlı. You are a local security official surveying the wreckage of two car bombs that have just torn through the crowded streets near the Syrian frontier.
evt-05-11-2013-2013-reyhanl-car-bombings.prompt: Who did Turkish authorities blame and act against in the investigation that followed?

choices.text: An Islamic State affiliate operating in Iraq
A far-right Turkish nationalist cell
A leftist militant group accused of ties to Syrian intelligence
The Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK)

evt-05-11-2013-2013-reyhanl-car-bombings.butterflyEffect: Turkish officials blamed a Marxist-Leninist militant group they said had ties to Syrian intelligence, and arrested several suspects with alleged links to Damascus. The bombings deepened Turkish-Syrian hostility during the Syrian civil war and heightened fears that the conflict was spilling violently across the border.

evt-05-11-2022-shireen-abu-akleh.scenario: It is May 11, 2022, in the Jenin refugee camp. You are a foreign correspondent standing beside Shireen Abu Akleh, both of you wearing marked blue press vests as you cover an Israeli military raid.
evt-05-11-2022-shireen-abu-akleh.prompt: In the aftermath of her killing, what did the ensuing investigations conclude?

choices.text: They concluded a Palestinian militant fired the fatal shot
They closed the case within days with no findings released
They concluded the shot likely came from Israeli military gunfire, but no charges followed
They found the death was caused by an accidental grenade explosion

evt-05-11-2022-shireen-abu-akleh.butterflyEffect: Multiple investigations, including one by the U.S. State Department, concluded the fatal shot likely came from Israeli forces but found no intent to kill and no one was ever charged. The case became a flashpoint over press safety and accountability in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, drawing international condemnation and calls for independent inquiries.

evt-05-11-2024-may-2024-solar-storms.scenario: It's 10 May 2024, planting season in the American Midwest. You're a farmer relying on a GPS-guided autosteer tractor as an unusually intense geomagnetic storm ripples overhead, and your guidance display suddenly starts drifting off course.
evt-05-11-2024-may-2024-solar-storms.prompt: As your GPS steering loses accuracy mid-field, what should you do?

choices.text: Switch to manual steering until the signal stabilizes
Shut down all field operations for the week
Keep trusting the autosteer system as normal
Recalibrate the GPS receiver's internal clock

evt-05-11-2024-may-2024-solar-storms.butterflyEffect: The storm's disturbance of satellite signals disrupted precision-agriculture GPS across parts of the U.S. Midwest, causing crooked planting rows and forcing many farmers to switch to manual steering during a critical planting window. It exposed how dependent modern agriculture had become on space-weather-sensitive technology.

evt-05-11-2024-eurovision-song-contest-2.scenario: It's the night of 11 May 2024 in Malmö Arena. The jury and public votes are tallying, and a Swiss entry with an unconventional, genre-defying performance is climbing toward the top of the leaderboard.
evt-05-11-2024-eurovision-song-contest-2.prompt: Who is crowned winner of the Eurovision Song Contest 2024?

choices.text: Angelina Mango, representing Italy
Nemo, representing Switzerland
Baby Lasagna, representing Croatia
Loreen, representing Sweden again

evt-05-11-2024-eurovision-song-contest-2.butterflyEffect: Nemo won for Switzerland with "The Code," becoming the first openly non-binary artist to win Eurovision and giving Switzerland its third victory. The win sparked wide discussion about gender identity and inclusion within the contest's future direction.

evt-05-12-1743-war-of-the-austrian-succe.scenario: Prague Castle, 12 May 1743. Austrian troops have driven out the Bavarian and French occupiers, and you stand among the assembled nobles as Maria Theresa prepares for her coronation ceremony.
evt-05-12-1743-war-of-the-austrian-succe.prompt: What crown is placed upon Maria Theresa at this Prague ceremony?

choices.text: The Imperial Crown of the Holy Roman Empire
The Crown of Saint Stephen, as Queen of Hungary
The Crown of Saint Wenceslas, as Queen of Bohemia
The Crown of Charlemagne

evt-05-12-1743-war-of-the-austrian-succe.butterflyEffect: She was crowned Queen of Bohemia with the Crown of Saint Wenceslas, reasserting Habsburg authority over a kingdom recently held by rival claimants. The coronation strengthened her legitimacy during the War of the Austrian Succession, helping secure her hereditary lands by the war's end.

evt-05-12-1846-donner-party.scenario: It is July 1846 near Fort Bridger, and you are traveling with the Donner Party. A trader urges you to try Lansford Hastings's new 'shortcut' to California instead of the proven trail.
evt-05-12-1846-donner-party.prompt: What is the wiser choice for the party at this fork in the trail?

choices.text: Split the wagons and send scouts ahead alone
Turn back east to wait out the season
Take Hastings Cutoff to save time
Stay on the established California Trail via Fort Hall

evt-05-12-1846-donner-party.butterflyEffect: The party ignored the proven route and took Hastings Cutoff, which cost weeks crossing the Wasatch Mountains and Great Salt Lake Desert. That delay left them trapped by early snow in the Sierra Nevada that winter, leading to starvation and the resort to cannibalism for which the group is remembered.

evt-05-12-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 12 May 1863, and you command a Confederate brigade near Raymond, Mississippi, believing you face only a small Union raiding party while Grant's real objective, Vicksburg, still seems far off.
evt-05-12-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: What happens when your brigade discovers the true size of the Union force before it?

choices.text: The brigade counterattacks and captures Grant's supply train
The brigade is routed and retreats in disorder toward Jackson
The brigade stands its ground and destroys the Union force
The brigade surrenders without a fight

evt-05-12-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Gregg's outnumbered Confederates were routed and forced to retreat toward Jackson. The unexpected fight convinced Grant to turn first against Jackson before pivoting on Vicksburg, a decision that helped isolate the Confederate stronghold, which surrendered after siege on 4 July 1863.

evt-05-12-1881-french-conquest-of-tunisi.scenario: It is spring 1881. French troops mass on the Algerian-Tunisian border and gunboats appear off the coast. As Muhammad III as-Sadiq, Bey of Tunis, you must respond to France's ultimatum before soldiers march on your capital.

choices.text: Flee into exile before French forces arrive
Refuse and appeal to the Ottoman Sultan for military aid
Declare war on France immediately
Sign the treaty accepting French protection

evt-05-12-1881-french-conquest-of-tunisi.butterflyEffect: The Bey signed the Treaty of Bardo, accepting French protection over Tunisia. A subsequent Tunisian rebellion was crushed by French forces later that year, cementing a protectorate that would last until Tunisian independence in 1956.

evt-05-12-1926-norge-airship.scenario: May 1926, aboard the airship Norge as it cruises toward 90°N under Roald Amundsen's command. The crew has trained for this exact moment for months.
evt-05-12-1926-norge-airship.prompt: What does the crew do upon reaching the North Pole?

choices.text: Parachute a crew member down to stand at the Pole
Turn back immediately without marking the location
Land the airship on the ice to plant a flag by hand
Drop the flags of Norway, Italy, and the United States onto the ice

evt-05-12-1926-norge-airship.butterflyEffect: The crew dropped the flags of Norway, Italy, and the United States onto the ice below, marking the achievement without landing. The flight proved a controlled aircraft could cross the polar cap, but rivalry between Amundsen and pilot Umberto Nobile deepened, and Nobile's push to repeat the feat led to the fatal Italia airship disaster in 1928.

evt-05-12-1932-rohm-scandal.scenario: It is 12 May 1932 inside the Reichstag building. You watch a group of Nazi deputies surround journalist Helmuth Klotz, furious that he has republished Ernst Röhm's private letters exposing the SA leader's homosexuality.
evt-05-12-1932-rohm-scandal.prompt: What happens next on the floor of parliament?

choices.text: Röhm challenges Klotz to a duel outside
The deputies issue a calm written rebuttal instead
Hitler orders Röhm's immediate dismissal from the SA
The deputies physically assault Klotz on the chamber floor

evt-05-12-1932-rohm-scandal.butterflyEffect: The Nazi deputies physically assaulted Klotz in the chamber. The scandal exposed tension between the party's public morality rhetoric and Röhm's private life, but Hitler kept him in command of the SA to preserve loyalty. Rivalries stirred by the affair fed into the suspicions that led to Röhm's killing in the 1934 Night of the Long Knives.

evt-05-12-1941-konrad-zuse.scenario: Berlin, May 1941. Konrad Zuse invites engineers and potential backers to watch his new machine, the Z3, calculate automatically from a program without human intervention at each step.
evt-05-12-1941-konrad-zuse.prompt: What breakthrough does the Z3 demonstrate to its audience?

choices.text: A mechanical differential analyzer for calculus
Electronic computing using vacuum tubes
A punched-card business accounting machine
Fully program-controlled binary calculation via relay logic

evt-05-12-1941-konrad-zuse.butterflyEffect: The Z3 was the world's first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer, using binary floating-point arithmetic controlled by punched film. Though destroyed in an Allied bombing raid in 1943, its design later earned Zuse recognition as a father of the modern computer.

evt-05-12-1948-high-explosive-research.scenario: It is 12 May 1948, and you sit in the House of Commons as the government reveals, for the first time, that Britain has secretly been building its own atomic bomb since early 1947.
evt-05-12-1948-high-explosive-research.prompt: What choice does this announcement confirm about Britain's nuclear path?

choices.text: Britain will develop the atomic bomb independently rather than depend on American cooperation
Britain will halt all weapons work and rely entirely on the American nuclear umbrella
Britain will merge its atomic program with France's nuclear effort
Britain will request renewed sharing under the wartime Quebec Agreement instead of building alone

evt-05-12-1948-high-explosive-research.butterflyEffect: Britain committed to building the bomb without depending on American technology, a program that culminated in the successful Operation Hurricane test off Australia in October 1952, making Britain the world's third nuclear power. The decision had been driven partly by the US Congress's 1946 McMahon Act, which had cut off the wartime nuclear-sharing arrangement between the two countries.

evt-05-12-1967-jimi-hendrix.scenario: London, 12 May 1967. You're a fan outside a record shop as the Jimi Hendrix Experience's debut LP hits shelves, full of fuzz-toned guitar and psychedelic sound unlike anything on the radio.
evt-05-12-1967-jimi-hendrix.prompt: Which album has just been released, launching Hendrix to stardom?

choices.text: Axis: Bold as Love
Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
Are You Experienced
Electric Ladyland

evt-05-12-1967-jimi-hendrix.butterflyEffect: Are You Experienced fused blues, psychedelia, and radical guitar effects like wah-wah and feedback, instantly marking Hendrix as a revolutionary force. Its influence reshaped how rock guitarists approached tone and technique for decades afterward.

evt-05-12-1968-vietnam-war.scenario: It is the night of 12 May 1968. Your Australian task force has only just dug in at newly established Fire Support Base Coral, north of Saigon, when North Vietnamese infantry surge out of the darkness against your unfinished perimeter.
evt-05-12-1968-vietnam-war.prompt: How do the defenders respond to hold the base through the night?

choices.text: Abandon the base immediately and retreat to Saigon
Attempt to negotiate a local ceasefire with the attackers
Call in artillery and air support while digging in to hold the perimeter
Hold fire and wait silently for the attackers to withdraw on their own

evt-05-12-1968-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: The garrison held on with close artillery support and reinforcement by tanks and extra infantry over the following days, in what became the costliest single action for Australian forces in the Vietnam War. The engagement, later named the Battle of Coral–Balmoral, exposed how exposed newly landed fire support bases were to determined North Vietnamese assault and changed how such bases were sited and defended afterward.

evt-05-12-1975-mayaguez-incident.scenario: It is 15 May 1975. You command Marines about to assault Koh Tang island to free the SS Mayaguez crew, but unconfirmed reports suggest the Khmer Rouge may already be releasing the hostages elsewhere.
evt-05-12-1975-mayaguez-incident.prompt: Do you launch the assault as planned, or hold for confirmation the crew is safe?

choices.text: Proceed with the assault on Koh Tang as planned
Wait for additional carrier reinforcements before moving
Cancel the operation and await diplomatic confirmation
Send unarmed negotiators ashore first

evt-05-12-1975-mayaguez-incident.butterflyEffect: The assault went ahead as planned. The crew was released unharmed by the Khmer Rouge shortly after fighting began, but Marines met fierce resistance, losing three helicopters. Three Marines left behind on Koh Tang were later executed; their names are the last inscribed on the Vietnam Veterans Memorial.

evt-05-12-1982-coppergate-helmet.scenario: It is May 1982, and you are part of the excavation crew digging beneath Coppergate in York ahead of the new Jorvik Viking Centre. At the bottom of what looks like an old well, your trowel strikes metal, revealing ornate decoration beneath centuries of soil.
evt-05-12-1982-coppergate-helmet.prompt: How do you handle the fragile find before removing it?

choices.text: Carefully record its position and lift it in a soil block for lab conservation
Pry the object free by hand to identify it immediately
Pour water over it on site to wash away the dirt
Rebury the pit and leave the object for a later excavation season

evt-05-12-1982-coppergate-helmet.butterflyEffect: The team carefully block-lifted the soil around the object for laboratory conservation. It proved to be an eighth-century Anglo-Saxon helmet, one of only six known to survive, remarkably preserved by its burial in the pit. It became a centerpiece of the Yorkshire Museum and reshaped understanding of Anglo-Saxon Northumbrian craftsmanship.

evt-05-12-1998-trisakti-shootings.scenario: You join thousands of students at Trisakti University in Jakarta on 12 May 1998, chanting for President Suharto's resignation, when soldiers suddenly open fire on the unarmed crowd.
evt-05-12-1998-trisakti-shootings.prompt: What did the deaths of the four students trigger in the days that followed?

choices.text: A nationwide closure of all universities for a year
An immediate military coup against Suharto
Nationwide riots that forced Suharto's resignation weeks later
United Nations peacekeepers deploying to Jakarta

evt-05-12-1998-trisakti-shootings.butterflyEffect: The killings ignited massive riots across Jakarta and a nationwide wave of protest that made Suharto's position untenable. He resigned before the end of the month, ending his 32-year rule and beginning Indonesia's Reformasi era.
