evt-05-12-2008-2008-sichuan-earthquake.scenario: Days after the Sichuan earthquake, you are an official touring Beichuan and see school buildings pancaked to rubble while neighboring government offices stand largely intact, angering grieving parents.
evt-05-12-2008-2008-sichuan-earthquake.prompt: How does the government respond to mounting anger over the collapsed schools?

choices.text: Blame the collapses solely on earthquake magnitude and close the matter
Pledge investigations into school construction standards
Ban journalists from covering damaged schools
Demolish all surviving schools regardless of condition

evt-05-12-2008-2008-sichuan-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Public fury over so-called "tofu-dreg" school construction forced officials to promise investigations into shoddy building standards, though full accountability for local corruption remained limited. The disaster also prompted China's first national day of mourning for ordinary citizens and lasting scrutiny of construction codes.

evt-05-12-2010-tripoli-international-air.scenario: It is dawn on 12 May 2010. Your Airbus A330 is on final approach into Tripoli after an overnight flight, the runway obscured by haze as the crew continues the descent.
evt-05-12-2010-tripoli-international-air.prompt: What did investigators later conclude went wrong on this approach?

choices.text: An engine failed catastrophically during descent
A bomb detonated in the cargo hold
The crew continued descending below a safe altitude without proper visual reference to the runway
The aircraft suffered a bird strike on both engines

evt-05-12-2010-tripoli-international-air.butterflyEffect: The aircraft struck the ground short of the runway; 103 of the 104 people aboard died, with a nine-year-old Dutch boy the sole survivor found in the wreckage. Investigators found the crew had continued descending without adequate visual reference to the runway, and the disaster intensified scrutiny of approach procedures and safety oversight at Libyan airports in the years that followed.

evt-05-12-2015-may-2015-nepal-earthquake.scenario: It is 12 May 2015. You are coordinating earthquake relief in Sindhupalchowk, already stretched thin from the April 25 disaster, when a powerful new tremor strikes districts further east near Kodari.
evt-05-12-2015-may-2015-nepal-earthquake.prompt: How should relief teams respond to this fresh, unexpected shock?

choices.text: Redirect teams and supplies toward the newly hit districts
Withdraw foreign aid workers immediately for safety
Continue focusing only on the original April quake zone
Suspend all relief operations until seismologists confirm the cause

evt-05-12-2015-may-2015-nepal-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The quake, centered near Kodari on the border of Dolakha and Sindhupalchowk, was later classified as an aftershock of the April 25 disaster despite its own severity. It struck already-devastated communities and triggered fresh landslides, further overwhelming Nepal's strained relief effort.

evt-05-12-2015-2015-philadelphia-train-d.scenario: You are the engineer of Amtrak Northeast Regional 188 approaching the sharp curve at Frankford Junction in Philadelphia on 12 May 2015, where signage warns of a 50 mph limit.
evt-05-12-2015-2015-philadelphia-train-d.prompt: What fatal error occurred as the train entered the curve?

choices.text: A signal malfunction routed the train onto the wrong track
The engineer accelerated far above the posted speed limit before the curve
The brakes failed mechanically without warning
Heavy rain had washed out the track bed

evt-05-12-2015-2015-philadelphia-train-d.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the train was traveling at 102 mph—more than double the posted limit—when it derailed, killing eight and injuring over 200. The disaster accelerated the mandated rollout of Positive Train Control safety systems across the Northeast Corridor.

evt-05-12-2022-event-horizon-telescope.scenario: April 2022, a global press conference. Astronomers who spent years combining data from radio telescopes across the planet are about to unveil an image years in the making.
evt-05-12-2022-event-horizon-telescope.prompt: What object does the Event Horizon Telescope reveal in this image?

choices.text: The black hole at the center of galaxy M87, for the first time
The dense star cluster orbiting the galactic center
A newly discovered exoplanet near the galactic core
The shadow of Sagittarius A*, the Milky Way's central black hole

evt-05-12-2022-event-horizon-telescope.butterflyEffect: The image showed the shadow of Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the Milky Way's center, matching predictions of general relativity despite it being far smaller and closer than the previously imaged M87 black hole. This confirmed that black hole physics holds consistently across vastly different scales.

evt-05-12-2024-may-2024-solar-storms.scenario: It is mid-May 2024, and the strongest geomagnetic storm to hit Earth since 1989 is disrupting satellite signals. You operate a fleet of GPS-guided tractors in the American Midwest during peak planting season.
evt-05-12-2024-may-2024-solar-storms.prompt: What should you do as your equipment's GPS accuracy suddenly collapses?

choices.text: Switch to manual steering until satellite accuracy is restored
Keep trusting the GPS coordinates as normal
Ignore the storm since it has no effect on agricultural equipment
Shut down the entire regional power grid as a precaution

evt-05-12-2024-may-2024-solar-storms.butterflyEffect: Many farmers across the US Midwest found their precision GPS-guided equipment unreliable during the storm and had to switch to manual operation, delaying planting for some. The same storm produced auroras visible as far south as Florida and Mexico, and prompted power grid operators worldwide to activate protective protocols, though widespread blackouts were avoided.

evt-05-13-1110-baldwin-i-of-jerusalem.scenario: It is 1110, and you serve among the Genoese sailors whose fleet has anchored off Beirut to aid King Baldwin I's siege. The Fatimid garrison holds the walls, but your ships block any hope of resupply by sea.
evt-05-13-1110-baldwin-i-of-jerusalem.prompt: What should the crusader force do to take the city?

choices.text: Withdraw and wait for the garrison to surrender out of hunger alone
Offer the Fatimid governor a truce in exchange for tribute
Abandon the siege and march inland toward Damascus instead
Blockade the harbor by sea while battering the land walls with siege engines

evt-05-13-1110-baldwin-i-of-jerusalem.butterflyEffect: Beirut fell after the combined land-and-sea assault, adding another key port to the Kingdom of Jerusalem. The Genoese and Pisan fleets that helped take it were rewarded with lucrative trading quarters, cementing Italian mercantile power across the crusader states for generations.

evt-05-13-1913-igor-sikorsky.scenario: It's 13 May 1913 near St. Petersburg. You are Igor Sikorsky, standing beside your Russky Vityaz, a strange four-engine machine rivals insist is too heavy and complicated to ever leave the ground.
evt-05-13-1913-igor-sikorsky.prompt: What happens when Sikorsky takes the Russky Vityaz into the air?

choices.text: It flies briefly but is dismissed as impractical and scrapped
It fails to leave the ground due to engine failure
It becomes the first successful four-engine aircraft to fly
It crashes on takeoff, ending the project

evt-05-13-1913-igor-sikorsky.butterflyEffect: The flight succeeded, making the Russky Vityaz the first successful four-engine aircraft in history. Sikorsky refined the concept into the Ilya Muromets, which became the world's first four-engine bomber, shaping the future of large multi-engine aviation for decades.

evt-05-13-1958-richard-nixon.scenario: It's 13 May 1958 and you're riding in Vice President Nixon's motorcade through Caracas on his goodwill tour of South America. Suddenly an anti-American mob surrounds the car, spitting on the windows and rocking it violently.
evt-05-13-1958-richard-nixon.prompt: How does the motorcade escape the mob in Caracas?

choices.text: The car is overturned and Nixon is briefly held hostage
Secret Service and Venezuelan police force the car through the crowd
Venezuelan troops open fire to disperse the crowd before it reaches the car
Nixon is evacuated by helicopter before the mob arrives

evt-05-13-1958-richard-nixon.butterflyEffect: Secret Service agents and Venezuelan police forced the car through the crowd and Nixon emerged unharmed, though shaken. The incident, occurring amid fierce anti-American sentiment after the fall of dictator Marcos Pérez Jiménez, alarmed Washington and helped push the Eisenhower administration toward a more aid-focused Latin America policy that Kennedy later formalized as the Alliance for Progress.

evt-05-13-1969-13-may-incident.scenario: It is 13 May 1969 in Kuala Lumpur. Opposition parties have just made stunning gains against the ruling Alliance Party, and jubilant supporters parading through the streets have collided with counter-demonstrators, sparking violence between Malay and Chinese residents.
evt-05-13-1969-13-may-incident.prompt: How did the Malaysian government respond to restore order?

choices.text: Declared a state of emergency and suspended Parliament
Opened power-sharing talks with opposition leaders that week
Called an immediate new general election
Requested British Commonwealth troops to intervene

evt-05-13-1969-13-may-incident.butterflyEffect: A state of emergency was declared and Parliament was suspended for nearly two years while the National Operations Council ruled by decree. The crisis led directly to the New Economic Policy, an affirmative-action program for the Malay majority that reshaped Malaysian politics and economics for decades.

evt-05-13-1985-philadelphia-police-depar.scenario: It is May 13, 1985, and you are a Philadelphia official overseeing a tense standoff on Osage Avenue, where the MOVE group has barricaded itself inside a rowhouse and exchanged gunfire with police for hours.
evt-05-13-1985-philadelphia-police-depar.prompt: What did the police commissioner ultimately order to end the standoff?

choices.text: Evacuate the block and withdraw police entirely overnight
Drop an explosive device onto the roof of the house
Cut off power and water and wait out the standoff
Send in negotiators to talk MOVE members into surrendering

evt-05-13-1985-philadelphia-police-depar.butterflyEffect: A police helicopter dropped an explosive device on the roof; the resulting fire was allowed to burn, killing eleven people, including five children, and destroying 61 homes in the neighborhood. The disaster brought lasting scrutiny of police tactics, and in 2020 the Philadelphia City Council formally apologized for the bombing.

evt-05-13-1989-1989-tiananmen-square-pro.scenario: It is mid-May 1989, and you are one of thousands of students occupying Tiananmen Square, now weakened by a hunger strike, as officials warn that their patience is running out.
evt-05-13-1989-1989-tiananmen-square-pro.prompt: What do you decide to do?

choices.text: Disperse immediately and return to your studies
Continue the occupation and hunger strike, hoping to force dialogue
Attack government buildings to escalate pressure
Ask the military to intervene on the protesters' behalf

evt-05-13-1989-1989-tiananmen-square-pro.butterflyEffect: The students stayed, and the government declared martial law days later. On the night of 3–4 June, troops and tanks moved into the square, crushing the protest by force. The crackdown brought international condemnation and decades of strict censorship around the event in China.

evt-05-13-1992-li-hongzhi.scenario: It is May 13, 1992, and you are among the crowd gathered in Changchun to hear a little-known teacher named Li Hongzhi introduce a new system of meditation and exercises he calls Falun Gong.
evt-05-13-1992-li-hongzhi.prompt: What happened to the movement Li Hongzhi launched that day?

choices.text: It grew into a mass movement later banned and suppressed by the Chinese government
It was immediately endorsed and promoted by the Chinese state
It remained a small local qigong club with little further attention
It merged with an existing officially recognized Buddhist association

evt-05-13-1992-li-hongzhi.butterflyEffect: Falun Gong spread rapidly across China through the 1990s, drawing tens of millions of practitioners. By 1999 the Chinese government banned it as a threat to social stability, launching a sustained crackdown that continues to draw international condemnation as one of the largest religious persecution campaigns of the modern era.

evt-05-13-1995-alison-hargreaves.scenario: You are Alison Hargreaves, standing at the South Col of Mount Everest in May 1995. You have already soloed every great north face in the Alps in a single season, and now you face the final push to the summit with no supplementary oxygen and no Sherpa support team.
evt-05-13-1995-alison-hargreaves.prompt: How do you approach the final ascent to become the first woman to summit Everest this way?

choices.text: Hire a Sherpa team to carry extra oxygen bottles as backup
Climb entirely alone, relying only on her own acclimatization and pace
Join a large commercial expedition for safety in numbers
Turn back and wait for a support team to fix ropes ahead of her

evt-05-13-1995-alison-hargreaves.butterflyEffect: Hargreaves reached the summit solo and without oxygen on 13 May 1995, a landmark in mountaineering. Just months later, in August 1995, she died descending K2 in a storm, and her career became a lasting point of debate about risk-taking by climbers who are also parents.

evt-05-13-1998-may-1998-indonesia-riots.scenario: It is May 13, 1998, and you run a shop in Jakarta's Chinese quarter as mobs move through the streets, looting and burning businesses owned by ethnic Chinese residents amid the economic crisis gripping Indonesia.
evt-05-13-1998-may-1998-indonesia-riots.prompt: What did many ethnic Chinese Indonesians do in the days that followed to survive the unrest?

choices.text: Report the violence to international media and wait for foreign intervention
Flee the city or leave the country until the violence subsided
Stay and openly confront the mobs to defend their property
Organize armed neighborhood militias to retaliate against attackers

evt-05-13-1998-may-1998-indonesia-riots.butterflyEffect: Thousands fled the country or went into hiding as the riots, looting, and violence against ethnic Chinese communities spread through several cities. The unrest fatally weakened President Suharto's grip on power, and he resigned just over a week later on May 21, 1998, ending his 32-year rule.

evt-05-13-2000-enschede-fireworks-disast.scenario: You are a fire officer arriving at a small blaze inside the SE Fireworks storage depot in Enschede on 13 May 2000. Residential streets sit close to the depot's fences, and you have no way of knowing how much explosive material is actually stored inside.
evt-05-13-2000-enschede-fireworks-disast.prompt: What is the safest immediate response to a fire at a fireworks storage site like this?

choices.text: Order a wide-area evacuation before attempting to fight the fire directly
Wait for the depot's own staff to assess the danger first
Focus only on protecting the nearest houses rather than evacuating them
Approach and fight the fire at close range as standard training dictates

evt-05-13-2000-enschede-fireworks-disast.butterflyEffect: The stored quantities far exceeded legal limits, and the fire escalated into a massive explosion that killed 23 people, including four firefighters, and destroyed hundreds of homes. The disaster forced the Netherlands to rewrite fireworks storage regulations, mandating much larger safety buffers between depots and residential areas.

evt-05-13-2006-2006-sao-paulo-violence-o.scenario: It is the night of May 12 into May 13, 2006, and you are a São Paulo state security commander as coordinated attacks on police stations, buses, and banks erupt across the city, ordered from inside the prison system.
evt-05-13-2006-2006-sao-paulo-violence-o.prompt: How did state authorities respond to the wave of coordinated attacks?

choices.text: Declare a state of emergency and suspend all public transport indefinitely
Open negotiations with imprisoned gang leaders for a truce
Deploy heavily armed police and lock down prisons across the state
Call in the national army to occupy São Paulo's favelas

evt-05-13-2006-2006-sao-paulo-violence-o.butterflyEffect: Police launched a massive crackdown that spread to other states, but the response was marred by widely reported reprisal killings of civilians by security forces, drawing international human rights criticism. The crisis exposed the reach of the prison-based Primeiro Comando da Capital, whose influence over Brazilian crime and politics only grew in the years that followed.

evt-05-13-2008-indian-mujahideen.scenario: It's the evening of 13 May 2008 in Jaipur's crowded Johari Bazaar. Nine bicycle-mounted bombs explode in rapid succession through the old city, and investigators have no idea who is responsible.
evt-05-13-2008-indian-mujahideen.prompt: Which previously unknown group later claimed responsibility for the Jaipur bombings?

choices.text: Harkat-ul-Jihad-al-Islami
Students' Islamic Movement of India
Lashkar-e-Taiba
Indian Mujahideen

evt-05-13-2008-indian-mujahideen.butterflyEffect: The attacks marked the emergence of the Indian Mujahideen as a distinct terror brand, having grown out of the banned Students' Islamic Movement of India. The group went on to strike several more Indian cities over the following years, and the wave of bombings helped push India to create the National Investigation Agency in 2009.

evt-05-13-2011-2011-charsadda-bombing.scenario: It's 13 May 2011 at Shabqadar Fort in Charsadda. You are a Frontier Constabulary cadet finally boarding a bus for ten days' leave after weeks of grueling training, unaware two suicide bombers are already waiting among the crowd.
evt-05-13-2011-2011-charsadda-bombing.prompt: What motive did the militant group later claim for this attack?

choices.text: Protest against a Pakistani army offensive in Swat
Anger over NATO drone strikes in Waziristan
Retaliation for the death of a local militant commander
Revenge for Osama bin Laden's killing by US forces

evt-05-13-2011-2011-charsadda-bombing.butterflyEffect: The Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan claimed the bombing as revenge for the killing of Osama bin Laden by US forces in Abbottabad eleven days earlier. The attack deepened scrutiny of Pakistan's security services just as US-Pakistan relations were already strained by bin Laden's discovery on Pakistani soil.

evt-05-13-2014-soma-mine-disaster.scenario: It is 13 May 2014 in Soma, Manisa. You are a mining engineer reviewing safety reports for the Eynez coal mine just before blasting begins at shift change, amid earlier warnings about ventilation and gas risks underground.
evt-05-13-2014-soma-mine-disaster.prompt: What does the disaster prompt authorities to do in its aftermath?

choices.text: Immediately privatize all state-run mines for efficiency
Award the mine operator a safety commendation
Ban coal mining nationwide within a year
Launch investigations and prosecute mine officials over safety failures

evt-05-13-2014-soma-mine-disaster.butterflyEffect: After 301 miners died, investigations exposed serious regulatory and safety failures at the mine. Several company officials faced prosecution, and the disaster triggered nationwide protests over labor conditions, pushing mine safety enforcement into sharper public and political focus across Turkey.

evt-05-13-2017-eurovision-song-contest-2.scenario: You are Salvador Sobral, about to walk onto the Eurovision stage in Kyiv representing Portugal, a country that has never won in over fifty years of trying. Every rival act around you is rehearsing pyrotechnics, dancers, and giant LED screens.
evt-05-13-2017-eurovision-song-contest-2.prompt: What staging choice do you make for your song "Amar pelos dois"?

choices.text: Perform a minimalist, understated arrangement with just himself at the microphone
Project elaborate video graphics behind him throughout the song
Bring on a troupe of backup dancers for a high-energy routine
Add a full pyrotechnic display to match the other finalists

evt-05-13-2017-eurovision-song-contest-2.butterflyEffect: Sobral performed the stripped-down jazz ballad with no dancers or effects, just himself and later his sister Luísa on a near-bare stage, and won by the largest points margin in the contest's history at that time. Portugal's first-ever victory ended a 53-year losing streak and earned Lisbon the right to host Eurovision 2018.

evt-05-14-1264-second-barons-war.scenario: It is 14 May 1264 near Lewes. You fight in King Henry III's army as Simon de Montfort's baronial forces charge down from the Downs, scattering the royalist ranks and surrounding the king's own position.
evt-05-14-1264-second-barons-war.prompt: What happened to Henry III after the battle was lost?

choices.text: He escaped and fled into exile in France
He was killed on the field, ending the Plantagenet line
He was captured and forced to accept baronial rule
He negotiated a truce that immediately ended the war

evt-05-14-1264-second-barons-war.butterflyEffect: Henry III was captured and forced to accept government by a baronial council, with de Montfort broadening parliament to include representatives of the commons for the first time. The arrangement collapsed within a year when de Montfort was killed at the Battle of Evesham, but the precedent of a wider parliament endured.

evt-05-14-1804-meriwether-lewis.scenario: It's 14 May 1804, and you stand with the Corps of Discovery as your boats push off from Camp Dubois into the Missouri River's current, bound for unmapped country.
evt-05-14-1804-meriwether-lewis.prompt: What is the expedition's primary mission as you head upriver?

choices.text: Establish a permanent fur-trading colony under direct federal control
Find a practical water route to the Pacific and assert U.S. claims over the Louisiana Purchase
Negotiate the purchase of Spanish Florida from local governors
Reinforce the garrison at Detroit against British incursions

evt-05-14-1804-meriwether-lewis.butterflyEffect: Lewis and Clark spent over two years mapping a route to the Pacific, cataloguing species, and negotiating with dozens of Native nations. Their reports fueled American westward expansion and fur trade interest, reshaping U.S. relations with Indigenous peoples across the continent for generations.

evt-05-14-1857-mindon-min.scenario: It's 1857, and you advise the newly crowned King Mindon of Burma, who is determined to strengthen his kingdom after Britain's annexation of Lower Burma five years earlier.
evt-05-14-1857-mindon-min.prompt: What major step does Mindon take to modernize and secure his kingdom?

choices.text: He closes the kingdom entirely to foreign trade and diplomats
He founds a new royal capital at Mandalay and pursues administrative reforms
He allies militarily with France to expel the British by force
He voluntarily cedes Upper Burma to avoid further conflict

evt-05-14-1857-mindon-min.butterflyEffect: Mindon founded a new royal capital at Mandalay and pursued administrative, military, and monetary reforms while sponsoring the Fifth Buddhist Council, cementing his reputation as one of Burma's most revered kings. Yet his efforts to hold off British encroachment ultimately failed: his son Thibaw lost Upper Burma to Britain in 1885.

evt-05-14-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It is May 14, 1863. You serve under General Sherman as Union forces seize Jackson, Mississippi, the state capital, during the campaign to isolate the Confederate stronghold at Vicksburg.
evt-05-14-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: What do Union troops do after taking Jackson?

choices.text: Withdraw north to consolidate forces at Memphis
Destroy railroads and war supplies to cripple aid to Vicksburg
March directly on Vicksburg without securing Jackson further
Garrison the city permanently and end the campaign there

evt-05-14-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Sherman's men destroyed railroads, factories, and military supplies in Jackson, earning it the nickname "Chimneyville." This crippled the Confederacy's ability to reinforce or resupply Vicksburg, and Union forces turned west to besiege the city, which fell on July 4, 1863, splitting the Confederacy along the Mississippi River.

evt-05-14-1868-boshin-war.scenario: It is 14 May 1868 and you fight alongside former Shinsengumi commander Hijikata Toshizo defending Utsunomiya Castle. Imperial forces press the attack as fires spread through the castle town around you.
evt-05-14-1868-boshin-war.prompt: What do the Tokugawa loyalist defenders do as the battle turns against them?

choices.text: They counterattack and retake the castle
They surrender the castle immediately
They retreat all the way to Edo Castle
They withdraw north to continue resistance

evt-05-14-1868-boshin-war.butterflyEffect: The shogunate troops withdrew northward rather than surrender, continuing the fight toward Aizu. That retreat prolonged the Boshin War through the brutal Battle of Aizu and ultimately to Hijikata's final stand in Hokkaido's short-lived Republic of Ezo, where he died in 1869.

evt-05-14-1878-salem-witchcraft-trial-18.scenario: It's May 1878 in Salem, Massachusetts, and you preside over a civil suit: Christian Scientist Lucretia Brown claims fellow believer Daniel Spofford is harming her through "mesmeric" mental powers.
evt-05-14-1878-salem-witchcraft-trial-18.prompt: How do you rule on Brown's claim of mental malpractice?

choices.text: Refer the matter to a church tribunal instead of a civil court
Order Spofford to pay monetary damages to Brown
Dismiss the case for lack of legal standing
Find Spofford guilty and sentence him to prison

evt-05-14-1878-salem-witchcraft-trial-18.butterflyEffect: The judge dismissed the case for lack of legal standing, since no statute recognized harm by thought alone. The trial became known as the last witchcraft-style prosecution in the United States and exposed early doctrinal rifts within the young Christian Science movement.

evt-05-14-1931-adalen.scenario: It is May 1931 in Ådalen, Sweden, days after soldiers sent to guard strikebreaking mill workers opened fire on a crowd of demonstrating strikers and bystanders. You are a journalist covering the shockwaves through Swedish society.
evt-05-14-1931-adalen.prompt: What did the Ådalen shootings help bring about in Swedish politics?

choices.text: The permanent disbanding of the Swedish armed forces
A surge in support for the Social Democrats and the welfare state they built
A prolonged civil war between labor and government forces
The immediate collapse of the Swedish monarchy

evt-05-14-1931-adalen.butterflyEffect: National outrage over the shootings helped propel the Social Democrats to power in the 1932 election, beginning decades of dominance during which Sweden built its modern welfare state. The killings also established a lasting norm against using the military against striking workers.

evt-05-14-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It's before dawn on 14 May 1943, and you serve aboard the AHS Centaur, an Australian hospital ship clearly marked with red crosses, sailing off the Queensland coast toward New Guinea.
evt-05-14-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What happened as a Japanese submarine sighted the illuminated hospital ship?

choices.text: It torpedoed the Centaur despite its protected hospital-ship status
It mistook the ship for a merchant vessel and radioed a warning
It surfaced, inspected the ship's papers, and let it pass
Allied escorts intercepted and sank the submarine first

evt-05-14-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The submarine torpedoed the Centaur without warning, killing 268 people; only 64 survived, including nurse Ellen Savage. The attack on a protected hospital ship outraged Australians and became the rallying cry "Avenge the Centaur," fueling wartime recruitment and bond drives.

evt-05-14-1948-israeli-declaration-of-in.scenario: It is the afternoon of 14 May 1948 at the Tel Aviv Museum. The British Mandate over Palestine ends at midnight, Arab armies are massing on the borders, and David Ben-Gurion must decide whether to proclaim statehood now or wait for firmer international backing.
evt-05-14-1948-israeli-declaration-of-in.prompt: What did Ben-Gurion decide to do?

choices.text: Wait for formal United States recognition before declaring
Accept a temporary UN trusteeship instead of full statehood
Delay the declaration until the United Nations sent peacekeepers
Proclaim the State of Israel immediately, before the Mandate expired

evt-05-14-1948-israeli-declaration-of-in.butterflyEffect: Ben-Gurion read the Declaration of Independence that afternoon, and the United States recognized the new state within minutes. The next day, neighboring Arab states invaded, beginning the 1948 Arab-Israeli War that would define the region's borders and conflicts for generations.

evt-05-14-1951-talyllyn-railway.scenario: It is 1951 and the Talyllyn Railway in Wales, a slate-hauling line since 1865, has fallen into disrepair with its aging owner unable to keep it running. You are among a group of railway enthusiasts determined to save it.
evt-05-14-1951-talyllyn-railway.prompt: What do you do to keep the Talyllyn Railway running?

choices.text: Petition the British government to nationalise it under British Railways
Let the line close and sell the track for scrap
Sell the railway to a private slate company for freight only
Form a volunteer preservation society to run the line themselves

evt-05-14-1951-talyllyn-railway.butterflyEffect: Volunteers formed the Talyllyn Railway Preservation Society and took over operations themselves, making it the world's first railway preserved and run by volunteers as a heritage line. The model proved so successful it inspired the global heritage railway movement, with hundreds of lines worldwide later saved the same way.

evt-05-14-1955-cold-war.scenario: It is May 1955 in Warsaw. West Germany has just joined NATO, and Soviet-aligned leaders from across Eastern Europe have gathered to decide how to answer this shift in the balance of power.
evt-05-14-1955-cold-war.prompt: What did the Soviet Union and its Eastern Bloc allies do in response?

choices.text: Formed a purely economic alliance with no military terms
Signed the Warsaw Pact mutual defense treaty
Agreed to unilaterally disarm their conventional forces
Each state individually sought its own agreement with NATO

evt-05-14-1955-cold-war.butterflyEffect: They signed the Warsaw Pact, a mutual defense treaty binding eight communist states militarily to Moscow. It formalized Soviet control over Eastern Europe and later provided the pretext for interventions in Hungary in 1956 and Czechoslovakia in 1968, lasting until the bloc's collapse in 1991.

evt-05-14-2004-frederik-x.scenario: It is 14 May 2004 inside Copenhagen Cathedral. Crown Prince Frederik stands at the altar awaiting his Australian bride, Mary Donaldson, as the wedding of the future Danish monarch begins.
evt-05-14-2004-frederik-x.prompt: What happens later in Frederik and Mary's royal life together?

choices.text: Frederik becomes king in 2024 after his mother's abdication
The couple never have children
Mary becomes queen only after Frederik's father dies
Frederik renounces the throne for love

evt-05-14-2004-frederik-x.butterflyEffect: The couple went on to have four children, and in January 2024 Queen Margrethe II abdicated rather than reign until death, an unusual step for Danish monarchs. Frederik and Mary became King and Queen of Denmark, continuing a modernised, publicly engaged style of monarchy.

evt-05-14-2008-2008-uefa-cup-final-riots.scenario: It's the afternoon of 14 May 2008 in Manchester's Piccadilly Gardens. Tens of thousands of ticketless Rangers fans are packed in to watch the UEFA Cup final on a big screen, and the feed just failed.
evt-05-14-2008-2008-uefa-cup-final-riots.prompt: What actually followed the screen failure in the crowded square?

choices.text: Riots erupted, causing injuries, arrests, and property damage
Organisers quickly repaired the screen and disorder never started
Police had already cancelled the screening hours earlier
The crowd dispersed calmly to nearby pubs

evt-05-14-2008-2008-uefa-cup-final-riots.butterflyEffect: Serious disorder broke out, injuring fifteen police officers and prompting 52 ambulance callouts for assault. A council inquiry into the chaos reshaped how English cities planned fan zones and alcohol controls for future European finals hosted away from the stadium.

evt-05-14-2010-stephen-timms.scenario: It is 14 May 2010 at your East Ham constituency surgery. A young constituent waiting to speak with you suddenly pulls a knife from her bag.
evt-05-14-2010-stephen-timms.prompt: What happens to Stephen Timms during the attack?

choices.text: He is unharmed as a bodyguard intervenes
He disarms the attacker unaided
He is stabbed but survives after emergency surgery
He is fatally wounded in the attack

evt-05-14-2010-stephen-timms.butterflyEffect: Timms was stabbed twice but survived after emergency surgery. His attacker, Roshonara Choudhry, had radicalised herself watching online sermons and targeted him over his vote for the Iraq War, making the case an early, widely cited example of internet-driven 'lone wolf' extremism that shaped later UK counter-radicalisation policy.

evt-05-14-2010-space-shuttle-atlantis.scenario: It's 14 May 2010, and you're strapped into Space Shuttle Atlantis's cockpit for STS-132, a mission NASA has billed as the orbiter's final scheduled flight.
evt-05-14-2010-space-shuttle-atlantis.prompt: What critical cargo are you delivering to the International Space Station?

choices.text: A new set of solar array wings for the station
Russia's Rassvet module, the first Russian module delivered by a U.S. shuttle
The Canadian Dextre robotic arm
Japan's Kibo laboratory module

evt-05-14-2010-space-shuttle-atlantis.butterflyEffect: Atlantis delivered Russia's Rassvet module, the first Russian module ever carried by a U.S. shuttle, expanding the station's Russian segment. Contrary to expectations, Atlantis was not retired afterward; budget and schedule changes gave it one more flight, STS-135, which became the final shuttle mission of the entire program in 2011.

evt-05-14-2012-agni-air-flight-cht.scenario: It is 14 May 2012 aboard a Dornier 228 approaching Jomsom Airport in Nepal's Mustang valley. Sudden gusts force the pilots to abandon the landing and attempt a go-around over the riverbed below.
evt-05-14-2012-agni-air-flight-cht.prompt: What happens after the aborted landing attempt?

choices.text: A bird strike disables the aircraft
An engine catches fire mid-flight
The plane overruns the far end of the runway
The plane loses altitude and crashes short of the runway

evt-05-14-2012-agni-air-flight-cht.butterflyEffect: The aircraft failed to gain altitude during the go-around and crashed near the airport, killing 15 of the 21 aboard, including young Indian actress Taruni Sachdev and her mother. The disaster renewed scrutiny of the extreme weather risks at Jomsom, one of the world's most difficult airports, and pushed Nepalese aviation authorities to tighten wind-based landing restrictions there.

evt-05-14-2021-zhurong-rover.scenario: It is 14 May 2021 in mission control near Beijing. The Tianwen-1 lander carrying the Zhurong rover is plunging through the Martian atmosphere toward Utopia Planitia, and you wait for confirmation of a safe touchdown.
evt-05-14-2021-zhurong-rover.prompt: What does Zhurong later find as it explores the Martian surface?

choices.text: Signs that water may have persisted longer than expected
Definitive fossil evidence of past microbial life
A previously unknown moon of Mars
An active volcano still erupting

evt-05-14-2021-zhurong-rover.butterflyEffect: Zhurong operated far beyond its 90-day design life and detected features, including hydrated minerals and dune patterns, suggesting liquid water may have lingered on Mars longer than previously thought. Its success cemented China's rapid rise in planetary exploration and set the stage for the planned Tianwen-3 Mars sample-return mission.

evt-05-14-2022-2022-buffalo-shooting.scenario: It is the afternoon of May 14, 2022. You are a Twitch moderator and notice a livestream showing an armed man entering a supermarket in Buffalo, New York, and opening fire.
evt-05-14-2022-2022-buffalo-shooting.prompt: What is the appropriate immediate action for the platform to take?

choices.text: Share the stream publicly to warn nearby residents
Edit the footage before removing it to preserve evidence
Immediately terminate the stream and alert law enforcement
Let it continue running so investigators can gather footage later

evt-05-14-2022-2022-buffalo-shooting.butterflyEffect: Twitch removed the stream in under two minutes, but clips had already spread across other platforms. The attack, which killed ten Black victims in a racially motivated shooting, intensified national scrutiny of online radicalization, livestreamed violence, and platform moderation policies, and renewed debate over gun laws and domestic extremism.

evt-05-15-1252-pope-innocent-iv.scenario: You are an inquisitor in Italy in 1252, newly armed with a fresh papal bull from Innocent IV instructing local authorities on how heretics should be handled during questioning.
evt-05-15-1252-pope-innocent-iv.prompt: What did the bull Ad extirpanda authorize you to do to suspected heretics?

choices.text: Exile suspected heretics without questioning them at all
Confiscate all property from heretics before any hearing
Execute suspected heretics immediately without any trial
Use torture to extract confessions from suspected heretics

evt-05-15-1252-pope-innocent-iv.butterflyEffect: The bull explicitly sanctioned the use of torture to extract confessions from suspected heretics, provided it stopped short of causing death or permanent injury. This gave formal papal cover to practices that shaped inquisitorial procedure across Europe for centuries afterward.

evt-05-15-1602-bartholomew-gosnold.scenario: It is May 1602 and your small ship has just rounded a hooked, sandy peninsula thick with cod off the New England coast. You are the first Englishman recorded to set foot here, and you must decide what to call this place and where to make landfall next.
evt-05-15-1602-bartholomew-gosnold.prompt: What did Gosnold do after sighting this hook of land teeming with fish?

choices.text: Named it Cape Cod after the fish his crew hauled in
Named it in honor of Queen Elizabeth I
Claimed it for Spain to secure a trade alliance
Sailed past without landing, judging it barren

evt-05-15-1602-bartholomew-gosnold.butterflyEffect: Gosnold named the peninsula Cape Cod for the abundant fish his crew caught there, then went on to explore Martha's Vineyard and establish a short-lived post on Cuttyhunk Island. Five years later he helped found Jamestown, making him a key figure bridging early exploration and permanent English colonization in America.

evt-05-15-1836-francis-baily.scenario: It is 15 May 1836 and you watch the Moon's edge creep across the Sun in an annular eclipse. As totality nears, sunlight breaks through the Moon's rugged limb into a string of brilliant points rather than a smooth ring.
evt-05-15-1836-francis-baily.prompt: What did Francis Baily conclude explained this beading of light?

choices.text: Reflections from the telescope's imperfect lens
Refraction of sunlight through Earth's own atmosphere
Sunlight passing through lunar valleys and mountains on the Moon's edge
Sunspots aligning briefly with the Moon's edge

evt-05-15-1836-francis-baily.butterflyEffect: Baily correctly attributed the beads to sunlight streaming through valleys and irregularities on the Moon's mountainous limb. The phenomenon, forever named Baily's beads, became a standard reference point for eclipse observers and helped refine measurements of the Moon's surface topography.

evt-05-15-1855-great-gold-robbery.scenario: It's the night of May 15, 1855, aboard the guard's van of the London-to-Folkestone boat train. You're one of the conspirators, and the boxes of gold bullion bound for Paris are within reach before the train reaches port.
evt-05-15-1855-great-gold-robbery.prompt: How do you steal the gold without anyone noticing until it's too late?

choices.text: Bribe the customs officers waiting at Folkestone
Simply throw the boxes off the moving train to an accomplice
Swap the boxes with empty crates from another train
Replace the stolen gold bars with lead shot of equal weight

evt-05-15-1855-great-gold-robbery.butterflyEffect: The gang replaced the stolen gold with an equal weight of lead shot, so the theft wasn't discovered until the boxes were opened in France. The crime went unsolved for months until a falling-out among the conspirators led to confessions, and it's remembered as one of the earliest great train robberies in Britain.

evt-05-15-1862-fertilisation-of-orchids.scenario: It is 1862 and a strange Madagascar orchid, Angraecum sesquipedale, sits on your desk with a nectar spur nearly a foot long. No known moth has a proboscis that could possibly reach its nectar.
evt-05-15-1862-fertilisation-of-orchids.prompt: What did Darwin predict must exist to pollinate this extraordinary orchid?

choices.text: Wind pollination without any insect involved
A beetle capable of chewing through the flower's spur
A hummingbird species migrated from the Americas
A moth with an unusually long proboscis, not yet discovered

evt-05-15-1862-fertilisation-of-orchids.butterflyEffect: Darwin predicted an undiscovered moth with an extraordinarily long proboscis suited to the flower's spur. Decades after his death, entomologists found exactly such a moth, Xanthopan morganii praedicta, vindicating his reasoning about coevolution and cementing the book's argument for natural selection shaping intricate plant-insect relationships.

evt-05-15-1869-susan-b-anthony.scenario: It is May 1869 and the suffrage movement has just split bitterly over the 15th Amendment. You stand with Susan B. Anthony and Elizabeth Cady Stanton as they form a new organization, refusing to wait behind Black male suffrage for their cause.
evt-05-15-1869-susan-b-anthony.prompt: What did Anthony and Stanton's new organization prioritize above all else?

choices.text: Support for the 15th Amendment first, women's suffrage later
State-by-state referendums as the only path to suffrage
Alliance with temperance societies as the primary vehicle for reform
A single federal constitutional amendment granting women the vote nationwide

evt-05-15-1869-susan-b-anthony.butterflyEffect: The National Woman Suffrage Association pushed for a federal constitutional amendment granting women the vote, rivaling the more moderate American Woman Suffrage Association. The two groups remained split for two decades until merging in 1890, and the federal strategy Anthony championed finally succeeded with the 19th Amendment in 1920.

evt-05-15-1891-pope-leo-xiii.scenario: It is 1891 and industrial cities are choked with strikes and squalor. As Pope Leo XIII, you must issue a statement addressing the plight of workers without endorsing the socialist revolutions sweeping Europe.
evt-05-15-1891-pope-leo-xiii.prompt: What stance did Leo XIII take in his encyclical Rerum novarum?

choices.text: Urged workers to accept their conditions as divinely ordained
Endorsed state seizure of factories to protect laborers
Defended private property but demanded fair wages and the right to unionize
Called for the abolition of private property in favor of common ownership

evt-05-15-1891-pope-leo-xiii.butterflyEffect: Rerum novarum defended private property while insisting employers pay just wages and allow workers to form unions, laying the foundation of modern Catholic social teaching. It shaped decades of Catholic labor activism and influenced later encyclicals and Christian democratic political movements across Europe and Latin America.

evt-05-15-1904-russo-japanese-war.scenario: It is 15 May 1904 off Port Arthur. You command a Japanese battleship patrolling waters you believe are clear, unaware Russian forces have sown mines along your route.
evt-05-15-1904-russo-japanese-war.prompt: What happened to the battleships Hatsuse and Yashima that day?

choices.text: They collided with each other during a storm
They were sunk by Russian submarine torpedoes
They struck Russian mines and sank within hours
They were captured intact by a Russian raiding party

evt-05-15-1904-russo-japanese-war.butterflyEffect: Both ships struck Russian mines and sank, a stunning single-day loss of two capital ships for the Imperial Japanese Navy. The disaster forced Japan to reassess mine countermeasures and naval caution, yet the fleet still went on to dominate the war, culminating in the decisive victory at Tsushima the following year.

evt-05-15-1911-mexican-revolution.scenario: It is May 1911 in Torreón, and Madero's revolutionary forces have just seized the city from Federal troops. Rumors spread through the ranks blaming local Chinese merchants for having favored the old regime.
evt-05-15-1911-mexican-revolution.prompt: What follows in the city over the next hours?

choices.text: Chinese merchants are peacefully expelled but not harmed
The Chinese community is placed under revolutionary protection
Federal troops retake the city and the Chinese residents are spared
Maderista soldiers and townspeople massacre hundreds of Chinese residents

evt-05-15-1911-mexican-revolution.butterflyEffect: Maderista soldiers and townspeople killed over 300 Chinese residents in one of the deadliest anti-Chinese massacres in the Americas. The Chinese government formally protested and demanded reparations, straining Sino-Mexican relations for years and foreshadowing further anti-Chinese campaigns elsewhere in Mexico during the revolution.

evt-05-15-1912-ty-cobb.scenario: It is 15 May 1912 in New York, and you are a Detroit Tigers teammate watching Ty Cobb climb into the stands to attack a fan who had been heckling him relentlessly.
evt-05-15-1912-ty-cobb.prompt: How do you and your teammates respond when the league suspends Cobb indefinitely?

choices.text: Refuse to play in protest, going on strike in support of Cobb
Demand the league permanently ban Cobb from baseball
Ask the league president to reverse the suspension without any protest
Accept the suspension quietly and take the field without him

evt-05-15-1912-ty-cobb.butterflyEffect: The Tigers went on strike in solidarity with Cobb, forcing the club to field a hastily assembled team of amateurs who lost 24-2 to the Athletics. The embarrassing fiasco pressured league officials to shorten Cobb's suspension and fine him instead, an early example of players collectively challenging management discipline.

evt-05-15-1916-lynching-of-jesse-washing.scenario: It is late May 1916, days after Jesse Washington's lynching in Waco. The NAACP has sent you, an investigator, to gather the truth for its magazine The Crisis.
evt-05-15-1916-lynching-of-jesse-washing.prompt: How do you expose what happened to a national audience?

choices.text: Wait for a federal commission to investigate before acting
Ask sympathetic newspapers to downplay the story to avoid backlash
Publish photographs and eyewitness testimony in The Crisis magazine
Quietly petition local courts to prosecute individual mob members

evt-05-15-1916-lynching-of-jesse-washing.butterflyEffect: The investigator's findings became "The Waco Horror," an NAACP supplement with photographs and eyewitness accounts distributed nationwide. It shocked white readers unfamiliar with lynching's brutality, swelled NAACP membership, and strengthened the organizing push behind later federal anti-lynching legislation like the Dyer Bill.

evt-05-15-1928-mickey-mouse.scenario: It's May 15, 1928, and Walt Disney has just privately screened his new cartoon, Plane Crazy, starring a mouse he's created with Ub Iwerks. Audience reaction is lukewarm, and no distributor wants it.
evt-05-15-1928-mickey-mouse.prompt: What does Disney do next to get his mouse noticed?

choices.text: Add synchronized sound and release Steamboat Willie as the real breakthrough
Shelve the mouse character permanently
Sell the rights to a rival animation studio
Rerelease Plane Crazy nationally unchanged

evt-05-15-1928-mickey-mouse.butterflyEffect: Disney reworked the character with synchronized sound, releasing Steamboat Willie that November—it became a sensation and is popularly remembered as Mickey's true debut. The sound gimmick set Disney apart from silent-era rivals and launched Mickey as an enduring American icon.

evt-05-15-1945-british-army.scenario: It is May 1945 near Bleiburg on the Austrian-Yugoslav border. Tens of thousands of retreating Croatian soldiers and civilians, fleeing Tito's advancing Partisans, surrender to your British unit and beg to be taken into British custody rather than handed back.
evt-05-15-1945-british-army.prompt: What did British forces do with these surrendering men?

choices.text: Allow them free passage into Allied-occupied Austria
Disarm them and release them to return home unsupervised
Hand them over to the advancing Yugoslav Partisan forces
Intern them permanently in British-run camps in Italy

evt-05-15-1945-british-army.butterflyEffect: British commanders turned the surrendered forces over to the Yugoslav Partisans, who executed or imprisoned many of them in the mass killings and death marches that followed. The episode, remembered bitterly as the Bleiburg tragedy, became a lasting source of grievance in Croatian communities and a symbol of Allied complicity in postwar reprisals.

evt-05-15-1953-pinewood-derby.scenario: It's May 15, 1953, in Manhattan Beach, California. As Cub Scout leader Don Murphy, you're organizing the very first race of its kind, using nothing but simple materials scouts can shape themselves.
evt-05-15-1953-pinewood-derby.prompt: What kind of car do the scouts build to race?

choices.text: Rubber-band powered wind-up racers
Full-size soap box derby cars
Unpowered wooden cars carved from a pine block, raced by gravity down a sloped track
Small battery-powered electric cars

evt-05-15-1953-pinewood-derby.butterflyEffect: Murphy's design—an unpowered block of pine wood with plastic wheels raced down a gravity-fed track—became the template for the Pinewood Derby. It spread nationwide through Scouting America and inspired copycat races by other organizations, though the name itself remains trademarked.

evt-05-15-1957-thermonuclear-weapon.scenario: It is 15 May 1957, and you are a British scientist reviewing data from the first UK hydrogen bomb test over Malden Island. The yield is far lower than what was promised to the public.
evt-05-15-1957-thermonuclear-weapon.prompt: What does the government decide to do with this disappointing result?

choices.text: Present the test to the world as a full thermonuclear success despite the shortfall
Hand control of the program over to American scientists
Postpone all further testing indefinitely
Publicly admit the test failed and cancel further trials

evt-05-15-1957-thermonuclear-weapon.butterflyEffect: Officials publicized the test as a full thermonuclear triumph to preserve Britain's deterrent credibility on the world stage. Later Grapple tests achieved genuine megaton yields, and the program's eventual success helped secure the 1958 US-UK Mutual Defence Agreement, restoring nuclear cooperation between the two allies.

evt-05-15-1990-vincent-van-gogh.scenario: It's May 15, 1990, inside Christie's auction house in New York. Van Gogh's Portrait of Dr. Gachet is on the block, and the bidding has already blown past every pre-sale estimate as the room falls silent between raised paddles.
evt-05-15-1990-vincent-van-gogh.prompt: What happens to the final price of the painting?

choices.text: It sells for $82.5 million, a new world record for a painting
It sells below estimate due to lack of interest
It fails to meet reserve and is withdrawn from sale
It's pulled from sale after being questioned as a forgery

evt-05-15-1990-vincent-van-gogh.butterflyEffect: The painting sold for $82.5 million to Japanese businessman Ryoei Saito, a new world record for any artwork at auction. The sale became a symbol of Japan's late-1980s asset bubble, and after Saito's death the painting's whereabouts grew uncertain, fueling rumors about its fate.

evt-05-15-2001-csx-8888-incident.scenario: It's May 15, 2001, in Ohio, and locomotive #8888 is barreling along unmanned at over 50 mph, hauling 47 cars including two loaded with molten phenol. You're part of the crew scrambling to stop it before it reaches a populated area.
evt-05-15-2001-csx-8888-incident.prompt: What do you do to bring the runaway train under control?

choices.text: Have police shoot out its air brake lines
Chase it with a catch locomotive and couple to the rear car to slow it
Wait for it to run out of fuel on its own
Deliberately derail it using a track switch ahead

evt-05-15-2001-csx-8888-incident.butterflyEffect: A crew in a catch locomotive chased down the train, coupled to its rear car, and gradually slowed it enough to stop safely without derailment. The two-hour ordeal exposed gaps in railroad safety procedure and later inspired the 2010 film Unstoppable.

evt-05-15-2010-jessica-watson.scenario: It is 15 May 2010, and you are sixteen-year-old Jessica Watson sailing into Sydney Harbour after seven months alone at sea, having looped the globe in your small yacht.
evt-05-15-2010-jessica-watson.prompt: What happens when officials measure your route against the official circumnavigation rules?

choices.text: Officials find her route fell short of the distance criteria, but she is still celebrated as a national hero
Her voyage is ruled invalid and quietly forgotten
She is disqualified for receiving assistance during the crossing
She is declared the youngest person to sail solo around the world, unassisted, without dispute

evt-05-15-2010-jessica-watson.butterflyEffect: Because her route hugged latitudes closer to the poles, her distance fell nearly 2,000 nautical miles short of the equatorial standard for a true circumnavigation. Despite this technicality, Australia still celebrated her: she was named 2011 Young Australian of the Year and received the Medal of the Order of Australia, and her voyage later inspired the Netflix film True Spirit.

evt-05-15-2024-prime-minister-of-slovaki.scenario: You are standing in the crowd in Handlová on 15 May 2024 as Prime Minister Robert Fico greets supporters after a public event. Suddenly a man steps forward and fires several shots at close range before being tackled to the ground.
evt-05-15-2024-prime-minister-of-slovaki.prompt: What was Fico's fate after being rushed into emergency surgery?

choices.text: He died from his wounds before reaching the hospital
He survived after emergency surgery and a prolonged recovery
The gunman fled the scene and was never identified
He escaped the shooting completely unharmed

evt-05-15-2024-prime-minister-of-slovaki.butterflyEffect: Fico survived after undergoing emergency surgery and a lengthy hospital recovery. The attack intensified already sharp political polarization in Slovakia, with his government and opposition trading accusations over the climate of political rhetoric that preceded it.

evt-05-16-1777-button-gwinnett.scenario: It is 16 May 1777, and you are Button Gwinnett, a signer of the Declaration of Independence, standing across from your political rival Lachlan McIntosh after a bitter dispute over your failed invasion of East Florida.
evt-05-16-1777-button-gwinnett.prompt: What do you do when McIntosh challenges you to settle the feud with pistols?

choices.text: Flee Georgia to avoid the confrontation
Apologize publicly to end the feud
Refuse and demand a court martial instead
Accept the duel and exchange shots with McIntosh

evt-05-16-1777-button-gwinnett.butterflyEffect: Gwinnett accepted and was mortally wounded, dying days later, making him the first signer of the Declaration to die by violence. McIntosh was tried and acquitted, and Gwinnett's name lives on in Georgia's Gwinnett County.

evt-05-16-1811-peninsular-war.scenario: It is 16 May 1811 at Albuera in Spain. French cavalry has just shattered a Spanish and British brigade, and the road to your position lies open. Marshal Beresford is wavering between retreat and a desperate counterattack with the fusilier brigade in reserve.
evt-05-16-1811-peninsular-war.prompt: What should the Allied command do to save the battle?

choices.text: Hold position and wait for Portuguese reinforcements to arrive
Order a full retreat toward Badajoz to preserve the army
Send the fusilier brigade forward in a counterattack on the French center
Withdraw the artillery and abandon the field to the French

evt-05-16-1811-peninsular-war.butterflyEffect: On the urging of officers like Henry Hardinge, Beresford sent the fusilier brigade forward; it broke the French center in one of the bloodiest actions of the whole war, with both sides losing roughly a third of their men. The costly Allied win kept the siege of Badajoz alive and became a byword for British infantry endurance under Wellington's command.

evt-05-16-1832-juan-godoy.scenario: It's 1832, and you're prospecting the dry hills south of Copiapó, Chile. You spot a strange glinting outcrop — could this be the silver deposit rumored to lie hidden in these mountains?
evt-05-16-1832-juan-godoy.prompt: What does Juan Godoy's discovery at Chañarcillo trigger?

choices.text: The founding of Santiago as Chile's capital
Chile's declaration of independence from Spain
A gold rush drawing prospectors from California
A massive Chilean silver rush that transforms the region's economy

evt-05-16-1832-juan-godoy.butterflyEffect: Godoy's find opened the fabulously rich Chañarcillo silver mines, making Chile one of the world's leading silver producers for decades. The wealth funded railways, ports, and a new mining elite, reshaping the economy of northern Chile.

evt-05-16-1866-shield-nickel.scenario: You are a die-sinker at the U.S. Mint in the years just after 1866, watching the new Shield nickel's dies crack again and again under the press because James Longacre's design carries too much relief, especially around the rays on the reverse.
evt-05-16-1866-shield-nickel.prompt: What change does the Mint make to solve the coin's persistent striking problems?

choices.text: Remove the rays from the reverse design
Switch the coin's metal to pure silver
Shrink the coin's overall diameter
Add a reeded edge to strengthen the coin

evt-05-16-1866-shield-nickel.butterflyEffect: In 1867 the Mint removed the rays between the stars on the reverse, lowering the relief and easing die failures, and the simplified design continued until the Shield nickel was replaced by the Liberty Head nickel in 1883. The episode helped cement copper-nickel as the standard alloy for America's five-cent piece going forward.

evt-05-16-1918-sedition-act-of-1918.scenario: You edit a small-town newspaper in the summer of 1918. Congress has just passed a sweeping new law, and federal agents are already asking questions about your recent editorials on the war.
evt-05-16-1918-sedition-act-of-1918.prompt: What does the Sedition Act of 1918 make illegal?

choices.text: Refusing to buy Liberty Bonds
Criticizing the government, war effort, or military in speech or print
Selling war bonds without a license
Publishing troop movement locations

evt-05-16-1918-sedition-act-of-1918.butterflyEffect: The Act led to hundreds of prosecutions, including socialist leader Eugene V. Debs, silencing anti-war voices nationwide. Repealed in 1920 amid public backlash, its use in cases like Schenck v. United States still shaped free-speech law for decades to come.

evt-05-16-1929-1st-academy-awards.scenario: You hold one of only 270 tickets, bought for five dollars, to a private dinner at the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel honoring the best films of 1927 and 1928. The ceremony itself will last barely fifteen minutes.
evt-05-16-1929-1st-academy-awards.prompt: How had most guests already learned who the winners were before this ceremony began?

choices.text: A radio broadcast revealed the winners the night before
Results were kept secret until the following year's ceremony
The results had already been published in the press months earlier
Winners opened sealed envelopes live on stage

evt-05-16-1929-1st-academy-awards.butterflyEffect: AMPAS had announced the winners in newspapers three months before the dinner, so the event carried little suspense. The Academy scrapped this practice for the following year, introducing sealed envelopes to keep results secret until announced on stage, a tradition that has defined the Oscars ever since.

evt-05-16-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 16 May 1943, and you pilot a Lancaster bomber of RAF 617 Squadron approaching the Möhne Dam with Barnes Wallis's experimental bouncing bomb aboard.
evt-05-16-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: How must you release the bomb for it to work as designed?

choices.text: Fly at exactly 60 feet and a precise speed so the bomb skips across the water
Drop the bomb straight down onto the dam wall from a hover
Dive steeply and glide the bomb directly into the dam face
Release the bomb from high altitude for greater accuracy

evt-05-16-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Flying at exactly 60 feet and 232 mph let the bomb skip across the water and breach the Möhne and Eder Dams, flooding the Ruhr valley and delivering a major propaganda victory. The raid made 617 Squadron legendary as the "Dambusters" and prompted Germany to reinforce its remaining dams.

evt-05-16-1960-theodore-maiman.scenario: It's May 16, 1960, and you are physicist Theodore Maiman at Hughes Research Laboratories, attempting to prove that stimulated emission can produce a coherent beam of light for the first time.
evt-05-16-1960-theodore-maiman.prompt: What material do you use as the gain medium to fire the first working laser?

choices.text: A synthetic ruby crystal
Carbon dioxide gas
A gallium arsenide semiconductor
Helium-neon gas

evt-05-16-1960-theodore-maiman.butterflyEffect: Maiman's ruby crystal laser worked, and Hughes announced it to the world at a July 1960 press conference. The breakthrough launched an entire field, leading to gas, semiconductor, and other laser types now used in medicine, telecommunications, and manufacturing.

evt-05-16-1961-park-chung-hee.scenario: Before dawn on 16 May 1961 in Seoul, you are an army officer summoned by Major General Park Chung Hee, who is moving troops against the civilian government amid political chaos and economic stagnation.
evt-05-16-1961-park-chung-hee.prompt: What does Park's Military Revolution Committee do that morning?

choices.text: Stage a public referendum before taking any action
Call for United Nations mediation to resolve the crisis
Negotiate a coalition government with the sitting president
Seize key government and broadcast facilities in a bloodless coup

evt-05-16-1961-park-chung-hee.butterflyEffect: The coup succeeded almost without bloodshed, and Park soon consolidated power as president, ruling South Korea until his assassination in 1979. His authoritarian government drove rapid state-led industrialization, transforming South Korea's economy while suppressing political dissent, a legacy still debated in Korea today.

evt-05-16-1968-gas-explosion.scenario: It is the early hours of 16 May 1968, and a resident on the 18th floor of London's newly built Ronan Point tower lights her stove to make tea, unaware gas has been leaking into her flat.
evt-05-16-1968-gas-explosion.prompt: What structural weakness does the ensuing explosion expose in the building's design?

choices.text: The central elevator shaft carried the blast through every floor
Faulty wiring triggered a chain of secondary explosions
The precast concrete panels lacked resistance to progressive collapse once one wall was blown out
The tower's foundations were built too shallow for its height

evt-05-16-1968-gas-explosion.butterflyEffect: The blast blew out a load-bearing precast panel, and the tower's Larsen Nielsen construction could not resist the resulting progressive collapse, bringing down a whole corner of the building. The disaster forced Britain to rewrite building regulations to require structures resist disproportionate collapse, reshaping tower block safety worldwide before Ronan Point itself was demolished in 1986.

evt-05-16-1975-kingdom-of-sikkim.scenario: It is mid-May 1975. A referendum held weeks earlier has returned an overwhelming vote to abolish the monarchy and merge Sikkim with India, and as Chogyal you must respond to the Indian Parliament's move to formalize the result.
evt-05-16-1975-kingdom-of-sikkim.prompt: What follows for the centuries-old Kingdom of Sikkim?

choices.text: The monarchy is restored with expanded constitutional powers
Sikkim is partitioned between India and Nepal
Sikkim gains full independence recognized by the United Nations
Sikkim becomes the 22nd state of India and the monarchy is abolished

evt-05-16-1975-kingdom-of-sikkim.butterflyEffect: Sikkim was formally annexed and became India's 22nd state, ending over 300 years of rule by the Namgyal dynasty. The Chogyal, Palden Thondup Namgyal, remained a figurehead without political power, and Sikkim's incorporation remains a point of friction in India's relations with China, which only recognized it decades later.

evt-05-16-1975-junko-tabei.scenario: Days into your Everest attempt in 1975, an avalanche has just struck your camp, burying you and several teammates. You are pulled out bruised and briefly unconscious, still far below the summit with the expedition's chance slipping away.
evt-05-16-1975-junko-tabei.prompt: What does Junko Tabei do after being dug out of the avalanche?

choices.text: Hand leadership of the expedition to a male climber
Recover and continue the climb toward the summit
Abandon the expedition and descend to Kathmandu
Wait at base camp for a full year before trying again

evt-05-16-1975-junko-tabei.butterflyEffect: Tabei recovered and pressed on, reaching the summit twelve days later on 16 May 1975 to become the first woman to stand atop Everest. She went on to complete the Seven Summits, inspiring generations of women climbers and later devoting herself to environmental protection of mountain regions.

evt-05-16-1997-mobutu-sese-seko.scenario: It is May 1997 in Kinshasa. Laurent-Désiré Kabila's rebel forces are closing on the capital after months of advance, your army is collapsing, and you are the aging, ailing president who has ruled Zaire for over three decades.
evt-05-16-1997-mobutu-sese-seko.prompt: What does Mobutu do as the rebels approach the capital?

choices.text: Request French military intervention to hold the capital
Order the army to make a last stand in Kinshasa
Negotiate a power-sharing government with Kabila
Flee the country into exile

evt-05-16-1997-mobutu-sese-seko.butterflyEffect: Mobutu fled into exile, first to Togo and then Morocco, where he died of cancer just months later. Kabila entered Kinshasa, renamed the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and his own troubled rule soon triggered the Second Congo War, one of the deadliest conflicts since World War II.

evt-05-16-2003-morocco.scenario: You are a Casablanca resident on the night of 16 May 2003, hearing news that coordinated suicide bombers have struck several sites across the city, including a Spanish social club and a Jewish community center.
evt-05-16-2003-morocco.prompt: How did the Moroccan government respond to the attacks in the months that followed?

choices.text: Closed all of Morocco's borders permanently
Opened negotiations directly with the bombing suspects
Ignored the bombings and made no policy changes
Launched a major crackdown and passed a new anti-terrorism law

evt-05-16-2003-morocco.butterflyEffect: Morocco launched a sweeping crackdown on Islamist militant networks and passed a new anti-terrorism law expanding police powers. Thousands were arrested in the following years, and while the campaign disrupted extremist cells, human rights groups criticized abuses committed during the crackdown.

evt-05-16-2005-kuwait.scenario: You are a Kuwaiti women's rights activist packed into the gallery of the National Assembly on 16 May 2005, waiting anxiously as members cast their votes on amending the election law.
evt-05-16-2005-kuwait.prompt: What did the National Assembly decide in this vote?

choices.text: Postpone any decision on women's suffrage indefinitely
Grant women the right to vote and stand for office
Allow women to vote only in municipal elections
Reject the suffrage amendment entirely

evt-05-16-2005-kuwait.butterflyEffect: The Assembly voted 35–23 to grant Kuwaiti women full political rights, including the right to vote and run for office. Women cast ballots for the first time in the 2006 parliamentary elections, and by 2009 Kuwait had elected its first female MPs.

evt-05-16-2011-sts-134.scenario: You are Commander Mark Kelly aboard Space Shuttle Endeavour on its 25th and final flight, preparing for the shuttle's last major delivery to the International Space Station.
evt-05-16-2011-sts-134.prompt: What key scientific instrument does STS-134 install on the ISS?

choices.text: A new Canadarm2 robotic arm
The Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer
A Multi-Purpose Logistics Module full of crew supplies only
The Hubble Space Telescope's replacement mirror

evt-05-16-2011-sts-134.butterflyEffect: Endeavour delivered the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer, a cosmic-ray detector built to hunt for dark matter and antimatter. Mounted on the station's truss, AMS has operated for over a decade, gathering billions of cosmic-ray events and reshaping astrophysicists' understanding of high-energy particles in space.

evt-05-16-2025-2025-st-louis-tornado.scenario: It's the afternoon of May 16, 2025, and a massive, rain-wrapped tornado is tearing through St. Louis, Missouri. As the city's emergency management director, you watch the storm level entire neighborhoods.
evt-05-16-2025-2025-st-louis-tornado.prompt: What do you request from the federal government in the storm's aftermath?

choices.text: Request federal disaster aid through FEMA
Rely solely on private insurance claims to cover damages
Deploy only the state National Guard and decline outside aid
Wait for neighboring states to volunteer assistance first

evt-05-16-2025-2025-st-louis-tornado.butterflyEffect: Officials requested federal disaster aid, and FEMA later called the residential damage the largest it had surveyed since the 2011 Joplin tornado. Damage estimates reached $1.6 billion, among the highest ever recorded for a single tornado, while volunteer engineers fanned out to survey homes as aid remained pending.

evt-05-16-2025-2025-somerset-london-torn.scenario: It is nearly midnight on May 16, 2025, and a violent tornado warning has just been issued for London, Kentucky. Most residents are asleep, and the storm is already tearing through neighborhoods in the dark.
evt-05-16-2025-2025-somerset-london-torn.prompt: What is the safest action for a resident when a nighttime EF4 tornado warning sounds?

choices.text: Move immediately to a basement or interior room away from windows
Stay in bed and wait to see if the storm passes
Go outside to check how close the storm is
Get in a car and try to outrun the tornado

evt-05-16-2025-2025-somerset-london-torn.butterflyEffect: This nocturnal EF4 tornado killed 18 people and injured 108 along a 60-mile track, one of two EF4s that struck that day amid a major mid-May outbreak. The tragedy renewed national attention on the added danger of tornadoes striking after dark, when many people never hear the warning at all.

evt-05-17-1395-wallachia.scenario: You stand with Wallachian prince Mircea the Elder's forces at Rovine, vastly outnumbered by the advancing army of Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I. The marshy terrain may be your only advantage.
evt-05-17-1395-wallachia.prompt: How does Mircea's army overcome the larger Ottoman force?

choices.text: Using terrain, guerrilla tactics, and knowledge of the land to wear down the invaders
Calling in reinforcements from Hungary before the battle begins
Bribing Ottoman commanders to withdraw
Meeting them in open cavalry battle on the plains

evt-05-17-1395-wallachia.butterflyEffect: Mircea's victory at Rovine halted the Ottoman advance into Wallachia, though he would later have to acknowledge Ottoman overlordship. The battle became a symbol of Romanian resistance, later immortalized in Mihai Eminescu's epic poem invoking Mircea's reign.

evt-05-17-1521-edward-stafford-3rd-duke-.scenario: It is May 1521, and you are Edward Stafford, Duke of Buckingham, standing trial in Westminster Hall on charges of treason before a panel of peers assembled by your cousin, King Henry VIII.
evt-05-17-1521-edward-stafford-3rd-duke-.prompt: What became of Buckingham after his trial?

choices.text: He was exiled to France for life
He was imprisoned in the Tower indefinitely
He was acquitted and restored to royal favor
He was executed by beheading

evt-05-17-1521-edward-stafford-3rd-duke-.butterflyEffect: Buckingham was convicted and beheaded on Tower Hill on 17 May 1521. His fall demonstrated Henry VIII's willingness to destroy even the mightiest nobles, a warning that echoed through the later purges of Henry's reign.

evt-05-17-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 17 May 1863. You serve with Grant's Union army pursuing Pemberton's Confederates, who are falling back in disarray toward the bridge over the Big Black River during the Vicksburg Campaign.
evt-05-17-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: What did Union forces do to exploit the Confederate retreat at the river?

choices.text: Bypassed the river entirely and marched directly on Jackson
Waited several days for reinforcements before advancing
Launched an immediate assault before the Confederates could regroup, capturing prisoners and artillery
Agreed to a local truce to let the Confederates withdraw unmolested

evt-05-17-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Union troops overran the Confederate lines before they could burn the bridge or regroup, capturing large numbers of prisoners and cannon and driving the survivors back into Vicksburg. This victory sealed the Confederate retreat and opened the way for the Siege of Vicksburg, which ended in surrender on 4 July 1863 and split the Confederacy along the Mississippi.

evt-05-17-1865-international-telecommuni.scenario: You are a delegate at the 1865 Paris conference, where representatives from twenty states have gathered because telegraph messages keep stalling at national borders, each country using its own codes and tariffs.
evt-05-17-1865-international-telecommuni.prompt: What should the delegates agree to do to fix cross-border telegraphy?

choices.text: Create a joint international postal stamp system instead
Hand control of all international telegraph lines to a single private company
Focus only on insurance rules for undersea cables
Establish shared technical rules and tariffs so messages could pass seamlessly between countries' telegraph networks

evt-05-17-1865-international-telecommuni.butterflyEffect: The delegates signed the International Telegraph Convention, creating uniform rules, tariffs, and Morse code standards across borders and founding the International Telegraph Union. The organization became the ITU in 1934, now the oldest agency in the UN system, still setting global communications standards.

evt-05-17-1890-cavalleria-rusticana.scenario: You are Pietro Mascagni in the late 1880s, an unknown composer who has entered his one-act opera into publisher Sonzogno's competition for new Italian works, hoping it will stand out among dozens of entries.
evt-05-17-1890-cavalleria-rusticana.prompt: What happened when Mascagni's opera was staged in Rome on 17 May 1890?

choices.text: It won the competition outright and became an instant sensation
It tied for the prize and was never performed publicly
It was banned by censors before its premiere
It was rejected by the judges and shelved for years

evt-05-17-1890-cavalleria-rusticana.butterflyEffect: Cavalleria rusticana won Sonzogno's competition and became an overnight sensation, launching Mascagni to international fame almost instantly. Its raw, small-town passions helped define the verismo movement in Italian opera, and it has been paired in performance with Leoncavallo's Pagliacci ever since.

evt-05-17-1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-o.scenario: You are Dorothy Gale, newly landed in the Land of Oz after a cyclone swept away your Kansas farmhouse, with the Good Witch of the North standing before you.
evt-05-17-1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-o.prompt: What does the Good Witch tell you to do to find your way home?

choices.text: Follow the yellow brick road to the Emerald City
Seek out the Wicked Witch of the West for guidance
Return immediately to the wreckage of the farmhouse
Wait in the cyclone cellar until help arrives

evt-05-17-1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-o.butterflyEffect: Dorothy follows the yellow brick road to the Emerald City to petition the Wizard, the journey that drives Baum's story. The book became a massive success and launched an Oz franchise; the 1939 MGM film later changed Dorothy's silver shoes to ruby slippers for Technicolor effect, cementing a different image in popular memory.

evt-05-17-1902-antikythera-mechanism.scenario: It is 17 May 1902, and you are archaeologist Valerios Stais, examining a corroded lump of bronze recovered two years earlier from an ancient shipwreck off Antikythera, when you notice a gear wheel embedded within it.
evt-05-17-1902-antikythera-mechanism.prompt: What should you conclude about this fragment?

choices.text: It is a fragment of a decorative bronze statue
It is a die used for minting coins
It is a broken astronomical clockwork device
It is merely a fitting from the ship's rigging

evt-05-17-1902-antikythera-mechanism.butterflyEffect: Stais correctly identified the object as part of a mechanical device, launching decades of study that revealed it as an astronomical calculator capable of predicting eclipses and tracking calendar cycles. Later research, including work by Derek de Solla Price and modern imaging teams, showed its gearing was far more sophisticated than any known ancient technology, reshaping views of Greek engineering.

evt-05-17-1947-chanel-no-5.scenario: It is 1947, and you are Coco Chanel, locked in a decades-long dispute with the Wertheimer brothers, who control Parfums Chanel and have paid you only a small fraction of Chanel No. 5's enormous profits.
evt-05-17-1947-chanel-no-5.prompt: What did Chanel do to claim a greater share of the perfume's fortune?

choices.text: She sued for and won outright ownership of the formula
She launched a rival perfume to compete directly
She renegotiated for a lucrative percentage of sales
She severed all ties to the fragrance entirely

evt-05-17-1947-chanel-no-5.butterflyEffect: Chanel renegotiated her agreement, securing roughly 2% of worldwide No. 5 sales, a deal that helped make her one of the wealthiest women in the world by the time of her death. The Wertheimer family retained control of the Chanel brand, a relationship that continues to the present day.
