evt-05-17-1954-supreme-court-of-the-unit.scenario: You are a parent in Topeka, Kansas, whose child has been barred from the all-white elementary school just blocks from home. Today, the Supreme Court hands down its ruling in your case.
evt-05-17-1954-supreme-court-of-the-unit.prompt: What does the Court rule in Brown v. Board of Education?

choices.text: Segregation is permissible if facilities are equal
Segregation applies only to state, not private, schools
Segregated public schools violate the Equal Protection Clause
States may decide school segregation policy independently

evt-05-17-1954-supreme-court-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: The unanimous ruling overturned Plessy v. Ferguson's "separate but equal" doctrine, declaring segregated schools inherently unequal. It ignited fierce Southern resistance but became a cornerstone of the civil rights movement, fueling later desegregation battles nationwide.

evt-05-17-1974-the-troubles.scenario: It is 17 May 1974 in Dublin. Without warning, car bombs planted by the Ulster Volunteer Force explode in the city and in Monaghan, causing devastation in the heart of the Republic of Ireland.
evt-05-17-1974-the-troubles.prompt: What long-running controversy followed the Dublin and Monaghan bombings?

choices.text: The Irish government immediately sealed the border with Northern Ireland
Suspects were swiftly extradited to Britain and convicted within weeks
The UVF announced a permanent ceasefire the next day
Allegations of collusion between the UVF and British security forces sparked decades of demands for an inquiry

evt-05-17-1974-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: Allegations that British security forces had colluded with the UVF in planning the attacks persisted for decades, fuelling calls from victims' families for a full public inquiry. The bombings remain the deadliest single attack of the Troubles carried out in the Republic, and unresolved questions about state collusion continued to shape Anglo-Irish relations long after 1998.

evt-05-17-1987-uss-stark-incident.scenario: It is the night of 17 May 1987 in the Persian Gulf, moments after your frigate USS Stark is struck by two Exocet missiles fired from an Iraqi jet, killing dozens of your fellow sailors.
evt-05-17-1987-uss-stark-incident.prompt: What followed for relations between the United States and Iraq after the attack?

choices.text: The US ended all support for Iraq in its war with Iran
Iraq apologized and paid compensation while ties continued
The US declared war on Iraq in response
US forces launched immediate retaliatory strikes on Iraqi ships

evt-05-17-1987-uss-stark-incident.butterflyEffect: Iraq apologized, blamed pilot error, and paid compensation, and Washington accepted the explanation rather than retaliating. The US continued its tacit support for Iraq against Iran and soon began escorting Gulf tankers under Operation Earnest Will, a step that led toward direct clashes with Iranian forces.

evt-05-17-1994-malawi.scenario: It is 17 May 1994, and you are casting a ballot in Malawi's first multiparty election in over three decades, choosing between longtime ruler Hastings Kamuzu Banda and challenger Bakili Muluzi.
evt-05-17-1994-malawi.prompt: What was the result of this landmark vote for Malawi?

choices.text: The military seizes power before results are announced
Banda wins another term in office
Muluzi wins, ending Banda's one-party rule
The election is declared invalid and re-run months later

evt-05-17-1994-malawi.butterflyEffect: Muluzi's United Democratic Front defeated Banda, ending his 30-year authoritarian one-party rule. The peaceful transfer of power marked Malawi's transition to multiparty democracy and became a reference point for democratic transitions elsewhere in Africa.

evt-05-17-1997-first-congo-war.scenario: It is May 1997. Your rebel coalition has just swept into Kinshasa after a seven-month march across Zaire, and President Mobutu Sese Seko has fled the country.
evt-05-17-1997-first-congo-war.prompt: What did Laurent-Désiré Kabila do upon taking power in Kinshasa?

choices.text: Restored the pre-independence Congolese monarchy
Handed power to a United Nations transitional council
Declared himself president and renamed Zaire the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Called immediate multiparty elections before taking any office

evt-05-17-1997-first-congo-war.butterflyEffect: Kabila renamed the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo and declared himself president, but he soon fell out with the Rwandan and Ugandan allies who had backed his rise. Those broken alliances helped trigger the Second Congo War in 1998, a far larger conflict drawing in multiple African nations.

evt-05-17-2000-2000-uefa-cup-semi-final-.scenario: It is the night before the 2000 UEFA Cup semi-final in Istanbul. Rival fans of Leeds United and Galatasaray have clashed in the streets, and two Leeds supporters have been fatally stabbed.
evt-05-17-2000-2000-uefa-cup-semi-final-.prompt: What followed the killings in the days after the violence?

choices.text: Turkish authorities closed all borders to English travellers
The match was immediately cancelled and never rescheduled
Leeds United withdrew from the competition in protest
Galatasaray fans were banned from attending the second leg in England

evt-05-17-2000-2000-uefa-cup-semi-final-.butterflyEffect: Four men were arrested and charged with the murders, and English outrage led UEFA and the clubs to ban Galatasaray supporters from attending the second leg in Leeds. The tragedy pushed European football authorities toward stricter segregation and policing of fans travelling to away matches in tense fixtures.

evt-05-17-2004-massachusetts.scenario: You stand outside Cambridge City Hall just after midnight, where couples have waited for hours. Massachusetts is about to become the first U.S. state to issue marriage licenses to same-sex couples.
evt-05-17-2004-massachusetts.prompt: What legal ruling made this day possible?

choices.text: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court's Goodridge decision
A statewide referendum vote
An executive order from the governor
A U.S. Supreme Court ruling striking down DOMA

evt-05-17-2004-massachusetts.butterflyEffect: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court's Goodridge decision forced the state to become the first to grant full marriage rights to same-sex couples. It set off a decade of state-by-state legal battles culminating in the 2015 Obergefell v. Hodges ruling that legalized same-sex marriage nationwide.

evt-05-17-2007-north-korea.scenario: You stand at the reconnected rail line crossing the 38th parallel, as the first train in over half a century prepares to cross the Korean Demilitarized Zone.
evt-05-17-2007-north-korea.prompt: What does this historic test-run represent for the two Koreas?

choices.text: A symbolic step toward reconciliation and eventual rail reconnection
The official reunification of North and South Korea
The permanent reopening of full commercial rail service
North Korea's abandonment of its nuclear weapons program

evt-05-17-2007-north-korea.butterflyEffect: The crossing was a landmark moment of inter-Korean cooperation, part of the broader "Sunshine Policy" engagement between North and South. Regular rail service never materialized, as rising tensions and North Korea's nuclear tests soon stalled further cross-border projects.

evt-05-18-1388-battle-of-buir-lake.scenario: It is 1388 on the steppe near Buir Lake, and you ride with Ming general Lan Yu's army as it closes in on the fleeing court of Northern Yuan khan Tögüs Temür.
evt-05-18-1388-battle-of-buir-lake.prompt: What was the outcome of Lan Yu's campaign against the Northern Yuan at Buir Lake?

choices.text: Tögüs Temür surrendered his court without any fighting
The Ming decisively defeated the Northern Yuan and captured much of their people
The Northern Yuan repelled the Ming and pursued them south
The two armies fought to an inconclusive stalemate

evt-05-18-1388-battle-of-buir-lake.butterflyEffect: The Ming won a decisive victory, capturing much of the Northern Yuan court and people. The defeat shattered Tögüs Temür's authority, and he was assassinated by a rival shortly afterward, deepening the fragmentation of Mongol power and easing Ming pressure on the steppe for years.

evt-05-18-1927-board-of-education.scenario: It is mid-morning on 18 May 1927 in Bath Township, Michigan. An explosion has just torn through Bath Consolidated School, and you are a farmer working a nearby field when you hear the blast.
evt-05-18-1927-board-of-education.prompt: What is the most useful thing you can do in the minutes that follow?

choices.text: Rush to the school with neighbors and dig through the rubble by hand for trapped children
Drive to the county courthouse to report the incident first
Wait at home for state police to organize an official rescue
Gather townspeople to search Andrew Kehoe's farmhouse

evt-05-18-1927-board-of-education.butterflyEffect: Local farmers and parents, arriving before any organized rescue service, dug survivors and victims from the debris with their bare hands. The bombing—carried out by school board treasurer Andrew Kehoe after disputes over taxes and his farm's foreclosure—remains the deadliest attack on a school in U.S. history and is still studied by investigators of workplace and grievance-driven violence.

evt-05-18-1933-franklin-d-roosevelt.scenario: It is May 18, 1933, and you stand beside President Roosevelt as he signs a bill creating a new federal authority to manage the Tennessee River and lift a poor, flood-prone region out of the Depression.
evt-05-18-1933-franklin-d-roosevelt.prompt: What was the newly created Tennessee Valley Authority chiefly tasked with delivering?

choices.text: Price supports for wheat and cotton farmers only
Construction of a national interstate highway system
Federal insurance for bank deposits nationwide
Flood control, hydroelectric power, and economic development for the region

evt-05-18-1933-franklin-d-roosevelt.butterflyEffect: The TVA became one of the New Deal's most ambitious agencies, building dams that controlled flooding and brought electricity to a largely rural region for the first time. It later served as a model for regional development and public power projects around the world.

evt-05-18-1944-deportation-of-the-crimea.scenario: It's dawn on 18 May 1944 in a Crimean village. NKVD soldiers bang on your door, giving your family only minutes to gather belongings before marching you toward waiting cattle trains.
evt-05-18-1944-deportation-of-the-crimea.prompt: Where are these trains ultimately taking you and your neighbors?

choices.text: The steppes of Kazakhstan
Western Ukraine's collective farms
Siberian Gulag labor camps
The distant Uzbek SSR

evt-05-18-1944-deportation-of-the-crimea.butterflyEffect: The trains carried at least 191,000 Crimean Tatars thousands of kilometers to the Uzbek SSR, with many dying en route or from starvation and disease in exile. The deportation emptied Crimea of its indigenous population for decades, and in 2015 Ukraine's parliament formally recognized it as genocide.

evt-05-18-1955-operation-passage-to-free.scenario: It's May 1955 in Haiphong, North Vietnam. The Geneva Accords give you until 18 May to decide whether to board a French or American ship heading south before the border seals for good.
evt-05-18-1955-operation-passage-to-free.prompt: What do you and hundreds of thousands of others ultimately choose to do?

choices.text: Flee west into Laos
Emigrate permanently to France
Remain in the North under Ho Chi Minh's government
Move south to non-communist South Vietnam

evt-05-18-1955-operation-passage-to-free.butterflyEffect: Between 600,000 and a million people, many of them Catholics, moved south, giving Ngo Dinh Diem's new government a loyal population base and reshaping South Vietnamese society. The movement also became a powerful Cold War propaganda symbol ahead of the 1956 unification elections that were never held.

evt-05-18-1965-eli-cohen.scenario: It is 18 May 1965 in Damascus, and world leaders, including the Pope, have appealed to Syria for clemency for the Israeli master spy Eli Cohen, sentenced to death for espionage.
evt-05-18-1965-eli-cohen.prompt: What does Syria's government do with Cohen's fate?

choices.text: Commutes his sentence to life imprisonment
Grants him asylum in a neutral country
Secretly deports him to Israel in a prisoner exchange
Publicly hangs him in Damascus's Marjeh Square

evt-05-18-1965-eli-cohen.butterflyEffect: Cohen was executed by public hanging, his body never returned to Israel. The intelligence he had already smuggled out—including detailed maps of Syrian fortifications on the Golan Heights—reportedly helped Israeli forces during the 1967 Six-Day War. He remains one of Israel's most celebrated intelligence martyrs.

evt-05-18-1980-mount-st-helens.scenario: It's the morning of 18 May 1980. You're a USGS observer stationed several miles from Mount St. Helens, watching the volcano's bulging north flank for signs it might give way.
evt-05-18-1980-mount-st-helens.prompt: What triggers the mountain's catastrophic collapse that morning?

choices.text: Days of heavy rainfall saturating the slope
A lightning strike on the summit crater
A magnitude 5.1 earthquake collapses the north flank
A sudden drop in barometric pressure

evt-05-18-1980-mount-st-helens.butterflyEffect: A magnitude 5.1 earthquake sent the bulging flank sliding away in the largest landslide ever recorded, unleashing a lateral blast that killed 57 people, including volcanologist David Johnston. The disaster reshaped how scientists monitor and map volcanic hazard zones across the Cascade Range.

evt-05-18-1996-republic-of-ireland.scenario: It's the night of 18 May 1996 in Oslo's Spektrum arena. You're an RTÉ producer watching Eimear Quinn take the stage to sing 'The Voice' for Ireland at the Eurovision Song Contest.
evt-05-18-1996-republic-of-ireland.prompt: What happens when the votes are tallied that night?

choices.text: Ireland is disqualified over a technical rule
The United Kingdom takes the title
Ireland wins for the seventh time
Ireland finishes as runner-up

evt-05-18-1996-republic-of-ireland.butterflyEffect: Ireland won for a record seventh time, a feat no country has matched since. The victory cemented Ireland's status as Eurovision's most successful nation and fueled ongoing debate about the rising cost of hosting the contest for smaller broadcasters like RTÉ.

evt-05-18-2005-hubble-space-telescope.scenario: It is 18 May 2005, and you are part of the team reviewing a fresh set of Hubble Space Telescope images of the Pluto system, hoping to confirm two faint objects first glimpsed months earlier near the icy world.
evt-05-18-2005-hubble-space-telescope.prompt: What did this new set of images confirm about the two faint objects near Pluto?

choices.text: They were two additional moons genuinely orbiting Pluto, not imaging artifacts
They were distant background stars coincidentally aligned with Pluto
They were fragments of a disintegrating comet passing near Pluto
They were a newly discovered dwarf planet beyond Pluto's orbit

evt-05-18-2005-hubble-space-telescope.butterflyEffect: The objects were confirmed as genuine moons, later named Nix and Hydra, joining Charon as Pluto's known satellites. The discovery heightened anticipation for NASA's New Horizons mission, which flew past Pluto in 2015 and found two more tiny moons, Kerberos and Styx.

evt-05-18-2006-federal-parliament-of-nep.scenario: It is 18 May 2006 in Kathmandu. Weeks of mass pro-democracy protests have forced King Gyanendra to reinstate the dissolved House of Representatives, and you sit among the lawmakers now voting on his remaining authority.
evt-05-18-2006-federal-parliament-of-nep.prompt: What does Parliament vote to strip from the king?

choices.text: Only his ceremonial titles, leaving royal command of the army intact
His right to reside in the royal palace
Nothing—the vote restores his full pre-2005 powers
His control over the army and his status as head of state, declaring Nepal secular

evt-05-18-2006-federal-parliament-of-nep.butterflyEffect: Parliament unanimously stripped Gyanendra of command of the army, his role in government, and his tax exemptions, and declared Nepal a secular state. Two years later, in 2008, the newly elected Constituent Assembly abolished the monarchy altogether, ending 240 years of the Shah dynasty.

evt-05-18-2013-murder-of-mark-carson.scenario: It is the night of May 18, 2013, in Greenwich Village. Mark Carson is walking with a friend when a man begins shouting anti-gay slurs and following the pair down the street.
evt-05-18-2013-murder-of-mark-carson.prompt: What happened afterward that turned this killing into a landmark hate-crime prosecution?

choices.text: Charges against Morales were dropped for lack of evidence
Morales pleaded to a minor misdemeanor charge
Morales was convicted of murder with a hate-crime designation and given 40 years to life
Morales was acquitted after a jury trial

evt-05-18-2013-murder-of-mark-carson.butterflyEffect: Elliot Morales was convicted in March 2016 with a hate-crime designation and sentenced to 40 years to life. Carson's murder galvanized vigils in Greenwich Village, long a center of gay life, and renewed calls for stronger enforcement of hate-crime protections for LGBTQ New Yorkers.

evt-05-18-2015-2015-colombian-landslide.scenario: It is the early hours of 18 May 2015 in Salgar, Antioquia. Days of relentless rain have soaked the slopes above your sleeping town, and local officials must decide how to respond as the ground begins to give way.
evt-05-18-2015-2015-colombian-landslide.prompt: As warning signs mount overnight, what should authorities prioritize above all?

choices.text: Wait for official rainfall data before issuing any public warning
Immediately warn and evacuate residents in the valley below the unstable slopes
Focus resources on building emergency levees along the riverbank
Notify international media before alerting local residents

evt-05-18-2015-2015-colombian-landslide.butterflyEffect: The landslide swept through Salgar's residential area, killing around 100 people. In the disaster's wake, the Colombian government and international agencies provided relief, and sociologists later studied the recovery to judge how well it reduced the town's ongoing vulnerability to future landslides.

evt-05-18-2018-cubana-de-aviacion-flight.scenario: You are ground staff at José Martí International Airport on 18 May 1918, watching the aging Global Air Boeing 737 taxi out for its domestic run to Holguín.
evt-05-18-2018-cubana-de-aviacion-flight.prompt: What action do Mexican aviation regulators take after the crash is investigated?

choices.text: They increase government subsidies to Global Air
They merge Global Air directly into Cubana's fleet
They take no formal regulatory action
They suspend Global Air's operating certificate

evt-05-18-2018-cubana-de-aviacion-flight.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the 39-year-old aircraft had been poorly maintained, and Mexico's civil aviation authority suspended Global Air's operating certificate. Cuba, heavily dependent on leased foreign aircraft for domestic routes, tightened its oversight of chartered carriers afterward.

evt-05-19-1655-anglo-spanish-war-1654-16.scenario: It's May 1655, and you're aboard an English fleet under Admiral William Penn and General Robert Venables. Cromwell sent this force to seize a Spanish Caribbean colony, but the attempt on Hispaniola has just failed disastrously.
evt-05-19-1655-anglo-spanish-war-1654-16.prompt: Where does the fleet turn next to salvage the expedition?

choices.text: Puerto Rico
Cuba
Jamaica
Trinidad

evt-05-19-1655-anglo-spanish-war-1654-16.butterflyEffect: The English fleet landed on Jamaica and overwhelmed its lightly defended Spanish settlers. England held the island permanently, and it grew into one of the most valuable sugar and slave-trade colonies in the Caribbean for the next two centuries.

evt-05-19-1743-jean-pierre-christin.scenario: It's 1743 in Lyon, and you're a physicist examining Anders Celsius's decade-old thermometer scale, which fixes 0 degrees at the boiling point of water and 100 at freezing.
evt-05-19-1743-jean-pierre-christin.prompt: What change do you propose to make the scale more intuitive?

choices.text: Leave the original orientation unchanged
Reverse it so 0° is freezing and 100° is boiling
Replace it with a Fahrenheit-style scale
Add a third fixed point at body temperature

evt-05-19-1743-jean-pierre-christin.butterflyEffect: Christin reversed the scale, setting 0 at freezing and 100 at boiling. Known for centuries afterward as the centigrade scale, it was eventually renamed Celsius and is now the standard temperature scale used by most of the world.

evt-05-19-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 19 May 1776, and you command the Continental garrison at the Cedars, west of Montreal. Captain George Forster's smaller force of British regulars, Canadian militia, and Native American allies has surrounded your post, and your men fear a massacre if they resist.
evt-05-19-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What does the garrison's commander decide to do?

choices.text: Surrender the fort without a fight
Attempt a breakout under cover of night
Fight to the last man rather than surrender
Negotiate a ceasefire while awaiting reinforcements

evt-05-19-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Major Isaac Butterfield surrendered nearly 500 men without a real fight, fearing his troops would be massacred by Native warriors allied with the British. The surrender, followed by a controversial prisoner exchange, embarrassed Congress and became a symbol of the collapsing American invasion of Canada, which was abandoned within weeks.

evt-05-19-1780-new-england-s-dark-day.scenario: It is midday on 19 May 1780 in Connecticut, and the sky has turned black as night. Candles are lit at noon, some neighbors are certain Judgment Day has arrived, and you sit in the state legislature as panic spreads through the chamber.
evt-05-19-1780-new-england-s-dark-day.prompt: What does Colonel Abraham Davenport urge his fellow legislators to do?

choices.text: Adjourn immediately so everyone can pray for the end times
Call for candles and continue the legislature's business as usual
Order everyone to flee the chamber in panic
Postpone the session indefinitely until the sky clears

evt-05-19-1780-new-england-s-dark-day.butterflyEffect: Davenport refused calls to adjourn and prayed, reportedly saying he wanted to be found doing his duty and calling for candles so business could continue. The darkness was later traced to smoke from massive wildfires to the north combined with heavy fog and cloud cover, but Davenport's calm response became a celebrated piece of New England lore.

evt-05-19-1828-united-states-congress.scenario: It is May 1828, and you are a Southern congressman watching Jacksonian allies pile ever-higher duties onto a tariff bill, gambling that New England will reject its own creation and the whole measure will collapse.
evt-05-19-1828-united-states-congress.prompt: How do you vote on the amended, harsher tariff bill?

choices.text: Vote against it outright to protect Southern cotton exports
Vote for it, expecting it to fail and embarrass President Adams
Abstain and let the North decide
Propose a compromise lowering all rates

evt-05-19-1828-united-states-congress.butterflyEffect: The gambit backfired: New England manufacturers accepted the higher rates, and the bill passed and was signed into law as the highest tariff in U.S. history to that point. Southerners denounced it as the 'Tariff of Abominations,' and South Carolina's resulting fury fed directly into the 1832 Nullification Crisis.

evt-05-19-1845-john-franklin.scenario: It is 19 May 1845, and you are a sailor aboard HMS Erebus as she and HMS Terror slip down the Thames from Greenhithe under Sir John Franklin's command, bound for the Northwest Passage with three years' provisions stowed below.
evt-05-19-1845-john-franklin.prompt: What ultimately happens to Franklin's expedition after it vanishes into the Arctic?

choices.text: Franklin turns back after one winter and returns safely
The ships become icebound and the entire crew perishes
The expedition successfully completes the Northwest Passage and returns to England
The crew is rescued by American whalers off Greenland

evt-05-19-1845-john-franklin.butterflyEffect: Erebus and Terror became icebound off King William Island; Franklin died in 1847, and by 1848 the surviving 129 men had abandoned ship and perished from starvation, scurvy, and cold. The disaster triggered decades of search expeditions that mapped vast stretches of the Arctic, and the wrecks themselves were not found until 2014 and 2016.

evt-05-19-1915-world-war-i.scenario: It is dawn on 19 May 1915 at Anzac Cove, Gallipoli, and you are dug into the trenches as thousands of Ottoman soldiers surge forward in a massed assault meant to drive the Anzacs back into the sea.
evt-05-19-1915-world-war-i.prompt: What happens as the Ottoman attack breaks against the Anzac line?

choices.text: The Ottomans capture the ridge and hold it for the rest of the campaign
Both sides agree to an immediate armistice before fighting begins
The attack is repelled with heavy Ottoman casualties
The Anzac line collapses and the beachhead is evacuated

evt-05-19-1915-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Ottoman forces suffered roughly 10,000 casualties in the failed assault, several times the Anzac losses. The carnage left thousands of unburied dead between the lines, prompting a brief truce on 24 May 1915 so both sides could recover and bury their fallen.

evt-05-19-1962-marilyn-monroe.scenario: It is 19 May 1962 at Madison Square Garden, ten days before John F. Kennedy's actual birthday. A packed Democratic fundraising gala is underway, and Marilyn Monroe has just been introduced to the crowd in a skin-tight, rhinestone-covered gown.
evt-05-19-1962-marilyn-monroe.prompt: What does Monroe do that becomes one of the most talked-about moments of the decade?

choices.text: She gives a speech instead of singing
She performs a sultry, breathy rendition of "Happy Birthday to You"
She declines to perform and simply presents a cake
She sings a traditional, upbeat version with the full crowd

evt-05-19-1962-marilyn-monroe.butterflyEffect: Monroe delivered a breathy, sultry rendition of "Happy Birthday to You" directly to the president, an image that instantly became iconic and fueled decades of speculation about their relationship. Only weeks later, in August 1962, Monroe was found dead, and the performance became forever entwined with her legend and the Kennedy mystique.

evt-05-19-1991-breakup-of-yugoslavia.scenario: It's 19 May 1991, and the Republic of Croatia is holding a referendum on independence from Yugoslavia. You are a Serb community leader in the Krajina region, and other Serb leaders are urging your community to abstain from voting.
evt-05-19-1991-breakup-of-yugoslavia.prompt: What do you and your fellow Serbs decide to do?

choices.text: Organize a rival referendum on the same day
Boycott the referendum entirely
Turn out en masse to vote yes
Turn out en masse to vote no

evt-05-19-1991-breakup-of-yugoslavia.butterflyEffect: Croatian Serbs boycotted the vote, and with them absent the referendum passed overwhelmingly in favor of independence. Croatia declared independence weeks later, and the exclusion of Serb voices from that vote became a flashpoint that helped ignite the Croatian War of Independence.

evt-05-19-1991-croatia.scenario: It is 19 May 1991, and you stand in line at a polling station in Zagreb as Croatia holds a referendum on separating from the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
evt-05-19-1991-croatia.prompt: How do you cast your ballot?

choices.text: Vote for a loose confederation with Serbia only
Vote for full independence and sovereignty for Croatia
Vote to remain within a reformed Yugoslav federation
Boycott the vote in protest

evt-05-19-1991-croatia.butterflyEffect: Over 93% of voters chose independence. Croatia formally declared independence a month later, on 25 June 1991, a step that accelerated the breakup of Yugoslavia and triggered the Croatian War of Independence, which lasted until 1995.

evt-05-19-2007-president-of-romania.scenario: It is 19 May 2007. Parliament suspended President Traian Băsescu weeks earlier over an alleged power struggle with the prime minister, and Romanians are now voting in a referendum on whether to remove him from office for good.
evt-05-19-2007-president-of-romania.prompt: What did the referendum ultimately decide?

choices.text: He survived the vote and returned to the presidency
He resigned before the results were announced
Voters approved his removal and he was impeached
The referendum was declared invalid for low turnout

evt-05-19-2007-president-of-romania.butterflyEffect: Turnout was only about 44%, but Romania's constitution requires no minimum turnout for an impeachment referendum, and roughly three-quarters of those who voted rejected removing him. Băsescu returned to office, the rivalry with his prime minister deepened, and Romanian politics stayed locked in confrontation between president and parliament for years afterward.

evt-05-19-2015-refugio-state-beach.scenario: It is 19 May 2015 at Refugio State Beach along California's Gaviota Coast. An underground pipeline has just ruptured, sending crude oil pouring across the sand and into the surf as beachgoers and wildlife crews watch in alarm.
evt-05-19-2015-refugio-state-beach.prompt: What did investigators later determine caused the pipeline to fail?

choices.text: An earthquake ruptured the pipeline
A valve failure at a pumping station caused an overpressure blast
Severe corrosion had weakened the pipeline wall
Deliberate sabotage caused the rupture

evt-05-19-2015-refugio-state-beach.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the pipeline, operated by Plains All American, had suffered severe external corrosion that went undetected for years. The spill fouled miles of coastline, killed marine wildlife, and shut beaches for months, ultimately pushing California to pass stricter pipeline safety and monitoring laws while the company faced criminal charges.

evt-05-19-2015-refugio-oil-spill.scenario: It is 19 May 2015 on California's Gaviota Coast, and you are a pipeline operator when a corroded section of Line 901 ruptures, sending crude oil down a culvert toward the ocean and one of the most biologically rich stretches of coastline in the state.
evt-05-19-2015-refugio-oil-spill.prompt: What ultimately happens to the pipeline responsible for the spill?

choices.text: It resumes normal operation within days
The spill is contained before any oil reaches the ocean
It is shut down for years amid investigations and lawsuits
The operator is cleared of any responsibility

evt-05-19-2015-refugio-oil-spill.butterflyEffect: Investigators found inadequate corrosion protection had let the pipeline wear through, and it stayed shut down for nearly three years while litigation played out. Owner Plains All American faced an estimated $257 million in cleanup, legal, and settlement costs, and the spill spurred tighter California pipeline safety regulations.

evt-05-19-2016-egyptair-flight-804.scenario: It is the early hours of 19 May 2016. EgyptAir Flight 804 has just entered Egyptian airspace over the Mediterranean on its way from Paris to Cairo when it vanishes from radar, and search crews scramble to locate any trace of the aircraft.
evt-05-19-2016-egyptair-flight-804.prompt: What happened in the search and investigation that followed?

choices.text: No wreckage or recorders were ever located
Investigators announced a definitive bomb finding within days
A hijacking group immediately claimed responsibility
The black boxes were recovered from the seabed after a lengthy search

evt-05-19-2016-egyptair-flight-804.butterflyEffect: Wreckage and the flight recorders were eventually recovered from roughly 3,000 meters down off Alexandria, months after the crash. Despite the recovered data, Egyptian and French investigators reached differing conclusions about whether smoke detected before the crash stemmed from a bomb or a technical fire, and the cause remains officially unresolved.

evt-05-19-2018-wedding-of-prince-harry-a.scenario: It's 19 May 2018 in St George's Chapel, Windsor. You're a guest watching Prince Harry marry Meghan Markle, and Bishop Michael Curry has just delivered an unusually fiery sermon on the power of love.
evt-05-19-2018-wedding-of-prince-harry-a.prompt: What title does the Queen grant the newlyweds right after the ceremony?

choices.text: Earl and Countess of Wessex
Duke and Duchess of York
Duke and Duchess of Cambridge
Duke and Duchess of Sussex

evt-05-19-2018-wedding-of-prince-harry-a.butterflyEffect: Harry and Meghan were made Duke and Duchess of Sussex that same day. Less than two years later they stepped back from royal duties and relocated to North America, a break that forced the monarchy to confront its relationship with the press and its own family in strikingly public terms.

evt-05-19-2024-2024-varzaqan-helicopter-.scenario: It is 19 May 2024. You are part of the security detail traveling in a convoy of three helicopters through thick fog over the mountains near Varzaqan, carrying President Ebrahim Raisi from the Qiz Qalasi Dam toward Tabriz.
evt-05-19-2024-2024-varzaqan-helicopter-.prompt: After the crash killed the president, what happened next under Iran's constitution?

choices.text: Parliament indefinitely postponed choosing a successor
The Supreme Leader personally took over presidential duties
The Revolutionary Guard commander assumed control
The First Vice President became acting president pending a snap election

evt-05-19-2024-2024-varzaqan-helicopter-.butterflyEffect: First Vice President Mohammad Mokhber became acting president, and Iran's constitution required a new presidential election within 50 days. That snap election was held in June and July 2024, ultimately bringing reformist candidate Masoud Pezeshkian to power in a political landscape reshaped almost overnight.

evt-05-20-325-first-council-of-nicaea.scenario: You are one of over three hundred bishops summoned by Emperor Constantine to Nicaea in May 325, gathered to settle the fierce dispute over whether Christ is truly divine or a created being subordinate to God.
evt-05-20-325-first-council-of-nicaea.prompt: What position do you support to end the Arian controversy?

choices.text: Declare the Son of one substance with the Father, as the Creed states
Argue there is no distinct Son at all, only one divine person
Support Arius's view that the Son was created and subordinate
Postpone any doctrinal decision until a later council

evt-05-20-325-first-council-of-nicaea.butterflyEffect: The council adopted the Nicene Creed, declaring the Son 'of one substance' (homoousios) with the Father, and condemned Arius's teaching. The dispute nonetheless raged for decades afterward, but the creed became the foundation of mainstream Christian doctrine and a model for later ecumenical councils.

evt-05-20-685-picts.scenario: It is 20 May 685. You scout for King Ecgfrith of Northumbria as he chases the retreating Picts of King Bridei into the narrow hills near Dun Nechtain, brushing aside warnings about the terrain ahead.
evt-05-20-685-picts.prompt: What happens when Ecgfrith presses the pursuit into the Pictish highlands?

choices.text: The Picts spring an ambush, destroying the Northumbrian army and killing Ecgfrith
The Picts surrender the field without a fight
Ecgfrith negotiates a truce and withdraws his army safely
The Northumbrians rout the Picts and extend their control over the north

evt-05-20-685-picts.butterflyEffect: The Picts sprang an ambush near a loch, annihilating the Northumbrian army and killing Ecgfrith himself. His death shattered Northumbrian dominance over northern Britain, permanently checking its expansion and securing Pictish independence for generations, a turning point on the long road to the kingdom of Alba.

evt-05-20-794-anglo-saxon-chronicle.scenario: You serve at the East Anglian court in 794 as King Æthelberht prepares to travel to Mercia, seeking marriage to King Offa's daughter despite whispers about Offa's ambitions toward East Anglia.
evt-05-20-794-anglo-saxon-chronicle.prompt: What happens to Æthelberht at Offa's court?

choices.text: He marries the princess and forms a lasting alliance
He flees into exile in Frankia
He is imprisoned but later released unharmed
He is beheaded on Offa's orders

evt-05-20-794-anglo-saxon-chronicle.butterflyEffect: Offa had Æthelberht beheaded, and Mercia moved to absorb East Anglia under its overlordship. The slain king was later venerated as a martyr-saint, and Hereford Cathedral was founded in his honor, turning a political murder into a lasting cult of sainthood.

evt-05-20-1217-first-barons-war.scenario: It is dawn on 20 May 1217, and you ride with William Marshal's relief force approaching Lincoln, where rebel English barons and their French allies under the Comte de Perche besiege the royal castle.
evt-05-20-1217-first-barons-war.prompt: What does Marshal's force do to break the siege?

choices.text: Wait outside the walls for reinforcements before engaging
Blockade the city and starve out the defenders
Negotiate a truce with the French commander before fighting
Force a surprise entry through a side gate to attack from within

evt-05-20-1217-first-barons-war.butterflyEffect: Marshal's men stormed through a side gate into the city, routing the besiegers in a rout later nicknamed the 'Fair of Lincoln' for the plunder that followed. The victory crushed baronial resistance, forced Prince Louis's withdrawal under the Treaty of Lambeth, and secured young Henry III's throne alongside the reissue of Magna Carta.

evt-05-20-1515-durer-s-rhinoceros.scenario: You serve at the court of King Manuel I of Portugal in 1515. A live Indian rhinoceros, sent as a diplomatic gift, has just arrived in Lisbon, and ancient texts claim this beast is the mortal enemy of the elephant.
evt-05-20-1515-durer-s-rhinoceros.prompt: What does King Manuel decide to do with the rhinoceros to settle the old legend?

choices.text: Quietly add it to the royal menagerie and tell no one
Release it back into the wild immediately
Stage a fight between the rhinoceros and an elephant to test the legend
Have it slaughtered and dissected by physicians

evt-05-20-1515-durer-s-rhinoceros.butterflyEffect: Manuel staged a public fight between the rhinoceros and a royal elephant, which fled in fright, seeming to confirm the ancient claim. Later that year he sent the rhinoceros as a gift to Pope Leo X, but it drowned in a shipwreck off Italy; a written description of it reached Albrecht Dürer, whose imagined woodcut of the animal shaped European ideas of rhinos for the next three centuries.

evt-05-20-1875-metre-convention.scenario: You are a delegate in Paris on 20 May 1875, representing your government among seventeen nations signing a treaty meant to end the chaos of incompatible national weights and measures.
evt-05-20-1875-metre-convention.prompt: What institution should the treaty create to keep global measurements uniform?

choices.text: An International Bureau of Weights and Measures to hold standard prototypes
An international patent office for new inventions
A global authority to standardize time zones
A world central bank to fix a single global currency

evt-05-20-1875-metre-convention.butterflyEffect: The treaty established the International Bureau of Weights and Measures at Sèvres, tasked with safeguarding the standard metre and kilogram prototypes. That framework still underpins the modern International System of Units, enabling standardized trade and science worldwide.

evt-05-20-1927-treaty-of-jeddah-1927.scenario: You are a British diplomat in Jeddah in May 1927, negotiating with Ibn Saud, who has recently conquered the Hejaz and consolidated his rule over Nejd after defeating the Hashemite dynasty.
evt-05-20-1927-treaty-of-jeddah-1927.prompt: What must Britain concede to secure peaceful relations with the new ruler?

choices.text: Insist Britain retain protectorate status over the region
Demand Ibn Saud restore the Hashemites to the throne
Recognize Ibn Saud's full sovereignty over Hejaz and Nejd
Require Ibn Saud to cede Red Sea ports to British control

evt-05-20-1927-treaty-of-jeddah-1927.butterflyEffect: Britain formally recognized Ibn Saud's full sovereignty over Hejaz and Nejd, abandoning its earlier ties to the ousted Hashemites. This recognition cleared the path for Ibn Saud to unify his realms into the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in 1932, setting the stage for later Western oil concessions.

evt-05-20-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It is dawn on 20 May 1941, and you command Commonwealth troops defending the airfield at Heraklion on Crete. German transport planes are droning overhead, and paratroopers are already tumbling out of the sky onto the fields around you.
evt-05-20-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: What should you order your men to do as the German paratroopers land?

choices.text: Withdraw the garrison to the coast immediately
Surrender the airfield to avoid casualties
Counterattack at once before the paratroopers can regroup
Hold position and wait passively for naval reinforcement

evt-05-20-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Commonwealth and Greek defenders engaged the paratroopers immediately, inflicting brutal casualties on Germany's elite airborne forces before Crete finally fell ten days later. The losses were so severe that Hitler, alarmed by the cost, never again authorized a major airborne invasion for the rest of the war.

evt-05-20-1943-luttra-woman.scenario: It is 20 May 1943, and you are cutting peat in a bog near Luttra, Sweden, when your blade strikes something hard. Brushing away the muck, you uncover a human skull, remarkably preserved by the bog itself.
evt-05-20-1943-luttra-woman.prompt: What is the right thing to do after uncovering the skull in the peat?

choices.text: Report the find to the authorities so archaeologists can examine it
Rebury it quietly and continue cutting peat
Sell it to a local collector for extra money
Keep the skull as a curiosity at home

evt-05-20-1943-luttra-woman.butterflyEffect: The remains, later called the Luttra Woman, were examined and radiocarbon-dated to 3928–3651 BC, making her the earliest known Neolithic individual from Western Sweden as of 2015. Raspberry seeds found in her stomach earned her the nickname Hallonflickan, and her case added valuable data to the study of Scandinavian bog bodies.

evt-05-20-1983-virology.scenario: You work in Luc Montagnier's laboratory at the Pasteur Institute in Paris, studying lymph node samples from patients showing early signs of the mysterious immune-collapse disease sweeping through hospitals.
evt-05-20-1983-virology.prompt: What breakthrough do you report to the scientific community on 20 May 1983?

choices.text: Proved the illness was a hereditary immune disorder
Identified a drug-resistant bacterial infection as the cause
Isolated a novel retrovirus that may cause the immune disease
Traced the disease to contaminated blood-clotting proteins alone

evt-05-20-1983-virology.butterflyEffect: Montagnier's team announced isolation of a novel retrovirus, later named HIV, from an AIDS patient. The finding launched a bitter transatlantic priority dispute with Robert Gallo's US lab, eventually resolved diplomatically, and led to Montagnier and Françoise Barré-Sinoussi sharing the 2008 Nobel Prize in Medicine.

evt-05-20-2012-2012-northern-italy-earth.scenario: It is May 2012 in Emilia-Romagna, Italy. The first earthquake has cracked walls in the cheese warehouses and workshops where you and your neighbours work, and managers are anxious to keep production running before a bigger loss hits their business.
evt-05-20-2012-2012-northern-italy-earth.prompt: What happens when a second, larger quake strikes days later while some employees are back at work?

choices.text: The second quake causes no additional structural damage anywhere
Workers who returned to damaged buildings die when they collapse in the second quake
All employees had already evacuated permanently, so no further deaths occur
Authorities had demolished every damaged factory before the second quake struck

evt-05-20-2012-2012-northern-italy-earth.butterflyEffect: Several of the 20 additional deaths in the second quake were workers who had returned to damaged factories and warehouses under pressure to keep production going. The disaster sparked lasting debate in Italy over employer responsibility during aftershock periods and led to tighter rules on reopening quake-damaged industrial buildings.

evt-05-20-2013-2013-moore-tornado.scenario: It is the afternoon of 20 May 2013 in Moore, Oklahoma. Sirens wail as a massive tornado bears down, and you are a teacher at Plaza Towers Elementary, herding children into the hallway because the school has no underground storm shelter.
evt-05-20-2013-2013-moore-tornado.prompt: What happens to Plaza Towers Elementary when the EF5 tornado strikes directly?

choices.text: Buses evacuate all the children safely before the tornado arrives
An underground storm shelter protects every student unharmed
The tornado levels the school, and several children die despite shelter efforts
The tornado veers away at the last moment, sparing the school entirely

evt-05-20-2013-2013-moore-tornado.butterflyEffect: The tornado leveled Plaza Towers Elementary, and seven children died despite staff efforts to shelter them in interior hallways. The tragedy fueled a statewide campaign for dedicated storm shelters in Oklahoma schools, though funding disputes left many schools still unprotected years afterward.

evt-05-20-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.scenario: You are one of the last Ukrainian defenders holed up in the ruins of the Azovstal steel plant in Mariupol. The city outside has fallen, ammunition is nearly gone, and Kyiv has just issued new orders about what to do next.
evt-05-20-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.prompt: What did the last defenders of Mariupol ultimately do as the siege ended?

choices.text: Break out overland toward friendly lines
Fight on until every last soldier was killed
Escape by boat across the Sea of Azov
Surrender under a negotiated evacuation as ordered by command

evt-05-20-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.butterflyEffect: Following orders, the remaining Azovstal defenders surrendered in a negotiated evacuation, becoming prisoners of war rather than fighting to the last man. Mariupol's fall gave Russia a strategic land corridor to Crimea, while the siege itself became an enduring symbol of Ukrainian resistance and a flashpoint in later prisoner-exchange negotiations.

evt-05-21-878-arab-byzantine-wars.scenario: It is early 878, and you are a Byzantine officer inside Syracuse, Sicily's greatest remaining Byzantine city, blockaded by an Aghlabid army for nearly a year. Messengers sent to Constantinople begging for a relief fleet have brought no answer.
evt-05-21-878-arab-byzantine-wars.prompt: What actually happened as the long siege reached its final weeks?

choices.text: A relief fleet arrived just in time to break the siege
The city held out and negotiated favorable terms of surrender
No relief came, and the city fell to the besiegers
The Aghlabids abandoned the siege due to disease in their camp

evt-05-21-878-arab-byzantine-wars.butterflyEffect: No Byzantine fleet ever arrived, and Syracuse fell to the Aghlabids in May 878, ending centuries of Byzantine rule over the city. The loss accelerated the Muslim conquest of Sicily, though Byzantine forces held on around Taormina in the island's northeast for another generation.

evt-05-21-1138-crusades.scenario: It is 1138, and you advise the Emir of Shaizar, whose city has endured weeks of siege by the combined army of Byzantine Emperor John II Komnenos and the Crusader princes of Antioch and Tripoli. Food is running short and no relief force is coming.
evt-05-21-1138-crusades.prompt: What should the Emir do to end the siege on the best terms available?

choices.text: Surrender unconditionally and abandon the city
Sue for terms and accept vassalage under Byzantine overlordship, paying tribute
Appeal to the Abbasid Caliph in Baghdad for immediate relief
Break out and attack the besiegers at night

evt-05-21-1138-crusades.butterflyEffect: The Emir bought off the siege with a large tribute and a nominal oath of vassalage to Byzantium. The uneasy Byzantine-Crusader alliance collapsed soon afterward over rival claims to Antioch, and Shaizar's Munqidhite rulers kept their effective independence for decades.

evt-05-21-1703-daniel-defoe.scenario: It is 1703 in London, and you hold copies of an anonymous pamphlet, "The Shortest Way with Dissenters," whose savage satire calling for the persecution of religious dissenters has just been taken as sincere by the authorities. Its author, Daniel Defoe, is about to be identified.
evt-05-21-1703-daniel-defoe.prompt: What happens to Defoe once he is revealed as the author?

choices.text: He is arrested and imprisoned for seditious libel
He is pardoned personally by Queen Anne
He is knighted for his cleverness
He flees to the Netherlands to escape prosecution

evt-05-21-1703-daniel-defoe.butterflyEffect: Defoe was arrested, pilloried, and imprisoned in Newgate for seditious libel, an ordeal that nearly ruined him financially but built his reputation as a fearless writer. He later turned to journalism and, in his fifties, to novels such as Robinson Crusoe, helping to establish the modern English novel.

evt-05-21-1851-congress-of-colombia.scenario: You sit in the Congress of Colombia in Bogotá on 21 May 1851. President José Hilario López's liberal government has pushed forward a bill to end slavery nationwide, and slaveholding members are demanding terms before they will let it pass.
evt-05-21-1851-congress-of-colombia.prompt: What did the final law actually provide to secure its passage?

choices.text: Freedom granted only to enslaved men who joined the army
Immediate freedom for all, with government bonds compensating former owners
A free-womb law freeing only children born after the decree
Immediate freedom with no compensation of any kind

evt-05-21-1851-congress-of-colombia.butterflyEffect: The law freed all enslaved people as of 1 January 1852, but compensated owners with government bonds rather than freeing slaves outright without payment. The measure, combined with other liberal reforms, angered conservative and slaveholding regions and helped spark armed uprisings later that year, though abolition itself was never reversed.

evt-05-21-1856-sacking-of-lawrence.scenario: It is May 21, 1856, in Lawrence, Kansas. A pro-slavery posse of some 800 men, led by the county sheriff and backed by cannon, marches on your free-state town to arrest its leaders and smash its printing presses.
evt-05-21-1856-sacking-of-lawrence.prompt: What do the free-state settlers of Lawrence do as the armed posse arrives?

choices.text: Offer no armed resistance and let the town be ransacked
Negotiate a bribe to spare the printing presses
Evacuate the entire town before the posse arrives
Arm themselves and fight the posse in the streets

evt-05-21-1856-sacking-of-lawrence.butterflyEffect: Free-state leaders chose not to resist, and the posse destroyed two printing presses and burned the Free State Hotel, though no one was killed in the attack itself. The sacking became a propaganda weapon for both sides and helped push John Brown toward the deadly Pottawatomie Massacre days later, deepening the violence of Bleeding Kansas.

evt-05-21-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: It is May 1864 near Spotsylvania Court House, Virginia. You serve under Ulysses S. Grant after ferocious fighting, including the brutal hand-to-hand combat at the "Bloody Angle," leaves both armies battered but neither broken.
evt-05-21-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What does Grant do after this costly, inconclusive battle against Lee?

choices.text: Propose a truce with Lee to negotiate peace
Retreat north across the Rapidan to regroup
Hand over command of the army to Sherman
Continue advancing south toward Richmond despite heavy losses

evt-05-21-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Rather than retreat as previous Union commanders had after setbacks, Grant pressed on southward toward Richmond, famously vowing to "fight it out on this line." This relentless pressure defined the Overland Campaign, leading to Cold Harbor and the long siege of Petersburg, and ultimately ground down Lee's army over the war's final year.

evt-05-21-1911-porfirio-diaz.scenario: It is May 1911, and revolutionary forces under Francisco Madero have captured Ciudad Juárez. After more than three decades in power, Porfirio Díaz's government is collapsing under the weight of the uprising.
evt-05-21-1911-porfirio-diaz.prompt: How does Díaz respond to end the fighting and save Mexico from further bloodshed?

choices.text: Call a snap election to renew his mandate
Sign a treaty agreeing to resign and go into exile
Order a full military crackdown on the rebels
Appoint Madero as his vice president

evt-05-21-1911-porfirio-diaz.butterflyEffect: Díaz signed the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez, agreeing to resign and sail into exile in France, where he died in 1915. His departure did not bring the stability he hoped for—Madero's presidency soon unraveled, plunging Mexico into a decade-long revolution that reshaped the country's politics and society.

evt-05-21-1925-doktor-faust.scenario: It is 1924, and you are Philipp Jarnach, pupil of the recently deceased composer Ferruccio Busoni, holding the unfinished manuscript of Busoni's opera Doktor Faust, which breaks off before its final scene.
evt-05-21-1925-doktor-faust.prompt: What do you do to bring Busoni's unfinished masterpiece to the stage?

choices.text: Leave the opera unfinished and unperformed out of respect
Complete the final scene using Busoni's sketches and stylistic voice
Rewrite the entire opera in your own style
Commission an entirely new libretto and score

evt-05-21-1925-doktor-faust.butterflyEffect: Jarnach completed the ending himself, and the opera premiered in Dresden in 1925, becoming the standard version performed for decades. Not until 1982 did musicologist Antony Beaumont produce an alternative completion using overlooked Busoni sketches, giving the opera a second ending still performed today.

evt-05-21-1927-charles-lindbergh.scenario: It is the dead of night somewhere over the mid-Atlantic. You have been awake for over twenty hours alone in the cramped cockpit of the Spirit of St. Louis, with no radio, no autopilot, and no visibility of the ocean below.
evt-05-21-1927-charles-lindbergh.prompt: With no modern instruments, how do you keep the aircraft on course to Paris?

choices.text: Navigate solely by following the North Star
Triangulate your position using radio beacon signals
Calculate heading, speed, and time using dead reckoning and a compass
Land briefly on the water to rest and recheck your position

evt-05-21-1927-charles-lindbergh.butterflyEffect: Lindbergh navigated purely by dead reckoning, using compass headings, airspeed, and elapsed time, fighting exhaustion for over 33 hours. His safe arrival in Paris made him a global celebrity and triggered the "Lindbergh Boom," a surge of public and commercial interest that rapidly expanded passenger aviation and air mail worldwide.

evt-05-21-1991-rajiv-gandhi.scenario: It is May 21, 1991, in Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu. Former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi is campaigning for re-election when a young woman steps forward from the crowd to greet him, an explosive belt concealed beneath her clothes.
evt-05-21-1991-rajiv-gandhi.prompt: What happens as she approaches him to bow at his feet?

choices.text: She is stopped by bodyguards before reaching him
She detonates the explosive belt, killing Gandhi and herself
She hands him a garland and steps back safely
She is searched and found to be unarmed

evt-05-21-1991-rajiv-gandhi.butterflyEffect: The bomber, a suicide attacker linked to the LTTE, detonated the device, killing Gandhi and herself in retaliation for his earlier deployment of Indian peacekeeping troops against the Tamil Tigers in Sri Lanka. The assassination shocked India, generated a wave of sympathy that helped Congress in the ongoing election, and led India to ban the LTTE outright.

evt-05-21-1998-suharto.scenario: You advise President Suharto in Jakarta on 21 May 1998. Weeks of student protests, deadly riots, and the collapse of the rupiah have stripped away his political support, and even his own ministers are wavering.
evt-05-21-1998-suharto.prompt: What does Suharto do that day?

choices.text: Dissolve the People's Consultative Assembly
Declare martial law and deploy the army against protesters
Flee the country for exile abroad
Resign the presidency, handing power to Vice President Habibie

evt-05-21-1998-suharto.butterflyEffect: Suharto resigned after 32 years in power, and Vice President B.J. Habibie was sworn in as his successor within hours. The fall of the New Order regime opened Indonesia's Reformasi era, bringing press freedom, decentralization, and the country's first free elections in 1999.

evt-05-21-2001-christiane-taubira.scenario: You are a deputy in the French National Assembly in May 2001, weighing the bill proposed by Christiane Taubira on how France should officially characterize the Atlantic and Indian Ocean slave trades and slavery in its history.
evt-05-21-2001-christiane-taubira.prompt: What did the Taubira law actually establish?

choices.text: A binding reparations fund paid directly to descendants
A formal apology delivered by the French President to former colonies
Official recognition of slavery as a crime against humanity and expanded school curricula on it
Criminal prosecution of living descendants of slave traders

evt-05-21-2001-christiane-taubira.butterflyEffect: The law formally recognized the slave trade and slavery as crimes against humanity and called for greater space in school curricula and historical research on the subject. It became a landmark of French memorial politics, later reinforced by the creation of a national day of remembrance and continuing debates over reparations.

evt-05-21-2003-2003-boumerdes-earthquake.scenario: It's just after 7:44 p.m. on May 21, 2003, in Boumerdès, Algeria. The ground has stopped shaking, but cracks now split the walls of the apartment blocks around you, and residents are unsure whether to go back inside.
evt-05-21-2003-2003-boumerdes-earthquake.prompt: As a structural engineer on the scene, what do you advise residents of the damaged buildings?

choices.text: Assume the buildings are fine since they are still standing
Advise everyone to stay inside since the worst has passed
Evacuate immediately in case aftershocks bring down weakened structures
Tell them to wait for an official inspection before making any decision

evt-05-21-2003-2003-boumerdes-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Many of the region's poorly constructed apartment blocks collapsed or were badly weakened, killing over 2,200 people. The disaster exposed decades of lax construction enforcement in Algeria's rapid postwar building boom, pushing authorities to tighten seismic building codes and inspection standards afterward.

evt-05-21-2006-republic-of-montenegro-19.scenario: It is May 21, 2006, and you are casting your vote in Montenegro's independence referendum. Under EU-brokered rules, a simple majority will not be enough to break the union with Serbia.
evt-05-21-2006-republic-of-montenegro-19.prompt: What threshold must the "yes" side clear for independence to pass?

choices.text: A two-thirds majority in parliament
Any simple majority over 50 percent
Approval by Serbia's own parliament
At least 55 percent of votes cast

evt-05-21-2006-republic-of-montenegro-19.butterflyEffect: The "yes" vote won with about 55.5 percent, narrowly clearing the required threshold. Montenegro declared independence on June 3, 2006, becoming the last republic to emerge from the breakup of Yugoslavia, and went on to join NATO and pursue EU membership.

evt-05-21-2014-2014-taipei-metro-attack.scenario: It's the afternoon of May 21, 2014, aboard a crowded Taipei Metro train nearing Jiangzicui Station. A young man has suddenly drawn two knives and begun attacking passengers around you.
evt-05-21-2014-2014-taipei-metro-attack.prompt: What is the safest immediate action to take as the train moves toward the next station?

choices.text: Force open the doors and jump from the moving train
Try to physically disarm the attacker alone
Alert the driver so the train can reach the next station and police can respond
Stay silent and hope the attacker moves to another carriage

evt-05-21-2014-2014-taipei-metro-attack.butterflyEffect: Passengers alerted the driver, who rushed the train to the next station where police were waiting and arrested the attacker, 21-year-old Cheng Chieh. It was the first fatal attack in the Taipei Metro's history, leading to visible security patrols and new safety protocols across the system; Cheng was executed in 2016.

evt-05-21-2015-islamic-state.scenario: It is May 2015, and you are Khaled al-Asaad, Palmyra's retired chief of antiquities, still living in the city as Islamic State fighters seize control. Militants demand you reveal where the ancient city's treasures have been hidden for safekeeping.
evt-05-21-2015-islamic-state.prompt: What does al-Asaad do when IS demands he disclose the hidden antiquities?

choices.text: Reveal the locations to save his life
Negotiate a bribe to buy his freedom
Flee the city before militants can question him
Refuse to cooperate despite the threat to his life

evt-05-21-2015-islamic-state.butterflyEffect: Al-Asaad refused, and he was publicly killed by IS that August, becoming a global symbol of resistance to cultural destruction. IS went on to demolish the Temple of Baalshamin and the Temple of Bel, but much of Palmyra's movable heritage survived because its location was never revealed.

evt-05-21-2017-ringling-bros-and-barnum-.scenario: It is 21 May 2017, and you are a longtime performer standing under the big top at Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum for what management has announced will be Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey's final show after 146 years on the road.
evt-05-21-2017-ringling-bros-and-barnum-.prompt: What did Feld Entertainment cite as the deciding factor in ending the circus?

choices.text: Declining ticket sales and high operating costs, worsened by the phase-out of elephant acts
A government ban on traveling animal exhibitions
A change in ownership that redirected the company toward film
Bankruptcy following a lawsuit from performers

evt-05-21-2017-ringling-bros-and-barnum-.butterflyEffect: Ticket sales fell sharply after elephants were retired from the show in 2016 amid animal-welfare pressure, and Feld Entertainment closed the circus in 2017 rather than keep running it at a loss. The brand didn't vanish for good: in 2023 Ringling relaunched as an animal-free touring show for a new generation.

evt-05-21-2024-greenfield-tornado.scenario: It's the afternoon of May 21, 2024, and you're operating a Doppler on Wheels radar unit tracking a violent supercell bearing down on Greenfield, Iowa. Your readings suddenly show winds inside the vortex spiking past 300 miles per hour.
evt-05-21-2024-greenfield-tornado.prompt: What should you do the moment the radar reveals these extreme wind speeds?

choices.text: Drive closer to get a clearer visual before reporting anything
Continue monitoring quietly until the tornado dissipates
Immediately relay the data so an emergency tornado warning can be issued
Wait for a second radar unit to confirm the reading before alerting anyone

evt-05-21-2024-greenfield-tornado.butterflyEffect: The tornado struck Greenfield with winds later estimated at 309–318 mph, one of only three times such extreme speeds have been measured by radar in a tornado. The event demonstrated the life-saving value of mobile Doppler radar and reinforced the push for faster, more localized tornado warnings in rural America.

evt-05-22-853-arab-byzantine-wars.scenario: It is 853, and you command a Byzantine naval squadron that has just landed at Damietta on the Nile Delta, finding the port's garrison unexpectedly absent and its warehouses full of arms and supplies.
evt-05-22-853-arab-byzantine-wars.prompt: What should the Byzantine raiders do with the undefended arsenal they have found?

choices.text: Burn the arsenal and carry off what can be taken, then withdraw
Garrison the port and try to hold it permanently
Negotiate a ransom with local officials before departing
Leave the supplies untouched and sail on toward Alexandria

evt-05-22-853-arab-byzantine-wars.butterflyEffect: The Byzantines burned the stockpiled weapons and supplies that had been gathered for an Abbasid naval campaign against Crete, dealing a serious setback to Muslim naval preparations. The humiliating raid also pushed Egypt's rulers to strengthen coastal defenses along the Nile Delta against further Byzantine incursions.

evt-05-22-1629-albrecht-von-wallenstein.scenario: You advise Emperor Ferdinand II in 1629 as his general Albrecht von Wallenstein negotiates with the defeated King Christian IV of Denmark, whose army has been driven from the war.
evt-05-22-1629-albrecht-von-wallenstein.prompt: What terms does Wallenstein offer to bring Denmark's king to peace?

choices.text: Require a permanent Habsburg garrison to be stationed in Denmark
Annex Danish territory as a permanent imperial possession
Restore his hereditary lands if he abandons his German allies and withdraws from imperial affairs
Force the king to convert to Catholicism as a condition of peace

evt-05-22-1629-albrecht-von-wallenstein.butterflyEffect: The Treaty of Lübeck restored Christian IV's hereditary lands in exchange for abandoning his German allies and staying out of imperial affairs. The lenient peace freed Ferdinand II to issue the aggressive Edict of Restitution, which alarmed Protestant princes and helped draw Sweden's Gustavus Adolphus into the war, prolonging the conflict for two more decades.

evt-05-22-1766-1766-istanbul-earthquake.scenario: It is the early hours before dawn on 22 May 1766. The ground beneath Constantinople convulses violently, and moments later you notice the sea along the shore of the Marmara beginning to withdraw unnaturally far from the beach.
evt-05-22-1766-1766-istanbul-earthquake.prompt: What should you do when you see the sea pull back after the shaking stops?

choices.text: Walk out onto the exposed seabed to look for stranded fish
Run inland to higher ground immediately
Return home to check on your belongings first
Wait calmly on the shore for the water to return naturally

evt-05-22-1766-1766-istanbul-earthquake.butterflyEffect: A tsunami followed the quake, battering the coast from Izmit to Rodosto and adding to the destruction. Among the casualties was the great dome of the Fatih Mosque, which collapsed and had to be rebuilt in a new style—one of many Istanbul landmarks reconstructed in the quake's aftermath.

evt-05-22-1816-ely-and-littleport-riots-.scenario: You are a farm labourer in Littleport, Cambridgeshire, in May 1816, watching neighbours smash into shops and threaten local magistrates over soaring bread prices and no work to be found.
evt-05-22-1816-ely-and-littleport-riots-.prompt: What happened to the rioters once troops restored order in the district?

choices.text: The rioters won higher wages from local farmers
All charges were dropped due to public sympathy
Many were tried at Ely, with several hanged for their part in the riots
Parliament abolished the Corn Laws in response

evt-05-22-1816-ely-and-littleport-riots-.butterflyEffect: Dragoons and armed townsmen put down the riot within days, and a special commission tried the rioters at Ely, convicting two dozen of them. Five men were hanged, making the episode one of the starkest symbols of the 'Bread or Blood' unrest that swept post-Napoleonic War England.

evt-05-22-1826-hms-beagle.scenario: You serve aboard HMS Beagle as she departs Plymouth on 22 May 1826 under Captain Pringle Stokes, bound for the far side of the Atlantic on Admiralty orders.
evt-05-22-1826-hms-beagle.prompt: What is the Beagle's assigned mission on this voyage?

choices.text: Transport of convicts to the penal colonies of Australia
Charting the west coast of Africa for the Royal Navy
Hydrographic survey of the coasts of Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego
A search for a Northwest Passage through the Arctic

evt-05-22-1826-hms-beagle.butterflyEffect: The Beagle was sent to survey the coasts of Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego for the Royal Navy's charts. Captain Stokes died by suicide during the harsh expedition, and his replacement, Robert FitzRoy, later commanded the Beagle's famous second voyage in 1831 that carried a young Charles Darwin around the world.

evt-05-22-1844-shiraz.scenario: It is the evening of 22 May 1844 in Shiraz. You are Mullá Husayn, a learned young cleric searching for the promised Qá'im, when a young merchant named Siyyid ʻAlí-Muhammad receives you and declares that he himself is that promised one.
evt-05-22-1844-shiraz.prompt: What does Mullá Husayn do upon hearing this startling claim?

choices.text: Accept him as a divine messenger and become his first follower
Dismiss the claim outright and leave Shiraz that night
Demand he perform a public miracle before considering it
Report the claim to the local Islamic authorities as heresy

evt-05-22-1844-shiraz.butterflyEffect: Mullá Husayn accepted the claim after the young merchant answered his questions and produced writings Husayn found miraculous, becoming the Báb's first disciple. The declaration is regarded as the founding moment of the Bábí religion, whose teachings later gave rise to the Baháʼí Faith, and the date is still commemorated as a holy day.

evt-05-22-1849-abraham-lincoln.scenario: You're a Springfield lawyer named Abraham Lincoln in 1849, tinkering with a model of inflatable bellows fitted to a boat's hull, an idea born after your own steamboat once ran aground on a shoal.
evt-05-22-1849-abraham-lincoln.prompt: What became of Lincoln's patented invention after it was granted?

choices.text: It was sold to a British shipping firm
It was never manufactured or used commercially
It was adopted by Mississippi riverboat companies
It became standard equipment on Union Navy ships

evt-05-22-1849-abraham-lincoln.butterflyEffect: Lincoln remains the only U.S. president to hold a patent, but his buoying device was never manufactured or put into commercial use. His hand-carved patent model survives today in the Smithsonian, a quirky reminder of his inventive streak before politics consumed his life.

evt-05-22-1856-charles-sumner.scenario: It is May 22, 1856, and you are on the floor of the United States Senate. Days earlier, Senator Charles Sumner delivered a blistering speech condemning slavery and insulting a South Carolina senator; now Congressman Preston Brooks strides toward Sumner's desk.
evt-05-22-1856-charles-sumner.prompt: What does Brooks do to Sumner in retaliation for his speech?

choices.text: Beats him repeatedly with a cane until he collapses
Moves to have him formally censured by the Senate
Has him arrested for disorderly conduct
Challenges him to a formal duel

evt-05-22-1856-charles-sumner.butterflyEffect: Brooks beat Sumner with a heavy cane until he collapsed unconscious, and it took Sumner years to fully recover and return to the Senate. The North hailed Sumner as a martyr to free speech while the South celebrated Brooks as a defender of honor, hardening sectional divisions on the road to civil war.

evt-05-22-1874-giuseppe-verdi.scenario: It's 22 May 1874, and you've packed into Milan's San Marco church for the premiere of a new choral work by Italy's most celebrated opera composer, who himself stands ready to conduct.
evt-05-22-1874-giuseppe-verdi.prompt: What occasion had moved Verdi to compose this Requiem?

choices.text: The death of King Victor Emmanuel II
The first anniversary of writer Alessandro Manzoni's death
The tenth anniversary of Italian unification
The death of fellow composer Gioachino Rossini

evt-05-22-1874-giuseppe-verdi.butterflyEffect: Verdi had once planned a collaborative requiem mourning Rossini's death in 1868 but shelved it. The death of writer Alessandro Manzoni in 1873 spurred him to finish a solo version, premiered on the first anniversary of Manzoni's death. It became one of the most performed choral works in history, fusing operatic drama with sacred music.

evt-05-22-1915-lassen-peak.scenario: It is the evening of May 22, 1915, and you live in the valley below Lassen Peak. The mountain, already smoking for months, suddenly erupts with terrifying violence, sending glowing rock and ash cascading down its slopes toward your farm.
evt-05-22-1915-lassen-peak.prompt: What should you do as the volcano unleashes its most violent eruption yet?

choices.text: Ignore it, since the mountain has smoked harmlessly for months
Climb closer to get a better look at the spectacle
Take shelter in a nearby mine shaft for safety
Flee immediately to higher ground away from the valley floor

evt-05-22-1915-lassen-peak.butterflyEffect: The eruption sent a pyroclastic flow and mudflow crashing through Hat Creek Valley, devastating the landscape, while ash drifted as far as Elko, Nevada. The event proved the Cascades were still active and helped prompt Congress to establish Lassen Volcanic National Park the following year, in 1916.

evt-05-22-1939-pact-of-steel.scenario: It is 22 May 1939 in Berlin. As Italy's foreign minister, you are about to put your signature beside Ribbentrop's on a new treaty binding Rome to Berlin.
evt-05-22-1939-pact-of-steel.prompt: What level of commitment does the Pact of Steel actually bind Italy to?

choices.text: An economic and trade cooperation agreement only
A non-aggression pact with no military obligations
Full unconditional mutual military support in any war
A purely defensive alliance triggered only if either nation is attacked

evt-05-22-1939-pact-of-steel.butterflyEffect: The pact obligated each power to support the other militarily in any war, offensive or defensive, with no opt-out for wars Italy hadn't chosen. Mussolini, despite knowing Italy was unprepared, felt bound to enter the Second World War alongside Germany in June 1940.

evt-05-22-1958-1958-anti-tamil-pogrom.scenario: It is 27 May 1958, and you serve in the government of Ceylon as ethnic riots targeting Tamils continue to spread across the island for a fifth day, with attacks and reprisals reported in multiple districts.
evt-05-22-1958-1958-anti-tamil-pogrom.prompt: What does the Prime Minister's government do to try to bring the violence under control?

choices.text: Resign and call for fresh elections to defuse tensions
Convene an immediate power-sharing conference with Tamil leaders
Leave the matter to local police without wider intervention
Declare a state of emergency and deploy the army to restore order

evt-05-22-1958-1958-anti-tamil-pogrom.butterflyEffect: Prime Minister S.W.R.D. Bandaranaike declared a state of emergency on 27 May 1958 and deployed troops to restore order, though sporadic violence continued for days afterward. The riots were the first island-wide ethnic violence since independence and badly damaged trust between Sinhalese and Tamil communities, a rupture that deepened over the following decades.

evt-05-22-1960-1960-valdivia-earthquake.scenario: It is the afternoon of 22 May 1960 near Valdivia, Chile. The ground has been shaking for what feels like an eternity, and when it finally stops, you notice the sea along the coast beginning to draw back sharply.
evt-05-22-1960-1960-valdivia-earthquake.prompt: What should you do as the ground stops shaking and the sea recedes?

choices.text: Flee immediately to high ground, away from the shoreline
Wait on the shore, assuming the worst has already passed
Stay in your house to gather valuables before leaving
Go down to the beach to see what caused the water to retreat

evt-05-22-1960-1960-valdivia-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The quake, later measured at roughly 9.5 on the moment magnitude scale, unleashed tsunamis that devastated southern Chile and then raced across the Pacific, killing people as far away as Hawaii, Japan and the Philippines hours later. Two days afterward, the nearby Cordón Caulle volcano erupted, and the disaster spurred major advances in plate tectonics research and tsunami warning systems.

evt-05-22-1972-dominion-of-ceylon.scenario: You sit in Ceylon's constituent assembly in May 1972, drafting a new constitution meant to sever the last symbolic ties to the British Crown while keeping the country within the Commonwealth of Nations.
evt-05-22-1972-dominion-of-ceylon.prompt: What fundamental change does the new constitution make to the nation's status?

choices.text: It splits the country into separate federal states
It makes the country a republic, ending the British monarch's role as head of state
It withdraws the country entirely from the Commonwealth of Nations
It restores a local hereditary monarchy in place of the British Crown

evt-05-22-1972-dominion-of-ceylon.butterflyEffect: Ceylon became the Republic of Sri Lanka, replacing the British monarch with a president as head of state while remaining in the Commonwealth. The new constitution also strengthened Sinhala nationalism in state policy, tensions that helped fuel the ethnic civil war that erupted a decade later.

evt-05-22-2002-federal-bureau-of-prisons.scenario: It is 22 May 2002. Searchers in Washington's Rock Creek Park have just uncovered skeletal remains believed to belong to Chandra Levy, the federal intern missing for nearly a year.
evt-05-22-2002-federal-bureau-of-prisons.prompt: What should investigators do with the newly found remains?

choices.text: Release the remains to the family without further testing
Close the case as an accidental death with no further inquiry
Immediately arrest Congressman Gary Condit on suspicion of murder
Order forensic identification and treat the site as a homicide investigation

evt-05-22-2002-federal-bureau-of-prisons.butterflyEffect: The remains were confirmed as Levy's and the case was reclassified as a homicide. The investigation eventually led to the 2010 conviction of Ingmar Guandique, but that conviction was overturned in 2015 and the murder remains officially unsolved.

evt-05-22-2010-mangaluru.scenario: You are the captain of Air India Express Flight 812 on approach to Mangalore's tabletop runway on 22 May 2010. The aircraft touches down well past the normal landing point, and your first officer questions whether you still have enough runway to stop safely.
evt-05-22-2010-mangaluru.prompt: What is the correct response the moment the touchdown is recognized as long?

choices.text: Continue the landing and brake as hard as possible
Execute an immediate go-around and abort the landing
Apply reverse thrust only and keep the nose wheel up
Extend flaps further and attempt to stop on the remaining strip

evt-05-22-2010-mangaluru.butterflyEffect: The crew continued the landing rather than aborting, and the aircraft overshot the runway, plunged into a gorge, and caught fire, with 158 of 166 aboard killed.
