The investigation cited the captain's failure to go around despite the first officer's warnings, and it prompted renewed scrutiny of pilot fatigue rules and India's tabletop runways.

evt-05-22-2014-prayut-chan-o-cha.scenario: It is 22 May 2014, and you are a Thai army officer watching General Prayut Chan-o-cha announce on national television that the military has taken full control of the government, two days after martial law was declared.
evt-05-22-2014-prayut-chan-o-cha.prompt: What did Prayut do immediately after seizing power?

choices.text: Dissolved the monarchy's role in government
Called for immediate new elections
Suspended the constitution and formed the National Council for Peace and Order
Restored the ousted prime minister to office

evt-05-22-2014-prayut-chan-o-cha.butterflyEffect: Prayut suspended the constitution and set up the National Council for Peace and Order (NCPO) to govern Thailand. The junta ruled for five years before elections in 2019 kept him in power as prime minister under a new constitution, a role he held until 2023.

evt-05-23-1430-hundred-years-war.scenario: It is 23 May 1430 outside the walls of Compiègne. You fight alongside Joan of Arc as Burgundian troops close in on the rearguard covering the town's retreat.
evt-05-23-1430-hundred-years-war.prompt: What happens as the defenders try to get back inside the gates?

choices.text: She surrenders voluntarily to negotiate a truce
French reinforcements arrive in time to save her
She escapes through a hidden tunnel beneath the walls
The gates close too soon and Joan is captured outside the walls

evt-05-23-1430-hundred-years-war.butterflyEffect: The gates were closed before Joan could re-enter, and she was pulled from her horse and captured by Burgundian soldiers. She was sold to the English, tried for heresy, and burned at the stake in 1431, later becoming a national symbol of France and a canonized saint.

evt-05-23-1533-thomas-cranmer.scenario: You are Thomas Cranmer, newly made Archbishop of Canterbury, presiding over the case of Henry VIII's marriage to Catherine of Aragon in May 1533.
evt-05-23-1533-thomas-cranmer.prompt: What ruling did Cranmer hand down on the king's first marriage?

choices.text: Delayed judgment indefinitely to avoid controversy
Annulled the marriage, ruling it had never been valid
Referred the case back to the Pope in Rome
Upheld the marriage and refused Henry's request

evt-05-23-1533-thomas-cranmer.butterflyEffect: Cranmer declared the marriage to Catherine null and void, clearing the way for Henry's marriage to the already-pregnant Anne Boleyn to stand and for their daughter Elizabeth to be born legitimate. The ruling deepened England's break from Rome and set Cranmer on the path to leading the English Reformation, for which he was later burned as a heretic under Mary I.

evt-05-23-1555-pope-paul-iv.scenario: You are a cardinal advising Pope Paul IV. Spanish troops have invaded parts of the Papal States, and the fiercely anti-Spanish pontiff is weighing how to strike back at the might of Habsburg Spain.
evt-05-23-1555-pope-paul-iv.prompt: What does Paul IV do to counter the Spanish invasion?

choices.text: Appeal to the Holy Roman Emperor for mediation
Excommunicate the Spanish king and his commanders
Negotiate a private settlement directly with King Philip II
Call for French military intervention against Spain

evt-05-23-1555-pope-paul-iv.butterflyEffect: Paul IV called for French military intervention, but the French were defeated and Spanish troops advanced to the edge of Rome. The two sides reached a compromise, both withdrawing their forces, and Paul IV was forced to abandon his anti-Spanish stance for a policy of neutrality between France and Spain for the rest of his papacy.

evt-05-23-1568-eighty-years-war.scenario: It is 23 May 1568 near Heiligerlee in Friesland. You ride with Louis of Nassau's rebel force, newly gathered against Spanish rule, facing royal troops commanded by the Duke of Aremberg.
evt-05-23-1568-eighty-years-war.prompt: What was the outcome of this first armed clash of the Dutch Revolt?

choices.text: The rebels won, killing the Spanish commander
Both sides withdrew without fighting
Louis of Nassau surrendered to avoid bloodshed
The Spanish crushed the rebel force outright

evt-05-23-1568-eighty-years-war.butterflyEffect: The rebels won, killing Aremberg, though Louis's brother Adolf also died in the fighting. The victory was short-lived—the Duke of Alva crushed the rebels weeks later at Jemmingen—but the clash is remembered as the opening battle of the Eighty Years' War, which ended in Dutch independence in 1648.

evt-05-23-1706-war-of-the-spanish-succes.scenario: It is 23 May 1706 near the village of Ramillies. You serve under the Duke of Marlborough as his Grand Alliance army faces a French and Bavarian force under Marshal Villeroi across open, rolling ground.
evt-05-23-1706-war-of-the-spanish-succes.prompt: How does Marlborough break the French line to win the battle?

choices.text: He stages a feint on one flank, then masses his strongest force to smash the weakened center
He bypasses the battle entirely and marches on Brussels
He orders a single massed frontal charge along the entire line
He waits overnight and ambushes the French camp in darkness

evt-05-23-1706-war-of-the-spanish-succes.butterflyEffect: Marlborough feinted heavily on the French right to draw off their reserves, then massed his cavalry and infantry for a crushing blow through the weakened center-left, routing Villeroi's army. The victory swept the French out of most of the Spanish Netherlands, handing the Grand Alliance control of Brussels and Antwerp within weeks.

evt-05-23-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 23 May 1862 at Front Royal, Virginia. You command a small Union garrison guarding a rail depot when Stonewall Jackson's much larger force suddenly appears out of the wooded hills to your east, cutting off your line of retreat toward Winchester.
evt-05-23-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: What does your garrison do when Jackson's men overwhelm your position?

choices.text: They retreat in a scattered, disorganized rout, and many are captured
They surrender immediately without firing a shot
They counterattack and drive Jackson's force back across the Shenandoah
They hold their ground and repel Jackson's attack entirely

evt-05-23-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Union garrison broke and fled in disorder, and many were captured as Jackson's Valley Campaign gathered momentum. The panic reached Washington, prompting Lincoln to divert troops meant to reinforce McClellan's advance on Richmond, weakening the Peninsula Campaign at a critical moment.

evt-05-23-1873-north-west-mounted-police.scenario: It is 1873 and you have just enlisted in Canada's newly created North-West Mounted Police, preparing to ride west into the vast North-West Territories.
evt-05-23-1873-north-west-mounted-police.prompt: What is your force's primary mission on the frontier?

choices.text: Serve strictly as a customs and tax-collection service
Wage a military campaign to annex US territory
Establish law, order and Canadian authority while easing tensions with the US and First Nations
Patrol Eastern Canadian cities against urban crime

evt-05-23-1873-north-west-mounted-police.butterflyEffect: The NWMP established law and judicial authority ahead of mass settlement, deliberately avoiding the violent 'Wild West' pattern seen south of the border. Renamed the Royal Canadian Mounted Police in 1920, it became a lasting symbol of Canadian federal authority in the West.

evt-05-23-1895-samuel-j-tilden.scenario: You are a trustee in New York in 1895, weighing whether to merge the Astor Library's vast reference collection with the smaller Lenox Library, using funds Samuel J. Tilden had left toward a great public library.
evt-05-23-1895-samuel-j-tilden.prompt: What did the trustees decide to do with the two libraries?

choices.text: Merge them to create the New York Public Library
Relocate the Lenox Library's holdings to Albany
Keep both libraries separate but under city funding
Sell the Astor collection to a private university

evt-05-23-1895-samuel-j-tilden.butterflyEffect: They merged, forming the New York Public Library, which opened its landmark Fifth Avenue building in 1911 and grew into one of the largest library systems in the world. Tilden's bequest, combined with the Astor and Lenox collections, became the seed of free public research access for millions of New Yorkers.

evt-05-23-1939-uss-sailfish-ss-192.scenario: It is 23 May 1939, and you are aboard USS Squalus during a test dive off Portsmouth, New Hampshire. The main induction valve has failed, and seawater is flooding the aft torpedo room and engine rooms fast.
evt-05-23-1939-uss-sailfish-ss-192.prompt: What must the surviving crew forward do to have any chance of rescue?

choices.text: Try to pump the flooded compartments dry from inside
Seal the watertight doors and wait for rescue
Escape immediately through the forward torpedo tubes
Attempt an emergency free ascent through the flooding

evt-05-23-1939-uss-sailfish-ss-192.butterflyEffect: The crew sealed the watertight doors, isolating the flooded compartments and drowning 26 men aft, but saving the 33 trapped forward. Rescuers used the McCann Rescue Chamber for the first time in history to bring all 33 survivors safely to the surface, and the salvaged sub returned to service in 1940 as USS Sailfish.

evt-05-23-1992-giovanni-falcone.scenario: It is 23 May 1992 on the A29 motorway near Capaci, Sicily. Giovanni Falcone, the judge who built the Maxi Trial case against the Sicilian Mafia, is driving from the airport toward Palermo, a route the Corleonesi have mined with explosives.
evt-05-23-1992-giovanni-falcone.prompt: What did Falcone's assassination trigger across Italy in the months that followed?

choices.text: Italy's anti-mafia courts were disbanded in the aftermath
The investigation into the bombing was closed within weeks for lack of leads
The government quietly negotiated a truce with the Corleonesi
Mass public outrage forced a sweeping anti-mafia crackdown and tougher prison laws

evt-05-23-1992-giovanni-falcone.butterflyEffect: Public outrage over Falcone's death, and Paolo Borsellino's murder weeks later, forced the Italian state into an unprecedented crackdown, including the harsh 41-bis prison isolation regime for mafia bosses. It also fueled the manhunt that captured Mafia boss Salvatore 'Totò' Riina in January 1993.

evt-05-23-1999-owen-hart.scenario: You are a WWF producer backstage at Kansas City's Kemper Arena on 23 May 1999. Owen Hart has just fallen fatally during a stunt entrance, and the live pay-per-view broadcast is still running.
evt-05-23-1999-owen-hart.prompt: What did WWF management actually do after learning of Hart's fatal fall?

choices.text: Continue the pay-per-view as scheduled without informing the live audience
Cut to a pre-taped rerun instead of the live event
Announce his death to the arena crowd right away
Cancel the remainder of the broadcast immediately

evt-05-23-1999-owen-hart.butterflyEffect: WWF continued broadcasting Over the Edge as scheduled, only announcing Hart's death after the show ended. The decision drew intense criticism, led to a wrongful-death lawsuit by his widow Martha Hart, and pushed wrestling promotions to abandon dangerous high-wire entrance stunts.

evt-05-23-2002-kyoto-protocol.scenario: It is 23 May 2002. Iceland has just deposited its ratification of the Kyoto Protocol, pushing the count of ratifying nations past the 55-party threshold. You are a UN climate official checking whether the treaty can now take legal effect.
evt-05-23-2002-kyoto-protocol.prompt: What else must happen before the Kyoto Protocol actually enters into force?

choices.text: The UN Security Council must formally approve the treaty
The treaty automatically takes effect once 55 parties ratify
Every UN member state must ratify it
Ratifying parties must also represent 55% of 1990 global emissions

evt-05-23-2002-kyoto-protocol.butterflyEffect: Hitting 55 ratifying parties was only half the bar; the treaty also needed ratifiers representing 55% of 1990 global emissions. With the US refusing to ratify, that threshold wasn't reached until Russia ratified in late 2004, letting Kyoto finally enter into force on 16 February 2005.

evt-05-23-2013-interstate-5-in-washingto.scenario: It is 23 May 2013 on Interstate 5 over the Skagit River near Mount Vernon. A truck hauling an oversized load approaches the old steel truss bridge, and its escort must judge whether the load will clear the overhead structure.
evt-05-23-2013-interstate-5-in-washingto.prompt: What should have been done to prevent the truck from striking the bridge's overhead truss?

choices.text: Increase speed to clear the truss before it could be struck
Lower the truck's height while already crossing the bridge
Secure a proper oversize-load permit confirming the bridge's exact clearance beforehand
Ignore posted clearance signs since trucks had crossed safely before

evt-05-23-2013-interstate-5-in-washingto.butterflyEffect: The truck's load struck an overhead girder, collapsing a span into the river; three people were injured but none killed. The collapse of a functioning interstate bridge stunned the public and reignited national debate over America's aging 'fracture-critical' infrastructure and oversize-load permitting.

evt-05-23-2015-tornado-outbreak-and-floo.scenario: It is the night of 23–24 May 2015 and you live along the Blanco River in Hays County, Texas. Rain has fallen for days and the river outside your window is rising with alarming speed.
evt-05-23-2015-tornado-outbreak-and-floo.prompt: What should you do as the floodwater rises through the night?

choices.text: Pack belongings carefully before leaving the house
Evacuate to higher ground immediately rather than wait for an official alert
Wait for a formal evacuation order before leaving
Climb to the roof and wait for the water to recede

evt-05-23-2015-tornado-outbreak-and-floo.butterflyEffect: The Blanco River surged more than 40 feet in hours, sweeping away entire blocks of homes near Wimberley and killing dozens across Texas and Oklahoma. The disaster exposed gaps in nighttime flash-flood warning systems and pushed Central Texas communities to overhaul emergency alerts and floodplain building rules.

evt-05-23-2016-islamic-state.scenario: It is 23 May 2016 in the government-held coastal city of Jableh, Syria. Suicide bombers strike crowded civilian targets far from any active front line.
evt-05-23-2016-islamic-state.prompt: What did these coordinated bombings signal about ISIS's strategy as it lost ground elsewhere?

choices.text: A shift from holding territory to striking civilians in government-held areas beyond its control
A negotiated ceasefire with the Syrian government
A retreat from all offensive operations
A formal alliance with Syrian opposition forces

evt-05-23-2016-islamic-state.butterflyEffect: As ISIS's territorial holdings in Iraq and Syria began shrinking under coalition and Syrian offensives, it increasingly relied on suicide bombings deep inside government-held areas. This shift toward asymmetric attacks on civilians outside its control foreshadowed the group's transition into an insurgency after its territorial defeat in 2017–2019.

evt-05-23-2017-rodrigo-duterte.scenario: It is 23 May 2017. Militants from the ISIS-linked Maute Group have seized parts of Marawi City, torched buildings, and taken hostages, including a Catholic priest. President Duterte, abroad in Moscow, must respond.
evt-05-23-2017-rodrigo-duterte.prompt: What does Duterte declare in response to the Marawi attack?

choices.text: Request immediate US airstrikes on the city
Open ceasefire negotiations with the Maute Group
Declare martial law across the entire Philippines
Declare martial law across all of Mindanao

evt-05-23-2017-rodrigo-duterte.butterflyEffect: Duterte declared martial law across the entire island of Mindanao, not just Marawi. The resulting Battle of Marawi dragged on for five months, devastated the city, and martial law over Mindanao was repeatedly extended by Congress for years afterward, drawing criticism over military overreach.

evt-05-23-2021-ryanair-flight-4978.scenario: You are the pilot of Ryanair Flight 4978, crossing Belarusian airspace en route from Athens to Vilnius on 23 May 2021, when Belarusian air traffic control claims a bomb threat and a MiG-29 appears alongside your aircraft, ordering you to divert.
evt-05-23-2021-ryanair-flight-4978.prompt: What do you do when ordered to divert to Minsk?

choices.text: Divert instead to the nearest airport in Lithuania
Hold current course while contacting airline headquarters
Comply and land the aircraft in Minsk
Refuse the order and continue on to Vilnius

evt-05-23-2021-ryanair-flight-4978.butterflyEffect: The crew complied and landed in Minsk, where authorities arrested passenger and dissident journalist Roman Protasevich along with his girlfriend. The incident was condemned internationally as state-sponsored air piracy, prompting the EU to ban Belarusian carriers from its airspace and impose new sanctions on the Lukashenko government.

evt-05-23-2022-anthony-albanese.scenario: You have just been sworn in as Australia's 31st Prime Minister on 23 May 2022, hours after your election win, with an international summit already on the calendar.
evt-05-23-2022-anthony-albanese.prompt: What did Albanese do immediately after being sworn in?

choices.text: Announced a snap referendum on the republic question
Called an immediate cabinet reshuffle before any travel
Delivered a first address to the full Australian Parliament
Flew to Tokyo to attend the Quad Leaders' Summit

evt-05-23-2022-anthony-albanese.butterflyEffect: He flew directly to Tokyo to join the Quad Leaders' Summit alongside the US, Japan, and India, signalling continuity in Australia's Indo-Pacific alliances despite the change of government. The swift trip reassured partners that AUKUS and regional security commitments would continue under Labor.

evt-05-24-1567-erik-xiv.scenario: It is 24 May 1567 in the dungeon of Uppsala Castle. King Erik XIV, convinced the imprisoned Sture family and other nobles are plotting against him, stands before them with a dagger drawn.
evt-05-24-1567-erik-xiv.prompt: What does Erik XIV do next?

choices.text: He stabs one prisoner himself while his guards kill four others
He pardons them publicly to calm rumors of a plot
He orders them exiled from Sweden instead of executed
He has the nobles quietly released after they swear new oaths of loyalty

evt-05-24-1567-erik-xiv.butterflyEffect: Erik personally stabbed Nils Svantesson Sture while his guards killed four other imprisoned nobles, an act that came to be remembered as the Sture Murders. The killings deepened widespread belief in the king's madness and eroded noble support for him, feeding directly into the rebellion led by his half-brother John that deposed him the following year.

evt-05-24-1667-louis-xiv.scenario: You are a French officer riding beside Louis XIV in May 1667 as his army crosses into the Spanish Netherlands. The King claims the territory belongs to his wife, Maria Theresa, under a supposed local inheritance custom rather than by outright conquest.
evt-05-24-1667-louis-xiv.prompt: What legal pretext does Louis use to justify the invasion?

choices.text: The 'law of devolution', claiming Maria Theresa's inheritance rights over an unpaid dowry
A direct declaration that France is annexing the land by right of conquest
A treaty ceding the provinces from the Dutch Republic
An appeal to the Holy Roman Emperor for the territory

evt-05-24-1667-louis-xiv.butterflyEffect: The invasion launched the War of Devolution, ending in the 1668 Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle with French gains in Flanders. It alarmed the Dutch Republic enough to form the Triple Alliance with England and Sweden, provoking Louis's larger war against the Dutch in 1672.

evt-05-24-1683-university-of-oxford.scenario: It is 24 May 1683, and Oxford dignitaries gather in a new purpose-built building to open an institution housing Elias Ashmole's donated collection of curiosities, alongside John Tradescant's famous cabinet.
evt-05-24-1683-university-of-oxford.prompt: What makes this new Oxford institution unlike anything Britain had seen before?

choices.text: It is the first museum in Britain to charge a mandatory entry fee
It is the first purpose-built museum open to the public and tied to university teaching
It is the first museum dedicated solely to natural history specimens
It is the first museum built with its own attached library and chapel

evt-05-24-1683-university-of-oxford.butterflyEffect: The Ashmolean became the world's first purpose-built museum attached to a university, open to the public and used for teaching. It set the template later followed by institutions like the British Museum, founded seventy years afterward, and helped establish museums as centres of research rather than mere private cabinets of curiosities.

evt-05-24-1689-toleration-act-1688.scenario: You sit in the English Parliament in May 1689, months after William and Mary took the throne in the Glorious Revolution. A bill before you would let Protestant dissenters worship outside the Church of England.
evt-05-24-1689-toleration-act-1688.prompt: What does the Toleration Act actually grant?

choices.text: Abolition of the Church of England as the established church
Toleration extended specifically to Roman Catholics
Freedom of worship for Trinitarian Protestant nonconformists, excluding Catholics and Unitarians
Full religious equality for every faith in England

evt-05-24-1689-toleration-act-1688.butterflyEffect: The Act let nonconformists such as Baptists and Quakers worship openly, though they still faced civil disabilities and Catholics remained excluded. It became a foundation stone for religious pluralism in Britain, though full Catholic emancipation had to wait until 1829.

evt-05-24-1738-moravian-church.scenario: It's the evening of 24 May 1738. As an Anglican priest wracked with doubt about your own salvation, you sit in a small room on Aldersgate Street, London, listening to someone read aloud from Luther's preface to the Epistle to the Romans.
evt-05-24-1738-moravian-church.prompt: What happens to you in this moment that reshapes your ministry forever?

choices.text: A sudden conviction that faith alone brings salvation, feeling his heart "strangely warmed"
A decision to abandon Christianity for Deism
A vision commanding him to sail immediately for the American colonies
A resolve to resign his Anglican ordination that very night

evt-05-24-1738-moravian-church.butterflyEffect: Wesley described his heart as "strangely warmed" and felt assured of salvation through faith alone. This Aldersgate experience became the spiritual turning point that launched the Methodist revival, eventually giving rise to a worldwide Methodist Church.

evt-05-24-1798-irish-rebellion-of-1798.scenario: It is late May 1798 in County Kildare. You are a United Irishman whose Dublin leaders have just been arrested and the planned coordinated uprising exposed before it could begin.
evt-05-24-1798-irish-rebellion-of-1798.prompt: What do the Kildare United Irishmen do now that the wider plan has collapsed?

choices.text: Rise up locally with pikes despite losing their Dublin leadership
Abandon the rebellion entirely and disperse quietly
Wait several months for French troops to land before acting
Surrender to the authorities in exchange for pardons

evt-05-24-1798-irish-rebellion-of-1798.butterflyEffect: Despite the betrayal of the Dublin plan, rebels in Kildare and elsewhere rose anyway, seizing towns with pikes and pitchforks. The rebellion spread but was crushed within weeks, and French reinforcements arrived too late in August; the failed uprising directly hastened the 1800 Act of Union abolishing the Irish Parliament.

evt-05-24-1830-nursery-rhyme.scenario: You are Sarah Josepha Hale, compiling a book of verse for children in Boston in 1830. A simple poem about a schoolgirl's pet lamb following her to class lands on your desk.
evt-05-24-1830-nursery-rhyme.prompt: What do you decide to do with the poem?

choices.text: Reject it as too trivial for serious literature
Credit it entirely to a schoolboy who supposedly wrote extra verses
Publish it in your collection, Poems for Our Children
Set it aside until it can be turned into a hymn

evt-05-24-1830-nursery-rhyme.butterflyEffect: Hale's decision preserved what became one of the most famous rhymes in the English language. Decades later, in 1877, its opening lines were reportedly the first words Thomas Edison recorded on his phonograph, carrying the nursery rhyme into the age of recorded sound.

evt-05-24-1883-brooklyn-bridge.scenario: It is 24 May 1883, opening day for the new Brooklyn Bridge, and the chief engineer Washington Roebling is too ill from caisson disease to attend the ceremony he spent fourteen years overseeing.
evt-05-24-1883-brooklyn-bridge.prompt: Who leads the ceremonial first crossing in his place?

choices.text: His wife, Emily Warren Roebling, who had helped manage construction
The bridge's chief construction foreman
President Chester Arthur, standing in as guest of honor
His son, who had trained as his assistant engineer

evt-05-24-1883-brooklyn-bridge.butterflyEffect: Emily Warren Roebling, his wife, made the first crossing carrying a rooster as a symbol of victory. She had effectively managed construction during her husband's illness, learning engineering and mathematics to do so, and is now remembered as one of the earliest women to lead a major engineering project.

evt-05-24-1913-princess-victoria-louise-.scenario: You attend the wedding of Princess Victoria Louise of Prussia to Prince Ernest Augustus of Hanover in Berlin, May 1913. Kaiser Wilhelm II beams beside Tsar Nicholas II and King George V, three royal cousins gathered under one roof.
evt-05-24-1913-princess-victoria-louise-.prompt: What makes this royal gathering historically significant in hindsight?

choices.text: It ends the Prussian-Hanoverian succession dispute through abdication
It is the last time Europe's reigning monarchs meet together before the First World War
It seals a permanent Anglo-German military alliance
It marks the founding of the League of Nations

evt-05-24-1913-princess-victoria-louise-.butterflyEffect: Fourteen months later these same cousins stood on opposing sides of the First World War. The marriage did reconcile the House of Hohenzollern with the deposed House of Hanover, annexed by Prussia in 1866, but could not prevent Europe's dynastic order from collapsing.

evt-05-24-1930-amy-johnson.scenario: It's 24 May 1930, and you have just guided your green Gipsy Moth biplane, Jason, down through the shimmering heat above Darwin, Australia, after nineteen days of flying solo from Croydon, England.
evt-05-24-1930-amy-johnson.prompt: What historic first have you just achieved by landing safely?

choices.text: First woman to fly solo across the Atlantic
First person to fly nonstop around the world
First woman to circumnavigate the globe by air
First woman to fly solo from England to Australia

evt-05-24-1930-amy-johnson.butterflyEffect: Amy Johnson became the first woman to fly solo from England to Australia, an instant international celebrity whose feat proved women could master long-distance aviation. She inspired a generation of female pilots before dying in 1941 while flying for the Air Transport Auxiliary in the Second World War.

evt-05-24-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It is dawn on 24 May 1941 in the Denmark Strait. You serve in the Royal Navy's Home Fleet as word arrives that the battlecruiser HMS Hood has just been destroyed by the German battleship Bismarck.
evt-05-24-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: What does the Royal Navy do next in response to the loss of Hood?

choices.text: Negotiate a temporary naval truce with Germany
Withdraw the Home Fleet to port to avoid further losses
Rely solely on submarines to track Bismarck from a distance
Launch every available warship in a fleet-wide hunt to sink Bismarck

evt-05-24-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Churchill ordered every available ship to hunt down Bismarck. Three days later, after a torpedo strike crippled her steering, British battleships sank her in the North Atlantic, ending Germany's use of surface raiders and shifting naval power decisively toward aircraft carriers.

evt-05-24-1948-1948-arab-israeli-war.scenario: It is late May 1948, days after Israel's declaration of independence. You serve as a liaison officer for the Arab League's war effort, watching Egyptian, Syrian, Jordanian, Iraqi and Lebanese forces advance along separate fronts into the former Mandate territory.
evt-05-24-1948-1948-arab-israeli-war.prompt: What glaring weakness threatens to undermine the Arab coalition's campaign?

choices.text: The armies lack a unified command and coordinate poorly with one another
Superior air power decisively favors the Arab side
Britain openly commits troops to fight alongside Egypt
The Soviet Union arms the invading Arab armies

evt-05-24-1948-1948-arab-israeli-war.butterflyEffect: The fragmented Arab command let Israeli forces defeat each front in turn. By the 1949 Armistice Agreements the Green Line was drawn, cementing Israeli statehood while roughly 700,000 Palestinians were displaced, a rift still shaping the region today.

evt-05-24-1956-eurovision-song-contest-1.scenario: It's the evening of 24 May 1956 in Lugano, and you are Lys Assia, about to perform 'Refrain', one of two songs Switzerland has entered in the very first Eurovision Song Contest — the only year any country was allowed two entries.
evt-05-24-1956-eurovision-song-contest-1.prompt: What happens when the votes are counted?

choices.text: You place second to the Netherlands' entry
The contest ends in an unresolved tie
You are disqualified for entering two songs
You win the inaugural contest for the host nation

evt-05-24-1956-eurovision-song-contest-1.butterflyEffect: Switzerland's win made Lugano the birthplace of Eurovision. The two-song rule was dropped the very next year and never repeated, and the contest grew into the world's longest-running annual TV music competition, still watched by hundreds of millions each May.

evt-05-24-1962-project-mercury.scenario: You are astronaut Scott Carpenter aboard Aurora 7 on 24 May 1962, nearing the end of your third orbit, when you notice your automatic attitude control system is behaving erratically and burning too much fuel.
evt-05-24-1962-project-mercury.prompt: What do you decide to do to bring yourself home?

choices.text: Prepare to eject and abandon the capsule immediately
Radio mission control and request an additional orbit to conserve fuel
Switch to manual control and fire the retro-rockets yourself
Trust the automatic system to correct itself before re-entry

evt-05-24-1962-project-mercury.butterflyEffect: Carpenter switched to manual control but fired his retro-rockets several seconds late and at a slightly wrong angle, causing Aurora 7 to overshoot its splashdown point by about 250 miles. The tense hours before recovery ships located him shook NASA's confidence in him, and he never flew in space again, later moving to the Navy's SEALAB program instead.

evt-05-24-1963-robert-f-kennedy.scenario: It is 24 May 1963 in a New York apartment. You are James Baldwin, having gathered Black writers and activists, including young CORE organizer Jerome Smith, to confront Attorney General Robert Kennedy about the government's civil rights failures.
evt-05-24-1963-robert-f-kennedy.prompt: What happens when Smith describes being beaten for his activism and Kennedy responds?

choices.text: The group reaches full agreement on next steps
Kennedy becomes defensive and the meeting turns hostile
Kennedy immediately pledges new civil rights legislation on the spot
Kennedy asks Baldwin to end the meeting early out of respect

evt-05-24-1963-robert-f-kennedy.butterflyEffect: Kennedy grew visibly defensive and the meeting collapsed into bitter confrontation, widely reported as a political failure. Yet the encounter is credited with sharpening Kennedy's grasp of Black Americans' anger, feeding into the administration's more forceful civil rights push that summer, including President Kennedy's June 1963 civil rights address.

evt-05-24-1991-israel-defense-forces.scenario: It is 24 May 1991. You are an Israeli defense official as Ethiopia's government collapses and thousands of Ethiopian Jews wait in Addis Ababa, cut off as rebel forces close in on the capital.
evt-05-24-1991-israel-defense-forces.prompt: What does Israel decide to do to get them out before the city falls?

choices.text: Charter a covert nonstop airlift using stripped-down jets
Request the United Nations organize a phased evacuation
Send naval ships to evacuate them by sea
Process visas gradually through normal immigration channels

evt-05-24-1991-israel-defense-forces.butterflyEffect: Israel launched Operation Solomon, stripping seats from El Al jets and flying 34 aircraft nonstop over 36 hours to airlift more than 14,000 Ethiopian Jews to safety, one of the largest and fastest airlifts in history, completed just as the Ethiopian capital fell to rebels.

evt-05-24-2014-islamic-extremism.scenario: It is early afternoon on 24 May 2014, and you are working the front desk of the Jewish Museum of Belgium in Brussels when a man carrying a hidden holdall walks in and pulls out a rifle without warning.
evt-05-24-2014-islamic-extremism.prompt: What happens to the gunman in the days after the attack?

choices.text: He turns out to be an unaffiliated lone domestic extremist
He is arrested at the scene and confesses to a neo-Nazi motive
He is caught in France days later, revealed to have fought with jihadists in Syria
He escapes to Syria and is never identified

evt-05-24-2014-islamic-extremism.butterflyEffect: Mehdi Nemmouche, who had killed four people, was arrested six days later in Marseille carrying weapons and a GoPro recording. He had recently fought with jihadist groups in Syria, making this the first attack in Europe by a returning European foreign fighter and a major alarm bell for European security services.

evt-05-24-2019-brexit.scenario: It's 24 May 2019, and outside 10 Downing Street you stand before the cameras, your voice breaking, having failed three times to get Parliament to approve your Brexit withdrawal agreement.
evt-05-24-2019-brexit.prompt: What do you announce to the nation?

choices.text: The calling of a snap general election
A second referendum on EU membership
Her resignation as party leader and, in time, as Prime Minister
An immediate no-deal Brexit

evt-05-24-2019-brexit.butterflyEffect: Theresa May announced her resignation as leader of the Conservative Party, triggering a leadership contest won by Boris Johnson. Johnson took a harder line on Brexit and led the UK out of the EU on 31 January 2020.

evt-05-24-2022-uvalde-school-shooting.scenario: In the aftermath of the shooting at Robb Elementary School, investigators examine the more than 70 minutes officers waited in the hallway before confronting the gunman.
evt-05-24-2022-uvalde-school-shooting.prompt: What did subsequent investigations conclude about the law enforcement response?

choices.text: Investigators found the response met all standard protocols
No formal investigation into the response was ever conducted
Officers violated protocol by waiting far too long to act
Reports concluded officers entered within the first two minutes

evt-05-24-2022-uvalde-school-shooting.butterflyEffect: A Texas House investigative report and a Justice Department review found systemic failures, including officers waiting despite active gunfire and children's 911 calls from inside the classroom. The findings led to the police chief's removal, several resignations, and renewed national debate over active-shooter protocols and school safety funding.

evt-05-25-1644-transition-from-ming-to-q.scenario: It is 1644 at Shanhai Pass. Rebel armies under Li Zicheng have taken Beijing and the Ming emperor is dead, while a Manchu army waits beyond the Great Wall. As Ming general, you must decide whether to open the pass to the Manchu to help crush the rebels.
evt-05-25-1644-transition-from-ming-to-q.prompt: What did General Wu Sangui do at Shanhai Pass?

choices.text: He surrendered the pass directly to Li Zicheng's rebels
He abandoned his post and fled south of the Yangtze
He opened the pass and allied with the Manchu against the rebels
He sealed the pass and fought the Manchu alone

evt-05-25-1644-transition-from-ming-to-q.butterflyEffect: Wu Sangui allowed the Manchu forces through the pass, and their combined armies crushed Li Zicheng's rebels near Beijing. This opened the road for the Manchu to seize the capital and found the Qing dynasty, which would rule China for over two and a half centuries.

evt-05-25-1782-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 1782 on the Ohio frontier. You ride with Colonel William Crawford's volunteer force marching toward Sandusky, aiming to strike Native American towns allied with the British, uncertain whether the expedition can outrun the warriors gathering to meet them.
evt-05-25-1782-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What happened to Crawford's expedition against the Sandusky towns?

choices.text: The expedition destroyed the Sandusky towns and returned victorious
Crawford negotiated a peace treaty with the Native towns
British reinforcements forced Crawford to retreat without a battle
The expedition was defeated and Crawford was captured and killed

evt-05-25-1782-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Crawford's force was routed by Native American and British-allied fighters, and Crawford himself was captured and executed by torture, an event that shocked frontier settlers and hardened hatred toward Native peoples in the Ohio country. The disaster fed a cycle of frontier violence that continued well after the Revolutionary War's larger conflict ended.

evt-05-25-1787-constitutional-convention.scenario: It's 25 May 1787, and you arrive in Philadelphia as a delegate, ostensibly sent to revise the weak Articles of Confederation that leave Congress unable to tax or raise an army.
evt-05-25-1787-constitutional-convention.prompt: What do delegates like Madison and Hamilton push the convention to do instead of simply amending the Articles?

choices.text: Invite a foreign monarch to rule over the states
Dissolve the union into separate regional confederacies
Simply grant Congress the power to levy taxes
Draft an entirely new frame of government

evt-05-25-1787-constitutional-convention.butterflyEffect: Rather than patch the Articles of Confederation, the delegates drafted an entirely new Constitution creating a stronger federal government with three branches. Ratified over the following year, it became the founding legal framework of the United States and a model studied by constitution-writers worldwide.

evt-05-25-1810-primera-junta.scenario: It is 25 May 1810 in Buenos Aires. The Spanish viceroy has been forced out amid the chaos of Napoleon's invasion of Spain, and the cabildo must decide who will govern the Río de la Plata in the king's absence.
evt-05-25-1810-primera-junta.prompt: Who is chosen to lead the new Primera Junta?

choices.text: Manuel Belgrano
Mariano Moreno
Cornelio Saavedra
Juan José Castelli

evt-05-25-1810-primera-junta.butterflyEffect: Cornelio Saavedra was named president of the Primera Junta, the first self-governing body of what would become Argentina. Though it claimed loyalty to the deposed Spanish king, the Junta set in motion a process of revolution and infighting that led to full Argentine independence in 1816.

evt-05-25-1816-kubla-khan.scenario: It is 1797, and Samuel Taylor Coleridge wakes from an opium-tinged dream inspired by a book about Kublai Khan's Xanadu, with vivid lines of poetry filling his mind. He begins writing them down furiously, determined to capture a vision meant to span hundreds of lines.
evt-05-25-1816-kubla-khan.prompt: What interrupted Coleridge's composition of Kubla Khan and left it unfinished?

choices.text: His publisher demanded he shorten the poem immediately
A fire broke out in his cottage and forced him outside
A person arriving on business from Porlock interrupted him
He fell back asleep before finishing the lines

evt-05-25-1816-kubla-khan.butterflyEffect: A visitor arriving on business from the nearby village of Porlock broke Coleridge's concentration, and by the time he returned to his desk the rest of the dream-vision had faded from memory. The poem remained an unfinished fragment for nearly twenty years until Lord Byron urged its publication in 1816, and it became one of the most famous incomplete works in English literature.

evt-05-25-1878-gilbert-and-sullivan.scenario: It is opening night, 25 May 1878, at London's Opera Comique, and W.S. Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan watch nervously as H.M.S. Pinafore has its premiere before a London audience.
evt-05-25-1878-gilbert-and-sullivan.prompt: What problem does the opera's runaway success create for its creators soon after?

choices.text: Unauthorised American productions of the opera pirate it without payment
The Lord Chamberlain bans the opera from further performance
The Savoy Theatre is forced to close due to low ticket sales
Sullivan refuses to work with Gilbert again

evt-05-25-1878-gilbert-and-sullivan.butterflyEffect: Pinafore became a smash hit, but because American copyright law did not protect British works, unauthorised 'pirated' productions sprang up across the United States without paying royalties. To protect their next opera, Gilbert and Sullivan staged the world premiere of The Pirates of Penzance in New York in 1879, simultaneously with London, to secure US copyright.

evt-05-25-1895-oscar-wilde.scenario: You are in the Old Bailey courtroom on 25 May 1895 as Justice Alfred Wills prepares to pass sentence on Oscar Wilde, convicted of gross indecency after a sensational trial that has scandalised London society.

choices.text: Two years of hard labour
Life imprisonment
A fine and immediate release
Deportation from Britain

evt-05-25-1895-oscar-wilde.butterflyEffect: Wilde was sentenced to two years' hard labour, which broke his health and finances. On his release in 1897 he wrote 'The Ballad of Reading Gaol' and left for exile in France, where he died in poverty in 1900, his reputation only later restored as one of the great figures of English letters.

evt-05-25-1936-remington-rand.scenario: You are a Remington Rand typewriter worker in 1936, walking a picket line as the company brings in replacement workers and armed guards to keep the plants running.
evt-05-25-1936-remington-rand.prompt: What tactic did company president James Rand Jr. use to try to break the strike?

choices.text: He shut down the company permanently rather than negotiate
He organized armed 'Citizens Committees' to intimidate strikers and reopen the plants
He immediately agreed to recognize the union and raise wages
He appealed directly to President Roosevelt to end the strike by executive order

evt-05-25-1936-remington-rand.butterflyEffect: Rand's company organized local vigilante "Citizens Committees" and armed guards to intimidate strikers and reopen plants, a strategy that became known as the "Mohawk Valley formula." The National Labor Relations Board later condemned it as a blueprint for union-busting, and its exposure helped shape future federal labor protections.

evt-05-25-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 25 May 1940 on the Channel coast. German panzer divisions have encircled the Allied forces racing to the sea, and the port of Boulogne-sur-Mer is under assault as British and French troops try to hold the line.
evt-05-25-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: What does the fall of Boulogne contribute to in the days that follow?

choices.text: The German invasion of Britain later that summer
The successful Allied breakout toward Paris
The surrender of the entire French army
The encirclement that leads directly to the Dunkirk evacuation

evt-05-25-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Boulogne fell to German forces on 25 May, one of several Channel ports lost as the Allied armies were pushed back toward the coast. Its capture, alongside Calais, helped seal the pocket around Dunkirk, from which over 300,000 Allied troops would be evacuated in the following days.

evt-05-25-1944-wehrmacht.scenario: Dawn breaks over Drvar in occupied Yugoslavia on 25 May 1944. German paratroopers are landing right outside the cave complex serving as Marshal Tito's partisan headquarters, and you are one of the guards responsible for getting him out alive.
evt-05-25-1944-wehrmacht.prompt: How do the partisans save Tito from the German airborne assault?

choices.text: Radio for immediate Allied air support to strafe the German positions
Barricade the cave entrance and fight the paratroopers head-on
Surrender headquarters staff to negotiate safe passage for Tito
Slip Tito out through a hidden mountain route away from the landing zones

evt-05-25-1944-wehrmacht.butterflyEffect: Tito escaped through a mountain gorge near Drvar as his headquarters was overrun, narrowly avoiding capture in Operation Rösselsprung (Knight's Move). His survival kept the Yugoslav Partisan movement intact, and Tito went on to lead a communist Yugoslavia after the war, one that would later break independently from Stalin's Soviet bloc.

evt-05-25-1955-joe-brown-climber.scenario: You are Joe Brown, roped to George Band, just feet below the summit of Kangchenjunga on 25 May 1955. The Maharaja of Sikkim had asked the expedition to leave the very top of the sacred mountain untouched.
evt-05-25-1955-joe-brown-climber.prompt: What do you do as you near the top of the world's third-highest peak?

choices.text: Wait for the rest of the expedition before going any further
Stop short of the actual summit out of respect for Sikkimese belief
Turn back immediately without reaching the top at all
Climb the final few feet to stand on the true summit

evt-05-25-1955-joe-brown-climber.butterflyEffect: Brown and Band stopped a few feet short of the true summit, honouring the promise made to Sikkim, and every subsequent British ascent of Kangchenjunga has followed the same tradition. The climb made Brown, a working-class Mancunian, one of the most celebrated mountaineers of his era, helping to reshape British climbing away from its upper-class amateur roots.

evt-05-25-1961-joint-session-of-the-unit.scenario: You sit in the gallery of a joint session of Congress on May 25, 1961, as President Kennedy rises to deliver a special message on urgent national needs during the tense early Cold War.
evt-05-25-1961-joint-session-of-the-unit.prompt: What ambitious goal did Kennedy announce to Congress that day?

choices.text: Building a permanent space station in orbit
Landing an American on the Moon before the end of the decade
Sending an unmanned probe to Mars within five years
Establishing a joint US-Soviet space program

evt-05-25-1961-joint-session-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: Kennedy committed the United States to landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to Earth before the decade was out, dramatically escalating the space race with the Soviet Union. The pledge redirected massive federal funding and talent into NASA, culminating in the Apollo 11 landing in July 1969.

evt-05-25-1961-bukit-ho-swee-fire.scenario: It is late afternoon on 25 May 1961. Smoke is rising over the crowded wooden squatter huts of Bukit Ho Swee, and thousands of families are fleeing with whatever they can carry as flames spread through the tightly packed settlement.
evt-05-25-1961-bukit-ho-swee-fire.prompt: What did the Singapore government do for the thousands left homeless by the fire?

choices.text: Deport displaced residents to Malaysia for resettlement
Leave residents to rebuild their own squatter huts on the same site
Rehouse survivors quickly in newly built high-rise public housing flats
Relocate all survivors permanently to rural farmland outside the city

evt-05-25-1961-bukit-ho-swee-fire.butterflyEffect: The fire destroyed over 2,800 homes and left about 16,000 people homeless, but the government responded with rapid emergency housing and accelerated public housing construction. The Housing and Development Board built new flats on the cleared site within months, and the disaster became a turning point that pushed forward Singapore's large-scale public housing program.

evt-05-25-1962-baltimore-steam-packet-co.scenario: You book passage on the Old Bay Line's overnight steamer from Baltimore to Norfolk in the spring of 1962, one of the last chances to sail this route after 122 years of continuous service.
evt-05-25-1962-baltimore-steam-packet-co.prompt: Why was the Baltimore Steam Packet Company forced to end its overnight steamboat service?

choices.text: A shipping accident destroyed its entire fleet
A labor strike shut down the company permanently
Highway and bridge competition drew away its passengers and freight
The federal government banned overnight steamship travel

evt-05-25-1962-baltimore-steam-packet-co.butterflyEffect: Rising competition from highways, bridges, and faster automobile and truck travel across the Chesapeake Bay had steadily drained the steamer line's passenger and freight business. Its closure in 1962 ended the last overnight steamship passenger service in the United States, marking the final chapter of a transportation era replaced by road and air travel.

evt-05-25-1967-kapsan-faction-incident.scenario: You are a senior North Korean official in 1967, watching as veteran comrades who once fought beside Kim Il Sung against Japan are suddenly denounced for pushing economic reform and questioning his growing cult of personality.
evt-05-25-1967-kapsan-faction-incident.prompt: What was the outcome for the Kapsan faction after their reform push failed?

choices.text: They defected en masse to South Korea
They successfully replaced Kim Il Sung as leader
They were purged from the party and removed from power
They were promoted and given greater authority over reforms

evt-05-25-1967-kapsan-faction-incident.butterflyEffect: Kim Il Sung purged the Kapsan faction, removing figures like Pak Kum-chol from power and eliminating the last organized internal challenge to his authority. The purge cleared the way for an even more absolute cult of personality and hereditary succession planning that would define North Korea's leadership for decades.

evt-05-25-1979-disappearance-of-etan-pat.scenario: It is the morning of 25 May 1979 in SoHo, New York. Six-year-old Etan Patz has begged to walk the two blocks to his school bus stop alone for the first time, and you are his parent deciding whether to let him go.
evt-05-25-1979-disappearance-of-etan-pat.prompt: What follows this ordinary morning that changes how America searches for missing children?

choices.text: It becomes a template for new legislation and search techniques for missing children
It has little lasting effect on child safety policy
It results in an immediate arrest and swift trial within the same year
It leads directly to the creation of the Amber Alert system

evt-05-25-1979-disappearance-of-etan-pat.butterflyEffect: Etan never arrived at school, and his case became a landmark in the missing children movement, prompting new laws, national databases, and the 1980s 'photo on a milk carton' campaigns. In 1983 President Reagan named May 25 National Missing Children's Day, and the case remained unresolved for decades until a 2012 confession led to a conviction years later.

evt-05-25-1979-o-hare-international-airp.scenario: It is May 25, 1979, and you are a ground engineer watching American Airlines Flight 191 begin its takeoff roll from O'Hare, unaware that a shortcut maintenance procedure has left the left engine dangerously weakened.
evt-05-25-1979-o-hare-international-airp.prompt: What happened moments after the DC-10 lifted off the runway?

choices.text: The plane suffered a bird strike but landed safely
An engine and its pylon tore away from the wing, causing the plane to crash
A cargo door blew open, forcing an emergency landing
The crew aborted takeoff after a tire blowout

evt-05-25-1979-o-hare-international-airp.butterflyEffect: The left engine and pylon separated from the wing during takeoff, severing hydraulic lines and causing the aircraft to roll and crash, killing all 271 aboard and two on the ground. Investigators traced the failure to a maintenance shortcut for removing the engine, prompting the FAA to ground all DC-10s in the U.S. and overhaul airline maintenance oversight.

evt-05-25-2009-2009-north-korean-nuclear.scenario: It is 25 May 2009. Seismic monitors around the world detect an underground blast in North Korea, its second nuclear test in under three years, followed swiftly by a string of missile launches.
evt-05-25-2009-2009-north-korean-nuclear.prompt: How did the international community respond to this second North Korean nuclear test?

choices.text: The Security Council took no formal action due to a veto deadlock
The United States immediately launched military strikes against North Korea
South Korea unilaterally invaded North Korea in retaliation
The UN Security Council passed a resolution imposing tighter sanctions

evt-05-25-2009-2009-north-korean-nuclear.butterflyEffect: The UN Security Council swiftly condemned the test and passed Resolution 1874, tightening sanctions and authorizing inspections of North Korean cargo suspected of carrying weapons materials. The test deepened North Korea's isolation and hardened the diplomatic standoff over its nuclear program for years afterward.

evt-05-25-2011-the-oprah-winfrey-show.scenario: You have a ticket to the taping of the final episode of The Oprah Winfrey Show at Chicago's United Center in May 2011, packed with thousands of fans after twenty-five years on the air.
evt-05-25-2011-the-oprah-winfrey-show.prompt: What did Oprah Winfrey do in the months just after ending her syndicated talk show?

choices.text: She sold the show's rights and stepped away from television production
She retired from all media work entirely
She launched and focused on building her own cable network, OWN
She became a nightly news anchor for a major network

evt-05-25-2011-the-oprah-winfrey-show.butterflyEffect: Winfrey shifted her energy into OWN, the Oprah Winfrey Network, a cable channel she had launched in January 2011 to extend her media brand beyond syndicated television. The finale closed out the highest-rated daytime talk show in U.S. history and marked Winfrey's transition from broadcast host to media mogul running her own network.

evt-05-25-2012-spacex-cots-demo-flight-2.scenario: It is 25 May 2012. You watch from mission control as SpaceX's uncrewed Dragon capsule closes in on the International Space Station, attempting something no private company has ever done before.
evt-05-25-2012-spacex-cots-demo-flight-2.prompt: What milestone did SpaceX's Dragon achieve on this mission?

choices.text: It became the first spacecraft to land astronauts on the ISS
It became the first commercial spacecraft to berth with the ISS
It became the first reusable rocket to return to Earth intact
It became the first spacecraft to orbit the Moon and return

evt-05-25-2012-spacex-cots-demo-flight-2.butterflyEffect: Dragon became the first commercial spacecraft to rendezvous and berth with the ISS, proving private companies could deliver cargo to orbit. The success validated NASA's Commercial Orbital Transportation Services program and paved the way for regular SpaceX cargo runs and, later, crewed commercial missions to the station.

evt-05-25-2020-george-floyd-protests.scenario: It's late May 2020, and video of George Floyd's arrest in Minneapolis has just gone viral, showing an officer kneeling on his neck for over nine minutes while bystanders pleaded for his release.
evt-05-25-2020-george-floyd-protests.prompt: What followed in the weeks after this footage spread across the world?

choices.text: Congress passed sweeping police reform legislation within a month
The officers involved were acquitted within days
The Minneapolis police department was immediately disbanded
Mass protests against police brutality spread to over 2,000 cities worldwide

evt-05-25-2020-george-floyd-protests.butterflyEffect: The footage sparked the largest protest movement in US history, reviving the Black Lives Matter movement across more than 60 countries. It also led to Derek Chauvin's 2021 conviction for murder, though many of the broader policing reforms activists sought stalled in Congress.

evt-05-26-946-edmund-i.scenario: It's 26 May 946, and you are King Edmund I, feasting at your royal hall in Pucklechurch, when you spot the outlaw Leofa, a man you once banished, sitting among your guests.
evt-05-26-946-edmund-i.prompt: What does the king do when he confronts the exiled outlaw?

choices.text: He orders guards to quietly escort the man out without incident
He has the man arrested and imprisoned for trial the next day
He pardons Leofa on the spot to avoid conflict
He grabs Leofa himself and is fatally stabbed in the struggle

evt-05-26-946-edmund-i.butterflyEffect: Edmund's impulsive act cost him his life, ending his seven-year reign at around age 25. His young sons Eadwig and Edgar were too small to rule, so the throne passed to Edmund's brother Eadred, and only later to Edmund's own sons, reshaping the West Saxon succession for a generation.

evt-05-26-1822-grue-church-fire.scenario: You are a parishioner packed into Grue Church for the Pentecost service of May 26, 1822, when smoke begins curling near the crowded entrance and panic spreads through the pews.
evt-05-26-1822-grue-church-fire.prompt: What lasting change did this disaster prompt for churches across Norway?

choices.text: The abolition of Pentecost services in rural parishes
New rules requiring safer, more numerous church exits
A nationwide ban on holding indoor religious services
The replacement of all wooden churches with stone ones within a year

evt-05-26-1822-grue-church-fire.butterflyEffect: At least 113 worshippers died, making it Norway's deadliest fire. The catastrophe pushed Norwegian authorities to tighten regulations on church construction, including requirements for wider, outward-opening exits to prevent crowds from being trapped in future fires.

evt-05-26-1865-american-civil-war.scenario: You serve under General Edmund Kirby Smith with the Confederacy's Trans-Mississippi army in late May 1865, having heard that Lee and Johnston have already surrendered their forces in the east.
evt-05-26-1865-american-civil-war.prompt: What did Kirby Smith do with his remaining army west of the Mississippi?

choices.text: He negotiated the surrender of his army, ending major Confederate resistance
He led his troops into Mexico to continue the fight from exile
He ordered his men to disperse and wage guerrilla warfare indefinitely
He merged his forces with allied tribal nations to keep fighting

evt-05-26-1865-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Kirby Smith negotiated his army's surrender on May 26, 1865, formalized on June 2, effectively ending organized Confederate resistance and closing the war's last major theater. His capitulation cleared the way for Reconstruction to begin in earnest across the former Confederacy.

evt-05-26-1868-impeachment-trial-of-andr.scenario: It is May 16, 1868, and you are a U.S. Senator seated in the chamber. President Andrew Johnson's fate hangs on your vote for conviction or acquittal on the eleventh article of impeachment, and the outcome is razor-thin.
evt-05-26-1868-impeachment-trial-of-andr.prompt: What actually happened when the Senate voted on the impeachment articles against Johnson?

choices.text: The Senate acquitted Johnson, falling one vote short of the two-thirds needed to convict
The House withdrew all articles before a Senate vote could be taken
The trial ended in a mistrial and Johnson resigned voluntarily
The Senate convicted Johnson by exactly two-thirds and removed him from office

evt-05-26-1868-impeachment-trial-of-andr.butterflyEffect: The Senate fell one vote short of the two-thirds needed to convict, with seven Republicans, including Edmund Ross of Kansas, joining Democrats to acquit. Johnson finished his term, and the near-miss set a lasting precedent that impeachment required overwhelming, bipartisan proof of wrongdoing, shaping how Congress approached later presidential impeachments.

evt-05-26-1888-the-diary-of-a-nobody.scenario: You are a Punch magazine subscriber in 1888, chuckling over a new intermittent serial narrated by a fussy London clerk who records his household's small triumphs and humiliations in diary form.
evt-05-26-1888-the-diary-of-a-nobody.prompt: What was this serial that later became a classic English comic novel?

choices.text: The Diary of a Nobody by George and Weedon Grossmith
The Wrong Box by Robert Louis Stevenson
Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K. Jerome
Vice Versa by F. Anstey

evt-05-26-1888-the-diary-of-a-nobody.butterflyEffect: The sketches, by brothers George and Weedon Grossmith, were collected and expanded into The Diary of a Nobody in 1892. Its portrait of the suburban clerk Charles Pooter became a byword for gentle social comedy and shaped a lasting British tradition of diary-format satire.

evt-05-26-1894-emanuel-lasker.scenario: It is 1894 and you are following the world chess championship match between the aging titleholder Wilhelm Steinitz and the young challenger Emanuel Lasker, whose sharp, modern style has stunned spectators.
evt-05-26-1894-emanuel-lasker.prompt: What was the outcome of the Steinitz–Lasker championship match?

choices.text: Steinitz withdrew before the match concluded, forfeiting the title
Lasker defeated Steinitz and became the new world champion
Steinitz retained his title after a narrow victory
The match was declared a draw and the title stayed vacant

evt-05-26-1894-emanuel-lasker.butterflyEffect: Lasker won decisively, dethroning Steinitz to become the second World Chess Champion. He went on to hold the title for 27 years, the longest reign in chess history, and his blend of psychological insight and practical strategy influenced generations of players who followed.

evt-05-26-1932-donoghue-v-stevenson.scenario: It is 1932 and you sit as a Law Lord in the House of Lords, weighing whether May Donoghue, who fell ill after drinking ginger beer containing a decomposed snail, can sue the manufacturer she never bought the drink from directly.
evt-05-26-1932-donoghue-v-stevenson.prompt: What did the House of Lords decide about a manufacturer's duty to a consumer with no contract between them?

choices.text: They dismissed the case as outside the court's jurisdiction
They ruled a manufacturer owes a duty of care to the ultimate consumer, establishing the neighbour principle
They ruled only the cafe owner, not the manufacturer, could be liable
They ruled no duty existed because Donoghue had no contract with the manufacturer

evt-05-26-1932-donoghue-v-stevenson.butterflyEffect: The Lords ruled that manufacturers owe a duty of care to the ultimate consumer, even without a direct contract, under Lord Atkin's 'neighbour principle.' This decision became the cornerstone of modern negligence law across common law countries, letting people sue for harm caused by carelessness far beyond simple contract disputes.

evt-05-26-1933-jimmie-rodgers.scenario: You are a Victor Records engineer in early 1933, running the final recording sessions for Jimmie Rodgers, the blue yodeler whose hillbilly records have made him a national star, even as his health visibly fails.
evt-05-26-1933-jimmie-rodgers.prompt: What happened to Rodgers shortly after these final New York sessions?

choices.text: He was killed in an automobile accident driving home from the studio
He died of tuberculosis at the Taft Hotel in New York City
He retired to Texas and lived for several more decades
He died in a plane crash while touring the South

evt-05-26-1933-jimmie-rodgers.butterflyEffect: On May 26, 1933, Rodgers died of tuberculosis at the Taft Hotel in New York City, aged 35. His blend of blues, yodeling, and rural balladry became the foundation of commercial country music, later cited as a direct influence by Hank Williams, Elvis Presley, and countless others.

evt-05-26-1938-house-un-american-activit.scenario: It's 1938 in Washington, and Congress has just voted to create a new committee tasked with investigating alleged 'un-American' activities among citizens, officials, and organizations.
evt-05-26-1938-house-un-american-activit.prompt: What did this committee eventually become known for over the following decades?

choices.text: Overseeing federal immigration quotas and enforcement
Auditing federal tax compliance among corporations
Regulating wartime industrial production
Investigating alleged communist ties, including blacklisting Hollywood figures

evt-05-26-1938-house-un-american-activit.butterflyEffect: HUAC became a standing committee in 1946 and gained notoriety for the Hollywood blacklist and aggressive Cold War hearings targeting suspected communists in entertainment and government. Its tactics drew lasting criticism as an example of civil-liberties overreach. The committee was finally abolished in 1975, its functions absorbed into the House Judiciary Committee.

evt-05-26-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It's dawn on 26 May 1940, and you're a British soldier trapped on the beaches at Dunkirk as German forces close in from the south.
evt-05-26-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: What is your only real hope of escape?

choices.text: An airborne evacuation using RAF transport planes
A counterattack to break through German lines toward Paris
Evacuation by a hastily assembled fleet of naval and civilian boats
Surrendering en masse to secure prisoner-of-war treatment

evt-05-26-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Operation Dynamo evacuated roughly 338,000 Allied troops from Dunkirk over the following days, using Royal Navy destroyers alongside civilian pleasure boats and fishing craft. Though the army left behind nearly all its heavy equipment, the rescued men formed the core of Britain's future fighting force, and the mix of disaster and defiance gave rise to the enduring 'Dunkirk spirit' that bolstered morale through the Blitz.

evt-05-26-1967-the-beatles.scenario: It's spring 1967 at EMI's offices in London, and you're reviewing the elaborate cardboard-cutout collage Peter Blake has designed for the Beatles' new album cover, days before its 26 May release—among the dozens of faces is Mahatma Gandhi.
evt-05-26-1967-the-beatles.prompt: Facing concerns about offending audiences in India, what do you decide about Gandhi's image?

choices.text: Replace Gandhi with a portrait of Winston Churchill
Keep the image exactly as originally designed
Print two different covers for different markets
Remove Gandhi's image from the final artwork

evt-05-26-1967-the-beatles.butterflyEffect: EMI had Gandhi's image removed from the finished cover to avoid controversy in India, and the album was released as Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band. It became a landmark concept album that reshaped how the music industry approached artwork, studio production, and the album as an artistic statement.

evt-05-26-1989-tropical-storm-cecil.scenario: It's late May 1989, and Severe Tropical Storm Cecil is battering Quảng Nam province in central Vietnam with torrential rain after making landfall near Hội An.
evt-05-26-1989-tropical-storm-cecil.prompt: What was the biggest danger facing villages in the storm's path?

choices.text: Widespread wildfires sparked by lightning strikes
Catastrophic flash flooding from the storm's heavy rainfall
A storm surge sweeping inland along the coast
A secondary earthquake triggered by the storm

evt-05-26-1989-tropical-storm-cecil.butterflyEffect: Cecil's floods killed 751 people across central Vietnam, making it one of the deadliest tropical cyclones to strike the region in decades. The disaster exposed the vulnerability of low-lying river communities and pushed later Vietnamese government investment into flood-warning systems and river management along the central coast.

evt-05-26-1998-supreme-court-of-the-unit.scenario: It is 26 May 1998, and you are a lawyer for the state of New Jersey standing before the Supreme Court, arguing over who actually controls Ellis Island after a century-old boundary dispute with New York.
evt-05-26-1998-supreme-court-of-the-unit.prompt: What did the Supreme Court ultimately rule in New Jersey v. New York?

choices.text: The filled-in portions of the island belong to New Jersey, the original island to New York
The island is declared federal territory with no state jurisdiction
The entire island belongs to New York as it had always claimed
The dispute is dismissed and both states retain joint control indefinitely

evt-05-26-1998-supreme-court-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: The Court ruled that most of Ellis Island—the land created by 19th- and 20th-century landfill—belonged to New Jersey, while the original small island remained under New York's jurisdiction. The decision ended decades of wrangling over tax revenue and administrative control of the historic immigration site.

evt-05-26-2002-i-40-bridge-disaster.scenario: It's the morning of 26 May 2002, and you're driving toward the Interstate 40 bridge near Webbers Falls, Oklahoma, unaware that a towboat pushing barges has just struck one of the bridge's support piers on the Arkansas River below.
evt-05-26-2002-i-40-bridge-disaster.prompt: What happens to the bridge in the moments after the barges strike the pier?

choices.text: The bridge is closed for inspection but no structural failure occurs
The barges sink but the bridge itself is undamaged
The bridge sustains only minor cosmetic damage and stays open
A section of the bridge collapses into the river as vehicles are crossing

evt-05-26-2002-i-40-bridge-disaster.butterflyEffect: The damaged pier gave way and a large section of the bridge collapsed into the river, sending vehicles plunging into the water and killing 14 people. Investigators found the towboat's captain had lost consciousness, prompting tighter scrutiny of medical fitness and drug testing for inland waterway pilots and renewed attention to bridge pier protection nationwide.

evt-05-26-2020-george-floyd-protests.scenario: It's May 26, 2020, in Minneapolis. A video of George Floyd's death in police custody has just gone viral, and crowds are gathering outside the store where he was arrested.
evt-05-26-2020-george-floyd-protests.prompt: What happened to the officers involved in Floyd's arrest in the days that followed?

choices.text: They were fired, and Derek Chauvin was later arrested and convicted of murder
Only Chauvin was fired; the other three officers kept their jobs
The Minneapolis Police Department cleared them of any wrongdoing
They were placed on paid administrative leave with no further action

evt-05-26-2020-george-floyd-protests.butterflyEffect: Chauvin and three colleagues were fired within a day; Chauvin was arrested soon after and convicted in April 2021 of murder, later sentenced to 22½ years. The case ignited the largest protest movement in U.S. history and pushed several states toward new police-reform legislation.

evt-05-26-2021-2021-san-jose-shooting.scenario: You are a dispatcher fielding frantic calls on the morning of May 26, 2021, as reports come in of gunfire inside a Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority rail yard in San Jose.
evt-05-26-2021-2021-san-jose-shooting.prompt: What was the outcome once police units reached the rail yard that morning?

choices.text: Police secured the site as the gunman died by suicide before capture
Armed coworkers subdued the gunman before police arrived
Officers arrested the gunman without incident at the scene
The gunman escaped and was arrested days later out of state

evt-05-26-2021-2021-san-jose-shooting.butterflyEffect: The gunman, a VTA employee, killed nine coworkers before taking his own life as officers arrived. It became the deadliest mass shooting in Bay Area history and intensified debate in California over workplace violence prevention and firearm regulation.

evt-05-27-1096-rhineland-massacres.scenario: It is 27 May 1096 in Mainz. You lead a Jewish community sheltering in the archbishop's palace as a crusader mob gathers outside, demanding baptism or death.
evt-05-27-1096-rhineland-massacres.prompt: Facing forced conversion, what does the community's leadership decide?

choices.text: Choose martyrdom rather than forced conversion
Convert to Christianity to save the community
Attempt to flee the city under cover of night
Pay a ransom to the archbishop for continued protection

evt-05-27-1096-rhineland-massacres.butterflyEffect: Many chose death rather than forced baptism, an act later recorded in Hebrew chronicles as Kiddush HaShem, sanctification of the Name. The Mainz massacre became the deadliest of the 1096 Rhineland pogroms, and its memory shaped Ashkenazi Jewish liturgy and communal identity for centuries afterward.

evt-05-27-1153-malcolm-iv-of-scotland.scenario: It is 27 May 1153, and you are a Scottish earl watching twelve-year-old Malcolm crowned at Scone Abbey, days after the death of his grandfather King David I. Several powerful nobles doubt a boy can hold the throne.
evt-05-27-1153-malcolm-iv-of-scotland.prompt: As one of the young king's guardians, what do you urge the court to do?

choices.text: Divide the kingdom among the leading nobles
Honor David I's wishes and support Malcolm's succession
Back a rival adult claimant to the throne instead
Invite the King of England to rule as regent

evt-05-27-1153-malcolm-iv-of-scotland.butterflyEffect: Malcolm IV's throne held despite early revolts from disgruntled nobles, but his youth left him exposed to Henry II of England, to whom he ceded Northumbria, Cumberland, and Westmorland in 1157. The concession earned him the nickname 'the Maiden' and set back Scottish claims in northern England for generations.

evt-05-27-1644-manchu-people.scenario: It is 27 May 1644. You serve under Ming general Wu Sangui at Shanhai Pass, squeezed between Li Zicheng's advancing rebel army and the waiting Manchu banners of regent Dorgon beyond the Great Wall.
evt-05-27-1644-manchu-people.prompt: What does Wu Sangui decide to do to save the pass?

choices.text: Retreat with his army toward Beijing
Surrender the pass outright to Li Zicheng
Open the pass and ally with Dorgon's Manchu forces
Negotiate a truce with Li Zicheng's rebels

evt-05-27-1644-manchu-people.butterflyEffect: Wu Sangui allied with Dorgon and opened Shanhai Pass, letting Manchu cavalry smash Li Zicheng's Shun army. Dorgon's forces then marched on Beijing, beginning nearly three centuries of Qing dynasty rule over China.

evt-05-27-1896-1896-st-louis-east-st-lou.scenario: It is the evening of 27 May 1896, and you watch a strange green sky roll over the Mississippi River as residents of St. Louis go about their business with no sign of alarm from the authorities.
evt-05-27-1896-1896-st-louis-east-st-lou.prompt: What warning, if any, could you expect from the U.S. Weather Bureau before the storm strikes?

choices.text: A river flood warning covering the Mississippi corridor
An official tornado warning tracked from Kansas earlier that day
No tornado warning at all, since the Bureau avoided using the word "tornado"
A hurricane warning, since the storm was misclassified

evt-05-27-1896-1896-st-louis-east-st-lou.butterflyEffect: The Weather Bureau had banned the word "tornado" from its forecasts since 1887, fearing the term would cause public panic, so no official warning preceded the storm that killed at least 255 people in about twenty minutes. The disaster intensified a long debate over whether warning the public did more harm than good, a policy not reversed until tornado forecasting was modernized in the 1950s.

evt-05-27-1915-hms-princess-irene.scenario: It is the morning of 27 May 1915 at Sheerness, Kent. You watch dockyard crews loading naval mines aboard the auxiliary minelayer HMS Princess Irene ahead of a deployment mission.
evt-05-27-1915-hms-princess-irene.prompt: What happens to the ship in the minutes that follow?

choices.text: A fire breaks out but is contained before reaching the mines
She explodes and sinks with heavy loss of life
She completes loading and departs safely on schedule
The mines are found defective and removed before any harm is done

evt-05-27-1915-hms-princess-irene.butterflyEffect: Princess Irene exploded catastrophically while the mines were still being loaded, sinking almost instantly with the loss of 352 lives, including many dockyard workers. The inquiry pointed to faulty handling of primers and detonators, and the Admiralty tightened procedures for arming mines aboard ship afterward.

evt-05-27-1923-andre-lagache.scenario: You are riding alongside André Lagache through the night at the very first 24 Hours of Le Mans, engines roaring past exhausted crews as dawn approaches on 27 May 1923.
evt-05-27-1923-andre-lagache.prompt: What approach helps Lagache and Léonard cover the most laps and take the win?

choices.text: Push the engine to its limit for maximum lap speed
Stop frequently overnight to rest the drivers
Drive a steady, conservative pace to protect the car
Switch to a lighter backup vehicle at midnight

evt-05-27-1923-andre-lagache.butterflyEffect: Lagache and Léonard's disciplined, steady pace outlasted rivals who pushed harder and broke down, establishing endurance and reliability as the defining test of Le Mans. This philosophy shaped the race's identity for a century, making it as much about mechanical survival as raw speed.

evt-05-27-1935-supreme-court-of-the-unit.scenario: It is 27 May 1935, and you are a lawyer for the Roosevelt administration listening as the Supreme Court reads its opinion in Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, a case testing the heart of the New Deal's recovery program.
evt-05-27-1935-supreme-court-of-the-unit.prompt: What does the unanimous ruling mean for the National Industrial Recovery Act?

choices.text: The Court strikes down only the poultry code, leaving the rest of the NIRA intact
The Court sends the case back to a lower court for retrial
The Court upholds the NIRA but narrows it strictly to interstate commerce
The NIRA is struck down entirely, voiding its codes of fair competition

evt-05-27-1935-supreme-court-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: The Court struck down the NIRA entirely as an unconstitutional delegation of legislative power, on what became known as "Black Monday." The defeat forced Roosevelt to pursue New Deal programs on firmer constitutional ground, such as the Wagner Act and Social Security, and it fueled his later, failed attempt to expand and "pack" the Supreme Court.

evt-05-27-1937-golden-gate-bridge.scenario: It is dawn on 27 May 1937, and you join a crowd of San Franciscans gathering to be among the first to cross the newly completed Golden Gate Bridge, which is not yet open to automobiles.
evt-05-27-1937-golden-gate-bridge.prompt: What happens on this opening day?

choices.text: Thick fog forces organizers to postpone the opening by a week
Part of the bridge deck collapses during the opening ceremony
The bridge opens exclusively to pedestrians, who cross by the tens of thousands
The bridge opens to vehicle traffic only, with pedestrians barred entirely
