evt-06-06-1513-war-of-the-league-of-camb.scenario: You are a French soldier camped outside Novara before dawn, confident the Swiss garrison inside the walls is starving and beaten, when shouts and pike-points suddenly erupt out of the darkness.
evt-06-06-1513-war-of-the-league-of-camb.prompt: What happens when the Swiss storm the French camp in this surprise dawn assault?

choices.text: French artillery crews shatter the Swiss advance
French forces panic and flee, losing their siege artillery
Both sides agree to a truce before fighting starts
French cavalry breaks through and wins the field

evt-06-06-1513-war-of-the-league-of-camb.butterflyEffect: The Swiss rout was total: French lines collapsed in panic and their prized artillery train was captured, forcing the French army to abandon the siege and withdraw from Milanese territory. The victory preserved Massimiliano Sforza's rule in Milan for a time and cemented Swiss pikemen's reputation as Europe's most feared mercenaries.

evt-06-06-1674-shivaji.scenario: It is June 1674 at Raigad Fort. You stand among the assembled nobles and priests as Shivaji, who has spent decades fighting Bijapur and the Mughals, ascends the throne in a grand Vedic ceremony.
evt-06-06-1674-shivaji.prompt: What title does Shivaji formally take at his coronation?

choices.text: Sultan
Chhatrapati
Padishah
Nizam

evt-06-06-1674-shivaji.butterflyEffect: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati, giving his hard-won territories the legitimacy of a sovereign Hindu kingdom rather than a mere rebel fiefdom. This act laid the foundation for the Maratha Empire, which would grow to challenge Mughal dominance across India for the next century.

evt-06-06-1749-1749-muslim-slave-revolt-.scenario: You serve the Knights of St John in Malta, June 1749, when whispers among the enslaved Muslim rowers reveal a plot to assassinate Grand Master Manuel Pinto da Fonseca during a procession and open the harbor to an Ottoman fleet.
evt-06-06-1749-1749-muslim-slave-revolt-.prompt: What do the Knights do once the plot is discovered?

choices.text: Negotiate the freedom of all slaves to prevent revolt
Evacuate the Grand Master to Sicily immediately
Arrest the ringleaders and execute the conspirators before they can act
Dismiss the rumors as idle slave gossip

evt-06-06-1749-1749-muslim-slave-revolt-.butterflyEffect: The Order's agents uncovered the conspiracy in time, arresting the ringleaders and executing dozens of conspirators before any uprising could begin, so the feared Ottoman-backed invasion never materialized. The episode hardened suspicion of Malta's enslaved population and led to even harsher controls over them in the following decades.

evt-06-06-1813-war-of-1812.scenario: It is the night of 6 June 1813 near Stoney Creek. You are an American officer camped after your advance into Upper Canada, unaware that British troops are creeping through the darkness toward your lines.
evt-06-06-1813-war-of-1812.prompt: What follows when the British launch their surprise night attack on the camp?

choices.text: The Americans retreat back toward Fort George
The Americans call in naval bombardment support
The Americans press on and seize Burlington Heights
The entire American force surrenders on the spot

evt-06-06-1813-war-of-1812.butterflyEffect: The chaotic night assault captured American generals Chandler and Winder and threw the camp into disorder, forcing the American army to abandon its advance and retreat to Fort George. The defeat ended that year's invasion of the Niagara Peninsula and gave a badly needed morale boost to British and Canadian defenders.

evt-06-06-1882-shewa.scenario: You march with King Menelik of Shewa's army at Embabo, June 1882, facing the forces of Negus Tekle Haymanot of Gojjam in a struggle for control over the rich Oromo lands to the west.
evt-06-06-1882-shewa.prompt: What does Menelik's victory allow him to secure?

choices.text: A military alliance with the Ottoman Empire
Shewan control over Wollega and its trade wealth
Immediate deposition of Emperor Yohannes IV
Recognition of Gojjame independence

evt-06-06-1882-shewa.butterflyEffect: Menelik's win broke Gojjame power and secured Shewan dominance over Wollega and its lucrative trade in gold, coffee, and ivory. That wealth and territory bankrolled Menelik's later rise to become Emperor of Ethiopia and helped fund the army that would defeat Italy at Adwa in 1896.

evt-06-06-1912-novarupta.scenario: It's early June 1912, and you live in the Alutiiq village of Katmai on the Alaska Peninsula. The ground has trembled for days, and now a towering column of ash is rising from nearby Trident volcano, darkening the sky over your home.
evt-06-06-1912-novarupta.prompt: What should you and your neighbors do?

choices.text: Climb toward the volcano to observe the eruption safely from a ridge
Shelter in place, since the village has weathered eruptions before
Wait for rescue ships already anchored offshore to arrive
Evacuate immediately by boat before ashfall makes travel impossible

evt-06-06-1912-novarupta.butterflyEffect: Villagers evacuated by boat just in time, and remarkably no deaths were recorded despite it being the largest eruption of the 20th century. Ash fell as far as Kodiak Island, plunging it into days of darkness, and the eruption's scientific value later led to the creation of Katmai National Monument, preserving the ash-buried 'Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes.'

evt-06-06-1944-normandy-landings.scenario: It is early June 1944 in southern England. You are General Eisenhower, facing marginal weather forecasts and a fleet of thousands waiting for the order to cross the Channel.
evt-06-06-1944-normandy-landings.prompt: Do you launch the invasion on 6 June or delay further?

choices.text: Launch immediately on 5 June as first planned
Launch the invasion on 6 June despite the weather
Postpone the invasion by at least two weeks
Cancel Overlord and revise the entire strategy

evt-06-06-1944-normandy-landings.butterflyEffect: Eisenhower launched the invasion on 6 June, exploiting a brief weather window the Germans hadn't anticipated, achieving surprise despite rough seas. The successful landings opened the Western Front, began the liberation of France, and set the Allies on course toward victory in Europe.

evt-06-06-1971-soyuz-11.scenario: You are one of three cosmonauts aboard Soyuz 11 in June 1971, sealing the capsule for re-entry after three weeks aboard Salyut 1. Cabin space is tight, and mission planners have made a fateful trade-off in what safety equipment you carry.
evt-06-06-1971-soyuz-11.prompt: What critical safety equipment did the Soyuz 11 crew lack during re-entry?

choices.text: A backup radio for ground communication
A secondary parachute system
Ejection seats for emergency descent
Individual pressure suits for each cosmonaut

evt-06-06-1971-soyuz-11.butterflyEffect: A pressure equalization valve jarred open during module separation, venting the cabin's air into space. Because all three seats were needed for the crew, none of the cosmonauts wore pressure suits, and they died within minutes. The disaster forced the Soviets to redesign Soyuz to carry only two cosmonauts, always in pressure suits, for years afterward.

evt-06-06-1975-referendum.scenario: It is 5 June 1975, and Britain is holding its first-ever national referendum. You stand in a polling booth, ballot in hand, deciding whether the United Kingdom should remain a member of the European Economic Community.
evt-06-06-1975-referendum.prompt: What did the referendum result show?

choices.text: A tie requiring a second referendum
A vote to leave but renegotiate immediate re-entry
A narrow vote to leave the EEC
An overwhelming vote to remain in the EEC

evt-06-06-1975-referendum.butterflyEffect: British voters chose to stay in the EEC by a landslide, roughly two to one. The result settled the question for a generation, but simmering Euroscepticism never fully vanished and resurfaced decades later, culminating in the 2016 Brexit referendum that reversed the decision.

evt-06-06-1982-1982-lebanon-war.scenario: It is early June 1982. Gunmen have just shot Israel's ambassador in London, and intelligence suggests the attackers were rivals of the PLO rather than the PLO itself. Israeli leaders must decide how to respond.
evt-06-06-1982-1982-lebanon-war.prompt: What did Israel do in response to the assassination attempt on its ambassador?

choices.text: Requested an international peacekeeping force instead
Launched a full invasion of Lebanon, blaming the PLO
Pursued only diplomatic protests through the UN
Struck only the specific group responsible for the shooting

evt-06-06-1982-1982-lebanon-war.butterflyEffect: Prime Minister Menachem Begin and Defense Minister Ariel Sharon used the attack as justification to launch Operation Peace for Galilee, invading southern Lebanon on 6 June 1982. The war led to a prolonged Israeli occupation of southern Lebanon and, in the chaos, helped give rise to the militant group Hezbollah.

evt-06-06-1985-josef-mengele.scenario: In São Paulo, forensic investigators exhume a grave marked "Wolfgang Gerhard" to test long-standing rumors that the Auschwitz doctor Josef Mengele had lived and died in hiding in Brazil.
evt-06-06-1985-josef-mengele.prompt: What does the examination of the exhumed remains establish?

choices.text: The grave is found empty, proving he escaped again
The remains belong to an unrelated German expatriate
The remains match Mengele's records, confirming he died in Brazil in 1979
Testing is inconclusive and the search continues

evt-06-06-1985-josef-mengele.butterflyEffect: Dental and skeletal analysis matched Mengele's known medical records, and DNA testing confirmed in 1992 that he had drowned off a Brazilian beach in 1979 after decades evading capture. The finding closed one of the most notorious Nazi-hunting cases and revealed how thoroughly Cold War-era South America had sheltered fugitive war criminals.

evt-06-06-1985-embu-das-artes.scenario: You are part of a forensic team in Embu, Brazil, on 6 June 1985, exhuming a grave marked with the name 'Wolfgang Gerhard' after tips suggest the remains may belong to a notorious Nazi fugitive who fled to South America after World War II.
evt-06-06-1985-embu-das-artes.prompt: What must the team do to confirm the true identity of the remains?

choices.text: Rely on a DNA test, since the technology was already standard and conclusive in 1985
Accept the name on the headstone as sufficient proof of identity
Ask local residents for eyewitness testimony as the sole means of confirmation
Compare the skeleton's measurements and dental records against wartime photographs and medical files

evt-06-06-1985-embu-das-artes.butterflyEffect: The 1985 examination concluded with high confidence that the skeleton was Josef Mengele, the Auschwitz 'Angel of Death,' who had drowned in Brazil in 1979 while living under the alias Wolfgang Gerhard. Genetic testing in 1992 later confirmed the identification, closing one of the most notorious Nazi-hunting cases of the postwar era.

evt-06-06-1992-copa-airlines-flight-201.scenario: It's the night of 6 June 1992. You are the captain of Copa Airlines Flight 201, flying through a tropical storm over the Panama-Colombia border, when your primary attitude indicator suddenly disagrees with your co-pilot's and the aircraft begins banking hard without your input.
evt-06-06-1992-copa-airlines-flight-201.prompt: What should you do to prevent losing control of the aircraft?

choices.text: Disengage all instruments and fly by visual reference to the horizon
Cross-check with the co-pilot's independent instrument and use the standby attitude indicator
Radio air traffic control for vectors while continuing to follow the disagreeing instrument
Trust the primary instrument's reading and correct the aircraft based on it

evt-06-06-1992-copa-airlines-flight-201.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew followed the failed instrument instead of cross-checking it against the working one, causing spatial disorientation and a fatal dive that broke the 737 apart over the Darién jungle, killing all 47 aboard. The disaster reinforced aviation's push for stronger crew resource management and instrument cross-check training.

evt-06-06-1993-punsalmaagiin-ochirbat.scenario: It's 6 June 1993, and you are a Mongolian voter casting a ballot in your country's first direct presidential election, three years after peaceful protests ended one-party communist rule. Incumbent Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat, backed by the democratic opposition, faces the candidate of his old party, the Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party.
evt-06-06-1993-punsalmaagiin-ochirbat.prompt: What was the outcome of this landmark vote?

choices.text: The MPRP's candidate won, restoring full one-party control
Ochirbat won a decisive majority as the reform-backed incumbent
The vote ended in a tie requiring a runoff months later
A boycott forced the election to be cancelled and rescheduled

evt-06-06-1993-punsalmaagiin-ochirbat.butterflyEffect: Ochirbat won decisively with democratic backing, becoming Mongolia's first popularly elected president and cementing its peaceful shift to multiparty democracy. He lost his 1997 re-election bid to the MPRP's Natsagiin Bagabandi, showing the former ruling party could return to power through the ballot box rather than force.

evt-06-06-2002-2002-eastern-mediterranea.scenario: You monitor US satellite sensors built to detect nuclear detonations. On 6 June 2002, they register a flash over the Mediterranean Sea releasing energy comparable to a small atomic bomb, at a moment when India and Pakistan are locked in dangerous nuclear tension.
evt-06-06-2002-2002-eastern-mediterranea.prompt: What should you determine before alerting nuclear command channels?

choices.text: Report it immediately as a Pakistani nuclear test given the regional tension
Assume it is a satellite malfunction and disregard the reading
Report it as an Israeli nuclear test conducted over international waters
Confirm it is a natural airburst using trajectory, altitude, and speed data before reacting

evt-06-06-2002-2002-eastern-mediterranea.butterflyEffect: Analysis confirmed the flash came from a small, previously undetected asteroid disintegrating in the upper atmosphere, not a weapons test. Because it coincided with real nuclear tension elsewhere, it highlighted how easily a natural airburst could be mistaken for a detonation, underscoring the value of better near-Earth object tracking.

evt-06-06-2017-syrian-civil-war.scenario: It is 6 June 2017. You fight with the Syrian Democratic Forces as they push into Raqqa, the Syrian city ISIS has held as its de facto capital, with US-led coalition aircraft striking ahead of your advance.
evt-06-06-2017-syrian-civil-war.prompt: What did the SDF's Raqqa offensive achieve by that October?

choices.text: ISIS reinforced and held the city long-term
A negotiated ceasefire left ISIS in partial control
Capture of Raqqa, ending ISIS's territorial capital
The SDF withdrew after heavy losses

evt-06-06-2017-syrian-civil-war.butterflyEffect: After months of brutal urban combat, SDF fighters captured Raqqa in October 2017, ending ISIS's control of its self-declared capital and marking a major collapse of the group's territorial caliphate. The battle also caused massive destruction and civilian casualties, and the SDF's gains later fueled tension with Turkey over Kurdish influence in northern Syria.

evt-06-06-2021-2021-london-ontario-truck.scenario: It is the week after 6 June 2021, and a truck attack has killed members of a Muslim family in London, Ontario. You are a federal official facing pressure to respond to rising Islamophobia.
evt-06-06-2021-2021-london-ontario-truck.prompt: What formal action follows in the weeks after the attack?

choices.text: Close the investigation without public comment
Hold a national summit on Islamophobia
Ban all pickup trucks within city limits
Deploy the military to patrol Ontario cities

evt-06-06-2021-2021-london-ontario-truck.butterflyEffect: The Canadian government convened a National Summit on Islamophobia in July 2021, bringing together community leaders and officials to address anti-Muslim hate. The attack, condemned as terrorism by Prime Minister Trudeau, intensified national debate over hate crime laws and community safety.

evt-06-06-2023-russo-ukrainian-war.scenario: You live in a village downstream of the Kakhovka Dam on the Dnipro River. On the morning of 6 June 2023 you are woken by explosions, and water begins rising fast through the streets.
evt-06-06-2023-russo-ukrainian-war.prompt: What did local authorities urge residents downstream to do immediately?

choices.text: Shelter in place in basements
Wait for further confirmation before moving
Cross the river to the opposite bank
Evacuate immediately to higher ground

evt-06-06-2023-russo-ukrainian-war.butterflyEffect: The dam's collapse unleashed catastrophic flooding across the lower Dnipro, submerging dozens of towns and villages in Kherson region. It triggered an ecological disaster, cut irrigation water to southern Ukraine and Crimea, and threatened cooling water supplies to the nearby Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant. Ukraine and Russia each accused the other of causing the breach, and responsibility remains disputed.

evt-06-07-421-theodosius-ii.scenario: You serve at the court in Constantinople in 421, where Emperor Theodosius II, urged on by his devout sister Pulcheria, has taken notice of Athenais, a learned pagan woman and daughter of an Athenian philosopher who came to court seeking justice.
evt-06-07-421-theodosius-ii.prompt: What did Theodosius II do concerning Athenais?

choices.text: He sent her home to Athens with a monetary settlement
He banished her from Constantinople for her paganism
He married her after her baptism as Aelia Eudocia
He appointed her tutor to the imperial children

evt-06-07-421-theodosius-ii.butterflyEffect: Athenais was baptized as Aelia Eudocia and married Theodosius, becoming empress. She patronized literature and composed Christian poetry, but later fell from imperial favor and retired to Jerusalem, where her building projects and piety made her a revered figure in the city's history.

evt-06-07-1628-petition-of-right.scenario: It is 7 June 1628. You sit among the Commons who have drafted the Petition of Right, demanding King Charles I stop forced loans, arbitrary imprisonment, and billeting troops in private homes without consent. The petition now awaits the king's answer.
evt-06-07-1628-petition-of-right.prompt: Desperate for funds to pay for his wars, what does Charles I do about the petition?

choices.text: He has the petitioners arrested for treason
He rewrites it to strengthen royal power further
He rejects it outright and dissolves Parliament that day
He gives his reluctant assent to secure funding

evt-06-07-1628-petition-of-right.butterflyEffect: Charles gave his assent, though reluctantly and without the full formal language Parliament wanted. He soon ignored its terms anyway, dissolved Parliament the following year, and ruled without it for eleven years, a period of tension that helped set the stage for civil war.

evt-06-07-1692-1692-jamaica-earthquake.scenario: It is midday on 7 June 1692 in Port Royal, Jamaica, the wealthiest port in the English Caribbean. The ground beneath the wharves suddenly liquefies and buildings begin tilting toward the harbor.
evt-06-07-1692-1692-jamaica-earthquake.prompt: What actually happens to much of Port Royal in the minutes after the quake?

choices.text: The harbor drains away, leaving ships stranded
The fortifications collapse but the town center is untouched
Much of the town sinks into the harbor as the ground liquefies
The town burns but the buildings remain standing

evt-06-07-1692-1692-jamaica-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Roughly two-thirds of the town, built on sandy landfill, sank into the harbor as the ground liquefied beneath it. Port Royal never fully recovered its former stature, and British colonial authority in Jamaica shifted decisively toward the new settlement of Kingston.

evt-06-07-1810-mariano-moreno.scenario: You are Mariano Moreno, secretary of Buenos Aires's newly formed Primera Junta in June 1810. The revolutionary government needs to explain its decisions and rally the population, most of whom never see the decrees posted quietly in the plaza.
evt-06-07-1810-mariano-moreno.prompt: What does Moreno launch to spread the Junta's revolutionary message?

choices.text: Hire town criers to announce decrees orally only
Send private letters to each town council individually
Launch the Gazeta de Buenos Ayres, the colony's first newspaper
Rely solely on church sermons to spread the message

evt-06-07-1810-mariano-moreno.butterflyEffect: Moreno founded the Gazeta de Buenos Ayres, the first newspaper in what would become Argentina, using it to publish Junta decrees and Enlightenment ideas. It became the revolution's mouthpiece and helped seed a politically engaged press across the region during the independence wars that followed.

evt-06-07-1832-reform-act-1832.scenario: It is early 1832. Riots have broken out across England after the House of Lords repeatedly rejects the Reform Bill, and Prime Minister Earl Grey needs a way to force the peers to yield.
evt-06-07-1832-reform-act-1832.prompt: What does the government do to finally force the Reform Bill through the House of Lords?

choices.text: The King threatens to create enough new peers to force the bill through
Troops are sent to occupy the House of Lords
Women's suffrage is added to win over reluctant peers
The bill is quietly withdrawn and shelved for a decade

evt-06-07-1832-reform-act-1832.butterflyEffect: King William IV agreed to create enough new peers to overwhelm Tory opposition if the Lords refused again, and rather than accept a flood of new members the Lords backed down and let the bill pass. The Act redrew constituencies and widened the franchise, setting a precedent that led to further reform acts in 1867 and 1884.

evt-06-07-1900-temperance-movement-in-th.scenario: It is 7 June 1900 in Kiowa, Kansas. Carrie Nation, convinced she has received a divine calling, strides into a saloon that the town has voted to keep illegal despite state prohibition law.
evt-06-07-1900-temperance-movement-in-th.prompt: What does Carrie Nation do inside the saloon that launches her national reputation?

choices.text: She files a lawsuit against the saloon owner
She hurls rocks and bricks to smash the bottles and bar fixtures
She kneels and leads the patrons in prayer
She sets fire to the building's entrance

evt-06-07-1900-temperance-movement-in-th.butterflyEffect: She hurled rocks and bricks to smash the bar's bottles, mirrors, and fixtures, an act she called doing "God's work." The Kiowa raid launched her career of saloon-smashing "hatchetations" across Kansas, giving the temperance movement a fierce and famous symbol on its road toward national Prohibition in 1920.

evt-06-07-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It is just before dawn on 7 June 1917 near Messines Ridge in Belgium. You crouch in a British trench as engineers finish months of tunnelling beneath the German lines, waiting for the signal to detonate the mines.
evt-06-07-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What did British commanders order the moment the mines exploded?

choices.text: A full retreat to avoid German counter-mines
A ceasefire to negotiate German surrender
A gas attack instead of an infantry advance
An immediate infantry assault to seize the shattered ridge

evt-06-07-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The blasts, heard as far as London, obliterated German front positions and British and Anzac troops swiftly captured Messines Ridge in one of the war's most successful set-piece attacks. The tactical triumph encouraged commanders to launch the much larger Third Ypres offensive weeks later, which bogged down catastrophically in the mud of Passchendaele.

evt-06-07-1929-lateran-treaty.scenario: It is 7 June 1929 and you serve in the Vatican as the Lateran Treaty is ratified, finally resolving the decades-old Roman Question that began when Italian unification stripped the Papal States away in 1870.
evt-06-07-1929-lateran-treaty.prompt: What does the ratified treaty grant the papacy?

choices.text: Full restoration of all the former Papal States
Only diplomatic recognition without any territory
Direct papal governance over the entire city of Rome
Sovereign statehood over Vatican City plus financial compensation

evt-06-07-1929-lateran-treaty.butterflyEffect: The treaty created Vatican City as a sovereign state under papal rule, alongside a financial settlement and recognition of Catholicism as Italy's state religion. It made Vatican City the world's smallest sovereign state and tied the Church closely to Mussolini's regime, a relationship that later grew strained.

evt-06-07-1948-1948-anti-jewish-riots-in.scenario: It is June 1948 in the Moroccan border town of Oujda. News of the Arab-Israeli war has inflamed local tensions, and as a Jewish resident hoping to eventually reach Israel, you sense the streets around you growing dangerous.
evt-06-07-1948-1948-anti-jewish-riots-in.prompt: What did the violence in Oujda and Jerada ultimately spur among Morocco's Jewish community?

choices.text: A mass movement of Jews further into Morocco's interior
An immediate French decision to open legal emigration routes
A push toward organized, often clandestine, emigration to Israel
A widespread return to normal daily life within days

evt-06-07-1948-1948-anti-jewish-riots-in.butterflyEffect: The riots, which killed dozens, deepened fears among Moroccan Jews and accelerated clandestine emigration networks working to move people toward Israel despite French restrictions. Over the following decade, tens of thousands of Moroccan Jews left the country, reshaping a community that had existed there for centuries.

evt-06-07-1962-organisation-armee-secret.scenario: It is 7 June 1962 in Algiers, days before Algeria's independence referendum. You work at the university library when armed OAS commandos storm in, carrying cans of fuel as part of their scorched-earth campaign against a French Algeria they refuse to abandon.
evt-06-07-1962-organisation-armee-secret.prompt: What did the OAS commandos do to the University of Algiers library?

choices.text: Looted its contents but left the building untouched
Occupied it peacefully to make a political statement
Set fire to it, destroying manuscripts and rare books
Bombed a nearby building instead, sparing the library

evt-06-07-1962-organisation-armee-secret.butterflyEffect: They set it ablaze, destroying countless irreplaceable manuscripts and books just weeks before Algeria formally gained independence on 5 July 1962. The arson became emblematic of the OAS's final destructive campaign, which sought to leave nothing intact for the incoming Algerian state.

evt-06-07-1965-supreme-court-of-the-unit.scenario: You run a Connecticut birth-control clinic in the early 1960s and have just been arrested under a state law banning contraceptive use, even by married couples. Your case has reached the U.S. Supreme Court.
evt-06-07-1965-supreme-court-of-the-unit.prompt: How did the Supreme Court rule in Griswold v. Connecticut?

choices.text: It dismissed the case as moot before ruling
It sent the matter back to the Connecticut legislature
It upheld the law as a valid exercise of state police power
It struck down the law, citing a constitutional right to privacy

evt-06-07-1965-supreme-court-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: The Court struck down the Connecticut law, finding a constitutional right to marital privacy in the 'penumbras' of the Bill of Rights. That reasoning became the legal foundation for later privacy rulings, including Roe v. Wade in 1973 and Lawrence v. Texas in 2003.

evt-06-07-1967-six-day-war.scenario: It is 7 June 1967, and you lead a company of Israeli paratroopers fighting through the narrow alleys of Jerusalem's Old City. Ahead lies Lion's Gate, the last barrier between your unit and the Temple Mount and Western Wall beyond.
evt-06-07-1967-six-day-war.prompt: What do you order your paratroopers to do at Lion's Gate?

choices.text: Open surrender negotiations with Jordanian defenders
Storm through Lion's Gate and push into the Old City
Halt and call for a lengthy artillery bombardment first
Bypass Jerusalem entirely and advance toward Jericho

evt-06-07-1967-six-day-war.butterflyEffect: Israeli paratroopers stormed through Lion's Gate and reached the Western Wall, with commander Motta Gur radioing 'The Temple Mount is in our hands.' Israel's capture of East Jerusalem ended 19 years of Jordanian control and began a still-contested Israeli claim over the whole city.

evt-06-07-1969-blind-faith.scenario: It is 7 June 1969, and you are one of the tens of thousands packed into London's Hyde Park for the free debut concert of Blind Faith, the new supergroup uniting Eric Clapton, Steve Winwood, Ginger Baker, and Ric Grech.
evt-06-07-1969-blind-faith.prompt: What happens to Blind Faith in the months following this one UK show?

choices.text: They split within months after one album and a short tour
They merge permanently with Cream's former members
They become the decade's most enduring touring act
They relocate to the United States for a five-year residency

evt-06-07-1969-blind-faith.butterflyEffect: Despite the huge anticipation, Blind Faith disbanded within months, leaving behind just one album and a short summer tour. Clapton drifted toward Delaney & Bonnie and then Derek and the Dominos, while Winwood returned to Traffic, showing how quickly even the era's biggest supergroups could dissolve.

evt-06-07-1975-sony.scenario: You are a Sony engineer in 1975 finalizing the design of the company's new home videocassette recorder. You must choose between a compact cassette that delivers sharp picture quality but only an hour of recording, or a bulkier format that records longer with lesser fidelity.
evt-06-07-1975-sony.prompt: Which design trade-off do you choose for the format launching as Betamax?

choices.text: Use an open-reel tape system instead of a cassette
Prioritize sharp picture quality with a compact one-hour cassette
Delay the launch to pursue digital recording technology
Prioritize longer recording time with a larger, bulkier cassette

evt-06-07-1975-sony.butterflyEffect: Sony prioritized picture quality with a compact, short-recording cassette. Within a few years JVC's rival VHS format offered far longer recording times, and consumers overwhelmingly chose VHS, letting it dominate the home video market despite Betamax's technically superior image.

evt-06-07-1977-silver-jubilee-of-elizabe.scenario: It is 7 June 1977, and you are pressed among the crowds outside St Paul's Cathedral as Queen Elizabeth II emerges from the Silver Jubilee thanksgiving service, twenty-five years into her reign.
evt-06-07-1977-silver-jubilee-of-elizabe.prompt: What did the Queen do next that broke with royal tradition?

choices.text: She boarded a barge for an immediate river procession
She retired immediately to Buckingham Palace for a private lunch
She reviewed troops at Horse Guards Parade
She conducted an unscripted public walkabout through the crowds

evt-06-07-1977-silver-jubilee-of-elizabe.butterflyEffect: Elizabeth and Prince Philip conducted an unprecedented walkabout through the cheering City of London crowds instead of departing directly by car. The gesture proved so popular that walkabouts became a standard feature of royal tours and public engagements for decades afterward.

evt-06-07-1981-israeli-air-force.scenario: It is 7 June 1981 and you are flying an Israeli F-16 in a low-altitude formation racing across foreign airspace toward Baghdad, part of a secret mission to strike a facility Israel believes will soon produce weapons-grade material.
evt-06-07-1981-israeli-air-force.prompt: What was the outcome of this raid on Iraq's nuclear reactor?

choices.text: The formation was intercepted and turned back before reaching the target
The mission targeted a Syrian air base rather than Iraq
They struck an oil refinery instead of the reactor
The jets destroyed the reactor before it could go critical

evt-06-07-1981-israeli-air-force.butterflyEffect: The strike, later known as Operation Opera, destroyed the Osirak reactor before it became operational, setting back Iraq's nuclear ambitions. It drew international condemnation at the UN but established a precedent for preemptive strikes on hostile nuclear programs that Israel would invoke again in later decades.

evt-06-07-1982-priscilla-presley.scenario: You are among the first visitors lining up outside the gates of Graceland in Memphis on 7 June 1982, curious to see inside the mansion Elvis Presley once called home.
evt-06-07-1982-priscilla-presley.prompt: What did opening Graceland to the public help accomplish for the Presley estate?

choices.text: It became federal property under a preservation order
It was sold outright to a national hotel chain
It generated revenue that helped settle the estate's debts and taxes
It was closed again within weeks due to lack of visitor interest

evt-06-07-1982-priscilla-presley.butterflyEffect: Ticket revenue from tourists helped pay off substantial estate debts and taxes that had threatened the Presley family's finances after Elvis's death. Graceland went on to become one of the most visited private homes in America, eventually expanding into a full entertainment complex.

evt-06-07-1991-mount-pinatubo.scenario: You are a volcanologist stationed near Clark Air Base on 7 June 1991, watching a fresh ash column from Mount Pinatubo climb roughly seven kilometres into the sky after weeks of ominous tremors.
evt-06-07-1991-mount-pinatubo.prompt: What did authorities do in response to this alarming eruption?

choices.text: They dismissed the ash column as a false alarm
They allowed evacuated residents to return home
They downgraded the volcano's alert level
They expanded the evacuation radius around the volcano

evt-06-07-1991-mount-pinatubo.butterflyEffect: Officials widened the evacuation zone and moved thousands more residents and airbase personnel to safety. The precaution proved vital: on 15 June, Pinatubo produced the second-largest volcanic eruption of the 20th century, and the earlier evacuations are credited with saving countless lives.

evt-06-08-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 8 June 1941, and you are an Australian infantryman crossing into Lebanon alongside Free French forces, advancing against Vichy French troops loyal to the Axis-aligned government in France.
evt-06-08-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: What is the Allied objective in launching this campaign?

choices.text: Secure Syria and Lebanon from Vichy France to deny Axis access to the Middle East
Push German forces out of Egypt
Open a second front against Italy in the Balkans
Capture Rommel's headquarters in Libya

evt-06-08-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The Syria–Lebanon campaign secured the Levant for the Allies by mid-July 1941, denying the Axis a potential base near the Suez Canal and Middle Eastern oil. Free French administration replaced Vichy control, setting the stage for Syrian and Lebanese independence movements after the war.

evt-06-08-1949-nineteen-eighty-four.scenario: It is June 1949, and you are a London bookseller unpacking the first crates of George Orwell's newly published novel, its stark cover promising a story set in a grim future Britain.
evt-06-08-1949-nineteen-eighty-four.prompt: What central warning does Orwell's novel deliver to its readers?

choices.text: A call for armed revolution against monarchy
The dangers of totalitarian surveillance and thought control
Optimism about scientific progress improving society
A critique of free-market capitalism alone

evt-06-08-1949-nineteen-eighty-four.butterflyEffect: Nineteen Eighty-Four became one of the century's most influential novels, giving the world terms like "Big Brother" and "doublethink" and coining the adjective "Orwellian." Its warnings about surveillance and state control continue to shape political debate, especially around modern mass-surveillance technology.

evt-06-08-1950-thomas-blamey.scenario: It is 1950 and Prime Minister Robert Menzies' government considers how to formally honour Thomas Blamey, Australia's senior wartime commander, for his decades of service.
evt-06-08-1950-thomas-blamey.prompt: What rank does the government confer on Blamey?

choices.text: Governor-General of Australia
A knighthood only, with no change in rank
Field marshal
Commander of the newly formed Australian Regular Army

evt-06-08-1950-thomas-blamey.butterflyEffect: Blamey was promoted to field marshal, the only Australian ever to hold the rank. He died the following year, meaning the honour came only shortly before the end of his life.

evt-06-08-1984-homosexuality.scenario: It is 1984 and you sit in the New South Wales Parliament as a bill to decriminalize consensual sex between men comes to a vote, years after other Australian states began similar reforms.
evt-06-08-1984-homosexuality.prompt: How does the Parliament resolve the bill?

choices.text: Send it to a public referendum first
Pass it, decriminalizing consensual sex between men
Delay debate indefinitely without a vote
Reject it outright and keep the existing criminal laws

evt-06-08-1984-homosexuality.butterflyEffect: The bill passed, decriminalizing male homosexual acts in NSW, though it set the age of consent at 18, higher than the heterosexual age of 16. That disparity remained until further reform equalized the age of consent in 2003.

evt-06-08-2007-space-shuttle-atlantis.scenario: It is 8 June 2007, and you are a mission specialist strapped into Space Shuttle Atlantis as it lifts off on STS-117, carrying hardware bound for the International Space Station.
evt-06-08-2007-space-shuttle-atlantis.prompt: What is the primary cargo Atlantis is delivering on this mission?

choices.text: A truss segment and solar arrays to expand station power
A replacement mirror for the Hubble Space Telescope
The Destiny laboratory module
Supplies for the aging Mir space station

evt-06-08-2007-space-shuttle-atlantis.butterflyEffect: Atlantis delivered the S3/S4 truss segment and a new pair of solar arrays, expanding the station's power supply. This upgrade was essential groundwork for adding future ISS modules and supporting larger crews as the station neared completion.

evt-06-08-2008-akihabara-massacre.scenario: It is 8 June 2008 in Tokyo's Akihabara district, moments after a driver has plowed a rented truck into the crowded pedestrian street and begun attacking people with a knife.
evt-06-08-2008-akihabara-massacre.prompt: What change followed in Japan's response to this attack?

choices.text: Abolition of Japan's death penalty
New national gun-control legislation
A nationwide ban on trucks in city centers
Tighter restrictions on the sale and carrying of knives

evt-06-08-2008-akihabara-massacre.butterflyEffect: The attack prompted Japan to tighten restrictions on the sale of certain knives and review laws on weapon possession. It also fueled national debate about precarious temporary employment and social isolation, since the attacker was a dispatch worker who had voiced despair online before the attack.

evt-06-08-2009-2009-imprisonment-of-amer.scenario: It is August 2009, and you are journalist Laura Ling, sentenced to twelve years of hard labor in a North Korean facility for crossing the border. Word spreads through your guards that a high-profile American visitor has just arrived in Pyongyang.
evt-06-08-2009-2009-imprisonment-of-amer.prompt: What happens next in your case?

choices.text: Kim Jong Il pardons you following the visit
You are transferred to a Chinese prison
The United Nations negotiates your release
You remain imprisoned for the full sentence

evt-06-08-2009-2009-imprisonment-of-amer.butterflyEffect: Kim Jong Il pardoned Ling and Lee on 5 August 2009, the day after former President Bill Clinton arrived on an unannounced visit. The episode became a case study in backchannel diplomacy, showing how personal, off-the-record missions could resolve crises that formal diplomacy could not touch.

evt-06-08-2023-donald-trump.scenario: It is June 8, 2023. Federal prosecutors have just unsealed an indictment against former President Donald Trump over boxes of government material recovered from his Mar-a-Lago estate.
evt-06-08-2023-donald-trump.prompt: What did the federal indictment actually charge him with?

choices.text: Illegal foreign campaign contributions
Federal tax fraud spanning a decade
Mishandling classified documents and obstructing the investigation
Inciting an insurrection at the Capitol

evt-06-08-2023-donald-trump.butterflyEffect: Trump was charged with willful retention of national defense information and obstruction, becoming the first former U.S. president indicted on federal charges. The case was later dismissed in July 2024 by the trial judge, who ruled the special counsel's appointment unconstitutional, leaving the underlying legal questions unresolved.

evt-06-09-1549-book-of-common-prayer-154.scenario: It is 9 June 1549, and Parliament's Act of Uniformity has just taken effect. You are a parish priest in rural England, and the churchwardens are waiting for you to lead the first English-language service ever held in your church.
evt-06-09-1549-book-of-common-prayer-154.prompt: What are you now legally required to do for every service?

choices.text: Continue saying the Latin Mass as before
Alternate Latin and English services depending on the congregation
Use the new book only for weddings and funerals
Use the new Book of Common Prayer exclusively, in English

evt-06-09-1549-book-of-common-prayer-154.butterflyEffect: Cranmer's English-language liturgy replaced Latin rites everywhere in England, sparking the Prayer Book Rebellion in Devon and Cornwall that year. Protestant critics still found it too traditional, so Cranmer issued a more sharply Protestant revision in 1552, which became the template for later Anglican prayer books.

evt-06-09-1856-mormon-handcart-pioneers.scenario: It's June 1856 in Iowa City, and you stand beside your family's two-wheeled handcart, loaded with everything you own, about to set out for Salt Lake City instead of buying an ox-drawn wagon.
evt-06-09-1856-mormon-handcart-pioneers.prompt: Why did church leaders promote handcarts over traditional ox-wagons for this migration?

choices.text: They moved faster than horse teams over mountain passes
They could carry twice the cargo of a standard wagon
Federal law required all migrants to use handcarts that year
They cost far less and let poor converts travel without expensive oxen

evt-06-09-1856-mormon-handcart-pioneers.butterflyEffect: The plan let poor converts travel cheaply, and most 1856 companies arrived safely. But the late-departing Willie and Martin handcart companies were caught by early snows in Wyoming that October, and the resulting deaths led the church to largely abandon handcarts for wagon trains afterward.

evt-06-09-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It is before dawn on 9 June 1863 near the Rappahannock River in Virginia. You ride with General Alfred Pleasonton's Union cavalry, ordered to ford the river and strike Confederate horsemen camped near Brandy Station before they can move.
evt-06-09-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: What should the Union cavalry do at first light?

choices.text: Retreat north to avoid contact with Stuart's cavalry
Send a truce flag to negotiate a prisoner exchange
Cross the river fords at dawn in a surprise attack
Wait several days for Union infantry to arrive first

evt-06-09-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Union troopers crossed at Beverly's and Kelly's Fords in a surprise dawn attack, triggering the largest cavalry battle of the war. Though J.E.B. Stuart's Confederates held the field by day's end, the fight proved Union cavalry could now match its Southern counterpart, a shift in confidence that carried into the Gettysburg campaign weeks later.

evt-06-09-1928-charles-kingsford-smith.scenario: It's June 9, 1928, and after nearly 90 hours in the air crossing the Pacific from California via Hawaii and Fiji, you're aboard the Southern Cross watching the Queensland coastline rise ahead.
evt-06-09-1928-charles-kingsford-smith.prompt: Where did Kingsford Smith and his crew land to complete the first transpacific flight?

choices.text: Perth
Brisbane
Sydney
Darwin

evt-06-09-1928-charles-kingsford-smith.butterflyEffect: The Southern Cross touched down at Eagle Farm, Brisbane, before a crowd of thousands, turning Kingsford Smith into a national hero overnight. The flight proved sustained trans-Pacific air travel was achievable and helped spur development of commercial air routes linking Australia to the Americas.

evt-06-09-1954-united-states-army.scenario: It is 9 June 1954, and you are seated in a packed Senate caucus room. Army counsel Joseph Welch has just been pressed by Senator Joseph McCarthy over a young lawyer's past ties, and the room falls silent waiting for Welch's reply.
evt-06-09-1954-united-states-army.prompt: What does Welch say that becomes the turning point of the Army-McCarthy hearings?

choices.text: "You are out of order, Senator, and I move to adjourn"
"Have you no sense of decency, sir?"
"I refuse to answer on constitutional grounds"
"This committee has no jurisdiction over this matter"

evt-06-09-1954-united-states-army.butterflyEffect: Welch's rebuke — 'Have you no sense of decency, sir?' — was broadcast live and crystallized public disgust with McCarthy's tactics. Public opinion turned sharply against him, and the Senate voted to censure McCarthy later that year, effectively ending his political power and the era known as McCarthyism.

evt-06-09-1959-uss-george-washington-ssb.scenario: It's 9 June 1959 at the Electric Boat shipyard in Groton, Connecticut. You watch USS George Washington slide down the ways, the first submarine built to carry ballistic missiles powered by a nuclear reactor, and planners are already arguing over how to prove she can do her job.
evt-06-09-1959-uss-george-washington-ssb.prompt: What milestone should the Navy pursue before declaring the submarine combat-ready?

choices.text: Decommission the missile tubes and use her as an attack submarine
Reassign her crew to a diesel-electric submarine instead
Conduct a submerged test launch of a Polaris missile
Send her straight into her first war patrol untested

evt-06-09-1959-uss-george-washington-ssb.butterflyEffect: In July 1960, George Washington successfully fired two Polaris missiles while submerged off Cape Canaveral, the first submerged ballistic missile launches in history. This proved the survivability of sea-based nuclear deterrence, launching the U.S. Navy's SSBN fleet and pushing the Soviet Union to accelerate its own submarine missile program.

evt-06-09-1965-south-vietnam.scenario: It is June 1965 in Saigon. Prime Minister Phan Huy Quat's civilian government has been paralyzed by factional infighting and pressure from South Vietnam's military leaders.
evt-06-09-1965-south-vietnam.prompt: What actually happens to Quat's civilian government?

choices.text: He is re-elected in a landslide popular vote
He resigns, and a military junta takes power
He negotiates a coalition government with the Viet Cong
He is assassinated by a rival faction

evt-06-09-1965-south-vietnam.butterflyEffect: Quat resigned, and power passed to a military junta led by Air Marshal Nguyen Cao Ky, with Nguyen Van Thieu as head of state. This began a period of sustained military rule in South Vietnam that lasted until the country's fall in 1975.

evt-06-09-1967-six-day-war.scenario: It is 9 June 1967, the fifth day of the Six-Day War. You command Israeli forces facing entrenched Syrian positions on the steep Golan Heights escarpment, with international pressure mounting for a ceasefire.
evt-06-09-1967-six-day-war.prompt: What should Israeli forces do before a ceasefire can take effect?

choices.text: Halt operations and await a United Nations resolution
Open direct negotiations with Damascus before advancing further
Press the assault up the escarpment to seize the heights
Withdraw troops to the pre-war border immediately

evt-06-09-1967-six-day-war.butterflyEffect: Israeli troops pressed the assault up the escarpment and overran Syrian defenses, capturing the Golan Heights before the ceasefire took hold the next day. Israel has held the territory since, formally annexing it in 1981 in a move most of the world has not recognized, making the Golan a lasting flashpoint in Israeli-Syrian relations.

evt-06-09-1968-lyndon-b-johnson.scenario: It is 9 June 1968, the day of Robert F. Kennedy's funeral. You are a White House aide finalizing President Johnson's proclamation as Kennedy's funeral train carries mourners toward Arlington National Cemetery.
evt-06-09-1968-lyndon-b-johnson.prompt: What does Johnson's proclamation order across the federal government that day?

choices.text: Only military installations observe mourning
Flags lowered to half-staff and federal offices closed
Flags remain at full staff but offices close
Congress permanently suspends its session

evt-06-09-1968-lyndon-b-johnson.butterflyEffect: Johnson ordered flags flown at half-staff and closed federal offices in mourning, the second such national mourning in barely two months after Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination. The back-to-back killings deepened the turmoil of the 1968 election year and helped push Congress toward passing the Gun Control Act later that year.

evt-06-09-1972-black-hills.scenario: It is the night of June 9, 1972, in Rapid City, South Dakota. Torrential rain has fallen on the Black Hills for hours and Rapid Creek is rising fast past its banks near your home.
evt-06-09-1972-black-hills.prompt: What is the safest thing to do as the water rises?

choices.text: Move immediately to higher ground away from the creek
Stay inside and wait for the rain to stop
Drive across the low bridge to reach family downtown
Move belongings to the basement first

evt-06-09-1972-black-hills.butterflyEffect: The Canyon Lake Dam failed that night, sending a wall of water through Rapid City that killed 238 people. In the aftermath, the city removed homes from the floodplain and built the Rapid City Greenway, reshaping how the region manages flood risk.

evt-06-09-1973-secretariat-horse.scenario: You are in the grandstand at Belmont Park on June 9, 1973, watching Secretariat attempt to become the first Triple Crown winner in 25 years. Coming out of the final turn, he has already opened a lead no one thought possible.
evt-06-09-1973-secretariat-horse.prompt: What happens as Secretariat crosses the Belmont Stakes finish line?

choices.text: He wins narrowly by about two lengths
He loses by a nose to his rival Sham
He is disqualified for interfering with another horse
He wins by 31 lengths, setting a record time that still stands

evt-06-09-1973-secretariat-horse.butterflyEffect: Secretariat won by 31 lengths in a time that still stands as the Belmont Stakes record, completing the Triple Crown and delivering what many call the greatest performance in thoroughbred racing history. The victory sparked a surge of popular interest in horse racing and secured his legendary status as one of the sport's all-time greats.

evt-06-09-1982-1982-lebanon-war.scenario: You are an Israeli Air Force pilot over Lebanon's Bekaa Valley on June 9, 1982, part of a massive strike force sent to knock out Syria's dense screen of surface-to-air missile batteries shielding its ground forces.
evt-06-09-1982-1982-lebanon-war.prompt: What is the outcome of this air operation against the Syrian SAM network?

choices.text: The operation is redirected to strike Beirut instead of the Bekaa Valley
Nearly all Syrian SAM batteries are destroyed and dozens of Syrian jets shot down for minimal Israeli losses
Syrian SAM batteries successfully repel the Israeli attack
The Israeli Air Force suffers heavy losses and the mission is aborted

evt-06-09-1982-1982-lebanon-war.butterflyEffect: Operation Mole Cricket 19 became one of the largest air battles since World War II: Israel destroyed nearly all of Syria's SAM batteries and shot down dozens of Syrian fighter jets while losing few or no aircraft of its own, using AWACS-style command control and electronic warfare. The lopsided result forced Syria to rebuild its air defenses and became a case study studied by air forces worldwide.

evt-06-09-1995-ansett-new-zealand-flight.scenario: It is the morning of 9 June 1995. You are flying the Dash 8 into Palmerston North, and low cloud is closing over the Tararua Range as the aircraft descends toward the airfield without the runway yet in sight.
evt-06-09-1995-ansett-new-zealand-flight.prompt: What flying error did investigators later identify as the direct cause of the crash?

choices.text: An uncontained engine failure from poor maintenance
Running out of fuel before reaching the airfield
Structural failure of the wing in turbulence
Descending below the minimum safe altitude without visual contact with the runway

evt-06-09-1995-ansett-new-zealand-flight.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew had descended below the minimum safe altitude before establishing visual contact with the runway, flying the aircraft into terrain in cloud. The accident pushed New Zealand's aviation authorities to tighten approach procedures and accelerate the fitting of terrain-awareness warning systems on regional airliners.

evt-06-09-1999-yugoslav-wars.scenario: It is June 9, 1999, in Kumanovo, Macedonia. After 78 days of relentless NATO bombing, your government's military delegation has just put pen to paper on an agreement with NATO commanders.
evt-06-09-1999-yugoslav-wars.prompt: What does the Kumanovo Agreement require Yugoslav forces to do?

choices.text: Accept formal partition of Kosovo into Serb and Albanian zones
Hand over all weapons directly to the Kosovo Liberation Army
Withdraw all Yugoslav military, police, and paramilitary forces from Kosovo
Continue fighting until a UN-mediated ceasefire is separately negotiated

evt-06-09-1999-yugoslav-wars.butterflyEffect: The agreement ended NATO's air campaign and mandated the complete withdrawal of Yugoslav military, police, and paramilitary forces from Kosovo. It paved the way for UN Security Council Resolution 1244 and the deployment of NATO-led KFOR peacekeepers, setting the stage for Kosovo's eventual unilateral declaration of independence in 2008.

evt-06-09-2019-david-ortiz.scenario: It's the night of 9 June 2019 at a bar in Santo Domingo. A gunman on a motorcycle has just shot David Ortiz in the back at close range, and people around him are deciding how to react in the chaotic seconds after.
evt-06-09-2019-david-ortiz.prompt: What actually happened to Ortiz in the aftermath of the shooting?

choices.text: He was flown to Boston and survived after multiple surgeries
He walked away with only minor injuries
He was never hospitalized and returned to broadcasting the next day
He died at the scene before help arrived

evt-06-09-2019-david-ortiz.butterflyEffect: Ortiz was rushed into emergency surgery in Santo Domingo, then flown to Boston for further treatment, surviving after having part of his intestines and gallbladder removed. Investigators later determined he had been the victim of mistaken identity in a contract hit meant for someone else, and several suspects were arrested in the Dominican Republic.

evt-06-10-1190-third-crusade.scenario: It is 10 June 1190. You march with Emperor Frederick Barbarossa's crusader army along the Saleph River in Anatolia, the men exhausted and overheated after weeks on the road toward the Holy Land.
evt-06-10-1190-third-crusade.prompt: What happens to Emperor Frederick Barbarossa here?

choices.text: He is ambushed by Seljuk cavalry
He drowns crossing the river
He is captured by Saladin's forces
He dies of plague in camp

evt-06-10-1190-third-crusade.butterflyEffect: Barbarossa drowned attempting to cross or bathe in the river, and much of his vast army, demoralized and leaderless, dispersed or turned back rather than continuing to the Holy Land. The Third Crusade's leadership fell to Richard I of England and Philip II of France, whose rivalry would soon fracture the campaign further.

evt-06-10-1329-byzantine-ottoman-wars.scenario: You march with Emperor Andronikos III Palaiologos's army toward Pelekanon near Nicomedia in 1329, moving to break the Ottoman siege and reassert Byzantine control over Bithynia.
evt-06-10-1329-byzantine-ottoman-wars.prompt: What follows after the emperor is wounded in the fighting?

choices.text: Both sides negotiate an immediate truce
The Byzantine army retreats in disarray, ceding the field
The Byzantines rally and rout the Ottoman forces
The Ottomans withdraw voluntarily before battle is joined

evt-06-10-1329-byzantine-ottoman-wars.butterflyEffect: The Byzantines withdrew in disorder after Andronikos III was wounded, and Orhan's Ottomans held the field. The defeat confirmed Ottoman dominance in Bithynia, paving the way for the fall of Nicaea in 1331 and Nicomedia in 1337, entrenching the Ottomans in Asia Minor decades before Constantinople itself fell.

evt-06-10-1624-thirty-years-war.scenario: You serve Cardinal Richelieu in 1624 as France weighs whether to quietly finance the Protestant Dutch Republic's war against Catholic Spain, despite France's own Catholic identity.
evt-06-10-1624-thirty-years-war.prompt: What does France decide regarding the Dutch Republic at Compiègne?

choices.text: France refuses any involvement in northern Europe's conflicts
France agrees to subsidize Dutch resistance to Spain
France declares war directly on the Dutch Republic
France offers the Dutch territory in exchange for neutrality

evt-06-10-1624-thirty-years-war.butterflyEffect: France agreed to subsidize the Dutch war effort against Spain, prioritizing Habsburg containment over religious solidarity. This treaty marked an early step in France's anti-Habsburg strategy that would culminate in direct French entry into the Thirty Years' War by 1635.

evt-06-10-1692-bridget-bishop.scenario: You are a magistrate in Salem in June 1692, weighing spectral testimony and rumor against Bridget Bishop, the first of the accused to face trial for witchcraft.
evt-06-10-1692-bridget-bishop.prompt: What do the magistrates decide regarding Bridget Bishop's fate?

choices.text: She is convicted and sentenced to hang
She is banished from the colony instead of tried
She confesses and is spared execution
She is acquitted for lack of credible evidence

evt-06-10-1692-bridget-bishop.butterflyEffect: Bishop was convicted and hanged, becoming the first person executed in the Salem witch trials. Her execution opened the way for eighteen more hangings and one death by pressing before public and clerical doubts about the evidence brought the hysteria to an end the following year.

evt-06-10-1782-rama-i.scenario: You stand among the court as King Rama I crosses the river to take up residence in the newly completed Grand Palace in 1782, following the turmoil that ended Taksin's reign in Thonburi.
evt-06-10-1782-rama-i.prompt: What is Rama I accomplishing by settling into this new palace?

choices.text: Founding a new capital for the Chakri dynasty
Restoring Ayutthaya as the kingdom's capital
Surrendering the throne to a rival claimant
Relocating the capital temporarily due to plague

evt-06-10-1782-rama-i.butterflyEffect: The move established Bangkok, then called Rattanakosin, as the new royal capital of Siam under the Chakri dynasty. That dynasty still reigns in Thailand today, and Bangkok grew from this founding into one of Southeast Asia's great capitals.

evt-06-10-1861-american-civil-war.scenario: You advance with Union troops toward Confederate earthworks at Big Bethel, Virginia, in June 1861, confident that a quick strike will scatter the outnumbered defenders.
evt-06-10-1861-american-civil-war.prompt: What happens to the Union assault at Big Bethel?

choices.text: Confederate troops surrender before the assault begins
Both sides withdraw without engaging
The attack fails chaotically, with the Union suffering the heavier losses
The Union overwhelms the position with minimal casualties

evt-06-10-1861-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Confused and poorly coordinated, the Union attack collapsed under Confederate fire, suffering far heavier losses than the defenders. The lopsided defeat, one of the war's first land battles, dented Northern confidence in an easy victory and boosted early Southern morale.

evt-06-10-1886-mount-tarawera.scenario: It's the early hours of 10 June 1886 near Rotorua, and Mount Tarawera erupts violently, sending ash and mud raining down over the surrounding Māori villages and lakes.
evt-06-10-1886-mount-tarawera.prompt: What renowned natural attraction was destroyed in the eruption's aftermath?

choices.text: The Pink and White Terraces
The Waitomo Caves
Huka Falls
Milford Sound

evt-06-10-1886-mount-tarawera.butterflyEffect: The eruption buried the village of Te Wairoa and obliterated the Pink and White Terraces, then celebrated worldwide as a natural wonder and major tourist draw. Their loss reshaped Rotorua's tourism and prompted some of New Zealand's earliest systematic studies of volcanic hazards.

evt-06-10-1916-hussein-king-of-hejaz.scenario: It's June 1916 in the Hejaz, and Sharif Hussein has just raised the flag of revolt against Ottoman rule, backed by promises of British arms and support against Constantinople.
evt-06-10-1916-hussein-king-of-hejaz.prompt: What did Hussein and his British backers lead the Arabs to expect from the revolt?

choices.text: Independence for a unified Arab kingdom
A permanent seat in the Ottoman parliament
Recognition as Caliph by all Muslim powers
Direct annexation of the Hejaz by Britain

evt-06-10-1916-hussein-king-of-hejaz.butterflyEffect: British officers, including T. E. Lawrence, helped coordinate guerrilla attacks on Ottoman rail lines, but secret Anglo-French agreements and later declarations meant the promised unified Arab kingdom never fully materialized. The broken promises fed Arab nationalist grievances that shaped Middle Eastern politics for decades afterward.

evt-06-10-1918-world-war-i.scenario: It is the night of June 10, 1918, in the Adriatic Sea. You command one of Luigi Rizzo's small Italian MAS torpedo boats and spot the Austro-Hungarian dreadnought SMS Szent Istvan steaming with its squadron.
evt-06-10-1918-world-war-i.prompt: What should the outgunned MAS boat do against the massive dreadnought?

choices.text: Signal for a full squadron of Italian cruisers to engage instead
Open fire with its deck gun to draw the dreadnought's attention
Attempt to ram the dreadnought's hull directly
Fire torpedoes and try to slip away before being spotted

evt-06-10-1918-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Rizzo's MAS boats launched a torpedo attack that sank the Szent Istvan, one of the few dreadnoughts ever sunk by such small craft. The loss convinced the Austro-Hungarian navy to abandon its planned offensive against the Otranto Barrage, keeping its battleship fleet largely idle for the rest of the war.

evt-06-10-1957-john-diefenbaker.scenario: It is election night, 10 June 1957. You sit by the radio as returns come in from across Canada, watching the long-ruling Liberal Party face its stiffest challenge in over two decades from John Diefenbaker's Progressive Conservatives.
evt-06-10-1957-john-diefenbaker.prompt: What is the outcome of the election for Diefenbaker's party?

choices.text: They form a coalition government with the CCF
They narrowly lose to the Liberals again
They win the most seats, forming a minority government
They win a commanding majority outright

evt-06-10-1957-john-diefenbaker.butterflyEffect: The Progressive Conservatives won the most seats, ending 22 years of unbroken Liberal government, though Diefenbaker led only a minority. He called a snap election the following year and won one of the largest majorities in Canadian history, reshaping federal politics for a generation.

evt-06-10-1996-northern-ireland.scenario: It's June 1996 at Stormont in Belfast, and multi-party talks on Northern Ireland's future open around a table with one prominent seat conspicuously empty.
evt-06-10-1996-northern-ireland.prompt: Why was Sinn Féin excluded from these 1996 Northern Ireland peace talks?

choices.text: Unionist parties vetoed any republican attendance permanently
Sinn Féin voluntarily boycotted the talks
Britain had outlawed all Irish nationalist parties
The IRA had ended its ceasefire with a bombing earlier that year

evt-06-10-1996-northern-ireland.butterflyEffect: The IRA had ended its ceasefire with the Docklands bombing months earlier, and Sinn Féin was barred until republicans renounced violence. A fresh ceasefire in 1997 finally brought the party into negotiations, which produced the Good Friday Agreement in April 1998, transforming the region's political future.

evt-06-10-1997-khmer-rouge.scenario: It is June 1997 in the Khmer Rouge's crumbling jungle stronghold near Anlong Veng. Pol Pot has grown convinced that his old comrade and defense chief Son Sen is secretly negotiating to defect to the Cambodian government.
evt-06-10-1997-khmer-rouge.prompt: What did Pol Pot order done to Son Sen?

choices.text: He orders Son Sen and his family killed
He exiles Son Sen across the Thai border
He puts Son Sen on public trial for treason
He promotes Son Sen to lead peace talks

evt-06-10-1997-khmer-rouge.butterflyEffect: Pol Pot had Son Sen and his family killed. The murders horrified remaining commanders like Ta Mok, who turned on Pol Pot, arrested him within weeks, and staged a show trial that sentenced him to life under house arrest — effectively ending the Khmer Rouge as a fighting force.

evt-06-10-2001-pope-john-paul-ii.scenario: You stand in St. Peter's Square in 2001 as Pope John Paul II declares the Lebanese nun Rafqa a saint, honoring her decades of quiet suffering and devotion.
evt-06-10-2001-pope-john-paul-ii.prompt: What is the Vatican achieving with this canonization?

choices.text: Naming Lebanon's first native female saint
Appointing Lebanon's first cardinal
Reconciling the Maronite and Roman rites permanently
Establishing the first Maronite diocese in Rome

evt-06-10-2001-pope-john-paul-ii.butterflyEffect: Rafqa became Lebanon's first native female saint, strengthening Maronite Catholic identity within Lebanon's fractured religious landscape. Pilgrimage to her shrine in Jrabta grew, and the canonization reinforced the Vatican's continuing outreach to Middle Eastern Christian communities.

evt-06-10-2002-kevin-warwick.scenario: It is 2002 in Reading, England. You are part of Kevin Warwick's cyborg research, an electrode array implanted in your arm, waiting to see whether a nerve signal from another person's nervous system can trigger a response in yours.
evt-06-10-2002-kevin-warwick.prompt: What did this landmark experiment demonstrate?

choices.text: Wireless transmission of a video feed from one brain to another
The first computer-to-human speech synthesis link
Direct electronic signal exchange between two human nervous systems
Remote control of a robotic arm using only human thought

evt-06-10-2002-kevin-warwick.butterflyEffect: Warwick's implant relayed signals directly between his own nervous system and that of his wife, Irena, marking the first purely electronic nervous-system-to-nervous-system link between two people. The work became a foundational reference point for later brain-computer interface and neuroprosthetic research.

evt-06-10-2003-spirit-rover.scenario: It is June 10, 2003, and you are a mission engineer at Cape Canaveral watching a Delta II rocket carrying NASA's Spirit rover thunder into the sky toward Mars.
evt-06-10-2003-spirit-rover.prompt: What happened when Spirit finally reached the Martian surface?

choices.text: It burned up during atmospheric entry
It landed successfully inside Gusev Crater
It crashed after its parachute failed to deploy
It landed at Meridiani Planum alongside Opportunity

evt-06-10-2003-spirit-rover.butterflyEffect: Spirit landed safely inside Gusev Crater on January 4, 2004, three weeks ahead of its twin Opportunity, which touched down at Meridiani Planum. Designed for a 90-day mission, Spirit kept exploring for over six years until it became stuck in soft sand in 2009 and lost contact in 2010.

evt-06-10-2009-united-states-holocaust-m.scenario: It is June 10, 2009, and you are a security officer at the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum in Washington, D.C., when an elderly man raises a rifle at the entrance.
evt-06-10-2009-united-states-holocaust-m.prompt: What ultimately became of the shooter, James von Brunn?

choices.text: He was captured unharmed and later convicted at trial
He escaped the museum and was caught crossing state lines
He was wounded by guards, arrested, and died in custody before trial
He was killed at the scene by responding police

evt-06-10-2009-united-states-holocaust-m.butterflyEffect: Von Brunn fatally shot security guard Stephen Tyrone Johns before other guards returned fire and wounded him. He was arrested but died in federal custody in January 2010 while awaiting trial, and the attack prompted museums and memorial sites nationwide to reassess security against domestic extremist threats.

evt-06-10-2018-opportunity-rover.scenario: It's June 2018 on Mars, and a colossal dust storm has swallowed the sky over Opportunity's solar panels, cutting off the power that has kept it running for over fourteen years past its planned lifespan.
evt-06-10-2018-opportunity-rover.prompt: What ultimately silenced the Opportunity rover after this final transmission?

choices.text: A wheel mechanism jammed, stranding it permanently
Its nuclear power source was depleted
A planet-wide dust storm blocked sunlight to its solar panels
It fell into a deep, unmapped crater

evt-06-10-2018-opportunity-rover.butterflyEffect: Unable to recharge its batteries in the storm's darkness, Opportunity never woke again. NASA made hundreds of recovery attempts before formally ending the mission in February 2019, closing out a rover that had outlasted its 90-sol design life by more than fourteen years.

evt-1509-henry-viii-marriage.scenario: London, June 1509. You are Henry VIII, crowned weeks ago at seventeen. Your councillors urge you to honour the alliance with Spain and marry your late brother's widow — but the union needs a special ruling from Rome.
evt-1509-henry-viii-marriage.prompt: You proceed with the marriage. What long-term risk are you accepting?

choices.text: The papal dispensation can later be weaponized to contest the marriage itself
Spain will immediately declare war over the dowry
The match bars Henry from ever claiming the French crown
Parliament gains the power to annul royal marriages at will

evt-1509-henry-viii-marriage.butterflyEffect: When Henry sought an annulment in the 1520s, that dispensation became the legal battleground. Rome would not undo its own ruling — so Henry broke with Rome entirely, and the Church of England was born in 1534.

evt-06-11-1509-catherine-of-aragon.scenario: It is 11 June 1509, and you stand among the courtiers at Greenwich as the newly crowned Henry VIII marries Catherine of Aragon, widow of his late brother Arthur.
evt-06-11-1509-catherine-of-aragon.prompt: What alliance did this marriage secure for England?

choices.text: An Anglo-Portuguese trade alliance
An Anglo-French alliance against the Holy Roman Empire
An Anglo-Spanish alliance through Catherine's father, Ferdinand II of Aragon
An Anglo-Scottish alliance to secure the northern border

evt-06-11-1509-catherine-of-aragon.butterflyEffect: The marriage bound England to Spain against France for two decades under Catherine's father, Ferdinand II of Aragon. But Catherine's inability to produce a surviving male heir eventually drove Henry to seek an annulment, a rupture with Rome that launched the English Reformation.

evt-1770-endeavour-reef.scenario: Coral Sea, near midnight, 11 June 1770. You are James Cook. Endeavour is impaled on coral and taking water, 24 kilometres from an uncharted shore. The next high tide is your one chance.
evt-1770-endeavour-reef.prompt: What is your call to save the ship?

choices.text: Jettison the cannons and ballast to lighten her, then haul off on the tide
Throw the provisions overboard but keep the guns for defence
Abandon ship at once and row for the coast
Hold position and wait for rescue from passing vessels

evt-1770-endeavour-reef.butterflyEffect: Cook's gamble — dumping six cannons and 50 tonnes of ballast — floated her free after 23 hours. The seven-week repair stop produced charts and specimens that shaped Britain's claim to Australia eighteen years later.

evt-06-11-1775-battle-of-machias.scenario: It is June 1775 in Machias, Maine. A British armed schooner, the Margaretta, sits in the harbor demanding lumber for the King's troops and warning you not to raise a liberty pole in town.
evt-06-11-1775-battle-of-machias.prompt: What should the Machias settlers do about the Margaretta?

choices.text: Abandon the town and flee inland
Petition the Massachusetts legislature for guidance first
Board and seize the British schooner by force
Supply the lumber as demanded to avoid conflict

evt-06-11-1775-battle-of-machias.butterflyEffect: Local militia and townsmen stormed and captured the Margaretta in a bloody boarding action, the first naval capture of the Revolutionary War. Dubbed the 'Lexington of the Seas,' the victory encouraged colonial resistance at sea and foreshadowed the creation of the Continental Navy.

evt-1776-committee-of-five.scenario: Philadelphia, 11 June 1776. You are John Adams, just named to a five-man drafting committee. The declaration must bind thirteen quarrelsome colonies — and the committee looks to you, the revolution's loudest voice, to hold the pen.

choices.text: Insist Jefferson writes — a Virginian's pen will bind the South to the cause
Draft it yourself and dare Congress to soften it
Hand it to Franklin, whose fame will carry it in Europe

evt-1776-committee-of-five.butterflyEffect: Adams refused the pen and pushed it to Jefferson. The Virginian's draft — 'all men are created equal' — became the core of American identity and the template for more than a hundred later declarations of independence.

evt-06-11-1847-afonso-prince-imperial-of.scenario: It is June 1847 in Rio de Janeiro, and you are a courtier at the imperial palace as word spreads that the two-year-old Prince Afonso, heir to Emperor Pedro II, has died.
evt-06-11-1847-afonso-prince-imperial-of.prompt: What did his death mean for the succession of the Brazilian throne?

choices.text: His elder sister Isabel became heir presumptive to the Brazilian throne
Pedro II adopted a male heir from a noble family
The empire immediately transitioned toward republican government
The throne passed to a cousin in the Portuguese royal line

evt-06-11-1847-afonso-prince-imperial-of.butterflyEffect: With no surviving sons, Pedro II's daughter Isabel became heir presumptive. She later served as regent and, in 1888, signed the Lei Áurea abolishing slavery in Brazil during her father's absence abroad, though the monarchy itself was overthrown the following year.

evt-06-11-1914-1914-kenwood-house-ball.scenario: It is the night of 11 June 1914 at Kenwood House, London. Grand Duke Michael Mikhailovich of Russia is hosting a glittering ball for his daughter's coming-out, and King George V and Queen Mary are among the 2,000 guests watching a dance demonstration.
evt-06-11-1914-1914-kenwood-house-ball.prompt: What dance did Queen Mary specifically ask to see performed that evening?

choices.text: The tango
The waltz
The foxtrot
The quadrille

evt-06-11-1914-1914-kenwood-house-ball.butterflyEffect: Maurice Mouvet and Florence Walton performed the tango at Mary's request, marking the first royal command performance by North American dancers and helping legitimise the once-scandalous dance in British high society. Weeks later, the outbreak of the First World War swept away this world of grand aristocratic balls almost overnight.

evt-06-11-1917-alexander-of-greece.scenario: It is June 1917 and Allied powers are threatening to blockade Greece unless King Constantine I, suspected of pro-German sympathies, steps aside. His heir, Crown Prince George, is viewed with the same suspicion by the Allies.
evt-06-11-1917-alexander-of-greece.prompt: Who should the Allies insist take the Greek throne instead?

choices.text: Abolish the monarchy and form a republic
Crown Prince George, his heir apparent
His younger brother, Prince Nicholas
His second son, Alexander

evt-06-11-1917-alexander-of-greece.butterflyEffect: Constantine abdicated and his second son Alexander was installed as king, bypassing Crown Prince George entirely. Under Alexander, Venizelist Greece aligned fully with the Allies for the rest of the war, though Alexander's own brief reign ended in 1920 after a fatal monkey bite, paving the way for Constantine's return.

evt-06-11-1920-1920-republican-national-.scenario: It is June 1920 inside the Chicago Coliseum. Ballot after ballot has failed to produce a majority, and exhausted party bosses have retreated to a smoke-filled hotel room to settle on a compromise candidate.
evt-06-11-1920-1920-republican-national-.prompt: Which little-known senator do the party bosses settle on as the compromise nominee?

choices.text: Senator Warren G. Harding
Senator Hiram Johnson
General Leonard Wood
Governor Frank Lowden

evt-06-11-1920-1920-republican-national-.butterflyEffect: The deadlocked convention chose Ohio Senator Warren G. Harding, coining the phrase "smoke-filled room" for backroom deal-making. Harding won the presidency on a promise of "return to normalcy," but his administration was later engulfed by the Teapot Dome scandal, and his sudden death in 1923 brought Calvin Coolidge to power.

evt-06-11-1923-jasper-abraham-murder-cas.scenario: It is June 1923 in a Kenya Colony courtroom near Molo. British settler Jasper Abraham stands accused of murder after African labourer Kitosh died from a flogging Abraham ordered on his farm, and twelve fellow European settlers now sit as the jury.
evt-06-11-1923-jasper-abraham-murder-cas.prompt: What verdict does the all-European jury return against Abraham?

choices.text: Guilty of grievous hurt only
Not guilty, fully acquitted
Guilty of murder
Guilty of manslaughter with hard labour

evt-06-11-1923-jasper-abraham-murder-cas.butterflyEffect: The jury convicted Abraham only of the lesser charge of grievous hurt, and he received a two-year prison sentence rather than a murder conviction. The leniency of the verdict became a widely cited example of colonial double standards in Kenyan justice, fueling growing African political grievance in the years leading to organized resistance against settler rule.

evt-1944-normandy-linkup.scenario: Normandy, D+5. You command the Allied ground forces. Five beachheads have just fused into one 80-kilometre front, but you hold no deep-water port — and Channel storms are coming.
evt-1944-normandy-linkup.prompt: How do you keep 326,000 troops supplied?

choices.text: Tow prefabricated Mulberry harbours across the Channel and assemble them offshore
Land everything over open beaches and accept the storm losses
Halt the advance until Cherbourg's port is captured intact
Supply the entire front by air drop
