evt-1944-normandy-linkup.butterflyEffect: The artificial harbours — an idea mocked on the drawing board — moved millions of tonnes of supply without a captured port. The front held, broke out, and the war in Europe ended within eleven months.

evt-1963-jfk-civil-rights.scenario: The Oval Office, 11 June 1963. Alabama's governor blocked two Black students from enrolling this morning until federal troops arrived. Your aides warn that a national address tonight could cost the entire Southern vote.
evt-1963-jfk-civil-rights.prompt: You are President Kennedy. What do you do tonight?

choices.text: Go on live television and frame civil rights as a moral issue
Defer the question to Congress without public comment
Release a quiet written statement to the wire services

evt-1963-jfk-civil-rights.butterflyEffect: Kennedy spoke that night, largely improvising the ending — the first time a president called civil rights 'a moral issue.' The bill he announced became the Civil Rights Act of 1964, signed after his death.

evt-06-11-1963-bhikkhu.scenario: It is June 11, 1963, at a busy Saigon intersection. You are an American reporter tipped off that something significant is about to happen involving a Buddhist monk protesting the Diem government's persecution of Buddhists.
evt-06-11-1963-bhikkhu.prompt: What should you do as the scene unfolds before you?

choices.text: Photograph and document the event to record it for the world
Alert South Vietnamese police before anything happens
Leave immediately to avoid involvement
Physically intervene to stop the protest

evt-06-11-1963-bhikkhu.butterflyEffect: Malcolm Browne's photograph of Thích Quảng Đức's self-immolation shocked the world and exposed the brutality of the Diem regime's religious persecution. The image eroded American support for Diem and contributed to the coup that overthrew and killed him later that year.

evt-06-11-2001-timothy-mcveigh.scenario: It is the early morning of 11 June 2001 outside the federal prison in Terre Haute, Indiana. Reporters and victims' families gather as officials prepare to carry out the sentence handed down for the Oklahoma City bombing.
evt-06-11-2001-timothy-mcveigh.prompt: What happened to Timothy McVeigh that morning?

choices.text: He died in his cell of natural causes
He was transferred to a maximum-security facility for further appeals
He was executed by lethal injection
He was granted a last-minute stay of execution

evt-06-11-2001-timothy-mcveigh.butterflyEffect: McVeigh was executed by lethal injection, becoming the first person put to death by the federal government since 1963. The execution reignited national debate over capital punishment and closed the legal chapter on the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history, though its wounds shaped American counterterrorism policy for years afterward.

evt-06-11-2001-tesco-bomb-campaign.scenario: You are a Dorset detective in early 2001. A blackmailer calling themselves "Sally" has threatened to bomb Tesco stores unless modified Clubcards, rigged to dispense cash from ATMs, are hidden in local newspapers.
evt-06-11-2001-tesco-bomb-campaign.prompt: How do detectives finally close in on the blackmailer without risking the public?

choices.text: They relied on an informant inside Tesco head office
They covertly watched the ATMs where the rigged cards were used
They traced the demand letters through the newspaper's printer
They paid the ransom in full to draw him out later

evt-06-11-2001-tesco-bomb-campaign.butterflyEffect: Police covertly tracked the modified Clubcards to the cash machines where withdrawals were made, using surveillance to identify Robert Edward Dyer as he collected the money. He was arrested, convicted, and sentenced to 16 years, and the case became a textbook example for British police handling of extortion-by-retail-loyalty-scheme threats.

evt-06-11-2002-antonio-meucci.scenario: It is June 2002 and you are a member of the US House of Representatives voting on a resolution concerning the Italian immigrant inventor Antonio Meucci and his role in the telephone's invention.
evt-06-11-2002-antonio-meucci.prompt: What did the resolution formally acknowledge?

choices.text: A posthumous US patent awarded directly to Meucci
That the telephone patent should transfer to Meucci's heirs
That Alexander Graham Bell's 1876 patent was fraudulent and void
Meucci's contributions to the invention of the telephone, without overturning Bell's patent

evt-06-11-2002-antonio-meucci.butterflyEffect: House Resolution 269 was a symbolic, non-binding recognition of Meucci's pioneering work on voice communication devices decades before Bell's 1876 patent. It renewed public and Italian-American interest in his story and reignited debate over telephone history, but it did not legally alter Bell's patent or its recognition.

evt-06-11-2004-cassini-huygens.scenario: It is 11 June 2004. You are a mission scientist watching data stream in as the Cassini spacecraft makes its closest flyby of Saturn's outer moon Phoebe, just weeks before entering orbit around Saturn itself.
evt-06-11-2004-cassini-huygens.prompt: What did the flyby suggest about Phoebe's true origin?

choices.text: The remnant of a shattered planet
A fragment shed from Saturn's rings
A captured icy object from the Kuiper belt
A native moon that formed alongside Saturn

evt-06-11-2004-cassini-huygens.butterflyEffect: Cassini's images and density measurements supported the idea that Phoebe is not a native Saturnian moon but a captured icy body from the outer solar system, likely a former Kuiper belt object. The finding reshaped models of how Saturn's irregular moons were acquired and previewed the wealth of discoveries Cassini would make over its thirteen years orbiting the planet.

evt-06-11-2007-2007-chittagong-mudslides.scenario: It is early June 2007 and you are a local official in Chittagong, aware that experts have long warned illegal hill-cutting near the city's slums makes them dangerously vulnerable once the monsoon rains arrive.
evt-06-11-2007-2007-chittagong-mudslides.prompt: What should authorities have done to prevent disaster as the rains intensified?

choices.text: Encourage further hill-cutting to expand housing for the growing slum population
Focus solely on road repairs rather than slope stability
Wait until the monsoon season ended before assessing any risk
Enforce the existing ban on hill-cutting and relocate residents from the most at-risk slopes

evt-06-11-2007-2007-chittagong-mudslides.butterflyEffect: Despite prior warnings, illegal hill-cutting continued and slum settlements remained on unstable slopes. Days of heavy monsoon rain triggered mudslides that devastated these communities, and the tragedy pushed the government to promise stricter enforcement against hill-cutting, though implementation remained inconsistent in the years that followed.

evt-06-11-2008-stephen-harper.scenario: It is 11 June 2008 and you are seated in the House of Commons gallery, one of many residential school survivors watching Prime Minister Stephen Harper rise to address Parliament and the nation.
evt-06-11-2008-stephen-harper.prompt: What did Harper do in this historic address?

choices.text: Announced financial reparations but offered no apology
Resigned in protest against past governments' policies
Formally apologized on behalf of the government for the residential school system and its harms
Called for an independent judicial inquiry before making any statement

evt-06-11-2008-stephen-harper.butterflyEffect: Harper delivered the first formal apology by a Canadian prime minister for the government's role in the residential school system, acknowledging the harm done to Indigenous children and families. It ran alongside the Indian Residential Schools Settlement Agreement and helped pave the way for the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's work through the following decade, though survivors continued pressing for concrete follow-through.

evt-06-11-2008-prime-minister-of-canada.scenario: You sit in the House of Commons on 11 June 2008 as Prime Minister Stephen Harper rises to deliver a formal statement to Indigenous leaders and residential school survivors gathered in the chamber.
evt-06-11-2008-prime-minister-of-canada.prompt: What does Harper's historic statement formally apologize for?

choices.text: The internment of Japanese Canadians during the Second World War
The 1969 White Paper policy proposal
The government's operation of the Indian residential school system
Historic treaty land violations in British Columbia

evt-06-11-2008-prime-minister-of-canada.butterflyEffect: Harper apologized on behalf of the Government of Canada for the Indian residential school system, which had forcibly separated generations of Indigenous children from their families and cultures. The apology accompanied the work of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, whose 2015 final report and 94 Calls to Action shaped Canada's ongoing reconciliation efforts.

evt-06-11-2008-fermi-gamma-ray-space-tel.scenario: You are a mission scientist at Cape Canaveral on 11 June 2008, watching a Delta II rocket carry the newly built gamma-ray observatory, then still called GLAST, into low Earth orbit.
evt-06-11-2008-fermi-gamma-ray-space-tel.prompt: What major discovery does the telescope's Large Area Telescope go on to make?

choices.text: It found dozens of previously unknown gamma-ray pulsars
It discovered the first confirmed exoplanet
It photographed the surface of a black hole for the first time
It detected gravitational waves from colliding black holes

evt-06-11-2008-fermi-gamma-ray-space-tel.butterflyEffect: After launch the observatory was renamed the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, and its Large Area Telescope went on to discover dozens of new gamma-ray pulsars and map high-energy sources across the sky. Its ongoing survey has reshaped the study of active galactic nuclei and helped constrain models of dark matter.

evt-06-11-2012-2012-afghanistan-earthqua.scenario: It is 15 June 2012. You are coordinating rescue crews at Sayi Hazara, a northern Afghan village buried by a landslide after two earthquakes struck four days ago. Seventy-one people remain trapped under tons of rock and earth.
evt-06-11-2012-2012-afghanistan-earthqua.prompt: What decision did rescue teams ultimately make about the search?

choices.text: Call off the search after recovering only a handful of bodies
Continue digging for several more weeks with heavy machinery
Evacuate the area entirely and abandon recovery efforts immediately
Request an international excavation team and wait for its arrival

evt-06-11-2012-2012-afghanistan-earthqua.butterflyEffect: After four days of digging through unstable debris, crews recovered only five bodies and called off the search, leaving most victims unrecovered. The disaster underscored how landslide-prone mountain villages in Afghanistan remained acutely vulnerable, with rescue capacity unable to match the scale of sudden burial events.

evt-06-11-2013-hellenic-broadcasting-cor.scenario: It is June 2013 and you are Greek Prime Minister Antonis Samaras, under intense pressure from international creditors to slash public spending during the debt crisis. The state broadcaster ERT is seen as bloated and costly.
evt-06-11-2013-hellenic-broadcasting-cor.prompt: What do you do about ERT to satisfy austerity demands?

choices.text: Privatize ERT and sell it to a media conglomerate
Leave ERT's budget and staffing untouched
Shut down ERT immediately and lay off its staff
Gradually restructure ERT over several years

evt-06-11-2013-hellenic-broadcasting-cor.butterflyEffect: Samaras ordered ERT's immediate closure, cutting off broadcasts and roughly 2,700 jobs overnight. Outraged staff occupied the building and kept streaming online for years in protest, and after political backlash a successor broadcaster, NERIT, was created before ERT itself was eventually restored in 2015.

evt-06-12-1240-disputation-of-paris.scenario: It is 1240 in the court of King Louis IX of Paris. You are one of four rabbis summoned to answer Nicholas Donin's charges that the Talmud contains blasphemies against Christianity, with royal and church officials watching your every word.
evt-06-12-1240-disputation-of-paris.prompt: What ultimately happened to the Talmud as a result of this disputation?

choices.text: Nicholas Donin was executed for false accusations
It was condemned and copies were publicly burned in Paris
All Jews were expelled from France immediately afterward
It was declared free of blasphemy and fully exonerated

evt-06-12-1240-disputation-of-paris.butterflyEffect: Although the rabbis mounted a vigorous defense, church authorities ruled against the Talmud, and in 1242 some twenty-four cartloads of Talmudic manuscripts were burned in Paris. The episode set a template for later church-sponsored trials and burnings of Jewish texts across medieval Europe.

evt-06-12-1775-thomas-gage.scenario: You are a Boston shopkeeper on 12 June 1775, reading Governor Thomas Gage's freshly posted proclamation. It declares martial law across Massachusetts and offers pardon to any rebel who lays down arms—except for two named ringleaders.
evt-06-12-1775-thomas-gage.prompt: Which two rebel leaders does Gage's proclamation deny any pardon?

choices.text: Samuel Adams and Paul Revere
John Adams and Samuel Adams
Samuel Adams and John Hancock
John Hancock and Paul Revere

evt-06-12-1775-thomas-gage.butterflyEffect: Gage named Samuel Adams and John Hancock as unpardonable traitors, marking them as the Crown's most wanted men. The proclamation hardened colonial defiance rather than pacifying it, and days later British and colonial forces clashed at Bunker Hill, pushing Massachusetts irreversibly toward open war.

evt-06-12-1776-fifth-virginia-convention.scenario: It's June 12, 1776, in Williamsburg. You sit among the delegates of the Fifth Virginia Convention, debating George Mason's draft declaring the natural rights of all men, weeks before independence is even declared.
evt-06-12-1776-fifth-virginia-convention.prompt: What principle does the convention adopt as the basis of legitimate government?

choices.text: Government derives its just powers from the consent of the governed
Virginia's royal governor retains ultimate authority
The Anglican Church remains the established state religion
Only property owners may hold any rights at all

evt-06-12-1776-fifth-virginia-convention.butterflyEffect: The convention adopted the Virginia Declaration of Rights, asserting that all men are 'by nature equally free' and that government exists by consent of the governed. Thomas Jefferson drew directly on its language weeks later while drafting the Declaration of Independence, and it later shaped the U.S. Bill of Rights.

evt-06-12-1798-french-invasion-of-malta.scenario: It's June 1798. Napoleon's massive invasion fleet, en route to Egypt, anchors off Malta and demands the Knights Hospitaller surrender the island. You stand beside Grand Master Hompesch as he must decide how to respond.
evt-06-12-1798-french-invasion-of-malta.prompt: How does the Grand Master respond to Napoleon's ultimatum?

choices.text: Appeal to Britain for an emergency naval rescue
Surrender within days after only token resistance and internal defections
Order the fortress guns to fight to the last man
Flee immediately with the treasury to Sicily

evt-06-12-1798-french-invasion-of-malta.butterflyEffect: With French-born knights refusing to fight their countrymen and the order's defenses hollowed out, Hompesch capitulated after brief skirmishes, and Malta fell to France almost bloodlessly. French rule proved so unpopular that Maltese rebels, backed by the British Navy, expelled them within two years, beginning over 160 years of British control of the island.

evt-06-12-1864-union-american-civil-war.scenario: It is June 12, 1864, days after wave after wave of Union soldiers were slaughtered assaulting entrenched Confederate lines at Cold Harbor. You serve on Grant's staff as he weighs the army's next move.
evt-06-12-1864-union-american-civil-war.prompt: What does Grant order after the disaster at Cold Harbor?

choices.text: Renew frontal assaults until Lee's line breaks
Withdraw north toward Washington to regroup
Secretly march the army south across the James River toward Petersburg
Sue for a negotiated armistice with Lee

evt-06-12-1864-union-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Grant disengaged and marched the Army of the Potomac south, crossing the James River to strike at Petersburg, a vital rail hub supplying Richmond. The resulting Siege of Petersburg dragged on for nearly ten months, grinding down Confederate manpower and setting up Lee's eventual surrender at Appomattox in April 1865.

evt-06-12-1963-cleopatra-1963-film.scenario: It is 12 June 1963 at the New York premiere of Cleopatra. You are a 20th Century Fox executive watching flashbulbs pop for Elizabeth Taylor, aware the production has already spiraled into the most expensive film ever made.
evt-06-12-1963-cleopatra-1963-film.prompt: What real consequence followed for the studio from the film's runaway costs?

choices.text: It was pulled from theaters after one week
Elizabeth Taylor won the Academy Award for the role
It nearly bankrupted 20th Century Fox despite strong ticket sales
The film was banned from release in the United States

evt-06-12-1963-cleopatra-1963-film.butterflyEffect: Despite being the highest-grossing film of 1963, Cleopatra's astronomical budget meant it still lost money and nearly bankrupted 20th Century Fox. The debacle forced a studio shake-up and tighter budget controls across Hollywood, while the on-set romance between Taylor and Richard Burton became a global tabloid sensation.

evt-06-12-1967-supreme-court-of-the-unit.scenario: It is June 1967 and you are arguing before the U.S. Supreme Court on behalf of Richard and Mildred Loving, an interracial couple convicted under Virginia's ban on interracial marriage.
evt-06-12-1967-supreme-court-of-the-unit.prompt: What is your core constitutional argument against Virginia's law?

choices.text: The law violates federal commerce regulations
The law only needs legislative repeal, not judicial action
The law should be left to individual states to decide
The law violates the Fourteenth Amendment's equal protection and due process guarantees

evt-06-12-1967-supreme-court-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: The Court ruled unanimously in Loving v. Virginia that bans on interracial marriage violated the Fourteenth Amendment's Equal Protection and Due Process Clauses, striking down such laws in the sixteen states that still had them. The ruling's reasoning was later cited directly in Obergefell v. Hodges (2015), which legalized same-sex marriage nationwide.

evt-06-12-1978-david-berkowitz.scenario: It's June 12, 1978, in a Brooklyn courtroom. David Berkowitz, the self-proclaimed 'Son of Sam,' stands before the judge for sentencing after pleading guilty to six murders that terrorized New York City.
evt-06-12-1978-david-berkowitz.prompt: What sentence does the judge impose for the Son of Sam killings?

choices.text: Death by execution
A single term of life without parole
Six consecutive terms of 25 years to life
Indefinite commitment to a psychiatric hospital

evt-06-12-1978-david-berkowitz.butterflyEffect: Berkowitz received six consecutive terms of 25 years to life, effectively guaranteeing he would die in prison. The frenzy over the case, and fears he might profit from book or movie deals, pushed New York to pass the first 'Son of Sam law' barring criminals from cashing in on their crimes' notoriety; many other states soon copied it.

evt-06-12-1987-tear-down-this-wall.scenario: It is June 1987 and you are helping draft Ronald Reagan's speech for the Brandenburg Gate. State Department officials warn that directly challenging Gorbachev over the Berlin Wall is too provocative and want the line cut.
evt-06-12-1987-tear-down-this-wall.prompt: Should the line demanding Gorbachev tear down the wall stay in the speech?

choices.text: Replace it with praise for existing reforms
Soften it to a vague call for 'greater openness'
Remove it to avoid provoking the Soviets
Keep it in, over the objections of cautious advisors

evt-06-12-1987-tear-down-this-wall.butterflyEffect: Reagan overruled his advisors and delivered the line anyway, and it became one of the most quoted moments of his presidency. Though the Wall did not fall for another two years, the speech was later remembered as a defining Cold War moment once Germany was reunified in 1990.

evt-06-12-1994-boeing-777.scenario: It is 12 June 1994 at Paine Field, Washington. You are a Boeing test engineer watching the prototype 777 lift off, carrying a flight control system unlike anything Boeing has flown before.
evt-06-12-1994-boeing-777.prompt: What design choice made this maiden flight historic for Boeing?

choices.text: The first supersonic airliner design
Fully digital fly-by-wire flight controls
Fully autonomous, pilotless operation
A four-engine layout for extra range

evt-06-12-1994-boeing-777.butterflyEffect: The 777 was Boeing's first airliner with fully digital fly-by-wire flight controls, replacing traditional cables and hydraulics with electronic signaling. It entered service with United Airlines in 1995, went on to become the best-selling wide-body twinjet in history, and its long-range ETOPS certification let airlines retire aging three- and four-engine jets on overwater routes.

evt-06-12-1999-nato-bombing-of-yugoslavi.scenario: It is 12 June 1999 near Pristina airport in Kosovo. You are British General Sir Michael Jackson, commanding NATO's advance force, and US Supreme Allied Commander Wesley Clark orders you to block the runway before Russian troops can occupy it.
evt-06-12-1999-nato-bombing-of-yugoslavi.prompt: What did General Jackson actually do when given the order?

choices.text: He called in airstrikes on the runway
He ordered his men to open fire on the Russian column
He refused the order, avoiding a direct clash with Russian troops
He withdrew all NATO forces from Kosovo immediately

evt-06-12-1999-nato-bombing-of-yugoslavi.butterflyEffect: Jackson refused, reportedly telling Clark he was "not going to start the Third World War for you." The standoff was resolved diplomatically instead, with Russian troops given a role within the NATO-led KFOR peacekeeping mission rather than a separate sector, and the Kosovo peacekeeping operation proceeded without a direct NATO-Russia clash.

evt-06-12-2009-2009-iranian-presidential.scenario: It is the morning of 13 June 2009 in Tehran. State media has just announced Ahmadinejad's landslide win, and you are among the crowds gathering in disbelief, ready to march for challenger Mir-Hossein Mousavi.
evt-06-12-2009-2009-iranian-presidential.prompt: What color did the protest movement adopt as its symbol?

choices.text: Red, symbolizing revolution
The colors of the Iranian flag only
White, worn as a sign of mourning
Green, Mousavi's campaign color

evt-06-12-2009-2009-iranian-presidential.butterflyEffect: Protesters rallied under green, Mousavi's campaign color, giving the uprising its name: the Green Movement. Security forces cracked down violently, killing and jailing demonstrators, and while the movement was suppressed within months, it foreshadowed the social-media-driven uprisings of the Arab Spring two years later.

evt-06-12-2010-abby-sunderland.scenario: You are aboard a search vessel scanning the remote southern Indian Ocean on 12 June 2010. Sixteen-year-old sailor Abby Sunderland's yacht Wild Eyes has been dismasted in heavy seas, far from any shipping lane, and her emergency beacons are blaring.
evt-06-12-2010-abby-sunderland.prompt: What vessel actually reaches Sunderland to complete her rescue?

choices.text: A US Navy destroyer patrolling nearby
A commercial cruise liner rerouted to assist
An Australian coast guard helicopter
A French fishing vessel diverted to her position

evt-06-12-2010-abby-sunderland.butterflyEffect: A French fishing boat, the Ile de la Reunion, diverted hundreds of miles to retrieve her from the crippled yacht. The rescue reignited debate over the safety of youth solo-sailing records, prompting several countries to tighten age restrictions on offshore attempts.

evt-06-12-2018-united-states.scenario: It is 12 June 2018 on Sentosa Island, Singapore. You are part of the American delegation as President Trump prepares to shake hands with Kim Jong-un, the first sitting US president to meet a North Korean leader.
evt-06-12-2018-united-states.prompt: As a goodwill gesture after the summit, what did Trump agree to suspend?

choices.text: All economic sanctions on North Korea
US troop deployments to Japan
Joint military exercises with South Korea
Diplomatic recognition of South Korea

evt-06-12-2018-united-states.butterflyEffect: Trump announced he would halt joint US-South Korea military exercises, a move that startled the Pentagon and Seoul, who had not been consulted. The summit produced only a vague joint statement on denuclearization, talks later stalled, and North Korea resumed missile tests within a few years.

evt-06-13-1514-henry-grace-a-dieu.scenario: You are a shipwright at the Woolwich dockyard on 13 June 1514, watching the launch of Henry Grace à Dieu, a vessel already whispered to be the largest warship afloat.
evt-06-13-1514-henry-grace-a-dieu.prompt: What role will this great ship serve for Henry VIII?

choices.text: A merchant vessel for the wool trade
Decommissioned immediately after launch
Flagship of the English fleet
A ceremonial barge used only for river pageants

evt-06-13-1514-henry-grace-a-dieu.butterflyEffect: Henry Grace à Dieu became Henry VIII's flagship, a floating symbol of Tudor naval ambition alongside the Mary Rose. Its scale pushed English shipbuilders toward ever larger warships, shaping the growth of the Tudor navy in the decades that followed.

evt-06-13-1525-martin-luther.scenario: You are Martin Luther in Wittenberg in 1525, a former monk who has spent years arguing that clergy should be free to marry. Katharina von Bora, a former nun who fled her convent, is now part of your household.
evt-06-13-1525-martin-luther.prompt: What does Luther do to make his theological argument for clerical marriage concrete?

choices.text: He marries her secretly and denies it publicly
He arranges for Katharina to marry another reformer instead
He remains celibate to avoid controversy
He marries Katharina von Bora publicly

evt-06-13-1525-martin-luther.butterflyEffect: Luther married Katharina von Bora in a public ceremony, scandalizing critics but setting a lasting precedent for Protestant clergy. Their marriage and six children became a model of the Lutheran pastor's household, helping normalize clerical marriage across Protestant Europe.

evt-06-13-1805-lewis-and-clark-expeditio.scenario: You are Meriwether Lewis, scouting ahead of the main party along the Missouri River on 13 June 1805. A distant roar grows louder, and mist rises above the plain ahead of you.
evt-06-13-1805-lewis-and-clark-expeditio.prompt: What landmark do you become the first white American to document?

choices.text: The confluence of the Missouri and Yellowstone Rivers
Celilo Falls on the Columbia River
The Continental Divide
The Great Falls of the Missouri River

evt-06-13-1805-lewis-and-clark-expeditio.butterflyEffect: Lewis had reached the Great Falls of the Missouri River, a series of five cascades that forced the expedition into a grueling overland portage of nearly a month. The delay pushed the Corps of Discovery dangerously close to winter before they could cross the Continental Divide, reshaping their timetable for the rest of the journey.

evt-06-13-1881-jeannette-expedition.scenario: You are a sailor aboard the USS Jeannette in the Arctic pack ice, June 1881. The hull has just been crushed by the ice under Lieutenant Commander George De Long's command, and the ship is sinking beneath you.
evt-06-13-1881-jeannette-expedition.prompt: With the Jeannette lost, what does the crew do to try to survive?

choices.text: They stay put and wait for a Russian rescue ship
They attempt to sail directly north to reach the pole on foot
They abandon all equipment and swim for open water
They drag the ship's boats and supplies across the ice toward the Siberian mainland

evt-06-13-1881-jeannette-expedition.butterflyEffect: The men dragged small boats and supplies across the ice toward the Siberian coast, splitting into three groups. Most, including De Long, died of starvation and exposure in the Lena Delta; only a handful survived. Wreckage later found off Greenland helped confirm a transpolar drift current, inspiring Fridtjof Nansen's Fram expedition.

evt-06-13-1916-world-war-i.scenario: It is 13 June 1916 near Ypres. You are a Canadian infantryman ordered to retake the trenches at Mont Sorrel that German forces seized nearly two weeks earlier.
evt-06-13-1916-world-war-i.prompt: What tactic secures the Canadian recapture of the lost ground?

choices.text: A flanking cavalry charge
A silent night raid without artillery support
A gas attack across no man's land
A massed artillery barrage followed by a dawn infantry assault

evt-06-13-1916-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: A massed artillery bombardment followed by a coordinated infantry assault, led by Arthur Currie's brigade, restored the line at Mont Sorrel and recovered the ground lost on 2 June. The victory gave the Canadian Corps its first major independent success of the war, building a reputation it carried into the far bloodier fighting at the Somme.

evt-06-13-1935-boxing.scenario: You are ringside at the Madison Square Garden Bowl on 13 June 1935. James Braddock, a journeyman fighter once on public relief, steps into the ring against heavyweight champion Max Baer as a massive underdog.
evt-06-13-1935-boxing.prompt: What is the outcome of this heavyweight title fight?

choices.text: The fight is ruled a draw
Baer knocks out Braddock in the early rounds
Braddock wins by unanimous decision
Braddock loses by decision but is praised for lasting the distance

evt-06-13-1935-boxing.butterflyEffect: Braddock won by unanimous decision, one of boxing's greatest upsets, earning him the nickname "Cinderella Man" as a symbol of Depression-era hope. He lost the title to Joe Louis in 1937, but his win remains a defining sports story of the era.

evt-06-13-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 13 June 1944 and you command a tank near the head of a British armoured column halted in the streets of Villers-Bocage, Normandy, when a lone German Tiger under Michael Wittmann opens fire from close range.
evt-06-13-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What follows the ambush at the head of the British column?

choices.text: The column pushes on and captures the town
American reinforcements arrive to relieve the column
British forces withdraw from Villers-Bocage by nightfall
The Germans surrender the town by evening

evt-06-13-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Wittmann's Tiger destroyed much of the column's lead armour before British anti-tank guns and Cromwells drove the Germans back later that day, but 7th Armoured Division still withdrew from the town by nightfall. The failed advance stalled the British attempt to outflank Caen and prolonged the Normandy stalemate for weeks.

evt-06-13-1952-catalina-affair.scenario: You are a signals officer aboard a Swedish Air Force DC-3 over the Baltic Sea on 13 June 1952, listening in on Soviet radio traffic, when two MiG fighters suddenly close in on your aircraft.
evt-06-13-1952-catalina-affair.prompt: What follows this encounter over international waters?

choices.text: The Swedish plane is forced to land inside Soviet territory
The DC-3 is shot down over international waters
The DC-3 outmaneuvers the fighters and returns undamaged
The MiGs escort the plane safely back to Sweden

evt-06-13-1952-catalina-affair.butterflyEffect: The DC-3 was shot down with the loss of its entire crew, and days later a Swedish Catalina searching for survivors was also attacked, giving the crisis its name. The Soviet Union denied responsibility for decades, only admitting the shootdown in 1991, and the wreck was not located until 2003.

evt-06-13-1983-pioneer-10.scenario: You monitor telemetry at NASA Ames Research Center on 13 June 1983 as Pioneer 10's distance readout ticks past a marker no human-made object has ever crossed before.
evt-06-13-1983-pioneer-10.prompt: What milestone does Pioneer 10 achieve by crossing this boundary?

choices.text: First spacecraft to enter a stable Earth orbit
First man-made object to leave the orbit of the outer planets
First probe to photograph Neptune's surface
First probe to reach the asteroid belt

evt-06-13-1983-pioneer-10.butterflyEffect: Pioneer 10 became the first spacecraft to travel beyond the orbit of the outermost known planet at the time, effectively leaving the region of the classical Solar System. It kept transmitting data until contact was lost in 2003, helping scientists understand the outer heliosphere ahead of the Voyager probes.

evt-06-13-1997-timothy-mcveigh.scenario: It is 13 June 1997 in a Denver courtroom. You are a juror who has just convicted Timothy McVeigh of the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing and must now decide his sentence.
evt-06-13-1997-timothy-mcveigh.prompt: What sentence does the jury hand down?

choices.text: Life imprisonment without parole
A lengthy prison term with parole eligibility
Commitment to a psychiatric institution
Death by execution

evt-06-13-1997-timothy-mcveigh.butterflyEffect: The jury sentenced McVeigh to death, and he was executed by lethal injection in June 2001, the first federal execution in the United States in 38 years. The bombing and trial spurred new federal anti-terrorism legislation and lasting security changes at government buildings nationwide.

evt-06-13-2000-mehmet-ali-agca.scenario: You are an Italian justice ministry official in 2000. Pope John Paul II has publicly forgiven the man who shot him in 1981, and pressure is mounting to grant Mehmet Ali Ağca clemency after nearly two decades in an Italian prison.
evt-06-13-2000-mehmet-ali-agca.prompt: After Italy pardons and releases Ağca, what actually happens to him next?

choices.text: He is handed over to the Vatican for trial under canon law
He is granted full freedom and settles quietly in Italy
He is deported to Bulgaria, where his conspirators were based
He is extradited to Turkey to serve his sentence for Abdi İpekçi's murder

evt-06-13-2000-mehmet-ali-agca.butterflyEffect: Rather than walking free, Ağca was extradited to Turkey, where he still owed time for the 1979 murder of journalist Abdi İpekçi. He served additional years there before his eventual release in 2010, and the case remained a touchstone for debates over political violence and papal forgiveness.

evt-06-13-2002-anti-ballistic-missile-tr.scenario: You are a diplomat in Moscow on 13 June 2002, as Washington's six-month withdrawal notice from the 1972 Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty formally takes effect, ending three decades of mutual restraint on missile defense.
evt-06-13-2002-anti-ballistic-missile-tr.prompt: What does the US do with its newfound freedom from the treaty's limits?

choices.text: It deploys nuclear missiles across NATO Europe
It signs a new bilateral treaty with Russia limiting ABM systems
It rejoins the ABM Treaty under revised terms
It deploys the Ground-Based Midcourse Defense system in Alaska and California

evt-06-13-2002-anti-ballistic-missile-tr.butterflyEffect: The US built out the Ground-Based Midcourse Defense system in Alaska and California, alongside the sea-based Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense System. Russia responded by maintaining and modernizing its own A-135 system around Moscow, and the collapse of the ABM framework became a lasting sticking point in arms-control relations between the two powers.

evt-06-13-2007-2007-al-askari-mosque-bom.scenario: It is the morning of 13 June 2007 in Samarra. You are an Iraqi security official as insurgents detonate a second bomb at the al-Askari shrine, toppling its two minarets and reviving memories of the 2006 dome bombing that triggered nationwide sectarian killings.
evt-06-13-2007-2007-al-askari-mosque-bom.prompt: What immediate step do authorities take to head off a repeat of that violence?

choices.text: Detain local Sunni leaders without investigation
Leave the response entirely to local police
Impose a curfew and deploy additional troops
Open the shrine immediately for public mourning

evt-06-13-2007-2007-al-askari-mosque-bom.butterflyEffect: Iraqi and coalition forces moved quickly to impose curfews and deploy extra troops in Samarra and Baghdad, and the feared wave of mass sectarian reprisals seen in 2006 was largely averted. The attack nonetheless deepened distrust in the security gains claimed during the ongoing US troop surge.

evt-06-13-2007-al-askari-shrine.scenario: It is 13 June 2007 in Samarra, Iraq. You guard the al-Askari Shrine, already scarred by a 2006 bombing that destroyed its golden dome, when a fresh explosion tears through the site's remaining minarets.
evt-06-13-2007-al-askari-shrine.prompt: What follows this second attack across Iraq?

choices.text: Calm prevails and no reprisals occur
Sectarian reprisal violence spikes and curfews are imposed
The attackers are captured within hours and peace is restored
Sunni and Shia leaders jointly rebuild the shrine within days

evt-06-13-2007-al-askari-shrine.butterflyEffect: The bombing destroyed the shrine's two minarets and triggered a fresh wave of sectarian reprisal attacks between Sunni and Shia communities, deepening Iraq's civil conflict. The government imposed curfews and tightened security around Shia holy sites, and reconstruction of the shrine took years.

evt-06-13-2010-hayabusa.scenario: You are a JAXA engineer in the Australian outback on 13 June 2010, watching a small capsule streak down under parachute after Hayabusa's seven-year round trip to the asteroid Itokawa.
evt-06-13-2010-hayabusa.prompt: What do scientists confirm after opening the recovered capsule?

choices.text: Only camera and instrument data, with no physical sample
The capsule is empty due to a landing failure
Ice crystals mistaken for asteroid dust
Tiny grains of genuine asteroidal material from Itokawa

evt-06-13-2010-hayabusa.butterflyEffect: Inside were roughly 1,500 tiny grains of rocky material, confirmed as the first-ever sample returned from an asteroid's surface. The success proved sample-return technology from small bodies and directly paved the way for the more ambitious Hayabusa2 mission to asteroid Ryugu.

evt-06-13-2011-june-2011-christchurch-ea.scenario: You are a civil engineer in Christchurch on 13 June 2011. A fresh magnitude-6.0 quake has struck the already-battered city, just months after February's devastating tremor, and cracks are spreading through buildings authorities had hoped to soon reopen.
evt-06-13-2011-june-2011-christchurch-ea.prompt: What decision do authorities make about the central city in response?

choices.text: They relocate the capital of New Zealand temporarily
They declare the earthquake risk over and lift all restrictions
They extend the central city cordon instead of reopening it
They immediately reopen the CBD to reassure residents

evt-06-13-2011-june-2011-christchurch-ea.butterflyEffect: Officials extended the CBD 'red zone' cordon rather than allowing the planned reopening, judging the cumulative damage too dangerous. The repeated aftershocks ultimately led to the demolition of hundreds of buildings, including much of the historic cathedral, reshaping Christchurch's rebuild for years afterward.

evt-06-13-2018-volkswagen.scenario: It is June 2018 and you sit on Volkswagen's board in Wolfsburg. Prosecutors in Braunschweig have just imposed a one-billion-euro fine over the diesel emissions cheating scandal first exposed in 2015.
evt-06-13-2018-volkswagen.prompt: How does Volkswagen respond to the fine?

choices.text: Pay the fine without contesting it
Declare bankruptcy to avoid payment
Appeal the fine through the German courts
Sue individual engineers to recover the cost

evt-06-13-2018-volkswagen.butterflyEffect: Volkswagen paid the fine without appeal, closing the corporate criminal probe in Germany while individual prosecutions of executives like Martin Winterkorn continued separately. Dieselgate ultimately cost the company over $30 billion worldwide and pushed it to accelerate its shift toward electric vehicles.

evt-06-13-2023-kwara-boat-disaster.scenario: You are a wedding guest on the banks of the Niger River near Pategi in June 2023. Heavy rain has stranded your group, and the only way to reach the celebration is a wooden boat already crowded with passengers and their motorcycles.
evt-06-13-2023-kwara-boat-disaster.prompt: What is the safest choice as the overloaded boat prepares to depart?

choices.text: Wait for a later, lighter-loaded trip across the river
Swim across instead of waiting for any boat
Board anyway since the crossing is short
Insist on adding more motorcycles to save a second trip

evt-06-13-2023-kwara-boat-disaster.butterflyEffect: Overloaded far beyond safe capacity, the boat capsized and split apart in the river, killing over a hundred people. The tragedy renewed calls in Nigeria for enforcement of boat capacity limits and safety equipment on inland waterways, where such disasters have recurred for years.

evt-06-13-2023-2023-nottingham-attacks.scenario: It is the early hours of 13 June 2023 in Nottingham. You are a police officer responding to reports of stabbings and a stolen van driven into people at a bus stop before the attacker, Valdo Calocane, is arrested.
evt-06-13-2023-2023-nottingham-attacks.prompt: What follows once Calocane is charged over the attacks?

choices.text: The case is dropped for lack of evidence
He is convicted of murder
He pleads guilty to manslaughter due to diminished responsibility
He is found not guilty and released

evt-06-13-2023-2023-nottingham-attacks.butterflyEffect: Calocane pleaded guilty to manslaughter by reason of diminished responsibility rather than murder, owing to his diagnosed schizophrenia, and was given a hospital order. The outcome provoked public outrage and triggered inquiries into repeated failures by mental health and police services to act on earlier warnings about him.

evt-06-13-2025-twelve-day-war.scenario: You are an Israeli defense planner on 13 June 2025, watching the first wave of surprise strikes hit Iranian nuclear and military sites, killing senior commanders and scientists in the opening hours of what will become the Twelve-Day War.
evt-06-13-2025-twelve-day-war.prompt: How does Iran respond in the hours that follow the strikes?

choices.text: It launches over 550 ballistic missiles and 1,000 drones at Israel
It immediately requests a ceasefire through the United Nations
It formally declares war on the United States
It blockades the Strait of Hormuz to shipping

evt-06-13-2025-twelve-day-war.butterflyEffect: Iran launched over 550 ballistic missiles and more than 1,000 drones at Israeli targets, hitting civilian areas, a hospital, and military sites. The escalation drew in the United States, which bombed three Iranian nuclear facilities on 22 June before Iran struck a US base in Qatar; a US-brokered ceasefire finally halted the fighting on 24 June.

evt-06-14-1381-peasants-revolt.scenario: It is 14 June 1381, and you are a royal guard inside the Tower of London as Wat Tyler's rebels breach the walls, hunting for the King's most hated ministers hiding within.
evt-06-14-1381-peasants-revolt.prompt: Who do the rebels find and kill inside the Tower?

choices.text: King Richard II himself, captured while hiding in the keep
Archbishop Simon Sudbury and Treasurer Robert Hales, blamed for the poll tax
Foreign merchants who had taken refuge in the Tower's storerooms
Only the prison guards, freeing all inmates without further violence

evt-06-14-1381-peasants-revolt.butterflyEffect: The rebels dragged out Archbishop Simon Sudbury, also serving as Lord Chancellor, and Treasurer Robert Hales, and beheaded both on Tower Hill, blaming them for the despised poll tax. The killings shocked the fourteen-year-old Richard II, who met the rebels at Smithfield the next day, where Wat Tyler was killed and the revolt swiftly collapsed.

evt-06-14-1644-first-english-civil-war.scenario: You serve under Prince Maurice outside Lyme Regis in the spring of 1644, where weeks of Royalist assaults have failed to break the small Parliamentary garrison, and word arrives that the Earl of Essex's relief army is closing in.
evt-06-14-1644-first-english-civil-war.prompt: What did Prince Maurice decide to do as Essex's relieving force approached?

choices.text: Abandon the siege and withdraw his forces
Negotiate the town's surrender in exchange for safe passage
Launch one final all-out assault regardless of losses
Burn the town before retreating inland

evt-06-14-1644-first-english-civil-war.butterflyEffect: On 14 June 1644 Maurice abandoned the siege and withdrew rather than risk being trapped between the town and Essex's advancing army. The relief preserved a vital Parliamentary port in the west, denying Royalists a foothold to land men and supplies from abroad.

evt-06-14-1646-franco-spanish-war-1635-1.scenario: You serve under the Duke of Brézé, commanding a French fleet blockading the besieged Tuscan port of Orbetello in June 1646, when a Spanish relief fleet appears on the horizon.
evt-06-14-1646-franco-spanish-war-1635-1.prompt: What happens when the French and Spanish fleets clash off Orbetello?

choices.text: The entire Spanish fleet is captured and towed to a French port
The French fleet annihilates the Spanish relief force outright
The French withdraw without engaging, letting the Spanish pass unopposed
The battle is inconclusive, Brézé is killed, and Spain manages to resupply the garrison

evt-06-14-1646-franco-spanish-war-1635-1.butterflyEffect: The battle ended inconclusively, but the young and talented Duke of Brézé was killed, a serious loss for French naval leadership. The Spanish fleet succeeded in resupplying the besieged garrison, and the French were soon forced to abandon the siege of Orbetello altogether.

evt-06-14-1777-second-continental-congre.scenario: It is 14 June 1777 in Philadelphia, and you sit among the delegates of the Second Continental Congress, debating what emblem should represent the fledgling United States on its ships and in its forts.
evt-06-14-1777-second-continental-congre.prompt: What flag design do the delegates vote to adopt for the new nation?

choices.text: A rattlesnake coiled over thirteen stripes with the words 'Don't Tread on Me'
A plain blue field with a single large white star
The Grand Union Flag, keeping the British canton in the corner
Thirteen alternating red and white stripes with thirteen white stars on a blue field

evt-06-14-1777-second-continental-congre.butterflyEffect: The Flag Resolution of 14 June 1777 declared that the flag would have thirteen alternating red and white stripes and thirteen white stars on a blue field, without specifying their exact arrangement. The date is now observed annually in the United States as Flag Day, and the design's open wording allowed decades of variation in star patterns before later standardization.

evt-06-14-1800-war-of-the-second-coaliti.scenario: It is the afternoon of 14 June 1800 near Marengo, Italy. Austrian forces under General Melas have driven your French army into a chaotic retreat, and Napoleon's entire Italian campaign seems on the verge of collapse.
evt-06-14-1800-war-of-the-second-coaliti.prompt: What turns the battle back in France's favor before nightfall?

choices.text: Murat's reserves outflank the Austrians from the north
Napoleon personally leads a cavalry charge that breaks the Austrian line
The Austrians run out of ammunition and withdraw on their own
General Desaix arrives with reinforcements and launches a counterattack

evt-06-14-1800-war-of-the-second-coaliti.butterflyEffect: General Louis Desaix marched his division back to the field and led a devastating counterattack that shattered the exhausted Austrians, though Desaix himself was killed. The victory secured Napoleon's grip on northern Italy and his political standing as First Consul, paving the way toward his eventual coronation as Emperor.

evt-06-14-1846-sonoma-california.scenario: It is dawn on 14 June 1846 in Sonoma, California. You are one of about thirty American settlers who fear Mexican authorities are about to expel foreigners from the territory, and you have just surrounded the home of the local Mexican military commander.
evt-06-14-1846-sonoma-california.prompt: What do the settlers do to the Mexican garrison commander in Sonoma?

choices.text: Burn the local mission to provoke a Mexican response
Arrest him and raise a homemade flag declaring an independent republic
Wait quietly for the U.S. Army to arrive first
Petition him peacefully for Mexican citizenship rights

evt-06-14-1846-sonoma-california.butterflyEffect: The settlers arrested General Mariano Vallejo and raised a homemade flag bearing a grizzly bear, declaring the independent California Republic. The republic lasted barely a month before U.S. forces arrived amid the Mexican-American War, but the bear flag design survived to become California's state flag.

evt-06-14-1940-soviet-ultimatum-to-lithu.scenario: It is the night of 14 June 1940. You serve in the Lithuanian government as Moscow delivers an ultimatum: admit an unlimited number of Soviet troops and accept a new pro-Soviet cabinet, or face the consequences.
evt-06-14-1940-soviet-ultimatum-to-lithu.prompt: What does Lithuania's leadership decide to do about the ultimatum?

choices.text: Declare neutrality and request German protection
Reject it and appeal to the League of Nations
Accept the ultimatum to avoid armed conflict
Mobilize the army and resist by force

evt-06-14-1940-soviet-ultimatum-to-lithu.butterflyEffect: The government chose to accept rather than fight, and the Red Army occupied the country within days. A puppet government was installed, rigged elections followed, and Lithuania was formally annexed into the Soviet Union by August 1940, beginning five decades of Soviet rule that did not end until 1990.

evt-06-14-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 14 June 1944, and you command a British armored column pushing toward Caen through the town of Villers-Bocage, where German Tiger tanks have just inflicted heavy losses on your advance.
evt-06-14-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What does British command decide to do about the drive on Caen?

choices.text: Push forward into Caen regardless of losses
Request immediate American reinforcements to continue
Call off the attack and pull the armored column back
Bypass Caen entirely with an amphibious landing

evt-06-14-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: British forces called off the flanking attack and withdrew, ending the attempt to seize Caen quickly. The city instead became the center of a grinding, weeks-long battle of attrition that delayed the Allied breakout from Normandy until Operation Cobra in late July.

evt-06-14-1966-holy-see.scenario: You are a parish priest in June 1966, reading a startling bulletin from Rome: the Vatican has just acted on the Index Librorum Prohibitorum, the list of forbidden books that has shaped Catholic reading for over four centuries.
evt-06-14-1966-holy-see.prompt: What did the Vatican do with the centuries-old Index of banned books?

choices.text: Abolished it entirely, ending its binding authority
Expanded it to include new categories of media like film and radio
Transferred its enforcement solely to local bishops with no change in scope
Replaced it with a mandatory approval process for all new Catholic books

evt-06-14-1966-holy-see.butterflyEffect: Pope Paul VI formally abolished the Index in 1966, ending its legal force though the Church still cautioned against works it once condemned. The move reflected the broader liberalization of Vatican II and gave Catholic readers and publishers far greater freedom.

evt-06-14-1985-european-economic-communi.scenario: It is 14 June 1985, and you are a diplomat aboard a boat moored on the Moselle River near the village of Schengen, where officials from five European Economic Community nations are about to put their signatures to a new agreement.
evt-06-14-1985-european-economic-communi.prompt: What do the five nations commit to doing under the agreement they sign?

choices.text: Gradually abolish border checks between their countries
Establish a joint European defense pact
Merge into a single political federation
Introduce a single shared currency

evt-06-14-1985-european-economic-communi.butterflyEffect: France, West Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg agreed to gradually abolish checks at their shared borders. The accord grew into the Schengen Area, eventually covering most of Europe and allowing passport-free travel across the continent for hundreds of millions of people.

evt-06-14-1986-mindbender-galaxyland.scenario: You are waiting in line at Galaxyland inside West Edmonton Mall on June 14, 1986, when the Mindbender roller coaster suddenly fails mid-ride and its rear car leaves the track during a turn.
evt-06-14-1986-mindbender-galaxyland.prompt: What caused the Mindbender's fatal derailment that day?

choices.text: A structural failure caused the rear car to separate from the track
Riders had overloaded a single car beyond its rated capacity
The operator dispatched two trains onto the same section of track
A power surge sent the train through the loop at excessive speed

evt-06-14-1986-mindbender-galaxyland.butterflyEffect: Investigators found a structural failure in the rear car's undercarriage caused it to separate from the track during a turn, thowing riders from the car. The ride was closed for months and rebuilt with strengthened components, and the disaster pushed Canadian provinces toward stricter amusement-ride inspection standards.

evt-06-14-1996-foreclosure.scenario: It is spring 1996 on a foreclosed ranch outside Jordan, Montana. You are an FBI negotiator facing the anti-government 'Freemen,' who have barricaded themselves inside for weeks rather than accept eviction and answer fraud charges.
evt-06-14-1996-foreclosure.prompt: How does the 81-day standoff finally come to an end?

choices.text: The standoff ends in a gun battle with casualties on both sides
The Freemen surrender peacefully after prolonged negotiations
The group slips away across the state line undetected
FBI agents storm the compound under cover of darkness

evt-06-14-1996-foreclosure.butterflyEffect: After patient negotiation involving other militia figures as intermediaries, the Freemen surrendered without bloodshed, avoiding a repeat of the Waco and Ruby Ridge tragedies that had made federal agencies wary of forceful action. The peaceful resolution was later cited as a model for de-escalating standoffs with armed anti-government groups.

evt-06-14-2002-near-earth-object.scenario: You are an astronomer scanning survey images in June 2002 when you realize an asteroid, later named 2002 MN, passed within 75,000 miles of Earth days earlier — and nobody spotted it until after it was already gone.
evt-06-14-2002-near-earth-object.prompt: What did this near-miss reveal about planetary defense at the time?

choices.text: Ground telescopes tracked it days in advance, allowing evacuation plans to be drafted
Existing surveys could miss dangerous asteroids until after they had already passed
It triggered the immediate launch of a deflection spacecraft toward the object
It proved current instruments could reliably catch all such close approaches

evt-06-14-2002-near-earth-object.butterflyEffect: 2002 MN was only discovered three days after its closest approach, exposing serious gaps in the sky surveys meant to catch city-threatening asteroids before they arrive. The scare added momentum to NASA's Spaceguard efforts and later funding pushes to more completely catalog near-Earth objects.

evt-06-14-2014-war-in-donbas.scenario: It is 14 June 2014, and you are aboard a Ukrainian Il-76 transport plane carrying reinforcements toward Luhansk airport, which is under siege by pro-Russian separatists as the aircraft begins its approach.
evt-06-14-2014-war-in-donbas.prompt: What happens to the transport plane as it nears the airport?

choices.text: It is shot down while approaching the airport
It is diverted back to Kyiv without incident
It lands safely and delivers its reinforcements
It is intercepted and forced down by Russian jets

evt-06-14-2014-war-in-donbas.butterflyEffect: The aircraft was shot down by separatist fire as it approached, killing everyone aboard in one of the deadliest single losses for Ukraine's forces early in the war. The disaster hardened resolve on both sides and foreshadowed the grinding, years-long conflict over Donbas that preceded Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

evt-06-14-2014-2014-ukrainian-air-force-.scenario: It is 14 June 2014, and you are aboard an Ilyushin Il-76 transport carrying reinforcements and equipment toward Luhansk International Airport, deep in the escalating war in Donbas.
evt-06-14-2014-2014-ukrainian-air-force-.prompt: What did this shootdown reveal about the danger now facing aircraft over the conflict zone?

choices.text: It caused Ukraine to permanently halt all airlift operations in the region
It triggered a full ceasefire between Kyiv and the Luhansk separatists
It exposed that separatist forces possessed weapons capable of downing high-flying aircraft, foreshadowing the MH17 disaster weeks later
It led to an immediate NATO-enforced no-fly zone over eastern Ukraine

evt-06-14-2014-2014-ukrainian-air-force-.butterflyEffect: The loss of the Il-76 showed that separatist forces now wielded weapons able to strike aircraft at altitude, a warning largely unheeded at the time. Five weeks later, on 17 July 2014, Malaysia Airlines Flight MH17 was shot down over the same war zone, killing 298 people and drawing global condemnation of Russia's role in the conflict.

evt-06-14-2017-grenfell-tower-fire.scenario: It is the early hours of 14 June 2017, and you live on an upper floor of Grenfell Tower in West London. You wake to the smell of smoke and watch flames racing up the outside of the building far faster than you expected.
evt-06-14-2017-grenfell-tower-fire.prompt: What allows the fire to spread so quickly up the tower's exterior?

choices.text: Faulty electrical wiring inside a single kitchen
Overcrowded stairwells trapping residents on lower floors
Flammable cladding installed in a recent building renovation
A total absence of fire extinguishers on every floor

evt-06-14-2017-grenfell-tower-fire.butterflyEffect: Flammable aluminum composite cladding, installed during a 2016 refurbishment, acted as fuel and let the fire race up the building's outside within minutes. The disaster led to a public inquiry, a UK-wide program to strip dangerous cladding from tower blocks, and sweeping reforms to building safety regulation.

evt-06-14-2017-steve-scalise.scenario: It is the morning of June 14, 2017, at a baseball field in Alexandria, Virginia. You are among the Republican congressmen practicing for the annual charity game when a gunman suddenly opens fire from behind the outfield fence.
evt-06-14-2017-steve-scalise.prompt: What happens to House Majority Whip Steve Scalise in the attack?

choices.text: He wrestles the gunman's weapon away before anyone is hurt
He escapes unharmed after diving behind a dugout
He is shot and critically wounded, requiring multiple surgeries
He is grazed but finishes the practice before seeking treatment

evt-06-14-2017-steve-scalise.butterflyEffect: Scalise was struck in the hip and critically wounded, undergoing multiple surgeries and months of rehabilitation before returning to the House floor to a bipartisan standing ovation. The shooting led to a lasting increase in security for members of Congress and brief calls for greater civility across party lines.

evt-06-15-1215-magna-carta.scenario: It is 15 June 1215 in the meadow at Runnymede. You stand among the rebellious barons confronting King John, demanding he accept a charter limiting his power after months of unrest and threatened civil war.
evt-06-15-1215-magna-carta.prompt: What does King John do once the charter is sealed?

choices.text: He signs it and immediately abdicates the throne
He refuses outright and flees to France
He seals it under pressure, then later seeks a papal annulment, sparking war
He has the assembled barons arrested on the spot

evt-06-15-1215-magna-carta.butterflyEffect: John soon repudiated his promise, securing an annulment from Pope Innocent III that triggered the First Barons' War. Reissued after his death and confirmed as statute law under Edward I, Magna Carta endured as a foundation of English constitutional rights, later inspiring documents like the U.S. Bill of Rights.

evt-06-15-1520-pope-leo-x.scenario: It is 1520 and Martin Luther's writings, attacking indulgences and papal authority, are spreading fast through the German lands. As Pope Leo X, you must respond before the challenge grows further.
evt-06-15-1520-pope-leo-x.prompt: What does the papal bull Exsurge Domine actually demand of Luther?

choices.text: Condemn 41 of his teachings and give him 60 days to recant
Dismiss his writings as too minor to require any response
Excommunicate him immediately with no chance to respond
Invite him to a public debate before the College of Cardinals

evt-06-15-1520-pope-leo-x.butterflyEffect: The bull condemned 41 of Luther's propositions as heretical and gave him 60 days to recant or face excommunication. Luther publicly burned the bull instead, was formally excommunicated in 1521, and the standoff hardened into the permanent split of the Reformation.

evt-06-15-1800-war-of-the-second-coaliti.scenario: It is the morning after your crushing defeat at Marengo. You are Austrian General Michael von Melas, and Bonaparte's terms for a ceasefire in Italy await your signature.

choices.text: Sign the convention and withdraw Austrian forces from northern Italy
Seek separate peace terms from Britain instead
Refuse the terms and continue fighting in Italy
Retreat immediately to defend Vienna

evt-06-15-1800-war-of-the-second-coaliti.butterflyEffect: Melas signed the Convention of Alessandria, withdrawing Austrian forces from Lombardy and Piedmont and restoring French dominance in northern Italy. The victory cemented Napoleon's prestige as First Consul and pushed Austria toward the 1801 Treaty of Lunéville, which ended its part in the war.

evt-06-15-1859-san-juan-islands.scenario: It is June 15, 1859, on San Juan Island. A Hudson's Bay Company pig has trampled through your potato patch again, and your rifle is within easy reach.

choices.text: Report the pig to the Hudson's Bay Company and demand compensation
Fence off your garden to keep the pig out
Ignore the pig and let it roam freely
Shoot the pig, triggering a border dispute between Britain and the US

evt-06-15-1859-san-juan-islands.butterflyEffect: American settler Lyman Cutlar shot the pig, sparking a dispute over compensation that escalated into a military standoff between US and British forces on the island. The crisis was resolved without bloodshed and eventually settled by arbitration in 1872, when Kaiser Wilhelm I awarded the San Juan Islands to the United States.

evt-06-15-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: It is the afternoon of 15 June 1864 outside Petersburg, Virginia. Your Union corps has just broken through a thinly held stretch of Confederate earthworks, and the road to the city seems open before nightfall.
evt-06-15-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What should Union commanders do with this fleeting advantage?

choices.text: Press the attack immediately before Confederate reinforcements arrive
Halt the advance and wait for orders and reinforcements
Withdraw entirely to safer positions south of the city
Negotiate a local truce with Confederate defenders

evt-06-15-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Union generals hesitated and failed to press the attack that evening, giving Robert E. Lee just enough time to rush reinforcements into the lines. The lost opportunity turned a nearly undefended city into the center of a nine-and-a-half-month siege that dragged the war into the spring of 1865.

evt-06-15-1878-eadweard-muybridge.scenario: It is 1878 and railroad baron Leland Stanford has paid you to settle a bitter argument: does a galloping horse ever have all four hooves off the ground at once? A single camera has failed to catch it.
evt-06-15-1878-eadweard-muybridge.prompt: How do you finally capture the horse's stride clearly enough to prove the point?

choices.text: Use one camera with the fastest shutter speed available
Project the horse's shadow through a magic lantern
Set up a row of cameras triggered in sequence by tripwires
Have an artist sketch the horse from careful observation

evt-06-15-1878-eadweard-muybridge.butterflyEffect: Muybridge lined up a battery of cameras along the track, each tripped by a wire the horse's legs snapped as it passed, freezing the gallop frame by frame. The images proved all four hooves do leave the ground, and his sequential photography became a direct forerunner of motion pictures.

evt-06-15-1904-ps-general-slocum.scenario: It is June 15, 1904, aboard the General Slocum on the East River. Smoke is pouring from a storeroom below deck, and panicked parishioners from a Lutheran church outing crowd the rails. You are Captain William Van Schaick.
evt-06-15-1904-ps-general-slocum.prompt: What do you do as the fire spreads?

choices.text: Continue steaming upriver toward North Brother Island instead of grounding immediately
Order all passengers to jump overboard at once
Immediately beach the ship on the nearest Manhattan shore
Turn back to the pier of departure

evt-06-15-1904-ps-general-slocum.butterflyEffect: Van Schaick chose to keep steaming toward North Brother Island rather than grounding immediately, and the wind fanned the flames, worsening the disaster. Over a thousand people died, and the catastrophe exposed rotted life preservers and unusable lifeboats, driving major reforms in American steamboat safety inspection.

evt-06-15-1919-john-alcock-raf-officer.scenario: It is dawn on 15 June 1919. After sixteen hours battling fog, ice, and engine trouble over the Atlantic, you are Captain John Alcock, and through the mist you spot what looks like flat green ground near the Irish coast.
evt-06-15-1919-john-alcock-raf-officer.prompt: What do you do with your modified Vickers Vimy bomber?

choices.text: Ditch the aircraft in the sea just offshore
Turn back out over the Atlantic to search for a ship
Circle for hours searching for a paved runway
Attempt to land on the green ground below

evt-06-15-1919-john-alcock-raf-officer.butterflyEffect: Alcock brought the aircraft down nose-first into what turned out to be a bog near Clifden, Ireland, damaging the plane but leaving both airmen unhurt. Their nonstop crossing won the Daily Mail's £10,000 prize and proved transatlantic flight possible, though Alcock died in another flying accident just months later.

evt-06-15-1921-bessie-coleman.scenario: It's June 1921 near Paris. You are a 29-year-old Black American woman who has trained for months with French instructors, determined to become the first African American to hold an international pilot's license.
evt-06-15-1921-bessie-coleman.prompt: What must you do to earn the coveted FAI license?

choices.text: Obtain a formal endorsement from a US military officer
Simply pay a membership fee to the local aero club
Fly solo across the English Channel unassisted
Complete a series of prescribed flight maneuvers and altitude tests before French examiners

evt-06-15-1921-bessie-coleman.butterflyEffect: Bessie Coleman passed her tests and became the first African American and first Native American to hold an FAI license, and the earliest known Black person to do so internationally. She returned home as "Queen Bess," barnstorming and lecturing against segregation until her death in 1926, inspiring generations of Black aviators.

evt-06-15-1977-death-and-funeral-of-fran.scenario: It is 15 June 1977 in Madrid. You queue outside a polling station, ballot in hand, for Spain's first free general election since 1936, less than two years after Franco's death.
evt-06-15-1977-death-and-funeral-of-fran.prompt: What is the outcome of this first democratic vote?

choices.text: The election is annulled amid army intervention
Suárez's centrist coalition wins a plurality of seats
Franco loyalists retain control of parliament
The Communist Party wins an outright majority

evt-06-15-1977-death-and-funeral-of-fran.butterflyEffect: Adolfo Suárez's centrist Union of the Democratic Centre won the most seats, narrowly ahead of the Socialists, giving reformists a mandate to negotiate rather than rupture with the old order. The new parliament went on to draft the 1978 constitution, cementing Spain's peaceful transition to democracy under King Juan Carlos.

evt-06-15-1978-hussein-of-jordan.scenario: It is June 15, 1978, in Amman. You are Lisa Halaby, an American-born Princeton graduate who has fallen in love with King Hussein of Jordan.
evt-06-15-1978-hussein-of-jordan.prompt: What do you do to marry the king and become queen?

choices.text: Convert to Islam and take the name Noor al-Hussein
Decline the marriage over political concerns
Marry secretly without public acknowledgment
Retain her American citizenship and Christian faith

evt-06-15-1978-hussein-of-jordan.butterflyEffect: Lisa Halaby converted to Islam and took the name Noor al-Hussein, becoming Queen Noor of Jordan. She went on to champion humanitarian causes, cultural dialogue, and landmine removal, remaining a prominent public voice after King Hussein's death in 1999.

evt-06-15-1988-ariane-4.scenario: It is 15 June 1988 at the Guiana Space Centre. Engineers must choose which configuration of the new Ariane 4 rocket to risk on its untested maiden flight, from a bare core stage to versions bristling with strap-on boosters.
evt-06-15-1988-ariane-4.prompt: Which configuration do engineers choose for this first, unproven launch?

choices.text: The fully boosted version with four solid and liquid strap-ons
A reused Ariane 3 upper stage bolted to a new core
The baseline core with no strap-on boosters
A stripped-down suborbital test article

evt-06-15-1988-ariane-4.butterflyEffect: They flew the simplest baseline version, without any solid or liquid strap-on boosters, to minimize risk on an unproven vehicle. The cautious choice paid off, and Ariane 4 went on to log 113 successful launches out of 116 over fifteen years, making it the workhorse of the commercial launch market.

evt-06-15-1992-supreme-court-of-the-unit.scenario: It is June 1992. You are Humberto Álvarez-Machaín, a Mexican doctor forcibly seized by bounty hunters working for U.S. agents and brought across the border to face trial for his alleged role in a DEA agent's torture and murder.
evt-06-15-1992-supreme-court-of-the-unit.prompt: How does the Supreme Court rule on the legality of your abduction?

choices.text: The Court rules only Congress can authorize such abductions
The abduction violates the treaty and charges are dismissed
Forcible abduction does not violate the treaty, so trial may proceed
The Court orders his immediate return to Mexico

evt-06-15-1992-supreme-court-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: The Court held that forcible abduction did not violate the U.S.-Mexico extradition treaty, so American courts could still try him despite the illegal manner of his capture. Álvarez-Machaín was later acquitted at trial, but the ruling drew sharp international criticism and became a lasting precedent in debates over U.S. extraterritorial law enforcement and rendition.

evt-06-15-1996-the-troubles.scenario: It is Saturday morning, 15 June 1996, and you are a police officer in Manchester city centre. A coded warning has just come in about a bomb-laden truck parked outside a department store on a street packed with weekend shoppers.
evt-06-15-1996-the-troubles.prompt: What do you do in the minutes after the warning?

choices.text: Wait for army bomb disposal without clearing shoppers first
Assume it is a hoax and continue normal patrols
Evacuate the area immediately and cordon off the streets
Attempt to move the truck yourself before backup arrives

evt-06-15-1996-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: Police evacuated roughly 75,000 people from the city centre before the 1,500 kg IRA bomb detonated, causing over 200 injuries but no deaths. The devastation forced a massive rebuilding of Manchester's core, accelerating a regeneration that reshaped the city for decades.

evt-06-15-2006-george-w-bush.scenario: It is 15 June 2006, and you are briefing President George W. Bush on a proposal to protect a vast, remote stretch of ocean around the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands teeming with coral reefs and rare species.
evt-06-15-2006-george-w-bush.prompt: What does President Bush decide to do with this stretch of Pacific ocean?

choices.text: Approve offshore oil exploration surveys there
Open it to expanded commercial fishing leases
Designate it a fully protected marine national monument
Transfer control of the waters to the state of Hawaii

evt-06-15-2006-george-w-bush.butterflyEffect: Bush designated the area the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument, at the time the largest fully protected marine area on Earth. It banned commercial fishing and extraction across roughly 140,000 square miles, and became a model cited when later administrations created even larger marine reserves in the Pacific.

evt-06-16-632-sasanian-empire.scenario: You are a Sasanian noble in 632 CE, gathered with other magnates after a chaotic string of short-lived rulers following Khosrow II's fall, desperate to find someone who can hold the empire together.
evt-06-16-632-sasanian-empire.prompt: Whom does the nobility crown to stabilize the shaken Sasanian throne?

choices.text: Invite a Parthian claimant to take the throne
Form an indefinite regency council of nobles
Crown young Yazdegerd III, the last surviving heir of the royal bloodline
Install the general Rostam Farrokhzad as a stopgap ruler

evt-06-16-632-sasanian-empire.butterflyEffect: The nobles crowned young Yazdegerd III, the last of the Sasanian royal line, but his reign coincided with the rise of the Arab Muslim armies. Despite resistance at battles like Qadisiyyah and Nahavand, the empire collapsed within two decades, and Yazdegerd's assassination in 651 ended over four centuries of Sasanian rule and pre-Islamic Persian kingship.

evt-06-16-1407-ming-dynasty.scenario: You serve Hồ Quý Ly, ruler of Đại Ngu, as Ming armies overrun your fortifications in northern Vietnam in 1407 and the capital falls.
evt-06-16-1407-ming-dynasty.prompt: What does Hồ Quý Ly attempt as Ming forces close in on his position?

choices.text: Surrender immediately to negotiate terms
Flee south by land and sea, hoping to regroup his forces
Retreat into the mountains to wage guerrilla war at once
Send tribute to the Ming court to sue for peace

evt-06-16-1407-ming-dynasty.butterflyEffect: Hồ Quý Ly and his son fled south but were captured and taken captive to China, ending the short-lived Hồ dynasty as Ming forces annexed Vietnam into their empire. Harsh Ming rule fueled resentment that erupted into the Lam Sơn uprising led by Lê Lợi, who expelled the Chinese and founded the Lê dynasty in 1428.

evt-06-16-1755-battle-of-fort-beausejour.scenario: You command the French garrison at Fort Beauséjour in 1755, and after two weeks of British bombardment your walls are crumbling with no relief force in sight.
evt-06-16-1755-battle-of-fort-beausejour.prompt: What do you do as the siege grinds on with no hope of reinforcement?

choices.text: Surrender the fort to preserve the garrison
Attempt a breakout under cover of darkness
Fight on until the last man falls
Wait for Acadian militia to relieve the siege

evt-06-16-1755-battle-of-fort-beausejour.butterflyEffect: The French commander surrendered the fort to British forces under Robert Monckton, opening the Chignecto isthmus to British control. The victory launched a wider British offensive in Acadia that led directly to the mass deportation of Acadians later that year and hastened the end of French colonial power in North America.

evt-06-16-1819-1819-rann-of-kutch-earthq.scenario: It is the evening of 16 June 1819 near Kutch, Gujarat. The ground has just convulsed violently and a tsunami is surging inland, while the landscape itself seems to be rearranging beneath your feet.
evt-06-16-1819-1819-rann-of-kutch-earthq.prompt: What lasting geographic feature does the quake's uplift leave behind?

choices.text: A newly formed volcanic island offshore
A natural dam known as the Allah Bund
A deep canyon cutting through the Kutch plain
The complete disappearance of the Indus delta

evt-06-16-1819-1819-rann-of-kutch-earthq.butterflyEffect: The earthquake raised a long ridge of ground later called the Allah Bund, which dammed a nearby river and permanently altered local drainage, while subsidence elsewhere formed Sindri Lake. The event remains one of the earliest well-documented examples of coseismic land uplift, still studied by geologists today.

evt-06-16-1963-vostok-6.scenario: It is 16 June 1963 and you are strapped into the Vostok 6 capsule as it climbs toward orbit, a former textile worker turned cosmonaut about to make history for the Soviet space program.
evt-06-16-1963-vostok-6.prompt: What historic first is Valentina Tereshkova about to achieve?

choices.text: The first crewed flight around the Moon
The first person to perform a spacewalk
The first woman to fly in space
The first docking of two crewed spacecraft

evt-06-16-1963-vostok-6.butterflyEffect: Tereshkova became the first woman to fly in space, orbiting Earth 48 times over nearly three days, a major propaganda triumph for the USSR in the space race. Yet the Soviets did not send another woman into orbit for almost two decades, and NASA would not fly a woman until Sally Ride in 1983.

evt-06-16-1972-david-bowie.scenario: You are a London music journalist in June 1972, handed an advance copy of David Bowie's new record alongside photos of him in flame-red hair and an alien stage persona.
evt-06-16-1972-david-bowie.prompt: What bold choice has Bowie made to launch this record?

choices.text: Introduce a full alter-ego, Ziggy Stardust, with costume and backstory
Delay the release for a longer marketing campaign
Perform the songs under his own name with no theatrics
Release a companion film before any live shows

evt-06-16-1972-david-bowie.butterflyEffect: Bowie released The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars, fully inhabiting the androgynous alien rock star Ziggy on stage and in interviews, blurring the line between performer and persona. The character ignited the glam rock movement, and Bowie's shocking on-stage "retirement" of Ziggy in 1973 became one of rock's most talked-about reinventions.

evt-06-16-1976-soweto-uprising.scenario: It is the morning of 16 June 1976 and you are a student gathering with thousands of classmates in the streets of Soweto, placards in hand, marching toward Orlando Stadium.
evt-06-16-1976-soweto-uprising.prompt: What government policy is the march protesting?

choices.text: A curfew restricting movement after dark
The closure of black-owned businesses in Soweto
The compulsory use of Afrikaans as a teaching language in black schools
A new tax imposed on township residents
