evt-06-16-1976-soweto-uprising.butterflyEffect: The demonstration was against a directive forcing black schools to teach in Afrikaans, a language many students associated with the apartheid state. Police opened fire on the unarmed marchers, and the resulting outrage spread nationwide, drawing international condemnation and becoming a turning point that hardened global opposition to apartheid.

evt-06-16-2000-united-nations-security-c.scenario: You are a UN monitor in June 2000 tasked with verifying that Israeli troops have withdrawn from southern Lebanon as required by a 1978 Security Council resolution.
evt-06-16-2000-united-nations-security-c.prompt: What must you confirm on the ground to certify Israel's compliance?

choices.text: That control of the south has passed to Syrian forces
That Hezbollah fighters have disarmed first
That Israeli withdrawal is conditional on a prisoner exchange
That Israeli forces have pulled back to the internationally recognized Blue Line

evt-06-16-2000-united-nations-security-c.butterflyEffect: Secretary-General Kofi Annan confirmed Israel's withdrawal to the UN-drawn Blue Line, ending a 22-year occupation of southern Lebanon. Hezbollah claimed the withdrawal as a victory, boosting its political standing, while disputes over the Shebaa Farms border area kept tensions alive, eventually contributing to the 2006 Lebanon War.

evt-06-16-2012-liu-yang-taikonaut.scenario: You watch the Shenzhou 9 rocket lift off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center on 16 June 2012, knowing one of the three taikonauts aboard is about to make history as the capsule heads toward a docking with the Tiangong-1 space station.
evt-06-16-2012-liu-yang-taikonaut.prompt: What historic milestone does crew member Liu Yang achieve on this mission?

choices.text: First uncrewed docking test for China
First Chinese woman to perform a spacewalk
First Chinese woman to command a mission
First Chinese woman in space

evt-06-16-2012-liu-yang-taikonaut.butterflyEffect: Liu Yang became the first Chinese woman to fly in space, and the mission successfully completed China's first crewed docking with Tiangong-1. Her flight opened the door for further Chinese women, including Wang Yaping, to join the national space program.

evt-06-16-2013-2013-north-india-floods.scenario: You are a pilgrim caught at the Kedarnath shrine in Uttarakhand as a sudden cloudburst sends a wall of water and debris roaring down the valley in June 2013.
evt-06-16-2013-2013-north-india-floods.prompt: Where do you take shelter as the flood surge hits the temple complex?

choices.text: Cross the swollen river to reach the opposite bank
Flee immediately down the open pilgrim trail toward Rambada
Take shelter behind the temple, where a huge boulder blocks the debris flow
Climb onto the temple roof and wait for rescue

evt-06-16-2013-2013-north-india-floods.butterflyEffect: A massive boulder became lodged directly behind the Kedarnath temple, splitting the debris flow and sparing the ancient structure even as the surrounding town was obliterated. The disaster triggered one of India's largest-ever military rescue operations and led to stricter regulation of Himalayan pilgrimage and construction.

evt-06-16-2015-business-career-of-donald.scenario: You are a reporter crammed into the lobby of Trump Tower on 16 June 2015, watching Donald Trump ride the escalator down to a podium crowded with cameras. He has spent decades building a real-estate and entertainment brand and now has something to say.
evt-06-16-2015-business-career-of-donald.prompt: What does Trump announce at this Trump Tower event?

choices.text: His endorsement of another Republican candidate
A new international hotel chain
His retirement from The Apprentice
His campaign to run for President of the United States

evt-06-16-2015-business-career-of-donald.butterflyEffect: Trump declared his candidacy for President of the United States as a Republican, delivering a speech that included controversial remarks about immigration that dominated headlines for days. The long-shot campaign eventually won him the 2016 Republican nomination and the presidency.

evt-06-16-2019-2019-2020-hong-kong-prote.scenario: You march through the streets of Hong Kong Island on 16 June 2019 alongside what will be counted as roughly two million fellow demonstrators, dressed in black, one week after the government suspended but did not scrap its extradition bill.
evt-06-16-2019-2019-2020-hong-kong-prote.prompt: What is the crowd's central demand as it marches today?

choices.text: Full withdrawal of the extradition bill
Independence for Hong Kong from China
Direct elections for the Chief Executive
Release of all previously arrested protesters

evt-06-16-2019-2019-2020-hong-kong-prote.butterflyEffect: Protesters demanded the full withdrawal of the extradition bill along with an independent inquiry and Carrie Lam's resignation. The bill was formally withdrawn that September, but unrest continued for months and ultimately led Beijing to impose a national security law on Hong Kong in 2020.

evt-06-17-653-pope-martin-i.scenario: You are Pope Martin I in the Lateran Palace, having just condemned the emperor's favored Monothelite doctrine at a Roman council, when soldiers sent by the Exarch of Ravenna arrive at your door.
evt-06-17-653-pope-martin-i.prompt: What ultimately happens to Martin after his arrest?

choices.text: He flees to Ravenna and continues governing as pope from exile
He recants his opposition and is restored to the papacy
He is tried in Constantinople and exiled to Cherson, where he dies
He is executed on the spot in the Lateran Palace

evt-06-17-653-pope-martin-i.butterflyEffect: Martin was shipped to Constantinople, subjected to a humiliating show trial, and exiled to Cherson in the Crimea, where he died from the hardship around 655. His fate made him the last pope venerated as a martyr and became a lasting symbol of papal defiance against imperial interference in Church doctrine.

evt-06-17-1397-kalmar-union.scenario: You are a Danish noble at the assembly in Kalmar in 1397, watching Queen Margaret press the gathered Scandinavian lords to settle how three restless kingdoms should be governed together.
evt-06-17-1397-kalmar-union.prompt: What arrangement do the nobles agree to at Kalmar?

choices.text: The kingdoms will rotate a shared regency council each year
One monarch will rule all three kingdoms jointly
Each kingdom keeps its own king under a mutual defense treaty
The union is symbolic only and dissolves after the coronation

evt-06-17-1397-kalmar-union.butterflyEffect: The three kingdoms were joined under a single monarch while keeping their own laws, creating the Kalmar Union. It endured until Sweden broke away in 1523, while Denmark and Norway remained linked in one form or another until 1814.

evt-06-17-1462-hungarian-ottoman-wars.scenario: It is the night of 17 June 1462, and you ride with Vlad III Dracula's Wallachian raiders as they slip, torches doused, into the sprawling Ottoman camp near Târgoviște, hoping to strike before Sultan Mehmed II wakes.
evt-06-17-1462-hungarian-ottoman-wars.prompt: What is the raiders' chief objective once inside the camp?

choices.text: Burn the supply wagons and retreat immediately
Free Christian prisoners held in the camp
Push directly toward Mehmed II's tent to kill the sultan
Capture high-ranking officers to hold for ransom

evt-06-17-1462-hungarian-ottoman-wars.butterflyEffect: Vlad's night raid caused chaos and heavy Ottoman losses, but the sultan's guards had shifted his tent, and Mehmed II survived unharmed. The Ottomans pressed on regardless, and within months they installed Vlad's own brother Radu as a more compliant ruler of Wallachia.

evt-06-17-1579-francis-drake.scenario: You are a sailor aboard the Golden Hind in June 1579, as Sir Francis Drake brings the battered ship ashore on an unfamiliar stretch of the northern California coast to make repairs before crossing the Pacific.
evt-06-17-1579-francis-drake.prompt: What does Drake do upon landing?

choices.text: Trades exclusively with nearby Spanish settlers
Establishes a permanent English colony on the spot
Burns his own ship to prevent a mutiny
Claims the land for England, naming it Nova Albion

evt-06-17-1579-francis-drake.butterflyEffect: Drake claimed the land for England, naming it Nova Albion, though no permanent colony followed. The claim later gave England grounds to dispute Spanish dominance of the Pacific coast, and the exact landing site remains debated by historians today.

evt-06-17-1631-mumtaz-mahal.scenario: It is 17 June 1631 at Burhanpur, and Mumtaz Mahal has just died delivering her fourteenth child. Shah Jahan, inconsolable, turns to you and his court architects to decide how his empress should be remembered.
evt-06-17-1631-mumtaz-mahal.prompt: What does Shah Jahan ultimately commission in her memory?

choices.text: The Taj Mahal mausoleum complex at Agra
A new mosque in Delhi bearing her name
An annual empire-wide day of mourning only
A modest garden tomb near Burhanpur

evt-06-17-1631-mumtaz-mahal.butterflyEffect: Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal at Agra, a white marble mausoleum built over roughly two decades by thousands of craftsmen. It became the crowning achievement of Mughal architecture and today stands as one of the most recognized monuments on earth.

evt-06-17-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: You are a British officer at the base of Breed's Hill outside Boston, ordered to dislodge the entrenched colonial militia above you in broad daylight.
evt-06-17-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: How do British forces finally take the hill?

choices.text: With a surprise night ambush from the rear
Through repeated frontal bayonet charges up the exposed slope
By a naval bombardment that forced the militia to surrender
Through a negotiated withdrawal arranged before the battle

evt-06-17-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: The British captured the position only after three costly frontal assaults, suffering over a thousand casualties, roughly half their attacking force. The staggering losses for a single hill stunned London and proved that colonial militia could stand against professional regulars, hardening resolve on both sides of the war.

evt-06-17-1861-american-civil-war.scenario: It's June 17, 1861, and you command a train carrying Ohio infantry along a rail line near Vienna, Virginia, unaware that Confederate artillery is waiting ahead in the trees.
evt-06-17-1861-american-civil-war.prompt: What do your soldiers do when hidden guns suddenly open fire on the train?

choices.text: They leap from the cars and scatter into the woods, retreating on foot
They form ranks beside the tracks and charge the guns
They order the train to push forward through the ambush
They wave a flag of surrender from the train windows

evt-06-17-1861-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Confederate battery, positioned under Colonel Maxcy Gregg, raked the train with cannon fire, killing and wounding several soldiers as survivors leapt from the cars and fled on foot back toward Alexandria. The skirmish, one of the war's first uses of artillery against a train, exposed the dangers of moving troops by rail into contested territory ahead of larger battles like Bull Run.

evt-06-17-1900-boxer-rebellion.scenario: It's June 17, 1900, and you command an allied warship anchored off the Dagu (Taku) Forts, the gateway guarding the river route to Tianjin and the besieged foreign legations in Beijing.
evt-06-17-1900-boxer-rebellion.prompt: What do the allied commanders decide when the Qing garrison refuses to hand over the forts?

choices.text: Launch a coordinated naval bombardment and land assault to seize the forts
Blockade the river without attacking the forts directly
Wait offshore for reinforcements before acting
Withdraw the fleet and press for negotiations instead

evt-06-17-1900-boxer-rebellion.butterflyEffect: The Eight-Nation Alliance bombarded and stormed the forts, seizing them within hours and opening the river route toward Tianjin. The attack pushed the Qing court to formally declare war on the foreign powers, turning a regional uprising into a full international conflict that ended with allied occupation of Beijing.

evt-06-17-1919-epsom-riot.scenario: You are a Canadian soldier camped near Epsom in June 1919, still waiting months after the armistice to be shipped home, as frustration among the men boils over into a march on the local police station.
evt-06-17-1919-epsom-riot.prompt: What happens when the angry crowd of soldiers reaches the station?

choices.text: They negotiate peacefully with the sergeant on duty
They storm and attack the station, and Sergeant Green is fatally injured
Military police disperse the crowd before any violence occurs
They march instead toward London to petition Parliament

evt-06-17-1919-epsom-riot.butterflyEffect: The soldiers stormed the station and in the chaos Station Sergeant Thomas Green was fatally injured, dying the next day. The riot became a stark symbol of the anger and mismanagement surrounding delayed demobilization, embarrassing military authorities on both sides of the Atlantic.

evt-06-17-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: You watch from the docks at Saint-Nazaire as thousands of retreating British soldiers and civilians crowd aboard the requisitioned liner RMS Lancastria, far beyond her rated capacity, as German aircraft circle overhead.
evt-06-17-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: What happens to the Lancastria that afternoon?

choices.text: She is struck by a German bomb and sinks with massive loss of life
She departs safely and lands all passengers in England
She runs aground on a sandbar before ever leaving harbor
She is torpedoed by a U-boat while still in port

evt-06-17-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: A German bomber scored a direct hit and the overcrowded liner sank in minutes, killing an estimated 4,000 or more people, Britain's worst-ever maritime disaster, exceeding the combined losses of the Titanic and Lusitania. Fearing the blow to morale so soon after Dunkirk, Churchill's government suppressed news of the sinking, and it remained largely unacknowledged for decades.

evt-06-17-1952-guatemalan-revolution.scenario: It's June 17, 1952, and you serve in President Jacobo Árbenz's government as the Guatemalan Congress votes on a sweeping land reform law targeting idle estate land, including vast holdings of the United Fruit Company.
evt-06-17-1952-guatemalan-revolution.prompt: What does Decree 900 authorize the government to do?

choices.text: Abolish private land ownership across Guatemala
Nationalize all foreign-owned industries outright
Seize land from large landowners without any compensation
Expropriate unused estate land and redistribute it to landless peasants

evt-06-17-1952-guatemalan-revolution.butterflyEffect: The law expropriated uncultivated portions of large estates and redistributed them to landless peasants, compensating owners based on the low values they themselves had declared for tax purposes. United Fruit's resulting outrage helped drive US backing for the 1954 CIA-orchestrated coup that toppled Árbenz, ending Guatemala's reform era and setting off decades of civil conflict.

evt-06-17-1972-watergate-complex.scenario: It is just after midnight on 17 June 1972, and as a night security guard making rounds at the Watergate complex, you notice a door leading to the Democratic National Committee offices has its lock taped over.

choices.text: Ignore it and continue your rounds as usual
Call the police, leading to the arrest of five burglars inside
Report it only to your supervisor without calling police
Confront the men in the office yourself

evt-06-17-1972-watergate-complex.butterflyEffect: The guard, Frank Wills, called police, who arrested five men carrying wiretapping equipment and cash inside the DNC offices. The break-in unraveled into the Watergate scandal, ultimately forcing President Nixon's resignation in 1974 and reshaping American attitudes toward presidential power and press oversight.

evt-06-17-1992-george-h-w-bush.scenario: You are a U.S. negotiator standing beside President Bush at the White House in June 1992, unveiling a new framework hammered out with Russian President Yeltsin for slashing both nations' nuclear stockpiles.
evt-06-17-1992-george-h-w-bush.prompt: What does this 'joint understanding' commit the two sides to?

choices.text: A joint program to build an orbiting space station
Deep cuts to strategic nuclear warhead numbers
Mutual withdrawal of all troops stationed in Europe
Complete elimination of all nuclear weapons by both sides

evt-06-17-1992-george-h-w-bush.butterflyEffect: The framework committed both countries to cut strategic nuclear warheads well below existing START I limits. It became the basis for the START II treaty signed in January 1993, though that treaty never entered into force after the Russian Duma withheld ratification for years.

evt-06-17-1994-o-j-simpson.scenario: It's the evening of June 17, 1994, and you command the LAPD units trailing a white Ford Bronco carrying a fugitive murder suspect and a friend at his wheel, broadcast live to tens of millions of viewers.
evt-06-17-1994-o-j-simpson.prompt: What do you order as the Bronco nears the suspect's Brentwood home?

choices.text: Set up a roadblock ahead to end the chase at once
Order a tactical team to storm the vehicle mid-pursuit
Ram the Bronco to force it off the freeway immediately
Follow at a distance without forcing a stop, letting him drive to his own home

evt-06-17-1994-o-j-simpson.butterflyEffect: Police followed at a distance rather than forcing a stop, letting the Bronco reach Simpson's home, where he eventually surrendered after a tense standoff with a gun to his own head. The slow chase, watched by roughly 95 million Americans, became the opening scene of the media spectacle that engulfed his subsequent murder trial.

evt-06-17-2015-charleston-church-shootin.scenario: Two days after the shooting, you sit in a Charleston courtroom as relatives of the nine victims are given the chance to address the shooter directly for the first time.
evt-06-17-2015-charleston-church-shootin.prompt: What do several grieving family members choose to say to the killer at the bond hearing?

choices.text: They demand the death penalty be sought immediately
They refuse to speak and leave the courtroom in silence
They ask the judge to consider the shooter's mental illness for leniency
They offer forgiveness while describing their grief and loss

evt-06-17-2015-charleston-church-shootin.butterflyEffect: Family members stunned the nation by offering forgiveness to Dylann Roof even as they described their grief. The moment of grace, combined with the massacre itself, accelerated a national reckoning that led South Carolina to remove the Confederate battle flag from its State House grounds weeks later.

evt-06-17-2017-june-2017-portugal-wildfi.scenario: It is the afternoon of 17 June 2017, and within minutes four separate fires erupt across the tinder-dry forests of central Portugal. As officials, you must decide how the nation will respond in the disaster's immediate aftermath.
evt-06-17-2017-june-2017-portugal-wildfi.prompt: What official response follows within days of the fires?

choices.text: Portugal declares three days of national mourning
The government dissolves parliament immediately
NATO deploys troops to assist firefighting
A nationwide curfew is imposed for a month

evt-06-17-2017-june-2017-portugal-wildfi.butterflyEffect: Portugal declared three days of national mourning for the victims. The disaster exposed severe gaps in forest management and rural road safety, feeding a broader reckoning that intensified after further deadly fires later that same year and led to reforms of the country's civil protection system.

evt-06-17-2021-juneteenth.scenario: It's June 17, 2021, and you're a reporter in the Oval Office as President Biden prepares to sign a bill, passed unanimously by the Senate, making Juneteenth a federal holiday just two days before its first official observance.
evt-06-17-2021-juneteenth.prompt: What happens at the signing ceremony?

choices.text: He delays the signing pending further congressional review
He signs it privately with no public ceremony
He vetoes it over cost concerns for federal employees
He signs it surrounded by lawmakers and activists, calling it a historic honor

evt-06-17-2021-juneteenth.butterflyEffect: Biden signed the bill surrounded by Black lawmakers and longtime Juneteenth activists, calling it one of the great honors of his presidency, and it became the first new federal holiday created since Martin Luther King Jr. Day in 1983. Its recognition prompted schools, states, and companies nationwide to formally begin observing June 19th, while also sparking debate over whether commemoration alone addressed deeper racial inequities.

evt-06-18-618-transition-from-sui-to-tan.scenario: It is 618 in Chang'an. As the powerful general who installed the boy Yang You as a puppet emperor after the Sui collapse, you now hold real military and political power while he holds only the title.
evt-06-18-618-transition-from-sui-to-tan.prompt: What do you do about the puppet emperor?

choices.text: Continue ruling indefinitely as his regent
Restore full power to the Sui imperial family
Install a different Sui prince as a new puppet
Depose and execute him, then declare himself emperor

evt-06-18-618-transition-from-sui-to-tan.butterflyEffect: Li Yuan had Yang You deposed and executed, then proclaimed himself Emperor Gaozu, founding the Tang dynasty. The Tang would go on to become one of China's greatest imperial dynasties, ushering in centuries of cultural flourishing, territorial expansion, and administrative innovation.

evt-06-18-1757-third-silesian-war.scenario: It is 18 June 1757 near Kolín in Bohemia. Your Prussian army has attacked Marshal Daun's Austrian force covering your siege of Prague, but the assault is faltering under heavy fire.
evt-06-18-1757-third-silesian-war.prompt: What must you do after this costly defeat?

choices.text: Lift the siege of Prague and withdraw from Bohemia
Negotiate a truce with Austria on the battlefield
Press forward and storm Prague immediately
Retreat all the way back to Berlin

evt-06-18-1757-third-silesian-war.butterflyEffect: Kolín was Frederick the Great's first major defeat and forced Prussia to abandon Bohemia entirely. The loss shifted momentum in the Seven Years' War, exposing Prussia to Austrian, Russian, and French pressure that nearly overwhelmed Frederick over the following years.

evt-06-18-1815-battle-of-waterloo.scenario: It's the afternoon of 18 June 1815 at Hougoumont farm, and wave after wave of French infantry hurls itself at your walls. Wellington has ordered the position held at all costs while the main battle rages beyond.
evt-06-18-1815-battle-of-waterloo.prompt: What is the outcome of the day-long fight for Hougoumont?

choices.text: Napoleon personally leads its capture
The farm falls by midday, exposing Wellington's flank
The garrison surrenders when ammunition runs out
The farm holds all day, anchoring Wellington's right flank

evt-06-18-1815-battle-of-waterloo.butterflyEffect: Hougoumont held throughout the battle, tying down a disproportionate number of French troops, including elements of the Imperial Guard. That drain on Napoleon's reserves, combined with the timely arrival of Blücher's Prussians, helped seal his defeat and end the Hundred Days, sending him into final exile on St Helena.

evt-06-18-1858-charles-darwin.scenario: It is June 1858 at Down House. You open a parcel from Alfred Russel Wallace in the Malay Archipelago and find, to your shock, an essay laying out a theory of natural selection nearly identical to the one you have kept unpublished for twenty years.
evt-06-18-1858-charles-darwin.prompt: What do you do with Wallace's manuscript?

choices.text: Destroy the letter and continue working in secret
Send a public letter denouncing Wallace's theory as plagiarism
Arrange a joint reading of both theories before the Linnean Society
Publish Wallace's essay under his own name to claim priority

evt-06-18-1858-charles-darwin.butterflyEffect: Darwin, with help from Charles Lyell and Joseph Hooker, arranged for extracts of his own work and Wallace's essay to be read jointly to the Linnean Society in July 1858, sharing credit without direct confrontation. The episode spurred Darwin to rapidly finish and publish On the Origin of Species the following year, reshaping biology forever.

evt-06-18-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 18 June 1940 in London. France has just collapsed and an armistice with Germany looms. You are a French soldier who has just heard General de Gaulle's radio broadcast urging France not to accept defeat.
evt-06-18-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: What do you do after hearing the Appeal of 18 June?

choices.text: Surrender to advancing German forces immediately
Return to France and accept the Vichy government
Flee to a neutral country and await the war's end
Cross to Britain and join the Free French forces

evt-06-18-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Thousands of French servicemen and civilians who heard or later read of the broadcast rallied to de Gaulle, forming the nucleus of the Free French forces that kept France fighting alongside the Allies. The speech became a founding text of the French Resistance and secured de Gaulle's postwar claim to speak for France.

evt-06-18-1954-carlos-castillo-armas.scenario: It is 18 June 1954. You march with Carlos Castillo Armas's exile force as it crosses from Honduras into Guatemala, backed by CIA planning and air support, aiming to topple President Jacobo Árbenz.
evt-06-18-1954-carlos-castillo-armas.prompt: What was the immediate outcome of this invasion in the weeks that followed?

choices.text: The United Nations intervened and restored the prior government
Guatemala and Honduras went to open war over the incursion
President Árbenz resigned and Castillo Armas took power
The invasion failed outright and Árbenz remained in office

evt-06-18-1954-carlos-castillo-armas.butterflyEffect: Facing CIA-orchestrated military and psychological pressure, Árbenz resigned in early July 1954, and Castillo Armas soon took the presidency. He reversed Árbenz's land reforms and banned leftist parties, setting Guatemala on a path toward decades of military rule and civil war, while the operation became a template the CIA would later try to repeat at the Bay of Pigs.

evt-06-18-1967-jimi-hendrix.scenario: It is 18 June 1967 at the Monterey Pop Festival. You watch Jimi Hendrix tear through a searing cover of 'Wild Thing,' knowing The Who smashed their gear earlier that day and Hendrix wants to top it.
evt-06-18-1967-jimi-hendrix.prompt: How does Hendrix cap off his performance to end the set?

choices.text: He auctions the guitar on stage to the highest bidder
He simply smashes the guitar against his amplifier without fire
He set the guitar on fire with lighter fluid, then smashes the burning remains
He hands the guitar, still playing, to a fan in the front row

evt-06-18-1967-jimi-hendrix.butterflyEffect: Hendrix knelt over his guitar, doused it in lighter fluid, and set it ablaze before smashing the burning remains and tossing pieces to the crowd. The stunt, captured on film, became one of rock's most iconic images and cemented his reputation as rock's most electrifying showman; fragments of guitars from similar stunts later sold for enormous sums at auction.

evt-06-18-1972-british-european-airways-.scenario: It is 18 June 1972. You are a first officer aboard a Trident jet climbing out of Heathrow toward Brussels, moments after a reduced-power takeoff. The aircraft is slow, and someone's hand is on the droop lever.
evt-06-18-1972-british-european-airways-.prompt: What action in the cockpit doomed the climb-out?

choices.text: The droops were retracted prematurely at too low a speed, causing a stall
The aircraft ran out of fuel due to a loading error
A bird strike disabled an engine shortly after liftoff
A bomb detonated in the cargo hold

evt-06-18-1972-british-european-airways-.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the leading-edge droops had been retracted far too early at low airspeed, stalling the Trident, which plunged into a field near Staines killing all 118 aboard—Britain's deadliest air disaster. The inquiry also raised questions about crew stress and health, prompting tighter cockpit procedures and stall-warning safeguards across the airline industry.

evt-06-18-1981-lockheed-f-117-nighthawk.scenario: It is June 18, 1981, at the secret Groom Lake test site in Nevada. You are the test pilot strapped into a bizarre, faceted black jet that almost no one is supposed to know exists, cleared for its first flight.
evt-06-18-1981-lockheed-f-117-nighthawk.prompt: What milestone does this flight achieve for military aviation?

choices.text: It becomes the first aircraft ever flown that was designed from the outset around stealth technology.
It becomes the first aircraft to break the sound barrier in level flight.
It becomes the first jet-powered aircraft to enter US Air Force service.
It becomes the first aircraft equipped with radar-guided missiles.

evt-06-18-1981-lockheed-f-117-nighthawk.butterflyEffect: The F-117 flew successfully and entered secret Air Force service in 1983, its existence not publicly confirmed until 1988. Its 1991 Gulf War debut, striking central Baghdad on the first night while evading Iraqi radar, proved stealth design could reshape modern air warfare and spurred a new generation of low-observable aircraft.

evt-06-18-1983-space-shuttle-challenger.scenario: You watch Challenger climb into the sky on 18 June 1983, carrying Sally Ride into orbit on its second mission. The orbiter still has a long career ahead of it.
evt-06-18-1983-space-shuttle-challenger.prompt: What ultimately becomes of Challenger three years later?

choices.text: It completes over 50 missions before being decommissioned
It is retired to a museum after ten years of service
It is destroyed 73 seconds after launch in January 1986, killing all seven aboard
It is transferred to the U.S. Air Force for classified missions

evt-06-18-1983-space-shuttle-challenger.butterflyEffect: Challenger disintegrated during launch of STS-51-L on 28 January 1986 due to an O-ring seal failure in cold weather, killing all seven crew including teacher Christa McAuliffe. The disaster grounded the shuttle fleet for 32 months and led to a major redesign of shuttle safety systems and NASA's management culture.

evt-06-18-1983-space-shuttle-program.scenario: It's 18 June 1983, and you are strapped into Space Shuttle Challenger as it thunders off the pad on mission STS-7. You are about to make history simply by being aboard.
evt-06-18-1983-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What historic first do you achieve on this flight?

choices.text: You become the first female shuttle commander
You become the first American woman in space
You become the first American to orbit the Moon
You become the first woman to walk in space

evt-06-18-1983-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: Sally Ride's flight made her the first American woman in space, following Soviet cosmonauts Valentina Tereshkova (1963) and Svetlana Savitskaya. Her visibility spurred NASA to recruit and fly far more women astronauts in subsequent decades, reshaping the astronaut corps' composition.

evt-06-18-1984-battle-of-orgreave.scenario: It is 18 June 1984 at the British Steel coking plant in Orgreave. You stand among thousands of striking miners facing lines of mounted police and riot shields, as tension over the picket boils toward violence.
evt-06-18-1984-battle-of-orgreave.prompt: What happened to the mass riot charges brought against arrested miners after this clash?

choices.text: The miners pleaded guilty in exchange for suspended sentences
Most miners were convicted of riot and served prison sentences
Charges were quietly dropped for lack of any witnesses
The trials collapsed after police evidence was discredited, and the miners were acquitted

evt-06-18-1984-battle-of-orgreave.butterflyEffect: The 1985 trials collapsed after it emerged that police officers' statements had been coordinated or fabricated, and all defendants were acquitted. The episode badly damaged trust in South Yorkshire Police and, alongside the later Hillsborough disaster, fuelled decades of campaigning for a full public inquiry into policing at Orgreave, which has never been granted.

evt-06-18-1994-the-troubles.scenario: It is the evening of 18 June 1994. Inside the packed Heights Bar in Loughinisland, County Down, customers are cheering Ireland's World Cup match against Italy, unaware that masked gunmen are approaching the door.
evt-06-18-1994-the-troubles.prompt: What did a later official investigation find about the RUC's handling of this attack?

choices.text: It found evidence of collusion between police and the loyalist gunmen, and failures to pursue known suspects
It attributed the attack to a feud within republican paramilitary groups
It confirmed the killers were swiftly identified, tried, and convicted
It concluded the RUC had acted properly and closed the case with no criticism

evt-06-18-1994-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: A 2016 Police Ombudsman report found collusion between the RUC and the loyalist gunmen, including failures to act on prior intelligence and to pursue known suspects. The findings, and a subsequent documentary, kept pressure on authorities for a full public inquiry into police collusion during the Troubles, a demand still unresolved decades later.

evt-06-18-1998-propair-flight-420.scenario: You are the captain of a Metroliner charter climbing out of Dorval airport on 18 June 1998 when a warning light shows fire in the engine nacelle, with Peterborough still far ahead.
evt-06-18-1998-propair-flight-420.prompt: What is the correct emergency response to the in-flight fire?

choices.text: Shut down all electrical systems and glide to a field
Circle to burn off fuel before returning to Dorval
Continue to the scheduled destination at reduced power
Divert immediately for an emergency landing at nearby Mirabel

evt-06-18-1998-propair-flight-420.butterflyEffect: The crew diverted to Mirabel, but the fire had already weakened the wing structure, which failed during landing; all eleven aboard were killed. The investigation into the fire's cause and the wing's failure led to changes in maintenance inspection and fire-detection procedures for similar aircraft.

evt-06-18-2007-charleston-sofa-super-sto.scenario: It's the evening of 18 June 2007 at the Charleston Sofa Super Store. Smoke is showing at the loading dock but the showroom looks calm, and crews are eager to push inside to search for trapped customers.
evt-06-18-2007-charleston-sofa-super-sto.prompt: What critical tactical decision shapes how the fire is fought?

choices.text: The building is fully evacuated before any entry is made
Crews commit to an aggressive interior search-and-attack
Command orders an immediate defensive exterior-only attack
Aerial ladder trucks survey the roof before any entry

evt-06-18-2007-charleston-sofa-super-sto.butterflyEffect: Crews committed to an aggressive interior search while fire spread unseen through the unsprinklered warehouse behind false walls, and the structure collapsed with nine firefighters still inside. It became one of the most studied line-of-duty-death incidents in US fire service history, driving national pushes for sprinkler mandates and stricter fireground command protocols.

evt-06-18-2009-lunar-reconnaissance-orbi.scenario: It is 18 June 2009 at Cape Canaveral. You watch an Atlas V rocket lift off carrying NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and its companion craft toward the Moon, tasked with mapping the lunar surface in unprecedented detail.
evt-06-18-2009-lunar-reconnaissance-orbi.prompt: What did LRO's detailed mapping data ultimately help NASA select for future missions?

choices.text: A location for a permanent radio telescope on the Moon's far side
The precise age of the Moon's core
A relay satellite network for Mars communications
Safe landing sites near the lunar south pole for future crewed missions

evt-06-18-2009-lunar-reconnaissance-orbi.butterflyEffect: LRO's high-resolution maps identified permanently shadowed polar craters holding water ice and produced detailed imagery of the old Apollo landing sites. That data became foundational for choosing candidate landing zones for NASA's Artemis program, decades after the orbiter's launch.

evt-06-18-2012-salman-of-saudi-arabia.scenario: It is June 2012 in Riyadh. Crown Prince Nayef has just died, and King Abdullah must choose the next heir to the Saudi throne from among his surviving half-brothers.
evt-06-18-2012-salman-of-saudi-arabia.prompt: Whom does King Abdullah name as the new crown prince?

choices.text: Mutaib bin Abdullah Al Saud
Bandar bin Sultan Al Saud
Muqrin bin Abdulaziz Al Saud
Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud

evt-06-18-2012-salman-of-saudi-arabia.butterflyEffect: Salman became crown prince and, on Abdullah's death in 2015, king. He soon elevated his own son, Mohammed bin Salman, to heir, concentrating power in ways that reshaped Saudi politics, economics, and foreign policy under the Vision 2030 program.

evt-06-19-1838-maryland.scenario: It is June 19, 1838, and you are a Jesuit provincial in Maryland weighing a contract to sell 272 enslaved men, women, and children to plantation owners in Louisiana to settle the province's debts.
evt-06-19-1838-maryland.prompt: What does the sale ultimately help fund?

choices.text: The continued operation and debts of Georgetown College, later Georgetown University
The founding of a new Jesuit college in Louisiana
A mission to convert Native Americans in the Louisiana Territory
The construction of a new cathedral in Baltimore

evt-06-19-1838-maryland.butterflyEffect: The sale separated families and sent them to harsher plantations in the Deep South. In 2016 Georgetown University publicly acknowledged the sale, and descendants of the 'GU272' pressed for reconciliation, leading the university to offer preferential admissions status and pursue a reparations fund.

evt-06-19-1846-baseball.scenario: It is 19 June 1846 at the Elysian Fields in Hoboken, New Jersey. You take the field with the New York Knickerbocker Base Ball Club against the New York Nine, playing under Alexander Cartwright's newly written rules for the first time.
evt-06-19-1846-baseball.prompt: How did this first officially recorded modern-rules game end?

choices.text: The Knickerbockers won in a rout
The game ended in a tie after darkness fell
The New York Nine defeated the Knickerbockers 23–1
Rain forced the game to be abandoned early

evt-06-19-1846-baseball.butterflyEffect: The New York Nine crushed the Knickerbockers 23–1, but the lopsided score mattered less than the rulebook itself. The Knickerbocker Rules, with features like foul lines and tagging runners instead of throwing the ball at them, became the template that modern baseball was built on.

evt-06-19-1865-juneteenth.scenario: It is June 19, 1865, in Galveston, Texas. Union Major General Gordon Granger stands before the assembled town to read a formal order enforcing the Emancipation Proclamation, more than two years after it was signed.
evt-06-19-1865-juneteenth.prompt: What does Granger's General Order No. 3 declare?

choices.text: That all enslaved people in Texas are free, with equal rights, and encouraged to work for wages
That the Confederate army must surrender its remaining weapons
That slaveholders will be compensated for freed laborers
That Texas will be readmitted to the Union immediately

evt-06-19-1865-juneteenth.butterflyEffect: News of freedom had been delayed to the last Confederate holdout state, and freed Texans began marking June 19 with annual celebrations the following year. Juneteenth spread nationwide through the Great Migration and Civil Rights era commemorations, becoming a federal holiday in 2021.

evt-06-19-1867-second-french-interventio.scenario: It is June 19, 1867, on the Cerro de las Campanas outside Querétaro. Emperor Maximilian I, abandoned by French troops and captured by Republican forces, faces a firing squad alongside two of his loyal generals.
evt-06-19-1867-second-french-interventio.prompt: What happens to Maximilian's Second Mexican Empire after his execution?

choices.text: It collapses entirely, and Benito Juárez's Republican government is restored to power
France sends fresh troops to restore the monarchy within months
It survives under regency until his son comes of age
The Mexican conservatives crown a new emperor from Austria

evt-06-19-1867-second-french-interventio.butterflyEffect: Juárez's restored republic ended foreign monarchy in the Americas and reasserted the Monroe Doctrine's relevance, discouraging further European intervention in the hemisphere. The episode also damaged Napoleon III's prestige at home, contributing to French weakness ahead of the Franco-Prussian War.

evt-06-19-1939-lou-gehrig.scenario: You are Lou Gehrig, the Yankees' "Iron Horse," who pulled himself from the lineup after 2,130 straight games. At the Mayo Clinic on 19 June 1939, doctors deliver a diagnosis: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, a fatal, incurable disease.
evt-06-19-1939-lou-gehrig.prompt: What did Gehrig do in the weeks after receiving this diagnosis?

choices.text: He sued the Yankees for concealing his condition
He quietly retired without any public statement
He delivered a farewell speech to a packed Yankee Stadium
He attempted to keep playing through the season

evt-06-19-1939-lou-gehrig.butterflyEffect: On 4 July 1939, Gehrig delivered his "Luckiest Man" farewell speech at Yankee Stadium, one of the most famous speeches in sports history. ALS became widely known in America as "Lou Gehrig's disease," and the Yankees retired his number 4 that year, the first uniform retirement in MLB history.

evt-06-19-1953-julius-and-ethel-rosenber.scenario: It is the evening of 19 June 1953 at Sing Sing prison. Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, convicted of passing atomic secrets to the Soviet Union, have exhausted their appeals as worldwide clemency pleas pour in.
evt-06-19-1953-julius-and-ethel-rosenber.prompt: What does the final decision on clemency turn out to be?

choices.text: The Supreme Court grants an indefinite stay
Eisenhower commutes both sentences to life imprisonment
A new trial is ordered on appeal
Clemency is denied and the execution proceeds

evt-06-19-1953-julius-and-ethel-rosenber.butterflyEffect: President Eisenhower refused to intervene, and the Rosenbergs were executed that night, becoming the first American civilians put to death for espionage. Their case became a lasting flashpoint in Cold War politics, later intelligence (the Venona decrypts) confirming Julius's spying while Ethel's exact role remained fiercely debated for decades.

evt-06-19-1965-nguyen-cao-ky.scenario: It is 19 June 1965 in Saigon. South Vietnam's government has collapsed yet again, and you sit with the young generals of the Armed Forces Council deciding who will lead the new military junta.
evt-06-19-1965-nguyen-cao-ky.prompt: Who does the council choose to head the government as prime minister?

choices.text: Nguyễn Văn Thiệu
Dương Văn Minh
Nguyễn Cao Kỳ
Nguyễn Khánh

evt-06-19-1965-nguyen-cao-ky.butterflyEffect: The generals picked the flamboyant air force commander Nguyễn Cao Kỳ, who steadied the junta enough for the United States to escalate its commitment to the war. Kỳ later became vice president under his rival Nguyễn Văn Thiệu from 1967 to 1971, their uneasy partnership shaping South Vietnam's wartime leadership.

evt-06-19-1987-basque-nationalism.scenario: It is 19 June 1987, and a car bomb planted by ETA has just torn through the underground parking garage of the Hipercor shopping centre in Barcelona, killing and injuring dozens of shoppers.
evt-06-19-1987-basque-nationalism.prompt: What lasting effect did this attack have on ETA's campaign?

choices.text: The bombing sped up the Basque Country's path to full independence
It provoked mass public outrage, even among Basque nationalists, and eroded sympathy for ETA's cause
The Spanish government opened immediate peace talks with ETA
ETA announced a permanent ceasefire within weeks

evt-06-19-1987-basque-nationalism.butterflyEffect: The Hipercor bombing killed 21 people and remains ETA's deadliest single attack. It sparked mass protests across Spain, including in the Basque Country itself, and hardened both government policy and public opinion against the group, a shift that slowly isolated ETA in the decades before its 2018 dissolution.

evt-06-19-1988-pope-john-paul-ii.scenario: You stand in St. Peter's Square on 19 June 1988 as Pope John Paul II formally declares 117 Vietnamese Catholics, martyred over the preceding centuries of persecution, to be saints of the Church.
evt-06-19-1988-pope-john-paul-ii.prompt: What did this canonization mean for Vietnam's Catholic community afterward?

choices.text: It gave Vietnam's Catholics a lasting symbol of resilience despite continued state restrictions
It triggered a wave of Vietnamese Catholics emigrating to Rome
It led to the restoration of Vatican-Vietnam diplomatic relations that year
It immediately ended religious persecution in Vietnam

evt-06-19-1988-pope-john-paul-ii.butterflyEffect: The ceremony became a lasting symbol of endurance for Vietnamese Catholics still living under a wary communist state, deepening devotion and pilgrimage to the martyrs' shrines. It did not end state monitoring of the Church, but it strengthened Catholic identity and cross-border solidarity with the Vietnamese diaspora.

evt-06-19-2005-auto-racing.scenario: It is race day at the 2005 United States Grand Prix in Indianapolis. Michelin has just told your team its tyres cannot safely handle the banked final corner after violent practice crashes, and race stewards have rejected your proposed chicane fix.
evt-06-19-2005-auto-racing.prompt: As a Michelin-supplied team principal, what do you decide?

choices.text: Borrow spare Bridgestone tyres from a rival team
Withdraw your cars after the pace lap, leaving the grid to Bridgestone runners
Race anyway and hope the tyres hold up
Refuse to send your cars out for the pace lap at all

evt-06-19-2005-auto-racing.butterflyEffect: Fourteen Michelin-shod cars pulled in after the pace lap, leaving just six Bridgestone runners to complete a farcical race won by Michael Schumacher. Furious fans booed and threw debris, lawsuits followed, and the debacle pushed Formula One toward mandating a single tyre supplier starting in 2007.

evt-06-19-2005-michelin.scenario: Days after the Indianapolis fiasco, you are a Michelin executive facing a flood of angry letters and lawsuit threats from ticket-holders who watched only six cars race.
evt-06-19-2005-michelin.prompt: What did Michelin actually do to address the backlash?

choices.text: Offer financial compensation, worth millions of dollars, to affected ticket-holders
Withdraw from Formula One competition for the remainder of the decade
Successfully sue the FIA for forcing the tyre crisis
Ban its teams from ever racing on oval circuits again

evt-06-19-2005-michelin.butterflyEffect: Michelin paid out roughly $20 per ticket, totalling millions of dollars, to placate furious fans and avoid prolonged litigation. The embarrassment accelerated Formula One's shift toward a single tyre supplier, and Michelin left F1 at the end of 2006 rather than continue the costly tyre war with Bridgestone.

evt-06-19-2009-war-in-afghanistan-2001-2.scenario: It is 19 June 2009 in Helmand Province, Afghanistan. You command British troops launching Operation Panther's Claw into the Babaji area, weeks before Afghans are due to vote in a presidential election.
evt-06-19-2009-war-in-afghanistan-2001-2.prompt: What was the operation intended to accomplish before the election?

choices.text: Secure the road link to the Pakistani border
Establish a permanent British base in Kabul
Clear the Babaji area of Taliban to enable safer voting
Capture Taliban founder Mullah Omar

evt-06-19-2009-war-in-afghanistan-2001-2.butterflyEffect: British forces pushed Taliban fighters out of the Babaji canal zone to allow safer voting conditions, but the campaign proved one of the costliest of the war for Britain, fueling fierce debate at home over the mission's cost. It also set the stage for the larger joint operation, Moshtarak, launched with US and Afghan forces the following year.

evt-06-19-2010-wedding-of-victoria-crown.scenario: You are covering the royal wedding at Stockholm Cathedral on 19 June 2010, where Crown Princess Victoria marries Daniel Westling, her former personal trainer, in what press call Europe's biggest royal wedding since 1981.
evt-06-19-2010-wedding-of-victoria-crown.prompt: What title did Daniel Westling receive upon marrying the Crown Princess?

choices.text: He was named King consort of Sweden
He became Duke of Västergötland
He received no formal title
He was made a foreign ambassador as a courtesy title

evt-06-19-2010-wedding-of-victoria-crown.butterflyEffect: Daniel acquired Victoria's ducal title, becoming Duke of Västergötland and Prince of Sweden, the first commoner to marry into the Swedish royal house in modern times. The marriage reflected a broader modernizing trend among European monarchies and positioned their future children in the line of succession.

evt-06-19-2012-assange-v-swedish-prosecu.scenario: It is 19 June 2012 in London. You are Julian Assange, wanted for extradition to Sweden over sexual assault allegations, and you have just breached your bail conditions with the courts closing in.
evt-06-19-2012-assange-v-swedish-prosecu.prompt: What does Assange do to escape extradition?

choices.text: He surrenders to Swedish authorities voluntarily
He appeals directly to the European Court of Human Rights and waits at home
He flees to Moscow on a diplomatic passport
He seeks asylum inside Ecuador's embassy in London

evt-06-19-2012-assange-v-swedish-prosecu.butterflyEffect: He sought asylum inside Ecuador's embassy in London, where Ecuador granted him refuge, trapping him there for nearly seven years until British police dragged him out in 2019. The standoff turned WikiLeaks and Assange into a global flashpoint over press freedom, extradition law, and diplomatic asylum.

evt-06-20-1782-congress-of-the-confedera.scenario: You're a delegate reviewing the final design for the young nation's Great Seal in June 1782: an eagle grasping an olive branch and arrows, with a ribbon left for a motto.
evt-06-20-1782-congress-of-the-confedera.prompt: What Latin motto does Congress adopt for the new seal?

choices.text: Novus Ordo Seclorum
In God We Trust
E Pluribus Unum
Annuit Coeptis

evt-06-20-1782-congress-of-the-confedera.butterflyEffect: Congress approved "E Pluribus Unum" — Out of Many, One — along with Charles Thomson's eagle design. The seal became the enduring emblem of the United States, still affixed to treaties, currency, and official documents more than two centuries later.

evt-06-20-1837-queen-victoria.scenario: It's dawn on 20 June 1837 at Kensington Palace, and messengers rouse you from sleep to tell you that King William IV has died in the night, making you queen at eighteen.
evt-06-20-1837-queen-victoria.prompt: What is your first act as the new monarch?

choices.text: Immediately dissolve Parliament and call new elections
Delay accepting the crown until your coronation ceremony
Summon the Privy Council to formally proclaim your accession
Retreat to mourn privately before addressing any state business

evt-06-20-1837-queen-victoria.butterflyEffect: Victoria met her Privy Council that same morning, insisting on receiving them alone without her mother's advisers, a small act signalling her independence. Her reign that followed lasted 63 years, the longest of any British monarch until Elizabeth II, and gave its name to the Victorian era of industrial and imperial expansion.

evt-06-20-1900-boxer-rebellion.scenario: It's 20 June 1900 in Peking, and word arrives that Boxer fighters and imperial troops are closing in on the foreign Legation Quarter where you and hundreds of diplomats, missionaries, and civilians have taken refuge.
evt-06-20-1900-boxer-rebellion.prompt: What should the legations' defenders do as the siege begins?

choices.text: Attempt to flee the city under cover of darkness
Surrender immediately to avoid provoking the Qing court
Negotiate a separate truce with local Boxer leaders
Fortify the legation compounds and hold out for a relief force

evt-06-20-1900-boxer-rebellion.butterflyEffect: The defenders held the Legation Quarter for 55 days until an Eight-Nation Alliance relief force broke the siege in August 1900. The rebellion's defeat forced the Qing dynasty into the humiliating Boxer Protocol, deepening the dynasty's decline in the years before its collapse in 1911.

evt-06-20-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is June 1943, and you're a Lancaster crew of RAF Bomber Command who has just struck the Zeppelin works at Friedrichshafen, a factory producing German radar sets. Turning for home would mean crossing heavily defended airspace in daylight.
evt-06-20-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: Where do you fly to avoid German night-fighter defenses on the return leg?

choices.text: Fly on to land at an Allied airfield in French North Africa
Ditch the aircraft in the Mediterranean and be rescued
Return directly across occupied France to England
Land in neutral Switzerland to refuel

evt-06-20-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The bombers flew on to land at Blida airfield in French North Africa instead of returning to Britain, one of the first RAF shuttle-bombing raids. The tactic reduced exposure to enemy defenses and damaged German radar production, and it became a model for later long-range Allied bombing operations.

evt-06-20-1960-mali-federation.scenario: It is 20 June 1960 in Dakar. You stand beside Premier Modibo Keïta as the tricolor of France is lowered and the flag of the new Mali Federation, uniting Senegal and the Sudanese Republic, is raised for the first time.
evt-06-20-1960-mali-federation.prompt: What happens to this federation just two months after independence?

choices.text: It collapses when Senegal withdraws after an army mobilization crisis
It merges its currency and military fully with Ivory Coast
It expands to formally absorb French Guinea
It is dissolved and both territories rejoin the French Community permanently

evt-06-20-1960-mali-federation.butterflyEffect: On 19 August 1960 Sudanese Republic leaders mobilized the army to seize control; Senegal countered with its gendarmerie, and the next day Senegal withdrew from the federation. The Sudanese Republic renamed itself the Republic of Mali, with Modibo Keïta becoming its first president, while Senegal continued alone under Léopold Senghor.

evt-06-20-1975-steven-spielberg.scenario: It's June 1975, and you're a marketing executive at Universal Pictures deciding how to launch a shark thriller nobody in the industry has tried to sell this way before.
evt-06-20-1975-steven-spielberg.prompt: What unconventional release strategy do you approve for Jaws?

choices.text: Limit it to drive-in theaters for a summer test run
Release it wide nationwide with saturation TV advertising
Use a slow platform release, expanding city by city
Debut it only as a roadshow with reserved seating

evt-06-20-1975-steven-spielberg.butterflyEffect: Universal opened Jaws wide on hundreds of screens backed by heavy national TV advertising, breaking from the traditional slow city-by-city rollout. The gamble paid off spectacularly, and studios soon copied the formula, creating the modern summer blockbuster model that still shapes Hollywood release schedules today.

evt-06-20-1979-bill-stewart-journalist.scenario: You are an ABC News correspondent in Managua on 20 June 1979, filming the Sandinista uprising against Somoza. Your crew approaches a National Guard checkpoint to ask for passage, and a soldier orders you to lie face down on the ground.
evt-06-20-1979-bill-stewart-journalist.prompt: What happened next, captured on your own camera crew's film?

choices.text: He was arrested and deported to the United States
He was executed on the spot by the soldier
He bribed his way past the checkpoint
He was questioned briefly and allowed to continue filming

evt-06-20-1979-bill-stewart-journalist.butterflyEffect: The soldier executed Stewart on the spot, and the footage aired repeatedly on American television, shocking viewers and turning U.S. public opinion sharply against the Somoza regime. Congressional and public pressure accelerated the collapse of American support for Somoza, who fled Nicaragua within weeks as the Sandinistas took power.

evt-06-20-1979-abc-news-united-states.scenario: You're a television correspondent covering the Nicaraguan uprising in June 1979, approaching a National Guard checkpoint in Managua with your cameraman rolling.
evt-06-20-1979-abc-news-united-states.prompt: What happens when Bill Stewart is stopped and ordered to lie on the ground?

choices.text: He is turned back and escorted to safety
He is shot dead by a National Guard soldier despite complying
He is waved through the checkpoint without incident
He is briefly detained and released unharmed

evt-06-20-1979-abc-news-united-states.butterflyEffect: A National Guard soldier shot Stewart dead while he lay prone, and his own cameraman captured it on film, which aired on American television. The graphic footage shocked the US public, hastened the collapse of support for the Somoza government, and hastened the Sandinistas' eventual victory that July.

evt-06-20-1982-corbeta-uruguay-base.scenario: It's 20 June 1982 on remote Southern Thule, days after Argentina's surrender in the Falklands War, and your Royal Marine detachment approaches the isolated Corbeta Uruguay base to demand its garrison give up.
evt-06-20-1982-corbeta-uruguay-base.prompt: What is the best approach to end this outpost's occupation?

choices.text: Bombard the base from offshore before landing
Wait for the garrison to run out of supplies and abandon it
Launch a full assault to retake the base by force
Offer the garrison a peaceful surrender without firing a shot

evt-06-20-1982-corbeta-uruguay-base.butterflyEffect: The Argentine garrison surrendered without resistance, and the base was soon dismantled, closing the last active Argentine foothold in the South Sandwich Islands. Its bloodless end marked the formal conclusion of British military operations from the Falklands War.

evt-06-20-1988-leslie-manigat.scenario: It is early 1988 and you have just been sworn in as Haiti's president under a military-controlled election. You know real power still rests with army commander Henri Namphy, and you decide to test that power by reshuffling the military's top ranks.
evt-06-20-1988-leslie-manigat.prompt: What happened when Manigat challenged Namphy's authority in June 1988?

choices.text: He was reelected in a snap referendum
He was ousted in a coup led by Namphy
He resigned voluntarily to avoid conflict
He won a decisive power struggle over the army

evt-06-20-1988-leslie-manigat.butterflyEffect: Namphy's loyalists staged a coup that removed Manigat after barely four months in office. Far from stabilizing Haiti, the coup opened a cycle of further military takeovers—Namphy himself was overthrown just months later—delaying any real democratic transition until Jean-Bertrand Aristide's election in 1990.

evt-06-20-1990-asteroid.scenario: On the night of 20 June 1990, you're peering through a telescope, tracking a faint point of light drifting near Mars's orbital path.
evt-06-20-1990-asteroid.prompt: What should you do to confirm this object's unusual status?

choices.text: Calculate its orbit to see if it shares Mars's orbital path as a trojan
Classify it immediately as a comet because of a faint tail
Dismiss it as background noise since Mars has no known asteroids
Assume it's a captured moon of Mars and stop tracking it

evt-06-20-1990-asteroid.butterflyEffect: Astronomer David Levy's discovery, later named 5261 Eureka, was confirmed as the first known Mars trojan asteroid, sharing Mars's orbit at a stable Lagrangian point. The find opened a new search for similar objects and sharpened understanding of resonant asteroid populations throughout the Solar System.

evt-06-20-1990-1990-manjil-rudbar-earthq.scenario: It is late June 1990 in northern Iran. The magnitude 7.4 Manjil–Rudbar earthquake has just leveled towns across a vast stretch of the Caspian region, and officials must decide how the country builds back.
evt-06-20-1990-1990-manjil-rudbar-earthq.prompt: What lasting change follows in how Iran approaches construction?

choices.text: Iran prohibits any buildings taller than one story nationwide
Iran bans reconstruction in the affected provinces entirely
Iran adopts stricter seismic building codes for new construction
Iran leaves building standards unchanged

evt-06-20-1990-1990-manjil-rudbar-earthq.butterflyEffect: The catastrophic collapse of poorly built masonry structures, which caused most of the tens of thousands of deaths, pushed Iranian authorities toward stricter seismic building codes and reinforced construction standards in the following years. The disaster remains one of the deadliest earthquakes of the 20th century.

evt-06-20-1991-bundestag.scenario: You're a member of the German Bundestag in June 1991, casting a vote on whether the reunified nation's parliament and government should relocate from Bonn to Berlin.
evt-06-20-1991-bundestag.prompt: How does this closely contested vote conclude?

choices.text: It narrowly votes to move the seat of government to Berlin
It votes decisively to keep Bonn as the permanent capital
It votes to split government functions evenly between both cities
It postpones the decision indefinitely for further study

evt-06-20-1991-bundestag.butterflyEffect: The Bundestag voted narrowly, 338 to 320, to make Berlin the seat of government and parliament, completing the symbolic reunification of the country. Bonn nonetheless retained several federal ministries under a later compromise, and the actual move took years to complete.

evt-06-20-1994-imam-reza-shrine-bombing.scenario: It's Ashura, 20 June 1994, and you are among the pilgrims crowded into the prayer hall at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad, one of Shia Islam's holiest sites, when an explosion tears through the gathering.
evt-06-20-1994-imam-reza-shrine-bombing.prompt: What did Iranian authorities do in the aftermath of the bombing?

choices.text: Accuse a rival Sunni state and sever diplomatic ties
Close the shrine permanently to prevent further attacks
Blame the exiled Mujahedin-e-Khalq and launch mass arrests
Ignore the attack publicly to avoid panic among pilgrims

evt-06-20-1994-imam-reza-shrine-bombing.butterflyEffect: Iran's government attributed the bombing to the exiled opposition group Mujahedin-e-Khalq, leading to arrests and executions of alleged conspirators. The attack deepened Tehran's hostility toward the group and hardened security around Shia holy sites during later Ashura commemorations.

evt-06-20-1996-space-shuttle-columbia.scenario: It is June 1996, and Space Shuttle Columbia has been in orbit for over two weeks on STS-78, its crew running an unusually long slate of life science and microgravity experiments in the Spacelab module.
evt-06-20-1996-space-shuttle-columbia.prompt: What milestone does this extended mission achieve for the shuttle program?

choices.text: It sets a new record for the longest Space Shuttle mission to date
It deploys the Hubble Space Telescope
It completes the first shuttle docking with the Mir space station
It flies the first American woman commander

evt-06-20-1996-space-shuttle-columbia.butterflyEffect: STS-78 became the longest Space Shuttle mission flown up to that point, lasting nearly 17 days, and its extensive life-science data helped inform how astronauts would later be monitored during long stays aboard the International Space Station.

evt-06-20-2003-wikimedia-foundation.scenario: It is 2003, and Wikipedia has grown far beyond what Jimmy Wales's for-profit company Bomis was built to support. You must decide how the encyclopedia and its sister projects will be funded and governed going forward.
evt-06-20-2003-wikimedia-foundation.prompt: What structure do you choose to sustain Wikipedia beyond Bomis?

choices.text: Hand control to a government-funded research agency
Sell the project to an established encyclopedia publisher
Keep Wikipedia as a product of Bomis, funded by advertising
Create an independent nonprofit foundation funded by donations

evt-06-20-2003-wikimedia-foundation.butterflyEffect: Wales established the Wikimedia Foundation as a nonprofit in St. Petersburg, Florida, funded by donations rather than advertising or ownership by a single company. The foundation went on to host fourteen collaborative projects and steward MediaWiki, the software still powering wikis worldwide.

evt-06-20-2011-rusair-flight-9605.scenario: It's night on 20 June 2011, and your Tupolev Tu-134 is on final approach to Petrozavodsk, wrapped in thick fog with the runway lights barely visible below.
evt-06-20-2011-rusair-flight-9605.prompt: What should the crew have done as visibility fell below safe minimums?

choices.text: Descend below the minimum decision height to get a visual fix on the runway
Execute a go-around and divert to an airport with clear weather
Hold overhead until the fog cleared, burning remaining fuel
Continue the approach on instruments alone, trusting the glide slope

evt-06-20-2011-rusair-flight-9605.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew continued descending below the decision height in the fog and struck trees short of the runway, killing 47 of the 52 aboard. The disaster renewed scrutiny of Russia's aging Tu-134 fleet and hastened the type's retirement from passenger service.

evt-06-20-2019-2019-iranian-shoot-down-o.scenario: It is the night of 20 June 2019, and you are advising President Trump in the White House Situation Room. Iran's Revolutionary Guard has just shot down a U.S. Global Hawk drone over the Strait of Hormuz, and retaliatory airstrikes on Iranian targets are already being readied for launch.
evt-06-20-2019-2019-iranian-shoot-down-o.prompt: What did Trump ultimately decide about the retaliatory strikes?

choices.text: He flew to Tehran to negotiate directly
He let the retaliatory strikes proceed as planned
He publicly denied the drone had been shot down
He called off the strikes minutes before launch

evt-06-20-2019-2019-iranian-shoot-down-o.butterflyEffect: Trump called off the strikes roughly ten minutes before launch, reportedly after learning they could kill around 150 people, judging the response disproportionate to a downed drone. The crisis instead shifted toward cyberattacks and sanctions, but tensions kept simmering and escalated further into 2020, culminating in the killing of Qasem Soleimani.

evt-06-20-2025-2025-enderlin-tornado.scenario: It is the morning after 20 June 2025. You are a National Weather Service damage surveyor walking the shredded path near Enderlin, North Dakota, where engineered structures were leveled and debris was thrown for miles.
evt-06-20-2025-2025-enderlin-tornado.prompt: Based on the damage, what rating do you assign this tornado?

choices.text: EF5
EF3
F5 on the original Fujita scale
EF4

evt-06-20-2025-2025-enderlin-tornado.butterflyEffect: Surveyors confirmed EF5 damage with winds over 210 mph, the first EF5 rating issued in the United States in 12 years, since the 2013 Moore, Oklahoma tornado. It became the deadliest tornado to strike North Dakota since 1978, killing three people and renewing debate over rural tornado warning times.

evt-06-21-bce217-second-punic-war.scenario: You march with the Roman army of consul Gaius Flaminius along the misty shore of Lake Trasimene in 217 BC, pursuing Hannibal's retreating Carthaginians, unaware his men are concealed in the surrounding hills.
evt-06-21-bce217-second-punic-war.prompt: What happens as Hannibal springs his trap on the strung-out Roman column?

choices.text: The Romans break through and rout Hannibal's army
Hannibal offers terms and the two armies disperse without battle
Flaminius detects the ambush in time and withdraws safely
Hannibal's concealed troops ambush and destroy the Roman column along the shore

evt-06-21-bce217-second-punic-war.butterflyEffect: Hannibal's hidden forces annihilated the Roman army, killing Flaminius and thousands of his men in one of Rome's worst defeats. The disaster forced Rome to appoint Fabius Maximus dictator, whose cautious delaying strategy against Hannibal would ultimately help save the Republic.

evt-06-21-1529-war-of-the-league-of-cogn.scenario: You serve under Francis de Bourbon, Count of Saint-Pol, as your French army camps near Landriano in Lombardy in June 1529. Imperial Spanish troops under Antonio de Leyva have appeared with startling speed.
evt-06-21-1529-war-of-the-league-of-cogn.prompt: What happens to the French army in this encounter?

choices.text: It wins a decisive victory over the Spanish
It is destroyed and its commander captured
It withdraws safely across the Alps
It is relieved by Venetian reinforcements

evt-06-21-1529-war-of-the-league-of-cogn.butterflyEffect: The French force was routed and Saint-Pol himself captured. The disaster crippled France's ability to press its Italian claims, paving the way for the Peace of Cambrai later that year, in which Francis I renounced his Italian ambitions to Charles V.

evt-06-21-1788-new-hampshire.scenario: It is June 1788 in Exeter, New Hampshire, and you are a delegate at the state's ratifying convention, aware that eight states have already approved the new Constitution and only one more vote is needed to bring it into force.
evt-06-21-1788-new-hampshire.prompt: What did New Hampshire's ratification on 21 June 1788 achieve?

choices.text: It made the Constitution legally operative as the ninth ratification
It compelled Virginia to reject the Constitution
It forced Rhode Island to secede from the union
It triggered the drafting of the Bill of Rights

evt-06-21-1788-new-hampshire.butterflyEffect: New Hampshire became the ninth state to ratify, meeting the threshold the Constitution itself required to take legal effect, even though Virginia and New York had not yet voted. This cleared the way for the new federal government to organize under Washington in 1789, though the outcome in the larger, still-undecided states remained politically uncertain for weeks after.

evt-06-21-1848-wallachian-revolution-of-.scenario: It's 21 June 1848 in Bucharest. Ion Heliade Rădulescu and Christian Tell have just forced Prince Gheorghe Bibescu to accept a provisional government. As a leader of the new regime, you must decide what to promise the crowds gathered at Islaz regarding the boyars' feudal privileges.
evt-06-21-1848-wallachian-revolution-of-.prompt: What does the new provisional government proclaim regarding boyar privilege?

choices.text: Preserve boyar privileges to secure noble support
Abolish boyar privileges and enact liberal reforms per the Proclamation of Islaz
Declare full independence from the Ottoman Empire immediately
Restore the exiled prince to calm Russian fears

evt-06-21-1848-wallachian-revolution-of-.butterflyEffect: The Proclamation of Islaz promised the end of certain feudal obligations and a future National Assembly, alarming the Ottomans and Russians, who invaded later in 1848 to crush the movement and restore the old order. Though short-lived, its liberal ideals and leaders fed directly into the 1859 union of Wallachia and Moldavia that created modern Romania.

evt-06-21-1864-new-zealand-wars.scenario: You march with Colonel Greer's British column near Tauranga on 21 June 1864, tracking Māori warriors of the King Movement who are still digging fresh rifle pits at Te Ranga, months after their triumph at Gate Pā.
evt-06-21-1864-new-zealand-wars.prompt: What should Greer order upon finding the entrenchments unfinished?

choices.text: Open negotiations for a ceasefire
Attack at once before the defences are finished
Withdraw and wait for artillery to arrive
Retreat to fortified positions at Tauranga

evt-06-21-1864-new-zealand-wars.butterflyEffect: Greer attacked immediately, before the pits could be completed, and the British broke through in close combat. The victory at Te Ranga avenged Gate Pā and effectively ended the Tauranga campaign, hastening land confiscations across the Bay of Plenty.

evt-06-21-1898-capture-of-guam.scenario: You are a Spanish official on Guam in June 1898, cut off from news of the outside world, when the American cruiser USS Charleston suddenly anchors offshore and fires its guns.
evt-06-21-1898-capture-of-guam.prompt: What does the isolated Spanish garrison do when confronted by the American warship?

choices.text: Send a ship to Manila to request reinforcements before responding
Surrender at once, having no knowledge the two nations were at war
Open fire from coastal fortifications
Flee inland to wage guerrilla resistance

evt-06-21-1898-capture-of-guam.butterflyEffect: The garrison, unaware Spain and the U.S. were even at war, surrendered without a fight. Guam passed to American control and was formally ceded under the Treaty of Paris later that year, becoming a lasting U.S. Pacific territory and naval outpost.

evt-06-21-1919-winnipeg-general-strike.scenario: It is 21 June 1919 in Winnipeg. You stand with thousands of strikers on Main Street as a silent parade turns tense, and mounted police begin advancing on the crowd.
evt-06-21-1919-winnipeg-general-strike.prompt: What happens as the Royal North-West Mounted Police charge the strikers?

choices.text: Strikers scatter under the charge and two men are killed, dozens more injured
Strike leaders negotiate a truce with police on the spot
The crowd overwhelms the police and forces immediate concessions
The mayor personally halts the charge before anyone is hurt

evt-06-21-1919-winnipeg-general-strike.butterflyEffect: The clash, remembered as Bloody Saturday, left two strikers dead and dozens injured as police and federal troops broke up the crowd. Strike leaders were arrested and the general strike collapsed days later, but the episode became a founding legend of Canadian labour politics, shaping figures like J.S. Woodsworth who later helped found the CCF.

evt-06-21-1921-irish-war-of-independence.scenario: It is 21 June 1921 in Knockcroghery, County Roscommon. British forces have moved into the village in reprisal for IRA activity, and you watch soldiers set fire to the shops and houses along the main street.
evt-06-21-1921-irish-war-of-independence.prompt: What happens to the village that night?

choices.text: Local priests negotiate a halt before the fires are lit
Most of the village's buildings are destroyed by fire
The RIC intervenes to stop the burning and rebuilds the homes
The IRA repels the soldiers before any damage is done

evt-06-21-1921-irish-war-of-independence.butterflyEffect: Most of Knockcroghery was burned to the ground, one of many reprisal burnings carried out by British forces during the war. Coming just weeks before the July 1921 truce, such reprisals intensified public revulsion at British tactics and hardened support for Irish independence.

evt-06-21-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 21 June 1940. Mussolini's army has launched a full assault on your fortified positions in the French Alps, even as Paris negotiates an armistice with Germany. You command a garrison on the Alpine Line, unsure whether resistance still matters.
evt-06-21-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: What do you do as Italian forces attack while an armistice looms?

choices.text: Hold the fortified Alpine Line and repel the attacks
Surrender to negotiate favorable terms with Italy
Retreat immediately to avoid encirclement
Counterattack into Italian territory

evt-06-21-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: French Alpine defenders held their fortified line, and Italy's offensive gained almost no ground despite heavy casualties, embarrassing Mussolini just before the armistice took effect. The poor showing exposed Italian military weakness, a pattern that later forced Hitler to prop up struggling Italian campaigns in Greece and North Africa.

evt-06-21-1948-manchester-baby.scenario: You are an engineer at the University of Manchester on 21 June 1948, watching Frederic Williams, Tom Kilburn, and Geoff Tootill attempt to run a program on their new machine, the Small-Scale Experimental Machine.
evt-06-21-1948-manchester-baby.prompt: What historic milestone does the machine achieve moments later?

choices.text: It successfully breaks a wartime Enigma-coded message
It executes a stored program from memory, the first machine ever to do so
It links electronically to a second computer for the first time
It calculates pi to a record number of digits

evt-06-21-1948-manchester-baby.butterflyEffect: The Baby successfully ran a stored program to find the highest factor of a number, proving that instructions and data could share the same electronic memory, the core idea behind nearly all modern computers. The success led directly to the commercial Ferranti Mark 1 and cemented Manchester's place at the birth of computer science.

evt-06-21-1957-ellen-fairclough.scenario: It is 21 June 1957 in Ottawa. You are a newly elected Progressive Conservative MP for Hamilton West as Prime Minister John Diefenbaker forms his first cabinet.
evt-06-21-1957-ellen-fairclough.prompt: What historic first are you about to achieve when sworn in?

choices.text: You become the first woman to lead a federal political party
You become the first woman appointed to the Senate
You become the first woman elected to the House of Commons
You become the first woman appointed to the federal cabinet

evt-06-21-1957-ellen-fairclough.butterflyEffect: Ellen Fairclough became the first woman to serve in the Canadian federal cabinet. She later served as Minister of Citizenship and Immigration, where she pushed reforms reducing racial discrimination in immigration policy, and her appointment opened the door for later generations of women in Canadian federal politics.

evt-06-21-1973-supreme-court-of-the-unit.scenario: You run a small bookstore in California in 1973, and local prosecutors have charged you under obscenity law for material you sell through the mail. The Supreme Court has just handed down its ruling in Miller v. California.
evt-06-21-1973-supreme-court-of-the-unit.prompt: What new test did the Court set for deciding whether material is legally obscene?

choices.text: It was banned in the state where it was mailed, regardless of content
It was produced primarily for commercial profit
It appeals to prurient interest, is patently offensive under state law, and lacks serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value
It violates federal broadcast decency standards

evt-06-21-1973-supreme-court-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: The 'Miller test' replaced the vaguer 'utterly without redeeming social value' standard, requiring works to appeal to prurient interest, be patently offensive under state law, and lack serious literary, artistic, political or scientific value. It let local community standards vary by state, shaping American obscenity prosecutions and adult-content regulation for decades afterward.
