evt-06-21-2000-bill-clinton.scenario: You served with the 442nd Regimental Combat Team in Italy in 1944, decorated with a Distinguished Service Cross for valor under fire. Decades later, you learn the Pentagon has reviewed WWII records and found the medal you received was capped by racial bias.
evt-06-21-2000-bill-clinton.prompt: What does President Clinton do on 21 June 2000 to correct this?

choices.text: He orders a new law lowering the threshold for the Medal of Honor
He responds to a class-action lawsuit filed by veterans' families
He signs a bill waiving the statute of limitations on military honors
He awards 22 Asian American veterans the Medal of Honor after a bias review of their records

evt-06-21-2000-bill-clinton.butterflyEffect: Clinton upgraded 22 Asian American WWII veterans, including future Senator Daniel Inouye, from lesser decorations to the Medal of Honor. The ceremony formally acknowledged decades of discrimination against Japanese American soldiers and cemented the 100th/442nd's legacy as the most decorated unit of its size in US military history.

evt-06-21-2006-pluto.scenario: It's early 2006. As part of the team that spotted two faint new moons circling Pluto in 2005 (nicknamed P1 and P2), you must submit official names to the International Astronomical Union, fitting the underworld mythology already used for Pluto and its moon Charon.
evt-06-21-2006-pluto.prompt: What names do you propose for Pluto's two newly discovered moons?

choices.text: Kerberos and Styx
Charon and Nyx
Nix and Hydra
Persephone and Erebus

evt-06-21-2006-pluto.butterflyEffect: The IAU adopted Nix and Hydra in June 2006, names chosen partly because their initials echoed the New Horizons spacecraft then en route to Pluto. New Horizons photographed both moons up close in 2015, and two more moons found in 2011 and 2012 were later named Kerberos and Styx, completing the mythological family.

evt-06-21-2009-greenland.scenario: It is 21 June 2009 in Nuuk, and you are a Greenlandic official watching the flag-raising ceremony that formally replaces the 1979 home rule arrangement with a new self-government act.
evt-06-21-2009-greenland.prompt: What new power did this self-rule agreement give Greenland beyond home rule?

choices.text: An independent Greenlandic military
Automatic membership in the European Union
Control over natural resources, policing, and courts
Full independence from Denmark

evt-06-21-2009-greenland.butterflyEffect: Self-rule recognized Greenlanders as a people under international law and handed Greenland control over its natural resources, policing, and judicial system, while Denmark retained defense and foreign policy. The resource control clause later fueled fierce debates over mining and oil exploration and put Greenland's strategic and mineral wealth—and its path toward eventual independence—firmly in the international spotlight.

evt-06-22-1593-habsburg-monarchy.scenario: It's June 22, 1593, near Sisak in Croatia. An Ottoman raiding force returning from Habsburg territory is bogged down trying to cross the flooded Kupa river as your smaller relief force arrives.
evt-06-22-1593-habsburg-monarchy.prompt: As commander of the Habsburg force, what should you do?

choices.text: Wait for reinforcements before engaging
Attack at once while the Ottomans are pinned against the river
Withdraw to defend Zagreb instead
Negotiate a truce with the raiders

evt-06-22-1593-habsburg-monarchy.butterflyEffect: The Habsburg force struck immediately, routing the Ottoman raiders, many of whom drowned trying to escape across the swollen river, in one of the first major Ottoman defeats in decades. The victory at Sisak helped trigger the outbreak of the Long Turkish War between the Habsburgs and Ottomans, which lasted until 1606.

evt-06-22-1807-hms-leopard-1790.scenario: It's June 22, 1807, off the coast of Virginia. HMS Leopard has drawn alongside your frigate, USS Chesapeake, and its captain demands to board and search your crew for British deserters.
evt-06-22-1807-hms-leopard-1790.prompt: As Chesapeake's commander, what do you do?

choices.text: Refuse the demand to search your crew
Comply immediately and hand over the men
Flee back to port under full sail
Open fire preemptively on Leopard

evt-06-22-1807-hms-leopard-1790.butterflyEffect: Commodore Barron refused the demand, and Leopard opened fire, killing three and wounding eighteen before forcing Chesapeake's surrender and seizing four alleged deserters. The incident inflamed American outrage over impressment and became one of the grievances cited when the United States declared war on Britain in 1812.

evt-06-22-1812-1812-french-declaration-o.scenario: It is 22 June 1812 in Saint Petersburg. French ambassador Jacques Lauriston has just handed Russian Foreign Minister Alexander Saltykov a note declaring that Napoleon now considers himself at war with Russia.
evt-06-22-1812-1812-french-declaration-o.prompt: What happens two days after this declaration is delivered?

choices.text: Austria mediates a truce between the two empires
Russian forces launch a preemptive invasion of Poland
Napoleon's Grande Armée crosses the Niemen and invades Russia
Tsar Alexander I signs a new peace treaty with France

evt-06-22-1812-1812-french-declaration-o.butterflyEffect: On 24 June 1812, Napoleon's Grande Armée crossed the Niemen River, beginning the invasion of Russia. The campaign's brutal retreat destroyed most of his army and marked the turning point that led to his eventual defeat and exile.

evt-06-22-1813-war-of-1812.scenario: It's June 22, 1813, near Fort George in Upper Canada. Laura Secord, who overheard American officers billeted in her home planning a surprise attack, has just reached your outpost after an exhausting overland trek to warn you.
evt-06-22-1813-war-of-1812.prompt: As Lieutenant FitzGibbon, what should you do with this intelligence?

choices.text: Dismiss the warning as unreliable gossip
Retreat immediately to Fort George
Send word to Quebec and wait for further orders
Organize an ambush with allied Kahnawake and Mohawk warriors near Beaver Dams

evt-06-22-1813-war-of-1812.butterflyEffect: FitzGibbon used the warning to organize Mohawk and Caughnawaga warriors, who ambushed and forced the surrender of the American force at the Battle of Beaver Dams two days later. The victory checked American momentum on the Niagara frontier and made Laura Secord a lasting figure in Canadian memory.

evt-06-22-1911-george-v.scenario: It's June 22, 1911, in Westminster Abbey. You stand among the assembled peers and dignitaries as the Archbishop of Canterbury prepares to place the crown of St Edward on the new king's head.
evt-06-22-1911-george-v.prompt: What title, unique among British monarchs, did George V hold alongside King of the United Kingdom?

choices.text: Emperor of India
King of France
Protector of the Commonwealth
Holy Roman Emperor

evt-06-22-1911-george-v.butterflyEffect: George V's coronation confirmed him as monarch over a vast empire, including his role as Emperor of India, a title further formalized at the Delhi Durbar he attended later that year. His reign would see the British Empire reach its territorial peak after the First World War, followed by the first signs of imperial retreat.

evt-06-22-1922-irish-republican-army-192.scenario: It is the morning of 22 June 1922 outside Field Marshal Sir Henry Wilson's London home. He has just unveiled a war memorial and is walking to his front door when two IRA gunmen approach him on the street.
evt-06-22-1922-irish-republican-army-192.prompt: What happens to Wilson in this attack?

choices.text: He is kidnapped and held for ransom
He escapes into his house unharmed
He fights off the gunmen with his service revolver
He is shot dead on his doorstep

evt-06-22-1922-irish-republican-army-192.butterflyEffect: Wilson was shot dead on his own doorstep. The assassination shocked the British government, which pressed the new Irish Free State to act against anti-Treaty IRA forces occupying Dublin's Four Courts, a confrontation that helped trigger the outbreak of the Irish Civil War days later.

evt-06-22-1941-operation-barbarossa.scenario: It is the early hours of 22 June 1941. You are a Soviet intelligence officer who has spent weeks forwarding reports of German troop buildups along the border, despite the Molotov-Ribbentrop non-aggression pact.
evt-06-22-1941-operation-barbarossa.prompt: How does Stalin respond to these repeated warnings of invasion?

choices.text: He evacuates the Soviet government from Moscow
He dismisses them as Western provocation
He signs a new pact directly with Hitler
He orders full mobilization along the border

evt-06-22-1941-operation-barbarossa.butterflyEffect: Stalin dismissed the warnings as provocations meant to drag the USSR into war, leaving Soviet forces unprepared when 3.8 million Axis troops struck. The catastrophic early losses were staggering, but the failure to seize Moscow before winter ultimately doomed Germany to a grinding two-front war it could not win.

evt-06-22-1969-cuyahoga-river.scenario: It's June 22, 1969, in industrial Cleveland. Oil-soaked debris floating on the Cuyahoga River has just ignited, sending flames and black smoke over the water in the latest of a long string of river fires.
evt-06-22-1969-cuyahoga-river.prompt: What did this fire ultimately help spur in American environmental policy?

choices.text: Passage of the Clean Water Act and creation of the EPA
Federal takeover of the Cuyahoga River
Immediate nationwide ban on industrial river dumping
Closure of all Cleveland steel mills

evt-06-22-1969-cuyahoga-river.butterflyEffect: Though the fire itself was minor and lasted under thirty minutes, national media coverage turned it into a symbol of industrial pollution and galvanized public support for the environmental movement. It contributed to passage of the Clean Water Act of 1972 and creation of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency in 1970.

evt-06-22-1978-charon-moon.scenario: It is 1978 and you are an astronomer at the US Naval Observatory in Washington, D.C., poring over photographic plates of the distant dwarf planet Pluto taken at the Flagstaff station.
evt-06-22-1978-charon-moon.prompt: What unusual feature in the images led to the discovery of a moon orbiting Pluto?

choices.text: A shadow passing in front of a background star
An unexpected radio signal detected near Pluto
A recurring bulge or elongation on one side of Pluto's image
A sudden brightening of Pluto's entire disk

evt-06-22-1978-charon-moon.butterflyEffect: Astronomer James Christy noticed a periodic elongation, or bulge, in Pluto's image that turned out to be a separate body orbiting it, later named Charon. The discovery let astronomers finally calculate Pluto's mass accurately, revealing it was far smaller than once thought and fuelling later debates over its planetary status.

evt-06-22-1979-liberal-party-uk.scenario: It is 22 June 1979 and you sit in the Old Bailey courtroom as the jury returns its verdict on former Liberal Party leader Jeremy Thorpe, accused of conspiring to murder his former lover Norman Scott.
evt-06-22-1979-liberal-party-uk.prompt: What verdict did the jury deliver in Thorpe's sensational trial?

choices.text: Acquitted on all charges
The jury could not reach a verdict
Convicted and sentenced to prison
The case was dismissed before verdict

evt-06-22-1979-liberal-party-uk.butterflyEffect: Thorpe was acquitted on all charges, but the trial had already destroyed his political career and cast a long shadow over the Liberal Party's reputation. The case remains one of the most notorious political scandals in modern British history, feeding decades of press and cultural fascination.

evt-06-22-1984-virgin-atlantic.scenario: It is 22 June 1984 and you board a single Boeing 747 taking off from Gatwick to Newark, the maiden flight of a brash new airline backed by Richard Branson and challenging the giants of transatlantic travel.
evt-06-22-1984-virgin-atlantic.prompt: What became of this one-plane upstart in the years that followed?

choices.text: It merged with British Airways soon after launch
It grew into a major long-haul rival to British Airways
It folded within two years due to competition
It was absorbed into Pan Am's route network

evt-06-22-1984-virgin-atlantic.butterflyEffect: Virgin Atlantic grew steadily by emphasising service, in-flight entertainment and lower fares in premium classes, eventually becoming one of Britain's major long-haul carriers. Its rise provoked a bitter rivalry with British Airways, including the infamous 'dirty tricks' campaign that BA was later forced to apologise for.

evt-06-22-1986-the-hand-of-god.scenario: It is the 1986 World Cup quarter-final in Mexico City. As referee, you see Diego Maradona rise for a header against England's goalkeeper, but you're too far away to see his fist connect with the ball first.
evt-06-22-1986-the-hand-of-god.prompt: With no clear view of the handball, what do you rule?

choices.text: Disallow the goal for handball
Book Maradona for unsporting behaviour and replay the point
Award England a free kick
Allow the goal to stand

evt-06-22-1986-the-hand-of-god.butterflyEffect: Referee Ali Bin Nasser allowed the goal to stand, giving Argentina a 1-0 lead. Maradona scored the legendary 'Goal of the Century' minutes later, Argentina won 2-1, and went on to lift the World Cup, cementing the Hand of God as one of football's most infamous moments.

evt-06-22-1990-cold-war.scenario: It is 22 June 1990 and you stand in a crowd of Berliners watching cranes lift away the famous guard hut at Checkpoint Charlie, the Cold War's most photographed border crossing.
evt-06-22-1990-cold-war.prompt: What did the removal of Checkpoint Charlie signal about the state of Germany?

choices.text: That the Berlin Wall was being rebuilt further east
That NATO forces were taking over administration of East Berlin
That East and West Germany were moving swiftly toward reunification
That the Soviet Union was tightening border controls in Berlin

evt-06-22-1990-cold-war.butterflyEffect: The dismantling was a symbolic milestone in the rapid process of German reunification, which was formally completed on 3 October 1990. The hut itself was preserved and later became a museum piece, while the crossing point vanished from a city that was fast erasing its Cold War divisions.

evt-06-22-2000-wuhan-airlines-flight-343.scenario: It is 22 June 2000, and your Wuhan Airlines Xian Y-7 is flying toward Wuhan through a rapidly building storm cell, its onboard weather radar struggling to track the danger ahead.
evt-06-22-2000-wuhan-airlines-flight-343.prompt: What ultimately brings the aircraft down?

choices.text: Pilot error in navigation
A lightning strike combined with severe windshear
Fuel exhaustion before landing
Engine failure during takeoff

evt-06-22-2000-wuhan-airlines-flight-343.butterflyEffect: The aircraft was struck by lightning and hit severe windshear, causing it to crash into a residential area near Hanyang. The disaster drew scrutiny to the aging Y-7 turboprop's outdated weather-detection equipment and accelerated calls for stricter storm-avoidance procedures on Chinese domestic routes.

evt-06-22-2007-elie-manitoba.scenario: It's the afternoon of June 22, 2007, near Elie, Manitoba. Dark, rotating clouds are bearing down on the town, and residents can see a violent funnel forming on the horizon.
evt-06-22-2007-elie-manitoba.prompt: What is the safest action for residents in its path?

choices.text: Shelter under a highway overpass
Drive away from the storm at high speed
Go outside to film the tornado up close
Take shelter immediately in a basement or interior room

evt-06-22-2007-elie-manitoba.butterflyEffect: The tornado was later confirmed as an F5, the highest rating and the most intense ever recorded in Canada, tearing through farmland and flinging a house off its foundation. Remarkably it caused no fatalities, and dramatic video of the funnel made it one of the most widely studied tornadoes in Canadian history.

evt-06-22-2009-washington-metro.scenario: It is the morning of 22 June 2009 on the Red Line near Fort Totten. A track circuit has failed to detect a stalled train ahead, and your train is closing in fast under automatic control.
evt-06-22-2009-washington-metro.prompt: What does the investigation later find led to this collision, and what follows?

choices.text: Fares are tripled overnight to fund repairs
WMATA retires the crash-vulnerable 1000-series railcars
The entire Metro system is permanently shut down
Driverless trains are introduced across the network immediately

evt-06-22-2009-washington-metro.butterflyEffect: A faulty track circuit failed to register the stopped train, causing the deadliest crash in Metro's history. The disaster prompted WMATA to retire its vulnerable 1000-series railcars and overhaul its automatic train control system under new federal safety oversight.

evt-06-22-2012-paraguay.scenario: You are a senator in Paraguay's Congress in June 2012, days after a deadly clash between police and landless farmers at Curuguaty, called to vote in a hastily arranged impeachment trial of President Fernando Lugo.
evt-06-22-2012-paraguay.prompt: What is the outcome of the Senate's vote?

choices.text: Lugo resigns before the vote can be held
The Senate acquits him and he remains president
The military intervenes and cancels the vote
The Senate convicts him, removing him from office within a day

evt-06-22-2012-paraguay.butterflyEffect: The Senate convicted Lugo and removed him from office within roughly 24 hours of the trial opening, installing Vice President Federico Franco as president. Many neighboring governments called the process a parliamentary coup, and Mercosur and Unasur suspended Paraguay's membership until elections restored democratic legitimacy in 2013.

evt-06-22-2015-national-assembly-afghani.scenario: It is 22 June 2015 inside Kabul's parliament compound. A suicide bomber has just detonated at the gate, and gunmen are now storming toward the chamber where lawmakers are in session.
evt-06-22-2015-national-assembly-afghani.prompt: What actually happens to the lawmakers inside during the assault?

choices.text: The building is destroyed and parliament is dissolved
The gunmen take dozens of lawmakers hostage for days
Lawmakers negotiate directly with the attackers for a ceasefire
Security forces kill the attackers before they breach the chamber

evt-06-22-2015-national-assembly-afghani.butterflyEffect: Afghan security forces fought off the attackers, killing all of them before they reached the chamber; no lawmakers were killed, though several people were wounded. The Taliban-claimed attack underscored the insurgency's continued reach into the heart of Kabul even as peace efforts were being discussed.

evt-06-22-2022-june-2022-afghanistan-ear.scenario: You are a relief coordinator in Paktika province hours after the earthquake struck in the early morning of 22 June 2022. Villages in the surrounding mountains are cut off, their homes collapsed and roads impassable.
evt-06-22-2022-june-2022-afghanistan-ear.prompt: What becomes the greatest obstacle to reaching survivors?

choices.text: Damaged roads and lack of helicopters to reach isolated villages
A shortage of food stockpiles in nearby cities
An immediate outbreak of cholera among survivors
Volcanic activity triggered by the earthquake

evt-06-22-2022-june-2022-afghanistan-ear.butterflyEffect: The remote, mountainous terrain and a shortage of helicopters made it extremely difficult to reach devastated villages quickly. The disaster exposed how international sanctions and limited aid infrastructure under Taliban rule slowed the humanitarian response for months afterward.

evt-06-22-2025-united-states.scenario: You are a US military planner in June 2025, tasked with striking Iran's deeply buried Fordow enrichment site amid escalating conflict between Israel and Iran.
evt-06-22-2025-united-states.prompt: What method is used to strike the hardened underground facility at Fordow?

choices.text: Cruise missiles launched from naval destroyers
A special forces raid on the ground
A cyberattack disabling the centrifuges remotely
B-2 bombers drop GBU-57 bunker-buster bombs

evt-06-22-2025-united-states.butterflyEffect: B-2 stealth bombers dropped GBU-57 Massive Ordnance Penetrator bunker-busting bombs on Fordow, marking direct US military action against Iran's nuclear program. Iran responded with missile strikes, and within days a fragile ceasefire was brokered to halt further escalation.

evt-06-23-1865-stand-watie.scenario: It's June 1865. Lee surrendered at Appomattox two months ago, but you still command Cherokee, Muscogee, and Seminole troops fighting for the Confederacy in the Trans-Mississippi Theater, weighing whether to keep resisting.
evt-06-23-1865-stand-watie.prompt: What did you decide to do?

choices.text: Fled with your troops into Mexico
Switched allegiance to the Union army
Surrendered your remaining forces
Continued fighting as guerrillas indefinitely

evt-06-23-1865-stand-watie.butterflyEffect: Stand Watie surrendered his forces on 23 June 1865 at Doaksville, becoming the last Confederate general to lay down arms and marking the practical end of organized Confederate resistance.

evt-06-23-1887-parliament-of-canada.scenario: You are a member of Canada's Parliament in 1887, debating a bill to protect the hot springs and mountain scenery around Banff from unchecked commercial development.
evt-06-23-1887-parliament-of-canada.prompt: What did the Rocky Mountains Park Act actually establish?

choices.text: A private hunting reserve for wealthy railway investors
A new mining concession zone in the Rocky Mountains
Canada's first national park, later known as Banff National Park
A military training ground for the Canadian militia

evt-06-23-1887-parliament-of-canada.butterflyEffect: The act created Rocky Mountains Park, later renamed Banff National Park, as Canada's first national park. It became the template for a growing national park system across the country, tying Canadian identity to preserved wilderness for generations afterward.

evt-06-23-1926-college-board.scenario: It's June 23, 1926, and you are one of roughly 8,000 high school seniors nationwide sitting down to a brand-new exam built on Army intelligence testing methods, meant to measure aptitude rather than memorized coursework.
evt-06-23-1926-college-board.prompt: What did this new Scholastic Aptitude Test go on to become for American higher education?

choices.text: It was discontinued within a decade for being unreliable
It became the dominant standardized test for U.S. college admissions
It was adopted only by the U.S. military for recruit screening
It was replaced immediately by a purely interview-based system

evt-06-23-1926-college-board.butterflyEffect: Designed by psychologist Carl Brigham, the SAT was gradually adopted by more colleges as a standardized admissions tool. Over the following decades it became the dominant gatekeeper exam for U.S. college admissions, repeatedly revised and renamed, and shaping how millions of students were sorted for higher education.

evt-06-23-1944-the-holocaust.scenario: It's 23 June 1944. You are a Red Cross delegate touring Theresienstadt, shown freshly painted facades, a staged café, and a children's choir performance arranged by SS officials just for your visit.
evt-06-23-1944-the-holocaust.prompt: What did you report to the outside world afterward?

choices.text: A refusal to issue any report at all
A demand for the immediate closure of the ghetto
A favorable report describing decent living conditions
A report exposing it as a site of mass murder

evt-06-23-1944-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: The delegation issued a favorable report accepting the staged conditions as genuine, which the Nazi regime used to counter growing evidence of genocide. Deportations to Auschwitz resumed soon after, and most people shown during the visit were later murdered.

evt-06-23-1956-1956-egyptian-referendum.scenario: You are an Egyptian citizen casting your ballot in the June 1956 referendum, choosing whether to confirm Gamal Abdel Nasser as president and approve a new constitution replacing the old monarchy's framework.
evt-06-23-1956-1956-egyptian-referendum.prompt: What did the referendum's outcome set in motion later that same year?

choices.text: Egypt joined NATO as part of the new constitutional order
Egypt immediately restored the monarchy under King Farouk
Nasser's consolidated power led directly to the Suez Canal nationalization crisis
The referendum results were annulled by British administrators

evt-06-23-1956-1956-egyptian-referendum.butterflyEffect: Official results showed near-unanimous approval, cementing Nasser's control after the 1952 revolution. Within weeks of becoming president under the new constitution, Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal Company, triggering the Suez Crisis when Britain, France and Israel intervened militarily.

evt-06-23-1972-richard-nixon.scenario: It's 23 June 1972. You watch President Nixon sign the Education Amendments Act, uncertain just how far its ban on sex discrimination will reach into classrooms and locker rooms across the country.
evt-06-23-1972-richard-nixon.prompt: What lasting change did this law's Title IX provision bring?

choices.text: Mandated racial desegregation of public schools
Set a federal minimum wage for teachers
Created the federal student loan program
Banned sex discrimination in federally funded education, including athletics

evt-06-23-1972-richard-nixon.butterflyEffect: Title IX banned sex discrimination in any federally funded education program, and its reach expanded dramatically into athletics. It transformed girls' and women's access to school sports and fueled decades of litigation over equal opportunity in education.

evt-06-23-1973-los-angeles-dodgers.scenario: You're a fan at Dodger Stadium on June 23, 1973, watching a young infield of Steve Garvey, Davey Lopes, Bill Russell, and Ron Cey take the field together for the first time as a unit.
evt-06-23-1973-los-angeles-dodgers.prompt: What record would this infield combination go on to set?

choices.text: The first all-rookie infield to win a World Series
The highest combined salary of any infield at the time
The most home runs by an infield in a single season
The longest-tenured infield combination in MLB history

evt-06-23-1973-los-angeles-dodgers.butterflyEffect: Garvey, Lopes, Russell, and Cey stayed together as the Dodgers' starting infield from 1973 through 1981, the longest-tenured infield in Major League Baseball history. Their continuity helped anchor the Dodgers to multiple pennants and the 1981 World Series title.

evt-06-23-1982-killing-of-vincent-chin.scenario: You're at a bachelor party for Vincent Chin in Highland Park, Michigan, in June 1982, when two men who blame Japan for lost auto jobs mistake Chin, who is Chinese American, for Japanese and confront him.
evt-06-23-1982-killing-of-vincent-chin.prompt: What lasting effect followed Chin's beating death?

choices.text: It triggered new federal immigration restrictions on Japanese nationals
It led to immediate prison sentences of life without parole for both men
It caused Chrysler to shut down the Highland Park plant in response
It sparked a pan-Asian American civil rights movement and a federal hate-crime trial

evt-06-23-1982-killing-of-vincent-chin.butterflyEffect: Ebens and Nitz pleaded to manslaughter but received only probation and fines, sparking national outrage over the light sentence. The case galvanized a pan-Asian American civil rights movement, led to the founding of American Citizens for Justice, and prompted a federal civil rights trial, becoming a landmark moment in Asian American activism.

evt-06-23-1985-1985-narita-international.scenario: You're a baggage handler at Narita International Airport on the morning of June 23, 1985, sorting a suitcase in transit toward an Air India flight. At 6:19am it detonates in your handling room.
evt-06-23-1985-1985-narita-international.prompt: What was this bomb secretly part of?

choices.text: A rehearsal for an attack on the 1988 Tokyo Olympics
Retaliation by airport workers over a labor dispute
An isolated act unconnected to any wider conspiracy
A coordinated double-bombing plot that also destroyed Air India Flight 182 that same day

evt-06-23-1985-1985-narita-international.butterflyEffect: The bomb went off prematurely, killing two baggage handlers, because it had been set to detonate mid-flight rather than on the ground. It was one half of a coordinated Babbar Khalsa plot; the second bomb succeeded, destroying Air India Flight 182 over the Atlantic that same day and killing all 329 aboard. Bomb-maker Inderjit Singh Reyat was eventually convicted over both attacks.

evt-06-23-1991-sonic-the-hedgehog.scenario: You're a Sega executive in June 1991, watching the launch of a new blue hedgehog character meant to give the Genesis console an edge over Nintendo's Mario.
evt-06-23-1991-sonic-the-hedgehog.prompt: What did Sega do that turned Sonic into a serious rival to Mario?

choices.text: Priced it far above rival Nintendo titles as a premium product
Delayed the Western release by several years to build hype
Bundled the game free with the Genesis console to drive hardware sales
Released it exclusively in arcades before any home version

evt-06-23-1991-sonic-the-hedgehog.butterflyEffect: Sega bundled Sonic the Hedgehog with the Genesis console and marketed his speed as the opposite of Mario's cautious platforming, sharply lifting Genesis sales in North America. The rivalry defined the early-1990s console wars and turned Sonic into a lasting multimedia franchise spanning games, cartoons, and later feature films.

evt-06-23-2001-2001-southern-peru-earthq.scenario: You are standing in a coastal town in southern Peru moments after violent shaking finally stops, plaster dust still hanging in the air and cracks running through the walls around you.
evt-06-23-2001-2001-southern-peru-earthq.prompt: What should you do immediately, given the earthquake's location just offshore?

choices.text: Return indoors to retrieve valuables before aftershocks hit
Move to higher ground immediately in case of a tsunami
Gather in the town square, assuming the danger has passed
Wait by the shoreline to watch for unusual wave activity

evt-06-23-2001-2001-southern-peru-earthq.butterflyEffect: A tsunami generated by the offshore rupture struck the coast at Camaná shortly afterward, catching residents who had not moved to higher ground and causing many of the disaster's deaths. The quake also collapsed colonial buildings in Arequipa, including parts of its cathedral, prompting later reviews of building codes in the region.

evt-06-23-2013-nik-wallenda.scenario: You are Nik Wallenda, about to step onto a two-inch steel cable stretched over a gorge near the Grand Canyon in June 2013, live on television, with no net below you.
evt-06-23-2013-nik-wallenda.prompt: What safety requirement does the broadcaster force on you for this walk, unlike your usual style?

choices.text: A parachute strapped to his back
An oxygen mask due to high altitude
A safety net strung beneath the entire walk
A mandatory tether harness connected to the cable

evt-06-23-2013-nik-wallenda.butterflyEffect: Discovery Channel required Wallenda to wear a tether harness for the broadcast, a first for him, though he resisted the idea as against his family's high-wire tradition. He completed the roughly 1,500-foot crossing in about 23 minutes despite strong winds, cementing his reputation and leading to later untethered feats like his 2020 walk over the Masaya Volcano.

evt-06-23-2013-nanga-parbat.scenario: You are a foreign climber asleep in your tent at Nanga Parbat's base camp when gunmen disguised as local police fan out through the camp before dawn, rousing mountaineers from around the world.
evt-06-23-2013-nanga-parbat.prompt: What was the immediate consequence for foreign mountaineering in Pakistan after the attack?

choices.text: Insurance companies began fully covering high-altitude expeditions there
The United Nations banned all mountaineering in the region
Foreign expedition numbers to Pakistan's mountains collapsed for years
Pakistan immediately opened new peaks to attract more climbers

evt-06-23-2013-nanga-parbat.butterflyEffect: A Taliban splinter group claimed the raid as revenge for a drone strike, and ten foreign climbers and a Pakistani guide were killed. International expedition bookings to Pakistan's peaks collapsed for years afterward as governments issued travel warnings and mountaineers shifted to Nepal instead.

evt-06-23-2014-syrian-chemical-weapons-p.scenario: It's 23 June 2014 at a Syrian port. As part of the joint OPCW-UN mission, you're overseeing the loading of the last declared chemical weapons stockpile onto a ship, following the outcry over the 2013 Ghouta attack.
evt-06-23-2014-syrian-chemical-weapons-p.prompt: What happened to these chemical agents after they left Syria?

choices.text: Transferred to Russia for long-term storage
Destroyed at sea aboard a US Navy vessel using hydrolysis
Buried in sealed bunkers in the Syrian desert
Shipped to Iraq for disposal

evt-06-23-2014-syrian-chemical-weapons-p.butterflyEffect: The US vessel Cape Ray neutralized the agents at sea using hydrolysis, completing the declared destruction program. Despite this, later attacks like the 2017 Khan Shaykhun sarin strike revealed Syria had concealed additional stocks.

evt-06-23-2016-2016-united-kingdom-europ.scenario: It's 23 June 2016. You queue at a polling station in Britain after months of fierce campaigning over sovereignty, immigration, and trade, about to mark your ballot on EU membership.
evt-06-23-2016-2016-united-kingdom-europ.prompt: What did the referendum ultimately decide?

choices.text: The vote was declared void and re-run
Remain won comfortably
Parliament overturned the result immediately
Leave won a narrow majority

evt-06-23-2016-2016-united-kingdom-europ.butterflyEffect: Leave won narrowly, 51.9% to 48.1%. David Cameron resigned the next morning, Theresa May became PM, and years of fraught negotiation followed until the UK formally left the EU in January 2020.

evt-06-23-2018-tham-luang-cave-rescue.scenario: You're part of the international rescue team at Tham Luang cave in July 2018, having finally located twelve boys and their coach alive on a ledge deep past flooded, narrow passages.
evt-06-23-2018-tham-luang-cave-rescue.prompt: How do rescuers get the boys out through the flooded tunnels?

choices.text: Sedate each boy and guide him out wearing a full-face diving mask
Drain the entire cave system before extraction
Drill a rescue shaft directly down to their ledge
Have the boys swim out unaided, following a guide rope

evt-06-23-2018-tham-luang-cave-rescue.butterflyEffect: Divers sedated each boy, fitted him with a full-face mask, and guided him through the flooded passages one at a time over three days, successfully extracting all thirteen. Thai Navy SEAL diver Saman Kunan died during the operation while running supply lines, a loss honored worldwide; the rescue became the subject of documentaries and dramatizations.

evt-06-24-474-western-roman-empire.scenario: You serve in the invasion force of Julius Nepos, sailing to Italy in 474 to unseat Glycerius, the Western emperor whom the Eastern court in Constantinople never recognized.
evt-06-24-474-western-roman-empire.prompt: What happens to Glycerius once Nepos' forces reach him?

choices.text: He is captured and executed immediately
He negotiates a power-sharing peace and remains emperor
He flees to the Vandal court in North Africa
He surrenders and is made a bishop rather than killed

evt-06-24-474-western-roman-empire.butterflyEffect: Glycerius surrendered without a real fight and was spared, made Bishop of Salona instead of executed. Nepos' own reign proved brief too, deposed within a year, showing the rapid, unstable succession that preceded the Western Empire's final collapse in 476.

evt-06-24-1314-first-war-of-scottish-ind.scenario: It's 24 June 1314 near Stirling Castle. You stand shoulder to shoulder with fellow spearmen in Robert the Bruce's ranks as English heavy cavalry thunders toward you across boggy, pitted ground.
evt-06-24-1314-first-war-of-scottish-ind.prompt: What formation do the Scots rely on to repel the cavalry charge?

choices.text: A naval flanking attack along the river
A feigned retreat to lure the cavalry into a trap
Massed longbow volleys from the flanks
Tight schiltrons of spearmen holding formation

evt-06-24-1314-first-war-of-scottish-ind.butterflyEffect: The tightly packed schiltrons held their ground and broke the English charge, and Edward II's army routed. The victory secured de facto Scottish independence, though formal recognition waited until the Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton in 1328, and Bannockburn endured as a defining symbol of Scottish nationhood.

evt-06-24-1340-hundred-years-war.scenario: It's 24 June 1340, off the Flemish coast near Sluys. You stand aboard Edward III's flagship as the French and Genoese fleet waits ahead, ships lashed together in defensive lines across the harbor mouth.
evt-06-24-1340-hundred-years-war.prompt: What tactic does the English fleet use to break the enemy formation?

choices.text: Fire ships sent drifting into the chained fleet
A blockade intended to starve the French fleet out
Longbow volleys to clear the decks, followed by boarding actions
A land assault launched from the nearby coast

evt-06-24-1340-hundred-years-war.butterflyEffect: English longbowmen raked the packed French decks before ships closed to board, and the enemy fleet was almost annihilated. The victory gave England control of the Channel for years, allowing Edward III to launch continental campaigns without fear of invasion at home.

evt-06-24-1374-dancing-mania.scenario: It is midsummer 1374 in Aachen, and dozens of townsfolk are dancing wildly through the streets, screaming and collapsing from exhaustion, unable to stop themselves.
evt-06-24-1374-dancing-mania.prompt: What do the town's clergy and authorities do to try to end the affliction?

choices.text: They arrest the dancers for witchcraft and put them on trial
They quarantine the dancers as plague carriers
They lead the afflicted in religious processions to shrines for prayer and exorcism
They summon physicians to bleed the dancers as a cure for melancholy

evt-06-24-1374-dancing-mania.butterflyEffect: Sufferers were led in processions to chapels and shrines for prayer and exorcism rather than treated as physically ill. The outbreak spread rapidly to other Rhineland towns, and similar episodes recurred for centuries, later becoming linked to the legend of St. Vitus's Dance.

evt-06-24-1559-book-of-common-prayer-155.scenario: It is 1559. You are a parish priest in England as Elizabeth I's new Act of Uniformity takes effect, ordering every church to adopt the revised Book of Common Prayer in place of the Catholic Latin Mass.
evt-06-24-1559-book-of-common-prayer-155.prompt: How do most English clergy respond to the new legal requirement?

choices.text: Adopt the new prayer book publicly to comply with the Act of Uniformity
Flee immediately to Rome to serve exiled English Catholics
Petition Parliament to keep Edward VI's 1552 prayer book unchanged
Continue celebrating the Latin Mass openly in defiance of the law

evt-06-24-1559-book-of-common-prayer-155.butterflyEffect: Most clergy complied publicly and adopted the new liturgy to avoid fines and deprivation, while a minority became recusants who quietly kept Catholic practice alive in secret. The 1559 prayer book became the enduring core of Anglican worship, and enforcement of uniformity fueled religious tension in England for generations.

evt-06-24-1724-nativity-of-john-the-bapt.scenario: You are Johann Sebastian Bach, newly installed as Thomaskantor in Leipzig, preparing a cantata for the Feast of St. John the Baptist built around Luther's baptismal hymn 'Christ unser Herr zum Jordan kam.'
evt-06-24-1724-nativity-of-john-the-bapt.prompt: What structural approach do you take in composing this cantata?

choices.text: Write freely composed arias with no reference to the hymn
Borrow arias from Italian opera and set new German words
Recycle an earlier cantata written for a different feast
Build every movement around the chorale tune itself

evt-06-24-1724-nativity-of-john-the-bapt.butterflyEffect: Bach based every movement on the chorale melody itself, launching his ambitious second Leipzig cycle of chorale cantatas for the church year. That cycle became one of the towering achievements of Lutheran sacred music, still performed and studied today.

evt-06-24-1812-napoleonic-wars.scenario: It is dawn on 24 June 1812. You ride with Napoleon's staff as the Grande Armée, over 400,000 strong, reaches the banks of the Neman River on the edge of Russian territory.
evt-06-24-1812-napoleonic-wars.prompt: What does Napoleon decide as his army crosses into Russia?

choices.text: Press on rapidly to force a decisive battle deep in Russian territory
Turn the army south to seize Ukraine's farmland instead
Wait through the summer for reinforcements before advancing
Halt at the border to negotiate a settlement with the Tsar

evt-06-24-1812-napoleonic-wars.butterflyEffect: Napoleon pressed deep into Russia seeking a decisive battle, but the Russians retreated and burned resources rather than fight, drawing the French toward Moscow. The brutal retreat that followed destroyed the Grande Armée and marked the beginning of Napoleon's fall from power.

evt-06-24-1880-o-canada.scenario: You are a chorister in Quebec City on 24 June 1880, preparing to premiere a new patriotic song commissioned by the lieutenant governor for that year's Saint-Jean-Baptiste Day festivities.
evt-06-24-1880-o-canada.prompt: What song does your choir perform for the first time that day?

choices.text: "The Maple Leaf Forever"
"O Canada," composed by Calixa Lavallée
"God Save the Queen"
"La Marseillaise"

evt-06-24-1880-o-canada.butterflyEffect: The song was "O Canada," with music by Calixa Lavallée and French lyrics by Adolphe-Basile Routhier. English lyrics followed in 1908, and after decades as an unofficial favorite, it became Canada's official national anthem exactly a century later, in 1980.

evt-06-24-1932-siamese-revolution-of-193.scenario: It is dawn on 24 June 1932 in Bangkok. You are an officer with the Khana Ratsadon, and your soldiers have just seized key government buildings while King Prajadhipok is away at the seaside palace.
evt-06-24-1932-siamese-revolution-of-193.prompt: To keep the coup bloodless, what do you demand from the king?

choices.text: That he hand power directly to the army chief as dictator
That he accept a constitution and remain as a constitutional monarch
That he abdicate the throne immediately
That he flee the country within 24 hours

evt-06-24-1932-siamese-revolution-of-193.butterflyEffect: Prajadhipok accepted, ending absolute monarchy and creating Siam's first constitution and National Assembly without bloodshed. The compromise proved fragile: factional infighting followed, the king abdicated in 1935, and the military came to dominate Thai politics for decades.

evt-06-24-1939-thai-cultural-mandates.scenario: You serve in Field Marshal Phibunsongkhram's government in June 1939, tasked with drafting the very first of a planned series of cultural mandates meant to forge a modern, unified national identity.
evt-06-24-1939-thai-cultural-mandates.prompt: What does this first mandate change?

choices.text: The calendar system to the Gregorian calendar
The national dress code to Western clothing
The country's official name, from Siam to Thailand
The national religion to state secularism

evt-06-24-1939-thai-cultural-mandates.butterflyEffect: The mandate renamed Siam to Thailand, promoting an ethnic-nationalist vision of the Thai state. Eleven further mandates followed through 1942, dictating dress, language, and daily customs; many were later relaxed, but the name Thailand endured permanently.

evt-06-24-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It's the night of 24 June 1940. You creep ashore with a small British raiding party near Boulogne, part of the very first Commando operation of the war against newly occupied France.
evt-06-24-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: What is the primary goal of this pioneering raid?

choices.text: Capture a German general for intelligence
Rescue soldiers stranded in France after Dunkirk
Sabotage a major U-boat pen
Reconnaissance and testing raiding tactics against the occupied coast

evt-06-24-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Operation Collar achieved little materially, with the small parties finding scant enemy contact along the coast. But it proved raiding was feasible, giving Churchill the case he needed to expand the Commando concept, which grew into larger operations like the 1942 St Nazaire raid.

evt-06-24-1989-1989-tiananmen-square-pro.scenario: It is late June 1989 in Beijing, days after troops cleared Tiananmen Square. The 13th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party meets to decide the fate of General Secretary Zhao Ziyang, who had shown sympathy toward the student demonstrators.
evt-06-24-1989-1989-tiananmen-square-pro.prompt: What did the Central Committee decide about Zhao Ziyang's position?

choices.text: He was promoted to head the Central Military Commission
He was permitted to resign quietly and live abroad
He was reinstated with full authority over the Party
He was dismissed from his posts and placed under house arrest

evt-06-24-1989-1989-tiananmen-square-pro.butterflyEffect: Zhao Ziyang was stripped of all his posts and placed under house arrest, where he remained until his death in 2005. Shanghai party chief Jiang Zemin was elevated to General Secretary in his place, beginning a decade-long rise to national leadership and cementing hardline control over China's political direction even as economic reform continued.

evt-06-24-2004-capital-punishment.scenario: You sit on New York's highest court in 2004, reviewing the case of a death-row inmate who argues the state's capital sentencing law coerces juries into choosing execution over a lesser sentence.
evt-06-24-2004-capital-punishment.prompt: How does the Court of Appeals rule on New York's death penalty statute?

choices.text: The court orders a new trial but leaves the statute intact
The court upholds the statute as written
The court declares the sentencing provision unconstitutional, effectively voiding the statute
The court refers the matter to the U.S. Supreme Court without ruling

evt-06-24-2004-capital-punishment.butterflyEffect: The court struck down the statute's jury-deadlock instruction as unconstitutional, effectively halting executions in New York. The legislature never passed a fix, and the state has had no valid death penalty since.

evt-06-24-2010-julia-gillard.scenario: It is 24 June 2010 in Canberra. Labor's primary vote is collapsing under Prime Minister Kevin Rudd, and you are a backbencher watching Deputy PM Julia Gillard move against him just hours before caucus meets.
evt-06-24-2010-julia-gillard.prompt: How does Gillard actually take the prime ministership that day?

choices.text: She calls a snap general election to bypass him
She challenges him in a Labor caucus leadership ballot
She defects to form a new party
She resigns from cabinet to force his hand

evt-06-24-2010-julia-gillard.butterflyEffect: Rudd stood aside rather than face a lost ballot, and Gillard was sworn in as Australia's first female prime minister that afternoon. She led a fragile minority government after the 2010 election, before Rudd reclaimed the leadership from her in 2013.

evt-06-24-2010-john-isner.scenario: It's 24 June 2010, the third day of your first-round Wimbledon match against Nicolas Mahut. You've traded service holds for hours in an untiebroken fifth set, and the game count has climbed far beyond anything either of you expected.
evt-06-24-2010-john-isner.prompt: How does the marathon match finally end?

choices.text: You finally break serve and win the fifth set 70-68
The umpire declares the match a draw due to a curfew
Mahut retires from the court with cramp
The match is decided by a tiebreak at 24-24

evt-06-24-2010-john-isner.butterflyEffect: Isner won the fifth set 70-68, completing the longest match in tennis history at 11 hours 5 minutes over three days. The spectacle fed into a broader push for change, and Wimbledon eventually introduced a final-set tiebreak at 12-12, starting in 2019.

evt-06-24-2012-lonesome-george.scenario: You work at the Charles Darwin Research Station in the Galápagos in the 2000s, caring for Lonesome George, the last known Pinta Island tortoise, with no confirmed mate of his subspecies left alive.
evt-06-24-2012-lonesome-george.prompt: What do conservationists try in a last effort to save his lineage?

choices.text: Pair him with closely related tortoises from other islands and hope for offspring
Import an unrelated tortoise species to breed with him
Leave him isolated and make no breeding attempts
Attempt to clone him from preserved tissue

evt-06-24-2012-lonesome-george.butterflyEffect: Keepers paired George with genetically similar females from Isabela and Wolf Volcano and offered a reward for a true mate, but no viable offspring ever hatched. When George died on 24 June 2012, his subspecies was declared extinct, though later genetic surveys found hybrid descendants on Wolf Volcano carrying some of his ancestry.

evt-06-24-2013-prime-minister-of-italy.scenario: You are a reporter in a packed Milan courtroom on 24 June 2013, awaiting the verdict in the case against former Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi over the so-called Rubygate scandal.
evt-06-24-2013-prime-minister-of-italy.prompt: What does the court convict Berlusconi of that day?

choices.text: Illegal wiretapping of political rivals
Bribing judges to influence a business case
Abuse of office and paying an underage girl for sex
Tax fraud involving Mediaset's accounts

evt-06-24-2013-prime-minister-of-italy.butterflyEffect: Berlusconi was found guilty of abuse of office and paying for sex with an underage nightclub dancer, and sentenced to seven years and a ban from public office. The conviction was overturned on appeal in 2014, and he remained active in Italian politics until his death in 2023.

evt-06-24-2021-surfside-condominium-coll.scenario: It's the early hours of 24 June 2021 in Surfside, Florida. Champlain Towers South has just partially collapsed, and officials must decide what to do with the portion of the tower still standing as rescue efforts continue below it.
evt-06-24-2021-surfside-condominium-coll.prompt: What do officials ultimately decide to do with the remaining structure?

choices.text: Reinforce and stabilize it to continue rescue operations indefinitely
Convert it immediately into a permanent memorial site
Demolish it before an approaching storm, citing safety concerns
Leave it standing pending a lengthy structural review

evt-06-24-2021-surfside-condominium-coll.butterflyEffect: Ten days later, with Hurricane Elsa approaching and engineers warning the remaining structure was unstable, officials had it controlled-demolished. The disaster led Florida to pass new laws in 2022 requiring milestone structural inspections and reserve funding studies for older condominium buildings statewide.

evt-06-24-2026-2026-venezuela-earthquake.scenario: It is the evening of 24 June 2026 in La Guaira, Venezuela. A sharp foreshock has just passed, and thirty seconds later the ground begins to heave violently as a far larger quake, centered just offshore, strikes the coast.
evt-06-24-2026-2026-venezuela-earthquake.prompt: Given the offshore epicenter, what is the safest immediate action to take?

choices.text: Return home to check on your belongings
Move quickly to higher ground away from the shoreline
Stay put and call relatives before deciding what to do
Go to the shore to watch for unusual wave activity

evt-06-24-2026-2026-venezuela-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The Mw 7.5 mainshock centered off La Guaira caused roughly 80% of the state's buildings to collapse, with fatalities exceeding 6,500 confirmed by August 2026 and tens of thousands still missing. It became one of the deadliest disasters in Venezuelan history, overwhelming emergency services for months.

evt-06-25-1910-united-states-congress.scenario: It is June 1910, and you sit in the gallery of the U.S. Congress as lawmakers debate a bill aimed at combating so-called 'white slavery,' the forced transport of women for prostitution across state lines.
evt-06-25-1910-united-states-congress.prompt: What does the Mann Act, passed by Congress this day, actually prohibit?

choices.text: Employing children under twelve in interstate factories
Selling alcoholic beverages to minors in federal territories
Interstate shipment of firearms without a federal license
Transporting women across state lines for prostitution or other immoral purposes

evt-06-25-1910-united-states-congress.butterflyEffect: The Mann Act made it a federal crime to transport women across state lines for prostitution or other immoral purposes. While used against genuine trafficking, it was also wielded to prosecute consensual interracial and unconventional relationships, most famously boxer Jack Johnson, making it one of the most controversial morality laws of the era.

evt-06-25-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is June 25, 1944, and you serve aboard a U.S. Navy warship off Cherbourg, tasked with silencing German coastal batteries defending the vital port as Allied troops close in on land.
evt-06-25-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What happened when the German shore batteries returned fire during the bombardment?

choices.text: The German garrison surrendered the moment firing started
Allied ships were damaged and forced to withdraw despite the pressure they applied
The bombardment was called off before it began
The batteries were destroyed instantly with no Allied losses

evt-06-25-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Several Allied ships were damaged by accurate German counter-battery fire and had to withdraw, but the combined naval and ground pressure proved decisive. The German garrison commander surrendered Cherbourg the next day, though demolished harbor facilities meant the port wasn't fully usable until September, delaying the Allied supply buildup.

evt-06-25-1950-korean-war.scenario: It is 25 June 1950. North Korean tanks have just crossed the 38th parallel in force, and word reaches the United Nations Security Council that South Korea is under full-scale invasion.
evt-06-25-1950-korean-war.prompt: What does the United Nations do in response to the invasion?

choices.text: Condemn the invasion and authorize an international force to defend South Korea
Impose only economic sanctions on North Korea and China
Treat it as a purely internal Korean matter and take no action
Transfer administrative control of the peninsula to Japan

evt-06-25-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: The Security Council condemned the invasion and called on member states to help repel it, and Truman ordered US forces into action within days. The resulting UN-backed intervention, capped by the Inchon landing, escalated into a three-year war that entrenched Korea's division, which persists to this day.

evt-06-25-1960-cryptography.scenario: It is June 25, 1960, and two NSA cryptanalysts you work alongside tell colleagues they are heading off on a routine vacation. Their travel plans seem oddly circuitous, but no one raises an alarm.
evt-06-25-1960-cryptography.prompt: What did these two NSA cryptologists actually do after leaving on "vacation"?

choices.text: Were captured attempting to sell codes to Cuba
Resigned quietly to take private-sector jobs
Defected to the Soviet Union and revealed NSA secrets
Reported to work as scheduled after their trip

evt-06-25-1960-cryptography.butterflyEffect: Bernon Mitchell and William Martin resurfaced in Moscow that September, publicly defecting and exposing details of NSA's signals intelligence operations against the Soviet Union. Their defection became one of the Cold War's most damaging security scandals, forcing sweeping reforms in how the NSA vetted and monitored its own personnel.

evt-06-25-1976-missouri.scenario: It is 1976, and America's Bicentennial has renewed attention on old wrongs. You advise Missouri Governor Kit Bond, who is weighing whether to formally address the 1838 order that had driven Latter-day Saints from the state at gunpoint.
evt-06-25-1976-missouri.prompt: What does Governor Bond do about the 138-year-old Extermination Order?

choices.text: Reaffirm the order as a matter of historical record
Decline to act, citing the statute's obsolescence
Sign an executive order formally rescinding the 1838 Extermination Order
Refer the matter to the Missouri courts for a ruling

evt-06-25-1976-missouri.butterflyEffect: Bond signed an executive order formally rescinding Governor Lilburn Boggs's 1838 Extermination Order, which had authorized expelling or killing Mormons in Missouri. Though largely symbolic by 1976, the rescission was seen as a gesture of reconciliation acknowledging the violent expulsion that had pushed Latter-day Saints toward their eventual settlement in Utah.

evt-06-25-1981-microsoft.scenario: It's 25 June 1981 in Bellevue, Washington. Your small software partnership with Paul Allen has grown fast, and lawyers are urging you to change its legal structure before signing bigger contracts and hiring more staff.
evt-06-25-1981-microsoft.prompt: What structural change do you make to the company?

choices.text: Remain an informal partnership indefinitely
Incorporate the company in Washington State
Merge with a larger East Coast software firm
Sell the company outright to IBM

evt-06-25-1981-microsoft.butterflyEffect: Microsoft reincorporated as a Washington State company, shielding its founders from personal liability and laying the legal groundwork for future growth. Five years later this structure enabled Microsoft's 1986 IPO, which made Bill Gates the youngest self-made billionaire in American history.

evt-06-25-1991-breakup-of-yugoslavia.scenario: It is 25 June 1991, and you sit in Slovenia's parliament as it formally declares independence from Yugoslavia, just as Croatia does the same.
evt-06-25-1991-breakup-of-yugoslavia.prompt: How did the Yugoslav federal army respond to Slovenia's declaration of independence?

choices.text: It accepted the declaration without incident
It ignored the declaration entirely
It requested UN peacekeepers immediately
It sent troops to try to block the secession

evt-06-25-1991-breakup-of-yugoslavia.butterflyEffect: Within days the Yugoslav People's Army moved to block Slovenia's secession, triggering the brief Ten-Day War. Slovenia's successful breakaway emboldened Croatia's independence drive, and the unresolved tensions spiraled into the wider Yugoslav Wars that would devastate the region for the rest of the decade.

evt-06-25-1992-space-shuttle-columbia.scenario: It is June 25, 1992, and you are a flight controller in Houston as Columbia lifts off carrying the U.S. Microgravity Laboratory. Consumables are limited, and mission planners are watching the numbers closely as the days stretch on.
evt-06-25-1992-space-shuttle-columbia.prompt: What did NASA decide to do as the mission ran longer than any shuttle flight before it?

choices.text: Extend the mission using an Extended Duration Orbiter kit, setting a new shuttle endurance record
Abort and return early due to a payload malfunction
Cut the mission short to conserve oxygen and power
Dock with Mir to resupply consumables

evt-06-25-1992-space-shuttle-columbia.butterflyEffect: Columbia's STS-50 flight was extended to nearly 14 days, becoming the longest shuttle mission flown to that date. The success proved the orbiter could support extended-duration science flights, paving the way for later long-duration missions that helped prepare NASA for sustained operations aboard the future International Space Station.

evt-06-25-1993-kim-campbell.scenario: It is 25 June 1993, and you have just been sworn in as Canada's first female prime minister, inheriting a Progressive Conservative government battered by years of unpopular policies and a looming election.
evt-06-25-1993-kim-campbell.prompt: What happened when Campbell led the PC party into the general election that autumn?

choices.text: The Progressive Conservatives won a comfortable majority
The party was reduced to just two seats in Parliament
She resigned before the election was held
She formed a coalition government with the NDP

evt-06-25-1993-kim-campbell.butterflyEffect: In the October 1993 election, the Progressive Conservatives collapsed from 156 seats to just 2, the worst defeat ever suffered by a governing party in Canadian history. Campbell lost her own seat, and the PC party never recovered its former strength before merging into the new Conservative Party of Canada in 2003.

evt-06-25-1996-khobar-towers-bombing.scenario: It is 25 June 1996, and you are stationed at the Khobar Towers housing complex near Dhahran when a fuel tanker parked outside the perimeter fence detonates with devastating force.
evt-06-25-1996-khobar-towers-bombing.prompt: Who did U.S. investigators later conclude was responsible for planning the attack?

choices.text: A domestic Saudi militia group
Iraqi intelligence agents
Saudi Hezbollah operatives backed by Iran
Al-Qaeda operatives acting alone

evt-06-25-1996-khobar-towers-bombing.butterflyEffect: American investigators eventually indicted members of Saudi Hezbollah, concluding that Iran's Revolutionary Guard had directed and supported the bombing. The attack hardened U.S. policy toward Iran and pushed American forces in the Gulf toward more secure, isolated bases.

evt-06-25-1996-jay-z.scenario: It's 25 June 1996 in Brooklyn. Major labels have passed on your demo tapes, so you and your partners Damon Dash and Kareem Burke must decide how to get your debut album into stores.
evt-06-25-1996-jay-z.prompt: How do you release your debut album, Reasonable Doubt?

choices.text: Release it only as scattered mixtapes on the street
Sign an exclusive deal with a major label like Def Jam
Shelve the album and focus on production work for others
Self-release it through his own new label, Roc-A-Fella Records

evt-06-25-1996-jay-z.butterflyEffect: Jay-Z released the album through Roc-A-Fella Records, the independent label he co-founded, distributed via Priority Records. That independent-first model became the blueprint for his later business empire, proving hip-hop artists could bypass major labels and control their own careers.

evt-06-25-1997-progress-m-34.scenario: It is 25 June 1997 aboard Mir, and you watch cosmonaut Vasily Tsibliyev manually steer an uncrewed Progress supply craft during a docking test when it suddenly drifts off course toward the station.
evt-06-25-1997-progress-m-34.prompt: What did the crew do after the Progress craft struck and punctured the Spektr module?

choices.text: They fired thrusters to boost Mir into a higher orbit
They evacuated the station entirely in the emergency Soyuz
They sealed off the damaged Spektr module to stop the leak
They deliberately vented the station's atmosphere

evt-06-25-1997-progress-m-34.butterflyEffect: The collision tore a hole in the Spektr module, causing a rapid pressure leak; the crew scrambled to seal it off before all air escaped, saving the station but permanently losing Spektr's solar power and science instruments. The near-disaster intensified scrutiny of Mir's aging systems just as planning for the International Space Station was accelerating.

evt-06-25-2009-michael-jackson.scenario: It's the early hours of 25 June 2009 in a rented Los Angeles mansion. As Michael Jackson's personal physician, you face an exhausted, sleep-deprived pop icon begging for anything that will let him rest before his comeback tour rehearsals resume.
evt-06-25-2009-michael-jackson.prompt: What do you administer to help him sleep?

choices.text: Insist he be hospitalized overnight for observation
Prescribe only a standard over-the-counter sleep aid
Administer propofol, an anesthetic, despite lacking proper monitoring equipment
Refuse and recommend cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia instead

evt-06-25-2009-michael-jackson.butterflyEffect: Dr. Conrad Murray gave Jackson propofol, a surgical anesthetic, without proper monitoring equipment, and Jackson died of acute propofol intoxication. Murray was later convicted of involuntary manslaughter, and the case triggered nationwide scrutiny of physicians who prescribe powerful drugs for wealthy private clients outside hospital settings.

evt-06-25-2009-death-of-michael-jackson.scenario: It is the afternoon of June 25, 2009, and you are a paramedic arriving at a Holmby Hills mansion to find Michael Jackson unresponsive, with his personal physician performing CPR on the bedroom floor.
evt-06-25-2009-death-of-michael-jackson.prompt: What did paramedics and doctors do after finding Jackson without a pulse?

choices.text: Transported him to UCLA Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead
Declared him dead on the scene and did not attempt transport
Left him with his physician and departed without treatment
Administered more propofol to stabilize him

evt-06-25-2009-death-of-michael-jackson.butterflyEffect: Jackson was rushed to Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead at 2:26 p.m. His death, caused by acute propofol intoxication, triggered a worldwide outpouring of grief and a criminal investigation that led to physician Conrad Murray's 2011 conviction for involuntary manslaughter.

evt-06-25-2022-russo-ukrainian-war-2022-.scenario: It is late June 2022 in Sievierodonetsk, and you are among hundreds of civilians and wounded soldiers sheltering as Russian forces close in around the city's massive Azot chemical plant, the last pocket of Ukrainian-held ground.
evt-06-25-2022-russo-ukrainian-war-2022-.prompt: What did the people trapped at the Azot plant do as the city fell?

choices.text: Held the plant indefinitely without any losses
Sheltered in the plant's bunkers before evacuating as the city fell
Surrendered immediately to Russian troops at the gates
Were airlifted out by Ukrainian helicopters

evt-06-25-2022-russo-ukrainian-war-2022-.butterflyEffect: Civilians and remaining fighters sheltered in the plant's underground bunkers before eventually evacuating across the river as Russian forces took full control of the city. The capture gave Russia command of most of Luhansk Oblast, and neighboring Lysychansk fell within days, completing the region's occupation.

evt-06-25-2022-sheikh-hasina.scenario: It is 25 June 2022 and you stand among the crowds at the opening of the Padma Bridge, a project that had to be rebuilt financially from scratch after its original foreign backer pulled out years earlier.
evt-06-25-2022-sheikh-hasina.prompt: What controversy forced Bangladesh to fund the Padma Bridge without its original international lender?

choices.text: Allegations of corruption in the construction bidding process
Public opposition to hiring foreign contractors
A territorial dispute with India over the river
A cyclone destroyed the original funding infrastructure

evt-06-25-2022-sheikh-hasina.butterflyEffect: The World Bank cancelled a $1.2 billion credit in 2012 over corruption allegations linked to the bidding process, prompting Bangladesh to finance the entire bridge domestically. Its completion became a symbol of national self-reliance and dramatically improved transport links across southern Bangladesh.

evt-06-25-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.scenario: It is late June 2022, and you command Ukrainian troops holding the last blocks of Sievierodonetsk. Russian artillery has reduced the city to rubble, and the roads out are narrowing under constant fire.
evt-06-25-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.prompt: What did Ukrainian commanders decide to do to avoid their troops being encircled?

choices.text: Ordered a full withdrawal to more defensible positions in Lysychansk
Negotiated a local ceasefire to evacuate only civilians
Launched a counteroffensive to retake the city's outskirts
Held every position regardless of losses

evt-06-25-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.butterflyEffect: Ukrainian forces withdrew across the river to Lysychansk to avoid encirclement, ending the grinding battle after weeks of some of the war's heaviest fighting. Lysychansk itself fell days later, giving Russia control of nearly all of Luhansk Oblast at enormous cost to both sides.

evt-06-25-2022-oslo.scenario: It's the morning of 25 June 2022 in Oslo. Gunfire has just erupted near the London Pub in the city center, and thousands are expected downtown later for the annual Pride parade.
evt-06-25-2022-oslo.prompt: What do organizers do about the scheduled Pride parade?

choices.text: Postpone the parade by exactly one week
Reroute the parade through a different city entirely
Proceed with the parade as planned without changes
Cancel the parade for public safety

evt-06-25-2022-oslo.butterflyEffect: Organizers cancelled Oslo Pride's parade that day as police investigated the attack, which killed two people and wounded twenty-one near LGBT nightlife venues. The shooting was treated as a targeted attack on the queer community, and the following year's Pride drew record crowds in defiant response.

evt-06-25-2024-2024-storming-of-the-keny.scenario: It's 25 June 2024 outside Kenya's Parliament Buildings in Nairobi. You're one of thousands of young protesters who have breached the gates, furious that MPs have just passed the Finance Bill 2024 raising taxes during a painful cost-of-living crisis.
evt-06-25-2024-2024-storming-of-the-keny.prompt: What happens to the bill you're protesting against?

choices.text: Parliament reintroduces an identical bill within a week
The Kenyan judiciary strikes down the bill months later
President Ruto vetoes the bill the following day
The bill is signed into law unchanged

evt-06-25-2024-2024-storming-of-the-keny.butterflyEffect: President William Ruto vetoed the Finance Bill the very next day, bowing to the unprecedented public pressure. The protests, and the deadly police response to them, became a defining moment of Kenya's Gen Z-led movement against government overreach and corruption.

evt-06-26-1409-council-of-pisa.scenario: You sit among the cardinals gathered at Pisa in 1409, drawn from both the Avignon and Roman obediences. Two rival popes, Benedict XIII and Gregory XII, have just been declared deposed for schism and heresy, and the assembled college must decide what to do next.
evt-06-26-1409-council-of-pisa.prompt: What does the council do to fill the vacant papacy?

choices.text: Formally submit to Gregory XII as the legitimate pope
Leave the papacy vacant until both rivals died
Recognize Benedict XIII in Avignon as sole pontiff
Elect a new pope, Alexander V, to replace both rivals

evt-06-26-1409-council-of-pisa.butterflyEffect: The cardinals elected Peter of Candia as Pope Alexander V, but neither deposed pope recognized the decision, leaving Christendom with three simultaneous claimants instead of two. The impasse dragged on until the Council of Constance finally resolved the Western Schism in 1417.

evt-06-26-1886-henri-moissan.scenario: It is 26 June 1886 in your Paris laboratory. Chemists have failed for decades to isolate fluorine, and several rivals have been poisoned or blinded trying. You stand before your platinum-iridium apparatus, ready to attempt it again.
evt-06-26-1886-henri-moissan.prompt: What method do you use to finally isolate elemental fluorine?

choices.text: Heating fluorspar with concentrated sulfuric acid over an open flame
Passing chlorine gas through molten calcium fluoride
Distilling liquid air to separate out the gas
Electrolysis of potassium fluoride dissolved in anhydrous hydrofluoric acid

evt-06-26-1886-henri-moissan.butterflyEffect: Moissan electrolysed a mixture of dry potassium fluoride and anhydrous hydrofluoric acid at low temperature, using platinum-iridium electrodes to resist the gas's extreme corrosiveness. The feat won him the 1906 Nobel Prize and opened the door to fluorine chemistry that would later underpin refrigerants, Teflon, and uranium enrichment via UF6.

evt-06-26-1907-vladimir-lenin.scenario: It is 26 June 1907, and you are part of a Bolshevik militant group in Tiflis, waiting in Yerevan Square as a bank convoy approaches. The operation, organized with the knowledge of Lenin and Stalin's allies, is meant to fund the underground party.
evt-06-26-1907-vladimir-lenin.prompt: What happens when the group strikes the convoy?

choices.text: Lenin himself is captured during the raid
The convoy guards repel the attack without any losses
The raiders seize a large sum of cash to fund Bolshevik activities
The plot fails and every conspirator is arrested on the spot

evt-06-26-1907-vladimir-lenin.butterflyEffect: Bombs and gunfire in the square killed and wounded dozens of bystanders as the raiders seized a large sum of money for Bolshevik coffers, though much of it later proved impossible to launder abroad. The robbery deepened splits with the Mensheviks, who condemned such expropriations, while burnishing Stalin's reputation among the Bolshevik underground.

evt-06-26-1981-dan-air-flight-240.scenario: It is the early hours of 26 June 1981. Your Hawker Siddeley HS 748 climbs into the night sky from Gatwick, mail sacks lashed down behind you, bound for East Midlands Airport over the dark fields of Leicestershire.
evt-06-26-1981-dan-air-flight-240.prompt: What actually brings the aircraft down over Nailstone minutes later?

choices.text: Structural failure caused by a cabin door coming open in flight
Both engines flaming out from fuel contamination
Pilot disorientation in fog leading to controlled flight into terrain
A mid-air collision with another aircraft

evt-06-26-1981-dan-air-flight-240.butterflyEffect: A cabin door failed in flight, triggering a catastrophic structural failure that destroyed the aircraft and killed all three crew. The accident prompted a fresh look at door-locking mechanisms and structural inspection standards on ageing turboprop freighters across British regional carriers.

evt-06-26-1995-hamad-bin-khalifa-al-than.scenario: It is 26 June 1995 in Doha. Your father, Emir Khalifa bin Hamad Al Thani, is abroad in Switzerland, and as Crown Prince you have quietly secured the loyalty of the security forces to take power in his absence.
evt-06-26-1995-hamad-bin-khalifa-al-than.prompt: What happens to the deposed Emir Khalifa after the bloodless coup?

choices.text: He is sent into exile abroad, later reconciling with his son
He is placed under permanent house arrest in Doha
He retains a ceremonial ruling title alongside his son
He is tried and imprisoned by a new government tribunal

evt-06-26-1995-hamad-bin-khalifa-al-than.butterflyEffect: Khalifa went into exile abroad, initially resisting the takeover, before the two eventually reconciled years later. Hamad's rule that followed transformed Qatar diplomatically and economically, launching Al Jazeera in 1996 and setting Qatar on the path to hosting the 2022 World Cup.

evt-06-26-1997-j-k-rowling.scenario: It is 26 June 1997, and a small London publisher, Bloomsbury, releases a debut children's novel about a boy wizard by a little-known author writing as J. K. Rowling. The initial print run is modest, and no one yet knows how it will sell.
evt-06-26-1997-j-k-rowling.prompt: What actually happened to the book in the years that followed?

choices.text: It became the start of the best-selling book series in history
It was banned from British school libraries within a year
It sold only modestly and was quietly discontinued after two sequels
It failed to secure any publisher outside the United Kingdom

evt-06-26-1997-j-k-rowling.butterflyEffect: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone grew word of mouth into a global phenomenon, spawning six sequels, a film franchise, and over 600 million copies sold, making it the best-selling book series in history. Rowling went from a struggling single mother to one of the wealthiest authors alive.

evt-06-26-2006-mari-alkatiri.scenario: It is 26 June 2006, and you are Prime Minister Mari Alkatiri of East Timor. Weeks of factional violence, an army mutiny, and allegations that you armed a secret hit squad to eliminate rivals have left your government paralyzed.
evt-06-26-2006-mari-alkatiri.prompt: What does Alkatiri do under this mounting pressure?

choices.text: Declare martial law and suppress the mutiny by force
Dissolve Fretilin and form a new ruling party
Resign as Prime Minister
Call for immediate UN administration of the country

evt-06-26-2006-mari-alkatiri.butterflyEffect: Alkatiri resigned, ending a crisis that had already forced tens of thousands from their homes and drawn in international peacekeepers. The upheaval reshaped East Timorese politics, paving the way for new leadership and continued UN involvement in stabilizing the young nation.

evt-06-26-2010-2010-g20-toronto-summit.scenario: You are a police commander in downtown Toronto on 26 June 2010, as world leaders meet behind a massive security perimeter for the G20 summit. Outside, thousands of protesters have gathered, and some are smashing storefronts and setting police cars alight.
evt-06-26-2010-2010-g20-toronto-summit.prompt: What happened in the streets during the summit weekend?

choices.text: Police conducted the largest mass arrest in Canadian history
Protesters were kept miles away and no arrests were made
The Canadian army was deployed to occupy downtown Toronto
The summit was cancelled and leaders evacuated by helicopter

evt-06-26-2010-2010-g20-toronto-summit.butterflyEffect: Police carried out the largest mass arrest in Canadian history, detaining over a thousand people, many later released without charge. The heavy-handed response triggered public inquiries and lasting criticism of policing tactics at major international summits.

evt-06-26-2024-julian-assange.scenario: It is 26 June 2024, and you are Julian Assange, boarding a flight from the Northern Mariana Islands back to Australia. Hours earlier, in a US federal courtroom on Saipan, you signed a plea agreement ending fourteen years of legal battles.
evt-06-26-2024-julian-assange.prompt: What did Assange plead guilty to in the deal that freed him?

choices.text: Espionage on behalf of a foreign government
Perjury committed during his extradition hearings
Conspiracy to unlawfully obtain and disclose classified national defense information
Computer hacking under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act

evt-06-26-2024-julian-assange.butterflyEffect: He pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to obtain and disclose classified US national defense documents, receiving a sentence equal to time already served in Belmarsh prison. The deal ended his imprisonment but left unresolved the debate over whether publishing leaked material can be prosecuted as espionage, a question that now looms over future national-security journalism.

evt-06-27-678-pope-agatho.scenario: The year is 679. You are Wilfrid, bishop of York, driven from your see after Archbishop Theodore split your diocese without your consent. You have journeyed to Rome to plead your case before Pope Agatho.
evt-06-27-678-pope-agatho.prompt: What do you ask the pope to rule?

choices.text: That Canterbury be formally recognized as having authority over York
That you be fully restored to your original, undivided diocese of York
