That Archbishop Theodore be excommunicated for his actions
That you be granted an independent monastery free of any bishop's authority

evt-06-27-678-pope-agatho.butterflyEffect: Agatho's council ruled in Wilfrid's favor, ordering his restoration to York. But King Ecgfrith of Northumbria refused to comply and imprisoned him instead, exposing the real limits of papal authority over Anglo-Saxon kings and foreshadowing centuries of church-state friction in England.

evt-06-27-1571-elizabeth-i.scenario: You are Hugh Price, a Welsh churchman petitioning Queen Elizabeth I in 1571 for royal backing to found a new Protestant college at Oxford, aimed especially at educating Welsh clergy.
evt-06-27-1571-elizabeth-i.prompt: What do you ask the Queen to grant?

choices.text: A grant of land for a cathedral school in Wales itself
Royal funds to expand an existing Oxford college
A royal charter establishing a new college, Jesus College
Permission to convert a dissolved monastery into a private school

evt-06-27-1571-elizabeth-i.butterflyEffect: Elizabeth granted the royal charter, establishing Jesus College as the first Oxford college founded after the Reformation. It developed a lasting association with Wales, producing generations of Welsh clergy, scholars, and public figures down to the present day.

evt-06-27-1743-war-of-the-austrian-succe.scenario: You are King George II at the Battle of Dettingen on 27 June 1743, watching French cavalry threaten to crush your Pragmatic Army trapped along the Main river. Your officers urge you to withdraw to safety.
evt-06-27-1743-war-of-the-austrian-succe.prompt: Do you dismount and personally lead the infantry into the counterattack?

choices.text: Dismount and lead the infantry counterattack on foot
Retreat behind the lines and let generals direct the battle
Order an immediate full retreat across the Main
Remain mounted at the rear to direct the cavalry only

evt-06-27-1743-war-of-the-austrian-succe.butterflyEffect: George II fought on foot alongside his infantry, and the army repelled the French and escaped the trap. It was the last time a reigning British monarch personally led troops in battle, after which British sovereigns directed wars from home rather than the field.

evt-06-27-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: It is June 27, 1864, near Kennesaw Mountain, Georgia. You command a Union brigade ordered by General Sherman to make a direct frontal assault on Confederate General Johnston's entrenched lines defending Atlanta.
evt-06-27-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What happens when your men advance?

choices.text: You are ordered to retreat before making contact
You successfully outflank the Confederate position
You are repulsed with heavy losses, forcing Sherman back to flanking maneuvers
You break through the Confederate line and rout Johnston's army

evt-06-27-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The assault was repulsed with roughly 3,000 Union casualties against far fewer Confederate losses. Sherman abandoned further direct attacks and returned to his preferred strategy of flanking maneuvers, eventually working his way around Kennesaw to continue the campaign toward Atlanta.

evt-06-27-1869-battle-of-hakodate.scenario: You are Enomoto Takeaki, admiral of the remnant shogunate fleet, holding out inside Goryōkaku fortress as Imperial forces close in around Hakodate after months of siege.
evt-06-27-1869-battle-of-hakodate.prompt: With defeat certain, what do you do?

choices.text: Flee north to continue a guerrilla resistance
Fight to the last man rather than yield the fortress
Surrender to spare the lives of your remaining men
Negotiate for Hokkaido to become an independent state

evt-06-27-1869-battle-of-hakodate.butterflyEffect: Enomoto surrendered, ending the Boshin War and the military phase of the Meiji Restoration. Rather than being executed, he was later pardoned and went on to serve as a minister in the very Meiji government he had fought, becoming a symbol of reconciliation between the old order and the new.

evt-06-27-1869-meiji-restoration.scenario: You advise the new Meiji government. Word has just arrived that Enomoto Takeaki's forces have surrendered at Hakodate, ending the last armed resistance to imperial rule.
evt-06-27-1869-meiji-restoration.prompt: What should the government do next to secure its authority?

choices.text: Restore the shogunate under new, more loyal leadership
Grant the daimyo full autonomy in exchange for loyalty oaths
Press ahead with abolishing the domains and centralizing power under the emperor
Disband the imperial army now that peace has returned

evt-06-27-1869-meiji-restoration.butterflyEffect: With resistance over, the Meiji government pressed forward and by 1871 abolished the old han (domains), replacing them with centrally administered prefectures under direct imperial control. This consolidation cleared the way for Japan's rapid program of Westernizing reform and industrialization.

evt-06-27-1899-a-e-j-collins.scenario: You're a 13-year-old schoolboy at Clifton College in June 1899, still batting in a junior house match that has stretched into its fourth afternoon, with your score already past 500 not out.
evt-06-27-1899-a-e-j-collins.prompt: What do you do as your innings drags on toward an extraordinary total?

choices.text: Retire out to give your teammates a chance to bat
Deliberately get out to end the spectacle
Ask the umpires to declare the innings closed
Keep batting and pushing the score higher

evt-06-27-1899-a-e-j-collins.butterflyEffect: Collins kept batting until he reached 628 not out, a score that stood as cricket's highest recorded innings for 116 years. He never played first-class cricket and was killed in action in 1914, but his schoolboy record was only broken in 2016 by Indian teenager Pranav Dhanawade.

evt-06-27-1905-russian-revolution-of-190.scenario: You are a sailor aboard the battleship Potemkin in the Black Sea, June 1905. The crew has been served borscht made from meat crawling with maggots, and an officer threatens to shoot anyone who refuses to eat it.
evt-06-27-1905-russian-revolution-of-190.prompt: What do you do when officers order punishment for refusing rotten meat?

choices.text: Quietly desert the ship at the next port
Obey the order and eat the soup to avoid punishment
Join the mutiny and help the crew seize the ship
File a formal written complaint through the chain of command

evt-06-27-1905-russian-revolution-of-190.butterflyEffect: The crew mutinied, killed several officers, and seized the ship, sailing to Odessa in hopes of sparking a wider uprising before surrendering it in Romania. The mutiny became an international symbol of revolt against tsarist injustice and was later immortalized in Sergei Eisenstein's 1925 film Battleship Potemkin.

evt-06-27-1950-korean-war.scenario: You are a US Air Force pilot flying an F-82 Twin Mustang over Suwon airfield on 27 June 1950, escorting evacuation flights just two days after North Korea's invasion. Five North Korean fighters suddenly dive toward the transport planes you are protecting.
evt-06-27-1950-korean-war.prompt: Do you break formation to intercept the attacking fighters?

choices.text: Radio Tokyo and wait for further orders before acting
Attempt to ram one of the enemy aircraft to save ammunition
Engage the enemy fighters to protect the evacuation planes
Break off and fly the transports back to Japan immediately

evt-06-27-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: American pilots engaged and shot down several North Korean aircraft, scoring the first aerial victories of the Korean War. The clash marked the moment American forces moved from evacuation duty into direct combat, signaling the start of full US military involvement under the United Nations Command.

evt-06-27-1954-jacobo-arbenz.scenario: It's 27 June 1954 in Guatemala City. A CIA-backed campaign of psychological warfare and armed incursion has shattered your government's authority, and your own military high command is now urging you to step aside.
evt-06-27-1954-jacobo-arbenz.prompt: What did President Árbenz do to end the crisis?

choices.text: Fled the country immediately without addressing the nation
Declared martial law and ordered the army to fight the invasion
Resigned and transferred power to the military
Appealed directly to the United Nations for troops

evt-06-27-1954-jacobo-arbenz.butterflyEffect: Árbenz resigned and handed power to a military colonel, ending Guatemala's decade of democratic reform and land redistribution. The coup opened decades of military rule and set the stage for a brutal 36-year civil war, while Árbenz spent the rest of his life in exile.

evt-06-27-1957-hurricane-audrey.scenario: It is 27 June 1957 along the Louisiana coast near Cameron. Hurricane Audrey has exploded in strength overnight into a major hurricane, and its storm surge is already pushing far inland before most residents have left their homes.
evt-06-27-1957-hurricane-audrey.prompt: Why does the death toll from Audrey become so catastrophic?

choices.text: Residents ignored repeated, timely evacuation warnings out of complacency
Levees built to hold back the storm surge collapsed under the strain
A communications blackout prevented any warnings from being issued at all
The storm strengthened so quickly overnight that evacuation orders came too late

evt-06-27-1957-hurricane-audrey.butterflyEffect: Audrey intensified so rapidly overnight that evacuation warnings reached many coastal communities too late, and the storm surge drove up to 20 miles inland before residents could flee. The disaster spurred improvements in hurricane forecasting and evacuation timing along the Gulf Coast in the years that followed.

evt-06-27-1976-ebola.scenario: It is late June 1976 in Nzara, southern Sudan. A worker at the local cotton factory has fallen gravely ill with fever and bleeding that doctors have never seen before, and cases are beginning to spread among his contacts.
evt-06-27-1976-ebola.prompt: Where does this first identifiable outbreak trace its origin to?

choices.text: A hunter who had recently butchered bushmeat
A missionary returning from the Congo River basin
A worker at a cotton factory in Nzara
A hospital nurse treating malaria patients

evt-06-27-1976-ebola.butterflyEffect: The index case was a worker at a cotton factory in Nzara, and the outbreak spread through his contacts before health authorities intervened. Investigators later connected it to a nearly simultaneous outbreak in Zaire, leading to the naming and identification of the Ebola virus and shaping how future haemorrhagic fever outbreaks would be tracked and contained.

evt-06-27-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.scenario: It is June 1991 in Osijek, Croatia. A column of Yugoslav Army tanks rolls toward the city center as Croatia's declaration of independence hangs in the balance, and you are a civilian standing in the street watching them approach.
evt-06-27-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.prompt: What does the civilian famously do to try to halt the tank column?

choices.text: He parks his car directly in the tank's path
He flees the city with his family immediately
He runs to alert Croatian National Guard units
He throws a Molotov cocktail at the lead tank

evt-06-27-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.butterflyEffect: He pulled his own car across the road directly in front of the lead tank, forcing a standoff that was photographed and broadcast worldwide. The image became an early symbol of civilian defiance in the Croatian War of Independence, rallying international sympathy even as fighting dragged on until the 1995 peace agreements.

evt-06-27-1994-aum-shinrikyo.scenario: You are a police investigator in Matsumoto, Nagano, on the night of 27 June 1994, after residents near a courthouse dormitory suddenly collapse from a toxic gas with no clear source. A local resident who first reported the smell has homemade chemicals in his yard.
evt-06-27-1994-aum-shinrikyo.prompt: Where should the investigation focus first?

choices.text: Suspect the neighbor who reported the smell and search his property
Immediately question members of the Aum Shinrikyo cult
Treat it as an isolated accidental poisoning and close the case
Investigate a possible gas leak from a nearby factory

evt-06-27-1994-aum-shinrikyo.butterflyEffect: Police wrongly suspected the neighbor who reported the gas, Yoshiyuki Kono, and he was vilified in the press for months despite being an innocent victim himself. This misdirection let the real perpetrators, the Aum Shinrikyo cult, escape scrutiny, and less than a year later the same group carried out the larger Tokyo subway sarin attack.

evt-06-27-2008-robert-mugabe.scenario: It's late June 2008 in Zimbabwe. Morgan Tsvangirai has just withdrawn from the presidential runoff, citing a campaign of violence against his supporters, leaving Robert Mugabe as the only name effectively on the ballot.
evt-06-27-2008-robert-mugabe.prompt: What did Mugabe do to secure his re-election in this runoff?

choices.text: Step down in favor of a caretaker government
Call for fresh elections with international monitors
Postpone the runoff indefinitely to negotiate a settlement
Proceed with the runoff as sole candidate and claim victory

evt-06-27-2008-robert-mugabe.butterflyEffect: Mugabe proceeded with the runoff largely unopposed and was declared the overwhelming winner, drawing international condemnation of the vote as illegitimate. Regional pressure led to a power-sharing deal months later, making Tsvangirai prime minister in a fragile unity government alongside Mugabe.

evt-06-27-2015-2015-new-taipei-water-par.scenario: You help run an outdoor color-powder party at Formosa Fun Coast water park in New Taipei City. Staff are about to fire another burst of corn starch powder over the crowd, right near the stage's lights and speakers.
evt-06-27-2015-2015-new-taipei-water-par.prompt: What should you do before the next burst?

choices.text: Continue as scheduled to keep the crowd's energy up
Halt spraying until all lighting and electrical sources are shielded or cleared
Only switch off the lights closest to the DJ booth
Add extra powder for a more dramatic effect

evt-06-27-2015-2015-new-taipei-water-par.butterflyEffect: The powder ignited near an ignition source, and the resulting flash fire swept over the crowd in about 40 seconds, injuring over 500 people and killing 15. The disaster led Taiwan to ban color-powder events and impose strict new fire-safety rules for temporary outdoor stages.

evt-06-27-2017-2017-ukraine-ransomware-a.scenario: It's the afternoon of 27 June 2017, and you're an IT administrator at a Kyiv bank. Every screen on your network suddenly locks with a ransom demand, and colleagues report the same thing happening at ministries and power companies across the country.
evt-06-27-2017-2017-ukraine-ransomware-a.prompt: What is the correct immediate response to contain the outbreak?

choices.text: Isolate infected machines and disconnect them from the network at once
Reboot the affected computers repeatedly until they clear
Pay the Bitcoin ransom immediately to restore access
Keep systems running and wait for a vendor patch

evt-06-27-2017-2017-ukraine-ransomware-a.butterflyEffect: Investigators soon found the ransom mechanism was broken by design—this was 'NotPetya,' a destructive weapon disguised as ransomware, widely attributed to Russian military intelligence targeting Ukraine. It spread globally regardless, costing firms like Maersk and Merck hundreds of millions of dollars and becoming one of the most damaging cyberattacks in history.

evt-06-27-2018-hayabusa2.scenario: You're a JAXA flight controller on 27 June 2018, watching telemetry as the Hayabusa2 probe, after three and a half years of travel, closes in on the tiny, rubble-pile asteroid Ryugu.
evt-06-27-2018-hayabusa2.prompt: How does the team safely bring the probe to its rendezvous with the asteroid?

choices.text: Release all samples-collection hardware before arrival
Orbit the asteroid at high speed without stopping
Slowly match velocity and hover at a safe station-keeping distance
Fire retro-rockets to crash-land directly onto the surface

evt-06-27-2018-hayabusa2.butterflyEffect: Hayabusa2 held station near Ryugu for a year and a half, deploying rovers and even firing a projectile to collect subsurface samples. It returned those samples to Earth in December 2020, giving scientists pristine asteroid material and pointing the extended mission toward two more asteroid encounters through 2031.

evt-06-27-2024-president-of-the-united-s.scenario: You are a Democratic Party strategist watching the presidential debate in Atlanta on 27 June 2024, as President Biden struggles with his delivery against former President Trump. Party donors and officials are already calling your phone.
evt-06-27-2024-president-of-the-united-s.prompt: What follows in the weeks after this widely criticized debate performance?

choices.text: The debate is rescheduled after technical complaints
Biden's approval ratings surge following the debate
Biden announces a new running mate the following week
Biden withdraws from the race and endorses Kamala Harris

evt-06-27-2024-president-of-the-united-s.butterflyEffect: Doubts about Biden's fitness for a second term intensified rapidly after the debate. On 21 July 2024 he withdrew from the presidential race and endorsed Vice President Kamala Harris, who then became the Democratic nominee against Trump.

evt-06-28-572-alboin.scenario: It is 572 in Verona. At a royal banquet, your husband King Alboin has just forced you to drink wine from a cup fashioned from your own father's skull, humiliating you before the entire Lombard court.
evt-06-28-572-alboin.prompt: As Queen Rosamund, what do you do to answer this insult?

choices.text: Flee immediately to her father's former kingdom for protection
Publicly denounce him before his warriors and demand an apology
Report the insult to the Byzantine emperor and request intervention
Conspire secretly with allies at court to have him assassinated

evt-06-28-572-alboin.butterflyEffect: Rosamund conspired with her lover Helmichis and the strongman Peredeo to murder Alboin in his chamber. The killing plunged the Lombard kingdom into chaos, and after a decade without a strong central king, Lombard nobles ruled Italy through fragmented duchies for years afterward.

evt-06-28-1461-edward-iv.scenario: It is 28 June 1461, and you stand inside Westminster Abbey as the young Yorkist claimant Edward Plantagenet is crowned King of England, fresh from his decisive victories over Lancastrian forces.
evt-06-28-1461-edward-iv.prompt: What must Edward do now to secure the throne he has just claimed?

choices.text: Marry Margaret of Anjou to unite the rival factions
Abolish the House of Lords to weaken rival nobles
Retire from active rule and govern through a regency council
Continue military campaigns against Lancastrian resistance and Henry VI's supporters

evt-06-28-1461-edward-iv.butterflyEffect: Edward IV's coronation did not end the Wars of the Roses; Lancastrian resistance and the exiled Henry VI's supporters kept fighting for years. Edward was even briefly deposed in 1470–71 before reclaiming the crown, and his eventual death in 1483 opened the door for Richard III's controversial seizure of power.

evt-06-28-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: You are a South Carolina militiaman inside the unfinished palmetto-log fort on Sullivan's Island as a British fleet opens fire at close range on 28 June 1776.
evt-06-28-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What should the garrison do as cannonballs sink harmlessly into the fort's spongy walls?

choices.text: Keep firing steadily back at the British warships
Abandon the fort and retreat to the mainland
Surrender before the walls collapse
Launch small boats to board the enemy ships

evt-06-28-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: The soft palmetto logs absorbed the British cannonballs instead of splintering, and Colonel Moultrie's men held their fire discipline and drove off Commodore Parker's fleet. The victory boosted Patriot morale in the South and led South Carolina to place the palmetto tree on its state flag; the fort was renamed Fort Moultrie in his honor.

evt-06-28-1841-giselle.scenario: It is June 1841, days before the premiere of a new romantic ballet at the Paris Opéra. You must cast the demanding title role of Giselle, and an unproven young Italian dancer, Carlotta Grisi, is being considered over more established ballerinas.
evt-06-28-1841-giselle.prompt: As the choreographer, do you risk casting the unknown Grisi in the lead role?

choices.text: Cast a senior, already-famous ballerina to guarantee success
Split the role between two dancers to reduce the risk
Cast Carlotta Grisi despite her inexperience
Postpone the premiere until a proven dancer is available

evt-06-28-1841-giselle.butterflyEffect: Grisi was cast, and her performance on 28 June 1841 was a triumph that made her an international star overnight. Giselle became a cornerstone of the Romantic ballet repertoire, still performed by major companies worldwide nearly two centuries later.

evt-06-28-1846-adolphe-sax.scenario: It is 1846 in Paris. You are the instrument maker Adolphe Sax, and rival workshops have begun copying the brass-and-reed instrument you developed a few years earlier.
evt-06-28-1846-adolphe-sax.prompt: What should you do to protect your new instrument from being copied by competitors?

choices.text: Keep the construction details a closely guarded trade secret
Publish the design freely to build his reputation as an inventor
Sell the design outright to a large instrument manufacturer
File a formal patent to legally protect the design

evt-06-28-1846-adolphe-sax.butterflyEffect: Sax secured a patent on 28 June 1846, giving him exclusive rights to manufacture the saxophone for years. When the patent expired in 1866, other makers flooded the market, but by then the instrument had already spread into military bands and, decades later, into jazz, becoming one of the most recognizable instruments in modern music.

evt-06-28-1880-cultural-icon.scenario: You are a Victoria police trooper at dawn on 28 June 1880, surrounding the Glenrowan Inn where bushranger Ned Kelly and his gang have holed up after weeks on the run.
evt-06-28-1880-cultural-icon.prompt: What extraordinary sight confronts you as Kelly walks out to fight in the morning mist?

choices.text: Kelly gallops through the police cordon on horseback
Kelly advances wearing homemade iron armour
Kelly surrenders unarmed at once
Kelly sets the inn alight and flees through a tunnel

evt-06-28-1880-cultural-icon.butterflyEffect: Police found Kelly's legs unprotected beneath his crude iron armour and shot him down, capturing him alive while the rest of his gang died in the siege. Tried and hanged that November, his defiant last stand at Glenrowan turned him into an enduring folk hero and a lasting symbol of resistance in Australian culture.

evt-06-28-1895-united-states-court-of-pr.scenario: It is 1895, and you are a settler in Arizona Territory whose homestead sits inside the vast tract claimed by James Reavis, self-styled 'Baron of Arizona,' who insists a Spanish land grant gives him title to 18,600 square miles.
evt-06-28-1895-united-states-court-of-pr.prompt: What does the U.S. Court of Private Land Claims rule on Reavis's massive claim?

choices.text: The court declares the land grant a fraud and voids Reavis's claim
The court refers the case to Congress for a special land treaty
The court upholds the grant and orders settlers to pay Reavis rent
The court splits the territory between Reavis and the federal government

evt-06-28-1895-united-states-court-of-pr.butterflyEffect: The court found Reavis's land grant to be an elaborate forgery, and he was later convicted of fraud and imprisoned. The ruling protected thousands of settlers' titles across Arizona and New Mexico and stands as one of the most audacious land fraud schemes in American history.

evt-06-28-1904-ss-norge.scenario: It is before dawn on 28 June 1904. Your ship, the emigrant liner SS Norge, has just struck a submerged rock near the remote islet of Rockall and is taking on water fast, with far too few lifeboats for everyone aboard.
evt-06-28-1904-ss-norge.prompt: As a crew member, what is the best immediate action to save the most lives?

choices.text: Immediately organize passengers into the few lifeboats available, launching them without delay
Wait for a passing ship before risking any lifeboat launch
Order everyone to remain calm below decks until the crew assesses the damage fully
Try to sail the ship to the nearest port before abandoning it

evt-06-28-1904-ss-norge.butterflyEffect: Chaotic, ill-organized evacuation meant more than 600 people died, mostly Scandinavian emigrants bound for new lives in America. The disaster remains the deadliest ever involving a Danish merchant ship and spurred later calls for stricter lifeboat capacity rules, debates revisited after the Titanic sank eight years later.

evt-06-28-1911-nakhla-meteorite.scenario: It is mid-morning on 28 June 1911 near Nakhla, Egypt, and you watch a fireball burst overhead, scattering roughly forty stones across the fields as startled villagers rush out to see what has fallen.
evt-06-28-1911-nakhla-meteorite.prompt: What do local witnesses claim happened as the fragments rained down?

choices.text: The stones are found glowing red hot, scorching the sand around them
The stones ignite a fire that burns down several homes
A camel caravan is reported buried under the falling debris
A dog is said to have been struck and killed by one of the falling stones

evt-06-28-1911-nakhla-meteorite.butterflyEffect: Villagers reported that a dog was struck and killed by one of the falling fragments, making it one of the only claimed meteorite fatalities on record, though the story cannot be fully verified. Decades later, analysis of Nakhla's minerals revealed signs of ancient water alteration, making it a key piece of evidence for past water on Mars.

evt-06-28-1914-assassination-of-archduke.scenario: It is 28 June 1914 in Sarajevo. Archduke Franz Ferdinand's driver has taken a wrong turn onto Franz Joseph Street and stalls the car while reversing, stopping just feet from a young Bosnian Serb nationalist who has been waiting all morning with a pistol.
evt-06-28-1914-assassination-of-archduke.prompt: What does Gavrilo Princip do in this sudden opportunity?

choices.text: He only manages to wound the archduke's driver
He loses his nerve and slips back into the crowd
He throws a bomb that misses the car entirely
He shoots Franz Ferdinand and Sophie at close range

evt-06-28-1914-assassination-of-archduke.butterflyEffect: Princip shot and killed both Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie at close range. The assassination triggered the July Crisis, Austria-Hungary's declaration of war on Serbia, and within weeks the alliance system pulled the great powers of Europe into the First World War.

evt-06-28-1916-world-war-i.scenario: You are a Berlin munitions worker on 28 June 1916, joining tens of thousands walking out of the factories in anger over the harsh sentencing of a well-known antiwar Reichstag deputy.
evt-06-28-1916-world-war-i.prompt: Whose imprisonment for opposing the war sparks this mass strike?

choices.text: Karl Liebknecht's
Philipp Scheidemann's
Friedrich Ebert's
Rosa Luxemburg's

evt-06-28-1916-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The strike protested Karl Liebknecht's imprisonment following his May Day antiwar demonstration and treason conviction, one of the first major displays of German working-class opposition to the war effort. Such wartime unrest grew steadily and helped set the stage for the revolution of November 1918 that ended the war and toppled the Kaiser.

evt-06-28-1919-treaty-of-versailles.scenario: It is 28 June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles. German delegates, barred from the negotiations that produced it, are handed a treaty demanding disarmament, territorial losses, and acceptance of sole responsibility for the war.
evt-06-28-1919-treaty-of-versailles.prompt: What do the German representatives ultimately do?

choices.text: They walk out and resume fighting
They sign the treaty as presented
They successfully negotiate softer terms
They appeal directly to the League of Nations

evt-06-28-1919-treaty-of-versailles.butterflyEffect: Facing renewed Allied invasion and blockade, Germany signed the treaty under protest. The harsh reparations and the 'War Guilt' clause bred lasting resentment that nationalist movements, including the Nazis, later exploited, helping set the stage for the Second World War.

evt-06-28-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: You are a German staff officer on 28 June 1942 as Wehrmacht divisions surge across the southern Soviet steppe in Case Blue, the great summer offensive.
evt-06-28-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What strategic prize does Hitler set as the offensive's ultimate goal?

choices.text: Break the siege of Leningrad
Capture Moscow before the onset of winter
Seize the Caucasus oil fields and reach the Volga at Stalingrad
Push through Persia toward the Middle East

evt-06-28-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Case Blue split into thrusts toward the Caucasus oil fields and toward Stalingrad on the Volga, overextending German forces across a vast front. The advance culminated in the catastrophic Battle of Stalingrad, whose Soviet victory that winter became the turning point of the war in the East.

evt-06-28-1950-korean-war.scenario: It is late June 1950 and you are a South Korean police official as North Korean forces push south. Orders arrive concerning the thousands of registered members of the Bodo League, a state 're-education' program for former leftists.
evt-06-28-1950-korean-war.prompt: What order do South Korean authorities carry out against the detained Bodo League members?

choices.text: They transfer detainees to United Nations-run refugee camps
They release all detainees and evacuate them south with the army
They conscript the detainees directly into the South Korean army
They execute detained Bodo League members en masse without trial

evt-06-28-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: Tens of thousands of Bodo League members and suspected leftists were executed without trial in the war's opening weeks, one of the conflict's least acknowledged mass killings. The massacre remained suppressed under South Korea's anti-communist governments for decades until a truth commission formally investigated it in the 2000s.

evt-06-28-1956-1956-poznan-protests.scenario: It is 28 June 1956, and you are a worker at Poznań's Cegielski Factories, marching with thousands of colleagues through the city center demanding bread, better wages, and freedom from Communist rule.
evt-06-28-1956-1956-poznan-protests.prompt: What follows as the peaceful strike turns into a citywide uprising?

choices.text: Government tanks and troops open fire, killing dozens of protesters
Local police negotiate a wage increase and marchers disperse peacefully
Soviet paratroopers occupy the city and the mayor resigns
The march is ignored by authorities and dissolves quietly by evening

evt-06-28-1956-1956-poznan-protests.butterflyEffect: Polish army units and tanks crushed the revolt, killing at least 57 people and wounding hundreds. The shock forced the Communist Party to install reformist Władysław Gomułka that October, easing repression, and Poznań became a touchstone for later uprisings in 1970 and 1980 that fed into Solidarity.

evt-06-28-1963-profumo-affair.scenario: You are a reporter outside the Old Bailey in the summer of 1963, following the trial of osteopath Stephen Ward, the man who introduced Christine Keeler to War Minister John Profumo.
evt-06-28-1963-profumo-affair.prompt: What happens to Ward as the case against him reaches its conclusion?

choices.text: He is acquitted and returns to his practice
He flees to the Continent before sentencing
He is sentenced to many years of hard labour
He takes a fatal overdose before the verdict is delivered

evt-06-28-1963-profumo-affair.butterflyEffect: Ward took a fatal overdose of barbiturates before the jury returned its verdict and died days later; he was found guilty in his absence on charges of living off immoral earnings. His death fueled public suspicion that he had been made a scapegoat, deepening the scandal that forced Harold Macmillan's resignation as Prime Minister that October.

evt-06-28-1969-stonewall-inn.scenario: It is the early hours of 28 June 1969, and NYPD officers are raiding the Stonewall Inn in Greenwich Village, roughly detaining patrons as a crowd of onlookers gathers on Christopher Street outside.
evt-06-28-1969-stonewall-inn.prompt: How do the patrons and bystanders respond to the raid?

choices.text: They resist and riot against the police
They negotiate a settlement with officers on scene
They quietly disperse as ordered
They file formal complaints the next day instead

evt-06-28-1969-stonewall-inn.butterflyEffect: Rather than dispersing, the crowd fought back, and rioting continued outside the bar for several nights. The Stonewall uprising galvanized the modern gay liberation movement, leading to the first Pride marches a year later and lasting momentum for LGBTQ rights in America.

evt-06-28-1989-slobodan-milosevic.scenario: It is 28 June 1989, the 600th anniversary of the Battle of Kosovo, and you stand among hundreds of thousands gathered at Gazimestan to hear Serbian President Slobodan Milošević address the crowd.
evt-06-28-1989-slobodan-milosevic.prompt: What does Milošević's speech signal about his approach to Serbian nationalism and Kosovo?

choices.text: He proposes a federal power-sharing agreement with Croatia and Slovenia
He announces Serbia's full withdrawal from Kosovo
He calls for greater autonomy and rights for Kosovo's Albanian majority
He warns that Serbs must be prepared to fight again, fueling nationalist mobilization

evt-06-28-1989-slobodan-milosevic.butterflyEffect: The speech is widely regarded as a turning point that legitimized aggressive Serbian nationalism at a moment of rising ethnic tension. It helped set the tone for the Yugoslav Wars of the 1990s, and Milošević would later become the first sitting head of state charged with war crimes and genocide.

evt-06-28-2004-iraq-war.scenario: You are a Coalition official in Baghdad's Green Zone on 28 June 2004, moving the ceremony to transfer sovereignty two days earlier than planned to reduce the risk of an insurgent attack.
evt-06-28-2004-iraq-war.prompt: How does administrator Paul Bremer handle the handover of power?

choices.text: Hold the handover secretly and depart immediately after
Announce the ceremony publicly well in advance
Broadcast the ceremony live on international television
Delay the transfer until security improves

evt-06-28-2004-iraq-war.butterflyEffect: Bremer signed the transfer documents in a brief, unannounced ceremony and left Iraq within hours, ending the Coalition Provisional Authority ahead of schedule. Sovereignty passed to interim Prime Minister Iyad Allawi, though US troops remained, and the insurgency that followed continued for years despite the formal end of occupation.

evt-06-28-2009-honduras.scenario: It is dawn on 28 June 2009 in Tegucigalpa. You are a Honduran soldier sent to the presidential residence, under orders from military commanders backed by the Supreme Court, to remove President Manuel Zelaya after his push for a referendum on constitutional reform.
evt-06-28-2009-honduras.prompt: What do you do with the president once you reach his residence?

choices.text: Escort him safely to the National Congress for a vote
Place him under house arrest inside the presidential residence
Refuse the order and defend the sitting president
Arrest him and fly him out of the country to Costa Rica

evt-06-28-2009-honduras.butterflyEffect: Soldiers seized Zelaya in his pajamas and flew him into exile in Costa Rica, triggering international condemnation and Honduras's suspension from the Organization of American States. The crisis deepened political polarization for years and became a flashpoint in later disputes over democratic backsliding across Central America.

evt-06-28-2012-supreme-court-of-the-unit.scenario: It is 28 June 2012, and the Supreme Court is about to announce its ruling on the Affordable Care Act's individual mandate, with Chief Justice Roberts holding the deciding vote in a closely watched case.
evt-06-28-2012-supreme-court-of-the-unit.prompt: On what basis does the Court's majority opinion uphold the individual mandate?

choices.text: As a valid exercise of Congress's taxing power
As a valid exercise of the Commerce Clause
As authorized under the Necessary and Proper Clause alone
The majority strikes down the mandate entirely

evt-06-28-2012-supreme-court-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: Roberts joined the Court's liberal justices to uphold the mandate as a valid exercise of Congress's taxing power, while rejecting it under the Commerce Clause. The ruling preserved Obama's signature healthcare law and reshaped later legal battles over federal power and healthcare policy.

evt-06-28-2016-2016-ataturk-airport-atta.scenario: It is the evening of 28 June 2016. You are a security officer at the international terminal of Istanbul's Atatürk Airport when gunmen wearing explosive vests open fire near the entrance, sending travelers fleeing in panic.
evt-06-28-2016-2016-ataturk-airport-atta.prompt: What is the most effective way to stop the attackers before they reach the crowded terminal?

choices.text: Evacuate everyone through the nearest exits without confronting the gunmen
Lock down all terminal doors and wait for backup to arrive
Negotiate with the attackers to prevent detonation
Engage and fire on the attackers before they can advance further into the terminal

evt-06-28-2016-2016-ataturk-airport-atta.butterflyEffect: Police fired on the gunmen, and at least one attacker detonated his suicide vest at a security checkpoint rather than penetrating further inside. Three attackers and forty-five others were killed; the attack, widely attributed to ISIL though never claimed, led Turkey to tighten airport security and reinforced its resolve against the group's presence near its borders.

evt-06-29-1613-globe-theatre.scenario: It's June 29, 1613, and you're in the packed galleries of the Globe watching Shakespeare's new play Henry VIII. A stage cannon fires to salute the king's entrance, and sparks catch in the thatched roof above you.

choices.text: The audience riots, blaming the actors for the mishap
The play continues uninterrupted while stagehands quietly extinguish the blaze
The thatch roof catches fully and the entire theatre burns to the ground within an hour
The fire is doused quickly by attendants with buckets, no real damage done

evt-06-29-1613-globe-theatre.butterflyEffect: The Globe burned to the ground in under an hour; remarkably, the only recorded injury was a man whose breeches caught fire, put out with a bottle of ale. Shakespeare's company rebuilt it with a tiled roof by June 1614, and the new Globe operated until Puritan authorities closed London's theatres in 1642.

evt-06-29-1864-swing-bridge.scenario: It is just after midnight on 29 June 1864. Your train, crowded with German immigrant families bound for Quebec City, races through the darkness toward a swing bridge over the Richelieu River near Beloeil. The bridge has been swung open to let river traffic pass, and the signal ahead is faint.
evt-06-29-1864-swing-bridge.prompt: As engineer, what is the safe response to an unclear signal at the swing bridge?

choices.text: Proceed at reduced speed, trusting the printed timetable that the bridge should be closed
Stop the train immediately until the bridge's position is visually confirmed
Sound the whistle and continue, assuming river traffic has already cleared
Send the brakeman to inspect the bridge while the train keeps moving

evt-06-29-1864-swing-bridge.butterflyEffect: The train failed to stop in time and plunged into the river, killing roughly 99 people—the worst railway disaster in Canadian history to that date. The tragedy forced railways across North America to adopt stricter interlocking and signalling rules for movable bridges, so operators could never again rely on a dim lantern to confirm a bridge was closed.

evt-06-29-1889-hyde-park-township-illino.scenario: It is June 29, 1889, and you own a modest home in Hyde Park Township, just south of Chicago. A ballot question asks whether your township, along with Lake View, Jefferson, and Lake, should be absorbed into the city of Chicago.
evt-06-29-1889-hyde-park-township-illino.prompt: How did Hyde Park and its neighboring townships vote on the annexation referendum?

choices.text: They overwhelmingly voted yes, joining Chicago
They rejected annexation to preserve local self-rule
They voted to annex Chicago instead
The vote was postponed indefinitely by court injunction

evt-06-29-1889-hyde-park-township-illino.butterflyEffect: Voters approved annexation by a wide margin, and Chicago's area and population more than tripled overnight in one of the largest municipal annexations in American history. The newly absorbed South Side land, including Hyde Park's Jackson Park, became the site of the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition just four years later.

evt-06-29-1913-union-army.scenario: It is 3 July 1913, fifty years after the battle. You are an elderly Union veteran standing at the stone wall on Cemetery Ridge, and across the field a line of aging Confederate veterans begins the long walk toward you, retracing Pickett's Charge.
evt-06-29-1913-union-army.prompt: What do the veterans do when the two lines finally meet at the wall?

choices.text: They hold separate ceremonies on opposite sides of the field
They shake hands and embrace across the stone wall
They stage a mock battle using blank cartridges
They refuse to approach the wall out of lingering bitterness

evt-06-29-1913-union-army.butterflyEffect: Instead of clashing, the old soldiers embraced and shook hands across the wall, a staged reenactment that became one of the era's most famous images of North-South reconciliation. Later historians criticized the reunion for celebrating white veterans' friendship while ignoring slavery and the exclusion of Black soldiers from the ceremony.

evt-06-29-1927-united-states-army-air-co.scenario: It's June 29, 1927, and you're aboard the Fokker C-2 Bird of Paradise, somewhere over open Pacific water with no visible landmarks. Your only guide to Hawaii is radio direction-finding equipment and dead reckoning.
evt-06-29-1927-united-states-army-air-co.prompt: What happens as you near the end of the flight?

choices.text: You run out of fuel and are forced to ditch near the islands
You are intercepted and escorted in by Navy ships
Poor radio signals force you to turn back to California
You successfully land at Wheeler Field, completing the first transpacific flight to Hawaii

evt-06-29-1927-united-states-army-air-co.butterflyEffect: Lieutenants Lester Maitland and Albert Hegenberger landed safely at Wheeler Field after a 25-hour flight from Oakland, proving long-range aerial navigation over open ocean was possible. Their radio-beacon navigation technique became a model for later transpacific routes, helping justify Hawaii's growing strategic importance to American air power.

evt-06-29-1950-united-states-men-s-natio.scenario: It is 29 June 1950 in Belo Horizonte, Brazil. You are an amateur American player, most of your teammates dockworkers, mailmen, and students, about to kick off against England, the reigning kings of world football.
evt-06-29-1950-united-states-men-s-natio.prompt: What is the final result of this World Cup match?

choices.text: The match ends in a 1–1 draw
The United States wins 1–0
The game is abandoned due to a pitch invasion
England wins 3–0 as expected

evt-06-29-1950-united-states-men-s-natio.butterflyEffect: The United States won 1–0 on a goal by Joe Gaetjens, one of the greatest upsets in World Cup history, later dubbed the 'Miracle on Grass.' English newspapers reportedly assumed the wire-service score was a typo for 10–1. The result was largely forgotten in the US for decades until the sport's later growth revived interest in it.

evt-06-29-1967-jayne-mansfield.scenario: In the early hours of 29 June 1967, you are driving on a Louisiana highway still hazy with insecticide fog from a mosquito-spraying truck. Ahead, a car carrying actress Jayne Mansfield closes rapidly on a slow-moving tractor-trailer that has stopped in the roadway.
evt-06-29-1967-jayne-mansfield.prompt: What safety feature later became mandatory on trailers because of this crash?

choices.text: Rear underride guards to stop cars sliding beneath trailers
Reflective mud flaps on all trailers
Automatic headlight dimmers for oncoming traffic
Mandatory anti-lock brakes on passenger cars

evt-06-29-1967-jayne-mansfield.butterflyEffect: Mansfield's car struck the underside of the trailer, killing her, her boyfriend Sam Brody, and the driver; her children in the back seat survived. The horrific underride crash spurred decades of advocacy for rear guards on trucks, eventually leading regulators to mandate them—devices still informally called 'Mansfield bars.'

evt-06-29-1971-soyuz-11.scenario: It's June 29, 1971, and you are one of three cosmonauts preparing your Soyuz 11 capsule for re-entry after three weeks aboard Salyut 1. As you undock and begin the descent sequence, a pressure equalization valve opens early.
evt-06-29-1971-soyuz-11.prompt: What happens to the crew during re-entry?

choices.text: They eject in emergency capsules and parachute to safety
The cabin depressurizes and all three cosmonauts die before landing
They seal the valve manually and land safely
Ground control aborts re-entry and they return to the station

evt-06-29-1971-soyuz-11.butterflyEffect: Georgy Dobrovolsky, Vladislav Volkov, and Viktor Patsayev died from asphyxiation when the capsule lost pressure; they remain the only humans known to have died in space. The Soviet space program grounded Soyuz for over two years, redesigned the capsule for two crew members instead of three, and made wearing pressure suits during launch and re-entry mandatory.

evt-06-29-1975-pope-paul-vi.scenario: You kneel among 350 seminarians in St. Peter's Square on June 29, 1975, waiting for Pope Paul VI to ordain you during Rome's great Jubilee year, which has drawn pilgrims from across the world.
evt-06-29-1975-pope-paul-vi.prompt: What occasion made this unusually large ordination possible in 1975?

choices.text: The 1975 Holy Year jubilee celebrations in Rome
The canonization of a newly named saint
The dedication of a rebuilt St. Peter's Basilica facade
The tenth anniversary of Vatican II's closing session

evt-06-29-1975-pope-paul-vi.butterflyEffect: The ordination coincided with the 1975 Holy Year, one of the largest jubilee pilgrimages of Paul VI's pontificate, which drew huge crowds to Rome a decade after Vatican II. The event signaled renewed institutional confidence in the post-conciliar Church and foreshadowed the massive papal gatherings later staged under John Paul II.

evt-06-29-1976-seychelles.scenario: It's June 29, 1976, and you stand in Victoria's central square as the Union Jack is lowered for the last time. James Mancham has just been sworn in as the Seychelles' first president.
evt-06-29-1976-seychelles.prompt: What happens to Mancham's government within the next year?

choices.text: He is overthrown in a coup while abroad, and one-party rule follows
He voluntarily hands power to a UN-appointed transitional council
He wins a landslide re-election and stays in power for two decades
He negotiates a return to British protectorate status

evt-06-29-1976-seychelles.butterflyEffect: In June 1977, while Mancham was in London for a Commonwealth conference, his prime minister France-Albert René seized power in a coup backed by Tanzanian-trained fighters. René's Seychelles People's Progressive Front ruled as a one-party socialist state until multiparty elections were restored in 1993.

evt-06-29-1995-space-shuttle-atlantis.scenario: You are part of the STS-71 crew aboard Atlantis on 29 June 1995, moments after hard-docking with Mir, preparing to open the hatch between the two craft for the first time.
evt-06-29-1995-space-shuttle-atlantis.prompt: What major exchange does this mission accomplish once the hatch opens?

choices.text: The first transfer of a satellite between spacecraft
The first exchange of resident space station crew members between nations
The first refueling of a station's propulsion system
The first live television broadcast from orbit

evt-06-29-1995-space-shuttle-atlantis.butterflyEffect: STS-71 carried out the first on-orbit exchange of a space station crew between two nations, replacing Mir's resident cosmonauts with a fresh team via the Shuttle. This crew-rotation model became a template for how the later International Space Station would be staffed by rotating international crews.

evt-06-29-1995-space-shuttle-program.scenario: It is 29 June 1995 and you are aboard Space Shuttle Atlantis, closing the final meters toward the Russian space station Mir high above the Earth.
evt-06-29-1995-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What historic first does today's docking achieve for the Shuttle program?

choices.text: The first uncrewed Shuttle mission
The first Shuttle launch of a foreign-built module
The first American docking with a foreign space station
The first American spacewalk in orbit

evt-06-29-1995-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: Atlantis became the first American spacecraft to dock with Mir, launching the Shuttle–Mir Program, a joint venture born from the end of the Cold War space race. The cooperation built the technical and diplomatic foundation later used to construct and operate the International Space Station.

evt-06-29-1995-sampoong-department-store.scenario: It is the morning of June 29, 1995, in Seocho District, Seoul. Engineers have just told Sampoong Department Store's management that cracks are spreading through the fifth-floor ceiling and the building may be unsafe.
evt-06-29-1995-sampoong-department-store.prompt: What did the store's management actually do after receiving these warnings?

choices.text: They called in structural engineers to reinforce the building on the spot
They evacuated all customers and closed the store immediately
They notified city officials and requested a safety inspection first
They kept the store open and continued business as usual

evt-06-29-1995-sampoong-department-store.butterflyEffect: Management kept the store open to avoid losing a day's revenue, and hours later the structure gave way, killing 502 people and injuring 937 in South Korea's deadliest peacetime disaster. The catastrophe, caused by illegal design changes and added floors, forced sweeping reforms of Korean building codes and led to prison sentences for the store's executives.

evt-06-29-2002-battle-of-yeonpyeong-2002.scenario: It is 29 June 2002 and you command a South Korean patrol boat near Yeonpyeong Island as North Korean vessels cross the disputed maritime border and open fire without warning.
evt-06-29-2002-battle-of-yeonpyeong-2002.prompt: Under standing rules of engagement, what does your boat do in response?

choices.text: Attempt radio negotiation before any action
Return fire in self-defense per standing orders
Ram the North Korean vessel to force it back
Withdraw immediately without engaging

evt-06-29-2002-battle-of-yeonpyeong-2002.butterflyEffect: South Korean patrol boats returned fire, and North Korean boats withdrew before reinforcements arrived, but not before South Korean sailors were killed. The clash came days after South Korea's celebrated co-hosting of the World Cup, straining inter-Korean relations and reminding both nations that the Yellow Sea border remained a live flashpoint.

evt-06-29-2003-2003-chicago-balcony-coll.scenario: It is the night of June 29, 2003, and you are among dozens of guests packed onto a wooden back porch during a party at a Chicago apartment building. The structure begins to groan and sway under the crowd's weight.
evt-06-29-2003-2003-chicago-balcony-coll.prompt: What should the partygoers have done as the porch began to sway?

choices.text: Ask more guests to join to balance the weight evenly
Move everyone toward the railing for a better view
Evacuate the porch immediately and move guests indoors
Continue the party since old porches often creak

evt-06-29-2003-2003-chicago-balcony-coll.butterflyEffect: The overloaded porch collapsed, killing thirteen people and injuring fifty-seven in the deadliest porch collapse in U.S. history. The disaster pushed Chicago to tighten enforcement of porch construction and occupancy codes across the city's dense residential neighborhoods.

evt-06-29-2007-apple-inc.scenario: It is the morning of 29 June 2007 and you have camped outside an Apple Store for hours, waiting for the doors to open on a device Steve Jobs has spent months hyping as reinventing the phone.
evt-06-29-2007-apple-inc.prompt: What device are you lining up to buy today?

choices.text: The iPod Touch
The first iPhone
The first iPad
The MacBook Air

evt-06-29-2007-apple-inc.butterflyEffect: The original iPhone went on sale, combining a phone, iPod, and internet device into one touchscreen product exclusive to AT&T in the US. Its success pushed Apple to pivot from a computer company into the world's dominant smartphone maker, and the 2008 App Store it enabled reshaped software distribution industry-wide.

evt-06-29-2012-derecho.scenario: It is a scorching evening on 29 June 2012, and you are outside in the Washington–Baltimore area when the sky suddenly turns black. A wall of wind and dust races toward you far faster than any storm you've seen, with no tornado siren sounding.
evt-06-29-2012-derecho.prompt: What should you do as the derecho's leading edge bears down?

choices.text: Keep working outside since it's likely just a passing shower
Drive quickly to try to outrun the storm front
Take shelter immediately away from windows and trees
Open all the windows to equalize pressure in the house

evt-06-29-2012-derecho.butterflyEffect: The derecho tore across the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic with gusts over 80 mph, toppling trees onto power lines and killing dozens. Roughly four million homes lost power during a brutal heat wave, exposing how vulnerable the electrical grid was to sudden, fast-moving windstorms and prompting utilities to review tree-trimming and grid-hardening practices.

evt-06-29-2014-islamic-state.scenario: It's June 29, 2014, and ISIL fighters control swathes of Iraq and Syria. From Mosul, a spokesman makes an announcement that will change the group's name and ambitions.

choices.text: A worldwide caliphate, renaming itself simply 'Islamic State'
Dissolution of the organization in favor of local militias
A ceasefire with the Iraqi government
Formal alliance with al-Qaeda's central leadership

evt-06-29-2014-islamic-state.butterflyEffect: The group declared Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi caliph and demanded allegiance from Muslims worldwide, a claim rejected by nearly all Muslim authorities. The declaration triggered a US-led international coalition's bombing campaign and years of urban warfare that eventually destroyed the physical 'caliphate' by 2019, though the group's ideology continued inspiring attacks globally.

evt-06-30-1398-ming-dynasty.scenario: It is 1398, and the Hongwu Emperor has just died. As his grandson Zhu Yunwen, you inherit the Ming throne over the heads of your uncles, several of whom command their own private armies as regional princes.
evt-06-30-1398-ming-dynasty.prompt: What should you do about your powerful uncles before they threaten your rule?

choices.text: Exile your uncles to distant frontier provinces immediately
Appoint all your uncles as senior ministers in the capital
Ignore the uncles and focus on civil administration
Begin stripping the princely uncles of their military authority

evt-06-30-1398-ming-dynasty.butterflyEffect: The Jianwen Emperor moved to strip his uncles of military power, provoking his uncle Zhu Di to launch the Jingnan Rebellion. By 1402 Zhu Di had seized the throne as the Yongle Emperor, later moving the capital to Beijing and building the Forbidden City, reshaping Ming China for centuries.

evt-06-30-1559-jousting.scenario: It is 30 June 1559, in Paris, and you watch King Henry II joust against Gabriel de Montgomery, captain of the Scottish Guard, during celebrations for the Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis. After their first pass shatters both lances, the king insists on riding a second course despite Montgomery's reluctance.
evt-06-30-1559-jousting.prompt: What happens when the two horsemen collide on the second pass?

choices.text: The king is unhorsed but rises unharmed, laughing off the fall
Montgomery's lance shatters, driving splinters through the king's open visor into his eye
Montgomery is thrown from his horse and badly injured instead
Both riders miss entirely and the joust ends without incident

evt-06-30-1559-jousting.butterflyEffect: Montgomery's shattered lance drove splinters through the king's raised visor into his eye and brain; Henry II died ten days later. His death brought his young sons Francis II, Charles IX, and eventually Henry III to the throne in quick succession, with his widow Catherine de' Medici wielding enormous power as regent, and jousting swiftly fell from favor at the French court.

evt-06-30-1598-anglo-spanish-war-1585-16.scenario: You serve under George Clifford, Earl of Cumberland, as his English fleet finally forces the Spanish garrison of San Juan to surrender after a fifteen-day siege in June 1598.
evt-06-30-1598-anglo-spanish-war-1585-16.prompt: With the city taken but dysentery spreading through your ranks, what should the fleet do next?

choices.text: Garrison the city permanently as a new English colony
Loot what you can and withdraw quickly before disease destroys the force
Ransom the city back to Spain for a large payment
Burn the city completely before leaving

evt-06-30-1598-anglo-spanish-war-1585-16.butterflyEffect: Disease devastated Cumberland's men within weeks, forcing the English to abandon San Juan and sail home with what plunder they could carry rather than hold the island. Spain kept Puerto Rico and strengthened its fortifications, which helped repel later attacks on the port for decades.

evt-06-30-1859-charles-blondin.scenario: You stand among the crowd at Niagara Gorge on 30 June 1859, watching French acrobat Charles Blondin step onto a rope strung high above the rapids for his very first crossing.
evt-06-30-1859-charles-blondin.prompt: What does Blondin do on this first crossing to astonish the crowd?

choices.text: Stops midway to cook and eat an omelette
Walks straight across using only a long balancing pole
Carries his manager on his back the whole way
Pushes a wheelbarrow across the entire rope

evt-06-30-1859-charles-blondin.butterflyEffect: Blondin simply walked the rope with a balancing pole and made it across safely, instantly becoming an international celebrity. Emboldened by the acclaim, he returned throughout the summer to perform ever riskier stunts over the gorge, including crossing blindfolded and carrying his manager on his back.

evt-06-30-1894-tower-bridge.scenario: It is 30 June 1894, and you are an engineer making final checks before London's new bridge over the Thames opens to the public, needing to let tall-masted ships pass beneath while carrying road traffic above.
evt-06-30-1894-tower-bridge.prompt: What mechanism must you ensure works to solve this problem?

choices.text: The hydraulic bascule mechanism that raises the road sections
A retractable pontoon that sinks beneath passing vessels
A permanently fixed high arch too tall for any ship to need clearance
A swing span that rotates the entire bridge horizontally

evt-06-30-1894-tower-bridge.butterflyEffect: The bridge's twin bascules could be raised hydraulically to let ships through the Pool of London, while high-level walkways let pedestrians cross even when the road was lifted. The design became one of London's most recognisable landmarks and a lasting symbol of Victorian engineering ambition.

evt-06-30-1960-belgian-congo.scenario: It is 30 June 1960 in Léopoldville. King Baudouin of Belgium has just addressed the independence ceremony, praising the achievements of colonial rule. As Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba, you were not originally scheduled to speak.
evt-06-30-1960-belgian-congo.prompt: What do you do in response to the king's speech?

choices.text: Walk out of the ceremony in protest without speaking
Stay silent and let the ceremony proceed as planned
Give an unscheduled speech denouncing the abuses of colonial rule
Publicly thank Belgium for a smooth transition to independence

evt-06-30-1960-belgian-congo.butterflyEffect: Lumumba rose to deliver an unscheduled, fiery speech denouncing decades of Belgian colonial abuse, shocking the Belgian delegation. The confrontation deepened tensions between Congo's new government and Belgium, fueling the chaos of the Congo Crisis that led to Lumumba's assassination within a year.

evt-06-30-1963-coronation-of-pope-paul-v.scenario: It is 30 June 1963 in St Peter's Square. You watch as Paul VI, elected just nine days earlier, is crowned with a jewelled papal tiara before representatives of over ninety nations, continuing a centuries-old tradition.
evt-06-30-1963-coronation-of-pope-paul-v.prompt: What did Paul VI later do with this tiara, and what did it foreshadow?

choices.text: He kept the tiara in permanent private display at the Vatican Museums
He commissioned an even heavier, more ornate tiara for future ceremonies
He gave up the tiara for charity, and future popes dropped coronations altogether
He established a joint coronation ritual shared with the Orthodox Patriarch

evt-06-30-1963-coronation-of-pope-paul-v.butterflyEffect: Paul VI later renounced the tiara, having it sold with proceeds given to the poor; it now resides in the Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception in Washington, D.C. His successors, beginning with John Paul I, abandoned the coronation ceremony entirely in favor of simpler inauguration Masses, ending centuries of papal coronation tradition.

evt-06-30-1985-ryan-white.scenario: It is early 1985 in Kokomo, Indiana, and you sit on the local school board. Thirteen-year-old Ryan White, diagnosed with AIDS after a contaminated blood treatment for hemophilia, wants to return to his classroom, but parents and teachers are terrified of contagion.
evt-06-30-1985-ryan-white.prompt: What does the school board decide about Ryan's return to class?

choices.text: Welcome him back immediately with full support from parents
Offer him a scholarship to a private school out of state
Let his family choose homeschooling with no board involvement
Bar him from attending regular classes, citing fear of contagion

evt-06-30-1985-ryan-white.butterflyEffect: The board barred Ryan from attending regular classes, and his family's legal fight to overturn that decision drew national media attention, making him a symbol of AIDS education and anti-discrimination efforts. After his death in 1990, Congress passed the Ryan White CARE Act, which remains the largest federally funded program for HIV/AIDS care in the United States.

evt-06-30-2007-jeep-cherokee.scenario: It is 30 June 2007 and a burning Jeep Cherokee packed with propane canisters has just rammed the terminal doors at Glasgow Airport. The driver, engulfed in flames, staggers out and lunges at bystanders.
evt-06-30-2007-jeep-cherokee.prompt: What do the airport staff and onlookers nearby do in response?

choices.text: Flee the terminal immediately without intervening
Attempt to negotiate with the attacker from a distance
Tackle and restrain the attacker despite the flames
Wait for armed police before doing anything

evt-06-30-2007-jeep-cherokee.butterflyEffect: Baggage handler John Smeaton and several bystanders tackled and restrained the burning attacker, preventing further harm, and Smeaton became a brief folk hero in the UK press. The attack raised Britain's terror threat level and prompted airports nationwide to strengthen vehicle barriers at terminal entrances.

evt-06-30-2009-yemenia-flight-626.scenario: It is the middle of the night on 30 June 2009. You are twelve-year-old Bahia Bakari, suddenly thrown into the dark, storm-tossed waters of the Indian Ocean as the Yemenia jet breaks apart around you, with pieces of wreckage scattered nearby.
evt-06-30-2009-yemenia-flight-626.prompt: What should you do to survive until rescuers can find you?

choices.text: Dive underwater to search for other survivors
Remove your clothing to swim faster
Cling tightly to a piece of floating wreckage and conserve energy
Swim as hard as possible toward where you think shore might be

evt-06-30-2009-yemenia-flight-626.butterflyEffect: Bakari clung to a floating piece of wreckage for over thirteen hours until fishermen rescued her, the sole survivor among 153 people aboard. Her survival made her an international symbol of resilience; she later wrote a memoir, and scrutiny of Yemenia's safety record intensified, contributing to the airline being barred from European Union airspace.

evt-06-30-2013-june-2013-egyptian-protes.scenario: It is 30 June 2013, the first anniversary of Mohamed Morsi's inauguration, and you stand in a packed Tahrir Square as millions answer the Tamarod petition's call, demanding the president's resignation.
evt-06-30-2013-june-2013-egyptian-protes.prompt: What happens in the days immediately following these mass protests?

choices.text: The military ousts Morsi and suspends the constitution
The protests dissipate without any change in government
The Muslim Brotherhood negotiates a lasting power-sharing deal
Morsi voluntarily resigns and calls new elections

evt-06-30-2013-june-2013-egyptian-protes.butterflyEffect: On 3 July, the military under General Abdel Fattah el-Sisi issued an ultimatum and then removed Morsi from power, suspending the constitution and installing a transitional government. Sisi later became president, the Muslim Brotherhood was banned and heavily suppressed, and Egypt's brief experiment with elected Islamist government came to an abrupt end.

evt-06-30-2019-donald-trump.scenario: You are part of the advance security team at Panmunjom on 30 June 2019, watching President Trump step toward the demarcation line to meet Kim Jong Un.
evt-06-30-2019-donald-trump.prompt: What historic first does this moment mark?

choices.text: The first US president ever to visit South Korea
The formal end of the Korean War armistice
The first ever summit between a US and North Korean leader
The first sitting US president to step onto North Korean territory

evt-06-30-2019-donald-trump.butterflyEffect: Trump became the first sitting US president to set foot on North Korean soil, a striking image that dominated headlines worldwide. Despite the symbolism, no substantive denuclearization agreement followed, and talks stalled later that year as North Korea resumed weapons testing.

evt-06-30-2020-2020-hong-kong-national-s.scenario: It is the night of 30 June 2020 and you lead a pro-democracy group in Hong Kong. Word arrives that Beijing's Standing Committee has just passed a sweeping national security law, effective at midnight.
evt-06-30-2020-2020-hong-kong-national-s.prompt: As the law takes effect, what should your group do to protect its members?

choices.text: Immediately flee to mainland China for safety
Announce the group's dissolution before the law can be used against it
Continue operating openly, betting on international pressure to block enforcement
Publicly burn symbols of Chinese authority in protest

evt-06-30-2020-2020-hong-kong-national-s.butterflyEffect: Within hours, prominent groups like Demosisto announced their dissolution to shield members from prosecution, and its co-founders soon fled abroad while others were later arrested. The law became the legal basis for dozens of sedition and secession charges, effectively ending the mass street protests that had defined Hong Kong since 2019.

evt-07-01-1523-jan-van-essen-and-hendrik.scenario: It is 1 July 1523 in Brussels. You are Hendrik Vos, an Augustinian monk condemned by the Council of Brabant for preaching Luther's doctrine, and the inquisitors offer you one last chance before the flames are lit.
evt-07-01-1523-jan-van-essen-and-hendrik.prompt: What does Vos choose in this final moment?

choices.text: Attempt to flee custody
Appeal directly to Emperor Charles V
Publicly recant his beliefs
Refuse to recant and accept death

evt-07-01-1523-jan-van-essen-and-hendrik.butterflyEffect: Vos and his fellow monk Jan van Essen refused to recant and were burned at the stake, becoming the first martyrs of the Lutheran Reformation. Luther himself commemorated their deaths in a hymn, and their execution helped galvanize Protestant sympathy across the Low Countries.

evt-07-01-1643-westminster-assembly.scenario: It is 1 July 1643 in the Jerusalem Chamber at Westminster, and you are one of the divines summoned by Parliament amid civil war to reshape the Church of England's governance. Bishops, Presbyterians, and Independents in the room all press for a different structure.
evt-07-01-1643-westminster-assembly.prompt: What form of church government does the Assembly ultimately draft?

choices.text: An Erastian church placed entirely under Parliament's direct control
Fully independent congregations, each governing itself with no central authority
A Presbyterian system of elected elders and regional assemblies
Retention of the existing episcopal hierarchy under bishops

evt-07-01-1643-westminster-assembly.butterflyEffect: The Assembly produced a Presbyterian Form of Church Government along with the Westminster Confession of Faith and two catechisms. Though England itself abandoned Presbyterianism after the Restoration, the Confession was adopted by the Church of Scotland and carried by Presbyterian and Reformed churches into New England and beyond, shaping English-speaking Protestant theology for centuries.

evt-07-01-1690-williamite.scenario: It is 1 July 1690, and you serve in King James II's Jacobite army as William III's Williamite forces force a crossing of the River Boyne near Drogheda, splitting your lines to meet a flanking column upstream.
evt-07-01-1690-williamite.prompt: What follows for King James II after this Williamite victory?

choices.text: James is captured on the battlefield
James flees to France
James rallies his troops and retakes Dublin
James negotiates a truce with William

evt-07-01-1690-williamite.butterflyEffect: James's army broke and he fled to France rather than regroup, ending any real hope of a Catholic Stuart restoration in Ireland. William's win secured the Protestant Ascendancy, and the battle remains commemorated annually by the Orange Order.

evt-07-01-1849-epaulettes-stamp.scenario: You run a shop in Brussels in 1849 and need to send a letter to Antwerp. The post office clerk shows you Belgium's brand-new adhesive stamps bearing King Leopold I's portrait.
evt-07-01-1849-epaulettes-stamp.prompt: What does buying and affixing this stamp yourself change about how the letter is paid for?

choices.text: The stamp only covers letters within Brussels, not to other cities
The stamp must be redeemed for cash rather than used for postage
The recipient in Antwerp will still be billed for the postage on delivery
You prepay the postage yourself, so the recipient owes nothing on delivery

evt-07-01-1849-epaulettes-stamp.butterflyEffect: The Epaulettes stamps let senders prepay postage instead of leaving recipients to pay on delivery, following Britain's 1840 reform. Mail volume in Belgium rose sharply as a result, and the design's success inspired later commemorative stamp series.

evt-07-01-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 1 July 1862 at Malvern Hill, Virginia. You are a Confederate officer under Robert E. Lee, ordered to send your men forward in yet another piecemeal assault against Union artillery massed on the high ground, the last of the Seven Days Battles.
evt-07-01-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: What was the result of Lee's disjointed, uncoordinated attacks on the Union position?

choices.text: McClellan surrendered his army on the field
Union artillery lines broke and Richmond's road lay open
Both sides withdrew without further fighting that day
Confederate assaults were repulsed with heavy casualties

evt-07-01-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Confederates suffered severe casualties in the repeated, poorly coordinated charges and were repulsed with heavy loss. Yet the battle still ended the Seven Days Battles, forcing General McClellan to abandon his advance and withdraw down the Peninsula, lifting the immediate threat to Richmond and freeing Lee to take the offensive northward later that summer.

evt-07-01-1874-sholes-and-glidden-typewr.scenario: It is 1874 and you are a clerk in New York eyeing E. Remington and Sons' newly perfected writing machine, refined from Christopher Latham Sholes' design after years of tinkering by Densmore and others.
evt-07-01-1874-sholes-and-glidden-typewr.prompt: What does Remington, an arms manufacturer, decide to do with this device?

choices.text: Keep it as an internal tool for drafting Remington's own business letters
Sell it commercially to offices and the public as a writing machine
License the design exclusively to the U.S. government for military use
Shelve the project after deciding it had no commercial value

evt-07-01-1874-sholes-and-glidden-typewr.butterflyEffect: Remington placed the machine on the open market as the first commercially successful typewriter, diversifying beyond weapons manufacturing. Its keyboard layout and mechanism set the template for office writing machines for the next century.

evt-07-01-1916-world-war-i.scenario: It is dawn on 1 July 1916 near Albert on the Somme. You are a British infantryman waiting for the whistle, ordered to advance across open ground toward the German lines after a week-long artillery bombardment.
evt-07-01-1916-world-war-i.prompt: What formation and pace are you ordered to advance in as you cross no man's land?

choices.text: Advance at a steady walk in evenly spaced lines
Sprint forward in short rushes between shell craters
Wait for tanks to breach the wire before moving at all
Crawl forward under cover of darkness only

evt-07-01-1916-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Commanders ordered men to walk forward in extended lines, expecting the bombardment to have cleared the wire and silenced defenders. It had not, and machine-gun fire produced roughly 57,000 British casualties on the first day alone, forcing a grim reassessment of infantry tactics as the Somme offensive dragged on for months.

evt-07-01-1979-sony.scenario: You are a Sony marketing executive in July 1979, preparing to launch the company's new portable stereo cassette player worldwide, but regional teams in Japan, the US, the UK and Sweden are each pushing a different name for it.
evt-07-01-1979-sony.prompt: Which name should Sony adopt globally to build a lasting brand identity?

choices.text: Walkman
Stowaway
Soundabout
Freestyle

evt-07-01-1979-sony.butterflyEffect: Sony unified all markets under the name Walkman, abandoning regional names like Soundabout, Stowaway and Freestyle. The word became so ubiquitous it entered the Oxford English Dictionary and came to define an entire era of personal, portable audio.

evt-07-01-1999-devolution-in-the-united-.scenario: It is 1 July 1999 in Edinburgh, and you stand among the crowds as the reconvened Scottish Parliament formally takes on powers transferred from the Scottish Office for the first time in nearly 300 years.
evt-07-01-1999-devolution-in-the-united-.prompt: What actually changes for Scotland on this day?

choices.text: The Scottish Office is abolished with no replacement created
Scotland is granted a separate seat at the United Nations
Legislative powers are devolved from Westminster to Holyrood
Scotland gains full independence from the UK

evt-07-01-1999-devolution-in-the-united-.butterflyEffect: Legislative authority over areas like health, education and justice passed from Westminster to the new Holyrood Parliament. The shift reshaped UK governance and fed directly into later debates over Scottish independence, culminating in the 2014 referendum.

evt-07-01-2002-2002-uberlingen-mid-air-c.scenario: It is just before midnight on 1 July 2002, over Lake Constance. You are the co-pilot of the Tupolev Tu-154, and within seconds the ground controller orders you to descend while your onboard TCAS collision-avoidance system commands you to climb.
evt-07-01-2002-2002-uberlingen-mid-air-c.prompt: With conflicting orders, which instruction should the crew have followed?

choices.text: Ignore both and turn away from the other aircraft's track
Follow the controller and descend
Follow TCAS and climb
Query the controller and hold current altitude

evt-07-01-2002-2002-uberlingen-mid-air-c.butterflyEffect: The crew obeyed the controller and descended, while the DHL 757's TCAS also told it to descend; both planes converged and collided, killing all 71 aboard. The disaster led to a binding international rule that TCAS resolution advisories always override air traffic control instructions.

evt-07-01-2008-2008-riot-in-mongolia.scenario: It is the evening of 1 July 2008 in Ulaanbaatar. Crowds furious over alleged fraud in the recent parliamentary election have gathered outside the ruling party's headquarters, and the mood is turning from protest to riot.
evt-07-01-2008-2008-riot-in-mongolia.prompt: What did the Mongolian government do as the unrest spiraled out of control?

choices.text: Ordered the ruling party's leadership to resign at once
Called in the United Nations to mediate the dispute
Declared the country's first state of emergency and deployed troops
Immediately annulled and rescheduled the disputed election

evt-07-01-2008-2008-riot-in-mongolia.butterflyEffect: The riot led to Mongolia's first-ever state of emergency, lasting four days, with troops sent into the capital and the party headquarters set ablaze. Known locally as "Black Day," the crisis exposed deep strains in Mongolia's young democracy and pushed the two rival parties toward an uneasy coalition government.

evt-07-02-626-emperor-taizong-of-tang.scenario: It is 2 July 626, and you are Li Shimin, Prince of Qin, waiting in ambush near the Xuanwu Gate of the imperial palace as your brothers Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji approach.
evt-07-02-626-emperor-taizong-of-tang.prompt: What does Li Shimin do as his brothers ride through the gate?

choices.text: He negotiates a three-way division of the empire
He arrests them and hands them to their father for judgment
He flees the capital to raise his own army
He kills both brothers in the ambush

evt-07-02-626-emperor-taizong-of-tang.butterflyEffect: Li Shimin's men killed Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji at the Xuanwu Gate, and within weeks he forced his father Emperor Gaozu to abdicate. As Emperor Taizong, he went on to preside over one of the most celebrated golden ages in Chinese history.

evt-07-02-1644-first-english-civil-war.scenario: It is the evening of 2 July 1644, and you command Parliamentarian cavalry on Marston Moor as Prince Rupert's Royalist horse threatens to break your line.
evt-07-02-1644-first-english-civil-war.prompt: What decisive move turns the battle in Parliament's favor?

choices.text: Oliver Cromwell's cavalry routs the Royalist horse on the flank
