Both armies withdraw without a clear result
Royalist infantry breaks through the center and wins the field
The Scots Covenanters withdraw, forcing a truce

evt-07-02-1644-first-english-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Oliver Cromwell's disciplined cavalry shattered the Royalist horse, and the combined Parliamentarian-Covenanter army went on to destroy Prince Rupert's force in the war's largest battle. The victory gave Parliament control of northern England and elevated Cromwell's reputation, paving the way for the New Model Army.

evt-07-02-1779-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 2 July 1779. You wade ashore near St. George's, Grenada, with Admiral d'Estaing's French landing force, the British garrison's fortifications looming on the heights above the harbor.
evt-07-02-1779-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What move do the French forces make to break the British defense?

choices.text: Open negotiations with the governor for a peaceful handover
Blockade the harbor and wait for the garrison to starve
Storm the Hospital Hill fortifications under cover of night
Withdraw after spotting a British relief squadron offshore

evt-07-02-1779-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: On the night of 3–4 July, French troops stormed the Hospital Hill fortifications overlooking St. George's, forcing British Governor Lord Macartney to surrender the island. The victory gave France a valuable sugar colony and further stretched Britain's overextended Caribbean and American forces during the war.

evt-07-02-1881-james-a-garfield.scenario: It is the morning of 2 July 1881. You are waiting on the platform of a Washington railroad station as President Garfield walks through, unaware that Charles Guiteau is closing in behind him.
evt-07-02-1881-james-a-garfield.prompt: What does Guiteau do to the president in this moment?

choices.text: Poisons his drink at a reception
Stabs him with a concealed knife
Shouts threats but is restrained before acting
Shoots him twice, one wound ultimately proving fatal

evt-07-02-1881-james-a-garfield.butterflyEffect: Guiteau shot Garfield twice; the president lingered for weeks before dying in September from infection worsened by his doctors' unsterile probing for the bullet. Guiteau's motive—a rejected office-seeker's grudge—galvanized public outrage that helped pass the Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act of 1883.

evt-07-02-1921-world-war-i.scenario: It is July 1921 in Washington. You watch President Warren G. Harding at his desk, nearly three years after the guns fell silent, still without a formal U.S. peace settlement with Germany.
evt-07-02-1921-world-war-i.prompt: What does Harding do to officially end America's involvement in the war?

choices.text: Submit the League of Nations Covenant for ratification
Sign the Knox–Porter Resolution declaring the war officially ended
Sign the Treaty of Versailles as originally negotiated
Ask Congress to declare a renewed state of war with Germany

evt-07-02-1921-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Harding signed the Knox–Porter Resolution, giving Congress's own declaration that the war was over after the Senate had twice rejected the Treaty of Versailles. It cleared the way for separate U.S. peace treaties with Germany, Austria, and Hungary later that year, while keeping America out of the League of Nations.

evt-07-02-1934-night-of-the-long-knives.scenario: It is dawn on 30 June 1934, and you are Ernst Röhm, roused from sleep at a hotel in Bad Wiessee by SS men sent on Hitler's orders.
evt-07-02-1934-night-of-the-long-knives.prompt: What choice does Hitler give Röhm in the hours that follow?

choices.text: Sign over command of the SA to Himmler and retire quietly
Flee to Austria under safe passage
Stand trial before a Nazi party court
Take his own life or be shot by the SS

evt-07-02-1934-night-of-the-long-knives.butterflyEffect: Röhm refused to take his own life and was shot in his cell on 1 July. The three-day purge killed dozens of SA leaders and other perceived enemies, crushed the SA as a rival power, and bound the army's loyalty directly to Hitler, clearing his path to absolute dictatorship.

evt-07-02-1937-amelia-earhart.scenario: It is 2 July 1937. You are Amelia Earhart, low on fuel over the Pacific, trying to find tiny Howland Island. You can transmit to the Coast Guard cutter Itasca but cannot hear their return signals clearly.
evt-07-02-1937-amelia-earhart.prompt: With no reliable radio bearing, what do you do to try to find the island?

choices.text: Fly a standard search pattern along a calculated sun-line course
Climb to a much higher altitude to extend radio range
Turn back immediately toward Lae, New Guinea
Land on the open ocean to await rescue

evt-07-02-1937-amelia-earhart.butterflyEffect: Earhart flew along a sun-line course of 157/337 degrees, hoping to cross the island's latitude, but neither she nor navigator Fred Noonan were ever found. The disappearance exposed weaknesses in aviation radio direction-finding and spurred decades of search theories and improved rescue protocols.

evt-07-02-1964-civil-rights-movement.scenario: It is 2 July 1964, and you stand in the East Room of the White House as President Lyndon Johnson prepares to sign a landmark bill after months of Senate filibuster.
evt-07-02-1964-civil-rights-movement.prompt: What sweeping change does the Act just signed put into federal law?

choices.text: It guarantees federal oversight of voter registration drives
It outlaws poll taxes in federal elections
It desegregates the U.S. armed forces
It bans segregation in public accommodations and employment discrimination

evt-07-02-1964-civil-rights-movement.butterflyEffect: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 outlawed discrimination in public accommodations, employment and federally funded programs, dismantling the legal scaffolding of Jim Crow. It set the stage for the Voting Rights Act of 1965 and accelerated a political realignment as many white Southern Democrats shifted toward the Republican Party.

evt-07-02-1976-vietnam-war.scenario: It is 2 July 1976, more than a year after Saigon's fall. You sit among delegates in Hanoi's National Assembly as officials prepare to formalize the country's future.
evt-07-02-1976-vietnam-war.prompt: What formal step does the Assembly take on this day?

choices.text: Establish a federal system with separate northern and southern governments
Declare a permanent two-state partition along the old DMZ
Postpone unification pending an international peace conference
Proclaim the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, unifying north and south

evt-07-02-1976-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: The National Assembly proclaimed the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, merging North and South into a single state and renaming Saigon as Ho Chi Minh City. The move ended the postwar transitional period but also triggered land reforms, reeducation camps, and a wave of emigration that produced the "boat people" crisis in the years that followed.

evt-07-02-1986-rodrigo-rojas-de-negri.scenario: It is July 1986 in Santiago, days after a military patrol set fire to photographer Rodrigo Rojas and student Carmen Gloria Quintana during an anti-Pinochet protest. You are US Ambassador Harry Barnes, and the regime has made clear your attendance at the funeral would be unwelcome.
evt-07-02-1986-rodrigo-rojas-de-negri.prompt: Do you attend Rodrigo Rojas's funeral despite Pinochet's displeasure?

choices.text: You issue a private letter of condolence only
Yes, you attend openly, standing with the family
You send a low-level embassy staffer instead
You decline entirely to avoid a diplomatic incident

evt-07-02-1986-rodrigo-rojas-de-negri.butterflyEffect: Barnes did attend, standing publicly with the grieving family in a direct rebuke to the dictatorship. The gesture signaled Washington's break with Pinochet and fed growing international pressure that helped isolate the regime ahead of the 1988 plebiscite that ended his rule.

evt-07-02-1990-1990-mecca-tunnel-tragedy.scenario: It is July 1990, and you are among over a million pilgrims moving through the crowded Al-Ma'aisim pedestrian tunnel linking Mina and Mecca during the Hajj.
evt-07-02-1990-1990-mecca-tunnel-tragedy.prompt: What went catastrophically wrong inside the tunnel that day?

choices.text: A fire broke out at a food stall inside the tunnel
A power failure disabled ventilation, causing panic and a fatal crush in the heat
A bridge overhead collapsed onto the crowd
False rumors of an attack triggered a stampede

evt-07-02-1990-1990-mecca-tunnel-tragedy.butterflyEffect: A power failure knocked out the tunnel's ventilation and lighting, and in the resulting heat and darkness a crush developed that suffocated over a thousand pilgrims. The disaster pushed Saudi authorities to widen pilgrimage routes and overhaul crowd-management infrastructure, though further Hajj crushes would follow in later decades.

evt-07-02-1993-sivas.scenario: It is 2 July 1993, and you are among the poets, singers and Alevi intellectuals gathered at the Hotel Madımak in Sivas for a festival honoring Pir Sultan Abdal, as an angry crowd outside grows louder.
evt-07-02-1993-sivas.prompt: What do local police and fire crews do as the siege drags on for hours?

choices.text: They evacuate the hotel calmly before the mob arrives
They storm the building at once to rescue everyone inside
They disperse the crowd within minutes of it forming
They arrive quickly but stand by for hours before intervening

evt-07-02-1993-sivas.butterflyEffect: Police and fire crews were slow to intervene, and the mob set the hotel ablaze, killing dozens of people, most of them Alevi writers, poets and musicians who had gathered for the festival. The Sivas massacre became a defining wound for Turkey's Alevi community and a lasting symbol of the state's failure to protect a religious minority.

evt-07-02-1994-usair-flight-1016.scenario: It is the afternoon of 2 July 1994, and you are the captain of USAir Flight 1016, guiding your DC-9 toward Charlotte Douglas Airport through a line of thunderstorms.
evt-07-02-1994-usair-flight-1016.prompt: As windshear warnings crackle over the radio on final approach, what should you do?

choices.text: Continue the approach, trusting the windshear will pass
Reduce speed and attempt to land on a shorter runway
Divert immediately without informing the tower
Execute a go-around and climb away from the storm cell

evt-07-02-1994-usair-flight-1016.butterflyEffect: The crew continued the approach into a microburst and crashed short of the runway, killing 37 of the 57 aboard. Investigators found the windshear warnings had come too late, prompting the FAA to speed up installation of terminal Doppler weather radar and mandatory windshear-escape training nationwide.

evt-07-02-2000-vicente-fox.scenario: It is election night, 2 July 2000. You watch the returns come in across Mexico as a candidate outside the long-ruling party edges toward an unprecedented result.
evt-07-02-2000-vicente-fox.prompt: What is the historic outcome of this presidential election?

choices.text: The military installs a caretaker government pending a recount
The PRI candidate wins another six-year term
The election is annulled amid fraud allegations
Fox wins, ending the PRI's 71-year hold on the presidency

evt-07-02-2000-vicente-fox.butterflyEffect: Vicente Fox's win ended 71 unbroken years of rule by the Institutional Revolutionary Party, the first opposition victory since 1911. It marked Mexico's definitive shift to competitive multiparty democracy, and his administration later launched Seguro Popular, expanding healthcare access to millions of previously uninsured workers.

evt-07-03-1778-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is July 3, 1778, in the Wyoming Valley of Pennsylvania. You are among the Patriot militia at Forty Fort, watching Loyalist Rangers and their Iroquois allies gather outside, and your commander must decide whether to march out and fight or hold the walls.
evt-07-03-1778-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What did the Patriot militia commander decide to do?

choices.text: Marched the militia out to attack the Loyalist-Iroquois force
Evacuated the valley without engaging the enemy
Held the fort and waited for reinforcements
Negotiated a surrender before any fighting began

evt-07-03-1778-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Colonel Zebulon Butler led the militia into open ground, where they were outflanked and routed, with over 300 killed in the Battle of Wyoming. News of the defeat spread panic through the frontier and helped prompt the Sullivan Expedition of 1779, a retaliatory campaign that devastated Iroquois territory.

evt-07-03-1863-confederate-states-army.scenario: It is the morning of 3 July 1863 at Gettysburg. You are General Robert E. Lee, having failed to break the Union flanks on the previous two days, now studying the Union center on Cemetery Ridge.
evt-07-03-1863-confederate-states-army.prompt: What does Lee order to try to break the Union line?

choices.text: A flanking maneuver around Little Round Top
A cavalry charge led by Jeb Stuart against the front line
An immediate withdrawal toward Virginia
A massed infantry assault on the Union center after an artillery barrage

evt-07-03-1863-confederate-states-army.butterflyEffect: Lee ordered a massive artillery barrage followed by a massed infantry assault, Pickett's Charge, across open ground toward the Union center. The attack was repulsed with devastating losses, forcing Lee's retreat to Virginia and marking the war's turning point, coinciding with the Union victory at Vicksburg the same week.

evt-07-03-1938-1938-gettysburg-reunion.scenario: It is 3 July 1938. You are among a few hundred surviving Civil War veterans, many over ninety, gathered on the Gettysburg battlefield as President Roosevelt prepares to speak on the 75th anniversary.
evt-07-03-1938-1938-gettysburg-reunion.prompt: What does FDR's address that day formally dedicate?

choices.text: The Eternal Light Peace Memorial
The Soldiers' National Monument
The High Water Mark Memorial
The Gettysburg National Cemetery

evt-07-03-1938-1938-gettysburg-reunion.butterflyEffect: Roosevelt dedicated the Eternal Light Peace Memorial, remotely triggering its flame as a symbol of North-South reconciliation just as war loomed in Europe. Footage of the ceremony was placed in the Westinghouse Time Capsule at the 1939 World's Fair, sealed for the year 6939.

evt-07-03-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 3 July 1940 off French Algeria. Admiral Somerville's Force H has delivered an ultimatum to the French fleet at Mers-el-Kébir: join the British, sail to a neutral port, or be destroyed, to keep the ships from Germany's reach.
evt-07-03-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: What happened after the French commander refused the British terms?

choices.text: The French fleet quietly sailed to a British-controlled port
Both sides agreed to a temporary truce and further talks
The French fleet surrendered without a shot being fired
The Royal Navy opened fire, sinking or damaging most of the French squadron

evt-07-03-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The Royal Navy opened fire, killing around 1,300 French sailors and destroying or crippling several capital ships, including the battleship Bretagne. The attack embittered Vichy France toward Britain for years and became a defining, controversial proof that Britain would fight on alone after France's collapse.

evt-07-03-1944-minsk-offensive.scenario: It is 3 July 1944, and Red Army tank columns have just entered Minsk, cutting off the retreat routes of the German Fourth Army caught east of the city during Operation Bagration.
evt-07-03-1944-minsk-offensive.prompt: What happens next to the tens of thousands of German troops trapped in the Minsk pocket?

choices.text: They break out and rejoin the main German lines
They surrender the city without resistance before being encircled
They are encircled and largely destroyed or captured within days
The Luftwaffe airlifts most of them out of the pocket

evt-07-03-1944-minsk-offensive.butterflyEffect: The pocket collapsed within days, with most of the German Fourth Army killed or captured — one of the worst German defeats of the entire war. The disaster tore open the Eastern Front, letting the Red Army race toward the Baltic states, Poland, and eventually East Prussia itself.

evt-07-03-1952-constitution-of-puerto-ri.scenario: It is July 3, 1952, and Congress is reviewing the constitution Puerto Rican voters approved months earlier. Before final ratification, lawmakers object to one section of the proposed bill of rights as incompatible with a U.S. territory's charter.
evt-07-03-1952-constitution-of-puerto-ri.prompt: What did Congress require Puerto Rico to remove before ratifying the constitution?

choices.text: The provision establishing Spanish as an official language
The article creating a bicameral legislature
The clause allowing residents to vote in U.S. presidential elections
A clause guaranteeing rights to work, education, and social protection

evt-07-03-1952-constitution-of-puerto-ri.butterflyEffect: Congress conditioned approval on striking Section 20 of the Bill of Rights, which guaranteed rights to work, education, and social protection resembling clauses in socialist constitutions of the era. Puerto Rico's legislature complied, and Congress ratified the amended document, cementing the island's unique Commonwealth relationship with the United States.

evt-07-03-1988-united-states-navy.scenario: It is 3 July 1988 in the Persian Gulf. Aboard USS Vincennes, radar shows an aircraft climbing out of Bandar Abbas airport, and the captain has only moments to decide whether it poses a threat before it closes on his ship.
evt-07-03-1988-united-states-navy.prompt: What did Captain Rogers decide to do?

choices.text: Held fire and issued further radio warnings until the aircraft passed
Ordered the ship to withdraw from the area immediately
Requested visual confirmation from a nearby aircraft before acting
Fired two missiles, believing the aircraft was a hostile fighter jet

evt-07-03-1988-united-states-navy.butterflyEffect: The missiles destroyed Iran Air Flight 655, a civilian Airbus on a scheduled flight, killing all 290 people aboard. The United States later expressed regret and paid compensation but never formally apologized, and the incident remains a bitter grievance cited for years in tensions between the two countries.

evt-07-03-1996-john-major.scenario: It is 3 July 1996, and Prime Minister John Major rises in the House of Commons to make an announcement about a medieval relic that has sat in England for exactly 700 years.
evt-07-03-1996-john-major.prompt: What did Major announce would happen to the Stone of Scone?

choices.text: It would remain under the Coronation Chair at Westminster Abbey
It would be returned to Scotland and placed in Edinburgh Castle
It would be given to the Church of Scotland to keep at St Giles' Cathedral
It would be loaned permanently to the British Museum

evt-07-03-1996-john-major.butterflyEffect: The Stone was returned to Edinburgh Castle in November 1996, ending its 700-year residence beneath the English coronation throne. Made ahead of Scottish devolution, the gesture was widely read as a symbolic concession to Scottish national feeling, though the Stone is still due to travel south for future coronations.

evt-07-03-2013-abdel-fattah-el-sisi.scenario: It is 3 July 2013, and you are a senior Egyptian officer standing beside General Abdel Fattah el-Sisi as he prepares to address the nation on television, with President Mohamed Morsi already held by the military.
evt-07-03-2013-abdel-fattah-el-sisi.prompt: What does Sisi announce to the country in this broadcast?

choices.text: New elections will be held immediately with Morsi as a candidate
A referendum on Morsi's rule will be held within the week
Morsi is removed from office and the constitution suspended
Morsi will keep the presidency but with reduced powers

evt-07-03-2013-abdel-fattah-el-sisi.butterflyEffect: Sisi announced Morsi's removal from power and the suspension of the constitution, installing an interim government backed by the military. He was elected president in 2014 and has ruled since, overseeing a sweeping crackdown on the Muslim Brotherhood and a broader closing of the political space opened by the 2011 revolution.

evt-07-04-414-theodosius-ii.scenario: It's 414 in Constantinople, and your emperor Theodosius II is still a boy. His elder sister, Aelia Pulcheria, has just been proclaimed Augusta.
evt-07-04-414-theodosius-ii.prompt: What role did Pulcheria take on after her elevation?

choices.text: She retired to a convent and left governance to generals
She married a Western emperor to unite the two halves of Rome
She was exiled by rival courtiers within the year
She acted as regent, guiding imperial policy and her brother's upbringing

evt-07-04-414-theodosius-ii.butterflyEffect: Pulcheria effectively steered the Eastern Empire during Theodosius's minority, shaping its firm Christian orthodoxy. After Theodosius died in 450 without an heir, she married the general Marcian and continued to rule as empress, helping secure the succession and the empire's doctrinal direction at the Council of Chalcedon.

evt-07-04-1054-chinese-astronomy.scenario: It is July 4, 1054, and you serve as an imperial astronomer in Song China. Scanning the night sky near the constellation you call Tianguan, you spot a brilliant point of light that was not there before, bright enough to be seen in daylight.
evt-07-04-1054-chinese-astronomy.prompt: What is the correct duty of an imperial astronomer confronted with this new 'guest star'?

choices.text: Meticulously record its position, brightness and duration for the official chronicles
Classify it as a comet and track the length of its tail
Assume it is simply the planet Venus shining unusually bright and note nothing further
Keep the sighting secret from the court to avoid public panic

evt-07-04-1054-chinese-astronomy.butterflyEffect: Chinese court astronomers meticulously logged the star's position and brightness, noting it stayed visible in daylight for 23 days and at night for almost two years. Centuries later, astronomers matched their records to the Crab Nebula, and the 1968 discovery of a pulsar at its heart confirmed this had been a supernova, linking ancient Chinese record-keeping directly to modern astrophysics.

evt-07-04-1776-united-states-declaration.scenario: It is July 4, 1776, and you are a delegate inside the Pennsylvania State House in Philadelphia as the Second Continental Congress takes up Thomas Jefferson's draft explaining why the colonies must break from Britain.
evt-07-04-1776-united-states-declaration.prompt: What does Congress do with the draft on this day?

choices.text: Adopt it unanimously as the Declaration of Independence
Reject it and continue negotiating with the Crown
Send it back to Franklin for a complete rewrite
Postpone any vote on it for another year

evt-07-04-1776-united-states-declaration.butterflyEffect: Congress adopted the Declaration unanimously, formally severing the Thirteen Colonies from British rule and laying out the philosophical justification for revolution. The document went on to inspire independence and rights movements far beyond America, even as the war it justified would grind on for seven more years until Britain's defeat in 1783.

evt-07-04-1837-grand-junction-railway.scenario: It's 1837 and you are an engineer inspecting the new Grand Junction Railway, which links the Liverpool and Manchester Railway to Birmingham using steam locomotives across the entire route.
evt-07-04-1837-grand-junction-railway.prompt: What followed the opening of this pioneering long-distance steam line?

choices.text: It remained an isolated local line with no further connections
It was abandoned within a year due to boiler failures
It sparked a boom in trunk railway building across Britain
It was converted to horse traction after public protest

evt-07-04-1837-grand-junction-railway.butterflyEffect: The GJR proved that steam-hauled trunk lines could work over long distances, and within a year it connected at Birmingham's Curzon Street with the London and Birmingham Railway, creating a through route from Liverpool and Manchester to London. This success helped trigger the 'Railway Mania' investment boom of the 1840s that built much of Britain's rail network.

evt-07-04-1862-river-thames.scenario: It is July 4, 1862, and you are one of the young Liddell sisters being rowed up the Thames from Oxford to Godstow by a friend and the Reverend Charles Dodgson, a mathematics don with a talent for storytelling.
evt-07-04-1862-river-thames.prompt: To pass the long, warm afternoon on the river, what do you beg Dodgson to do?

choices.text: Recite passages of Latin poetry from memory
Tell a story about a girl who falls down a rabbit hole into a strange world
Teach the sisters how to fish from the boat
Sketch the passing riverbank scenery

evt-07-04-1862-river-thames.butterflyEffect: Dodgson improvised a tale about a girl named Alice who follows a rabbit down a hole into a fantastical world. He later wrote it down and, publishing under the pen name Lewis Carroll, released it in 1865 as Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, one of the most enduring works of English literature and the source of a sequel, Through the Looking-Glass.

evt-07-04-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It is dawn on 4 July 1863 near Helena, Arkansas. You march with Confederate troops under General Sterling Price, ordered to storm the fortified Union hilltop batteries guarding the town in hopes of easing pressure on besieged Vicksburg.
evt-07-04-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: What does the Confederate command order the attacking columns to do?

choices.text: Wait for additional reinforcements before attempting any attack
Bypass Helena entirely and march straight toward Vicksburg
Launch a direct frontal assault on the fortified Union hilltop positions
Open negotiations with the Union garrison for a peaceful surrender

evt-07-04-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Confederates charged the entrenched Union batteries directly and were repulsed with heavy losses. The defeat at Helena came the very same day Vicksburg surrendered to Grant, giving the Union control of the Mississippi River and splitting the Confederacy in two—a double blow historians mark as the war's turning point.

evt-07-04-1918-world-war-i.scenario: It's dawn on 4 July 1918 near Le Hamel, and you are part of an Allied force under Australian general John Monash, using tanks, infantry, artillery, and aircraft together in a tightly timed plan.
evt-07-04-1918-world-war-i.prompt: What was the result of Monash's combined-arms attack at Hamel?

choices.text: Objectives were captured in around 93 minutes, a stunning success
German counterattacks retook the village by nightfall
The attack stalled after tanks became bogged in mud
The battle ended in stalemate after weeks of fighting

evt-07-04-1918-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The Battle of Hamel became a model for combined-arms warfare, meeting its objectives almost exactly on schedule. Monash's methods influenced the planning of the Hundred Days Offensive later that year, which helped bring the war to an end by November 1918.

evt-07-04-1941-aktion-ab.scenario: It is early July 1941, only days after German forces have captured Lwów, and you are a Nazi security officer holding a list of the city's university professors and intellectuals marked for arrest under Aktion AB.
evt-07-04-1941-aktion-ab.prompt: What order is carried out against the men on this list?

choices.text: Release them after a formal warning
Recruit them to run a new German-controlled university
Execute them along with members of their households
Deport them to labor camps in Germany

evt-07-04-1941-aktion-ab.butterflyEffect: The professors were shot within days in what became known as the Massacre of Lwów professors, one episode within the broader Aktion AB campaign to eliminate Poland's educated classes. The killings devastated the city's academic institutions and stand as a stark early marker of the Nazi policy to destroy Polish national identity before the machinery of genocide expanded elsewhere.

evt-07-04-1943-w-adys-aw-sikorski.scenario: It's the night of 4 July 1943 at Gibraltar, and General Władysław Sikorski, prime minister of the Polish government-in-exile, has just boarded his aircraft after inspecting Polish troops in the Middle East.
evt-07-04-1943-w-adys-aw-sikorski.prompt: What happened to Sikorski's aircraft shortly after takeoff?

choices.text: It crashed into the sea seconds after takeoff, killing him
It was forced down by engine trouble but all aboard survived
It landed safely in London later that night
It was shot down by German fighters over the Mediterranean

evt-07-04-1943-w-adys-aw-sikorski.butterflyEffect: Only the Czech pilot survived the crash, and Sikorski's death removed the most respected leader of the Polish government-in-exile at a critical moment in relations with Stalin. His loss weakened Polish influence over its own postwar fate, and conspiracy theories about sabotage have persisted ever since.

evt-07-04-1951-william-shockley.scenario: You are a science reporter at a Bell Labs press event on July 4, 1951. William Shockley, head of the semiconductor research group, is about to unveil a new device meant to surpass the crude point-contact transistor his colleagues built in 1947.
evt-07-04-1951-william-shockley.prompt: What device does Shockley announce as the breakthrough improvement?

choices.text: A new microwave amplifier tube
A silicon diode intended for radio receivers
The junction transistor
An improved version of the 1947 point-contact transistor

evt-07-04-1951-william-shockley.butterflyEffect: Shockley's junction transistor was far easier to manufacture reliably than the fragile point-contact device, making mass-produced solid-state electronics practical. It earned him a share of the 1956 Nobel Prize and later led him to found Shockley Semiconductor in California, whose disgruntled 'Traitorous Eight' engineers went on to found Fairchild Semiconductor, seeding what became Silicon Valley.

evt-07-04-1954-1954-fifa-world-cup-final.scenario: It is July 4, 1954, at Wankdorf Stadium in Bern. You play for West Germany, already down 2-0 to Hungary's famed Golden Team in the World Cup final, the same side that thrashed you 8-3 in the group stage.
evt-07-04-1954-1954-fifa-world-cup-final.prompt: How does West Germany turn this seemingly hopeless final around?

choices.text: Battle back from 2-0 down to win 3-2
Force a 2-2 draw and win on penalties
Benefit from a late own goal by Hungary's keeper
Win by walkover after Hungary forfeits

evt-07-04-1954-1954-fifa-world-cup-final.butterflyEffect: West Germany fought back to win 3-2, with Helmut Rahn scoring the decisive goal in the 84th minute. The upset, remembered in Germany as the 'Miracle of Bern,' became a symbol of postwar national recovery and pride, while Hungary's celebrated Golden Team never won the trophy their talent seemed to promise.

evt-07-04-1976-israel-defense-forces.scenario: It is the night of 3–4 July 1976. You are part of an Israeli commando team that has just landed by transport plane at Entebbe airport in Uganda, where hijackers hold over 100 hostages from a diverted Air France flight.
evt-07-04-1976-israel-defense-forces.prompt: How should the assault team approach the terminal without alerting the guards?

choices.text: Call in an airstrike on the terminal building to eliminate the hijackers
Drive vehicles disguised as Amin's motorcade toward the terminal, then storm it by surprise
Broadcast a surrender ultimatum to the hijackers over the airport's speakers
Hold position outside the perimeter while diplomats negotiate a release

evt-07-04-1976-israel-defense-forces.butterflyEffect: The commandos drove toward the terminal in a black Mercedes and Land Rovers disguised as President Idi Amin's motorcade, then stormed the building. Within minutes almost all hostages were freed; the raid's commander, Yonatan Netanyahu, was killed. The operation became a landmark in counter-terrorism doctrine and badly strained Israel–Uganda relations.

evt-07-04-1988-kylie-minogue.scenario: It's July 1988 and a nineteen-year-old Australian soap actress named Kylie Minogue has just released her self-titled debut album, built around her surprise chart-topping cover of 'The Loco-Motion'.
evt-07-04-1988-kylie-minogue.prompt: What did this debut album launch for Kylie Minogue?

choices.text: A career mainly as a songwriter for other artists
A one-hit novelty career that ended within the year
A decades-long international pop career and multiple Grammy/Brit awards
A quick return to acting with no further music releases

evt-07-04-1988-kylie-minogue.butterflyEffect: Kylie became one of the best-selling Australian artists ever, going on to win two Grammy Awards and four Brit Awards and sell over 80 million records, cementing her status as a global 'Princess of Pop' across four decades.

evt-07-04-2012-higgs-boson.scenario: It is July 2012 at CERN. Data from both the ATLAS and CMS detectors independently show a striking bump near 125 GeV, matching decades of theoretical prediction for the Higgs boson.
evt-07-04-2012-higgs-boson.prompt: How should CERN characterize the finding when it goes public on 4 July?

choices.text: Withhold the results for several more years until absolute certainty is reached
Declare the Higgs boson definitively discovered beyond any doubt
Dismiss the signal as statistical background noise and rerun the experiment
Announce a particle consistent with the Higgs boson, pending further confirmation

evt-07-04-2012-higgs-boson.butterflyEffect: CERN announced the observation of a new particle "consistent with" the long-sought Higgs boson, careful to note further data was needed before calling it confirmed. Subsequent analysis in 2013 verified it, earning Peter Higgs and François Englert the Nobel Prize and completing the Standard Model's picture of how particles acquire mass.

evt-07-04-2015-chile-national-football-t.scenario: It is July 4, 2015, at the National Stadium in Santiago. Host nation Chile has battled Argentina to a scoreless draw through extra time in the Copa América final, and the match now hangs on a decision beyond regulation play.
evt-07-04-2015-chile-national-football-t.prompt: How does Chile finally claim its first-ever major international football title?

choices.text: Advancing on the away-goals rule
Winning a penalty shootout after the scoreless draw
Winning by default after Argentina fielded an ineligible player
Scoring a golden goal deep into extra time

evt-07-04-2015-chile-national-football-t.butterflyEffect: Chile won a penalty shootout 4–1, with Alexis Sánchez sealing it with a cheeky chipped finish. The victory launched a golden era for La Roja, who beat Argentina again in the 2016 Copa América Centenario final, cementing the Sánchez–Vidal generation as the most successful in Chilean football history.

evt-07-05-1830-invasion-of-algiers-1830.scenario: It is 5 July 1830, and you are Hussein Dey, ruler of the Regency of Algiers. French warships have bombarded the city and French troops have landed nearby after three years of blockade following the 'Fan Affair'.
evt-07-05-1830-invasion-of-algiers-1830.prompt: With the city surrounded and no relief in sight, what should the Dey do?

choices.text: Abandon the city and flee to Tunis
Fight on street by street until reinforcements arrive
Surrender the city to French forces
Appeal to the Ottoman Sultan for immediate military aid

evt-07-05-1830-invasion-of-algiers-1830.butterflyEffect: Hussein Dey surrendered Algiers to the French, ending centuries of Ottoman-linked rule. The conquest began 132 years of French colonial control over Algeria, which would only end after a bitter war of independence in 1962.

evt-07-05-1841-thomas-cook.scenario: It is 5 July 1841. You are a member of the Leicester Temperance Society, gathering at the station where a Baptist preacher named Thomas Cook has chartered an entire train to carry you to a rally in Loughborough.
evt-07-05-1841-thomas-cook.prompt: What has Cook arranged that makes this trip novel?

choices.text: A fleet of horse-drawn coaches hired for the day
A guided walking tour along the canal towpath
A chartered riverboat down the Soar to Loughborough
A chartered excursion train with a single ticket covering travel and refreshments

evt-07-05-1841-thomas-cook.butterflyEffect: Cook had chartered a special excursion train and sold an all-inclusive ticket covering travel and refreshments, one of the first packaged group trips by rail. Its success led him to organise tours across Britain and eventually abroad, and he later founded Thomas Cook & Son, helping make leisure travel accessible to ordinary people.

evt-07-05-1922-tenentism.scenario: You are a young officer holed up at Fort Copacabana in Rio de Janeiro on 5 July 1922. The wider rebellion against the federal government has already collapsed, and government troops now surround your position.
evt-07-05-1922-tenentism.prompt: What do you and your fellow rebels do as the fort's position becomes hopeless?

choices.text: March out onto the beach to confront the surrounding troops directly
Escape by boat under cover of darkness
Surrender the fort immediately to avoid bloodshed
Negotiate a general amnesty with the government commander

evt-07-05-1922-tenentism.butterflyEffect: Eighteen officers, later remembered as the '18 of the Fort,' marched out onto Copacabana beach to face overwhelming government forces rather than surrender, and nearly all were killed. Their doomed stand became a founding legend of Tenentism, inspiring further revolts that helped bring down the First Brazilian Republic in 1930.

evt-07-05-1937-hormel-foods.scenario: It is early 1937 and Hormel has just perfected a new canned spiced ham product, but it still has no name. The company launches a public contest, offering $100 for the best suggestion.
evt-07-05-1937-hormel-foods.prompt: Which name wins the contest and gets stamped on the can?

choices.text: Hormel Ham Loaf
Prepared Pork Delight
Spam
Miracle Meat

evt-07-05-1937-hormel-foods.butterflyEffect: Actor Kenneth Daigneau, brother of a Hormel vice president, won the $100 prize with the name Spam. The product became a staple of Allied rations in World War II, fed troops and civilians across Europe and the Pacific, and later entered global slang as shorthand for unwanted bulk email.

evt-07-05-1948-aneurin-bevan.scenario: It is 5 July 1948 in Manchester. You have nursed a painful ear infection for months because you could never afford the doctor's fee, but today you are told to simply walk into the surgery.
evt-07-05-1948-aneurin-bevan.prompt: Under the NHS launching today, what happens when you see the doctor?

choices.text: You are treated for free, with the cost covered by taxation and national insurance
You pay a small fixed fee set by the local council
You must first take out a private insurance policy to qualify
You are turned away because the scheme only covers hospital care

evt-07-05-1948-aneurin-bevan.butterflyEffect: The NHS opened providing care free at the point of use, funded through taxation and national insurance rather than fees. It became the cornerstone of Britain's postwar welfare state and a template debated and adapted by health systems worldwide, while remaining a fixture of British political life ever since.

evt-07-05-1950-korean-war.scenario: It is 5 July 1950 near Osan, South Korea. You command Task Force Smith, a small American force hastily sent to block the advancing North Korean army, and enemy tanks are approaching your thin defensive line.
evt-07-05-1950-korean-war.prompt: With North Korean armor bearing down and your unit badly outgunned, what should you do?

choices.text: Hold the line to delay the North Korean advance
Withdraw immediately without engaging
Call in naval bombardment and wait offshore
Negotiate a local ceasefire with North Korean commanders

evt-07-05-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: Task Force Smith held its ground briefly but was overwhelmed and forced into a costly retreat, suffering heavy casualties in the first clash between American and North Korean forces. The defeat exposed how unprepared US occupation troops were for combat, spurring a rapid buildup that led to the Inchon landing later that year.

evt-07-05-1954-elvis-presley.scenario: It is a late night in July 1954 at Sun Records in Memphis. You are producer Sam Phillips, and a nervous young truck driver named Elvis Presley has just cut a loose, playful version of "That's All Right" during a break, backed only by guitar and bass.
evt-07-05-1954-elvis-presley.prompt: What should Sam Phillips do with this raw, unplanned take?

choices.text: Shelve it as unfinished and unpolished
Release it immediately as a single
Re-record it with a full studio orchestra
Sell the recording rights to a rival label

evt-07-05-1954-elvis-presley.butterflyEffect: Phillips rushed the recording to a local DJ, who played it on air to an enthusiastic response. Released as Presley's first single days later, it launched the rockabilly sound that would carry him to national fame and help ignite the rock and roll era.

evt-07-05-1969-brian-jones.scenario: You're packed into Hyde Park, London, on 5 July 1969. The Rolling Stones are about to play their first UK show in years, just two days after founder Brian Jones was found dead in his swimming pool.
evt-07-05-1969-brian-jones.prompt: How does Mick Jagger open the show in tribute to Jones?

choices.text: He dedicates the entire set list to Jones without comment
He reads a poem by Shelley and releases butterflies
He plays a recording of Jones's guitar solos before the band starts
He leads the crowd in a moment of silence before playing

evt-07-05-1969-brian-jones.butterflyEffect: Jagger read a passage from Shelley's elegy 'Adonais' and thousands of white butterflies were released over the crowd, many of which had died in their boxes beforehand. The free concert also introduced new guitarist Mick Taylor and became one of the era's defining rock spectacles.

evt-07-05-1973-juvenal-habyarimana.scenario: You serve under Major General Juvénal Habyarimana in the Rwandan army on 5 July 1973, as he moves against President Grégoire Kayibanda's increasingly troubled government.
evt-07-05-1973-juvenal-habyarimana.prompt: How does Habyarimana seize power that day?

choices.text: A bloodless coup that deposes Kayibanda without violence
A popular uprising that forces Kayibanda to resign
A negotiated power-sharing agreement with Kayibanda
A violent armed assault on the presidential palace

evt-07-05-1973-juvenal-habyarimana.butterflyEffect: Habyarimana staged a bloodless coup, deposed Kayibanda, suspended the constitution, and installed himself as president, ruling for the next twenty-one years under a one-party state. His assassination in 1994 became the immediate trigger for the Rwandan genocide.

evt-07-05-1989-united-states-national-se.scenario: You are in a Washington D.C. federal courtroom on 5 July 1989, waiting as Judge Gerhard Gesell prepares to sentence Oliver North for his role in the Iran-Contra affair.
evt-07-05-1989-united-states-national-se.prompt: What sentence does North actually receive?

choices.text: A suspended sentence with probation and community service, no prison time
A life sentence for treason
Complete acquittal on all charges
Six years in federal prison

evt-07-05-1989-united-states-national-se.butterflyEffect: North got a suspended sentence with two years' probation, a fine, and community service, rather than prison time. His convictions were later thrown out on appeal in 1990 because his immunized congressional testimony had tainted the trial, and he went on to a career in conservative politics and media.

evt-07-05-1996-ian-wilmut.scenario: You are a researcher at the Roslin Institute near Edinburgh. A lamb has just been born from an egg cell that once carried the nucleus of an ordinary mammary cell taken from an adult ewe.
evt-07-05-1996-ian-wilmut.prompt: What technique produced this lamb, later named Dolly?

choices.text: Selective breeding over several generations for a desired trait
Somatic cell nuclear transfer, inserting an adult cell's nucleus into an emptied egg
Editing the embryo's genes directly with molecular scissors
Splitting a single embryo into two genetically identical twins

evt-07-05-1996-ian-wilmut.butterflyEffect: Dolly was created by somatic cell nuclear transfer, proving an adult body cell's genetic material could reprogram an egg into a whole new animal. The 1997 announcement of her existence triggered worldwide debate over cloning ethics and spurred research into stem cells and reprogramming that underpins regenerative medicine today.

evt-07-05-1999-bill-clinton.scenario: It is July 1999, and you advise President Clinton as his administration weighs how to pressure Afghanistan's Taliban government, which continues to shelter Osama bin Laden after the 1998 U.S. embassy bombings in Africa.
evt-07-05-1999-bill-clinton.prompt: What action does the Clinton administration take against the Taliban?

choices.text: Impose trade and economic sanctions on the Taliban
Open unconditional diplomatic talks with the Taliban
Launch a full military invasion of Afghanistan
Formally recognize the Taliban government

evt-07-05-1999-bill-clinton.butterflyEffect: Clinton signed an executive order imposing trade and economic sanctions, freezing Taliban assets in the United States and banning trade with the regime. The sanctions failed to dislodge bin Laden from Afghanistan, and tensions between Washington and the Taliban continued escalating toward the confrontation that followed the September 11 attacks two years later.

evt-07-05-2003-world-health-organization.scenario: It is early July 2003, and you are a WHO official reviewing the last known chains of transmission of the SARS virus, with no new cases reported for weeks in the final affected regions.
evt-07-05-2003-world-health-organization.prompt: Based on the data, what should the WHO announce?

choices.text: That the outbreak has become a global pandemic
That travel advisories must be extended indefinitely
That the outbreak is officially contained
That funding for further monitoring should be withdrawn

evt-07-05-2003-world-health-organization.butterflyEffect: The WHO declared the SARS outbreak contained, lifting the last travel advisories and closing a global health scare that had infected thousands. The rapid international cooperation and surveillance methods used against SARS became a template later applied to H1N1 and COVID-19 responses.

evt-07-05-2004-2004-indonesian-president.scenario: It is September 2004, and you are a first-time voter in Jakarta, marking your ballot in Indonesia's first-ever direct presidential runoff. Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono and incumbent Megawati Sukarnoputri are the final two candidates.
evt-07-05-2004-2004-indonesian-president.prompt: What was the outcome of this historic runoff election?

choices.text: Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono wins the presidency
The military intervenes to select a president
The election is annulled for fraud
Megawati Sukarnoputri wins re-election

evt-07-05-2004-2004-indonesian-president.butterflyEffect: Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono won decisively, becoming Indonesia's first directly elected president. His victory ended the era of parliamentary-selected presidents and set a precedent for peaceful democratic transitions that has held in every Indonesian election since.

evt-07-05-2009-staffordshire-hoard.scenario: You are metal detecting a recently ploughed field in Staffordshire in July 2009 when your detector signals wildly, and you begin pulling gold and garnet-studded fragments from the soil, far more than any ordinary find.
evt-07-05-2009-staffordshire-hoard.prompt: What is the correct thing for you to do with this discovery?

choices.text: Quietly sell the pieces to private collectors
Report it to authorities under the Treasure Act
Melt the gold down for its material value
Keep it hidden and tell no one

evt-07-05-2009-staffordshire-hoard.butterflyEffect: Terry Herbert reported the find under the Treasure Act, and archaeologists confirmed it as the largest hoard of Anglo-Saxon gold and silver ever found, nearly 4,600 pieces including sword fittings and jewellery. Its cloisonné garnet work reshaped scholarly understanding of seventh-century Mercian warrior culture and craftsmanship.

evt-07-05-2012-the-shard.scenario: You stand at the base of Renzo Piano's glass-clad tower on London Bridge in July 2012, watching light beams and fireworks mark its inauguration after years of construction on the site of the old Southwark Towers.
evt-07-05-2012-the-shard.prompt: What milestone does the Shard claim for London's skyline that night?

choices.text: Tallest building in the entire world
First skyscraper ever built in London
Tallest wooden structure in Europe
Tallest building in the United Kingdom and Western Europe

evt-07-05-2012-the-shard.butterflyEffect: The Shard, at 309.6 metres, became the tallest building in the United Kingdom and Western Europe. Its opening cemented Renzo Piano's pyramid-shaped design as a new London landmark and spurred further high-rise development around the South Bank and Bermondsey.

evt-07-05-2016-juno-spacecraft.scenario: You are a flight controller at JPL on 5 July 2016. Juno is racing toward Jupiter, and unless the spacecraft fires its engine at exactly the right moment, it will fly past the planet forever.
evt-07-05-2016-juno-spacecraft.prompt: What must Juno's onboard computer do to be captured into orbit?

choices.text: Release a small lander toward the cloud tops
Use a gravity assist from one of Jupiter's moons
Fire its main engine for a lengthy burn to slow into orbit
Deploy a parachute to slow its approach

evt-07-05-2016-juno-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: Juno performed a roughly 35-minute main engine burn that slowed it enough for Jupiter's gravity to capture it into a long polar orbit. The successful insertion let Juno spend years studying the planet's atmosphere, magnetic field and deep interior, and its mission was later extended to include close flybys of Jupiter's inner moons.

evt-07-05-2023-ariane-5.scenario: You are a mission engineer at the Guiana Space Centre on 5 July 2023, watching the countdown for a rocket that has flown European and international payloads into orbit since 1996, carrying the Heinrich Hertz and Syracuse 4B satellites aloft.
evt-07-05-2023-ariane-5.prompt: What happens to this launch vehicle after tonight's flight?

choices.text: It continues flying for another decade unchanged
It is sold to a private American launch company
It fails to reach orbit and is grounded permanently
It is retired, handing launches to the incoming Ariane 6

evt-07-05-2023-ariane-5.butterflyEffect: This was Ariane 5's final flight after nearly three decades of service, including a remarkable streak of 82 consecutive successful launches. It was retired in favour of its successor, Ariane 6, which had been in development since 2014 and made its own debut launch the following year.

evt-07-06-1483-house-of-york.scenario: It is 6 July 1483 in Westminster Abbey. You kneel among the assembled nobles as Richard, Duke of Gloucester, is crowned Richard III, his young nephews having been set aside as illegitimate heirs.
evt-07-06-1483-house-of-york.prompt: What is the safest course for a nobleman as the crown is placed on Richard's head?

choices.text: Swear fealty to the new king to secure your position at court
Publicly proclaim the young prince the rightful king
Flee at once to join Henry Tudor in exile
Refuse to attend the ceremony in protest

evt-07-06-1483-house-of-york.butterflyEffect: Richard's coronation followed the declaration that Edward IV's marriage was invalid, disinheriting the young princes. Just two years later Richard died at the Battle of Bosworth, ending Plantagenet rule and opening the way for the Tudor dynasty under Henry VII.

evt-07-06-1614-ottoman-empire.scenario: You are a Knight of St. John manning the coastal watch near Marsascala on 6 July 1614, as an Ottoman fleet lands troops for what will prove to be the last major raid on Malta.
evt-07-06-1614-ottoman-empire.prompt: What should the defenders do to stop the landing force before it entrenches?

choices.text: Wait passively for reinforcements to arrive from Sicily before acting
Abandon the coast entirely and withdraw all forces into Valletta
Rally militia and cavalry to counterattack before the Ottomans fortify their position
Offer tribute to persuade the fleet to withdraw peacefully

evt-07-06-1614-ottoman-empire.butterflyEffect: Local militia and cavalry, mobilized quickly by Grand Master Alof de Wignacourt's coastal defense system, drove the raiders back to their ships within a day. The failed raid ended serious Ottoman attempts against Malta and pushed the Knights to expand their network of coastal watchtowers.

evt-07-06-1685-james-ii-of-england.scenario: It is the pre-dawn hours of 6 July 1685 near Westonzoyland in Somerset. You march with the Duke of Monmouth's rebel army of farmers and dissenters, easing through the marshy fog to surprise King James II's disciplined royal troops camped nearby.
evt-07-06-1685-james-ii-of-england.prompt: What happens when the royal army detects your night attack across the moor?

choices.text: Monmouth's rebels are routed and scattered
Both sides withdraw and agree to a truce
Monmouth wins a decisive victory over the king's army
James II abandons the field and flees to France

evt-07-06-1685-james-ii-of-england.butterflyEffect: The royal forces held their line and shattered Monmouth's rebels at the Battle of Sedgemoor, the last pitched battle fought on English soil. Monmouth was captured and executed, and the brutal reprisals of the 'Bloody Assizes' that followed deepened resentment of James's rule, helping set the stage for his overthrow in the Glorious Revolution of 1688.

evt-07-06-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It's July 5, 1777, at Fort Ticonderoga. You serve under General Arthur St. Clair, watching British troops haul cannon onto Mount Defiance, a height overlooking the fort that your own engineers had judged too steep to fortify.
evt-07-06-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: With the fort now exposed to bombardment, what should St. Clair order?

choices.text: Evacuate the garrison at once across the bridge to Mount Independence
Hold the fort and fight to the last man
Open surrender negotiations with Burgoyne
Wait in place for reinforcements from the south

evt-07-06-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: St. Clair evacuated the garrison overnight across a bridge of boats to Mount Independence, saving most of his men and equipment but abandoning the fort and its guns to Burgoyne. The loss shocked Congress and nearly ended St. Clair's career, but the preserved army went on to help defeat Burgoyne later that year at Saratoga.

evt-07-06-1801-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: It's July 6, 1801, in Algeciras Bay. You serve under Sir James Saumarez, whose six British ships of the line close on three French warships anchored under the protection of Spanish shore batteries, with the wind falling away to nothing.
evt-07-06-1801-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What is the outcome as Saumarez presses the attack in the failing wind?

choices.text: The British destroy all three French ships within the hour
The British withdraw damaged, losing one ship, unable to destroy the French squadron
The Spanish shore batteries sink the entire British squadron
The French squadron surrenders without firing a shot

evt-07-06-1801-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: Becalmed under heavy fire from the Spanish batteries, the British squadron was driven off with one ship-of-the-line run aground and captured, and the French escaped destruction. Saumarez limped back to Gibraltar for repairs, but days later his refitted squadron ambushed a larger Franco-Spanish fleet, sinking two Spanish ships in a confused night action that became a far greater British triumph.

evt-07-06-1809-napoleon.scenario: It is dawn on 6 July 1809 and you command a French corps on the Marchfeld plain near Vienna, facing Archduke Charles' entrenched Austrian army on the second day of Wagram.
evt-07-06-1809-napoleon.prompt: How should the French break the Austrian center to win the battle?

choices.text: Send cavalry alone to outflank the Austrians via the Danube islands
Withdraw to Vienna and wait for Austrian reinforcements to disperse
Offer an immediate armistice to Archduke Charles
Mass artillery into a grand battery and drive an infantry column through the center

evt-07-06-1809-napoleon.butterflyEffect: Napoleon massed a huge grand battery of artillery and sent Macdonald's column smashing through the Austrian center, forcing Charles to retreat. The victory led to the Treaty of Schönbrunn, stripping Austria of territory and setting up Napoleon's later marriage to Archduchess Marie Louise.

evt-07-06-1916-world-war-i.scenario: You serve with the Polish Legions, dug into trenches near the village of Kostiuchnówka in Volhynia, part of the Austro-Hungarian line. As the Brusilov Offensive erupts, wave after wave of Russian infantry storms your position.
evt-07-06-1916-world-war-i.prompt: What do you do as the Russian assault threatens to overrun your trench?

choices.text: Launch an unsupported bayonet charge into open ground
Abandon the trench without engaging the enemy
Hold the line despite the odds, inflicting casualties before being pushed back
Surrender the position immediately to avoid casualties

evt-07-06-1916-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The Legions held their ground for three brutal days, inflicting heavy losses before being forced to withdraw as the Russians took the position. The stand became known as the 'Polish Thermopylae,' a legend that boosted the prestige of Piłsudski's Legions and fed the postwar case for Polish independence.

evt-07-06-1940-story-bridge.scenario: You are a Brisbane laborer watching the official opening of the Story Bridge on 6 July 1940, a structure many locals credit with keeping food on their tables through the hardest years of the Depression.
evt-07-06-1940-story-bridge.prompt: Beyond crossing the Brisbane River, what was the bridge project chiefly intended to deliver to the city?

choices.text: A direct highway link to interstate New South Wales
A free, toll-less crossing from its opening day
Employment for workers left jobless by the Great Depression
A dedicated tramway bypassing the city center

evt-07-06-1940-story-bridge.butterflyEffect: Built largely as a Depression-era relief scheme, the Story Bridge gave thousands of unemployed Brisbane workers paid jobs during its construction, though several men died on the project. It opened as a toll bridge and remains the longest cantilever bridge in Australia, now heritage-listed.

evt-07-06-1989-1989-tel-aviv-jerusalem-b.scenario: It is 6 July 1989, and reports reach investigators of a horrific crash: Egged bus 405, en route from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem, has plunged off a cliff into a ravine near Qiryat Ye'arim, killing many passengers.
evt-07-06-1989-1989-tel-aviv-jerusalem-b.prompt: What do investigators determine caused the bus to plunge off the road?

choices.text: The bus suffered sudden brake failure on the mountain road
An explosive device detonated beneath the bus
The driver fell asleep at the wheel
A militant grabbed the steering wheel and forced the bus off the road

evt-07-06-1989-1989-tel-aviv-jerusalem-b.butterflyEffect: Investigators found that Abd al-Hadi Ghanim, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad militant, had seized the steering wheel and forced the bus off the cliff. The group claimed responsibility, and the attack became one of the deadliest against Israeli civilians to that date, hardening security measures on public transport in the years that followed.

evt-07-06-1995-bosnian-war.scenario: It's July 6, 1995, in the besieged Srebrenica enclave. You are among the Dutch UN peacekeepers as Bosnian Serb forces under General Ratko Mladić begin shelling the safe area and pressing in on its defenses.
evt-07-06-1995-bosnian-war.prompt: What should the Dutch commander urgently request from NATO as the enclave's perimeter fails?

choices.text: Full withdrawal of all peacekeepers without engaging
A call for additional UN ground troop reinforcements only
Immediate NATO air strikes on the advancing Bosnian Serb forces
Direct ceasefire negotiations with Mladić alone

evt-07-06-1995-bosnian-war.butterflyEffect: Requests for NATO air strikes were delayed and ultimately limited, and Mladić's forces overran the enclave within days. The fall of Srebrenica led to the massacre of thousands of Bosniak men and boys, later judged genocide by international courts, and the failure of the response drove sweeping reforms in UN peacekeeping mandates and NATO's willingness to intervene in the Balkans.

evt-07-06-1996-mcdonnell-douglas-md-80.scenario: It's July 6, 1996, at Pensacola Regional Airport. You are aboard Delta Air Lines Flight 1288, an MD-88, accelerating down the runway when the left engine suddenly disintegrates, hurling debris toward the fuselage.
evt-07-06-1996-mcdonnell-douglas-md-80.prompt: What happens in the seconds after the engine failure during the takeoff roll?

choices.text: The crew safely aborts, but flying engine debris kills two people
All aboard evacuate with no injuries at all
The aircraft takes off normally on the remaining engine
The plane explodes fully on the runway

evt-07-06-1996-mcdonnell-douglas-md-80.butterflyEffect: The crew aborted the takeoff safely, but shrapnel from the disintegrating engine pierced the cabin, killing two passengers and injuring several others on the ground and aboard. Investigators traced the failure to a fatigue crack in the titanium fan hub, leading the FAA to order stricter inspection regimes for that engine family.

evt-07-06-1997-the-troubles.scenario: It is July 1997 in Portadown, and the Orange Order is set to march from Drumcree Church back along the Garvaghy Road, a route running through a nationalist Catholic neighbourhood. Tension has built for years over whether the march should be allowed to pass.
evt-07-06-1997-the-troubles.prompt: What does the RUC decide to do to get the march through?

choices.text: Ban the march outright for that year
Reroute the march entirely away from Catholic neighbourhoods
Force the march through under heavy police protection, sparking nationalist riots
Allow the march only if marchers surrendered their sashes and banners

evt-07-06-1997-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The RUC forced the march through Garvaghy Road under heavy security in the early hours, and the decision triggered several nights of rioting across Northern Ireland. The unrest deepened sectarian mistrust even as the peace process advanced, and it helped push authorities toward creating the Parades Commission the following year to arbitrate contentious marches.

evt-07-06-2006-martin-rios-murderer.scenario: You are a Buenos Aires police officer called to Belgrano on 6 July 2006 after another shooting, the latest in a string of unexplained gun attacks in the neighborhood over the past year.
evt-07-06-2006-martin-rios-murderer.prompt: What did the investigation into this final, deadliest attack ultimately lead to?

choices.text: Closure of the case as an isolated gang shooting with no further leads
Identification and arrest of a serial shooter later linked to prior attacks
Dismissal of the shootings as unrelated random incidents
Confirmation the attacker had already fled the country

evt-07-06-2006-martin-rios-murderer.butterflyEffect: Investigators eventually identified and arrested Martín Ríos, whose spree had killed one person and wounded several others across multiple attacks. His case, and his later diagnosis, fueled public debate in Argentina over gun licensing and gaps in mental health monitoring.

evt-07-06-2006-nathu-la.scenario: You stand at the Nathu La barrier on the Sikkim–Tibet border on 6 July 2006, watching officials remove barbed wire that has sealed the pass since the 1962 war.
evt-07-06-2006-nathu-la.prompt: What did the reopening actually permit across this Himalayan crossing?

choices.text: Tourist visas for foreign nationals to cross into Tibet
A joint military exercise between Indian and Chinese troops
Restricted seasonal trade in specified goods under strict quotas
Unrestricted free trade and open migration between the two countries

evt-07-06-2006-nathu-la.butterflyEffect: Nathu La reopened for limited, quota-based border trade in traditional goods like wool, borax and silk, the first such crossing to reopen since 1962. It became a symbol of thawing India-China relations, though it has been closed repeatedly during later flare-ups, including the 2017 Doklam standoff.

evt-07-06-2009-jadranka-kosor.scenario: It is July 2009 in Zagreb. Prime Minister Ivo Sanader has just resigned without warning, and the ruling HDZ party must quickly choose a successor to steer Croatia through its final EU accession talks.
evt-07-06-2009-jadranka-kosor.prompt: Who does the party turn to, becoming Croatia's first female prime minister?

choices.text: Jadranka Kosor
Andrija Hebrang
Vesna Pusić
Kolinda Grabar-Kitarović

evt-07-06-2009-jadranka-kosor.butterflyEffect: The party chose Jadranka Kosor, a former journalist and deputy PM, who became Croatia's first woman to hold the office. She led the government through the completion of EU accession negotiations, and Croatia signed its accession treaty in 2011, joining the European Union in 2013.

evt-07-06-2013-boeing-777.scenario: It's July 6, 2013, over San Francisco Bay. You are flying Asiana Flight 214, a Boeing 777, on a visual approach into SFO with the runway's glideslope beacon out of service, and your airspeed is falling below what final approach requires.
evt-07-06-2013-boeing-777.prompt: What must the crew do as the aircraft becomes dangerously slow on short final?

choices.text: Continue the approach, trusting the autothrottle to hold speed
Add power immediately and execute a go-around
Extend the flaps further to slow the descent
Request an immediate runway change from the tower

evt-07-06-2013-boeing-777.butterflyEffect: The crew failed to catch the decaying airspeed in time, and the jet struck the seawall short of the runway, killing three people in the first fatal crash of a 777. Investigators found the crew had over-relied on automation that was not actually maintaining speed, prompting airlines worldwide to reinforce manual-flying proficiency training.

evt-07-06-2013-lac-megantic-rail-disaste.scenario: It's the night of July 5, 2013. You are the lone engineer of a runaway-prone freight train hauling 73 tank cars of crude oil, parked on a descending grade above Lac-Mégantic before you leave it unattended for the night.
evt-07-06-2013-lac-megantic-rail-disaste.prompt: What must you do to secure the loaded train safely without a crew present?

choices.text: Trust the locomotive's automatic air brakes since hand brakes are only a backup
Set enough hand brakes alone to hold the train without depending on air pressure
Leave one crew member aboard overnight to monitor the brakes
Chain the wheels manually to the rails as a permanent measure

evt-07-06-2013-lac-megantic-rail-disaste.butterflyEffect: The engineer set only seven hand brakes, relying on the idling locomotive's air brakes to hold the rest. When firefighters extinguished a locomotive fire and shut the engine down, air pressure bled away, the brakes released, and the train rolled downhill into town and exploded, killing 47 people. The disaster forced new North American rules on hand-brake minimums, crew size, and the phase-out of the tank car design involved.

evt-07-06-2021-antonov-an-26.scenario: You are the captain of the An-26 turboprop approaching Palana's coastal airstrip on 6 July 2021. Thick fog has swallowed the runway and radio contact with the tower is patchy.
evt-07-06-2021-antonov-an-26.prompt: With visibility near zero, what should you do before continuing the approach?

choices.text: Descend below the cloud layer using visual cues from the coastline
Continue the instrument approach exactly as briefed
Abort the approach and divert to an airport with clear weather
Circle indefinitely waiting for fog to lift without declaring an emergency

evt-07-06-2021-antonov-an-26.butterflyEffect: The crew continued their descent through the fog and the aircraft struck terrain short of the runway, killing all 28 people aboard. The disaster renewed scrutiny of ageing Soviet-era transport aircraft and lax instrument-approach discipline at remote Russian Far East airstrips.

evt-07-06-2022-georgia-guidestones.scenario: You live near Elbert County, Georgia, and are woken at dawn on 6 July 2022 by a loud explosion near the granite monument known as the Georgia Guidestones.
evt-07-06-2022-georgia-guidestones.prompt: What happens to the monument in the aftermath?

choices.text: It is quietly relocated to a museum for preservation
It is repainted with graffiti but left standing
It is partially destroyed by an explosion and then fully demolished for safety
It collapses on its own due to erosion after decades of weathering

evt-07-06-2022-georgia-guidestones.butterflyEffect: A bomb partially destroyed one of the granite slabs, and authorities demolished the remaining structure for safety reasons later that day. No one was ever charged, and the mysterious destruction only intensified decades of conspiracy theories surrounding the monument's origins and purpose.

evt-07-07-1575-anglo-scottish-wars.scenario: You stand at the Redeswire on the border, 7 July 1575, where English Warden Sir John Forster and Scottish Warden Sir John Carmichael meet at a truce day to settle a dispute over a wanted man. Tempers flare between the two parties.
evt-07-07-1575-anglo-scottish-wars.prompt: What happens next at this tense border meeting?

choices.text: Both wardens are arrested by their own governments
The meeting is quietly cancelled without incident
Fighting breaks out between the English and Scottish parties
Both wardens sign a lasting peace treaty on the spot

evt-07-07-1575-anglo-scottish-wars.butterflyEffect: The dispute erupted into open fighting known as the Raid of the Redeswire, leaving several men dead, including an English officer. Both governments moved quickly to disavow the clash to preserve the fragile Anglo-Scottish peace, and it is remembered as one of the last major skirmishes of the Border wars before the 1603 Union of the Crowns.

evt-07-07-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 7 July 1777 in the hills near Hubbardton in the Vermont wilderness. You command the rearguard covering the Continental Army's retreat from Fort Ticonderoga when British and German troops under General Simon Fraser suddenly appear on the road behind you.
evt-07-07-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What must the rearguard do to let the main retreating force escape?

choices.text: Counterattack immediately to retake Fort Ticonderoga
Abandon all baggage and flee without engaging
Stand and fight a delaying action to cover the retreat
Surrender to negotiate safe passage for the army

evt-07-07-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: The Americans turned to fight the delaying action known as the Battle of Hubbardton. Though they suffered a tactical defeat, the stand bought crucial time for the main Continental force to escape southward, a delay that contributed to General Burgoyne's eventual, decisive defeat at Saratoga later that year.

evt-07-07-1911-north-pacific-fur-seal-co.scenario: You are a diplomat in Washington in 1911, watching Pribilof Islands fur seal herds collapse from decades of unregulated pelagic hunting by ships from multiple nations on the open sea.
evt-07-07-1911-north-pacific-fur-seal-co.prompt: What do the United States, Britain, Japan, and Russia agree to do about the crisis?

choices.text: They impose a total hunting ban with no exceptions for any party
They agree to divide the seal populations equally among themselves
They refer the dispute to unilateral national courts for resolution
They agree to ban pelagic sealing and regulate onshore harvests

evt-07-07-1911-north-pacific-fur-seal-co.butterflyEffect: The four powers signed the North Pacific Fur Seal Convention, banning open-water seal hunting while recognizing U.S. jurisdiction over onshore harvesting at the Pribilofs. It became the first international wildlife-conservation treaty, setting a template for later multinational agreements protecting migratory and shared species.

evt-07-07-1937-peel-commission.scenario: It is 7 July 1937, and you sit on the Peel Commission in London, tasked with resolving the violence in Mandatory Palestine after a six-month Arab general strike. Your report is about to be published.
evt-07-07-1937-peel-commission.prompt: What solution does the Commission recommend for Palestine's future?

choices.text: Continue the British Mandate unchanged indefinitely
Partition the territory into separate Arab and Jewish states
Transfer administration entirely to the League of Nations
Hand full sovereignty to a single Arab-led government

evt-07-07-1937-peel-commission.butterflyEffect: The Commission proposed partitioning Palestine into separate Arab and Jewish states, the first official partition plan for the territory. Arab leaders rejected it outright and Zionist leaders accepted it only with reservations, but the idea of partition endured and directly shaped the UN's 1947 partition plan a decade later.

evt-07-07-1985-boris-becker.scenario: You are 17-year-old Boris Becker, an unseeded, unheralded German serving huge and diving for volleys through Wimbledon's fortnight in 1985, with the men's final now in front of you.
evt-07-07-1985-boris-becker.prompt: What actually happens in the final, and what record does it set?

choices.text: He retires injured mid-match and the title is awarded to his opponent
He loses in five sets but wins acclaim for his serve-and-volley style
He wins but is later stripped of the title for a doubles-partner dispute
He wins, becoming the youngest men's champion in Wimbledon history

evt-07-07-1985-boris-becker.butterflyEffect: Becker beat Kevin Curren to become the youngest men's singles champion in Wimbledon history at 17 years, 7 months. The win launched him as tennis's first modern teenage superstar and a fixture of the German-led rivalries that defined men's tennis into the 1990s.

evt-07-07-1991-yugoslav-wars.scenario: It is 7 July 1991 on the Brijuni islands. As a Slovenian delegate, you sit across from Croatian and Yugoslav federal representatives, with European Community mediators pressing all sides to halt the fighting of the Ten-Day War.
evt-07-07-1991-yugoslav-wars.prompt: What concession does the Brioni Agreement extract from Slovenia and Croatia?

choices.text: Croatia cedes disputed border territory to Serbia
Slovenia agrees to remain permanently within Yugoslavia
The JNA is granted permanent bases inside Slovenia
Both agree to a three-month suspension of their independence declarations

evt-07-07-1991-yugoslav-wars.butterflyEffect: Both republics agreed to suspend their declarations of independence for three months while the JNA withdrew from Slovenia. The pause did not hold Yugoslavia together: fighting soon erupted in Croatia, and Slovenia's independence took full effect that October, becoming a model other republics followed as the federation broke apart.

evt-07-07-1992-new-york-court-of-appeals.scenario: It is 1992, and you are a woman in New York charged under a state indecency law that bars females, but not males, from baring their chests in public. Your case has climbed all the way to the state's highest court.
evt-07-07-1992-new-york-court-of-appeals.prompt: How does the New York Court of Appeals rule on the sex-based public nudity law?

choices.text: It upholds the law as a valid public decency measure
It rules the law unconstitutional as applied only to women
It sends the case back without deciding the constitutional question
It rules the law only applies inside private clubs

evt-07-07-1992-new-york-court-of-appeals.butterflyEffect: In People v. Santorelli, the court struck down the law's unequal application, ruling that punishing women but not men for the same act of bare-chestedness violated equal protection. The decision became a foundational precedent later cited by 'Free the Nipple' and gender-equality activists across the United States.

evt-07-07-2003-nasa.scenario: It is 7 July 2003 at Cape Canaveral. You watch a Delta II rocket lift off carrying Opportunity, the second of NASA's twin Mars Exploration Rovers, bound for a plain called Meridiani Planum to search for signs of ancient water.
evt-07-07-2003-nasa.prompt: What does Opportunity's mission ultimately reveal after it lands on Mars?

choices.text: It discovers active volcanic eruptions on the surface
It finds mineral evidence that Mars once had liquid water
It detects breathable oxygen levels in the atmosphere
It finds no evidence of past water anywhere on Mars

evt-07-07-2003-nasa.butterflyEffect: Opportunity landed successfully in January 2004 and found mineral evidence that liquid water once existed on the Martian surface, confirming the planet's wetter past. Designed for a 90-day mission, it kept operating for nearly 15 years, paving the way for later rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance to search for signs of past life.

evt-07-07-2005-7-july-2005-london-bombin.scenario: It is the days after 7 July 2005, when four suicide bombs tore through London's Underground and a bus during the morning rush hour. Police forces across Britain are urgently reassessing how to stop a suicide bomber before detonation.
evt-07-07-2005-7-july-2005-london-bombin.prompt: What controversial policy did British police adopt in the weeks after the bombings?

choices.text: A shoot-to-kill policy for suspected suicide bombers
Mandatory ID cards for all Underground passengers
A nationwide curfew after dark
Permanent closure of the entire Underground network

evt-07-07-2005-7-july-2005-london-bombin.butterflyEffect: Police adopted a shoot-to-kill policy toward suspects believed to be suicide bombers. On 22 July 2005 this led officers to fatally shoot Jean Charles de Menezes, an innocent Brazilian electrician mistaken for a bombing suspect, sparking lasting controversy over the policy's use.

evt-07-07-2011-2011-grand-rapids-shootin.scenario: It is the afternoon of 7 July 2011 in Grand Rapids, Michigan. You are a police officer pursuing Rodrick Dantzler's car after a string of shootings, and his vehicle finally becomes disabled near a wooded highway shoulder where he then takes hostages in a nearby house.
evt-07-07-2011-2011-grand-rapids-shootin.prompt: How does the hours-long standoff that follows actually end?

choices.text: SWAT storms the house and kills him in a shootout
He surrenders peacefully to negotiators
He takes his own life after the hostage standoff
He escapes on foot and evades capture for weeks

evt-07-07-2011-2011-grand-rapids-shootin.butterflyEffect: After holding hostages for several hours, Dantzler took his own life, ending the standoff without further loss of life. The spree, which claimed seven lives including his estranged wife and daughter, prompted local debate over domestic-violence warning signs and police pursuit protocols.
