evt-07-07-2012-2012-krasnodar-krai-flood.scenario: It is the night of 6-7 July 2012 in Krymsk, Krasnodar Krai. As a local official, you watch radar showing months' worth of rain falling in hours, but sounding sirens risks a costly false alarm if the storm passes.
evt-07-07-2012-2012-krasnodar-krai-flood.prompt: What should officials have done as the floodwaters rose overnight?

choices.text: Wait for confirmation from Moscow before alerting residents
Delay any warning until morning to avoid panic
Issue immediate, loud public warnings and begin evacuations at once
Rely on residents to check weather forecasts themselves

evt-07-07-2012-2012-krasnodar-krai-flood.butterflyEffect: Warnings were delayed or never reached many residents, and floodwaters swept through towns like Krymsk while people slept, killing at least 171 people. Public anger over the failed alert system led to arrests of local officials and lasting reforms to Russia's flood-warning protocols.

evt-07-07-2016-united-states-army-reserv.scenario: It is the night of 7 July 2016 in downtown Dallas. A peaceful protest march has just ended when a lone Army Reserve veteran opens fire on police, then barricades himself in a parking garage, exchanging gunfire with officers for hours.
evt-07-07-2016-united-states-army-reserv.prompt: How do Dallas police finally end the armed standoff in the garage?

choices.text: They send in a bomb-disposal robot rigged with an explosive charge
They negotiate a peaceful surrender after several hours
SWAT snipers shoot him through a window
They evacuate and wait for him to run out of ammunition

evt-07-07-2016-united-states-army-reserv.butterflyEffect: After negotiations failed, police used a robot carrying an explosive device to kill the gunman, one of the first known uses of a robot in this way by U.S. law enforcement. Five officers died and several others were wounded, prompting a national debate over policing tactics, officer safety, and the use of robotic force.

evt-07-07-2019-united-states-women-s-nat.scenario: It is the second half of the 2019 World Cup final against the Netherlands. You are the referee reviewing a VAR replay after a Dutch defender's arm blocks a shot inside the box.
evt-07-07-2019-united-states-women-s-nat.prompt: What is the correct call, and what happens next in the match?

choices.text: A penalty is awarded and Rapinoe scores to put the U.S. ahead
A yellow card is issued instead of a penalty
No penalty is given and play continues
The goal is disallowed for offside before the handball occurs

evt-07-07-2019-united-states-women-s-nat.butterflyEffect: The referee awarded a penalty, which Megan Rapinoe converted to open the scoring; Rose Lavelle added a second goal later, giving the U.S. a 2-0 win and its fourth World Cup title. The victory fueled the team's parallel fight for equal pay, which ended in a landmark settlement with U.S. Soccer in 2022.

evt-07-07-2021-haitian-crisis-2018-prese.scenario: It is just after 1 a.m. on 7 July 2021. You are a member of President Jovenel Moïse's security detail at his private residence in Pèlerin when armed men shouting that they are DEA agents storm the gates.
evt-07-07-2021-haitian-crisis-2018-prese.prompt: What actually happens when the armed group breaches the president's residence?

choices.text: Moïse negotiates his surrender and is taken into exile
The gunmen are captured at the gate before reaching the residence
Presidential guards repel the attackers and Moïse escapes unharmed
The attackers kill Moïse and wound his wife before fleeing

evt-07-07-2021-haitian-crisis-2018-prese.butterflyEffect: The gunmen, mostly Colombian mercenaries, killed Moïse and wounded First Lady Martine Moïse. The assassination deepened Haiti's political vacuum, empowering armed gangs and eventually prompting an international security mission years later, while the killers' full motives remain disputed in ongoing trials.

evt-07-08-1758-french-and-indian-war.scenario: It's July 8, 1758, near Fort Carillon. You command a British force of roughly 16,000 men facing a much smaller French garrison under the Marquis de Montcalm, who has built log breastworks across the approach.
evt-07-08-1758-french-and-indian-war.prompt: What did General Abercrombie order his troops to do?

choices.text: Wait for artillery to be brought up before attacking
Launch repeated frontal infantry assaults directly against the fortified French lines
Negotiate a truce with Montcalm
Withdraw and attempt to flank the position

evt-07-08-1758-french-and-indian-war.butterflyEffect: The frontal assaults were repelled with devastating British losses—nearly 2,000 casualties against a few hundred French. The humiliating defeat at Carillon was soon overshadowed when British fortunes reversed with the capture of Louisbourg and Fort Frontenac later that year.

evt-07-08-1874-north-west-mounted-police.scenario: It's July 8, 1874, at Fort Dufferin. You command part of a column of over 300 North-West Mounted Police setting out across open prairie toward the Cypress Hills, with maps sparse and water growing scarce.
evt-07-08-1874-north-west-mounted-police.prompt: As horses weaken on the dry prairie, what do you decide to do?

choices.text: Turn the whole expedition back to Fort Dufferin
Split the column, sending the weaker element to resupply while the rest push west
Halt the march indefinitely and wait for rain
Keep the entire column together and press on regardless

evt-07-08-1874-north-west-mounted-police.butterflyEffect: At Roche Percée the force actually split, sending exhausted men and horses to establish a post near Swan River while the main column pushed on toward the Cypress Hills and beyond. That surviving column went on to found Fort Macleod, allowing the NWMP to shut down the whisky trade and open talks with Blackfoot leaders, shaping the force that became the RCMP.

evt-07-08-1947-roswell-incident.scenario: It's July 8, 1947, at Roswell Army Air Field. Debris recovered from a nearby ranch has just been examined, and headquarters wants a statement issued to the press today.
evt-07-08-1947-roswell-incident.prompt: What does the base announce to the waiting reporters?

choices.text: It's just a weather balloon, nothing more
We have recovered a flying disc
It appears to be wreckage from a Soviet aircraft
We cannot comment, the matter is classified

evt-07-08-1947-roswell-incident.butterflyEffect: The Army's statement that it had recovered a 'flying disc' made international headlines, but was retracted within a day in favor of a weather balloon story to protect the secret Project Mogul, which monitored Soviet nuclear tests. That contradiction and the secrecy behind it fueled decades of UFO conspiracy theories about a government cover-up.

evt-07-08-1962-1962-rangoon-university-p.scenario: It's the morning of July 8, 1962, the day after troops fired on demonstrators at Rangoon University. You watch as military engineers move toward the historic Students' Union building with explosives.
evt-07-08-1962-1962-rangoon-university-p.prompt: What do the soldiers do to the Students' Union building?

choices.text: They seal it off but leave it standing
They hand it back to students to repair
They blow it up, destroying it completely
They convert it into a military barracks

evt-07-08-1962-1962-rangoon-university-p.butterflyEffect: The military demolished the building entirely, hoping to erase a structure that had symbolized anti-colonial nationalism since the 1920s. Instead its destruction became a lasting emblem of resistance to military rule, remembered and invoked again during the pro-democracy uprisings of 1988 and 2021.

evt-07-08-1965-canadian-pacific-air-line.scenario: Days after a DC-6B bound for Whitehorse exploded in mid-air near 100 Mile House, you are an investigator sifting through scattered wreckage, looking for the blast's point of origin.
evt-07-08-1965-canadian-pacific-air-line.prompt: What does the physical evidence tell investigators caused the explosion?

choices.text: An engine fire spread to the fuel tanks
A bomb had been planted aboard the aircraft
Metal fatigue caused the fuselage to fail
The plane collided with another aircraft

evt-07-08-1965-canadian-pacific-air-line.butterflyEffect: The inquest concluded that a bomb had destroyed the aircraft, killing all 52 aboard, but the person responsible and their motive were never identified. The case remains one of Canada's unsolved aviation mysteries and pushed airlines toward tighter scrutiny of checked baggage in the years that followed.

evt-07-08-1966-mwambutsa-iv-of-burundi.scenario: It's July 8, 1966. You are King Mwambutsa IV of Burundi, currently abroad seeking medical treatment in Europe, when word reaches you that your own son has moved against your throne back home.
evt-07-08-1966-mwambutsa-iv-of-burundi.prompt: What did Prince Charles Ndizeye do next?

choices.text: Restored his father to the throne after a brief show of force
Called for immediate multi-party elections
Fled the country himself to avoid civil war
Proclaimed himself King Ntare V with the backing of army officer Michel Micombero

evt-07-08-1966-mwambutsa-iv-of-burundi.butterflyEffect: Ndizeye ruled briefly as Ntare V, but within months Prime Minister Michel Micombero seized power himself in November 1966, abolished the monarchy, and declared Burundi a republic. Ntare V was later killed in 1972, and Micombero ruled the new republic for years.

evt-07-08-1972-mossad.scenario: It is the morning of 8 July 1972 in Beirut. You are Ghassan Kanafani, Palestinian novelist and PFLP spokesman, about to drive your seventeen-year-old niece on an errand in the car parked outside your apartment.
evt-07-08-1972-mossad.prompt: What happens as you start the car's engine?

choices.text: The engine starts normally, but a hidden bomb detonates
A sniper shoots you from a nearby rooftop
Armed gunmen ambush you on the street instead
You notice tampering and escape unharmed

evt-07-08-1972-mossad.butterflyEffect: A bomb planted by Mossad agents in the car detonated, killing Kanafani and his niece Lamees Najim instantly. His assassination, ordered in retaliation for the Lod Airport massacre, made him a martyr whose fiction—especially Men in the Sun—gained lasting influence in Palestinian literature and politics.

evt-07-08-1982-saddam-hussein.scenario: It's July 8, 1982, in Dujail, Iraq. Gunmen from a Shia Islamist group open fire on your motorcade as you tour the town, and you survive the ambush unharmed.
evt-07-08-1982-saddam-hussein.prompt: What did Saddam order in retaliation for the attack?

choices.text: A public amnesty for the town's residents
A mass reprisal against Dujail, including executions and the destruction of orchards
A formal investigation handled entirely by civilian courts
An immediate ceasefire with Iran

evt-07-08-1982-saddam-hussein.butterflyEffect: Saddam's regime executed and imprisoned hundreds of Dujail residents and razed the town's date orchards. Decades later this massacre became the basis of the first trial against him after his 2003 capture, and he was convicted and hanged for it in December 2006.

evt-07-08-1994-kim-jong-il.scenario: It is 8 July 1994 in Pyongyang. Kim Il Sung, North Korea's founding leader, has just died, and you are a senior Workers' Party official awaiting word on succession.
evt-07-08-1994-kim-jong-il.prompt: What happens to leadership in the years following Kim Il Sung's death?

choices.text: The party holds open elections for a new leader
Kim Il Sung's brother takes over immediately
The military stages a coup and installs a new general
Kim Jong Il gradually assumes power as the designated successor

evt-07-08-1994-kim-jong-il.butterflyEffect: Kim Jong Il, already groomed as heir, gradually assumed formal titles over several years, notably leaving the presidency permanently reserved for his father as 'Eternal President.' He entrenched a 'military-first' (Songun) policy even as famine, the Arduous March, devastated the country in the mid-1990s.

evt-07-08-1994-space-shuttle-columbia.scenario: It's July 8, 1994, and you are a mission specialist strapped into Columbia's Spacelab module as STS-65 lifts off, carrying dozens of experiments contributed by researchers from multiple nations.
evt-07-08-1994-space-shuttle-columbia.prompt: What is this mission's primary purpose once you reach orbit?

choices.text: Conduct microgravity science experiments for international partners
Service and repair the Hubble Space Telescope
Test a new generation of shuttle main engines
Deploy a new communications satellite

evt-07-08-1994-space-shuttle-columbia.butterflyEffect: STS-65 carried the International Microgravity Laboratory-2, running experiments for scientists from over a dozen countries and setting, at the time, the longest Space Shuttle flight duration. The mission's cooperative science model helped build the international partnerships that would later underpin research aboard the International Space Station.

evt-07-08-2011-space-shuttle-atlantis.scenario: It's July 8, 2011, at Kennedy Space Center. You are one of four astronauts strapped into Atlantis for STS-135, the very last scheduled flight of NASA's Space Shuttle program, watched by a nation uncertain what comes next for American spaceflight.
evt-07-08-2011-space-shuttle-atlantis.prompt: What actually followed the shuttle program's end?

choices.text: NASA immediately launched a new shuttle successor vehicle
The ISS was abandoned without shuttle support
NASA relied on Russian Soyuz rockets to reach the ISS for nearly a decade
Private companies took over all NASA missions within a year

evt-07-08-2011-space-shuttle-atlantis.butterflyEffect: For nine years, American astronauts flew to the ISS only aboard Russian Soyuz spacecraft, at a cost of tens of millions of dollars per seat. That gap ended in 2020 when SpaceX's Crew Dragon, developed under NASA's Commercial Crew Program, restored U.S. human spaceflight capability from American soil.

evt-07-08-2014-brazil-national-football-.scenario: It's July 8, 2014, in Belo Horizonte. You are head coach Luiz Felipe Scolari, sending your Brazil squad out for a World Cup semifinal against Germany without the injured Neymar and suspended captain Thiago Silva.
evt-07-08-2014-brazil-national-football-.prompt: What happened in the opening minutes of the match?

choices.text: The match stayed scoreless until extra time
Brazil's defense held firm despite the missing players
Germany scored five goals in under 20 minutes on the way to a 7-1 rout
Brazil took an early lead and controlled the match

evt-07-08-2014-brazil-national-football-.butterflyEffect: The 7-1 defeat, remembered in Brazil as the 'Mineirazo,' equaled the country's worst-ever loss and triggered Scolari's dismissal along with a national reckoning over Brazilian football's decline. Germany went on to win the tournament days later.

evt-07-08-2022-shinzo-abe.scenario: It is 8 July 2022 in Nara. Former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe is giving an open-air campaign speech on a street corner ahead of upper house elections, standing close to the public with no barrier behind him.
evt-07-08-2022-shinzo-abe.prompt: What does his security detail's positioning reflect about Japanese political norms?

choices.text: Plainclothes snipers watch from surrounding rooftops
Heavy barricades and armored vehicles surround the podium
Minimal crowd barriers, reflecting Japan's low-key approach to politician security
A private security firm screens all attendees with metal detectors

evt-07-08-2022-shinzo-abe.butterflyEffect: A gunman fired an improvised shotgun from behind, fatally wounding Abe—Japan's traditionally light security for politicians left him exposed. The assassin's stated motive, revenge over his family's ruin from donations to the Unification Church, exposed deep LDP ties to the church and triggered a political scandal and resignations.

evt-07-09-551-551-beirut-earthquake.scenario: You live in a coastal town near Berytus on July 9, 551, when a violent earthquake shakes the harbor and, moments later, you watch the sea pull back unnaturally far from the shore.
evt-07-09-551-551-beirut-earthquake.prompt: What should you do when you see the sea retreat like this?

choices.text: Flee immediately to high ground away from the shore
Rush to the harbor to secure the boats
Gather valuables left exposed on the newly bared seabed
Wait calmly to see if the sea returns to normal

evt-07-09-551-551-beirut-earthquake.butterflyEffect: A massive tsunami followed, devastating the coastal towns of Phoenicia and killing an estimated 30,000 people at Berytus alone according to a contemporary pilgrim's account. The disaster disrupted Mediterranean trade along the Levantine coast for years and remains one of the deadliest recorded tsunamis in the region's history.

evt-07-09-1640-virginia-governor-s-counc.scenario: It is 9 July 1640 in Jamestown. Three indentured servants who fled to Maryland have been recaptured and stand before you, a member of the Governor's Council deciding their punishment.
evt-07-09-1640-virginia-governor-s-counc.prompt: What sentence do you hand down to John Punch, the African servant, compared to his two European companions?

choices.text: All three receive identical extended terms of servitude
All three are executed as an example to other servants
All three are fined and released without further punishment
Punch alone is sentenced to servitude for life

evt-07-09-1640-virginia-governor-s-counc.butterflyEffect: The council extended the two European servants' indentures by four years but sentenced Punch, the African, to serve his master for the rest of his life. Historians regard this as one of the earliest legal distinctions based on race in English North America, a precedent that helped harden the colony's later system of race-based chattel slavery.

evt-07-09-1790-russo-swedish-war-1788-17.scenario: You command the Swedish fleet near the Svensksund skerries in 1790. The Russian fleet bearing down on you is far larger, but the water here is shallow, narrow, and treacherous for big ships.
evt-07-09-1790-russo-swedish-war-1788-17.prompt: How do you use the terrain to defeat the larger Russian fleet?

choices.text: Lure the Russian fleet into the narrow, shallow waters where their larger ships would struggle
Wait offshore for reinforcements from Sweden's allies before engaging
Retreat immediately to open sea to avoid the larger fleet
Send envoys to negotiate a truce before any battle began

evt-07-09-1790-russo-swedish-war-1788-17.butterflyEffect: The Swedes lured the Russian fleet into the cramped waters of Svensksund, where many larger vessels ran aground or were shredded by Swedish gunboats and galleys, resulting in a crushing Swedish victory. The defeat pushed Russia to the negotiating table, producing the Treaty of Värälä weeks later, which ended the war without territorial change and let Gustav III turn his attention to the growing crisis in revolutionary France.

evt-07-09-1811-david-thompson-explorer.scenario: It is 9 July 1811, and you have just reached the confluence of the Columbia and Snake Rivers after a grueling overland trek from the North West Company's posts. You know an American-backed expedition is racing to establish claims on the lower Columbia before you.
evt-07-09-1811-david-thompson-explorer.prompt: What do you do to assert British claims to the region?

choices.text: Immediately construct a fortified trading post to physically hold the ground
Sign a formal treaty with local tribal leaders ceding the land to Britain
Wait for reinforcements before making any claim
Post a written notice claiming the territory for Britain and the North West Company

evt-07-09-1811-david-thompson-explorer.butterflyEffect: Thompson posted a notice claiming the district for Great Britain and the North West Company, but he arrived at the Columbia's mouth months after the Pacific Fur Company had already built Fort Astoria. This near-miss weakened Britain's territorial claims and fed decades of Anglo-American boundary disputes, eventually settled by the Oregon Treaty of 1846.

evt-07-09-1850-zachary-taylor.scenario: It is July 9, 1850, and President Zachary Taylor has just died after a sudden stomach illness. As Vice President, the Constitution makes you next in line, and the nation waits to see what you will do.
evt-07-09-1850-zachary-taylor.prompt: As Millard Fillmore, what is your immediate constitutional duty?

choices.text: Call for a special national election
Wait for Congress to formally appoint a new president
Take the oath of office immediately and assume the presidency
Defer the presidency to the Speaker of the House

evt-07-09-1850-zachary-taylor.butterflyEffect: Fillmore took the presidential oath that same day and, unlike Taylor, threw his support behind the Compromise of 1850, including the Fugitive Slave Act. This shift helped delay sectional conflict over slavery for another decade, postponing the Civil War.

evt-07-09-1937-nitrocellulose.scenario: It's the night of 9 July 1937 at a 20th Century Fox film storage vault in Little Ferry, New Jersey. Decomposing nitrate reels have begun to smoke, and you know nitrate film burns even underwater and cannot be smothered.
evt-07-09-1937-nitrocellulose.prompt: What is the correct response to a nitrate film fire breaking out in the vault?

choices.text: Carry the burning reels outside by hand to save the footage
Seal the vault doors shut to starve the fire of oxygen
Evacuate immediately and alert the fire department, since water and enclosure won't stop it
Throw water on the smoking reels to extinguish them before they spread

evt-07-09-1937-nitrocellulose.butterflyEffect: The vault fire destroyed the building and most of Fox's pre-1932 negatives, wiping out many silent-era films forever. It remains one of the largest single losses of early film history, a major reason so much silent cinema survives today only in fragments or not at all.

evt-07-09-1955-albert-einstein.scenario: It is July 9, 1955, three months after Einstein's death, and you are among eleven scientists, including Bertrand Russell, releasing a statement Einstein signed before he died, warning the world of the existential danger posed by nuclear weapons.
evt-07-09-1955-albert-einstein.prompt: What does the manifesto urge world leaders and scientists to pursue?

choices.text: Renounce war and seek peaceful resolution of conflicts
Accelerate the arms race to ensure deterrence
Push for unilateral disarmament by only the United States
Keep nuclear research secret from all governments

evt-07-09-1955-albert-einstein.butterflyEffect: The Russell–Einstein Manifesto led directly to the founding of the Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs, which brought scientists from both sides of the Cold War together to discuss nuclear disarmament. The organization later won the 1995 Nobel Peace Prize.

evt-07-09-1962-starfish-prime.scenario: It is 9 July 1962, and you are monitoring instruments at a Pacific tracking station as a thermonuclear warhead detonates 400 kilometers above Johnston Atoll, far higher than any weapon test before it.
evt-07-09-1962-starfish-prime.prompt: What happened in the hours after the Starfish Prime detonation?

choices.text: The electromagnetic pulse knocked out streetlights and telephone equipment in Honolulu and damaged orbiting satellites
The detonation triggered a tsunami warning across the Pacific basin
Only satellites already in orbit near the blast were affected, with no ground effects
No measurable effects were detected anywhere outside the immediate test zone

evt-07-09-1962-starfish-prime.butterflyEffect: The blast's electromagnetic pulse knocked out streetlights and damaged phone equipment in Honolulu, roughly 1,300 kilometers away, and created an artificial radiation belt that disabled or destroyed several satellites, including one of the first commercial ones. The unexpected scale of the damage helped push the US and Soviet Union toward the 1963 Partial Test Ban Treaty, banning atmospheric and space nuclear tests.

evt-07-09-1981-nintendo.scenario: It is 1982, and you are president of Nintendo of America. Universal City Studios has just sued you, claiming your new arcade hit Donkey Kong infringes their King Kong trademark and could destroy the game's American rollout.
evt-07-09-1981-nintendo.prompt: How do you respond to Universal's lawsuit?

choices.text: Fight the lawsuit in court, arguing there was no real infringement
Withdraw the game from the American market entirely
Quietly settle and pay Universal ongoing royalties
Rename the game and its characters to avoid any legal dispute

evt-07-09-1981-nintendo.butterflyEffect: Nintendo fought the case in court and won: in Universal City Studios, Inc. v. Nintendo Co., Ltd. (1984), the court found no infringement, ruling Universal did not even hold clear rights to the King Kong story. The victory protected Donkey Kong and its new hero, later renamed Mario, and set an early precedent shielding video game makers from broad trademark claims.

evt-07-09-1995-sri-lankan-civil-war.scenario: It is 9 July 1995 in the Jaffna peninsula. Amid intense fighting, authorities have urged civilians to seek safety in places of worship believed to be off-limits to attack, and hundreds gather inside St. Peter's Church in Navaly.
evt-07-09-1995-sri-lankan-civil-war.prompt: What happened to the civilians sheltering inside the church that day?

choices.text: A ceasefire was declared and the area was left untouched by fighting
International peacekeepers arrived and secured the site from harm
The church was bombed by Sri Lankan forces, killing many of the civilians sheltering inside
LTTE fighters evacuated everyone to safety before any attack occurred

evt-07-09-1995-sri-lankan-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Sri Lankan Air Force bombed the church, killing over a hundred civilians who had sought refuge there believing it would be spared. The Navaly church bombing drew international condemnation, intensified scrutiny of the military's conduct toward civilians, and became a lasting symbol invoked by Tamil communities and human rights advocates in the years that followed.

evt-07-09-2006-italy-national-football-t.scenario: It is July 9, 2006, in Berlin, and the World Cup Final between Italy and France is deadlocked at 1-1 after extra time, made more dramatic by Zinedine Zidane's ejection for headbutting Materazzi.
evt-07-09-2006-italy-national-football-t.prompt: How does Italy ultimately claim the trophy?

choices.text: France being disqualified after Zidane's red card
Winning the penalty shootout 5-3
Scoring a golden goal in extra time
Advancing on the away-goals rule

evt-07-09-2006-italy-national-football-t.butterflyEffect: Italy won the ensuing penalty shootout 5-3 to claim their fourth World Cup title. Zidane's headbutt became one of the most infamous moments in World Cup history, an ignominious end to his celebrated international career.

evt-07-09-2006-s7-airlines-flight-778.scenario: You are the flight crew of an Airbus A310 landing at Irkutsk on the rain-dampened morning of July 9, 2006, when one engine unexpectedly spools toward takeoff power instead of reversing, and the aircraft refuses to slow down.
evt-07-09-2006-s7-airlines-flight-778.prompt: What is the critical action needed to prevent a runway overrun?

choices.text: Shut down the malfunctioning engine immediately
Deploy the landing gear brakes only after full stop of engines
Increase braking pressure and wait for the engine to correct itself
Radio air traffic control and continue the landing as planned

evt-07-09-2006-s7-airlines-flight-778.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew failed to shut down the malfunctioning engine in time, and the aircraft overran the runway, crashed through the perimeter fence, and struck garages, killing 125 people. The disaster prompted renewed scrutiny of A310 thrust-reverser systems and crew procedures for rejected landings in Russian aviation.

evt-07-09-2011-south-sudan.scenario: It is 9 July 2011 in Juba. Crowds gather to celebrate the birth of a new nation, months after a referendum in the south delivered an overwhelming vote to break from Sudan following decades of civil war.
evt-07-09-2011-south-sudan.prompt: What process directly enabled South Sudan's independence this day?

choices.text: Colonial-era borders were redrawn by Britain
A popular referendum following the 2005 peace agreement
Southern rebel forces militarily conquered Khartoum
A UN Security Council resolution partitioned Sudan by decree

evt-07-09-2011-south-sudan.butterflyEffect: The 2011 referendum, guaranteed by the 2005 Comprehensive Peace Agreement that ended Sudan's second civil war, saw nearly 99% vote for secession, making South Sudan the world's newest country. Yet within two years, a power struggle between President Salva Kiir and Vice President Riek Machar plunged the fledgling nation into a devastating civil war.

evt-07-10-645-soga-clan.scenario: It is 645 at the Yamato court. You are Prince Naka no Oe, watching Soga no Iruka sit before Empress Kōgyoku during an audience with Korean envoys, knowing his family's grip on the throne must be broken now or never.
evt-07-10-645-soga-clan.prompt: What do you do to end Soga no Iruka's power?

choices.text: Poison his food before the ceremony begins
Have him arrested publicly by palace guards
Assassinate Iruka openly during the court audience
Negotiate a marriage alliance to weaken his influence

evt-07-10-645-soga-clan.butterflyEffect: Naka no Oe's men struck Iruka down in the imperial court itself, and his father surrendered the next day. The killing broke Soga dominance and launched the Taika Reforms, which centralized power around the emperor and reshaped Japanese governance for centuries.

evt-07-10-1372-treaty-of-tagilde.scenario: It's 10 July 1372 in the Portuguese village of Tagilde. You represent King Ferdinand I of Portugal, meeting envoys of John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster, who claims the Castilian throne and offers English military backing against Castile.
evt-07-10-1372-treaty-of-tagilde.prompt: What should Portugal do to secure English support against Castile?

choices.text: Demand English troops occupy Portuguese territory before any treaty is signed
Decline any alliance and remain strictly neutral in the Castilian succession dispute
Sign the agreement, binding Portugal and the English claimant in mutual alliance
Break off talks and instead seek an alliance with Castile itself

evt-07-10-1372-treaty-of-tagilde.butterflyEffect: The Treaty of Tagilde laid the legal foundation for the Anglo-Portuguese Alliance, confirmed by further treaties in 1373 and 1386. That alliance has never been broken and remains the oldest continuously active treaty relationship in the world, later invoked in both World Wars.

evt-07-10-1553-lady-jane-grey.scenario: It is 10 July 1553. Edward VI has just died, and his will names his cousin Jane Grey as successor, bypassing his half-sisters. As a Privy Councillor, you must decide whose claim to back before Mary Tudor's supporters can rally.
evt-07-10-1553-lady-jane-grey.prompt: What does the Privy Council do at this moment?

choices.text: Declare a regency council until the succession is settled by Parliament
Refuse to act and wait for the King's council in exile
Proclaim Jane Grey queen as Edward's will instructed
Immediately proclaim Mary Tudor as the rightful heir

evt-07-10-1553-lady-jane-grey.butterflyEffect: The Council proclaimed Jane queen, but support collapsed within days as nobles rallied to Mary Tudor. Jane was deposed after just nine days and later executed for treason in 1554, cementing Mary's Catholic restoration.

evt-07-10-1645-english-civil-war.scenario: It is 10 July 1645 near Langport in Somerset. You command Parliament's cavalry, facing George Goring's Royalist army across boggy ground, with a narrow lane held by musketeers blocking your advance.
evt-07-10-1645-english-civil-war.prompt: How does the New Model Army force its way across to break Goring's line?

choices.text: March the whole army around the hills to outflank Goring
Bombard the Royalist position with artillery for a day first
Send cavalry charging directly down the defended lane
Offer Goring terms for a negotiated withdrawal

evt-07-10-1645-english-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Parliamentarian cavalry charged down the narrow, musket-lined lane and broke through, routing the Royalist force. The defeat destroyed the last significant Royalist field army in the west, opening the way for Parliament to take Bristol and effectively deciding the First Civil War.

evt-07-10-1668-anglo-spanish-war-1654-16.scenario: It is July 1668. You sail with Henry Morgan's privateer fleet toward Portobelo, one of Spain's most heavily fortified silver ports in Panama, hoping to seize its treasure before Spanish reinforcements arrive.
evt-07-10-1668-anglo-spanish-war-1654-16.prompt: How does Morgan's force break the city's defenses?

choices.text: Storm the main gate in a direct frontal charge
Bribe the Spanish garrison commander to open the gates
Force captured religious captives to carry ladders as human shields
Bombard the fort from ships until it surrendered

evt-07-10-1668-anglo-spanish-war-1654-16.butterflyEffect: Morgan's men forced captured priests and nuns to carry scaling ladders against the fort, breaking Spanish resistance and taking the city. The huge ransom he extracted enraged Madrid, embarrassed London's peace diplomacy, and only deepened England's reliance on privateers against Spain's colonies.

evt-07-10-1806-sepoy.scenario: It's the night of 10 July 1806 at Vellore Fort in southern India. Sepoys of the Madras Army, enraged by new East India Company regulations banning caste marks and beards while requiring a turban resembling a European hat, have just stormed the fort and killed dozens of British officers.
evt-07-10-1806-sepoy.prompt: How did the East India Company respond to crush the mutiny at Vellore?

choices.text: Colonel Rollo Gillespie led a relief force from Arcot that retook the fort within hours
The mutiny spread to Madras before being suppressed a month later
British troops besieged the fort for a week before it surrendered
The Company negotiated a truce and withdrew the regulations immediately

evt-07-10-1806-sepoy.butterflyEffect: Colonel Rollo Gillespie led a rapid cavalry charge from nearby Arcot and retook the fort within hours, and the rebellion was crushed with hundreds of sepoys killed in reprisal. The Company quietly rescinded the offending dress regulations, but the episode foreshadowed the far larger Indian Rebellion of 1857, when similar grievances over cultural and religious interference exploded into nationwide revolt.

evt-07-10-1913-furnace-creek-california.scenario: It's midday on 10 July 1913 at Greenland Ranch, deep in Death Valley. The thermometer keeps climbing toward a reading no one has ever recorded, and you still have chores and animals to tend outside.
evt-07-10-1913-furnace-creek-california.prompt: What should you do to survive the extreme afternoon heat?

choices.text: Rest in shade, drink water, and avoid strenuous outdoor work until evening
Climb to higher ground immediately, assuming altitude will bring instant relief
Push through the ranch chores as usual, since the desert heat is nothing new
Head toward the nearest creek for a midday swim to cool off

evt-07-10-1913-furnace-creek-california.butterflyEffect: The reading of 134°F (56.7°C) was accepted as the highest air temperature ever officially recorded on Earth. It cemented Death Valley's reputation as one of the planet's most extreme environments, though modern meteorologists have since raised doubts about the accuracy of that 1913 measurement.

evt-07-10-1921-irish-war-of-independence.scenario: It is 10 July 1921, the day after a truce was agreed between the IRA and British forces. You are an IRA volunteer who has spent two years on ambushes and flying columns, and the ceasefire takes effect tomorrow.
evt-07-10-1921-irish-war-of-independence.prompt: What should you and your unit do now that the truce is set to begin?

choices.text: Stand down operations and await the outcome of political talks
Intensify ambushes to gain leverage before the ceasefire begins
Disband the flying columns and surrender all arms immediately
Move units north to open a new front in Ulster

evt-07-10-1921-irish-war-of-independence.butterflyEffect: IRA units stood down their attacks as the truce took hold on 11 July, opening the way for negotiations in London. Those talks produced the Anglo-Irish Treaty in December 1921, creating the Irish Free State but splitting the republican movement, a division that erupted into the Irish Civil War the following year.

evt-07-10-1925-guru.scenario: It's 10 July 1925 in India, and your teacher Meher Baba has just told his followers he will stop speaking entirely, with no set end date. You wonder how he will still guide his growing circle of devotees.
evt-07-10-1925-guru.prompt: How did Meher Baba go on to communicate with followers during his silence?

choices.text: Through written letters in a secret script only disciples could read
By having a designated speaker recite his private thoughts aloud
Through an alphabet board and, later, a unique set of hand gestures
By breaking his silence once a week to deliver sermons

evt-07-10-1925-guru.butterflyEffect: Meher Baba kept his silence for 44 years until his death in 1969, using the alphabet board and later distinctive hand gestures. His teachings and silence drew a global following, including Western devotees like musician Pete Townshend, who drew on Baba's ideas while writing The Who's album Tommy.

evt-07-10-1941-the-holocaust.scenario: It is July 1941 in the small Polish town of Jedwabne, days after Nazi Germany's invasion of the Soviet-occupied zone. Local Polish residents, not German soldiers, carry out a massacre of their Jewish neighbors, an atrocity official Polish history will bury for the next sixty years.
evt-07-10-1941-the-holocaust.prompt: How did the true nature of the Jedwabne massacre finally come to light decades later?

choices.text: Leaked Wehrmacht records revealed the truth in the 1950s
Soviet archives released after 1991 immediately exposed the killers' identities
A war crimes trial at Nuremberg named local perpetrators in 1946
Historian Jan T. Gross's book forced a reckoning, leading to an official Polish state investigation

evt-07-10-1941-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: Historian Jan T. Gross's 2000 book 'Neighbors' revealed, based on survivor testimony, that Polish neighbors carried out the killing. Poland's Institute of National Remembrance confirmed key findings in 2002, and President Aleksander Kwaśniewski issued a formal apology at Jedwabne's 60th-anniversary memorial in 2001, opening a national reckoning over Polish complicity in the Holocaust.

evt-07-10-1942-akutan-zero.scenario: You are a US Navy engineer in 1942 examining a nearly intact Japanese Zero fighter recovered from the Alaskan tundra. American pilots have struggled against this plane's reputation for invincibility in dogfights.
evt-07-10-1942-akutan-zero.prompt: What critical weakness do test flights of the captured Zero reveal to American pilots?

choices.text: It carried heavier armor plating than expected
It lacked forward-firing machine guns entirely
Its ailerons stiffen badly at high speed, limiting maneuverability
Its top speed exceeded every American fighter

evt-07-10-1942-akutan-zero.butterflyEffect: Tests showed the Zero's controls stiffened badly at high speed, robbing it of maneuverability in fast dives and rolls, and that it carried no armor or self-sealing fuel tanks. American pilots were taught to avoid slow turning fights and instead dive, strike, and disengage at speed, tactics later built into the design of the F6F Hellcat.

evt-07-10-1966-martin-luther-king-jr.scenario: It is 10 July 1966. You stand with tens of thousands at Soldier Field, having just heard Martin Luther King Jr. speak on ending slums and housing discrimination in Chicago. The crowd begins moving toward downtown.
evt-07-10-1966-martin-luther-king-jr.prompt: What does King do after the rally at Soldier Field?

choices.text: Lead a sit-in at a segregated Chicago restaurant
Fly immediately to Washington to meet President Johnson
Call for an immediate citywide boycott of public transit
March to City Hall and post a list of housing demands on its door

evt-07-10-1966-martin-luther-king-jr.butterflyEffect: King led marchers to City Hall and posted a list of demands on its door, echoing Luther's theses. The pressure led to the August 1966 Summit Agreement, in which the city pledged to pursue fair housing—though enforcement proved weak in the years after.

evt-07-10-1973-john-paul-getty-iii.scenario: It's mid-1973 in Rome, and 16-year-old John Paul Getty III has been kidnapped by Calabrian gangsters demanding a $17 million ransom. His billionaire grandfather, J. Paul Getty, refuses to pay, calling it a dangerous precedent.
evt-07-10-1973-john-paul-getty-iii.prompt: What finally forced J. Paul Getty to negotiate a ransom for his grandson?

choices.text: The boy escaped on his own after five months
Italian police stormed the hideout and rescued him unharmed
Kidnappers mailed the boy's severed ear to a newspaper along with a lock of hair
The family paid the full $17 million ransom immediately

evt-07-10-1973-john-paul-getty-iii.butterflyEffect: After the gruesome proof arrived, Getty Sr. agreed to pay roughly $2.2 million—the maximum amount he could deduct from taxes, and he lent the rest to his son's father at interest. John Paul III was released in December 1973 but never recovered, later suffering a drug-induced stroke that left him paralyzed for life.

evt-07-10-1978-moktar-ould-daddah.scenario: It is 10 July 1978 in Nouakchott. After eighteen years as Mauritania's only president, you are woken to find army officers at the palace gates, unhappy with the costly, stalemated war in Western Sahara.
evt-07-10-1978-moktar-ould-daddah.prompt: What happens to President Daddah in this coup?

choices.text: He retains a ceremonial presidency under the junta
He is executed within days of the coup
He is arrested and detained by the coup leaders
He successfully flees the country before the coup begins

evt-07-10-1978-moktar-ould-daddah.butterflyEffect: Daddah was arrested and detained by the military junta that seized power, ending civilian rule. He was eventually released and went into exile in France, while Mauritania entered decades of military-dominated governments.

evt-07-10-1999-united-states-women-s-nat.scenario: It's July 10, 1999, at the Rose Bowl, and 90,000 fans watch the Women's World Cup final between the US and China end scoreless after extra time. You're on Team USA, facing a decisive penalty shootout to decide the title.
evt-07-10-1999-united-states-women-s-nat.prompt: What happened to seal the United States' World Cup victory?

choices.text: China's goalkeeper was sent off for a foul inside the box
The match was replayed after a disputed offside call
Mia Hamm scored the winning goal in sudden-death extra time
Brandi Chastain scored the winning penalty and tore off her jersey in celebration

evt-07-10-1999-united-states-women-s-nat.butterflyEffect: Brandi Chastain's fifth and final penalty, after goalkeeper Briana Scurry saved China's third attempt, won the U.S. its second Women's World Cup title. Chastain's jersey-tearing celebration became one of the most iconic images in women's sports and helped fuel a lasting surge in youth soccer participation across America.

evt-07-10-2017-war-in-iraq-2013-2017.scenario: It's 10 July 2017 in Mosul's shattered Old City. Iraqi forces have just crushed the last Islamic State holdouts after nine months of brutal urban fighting, and Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi arrives to declare the city liberated.
evt-07-10-2017-war-in-iraq-2013-2017.prompt: What actually followed Abadi's declaration of Mosul's liberation?

choices.text: The Iraqi army was disbanded and replaced entirely by militia forces
Iraqi forces continued clearing remaining pockets of fighters while reconstruction began amid heavy destruction
United Nations peacekeepers took direct control of administering the city
ISIL immediately surrendered across all of Iraq and Syria

evt-07-10-2017-war-in-iraq-2013-2017.butterflyEffect: Much of Mosul's Old City, including its famed al-Nuri Mosque, lay in ruins, and thousands of civilians had died in the fighting. ISIL's self-declared caliphate continued to collapse, losing its Syrian capital Raqqa months later, but insurgent attacks and the task of rebuilding Mosul dragged on for years afterward.

evt-07-10-2018-association-football.scenario: It is 10 July 2018 deep inside Tham Luang cave in Thailand. You are one of the last rescue divers, with the final boys of the trapped youth football team and their coach still waiting in a flooded chamber miles from the entrance.
evt-07-10-2018-association-football.prompt: How do the divers get the boys out through the flooded tunnels?

choices.text: Pull them out one by one using a rope and harness system
Wait for pumps to lower the water level enough to walk out
Sedate each boy and guide them out while diving
Drill a new vertical shaft directly to their chamber

evt-07-10-2018-association-football.butterflyEffect: Divers sedated each boy and guided them through the submerged passages strapped to their own equipment, completing the rescue of all twelve boys and their coach after eighteen days underground. The operation became a global story of international cooperation and reshaped cave-rescue protocols worldwide.

evt-07-10-2018-tham-luang-cave-rescue.scenario: It is early July 2018 and you are part of the international dive team reaching the boys and their coach deep inside the flooded Tham Luang cave. Monsoon rains are rising fast and the boys have never dived before.
evt-07-10-2018-tham-luang-cave-rescue.prompt: How do rescuers get the trapped boys safely through the flooded passages?

choices.text: Teach the boys to scuba dive themselves over several days
Drill a vertical shaft directly down to their chamber
Wait several weeks for the floodwater to fully recede
Sedate each boy and dive him out strapped to an escorting diver

evt-07-10-2018-tham-luang-cave-rescue.butterflyEffect: Each boy was sedated and fitted with a full-face mask, then guided out by pairs of divers through the flooded tunnels over three days. All twelve boys and their coach survived, though Thai Navy SEAL diver Saman Kunan died during the operation, and the rescue became a global model for cave-diving emergency response.

evt-07-10-2019-volkswagen-beetle.scenario: It's July 10, 2019, at Volkswagen's Puebla, Mexico plant, and workers watch the last-ever Beetle roll off the same line that has built the car since 1967.
evt-07-10-2019-volkswagen-beetle.prompt: What did Volkswagen do with the Puebla production line after the final Beetle?

choices.text: Production moved unchanged to a new plant in Germany
The Puebla plant shifted to building SUVs and other models as VW pivoted away from the Beetle
The plant was closed permanently and demolished
Volkswagen immediately began building a new Beetle model at the same plant

evt-07-10-2019-volkswagen-beetle.butterflyEffect: That final Beetle, a blue 'Denim' special edition, ended a nameplate that had run for 81 years and over 21 million cars worldwide. Volkswagen redirected its Puebla resources toward SUVs like the Taos and its emerging electric ID lineup, marking the definitive close of the classic Beetle era in favor of the company's electric future.

evt-07-11-1302-franco-flemish-war.scenario: It is 11 July 1302, and you command a line of Flemish militia and townsmen near Kortrijk. Across the field, a large force of French knights, Europe's finest heavy cavalry, prepares to charge, but the ground before you is crossed with streams and ditches.
evt-07-11-1302-franco-flemish-war.prompt: How do you use the terrain to counter the French cavalry charge?

choices.text: Send envoys to negotiate surrender before the fighting starts
Charge out to meet the knights in open cavalry-to-cavalry combat
Retreat behind Kortrijk's walls and wait out a siege
Hold a fortified line behind the streams and ditches, forcing the cavalry to bog down

evt-07-11-1302-franco-flemish-war.butterflyEffect: The Flemish held their fortified line as French knights floundered in the marshy, ditch-crossed ground, and the infantry cut them down with pikes and goedendags. Hundreds of gilded spurs were stripped from dead knights and hung in a church, giving the battle its name, and the victory became a landmark proof that disciplined foot soldiers could break feudal cavalry.

evt-07-11-1405-ming-treasure-voyages.scenario: It is 1405 in the shipyards of the Yangtze delta. The Yongle Emperor has entrusted his admiral Zheng He with a colossal fleet of treasure ships, ordering him to sail beyond China's shores into the unfamiliar waters of Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean.
evt-07-11-1405-ming-treasure-voyages.prompt: What is the fleet's mission as it departs on its first great voyage?

choices.text: To chart a westward sea route to Europe
To conquer foreign ports and establish exclusive trade monopolies
To project Ming imperial power and collect tribute from distant rulers
To found permanent Chinese colonies along the Indian Ocean coast

evt-07-11-1405-ming-treasure-voyages.butterflyEffect: Zheng He's fleet sailed to Calicut and beyond, exchanging gifts, collecting tribute, and projecting Ming naval power without seeking territorial conquest. Six more voyages followed under his command, reaching as far as East Africa, but after 1433 the court turned inward, dismantled the fleet, and abandoned overseas expansion just as European powers were beginning their own age of exploration.

evt-07-11-1789-french-revolution.scenario: It is 11 July 1789 in Paris. Word spreads through the streets that King Louis XVI has just dismissed Jacques Necker, the finance minister many saw as the crown's one sympathetic reformer.
evt-07-11-1789-french-revolution.prompt: What followed once news of Necker's dismissal reached the Parisian crowds?

choices.text: The National Assembly immediately dissolved itself
Riots and arming of citizens that led to the storming of the Bastille days later
Necker was reinstated the same afternoon with no unrest
A quiet acceptance of the king's decision

evt-07-11-1789-french-revolution.butterflyEffect: Outrage over Necker's dismissal fueled riots and a rush to arms across Paris, culminating three days later in the storming of the Bastille on 14 July. The king was forced to recall Necker within days, but the fall of the Bastille had already turned unrest into open revolution.

evt-07-11-1792-belfast-harp-festival.scenario: It is July 1792 in Belfast's Assembly Room on Waring Street. Ten aging harpers, several of them blind, have gathered for a rare competition meant to rescue a fading tradition, and organisers have hired a young classically trained organist to sit beside them with manuscript paper.
evt-07-11-1792-belfast-harp-festival.prompt: What does Edward Bunting do at the festival that proves historically vital?

choices.text: He notates the forty tunes performed by the ten harpists
He composes new harp music especially for the occasion
He judges the contest and personally awards the prizes
He teaches the harpers modern classical techniques

evt-07-11-1792-belfast-harp-festival.butterflyEffect: Bunting notated the forty tunes performed, work that became the backbone of his 1796 General Collection of the Ancient Irish Music. Without his transcriptions many of these melodies, carried only in the memories of the last generation of harpers, would likely have been lost, and the collection later fed directly into the 19th-century Gaelic cultural revival.

evt-07-11-1833-yagan.scenario: You are a Noongar man in the Swan River Colony in 1833. A settler's servant has shot Noongar people for taking food, and your kinsman Yagan has struck back by killing another servant in retaliation.
evt-07-11-1833-yagan.prompt: How did the colonial government respond to Yagan's continued resistance?

choices.text: They ignored his actions entirely
They offered a bounty for his capture, dead or alive
They granted his people formal land rights
They negotiated a peace treaty with him

evt-07-11-1833-yagan.butterflyEffect: Authorities placed a bounty on Yagan, dead or alive, and settler William Keats shot him for the reward. His head was later sent to England as a curiosity and was not returned to Australia for reburial until 1997, making Yagan a lasting symbol of Noongar resistance and reconciliation.

evt-07-11-1846-death-of-frederick-john-w.scenario: You are Private Frederick John White of the 7th Hussars, tied to a ladder before your assembled regiment at Hounslow barracks in 1846, sentenced to 150 lashes for drunkenly touching a sergeant with a metal bar.
evt-07-11-1846-death-of-frederick-john-w.prompt: What happened to White in the weeks after his flogging?

choices.text: He was quietly discharged unharmed
He deteriorated and died of his injuries
He fully recovered and returned to duty
He was pardoned and promoted

evt-07-11-1846-death-of-frederick-john-w.butterflyEffect: White seemed to recover at first but then deteriorated and died on 11 July 1846. Public outrage over his death fueled a growing campaign against military flogging, contributing to its restriction in peacetime by 1868 and eventual abolition in the British Army in 1881.

evt-07-11-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 11 July 1864. You are a Union officer at Fort Stevens on the outskirts of Washington, D.C., watching Jubal Early's Confederate troops probe the capital's thin defenses while President Lincoln himself stands on the parapet nearby.
evt-07-11-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What move saved the capital from Early's threatened assault?

choices.text: Evacuate the government to Philadelphia
Rely solely on the Home Guard militia already in the city
Negotiate a local truce with Early's officers
Rush veteran reinforcements from Grant's army by boat to the city's forts

evt-07-11-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Union commanders rushed veteran troops from Grant's army by steamer to reinforce the capital just in time, and Early's outnumbered force withdrew after skirmishing at Fort Stevens. It was the last Confederate attempt to threaten Washington directly, and it embarrassed Union planners into strengthening the capital's permanent defenses.

evt-07-11-1914-uss-nevada-bb-36.scenario: You are a naval engineer at the Fore River Shipyard finalizing specifications for the new battleship Nevada before her launch. Coal has powered every US battleship built so far, but a new fuel is under debate.
evt-07-11-1914-uss-nevada-bb-36.prompt: What fuel choice for Nevada set the pattern for future US battleships?

choices.text: Oil-fired boilers
Coal, kept for reliability
A mixed coal-and-oil system
Early diesel propulsion

evt-07-11-1914-uss-nevada-bb-36.butterflyEffect: Nevada was built to run on oil instead of coal, giving her greater range and speed and requiring less manpower to fuel. Every subsequent US battleship followed this standard, tying the fleet's fighting power to secure oil supplies—a strategic concern that shaped naval planning through both World Wars.

evt-07-11-1960-to-kill-a-mockingbird.scenario: It is July 1960, and a debut novel by an unknown Alabama author has just arrived on your bookstore shelves. It follows a young girl watching her lawyer father defend a Black man falsely accused of rape in the Depression-era South.
evt-07-11-1960-to-kill-a-mockingbird.prompt: What recognition did this novel receive the following year?

choices.text: It won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction
It was immediately adapted into a Broadway musical
It was banned from publication nationwide
It sold poorly and went out of print

evt-07-11-1960-to-kill-a-mockingbird.butterflyEffect: In 1961, To Kill a Mockingbird won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. It became a fixture of American middle and high school curricula and was adapted into an Oscar-winning 1962 film starring Gregory Peck, cementing its lasting cultural influence on discussions of racial justice.

evt-07-11-1982-italy-national-football-t.scenario: It is 11 July 1982 at the Santiago Bernabéu in Madrid. You are an Italian midfielder in the World Cup final against West Germany, still scoreless at halftime despite a tense, tight match.
evt-07-11-1982-italy-national-football-t.prompt: What did Italy do in the second half to claim the title?

choices.text: Score three unanswered goals to win outright
Play for a single late goal and defend the lead
Hold on for a 0-0 draw and win on penalties
Concede early but rally to force extra time

evt-07-11-1982-italy-national-football-t.butterflyEffect: Italy erupted with three second-half goals from Paolo Rossi, Marco Tardelli, and Alessandro Altobelli to win 3–1. Rossi finished as the tournament's top scorer, Tardelli's roaring celebration became one of football's most replayed images, and Italy claimed its third World Cup, matching the era's elite football nations.

evt-07-11-1995-srebrenica-massacre.scenario: It is 11 July 1995. You command the outnumbered Dutch UN battalion as Bosnian Serb forces under General Mladić overrun the Srebrenica 'safe area'. Thousands of terrified Bosniak civilians crowd into your compound at Potočari begging for protection, and NATO air support has not arrived.
evt-07-11-1995-srebrenica-massacre.prompt: With no reinforcements coming, what does the UN commander decide to do?

choices.text: Call in immediate NATO airstrikes on the advancing Serb columns
Negotiate the evacuation of refugees directly with General Mladić
Evacuate the compound immediately, leaving the refugees behind
Order Dutch troops to fight and hold the perimeter

evt-07-11-1995-srebrenica-massacre.butterflyEffect: Commander Karremans negotiated with Mladić rather than resisting, and the enclave was handed over. Serb forces separated men and boys from women, then murdered more than 8,000 in the days that followed. The massacre was later ruled genocide by international courts, the Dutch government resigned over its failure in 2002, and Srebrenica became the defining indictment of UN peacekeeping's limits.

evt-07-11-2006-2006-mumbai-train-bombing.scenario: It is the evening rush hour on 11 July 2006, and you are boarding a crowded train on Mumbai's Western Line, unaware that pressure-cooker bombs have been planted aboard several first-class compartments.
evt-07-11-2006-2006-mumbai-train-bombing.prompt: Which group did Indian investigators ultimately blame for orchestrating the bombings?

choices.text: Kashmiri separatists acting independently
Lashkar-e-Taiba with local Indian operatives
Al-Qaeda acting directly through its own cell
Naxalite insurgents from central India

evt-07-11-2006-2006-mumbai-train-bombing.butterflyEffect: Investigators concluded that Lashkar-e-Taiba, working with local operatives from the banned Students Islamic Movement of India, planned and executed the attack. The case led to lengthy trials and convictions, though defense claims of coerced confessions kept the investigation controversial for years, and it spurred major security upgrades across Mumbai's rail network.

evt-07-11-2007-siege-of-lal-masjid.scenario: It is July 2007 in Islamabad. Armed militants and students remain barricaded inside the Lal Masjid and its adjoining madrasah after days of negotiation, and President Musharraf's government must decide how the standoff will end.
evt-07-11-2007-siege-of-lal-masjid.prompt: What action did the Pakistani government take to end the siege?

choices.text: Launch a military assault to storm the compound
Accept the militants' demands for Sharia enforcement
Cut off utilities and wait indefinitely without force
Withdraw all forces and let the militants leave freely

evt-07-11-2007-siege-of-lal-masjid.butterflyEffect: Security forces launched a full military assault, Operation Silence, storming the complex after negotiations collapsed. The bloody outcome radicalized many across Pakistan's tribal areas and is widely seen as a catalyst for the formation of Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan and a subsequent wave of suicide bombings.

evt-07-11-2011-evangelos-florakis-naval-.scenario: It is the early hours of 11 July 2011 at the Evangelos Florakis Naval Base in Mari, Cyprus. Confiscated munitions, seized from an Iranian-flagged ship years earlier, have sat stacked in shipping containers under the Mediterranean sun despite repeated warnings from officers about the risk.
evt-07-11-2011-evangelos-florakis-naval-.prompt: What happens when the poorly stored stockpile finally detonates?

choices.text: The explosion kills over a dozen people and wrecks the neighbouring power station
Firefighters manage to contain the blaze before any detonation occurs
A planned controlled detonation destroys the cargo without casualties
A bomb disposal squad safely defuses the munitions overnight

evt-07-11-2011-evangelos-florakis-naval-.butterflyEffect: The blast, equivalent to roughly 481 tons of TNT, killed 13 people including the navy commander and six firefighters, and destroyed the adjacent Vasilikos power station. The loss of the island's largest power plant triggered rolling blackouts and deepened Cyprus's economic troubles ahead of its 2013 bailout, while public outrage forced the resignation of the defence minister and National Guard chief.

evt-07-11-2015-el-chapo.scenario: It is July 2015, and you are Joaquín "El Chapo" Guzmán, locked in a cell at Mexico's supposedly inescapable Altiplano prison. For months your allies have been quietly working beneath the floor of your own shower stall.
evt-07-11-2015-el-chapo.prompt: How do you make your escape from the maximum-security cell?

choices.text: By hiding inside a laundry truck leaving the facility
Through a tunnel dug beneath his cell, fitted with rails and a motorcycle
By scaling the outer perimeter wall during a prisoner transfer
By bribing a guard for keys and walking out the front gate

evt-07-11-2015-el-chapo.butterflyEffect: Guzmán vanished through a mile-long tunnel dug directly under his shower, complete with lighting, ventilation, and a motorcycle on rails. The escape triggered a massive international manhunt; he was recaptured in Los Mochis in January 2016 after a Sean Penn interview drew attention to his hideout, and was extradited to the US, where he received a life sentence in 2019.

evt-07-12-927-thelstan.scenario: It is 927 at Eamont Bridge in Cumbria. You are King Æthelstan, and four powerful rulers from the north and west of Britain — including Constantine II of Scotland and Owain of Strathclyde — have come to meet you after your seizure of York from the Vikings.
evt-07-12-927-thelstan.prompt: What did Æthelstan secure from these northern rulers at this meeting?

choices.text: A promise to pay an annual gold tribute only, with no political submission
Their acknowledgment of him as overlord and a pledge to keep the peace
A military alliance to jointly invade Ireland
The direct cession of York to Æthelstan's personal rule

evt-07-12-927-thelstan.butterflyEffect: The rulers submitted to Æthelstan's overlordship, formally recognizing him as the dominant power in Britain, a moment historians treat as the effective birth of a unified English kingdom. The peace did not last: Constantine later broke with Æthelstan, and the alliance's collapse led to the great Battle of Brunanburh in 937.

evt-07-12-1561-saint-basil-s-cathedral.scenario: You stand in Red Square in Moscow on this day in 1561 as bells ring for the consecration of a strange, many-domed church beside the Kremlin walls. Tsar Ivan the Terrible himself ordered its construction six years earlier.
evt-07-12-1561-saint-basil-s-cathedral.prompt: What victory did Ivan commission this cathedral to commemorate?

choices.text: The capture of Kazan and Astrakhan
The defeat of the Livonian Order
The founding of Moscow itself
The coronation of Ivan as tsar

evt-07-12-1561-saint-basil-s-cathedral.butterflyEffect: The cathedral marked Ivan's capture of the Khanates of Kazan and Astrakhan, cementing Muscovy's expansion east. It survived Napoleon's occupation and Soviet-era demolition threats to become Russia's most recognisable architectural symbol.

evt-07-12-1801-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: It is the night of 12 July 1801 off Algeciras Bay. Your British squadron under Sir James Saumarez is heavily outnumbered by a combined French and Spanish fleet trying to slip through to Cadiz.
evt-07-12-1801-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What does Saumarez order as the enemy fleet tries to pass in the dark?

choices.text: Close and engage the fleet despite being outnumbered
Send a negotiator to arrange safe passage
Withdraw to Gibraltar and wait for reinforcements
Blockade the bay and starve them out

evt-07-12-1801-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: The British pressed the attack in darkness, and in the confusion two huge Spanish ships, the Real Carlos and San Hermenegildo, collided and caught fire, both eventually blowing up with heavy loss of life. The disaster turned a numerically hopeless fight into a stunning British victory that boosted Royal Navy morale.

evt-07-12-1913-second-balkan-war.scenario: It is July 1913, and you command Serbian forces converging on the Bulgarian fortress of Vidin on the Danube, one of the last strongholds resisting your alliance's advance. Romanian troops close in from the north as Bulgaria's army buckles on every front.
evt-07-12-1913-second-balkan-war.prompt: What tactic should you use to reduce the fortress at Vidin?

choices.text: Encircle Vidin and open a sustained siege, cutting the garrison's supply lines
Storm the walls immediately with massed infantry before Bulgaria can reinforce
Bypass the fortress and race for Sofia to force a quicker surrender
Offer the garrison commander a bribe to open the gates

evt-07-12-1913-second-balkan-war.butterflyEffect: The siege dragged on for weeks and Vidin never fell by force; the war ended first, with the Treaty of Bucharest signed on 10 August 1913. Bulgaria, defeated by its former Balkan League partners and Romania, lost territory on nearly every side and emerged bitter and isolated, an isolation it would seek to reverse by joining the Central Powers in World War I.

evt-07-12-1916-world-war-i.scenario: It is 12 July 1916 at Fort Souville, near Verdun. German troops have pushed further than at any point in the battle and are closing on your position. As the officer in command, you must decide how to stop them before they break through to the open ground beyond the fort.
evt-07-12-1916-world-war-i.prompt: What did Second Lieutenant Kléber Dupuy order to halt the German advance?

choices.text: A request for a local truce to evacuate the wounded
An immediate retreat to the second defensive line
A bayonet charge to break the German formation
French artillery fire onto his own position to stop the Germans

evt-07-12-1916-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Dupuy called down French artillery fire directly onto his own position to stop the advancing Germans, and the attack was broken. The failed assault marked the furthest German advance of the entire Battle of Verdun, often called its "high-water mark," after which the initiative shifted decisively to French counterattacks later in 1916.

evt-07-12-1920-soviet-lithuanian-peace-t.scenario: You are a Lithuanian delegate in Moscow on 12 July 1920, negotiating with Soviet Russia while Poland presses on your borders. Moscow wants free movement for its troops fighting Poland; you want recognition of Lithuania's independence and territory.
evt-07-12-1920-soviet-lithuanian-peace-t.prompt: What must Lithuania grant Soviet Russia to secure recognition of its sovereignty and borders?

choices.text: Control of the port of Klaipeda
Lithuanian membership in the Soviet Union
A military alliance against Poland
Permission for Soviet troops to move through Lithuanian territory

evt-07-12-1920-soviet-lithuanian-peace-t.butterflyEffect: Lithuania agreed to Soviet troop movements across its territory in exchange for recognized sovereignty and eastern borders including the Vilnius region. Poland seized Vilnius later that year anyway, leaving the treaty's borders disputed for the rest of the interwar period.

evt-07-12-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: You command a T-34 crew near Prokhorovka on 12 July 1943, part of the Kursk offensive. Ahead, German Tiger tanks with longer-ranged guns are dug in across the open steppe.
evt-07-12-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What tactic gives your lighter, shorter-ranged tank a chance against the Tigers?

choices.text: Retreat and let artillery soften them first
Hold position and duel at maximum range
Close the range quickly to fight at close quarters
Wait for air support before advancing

evt-07-12-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Soviet tank crews closed distance rapidly to fight inside the range where German gun advantages mattered less, at heavy cost to both sides. The battle helped blunt the German offensive at Kursk, after which the strategic initiative on the Eastern Front passed permanently to the Soviets.

evt-07-12-1948-1948-arab-israeli-war.scenario: It is July 1948, and Israeli forces have just captured the towns of Lydda and Ramle during Operation Dani. You are an officer awaiting word from Yitzhak Rabin on what to do with the thousands of Arab residents still inside the towns.
evt-07-12-1948-1948-arab-israeli-war.prompt: What did Rabin's signed order instruct troops to do with the population?

choices.text: Hold a local vote on whether the towns would join Israel
Disarm residents but let them remain under military rule
Arrest only men of military age and release the rest
Expel the Arab population from the towns immediately

evt-07-12-1948-1948-arab-israeli-war.butterflyEffect: Rabin's order set in motion the forced expulsion of tens of thousands of Palestinian residents from Lydda and Ramle, who were marched out toward Arab-held territory in what became known as the Lydda exodus. The episode remains one of the most cited events of the 1948 Palestinian exodus, shaping decades of dispute over refugees' right of return.

evt-07-12-1962-the-rolling-stones.scenario: You are in the crowd at London's Marquee Club on 12 July 1962, watching a scruffy new rhythm and blues combo take the stage for the very first time, billed under a name borrowed from an old Muddy Waters record.
evt-07-12-1962-the-rolling-stones.prompt: What name did the band perform under for this debut gig?

choices.text: The High Numbers
The Detours
The Blues Incorporated
The Rollin' Stones

evt-07-12-1962-the-rolling-stones.butterflyEffect: They billed themselves as "The Rollin' Stones," later adding the final g. Built around the Jagger–Richards songwriting partnership that soon emerged, the band went on to become one of rock music's most influential and enduring acts.

evt-07-12-1979-comiskey-park.scenario: It is 12 July 1979, and you are in the stands at Comiskey Park between games of a White Sox doubleheader, watching a crate of disco records get set up in center field for a promotional explosion.
evt-07-12-1979-comiskey-park.prompt: What happens right after the crate of records is detonated?

choices.text: Fans rush onto the field, causing a riot and forcing a forfeit of the second game
Players take the field on schedule and the second game proceeds normally
Police quickly disperse the crowd with no disruption to play
The crowd calmly returns to their seats for the second game

evt-07-12-1979-comiskey-park.butterflyEffect: The explosion tore a hole in the outfield turf and thousands of fans poured onto the field in a riot, forcing the White Sox to forfeit the second game to the Detroit Tigers. "Disco Demolition Night" became a notorious symbol of the era's anti-disco backlash and is often cited as a marker of disco's rapid fall from mainstream popularity.

evt-07-12-1997-hayao-miyazaki.scenario: It is 1997, and Miramax has acquired Princess Mononoke for U.S. distribution. Harvey Weinstein wants to trim the sprawling film for American audiences, and you are the executive who has just received an unusual package from Miyazaki's studio in response.
evt-07-12-1997-hayao-miyazaki.prompt: What did the studio send Weinstein to insist the film run uncut?

choices.text: A first-class ticket demanding an in-person meeting
A formal legal threat to void the contract
A katana sword
A box of unreleased storyboards

evt-07-12-1997-hayao-miyazaki.butterflyEffect: The gift, accompanied by a note reading simply "No cuts," convinced Miramax to release Princess Mononoke largely intact in 1999. Its success helped cement Miyazaki's reputation in the West and opened the door for Studio Ghibli's films to reach wider international audiences with their original visions preserved.

evt-07-12-1998-ulster-volunteer-force.scenario: It is the height of the Drumcree marching crisis in July 1998, and Northern Ireland has spent days gripped by loyalist protests and street violence. Overnight, a petrol bomb attack on a family's home in Ballymoney kills three young Catholic brothers, shocking the province.
evt-07-12-1998-ulster-volunteer-force.prompt: How did political and paramilitary leaders across the divide respond to the killings?

choices.text: Unionist leaders publicly condemned the killings and loyalist groups faced pressure to hold their ceasefires
The British government suspended the Good Friday Agreement in response
Loyalist paramilitaries announced a formal end to all ceasefires that week
The Orange Order called for an immediate escalation of the Drumcree protests

evt-07-12-1998-ulster-volunteer-force.butterflyEffect: The murders of the Quinn brothers provoked near-universal condemnation from unionist and loyalist figures as well as nationalists, deepening public revulsion against paramilitary violence just months after the Good Friday Agreement. The killings are widely seen as having strengthened loyalist paramilitaries' commitment to maintaining their ceasefires rather than escalating sectarian attacks.

evt-07-12-2001-space-shuttle-program.scenario: You are part of the STS-104 crew aboard Space Shuttle Atlantis, docked with the International Space Station. Mission planners have given you a critical piece of hardware to install before the crew can begin independent spacewalks from the U.S. segment.
evt-07-12-2001-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What did the STS-104 crew install on the ISS during this mission?

choices.text: The Destiny laboratory module
The Quest Joint Airlock
The Canadarm2 robotic arm
The Zvezda service module

evt-07-12-2001-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: Atlantis delivered and installed the Quest Joint Airlock, the first airlock allowing astronauts to conduct spacewalks directly from the U.S. side of the station using American spacesuits, rather than relying on the Russian segment. This gave NASA independent EVA capability that supported years of station assembly and maintenance work to come.

evt-07-12-2006-2006-hezbollah-cross-bord.scenario: It is 12 July 2006, and you are advising the Israeli cabinet after Hezbollah fighters ambushed a border patrol, killing several soldiers and dragging two others across into Lebanon.
evt-07-12-2006-2006-hezbollah-cross-bord.prompt: What does Israel do in response to the raid and abductions?

choices.text: Downplay the incident publicly to avoid escalating tensions
Request UN peacekeepers without any independent military action
Launch a large-scale air and ground military campaign against Hezbollah in Lebanon
Immediately agree to a prisoner exchange to secure the soldiers' release

evt-07-12-2006-2006-hezbollah-cross-bord.butterflyEffect: Israel launched a large-scale air and ground campaign into Lebanon, beginning the 34-day 2006 Lebanon War that caused heavy destruction and casualties on both sides before a UN-brokered ceasefire. The captured soldiers' bodies were only returned in 2008, in a prisoner exchange for Samir Kuntar and four other Hezbollah detainees.

evt-07-12-2007-united-states-army.scenario: On 12 July 2007, a U.S. Army Apache crew engages a group of men on a Baghdad street, believing them to be armed insurgents. Among those killed are two Reuters news staff carrying camera equipment. The incident draws little public attention at the time.
evt-07-12-2007-united-states-army.prompt: What later event turned this Baghdad airstrike into an internationally known controversy?

choices.text: A congressional inquiry immediately court-martialed the helicopter crew
The United Nations opened a war crimes tribunal into the strike
Reuters won a lawsuit forcing the Pentagon to release the footage in 2007
WikiLeaks released leaked cockpit footage of the strike in 2010

evt-07-12-2007-united-states-army.butterflyEffect: In 2010, WikiLeaks published leaked cockpit video of the strike, titled "Collateral Murder," which spread worldwide and became a flashpoint in debates over U.S. conduct in Iraq and the treatment of journalists in war zones. The leak, sourced from Army intelligence analyst Chelsea Manning, also triggered a major U.S. prosecution over classified disclosures.

evt-07-12-2013-bretigny-sur-orge-train-c.scenario: It is the evening of 12 July 2013, and you are waiting on the platform at Brétigny-sur-Orge as a crowded intercity train from Paris approaches the station without slowing for a scheduled stop.
evt-07-12-2013-bretigny-sur-orge-train-c.prompt: What did investigators later determine caused the train to derail at the switch?

choices.text: A signal failure that sent the train onto the wrong track
A worn track fishplate that dislodged into the switch
A deliberate act of sabotage on the line
Driver error in approaching the station too fast

evt-07-12-2013-bretigny-sur-orge-train-c.butterflyEffect: Investigators found that a loose fishplate had become dislodged and jammed a track switch, throwing the train off the rails as it passed through the station. The disaster exposed years of deferred maintenance on France's rail network and fueled a national push for greater investment in track infrastructure.

evt-07-13-1643-english-civil-war.scenario: It is 13 July 1643 on the high ground above Devizes. You command Parliamentarian infantry under Sir William Waller as Royalist cavalry, having force-marched to relieve the town, suddenly charge onto the open down.
evt-07-13-1643-english-civil-war.prompt: What happens to Waller's Parliamentarian army at the Battle of Roundway Down?

choices.text: They are routed, with many driven off a steep escarpment
They retreat in good order to Bristol
They repel the cavalry charge and hold the field
They negotiate a truce with the Royalist commanders

evt-07-13-1643-english-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Royalist cavalry shattered Waller's force, driving many fleeing troops over a steep escarpment later called 'Bloody Ditch.' Combined with the fall of Bristol days later, the victory gave the King control of the West Country and marked the Royalists' high tide in 1643.

evt-07-13-1831-wallachia.scenario: It is July 1831 in Bucharest, and Wallachia's boyar assembly, working under the oversight of Russian administrator Pavel Kiselyov after Russia's occupation of the principality, is about to adopt a new organizing law for government.
evt-07-13-1831-wallachia.prompt: What kind of document did the Wallachian assembly adopt?

choices.text: A treaty formally uniting Wallachia and Moldavia into one state
A full modern constitution granting universal male suffrage
A declaration of complete independence from the Ottoman Empire
