A quasi-constitutional charter, the Regulamentul Organic, defining government structure and boyar privilege

evt-07-13-1831-wallachia.butterflyEffect: The Regulamentul Organic created Wallachia's first modern administrative and legislative framework, entrenching boyar power while modernizing tax and justice systems under Russian tutelage. A near-identical statute followed in Moldavia in 1832, and the shared institutions the two documents created helped pave the way for the eventual union of the principalities into Romania in 1859.

evt-07-13-1863-new-york-city-draft-riots.scenario: It is July 1863 and the first draft lottery under the new conscription law has just been held in New York City. Anger is boiling among working-class men who cannot afford the $300 commutation fee that lets wealthier draftees buy their way out.
evt-07-13-1863-new-york-city-draft-riots.prompt: What did President Lincoln do to restore order in the city?

choices.text: Order the arrest of every newspaper editor critical of the war
Divert Union regiments fresh from Gettysburg to occupy the city
Suspend the draft entirely across the North
Declare martial law and cancel all civil government in New York

evt-07-13-1863-new-york-city-draft-riots.butterflyEffect: Lincoln sent battle-hardened troops straight from Gettysburg, and their arrival ended the four days of rioting, one of the deadliest civil disturbances in American history to that point. The unrest exposed deep class and racial fault lines in the wartime North and left a lasting stain on the city's history.

evt-07-13-1878-treaty-of-berlin-1878.scenario: It is July 1878 in Berlin, and you are a delegate at the Congress chaired by Otto von Bismarck, tasked with redrawing the Balkan map after Russia's victory over the Ottomans. The preliminary Treaty of San Stefano created a large Bulgaria that alarmed Austria-Hungary and Britain.
evt-07-13-1878-treaty-of-berlin-1878.prompt: What should the Congress do about the oversized Bulgaria created at San Stefano?

choices.text: Abolish Bulgarian autonomy entirely and restore full Ottoman control
Confirm the large Bulgaria exactly as Russia had drawn it
Grant Bulgaria full independence with its San Stefano borders intact
Shrink Bulgaria and divide it into smaller autonomous and Ottoman-controlled zones

evt-07-13-1878-treaty-of-berlin-1878.butterflyEffect: The Congress split Bulgaria into a smaller autonomous principality and the separate province of Eastern Rumelia, while recognizing full independence for Romania, Serbia, and Montenegro. Bulgarians never forgot the reduction, and resentment over 'lost' San Stefano borders fueled Balkan nationalism and conflict for decades, including the wars of 1912–13.

evt-07-13-1930-1930-fifa-world-cup.scenario: It is 13 July 1930 at the Estadio Pocitos in Montevideo. You are French forward Lucien Laurent, and a loose ball drops to you in the box during the opening World Cup match against Mexico.
evt-07-13-1930-1930-fifa-world-cup.prompt: What do you do to become the scorer of the first goal in World Cup history?

choices.text: Wait for a penalty to be awarded
Lay it off for a teammate's tap-in
Dribble past two defenders before shooting
Strike it first-time on the volley

evt-07-13-1930-1930-fifa-world-cup.butterflyEffect: Laurent volleyed the ball home in the 19th minute, and France went on to win 4-1, one of two matches played simultaneously that day alongside the United States' 3-0 win over Belgium. His strike is remembered as the tournament's first goal, launching what would become football's premier global event, now held every four years.

evt-07-13-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 13 July 1943. Your parachute stick has been scattered by flak and anti-aircraft fire over Sicily, and you find yourself alone near the Simeto River, far from your intended drop zone at Primosole Bridge.
evt-07-13-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What do you do to fulfil your mission for Operation Fustian?

choices.text: Attempt a solo assault on Catania itself
Wait at the drop zone until daylight for orders
Move toward the bridge, rally with any other scattered troops, and dig in
Head for the coast to rejoin the naval landing force

evt-07-13-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Despite a badly scattered drop and fierce fighting against German paratroopers who recaptured the bridge, British ground forces of XIII Corps eventually broke through and secured Primosole Bridge, opening the road toward Catania. The operation's heavy casualties and coordination failures became a hard lesson studied by Allied planners ahead of the Normandy airborne drops the following year.

evt-07-13-1973-watergate-scandal.scenario: It is 13 July 1973 in a closed session with Senate Watergate Committee staff. You are Alexander Butterfield, a former White House aide, and an investigator asks you point-blank whether the Oval Office is wired for sound.
evt-07-13-1973-watergate-scandal.prompt: How does Butterfield answer the question about a taping system?

choices.text: He refuses to answer, citing executive privilege
He denies any recording system exists
He confirms Nixon secretly taped virtually all Oval Office conversations
He claims he has no knowledge of White House operations

evt-07-13-1973-watergate-scandal.butterflyEffect: Butterfield confirmed Nixon had secretly recorded nearly all Oval Office conversations. The revelation gave investigators grounds to subpoena the tapes, triggering the 'Saturday Night Massacre' months later and ultimately Nixon's resignation in August 1974 once the recordings proved his role in the cover-up.

evt-07-13-2011-mumbai.scenario: It is the evening rush hour on 13 July 2011 in Mumbai, and three bombs have just exploded within minutes of each other in crowded market and business districts. Investigators must move fast before evidence and witnesses disappear.
evt-07-13-2011-mumbai.prompt: What did Indian authorities do in the aftermath to pursue those responsible?

choices.text: Close all of Mumbai's markets permanently for public safety
Launch a coordinated investigation by the National Investigation Agency amid suspicion of Indian Mujahideen involvement
Immediately declare war on a neighboring country believed responsible
Publicly execute suspects within days without trial

evt-07-13-2011-mumbai.butterflyEffect: No group claimed responsibility, and investigators suspected the Indian Mujahideen network, though prosecutions proved difficult and took years to conclude. The attack led to tighter surveillance and security measures across Indian cities, part of a wider pattern of low-tech, hard-to-trace bombings in the years after the 2008 Mumbai attacks.

evt-07-13-2011-noar-linhas-aereas-flight.scenario: You are a Brazilian civil aviation official reviewing the fatal crash of a small turboprop that went down moments after takeoff from Recife on 13 July 2011, killing everyone aboard.
evt-07-13-2011-noar-linhas-aereas-flight.prompt: What regulatory action follows the investigation into the airline's safety record?

choices.text: The government subsidizes the airline to expand its fleet
The airline merges with a larger national carrier
ANAC suspends the airline's operating certificate
No action is taken and the airline continues unaffected

evt-07-13-2011-noar-linhas-aereas-flight.butterflyEffect: Brazil's aviation authority, ANAC, suspended Noar Linhas Aéreas's operating certificate over safety and maintenance failures. The carrier never resumed regular passenger service, and the crash sharpened scrutiny of small regional turboprop operators serving Brazil's Northeast.

evt-07-13-2013-typhoon-soulik-2013.scenario: It is 12 July 2013, and Typhoon Soulik is bearing down on Taiwan and the Fujian coast with destructive winds and torrential rain. You are a local official responsible for public safety ahead of landfall.
evt-07-13-2013-typhoon-soulik-2013.prompt: What is the most effective order you can give to protect residents before the storm arrives?

choices.text: Deploy troops solely to guard government buildings
Close schools but let residents decide for themselves
Order evacuations of low-lying and landslide-prone areas immediately
Wait until after landfall to assess the need for evacuation

evt-07-13-2013-typhoon-soulik-2013.butterflyEffect: Soulik made landfall on 13 July 2013, bringing landslides and severe flooding to Taiwan and East China that killed at least 20 people. The scale of the damage reinforced calls for earlier evacuation warnings and stronger flood defenses in typhoon-prone coastal provinces.

evt-07-13-2016-prime-minister-of-the-uni.scenario: It is the afternoon of 13 July 2016 outside 10 Downing Street. You are David Cameron, about to give your final statement as Prime Minister after losing the Brexit referendum.
evt-07-13-2016-prime-minister-of-the-uni.prompt: What does Cameron do immediately after his farewell speech?

choices.text: He calls a general election before leaving office
He recommends the Queen invite Theresa May to form a new government
He appoints his successor directly without royal involvement
He stays on as caretaker until a full leadership election concludes

evt-07-13-2016-prime-minister-of-the-uni.butterflyEffect: Cameron went straight to Buckingham Palace and advised the Queen to invite Theresa May to form a government. Because rival candidates withdrew, May became PM that same evening without a full leadership contest, and she inherited the task of negotiating Britain's exit from the EU.

evt-07-13-2020-naya-rivera.scenario: It is July 8, 2020, on Lake Piru, California. Rescuers pull an unmoving rental boat to shore and find only a sunburned four-year-old boy aboard, alone. You are the sheriff's deputy taking his account of what happened.
evt-07-13-2020-naya-rivera.prompt: What does the boy tell investigators about his mother's final moments?

choices.text: He was alone the entire trip and never saw her
She lifted him back onto the boat but couldn't climb back up herself
She fell overboard while he was asleep below deck
She swam ahead to find help and never returned

evt-07-13-2020-naya-rivera.butterflyEffect: Naya Rivera had swum with her son, lifted him back onto the boat, but was unable to pull herself up and slipped under the water. After a five-day search of the lake, her body was recovered on July 13, 2020. The tragedy prompted renewed public attention to open-water swim safety and a wave of tributes from the Glee cast and fans.

evt-07-14-1223-louis-viii-of-france.scenario: It is 14 July 1223, and you have just become King of France as Louis VIII, called "the Lion." The south of your realm remains riddled with Cathar heretics, and the Church is pressing you to act where your father hesitated.
evt-07-14-1223-louis-viii-of-france.prompt: What campaign does the new king undertake to extend royal authority?

choices.text: He leads the Albigensian Crusade against the Cathars in the south
He wages war against the Holy Roman Emperor in Burgundy
He invades England again to reclaim the throne he was once offered
He focuses entirely on administrative reform in the Île-de-France

evt-07-14-1223-louis-viii-of-france.butterflyEffect: Louis VIII personally led the Albigensian Crusade into Languedoc in 1226, extending direct royal control over southern France. He died of dysentery during the campaign, but the conquest paved the way for the eventual annexation of the south under his son, Louis IX.

evt-07-14-1789-storming-of-the-bastille.scenario: It is the morning of 14 July 1789. You are among the Parisian crowd that has already seized muskets from the Hôtel des Invalides, but you have no gunpowder to fire them. Word spreads that the Bastille fortress holds a large store of powder.
evt-07-14-1789-storming-of-the-bastille.prompt: What does the crowd do next?

choices.text: Attack the Palais Royal to arrest suspected royalist officers
Storm the Bastille to seize its gunpowder and arms
March instead on the Palace of Versailles to confront the king directly
Disperse and wait for the National Assembly to negotiate

evt-07-14-1789-storming-of-the-bastille.butterflyEffect: The insurgents stormed the Bastille after four hours of fighting, killing the governor and seizing its powder stores. The fortress held only seven prisoners, but its fall became the symbolic flashpoint of the French Revolution, commemorated ever since as Bastille Day.

evt-07-14-1791-priestley-riots.scenario: It is 14 July 1791 in Birmingham. A dinner is being held to mark the second anniversary of the storming of the Bastille, and a hostile crowd is gathering outside, angry at dissenters like Joseph Priestley for their sympathy with the French Revolution.
evt-07-14-1791-priestley-riots.prompt: As a local magistrate, what do you do as the crowd's anger boils over?

choices.text: Negotiate directly with the rioters to cancel the dinner
Call out the militia at once to protect Priestley's house and meeting houses
Arrest Priestley himself to calm the crowd
Delay sending troops, allowing the crowd to attack dissenters' property unchecked

evt-07-14-1791-priestley-riots.butterflyEffect: The mob went on to burn Priestley's house, laboratory, and papers, along with several other dissenting meeting houses and homes over four days of rioting. Priestley fled to London and later emigrated to the United States, and the riots became a notorious symbol of intolerance toward religious and political dissent in Georgian England.

evt-07-14-1798-alien-and-sedition-acts.scenario: It is July 1798, and you are a Federalist congressman weighing whether to back a new bill criminalizing false or malicious criticism of the federal government amid fears of French subversion.
evt-07-14-1798-alien-and-sedition-acts.prompt: What argument should you make to justify passing the Sedition Act?

choices.text: It is needed to guard against French-inspired subversion during a national crisis
It will strengthen protections for a free press
It defends states' rights against federal overreach
It is primarily meant to regulate interstate commerce

evt-07-14-1798-alien-and-sedition-acts.butterflyEffect: The Act passed, but prosecutions of Democratic-Republican journalists were widely seen as political persecution rather than security measures. Public backlash helped Thomas Jefferson defeat Adams in the 1800 election and shaped early American debates over free speech.

evt-07-14-1865-first-ascent-of-the-matte.scenario: It is July 14, 1865. You are part of Edward Whymper's seven-man team beginning the descent from the Matterhorn's newly conquered summit, roped together along the steep, icy north face.
evt-07-14-1865-first-ascent-of-the-matte.prompt: What precaution should the team take to keep one slip from endangering everyone?

choices.text: Untie from each other and descend individually for speed
Anchor the rope securely to the rock rather than relying on simple hand-ties
Descend as quickly as possible before weather worsens
Rest longer at the summit before starting down

evt-07-14-1865-first-ascent-of-the-matte.butterflyEffect: The rope connecting the climbers was not properly anchored, and when Hadow slipped, he pulled Croz, Hudson, and Douglas to their deaths; only the rope's snap spared Whymper and the Taugwalders. An inquiry cleared the survivors of cutting the rope, but the disaster made the triumphant first ascent one of mountaineering's most haunting tragedies and pushed for stricter roping practices.

evt-07-14-1874-chicago-fire-of-1874.scenario: It is July 14, 1874, and you are a Chicago fire captain rushing to a blaze spreading rapidly through the neighborhoods just south of the Loop, only three years after the Great Chicago Fire devastated the city.
evt-07-14-1874-chicago-fire-of-1874.prompt: What should your crew do to keep the fire from consuming even more of the district?

choices.text: Focus only on rescuing valuables from burning homes
Wait for rain to help extinguish the blaze
Demolish buildings ahead of the flames to create a firebreak
Fight the fire solely at its point of origin

evt-07-14-1874-chicago-fire-of-1874.butterflyEffect: Firefighters demolished structures to create firebreaks, but the fire still destroyed 812 buildings and killed 20 people, displacing many Jewish and African-American families who never returned to the neighborhood. The disaster pushed the city to tighten building codes and fire regulations already prompted by the 1871 fire.

evt-07-14-1881-billy-the-kid.scenario: It is the night of July 14, 1881, in Fort Sumner, New Mexico. You are Sheriff Pat Garrett, sitting in a darkened bedroom, when a figure you believe to be Billy the Kid steps inside and asks in Spanish, "¿Quién es?"
evt-07-14-1881-billy-the-kid.prompt: What should Garrett do the instant the figure enters the dark room?

choices.text: Fire immediately at the figure in the dark
Announce himself and demand surrender first
Strike a match to identify the man before acting
Wait silently for backup to arrive

evt-07-14-1881-billy-the-kid.butterflyEffect: Garrett fired without hesitation, killing Billy the Kid on the spot. The shooting made Garrett a controversial celebrity, and his own account of the hunt helped cement the outlaw's legend as one of the Old West's most famous figures.

evt-07-14-1902-st-mark-s-campanile.scenario: It is 14 July 1902 in Venice, and cracks have been spreading through the ancient brickwork of St Mark's Campanile for days. City engineers have cleared the square, and the great bell tower now leans dangerously over the Piazza.
evt-07-14-1902-st-mark-s-campanile.prompt: What happens to the medieval campanile that day, and how is it treated afterward?

choices.text: It collapses and a modern steel tower replaces it
It is shored up and survives standing but visibly damaged
It collapses and is rebuilt as an exact replica on the same site
It collapses and the site is left as rubble in memory of the loss

evt-07-14-1902-st-mark-s-campanile.butterflyEffect: The Campanile collapsed completely that afternoon, but the evacuation meant no one was killed. Venetian authorities adopted the motto "dov'era, com'era" ("where it was, as it was") and rebuilt it stone for stone on the same site, completing the replica in 1912.

evt-07-14-1902-agustin-lizarraga.scenario: It is July 1902, and you are a Peruvian farmer climbing through cloud forest above the Urubamba River, following local guides who speak of stone ruins hidden on a ridge nobody outside the valley has ever mapped.
evt-07-14-1902-agustin-lizarraga.prompt: What do you do after finding the overgrown Inca ruins at Machu Picchu?

choices.text: Guide a team of European scientists there within the month
Send word immediately to newspapers in Lima announcing the find
Claim legal ownership of the site and begin excavating for treasure
Carve your name and the date on a wall, then return quietly to farming

evt-07-14-1902-agustin-lizarraga.butterflyEffect: Lizárraga scratched his name and the date onto a wall but otherwise returned to his farming life, and word of the ruins stayed largely local. Nine years later, American explorer Hiram Bingham was led to the same site by local farmers and publicized it internationally, so Bingham's name became attached to the "discovery" while Lizárraga's earlier visit was nearly forgotten by history.

evt-07-14-1916-battle-of-delville-wood.scenario: It is mid-July 1916 near Longueval on the Somme. You command the South African Brigade, ordered to seize and hold Delville Wood as German artillery pounds the tree line and counterattacks mass on your flanks.
evt-07-14-1916-battle-of-delville-wood.prompt: What are your orders regarding the wood?

choices.text: Withdraw quietly to safer ground at Longueval
Negotiate a local truce with the opposing German unit
Hold the wood at all costs as ordered by brigade command
Abandon the position and fall back to the original start line

evt-07-14-1916-battle-of-delville-wood.butterflyEffect: The brigade held Delville Wood for six days against relentless bombardment and counterattacks, suffering catastrophic losses before being relieved. The battle became a defining moment of South African memory of the First World War, commemorated at the Delville Wood Cemetery and memorial in France.

evt-07-14-1987-montreal-flood-of-1987.scenario: It is early afternoon on July 14, 1987. You are driving on the sunken Décarie Expressway in Montreal when a sudden torrential downpour begins dumping more than 100 mm of rain in under three hours, and water is rising fast around your car.
evt-07-14-1987-montreal-flood-of-1987.prompt: What should you do as the sunken highway fills with water?

choices.text: Abandon the car immediately and climb to higher ground
Try to drive faster to outrun the rising water
Call for a tow truck and remain parked
Stay inside the car and wait for the water to recede

evt-07-14-1987-montreal-flood-of-1987.butterflyEffect: Many motorists were trapped as the Décarie filled completely; two people died, one drowned in a submerged car and another electrocuted. The disaster exposed how badly Montreal's sewers were overwhelmed and pushed the city toward major drainage and flood-control upgrades.

evt-07-14-2002-jacques-chirac.scenario: It is Bastille Day, 14 July 2002, and you stand among the crowd lining the Champs-Élysées as President Jacques Chirac's open car rolls past during the annual military parade.
evt-07-14-2002-jacques-chirac.prompt: What happens when a lone gunman raises a hidden rifle toward Chirac's motorcade?

choices.text: Chirac's driver crashes the car while swerving away
He fires several rounds, wounding a nearby official
Bystanders tackle him before he can fire a second shot
Security guards shoot him dead on the spot

evt-07-14-2002-jacques-chirac.butterflyEffect: Maxime Brunerie, a young far-right extremist, fired once and missed before bystanders wrestled him to the ground; Chirac was unharmed and the parade continued. The attack exposed Brunerie's ties to the neo-Nazi group Unité Radicale, which French authorities banned within weeks, and it added to public alarm over far-right extremism during a year when Jean-Marie Le Pen had already reached the presidential runoff.

evt-07-14-2003-valerie-plame.scenario: It is July 2003. You are a Washington newspaper columnist who has just learned, from senior administration sources, that the wife of a prominent Iraq War critic works for the CIA.
evt-07-14-2003-valerie-plame.prompt: What do you do with this information about the CIA officer's identity?

choices.text: Refuse to use the information and destroy your notes
Take the story straight to a congressional committee instead
Publish her name and CIA role in your column immediately
Quietly warn the CIA that her cover may be blown

evt-07-14-2003-valerie-plame.butterflyEffect: Columnist Robert Novak published Valerie Plame's identity, triggering a federal investigation into who leaked it. The probe led to the perjury and obstruction conviction of Vice President Cheney's chief of staff, Scooter Libby, and reignited debate over the Bush administration's justifications for the Iraq War.

evt-07-14-2015-nasa.scenario: It is 14 July 2015 aboard mission control for NASA's New Horizons probe. The spacecraft is about to make its closest approach to Pluto, but it cannot both aim its instruments at the planet and beam a live signal back to Earth at the same time.
evt-07-14-2015-nasa.prompt: What does the mission team have the probe do during closest approach?

choices.text: Prioritize collecting science data over communicating with Earth
Slow down and enter orbit around Pluto instead of a flyby
Maintain a continuous live signal to Earth throughout the flyby
Abort the flyby to preserve fuel for a return trip

evt-07-14-2015-nasa.butterflyEffect: New Horizons turned its instruments toward Pluto and stayed silent for the flyby, only phoning home hours later to confirm success. The data revealed nitrogen ice glaciers and towering mountains, overturning the old image of Pluto as a dead, frozen rock.

evt-07-14-2016-2016-nice-truck-attack.scenario: It is the evening of July 14, 2016. You are a police officer stationed near the Promenade des Anglais in Nice as Bastille Day fireworks end, when a 19-tonne cargo truck suddenly veers into the crowd ahead of you.
evt-07-14-2016-2016-nice-truck-attack.prompt: What must you do to stop the truck attack in progress?

choices.text: Radio for backup and wait for reinforcements before acting
Open fire on the driver to stop the vehicle
Try to wave the truck to a stop
Chase the truck on foot to catch up

evt-07-14-2016-2016-nice-truck-attack.butterflyEffect: Officers opened fire on the driver, Mohamed Lahouaiej-Bouhlel, killing him and ending the attack after he had already killed 86 people. The massacre led France and other countries to install permanent vehicle barriers at public gatherings and rethink crowd security at outdoor events.

evt-07-15-1410-crown-of-the-kingdom-of-p.scenario: It is the morning of 15 July 1410 near Grunwald. Teutonic heralds ride up and thrust two naked swords into the ground before you and Grand Duke Vytautas, taunting the Polish-Lithuanian host to fight or flee.
evt-07-15-1410-crown-of-the-kingdom-of-p.prompt: How do you respond to the Teutonic Knights' sword challenge?

choices.text: Send envoys to negotiate a truce first
Withdraw the army to avoid a trap
Accept the challenge and order the advance
Wait for reinforcements before engaging

evt-07-15-1410-crown-of-the-kingdom-of-p.butterflyEffect: Jogaila accepted the challenge and battle was joined; the Teutonic army was crushed and Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen was killed. The defeat broke the Order's military dominance in the Baltic and led to the Peace of Thorn, beginning its long decline.

evt-07-15-1815-hms-bellerophon-1786.scenario: It's 15 July 1815. Defeated after Waterloo and blockaded by the Royal Navy near Rochefort, you are Emperor Napoleon Bonaparte, rowing out to surrender aboard HMS Bellerophon rather than fall into Bourbon or Prussian hands.
evt-07-15-1815-hms-bellerophon-1786.prompt: What do you request from Captain Frederick Maitland as terms of surrender?

choices.text: Immediate return to exile on Elba
A negotiated restoration of his throne
Asylum and safe passage to live in England
Passage to lead French exiles in America

evt-07-15-1815-hms-bellerophon-1786.butterflyEffect: Maitland accepted no formal terms, and the British government refused Napoleon's hoped-for asylum in England. Instead he was exiled to the remote island of Saint Helena, where he remained until his death in 1821.

evt-07-15-1870-rupert-s-land.scenario: It is 15 July 1870 at the Red River settlement. Rupert's Land has just passed from the Hudson's Bay Company to Canada, and Louis Riel's provisional government has spent months negotiating terms for the Métis population living there.
evt-07-15-1870-rupert-s-land.prompt: What immediate step follows the formal transfer of Rupert's Land to Canada on this day?

choices.text: The Hudson's Bay Company retains full governing control as before
Manitoba is created as a new Canadian province with negotiated Métis protections
The land is returned entirely to independent Indigenous governance
The territory is annexed outright by the United States

evt-07-15-1870-rupert-s-land.butterflyEffect: Manitoba was created as Canada's fifth province the very same day, under the Manitoba Act negotiated by Riel's delegates, which promised land grants and French-language and Catholic school rights. Many of those promises were later broken or delayed, fueling Métis grievances that resurfaced in the 1885 North-West Rebellion and Riel's execution.

evt-07-15-1946-north-borneo.scenario: It is 1946, and you are a director of the British North Borneo Company, staring at ledgers showing the territory devastated by Japanese occupation and Allied bombing, far beyond the Company's means to rebuild.
evt-07-15-1946-north-borneo.prompt: What did the Company decide to do with its administration of North Borneo?

choices.text: Declare North Borneo an independent republic
Cede the territory's administration to the British Crown
Sell the territory to the Sultan of Brunei
Request that the United States administer it as a trust territory

evt-07-15-1946-north-borneo.butterflyEffect: The Company ceded its rights and administration to the British Crown, and North Borneo became a Crown Colony on July 15, 1946. It remained under direct British rule until 1963, when it joined the Federation of Malaysia as the state of Sabah.

evt-07-15-1954-boeing-367-80.scenario: It is 15 July 1954 at Boeing Field, and you watch the company's radical new four-engine jet prototype, the 367-80, lift off on its maiden flight, a private gamble built without a guaranteed buyer.
evt-07-15-1954-boeing-367-80.prompt: What did the successful first flight of the Dash 80 lead Boeing to do next?

choices.text: Sell the prototype design outright to a European manufacturer
Develop both a military tanker and a commercial airliner from the same design
Abandon the jet design in favor of continued propeller airliners
Restrict the design to cargo transport use only

evt-07-15-1954-boeing-367-80.butterflyEffect: The single Dash 80 airframe became the shared basis for two production lines: the KC-135 Stratotanker for the Air Force and the 707 for commercial airlines. That dual-use strategy let Boeing recoup its investment quickly and launch the jet age for American passenger aviation.

evt-07-15-1966-vietnam-war.scenario: It's 15 July 1966 in Quảng Trị Province. You command a Marine battalion landing by helicopter as Operation Hastings begins, tasked with intercepting NVA regulars who have crossed the Demilitarized Zone into South Vietnam.
evt-07-15-1966-vietnam-war.prompt: What is the immediate objective of Operation Hastings?

choices.text: Establish a permanent airbase at Khe Sanh
Capture the North Vietnamese capital of Hanoi
Negotiate a local ceasefire with NVA commanders
Block and drive the NVA division back across the DMZ

evt-07-15-1966-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: US and South Vietnamese forces fought the NVA's 324B Division to a costly standstill and pushed it back across the DMZ. The operation revealed regular North Vietnamese units were now fighting conventionally in the south, foreshadowing the grinding battles around the DMZ that followed, including Con Thien and Khe Sanh.

evt-07-15-1975-space-race.scenario: You are astronaut Thomas Stafford, commanding the Apollo capsule launched on 15 July 1975. Hours earlier a Soyuz carrying cosmonauts Alexei Leonov and Valeri Kubasov lifted off from Baikonur for the first joint US-Soviet spaceflight.
evt-07-15-1975-space-race.prompt: What happens when the two craft successfully dock two days later?

choices.text: The crews exchange full technical blueprints of their spacecraft
The crews swap capsules and land in each other's country
The two crews perform a joint spacewalk together
The astronauts and cosmonauts shake hands through the open hatch

evt-07-15-1975-space-race.butterflyEffect: Stafford and Leonov shook hands through the open hatch, a moment broadcast worldwide as a symbol of détente. The Apollo-Soyuz Test Project became the template for later cooperation, foreshadowing Shuttle-Mir and the International Space Station.

evt-07-15-1979-president-of-the-united-s.scenario: It is the evening of July 15, 1979, and you are one of millions of Americans watching President Carter address the nation on live television about long gas lines, the energy crisis, and what he calls a crisis of confidence.
evt-07-15-1979-president-of-the-united-s.prompt: What did Carter do just days after delivering this address?

choices.text: Announced he would not seek reelection
Requested resignations from his entire Cabinet
Declared a national emergency over oil prices
Resigned the presidency

evt-07-15-1979-president-of-the-united-s.butterflyEffect: Carter abruptly asked his entire Cabinet to submit resignations and accepted several, including his Treasury and Energy secretaries, in a jarring shakeup that undercut the speech's message of unity. Though initially well-received, the address became remembered as the "malaise speech" (a word Carter never actually said), symbolizing a presidency seen as adrift and helping pave the way for Reagan's 1980 victory.

evt-07-15-1983-nintendo.scenario: It is 15 July 1983 in Japan, and Nintendo is launching the Family Computer, its first cartridge-based home console, into a marketplace still shaken by earlier video game busts.
evt-07-15-1983-nintendo.prompt: What pricing strategy did Nintendo choose to win over Japanese households?

choices.text: Price it well below rival consoles to maximize household adoption
Bundle it exclusively with expensive arcade conversion cartridges
Lease the console monthly through electronics retailers
Position it as a premium machine for hobbyist enthusiasts only

evt-07-15-1983-nintendo.butterflyEffect: Nintendo priced the Famicom at just 14,800 yen, far cheaper than rival machines, while delivering arcade-quality graphics through custom chips. That affordability and quality let it dominate Japan, and its Western relaunch as the NES in 1985 helped revive the entire video game industry after the 1983 North American crash.

evt-07-15-1996-belgian-air-force.scenario: It is 15 July 1996 and a Belgian Air Force C-130 Hercules is on approach to Eindhoven Airbase, carrying the Royal Netherlands Army marching band home from a ceremony. During final approach the aircraft strikes a flock of birds.
evt-07-15-1996-belgian-air-force.prompt: What did the subsequent investigation identify as the cause of the crash?

choices.text: A bird strike disabled multiple engines on approach
Pilot error during a low-altitude flyover maneuver
A fuel contamination issue traced to ground refueling
A structural fatigue failure in the wing spar

evt-07-15-1996-belgian-air-force.butterflyEffect: The C-130 lost engine power after ingesting birds on approach and crashed short of the runway, killing most of the band. The disaster pushed European military aviation to overhaul bird-strike mitigation at airbases, including tighter wildlife management near runways and stricter engine-ingestion certification reviews.

evt-07-15-2002-taliban.scenario: It is 15 July 2002 in a federal courtroom in Alexandria, Virginia. You are John Walker Lindh, the young American captured fighting alongside the Taliban in Afghanistan, and prosecutors have offered you a deal to avoid the most serious charges.
evt-07-15-2002-taliban.prompt: What plea do you enter to avoid a possible life sentence on terrorism charges?

choices.text: Plead guilty to all original charges including attempted murder
Plead guilty to two lesser charges in exchange for dropped terrorism counts
Accept a life sentence without any negotiated plea deal
Plead not guilty and take the case to a full jury trial

evt-07-15-2002-taliban.butterflyEffect: Lindh pleaded guilty to two lesser counts—supplying services to the Taliban and carrying an explosive device—in exchange for the government dropping charges tied to the death of a CIA officer, receiving a 20-year sentence. His case became a touchstone in debates over how the U.S. should prosecute citizens captured fighting for enemy forces abroad; he was released in 2019 after serving 17 years.

evt-07-15-2006-x-social-network.scenario: You are a co-founder at the San Francisco startup Odeo in July 2006, watching your side project—a simple service for sharing short status updates by text message—open to the public for the first time.
evt-07-15-2006-x-social-network.prompt: What is this new service designed to let users do?

choices.text: Host and stream video podcasts
Share and organize photo albums
Build professional networking profiles
Send short 140-character status updates via SMS

evt-07-15-2006-x-social-network.butterflyEffect: The service, soon renamed Twitter, grew from a niche SMS tool into a global microblogging platform that reshaped breaking news, politics, and celebrity culture. In 2023 it was rebranded X after Elon Musk's acquisition of the company.

evt-07-15-2009-space-shuttle-program.scenario: It's 15 July 2009 at Kennedy Space Center. After five scrubbed attempts from weather and a hydrogen leak, you're aboard Space Shuttle Endeavour on STS-127, tasked with finishing assembly of Japan's Kibo laboratory on the ISS.
evt-07-15-2009-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What key payload does this mission deliver to the ISS?

choices.text: Kibo's Exposed Facility and Experiment Logistics Module
The US Destiny laboratory module
The Canadarm2 robotic arm
A new set of solar arrays for station power

evt-07-15-2009-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: Endeavour delivered Kibo's Exposed Facility and Experiment Logistics Module, giving the ISS its first external science platform. The mission, one of the longest shuttle flights ever, marked a major step toward completing the station before the shuttle program's retirement in 2011.

evt-07-15-2018-mario-mandzukic.scenario: It is the 2018 World Cup final in Moscow, and Antoine Griezmann steps up to take a free kick just outside the Croatian box in the first half.
evt-07-15-2018-mario-mandzukic.prompt: What happened when Griezmann's free kick reached the Croatian penalty area?

choices.text: It deflected off Mandžukić's head into his own goal
It was cleared off the line by a Croatian defender
The goalkeeper punched it out for a corner
Mandžukić headed it clear for a goal kick

evt-07-15-2018-mario-mandzukic.butterflyEffect: The free kick deflected off Mario Mandžukić's head and looped into his own net, the first own goal ever scored in a World Cup final. France capitalized on the early lead and went on to win 4-2, claiming their second World Cup title.

evt-07-16-1054-east-west-schism.scenario: It is July 16, 1054, inside the Hagia Sophia. Cardinal Humbert, papal legate, has just laid a bull of excommunication against Patriarch Michael Cerularius on the altar during the liturgy and stormed out toward Rome.
evt-07-16-1054-east-west-schism.prompt: What does Patriarch Cerularius do in response?

choices.text: Accept the Pope's claim to universal jurisdiction
Ignore the bull and continue services as before
Excommunicate the papal legates in return
Appeal to Emperor Constantine IX to arbitrate the dispute

evt-07-16-1054-east-west-schism.butterflyEffect: Cerularius convened his own synod and excommunicated Humbert and the other legates in return. Because Pope Leo IX had already died, the legates' authority was questionable, yet the mutual excommunications hardened into the lasting break between the Catholic and Orthodox Churches, a division still unhealed today.

evt-07-16-1232-muhammad-i-of-granada.scenario: It is 1232, and you are Muhammad ibn Yusuf, having just seized power in your native Arjona by rebelling against Ibn Hud, the dominant strongman of Al-Andalus.
evt-07-16-1232-muhammad-i-of-granada.prompt: What move do you make to capitalize on the rebellion's momentum?

choices.text: Ally openly with Ibn Hud against the Christian kingdoms
Immediately request Castilian protection against Ibn Hud
March out and seize Córdoba and Seville while Ibn Hud is weak
Retreat and fortify only Arjona, avoiding further conflict

evt-07-16-1232-muhammad-i-of-granada.butterflyEffect: Muhammad briefly seized Córdoba and Seville before losing both back to Ibn Hud, retaining only Arjona and Jaén. In 1236 he betrayed Ibn Hud by helping Ferdinand III of Castile take Córdoba, then went on to seize Granada, Almería and Málaga, founding the Nasrid dynasty that made Granada the last independent Muslim state in Iberia for over two centuries.

evt-07-16-1377-richard-ii-of-england.scenario: It is 16 July 1377 at Westminster Abbey. You watch as ten-year-old Richard II is crowned King of England, too young to rule in his own right.
evt-07-16-1377-richard-ii-of-england.prompt: What governing arrangement is put in place because the new king is a child?

choices.text: A council of nobles governs in his name until he comes of age
The Pope appoints a regent from Rome
Parliament abolishes the monarchy temporarily
John of Gaunt is crowned co-king

evt-07-16-1377-richard-ii-of-england.butterflyEffect: A regency-style council of magnates, heavily influenced by his powerful uncle John of Gaunt, governed in Richard's name. Resentment over taxation under this arrangement helped spark the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, and Richard's later assertion of personal, autocratic rule eventually led to his deposition by Henry IV in 1399.

evt-07-16-1782-wolfgang-amadeus-mozart.scenario: It is 16 July 1782 at Vienna's Burgtheater, and you sit among the audience for the premiere of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's new German-language opera, Die Entführung aus dem Serail, commissioned by Emperor Joseph II himself for his National Theater.
evt-07-16-1782-wolfgang-amadeus-mozart.prompt: How does the court and public receive Mozart's ambitious new opera?

choices.text: It is judged too difficult for the singers and cancelled after one night
It is hailed as a triumph, proving German opera can rival Italian works
Court censors ban it for its harem setting
It is dismissed as a vulgar imitation of Turkish music and withdrawn

evt-07-16-1782-wolfgang-amadeus-mozart.butterflyEffect: The premiere was a genuine success, helping prove that German-language opera (singspiel) could rival the dominant Italian tradition. Joseph II reportedly told Mozart the work had 'too many notes'—a remark Mozart supposedly deflected with wit. The opera's popularity strengthened Mozart's reputation in Vienna and paved the way for later masterworks like The Magic Flute.

evt-07-16-1790-george-washington.scenario: You are a congressman in 1790 watching President Washington sign a bill settling the long, bitter dispute over where the nation's permanent capital will stand, part of a bargain struck over dinner with Jefferson, Hamilton, and Madison.
evt-07-16-1790-george-washington.prompt: What compromise persuaded Southern states to accept federal assumption of state war debts?

choices.text: Making Philadelphia the capital permanently
Banning slavery in all new federal territories
Keeping New York as the permanent capital
Locating the new national capital on the Potomac River

evt-07-16-1790-george-washington.butterflyEffect: The Residence Act placed the permanent capital on the Potomac River, satisfying Southern demands, while Philadelphia served as temporary capital for a decade during construction. The deal cemented federal financial credit under Hamilton's plan and gave rise to the city that would become Washington, D.C.

evt-07-16-1931-haile-selassie.scenario: It is 16 July 1931, and Emperor Haile Selassie presents Ethiopia's first written constitution, aiming to present his empire as a modern state to the wider world.
evt-07-16-1931-haile-selassie.prompt: What kind of government does the new constitution actually create?

choices.text: The monarchy is abolished in favor of a republic
Full voting rights are granted to all Ethiopian citizens
Legislative power is transferred entirely to regional nobles
A bicameral parliament is created while the emperor retains supreme authority

evt-07-16-1931-haile-selassie.butterflyEffect: The constitution established a bicameral parliament, but its members were appointed by the emperor and nobility rather than elected, leaving Haile Selassie's authority essentially absolute. It was mainly a gesture toward modernization ahead of growing international tensions with Italy, and was eventually replaced by a revised constitution in 1955 after the Italian occupation ended.

evt-07-16-1945-trinity-nuclear-test.scenario: It is 5:29 a.m. on July 16, 1945, in the New Mexico desert. You are among the scientists at base camp, uncertain whether the untested plutonium implosion design will work or simply fizzle after months of doubt.
evt-07-16-1945-trinity-nuclear-test.prompt: What happens when the device detonates?

choices.text: It detonates successfully, yielding roughly 25 kilotons of explosive force
It fails to detonate and must be defused by hand
It fizzles, producing only a minor chemical explosion
It detonates far beyond predictions, forcing a mass evacuation

evt-07-16-1945-trinity-nuclear-test.butterflyEffect: The bomb performed as designed, releasing an explosive force equivalent to about 25 kilotons of TNT and confirming the implosion design was viable. This success cleared the way for the Fat Man bomb dropped on Nagasaki weeks later and opened the nuclear age.

evt-07-16-1951-the-catcher-in-the-rye.scenario: It is 16 July 1951, and Little, Brown and Company release J. D. Salinger's debut novel, following a disillusioned teenager named Holden Caulfield through New York City.
evt-07-16-1951-the-catcher-in-the-rye.prompt: What fate awaits this novel in American schools and libraries in the decades ahead?

choices.text: US obscenity laws force it to be published only in Europe
School boards immediately adopt it as required reading nationwide
It is ignored by critics and sells only a few hundred copies
It becomes a bestseller but is repeatedly banned or challenged in schools

evt-07-16-1951-the-catcher-in-the-rye.butterflyEffect: The Catcher in the Rye became a huge bestseller and a touchstone for teenage alienation, yet its profanity and frank content also made it one of the most frequently banned or challenged books in American schools for decades. Its cultural weight grew darker still when it was found in the possession of Mark David Chapman after he shot John Lennon, and later near John Hinckley Jr.'s attempt on Ronald Reagan.

evt-07-16-1965-army-of-the-republic-of-v.scenario: You are a South Vietnamese officer who has long suspected Colonel Phạm Ngọc Thảo of secretly serving Hanoi while orchestrating coup after coup within the ARVN's own ranks. Word now reaches you that his double life has finally caught up with him.
evt-07-16-1965-army-of-the-republic-of-v.prompt: What happens to Colonel Thảo after his communist ties and coup plotting are exposed?

choices.text: He escapes north and joins the Viet Minh openly
He is promoted to general as a reward for loyalty
He is exiled to France for the remainder of the war
He is captured and killed by South Vietnamese government forces

evt-07-16-1965-army-of-the-republic-of-v.butterflyEffect: Thảo was captured and killed by government forces in July 1965, ending one of the deepest and longest-running communist infiltrations of the South Vietnamese military. His decade of coup-plotting had already destabilized several Saigon governments, and his story later became emblematic of how thoroughly Hanoi's agents had penetrated the ARVN.

evt-07-16-1983-sikorsky-s-61.scenario: It is the evening of 16 July 1983, and you are aboard a British Airways Helicopters Sikorsky S-61N descending toward St Mary's, Isles of Scilly, through a bank of thick fog.
evt-07-16-1983-sikorsky-s-61.prompt: What goes wrong as the helicopter makes its final approach?

choices.text: The engines run out of fuel, forcing a ditching
The pilots misjudge their descent in the fog and the aircraft strikes the sea
The helicopter collides with another aircraft hidden in the fog
A rotor mechanism fails, causing loss of control

evt-07-16-1983-sikorsky-s-61.butterflyEffect: The helicopter struck the sea short of the airport after the crew misjudged their altitude in the fog, killing 20 of the 26 people aboard. The subsequent inquiry pushed for stricter instrument-approach procedures and altimeter-setting protocols for helicopter services to remote islands, reshaping safety practice for offshore and inter-island flights.

evt-07-16-1990-1990-luzon-earthquake.scenario: It is 4:26 p.m. on 16 July 1990. Violent shaking rips through Central Luzon and the Cordillera as the Philippine and Digdig Faults rupture beneath you. You are inside a multi-story building in the region when the floor begins to lurch.
evt-07-16-1990-1990-luzon-earthquake.prompt: What is the correct action to take as the shaking intensifies indoors?

choices.text: Get on the phone right away to call for help before moving
Stand in a doorway and lean out of a window to watch the street
Run outside immediately to escape the building
Drop to the floor, take cover under sturdy furniture, and hold on until the shaking stops

evt-07-16-1990-1990-luzon-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The magnitude-7.8 quake produced a 125 km surface rupture from Dingalan to Kayapa along the Philippine and Digdig Faults, with the epicenter near Rizal, Nueva Ecija. Roughly 1,621 people died, most in Central Luzon and the Cordillera, and the newly exposed Digdig Fault reshaped how Philippine seismologists mapped and monitored earthquake hazards on Luzon.

evt-07-16-2007-2007-chuetsu-offshore-ear.scenario: It is 10:13 a.m. on 16 July 2007. A magnitude-6.6 quake tears through a previously unmapped offshore fault near Niigata. You are a control-room operator at the nearby Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant, the largest of its kind in the world, when the seismic alarms sound.
evt-07-16-2007-2007-chuetsu-offshore-ear.prompt: What is the immediate, correct response to the seismic alert?

choices.text: Keep the reactors running to avoid disrupting power output
Wait for confirmation from Tokyo before taking any action
Evacuate the control room without shutting down the reactors
Trigger automatic reactor shutdown and follow emergency protocol

evt-07-16-2007-2007-chuetsu-offshore-ear.butterflyEffect: The reactors did automatically shut down, but a transformer fire broke out and a small radioactive leak occurred; engineers later found the shaking had exceeded the plant's original design assumptions. The plant stayed offline for over a year, and the incident pushed regulators worldwide to reassess seismic safety standards for nuclear facilities. In the town itself, eleven people died and 342 mostly older wooden buildings collapsed.

evt-07-16-2008-2008-chinese-milk-scandal.scenario: It is mid-2008, and you work in quality control at Sanlu Group as reports mount that infants fed on the company's formula are developing kidney stones. Your tests confirm melamine has been added to disguise diluted milk as high-protein product.
evt-07-16-2008-2008-chinese-milk-scandal.prompt: What should you do with this information?

choices.text: Stay silent to protect the company's reputation
Report the adulteration to food safety regulators immediately
Wait for more complaints before taking any action
Alter the test results to hide the melamine

evt-07-16-2008-2008-chinese-milk-scandal.butterflyEffect: Sanlu executives instead concealed the danger for months, and melamine adulteration was later found across dozens of Chinese dairy brands, sickening around 300,000 children and killing at least six infants. The scandal triggered global bans on Chinese dairy imports and forced Beijing to overhaul its food-safety laws and regulatory agencies.

evt-07-16-2009-teoh-beng-hock.scenario: News breaks that Teoh Beng Hock, a political aide questioned overnight by anti-corruption investigators, has been found dead on a rooftop below their offices. Public anger is mounting fast.
evt-07-16-2009-teoh-beng-hock.prompt: What did opposition leaders and the public demand in response to his death?

choices.text: A Royal Commission of Inquiry into his death
Dissolution of the Anti-Corruption Commission
Declaration of martial law in Selangor
Immediate resignation of the Prime Minister

evt-07-16-2009-teoh-beng-hock.butterflyEffect: Sustained pressure led the government to establish a Royal Commission of Inquiry, which found that intimidating interrogation tactics likely contributed to his death. The case became a lasting symbol in Malaysian politics of demands for reform of the Anti-Corruption Commission's detention and interrogation procedures.

evt-07-16-2013-bihar-school-meal-poisoni.scenario: You are a health inspector called to a village school kitchen in Bihar after dozens of children fell gravely ill from their free midday meal. You must trace the contamination to its source.
evt-07-16-2013-bihar-school-meal-poisoni.prompt: What did investigators identify as the likely cause of the poisoning?

choices.text: Rice spoiled from improper drying
Cooking oil stored in a reused pesticide container
Lentils past their expiration date
Contaminated well water used for cooking

evt-07-16-2013-bihar-school-meal-poisoni.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the cooking oil had been stored in a container previously used for the pesticide monocrotophos. The tragedy forced the Bihar government to overhaul the Midday Meal Scheme, mandating separate storage for food and chemicals and better training for school cooks nationwide.

evt-07-16-2015-united-states-marine-corp.scenario: News spreads of a gunman opening fire on unarmed Marines and a sailor at two military facilities in Chattanooga. In the aftermath, officials and lawmakers debate how to protect personnel at recruiting stations across the country.
evt-07-16-2015-united-states-marine-corp.prompt: What policy change did the attack push officials to seriously consider?

choices.text: Closing all military recruiting stations nationwide
Arming only civilian security guards, not service members
Doubling the number of recruiters per station
Allowing military personnel to carry firearms at recruiting stations

evt-07-16-2015-united-states-marine-corp.butterflyEffect: The shootings intensified a national debate over allowing military recruiters and reservists to carry firearms at their duty stations, historically treated as gun-free zones. In the following months, the Pentagon and several state governors moved to authorize limited arming of personnel at select military and National Guard facilities.

evt-07-17-1453-battle-of-castillon.scenario: It's 17 July 1453 near Castillon, and you serve under John Talbot, Earl of Shrewsbury. Scouts wrongly report the French retreating from their fortified camp, and Talbot orders his vanguard to attack alone, ahead of the main English force.

choices.text: Waits for the full army before advancing
Sends scouts to verify the French position first
Attacks immediately with his vanguard, believing the French are retreating
Retreats to regroup his forces

evt-07-17-1453-battle-of-castillon.butterflyEffect: Talbot's premature assault let French field artillery cut down his men piecemeal, and Talbot himself was killed in the rout. The defeat ended English hopes of recovering Gascony, effectively closing the Hundred Years' War and confirming artillery's growing dominance on European battlefields.

evt-07-17-1771-dene.scenario: It's July 17, 1771, on the Coppermine River in what is now Nunavut. You are travelling with Samuel Hearne's expedition, and the Dene guides led by Matonabbee are preparing to fall upon a sleeping Inuit camp at what will become known as Bloody Falls.
evt-07-17-1771-dene.prompt: What does Hearne later say he did as the attack began?

choices.text: He personally led the attack on the camp
He secretly warned the Inuit camp beforehand
He abandoned the expedition immediately afterward
He tried to intervene but was unable to stop the massacre

evt-07-17-1771-dene.butterflyEffect: Hearne recorded that he tried to persuade the Dene against the attack but was unable to prevent it, and the Inuit camp was massacred. His published journal became one of the most vivid firsthand accounts of violence during European-guided exploration, shaping how later generations understood contact between Indigenous nations in the Arctic.

evt-07-17-1850-william-cranch-bond.scenario: It is July 1850 at Harvard College Observatory. You watch William Cranch Bond and John Adams Whipple carefully align the Great Refractor telescope on a bright star, testing whether the new daguerreotype process can capture light from beyond the solar system.
evt-07-17-1850-william-cranch-bond.prompt: What historic image did Bond and Whipple succeed in capturing that night?

choices.text: The first daguerreotype photograph of a star, Vega
The first photograph of a solar eclipse
The first photograph of the surface of the Moon
The first photograph of Halley's Comet

evt-07-17-1850-william-cranch-bond.butterflyEffect: They produced the first successful daguerreotype of a star other than the Sun, the bright star Vega. Their success proved photography could record celestial objects invisible to the naked eye on film, launching the field of astrophotography that would later reveal galaxies and nebulae.

evt-07-17-1863-new-zealand-wars.scenario: It is July 1863 and you march with General Duncan Cameron's British troops toward the Mangatawhiri River, the boundary of the Kingitanga Māori movement's territory in the Waikato.
evt-07-17-1863-new-zealand-wars.prompt: What was the purpose of Cameron's invasion of the Waikato?

choices.text: Escort missionaries safely through Māori territory
Crush the Kingitanga movement and seize Waikato land for settlers
Negotiate a permanent land-sharing treaty with the Kingitanga
Withdraw British forces from the North Island entirely

evt-07-17-1863-new-zealand-wars.butterflyEffect: Cameron's campaign aimed to crush the Kingitanga movement and open fertile Waikato lands to European settlement. Following the Māori defeat, the New Zealand Settlements Act allowed the confiscation of vast tracts of Māori land, a grievance that shaped Māori-Crown relations for generations.

evt-07-17-1918-rms-carpathia.scenario: It's July 17, 1918, and RMS Carpathia, the ship famed for rescuing Titanic's survivors six years earlier, is steaming in convoy off the Irish coast when a German U-boat's torpedoes strike her hull.
evt-07-17-1918-rms-carpathia.prompt: What happens to Carpathia and the people aboard her?

choices.text: She sinks, but nearly all aboard are rescued by an escort ship
She survives the attack and limps safely to port
The torpedoes miss and the U-boat is sunk instead
She sinks with all hands lost

evt-07-17-1918-rms-carpathia.butterflyEffect: Carpathia sank, but nearly all aboard were saved when the escort ship HMS Snowdrop rescued survivors, with only a handful of crew lost. The ship that had once saved over 700 Titanic survivors was itself sunk by U-55, and her wreck was finally located on the Atlantic seabed in 1999.

evt-07-17-1918-russian-revolution.scenario: It's the night of 16–17 July 1918 in Ekaterinburg. As White forces advance on the city, Bolshevik guards wake the imprisoned Tsar Nicholas II and his family and order them to dress and gather in the basement of their prison house.
evt-07-17-1918-russian-revolution.prompt: What did the Bolshevik guards do next?

choices.text: Executed the entire family and their servants to prevent them becoming a rallying symbol
Held them for a prisoner exchange with the Whites
Released them into exile abroad
Transferred them to Moscow for a public trial

evt-07-17-1918-russian-revolution.butterflyEffect: The family and their servants were executed on Bolshevik orders, eliminating any legal claimant to the throne as the Russian Civil War intensified. Rumors of survivors, especially of Anastasia, persisted among exile communities for decades until DNA testing in the 1990s confirmed the remains.

evt-07-17-1936-nationalist-faction-spani.scenario: It is 17 July 1936, and you are an army officer stationed in Spanish Morocco. Word spreads that garrisons across Spain are coordinating a rising against the Republican government, and your commanders await your signal.

choices.text: Join the coup, rising against the Republican government
Negotiate a truce between rival army factions
Report the plot to Republican authorities in Madrid
Stay neutral and await the outcome

evt-07-17-1936-nationalist-faction-spani.butterflyEffect: The uprising, led by Franco and fellow officers, spread from Morocco to the mainland but failed to seize power outright, splitting Spain and igniting a three-year civil war. Franco's eventual victory in 1939 established a dictatorship that lasted until his death in 1975.

evt-07-17-1944-port-chicago-disaster.scenario: It's the evening of July 17, 1944, at the Port Chicago Naval Magazine in California. You are one of the Black sailors ordered to load bombs and shells onto cargo ships bound for the Pacific, work rushed by white officers who never handle the munitions themselves.
evt-07-17-1944-port-chicago-disaster.prompt: What followed the massive explosion that killed hundreds that night?

choices.text: Sailors who refused to resume loading without safety changes were tried for mutiny
Congress immediately ordered the desegregation of the Navy
Surviving sailors were granted extra pay and immediate discharge
The Navy shut down all munitions loading operations nationwide

evt-07-17-1944-port-chicago-disaster.butterflyEffect: Some surviving sailors, still terrified after the blast, refused to resume loading under the same unsafe conditions and were tried for mutiny, sparking a national civil rights case defended in part by a young NAACP lawyer, Thurgood Marshall. The disaster and trial became key evidence in the push that led President Truman to order the desegregation of the U.S. armed forces in 1948.

evt-07-17-1948-olympia-greece.scenario: It's 17 July 1948, and you stand among the flame-bearers at ancient Olympia, about to carry the Olympic torch on its first relay since the Second World War, bound for the London Games.
evt-07-17-1948-olympia-greece.prompt: What symbolic message did organizers attach to this relay?

choices.text: It was billed as a "relay of peace" marking the Games' return after wartime cancellations
It marked the founding of the United Nations
It commemorated the ancient Olympic truce between city-states
It celebrated Greece's entry into NATO

evt-07-17-1948-olympia-greece.butterflyEffect: The 1948 London Games, the first Olympics since 1936, used the torch relay to project postwar reconciliation to a war-weary world. The ritual cemented the torch relay as a permanent feature of the modern Olympics, carried by host nations ever since.

evt-07-17-1968-ahmed-hassan-al-bakr.scenario: It is 17 July 1968 in Baghdad. You are a Ba'ath Party officer moving into position before dawn, ready to move against President Abdul Rahman Arif's government with the help of sympathetic army units.
evt-07-17-1968-ahmed-hassan-al-bakr.prompt: How did the Ba'ath Party seize control of Iraq that day?

choices.text: A bloodless coup using army units to force President Arif from power
A negotiated power-sharing agreement following free elections
An alliance with Iraqi communists to storm the presidential palace
A public assassination of Arif during a military parade

evt-07-17-1968-ahmed-hassan-al-bakr.butterflyEffect: The coup was nearly bloodless, forcing Arif into exile and installing Ahmed Hassan al-Bakr as president. His deputy, Saddam Hussein, used the following decade to build a personal power base, ultimately succeeding al-Bakr in 1979 and ruling Iraq for over two decades.

evt-07-17-1992-manchester-metrolink.scenario: It's July 17, 1992, and Greater Manchester opens Britain's first modern street-running tram line, sending trams through city-centre streets shared with cars and pedestrians for the first time in decades.
evt-07-17-1992-manchester-metrolink.prompt: What did the Metrolink's launch demonstrate to other British cities?

choices.text: That trams were too dangerous to mix with road traffic
That British cities should abandon rail in favour of buses
That light rail could revive city-centre transport without full subway costs
That light rail required underground tunnels to succeed

evt-07-17-1992-manchester-metrolink.butterflyEffect: Metrolink proved that light rail could revitalise urban transport without the enormous cost of full underground systems. Its success became the template other UK cities followed, including Sheffield, Croydon and Nottingham, and Metrolink itself grew into the largest light rail network in Britain.

evt-07-17-1994-brazil-national-football-.scenario: It's July 17, 1994, at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena. Brazil and Italy have battled through 120 scoreless minutes in the World Cup final, and the title will now be decided by a penalty shootout.
evt-07-17-1994-brazil-national-football-.prompt: What happened in the decisive moment of the shootout?

choices.text: Brazil missed the decisive kick, handing Italy the title
Referees called off the shootout due to a pitch invasion
Roberto Baggio missed Italy's decisive kick, giving Brazil the title
The match resumed with extra time after a video review

evt-07-17-1994-brazil-national-football-.butterflyEffect: Roberto Baggio's final penalty sailed over the crossbar, handing Brazil their fourth World Cup title and first since 1970. The miss became one of the most replayed images in football history and haunted Baggio's legacy, while Brazil's win cemented the country's status as the sport's most successful nation.

evt-07-17-2000-jay-prakash-narayan-airpo.scenario: It's the morning of 17 July 2000, and you are the pilot of a Boeing 737 on approach to Patna's airport in thick haze. Air traffic control warns of poor visibility as you begin your final descent toward the runway.
evt-07-17-2000-jay-prakash-narayan-airpo.prompt: What decision by the flight crew led to the crash short of the runway?

choices.text: Aborting the flight before descent began
Attempting a low, unstabilized go-around that lost altitude too quickly
Diverting to an alternate airport due to fog
Landing safely after a delayed approach

evt-07-17-2000-jay-prakash-narayan-airpo.butterflyEffect: The aircraft, attempting a mishandled go-around, lost altitude too quickly and struck a residential colony short of the runway. The disaster prompted Indian aviation authorities to tighten enforcement of decision-height rules and go-around procedures at airports with limited visibility infrastructure.

evt-07-17-2014-malaysia-airlines-flight-.scenario: It's July 2014, and eastern Ukraine's skies remain open to commercial traffic even as fighting rages below between Russian-backed separatists and government forces. Airlines continue routing flights across the contested region.
evt-07-17-2014-malaysia-airlines-flight-.prompt: What followed the shootdown of Flight MH17 over the conflict zone?

choices.text: Investigators traced the missile to Russian-backed forces, prompting new Western sanctions
Russia and Ukraine agreed to a full ceasefire soon after
Airlines resumed prior routes after the strike was ruled a technical malfunction
The United Nations declared eastern Ukraine a demilitarized zone

evt-07-17-2014-malaysia-airlines-flight-.butterflyEffect: A Dutch-led investigation traced the missile to a Russian-supplied Buk system in separatist-held territory, and a 2022 Dutch court convicted three men in absentia. The disaster hardened Western resolve against Russia, prompting wider sanctions and a lasting shift by airlines worldwide to avoid active conflict airspace.

evt-07-18-1290-edward-i.scenario: You are a Jewish moneylender in London on July 18, 1290, when royal officials post Edward I's new edict throughout the city, ordering every Jew out of the kingdom.
evt-07-18-1290-edward-i.prompt: What must Jewish residents of England do under the edict?

choices.text: Pay a special royal tax to be granted an exemption
Leave England entirely by the deadline set in the edict
Relocate quietly under the protection of sympathetic barons
Convert to Christianity to remain legally in the country

evt-07-18-1290-edward-i.butterflyEffect: Thousands of Jews left England by the All Saints' Day deadline that November, their property seized by the crown. England became the first European kingdom to expel its entire Jewish population, and Jews were not officially permitted to resettle there until Oliver Cromwell's era in 1656.

evt-07-18-1806-1806-birgu-polverista-exp.scenario: It is 18 July 1806 in Birgu, Malta. You are a worker helping transfer shells from a magazine holding tens of thousands of pounds of gunpowder, part of the British garrison's routine munitions handling.
evt-07-18-1806-1806-birgu-polverista-exp.prompt: What caused the catastrophic explosion that struck the magazine that day?

choices.text: An accidental cooking fire spreading from nearby quarters
A lightning strike igniting the powder store
Negligent handling of shells during the transfer process
Deliberate sabotage by enemy agents

evt-07-18-1806-1806-birgu-polverista-exp.butterflyEffect: An investigation found the blast was caused by negligence during the shell-transfer process, not sabotage or accident of nature. The explosion killed roughly 200 people and destroyed fortifications and homes, prompting the British authorities to overhaul munitions storage and handling procedures across Malta's garrisons.

evt-07-18-1841-pedro-ii-of-brazil.scenario: It is 18 July 1841 in the Old Cathedral of Rio de Janeiro. You watch as a slender fifteen-year-old, Pedro II, is crowned Emperor of Brazil five years earlier than the constitution technically allows.
evt-07-18-1841-pedro-ii-of-brazil.prompt: What follows over the next nearly five decades of his reign?

choices.text: He abdicates immediately in favor of a republic
He presides over Brazil's longest, most stable reign, later deposed by an 1889 military coup
He is assassinated within a decade, plunging Brazil into civil war
He leads Brazil into a war of conquest against Argentina and Uruguay

evt-07-18-1841-pedro-ii-of-brazil.butterflyEffect: Pedro II went on to preside over the longest and most stable reign in Brazilian history, overseeing the abolition of slavery in 1888. In 1889 he was deposed in a military coup that ended the monarchy and founded the First Brazilian Republic.

evt-07-18-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It is dusk on July 18, 1863. You are a soldier of the all-Black 54th Massachusetts Infantry, and Colonel Robert Gould Shaw has just ordered your regiment to lead the assault across open sand toward the guns of Fort Wagner.
evt-07-18-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: What does the 54th Massachusetts do when given the order to attack?

choices.text: Attempt a flanking march through the marshes at night
Charge forward across the beach toward the fort's walls
Refuse the order and fall back to the rear lines
Wait offshore for naval bombardment to finish first

evt-07-18-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The regiment charged directly into withering fire, and though the attack failed with heavy losses including Shaw's death, their courage was widely publicized and helped convince the Union to recruit tens of thousands more Black soldiers, reshaping the war's manpower and its meaning.

evt-07-18-1936-nationalist-faction-spani.scenario: It's the night of 17–18 July 1936 and you command an army garrison in a Spanish provincial capital. Radio reports say fellow officers in Morocco have risen against the Republic, and messengers await your order.
evt-07-18-1936-nationalist-faction-spani.prompt: What do you do to bring the city over to the rising?

choices.text: Await instructions from Madrid before acting
Declare martial law, arrest the civil governor, and seize key public buildings
Negotiate a truce with local trade unions
Surrender the garrison's weapons to Republican militias

evt-07-18-1936-nationalist-faction-spani.butterflyEffect: Across Spain, garrisons that followed this pattern captured many towns overnight, but stiff resistance elsewhere—especially in Madrid and Barcelona—turned the coup into a prolonged civil war. That war lasted until 1939, ended in Nationalist victory, and installed Francisco Franco as dictator for the next 36 years.

evt-07-18-1949-francisco-javier-arana.scenario: It is 18 July 1949 in Guatemala City. You are a loyalist bodyguard for President Arévalo, and word arrives that Chief of the Armed Forces Francisco Arana is en route with an ultimatum, threatening a coup unless his demands are met.
evt-07-18-1949-francisco-javier-arana.prompt: How does Arévalo's camp respond to Arana's ultimatum?

choices.text: Arrest him quietly and exile him abroad
Confront Arana's convoy and open fire, killing him in the shootout
Call for new elections to settle the dispute
Concede to his demands and hand over the presidency

evt-07-18-1949-francisco-javier-arana.butterflyEffect: Arana was killed in the resulting gun battle, removing the most powerful rival to the government from the scene. His death let fellow officer Jacobo Árbenz consolidate control of the army, win the 1950 election, and pursue land reforms that provoked the CIA-backed coup of 1954.

evt-07-18-1976-1976-summer-olympics.scenario: It's 18 July 1976 at the Montreal Forum. You're in the crowd as fourteen-year-old Nadia Comăneci finishes a flawless uneven bars routine, and the arena falls silent waiting for her score to appear.
evt-07-18-1976-1976-summer-olympics.prompt: What does the scoreboard actually show right after her routine?

choices.text: 1.00, because the display couldn't register a perfect 10
10.00, printed correctly for the first time in Olympic history
9.95, a fraction short of perfection
An error message, with no score shown at all

evt-07-18-1976-1976-summer-olympics.butterflyEffect: The judges had in fact awarded the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics history, but the scoreboard hardware, never built to show more than 9.99, flashed 1.00 instead. Comăneci went on to score six more perfect 10s that Games, becoming an instant global icon and prompting gymnastics scoring systems to eventually be redesigned.

evt-07-18-1989-rebecca-schaeffer.scenario: It is July 18, 1989, in Los Angeles. A fan who has been writing to you for years and who obtained your home address through California's Department of Motor Vehicles records rings your apartment buzzer.
evt-07-18-1989-rebecca-schaeffer.prompt: What change in law followed Rebecca Schaeffer's killing by this stalker?

choices.text: Congress banned private investigators from operating in California
National gun purchase waiting periods were extended to 30 days
No significant legal changes resulted from the case
California passed the first anti-stalking law and restricted DMV record access

evt-07-18-1989-rebecca-schaeffer.butterflyEffect: Robert Bardo shot and killed Schaeffer at her door after tracking her through DMV records obtained via a private investigator. Her death prompted California to pass the nation's first anti-stalking law in 1990 and to restrict public access to DMV address information, a model later copied nationwide.

evt-07-18-1994-rwandan-genocide.scenario: It is mid-July 1994. Rwandan Patriotic Front columns are pushing into the northwest, closing in on Gisenyi, the last major stronghold of the genocidal government forces near the Zaire border.
evt-07-18-1994-rwandan-genocide.prompt: What followed the RPF's capture of Gisenyi and the collapse of the government?

choices.text: The genocidal government collapsed and vast numbers fled into Zaire, triggering a refugee crisis
The government negotiated a peaceful power-sharing deal with the RPF
The fighting ended with no significant population movement
A large UN peacekeeping force disarmed all militias within the region

evt-07-18-1994-rwandan-genocide.butterflyEffect: The genocidal government fled, and roughly a million Hutu civilians and soldiers poured across the border into Zaire within days, fearing reprisals. The resulting refugee camps became bases for armed militias, a destabilizing factor that helped ignite the First and Second Congo Wars.

evt-07-18-1995-selena.scenario: It is July 18, 1995, less than four months after Selena's murder. Her label releases 'Dreaming of You', pairing new English-language tracks with her Spanish-language hits to test whether Tejano's biggest star could cross into the mainstream US market.
evt-07-18-1995-selena.prompt: What milestone did 'Dreaming of You' achieve on release?

choices.text: It was pulled from shelves due to licensing disputes
It charted only on Billboard's Latin music charts
It sold poorly and was quickly discontinued
It debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 album chart

evt-07-18-1995-selena.butterflyEffect: The album debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, becoming the first predominantly Spanish-language album to top the chart. Its success proved a Latin artist could dominate mainstream American music, paving the way for the late-1990s Latin pop explosion led by artists like Ricky Martin and Jennifer Lopez, who portrayed Selena in her 1997 biopic.

evt-07-18-1995-montserrat.scenario: It is July 1995 and you live in Plymouth, the capital of Montserrat, as the long-dormant Soufrière Hills volcano suddenly roars to life, sending ash drifting over the town's rooftops.
evt-07-18-1995-montserrat.prompt: What should authorities urge Plymouth's residents to do as the volcano awakens?

choices.text: Continue normal activities since the volcano had been dormant for centuries
Shelter indoors and wait for the ash to settle
Move everyone to the volcano's northern slopes for safety
Evacuate Plymouth and the volcano's southern danger zone

evt-07-18-1995-montserrat.butterflyEffect: Officials began evacuating the southern part of the island, a process that intensified as eruptions worsened over the following two years. By 1997, pyroclastic flows had buried Plymouth entirely, forcing roughly two-thirds of Montserrat's population to leave the island and shifting the capital north to Brades.

evt-07-18-1996-saguenay-flood.scenario: It is the night of July 19-20, 1996, and days of torrential rain have swollen the Saguenay River until dams upstream begin to fail, sending walls of water toward riverside neighborhoods in Quebec.
evt-07-18-1996-saguenay-flood.prompt: What should residents do as the dams give way and water rises through the night?

choices.text: Stay behind to sandbag and protect their homes
Evacuate immediately to higher ground away from the river
Attempt to reinforce the weakening dam themselves
Wait for an official all-clear before leaving

evt-07-18-1996-saguenay-flood.butterflyEffect: Officials ordered mass evacuations as the flood became the worst overland flood in 20th-century Canadian history, killing several people and destroying hundreds of homes with over a billion dollars in damage. The disaster prompted Quebec to overhaul dam safety inspections and floodplain development rules.

evt-07-18-2012-2012-burgas-bus-bombing.scenario: In the hours after the blast at Burgas Airport, you are among the Bulgarian investigators sifting through the wreckage of the tour bus, searching for who was responsible for the attack on the Israeli tourists.
evt-07-18-2012-2012-burgas-bus-bombing.prompt: What did the investigation ultimately determine about the attackers?

choices.text: An al-Qaeda affiliated cell
A local Bulgarian criminal network
Operatives connected to Hezbollah
A rogue Bulgarian security officer

evt-07-18-2012-2012-burgas-bus-bombing.butterflyEffect: Bulgarian and international investigators concluded the bombing was carried out by operatives linked to Hezbollah. The finding contributed directly to the European Union's 2013 decision to designate Hezbollah's military wing a terrorist organization, straining EU relations with Lebanon and Iran.

evt-07-18-2014-islamic-state.scenario: It is July 2014 and you are a Christian shopkeeper in Mosul. Loudspeakers announce that the Islamic State has posted an ultimatum on your street: convert, pay a special tax, or leave the city by nightfall, on pain of death.
evt-07-18-2014-islamic-state.prompt: What do you do before the deadline?

choices.text: Gather your family and flee the city immediately
Report the ultimatum to Iraqi army headquarters and wait for protection
Pay the tax and stay in your home
Refuse to leave and openly display your faith
