evt-07-18-2014-islamic-state.butterflyEffect: Most of Mosul's Christians chose to leave rather than risk their lives, ending a continuous Christian presence in the city that stretched back nearly two thousand years. Tens of thousands became refugees in Iraqi Kurdistan, and Mosul's churches were later looted or destroyed during IS occupation.

evt-07-18-2019-kyoto-animation-arson-att.scenario: It is the morning of July 18, 2019, in Kyoto. News breaks that a man has set fire to Studio 1 of a beloved animation house, killing dozens of artists inside.
evt-07-18-2019-kyoto-animation-arson-att.prompt: What outpouring followed the attack on Kyoto Animation's studio?

choices.text: The Japanese government permanently banned commercial animation production
A global fundraising campaign raised tens of millions of dollars for victims and rebuilding
Kyoto Animation closed and never produced another series
International fans largely remained unaware of the incident

evt-07-18-2019-kyoto-animation-arson-att.butterflyEffect: Fans and studios worldwide launched fundraising campaigns that ultimately raised tens of millions of dollars for victims' families and the studio's rebuilding, one of the largest such responses in the anime industry's history. The tragedy also sparked wider conversations about safety and working conditions inside Japan's animation studios.

evt-07-19-1545-mary-rose.scenario: It is 19 July 1545 in the Solent, off Portsmouth. You watch from the shore as King Henry VIII's carrack Mary Rose leads the English fleet's attack against the galleys of an invading French force.
evt-07-19-1545-mary-rose.prompt: What happens to the Mary Rose during this engagement?

choices.text: She sinks the lead French galley and secures a decisive English victory
She is boarded and captured intact by French forces
She runs aground but is towed safely back to harbor
She heels over and sinks, with most of her crew lost

evt-07-19-1545-mary-rose.butterflyEffect: The Mary Rose suddenly heeled over and sank, killing most of her crew of roughly 500. She lay on the seabed for over four centuries until she was raised in 1982, and her remarkably preserved contents have since given historians an unmatched window into Tudor naval life.

evt-07-19-1553-mary-i.scenario: It is 19 July 1553 and you sit on the Privy Council in London. Jane Grey has worn the crown for nine uneasy days, but reports say Mary Tudor has rallied support in East Anglia and public loyalty is crumbling.
evt-07-19-1553-mary-i.prompt: What did the Council actually decide to do this day?

choices.text: Proclaim Mary as the rightful queen
Dissolve the Council and flee London
Reaffirm their support for Queen Jane
Declare for Princess Elizabeth instead

evt-07-19-1553-mary-i.butterflyEffect: The Council abandoned Jane Grey and proclaimed Mary queen, and she soon entered London in triumph. Jane was imprisoned and later executed, while Mary began reversing the Reformation, a campaign of religious persecution that would earn her the name "Bloody Mary."

evt-07-19-1702-great-northern-war.scenario: It is 19 July 1702 near Kliszów in southern Poland. You serve under Augustus II the Strong, whose combined Saxon-Polish army outnumbers the approaching Swedish force under the young King Charles XII.
evt-07-19-1702-great-northern-war.prompt: What actually followed as the two armies clashed at Kliszów?

choices.text: Charles XII's smaller army broke the Polish-Saxon lines in a decisive victory
Augustus II's numerical superiority secured a crushing win
Russian reinforcements arrived in time to save Augustus's army
The battle ended in stalemate and both sides withdrew

evt-07-19-1702-great-northern-war.butterflyEffect: Charles XII's disciplined infantry and tactical skill overcame the odds, routing Augustus's forces and opening much of Poland to Swedish occupation. The victory cemented Charles's reputation as a military genius, but the long Polish campaign that followed drained Swedish resources, contributing to Sweden's eventual disaster at Poltava in 1709.

evt-07-19-1843-ss-great-britain.scenario: It is 19 July 1843 at Bristol's Great Western Dockyard. You watch Isambard Kingdom Brunel's newest ship slide toward the water, built with an iron hull and driven by a screw propeller, a combination no ocean-going vessel has ever attempted before.
evt-07-19-1843-ss-great-britain.prompt: What does this ship go on to achieve at sea?

choices.text: Her iron hull cracks and she sinks on her maiden voyage
She is judged impractical and scrapped within a year
She becomes the first iron steamer to cross the Atlantic, doing so in 14 days
She is converted into a Royal Navy warship before ever carrying passengers

evt-07-19-1843-ss-great-britain.butterflyEffect: In 1845, SS Great Britain became the first iron steamer to cross the Atlantic, making the voyage in just 14 days. She proved iron hulls and screw propulsion could work together on an ocean-going scale, shaping shipbuilding for the rest of the century; she survives today as a museum ship in Bristol.

evt-07-19-1845-great-new-york-city-fire-.scenario: It is 19 July 1845 and you are a volunteer firefighter battling a spreading blaze in Lower Manhattan. Flames are advancing toward a Broad Street warehouse known to be packed with saltpeter, a highly explosive substance.
evt-07-19-1845-great-new-york-city-fire-.prompt: What should the firefighters do as the fire nears the saltpeter warehouse?

choices.text: Enter the building to remove the stored saltpeter
Retreat immediately to a safe distance
Break down the warehouse walls by hand to vent the fire
Keep pouring water directly onto the warehouse walls

evt-07-19-1845-great-new-york-city-fire-.butterflyEffect: The saltpeter ignited in a massive explosion that killed several firefighters and onlookers and hurled the fire even further across the district, ultimately destroying 345 buildings. The disaster pushed city officials to tighten regulations on storing hazardous materials and to push for more fireproof construction.

evt-07-19-1848-seneca-falls-convention.scenario: It is July 19, 1848, in the Wesleyan Chapel at Seneca Falls. Elizabeth Cady Stanton has drafted a Declaration of Sentiments, but one resolution—demanding women's right to vote—is considered too radical even by some organizers.
evt-07-19-1848-seneca-falls-convention.prompt: What happens to the women's suffrage resolution when it comes to a vote?

choices.text: It narrowly passes after Frederick Douglass speaks in its favor
It passes unanimously without any debate
It is withdrawn after fierce objections and dropped entirely
It is tabled for a future convention and never revisited

evt-07-19-1848-seneca-falls-convention.butterflyEffect: Frederick Douglass's support helped push the suffrage resolution through by a narrow margin, making it the only resolution not adopted unanimously at the convention. The Declaration of Sentiments became a founding document of the American women's suffrage movement, inspiring decades of activism that culminated in the 19th Amendment in 1920.

evt-07-19-1916-world-war-i.scenario: It is the night of 19 July 1916 near Fromelles in northern France. You are an Australian infantryman ordered forward across open ground toward heavily fortified German trenches, part of an attack meant to distract from the Somme offensive further south.
evt-07-19-1916-world-war-i.prompt: What happened to the attacking Australian troops at Fromelles?

choices.text: They captured the trench with almost no casualties
They broke through and captured the German front line
They suffered catastrophic losses attacking well-defended positions with little support
They were withdrawn before the assault began

evt-07-19-1916-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The attack failed catastrophically: Australian forces suffered over 5,500 casualties in a single night, exceeding the toll of any full day at Gallipoli. It became known as the worst 24 hours in Australian military history and deepened distrust of British commanders' costly diversionary tactics.

evt-07-19-1989-united-airlines-flight-23.scenario: It is July 19, 1989, and you are Captain Al Haynes aboard United Flight 232. An uncontained engine failure has severed all hydraulic lines, leaving your DC-10 with no conventional flight controls as you approach Sioux City.
evt-07-19-1989-united-airlines-flight-23.prompt: How do you and your crew manage to steer the crippled jet toward the runway?

choices.text: By manually cranking the rudder cables from the cockpit
By switching to a backup hydraulic system built for emergencies
By adjusting throttles on the two remaining wing engines to create differential thrust
By engaging the autopilot's emergency glide mode

evt-07-19-1989-united-airlines-flight-23.butterflyEffect: With off-duty DC-10 instructor Dennis Fitch working the throttles from the cabin, the crew coaxed the plane toward Sioux Gateway Airport, but without normal controls it cartwheeled on landing. Remarkably, 184 of 296 aboard survived, and the crew's improvised throttle-only technique became a landmark case study in flight simulators and crew resource management.

evt-07-19-1992-via-d-amelio-bombing.scenario: It is Palermo in the summer of 1992. You work alongside magistrate Paolo Borsellino, who continues investigating the Mafia despite the assassination of his close colleague Giovanni Falcone just weeks earlier and mounting threats against his own life.
evt-07-19-1992-via-d-amelio-bombing.prompt: What followed the car bomb attack that killed Borsellino and his escort on 19 July?

choices.text: All Mafia leaders were arrested within days
Outrage led to tougher anti-Mafia laws and prison measures
The investigation into the bombing was quickly closed
The government abandoned anti-Mafia efforts out of fear

evt-07-19-1992-via-d-amelio-bombing.butterflyEffect: Public outrage over the killings forced the Italian state to harden its response, including making the strict 41-bis prison regime for mafia convicts permanent and intensifying prosecutions. The deaths of Falcone and Borsellino became a turning point that galvanized Italy's anti-Mafia movement for decades.

evt-07-19-1997-the-troubles.scenario: It is 19 July 1997 and you are a Sinn Féin negotiator waiting anxiously to hear whether the IRA will resume the ceasefire it broke the previous year, a decision that will determine whether your party can join upcoming peace talks.
evt-07-19-1997-the-troubles.prompt: What did the IRA announce on this day?

choices.text: A restored ceasefire, allowing Sinn Féin into talks
Rejection of all future negotiations
A new bombing campaign in London
A permanent end to the organisation itself

evt-07-19-1997-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The IRA restored its ceasefire, clearing the way for Sinn Féin to enter the multi-party negotiations from which the Good Friday Agreement emerged in April 1998, largely ending three decades of violence in Northern Ireland.

evt-07-19-2013-nasa.scenario: It is July 19, 2013, and Cassini is aimed at Earth from nearly 900 million miles away, deep in Saturn's shadow. As a NASA outreach coordinator, you must decide whether to tell the public exactly when to look up and smile for the camera.
evt-07-19-2013-nasa.prompt: What made this photograph, later called 'The Day the Earth Smiled', unusual for a NASA image?

choices.text: It revealed rings around Saturn that had never been seen before
It was the first time Earth had ever been photographed from space
People on Earth were told in advance and asked to smile for the camera
It was Cassini's final image before it burned up in Saturn's atmosphere

evt-07-19-2013-nasa.butterflyEffect: NASA's advance announcement let millions of people knowingly pose for the camera, turning a routine imaging sequence into the largest coordinated 'wave' at another planet in history. The resulting mosaic showed Earth as a tiny blue dot beside the Moon, echoing Voyager's 1990 'Pale Blue Dot' image and boosting public engagement with Cassini ahead of its 2017 plunge into Saturn.

evt-07-20-1651-wars-of-the-three-kingdom.scenario: It is 20 July 1651, and you are a soldier in General John Lambert's force, freshly ferried across the Firth of Forth into Fife, facing a Scottish army near Inverkeithing sent to block your advance.
evt-07-20-1651-wars-of-the-three-kingdom.prompt: What did your victory that day open the way for?

choices.text: The capture of Edinburgh Castle that same week
Cromwell's army to cut off Perth and outflank the main Scottish force
An immediate Scottish surrender ending the war outright
A truce restoring Charles II without further fighting

evt-07-20-1651-wars-of-the-three-kingdom.butterflyEffect: The victory at Inverkeithing let Cromwell's forces cut off Perth and isolate the main Scottish army, prompting Charles II's desperate march south into England. That invasion ended in catastrophic defeat at Worcester that September, effectively closing the civil wars and Charles's hopes of the throne for nine years.

evt-07-20-1793-alexander-mackenzie-explo.scenario: It's 20 July 1793, and after months hauling canoes through mountain passes and hostile rivers, you stand with Alexander Mackenzie's small party at Bella Coola, looking out at tidal water on the Pacific coast.
evt-07-20-1793-alexander-mackenzie-explo.prompt: What was Mackenzie ultimately trying to establish for the North West Company?

choices.text: A new Hudson's Bay Company monopoly zone
A missionary settlement among coastal peoples
A viable overland trade route linking fur country to Pacific and Asian markets
A permanent Royal Navy base on the Pacific coast

evt-07-20-1793-alexander-mackenzie-explo.butterflyEffect: Mackenzie's crossing proved a continental route to the Pacific existed years before Lewis and Clark's expedition, strengthening British claims to the Pacific Northwest. It encouraged plans for a transcontinental fur trade network that later shaped Canada's westward expansion and boundary disputes with the United States.

evt-07-20-1867-united-states-congress.scenario: It's July 20, 1867. Congress has just voted to form a special commission after years of costly warfare against Plains tribes, hoping negotiation can succeed where army campaigns have failed.
evt-07-20-1867-united-states-congress.prompt: What is the Indian Peace Commission tasked with doing?

choices.text: Negotiate treaties moving Plains tribes onto reservations to end the wars
Establish an independent Native American state within US territory
Grant immediate US citizenship to all Native Americans
Formally recognize tribal nations as equal to foreign governments

evt-07-20-1867-united-states-congress.butterflyEffect: The commission negotiated treaties such as Medicine Lodge (1867) and Fort Laramie (1868), pushing tribes onto reservations in exchange for promised supplies and protection. Those promises were soon broken by settlers and the government, fueling later conflicts like the Great Sioux War of 1876.

evt-07-20-1914-george-v.scenario: It's mid-July 1914, and you stand aboard a warship at Spithead as King George V reviews over 200 Royal Navy vessels, the largest fleet ever assembled in British waters. Weeks earlier, an archduke was assassinated in Sarajevo, and Europe's alliances are straining.
evt-07-20-1914-george-v.prompt: What happens to this fleet in the days immediately after the review?

choices.text: It is decommissioned under new disarmament talks
It disperses immediately for summer leave as planned
It sails to reinforce colonial garrisons overseas
It is kept mobilized as Europe edges toward war

evt-07-20-1914-george-v.butterflyEffect: Rather than dispersing for planned summer leave, the fleet was kept mobilized on the orders of Winston Churchill and Prince Louis of Battenberg. This gave Britain a fully assembled navy ready when war broke out on 4 August 1914, letting it secure the North Sea and blockade Germany from the war's very start.

evt-07-20-1917-nikola-pasic.scenario: You are an exiled Serbian official on the island of Corfu on 20 July 1917, watching Prime Minister Nikola Pašić and Yugoslav Committee president Ante Trumbić put their signatures to a joint declaration.
evt-07-20-1917-nikola-pasic.prompt: What did the document they signed commit both men to?

choices.text: Serbia's unconditional surrender to Austria-Hungary
A future union of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes under the Karađorđević dynasty
Restoration of Serbia's pre-war borders alone, with no wider union
An independent Croatian republic separate from Serbia

evt-07-20-1917-nikola-pasic.butterflyEffect: The Corfu Declaration laid the diplomatic foundation for the 1918 creation of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, later Yugoslavia. But the unresolved tension between Pašić's centralist vision and Trumbić's federalist hopes would resurface repeatedly in the interwar kingdom's political crises.

evt-07-20-1936-july-1936-military-uprisi.scenario: You are an anarchist militia fighter behind a barricade of overturned trams in Barcelona on 20 July 1936, as army units loyal to the rebellion try to hold the city center against a swelling crowd of armed workers.
evt-07-20-1936-july-1936-military-uprisi.prompt: What ultimately breaks the military uprising's hold on Barcelona?

choices.text: Franco orders the uprising called off from Morocco
French troops cross the border to intervene directly
The army commanders negotiate a peaceful withdrawal
Civil Guard units join the Republic and militias storm the rebel barracks

evt-07-20-1936-july-1936-military-uprisi.butterflyEffect: Civil Guard units sided with the Republic, and anarchist militias stormed the Atarazanas barracks, crushing the rebellion within a day. The victory left Barcelona under the control of revolutionary workers' committees, launching a social revolution in Catalonia that would later collide with the Republic's own government during the 1937 May Days.

evt-07-20-1951-abdullah-i-of-jordan.scenario: You are a member of the royal entourage walking beside King Abdullah I as he enters the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem for Friday prayers on 20 July 1951, only weeks after rumors spread that he had been secretly negotiating peace with Israel.
evt-07-20-1951-abdullah-i-of-jordan.prompt: What happens to the king's young grandson walking at his side when the gunman opens fire?

choices.text: He is captured and held hostage by the assassin
He is killed alongside his grandfather
He is struck by a bullet that ricochets off a medal on his chest, sparing his life
He escapes the mosque entirely unharmed and unnoticed

evt-07-20-1951-abdullah-i-of-jordan.butterflyEffect: A bullet struck a medal pinned to the young prince's chest and did not kill him; that boy was the future King Hussein, who ascended the throne the following year and ruled Jordan for nearly half a century, eventually signing Jordan's own peace treaty with Israel in 1994.

evt-07-20-1969-apollo-11.scenario: It's July 20, 1969. You are Neil Armstrong, piloting the Lunar Module Eagle toward the Sea of Tranquility, when the guidance computer suddenly flashes unfamiliar alarm codes and you see the autopilot is steering toward a boulder-strewn crater.
evt-07-20-1969-apollo-11.prompt: What do you do in the final moments of the descent?

choices.text: Stop the descent to attempt a full computer restart
Abort the landing immediately and fire the ascent engine back to orbit
Hand control to Michael Collins in the Command Module and land by radio guidance
Trust Houston's assessment that the alarms aren't fatal and take manual control to find safer ground

evt-07-20-1969-apollo-11.butterflyEffect: Armstrong trusted Mission Control's call that the alarms weren't fatal, took manual control, and flew past the boulders to land with roughly 25 seconds of fuel left. The successful touchdown fulfilled Kennedy's 1961 challenge and set the template for five more crewed Moon landings through 1972.

evt-07-20-1976-viking-1.scenario: You are a controller in JPL's Mission Control on 20 July 1976, watching the data stream go silent for the agonizing minutes it takes signals to cross space, waiting to learn whether Viking 1 survived its blind six-minute descent to the Martian surface.
evt-07-20-1976-viking-1.prompt: What does Viking 1 do within hours of touching down safely on Mars?

choices.text: It drills a deep core sample and returns it to Earth
It launches a small rover to explore nearby craters
It transmits the first photograph ever taken from the surface of Mars
It broadcasts the first human voice recording from Mars

evt-07-20-1976-viking-1.butterflyEffect: Viking 1 transmitted the first photograph ever taken from the surface of Mars, followed by soil experiments searching for microbial life. It operated for over six years, the longest extraterrestrial surface mission until NASA's Opportunity rover surpassed it in 2010, and its data shaped every Mars mission that followed.

evt-07-20-1977-johnstown-flood-of-1977.scenario: It's the night of July 19, 1977, and you live below a chain of aging dams in the Conemaugh Valley near Johnstown, Pennsylvania. A stalled thunderstorm has just dumped nearly a foot of rain in a few hours, and the water behind the dams is rising fast.
evt-07-20-1977-johnstown-flood-of-1977.prompt: What is the safest immediate action for residents downstream of the dams?

choices.text: Evacuate immediately to higher ground
Move closer to the riverbank to monitor water levels
Go to the dams to try to reinforce them
Stay indoors and wait out the storm

evt-07-20-1977-johnstown-flood-of-1977.butterflyEffect: Six dams failed that night, sending flash floods through the valley and killing 84 people, decades after the infamous 1889 Johnstown Flood had struck the same city. The disaster led Pennsylvania to overhaul its dam-safety inspection program.

evt-07-20-1982-provisional-irish-republi.scenario: It's July 20, 1982. You are riding with the Household Cavalry through Hyde Park on ceremonial duty, unaware that a car bomb has been hidden along your route, timed for the moment you pass.
evt-07-20-1982-provisional-irish-republi.prompt: What follows this attack and a second bombing hours later in Regent's Park?

choices.text: Both bombs are defused before causing any harm
Soldiers and horses are killed in twin bombings that shock Britain
The attacks strike Parliament instead of ceremonial troops
The IRA calls off the bombings at the last moment

evt-07-20-1982-provisional-irish-republi.butterflyEffect: The Hyde Park bomb killed four soldiers and injured many bystanders, while a second bomb under a bandstand in Regent's Park killed seven army bandsmen; several horses died as well. The twin attacks shocked Britain and hardened public and government resolve against the IRA during the Troubles.

evt-07-20-1997-uss-constitution.scenario: It's July 21, 1997. You stand on the deck of USS Constitution, moored in Boston Harbor, where for over a century she has only been towed out for ceremonial turns. Today, on her 200th anniversary, the Navy has a bolder plan.
evt-07-20-1997-uss-constitution.prompt: What unprecedented feat does Constitution achieve to mark her bicentennial?

choices.text: She is towed to a new permanent museum berth
She fires a full broadside for the first time since the War of 1812
She sails under her own sail power for the first time in over a century
She is permanently decommissioned from the Navy

evt-07-20-1997-uss-constitution.butterflyEffect: Constitution sailed under her own sail power off Marblehead, Massachusetts, the first time she had done so since 1881. The feat proved the old frigate remained genuinely seaworthy, and she has made short unassisted anniversary sails in the years since.

evt-07-20-2001-killing-of-carlo-giuliani.scenario: You're a Carabinieri officer trapped inside an armored jeep in Genoa on July 20, 2001, during riots outside the G8 summit. A masked protester swings a fire extinguisher toward your window as the vehicle is surrounded.
evt-07-20-2001-killing-of-carlo-giuliani.prompt: What happened next that made this the anti-globalization movement's first fatality?

choices.text: The officer used tear gas to disperse the crowd
The jeep reversed and fled the scene unharmed
The officer fired, killing the protester
Riot police arrived and arrested the protester peacefully

evt-07-20-2001-killing-of-carlo-giuliani.butterflyEffect: The officer fired, killing 23-year-old Carlo Giuliani, and images of his death became a rallying symbol for the anti-globalization movement. The killing intensified scrutiny of police tactics at G8 and WTO protests in the years that followed.

evt-07-20-2005-civil-marriage-act.scenario: It is June 2005, and you sit as a Member of Canada's House of Commons debating the Civil Marriage Act. Courts have already legalized same-sex marriage in most provinces and territories, but Alberta and a few others still ban it.
evt-07-20-2005-civil-marriage-act.prompt: What does Parliament do to resolve this patchwork of provincial rulings?

choices.text: Leave marriage law entirely to individual provinces
Pass the Civil Marriage Act, legalizing same-sex marriage nationwide
Amend the constitution to explicitly ban same-sex marriage
Call a national referendum on the issue

evt-07-20-2005-civil-marriage-act.butterflyEffect: Parliament passed the Civil Marriage Act, making Canada the fourth country in the world—and the first outside Europe—to legalize same-sex marriage nationwide. The law became a reference point cited in legislative debates in other countries for years afterward.

evt-07-20-2015-suruc-bombing.scenario: You are one of the young activists gathered outside the Amara Culture Centre in Suruç on 20 July 2015, preparing to travel on to help rebuild the Syrian border town of Kobanî.
evt-07-20-2015-suruc-bombing.prompt: What followed the suicide bombing that struck the crowd that day?

choices.text: Turkey opened its southern border to unrestricted Kurdish refugee crossings
Turkey launched strikes against both ISIL and PKK positions, ending the ceasefire with Kurdish militants
The Turkish government opened negotiations with ISIL representatives
NATO deployed ground troops into Şanlıurfa province

evt-07-20-2015-suruc-bombing.butterflyEffect: The attack killed 34 young activists and shattered the fragile Kurdish peace process. Turkey responded with a two-front military campaign—airstrikes against ISIL in Syria and against PKK camps in northern Iraq—reigniting years of armed conflict between the Turkish state and Kurdish militants.

evt-07-20-2015-united-states.scenario: It's July 20, 2015. After 54 years of severed ties, American and Cuban diplomats gather in Washington and Havana, flags in hand, ready to mark the end of a Cold War-era freeze.
evt-07-20-2015-united-states.prompt: What formal step restores US-Cuba relations today?

choices.text: The two nations reopen embassies in each other's capitals
Cuba is readmitted to the Organization of American States
The United States removes Cuba from its state sponsors of terrorism list
The United States lifts its trade embargo on Cuba

evt-07-20-2015-united-states.butterflyEffect: Embassies in Washington and Havana officially reopened, ending 54 years without formal diplomatic ties. The thaw led to Obama's historic 2016 visit to Havana, though the trade embargo stayed in place and relations cooled again under later administrations.

evt-07-20-2017-o-j-simpson.scenario: It's 20 July 2017, and you sit beside O. J. Simpson before the Nevada Board of Parole Commissioners, nine years into his sentence for a Las Vegas robbery and kidnapping conviction.

choices.text: Ordered a new trial on the original robbery charges
Denied parole, requiring him to serve his full sentence
Granted parole, with release set for later that year
Granted a full pardon clearing his record entirely

evt-07-20-2017-o-j-simpson.butterflyEffect: Simpson walked free in October 2017 after nine years served. His release reignited national debate over his notorious 1995 acquittal in the murders of Nicole Brown and Ron Goldman, and he remained a divisive celebrity figure until his death in 2024.

evt-07-20-2019-soyuz-ms-13.scenario: It's 20 July 2019, exactly fifty years after Apollo 11 touched down on the Moon, and you are strapped into the Soyuz MS-13 capsule on the pad at Baikonur, about to launch for the ISS.
evt-07-20-2019-soyuz-ms-13.prompt: Why had NASA sought extra Soyuz seats for missions like this one?

choices.text: Delays in the Commercial Crew Program meant no American vehicle was yet ready to fly astronauts
Soyuz seats were simply cheaper than any American alternative
Russia had banned all other nations from launching crews to the ISS
The Space Shuttle program needed one final resupply flight

evt-07-20-2019-soyuz-ms-13.butterflyEffect: NASA's purchase of additional Soyuz seats reflected years of delay in the Commercial Crew Program. Within a year SpaceX's Crew Dragon finally flew astronauts, ending nearly a decade of American reliance on Russian rockets to reach the ISS.

evt-07-20-2021-jeff-bezos.scenario: You are strapped into the New Shepard capsule beside Jeff Bezos on the morning of 20 July 2021, minutes from launch on the rocket's first crewed flight, sharing the cabin with three other passengers of very different ages.
evt-07-20-2021-jeff-bezos.prompt: What notable record does this flight set alongside carrying Bezos into space?

choices.text: It is the first flight to dock with the International Space Station
It carries the oldest and youngest people ever to fly to space
It becomes the first crewed flight to reach lunar orbit
It sets the record for the longest spaceflight in history

evt-07-20-2021-jeff-bezos.butterflyEffect: The flight carried Wally Funk, 82, and Oliver Daemen, 18, making them the oldest and youngest people ever to fly to space at the time. The mission accelerated the commercial spaceflight race with Virgin Galactic and SpaceX, pushing suborbital tourism toward becoming a viable, if exclusive, industry.

evt-07-21-230-pope-pontian.scenario: It is 21 July 230, and you have just succeeded Urban I as Bishop of Rome. The empire's tolerance for Christians can shift violently with each new emperor, and you cannot know what the coming years will bring.
evt-07-21-230-pope-pontian.prompt: What happens to Pontian five years into his pontificate, in 235?

choices.text: He is named co-emperor alongside Maximinus
He is executed publicly in the Colosseum
He retires peacefully to a country estate
He is arrested and exiled to the mines of Sardinia

evt-07-21-230-pope-pontian.butterflyEffect: When Maximinus Thrax's persecution reached Rome in 235, Pontian was arrested and exiled to the mines of Sardinia, where the harsh conditions likely killed him. He abdicated the papacy before his death so a successor could be elected without delay, making him the first pope known to have resigned.

evt-07-21-365-ad-365.scenario: It is dawn on July 21, 365, and you are a merchant on the docks of Alexandria. The harbor water has just vanished, leaving ships stranded on bare sand and fish flopping in the mud.
evt-07-21-365-ad-365.prompt: What should you do as the sea suddenly disappears before you?

choices.text: Rush onto the exposed seabed to gather stranded fish
Flee immediately to high ground inland
Wait to see if the tide returns naturally before acting
Stay by the docks to secure your moored boat

evt-07-21-365-ad-365.butterflyEffect: A massive earthquake near Crete triggered a tsunami that crashed back over Alexandria and the eastern Mediterranean coast, hurling ships onto rooftops and killing thousands. The disaster was so devastating that Alexandria commemorated the date annually for centuries afterward as a day of horror.

evt-07-21-905-louis-the-blind.scenario: It is 905, and you are Louis III, returned to Italy to reclaim the imperial crown from your rival Berengar of Friuli, despite once swearing an oath never to set foot there again. Berengar's forces have just closed in and taken you captive.
evt-07-21-905-louis-the-blind.prompt: What fate does Berengar impose on you after your capture?

choices.text: Ransom back to his Burgundian allies unharmed
Execution before the assembled Italian nobles
Blinding, followed by exile back to Provence
Permanent imprisonment in a Veronese fortress

evt-07-21-905-louis-the-blind.butterflyEffect: Berengar had Louis blinded and sent back to his remaining lands in Provence and Burgundy, ending his ability to rule in person and earning him the name Louis the Blind. Berengar secured control of Italy, while the imperial title itself fell vacant for decades until Otto I revived it in 962.

evt-07-21-1378-ciompi-revolt.scenario: You are a wool-carder in Florence in July 1378, one of thousands of labourers barred from the city's guilds and crushed by taxes you cannot pay. Rumours spread that the unrepresented workers are ready to march on the government palaces.
evt-07-21-1378-ciompi-revolt.prompt: What do you do as the unrest boils over?

choices.text: Flee Florence for a rival city-state
Quietly petition the Signoria for tax relief
Join the uprising and help seize the city's government
Appeal directly to the Pope in Avignon for intervention

evt-07-21-1378-ciompi-revolt.butterflyEffect: The ciompi rose up, seized the Palazzo della Signoria, and forced the creation of new guilds giving unskilled workers a voice in government for the first time. The radical regime lasted only about three and a half years before Florence's patrician oligarchy clawed back control in 1382, but the revolt remained a landmark early challenge to guild-based exclusion.

evt-07-21-1877-pittsburgh.scenario: It's July 21, 1877, and you are a militiaman sent from Philadelphia to Pittsburgh to break up a railroad strike. Furious workers protesting wage cuts have blocked freight trains, and a hostile crowd now surrounds your unit.
evt-07-21-1877-pittsburgh.prompt: What happens after your unit opens fire on the crowd?

choices.text: Local police reinforce the militia and restore calm without further violence
The strikers immediately disperse and the strike ends peacefully
Railroad owners agree to restore wages that same day
Furious rioters burn and loot rail yards across the city

evt-07-21-1877-pittsburgh.butterflyEffect: The gunfire killed roughly twenty people and ignited days of arson and looting that destroyed Pennsylvania Railroad yards and rolling stock across the city. The violence, part of the nationwide Great Railroad Strike of 1877, pushed many American cities to build armories and expand militia forces to suppress future labor unrest.

evt-07-21-1918-world-war-i.scenario: It is 21 July 1918 and you watch from Nauset Beach as a surfaced German U-boat opens fire on a tug and its string of barges just offshore, the only enemy attack on the American mainland during the war.
evt-07-21-1918-world-war-i.prompt: What do you do to counter the attack?

choices.text: Evacuate the town and wait for the attack to end
Alert the naval air station to send aircraft against the submarine
Row out to the barges to rescue cargo under fire
Signal nearby fishing boats to ram the U-boat

evt-07-21-1918-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Aircraft scrambled from the nearby Chatham Naval Air Station to bomb the submarine, but their ordnance failed to detonate and the U-boat escaped unharmed after sinking the barges. No Americans were killed, yet the raid shocked coastal communities and spurred renewed calls for home-front vigilance and war-bond drives.

evt-07-21-1925-john-t-scopes.scenario: It is July 21, 1925, in a packed Dayton, Tennessee courtroom. You are John Scopes, standing before the jury after Clarence Darrow and William Jennings Bryan spent days clashing over evolution and the Bible on your behalf and against you.
evt-07-21-1925-john-t-scopes.prompt: What is the jury's verdict on the charge of teaching evolution?

choices.text: Acquitted for lack of evidence
Mistrial declared by the judge
Guilty, with a $100 fine
Case dismissed before reaching the jury

evt-07-21-1925-john-t-scopes.butterflyEffect: Scopes was found guilty and fined $100, though the Tennessee Supreme Court later overturned the conviction on a technicality, sparing further appeal. The trial became a lasting cultural touchstone in the debate over evolution and religion in American schools, later dramatized in the play and film Inherit the Wind.

evt-07-21-1946-1946-la-paz-riots.scenario: It is July 21, 1946, and you are a foreign diplomat in La Paz watching a furious crowd, swollen by weeks of strikes and unrest, break through the gates of the presidential palace where Gualberto Villarroel is holed up.
evt-07-21-1946-1946-la-paz-riots.prompt: What happens to President Villarroel as the mob overwhelms the palace?

choices.text: He escapes the country into exile
He negotiates a peaceful handover of power
He is captured by the crowd and lynched
He is arrested and stands trial in court

evt-07-21-1946-1946-la-paz-riots.butterflyEffect: Villarroel was seized and lynched, his body hanged from a lamppost in the Plaza Murillo, a scene that shocked Bolivia and the world. Power passed briefly to a junta drawn from the striking factions, and Villarroel's death later became a rallying memory for the MNR movement that seized power in the 1952 revolution.

evt-07-21-1952-1952-kern-county-earthqua.scenario: It is 4:52 a.m. on July 21, 1952, in Bakersfield, California. The ground beneath the San Joaquin Valley suddenly convulses as a 7.3-magnitude quake tears along the White Wolf Fault, the strongest to hit the state since 1906.
evt-07-21-1952-1952-kern-county-earthqua.prompt: As the violent shaking continues, what is the safest thing to do right now?

choices.text: Drop and take cover under sturdy furniture, away from windows
Stand in a doorway and wait it out
Run outside into the open street immediately
Get in your car and drive away from the area

evt-07-21-1952-1952-kern-county-earthqua.butterflyEffect: Twelve people died and property damage reached about $60 million, with a damaging aftershock striking Bakersfield again a month later. The quake exposed the danger of thrust faults distinct from the San Andreas system and pushed California toward stricter seismic building codes and closer scientific study of the region's fault network.

evt-07-21-1959-international-mathematica.scenario: You are a Bulgarian student in Bucharest in July 1959, sitting alongside teams from six Eastern Bloc nations for a brand-new competition testing pure mathematical problem-solving, with no precedent to tell you what it will become.
evt-07-21-1959-international-mathematica.prompt: What happens to this fledgling contest in the decades that follow?

choices.text: It is absorbed into the Olympic Games as a demonstration event
It becomes a global annual tradition drawing over 100 nations
It is abandoned after a few years for lack of interest
It stays confined permanently to Eastern Bloc countries

evt-07-21-1959-international-mathematica.butterflyEffect: The Olympiad became an annual fixture, skipped only once in 1980, and expanded far beyond the Eastern Bloc to draw teams from over 100 countries today. It grew into the most prestigious pre-university mathematics competition in the world, launching the careers of many future leading mathematicians.

evt-07-21-1960-sirimavo-bandaranaike.scenario: You sit on the Sri Lanka Freedom Party's central committee in early 1960. The party's leader, Solomon Bandaranaike, was assassinated the previous year, and the party needs a new figurehead to lead it into the coming election.
evt-07-21-1960-sirimavo-bandaranaike.prompt: Whom does the party choose to lead it, a decision that will make history?

choices.text: A prominent opposition figure to broker unity
A senior male cabinet minister from the previous government
A retired army general with no party ties
Sirimavo Bandaranaike, widow of the slain leader

evt-07-21-1960-sirimavo-bandaranaike.butterflyEffect: The party selected Sirimavo Bandaranaike, the assassinated leader's widow, and she led the SLFP to victory. On 21 July 1960 she was sworn in, becoming the world's first democratically elected female prime minister, a milestone that opened the door for women heads of government worldwide.

evt-07-21-1972-the-troubles.scenario: It is the afternoon of July 21, 1972, in Belfast city centre. In the space of about an hour, telephoned warnings pour in as the Provisional IRA detonates roughly twenty bombs across the city, overwhelming police and army efforts to clear the streets in time.
evt-07-21-1972-the-troubles.prompt: What major British military response did this attack help trigger two weeks later?

choices.text: The introduction of internment without trial
Operation Motorman to retake IRA "no-go" areas
A negotiated ceasefire with the Provisional IRA
Declaration of martial law across Northern Ireland

evt-07-21-1972-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: Bloody Friday killed nine people and injured well over a hundred, and public revulsion at the scale of the attack turned opinion sharply against the IRA. On 31 July 1972 the British Army launched Operation Motorman, its largest operation since Suez, moving in force to dismantle the IRA-controlled "no-go" areas of Belfast and Derry.

evt-07-21-2010-barack-obama.scenario: It is July 21, 2010, and you are a senior White House aide watching President Obama prepare to sign the sweeping Wall Street reform bill, drafted in response to the 2008 financial crash. Banks are lobbying hard against new oversight.
evt-07-21-2010-barack-obama.prompt: What new federal watchdog does this law create to protect ordinary consumers?

choices.text: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
The Securities and Exchange Commission
The Federal Trade Commission
The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation

evt-07-21-2010-barack-obama.butterflyEffect: Dodd-Frank created the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the first federal agency devoted solely to consumer financial protection. It also imposed stress tests and stricter oversight on big banks, though later administrations would roll back parts of it.

evt-07-21-2011-nasa.scenario: It's July 21, 2011, and you watch Space Shuttle Atlantis glide to a predawn landing at Kennedy Space Center, completing mission STS-135. Thirty years of shuttle flights are ending with no replacement vehicle ready to fly.
evt-07-21-2011-nasa.prompt: What does NASA rely on to send astronauts to the ISS in the years immediately following?

choices.text: The Constellation program's shuttle successor
SpaceX Dragon flights, launching that same year
Russian Soyuz spacecraft
The new Orion capsule

evt-07-21-2011-nasa.butterflyEffect: With no shuttle successor ready, NASA paid Russia for seats on Soyuz spacecraft until SpaceX's Crew Dragon began carrying astronauts in 2020. The gap accelerated NASA's Commercial Crew Program, reshaping how the agency partners with private companies for human spaceflight.

evt-07-21-2019-2019-2020-hong-kong-prote.scenario: It is the evening of 21 July 2019. You are riding the MTR home through Yuen Long station after joining an anti-extradition-bill march, still recognizable in your protest clothing.
evt-07-21-2019-2019-2020-hong-kong-prote.prompt: What waits for you and other passengers when the train doors open at Yuen Long?

choices.text: A welcoming committee hands out water and snacks
Monks gather on the platform to bless the protesters
A mob of white-shirted men attacks passengers with rods and clubs
Riot police mass to arrest everyone on the platform

evt-07-21-2019-2019-2020-hong-kong-prote.butterflyEffect: Roughly a hundred men in white shirts, widely believed to have triad connections, stormed the station and beat passengers, journalists, and lawmakers with rods and clubs, injuring dozens. Police were slow to respond, and the attack became a rallying symbol of alleged collusion between authorities and organized crime, hardening the movement's resolve through the following months.

evt-07-21-2023-barbenheimer.scenario: You run marketing for a struggling multiplex chain in July 2023. Two wildly different blockbusters, a pink fantasy comedy and a grim nuclear-history biopic, open on the very same day, and the internet is already mashing them together into one joke.
evt-07-21-2023-barbenheimer.prompt: How do you respond to the online 'Barbenheimer' meme?

choices.text: Push one studio to delay its release to avoid the clash
Ban costumes and memes from your theaters as distractions
Ignore the trend entirely and market the films separately
Lean into it with double-feature screenings and themed promotions

evt-07-21-2023-barbenheimer.butterflyEffect: Theaters embraced the joke, selling double-feature tickets and costume nights instead of fighting the mashup. The pairing drove one of the biggest box-office weekends since the pandemic and turned 'Barbenheimer' into shorthand for the power of internet-driven counter-programming to revive cinema-going.

evt-07-21-2024-joe-biden.scenario: It is July 21, 2024, and you are a senior campaign aide as President Biden, facing weeks of pressure after a shaky debate performance, weighs whether to continue his re-election bid.
evt-07-21-2024-joe-biden.prompt: What does Biden announce this day about his campaign?

choices.text: He delays any decision until the convention
He withdraws from the race and endorses Kamala Harris
He stays in the race and doubles down on campaigning
He announces a new running mate but stays on the ticket

evt-07-21-2024-joe-biden.butterflyEffect: Biden withdrew from the race and endorsed Vice President Kamala Harris within hours, upending a presidential contest just months before the election. Harris quickly secured the Democratic nomination but went on to lose the November election to Donald Trump.

evt-07-22-838-arab-byzantine-wars.scenario: It is July 838, and you march with Emperor Theophilos's army near Anzen in Byzantine Anatolia. Caliph al-Mu'tasim's Abbasid forces bear down on your lines, and the emperor himself is caught in the melee.
evt-07-22-838-arab-byzantine-wars.prompt: What happens to the Byzantine army in this clash?

choices.text: The armies negotiate a truce before fighting begins
Theophilos is captured and held for ransom
The Byzantines win a decisive victory
Theophilos is defeated and narrowly escapes capture

evt-07-22-838-arab-byzantine-wars.butterflyEffect: The Byzantines were routed and Theophilos barely escaped with his life. Weeks later the Abbasids pressed on to sack Amorium, the emperor's ancestral home city, a devastating blow that shook Byzantine morale for a generation.

evt-07-22-1209-beziers.scenario: It is 22 July 1209, and you lead a crusading army camped outside Béziers. Inside the walls, Catholics and Cathars alike have refused your demand to hand over the heretics among them, and dusk is falling.
evt-07-22-1209-beziers.prompt: What does the crusading army do next?

choices.text: Storm the city and kill nearly everyone inside
Negotiate a truce and withdraw peacefully
Lay siege for months and wait them out
Accept a ransom and spare the city

evt-07-22-1209-beziers.butterflyEffect: The crusaders breached the walls and slaughtered the population without distinguishing Catholic from Cathar, an atrocity later linked to the phrase "Kill them all, God will know his own." The sack of Béziers set the brutal tone for the Albigensian Crusade, terrifying other towns into surrender and cementing Simon de Montfort's fearsome reputation as the campaign pressed on.

evt-07-22-1298-first-war-of-scottish-ind.scenario: It is 22 July 1298 near Falkirk. You stand shoulder to shoulder in one of William Wallace's schiltrons, spears bristling outward, as Edward I's cavalry probes your ranks while English archers take up position at range.
evt-07-22-1298-first-war-of-scottish-ind.prompt: What proves decisive in breaking the Scottish schiltrons?

choices.text: Longbowmen break the schiltrons with arrow volleys, opening gaps for cavalry
Scottish spearmen surrender before the fighting starts
A sudden storm forces both armies to withdraw
Wallace is captured early, causing his army to collapse

evt-07-22-1298-first-war-of-scottish-ind.butterflyEffect: English and Welsh longbowmen shredded the tightly packed schiltrons with volleys before cavalry rode through the gaps, crushing Wallace's army. Wallace resigned as Guardian of Scotland soon after, and the tactic of massed archery against infantry formations would reappear to devastating effect decades later at Crécy and Agincourt.

evt-07-22-1691-williamite.scenario: It is 12 July 1691 (Old Style) on the boggy ground near Aughrim, Ireland. You command Jacobite forces holding strong ground, and your general, the Marquis de St Ruth, has just boasted the day will end in victory before leading a cavalry charge.
evt-07-22-1691-williamite.prompt: What happens next that shatters the Jacobite position?

choices.text: St Ruth is killed by a cannonball and his army disintegrates
French reinforcements arrive to save the Jacobite line
A sudden storm floods the bog and halts the battle
William III personally leads a counter-charge that turns the tide

evt-07-22-1691-williamite.butterflyEffect: St Ruth was killed instantly by a cannonball at the moment of apparent victory, and the leaderless Jacobite army collapsed into rout. Aughrim effectively ended organised Jacobite resistance in Ireland, leading within months to the Treaty of Limerick and the consolidation of Protestant Ascendancy rule.

evt-07-22-1802-gia-long.scenario: It is 1802 and after decades of civil war against the Tây Sơn dynasty, your forces under Nguyễn Ánh have just taken Hanoi, the last major stronghold standing between you and control of the whole Vietnamese coast.
evt-07-22-1802-gia-long.prompt: What does Nguyễn Ánh do next to secure his new rule?

choices.text: Requests French annexation of Vietnam as a colony
Proclaims himself emperor, founding the Nguyễn dynasty
Divides the country between rival warlords to keep peace
Restores the Tây Sơn leadership as figurehead rulers

evt-07-22-1802-gia-long.butterflyEffect: He proclaimed himself Emperor Gia Long, founding the Nguyễn dynasty and unifying the territory of modern Vietnam under one throne for the first time in centuries. He sought recognition from the Qing court and adopted the name 'Việt Nam' for his realm, a dynasty that would rule until 1945.

evt-07-22-1817-windham-sadler.scenario: It is 22 July 1817, and you stand in the basket of a hydrogen balloon lifting off from Ireland, the grey water of the Irish Sea spreading beneath you. Your father attempted this same crossing and failed.
evt-07-22-1817-windham-sadler.prompt: What does Sadler achieve by the day's end?

choices.text: He crashes into the sea and is rescued by a passing ship
He lands in France instead of England
He turns back due to sudden storms
He completes the first successful balloon crossing of the Irish Sea

evt-07-22-1817-windham-sadler.butterflyEffect: Sadler completed the first successful balloon crossing of the Irish Sea, proving manned flight could reliably span open water and inspiring further sea-crossing attempts across Europe. He continued ballooning until his death in a crash near Blackburn in 1824.

evt-07-22-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 22 July 1864 outside Atlanta, and you command Confederate troops under General Hood who marched overnight to strike an exposed flank of Sherman's advancing army.
evt-07-22-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What is the outcome of the attack?

choices.text: The attack routs the Union army and forces a retreat
Both sides withdraw without engaging
The Union surrenders Atlanta immediately
The assault fails with heavy Confederate losses despite early gains

evt-07-22-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The assault, known as the Battle of Atlanta, failed with heavy Confederate casualties despite initial gains. The defeat set up Atlanta's fall that September, a victory that bolstered Lincoln's reelection chances and became a turning point in the war.

evt-07-22-1894-jules-albert-de-dion.scenario: It is 22 July 1894, and your steam-powered car has just crossed the finish line first in the Paris-Rouen trial, the world's first organized motor competition.
evt-07-22-1894-jules-albert-de-dion.prompt: What happens to your first-place finish?

choices.text: Judges disqualify him because his steam car needs an extra stoker
The race is declared void by organizers
He is awarded outright victory and prize money
He is disqualified for exceeding a speed limit

evt-07-22-1894-jules-albert-de-dion.butterflyEffect: Judges disqualified de Dion because his steam tractor required an extra crewman to stoke it, against the contest's rules for practical vehicles. Panhard-Levassor and Peugeot were instead ranked joint first, and the trial's success launched competitive motoring in France.

evt-07-22-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 22 July 1944 in newly liberated Lublin. Soviet-backed Polish communists have just proclaimed the Polish Committee of National Liberation, directly rivaling the Polish government-in-exile still recognized in London.
evt-07-22-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What did the PKWN's establishment set in motion for postwar Poland?

choices.text: Stalin dissolved it within weeks of its founding
It handed all power directly to the Polish Home Army
It became the basis for a Soviet-aligned communist government
It merged peacefully with the London government-in-exile

evt-07-22-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The PKWN evolved into the Provisional Government of Poland, recognized by Stalin while the London government-in-exile was diplomatically sidelined. This maneuver laid the groundwork for four decades of communist rule in Poland after the war.

evt-07-22-1951-soviet-space-dogs.scenario: It is 22 July 1951 at a Soviet rocket range. You are a technician preparing two stray dogs, Dezik and Tsygan, for a sub-orbital launch meant to test whether a living creature can survive the trip to the edge of space and back.
evt-07-22-1951-soviet-space-dogs.prompt: What is the outcome scientists are hoping to prove with this launch?

choices.text: That a rocket engine can achieve orbital velocity
That a mammal can survive high-altitude rocket flight and recovery
That radio signals can be sent from space to Earth
That a parachute can slow a returning satellite

evt-07-22-1951-soviet-space-dogs.butterflyEffect: Dezik and Tsygan both survived the flight and were recovered alive, the first living creatures to survive spaceflight. The success paved the way for further canine test flights and, ultimately, for Yuri Gagarin's 1961 human orbital flight.

evt-07-22-1954-declaration-of-martial-la.scenario: It is July 1954, and as governor you face a county where the sheriff's office and city police are entangled with gambling rings and the murder of an attorney general nominee.
evt-07-22-1954-declaration-of-martial-la.prompt: What action does Governor Persons take?

choices.text: He disbands the county government outright
He requests federal troops from Washington
He declares martial law and hands policing to the National Guard
He calls for immediate new local elections

evt-07-22-1954-declaration-of-martial-la.butterflyEffect: The National Guard took over law enforcement duties in Phenix City, breaking organized crime's decades-long grip on local government. The cleanup became a nationally publicized model of state intervention against entrenched vice rings.

evt-07-22-1975-stanley-forman.scenario: It is 22 July 1975 in Boston. You are photojournalist Stanley Forman, camera raised, when a fire escape suddenly gives way beneath a woman and a child being rescued from a burning building, sending them plunging toward the street.
evt-07-22-1975-stanley-forman.prompt: What does Forman do in the split second the fire escape collapses?

choices.text: Shouts instructions to firefighters instead of photographing
Drops his camera and runs to catch them
Stops shooting out of respect and looks away
Keeps shooting, capturing the fall as it happens

evt-07-22-1975-stanley-forman.butterflyEffect: Forman kept shooting, capturing the fall in a sequence that ran on front pages nationwide and won him the Pulitzer Prize. The woman, Diana Bryant, did not survive, but the child landed on her and lived; the horrifying images prompted cities across the country to overhaul fire escape safety codes.

evt-07-22-1976-philippines.scenario: It is 22 July 1976, and you work in the Philippine finance ministry, tracking a reparations schedule signed with Tokyo two decades earlier, in 1956.
evt-07-22-1976-philippines.prompt: What milestone in Japan's war reparations to the Philippines is reached today?

choices.text: Japan completes its final reparations payment to the Philippines
The Philippines forgives the outstanding reparations debt
A new reparations treaty is signed to replace the old one
Japan cancels the remaining reparations agreement

evt-07-22-1976-philippines.butterflyEffect: Japan made its final payment under the 1956 Reparations Agreement, closing a twenty-year arrangement negotiated after the devastation of the Japanese occupation. The completed payments helped fund postwar reconstruction and smoothed the path toward Japan becoming one of the Philippines' largest trade and investment partners in later decades.

evt-07-22-1991-serial-killer.scenario: It is the night of 22 July 1991 in Milwaukee. You are one of two patrol officers who found a dazed man with a dangling handcuff on his wrist, claiming a stranger drugged and threatened him. The calm man now standing before you insists it was just a lovers' spat.
evt-07-22-1991-serial-killer.prompt: What should the officers do next to resolve the conflicting stories?

choices.text: Accept his explanation and let him go with a caution
Leave both men and file no report
Return to the apartment to check his account against the room
Arrest the injured man for public disturbance

evt-07-22-1991-serial-killer.butterflyEffect: The officers went back to the apartment and found Polaroids of dismembered victims, leading to Jeffrey Dahmer's arrest. Investigators recovered human remains on site, and Dahmer was later convicted of murdering seventeen men and boys, a case that also sparked lasting scrutiny of how police had handled an earlier warning about one of his victims.

evt-07-22-1997-blue-water-bridge.scenario: It is 22 July 1997, and you are a customs officer at the border crossing linking Point Edward, Ontario, with Port Huron, Michigan, where trucks have queued for years on the lone 1938 span.
evt-07-22-1997-blue-water-bridge.prompt: What opens today to finally relieve the bottleneck on the original bridge?

choices.text: A new twin span of the Blue Water Bridge
A vehicle tunnel beneath the St. Clair River
A rail-only bridge for freight trains
A new car ferry service between the two towns

evt-07-22-1997-blue-water-bridge.butterflyEffect: A second, companion span of the Blue Water Bridge opened, doubling capacity just as NAFTA-driven truck traffic between Ontario and Michigan was surging. The crossing went on to become one of the busiest trade gateways on the Canada-US border, carrying a substantial share of bilateral commerce in the years that followed.

evt-07-22-2002-israel-defense-forces.scenario: It is July 2002, and Israeli military planners are weighing whether to strike a Hamas military commander's home in a crowded Gaza City neighborhood at night.
evt-07-22-2002-israel-defense-forces.prompt: What followed the decision to proceed with the airstrike?

choices.text: The strike missed its target entirely
The operation was called off at the last moment
Shehade surrendered before the strike occurred
The strike killed Shehade but also caused civilian deaths, sparking condemnation

evt-07-22-2002-israel-defense-forces.butterflyEffect: The bombing killed Salah Shehade along with several civilians, including children, drawing widespread international condemnation of the targeting decision. The episode became a lasting reference point in debates over civilian harm from strikes in populated areas.

evt-07-22-2003-iraq-war.scenario: It is 22 July 2003 in Mosul. You lead soldiers of the 101st Airborne and Special Forces surrounding a villa where Saddam Hussein's sons Uday and Qusay are holed up, refusing every call to surrender after hours of gunfire.
evt-07-22-2003-iraq-war.prompt: How do coalition forces finally break the six-hour standoff?

choices.text: Negotiate a surrender through intermediaries
Fire anti-tank missiles into the building
Call in a fighter jet airstrike on the villa
Withdraw and besiege the villa for days

evt-07-22-2003-iraq-war.butterflyEffect: Forces fired TOW anti-tank missiles into the villa, killing Uday and Qusay Hussein. The US later released photographs and DNA confirmation to convince skeptical Iraqis the regime's heirs were truly dead, undercutting insurgent claims and rewarding the informant with a $30 million payment.

evt-07-22-2011-2011-norway-attacks.scenario: It is the evening of 22 July 2011 in Oslo. A bomb has just torn through government buildings and reports are coming in of a shooting at a youth camp on Utøya. As a Norwegian leader, you must decide how the nation should respond in the days ahead.
evt-07-22-2011-2011-norway-attacks.prompt: What did Norway's government pledge as its response to the attacks?

choices.text: Meet the attack with more democracy and more openness
Declare a state of emergency and suspend public gatherings
Reinstate the death penalty for terrorism
Close Norway's borders indefinitely

evt-07-22-2011-2011-norway-attacks.butterflyEffect: Prime Minister Jens Stoltenberg publicly vowed that Norway would answer the attacks with 'more democracy, more openness' rather than fear or repression. The country largely resisted calls for harsher security crackdowns, and the response became a widely cited model for meeting terrorism with civic resilience.

evt-07-23-1921-1st-national-congress-of-.scenario: It is late July 1921. You are one of thirteen delegates meeting secretly in a house in Shanghai's French Concession to found a communist party, when a suspicious stranger peers through the gate and police begin circling the block.
evt-07-23-1921-1st-national-congress-of-.prompt: What do the delegates do to save the congress?

choices.text: Move openly to a foreign consulate for protection
Disband the congress and abandon the party project
Flee to Jiaxing and complete the congress aboard a boat on South Lake
Stay and finish the meeting in the same house

evt-07-23-1921-1st-national-congress-of-.butterflyEffect: The delegates fled Shanghai and finished the congress aboard a pleasure boat on South Lake in Jiaxing, formally founding the Chinese Communist Party with barely fifty members nationwide. That small underground gathering grew into the party that would rule China from 1949 onward, with attendee Mao Zedong eventually becoming its paramount leader.

evt-07-23-1942-the-holocaust.scenario: It is July 23, 1942, at the newly opened Treblinka camp in occupied Poland. You are among the SS staff tasked with processing trainloads of Jewish deportees who believe they have arrived at a transit station.
evt-07-23-1942-the-holocaust.prompt: What method does the camp use to prevent panic among the new arrivals?

choices.text: A disguised fake train station with painted signs and a false ticket window
Indefinite delay of all incoming transports
Open announcement of the camp's true purpose
Immediate mass violence upon arrival

evt-07-23-1942-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: Treblinka's staff built an elaborate deception, complete with a fake station clock and timetable, to move deportees toward the gas chambers without resistance. Between 1942 and 1943 roughly 800,000 people, most from the Warsaw Ghetto, were murdered there; in August 1943 prisoners staged an uprising and set the camp ablaze before the Germans could fully erase it.

evt-07-23-1942-nikola-vaptsarov.scenario: It is 23 July 1942 in Sofia, and you are part of Bulgaria's underground anti-fascist resistance, mourning the machinist-poet Nikola Vaptsarov, just executed by firing squad for his communist activities under wartime rule.
evt-07-23-1942-nikola-vaptsarov.prompt: What actually followed for Vaptsarov's legacy after the war?

choices.text: His work was forgotten until rediscovery in the 1990s
His poems were permanently banned by the new government
He was posthumously honored as a national hero and his poetry celebrated
He was publicly denounced as a traitor by fellow communists

evt-07-23-1942-nikola-vaptsarov.butterflyEffect: After Bulgaria's postwar communist government took power, Vaptsarov was posthumously honored as a national hero and his poetry, including the collection Motor Songs, entered the school curriculum. An international poetry prize was later established in his name, cementing his place in Bulgarian literary memory.

evt-07-23-1968-glenville-shootout.scenario: It is the morning after the Glenville shootout, July 24, 1968. As Cleveland's newly elected Black mayor, you must decide how to police a neighborhood still simmering with rage after a night of gunfire between officers and a Black nationalist group.
evt-07-23-1968-glenville-shootout.prompt: What should Mayor Carl Stokes do to prevent the unrest from spreading?

choices.text: Flood the neighborhood with National Guard troops
Impose a citywide curfew enforced by state police
Arm local shopkeepers for self-defense
Withdraw white police and let Black officers and community leaders patrol

evt-07-23-1968-glenville-shootout.butterflyEffect: Stokes pulled white officers and the National Guard back overnight, letting Black police and community figures patrol Glenville, and the wider rioting subsided within days. The decision made him a target of criticism from the police union and many white residents, straining his second term, but it also became a defining example of Black political power reshaping urban policing.

evt-07-23-1982-twilight-zone-accident.scenario: It is the night of 22–23 July 1982 at Indian Dunes in Valencia, California. Director John Landis wants a helicopter hovering low over a river while explosive charges detonate for a wartime scene, with two child actors working past legal hours and without required permits.
evt-07-23-1982-twilight-zone-accident.prompt: What decision by the production ultimately caused the helicopter to crash onto the actors below?

choices.text: They postponed the shoot until daylight for better visibility
They used a mechanical stand-in instead of a real helicopter
They detonated explosives so close to the low-flying helicopter that it lost control and crashed
They filmed at a safe altitude with full safety clearances

evt-07-23-1982-twilight-zone-accident.butterflyEffect: The explosions damaged the low-flying helicopter's tail rotor, sending it crashing onto Vic Morrow and child actors Myca Dinh Le and Renee Shin-Yi Chen, killing all three. The disaster led to a lengthy manslaughter trial that ended in acquittals, but it permanently reshaped safety regulations and child labor enforcement across the American film industry.

evt-07-23-1984-vanessa-williams.scenario: It's July 1984, and you are a Miss America Organization official facing an unfolding scandal: nude photographs of the reigning titleholder, Vanessa Williams, taken before her crowning, are about to be published without her consent.
evt-07-23-1984-vanessa-williams.prompt: What did Vanessa Williams ultimately do in response to the controversy?

choices.text: Pageant officials publicly defended her and took no action
She sued the magazine and finished her reign as planned
She ignored the story and it quietly faded away
She resigned the Miss America title before her reign ended

evt-07-23-1984-vanessa-williams.butterflyEffect: Williams resigned her title, becoming the first Miss America to do so before her reign ended. She went on to a major career in music, film, and television, and in 2016 the Miss America Organization publicly apologized to her for how the scandal was handled.

evt-07-23-1995-comet-hale-bopp.scenario: It is the night of 23 July 1995 in the Arizona desert. Peering through a friend's telescope near the star cluster M70, you notice a faint fuzzy object that shouldn't be there.
evt-07-23-1995-comet-hale-bopp.prompt: What should you do with your discovery?

choices.text: Report the position immediately to the Central Bureau for Astronomical Telegrams
Wait several more nights to confirm alone before telling anyone
Dismiss it as a passing satellite reflection
Assume it is the known globular cluster and say nothing

evt-07-23-1995-comet-hale-bopp.butterflyEffect: Thomas Bopp reported the object immediately, and it was confirmed the same night as a new comet independently spotted by Alan Hale, giving it the joint name Hale–Bopp. Its unusual brightness at such a great distance from the sun signaled an exceptionally large nucleus, and it became the naked-eye "Great Comet of 1997," visible for a record eighteen months and, tragically, a trigger for the Heaven's Gate mass suicides.

evt-07-23-1999-1999-tulia-drug-arrests.scenario: It is July 1999 in Tulia, Texas. You are a local defense attorney reviewing a sweeping drug bust that relies almost entirely on the uncorroborated testimony of a single undercover agent.
evt-07-23-1999-1999-tulia-drug-arrests.prompt: What should you do about a case built on one agent's word alone?

choices.text: Refuse to represent any of the defendants
Accept the agent's testimony as sufficient
Demand corroborating evidence before trial
Advise your client to plead guilty regardless

evt-07-23-1999-1999-tulia-drug-arrests.butterflyEffect: Agent Tom Coleman's testimony convicted 38 of the 47 defendants, nearly all Black, though it lacked physical evidence or corroboration. Years of appeals revealed Coleman's own record of dishonesty; Governor Rick Perry pardoned 35 of the convicted in 2003, and the scandal became a landmark case in exposing racial bias in the drug war.

evt-07-23-1999-all-nippon-airways-flight.scenario: It is 23 July 1999, and you are the first officer of ANA Flight 61, a Boeing 747 over Tokyo carrying more than 500 passengers. A passenger armed with a knife has just forced his way into the cockpit and stabbed the captain.
evt-07-23-1999-all-nippon-airways-flight.prompt: What should you do to save the aircraft and everyone aboard?

choices.text: Attempt to negotiate with the hijacker over the intercom
Radio air traffic control and wait for instructions before acting
Order the cabin crew to evacuate passengers via emergency slides mid-flight
Physically overpower the hijacker and take control of the aircraft to land it

evt-07-23-1999-all-nippon-airways-flight.butterflyEffect: First officer Tetsuo Shirai physically wrestled control from hijacker Yuji Nishizawa and landed the jumbo jet safely back at Haneda Airport. Nishizawa was arrested and later imprisoned, and the incident led Japanese carriers to review cockpit access procedures on domestic flights.

evt-07-23-1999-space-shuttle-columbia.scenario: It is July 23, 1999. You are Commander Eileen Collins, the first woman to command a Space Shuttle mission, and moments after liftoff a short circuit and a fuel leak threaten Columbia's climb to orbit.
evt-07-23-1999-space-shuttle-columbia.prompt: What should you do as Columbia's ascent falls short of its planned trajectory?

choices.text: Abort to a lower fixed orbit and end the mission early
Continue the ascent and compensate with orbital maneuvering burns
Trigger a return-to-launch-site abort
Shut down the remaining engines and eject the crew

evt-07-23-1999-space-shuttle-columbia.butterflyEffect: Collins and her crew rode out the anomalies and used the shuttle's orbital maneuvering engines to reach the altitude needed to deploy the Chandra X-ray Observatory. The investigation into the wiring short led NASA to inspect and repair damaged wiring across the entire shuttle fleet, a safety measure that outlasted the mission itself.

evt-07-23-2001-megawati-sukarnoputri.scenario: It is 23 July 2001 in Jakarta. President Abdurrahman Wahid has just issued a decree trying to dissolve parliament, and you sit among the members of Indonesia's People's Consultative Assembly deciding how to respond.
evt-07-23-2001-megawati-sukarnoputri.prompt: What does the Assembly do next?

choices.text: Reinstate Wahid's authority and disband itself
Declare martial law and suspend the constitution
Call immediate new elections before any transfer of power
Impeach Wahid and swear in Megawati Sukarnoputri as president

evt-07-23-2001-megawati-sukarnoputri.butterflyEffect: The MPR rejected Wahid's decree, impeached him for incompetence, and swore in Vice President Megawati Sukarnoputri as Indonesia's first female president that same day. She steadied the post-Suharto economy but lost the country's first direct presidential election in 2004 to Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono.

evt-07-23-2010-one-direction.scenario: It is 2010, and you are a producer on The X Factor UK. Five young male contestants — Niall, Liam, Harry, Louis and Zayn — have each auditioned as soloists, but none seems strong enough alone to reach the live shows.
evt-07-23-2010-one-direction.prompt: What does judge Simon Cowell decide to do with them?

choices.text: Eliminate all five from the competition
Offer them a spot as backup dancers for another act
Ask each to return solo the following year
Combine them into a new boy band to compete as a group

evt-07-23-2010-one-direction.butterflyEffect: Cowell merged the five into a group called One Direction for the boy-band category. They finished only third on the show, but Cowell signed them to his label anyway, and the band went on to sell over 70 million records worldwide before splitting in 2016.

evt-07-23-2011-high-speed-rail.scenario: It is the night of 23 July 2011 near Wenzhou, China. A lightning strike has knocked out signals on the Yongtaiwen line, and a moving high-speed train has just rear-ended a stalled one on an elevated viaduct. As an official surveying the wreckage, you must decide how to handle the crushed carriages.
evt-07-23-2011-high-speed-rail.prompt: What did Chinese authorities actually do with the wrecked train cars in the crash's immediate aftermath?

choices.text: Displayed them publicly as a safety warning
Sold the wreckage for scrap metal
Preserved them intact for a lengthy independent investigation
Buried the wrecked carriages at the crash site soon afterward

evt-07-23-2011-high-speed-rail.butterflyEffect: Officials had the mangled carriages buried at the site within days, before independent investigators could examine them fully. The move triggered a furious public backlash on Chinese social media over transparency, forcing the government to exhume the wreckage and prompting broader reforms in high-speed rail safety oversight.

evt-07-23-2012-july-2012-solar-storm.scenario: You are a solar physicist on 23 July 2012, watching NASA's STEREO-A spacecraft record one of the most powerful coronal mass ejections ever observed erupting from the Sun.
evt-07-23-2012-july-2012-solar-storm.prompt: What actually happened when this CME's trajectory crossed Earth's orbital path?

choices.text: Earth's magnetosphere deflected it before impact
It struck Earth directly, causing global blackouts
It dissipated completely before reaching Earth's orbit
It missed Earth because the eruption site had already rotated away from Earth's facing side

evt-07-23-2012-july-2012-solar-storm.butterflyEffect: The storm missed Earth by about nine days because the eruption site had already rotated away from an Earth-facing position as the Sun spun on its axis. Scientists calculated that a direct hit could have caused Carrington-Event-level damage to satellites and power grids, spurring renewed research into protecting modern infrastructure from solar storms.

evt-07-23-2014-transasia-airways-flight-.scenario: It's the evening of 23 July 2014, and you are the crew of TransAsia Flight 222 approaching Magong Airport on Penghu Island as Typhoon Matmo brings low visibility, rain, and gusting crosswinds to the runway.
evt-07-23-2014-transasia-airways-flight-.prompt: What did the crew do as the aircraft descended below minimum altitude in the storm?

choices.text: They landed without incident on the first approach
They aborted early and diverted safely to another airport
They held in a circling pattern for over an hour before diverting
They descended below minimum altitude and attempted a late go-around before striking terrain

evt-07-23-2014-transasia-airways-flight-.butterflyEffect: The aircraft continued below the minimum descent altitude and struck buildings while attempting a late go-around, killing 48 of the 58 people aboard. Investigators cited pilot decision-making and poor crew coordination in bad weather, prompting new TransAsia safety procedures ahead of the airline's eventual 2016 shutdown after another fatal crash.

evt-07-23-2015-nasa.scenario: It is July 23, 2015, and you are part of the NASA team preparing to announce Kepler's discovery of a planet strikingly similar in size and orbit to Earth, circling a Sun-like star 1,400 light-years away.
evt-07-23-2015-nasa.prompt: How should you characterize the new world to the waiting press?

choices.text: As a failed observation to be quietly retracted
As a confirmed habitable planet
As a promising habitable-zone candidate that needs further study
As proof of extraterrestrial life

evt-07-23-2015-nasa.butterflyEffect: NASA presented Kepler-452b as Earth's 'bigger, older cousin,' a planet in its star's habitable zone, without claiming confirmed habitability. Its distance made further characterization impossible with existing instruments, but the discovery sharpened public and scientific interest in exoplanet atmospheres, feeding into later missions like TESS and the James Webb Space Telescope.

evt-07-23-2018-2018-attica-wildfires.scenario: It's the afternoon of 23 July 2018 in the seaside town of Mati, and fast-moving flames driven by high winds have cut off the inland roads, trapping residents and holidaymakers between the fire and steep cliffs above the sea.
evt-07-23-2018-2018-attica-wildfires.prompt: What did many of the trapped residents do to try to escape the flames?

choices.text: They fled down to the sea and waited in the water for rescue
They sheltered in underground bunkers built for emergencies
They climbed to rooftops to wait for helicopter rescue
They drove directly through the flames toward Athens

evt-07-23-2018-2018-attica-wildfires.butterflyEffect: Many fled down steep paths to the water and waited in the sea for rescue, but dozens still died from smoke, flames, or drowning during the descent. The disaster exposed illegal coastal construction and a lack of evacuation planning, triggering a national inquiry and the resignation of senior officials.

evt-07-24-1411-scottish-clan.scenario: It is 24 July 1411 near Inverurie in Aberdeenshire. You stand in the ranks of Alexander Stewart, Earl of Mar, facing the advancing Highland army of Donald of Islay, Lord of the Isles, who claims the earldom of Ross.
evt-07-24-1411-scottish-clan.prompt: What was the outcome of this brutal clash, later remembered as "Red Harlaw"?

choices.text: Both sides suffered such heavy losses that Donald's advance into the Lowlands was halted
A truce was reached and no battle was fought
Mar's army routed before battle was joined
Donald's Highlanders crushed Mar's force and seized Aberdeen

evt-07-24-1411-scottish-clan.butterflyEffect: Casualties were so severe on both sides that the battle is remembered as one of the bloodiest in Scottish history, and though inconclusive, it halted Donald's advance toward Aberdeen and the Lowlands.
