Harlaw became a lasting symbol of Highland-Lowland conflict, commemorated for centuries in ballads and local memory.

evt-07-24-1567-mary-queen-of-scots.scenario: It is July 1567. Imprisoned at Lochleven Castle after rebellious nobles rose against her, you are Mary, Queen of Scots, and documents of abdication have been placed before you.

choices.text: Flee immediately to France for refuge with Catholic allies
Appeal directly to Elizabeth I of England to restore your throne
Sign the abdication in favour of your infant son
Refuse and call on loyal nobles to crush the rebellion

evt-07-24-1567-mary-queen-of-scots.butterflyEffect: Mary signed the abdication, and her one-year-old son was crowned James VI of Scotland, raised under a Protestant regency. Mary escaped captivity the following year but fled to England seeking Elizabeth I's protection, leading instead to nineteen years of imprisonment and her execution in 1587 — while James eventually inherited the English throne too, uniting the crowns in 1603.

evt-07-24-1920-franco-syrian-war.scenario: It's July 1920, and you serve in King Faisal's hastily assembled Syrian army, facing a French ultimatum to disband or accept the mandate as French troops advance toward Damascus.
evt-07-24-1920-franco-syrian-war.prompt: What follows when Faisal's forces make their stand at Maysalun?

choices.text: Faisal's forces repel the French advance
Ottoman reinforcements arrive to reinforce Faisal's army
A negotiated ceasefire preserves Syrian independence
French troops decisively defeat the Syrian army and take Damascus

evt-07-24-1920-franco-syrian-war.butterflyEffect: French forces decisively defeated the Syrians and entered Damascus the next day, ending Syrian independence and installing a pro-French government. Britain, keen to placate Faisal, made him king of the new Iraqi mandate instead, reshaping the map of the postwar Middle East.

evt-07-24-1923-treaty-of-lausanne.scenario: It's 1923, and you're a Turkish delegate at Lausanne, tasked with replacing the failed Treaty of Sèvres that the Turkish National Movement had rejected and fought against.
evt-07-24-1923-treaty-of-lausanne.prompt: What must the new treaty do to succeed where Sèvres failed?

choices.text: Reimpose the old Capitulations exempting foreigners from Ottoman law
Recognize Turkish sovereignty over Anatolia and abandon partition plans
Divide Anatolia into separate Greek and Armenian states
Restore the Ottoman Sultanate under Allied protection

evt-07-24-1923-treaty-of-lausanne.butterflyEffect: The treaty recognized the sovereignty and borders of the new Republic of Turkey, abandoning earlier partition plans, and mandated a population exchange between Greece and Turkey. It became a founding document of modern Turkish statehood, still commemorated in Turkey today.

evt-07-24-1967-montreal.scenario: It is 24 July 1967. From the balcony of Montreal's city hall, French President Charles de Gaulle has just cried "Vive le Québec libre!" to a roaring crowd, and you are an aide to Prime Minister Lester Pearson deciding how Ottawa should respond.
evt-07-24-1967-montreal.prompt: How does the Canadian government answer de Gaulle's declaration?

choices.text: Pearson publicly rebukes de Gaulle for interfering in Canadian sovereignty
Expel the French ambassador immediately
Invite de Gaulle to Ottawa to celebrate the statement
Ignore the remark and proceed with the visit as planned

evt-07-24-1967-montreal.butterflyEffect: Pearson publicly rebuked de Gaulle, declaring that Canadians did not need to be liberated, and de Gaulle cut his visit short, returning to France without an official stop in Ottawa. The episode inflamed Quebec's sovereignty movement and helped set the stage for the founding of the Parti Québécois the following year.

evt-07-24-1967-charles-de-gaulle.scenario: You stand in a roaring crowd outside Montreal's city hall on 24 July 1967, listening to French President Charles de Gaulle address the balcony during his official visit for Expo 67.
evt-07-24-1967-charles-de-gaulle.prompt: What did de Gaulle declare that set off a diplomatic firestorm with Ottawa?

choices.text: "Vive le Canada uni!"
"Vive le Québec libre!"
"Vive la Révolution tranquille!"
"Vive la France libre!"

evt-07-24-1967-charles-de-gaulle.butterflyEffect: His cry of "Vive le Québec libre!" was taken by Prime Minister Lester Pearson as incitement to Quebec secession; Ottawa publicly rebuked him and de Gaulle cut his visit short, returning to France early. The phrase became a lasting rallying cry for the Quebec sovereignty movement for decades afterward.

evt-07-24-1969-apollo-program.scenario: You are a Navy diver from the USS Hornet, first to reach the Apollo 11 capsule bobbing in the Pacific after Armstrong, Aldrin, and Collins splash down from the Moon.
evt-07-24-1969-apollo-program.prompt: What must you have the astronauts do before they can board the recovery ship?

choices.text: Have them don Biological Isolation Garments before leaving the raft
Let them swim straight to a waiting helicopter
Give them a celebratory meal on the raft before recovery
Transfer them immediately to the open deck for photographs

evt-07-24-1969-apollo-program.butterflyEffect: Fearing unknown lunar microbes, NASA required the astronauts to don Biological Isolation Garments and then endure 21 days in a Mobile Quarantine Facility and Lunar Receiving Laboratory. No pathogens were ever found, and by Apollo 15 the quarantine protocol was dropped entirely.

evt-07-24-1977-egyptian-libyan-war.scenario: It's July 1977, and you're an Egyptian officer stationed along the Libyan frontier after months of Gaddafi-backed subversion aimed at toppling President Sadat.
evt-07-24-1977-egyptian-libyan-war.prompt: How does Sadat respond to Libyan provocations at the border?

choices.text: He requests UN peacekeepers to patrol the frontier
He launches a brief cross-border offensive against Libyan forces
He requests Arab League mediation before taking any military action
He proposes political union with Libya to defuse the crisis

evt-07-24-1977-egyptian-libyan-war.butterflyEffect: Egypt launched a brief cross-border offensive, and four days of fighting followed before Arab mediation brought a ceasefire. Relations between Cairo and Tripoli stayed hostile for years, deepening Egypt's isolation in the Arab world after Sadat's later peace with Israel.

evt-07-24-1983-black-july.scenario: It is 24 July 1983 in Colombo. Word has spread that Tamil Tiger guerrillas ambushed and killed thirteen Sri Lankan soldiers, and armed mobs are gathering with lists identifying Tamil-owned homes and shops.
evt-07-24-1983-black-july.prompt: What did this eruption of violence ultimately set in motion for Sri Lanka?

choices.text: An India-brokered ceasefire that ended Tamil militancy
The start of the full-scale Sri Lankan Civil War between the government and Tamil militants
A power-sharing agreement between Sinhalese and Tamil political parties
Immediate independence for the Tamil-majority north

evt-07-24-1983-black-july.butterflyEffect: The pogrom, which killed and displaced large numbers of Tamils and destroyed Tamil-owned property and businesses, is widely regarded as the point of no return that hardened support for Tamil militancy. It is commonly cited as the effective start of the Sri Lankan Civil War, which continued until 2009.

evt-07-24-1983-george-brett.scenario: It's July 24, 1983, at Yankee Stadium. George Brett's ninth-inning home run has just put the Royals ahead, but Yankees manager Billy Martin marches out to the umpires, pointing at the pine tar smeared far up the handle of Brett's bat.
evt-07-24-1983-george-brett.prompt: What do the umpires rule after inspecting the bat?

choices.text: The bat is ruled illegal and Brett's home run is nullified, making him the final out
The umpires forfeit the game to the Yankees on the spot
Brett is ejected from the game for arguing with the umpires
The umpires dismiss Martin's protest and the home run stands as called

evt-07-24-1983-george-brett.butterflyEffect: Umpire Tim McClelland ruled the bat illegal under a rule limiting pine tar height, calling Brett out and ending the game in a Yankees win. The Royals protested, and American League president Lee MacPhail overturned the call, ordering the game resumed from that point 25 days later — a resumption the Royals won, making the 'Pine Tar Incident' one of baseball's most famous rules disputes.

evt-07-24-1987-ss-bridgeton.scenario: It's July 24, 1987, and you're aboard the reflagged tanker Bridgeton, leading the first US-escorted convoy through the Persian Gulf under Operation Earnest Will.
evt-07-24-1987-ss-bridgeton.prompt: What happens as Bridgeton nears Farsi Island?

choices.text: Bridgeton strikes a mine but survives, embarrassing US escorts
Iranian gunboats intercept and board the convoy
The convoy detects and destroys an Iranian mine before impact
The convoy safely reroutes around a known minefield

evt-07-24-1987-ss-bridgeton.butterflyEffect: Bridgeton's hull held after striking an Iranian mine, but the incident embarrassed Washington by exposing the US Navy's inability to protect its own escorted convoy. It spurred an urgent buildup of American minesweeping forces in the Gulf and marked a sharp escalation in the so-called Tanker War.

evt-07-24-1998-united-states-capitol.scenario: It is 24 July 1998. You are on duty at a Capitol security checkpoint when an armed man rushes past the metal detector, heading toward the offices of the House leadership.
evt-07-24-1998-united-states-capitol.prompt: What happens as officers try to stop him?

choices.text: Call for backup and wait outside without engaging
Let him pass because he seems harmless
Quietly evacuate the building without confronting him
Chestnut blocks him and is shot, then Gibson engages and stops him at the cost of his own life

evt-07-24-1998-united-states-capitol.butterflyEffect: Officer Jacob Chestnut moved to block the gunman and was shot dead; Officer John Gibson then engaged the attacker, fatally wounding him but dying of his own injuries. Both officers were honored with a lying-in-honor at the Capitol, and the incident led to expanded security screening and a memorial named for them near the building's entrance.

evt-07-24-2014-air-algerie-flight-5017.scenario: You are the co-pilot of Air Algérie Flight 5017, an MD-83 climbing through the night over Mali into a massive wall of thunderstorms that stretches for hundreds of miles across your route.
evt-07-24-2014-air-algerie-flight-5017.prompt: What critical step did investigators later say the crew failed to take before ice disrupted their instruments?

choices.text: Switch on the engine anti-icing system before entering the storm
Descend below the storm cell before continuing
Disengage the autopilot and fly manually the entire time
Increase airspeed to punch through the storm quickly

evt-07-24-2014-air-algerie-flight-5017.butterflyEffect: The crew had not activated the engine anti-icing system, allowing ice to affect the aircraft's angle-of-attack sensors; the autopilot disengaged and the plane entered a stall the crew failed to recognize or recover from in time. All 116 people aboard died, and the disaster renewed scrutiny of crew training for high-altitude stall recovery in tropical storm systems.

evt-07-24-2025-angara-airlines-flight-23.scenario: It's July 24, 2025, and you're aboard an aging Antonov An-24 circling back toward Tynda Airport in eastern Russia after a failed first landing attempt. Thick fog blankets the runway below.
evt-07-24-2025-angara-airlines-flight-23.prompt: What happens when the pilots attempt a second landing?

choices.text: The plane diverts to a nearby airport and lands safely
The plane holds in a pattern until visibility improves
The plane makes an emergency landing on a nearby road
The plane crashes into forest short of the runway

evt-07-24-2025-angara-airlines-flight-23.butterflyEffect: The aircraft crashed into forest about 16 kilometres from the airport, killing all 48 aboard. The disaster renewed scrutiny of Russia's remote regional carriers still flying Soviet-era An-24s decades past their design life, made harder to maintain by sanctions-driven parts shortages.

evt-07-25-306-constantine-the-great.scenario: It is 25 July 306 at Eboracum in Britain. Your father, Emperor Constantius Chlorus, has just died on campaign, and his legions gather around you, his son, ready to declare you their new ruler.
evt-07-25-306-constantine-the-great.prompt: What do you do as the assembled troops proclaim you emperor?

choices.text: Accept the troops' proclamation as emperor and seek recognition from Rome
Refuse the title and defer to Galerius's chosen successor
Flee to Gaul to avoid a succession dispute
Wait for the Senate to confirm the succession before acting

evt-07-25-306-constantine-the-great.butterflyEffect: Constantine accepted the army's acclamation, though senior emperor Galerius recognized him only as Caesar rather than Augustus, sparking years of rivalry within the fracturing Tetrarchy. That struggle culminated in Constantine's victory at the Milvian Bridge in 312 and his eventual conversion to Christianity, reshaping the empire's religious future.

evt-07-25-1893-corinth-canal.scenario: It's 25 July 1893, and officials formally open the Corinth Canal, slicing through the Isthmus of Corinth after centuries of failed attempts to link the Ionian and Aegean seas without sailing around the Peloponnese.
evt-07-25-1893-corinth-canal.prompt: What is the immediate consequence for shipping in the region?

choices.text: Emperor Nero's ancient canal design is finally completed as originally planned
Structural flaws force the canal to close within weeks
The canal becomes the busiest shipping route in the Mediterranean
Ships gain a much shorter route, but many modern vessels remain too wide to use it

evt-07-25-1893-corinth-canal.butterflyEffect: The canal cut hundreds of kilometres off journeys around the Peloponnese, but at only 24.6 metres wide at sea level, it could never accommodate many modern ships. Today it survives mainly as a tourist attraction rather than the major trade route its builders envisioned.

evt-07-25-1898-spanish-american-war.scenario: It is 25 July 1898. You are aboard a US Army transport off Puerto Rico's south coast as General Nelson Miles orders ships toward the small port of Guánica instead of the expected target of San Juan.
evt-07-25-1898-spanish-american-war.prompt: Why does Miles choose to land at Guánica rather than San Juan?

choices.text: Guánica had weaker Spanish defenses and a safe deep-water anchorage
It let them link up directly with Cuban rebel forces
It was the closest point to Puerto Rico's capital city
Spanish forces had already surrendered the port

evt-07-25-1898-spanish-american-war.butterflyEffect: The landing met almost no resistance, and US forces advanced across Puerto Rico with barely a fight before Spain sought an armistice days later. The island passed to American control under the Treaty of Paris, beginning over a century of US sovereignty there.

evt-07-25-1943-grand-council-of-fascism.scenario: It is the night of 24-25 July 1943 inside Rome's Palazzo Venezia. You sit on the Grand Council of Fascism as Dino Grandi reads a motion demanding King Victor Emmanuel III reclaim command of Italy's armed forces from Mussolini.
evt-07-25-1943-grand-council-of-fascism.prompt: How do you cast your vote on Grandi's motion of no confidence?

choices.text: Vote for the motion, joining the majority against Mussolini
Walk out of the session before the vote is called
Vote against the motion to preserve Mussolini's authority
Abstain to avoid taking a side

evt-07-25-1943-grand-council-of-fascism.butterflyEffect: The motion passed by a wide margin, and the next day the King had Mussolini arrested, replacing him with Marshal Pietro Badoglio. Germany rescued Mussolini weeks later and installed him as puppet ruler of the Salò Republic, splitting Italy into two warring halves for the rest of the war.

evt-07-25-1976-viking-1.scenario: It is 25 July 1976, and you are a NASA imaging scientist reviewing fresh orbital photographs of Mars's Cydonia region beamed back by Viking 1. One frame shows a mesa lit at a low sun angle that looks eerily like a giant human face staring up from the surface.
evt-07-25-1976-viking-1.prompt: What do NASA scientists conclude about the image at release?

choices.text: They cancel further Cydonia imaging out of caution.
They classify the image and withhold it from the public for decades.
They announce evidence of an artificial monument built by an ancient civilization.
They describe it as a trick of light and shadow on an ordinary eroded landform.

evt-07-25-1976-viking-1.butterflyEffect: NASA's own caption called the 'face' a trick of light and shadow, but the image spread widely and fueled decades of pseudoscientific speculation about a Martian monument. When NASA's Mars Global Surveyor photographed the same mesa in far higher resolution in 1998, it revealed a plain, eroded hill, quietly ending the mainstream version of the myth.

evt-07-25-1978-in-vitro-fertilisation.scenario: It's 1978, and you are part of the medical team treating Lesley Brown, whose earlier attempts at pregnancy using hormone-stimulated IVF cycles have failed. You must decide how to proceed with this attempt.
evt-07-25-1978-in-vitro-fertilisation.prompt: What approach do you take for this fertilisation attempt?

choices.text: Administer high-dose hormone stimulation to produce multiple eggs
Use a donor egg instead of the mother's own
Use a natural cycle with no hormone stimulation drugs
Transfer several embryos simultaneously to improve the odds

evt-07-25-1978-in-vitro-fertilisation.butterflyEffect: The team used a natural, unstimulated cycle, and Louise Brown was born on 25 July 1978 at Dr Kershaw's Cottage Hospital in Oldham — the first person ever conceived by IVF. Robert Edwards later won the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the breakthrough, and by the 2020s more than twelve million children worldwide had been born through IVF and related techniques.

evt-07-25-1983-black-july.scenario: It is 25 July 1983, and you are a guard at Welikada high-security prison in Colombo, where thirty-seven Tamil political prisoners are held amid mounting anti-Tamil riots across the city.
evt-07-25-1983-black-july.prompt: What happens to the Tamil prisoners at Welikada that day?

choices.text: Sinhalese prisoners, in an attack later described as organized, kill dozens of the Tamil detainees inside the prison.
A prison riot is suppressed without any deaths.
The army evacuates them by helicopter to Jaffna.
The prisoners are quietly transferred to a safer facility.

evt-07-25-1983-black-july.butterflyEffect: The Welikada massacre became one of the defining atrocities of Black July, in which mobs killed thousands of Tamils across Sri Lanka. The violence hardened Tamil support for militant separatism, accelerating the Sri Lankan Civil War that would last until 2009.

evt-07-25-1984-salyut-7.scenario: It is 25 July 1984 aboard Salyut 7, and you are cosmonaut Svetlana Savitskaya, suited up at the airlock with crewmate Vladimir Dzhanibekov. No woman has ever stepped outside a spacecraft in orbit.

choices.text: She becomes the first woman to fly solo to a space station instead.
She aborts the walk after a suit malfunction.
She stays inside while Dzhanibekov performs the walk alone.
She exits the airlock and completes a spacewalk, testing a metal-cutting and welding tool in vacuum.

evt-07-25-1984-salyut-7.butterflyEffect: Savitskaya became the first woman to walk in space, three months before NASA's Kathryn Sullivan matched the feat during a Shuttle mission. Her EVA, which included testing a tool for cutting and welding metal, demonstrated Soviet capability for future station maintenance work.

evt-07-25-1993-lebanon.scenario: It is 25 July 1993. You are an Israeli commander ordered to launch a massive bombardment of southern Lebanon after weeks of Hezbollah rocket fire on Israeli towns.
evt-07-25-1993-lebanon.prompt: What is the stated goal of this offensive, later called Operation Accountability?

choices.text: Displace refugees toward Beirut to pressure Lebanon into restraining Hezbollah
Establish a new long-term Israeli occupation zone as far as Beirut
Permanently annex a strip of southern Lebanese territory
Capture Hezbollah's spiritual leader Sheikh Fadlallah

evt-07-25-1993-lebanon.butterflyEffect: The bombardment drove hundreds of thousands of Lebanese civilians toward Beirut, pressuring the Lebanese and Syrian governments to restrain Hezbollah. It ended in an unwritten US-brokered understanding on the rules of engagement that governed the border for years, until it collapsed with 1996's Operation Grapes of Wrath.

evt-07-25-1994-jordan.scenario: You are King Hussein of Jordan, standing beside Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin in Washington on 25 July 1994, decades of official war between your two nations behind you.
evt-07-25-1994-jordan.prompt: What do you agree to declare together?

choices.text: A full military alliance against neighbouring states
An end to the state of war between Jordan and Israel
A joint declaration recognising a Palestinian state
An immediate exchange of disputed territories

evt-07-25-1994-jordan.butterflyEffect: The Washington Declaration formally ended the state of belligerency between Jordan and Israel, opening border crossings and setting the stage for a full peace treaty signed that October. Jordan became only the second Arab state, after Egypt, to make peace with Israel, reshaping regional diplomacy for decades.

evt-07-25-1995-1995-france-bombings.scenario: It is the evening rush hour of 25 July 1995 at Saint-Michel station in Paris. A bomb hidden in a train has just killed eight people and wounded nearly 200, and panic is spreading through the Métro network.
evt-07-25-1995-1995-france-bombings.prompt: What did the French government do in the attack's immediate aftermath?

choices.text: Resume normal Métro service within the hour without added security
Shut down all border crossings with Algeria indefinitely
Impose a nationwide curfew on public transport
Activate the Vigipirate plan, deploying armed patrols across the transit network

evt-07-25-1995-1995-france-bombings.butterflyEffect: Paris activated its Vigipirate security plan, flooding transport hubs with armed patrols and searches. Investigators eventually traced the campaign to Algerian militant Khaled Kelkal, killed weeks later; Vigipirate itself became a permanent fixture of French life, still invoked after the 2015 attacks.

evt-07-25-1996-1996-burundian-coup-d-eta.scenario: It is 25 July 1996, and you serve in President Sylvestre Ntibantunganya's government in Bujumbura. Word arrives that former president Pierre Buyoya's soldiers have surrounded the palace, ending a fragile power-sharing deal amid Burundi's civil war.
evt-07-25-1996-1996-burundian-coup-d-eta.prompt: What follows in the weeks after Buyoya seizes power?

choices.text: Buyoya immediately holds free elections to legitimize his rule.
The UN swiftly restores Ntibantunganya to office.
Reprisal killings sweep the country, leaving thousands dead and Burundi diplomatically isolated by its neighbors.
Hutu and Tutsi factions sign a lasting peace within days.

evt-07-25-1996-1996-burundian-coup-d-eta.butterflyEffect: Amnesty International recorded more than 6,000 deaths in the coup's aftermath, and regional states led by Tanzania imposed an economic embargo on Buyoya's government. The pressure eventually pushed Burundi toward the Arusha peace process, which produced the 2000 Arusha Accords and a framework for ending the civil war.

evt-07-25-2000-air-france-flight-4590.scenario: It is 25 July 2000 at Charles de Gaulle Airport, and you are the flight engineer on Air France Flight 4590. Seconds after your Concorde starts its takeoff roll, a tire bursts and flames erupt beneath the left wing, but the aircraft has already passed decision speed.

choices.text: They continue the takeoff as required past V1, then struggle to control the burning, engine-damaged jet.
They abort the takeoff and stop safely on the runway.
They eject the crew via emergency parachutes.
They circle the airport for an hour to burn off fuel before landing.

evt-07-25-2000-air-france-flight-4590.butterflyEffect: The Concorde, crippled by fire from a ruptured fuel tank, crashed into a hotel in Gonesse minutes after takeoff, killing all 109 aboard and 4 on the ground. The disaster, traced to a titanium strip on the runway that shredded a tire, grounded the Concorde fleet and hastened its permanent retirement in 2003.

evt-07-25-2000-concorde.scenario: It is 25 July 2000 at Charles de Gaulle Airport. Aboard Air France Flight 4590, a tire has just burst on the runway and flames are erupting beneath the wing as the aircraft nears its takeoff decision speed.
evt-07-25-2000-concorde.prompt: What must the captain decide as the burning aircraft passes V1?

choices.text: Abort the takeoff and brake immediately
Steer onto a taxiway to slow down safely
Request permission to land on the grass median
Continue the takeoff, since there is no longer enough runway to stop

evt-07-25-2000-concorde.butterflyEffect: The crew continued the takeoff, as there was no longer enough runway to stop safely, but the burning jet lost power and crashed into a hotel in Gonesse, killing all 109 aboard and four on the ground. The disaster led to modified fuel tanks and tires, but Concorde never regained public confidence and was retired in 2003.

evt-07-25-2018-2018-suwayda-attacks.scenario: It is dawn on 25 July 2018 in the Druze villages around As-Suwayda, and gunmen loyal to the Islamic State are storming homes and detonating suicide vests in a coordinated assault.
evt-07-25-2018-2018-suwayda-attacks.prompt: How does the Syrian government respond to the attacks?

choices.text: It hands security of the province over to Druze militias permanently.
It withdraws all forces from Suwayda province.
It launches airstrikes and a ground offensive against ISIL's remaining enclave in the nearby Yarmouk Basin.
It negotiates a ceasefire granting ISIL fighters safe passage out of Syria.

evt-07-25-2018-2018-suwayda-attacks.butterflyEffect: The attacks killed at least 258 people, among the deadliest strikes on Syria's Druze minority in the war. In response, Damascus intensified its campaign against ISIL's last pocket in the Yarmouk Basin near the Golan Heights, contributing to the group's near-total territorial collapse in Syria later that year.

evt-07-26-1184-erfurt-latrine-disaster.scenario: It is July 26, 1184, and you are crammed into an upper-floor hall in Erfurt where King Henry VI has convened a Hoftag to settle a bitter dispute between the Archbishop of Mainz and the Landgrave of Thuringia. The floor groans beneath the crowd of assembled nobles.
evt-07-26-1184-erfurt-latrine-disaster.prompt: How does King Henry VI survive as the floor gives way beneath the room?

choices.text: Guards catch him as he falls into the cesspit
He is standing in a stone window alcove that does not give way
He had already left the hall moments before the collapse
He leaps from a second-floor window onto the street below

evt-07-26-1184-erfurt-latrine-disaster.butterflyEffect: The floor collapsed through to the latrine cesspit below, killing around sixty nobles who drowned or were crushed, while Henry VI survived because he was standing in a stone window recess that held firm. The disaster removed a generation of regional nobility at a stroke and became a grim byword for catastrophe in medieval chronicles.

evt-07-26-1551-knights-hospitaller.scenario: It is July 1551, and you command the small Hospitaller garrison inside Gozo's Cittadella as an Ottoman fleet under Sinan Pasha and the corsair Dragut lands thousands of troops, far outnumbering your defenders.
evt-07-26-1551-knights-hospitaller.prompt: With the population sheltering inside, what should you do?

choices.text: Surrender the castello to spare the sheltering population
Abandon the fortress and flee by ship with what treasure you can carry
Hold the walls indefinitely and wait for relief from Malta
Launch a sortie against the landing troops

evt-07-26-1551-knights-hospitaller.butterflyEffect: The garrison surrendered rather than fight on, and the Ottomans then rounded up nearly the entire population of Gozo—thousands of men, women, and children—and carried them off into slavery. The island was left almost empty, forcing decades of resettlement and pushing the Knights to overhaul Malta's own fortifications against future raids.

evt-07-26-1887-l-l-zamenhof.scenario: You are a young Warsaw ophthalmologist in 1887, about to publish a slim booklet under the pseudonym "Doktoro Esperanto," describing a new language you hope the whole world might one day share.
evt-07-26-1887-l-l-zamenhof.prompt: How should you release your language so it can actually spread?

choices.text: Sell exclusive rights to a European government
Publish the grammar and vocabulary freely for anyone to use
Keep it as a private project shared only with family
Limit its use strictly to religious translation

evt-07-26-1887-l-l-zamenhof.butterflyEffect: Zamenhof's Unua Libro launched Esperanto by openly publishing its grammar and vocabulary for anyone to learn and adapt, rather than restricting it. The language spread through grassroots clubs and international congresses, becoming the most widely spoken constructed language in the world, still used by communities today.

evt-07-26-1936-canadian-national-vimy-me.scenario: You stand among thousands of Canadian veterans and pilgrims gathered on the ridge in Pas-de-Calais on July 26, 1936, as the towering new monument to the fallen of Vimy Ridge is unveiled before the crowd.
evt-07-26-1936-canadian-national-vimy-me.prompt: Which head of state personally unveils the completed Vimy memorial?

choices.text: General Arthur Currie
King Edward VIII
The President of France
Prime Minister William Lyon Mackenzie King

evt-07-26-1936-canadian-national-vimy-me.butterflyEffect: King Edward VIII performed the unveiling, one of his last major public duties before the abdication crisis engulfed him later that year. The ceremony, attended by huge crowds of veterans, cemented Vimy Ridge as a founding symbol of Canadian national identity and wartime sacrifice.

evt-07-26-1953-colorado-city-arizona.scenario: It is dawn on 26 July 1953, and you are part of a large Arizona state force raiding the polygamist community of Short Creek. Roughly 400 residents, many of them children, are being rounded up on the governor's orders.
evt-07-26-1953-colorado-city-arizona.prompt: What does the state plan to do with the children of the arrested families?

choices.text: Leave them with elderly relatives in Short Creek
Return them to the community under state supervision
Place them in foster homes while parents face charges
Send them to boarding schools out of state

evt-07-26-1953-colorado-city-arizona.butterflyEffect: Children were placed in foster care while parents faced prosecution, but photographs of sobbing families separated by armed officers turned public opinion against the raid. The backlash helped end Governor Howard Pyle's political career and made Arizona and Utah wary of mass polygamy raids for the next half-century.

evt-07-26-1953-battle-of-the-samichon-ri.scenario: It is the night of 24-25 July 1953, and you command a platoon of the 2nd Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment, holding the position known as 'the Hook' on the Jamestown Line as Chinese forces launch massed night assaults just before the armistice.
evt-07-26-1953-battle-of-the-samichon-ri.prompt: With the enemy attacking in waves, what should your unit do?

choices.text: Hold the position and call in artillery support
Retreat to a secondary defensive line
Request an immediate local ceasefire
Abandon the position to strengthen the truce talks

evt-07-26-1953-battle-of-the-samichon-ri.butterflyEffect: UN troops held the Hook, repelling repeated Chinese assaults with heavy artillery and small-arms fire and inflicting severe casualties. The Chinese failed to gain a last-minute victory, and the armistice was signed on 27 July 1953, fixing the Jamestown Line as the basis for the Korean Demilitarized Zone that still divides the peninsula.

evt-07-26-1971-apollo-program.scenario: It's July 26, 1971, at Kennedy Space Center, and you're part of the ground crew for Apollo 15, the first "J-mission" built for extended lunar surface exploration far beyond earlier landing sites.
evt-07-26-1971-apollo-program.prompt: What new piece of equipment will let the astronauts range miles from the lunar module for the first time?

choices.text: A battery-powered Lunar Roving Vehicle
A motorized cargo sled towed behind the module
A rocket-powered flying backpack
A pressurized long-range rover truck

evt-07-26-1971-apollo-program.butterflyEffect: The Lunar Roving Vehicle let commander Dave Scott and pilot Jim Irwin drive miles across the Moon's surface, reaching sites impossible to walk to, including the famous Genesis Rock. The rover became standard equipment for the final two Apollo missions, 16 and 17, transforming how astronauts explored the Moon.

evt-07-26-1974-prime-minister-of-greece.scenario: It is late July 1974. The military junta has just collapsed amid the disaster in Cyprus, and you are summoned home from exile in Paris to form Greece's first civilian government in seven years.
evt-07-26-1974-prime-minister-of-greece.prompt: What should be the new government's most urgent priority?

choices.text: Reinstate the exiled king at once
Seek a formal alliance with the Soviet Union
Declare war on Turkey immediately over Cyprus
Legalize political parties and restore free elections

evt-07-26-1974-prime-minister-of-greece.butterflyEffect: Konstantinos Karamanlis led the Metapolitefsi, legalizing all political parties—including the long-banned Communist Party—and holding free elections that November. Weeks later a referendum abolished the monarchy, founding the Third Hellenic Republic that governs Greece today.

evt-07-26-1977-quebec.scenario: It is 26 July 1977, and Quebec's National Assembly is moving to make French the sole official language of government, courts, and the workplace across the province. You run an English-language firm in Montreal.
evt-07-26-1977-quebec.prompt: What must your business now do to comply with the new language law?

choices.text: Continue operating in English, since the law is unenforceable
Shift signage and daily operations to predominantly French
Relocate headquarters to another province immediately
Appeal directly to the federal government for a permanent exemption

evt-07-26-1977-quebec.butterflyEffect: The measure became the core of the Charter of the French Language (Bill 101), requiring French on signage and in commerce and schooling. It triggered a wave of anglophone businesses relocating to Toronto and decades of legal challenges, but it also cemented French as the everyday language of Quebec public life.

evt-07-26-1990-americans-with-disabiliti.scenario: You stand on the White House South Lawn on July 26, 1990, among wheelchair users and disability advocates who fought for years to get this bill to the president's desk. George H. W. Bush is about to sign it into law.
evt-07-26-1990-americans-with-disabiliti.prompt: Beyond banning discrimination, what new duty does this law place on employers?

choices.text: Raise the federal minimum wage nationwide
Guarantee paid family leave to all workers
Provide reasonable accommodations for employees with disabilities
Require mandatory union membership in covered workplaces

evt-07-26-1990-americans-with-disabiliti.butterflyEffect: The ADA required covered employers and public accommodations to provide reasonable accommodations and accessible facilities, going further than the 1964 Civil Rights Act's protections. It became the model disability-rights framework worldwide and was later broadened by the 2008 ADA Amendments Act.

evt-07-26-1993-asiana-airlines-flight-73.scenario: It is 26 July 1993, and you are in the cockpit of Asiana Flight 733, descending toward Mokpo Airport through heavy rain and thick cloud with the runway still not in sight.
evt-07-26-1993-asiana-airlines-flight-73.prompt: With visibility below minimums, what is the safe course of action?

choices.text: Descend further to try to spot the runway visually
Request the tower to switch on extra runway lighting and press on
Execute a go-around and attempt another approach
Continue on instruments alone at the current altitude

evt-07-26-1993-asiana-airlines-flight-73.butterflyEffect: The crew instead continued descending below the minimum safe altitude without adequate visual reference, and the Boeing 737 struck a mountain near Haenam, killing 68 of the 116 aboard. Investigators ruled it controlled flight into terrain caused by pilot error, and the crash became a case study in South Korea's push to tighten cockpit discipline on approach.

evt-07-26-2005-space-shuttle-program.scenario: It's July 26, 2005, and you're a NASA engineer watching new external-tank cameras during Discovery's ascent, the first shuttle launch since Columbia broke apart on reentry two and a half years earlier.
evt-07-26-2005-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What troubling flaw do the cameras reveal during the climb to orbit?

choices.text: A booster fails to separate cleanly at staging
A bird strike cracks a wing tile on ascent
The main engines shut down seconds early
A chunk of foam insulation sheds from the external tank

evt-07-26-2005-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: A large piece of foam broke off the external tank during ascent, echoing the exact flaw that doomed Columbia, though it missed Discovery. NASA grounded the shuttle fleet again for nearly a year to fix the tank design before flights resumed with STS-121.

evt-07-26-2005-mumbai.scenario: It is the afternoon of 26 July 2005, and Mumbai has already received nearly a metre of rain since morning. You are stuck in your car on a suburban road as filthy water climbs past the door sills and traffic has stopped dead.
evt-07-26-2005-mumbai.prompt: What should you do to survive the rising floodwater around your car?

choices.text: Honk continuously to alert nearby traffic police
Stay inside the car and wait for rescue
Abandon the car and move on foot toward higher ground
Drive forward through the flooded stretch to reach home faster

evt-07-26-2005-mumbai.butterflyEffect: Officials later urged residents to abandon vehicles for higher ground, since many of the 500-plus deaths came from people trapped in cars, swept into open drains, or electrocuted by submerged wires. The '26/7' deluge exposed Mumbai's chronic drainage failures and pushed the city toward a long-delayed overhaul of its storm-water system.

evt-07-26-2009-nigeria.scenario: It is 26 July 2009, and a small band of Boko Haram militants has just attacked a police station in Bauchi, northern Nigeria, in retaliation for a crackdown on the sect. You command the local police response as reports of arson and gunfire spread across the city.
evt-07-26-2009-nigeria.prompt: What did Nigerian security forces do in the days after this attack?

choices.text: Launch a coordinated crackdown across multiple states to crush the uprising
Negotiate a ceasefire and release detained sect members
Withdraw police from the region and let local militias handle it
Declare a national state of emergency and call in UN peacekeepers

evt-07-26-2009-nigeria.butterflyEffect: The clashes spread to Borno, Yobe and Kano, killing hundreds before the military stormed Boko Haram's compound in Maiduguri. Founder Mohammed Yusuf was captured and killed in police custody days later, an act many historians say radicalized the movement into the far deadlier insurgency that followed under Abubakar Shekau.

evt-07-26-2016-hillary-clinton.scenario: It's July 26, 2016, on the floor of the Democratic National Convention in Philadelphia. Bernie Sanders, your candidate through a hard-fought primary, suddenly moves from the floor to halt the roll call and nominate Hillary Clinton by acclamation.
evt-07-26-2016-hillary-clinton.prompt: As a Sanders delegate, how do you respond to his motion?

choices.text: Call for a recount of the primary results
Demand the roll call continue to a full count
Join the acclamation to show party unity
Walk out of the convention hall immediately

evt-07-26-2016-hillary-clinton.butterflyEffect: Sanders' motion passed, and Clinton became the first woman nominated for president by a major U.S. party, though many Bernie delegates walked out in protest rather than cheer. The visible split foreshadowed lingering party disunity that some analysts later cited as a factor in her narrow loss to Donald Trump that November.

evt-07-26-2016-sagamihara-stabbings.scenario: In the days after the July 26, 2016 attack at a Kanagawa care home, Japanese police and news outlets face a decision about how to report on the victims, most of whom lived with severe disabilities.
evt-07-26-2016-sagamihara-stabbings.prompt: What did officials decide about identifying the victims to the public?

choices.text: Release only the victims' ages and nothing else
Publish full names and photographs as standard practice
Delay all reporting until the trial concluded years later
Withhold most victims' names to protect families from stigma

evt-07-26-2016-sagamihara-stabbings.butterflyEffect: Police withheld most victims' names at families' request, citing fear of social stigma toward disability in Japan. The decision ignited a national debate about disability rights and visibility, with advocacy groups arguing that anonymity, however well-intentioned, could reinforce the same stigma the attacker had voiced.

evt-07-26-2016-solar-impulse.scenario: You watch from the tarmac in Abu Dhabi on July 26, 2016, as pilot Bertrand Piccard guides the fragile, wide-winged Solar Impulse 2 down for its final landing after a journey around the entire globe powered by nothing but sunlight.
evt-07-26-2016-solar-impulse.prompt: What does this flight's completion prove about aviation?

choices.text: Sustained flight powered entirely by the sun, without fuel, is achievable
Jet fuel efficiency had been doubled by new engine designs
An uncrewed aircraft had circled the globe for the first time
Supersonic flight was now possible using solar power

evt-07-26-2016-solar-impulse.butterflyEffect: Solar Impulse 2 became the first aircraft to circumnavigate the Earth using only solar power, with no fuel at all, after 17 legs and over a year of flying. Its success validated solar aviation technology and spurred further research into long-endurance solar drones and clean-energy flight.

evt-07-27-1689-jacobite-rising-of-1689.scenario: It's 27 July 1689, and you charge downhill with John Graham of Claverhouse, Viscount Dundee, as his Highlanders sweep through the pass of Killiecrankie toward Hugh Mackay's government redcoats waiting below.
evt-07-27-1689-jacobite-rising-of-1689.prompt: What is the outcome of this Highland charge?

choices.text: Both sides withdraw without a decisive engagement
French reinforcements arrive and tip the battle further
The Jacobites shatter Mackay's army, but Dundee is fatally wounded
Mackay's disciplined volleys break the charge and rout the Highlanders

evt-07-27-1689-jacobite-rising-of-1689.butterflyEffect: The Jacobites shattered Mackay's army, but Dundee was mortally wounded in the moment of victory. Without his leadership the rising lost momentum, collapsing within weeks and leaving Stuart hopes in Scotland unfulfilled for another generation.

evt-07-27-1778-battle-of-ushant-1778.scenario: It is 27 July 1778, 100 miles west of Ushant. You serve aboard a British ship of the line under Admiral Keppel, watching the French fleet under d'Orvilliers maneuver to avoid a decisive close engagement.
evt-07-27-1778-battle-of-ushant-1778.prompt: What was the outcome of this first fleet clash of the American Revolutionary War?

choices.text: The fleets fought an inconclusive action and both withdrew without a clear victor
The British decisively destroyed the French fleet
The French fleet was captured intact after surrendering
The two fleets never made contact and sailed past each other

evt-07-27-1778-battle-of-ushant-1778.butterflyEffect: The battle was inconclusive, with both fleets suffering damage but neither achieving a decisive victory before the French withdrew. The murky result sparked a bitter political and court-martial controversy in Britain over Admiral Keppel's conduct, exposing deep factional splits within the Royal Navy's officer corps just as France entered the war on America's side.

evt-07-27-1919-red-summer.scenario: It's a scorching July 27, 1919, on a Lake Michigan beach in Chicago. You watch white youths hurl stones at Eugene Williams, a black teenager, after his raft drifts across an unofficial racial line in the water, and he slips under.
evt-07-27-1919-red-summer.prompt: What follows after Williams drowns and police refuse to arrest the man responsible?

choices.text: The city quickly arrests and prosecutes the man responsible
Rage boils over into days of racial violence across Chicago
Black and white beachgoers reconcile peacefully that afternoon
The National Guard prevents any unrest that week

evt-07-27-1919-red-summer.butterflyEffect: Fury over the drowning ignited days of racial violence across Chicago, part of the wider Red Summer of white supremacist terror in over three dozen American cities that year. The bloodshed helped galvanize the NAACP's growing civil rights organizing in the years that followed.

evt-07-27-1949-jet-airliner.scenario: It's July 27, 1949, at Hatfield Aerodrome in England. You are test pilot John Cunningham, throttling up the sleek new de Havilland Comet for its maiden flight while the world's airlines wait to see if a jet engine can carry paying passengers.
evt-07-27-1949-jet-airliner.prompt: What does this flight prove about the future of civil aviation?

choices.text: Jet engines are too unreliable for civilian aircraft
Propeller aircraft remain faster over long distances
Jet propulsion can power a viable passenger airliner
The test fails, delaying jet airliners for a decade

evt-07-27-1949-jet-airliner.butterflyEffect: The Comet became the first commercial jet airliner, entering service in 1952 and briefly making Britain the leader in jet travel. But a series of fatal 1954 crashes caused by metal fatigue grounded the fleet, opening the door for Boeing's 707 and Douglas's DC-8 to dominate the jet age instead.

evt-07-27-1990-jamaat-al-muslimeen.scenario: It is 27 July 1990 in Port of Spain. Armed members of the Jamaat al Muslimeen, led by Yasin Abu Bakr, storm the Red House parliament building and the television station, taking the Prime Minister and other officials hostage.
evt-07-27-1990-jamaat-al-muslimeen.prompt: What did the group's leaders demand in exchange for releasing the hostages?

choices.text: The release of foreign prisoners held abroad
Immediate independence for a new Islamic state
A ransom paid directly to the group's leader
An amnesty for the gunmen and resignation of the government

evt-07-27-1990-jamaat-al-muslimeen.butterflyEffect: The uprising held the government hostage for six days before the gunmen surrendered under a negotiated amnesty. That amnesty was later challenged and partly overturned in the courts, and the episode left Trinidad and Tobago's security establishment permanently wary of homegrown armed religious movements.

evt-07-27-1996-atlanta.scenario: It's just past midnight on July 27, 1996, in Atlanta's Centennial Olympic Park, where a late-night concert crowd is gathered during the Summer Olympics—and a backpack left near the sound tower has just detonated.
evt-07-27-1996-atlanta.prompt: What followed in the investigation of the Olympic Park bombing?

choices.text: Security guard Richard Jewell was wrongly named a suspect before the true bomber was found
The Games were immediately cancelled and moved to another city
A foreign terrorist cell was quickly identified and arrested
The explosion caused no injuries at all

evt-07-27-1996-atlanta.butterflyEffect: Two people died and over a hundred were injured. Security guard Richard Jewell, who had helped clear the area before the blast, was wrongly named a suspect and vilified by the press for months before being cleared; the real bomber, Eric Rudolph, evaded capture for five years. The case became a landmark example of media rumor overtaking due process.

evt-07-27-2007-car-chase.scenario: It's July 27, 2007, and you're a cameraman aboard a Phoenix TV news helicopter, banking tight to keep a live police chase in frame while a rival station's helicopter closes in for the same shot.
evt-07-27-2007-car-chase.prompt: What actually happens when the two aircraft converge on the same suspect vehicle?

choices.text: One helicopter runs low on fuel and breaks off first
Air traffic control redirects one aircraft before they get close
The pilots radio each other and maintain safe separation
The helicopters collide midair, killing all four crew members aboard

evt-07-27-2007-car-chase.butterflyEffect: The two helicopters collided in midair, killing all four crew members aboard both aircraft. The tragedy triggered FAA and NTSB reviews of aerial news coverage, and many stations moved toward pooled footage and stricter altitude separation rules for chase coverage.

evt-07-27-2010-mummy.scenario: It's July 2010, and as a Tokyo welfare official you've been trying for weeks to visit Sogen Kato, believed to be the city's oldest living man, only to have his family repeatedly turn you away at the door.
evt-07-27-2010-mummy.prompt: What do officials find when they finally force entry into his room?

choices.text: His mummified remains, dead for over 30 years while relatives collected his pension
Evidence that Kato had secretly emigrated decades earlier
An empty room; officials conclude Kato never existed
Kato alive but refusing all visitors out of shyness

evt-07-27-2010-mummy.butterflyEffect: They discovered his mummified remains, dead for more than 30 years while relatives had quietly kept collecting his pension. The scandal exposed a wider pattern of Japan's unaccounted-for elderly, prompting nationwide welfare audits and tighter pension-verification rules.

evt-07-27-2016-aston-martin-db9.scenario: It's July 27, 2016, at Aston Martin's Gaydon plant, and you watch the final Aston Martin DB9 roll off the line after twelve years as the marque's flagship grand tourer.
evt-07-27-2016-aston-martin-db9.prompt: Which new model takes over as Aston Martin's flagship grand tourer?

choices.text: The Aston Martin Vantage
The Aston Martin Rapide
The Aston Martin Vanquish
The Aston Martin DB11

evt-07-27-2016-aston-martin-db9.butterflyEffect: The Aston Martin DB11 launched later that year as a full redesign, introducing turbocharged engines and a new aluminum architecture. It marked the start of a new design language that would carry through the rest of Aston Martin's lineup.

evt-07-28-1148-crusades.scenario: It is late July 1148 outside Damascus. You stand among the crusader host of King Baldwin III and Conrad III, orchards cut down around the city walls, as word spreads that a large Muslim relief force is marching to break the siege.
evt-07-28-1148-crusades.prompt: What did the crusader leaders decide as the relief force approached?

choices.text: They handed command to the Byzantine emperor to continue the siege
They pressed the assault and stormed the city that night
They negotiated a permanent alliance with the city's rulers
They abandoned the siege and withdrew amid disputes and fear of relief forces

evt-07-28-1148-crusades.butterflyEffect: Divided by disputes over who would rule Damascus if it fell, and alarmed by reports of Nur ad-Din's approaching army, the crusader leaders abandoned the siege and withdrew. The failure effectively ended the Second Crusade's main campaign and left Damascus firmly aligned with the rising power of Nur ad-Din against the Crusader states.

evt-07-28-1540-henry-viii.scenario: It is 28 July 1540, and you stand among the crowd on Tower Hill in London, watching Thomas Cromwell, the king's once-indispensable chief minister, mount the scaffold.
evt-07-28-1540-henry-viii.prompt: What charge has sent Cromwell to his death?

choices.text: Plotting to assassinate the king
Refusing to swear the Act of Supremacy
Treason and heresy, tied to the failed marriage with Anne of Cleves
Adultery with the queen

evt-07-28-1540-henry-viii.butterflyEffect: Cromwell was executed for treason and heresy, blamed for the disastrous marriage to Anne of Cleves and accused of tolerating Protestant extremism. His fall removed the chief architect of the English Reformation's administration, and Henry married Catherine Howard the very same day, underscoring how quickly Tudor favor could turn to ruin.

evt-07-28-1821-peruvian-war-of-independe.scenario: It's July 28, 1821, and you stand in Lima's main square as Argentine general José de San Martín proclaims Peru's independence from Spain before a crowd.
evt-07-28-1821-peruvian-war-of-independe.prompt: What title does San Martín take to lead the new state?

choices.text: Viceroy of Peru
Protector of Peru
President of the Republic
Emperor of Peru

evt-07-28-1821-peruvian-war-of-independe.butterflyEffect: San Martín governed as "Protector of Peru" but ceded leadership after his 1822 meeting with Simón Bolívar in Guayaquil. Full Spanish rule in South America ended only after Bolívar's forces won the decisive Battle of Ayacucho in 1824.

evt-07-28-1866-vinnie-ream.scenario: It is 1866 in the U.S. Capitol, and you are a senator weighing an unprecedented $10,000 federal commission for a marble statue of the slain President Lincoln. The leading candidate is Vinnie Ream, an eighteen-year-old Missouri sculptor with no formal academy training, up against seasoned male artists.
evt-07-28-1866-vinnie-ream.prompt: Do you vote to award the historic commission to the young, untested sculptor?

choices.text: Postpone the decision until a national design competition can be held
Give the commission to an established male sculptor instead
Award the commission to Vinnie Ream despite her age and inexperience
Split the commission between two competing artists

evt-07-28-1866-vinnie-ream.butterflyEffect: Congress awarded Ream the commission, making her the first woman and youngest artist ever to receive a U.S. government arts commission. She completed the Lincoln statue in 1871, now standing in the Capitol rotunda, and her win opened the door for women to compete for federal public art commissions.

evt-07-28-1911-australasian-antarctic-ex.scenario: It is 28 July 1911 at a London dock. You watch SY Aurora cast off, carrying Douglas Mawson and his men south to chart thousands of miles of unknown Antarctic coastline and test new wireless technology against the ice.
evt-07-28-1911-australasian-antarctic-ex.prompt: What tragedy struck one of the expedition's sledging parties in the following year?

choices.text: Two men died on a sledging journey after a crevasse fall and later exhaustion
The ship Aurora was crushed by pack ice with all hands lost
A fire destroyed the main base hut and all scientific records
The wireless station failed permanently, cutting off contact with Australia

evt-07-28-1911-australasian-antarctic-ex.butterflyEffect: In December 1912, Belgrave Ninnis fell into a crevasse with his sledge team and vital supplies, and Xavier Mertz later died of exhaustion and possible vitamin poisoning, leaving Mawson to trek back alone. His harrowing solo survival became one of the most famous stories in polar exploration and cemented the expedition's scientific legacy, including the discovery of the first Antarctic meteorite.

evt-07-28-1915-united-states-marine-corp.scenario: It is 28 July 1915, and you are a US Marine officer wading ashore at Port-au-Prince. Haiti's president has just been torn apart by a mob, and Washington has ordered you to secure the capital and protect American interests.
evt-07-28-1915-united-states-marine-corp.prompt: What is your mission as the occupation begins?

choices.text: Withdraw immediately once street order is restored
Support the mob leaders and help install their chosen government
Confine your men to guarding only the US legation building
Establish martial law and take control of Haiti's customs houses and treasury

evt-07-28-1915-united-states-marine-corp.butterflyEffect: Marines declared martial law, seized customs houses, and took control of Haiti's treasury, beginning a 19-year occupation. Forced labor policies sparked the Caco rebellion, and American oversight of Haitian finances and infrastructure left a legacy of resentment that shaped US-Haiti relations for decades after withdrawal in 1934.

evt-07-28-1945-north-american-b-25-mitch.scenario: It is a foggy Saturday morning, 28 July 1945, and you are working on the 79th floor of the Empire State Building when you hear engines roaring far too close through the mist.

choices.text: A German V-1 rocket strikes the tower
An electrical fault sparks a fire on the upper floors
A Japanese kamikaze aircraft hits the building
A B-25 bomber, lost in the fog, crashes into the building's 79th floor

evt-07-28-1945-north-american-b-25-mitch.butterflyEffect: A disoriented B-25 pilot, blinded by fog, slammed into the building's 79th floor, killing the crew and several office workers. Elevator operator Betty Lou Oliver survived a record-setting fall when a cable snapped, and the crash later helped establish precedent for suing the federal government for military accidents under the Federal Tort Claims Act.

evt-07-28-1976-1976-tangshan-earthquake.scenario: It's the days after July 28, 1976, and you're a Chinese official assessing the ruins of Tangshan. Foreign governments have offered emergency rescue teams and supplies.
evt-07-28-1976-1976-tangshan-earthquake.prompt: What does China's leadership decide about the offers of foreign aid?

choices.text: Accept the aid to speed up rescue and rebuilding
Decline nearly all foreign aid, relying on domestic resources instead
Hand relief operations over to the United Nations
Request help only from allied communist nations

evt-07-28-1976-1976-tangshan-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Beijing declined nearly all foreign assistance, relying instead on the military and domestic resources under the era's policy of national self-reliance. The scale of the disaster and the strain of going it alone later fed into arguments for the greater openness to outside help China would show under Deng Xiaoping's reforms.

evt-07-28-1984-olympic-games.scenario: It's July 28, 1984, and you're in the packed Los Angeles Coliseum as the Games of the XXIII Olympiad open. The Soviet Union and over a dozen allied nations have already announced a boycott in retaliation for the US-led boycott of Moscow in 1980.
evt-07-28-1984-olympic-games.prompt: Despite the boycott, what happens to these Games?

choices.text: They become a financial success and draw record crowds despite the absences
The IOC postpones them to the following year
The United States withdraws in retaliation for the boycott
They are cancelled due to insufficient participating nations

evt-07-28-1984-olympic-games.butterflyEffect: The 1984 Games went ahead with 140 nations and, under organizer Peter Ueberroth's corporate-sponsorship model, turned a large profit—the first Olympics to do so since 1932. That financial success reshaped how future host cities approached funding the Games.

evt-07-28-1995-rajneesh-movement.scenario: It is 1985, and you are Charles Turner, the U.S. Attorney in Oregon leading the investigation into the Rajneeshpuram commune, whose leadership has grown desperate to stop your inquiry into their activities.
evt-07-28-1995-rajneesh-movement.prompt: What ultimately happens to the two followers who plotted to have you killed?

choices.text: They flee the country and are never located
They turn themselves in and are granted immunity for testimony
They are acquitted for lack of evidence
They are convicted in 1995 after a long investigation

evt-07-28-1995-rajneesh-movement.butterflyEffect: In 1995, a decade after the plot was uncovered, two Rajneesh followers were convicted for conspiring to assassinate Turner. The case closed one of the final chapters of the Rajneeshee scandal, which had already seen commune leaders convicted over the 1984 salmonella poisoning attack on The Dalles, Oregon's residents.

evt-07-28-1996-prehistory.scenario: It's July 28, 1996, and two college students wading in the shallows of the Columbia River near Kennewick, Washington, find a human skull lodged in the mud.
evt-07-28-1996-prehistory.prompt: What follows once archaeologists examine the ancient remains?

choices.text: The remains are shipped overseas for study and never returned
The discovery site is immediately turned into a national park
They are quietly reburied without any further examination
They spark a long legal battle between scientists and Native American tribes over repatriation

evt-07-28-1996-prehistory.butterflyEffect: The remains, dubbed Kennewick Man, became the center of a decades-long legal fight between scientists seeking to study them and local tribes demanding repatriation under federal law. A 2015 DNA study finally showed close genetic ties to modern Native Americans, and in 2017 the remains were reburied by a coalition of tribes.

evt-07-28-2001-ian-thorpe.scenario: It is July 2001 in Fukuoka, Japan, and you are Ian Thorpe preparing to swim the anchor leg of the final relay at the World Aquatics Championships. Five gold medals already hang around your neck, and one more race stands between you and a first in the sport's history.
evt-07-28-2001-ian-thorpe.prompt: What must happen in this final race for Thorpe to make swimming history?

choices.text: Withdraw from the final event to rest for the Olympics
Simply finish the meet without disqualification to preserve his five golds
Break the 1500m freestyle world record instead of swimming the relay
Anchor his team to gold, completing an unprecedented six golds at one Worlds

evt-07-28-2001-ian-thorpe.butterflyEffect: Australia won the relay, giving Thorpe six gold medals at a single World Championships, the first swimmer ever to do so. The feat cemented his status as the sport's dominant force heading into the 2004 Athens Olympics and made him a national icon in Australia.

evt-07-28-2002-coal-mining.scenario: It is July 27, 2002, and you are overseeing rescue operations above the flooded Quecreek Mine in Somerset County, Pennsylvania. Nine miners are trapped in a pocket of air 240 feet underground, and rising water threatens to drown them before help can reach them.
evt-07-28-2002-coal-mining.prompt: What is the rescue team's best chance of reaching the trapped miners alive?

choices.text: Drill a narrow borehole to pump pressurized air, then bore a larger rescue shaft
Send divers down through the flooded shaft to search for survivors
Dig a horizontal tunnel from a neighboring mine shaft
Pump the mine dry before attempting any drilling

evt-07-28-2002-coal-mining.butterflyEffect: Crews drilled a six-inch borehole to pump pressurized warm air into the pocket, then bored a wider rescue shaft, and all nine miners were pulled out alive after 77 hours underground. The dramatic rescue became a national media sensation and drew renewed attention to mine safety and old mine-map hazards.

evt-07-28-2005-provisional-irish-republi.scenario: It's July 28, 2005, and you're reading the Provisional IRA's statement ordering all its units to end the armed campaign and dump their weapons, pursuing only peaceful and democratic means.
evt-07-28-2005-provisional-irish-republi.prompt: What follows this declaration in the peace process?

choices.text: Sinn Féin is banned from standing in elections
The British Army immediately withdraws entirely from Northern Ireland
An independent commission verifies the IRA has decommissioned its weapons within months
The Good Friday Agreement is signed for the first time

evt-07-28-2005-provisional-irish-republi.butterflyEffect: In September 2005, the Independent International Commission on Decommissioning confirmed the IRA had put its entire arsenal beyond use. The move helped restore confidence in the peace process and paved the way toward the eventual restoration of devolved government in Northern Ireland.

evt-07-28-2010-airblue-flight-202.scenario: It is the morning of 28 July 2010. You are an air traffic controller in Islamabad watching Airblue Flight 202 make its approach to Benazir Bhutto International Airport through poor visibility and heavy monsoon cloud over the Margalla Hills.
evt-07-28-2010-airblue-flight-202.prompt: What did the subsequent investigation identify as central to the crash?

choices.text: The crew descended below safe altitude in poor weather during an unstabilized approach
Structural failure of the wing caused a mid-air breakup
A bomb planted by militants detonated in the cargo hold
A bird strike disabled both engines on final approach

evt-07-28-2010-airblue-flight-202.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew descended below the safe minimum altitude during an unstabilized approach in bad weather, flying the Airbus A321 into the Margalla Hills and killing all 152 aboard. The disaster, Pakistan's deadliest air accident, prompted scrutiny of cockpit discipline and approach procedures at Pakistani carriers.

evt-07-28-2017-nawaz-sharif.scenario: It is 28 July 2017, and you are Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in Islamabad. The Supreme Court has spent months probing your family's offshore wealth after the Panama Papers leak, and today it delivers its verdict.
evt-07-28-2017-nawaz-sharif.prompt: What does the Supreme Court rule?

choices.text: Disqualify him from holding public office for life over concealed assets
Refer the matter to parliament for a political resolution
Sentence him immediately to prison without further proceedings
Acquit him and dismiss the corruption allegations entirely

evt-07-28-2017-nawaz-sharif.butterflyEffect: The court disqualified Sharif for life for concealing assets, forcing his resignation and elevating Shahid Khaqan Abbasi as interim PM. Sharif was later convicted in an accountability court, and the ruling deepened political instability that helped fuel Imran Khan's rise to power in 2018.

evt-07-28-2022-2022-appalachian-floods.scenario: It's July 28, 2022, and you're a resident in eastern Kentucky watching floodwater climb past your porch faster than you've ever seen, with the roads out of town already submerged.
evt-07-28-2022-2022-appalachian-floods.prompt: What is the safest action to take right now?

choices.text: Stay in the basement to protect your belongings
Move to higher ground immediately and wait there for rescue
Wait until nightfall before trying to reach a neighbor's house
Drive quickly through the flooded roads to reach town

evt-07-28-2022-2022-appalachian-floods.butterflyEffect: Rescuers ultimately carried out over 600 helicopter rescues and countless boat rescues across the region as the floods became the deadliest natural disaster to hit eastern Kentucky in more than 80 years. The catastrophe prompted a federal disaster declaration and renewed scrutiny of flood preparedness in Appalachian communities.

evt-07-29-904-arab-byzantine-wars.scenario: It's late July 904, and you live in Thessalonica, the Byzantine Empire's second city, as the fleet of renegade commander Leo of Tripoli breaches the harbor defenses and pours into the streets.
evt-07-29-904-arab-byzantine-wars.prompt: What befalls the city and its people once the fleet takes it?

choices.text: It is burned completely and left uninhabited
It pays tribute and the fleet withdraws peacefully
It is sacked and thousands of residents are taken captive
It is annexed and garrisoned as a caliphate outpost

evt-07-29-904-arab-byzantine-wars.butterflyEffect: Thessalonica was sacked and thousands of its inhabitants were carried off into captivity, a disaster chronicled by the eyewitness John Kaminiates. The raid exposed how vulnerable even major Byzantine cities were to seaborne attack, prompting the empire to overhaul its Aegean fleet and coastal fortifications in the following decades.

evt-07-29-1014-byzantine-bulgarian-wars.scenario: It is 29 July 1014 near Kleidion, in the mountain passes of the Belasica range. You serve in Emperor Basil II's army, which has just trapped and shattered the forces of Tsar Samuel of Bulgaria.
evt-07-29-1014-byzantine-bulgarian-wars.prompt: What does Basil II order done with the thousands of captured Bulgarian soldiers?

choices.text: Exile them to Anatolia as farmers
Ransom them back to Samuel for gold
Conscript them into the Byzantine army
Blind the captured soldiers and send them home

evt-07-29-1014-byzantine-bulgarian-wars.butterflyEffect: Basil ordered the prisoners blinded and sent back to Samuel, earning himself the epithet "Bulgar-Slayer." Samuel reportedly collapsed and died upon seeing his ruined army, and Bulgarian resistance crumbled, leading to full Byzantine annexation of Bulgaria by 1018.

evt-07-29-1567-james-vi-and-i.scenario: You are a Scottish noble at Stirling in July 1567, days after Mary, Queen of Scots was forced to abdicate. Her infant son is about to be crowned, but he is far too young to rule.
evt-07-29-1567-james-vi-and-i.prompt: What must the assembled lords arrange to govern in the new king's name?

choices.text: Appoint a regent to govern until he comes of age
Dissolve the Scottish Parliament entirely
Invite Elizabeth I to rule Scotland directly
Crown Mary's husband as king instead

evt-07-29-1567-james-vi-and-i.butterflyEffect: The lords appointed the Earl of Moray as regent, the first of several regents who ruled Scotland through James's long minority. James eventually came of age, and in 1603 he inherited the English throne as well, uniting the Scottish and English crowns under one monarch for the first time.

evt-07-29-1693-nine-years-war.scenario: It is 29 July 1693 near the village of Neerwinden in the Spanish Netherlands. You serve in William III's Grand Alliance army as Marshal Luxembourg's French troops storm your entrenched lines after hours of brutal assault.
evt-07-29-1693-nine-years-war.prompt: As the defenses buckle, what does William III's battered army do?

choices.text: Hold the entrenchments to the last man
Retreat across the Geer river under pressure
Launch a full cavalry counterattack on Luxembourg's center
Surrender the camp immediately

evt-07-29-1693-nine-years-war.butterflyEffect: The Allies retreated across the Geer river in disorder, suffering some of the heaviest casualties of the century, though William himself escaped capture. Despite the costly French victory, Luxembourg failed to press the advantage, and the war ground on to stalemate, ending in 1697 with the Treaty of Ryswick, which recognized William as England's king.

evt-07-29-1818-augustin-jean-fresnel.scenario: You sit on the French Academy panel judging Fresnel's 1818 memoir on light diffraction. Fellow judge Poisson has just used Fresnel's own wave equations to predict something seemingly absurd: a bright spot at the very center of a circular object's shadow.
evt-07-29-1818-augustin-jean-fresnel.prompt: How should the panel respond to this apparently impossible prediction?

choices.text: Test the prediction experimentally before judging
Disqualify the memoir for contradicting Newton
Reject the wave theory outright as absurd
Award the prize without further scrutiny

evt-07-29-1818-augustin-jean-fresnel.butterflyEffect: Rather than dismiss it, the Academy had the prediction tested experimentally. Arago performed the experiment and found the bright spot exactly where the wave theory predicted, turning a supposed refutation into decisive proof. Fresnel won the prize, and wave theory dominated optics until quantum physics revived light's particle nature.

evt-07-29-1900-gaetano-bresci.scenario: You are a plainclothes officer working the crowd in Monza on 29 July 1900. King Umberto I is riding through in an open carriage after a sporting event, and a returned emigrant with a grudge over the Bava Beccaris massacre is somewhere in the throng.
evt-07-29-1900-gaetano-bresci.prompt: What happens as the king's carriage passes through the crowd?

choices.text: Royal guards form a human shield and Bresci is disarmed
Bresci throws a bomb that explodes harmlessly nearby
Police intercept Bresci before he can draw his weapon
Bresci fires four shots, killing the king instantly

evt-07-29-1900-gaetano-bresci.butterflyEffect: Bresci fired four pistol shots, killing Umberto I instantly. His son Victor Emmanuel III succeeded him as king. Bresci was sentenced to life imprisonment at Santo Stefano and died within the year, officially ruled a suicide under circumstances many still question.

evt-07-29-1914-river-monitor.scenario: You serve aboard the Austro-Hungarian river monitor Bodrog on the Danube in the last days of July 1914, hours after Austria-Hungary's declaration of war on Serbia, with orders to open fire across the river.
evt-07-29-1914-river-monitor.prompt: What target does Bodrog's crew shell to fire the war's opening shots?

choices.text: Serbian rail lines north of Niš
The Serbian fortress at Smederevo
The bridge linking Belgrade to Zemun
Belgrade, the Serbian capital directly across the river

evt-07-29-1914-river-monitor.butterflyEffect: Bodrog and other Austro-Hungarian monitors shelled Belgrade on 29 July 1914, firing what are considered the first shots of the First World War. The bombardment forced Serbia's government to relocate from its capital, and fighting along the Danube continued as a persistent secondary front through the war that soon engulfed Europe.

evt-07-29-1921-adolf-hitler.scenario: It's July 1921 in Munich. You are a member of the small National Socialist German Workers' Party, watching Hitler threaten to quit unless he is granted absolute, dictatorial control over the party after a bitter internal power struggle.
evt-07-29-1921-adolf-hitler.prompt: How does the party respond to Hitler's ultimatum?

choices.text: They call his bluff and he backs down
The party splits into two rival factions
They expel him from the party for insubordination
They accept his demands, granting him dictatorial control

evt-07-29-1921-adolf-hitler.butterflyEffect: The party capitulated, giving Hitler near-total control as Führer of the movement. This consolidation of power inside a fringe Munich party became the foundation for his later seizure of the German state and the catastrophe that followed.

evt-07-29-1950-korean-war.scenario: You are an American cavalry officer near No Gun Ri in late July 1950. Thousands of Korean refugees approach your position along a rail line, and command fears North Korean soldiers may be hidden among them.
evt-07-29-1950-korean-war.prompt: Before any order to fire on the crowd, what should be required first?

choices.text: Withdraw the unit without engaging at all
Fire on the entire group as ordered
Positively identify armed combatants before firing
Let the refugees pass without any check

evt-07-29-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: Instead, troops opened fire on the refugee column at the No Gun Ri bridge and tunnel over several days, killing hundreds of civilians. The killings were suppressed for decades until a 1999 Associated Press investigation forced the US and South Korean governments to acknowledge them, leading to a formal expression of regret in 2001.

evt-07-29-1981-wedding-of-prince-charles.scenario: It is July 1981, and you are on the committee planning the wedding of Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer. Westminster Abbey has hosted nearly every royal wedding for generations, but it cannot seat the crowd this event demands.
evt-07-29-1981-wedding-of-prince-charles.prompt: Where do you stage the ceremony to accommodate the huge guest list and global audience?

choices.text: Westminster Abbey
Buckingham Palace gardens
St Paul's Cathedral
Windsor Castle chapel

evt-07-29-1981-wedding-of-prince-charles.butterflyEffect: Planners broke with tradition and chose St Paul's Cathedral for its far greater capacity and acoustics for the choir and trumpeters. An estimated 750 million people worldwide watched the ceremony, making it one of the most-watched broadcasts in history, and Diana became a global celebrity whose marriage and later divorce reshaped the monarchy's relationship with the press.

evt-07-29-1981-abolhassan-banisadr.scenario: You are Abolhassan Banisadr, Iran's ousted president, in hiding after your impeachment on June 21, 1981. Massoud Rajavi, leader of the Mujahedin-e-Khalq, offers a dangerous way out of the country.
evt-07-29-1981-abolhassan-banisadr.prompt: With arrest imminent, what should Banisadr do?

choices.text: Seek asylum inside the Soviet embassy
Surrender to the Revolutionary Guards
Remain hidden inside Iran indefinitely
Flee by air to France with Rajavi

evt-07-29-1981-abolhassan-banisadr.butterflyEffect: Banisadr and Rajavi escaped aboard a hijacked Iranian Air Force jet and flew to Paris, where they formed the National Council of Resistance of Iran. The alliance soon collapsed, and Banisadr spent the rest of his life in French exile as a leading dissident voice against the Islamic Republic.

evt-07-29-1985-space-shuttle-challenger.scenario: You are seated at a console in Houston's Mission Control on 29 July 1985 as Space Shuttle Challenger climbs toward orbit on STS-51-F, when a faulty sensor triggers an unplanned shutdown of a main engine mid-ascent.
evt-07-29-1985-space-shuttle-challenger.prompt: What call from Mission Control saves the flight after the engine failure?

choices.text: Shutdown of remaining engines and mission scrub
A full abort with crew bailout
An immediate return-to-launch-site landing
An "abort to orbit," settling for a lower stable orbit

evt-07-29-1985-space-shuttle-challenger.butterflyEffect: Controllers ordered the first-ever "Abort to Orbit," and Challenger settled into a lower but stable orbit, completing its science mission safely. The close call exposed how narrow the shuttle's safety margins really were, just months before Challenger was lost entirely during STS-51-L in January 1986.

evt-07-29-1987-rajiv-gandhi.scenario: You are an aide to Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in July 1987, watching him prepare to sign an accord with Sri Lankan President J. R. Jayewardene meant to end the island's ethnic civil war and grant devolution to Tamil-majority areas.
evt-07-29-1987-rajiv-gandhi.prompt: What did the accord commit India to sending into Sri Lanka?

choices.text: Indian economic sanctions against the Sri Lankan government
An Indian naval blockade of Tamil Tiger supply routes
A jointly commanded UN peacekeeping mission
An Indian Peacekeeping Force to enforce disarmament of Tamil militants

evt-07-29-1987-rajiv-gandhi.butterflyEffect: The accord dispatched Indian troops as the Indian Peacekeeping Force to disarm Tamil militants. The IPKF instead became mired in years of fighting against the LTTE, suffering heavy losses before withdrawing in 1990. Militant fury over the intervention is widely linked to Rajiv Gandhi's own assassination by an LTTE suicide bomber in 1991.

evt-07-29-1993-supreme-court-of-israel.scenario: It is 1993 and you sit on the Israeli Supreme Court panel reviewing John Demjanjuk's death sentence for allegedly being 'Ivan the Terrible' of Treblinka. Newly opened Soviet archives cast doubt on the identification.
