evt-07-29-1993-supreme-court-of-israel.prompt: Facing new evidence of doubtful identity, how should the court rule?

choices.text: Uphold the death sentence regardless of the new evidence
Acquit him due to reasonable doubt over his identity
Commute the sentence to life imprisonment
Order a new trial focused solely on Sobibor charges

evt-07-29-1993-supreme-court-of-israel.butterflyEffect: The court acquitted Demjanjuk, finding reasonable doubt after Soviet records suggested another man, Ivan Marchenko, was the real 'Ivan the Terrible.' He returned to the US, but was later stripped of citizenship and deported to Germany, where in 2011 he was convicted of separate crimes as a guard at Sobibor before dying pending appeal.

evt-07-29-2005-eris-dwarf-planet.scenario: It's January 2005, and you're part of Mike Brown's team at Palomar Observatory reviewing images of a bright, distant object beyond Neptune that appears to rival Pluto in size.
evt-07-29-2005-eris-dwarf-planet.prompt: Before going public, what should the team do first?

choices.text: Verify the object's orbit and mass through further observation
Dismiss it as a comet and move on
Announce it immediately as the tenth planet
Wait for NASA to send a probe before saying anything

evt-07-29-2005-eris-dwarf-planet.butterflyEffect: The team spent months confirming Eris's orbit and mass before announcing the discovery in July 2005. Its size, comparable to Pluto's, forced the IAU to define "planet" in 2006 — a decision that demoted Pluto to dwarf planet status.

evt-07-29-2015-malaysia-airlines-flight-.scenario: You are a French investigator on Réunion Island in July 2015, examining a barnacle-covered wing fragment washed ashore more than a year after MH370 vanished.
evt-07-29-2015-malaysia-airlines-flight-.prompt: What should investigators do to confirm this piece came from the missing airliner?

choices.text: Match the part's serial number to Boeing maintenance records
Rely solely on eyewitness accounts from the beach
Judge it only by the barnacle growth pattern
Assume it is unrelated ocean debris

evt-07-29-2015-malaysia-airlines-flight-.butterflyEffect: Investigators matched the part's maintenance number to Boeing 777 records, confirming it was a flaperon from MH370. The discovery proved the plane had crashed into the southern Indian Ocean, ending theories of a hijacking to a hidden airfield and refocusing the search along drift-modeled currents, though the main wreckage was never recovered.

evt-07-29-2021-international-space-stati.scenario: It's 29 July 2021, and you're a flight controller in Houston when the newly docked Russian Nauka module's thrusters unexpectedly fire on their own, slowly tilting the entire International Space Station out of position.
evt-07-29-2021-international-space-stati.prompt: What must mission control do to stop the station from spinning further?

choices.text: Evacuate the crew immediately in the Soyuz capsule
Detach Nauka from the station entirely
Fire opposing thrusters on other docked modules to counteract the spin
Power down the entire station and wait it out

evt-07-29-2021-international-space-stati.butterflyEffect: Ground teams fired counter-thrusters on the Zvezda module and a docked Progress spacecraft to cancel out Nauka's misfire, restoring the station's orientation after about 45 minutes and roughly one and a half rotations. The incident raised fresh concerns about Nauka's software reliability within the ongoing US-Russian partnership aboard the ISS.

evt-07-30-1811-miguel-hidalgo-y-costilla.scenario: It is July 30, 1811, in Chihuahua. You are Father Miguel Hidalgo, captured months after your Grito de Dolores launched Mexico's fight for independence, and Spanish authorities have condemned you as a rebel priest.
evt-07-30-1811-miguel-hidalgo-y-costilla.prompt: What is Hidalgo's fate on this day?

choices.text: He is sentenced to life imprisonment
He is executed by firing squad
He escapes and continues leading the rebellion
He is pardoned and exiled to Spain

evt-07-30-1811-miguel-hidalgo-y-costilla.butterflyEffect: Hidalgo was executed by firing squad and beheaded, his head displayed publicly for a decade as a warning to rebels. His death made him a martyr, and the independence movement continued under other leaders until Mexico finally won independence in 1821; he is honored today as the Father of the Nation.

evt-07-30-1916-world-war-i.scenario: It is just after midnight on 30 July 1916. You are a night watchman on Black Tom Island in New York Harbor, guarding piers stacked with munitions bound for the Allies, when you notice small fires flickering among the crates.
evt-07-30-1916-world-war-i.prompt: What follows this act of German sabotage at the munitions depot?

choices.text: Several ships sink but Manhattan itself is untouched
The munitions are safely removed before any damage occurs
A small, contained fire is quickly extinguished with no casualties
A massive explosion rocks the harbor, damaging the Statue of Liberty and shattering windows across Manhattan

evt-07-30-1916-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: A massive explosion tore through Black Tom, killing several people, shattering windows across Manhattan, and sending shrapnel into the Statue of Liberty. The attack fueled American suspicion of German sabotage, boosted the preparedness movement, and later led to a postwar claims case holding Germany financially responsible.

evt-07-30-1930-montevideo.scenario: It is 30 July 1930, and you are packed into the newly built Estadio Centenario in Montevideo, watching the host nation Uruguay face Argentina in the very first FIFA World Cup final.
evt-07-30-1930-montevideo.prompt: What is the result of this historic final?

choices.text: The final is abandoned after crowd trouble
Argentina wins 2–1 in extra time
The match ends in a scoreless draw
Uruguay wins 4–2 to become the first World Cup champions

evt-07-30-1930-montevideo.butterflyEffect: Uruguay won 4–2, cementing the young nation's status as an early football power and giving the World Cup instant legitimacy as a global spectacle. The bitter final also deepened the Uruguay–Argentina rivalry, souring relations enough that Argentina boycotted the next World Cup in 1934.

evt-07-30-1950-royal-question.scenario: It is 30 July 1950, and Belgium is gripped by a general strike over King Leopold III's return from exile. At Grâce-Berleur near Liège, you watch striking miners advance on a power station as gendarmes block their path.
evt-07-30-1950-royal-question.prompt: What happens as the confrontation at Grâce-Berleur reaches its peak?

choices.text: Leopold personally addresses the crowd and calms the unrest
The strikers disperse peacefully after brief negotiations
The army arrests King Leopold on the spot
Gendarmes open fire, killing four strikers

evt-07-30-1950-royal-question.butterflyEffect: Gendarmes opened fire, killing four strikers and shocking the nation, pushing Belgium to the edge of civil war. The bloodshed forced a political compromise in which Leopold agreed to transfer his royal powers to his son Baudouin, leading to his formal abdication in 1951.

evt-07-30-1975-jimmy-hoffa.scenario: It is the evening of July 30, 1975, outside the Machus Red Fox restaurant in suburban Detroit. You are Jimmy Hoffa, waiting for a meeting with mob-connected associates you believe will help you reclaim control of the Teamsters.
evt-07-30-1975-jimmy-hoffa.prompt: What happens to Hoffa after he leaves this meeting spot?

choices.text: He is arrested for tax evasion
He testifies before Congress on organized crime
He wins reinstatement as Teamsters president
He is never seen again, and his body is never found

evt-07-30-1975-jimmy-hoffa.butterflyEffect: Hoffa vanished after leaving the restaurant and was never seen again, presumed murdered by organized-crime figures threatened by his push to retake the Teamsters presidency. Despite decades of investigation, his remains have never been found, and the case remains officially unsolved.

evt-07-30-1981-1981-polish-hunger-demons.scenario: It is 30 July 1981, and you march through the streets of Łódź with thousands of women and children, banging empty pots to protest bare shelves and food rationing under Communist rule.
evt-07-30-1981-1981-polish-hunger-demons.prompt: What follows in the months after these peaceful hunger demonstrations spread across Poland?

choices.text: The marches are violently crushed by police at the scene
The government immediately resigns and calls free elections
Food shortages are quickly resolved through new trade deals
The government eventually declares martial law that December

evt-07-30-1981-1981-polish-hunger-demons.butterflyEffect: The hunger marches exposed how deeply the economic crisis had eroded public patience, adding to the pressure on the Communist government. By December 1981, General Jaruzelski declared martial law, arresting Solidarity leaders in a crackdown that shaped Poland's politics for the rest of the decade.

evt-07-30-2003-volkswagen-beetle.scenario: You are a factory worker in Puebla, Mexico, on 30 July 2003, watching the final 'Última Edición' Beetle roll off the line after 65 years of continuous production.
evt-07-30-2003-volkswagen-beetle.prompt: What made this particular Beetle a milestone in automotive history?

choices.text: It marked the one millionth Beetle built in Mexico
It was the first Beetle ever exported to the United States
It was the final original Type 1 Beetle, ending 65 years of production
It was the first Beetle fitted with a diesel engine

evt-07-30-2003-volkswagen-beetle.butterflyEffect: It was the last of the original Type 1 design ever built, closing out 65 years and 21.5 million units, the longest production run of any single car generation. Volkswagen had already launched the retro-styled 'New Beetle' in 1998, ensuring the shape lived on as a design icon even after the original engineering ceased.

evt-07-30-2003-pyrenean-ibex.scenario: Three years after Celia, the last Pyrenean ibex, died, you are part of a Spanish team implanting a clone made from her preserved skin cells into a surrogate goat, hoping to reverse the subspecies' extinction.
evt-07-30-2003-pyrenean-ibex.prompt: What happens when the cloned kid is finally born?

choices.text: The clone is born alive but dies within minutes from a lung defect
The pregnancy fails and no birth occurs at all
The clone survives and is raised successfully in captivity for years
The clone survives and later breeds to restore the population

evt-07-30-2003-pyrenean-ibex.butterflyEffect: The clone was born alive on 30 July 2003 but died within minutes from a severe lung defect, briefly making the Pyrenean ibex the first species to go extinct twice. The attempt, though a failure in the long run, became a landmark proof-of-concept that later inspired renewed "de-extinction" research on other lost species.

evt-07-30-2006-top-of-the-pops.scenario: You are a producer in the BBC studio on 30 July 2006, cueing the closing countdown for Top of the Pops after 42 years as Britain's weekly chart show.
evt-07-30-2006-top-of-the-pops.prompt: What led the BBC to finally cancel the world's longest-running music show?

choices.text: A licensing dispute with record labels over performance fees
A government ruling banning chart shows on the BBC
Declining ratings as audiences shifted to music channels and the internet
A presenter scandal that forced the show off air

evt-07-30-2006-top-of-the-pops.butterflyEffect: Ratings had collapsed as viewers turned to music channels, downloads, and the internet for new songs, making a weekly chart countdown feel outdated. The cancellation marked the end of appointment-viewing pop television in Britain, though the format was occasionally revived for Christmas specials and archive rebroadcasts.

evt-07-30-2006-2006-qana-airstrike.scenario: It's July 30, 2006, and reports arrive that an Israeli airstrike has struck a building in Qana, Lebanon, killing 28 civilians, 16 of them children. Diplomats worldwide scramble to respond as outrage grows.
evt-07-30-2006-2006-qana-airstrike.prompt: What did Israel do in the immediate aftermath of the strike?

choices.text: Israel declared an immediate, permanent ceasefire
Israel expanded airstrikes across all of Lebanon
Israel withdrew all forces from Lebanon that day
Israel halted airstrikes for 48 hours

evt-07-30-2006-2006-qana-airstrike.butterflyEffect: Israel halted airstrikes for 48 hours amid global condemnation and intensifying calls for a ceasefire. That pause gave diplomats room to negotiate, and within two weeks a UN-brokered ceasefire ended the 34-day Lebanon War on August 14, 2006.

evt-07-30-2011-zara-tindall.scenario: It's July 30, 2011, and you're among the guests at Canongate Kirk in Edinburgh, watching Zara Phillips, the Queen's eldest granddaughter, marry rugby player Mike Tindall.
evt-07-30-2011-zara-tindall.prompt: What title did Zara receive from the Queen upon her marriage?

choices.text: No title
Countess of Strathearn
Duchess of Edinburgh
Princess Royal

evt-07-30-2011-zara-tindall.butterflyEffect: Zara declined the peerage the Queen offered, remaining plain Mrs Tindall rather than becoming a duchess or countess. Her choice reinforced a pattern among the monarch's grandchildren of stepping back from formal royal titles while staying close to the family.

evt-07-30-2012-2012-india-blackouts.scenario: You are a grid controller in northern India on 30 July 2012, watching the frequency needle sink as state after state draws far more power than its allotted share.
evt-07-30-2012-2012-india-blackouts.prompt: What triggered the cascading failure that would black out over 600 million people?

choices.text: States overdrawing power beyond their quotas overloaded the interconnected grid
A cyberattack disabled grid control software
A coordinated attack on transmission substations
Monsoon flooding destroyed key transmission towers

evt-07-30-2012-2012-india-blackouts.butterflyEffect: States repeatedly overdrew power beyond their allocated quotas, and when the strained grid could no longer cope it collapsed in a cascade across 22 states. The disaster, then the largest blackout in history, forced India to tighten grid discipline and strengthen the powers of its national load dispatch centre to enforce quota limits.

evt-07-30-2018-emmerson-mnangagwa.scenario: You are an opposition supporter in Harare on 30 July 2018, waiting anxiously as results come in from Zimbabwe's first election since Robert Mugabe's fall.
evt-07-30-2018-emmerson-mnangagwa.prompt: What followed the announcement of Mnangagwa's narrow victory?

choices.text: The election was peacefully re-run within weeks
International observers declared the vote the fairest in Zimbabwe's history
Mnangagwa immediately stepped down after opposition pressure
Troops fired on protesters disputing the result, killing several people in Harare

evt-07-30-2018-emmerson-mnangagwa.butterflyEffect: Soldiers opened fire on protesters disputing the result in Harare, killing six people, even as opposition leader Nelson Chamisa challenged the outcome in court. Zimbabwe's Constitutional Court ultimately upheld Mnangagwa's win, and ZANU–PF's grip on power continued largely unbroken despite hopes that Mugabe's departure would bring genuine reform.

evt-07-30-2020-mars-2020.scenario: You are a NASA engineer at Cape Canaveral on 30 July 2020, watching the Atlas V rocket carrying the Perseverance rover climb into the sky during a pandemic-quiet launch.
evt-07-30-2020-mars-2020.prompt: What made Perseverance's mission distinct from earlier Mars rovers?

choices.text: It was designed to search for biosignatures and cache samples for eventual return to Earth
It was designed primarily to map the planet's magnetic field
It was built to drill for water ice at the Martian poles
It carried the first crewed habitat module to Mars

evt-07-30-2020-mars-2020.butterflyEffect: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater, an ancient lakebed, and began sealing rock samples for a future Mars Sample Return mission. Its companion, the helicopter Ingenuity, went on to make the first powered flight on another planet before retiring in 2024, proving aerial scouting of Mars was possible.

evt-07-30-2023-islamic-state-khorasan-pr.scenario: It's July 30, 2023, and thousands have gathered in Khar, in Pakistan's Bajaur district, for a political rally ahead of the coming elections. As speeches begin, a suicide bomber moves toward the stage.
evt-07-30-2023-islamic-state-khorasan-pr.prompt: Which political party's rally was the target of the bombing that killed over 60 people?

choices.text: Pakistan Peoples Party
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf
Awami National Party
Pakistan Muslim League (N)

evt-07-30-2023-islamic-state-khorasan-pr.butterflyEffect: The bomber struck an Awami National Party gathering, and ISIS-K claimed responsibility, part of its campaign against secular and mainstream Pakistani parties. The attack intensified security debates ahead of national elections and underscored the group's ability to strike political targets despite years of counterterrorism operations.

evt-07-30-2025-2025-kamchatka-earthquake.scenario: It is 30 July 2025, and you head an emergency management office on the Pacific coast of Japan. Word arrives that a magnitude 8.8 earthquake has just struck off Kamchatka, and tsunami models are still being calculated.
evt-07-30-2025-2025-kamchatka-earthquake.prompt: With the wave's size still uncertain, what do you order for coastal residents?

choices.text: Advise residents the distance makes any wave negligible
Wait until the wave is visually confirmed before acting
Issue evacuation orders for low-lying coastal areas
Evacuate only fishing boats, leaving residents in place

evt-07-30-2025-2025-kamchatka-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Authorities across the Pacific issued evacuation orders as a precaution. The resulting tsunami was smaller than feared in most locations, roughly a metre or less, though one narrow inlet near Vestnik Bay saw a run-up over 33 metres. In Japan, evacuation-related incidents caused one indirect death and 21 injuries, showing that the response itself carried real risk even when the wave did not.

evt-07-31-1667-second-anglo-dutch-war.scenario: You are an English negotiator at Breda in July 1667, still stinging from the Dutch fleet's raid up the Medway weeks earlier, working out final terms to end the naval war with the Dutch Republic.
evt-07-31-1667-second-anglo-dutch-war.prompt: What key territorial arrangement did the Treaty of Breda confirm?

choices.text: England kept New Netherland while the Dutch kept Suriname
The Dutch surrendered all their colonies in the New World
England gained control of Dutch trade routes in the East Indies
England ceded New Amsterdam back to the Dutch

evt-07-31-1667-second-anglo-dutch-war.butterflyEffect: England retained the North American colony of New Netherland, including New Amsterdam, which it renamed New York, while the Dutch kept their South American colony of Suriname. This settlement entrenched English colonial power along the American Atlantic coast for the following century.

evt-07-31-1777-second-continental-congre.scenario: You sit among the delegates in Philadelphia on 31 July 1777, weighing a request from an eager nineteen-year-old French nobleman who has crossed the Atlantic asking to serve America's cause without pay.
evt-07-31-1777-second-continental-congre.prompt: What did the Second Continental Congress do about the young Frenchman's request?

choices.text: Commissioned him as a major general in the Continental Army
Offered him only a minor advisory role with no rank
Rejected his request and sent him back to France
Commissioned him as a colonel, well below what he sought

evt-07-31-1777-second-continental-congre.butterflyEffect: Congress commissioned the Marquis de Lafayette as a major general in the Continental Army. He became one of George Washington's most trusted officers, helped secure crucial French military support for the Revolution, and played a key role in the decisive Siege of Yorktown four years later.

evt-07-31-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It is 31 July 1917 near Ypres, and you advance with British and Commonwealth infantry into the Flanders salient as General Haig's long-planned offensive finally opens.
evt-07-31-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What happened to the offensive once the heavy Flanders rains began?

choices.text: Cavalry charged through open ground to capture Ostend that week
Rain and shellfire turned the ground to mud, bogging down men and tanks for months
The offensive broke through quickly, reaching the Belgian coast within days
Both sides declared an immediate armistice due to weather

evt-07-31-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Torrential rain turned the reclaimed farmland into a drowning quagmire, swallowing men, horses, and tanks and slowing the advance to a crawl. The battle ground on for over three months, capturing only the shattered village of Passchendaele at enormous cost, and it became a lasting symbol of the war's mud-choked attrition.

evt-07-31-1941-the-holocaust.scenario: It is July 31, 1941, in Berlin. You are Reinhard Heydrich, receiving written authorization from Hermann Göring to prepare a comprehensive plan for what the Nazi regime calls the 'final solution to the Jewish question'.
evt-07-31-1941-the-holocaust.prompt: What does this directive set in motion?

choices.text: Heydrich resigns rather than carry out the order
Heydrich organizes the Wannsee Conference to coordinate the genocide's implementation
The directive is quietly shelved and never acted upon
Heydrich transfers the task entirely to local police forces

evt-07-31-1941-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: Heydrich used this authorization to convene the Wannsee Conference in January 1942, coordinating the machinery of genocide across Nazi-occupied Europe. The directive marked a shift from mass shootings toward systematic, industrialized murder in extermination camps, accelerating the killing of six million Jews.

evt-07-31-1954-1954-italian-expedition-t.scenario: You are high on K2 in July 1954, exhausted after weeks of siege tactics on the world's most dangerous mountain, deciding who among the team will make the final push while others carry vital oxygen bottles up to the last camp.
evt-07-31-1954-1954-italian-expedition-t.prompt: Who actually reached K2's summit on this day, becoming the first to do so?

choices.text: Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli
Walter Bonatti and Amir Mahdi, the support climbers
Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay
Reinhold Messner and Peter Habeler

evt-07-31-1954-1954-italian-expedition-t.butterflyEffect: Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli reached the summit, but their triumph was clouded by controversy: support climber Walter Bonatti, who had carried oxygen to their high camp overnight at great personal risk, felt betrayed by the summit pair's account. Decades later new evidence forced a partial rewriting of the official story, and Bonatti was posthumously vindicated.

evt-07-31-1987-edmonton-tornado.scenario: You live in eastern Edmonton on the afternoon of Friday, 31 July 1987, and the sky has turned an ominous greenish-black as tornado sirens begin to sound across your neighborhood.
evt-07-31-1987-edmonton-tornado.prompt: What is the safest action to take as the warning sounds?

choices.text: Assume it is a false alarm and continue as normal
Take shelter immediately in a basement or interior room away from windows
Watch from a window to track the tornado's path
Drive away quickly to outrun the storm

evt-07-31-1987-edmonton-tornado.butterflyEffect: The tornado that followed, an F4, tore through industrial and residential areas and killed 27 people, making it one of the deadliest in Canadian history. The disaster, remembered locally as "Black Friday," led to significant improvements in Alberta's severe weather warning systems and emergency preparedness.

evt-07-31-1991-soviet-union.scenario: You stand in the Kremlin on 31 July 1991 as George H.W. Bush and Mikhail Gorbachev prepare to sign a landmark arms treaty after nearly a decade of negotiation.
evt-07-31-1991-soviet-union.prompt: What did the START I treaty actually require of both superpowers?

choices.text: Freeze existing arsenals at current levels without any reductions
Restrict only anti-ballistic missile defense systems
Eliminate all nuclear weapons from both arsenals entirely
Reduce strategic nuclear warheads to about 6,000 each with verification measures

evt-07-31-1991-soviet-union.butterflyEffect: START I mandated cutting strategic arsenals to roughly 6,000 warheads and 1,600 delivery vehicles each, with intrusive verification. It took effect in 1994, but the Soviet collapse months after signing meant Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, and Kazakhstan all had to be brought into its framework, leading directly to further reductions like START II.

evt-07-31-1992-georgia-country.scenario: It is July 31, 1992. You are part of Georgia's delegation as the young republic, independent from the Soviet Union for less than a year, is formally admitted to the United Nations.
evt-07-31-1992-georgia-country.prompt: What conflict is already tearing at the new nation as it joins the UN?

choices.text: The Nagorno-Karabakh war spreads into Georgian territory
Civil war erupts in Chechnya
Georgia annexes South Ossetia outright
War breaks out in the breakaway region of Abkhazia

evt-07-31-1992-georgia-country.butterflyEffect: Within weeks of joining the UN, fighting escalated in Abkhazia, which sought separation from Georgia with covert Russian support. The 1992-93 war ended in Georgian defeat and the de facto loss of Abkhazia, a wound in sovereignty that remains unresolved and fed later conflicts with Russia, including the 2008 war.

evt-07-31-1992-thai-airways-internationa.scenario: You are on the flight deck of TG311 on the morning of 31 July 1992, descending toward Kathmandu's Tribhuvan airport through cloud and mountainous terrain on a demanding non-precision approach.
evt-07-31-1992-thai-airways-internationa.prompt: What error is believed to have led the aircraft into the mountainside?

choices.text: A sudden engine failure caused an uncontrolled descent
A bird strike disabled the aircraft's navigation instruments
Confusion over the approach clearance led to controlled flight into the mountain
The crew deliberately deviated from the assigned flight path

evt-07-31-1992-thai-airways-internationa.butterflyEffect: Investigators concluded that confusion between the crew and air traffic control over the approach routing led the Airbus A310 into terrain in cloud, with no mechanical fault found. It remains Nepal's deadliest aviation disaster and prompted a lasting review of approach procedures at one of the world's most challenging airports.

evt-07-31-1992-space-shuttle-program.scenario: Aboard Space Shuttle Atlantis on STS-46, you are testing a satellite meant to unspool 20 kilometers of tether behind the orbiter, but the reel mechanism suddenly jams after only a short deployment.
evt-07-31-1992-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What does the crew do once the tether deployment jams?

choices.text: Halt further deployment and retrieve the satellite back into the bay
Cut the tether and let the satellite drift into orbit alone
Force the reel motor to keep extending the tether regardless
Jettison the entire experiment package immediately

evt-07-31-1992-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: The Tethered Satellite System deployed only about 256 meters before jamming, forcing an early retrieval and ending the experiment far short of its goal. NASA reflew the concept as TSS-1R in 1996, where the tether was paid out to nearly 19 kilometers before it snapped, giving engineers dramatic new data on electrodynamic tethers.

evt-07-31-1997-fedex-express-flight-14.scenario: You are aboard the MD-11 cargo jet of FedEx Express Flight 14, nearing the end of a long haul from Singapore via Taiwan and Alaska, as the plane descends toward Newark International Airport on 31 July 1997.
evt-07-31-1997-fedex-express-flight-14.prompt: What happened to the aircraft in the final moments of its landing?

choices.text: It landed hard, flipped over, and caught fire
It suffered a bird strike and lost an engine on approach
It aborted the landing and diverted to another airport
It landed safely without incident

evt-07-31-1997-fedex-express-flight-14.butterflyEffect: The MD-11 crashed on landing, flipped upside down, and caught fire on the runway, yet all five people aboard survived. The accident added to a string of MD-11 landing incidents that raised concerns about the aircraft's landing gear and handling characteristics during hard touchdowns.

evt-07-31-1999-discovery-program.scenario: You are a mission controller in July 1999, watching as the exhausted Lunar Prospector spacecraft is deliberately steered into a permanently shadowed crater near the Moon's south pole to end its mission.
evt-07-31-1999-discovery-program.prompt: What did NASA hope the impact would reveal to telescopes on Earth?

choices.text: A measurable shift in the Moon's orbital path
Evidence of ongoing volcanic activity on the Moon
A detectable plume of water vapor from ice hidden in the crater
Signs of an artificial structure buried in the crater

evt-07-31-1999-discovery-program.butterflyEffect: The impact produced no plume detectable by Earth-based telescopes, leaving the question of lunar polar ice unresolved at the time. A decade later, the 2009 LCROSS mission repeated the idea with better instrumentation aboard the impactor itself, directly confirming water molecules in the ejected debris.

evt-07-31-2012-2012-india-blackouts.scenario: It is July 30, 2012, and you monitor India's northern power grid as several states draw far more electricity than their allotted share during a weak monsoon season.
evt-07-31-2012-2012-india-blackouts.prompt: What happens to the grid as demand keeps exceeding quotas?

choices.text: The overloaded grid collapses, triggering a massive blackout
Automatic safeguards isolate the states without wider disruption
Rolling blackouts are implemented smoothly with no cascading failure
Emergency imports from neighboring countries prevent failure

evt-07-31-2012-2012-india-blackouts.butterflyEffect: The overloaded grid collapsed, cutting power to over 600 million people across 22 states for hours and crippling trains, hospitals, and water systems. The disaster exposed chronic overdrawing by individual states and pushed India toward major grid-discipline reforms in the years that followed.

evt-07-31-2012-michael-phelps.scenario: It is July 31, 2012, in the London Aquatics Centre. You are Michael Phelps, anchoring the U.S. 4x200m freestyle relay, one medal away from surpassing Larisa Latynina's 48-year-old Olympic record.

choices.text: Phelps false-starts and is disqualified
The U.S. team finishes second, delaying the record
The relay team wins bronze
The U.S. team wins gold, giving Phelps his 19th Olympic medal and the record

evt-07-31-2012-michael-phelps.butterflyEffect: Phelps and his teammates won gold, pushing his career total past Latynina's mark and cementing his status as the most decorated Olympian ever. He went on to add more medals in London and Rio, finishing his career with 28 total, a record considered nearly unbreakable.

evt-07-31-2014-2014-kaohsiung-gas-explos.scenario: You are a first responder in Kaohsiung on the night of 31 July 2014, after residents in the Cianjhen and Lingya districts report a strange gas smell rising from the streets, hours before a series of explosions rips through the roads.
evt-07-31-2014-2014-kaohsiung-gas-explos.prompt: What was later confirmed as the cause of the explosions?

choices.text: An explosion at an oil refinery on the city's edge
An explosion in the city's subway gas mains
A fire at a nearby chemical manufacturing plant
Leaking underground propene pipelines that ignited

evt-07-31-2014-2014-kaohsiung-gas-explos.butterflyEffect: Leaking underground propene pipelines, not properly identified or shut off despite hours of warning signs, ignited and caused a chain of explosions that killed 32 people and injured hundreds. The disaster exposed gaps in Taiwan's underground pipeline oversight and led to new regulations holding petrochemical companies accountable for buried infrastructure.

evt-08-01-1774-joseph-priestley.scenario: It is 1 August 1774 in your Wiltshire laboratory. Using a burning glass to heat red mercuric oxide, you collect a gas in which a candle flame flares up brilliantly and a mouse thrives far longer than in ordinary air.
evt-08-01-1774-joseph-priestley.prompt: Working within phlogiston theory, what does Priestley name this remarkable gas?

choices.text: Inflammable air
Fixed air
Dephlogisticated air
Vital air

evt-08-01-1774-joseph-priestley.butterflyEffect: Priestley called it "dephlogisticated air," believing it was air stripped of phlogiston. Antoine Lavoisier later repeated and reinterpreted the experiment, renaming the gas "oxygen" and using it to demolish phlogiston theory entirely, laying a cornerstone of modern chemistry.

evt-08-01-1798-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: It is 1 August 1798 in Aboukir Bay, Egypt. You serve aboard a British ship under Nelson, who has just sighted the French fleet anchored in a defensive line close to shore, believing themselves safe until morning.
evt-08-01-1798-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What did Nelson order his fleet to do?

choices.text: Withdraw to blockade the bay from a distance
Bombard the French ships only from long range
Wait until dawn to attack in clear light
Attack the French line from both sides at once

evt-08-01-1798-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: Nelson attacked immediately, sending ships to both the seaward and landward sides of the French line, trapping and annihilating it. The Battle of the Nile destroyed Napoleon's fleet, stranding his army in Egypt and shifting Mediterranean naval dominance decisively to Britain.

evt-08-01-1834-slavery-abolition-act-183.scenario: It is 1 August 1834 on a sugar estate in Jamaica. The Slavery Abolition Act has just taken legal effect across the British Empire, and enslaved workers gather to hear what freedom actually means for them today.
evt-08-01-1834-slavery-abolition-act-183.prompt: What did the Act actually require of most enslaved workers on this day?

choices.text: Slavery ended only in the Caribbean, continuing elsewhere in the Empire
They were freed outright with no further obligation
They entered a compulsory apprenticeship, still labouring for their former masters
They received immediate cash compensation from Parliament

evt-08-01-1834-slavery-abolition-act-183.butterflyEffect: Rather than immediate freedom, most were bound into a compulsory 'apprenticeship' system, still working unpaid for their former owners until 1838. Meanwhile Parliament paid roughly £20 million in compensation to slave-owners, not to the enslaved, a grievance that fuelled later abolitionist and reparations campaigns.

evt-08-01-1842-lombard-street-riot.scenario: It is 1 August 1842 on Lombard Street in Philadelphia. Black temperance societies are marching to mark the anniversary of emancipation in the British West Indies when a white mob surges toward the parade.
evt-08-01-1842-lombard-street-riot.prompt: What does the mob destroy over the three days of rioting that follow?

choices.text: Black homes, a church, and a meeting hall
Only market stalls along the parade route
The offices of an abolitionist newspaper alone
Philadelphia's City Hall

evt-08-01-1842-lombard-street-riot.butterflyEffect: Rioters burned a Black church and a benevolent hall and ransacked homes in the neighborhood before militia finally restored order. The attack was part of a wave of anti-abolitionist mob violence in Northern cities, exposing how precarious free Black communities remained even outside the slave South.

evt-08-01-1876-colorado.scenario: It is early 1876 in Washington, and Colorado's territorial delegates are pressing Congress to admit their territory as a state in time for the nation's centennial year.
evt-08-01-1876-colorado.prompt: What did Congress and President Grant do with Colorado's statehood bid?

choices.text: They postponed admission until the 1880 census
They admitted Colorado as the 38th state on 1 August 1876
They required Colorado to merge with a neighboring territory first
They rejected the bid over mining land disputes

evt-08-01-1876-colorado.butterflyEffect: Colorado was admitted on 1 August 1876 as the 38th state, earning the nickname 'the Centennial State' for its timing alongside America's hundredth anniversary. Its new statehood soon gave it a voice in national politics, including the silver-mining interests that would fuel the later Free Silver movement.

evt-08-01-1911-harriet-quimby.scenario: It's August 1, 1911, and you're Harriet Quimby, a journalist turned aviator, sitting for the flight examination that could make you America's first licensed woman pilot.
evt-08-01-1911-harriet-quimby.prompt: What does Quimby go on to achieve the following year, building on this license?

choices.text: She founds the first all-female flying club in the US
She sets the first transcontinental flight record
She becomes the first woman to pilot a commercial airliner
She becomes the first woman to fly solo across the English Channel

evt-08-01-1911-harriet-quimby.butterflyEffect: In April 1912, Quimby flew solo across the English Channel, a feat overshadowed in the press by the Titanic sinking days earlier. She died later that year in a flying accident, but her achievements helped open aviation to women pilots who followed.

evt-08-01-1946-partisan-congress-riots.scenario: It is early August 1946 in Bratislava. A Partisan Congress has drawn crowds into the streets, and tension is rising against Jewish Holocaust survivors who have returned to reclaim homes and shops taken from them during the war.
evt-08-01-1946-partisan-congress-riots.prompt: What underlying grievance fuels the anti-Jewish violence that erupts in the city?

choices.text: Resentment over Jews reclaiming property seized during the Holocaust
A dispute over factory wages
A clash over competing religious festivals
Anger over a disputed local election

evt-08-01-1946-partisan-congress-riots.butterflyEffect: Resentment over Jewish survivors reclaiming confiscated property, layered on wartime fascist propaganda, boiled over into days of attacks across Slovak towns. Coming the same year as Poland's Kielce pogrom, such violence convinced many surviving Jews that Europe held no future for them and hastened emigration to Palestine.

evt-08-01-1971-the-concert-for-banglades.scenario: It's August 1, 1971, and Madison Square Garden has just hosted two sold-out benefit shows for refugees fleeing the Bangladesh Liberation War. George Harrison and Ravi Shankar want the impact to outlast the applause.
evt-08-01-1971-the-concert-for-banglades.prompt: What do the organizers do next to keep funding refugee relief?

choices.text: Release a live album and documentary film from the concerts
Ask ticket holders to donate their tickets back for resale
Auction Harrison's guitars to raise extra funds
Stage a single repeat concert the following month

evt-08-01-1971-the-concert-for-banglades.butterflyEffect: The Concert for Bangladesh live album and Apple Films' 1972 documentary became bestsellers, funneling millions more toward UNICEF relief and setting the template for later benefit spectacles such as Live Aid and Live 8.

evt-08-01-1984-peat.scenario: It is 1 August 1984 at Lindow Moss in Cheshire. You are cutting peat commercially when the machinery snags on something unexpected, and a human foot emerges from the dark, waterlogged ground.
evt-08-01-1984-peat.prompt: What do you do after uncovering the remains?

choices.text: Sell the remains privately to a collector
Report the find to the police as a suspected body
Rebury it quietly without telling anyone
Discard it, assuming it is a tree root

evt-08-01-1984-peat.butterflyEffect: The find was reported to police, who initially suspected a recent murder before archaeologists identified it as an Iron Age bog body, later named Lindow Man. Remarkably preserved by the peat's chemistry, he became one of the most studied ancient bodies in Britain, revealing details of Iron Age diet, injury, and possible ritual death.

evt-08-01-1991-george-h-w-bush.scenario: It's August 1, 1991, and you're advising President George H. W. Bush before he addresses the Ukrainian parliament, weeks before the Soviet Union's collapse. Nationalist movements are gaining momentum across the republics.
evt-08-01-1991-george-h-w-bush.prompt: What central message does Bush's speech urge on Ukraine's independence movement?

choices.text: A demand that Ukraine surrender its nuclear weapons at once
Full-throated endorsement of immediate Ukrainian independence
Caution against pursuing independence and support for Gorbachev's reforms
A call for Ukraine to join NATO immediately

evt-08-01-1991-george-h-w-bush.butterflyEffect: Dubbed the 'Chicken Kiev speech,' Bush's caution against 'suicidal nationalism' badly misjudged the moment. Ukraine declared independence weeks later and confirmed it by referendum that December, helping seal the Soviet Union's dissolution.

evt-08-01-2007-i-35w-mississippi-river-b.scenario: It is evening rush hour on 1 August 2007. You are stopped in traffic on the I-35W bridge over the Mississippi in Minneapolis when the deck beneath you suddenly gives way.
evt-08-01-2007-i-35w-mississippi-river-b.prompt: What structural flaw did investigators later determine caused the collapse?

choices.text: Corrosion of the suspension cables gave way
An earthquake shook the bridge's foundations
A single overloaded truck alone snapped the span
Undersized gusset plates failed under the load

evt-08-01-2007-i-35w-mississippi-river-b.butterflyEffect: The NTSB found that undersized gusset plates, too thin for the loads they bore, tore along a line of rivets, worsened by construction-related weight on the deck that day. The disaster triggered nationwide inspections of steel truss bridges and a reassessment of aging U.S. infrastructure funding.

evt-08-01-2008-beijing-tianjin-intercity.scenario: It's August 1, 2008, just days before the Beijing Olympics open, and China unveils a new intercity railway built to link the capital with the port city of Tianjin at unprecedented speed.
evt-08-01-2008-beijing-tianjin-intercity.prompt: What distinction did this new line hold when it opened?

choices.text: It became the fastest commuter rail service in the world at the time
It was China's first railway built entirely by foreign contractors
It became the longest railway tunnel network in Asia
It became the first railway to connect China directly to Russia

evt-08-01-2008-beijing-tianjin-intercity.butterflyEffect: The line showcased China's high-speed rail ambitions just before the Olympics and became a proving ground for technology later expanded across the country's massive high-speed network, which grew to be the largest in the world within a decade.

evt-08-01-2008-2008-k2-disaster.scenario: It is the afternoon of 1 August 2008, high on K2's Bottleneck. An ice avalanche has just swept away the fixed ropes above you, and climbers from several expeditions are stalled on the narrow traverse with darkness approaching.
evt-08-01-2008-2008-k2-disaster.prompt: What did many climbers do next, deepening the unfolding disaster?

choices.text: They continued climbing toward the summit despite the lost ropes
They abandoned their oxygen to move faster downhill
They waited together at the Bottleneck for rescue helicopters
They all turned back immediately to Camp IV

evt-08-01-2008-2008-k2-disaster.butterflyEffect: Many pushed on toward the summit despite the lost ropes and mounting delays, leaving them descending in darkness and exhaustion when a second ice collapse struck the Bottleneck. Eleven climbers died in the ensuing hours, making it the deadliest single episode in K2's history and prompting lasting scrutiny of overcrowding and turnaround discipline on 8,000-metre peaks.

evt-08-01-2009-tel-aviv-gay-centre-shoot.scenario: It's the night of August 1, 2009, and a masked gunman has opened fire inside the Tel Aviv branch of Israel's LGBT association, the Aguda, wounding many and killing two young people. Community leaders must decide how to respond in the days that follow.
evt-08-01-2009-tel-aviv-gay-centre-shoot.prompt: How did Tel Aviv's LGBT community and its allies respond in the aftermath?

choices.text: They called for the Aguda organization to be disbanded
They asked the government to ban all future LGBT gatherings
They quietly closed all LGBT venues in the city indefinitely
They organized a mass public rally demanding action against anti-LGBT violence

evt-08-01-2009-tel-aviv-gay-centre-shoot.butterflyEffect: Tens of thousands marched through Tel Aviv demanding the government confront homophobic violence, and the attack pushed LGBT rights further into mainstream Israeli political debate. The shooter was never definitively identified or caught.

evt-08-01-2023-donald-trump.scenario: It is 1 August 2023 in Washington, D.C. A federal grand jury has just returned an indictment against former President Donald Trump over efforts to overturn the 2020 election results.
evt-08-01-2023-donald-trump.prompt: What ultimately becomes of this federal case in the years that follow?

choices.text: Trump is convicted at trial in early 2024
Trump pleads guilty to a reduced misdemeanor
It is dismissed after Trump wins the 2024 election
The charges are dropped for lack of evidence

evt-08-01-2023-donald-trump.butterflyEffect: The case dragged through appeals over presidential immunity and never reached trial. After Trump won the 2024 election, the Justice Department moved to dismiss the charges, citing longstanding policy against prosecuting a sitting president, leaving the legal questions it raised unresolved.

evt-08-02-bce338-philip-ii-of-macedon.scenario: August 338 BC: you stand in the front rank of the Theban Sacred Band at Chaeronea, watching Philip's Macedonian phalanx wheel unexpectedly against the allied Greek line.
evt-08-02-bce338-philip-ii-of-macedon.prompt: What does Philip's army achieve in this battle?

choices.text: A narrow win for the Athenian-Theban alliance
An inconclusive stalemate ending in truce
A Persian intervention that decides the battle
A decisive Macedonian victory over the Greek coalition

evt-08-02-bce338-philip-ii-of-macedon.butterflyEffect: Philip crushed the combined Athenian and Theban forces, effectively ending independent Greek city-state resistance. He then formed the League of Corinth to unite Greece under Macedonian leadership, the platform his son Alexander would use to conquer Persia.

evt-08-02-bce216-battle-of-cannae.scenario: It is 2 August 216 BC near Cannae. As consul, you command a Roman army far larger than Hannibal's, and you must decide how to array your legions before the battle line closes.
evt-08-02-bce216-battle-of-cannae.prompt: What formation do you order your heavy infantry into?

choices.text: A thin, extended line designed to outflank Hannibal
A cavalry-led charge before the infantry engages
A defensive stand inside the fortified camp
A deeper-than-usual massed infantry formation

evt-08-02-bce216-battle-of-cannae.butterflyEffect: Varro massed the legions unusually deep, hoping sheer weight would smash through the Carthaginian center. Hannibal let his center bow inward while his cavalry swept around both flanks, trapping the packed Romans in a double envelopment that annihilated the army—one of the costliest single days of fighting in ancient history and a blow that pushed several Italian cities to defect to Carthage.

evt-08-02-1100-new-forest.scenario: It's an August afternoon in 1100, and you ride beside King William II through the New Forest's oak groves as the royal hunting party fans out after a fleeing stag.
evt-08-02-1100-new-forest.prompt: What happens to the king during this hunt?

choices.text: He dies suddenly of a fever that night
He is struck and killed by an arrow
He is ambushed by rebellious nobles
He falls fatally from his horse

evt-08-02-1100-new-forest.butterflyEffect: William Rufus was struck and killed by an arrow, reportedly loosed by Walter Tirel, and left where he fell. His sudden death let his younger brother Henry race to seize the throne within days as Henry I, reshaping the Anglo-Norman succession.

evt-08-02-1790-1790-united-states-census.scenario: You are a US marshal in August 1790, walking a rural county with a ledger, trying to count every household before the young nation's first census closes.
evt-08-02-1790-1790-united-states-census.prompt: Which categories must you record for each free household you visit?

choices.text: Income, property value, and debts owed
Age, literacy, and land holdings
Free white males and females, other free persons, and slaves
Occupation, religion, and marital status

evt-08-02-1790-1790-united-states-census.butterflyEffect: The completed count tallied 3,929,214 people and became the basis for congressional apportionment and federal taxation. It also established the decennial census as a lasting constitutional institution shaping American political representation ever since.

evt-08-02-1870-tower-subway.scenario: You are an engineer in London in 1869, using James Greathead's new iron tunneling shield to bore a passage beneath the Thames. When it opens in August 1870, you must decide how passengers will cross.
evt-08-02-1870-tower-subway.prompt: How do the first passengers travel through the newly opened Tower Subway?

choices.text: An early electric elevator lowers them to a walkway
A horse-drawn omnibus is led through on foot
A cable-hauled tram car pulls them through the tunnel
A steam locomotive hauls carriages beneath the river

evt-08-02-1870-tower-subway.butterflyEffect: The tunnel opened with a small cable-hauled tram car, but the service proved unprofitable and closed within months, after which the tunnel became a pedestrian toll subway. Its real legacy was technical: Greathead's shield method became the standard technique for boring London's later deep tube lines.

evt-08-02-1914-grand-quartier-general-19.scenario: It is August 2, 1914. German patrols have just crossed into French territory, and the French parliament authorizes the activation of a new military command to direct the nation's response.
evt-08-02-1914-grand-quartier-general-19.prompt: What was this new headquarters, the Grand Quartier Général, established to do?

choices.text: Manage the naval blockade of Germany
Negotiate a peace settlement with Germany
Coordinate and command the French army's war effort
Oversee only France's colonial troops

evt-08-02-1914-grand-quartier-general-19.butterflyEffect: The GQG became the nerve center directing French forces throughout the First World War, under commanders including Joseph Joffre. It shaped French strategy through the Marne, Verdun, and the war's end, remaining active until 1919.

evt-08-02-1920-krishna-lal-adhikari.scenario: It is 1920 in Kathmandu, and you have just published Makaiko Kheti, a plain guide to growing maize. Officials of the ruling Rana regime summon you to answer for the book's supposedly dangerous ideas.
evt-08-02-1920-krishna-lal-adhikari.prompt: What charge do the authorities use to justify imprisoning you?

choices.text: Defamation of a local court official
Blasphemy against the state religion
Tax fraud in the sale of his book
Treason against the state

evt-08-02-1920-krishna-lal-adhikari.butterflyEffect: Adhikari was sentenced to nine years and died in jail in 1923. His death for writing a farming manual made him Nepal's first recognised 'literary martyr,' and Tinlal Park in Manthali now honours his name.

evt-08-02-1923-calvin-coolidge.scenario: It is the middle of the night on August 3, 1923, at a Vermont farmhouse. Word has just arrived that President Harding has died, and Vice President Calvin Coolidge must be sworn in at once.
evt-08-02-1923-calvin-coolidge.prompt: Who administered Coolidge's first oath of office?

choices.text: His father, a local notary public
A federal judge in Washington
The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
The Secretary of State

evt-08-02-1923-calvin-coolidge.butterflyEffect: His own father, a notary public, swore him in by kerosene lamp light in the family parlor. Legal doubts about a state notary administering a federal oath led Coolidge to be re-sworn later in Washington, and he went on to preside over the pro-business, small-government 1920s known as 'Coolidge Prosperity.'

evt-08-02-1939-leo-szilard.scenario: It is August 1939. You are physicist Leo Szilard, drafting a letter for Albert Einstein's signature, warning that Nazi Germany could be racing to build an atomic weapon from uranium.
evt-08-02-1939-leo-szilard.prompt: What should the letter urge President Roosevelt to do?

choices.text: Publicly release all American nuclear research findings
Declare war on Germany immediately
Fund research into uranium and stockpile ore before Germany can
Ignore the threat as scientifically implausible

evt-08-02-1939-leo-szilard.butterflyEffect: Roosevelt read the letter and set up the Advisory Committee on Uranium, the first step toward the Manhattan Project. Szilard's warning ultimately helped launch the American effort that produced the atomic bomb by 1945, a weapon he later petitioned Truman not to use on civilians.

evt-08-02-1947-1947-bsaa-avro-lancastria.scenario: It is August 2, 1947. The BSAA airliner Star Dust is descending toward Santiago over the Andes when its radio operator taps out a strange final morse message ending in the puzzling word 'STENDEC.'
evt-08-02-1947-1947-bsaa-avro-lancastria.prompt: What actually happened to Star Dust moments later?

choices.text: It landed safely at an emergency airstrip
It crashed into a glacier on Mount Tupungato
It was hijacked and diverted
It returned safely to Buenos Aires

evt-08-02-1947-1947-bsaa-avro-lancastria.butterflyEffect: The aircraft struck the glacier on Mount Tupungato and vanished without a trace for over fifty years. Wreckage and remains only surfaced in the late 1990s as the glacier melted, finally solving the disappearance, though the meaning of 'STENDEC' remains debated to this day.

evt-08-02-1971-the-who.scenario: You are working with Pete Townshend in 1971 after his ambitious multimedia Lifehouse project has collapsed under its own complexity, leaving a pile of unused songs and studio recordings.
evt-08-02-1971-the-who.prompt: What does the band do with the abandoned Lifehouse material?

choices.text: Disband the group over the creative disagreement
Push ahead with Lifehouse exactly as originally planned
Rework the strongest songs into a standalone studio album
Scrap the songs entirely and write a fresh album from scratch

evt-08-02-1971-the-who.butterflyEffect: The Who reshaped the strongest Lifehouse songs into a conventional studio album, Who's Next, released 2 August 1971. It became the band's only UK number-one album, introduced synthesizers to rock via tracks like "Baba O'Riley," and is now regarded as one of the greatest rock albums ever made.

evt-08-02-1973-summerland-disaster.scenario: It's the night of 2 August 1973, and you are a firefighter arriving at the Summerland leisure complex in Douglas, Isle of Man, watching flames race up the building's shining plastic-clad walls far faster than any normal fire.
evt-08-02-1973-summerland-disaster.prompt: What building material do investigators later blame for the fire's terrifying speed?

choices.text: Acrylic and plastic-coated wall panels
Faulty gas heaters in the changing rooms
Untreated timber flooring throughout the complex
Overcrowded emergency exits alone

evt-08-02-1973-summerland-disaster.butterflyEffect: The inquiry found that acrylic sheeting and combustible cavity-wall construction let flames spread with unusual speed, killing 50 people. The disaster pushed UK and Isle of Man authorities toward far stricter fire-safety rules on cladding materials in public buildings.

evt-08-02-1980-bologna-massacre.scenario: It is the morning of August 2, 1980. A bomb has just torn through the crowded waiting room of Bologna's central train station, and officials must quickly explain to a shocked public what happened.
evt-08-02-1980-bologna-massacre.prompt: What did authorities initially claim caused the explosion?

choices.text: An accidental boiler explosion in the station
A bombing by the Red Brigades
Structural collapse of the station roof
A foreign state-sponsored terrorist attack

evt-08-02-1980-bologna-massacre.butterflyEffect: The story of an accidental boiler explosion collapsed within hours as evidence pointed to a deliberate bomb. Investigations eventually convicted members of the neo-fascist group Nuclei Armati Rivoluzionari, and decades later prosecutors implicated Propaganda Due lodge figures like Licio Gelli in orchestrating the attack.

evt-08-02-1985-delta-air-lines-flight-19.scenario: You are the captain of Delta Flight 191, on final approach to Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport on 2 August 1985. Ahead, a dark thunderstorm cell sits directly over the runway threshold.
evt-08-02-1985-delta-air-lines-flight-19.prompt: What is the correct response to the storm cell ahead of you?

choices.text: Increase flap setting to power through the wind shift
Slow the aircraft further to counter expected turbulence
Continue the approach, since microbursts rarely form over runways
Abort the approach and go around, avoiding the cell entirely

evt-08-02-1985-delta-air-lines-flight-19.butterflyEffect: The crew continued the approach and flew into a microburst just before touchdown; the TriStar crashed a mile short of the runway, killing 137 people. The disaster, alongside similar wind-shear accidents, pushed the FAA to mandate airborne wind-shear detection systems and rewrite pilot training on microburst avoidance across the US airline industry.

evt-08-02-1989-1989-valvettiturai-massac.scenario: It is 2 August 1989 in Valvettiturai, on Sri Lanka's Jaffna Peninsula. Tamil Tiger fighters have just ambushed Indian Peace Keeping Force soldiers, killing six including an officer, and IPKF units are now moving through the town.
evt-08-02-1989-1989-valvettiturai-massac.prompt: What did the Indian soldiers do in the two days that followed?

choices.text: Killed dozens of civilians in the town in apparent reprisal
Arrested LTTE suspects and withdrew without further incident
Called in Indian Air Force strikes on rebel positions nearby
Negotiated an immediate truce with local Tamil leaders

evt-08-02-1989-1989-valvettiturai-massac.butterflyEffect: Over 2-3 August, IPKF soldiers killed 64 Tamil civilians in the town, which Indian authorities described as crossfire deaths but journalists and human rights groups documented as a massacre. Indian defence minister George Fernandes later called it India's My Lai, and the episode deepened Tamil distrust of the IPKF, hastening India's eventual withdrawal from Sri Lanka in 1990.

evt-08-02-1990-invasion-of-kuwait.scenario: It is dawn on 2 August 1990. You watch from a rooftop in Kuwait City as Iraqi armor rolls across the border, moving swiftly on the emir's palace and key government buildings.
evt-08-02-1990-invasion-of-kuwait.prompt: How does the international community respond in the weeks after the invasion?

choices.text: NATO immediately launches a ground invasion of Iraq itself
The Arab League unanimously endorses Iraq's annexation
The UN takes no action, leaving Kuwait to negotiate alone
The UN condemns the invasion and later authorizes a coalition to expel Iraq by force

evt-08-02-1990-invasion-of-kuwait.butterflyEffect: The UN Security Council condemned the invasion and, after Iraq annexed Kuwait outright, authorized an American-led coalition to use force if Iraq did not withdraw. When the deadline passed, the coalition launched the Gulf War in January 1991, liberating Kuwait by late February after Iraqi forces set its oil wells ablaze in retreat.

evt-08-02-1991-space-shuttle-atlantis.scenario: It is August 2, 1991. You are part of the STS-43 crew aboard Space Shuttle Atlantis, preparing to release a large communications satellite into orbit high above Earth.
evt-08-02-1991-space-shuttle-atlantis.prompt: What was the TDRS-5 satellite deployed to accomplish?

choices.text: Photograph deep space like the Hubble telescope
Extend NASA's network for tracking and communicating with spacecraft
Dock permanently with the Mir space station
Serve as a new GPS navigation satellite

evt-08-02-1991-space-shuttle-atlantis.butterflyEffect: TDRS-5 joined NASA's Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System, a network of satellites that let mission control stay in constant contact with orbiting spacecraft instead of relying on scattered ground stations. The system became essential infrastructure for later shuttle missions and the International Space Station.

evt-08-02-2005-air-france-flight-358.scenario: You are a flight attendant aboard Air France Flight 358, which has just overrun the runway at Toronto Pearson and come to rest broken apart in Etobicoke Creek. Smoke and flames are already visible outside.
evt-08-02-2005-air-france-flight-358.prompt: What is your first move as cabin crew?

choices.text: Wait for the captain's formal evacuation order before acting
Open exits and begin evacuating passengers immediately
Tell passengers to gather carry-on luggage before leaving
Radio ground control and wait for further instructions

evt-08-02-2005-air-france-flight-358.butterflyEffect: Flight attendants opened exits and ordered evacuation on their own initiative without waiting for a formal command from the flight deck, getting all 309 people off before fire consumed the fuselage. The accident became a textbook case in aviation safety training, showing that decisive crew action, not just aircraft design, is what turns a survivable crash into a survivable evacuation.

evt-08-03-1347-hundred-years-war.scenario: It is August 1347. Calais has starved for eleven months under English siege, and Edward III says he will spare the town only if a handful of its leading citizens surrender themselves to him, barefoot and in nooses, to face his justice.
evt-08-03-1347-hundred-years-war.prompt: What do the town's burghers do to save Calais from destruction?

choices.text: March out and attack the English lines in a final desperate sortie
Offer six leading citizens as hostages to Edward III to spare the rest
Appeal directly to the King of France to break the siege
Surrender unconditionally and trust to English mercy alone

evt-08-03-1347-hundred-years-war.butterflyEffect: Six burghers, led by Eustache de Saint-Pierre, offered themselves for execution; Edward III's pregnant queen, Philippa of Hainault, begged for their lives and he relented. Calais became an English possession for over two centuries and a vital Channel foothold, and the episode later inspired Rodin's sculpture The Burghers of Calais.

evt-08-03-1460-james-ii-of-scotland.scenario: It is August 1460 at the siege of Roxburgh Castle. You are a gunner tending one of the great bombards, and King James II, thrilled by the artillery, strides forward to watch it fire up close.
evt-08-03-1460-james-ii-of-scotland.prompt: What should you tell the king before the next shot is loaded?

choices.text: Invite him to help light the fuse himself
Urge him to step well back before the cannon fires
Assure him bombards never misfire
Ask him to inspect the powder stores instead

evt-08-03-1460-james-ii-of-scotland.butterflyEffect: James ignored such warnings and stood too near the gun; it burst on firing and killed him instantly. His six-year-old son became James III, plunging Scotland into another royal minority, though the Scots pressed on and took Roxburgh Castle from the English soon after.

evt-08-03-1903-internal-macedonian-revol.scenario: It is early August 1903 in Kruševo. IMRO rebels have just declared a republic and formed a revolutionary government during the Ilinden Uprising, while Ottoman troops mass in the hills above the town.
evt-08-03-1903-internal-macedonian-revol.prompt: What happened to the Kruševo Republic in the days after its declaration?

choices.text: Ottoman troops stormed the town and burned it down
European powers formally recognized its independence
It peacefully rejoined Ottoman administration
Its rebels expanded control across all of Macedonia

evt-08-03-1903-internal-macedonian-revol.butterflyEffect: Ottoman forces retook Kruševo within ten days, burning much of the town and killing many rebels and civilians in the process. The uprising's brutal suppression drew the attention of the European Great Powers to conditions in Macedonia, and the short-lived republic later became a founding symbol of Macedonian national identity.

evt-08-03-1913-wheatland-california.scenario: It is August 1913 and you are among thousands of hop-pickers crammed into filthy camps at the Durst Ranch in Wheatland, California. An IWW organizer is mid-speech at a protest rally when armed deputies push into the crowd to arrest him.
evt-08-03-1913-wheatland-california.prompt: What happens when the deputies move to seize the speaker from the crowd?

choices.text: State militia arrives beforehand and prevents any confrontation
Workers elect a delegate who negotiates the speaker's release
The crowd disperses quietly and the arrest proceeds without incident
A shot is fired and the confrontation erupts into a deadly riot

evt-08-03-1913-wheatland-california.butterflyEffect: A deputy fired a shot into the air to disperse the crowd, panic and gunfire followed, and four people including the district attorney and a deputy were killed. The Wheatland Hop Riot exposed brutal migrant labor conditions and pushed California to create its first Commission of Immigration and Housing.

evt-08-03-1929-jiddu-krishnamurti.scenario: You are a devoted member of the Order of the Star in the East, gathered at the Ommen camp in the Netherlands in August 1929 to hear Jiddu Krishnamurti, the young man Theosophists have raised as the coming World Teacher.
evt-08-03-1929-jiddu-krishnamurti.prompt: What does Krishnamurti announce to the stunned crowd?

choices.text: He names a successor to lead the Order after him
He formally accepts the title of World Teacher
He disbands the Order and renounces the prophesied role
He merges the Order fully into the Theosophical Society

evt-08-03-1929-jiddu-krishnamurti.butterflyEffect: Krishnamurti dissolved the Order of the Star, rejected the role of World Teacher, and broke from organized Theosophy. He spent the rest of his life as an independent speaker urging people toward self-discovery rather than doctrine, influencing modern spirituality and education far beyond the movement that had raised him.

evt-08-03-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is August 1940 and you command the small British garrison in Somaliland, facing an Italian invasion force many times your size pouring in from Ethiopia. Reinforcement is not coming, and holding the border is no longer possible.
evt-08-03-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: What should the British commander do to save his outnumbered force?

choices.text: Retreat inland to link up with Ethiopian rebels
Stand and fight to the last man at the border
Surrender the colony immediately without a fight
Order a fighting withdrawal and evacuate the garrison by sea to Aden

evt-08-03-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: After a stubborn stand at Tug Argan, the garrison was evacuated by sea to Aden rather than being destroyed, and British Somaliland fell — Mussolini's only outright conquest of British territory in the war. It proved short-lived: British and Commonwealth forces retook it in early 1941 during the East African Campaign.

evt-08-03-1960-niger.scenario: It is 3 August 1960 in Niamey. France's tricolour is coming down over the new Republic of Niger, and as a delegate to the National Assembly you must help choose who will lead the country's first independent government.
evt-08-03-1960-niger.prompt: Who becomes independent Niger's first president?

choices.text: Léopold Sédar Senghor
Ahmed Sékou Touré
Djibo Bakary
Hamani Diori

evt-08-03-1960-niger.butterflyEffect: Hamani Diori became Niger's first president, steering the young republic into a close alliance with France under a single-party system. His rule lasted until a devastating Sahel drought and economic crisis helped trigger a military coup led by Seyni Kountché in 1974.

evt-08-03-1971-fighting-dinosaurs.scenario: It is 1971 in Mongolia's Gobi Desert, and your team has just uncovered an extraordinary fossil: a Velociraptor and a Protoceratops locked together exactly as they died, claws and jaws still interlocked after tens of millions of years.
evt-08-03-1971-fighting-dinosaurs.prompt: What does the leading hypothesis say actually killed and preserved these two animals together?

choices.text: Both animals drowned separately and washed together by a flood
Volcanic ash fell on them while they slept nearby each other
A sudden dune collapse or sandstorm buried them mid-fight
They died weeks apart and were fossilized together by coincidence

evt-08-03-1971-fighting-dinosaurs.butterflyEffect: Most researchers favor sudden burial by a collapsing sand dune or sandstorm during the fight, freezing the struggle in place before scavengers or decay could separate the bodies. The specimen became the most direct fossil evidence of predatory combat in dinosaurs and shaped popular imagination of raptors as fierce hunters, later amplified by films like Jurassic Park.

evt-08-03-1972-united-states-senate.scenario: It is August 1972 and you are a US Senator voting on the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty just signed by Nixon and Brezhnev, which would sharply limit how many missile defense sites each superpower may build.
evt-08-03-1972-united-states-senate.prompt: How do you vote on ratifying the ABM Treaty?

choices.text: Vote to ratify, accepting strict limits on missile defense sites
Postpone the vote until Soviet missile numbers are verified
Vote against, arguing it leaves America undefended
Demand an amendment allowing unlimited testing before voting

evt-08-03-1972-united-states-senate.butterflyEffect: The Senate ratified the treaty overwhelmingly, 88 to 2, capping US and Soviet missile defenses and making it a cornerstone of Cold War arms control for the next thirty years. The United States withdrew from the treaty in 2002 under George W. Bush to pursue a national missile defense shield.

evt-08-03-2004-statue-of-liberty.scenario: It is August 2004 and you oversee reopening Liberty Island, closed since the September 11 attacks nearly three years earlier. Visitors are eager to climb the statue again, but fire-safety officials warn that the narrow crown stairway is a death trap in an emergency.
evt-08-03-2004-statue-of-liberty.prompt: How much of the Statue of Liberty should you reopen to the public?

choices.text: Keep all of Liberty Island closed indefinitely
Reopen the pedestal only, keeping the crown closed for safety
Reopen the full statue including the crown immediately
Open only the surrounding island grounds, not any building

evt-08-03-2004-statue-of-liberty.butterflyEffect: Officials reopened the pedestal with new airport-style security screening but kept the crown closed, citing evacuation risks exposed by 9/11. The crown did not reopen to visitors until 2009, a five-year gap that became a symbol of post-9/11 security caution at national monuments.

evt-08-03-2005-maaouya-ould-sid-ahmed-ta.scenario: It is 3 August 2005 in Nouakchott. President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya is abroad attending King Fahd's funeral in Saudi Arabia, and army officers are moving on the presidential palace.
evt-08-03-2005-maaouya-ould-sid-ahmed-ta.prompt: Who seized power in Mauritania while Taya was out of the country?

choices.text: French paratroopers sent to restore the president
A military council led by Colonel Ely Ould Mohamed Vall
A civilian opposition coalition backed by France
Taya's own prime minister, ruling in his name

evt-08-03-2005-maaouya-ould-sid-ahmed-ta.butterflyEffect: Colonel Ely Ould Mohamed Vall led a bloodless coup and headed a Military Council for Justice and Democracy that promised a transition to civilian rule. Elections in 2007 brought Sidi Ould Cheikh Abdallahi to power, but he too was overthrown in a coup the following year, extending Mauritania's cycle of military intervention.

evt-08-03-2014-2014-ludian-earthquake.scenario: It is 3 August 2014, minutes after a magnitude 6.1 quake has flattened villages in mountainous Ludian County, Yunnan. As a rescue coordinator, you must find a way to reach survivors trapped in the rubble of collapsed rural homes.
evt-08-03-2014-2014-ludian-earthquake.prompt: What most hampers rescue teams trying to reach the earthquake's remote villages?

choices.text: Volcanic ash grounded all rescue helicopters
A tsunami warning kept rescue boats offshore
Ongoing fighting in the region blocked access
Landslides blocked the mountain roads into remote villages

evt-08-03-2014-2014-ludian-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Landslides triggered by the quake blocked mountain roads into Ludian, delaying rescue convoys and forcing many teams to hike or use motorcycles to reach cut-off villages. The disaster exposed how poorly built rural housing in seismic mountain zones magnified casualties, spurring renewed Chinese investment in rural building codes and mountain-road disaster resilience.

evt-08-03-2014-yazidi-genocide.scenario: It is 3 August 2014 near Sinjar, northern Iraq. ISIL fighters are pouring into Yazidi villages as Kurdish peshmerga forces withdraw, and your family must decide where to run.
evt-08-03-2014-yazidi-genocide.prompt: Where did tens of thousands of Yazidis flee to escape the ISIL assault?

choices.text: Marched directly to Baghdad for government protection
Surrendered to the retreating Iraqi army for evacuation
Stayed in their villages to negotiate safe passage with ISIL
Fled on foot to the barren heights of Mount Sinjar

evt-08-03-2014-yazidi-genocide.butterflyEffect: Tens of thousands of Yazidis fled to barren Mount Sinjar, where they were besieged without food or water. The crisis prompted US airstrikes and airdrops, and Kurdish YPG fighters cut a corridor into Syria to evacuate survivors, while Sinjar itself was not fully retaken from ISIL until late 2015.

evt-08-03-2019-2019-el-paso-walmart-shoo.scenario: You are a Walmart employee in El Paso on the morning of August 3, 2019, when gunfire erupts near the entrance. Shoppers are frozen in the aisles, and you have seconds to act.
evt-08-03-2019-2019-el-paso-walmart-shoo.prompt: What is the most effective way to protect the shoppers around you?

choices.text: Sound an alarm and direct shoppers toward the nearest exits
Approach the gunman calmly to try to talk him down
Herd everyone into the front checkout lanes to wait it out
Call corporate headquarters before doing anything else

evt-08-03-2019-2019-el-paso-walmart-shoo.butterflyEffect: Employees triggered alarms and shouted warnings, helping many flee before police arrived; the gunman, Patrick Crusius, was arrested and the attack was classified as domestic terrorism and a hate crime targeting Latinos. The massacre intensified national debate over gun laws and rising white-nationalist violence, and El Paso later built a memorial to the victims.

evt-08-03-2019-lyubov-sobol.scenario: It is 3 August 2019 in central Moscow. You join a crowd of thousands demanding fair elections after opposition candidates, including Lyubov Sobol, were barred from the Moscow City Duma ballot. Riot police begin moving through the crowd.
evt-08-03-2019-lyubov-sobol.prompt: What happened to Sobol and hundreds of fellow protesters that day?

choices.text: Allowed to march unimpeded to Red Square
Detained by riot police along with hundreds of others
Granted an on-the-spot meeting with Moscow's mayor
Told the barred candidates would be reinstated immediately

evt-08-03-2019-lyubov-sobol.butterflyEffect: Over a thousand people, including Sobol, were detained in one of the largest crackdowns of the summer's protest wave. Several detainees later faced criminal charges in the so-called "Moscow case," and the harsh response drew international criticism while sharpening Navalny's push for tactical "smart voting" against Kremlin-backed candidates.

evt-08-04-1265-second-barons-war.scenario: You fight among Simon de Montfort's men near Evesham on 4 August 1265, hemmed in by Prince Edward's royal army after a rapid forced march cuts off your retreat.
evt-08-04-1265-second-barons-war.prompt: What happened to Simon de Montfort as the battle was decided?

choices.text: He negotiated a truce with Prince Edward
He was captured and later ransomed
He was killed, ending baronial rule of England
He escaped to France and continued the rebellion

evt-08-04-1265-second-barons-war.butterflyEffect: De Montfort was killed and his body mutilated, ending baronial rule and restoring Henry III's authority. Yet the parliamentary innovation he pioneered—summoning representatives of the commons—survived his death and shaped the later development of the English Parliament.

evt-08-04-1356-hundred-years-war.scenario: It is early August 1356, and you ride with Edward, the Black Prince, as his Anglo-Gascon army sets out from Bergerac, burning towns and gathering plunder as it pushes deep into French territory.
evt-08-04-1356-hundred-years-war.prompt: What did this great mounted raid ultimately lead to six weeks later?

choices.text: The prolonged Siege of Calais
The Battle of Poitiers, where the Black Prince captured King John II of France
A negotiated truce that ended the war early
The Battle of Crécy, a decisive English victory a decade earlier

evt-08-04-1356-hundred-years-war.butterflyEffect: The chevauchée culminated in the Battle of Poitiers on 19 September 1356, where the Black Prince's outnumbered force captured King John II of France. His captivity plunged France into crisis, helping spark the Jacquerie peasant revolt and forcing the humiliating Treaty of Brétigny in 1360.

evt-08-04-1704-war-of-the-spanish-succes.scenario: It is 4 August 1704. You serve aboard an Anglo-Dutch fleet under Admiral George Rooke, anchored off a Spanish fortress on a narrow peninsula guarding the entrance to the Mediterranean.
evt-08-04-1704-war-of-the-spanish-succes.prompt: What did this fleet accomplish that day, reshaping British strategy for centuries?

choices.text: Destroyed the Spanish treasure fleet returning from the Americas
Was repelled and forced to retreat to Lisbon
Captured Gibraltar, seizing a strategic naval base for Britain
Successfully invaded and held Cadiz

evt-08-04-1704-war-of-the-spanish-succes.butterflyEffect: The Anglo-Dutch fleet captured Gibraltar on 4 August 1704, and Britain retained it under the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht. This gave Britain a permanent foothold controlling the strait between the Atlantic and Mediterranean, a strategic asset it still holds today.

evt-08-04-1862-brooklyn.scenario: It is 4 August 1862, and you work in a Brooklyn tobacco factory. Word spreads that Black laborers there are taking jobs that Irish immigrant workers want, and an angry crowd is gathering outside.
evt-08-04-1862-brooklyn.prompt: What underlying grievance fueled this outbreak of mob violence?

choices.text: Outrage over a local newspaper's abolitionist editorial
A rumor that Confederate agents were recruiting nearby
Fear among Irish immigrant workers that Black laborers would undercut wages and take scarce jobs
A dispute over a contested mayoral election
