choices.text: Divert to the secondary target, Nagasaki
Circle until the clouds over Kokura clear
Abort the mission and return the bomb to base
Drop the bomb blindly through the cloud over Kokura

evt-08-09-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The Bockscar crew diverted to the secondary target, Nagasaki, where they dropped the Fat Man bomb. Japan surrendered days later, ending the Second World War, and the bombing became a central reference point in postwar debates over nuclear weapons.

evt-08-09-1960-albert-kalonji.scenario: It is August 1960 in Bakwanga. You listen as Albert Kalonji declares South Kasai's secession from the newly independent Congo, citing threats from Prime Minister Lumumba's central government.
evt-08-09-1960-albert-kalonji.prompt: What followed Kalonji's declaration of South Kasai's secession?

choices.text: The United Nations immediately recognized South Kasai as independent
Congolese central government forces moved to suppress the secession, sparking ethnic violence
Kalonji peacefully negotiated reintegration within weeks
Belgium annexed South Kasai as a colony

evt-08-09-1960-albert-kalonji.butterflyEffect: Congolese central government troops under Lumumba's orders invaded South Kasai, and the conflict escalated into brutal ethnic violence between Baluba and Lulua populations. The instability deepened the wider Congo Crisis, fueling the international interventions that eventually paved the way for Mobutu's rise to power.

evt-08-09-1969-manson-family.scenario: It is the morning of 9 August 1969. You are the housekeeper arriving at the Cielo Drive residence in Los Angeles, and you find a horrifying scene inside.
evt-08-09-1969-manson-family.prompt: What should you do first upon discovering the scene?

choices.text: Wait silently for the homeowners to return before acting
Call the police immediately and leave the scene undisturbed
Contact a newspaper reporter before calling authorities
Enter the house to search for survivors yourself

evt-08-09-1969-manson-family.butterflyEffect: The housekeeper, Winifred Chapman, fled screaming to alert neighbors, who called police. The murders of Sharon Tate and others became one of the most notorious crimes of the era, and the subsequent trial exposed the Manson Family's ideology, reshaping public fears about cults and the counterculture.

evt-08-09-1971-the-troubles.scenario: It is before dawn on 9 August 1971 in Belfast. You are a British soldier moving through nationalist neighborhoods with a list of names, part of a sweeping operation to round up suspected republican paramilitaries without trial.
evt-08-09-1971-the-troubles.prompt: What was the result of this mass internment operation?

choices.text: It alienated the nationalist community and fueled further violence
It triggered immediate peace negotiations
It led both communities to embrace power-sharing
It ended paramilitary activity within weeks

evt-08-09-1971-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: Operation Demetrius interned hundreds of suspected republicans, almost all Catholic, many with little evidence against them. Rather than pacifying the situation, it enraged the nationalist community, fueled IRA recruitment, and is widely seen as a turning point that deepened the Troubles for years afterward.

evt-08-09-1974-impeachment-process-again.scenario: It is the morning of 9 August 1974 in the White House. You are a senior aide to President Richard Nixon, who faces near-certain impeachment and removal over the Watergate scandal and must decide how to end his presidency.
evt-08-09-1974-impeachment-process-again.prompt: What did Nixon do that morning to avoid a Senate impeachment trial?

choices.text: He invoked executive privilege to block the House inquiry
He demanded a public trial before the full Congress
He fired the special prosecutor investigating Watergate
He resigned the presidency, becoming the first US president to do so

evt-08-09-1974-impeachment-process-again.butterflyEffect: Nixon resigned the presidency effective at noon, the first American president to do so, and Vice President Gerald Ford was sworn in immediately after. A month later Ford granted Nixon a full pardon, a decision that shaped public trust in the presidency for a generation.

evt-08-09-1974-watergate-scandal.scenario: It is morning on 9 August 1974 in Washington, D.C. You watch as President Richard Nixon boards a helicopter on the White House lawn after announcing his resignation the night before.
evt-08-09-1974-watergate-scandal.prompt: What happened immediately after Nixon's resignation took effect?

choices.text: Speaker of the House Carl Albert became acting president
Congress moved forward with impeachment proceedings anyway
Nixon was immediately arrested on federal charges
Vice President Gerald Ford was sworn in as president

evt-08-09-1974-watergate-scandal.butterflyEffect: Gerald Ford was sworn in within hours, becoming the only U.S. president never elected to national office. A month later he issued a controversial full pardon of Nixon, a decision many historians believe cost Ford the 1976 election.

evt-08-09-1988-wayne-gretzky.scenario: It is August 1988. You are Edmonton Oilers owner Peter Pocklington, facing mounting financial pressure, while Los Angeles Kings owner Bruce McNall dangles a record-breaking offer for your superstar center, Wayne Gretzky.
evt-08-09-1988-wayne-gretzky.prompt: What does Pocklington do with 'The Great One'?

choices.text: Trade Gretzky to the Kings for players, picks, and $15 million
Trade Gretzky to the New York Rangers instead
Refuse every offer and keep Gretzky in Edmonton
Retire Gretzky's jersey and end his career immediately

evt-08-09-1988-wayne-gretzky.butterflyEffect: Pocklington traded Gretzky to the Kings for players, draft picks, and $15 million, a deal so shocking it was debated in the Canadian Parliament. The trade helped ignite hockey's popularity across the American Sun Belt and paved the way for future NHL expansion into non-traditional markets.

evt-08-09-1993-liberal-democratic-party-.scenario: You are a Japanese lawmaker in 1993, watching defectors from the ruling party join opposition parties in a no-confidence vote that finally breaks the Liberal Democratic Party's 38-year grip on government.
evt-08-09-1993-liberal-democratic-party-.prompt: What government forms after the LDP's historic defeat?

choices.text: Direct rule reinstated by the Emperor
A military caretaker administration
A coalition government led by Morihiro Hosokawa
A merger forming a single new ruling party with the LDP

evt-08-09-1993-liberal-democratic-party-.butterflyEffect: A coalition of opposition parties took power under Prime Minister Morihiro Hosokawa, ending the LDP's unbroken postwar rule. The LDP returned to power within a few years, but the episode forced electoral reforms and showed that Japan's one-party dominance could be broken.

evt-08-09-1995-aviateca-flight-901.scenario: It is the evening of 9 August 1995. You are the captain of Aviateca Flight 901, descending through thick cloud toward Comalapa International Airport as the unseen slopes of San Vicente volcano rise ahead of you.
evt-08-09-1995-aviateca-flight-901.prompt: What did investigators conclude ultimately caused the crash?

choices.text: Pilot error combined with an air traffic control mistake in bad weather
A hijacking attempt that went wrong
A catastrophic engine failure shortly after takeoff
The aircraft ran out of fuel before landing

evt-08-09-1995-aviateca-flight-901.butterflyEffect: The Civil Aviation Authority found that pilot error, compounded by an air traffic control mistake during poor weather, caused the Boeing 737 to strike San Vicente volcano. All 65 aboard died, making it the deadliest aviation disaster in El Salvador's history and a case study in controlled-flight-into-terrain accidents.

evt-08-09-1999-boris-yeltsin.scenario: It is 9 August 1999 in the Kremlin. You are an aide to President Boris Yeltsin, who has just dismissed his fourth prime minister in seventeen months and is about to announce a little-known successor on television.
evt-08-09-1999-boris-yeltsin.prompt: Who did Yeltsin name as the new prime minister and his preferred successor?

choices.text: Yevgeny Primakov
Viktor Chernomyrdin
Vladimir Putin
Sergei Kiriyenko

evt-08-09-1999-boris-yeltsin.butterflyEffect: Yeltsin appointed the little-known Vladimir Putin, publicly declaring him his chosen successor. Within months Yeltsin resigned, Putin became acting president, and went on to win election in 2000, beginning more than two decades of dominance over Russian politics.

evt-08-09-2001-second-intifada.scenario: It is midday on 9 August 2001. You are an Israeli security official in Jerusalem, arriving at the smoking wreckage of a crowded pizza restaurant just destroyed by a suicide bomber during the Second Intifada.
evt-08-09-2001-second-intifada.prompt: What major step did Israel take in East Jerusalem in the bombing's immediate aftermath?

choices.text: Invited United Nations peacekeepers into Jerusalem
Signed a new interim peace accord with the Palestinian Authority
Withdrew all Israeli troops from the West Bank
Seized Orient House, the PLO's de facto headquarters in East Jerusalem

evt-08-09-2001-second-intifada.butterflyEffect: Within days, Israeli forces seized Orient House, the de facto PLO headquarters in East Jerusalem, shutting down the Palestinian political presence there. The move deepened the diplomatic rupture and hardened both sides as the intifada's cycle of bombings and reprisals continued for years.

evt-08-09-2006-2006-transatlantic-aircra.scenario: It is August 2006, and you are queuing to board a transatlantic flight from London when armed police suddenly flood the terminal, grounding departures and confiscating drinks bottles from every passenger.
evt-08-09-2006-2006-transatlantic-aircra.prompt: What lasting airport security rule followed the plot's discovery?

choices.text: A total ban on liquids that was never lifted
A 100ml limit on liquids carried in hand luggage
Mandatory removal of shoes at every checkpoint worldwide
A permanent ban on all carry-on laptops

evt-08-09-2006-2006-transatlantic-aircra.butterflyEffect: British police uncovered a plan to smuggle liquid explosives disguised as soft drinks onto US-bound airliners. In the aftermath, airports worldwide banned carry-on liquids entirely before settling on the now-familiar 100ml container limit, a restriction still enforced two decades later.

evt-08-09-2014-ferguson-missouri.scenario: It is the afternoon of 9 August 2014 in Ferguson, Missouri. Word spreads through the neighborhood that police officer Darren Wilson has fatally shot unarmed 18-year-old Michael Brown in the street.
evt-08-09-2014-ferguson-missouri.prompt: What did the shooting set in motion over the following days and months?

choices.text: An instant federal takeover of the Ferguson police department
Widespread protests and unrest that sparked a national reckoning over policing
The immediate resignation of the entire city government
A quiet, uneventful vigil with no lasting attention

evt-08-09-2014-ferguson-missouri.butterflyEffect: Ferguson erupted into sustained protests and unrest that drew national and international attention to policing and race in America. A Department of Justice investigation later found a pattern of racial bias in Ferguson's police and courts, and the event became a defining flashpoint for the Black Lives Matter movement.

evt-08-09-2023-fernando-villavicencio.scenario: It is the evening of 9 August 2023 in Quito. You are part of presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio's security detail as he leaves a campaign rally, gunfire suddenly erupting around his vehicle.
evt-08-09-2023-fernando-villavicencio.prompt: What did the Ecuadorian government do in the immediate aftermath of the assassination?

choices.text: Postponed the general election indefinitely
Named a new interim president
Declared martial law and canceled all campaigning
Declared a state of emergency and vowed the election would proceed

evt-08-09-2023-fernando-villavicencio.butterflyEffect: President Guillermo Lasso declared a 60-day state of emergency but let the election proceed on schedule. Villavicencio's running mate Andrea González stepped into the spotlight, and the race went to a runoff eventually won by Daniel Noboa, Ecuador's youngest ever president.

evt-08-10-1628-vasa-ship.scenario: It is 10 August 1628, and you stand on the deck of the newly built warship Vasa as she sets off from Stockholm on her maiden voyage, guns gleaming and crowds cheering from the shore.
evt-08-10-1628-vasa-ship.prompt: Minutes earlier, a stability test showed the ship rocking dangerously. Do you sail anyway?

choices.text: Sail as ordered, trusting the king's timetable over the test
Remove several of the upper gun decks to lighten the ship
Order the mainmast shortened before departure
Delay the launch and add more ballast to the hold

evt-08-10-1628-vasa-ship.butterflyEffect: Vasa sailed as ordered and capsized after barely 1,300 metres, sunk by a gust of wind she was too narrow and top-heavy to survive. She lay forgotten for over three centuries until her remarkably preserved hull was raised in 1961, becoming one of the world's most visited maritime museum exhibits.

evt-08-10-1792-french-revolution.scenario: It is 10 August 1792 in Paris. King Louis XVI has already fled the Tuileries Palace for the Legislative Assembly's protection as an armed crowd of insurrectionists storms the palace gates behind you.
evt-08-10-1792-french-revolution.prompt: What follows for the French monarchy once the palace falls that day?

choices.text: The king is executed by the crowd that same day
The king is restored to full power by the Assembly
A constitutional compromise ends the crisis peacefully
The monarchy is suspended and the king is imprisoned

evt-08-10-1792-french-revolution.butterflyEffect: The Legislative Assembly suspended the monarchy and had Louis XVI imprisoned, ending centuries of royal authority in France in a single day. The fall of the Tuileries paved the way for the National Convention, the abolition of the monarchy weeks later, and Louis's eventual execution in January 1793.

evt-08-10-1793-louvre.scenario: It is 10 August 1793, one year to the day since the monarchy fell, and the revolutionary government throws open the doors of the former royal palace on the Seine.
evt-08-10-1793-louvre.prompt: What does the new government do with the vast art collection once reserved for kings?

choices.text: Destroy portraits of the royal family as symbols of tyranny
Seal the palace indefinitely for security reasons
Auction the royal paintings to foreign collectors for revenue
Open it as a public museum for ordinary citizens to view

evt-08-10-1793-louvre.butterflyEffect: The Louvre opened that day as the Muséum central des arts, putting royal treasures on public display for the first time. It set the template for the modern public art museum, and today it remains the most visited museum on Earth.

evt-08-10-1844-friedrich-wilhelm-bessel.scenario: You are an astronomer in 1844 poring over years of precise position measurements of Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, and you notice it does not move in a smooth, straight path as expected.
evt-08-10-1844-friedrich-wilhelm-bessel.prompt: What do you conclude is causing Sirius's irregular, wobbling motion across the sky?

choices.text: Atmospheric refraction is distorting the telescope's measurements
The telescope's mechanism has a systematic calibration error
An unseen companion star is orbiting it and pulling it off course
A large undiscovered planet is passing in front of it

evt-08-10-1844-friedrich-wilhelm-bessel.butterflyEffect: Bessel correctly predicted an unseen companion tugging Sirius gravitationally, and in 1862 telescope maker Alvan Graham Clark spotted the faint white dwarf now called Sirius B. The confirmation of invisible companions through orbital wobble became a foundational technique for discovering unseen stars and, later, exoplanets.

evt-08-10-1861-american-civil-war.scenario: It is dawn on 10 August 1861 near Springfield, Missouri. You serve under Union General Nathaniel Lyon, whose small force is about to attack a much larger Confederate and Missouri State Guard army at Wilson's Creek.
evt-08-10-1861-american-civil-war.prompt: What happens as Lyon presses the attack despite being badly outnumbered?

choices.text: Both sides agree to a truce and withdraw peacefully
The Union force is defeated and Lyon is killed on the field
The Confederate force surrenders without a fight
The Union wins a decisive victory and secures Missouri for the North

evt-08-10-1861-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Lyon was killed in the fighting, becoming the first Union general to die in the war, and his outnumbered troops were forced to retreat to Rolla. The Confederate victory could not fully secure Missouri, and the state descended into years of brutal guerrilla warfare that outlasted the conventional war itself.

evt-08-10-1901-amalgamated-association-o.scenario: It is 1901 and you organize for the Amalgamated Association of Iron, Steel and Tin Workers, calling members out on strike against the newly formed U.S. Steel Corporation after it refuses to recognize the union at its non-union mills.
evt-08-10-1901-amalgamated-association-o.prompt: What is the eventual outcome for organized labor at U.S. Steel after months of striking?

choices.text: Federal troops force the company into binding arbitration favoring workers
The strike fails and U.S. Steel stays largely non-union for decades
U.S. Steel recognizes the union at every one of its plants
Steelworkers nationwide win an eight-hour day as a result

evt-08-10-1901-amalgamated-association-o.butterflyEffect: The strike collapsed, and U.S. Steel remained essentially union-free for the next three decades, crippling the AA as an organization. Only in the 1930s did the CIO's Steel Workers Organizing Committee rebuild steel unionism, and the AA finally merged into the new United Steelworkers in 1942.

evt-08-10-1966-heron-road-workers-memori.scenario: It is August 1966, and you are working on the unfinished Heron Road bridge spanning the Rideau River in Ottawa when the deck beneath you suddenly gives way.
evt-08-10-1966-heron-road-workers-memori.prompt: What is the outcome for the crew working on the bridge that day?

choices.text: Emergency shoring stops the deck from fully collapsing
All the workers manage to escape without serious injury
Only a few minor injuries occur among the crew
Nine workers are killed and dozens more injured in the collapse

evt-08-10-1966-heron-road-workers-memori.butterflyEffect: Nine workers were killed and more than sixty injured, the worst construction accident in Ottawa's and Ontario's history. The finished bridge opened in 1967, and in 2016 it was renamed the Heron Road Workers Memorial Bridge to honor those who died.

evt-08-10-1988-civil-liberties-act-of-19.scenario: You spent years of your childhood behind barbed wire in a wartime internment camp for Japanese Americans, and now in August 1988 you watch President Reagan sign a bill into law in the Rose Garden.
evt-08-10-1988-civil-liberties-act-of-19.prompt: What does the Civil Liberties Act actually provide to internment survivors like you?

choices.text: A formal apology and a $20,000 reparations payment
A national memorial with no apology or compensation
Return of confiscated property with no direct payments
Restoration of citizenship that had been revoked during the war

evt-08-10-1988-civil-liberties-act-of-19.butterflyEffect: The act delivered a formal government apology and a $20,000 payment to each surviving internee, with payments eventually reaching more than 82,000 people. It became a landmark precedent cited by later redress movements seeking acknowledgment for other historic government wrongs.

evt-08-10-2007-queen-s-pier.scenario: You are a young activist in Central, Hong Kong, in 2007. Bulldozers wait nearby as the government prepares to demolish the historic Queen's Pier for a harbourfront redevelopment.
evt-08-10-2007-queen-s-pier.prompt: What do you and fellow activists do to try to stop the demolition?

choices.text: Quietly file a request for UNESCO World Heritage status
Occupy the pier and stage a hunger strike, refusing to leave
Petition Beijing directly for intervention
Boycott the upcoming Legislative Council election

evt-08-10-2007-queen-s-pier.butterflyEffect: Activists occupied the pier for weeks and some staged hunger strikes, but the government demolished it in 2008 anyway. The campaign became a landmark moment for Hong Kong's heritage-conservation movement, shaping the tactics and political consciousness of the localist activism that followed in the next decade.

evt-08-10-2014-sepahan-airlines-flight-5.scenario: You are the captain of an IrAn-140 turboprop climbing out of Tehran's Mehrabad Airport on 10 August 2014, bound for Tabas, when one of your engines suddenly loses power.
evt-08-10-2014-sepahan-airlines-flight-5.prompt: What actually happens next to Flight 5915?

choices.text: It crashes into a boulevard near Azadi Stadium during the attempted return
The crew successfully lands back at Mehrabad without injury
The plane diverts safely to a nearby military airbase
The crew ditches the aircraft in a reservoir outside the city

evt-08-10-2014-sepahan-airlines-flight-5.butterflyEffect: The aircraft went down into a boulevard near Azadi Stadium as the crew tried to turn back, killing 40 of the 48 aboard. The crash intensified scrutiny of Iran's aging, sanctions-starved aircraft fleet and added to international pressure for easing restrictions that blocked Iran from buying modern, safer planes.

evt-08-10-2018-horizon-air.scenario: It is the evening of 10 August 2018 at Sea-Tac Airport. A ground service agent with no pilot training has just stolen an empty Horizon Air turboprop and taken off, and you are the air traffic controller now on the radio with him as fighter jets scramble.
evt-08-10-2018-horizon-air.prompt: What is the best course of action as the stolen plane climbs over Puget Sound?

choices.text: Order the fighter jets to shoot the aircraft down immediately
Keep him talking calmly and try to guide him toward a safe landing
Cut off radio contact so he cannot be traced
Evacuate the airport terminal and do nothing else

evt-08-10-2018-horizon-air.butterflyEffect: Controllers spent nearly an hour calmly talking Richard Russell through basic flight maneuvers while National Guard F-15s shadowed but never fired on the plane. After performing loops over the Sound, he deliberately crashed into sparsely populated Ketron Island, killing only himself, and the incident led airlines to tighten scrutiny of ground-crew access to aircraft.

evt-08-10-2018-2017-2019-romanian-protes.scenario: You stand in Victoriei Square in Bucharest on the night of 10 August 2018, among tens of thousands from the Romanian diaspora demanding an end to government corruption, when gendarmes suddenly fire tear gas into the crowd.
evt-08-10-2018-2017-2019-romanian-protes.prompt: What follows the gendarmes' violent crackdown on the protest?

choices.text: The government immediately resigns en masse
The European Union imposes immediate sanctions on Romania
Hundreds are injured, sparking outrage and resignation demands against officials
The protest disperses quietly with no further consequences

evt-08-10-2018-2017-2019-romanian-protes.butterflyEffect: Hundreds of protesters were injured in the crackdown, which was filmed and broadcast widely, sparking outrage at home and abroad and calls for the interior minister's resignation. The images galvanized Romania's anti-corruption movement for months afterward and fed into growing public distrust that contributed to the ruling coalition's later political troubles.

evt-08-10-2019-jeffrey-epstein.scenario: It is early morning at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in Manhattan. You are a guard on the unit housing a financier awaiting trial on federal sex-trafficking charges.
evt-08-10-2019-jeffrey-epstein.prompt: What happens to Jeffrey Epstein this morning at the MCC?

choices.text: He is granted bail pending trial
He is acquitted after a surprise plea deal
He is quietly transferred to a witness protection facility
He is found dead in his cell, ruled a suicide

evt-08-10-2019-jeffrey-epstein.butterflyEffect: Epstein was found dead in his cell, and the medical examiner ruled it a suicide by hanging. His death before trial fueled years of conspiracy theories, prompted lawsuits from victims against his estate and associates, and led to the firing of the jail's warden and criminal charges against two guards for falsifying watch logs.

evt-08-10-2019-2019-b-rum-murder-and-mos.scenario: It is midday on 10 August 2019, and you are one of the few worshippers still inside the Al-Noor Islamic Centre in Bærum, Norway, when an armed man shoots his way through the glass entrance.
evt-08-10-2019-2019-b-rum-murder-and-mos.prompt: What do the men inside the mosque do as the gunman opens fire?

choices.text: Rush and physically subdue him before he can hurt anyone
Attempt to talk him into putting down the weapon
Flee immediately through the nearest exit
Barricade themselves in a back room and call police

evt-08-10-2019-2019-b-rum-murder-and-mos.butterflyEffect: The men tackled and restrained the attacker, Philip Manshaus, before he could harm anyone, though he had already murdered his stepsister at home that day. He was convicted of murder and a terrorist act, and the case intensified Norway's debate over far-right extremism and firearm access.

evt-08-10-2020-2020-midwest-derecho.scenario: You are a farmer standing in your Iowa cornfield on 10 August 2020. The sky turns an eerie green and within minutes the wind roars past 100 mph with no warning from forecasters.
evt-08-10-2020-2020-midwest-derecho.prompt: What should you do right now as the sudden windstorm hits?

choices.text: Take shelter immediately in a basement or low ditch
Assume it's a passing shower and continue working
Go out to manually stake down the crops
Keep driving your truck to outrun the storm

evt-08-10-2020-2020-midwest-derecho.butterflyEffect: The derecho flattened millions of acres of corn and soybeans and tore through cities like Cedar Rapids with no advance warning, becoming the costliest thunderstorm disaster in U.S. history at over $11 billion in damage. It exposed gaps in derecho forecasting and pushed meteorologists to improve detection of these fast-moving wind events.

evt-08-11-1309-reconquista.scenario: It is August 1309, and you stand with King James II of Aragon's forces as they come ashore near Almería, part of a coordinated Christian offensive against Granada launched alongside Castile.
evt-08-11-1309-reconquista.prompt: What is the eventual outcome of the Aragonese siege of Almería?

choices.text: Almería falls and is annexed to Aragon
The siege fails and Aragonese forces withdraw
The city surrenders after a negotiated truce
Castilian reinforcements capture the city instead

evt-08-11-1309-reconquista.butterflyEffect: The siege dragged on without success and Aragonese forces withdrew in 1310, ending the coordinated offensive. Almería remained in Muslim hands for another 180 years, and the setback slowed Aragon's involvement in the final conquest of Granada for generations.

evt-08-11-1492-1492-conclave.scenario: It is August 1492, and you are a cardinal locked inside the newly frescoed Sistine Chapel. Innocent VIII is dead, and after three inconclusive ballots the College of Cardinals must settle on a successor.
evt-08-11-1492-1492-conclave.prompt: On the fourth ballot, which cardinal does the conclave elect as pope?

choices.text: Oliviero Carafa, cardinal of Naples
Giuliano della Rovere, future Pope Julius II
Ascanio Sforza, ally of the Milanese court
Rodrigo Borja, vice chancellor of the Church

evt-08-11-1492-1492-conclave.butterflyEffect: Cardinal Rodrigo Borja won and took the name Alexander VI. His papacy became notorious for nepotism and political scheming, and in 1494 his arbitration produced the Treaty of Tordesillas dividing the New World between Spain and Portugal, a decision whose effects on colonization lasted centuries.

evt-08-11-1786-francis-light.scenario: It is 11 August 1786, and Francis Light has just secured Penang for the East India Company from the Sultan of Kedah. Standing before the new settlement of George Town, he must decide how to draw traders and settlers to an unproven port.
evt-08-11-1786-francis-light.prompt: What policy did Light use to attract merchants and settlers to George Town?

choices.text: Restricted trade to an East India Company monopoly
Made George Town a free port with no import duties
Built the settlement's economy on a slave-plantation system
Imposed high tariffs to fund the settlement's defenses

evt-08-11-1786-francis-light.butterflyEffect: Light declared Penang a free port with no import duties, drawing traders from across Asia almost immediately and rapidly building its population and commerce. The free-port model he pioneered later influenced Stamford Raffles' founding of Singapore, and Penang became a cornerstone of the British Straits Settlements.

evt-08-11-1945-krakow.scenario: It is August 1945 in Kraków. A false rumor is spreading through the market that Jewish residents near Miodowa Street have kidnapped Christian children, and an agitated crowd is gathering close to the synagogue.
evt-08-11-1945-krakow.prompt: What should authorities have done as the rumor pushed the crowd toward violence?

choices.text: Ignore the rumor, assuming it would fade on its own
Investigate and publicly refute the false rumor before it incited a mob
Arm the crowd so they could search homes themselves
Confirm the rumor publicly to calm the crowd's anger

evt-08-11-1945-krakow.butterflyEffect: Police and soldiers failed to stop the mob in time; rioters attacked Jewish residents and the Kupa Synagogue, killing at least one person and injuring others. The pogrom was one of several postwar outbreaks of antisemitic violence in Poland that convinced many Holocaust survivors there was no safe future in the country, accelerating emigration to Palestine and the West.

evt-08-11-1952-talal-of-jordan.scenario: It is 11 August 1952 in Amman. King Talal's worsening mental illness has made him unable to govern, and Jordan's parliament must decide how the throne will pass on.
evt-08-11-1952-talal-of-jordan.prompt: What did Jordan's parliament do in response to King Talal's illness?

choices.text: Appointed a permanent regency council with no successor named
Exiled him permanently from Jordan
Abolished the Hashemite monarchy entirely
Forced his abdication and installed his young son Hussein as heir

evt-08-11-1952-talal-of-jordan.butterflyEffect: Parliament forced Talal's abdication and passed the crown to his teenage son, Hussein, who took the throne fully in 1953 after a brief regency. Hussein would go on to rule Jordan for nearly 47 years, steering it through wars with Israel, the loss of the West Bank, and eventually a peace treaty in 1994.

evt-08-11-1965-watts-riots.scenario: It is the evening of 11 August 1965 in Watts, Los Angeles. A crowd has gathered around a California Highway Patrol officer arresting a Black motorist, and tempers in the neighborhood are already raw over years of police treatment and poverty.
evt-08-11-1965-watts-riots.prompt: What incident actually ignited six days of unrest in Watts?

choices.text: The assassination of a local civil rights leader
A dispute over water rights in South Central Los Angeles
A court order to desegregate Los Angeles schools
A traffic stop and arrest that drew an angry crowd and allegations of police brutality

evt-08-11-1965-watts-riots.butterflyEffect: A roadside argument during the arrest of motorist Marquette Frye escalated into a confrontation with police that spread through Watts over six days, leaving dozens dead and vast property damage. The subsequent McCone Commission report exposed the poverty, unemployment, and police-community tensions underlying the violence, shaping national debate on urban policy for years afterward.

evt-08-11-1969-apollo-11.scenario: It is 11 August 1969, and Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins have spent three weeks sealed inside a quarantine facility since splashing down from the Moon, watched closely by NASA physicians.
evt-08-11-1969-apollo-11.prompt: Why were the returning Apollo 11 astronauts kept in strict quarantine?

choices.text: To rule out contamination by unknown lunar microorganisms
To debrief them on classified mission details
To build public anticipation before a televised celebration
To treat suspected radiation sickness from the flight

evt-08-11-1969-apollo-11.butterflyEffect: NASA feared the astronauts might have brought back unknown lunar microorganisms that could threaten Earth's biosphere, so all three were isolated for 21 days along with their capsule and Moon samples. No pathogens were ever found, and quarantine requirements were progressively relaxed for later Apollo crews.

evt-08-11-1972-vietnam-war.scenario: You serve in the 3rd Battalion, 21st Infantry, boarding transport out of South Vietnam in August 1972 as the last American ground combat unit still in the country.
evt-08-11-1972-vietnam-war.prompt: What did your unit's departure mark for the U.S. role in the war?

choices.text: The beginning of U.S. bombing campaigns against North Vietnam
The complete withdrawal of all American personnel from Vietnam
The end of direct U.S. ground combat units in Vietnam, though advisors remained
The start of full-scale U.S. combat operations

evt-08-11-1972-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: The withdrawal ended direct U.S. ground combat units in Vietnam, though advisors and air power remained. South Vietnam's growing reliance on its own forces foreshadowed the 1973 Paris Peace Accords and, ultimately, its collapse in 1975 once American support fully ended.

evt-08-11-1973-dj-kool-herc.scenario: You're at Cindy Campbell's back-to-school party in the rec room at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue in the Bronx, August 1973. Her brother Clive spins funk records, but dancers keep drifting off the floor whenever a song shifts into vocals.
evt-08-11-1973-dj-kool-herc.prompt: What turntable trick should the DJ use to keep dancers moving through the song?

choices.text: Switch to only slow ballads for the rest of the night
Use two copies of the same record to extend the instrumental break
Play each song straight through without any interruption
Sing live vocals over a single turntable's playback

evt-08-11-1973-dj-kool-herc.butterflyEffect: Clive Campbell, soon known as DJ Kool Herc, used two copies of the same record to loop and extend the instrumental drum "break," and began chanting over it to the crowd. This breakbeat technique and his rhythmic call-outs became the foundations of DJing and rapping, and the Bronx party is now regarded as hip-hop's birthplace.

evt-08-11-1973-1520-sedgwick-avenue.scenario: It is 11 August 1973, and you are dancing in the recreation room of 1520 Sedgwick Avenue in the Bronx, where a young DJ named Clive Campbell is hosting a back-to-school party for his sister.
evt-08-11-1973-1520-sedgwick-avenue.prompt: What technique does DJ Kool Herc introduce on the turntables that night?

choices.text: Rapping continuously over a full disco track
Mixing a live band with prerecorded vocals
Scratching a record backward for rhythmic effect
Looping breakbeats using two copies of the same record

evt-08-11-1973-1520-sedgwick-avenue.butterflyEffect: Herc used two copies of the same record to loop and extend the instrumental breakbeat, giving dancers a longer groove to move to. That technique became the foundation of hip-hop DJing, and within years it fed into MCing, breakdancing, and graffiti, the culture's four founding pillars.

evt-08-11-1979-aeroflot.scenario: It is 11 August 1979, and you are an air traffic controller tracking two Aeroflot Tupolev jets converging over Dniprodzerzhynsk in Ukrainian airspace, one of them carrying the Pakhtakor Tashkent football club.
evt-08-11-1979-aeroflot.prompt: What caused the two aircraft to collide in mid-air?

choices.text: A ground controller's routing and altitude error
A mechanical failure in one aircraft's navigation system
Pilot error during a scheduled altitude change
Severe unforecast thunderstorms over the route

evt-08-11-1979-aeroflot.butterflyEffect: An air traffic controller's error placed both jets on the same flight level and collision course, killing all 178 people aboard, including the entire Pakhtakor Tashkent team. The disaster forced Soviet aviation authorities to tighten altitude separation and controller procedures across the USSR's crowded air corridors.

evt-08-11-1992-mall-of-america.scenario: You're among the crowds at the ribbon-cutting for Mall of America in Bloomington, Minnesota, built on the site of the old Metropolitan Stadium, on its opening day in August 1992.
evt-08-11-1992-mall-of-america.prompt: What made this new mall stand apart from a typical American shopping center?

choices.text: It banned all national chain retailers from leasing space
It required a paid membership to enter the building
It was built entirely underground for weather protection
It combined shopping with a full indoor amusement park and aquarium

evt-08-11-1992-mall-of-america.butterflyEffect: Mall of America paired retail with a full indoor amusement park and aquarium under one roof, becoming the largest mall in the Western Hemisphere. Its entertainment-driven model became a template for "experiential" malls worldwide as later retailers scrambled to compete with e-commerce.

evt-08-11-1999-1999-salt-lake-city-torna.scenario: It is midday on 11 August 1999 and the sky over downtown Salt Lake City has turned a sickly green. Sirens begin to wail as a funnel cloud drops toward the city center where you are working.
evt-08-11-1999-1999-salt-lake-city-torna.prompt: As the tornado bears down on downtown, what should you do?

choices.text: Head outside to take photographs for the news
Move to an interior room or basement away from windows
Stand near a window to watch the funnel approach
Get in your car and try to outrun it through downtown traffic

evt-08-11-1999-1999-salt-lake-city-torna.butterflyEffect: The tornado, a rare F2 for the region, tore through downtown and Memory Grove Park, killing one person struck by falling debris and injuring over 100. It remains the only tornado fatality on record in Utah and spurred improved severe-weather warning systems for a region long considered low-risk for tornadoes.

evt-08-11-1999-ken-levine-game-developer.scenario: It is August 1999, and you work at Looking Glass Studios watching sales figures trickle in for System Shock 2, the survival-horror game Ken Levine has just helped design.
evt-08-11-1999-ken-levine-game-developer.prompt: Despite weak sales, what does System Shock 2 achieve that shapes Levine's future career?

choices.text: Universal panning by critics and press
Immediate blockbuster commercial success
Cancellation of the System Shock license entirely
Cult critical acclaim that later shapes BioShock's design

evt-08-11-1999-ken-levine-game-developer.butterflyEffect: The game sold poorly but earned lasting critical acclaim for its atmosphere, storytelling, and RPG-infused shooter design. Those ideas became the blueprint for BioShock in 2007, which Levine led at Irrational Games, cementing his reputation as one of gaming's leading narrative designers.

evt-08-11-2003-nato.scenario: You are a NATO staff officer in Kabul in August 2003 as the alliance formally assumes command of the International Security Assistance Force from the rotating national leadership that had run it before.
evt-08-11-2003-nato.prompt: What was historically significant about NATO taking this command?

choices.text: It marked NATO's suspension of its Article 5 defense obligations
It was NATO's first-ever mission outside Europe and North America
It ended all foreign troop presence in Afghanistan
It transferred command of the force to the United Nations

evt-08-11-2003-nato.butterflyEffect: This was NATO's first-ever operational command outside Europe and North America. It drew the alliance into a decade-plus counterinsurgency campaign involving troops from dozens of member and partner nations, reshaping NATO's post-Cold War identity into an expeditionary force well beyond its original defensive mission.

evt-08-11-2006-oil-tanker.scenario: You're a shipping official monitoring reports on 11 August 2006 as the tanker MT Solar 1, loaded with bunker fuel for Petron Corporation, radios distress in rough seas near Guimaras Island in the Philippines.
evt-08-11-2006-oil-tanker.prompt: What followed once the tanker went down off Guimaras?

choices.text: The Philippines' worst oil spill, devastating mangroves, reefs, and fisheries
A quick, fully contained cleanup with no lasting ecological damage
A spill confined to open ocean that never reached the coastline
Successful transfer of the entire cargo before the ship sank

evt-08-11-2006-oil-tanker.butterflyEffect: The sinking caused the Philippines' worst oil spill, coating Guimaras' coastline, mangroves, and coral reefs in thick bunker fuel and devastating local fishing communities for years. The disaster pushed the Philippine government to tighten maritime safety rules and hold shipping operators more accountable for environmental damage.

evt-08-11-2023-luna-25.scenario: It is August 2023, and you are a Roscosmos flight controller tracking Russia's first lunar mission since 1976. Luna 25 is preparing to fire its engines and drop into a lower orbit ahead of its planned landing near the south pole.
evt-08-11-2023-luna-25.prompt: What happens when Luna 25 attempts this pre-landing orbital maneuver?

choices.text: It crashes into the lunar surface after an engine anomaly
The burn is aborted and the probe returns to Earth orbit
It lands but all instruments fail on touchdown
It lands safely and begins transmitting data

evt-08-11-2023-luna-25.butterflyEffect: An error during the engine burn sent Luna 25 into an uncontrolled orbit, and it crashed into the Moon on 19 August 2023. The failure came just days before India's Chandrayaan-3 successfully touched down near the south pole, underscoring how far Russia's once-dominant space program had fallen behind.

evt-08-12-1099-crusades.scenario: You are a knight in Godfrey of Bouillon's army camped outside Ascalon in August 1099, weeks after the fall of Jerusalem, as a large Fatimid relief force under al-Afdal Shahanshah approaches.
evt-08-12-1099-crusades.prompt: What should the exhausted crusader army do?

choices.text: Launch a surprise assault despite being exhausted from the siege
Negotiate a truce with al-Afdal to avoid further losses
Retreat to Jerusalem and wait for reinforcements from Europe
Attack immediately before the Fatimid force can organize

evt-08-12-1099-crusades.butterflyEffect: The crusaders attacked at once and routed al-Afdal's army, which fled back into Egypt. The victory secured the infant Kingdom of Jerusalem in its first vulnerable months, though quarrels among the crusader leaders stopped them from taking Ascalon itself, leaving it a Fatimid stronghold for decades.

evt-08-12-1323-novgorod-republic.scenario: You are a Novgorod envoy meeting Swedish delegates at the fortress of Nöteborg on Lake Ladoga in 1323, seeking to end decades of fighting over the Karelian frontier.
evt-08-12-1323-novgorod-republic.prompt: What do the two sides agree upon to settle the conflict?

choices.text: A formal border dividing Karelia between Sweden and Novgorod
Novgorod's surrender of its Hanseatic trading rights to Sweden
Joint Swedish-Novgorodian rule over all of Finland
Swedish annexation of the city of Novgorod itself

evt-08-12-1323-novgorod-republic.butterflyEffect: The Treaty of Nöteborg drew the first officially recognized border between Sweden and Novgorod, dividing Karelia between them. That line shaped centuries of Russo-Swedish relations and border disputes, later revisited in treaties such as Teusina in 1595.

evt-08-12-1883-quagga.scenario: You are a keeper at Amsterdam's Natura Artis Magistra zoo in August 1883. The zoo's striped mare, a quagga, lies dying in her enclosure, and no zoo in Europe has ever managed to breed one in captivity.
evt-08-12-1883-quagga.prompt: What becomes clear about the quagga after this animal dies?

choices.text: She was the last of her kind; the quagga becomes extinct
A breeding pair turns up in a private German menagerie
A small wild herd is later confirmed surviving in South Africa's interior
London Zoo announces it will continue the bloodline from its own stock

evt-08-12-1883-quagga.butterflyEffect: This animal was the last known quagga; the subspecies of plains zebra went extinct with her death. Only one photograph of a living quagga exists, and the loss later became a touchstone for early conservation and de-extinction efforts, including 20th-century DNA-based breeding projects aiming to recreate its coat pattern.

evt-08-12-1914-world-war-i.scenario: You ride with Belgian defenders at the crossroads town of Halen on 12 August 1914, as waves of German Uhlan cavalry probe toward the Gete river, trying to swing around Liège's forts.
evt-08-12-1914-world-war-i.prompt: How did the outnumbered Belgians break the German cavalry's repeated charges?

choices.text: Massed artillery bombardment shattered the German cavalry before it reached the town
French reinforcements arrived and routed the Germans before the Belgians engaged
Dismounted riflemen and cyclists using barricades broke wave after wave of cavalry charges
They retreated behind fortified lines and let the Germans pass unopposed

evt-08-12-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Dismounted Belgian cavalry and cyclists used rifle fire and improvised barricades to shatter charge after charge, inflicting such losses on the German horsemen that the fight became known as the Battle of the Silver Helmets. Though only a brief delay to the German advance, the victory boosted Belgian and Allied morale early in the war and fed the propaganda narrative of Belgian heroic resistance.

evt-08-12-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: You live in the small Tuscan village of Sant'Anna di Stazzema in August 1944, where hundreds of local families and refugees have gathered, hoping the hillside will be spared as partisans and German troops clash nearby.
evt-08-12-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What did the Waffen-SS unit do when it entered the village that morning?

choices.text: They rounded up and massacred the civilians sheltering in the village
They requisitioned food and livestock and withdrew without violence
They evacuated the villagers peacefully to a nearby town
They arrested only men suspected of partisan ties and left the rest untouched

evt-08-12-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: SS troops rounded up and killed hundreds of villagers, mostly women, children, and the elderly, then burned much of the village in reprisal for partisan resistance in the area. Decades later, a 2005 trial in La Spezia convicted several former SS officers in absentia, and the site is now preserved as a national memorial park for peace.

evt-08-12-1945-smyth-report.scenario: It is August 12, 1945, days after the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. As a government official reviewing physicist Henry Smyth's draft account of the Manhattan Project before its public release, you must decide what level of detail is safe to disclose.
evt-08-12-1945-smyth-report.prompt: What does the released report ultimately reveal to the public?

choices.text: Complete engineering blueprints for building an atomic bomb
Only the personal biographies of the scientists involved
General scientific principles behind the bomb, with engineering and production details withheld
Nothing at all; the entire project remains fully classified

evt-08-12-1945-smyth-report.butterflyEffect: The Smyth Report gave the public a broad scientific narrative of how the bomb was built while deliberately withholding engineering and production secrets. It became an unlikely bestseller and set a precedent for controlled official disclosure, though some historians argue it still offered clues that aided other nations' nuclear efforts.

evt-08-12-1952-night-of-the-murdered-poe.scenario: You are a member of Moscow's Jewish Anti-Fascist Committee, held since 1948 and forced through years of interrogation to sign confessions to espionage you never committed.
evt-08-12-1952-night-of-the-murdered-poe.prompt: What happened to you and your twelve fellow defendants on the night of 12 August 1952?

choices.text: You were executed by firing squad in Lubyanka Prison
You were released after international pressure on Moscow
You were exiled internally and stripped of citizenship
You were sentenced to hard labor in a Siberian Gulag camp

evt-08-12-1952-night-of-the-murdered-poe.butterflyEffect: All thirteen defendants, including five prominent Yiddish writers, were executed by firing squad in Lubyanka Prison that night. The killings marked the height of Stalin's postwar antisemitic campaign and, once exposed after his death, became a lasting symbol of Soviet state persecution of Jewish intellectuals.

evt-08-12-1969-the-troubles.scenario: It is August 12, 1969, in the Bogside district of Derry. An Apprentice Boys parade has just passed nearby, and stones are being thrown as clashes erupt between residents and police that will last for days.
evt-08-12-1969-the-troubles.prompt: What follows once the rioting proves too much for local police to control?

choices.text: Community leaders negotiate an instant, lasting truce
The Apprentice Boys parade is permanently banned by the government
The Northern Ireland government immediately resigns en masse
The British Army is deployed to restore order in Northern Ireland

evt-08-12-1969-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: British troops were deployed onto Northern Ireland's streets on August 14, in what was meant to be a temporary peacekeeping measure. It became Operation Banner, the longest continuous deployment in British Army history, lasting until 2007, and the Battle of the Bogside is widely seen as marking the start of the Troubles.

evt-08-12-1977-approach-and-landing-test.scenario: You are pilot Fred Haise aboard the prototype orbiter Enterprise on 12 August 1977. Riding piggyback atop the Shuttle Carrier Aircraft over the Mojave Desert, you have just separated for the first time to fly the shuttle on your own.
evt-08-12-1977-approach-and-landing-test.prompt: How must you bring the unpowered orbiter safely to the ground?

choices.text: Glide it down to a runway landing at Edwards Air Force Base
Reattach to the carrier aircraft and ride it down together
Deploy a parachute for a controlled water landing
Fire orbital maneuvering thrusters to slow the descent

evt-08-12-1977-approach-and-landing-test.butterflyEffect: Enterprise glided unpowered to a successful landing on the dry lakebed runway at Edwards Air Force Base. The test proved the shuttle's dead-stick landing approach was viable, clearing the way for Columbia's first orbital flight in 1981.

evt-08-12-1981-ibm-personal-computer.scenario: It is 1981, and you are part of the IBM team in Boca Raton racing to launch a personal computer that can compete with Apple. You must decide how tightly to control the machine's hardware and software.
evt-08-12-1981-ibm-personal-computer.prompt: What approach does the team take with the new PC's design?

choices.text: Build entirely proprietary, closed hardware and software in-house
Use an open architecture with off-the-shelf parts and a licensed operating system
Partner exclusively with Apple to share a single design
Sell only bare hardware with no operating system at all

evt-08-12-1981-ibm-personal-computer.butterflyEffect: IBM built the PC from off-the-shelf components with an open architecture and licensed an operating system, MS-DOS, from Microsoft on a non-exclusive basis. That openness let rivals build "IBM-compatible" clones and let Microsoft sell DOS to everyone, fueling Microsoft's rise even as IBM eventually lost control of the market it had created.

evt-08-12-1985-japan-air-lines-flight-12.scenario: You are a passenger aboard Japan Air Lines Flight 123 climbing out of Tokyo on the evening of 12 August 1985, when a sudden bang tears through the cabin and the plane begins pitching wildly for the next half hour.
evt-08-12-1985-japan-air-lines-flight-12.prompt: What underlying failure left the crew unable to control the aircraft despite their 32-minute struggle?

choices.text: A badly repaired rear pressure bulkhead failed and destroyed the tail's hydraulic controls
A fuel tank explosion in the wing severed control cables
A bird strike knocked out both wing engines simultaneously
Pilot error during a rushed descent caused a structural overspeed

evt-08-12-1985-japan-air-lines-flight-12.butterflyEffect: An improperly repaired rear pressure bulkhead, patched after a 1978 tailstrike, failed under repeated pressurization and blew off much of the tail fin, severing all four hydraulic lines and leaving the crew with almost no control. It remains the deadliest single-aircraft accident in history, and the disaster forced sweeping reforms in Boeing's repair inspections and Japanese airline safety oversight.

evt-08-12-1990-faith-south-dakota.scenario: It is August 1990, and you are paleontologist Sue Hendrickson, scouting the eroding badlands near Faith, South Dakota. You notice small bone fragments crumbling from the base of a cliff face and look up to see more bone exposed above.
evt-08-12-1990-faith-south-dakota.prompt: What should you do about the bones you've spotted eroding from the cliff?

choices.text: Assume they are ordinary cattle bones and move on
Pry the visible bones loose immediately with hand tools before anyone else finds them
Rebury the exposed bone to protect it from weather and return next season
Mark the location and carefully begin documenting and excavating the site

evt-08-12-1990-faith-south-dakota.butterflyEffect: Hendrickson's find turned out to be the most complete Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton ever discovered, later named "Sue" in her honor. A bitter ownership dispute followed between the landowner, the excavating institute, and the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe, ending with an FBI seizure and a 1997 auction where the Field Museum bought Sue for $8.36 million.

evt-08-12-1990-sue-dinosaur.scenario: You are fossil hunter Sue Hendrickson, exploring eroding badlands cliffs near Faith, South Dakota, on 12 August 1990, when you spot Tyrannosaurus bones weathering out of the rock.
evt-08-12-1990-sue-dinosaur.prompt: What ultimately happens to this fossil's ownership in the years that follow?

choices.text: It is returned immediately and quietly to the landowner's ranch
It is donated permanently to a South Dakota state museum
It becomes the center of a legal dispute, later auctioned to Chicago's Field Museum
The Black Hills Institute keeps it as a private research specimen indefinitely

evt-08-12-1990-sue-dinosaur.butterflyEffect: A legal battle erupted between the excavators, the landowner, and the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe over the fossil's ownership; the FBI seized the bones in 1992. The dispute was resolved in 1997 when Sotheby's auctioned the skeleton to Chicago's Field Museum for a record $8.36 million, and "Sue" remains one of the most complete T. rex specimens ever found.

evt-08-12-1992-north-american-free-trade.scenario: It is August 12, 1992, and you are a trade negotiator for one of the three governments announcing that talks on a sweeping North American trade deal have concluded.
evt-08-12-1992-north-american-free-trade.prompt: What must happen before this newly negotiated agreement can take effect?

choices.text: Each country's supreme court must first approve its constitutionality
The United Nations must formally endorse the trade bloc
It takes effect immediately upon the negotiators' announcement
Legislatures in each country must ratify it before it enters into force

evt-08-12-1992-north-american-free-trade.butterflyEffect: NAFTA was signed later that year and ratified by the U.S., Canadian, and Mexican legislatures, entering into force on January 1, 1994. It reshaped North American manufacturing and trade for a generation, but growing political backlash over job losses eventually led to its replacement by the USMCA in 2020.

evt-08-12-1994-major-league-baseball.scenario: You are a players' union representative in August 1994, as talks with team owners over a proposed salary cap collapse and the season's final weeks hang in the balance.
evt-08-12-1994-major-league-baseball.prompt: What happens as the players' strike drags on through the autumn?

choices.text: Owners quickly abandon the salary cap and play resumes
The season finishes using replacement players
The World Series is cancelled for the first time since 1904
A settlement is reached within days and the season continues normally

evt-08-12-1994-major-league-baseball.butterflyEffect: The strike ran 232 days and forced cancellation of the 1994 World Series, the first lost since 1904. It delayed the start of the 1995 season, cost both sides hundreds of millions of dollars, and left attendance and fan trust depressed for years afterward.

evt-08-12-2000-russian-navy.scenario: It is 12 August 2000, and the submarine Kursk is taking part in naval exercises in the Barents Sea when a torpedo malfunction triggers a catastrophic explosion. The vessel sinks, and sailors may be alive in a flooded rear compartment.
evt-08-12-2000-russian-navy.prompt: What does the Russian government initially decide about outside rescue help?

choices.text: Immediately accept British and Norwegian rescue offers
Request only American naval assistance
Refuse foreign rescue assistance for several critical days
Launch a joint NATO-Russian rescue operation within hours

evt-08-12-2000-russian-navy.butterflyEffect: Moscow refused foreign assistance for several days, and by the time Norwegian divers reached the wreck, all 118 crew aboard had died. The delay drew fierce domestic and international criticism, becoming an early crisis for President Putin and prompting later reforms to Russian submarine safety and rescue protocols.

evt-08-12-2015-2015-tianjin-explosions.scenario: You are a firefighter arriving at a burning container warehouse in the Binhai New Area of Tianjin on the night of 12 August 2015, unaware of the chemicals stacked inside.
evt-08-12-2015-2015-tianjin-explosions.prompt: What should crews do before attacking the blaze with water hoses?

choices.text: Call for police to secure the perimeter and do nothing else
Douse the fire immediately with water to prevent it spreading
Confirm the chemical inventory and evacuate before any water is applied
Let the fire burn out on its own without intervention

evt-08-12-2015-2015-tianjin-explosions.butterflyEffect: Firefighters doused the fire with water, which reacted violently with stored chemicals including ammonium nitrate, triggering a second, far larger blast that killed many responders. The disaster exposed illegal storage of hazardous materials near housing, leading to prosecutions of officials and tighter Chinese regulations on chemical warehousing near populated areas.

evt-08-12-2016-syrian-civil-war.scenario: You are a Syrian Democratic Forces fighter on the edge of Manbij in August 2016, after a grinding two-and-a-half-month siege against Islamic State fighters dug into the city, with US-led coalition jets circling overhead.
evt-08-12-2016-syrian-civil-war.prompt: How did the SDF finally end ISIS control of Manbij?

choices.text: They simply besieged the city until ISIS fighters starved and surrendered
They negotiated an ISIS withdrawal that used civilian hostages as a human shield out of the city
They partnered with Turkish-backed rebels to storm the city together
They handed the siege over to Syrian government forces to finish

evt-08-12-2016-syrian-civil-war.butterflyEffect: ISIS agreed to withdraw its remaining fighters in a convoy that used civilians as human shields; the SDF took the city on 12 August 1916, and coalition strikes later hit the retreating convoy. The Kurdish-led SDF's expansion west of the Euphrates alarmed Turkey, fueling the cross-border tensions that led to Turkey's own military incursions into northern Syria.

evt-08-12-2017-unite-the-right-rally.scenario: It is the afternoon of August 12, 2017, in Charlottesville, Virginia. The rally has already been declared an unlawful assembly and dispersed by police, but marchers and counter-protesters remain scattered through the downtown streets.
evt-08-12-2017-unite-the-right-rally.prompt: What happens next as the crowds disperse through the streets that afternoon?

choices.text: A car is driven into a crowd of counter-protesters, killing one
Rally organizers are arrested on the spot by city police
Both sides agree to a negotiated truce and go home peacefully
The National Guard opens fire to disperse the remaining crowd

evt-08-12-2017-unite-the-right-rally.butterflyEffect: A car was deliberately driven into a crowd of counter-protesters, killing Heather Heyer and injuring dozens. The driver, James Alex Fields Jr., was later convicted of first-degree murder and federal hate crimes; the attack, combined with President Trump's widely criticized response, intensified national debate over Confederate monuments and domestic extremism.

evt-08-13-582-maurice-emperor.scenario: It is 582 in Constantinople, and Emperor Tiberius II Constantine is dying. He has no son, only a daughter, Constantina, and he must choose the general who will marry her and inherit the Eastern Roman throne.
evt-08-13-582-maurice-emperor.prompt: Whom does the dying emperor name as his heir and son-in-law?

choices.text: Priscus, a rival military commander
Philippicus, his own brother-in-law
Maurice, his trusted general and future son-in-law
Germanus, a distant relative of Justinian

evt-08-13-582-maurice-emperor.butterflyEffect: Tiberius chose Maurice, a capable general fresh from campaigns against Persia, who married Constantina and became emperor. Maurice reformed the army and stabilized the eastern frontier for two decades, but his harsh economies provoked a mutiny in 602 that overthrew and killed him, plunging the empire into the disastrous reign of Phocas and a ruinous war with Persia.

evt-08-13-1650-george-monck-1st-duke-of-.scenario: It is 1650, and General George Monck, a soldier who has fought on both sides of England's civil wars, is raising a new regiment of foot to serve under the Commonwealth.
evt-08-13-1650-george-monck-1st-duke-of-.prompt: What long-term role would this regiment come to play in English history?

choices.text: It became the Coldstream Guards, a regiment still active today
It was disbanded within a year for disloyalty to Cromwell
It later formed the core of the Royal Navy's marine forces
It was absorbed into the New Model Army's cavalry wing

evt-08-13-1650-george-monck-1st-duke-of-.butterflyEffect: Monck's Regiment of Foot became one of the few Commonwealth units retained after the Restoration, evolving into the Coldstream Guards, still one of the British Army's most senior regiments today. Monck's own support for Charles II's return in 1660 made him a key architect of the Restoration itself.

evt-08-13-1704-war-of-the-spanish-succes.scenario: It is 13 August 1704 near the Bavarian village of Blindheim. You are a cavalry officer under the Duke of Marlborough, watching the entrenched French and Bavarian army of Marshal Tallard across the field.
evt-08-13-1704-war-of-the-spanish-succes.prompt: What is Marlborough's key tactical move to break the enemy line?

choices.text: Wait for naval gunfire support from the Rhine
Withdraw to preserve the army for a later campaign
Order a single massed cavalry charge across the whole front
Pin the flanks, then drive a combined infantry-cavalry assault through the weakened center

evt-08-13-1704-war-of-the-spanish-succes.butterflyEffect: The Allied victory shattered French dominance in Europe, saved Vienna from Franco-Bavarian conquest, and became one of the most decisive battles of the century. Marlborough's triumph secured his fame and later Blenheim Palace, granted by a grateful Queen Anne.

evt-08-13-1762-anglo-spanish-war-1762-17.scenario: It is July 1762, and your British force has besieged Havana for five sweltering weeks. Yellow fever has killed more of your men than Spanish cannon fire, but sappers report the Morro Castle's walls are finally close to collapse.

choices.text: Lift the siege and withdraw the fleet immediately
Press the final assault on the weakened fortress
Wait offshore for reinforcements from Jamaica before attacking
Offer the Spanish governor a ransom to avoid further losses

evt-08-13-1762-anglo-spanish-war-1762-17.butterflyEffect: The British pressed the siege, breached the Morro, and forced Havana's surrender on 13 August 1762, seizing an enormous haul of ships and treasure. Britain held the city for less than a year before trading it back to Spain for Florida in the 1763 Treaty of Paris, reshaping the colonial map of North America.

evt-08-13-1868-1868-arica-earthquake.scenario: It is 13 August 1868 off Arica, Peru. You are aboard the shallow-draft USS Wateree, anchored in the harbor, when a massive earthquake strikes and the sea suddenly drains away from the shore.
evt-08-13-1868-1868-arica-earthquake.prompt: What happens to your ship in the tsunami that follows minutes later?

choices.text: It outruns the wave and reaches open sea safely
It sinks at anchor within minutes
It is lifted by the wave and carried nearly two miles inland, landing upright with the crew unharmed
It capsizes offshore with total loss of life

evt-08-13-1868-1868-arica-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The Wateree survived intact, lifted by the wave and deposited nearly two miles inland with her crew unharmed, an almost unbelievable stroke of luck amid a disaster that devastated Arica and sent tsunami waves across the Pacific as far as Hawaii and New Zealand. The stranded ship became a lasting landmark and cautionary tale about tsunami power on shallow coastal vessels.

evt-08-13-1876-das-rheingold.scenario: It is 13 August 1876, and you are seated in Richard Wagner's newly built Festspielhaus in Bayreuth, watching Das Rheingold open the very first complete performance of the Ring cycle he has spent over two decades composing.
evt-08-13-1876-das-rheingold.prompt: What made this premiere historically significant beyond the music itself?

choices.text: It marked Wagner's reconciliation with King Ludwig II after years of estrangement
It was the first performance in a theatre built specifically to stage Wagner's own works
It was the first opera ever performed with electric stage lighting
It was the first Ring performance sung entirely in French

evt-08-13-1876-das-rheingold.butterflyEffect: This was the first time the full Ring des Nibelungen cycle was staged as Wagner intended, in a theatre purpose-built to his specifications with an innovative sunken orchestra pit. The Bayreuth Festival born that summer became an enduring institution and a model for composer-controlled staging that influenced opera production for generations.

evt-08-13-1906-25th-infantry-regiment-un.scenario: It is 13 August 1906 in Brownsville, Texas. Shots have just rung out in town, a bartender lies dead, and suspicion immediately falls on nearby soldiers of the all-Black 25th Infantry Regiment, though many were confined to barracks that night.
evt-08-13-1906-25th-infantry-regiment-un.prompt: How did the Army resolve the accusation against the regiment?

choices.text: Roosevelt ordered mass dishonorable discharges without trial
A military court-martial acquitted the entire regiment
Congress launched a formal inquiry that exonerated the soldiers immediately
The regiment was disbanded and its officers imprisoned

evt-08-13-1906-25th-infantry-regiment-un.butterflyEffect: President Theodore Roosevelt ordered the dishonorable discharge of 167 soldiers without trial after none would confess or implicate others, an act widely condemned as unjust and racially motivated. The Brownsville Affair damaged Roosevelt's standing among Black voters and was not formally corrected until 1972, when the Army reversed the discharges and granted honorable status.

evt-08-13-1918-opha-may-johnson.scenario: It is August 13, 1918, outside Marine Corps Headquarters in Washington, D.C. You are one of hundreds of women who have shown up to answer a wartime call for clerical help, and you are next in line to sign the enlistment papers.
evt-08-13-1918-opha-may-johnson.prompt: What role does signing up as a Marine Reservist actually give you?

choices.text: An honorary title with no actual military duties
A nursing assignment with the Navy Medical Corps
A clerical post in the Marine Corps Reserve to free a man for the front
A combat commission overseas alongside male Marines

evt-08-13-1918-opha-may-johnson.butterflyEffect: Opha May Johnson became the first woman sworn into the Marine Corps Reserve, one of over 300 'Marinettes' who took clerical jobs to free men for combat in France. The wartime Women's Reserve was disbanded after the armistice, but it set the precedent the Corps drew on when it formed the Women's Reserve again in 1943.

evt-08-13-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 13 August 1940, Adlertag. You are a Royal Air Force fighter controller at Group Headquarters as radar plots show waves of German bombers and fighters crossing the Channel to strike southern England.
evt-08-13-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: How should Fighter Command respond to this mass Luftwaffe assault?

choices.text: Mass every fighter over London regardless of the incoming raid's location
Scramble squadrons based on radar-directed interception
Send all available fighters to bomb Luftwaffe airfields in France first
Withdraw squadrons north to preserve them for a later battle

evt-08-13-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Fighter Command used radar tracking and the Observer Corps to scramble squadrons precisely where and when they were needed, conserving aircraft and pilots through the Battle of Britain. This integrated defense held through the summer, forcing Hitler to postpone Operation Sea Lion and delivering Nazi Germany's first major strategic failure of the war.

evt-08-13-1960-central-african-republic.scenario: You stand in Bangui's central square on 13 August 1960 as the French tricolour is lowered and the new republic's flag rises. France's former colony of Ubangi-Shari has just become independent.
evt-08-13-1960-central-african-republic.prompt: Who becomes the Central African Republic's first president after this independence?

choices.text: Jean-Bedel Bokassa
David Dacko
Ange-Félix Patassé
Barthélémy Boganda

evt-08-13-1960-central-african-republic.butterflyEffect: David Dacko, a protégé of the late nationalist leader Barthélémy Boganda, became the country's first president. His rule proved unstable, and in 1966 he was overthrown in a coup by his cousin Jean-Bedel Bokassa, ushering in decades of turbulent, often violent governance.

evt-08-13-1961-berlin-wall.scenario: It is the early hours of 13 August 1961. You live in East Berlin and word spreads that soldiers are stringing barbed wire across streets leading to the West, though the concrete has not yet gone up.
evt-08-13-1961-berlin-wall.prompt: What is an East Berliner's best chance of reaching the West this morning?

choices.text: Apply through the West German embassy for a resettlement visa
Take the S-Bahn train, which will keep running freely between sectors
Try to cross immediately, before the barricades are fully sealed
Wait for the East German government to issue official exit permits

evt-08-13-1961-berlin-wall.butterflyEffect: Thousands did rush the gaps before the barrier hardened, but within days barbed wire was replaced by concrete blocks and the crossing sealed almost completely. The Wall stood for 28 years, splitting families and becoming the era's starkest symbol of the Iron Curtain until its fall in November 1989.

evt-08-13-1968-alexandros-panagoulis.scenario: It is 13 August 1968 on a coastal road near Varkiza, Greece. You are Alexandros Panagoulis, crouched by a hidden explosive device, waiting for the motorcade of military dictator Georgios Papadopoulos to pass.
evt-08-13-1968-alexandros-panagoulis.prompt: What do you do as the dictator's car approaches?

choices.text: Abort and slip away unseen
Signal the guards to negotiate a truce
Detonate the bomb
Wait for a state visit with looser security

evt-08-13-1968-alexandros-panagoulis.butterflyEffect: The bomb failed to kill Papadopoulos, and Panagoulis was captured, tortured, and sentenced to death. International pressure won him a reprieve; after the junta fell in 1974 he was elected to parliament, becoming a symbol of resistance until his death in a 1976 car crash that many still consider suspicious.

evt-08-13-1969-apollo-11.scenario: It is 13 August 1969. You are among the crowds lining the streets of New York City as Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins ride through a ticker-tape parade, having returned safely from the Moon.
evt-08-13-1969-apollo-11.prompt: What did the astronauts do later that same day?

choices.text: Attended a state dinner in Los Angeles hosted by President Nixon
Flew directly to Congress to testify about the mission
Returned immediately to quarantine at the Lunar Receiving Laboratory
Began a worldwide goodwill tour that same night

evt-08-13-1969-apollo-11.butterflyEffect: After parades in New York, Chicago, and Los Angeles that day, the astronauts attended a state dinner in Los Angeles hosted by President Nixon, who awarded them the Presidential Medal of Freedom. The triple celebration cemented Apollo 11 as a national triumph and launched the astronauts into a world tour showcasing American achievement abroad.

evt-08-13-1977-national-front-uk.scenario: It is 13 August 1977 in Lewisham, south London. You are a police officer facing a National Front march through a multiracial neighbourhood, with hundreds of anti-fascist counter-demonstrators blocking the route and hurling bricks.
evt-08-13-1977-national-front-uk.prompt: What tactic do police use for the first time on mainland Britain to hold the line?

choices.text: Tear gas canisters
Water cannons
Armoured vehicles
Riot shields

evt-08-13-1977-national-front-uk.butterflyEffect: Police used riot shields on the British mainland for the first time, and the violent clashes discredited the NF's claim to respectability. Weeks later the Anti-Nazi League formed to counter the far right, and the NF's electoral support collapsed over the following years.

evt-08-13-1999-act-on-national-flag-and-.scenario: It is 13 August 1999 in Japan's Diet chamber. Months after a school principal's suicide amid conflict over mandatory flag-and-anthem ceremonies deepened the debate, you are a lawmaker voting on a bill to legally codify the Hinomaru flag and Kimigayo anthem.

choices.text: The bill fails after opposition lawmakers block it
The bill passes, giving Japan its first legally official flag and anthem
Only the flag is formally adopted, leaving the anthem unofficial
A national referendum is called instead

evt-08-13-1999-act-on-national-flag-and-.butterflyEffect: The law passed without penalties for non-compliance, but schools kept mandating ceremonies, and disputes over teachers' freedom of conscience escalated. Cases over compelled participation eventually reached Japan's Supreme Court in the following decade.

evt-08-13-2004-democratic-republic-of-th.scenario: You are an aid coordinator at the Gatumba refugee camp on the Burundi-DRC border on the night of 13 August 2004, when armed men storm the camp housing Congolese Tutsi refugees.
evt-08-13-2004-democratic-republic-of-th.prompt: Which armed group is blamed for the attack in its immediate aftermath?

choices.text: Mai-Mai militia fighters
The Interahamwe militia
The Rwandan Patriotic Front
The National Liberation Forces (FNL)

evt-08-13-2004-democratic-republic-of-th.butterflyEffect: The Hutu rebel group known as the National Liberation Forces (FNL) was blamed for the assault, though the Congolese government also accused Rwanda and Burundi of complicity. The massacre inflamed regional distrust between Burundi, the DRC, and Rwanda at a fragile moment in Central Africa's peace processes.

evt-08-13-2008-russo-georgian-war.scenario: It is 13 August 2008 in Gori, Georgia, days into the war, as Russian units move into the city despite a ceasefire brokered by French President Nicolas Sarkozy.
evt-08-13-2008-russo-georgian-war.prompt: What do most residents of Gori do as the troops arrive?

choices.text: Take up arms and mount street resistance
Welcome the Russian forces as liberators
Evacuate north into South Ossetia
Flee toward Tbilisi as refugees

evt-08-13-2008-russo-georgian-war.butterflyEffect: Thousands fled Gori, part of a wider exodus as Russian forces briefly occupied swaths of Georgian territory before withdrawing weeks later. The war froze Georgia's NATO ambitions, cemented Russian recognition of South Ossetia and Abkhazia, and foreshadowed Moscow's later interventions in Ukraine.

evt-08-13-2010-mv-sun-sea-incident.scenario: It is August 13, 2010, and your cargo ship, the MV Sun Sea, has just been boarded by Canadian naval and border officers off the coast of British Columbia after weeks at sea carrying Tamil asylum seekers from Sri Lanka.
evt-08-13-2010-mv-sun-sea-incident.prompt: What happens to you and the other passengers next?

choices.text: Deported directly back to Sri Lanka the same week
Granted asylum on the spot with no further review
Released immediately with permanent resident status
Transferred into detention while refugee claims are processed

evt-08-13-2010-mv-sun-sea-incident.butterflyEffect: All 492 passengers were taken into custody and transferred to detention facilities in the Lower Mainland while officials screened them for security concerns and processed refugee claims. The prolonged detentions drew criticism from human rights groups and fed into Canada's 2012 immigration law overhaul, which toughened rules for mass arrivals by sea.

evt-08-13-2020-israel-united-arab-emirat.scenario: It is 13 August 2020, and the White House has just announced that Israel and the United Arab Emirates will normalize relations, brokered with U.S. involvement. You are a diplomat watching decades of quiet, informal contact suddenly become official.
evt-08-13-2020-israel-united-arab-emirat.prompt: What did this normalization directly lead to within weeks?

choices.text: The signing of the Abraham Accords at the White House the following month
Israel's immediate withdrawal from the West Bank
The collapse of the Camp David Accords with Egypt
The UAE joining a military alliance against Iran

evt-08-13-2020-israel-united-arab-emirat.butterflyEffect: The announcement led to the formal signing of the Abraham Accords at the White House on 15 September 1920, with the UAE becoming the first Gulf state to normalize ties with Israel. Bahrain, Sudan, and Morocco followed suit in the months after, reshaping regional diplomacy and trade.

evt-08-14-1720-villasur-expedition.scenario: You are a soldier in Pedro de Villasur's column, camped along the Platte River in present-day Nebraska in August 1720. At dawn, Pawnee and Otoe warriors, allied with French traders, close in on your unguarded camp.
evt-08-14-1720-villasur-expedition.prompt: What happens to the Villasur expedition?
