choices.text: It is ambushed and nearly wiped out, with survivors fleeing back to New Mexico
It defeats the attackers and establishes a permanent fort
It negotiates a treaty with the Pawnee and returns triumphant
It turns back before reaching the Platte, avoiding any conflict

evt-08-14-1720-villasur-expedition.butterflyEffect: The ambush killed Villasur and most of his men, crippling Spain's attempt to check French influence on the northern Plains. French traders remained dominant among the Pawnee and Otoe for decades, and New Mexico's Spanish garrison turned inward, abandoning further ventures onto the Plains.

evt-08-14-1816-tristan-da-cunha.scenario: You are a British naval officer arriving at the remote, barely inhabited islands of Tristan da Cunha in August 1816, with orders to raise the flag and leave a garrison behind.
evt-08-14-1816-tristan-da-cunha.prompt: Why does Britain formally annex this isolated South Atlantic archipelago?

choices.text: To secure a whaling station for the Royal Navy
To claim a coaling station for future steamships
To prevent it being used as a base to help rescue Napoleon from nearby St Helena
To establish a penal colony for Irish rebels

evt-08-14-1816-tristan-da-cunha.butterflyEffect: The garrison stayed on even after Napoleon died on St Helena in 1821, and a handful of soldiers and sailors became the nucleus of a permanent settlement. Tristan da Cunha remains a British Overseas Territory today, one of the most isolated inhabited places on Earth.

evt-08-14-1945-kenji-hatanaka.scenario: You are an officer in Tokyo's Imperial Guard Division on the night of 14-15 August 1945, as Major Kenji Hatanaka urges you to help seize the palace and stop the Emperor's surrender broadcast from airing.
evt-08-14-1945-kenji-hatanaka.prompt: What happens to Hatanaka's coup attempt?

choices.text: It succeeds temporarily until Allied troops intervene
It is called off before it begins due to lack of support
It fails within hours, and the surrender broadcast airs as planned
It succeeds, and the war continues for another year

evt-08-14-1945-kenji-hatanaka.butterflyEffect: Hatanaka failed to win over senior commanders, and once his plot collapsed he took his own life. Hirohito's recorded surrender speech aired on 15 August as scheduled, ending World War II and confirming civilian and imperial control over the surrender process.

evt-08-14-1974-turkish-invasion-of-cypru.scenario: You are a UN peacekeeper near Nicosia in mid-August 1974, watching Turkish forces resume their advance across Cyprus after a brief ceasefire collapses.
evt-08-14-1974-turkish-invasion-of-cypru.prompt: What does the second phase of Turkey's invasion achieve?

choices.text: Greek and Turkish Cypriots agree to immediate reunification
Turkish forces are repelled back to their original beachhead
Turkish forces expand their control to roughly the northern third of the island
Turkish forces withdraw under UN pressure before advancing further

evt-08-14-1974-turkish-invasion-of-cypru.butterflyEffect: The offensive left Cyprus divided along the Green Line, with Turkish Cypriots controlling the north and Greek Cypriots the south. That partition was formalized in 1983 by the unrecognized Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus and remains unresolved decades later.

evt-08-14-1994-carlos-the-jackal.scenario: It's August 14, 1994, and you are a French intelligence operative in Khartoum, Sudan, closing in on a disguised, aging fugitive wanted for a string of bombings and assassinations across Europe in the 1970s and 80s.
evt-08-14-1994-carlos-the-jackal.prompt: What happens to this fugitive, Ilich Ramírez Sánchez, that day?

choices.text: Sudan hands him to French agents, who fly him to Paris for trial
He is assassinated by an Israeli intelligence team
Sudan grants him permanent asylum, refusing extradition
He escapes and is granted asylum in Cuba

evt-08-14-1994-carlos-the-jackal.butterflyEffect: Sudanese authorities handed Carlos over to French agents, who flew him to Paris to face trial. With his Cold War patrons—the Stasi and KGB—gone after the fall of communism, he had lost the protection that once let him operate freely; France convicted him of multiple killings in 1997 and later added more charges tied to 1970s and 80s attacks.

evt-08-14-2003-northeast-blackout-of-200.scenario: It's 4:10 p.m. on 14 August 2003. In an Ohio utility's control room, an alarm system has silently failed while overloaded transmission lines begin tripping one after another across the regional grid.
evt-08-14-2003-northeast-blackout-of-200.prompt: What actually caused the cascading blackout that would darken 50 million people?

choices.text: A failed alarm system let overloaded lines trip unnoticed, cascading through untrimmed tree lines
Utilities deliberately imposed rolling blackouts to conserve fuel during a heat wave
A lightning strike destroyed the main hydroelectric station at Niagara Falls
A terrorist attack disabled a nuclear power plant near Niagara Falls

evt-08-14-2003-northeast-blackout-of-200.butterflyEffect: Investigators found a software bug disabled FirstEnergy's control-room alarms just as sagging lines, uncut by tree-trimming crews, brushed overgrown branches in Ohio, triggering a cascade across the interconnected grid. Congress responded with the Energy Policy Act of 2005, making NERC reliability standards legally enforceable for the first time in North America.

evt-08-14-2005-helios-airways-flight-522.scenario: It's August 14, 2005, and you are the one cabin crew member aboard Helios Airways Flight 522 who holds a private pilot's license, entering the cockpit to find both pilots unconscious from a slow decompression as the plane flies on autopilot over Greece.
evt-08-14-2005-helios-airways-flight-522.prompt: What do you attempt to do as the aircraft nears fuel exhaustion?

choices.text: Try to take manual control and radio air traffic control for help
Shut down both engines to force an emergency descent
Deploy the life rafts in preparation for a water landing
Open the emergency exits to relieve cabin pressure

evt-08-14-2005-helios-airways-flight-522.butterflyEffect: The crew member, Andreas Prodromou, was seen by intercepting Greek F-16s trying to reach the controls, but he had too little time before the engines flamed out and the Boeing 737 crashed near Grammatiko, killing all 121 aboard. Investigators found the pressurization system had been left in manual mode after maintenance, and the pilots misread the warning horn as a takeoff configuration alert—a finding that prompted airlines worldwide to retrain crews on distinguishing pressurization warnings.

evt-08-14-2006-sri-lankan-civil-war.scenario: It is 14 August 2006, and the Sri Lankan Air Force has just carried out an airstrike on a facility at Chencholai in Tamil Tiger-controlled territory, killing dozens of girls housed there.
evt-08-14-2006-sri-lankan-civil-war.prompt: What did the Sri Lankan military claim the target was?

choices.text: A propaganda broadcasting station
A rebel command headquarters
A weapons storage depot
A camp training female LTTE combatants

evt-08-14-2006-sri-lankan-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The LTTE and international human rights observers said the site was a girls' orphanage and vocational training home, not a military target, contradicting the government's account. The bombing drew global condemnation and became one of the incidents later cited in accusations of war crimes during the conflict's final years.

evt-08-14-2013-rabaa-massacre.scenario: It's dawn on August 14, 2013, and you are camped with thousands of supporters of ousted President Mohamed Morsi at Rabaa al-Adawiya Square in Cairo as security forces move to end the six-week sit-in.
evt-08-14-2013-rabaa-massacre.prompt: What happens when the security forces move in that morning?

choices.text: Morsi is released and reinstated as president that day
Forces storm the camps with lethal force, killing hundreds within hours
Protesters voluntarily disperse after a peaceful negotiation
United Nations peacekeepers intervene to separate the two sides

evt-08-14-2013-rabaa-massacre.butterflyEffect: Police and army units cleared both camps with lethal force within hours, killing hundreds of protesters in one of the deadliest single-day crackdowns on demonstrators in modern history. The dispersal deepened Egypt's political polarization, hardened the Muslim Brotherhood's exclusion from politics, and consolidated the authority of Defense Minister Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, who became president the following year.

evt-08-14-2013-egypt.scenario: It is dawn on August 14, 2013, at the Rabaa al-Adawiya sit-in in Cairo. You have camped here for weeks with fellow supporters of ousted President Morsi, and security forces are now massing around the square with orders to clear it.
evt-08-14-2013-egypt.prompt: What follows the security forces' move on the camp?

choices.text: Foreign governments intervene to halt the operation
Negotiators broker a peaceful, voluntary dispersal
The protesters disband and leave before forces arrive
Security forces storm the camps, and hundreds are killed

evt-08-14-2013-egypt.butterflyEffect: Egyptian security forces stormed the Rabaa and Nahda sit-ins, killing hundreds of protesters in one of the deadliest crackdowns in modern Egyptian history, prompting the government to declare a nationwide state of emergency. The violence deepened the country's political split, drew international condemnation, and helped entrench the military-backed government that followed under Abdel Fattah el-Sisi.

evt-08-14-2013-ups-airlines-flight-1354.scenario: It's 4:47 a.m. on August 14, 2013, and you are one of two pilots flying a UPS cargo Airbus A300 into Birmingham, Alabama, on a non-precision approach after a fatiguing overnight duty period.
evt-08-14-2013-ups-airlines-flight-1354.prompt: What critical mistake leads to the crash short of the runway?

choices.text: A bird strike disabling both engines
A landing gear failure during final approach
Running out of fuel before reaching the airport
Descending below the glide path and not aborting despite losing sight of the runway

evt-08-14-2013-ups-airlines-flight-1354.butterflyEffect: The NTSB found the crew descended below the proper glide path and failed to execute a missed approach despite not having the runway in sight, striking trees and terrain short of the airport; both pilots died. Investigators cited pilot fatigue and non-adherence to procedures, reviving debate over why cargo airlines were exempt from the stricter rest rules imposed on passenger carriers after 2011.

evt-08-14-2015-embassy-of-the-united-sta.scenario: It's August 14, 2015, and you watch as Secretary of State John Kerry arrives in Havana, the first U.S. Secretary of State to visit in 70 years, ready to raise the flag over a building shuttered since 1961.
evt-08-14-2015-embassy-of-the-united-sta.prompt: What historic step does this ceremony mark in U.S.-Cuba relations?

choices.text: Kerry expels Cuba's diplomats from Washington
Kerry formally reopens the embassy, restoring full diplomatic relations
Kerry announces the reimposition of the full trade embargo
Kerry declares that Guantanamo Bay will be returned to Cuba

evt-08-14-2015-embassy-of-the-united-sta.butterflyEffect: Kerry formally reopened the U.S. Embassy in Havana, completing the restoration of full diplomatic relations that Obama and Raúl Castro had announced the previous December. It capped decades of Cold War estrangement, though later tensions over alleged 'Havana Syndrome' attacks and policy reversals under Trump would limit how far the thaw actually went.

evt-08-14-2021-2021-haiti-earthquake.scenario: It's the morning of August 14, 2021, and you are a local official near Petit-Trou-de-Nippes on Haiti's Tiburon Peninsula as a violent magnitude 7.2 earthquake collapses homes across the Sud Department.
evt-08-14-2021-2021-haiti-earthquake.prompt: What must you organize immediately in the hours after the quake?

choices.text: Prioritize rebuilding tourist infrastructure along the coast
Focus resources on Port-au-Prince, since the epicenter was there
Wait for insurance assessors before allowing any rescue operations
Coordinate search-and-rescue teams and route medical aid to the hardest-hit areas

evt-08-14-2021-2021-haiti-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Rescue teams struggled to reach the remote peninsula as roads and bridges were damaged, and Tropical Storm Grace struck just two days later, hampering relief efforts further. The disaster strained Haiti's already fragile government, which was reeling from President Jovenel Moïse's assassination weeks earlier, complicating the international response.

evt-08-14-2023-donald-trump.scenario: You are a Fulton County grand juror in August 2023, reviewing evidence of efforts to overturn Georgia's 2020 election results, including a recorded phone call pressuring the secretary of state.
evt-08-14-2023-donald-trump.prompt: What charges does the grand jury bring against Trump and his co-defendants?

choices.text: Charges of mishandling classified documents
Racketeering (RICO) conspiracy charges tied to election interference
Charges of campaign finance violations
Federal charges of inciting insurrection

evt-08-14-2023-donald-trump.butterflyEffect: The Georgia indictment charged Trump and 18 co-defendants under the state's racketeering statute, making it one of four criminal cases filed against him in 2023 and the only one focused on Georgia's 2020 vote count. The case became mired in years of pretrial disputes over prosecutor conduct and venue.

evt-08-15-718-umayyad-caliphate.scenario: It is August 718, and you are an Umayyad commander camped outside Constantinople's walls after a year of siege, your army ravaged by Greek fire, Bulgar attacks, disease, and a brutal winter.
evt-08-15-718-umayyad-caliphate.prompt: What does the Umayyad army do this month?

choices.text: Storm the city with newly arrived Bulgar allies
Abandon the siege and withdraw, having failed to take the city
Launch a final assault that breaches the walls
Negotiate a truce that hands over the city

evt-08-15-718-umayyad-caliphate.butterflyEffect: The Umayyads abandoned the siege and withdrew, their retreating fleet further battered by storms and Byzantine Greek fire. The failure marked the high-water mark of Arab expansion toward Europe and preserved Constantinople as a Christian bulwark for centuries to come.

evt-08-15-1261-michael-viii-palaiologos.scenario: It is late July 1261, and you command a small Nicaean detachment that has found Constantinople's gates left almost undefended while the Latin garrison and Venetian fleet are away on a raid.
evt-08-15-1261-michael-viii-palaiologos.prompt: What should you do with the city so lightly guarded?

choices.text: Burn the city to keep it from Latin hands
Offer a truce to the absent Latin emperor
Seize the city at once and send word to Michael VIII
Wait outside until the full Nicaean army arrives

evt-08-15-1261-michael-viii-palaiologos.butterflyEffect: General Alexios Strategopoulos seized Constantinople with almost no bloodshed, and Michael VIII Palaiologos entered in triumph, being crowned in Hagia Sophia soon after. This ended 57 years of Latin rule, restored the Byzantine Empire, and founded the Palaiologan dynasty that would govern until the city's fall in 1453.

evt-08-15-1812-war-of-1812.scenario: You are Captain Nathan Heald at Fort Dearborn in August 1812, ordered to evacuate the garrison and settlers toward Fort Wayne. Potawatomi escorts have been promised the fort's supplies in return for safe passage.
evt-08-15-1812-war-of-1812.prompt: What did Heald order destroyed before the march, angering the waiting Potawatomi?

choices.text: The settlers' personal livestock
The fort's surplus weapons, gunpowder, and whiskey
The fort's buildings and stockade walls
The fort's entire food stores

evt-08-15-1812-war-of-1812.butterflyEffect: Heald had the surplus muskets, gunpowder, and whiskey destroyed or dumped rather than handed over as promised. Shortly after the column departed, Potawatomi warriors attacked it near the lakeshore, killing most of the soldiers and several settlers in what became known as the Fort Dearborn Massacre, a disaster that fueled American resolve in the wider war.

evt-08-15-1909-goudi-coup.scenario: You are a junior officer gathered with the Military League at the Goudi barracks outside Athens on the night of 15 August 1909, frustrated by a stagnant government and an unmodernized army.
evt-08-15-1909-goudi-coup.prompt: What did the officers demand from the government and the king?

choices.text: A military alliance with Bulgaria against Serbia
Resignation of the government and reform of the armed forces
An immediate declaration of war on the Ottoman Empire
Abolition of the monarchy and creation of a republic

evt-08-15-1909-goudi-coup.butterflyEffect: The League forced the government's resignation and pressed for sweeping military and political reform without abolishing the monarchy. The crisis led to the recall of Cretan politician Eleftherios Venizelos to Athens, who became prime minister in 1910 and launched a era of modernization that reshaped Greek politics for decades.

evt-08-15-1941-deportation-of-soviet-ger.scenario: It is August 1941, and you are an ethnic German farmer in Crimea. German troops have invaded the Soviet Union, and NKVD officers arrive at your village with orders from Moscow, giving your family only days to prepare.
evt-08-15-1941-deportation-of-soviet-ger.prompt: What does the Soviet decree order for Crimea's ethnic Germans?

choices.text: They are placed under local surveillance but allowed to stay
They are conscripted directly into the Red Army
They are exchanged with Germany for Soviet prisoners of war
They are deported to special settlements in Kazakhstan and Siberia

evt-08-15-1941-deportation-of-soviet-ger.butterflyEffect: The decree, soon extended to all Soviet Germans, sent hundreds of thousands to special settlements and forced labor camps in Kazakhstan and Siberia; the Volga German Autonomous Republic was abolished entirely. At least 228,800 deportees are estimated to have died, and the community was never permitted to return to its former homelands after the war.

evt-08-15-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is dawn on 15 August 1944, and you are wading ashore with Allied forces along the beaches of Provence as Operation Dragoon begins, months after the Normandy landings.
evt-08-15-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What is this southern invasion meant to achieve?

choices.text: Cut off the German retreat from Normandy
Secure the ports of Marseille and Toulon to speed Allied supply lines
Support Soviet advances into the Balkans
Open a direct route to Berlin through the Alps

evt-08-15-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Allied troops swiftly captured the vital ports of Marseille and Toulon, opening a much-needed supply route and driving German forces up the Rhône valley. The rapid advance linked with Allied armies from Normandy weeks later, hastening the full liberation of France.

evt-08-15-1947-partition-of-india.scenario: It is mid-August 1947. You are a minor official tasked with splitting British India's army, railways, and treasury between two new dominions, along a border drawn by a commission that never visited the provinces it divided.
evt-08-15-1947-partition-of-india.prompt: What crisis unfolds across Punjab and Bengal in the weeks after independence?

choices.text: British administrators remain in charge of both dominions until 1950
All princely states merge into the two dominions within days without incident
Millions are displaced as they cross the new borders amid communal violence
The transfer of assets and territory proceeds smoothly with no unrest

evt-08-15-1947-partition-of-india.butterflyEffect: Between 12 and 20 million people crossed the new borders in one of history's largest migrations, accompanied by widespread communal violence between Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs. The upheaval still shapes the politics, borders, and rivalries of India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh today.

evt-08-15-1963-fulbert-youlou.scenario: You are a trade unionist in Brazzaville during "Les Trois Glorieuses," three days of mass demonstrations in August 1963, as crowds fill the streets demanding President Fulbert Youlou's resignation.
evt-08-15-1963-fulbert-youlou.prompt: What happened to Youlou as a direct result of the uprising?

choices.text: He was re-elected to a new term shortly after
He was assassinated by demonstrators
He crushed the uprising with military force
He was forced to resign and fled into exile

evt-08-15-1963-fulbert-youlou.butterflyEffect: Youlou resigned under pressure and went into exile, ending Congo-Brazzaville's first presidency. Alphonse Massemba-Débat succeeded him, steering the country toward one-party socialist rule under the National Revolutionary Movement, setting the pattern for decades of instability and shifting alliances in Congolese politics.

evt-08-15-1977-ohio-state-university-rad.scenario: You are a volunteer astronomer reviewing computer printouts from Ohio State's Big Ear radio telescope on the night of 15 August 1977, when a 72-second burst far stronger than background noise appears on the page.
evt-08-15-1977-ohio-state-university-rad.prompt: What did the astronomer reviewing the data famously do?

choices.text: Shut down the telescope for a full recalibration
Immediately announced contact with aliens to the press
Discarded the printout as a routine equipment glitch
Circled the reading on the printout and wrote "Wow!" beside it

evt-08-15-1977-ohio-state-university-rad.butterflyEffect: Jerry Ehman circled the anomalous reading and wrote "Wow!" in the margin, giving the signal its enduring name. Despite decades of follow-up observations, it has never been detected again, and it remains one of the strongest candidate signals in SETI history, fueling continued searches for extraterrestrial radio transmissions.

evt-08-15-1998-the-troubles.scenario: It is Saturday, 15 August 1998, market day in Omagh town centre. A telephoned warning about a car bomb has just come in, but the caller gave the wrong location, and police are moving shoppers toward what they believe is safety.
evt-08-15-1998-the-troubles.prompt: What did the Real IRA do in the days after the bombing's public outrage?

choices.text: They escalated their bombing campaign across Britain
They formally merged back into the Provisional IRA
They declared a ceasefire under intense public pressure
They immediately disbanded as an organisation

evt-08-15-1998-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The bomb killed 29 people, including a woman pregnant with twins, and injured over 220. The scale of public revulsion, in both Ireland and Britain, forced the Real IRA to announce a ceasefire just three days later, and the atrocity became a defining argument for why the Good Friday Agreement's peace process had to hold.

evt-08-15-1998-northern-ireland.scenario: It's a busy Saturday afternoon in Omagh town centre. A coded warning about a car bomb has just come through, but the location given sends police moving shoppers toward the device rather than away from it.
evt-08-15-1998-northern-ireland.prompt: What follows for the peace process after the bomb detonates minutes later?

choices.text: Police evacuate the area in time and the device is safely defused
The bomb fails to detonate due to a technical fault
Only property is damaged, with no serious casualties
It becomes the deadliest single bombing of the Troubles, and outrage strengthens support for the peace deal

evt-08-15-1998-northern-ireland.butterflyEffect: The Real IRA, a dissident republican splinter group opposed to the Good Friday Agreement signed months earlier, claimed responsibility. Public revulsion at the attack isolated paramilitary hardliners and strengthened cross-community support for the peace settlement rather than derailing it.

evt-08-15-1998-apple-inc.scenario: It is August 1998 and you run a computer store deciding whether to stock Apple's strange new all-in-one machine — a candy-colored translucent case with no floppy disk slot at all.
evt-08-15-1998-apple-inc.prompt: What radical decision did Apple make with the iMac's connectors?

choices.text: It added a built-in floppy drive as its main storage
It shipped without any ports, using wireless only
It kept the older SCSI and serial ports for compatibility
It used only USB ports and abandoned the floppy drive

evt-08-15-1998-apple-inc.butterflyEffect: The iMac dropped legacy ports like SCSI and the floppy drive entirely, betting everything on the then-obscure USB standard. Peripheral makers scrambled to build USB devices, the format became the industry norm within a few years, and the iMac's runaway sales pulled Apple back from the brink of bankruptcy, setting up the iPod and iPhone era.

evt-08-15-2005-free-aceh-movement.scenario: You are a Free Aceh Movement negotiator in Helsinki in August 2005, months after the tsunami devastated your homeland and killed tens of thousands, sitting across from Indonesian government envoys to end nearly three decades of war.
evt-08-15-2005-free-aceh-movement.prompt: What did GAM ultimately agree to accept in exchange for ending the insurgency?

choices.text: Special autonomy for Aceh within Indonesia
Continued armed resistance under UN protection
Full independence as a separate state
A federation merging Aceh with Malaysia

evt-08-15-2005-free-aceh-movement.butterflyEffect: GAM dropped its demand for full independence in exchange for special autonomy and the right to form local political parties. It disarmed and transformed into the Aceh Party, and the province has remained largely peaceful since, governed under its own Sharia-influenced regional laws.

evt-08-15-2005-israeli-disengagement-fro.scenario: You are an Israeli soldier ordered into the Gush Katif settlements in the Gaza Strip in August 2005, tasked with carrying out the government's disengagement plan among residents who refuse to leave voluntarily.
evt-08-15-2005-israeli-disengagement-fro.prompt: What was your unit ordered to do under the disengagement plan?

choices.text: Remove settlers by force if necessary and dismantle the settlements
Negotiate directly with Hamas over the settlements' future
Expand the settlements to strengthen Israel's claim to the land
Reinforce the settlements against Palestinian attacks

evt-08-15-2005-israeli-disengagement-fro.butterflyEffect: Israeli forces evacuated settlers and dismantled all 21 settlements in the Gaza Strip, ending the Israeli civilian presence there. Israel retained control over Gaza's borders, airspace, and coastline, so many international bodies still considered it occupied; the following years saw Hamas's 2006 election win and 2007 takeover, leading to a blockade and recurring conflict.

evt-08-15-2007-2007-peru-earthquake.scenario: It is the evening of 15 August 2007 and you are in Ica, Peru, when the ground begins to shake violently and does not stop for nearly two minutes.
evt-08-15-2007-2007-peru-earthquake.prompt: What is the safest immediate action as the shaking continues?

choices.text: Run immediately to the nearest coastline to watch for a tsunami
Move away from buildings to open ground until the shaking stops
Stay in a doorway on an upper floor of a tall building
Take the elevator to the ground floor as quickly as possible

evt-08-15-2007-2007-peru-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The magnitude 8.0 quake killed at least 595 people and injured thousands, collapsing adobe and poorly reinforced buildings across Ica and nearby regions. The disaster exposed weak construction standards in Peru and spurred renewed government efforts to enforce stricter building codes and improve disaster response in coastal cities.

evt-08-15-2013-smithsonian-institution.scenario: It is August 2013, and you are a Smithsonian zoologist who has spent years re-examining museum specimens long misfiled as olingos, cross-checking them against new field observations from Andean cloud forests.
evt-08-15-2013-smithsonian-institution.prompt: What do you announce to the world?

choices.text: A genetic reclassification of the giant panda
The rediscovery of a species thought extinct
A new subspecies of red panda
The discovery of the olinguito, a new carnivore species

evt-08-15-2013-smithsonian-institution.butterflyEffect: The team unveiled the olinguito, the first new carnivore species described in the Americas in 35 years, native to the cloud forests of Colombia and Ecuador. The discovery showcased how old museum collections combined with modern genetics could reveal overlooked species, and drew fresh conservation attention to its shrinking habitat.

evt-08-15-2015-north-korea.scenario: On 15 August 2015, the 70th anniversary of liberation from Japanese rule, North Korean state media announces that the nation's clocks will be set back by thirty minutes.
evt-08-15-2015-north-korea.prompt: What reason does Pyongyang give for creating this new half-hour time zone?

choices.text: To match a proposed reunification calendar with South Korea
To align with Beijing time for easier trade with China
To conserve electricity during a national energy shortage
To cast off the time zone imposed by Japanese colonial rule

evt-08-15-2015-north-korea.butterflyEffect: "Pyongyang Time" restored the meridian used before Japan standardized Korean time in 1912, framed as shedding a colonial legacy. North Korea quietly abandoned the experiment in 2018, resetting clocks to match South Korea as a goodwill gesture ahead of inter-Korean summits.

evt-08-15-2020-sputnik-v-covid-19-vaccin.scenario: You are a Russian health ministry official on 15 August 2020, tasked with starting mass production of Sputnik V, even though the vaccine's Phase 3 trial has not yet been completed.
evt-08-15-2020-sputnik-v-covid-19-vaccin.prompt: What was the main criticism international scientists raised about Sputnik V at this point?

choices.text: It was developed entirely without state funding
It was banned for use within Russia itself
It was approved before Phase 3 trials were completed
It had never been tested in animal trials

evt-08-15-2020-sputnik-v-covid-19-vaccin.butterflyEffect: Sputnik V was approved and put into production before Phase 3 trial data existed, drawing sharp criticism from Western scientists over safety and transparency. Full Phase 3 results published later in The Lancet showed roughly 91.6% efficacy, and the vaccine went on to be used widely in countries with limited access to Western-made vaccines, though slow WHO approval restricted its broader global rollout.

evt-08-15-2021-kabul.scenario: It's 15 August 2021. You're inside the fortified U.S. embassy compound in Kabul as radio traffic reports Taliban fighters entering the city without resistance from government forces.
evt-08-15-2021-kabul.prompt: What does President Ashraf Ghani's government do in these final hours?

choices.text: NATO reinforcements arrive to retake the city and restore the government
Ghani flees the country as the government dissolves
Ghani rallies remaining army units for a last stand in the capital
Parliament transfers power to a caretaker military council

evt-08-15-2021-kabul.butterflyEffect: Ghani's flight triggered the immediate collapse of the Western-backed government, and the Taliban swiftly declared the restoration of their Islamic Emirate. The chaotic evacuation that followed at Kabul airport became a defining image of the war's end and reshaped debates over the costs of the twenty-year intervention.

evt-08-16-1513-war-of-the-league-of-camb.scenario: It is 16 August 1513 near Guinegate. You ride with the French cavalry as English and Imperial guns open up, and your officers must decide whether to hold the line or wheel away.
evt-08-16-1513-war-of-the-league-of-camb.prompt: What actually happens to the French cavalry under fire?

choices.text: They hold firm and repel the English and Imperial advance
They surrender en masse without firing a shot
They break formation and flee in a headlong, humiliating retreat
They launch a successful counter-charge that wins the field

evt-08-16-1513-war-of-the-league-of-camb.butterflyEffect: The French horsemen broke and fled so fast that the clash became known as the Battle of the Spurs. The humiliating rout boosted young Henry VIII's martial reputation early in his reign and strengthened the Anglo-Imperial alliance against France in the ongoing Italian Wars.

evt-08-16-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 16 August 1777 near Bennington. You serve under General John Stark, facing a detachment of British and German troops sent by Burgoyne to seize badly needed supplies.
evt-08-16-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What happened when Stark's militia engaged the British and German force?

choices.text: The British force broke through and seized the supplies at Bennington
Stark's militia decisively routed the British and German troops
Stark's men retreated after running low on ammunition
Both sides fought to a stalemate and withdrew

evt-08-16-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Stark's militia routed the British and Brunswick troops, capturing many and denying Burgoyne critical supplies and reinforcements. The defeat weakened Burgoyne's campaign and contributed directly to his surrender at Saratoga two months later, a turning point that helped bring France into the war on the American side.

evt-08-16-1819-cavalry.scenario: It is 16 August 1819 at St Peter's Field in Manchester. You stand among tens of thousands gathered peacefully to demand parliamentary reform when mounted yeomanry and cavalry are ordered to advance into the crowd.
evt-08-16-1819-cavalry.prompt: What happened when the cavalry charged into the reform meeting?

choices.text: They fired warning shots into the air and the crowd dispersed unharmed
The crowd overpowered the cavalry and drove them off the field
Local magistrates intervened and halted the charge before it began
They killed around 15 people and injured hundreds in the crowd

evt-08-16-1819-cavalry.butterflyEffect: The charge killed around 15 people and injured hundreds, becoming known as the Peterloo Massacre. Public outrage helped found the Manchester Guardian and, despite the government's repressive Six Acts, fed a longer campaign that culminated in the Reform Act of 1832.

evt-08-16-1837-daaga.scenario: It's 1837 at the St. Joseph barracks in Trinidad. You are one of the African-born recruits of the 1st West India Regiment, taken from a slave ship and drilled under officers who still treat you like the enslaved men you were rescued from becoming.
evt-08-16-1837-daaga.prompt: What does Daaga lead his fellow soldiers to do?

choices.text: Submit a formal written petition to the governor
Desert quietly into the surrounding forest
Rise up in armed mutiny against their officers
Refuse orders while remaining peacefully in the barracks

evt-08-16-1837-daaga.butterflyEffect: The mutiny was crushed within hours, and Daaga and two other ringleaders were court-martialed and executed by firing squad. The uprising exposed the brutal treatment of African recruits in the West India Regiments and fed into later debates over how liberated Africans were incorporated into British colonial forces.

evt-08-16-1891-san-sebastian-church-mani.scenario: You are the architect planning a new church for Manila in the 1880s, in a city repeatedly leveled by earthquakes and fires. Belgian foundries can prefabricate an entire building frame and ship it across the ocean.
evt-08-16-1891-san-sebastian-church-mani.prompt: What structural material do you choose for the church's frame?

choices.text: Reinforced concrete poured on site
Heavy timber framing in the local style
Traditional stone and coral block masonry
Prefabricated steel and iron panels bolted together on site

evt-08-16-1891-san-sebastian-church-mani.butterflyEffect: The church was built almost entirely of prefabricated steel shipped from Belgium and consecrated on 16 August 1891, making it one of the only all-steel churches in Asia. Its metal skeleton let it withstand earthquakes that had destroyed earlier masonry churches, and it was later declared a National Historical Landmark of the Philippines.

evt-08-16-1896-george-carmack.scenario: It is August 1896 and you are panning gravel along Bonanza Creek in the Yukon with George Carmack, Skookum Jim Mason, and Dawson Charlie. Your pan suddenly fills with coarse gold flakes.
evt-08-16-1896-george-carmack.prompt: What do you do immediately after finding the gold?

choices.text: Stake a discovery claim on the spot before telling anyone else
Keep the find secret and quietly mine it alone
Sell the rights to a mining company immediately
Travel to Ottawa first to register the claim with officials

evt-08-16-1896-george-carmack.butterflyEffect: The party staked the Discovery Claim, and word of the find spread to the outside world within months, igniting the Klondike Gold Rush. Tens of thousands of prospectors poured into the Yukon over the following two years, transforming Dawson City into a boomtown and reshaping the region's economy and Indigenous communities.

evt-08-16-1906-1906-valparaiso-earthquak.scenario: It is 7:55 pm on 16 August 1906 in Valparaíso, Chile. The ground beneath your feet begins to heave violently as masonry walls around you start to crack, just half an hour after a massive quake struck far away near Alaska.
evt-08-16-1906-1906-valparaiso-earthquak.prompt: What do you do in the first seconds of the shaking to protect yourself?

choices.text: Head toward the harbor to board a ship immediately
Run into the open street, away from walls and balconies
Climb to the rooftop to signal for help
Stay inside and shelter under a heavy wooden table

evt-08-16-1906-1906-valparaiso-earthquak.butterflyEffect: The 8.2 Mw quake devastated much of Valparaíso, causing widespread destruction and heavy loss of life along Chile's central coast. The disaster pushed Chilean authorities toward stricter building codes and renewed the country's ongoing effort to build seismic resilience into its growing port cities.

evt-08-16-1920-battle-of-radzymin-1920.scenario: It is 16 August 1920 near Radzymin, just northeast of Warsaw. Soviet forces are pressing hard toward the Polish capital, and you are among the defenders holding the line.
evt-08-16-1920-battle-of-radzymin-1920.prompt: What was the outcome of the fighting at Radzymin?

choices.text: Polish forces abandoned the position and retreated toward Krakow
Both sides withdrew and the front stabilized without a clear victor
Soviet forces broke through and captured Warsaw days later
Polish forces repelled the Soviet assault, helping turn back the advance on Warsaw

evt-08-16-1920-battle-of-radzymin-1920.butterflyEffect: Polish forces held and repelled the Soviet assault, a key part of the broader Battle of Warsaw that became known as the 'Miracle at the Vistula.' The victory halted the Red Army's westward advance and secured Polish independence for the interwar period.

evt-08-16-1920-blind-persons-act-1920.scenario: It's April 1920, and you've just finished a three-week march from Manchester to London with the National League of the Blind, demanding a state pension because so many blind workers live in poverty. Parliament has agreed to debate a bill in response.
evt-08-16-1920-blind-persons-act-1920.prompt: At what age can blind claimants start receiving the new pension once the bill becomes law?
evt-08-16-1920-blind-persons-act-1920.butterflyEffect: The Blind Persons Act received royal assent on 16 August 1920, granting pensions from age 50 and ordering local authorities to provide for blind welfare — Britain's first disability-specific welfare law. Its pension clause was later folded into the Old Age Pensions Act 1936 and the rest into the National Assistance Act 1948, though it still stands in Ireland.

evt-08-16-1920-ray-chapman.scenario: It's the fifth inning at the Polo Grounds on 16 August 1920. You are Cleveland shortstop Ray Chapman, crowding the plate as usual against Yankees submarine-style pitcher Carl Mays, unable to pick up the scuffed, darkened ball in the fading light.
evt-08-16-1920-ray-chapman.prompt: What follows when Mays's pitch strikes Chapman in the head?

choices.text: He hits a home run on the very next pitch
He collapses at the plate and dies from the injury the following day
He is ejected for charging the mound
He shakes off the hit and stays in the game

evt-08-16-1920-ray-chapman.butterflyEffect: Chapman collapsed and died the next morning, the only fatality from an in-game injury in Major League Baseball history. The tragedy pushed umpires to keep clean, visible balls in play and helped end the spitball era, laying groundwork for the batting helmets introduced decades later.

evt-08-16-1929-western-wall.scenario: You are a Jewish worshipper at the Western Wall on 16 August 1929, the day after young Jewish nationalists staged a demonstration there. A large crowd is now pouring out of Friday prayers on the Temple Mount above, angry at what they see as a threat to Muslim rights over the site.
evt-08-16-1929-western-wall.prompt: What is your best chance of getting through the next few minutes unharmed?

choices.text: Flee the plaza as the crowd surges in
Begin negotiating with religious leaders on the spot
Call for British reinforcements with a bugle
Stand your ground and confront the crowd

evt-08-16-1929-western-wall.butterflyEffect: The crowd attacked worshippers at the Wall, tearing up prayer books and beating people, an incident that helped ignite the wider Palestine riots that erupted a week later. Violence spread to Hebron and Safed, killing roughly 133 Jews and 116 Arabs, and the British response — the Shaw Commission and later the Passfield White Paper — restricted Jewish immigration, deepening Arab-Jewish mistrust for years.

evt-08-16-1945-stanley-internment-camp.scenario: It is mid-August 1945 inside Stanley Internment Camp, Hong Kong. Word has reached the compound that Japan has surrendered, but no Allied forces have yet arrived to take formal control.
evt-08-16-1945-stanley-internment-camp.prompt: What did the senior internees do as liberation approached?

choices.text: They fled the camp en masse into the countryside
They staged an armed uprising against the remaining guards
They waited and moved to reassert British colonial administration pending Allied arrival
They negotiated directly with Chinese Nationalist forces for control of the colony

evt-08-16-1945-stanley-internment-camp.butterflyEffect: Franklin Gimson, the senior colonial official held in the camp, proclaimed the resumption of British civil administration even before Allied forces formally arrived, helping to re-establish British authority in Hong Kong ahead of Japan's official surrender on 2 September 1945.

evt-08-16-1946-direct-action-day.scenario: It is 16 August 1946 in Calcutta. The Muslim League has called for a general strike demanding a separate homeland, and tensions between communities are boiling over in the streets.
evt-08-16-1946-direct-action-day.prompt: What actually followed the Muslim League's Direct Action Day call in Calcutta?

choices.text: It triggered days of severe communal rioting and killing across the city
British troops dispersed crowds before any unrest began
Hindu and Muslim leaders reached an immediate truce that day
It passed as a peaceful, orderly strike with no violence

evt-08-16-1946-direct-action-day.butterflyEffect: The strike collapsed into days of brutal Hindu-Muslim violence known as the Great Calcutta Killings, leaving thousands dead. The bloodshed deepened communal mistrust across Bengal and is widely seen as a grim precursor to the mass violence that accompanied Partition the following year.

evt-08-16-1962-the-beatles.scenario: You are drummer Pete Best, summoned into manager Brian Epstein's Liverpool office on 16 August 1962 with no explanation given beforehand.
evt-08-16-1962-the-beatles.prompt: What does Epstein tell you is happening to your place in the Beatles?

choices.text: You're being replaced as drummer
You're being promoted to co-manager
You must switch to bass guitar
The band is disbanding

evt-08-16-1962-the-beatles.butterflyEffect: Epstein fired Best that day, and Ringo Starr — already friendly with Lennon and McCartney from the Merseyside club circuit — joined within days. Ringo's steady playing and easy charm became central to the band's chemistry and Beatlemania, while Best, despite his years on stage with them, never played with a major band again.

evt-08-16-1977-elvis-presley.scenario: It is the morning of 16 August 1977 at Graceland. You are part of Elvis Presley's household staff and you have just found him unresponsive on the bathroom floor.
evt-08-16-1977-elvis-presley.prompt: What is the first thing you do?

choices.text: Wait for his personal physician to arrive first
Try to revive him yourself before telling anyone
Contact the record label before calling for help
Call for emergency medical help immediately

evt-08-16-1977-elvis-presley.butterflyEffect: Elvis was rushed to Baptist Memorial Hospital in Memphis, where he was pronounced dead; the official cause was later given as cardiac arrhythmia linked to prescription drug use. His death triggered a global outpouring of grief, cemented Graceland as a pilgrimage site, and fueled decades of conspiracy theories and tribute culture.

evt-08-16-1986-typhoon-wayne-1986.scenario: You are a duty forecaster at Hong Kong's Royal Observatory in late August 1986, tracking Typhoon Wayne as it loops erratically through the South China Sea instead of moving off in one direction.
evt-08-16-1986-typhoon-wayne-1986.prompt: What unusual step must you take because of Wayne's repeated approaches toward Hong Kong?

choices.text: Issue only one signal for the entire event
Refuse to issue any signal since the storm keeps leaving
Wait until landfall to issue any warning
Raise tropical cyclone warning signals three separate times

evt-08-16-1986-typhoon-wayne-1986.butterflyEffect: Wayne's bizarre 21-day track made it one of the longest-lived tropical cyclones on record, forcing Hong Kong to raise and lower its storm signals three separate times. The storm killed 490 people and caused US$399 million in damage across the Philippines, Taiwan, China, Hainan and Vietnam, and its behaviour became a case study in how storms can stall inside a monsoon trough.

evt-08-16-2012-south-african-police-serv.scenario: It is 16 August 2012 at the Lonmin platinum mine near Marikana. You command a line of police facing thousands of striking miners armed with machetes and traditional weapons who refuse to disperse.
evt-08-16-2012-south-african-police-serv.prompt: What order do you give as the miners advance and refuse to lay down arms?

choices.text: Use only tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse them
Order live ammunition fired into the advancing crowd
Withdraw the line and open wage negotiations on the spot
Call for unarmed mediators from the union to intervene first

evt-08-16-2012-south-african-police-serv.butterflyEffect: Police opened fire, killing 34 miners and wounding 78 more in the bloodiest use of force by South African security since apartheid. The Marikana massacre triggered the Farlam Commission, exposed brutal conditions in the platinum sector, and became a lasting symbol of unfinished promises of post-apartheid justice.

evt-08-16-2013-mv-st-thomas-aquinas.scenario: You are a passenger aboard the ferry St. Thomas Aquinas on the night of 16 August 2013 when it collides with the cargo ship Sulpicio Express Siete in the Mactan Channel near Cebu, and the deck beneath you begins to tilt.
evt-08-16-2013-mv-st-thomas-aquinas.prompt: What is your best chance of survival in the minutes after the collision?

choices.text: Stay below deck and wait for crew instructions
Try to swim to Cebu city, miles away
Get to open deck, jump clear, and wait to be pulled from the water
Remain in your cabin to avoid the chaos

evt-08-16-2013-mv-st-thomas-aquinas.butterflyEffect: Of roughly 870 people aboard, 733 were pulled from the water by nearby boats and coast guard crews that reached the scene within minutes, but 108 died and 29 were never found. The disaster triggered a Philippine Coast Guard inquiry into vessel traffic in the crowded Mactan Channel and renewed pressure to tighten ferry safety enforcement nationwide.

evt-08-16-2015-trigana-air-flight-267.scenario: You are the pilot of Trigana Air Flight 267 on approach to Oksibil airstrip on 16 August 2015. Thick cloud is closing over the surrounding mountains of Papua's interior, obscuring the runway ahead.
evt-08-16-2015-trigana-air-flight-267.prompt: What should you do as visibility drops near the mountainous approach?

choices.text: Continue the visual approach as originally planned
Descend below the minimum safe altitude to get under the clouds
Speed up the descent to land before the cloud fully closes in
Abort the approach and hold or divert until visibility clears

evt-08-16-2015-trigana-air-flight-267.butterflyEffect: The ATR 42 continued its descent in poor visibility and struck high terrain short of the runway, killing everyone aboard. The crash renewed scrutiny of safety standards among Indonesia's regional carriers operating into remote, mountain-ringed airstrips with limited instrument approach infrastructure.

evt-08-16-2020-august-complex-fire.scenario: It is late August 2020, and you're a fire commander in Northern California watching dozens of lightning-sparked blazes merge across the Coast Range into one sprawling front.
evt-08-16-2020-august-complex-fire.prompt: What ultimately happened to this fire complex by the time it was contained?

choices.text: It became the largest wildfire complex in California's recorded history
It was fully contained within a week without major spread
It was extinguished by early September rains
It merged into a single fire smaller than the 2018 Mendocino Complex

evt-08-16-2020-august-complex-fire.butterflyEffect: The Doe Fire and its neighbors merged into the largest single wildfire complex in California history, burning over one million acres before being extinguished in November. It became the first 'gigafire' recorded in the modern era and intensified debate over forest management and climate-driven fire seasons.

evt-08-17-986-byzantine-bulgarian-wars.scenario: You march with Emperor Basil II's Byzantine army as it retreats through a narrow mountain pass in the Balkans in August 986, after abandoning a failed siege of Sofia.
evt-08-17-986-byzantine-bulgarian-wars.prompt: What did the Bulgarian forces under Samuel do to the retreating Byzantine column?

choices.text: They met the Byzantines in open cavalry battle on the plain
They besieged only the rear guard while letting the main force pass
They ambushed the column in the narrow gorge, trapping and slaughtering the soldiers
They blockaded the army's supply ships along the coast

evt-08-17-986-byzantine-bulgarian-wars.butterflyEffect: At the Battle of the Gates of Trajan, Bulgarian forces ambushed the trapped Byzantine army in the gorge, inflicting a devastating defeat from which Basil II barely escaped. The victory emboldened Bulgarian resistance under Samuel, delaying the empire's eventual reconquest of Bulgaria for another three decades.

evt-08-17-1676-scanian-war.scenario: It is 17 August 1676 near Halmstad. A Danish force is pushing north into Sweden's territory, and King Charles XI's army moves to intercept before the Danes can link up with rebels in Scania.
evt-08-17-1676-scanian-war.prompt: What was the outcome of the Battle of Halmstad for the Danish advance?

choices.text: Swedish forces halted the Danish advance and forced a retreat
Both armies withdrew without engaging
The battle ended the war immediately with a Swedish surrender
The Danes broke through and captured Halmstad outright

evt-08-17-1676-scanian-war.butterflyEffect: The Swedish army broke the Danish force and halted its advance, forcing a retreat back toward Scania. The war nonetheless dragged on for three more bloody years, culminating in the even larger Battle of Lund, before an inconclusive peace restored the prewar borders.

evt-08-17-1876-gotterdammerung.scenario: You take your seat in the newly built Bayreuth Festspielhaus on 17 August 1876, watching Wagner's Ring cycle reach its fiery conclusion with the premiere of Götterdämmerung.
evt-08-17-1876-gotterdammerung.prompt: What immediate outcome followed this first complete Bayreuth Festival?

choices.text: Critics forced Wagner to withdraw the cycle from future performance
The Bavarian government seized the Festspielhaus over unpaid debts
A crippling financial deficit forced the festival to close for years
Ticket profits immediately funded a second theater

evt-08-17-1876-gotterdammerung.butterflyEffect: Despite artistic acclaim, the festival ran at a massive financial loss, leaving Wagner deeply in debt. Bayreuth went dark for six years before reopening in 1882 with Parsifal, and the festival's survival depended on patrons like King Ludwig II and new fundraising efforts.

evt-08-17-1907-pike-place-market.scenario: It's 17 August 1907, and you are a farmer near Seattle, fed up with commission merchants who buy your potatoes cheap and resell them to city shoppers at a steep markup.
evt-08-17-1907-pike-place-market.prompt: What new venue lets you sell your produce directly to Seattle's shoppers?

choices.text: A city-run fixed-price grocery cooperative
Pike Place Market, opening for direct farm-to-consumer sales
A state law banning commission merchants outright
A farmers' mail-order catalog service

evt-08-17-1907-pike-place-market.butterflyEffect: Pike Place Market opened that day, letting farmers bypass middlemen and sell straight to the public. It grew into one of the oldest continuously operating public markets in the country and remains Seattle's signature landmark, drawing over twenty million visitors a year.

evt-08-17-1914-world-war-i.scenario: It is 17 August 1914 in East Prussia, and you are General Hermann von François, whose I Corps has been ordered to retreat before advancing Russian forces near Stallupönen.
evt-08-17-1914-world-war-i.prompt: Do you obey the retreat order or strike the Russians first?

choices.text: Disobey orders and attack the Russian forces directly
Request reinforcements before making any move
Open truce talks with the Russian commander
Retreat as instructed by high command

evt-08-17-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: François defied the order and attacked, winning a sharp tactical victory at Stallupönen. His aggression foreshadowed the German command's boldness days later at Tannenberg, where the Russian First and Second Armies were decisively crushed.

evt-08-17-1915-1915-galveston-hurricane.scenario: You are a Galveston resident on 16 August 1915, watching storm warnings for a hurricane approaching the same coast devastated by the catastrophic 1900 storm.
evt-08-17-1915-1915-galveston-hurricane.prompt: What made this storm less devastating for the city of Galveston itself than the 1900 disaster?

choices.text: The recently built Galveston Seawall protected the city from the worst surge
The storm weakened dramatically just before reaching the coast
The hurricane veered away from Galveston at the last moment
The entire population had evacuated inland before landfall

evt-08-17-1915-1915-galveston-hurricane.butterflyEffect: The newly completed Galveston Seawall held back the worst of the storm surge within the city, but hundreds still died along unprotected stretches of the Texas coast, with total damage reaching roughly $30 million. The contrast reinforced the seawall's value and encouraged further coastal defense investment across the Gulf.

evt-08-17-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 17-18 August 1943, and you are a navigator in a Royal Air Force Lancaster crossing the Baltic Sea, briefed to hit a secretive research site on Germany's northern coast.
evt-08-17-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What is the RAF bombing force's target that night?

choices.text: The secret rocket research facility at Peenemünde
The industrial heartland of the Ruhr Valley
The German capital, Berlin
The U-boat pens at Kiel

evt-08-17-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The raid, Operation Hydra, struck Peenemünde, Germany's V-2 rocket development site, killing several scientists and forced laborers and setting the program back by weeks. In response, the Nazis relocated rocket production underground to the Mittelwerk factory, worked by concentration camp prisoners under horrific conditions.

evt-08-17-1943-winston-churchill.scenario: It is August 1943, and you are an aide inside the Citadelle in Quebec, where Churchill and Roosevelt have gathered away from public view to settle the shape of the war's next phase.
evt-08-17-1943-winston-churchill.prompt: What key decision emerges from this secret Quadrant Conference?

choices.text: A plan to negotiate a separate peace with Italy alone
A decision to invade the Balkans instead of France
An agreement to delay any invasion until 1946
Agreement to launch a cross-Channel invasion of France

evt-08-17-1943-winston-churchill.butterflyEffect: The leaders committed to a cross-Channel invasion of France, laying the groundwork for what became Operation Overlord in June 1944. They also signed the Quebec Agreement, formalizing British-American cooperation on atomic bomb research that fed into the Manhattan Project.

evt-08-17-1945-animal-farm.scenario: It is 1944 and George Orwell is shopping his manuscript for Animal Farm around London publishers, several of whom balk at satirizing wartime ally the Soviet Union.
evt-08-17-1945-animal-farm.prompt: What happened once Secker & Warburg finally published the book on 17 August 1945?

choices.text: It became a bestseller, especially as Cold War tensions with the USSR grew
It was quietly banned in Britain and withdrawn from sale
It was published uncensored in the Soviet Union to wide acclaim
It sold only a handful of copies and was soon forgotten

evt-08-17-1945-animal-farm.butterflyEffect: The book became a huge success, especially in the United States as Cold War tensions with the USSR deepened, cementing Orwell's reputation and turning phrases like 'some animals are more equal than others' into lasting political shorthand. Soviet-bloc governments later banned it outright.

evt-08-17-1945-proclamation-of-indonesia.scenario: It is the morning of 17 August 1945 in Jakarta. Japan has just surrendered, its occupying forces still hold the city, and Sukarno and Hatta have finished drafting a short proclamation of independence.
evt-08-17-1945-proclamation-of-indonesia.prompt: What did Sukarno and Hatta do immediately after signing the proclamation?

choices.text: They waited for Allied forces to formally approve the declaration first
They delayed announcing it until the Dutch colonial administration returned
They asked the Japanese military governor to co-sign and legitimize it
They broadcast and printed it immediately to spread the news before it could be suppressed

evt-08-17-1945-proclamation-of-indonesia.butterflyEffect: They had it broadcast by radio and printed in newspapers within hours, spreading word nationwide before Japanese authorities or returning Dutch forces could suppress it. This triggered the four-year Indonesian National Revolution, ending with the Netherlands formally recognizing Indonesian independence in 1949.

evt-08-17-1950-korean-war.scenario: It is August 17, 1950, near Waegwan, South Korea. You command a U.S. relief column pushing toward Hill 303, where American soldiers captured by retreating North Korean troops are being held as your force closes in.
evt-08-17-1950-korean-war.prompt: What did the North Korean captors do to the American prisoners as your column approached?

choices.text: Executed them before retreating
Marched them north to a permanent POW camp
Held them for a prisoner exchange
Released them unharmed as they withdrew

evt-08-17-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: The North Korean troops machine-gunned the 42 captured Americans rather than let them be recaptured. News of the Hill 303 massacre hardened American resolve during the desperate defense of the Pusan Perimeter and became a rallying point in wartime propaganda about enemy conduct toward POWs.

evt-08-17-1959-miles-davis.scenario: It is August 17, 1959, and you are a jazz critic holding a fresh copy of Miles Davis's new record, unsure why musicians are already calling it a break from everything bebop had trained your ear to expect.
evt-08-17-1959-miles-davis.prompt: What makes this album, Kind of Blue, so different?

choices.text: It builds improvisation on modal scales instead of chord changes
It is the first jazz album to use electric instruments throughout
It fuses jazz with rock rhythms for the first time
It is recorded live before an audience rather than in a studio

evt-08-17-1959-miles-davis.butterflyEffect: Davis and his sidemen improvised over sparse modal scales rather than dense chord changes, a radical simplification that opened new melodic freedom. Kind of Blue went on to become the best-selling jazz album in history and a foundational text for modal jazz.

evt-08-17-1988-zia-ul-haq.scenario: It is the afternoon of 17 August 1988. General Zia-ul-Haq's C-130 has just gone down near Bahawalpur, killing him and the US ambassador, and Pakistan has no sitting president.
evt-08-17-1988-zia-ul-haq.prompt: Under Pakistan's constitution, who actually took over as acting president after the crash?

choices.text: The army chief declared himself president and extended martial law
Senate Chairman Ghulam Ishaq Khan became acting president
A council of provincial governors ruled jointly until new elections
Prime Minister's office was left vacant pending Zia's chosen successor

evt-08-17-1988-zia-ul-haq.butterflyEffect: Senate Chairman Ghulam Ishaq Khan became acting president, and elections were held later that year as Zia's martial-law order lapsed. Benazir Bhutto's PPP won, making her the first woman to lead a modern Muslim-majority country, though friction between civilian government and the military establishment Zia had built persisted for years.

evt-08-17-1998-clinton-lewinsky-scandal.scenario: It is January 26, 1998, and you are a White House aide watching President Clinton step to the microphones after weeks of swirling tabloid rumors about an intern.
evt-08-17-1998-clinton-lewinsky-scandal.prompt: What does Clinton tell the cameras that day?

choices.text: He denies any sexual relationship with Monica Lewinsky
He refuses to comment and ends the press conference early
He admits to an affair and apologizes to the nation
He announces his resignation effective immediately

evt-08-17-1998-clinton-lewinsky-scandal.butterflyEffect: He flatly denied any sexual relationship, later famously wagging his finger while saying "I did not have sexual relations with that woman." The statement proved false under oath, and the resulting perjury and obstruction charges led to his impeachment by the House in December 1998, though the Senate acquitted him in February 1999.

evt-08-17-1999-1999-izmit-earthquake.scenario: It's the early hours of 17 August 1999. You are coordinating emergency response in Kocaeli province as apartment blocks lie collapsed and international offers of help begin arriving from unexpected quarters.
evt-08-17-1999-1999-izmit-earthquake.prompt: Whose rapid rescue teams and aid became a turning point in strained regional relations?

choices.text: Syria
Armenia
Bulgaria
Greece

evt-08-17-1999-1999-izmit-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Greek rescue teams and aid arrived within a day, and Turkey reciprocated weeks later when a quake struck Athens. The exchange sparked what became known as 'earthquake diplomacy,' helping thaw decades of Greek-Turkish tension and opening space for improved cooperation between the two states.

evt-08-17-2005-israeli-settlement.scenario: You are an Israeli soldier ordered into the Gush Katif settlement bloc in Gaza on 17 August 2005, the day forced evacuations begin under Prime Minister Sharon's disengagement plan, and a family refuses to leave their home.
evt-08-17-2005-israeli-settlement.prompt: What are you ordered to do with settlers who refuse to leave voluntarily?

choices.text: Refuse the order out of solidarity with the settlers
Physically carry out the removal as ordered by the government
Grant an indefinite extension to avoid confrontation
Open fire to force immediate compliance

evt-08-17-2005-israeli-settlement.butterflyEffect: Israeli soldiers and police forcibly removed thousands of resisting settlers over the following weeks, completing the withdrawal from all Gaza settlements by mid-September 2005. The vacated territory came under Hamas control after 2006–2007, setting the stage for Israel's blockade and the recurring conflicts that followed.

evt-08-17-2005-2005-bangladesh-bombings.scenario: It is midday on 17 August 2005, and you are a security official in Dhaka receiving reports that hundreds of small bombs have gone off almost simultaneously across nearly every district of Bangladesh.
evt-08-17-2005-2005-bangladesh-bombings.prompt: How should the government respond to this coordinated nationwide attack?

choices.text: Outlaw the militant groups responsible and launch a crackdown
Treat it as an isolated local incident needing no national response
Limit the security response to the capital city alone
Open negotiations with the bombers' leadership

evt-08-17-2005-2005-bangladesh-bombings.butterflyEffect: The government banned Jama'atul Mujahideen Bangladesh and the allied Harkat-ul-Jihad al-Islami, launching a sustained crackdown on Islamist militancy. Several JMB leaders, including Shaykh Abdur Rahman, were later captured and executed in 2007, marking a turning point in Bangladesh's counterterrorism efforts.

evt-08-17-2008-michael-phelps.scenario: You are in the stands at the Beijing National Aquatics Center on the final night of swimming finals, 17 August 2008, as Michael Phelps swims the butterfly leg of the men's 4x100m medley relay.
evt-08-17-2008-michael-phelps.prompt: What happened in that relay to secure Phelps's record-breaking eighth gold medal?

choices.text: USA won gold, breaking Mark Spitz's record of seven golds in one Games
Australia edged out the USA team for gold
The USA tied Spitz's record but did not surpass it
Phelps swam the anchor freestyle leg himself to seal the win

evt-08-17-2008-michael-phelps.butterflyEffect: Team USA won the relay, giving Phelps eight gold medals at a single Games and breaking Mark Spitz's 1972 record of seven. The feat cemented Phelps as the sport's defining figure and set up his later hauls in London and Rio, where he became the most decorated Olympian in history.

evt-08-17-2009-sayano-shushenskaya-power.scenario: You are a control-room operator at the Sayano-Shushenskaya hydroelectric plant in the early morning of 17 August 2009 when Turbine No. 2 begins vibrating violently, its mounting bolts starting to shear.
evt-08-17-2009-sayano-shushenskaya-power.prompt: What actually happened when the turbine tore free of its housing?

choices.text: Automatic safety systems shut it down before any structural damage occurred
Blast doors sealed the turbine bay and the rest of the plant kept running normally
It shot up through the floor, flooding the hall and wrecking most of the plant's turbines
Backup generators isolated the fault with no injuries or loss of output

evt-08-17-2009-sayano-shushenskaya-power.butterflyEffect: The turbine was ejected upward, flooding the turbine hall and destroying or damaging nine of the plant's ten units. Seventy-five workers died, all 6,400 MW of output was lost, and the disaster triggered a national reckoning over the safety of Russia's aging Soviet-era hydroelectric infrastructure.

evt-08-17-2015-2015-bangkok-bombing.scenario: You are a Thai police investigator combing through CCTV footage hours after a bomb tore through the crowded Erawan Shrine at rush hour on 17 August 2015.
evt-08-17-2015-2015-bangkok-bombing.prompt: What motive did investigators come to suspect drove the bombing?

choices.text: Retaliation linked to Thailand's deportation of Uyghur refugees back to China
A personal grievance from a single disgruntled shrine employee
An extortion attempt against local business owners
A political feud between rival Thai factions

evt-08-17-2015-2015-bangkok-bombing.butterflyEffect: Two Uyghur men were arrested, with one initially confessing and later retracting; prosecutors linked the attack to anger over Thailand's forced deportation of Uyghur refugees to China weeks earlier. The case dragged through Thai courts for over a decade, with both men finally convicted and sentenced to death in 2026.

evt-08-17-2017-2017-barcelona-attacks.scenario: It is the afternoon of 17 August 2017. A van has just torn through crowds on La Rambla, the driver has fled on foot into the city, and police must decide how to respond to a possible wider plot.
evt-08-17-2017-2017-barcelona-attacks.prompt: What did the investigation reveal about the scope of the attack in the days that followed?

choices.text: It was part of a larger bomb plot that collapsed after an accidental explosion the night before
The attack was quickly linked to a foreign government rather than a local cell
It was an isolated act by a single individual with no wider network
The driver surrendered to police within the hour

evt-08-17-2017-2017-barcelona-attacks.butterflyEffect: Police pursued the driver, Younes Abouyaaqoub, for four days before shooting him near Subirats on 21 August. Investigators traced the attack to a Ripoll-based cell that had planned a larger bombing campaign using gas canisters, a plan that collapsed after an accidental explosion at their Alcanar bomb factory the night before, forcing them into smaller vehicle attacks in Barcelona and Cambrils instead.

evt-08-18-1487-reconquista.scenario: It is August 1487, and you serve as an advisor to Ferdinand and Isabella outside the walls of Málaga. The city has held out for four grueling months against the royal siege, draining the Crown's treasury and patience, before finally offering to surrender.
evt-08-18-1487-reconquista.prompt: What terms do the Catholic Monarchs impose on Málaga after its prolonged resistance?

choices.text: Immediate expulsion but retention of property
A heavy ransom in exchange for freedom
Mass enslavement as punishment for the long resistance
Free passage and mercy for all inhabitants

evt-08-18-1487-reconquista.butterflyEffect: Because the city had resisted so long and cost the Crown so dearly, most of Málaga's population was enslaved rather than shown the mercy earlier cities received. The harshness became a cautionary example, and it influenced Granada's decision in 1492 to negotiate surrender quickly rather than risk a similar siege.

evt-08-18-1612-pendle-witches.scenario: It is August 1612 at Lancaster Assizes, and you are one of twelve people from around Pendle Hill accused of murdering ten people through witchcraft. The evidence against you includes testimony from a nine-year-old girl, and the judges are eager to make an example of the case.
evt-08-18-1612-pendle-witches.prompt: What was the outcome for most of the accused Pendle witches?

choices.text: All were acquitted for lack of evidence
Most were found guilty and executed by hanging
They were pardoned by King James I before sentencing
They were exiled to the American colonies instead of executed

evt-08-18-1612-pendle-witches.butterflyEffect: Ten of the eleven who stood trial were convicted and hanged; only one was acquitted. The trial's detailed court records, published by clerk Thomas Potts, became one of the best-documented witch trials in English history and shaped how later generations understood the era's witch persecutions.

evt-08-18-1783-meteor-procession.scenario: You are on watch aboard a ship in the English Channel on the night of 18 August 1783 when a dazzling light, breaking into fragments, streaks low across the sky so close that it seems to skim the water and light the sails.
evt-08-18-1783-meteor-procession.prompt: Believing you may be looking at a burning vessel nearby, what should you do?

choices.text: Fire a warning cannon and continue on your original heading
Order the crew below deck for safety
Alter course and search for survivors of the apparent blaze
Log it as heat lightning and ignore it

evt-08-18-1783-meteor-procession.butterflyEffect: The light was in fact the Great Meteor of 1783, an exceptionally bright Earth-grazing meteor procession seen across Britain and beyond. Several crews reportedly altered course searching for a shipwreck that did not exist, and the widely reported sighting fed growing 18th-century scientific interest in the origin and nature of meteors.

evt-08-18-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: You are a Union officer of Warren's V Corps holding newly seized ground along the Weldon Railroad south of Petersburg on 18 August 1864, as Confederate troops mass for a counterattack to retake the line.
evt-08-18-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What should you do to keep this vital supply line cut?

choices.text: Push further south toward Ream's Station immediately
Wait for naval gunboats to support the position before holding firm
Entrench and hold the captured railroad position at all costs
Withdraw to the safety of the main Petersburg siege lines

evt-08-18-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Union forces entrenched and held the Weldon Railroad despite fierce Confederate assaults, permanently severing one of Petersburg's key supply routes. Confederate wagons were forced onto longer overland hauls, tightening the siege of Petersburg and hastening the eventual collapse of Lee's defenses in 1865.

evt-08-18-1877-asaph-hall.scenario: You are an assistant at the US Naval Observatory in Washington in mid-August 1877, watching Asaph Hall painstakingly search the glare around Mars during its close opposition, having already spotted one faint moon days earlier.
evt-08-18-1877-asaph-hall.prompt: What does Hall discover just days after finding Mars's outer moon, Deimos?

choices.text: A second, inner moon of Mars: Phobos
A previously unknown asteroid near Mars's orbit
A ring system around Mars
Evidence of polar ice caps on Mars

evt-08-18-1877-asaph-hall.butterflyEffect: Hall discovered Phobos, the larger and closer of Mars's two tiny moons, completing the pair he named for the sons of Ares who personified fear and panic. The discovery reshaped understanding of Mars's system and, over a century later, Phobos's rapidly decaying orbit became a key data point for planning future Mars missions.

evt-08-18-1919-russian-civil-war.scenario: You command a Royal Navy Coastal Motor Boat squadron ordered to slip into Kronstadt harbour, home base of the Bolshevik Baltic Fleet, under cover of a diversionary air raid.
evt-08-18-1919-russian-civil-war.prompt: How do you strike the anchored Soviet warships before their defenses react?

choices.text: Race in at speed and fire torpedoes at close range under cover of noise and smoke
Retreat and report the defenses as too strong to attack
Call in a cruiser squadron to bombard the harbour from range
Lay mines at the harbour entrance and withdraw

evt-08-18-1919-russian-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Led by Augustus Agar, the raiders sank the cruiser Pamyat Azova and damaged the battleship Andrei Pervozvanny, at the cost of several boats and men. The daring small-boat action boosted British prestige during the intervention and became a celebrated example of fast-attack naval tactics studied for decades after.

evt-08-18-1920-nineteenth-amendment-to-t.scenario: It is August 1920, and you are a suffragist watching the ratification count. Tennessee's legislature is deadlocked, and one young representative, Harry Burn, holds the deciding vote after receiving a note from his mother urging him to 'be a good boy' and vote for suffrage.
evt-08-18-1920-nineteenth-amendment-to-t.prompt: What did Tennessee's ratification actually accomplish?

choices.text: It triggered a Supreme Court challenge that delayed suffrage for two more years
It only granted suffrage within Tennessee itself
It secured the final state needed to add the amendment to the Constitution
It forced a national referendum on women's voting rights

evt-08-18-1920-nineteenth-amendment-to-t.butterflyEffect: Tennessee became the 36th state to ratify, providing the two-thirds majority needed to add the Nineteenth Amendment to the Constitution. Millions of American women were able to vote in the November 1920 presidential election for the first time, reshaping political campaigning and party strategy for decades afterward.

evt-08-18-1937-blackwater-fire-of-1937.scenario: It is August 18, 1937, in Shoshone National Forest, Wyoming. You are on a crew battling a lightning-sparked blaze when a dry front suddenly shifts the wind, and flames begin racing toward your line with terrifying speed.
evt-08-18-1937-blackwater-fire-of-1937.prompt: What should the firefighting crew do the moment the wind shift turns the fire deadly?

choices.text: Retreat immediately to a safe area away from the flames
Keep building the fireline to hold position
Wait for radio confirmation before moving
Split into smaller groups to outrun the fire in different directions

evt-08-18-1937-blackwater-fire-of-1937.butterflyEffect: Several crews failed to retreat in time and were trapped by the firestorm; nine died in the blaze and six more later from burns and smoke inhalation, making it one of the deadliest wildland fires in U.S. history. The disaster spurred the Forest Service to overhaul firefighter safety training, feeding into later standardized wildfire safety orders.

evt-08-18-1945-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 18 August 1945, three days after Emperor Hirohito's surrender broadcast. You command a Japanese garrison in the Koton fortified region of South Sakhalin, but Soviet troops keep attacking and no formal ceasefire order has reached you.
evt-08-18-1945-world-war-ii.prompt: What should your garrison do as the Soviet offensive continues despite the surrender broadcast?

choices.text: Open direct negotiations with the Soviet commander for a local truce
Keep resisting until a formal cease-fire order arrives through the chain of command
Surrender the position immediately and unconditionally
Abandon the fortifications and evacuate without engaging Soviet forces

evt-08-18-1945-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Many Japanese units, uncertain whether the Emperor's broadcast constituted a binding ceasefire, kept fighting for days. The Koton defenses held into late August, slowing the Soviet advance and buying time for civilians to evacuate south, but Sakhalin still fell fully under Soviet control, a division that outlasted the war itself.

evt-08-18-1948-fifth-test-1948-ashes-ser.scenario: It is 18 August 1948 at The Oval, and you are in the crowd as Don Bradman walks out for his final Test innings. He needs just four runs to finish his career with a batting average of exactly 100, and the England fielders give him a warm ovation as he takes his stance.
evt-08-18-1948-fifth-test-1948-ashes-ser.prompt: What happened when Bradman faced his final Test delivery?

choices.text: He was bowled out for zero, missing the average of 100 by a fraction
He was given out controversially on review and the match was replayed
He scored the four runs needed and retired immediately
Rain stopped play before he could bat
