evt-08-18-1948-fifth-test-1948-ashes-ser.butterflyEffect: Bradman was bowled for a duck by Eric Hollies, second ball, finishing his career with an average of 99.94 instead of the perfect 100. The near-miss became cricket's most famous statistic, and Australia went on to complete a 4-0 series win, sealing the 'Invincibles' tour as legendary.

evt-08-18-1966-vietnam-war.scenario: It is the afternoon of 18 August 1966 in a rubber plantation near Long Tan. Your company of about 100 Australian soldiers, out on patrol, has run into a Viet Cong and North Vietnamese force many times your size, and monsoon rain is closing in as ammunition runs low.
evt-08-18-1966-vietnam-war.prompt: How did the outnumbered Australian company survive the battle?

choices.text: American B-52 bombers were diverted to strike the enemy directly overhead
They retreated immediately and abandoned the position
They called in artillery fire and held on until an armoured relief force arrived
They negotiated a local ceasefire with enemy commanders

evt-08-18-1966-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: D Company held its ground through artillery support and a night resupply drop, then was relieved by armoured personnel carriers rushing from Nui Dat. The Battle of Long Tan became the defining action of Australia's Vietnam War, remembered annually as Long Tan Day / Vietnam Veterans' Day.

evt-08-18-1983-hurricane-alicia.scenario: It is mid-August 1983, and you are a Houston-area official watching Hurricane Alicia rapidly strengthen just off the Texas coast, its small, tight core aimed squarely at Galveston Island.
evt-08-18-1983-hurricane-alicia.prompt: What should officials do given Alicia's small size but sudden intensification near a major metro area?

choices.text: Issue evacuation warnings for coastal and low-lying areas
Wait until landfall to confirm intensity before warning residents
Focus warnings only on rural coastal communities, not Houston
Downplay the threat since the storm's small size limits its impact

evt-08-18-1983-hurricane-alicia.butterflyEffect: Alicia struck Galveston as a Category 3 hurricane and its eye passed just west of downtown Houston, causing roughly $3 billion in damage and becoming the costliest Atlantic hurricane up to that time. The storm exposed how rapid urban growth into coastal areas amplified hurricane risk, prompting stricter building codes and improved warning systems for the region.

evt-08-18-1993-american-international-ai.scenario: You are aboard American International Airways Flight 808, a DC-8 cargo jet, on final approach to Leeward Point Field at Guantanamo Bay on 18 August 1993. The aircraft's sink rate is dangerously high and the approach is unstable.
evt-08-18-1993-american-international-ai.prompt: What should the crew do to avoid disaster?

choices.text: Extend the flaps further to slow the descent rate
Execute a go-around and abort the landing
Continue the steep descent and try to salvage the landing
Request the runway lighting be adjusted for better visibility

evt-08-18-1993-american-international-ai.butterflyEffect: The crew failed to arrest the excessive descent and the DC-8 crashed short of the runway and broke apart in flames; remarkably, all three crew members survived. Investigators blamed the decision to continue an unstabilized visual approach, and the crash reinforced calls for stricter stabilized-approach discipline and crew coordination in cargo aviation.

evt-08-18-2008-pervez-musharraf.scenario: It is August 2008, and you are a close aide to President Pervez Musharraf. The ruling coalition of the PPP and PML-N has just tabled formal charges to impeach him in parliament, and his allies are melting away.
evt-08-18-2008-pervez-musharraf.prompt: Facing near-certain impeachment, what does Musharraf ultimately choose to do?

choices.text: Appeal directly to the Supreme Court to annul the charges
Resign the presidency before the vote
Dissolve parliament and call snap elections
Declare martial law to block the vote

evt-08-18-2008-pervez-musharraf.butterflyEffect: On 18 August 2008, Musharraf resigned rather than face a parliamentary vote, ending nearly nine years in power that began with his 1999 coup. Asif Ali Zardari was elected president weeks later, and Pakistan entered a period of fragile civilian-led governance under continued military influence.

evt-08-18-2008-uzbin-valley-ambush.scenario: You are a French officer with the 8th Marine Infantry Parachute Regiment on 18 August 2008, leading a patrol with Afghan troops through the narrow, high-walled Uzbin Valley east of Kabul as dusk approaches.
evt-08-18-2008-uzbin-valley-ambush.prompt: What immediate consequence followed this ambush for France's role in the war?

choices.text: NATO command was permanently relocated from Kabul
It sparked national debate in France over continuing the Afghan deployment
The Afghan government demanded French troops leave the province
France immediately withdrew all forces from Afghanistan

evt-08-18-2008-uzbin-valley-ambush.butterflyEffect: Ten French soldiers were killed, France's deadliest single engagement in decades, and it triggered fierce debate at home over the country's deepening commitment in Afghanistan. President Sarkozy visited the site personally, and the ambush became a lasting symbol of the war's cost for French public opinion.

evt-08-18-2011-2011-southern-israel-cros.scenario: It is 18 August 2011 along Highway 12 near Eilat. You are part of an Israeli security detail responding as gunfire hits a bus, a bomb strikes an army patrol, and an anti-tank missile hits a civilian vehicle in a coordinated ambush from the Egyptian border.
evt-08-18-2011-2011-southern-israel-cros.prompt: How did Israeli forces respond to the multi-stage ambush along the border road?

choices.text: Called in an airstrike deep into Egyptian Sinai territory
Engaged the militants directly, killing most of the attack squad
Withdrew from the area to avoid further casualties
Negotiated a ceasefire with the attackers on the spot

evt-08-18-2011-2011-southern-israel-cros.butterflyEffect: Israeli troops and a Yamam sniper engaged the attackers, killing eight of the roughly twelve militants, while Egyptian forces killed two more. The attack exposed the security vacuum in the Sinai after Egypt's revolution and accelerated Israeli plans to build a fortified fence along the entire Egyptian border.

evt-08-18-2019-iceland.scenario: You stand on a barren volcanic slope in Iceland on 18 August 2019 with scientists, officials, and mourners, gathered for a solemn ceremony marking the death of a glacier now reduced to a patch of ice.
evt-08-18-2019-iceland.prompt: What did the memorial plaque unveiled at the ceremony for Okjökull glacier say?

choices.text: It listed the glacier's exact size at its peak
It announced a plan to artificially regrow the glacier
It thanked tourists for visiting responsibly
It warned future generations about the consequences of climate change

evt-08-18-2019-iceland.butterflyEffect: The plaque, titled 'A letter to the future,' warned that only future generations would know whether enough was done to stop climate change. Okjökull's funeral became a widely covered symbol of glacial loss, cited afterward in climate reports and activism worldwide.

evt-08-19-1274-lord-edward-s-crusade.scenario: News reaches you in Sicily in November 1272: your father, King Henry III, has died, making you king of England. You are still making your way home from the Holy Land after Lord Edward's Crusade.
evt-08-19-1274-lord-edward-s-crusade.prompt: What do you do before returning to claim your throne?

choices.text: Return to the Holy Land to continue crusading
Send envoys to govern in your name indefinitely
Spend nearly two years touring your continental lands before returning
Rush home immediately to secure your crown

evt-08-19-1274-lord-edward-s-crusade.butterflyEffect: Edward took nearly two years touring his lands in Gascony and France before finally reaching England, where he was crowned on 19 August 1274. His unhurried return reflected a new principle taking hold: that kingship passed automatically at a predecessor's death rather than at coronation, a shift that shaped English succession for centuries.

evt-08-19-1725-johann-sebastian-bach.scenario: It is Sunday, 19 August 1725, in Leipzig's Thomaskirche. As cantor, Johann Sebastian Bach directs the choir and orchestra in a new cantata built around a beloved congregational hymn for the twelfth Sunday after Trinity.
evt-08-19-1725-johann-sebastian-bach.prompt: Which hymn does Bach's new cantata take as its musical foundation?

choices.text: "Ein feste Burg ist unser Gott"
"Lobe den Herren, den mächtigen König der Ehren"
"Jesu, meine Freude"
"Wachet auf, ruft uns die Stimme"

evt-08-19-1725-johann-sebastian-bach.butterflyEffect: Bach based the cantata on the hymn "Lobe den Herren, den mächtigen König der Ehren," weaving its melody through each movement in his signature chorale-cantata style. Works like this one, part of his second Leipzig cantata cycle, were largely forgotten until the 19th-century Bach Revival restored his reputation as one of history's greatest composers.

evt-08-19-1745-charles-edward-stuart.scenario: You stand among a small crowd at Glenfinnan as a young Stuart prince, freshly landed from France, unfurls a red and white silk banner and calls on the Highland clans to rise for his father's crown.
evt-08-19-1745-charles-edward-stuart.prompt: What do you do as the standard is raised?

choices.text: Wait to see if the government garrison responds first
Urge Charles to return to France before it is too late
Report the gathering to Hanoverian authorities
Pledge your clan's men to march for Prince Charles

evt-08-19-1745-charles-edward-stuart.butterflyEffect: Charles Edward Stuart's gamble launched the Jacobite Rising of 1745, which swept through Scotland and reached as far as Derby before collapsing at Culloden in April 1746. The crushing defeat ended serious Stuart hopes forever and led to the systematic dismantling of clan society in the Highlands, including bans on tartan and the bearing of arms.

evt-08-19-1759-seven-years-war.scenario: It is August 1759, and you serve under Admiral Edward Boscawen, chasing a fleeing French Mediterranean squadron along the Portuguese coast near Lagos after a clash off Gibraltar.
evt-08-19-1759-seven-years-war.prompt: What does the British fleet do when the French ships take shelter in neutral Portuguese waters?

choices.text: Abandon the chase and return to blockade Toulon
Wait offshore for a formal declaration of war on Portugal
Press the attack into the bay despite Portuguese neutrality
Withdraw out of respect for Portugal's neutrality

evt-08-19-1759-seven-years-war.butterflyEffect: Boscawen's ships pursued into Lagos Bay regardless of Portuguese neutrality, destroying or capturing several French ships of the line. The victory, part of Britain's 1759 "Year of Victories," helped cripple French naval plans to invade Britain that year.

evt-08-19-1897-bersey-electric-cab.scenario: You are a London cab driver watching a quiet, battery-powered carriage glide past Piccadilly without a horse in sight. Walter Bersey's new fleet has just entered service, and passengers are curious to try this silent alternative to the clattering hansom cab.
evt-08-19-1897-bersey-electric-cab.prompt: What made the Bersey cab stand out to Londoners that day?

choices.text: It ran silently on batteries instead of a horse
It ran on rails laid specially through the city streets
It was steam-powered and required a boiler stop every hour
It could travel over 100 miles on a single charge

evt-08-19-1897-bersey-electric-cab.butterflyEffect: The Bersey Electric Cab was London's first electric taxi service, nicknamed 'Hummingbirds' for their quiet hum, but heavy batteries, high running costs, and frequent tire wear made the venture commercially unviable within a couple of years. The experiment nonetheless proved electric propulsion could work in dense city traffic, a lesson revisited decades later as cities again turned to electric vehicles.

evt-08-19-1920-russian-civil-war.scenario: You are a grain farmer in Tambov Governorate. Bolshevik requisition squads have seized nearly everything your family grew, leaving you to face winter with empty stores, while neighbors whisper of joining Alexander Antonov's partisans in the forests.
evt-08-19-1920-russian-civil-war.prompt: What should you and your fellow peasants do about the grain requisitions?

choices.text: Petition the local Soviet for a formal exemption
Hide grain and quietly wait for policy to change on its own
Flee immediately to White-held territory in the south
Join the rebels fighting the Red Army's requisition squads

evt-08-19-1920-russian-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Tambov Rebellion became one of the largest peasant uprisings against Bolshevik rule, crushed in 1921 by Red Army forces under Tukhachevsky using mass reprisals and poison gas against rebel-held villages. The scale of peasant resistance nationwide convinced Lenin to abandon forced grain requisitioning for the New Economic Policy, a market-based retreat from pure communism.

evt-08-19-1934-1934-german-head-of-state.scenario: You are a German voter at a polling station just weeks after President Hindenburg's death. Party officials watch as you fill out your ballot on whether Adolf Hitler should formally combine the powers of Chancellor and President.
evt-08-19-1934-1934-german-head-of-state.prompt: What was the outcome of this referendum, held under Nazi intimidation?

choices.text: The referendum passed overwhelmingly, confirming Hitler as sole head of state
The vote was annulled after evidence of fraud emerged
The referendum failed, forcing new presidential elections
The result was too close to call and a runoff was held

evt-08-19-1934-1934-german-head-of-state.butterflyEffect: Nearly 90% of recorded votes approved merging the offices, despite widespread coercion and fraud, giving Hitler the title of Führer and Reich Chancellor with unchecked authority over the state and military. This vote cemented one-man rule in Germany, removing the last constitutional check that a separate presidency might have provided.

evt-08-19-1981-gulf-of-sidra-incident-19.scenario: It is 19 August 1981, and you are flying an F-14A Tomcat over the Gulf of Sidra when two Libyan Su-22 fighters suddenly fire a missile at your formation.
evt-08-19-1981-gulf-of-sidra-incident-19.prompt: How do you respond to being fired upon by the Libyan jets?

choices.text: Break off and radio the carrier without returning fire
Perform evasive maneuvers only, holding fire under strict rules of engagement
Fire Sidewinder missiles and shoot down the attacking jets
Retreat immediately to the aircraft carrier

evt-08-19-1981-gulf-of-sidra-incident-19.butterflyEffect: The Tomcats returned fire with AIM-9L Sidewinders, shooting down both Libyan Su-22s in the first U.S. aircraft kills over the Mediterranean since World War II. The clash escalated tensions between Washington and Gaddafi's Libya, setting the stage for further confrontations in the Gulf of Sidra later in the decade.

evt-08-19-1989-wojciech-jaruzelski.scenario: It is 19 August 1989 in Warsaw. Communist candidate Czesław Kiszczak has just failed to form a government after Solidarity's landslide June election win. As president, you must now choose someone else to lead Poland.
evt-08-19-1989-wojciech-jaruzelski.prompt: Who does Jaruzelski nominate as prime minister?

choices.text: Tadeusz Mazowiecki
Czesław Kiszczak
Lech Wałęsa
Mieczysław Rakowski

evt-08-19-1989-wojciech-jaruzelski.butterflyEffect: Jaruzelski nominated Solidarity activist Tadeusz Mazowiecki, who became the first non-communist prime minister in the Soviet bloc since the 1940s. His appointment broke the political deadlock and emboldened reform movements across Eastern Europe, helping trigger the wave of revolutions that swept the region later that year.

evt-08-19-1989-east-germany.scenario: It is 19 August 1989 near Sopron, Hungary. A 'Pan-European Picnic' has been staged as a symbolic gesture of friendship at the Austrian border, and you notice the border gate standing unguarded amid the crowd of East German tourists.

choices.text: Cross into Austria immediately, fleeing to the West
Wait for official permission from East German authorities
Stay at the picnic and return to your campsite that night
Report the opening to Hungarian border guards

evt-08-19-1989-east-germany.butterflyEffect: Several hundred East Germans dashed across during the Pan-European Picnic, the largest single breach of the Iron Curtain since 1961. Hungary's choice not to stop them signaled that the bloc's border controls were crumbling, emboldening tens of thousands more East Germans to flee in the following weeks and helping trigger the fall of the Berlin Wall that November.

evt-08-19-1991-dissolution-of-the-soviet.scenario: It is 19 August 1991. You wake in Moscow to state television announcing that President Gorbachev is 'ill' and unable to perform his duties, while tanks roll toward the Russian parliament building.
evt-08-19-1991-dissolution-of-the-soviet.prompt: As a Muscovite, what do you do?

choices.text: Join Yeltsin and crowds resisting the coup outside the Russian parliament
Report to the KGB for further instructions
Follow the new State Committee's curfew and stay indoors
Flee the city for the countryside

evt-08-19-1991-dissolution-of-the-soviet.butterflyEffect: Thousands answered Boris Yeltsin's call to resist, and the coup collapsed within three days. Its failure discredited the hardline plotters, hastened Gorbachev's political fall, and accelerated the Soviet Union's collapse, which was formally dissolved by December 1991.

evt-08-19-1999-belgrade.scenario: It is 19 August 1999, months after NATO's bombing campaign ended the war over Kosovo. You join tens of thousands of Serbians packing the streets of Belgrade, chanting against President Slobodan Milošević's government.
evt-08-19-1999-belgrade.prompt: What are the demonstrators demanding from the government?

choices.text: Immediate withdrawal of all NATO peacekeepers from Kosovo
Formal annexation of Republika Srpska
The resignation of President Slobodan Milošević
Restoration of the Serbian monarchy

evt-08-19-1999-belgrade.butterflyEffect: The opposition alliance was demanding Milošević's resignation, blaming him for the ruinous war and NATO bombing. The protests marked the start of a sustained opposition movement that finally toppled Milošević after the disputed October 2000 election, when mass demonstrations forced him from power.

evt-08-19-2002-second-chechen-war.scenario: You are a Russian military commander near Khankala, Chechnya, on 19 August 2002, as reports arrive that a heavily loaded Mi-26 transport helicopter has been struck by a missile fired by separatist fighters.
evt-08-19-2002-second-chechen-war.prompt: What lasting change follows for Russian military transport practices?

choices.text: Russia announces a full withdrawal from Chechnya within the year
All helicopters are replaced with fixed-wing transports
The war ends with a negotiated ceasefire
Command imposes strict new limits on troops carried per helicopter

evt-08-19-2002-second-chechen-war.butterflyEffect: The Mi-26, carrying far more troops than its rated capacity, was brought down by a shoulder-fired missile, becoming the deadliest single loss of Russian personnel in the war. The disaster exposed dangerous overcrowding on Russian transport helicopters and led to new limits on the number of troops carried per aircraft.

evt-08-19-2003-canal-hotel-bombing.scenario: It is August 2003, five days into the new United Nations mission in Baghdad. You are advising on how to secure the Canal Hotel, the mission's makeshift headquarters, as threats against foreign occupiers mount across the city.
evt-08-19-2003-canal-hotel-bombing.prompt: What security posture does the UN mission adopt for its Baghdad headquarters?

choices.text: Relocate the entire mission outside Iraq immediately
Request a dedicated U.S. military garrison at the hotel
Keep barriers minimal to preserve the UN's image of neutrality
Surround the compound with tanks and armored checkpoints

evt-08-19-2003-canal-hotel-bombing.butterflyEffect: The UN deliberately kept fortifications light to project neutrality, leaving the hotel exposed when a suicide truck bomb struck on 19 August, killing envoy Sérgio Vieira de Mello and 22 others. Within weeks most of the 600-strong staff withdrew from Iraq, and the attack permanently reshaped UN security doctrine worldwide, ending the era of relying on neutrality alone for protection.

evt-08-19-2004-google.scenario: You are an early investor watching Google's unusual Dutch auction IPO unfold. The young Silicon Valley company, barely six years old, is about to start trading on Nasdaq under a pricing method almost no one on Wall Street has used before.
evt-08-19-2004-google.prompt: What happened when Google shares began trading that day?

choices.text: Shares opened flat and stayed unchanged all day
Shares opened and immediately rose sharply above the offer price
The IPO was postponed due to lack of investor interest
Trading was halted after the stock collapsed below its offer price

evt-08-19-2004-google.butterflyEffect: Google priced at $85 a share, below its original target range, and raised about $1.67 billion, but shares jumped over 18% on the first day of trading. The IPO's unconventional auction structure and founders' famous letter promising to prioritize long-term innovation over quarterly results set a template that shaped how tech companies would approach going public for years afterward.

evt-08-19-2010-iraq-war.scenario: It is 19 August 2010, and you are riding in the last U.S. brigade combat team crossing the border from Iraq into Kuwait, cameras rolling as commanders declare an end to combat operations under Operation Iraqi Freedom.
evt-08-19-2010-iraq-war.prompt: What happened to the U.S. military presence in Iraq immediately after this withdrawal?

choices.text: The Iraqi civil conflict ended completely
Operation New Dawn began, with tens of thousands of troops staying in an advisory role
The Iraqi government was dissolved and replaced by a coalition authority
Every American soldier left Iraq that same week

evt-08-19-2010-iraq-war.butterflyEffect: The mission was renamed Operation New Dawn, and roughly 50,000 troops remained in an advise-and-assist role rather than combat. Full withdrawal followed in December 2011, but the vacuum left behind contributed to instability that drew the U.S. back into Iraq in 2014 to fight the Islamic State.

evt-08-19-2013-dhamara-ghat-train-accide.scenario: It is the night of 19 August 2013. A speeding express train has just struck a crowd of Hindu pilgrims gathered on the tracks at Dhamara Ghat station in Bihar, and furious survivors are turning on railway staff. As the state's chief minister, you must respond at once.
evt-08-19-2013-dhamara-ghat-train-accide.prompt: What did Bihar's chief minister do to address the grieving families?

choices.text: Pledge 200,000 rupees in compensation to each victim's family
Publicly blame the pilgrims for standing too close to the tracks
Resign from office over the tragedy
Order the immediate closure of the Dhamara Ghat station permanently

evt-08-19-2013-dhamara-ghat-train-accide.butterflyEffect: Nitish Kumar pledged 200,000 rupees (about $3,180) to each victim's family and pressed the national railway ministry to match it. The disaster renewed public anger over unguarded level crossings and crowded platforms, fueling a long-running Indian debate over railway safety funding that continued for years afterward.

evt-08-20-917-byzantine-bulgarian-wars.scenario: It's August 20, 917, and you stand among Bulgarian troops near Anchialus on the Black Sea coast, watching Tsar Simeon I study a large, weary Byzantine army that has just completed a long march and has not yet formed its battle lines.
evt-08-20-917-byzantine-bulgarian-wars.prompt: What does Simeon I order his forces to do?

choices.text: Blockade the Byzantine fleet before engaging on land
Attack the tired, unformed Byzantine column before it deploys
Withdraw and wait for reinforcements from the north
Offer immediate terms of surrender to avoid battle

evt-08-20-917-byzantine-bulgarian-wars.butterflyEffect: Simeon launched a devastating surprise attack, and the Byzantine army was routed in one of its worst defeats of the era. The victory let Simeon dominate the Balkans for years, style himself emperor of the Bulgarians and Romans, and forced Byzantium into decades of costly negotiation before lasting peace was reached.

evt-08-20-1710-war-of-the-spanish-succes.scenario: It is 20 August 1710, and you serve in the Allied army of Archduke Charles as it clashes with the Bourbon force of the Marquis de Bay near Zaragoza, the last major obstacle before central Spain.
evt-08-20-1710-war-of-the-spanish-succes.prompt: What did the Allied victory at Zaragoza let Archduke Charles's forces do next?

choices.text: Invade Portugal to secure the border
March on and briefly occupy Madrid
Sign an armistice with Philip V
Retreat immediately to Barcelona

evt-08-20-1710-war-of-the-spanish-succes.butterflyEffect: The Allies won and pushed on to occupy Madrid in September 1710, but with little local support and overstretched supply lines they soon withdrew. Bourbon forces rallied and crushed the retreating Allied army that December at Brihuega and Villaviciosa, effectively deciding the war in Spain for Philip V.

evt-08-20-1909-pluto.scenario: It's August 20, 1909, and at Yerkes Observatory an astronomer exposes a photographic plate of a faint, undistinguished point of light in the night sky, with no idea it is a distant world that will not be identified for another twenty-one years.
evt-08-20-1909-pluto.prompt: What ultimately happens to this early photographic record of Pluto?

choices.text: It leads directly to Pluto's official discovery that same year
The plate is destroyed before anyone can study it
It sits unrecognized until later searches identify it retroactively
Observatory astronomers immediately announce a new planet

evt-08-20-1909-pluto.butterflyEffect: The image went unrecognized for decades until, after Clyde Tombaugh's 1930 discovery, astronomers combed archived plates and found Pluto had already been unknowingly photographed years earlier. The episode became a classic lesson in how discovery often depends on knowing what to look for, not just having the data.

evt-08-20-1910-washington-state.scenario: It is 20 August 1910 near Wallace, Idaho. Hurricane-force winds have merged hundreds of small fires into a firestorm racing through the forests of Washington, Idaho, and Montana, trapping your firefighting crew.
evt-08-20-1910-washington-state.prompt: As crew foreman Ed Pulaski, what do you do to save your men?

choices.text: Order the men to run downhill toward the nearest river
Lead the crew into an abandoned mine tunnel and hold them there against the smoke
Split the crew to search for multiple escape routes
Have the crew dig individual trenches and wait it out in the open

evt-08-20-1910-washington-state.butterflyEffect: Pulaski forced his men into the Nicholson mine tunnel, saving all but a handful from the inferno that killed roughly 87 people and burned about three million acres in two days. His survival story and tool design became foundational to American firefighting, and the disaster pushed the young U.S. Forest Service toward aggressive fire-suppression policy for decades.

evt-08-20-1950-korean-war.scenario: It is late August 1950 and your UN unit is dug in along the shrinking Pusan Perimeter in southeastern Korea. North Korean troops are pressing hard to break through before American reinforcements can arrive.
evt-08-20-1950-korean-war.prompt: Do you hold your position on the perimeter or pull back further south?

choices.text: Evacuate all forces by sea to Japan
Negotiate a local ceasefire with North Korean commanders
Hold the line and wait for reinforcements
Retreat further south toward Busan's port

evt-08-20-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: UN and South Korean forces held the Pusan Perimeter, denying North Korea a quick victory. That foothold gave General MacArthur time to prepare the Inchon landing in September 1950, which reversed the course of the war.

evt-08-20-1988-the-troubles.scenario: You are a young British Army soldier boarding a coach near Ballygawley, County Tyrone in August 1988, heading back to barracks after leave.
evt-08-20-1988-the-troubles.prompt: What happens to the bus on this journey?

choices.text: It is destroyed by an IRA roadside bomb
It passes through safely after a security search
It is ambushed by gunmen at a checkpoint
It is hijacked and diverted across the border

evt-08-20-1988-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: A Provisional IRA roadside bomb destroyed the bus, killing eight soldiers in one of the deadliest single attacks on British forces during the Troubles. The atrocity intensified pressure for hardened military transport and convoy procedures across Northern Ireland and fed into the grinding cycle of attack and reprisal that marked the conflict's later years.

evt-08-20-1988-yellowstone-fires-of-1988.scenario: It is 20 August 1988, later called 'Black Saturday.' Hurricane-force winds drive flames across Yellowstone, and more than 150,000 acres burn in a single day, threatening the historic Old Faithful Inn.
evt-08-20-1988-yellowstone-fires-of-1988.prompt: As park managers, what approach guides your response?

choices.text: Use controlled backburns exclusively without engaging the wildfire directly
Immediately evacuate and abandon all firefighting efforts
Call for aerial bombing to cut fire lines
Continue the long-standing 'natural burn' policy while defending structures directly threatened

evt-08-20-1988-yellowstone-fires-of-1988.butterflyEffect: Firefighters saved Old Faithful Inn and other key sites, but the fires burned on until autumn snows finally extinguished them, consuming over a third of the park. The scale of Black Saturday forced a public reassessment of the Park Service's 'let it burn' natural fire policy, reshaping wildfire management nationwide.

evt-08-20-1992-meitei-language.scenario: It's August 20, 1992, and you sit in India's Parliament as lawmakers debate amending the Constitution's Eighth Schedule to formally recognize languages spoken across the northeast, including Meitei from Manipur.
evt-08-20-1992-meitei-language.prompt: What do lawmakers decide about Meitei?

choices.text: Reject it for having too few speakers
Add it to the Eighth Schedule as an official scheduled language
Classify it as a dialect of Assamese
Postpone the decision indefinitely for further study

evt-08-20-1992-meitei-language.butterflyEffect: Meitei was added to the Eighth Schedule, guaranteeing it status in government use, education, and competitive exams. The recognition strengthened Manipuri cultural identity and encouraged other regional language communities to push for similar constitutional inclusion in later decades.

evt-08-20-1998-al-shifa-pharmaceutical-f.scenario: It's August 20, 1998, and cruise missiles are streaking toward a factory complex outside Khartoum, days after deadly bombings of US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania. You're a US official reviewing the target list, told the plant makes chemical weapons precursors tied to Osama bin Laden.
evt-08-20-1998-al-shifa-pharmaceutical-f.prompt: What does the US claim justifies striking the Al-Shifa factory?

choices.text: It manufactures chemical weapons precursors linked to al-Qaeda
It is a Sudanese army chemical weapons depot
It is a training camp for foreign fighters
It stores conventional weapons for the Sudanese government

evt-08-20-1998-al-shifa-pharmaceutical-f.butterflyEffect: The strike proved based on shaky intelligence: outside investigators and Sudan insisted the plant only made medicine. The bombing fueled anti-American anger in Sudan and became an early cautionary tale about weak evidence driving military strikes, a debate that resurfaced before the 2003 Iraq invasion.

evt-08-20-1998-supreme-court-of-canada.scenario: You are a constitutional lawyer in Ottawa in August 1998, awaiting the Supreme Court of Canada's answer to the reference question on whether Quebec can unilaterally declare independence.
evt-08-20-1998-supreme-court-of-canada.prompt: What does the Court rule on unilateral secession?

choices.text: Secession is declared legal only under international law
The Court declines jurisdiction over the political question
Quebec has an unrestricted right to secede at will
No unilateral right to secede, but a clear majority triggers a duty to negotiate

evt-08-20-1998-supreme-court-of-canada.butterflyEffect: The Court ruled Quebec had no right to secede unilaterally under Canadian or international law, but held that a clear referendum majority for secession would create a duty on Ottawa to negotiate in good faith. This reasoning directly shaped Parliament's 2000 Clarity Act, which set rules for judging referendum questions and majorities.

evt-08-20-1998-1998-united-states-embass.scenario: It is 20 August 1998, thirteen days after truck bombs devastated the US embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam, and you sit in on President Clinton's decision over how to retaliate.
evt-08-20-1998-1998-united-states-embass.prompt: What does the United States strike with cruise missiles in response?

choices.text: Libyan military airbases
Iraqi weapons research facilities
A pharmaceutical plant in Sudan and militant training camps in Afghanistan
Iranian nuclear research sites

evt-08-20-1998-1998-united-states-embass.butterflyEffect: Missiles hit the Al-Shifa pharmaceutical plant in Sudan, suspected of aiding chemical weapons production, and al-Qaeda training camps in Afghanistan, but bin Laden survived and the strikes were widely criticized as ineffective. The operation became an early, contested chapter in the growing confrontation between the US and al-Qaeda that culminated in the September 11 attacks three years later.

evt-08-20-2002-saddam-hussein.scenario: It's August 20, 2002, and you're among a group of Iraqi opposition activists who have just taken control of Iraq's embassy in Berlin, hoping to draw world attention to Saddam Hussein's rule months before an American-led invasion looms on the horizon.
evt-08-20-2002-saddam-hussein.prompt: How does the standoff at the embassy end?

choices.text: The activists are granted permanent asylum inside the embassy
Activists are killed in a police raid on the embassy
Iraqi security agents retake the embassy by force
Activists surrender peacefully after negotiations with police

evt-08-20-2002-saddam-hussein.butterflyEffect: The activists ended the occupation peacefully after negotiations with German authorities, releasing embassy staff without bloodshed. The brief incident drew international media attention to Iraqi exile opposition groups just as diplomatic tensions were escalating toward the 2003 US-led invasion of Iraq.

evt-08-20-2007-china-airlines-flight-120.scenario: You are a flight attendant on China Airlines Flight 120, which has just landed at Naha Airport on 20 August 2007 and is taxiing toward the gate. Smoke suddenly billows from beneath the right wing.

choices.text: Wait for ground crew to bring stairs to the gate
Continue taxiing until the aircraft reaches the gate
Keep passengers seated and call for fire trucks only
Immediate evacuation using the emergency slides

evt-08-20-2007-china-airlines-flight-120.butterflyEffect: The crew ordered an emergency evacuation via slides, and all 165 people aboard escaped before the aircraft burst into flames and was destroyed minutes later—remarkably with no deaths. Investigators traced the fire to a loose bolt that punctured a fuel tank, prompting Boeing and the FAA to issue new inspection directives for 737 fleets worldwide.

evt-08-20-2016-august-2016-gaziantep-bom.scenario: It is 20 August 2016, and you are among the guests dancing at a Kurdish wedding procession in Gaziantep, Turkey, when a suicide bomber detonates himself in the crowd.
evt-08-20-2016-august-2016-gaziantep-bom.prompt: Which group did Turkish authorities blame for the attack?

choices.text: The Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK)
The Islamic State (ISIL)
The Assad government
A Turkish nationalist militia

evt-08-20-2016-august-2016-gaziantep-bom.butterflyEffect: Turkish officials attributed the bombing to ISIL, which was seeking to punish Kurdish communities resisting its presence along the Syrian border. The atrocity hardened Turkey's resolve to intensify its cross-border military operations against ISIL in northern Syria in the following weeks.

evt-08-20-2018-silent-sam.scenario: You are a student on UNC-Chapel Hill's campus on the night of 20 August 2018. A crowd has gathered around the Confederate statue known as Silent Sam, ropes already looped around its bronze frame.
evt-08-20-2018-silent-sam.prompt: What happens to the statue that night?

choices.text: Administrators quietly remove it by crane before dawn
A court order postpones any action indefinitely
University police disperse the crowd and it stays standing
Protesters topple it from its pedestal

evt-08-20-2018-silent-sam.butterflyEffect: Protesters pulled Silent Sam from its pedestal, ending its 105-year presence on McCorkle Place. The university later removed the empty base, and the statue became the center of a prolonged legal fight over Confederate monuments, culminating in a contested 2019 settlement with a Confederate heritage group that a judge later voided.

evt-08-20-2020-joe-biden.scenario: It is 20 August 2020, and with the coronavirus pandemic emptying arenas nationwide, you tune in to watch the final night of the Democratic National Convention unfold almost entirely online.
evt-08-20-2020-joe-biden.prompt: How does Joe Biden accept the Democratic presidential nomination this year?

choices.text: He delivers it virtually from Delaware
He releases only a written statement
He holds a large in-person rally as usual
He skips the acceptance speech entirely

evt-08-20-2020-joe-biden.butterflyEffect: Biden delivered his acceptance speech from a nearly empty hall in Wilmington, Delaware, rather than before a packed convention crowd. The pandemic-shaped, largely virtual campaign that followed helped define his contest against incumbent Donald Trump, which Biden went on to win that November.

evt-08-21-1689-jacobitism.scenario: You are a Cameronian soldier holding the small town of Dunkeld in 1689, days after Bonnie Dundee died winning Killiecrankie. A much larger force of Jacobite Highlanders now storms the streets toward your position.
evt-08-21-1689-jacobitism.prompt: How do the outnumbered Covenanters survive the Jacobite assault?

choices.text: They abandon the town immediately without a fight
They charge out to meet the Highlanders in open cavalry formation
They barricade the houses and fight street by street, firing from windows
They negotiate a peaceful surrender with the clan chiefs

evt-08-21-1689-jacobitism.butterflyEffect: The Cameronians barricaded houses and poured fire from windows and doorways, grinding down the Highland charge in brutal street fighting until the Jacobites withdrew. Without Dundee's leadership, the rising lost momentum, and the failure at Dunkeld helped the 1689 Jacobite rebellion collapse within weeks.

evt-08-21-1716-ottoman-venetian-war-1714.scenario: You defend Corfu's fortress walls under Count Schulenburg as a massive Ottoman army presses its siege. Word arrives of an Austrian victory far to the north, and a violent storm has just struck the besiegers' camp.
evt-08-21-1716-ottoman-venetian-war-1714.prompt: What happens to the Ottoman siege of Corfu in the days that follow?

choices.text: Venice surrenders the island under negotiated terms
The Ottomans lift the siege and withdraw their forces
The siege settles into a years-long stalemate
The Ottomans storm and capture the fortress

evt-08-21-1716-ottoman-venetian-war-1714.butterflyEffect: News of Prince Eugene's victory at Petrovaradin, combined with storm damage and failed assaults, led the Ottomans to abandon the siege and withdraw. Corfu remained Venetian, though the war still ended in 1718 with Venice ceding the Peloponnese under the Treaty of Passarowitz.

evt-08-21-1717-austro-turkish-war-1716-1.scenario: You serve in Prince Eugene of Savoy's army outside besieged Belgrade in August 1717, caught between the Ottoman garrison inside the walls and a large relief army now approaching from the east.
evt-08-21-1717-austro-turkish-war-1716-1.prompt: What should Eugene's forces do before the two Ottoman forces can combine?

choices.text: Wait for reinforcements from Vienna before engaging either force
Withdraw the siege lines and retreat toward Austrian territory
Attack and defeat the relief army before it links up with the garrison
Offer the garrison generous terms to surrender immediately

evt-08-21-1717-austro-turkish-war-1716-1.butterflyEffect: Eugene struck the relief army in a bold night attack on 16 August and routed it, forcing Belgrade's garrison to surrender days later. The victory led to the 1718 Treaty of Passarowitz, which handed Belgrade and northern Serbia to the Habsburgs and marked the high point of Austrian expansion into the Balkans.

evt-08-21-1808-peninsular-war.scenario: It is 21 August 1808 near Vimeiro, Portugal. You stand in Sir Arthur Wellesley's ranks as General Junot's French columns advance up the ridge toward your thin red line.
evt-08-21-1808-peninsular-war.prompt: What tactic breaks the French assault at Vimeiro?

choices.text: A massed cavalry charge routs the French before they reach the ridge
The British abandon the ridge and retreat toward the coast
Artillery alone, without infantry support, disperses the attack
Volley fire from a thin two-deep line breaks the advancing French columns

evt-08-21-1808-peninsular-war.butterflyEffect: Wellesley's two-deep firing line shattered the French columns, and the defeat forced Junot to negotiate the Convention of Cintra, evacuating French troops from Portugal. The victory launched the Peninsular War proper and made Wellesley's reputation, though the generous terms of the convention caused outrage in Britain.

evt-08-21-1911-leonardo-da-vinci.scenario: It is the morning of 22 August 1911 at the Louvre, and a guard has just noticed an empty space on the wall where the Mona Lisa hung the day before. You are called in to help investigate the disappearance.
evt-08-21-1911-leonardo-da-vinci.prompt: What actually happened to the Mona Lisa after this theft?

choices.text: It was found within days in a Paris warehouse
It was recovered immediately from a rival museum in Berlin
It was recovered over two years later when the thief tried to sell it in Florence
It was never recovered and remains missing today

evt-08-21-1911-leonardo-da-vinci.butterflyEffect: The thief, museum employee Vincenzo Peruggia, kept the painting hidden in his Paris apartment for over two years before trying to sell it to a Florence art dealer in 1913, when he was caught. The sensational theft and recovery made the Mona Lisa a global celebrity, cementing its fame as the world's most recognized painting.

evt-08-21-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 21 August 1944 near Falaise. You are a Canadian officer whose troops have just linked up with the Polish 1st Armoured Division, sealing the last escape route for the trapped German Seventh Army.
evt-08-21-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What should the combined force do now that the Falaise gap is closed?

choices.text: Hold the ring tight and pound the trapped Germans with artillery and air power
Negotiate a local ceasefire with the trapped German commanders
Withdraw to consolidate a defensive line further north
Open a corridor to let German forces retreat peacefully

evt-08-21-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The closing of the Falaise pocket trapped and destroyed much of Germany's Army Group B, with tens of thousands captured or killed. The collapse opened the road to Paris and accelerated the liberation of France that autumn.

evt-08-21-1945-harry-daghlian.scenario: You are Harry Daghlian, working alone late at night at Los Alamos's Omega Site, stacking tungsten carbide bricks around a plutonium core to see how close it can safely come to criticality.
evt-08-21-1945-harry-daghlian.prompt: What happens when your hand slips and a brick falls onto the assembly?

choices.text: The brick bounces harmlessly off the outer casing
The brick pushes the assembly briefly critical, releasing a fatal radiation burst
Nothing happens because the core was not yet loaded
The assembly automatically shuts down without incident

evt-08-21-1945-harry-daghlian.butterflyEffect: The brick pushed the core briefly supercritical, flooding the room with radiation before Daghlian could disassemble it. He died 25 days later of radiation poisoning, and the same core later killed physicist Louis Slotin in 1946, earning it the grim nickname "the demon core" and prompting strict new criticality safety rules at Los Alamos.

evt-08-21-1963-army-of-the-republic-of-v.scenario: It is the night of 20-21 August 1963 in Saigon. You command a unit of Ngô Đình Nhu's special forces, disguised in regular army uniforms, with orders to move against the Xá Lợi Pagoda and other Buddhist temples.
evt-08-21-1963-army-of-the-republic-of-v.prompt: What order do you carry out against the pagodas that night?

choices.text: Storm the pagodas, arrest the monks, and suppress the Buddhist protest movement
Withdraw and report the mission as too politically risky
Cordon the pagodas but allow monks to leave freely
Negotiate with Buddhist leaders instead of using force

evt-08-21-1963-army-of-the-republic-of-v.butterflyEffect: The nationwide raids saw hundreds of monks arrested and pagodas ransacked, shocking the American press and public. Washington withdrew its backing from Diệm, paving the way for the November 1963 coup in which both Diệm and Nhu were killed.

evt-08-21-1983-ninoy-aquino.scenario: You are a reporter at Manila International Airport on 21 August 1983, watching exiled opposition leader Benigno Aquino Jr. descend the aircraft steps, tightly flanked by soldiers of the Marcos government.
evt-08-21-1983-ninoy-aquino.prompt: What happened to Aquino moments after he stepped onto the tarmac?

choices.text: He was placed straight onto a departing flight back to the US
He was quietly returned to prison without incident
He was shot and killed on the tarmac by his military escort
He addressed a cheering crowd of supporters unharmed

evt-08-21-1983-ninoy-aquino.butterflyEffect: Aquino was shot dead on the tarmac, an assassination widely blamed on the Marcos regime despite official denials. Public outrage over his killing fueled the opposition movement that culminated in the 1986 People Power Revolution, which toppled Marcos and installed Aquino's widow, Corazon, as president.

evt-08-21-1986-limnic-eruption.scenario: You live in a village near Lake Nyos, Cameroon, on the night of 21 August 1986. A strange rumbling sound rolls across the water, followed by an odd smell, moments before you and your neighbors begin to collapse.
evt-08-21-1986-limnic-eruption.prompt: What actually happened to the surrounding villages that night?

choices.text: A sudden volcanic eruption buried the villages in ash and lava
A dense carbon dioxide cloud flowed down the valleys and asphyxiated people and animals
An earthquake caused the lake's natural dam to collapse and flood the valley
A toxic algae bloom poisoned the lake's drinking water supply

evt-08-21-1986-limnic-eruption.butterflyEffect: A massive cloud of carbon dioxide erupted from the lake's depths and, being denser than air, flowed silently down the valleys, suffocating an estimated 1,700 people and thousands of livestock in their sleep. The disaster led scientists to install degassing pipes at Lake Nyos and prompted urgent monitoring of Lake Kivu in the Great Lakes region, where a similar eruption could threaten millions.

evt-08-21-1986-volcano.scenario: It is the night of 21 August 1986 near Cameroon's Lake Nyos. You wake to a strange hissing sound and a smell like rotten eggs drifting up from the valley below your village.
evt-08-21-1986-volcano.prompt: What should you do to survive the invisible cloud rolling out of the lake?

choices.text: Gather in the village square to wait for help
Run toward the lakeshore to see what happened
Stay low and shelter indoors
Climb to higher ground away from the valley floor

evt-08-21-1986-volcano.butterflyEffect: A massive cloud of carbon dioxide, released in a sudden limnic eruption, rolled down the valleys and settled in low ground, suffocating people, animals, and vegetation in nearby villages. Afterward, scientists installed degassing pipes in the lake to vent dissolved gas continuously and prevent another buildup.

evt-08-21-1991-latvia.scenario: It is 21 August 1991 in Riga. News is arriving that the coup against Gorbachev in Moscow is collapsing, and you sit in the Latvian Supreme Council chamber facing a vote on independence.
evt-08-21-1991-latvia.prompt: Do you vote to declare the full restoration of Latvian independence now?

choices.text: Wait for Moscow's formal approval first
Push instead for greater autonomy within the Union
Declare full independence immediately
Call for a new referendum before acting

evt-08-21-1991-latvia.butterflyEffect: The Council voted to declare full independence, seizing the moment of Soviet confusion. Latvia's move, alongside similar declarations by Estonia and Lithuania, was recognized internationally within months and set the country on the path to eventual EU and NATO membership.

evt-08-21-1991-1991-soviet-coup-attempt.scenario: It is 21 August 1991, and you command a tank unit ordered to storm the Russian parliament building where Boris Yeltsin and his supporters have gathered against the coup plotters in Moscow.
evt-08-21-1991-1991-soviet-coup-attempt.prompt: Do you carry out the order to storm the building, or refuse?

choices.text: Carry out the assault as ordered
Withdraw the unit entirely from Moscow
Negotiate with Yeltsin's supporters instead of attacking
Refuse the order and stand down

evt-08-21-1991-1991-soviet-coup-attempt.butterflyEffect: Military units across Moscow refused to fire on crowds and the White House, and the coup collapsed within three days. Its failure discredited the hardliners, elevated Yeltsin, and accelerated the Soviet Union's dissolution by December 1991.

evt-08-21-1993-nasa.scenario: You are a mission controller at JPL on 21 August 1993. Three days before Mars Observer is due to fire its engines and slip into Mars orbit, the spacecraft suddenly stops responding to every command you send.
evt-08-21-1993-nasa.prompt: What did the later investigation conclude actually caused the loss of Mars Observer?

choices.text: A ruptured fuel line during propellant pressurization disabled its systems
A software error shut down its onboard computer permanently
Its solar panels failed, draining all power reserves
It collided with an undiscovered asteroid en route to Mars

evt-08-21-1993-nasa.butterflyEffect: A review board concluded a ruptured fuel line during propellant pressurization likely caused an explosion that sent the craft tumbling and its antenna off-Earth-point, so it was never heard from again. The costly failure pushed NASA toward its "faster, better, cheaper" philosophy, and a leaner replacement, Mars Global Surveyor, launched successfully in 1996.

evt-08-21-1994-royal-air-maroc-flight-63.scenario: You are an investigator reviewing the cockpit voice recorder from Royal Air Maroc Flight 630, which crashed minutes after leaving Agadir on 21 August 1994.
evt-08-21-1994-royal-air-maroc-flight-63.prompt: What did the investigation conclude was the cause of the crash?

choices.text: A pilot deliberately caused the crash
A catastrophic engine failure went uncorrected
A bomb planted by hijackers detonated onboard
Severe turbulence caused loss of control

evt-08-21-1994-royal-air-maroc-flight-63.butterflyEffect: Investigators determined the crash was deliberately caused by one of the pilots. The case became one of aviation's early documented instances of pilot-induced crash, later cited in discussions of cockpit psychological screening and crew monitoring procedures.

evt-08-21-1995-atlantic-southeast-airlin.scenario: It is 21 August 1995, and you are piloting an Embraer EMB 120 climbing out of Atlanta when a propeller blade separates, tearing the left engine apart and rolling the aircraft violently toward the ground.
evt-08-21-1995-atlantic-southeast-airlin.prompt: With altitude and control slipping away, what should the crew attempt?

choices.text: Order an immediate mid-air evacuation
Shut down all engines and attempt a dead-stick return to Atlanta
Fight for control and glide toward the most survivable open terrain
Circle to burn off fuel before attempting any landing

evt-08-21-1995-atlantic-southeast-airlin.butterflyEffect: The pilots fought the crippled aircraft down toward a clearing near Carrollton, Georgia, and their emergency landing saved most of those aboard despite nine fatalities. The crash, echoing a similar 1991 accident, exposed a propeller design flaw and led to mandatory inspections and redesign across the fleet.

evt-08-21-2000-tiger-woods.scenario: You are Tiger Woods, 24 years old, tied with Bob May after 72 holes of the 2000 PGA Championship at Valhalla. A three-hole aggregate playoff now decides the title.
evt-08-21-2000-tiger-woods.prompt: How does Woods win the playoff and make history?

choices.text: He concedes the playoff after a poor opening hole
He wins the three-hole playoff by a single stroke over Bob May
He wins the playoff by five strokes in a rout
He loses the playoff but wins on a rules technicality

evt-08-21-2000-tiger-woods.butterflyEffect: Woods edged Bob May by one stroke in the playoff, completing the career Grand Slam at the youngest age ever. Weeks later he would hold all four major titles at once, a feat nicknamed the "Tiger Slam" that cemented his dominance of the sport.

evt-08-21-2013-ghouta-chemical-attack.scenario: You are part of a United Nations team arriving in the Damascus suburbs days after reports of a devastating attack on the Ghouta area on 21 August 2013, with survivors describing a chemical agent falling from rockets overnight.
evt-08-21-2013-ghouta-chemical-attack.prompt: What should the inspection team prioritize to establish what happened?

choices.text: Wait for opposition fighters to deliver evidence directly to Geneva
Withdraw immediately due to the security situation on the ground
Accept the Syrian government's official account without independent testing
Collect physical samples and survivor testimony to independently verify the chemical agent used

evt-08-21-2013-ghouta-chemical-attack.butterflyEffect: UN inspectors collected soil, blood, and tissue samples and interviewed survivors, confirming the nerve agent sarin had been used, one of the deadliest chemical attacks of the war. The findings helped push through a US-Russia brokered deal for Syria to surrender its chemical weapons stockpile to the OPCW, though the process was never fully completed and further chemical attacks occurred in later years.

evt-08-21-2015-thalys.scenario: You are a passenger aboard Thalys train 9364 from Amsterdam to Paris on 21 August 2015, when a man emerges from a restroom carrying an AK-47 and opens fire in the carriage.
evt-08-21-2015-thalys.prompt: What do the passengers do to stop the gunman?

choices.text: The driver stops the train and lets the attacker flee
Everyone stays hidden until police board the moving train
Passengers, including off-duty American servicemen, tackle and subdue him
Passengers negotiate with the attacker until he surrenders

evt-08-21-2015-thalys.butterflyEffect: Off-duty American servicemen and other passengers rushed and physically subdued the gunman before he could carry out a mass shooting, though one passenger was wounded. The men were later awarded France's Legion of Honour, and the attack led to new security screening measures on European high-speed rail lines.

evt-08-21-2017-solar-eclipse-of-august-2.scenario: It is midday on 21 August 2017 and you stand in Oregon's path of totality, crowds around you gasping as the sky darkens for the first coast-to-coast American eclipse in nearly a century.
evt-08-21-2017-solar-eclipse-of-august-2.prompt: How should you safely view the partial phases before and after totality?

choices.text: View it only through ordinary sunglasses
Watch it through an unfiltered telescope for a clearer view
Look directly at the sun without any protection the whole time
Use certified eclipse glasses or filters, removing them only during full totality

evt-08-21-2017-solar-eclipse-of-august-2.butterflyEffect: Millions across the US watched safely using certified solar filters and pinhole projectors, and the event was livestreamed worldwide, sparking a surge of public interest in astronomy. It became one of the most-observed eclipses in history, setting a template for later American eclipses like 2024.

evt-08-22-1485-battle-of-bosworth-field.scenario: It is 22 August 1485 on Bosworth Field. You are Richard III, and across the battlefield you spot Henry Tudor's banner, guarded by only a small company.
evt-08-22-1485-battle-of-bosworth-field.prompt: Do you lead a direct cavalry charge straight at Henry Tudor himself?

choices.text: Send an envoy to negotiate terms
Yes, charge straight for Henry Tudor to end the battle quickly
Hold position and let your larger army grind Henry's forces down
Retreat and regroup for another day

evt-08-22-1485-battle-of-bosworth-field.butterflyEffect: Richard charged and cut down Henry's standard-bearer, nearly reaching Henry, but William Stanley's forces intervened and Richard was killed—the last English king to die in battle. His death ended the Plantagenet dynasty and opened the Tudor era, as Henry married Elizabeth of York to unite the warring houses.

evt-08-22-1639-vijayanagara-empire.scenario: It is 1639, and you are Francis Day, an agent of the English East India Company, negotiating with Damarla Venkatapathy Nayak, a local chief governing under the fading authority of the Vijayanagara Empire, for a strip of coastline near a fishing village.
evt-08-22-1639-vijayanagara-empire.prompt: What does Day secure from the local ruler in this negotiation?

choices.text: A naval alliance against Portuguese traders
Permanent sovereign rule over the surrounding region
A lease of land for a fortified trading post
An exclusive monopoly on the regional silk trade

evt-08-22-1639-vijayanagara-empire.butterflyEffect: Day obtained a lease on the narrow coastal strip, where the Company soon built Fort St. George. That fort became the nucleus of the city of Madras (now Chennai), one of the earliest and most important English footholds in India, shaping centuries of colonial trade and administration.

evt-08-22-1642-charles-i-of-england.scenario: You stand in a field outside Nottingham Castle on 22 August 1642 as King Charles I orders his banner raised before a small, uncertain gathering of supporters.
evt-08-22-1642-charles-i-of-england.prompt: What does this act formally signal?

choices.text: A declaration of war against Scotland
His abdication in favor of his son
The formal start of civil war against Parliament
A reconciliation ceremony with Parliament

evt-08-22-1642-charles-i-of-england.butterflyEffect: Raising the standard was Charles's formal declaration of war against Parliament, marking the start of the English Civil War. The conflict would end in his defeat, trial, and execution in 1649, and briefly abolish the English monarchy altogether.

evt-08-22-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is August 1777, and British and Native American forces are besieging Fort Stanwix in New York. You are Benedict Arnold, marching to relieve the fort but heavily outnumbered.
evt-08-22-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: How do you break the siege without risking a pitched battle?

choices.text: Send a local to spread wild rumors of a huge approaching force
Wait for reinforcements from Washington before advancing
Attack directly with your full column at dawn
Offer the besiegers a bribe to withdraw

evt-08-22-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Arnold's agent, a mentally unstable local named Hon Yost Schuyler, convinced the besiegers that thousands of Patriot troops were approaching, and panic broke the siege without a shot fired from Arnold's column. The relief of Fort Stanwix secured the Mohawk Valley and helped doom Burgoyne's campaign, contributing to the pivotal American victory at Saratoga weeks later.

evt-08-22-1851-america-yacht.scenario: You are aboard the schooner America off the Isle of Wight on 22 August 1851, racing a fleet of British yachts around the island before Queen Victoria's watching court.
evt-08-22-1851-america-yacht.prompt: What happens when America crosses the finish line?

choices.text: The race is called off due to weather
A British yacht overtakes her in the final stretch
Judges declare a dead heat between two yachts
She wins outright, and the trophy is later renamed in her honor

evt-08-22-1851-america-yacht.butterflyEffect: America won decisively, and the trophy she claimed—the Hundred Guinea Cup—was later renamed the America's Cup after her. It became sailing's most prestigious prize, contested internationally for over 170 years since.

evt-08-22-1864-henry-dunant.scenario: It is 22 August 1864 in Geneva. Delegates from a dozen European states have gathered, moved by Henry Dunant's account of the suffering he witnessed after the Battle of Solferino, to formalize protections for those wounded in war.
evt-08-22-1864-henry-dunant.prompt: What do the Geneva delegates adopt on this day?

choices.text: A peace treaty ending the Franco-Prussian War
The First Geneva Convention on the treatment of wounded soldiers
An international arbitration treaty between Prussia and France
The founding charter of the League of Nations

evt-08-22-1864-henry-dunant.butterflyEffect: The delegates signed the First Geneva Convention, obligating armies to care for wounded soldiers regardless of nationality and to respect medical personnel and facilities marked with the red cross emblem. It became the foundation of modern international humanitarian law, expanded through later conventions covering prisoners of war and civilians.

evt-08-22-1978-nicaraguan-revolution.scenario: You are inside the National Palace in Managua on 22 August 1978 when armed Sandinista commandos led by 'Comandante Cero' storm the building during a legislative session, taking you and hundreds of officials hostage.
evt-08-22-1978-nicaraguan-revolution.prompt: How did the Somoza government respond to the hostage-takers' demands?

choices.text: It negotiated, paying ransom and freeing political prisoners
Somoza resigned on the spot to end the crisis
It ignored the commandos and waited them out
It stormed the palace immediately with the National Guard

evt-08-22-1978-nicaraguan-revolution.butterflyEffect: Somoza's government negotiated, paying ransom, releasing dozens of political prisoners including future leaders, and broadcasting FSLN statements nationwide. The raid's success emboldened the Sandinistas and galvanized public opposition, accelerating the insurrection that toppled Somoza less than a year later.

evt-08-22-1978-district-of-columbia-voti.scenario: It is August 1978 and you sit in the House chamber as members vote to send a constitutional amendment to the states, one that would finally give the District of Columbia full voting seats in Congress.
evt-08-22-1978-district-of-columbia-voti.prompt: What ultimately happened to the amendment after Congress passed it?

choices.text: It was ratified by all 50 states within a year
President Carter vetoed it before it reached the states
The Supreme Court struck it down before any state could vote
It failed after too few states ratified it within the deadline

evt-08-22-1978-district-of-columbia-voti.butterflyEffect: Congress sent the amendment to the states with a seven-year ratification deadline, but only 16 of the required 38 states approved it before it expired in 1985. DC residents remain without full voting representation in Congress to this day, keeping statehood and representation as live political issues.

evt-08-22-1991-iceland.scenario: It is 22 August 1991. The coup against Gorbachev has just collapsed, and Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania are pressing the world for recognition of the independence they declared months earlier. You are Iceland's foreign minister.
evt-08-22-1991-iceland.prompt: Do you extend formal recognition to the Baltic states now, ahead of larger Western powers?

choices.text: Offer only trade ties, not diplomatic recognition
Refuse recognition to avoid provoking Moscow
Yes, recognize immediately, becoming the first country to do so
Wait for the US and USSR to act first

evt-08-22-1991-iceland.butterflyEffect: On 22 August 1991, Iceland became the first nation to formally recognize the restored independence of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania, days before the Soviet Union itself did so. The gesture gave the Baltic states early diplomatic momentum, and streets and honors in their capitals still commemorate Iceland's move.

evt-08-22-1992-federal-bureau-of-investi.scenario: It is 22 August 1992 outside a remote cabin on Ruby Ridge, Idaho, where a standoff between Randy Weaver's family and federal agents has already turned deadly a day earlier.
evt-08-22-1992-federal-bureau-of-investi.prompt: What actually followed once it emerged an FBI sniper had killed Vicki Weaver during the siege?

choices.text: The rules were adopted permanently by all law enforcement agencies
Congress upheld the rules and expanded them nationwide
It had no lasting effect on federal procedure
It was condemned as unconstitutional and prompted reform of FBI deadly-force policy

evt-08-22-1992-federal-bureau-of-investi.butterflyEffect: An FBI sniper's shot killed Vicki Weaver, who was unarmed and holding her infant, during the standoff. Congressional hearings later found the rules of engagement had violated constitutional use-of-force standards, forcing a rewrite of FBI deadly-force policy, and the siege became a rallying symbol for the American militia movement through the 1990s.

evt-08-22-2006-grigori-perelman.scenario: It is August 2006 in Madrid, and the International Congress of Mathematicians has just confirmed that your proof of the Poincaré conjecture has earned you the Fields Medal, the highest honor in mathematics. Officials wait for your response before the ceremony.
evt-08-22-2006-grigori-perelman.prompt: What does Perelman actually do when offered the Fields Medal?

choices.text: He accepts it in person at the ceremony
He sends a colleague to accept it on his behalf
He declines to accept the medal
He donates the prize money before accepting

evt-08-22-2006-grigori-perelman.butterflyEffect: Perelman declined the medal, saying he was not interested in money or fame and was disillusioned with ethical standards in mathematics. He later also refused the $1 million Clay Millennium Prize for the same proof, becoming the only mathematician ever to turn down a Fields Medal, and retreated into seclusion in Saint Petersburg.

evt-08-22-2007-texas-rangers-baseball.scenario: It is 22 August 2007 at Camden Yards, and your Texas Rangers already lead the Baltimore Orioles by nearly twenty runs in the middle innings.
evt-08-22-2007-texas-rangers-baseball.prompt: Do you keep your regular hitters swinging away, or pull them to end the rout early?

choices.text: Deliberately make outs to shorten the game
Ask the umpires to end the game early by mutual agreement
Pull all starters immediately to spare the Orioles further embarrassment
Keep the lineup in and keep scoring

evt-08-22-2007-texas-rangers-baseball.butterflyEffect: Texas kept hitting and finished with 30 runs, the most scored by a team in a single game in the modern era, surpassing the Boston Red Sox's 29-run game from 1950. The lopsided rout remains one of the most extreme blowouts in MLB history and a fixture of the record books.

evt-08-22-2015-2015-shoreham-airshow-cra.scenario: It is the autumn of 2015 and you sit on a UK Civil Aviation Authority review board. A Hawker Hunter jet has just crashed onto the A27 during a loop at the Shoreham Airshow, killing eleven people on the ground, and you must decide how British airshows should change.
evt-08-22-2015-2015-shoreham-airshow-cra.prompt: What safety change actually followed the Shoreham disaster?

choices.text: All UK airshows were permanently cancelled
Vintage jets were restricted from aerobatic manoeuvres over crowds and roads
Jet aircraft were banned outright from all UK air displays
Only military pilots were allowed to fly in future displays

evt-08-22-2015-2015-shoreham-airshow-cra.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the pilot had misjudged the loop's height and speed. The CAA responded by banning high-energy aerobatics by older jets like the Hunter over land, widening the separation between display lines and the public, and tightening pilot display authorisation rules across UK airshows.

evt-08-23-1305-william-wallace.scenario: It is 23 August 1305, and you stand in Westminster Hall as William Wallace faces trial for treason and rebellion against King Edward I. The court demands he answer the charges laid against him.
evt-08-23-1305-william-wallace.prompt: What does Wallace do when asked to answer to the charge of treason?

choices.text: He pleads not guilty and demands trial by a jury of his peers
He escapes custody before the verdict can be read
He pleads guilty and begs the king for mercy
He refuses to plead, insisting he never swore allegiance to Edward I

evt-08-23-1305-william-wallace.butterflyEffect: Wallace argued he could never be a traitor since he had never sworn fealty to Edward I, but the court condemned him regardless. He was executed by hanging, drawing and quartering that same day, and his death turned him into a martyr whose memory helped fuel the resistance that won independence under Robert the Bruce at Bannockburn in 1314.

evt-08-23-1775-george-iii.scenario: It is August 1775 in London. News of Lexington, Concord, and Bunker Hill has reached the court, and you sit among the King's advisors deciding how George III should respond to the colonies in arms.
evt-08-23-1775-george-iii.prompt: What should the King proclaim regarding the American colonists?

choices.text: Ignore the unrest and wait for it to subside
Grant the colonies direct representation in Parliament
Declare the colonists in open and avowed rebellion
Send peace commissioners to negotiate new terms

evt-08-23-1775-george-iii.butterflyEffect: George III issued the Proclamation of Rebellion, formally declaring the American colonists in "open and avowed rebellion" and closing the door on informal reconciliation. The hardened stance pushed moderates in Congress toward independence, culminating in the Declaration of Independence less than a year later.

evt-08-23-1873-albert-bridge-london.scenario: It's 23 August 1873, and crowds line the Chelsea and Battersea embankments to watch Rowland Ordish's elegant new cable-stayed bridge open across the Thames. As carts and pedestrians cross, the deck flexes and sways beneath their feet.
evt-08-23-1873-albert-bridge-london.prompt: What odd warning sign later has to be posted at each end of the bridge?

choices.text: A ban on heavy goods wagons crossing at any time
A toll notice demanding extra fare for horse-drawn carts
All troops must break step when marching over the bridge
A speed limit sign restricting early motor vehicles

evt-08-23-1873-albert-bridge-london.butterflyEffect: Because the deck could resonate dangerously under rhythmic footsteps, signs were erected ordering marching troops to break step while crossing. The bridge's original design proved structurally unsound, forcing Bazalgette to add suspension-style elements in the 1880s, and the GLC later inserted concrete piers in 1973 — leaving today's odd three-style hybrid.

evt-08-23-1898-southern-cross-expedition.scenario: It is 1898, and Carsten Borchgrevink is assembling his crew for a radical plan: not just to sail past Antarctica, but to leave a party ashore for the entire winter night, something no one has attempted.
evt-08-23-1898-southern-cross-expedition.prompt: What method does Borchgrevink pioneer to move men and supplies across the ice?

choices.text: Relying on motorized snow tractors
Hauling everything by hand-pulled sledges
Using dogs and sledges
Transporting supplies by pony teams

evt-08-23-1898-southern-cross-expedition.butterflyEffect: The expedition became the first to over-winter on the Antarctic mainland and the first since Ross's 1839–43 voyage to land on the Great Ice Barrier, using dog sledges for polar travel. Their techniques and hard-won lessons directly informed the later, more famous expeditions of Scott and Shackleton.

evt-08-23-1914-world-war-i.scenario: It is 23 August 1914 near the Belgian town of Mons. You command a company of the British Expeditionary Force, dug in along a canal, watching the German First Army advance in overwhelming numbers.
evt-08-23-1914-world-war-i.prompt: What should the BEF do to survive this first clash of the war?

choices.text: Fight a delaying action, then withdraw in good order to preserve the army
Hold the canal line at all costs and refuse to retreat
Surrender the position to avoid casualties
Launch an immediate counterattack against the German columns

evt-08-23-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: After a stubborn defensive stand, the outnumbered BEF withdrew in what became the fighting retreat from Mons, part of the wider Great Retreat. That retreat bought time for French and British forces to regroup and halt the Germans at the Marne in September, turning the war of movement into the trench stalemate that defined the Western Front.

evt-08-23-1933-1933-chesapeake-potomac-h.scenario: It's 23 August 1933, and you're a resident of Norfolk, Virginia, listening to crackling radio warnings as a powerful hurricane bears down on the Chesapeake coast. Officials urge everyone in low-lying neighborhoods to leave before the storm arrives.
evt-08-23-1933-1933-chesapeake-potomac-h.prompt: What unusual event occurs in Norfolk as the hurricane's eye reaches the city?

choices.text: The hurricane suddenly reverses course out to sea
The Chesapeake Bay Bridge collapses under storm surge
The storm's eye passes directly over the city
The storm merges with a cold front and dissipates instantly

evt-08-23-1933-1933-chesapeake-potomac-h.butterflyEffect: The eye passed directly over Norfolk — the first time that had happened there since 1821 — before the weakening storm pushed north toward Washington, D.C., causing the worst tropical flooding the capital had seen since 1896. Advance warnings that prompted evacuations are credited with limiting the death toll despite severe property damage.

evt-08-23-1939-molotov-ribbentrop-pact.scenario: You are a Soviet diplomat in Moscow on 23 August 1939, watching Molotov and Ribbentrop sign a non-aggression pact that stuns capitals across Europe.
evt-08-23-1939-molotov-ribbentrop-pact.prompt: What secret arrangement accompanies the public treaty?

choices.text: A mutual defense pact against Japan
A secret protocol dividing Eastern Europe into spheres of influence
An economic union merging their currencies
A joint plan to invade Britain

evt-08-23-1939-molotov-ribbentrop-pact.butterflyEffect: A secret protocol divided Eastern Europe into Soviet and German spheres of influence, carving up Poland and assigning the Baltic states and Finland to Soviet control. Within days Germany invaded Poland, and the Soviets followed weeks later, triggering the outbreak of the Second World War.

evt-08-23-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It's August 1943, and you command a Red Army tank unit near Kursk, where the Wehrmacht has just launched its last great offensive push on the Eastern Front. Word comes down that Soviet forces are now driving the Germans back.
evt-08-23-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What is the lasting strategic consequence of the Soviet victory at Kursk?

choices.text: Germany immediately surrenders unconditionally
The strategic initiative on the Eastern Front shifts permanently to the Soviets
Berlin is liberated within weeks of the battle
The United States formally enters the war against Germany

evt-08-23-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: After Kursk, Germany never again mounted a major strategic offensive on the Eastern Front. The initiative passed permanently to the Red Army, which began a sustained westward advance through Ukraine and Belarus that would not stop until Berlin fell in 1945.

evt-08-23-1989-singing-revolution.scenario: It is 23 August 1989, fifty years after the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact carved up your homeland. Across Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania, people are leaving their homes to line the roads.
evt-08-23-1989-singing-revolution.prompt: What do the participants do to protest Soviet annexation?

choices.text: Stage a general strike in all three capitals
Form a human chain linking the three capitals
March on Soviet military barracks
Boycott all Soviet-run elections that year

evt-08-23-1989-singing-revolution.butterflyEffect: Roughly two million people joined hands to form a human chain nearly 675 kilometers long linking Tallinn, Riga, and Vilnius, known as the Baltic Way. The demonstration drew global attention to the Baltic states' demand for independence and helped accelerate their eventual break from the Soviet Union in 1991.

evt-08-23-1990-saddam-hussein.scenario: It's 23 August 1990, and you are among a group of Western nationals detained in Iraq following Saddam Hussein's invasion of Kuwait. Iraqi state television cameras are rolling as Saddam personally greets you and your family on camera.
evt-08-23-1990-saddam-hussein.prompt: What does Saddam do on air that becomes a widely condemned image abroad?

choices.text: He grants the detainees exit visas on the spot
He pats a young British boy on the head while holding the foreigners captive
He orders the hostages moved to luxury Baghdad hotels for the press
He announces the immediate release of all detained foreigners

evt-08-23-1990-saddam-hussein.butterflyEffect: Saddam patted a young British boy, Stuart Lockwood, on the head and asked if he was being fed and looked after, while holding him and other foreign nationals as de facto hostages at strategic sites. The broadcast was condemned worldwide as coercive propaganda and hardened international resolve, contributing to the coalition that would launch the Gulf War months later.

evt-08-23-1990-armenia.scenario: It is 23 August 1990 in Yerevan. You are a deputy in the Armenian Supreme Soviet as the chamber debates a declaration asserting Armenia's sovereignty amid the Soviet Union's unraveling.
evt-08-23-1990-armenia.prompt: How should the Supreme Soviet act on the question of independence?

choices.text: Vote to remain fully integrated within the Soviet Union
Postpone any declaration until Moscow approves it
Merge Armenia's government functions with a neighboring republic
Adopt a declaration asserting sovereignty and independence

evt-08-23-1990-armenia.butterflyEffect: The declaration asserted Armenia's sovereignty and set the country on a path to full independence, confirmed by referendum in September 1991 as the USSR collapsed.
