Independence coincided with the outbreak of the Nagorno-Karabakh War against Azerbaijan, which shaped Armenia's foreign policy for decades.

evt-08-23-1990-german-reunification.scenario: It is August 1990, less than a year after the Berlin Wall fell. Negotiators from East and West Germany have just settled on a date to formally dissolve the GDR and unite the country.
evt-08-23-1990-german-reunification.prompt: What date do they announce for reunification?

choices.text: May 8, the anniversary of VE Day
November 9, marking the anniversary of the Wall's fall
October 3
January 1, to start the new year as one nation

evt-08-23-1990-german-reunification.butterflyEffect: They chose 3 October 1990, which became German Unity Day, still celebrated annually. On that date East and West Berlin also formally reunified into a single city that would go on to become the capital of a reunified Germany.

evt-08-23-1991-world-wide-web.scenario: It is August 1991. You are Tim Berners-Lee, and your hypertext system for linking documents over the internet is ready to leave the confines of CERN.
evt-08-23-1991-world-wide-web.prompt: What do you do with your new system?

choices.text: Release it publicly and freely on the internet
License it exclusively to CERN's partner universities
Patent the technology before sharing it
Keep it as an internal CERN research tool

evt-08-23-1991-world-wide-web.butterflyEffect: Berners-Lee released the World Wide Web publicly, making its underlying protocols and software freely available to anyone. That open, royalty-free approach let the Web spread rapidly beyond research labs and become the foundation of the modern internet as ordinary people use it today.

evt-08-23-1994-eugene-bullard.scenario: It is the mid-1910s. You are a Black American living in France, eager to fly combat missions, but the United States military bars Black men from its air service.
evt-08-23-1994-eugene-bullard.prompt: What do you do to become a fighter pilot in World War I?

choices.text: Enlist in the British Royal Flying Corps instead
Wait for the U.S. Army Air Service to change its policy
Join the French Foreign Legion and later the French air service
Serve only as ground crew for an American unit

evt-08-23-1994-eugene-bullard.butterflyEffect: Eugene Bullard enlisted with French forces and became one of the war's few Black combat pilots, earning the nickname "L'Hirondelle noire." Though the U.S. denied him a commission at home, France later honored him, and his story became a landmark in the history of Black military aviation.

evt-08-23-2000-gulf-air-flight-072.scenario: It is the night of 23 August 2000, and you are the flight crew of Gulf Air Flight 072 executing a go-around over the dark waters near Bahrain after an aborted landing.
evt-08-23-2000-gulf-air-flight-072.prompt: What did investigators later identify as the cause of the crash?

choices.text: Spatial disorientation during the go-around over dark water
Fuel exhaustion before reaching the runway
An engine failure shortly after takeoff
A bird strike disabling the controls

evt-08-23-2000-gulf-air-flight-072.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew suffered spatial disorientation during the nighttime go-around over featureless water, losing awareness of the aircraft's attitude before it struck the sea. The disaster, the deadliest in Gulf Air's history, prompted renewed emphasis on crew training for disorientation and go-around procedures across the industry.

evt-08-23-2006-natascha-kampusch.scenario: It is 23 August 2006. You have been held for over eight years in a hidden cellar, and your captor has just left you alone to vacuum his car in the garden, the door momentarily unguarded.
evt-08-23-2006-natascha-kampusch.prompt: What should you do with this rare moment alone?

choices.text: Wait for a more certain opportunity to escape later
Hide inside the house until he leaves the property
Confront your captor directly when he returns
Run immediately and seek help from a neighbor

evt-08-23-2006-natascha-kampusch.butterflyEffect: Kampusch ran to a neighbor's garden and called police, ending her captivity. Her captor, Wolfgang Přiklopil, took his own life shortly after, and her later memoir and advocacy work brought lasting international attention to long-term captivity cases.

evt-08-23-2010-manila-hostage-crisis.scenario: It is the afternoon of 23 August 2010 in Rizal Park, Manila. You are a police commander outside a hijacked tourist bus, where a dismissed officer holds hostages and demands reinstatement, and hours of negotiation have gone nowhere.
evt-08-23-2010-manila-hostage-crisis.prompt: After the standoff drags on with no resolution, what does the assault team finally do?

choices.text: Cut off all media coverage of the standoff
Grant Mendoza's demand for reinstatement to end the crisis peacefully
Withdraw all officers and let the situation resolve itself
Storm the bus with an armed assault team

evt-08-23-2010-manila-hostage-crisis.butterflyEffect: After nightfall, police stormed the bus in a chaotic assault that ended with Mendoza and most of the Hong Kong hostages dead. The botched operation triggered a serious diplomatic rift between Hong Kong and the Philippines, including a travel advisory that lasted years.

evt-08-23-2011-2011-virginia-earthquake.scenario: It's early afternoon on 23 August 2011, and you're touring the National Mall in Washington, D.C. when the ground suddenly begins to shake. Around you, tourists scramble away from the monuments as alarms sound.
evt-08-23-2011-2011-virginia-earthquake.prompt: What famous D.C. landmark is later found damaged and closed for years after this quake?

choices.text: The Lincoln Memorial
The Washington Monument
The Jefferson Memorial
The U.S. Capitol dome

evt-08-23-2011-2011-virginia-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The Washington Monument suffered cracks near its top, forcing it to close for repairs that lasted nearly three years and cost millions of dollars. The National Cathedral also lost decorative pinnacles, prompting new scrutiny of East Coast seismic risk in a region considered largely quake-safe.

evt-08-23-2011-muammar-gaddafi.scenario: It is 23 August 2011 in Tripoli. You are among the rebel fighters closing in on Bab al-Azizia, Muammar Gaddafi's heavily fortified compound, after weeks of civil war.
evt-08-23-2011-muammar-gaddafi.prompt: What happens as rebel forces reach the compound's walls?

choices.text: Withdraw and besiege the compound indefinitely
Negotiate Gaddafi's peaceful surrender at the gates
Break through and capture the compound by force
Call off the assault to await NATO airstrikes alone

evt-08-23-2011-muammar-gaddafi.butterflyEffect: Rebels broke through and overran Bab al-Azizia, a symbolic collapse of Gaddafi's rule in the capital, though Gaddafi himself had already fled. He was captured and killed near Sirte two months later, ending his 42-year rule and plunging Libya into years of factional conflict.

evt-08-24-bce49-caesar-s-civil-war.scenario: It is 49 BC in Roman Africa. You are Gaius Scribonius Curio, commanding Caesar's legions against the Pompeian governor Attius Varus, who has allied with King Juba I of Numidia and his formidable cavalry.
evt-08-24-bce49-caesar-s-civil-war.prompt: With Juba's cavalry threatening to encircle you, what should Curio do?

choices.text: Retreat immediately to the coast and re-embark the army
Abandon the campaign and sail back to Sicily without engaging
Stand and fight the combined Numidian and Pompeian forces
Negotiate a truce with Juba directly

evt-08-24-bce49-caesar-s-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Curio chose to stand and fight rather than retreat to his ships, and his army was surrounded and annihilated by Juba's forces; Curio himself was killed. The disaster destroyed a key Caesarian army and left Africa in Pompeian hands until Caesar's later campaign there culminated in the Battle of Thapsus.

evt-08-24-79-eruption-of-mount-vesuvius-.scenario: It is 24 August 79 AD. You are Pliny the Elder, commander of the Roman fleet at Misenum, watching a monstrous cloud rise over Vesuvius across the bay as word arrives that terrified townspeople are trapped on the shore near Stabiae.
evt-08-24-79-eruption-of-mount-vesuvius-.prompt: What does Pliny the Elder decide to do?

choices.text: He sails his fleet toward the disaster to attempt a rescue
He abandons his post and flees inland with his family
He orders the fleet to remain anchored at Misenum for safety
He sends a single scout ship while the fleet stays behind

evt-08-24-79-eruption-of-mount-vesuvius-.butterflyEffect: Pliny sailed his ships toward Stabiae to attempt a rescue but died there, likely overcome by toxic fumes, becoming one of the disaster's few named victims. His nephew Pliny the Younger, watching safely from Misenum, later wrote detailed eyewitness letters that remain the primary historical account of the eruption and gave the 'Plinian' eruption its name.

evt-08-24-410-sack-of-rome-410.scenario: It is 24 August 410, and you are inside the walls of Rome as Alaric's Visigothic army finally breaks into the city after a long siege that has starved its people.
evt-08-24-410-sack-of-rome-410.prompt: What does Alaric's army largely do as it holds the city for three days?

choices.text: Loot the city while largely sparing churches and those sheltering in them
Enslave every surviving inhabitant
Massacre the entire population
Burn the city completely to the ground

evt-08-24-410-sack-of-rome-410.butterflyEffect: Alaric, himself a Christian, ordered his troops to spare churches and those who took sanctuary in them, notably St. Peter's Basilica, even while looting the city's wealth. The sack shattered the myth of Rome's invincibility across the empire, prompting Augustine to begin writing 'The City of God' in response to pagan accusations that Christianity had caused the disaster.

evt-08-24-1456-gutenberg-bible.scenario: It is 1456 in Mainz. You are examining a newly finished copy of Johannes Gutenberg's Bible, its uniform lines of type strikingly different from any handwritten manuscript you have seen.
evt-08-24-1456-gutenberg-bible.prompt: What made this printed Bible so revolutionary compared to earlier handwritten copies?

choices.text: It was hand-copied by monks working around the clock in shifts
It was produced with mass-produced movable metal type, enabling multiple copies
It was the first Bible ever translated into German
It was the first Bible written on paper instead of parchment

evt-08-24-1456-gutenberg-bible.butterflyEffect: Gutenberg's movable-type press could produce Bibles far faster than scribes could copy them by hand, launching Europe's print revolution. Within decades, presses spread from Mainz to hundreds of cities, accelerating the Reformation, scientific exchange, and rising literacy that reshaped the continent.

evt-08-24-1643-dutch-expedition-to-valdi.scenario: It is 24 August 1643, and your Dutch fleet, now without its late commander Hendrik Brouwer, has just sailed into the ruined harbor of Valdivia, hoping local Mapuche allies will help you hold this remote Chilean coast against Spain.
evt-08-24-1643-dutch-expedition-to-valdi.prompt: What ultimately happens to the new colony you name Brouwershaven?

choices.text: It is abandoned within months due to lack of supplies and support
It is traded to Spain in a peace settlement
Spain immediately recaptures it by force
It thrives and becomes a permanent Dutch trading post

evt-08-24-1643-dutch-expedition-to-valdi.butterflyEffect: Without reinforcements and as native support faded, the Dutch abandoned Valdivia on 28 October 1643, barely two months after landing. The scare nonetheless alarmed Spain enough to resettle Valdivia and build an extensive fortification network in 1645, and the expedition proved to be the Dutch Republic's last attempt to gain a foothold on South America's Pacific coast.

evt-08-24-1662-book-of-common-prayer-166.scenario: It is 24 August 1662, St Bartholomew's Day. You are a Church of England clergyman, and the new Act of Uniformity has just come into force, requiring every minister to publicly accept a revised liturgy or lose his parish.
evt-08-24-1662-book-of-common-prayer-166.prompt: What must you do to keep your parish living under the new Act of Uniformity?

choices.text: Petition Parliament for a Presbyterian alternative liturgy
Continue using the Interregnum's Directory of Public Worship
Ignore the act and conduct services in local vernacular forms
Publicly assent to and use the 1662 Book of Common Prayer exclusively

evt-08-24-1662-book-of-common-prayer-166.butterflyEffect: Clergy who refused to conform were ejected from their livings in the 'Great Ejection' of 1662, driving many Puritan ministers into Nonconformity and swelling England's dissenting churches. The 1662 book's prose, alongside the King James Bible, shaped English devotional language for centuries and remains in official use today.

evt-08-24-1704-war-of-the-spanish-succes.scenario: It is 24 August 1704, off the coast of Málaga. You serve aboard Admiral Rooke's Anglo-Dutch fleet, facing the French fleet under the Count of Toulouse just weeks after the Allies seized Gibraltar.
evt-08-24-1704-war-of-the-spanish-succes.prompt: What was the outcome of this fierce naval clash near Málaga?

choices.text: Neither fleet won decisively, but the Allies kept control of Gibraltar
A Spanish fleet intervened and defeated both sides
The French fleet destroyed the entire Anglo-Dutch fleet
The Anglo-Dutch fleet captured the whole French fleet

evt-08-24-1704-war-of-the-spanish-succes.butterflyEffect: The Battle of Málaga was tactically indecisive with heavy casualties on both sides, but the French fleet withdrew and never seriously challenged Allied control of Gibraltar again. Britain's grip on the Rock, secured that summer, proved permanent, giving the Royal Navy a lasting strategic foothold in the Mediterranean.

evt-08-24-1814-war-of-1812.scenario: It is the night of 24 August 1814. British troops have just routed the American defenders at Bladensburg and now march unopposed into an evacuated Washington, D.C.
evt-08-24-1814-war-of-1812.prompt: What do the British commanders order their troops to do in the captured capital?

choices.text: Loot but spare all government buildings
Occupy the city permanently as a new base
Negotiate an immediate surrender of the whole country
Burn the public buildings in a symbolic act of retaliation

evt-08-24-1814-war-of-1812.butterflyEffect: British forces torched the Capitol, the White House, and other public buildings in retaliation for earlier American burnings in Canada. A storm the next day helped douse the flames, and the humiliation galvanized American resolve, fueling resistance that culminated in the Treaty of Ghent ending the war on status quo terms.

evt-08-24-1889-1888-89-new-zealand-nativ.scenario: It's late 1888 in Britain, and you're one of the Māori players on New Zealand's first overseas rugby team, waiting in the tunnel before a crowd that has never seen anything like your side before.
evt-08-24-1889-1888-89-new-zealand-nativ.prompt: What do you and your teammates do before kickoff to introduce your team?

choices.text: March in silent formation around the pitch
Present ceremonial gifts to the opposing captain
Sing the British national anthem
Perform a haka

evt-08-24-1889-1888-89-new-zealand-nativ.butterflyEffect: The Natives became the first New Zealand team to perform a haka before a match and the first to wear all black, setting precedents that the All Blacks would follow for generations. The tour's impact on the sport's development in New Zealand led to the team's induction into the World Rugby Hall of Fame in 2008.

evt-08-24-1914-battle-of-cer.scenario: It is mid-August 1914. You are a Serbian soldier dug in around Cer Mountain, facing an invading Austro-Hungarian army just weeks after the war's outbreak.
evt-08-24-1914-battle-of-cer.prompt: What did Serbian forces achieve at the Battle of Cer?

choices.text: They retreated across the border into Bulgaria
They repelled the invasion, delivering the Allies' first victory of WWI
They were overrun and Belgrade fell immediately
They negotiated an immediate ceasefire with Austria-Hungary

evt-08-24-1914-battle-of-cer.butterflyEffect: Serbia's victory at Cer forced the Austro-Hungarian Fifth Army to retreat across the Drina and Sava rivers, embarrassing Vienna and lifting Allied morale in the war's opening weeks. Serbia would face renewed invasions and be overrun in 1915, but Cer exposed the empire's army as far weaker than expected, shaping Allied strategy in the Balkans.

evt-08-24-1941-adolf-hitler.scenario: It is August 1941, and as an aide close to Hitler, you have seen reports of growing public unease in Germany, including clergy protests, over the secret killing of institutionalized patients under the T4 program.
evt-08-24-1941-adolf-hitler.prompt: What does Hitler decide to do in response to the unrest?

choices.text: Order the program moved entirely to occupied Poland
Order the formal suspension of the T4 program
Order a public investigation to clear the program's name
Order the program expanded to cover more institutions

evt-08-24-1941-adolf-hitler.butterflyEffect: Hitler ordered a formal halt to the centralized T4 gassing program, but killings of disabled patients continued covertly through starvation and lethal injection in what became known as 'wild euthanasia.' Personnel and gassing techniques developed under T4 were later transferred to the extermination camps of the Holocaust.

evt-08-24-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 24 August 1942, and you are a dive-bomber pilot launching from USS Saratoga near Guadalcanal, scout reports having just located a Japanese carrier force escorting reinforcements to the island.
evt-08-24-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What target do American carrier aircraft strike to blunt the Japanese advance?

choices.text: The troop transports directly
The fleet carrier Shōkaku
The light carrier Ryūjō
The battleship Yamato

evt-08-24-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: American aircraft sank the light carrier Ryūjō, forcing Japan to turn back its troop reinforcement convoy for Guadalcanal. The battle was one of several costly carrier engagements that steadily eroded Japan's naval air power during the Guadalcanal campaign.

evt-08-24-1954-getulio-vargas.scenario: It is 24 August 1954 in the Catete Palace. Military leaders and much of the press are demanding your resignation amid a corruption and assassination scandal engulfing your government.
evt-08-24-1954-getulio-vargas.prompt: Facing the military's ultimatum, what does President Vargas do?

choices.text: Take his own life rather than step down
Dissolve Congress and declare martial law
Resign quietly and leave for exile
Call on loyal troops to crush the military's demands

evt-08-24-1954-getulio-vargas.butterflyEffect: Vargas shot himself rather than resign, leaving a suicide letter denouncing foreign and domestic 'forces' against him. The letter turned public sympathy sharply in his favor, discrediting his opponents and helping his political heirs, including Juscelino Kubitschek, win power and continue his nationalist, developmentalist policies.

evt-08-24-1963-buddhist-crisis.scenario: It is 24 August 1963 in Saigon. A State Department cable has just reached you, Ambassador Henry Cabot Lodge Jr., instructing you on how to handle a South Vietnamese government cracking down on Buddhist dissent.
evt-08-24-1963-buddhist-crisis.prompt: What does Washington instruct Lodge to do about President Diem's government?

choices.text: Explore removing support from Diem and back potential coup plotters
Withdraw all American personnel from Vietnam immediately
Arrange for Diem's family to be granted asylum abroad
Publicly reaffirm unconditional support for Diem

evt-08-24-1963-buddhist-crisis.butterflyEffect: The cable directed Lodge to signal to South Vietnamese generals that Washington would not object to a coup against Diem if he did not curb the repression. This set in motion the November 1963 coup in which Diem was overthrown and killed, deepening America's political entanglement in South Vietnam just weeks before Kennedy's own assassination.

evt-08-24-1992-hurricane-andrew.scenario: It's the evening of 23 August 1992. You live in Homestead, Florida, and forecasters warn that Andrew has rapidly strengthened into a compact but extremely intense hurricane bearing down on South Dade County by morning.
evt-08-24-1992-hurricane-andrew.prompt: What is the safest decision for a resident to make tonight?

choices.text: Wait until morning since hurricane forecasts often change
Board up the windows and shelter inside a mobile home
Stay to protect the property using sandbags alone
Evacuate inland immediately, away from the storm's path

evt-08-24-1992-hurricane-andrew.butterflyEffect: Andrew struck the next morning as a Category 5 hurricane, stripping many houses down to their concrete slabs and flattening whole neighborhoods, especially mobile home communities. The catastrophic toll of 65 deaths and $27.3 billion in damage forced Florida to overhaul its building codes, producing some of the strictest hurricane-resistant construction standards in the country.

evt-08-24-2006-international-astronomica.scenario: It is 24 August 2006 in Prague. As a member astronomer at the IAU General Assembly, you are about to cast a vote on a controversial new definition of 'planet.'
evt-08-24-2006-international-astronomica.prompt: What does the IAU vote to do regarding Pluto's status?

choices.text: Leave Pluto's planetary status unchanged
Add several new bodies as full planets alongside Pluto
Rename Pluto entirely and strike it from all records
Reclassify Pluto as a dwarf planet

evt-08-24-2006-international-astronomica.butterflyEffect: The assembly adopted a definition requiring a planet to gravitationally dominate its orbital zone, and Pluto—unable to clear its neighborhood of other objects—was reclassified as a 'dwarf planet.' The decision remains debated among scientists and the public, and it added extra resonance to NASA's New Horizons probe, already en route to Pluto at the time.

evt-08-24-2016-august-2016-central-italy.scenario: It is 3:36 a.m. on 24 August 2016. You are a civil protection officer rushing toward Amatrice, where a violent earthquake has just collapsed centuries-old stone buildings across the mountains of central Italy.
evt-08-24-2016-august-2016-central-italy.prompt: What did Italian authorities prioritize in the earthquake's immediate aftermath?

choices.text: Suspending parliament to declare martial law
Closing all of Italy's national borders
Evacuating coastal areas for a feared tsunami
Deploying search-and-rescue teams to pull survivors from the rubble

evt-08-24-2016-august-2016-central-italy.butterflyEffect: Rescue teams worked through the rubble of towns like Amatrice and Pescara del Tronto, but the quake's shallow depth and old masonry construction caused catastrophic damage. The disaster renewed national debate over enforcing seismic building codes in Italy's historic hill towns, and a special reconstruction commissioner was appointed to oversee rebuilding, a process still incomplete years later.

evt-08-24-2020-erin-o-toole.scenario: It is August 2020. You are a Conservative Party of Canada delegate counting leadership ballots, choosing a successor to Andrew Scheer from a field including Peter MacKay and Erin O'Toole.
evt-08-24-2020-erin-o-toole.prompt: Who won the leadership race to become Leader of the Official Opposition?

choices.text: Derek Sloan
Erin O'Toole
Peter MacKay
Leslyn Lewis

evt-08-24-2020-erin-o-toole.butterflyEffect: O'Toole won on the third ballot, positioning himself as a 'true blue' conservative before pivoting toward the centre ahead of the 2021 election. He led the Conservatives to a popular-vote win but fewer seats than Trudeau's Liberals, and his own caucus ousted him in February 2022 after the disappointing result.

evt-08-24-2023-discharge-of-radioactive-.scenario: It is August 2023, and you work for Japan's fisheries ministry as the government prepares to act on over a decade of accumulated, treated wastewater from the wrecked Fukushima Daiichi plant, despite objections from local fishermen and neighboring countries.
evt-08-24-2023-discharge-of-radioactive-.prompt: What does the Japanese government proceed to do with the treated water?

choices.text: Divert the water for agricultural irrigation
Store the water indefinitely in new tanks
Ship the water abroad for disposal
Begin releasing the treated water into the Pacific Ocean

evt-08-24-2023-discharge-of-radioactive-.butterflyEffect: Japan began discharging the treated water into the Pacific Ocean in a process expected to continue for decades. China responded by banning imports of Japanese seafood, straining relations, while the IAEA maintained ongoing monitoring to reassure the public about safety.

evt-08-25-1270-philip-iii-of-france.scenario: You stand in the crusader camp outside Tunis in August 1270. King Louis IX has just died of illness during the Eighth Crusade, and his son Philip, still young and untested, must now be recognized as king far from home.
evt-08-25-1270-philip-iii-of-france.prompt: What should the crusader nobles do with the new king and the stalled campaign?

choices.text: Continue the siege of Tunis under Philip's command
Proclaim Philip king and withdraw the army toward France
Wait for confirmation from the Pope before acting
Return the throne to a regency council in Paris

evt-08-25-1270-philip-iii-of-france.butterflyEffect: Philip III was proclaimed king on the spot and led the army back to France, where he was formally anointed at Reims in 1271. The Eighth Crusade effectively ended with his father's death, and Philip's reign began under the shadow of a failed campaign and a fragile succession.

evt-08-25-1609-galileo-galilei.scenario: You are a Venetian senator in August 1609, watching a Tuscan mathematician named Galileo demonstrate a tube of lenses that makes distant ships and towers appear startlingly close.
evt-08-25-1609-galileo-galilei.prompt: What does the Venetian Senate do after seeing the device work?

choices.text: Order it destroyed as dangerous magic
Send it directly to Rome for the Pope's approval
Dismiss it as a mere parlor trick
Reward him and secure the instrument for the Republic

evt-08-25-1609-galileo-galilei.butterflyEffect: Impressed by its military and naval value, the Senate rewarded Galileo with a lifetime lectureship at Padua. Within months he turned the instrument skyward instead of seaward, discovering the moons of Jupiter and craters on the Moon, launching the observational astronomy that would eventually put him at odds with the Church.

evt-08-25-1835-the-sun-new-york-city.scenario: You are a printer at the New York Sun in August 1835, setting type for a sensational new series claiming a British astronomer has spotted bat-winged men and unicorns on the moon through a giant telescope.
evt-08-25-1835-the-sun-new-york-city.prompt: What should the paper do about the story's shaky sourcing before running it?

choices.text: Label it clearly as fiction or satire
Refuse to run an unverifiable science story
Contact Herschel in South Africa to verify it first
Print it as sensational fact to boost sales

evt-08-25-1835-the-sun-new-york-city.butterflyEffect: The Sun ran the 'Great Moon Hoax' anyway, falsely crediting astronomer Sir John Herschel, and circulation soared past every rival paper in the world. The hoax was never fully retracted, and it became a landmark case study in how a credible-sounding newspaper could manufacture mass belief.

evt-08-25-1875-matthew-webb.scenario: You stand on the shingle at Dover in August 1875, coated in porpoise oil, about to wade into the English Channel for an attempt that no unaided swimmer has ever completed, with only breaststroke and a following boat to guide you.
evt-08-25-1875-matthew-webb.prompt: What must you do to have any chance of reaching France alive?

choices.text: Swim steadily with the tides and pace yourself for many hours
Sprint as fast as possible from the start
Use a small flotation aid to conserve energy
Wait for a calm day and swim only at night

evt-08-25-1875-matthew-webb.butterflyEffect: Matthew Webb swam nearly 22 miles over almost 22 hours, fighting currents and jellyfish stings, and became the first person to swim the Channel without artificial aids. His feat made him a national celebrity and helped spark a Victorian craze for competitive and recreational swimming.

evt-08-25-1975-bruce-springsteen.scenario: You are Bruce Springsteen in a New York studio in 1975, months behind schedule and convinced the tapes for your make-or-break third album sound wrong. Columbia Records is losing patience and your career hangs on this record.
evt-08-25-1975-bruce-springsteen.prompt: What does Springsteen do to rescue the stalled 'Born to Run' sessions?

choices.text: Delay release indefinitely until a bigger label offer arrives
Scrap the sessions and release a live album instead
Fire the E Street Band and re-record with session musicians
Bring in rock critic Jon Landau as co-producer to reshape the sound

evt-08-25-1975-bruce-springsteen.butterflyEffect: He brought in critic Jon Landau as co-producer to help tighten the arrangements and mix. The finished album made Springsteen a star, landing him simultaneously on the covers of Time and Newsweek and launching his decades-long partnership with Landau as manager.

evt-08-25-1991-battle-of-vukovar.scenario: It is late August 1991. You are a lightly armed Croatian National Guard volunteer inside Vukovar, encircled by a vastly larger Yugoslav People's Army force with tanks and artillery. Reinforcements are uncertain and the shelling is constant.
evt-08-25-1991-battle-of-vukovar.prompt: Do you hold your position inside the city, hoping to buy time for Croatia?

choices.text: Negotiate an immediate surrender to spare the population further bombardment
Abandon the city immediately to save the garrison for a fight elsewhere
Request Yugoslav federal peacekeepers to enter and separate the sides
Hold your position and keep resisting, hoping reinforcements or international pressure arrive

evt-08-25-1991-battle-of-vukovar.butterflyEffect: The defenders held on for 87 days before Vukovar fell on 18 November 1991, far longer than anyone expected against JNA armor and artillery. The siege bought Croatia crucial time to organize its new army, and the city's fall was followed by mass killings of prisoners and civilians, later prosecuted as war crimes at the ICTY, making Vukovar a lasting symbol of the war.

evt-08-25-1991-linus-torvalds.scenario: You are a 21-year-old computer science student in Helsinki in 1991, having built a small kernel for your 386 PC just to learn how the hardware works. You're not sure anyone outside your room would care about it.
evt-08-25-1991-linus-torvalds.prompt: What does Torvalds do with his hobby kernel?

choices.text: Keep it private and use it only for his own coursework
Post the source code publicly and invite others to try it and contribute
Sell it to a software company and abandon further work
Submit it as a patch to the existing Minix operating system only

evt-08-25-1991-linus-torvalds.butterflyEffect: He posted it to the comp.os.minix newsgroup, calling it "just a hobby, won't be big and professional," and invited others to look at the source. Volunteer programmers worldwide began contributing, and that hobby kernel grew into Linux, the foundation of Android, most web servers, and countless embedded systems.

evt-08-25-1997-egon-krenz.scenario: You are Egon Krenz, once East Germany's last Communist leader, standing before a Berlin court in 1997 to answer for deaths of people shot trying to cross the Wall during his years in the Politburo.
evt-08-25-1997-egon-krenz.prompt: What verdict does the court reach against Krenz?

choices.text: Acquitted on grounds he had no direct command authority
Convicted of manslaughter over Wall deaths and sentenced to prison
Sentenced to death for crimes against the state
Given only a suspended sentence and a public apology requirement

evt-08-25-1997-egon-krenz.butterflyEffect: Krenz was convicted of manslaughter for his role in the shoot-to-kill border policy and sentenced to six and a half years in prison. The ruling became a landmark in Germany's efforts to hold former GDR leaders legally accountable for Cold War-era killings, though Krenz was paroled after serving part of the term.

evt-08-25-2001-aaliyah.scenario: It is August 25, 2001, at Marsh Harbour airport in the Bahamas. The video shoot for 'Rock the Boat' has wrapped, luggage and passengers are being crammed onto a small twin-engine plane, and everyone is eager to fly out that night.
evt-08-25-2001-aaliyah.prompt: What should the crew do about the overloaded aircraft before departure?

choices.text: Board as planned to keep the schedule
Reduce weight or wait for a second flight
Fly at a lower altitude to compensate
Switch pilots but keep the same load

evt-08-25-2001-aaliyah.butterflyEffect: The plane took off overloaded and crashed moments later, killing Aaliyah and eight others aboard. Investigators found the pilot was not properly certified for that aircraft and it was carrying far more weight than allowed, and the tragedy became a widely cited case in aviation safety discussions about small charter flights.

evt-08-25-2011-2011-monterrey-casino-att.scenario: It is August 2011 and news breaks that gunmen linked to Los Zetas have set fire to the Casino Royale in Monterrey, killing dozens of patrons and staff trapped inside. Outrage spreads across Mexico within hours.
evt-08-25-2011-2011-monterrey-casino-att.prompt: How did the Mexican government respond to the public fury over the attack?

choices.text: Deployed foreign peacekeeping troops to Monterrey
Opened negotiations for amnesty with Los Zetas leadership
Declared national mourning and intensified military operations against Los Zetas
Withdrew federal forces from Nuevo León to avoid provoking further attacks

evt-08-25-2011-2011-monterrey-casino-att.butterflyEffect: President Felipe Calderón declared national mourning and vowed to intensify the military-led offensive against Los Zetas in Nuevo León. The attack became a defining atrocity of Mexico's drug war, hardening public demand for a crackdown even as violence continued to escalate in the years that followed.

evt-08-25-2012-richard-iii-of-england.scenario: You are an archaeologist in Leicester in August 2012, digging beneath a council car park believed to sit atop the ruins of Grey Friars church, hunting for the lost grave of a king killed in battle over five centuries earlier.
evt-08-25-2012-richard-iii-of-england.prompt: What should the team look for to confirm the skeleton is Richard III?

choices.text: Armor fragments buried alongside the body
Skeletal trauma and spinal curvature matching records, then DNA testing
Royal jewelry found in the grave
A signed inscription on the coffin lid

evt-08-25-2012-richard-iii-of-england.butterflyEffect: The skeleton showed a curved spine and battle wounds matching historical accounts, and DNA comparison with living descendants confirmed it was Richard III. He was reburied with royal honors at Leicester Cathedral in 2015, closing a 527-year mystery about England's last Plantagenet king.

evt-08-25-2017-hurricane-harvey.scenario: It is 25 August 2017 and Hurricane Harvey is bearing down on Houston as a powerful Category 4 storm. City officials, remembering the deadly gridlock when residents fled Hurricane Rita in 2005, urge you to stay put rather than hit the highways.
evt-08-25-2017-hurricane-harvey.prompt: Do you shelter in place at home, as Houston's mayor is urging, or try to evacuate?

choices.text: Move immediately to a coastal shelter near Galveston
Wait for a state-ordered evacuation before deciding
Shelter in place at home, following the city's guidance
Join a mass evacuation out of the metro area by highway

evt-08-25-2017-hurricane-harvey.butterflyEffect: Houston's leadership chose not to order a mass evacuation, wary of repeating the fatal traffic chaos of the 2005 Rita evacuation. Harvey then stalled over the region for days, dumping record rainfall that flooded hundreds of thousands of homes and forced more than 17,000 water rescues, reviving fierce debate over evacuate-versus-shelter policy for future storms.

evt-08-25-2017-conflict-in-rakhine-state.scenario: It is late August 2017. You oversee a crossing point on the Bangladesh side of the Naf River as tens of thousands of Rohingya civilians arrive daily, fleeing violence in Myanmar's Rakhine State with almost nothing.
evt-08-25-2017-conflict-in-rakhine-state.prompt: Do you open the border and let the refugees cross into Bangladesh?

choices.text: Open the border and admit the refugees despite the strain on resources
Allow only registered ARSA-linked families to cross
Seal the border until Myanmar agrees to a formal repatriation deal
Turn refugees back and refer the crisis to the United Nations first

evt-08-25-2017-conflict-in-rakhine-state.butterflyEffect: Bangladesh chose to open its border, and by late September 2017 roughly 500,000 refugees had crossed, swelling Kutupalong into the world's largest refugee camp. The crisis drew UN accusations of ethnic cleansing against Myanmar's military and led to an ongoing genocide case at the International Court of Justice, while hundreds of thousands remain in camps years later.

evt-08-26-1346-hundred-years-war.scenario: It is 26 August 1346 near Crécy, and you stand with the English archers on a gentle hillside. Below, Genoese crossbowmen and French knights are massing for a charge across open ground.
evt-08-26-1346-hundred-years-war.prompt: What tactic should the English longbowmen use to break the French assault?

choices.text: Charge downhill on horseback to meet the French knights head-on
Retreat into the woods to draw the French into a forest ambush
Send envoys to negotiate terms before battle begins
Hold formation on the high ground and fire massed volleys as the enemy advances

evt-08-26-1346-hundred-years-war.butterflyEffect: The English held their defensive position and loosed devastating massed volleys, cutting down Genoese crossbowmen and unhorsing French knights before they could close. The stunning victory proved the longbow could defeat armored cavalry, shattered French nobility's ranks, and set the tactical pattern England would repeat at Poitiers and Agincourt.

evt-08-26-1748-lutheranism.scenario: It is 26 August 1748 in colonial Pennsylvania. You are a German-speaking Lutheran pastor meeting with colleagues under Henry Muhlenberg's guidance to bring order to the scattered Lutheran congregations of the colonies.
evt-08-26-1748-lutheranism.prompt: What did the assembled pastors do to formalize Lutheran church life in North America?

choices.text: Adopted the Book of Common Prayer for their services
Petitioned the Church of England to absorb their congregations
Founded the Pennsylvania Ministerium as an organized synod
Voted to dissolve all ties between congregations

evt-08-26-1748-lutheranism.butterflyEffect: The pastors founded the Pennsylvania Ministerium, the first organized Lutheran synod in North America, giving scattered German congregations a shared structure and liturgy. Under Muhlenberg's leadership it became the model for later American Lutheran synods, shaping the denomination's growth across the expanding United States.

evt-08-26-1826-quincy-market.scenario: It's the early 1820s and you're Boston Mayor Josiah Quincy. Stalls around Faneuil Hall have spilled into the surrounding streets, choking traffic, and the city desperately needs a new market hall without burdening taxpayers.
evt-08-26-1826-quincy-market.prompt: How do you fund and build the new market complex?

choices.text: Cut funding for other municipal services to cover construction costs
Fund construction with bonds repaid by market stall lease revenue on new landfill
Rely entirely on private investors with no city involvement
Impose a special tax on all merchants in the city

evt-08-26-1826-quincy-market.butterflyEffect: Quincy financed the project through filled tidal land and revenue from long-term stall leases, completing the market in 1826 without raising taxes. The self-financing model made the project a celebrated example of civic infrastructure, and the complex's later 1970s revival as Faneuil Hall Marketplace became a template for festival-marketplace urban renewal projects across the United States.

evt-08-26-1883-1883-eruption-of-krakatoa.scenario: It is 27 August 1883 in the Sunda Strait. Krakatoa has just produced its final, catastrophic explosion, and the sea itself is drawing back in an unnatural way along the coast.
evt-08-26-1883-1883-eruption-of-krakatoa.prompt: What should coastal villagers and sailors do in the minutes that follow?

choices.text: Move inland to high ground immediately, away from the shoreline
Gather on the beach to watch the retreating water
Sail closer to the island to see the eruption firsthand
Stay aboard ships in the harbor, believing they are safest at anchor

evt-08-26-1883-1883-eruption-of-krakatoa.butterflyEffect: Those who fled to high ground survived; tsunamis up to 30 meters high soon swept away entire coastal towns, killing more than 36,000 people. Ash thrown into the stratosphere lowered global temperatures for years and produced vivid red sunsets worldwide, while telegraph reports made it one of the first disasters known globally within hours.

evt-08-26-1920-nineteenth-amendment-to-t.scenario: You are U.S. Secretary of State Bainbridge Colby in August 1920. Tennessee has just become the 36th state to ratify the women's suffrage amendment, but it is not yet law until your office acts.
evt-08-26-1920-nineteenth-amendment-to-t.prompt: What does Colby do to make the Nineteenth Amendment official?

choices.text: Wait for two more states to ratify before certifying
Call for a nationwide referendum to confirm the states' votes
Sign the official proclamation certifying the amendment's ratification
Refer the ratification to the Supreme Court for review

evt-08-26-1920-nineteenth-amendment-to-t.butterflyEffect: Colby signed the certification of ratification on August 26, 1920, formally adding the amendment to the Constitution. Millions of American women were able to vote in the presidential election that November, just weeks later.

evt-08-26-1928-paisley-renfrewshire.scenario: It's August 26, 1928, at the Wellmeadow café in Paisley. Your friend has just poured you a glass of ginger beer from an opaque bottle, and as the last of it comes out, a decomposed snail tumbles into your glass. You feel shaken and ill.
evt-08-26-1928-paisley-renfrewshire.prompt: What should May Donoghue do about the snail in her drink?

choices.text: File a criminal complaint against the café for unsafe food handling
Sue the manufacturer directly for damages despite having no contract with him
Do nothing, since she never bought the bottle from the manufacturer herself
Complain only to the café owner since he sold her the bottle

evt-08-26-1928-paisley-renfrewshire.butterflyEffect: Donoghue sued the ginger beer manufacturer, Stevenson, even though she had no direct contract with him, having bought the bottle through a friend. The case reached the House of Lords as Donoghue v Stevenson (1932), establishing the "neighbour principle" that manufacturers owe consumers a duty of care regardless of contract, a cornerstone of modern negligence law across common law countries.

evt-08-26-1968-the-beatles.scenario: It's August 1968, and as a radio programmer you've just received the Beatles' new single, "Hey Jude." At over seven minutes, it runs far longer than any pop single your station normally airs.
evt-08-26-1968-the-beatles.prompt: Do you cut the song for airplay or run it in full?

choices.text: Play it in full despite its unusual length
Refuse to air it, citing its excessive runtime
Ask for the song to be released as a two-part single instead
Trim the extended "na na na" coda to fit a standard three-minute slot

evt-08-26-1968-the-beatles.butterflyEffect: Stations played "Hey Jude" uncut, coda and all, and it topped the UK charts as the longest single to do so up to that point. It became the Beatles' best-selling single ever and the first release on their new Apple Records label, a step toward greater creative and business independence from EMI.

evt-08-26-1978-august-1978-conclave.scenario: It is 26 August 1978 inside the Sistine Chapel. You are a cardinal elector casting a fourth ballot after earlier rounds failed to give any candidate the required two-thirds majority.
evt-08-26-1978-august-1978-conclave.prompt: Which relatively little-known cardinal did the conclave finally elect as a compromise candidate?

choices.text: Albino Luciani, Patriarch of Venice
Karol Wojtyła, Archbishop of Kraków
Giovanni Benelli, Archbishop of Florence
Sebastiano Baggio, Prefect of the Congregation for Bishops

evt-08-26-1978-august-1978-conclave.butterflyEffect: The conclave chose Albino Luciani, Patriarch of Venice, who took the name John Paul I. He died only 33 days later, prompting a second conclave in October 1978 that elected Karol Wojtyła as John Paul II, the first non-Italian pope in over 450 years and a figure who would help reshape the Cold War's end in Eastern Europe.

evt-08-26-1980-harvey-s-resort-hotel-bom.scenario: It's August 27, 1980, and you're part of the bomb squad called to Harvey's Resort Hotel in Stateline, Nevada. Inside, guests have been evacuated ahead of an elaborate, booby-trapped device containing 1,200 pounds of dynamite, and you must decide how to handle it.
evt-08-26-1980-harvey-s-resort-hotel-bom.prompt: What does the bomb squad attempt with the device?

choices.text: Negotiate with the bombers for instructions on remote defusal
Let it sit untouched and wait out its timer from a safe distance
Use a crane to lift it out of the hotel and detonate it outdoors
Attempt to defuse it manually in place using specialized tools

evt-08-26-1980-harvey-s-resort-hotel-bom.butterflyEffect: The bomb detonated during the disarming attempt, tearing through the hotel and causing roughly $18 million in damage, though the evacuation meant no one was killed or injured. Investigators traced the plot to gambler John Birges Sr., who had lost $750,000 at the casino; his conviction and the sheer complexity of the device pushed bomb squads nationwide toward remote-controlled robots rather than hands-on disarming.

evt-08-26-1999-second-chechen-war.scenario: It is late August 1999. Islamist fighters have poured out of Chechnya into neighboring Dagestan, and as Russia's newly appointed Prime Minister, you must decide how the Kremlin responds.
evt-08-26-1999-second-chechen-war.prompt: What does Russia do in response to the Dagestan incursion?

choices.text: Request NATO peacekeepers for the border region
Launch a full-scale military campaign into Chechnya
Leave the response to local Dagestani police and militias
Negotiate a ceasefire with Chechen separatist leaders

evt-08-26-1999-second-chechen-war.butterflyEffect: Russia launched a full-scale military campaign into Chechnya, beginning the Second Chechen War. The brutal, decade-long conflict crushed the separatist republic, cemented Vladimir Putin's rise to the presidency, and installed the Kadyrov family as Moscow-backed rulers of a heavily militarized Chechnya.

evt-08-26-2014-rotherham-child-sexual-ex.scenario: You are a Rotherham council official in August 2014 as Professor Alexis Jay's independent report is published, laying bare years of failures to stop organised child sexual exploitation in the town.
evt-08-26-2014-rotherham-child-sexual-ex.prompt: What did the report's publication trigger for local leadership?

choices.text: Immediate dissolution of Rotherham Council by central government
Criminal charges filed against every official named in the report
Resignations of the council leader and the police and crime commissioner
Closure of all care homes in South Yorkshire

evt-08-26-2014-rotherham-child-sexual-ex.butterflyEffect: Within days, council leader Roger Stone resigned, and South Yorkshire's police and crime commissioner Shaun Wright faced sustained pressure that led to his own resignation soon after. The scandal prompted a wider national reckoning over grooming gang failures and shaped subsequent inquiries into child protection across England.

evt-08-27-410-sack-of-rome-410.scenario: It is late August, 410 CE. Alaric's Visigothic warriors have breached Rome's walls and moved through the city for three days. You are a Roman senator waiting to learn what will become of the city, and of the empire, once they finally leave.
evt-08-27-410-sack-of-rome-410.prompt: How did Alaric's occupation of Rome come to an end after three days?

choices.text: The Senate crowned Alaric as the new Western Emperor
Alaric established a permanent Visigothic capital in Rome
The Visigoths burned the entire city to ashes and stayed
Alaric's forces withdrew south with loot and captives

evt-08-27-410-sack-of-rome-410.butterflyEffect: The Visigoths withdrew southward, carrying plundered wealth and hostages, including Galla Placidia, sister of Emperor Honorius. The sack shattered the myth of Rome's invincibility, inspired Augustine to write City of God, and marked a turning point in the Western Empire's long decline.

evt-08-27-1656-ahanta-people.scenario: You are an Ahanta chief meeting Dutch West India Company officials at Butre on the Gold Coast in 1656. They offer a formal treaty promising protection and a fort in exchange for control over your gold and trade.

choices.text: Accept the treaty, granting the Dutch trading rights and a fort in exchange for protection
Reject the Dutch offer and continue trading freely with all European powers
Ally exclusively with the Portuguese against the Dutch
Demand the Dutch leave the coast entirely and destroy their existing trading post

evt-08-27-1656-ahanta-people.butterflyEffect: The Ahanta accepted the Treaty of Butre, granting the Dutch a fort and trading rights while retaining local sovereignty. The agreement lasted over two centuries and was cited by the Netherlands in 1872 when it transferred the Dutch Gold Coast to Britain without Ahanta consent, sparking the Ahanta uprising known as Commandant Kesse's War.

evt-08-27-1776-william-howe-5th-viscount.scenario: It is the night of 27 August 1776. Your Continental Army has just been badly beaten by William Howe's forces on Long Island, and your men are pinned against the East River with the British closing in.
evt-08-27-1776-william-howe-5th-viscount.prompt: What should General Washington order to save the army from destruction?

choices.text: Surrender terms to Howe to spare the men
Stand and fight to hold the Brooklyn lines at all costs
Evacuate the army secretly across the East River by night
Split the army and retreat overland through New Jersey

evt-08-27-1776-william-howe-5th-viscount.butterflyEffect: Washington secretly ferried his entire army across the East River to Manhattan overnight, slipping away under cover of fog before Howe could strike the finishing blow. The escape preserved the Continental Army and allowed the war for independence to continue.

evt-08-27-1810-napoleonic-wars.scenario: August 1810, off Île de France in the Indian Ocean. You command a French frigate squadron facing a larger British force near the treacherous reefs of Grand Port harbour.
evt-08-27-1810-napoleonic-wars.prompt: What tactic should you use to turn the British numerical advantage into a weakness?

choices.text: Sue for terms before battle is joined
Retreat into harbour and wait out a siege
Meet the British fleet in open water for a conventional line battle
Draw the British ships into the narrow reef-lined channel where their size becomes a liability

evt-08-27-1810-napoleonic-wars.butterflyEffect: Duperré's squadron lured the British ships into the narrow, reef-strewn channel at Grand Port, where several ran aground and were destroyed or captured — the only naval battle of the Napoleonic Wars later inscribed on the Arc de Triomphe. The victory was short-lived: Britain returned with overwhelming force that December and seized Île de France, ending French naval power in the Indian Ocean.

evt-08-27-1832-black-hawk-sauk-leader.scenario: It is 27 August 1832. After the devastating fighting at the Bad Axe River, you are Black Hawk, hiding with a small band of followers, aware that most of your people have already been killed or scattered.
evt-08-27-1832-black-hawk-sauk-leader.prompt: What should Black Hawk do now to protect what remains of his people?

choices.text: Seek refuge with British authorities in Canada
Surrender to the Indian agent to end the bloodshed
Continue fleeing westward across the Mississippi
Launch one final attack to avenge the losses

evt-08-27-1832-black-hawk-sauk-leader.butterflyEffect: Black Hawk surrendered to Indian agent Joseph Street at Prairie du Chien rather than continue fighting. He was imprisoned and later toured eastern cities before dictating an autobiography, while the war's end forced the Sauk and Fox from their remaining lands in Illinois and Wisconsin.

evt-08-27-1859-edwin-drake.scenario: Titusville, Pennsylvania, August 1859. You are Edwin Drake, drilling for oil, but loose rock and groundwater keep collapsing your borehole before you can reach any depth.
evt-08-27-1859-edwin-drake.prompt: What method should you use to keep the well from collapsing?

choices.text: Dig the well by hand with shovels and timber shoring
Drive an iron pipe casing down to bedrock and drill through it
Abandon the site and search for a drier location
Use a conventional mining shaft without any casing

evt-08-27-1859-edwin-drake.butterflyEffect: Drake drove an iron pipe down to bedrock and drilled inside it, striking oil at about 69 feet on 27 August 1859 — the first successful drilled oil well in America. His pipe-casing technique became standard practice and sparked the Pennsylvania oil rush that launched the modern petroleum industry.

evt-08-27-1896-anglo-zanzibar-war.scenario: It is the morning of 27 August 1896. You are Sultan Khalid bin Barghash, barricaded inside the Zanzibar palace with your guards, having ignored a British ultimatum to step down and leave.
evt-08-27-1896-anglo-zanzibar-war.prompt: What happens after you refuse the British ultimatum?

choices.text: British warships bombard the palace, forcing a rapid surrender
German forces intervene on Zanzibar's behalf
British and Zanzibari envoys reach a negotiated compromise
Your palace guard repels the British landing party

evt-08-27-1896-anglo-zanzibar-war.butterflyEffect: British warships opened fire on the palace, and within 38 to 45 minutes the fighting was over, making it the shortest recorded war in history. Khalid fled into exile, and the British installed the more compliant Hamoud bin Mohammed as sultan, tightening their grip over Zanzibar.

evt-08-27-1979-the-troubles.scenario: You are a soldier in a British Army convoy passing Narrow Water Castle near Warrenpoint on 27 August 1979. A bomb has just exploded, and survivors are regrouping at the roadside to help the wounded.
evt-08-27-1979-the-troubles.prompt: What should the convoy do next to avoid further casualties?

choices.text: Withdraw the entire convoy back across the border immediately
Treat the site as still dangerous and hold back from the blast area
Call in an airstrike on suspected IRA positions nearby
Rush every available soldier to the scene to aid the wounded

evt-08-27-1979-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: A second, larger bomb hit the responders minutes later, killing eighteen soldiers in total — the British Army's worst single loss of the Troubles. The same day the IRA killed Lord Mountbatten in County Sligo, and the double blow pushed London toward harsher security measures and closer military-police cooperation in Northern Ireland.

evt-08-27-1980-1980-south-korean-preside.scenario: Seoul, 27 August 1980. You are a delegate to the National Conference for Unification, the electoral college convened to choose a president after Choi Kyu-hah's resignation following General Chun Doo-hwan's May coup.
evt-08-27-1980-1980-south-korean-preside.prompt: How do you cast your vote?

choices.text: Boycott the vote to protest military rule
Vote to retain outgoing president Choi Kyu-hah
Nominate opposition figure Kim Dae-jung
Vote for Chun Doo-hwan, the coup's leader and sole viable candidate

evt-08-27-1980-1980-south-korean-preside.butterflyEffect: The delegates elected Chun Doo-hwan president with an overwhelming, effectively unopposed vote, cementing the military's grip on power after the Gwangju massacre. Chun would go on to lead South Korea's authoritarian Fifth Republic until 1988, and was later convicted for his role in the coup and the Gwangju crackdown.

evt-08-27-1982-military-attache.scenario: It's Ottawa, August 1982. You are a Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer responsible for foreign diplomatic security, and intelligence has flagged that Armenian militant groups are targeting Turkish officials worldwide over their government's genocide denial.
evt-08-27-1982-military-attache.prompt: What should you recommend for the Turkish military attaché's daily routine?

choices.text: Recommend a public statement dismissing the threat to avoid alarming other diplomats
Rely on his diplomatic immunity as sufficient protection
Assign a fixed protective escort and vary his commuting route and schedule
Advise him to travel only within the embassy compound and cancel public appearances entirely

evt-08-27-1982-military-attache.butterflyEffect: Colonel Atilla Altıkat was shot dead in his car near the Turkish embassy, one of several attacks on Turkish diplomats worldwide claimed by Armenian militant groups. The killings pushed Canada and other Western governments to tighten diplomatic protection protocols and treat attaché security as a standing intelligence priority.

evt-08-27-1985-muhammadu-buhari.scenario: Lagos, August 1985. You are a senior officer in Nigeria's Supreme Military Council, watching Major General Muhammadu Buhari's regime falter under economic austerity, harsh decrees, and internal army resentment led by General Ibrahim Babangida.
evt-08-27-1985-muhammadu-buhari.prompt: What does the council do about Buhari's leadership?

choices.text: Back Babangida's coup to remove Buhari
Ask Buhari to voluntarily hand power to a civilian government
Reaffirm loyalty to Buhari and purge dissenting officers
Call for immediate multiparty elections to replace military rule

evt-08-27-1985-muhammadu-buhari.butterflyEffect: Babangida led a bloodless palace coup that removed Buhari from power on 27 August 1985 and installed himself as head of state. Babangida would rule until 1993, and Buhari himself would not return to power until winning Nigeria's democratic presidential election three decades later, in 2015.

evt-08-27-1985-space-shuttle-discovery.scenario: It is 27 August 1985. You are part of the STS-51-I crew aboard Discovery, tasked with deploying three communications satellites, but mission control also has an older, malfunctioning satellite waiting in orbit for your attention.
evt-08-27-1985-space-shuttle-discovery.prompt: What extra task did the crew perform beyond deploying the three satellites?

choices.text: Deployed a classified fourth military satellite
Launched a European science probe toward Venus
Repaired the malfunctioning Leasat-3 satellite via spacewalk
Tested experimental heat-resistant tiles

evt-08-27-1985-space-shuttle-discovery.butterflyEffect: Astronauts conducted a spacewalk to capture and repair the Leasat-3 satellite, which had failed to activate after an earlier shuttle mission. The successful in-orbit fix proved astronauts could service and rescue expensive satellites, a capability later relied upon for missions like the Hubble Space Telescope repairs.

evt-08-27-1990-stevie-ray-vaughan.scenario: It is the early hours of 27 August 1990 in East Troy, Wisconsin. You've just finished a blistering set with Eric Clapton, and a helicopter is waiting to fly you back toward Chicago through thick fog.
evt-08-27-1990-stevie-ray-vaughan.prompt: Should you board this early helicopter, or wait for a later flight or the tour bus?

choices.text: Stay overnight in East Troy and fly out at dawn
Wait for a later flight once conditions improve
Take the tour bus instead
Board the earlier helicopter despite the fog

evt-08-27-1990-stevie-ray-vaughan.butterflyEffect: Vaughan took a seat on the earlier helicopter, which crashed into a hill in the fog minutes after takeoff, killing him and four others. His death cut short a celebrated comeback and cemented his legacy as one of blues-rock's most influential guitarists through posthumous releases.

evt-08-27-1991-european-economic-communi.scenario: It is 27 August 1991. The Soviet Union is reeling from a failed coup, and Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania have declared independence. You sit among European Community foreign ministers in Brussels deciding how to respond to Moscow's crumbling grip.
evt-08-27-1991-european-economic-communi.prompt: What did the EC foreign ministers decide about the Baltic states?

choices.text: Refuse recognition until UN membership was granted
Defer entirely to whatever Moscow decides
Recognize their independence immediately
Recognize only limited autonomy within the USSR

evt-08-27-1991-european-economic-communi.butterflyEffect: The EC formally recognized the independence of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania on 27 August 1991, days before the Soviet Union itself did so in early September. The move emboldened other Soviet republics to seek recognition and accelerated the USSR's dissolution that December.

evt-08-27-1991-moldova.scenario: It is late August 1991. The failed coup in Moscow has shattered Soviet authority, and as a deputy in the Moldovan parliament, you face a vote on the republic's future.
evt-08-27-1991-moldova.prompt: What does the Moldovan parliament vote to do?

choices.text: Vote to unify with neighboring Romania
Declare full independence from the Soviet Union
Ask to join a new Baltic-style economic bloc
Remain a Soviet republic under a reformed union treaty

evt-08-27-1991-moldova.butterflyEffect: Moldova declared independence from the USSR, becoming a sovereign state that joined the UN in 1992. The move triggered a war with Russian-backed separatists in Transnistria, a breakaway region that remains outside Chișinău's control to this day.

evt-08-27-2003-mars.scenario: It is August 2003, and a forwarded email is circulating claiming Mars will loom as large as the full moon on the night of its closest approach in nearly 60,000 years. Friends keep asking you if it's true.
evt-08-27-2003-mars.prompt: What should you tell them about how Mars will actually appear that night?

choices.text: It will be invisible without a telescope
It will appear as large as the full moon
It will be bright but still appear as a small point of light
It will look like a second moon in the sky

evt-08-27-2003-mars.butterflyEffect: Mars was indeed unusually bright and close, but to the naked eye it remained a brilliant reddish point, not moon-sized. The exaggerated claim became known as the "Mars Hoax," and the same false email has resurfaced online every August since, regardless of Mars's actual distance that year.

evt-08-27-2006-comair-flight-5191.scenario: It's before dawn on 27 August 2006 at Blue Grass Airport in Lexington. You're the flight crew of Comair 5191, taxiing in darkness with construction markings altering the usual layout, cleared for takeoff on the main runway.
evt-08-27-2006-comair-flight-5191.prompt: What should the crew do before applying takeoff power?

choices.text: Trust the tower's clearance and begin the takeoff roll immediately
Ask ground control to close the airport until daylight
Switch to the alternate airport rather than risk night taxiing
Cross-check the runway heading and markings against instruments before rolling

evt-08-27-2006-comair-flight-5191.butterflyEffect: The crew lined up on the wrong, much shorter runway and the jet ran out of pavement, crashing and killing 49 of the 50 aboard. The disaster led to new FAA rules on cockpit sterility during taxi and pushed airports to improve runway signage and lighting to prevent similar confusion.

evt-08-27-2011-hurricane-irene.scenario: It is 27 August 2011, and Hurricane Irene is bearing down on the East Coast. You live in a low-lying coastal town under a mandatory evacuation order as the storm approaches.
evt-08-27-2011-hurricane-irene.prompt: What should you do as Irene approaches your coastal town?

choices.text: Move belongings to the basement and wait it out
Evacuate inland before the storm makes landfall
Ignore the order since prior storms fizzled out
Stay home and shelter in an upstairs room

evt-08-27-2011-hurricane-irene.butterflyEffect: Irene caused widespread flooding and power outages from North Carolina to New England, shutting down New York City's subway system for the first time ever due to a storm and killing dozens. The storm's inland flooding exposed gaps in preparedness for river flooding, prompting changes in evacuation and emergency planning up the East Coast.

evt-08-27-2013-2013-muzaffarnagar-riots.scenario: You are a district police officer in Muzaffarnagar on 27 August 2013. Rumors of an assault are spreading fast through village networks, and Hindu and Muslim residents are gathering in anger on both sides.
evt-08-27-2013-2013-muzaffarnagar-riots.prompt: What immediate step offers the best chance of preventing the violence from spreading?

choices.text: Arm village volunteers so each community can defend itself
Impose an immediate curfew and restrict rumor-spreading communications
Organize a public rally to reassure both communities
Dismiss the rumors as baseless and take no action

evt-08-27-2013-2013-muzaffarnagar-riots.butterflyEffect: The unrest could not be contained: clashes spread across the district, killing 62 people and displacing more than 50,000. The riots became a lasting flashpoint in Indian politics, cited for years afterward in debates over communal polarization and policing failures.

evt-08-28-1619-ferdinand-ii-holy-roman-e.scenario: It is August 1619 in Frankfurt, and you sit among the electors of the Holy Roman Empire. Word has just reached you that Bohemian rebels have already deposed Ferdinand as their king and offered the crown to Frederick V of the Palatinate, yet Ferdinand still stands before you as a candidate for Emperor.

choices.text: They delay the election until the Bohemian crisis is resolved
They split their votes, electing no emperor that year
They elect Ferdinand II Holy Roman Emperor unanimously, defying the Bohemian revolt
They elect Frederick V of the Palatinate as Emperor instead

evt-08-28-1619-ferdinand-ii-holy-roman-e.butterflyEffect: Ferdinand's unanimous election, even as Bohemia rejected him, hardened the empire's Catholic-Protestant divide and helped ignite the Thirty Years' War. His campaign to crush the Bohemian revolt at the Battle of White Mountain in 1620 reshaped the religious and political map of Central Europe for a generation.

evt-08-28-1789-william-herschel.scenario: On the night of 28 August 1789, you stand beside William Herschel at his newly finished 40-foot telescope, the largest in the world, as he swings it toward Saturn for its very first serious observation.
evt-08-28-1789-william-herschel.prompt: What did Herschel discover in these first observations with the giant telescope?

choices.text: The moon Enceladus
The planet Uranus
A bright new comet
A previously unknown ring around Neptune

evt-08-28-1789-william-herschel.butterflyEffect: Herschel spotted Enceladus, a small moon of Saturn previously invisible to smaller instruments. Coming eight years after his discovery of Uranus, it confirmed him as Europe's leading observational astronomer; centuries later, spacecraft found ice geysers on Enceladus, making it one of the solar system's top candidates in the search for life.

evt-08-28-1830-tom-thumb-locomotive.scenario: It's 28 August 1830 on a stretch of the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad, and you are engineer Peter Cooper driving your small steam locomotive Tom Thumb in a demonstration race against a horse-drawn railcar. Midway through, a belt on your machine begins to slip and the horse pulls ahead.
evt-08-28-1830-tom-thumb-locomotive.prompt: What happens as a result of the mechanical failure?

choices.text: The horse wins the race after Tom Thumb's belt fails, but the demonstration still convinces the railroad to adopt steam
The race is called a draw and rerun the next day
Cooper repairs the belt in seconds and overtakes the horse to win
The horse collapses from exhaustion, handing victory to Tom Thumb

evt-08-28-1830-tom-thumb-locomotive.butterflyEffect: Despite losing the race, Tom Thumb proved steam locomotion's potential, and the B&O Railroad committed to steam power, holding trials the following year for a full working engine. This decision helped launch America's railroad age, setting steam locomotives on course to transform 19th-century transportation and commerce.

evt-08-28-1909-1909-monterrey-hurricane.scenario: It is late August 1909, and a powerful hurricane has just struck the Mexican state of Tamaulipas after crossing the Yucatán and intensifying over the Gulf of Mexico. Rivers are rising fast around towns like Monterrey.
evt-08-28-1909-1909-monterrey-hurricane.prompt: What made this storm so catastrophic for communities far from the coast?

choices.text: A volcanic eruption combined with the storm's winds
Catastrophic inland river flooding far from the coast
A direct storm surge overwhelming coastal defenses only
An earthquake triggered by the storm's low pressure

evt-08-28-1909-1909-monterrey-hurricane.butterflyEffect: The hurricane's torrential rains caused the Santa Catarina River to flood Monterrey itself, far inland, contributing to the storm becoming the deadliest hurricane in Mexican recorded history. The disaster exposed the vulnerability of inland river towns to tropical cyclones and spurred later efforts at flood control along the Santa Catarina.

evt-08-28-1950-althea-gibson.scenario: It is August 28, 1950, at Forest Hills. You watch Althea Gibson walk onto the court to compete in the U.S. National Championships, the first African American woman ever to do so.
evt-08-28-1950-althea-gibson.prompt: What barrier did Gibson's appearance at this tournament break?

choices.text: The ban on women playing five-set matches
The exclusion of players from outside the Northeast
The prohibition on professional players entering amateur events
The color line in national tennis competition

evt-08-28-1950-althea-gibson.butterflyEffect: Gibson became the first Black player, man or woman, to compete in the U.S. National Championships, opening the door for future Black athletes in tennis. Within a few years she would go on to win multiple Grand Slam titles, including Wimbledon and the U.S. Nationals, becoming a trailblazer later honored in the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

evt-08-28-1963-i-have-a-dream.scenario: It is August 28, 1963, and you stand among a quarter of a million people crowded before the Lincoln Memorial. Dr. King has set aside his prepared text and begun speaking from the heart.
evt-08-28-1963-i-have-a-dream.prompt: What did King's improvised peroration become known as?

choices.text: The 'Promised Land' oration
The 'Content of Character' speech
The 'I Have a Dream' refrain
The 'Free at Last' address

evt-08-28-1963-i-have-a-dream.butterflyEffect: King's spontaneous 'I Have a Dream' passage, prompted partly by singer Mahalia Jackson's urging, became the most quoted portion of the speech and one of the most famous in American history. It galvanized support for the civil rights movement and helped build momentum toward the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Voting Rights Act of 1965.

evt-08-28-1973-norrmalmstorg-robbery.scenario: You are one of four hostages locked inside a bank vault at Norrmalmstorg Square in Stockholm on live television. Days pass, and when police finally offer you a way out, some hostages hesitate, seeming to trust their captor more than the officers outside.
evt-08-28-1973-norrmalmstorg-robbery.prompt: What did psychiatrists later name this bond hostages formed with their captor?

choices.text: Lima syndrome
Stockholm syndrome
Oslo syndrome
Helsinki syndrome

evt-08-28-1973-norrmalmstorg-robbery.butterflyEffect: Psychiatrist Nils Bejerot coined the term afterward, and "Stockholm syndrome" entered criminology and psychology worldwide as shorthand for hostages emotionally bonding with, or defending, the people holding them. The case remains a foundational reference point in hostage negotiation training decades later.

evt-08-28-1987-ryugyong-hotel.scenario: You are a planner in Pyongyang in 1987, tasked with breaking ground on a 105-story pyramid meant to be the tallest hotel on Earth, a showpiece to outdo hotels rising in South Korea.
evt-08-28-1987-ryugyong-hotel.prompt: What actually happened to construction in the years after the concrete shell went up?

choices.text: It was quickly converted into government apartments
Construction halted for over a decade after North Korea's economy collapsed
It opened on schedule as the world's tallest hotel in 1989
It was demolished within a few years due to a structural flaw

evt-08-28-1987-ryugyong-hotel.butterflyEffect: Work stopped in 1992 after North Korea's economy collapsed with the loss of Soviet aid, leaving the bare grey shell standing empty for over a decade and earning the nickname the "Hotel of Doom." The exterior was finally clad in glass panels around 2011, but the building has still never opened as a functioning hotel.

evt-08-28-1993-galileo-spacecraft.scenario: It is late August 1993, and the Galileo spacecraft has just sent back a burst of images of the asteroid 243 Ida as it speeds past on its long journey to Jupiter. Engineers at JPL begin the slow process of downlinking and studying every frame.
evt-08-28-1993-galileo-spacecraft.prompt: What did careful analysis of these Ida images later reveal?

choices.text: Clear evidence of liquid water on the surface
A tiny natural satellite orbiting Ida
An unexplained radio signal from the asteroid
A crater matching the Chicxulub impactor

evt-08-28-1993-galileo-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: Months later, scientists poring over the images spotted a tiny object orbiting Ida — Dactyl, the first natural satellite of an asteroid ever confirmed. The discovery upended assumptions about asteroids as simple lone rocks and opened a new field of study into binary and multiple asteroid systems.

evt-08-28-1998-second-congo-war.scenario: It is late August 1998, and rebel forces backed by Rwanda have pushed to the outskirts of Kinshasa, threatening to topple President Kabila's government within days. You command an Angolan intervention force just arriving to bolster the loyalist defense.
evt-08-28-1998-second-congo-war.prompt: What does the Angolan and Zimbabwean intervention achieve?

choices.text: It halts the rebel advance and repels them from Kinshasa, saving Kabila's government
It negotiates an immediate ceasefire ending the war entirely
It fails, and Kinshasa falls to the Rwandan-backed rebels within the week
It leads Angola to switch sides and support the rebels instead

evt-08-28-1998-second-congo-war.butterflyEffect: The intervention saved Kabila's government but transformed a Congolese civil conflict into a continent-spanning war drawing in nine nations and roughly 25 armed groups. The resulting Second Congo War became one of the deadliest conflicts since World War II, with instability persisting in eastern Congo for decades after the formal peace in 2003.

evt-08-28-1999-soyuz-tm-29.scenario: You are cosmonaut Sergei Avdeyev, already months into your mission aboard Mir when Soyuz TM-29 arrives in February 1999. Because two seats on the incoming craft were sold to a Slovak and a French visitor, you're told your own assignment must now double in length before you can return home.
evt-08-28-1999-soyuz-tm-29.prompt: What happens to your stay in space as a result?

choices.text: You remain aboard Mir far longer than planned, setting a new cumulative spaceflight record
You are rescued early by a rescue Soyuz sent up specifically for you
You transfer to the newly launched ISS instead of returning on Soyuz TM-28
You refuse the extension and return immediately with the outgoing crew

evt-08-28-1999-soyuz-tm-29.butterflyEffect: Avdeyev's extended tour, forced by the commercial sale of Soyuz seats, pushed his cumulative time in space past 747 days, a record that stood for over a decade. His flight foreshadowed how Mir's final years increasingly relied on paying spaceflight participants to fund the aging station.

evt-08-28-2003-federal-bureau-of-investi.scenario: It is August 28, 2003, in Erie, Pennsylvania. A pizza delivery driver walks into a bank with a strange metal device locked around his neck, claiming he was forced to rob it under threat that the device would explode.
evt-08-28-2003-federal-bureau-of-investi.prompt: What did the FBI investigation ultimately reveal about this bizarre case?

choices.text: The device was fake and the driver was in on the plan
It was a publicity stunt staged for a reality show
It was an elaborate multi-conspirator plot involving a real bomb
It was an insurance fraud scheme with no real explosive

evt-08-28-2003-federal-bureau-of-investi.butterflyEffect: The device was a real bomb, and the driver, Brian Wells, died when it detonated shortly after his arrest at the scene. Years of investigation revealed an elaborate, multi-conspirator plot; the case became one of the strangest in FBI history and the subject of extensive documentary coverage.

evt-08-28-2016-isro.scenario: It is August 28, 2016, at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre. You watch a small winged vehicle roar off the launch pad, carrying India's first indigenously developed scramjet engines into the upper atmosphere.
evt-08-28-2016-isro.prompt: What did this test flight demonstrate for ISRO's future reusable launch program?

choices.text: Docking with an orbiting space station module
Deployment of a geostationary communications satellite
Crewed re-entry and splashdown
Air-breathing scramjet propulsion at hypersonic speed

evt-08-28-2016-isro.butterflyEffect: The brief flight successfully ignited air-breathing scramjet engines at hypersonic speed, a first for India, validating technology meant to reduce the oxidizer a rocket must carry. It became a key milestone in ISRO's long-term Reusable Launch Vehicle Technology Demonstration program, aimed at cutting the cost of reaching orbit.

evt-08-28-2021-thomson-east-coast-line.scenario: It is 28 August 2021, and you step onto the platform at Caldecott as the second phase of Singapore's newest MRT line opens to the public. The line runs fully underground and promises driverless trains eventually linking the north to downtown and the east coast.
evt-08-28-2021-thomson-east-coast-line.prompt: What is significant about this new line for Singapore's transport network?

choices.text: It replaces the East-West Line entirely, retiring older trains from service
It is Singapore's first line to run above ground through the city centre
It connects directly to Malaysia's rail network for the first time
It becomes part of one of the world's longest fully underground, driverless MRT lines, eventually linking Woodlands to Changi Airport
