evt-08-28-2021-thomson-east-coast-line.butterflyEffect: The Thomson-East Coast Line would eventually stretch 57km across 32 stations when fully completed, becoming one of the world's longest fully underground, driverless MRT lines. Its full opening in 2024 finally linked Woodlands in the north to Changi Airport and Marina Bay, reshaping commutes across Singapore's east and north.

evt-08-29-1350-hundred-years-war.scenario: It is 29 August 1350, and you stand aboard King Edward III's cog off Winchelsea, watching a fleet of towering Castilian carracks — allies of France — bear down from the open Channel.
evt-08-29-1350-hundred-years-war.prompt: How does Edward's smaller English fleet close the fight?

choices.text: By retreating to Dover to avoid battle with the heavier ships.
By using longbowmen alone to sink the ships from a distance.
By negotiating a truce with the Castilian admiral before any fighting began.
By ramming and grappling the larger ships, storming aboard to fight hand-to-hand rather than trading fire at range.

evt-08-29-1350-hundred-years-war.butterflyEffect: The Battle of Winchelsea (Les Espagnols sur Mer) saw Edward III's outnumbered fleet grapple and board the taller Castilian ships, capturing or sinking a large part of the enemy fleet. The victory secured England's Channel trade routes and burnished Edward's reputation as a warrior-king during a lull in the wider Hundred Years' War.

evt-08-29-1475-treaty-of-picquigny.scenario: It is 29 August 1475, and you stand on the bridge at Picquigny beside Louis XI, watching Edward IV's English army camped nearby. Edward's invasion force is strong, but Burgundy has abandoned him and his troops are eager to go home.
evt-08-29-1475-treaty-of-picquigny.prompt: What does Louis XI offer Edward IV to end the war without a battle?

choices.text: A large cash payment plus an annual pension
Formal cession of Normandy back to England
The hand of his daughter in marriage and a French duchy
A joint crusade against the Ottomans

evt-08-29-1475-treaty-of-picquigny.butterflyEffect: Louis paid Edward 75,000 crowns immediately and promised an annual pension, buying peace without a fight. Freed from the English threat, Louis turned his full attention to crushing Charles the Bold of Burgundy. The treaty effectively ended the Hundred Years' War, though neither crown ever formally renounced its claims.

evt-08-29-1831-michael-faraday.scenario: You are an assistant in Michael Faraday's basement laboratory at the Royal Institution on 29 August 1831, watching him wind two coils of insulated wire around opposite sides of an iron ring.
evt-08-29-1831-michael-faraday.prompt: What does Faraday observe on his galvanometer when he interrupts the current in one coil?

choices.text: The second coil becomes permanently magnetized
A momentary current flickers in the second coil
No effect appears in either coil
Sparks appear only while current steadily increases

evt-08-29-1831-michael-faraday.butterflyEffect: A brief pulse of current appeared in the second coil at the instant the first was switched on or off, proving that a changing magnetic field could induce electric current. This principle became the basis for generators and transformers, powering the electrification of industry and cities within decades.

evt-08-29-1842-treaty-of-nanking.scenario: It is 29 August 1842 aboard a British warship in the Yangtze River, and you watch British and Qing officials sign the treaty ending three years of war fought partly over Britain's opium trade.
evt-08-29-1842-treaty-of-nanking.prompt: What does the Treaty of Nanking force Qing China to give Britain?

choices.text: Hong Kong Island, an indemnity, and five open treaty ports
Full control of the Chinese opium trade monopoly
Formal annexation of Guangzhou province
A permanent British garrison in Beijing

evt-08-29-1842-treaty-of-nanking.butterflyEffect: China ceded Hong Kong Island, paid a large indemnity, and opened five ports including Shanghai to British trade and residence. It was the first of the 'unequal treaties' that steadily eroded Qing sovereignty, setting a pattern other Western powers and Japan followed for the rest of the century.

evt-08-29-1885-gottlieb-daimler.scenario: It is late August 1885 in Cannstatt, Germany, and you watch engineer Gottlieb Daimler bolt his compact new petroleum engine onto a wooden-framed two-wheeler, creating a vehicle unlike anything else on the road.
evt-08-29-1885-gottlieb-daimler.prompt: What does Daimler call his new engine-powered two-wheeler when he patents it?

choices.text: The Daimler Cycle
The Petroleum-Fahrrad
The Reitwagen (riding car)
The Motorrad Eins

evt-08-29-1885-gottlieb-daimler.butterflyEffect: Daimler's Reitwagen, patented in 1885, is recognized as the world's first internal-combustion motorcycle. Though never intended for production, it proved his high-speed petrol engine could power independent vehicles, work he and Wilhelm Maybach used the same year in early automobile designs. Daimler's engines soon powered cars, boats and airships, making him one of the founding figures of the motor age.

evt-08-29-1903-russian-battleship-slava.scenario: It is 1903 at a St Petersburg shipyard, and you watch the newest Borodino-class battleship, Slava, slide into the water, the last of her five sister ships to be launched.
evt-08-29-1903-russian-battleship-slava.prompt: What fate awaits Slava's four sister ships that she herself will escape?

choices.text: They are sold to the Ottoman Navy before completion
They are scrapped for violating naval treaty limits
They are sunk or captured at the Battle of Tsushima
They mutiny and defect to Japan

evt-08-29-1903-russian-battleship-slava.butterflyEffect: Slava's construction ran late, so she missed the Russo-Japanese War entirely while her four sisters sailed to disaster at Tsushima in 1905, sunk or surrendered. Spared that fate, Slava served in the Baltic Fleet through World War I, finally being scuttled by her own crew in 1917 to block the Gulf of Riga to German ships.

evt-08-29-1911-yana-people.scenario: It is 29 August 1911 near Oroville, California, and a starving, frightened man — the last surviving member of the Yahi people — is found cornered by dogs outside a slaughterhouse, having lived alone in hiding for years.
evt-08-29-1911-yana-people.prompt: What happened to him after his capture?

choices.text: He refused all contact and disappeared into the wilderness again.
Anthropologists brought him to live at a University of California museum, where he shared his language and culture until his death.
He was deported to a reservation in Oklahoma.
He was returned to a hidden Yahi settlement still surviving in the hills.

evt-08-29-1911-yana-people.butterflyEffect: Known as Ishi, he spent his remaining years at the University of California's museum in San Francisco, where anthropologist Alfred Kroeber recorded his language, stories, and skills, producing invaluable records of Yahi culture. His life also became a symbol of the era's troubling anthropological practices, prompting later ethical debates over consent and the treatment of Indigenous people as living specimens.

evt-08-29-1916-united-states-congress.scenario: You are a Filipino nationalist leader in Manila on 29 August 1916, reading a telegram announcing that the U.S. Congress has just passed a new organic act reshaping colonial governance of the islands.
evt-08-29-1916-united-states-congress.prompt: What does the Philippine Autonomy Act promise for the islands' future?

choices.text: Immediate and unconditional independence
Eventual independence once a stable government is established
A path toward American statehood
Permanent incorporation as a U.S. territory

evt-08-29-1916-united-states-congress.butterflyEffect: The Act, sponsored by Congressman William Atkinson Jones, created the first elected Philippine Senate and pledged eventual independence once a stable government was established. It set a precedent that led directly to the 1934 Tydings-McDuffie Act, which scheduled full independence, achieved in 1946.

evt-08-29-1960-air-france-flight-343.scenario: You are the co-pilot of Air France Flight 343, descending toward Yoff Airport in dense pre-dawn fog on 29 August 1960. The captain, already reprimanded once by Air France for reckless flying, wants to bring the plane down by sight rather than follow the instrument approach.
evt-08-29-1960-air-france-flight-343.prompt: What does the captain do next, with fatal consequences for everyone aboard?

choices.text: He aborts the landing and diverts to Monrovia
He continues descending by sight, ignoring the instrument approach
He switches control to the co-pilot and follows radar guidance
He circles until dawn light improves visibility

evt-08-29-1960-air-france-flight-343.butterflyEffect: He continued the visual descent without instruments and the aircraft struck the Atlantic short of the runway, killing all 63 aboard. A tribunal ruled it willful misconduct, a landmark case establishing that airlines and crews could be held liable for reckless disregard of safety procedures.

evt-08-29-1966-the-beatles.scenario: You are in the crowd at Candlestick Park, San Francisco, on 29 August 1966, watching a Beatles concert that few in attendance realize will be their last performance before a paying audience.
evt-08-29-1966-the-beatles.prompt: What does the band do in the aftermath of this show?

choices.text: They launch an even larger world tour
They announce the band's breakup
They stop touring to focus entirely on studio recording
They replace their touring lineup with session musicians

evt-08-29-1966-the-beatles.butterflyEffect: The Beatles quietly stopped touring altogether, retreating into the studio where the freedom from live performance let them craft increasingly ambitious records like Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band. The shift helped establish the album as a serious artistic statement rather than just a touring souvenir.

evt-08-29-1970-chicano-moratorium.scenario: You march with roughly 30,000 demonstrators through East Los Angeles on 29 August 1970, protesting the disproportionate number of Mexican-American soldiers dying in Vietnam. The rally is heading toward Laguna Park for a planned afternoon of speeches.
evt-08-29-1970-chicano-moratorium.prompt: What happens at Laguna Park as the rally winds down?

choices.text: The crowd disperses peacefully after the speeches
Deputies move in with tear gas, and violence erupts
City officials join the marchers on stage
The National Guard is called in preemptively

evt-08-29-1970-chicano-moratorium.butterflyEffect: Sheriff's deputies declared the gathering an unlawful assembly and moved in with tear gas, and journalist Ruben Salazar was killed by a tear gas canister fired into a nearby bar. His death turned him into a martyr for the Chicano movement and intensified activism against police treatment of Mexican-Americans.

evt-08-29-1975-tacnazo.scenario: It is August 1975 in Lima, and you serve on the general staff as Prime Minister Francisco Morales Bermúdez moves against an ailing President Velasco Alvarado, whose leftist military government has grown isolated and economically troubled.
evt-08-29-1975-tacnazo.prompt: What does Morales Bermúdez do to seize power from Velasco?

choices.text: Requests US military intervention to remove Velasco
Calls immediate elections to replace Velasco
Leads a bloodless military coup forcing Velasco's resignation
Assassinates Velasco during a cabinet meeting

evt-08-29-1975-tacnazo.butterflyEffect: The Tacnazo coup was bloodless; Velasco resigned and Morales Bermúdez took over, launching the 'Second Phase' of the Revolutionary Government. He rolled back many of Velasco's leftist reforms and eventually oversaw the transition to elections in 1980, ending twelve years of military rule.

evt-08-29-1984-osho.scenario: It is late August 1984 in The Dalles, Oregon, and members of the nearby Rajneeshpuram commune are quietly testing ways to sicken local voters ahead of a county election the commune desperately wants to influence.
evt-08-29-1984-osho.prompt: What method did they use to spread illness through the town?

choices.text: Distributing tainted flu vaccines at a free clinic.
Poisoning the town's public water supply directly.
Releasing an airborne toxin at a county fair.
Contaminating salad bars at local restaurants with Salmonella bacteria.

evt-08-29-1984-osho.butterflyEffect: The salmonella attack sickened over 750 people, making it the largest bioterrorism attack in U.S. history at the time, though no one died. The scandal exposed wider crimes at Rajneeshpuram, leading to the collapse of the commune, Rajneesh's deportation, and prison sentences for several of his top aides.

evt-08-29-1991-supreme-soviet-of-the-sov.scenario: It is 29 August 1991 in Moscow. The hardline coup against Gorbachev has just collapsed, and as a deputy in the Supreme Soviet you must decide the fate of the party whose members backed the plotters.
evt-08-29-1991-supreme-soviet-of-the-sov.prompt: What does the Supreme Soviet vote to do to the Communist Party?

choices.text: Call immediate new elections while leaving the party untouched
Suspend all activities of the Soviet Communist Party nationwide
Expel Gorbachev from the party but leave the party intact
Declare martial law to restore party authority

evt-08-29-1991-supreme-soviet-of-the-sov.butterflyEffect: The Supreme Soviet suspended all Communist Party activities across the USSR, ending its 74-year monopoly on power almost overnight. Within four months the Soviet Union itself dissolved, as republics declared independence and Gorbachev resigned in December 1991.

evt-08-29-1996-vnukovo-airlines-flight-2.scenario: It is 29 August 1996, and you are in the cockpit of a Tupolev Tu-154 descending toward remote Svalbard Airport through low Arctic cloud, relying on instruments over unfamiliar, mountainous terrain.
evt-08-29-1996-vnukovo-airlines-flight-2.prompt: What critical safeguard did the crew fail to maintain on approach?

choices.text: Confirming the aircraft's actual position against its charted approach course, rather than trusting a drifting instrument reading.
Lowering the landing gear before beginning descent.
Requesting permission to land from Norwegian air traffic control.
Switching to a visual approach in clear weather.

evt-08-29-1996-vnukovo-airlines-flight-2.butterflyEffect: Small, uncorrected navigational errors let the aircraft drift 3.7 kilometres off its approach centerline, and it struck Operafjellet mountain, killing all 141 aboard — the deadliest aviation accident in Norwegian history. The crash prompted renewed scrutiny of approach procedures at remote Arctic airports with limited ground-based navigation aids.

evt-08-29-2003-sayyid.scenario: It is 29 August 2003, and worshippers are streaming out of the Imam Ali Shrine in Najaf after Friday prayers, where Ayatollah Mohammed Baqir al-Hakim has just finished addressing the crowd.
evt-08-29-2003-sayyid.prompt: What happened moments later outside the shrine?

choices.text: Al-Hakim announced a power-sharing agreement with Sunni leaders.
A rival cleric challenged him to public debate inside the shrine.
A massive car bomb detonated, killing al-Hakim and scores of worshippers in one of the deadliest attacks of the post-invasion period.
Coalition troops arrested al-Hakim on charges of inciting rebellion.

evt-08-29-2003-sayyid.butterflyEffect: The bombing, one of the deadliest attacks in Iraq since the 2003 invasion, killed al-Hakim and further inflamed sectarian tension in the chaotic aftermath of Saddam's fall. Leadership of his party, the Supreme Council for the Islamic Revolution in Iraq, passed to his brother Abdul Aziz al-Hakim, who became a central power broker in postwar Iraqi politics.

evt-08-29-2005-hurricane-katrina.scenario: You are a New Orleans emergency official on 29 August 2005 as Hurricane Katrina's storm surge pushes against the city's levee system, with reports of rising water reaching low-lying neighborhoods.
evt-08-29-2005-hurricane-katrina.prompt: What actually happens to the city's flood defenses that day?

choices.text: Only rural parishes outside the city flood
Floodgates installed years earlier fully contain the surge
Several levees and floodwalls fail, flooding most of the city
The levees hold, but wind damage alone causes losses

evt-08-29-2005-hurricane-katrina.butterflyEffect: Multiple levees and floodwalls failed, flooding roughly eighty percent of New Orleans and overwhelming shelters like the Superdome. The catastrophic, uneven government response became a national scandal that drove sweeping reforms to FEMA, levee engineering standards, and disaster preparedness policy.

evt-08-29-2016-chen-quanguo.scenario: You are a local Communist Party cadre in Urumqi in late August 2016, watching the region's new party secretary arrive fresh from tightening security in Tibet, promising a new approach to stability in Xinjiang.
evt-08-29-2016-chen-quanguo.prompt: What security approach does Chen Quanguo bring with him to Xinjiang?

choices.text: Expanded religious freedoms to ease ethnic tensions
Mass surveillance and internment camps for Uyghurs and other Muslims
A power-sharing agreement with local Uyghur leaders
Economic liberalization and loosened travel restrictions

evt-08-29-2016-chen-quanguo.butterflyEffect: Chen built on his Tibet playbook to implement grid-style policing and mass internment camps targeting Uyghurs and other Muslim minorities. The policy drew international condemnation, sanctions on Chinese officials, and accusations of crimes against humanity.

evt-08-29-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.scenario: It's 29 August 2022, and you are a Ukrainian officer near the Dnipro River as your unit begins the long-promised southern counteroffensive into Kherson Oblast. Russian lines are dug in deep, and headlines abroad expect a quick breakthrough.
evt-08-29-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.prompt: What actually followed this slow, grinding push into Kherson?

choices.text: A ceasefire was signed before Ukrainian troops crossed into Kherson Oblast.
Russian forces collapsed within days and Ukraine retook the entire oblast by mid-September.
It ground down Russian forces for months, masking a surprise Ukrainian breakthrough near Kharkiv, before Russia withdrew from Kherson city that November.
The offensive stalled completely and Ukraine abandoned it within two weeks.

evt-08-29-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.butterflyEffect: The Kherson counteroffensive advanced slowly against fortified Russian positions, but it drew Russian reserves south — clearing the way for Ukraine's rapid Kharkiv counteroffensive in September. Facing encirclement west of the Dnipro, Russian forces withdrew from Kherson city on 11 November 2022, the war's most significant Ukrainian territorial recovery to date.

evt-08-30-1574-guru-ram-das.scenario: It is 1574, and the aging third Sikh guru, Amar Das, must choose who will lead the growing Sikh community after him.
evt-08-30-1574-guru-ram-das.prompt: Whom does Guru Amar Das name as his successor, the fourth Sikh guru?

choices.text: His own son Mohan
His son-in-law Bhai Jetha
A senior disciple unrelated to his family
A descendant of Guru Nanak

evt-08-30-1574-guru-ram-das.butterflyEffect: Amar Das chose his devoted son-in-law, Bhai Jetha, who became Guru Ram Das. He went on to found the city that became Amritsar and began digging the sacred pool later home to the Golden Temple, while the guruship began passing hereditarily through his family for the remaining Sikh gurus.

evt-08-30-1594-james-vi-and-i.scenario: It is 30 August 1594 at Stirling Castle. You are helping stage the elaborate masque for the baptism of Prince Henry, King James VI's first child, and the script calls for a live lion to pull an allegorical chariot into the banqueting hall.
evt-08-30-1594-james-vi-and-i.prompt: What do the organizers decide once the lion is judged too dangerous for the crowded hall?

choices.text: They release the lion into the hall regardless of the risk
They have a man dressed as a blackamoor draw the chariot instead
They cancel the chariot pageant entirely
They postpone the baptism until a tamer animal can be found

evt-08-30-1594-james-vi-and-i.butterflyEffect: The lion was withdrawn and a man costumed as a blackamoor drew the chariot instead. Printed accounts of the baptism's spectacle circulated across Europe, showcasing Stuart court magnificence and James's ambitions, which he would later pursue as king of a united England and Scotland.

evt-08-30-1896-philippine-revolution.scenario: It is before dawn on 30 August 1896, and you stand among Andrés Bonifacio's Katipunero fighters outside Manila, armed mostly with bolos, staring at the Spanish powder magazine and waterworks at San Juan del Monte.
evt-08-30-1896-philippine-revolution.prompt: What does Bonifacio order his poorly armed force to do?

choices.text: Open negotiations with the Spanish governor-general
Retreat to Cavite to join Aguinaldo's forces first
Storm the Spanish garrison to seize its arms and water supply
Wait in place for reinforcements from Manila

evt-08-30-1896-philippine-revolution.butterflyEffect: The Katipuneros stormed the Spanish garrison at El Depósito but were repelled with heavy losses. News of the revolt spread quickly, prompting Spain to declare martial law across nearby provinces and ultimately leading to the execution of José Rizal months later.

evt-08-30-1914-world-war-i.scenario: It's late August 1914. Your Russian Second Army has pushed deep into East Prussia, but German forces under Hindenburg and Ludendorff are closing in on both of your exposed flanks near Tannenberg.
evt-08-30-1914-world-war-i.prompt: What happens to General Samsonov's Second Army?

choices.text: It is encircled and destroyed, and Samsonov dies by suicide
It negotiates a local truce with the German command
It retreats safely back across the Russian border
It is reinforced by the First Army and wins the battle

evt-08-30-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The Second Army was encircled and annihilated, and Samsonov took his own life rather than report the disaster. The victory made instant national heroes of Hindenburg and Ludendorff, launching the partnership that would come to dominate German strategy for the rest of the war.

evt-08-30-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It's the night of 30 August 1942 in the Egyptian desert. Rommel's Afrika Korps, running low on fuel, pushes into British minefields at the Alam Halfa ridge hoping for one last breakthrough toward the Nile.
evt-08-30-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What happens to Rommel's offensive at Alam Halfa?

choices.text: Montgomery's counterattack immediately destroys the Afrika Korps
Both sides agree to a local ceasefire in the desert
He breaks through and captures Alexandria
His panzers stall for lack of fuel and are forced to withdraw

evt-08-30-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Montgomery's dug-in defenses and Rommel's chronic fuel shortages stopped the Axis advance cold, forcing a withdrawal by early September. The failure ended German hopes of reaching Suez and set up the decisive Allied victory at Second El Alamein weeks later, the turning point of the North African campaign.

evt-08-30-1959-abdul-muis.scenario: It is 30 August 1959, and Sukarno's government is deciding who should become the very first person officially named an Indonesian national hero, honoring decades of nationalist journalism and independence advocacy.
evt-08-30-1959-abdul-muis.prompt: Whose legacy as a writer and Sarekat Islam-era nationalist earns him this first-ever title?

choices.text: Ki Hajar Dewantara
Sutan Sjahrir
Tan Malaka
Abdul Muis

evt-08-30-1959-abdul-muis.butterflyEffect: Abdul Muis became Indonesia's first officially designated national hero. The honor established a formal program that would later recognize figures like Sukarno, Hatta, and Kartini, cementing how the young republic chose to memorialize its independence struggle.

evt-08-30-1967-thurgood-marshall.scenario: It is 30 August 1967, and you sit in the Senate gallery as members vote on Lyndon Johnson's nominee, the lawyer who argued Brown v. Board of Education and dismantled segregation in America's courts.
evt-08-30-1967-thurgood-marshall.prompt: What is the outcome of the Senate's vote on Marshall's nomination?

choices.text: Confirmed, becoming the first African-American Supreme Court justice
Confirmed on condition he recuse himself from civil rights cases
Withdrawn by Johnson under political pressure
Rejected after Southern senators filibustered the nomination

evt-08-30-1967-thurgood-marshall.butterflyEffect: Marshall was confirmed as the first African-American Supreme Court justice, serving until 1991. He became the Court's most consistent liberal voice, dissenting frequently as the bench grew more conservative in his later years.

evt-08-30-1974-1974-mitsubishi-heavy-ind.scenario: It is the morning of 30 August 1974 in Marunouchi, Tokyo. A bomb hidden near the Mitsubishi Heavy Industries headquarters detonates, planted by the far-left East Asia Anti-Japan Armed Front to protest the conglomerate's wartime legacy and its role supplying the U.S. military during the Vietnam War.
evt-08-30-1974-1974-mitsubishi-heavy-ind.prompt: How do Japanese police ultimately respond to the group behind this bombing?

choices.text: They close Tokyo's ports to foreign shipping in retaliation
They negotiate a public amnesty with the bombers
They blame the attack on a rival corporation and drop the investigation
They launch a years-long manhunt that eventually leads to mass arrests of the group's members

evt-08-30-1974-1974-mitsubishi-heavy-ind.butterflyEffect: The bombing began a wave of attacks by the East Asia Anti-Japan Armed Front against major Japanese corporations. Police mounted a sustained manhunt, and most surviving members were arrested in May 1975 after further bombings, ending the group's campaign and prompting tighter corporate security across Japan.

evt-08-30-1981-mohammad-ali-rajai.scenario: It is late August 1981. Four weeks into his presidency, Mohammad-Ali Rajai and prime minister Mohammad-Javad Bahonar are killed instantly when a bomb detonates during a security meeting in Tehran.
evt-08-30-1981-mohammad-ali-rajai.prompt: Who is elevated to the presidency in the chaos that follows this double assassination?

choices.text: Ali Khamenei is elected president
Ayatollah Khomeini assumes the presidency himself
A military council rules Iran directly
Abolhassan Banisadr is reinstated as president

evt-08-30-1981-mohammad-ali-rajai.butterflyEffect: Ali Khamenei was elected Iran's third president in October 1981. He would go on to become Supreme Leader in 1989 after Khomeini's death, a position he still holds, making this bombing an unlikely hinge point in modern Iranian history.

evt-08-30-1984-space-shuttle-discovery.scenario: You are a NASA flight engineer in Houston on 30 August 1984, watching Discovery finally lift off weeks after a launch pad abort scrapped its first attempt, carrying a payload bay full of commercial cargo.
evt-08-30-1984-space-shuttle-discovery.prompt: What is Discovery's main objective on this maiden mission, STS-41-D?

choices.text: Repair the Hubble Space Telescope in orbit
Deploy three commercial communications satellites and test a solar array
Launch a classified military reconnaissance satellite
Dock with the Soviet Mir space station

evt-08-30-1984-space-shuttle-discovery.butterflyEffect: Discovery deployed three satellites and tested a large solar array, proving the shuttle's commercial value. It went on to fly more missions than any other orbiter, later launching Hubble and returning the fleet to flight after both the Challenger and Columbia disasters.

evt-08-30-1995-bosnian-war.scenario: It's 30 August 1995. Weeks after a mortar shell killed dozens in a Sarajevo market, NATO warplanes sit fueled and armed, aimed at Bosnian Serb Army positions across the country.
evt-08-30-1995-bosnian-war.prompt: What does NATO's bombing campaign ultimately force the Bosnian Serbs to do?

choices.text: Call on Russia to intervene militarily on their behalf
Agree to peace talks that produce the Dayton Accords
Escalate by shelling Sarajevo more heavily than before
Formally surrender all territory within days

evt-08-30-1995-bosnian-war.butterflyEffect: Operation Deliberate Force battered Bosnian Serb command and communications, forcing the withdrawal of heavy weapons from around Sarajevo. Within weeks the pressure pushed all parties to the negotiating table, producing the Dayton Accords that November and ending the war.

evt-08-30-2007-heavy-bomber.scenario: It's August 2007 at Minot Air Force Base. You're on the ground crew tasked with moving a rack of AGM-129 missiles onto a B-52 bound for Barksdale, and no one has confirmed whether the warheads were removed first.
evt-08-30-2007-heavy-bomber.prompt: What is discovered only after the bomber has landed and sat unguarded for hours?

choices.text: Ground crew caught the mistake before the plane ever took off
The bomber diverted mid-flight after cockpit alarms sounded
The missiles were still armed with live nuclear warheads
The missiles were inert training rounds all along

evt-08-30-2007-heavy-bomber.butterflyEffect: The missiles were live nuclear warheads, and the error went unnoticed for roughly 36 hours after the flight. The incident became one of the most serious US nuclear security lapses in decades, prompting reforms including the creation of Air Force Global Strike Command to tighten oversight of nuclear weapons handling.

evt-08-30-2021-2020-2021-us-troop-withdr.scenario: It's the night of 30 August 2021 at Kabul's airport. You are among the last American troops on the ground, minutes from boarding the final flight out after twenty years of war.
evt-08-30-2021-2020-2021-us-troop-withdr.prompt: What marks the literal end of America's military presence in Afghanistan?

choices.text: The last U.S. general boards the final C-17 as troops depart
The airport gate is bombed just as the last troops leave
Taliban negotiators board the same flight for talks abroad
The evacuation is suspended for several more months

evt-08-30-2021-2020-2021-us-troop-withdr.butterflyEffect: Major General Chris Donahue became the last U.S. soldier to board the final C-17 out of Kabul, closing the 20-year war. The chaotic final days of the airlift, and the scenes of desperation at the airport, drew intense scrutiny over the fate of Afghan allies left behind and the Taliban's swift return to power.

evt-08-31-1218-al-kamil.scenario: It is 1218, and you have just become Ayyubid sultan of Egypt when a Crusader fleet lands and lays siege to the port of Damietta. Your kingdom's survival may hinge on what you offer the invaders.
evt-08-31-1218-al-kamil.prompt: What bargain does Al-Kamil offer the crusaders to save Egypt?

choices.text: Offer a permanent truce along the current frontier with no land ceded
Refuse all terms and commit his full army to a decisive battle immediately
Cede Jerusalem and the old crusader kingdom in exchange for their withdrawal
Pay a massive tribute in gold to buy them off

evt-08-31-1218-al-kamil.butterflyEffect: Al-Kamil offered to cede Jerusalem and most of the former Kingdom of Jerusalem in exchange for the crusaders abandoning Damietta and Egypt. Papal legate Pelagius rejected the deal, the Fifth Crusade pressed on and was eventually crushed by Nile floods and Ayyubid forces. Al-Kamil would later strike a similar deal with Frederick II in 1229, peacefully handing over Jerusalem without a fight.

evt-08-31-1814-war-of-1812.scenario: It is the night of August 31, 1814, and you are a Maryland militiaman under Lt. Col. Philip Reed, dug in near Georgetown, Maryland. British Royal Marines under Sir Peter Parker are advancing through the dark to strike your camp before dawn.
evt-08-31-1814-war-of-1812.prompt: What happens when the British assault hits your lines at Caulk's Field?

choices.text: The British are repelled and Parker is killed
The militia retreats without engaging
The British overrun the militia camp
Both sides agree to a local truce

evt-08-31-1814-war-of-1812.butterflyEffect: The militia held its ground, and Sir Peter Parker was killed leading the charge, a loss mourned in Britain as a rising naval star. Coming just days after the burning of Washington, the American victory boosted morale in the Chesapeake and fed into the successful defense of Baltimore two weeks later.

evt-08-31-1876-murad-v.scenario: You are a senior Ottoman official in Constantinople in August 1876, watching Sultan Murad V's mental health collapse just weeks into his reign as ministers debate what to do.
evt-08-31-1876-murad-v.prompt: What does the palace decide regarding the destabilized sultan?

choices.text: Send Murad abroad for medical treatment while retaining his title
Declare Murad mentally unfit and depose him in favor of Abdul Hamid II
Keep Murad as a figurehead while ministers govern in his name
Restore his predecessor Abdulaziz to the throne instead

evt-08-31-1876-murad-v.butterflyEffect: Murad V was declared mentally unfit and deposed after only 93 days, replaced by his half-brother Abdul Hamid II. Abdul Hamid initially promised a constitution but suspended it within two years, ruling as an autocrat for three decades and reshaping the empire's final era.

evt-08-31-1886-1886-charleston-earthquak.scenario: It is just before 10 p.m. on 31 August 1886, and the ground beneath Charleston, South Carolina, begins to heave violently. Brick buildings crack and chimneys topple as families rush from their homes into the streets.
evt-08-31-1886-1886-charleston-earthquak.prompt: What do most terrified Charleston residents do in the nights after the quake?

choices.text: Return immediately to repair and re-occupy their homes
Camp outdoors in tents, refusing to sleep inside damaged buildings
Evacuate the city entirely by train within a day
Gather inside the sturdiest brick churches for safety

evt-08-31-1886-1886-charleston-earthquak.butterflyEffect: Fearing collapsing walls and aftershocks, thousands of residents slept outdoors in tents and makeshift shelters in parks and squares for weeks. The quake, unusual for its intraplate location far from typical fault boundaries, prompted early scientific study of seismic activity on the U.S. East Coast and remains a benchmark for assessing earthquake risk in the region today.

evt-08-31-1897-thomas-edison.scenario: It is 1897, and Thomas Edison has just secured a U.S. patent on the Kinetoscope, his peephole viewing device for motion pictures. Entrepreneurs across the country want to cash in on the novelty.
evt-08-31-1897-thomas-edison.prompt: How do audiences first experience Edison's motion pictures commercially?

choices.text: Peering individually through a viewer in coin-operated Kinetoscope parlors
Viewing films broadcast into private homes via early television sets
Attending free public screenings funded entirely by Edison's company
Watching films projected onto large screens in dedicated theaters

evt-08-31-1897-thomas-edison.butterflyEffect: Kinetoscope parlors sprang up in cities, letting customers pay a nickel to peer through a viewer at short moving films—a format that soon gave way to projected film shown to whole audiences at once. Edison's aggressive patent enforcement also sparked years of litigation with rival filmmakers, fueling the migration of the early film industry toward Hollywood, partly to escape his patent trust.

evt-08-31-1939-gleiwitz-incident.scenario: It is the night of 31 August 1939, and you are an SS officer dressed in a Polish uniform, sent to stage a fake attack on the German radio station at Gleiwitz to give Hitler his pretext for war.
evt-08-31-1939-gleiwitz-incident.prompt: What do you do to make the staged raid convincing?

choices.text: Seize the station and hold it under guard until the Wehrmacht arrives
Broadcast a brief anti-German message and leave a disguised body as staged evidence
Take hostages from the station back across the border into Germany
Destroy the transmitter equipment to cripple German broadcasts

evt-08-31-1939-gleiwitz-incident.butterflyEffect: The SS broadcast a brief anti-German message in Polish and left behind a drugged concentration-camp prisoner dressed as a dead saboteur as fabricated evidence. Along with two dozen similar staged incidents, it gave Hitler his casus belli, and German forces invaded Poland the very next morning, igniting the Second World War in Europe.

evt-08-31-1942-1942-matagorda-hurricane.scenario: It's 30 August 1942, and you're a Coast Guard officer stationed near Matagorda, Texas, watching barometers plunge as a Category 3 hurricane bears down on the wartime coastline.
evt-08-31-1942-1942-matagorda-hurricane.prompt: What is your top priority as the storm closes in on the Texas coast?

choices.text: Maintain the wartime coastal blackout and keep everyone in place
Evacuate coastal residents inland immediately
Suppress the storm warning to protect wartime secrecy
Send ships out to sea to intercept German U-boats

evt-08-31-1942-1942-matagorda-hurricane.butterflyEffect: Coastal residents and oil-industry workers were evacuated inland ahead of landfall near Matagorda on 30 August. The storm caused heavy damage to Gulf Coast infrastructure at a moment when wartime production made every refinery and port critical, prompting stronger hurricane preparedness along the Texas coast afterward.

evt-08-31-1969-isle-of-wight-festival-19.scenario: It's 31 August 1969, and you're packed among roughly 150,000 people on the Isle of Wight, waiting for the festival's closing headliner to finally take the stage.
evt-08-31-1969-isle-of-wight-festival-19.prompt: Which reclusive star ended a three-year retreat from touring to headline this closing night?

choices.text: Bob Dylan
Jimi Hendrix
Elvis Presley
The Beatles

evt-08-31-1969-isle-of-wight-festival-19.butterflyEffect: Bob Dylan's surprise return drew a crowd rivaling Woodstock's, but the event ran smoothly and without the chaos of its American counterpart. His appearance cemented the Isle of Wight as a major rival festival and paved the way for the even larger 1970 edition.

evt-08-31-1980-lech-wa-esa.scenario: It is 31 August 1980, and you are a shipyard worker standing beside Lech Wałęsa inside the Lenin Shipyard in Gdańsk, moments before he signs an agreement with the Polish government to end the strike.
evt-08-31-1980-lech-wa-esa.prompt: What did the Gdańsk Agreement grant that made Solidarity the Eastern Bloc's first independent union?

choices.text: The abolition of martial law across Poland
Poland's withdrawal from the Warsaw Pact
The right to form free trade unions independent of the Communist Party
Immediate multi-party elections for the Polish parliament

evt-08-31-1980-lech-wa-esa.butterflyEffect: The agreement recognized the right to form trade unions independent of the Communist Party. Solidarity's membership swelled past ten million, prompting martial law in 1981, but the movement survived underground and forced the 1989 Round Table talks that ended communist rule in Poland and hastened the Cold War's close.

evt-08-31-1993-lithuania.scenario: It is 31 August 1993, and you watch from the border as the final Russian soldiers cross out of Lithuania, the first Baltic state to see a complete withdrawal.
evt-08-31-1993-lithuania.prompt: What concession did Lithuania grant Russia to help secure this full troop withdrawal?

choices.text: A postponement of any future NATO membership bid
A free trade agreement favoring Russian goods
A permanent Russian naval base at Klaipėda
Transit rights for Russian military traffic to Kaliningrad

evt-08-31-1993-lithuania.butterflyEffect: Lithuania agreed to allow Russian military transit to and from the Kaliningrad exclave through its territory, easing Moscow's objections. The completed withdrawal let Lithuania move fastest among the Baltics toward Western institutions, joining both NATO and the EU in 2004.

evt-08-31-1994-estonia.scenario: It is August 1994, and you are an Estonian official watching the last convoy of Russian soldiers prepare to leave Estonian soil after years of stalled negotiations.
evt-08-31-1994-estonia.prompt: What condition had Russia insisted on before completing the withdrawal?

choices.text: Estonia's continued membership in the Commonwealth of Independent States
Guarantees for the rights and status of Estonia's Russian-speaking minority
A permanent Russian naval base on Estonian territory
A formal treaty of Estonian neutrality

evt-08-31-1994-estonia.butterflyEffect: Moscow linked withdrawal to guarantees for the rights of the large ethnic Russian population left in Estonia after Soviet rule. Once resolved, the pullout cleared a major obstacle to Estonia's Western integration, paving the way for eventual EU and NATO membership a decade later.

evt-08-31-1996-saddam-hussein.scenario: It is August 1996 in northern Iraq, and Kurdish leader Masoud Barzani's KDP forces are losing ground to the rival PUK, which is receiving backing from Iran.
evt-08-31-1996-saddam-hussein.prompt: What does Barzani decide to do to save his position around Irbil?

choices.text: Abandon the KDP's rivalry and ally openly with Iran instead
Seek direct American military intervention on the KDP's behalf
Negotiate a power-sharing deal with the PUK without outside help
Request that Saddam Hussein's army intervene militarily against the PUK

evt-08-31-1996-saddam-hussein.butterflyEffect: Barzani's appeal brought Saddam's army into Irbil, where it crushed PUK forces and rounded up and executed dozens of US-backed opposition operatives, gutting the CIA's covert network inside Iraq almost overnight. The debacle forced a hasty evacuation of remaining American assets and hardened Washington's later push for stricter containment of Baghdad.

evt-08-31-1997-diana-princess-of-wales.scenario: It is just past midnight on 31 August 1997 in Paris. Diana, Princess of Wales, and Dodi Fayed leave the Ritz Hotel with paparazzi in close pursuit, and their driver must choose how to lose the chasing motorcycles through the city streets.
evt-08-31-1997-diana-princess-of-wales.prompt: What happens as the car speeds to evade photographers through the Pont de l'Alma underpass?

choices.text: The car safely outruns the photographers and reaches the hotel
The driver pulls over and confronts the paparazzi directly
The car is deliberately forced off the road by a rival vehicle
The car crashes into a pillar in the tunnel at high speed

evt-08-31-1997-diana-princess-of-wales.butterflyEffect: The car, driven by Henri Paul at high speed while over the legal alcohol limit, crashed in the tunnel, killing Diana, Dodi Fayed, and Paul; only bodyguard Trevor Rees-Jones survived. The tragedy triggered an outpouring of public grief in Britain, intense scrutiny of paparazzi ethics and press regulation, and years of inquests into the crash's causes.

evt-08-31-1999-lineas-aereas-privadas-ar.scenario: It's 31 August 1999, and you're boarding LAPA Flight 3142 at Aeroparque Jorge Newbery in Buenos Aires for a short domestic hop, unaware the crew is rushing through their pre-takeoff checks.
evt-08-31-1999-lineas-aereas-privadas-ar.prompt: What critical step did the crew fail to complete before their fatal takeoff roll?

choices.text: Checking the fuel gauge readings
Setting the flaps and slats for takeoff
Verifying the autopilot was engaged
Confirming the landing gear had retracted

evt-08-31-1999-lineas-aereas-privadas-ar.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the crew, distracted by conversation, never properly configured the flaps and slats for takeoff, and ignored cockpit alarms warning of the error. The crash killed 65 people and led to LAPA's operations being progressively restricted, culminating in the airline losing its license in 2003 and Argentina tightening cockpit-discipline regulations.

evt-08-31-2002-typhoon-rusa.scenario: It is late August 2002, and you are a local official in Gangneung, South Korea, as Typhoon Rusa churns toward the coast carrying record-breaking rainfall.
evt-08-31-2002-typhoon-rusa.prompt: What is the most urgent action you should take before the storm makes landfall?

choices.text: Wait for the central government to issue a formal evacuation order first
Focus resources on protecting the rice harvest before dealing with residents
Order immediate evacuation of riverside and low-lying neighborhoods to higher ground
Delay any action until after the rains have peaked to assess real damage

evt-08-31-2002-typhoon-rusa.butterflyEffect: Rusa dumped record rainfall on South Korea, killing over 200 people and causing billions of dollars in damage, the worst typhoon disaster the country had seen. The catastrophe pushed South Korea to overhaul its flood-warning systems and disaster-response infrastructure in the years that followed.

evt-08-31-2005-2005-al-aimmah-bridge-dis.scenario: It is August 31, 2005, and you are among hundreds of thousands of Shia pilgrims crossing the Al-Aaimmah Bridge in Baghdad toward the Kadhimiya shrine. A rumor suddenly races through the packed crowd that a suicide bomber is hidden among you.
evt-08-31-2005-2005-al-aimmah-bridge-dis.prompt: What actually caused the mass casualties that followed on the bridge?

choices.text: A bomb detonated directly on the bridge deck
The bridge itself structurally collapsed from overcrowding
A boat crashed into a bridge support underneath
Panic caused a crowd surge that collapsed barriers, pushing people into the river

evt-08-31-2005-2005-al-aimmah-bridge-dis.butterflyEffect: The rumor sparked a panicked surge; barriers gave way and many were crushed or forced into the Tigris River below, drowning in the chaos. The tragedy exposed the dangers of unmanaged crowd control at Iraq's religious gatherings and led to calls for better security at future pilgrimages during the ongoing insurgency.

evt-08-31-2006-edvard-munch.scenario: It is August 31, 2006, more than two years after masked gunmen tore Edvard Munch's The Scream and Madonna off the walls of Oslo's Munch Museum in broad daylight. Norwegian police have just announced the missing masterpieces have finally been located.
evt-08-31-2006-edvard-munch.prompt: In what condition are the recovered paintings found?

choices.text: Replaced by forgeries, with the originals never found
Damaged but restorable, needing years of conservation work
Perfectly preserved with no damage at all
So badly ruined they could never be displayed again

evt-08-31-2006-edvard-munch.butterflyEffect: Both paintings had suffered damage, including moisture harm and tears, requiring years of careful restoration before returning to public display in 2008. The recovery also led to convictions of several men involved in the 2004 armed heist and prompted the museum to overhaul its security.

evt-09-01-1604-guru-granth-sahib.scenario: It is 1604 in Amritsar, and Guru Arjan Dev is compiling the sacred hymns of the Sikh Gurus into a single, definitive volume. You are helping him decide whose writings, beyond the Gurus' own, belong in the book.
evt-09-01-1604-guru-granth-sahib.prompt: Whose hymns does Guru Arjan Dev include alongside the Sikh Gurus' own writings?

choices.text: Sanskrit verses translated from Vedic scripture
Hymns from Hindu bhakti and Muslim Sufi saints like Kabir and Farid
Only writings by professed Sikhs
Persian court poetry favored by the Mughal emperor

evt-09-01-1604-guru-granth-sahib.butterflyEffect: Guru Arjan's Adi Granth wove together voices across faiths, and after the tenth Guru, Gobind Singh, declared the text itself the eternal Guru in 1708, it became the Guru Granth Sahib—still installed daily at the Golden Temple and revered as Sikhism's living spiritual authority.

evt-09-01-1774-thomas-gage.scenario: It is late August 1774 near Boston. Word spreads through the Massachusetts countryside that Governor Thomas Gage's redcoats have seized the colony's gunpowder from the provincial magazine.
evt-09-01-1774-thomas-gage.prompt: How do the alarmed colonial militias respond to news of the powder seizure?

choices.text: They rapidly muster thousands of armed men and march toward Boston
They quietly disband, deciding the loss of powder is not worth a response
They immediately storm British barracks in open battle
They send a formal petition to King George III and wait for his reply

evt-09-01-1774-thomas-gage.butterflyEffect: Tens of thousands of militiamen mobilized and marched toward Boston in what became known as the Powder Alarm, only stopping when they learned no bloodshed had occurred. The episode revealed how fast and how large colonial forces could rally, a lesson both sides drew on before Lexington and Concord the following spring.

evt-09-01-1804-karl-ludwig-harding.scenario: It's September 1804 at the Lilienthal observatory in Germany. Scanning the sky between Mars and Jupiter for the 'missing planet' predicted by Bode's law, you spot a faint point of light that wasn't on your star charts.
evt-09-01-1804-karl-ludwig-harding.prompt: What should you do to confirm this is a new discovery, not a fixed star?

choices.text: Immediately publish the coordinates without further observation
Assume it is a comet and stop observing
Wait for confirmation from the Paris Observatory before recording anything
Track its position over several nights to detect motion against the background stars

evt-09-01-1804-karl-ludwig-harding.butterflyEffect: Harding's careful tracking confirmed a new body, which he named Juno—the third such object found after Ceres and Pallas. When Vesta was found in 1807 and no further planets appeared for decades, astronomers realized these were a new class of small bodies, coining the term 'asteroid.'

evt-09-01-1859-carrington-event.scenario: It is the night of 1–2 September 1859. You operate a telegraph key in the eastern United States, and the line has suddenly gone wild with current no battery of yours produced, sparks jumping from the equipment.
evt-09-01-1859-carrington-event.prompt: What should you do to keep messages moving on the surging line?

choices.text: Shut the line down completely until the sparking stops
Add more battery power to overpower the interference
Ground the wire and wait for a repair crew
Disconnect the battery and send using the induced current alone

evt-09-01-1859-carrington-event.butterflyEffect: Some operators discovered they could disconnect their batteries entirely and send messages using only the induced current from the geomagnetic storm. The Carrington Event remains the benchmark for worst-case space weather, and modern grid and satellite operators still plan for a repeat.

evt-09-01-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: It is the afternoon of 1 September 1862 near Chantilly, Virginia. You command a Union rearguard covering the army's retreat from Second Bull Run as a thunderstorm breaks and Confederate troops under Stonewall Jackson appear on the flank.
evt-09-01-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: What do you do to protect the retreating Army of Virginia?

choices.text: Turn and fight a rearguard action to block the Confederate flanking attack
Continue the retreat without engaging the enemy
Surrender the rearguard to avoid further casualties
Halt and wait for McClellan's army to arrive as reinforcement

evt-09-01-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Union forces turned and fought a fierce rearguard action in a driving thunderstorm at Chantilly (Ox Hill), losing Generals Kearny and Stevens but blocking Jackson's attempt to cut off the retreat. The stand let Pope's battered army reach the safety of Washington, closing the Northern Virginia Campaign and setting the stage for Lee's invasion of Maryland weeks later at Antietam.

evt-09-01-1872-battle-of-orange-walk.scenario: It is 1 September 1872 in Orange Walk, British Honduras. You command a small West India Regiment garrison, and word arrives too late that Icaiche Maya fighters under Marcus Canul have crossed the border undetected and are attacking the town while your officers are still in the bath.
evt-09-01-1872-battle-of-orange-walk.prompt: What should the garrison do against the surprise attack?

choices.text: Fortify and defend the barracks building despite being caught off guard
Surrender the garrison to avoid civilian casualties in the town
Send a messenger to negotiate a truce with Canul before fighting begins
Abandon the town and retreat toward the coast immediately

evt-09-01-1872-battle-of-orange-walk.butterflyEffect: The garrison held its barracks building for hours, inflicting heavy losses on the attackers and fatally wounding Marcus Canul, who died soon after. His death and the Maya withdrawal into Mexico eased the threat to British settlements in the district and reinforced colonial confidence in Belize's frontier defenses.

evt-09-01-1914-passenger-pigeon.scenario: It is 1 September 1914 at the Cincinnati Zoo. You are a keeper checking on Martha, an aging pigeon in a cage who is, as far as anyone knows, the last of her kind left alive on Earth.
evt-09-01-1914-passenger-pigeon.prompt: What happens to Martha, and what does it mark?

choices.text: She dies, marking the extinction of the passenger pigeon
She successfully hatches chicks, saving the species
She is released into the wild to rejoin a surviving flock
She is transferred to another zoo for a breeding program

evt-09-01-1914-passenger-pigeon.butterflyEffect: Martha died that day, marking the extinction of the passenger pigeon, a species that had once numbered in the billions and darkened American skies during migration. Her death became a landmark symbol of human-caused extinction and helped spur early wildlife protection laws, including the Migratory Bird Treaty Act of 1918.

evt-09-01-1939-invasion-of-poland.scenario: It is dawn on September 1, 1939, and you command a Polish infantry unit near the German frontier. Word arrives that Wehrmacht columns have crossed the border without warning, backed by aircraft and armor far outmatching your defenses.
evt-09-01-1939-invasion-of-poland.prompt: What order do most Polish frontier units receive in these opening days?

choices.text: Hold in place and wait for a French offensive to draw German forces away
Surrender at once to spare civilian casualties
Withdraw from forward positions to more defensible lines further east
Launch an immediate full counteroffensive into Germany

evt-09-01-1939-invasion-of-poland.butterflyEffect: Polish forces fell back from exposed frontier positions toward more defensible lines, hoping to hold out until French and British aid arrived. That aid never came in time; within weeks the Soviet invasion from the east sealed Poland's defeat, and the war that began that morning would engulf the continent for six years.

evt-09-01-1952-ernest-hemingway.scenario: It is early September 1952, and you are an editor at Life magazine deciding whether to run Ernest Hemingway's new short novel, The Old Man and the Sea, complete in a single issue.
evt-09-01-1952-ernest-hemingway.prompt: What happens when the issue reaches newsstands?

choices.text: The issue sells poorly and is pulled from newsstands
Critics unanimously dismiss the novella as a minor work
The issue sells more than five million copies within two days
Hemingway demands the story instead be serialized over several issues

evt-09-01-1952-ernest-hemingway.butterflyEffect: The issue sold over five million copies within two days, an extraordinary reception for a work of literary fiction. The novella's success revived Hemingway's standing after a run of poor reviews and contributed directly to his Pulitzer Prize in 1953 and Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954.

evt-09-01-1967-1967-arab-league-summit.scenario: It is late August 1967 in Khartoum. You are among the Arab leaders meeting weeks after the catastrophic defeat in the Six-Day War, and the summit must decide its official stance toward Israel.
evt-09-01-1967-1967-arab-league-summit.prompt: What position do the assembled Arab states adopt toward Israel?

choices.text: Formal recognition of Israel in exchange for territorial withdrawal
Immediate peace talks brokered through the United Nations
No peace, no recognition, and no negotiations with Israel
A unilateral ceasefire with no further political demands

evt-09-01-1967-1967-arab-league-summit.butterflyEffect: The summit issued the Khartoum Resolution, the famous "Three No's": no peace, no recognition, no negotiation with Israel, while pledging oil revenues to aid the defeated states. That hardline stance shaped Arab-Israeli diplomacy for a decade, until Egypt broke with it at Camp David in 1978.

evt-09-01-1969-muammar-gaddafi.scenario: It is the night of 1 September 1969 in Libya. You are a young army officer with Muammar Gaddafi's inner circle; King Idris is abroad in Turkey, and your group has hours to seize the country before dawn.
evt-09-01-1969-muammar-gaddafi.prompt: What do you do to seize power with minimal bloodshed?

choices.text: Wait for the king to return and formally demand his abdication
Seize radio stations, airports, and military bases while the king is abroad
Organize a public referendum on ending the monarchy
Request that the British garrison mediate a transfer of power

evt-09-01-1969-muammar-gaddafi.butterflyEffect: The officers seized radio stations, airports, and military bases overnight in a bloodless coup, and Gaddafi announced the overthrow of the monarchy the next morning. He would rule Libya for 42 years, reshaping it through his own 'Third International Theory' until his overthrow in the 2011 civil war.

evt-09-01-1973-rescue-of-roger-mallinson.scenario: It is 1 September 1973. You are part of the rescue team above the Celtic Sea, where the submersible Pisces III lies stranded on the seabed at 1,575 feet with two men and dwindling air.
evt-09-01-1973-rescue-of-roger-mallinson.prompt: How do you get the trapped crew to the surface?

choices.text: Detonate charges to free it from the seabed
Send divers down to physically pull the vessel free
Wait for the crew's air supply to stabilize on its own
Send other submersibles down to attach lifting lines and winch it up

evt-09-01-1973-rescue-of-roger-mallinson.butterflyEffect: Sister submersibles Pisces V and Pisces II, aided by the ROV CURV, managed to hook lines onto Pisces III and haul it up with only minutes of air to spare. The 76-hour operation became the deepest successful submarine rescue in history and reshaped protocols for deep-sea emergency response.

evt-09-01-1981-david-dacko.scenario: It is 1 September 1981 in Bangui. General André Kolingba's soldiers have moved against your government, and as President you must decide how to respond to the coup unfolding around the palace.
evt-09-01-1981-david-dacko.prompt: What does President Dacko do as Kolingba's coup takes hold?

choices.text: He appeals to French paratroopers to crush the coup by force
He flees immediately to a neighboring country before any confrontation
He orders loyal troops to fight the coup plotters in the streets
He yields power without resistance, allowing a bloodless transfer

evt-09-01-1981-david-dacko.butterflyEffect: Dacko stepped aside without armed resistance, and the takeover passed into history as a bloodless coup. Kolingba would rule the Central African Republic for over a decade, while Dacko reinvented himself as an opposition figure and presidential candidate for the rest of his long political career.

evt-09-01-1985-titanic.scenario: It is September 1985 aboard the research vessel Knorr in the North Atlantic. You are part of Robert Ballard's team, towing a camera sled called Argo across the seabed in search of the Titanic, which has eluded searchers for over seventy years.
evt-09-01-1985-titanic.prompt: What search strategy finally leads the team to the wreck?

choices.text: Search only along the ship's last radioed coordinates before sinking
Follow the trail of debris scattered across the ocean floor instead of hunting for the hull
Use explosive charges to force buried wreckage to the surface
Rely solely on sonar pings without any visual camera equipment

evt-09-01-1985-titanic.butterflyEffect: Ballard's team found the wreck by following its scattered debris field rather than searching for the intact hull, locating Titanic broken in two at roughly 12,500 feet down. The discovery launched a new era of deep-sea archaeology and salvage expeditions, sparked legal battles over artifact recovery rights, and fueled decades of popular fascination, including the 1997 film.

evt-09-01-2000-speakers-corner-singapore.scenario: It is September 1, 2000, and Singapore has just opened Speakers' Corner in Hong Lim Park, a spot where citizens can speak on public issues without the usual licence required elsewhere in the country. You want to give a speech there this week.
evt-09-01-2000-speakers-corner-singapore.prompt: What must you do before you are allowed to speak at the new venue?

choices.text: Register your intent to speak with police beforehand
Submit the text of your speech for official pre-approval
Nothing at all, speeches required no formalities from the start
Obtain a full public entertainment licence from the government

evt-09-01-2000-speakers-corner-singapore.butterflyEffect: Speakers had to register with police at the Kreta Ayer Neighbourhood Police Post up to 30 days in advance, and could speak only between 7am and 7pm without amplification. The venue was Singapore's first tentative opening for public speech, and later reforms in 2008 dropped the registration rule for citizens and allowed round-the-clock use with amplification.

evt-09-01-2004-beslan-school-siege.scenario: It is 3 September 2004, day three of the Beslan school siege. You are a Russian special forces commander outside the besieged school as explosions suddenly rip through the gymnasium holding hundreds of hostages.
evt-09-01-2004-beslan-school-siege.prompt: What follows the explosions in the gymnasium?

choices.text: Special forces storm the building amid chaotic fighting
The hostage-takers surrender without further violence
Negotiators secure an immediate ceasefire and evacuation
Authorities withdraw all forces to avoid further casualties

evt-09-01-2004-beslan-school-siege.butterflyEffect: Russian forces stormed the building in chaotic fighting that followed the blasts, and the siege ended with 334 deaths, including 186 children. The crisis led President Putin to abolish direct elections for regional governors and centralize security powers, changes still debated as part of Russia's post-Soviet political trajectory.

evt-09-01-2008-iraq-war.scenario: It is 1 September 2008 in Ramadi, Anbar Province. You are a US Marine officer preparing a formal ceremony to hand provincial security over to the Iraqi government after years of brutal insurgent fighting.
evt-09-01-2008-iraq-war.prompt: What follows the handover ceremony in Anbar?

choices.text: Provincial elections in Anbar are postponed indefinitely
Iraqi Security Forces assume provincial control while US troops shift to an advisory role
US Marines withdraw entirely from Iraq that same day
Al-Qaeda in Iraq immediately retakes control of Fallujah

evt-09-01-2008-iraq-war.butterflyEffect: Iraqi Security Forces formally took control of Anbar, once the deadliest province of the insurgency, while US troops shifted to an advisory role. The handover, made possible by the Sunni tribal 'Anbar Awakening' against al-Qaeda in Iraq, was held up as proof the 2007 surge strategy was working and became a template for further provincial transfers ahead of the 2011 US withdrawal.

evt-09-02-bce31-battle-of-actium.scenario: It is 2 September 31 BC, and you serve aboard Mark Antony's fleet, blockaded in the Ambracian Gulf by Octavian's faster ships under Agrippa. Disease and desertion have thinned your crews, and the fleet must break out or starve.
evt-09-02-bce31-battle-of-actium.prompt: What does Antony's fleet attempt as battle is joined?

choices.text: Burn the ships and fight as infantry on the mainland
Surrender the fleet intact to Octavian to spare the crews
Retreat north to link up with Antony's legions in Macedonia
Force a breakout south while Cleopatra's squadron waits to flee with the treasury

evt-09-02-bce31-battle-of-actium.butterflyEffect: Antony's ships were routed, and he abandoned his own battle line to follow Cleopatra's fleeing squadron. The defeat left Antony and Cleopatra to take their own lives within a year, and Octavian's victory made him the unrivaled master of Rome—soon to be styled Augustus, first emperor of Rome.

evt-09-02-1666-great-fire-of-london.scenario: It is the early hours of 2 September 1666, and you are a baker's apprentice on Pudding Lane. A spark from the ovens has caught the timber-framed houses, and the flames are already leaping between the tightly packed buildings toward the Thames.
evt-09-02-1666-great-fire-of-london.prompt: What is the most effective way for Londoners to try to stop the fire's spread?

choices.text: Redirect the Thames water supply through the streets
Form bucket brigades to douse the flames directly
Pull down houses ahead of the flames to create firebreaks
Wait for the Lord Mayor to authorise the use of gunpowder immediately

evt-09-02-1666-great-fire-of-london.butterflyEffect: The fire burned for five days, destroying most of the medieval City of London including Old St Paul's Cathedral, but killed relatively few people. The rebuilding that followed, led by figures like Christopher Wren, introduced brick construction, wider streets, and some of the first fire insurance schemes in England.

evt-09-02-1789-united-states-department-.scenario: It is September 1789, and the First Congress has just created a Treasury Department to manage the young nation's crushing war debts. President Washington must now choose someone to run it.
evt-09-02-1789-united-states-department-.prompt: Who did Washington appoint as the first Secretary of the Treasury?

choices.text: Alexander Hamilton
John Jay
Robert Morris
Thomas Jefferson

evt-09-02-1789-united-states-department-.butterflyEffect: Alexander Hamilton took the post and built a national bank, assumed state war debts, and established federal credit. His financial system provoked fierce opposition from Jefferson and Madison, hardening the rivalry that produced America's first political parties.

evt-09-02-1792-french-revolution.scenario: It is 2 September 1792. Word has just reached Paris that Verdun has fallen to Prussian-led forces advancing on the capital. You sit on the Paris Commune as crowds gather outside the city's overcrowded prisons, convinced that the prisoners inside are traitors waiting to open the gates to the enemy.
evt-09-02-1792-french-revolution.prompt: What do the enraged Parisian crowds do to the prisoners over the following days?

choices.text: They demand the prisoners be conscripted into the army instead
They disperse peacefully once the National Guard arrives
They storm the prisons and kill hundreds of inmates over several days
They petition the Commune to hold speedy public trials for each prisoner

evt-09-02-1792-french-revolution.butterflyEffect: Mobs stormed the prisons and killed hundreds of inmates—priests, aristocrats, and common criminals alike—over roughly five days, an event remembered as the September Massacres. The killings shocked foreign observers, hardened European hostility toward the Revolution, and cast a shadow over leaders like Danton and Marat that fed into the later Terror.

evt-09-02-1870-franco-prussian-war.scenario: It is 1 September 1870, and you are an aide inside the encircled fortress town of Sedan. Emperor Napoleon III, trapped alongside 100,000 French troops by Prussian artillery on the surrounding heights, calls his commanders together to decide the army's fate.
evt-09-02-1870-franco-prussian-war.prompt: What does Napoleon III ultimately choose to do rather than keep fighting?

choices.text: Negotiate a ceasefire while awaiting Austrian reinforcements
Retreat the entire army to defend Paris
Order a breakout toward the fortress at Metz
Surrender himself and his army to Prussian forces

evt-09-02-1870-franco-prussian-war.butterflyEffect: Napoleon III surrendered himself along with his entire army, the single greatest French capitulation of the war. News of the disaster triggered the collapse of the Second Empire within days, the proclamation of the Third Republic in Paris, and set the stage for the Siege of Paris and the founding of a unified German Empire in early 1871.

evt-09-02-1885-rock-springs-wyoming.scenario: It is September 1885 in Rock Springs, Wyoming. White miners, resentful over wages and job competition, have just burned Chinese laborers' homes and driven survivors fleeing into the hills.
evt-09-02-1885-rock-springs-wyoming.prompt: What did the federal government do to protect the Chinese miners in the aftermath?

choices.text: The mining company shut down operations for good
Wyoming Territory permanently banned Chinese residents by law
Troops escorted the Chinese laborers back to the town
The rioters were tried and imprisoned by local courts

evt-09-02-1885-rock-springs-wyoming.butterflyEffect: U.S. Army troops were sent to escort the surviving Chinese laborers back into Rock Springs so mining could resume. Though Washington denied legal liability, Congress later paid China an indemnity, while the massacre fueled the anti-Chinese sentiment that hardened exclusion laws for decades.

evt-09-02-1901-theodore-roosevelt.scenario: It is September 2, 1901, and Vice President Theodore Roosevelt is addressing a crowd at the Minnesota State Fair, days before President McKinley's assassination will thrust him into the presidency.
evt-09-02-1901-theodore-roosevelt.prompt: What foreign policy doctrine did Roosevelt's phrase come to represent?

choices.text: Dollar diplomacy exclusively
"Big Stick" diplomacy
Repeal of the Monroe Doctrine
Strict American isolationism

evt-09-02-1901-theodore-roosevelt.butterflyEffect: The line became shorthand for "Big Stick" diplomacy, backing negotiation with the threat of military force. As president, Roosevelt used it to justify interventions across Latin America and the building of the Panama Canal.

evt-09-02-1912-arthur-rose-eldred.scenario: It is 2 September 1912, and you are a 16-year-old Boy Scout being interviewed by a panel that includes founders Ernest Thompson Seton and Daniel Carter Beard. They are deciding whether you deserve the Boy Scouts of America's brand-new highest rank.
evt-09-02-1912-arthur-rose-eldred.prompt: To earn this new top rank, what must you show the panel?

choices.text: That you have earned the required merit badges and mastered core scouting skills
That you have been nominated by your local mayor
That you have completed a period of military drill training
That your family has paid the necessary membership dues

evt-09-02-1912-arthur-rose-eldred.butterflyEffect: Arthur Rose Eldred passed the interview and became the first Eagle Scout in BSA history. More than two million scouts have since earned the rank, and it remains the organization's most prestigious achievement, later held by astronauts, senators, and business leaders.

evt-09-02-1945-surrender-of-japan.scenario: It is 2 September 1945, and you stand on the deck of the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, watching Japanese officials approach the surrender table before rows of Allied representatives.
evt-09-02-1945-surrender-of-japan.prompt: What happens as the documents are signed on the Missouri's deck?

choices.text: Japan agrees only to a temporary ceasefire pending further talks
Emperor Hirohito personally signs the instrument of surrender
Japan formally and unconditionally surrenders, ending World War II
The Soviet Union refuses to sign, delaying the ceremony

evt-09-02-1945-surrender-of-japan.butterflyEffect: The formal surrender ended six years of world war and began an Allied occupation of Japan led by General Douglas MacArthur. Japan would emerge from occupation with a new pacifist constitution and, within decades, one of the world's largest economies.

evt-09-02-1946-interim-government-of-ind.scenario: It is 2 September 1946, and Jawaharlal Nehru is swearing in India's new interim government, formed from the Constituent Assembly to steer the country toward independence. You watch the ceremony, aware that one major political force is conspicuously boycotting the proceedings.
evt-09-02-1946-interim-government-of-ind.prompt: Which party initially refuses to join Nehru's interim government?

choices.text: The All-India Muslim League
The Indian National Congress
The Communist Party of India
The Hindu Mahasabha

evt-09-02-1946-interim-government-of-ind.butterflyEffect: The All-India Muslim League boycotted the government at first, only joining in October 1946 after pressure from the British Viceroy. Its entry brought bitter friction with Congress ministers inside the cabinet, deepening the mutual distrust that culminated in the partition of British India into India and Pakistan the following August.

evt-09-02-1985-hurricane-elena.scenario: It is Labor Day weekend, 1985, and you run a hotel on Florida's Gulf Coast. Hurricane Elena has already reversed course twice, and forecasters now say it may stall just offshore instead of making landfall as predicted.
evt-09-02-1985-hurricane-elena.prompt: As Elena's track keeps shifting unpredictably, what should coastal residents do?

choices.text: Ignore the evacuation order since Labor Day business matters more
Stay open for tourists since the storm seems to be moving away
Evacuate as ordered, even though the track keeps changing
Wait until the eye is visible before deciding to leave

evt-09-02-1985-hurricane-elena.butterflyEffect: Elena's erratic path forced roughly a million people to evacuate the Florida coast, only for the storm to stall for two days before finally striking Biloxi, Mississippi, as a major hurricane. The episode became a textbook example of forecast uncertainty and pushed the National Hurricane Center toward better tools for tracking storms that stall or loop.

evt-09-02-1998-swissair-flight-111.scenario: It is the night of 2 September 1998. You are in the cockpit of Swissair Flight 111, an MD-11 bound for Geneva, when smoke suddenly appears behind the instrument panel. Halifax is the nearest suitable airport, but you are still carrying a full load of fuel for the transatlantic crossing.
evt-09-02-1998-swissair-flight-111.prompt: With smoke building in the cockpit, what does the crew do before attempting to land?

choices.text: Dump fuel and prepare the cabin for landing per checklist before diverting
Shut down all electrical systems and glide to the nearest beach
Immediately ditch in the ocean without attempting to reach land
Continue on to Geneva since the smoke seems minor

evt-09-02-1998-swissair-flight-111.butterflyEffect: The crew followed procedure and turned to dump fuel and prepare the cabin before landing, but the fire spread faster than expected and the aircraft crashed into the Atlantic before reaching Halifax, killing all 229 aboard. The investigation traced the fire to arcing wires near flammable Mylar insulation, leading to global bans on that material and a rewrite of aircraft wiring and smoke-response standards.

evt-09-02-2008-google.scenario: It is September 2, 2008, and Google has just released a comic book explaining a new web browser built to run JavaScript faster than Internet Explorer or Firefox.
evt-09-02-2008-google.prompt: What happened to this new browser, Chrome, over the following decade?

choices.text: It became the world's most widely used web browser
It remained a niche tool for developers only
It merged with Mozilla Firefox
Google discontinued it within a few years

evt-09-02-2008-google.butterflyEffect: Chrome's speedy V8 JavaScript engine helped it overtake Internet Explorer and Firefox, and by the early 2010s it had become the world's most-used browser. Its dominance let Google steer web standards and accelerate the shift toward browser-based applications.

evt-09-02-2011-chilean-air-force.scenario: It is 2 September 2011, and you are a flight controller tracking a Chilean Air Force CASA 212 carrying officials, aid workers, and a well-known television host toward remote Robinson Crusoe Island. The plane radios in as it begins its final approach through worsening conditions over the Pacific.
evt-09-02-2011-chilean-air-force.prompt: What causes the aircraft to lose contact and go down before reaching the island?

choices.text: The aircraft running out of fuel over open ocean
A mid-air collision with another aircraft
Severe weather during its approach to the island
A mechanical engine failure shortly after takeoff

evt-09-02-2011-chilean-air-force.butterflyEffect: Severe weather caused the CASA 212 to crash into the Pacific near Robinson Crusoe Island, killing all 21 people aboard, including television host Felipe Camiroaga. The disaster prompted a grieving national response and renewed scrutiny of aging military transport aircraft used for island supply runs.

evt-09-02-2013-eastern-span-replacement-.scenario: It's Labor Day weekend 2013, and you're a Caltrans engineer overseeing the switch of San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge traffic from the old eastern span to the newly finished one, set to open at 10:15 p.m. on 2 September.
evt-09-02-2013-eastern-span-replacement-.prompt: What must be done with the old span before the new one can open to traffic?

choices.text: Close the bridge entirely over the holiday weekend to reroute all traffic onto the new span
Open the new span only to commercial trucks first
Delay the opening indefinitely pending further seismic tests
Leave both spans open simultaneously to ease congestion

evt-09-02-2013-eastern-span-replacement-.butterflyEffect: The full weekend closure let crews complete the traffic switchover safely, and the new self-anchored suspension span opened as the widest bridge in the world. It capped an 11-year, $6.5 billion effort to secure the crossing against the kind of collapse the old span suffered in the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake.

evt-09-02-2018-national-museum-of-brazil.scenario: It is the night of September 2, 2018, in Rio de Janeiro, and flames are tearing through the Paço de São Cristóvão, home to 20 million irreplaceable items of Brazil's National Museum.
evt-09-02-2018-national-museum-of-brazil.prompt: Why did the fire destroy so much of the collection so quickly?

choices.text: Chronic underfunding had left it without sprinklers or fire safeguards
An arsonist deliberately targeted the archives
A flood had already weakened the building's structure
An explosive device had been planted inside

evt-09-02-2018-national-museum-of-brazil.butterflyEffect: Years of budget cuts had left the museum without a working sprinkler system or modern fire safety measures, allowing the blaze to consume roughly 92% of the collection. The disaster triggered a national reckoning over underfunded cultural institutions and drew international pledges to help rebuild.

evt-09-02-2019-hurricane-dorian.scenario: It is early September 2019 and you live in the Abaco Islands as Hurricane Dorian, now a Category 5 monster, bears down on the Bahamas with 185 mph winds. Forecasters warn it may stall directly overhead for more than a day.
evt-09-02-2019-hurricane-dorian.prompt: With landfall imminent, what is the safest choice for island residents?

choices.text: Evacuate to a designated shelter or leave the island entirely
Stay home since concrete houses can withstand any storm
Wait at the harbor to sail out once the storm arrives
Ignore the warnings since forecasts are often wrong
