evt-09-02-2019-hurricane-dorian.butterflyEffect: Dorian stalled over the Abacos and Grand Bahama for over 24 hours, flattening most structures and leaving tens of thousands homeless in the worst natural disaster in Bahamian history. The scale of destruction drew a massive international relief effort and renewed global attention to the vulnerability of low-lying island nations to slow-moving, intensified hurricanes.

evt-09-02-2019-sinking-of-mv-conception.scenario: It is just after 3 a.m. on 2 September 2019, and you are one of five crew members berthed on the top deck of the dive boat Conception, anchored off Santa Cruz Island, when you wake to smoke and flames spreading below.
evt-09-02-2019-sinking-of-mv-conception.prompt: What can the surviving crew do as fire blocks the stairwell to the passengers below?

choices.text: Use fire extinguishers to clear a path through the main deck
Wait for Coast Guard rescue before attempting any action
Radio a mayday, then jump overboard when routes below deck prove impassable
Force open the blocked stairwell to reach passengers directly

evt-09-02-2019-sinking-of-mv-conception.butterflyEffect: The crew's mayday call brought a swift Coast Guard response, but the single stairwell exit from the below-deck bunkroom had already been cut off by fire. The disaster led U.S. regulators to require secondary escape routes and continuous roving night watches on overnight passenger vessels.

evt-09-03-bce36-war-between-sextus-pompe.scenario: It is 3 September 36 BC off the coast of Naulochus in Sicily. You serve aboard Agrippa's flagship as his fleet closes on Sextus Pompey's navy, the last force still resisting the Triumvirate.
evt-09-03-bce36-war-between-sextus-pompe.prompt: What tactic does Agrippa's fleet use to break the enemy line?

choices.text: Offer Pompey's captains bribes to defect before battle is joined
Ram every enemy vessel broadside and withdraw before boarding
Wait offshore for land legions to encircle the harbor first
Fire the harpax, a catapult-launched grappling hook, to seize enemy ships for boarding

evt-09-03-bce36-war-between-sextus-pompe.butterflyEffect: Agrippa's harpax, a catapult-fired grappling hook, let marines lash enemy ships and board them in droves, shattering Pompey's fleet. Sextus Pompey fled and was later killed, ending organized opposition to the Triumvirate and clearing Octavian's path toward sole rule of Rome.

evt-09-03-1650-oliver-cromwell.scenario: It is dawn on 3 September 1650. You are Sir David Leslie, commanding the Scottish Covenanter army holding the high ground of Doon Hill above Dunbar, watching Cromwell's exhausted New Model Army seemingly trapped below.
evt-09-03-1650-oliver-cromwell.prompt: Pressed by the Committee of Estates' ministers, what does Leslie do?

choices.text: Retreats north toward Edinburgh to preserve the army
Descends from the ridge to attack the trapped English army
Holds firm on the high ground and waits them out
Opens negotiations for a truce with Cromwell

evt-09-03-1650-oliver-cromwell.butterflyEffect: Leslie moved his army off the high ground to attack, surrendering his advantage. Cromwell struck first at dawn, routing the Scots and capturing thousands — a defeat that broke Covenanter military power and opened the way for Cromwell's conquest of Scotland.

evt-09-03-1651-roundhead.scenario: It is 3 September 1651. You serve in Charles II's Anglo-Scottish royalist army, cornered at Worcester as Cromwell's larger Parliamentarian force crosses the Severn and Teme to attack from multiple sides.
evt-09-03-1651-roundhead.prompt: What happens to the royalist army by day's end?

choices.text: It wins, restoring the monarchy on the spot
A stalemate forces both sides into a truce
It is decisively defeated, and Charles II flees into exile
The Scots mutiny and desert before the fighting starts

evt-09-03-1651-roundhead.butterflyEffect: Worcester was the final battle of the English Civil Wars, ending in a crushing Parliamentarian victory. Charles II fled in disguise, famously hiding in an oak tree before escaping to France, and would not return to reign in England until the Restoration in 1660.

evt-09-03-1935-bonneville-salt-flats.scenario: It is September 3, 1935, on the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah. British racing driver Malcolm Campbell sits behind the wheel of his streamlined car Bluebird, preparing for a record attempt on the vast white salt pan.
evt-09-03-1935-bonneville-salt-flats.prompt: What milestone did Campbell achieve that day?

choices.text: Became the first person to exceed 300 mph on land
Became the first person to exceed 200 mph on land
Completed the first transcontinental car race
Set the first water speed record

evt-09-03-1935-bonneville-salt-flats.butterflyEffect: Campbell's Bluebird reached over 301 mph, making him the first person to break the 300 mph barrier on land. The feat cemented Bonneville's reputation as the premier venue for land speed records, drawing racers back for decades of attempts.

evt-09-03-1981-convention-on-the-elimina.scenario: It is September 3, 1981. Enough countries have ratified a new United Nations treaty on women's rights for it to formally enter into force as international law.
evt-09-03-1981-convention-on-the-elimina.prompt: What did this treaty require of ratifying states?

choices.text: To establish a UN peacekeeping force to protect women in conflict zones
To grant women the right to vote in all UN member states
To eliminate discrimination against women in law and practice, including in political and public life
To mandate equal pay laws enforced directly by the UN

evt-09-03-1981-convention-on-the-elimina.butterflyEffect: Known as CEDAW, the convention became the main international framework for advancing women's legal rights, eventually ratified by 189 states. The United States signed but never ratified it, leaving it as one of the few UN members outside the treaty's obligations.

evt-09-03-1987-jean-baptiste-bagaza.scenario: It is September 1987, and you are President Jean-Baptiste Bagaza, attending a summit abroad, when word reaches you that Major Pierre Buyoya has taken power in Bujumbura in your absence.
evt-09-03-1987-jean-baptiste-bagaza.prompt: What does Bagaza do in the years after losing power?

choices.text: Accept a ceremonial role under Buyoya's new government
Go into exile and later found an opposition political party
Retire permanently from all public and political life
Lead an armed column back into the country to retake the presidency

evt-09-03-1987-jean-baptiste-bagaza.butterflyEffect: Bagaza went into exile rather than trying to force his way back into office by arms. He later returned to Burundi and founded the PARENA political party, remaining active in opposition politics for years afterward.

evt-09-03-1987-1987-burundian-coup-d-eta.scenario: It is 3 September 1987 in Bujumbura. President Bagaza is abroad, and you are among the officers loyal to Major Pierre Buyoya who see this absence as their only chance to act.
evt-09-03-1987-1987-burundian-coup-d-eta.prompt: How do the plotters seize control without bloodshed?

choices.text: Request Belgian paratroopers to intervene on their behalf
Storm the presidential palace with tanks after a public announcement
Occupy the state radio station and government buildings while the president is away
Ambush the presidential motorcade on its return from the airport

evt-09-03-1987-1987-burundian-coup-d-eta.butterflyEffect: Buyoya's officers took the radio station and key government buildings while Bagaza was still travelling, and the takeover passed without a shot fired. Buyoya became president and initially eased Bagaza's tight restrictions, though Burundi's deeper ethnic tensions would erupt into civil war within a few years.

evt-09-03-2001-the-troubles.scenario: It is 3 September 2001, and the picket of Holy Cross Primary School in Ardoyne resumes as the new school term begins, weeks after an uneasy summer lull in the dispute.
evt-09-03-2001-the-troubles.prompt: What happens to the protest over the months that follow?

choices.text: It ends immediately after government intervention
The school closes permanently within days
It escalates into open riot with fatalities that day
It continues for weeks with police escorts before easing by winter

evt-09-03-2001-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The picket continued nightly for months under heavy police escort, becoming a global symbol of the Troubles' lingering grip on Northern Ireland even after the Good Friday Agreement. It gradually subsided by early 2002 following community mediation, but not before serious violence and lasting distrust scarred the neighbourhood.

evt-09-03-2001-belfast.scenario: It is the morning of 3 September 2001, the first day of the new school term, and you are a parent walking your young daughter to Holy Cross Primary School in Ardoyne, Belfast, past loyalist protesters massed along the route shouting abuse.
evt-09-03-2001-belfast.prompt: How do police get the children safely into school?

choices.text: They arrest every protester before the school day begins
They reroute all pupils to a different school building
They form a security cordon and escort the children through the protest
They cancel the start of term until tensions cool

evt-09-03-2001-belfast.butterflyEffect: Police formed a security cordon to escort the children and parents through the jeering crowds. Footage of small girls in school uniform confronting screaming adults was broadcast worldwide, drawing international condemnation and exposing how much sectarian bitterness survived the 1998 peace agreement.

evt-09-03-2004-beslan-school-siege.scenario: It is September 3, 2004, in Beslan, North Ossetia. Explosions have just torn through the school gymnasium where terrorists have held hundreds of hostages for three days, and Russian special forces are rushing in amid the chaos.
evt-09-03-2004-beslan-school-siege.prompt: What major political change did Russia's government pursue in the siege's aftermath?

choices.text: Opened negotiations with separatist leaders for regional autonomy
Granted Chechnya immediate independence
Abolished direct elections of regional governors, centralizing power in Moscow
Disbanded the FSB and created a new security agency

evt-09-03-2004-beslan-school-siege.butterflyEffect: Citing the siege, President Putin ended direct elections for regional governors, replacing them with Kremlin-appointed officials — a major step in the centralization of Russian political power that reshaped governance for over a decade.

evt-09-03-2016-china.scenario: It is September 3, 2016, in Hangzhou, China, ahead of the G20 summit. President Obama and President Xi Jinping stand together to formalize their nations' commitment to a global climate accord.
evt-09-03-2016-china.prompt: What did the two leaders do that day?

choices.text: Formally submitted their nations' instruments of ratification for the Paris Agreement
Pledged to jointly fund a global carbon tax
Announced a joint space exploration program
Signed a new bilateral trade agreement covering clean energy

evt-09-03-2016-china.butterflyEffect: With the world's two largest emitters formally on board, the Paris Agreement crossed the threshold needed for entry into force later that year. The commitment proved fragile, however: in 2017 the incoming Trump administration announced U.S. withdrawal, though the U.S. later rejoined in 2021.

evt-09-03-2017-2017-north-korean-nuclear.scenario: It is 3 September 2017, and seismographs across Northeast Asia register a powerful underground tremor near the Punggye-ri test site in North Korea. State media prepares an announcement.
evt-09-03-2017-2017-north-korean-nuclear.prompt: What does Pyongyang claim it has just successfully tested?

choices.text: A routine conventional artillery exercise
An accidental collapse in a coal mining tunnel
A satellite launch that failed on ascent
A successful thermonuclear weapon test for a long-range missile

evt-09-03-2017-2017-north-korean-nuclear.butterflyEffect: North Korea claimed a thermonuclear warhead capable of fitting an ICBM, its sixth and most powerful nuclear test yet. The blast escalated the 2017–2018 crisis, prompting tighter UN sanctions and fiery rhetoric from Washington, but the tensions eventually gave way to the 2018 Trump–Kim summits.

evt-09-03-2017-north-korea.scenario: It is September 3, 2017. Seismographs across Asia register a tremor near North Korea's Punggye-ri test site, far larger than any previous signal from the location.
evt-09-03-2017-north-korea.prompt: What did North Korea claim this test had achieved?

choices.text: A new submarine-launched cruise missile
A hydrogen bomb capable of being mounted on an intercontinental ballistic missile
A chemical weapons demonstration
A successful satellite launch into orbit

evt-09-03-2017-north-korea.butterflyEffect: The test, North Korea's sixth and most powerful, was estimated at over ten times the yield of earlier tests. It triggered new UN Security Council sanctions and a sharp escalation of rhetoric between Pyongyang and Washington, including warnings of 'fire and fury.'

evt-09-04-476-germanic-peoples.scenario: You are a Roman official in Ravenna on 4 September 476. Odoacer, commander of the Germanic soldiers in Roman service, has seized the city after his troops were denied the land grants they demanded, and now stands over the boy who wears the imperial purple, Romulus Augustus.
evt-09-04-476-germanic-peoples.prompt: What does Odoacer do with the deposed boy-emperor?

choices.text: He allows him to flee to Constantinople
He executes him immediately
He deposes him and pensions him off to a villa
He blinds and imprisons him for life

evt-09-04-476-germanic-peoples.butterflyEffect: Odoacer spared Romulus Augustus, pensioning him off to a villa in Campania, and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople rather than naming a new Western emperor. The event is traditionally dated as the end of the Western Roman Empire, with Odoacer ruling Italy as king while the Eastern Roman Empire endured for another thousand years as Byzantium.

evt-09-04-1666-great-fire-of-london.scenario: It is 4 September 1666, the third day of the Great Fire, and the flames are advancing toward the Tower of London. City officials have hesitated to destroy property, but the fire keeps spreading unchecked.
evt-09-04-1666-great-fire-of-london.prompt: What decisive action finally begins to halt the fire's advance?

choices.text: Evacuate the entire city and abandon firefighting efforts
Dig a canal from the Thames through the city center
Demolish houses with gunpowder to create firebreaks
Wait for rain to extinguish the flames naturally

evt-09-04-1666-great-fire-of-london.butterflyEffect: Authorities, including the Duke of York, ordered gunpowder demolitions to blow up houses and create firebreaks, finally checking the blaze by the next day. The disaster's scale led to the Rebuilding of London Act 1667, mandating brick and stone construction and wider streets to prevent such fires recurring.

evt-09-04-1800-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: You are a French soldier trapped inside Valletta, Malta, in September 1800. A British blockade has strangled the island for two years, and comrades are now dying of starvation and disease at a rate of roughly a hundred a day.
evt-09-04-1800-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What does the French garrison commander ultimately decide?

choices.text: Evacuate the garrison by sea to Sicily
Surrender the garrison to the British blockade
Wait for a relief fleet promised by Napoleon
Break out and fight to the death

evt-09-04-1800-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: The garrison surrendered to the British on 4 September 1800, ending the two-year siege. Britain retained Malta as a strategic naval base for the next century and a half, and the dispute over its status became a key grievance in the collapse of the Peace of Amiens, helping drag Britain and France back into war in 1803.

evt-09-04-1813-andrew-jackson.scenario: It is 4 September 1813 outside the City Hotel in Nashville, Tennessee. You watch as Andrew Jackson, having sided with a friend in a bitter feud, confronts Thomas Hart Benton and his brother Jesse, and the argument turns to drawn pistols.
evt-09-04-1813-andrew-jackson.prompt: What happens to Jackson in the gunfight that follows?

choices.text: He kills Jesse Benton on the spot
He escapes the fight unharmed
He is shot and severely wounded, but survives
He is killed in the exchange

evt-09-04-1813-andrew-jackson.butterflyEffect: Jesse Benton shot Jackson, shattering his shoulder; Jackson carried the bullet for years afterward and nearly lost his arm. Despite the brawl, Jackson and Thomas Hart Benton later reconciled, and Benton became one of Jackson's most powerful allies in the Senate during his presidency.

evt-09-04-1839-first-opium-war.scenario: It is September 1839 off Kowloon, and you command a British warship whose crew has been cut off from food and fresh water after Commissioner Lin Zexu banned local merchants from supplying British ships. A line of armed Chinese war junks now blocks your boats from the shore.
evt-09-04-1839-first-opium-war.prompt: How do you respond to the junks blocking your ships' food supply?

choices.text: Open fire on the junks to force them aside
Offer to pay the Chinese officials for safe passage
Sail back to Macau and wait for orders from London
Abandon the ships and march the crew overland

evt-09-04-1839-first-opium-war.butterflyEffect: British ships opened fire on the Chinese junks in what became known as the Battle of Kowloon, one of the first armed clashes of the conflict. The skirmish helped push both sides toward full-scale war in 1840, which ended with the Treaty of Nanking and the cession of Hong Kong to Britain.

evt-09-04-1843-teresa-cristina-of-the-tw.scenario: It's September 4, 1843, in Naples. You stand in as proxy for Emperor Pedro II of Brazil at his wedding to Princess Teresa Cristina of the Two Sicilies, a bride he has never met.
evt-09-04-1843-teresa-cristina-of-the-tw.prompt: What happens when the real couple finally meets in Brazil?

choices.text: The court hides the couple from each other for years
Teresa Cristina returns to Italy in protest of the mismatch
Pedro is initially disappointed but the marriage grows into a lasting, respected partnership
Pedro refuses to complete the marriage and it is annulled

evt-09-04-1843-teresa-cristina-of-the-tw.butterflyEffect: Pedro was reportedly disappointed at first sight of his new bride, but the marriage endured for decades. Teresa Cristina became a respected patron of the arts and sciences, earning the nickname "Mother of the Brazilians," and remained empress until the monarchy's fall in 1889.

evt-09-04-1886-united-states-army.scenario: It's September 4, 1886, in Skeleton Canyon, Arizona. You lead the last band of free Chiricahua Apache still resisting the U.S. Army after decades of war, and General Nelson Miles has offered terms.
evt-09-04-1886-united-states-army.prompt: What do you decide, facing overwhelming pursuit and dwindling numbers?

choices.text: Cross into Mexico to seek permanent asylum
Negotiate a reservation homeland in Arizona as a condition of peace
Continue fighting from the Sierra Madre mountains indefinitely
Surrender to General Miles and accept exile as prisoners of war

evt-09-04-1886-united-states-army.butterflyEffect: Geronimo surrendered, ending the last major armed Native American resistance against U.S. expansion in the Southwest. He and his followers were exiled as prisoners of war to Florida and later Oklahoma, and Geronimo himself became a national curiosity, later touring fairs and even riding in a presidential parade before his death in 1909.

evt-09-04-1912-albanian-revolt-of-1912.scenario: It is the summer of 1912 and you lead Albanian rebels who have spent months fighting Ottoman forces. Istanbul, weakened and eager to end the uprising before it spreads, now offers to negotiate.
evt-09-04-1912-albanian-revolt-of-1912.prompt: What do you demand in the settlement talks?

choices.text: Union of Albanian lands with the Kingdom of Serbia
Immediate full independence from the Ottoman Empire
An autonomous Albanian vilayet with local schools, administration, and conscription
Continued armed struggle with no negotiation

evt-09-04-1912-albanian-revolt-of-1912.butterflyEffect: On 4 September 1912 the Ottoman government agreed to nearly all rebel demands, granting an autonomous Albanian vilayet with Albanian-language schools, local administration, and regional conscription. The concession boosted Albanian national confidence, and within months, amid the outbreak of the First Balkan War, Albania declared full independence in November 1912.

evt-09-04-1934-evelyn-waugh.scenario: You are Tony Last, the ruined English gentleman of Evelyn Waugh's novel, deep in the Brazilian jungle and nursed back to health by the reclusive settler Mr. Todd, who demands you read Dickens aloud to him each evening.
evt-09-04-1934-evelyn-waugh.prompt: What ultimately becomes of Tony Last at the novel's end?

choices.text: He escapes alone through the jungle to civilization
A search party rescues him within weeks
He dies of fever shortly after arriving
He is forced to remain, reading Dickens aloud to Mr. Todd indefinitely

evt-09-04-1934-evelyn-waugh.butterflyEffect: Waugh's savage conclusion traps Tony forever, condemned to read Dickens aloud to Mr. Todd with no hope of rescue, a fate crueler than death. The bleakly ironic ending cemented Waugh's reputation for dark satire beneath comic prose and remains one of the most discussed closings in modern British fiction.

evt-09-04-1955-yumiko-chan-incident.scenario: It is September 1955 in Kadena, Okinawa, under U.S. military occupation. News spreads through the community that a young local girl has been murdered near the air base by an American serviceman, and grief turns to anger in the streets.
evt-09-04-1955-yumiko-chan-incident.prompt: What did this case ultimately spark among Okinawans?

choices.text: An immediate U.S. withdrawal from Okinawa
No public reaction due to strict censorship
A formal treaty ending the occupation that year
The first major organized protests against the U.S. military presence

evt-09-04-1955-yumiko-chan-incident.butterflyEffect: The case galvanized long-simmering anger over crimes by U.S. servicemen and the seizure of land for military bases, sparking the first major organized Okinawan protests against the occupation. That movement for local rights and reduced U.S. military presence continued to shape Okinawan politics and the U.S.-Japan security relationship for decades afterward.

evt-09-04-1957-orval-faubus.scenario: It is 4 September 1957 in Little Rock, Arkansas. Nine Black students arrive to enroll at Central High School under a federal desegregation order, but Governor Orval Faubus has already acted to stop them.
evt-09-04-1957-orval-faubus.prompt: What does Governor Faubus do to block the students' entry?

choices.text: Orders local police to arrest the students
Deploys the Arkansas National Guard to block their entry
Calls a special legislative session to repeal desegregation
Closes the school entirely for the year

evt-09-04-1957-orval-faubus.butterflyEffect: Faubus deployed the Arkansas National Guard to physically bar the Little Rock Nine from the school. The standoff forced President Eisenhower to federalize the Guard and send the 101st Airborne Division to escort the students inside, making Little Rock one of the first major federal enforcements of school desegregation and a defining moment of the Civil Rights Movement.

evt-09-04-1972-mark-spitz.scenario: It's September 4, 1972, in Munich. You are Mark Spitz, standing behind the blocks for your seventh individual event of these Olympics, already holding six gold medals and six world records.
evt-09-04-1972-mark-spitz.prompt: What happens in this final race?

choices.text: He wins gold and sets a seventh world record
He withdraws due to injury before the race
He settles for silver after a slow start
He ties for gold but misses the world record

evt-09-04-1972-mark-spitz.butterflyEffect: Spitz won his seventh gold medal in world-record time, an unmatched feat that stood for 36 years until Michael Phelps won eight golds at the 2008 Beijing Games, also setting seven world records along the way.

evt-09-04-1972-the-price-is-right.scenario: It's 1972, and you're a CBS producer relaunching a canceled 1950s game show format. You need a way to bring contestants out of the studio audience with maximum energy for the cameras.
evt-09-04-1972-the-price-is-right.prompt: What device do you adopt to summon contestants to the stage?

choices.text: Have the announcer shout "Come on down!" to call contestants forward
Have host walk into the audience with a microphone to interview everyone first
Draw names from a hat before each taping
Pre-select contestants and seat them onstage before filming begins

evt-09-04-1972-the-price-is-right.butterflyEffect: The announcer's call of "Come on down!" became the show's signature, and the format proved so durable that The Price Is Right is still airing today, making it American television's longest-running game show.

evt-09-04-1977-golden-dragon-massacre.scenario: It is the early hours of 4 September 1977 in San Francisco's Chinatown. Gunmen from the Joe Boys gang have just opened fire inside the Golden Dragon restaurant, and you are a police captain facing a city demanding answers.
evt-09-04-1977-golden-dragon-massacre.prompt: What lasting step does the police department take after the massacre?

choices.text: Create a dedicated Asian Gang Task Force to target gang violence
Impose a nightly curfew across all of Chinatown
Shut down every restaurant on Washington Street indefinitely
Deploy the National Guard to patrol the neighborhood

evt-09-04-1977-golden-dragon-massacre.butterflyEffect: None of the five people killed were gang members, and public outrage pushed the SFPD to create a dedicated Asian Gang Task Force. That unit is credited with helping end the wave of Chinatown gang violence by 1983.

evt-09-04-1985-buckminsterfullerene.scenario: It is September 1985 in a Rice University lab. After vaporizing graphite with a laser in a stream of helium, your mass spectrometer shows one peak towering above all others, corresponding to a cluster of exactly sixty carbon atoms.
evt-09-04-1985-buckminsterfullerene.prompt: How do you explain this oddly dominant, stable 60-atom cluster?

choices.text: Propose a closed, cage-like spherical structure
Conclude it is a tiny diamond fragment
Assume it is a simple straight carbon chain
Dismiss the peak as instrument contamination

evt-09-04-1985-buckminsterfullerene.butterflyEffect: Kroto, Curl, and Smalley proposed that the sixty carbons formed a hollow, soccer-ball-shaped cage, later named buckminsterfullerene after the geodesic domes of Buckminster Fuller. The discovery revealed an entirely new form of carbon, earned the trio the 1996 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, and opened the door to nanotechnology fields including carbon nanotubes.

evt-09-04-1989-leipzig.scenario: It is Monday, 4 September 1989, outside St. Nicholas Church in Leipzig, East Germany. After the weekly peace prayer, you and a small crowd step outside holding hand-lettered banners as Western TV cameras, in town for the trade fair, happen to be rolling.
evt-09-04-1989-leipzig.prompt: What do the demonstrators' banners demand that day?

choices.text: Legal recognition of independent opposition parties
Immediate reunification with West Germany
Freedom to travel abroad, rather than being forced to flee illegally
Release of all political prisoners

evt-09-04-1989-leipzig.butterflyEffect: The banners read 'Freedom to travel instead of mass exodus,' demanding legal emigration rather than the illegal flight through Hungary many East Germans were attempting. This small protest became the first of the Leipzig Monday Demonstrations, which swelled to hundreds of thousands by October and helped topple the East German regime, leading directly to the fall of the Berlin Wall that November.

evt-09-04-1995-camp-hansen.scenario: It's September 1995 on Okinawa. News breaks that three U.S. servicemen from Camp Hansen have abducted and assaulted a local schoolgirl, and outrage is spreading fast across the island.
evt-09-04-1995-camp-hansen.prompt: What does the resulting public and political backlash demand?

choices.text: Immediate and complete withdrawal of all U.S. forces from Japan
No official response, treated as an isolated incident
Renegotiation of the U.S.-Japan Status of Forces Agreement and reduced base footprint
Increased joint U.S.-Japan military exercises on Okinawa

evt-09-04-1995-camp-hansen.butterflyEffect: The case triggered mass protests on Okinawa, with tens of thousands demonstrating against the U.S. military presence. It led directly to the 1996 SACO agreement between Washington and Tokyo, which promised to reduce American bases and relocate Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, a promise still only partly fulfilled decades later.

evt-09-04-1998-google.scenario: It is August 1998 and you and your Stanford labmate have built a search engine outgrowing the university's servers. Sun co-founder Andy Bechtolsheim hands you a $100,000 check made out to 'Google Inc.'—a company that legally does not yet exist.
evt-09-04-1998-google.prompt: What do you do with the check?

choices.text: Rush to incorporate the company so the check can be deposited
Ask Bechtolsheim for stock options instead of cash
Cash it under their personal names
Decline the check since the company doesn't exist

evt-09-04-1998-google.butterflyEffect: Page and Brin scrambled to incorporate Google Inc. within two weeks so they could open a bank account and cash the check. That seed money let them set up shop in a Menlo Park garage, launching the company that would grow into Alphabet, one of the world's most valuable corporations.

evt-09-04-2001-tokyo-disneysea.scenario: It is 4 September 2001 in Urayasu, Chiba Prefecture. You are among the first guests passing through the gates of a brand-new park built beside Tokyo Disneyland, one themed entirely around the sea.
evt-09-04-2001-tokyo-disneysea.prompt: What draws crowds to this new park in its opening years?

choices.text: Nautical-themed lands and attractions unlike anything at Tokyo Disneyland
A collection of rides transplanted directly from Disneyland Paris
An exclusive focus on Star Wars attractions
Free admission for the park's first full year of operation

evt-09-04-2001-tokyo-disneysea.butterflyEffect: Built at a cost of 335 billion yen by the Oriental Land Company under license from Disney, Tokyo DisneySea grew into one of the most visited theme parks on Earth. By 2024 it drew 12.4 million visitors a year, ranking among the world's top parks.

evt-09-04-2002-oakland-athletics.scenario: It is the bottom of the ninth inning at the Oakland Coliseum on September 4, 2002. Your Athletics blew an 11-run lead and now trail the Kansas City Royals, with a shot at an American League-record 20th straight win slipping away. You need a hitter off the bench.
evt-09-04-2002-oakland-athletics.prompt: Who do you send up as the pinch hitter with the game on the line?

choices.text: Terrence Long
Scott Hatteberg
Ramon Hernandez
Jeremy Giambi

evt-09-04-2002-oakland-athletics.butterflyEffect: Manager Art Howe sent up Scott Hatteberg, who hit a walk-off home run to complete the comeback and give Oakland its 20th consecutive win, an AL record. The game became the climactic scene of the book and film "Moneyball," cementing the streak as the public face of sabermetric roster-building, even though Oakland lost the next night to end the run.

evt-09-04-2007-al-qaeda.scenario: It is early September 2007 and German intelligence has tracked a Sauerland cell to a rented cottage stockpiled with drums of concentrated hydrogen peroxide, enough to build massive car bombs aimed at American targets.
evt-09-04-2007-al-qaeda.prompt: What should the security services do before the devices are finished?

choices.text: Raid the site immediately to seize materials and make arrests
Wait months longer to gather more surveillance evidence
Arrest them only after an attack is attempted
Let the cell travel abroad before intervening

evt-09-04-2007-al-qaeda.butterflyEffect: On 4 September 2007, German police raided the cottage and arrested three men, seizing bomb-making chemicals before the plot against US facilities like Ramstein Air Base could be carried out. The 'Sauerland cell' trial exposed links to the Islamic Jihad Union and led to convictions in 2010, reshaping German counter-terrorism cooperation with the CIA and NSA.

evt-09-04-2024-2024-apalachee-high-schoo.scenario: In the days after the shooting at Apalachee High School near Winder, Georgia, Barrow County prosecutors weigh how far responsibility for the tragedy extends beyond the 14-year-old shooter himself.
evt-09-04-2024-2024-apalachee-high-schoo.prompt: What unusual step do prosecutors take regarding the shooter's father?

choices.text: Charge the school principal with negligence
Decline to pursue any charges beyond the shooter
Charge the father for providing his son access to the firearm
Charge classmates who reported prior warning signs

evt-09-04-2024-2024-apalachee-high-schoo.butterflyEffect: Colin Gray was charged with second-degree murder, involuntary manslaughter, and cruelty to children for giving his son access to the weapon used in the attack. The case became a closely watched test of parental criminal liability in school shootings, intensifying national debate over safe gun storage laws.

evt-09-05-1774-parliament-of-the-united-.scenario: It is September 5, 1774, in Philadelphia. You are a delegate representing your colony at a gathering convened after Parliament passed the so-called Intolerable Acts punishing Massachusetts for the Boston Tea Party.
evt-09-05-1774-parliament-of-the-united-.prompt: What should this new colonial congress do about the Intolerable Acts?

choices.text: Immediately declare independence from Britain
Petition only for lower tea taxes and disband
Raise a joint colonial army to march on Boston
Coordinate a unified colonial response, including a boycott of British goods

evt-09-05-1774-parliament-of-the-united-.butterflyEffect: The delegates, meeting as the First Continental Congress, went on to organize a colony-wide boycott of British goods and issue a statement of grievances to the Crown. The gathering set the precedent for coordinated colonial resistance that led to the Second Continental Congress and, within two years, the Declaration of Independence.

evt-09-05-1781-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 5 September 1781. You command the French fleet under Admiral de Grasse, anchored in Chesapeake Bay to support Washington's siege at Yorktown, when a British fleet under Admiral Graves appears offshore.
evt-09-05-1781-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What should the French fleet do as the British ships approach?

choices.text: Retreat north to New York to avoid battle
Sail out and engage the British fleet in open water
Wait offshore for reinforcements from the West Indies before acting
Unload all troops immediately and hide the fleet in the bay

evt-09-05-1781-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: De Grasse sailed out and fought the Battle of the Chesapeake, driving off the British fleet and sealing the bay. Unable to resupply or evacuate Cornwallis by sea, the British garrison at Yorktown was forced to surrender weeks later, effectively ending major fighting in the war.

evt-09-05-1887-exeter-theatre-royal-fire.scenario: On the night of 5 September 1887, fire tears through the backstage area of the Theatre Royal, Exeter, during a performance of The Romany Rye, trapping hundreds inside with too few ways out.
evt-09-05-1887-exeter-theatre-royal-fire.prompt: What sweeping change to British theatre design followed this disaster?

choices.text: Mandatory fireproof safety curtains and additional marked exits
Compulsory sprinkler systems installed in every auditorium
A nationwide ban on gas lighting in all theatres
A strict fifty-person limit on theatre audiences

evt-09-05-1887-exeter-theatre-royal-fire.butterflyEffect: The Exeter fire killed 186 people and exposed how few escape routes and how little fireproofing British theatres had. It forced new safety standards requiring fireproof safety curtains between stage and auditorium and additional, clearly marked exits, reshaping theatre construction across the country for generations.

evt-09-05-1905-theodore-roosevelt.scenario: It is September 1905 in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. You sit at the negotiating table as a Japanese delegate, facing exhausted Russian counterparts under the mediation of President Theodore Roosevelt, trying to end the costly Russo-Japanese War.
evt-09-05-1905-theodore-roosevelt.prompt: What compromise finally brings the negotiators to a signed treaty?

choices.text: Russia agrees to pay the full indemnity Japan originally demanded
Japan drops its indemnity demand and receives southern Sakhalin instead
Japan annexes all of Sakhalin and Russian Manchuria outright
Talks collapse and the war continues without a treaty

evt-09-05-1905-theodore-roosevelt.butterflyEffect: Japan dropped its demand for a war indemnity in exchange for southern Sakhalin, and the Treaty of Portsmouth ended the war. Roosevelt won the Nobel Peace Prize for the mediation, but Japanese public fury at receiving no indemnity triggered the Hibiya riots at home and left lingering resentment toward the United States.

evt-09-05-1915-zimmerwald-conference.scenario: You are a socialist delegate meeting in secret at Zimmerwald, Switzerland, in September 1915, drawn from nations already at war with one another. Lenin's faction demands revolutionary defeatism while others push for a milder statement against the slaughter.
evt-09-05-1915-zimmerwald-conference.prompt: What position does the conference's final manifesto actually adopt?

choices.text: A resolution pledging full socialist support for the Allied war effort
No manifesto at all, ending the conference in stalemate
Lenin's call to turn the imperialist war into a revolutionary civil war
A moderate manifesto condemning the war and demanding peace without annexations

evt-09-05-1915-zimmerwald-conference.butterflyEffect: The majority backed a moderate manifesto condemning the war and calling for peace without annexations, sidelining Lenin's call to turn the war into revolution. But the resulting 'Zimmerwald Left' faction endured, giving Lenin an organized international base that fed directly into the founding of the Communist Third International after 1917.

evt-09-05-1915-casablanca-fair-of-1915.scenario: You are a French colonial official touring the new Casablanca Fair in September 1915, sent to assess Moroccan craft goods on display and report back on the state of the protectorate's traditional industries.
evt-09-05-1915-casablanca-fair-of-1915.prompt: What action follows once officials judge the craft industry to be in decline?

choices.text: Training centres are set up to support and revive Moroccan craftsmanship
Steep tariffs are imposed on all locally made craft goods
Moroccan craftsmen are relocated to workshops in France
Traditional Moroccan crafts are banned in favor of French imports

evt-09-05-1915-casablanca-fair-of-1915.butterflyEffect: The fair's assessment of Moroccan craftsmanship led the protectorate to establish training centres for Moroccan artisans, part of a wider French policy of cultivating and controlling indigenous arts under Resident-General Lyautey. This shaped Morocco's applied-arts education and craft economy for decades to come.

evt-09-05-1926-dromcolliher.scenario: It is 5 September 1926 in the small Limerick village of Dromcolliher. A travelling picture show has set up in an upstairs room above a shop, packed shoulder to shoulder to watch a nitrate film reel by lamplight.
evt-09-05-1926-dromcolliher.prompt: What fatal design flaw turned this makeshift cinema into a death trap once fire broke out?

choices.text: The room had only one narrow stairwell serving as the sole exit
The local fire brigade was away at a training exercise
The projectionist ran outside instead of raising the alarm
The building lacked any fire extinguishers on site

evt-09-05-1926-dromcolliher.butterflyEffect: The Drumcollogher fire, sparked by highly flammable nitrate film in an unlicensed upstairs venue with a single narrow stairway, killed 48 people trapped inside. The tragedy exposed the dangers of showing film in unregulated premises and hastened stricter Irish licensing rules requiring proper exits and fireproof projection arrangements before nitrate film could be screened to the public.

evt-09-05-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 5 September 1943 over the Markham Valley in New Guinea. You are a paratrooper of the 503rd Parachute Infantry Regiment about to jump onto Nadzab, tasked with seizing the airstrip ahead of an Australian advance on Lae.
evt-09-05-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What should you and your fellow paratroopers do immediately after landing?

choices.text: Dig in and wait for a naval bombardment to clear the area
Charge directly toward Lae without regrouping
Retreat toward Port Moresby to regroup with the main force
Secure the airfield perimeter and prepare it for incoming reinforcements

evt-09-05-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The paratroopers secured Nadzab's airfield with minimal resistance, allowing Australian 7th Division troops to be flown in rapidly. This combined air-land operation helped force the fall of Lae days later, marking one of the first major Allied airborne operations in the Pacific theatre.

evt-09-05-1964-hurricane-cleo.scenario: It is early September 1964. Hurricane Cleo has already torn through Haiti with catastrophic flooding, and now its path is bending toward South Florida. You are a Miami-area resident watching the forecast.
evt-09-05-1964-hurricane-cleo.prompt: What should you do as Cleo's projected path nears your coastline?

choices.text: Drive toward the coast to watch the storm come in
Heed official warnings and evacuate to an inland shelter
Ignore the warnings since the storm looks weak on the radio
Leave your home unlocked and open all the windows

evt-09-05-1964-hurricane-cleo.butterflyEffect: Cleo struck the Miami area as a hurricane before curving up the Southeast coast, causing heavy damage but comparatively few deaths thanks to warnings and sturdier construction. In Haiti, where such warning systems and infrastructure were far weaker, the storm's flooding and mudslides caused the overwhelming majority of its roughly 156 deaths.

evt-09-05-1970-1970-italian-grand-prix.scenario: It is practice for the 1970 Italian Grand Prix at Monza. You are Jochen Rindt, strapping into your Lotus 72 before a run through the fast Parabolica corner, and you reach for the crotch strap of your safety harness.
evt-09-05-1970-1970-italian-grand-prix.prompt: What should you do with the harness before your run?

choices.text: Wear only the shoulder straps and skip the lap belt
Fasten the full harness, including the crotch strap
Skip the seatbelt entirely for this practice run
Leave the crotch strap loose for a quicker exit in case of fire

evt-09-05-1970-1970-italian-grand-prix.butterflyEffect: Rindt left the crotch strap unfastened, fearing it would slow an escape from a fire. His car crashed into the barriers at the Parabolica and he slid beneath his seatbelt, dying from his injuries. He remains Formula One's only posthumous World Champion, and his death accelerated the push for mandatory full harnesses.

evt-09-05-1975-squeaky-fromme.scenario: It is 5 September 1975 outside the California State Capitol in Sacramento. You are a Secret Service agent walking beside President Gerald Ford when you see a woman in a red robe raise a pistol toward him.
evt-09-05-1975-squeaky-fromme.prompt: What should you do in the instant you spot the weapon?

choices.text: Draw your own weapon and open fire on her
Assume the gun is unloaded and do nothing
Immediately grab the weapon before she can fire
Shout a warning and duck for cover

evt-09-05-1975-squeaky-fromme.butterflyEffect: Agent Larry Buendorf lunged and grabbed the pistol before it could be fired; it turned out no round was chambered. Lynette "Squeaky" Fromme was convicted of attempted assassination and sentenced to life in prison, and the scare prompted tighter Secret Service scrutiny just weeks before a second attempt on Ford's life in the same city.

evt-09-05-1977-voyager-1.scenario: You are a NASA mission planner in 1977 charting Voyager 1's route through the outer Solar System. You can only choose one close flyby target beyond Jupiter and Saturn, since the spacecraft's trajectory can't reach both.
evt-09-05-1977-voyager-1.prompt: Which body do you prioritize for the close flyby: Titan or Pluto?

choices.text: Pluto, to reach it before any other mission
Uranus, for a longer gravity-assist path
Titan, for its thick atmosphere
Neither, to save fuel for a return trip

evt-09-05-1977-voyager-1.butterflyEffect: NASA chose to send Voyager 1 past Saturn's moon Titan because it was known to have a substantial atmosphere worth studying closely. That choice ruled out a Pluto flyby for both Voyager probes, leaving Pluto unvisited by spacecraft until New Horizons arrived in 2015, decades after Voyager 1 became the first craft to reach interstellar space in 2012.

evt-09-05-1996-hurricane-fran.scenario: It is early September 1996, and you are an emergency management official in coastal North Carolina as Hurricane Fran strengthens into a 120 mph Category 3 storm bearing down on Cape Fear.
evt-09-05-1996-hurricane-fran.prompt: What do you order for coastal residents as the hurricane approaches?

choices.text: Leave evacuation decisions entirely to individual residents
Wait until landfall to decide on evacuations
Evacuate only offshore barrier islands, not the mainland
Order mandatory evacuation of coastal areas

evt-09-05-1996-hurricane-fran.butterflyEffect: Officials ordered mandatory evacuations of coastal North Carolina before Fran made landfall near Cape Fear on September 5, 1996. The storm caused roughly $5 billion in damage and severe inland flooding as far as Raleigh, but the evacuations are credited with keeping the death toll far lower than the destruction would otherwise have caused.

evt-09-05-2005-mandala-airlines-flight-0.scenario: You are the co-pilot of Mandala Airlines Flight 091, running through the final checklist before departure from Medan on the morning of September 5, 2005, with a full passenger load bound for Jakarta.
evt-09-05-2005-mandala-airlines-flight-0.prompt: What configuration must be verified before the takeoff roll begins?

choices.text: Flaps and slats extended for takeoff
Autopilot engaged before brake release
Overhead bins double-checked by cabin crew
Cabin lighting dimmed for taxi

evt-09-05-2005-mandala-airlines-flight-0.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the Boeing 737 took off without its flaps and slats properly extended, causing it to stall and crash into a residential area seconds after liftoff, killing 149 people including bystanders on the ground. The disaster intensified international scrutiny of Indonesian carrier safety, contributing to the European Union's 2007 ban on Indonesian airlines from its airspace.

evt-09-06-1492-christopher-columbus.scenario: It is 6 September 1492. You are a sailor aboard the Santa María as it clears the Canary Islands, the last known land, and turns west into open Atlantic water no European ship has charted before.
evt-09-06-1492-christopher-columbus.prompt: How does Columbus try to keep the anxious crew calm as the days pass with no land?

choices.text: He promises to divide his own share of gold among the crew immediately
He keeps a falsified log understating the distance already sailed
He turns the fleet back toward the Canaries after a week
He orders the ships to sail only by night to avoid panic

evt-09-06-1492-christopher-columbus.butterflyEffect: Columbus reportedly kept two logs, understating the true distance sailed in the one shown to the crew so the voyage would seem shorter than it was. Land was sighted on 12 October 1492, beginning sustained European contact with the Americas.

evt-09-06-1566-suleiman-the-magnificent.scenario: It is the siege of Szigetvár, September 1566. Sultan Suleiman has just died quietly in his tent, but the army outside does not know it and the campaign is not yet won. As Grand Vizier Sokollu Mehmed Pasha, you must decide what to tell the troops.
evt-09-06-1566-suleiman-the-magnificent.prompt: What does the Grand Vizier do about the sultan's death?

choices.text: Proclaim a new sultan on the battlefield at once
Announce the death immediately and withdraw the army
Conceal the death and continue issuing orders in the sultan's name
Open peace talks with the Habsburgs before news spreads

evt-09-06-1566-suleiman-the-magnificent.butterflyEffect: Sokollu Mehmed Pasha concealed Suleiman's death for weeks, issuing orders in the dead sultan's name until the fortress fell and Prince Selim II could be safely enthroned. The secrecy averted a succession crisis but also masked the empire's fading momentum, as Selim's reign began the slow end of Ottoman territorial expansion.

evt-09-06-1863-john-s-marmaduke.scenario: It's September 6, 1863, near Little Rock, Arkansas. You are Confederate General John S. Marmaduke, having publicly accused fellow general Lucius M. Walker of cowardice during a recent retreat, and the dispute has been settled the only way officers of honor know: a duel at fifteen paces.
evt-09-06-1863-john-s-marmaduke.prompt: What happens when the two generals face off with pistols?

choices.text: Marmaduke is wounded and forced to resign his command
They exchange fire, Marmaduke unhurt, Walker mortally wounded
Both men miss their shots and reconcile on the spot
Walker backs down and apologizes publicly before shots are fired

evt-09-06-1863-john-s-marmaduke.butterflyEffect: Walker was mortally wounded in the exchange and died the following day, while Marmaduke was briefly arrested before being released to resume command. The affair exposed the bitter personal rivalries plaguing Confederate leadership in the Trans-Mississippi theater at a moment the army could least afford disunity.

evt-09-06-1901-william-mckinley.scenario: It's September 6, 1901, at the Temple of Music inside Buffalo's Pan-American Exposition. You are a guard watching the long line of well-wishers waiting to shake President McKinley's hand, and you notice a man near the front with a handkerchief wrapped around his right hand.
evt-09-06-1901-william-mckinley.prompt: What happens when the man reaches the front of the line?

choices.text: He is stopped by guards before reaching McKinley
He tries to hand McKinley a written petition instead
He fires two shots concealed by the handkerchief, wounding McKinley fatally
He shakes hands and passes without incident

evt-09-06-1901-william-mckinley.butterflyEffect: Leon Czolgosz fired two concealed shots into McKinley, who died eight days later. Vice President Theodore Roosevelt succeeded him, launching an era of trust-busting and conservation, and Congress soon assigned the Secret Service permanent responsibility for presidential protection.

evt-09-06-1916-grocery-store.scenario: You walk into Clarence Saunders' new store in Memphis on September 6, 1916, expecting a clerk to fetch your groceries from behind a counter as usual. Instead you pass through a turnstile into a maze of aisles stocked with priced, packaged goods and a stack of baskets by the door.
evt-09-06-1916-grocery-store.prompt: What is different about how you shop here compared to a traditional grocery?

choices.text: You bargain with the shopkeeper over the price of each item
You order from a delivery boy who brings goods to your home
You serve yourself, choosing and carrying your own items through aisles before paying at checkout
You must join a membership club before buying from bulk bins

evt-09-06-1916-grocery-store.butterflyEffect: Saunders' Piggly Wiggly patented the self-service model, letting customers pick their own goods and pay at a single checkout. The idea spread rapidly across America, cutting labor costs and giving rise to the modern supermarket and the packaged-goods branding industry.

evt-09-06-1930-hipolito-yrigoyen.scenario: It's September 6, 1930, and you march with General José Félix Uriburu's troops on the Casa Rosada in Buenos Aires, aiming to force elderly President Hipólito Yrigoyen from power amid economic crisis and political paralysis.
evt-09-06-1930-hipolito-yrigoyen.prompt: What is the outcome of this uprising against Yrigoyen?

choices.text: Congress impeaches Yrigoyen before Uriburu's troops arrive
The coup succeeds and Yrigoyen is forced to resign, ending civilian government
Yrigoyen negotiates a peaceful transition and stays on as a ceremonial president
Yrigoyen crushes the uprising with loyal troops

evt-09-06-1930-hipolito-yrigoyen.butterflyEffect: The coup succeeded, and Yrigoyen was forced to resign, ending civilian rule under the Sáenz Peña Law he had championed. It was Argentina's first military coup of the twentieth century and opened decades of recurring military intervention in national politics.

evt-09-06-1963-presidency-of-john-f-kenn.scenario: It's early September 1963. President Kennedy has sent you, along with a State Department colleague, on a fact-finding mission to South Vietnam to judge whether Diem's crackdown on Buddhist protesters is crippling the war against the Viet Cong.
evt-09-06-1963-presidency-of-john-f-kenn.prompt: What do the two envoys report back to the president?

choices.text: Both agree the war effort is unaffected and Diem should be firmly supported
Both refuse to give any assessment, citing lack of evidence
Krulak reports the war is being won while Mendenhall reports political collapse, producing sharply contradictory conclusions
Both agree the government is collapsing and Diem must go immediately

evt-09-06-1963-presidency-of-john-f-kenn.butterflyEffect: General Krulak reported the war was being won militarily while diplomat Mendenhall warned the political crisis had shattered public morale, leaving Kennedy to famously ask if they had visited the same country. The clash of assessments deepened Washington's confusion over Diem, feeding into tacit U.S. support for the coup that overthrew him weeks later.

evt-09-06-1970-black-september.scenario: It is mid-September 1970 in Amman. PFLP hijackers have just seized four airliners, and PLO fighters now control whole districts of your capital. As King Hussein, you must decide how to answer the challenge to your throne.
evt-09-06-1970-black-september.prompt: What does King Hussein do to reassert control over Jordan?

choices.text: Order the Jordanian army to crush the PLO strongholds by force
Appeal to the Arab League to mediate a ceasefire and do nothing more
Abdicate in favor of a government led jointly with Arafat
Grant the PLO formal autonomy over Palestinian refugee areas

evt-09-06-1970-black-september.butterflyEffect: Hussein ordered the army to crush the PLO militarily; thousands died and the PLO leadership was expelled to Lebanon by 1971. The exiled fighters helped destabilize Lebanon, and a splinter faction calling itself "Black September" later carried out the 1972 Munich Olympics massacre.

evt-09-06-1976-viktor-belenko.scenario: You are an air traffic controller at Hakodate Airport, Japan, on September 6, 1976, when a Soviet MiG-25 fighter suddenly appears, low on fuel, and overshoots the runway on landing, nearly colliding with airport equipment.
evt-09-06-1976-viktor-belenko.prompt: What does the Soviet pilot do after climbing out of the cockpit?

choices.text: He waits calmly inside the cockpit for a Soviet recovery team
He immediately requests to be flown back to the Soviet Union
He destroys the plane's cockpit instruments before surrendering
He fires warning shots to keep bystanders away and demands asylum in the United States

evt-09-06-1976-viktor-belenko.butterflyEffect: Viktor Belenko fired warning shots to keep curious civilians away, then formally requested asylum in the United States. His MiG-25 was flown apart by American and Japanese engineers, revealing it was cruder than feared yet faster than expected, an intelligence windfall that reshaped Western assessments of Soviet air power and influenced future fighter design.

evt-09-06-2018-jair-bolsonaro.scenario: It is September 2018 in Juiz de Fora, and you are the surgeon rushed in after presidential candidate Jair Bolsonaro is stabbed at a campaign rally. His injuries are serious but survivable, and the election is weeks away.
evt-09-06-2018-jair-bolsonaro.prompt: What follows for Bolsonaro's campaign after the attack?

choices.text: He recovers slowly and campaigns remotely, gaining a sympathy boost
The election is postponed until he recovers
He withdraws from the race entirely due to his injuries
He loses the first round shortly after the attack

evt-09-06-2018-jair-bolsonaro.butterflyEffect: Bolsonaro survived surgery and, unable to campaign in person, ran much of his final push from a hospital bed and via social media. The attack generated a wave of sympathy that helped propel him to victory in the October 2018 election, making him Brazil's president.

evt-09-07-1159-pope-alexander-iii.scenario: Pope Adrian IV has just died, and you are a cardinal in Rome in September 1159. The College splits: a majority favors Cardinal Roland, but a minority backed by Emperor Frederick Barbarossa wants Cardinal Octavian instead.
evt-09-07-1159-pope-alexander-iii.prompt: Which candidate does the majority of cardinals elect as pope?

choices.text: Cardinal Roland, who becomes Pope Alexander III
Neither, and the see remains vacant for a year
A compromise candidate proposed by the Emperor
Cardinal Octavian, who becomes Pope Victor IV

evt-09-07-1159-pope-alexander-iii.butterflyEffect: The majority elected Cardinal Roland, who took the name Alexander III, while the minority faction crowned Octavian as the rival Victor IV with Barbarossa's backing. The resulting schism forced Alexander into exile in France for years and locked him in a long struggle with the Emperor that was not resolved until the Peace of Venice in 1177.

evt-09-07-1191-third-crusade.scenario: It is 7 September 1191 near Arsuf. You march in King Richard I's disciplined column along the coast toward Jaffa as Saladin's cavalry harass the rear, probing for a chance to break your ranks.
evt-09-07-1191-third-crusade.prompt: What should the Crusader column do as the harassment intensifies?

choices.text: Break formation and charge piecemeal at the first provocation
Halt and open negotiations with Saladin's envoys
Retreat immediately to the ships waiting offshore
Hold formation under discipline, then counter-charge at the decisive moment

evt-09-07-1191-third-crusade.butterflyEffect: Richard held the line until the moment was right, then launched a devastating counter-charge that scattered Saladin's forces at the Battle of Arsuf. The victory let the Crusaders secure Jaffa and cemented Richard's reputation as a formidable commander, though Jerusalem itself remained beyond reach.

evt-09-07-1778-anglo-french-war-1778-178.scenario: You serve as a minister to Louis XVI in early 1778. France has just signed treaties of alliance and commerce with the rebellious American colonies, and Britain's ambassador has already stormed home in protest.
evt-09-07-1778-anglo-french-war-1778-178.prompt: What should France do next in its confrontation with Britain?

choices.text: Wait for Spain to act first before making any move
Quietly fund the Americans while staying formally neutral
Declare war openly and commit the French navy against Britain
Limit support to shipments of muskets and gunpowder only

evt-09-07-1778-anglo-french-war-1778-178.butterflyEffect: France declared war on Britain in 1778, turning the American rebellion into a global war fought across the Channel, the Caribbean, and India. Spain and the Dutch Republic later joined against Britain, forcing London to fight on too many fronts at once and ultimately helping secure American independence.

evt-09-07-1822-pedro-i-of-brazil.scenario: It is 7 September 1822 on the banks of the Ipiranga River. You stand beside Prince Pedro as letters arrive from the Portuguese Cortes demanding he return to Lisbon and submit Brazil to renewed colonial control.
evt-09-07-1822-pedro-i-of-brazil.prompt: What does Pedro do upon reading the letters?

choices.text: He declares Brazil's independence from Portugal
He calls for a popular referendum before deciding
He flees into exile to avoid the confrontation
He submits and prepares to sail back to Portugal

evt-09-07-1822-pedro-i-of-brazil.butterflyEffect: Pedro proclaimed Brazil's independence on the spot, reportedly crying "Independence or Death!" He became Emperor Pedro I, and though Portugal did not formally recognize the split until 1825, Brazil emerged as a rare monarchy among the newly independent nations of the Americas.

evt-09-07-1901-eight-nation-alliance.scenario: You are a Qing court negotiator in Beijing in 1901. The Boxer Rebellion has been crushed, foreign troops still occupy the capital, and the eight allied powers have presented their terms for peace.
evt-09-07-1901-eight-nation-alliance.prompt: What did the resulting Boxer Protocol require the Qing government to accept?

choices.text: Abolish the imperial examination system immediately
Cede Manchuria outright to Russia and Japan
Pay a massive indemnity and allow foreign legation guards in Beijing
Abdicate the throne in favor of a foreign-appointed regent

evt-09-07-1901-eight-nation-alliance.butterflyEffect: The Boxer Protocol forced China to pay an enormous indemnity of 450 million taels of silver and allowed foreign powers to station troops permanently in the legation quarter. The crushing debt drained Qing finances for decades and fed the resentment that helped bring down the dynasty in the 1911 revolution.

evt-09-07-1936-thylacine.scenario: It is a cold night in early September 1936 at Hobart Zoo. You are the keeper responsible for the last known thylacine, an animal now legally protected, though the protection order came only weeks before this night.
evt-09-07-1936-thylacine.prompt: What must you do to keep this last thylacine alive through the night?

choices.text: Arrange an emergency breeding program with wild-caught thylacines
Ensure it has access to its heated indoor shelter overnight
Transfer it immediately to a mainland Australian zoo
Release it into a Tasmanian nature reserve that night

evt-09-07-1936-thylacine.butterflyEffect: The thylacine was reportedly locked out of its sheltered den and died of exposure that night, going extinct as a species just as legal protection had finally arrived, far too late to matter. Its death later became a byword for conservation failure, cited in debates that pushed Australia toward stronger endangered-species protections decades afterward.

evt-09-07-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 7 September 1940, and you sit in an RAF Fighter Command operations room as radar plots show the Luftwaffe's largest raid yet, this time streaming toward London instead of the airfields it has hammered for weeks.
evt-09-07-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: How should Fighter Command respond to this sudden change in German targeting?

choices.text: Redirect fighters to intercept the bombers over London while repairing airfields
Keep every available fighter defending airfields and ignore the raid on London
Withdraw all squadrons north of London to preserve aircraft
Ground the fighters and rely entirely on anti-aircraft batteries

evt-09-07-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The Luftwaffe's shift to bombing London, later called Black Saturday, gave battered RAF airfields and squadrons crucial time to repair and rebuild. Historians consider this switch a decisive German error that let Fighter Command retain air superiority, dooming plans for a German invasion of Britain.

evt-09-07-1984-c23-tragedy.scenario: It is 7 September 1984 off Qala, Gozo. You are part of an Armed Forces of Malta crew aboard the patrol boat C23, tasked with disposing of a cache of illegal fireworks at sea.
evt-09-07-1984-c23-tragedy.prompt: What happens during the disposal operation?

choices.text: The fireworks are dumped safely and the boat returns without incident
Engine failure forces the crew to abandon the mission before disposal
A small fire breaks out but is contained with no casualties
The cargo explodes aboard the boat, killing all but one of the crew

evt-09-07-1984-c23-tragedy.butterflyEffect: The fireworks detonated aboard C23, killing five soldiers and two policemen; only one man survived, severely injured. The tragedy led Malta's armed forces to overhaul procedures for handling and destroying seized explosives.

evt-09-07-1986-desmond-tutu.scenario: You are in the pews of St George's Cathedral in Cape Town in 1986, watching Desmond Tutu installed as Archbishop, the first Black African ever to hold the post in a church still shaped by apartheid's racial lines.
evt-09-07-1986-desmond-tutu.prompt: What did Tutu do with the new authority his office gave him?

choices.text: Withdrew from politics to focus solely on church administration
Called for armed resistance against the apartheid government
Negotiated privately with the government while staying silent in public
Kept publicly campaigning for sanctions and peaceful resistance to apartheid

evt-09-07-1986-desmond-tutu.butterflyEffect: Tutu used his pulpit to keep pressing for international economic sanctions and peaceful resistance against apartheid, even as the government cracked down on dissent. His moral standing carried into the 1990s, when he was chosen to chair South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission after apartheid's end.

evt-09-07-1996-tupac-shakur.scenario: It is the night of 7 September 1996 on the Las Vegas Strip. You are riding with Tupac Shakur's convoy after the Mike Tyson fight, tension still high from an earlier confrontation in the MGM Grand lobby, when gunfire erupts at a red light.
evt-09-07-1996-tupac-shakur.prompt: What happens to the investigation into Tupac's killing in the decades that follow?

choices.text: Orlando Anderson is convicted of the shooting before his own death
It remains formally unsolved for over 25 years until an arrest in 2023
Suge Knight is swiftly convicted of orchestrating the murder
The FBI closes the case permanently within a year with no leads

evt-09-07-1996-tupac-shakur.butterflyEffect: The case went unsolved for over 25 years until September 2023, when Duane "Keffe D" Davis, a former Crips leader, became the first person ever criminally charged over the shooting. The killing also deepened the East Coast–West Coast rap rivalry, a feud that preceded the still-unsolved murder of Notorious B.I.G. just six months later.

evt-09-07-1999-1999-izmit-earthquake.scenario: It is early September 1999, three weeks after the earthquake tore through İzmit. You are a Turkish citizen watching rescue crews still working through collapsed apartment blocks, and public anger is rising over how the government responded.
evt-09-07-1999-1999-izmit-earthquake.prompt: What lasting political consequence follows from the disaster?

choices.text: Public anger over the slow, chaotic response erodes trust in the coalition government
The government is widely praised for its swift and effective response
Martial law is declared across the affected provinces
Turkey withdraws from NATO in protest over the disaster response

evt-09-07-1999-1999-izmit-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Public fury over slow rescues, corrupt building practices, and government mismanagement badly damaged confidence in Turkey's coalition government. That anger fed into the political realignment that brought the AKP to power in 2002.

evt-09-07-2004-hurricane-ivan.scenario: It is dawn on 7 September 2004 in St George's, Grenada. Hurricane Ivan is bearing down as a major hurricane, the first of this strength to strike the island in generations, and you are a government official watching roofs begin to tear away.
evt-09-07-2004-hurricane-ivan.prompt: What does the Grenadian government do as the island is devastated?

choices.text: Wait until the storm fully passes before assessing any response
Declare a state of emergency and request regional disaster assistance
Restrict all outside communication until damage reports are finalized
Rely solely on private tourism-industry insurance to fund recovery

evt-09-07-2004-hurricane-ivan.butterflyEffect: Grenada declared a national disaster and CARICOM's regional disaster agency, CDERA, mounted one of the largest relief operations in Caribbean history. The destruction of most of the island's housing stock pushed Eastern Caribbean nations to overhaul building codes and expand hurricane insurance schemes.

evt-09-07-2010-2010-senkaku-boat-collisi.scenario: It is the morning of 7 September 2010 near the disputed Senkaku Islands. You command a Japanese Coast Guard patrol boat as a Chinese trawler, Minjinyu 5179, refuses orders to leave the area and collides with your vessels.
evt-09-07-2010-2010-senkaku-boat-collisi.prompt: What does the Coast Guard do after the collisions?

choices.text: They let the trawler sail back to China unchallenged
They seize the trawler and detain its captain under Japanese law
They sink the trawler to prevent further incursions
They escort the trawler to a neutral port for joint investigation

evt-09-07-2010-2010-senkaku-boat-collisi.butterflyEffect: Japan detained the trawler's captain and crew, triggering a major diplomatic row with Beijing. China responded with economic pressure, including restrictions on rare-earth exports, and the incident hardened both nations' positions on the disputed islands for years afterward.

evt-09-07-2011-lokomotiv-yaroslavl-plane.scenario: It is September 2011, and investigators are combing through the wreckage of Yak-Service Flight 9633 near Yaroslavl, trying to understand why the plane carrying the Lokomotiv hockey team never got off the ground.
evt-09-07-2011-lokomotiv-yaroslavl-plane.prompt: What do investigators conclude caused the crash?

choices.text: A pilot mistakenly applied the brakes instead of accelerating on takeoff
A bird strike disabled both engines during ascent
A mechanical fault in the fuel system caused an engine fire before takeoff
Air traffic control cleared the aircraft onto an occupied runway

evt-09-07-2011-lokomotiv-yaroslavl-plane.butterflyEffect: Investigators found that one pilot had mistakenly pressed the brake pedal instead of the throttle during takeoff, causing the plane to fail to gain enough speed before it ran out of runway. The disaster devastated Russian hockey, prompted the KHL to review team travel safety, and led to the Lokomotiv club being entirely rebuilt.

evt-09-07-2012-canada-iran-relations.scenario: It is September 2012, and as Canada's Foreign Minister you are weighing whether to keep an embassy open in Tehran despite Iran's nuclear defiance, support for Assad's regime, and open threats against Israel.
evt-09-07-2012-canada-iran-relations.prompt: What do you decide to do with Canada's diplomatic mission in Iran?

choices.text: Close the embassy and sever formal diplomatic ties entirely
Cut trade links while leaving the embassy staffed
Keep the embassy open but issue a formal diplomatic protest
Downgrade the mission to a low-level trade office only

evt-09-07-2012-canada-iran-relations.butterflyEffect: Canada closed its Tehran embassy, expelled Iranian diplomats from Ottawa, and gave them five days to leave, citing Iran's nuclear program, support for the Assad regime, and threats against Israel. The rupture has lasted over a decade, with Ottawa stating restoration would require a change of regime in Tehran.

evt-09-07-2017-2017-chiapas-earthquake.scenario: It is just before midnight on 7 September 2017, and you live in a coastal town in Chiapas. The ground has just convulsed violently for nearly a minute, and sirens begin warning of a possible tsunami along the Gulf of Tehuantepec.
evt-09-07-2017-2017-chiapas-earthquake.prompt: What is the safest immediate action to take?

choices.text: Drive along the coastal road to check on relatives first
Stay inside to protect your home from looters
Move immediately to higher ground away from the coastline
Wait for official confirmation before leaving your house

evt-09-07-2017-2017-chiapas-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Authorities issued tsunami warnings across Mexico and Central America, and coastal communities evacuated to higher ground as a precaution. The quake, one of the strongest ever recorded in Mexico, also renewed scrutiny of building codes just days before another major earthquake struck central Mexico on 19 September.

evt-09-07-2019-oleh-sentsov.scenario: It is 7 September 2019. You are Oleh Sentsov, a Ukrainian filmmaker imprisoned in Russia since 2015 for opposing the annexation of Crimea, and word arrives of a prisoner exchange being finalized.

choices.text: You are transferred to a harsher labor camp
Your sentence is extended after a new trial
You are released as part of a prisoner exchange between Russia and Ukraine
You escape during a prison transfer

evt-09-07-2019-oleh-sentsov.butterflyEffect: Sentsov was freed as part of a large prisoner exchange between Russia and Ukraine, one of the most significant swaps since the Crimea annexation. He returned to filmmaking and activism, and after Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion he joined the Ukrainian armed forces.

evt-09-07-2021-bitcoin.scenario: It is 7 September 2021 in San Salvador. You run a small shop, and today El Salvador's new Bitcoin Law takes effect, requiring businesses like yours to be able to accept bitcoin payments alongside the US dollar.
evt-09-07-2021-bitcoin.prompt: How do you comply while protecting yourself from bitcoin's price swings?

choices.text: Only accept bitcoin for purchases over a certain value
Use the government's Chivo wallet, which can instantly convert bitcoin to dollars
Refuse to accept any bitcoin payments despite the new law
Convert all incoming payments into gold instead of dollars

evt-09-07-2021-bitcoin.butterflyEffect: Most merchants used the government's Chivo wallet, which could auto-convert bitcoin into dollars, though rollout was plagued by technical failures and public skepticism. Adoption drew IMF warnings over financial risk, and in 2025 El Salvador revoked bitcoin's legal tender status as part of an IMF loan deal, even as it kept accumulating bitcoin as a national reserve asset.

evt-09-07-2021-national-unity-government.scenario: It is 7 September 2021. You sit with the National Unity Government's leadership, ousted parliamentarians and ethnic minority representatives, weighing how to respond to the military junta's escalating crackdown after the coup.
evt-09-07-2021-national-unity-government.prompt: What does the NUG decide to declare?

choices.text: A people's defensive war against the junta
A ceasefire and unconditional talks with the military
A call for international peacekeepers only, with no armed action
A formal surrender to preserve civilian lives

evt-09-07-2021-national-unity-government.butterflyEffect: The NUG declared a people's defensive war against the junta, formally endorsing armed resistance alongside ethnic armed organizations. This deepened Myanmar's civil conflict, expanding the People's Defense Forces and prolonging fighting across the country for years.

evt-09-08-1565-st-augustine-florida.scenario: You are Pedro Menéndez de Avilés, having just founded a Spanish settlement on Florida's coast in September 1565. A French Huguenot colony, Fort Caroline, sits not far to the north, and Spain wants no rival claim on this coast.
evt-09-08-1565-st-augustine-florida.prompt: What do you do next after establishing your new settlement?

choices.text: Sail back to Spain to report the founding to the crown
March overland to attack the French colony at Fort Caroline
Fortify the new settlement and wait for reinforcements from Spain
Negotiate a boundary treaty with the French settlers

evt-09-08-1565-st-augustine-florida.butterflyEffect: Menéndez marched his men overland and struck Fort Caroline, killing most of its French defenders and securing Spain's hold on Florida. His settlement, St. Augustine, went on to become the oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the continental United States.

evt-09-08-1566-ottoman-habsburg-wars.scenario: You serve as a vizier in the Ottoman camp before the fortress of Szigetvár in September 1566. Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent has just died in his tent, but the final assault on the last defenders is about to begin.
evt-09-08-1566-ottoman-habsburg-wars.prompt: What do you do about the sultan's death before the fortress falls?

choices.text: Order an immediate retreat back to Ottoman territory
Announce the death at once to rally the troops around a new commander
Declare a field regency and crown an heir on the spot
Keep the death secret and continue issuing orders in the sultan's name

evt-09-08-1566-ottoman-habsburg-wars.butterflyEffect: Grand Vizier Sokollu Mehmed Pasha concealed Suleiman's death for weeks, issuing orders in his name until his son Selim II could be secured on the throne. The ruse prevented panic or mutiny in the army and allowed a smooth succession, even as the siege marked the practical high-water mark of Ottoman expansion into Central Europe.

evt-09-08-1726-johann-sebastian-bach.scenario: It is the twelfth Sunday after Trinity, 1726, and you take your seat in a Leipzig church as Thomaskantor Johann Sebastian Bach readies his musicians to premiere a brand-new cantata.
evt-09-08-1726-johann-sebastian-bach.prompt: What unusual solo instrument does Bach feature to carry the piece's melodic weight?

choices.text: A solo oboe
A solo violin
A solo flute
An obbligato organ

evt-09-08-1726-johann-sebastian-bach.butterflyEffect: Bach wrote "Geist und Seele wird verwirret" (BWV 35) with an extensive obbligato organ part in a concerto-like style, an experiment he pursued in several cantatas of the mid-1720s. This blending of secular concerto form with sacred vocal music fed directly into his later organ and harpsichord concertos and cemented Leipzig's reputation for musically ambitious church services.

evt-09-08-1755-french-and-indian-war.scenario: You serve under Sir William Johnson near Lake George, New York. A detachment sent out that morning has just been ambushed and mauled by French and Native forces in what soldiers are calling the 'Bloody Morning Scout,' and the enemy is now advancing on your main camp.
evt-09-08-1755-french-and-indian-war.prompt: What does Johnson's force do to meet the advancing French and allied attack?

choices.text: Negotiate a truce with the approaching French force
Retreat southward toward Albany to regroup
Entrench behind hastily built breastworks and artillery to meet the attack
Launch an immediate counter-ambush into the forest

evt-09-08-1755-french-and-indian-war.butterflyEffect: Johnson's men held behind hastily thrown-up log breastworks and cannon, repelling the French assault and wounding and capturing their commander, Baron Dieskau. The victory boosted colonial morale early in the war, earned Johnson a baronetcy, and helped set the stage for later British campaigns toward Fort Ticonderoga.
