evt-09-08-1796-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: It is September 8, 1796, near Bassano in Venetia. You are General Napoleon Bonaparte, pursuing an Austrian army under General Wurmser that is retreating toward the fortress of Mantua.
evt-09-08-1796-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What does Napoleon do when he catches up with Wurmser's retreating force?

choices.text: Wait for fresh orders and reinforcements from Paris
Offer Wurmser terms for an armistice
Withdraw to consolidate supply lines before engaging
Attack and rout the Austrian force before it reaches Mantua

evt-09-08-1796-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: Napoleon's troops attacked and routed the Austrians at Bassano, driving the survivors to take refuge inside Mantua. The victory tightened the French siege of that fortress and further burnished Napoleon's growing reputation as the Republic's most formidable field commander in Italy.

evt-09-08-1831-russian-empire.scenario: It is September 8, 1831, and you are a Polish insurgent watching General Paskevich's Russian army break through the last barricades of Warsaw after a long siege.
evt-09-08-1831-russian-empire.prompt: What follows for the Polish uprising in its final days?

choices.text: The remaining army retreats and surrenders, its leaders fleeing into exile
French troops arrive to relieve the city
The Polish government negotiates full autonomy with the Tsar
The uprising spreads successfully into Russia itself

evt-09-08-1831-russian-empire.butterflyEffect: Within weeks the remaining Polish forces retreated toward the Prussian and Austrian borders and surrendered; thousands of officers, intellectuals and soldiers fled abroad in what became known as the Great Emigration, scattering Polish nationalist culture across Paris and London. Russia then abolished Poland's constitution and imposed direct rule, planting the resentment that would explode again in the 1863 uprising.

evt-09-08-1831-william-iv.scenario: It is 8 September 1831 at Westminster Abbey. King William IV, wary of public anger over royal extravagance amid talk of political reform, has insisted his coronation be far plainer than his brother George IV's lavish affair.
evt-09-08-1831-william-iv.prompt: How does William IV cut the cost and pomp of his coronation?

choices.text: He moves the entire ceremony outdoors to Hyde Park
He doubles the traditional banquet to win public favor
He postpones the coronation indefinitely to save money
He cancels the coronation banquet and reduces the ceremonial display

evt-09-08-1831-william-iv.butterflyEffect: William stripped away much of the traditional banquet and ceremony, earning the event the mocking nickname the "Half-Crownation." The pared-down spectacle reflected a monarchy adjusting to a more sceptical public mood, one that would soon force William to accept the transformative Reform Act of 1832.

evt-09-08-1860-paddle-steamer.scenario: You captain the schooner Augusta on Lake Michigan in the pre-dawn dark of 8 September 1860, after your vessel has just struck the crowded paddle steamer Lady Elgin in a storm.
evt-09-08-1860-paddle-steamer.prompt: What do you do after the collision?

choices.text: Anchor in place and fire distress signals all night
Radio nearby ships for assistance
Continue on to port, assuming the other vessel suffered only minor damage
Turn back immediately to search for survivors

evt-09-08-1860-paddle-steamer.butterflyEffect: Believing the damage minor, the Augusta sailed on to Chicago unaware the Lady Elgin was breaking apart behind her, and roughly 300 people died, many swept against the shore by the storm. Public outrage over the schooner's failure to render aid helped push for stronger navigation rules and better-funded lifesaving stations on the Great Lakes.

evt-09-08-1900-1900-galveston-hurricane.scenario: It is September 8, 1900, and Galveston, Texas has just been devastated by a storm surge with no seawall to hold it back. In the disaster's aftermath, city leaders and engineers must decide how to protect the island from ever suffering this again.
evt-09-08-1900-1900-galveston-hurricane.prompt: What major engineering response do city leaders undertake after the storm?

choices.text: Rely solely on federal levees along the ship channel
Raise the city's grade and build a massive seawall
Rebuild exactly as before with no new defenses
Abandon the island and relocate the city inland

evt-09-08-1900-1900-galveston-hurricane.butterflyEffect: Engineers raised the city's grade by as much as 17 feet and built a 10-mile seawall along the Gulf shore. Yet the disaster still frightened off investors, who turned to Houston instead, ending Galveston's era as the region's leading port and commercial center.

evt-09-08-1907-gertrude-stein.scenario: It is September 8, 1907, and you are visiting Gertrude Stein's Paris apartment when a newly arrived American, Alice B. Toklas, is introduced at the door.
evt-09-08-1907-gertrude-stein.prompt: What role will this newcomer come to play in Stein's life?

choices.text: A business partner in an art-dealing venture
A brief houseguest who returns to America within weeks
A rival hostess who competes for the same salon guests
Her lifelong domestic partner and secretary

evt-09-08-1907-gertrude-stein.butterflyEffect: Toklas became Stein's lifelong domestic partner, secretary, and household manager, quietly running the salon that hosted Picasso, Hemingway, and Matisse. Decades later Stein wrote "The Autobiography of Alice B. Toklas" (1933) in Toklas's voice, a bestseller that finally made Stein a mainstream literary celebrity.

evt-09-08-1921-atlantic-city-new-jersey.scenario: You are a judge on the Atlantic City boardwalk on 8 September 1921, part of a pageant organized to stretch the resort's tourist season past Labor Day. Sixteen-year-old Margaret Gorman stands among the contestants.
evt-09-08-1921-atlantic-city-new-jersey.prompt: What title is Margaret Gorman awarded as the pageant's winner?

choices.text: Golden Mermaid
Miss Atlantic City Eternal
Miss Boardwalk
Queen of Neptune

evt-09-08-1921-atlantic-city-new-jersey.butterflyEffect: Gorman was crowned the "Golden Mermaid," and the contest was soon retroactively recognized as the first Miss America pageant. What began as a tourism gimmick grew into an annual American institution blending beauty competition, scholarship, and decades of debate over the public judging of women.

evt-09-08-1935-huey-long.scenario: It is September 8, 1935, and you are standing in a corridor of the Louisiana State Capitol in Baton Rouge as Senator Huey Long strides past, flanked by his bodyguards.
evt-09-08-1935-huey-long.prompt: What happens next in the corridor?

choices.text: He narrowly escapes an assassination attempt unharmed
He is shot by a lone gunman
He is ambushed by a group of armed conspirators
He collapses from a sudden stroke

evt-09-08-1935-huey-long.butterflyEffect: Dr. Carl Weiss, a local physician with grievances against Long's political machine, shot him at close range; Long's bodyguards immediately killed Weiss in the chaos that followed. Long died two days later, ending his presidential ambitions and the momentum of his Share Our Wealth movement, though his family's political organization continued to dominate Louisiana politics for decades.

evt-09-08-1941-siege-of-leningrad.scenario: It is early September 1941, and German Army Group North has reached Leningrad's suburbs while Finnish forces close the ring from the north. The city's defenses are strong enough to make a direct assault costly.
evt-09-08-1941-siege-of-leningrad.prompt: What does the German command decide to do about the city instead of storming it?

choices.text: Launch an immediate full infantry assault to take the city
Bypass Leningrad entirely and push straight for Moscow
Cut off supply routes and starve the city into surrender
Offer the city a negotiated surrender with civilian safe passage

evt-09-08-1941-siege-of-leningrad.butterflyEffect: Hitler chose to bomb and blockade the city rather than risk a costly assault, aiming to starve its population into submission. The siege stretched to 872 days and cost an estimated 1.5 million lives, with the Soviets sustaining the city only through the perilous Road of Life across frozen Lake Ladoga.

evt-09-08-1974-watergate-scandal.scenario: You are President Gerald Ford, barely a month into office after Nixon's resignation. Your predecessor faces likely criminal indictment over Watergate, and the country is exhausted by the scandal.
evt-09-08-1974-watergate-scandal.prompt: What do you decide to do about Nixon's looming prosecution?

choices.text: Refer the decision to a special congressional committee
Let the Justice Department pursue criminal charges as usual
Offer a pardon only if Nixon publicly confesses guilt
Grant Nixon a full, unconditional pardon

evt-09-08-1974-watergate-scandal.butterflyEffect: On 8 September 1974 Ford granted Nixon a full and unconditional pardon for any Watergate crimes, hoping to let the nation move on. The decision triggered public outrage, badly damaged Ford's credibility, and is widely seen as a key reason he narrowly lost the 1976 election to Jimmy Carter.

evt-09-08-1991-tailhook-association.scenario: You are a Navy investigator called in after the September 1991 Tailhook Association symposium in Las Vegas, where dozens of women, including fellow naval officers, reported being groped and assaulted by aviators in a hotel hallway.
evt-09-08-1991-tailhook-association.prompt: What actually followed as the scandal became public?

choices.text: The allegations were dismissed and no action was taken
The symposium was expanded and given official Pentagon funding
The Navy Secretary resigned and sweeping harassment policy reforms followed
Dozens of officers were court-martialed and imprisoned

evt-09-08-1991-tailhook-association.butterflyEffect: The cover-up attempts and fallout forced the resignation of Navy Secretary H. Lawrence Garrett III and derailed numerous careers, though few faced criminal conviction. The scandal became a turning point for military policy on sexual harassment and accelerated the opening of combat aviation roles to women.

evt-09-08-1994-usair-flight-427.scenario: You are an NTSB investigator combing through the wreckage in the woods of Hopewell Township. The flight data recorder shows USAir Flight 427 rolled violently left and pitched into a fatal dive on final approach to Pittsburgh, with no clear pilot error or weather cause yet found.
evt-09-08-1994-usair-flight-427.prompt: What mechanical flaw does the years-long investigation eventually pin the crash on?

choices.text: A bird strike disabling one engine on approach
Pilot overcorrection during a routine crosswind landing
Wind shear from a passing thunderstorm
Wake turbulence from a preceding aircraft combined with a rudder power control unit malfunction

evt-09-08-1994-usair-flight-427.butterflyEffect: After nearly five years, investigators traced the crash to a jammed rudder power control unit that could deflect the rudder opposite the pilots' commands, a defect also implicated in United Flight 585 and Eastwind Flight 517. The finding forced Boeing to redesign the 737's rudder system and led to mandatory retrofits across the entire worldwide fleet.

evt-09-08-2022-elizabeth-ii.scenario: It is the morning of 8 September 2022 and you are a senior Buckingham Palace communications aide. Doctors at Balmoral have just told you the Queen's condition is worsening rapidly, and the world is waiting for news.
evt-09-08-2022-elizabeth-ii.prompt: What does the Palace do next as the Queen's health critically declines?

choices.text: Postpone any statement until Parliament reconvenes
Announce her death pre-emptively to prepare the public
Say nothing publicly until after her death
Issue a carefully worded statement expressing doctors' concern

evt-09-08-2022-elizabeth-ii.butterflyEffect: The Palace issued a rare statement saying doctors were "concerned" for the Queen's health, prompting royal family members to rush to Balmoral. She died that afternoon, ending a 70-year reign and making Charles III king immediately under the principle that the throne is never empty.

evt-09-09-9-battle-of-the-teutoburg-fore.scenario: It is September, 9 CE, and you march with three Roman legions through the dense Teutoburg Forest. Your guide, the Germanic officer Arminius, insists the path ahead is safe, even as scouts report warriors massing in the trees.
evt-09-09-9-battle-of-the-teutoburg-fore.prompt: What does Varus actually do when warned of a possible ambush?

choices.text: Sends envoys to negotiate directly with the Germanic tribes
Halts the column and fortifies a defensive camp
Dismisses the warnings and continues the march as planned
Orders an immediate retreat back to the Rhine

evt-09-09-9-battle-of-the-teutoburg-fore.butterflyEffect: Varus dismissed the warnings and trusted Arminius, who then led the legions into a devastating ambush that annihilated three legions and their auxiliaries. The disaster halted Roman expansion into Germania for good, fixing the Rhine as the empire's frontier and shaping the ethnic map of Europe for centuries.

evt-09-09-1493-ottoman-wars-in-europe.scenario: It is September 9, 1493, on the plain of Krbava Field in Croatia. You ride with the assembled Croatian nobility, intercepting an Ottoman raiding column laden with plunder and captives as it withdraws toward Bosnia.
evt-09-09-1493-ottoman-wars-in-europe.prompt: What actually followed the Croatian charge at Krbava Field?

choices.text: Both sides negotiated a truce before fighting began
The Ottomans retreated without engaging in battle
The Croatian force was catastrophically defeated, decimating its nobility
The Croatians won a decisive victory and freed all the captives

evt-09-09-1493-ottoman-wars-in-europe.butterflyEffect: The Croatian nobility suffered a catastrophic defeat, losing much of its military leadership in a single afternoon. The disaster became known as "the graveyard of the Croatian nobility" and left the kingdom dangerously exposed to further Ottoman incursions in the following decades.

evt-09-09-1570-ottoman-venetian-war-1570.scenario: It is September 1570, and you are a Venetian defender inside the walls of Nicosia, Cyprus, after forty days of relentless Ottoman bombardment, your powder and men nearly spent.
evt-09-09-1570-ottoman-venetian-war-1570.prompt: What happens when the Ottoman army finally storms the breach?

choices.text: The defenders repel the assault and the Ottomans withdraw from Cyprus
A Holy League relief fleet arrives just in time to break the siege
The city falls and is sacked, with much of the population massacred or enslaved
The garrison negotiates a peaceful surrender allowing safe passage to Venice

evt-09-09-1570-ottoman-venetian-war-1570.butterflyEffect: Nicosia fell on 9 September 1570 after the Ottomans stormed the breached walls, killing a large part of the population and enslaving thousands more. News of the massacre horrified Christian Europe and helped spur the formation of the Holy League, whose combined fleet would destroy the Ottoman navy at Lepanto the following year.

evt-09-09-1791-washington-d-c.scenario: It is 9 September 1791, and you are one of three commissioners appointed by President Washington to oversee the new federal city rising along the Potomac, drafting the letter that will fix its name for history.
evt-09-09-1791-washington-d-c.prompt: What do the commissioners decide to call the new capital and its district?

choices.text: They call it simply "Federal City" and leave the name undecided
They name the city "Columbia" in honor of the new nation
They name it "Jeffersonia" after the Secretary of State
They name the city "Washington" within the "Territory of Columbia"

evt-09-09-1791-washington-d-c.butterflyEffect: The commissioners' letter formally named the new capital "the City of Washington" within "the Territory of Columbia," honoring the first president in his own lifetime. That choice fixed the nation's civic identity around his name, and the district became the permanent seat of the federal government when it opened in 1800.

evt-09-09-1892-lick-observatory.scenario: It is September 1892, and you are peering through the great 36-inch refractor at Lick Observatory on Mount Hamilton, studying the glow of Jupiter, when you notice a faint point of light close to the planet that no star catalog accounts for.
evt-09-09-1892-lick-observatory.prompt: What should you do to confirm whether this faint object is a new moon of Jupiter?

choices.text: Dismiss it as a flaw in the telescope's optics
Announce it immediately as a new planet without further observation
Assume it is a passing comet and take no further notes
Track its position over several nights to determine if it orbits Jupiter

evt-09-09-1892-lick-observatory.butterflyEffect: Edward Emerson Barnard tracked the object over several nights and confirmed it was a new moon, later named Amalthea. It was the first moon discovered by direct visual observation since Galileo found Jupiter's four largest moons in 1610, and remains the last major moon found this way before photographic and later methods took over.

evt-09-09-1939-world-war-ii.scenario: It is September 9, 1939, on the narrow Hel Peninsula jutting into the Baltic. You are one of roughly 3,000 Polish troops manning coastal batteries here, cut off from the rest of the collapsing front but ordered to hold.
evt-09-09-1939-world-war-ii.prompt: What actually happened to the defenders of Hel in the weeks that followed?

choices.text: They held out for weeks before finally surrendering in early October
They broke the siege and retook Warsaw
They repelled the German invasion entirely
They surrendered within a single day of the assault

evt-09-09-1939-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The garrison held out for nearly a month, far longer than most Polish positions, before surrendering on October 2, 1939. Its stubborn resistance became a symbol of Polish defiance during the invasion, even as the rest of the country fell.

evt-09-09-1954-1954-chlef-earthquake.scenario: It is just after 2 a.m. on September 9, 1954, in Orléansville, French Algeria, and the ground beneath the town is convulsing violently, toppling masonry buildings built without any thought to seismic risk.
evt-09-09-1954-1954-chlef-earthquake.prompt: What should authorities do in the aftermath to protect the region from future quakes?

choices.text: Introduce and enforce modern seismic-resistant building codes
Rebuild exactly as before using traditional masonry
Rely on prayer and religious observance instead of construction changes
Abandon the town site entirely and forbid resettlement

evt-09-09-1954-1954-chlef-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The earthquake devastated Orléansville and led French colonial and later Algerian authorities to overhaul building codes, moving toward genuine seismic-resistant construction standards. Algeria has continued updating these regulations in the decades since, as the region remains prone to major earthquakes.

evt-09-09-1957-dwight-d-eisenhower.scenario: It is September 9, 1957, and President Eisenhower has just signed the Civil Rights Act after Senate Majority Leader Lyndon Johnson steered it through a divided Congress, the first such law since Reconstruction.
evt-09-09-1957-dwight-d-eisenhower.prompt: What key institution did the new act actually establish to enforce civil rights?

choices.text: A nationwide ban on literacy tests for voting
A Civil Rights Division in the Justice Department and a Civil Rights Commission
Federal control over all state voter registration rolls
Automatic federal prosecution of any reported discrimination

evt-09-09-1957-dwight-d-eisenhower.butterflyEffect: The act created the Civil Rights Division of the Justice Department and the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights. Though a jury-trial amendment weakened its enforcement power, it broke a 82-year legislative drought and set precedent for the stronger 1964 and 1965 Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts.

evt-09-09-1962-charles-de-gaulle.scenario: It is September 9, 1962, in Bonn's Hofgarten square. You stand among 20,000 young Germans as French President Charles de Gaulle addresses the crowd in German, calling for reconciliation between two nations that fought three wars in seventy years.
evt-09-09-1962-charles-de-gaulle.prompt: What formal agreement did this reconciliation tour help bring about the following January?

choices.text: The Élysée Treaty establishing formal Franco-German cooperation
West Germany's admission to NATO's nuclear planning group
The dissolution of the European Coal and Steel Community
A merger of the French and German armed forces

evt-09-09-1962-charles-de-gaulle.butterflyEffect: De Gaulle's Bonn visit deepened his partnership with Chancellor Adenauer, leading to the Élysée Treaty of January 1963, which established regular consultation and cooperation between France and West Germany. That treaty became the cornerstone of the Franco-German axis that has driven European integration ever since.

evt-09-09-1969-allegheny-airlines-flight.scenario: It is September 9, 1969, over rural Indiana, and you are guiding air traffic near Indianapolis. A DC-9 airliner and a small private Piper Cherokee are both flying in the same uncontrolled airspace, closing on each other without any system to alert either pilot.
evt-09-09-1969-allegheny-airlines-flight.prompt: What major air-safety change followed this catastrophic midair collision?

choices.text: Airlines switch entirely to propeller aircraft for regional routes
Air traffic control is abolished in favor of pilot self-reporting
The FAA expands controlled airspace and pushes mandatory transponder use
All private aircraft are banned from national airspace

evt-09-09-1969-allegheny-airlines-flight.butterflyEffect: The collision, which killed all 83 people aboard both aircraft and remains Indiana's deadliest aviation disaster, spurred the FAA to expand mandatory transponder requirements and enlarge controlled airspace around major airports. It became a landmark case for the push toward better separation of small aircraft and commercial airliners.

evt-09-09-2001-al-qaeda.scenario: It is September 9, 2001, in Khwaja Bahauddin, Afghanistan. You are an aide to Northern Alliance commander Ahmad Shah Massoud, ushering in two men posing as Moroccan journalists who have waited weeks for this interview.
evt-09-09-2001-al-qaeda.prompt: What happened when the visitors' hidden camera-bomb detonated during the meeting?

choices.text: Massoud was killed, removing the Taliban's chief remaining rival
Massoud was wounded but survived the blast
The attackers were revealed as Taliban negotiators seeking a truce
The bomb failed to detonate and the attackers were captured

evt-09-09-2001-al-qaeda.butterflyEffect: The explosion killed Massoud, eliminating the main military leader of Afghan resistance to the Taliban just two days before the September 11 attacks. Many analysts see the timing as coordinated with al-Qaeda's leadership to remove a key opponent before the anticipated American response in Afghanistan.

evt-09-09-2006-space-shuttle-atlantis.scenario: It is September 9, 2006, at Kennedy Space Center. You are a NASA mission manager watching Atlantis lift off on STS-115, the first shuttle flight to resume space station construction since the Columbia disaster grounded the fleet three and a half years earlier.
evt-09-09-2006-space-shuttle-atlantis.prompt: What was Atlantis's main cargo for the International Space Station on this mission?

choices.text: The Japanese Kibo laboratory module
The P3/P4 truss segment carrying new solar arrays
A final servicing kit for the Hubble Space Telescope
The European Columbus laboratory module

evt-09-09-2006-space-shuttle-atlantis.butterflyEffect: Atlantis delivered the P3/P4 truss segment with a new pair of solar arrays, restarting station assembly after the long post-Columbia pause. This expanded the station's power supply, paving the way for larger crews and the later addition of international lab modules.

evt-09-09-2010-natural-gas.scenario: It is the evening of September 9, 2010, in the Glenview neighborhood of San Bruno, California. Without warning, the ground shakes and a fireball erupts from beneath a residential street as a natural-gas pipeline fails.
evt-09-09-2010-natural-gas.prompt: What did the resulting explosion and fire do to the neighborhood?

choices.text: An earthquake, not a pipeline, caused the blast
A sinkhole swallowed several homes before any fire started
It killed eight residents and destroyed dozens of homes
It was quickly contained with no injuries or damage

evt-09-09-2010-natural-gas.butterflyEffect: The ruptured PG&E pipeline killed eight people and destroyed dozens of homes. Federal investigators traced the failure to a decades-old faulty weld and poor utility recordkeeping, leading to criminal charges against PG&E and a nationwide push for stricter pipeline safety oversight.

evt-09-09-2015-elizabeth-ii.scenario: It is 9 September 2015, and you are a royal correspondent stationed outside Windsor as Queen Elizabeth II travels to open a new railway line, the moment approaching when she will surpass a record held for over a century.
evt-09-09-2015-elizabeth-ii.prompt: What milestone does Queen Elizabeth II reach on this day?

choices.text: She surpasses Queen Victoria to become Britain's longest-reigning monarch
She is formally crowned Empress of India
She celebrates her Diamond Jubilee marking 60 years on the throne
She becomes the first British monarch to visit every Commonwealth nation

evt-09-09-2015-elizabeth-ii.butterflyEffect: Elizabeth II passed Queen Victoria's reign of 63 years and 216 days to become Britain's longest-reigning monarch. She went on to reign 70 years and 214 days in total, making her the second-longest-reigning sovereign of any nation in recorded history and the longest-reigning queen regnant ever.

evt-09-09-2016-north-korea.scenario: It is September 9, 2016, North Korea's National Day. Seismic stations across the region register a fresh shockwave from the Punggye-ri test site, the fifth and largest such tremor Pyongyang has produced.
evt-09-09-2016-north-korea.prompt: What actually followed North Korea's fifth nuclear test?

choices.text: The United States launched an immediate military strike on the test site
The Six-Party Talks resumed and quickly resolved the crisis
The UN Security Council imposed tighter sanctions, including coal export caps
North Korea agreed to full denuclearization talks within weeks

evt-09-09-2016-north-korea.butterflyEffect: The UN Security Council responded with Resolution 2321, tightening sanctions by capping North Korean coal exports and restricting other trade. Rather than halting the program, the test set the stage for even larger detonations, including a purported hydrogen bomb test in 2017.

evt-09-09-2025-2025-russian-drone-incurs.scenario: It is late on September 9, 2025. Radar screens across Poland light up as nearly two dozen drones, allegedly launched from Russia, cross into Polish airspace, forcing NATO air defenses into action overnight.
evt-09-09-2025-2025-russian-drone-incurs.prompt: What did NATO forces do in response to the incursion?

choices.text: Launched a ground invasion of Belarus in response
Ignored the drones as routine airspace traffic
Evacuated all of Warsaw as a precaution
Scrambled jets that shot down several of the drones

evt-09-09-2025-2025-russian-drone-incurs.butterflyEffect: Polish and allied aircraft, including Dutch jets, scrambled and shot down up to four of the drones while major airports briefly closed. Poland invoked NATO Article 4 consultations, pushing the alliance to reinforce air-defense readiness along its eastern flank.

evt-09-10-1547-anglo-scottish-wars.scenario: It's 10 September 1547 near Musselburgh. Your Scottish army holds strong high ground while Protector Somerset's fleet bombards your flank from the sea and English infantry probe your lines below.
evt-09-10-1547-anglo-scottish-wars.prompt: What fatal decision does the Scottish command make at the Battle of Pinkie?

choices.text: They dig in and wait out the naval bombardment
They abandon the ridge to attack downhill into cavalry and cannon fire
They open negotiations for a truce with Somerset
They withdraw to Edinburgh without engaging the English

evt-09-10-1547-anglo-scottish-wars.butterflyEffect: The Earl of Arran ordered the Scots off their defensible ridge to strike the English before they could regroup, exposing his men to cavalry charges and naval gunfire on open ground. The resulting slaughter, remembered as 'Black Saturday,' was the last full pitched battle between England and Scotland as separate kingdoms and pushed Scotland to seek closer ties with France against English pressure.

evt-09-10-1622-nagasaki.scenario: It is September 1622 in Nagasaki. Shogunate officials have rounded up dozens of Christians, missionaries and their Japanese converts, offering them one last chance to recant their faith before the executions begin.
evt-09-10-1622-nagasaki.prompt: What choice do the condemned make in what becomes known as the Great Genna Martyrdom?

choices.text: They bribe officials and are quietly exiled to Macau
They are pardoned after foreign traders intervene
They refuse to recant and are executed for their faith
They recant publicly and are released unharmed

evt-09-10-1622-nagasaki.butterflyEffect: Fifty-five Christians refused to recant and were executed by burning or beheading, part of the Tokugawa shogunate's escalating campaign to eradicate Christianity. The crackdown intensified over the following decades, feeding into the sakoku policy that sealed Japan off from most foreign contact and drove Christianity underground for over two centuries.

evt-09-10-1779-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 10 September 1779, and you command the small American sloop Morris on Lake Pontchartrain, spotting the British armed sloop West Florida patrolling ahead of you.
evt-09-10-1779-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What do you do as commander of the Morris?

choices.text: Retreat toward New Orleans to avoid a stronger force
Engage and capture the West Florida after a brief fight
Signal a nearby Spanish squadron to attack instead
Hold position and wait for reinforcements before engaging

evt-09-10-1779-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Captain William Pickles engaged and captured the West Florida in a short, sharp fight, giving American and allied Spanish forces control of Lake Pontchartrain. Coming as Spain moved against British holdings on the Gulf Coast, the victory helped secure the region for the anti-British coalition during the Revolutionary War.

evt-09-10-1845-john-doubleday-restorer.scenario: It's 1845 in London, and you are antiquities restorer John Doubleday, staring at a table scattered with over 200 fragments of the priceless Roman Portland Vase, shattered by a drunken museum visitor.
evt-09-10-1845-john-doubleday-restorer.prompt: How do you approach putting the ancient glass vase back together?

choices.text: Glue only the largest pieces and discard the tiny fragments
Commission an entirely new glass replica to display instead
Send the fragments to Venice to be melted and recast
Painstakingly piece the fragments back together by hand over months

evt-09-10-1845-john-doubleday-restorer.butterflyEffect: Doubleday painstakingly reassembled the vase piece by piece over months, a restoration widely praised as masterly that held for over a century until a later re-restoration in 1948. His meticulous, patient method helped establish careful conservation as a serious professional discipline within museums like the British Museum.

evt-09-10-1960-athletics-at-the-1960-sum.scenario: It's the evening of 10 September 1960 in Rome. You are Abebe Bikila, an Ethiopian runner at the Olympic marathon start line, and the shoes issued to you don't fit properly.
evt-09-10-1960-athletics-at-the-1960-sum.prompt: What do you do about footwear just before the race begins?

choices.text: Withdraw from the race until proper shoes can be found
Run the race barefoot, as you had trained
Borrow a teammate's shoes even though they're the wrong size
Wear the ill-fitting shoes anyway rather than risk disqualification

evt-09-10-1960-athletics-at-the-1960-sum.butterflyEffect: Bikila ran the entire course barefoot, as he had trained, and won in world record time, becoming the first sub-Saharan African Olympic gold medalist. His victory, achieved past an obelisk taken from Ethiopia by Mussolini's Italy, became a powerful symbol of African athletic rise during decolonization, and he repeated as champion in Tokyo 1964, this time wearing shoes.

evt-09-10-1961-1961-italian-grand-prix.scenario: It's 10 September 1961 at Monza. On the second lap, Wolfgang von Trips's Ferrari touches wheels with Jim Clark's Lotus as they fight for the lead entering the fast Parabolica corner.
evt-09-10-1961-1961-italian-grand-prix.prompt: What follows from this touch of wheels at the Parabolica?

choices.text: Clark's car catches fire but he escapes unharmed
Officials halt the race and it is rescheduled for the following week
His car is launched into the crowd, killing him and fifteen spectators
Both cars spin harmlessly onto the grass and rejoin the race

evt-09-10-1961-1961-italian-grand-prix.butterflyEffect: Von Trips's car was launched into the crowd, killing him and fifteen spectators in the deadliest crash in Formula One history to that point. The tragedy cost von Trips the championship he was leading, and teammate Phil Hill won the title that day while mourning his friend. Monza's barriers and crowd safety were overhauled in the aftermath.

evt-09-10-1967-1967-gibraltar-sovereignt.scenario: It's 10 September 1967, and you are a Gibraltarian voter marking your ballot: pass under Spanish sovereignty with special status, or remain under British rule with self-governing institutions.

choices.text: Britain cancels the referendum before results are counted
Gibraltarians vote to join Spain with a special autonomous status
Gibraltarians vote overwhelmingly to remain a British dependency
The vote is too close to call and a second referendum is scheduled

evt-09-10-1967-1967-gibraltar-sovereignt.butterflyEffect: Gibraltarians voted overwhelmingly to remain British, by 12,138 votes to 44. Spain refused to recognise the result and closed the land border with Gibraltar in 1969, not reopening it fully until 1985, while Britain granted Gibraltar a new constitution affirming self-government.

evt-09-10-2000-operation-barras.scenario: It's dawn on 10 September 2000 near Rokel Creek, Sierra Leone. You are part of a British special forces and Parachute Regiment task force planning to free captured soldiers held by the 'West Side Boys' militia in two camps on opposite banks.
evt-09-10-2000-operation-barras.prompt: How should the rescue force strike to prevent the rebels reinforcing each other?

choices.text: Call in an airstrike to level both camps before advancing
Cross the creek slowly by boat under cover of darkness
Send negotiators in first to arrange a peaceful hostage exchange
Launch simultaneous helicopter assaults on both rebel camps at once

evt-09-10-2000-operation-barras.butterflyEffect: British forces launched simultaneous helicopter-borne assaults on both Gberi Bana and Magbeni, freeing all the hostages after fierce fighting that killed dozens of militants and one British soldier. The operation effectively destroyed the West Side Boys as a fighting force and boosted confidence in Britain's wider intervention, which helped bring Sierra Leone's civil war to an end by 2002.

evt-09-10-2001-charles-ingram.scenario: It's September 2001, and you're watching the taping of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? as Major Charles Ingram reaches the final, £1,000,000 question, each of his answers oddly preceded by a cough from somewhere in the audience.
evt-09-10-2001-charles-ingram.prompt: What happens after Ingram wins the jackpot?

choices.text: He donates the winnings to a military charity before leaving the studio
The show's broadcaster cancels the episode before it airs
He is celebrated live on air as only the third person to win the jackpot
Producers suspect cheating, withhold the winnings and pursue prosecution

evt-09-10-2001-charles-ingram.butterflyEffect: Producers reviewed the tapes, noticed the pattern of coughs matching correct answers, and withheld the prize. Ingram, his wife Diana and an accomplice, Tecwen Whittock, were later convicted of deception in 2003, turning the case into one of British television's most notorious scandals and inspiring the later stage play and drama Quiz.

evt-09-10-2017-hurricane-irma.scenario: It's September 10, 2017, in the Florida Keys, and Hurricane Irma is making landfall on Cudjoe Key as a powerful Category 4 storm with the eyewall closing in.
evt-09-10-2017-hurricane-irma.prompt: What is the safest action to take as the eyewall approaches?

choices.text: Try to evacuate by car once the eyewall is already arriving
Take shelter inside a mobile home for stability
Go outside to film the storm as it makes landfall
Shelter in a sturdy interior room away from windows

evt-09-10-2017-hurricane-irma.butterflyEffect: Irma devastated much of the Keys, destroying or badly damaging a huge share of homes, especially mobile homes, and caused tens of billions of dollars in damage across Florida. The storm triggered one of the largest evacuations in US history, roughly 6.5 million people, and sparked renewed debate over building codes and housing resilience in hurricane-prone areas.

evt-09-10-2024-polaris-dawn.scenario: It's September 12, 2024, and Crew Dragon has climbed to a lower orbit for the mission's big moment: the first-ever commercial spacewalk. The capsule has no airlock, so the entire cabin must be exposed to vacuum.
evt-09-10-2024-polaris-dawn.prompt: What must the whole crew do since Dragon lacks an airlock for the spacewalk?

choices.text: Attach an external inflatable airlock module before opening the hatch
All four crew members wear pressurized EVA suits and depressurize the entire cabin
Only the two spacewalkers suit up while the others wait in a separate airlock chamber
Partially depressurize the cabin just enough to crack open the hatch

evt-09-10-2024-polaris-dawn.butterflyEffect: All four crew members donned new SpaceX-designed pressurized EVA suits and depressurized the whole cabin, with Isaacman and then Gillis briefly exiting the hatch while the others remained suited inside. The suit design and data gathered were explicitly meant to inform future spacesuits for lunar and Mars missions, making this a technical stepping stone beyond a publicity milestone.

evt-09-11-1297-first-war-of-scottish-ind.scenario: It is September 11, 1297. You stand with Andrew Moray and William Wallace on high ground above the River Forth, watching the English army of the Earl of Surrey begin filing across the narrow wooden bridge below.
evt-09-11-1297-first-war-of-scottish-ind.prompt: What do you order the Scottish spearmen to do?

choices.text: Charge once enough English troops are stranded on your side
Attack before any troops cross the bridge
Withdraw north and avoid battle
Wait for the entire English army to cross before engaging

evt-09-11-1297-first-war-of-scottish-ind.butterflyEffect: The Scots struck as the bridge bottlenecked the English column, cutting the army in two and routing it; treasurer Hugh de Cressingham was killed and reportedly flayed. The victory made Wallace a national hero and Guardian of Scotland, though the war ground on for decades before independence was secured.

evt-09-11-1649-cromwellian-conquest-of-i.scenario: It is 11 September 1649. You command the garrison inside Drogheda's walls, and Oliver Cromwell's New Model Army has just breached the defenses after you refused his demand to surrender the town.
evt-09-11-1649-cromwellian-conquest-of-i.prompt: What does Cromwell order once his troops pour through the breach?

choices.text: He accepts the garrison's belated surrender and spares all lives
He allows the garrison to march out under safe passage
He agrees to ransom the town for gold and withdraws his army
He orders no quarter, and the garrison and many others in the town are killed

evt-09-11-1649-cromwellian-conquest-of-i.butterflyEffect: Cromwell gave orders that no quarter be shown; the garrison and many clergy and townspeople inside were killed in the days that followed. Drogheda became a lasting symbol of Cromwellian brutality in Irish memory, hardening resistance in some later sieges while terrifying other garrisons into swift surrender, and it shaped Anglo-Irish relations for centuries.

evt-09-11-1697-great-turkish-war.scenario: It is September 11, 1697. You ride with Prince Eugene of Savoy's army near Zenta, watching a large Ottoman force struggling to cross a pontoon bridge over the Tisza River, its army split between the two banks.
evt-09-11-1697-great-turkish-war.prompt: What do you urge Prince Eugene to order?

choices.text: Attack immediately while the Ottoman force is divided
Retreat and avoid engaging a larger force
Wait until the whole Ottoman army has crossed
Open negotiations with the Ottoman commander

evt-09-11-1697-great-turkish-war.butterflyEffect: Eugene struck at once, trapping and destroying much of the Ottoman army against the river; the Grand Vizier was among the dead. The crushing defeat forced the Ottomans toward the 1699 Treaty of Karlowitz, their first major territorial losses in Europe.

evt-09-11-1758-seven-years-war.scenario: It's September 11, 1758, on the beach at Saint-Cast in Brittany. Your British raiding force, having wrecked French coastal defenses, is now trying to re-embark under fire as French troops converge from inland.
evt-09-11-1758-seven-years-war.prompt: What happens as the British attempt to escape back to their ships?

choices.text: A negotiated truce allows safe British withdrawal
The Royal Navy destroys the French fleet offshore
The British successfully re-embark with minimal losses
French forces trap and heavily defeat them on the beach

evt-09-11-1758-seven-years-war.butterflyEffect: French forces under the Duc d'Aiguillon trapped and heavily defeated the retreating British, inflicting hundreds of casualties and captures. The disaster discredited Britain's strategy of small coastal raids on France, pushing its war effort further toward the decisive campaigns in North America and India.

evt-09-11-1776-staten-island-peace-confe.scenario: It is September 11, 1776, at Billop Manor on Staten Island. Admiral Lord Howe has invited you, John Adams, along with Benjamin Franklin and Edward Rutledge, to discuss peace — but he can only address you as private citizens, not as representatives of an independent Congress.
evt-09-11-1776-staten-island-peace-confe.prompt: How do you respond to Howe's offer of reconciliation with the Crown?

choices.text: Accept a temporary truce while colonies remain under the Crown
Insist that independence has already been declared and is not negotiable
Propose colonial representation in Parliament instead of independence
Agree to revoke the Declaration of Independence in exchange for peace

evt-09-11-1776-staten-island-peace-confe.butterflyEffect: Adams, Franklin, and Rutledge insisted independence was already declared and not open to negotiation, and the conference collapsed within hours. The war continued for seven more years until the Treaty of Paris in 1783 finally secured British recognition of American independence.

evt-09-11-1789-alexander-hamilton.scenario: It is 11 September 1789. President Washington needs someone to build the young republic's financial system from nothing and manage its war debts.
evt-09-11-1789-alexander-hamilton.prompt: Whom does Washington choose as the first Secretary of the Treasury?

choices.text: Alexander Hamilton
Thomas Jefferson
John Jay
Robert Morris

evt-09-11-1789-alexander-hamilton.butterflyEffect: Washington's choice, Alexander Hamilton, used the post to design federal assumption of state debts, a national bank, and a tax system that put the new nation's credit on solid footing. His aggressive expansion of federal power provoked Thomas Jefferson's fierce opposition, helping spark America's first party system.

evt-09-11-1851-christiana-riot.scenario: It is dawn on September 11, 1851. You stand inside William Parker's house near Christiana, Pennsylvania, as a federal marshal and slaveholder Edward Gorsuch demand you surrender four escaped slaves sheltering inside.
evt-09-11-1851-christiana-riot.prompt: Do you hand over the fugitives or make a stand?

choices.text: Negotiate a ransom for the fugitives' freedom
Take up arms and resist the marshal's posse
Flee the house and abandon the fugitives
Surrender the fugitives peacefully

evt-09-11-1851-christiana-riot.butterflyEffect: The defenders opened fire, killing Gorsuch and wounding his son; the fugitives escaped to Canada. Federal prosecutors charged dozens with treason under the Fugitive Slave Act, but a Pennsylvania jury acquitted them, exposing how unwilling Northerners were to enforce the law and deepening the sectional rift that led toward civil war.

evt-09-11-1857-nauvoo-legion.scenario: It's September 11, 1857, at Mountain Meadows in Utah Territory. You are among the militiamen who have besieged a wagon train of California-bound emigrants for days, now approaching them under a flag of truce.
evt-09-11-1857-nauvoo-legion.prompt: What order do the militia leaders give regarding the emigrants who trust the promise of safe passage?

choices.text: To hold them for ransom until federal troops arrived
To escort them safely to the next town
To let them keep their wagons and continue west unharmed
To separate and kill the emigrants despite the truce

evt-09-11-1857-nauvoo-legion.butterflyEffect: Militia leaders and allied Paiute separated and killed the emigrants after luring them out under false promises, one of the deadliest atrocities committed by American settlers against fellow settlers. The massacre was covered up for years; only militia leader John D. Lee was ever executed for it, two decades later in 1877.

evt-09-11-1893-swami-vivekananda.scenario: It is 11 September 1893 in Chicago. You are an unknown Hindu monk about to give your first address to thousands of delegates at the opening of the World's Parliament of Religions, and you must choose how to greet a hall full of strangers.
evt-09-11-1893-swami-vivekananda.prompt: How do you open your address to the assembled crowd?

choices.text: "Sisters and Brothers of America"
With a formal recitation of his teacher Ramakrishna's titles
By opening with a quotation from the Christian Bible
"Distinguished delegates and honored guests"

evt-09-11-1893-swami-vivekananda.butterflyEffect: Vivekananda's simple greeting, "Sisters and Brothers of America," drew a two-minute standing ovation and made him an overnight sensation in the American press. The moment launched his lecture tours and the founding of Vedanta Societies across the West, marking a turning point in Hinduism's recognition as a major world religion.

evt-09-11-1897-gaki-sherocho.scenario: It is September 1897 in the highlands of Kaffa. Emperor Menelik II's armies have closed in after years of resistance, and your kingdom's last strongholds are falling one by one.
evt-09-11-1897-gaki-sherocho.prompt: What actually happens to King Gaki Sherocho as Menelik's forces close in?

choices.text: His forces defeat Menelik's army and preserve independence
He is captured, and the kingdom is absorbed into Menelik's empire
He escapes into exile and rules from abroad
He negotiates lasting autonomy for Kaffa within the empire

evt-09-11-1897-gaki-sherocho.butterflyEffect: Gaki Sherocho was captured by Menelik's forces, ending the independence of the Kingdom of Kaffa and bringing it under Ethiopian imperial rule. The conquest was one of the final major expansions of Menelik's empire, folding Kaffa's people and lands into the modern Ethiopian state.

evt-09-11-1914-world-war-i.scenario: It is September 11, 1914. You wade ashore near Rabaul with the Australian Naval and Military Expeditionary Force, ordered to push inland through thick jungle toward the German wireless station at Bita Paka.
evt-09-11-1914-world-war-i.prompt: What is your unit's objective on this landing?

choices.text: Secure gold reserves from the local bank
Seize the colonial governor's residence
Capture the German wireless station
Blockade the harbor entrance

evt-09-11-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: After sharp fighting against German and native police troops, the station fell, at the cost of Australia's first combat deaths of the war. German New Guinea surrendered days later, giving Australia control of the colony for the war's duration and beyond.

evt-09-11-1941-des-moines-iowa.scenario: It is September 11, 1941. You are a reporter in the crowd at an America First rally in Des Moines, Iowa, as aviator Charles Lindbergh steps up to name the groups he blames for pushing the United States toward war.
evt-09-11-1941-des-moines-iowa.prompt: How do you report Lindbergh's remarks in tomorrow's paper?

choices.text: Refuse to cover the rally at all
Quietly omit the controversial passages
Praise the speech as patriotic without detail
Print his words in full, including the antisemitic claims

evt-09-11-1941-des-moines-iowa.butterflyEffect: Lindbergh's speech, blaming the British, the Roosevelt administration, and Jews for war agitation, was published widely and denounced as antisemitic across the press. It badly damaged the isolationist America First Committee, and three months later Pearl Harbor rendered the entire debate moot.

evt-09-11-1945-imperial-japanese-army.scenario: It's September 11, 1945, in Sarawak, Borneo. Soldiers of the Australian 9th Division approach the gates of Batu Lintang, a camp holding thousands of Allied prisoners of war and civilian internees.
evt-09-11-1945-imperial-japanese-army.prompt: What do the liberating troops find as they enter the camp?

choices.text: A camp already evacuated with no prisoners remaining
Prisoners armed and in open revolt against their guards
Guards awaiting a formal surrender ceremony with full honors
Starving survivors abandoned by guards who fled before the advance

evt-09-11-1945-imperial-japanese-army.butterflyEffect: The liberation revealed years of starvation, disease, and brutal treatment of prisoners left largely without guards as Japan's surrender took hold. Survivor testimony later helped convict several camp officials of war crimes, and Batu Lintang stands as one of the last major POW camps freed in the Pacific War.

evt-09-11-1978-1978-smallpox-outbreak-in.scenario: It is 1978, and you sit on the government panel investigating how medical photographer Janet Parker contracted smallpox despite the disease's near-eradication, tracing her illness back to a virology laboratory at the University of Birmingham.
evt-09-11-1978-1978-smallpox-outbreak-in.prompt: What does the Shooter Inquiry recommend afterward?

choices.text: No changes, since the case was an isolated incident
Tighter safety regulations for handling dangerous pathogens in labs
Mass smallpox vaccination of the entire city
Closing every virology laboratory in Britain

evt-09-11-1978-1978-smallpox-outbreak-in.butterflyEffect: The inquiry, led by R.A. Shooter, found lax containment at the lab and forced sweeping reforms to how the UK regulates hazardous pathogen research. Amid the scandal, the lab's director took his own life, and the case gave fresh urgency to the WHO's global smallpox eradication effort, certified complete in 1980.

evt-09-11-1992-hurricane-iniki.scenario: It's the morning of September 11, 1992, on Kauai. Hurricane Iniki, a Category 4 storm, has unexpectedly turned north and is now barreling straight for the island, where a Hollywood film crew is on location.
evt-09-11-1992-hurricane-iniki.prompt: What should residents and the film crew do as the storm approaches?

choices.text: Continue filming and wait out the storm on set
Take immediate shelter and evacuate low-lying coastal areas
Head out to sea to avoid the storm surge
Move to the beach for better storm photography

evt-09-11-1992-hurricane-iniki.butterflyEffect: Iniki struck Kauai directly, killing several people, destroying thousands of homes, and causing over a billion dollars in damage, the costliest hurricane in Hawaiian history at the time. The Jurassic Park cast and crew sheltered safely in a hotel, and the storm's devastation later prompted reforms to Hawaii's building codes.

evt-09-11-1995-mir-eo-19.scenario: It's June 27, 1995. You are cosmonaut Anatoly Solovyev, strapped not into a Soyuz but into the American Space Shuttle Atlantis, on your way to relieve the crew already aboard the Russian station Mir.
evt-09-11-1995-mir-eo-19.prompt: What historic first does Atlantis's docking with Mir achieve?

choices.text: The first commercial cargo delivery to Mir
The first all-female crew exchange in orbit
The first docking of a US Space Shuttle with a Russian space station
The first Soyuz docking with an American station

evt-09-11-1995-mir-eo-19.butterflyEffect: STS-71 marked the first Space Shuttle docking with a Russian space station, launching the joint Shuttle-Mir Program. Solovyev and Budarin's 75-day mission tested procedures for crew handovers and station repairs that directly shaped construction of the International Space Station.

evt-09-11-2001-september-11-attacks.scenario: It is the morning of September 11, 2001. You are the national operations manager at the FAA's command center, watching reports of hijacked airliners striking the World Trade Center and the Pentagon, with a fourth plane still unaccounted for.
evt-09-11-2001-september-11-attacks.prompt: What extraordinary order do you give to every aircraft in U.S. airspace?

choices.text: Continue normal operations while investigating the crashes
Close only the airports in New York and Washington, D.C.
Ground every aircraft in the country immediately, ordering them to land at the nearest airport
Order all flights to circle in holding patterns until threats are identified

evt-09-11-2001-september-11-attacks.butterflyEffect: The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop, the first in U.S. history, forcing thousands of planes to land immediately or divert to Canada under what became known as Operation Yellow Ribbon. The attacks killed nearly 3,000 people and led President Bush to launch the invasion of Afghanistan and a decades-long Global War on Terror.

evt-09-11-2012-central-intelligence-agen.scenario: It's the night of September 11, 2012, in Benghazi. Armed militants have overrun the nearby U.S. diplomatic compound, and gunfire is now closing in on the CIA annex where American personnel have taken shelter.
evt-09-11-2012-central-intelligence-agen.prompt: What do the security team and staff do to survive through the night?

choices.text: They immediately evacuate by land convoy to Tripoli
They call in an immediate U.S. airstrike on the attackers
They defend the annex through the night while awaiting reinforcements
They surrender the annex to negotiate a truce

evt-09-11-2012-central-intelligence-agen.butterflyEffect: The security team held the annex until a relief team arrived from Tripoli, but a mortar attack near dawn killed two CIA contractors, adding to the deaths of Ambassador Chris Stevens and a State Department officer earlier that night. The attack triggered years of congressional investigations and reshaped debates over U.S. diplomatic security policy.

evt-09-11-2024-hurricane-francine.scenario: It is September 10, 2024, and you live along the Louisiana coast. Forecasters warn that Hurricane Francine, strengthening in the Gulf of Mexico, will make landfall as a major hurricane within a day.
evt-09-11-2024-hurricane-francine.prompt: With landfall imminent, what is the safest course of action?

choices.text: Evacuate low-lying and coastal areas ahead of the storm
Stay home and board up windows against wind damage only
Move inland only if a tornado warning is issued
Wait until the storm makes landfall to decide whether to leave

evt-09-11-2024-hurricane-francine.butterflyEffect: Francine made landfall in Louisiana on September 11 as a Category 2 hurricane with 105 mph winds, bringing extensive flooding to Louisiana and Mississippi before weakening rapidly. Its formation also ended an unusually quiet stretch of Atlantic hurricane activity that had persisted through most of August.

evt-09-11-2025-jair-bolsonaro.scenario: It is 11 September 2025 in Brasília. Brazil's Supreme Court has spent months weighing evidence that former president Jair Bolsonaro plotted to overturn his 2022 election loss, culminating in the storming of Congress on 8 January 2023.
evt-09-11-2025-jair-bolsonaro.prompt: What sentence does the court hand down to Bolsonaro?

choices.text: Full acquittal on all charges
House arrest with no prison time
27 years in prison
Referral for impeachment only, with no criminal penalty

evt-09-11-2025-jair-bolsonaro.butterflyEffect: The court convicted Bolsonaro and sentenced him to 27 years in prison for his role in the attempted coup, making him the first former Brazilian president imprisoned for trying to overturn an election. The ruling tested the resilience of Brazil's democratic institutions and reshaped the country's political landscape ahead of future elections.

evt-09-12-1309-reconquista.scenario: It's September 1309, and you serve in the army of Ferdinand IV of Castile, besieging the Moorish-held Rock of Gibraltar while ships blockade its harbor to cut the garrison off from Granada and North Africa.
evt-09-12-1309-reconquista.prompt: What strategy proves decisive in forcing Gibraltar's defenders to surrender?

choices.text: Bribing the garrison commander to open the gates
A prolonged siege and naval blockade cutting off resupply
A direct night assault scaling the Rock's cliffs
A negotiated prisoner exchange for the fortress

evt-09-12-1309-reconquista.butterflyEffect: The prolonged siege and naval blockade starved the garrison into submission, giving Castile its first hold on Gibraltar. The Rock would change hands several more times over the following century before Castile's final conquest in 1462, and its strategic value later made it a prize fought over again when Britain seized it in 1704.

evt-09-12-1885-1885-86-scottish-cup.scenario: You are the captain of Arbroath F.C. on the pitch in the first round of the Scottish Cup. Your opponents, Bon Accord, arrived without their usual kit and are struggling badly against your side's relentless attack.
evt-09-12-1885-1885-86-scottish-cup.prompt: What is the final scoreline when the referee blows the whistle?
evt-09-12-1885-1885-86-scottish-cup.butterflyEffect: Arbroath won 36–0, still the largest victory margin in the history of senior football and a Guinness World Record. The lopsided result exposed flaws in the Cup's early open-entry format, which was later tightened with regional qualifying rounds to prevent such mismatches.

evt-09-12-1910-gustav-mahler.scenario: It is the evening of 12 September 1910 in Munich's vast new Festhalle. Gustav Mahler stands before an enormous orchestra, eight vocal soloists, and two choirs of hundreds of singers, about to conduct the premiere of his mammoth Eighth Symphony.
evt-09-12-1910-gustav-mahler.prompt: How does the packed audience react when the final chord dies away?

choices.text: They walk out in protest at its length
They erupt into a prolonged standing ovation
Critics boo the choral finale as excessive
They sit in stunned, respectful silence

evt-09-12-1910-gustav-mahler.butterflyEffect: The premiere was a sensational triumph, drawing a thunderous, sustained ovation and cementing Mahler's fame as a composer during his own lifetime. It proved to be the last premiere he ever personally conducted; he died less than eight months later, and his music would only reach its widest audience decades afterward.

evt-09-12-1928-1928-okeechobee-hurricane.scenario: You farm the rich muck soil near the shore of Lake Okeechobee, Florida. Word spreads that a massive hurricane, already deadly in the Caribbean, is bearing down, and the low earthen dike protecting your community was never built to withstand a major storm surge.
evt-09-12-1928-1928-okeechobee-hurricane.prompt: What should you do as the storm closes in on the lake?

choices.text: Evacuate immediately to higher ground
Reinforce the dike with sandbags yourself
Wait for official word before moving
Stay to protect your crops and livestock

evt-09-12-1928-1928-okeechobee-hurricane.butterflyEffect: Many residents, mostly Black migrant farmworkers, had little warning and no way to evacuate; the dike failed and floodwaters killed thousands, making it one of the deadliest disasters in U.S. history. The catastrophe forced the federal government to build the much stronger Herbert Hoover Dike and reshaped U.S. flood-control and disaster-warning policy for decades.

evt-09-12-1933-leo-szilard.scenario: It is 12 September 1933 in London. You are physicist Leo Szilard, a Hungarian refugee, waiting at a traffic light on Southampton Row after reading Ernest Rutherford's dismissal in the Times of atomic energy as "moonshine." An idea about a self-sustaining nuclear reaction strikes you as the light changes.
evt-09-12-1933-leo-szilard.prompt: What do you do to protect and preserve this idea?

choices.text: File a patent and keep the details confidential
Dismiss it as impractical speculation and move on
Announce it publicly at once to claim credit
Publish the idea immediately in a physics journal

evt-09-12-1933-leo-szilard.butterflyEffect: Szilard filed a patent on the neutron-induced chain reaction in 1934 and later assigned it secretly to the British Admiralty to keep it out of hostile hands. The concept underpinned his 1939 Einstein–Szilard letter to Roosevelt, which helped launch the Manhattan Project and the atomic bomb.

evt-09-12-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 12 September 1942 on Guadalcanal. You are Marine Lieutenant Colonel Merritt Edson, holding a grassy ridge just south of Henderson Field as Japanese forces under General Kawaguchi press a fierce night assault to retake the vital airstrip.
evt-09-12-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: How do you reposition your exhausted men to survive the coming main assault?

choices.text: Withdraw to a shorter, tighter defensive line on the ridge crest
Request immediate evacuation of the airfield garrison
Hold the original extended line at all costs
Abandon the ridge entirely and fall back to the beach

evt-09-12-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Edson pulled his battered force back into a tighter perimeter on the ridge crest, allowing artillery and reserves to concentrate fire and break the main Japanese attack the next night. The ridge became known as "Bloody Ridge," Henderson Field remained in American hands, and Edson later received the Medal of Honor for the defense.

evt-09-12-1952-flatwoods-west-virginia.scenario: It is dusk in Flatwoods, West Virginia. You and a group of local boys chase a fiery light you saw fall onto a nearby hilltop, flashlights in hand, when a towering figure with a glowing, hissing face rises out of the darkness before you.
evt-09-12-1952-flatwoods-west-virginia.prompt: What do you do when the strange figure looms over the group?

choices.text: Flee back down the hill
Throw rocks at it
Approach it to get a closer look
Try to speak to it calmly

evt-09-12-1952-flatwoods-west-virginia.butterflyEffect: The group fled screaming and reported the encounter to authorities, sparking one of America's most famous cryptid legends, the Flatwoods Monster (or Braxton County Monster). The story fed the growing 1950s wave of UFO and creature sightings and remains a staple of American folklore and paranormal television to this day.

evt-09-12-1962-we-choose-to-go-to-the-mo.scenario: It is a sweltering afternoon on 12 September 1962. You sit in the packed stands of Rice Stadium in Houston as President John F. Kennedy takes the podium to defend the enormous cost of the race to the Moon.
evt-09-12-1962-we-choose-to-go-to-the-mo.prompt: What reason does Kennedy give the crowd for choosing this immense national effort?

choices.text: Because it will be profitable for private industry
Because it is strictly necessary for national defense
Because scientists demand it regardless of cost
Because it is hard, and hard things prove what a nation can do

evt-09-12-1962-we-choose-to-go-to-the-mo.butterflyEffect: Kennedy declared the nation chose to go to the Moon "not because it is easy, but because it is hard," reframing the space race as a test of national will rather than mere technology. The line became one of the most quoted defenses of ambitious public science funding, sustaining political support for Apollo through the decade until the 1969 landing.

evt-09-12-1983-boricua-popular-army.scenario: It's the early hours of September 12, 1983, and you are part of a clandestine Los Macheteros cell preparing to rob a Wells Fargo depot in West Hartford, Connecticut, to help finance the movement for Puerto Rican independence.
evt-09-12-1983-boricua-popular-army.prompt: Roughly how much does the operation net, making it one of the largest heists in U.S. history?

choices.text: About $7.2 million, one of the largest robberies in U.S. history
About $500,000 in cash and bonds
About $50 million in gold reserves
About $2 million split among several safe houses

evt-09-12-1983-boricua-popular-army.butterflyEffect: The robbery, orchestrated by Victor Gerena, netted about $7.2 million and triggered one of the FBI's largest and costliest investigations. Gerena fled to Cuba and remains on the FBI's Most Wanted list decades later, while several Machetero members were later convicted, and the case became a landmark in the movement's history.

evt-09-12-1992-space-shuttle-endeavour.scenario: It's September 12, 1992, and you are strapped into Space Shuttle Endeavour on mission STS-47, part of a crew of scientists and engineers about to spend eight days running experiments in microgravity.
evt-09-12-1992-space-shuttle-endeavour.prompt: What historic first does mission specialist Mae Jemison achieve on this flight?

choices.text: She becomes the first Black woman to travel into space
She becomes the first person to perform surgery in orbit
She becomes the first African American to walk in space
She becomes the first woman to command a shuttle mission

evt-09-12-1992-space-shuttle-endeavour.butterflyEffect: Jemison became the first Black woman to travel into space, spending eight days aboard Endeavour conducting life-science experiments. Her flight made her a lasting symbol in the push for diversity in STEM and the astronaut corps, and she went on to found science-education initiatives inspired by the mission.

evt-09-12-2008-2008-chatsworth-train-col.scenario: It's 4:22 p.m. on September 12, 2008, and you are the engineer of a Metrolink commuter train approaching a signal in the Chatsworth neighborhood of Los Angeles, exchanging text messages with a teenage rail enthusiast as you near the crossing.
evt-09-12-2008-2008-chatsworth-train-col.prompt: What should you do right now to prevent a catastrophe ahead?

choices.text: Radio dispatch to request permission before slowing
Continue texting since the signal is likely green
Put down the phone and stop at the red signal ahead
Slow slightly but proceed through without stopping

evt-09-12-2008-2008-chatsworth-train-col.butterflyEffect: The engineer, distracted by texting, missed a red signal and collided head-on with an oncoming Union Pacific freight train, killing 25 people and injuring over 100. The disaster prompted Congress to pass the Rail Safety Improvement Act of 2008, mandating Positive Train Control on major U.S. rail lines and banning cell phone use by on-duty engineers.

evt-09-12-2014-synagogue-church-of-all-n.scenario: It's early September 2014, and you are inspecting a multi-story guesthouse under construction at the Synagogue Church of All Nations in Lagos, where foreign pilgrims are due to stay ahead of upcoming services.
evt-09-12-2014-synagogue-church-of-all-n.prompt: What structural concern should you flag as an urgent risk before allowing guests inside?

choices.text: The building's distance from the main sanctuary
Extra floors added without proper structural reinforcement
The lack of air conditioning in the guest rooms
The absence of decorative finishes on the facade

evt-09-12-2014-synagogue-church-of-all-n.butterflyEffect: On September 12 the guesthouse collapsed, killing 115 people, most of them South African pilgrims, in one of Nigeria's deadliest building disasters. Investigators pointed to additional floors added without adequate structural support, though the church's leader controversially claimed a low-flying aircraft was to blame, and the tragedy intensified scrutiny of building safety enforcement in Lagos.

evt-09-13-bce509-temple-of-jupiter-optim.scenario: It is the first year of the new Roman Republic, 509 BCE. The great temple to Jupiter on the Capitoline Hill, begun by the exiled King Tarquinius Superbus, stands nearly finished, and the new government must decide what to do with a king's unfinished monument.
evt-09-13-bce509-temple-of-jupiter-optim.prompt: What does the new Republic do with the almost-completed royal temple?

choices.text: Demolish it as a symbol of tyranny
Leave it sealed until a new king is chosen
Complete it and have a consul dedicate it to Jupiter
Dedicate it in the exiled king's name to honor him

evt-09-13-bce509-temple-of-jupiter-optim.butterflyEffect: The temple was completed and dedicated by consul Marcus Horatius Pulvillus, deliberately severing it from royal memory and making it a symbol of the Republic itself. It became Rome's most sacred site, the endpoint of triumphal processions, and was rebuilt after fires for centuries as the city's religious heart.

evt-09-13-533-belisarius.scenario: It is September 533, and you march with Belisarius toward Carthage as Vandal King Gelimer springs a three-pronged ambush at Ad Decimum. The Vandal attack begins to unravel before your eyes.
evt-09-13-533-belisarius.prompt: What let Belisarius's smaller force defeat the Vandals at Ad Decimum?

choices.text: The Vandals' uncoordinated attack collapsed before it could unite
Belisarius deployed war elephants against the Vandal cavalry
A Vandal general defected with his troops mid-battle
A Byzantine fleet bombarded the Vandal lines from the coast

evt-09-13-533-belisarius.butterflyEffect: Gelimer's brother Ammatas attacked too early and was killed, and a separate Vandal force under his nephew was routed before the main armies even met, letting Belisarius destroy the disorganized Vandals piecemeal. The victory opened the road to Carthage, which fell days later, and led to the collapse of the Vandal Kingdom and its absorption into Justinian's reconquered empire.

evt-09-13-1541-john-calvin.scenario: You sit on Geneva's city council in September 1541, watching John Calvin step back into the city after three years of exile, ready to reshape how the Reformed church there is run.
evt-09-13-1541-john-calvin.prompt: What framework did Calvin draw up to govern morals and doctrine in Geneva?

choices.text: The Edict of Nantes, granting toleration to Protestants
The Thirty-Nine Articles, defining Anglican belief
The Augsburg Confession, defining Lutheran doctrine
The Ecclesiastical Ordinances, establishing a Consistory to oversee church discipline

evt-09-13-1541-john-calvin.butterflyEffect: Calvin's Ecclesiastical Ordinances created a Consistory of pastors and elders empowered to police both belief and behaviour, fusing civic and religious life in Geneva. The city became a training ground for Reformed pastors sent across Europe, spreading Calvinism into France, Scotland, and the Netherlands.

evt-09-13-1567-siege-of-inabayama-castle.scenario: It's 1567, and you serve among the Saitō clan's generals defending Inabayama Castle. As Oda Nobunaga's army closes in, several fellow commanders—later known as the Mino Triumvirate—are weighing whether to abandon Saitō Tatsuoki's cause.
evt-09-13-1567-siege-of-inabayama-castle.prompt: What do these wavering Saitō generals ultimately decide to do?

choices.text: Fight to the death defending Tatsuoki
Surrender the castle directly to a rival Saitō heir
Defect to Nobunaga's side before the final assault
Flee Mino Province entirely

evt-09-13-1567-siege-of-inabayama-castle.butterflyEffect: They defected to Nobunaga, fatally weakening the castle's defenses from within. Nobunaga captured Inabayama, renamed the town Gifu, and made it his base for the campaigns that would carry him toward unifying Japan.

evt-09-13-1759-french-and-indian-war.scenario: Dawn, 13 September 1759. You are General James Wolfe outside Quebec, having secretly landed your troops below the cliffs during the night, hoping to finally force the French into open battle.
evt-09-13-1759-french-and-indian-war.prompt: What do you order next to draw Montcalm's army out of the city?

choices.text: Bombard the city walls indefinitely
Wait for reinforcements from Louisbourg
Form a line of battle on the Plains of Abraham
Retreat to the ships before daylight

evt-09-13-1759-french-and-indian-war.butterflyEffect: Wolfe marched his men up onto the Plains of Abraham and formed a battle line before the walls. The short, decisive fight left both Wolfe and the French commander Montcalm mortally wounded, and Quebec's fall paved the way for British control of Canada under the 1763 Treaty of Paris.

evt-09-13-1814-war-of-1812.scenario: It is the night of 13–14 September 1814. You watch from a ship in Baltimore's harbor as British warships bombard Fort McHenry for over twenty-four hours straight, the sky lit by exploding shells.
evt-09-13-1814-war-of-1812.prompt: What do you see at dawn that moves you to write a poem?

choices.text: A British flag raised over the ruins
The fort completely destroyed and silent
The American flag still flying over the fort
No flag visible through the smoke

evt-09-13-1814-war-of-1812.butterflyEffect: The huge American flag was still flying over Fort McHenry, proof the fort had survived the bombardment. Francis Scott Key's poem, later set to music as "The Star-Spangled Banner," became America's national anthem in 1931, permanently linking this single night to national identity.

evt-09-13-1848-phineas-gage.scenario: It's September 13, 1848, near Cavendish, Vermont. An accidental explosion has just driven a 13-pound iron tamping rod clean through railroad foreman Phineas Gage's skull, and as the attending physician you must decide how to treat him.
evt-09-13-1848-phineas-gage.prompt: What did Dr. John Harlow actually do to treat Gage's wound?

choices.text: Sedate Gage permanently and abandon further treatment
Amputate the damaged portion of the skull entirely
Perform immediate exploratory brain surgery
Clean the wound, remove loose bone fragments, and let it drain while watching for infection

evt-09-13-1848-phineas-gage.butterflyEffect: Harlow's conservative treatment let Gage survive, but his altered temperament afterward became one of the earliest documented links between the frontal lobe and personality. The case still anchors neuroscience discussions of brain injury and behavior today.

evt-09-13-1919-boston-police-strike.scenario: It is September 13, 1919, and you are a Boston police officer who walked out days earlier over union recognition and wages. The state militia now patrols the streets, and Governor Calvin Coolidge must decide how to end the standoff.
evt-09-13-1919-boston-police-strike.prompt: What did Coolidge do about the striking officers seeking to return to duty?

choices.text: He ordered federal mediation to resolve the dispute
He refused to rehire any of the striking officers
He recognized the officers' union as requested
He negotiated a compromise wage increase to end the strike

evt-09-13-1919-boston-police-strike.butterflyEffect: Coolidge refused to reinstate any of the striking officers, declaring there was "no right to strike against the public safety." His hard line won national acclaim for restoring order, propelling him onto the 1920 Republican ticket as vice president and eventually into the presidency.

evt-09-13-1959-luna-2.scenario: It is 1959, and you are a Soviet engineer tracking the Luna 2 probe as it closes in on the Moon after days of travel through space.
evt-09-13-1959-luna-2.prompt: What happens when Luna 2 reaches the lunar surface?

choices.text: It orbits the Moon and returns to Earth
It performs a gentle soft landing
It burns up before reaching the surface
It crashes into the surface, releasing Soviet pennants

evt-09-13-1959-luna-2.butterflyEffect: Luna 2 struck the Moon at high speed, scattering Soviet pennants across the surface and becoming the first human-made object to touch another celestial body. The feat was a major propaganda win in the space race, intensifying American urgency that eventually fed into the Apollo program.

evt-09-13-1971-project-571.scenario: It is 13 September 1971. You are aboard a Chinese air force Trident jet with Lin Biao, Mao's designated successor, fleeing China after a plot against Mao has unraveled and loyalists close in.
evt-09-13-1971-project-571.prompt: Where does Lin Biao order the plane to fly?

choices.text: Vietnam
Hong Kong
The Soviet Union
Taiwan

evt-09-13-1971-project-571.butterflyEffect: The plane headed toward the Soviet Union but ran out of fuel and crashed in Mongolia, killing everyone aboard, including Lin Biao and his family. Mao used the affair to purge Lin's military allies, reshaping Chinese Communist Party politics in the years leading up to Mao's death in 1976.

evt-09-13-1979-venda-bantustan.scenario: You are a Venda official in September 1979, standing before crowds as Pretoria formally declares your homeland an independent republic under South Africa's apartheid policy of separate development.
evt-09-13-1979-venda-bantustan.prompt: How did the world beyond South Africa respond to Venda's declared independence?

choices.text: No country other than South Africa and its other Bantustans recognised it
Britain and the United States granted diplomatic recognition
The United Nations admitted Venda as a member state
Neighbouring African states recognised it to weaken South Africa

evt-09-13-1979-venda-bantustan.butterflyEffect: No government beyond South Africa and its fellow Bantustans, Transkei, Bophuthatswana, and Ciskei, ever recognised Venda, and the UN General Assembly condemned the 'independence' as an attempt to entrench apartheid. Venda's people remained South African citizens in international eyes, and the homeland was reincorporated into South Africa when apartheid ended in 1994.

evt-09-13-1987-goiania-accident.scenario: You run a small scrapyard in Goiânia, Brazil. Two men have just sold you a strange lead-and-steel canister salvaged from an abandoned hospital, and inside you find crystals glowing an eerie blue in the dark.
evt-09-13-1987-goiania-accident.prompt: What do you actually do with the glowing capsule?

choices.text: Share it with family and neighbors as a curiosity
Sell it intact to another buyer
Report it immediately to civil defense authorities
Bury it far from the scrapyard

evt-09-13-1987-goiania-accident.butterflyEffect: Ferreira shared the glowing caesium-137 with his family, neighbors, and workers, fascinated by its beauty, leading to widespread contamination that killed four people and required decontamination of hundreds of homes.
