The disaster became a landmark case in radiological safety, prompting the IAEA and national governments worldwide to tighten controls over abandoned and orphaned radioactive sources.

evt-09-13-1988-hurricane-gilbert.scenario: You are a resident of Kingston, Jamaica on 12 September 1988, as Hurricane Gilbert, now a Category 5 storm, bears down on the island with winds tearing at rooftops.
evt-09-13-1988-hurricane-gilbert.prompt: What is the safest action as the storm's eye approaches your neighbourhood?

choices.text: Wait for the eye to pass, then drive inland
Leave for a designated shelter well away from the coast
Stay home to guard your belongings from looters
Climb to the highest floor of your house and remain there

evt-09-13-1988-hurricane-gilbert.butterflyEffect: Gilbert tore across Jamaica, destroying tens of thousands of homes and knocking out power and phone lines across most of the island before crossing the Yucatán Peninsula and striking Mexico. Its central pressure of 888 mb made it the most intense Atlantic hurricane on record at the time, a mark it held until 2005's Hurricane Wilma.

evt-09-13-1993-nirvana-band.scenario: It is 1993 and you are an executive at Geffen Records, listening to Steve Albini's raw, unpolished mix of Kurt Cobain's new album. The label worries it is too abrasive to follow the massive success of Nevermind.
evt-09-13-1993-nirvana-band.prompt: How did Cobain respond to pressure over the album's harsh sound?

choices.text: He brought in producer Scott Litt to remix two songs for radio
He scrapped the album and started over from scratch
He delayed the release by a full year
He fired Albini and rerecorded the entire record

evt-09-13-1993-nirvana-band.butterflyEffect: Cobain agreed to let R.E.M. producer Scott Litt remix two tracks for radio play while leaving the rest of Albini's raw production intact. In Utero still debuted at number one, proving Cobain could reject pop polish on his own terms just months before his death.

evt-09-13-1993-yitzhak-rabin.scenario: You stand on the White House lawn on 13 September 1993, watching Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin hesitate for a long, tense moment before PLO leader Yasser Arafat extends his hand.
evt-09-13-1993-yitzhak-rabin.prompt: What does Rabin do, sealing the Oslo Accords before the world's cameras?

choices.text: Signs the agreement but avoids the photo opportunity
Shakes Arafat's hand in front of the cameras
Refuses the handshake and walks away
Insists Arafat bow before shaking hands

evt-09-13-1993-yitzhak-rabin.butterflyEffect: Rabin shook Arafat's hand, a historic gesture of mutual recognition between Israel and the PLO that launched the Oslo peace process. Two years later, in November 1995, Rabin was assassinated by an Israeli extremist opposed to the accords, and the peace process he had championed stalled without full resolution.

evt-09-13-1997-german-air-force.scenario: You are an air traffic controller tracking flights over the Atlantic off the coast of Namibia on 13 September 1997, as a German Air Force Tupolev Tu-154 and a US Air Force C-141 Starlifter converge on the same corridor at night.
evt-09-13-1997-german-air-force.prompt: What ultimately caused the two aircraft to collide in mid-air?

choices.text: A navigation satellite outage caused both crews to lose position data
Severe turbulence pushed the planes into each other
A sudden engine failure forced one aircraft off its assigned course
A breakdown in altitude coordination left both aircraft flying the same airspace

evt-09-13-1997-german-air-force.butterflyEffect: The two aircraft, carrying German and American personnel toward a joint exercise in South Africa, collided and crashed into the sea, killing everyone aboard both planes. The disaster prompted reviews of transatlantic military flight coordination and renewed pressure for wider fitting of collision-avoidance systems on military transports.

evt-09-13-2001-september-11-attacks.scenario: It is September 13, 2001. American airspace has been shut for three days after the attacks, and you are a gate agent as the FAA finally clears planes to fly again. Passengers crowd the terminal, but the checkpoint rules have changed overnight.
evt-09-13-2001-september-11-attacks.prompt: What new restriction greeted travelers as flights resumed?

choices.text: Free upgrades were offered to calm nervous fliers
Flights resumed with no changes to prior procedures
Only ticketed passengers were permitted past security checkpoints
Passports became mandatory for all domestic travel

evt-09-13-2001-september-11-attacks.butterflyEffect: Only ticketed passengers were allowed past security, curbside and gate access tightened, and armed air marshals expanded. Within two months Congress created the Transportation Security Administration, federalizing airport screening nationwide and permanently reshaping how Americans fly.

evt-09-13-2007-declaration-on-the-rights.scenario: You are a delegate at the UN General Assembly on September 13, 2007, casting a vote on the non-binding Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples. Most nations support it, but a handful of delegations signal opposition.
evt-09-13-2007-declaration-on-the-rights.prompt: Which four countries voted against adopting the declaration?

choices.text: France, Germany, Spain, and Italy
Australia, Canada, New Zealand, and the United States
Brazil, Mexico, Peru, and Chile
Russia, China, India, and Japan

evt-09-13-2007-declaration-on-the-rights.butterflyEffect: Australia, Canada, New Zealand, and the United States opposed it, citing concerns over land and resource rights. All four later reversed course and endorsed the declaration between 2009 and 2010, and it became a widely cited framework for indigenous rights advocacy despite lacking binding force.

evt-09-13-2008-delhi.scenario: It is early evening on 13 September 2008, and you are browsing stalls in Delhi's crowded Karol Bagh market when a string of bombs hidden in dustbins begins detonating across the city within minutes of each other.
evt-09-13-2008-delhi.prompt: Which group later claimed responsibility for the coordinated Delhi bombings?

choices.text: Khalistan Commando Force
Lashkar-e-Taiba
Indian Mujahideen
Communist Party of India (Maoist)

evt-09-13-2008-delhi.butterflyEffect: The Indian Mujahideen claimed the attacks by email minutes before the blasts, part of a wave of bombings the group carried out that year. The investigation, combined with the Mumbai attacks two months later, pushed India to create the National Investigation Agency in 2009 to handle terrorism cases nationally.

evt-09-13-2013-taliban.scenario: You are an Afghan guard posted outside the US consulate in Herat on the morning of 13 September 2013, when a truck bomb explodes at the perimeter and gunmen rush the breach.
evt-09-13-2013-taliban.prompt: What was the outcome as Afghan security forces responded to the assault?

choices.text: Afghan police and guards killed the attackers before they reached consulate staff
The consulate was destroyed and permanently closed that day
All American personnel were evacuated by helicopter under fire
The attackers held the compound for several hours before surrendering

evt-09-13-2013-taliban.butterflyEffect: Afghan security forces and consulate guards killed all the attackers in the gun battle that followed the bombing, and no American staff were killed. The assault, coming as coalition forces prepared to draw down ahead of 2014, underlined how deeply the insurgency still reached into western Afghanistan.

evt-09-14-1914-hmas-ae1.scenario: You are one of 35 officers and men aboard HMAS AE1, Australia's first submarine, patrolling waters off New Britain in September 1914 to help secure the German colony there. The sea is calm and the mission seems routine as you head back toward the depot ship.
evt-09-14-1914-hmas-ae1.prompt: What actually happened to AE1 after this patrol?

choices.text: She was intercepted and captured by a German gunboat
She returned safely to her depot ship that evening
She vanished without trace, her fate unknown for over 100 years
She was scuttled deliberately after running aground

evt-09-14-1914-hmas-ae1.butterflyEffect: AE1 vanished with all hands on 14 September 1914, becoming the Allies' first submarine loss of the First World War. The cause remained a mystery for over a century until wreckage was finally located near the Duke of York Islands in December 2017, closing one of the Royal Australian Navy's oldest unsolved cases.

evt-09-14-1940-ip-massacre.scenario: It is September 1940 in Northern Transylvania, recently transferred to Hungary. Two Hungarian soldiers have just died in an accidental explosion near the village of Ip, and false rumors are spreading through the ranks that ethnic Romanians were responsible.
evt-09-14-1940-ip-massacre.prompt: What eventually followed for those responsible for the massacre that resulted?

choices.text: The Romanian government formally endorsed the reprisal
Hungary awarded the soldiers involved official commendations
The killings were never investigated by any authority
Several officers involved were later tried for war crimes

evt-09-14-1940-ip-massacre.butterflyEffect: Hungarian troops massacred around 150 ethnic Romanian villagers in reprisal for a death they had not caused. After the war, several of the officers involved were tried for war crimes at postwar tribunals examining atrocities committed in wartime Transylvania, part of the broader reckoning with wartime violence in the region.

evt-09-14-2001-washington-national-cathe.scenario: It's September 14, 2001, and you sit inside Washington National Cathedral among three former presidents, watching President Bush rise to speak at the National Day of Prayer and Remembrance three days after the attacks.
evt-09-14-2001-washington-national-cathe.prompt: What did President Bush declare in his address that day?

choices.text: Plans for immediate full military mobilization
A call for a global ceasefire and diplomacy
An immediate declaration of war against Afghanistan
That the conflict would end 'at an hour of our choosing'

evt-09-14-2001-washington-national-cathe.butterflyEffect: Bush vowed the conflict 'was begun on the timing and terms of others; it will end in a way, and at an hour, of our choosing,' setting the resolute tone that would frame the coming War on Terror. Weeks later, the United States launched its invasion of Afghanistan.

evt-09-14-2003-kumba-yala.scenario: It is September 2003 in Bissau. Months of unpaid salaries and political deadlock have left President Kumba Ialá isolated, and soldiers under General Veríssimo Correia Seabra move to surround the presidential palace.
evt-09-14-2003-kumba-yala.prompt: What followed for President Ialá after the military moved against him?

choices.text: He was deposed and a transitional government took power
The country descended immediately into civil war
He crushed the coup and remained president
Portuguese troops intervened to restore him

evt-09-14-2003-kumba-yala.butterflyEffect: Ialá was deposed without bloodshed and a transitional civilian government under businessman Henrique Rosa was installed. Elections followed in 2005, but the coup set a pattern of military intervention that continued to destabilize Guinea-Bissau's politics for years afterward.

evt-09-14-2007-2008-financial-crisis.scenario: It's 14 September 2007, and news breaks that the Bank of England has granted Northern Rock emergency liquidity support. You're a depositor watching an anxious queue form outside your local branch.
evt-09-14-2007-2008-financial-crisis.prompt: What do worried depositors do in the days that follow?

choices.text: Keep their savings in place, trusting the bank
Convert their savings into gold
Withdraw their funds, triggering a full-scale bank run
Buy more Northern Rock shares

evt-09-14-2007-2008-financial-crisis.butterflyEffect: Depositors rushed to withdraw their savings, producing Britain's first bank run in over a century. The run deepened until Northern Rock was nationalized in February 2008, prompting the UK to overhaul its deposit protection guarantees.

evt-09-14-2008-aeroflot-flight-821.scenario: It's the dark early morning of 14 September 2008, and you are in the cockpit of Aeroflot Flight 821 descending toward Perm. The horizon has vanished into blackness, and the crew's sense of the aircraft's attitude is starting to slip.
evt-09-14-2008-aeroflot-flight-821.prompt: What should the crew do once they lose visual reference and become spatially disoriented?

choices.text: Radio the tower and wait for further instructions before acting
Disengage the autopilot and fly by feel toward the runway lights
Continue the descent at the same rate
Trust the instruments and execute a go-around to a safe altitude

evt-09-14-2008-aeroflot-flight-821.butterflyEffect: Instead of climbing away, the crew disengaged the autopilot and lost control in the dark, killing all 88 aboard, including a former Russian general. Investigators cited crew impairment and disorientation, and the damaged airline, Aeroflot-Nord, was rebranded as Nordavia soon after.

evt-09-14-2015-ligo.scenario: You are a physicist on the LIGO team on 14 September 2015 when both detectors, thousands of kilometres apart in Louisiana and Washington, register an identical, fleeting chirp within milliseconds of each other. It looks exactly like the signature theorists predicted for colliding black holes.
evt-09-14-2015-ligo.prompt: What does the team do before telling the world what they've found?

choices.text: Dismiss it as instrument noise and move on
Spend months verifying the signal before any public announcement
Announce the discovery to the press within hours
Keep the finding classified indefinitely

evt-09-14-2015-ligo.butterflyEffect: LIGO scientists spent nearly five months cross-checking the signal before announcing on 11 February 2016 that they had detected gravitational waves from two black holes merging 1.3 billion light-years away. The discovery confirmed a century-old prediction of Einstein's, opened the field of gravitational-wave astronomy, and earned three LIGO founders the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics.

evt-09-14-2019-yemen.scenario: It's 14 September 2019, and drone and missile strikes have just crippled Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq and Khurais facilities, wiping out roughly half the kingdom's oil output overnight. You're an Aramco official trying to keep exports flowing.
evt-09-14-2019-yemen.prompt: What did Saudi Arabia do to offset the sudden loss of production?

choices.text: Draw down strategic oil reserves to maintain exports
Cancel Aramco's planned stock listing permanently
Request American airstrikes inside Yemen at once
Immediately halt all oil exports indefinitely

evt-09-14-2019-yemen.butterflyEffect: Aramco drew on strategic reserves and repaired facilities faster than expected, restoring output within weeks, but oil prices still posted their biggest single-day jump in decades. The attack, claimed by the Houthis but blamed by Washington on Iran, sharpened Gulf tensions that simmered for years afterward.

evt-09-15-1462-ottoman-conquest-of-lesbo.scenario: It is September 1462, and you are Niccolò Gattilusio, Genoese lord of Lesbos, watching Sultan Mehmed II's Ottoman army and fleet tighten their siege around your fortress at Mytilene.
evt-09-15-1462-ottoman-conquest-of-lesbo.prompt: With the walls of Mytilene surrounded and no relief in sight, what do you do?

choices.text: Appeal to Venice to break the siege
Fight to the last man rather than yield
Surrender the fortress to the Sultan
Slip away to Genoa to raise a relief fleet

evt-09-15-1462-ottoman-conquest-of-lesbo.butterflyEffect: Niccolò surrendered, and the island's remaining forts followed suit, ending nearly a century of Genoese Gattilusio rule in the northeastern Aegean. The conquest also set the stage for the First Ottoman–Venetian War, which broke out the following year as Venice grew alarmed at Ottoman expansion.

evt-09-15-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is September 15, 1776. You are a Continental Army soldier posted near Kip's Bay on Manhattan Island as British warships open a thunderous bombardment ahead of a landing force.
evt-09-15-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: When the British troops come ashore, what does the shaken American militia do?

choices.text: Stand their ground and repel the landing
Launch a cavalry counterattack on the beachhead
Flee in disorder, abandoning the position
Surrender en masse to the British commanders

evt-09-15-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: The militia broke and fled in panic, leaving the landing unopposed and forcing Washington to hastily evacuate Manhattan, reportedly enraging him at the sight of his own men running. The British occupied New York City for the rest of the war, a major strategic loss for the American cause.

evt-09-15-1791-olympe-de-gouges.scenario: Paris, 1791. The revolutionary government has enshrined the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen, but you notice its promises of liberty and equality apply only to men.
evt-09-15-1791-olympe-de-gouges.prompt: What do you write and publish in response?

choices.text: A petition limiting voting rights to propertied men only
A treatise defending women's exclusion from public life
A pamphlet calling for restoration of the monarchy
The Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen

evt-09-15-1791-olympe-de-gouges.butterflyEffect: Olympe de Gouges published the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen, arguing women held the same natural rights as men, including within marriage. She was guillotined in 1793 for her political writings, but her declaration survived as a founding text later invoked by feminist and suffrage movements across the world.

evt-09-15-1795-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: It is 1795, and you command a British squadron off the Cape of Good Hope. The Netherlands has fallen under French-backed control, and the Dutch governor at the Cape refuses to hand the colony over peacefully.
evt-09-15-1795-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What does Britain do to secure the Cape Colony?

choices.text: Withdraw the fleet and leave the Dutch governor in charge
Hand the colony to Portugal for safekeeping
Seize the colony by force to secure the route to India
Ally with the Dutch garrison to resist the French together

evt-09-15-1795-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: British forces seized the Cape by force at Muizenberg, denying France a foothold on the vital sea route to India. Though briefly returned to the Dutch in 1803, Britain retook it in 1806 and kept it permanently, reshaping southern African history for the next century.

evt-09-15-1821-act-of-independence-of-ce.scenario: It is the night of 15 September 1821 in Guatemala City. News has just arrived that Mexico has broken from Spain, and the Provincial Council is meeting in emergency session to decide Central America's fate.
evt-09-15-1821-act-of-independence-of-ce.prompt: What does the council resolve to do with the other provinces of the captaincy general?

choices.text: Invite the other provinces to send envoys to a congress on independence
Pledge continued loyalty to the Spanish crown
Request a Spanish prince to rule as constitutional monarch
Immediately declare annexation to the Mexican Empire

evt-09-15-1821-act-of-independence-of-ce.butterflyEffect: The council invited the other provinces to send envoys to a congress deciding the region's future. That congress soon voted to annex Central America to the Mexican Empire, but the union collapsed within a year, and by 1823 the provinces broke away to form the Federal Republic of Central America, which itself splintered into five separate nations by 1841.

evt-09-15-1830-liverpool-and-manchester-.scenario: You are a guest of honor at Parkside station on opening day of the Liverpool and Manchester Railway, 15 September 1830, as locomotives pass along the newly laid double track.
evt-09-15-1830-liverpool-and-manchester-.prompt: What tragic event mars the celebrations?

choices.text: A bridge along the route collapses under a train
The opening proceeds without any incident at all
A dignitary is struck and killed by a passing locomotive
A locomotive boiler explodes, injuring the crowd

evt-09-15-1830-liverpool-and-manchester-.butterflyEffect: MP William Huskisson stepped onto the track and was struck and fatally injured by Stephenson's Rocket, becoming one of the first widely reported railway fatalities. The tragedy, rushed to Stephenson himself driving Huskisson toward medical help, only heightened public fascination with the new technology rather than deterring it.

evt-09-15-1974-air-vietnam-flight-706.scenario: You are the flight crew of Air Vietnam Flight 706 on 15 September 1974, hijackers now inside the cockpit as you bring the Boeing 727 down toward Phan Rang Air Base under their orders.
evt-09-15-1974-air-vietnam-flight-706.prompt: What does the crew attempt as the hijackers press their demands?

choices.text: Divert calmly to Saigon's main airport
Continue on the original route toward Da Nang
Attempt an emergency landing at Phan Rang Air Base
Negotiate a landing across the border in Cambodia

evt-09-15-1974-air-vietnam-flight-706.butterflyEffect: The crew attempted an emergency landing at Phan Rang, but the hijackers detonated hand grenades during the approach, and the aircraft crashed, killing everyone aboard. The disaster added to the toll of hijackings plaguing South Vietnamese aviation in the war's final chaotic year and pushed authorities to tighten airport security screening.

evt-09-15-1978-caesars-superdome.scenario: You are a ringside judge inside the Superdome on 15 September 1978, scoring the heavyweight rematch between Muhammad Ali and Leon Spinks, the largest indoor crowd ever to watch a boxing match.
evt-09-15-1978-caesars-superdome.prompt: How does the fight ultimately end?

choices.text: Ali wins by unanimous decision, reclaiming the title a third time
Spinks retains the title by split decision
Ali is knocked out in the early rounds
The bout is ruled a no-contest after an early stoppage

evt-09-15-1978-caesars-superdome.butterflyEffect: Ali outpointed Spinks by unanimous decision, becoming the first man to win the world heavyweight title a third time. The victory cemented his legend in the sport's history, and he retired from boxing the following year, only briefly returning in 1980.

evt-09-15-1981-united-states-senate-comm.scenario: It is 15 September 1981. You sit on the Senate Judiciary Committee reviewing President Reagan's nominee for the Supreme Court, Sandra Day O'Connor, an Arizona appeals judge with no prior federal bench experience.
evt-09-15-1981-united-states-senate-comm.prompt: What does the committee do with her nomination?

choices.text: Vote unanimously to approve her nomination
Split along party lines and forward it without recommendation
Delay the vote pending further hearings on her record
Reject her for lacking federal judicial experience

evt-09-15-1981-united-states-senate-comm.butterflyEffect: The committee approved her unanimously, and days later the full Senate confirmed her 99-0. She became the first woman to sit on the U.S. Supreme Court, a milestone that reshaped expectations for judicial nominations and opened the door for later women justices.

evt-09-15-2001-championship-auto-racing-.scenario: You are a track marshal at the Lausitzring in Germany on 15 September 2001, watching two CART cars collide at over 200 mph during a caution period, sending wreckage across the circuit.
evt-09-15-2001-championship-auto-racing-.prompt: What happens to driver Alex Zanardi after the impact?

choices.text: He is killed instantly at the scene
He is airlifted out and survives after losing both legs
The race continues without any medical intervention
He walks away with only minor bruises

evt-09-15-2001-championship-auto-racing-.butterflyEffect: Zanardi survived catastrophic injuries but lost both legs in the crash. He went on to become a champion Paralympic hand-cyclist, winning multiple gold medals and becoming a global symbol of resilience, before suffering another severe crash in a 2020 handbike race.

evt-09-15-2008-bankruptcy-of-lehman-brot.scenario: It is the weekend of September 13-14, 2008. You are a Federal Reserve official locked in emergency talks with Wall Street's biggest banks, trying to find a buyer or backstop for the collapsing Lehman Brothers before markets open Monday.
evt-09-15-2008-bankruptcy-of-lehman-brot.prompt: What did regulators ultimately decide to do about Lehman Brothers?

choices.text: Broker an emergency merger with a foreign bank in time to avert collapse
Let Lehman file for bankruptcy without government support
Arrange a taxpayer-backed bailout, as with Bear Stearns months earlier
Nationalize Lehman Brothers to protect its creditors

evt-09-15-2008-bankruptcy-of-lehman-brot.butterflyEffect: Talks collapsed and Lehman filed Chapter 11, still the largest bankruptcy in U.S. history. The Dow fell 4.5% in a single day, credit markets froze, and the panic forced the government into sweeping interventions including TARP and emergency Fed lending programs.

evt-09-15-2020-abraham-accords.scenario: It is September 15, 2020, and you stand on the White House lawn as an Emirati delegate, pen in hand, about to sign the Abraham Accords alongside Israeli and Bahraini officials under President Trump's sponsorship.
evt-09-15-2020-abraham-accords.prompt: What historic diplomatic milestone does your signature mark?

choices.text: The first Arab recognition of Israel since Egypt in 1979
Among the first Arab normalizations with Israel since Jordan in 1994
A military alliance treaty binding Gulf states to Israel's defense
A renewed Arab League boycott agreement against Israel

evt-09-15-2020-abraham-accords.butterflyEffect: The UAE and Bahrain became the first Arab states to formally recognize Israel since Jordan in 1994. Sudan and Morocco soon followed, and the Accords later expanded further, reshaping the diplomatic map of the Middle East for years afterward.

evt-09-15-2020-bahrain-israel-normalizat.scenario: You stand on the White House lawn on 15 September 2020 as a Bahraini official, cameras trained on the podium where President Trump waits with the Israeli and Emirati delegations.
evt-09-15-2020-bahrain-israel-normalizat.prompt: What historic act does Bahrain perform at this ceremony?

choices.text: Announce a boycott of any nation recognizing Israel
Sign a separate trade pact with Egypt instead
Reject the accord and withdraw the delegation
Sign an agreement normalizing diplomatic relations with Israel

evt-09-15-2020-bahrain-israel-normalizat.butterflyEffect: Bahrain formally signed a normalization agreement with Israel, becoming the fourth Arab state to recognize it and the second within a single month after the UAE. The deal, part of the broader Abraham Accords, opened direct diplomatic, trade, and security ties across the Gulf and encouraged Morocco and Sudan to follow with their own normalization steps.

evt-09-16-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is the morning of 16 September 1776 on Harlem Heights, Manhattan. Your battered Continental Army has just retreated from the disaster at Kip's Bay, and British light infantry below are blowing fox-hunting horns to mock your men as cowards.
evt-09-16-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: As General Washington, what do you order in response to the taunting?

choices.text: Continue the retreat further north without engaging
Hold position silently and ignore the provocation
Send troops to engage and drive off the British skirmishers
Send an officer to negotiate a ceasefire

evt-09-16-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Washington sent troops forward and drew the British skirmishers into a sharp firefight, routing them and forcing a withdrawal. It was the first clear American battlefield success of the New York campaign, restoring badly needed morale after weeks of retreat.

evt-09-16-1844-felix-mendelssohn.scenario: It is September 1844, and you are violinist Ferdinand David, who has spent years urging your friend Felix Mendelssohn to finish the violin concerto he promised you. He has just completed the full score.
evt-09-16-1844-felix-mendelssohn.prompt: What happens next with the finished concerto?

choices.text: It premieres in Leipzig with David as soloist
It is published but never performed in Mendelssohn's lifetime
It is dedicated to and premiered by Joseph Joachim
Mendelssohn himself performs it as soloist at its premiere

evt-09-16-1844-felix-mendelssohn.butterflyEffect: The concerto premiered in Leipzig in March 1845 with David as soloist; Mendelssohn, too ill to conduct, had Niels Gade lead the orchestra instead. The work's innovations, like the soloist entering almost immediately and the movements played without pause, made it a model for later Romantic concertos and one of the most performed violin concertos ever written.

evt-09-16-1920-wall-street-bombing.scenario: It is just after noon on 16 September 1920. A horse-drawn wagon has exploded outside the J.P. Morgan building at 23 Wall Street, and investigators are racing to identify who was behind the deadliest bombing the city has seen.
evt-09-16-1920-wall-street-bombing.prompt: What is the ultimate outcome of the official investigation into who planted the bomb?

choices.text: The case was closed without anyone ever being charged
A suspect confessed and received a life sentence
The bomber was identified and publicly executed
A foreign government was formally blamed and sanctioned

evt-09-16-1920-wall-street-bombing.butterflyEffect: Despite an extensive federal investigation, no one was ever charged, and the case was formally closed unsolved. Many historians later concluded Italian anarchist Mario Buda was responsible, acting in retaliation for the prosecution of Sacco and Vanzetti, and the attack deepened the era's Red Scare fears of radical violence.

evt-09-16-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 16 September 1940. Marshal Rodolfo Graziani's Italian 10th Army has just seized the Egyptian town of Sidi Barrani after a slow advance from Libya. British Commonwealth forces have pulled back, and Cairo lies further east.
evt-09-16-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: What does Graziani do next after capturing Sidi Barrani?

choices.text: He orders a full retreat back into Libya
He launches a surprise attack on Alexandria
He presses the advance immediately toward Mersa Matruh
He halts and digs in to wait for supplies before advancing further

evt-09-16-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Graziani halted the advance for three months to build supply depots, letting the British regroup. In December 1940, Operation Compass shattered the stationary Italian army, a disaster that drew German forces under Rommel into North Africa the following year.

evt-09-16-1961-national-hurricane-resear.scenario: You are a Weather Bureau scientist with the National Hurricane Research Project in September 1961, flying into Hurricane Esther with canisters of silver iodide. The goal is to see whether seeding the storm's clouds can weaken it.
evt-09-16-1961-national-hurricane-resear.prompt: What was the experimental technique researchers used to try to weaken the hurricane?

choices.text: Seeding the storm's clouds with silver iodide to disrupt its structure
Spraying oil on the ocean surface to reduce evaporation
Dropping ice directly into the eye to cool the ocean surface
Detonating explosives along the eyewall to break up convection

evt-09-16-1961-national-hurricane-resear.butterflyEffect: Seeding Esther with silver iodide appeared to cause some structural changes in the storm, encouraging the Weather Bureau to expand cloud-seeding experiments into the later Project Stormfury program. Those decades of hurricane-modification research ultimately proved inconclusive, and the idea was abandoned by the 1980s as scientists found storms were too powerful and variable to reliably control.

evt-09-16-1963-malaysia.scenario: It is 16 September 1963 in Kuala Lumpur. The Federation of Malaya has just formally merged with Singapore, Sabah, and Sarawak to create the new state of Malaysia, and you watch as the proclamation is read aloud.
evt-09-16-1963-malaysia.prompt: Which neighboring country's objection to this new federation soon erupts into armed conflict?

choices.text: Vietnam
Myanmar
Thailand
Indonesia

evt-09-16-1963-malaysia.butterflyEffect: Indonesia's President Sukarno denounced the merger as a neocolonial plot and launched Konfrontasi, a low-level armed conflict fought largely in Borneo from 1963 to 1966. The Philippines also disputed the inclusion of North Borneo, and within two years Singapore itself would separate from the federation in 1965.

evt-09-16-1979-east-germany-balloon-esca.scenario: You are part of the Strelzyk and Wetzel families in East Germany. Your first homemade hot-air balloon attempt has failed, and you fear the Stasi may soon trace the wreckage back to you.
evt-09-16-1979-east-germany-balloon-esca.prompt: What do the families do after their first balloon attempt fails?

choices.text: They give up the plan entirely out of fear of arrest
They try to bribe a border guard to let them cross on foot
They attempt to swim across a heavily guarded river instead
They build a third, improved balloon and attempt the crossing again

evt-09-16-1979-east-germany-balloon-esca.butterflyEffect: They built a third, larger balloon and successfully floated across the border at night two months later, landing safely in Bavaria. Their escape became an international sensation and was later dramatized in Disney's film Night Crossing.

evt-09-16-1982-elie-hobeika.scenario: You are an officer stationed at the perimeter of the Sabra and Shatila refugee camps in Beirut on 16 September 1982, as a Lebanese militia enters the camps to conduct a search operation. Reports begin reaching you of violence against civilians inside.
evt-09-16-1982-elie-hobeika.prompt: What should you do upon receiving these reports?

choices.text: Intervene immediately to stop the militia's actions
Wait for further orders before taking any action
Continue supporting the militia's search operation as planned
Withdraw your troops without investigating the reports

evt-09-16-1982-elie-hobeika.butterflyEffect: No effective intervention was made, and the militia carried out a massacre of civilians over the following days. An Israeli commission of inquiry later found indirect responsibility for failing to prevent it, forcing Defense Minister Ariel Sharon's resignation, while Elie Hobeika went on to a political career before his 2002 assassination.

evt-09-16-1987-montreal-protocol.scenario: You are a diplomat in Montreal in September 1987, watching scientists' warnings about a thinning ozone layer collide with industry lobbying over CFCs used in refrigerants and aerosols. Your delegation must decide whether to commit to binding cuts.
evt-09-16-1987-montreal-protocol.prompt: What did the negotiators agree to do about ozone-depleting chemicals?

choices.text: Fund research only, with no restrictions on chemical production
Leave regulation entirely to individual national governments
Ban CFCs immediately worldwide with no transition period
Phase out production of CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances on a set timetable

evt-09-16-1987-montreal-protocol.butterflyEffect: The Montreal Protocol committed nations to phasing out CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances, and every UN member state eventually ratified it. It became the first treaty to achieve universal ratification and is widely credited with putting the ozone layer on a path to recovery by the mid-21st century.

evt-09-16-1989-boris-yeltsin.scenario: You are touring the United States in September 1989 as a Soviet politician still years from the Kremlin. A stop at a Houston supermarket puts you face to face with aisles of goods unlike anything in a Moscow store.
evt-09-16-1989-boris-yeltsin.prompt: How did this grocery store visit affect your view of the Soviet system?

choices.text: It left him disillusioned with Soviet economic shortages and central planning
It persuaded him to abandon politics for private business
It convinced him Soviet supply chains were actually superior
It had no effect since he had seen Western stores many times before

evt-09-16-1989-boris-yeltsin.butterflyEffect: Yeltsin was reportedly stunned by the abundance and variety of ordinary American groceries, later writing that it deepened his disillusionment with Soviet central planning. The visit became a famous anecdote illustrating how firsthand exposure to consumer capitalism shaped the thinking of the man who would soon lead Russia away from Communist rule.

evt-09-16-1992-black-wednesday.scenario: You are a Bank of England official on 16 September 1992, watching sterling slide as speculators bet against it. Interest rates have already been hiked twice in one day to defend the currency's place in the European Exchange Rate Mechanism.
evt-09-16-1992-black-wednesday.prompt: What did the UK government ultimately do to stop the collapse of the pound?

choices.text: Raise interest rates further and stay in the ERM indefinitely
Withdraw the pound from the ERM and let it float
Devalue the pound within the ERM while remaining a member
Ask Germany to lower its own interest rates instead

evt-09-16-1992-black-wednesday.butterflyEffect: The UK withdrew the pound from the Exchange Rate Mechanism entirely, letting it float freely and devalue. The crisis discredited the Conservative government's economic management for years, boosted currency speculators like George Soros, and pushed Britain toward lasting scepticism about tying sterling to a European monetary system.

evt-09-16-1996-space-shuttle-atlantis.scenario: You are mission planner for STS-79 as Atlantis closes in on the Russian station Mir on 16 September 1996. Astronaut Shannon Lucid has spent months aboard Mir and a replacement is riding up with you.
evt-09-16-1996-space-shuttle-atlantis.prompt: What is Atlantis's central objective once it docks with Mir?

choices.text: Test a new docking mechanism never used before
Deploy a communications satellite near the station
Conduct emergency repairs on Mir's solar panels
Swap out the long-duration American astronaut for a new one

evt-09-16-1996-space-shuttle-atlantis.butterflyEffect: Atlantis delivered astronaut John Blaha to Mir and brought Shannon Lucid home after her record-setting stay. This crew rotation was part of the Shuttle-Mir program's steady buildup of joint US-Russian operations that directly informed how the International Space Station would later be built and crewed.

evt-09-16-2004-hurricane-ivan.scenario: You are a local official in Gulf Shores, Alabama, on 16 September 2004. Hurricane Ivan, a major hurricane, is bearing down on the coast and storm surge models show catastrophic flooding for low-lying neighborhoods.
evt-09-16-2004-hurricane-ivan.prompt: What order should you give to residents in the surge zone?

choices.text: Issue a mandatory evacuation of the coastal zone
Recommend sandbagging only, since the storm may weaken
Wait until the storm makes landfall to decide
Tell residents to shelter in place and board up windows

evt-09-16-2004-hurricane-ivan.butterflyEffect: Ivan struck near Gulf Shores as a strong Category 3 storm, devastating coastal Alabama and the Florida Panhandle and collapsing sections of the Interstate 10 bridge over Pensacola Bay. The widespread destruction pushed Gulf Coast states to tighten building codes and elevate future construction standards.

evt-09-16-2013-washington-navy-yard-shoo.scenario: It is the morning of 16 September 2013 at the Washington Navy Yard. A gunman with a valid security clearance, despite a history of prior warning signs, has just opened fire inside Building 197.
evt-09-16-2013-washington-navy-yard-shoo.prompt: What review did this attack prompt regarding federal security clearances?

choices.text: Transfer of all base security to local D.C. police
Permanent closure of the Washington Navy Yard
Elimination of security clearances for private contractors
A push toward continuous evaluation of clearance holders' records

evt-09-16-2013-washington-navy-yard-shoo.butterflyEffect: The shooter had retained a valid Department of Defense security clearance despite past mental health episodes and a prior weapons-related arrest that were never flagged. The attack triggered congressional hearings and a government-wide push to overhaul the security clearance process toward continuous evaluation rather than periodic review.

evt-09-16-2014-siege-of-kobani.scenario: You are a Kurdish YPG fighter in Kobani in mid-September 2014 as Islamic State forces push into the canton with tanks and heavy weapons seized from Iraq. Your lightly armed defenders are being pressed back toward the city itself.
evt-09-16-2014-siege-of-kobani.prompt: What turned the tide for Kobani's defenders in the months after the offensive began?

choices.text: Coalition airstrikes coordinated with YPG ground fighters
A negotiated withdrawal agreement with Islamic State commanders
A sudden Turkish military intervention on behalf of the Kurds
Syrian government forces retaking the city from IS

evt-09-16-2014-siege-of-kobani.butterflyEffect: The siege dragged into a months-long battle that drew US-led coalition airstrikes in support of the YPG, marking one of the first major instances of direct Western military cooperation with Kurdish forces against ISIS. Kobani's eventual defense became a symbol of Kurdish resistance and cemented the YPG as a key US partner in the fight against the Islamic State.

evt-09-16-2015-2015-illapel-earthquake.scenario: You live in a coastal apartment in Coquimbo, Chile, on the evening of 16 September 2015. The ground has just stopped shaking violently after a massive offshore earthquake, and sirens are sounding along the shore.
evt-09-16-2015-2015-illapel-earthquake.prompt: What should you do right now?

choices.text: Stay inside to protect your belongings from looters
Head immediately to high ground away from the coast
Go down to the beach to check the water level yourself
Wait for a phone call from authorities before moving

evt-09-16-2015-2015-illapel-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Chile's government issued a tsunami warning and evacuated over a million people from coastal areas. Waves several meters high struck the shore, but the rapid, well-drilled evacuation kept the death toll to 15 — a testament to lessons learned after the devastating 2010 Maule earthquake.

evt-09-16-2021-inspiration4.scenario: It is 16 September 2021 and you are watching the Crew Dragon Resilience lift off from Kennedy Space Center. None of the four people aboard, including a childhood cancer survivor now working as a physician assistant, are professional government astronauts.
evt-09-16-2021-inspiration4.prompt: What made this crew historically different from earlier orbital missions?

choices.text: It was the first crew made up entirely of foreign nationals
It was the first all-female spaceflight crew
It was the first all-civilian crew with no professional astronauts
It was the first crew launched entirely without NASA facilities

evt-09-16-2021-inspiration4.butterflyEffect: Inspiration4 was the first orbital spaceflight crewed entirely by private civilians with no professional astronauts aboard, raising funds and awareness for St. Jude Children's Research Hospital. It demonstrated that SpaceX could independently fly ordinary people to orbit, opening the door to further private missions like Polaris Dawn.

evt-09-17-1176-byzantine-seljuk-wars.scenario: It is September 17, 1176, and you march with Emperor Manuel I Komnenos's army through the narrow mountain pass of Myriokephalon in Phrygia, deep in Seljuk-held territory.
evt-09-17-1176-byzantine-seljuk-wars.prompt: What happens to the Byzantine army as it moves through this pass?

choices.text: It crushes the Seljuk army and reclaims central Anatolia
It is ambushed and routed by Kilij Arslan II's Seljuk forces
It negotiates a peaceful withdrawal without any battle
It captures the Seljuk capital of Konya

evt-09-17-1176-byzantine-seljuk-wars.butterflyEffect: Kilij Arslan II's Seljuk forces ambushed and routed the Byzantines in the narrow terrain, shattering Manuel's baggage train and siege engines. The defeat ended Byzantine hopes of reconquering central Anatolia, cementing Turkish control there and shaping the region's future for centuries.

evt-09-17-1382-louis-i-of-hungary.scenario: King Louis I of Hungary has just died leaving no son, only two young daughters. As a Hungarian noble at court, you must decide how the realm should be governed.
evt-09-17-1382-louis-i-of-hungary.prompt: Do you accept his daughter Mary as crowned queen, or push for a male successor instead?

choices.text: Declare an interregnum until an heir is born
Offer the throne to a Polish prince
Invite Charles of Durazzo to take the crown
Crown Mary as queen regnant

evt-09-17-1382-louis-i-of-hungary.butterflyEffect: Mary was crowned queen, but factions of nobles refused to accept a woman's rule and invited Charles of Durazzo, who briefly seized the throne in 1385. His murder soon after restored Mary, and the ensuing turmoil paved the way for her husband Sigismund of Luxembourg to become king in 1387.

evt-09-17-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 17 September 1775, and you are with Richard Montgomery's Continental Army outside British-held Fort St. Jean on the Richelieu River, the gateway to Quebec. Your artillery is thin and the fort's garrison is dug in.
evt-09-17-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: Do you order an immediate assault, or settle in for a prolonged siege?

choices.text: Begin a formal siege and wait it out
Storm the fort immediately with bayonets
Withdraw south to Fort Ticonderoga
Offer the garrison terms to defect

evt-09-17-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Montgomery chose a siege, which dragged on for 45 days before the fort finally surrendered on 3 November 1775. The delay gave Quebec City's defenders precious time to prepare, and when Montgomery finally attacked the city that December he was killed and the invasion of Canada collapsed.

evt-09-17-1793-war-of-the-pyrenees.scenario: It is 17 September 1793 near Perpignan. You serve under General Dagobert with the French Army of the Eastern Pyrenees, and Spanish forces under General Ricardos have besieged the city, threatening to break the republic's southern defenses.
evt-09-17-1793-war-of-the-pyrenees.prompt: What move does Dagobert make to break the siege at Peyrestortes?

choices.text: He launches a surprise dawn assault on the Spanish camp
He waits for Portuguese troops to join the French line
He negotiates a truce to buy time for reinforcements
He orders a full retreat toward Toulon

evt-09-17-1793-war-of-the-pyrenees.butterflyEffect: Dagobert's forces launched a surprise dawn assault on the Spanish positions at Peyrestortes, routing Ricardos's army and forcing him to lift the siege of Perpignan. The victory stabilized the French line in Roussillon during a difficult year and became one of the Republic's few clear successes against the First Coalition before further campaigns turned the tide more decisively.

evt-09-17-1849-harriet-tubman.scenario: It is September 1849, and you are enslaved on a Maryland plantation, fearing sale further south. Under cover of night, you slip away, knowing a network of safe houses may lie somewhere ahead.
evt-09-17-1849-harriet-tubman.prompt: How do you make your way to freedom?

choices.text: Travel openly by stagecoach to Canada
Stow away on a merchant ship to Boston
Join an armed uprising on the plantation
Follow the Underground Railroad's safe houses north

evt-09-17-1849-harriet-tubman.butterflyEffect: Tubman followed the Underground Railroad north to Philadelphia, reaching free soil. She then risked her own freedom repeatedly, returning roughly thirteen times to guide about seventy enslaved people north, and later served the Union Army as an armed scout and spy during the Civil War.

evt-09-17-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: It is September 17, 1862, along Antietam Creek in Maryland. You are a Union officer watching McClellan's army clash with Lee's Army of Northern Virginia in what becomes the deadliest single day in American history.
evt-09-17-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: What strategic outcome does this bloody standoff hand Lincoln?

choices.text: It gives Lincoln the tactical victory needed to issue the Emancipation Proclamation
It convinces Britain to formally recognize the Confederacy
It leads to McClellan's promotion to commander of all Union armies
It forces Lincoln to sue for peace with the Confederacy

evt-09-17-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The battle halted Lee's invasion of Maryland, giving Lincoln the narrow victory he needed to issue the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation days later. This reframed the war as a fight against slavery and helped deter Britain and France from recognizing the Confederacy.

evt-09-17-1914-andrew-fisher.scenario: It is September 1914. Britain has just gone to war with Germany, and as a member of the Australian Parliament you await word from Prime Minister Andrew Fisher on how far Australia will go to support the Empire.
evt-09-17-1914-andrew-fisher.prompt: What pledge does Fisher famously make for Australia's war commitment?

choices.text: A demand for full independence before committing troops
Support to the last man and the last shilling
Immediate conscription for overseas service
Only naval assistance, keeping troops at home

evt-09-17-1914-andrew-fisher.butterflyEffect: Fisher pledged Australia would support Britain "to the last man and the last shilling," committing the young nation to full-scale participation in the First World War. That commitment led to the raising of the Australian Imperial Force, the landing at Gallipoli in 1915, and years later the bitter conscription referendums that split his own Labor Party after Fisher had left office.

evt-09-17-1939-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 17 September 1939, barely two weeks into the war, and the aircraft carrier HMS Courageous is patrolling the Western Approaches hunting German U-boats, her escorting destroyers detached to assist a merchant ship.
evt-09-17-1939-world-war-ii.prompt: What happened as a result of the carrier being left without full escort?

choices.text: She was torpedoed and sunk by U-29
She sank U-29 before it could fire
She was reassigned to convoy escort duty unharmed
She returned safely to Scapa Flow

evt-09-17-1939-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: U-29 torpedoed Courageous, sinking her within minutes and killing over 500 of her crew—the Royal Navy's first warship lost in the war. The disaster forced the Admiralty to withdraw carriers from independent anti-submarine patrols, restricting them to escorted convoy duty for the rest of the war.

evt-09-17-1962-nasa.scenario: It is 17 September 1962, and NASA has just called your name among the newly announced 'Next Nine' astronauts, joining the original Mercury Seven. You report for training knowing the agency has a specific two-man spacecraft program in mind before any Moon attempt.
evt-09-17-1962-nasa.prompt: What program are you selected to fly first?

choices.text: Project Gemini
The Space Shuttle
Skylab
Project Mercury

evt-09-17-1962-nasa.butterflyEffect: The Next Nine, including Neil Armstrong, Jim Lovell, and John Young, trained to fly Project Gemini, mastering rendezvous, docking, and spacewalks. That experience directly enabled the Apollo program, and several of this group later walked on or orbited the Moon.

evt-09-17-1970-amman.scenario: It is September 17, 1970, in Amman. You are a resident as King Hussein's army pushes through the city, opening fire on positions held by Palestinian fedayeen loyal to the PLO.
evt-09-17-1970-amman.prompt: What does this crackdown, later called Black September, achieve for King Hussein?

choices.text: It ends in Syrian annexation of northern Jordan
It results in a unified Jordanian-Palestinian government
It topples King Hussein's monarchy
It expels PLO forces from Jordan, forcing their relocation to Lebanon

evt-09-17-1970-amman.butterflyEffect: The Jordanian army expelled PLO forces, who relocated their base of operations to Lebanon, a shift that helped fuel that country's slide into civil war. The crisis also gave its name to a militant group responsible for the 1972 Munich Olympics massacre.

evt-09-17-2001-george-w-bush.scenario: It is September 17, 2001, six days after the September 11 attacks. You are a White House aide preparing President Bush's remarks for his visit to the Islamic Center of Washington, as reports of harassment against Muslim Americans spread nationwide.
evt-09-17-2001-george-w-bush.prompt: What message should Bush deliver to calm the rising backlash against Muslim Americans?

choices.text: Call for a temporary ban on Muslim immigration
Declare that "Islam is peace" and denounce attacks on Muslim Americans
Blame the attacks on the broader Muslim world
Avoid the topic entirely and focus only on al-Qaeda

evt-09-17-2001-george-w-bush.butterflyEffect: Bush declared "Islam is peace" and condemned attacks on Muslim Americans, distinguishing the terrorists from the broader faith. The speech became a touchstone cited by both supporters and critics of the war on terror's framing of Islam, even as hate crimes against Muslims still rose sharply in the following months.

evt-09-17-2008-al-qaeda-in-yemen.scenario: It is 17 September 2008. You stand guard outside the U.S. Embassy in Sanaa when a convoy of armed men and vehicles laden with explosives suddenly moves toward the compound's gates.
evt-09-17-2008-al-qaeda-in-yemen.prompt: What do the embassy's security forces do to stop the attackers?

choices.text: They engage the attackers in a firefight at the outer perimeter
They abandon their posts and flee the compound
They open the gates to negotiate with the attackers
They call for an immediate American airstrike on the convoy

evt-09-17-2008-al-qaeda-in-yemen.butterflyEffect: Yemeni guards and embassy security exchanged fire with the attackers at the outer perimeter, preventing the assailants from breaching the compound itself, though the assault killed sixteen people, including an American student and several attackers. The attack, claimed by al-Qaeda's Yemeni affiliate, highlighted the group's growing reach months before it formally rebranded as al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula in 2009.

evt-09-17-2011-occupy-wall-street.scenario: It is September 17, 2011, and you join a few hundred protesters setting up camp in Zuccotti Park near Wall Street, carrying signs about income inequality and corporate greed.
evt-09-17-2011-occupy-wall-street.prompt: What tactic does the movement use to make decisions without formal leaders?

choices.text: A formal alliance with a political party
Consensus-based general assemblies and the human microphone
Delegated voting through elected representatives
A strict hierarchical union-style leadership

evt-09-17-2011-occupy-wall-street.butterflyEffect: Occupy Wall Street relied on consensus-based general assemblies and the "human microphone" to amplify speech without electronics. The movement spread to hundreds of cities worldwide and popularized the phrase "We are the 99%," reshaping political debate on inequality even after police cleared the camp that November.

evt-09-18-324-constantine-the-great.scenario: You stand among Constantine's legions on the shore near Chrysopolis, across the Bosporus from Byzantium. Licinius, the last rival emperor, has drawn up his army in a final stand for control of the Roman world.
evt-09-18-324-constantine-the-great.prompt: What actually happened to Licinius after his defeat at Chrysopolis?

choices.text: He died fighting on the battlefield at Chrysopolis
He was reinstated as co-emperor under a new treaty
He fled east and continued the war from Persian territory
He surrendered and was spared for a time, but later executed

evt-09-18-324-constantine-the-great.butterflyEffect: Licinius surrendered at Nicomedia and was spared through the intercession of Constantine's sister, only to be executed the following year on suspicion of plotting. Constantine's victory made him sole emperor, freeing him to found Constantinople and convene the Council of Nicaea in 325, decisions that shaped Christian doctrine and the empire's future for a thousand years.

evt-09-18-1850-united-states-congress.scenario: It is September 1850 in Boston. Congress has just passed the Fugitive Slave Act, making it a federal crime to help an escaped enslaved person and requiring ordinary citizens, even in free states, to assist in their capture.
evt-09-18-1850-united-states-congress.prompt: As a Northern abolitionist, how do you respond to the new law?

choices.text: Comply fully and report any fugitives you encounter
Join a vigilance committee to help fugitives escape further north
Petition Congress and wait quietly for repeal
Move to the South to avoid the controversy

evt-09-18-1850-united-states-congress.butterflyEffect: Many Northerners defied the law openly, forming vigilance committees and expanding the Underground Railroad, while some states passed personal liberty laws undermining it. The backlash helped inspire Harriet Beecher Stowe's 'Uncle Tom's Cabin' in 1852 and hardened sectional divisions that pushed the country toward civil war.

evt-09-18-1870-nathaniel-p-langford.scenario: On 18 September 1870 you ride with the Washburn–Langford–Doane Expedition through the Yellowstone wilderness when your party stumbles upon a thundering geyser unlike anything you've documented before.
evt-09-18-1870-nathaniel-p-langford.prompt: What does the expedition do with these remarkable discoveries?

choices.text: Stake private mining claims on the thermal features
Carefully document and publicize the findings to push for federal protection
Abandon the site as unremarkable and move on
Keep the location secret to protect personal profit

evt-09-18-1870-nathaniel-p-langford.butterflyEffect: Langford's vivid published accounts and lectures about the geysers, canyons, and hot springs helped convince Congress that the region deserved federal protection. In 1872 Yellowstone became the world's first national park, launching a conservation movement that spread across the globe.

evt-09-18-1873-panic-of-1873.scenario: You are a Wall Street investor on 18 September 1873, and word has just reached the floor that Jay Cooke & Company, financier of the Northern Pacific Railroad, has collapsed.
evt-09-18-1873-panic-of-1873.prompt: What actually followed Jay Cooke's failure on Wall Street?

choices.text: The federal government bailed out Jay Cooke & Company
European banks stepped in to fund an immediate recovery
The New York Stock Exchange shut down trading for ten days
Stocks rallied within days on rumors of a merger

evt-09-18-1873-panic-of-1873.butterflyEffect: The New York Stock Exchange closed its doors for ten days, the first suspension in its history, as panic spread to banks and railroads nationwide. The resulting depression, then called the Great Depression, dragged on for years and helped spark the widespread railroad worker strikes of 1877.

evt-09-18-1875-1875-indianola-hurricane.scenario: It is 16 September 1875, and a massive storm surge is bearing down on the port town of Indianola, Texas, with no modern warning system to alert residents of the hurricane's approach.
evt-09-18-1875-1875-indianola-hurricane.prompt: What ultimately became of Indianola in the years after this storm?

choices.text: The town declined and was later destroyed for good by another hurricane in 1886
The town rebuilt and became Texas's leading port
Residents relocated the entire town inland within a year
Federal engineers built a seawall that protected it permanently

evt-09-18-1875-1875-indianola-hurricane.butterflyEffect: The 1875 hurricane devastated the town and crippled its standing as a major Texas port, shifting trade toward Galveston and other harbors. A second catastrophic hurricane in 1886 finished what the first began, and Indianola was never rebuilt, becoming a ghost town remembered only through historical markers.

evt-09-18-1918-world-war-i.scenario: You are a Bulgarian soldier holding the heights of Dobro Pole in Macedonia as Serbian and French guns pound your trenches. The Allied breakthrough here threatens to unravel the entire Balkan front.
evt-09-18-1918-world-war-i.prompt: What actually followed the Allied victory at Dobro Pole?

choices.text: Bulgaria requested an armistice, the first Central Power to quit the war
German reinforcements arrived and restored the Balkan front
The Ottoman Empire sent fresh troops to stabilize the line
Bulgaria annexed further Serbian territory after the battle

evt-09-18-1918-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The collapse at Dobro Pole forced Bulgaria to seek an armistice on 29 September 1918, making it the first Central Power to leave the war. Its exit exposed the Ottoman Empire and Austria-Hungary to Allied pressure from the south, and within six weeks all the Central Powers had followed Bulgaria out of the war.

evt-09-18-1950-korean-war.scenario: It is mid-September 1950. North Korean forces are pulling back from the Pusan Perimeter after weeks of failed assaults, and you command UN troops deciding how to press the advantage.
evt-09-18-1950-korean-war.prompt: What should UN forces do now that the North Korean army is retreating from the perimeter?

choices.text: Break out of the perimeter to link up with the Inchon landing force
Open ceasefire talks with North Korea
Hold the defensive line and wait for reinforcements
Withdraw further south to consolidate positions

evt-09-18-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: UN troops broke out of the perimeter and drove north to link up with the Inchon landing force, trapping and shattering much of the North Korean army. The combined victories let UN forces retake Seoul and push toward the Yalu River, an advance so rapid it provoked Chinese intervention weeks later.

evt-09-18-1961-1961-ndola-transair-swede.scenario: It is September 1961. UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld is flying into the Congo Crisis to broker a ceasefire between UN forces and Katangan leader Moïse Tshombe, when his plane goes down near Ndola.
evt-09-18-1961-1961-ndola-transair-swede.prompt: After three official inquiries into the crash, what did investigators conclude?

choices.text: A mechanical fault was proven beyond doubt
Pilot error caused the crash, case closed definitively
Katangan forces were formally blamed and prosecuted
The cause remained officially inconclusive despite years of investigation

evt-09-18-1961-1961-ndola-transair-swede.butterflyEffect: No inquiry ever conclusively determined the cause of the crash, leaving sabotage theories unresolved for decades. The UN later reopened investigations in the 2010s after new evidence surfaced, and Hammarskjöld's death remains one of the great unsolved mysteries of the Cold War, deepening suspicion around great-power interference in Congo's decolonization.

evt-09-18-2001-anthrax.scenario: It is 18 September 2001, just a week after the September 11 attacks. Letters laced with anthrax spores are mailed from Trenton, New Jersey, to news media offices and, soon after, to U.S. senators.
evt-09-18-2001-anthrax.prompt: What did the FBI's years-long 'Amerithrax' investigation eventually conclude?

choices.text: The case remained permanently unsolved with no suspects
A U.S. Army scientist was identified as the likely perpetrator before he died
Al-Qaeda formally claimed responsibility and was confirmed
A foreign terrorist cell was identified and prosecuted

evt-09-18-2001-anthrax.butterflyEffect: The investigation dragged on for years before focusing on Bruce Ivins, a U.S. Army biodefense scientist, who died by suicide in 2008 before any charges were filed. The case was formally closed in 2010, and the attacks spurred a major expansion of U.S. biodefense research funding and mail-screening security.

evt-09-18-2006-the-cw.scenario: It is 2006, and executives at the newly formed CW Network are choosing how to position their fall lineup after merging UPN and The WB, competing against four established broadcast giants.
evt-09-18-2006-the-cw.prompt: What programming strategy did The CW adopt to define its identity?

choices.text: Compete directly for older male sports viewers
Build a lineup around classic sitcom reruns
Target young adults with teen and supernatural dramas
Focus exclusively on live news programming

evt-09-18-2006-the-cw.butterflyEffect: The CW built its brand around young-adult dramas like 'Supernatural' and 'Gilmore Girls,' later adding hits like 'Gossip Girl.' This niche identity sustained the network for years until financial pressures led Nexstar to acquire majority ownership in 2022 and pivot toward reality and sports programming.

evt-09-18-2007-saffron-revolution.scenario: It is September 2007 in Yangon. Fuel prices have quintupled overnight under military decree, and you are a Buddhist monk watching columns of protesters pass your monastery gate.
evt-09-18-2007-saffron-revolution.prompt: Do you join the lay protesters marching against the junta's fuel price hikes?

choices.text: Stay inside the monastery and remain neutral
Leave the country before unrest escalates
Join the march, lending the protest religious moral authority
Report the protest organizers to the local government

evt-09-18-2007-saffron-revolution.butterflyEffect: Thousands of monks did join, turning economic protest into a moral challenge the junta could not easily dismiss. Troops crushed the march within weeks, killing protesters and monks and drawing global condemnation, but the unrest cracked the regime's confidence and fed into the political opening and elections that followed in the early 2010s.

evt-09-18-2010-philippe-croizon.scenario: On 18 September 1968... it is 2010, and you are Philippe Croizon, a quadruple amputee, entering the cold water at the coast to attempt a swim across the English Channel using specially built prosthetics.
evt-09-18-2010-philippe-croizon.prompt: What equipment allows you to attempt this swim without natural arms or legs?

choices.text: A full mechanical exoskeleton that swims for him
Relay teammates who swim in his place at intervals
Custom-designed prosthetic fins attached to his limbs for propulsion
A support boat that tows him the entire distance

evt-09-18-2010-philippe-croizon.butterflyEffect: After roughly 13 and a half hours, Croizon became the first quadruple amputee to swim the Channel, proving adaptive prosthetics could conquer one of endurance sport's toughest challenges. He went on to complete the grueling Rally Dakar, inspiring wider recognition of what adaptive athletes could achieve.

evt-09-18-2013-via-rail.scenario: You drive an OC Transpo double-decker bus approaching a level crossing on Ottawa's western Transitway on the morning of 18 September 2013, just as a VIA Rail passenger train nears the same intersection.
evt-09-18-2013-via-rail.prompt: What is the safe course of action at the crossing?

choices.text: Honk and proceed since the gates appeared open
Reverse away from the intersection entirely
Accelerate to clear the crossing before the train arrives
Stop well before the tracks and wait for the train to pass

evt-09-18-2013-via-rail.butterflyEffect: The bus failed to stop and collided with the train, killing the driver and five passengers in one of Ottawa's deadliest transit disasters. The investigation exposed inadequate crossing safeguards on the Transitway and accelerated the city's push to replace bus rapid transit with a grade-separated light rail line.

evt-09-18-2014-2014-scottish-independenc.scenario: It is mid-September 2014, days before Scotland's independence referendum. Polls show the race tightening, and undecided voters hold the balance.
evt-09-18-2014-2014-scottish-independenc.prompt: What did UK party leaders offer in a last-minute push to keep wavering Scots voting No?

choices.text: Immediate EU membership guarantees for an independent Scotland
A promise of new powers for the Scottish Parliament, known as 'The Vow'
A pledge to relocate the UK Parliament to Edinburgh
A guarantee of a separate Scottish currency backed by the Bank of England

evt-09-18-2014-2014-scottish-independenc.butterflyEffect: The leaders of the three main UK parties signed 'The Vow,' promising greater devolved powers to the Scottish Parliament if Scotland stayed in the Union. This pledge helped secure the No victory and led to the Scotland Act 2016, though debates over its fulfillment fueled renewed independence campaigning after Brexit.

evt-09-18-2016-2016-uri-attack.scenario: It is 18 September 2016. Militants have just struck an Indian Army brigade base near Uri, killing nineteen soldiers, and you sit among the officers advising the government on how to respond.
evt-09-18-2016-2016-uri-attack.prompt: What retaliation do you recommend against the militant infrastructure across the border?

choices.text: Refer the matter to the United Nations for mediation
Maintain defensive posture and take no cross-border action
Conduct covert cross-border surgical strikes on militant launch pads
Launch a full-scale conventional invasion of Pakistan

evt-09-18-2016-2016-uri-attack.butterflyEffect: Eleven days later, Indian special forces crossed the Line of Control and struck militant launch pads in what New Delhi called "surgical strikes," a first public admission of cross-border action. The move set a new, more overt template for Indian retaliation that shaped the 2019 Balakot strikes and hardened the cycle of confrontation with Pakistan.

evt-09-18-2017-toys-r-us.scenario: You manage a Toys "R" Us store on 18 September 2017, the day corporate announces the company has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. Panicked employees ask what happens next.
evt-09-18-2017-toys-r-us.prompt: What should you tell staff about the stores' immediate future?

choices.text: Stores will keep operating normally through the holidays while the company restructures
Amazon will immediately buy and rebrand every location
All merchandise will be donated to charity
Stores will close within days

evt-09-18-2017-toys-r-us.butterflyEffect: Toys "R" Us stayed open through the 2017 holiday season while restructuring, but the plan to shed billions in debt from a 2005 leveraged buyout failed. By 2018 the chain liquidated all US stores, becoming a stark symbol of retail's struggle against online competitors like Amazon.

evt-09-19-1356-hundred-years-war.scenario: It is 19 September 1356 near Poitiers. You stand among the French ranks as King John II personally leads a final charge against Edward the Black Prince's outnumbered English and Gascon force.
evt-09-19-1356-hundred-years-war.prompt: What actually followed the French king's charge?

choices.text: King John II is captured by the English
Both sides agree to a truce before fighting begins
King John II escapes back to Paris unharmed
The French rout the English and win the battle

evt-09-19-1356-hundred-years-war.butterflyEffect: The charge collapsed and King John II was captured on the field, an enormous prize for England. His captivity led to the ruinous Treaty of Brétigny and a crushing ransom, plunging France into further chaos, including the Jacquerie peasant revolt.

evt-09-19-1692-salem-witch-trials.scenario: You are Giles Corey, standing before the Salem court in September 1692. The magistrates demand you enter a plea of guilty or not guilty to witchcraft, and you refuse to speak either word.
evt-09-19-1692-salem-witch-trials.prompt: Under the court's procedure, what happens to a defendant who refuses to plead?

choices.text: They are automatically convicted and hanged
They are automatically acquitted for lack of a plea
They are pressed under stones until they plead or die
They are banished from the colony instead of tried

evt-09-19-1692-salem-witch-trials.butterflyEffect: Corey was subjected to peine forte et dure, pressed beneath heavy stones until he died on 19 September 1692 without ever entering a plea. His brutal death shocked observers and helped turn public sentiment against the trials, which collapsed within months.

evt-09-19-1846-la-salette-fallavaux.scenario: You are one of two shepherd children tending cattle on a mountainside above La Salette, France, on 19 September 1846, when a weeping, luminous woman appears and begins speaking to you and your companion.
evt-09-19-1846-la-salette-fallavaux.prompt: What does she instruct the two of you to do with her message?

choices.text: Build a shrine yourselves before telling anyone
Keep the encounter secret for the rest of your lives
Report it only to the local bishop and no one else
Make her warning known to all her people

evt-09-19-1846-la-salette-fallavaux.butterflyEffect: The children, Mélanie Calvat and Maximin Giraud, spread word of the apparition and its call to repentance; the Catholic Church investigated and formally approved the apparition in 1851. A basilica rose at the site, making La Salette one of the earliest of the great 19th-century Marian pilgrimage shrines, a wave that would later include Lourdes.

evt-09-19-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 20 September 1863 near Chickamauga Creek, Georgia. You are a Union staff officer carrying General Rosecrans's order to shift General Wood's division to close what he believes is a gap in the line—though no gap actually exists yet.
evt-09-19-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: Do you obey the order literally and pull Wood's division out at once?

choices.text: Move only half the division to hedge the risk
Obey immediately, pulling the division out of line
Refuse the order and report it as a mistake
Delay and ride ahead to verify the gap truly exists

evt-09-19-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Wood obeyed to the letter, opening a real gap just as Longstreet's Confederate corps struck. The Union right collapsed and fled toward Chattanooga, while General George Thomas held Snodgrass Hill and earned the nickname "Rock of Chickamauga." Bragg's costly victory trapped Rosecrans's army in the Siege of Chattanooga that followed.

evt-09-19-1893-women-s-suffrage-in-new-z.scenario: It is 19 September 1893, and you stand alongside Kate Sheppard in Wellington as the Governor prepares to sign the Electoral Act into law after years of petitions and campaigning by suffragists across New Zealand.
evt-09-19-1893-women-s-suffrage-in-new-z.prompt: What right did the newly signed Electoral Act grant to women?

choices.text: The right to vote only in local council elections
The right to hold cabinet office
The right to stand for election to parliament
The right to vote in parliamentary elections

evt-09-19-1893-women-s-suffrage-in-new-z.butterflyEffect: The Act made New Zealand the first self-governing country where all women could vote in parliamentary elections, though they still could not stand as candidates. The victory inspired suffrage movements worldwide, and other nations gradually followed New Zealand's lead over the next decades.

evt-09-19-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 19 September 1944, and you sit among the Finnish delegation in Moscow. Soviet negotiators have laid out harsh terms to end your country's war, and your government must decide how far to bend to keep Finland out of full occupation.
evt-09-19-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What did Finland agree to do to secure the Moscow Armistice?

choices.text: Surrender unconditionally and accept full Soviet occupation
Continue fighting alongside Germany against the Soviets
Cede more territory to the USSR and turn on German forces in Finland
Join the Allies in an invasion of German-held Norway

evt-09-19-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Finland ceded further territory, paid reparations, and agreed to expel German troops still on its soil, triggering the Lapland War against its former ally. By accepting these harsh terms rather than fighting on, Finland preserved its independence and avoided Soviet occupation, later charting a unique neutral path through the Cold War.

evt-09-19-1976-1976-tehran-ufo-incident.scenario: It is the night of 19 September 1976, and you are flying an Imperial Iranian Air Force F-4 Phantom toward a brilliant, erratic light over Tehran. As you close in, your instruments falter and your weapons systems refuse to respond just as you prepare to fire.
evt-09-19-1976-1976-tehran-ufo-incident.prompt: What do you do as your jet's systems fail on approach to the object?

choices.text: Force the weapons to fire manually despite the failure
Withdraw from the object and regain control of your systems
Ram the object with your aircraft
Eject from the aircraft immediately

evt-09-19-1976-1976-tehran-ufo-incident.butterflyEffect: The pilot broke off and withdrew, and his instruments and weapons came back online as he pulled away. The incident was later documented in U.S. intelligence files and became one of the most cited cases in modern government studies of unidentified aerial phenomena.

evt-09-19-1985-1985-mexico-city-earthqua.scenario: It is the morning of 19 September 1985, and you stand amid collapsed apartment blocks in Mexico City hours after a magnitude 8.0 earthquake, watching neighbors dig through rubble with their bare hands while official rescue crews are overwhelmed.
evt-09-19-1985-1985-mexico-city-earthqua.prompt: What grassroots response emerges as government aid falls short?

choices.text: The military takes total control, barring civilian involvement
International rescue aid is turned away at the border
Volunteer citizen brigades form to search for survivors independently
The entire city is evacuated before any rescue attempts begin

evt-09-19-1985-1985-mexico-city-earthqua.butterflyEffect: Ordinary citizens organized themselves into volunteer rescue brigades, some later known as the "topos," filling the gap left by a slow and distrusted government response. The disaster's aftermath fueled the growth of independent civil society organizations in Mexico and is credited with weakening the long-dominant PRI's grip on power.

evt-09-19-1991-otzi.scenario: You are hiking off the marked trail in the Ötztal Alps on 19 September 1991 when you notice a human head and shoulders emerging from the melting glacial ice.
evt-09-19-1991-otzi.prompt: What do authorities initially assume the body to be?

choices.text: A soldier killed in the First World War
An ancient mummy, recognized on sight
A recently deceased mountaineer or climbing accident victim
A murder victim requiring a homicide investigation

evt-09-19-1991-otzi.butterflyEffect: Investigators first treated the find as a recently deceased mountaineer, even using a jackhammer that damaged the remains during recovery. Archaeologists soon realized artifacts nearby were ancient; radiocarbon dating revealed the man had died over 5,000 years earlier, making Ötzi Europe's oldest known natural mummy and transforming understanding of Copper Age life, tools, and diet.

evt-09-19-1995-industrial-society-and-it.scenario: You are an editor at The Washington Post in September 1995, holding a 35,000-word manifesto sent by a serial bomber who has promised to stop killing if it is published in full.
evt-09-19-1995-industrial-society-and-it.prompt: Do you publish the manifesto in full, hoping someone recognizes its author?

choices.text: Print only a short, heavily edited summary
Publish it in full as demanded
Refuse outright and risk further bombings
Publish it anonymously without any attribution
