evt-09-19-1995-industrial-society-and-it.butterflyEffect: The Post and New York Times jointly published the manifesto on 19 September 1995. Ted Kaczynski's brother David recognized the ideas and phrasing, alerted the FBI, and Ted was arrested in April 1996, ending a bombing campaign that had killed three people and injured twenty-three over nearly two decades.

evt-09-19-2006-2006-thai-coup-d-etat.scenario: You are Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra, addressing the UN General Assembly in New York on 19 September 2006, when word reaches you that army tanks are rolling through Bangkok.
evt-09-19-2006-2006-thai-coup-d-etat.prompt: What did Thaksin attempt from abroad as the coup unfolded?

choices.text: Request emergency UN Security Council intervention
Resign the premiership on the spot
Fly back to Bangkok immediately to rally loyal troops
Try to broadcast a state of emergency dismissing the army chief

evt-09-19-2006-2006-thai-coup-d-etat.butterflyEffect: Thaksin tried to broadcast a state of emergency dismissing the army chief, but soldiers seized the television station before it could air. The coup succeeded in his absence, the 1997 constitution was abrogated, and Thaksin entered exile, setting off years of red-shirt/yellow-shirt turmoil in Thai politics.

evt-09-19-2008-learjet-60.scenario: You are aboard a Learjet 60 taking off from Columbia, South Carolina, on 19 September 1908— no, 2008—carrying musicians Travis Barker and DJ AM home from a show, when a tire fails partway down the runway.
evt-09-19-2008-learjet-60.prompt: What happens when the crew tries to abort the takeoff after the tire blows?

choices.text: The jet overruns the runway, crashes and catches fire
Emergency arresting cables halt the jet unharmed
The pilots abort but taxi back for a second attempt
The jet stops safely before the end of the runway

evt-09-19-2008-learjet-60.butterflyEffect: The jet could not stop in time, overran the runway, struck an embankment and burst into flames, killing both pilots and two of the musicians' assistants. Barker and Goldstein survived with severe burns; Goldstein, traumatized, died of an accidental overdose the following year, while Barker got sober and became a vocal advocate for burn recovery.

evt-09-19-2010-deepwater-horizon-oil-spi.scenario: You are an engineer aboard a response vessel in the Gulf of Mexico on 19 September 2010, monitoring pressure readings after months of failed attempts to stop the Macondo well from leaking.
evt-09-19-2010-deepwater-horizon-oil-spi.prompt: Which combination of techniques finally seals the well for good?

choices.text: Chemical dispersants that dissolved the leak at its source
A static kill paired with a relief well bottom kill
A containment dome that simply captured all the oil
A top kill procedure used alone

evt-09-19-2010-deepwater-horizon-oil-spi.butterflyEffect: A static kill combined with a relief well intercepting and cementing the well from below finally declared it "effectively dead" after an 87-day spill. The disaster led to record fines against BP, an overhaul of US offshore drilling regulation, and years of Gulf ecosystem monitoring.

evt-09-19-2011-mariano-rivera.scenario: It is 19 September 2011 at Yankee Stadium. You watch Mariano Rivera jog in from the bullpen for the ninth inning, needing just one more save to pass Trevor Hoffman atop the all-time list.
evt-09-19-2011-mariano-rivera.prompt: What happened on the mound that night?

choices.text: He blew the save, tying the record instead of breaking it
He converted the save to become MLB's all-time saves leader
He set the record in an earlier game that week, not this one
He was pulled before the ninth inning for a reliever

evt-09-19-2011-mariano-rivera.butterflyEffect: Rivera closed out the game for save number 602, surpassing Hoffman to become baseball's all-time saves leader. He extended the record to 652 before retiring in 2013, and it still stands untouched today.

evt-09-19-2017-2017-puebla-earthquake.scenario: It is early afternoon on 19 September 2017 in Mexico City. Just two hours earlier, your office building took part in the annual citywide earthquake drill marking the 1985 disaster — and now the ground has genuinely begun to shake.
evt-09-19-2017-2017-puebla-earthquake.prompt: What is the correct response as the real earthquake hits, so soon after the drill?

choices.text: Drop, cover, and hold, then evacuate calmly via the drill's rehearsed routes
Rush to the elevators to reach the ground floor fastest
Assume the drill is repeating and ignore the shaking
Wait for an official radio announcement before moving

evt-09-19-2017-2017-puebla-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The magnitude 7.1 quake struck on the same calendar date as the catastrophic 1985 earthquake, killing 370 people and collapsing more than 40 buildings across Puebla, Morelos, and Mexico City. The eerie timing intensified scrutiny of building codes and led to prosecutions over improperly certified construction in several collapsed structures.

evt-09-19-2021-cumbre-vieja.scenario: It is 19 September 2021, and you live in the village of Las Manchas on La Palma. Cumbre Vieja has just torn open nearby, and lava is beginning to creep toward the edge of town.
evt-09-19-2021-cumbre-vieja.prompt: What should you do as the lava flow advances on your neighborhood?

choices.text: Stay behind to defend your house with buckets of water
Wait a few days to see if the flow changes direction
Follow the evacuation order and leave immediately with only essentials
Move belongings to the roof and shelter in place

evt-09-19-2021-cumbre-vieja.butterflyEffect: Authorities evacuated thousands ahead of the flows, and the 85-day eruption destroyed nearly 3,000 buildings and buried banana plantations without a single direct death. Lava pouring into the sea added new land to the island's coastline before the volcano fell silent in December.

evt-09-19-2022-2022-michoacan-earthquake.scenario: It is 13:05 on 19 September 2022 in Michoacán, and you have just finished Mexico's annual national earthquake drill, held every year on this date to mark the deadly 1985 and 2017 quakes. Minutes later, the ground genuinely begins to shake.
evt-09-19-2022-2022-michoacan-earthquake.prompt: What should you do when the drill alarm is followed by a real earthquake?

choices.text: Assume it is a continuation of the drill and stay seated
Follow the drill protocol: drop, cover, and hold on or evacuate calmly
Ignore it since the drill had just ended
Sprint outside immediately without taking cover

evt-09-19-2022-2022-michoacan-earthquake.butterflyEffect: A magnitude 7.6–7.7 earthquake struck moments after that year's drill, killing two people and injuring dozens; many survived by following the drop-cover-hold protocol just practiced. A magnitude 6.8 aftershock three days later killed three more, deepening Mexico's grim pattern of major quakes striking on 19 September.

evt-09-19-2023-azerbaijan.scenario: It is 19 September 2023, and you are a resident of Stepanakert as Azerbaijan launches a sudden military offensive against the Republic of Artsakh, calling it an anti-terrorist operation. Within hours, artillery is falling near your neighborhood and local authorities must decide how to respond.
evt-09-19-2023-azerbaijan.prompt: What did Artsakh's forces do within a day of the offensive beginning?

choices.text: Agree to a ceasefire and disarm within a day
Declare full independence from Armenia to negotiate separately
Fight on regardless of losses
Call on Russian peacekeepers to launch a counteroffensive

evt-09-19-2023-azerbaijan.butterflyEffect: Facing overwhelming force and no outside intervention, Artsakh's authorities agreed to a ceasefire and disarmament within about a day. The republic dissolved itself by January 2024, and nearly the entire ethnic Armenian population fled to Armenia, ending decades of dispute over Nagorno-Karabakh.

evt-09-20-1066-harald-hardrada.scenario: It is 20 September 1066 outside York. You stand in the shield wall of Earls Morcar and Edwin, facing the invading army of Harald Hardrada and Tostig Godwinson at Fulford.
evt-09-20-1066-harald-hardrada.prompt: What happens to the northern earls' army at Fulford?

choices.text: They repel Harald's forces and hold the city
The battle ends in a truce with no clear victor
They are defeated and York falls to the invaders
They join forces with Harald against King Harold

evt-09-20-1066-harald-hardrada.butterflyEffect: Harald and Tostig crushed the earls' forces and took York, seemingly securing northern England for Norway. But their triumph was short-lived: days later King Harold Godwinson's army arrived and annihilated the Norwegians at Stamford Bridge, killing both Harald and Tostig—then marched south to meet William of Normandy at Hastings, exhausted from the campaign.

evt-09-20-1260-prussian-uprisings.scenario: It is 1260. Word reaches your clan that the Lithuanians have crushed the Teutonic Knights at the Battle of Durbe, and warriors across Old Prussia are weighing whether the Order's grip has finally weakened enough to strike.
evt-09-20-1260-prussian-uprisings.prompt: Do you join the rising against the Teutonic Knights while their forces are shaken?

choices.text: Join the revolt, exploiting the Order's weakness after Durbe
Stay loyal to the Knights to avoid harsh reprisals
Send envoys to the Pope asking him to restrain the Knights
Migrate your clan away from Teutonic lands entirely

evt-09-20-1260-prussian-uprisings.butterflyEffect: Prussian clans rose in what became the Great Prussian Uprising, led by figures such as Herkus Monte, and the revolt dragged on for over a decade, inflicting serious losses on the Teutonic Order. The Knights eventually suppressed the uprising, but the prolonged struggle delayed their conquest of Prussia and hardened their later policy of subjugating and resettling the region.

evt-09-20-1643-first-english-civil-war.scenario: It is 20 September 1643 at Newbury. You march with the Earl of Essex's parliamentary army, trying to force your way past Royalist forces blocking the road back to London after relieving besieged Gloucester.
evt-09-20-1643-first-english-civil-war.prompt: What is the outcome of the fighting at Newbury?

choices.text: Essex surrenders his forces rather than continue fighting
Essex's army fights through and completes its march to London
Both armies withdraw without any fighting taking place
The Royalists win a decisive victory and destroy Essex's army

evt-09-20-1643-first-english-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The battle was tactically inconclusive, but Essex's army broke through and reached London safely, delivering a much-needed morale boost to Parliament. The steady performance of London's trained-band militia against seasoned Royalist cavalry demonstrated that citizen soldiers could hold their own, encouraging Parliament to invest further in organized regional forces.

evt-09-20-1697-peace-of-ryswick.scenario: You are a diplomat at Rijswijk on 20 September 1697, watching French and Allied delegates sign the first of several treaties ending nine years of war between France and the Grand Alliance.
evt-09-20-1697-peace-of-ryswick.prompt: What did Louis XIV concede in this settlement?

choices.text: French control over the entire Rhineland
Abandonment of all French colonial claims in North America
Permanent French annexation of the Spanish Netherlands
Recognition of William III as King of England and return of captured territories

evt-09-20-1697-peace-of-ryswick.butterflyEffect: The treaties restored the pre-war territorial status quo and forced Louis XIV to recognize William III as King of England while returning captured Dutch and Spanish territories. The peace proved short-lived, as disputes over the Spanish succession would plunge Europe back into war within five years.

evt-09-20-1792-french-army.scenario: It is 20 September 1792 near Valmy. You stand in the ranks of the French Revolutionary Army, raw and poorly trained, as Prussian and Austrian forces advance to crush the Revolution and restore the monarchy.
evt-09-20-1792-french-army.prompt: What happens when the armies clash at Valmy?

choices.text: The two armies sign a truce before any fighting starts
French troops mutiny and desert before the battle begins
French artillery holds and the Prussians withdraw without attacking
The French army collapses and Paris is left undefended

evt-09-20-1792-french-army.butterflyEffect: French artillery held firm under bombardment, and the shaken Prussians withdrew rather than press the attack—a defensive victory that stopped the Coalition's advance on Paris. The very next day the National Convention proclaimed the French Republic; the poet Goethe, watching from the Prussian side, reportedly declared that a new era of world history had begun.

evt-09-20-1870-bersaglieri.scenario: It is dawn on 20 September 1870. You are a Bersagliere crouched behind artillery as Italian guns pound a breach into the ancient wall near Rome's Porta Pia, the last barrier protecting the Pope's temporal rule.
evt-09-20-1870-bersaglieri.prompt: What happens once the breach opens?

choices.text: French garrison troops rush in to defend the Pope
Garibaldi arrives to negotiate a peaceful transfer of power
Italian troops storm through and seize the city, ending papal rule over Rome
The Pope's Swiss Guard repels the assault entirely

evt-09-20-1870-bersaglieri.butterflyEffect: Italian troops poured through the breach and Rome fell within hours, completing Italian unification and ending over a thousand years of Papal temporal sovereignty. Pope Pius IX retreated into the Vatican, refusing to recognize the new Kingdom of Italy—a standoff called the "Roman Question" that lasted until the 1929 Lateran Treaty.

evt-09-20-1906-rms-mauretania-1906.scenario: It is 20 September 1906, and you stand among the crowds at Wallsend on the River Tyne as Cunard's newest liner, the Mauretania, slides down the launch ways into the water—the largest ship the world has yet seen.
evt-09-20-1906-rms-mauretania-1906.prompt: What record does the Mauretania seize the following year?

choices.text: The record for largest number of passengers carried
The Blue Riband for the fastest transatlantic crossing
The first liner to complete a crossing without stopping for coal
The first ship fitted with lifeboats for every passenger

evt-09-20-1906-rms-mauretania-1906.butterflyEffect: On her maiden return voyage in December 1907, Mauretania captured the eastbound Blue Riband for the fastest Atlantic crossing, later adding the westbound record too. She held both speed records for two decades, cementing Britain's shipbuilding prestige until the Titanic disaster shifted the era's priorities from speed toward safety.

evt-09-20-1920-irish-war-of-independence.scenario: It is the night of 20 September 1920 in the small Irish town of Balbriggan. An RIC district inspector has just been shot dead in the town, and Black and Tans are moving through the streets with torches in retaliation.
evt-09-20-1920-irish-war-of-independence.prompt: What did the Black and Tans do to the town that night?

choices.text: Arrested every male resident for questioning
Burned homes, shops and a hosiery factory in reprisal
Called off the reprisal after negotiating with the parish priest
Distributed food and left peacefully

evt-09-20-1920-irish-war-of-independence.butterflyEffect: The Sack of Balbriggan saw dozens of homes, shops and a major local hosiery factory burned in reprisal. It became one of the most notorious British reprisals of the war, drawing international press condemnation and hardening opinion against British rule, feeding pressure toward the 1921 truce and treaty.

evt-09-20-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is September 20, 1944. You lead an Allied unit advancing on San Marino, the tiny neutral republic that German forces have occupied and fortified along the Gothic Line.
evt-09-20-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: How do you approach clearing the German positions from this officially neutral state?

choices.text: Advance carefully, flanking German positions while limiting damage to the neutral republic
Level the town with heavy artillery regardless of its neutral status
Halt the advance and seek Vatican mediation for a ceasefire
Bypass San Marino entirely and let the Germans withdraw on their own

evt-09-20-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Allied troops fought through the German defenses and captured San Marino, ending its wartime occupation and restoring the republic's independence. The episode became a small but telling example of how declared neutrality offered little protection once the front line crossed a nation's borders.

evt-09-20-1971-hurricane-irene-olivia.scenario: It is September 19, 1971. You are a forecaster watching Hurricane Irene come ashore in southeastern Nicaragua, its low-pressure core still visible on satellite as it crosses the low-lying isthmus toward the Pacific.
evt-09-20-1971-hurricane-irene-olivia.prompt: What do you expect to happen as the storm's remnants reach the Pacific Ocean?

choices.text: It weakens into a permanent tropical depression with no further development
It dissipates completely over Nicaragua's terrain
It regenerates into a new hurricane, becoming the first tracked Atlantic-to-Pacific crossover storm
It stalls and turns back into the Caribbean Sea

evt-09-20-1971-hurricane-irene-olivia.butterflyEffect: The circulation survived the land crossing and re-strengthened into Hurricane Olivia, the first tropical cyclone ever tracked moving from the Atlantic into the eastern Pacific basin. The event became a benchmark case for forecasters studying cross-basin storm survival, a phenomenon still considered rare decades later.

evt-09-20-1973-billie-jean-king.scenario: It is the night of 20 September 1973 in the Houston Astrodome, and you are among 30,000 spectators watching 29-year-old Billie Jean King face 55-year-old former champion Bobby Riggs in the heavily hyped 'Battle of the Sexes'.
evt-09-20-1973-billie-jean-king.prompt: What was the outcome of this widely watched exhibition match?

choices.text: King defeated Riggs in straight sets
King withdrew mid-match with an injury
Riggs defeated King in straight sets
The match ended in a draw due to darkness

evt-09-20-1973-billie-jean-king.butterflyEffect: King won decisively, 6–4, 6–3, 6–3, before a record television audience for tennis. The victory became a landmark for the women's sports movement, bolstering the push for equal pay and opportunities in tennis and beyond, and cementing King's legacy as a pioneer for gender equity in sport.

evt-09-20-1984-the-cosby-show.scenario: It is 20 September 1984, and you're an NBC executive watching the network debut a new family sitcom starring comedian Bill Cosby as an upper-middle-class Brooklyn obstetrician.
evt-09-20-1984-the-cosby-show.prompt: What does this new show go on to achieve for NBC?

choices.text: It airs only overseas after being rejected by American audiences
It becomes the top-rated show in America and revives NBC's ratings
It is cancelled after low ratings within its first season
It is immediately pulled for controversial content before broadcast

evt-09-20-1984-the-cosby-show.butterflyEffect: The Cosby Show became a ratings juggernaut, anchoring NBC's Thursday lineup and helping the network dominate primetime for years. It also broke ground for its portrayal of an affluent Black American family, spawning the spin-off A Different World—though decades later Cosby's sexual assault convictions led many broadcasters to pull the series from syndication.

evt-09-20-2001-war-on-terror.scenario: It is the evening of 20 September 2001, and you are seated in the House chamber as President George W. Bush rises to address a joint session of Congress, nine days after the September 11 attacks.
evt-09-20-2001-war-on-terror.prompt: What did Bush declare in this address?

choices.text: An immediate declaration of war against Iraq
A unilateral withdrawal of U.S. forces from the Middle East
A new alliance with the Taliban against al-Qaeda
A global 'war on terror' targeting al-Qaeda and demanding the Taliban surrender its leaders

evt-09-20-2001-war-on-terror.butterflyEffect: Bush announced a global 'war on terror' against al-Qaeda and demanded the Taliban surrender its leaders. The campaign expanded far beyond Afghanistan, eventually justifying the 2003 invasion of Iraq and reshaping U.S. foreign and domestic policy for decades, including the Patriot Act and creation of the Department of Homeland Security.

evt-09-20-2003-2003-maldives-civil-unres.scenario: It is 20 September 2003 in Malé, the Maldivian capital. News has just spread that a young prisoner, Hassan Evan Naseem, has died from mistreatment at Maafushi Prison, and crowds are gathering angrily in the streets.
evt-09-20-2003-2003-maldives-civil-unres.prompt: What happened at Maafushi Prison as the unrest spread?

choices.text: Guards opened fire on inmates, killing three more prisoners
All prisoners were immediately released
Protesters negotiated a formal ceasefire with guards
The prison was permanently shut down that day

evt-09-20-2003-2003-maldives-civil-unres.butterflyEffect: Guards opened fire on inmates at Maafushi, killing three more prisoners and injuring others, which ignited the largest anti-government protests the Maldives had seen in decades. The unrest fed a broader pro-democracy movement that pressured President Gayoom's government toward reforms and eventual multi-party elections.

evt-09-20-2018-sinking-of-mv-nyerere.scenario: It is late afternoon on 20 September 2018, and you are a deckhand on the MV Nyerere as it nears the pier on Ukara Island, Lake Victoria. The ferry is packed far beyond its rated capacity with market-day passengers, livestock and cargo.
evt-09-20-2018-sinking-of-mv-nyerere.prompt: What safety measure could have prevented the ferry from capsizing at the pier?

choices.text: Sailing only during daylight hours
Posting an armed guard at the gangway
Limiting passengers and cargo to the ferry's rated capacity
Issuing more life jackets once at sea

evt-09-20-2018-sinking-of-mv-nyerere.butterflyEffect: The overloaded MV Nyerere capsized as passengers shifted toward one side while docking, killing at least 228 people, most of them market traders and children. The disaster led Tanzanian authorities to arrest ferry operators for negligence and prompted a crackdown on overloading across Lake Victoria's ferry network.

evt-09-20-2019-september-2019-climate-st.scenario: It is September 20, 2019, three days before the UN Climate Summit, and you are a student deciding whether to walk out of class to join millions marching worldwide in the Fridays for Future strike.
evt-09-20-2019-september-2019-climate-st.prompt: What should you do to maximize pressure on world leaders before the summit?

choices.text: Stay in class and wait for official government policy changes
Sign an online petition instead and avoid missing school
Organize a separate, smaller protest the following month
Walk out and join the strike, timing it to pressure leaders ahead of the summit

evt-09-20-2019-september-2019-climate-st.butterflyEffect: Roughly six to seven million people struck across 150 countries, making it the largest climate mobilization in history and dominating headlines just before the UN Climate Action Summit. The turnout amplified Greta Thunberg's profile, pushed several governments toward emergency climate declarations, and energized youth climate activism for years afterward.

evt-09-21-1170-anglo-norman-invasion-of-.scenario: It is September 1170. You ride with Strongbow's Anglo-Norman force alongside the deposed king Diarmait Mac Murchada, closing in on Dublin. Inside the walls, the city's Norse-Gaelic ruler Ascall mac Ragnaill is negotiating terms of surrender.
evt-09-21-1170-anglo-norman-invasion-of-.prompt: Do you press the attack before those surrender talks are concluded?

choices.text: Attack the city before the surrender terms are settled
Withdraw and starve the city into submission
Offer Ascall an alliance against other Irish kings
Wait patiently for the negotiated surrender

evt-09-21-1170-anglo-norman-invasion-of-.butterflyEffect: The Normans stormed the city while negotiations were still underway, and Dublin fell by force rather than treaty. Ascall fled but was soon captured and killed, and Dublin became the Anglo-Normans' first great foothold in Ireland, launching over eight centuries of English involvement there.

evt-09-21-1435-congress-of-arras.scenario: It is September 1435 at the Congress of Arras, and you advise Philip the Good, Duke of Burgundy. The English delegation has stormed out rather than accept France's terms, and Charles VII's envoys now press you for a separate peace.
evt-09-21-1435-congress-of-arras.prompt: Does Burgundy sign a separate treaty with France, abandoning its English alliance?

choices.text: Declare Burgundy neutral in the war
Walk out of the congress entirely
Sign the treaty with France, breaking with England
Renew the alliance with England instead

evt-09-21-1435-congress-of-arras.butterflyEffect: Philip the Good signed the Treaty of Arras, ending the Anglo-Burgundian alliance and formally reconciling with Charles VII in exchange for concessions and an apology for his father's murder. Deprived of its key continental ally, England's position in France collapsed within decades, and the treaty is remembered as an early modern-style peace congress.

evt-09-21-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is the night of 21 September 1776 in British-occupied New York City. Flames are spreading rapidly near Whitehall Slip, and British soldiers suspect the fire was deliberately set by Patriot sympathizers.
evt-09-21-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What do British forces do as the fire rages through the city?

choices.text: Order an immediate evacuation of all colonial civilians from the city
Negotiate a truce with nearby Patriot forces to jointly fight the fire
Hunt for suspected rebel arsonists and execute several on the spot
Abandon the city entirely and retreat to the ships in the harbor

evt-09-21-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: The fire destroyed roughly a quarter of New York City. British suspicion of rebel arson, though never proven, hardened occupation policy, and the city remained under British control for the rest of the war until the 1783 Treaty of Paris ended it.

evt-09-21-1897-the-sun-new-york-city.scenario: You are an editorial writer at The Sun in New York in 1897. Eight-year-old Virginia O'Hanlon has written asking whether Santa Claus is real, after friends told her he was not, and your editor hands you the letter to answer.
evt-09-21-1897-the-sun-new-york-city.prompt: How do you respond to Virginia's letter?

choices.text: Bluntly confirm her friends are correct, Santa is not real
Ignore the letter as too trivial for the paper
Print a scientific explanation of why flying reindeer are impossible
Write a heartfelt editorial affirming Santa Claus as a symbol of generosity and faith

evt-09-21-1897-the-sun-new-york-city.butterflyEffect: Francis Pharcellus Church wrote the unsigned editorial 'Yes, Virginia, there is a Santa Claus,' affirming that Santa embodied love, generosity, and childlike faith even if unseen. It became the most reprinted editorial in the English language, republished by The Sun every Christmas until the paper closed in 1950, and remains a fixture of American holiday culture.

evt-09-21-1918-world-war-i.scenario: It is dawn on 20 September 1918. You ride with a British Empire cavalry column racing toward Nazareth, hoping to seize the town before German commander Otto Liman von Sanders can escape his headquarters there.
evt-09-21-1918-world-war-i.prompt: What happens when your cavalry storms into Nazareth?

choices.text: Von Sanders is captured along with his staff
The town surrenders without any resistance
Von Sanders narrowly escapes the raid
The cavalry raid is repelled by German defenders

evt-09-21-1918-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Von Sanders escaped capture by minutes, fleeing in his nightclothes as British and Indian cavalry seized his headquarters and papers. The raid, part of the wider Battle of Megiddo, wrecked Ottoman-German command coordination and hastened the collapse of their front in Palestine.

evt-09-21-1934-1934-muroto-typhoon.scenario: You live on the coast of Shikoku in September 1934 as a violent typhoon with record-low pressure bears down, its winds already stripping roofs from wooden houses.
evt-09-21-1934-1934-muroto-typhoon.prompt: With landfall hours away, what should you and your family do?

choices.text: Move to a sturdier reinforced building or higher ground away from the coast
Wait for a second warning before deciding to move
Stay home and reinforce the wooden house with extra boards
Take shelter aboard a fishing boat in the harbor

evt-09-21-1934-1934-muroto-typhoon.butterflyEffect: The Muroto typhoon killed more than 3,000 people, many when flimsy wooden school buildings and homes collapsed. The disaster pushed Japanese authorities to strengthen building codes, favoring reinforced concrete for schools and public shelters in typhoon-prone regions in the years that followed.

evt-09-21-1937-j-r-r-tolkien.scenario: It is late September 1937 in London, and George Allen & Unwin has just released a peculiar children's book about a hobbit's journey. Early reviewers and readers are enthusiastic, and the first print run is selling out before Christmas.
evt-09-21-1937-j-r-r-tolkien.prompt: What did the book's swift success lead the publisher to ask Tolkien for?

choices.text: A scholarly edition with academic notes
A stage adaptation for London theatres
A sequel focused entirely on elves
A sequel featuring more hobbits

evt-09-21-1937-j-r-r-tolkien.butterflyEffect: Buoyed by demand, Stanley Unwin asked Tolkien for a sequel about hobbits. Tolkien's response grew over seventeen years into The Lord of the Rings, published 1954–1955, which transformed the fantasy genre and made Middle-earth a permanent fixture of popular culture.

evt-09-21-1938-1938-new-england-hurrican.scenario: It is the afternoon of 21 September 1938 on the Long Island coast. The Weather Bureau's forecast promised the storm would veer out to sea, but the surf is rising fast and the sky has turned an odd copper color.
evt-09-21-1938-1938-new-england-hurrican.prompt: With no official warning issued, what should you do?

choices.text: Take a boat out to open water to ride out the storm safely
Recognize the falling pressure and rising surf as danger signs and evacuate to higher ground
Trust the forecast that the storm will pass out to sea and continue as normal
Head down to the beach to watch the unusually large waves

evt-09-21-1938-1938-new-england-hurrican.butterflyEffect: The storm made landfall as a major hurricane with almost no warning, killing an estimated 682 people, largely because forecasters had misjudged its northward turn. The catastrophe exposed serious gaps in U.S. storm forecasting and pushed the Weather Bureau toward major reforms in hurricane tracking and public warning systems.

evt-09-21-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is September 1943 on the Greek island of Cephalonia. Italy has just signed an armistice with the Allies, and German forces demand your division either surrender its weapons or fight alongside them. You are General Antonio Gandin, commanding the Acqui Division.
evt-09-21-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: Do you order your men to resist the German ultimatum?

choices.text: Order the division to resist the German demand
Evacuate the division to the Italian mainland
Agree to fight alongside German forces
Surrender all weapons peacefully to the Germans

evt-09-21-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Gandin chose to resist, and after days of fierce fighting his outnumbered division was overwhelmed. Hitler had explicitly ordered no prisoners be taken, and thousands of captured Italian soldiers were executed—one of the war's most notorious massacres of POWs, later a defining symbol of Italy's postwar reckoning with the war.

evt-09-21-1965-rhodesian-mission-in-lisb.scenario: It is June 1965 in Salisbury. You advise the Rhodesian government, which wants to open a diplomatic mission in Lisbon independent of the British Embassy there. London has just refused to endorse the idea.
evt-09-21-1965-rhodesian-mission-in-lisb.prompt: Do you proceed with the Lisbon mission despite Britain's refusal?

choices.text: Redirect diplomatic efforts to Pretoria instead
Ask Portugal to mediate with Britain first
Defer to Whitehall and cancel the mission
Proceed with the mission regardless of London's objection

evt-09-21-1965-rhodesian-mission-in-lisb.butterflyEffect: Rhodesia went ahead anyway, appointing Harry Reedman to head the mission—its first unilateral diplomatic act. It foreshadowed the Unilateral Declaration of Independence that November, and the Lisbon mission gave Rhodesia a diplomatic foothold in a sympathetic authoritarian Portugal until 1975.

evt-09-21-1968-zond-5.scenario: It is September 1968. You are a Soviet space program engineer tracking Zond 5, an unmanned capsule looping around the Moon with tortoises, fly eggs, and plants aboard, as it plunges back toward Earth's atmosphere.

choices.text: It landed precisely on target in Kazakhstan
The capsule burned up before reaching Earth
It failed to leave lunar orbit and crashed on the Moon
A guidance failure caused a steep ballistic reentry, splashing down off-course in the Indian Ocean

evt-09-21-1968-zond-5.butterflyEffect: A guidance failure sent Zond 5 into a steep, uncontrolled ballistic reentry rather than the planned skip trajectory, subjecting its cargo to punishing g-forces before it splashed down off course in the Indian Ocean. The scare exposed serious risks in the Soviet human circumlunar plan, contributing to delays that let NASA's crewed Apollo 8 beat the USSR around the Moon that December.

evt-09-21-1996-defense-of-marriage-act.scenario: It is September 1996, weeks before your re-election. Congress has passed the Defense of Marriage Act by veto-proof majorities, and your advisors warn that a veto could hand your opponent a potent campaign issue.
evt-09-21-1996-defense-of-marriage-act.prompt: As President Clinton, do you sign the bill defining marriage as one man and one woman for federal purposes?

choices.text: Send it to the Supreme Court for review first
Veto the bill
Sign the bill into law
Let it become law without his signature

evt-09-21-1996-defense-of-marriage-act.butterflyEffect: Clinton signed DOMA into law, and it barred federal recognition of same-sex marriages for years. The Supreme Court struck down its central provision in United States v. Windsor (2013), Obergefell v. Hodges (2015) legalized same-sex marriage nationwide, and Congress finally repealed DOMA outright with the Respect for Marriage Act in 2022.

evt-09-21-2004-green-day.scenario: It is September 2004. You are an executive at Reprise Records reviewing the master tapes for Green Day's new album, a sprawling punk rock opera about a disillusioned American named 'Jesus of Suburbia,' loaded with pointed political commentary.
evt-09-21-2004-green-day.prompt: What happened after Green Day released American Idiot?

choices.text: It became a massive hit, reviving the band and later inspiring a Broadway musical
The band was dropped by their label shortly after release
The album flopped and Green Day nearly disbanded
Radio stations refused to play it due to its political content

evt-09-21-2004-green-day.butterflyEffect: American Idiot became a critical and commercial smash, selling over 16 million copies worldwide and revitalizing Green Day's career after years of declining sales. Its success proved a concept album with explicit political themes could dominate mainstream rock, and it was later adapted into a Broadway musical in 2010.

evt-09-21-2013-westgate-shopping-mall-at.scenario: You are shopping in Nairobi's Westgate mall when gunfire erupts near the entrance on 21 September 2013. Screaming shoppers scatter as armed men move floor to floor.
evt-09-21-2013-westgate-shopping-mall-at.prompt: What is your best chance of surviving as the gunmen search the mall?

choices.text: Run for the main entrance in full view of the gunmen
Barricade yourself in a defensible room and stay silent until rescue arrives
Throw merchandise to distract the gunmen and slip past them
Try to negotiate directly with the attackers

evt-09-21-2013-westgate-shopping-mall-at.butterflyEffect: Survivors who hid quietly in storerooms and a walk-in freezer lived through the four-day siege; Kenyan special forces eventually retook the mall after part of it collapsed in a fire. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack as revenge for Kenya's military intervention in Somalia, and it triggered a major overhaul of Kenyan security and mall safety practices.

evt-09-21-2018-zak-kostopoulos.scenario: It is late afternoon on 21 September 2018 near Omonoia Square in Athens. Zak Kostopoulos, a well-known LGBT activist and drag performer, has entered a jewellery shop; a crowd gathers outside as shopkeepers accuse him of attempting a robbery.
evt-09-21-2018-zak-kostopoulos.prompt: What follows on the street outside the shop?

choices.text: He leaves the scene unharmed
Police arrive and protect him from the crowd
Shop owners calm the crowd before anyone is hurt
He is beaten by bystanders and then by police

evt-09-21-2018-zak-kostopoulos.butterflyEffect: Kostopoulos was beaten first by bystanders and then by responding police officers, dying on the way to hospital. Footage of the attack spread widely, galvanizing Greece's LGBT rights movement, and years later two men were convicted in connection with his killing.

evt-09-21-2019-2019-albania-earthquake.scenario: It is just after 3am in Durrës as a magnitude 5.6 earthquake shakes your apartment block, cracking walls and knocking plaster loose. Dozens of neighbors are already in the street.
evt-09-21-2019-2019-albania-earthquake.prompt: What should you do once the shaking stops?

choices.text: Go back inside to gather valuables before any aftershock arrives
Head straight to the port to leave the city by boat
Stay on your balcony to watch for further tremors
Move to open ground away from buildings and wait for official safety checks

evt-09-21-2019-2019-albania-earthquake.butterflyEffect: This September quake, which injured 49 people, turned out to be a warning tremor. On 26 November a far stronger magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck the same region, killing 51 people and becoming Albania's deadliest earthquake in nearly a century, exposing how many buildings had not been made safe after the first shock.

evt-09-22-1236-livonian-crusade.scenario: It is 22 September 1236, and you march with the Livonian Brothers of the Sword through the marshy forests of Samogitia, confident in your armored knights, when a pagan Samogitian army suddenly surrounds your column near Saule.
evt-09-22-1236-livonian-crusade.prompt: After this crushing defeat, what should the shattered Order do to survive?

choices.text: Ally with the pagan Samogitians against Novgorod
Merge the surviving brothers into the Teutonic Knights
Abandon the Baltic crusade and return to Germany
Appeal to the Pope for an entirely new crusading order

evt-09-22-1236-livonian-crusade.butterflyEffect: The Livonian Brothers of the Sword suffered catastrophic losses, including the death of their Grand Master, and the Order could no longer stand alone. In 1237 the survivors were absorbed into the Teutonic Knights as the semi-autonomous Livonian Order, cementing Teutonic dominance over the Baltic crusades for centuries.

evt-09-22-1789-united-states-postmaster-.scenario: You sit in the First Congress in 1789 as it formally establishes the office that will run the young nation's mail system under the new Constitution.
evt-09-22-1789-united-states-postmaster-.prompt: Who was appointed the first Postmaster General under this new office?

choices.text: Samuel Osgood
Alexander Hamilton
John Jay
Benjamin Franklin

evt-09-22-1789-united-states-postmaster-.butterflyEffect: Samuel Osgood became the first Postmaster General under the Constitution, a role distinct from Benjamin Franklin's earlier Continental Congress post. The office grew into a Cabinet position for nearly two centuries until the 1971 postal reorganization turned it into the independent US Postal Service.

evt-09-22-1869-das-rheingold.scenario: You hold a ticket for the National Theatre in Munich on 22 September 1869, where King Ludwig II has ordered a performance the composer himself is furious about.
evt-09-22-1869-das-rheingold.prompt: Why was Wagner so displeased with this premiere?

choices.text: He had not finished composing the score in time
He wanted it performed only as part of the complete four-opera Ring cycle
He demanded it be staged in Bayreuth instead
He objected to the singers cast in the lead roles

evt-09-22-1869-das-rheingold.butterflyEffect: Ludwig II forced the standalone premiere against Wagner's explicit wish to unveil the opera only as part of the complete Ring cycle. Wagner got his way seven years later, when the full cycle premiered at his purpose-built Bayreuth Festspielhaus in 1876, cementing Bayreuth as the home of Wagnerian opera.

evt-09-22-1908-independence-of-bulgaria.scenario: It is October 1908 in the old capital of Tarnovo. You stand beside Prince Ferdinand as he prepares to proclaim Bulgaria's full independence from the Ottoman Empire and take a new title for himself.
evt-09-22-1908-independence-of-bulgaria.prompt: What title does Ferdinand adopt to mark Bulgaria's new sovereign status?

choices.text: Emperor of the Balkans
Tsar
King
Sultan

evt-09-22-1908-independence-of-bulgaria.butterflyEffect: Ferdinand proclaimed himself Tsar, deliberately evoking Bulgaria's medieval imperial past. The declaration coincided with Austria-Hungary's annexation of Bosnia, and the combined shocks destabilized the Balkans, feeding the tensions that erupted into the Balkan Wars and, ultimately, the First World War.

evt-09-22-1914-world-war-i.scenario: You command the German submarine U-9, patrolling the North Sea off the Dutch coast. Through your periscope you spot three obsolete British cruisers steaming in a line without any destroyer escort.
evt-09-22-1914-world-war-i.prompt: What do you do when the second and third cruisers stop to rescue survivors from the first?

choices.text: Withdraw immediately, satisfied with sinking one cruiser
Save your remaining torpedoes for a larger warship later
Surface and offer the crews a chance to surrender
Torpedo the rescuing ships as well, since they present easy stationary targets

evt-09-22-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Weddigen sank HMS Aboukir first, then torpedoed HMS Hogue and HMS Cressy as they stopped to pull survivors from the water, killing roughly 1,450 British sailors in under an hour. The single-handed destruction of three cruisers by one small submarine shocked the Royal Navy and forced a rapid rethink of anti-submarine tactics and the vulnerability of surface warships.

evt-09-22-1934-gresford-disaster.scenario: It is the days after the 22 September 1934 explosion and fire at Gresford Colliery. Rescue teams have been unable to safely reach the ravaged underground sections, and colliery officials must decide how to proceed.
evt-09-22-1934-gresford-disaster.prompt: What did colliery management ultimately decide to do with the damaged underground workings?

choices.text: Continue recovery efforts until every body was found
Seal the sections permanently
Reopen the sections for full-scale mining within weeks
Abandon and flood the entire colliery immediately

evt-09-22-1934-gresford-disaster.butterflyEffect: Officials sealed the damaged sections permanently, meaning the bodies of most of the 261 men killed were never recovered. Combined with an inquiry that failed to conclusively establish a cause, the decision left lasting public anger and became a rallying point for miners' unions demanding stronger safety enforcement in British coal mining.

evt-09-22-1939-german-soviet-military-pa.scenario: You are a German officer standing in Brest-Litovsk on 22 September 1939, watching your troops line up alongside Soviet counterparts after weeks of fighting in occupied Poland.
evt-09-22-1939-german-soviet-military-pa.prompt: What did this joint parade actually mark?

choices.text: It announced the annexation of the city into Germany
It marked Germany's withdrawal to the pact's demarcation line and handover of the city to Soviet forces
It celebrated a formal military alliance treaty between the two powers
It was staged to accept Poland's formal surrender

evt-09-22-1939-german-soviet-military-pa.butterflyEffect: The parade formalized the German withdrawal to the demarcation line secretly agreed in the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact, handing Brest-Litovsk and its fortress to the Red Army. This visible cooperation cemented the partition of Poland and the uneasy German-Soviet alliance that would collapse less than two years later with Operation Barbarossa.

evt-09-22-1957-francois-duvalier.scenario: It is 22 September 1957, and you are a Haitian voter weighing your ballot, drawn to a soft-spoken country doctor named François Duvalier who campaigns as a populist champion of Haiti's black majority against the old mulatto elite.
evt-09-22-1957-francois-duvalier.prompt: What did Duvalier do after winning the presidency?

choices.text: He restored full democratic elections within a year
He built a repressive dictatorship backed by a personal militia
He stepped down peacefully after a single term as promised
He handed power to a coalition of the old elite parties

evt-09-22-1957-francois-duvalier.butterflyEffect: Duvalier, known as Papa Doc, swiftly built a personal dictatorship, creating the feared Tonton Macoute militia to crush opposition and declaring himself president for life in 1964. His brutal rule lasted until his death in 1971, when power passed to his son Jean-Claude, extending Duvalier family control over Haiti for nearly three decades.

evt-09-22-1965-india-pakistan-war-of-196.scenario: It is 22 September 1965, and you command troops dug in along the Kashmir front, having fought Pakistani forces for weeks, when word arrives that the United Nations Security Council has demanded an immediate halt to hostilities.
evt-09-22-1965-india-pakistan-war-of-196.prompt: What happens to the fighting as the UN ceasefire takes effect?

choices.text: Fighting escalates into a full-scale war over Punjab
Both armies comply and the guns fall silent along the front
Pakistan rejects the ceasefire and pushes deeper into Kashmir
India annexes Pakistani-held Kashmir before the ceasefire begins

evt-09-22-1965-india-pakistan-war-of-196.butterflyEffect: Both India and Pakistan accepted the UN-mandated ceasefire, ending weeks of inconclusive fighting over Kashmir. The following January, Soviet mediation produced the Tashkent Declaration, restoring pre-war positions, but the unresolved Kashmir dispute would help trigger another war between the two nations in 1971.

evt-09-22-1975-sara-jane-moore.scenario: It's September 22, 1975, outside San Francisco's St. Francis Hotel. President Gerald Ford steps toward his car as Sara Jane Moore, standing in the crowd, raises a revolver and fires.
evt-09-22-1975-sara-jane-moore.prompt: What actually happened as Moore fired her shot at Ford?

choices.text: A bystander grabbed her arm, deflecting the shot so it missed Ford
Secret Service agents tackled Ford to the ground before she could fire
Her gun jammed, preventing any shot from being fired
She fired twice, and the second shot struck Ford's motorcade car

evt-09-22-1975-sara-jane-moore.butterflyEffect: A bystander, Vietnam veteran Oliver Sipple, grabbed Moore's arm as she fired, deflecting the shot so it missed Ford and only slightly wounded another man nearby. Coming just weeks after Lynette Fromme's attempt on Ford, the incident triggered a major overhaul of Secret Service protective procedures; Sipple, meanwhile, was outed as gay by the press coverage that followed.

evt-09-22-1979-vela-satellite.scenario: It is 22 September 1979, and you are a US intelligence analyst reviewing data from a Vela reconnaissance satellite, which has just registered a distinctive double flash of light over the remote South Atlantic near the Prince Edward Islands.
evt-09-22-1979-vela-satellite.prompt: What should you tell your superiors the signal most likely indicates?

choices.text: A likely nuclear weapons test by an undeclared nuclear power
A malfunction in the satellite's own sensor equipment, nothing more
A routine solar flare with no security implications
A confirmed Soviet missile test in international waters

evt-09-22-1979-vela-satellite.butterflyEffect: Officially, a scientific panel concluded the signal was probably not a nuclear detonation, attributing it to a possible meteoroid strike or sensor glitch, though many analysts suspected a clandestine nuclear test by South Africa, possibly with Israeli involvement. The unresolved verdict became one of the Cold War's enduring mysteries and fueled decades of speculation about covert nuclear proliferation.

evt-09-22-1980-iraqi-invasion-of-iran.scenario: It is late September 1980. You advise Saddam Hussein, who believes Iran's post-revolutionary chaos makes it ripe for a quick, decisive strike to seize disputed border territory.
evt-09-22-1980-iraqi-invasion-of-iran.prompt: What actually happened to Iraq's invasion within its first two months?

choices.text: It swiftly captured Tehran, forcing an Iranian surrender
It triggered an immediate Iranian nuclear response
It was repelled entirely within days, never crossing the border
It stalled after occupying roughly 25,900 square kilometers of Iranian land

evt-09-22-1980-iraqi-invasion-of-iran.butterflyEffect: Iraq's advance stalled after seizing about 25,900 square kilometers, as Iranian forces mounted fierce resistance instead of collapsing. The stalemate dragged into an eight-year war of attrition that devastated both economies and left Iraq deeply in debt—debt that fed Saddam's later decision to invade Kuwait in 1990.

evt-09-22-1993-big-bayou-canot-rail-acci.scenario: You are the mate on a towboat pushing barges through fog on the Mobilee River at night. Your tow just struck something hard in the darkness — a railroad bridge you didn't see coming.
evt-09-22-1993-big-bayou-canot-rail-acci.prompt: What should you do immediately after your barges strike the rail bridge?

choices.text: Wait until daylight to inspect the bridge visually
Continue on your route since no damage is visible from the wheelhouse
Only file a report if the Coast Guard later asks about it
Immediately radio the railroad to report the collision

evt-09-22-1993-big-bayou-canot-rail-acci.butterflyEffect: The towboat crew did not report the strike, and eight minutes later Amtrak's Sunset Limited derailed on the damaged, misaligned bridge, killing 47 people in the deadliest wreck in Amtrak history. The disaster led to federal rules requiring vessel operators to immediately report any bridge collision to the railroad so tracks can be checked before trains cross.

evt-09-22-1993-1993-sukhumi-airliner-att.scenario: You are a loadmaster aboard a Georgian Tu-154 flying supplies into besieged Sukhumi during the war in Abkhazia, aware that separatist forces near the airport are armed with anti-aircraft weapons.
evt-09-22-1993-1993-sukhumi-airliner-att.prompt: What actually happened to the airliner as it approached Sukhumi?

choices.text: It took gunfire damage but made an emergency landing
It landed safely despite ground fire
It was intercepted and diverted to Sochi
It was hit by a surface-to-air missile and crashed, killing all aboard

evt-09-22-1993-1993-sukhumi-airliner-att.butterflyEffect: The aircraft was struck by a missile and crashed, killing everyone aboard. It was one of several airliners shot down over Sukhumi that week, deepening the humanitarian crisis of the siege and contributing to Georgia's loss of Abkhazia, which remains a breakaway region to this day.

evt-09-22-1995-1995-alaska-boeing-e-3-se.scenario: You are aboard Yukla 27, an E-3 Sentry AWACS lifting off from Elmendorf Air Force Base in Alaska, when a flock of Canada geese is ingested into both left engines just after rotation.
evt-09-22-1995-1995-alaska-boeing-e-3-se.prompt: What happened to the aircraft in the seconds after the bird strike?

choices.text: It circled back and landed safely on the remaining engines
It stalled and crashed into the woods, killing everyone aboard
It made an emergency landing on a taxiway
The crew ejected safely before impact

evt-09-22-1995-1995-alaska-boeing-e-3-se.butterflyEffect: With thrust lost on both left engines, the aircraft stalled and crashed into wooded terrain less than a mile from the runway, killing all 24 crew members aboard. The disaster pushed the Air Force to expand Bird/Wildlife Aircraft Strike Hazard (BASH) programs, including habitat management and radar-based bird detection near air bases.

evt-09-22-2006-maglev.scenario: It's September 22, 2006, at the Emsland maglev test track near Lathen, Germany. A Transrapid train is dispatched for a routine run along the elevated guideway, while a maintenance vehicle still sits on the track ahead.
evt-09-22-2006-maglev.prompt: What critical failure led to the collision that followed?

choices.text: Staff dispatched the train without confirming the guideway was clear of the maintenance vehicle
Severe weather forced the train off its magnetic track
A software glitch caused the magnetic levitation system to fail entirely
Anti-maglev protesters sabotaged the train's braking system

evt-09-22-2006-maglev.butterflyEffect: Staff failed to confirm the maintenance vehicle had cleared the guideway before dispatching the train, which struck it at high speed, killing 23 people. The disaster effectively ended Germany's domestic ambitions for the Transrapid technology, and serious maglev development shifted abroad, most notably to the Shanghai maglev line built with German technical input.

evt-09-22-2013-insurgency-in-khyber-pakh.scenario: It is Sunday morning, 22 September 2013, and you are part of the congregation filing out of All Saints Church in Peshawar after Mass, one of the city's oldest Christian communities gathered as they do every week.
evt-09-22-2013-insurgency-in-khyber-pakh.prompt: What happened as worshippers left the church that morning?

choices.text: Security forces intercepted a gunman before he could open fire
A car bomb in the parking area was defused before detonation
Militants set the church alight, forcing an evacuation with no casualties
Two suicide bombers detonated explosives among the crowd

evt-09-22-2013-insurgency-in-khyber-pakh.butterflyEffect: Two suicide bombers detonated their explosives among the departing congregation, killing scores of worshippers in one of the deadliest attacks on Pakistan's Christian minority. A faction linked to the Pakistani Taliban claimed responsibility, sparking nationwide protests and pushing the government to pledge greater protection for religious minorities amid ongoing sectarian violence.

evt-09-23-1122-pope-callixtus-ii.scenario: It's September 23, 1122, at Worms. You advise Emperor Henry V, who has fought bitterly with Rome for decades over who has the right to appoint bishops and abbots with the symbols of their office.
evt-09-23-1122-pope-callixtus-ii.prompt: To finally end the Investiture Controversy, what compromise should be reached?

choices.text: The Church alone controls spiritual investiture, the emperor retains a role in elections and temporal investiture
The emperor keeps sole power to appoint and invest bishops
The papacy renounces all claims over German bishoprics
Bishops are elected solely by local nobility, bypassing both emperor and pope

evt-09-23-1122-pope-callixtus-ii.butterflyEffect: The Concordat of Worms split investiture: the Church alone would grant the spiritual symbols of ring and staff, while the emperor kept a role in elections and could invest bishops with secular authority. The deal ended decades of conflict but permanently curtailed imperial control over the German church, weakening royal authority over time.

evt-09-23-1338-battle-of-arnemuiden.scenario: It is September 23, 1338, off the coast of Zeeland. You command the English cog Christopher, one of the few ships fitted with cannon and a handgun, but the French and their Genoese-hired galleys vastly outnumber your small fleet.
evt-09-23-1338-battle-of-arnemuiden.prompt: Badly outnumbered at sea, what should the English commanders do?

choices.text: Stand and fight despite being outnumbered, relying on the new artillery
Surrender immediately to avoid losses
Try to break through and flee toward an English port
Scuttle the ships rather than let them be captured

evt-09-23-1338-battle-of-arnemuiden.butterflyEffect: The English fleet was overwhelmed; Christopher and other ships were captured, and the engagement became the first recorded European naval battle to use artillery. The defeat was an early setback for England in the Hundred Years' War and signaled that gunpowder weapons would soon reshape naval warfare.

evt-09-23-1642-first-english-civil-war.scenario: It is September 23, 1642, near Worcester. You ride with Prince Rupert's Royalist cavalry, screening the King's baggage train, when Parliamentarian horse under Colonel Edwin Sandys suddenly appears near Powick Bridge.
evt-09-23-1642-first-english-civil-war.prompt: What does Rupert's cavalry do when the enemy horsemen appear?

choices.text: Charge immediately and rout the surprised Parliamentarian horsemen
Retreat across the bridge to avoid engagement
Dismount and form an infantry square
Negotiate a truce with Sandys before fighting begins

evt-09-23-1642-first-english-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Rupert's charge scattered the surprised Parliamentarian troopers in the war's first real cavalry clash, boosting Royalist confidence and cementing Rupert's reputation as a bold cavalry leader. The tactics proven at Powick Bridge were repeated a month later at Edgehill, the war's first major battle.

evt-09-23-1780-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is September 23, 1780, near Tarrytown, New York. You are one of three militiamen guarding the road when a well-dressed traveler claiming to be a civilian named 'John Anderson' rides up with a pass, but something about his boots looks wrong.
evt-09-23-1780-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What do you do about the suspicious traveler and his boots?

choices.text: Accept his pass and let him continue on his way
Escort him directly to the nearest British outpost
Shoot him on suspicion of spying without further inquiry
Search him thoroughly and hold him for questioning

evt-09-23-1780-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: The militiamen searched him and found hidden papers detailing West Point's defenses in Benedict Arnold's handwriting. The traveler was really British officer John André, whose capture exposed Arnold's plot to surrender the fort; Arnold fled to the British, and André was hanged as a spy on October 2, 1780. The plot's failure kept the Hudson River, and American momentum, intact.

evt-09-23-1803-maratha-empire.scenario: It's September 23, 1803, near the village of Assaye in India. You are Major-General Arthur Wellesley, and your small Anglo-Indian force faces a Maratha army many times its size, dug in behind a river.
evt-09-23-1803-maratha-empire.prompt: With no time to wait for reinforcements, what should Wellesley do?

choices.text: Attack immediately by crossing the river at an unguarded ford
Offer terms of negotiation to the Maratha commanders
Retreat and seek a more favorable position
Wait for reinforcements before engaging

evt-09-23-1803-maratha-empire.butterflyEffect: Wellesley launched a bold direct assault, crossing the river at an unguarded ford and routing the much larger Maratha force in brutal fighting. The victory at Assaye made his reputation, helped cement British dominance in India, and he later called it the finest thing he ever did in battle, Waterloo included.

evt-09-23-1920-1920-louisiana-hurricane.scenario: It is September, 1920, and a hurricane that formed off Nicaragua has intensified rapidly in the Gulf of Mexico into a Category 2 storm with 100 mph winds, now aimed squarely at Houma, Louisiana.
evt-09-23-1920-1920-louisiana-hurricane.prompt: As the storm bears down on your town, what is the safest course of action?

choices.text: Shelter in a sturdy inland building away from the coast
Wait until winds arrive before deciding what to do
Stay on the property to protect crops and livestock
Take a small boat out to open water to ride out the storm

evt-09-23-1920-1920-louisiana-hurricane.butterflyEffect: The hurricane struck Houma at full Category 2 strength with no weakening, then rapidly lost power over land as it pushed north. Remarkably, it stayed organized enough to be tracked all the way to eastern Kansas, where it finally dissipated on September 23 -- one of the farthest inland tracks of any Gulf hurricane of that era.

evt-09-23-1952-richard-nixon.scenario: It is September 23, 1952. You are Richard Nixon, Eisenhower's running mate, accused of pocketing an $18,000 political slush fund. Eisenhower is wavering on dropping you from the ticket, and tonight's national television broadcast is your only chance to save yourself.
evt-09-23-1952-richard-nixon.prompt: What does Nixon do to salvage his place on the Republican ticket?

choices.text: Deliver an emotional televised speech disclosing his finances and mentioning the family dog, Checkers
Sue the newspapers that published the allegations for libel
Refuse to address the allegations publicly, calling them baseless
Resign immediately from the ticket to spare Eisenhower embarrassment

evt-09-23-1952-richard-nixon.butterflyEffect: The televised speech, in which Nixon disclosed his finances and famously mentioned the family dog Checkers, drew a massive emotional response and flooded Republican headquarters with supportive telegrams. Eisenhower kept him on the ticket, and the broadcast became a landmark demonstration of television's power to let politicians appeal directly to voters over the heads of party leaders and the press.

evt-09-23-1961-john-f-kennedy.scenario: It is September 23, 1961. President Kennedy must fill a vacancy on the powerful U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, and civil rights attorney Thurgood Marshall, who argued Brown v. Board of Education, is under consideration despite fierce opposition from Southern senators.
evt-09-23-1961-john-f-kennedy.prompt: What does Kennedy do about the vacancy?

choices.text: Appoint Marshall as U.S. Attorney General
Nominate Marshall directly to the Supreme Court instead
Nominate Thurgood Marshall to the Second Circuit Court of Appeals
Withdraw Marshall's name to avoid a Senate confirmation fight

evt-09-23-1961-john-f-kennedy.butterflyEffect: Kennedy nominated Marshall, but Southern senators stalled the confirmation for nearly a year before he finally took his seat in 1962. The appellate record Marshall built there gave President Johnson the grounds to nominate him to the Supreme Court in 1967, making him the first African American justice.

evt-09-23-1962-flying-tiger-line-flight-.scenario: It is September 23, 1962, and you command a Super Constellation over the North Atlantic carrying 68 US soldiers. One engine is already shut down after a fire warning, a second has just lost oil pressure by accident, and now a third catches fire as you try to divert toward Shannon.
evt-09-23-1962-flying-tiger-line-flight-.prompt: With the aircraft crippled, what do you decide to do?

choices.text: Push on toward Shannon on the remaining engines
Attempt an emergency landing on the water near Iceland
Ditch the aircraft in the ocean and deploy life rafts
Turn back to Gander despite the distance

evt-09-23-1962-flying-tiger-line-flight-.butterflyEffect: The crew ditched the aircraft in the open Atlantic. Of the 68 aboard, 48 survived six hours in a life raft before the merchant ship MS Celerina found them. The disaster became a case study in cascading mechanical and human error during multi-engine emergencies.

evt-09-23-1964-typhoon-wilda-1964.scenario: It is late September 1964, and Typhoon Wilda, tied for the lowest pressure of any storm that year, is bearing down on Kyushu after peaking over the Philippine Sea. As a coastal official, you must brief residents on what to expect from the storm's path.
evt-09-23-1964-typhoon-wilda-1964.prompt: What actually followed after Wilda made landfall in Japan?

choices.text: It stalled over Kyushu for several days before dissipating
It crossed into the Sea of Japan, made a second landfall, then raced toward the Aleutians
It dissipated immediately upon reaching the coast
It curved back south toward the Philippines and dissipated there

evt-09-23-1964-typhoon-wilda-1964.butterflyEffect: Wilda made a first landfall on September 24, crossed into the Sea of Japan, then struck again on September 25 as a weakening tropical storm before racing northeast. It finally dissipated as a powerful extratropical cyclone near the Aleutian Islands, showing how far a typhoon's energy could travel after landfall.

evt-09-23-1967-1967-coho-salmon-fishing-.scenario: It's September 23, 1967, and you're one of hundreds of anglers crowding small boats onto Lake Michigan for the coho salmon run. The sky darkens fast and a sudden squall begins whipping the water into whitecaps.
evt-09-23-1967-1967-coho-salmon-fishing-.prompt: As the storm hits without warning, what is the safest immediate action for small-boat anglers?

choices.text: Anchor in place and wait out the squall on open water
Head immediately for the nearest shore, even against the wind
Keep fishing since the coho run would not last much longer
Raft boats together for stability until the storm passed

evt-09-23-1967-1967-coho-salmon-fishing-.butterflyEffect: More than 150 boats capsized, seven anglers drowned, and 46 were injured when the squall struck the crowded lake with little warning. The disaster exposed how unprepared small recreational boats were for sudden Great Lakes weather, spurring calls for better marine weather forecasting and safety education for sport fishermen.

evt-09-23-1973-september-1973-argentine-.scenario: It's September 23, 1973, and you're an Argentine voter heading to the polls months after Juan Perón returned from eighteen years of exile, running once again for the presidency with his wife Isabel as running mate.
evt-09-23-1973-september-1973-argentine-.prompt: What is the outcome as Argentines cast their votes in this election?

choices.text: Perón and Isabel win by a narrow margin
The election ends inconclusively, forcing a runoff
Perón and Isabel win in a landslide victory
Perón's opponents secure a surprise upset

evt-09-23-1973-september-1973-argentine-.butterflyEffect: Perón and Isabel won in a landslide with over 60 percent of the vote, but Perón died less than a year later, making Isabel the first woman to become president of a country in the Americas. Her troubled presidency amid economic crisis and violence set the stage for the military coup of 1976 and the brutal Dirty War that followed.

evt-09-23-1983-gulf-air-flight-771.scenario: It's September 23, 1983. Gulf Air Flight 771 begins its final approach into Abu Dhabi after departing Karachi, its baggage hold carrying a device planted hours earlier by militants.
evt-09-23-1983-gulf-air-flight-771.prompt: Which group was later identified as responsible for the bomb that destroyed the aircraft?

choices.text: The mainstream Palestine Liberation Organization
The Abu Nidal Organization
Iranian Revolutionary Guard operatives
Libyan state intelligence services

evt-09-23-1983-gulf-air-flight-771.butterflyEffect: Investigators traced the bombing to the Abu Nidal Organization, an Iraqi-based Palestinian militant splinter group. All 112 people aboard died, and the disaster remains the deadliest in UAE aviation history, prompting Gulf carriers to tighten baggage-screening security in the years that followed.

evt-09-23-1999-qantas-flight-1.scenario: It is the night of September 23, 1999. You are the captain of Qantas Flight 1, a Boeing 747 on approach to Bangkok's Don Mueang Airport through a violent thunderstorm, with the runway ahead reported as flooded.
evt-09-23-1999-qantas-flight-1.prompt: What happens as the aircraft attempts to land in the storm?

choices.text: The pilots abort the landing and divert to another airport
Air traffic control closes the runway before the aircraft can attempt landing
The aircraft lands safely without incident despite the storm
The jet touches down long and overruns the runway into rough ground beyond

evt-09-23-1999-qantas-flight-1.butterflyEffect: The 747 touched down long on the rain-soaked runway and skidded off the end into rough ground, injuring dozens of people aboard but killing no one. The accident became a widely cited case study on the dangers of landing on flooded runways and prompted a review of wet-weather landing procedures across the airline.

evt-09-23-2004-haiti.scenario: It's late September 2004 in Gonaïves, Haiti. Rain from Hurricane Jeanne pours onto hillsides long stripped bare by years of logging, and floodwater begins rushing through streets never built to hold it.
evt-09-23-2004-haiti.prompt: What underlying environmental factor turned this storm into one of Haiti's deadliest disasters?

choices.text: An earthquake struck simultaneously, worsening the flooding
The hurricane made a second direct landfall over the same area days later
Widespread deforestation left hillsides unable to absorb rain, causing flash floods and mudslides
A dam upstream collapsed, releasing a wall of water into the city

evt-09-23-2004-haiti.butterflyEffect: Decades of deforestation, driven largely by charcoal production, had left Gonaïves' hillsides unable to absorb rainfall, so Jeanne's rains triggered flash floods and mudslides that killed more than 3,000 people. The disaster exposed Haiti's severe environmental vulnerability, and the city would flood catastrophically again in later storms.

evt-09-23-2008-kauhajoki-school-shooting.scenario: It's September 23, 2008, less than a year after a similar attack at Jokela High School shook Finland. You are a lawmaker reviewing whether the licensing reforms passed after Jokela went far enough, as reports arrive of another shooting at a vocational college in Kauhajoki.
evt-09-23-2008-kauhajoki-school-shooting.prompt: What change did Finnish authorities pursue in firearms policy after this second attack?

choices.text: They installed metal detectors in every Finnish school
They restricted university admissions based on psychological screening
They raised the minimum age and tightened medical checks for handgun licenses
They banned all semi-automatic firearms nationwide

evt-09-23-2008-kauhajoki-school-shooting.butterflyEffect: Finland raised the minimum age for handgun licenses and tightened requirements for medical and psychological checks, part of a broader push to close gaps exposed by two shootings within a year. Critics argued enforcement still lagged, and debate over gun control continued after a further shooting in 2009.

evt-09-23-2016-rape-in-germany.scenario: It is 2016, and you are a Bundestag lawmaker under pressure after a wave of high-profile sexual assaults, including mass attacks on New Year's Eve in Cologne, exposed how narrowly German rape law was written.
evt-09-23-2016-rape-in-germany.prompt: What change do you push through to close the law's biggest gap?

choices.text: Limit the reform to criminalizing marital rape only
Leave the resistance requirement in place but add fines for harassment
Remove the requirement that victims physically resist their attacker
Simply raise minimum prison sentences for existing offenses

evt-09-23-2016-rape-in-germany.butterflyEffect: The Bundestag rewrote Section 177 to drop the old requirement that victims physically resist or be overcome by force, recognizing any clear verbal or physical refusal as non-consent. The reform also made group-committed assaults and unwanted groping easier to prosecute, and it mandated deportation for migrants convicted of sexual offenses, reshaping debates on migration and consent law across Germany.

evt-09-23-2022-election.scenario: It's September 23, 2022, in Russian-occupied Kherson. Armed soldiers go door to door with ballot boxes, asking residents to vote on joining Russia, as Ukrainian forces press a counteroffensive nearby.
evt-09-23-2022-election.prompt: Facing occupying soldiers at your door with a ballot, what is your safest course of action?

choices.text: Flee to Ukrainian-held territory before voting begins
Organize public protests against the referendum
Refuse outright and risk retaliation from occupying forces
Vote under duress to avoid drawing attention, as many residents did

evt-09-23-2022-election.butterflyEffect: Russia declared overwhelming support and formally annexed four Ukrainian regions days later, a move most of the world condemned as illegal and refused to recognize. The annexation deepened the war rather than ending it, as Ukraine continued fighting to retake the very territories Moscow claimed.

evt-09-24-1568-san-juan-de-ulua.scenario: It is September 1568, and your storm-battered English fleet under John Hawkins is anchored inside the harbor of San Juan de Ulúa when a Spanish treasure fleet under the new viceroy arrives and demands entry to the same narrow port.
evt-09-24-1568-san-juan-de-ulua.prompt: What does Hawkins do to avoid an immediate battle he cannot win?

choices.text: Attack the Spanish fleet before it can land
Abandon the ships and flee overland
Negotiate a truce to share the harbor peacefully
Surrender the fleet immediately to the viceroy

evt-09-24-1568-san-juan-de-ulua.butterflyEffect: The Spanish broke the truce days later, launching a surprise assault that destroyed most of the English ships; only two vessels, commanded separately by Hawkins and Francis Drake, escaped to England after a brutal voyage. The betrayal fueled Drake's lifelong hatred of Spain and helped inspire the wave of English privateering against Spanish treasure fleets that followed.

evt-09-24-1645-english-civil-war.scenario: It is 24 September 1645 near Chester. You ride with King Charles I's cavalry, sent out to relieve the besieged Royalist city, while the King himself watches from the city walls as Parliamentarian forces close in.
evt-09-24-1645-english-civil-war.prompt: What follows this clash outside Chester?

choices.text: The Royalists are decisively defeated, dooming the relief of Chester
Charles I is captured on the battlefield
Both armies withdraw without fighting
The Royalists break the siege and save Chester

evt-09-24-1645-english-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Royalists were routed at what became known as the Battle of Rowton Heath, one of the last major Royalist field armies broken in the war's aftermath following Naseby. The defeat doomed the relief of Chester and accelerated the collapse of Charles's cause, leading to his surrender to the Scots in 1646.

evt-09-24-1789-judiciary-act-of-1789.scenario: It is September 1789, and you sit in the First Congress tasked with turning Article III's bare promise of 'one Supreme Court' into an actual working judiciary. The Constitution left every detail of size and structure to you.
evt-09-24-1789-judiciary-act-of-1789.prompt: How many justices does Congress set for the new Supreme Court?

choices.text: Six justices
Nine justices
Seven justices
Five justices

evt-09-24-1789-judiciary-act-of-1789.butterflyEffect: The Act created a six-justice Supreme Court, 13 district courts, and 3 circuit courts, and established the office of Attorney General. Its Section 25, giving the Court appellate power over state court rulings on federal law, became the legal foundation for Marbury v. Madison in 1803.

evt-09-24-1841-omar-ali-saifuddin-ii.scenario: It is 1841 and you are Raja Muda Hashim, uncle to the Sultan of Brunei, struggling to crush a rebellion in Sarawak. The English adventurer James Brooke has offered his ships and men to help you restore order, but he wants something in return.
evt-09-24-1841-omar-ali-saifuddin-ii.prompt: What do you grant James Brooke in exchange for his military help?

choices.text: A monopoly on Brunei's pepper trade
The title and governorship of Sarawak
The island of Labuan as a personal estate
Command of Brunei's royal navy

evt-09-24-1841-omar-ali-saifuddin-ii.butterflyEffect: Hashim ceded Brooke the governorship of Sarawak, and by 1842 the Sultan formally confirmed him as Rajah of Sarawak. This founded the Brooke dynasty, which ruled Sarawak as a private kingdom for over a century until it was ceded to Britain in 1946 and later became part of Malaysia.

evt-09-24-1869-jay-gould.scenario: It is the morning of September 24, 1869, and you trade gold on Wall Street as the price rockets past 160, driven by Jay Gould and James Fisk's scheme to corner the market while President Grant's administration watches from Washington.
evt-09-24-1869-jay-gould.prompt: What does the U.S. Treasury do that afternoon to break the corner?

choices.text: Raise interest rates to cool speculation
Arrest Gould and Fisk on the trading floor
Ban all further gold trading for a month
Sell several million dollars of government gold reserves

evt-09-24-1869-jay-gould.butterflyEffect: The Treasury dumped roughly $4 million in gold onto the market, crashing the price from 160 to 133 within minutes and ruining many speculators caught on the wrong side. The panic, remembered as Black Friday, triggered a congressional investigation that exposed Gould and Fisk's ties to Grant's brother-in-law and sharpened public scrutiny of Gilded Age market manipulation.

evt-09-24-1877-battle-of-shiroyama.scenario: It is dawn on 24 September 1877. You are one of the last samurai loyal to Saigō Takamori, surrounded on the slopes of Shiroyama by thousands of Imperial troops armed with rifles and artillery.
evt-09-24-1877-battle-of-shiroyama.prompt: With no hope of relief and only swords against modern guns, what do the samurai do?

choices.text: Scatter into the countryside to continue guerrilla resistance
Charge down the hill in one final desperate attack
Negotiate terms through intermediaries with the Meiji government
Lay down arms and surrender to the Imperial forces

evt-09-24-1877-battle-of-shiroyama.butterflyEffect: Saigō's remaining men made a final desperate charge down the hill and were annihilated, along with Saigō himself. The Imperial Army's victory crushed the last armed samurai resistance, cemented Meiji government authority, and turned Saigō into a legendary tragic hero in Japanese memory.

evt-09-24-1903-alfred-deakin.scenario: It is September 1903, and you sit in Australia's young federal Parliament as Edmund Barton steps down, leaving the country's second prime ministership open to whoever can command a working majority in the new Commonwealth.
evt-09-24-1903-alfred-deakin.prompt: Which party base does Alfred Deakin lead into government?

choices.text: The Nationalist Party
The Protectionist Party
The Australian Labor Party
The Free Trade Party

evt-09-24-1903-alfred-deakin.butterflyEffect: Deakin formed a minority Protectionist government that depended on Labor support to survive votes, setting the pattern of shifting three-party alliances that defined early federal politics. He later fused the Protectionists with the Free Trade Party in 1909 to form the Commonwealth Liberal Party.
