evt-09-24-1911-hma-no-1.scenario: It is 24 September 1911 at Barrow-in-Furness. You are part of the Royal Navy ground crew walking His Majesty's Airship No. 1, nicknamed 'Mayfly', out of its shed on the water ahead of its first flight, as a strong crosswind picks up.
evt-09-24-1911-hma-no-1.prompt: With gusty wind buffeting the untested airship's hull, what should the crew do?

choices.text: Halt and wait for calmer conditions before moving it further
Proceed quickly to keep to the planned schedule
Rig a mooring mast on the spot and let it ride out the gusts
Add extra ballast to stabilize it in the wind

evt-09-24-1911-hma-no-1.butterflyEffect: The crew pressed on, and the airship's structurally weak frame broke in two under the crosswind before it ever flew. The loss set back Britain's rigid airship program just as Germany's Zeppelins were advancing, forcing Britain to restart its rigid airship efforts years later.

evt-09-24-1964-warren-commission.scenario: It is September 1964. You sit on the commission tasked with explaining President Kennedy's assassination to a shaken nation, weighing conflicting witness testimony and ballistic evidence before signing off on a final verdict.
evt-09-24-1964-warren-commission.prompt: What did the Warren Commission conclude in its report?

choices.text: Organized crime figures orchestrated the assassination
Cuban intelligence agents were behind the killing
A second gunman fired from the grassy knoll
Oswald acted alone, with no evidence of a conspiracy

evt-09-24-1964-warren-commission.butterflyEffect: The commission found that Lee Harvey Oswald acted alone in killing Kennedy, a conclusion many Americans doubted from the start. Persistent public skepticism fueled decades of conspiracy theories, prompted a 1970s House Select Committee re-investigation, and led Congress to pass the 1992 JFK Records Act mandating fuller disclosure of assassination-related files.

evt-09-24-1975-dougal-haston.scenario: It is 24 September 1975. You and Doug Scott have just become the first climbers to reach Everest's summit via the formidable Southwest Face, but darkness is falling fast and your oxygen is nearly spent far above any camp.
evt-09-24-1975-dougal-haston.prompt: What do you do to survive the night near the summit?

choices.text: Dig a snow hole and bivouac without oxygen overnight
Use remaining oxygen to force a rapid descent to base camp
Descend immediately in the dark toward the nearest camp
Signal for a helicopter rescue from the summit

evt-09-24-1975-dougal-haston.butterflyEffect: Haston and Scott dug a snow hole near the summit and survived a bivouac above 8,700 meters without supplemental oxygen or a tent, an unprecedented feat at the time. Their survival helped demonstrate that climbers could endure extreme altitude without bottled oxygen, influencing the lightweight, alpine-style ascents that followed, including Messner and Habeler's oxygen-free Everest summit in 1978.

evt-09-24-1993-norodom-sihanouk.scenario: It is September 1993 in Phnom Penh, and you sit in Cambodia's new constituent assembly, elected under UN supervision, deciding what kind of state should emerge after two decades of war and revolution.
evt-09-24-1993-norodom-sihanouk.prompt: What form of government does the assembly's new constitution establish?

choices.text: A republic led by an elected president
A one-party state under Hun Sen
An extended UN transitional administration
A constitutional monarchy under Sihanouk

evt-09-24-1993-norodom-sihanouk.butterflyEffect: The assembly restored a constitutional monarchy, crowning Norodom Sihanouk king while power was shared uneasily between co-premiers Prince Ranariddh and Hun Sen. The monarchy remained largely ceremonial, and Hun Sen's political dominance only grew, outlasting Sihanouk's 2004 abdication in favor of his son Sihamoni.

evt-09-24-2007-saffron-revolution.scenario: It is 24 September 2007 in Yangon. You march alongside tens of thousands in the streets, many of them Buddhist monks in saffron robes, protesting fuel price hikes imposed by Myanmar's military government. Soldiers are massing at intersections.
evt-09-24-2007-saffron-revolution.prompt: What happens as the junta responds to the swelling protests?

choices.text: The military violently cracks down on protesters and monasteries
The junta immediately reverses the fuel price increase
The army joins the protesters against the government
The generals agree to open multiparty elections that week

evt-09-24-2007-saffron-revolution.butterflyEffect: Within days the military launched a violent crackdown, raiding monasteries, beating and killing demonstrators, and arresting monks and activists. The brutal suppression drew global condemnation, but the movement's memory helped fuel pressure for the political reforms and elections Myanmar undertook starting in 2011.

evt-09-24-2014-mars-orbiter-mission.scenario: It is 24 September 2014 in ISRO's control room in Bangalore. After a nearly year-long journey, India's Mangalyaan probe approaches Mars for its first and only chance at orbital insertion.
evt-09-24-2014-mars-orbiter-mission.prompt: What maneuver must the spacecraft execute to be captured into Mars orbit?

choices.text: Use only small thrusters, keeping the main engine off
Accelerate further to slingshot into a wider orbit
Maintain current speed and rely on gravity alone to capture it
Fire the main engine for a controlled deceleration burn

evt-09-24-2014-mars-orbiter-mission.butterflyEffect: The probe fired its liquid engine for a precise deceleration burn and slipped into Martian orbit, making India the fourth space agency to reach Mars and the first nation to succeed on its maiden attempt. The mission's low cost boosted ISRO's global reputation and paved the way for later Indian interplanetary ambitions.

evt-09-24-2015-2015-mina-crowd-crush.scenario: It is 24 September 2015 near Mina, outside Mecca. You are a Hajj official watching two massive streams of pilgrims converge at a narrow street intersection en route to the stoning ritual at Jamarat.
evt-09-24-2015-2015-mina-crowd-crush.prompt: To prevent disaster, what crowd-management step is essential at this converging junction?

choices.text: Open additional side streets without added supervision
Withdraw security personnel to reduce crowd tension
Keep the two converging pilgrim routes physically separated
Raise the daily pilgrim quota to speed up the ritual

evt-09-24-2015-2015-mina-crowd-crush.butterflyEffect: The two pilgrim flows collided at the intersection, triggering a crush that killed more than a thousand people, the deadliest Hajj disaster on record. The tragedy prompted international scrutiny of Saudi crowd-control procedures and strained diplomatic relations with countries whose citizens made up large numbers of the dead.

evt-09-24-2023-nasa.scenario: It is 24 September 2023 in the Utah desert. You are part of NASA's recovery team as the OSIRIS-REx sample capsule, carrying material scooped from asteroid Bennu, drifts down under parachute after a seven-year journey.
evt-09-24-2023-nasa.prompt: What must the team do immediately after retrieving the capsule to protect its contents?

choices.text: Move it into a sealed, contaminant-free clean room before opening it
Ship it unopened straight to a foreign laboratory for analysis
Expose it briefly to open air to test for gas leaks
Pry it open immediately in the desert to check the sample

evt-09-24-2023-nasa.butterflyEffect: The capsule was flown to a temporary clean room before its main canister was opened, revealing more asteroid material than expected, some scattered outside the sealed container. Analysis of the Bennu samples later confirmed water-bearing minerals and organic compounds, strengthening theories that asteroids delivered life's building blocks to early Earth.

evt-09-25-275-aurelian.scenario: It's September 275. News reaches the Senate that Emperor Aurelian has been murdered by his own officers on campaign. For the first time in decades, the legions have left the choice of a new emperor to you and your fellow senators.
evt-09-25-275-aurelian.prompt: Whom does the Senate elevate to the purple?

choices.text: One of Aurelian's own military commanders
The praetorian prefect who led the assassination plot
A surviving relative of Aurelian
The respected elder senator Tacitus

evt-09-25-275-aurelian.butterflyEffect: The Senate chose the elderly senator Tacitus, a rare moment of civilian authority over the throne. He died within months, likely murdered, and the army swiftly reasserted control by elevating the general Probus, restoring the pattern of military-selected emperors.

evt-09-25-1066-harold-godwinson.scenario: It's 25 September 1066. You are King Harold Godwinson, fresh from a hard-fought victory over Harald Hardrada and Tostig at Stamford Bridge, when a rider brings word that William of Normandy has landed his invasion fleet in the south.
evt-09-25-1066-harold-godwinson.prompt: What do you do with your battle-weary army?

choices.text: Rest the army in York for several weeks first
March south at once to confront William before he can advance
Send envoys to negotiate a truce with William
Wait for Harald Hardrada's remaining allies to regroup against him

evt-09-25-1066-harold-godwinson.butterflyEffect: Harold force-marched his exhausted troops nearly 250 miles south in under three weeks, giving them little time to rest or gather fresh reinforcements. He met William at Hastings on 14 October with a depleted force and was killed, opening England to Norman conquest.

evt-09-25-1237-henry-iii-of-england.scenario: You advise Alexander II of Scotland as he meets Henry III at York in 1237. For generations Scottish kings have claimed the northern English counties, and now a settlement must be struck.
evt-09-25-1237-henry-iii-of-england.prompt: What did Alexander II accept in exchange for giving up Scotland's claim to northern England?

choices.text: Full sovereignty over Northumberland
A large one-time cash payment from Henry III
Control of the Isle of Man
Estates and manors in northern England, plus a fixed border

evt-09-25-1237-henry-iii-of-england.butterflyEffect: Alexander renounced Scottish claims to Northumberland, Cumberland and Westmorland, receiving instead estates held in fee within those counties. The border fixed by the treaty runs close to today's England-Scotland boundary, making it one of the oldest stable frontiers in Europe.

evt-09-25-1396-ottoman-wars-in-europe.scenario: It is September 1396 at Nicopolis, and you ride with the French knights of the crusader army, facing Bayezid I's entrenched Ottoman lines while Hungarian commanders urge patience.
evt-09-25-1396-ottoman-wars-in-europe.prompt: Do you launch an immediate cavalry charge against the Ottoman position?

choices.text: Retreat under cover of darkness to regroup
Wait for Sigismund's Hungarian troops to advance together
Charge immediately, ignoring Hungarian warnings to wait
Send envoys to negotiate a truce with Bayezid I

evt-09-25-1396-ottoman-wars-in-europe.butterflyEffect: The French knights charged ahead of the main army, broke through the first Ottoman line, then were encircled and cut down when Ottoman reserves and cavalry closed in. The crusader defeat ended the campaign, cemented Ottoman power in the Balkans for generations, and left many captured nobles to be ransomed at great cost.

evt-09-25-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is September 1775, and you lead a small mixed force of American volunteers and Quebec militia toward Montreal, believing the city is lightly defended and ripe for the taking.
evt-09-25-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What happens when you attempt to storm Montreal with your undersized force?

choices.text: You successfully seize Montreal and hold it for the Continental Congress
You retreat safely back to Fort Ticonderoga
You are surrounded and forced to surrender to British and Canadian militia
You link up with Benedict Arnold's column to besiege Quebec together

evt-09-25-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: British regulars and Canadian militia surrounded and captured Ethan Allen's party at Longue-Pointe. Allen was shipped to England as a prisoner, and the failed raid signaled that Canadians would not rally to the American cause, weakening the broader invasion of Canada.

evt-09-25-1962-north-yemen-civil-war.scenario: You are an officer in the Yemeni army in September 1962, days after Imam Muhammad al-Badr's coronation, as Abdullah al-Sallal moves troops toward the palace to declare a republic.
evt-09-25-1962-north-yemen-civil-war.prompt: Do you join al-Sallal's coup against the newly crowned Imam?

choices.text: Flee immediately to Saudi Arabia to avoid taking sides
Stay loyal to Imam al-Badr and defend the palace
Broker a power-sharing deal between the army and the imamate
Join al-Sallal's revolutionaries and help declare Yemen a republic

evt-09-25-1962-north-yemen-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Al-Sallal's forces dethroned al-Badr, who escaped to the Saudi border and rallied northern tribes to fight back, igniting a full civil war that lasted until 1970. Egypt backed the republicans and Saudi Arabia the royalists, turning Yemen into an early proxy battleground of the wider Arab Cold War.

evt-09-25-1981-sandra-day-o-connor.scenario: It is September 1981, and you sit in the U.S. Senate chamber as President Reagan's nominee, Arizona judge Sandra Day O'Connor, awaits the final vote to become the first woman on the Supreme Court.
evt-09-25-1981-sandra-day-o-connor.prompt: How does the Senate vote on confirming O'Connor?

choices.text: They confirm her by a narrow party-line vote
They confirm her unanimously, 99 to 0
They reject her over concerns about abortion rulings
They send the nomination back to committee for more hearings

evt-09-25-1981-sandra-day-o-connor.butterflyEffect: The Senate confirmed O'Connor unanimously, 99–0, making her the first woman to sit on the Supreme Court. She became a decisive swing vote for 25 years on issues from abortion to affirmative action before retiring in 2006.

evt-09-25-1987-penaia-ganilau.scenario: It's 25 September 1987 in Suva. You are Governor-General Ratu Sir Penaia Ganilau, having spent months trying to broker a compromise government after May's coup, when Lieutenant Colonel Sitiveni Rabuka strikes again, seizing power a second time.
evt-09-25-1987-penaia-ganilau.prompt: What does Rabuka do with the country's constitutional status this time?

choices.text: Declares Fiji a republic and abolishes the monarchy
Reinstates Ganilau with expanded powers under the Crown
Hands executive power to Indo-Fijian political leaders
Restores the elected Bavadra government

evt-09-25-1987-penaia-ganilau.butterflyEffect: Rabuka abolished the monarchy and declared Fiji a republic, stripping Ganilau of his role as Governor-General. Fiji left the Commonwealth, Ganilau became its first President that December, and the coup entrenched a pattern of military intervention that recurred in 2000 and 2006.

evt-09-25-1990-ram-rath-yatra.scenario: It's October 1990, and L. K. Advani's rath yatra is rolling through Bihar toward Ayodhya, whipping up huge crowds and rising communal tension along the way. As Chief Minister of Bihar, the yatra is about to cross into your state on its way to the disputed site.
evt-09-25-1990-ram-rath-yatra.prompt: What do you do to stop the yatra reaching Ayodhya?

choices.text: Provide a full police escort to let it pass peacefully
Order state police to arrest Advani and halt the convoy
Ask the central government to deploy the army
Negotiate directly with VHP leaders for a diversion

evt-09-25-1990-ram-rath-yatra.butterflyEffect: Bihar CM Lalu Prasad Yadav had Advani arrested at Samastipur, halting the yatra. The BJP withdrew support from V. P. Singh's government in protest, collapsing it, while the VHP campaign continued and culminated in the 1992 demolition of the Babri Masjid.

evt-09-25-1992-nasa.scenario: You are a mission engineer at JPL watching the Titan rocket carry the Mars Observer spacecraft skyward, the first American mission to Mars in nearly two decades.
evt-09-25-1992-nasa.prompt: What happens to Mars Observer eleven months later, as it nears the planet?

choices.text: Contact with the spacecraft is lost just before orbit insertion, and the mission is declared lost
It enters Mars orbit successfully and begins years of mapping
Ground controllers redirect it to fly past an asteroid instead
It crash-lands intact on the Martian surface and keeps transmitting

evt-09-25-1992-nasa.butterflyEffect: Contact with Mars Observer was lost on 21 August 1993, just before it was to fire its engines and enter orbit, likely due to a fuel line rupture. The costly failure pushed NASA toward its "faster, better, cheaper" strategy, leading to smaller, more frequent Mars missions like Global Surveyor and Pathfinder.

evt-09-25-2003-2003-tokachi-earthquake.scenario: It's 26 September 2003, before dawn on Japan's Tomakomai coast. A magnitude 8.3 earthquake off Hokkaido sends long, rolling shockwaves through the ground, and the crude oil inside the refinery's huge storage tanks begins to slosh violently against the tank walls.
evt-09-25-2003-2003-tokachi-earthquake.prompt: What danger from the tanks must responders act fastest to contain?

choices.text: Collapse of the refinery's main office building
Tsunami waves overtopping the harbor seawall
Rupture of the city's underground gas mains
Fire breaking out from sloshing oil inside the tanks

evt-09-25-2003-2003-tokachi-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The sloshing crude ignited, sparking fires at the Idemitsu refinery in Tomakomai that burned for days. It became one of the clearest cases of long-period ground motion causing tank fires far from the epicenter, prompting Japan to overhaul storage tank seismic design standards.

evt-09-26-bce46-julius-caesar.scenario: You stand in Caesar's newly built Forum in Rome, 46 BC, as Julius Caesar dedicates a grand temple to Venus, whom his family the Julii claim as their divine ancestress.
evt-09-26-bce46-julius-caesar.prompt: What is this dedication meant to proclaim about Caesar?

choices.text: That his family descends from the goddess Venus, giving him divine legitimacy
That he is renouncing the title of dictator
That he is declaring war on Egypt
That he intends to step down and restore the old Republic

evt-09-26-bce46-julius-caesar.butterflyEffect: The Temple of Venus Genetrix publicly asserted that Caesar's family descended from a goddess, binding his political power to divine legitimacy. His heir Augustus later built on this claim, using descent from Venus to help justify the imperial cult and his own authority as Rome's first emperor.

evt-09-26-1087-william-ii-of-england.scenario: It is September 1087, and you are an English baron gathered at William the Conqueror's deathbed in Normandy. His sons dispute the succession, and the old king must decide who receives the crown of England.
evt-09-26-1087-william-ii-of-england.prompt: Which son does the dying Conqueror name to inherit the English throne?

choices.text: Odo of Bayeux, his half-brother
Henry, his youngest son
Robert Curthose, his eldest son
William, who becomes King William II of England

evt-09-26-1087-william-ii-of-england.butterflyEffect: William named his second surviving son William, who was crowned William II within days while eldest son Robert Curthose received Normandy instead. The split inheritance sparked years of conflict between the brothers, ending only when their youngest brother Henry reunited England and Normandy after defeating Robert at Tinchebray in 1106.

evt-09-26-1142-stephen-king-of-england.scenario: It is late 1142, and you stand guard inside Oxford Castle beside Empress Matilda. King Stephen's army has surrounded the walls for weeks, supplies are dwindling, and the Thames beyond the ramparts has frozen solid under heavy snow.
evt-09-26-1142-stephen-king-of-england.prompt: How does Matilda escape the besieged castle?

choices.text: Wait inside the castle for Robert of Gloucester's army to arrive
Lead a mounted breakout through Stephen's siege lines
Slip out at night in white clothing and cross the frozen river on foot
Negotiate an immediate surrender with King Stephen

evt-09-26-1142-stephen-king-of-england.butterflyEffect: Matilda slipped out at night, dressed in white to vanish against the snow, and crossed the frozen river to reach safety at Abingdon and then Wallingford. Her escape kept her cause alive, prolonging the Anarchy for another decade until the Treaty of Wallingford secured the throne for her son, Henry II.

evt-09-26-1493-pope-alexander-vi.scenario: You are a Portuguese diplomat at the papal court in 1493. Pope Alexander VI has already granted Spain sweeping rights to newly found lands across the Atlantic, and now a fresh bull threatens to push the line dividing Spanish and Portuguese claims even further in Spain's favour.
evt-09-26-1493-pope-alexander-vi.prompt: What did Portugal do in response to these papal bulls favouring Spain?

choices.text: Appealed to England to arbitrate the dispute
Negotiated directly with Spain, leading to the Treaty of Tordesillas
Accepted the bull without objection and abandoned overseas exploration
Declared war on Spain immediately over the disputed claims

evt-09-26-1493-pope-alexander-vi.butterflyEffect: Dudum siquidem extended Spain's claims westward, alarming Portugal enough that it bypassed the Pope and negotiated directly with Spain. The result was the Treaty of Tordesillas in 1494, which redrew the dividing line and shaped the colonial boundaries of the Americas, including Portugal's later claim to Brazil.

evt-09-26-1580-francis-drake.scenario: You are aboard the Golden Hind as she noses into Plymouth harbour after nearly three years at sea, her hold heavy with Spanish silver and spices, her crew reduced to a weary handful. England has been at peace with Spain, at least on paper, and you know this cargo could change that.
evt-09-26-1580-francis-drake.prompt: What honour did Francis Drake receive after completing this voyage?

choices.text: He was knighted by Queen Elizabeth I aboard his own ship
He was ordered to return the treasure to the Spanish crown
He retired immediately from the sea on the Queen's orders
He was quietly stripped of his command to appease Spain

evt-09-26-1580-francis-drake.butterflyEffect: In 1581 Queen Elizabeth I boarded the Golden Hind at Deptford and knighted Drake in person, publicly endorsing a voyage that had plundered Spanish ships and ports. The gesture enraged Spain, deepened Anglo-Spanish hostility, and fed directly into the tensions that erupted in the Spanish Armada of 1588.

evt-09-26-1907-colony-of-new-zealand.scenario: You sit in New Zealand's parliament in 1907 as members debate a royal proclamation elevating the colony to Dominion status, a title already held by Canada and soon to be shared by Australia.
evt-09-26-1907-colony-of-new-zealand.prompt: What actually changed for New Zealand's government the moment Dominion status took effect?

choices.text: New Zealand immediately took over its own foreign policy
Māori gained full citizenship rights for the first time
New Zealand became a republic with an elected head of state
Little practical change at first; the governor still oversaw government

evt-09-26-1907-colony-of-new-zealand.butterflyEffect: The change was mostly one of title and prestige; the governor still represented the Crown and Britain retained control over foreign affairs. Dominion status nonetheless set New Zealand on the path toward full legislative independence, formalized decades later through the Statute of Westminster.

evt-09-26-1917-world-war-i.scenario: Dawn, 26 September 1917, near Ypres. You are an Australian infantryman waiting to advance on the German-held ridge of Polygon Wood as part of the Passchendaele offensive.
evt-09-26-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What tactic does your unit rely on to take the wood?

choices.text: A creeping artillery barrage advancing just ahead of the infantry
Detonating mines tunneled beneath German lines
A sustained gas bombardment alone, without infantry assault
A surprise night bayonet charge with no artillery support

evt-09-26-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The attack succeeded using a tightly timed creeping artillery barrage that advanced just ahead of the infantry, a "bite and hold" method proven days earlier at Menin Road. The victory reinforced this limited-advance tactic for the rest of the Passchendaele campaign, though the wider battle ground on for weeks at immense cost.

evt-09-26-1933-machine-gun-kelly-gangste.scenario: You are an FBI agent in Memphis on 26 September 1933, closing in on a house where the notorious kidnapper Machine Gun Kelly is holed up after the Urschel ransom job. Guns drawn, you kick in the door.
evt-09-26-1933-machine-gun-kelly-gangste.prompt: What does Kelly do when your team bursts in?

choices.text: He surrenders peacefully, reportedly shouting "Don't shoot, G-Men!"
He offers agents a bribe to let him go
He escapes through a back window
He opens fire with his Thompson submachine gun

evt-09-26-1933-machine-gun-kelly-gangste.butterflyEffect: Kelly surrendered without a fight, allegedly shouting "Don't shoot, G-Men!" — a phrase that stuck and helped popularize the FBI's nickname. The peaceful, headline-grabbing capture boosted J. Edgar Hoover's young Bureau and its public image as a modern crime-fighting force.

evt-09-26-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: You are a Red Army soldier pushing toward Tallinn in late September 1944, as retreating German forces and their Estonian auxiliaries race for the harbor to escape by sea.
evt-09-26-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What is the Red Army's key objective in this final push?

choices.text: Link up with Finnish troops still fighting Germany
Establish a corridor to besieged Leningrad
Seize Tallinn's port before German forces can evacuate by sea
Capture Estonian oil fields for the Soviet war effort

evt-09-26-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Soviet forces took Tallinn on 22 September 1944, though part of the German garrison managed a sea evacuation. The offensive completed the Red Army's reconquest of Estonia, beginning nearly five decades of Soviet occupation that lasted until Estonia regained independence in 1991.

evt-09-26-1959-typhoon-vera.scenario: It is the afternoon of 26 September 1959, and you live near Ise Bay on Japan's coast. Radio reports warn of an enormous typhoon approaching, but your house sits close to the shoreline and holds everything your family owns.
evt-09-26-1959-typhoon-vera.prompt: What should you do as the typhoon closes in on the bay?

choices.text: Stay inside your wooden house to protect it from looters
Move valuables to the roof and ride out the storm at home
Wait for an official evacuation order before moving
Evacuate immediately to higher ground before the storm surge arrives

evt-09-26-1959-typhoon-vera.butterflyEffect: Vera's storm surge overwhelmed sea walls and drowned low-lying areas around Ise Bay, killing over 5,000 people, many who had stayed in their homes. The catastrophe exposed how unprepared Japan's disaster response was and led directly to the 1961 Disaster Countermeasures Basic Act, reshaping national emergency management.

evt-09-26-1968-the-beatles.scenario: You're in the studio with the Beatles in September 1968, trying to finish John Lennon's "Happiness Is a Warm Gun" for the White Album. The song keeps lurching between wildly different tempos and styles within a single take.
evt-09-26-1968-the-beatles.prompt: What made this session especially demanding for the band and engineers?

choices.text: It was recorded in one take with no overdubs
Its multiple abrupt tempo and style changes required many takes
Yoko Ono's presence caused the session to be cancelled
Lennon insisted on recording live with a full orchestra

evt-09-26-1968-the-beatles.butterflyEffect: The song's abrupt shifts between several distinct musical sections meant dozens of takes were needed before one held together cleanly. Its fragmented, collage-like structure became a hallmark of the White Album's experimentation and later fueled outside conspiracy theories about hidden meanings in Beatles lyrics.

evt-09-26-1983-cold-war.scenario: It is just after midnight on 26 September 1983, deep in the Serpukhov-15 bunker outside Moscow. Soviet early-warning satellites suddenly report five US Minuteman missiles launched toward the USSR, and protocol says you must report it up the chain immediately.
evt-09-26-1983-cold-war.prompt: As duty officer, what do you decide to report?

choices.text: Confirm it as a genuine nuclear attack and pass it up for retaliation
Order an immediate counter-launch without waiting for confirmation
Refuse to make a call and abandon your post
Classify it as a system malfunction and do not escalate it as an attack

evt-09-26-1983-cold-war.butterflyEffect: Stanislav Petrov judged the alert a false alarm, reasoning that a real US first strike would involve far more missiles and that ground radar showed nothing. He was right — sunlight reflecting off clouds had confused the satellite sensors. His restraint, unrecognized for years, likely prevented a retaliatory nuclear launch and earned him posthumous fame as "the man who saved the world."

evt-09-26-1983-yacht-racing.scenario: It is 26 September 1983 off Newport, Rhode Island, and you're crewing aboard Australia II in the deciding seventh race of the America's Cup. Your syndicate trails the series and everyone aboard knows the New York Yacht Club has never lost this trophy in 132 years.
evt-09-26-1983-yacht-racing.prompt: What technical advantage helps Australia II claw back the series?

choices.text: A lighter aluminum hull untested by other syndicates
A larger mainsail that caught more wind than rivals
An additional crew member for faster tacking
A secret winged keel that improved upwind speed and turning

evt-09-26-1983-yacht-racing.butterflyEffect: Australia II's radical winged keel gave it superior speed and maneuverability, and the yacht won the deciding race to take the Cup 4–3. It ended the longest winning streak in sports history and shattered the New York Yacht Club's century-long monopoly, opening the America's Cup to fierce international competition and design innovation ever since.

evt-09-26-2008-yves-rossy.scenario: You stand on a cliff above Calais wearing a rigid carbon-fibre wing strapped to your back, four small jet engines humming beneath it. Below you stretches the open water of the English Channel, and Dover is barely visible on the horizon.
evt-09-26-2008-yves-rossy.prompt: How does the jetman actually get down safely once he reaches England?

choices.text: Glide the wing itself down onto a runway like a plane
Ditch in the sea and swim the last stretch
Deploy a parachute and drift down separately from the wing
Be winched down by a following helicopter

evt-09-26-2008-yves-rossy.butterflyEffect: Yves Rossy crossed the Channel in about 13 minutes, hitting speeds near 200 km/h, then deployed a parachute to land near Dover since the wing itself could not land. The flight cemented his "Jetman" fame and pushed forward personal jet-flight technology later showcased in military and entertainment demonstrations worldwide.

evt-09-26-2014-ayotzinapa-rural-normal-s.scenario: It is the night of 26 September 2014 in Iguala, Guerrero. Students from the Ayotzinapa Rural Teachers' College have commandeered buses, a common practice for travel to protests, when municipal police open fire on their convoy.
evt-09-26-2014-ayotzinapa-rural-normal-s.prompt: What happened to the 43 students after police intercepted them that night?

choices.text: Arrested and released the next morning
Taken to a military base and put on trial
Handed over to a criminal gang and forcibly disappeared
They escaped and returned to the school safely

evt-09-26-2014-ayotzinapa-rural-normal-s.butterflyEffect: Evidence and testimony indicated police handed the students to the Guerreros Unidos criminal group, and they were forcibly disappeared; only a handful of remains have since been identified. The case exposed deep collusion between local officials, police and organized crime, triggering nationwide protests and years of unresolved investigation that still shape distrust in Mexico's justice system.

evt-09-26-2016-ecnomiohyla-rabborum.scenario: You care for Toughie, the last known Rabbs' fringe-limbed treefrog, at the Atlanta Botanical Garden. Years after his species was rescued from a fungal epidemic in Panama, he is now alone in his enclosure.
evt-09-26-2016-ecnomiohyla-rabborum.prompt: Why couldn't keepers prevent the species from going extinct despite years of captive care?

choices.text: No surviving females remained to breed with him
Fungal disease killed his offspring before they matured
He was released to the wild and never found again
Keepers never attempted captive breeding

evt-09-26-2016-ecnomiohyla-rabborum.butterflyEffect: No surviving females of the species could be found, so Toughie had no mate and the species could not reproduce in captivity. His death in 2016 became a symbol of the global amphibian extinction crisis driven by chytrid fungus, spurring wider efforts to build captive 'arks' for other endangered frog species.

evt-09-26-2024-hurricane-helene.scenario: You are an emergency manager in Florida's Big Bend region as Helene bears down, forecast to make landfall as a Category 4 hurricane. Storm surge models show catastrophic flooding, and you must decide how hard to push residents to leave before the storm arrives.
evt-09-26-2024-hurricane-helene.prompt: What did officials do as Helene approached the Big Bend coast?

choices.text: They ordered mandatory evacuations for coastal and low-lying areas
They evacuated only tourists and left residents to decide for themselves
They delayed any warnings until the storm made landfall
They advised residents to shelter in place since the storm would weaken

evt-09-26-2024-hurricane-helene.butterflyEffect: Mandatory evacuations were ordered for low-lying coastal counties, but Helene's damage extended far beyond the coast, dumping torrential rain that caused catastrophic inland flooding in Georgia and the Appalachians of North Carolina. It became the deadliest hurricane to strike the U.S. mainland since Katrina, reshaping how forecasters communicate inland flood risk from major hurricanes.

evt-09-27-1422-treaty-of-melno.scenario: It is 27 September 1422 at the shore of Lake Melno. As an envoy for Grand Duke Vytautas, you sit across from Teutonic Knights delegates, hammering out the border that will end the Gollub War.
evt-09-27-1422-treaty-of-melno.prompt: What should you insist on securing for Lithuania in the treaty?

choices.text: Cession of Samogitia to the Teutonic Knights
Only a temporary truce, not a final border
Lithuanian control over Samogitia
Complete Teutonic withdrawal from Prussia

evt-09-27-1422-treaty-of-melno.butterflyEffect: The treaty fixed Samogitia within Lithuania while the Knights kept Lithuania Minor, and the resulting border held almost unchanged for roughly 500 years. A fragment of that 1422 line still marks the modern boundary between Lithuania and Russia's Kaliningrad Oblast.

evt-09-27-1851-east-india-company.scenario: It's 1851, and you are a ship's captain navigating the eastern approach to the Singapore Strait, one of the busiest and most hazardous shipping lanes in Asia.
evt-09-27-1851-east-india-company.prompt: Why has the East India Company just built a new lighthouse on the rocky outcrop of Pedra Branca?

choices.text: To mark a border between British and Dutch colonial territory
To warn ships away from dangerous rocks at the strait's entrance
To signal the location of a new naval base
To guide company ships toward a secret trading post

evt-09-27-1851-east-india-company.butterflyEffect: The Horsburgh Lighthouse cut shipwrecks along a vital trade route linking the Indian Ocean to East Asia. It later became the center of a long sovereignty dispute between Singapore and Malaysia, settled by the International Court of Justice in 2008 in Singapore's favor.

evt-09-27-1854-paddle-steamer.scenario: It is 27 September 1854 in dense fog off Newfoundland. You are a crewman aboard the paddle steamer SS Arctic, which has just collided with the French steamer Vesta and is taking on water fast, with too few lifeboats for everyone aboard.
evt-09-27-1854-paddle-steamer.prompt: What did the crew and male passengers actually do as the ship began to sink?

choices.text: Boat seats were assigned by lottery to ensure fairness
Crew and male passengers took the lifeboats, leaving women and children to die
The crew launched women and children into the boats first, as maritime custom demanded
Everyone stayed aboard together on the captain's orders until rescue arrived

evt-09-27-1854-paddle-steamer.butterflyEffect: Most crew and male passengers seized the lifeboats for themselves, and every woman and child aboard, including Captain James Luce's own wife and children, died. The disaster became a lasting scandal about the failure of "women and children first" at sea, fuelling public debate over maritime discipline and lifeboat regulation for decades afterward.

evt-09-27-1908-ford-model-t.scenario: It is 1 October 1908 at Ford's Piquette Avenue Plant. You are a foreman overseeing the very first production Model T, and Henry Ford wants a car ordinary families can actually afford.
evt-09-27-1908-ford-model-t.prompt: What production method should you adopt to keep the price low?

choices.text: Importing finished parts from European workshops
Custom handcrafting of each individual car
Standardized parts moving along an assembly line
Building only to special order like luxury makers

evt-09-27-1908-ford-model-t.butterflyEffect: Ford's assembly-line approach let the Model T's price fall from $780 in 1910 to just $290 by 1924, putting car ownership within reach of the American middle class. It reshaped daily life, spurring suburban growth and highway building across the 20th century.

evt-09-27-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 27 September 1940 in Berlin. As a Japanese diplomat, you are about to put your signature beside German and Italian counterparts on a pact meant to warn off outside intervention in the war.
evt-09-27-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: What commitment does signing the Tripartite Pact bind you to?

choices.text: Mutual defense if attacked by a power not yet at war
Sharing of military technology between all three nations
A single unified command over all Axis armies
An immediate joint invasion of the Soviet Union

evt-09-27-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The pact bound Germany, Italy and Japan to mutual defense if attacked by a power not yet in the war, aimed squarely at deterring the United States. It hardened American opposition to Japanese expansion and helped set the course toward the attack on Pearl Harbor fifteen months later.

evt-09-27-1949-chinese-people-s-politica.scenario: It's September 27, 1949, and you're a delegate at the first Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference session in Beiping, days before the People's Republic of China is due to be proclaimed.
evt-09-27-1949-chinese-people-s-politica.prompt: What national symbols does the conference adopt for the new state?

choices.text: Beijing as capital, the five-star flag, and a national anthem
A new official language and currency system
A federal constitution granting provincial autonomy
Nanjing as the new national capital

evt-09-27-1949-chinese-people-s-politica.butterflyEffect: The conference fixed Beijing as the capital, the five-star red flag, and 'March of the Volunteers' as the anthem, just days before the PRC's official founding on October 1, 1949. These symbols have endured as the identity of the People's Republic ever since.

evt-09-27-1964-bac-tsr-2.scenario: It is 27 September 1964 at Boscombe Down. You are test pilot Roland Beamont, strapped into the brand-new TSR-2, Britain's supersonic strike-and-reconnaissance prototype, cleared for its first flight.
evt-09-27-1964-bac-tsr-2.prompt: What did this first flight actually achieve for the TSR-2 programme?

choices.text: It broke the sound barrier on its very first flight, exceeding all expectations
It crashed on takeoff, killing the pilot and dooming the project immediately
It failed to leave the runway due to an engine fault
It completed a successful test flight, proving the airframe's basic soundness

evt-09-27-1964-bac-tsr-2.butterflyEffect: The TSR-2 flew successfully and showed real promise, but the project was cancelled by the new Labour government in 1965 over spiralling costs. Britain instead ordered American F-111s (later cancelled too) before settling on the Anglo-German Panavia Tornado in the 1970s, and the TSR-2's demise remains a byword for British aerospace ambition cut short by politics and budgets.

evt-09-27-1983-richard-stallman.scenario: It's September 27, 1983, and you're reading the Usenet newsgroup net.unix-wizards when a message from MIT programmer Richard Stallman appears, laying out an ambitious plan.
evt-09-27-1983-richard-stallman.prompt: What does Stallman announce he intends to build?

choices.text: A new hardware standard for personal computers
A free, Unix-compatible operating system called GNU
A proprietary Unix clone for IBM PCs
An early version of the World Wide Web

evt-09-27-1983-richard-stallman.butterflyEffect: The post launched the GNU Project, giving rise to GNU Emacs, the GNU C Compiler, and the GPL license. Combined with the Linux kernel years later, GNU software became the backbone of servers, Android, and much of today's internet infrastructure.

evt-09-27-1988-aung-san-suu-kyi.scenario: It is September 27, 1988, in Yangon. Weeks after the military crushed nationwide pro-democracy protests, activists gather to found a new political party to challenge the junta.
evt-09-27-1988-aung-san-suu-kyi.prompt: What role do the founders give Aung San Suu Kyi in the new party?

choices.text: General secretary of the National League for Democracy
Head of the ruling military council
Commander of the armed forces
Ambassador to the United Nations

evt-09-27-1988-aung-san-suu-kyi.butterflyEffect: She became general secretary of the National League for Democracy, which won a landslide in the 1990 election that the junta refused to honor. Decades of house arrest, a 1991 Nobel Peace Prize, and eventual leadership as State Counsellor from 2016-2021 followed.

evt-09-27-1996-taliban.scenario: It is 27 September 1996. You serve in President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government as Taliban fighters close in on Kabul, and the city's defenses are collapsing around you.
evt-09-27-1996-taliban.prompt: What should you do as the Taliban seize the capital?

choices.text: Publicly pledge loyalty to the Taliban
Flee north to join resistance forces
Surrender and negotiate a power-sharing government
Barricade the presidential palace and fight on alone

evt-09-27-1996-taliban.butterflyEffect: Rabbani fled north and became a leading figure of the Northern Alliance, which fought the Taliban for the next five years. The Taliban then ruled some 90% of Afghanistan, imposing strict Islamic law, until a US-led invasion following the September 11 attacks toppled their government in 2001.

evt-09-27-2014-2014-mount-ontake-eruptio.scenario: It's just before noon on September 27, 2014, and you're hiking near the crowded summit of Mount Ontake when the mountain erupts without warning, hurling rock and ash over the trail.
evt-09-27-2014-2014-mount-ontake-eruptio.prompt: What should you do to survive the sudden eruption?

choices.text: Run toward the summit to see the eruption
Take cover behind rocks or in a shelter and protect your head
Keep climbing to finish the hike quickly
Sprint downhill directly through the ash cloud

evt-09-27-2014-2014-mount-ontake-eruptio.butterflyEffect: The unannounced eruption during peak hiking season killed 63 people, mostly struck by falling rock, making it Japan's deadliest eruption in decades. It forced a national reassessment of volcanic monitoring and hiker safety warnings.

evt-09-27-2019-september-2019-climate-st.scenario: It is 27 September 2019. Word has spread through your school that students worldwide are walking out to demand climate action, part of a wave inspired by Greta Thunberg.
evt-09-27-2019-september-2019-climate-st.prompt: What should you do on the day of the global climate strike?

choices.text: Stay in class and ignore the strike entirely
Organize a counter-protest against the strikers
Walk out of class and join the mass demonstration
Wait for school administrators to officially approve participation

evt-09-27-2019-september-2019-climate-st.butterflyEffect: Millions of people across roughly 4,500 locations in 150 countries walked out that week, timed just before the UN Climate Summit. The strikes marked one of the largest coordinated youth-led protests in history and pushed climate policy further into mainstream political debate.

evt-09-27-2020-second-nagorno-karabakh-w.scenario: It's September 27, 2020, and fighting has erupted along the line of contact between Armenian and Azerbaijani forces in Nagorno-Karabakh.
evt-09-27-2020-second-nagorno-karabakh-w.prompt: What weapon proved decisive in Azerbaijan's offensive?

choices.text: A naval blockade of Armenian ports
Long-range nuclear-capable missiles
Turkish-supplied combat drones
Chemical weapons

evt-09-27-2020-second-nagorno-karabakh-w.butterflyEffect: Azerbaijan's drone-heavy campaign, using Turkish and Israeli technology, overwhelmed Armenian defenses within 44 days. The defeat led to a Russian-brokered ceasefire, territorial losses for Artsakh, and protests that nearly toppled Armenia's government.

evt-09-27-2024-hurricane-helene.scenario: It is late September 2024 and you live in Asheville, North Carolina, hundreds of miles from the Gulf Coast where Hurricane Helene is making landfall as a major hurricane.
evt-09-27-2024-hurricane-helene.prompt: Given you're far inland, what should you actually do to prepare?

choices.text: Wait for an official coastal-style storm surge warning before acting
Prepare urgently for severe flooding and landslides despite being far inland
Prepare only for strong winds, since flooding is a coastal problem
Relax, since hurricane warnings only matter for coastal residents

evt-09-27-2024-hurricane-helene.butterflyEffect: Helene's remnants dumped catastrophic rainfall on the Appalachians, and inland flooding in western North Carolina proved deadlier than the coastal landfall itself, killing many who believed distance from the coast meant safety. The disaster exposed major gaps in inland flood warning systems and reshaped how emergency planners communicate risk for storms far from where they make landfall.

evt-09-28-bce48-pompey.scenario: It is 28 September 48 BCE. Defeated at Pharsalus by Caesar, you flee to Egypt seeking refuge with the boy-king Ptolemy XIII, whose father you once helped restore to his throne. A small boat rows out to bring you ashore at Pelusium.
evt-09-28-bce48-pompey.prompt: Do you board the small boat and go ashore to meet the Egyptian court?

choices.text: Head for Africa to join Cato and the remaining Republican legions
Accept the boat and go ashore, trusting Ptolemy's court
Return toward Rome to negotiate terms directly with Caesar
Sail on to Cyprus to regroup with loyal forces

evt-09-28-bce48-pompey.butterflyEffect: Pompey trusted the invitation and was stabbed to death by Lucius Septimius as he stepped ashore, then beheaded. When Caesar arrived days later and was shown the head, he reportedly wept; the murder helped push him into the Alexandrian War and his alliance with Cleopatra against her brother.

evt-09-28-235-pope-pontian.scenario: It is 235 AD. Emperor Maximinus Thrax has arrested you during a persecution of Christians and sentenced you to the mines of Sardinia, an exile from which few return. You know the Roman church cannot function with an absent, imprisoned bishop.
evt-09-28-235-pope-pontian.prompt: What do you do about the papal office you can no longer carry out from exile?

choices.text: Resign the papacy so Rome can elect a new bishop
Continue governing the church secretly by letter
Appoint a coadjutor to govern in your name
Refuse to act and wait to be reinstated

evt-09-28-235-pope-pontian.butterflyEffect: Pontian resigned, becoming the first pope in history to abdicate rather than die in office, clearing the way for Anterus to be elected in Rome while Pontian died in the Sardinian mines soon after. His resignation set a precedent later invoked by popes such as Celestine V and Benedict XVI.

evt-09-28-351-constantius-ii.scenario: It is 28 September 351 on the plains near Mursa in Pannonia. You stand among Constantius II's eastern legions facing the army of the usurper Magnentius, whose seizure of the western throne has plunged the empire into civil war.
evt-09-28-351-constantius-ii.prompt: What was the outcome of this clash for Magnentius?

choices.text: He was captured and executed on the field
His forces were decisively defeated, and he later took his own life
The battle ended in stalemate and years of further siege
He won a clear victory and secured the western empire

evt-09-28-351-constantius-ii.butterflyEffect: Mursa Major was among the bloodiest battles of the age, gutting the field armies of both sides. Magnentius escaped the field but never recovered, taking his own life in 353 after further defeat, leaving Constantius sole emperor but commanding legions too weakened to easily face renewed threats from Persia and the Germanic frontier.

evt-09-28-1066-william-the-conqueror.scenario: You wade ashore at Pevensey on 28 September 1066 with Duke William's invasion fleet, boots sinking into the marshy Sussex shoreline as hundreds of ships disgorge men, horses, and timber.
evt-09-28-1066-william-the-conqueror.prompt: What does William do first to secure his beachhead?

choices.text: He marches immediately on London before Harold can react
He opens negotiations with Harold Godwinson for a truce
He disbands part of the fleet to save on provisions
He orders a temporary wooden fort built to secure the landing site

evt-09-28-1066-william-the-conqueror.butterflyEffect: William had his men erect a prefabricated wooden castle at Pevensey using timber shipped from Normandy, then moved his army to Hastings to build a second stronghold. This secured base allowed him to fight and win the Battle of Hastings on 14 October, launching the Norman Conquest that transformed English language, law, and aristocracy.

evt-09-28-1106-battle-of-tinchebray.scenario: It is 28 September 1106 near Tinchebray in Normandy. You ride with Duke Robert Curthose's knights as King Henry I's English and Norman forces close in for a decisive clash between the sons of William the Conqueror.
evt-09-28-1106-battle-of-tinchebray.prompt: What happened to Duke Robert Curthose after the battle?

choices.text: He was killed on the battlefield
He escaped to rally fresh forces in Normandy
He was captured and imprisoned by Henry for the rest of his life
He negotiated a truce and kept his dukedom

evt-09-28-1106-battle-of-tinchebray.butterflyEffect: Henry's decisive victory reunited England and Normandy under one ruler for the first time since the Conqueror's death, while Robert spent nearly three decades as a prisoner until his death in 1134. The battle cemented Henry's control of his father's cross-Channel realm and shaped Anglo-Norman politics for generations.

evt-09-28-1821-declaration-of-independen.scenario: It is 28 September 1821 in the National Palace, Mexico City. Agustín de Iturbide's Army of the Three Guarantees has just entered the capital, and as secretary you must draft the document declaring Mexico's independence from Spain in line with the Plan of Iguala.
evt-09-28-1821-declaration-of-independen.prompt: What form of government does the declaration commit newly independent Mexico to?

choices.text: A council of regional caudillos ruling without a single head of state
An immediate federal republic modeled on the United States
An independent monarchy, inviting a European prince to the throne
Continued union with Spain under greater autonomy

evt-09-28-1821-declaration-of-independen.butterflyEffect: The declaration followed the Plan of Iguala's promise of a constitutional monarchy, and when no European prince accepted the throne, Iturbide had himself crowned Emperor Agustín I in 1822. His empire collapsed within a year, and Mexico became a republic in 1823.

evt-09-28-1901-philippine-american-war.scenario: It is dawn on 28 September 1901 in Balangiga, Samar. You are a U.S. Army private eating breakfast with your company when armed townsmen and bolomen suddenly rush the mess hall from the church across the plaza.
evt-09-28-1901-philippine-american-war.prompt: What followed for the American garrison at Balangiga?

choices.text: Reinforcements arrived in time to save most of the men
Nearly the entire company was killed in the surprise attack
The garrison surrendered and was released unharmed
The garrison repelled the attackers without losses

evt-09-28-1901-philippine-american-war.butterflyEffect: Over forty American soldiers were killed, the U.S. Army's worst single loss since Little Bighorn. General Jacob Smith ordered savage reprisals across Samar, and the captured church bells were taken as war trophies to the United States, remaining a diplomatic sore point until returned to the Philippines in 2018.

evt-09-28-1924-united-states-army-air-se.scenario: It is 28 September 1924, and you are one of two surviving Douglas World Cruiser crews easing your plane down onto the water off Seattle. You have not seen home in over five months, since the flight departed on this same route back in April.
evt-09-28-1924-united-states-army-air-se.prompt: What does your landing at Seattle accomplish for the Army Air Service?

choices.text: You are forced to ditch just short of the finish
You set a new nonstop transatlantic distance record
You complete the first nonstop transcontinental U.S. flight
You complete the first circumnavigation of the globe by aircraft

evt-09-28-1924-united-states-army-air-se.butterflyEffect: The two surviving planes completed the first circumnavigation of the globe by air, having covered roughly 27,000 miles through 22 countries. The feat proved long-range military aviation was viable, boosted public and congressional support for air power, and became a landmark in the path toward a separate U.S. Air Force.

evt-09-28-1928-alexander-fleming.scenario: It is 28 September 1928 at St Mary's Hospital, London. You are Alexander Fleming, returning from holiday to find one of your discarded petri dishes of Staphylococcus contaminated by a stray mould, with a clear ring where the bacteria have died around it.
evt-09-28-1928-alexander-fleming.prompt: What should you do with this seemingly ruined culture dish?

choices.text: Log it as a minor error and repeat the experiment unchanged
Investigate why the mould is killing the bacteria around it
Discard the dish as a failed, contaminated experiment
Sterilize the lab immediately to prevent further contamination

evt-09-28-1928-alexander-fleming.butterflyEffect: Fleming investigated instead of discarding the dish, identifying the mould as Penicillium and its bacteria-killing substance as what would become penicillin, the first antibiotic. Developed for mass use during the Second World War, it transformed the treatment of infection and earned Fleming a share of the 1945 Nobel Prize.

evt-09-28-1972-cold-war.scenario: It is 28 September 1972 in Moscow's Luzhniki Ice Palace. You are on the Team Canada bench for the eighth and deciding game of the Summit Series, the score tied late in the third period against the Soviets.
evt-09-28-1972-cold-war.prompt: What happens in the final minute to decide the series?

choices.text: Paul Henderson scores the series-winning goal for Canada
The Soviets score late to force overtime
Canada loses the game and the series
The game ends in a tie, splitting the series

evt-09-28-1972-cold-war.butterflyEffect: Paul Henderson scored with 34 seconds left, giving Canada a 6-5 win and the series victory 4 games to 3 with 1 tie. The goal became one of the most celebrated moments in Canadian sports history and a symbolic Cold War triumph, cementing the Summit Series as proof that Soviet hockey could be beaten by NHL professionals.

evt-09-28-1975-knightsbridge.scenario: It is 28 September 1975, and you are a Metropolitan Police officer stationed outside Spaghetti House in Knightsbridge, where three armed robbers have barricaded themselves in the basement with staff hostages after a raid went wrong.
evt-09-28-1975-knightsbridge.prompt: How does the standoff finally end days later?

choices.text: Police storm the basement, ending the siege by force
The robbers escape through a service tunnel
The hostages are killed before police can intervene
The gunmen surrender and the hostages walk free unharmed

evt-09-28-1975-knightsbridge.butterflyEffect: After six tense days, the gunmen surrendered and released the hostages unharmed. The siege drew intense media coverage, spotlighted police negotiation tactics over armed assault, and fed contemporary debate in Britain over race, radical politics, and crime after claims linked the raiders to black liberation politics.

evt-09-28-1978-pope-john-paul-i.scenario: It is the early morning of 28 September 1978 in the Apostolic Palace. You are a Vatican aide who finds Pope John Paul I unresponsive in bed, just 33 days after his election.
evt-09-28-1978-pope-john-paul-i.prompt: What does the Vatican announce as the cause of his sudden death?

choices.text: An undiagnosed pre-existing illness worsened by travel
Food poisoning from a prior meal
A stroke suffered overnight
A myocardial infarction (heart attack)

evt-09-28-1978-pope-john-paul-i.butterflyEffect: The Vatican attributed his death to a heart attack. His sudden passing forced a second conclave within weeks, which elected Cardinal Karol Wojtyla as Pope John Paul II, the first non-Italian pope in over four centuries, who would go on to shape the Church's role in the Cold War's final decade.

evt-09-28-2006-typhoon-xangsane.scenario: It is 28 September 2006, and Typhoon Xangsane, known locally as Milenyo, is barreling toward Manila with destructive winds after already battering the eastern Philippines. As a city official, you must decide how to protect residents before landfall.
evt-09-28-2006-typhoon-xangsane.prompt: What should authorities prioritize as the typhoon closes in on the capital?

choices.text: Wait until after landfall to organize any response
Downplay the storm to prevent panic buying
Evacuate low-lying and coastal residents and halt public transport
Keep offices and schools open as scheduled

evt-09-28-2006-typhoon-xangsane.butterflyEffect: Xangsane tore through Manila and central Luzon before crossing the South China Sea to devastate parts of Vietnam and Laos, killing several hundred people and causing extensive flood and wind damage. The storm's toll pushed Philippine and Vietnamese agencies to strengthen early-warning systems and pre-emptive evacuation planning for future typhoons.

evt-09-28-2008-falcon-1.scenario: It is 28 September 2008 at Kwajalein Atoll. Your small company, SpaceX, has just one rocket and enough money left for a single attempt after three consecutive Falcon 1 launch failures nearly bankrupted the firm.
evt-09-28-2008-falcon-1.prompt: Do you proceed with this fourth Falcon 1 launch attempt?

choices.text: Scrub it and redesign the engine once more
Proceed with the launch despite the string of failures
Fly a stripped-down single-stage test instead
Delay until NASA announces its funding decision

evt-09-28-2008-falcon-1.butterflyEffect: SpaceX proceeded, and Falcon 1 became the first privately developed liquid-fueled rocket to reach orbit. The success arrived just weeks before SpaceX won a NASA cargo resupply contract, funding that led directly to the Falcon 9 rocket and the Dragon spacecraft.

evt-09-28-2012-battle-of-kismayo-2012.scenario: It is 28 September 2012. As a Kenya Defence Forces commander in Operation Sledge Hammer, you face Al-Shabaab's last major stronghold, the port of Kismayo, whose charcoal exports fund the insurgency. Ships carrying your troops and Raskamboni militia allies sit offshore.
evt-09-28-2012-battle-of-kismayo-2012.prompt: How do you move to seize the port city from Al-Shabaab?

choices.text: Rely solely on airstrikes against the port facilities
Launch a coordinated amphibious assault with Raskamboni forces
Negotiate a withdrawal directly with Al-Shabaab elders
Besiege the city and wait for Al-Shabaab to surrender

evt-09-28-2012-battle-of-kismayo-2012.butterflyEffect: KDF and Raskamboni forces launched an amphibious assault and captured Kismayo, cutting off Al-Shabaab's lucrative charcoal-export revenue. Denied its main financial base, the group increasingly turned to rural guerrilla tactics and cross-border attacks, including the 2013 Westgate mall siege in Nairobi.

evt-09-28-2014-2014-hong-kong-protests.scenario: It is the evening of 28 September 2014 outside Hong Kong's government headquarters. Riot police have begun firing tear gas into the crowd below you, who are blocking the road to protest Beijing's restrictive plan for the 2017 chief executive election.
evt-09-28-2014-2014-hong-kong-protests.prompt: What everyday object do protesters raise to shield themselves from the gas, giving the movement its name?

choices.text: A raincoat
A gas mask
A hard hat
An umbrella

evt-09-28-2014-2014-hong-kong-protests.butterflyEffect: The image of umbrellas raised against tear gas gave the 79-day occupation its lasting name, the Umbrella Movement. Though the government made no concessions on electoral reform, the movement forged a generation of activists and protest tactics that resurfaced on a larger scale in the 2019 Hong Kong protests.

evt-09-28-2018-2018-sulawesi-earthquake-.scenario: It is the evening of 28 September 2018 in Palu, Indonesia, minutes after a powerful magnitude 7.5 earthquake. Sirens sound a tsunami warning along the bay, but officials cancel it only a short time later.
evt-09-28-2018-2018-sulawesi-earthquake-.prompt: What is the safest choice for residents near the shoreline?

choices.text: Wait for a second earthquake before deciding
Move to higher ground regardless of the warning being lifted
Return home since the official warning has ended
Gather on the beach to watch for waves

evt-09-28-2018-2018-sulawesi-earthquake-.butterflyEffect: The warning was lifted roughly half an hour after being issued, just before waves several metres high struck Palu's coast, catching many who had gone back to low ground. Combined with catastrophic soil liquefaction that swallowed neighborhoods like Petobo and Balaroa, the disaster forced a rework of Indonesia's tsunami-warning system and evacuation procedures.

evt-09-28-2023-sycamore-gap-tree.scenario: It is 28 September 2023 near Hadrian's Wall in Northumberland. You arrive to find the beloved Sycamore Gap tree, a century-old landmark made famous by Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves, felled overnight in its dip beside the wall.
evt-09-28-2023-sycamore-gap-tree.prompt: What should authorities do upon discovering the tree has been deliberately cut down?

choices.text: Immediately plant a replacement sapling without investigating the cause
Launch a criminal investigation, since the tree was deliberately felled on protected land
Assume storm damage and quietly clear the site
Treat it as harmless vandalism not worth pursuing

evt-09-28-2023-sycamore-gap-tree.butterflyEffect: The felling was treated as criminal damage to a protected landmark near a World Heritage Site, and two men, Daniel Graham and Adam Carruthers, were later convicted and imprisoned. The stump has since sprouted new shoots, and conservationists have propagated saplings from its seeds to grow replacements across the country.

evt-09-29-1011-siege-of-canterbury.scenario: It is late September 1011. For three weeks Thorkell the Tall's Viking army has surrounded Canterbury, and a traitorous ealdorman has offered to open the gates. You are Archbishop Ælfheah, watching the walls about to fall.
evt-09-29-1011-siege-of-canterbury.prompt: What does the archbishop do as the city is overrun?

choices.text: Surrender the cathedral's treasury in exchange for safe passage alone
Stay with his flock and is captured by the Vikings
Lead a counterattack to drive out the raiders
Escape secretly through a hidden tunnel

evt-09-29-1011-siege-of-canterbury.butterflyEffect: Ælfheah refused to flee and was captured along with much of the city; when the Vikings later demanded a huge ransom for him, he forbade his people from paying it and was killed in April 1012. His martyrdom made him one of England's most venerated saints, and his cult at Canterbury predated and helped shape the later devotion to Thomas Becket in the same cathedral.

evt-09-29-1724-johann-sebastian-bach.scenario: It is Michaelmas, 29 September 1724, in Leipzig's St. Thomas Church. As Thomaskantor, you present a new cantata honoring the Archangel Michael, part of an ambitious yearly plan you began months earlier.
evt-09-29-1724-johann-sebastian-bach.prompt: What compositional plan is Bach following for this year's cantata cycle?

choices.text: A reuse of cantatas he had already composed years earlier in Weimar
A purely instrumental cycle without any vocal parts
A cycle built on strict musical paraphrases of each week's designated Lutheran chorale hymn
A set of cantatas modeled on Italian opera arias with no chorale material

evt-09-29-1724-johann-sebastian-bach.butterflyEffect: BWV 130 belongs to Bach's second annual cycle in Leipzig, the 'chorale cantata cycle,' in which nearly every week's piece paraphrases a set Lutheran hymn. This sustained project became one of the towering achievements of Baroque music and, after near-obscurity, was central to the 19th-century Bach Revival led by Mendelssohn.

evt-09-29-1923-mandate-for-palestine.scenario: It is 29 September 1923, and you are a British colonial official taking up your post administering Palestine under the newly ratified League of Nations mandate, charged with honoring commitments made to two different populations at once.
evt-09-29-1923-mandate-for-palestine.prompt: What dual obligation does the mandate instruct you to balance?

choices.text: Immediately create a fully independent Arab state
Partition Palestine into two sovereign states at once
Establish a Jewish national home while safeguarding the rights of the non-Jewish population
Transfer all administration directly to Jewish settlers

evt-09-29-1923-mandate-for-palestine.butterflyEffect: The mandate bound Britain to foster a Jewish national home per the Balfour Declaration while also protecting the civil and religious rights of Palestine's Arab majority. These conflicting commitments fueled recurring unrest through the 1920s and 1930s and left an unresolved territorial dispute when Britain withdrew in 1948.

evt-09-29-1940-royal-australian-air-forc.scenario: It is 29 September 1940 over Brocklesby, New South Wales. You are flying a Tiger Moth in a training exercise when another trainee's aircraft collides with yours mid-air, and the two planes lock together with one engine dead.
evt-09-29-1940-royal-australian-air-forc.prompt: What does the pilot of the still-powered aircraft do to bring both planes down safely?

choices.text: Attempt to cut the aircraft apart while still airborne
Both pilots immediately bail out and parachute to safety
Fly the locked pair of aircraft down to a controlled landing in a paddock
Radio for a mid-air rescue by a third aircraft

evt-09-29-1940-royal-australian-air-forc.butterflyEffect: The top aircraft's engine kept running, and its pilot flew the locked-together pair to a controlled landing in a paddock near Brocklesby, with both airmen walking away unhurt. The extraordinary escape became one of the RAAF's most celebrated wartime training stories and is still commemorated locally today.

evt-09-29-1941-the-holocaust.scenario: It is 29 September 1941 in German-occupied Kyiv. Posted notices order Jewish residents to report the next morning with documents and valuables, ostensibly for resettlement, to an assembly point near the Babi Yar ravine.
evt-09-29-1941-the-holocaust.prompt: What pretext did German occupation authorities give for this mass order?

choices.text: Relocation to a newly built ghetto within Kyiv
Reprisal for explosions that had destroyed German-occupied buildings in the city
Resettlement to farmland in occupied Poland
Transfer to factories for compulsory wartime labor

evt-09-29-1941-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: German forces used recent explosions in occupied Kyiv—actually set by retreating Soviet NKVD demolition teams—as a pretext for reprisal. Over two days at Babi Yar, Einsatzgruppen and local collaborators carried out one of the largest single mass shootings of the Holocaust, a method of killing that became a template for the systematic murder campaign across occupied Soviet territory.

evt-09-29-1954-willie-mays.scenario: It is Game 1 of the 1954 World Series at the Polo Grounds. Vic Wertz has just crushed a ball to the deepest part of center field, and you are Willie Mays, sprinting away from home plate with your back to the infield.
evt-09-29-1954-willie-mays.prompt: How does Mays make the play on the ball?

choices.text: Lets it drop and plays it on the bounce off the wall
Dives and traps the ball against the wall
Sprints flat-out and makes an over-the-shoulder basket catch
Climbs the outfield fence to make the catch

evt-09-29-1954-willie-mays.butterflyEffect: Mays hauled it in with an over-the-shoulder basket catch some 420 feet from home, then spun and fired a throw that kept the runner from scoring. The Giants won that game and swept the heavily favored Indians in four straight, and "The Catch" became the enduring visual symbol of great defensive baseball.

evt-09-29-1990-lockheed-yf-22.scenario: It is 29 September 1990 at Edwards Air Force Base. You are part of the test team rolling the new Lockheed YF-22 prototype into the air for the first time, locked in a head-to-head contest with Northrop's YF-23 for the Air Force's next stealth fighter.
evt-09-29-1990-lockheed-yf-22.prompt: What happened when the Advanced Tactical Fighter competition was decided?

choices.text: The YF-23 was selected for full production instead
The two designs were merged into a single new airframe
The YF-22 was selected and became the basis for the F-22 Raptor
Both designs were cancelled in favor of an upgraded F-15

evt-09-29-1990-lockheed-yf-22.butterflyEffect: The Lockheed-led YF-22 team beat the Northrop YF-23 for full-scale development, and the design evolved into the F-22 Raptor, which entered service in 2005 as the world's premier air-superiority stealth fighter. High costs later limited production to just 187 aircraft, reshaping U.S. Air Force fighter procurement for decades.

evt-09-29-1991-walt-disney-animation-stu.scenario: It is 29 September 1991 at the New York Film Festival, and you are a Disney executive facing a screening deadline for Beauty and the Beast even though several sequences are still unfinished, shown only in rough pencil-test animation rather than full color.
evt-09-29-1991-walt-disney-animation-stu.prompt: What do you decide to do about screening the incomplete film?

choices.text: Show only a short trailer instead of the full film
Screen it anyway as a work-in-progress premiere
Cancel the festival screening entirely
Postpone the festival slot until every scene is fully colored

evt-09-29-1991-walt-disney-animation-stu.butterflyEffect: Disney showed the film anyway, making it the first animated feature ever presented at the New York Film Festival, unfinished scenes and all. The enthusiastic reception confirmed the film's strength before its full theatrical release that November, and it went on to become the first animated film nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture.

evt-09-29-2005-john-roberts.scenario: It is 29 September 2005. Chief Justice William Rehnquist has died and President Bush has nominated federal appeals judge John Roberts to replace him. You are a U.S. Senator about to cast the deciding vote.
evt-09-29-2005-john-roberts.prompt: How does the Senate vote on confirming John Roberts as Chief Justice?

choices.text: Send it back to committee for further hearings
Reject the nomination in a close party-line vote
Confirm him by a wide bipartisan margin, 78–22
Filibuster the nomination indefinitely

evt-09-29-2005-john-roberts.butterflyEffect: The Senate confirmed Roberts 78–22, and he was sworn in the same day as the youngest chief justice in nearly two centuries. He went on to preside over decades of landmark rulings, including Citizens United, the Affordable Care Act cases, and later Dobbs v. Jackson, steering the Court's ideological direction well into the 21st century.

evt-09-29-2006-gol-transportes-aereos-fl.scenario: It is 29 September 2006, high over the Amazon in Mato Grosso. You are an investigator examining why a Boeing 737 and an Embraer Legacy business jet, both cruising at the same assigned altitude on opposite headings, failed to detect each other in time.
evt-09-29-2006-gol-transportes-aereos-fl.prompt: What key technical failure did investigators identify aboard the Legacy jet?

choices.text: The Legacy's engines had lost power minutes earlier
The Legacy's transponder was inadvertently switched off
The 737's autopilot malfunctioned and climbed without clearance
A severe thunderstorm forced both aircraft off course

evt-09-29-2006-gol-transportes-aereos-fl.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the Legacy's transponder had been inadvertently switched off, disabling the collision-avoidance warnings that should have alerted both crews. The disaster killed all 154 aboard the 737, triggered a lengthy binational legal battle over the American pilots, and led Brazil to overhaul air traffic control procedures and cockpit transponder protocols.

evt-09-29-2013-gujba-college-massacre.scenario: It is 29 September 2013, hours after Boko Haram gunmen attacked the College of Agriculture dormitory in Gujba, Yobe State. You are a state education official deciding how to protect students across the region.
evt-09-29-2013-gujba-college-massacre.prompt: What emergency measure follows for schools in Yobe State?

choices.text: Order the closure of schools across the state
Merge all colleges into one heavily guarded campus
Arm teachers and continue classes as normal
Deploy students to relocate classes inside military barracks

evt-09-29-2013-gujba-college-massacre.butterflyEffect: Yobe State shut down its schools indefinitely for fear of further attacks, part of a wider pattern of school closures across northeastern Nigeria as Boko Haram targeted students and educators. The crisis deepened international attention on the group's campaign against Western-style education, a theme that culminated the following year in the Chibok kidnappings.

evt-09-29-2016-2016-uri-attack.scenario: It is 29 September 2016, eleven days after militants killed 19 soldiers at an army base in Uri. You are an Indian military planner briefing the government on how to respond to camps just across the Line of Control.
evt-09-29-2016-2016-uri-attack.prompt: What action does India take against the militant launch pads?

choices.text: Limit the response to a formal diplomatic protest at the UN
Launch overnight surgical strikes on the launch pads across the LoC
Declare a full-scale war and mobilize the army along the border
Impose only an economic and trade blockade on Pakistan

evt-09-29-2016-2016-uri-attack.butterflyEffect: Indian special forces conducted publicly announced "surgical strikes" on militant launch pads across the Line of Control, the first time India openly acknowledged such an operation. It set a new precedent for overt cross-border retaliation, later echoed by the 2019 Balakot airstrikes after the Pulwama attack.

evt-09-29-2019-2019-afghan-presidential-.scenario: It is 28–29 September 2019 in Kabul. You work for candidate Abdullah Abdullah as preliminary results, amid Taliban threats and record-low turnout, show incumbent Ashraf Ghani narrowly ahead.
evt-09-29-2019-2019-afghan-presidential-.prompt: What did Abdullah Abdullah actually do after rejecting the disputed results?

choices.text: He conceded defeat and congratulated Ghani publicly
He rejected the results and set up a rival, parallel government
He called for the election to be re-run within a month
He withdrew from politics and left the country

evt-09-29-2019-2019-afghan-presidential-.butterflyEffect: Abdullah refused to accept the results and moved to form a parallel government with his own inauguration, plunging Afghanistan into a political crisis just as peace talks with the Taliban were gaining urgency. The standoff was only resolved in May 2020 when Ghani and Abdullah signed a power-sharing deal, with Abdullah taking charge of the peace process.

evt-09-30-1342-battle-of-morlaix.scenario: It is 30 September 1342 near Morlaix in Brittany. Your small Anglo-Breton force is vastly outnumbered by Charles of Blois's Franco-Breton army, and the enemy cavalry is preparing to charge your line.
evt-09-30-1342-battle-of-morlaix.prompt: What defensive tactic do the English commanders adopt to blunt the charge?

choices.text: Rely solely on archers standing in open ground
Charge the French cavalry head-on in the open field
Withdraw entirely without engaging the larger force
Dig concealed pits and ditches to disrupt the charging cavalry

evt-09-30-1342-battle-of-morlaix.butterflyEffect: The English dug concealed pits and ditches in front of their position, breaking up the French cavalry charge and allowing the outnumbered force to hold the field before withdrawing into nearby woods. The tactic of using field obstacles to protect dismounted men-at-arms and archers foreshadowed the defensive schemes England would use to great effect at Crécy and Poitiers.

evt-09-30-1791-wolfgang-amadeus-mozart.scenario: You are seated in the Theater auf der Wieden in Vienna on September 30, 1791, as Mozart himself takes the podium to conduct the premiere of his new opera, Die Zauberflöte.
evt-09-30-1791-wolfgang-amadeus-mozart.prompt: What role does the theater's manager, Emanuel Schikaneder, play on this opening night?

choices.text: He plays the high priest Sarastro
He plays the bird-catcher Papageno
He does not appear on stage at all
He plays the prince Tamino

evt-09-30-1791-wolfgang-amadeus-mozart.butterflyEffect: Schikaneder, who had also written the libretto, performed the comic role of Papageno at the premiere. The opera became an immediate popular success, though Mozart would die just over two months later, and The Magic Flute has remained one of the most frequently performed operas in the world.

evt-09-30-1863-georges-bizet.scenario: You are a Paris music critic in the audience at the Théâtre Lyrique on 30 September 1863, watching the young Georges Bizet's new opera Les pêcheurs de perles unfold before you.
evt-09-30-1863-georges-bizet.prompt: What is the general critical verdict on the new opera you file the next morning?

choices.text: Critics ignore it entirely in favor of rival premieres that week
The music is beautiful, but the libretto is thin and unconvincing
It is an instant, unanimous masterpiece hailed by all of Paris
The score is dismissed as derivative and forgettable
