evt-09-30-1863-georges-bizet.butterflyEffect: Critics largely praised Bizet's melodic gift while faulting the weak, formulaic libretto. The opera ran a modest eighteen performances, enough to mark Bizet as a composer to watch, though real fame would only arrive posthumously with Carmen over a decade later.

evt-09-30-1882-vulcan-street-plant.scenario: It is September 1882, and you are H.J. Rogers, a paper mill owner in Appleton, Wisconsin, who has just read about Edison's new Pearl Street Station lighting lower Manhattan. You want electric light for your mill and the town, but Appleton has no coal-fired power plant like New York's.
evt-09-30-1882-vulcan-street-plant.prompt: What power source do you use to run your new Edison generating station?

choices.text: Wind turbines along the riverbank
A coal-fired steam engine like Pearl Street's
Water power from the Fox River
Imported gas-powered generators

evt-09-30-1882-vulcan-street-plant.butterflyEffect: Rogers harnessed the Fox River's flow to drive the generator, creating the Vulcan Street Plant, the first hydroelectric station built to serve private and commercial customers in North America. Its success helped prove that falling water, not just coal, could electrify entire towns, encouraging hydroelectric development across the country.

evt-09-30-1918-nestor-makhno.scenario: It is 30 September 1918, and you ride with Nestor Makhno and Fedir Shchus as your small insurgent band prepares to strike an Austro-German occupation force near the Dibrivka forest in Ukraine.
evt-09-30-1918-nestor-makhno.prompt: How do Makhno's insurgents strike the much larger occupying force?

choices.text: Wait for Red Army reinforcements before attacking
Negotiate a truce before engaging
Challenge the garrison to an open pitched battle on flat ground
Launch a sudden ambush relying on surprise and local terrain

evt-09-30-1918-nestor-makhno.butterflyEffect: Makhno's fighters launched a surprise ambush that routed the occupying troops despite being badly outnumbered, a victory that spread his reputation across the Katerynoslav countryside. The win helped grow the Makhnovshchina into a mass peasant movement that would control large parts of southern Ukraine for the next three years.

evt-09-30-1938-munich-agreement.scenario: It is 30 September 1938, and you are a British diplomat waiting outside the conference room in Munich. Hitler, Chamberlain, Daladier and Mussolini are deciding the fate of Czechoslovakia's Sudetenland without a single Czechoslovak representative in the room.
evt-09-30-1938-munich-agreement.prompt: What does the Munich conference actually decide to do?

choices.text: Refer the dispute to the League of Nations for arbitration
Guarantee Czechoslovakia's borders and demand German withdrawal
Hand the Sudetenland to Germany without Czechoslovak consent
Partition the Sudetenland between Germany and Czechoslovakia equally

evt-09-30-1938-munich-agreement.butterflyEffect: The four powers ceded the Sudetenland to Germany, and Chamberlain returned home promising "peace for our time." Czechoslovakia lost its fortified border region and much of its industry; within six months Germany occupied the rest of the country, and within a year Britain and France were at war with Hitler anyway.

evt-09-30-1939-nbc.scenario: It is September 30, 1939, and you are part of NBC's small crew perched with a single bulky camera in the stands at Randalls Island, about to televise a college football game to the handful of homes in New York with a television set.
evt-09-30-1939-nbc.prompt: What actually happened after this broadcast reached viewers?

choices.text: It was seen live by a nationwide audience
The NFL banned television cameras afterward
It reached only a few hundred sets in the New York area
NBC immediately signed a national network of affiliates

evt-09-30-1939-nbc.butterflyEffect: The Fordham–Waynesburg game reached only a few hundred television sets scattered across New York City, since sets were rare and expensive. It was nonetheless the first televised American football game, and it planted the seed for what would eventually become a multibillion-dollar sports broadcasting industry.

evt-09-30-1939-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 30 September 1939. Poland has been overrun by German and Soviet forces, and its government has fled abroad through Romania to France. Polish officials abroad must decide who will lead a government-in-exile to keep the nation's cause alive.
evt-09-30-1939-world-war-ii.prompt: What happens next for the exiled Polish leadership?

choices.text: Polish officials negotiate a settlement with Germany
Sikorski is named prime minister of a Polish government-in-exile
The government dissolves, leaving only underground resistance cells
A Soviet-backed provisional government is formed instead

evt-09-30-1939-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: General Władysław Sikorski became prime minister of the Polish government-in-exile, first in France and later London, which the Allies recognized as Poland's legitimate government. Polish forces under his authority fought on in the Battle of Britain and at Monte Cassino, while relations with the Soviets fractured after the 1943 Katyn revelations; Sikorski himself died in a plane crash later that year.

evt-09-30-1955-james-dean.scenario: It is the afternoon of 30 September 1955, and you are James Dean, driving your new Porsche 550 Spyder along a California highway toward a road race in Salinas, with dusk approaching and the open road ahead.
evt-09-30-1955-james-dean.prompt: What happens as Dean's Porsche reaches a highway intersection near Cholame?

choices.text: He stops safely to let the other car pass
His car collides with another vehicle turning at the intersection
He is pulled over for speeding before reaching the intersection
He arrives at the race without incident

evt-09-30-1955-james-dean.butterflyEffect: Dean's Porsche collided with another car at the intersection, and he died of his injuries at just 24 years old, before two of his three major films had even been released. The crash cemented his image as a symbol of youthful rebellion, and Rebel Without a Cause and Giant reached audiences already mourning a legend.

evt-09-30-1982-cheers.scenario: You are an NBC scheduling executive in October 1982. Cheers has just aired its pilot and the overnight ratings place it near the bottom of the week's rankings, far behind established sitcoms.
evt-09-30-1982-cheers.prompt: What does NBC decide to do with the low-rated new show?

choices.text: Sell the show to a rival network
Cancel it immediately after the pilot
Renew it despite the poor ratings
Recast the leads and reshoot the pilot

evt-09-30-1982-cheers.butterflyEffect: NBC kept Cheers on the air despite its weak start, betting on critical praise and word of mouth. The show slowly built an audience, ran for eleven seasons, won multiple Emmys, and its bar-room setting and cast later spun off the hit series Frasier.

evt-09-30-1994-space-shuttle-endeavour.scenario: It is 30 September 1994 at Kennedy Space Center. You are part of the launch team preparing Endeavour's second countdown for STS-68, after an engine sensor scrubbed the first attempt just 1.9 seconds before liftoff in August.
evt-09-30-1994-space-shuttle-endeavour.prompt: What happens on this second countdown attempt?

choices.text: A booster seal issue forces a lengthy postponement
Endeavour launches successfully carrying the Space Radar Laboratory
The same engine sensor triggers another shutdown at the pad
The launch is scrubbed again due to weather over the Cape

evt-09-30-1994-space-shuttle-endeavour.butterflyEffect: Endeavour lifted off successfully, carrying the Space Radar Laboratory to map Earth's surface and monitor environmental change from orbit. The near-pad abort in August led engineers to refine sensor calibration procedures, reducing the risk of similar last-second shutdowns on later shuttle missions.

evt-09-30-1999-tokaimura-nuclear-acciden.scenario: It is 30 September 1999 at the JCO fuel processing plant in Tōkai, Japan. You and two colleagues are manually pouring uranyl nitrate solution from buckets into a precipitation tank, bypassing the plant's approved procedure to finish the batch faster.
evt-09-30-1999-tokaimura-nuclear-acciden.prompt: What should the technicians do to avoid a criticality accident?

choices.text: Follow the certified procedure and equipment limiting batch size and mass
Keep pouring by hand with larger buckets to save time
Combine several days' batches into one tank for efficiency
Skip the tank's neutron absorbers since the batch seems small

evt-09-30-1999-tokaimura-nuclear-acciden.butterflyEffect: The workers' shortcut concentrated far more fissile uranium in the tank than its design allowed, triggering an uncontrolled chain reaction that bathed the room in radiation. Two of the three technicians, Hisashi Ouchi and Masato Shinohara, later died from their exposure, and the accident forced Japan to overhaul nuclear plant safety oversight and worker training nationwide.

evt-09-30-2009-2009-sumatra-earthquakes.scenario: It is the evening of 30 September 2009, and you coordinate emergency response in Padang, West Sumatra, hours after a magnitude 7.6 earthquake has collapsed thousands of buildings across the region.
evt-09-30-2009-2009-sumatra-earthquakes.prompt: What is the most urgent priority for responders in the first hours after the quake?

choices.text: Wait for international teams to arrive before starting search efforts
Prioritize restoring electricity over search and rescue
Begin rebuilding damaged roads before addressing casualties
Search collapsed buildings for trapped survivors before aftershocks bring down more structures

evt-09-30-2009-2009-sumatra-earthquakes.butterflyEffect: Rescue teams focused on pulling survivors from collapsed multi-story buildings in Padang while roads and communications remained badly damaged, slowing aid to outlying districts like Padang Pariaman. The disaster drew international relief efforts and renewed scrutiny of weak construction standards across seismically active Sumatra.

evt-09-30-2016-hurricane-matthew.scenario: It is 30 September 2016, and Hurricane Matthew has just strengthened into a Category 5 storm in the Caribbean. You are a Florida emergency official watching its track edge toward the southeastern U.S. coastline.
evt-09-30-2016-hurricane-matthew.prompt: What do you order as the storm approaches, before its final path is certain?

choices.text: Focus resources solely on the Bahamas rather than Florida
Order coastal evacuations ahead of the storm's uncertain track
Advise residents the storm poses no threat since it may stay offshore
Wait until landfall is confirmed before issuing any warnings

evt-09-30-2016-hurricane-matthew.butterflyEffect: Matthew devastated Haiti and battered Cuba and the Bahamas before paralleling Florida's coast just offshore, sparing the mainland the direct hit officials feared. Evacuation orders issued along the coastline turned out to be a costly precaution rather than a necessity for Florida, though Haiti's humanitarian crisis from the storm was severe.

evt-09-30-2016-van-gogh-museum.scenario: You are an Italian anti-mafia investigator in September 2016. A tip leads your team to a countryside property near Naples linked to the Camorra, where two paintings stolen from Amsterdam's Van Gogh Museum back in 2002 are believed to be hidden.
evt-09-30-2016-van-gogh-museum.prompt: What do investigators do to recover the missing paintings?

choices.text: Purchase the paintings quietly on the black market
Wait for a ransom demand from the thieves
Negotiate a reward through the museum's insurer
Raid the Camorra-linked property directly

evt-09-30-2016-van-gogh-museum.butterflyEffect: Italian authorities raided the property and recovered 'Poppy Flowers' and 'View of the Sea at Scheveningen,' stolen in a 2002 museum heist, worth a combined 100 million dollars. Their return to the Van Gogh Museum exposed how organized crime groups had come to treat stolen masterpieces as long-term financial assets rather than quick cash.

evt-09-30-2019-martin-vizcarra.scenario: You are President Martín Vizcarra on September 30, 2019, locked in a bitter standoff with a Congress that keeps blocking your anti-corruption reforms and has just moved to appoint judges over your objections.
evt-09-30-2019-martin-vizcarra.prompt: What does Vizcarra do to break the deadlock with Congress?

choices.text: Negotiate a compromise reform package
Resign the presidency
Dissolve Congress and call new elections
Declare martial law across Peru

evt-09-30-2019-martin-vizcarra.butterflyEffect: Vizcarra dissolved Congress and called for new legislative elections, arguing lawmakers had denied him a vote of confidence. The move triggered a constitutional crisis, new elections in January 2020, and set off a chain of instability that eventually saw Vizcarra himself impeached later that same year.

evt-10-01-959-edgar-king-of-england.scenario: It is 959. Your brother King Eadwig, who ruled Wessex while you governed Mercia and Northumbria after an earlier rift split the kingdom, has just died. As Edgar, you now stand to claim the whole of England.

choices.text: The kingdom splits further among rival claimants
The witan refuses to recognize any king for a decade
England is reunited under a single king for the first time since the split
A Danish army seizes the throne amid the confusion

evt-10-01-959-edgar-king-of-england.butterflyEffect: Edgar became king of a reunited England, ending the division Eadwig's reign had caused. He then delayed his own coronation until 973, staging it at Bath in a rite devised by Archbishop Dunstan that became the template for English coronations, including those still performed centuries later.

evt-10-01-1800-third-treaty-of-san-ildef.scenario: It's 1 October 1800 at the palace of San Ildefonso. As a Spanish minister, you're finalizing a secret arrangement with Napoleon's envoy, trading away Spain's vast North American colony for a promise of territory in Italy.
evt-10-01-1800-third-treaty-of-san-ildef.prompt: What does Spain agree to in this secret treaty?

choices.text: Sell Louisiana directly to the United States
Cede Louisiana to France in exchange for territory in Tuscany
Keep Louisiana but grant France exclusive trade rights
Cede Florida to France instead of Louisiana

evt-10-01-1800-third-treaty-of-san-ildef.butterflyEffect: Spain secretly agreed to hand Louisiana back to France in exchange for Tuscan lands for a Spanish Bourbon relative. Napoleon, unable to hold or defend the territory amid renewed war with Britain, sold Louisiana to the United States just three years later, doubling the young nation's size overnight.

evt-10-01-1890-john-muir.scenario: It is 1890, and you sit in the U.S. Congress reading John Muir's vivid magazine essays describing Yosemite Valley's meadows being trampled by sheep and its forests marked for logging.
evt-10-01-1890-john-muir.prompt: What should Congress do to protect Yosemite's wilderness?

choices.text: Auction the valley to private conservation buyers
Leave management to local ranchers and loggers
Hand the land to California to manage as a state park
Pass a bill establishing Yosemite as a national park

evt-10-01-1890-john-muir.butterflyEffect: On October 1, 1890, Congress created Yosemite National Park, only the third in the nation. Muir's campaign, amplified by editor Robert Underwood Johnson, helped launch the American conservation movement, leading to the Sierra Club in 1892 and eventually the National Park Service in 1916.

evt-10-01-1891-stanford-university.scenario: It's opening day, 1 October 1891, on a raw, half-finished campus near Palo Alto. Railroad baron Leland Stanford and his wife Jane have poured their fortune into a university built in memory of their son who died young, and you're among the first students walking through its unfinished quads.
evt-10-01-1891-stanford-university.prompt: What defining decision did the Stanfords make about their new university?

choices.text: It would teach only engineering and mining
Only male students would be admitted
It would function strictly as a religious seminary
Tuition would be free for all admitted students

evt-10-01-1891-stanford-university.butterflyEffect: Stanford opened tuition-free and coeducational from the start, an unusual combination for the era that drew ambitious students regardless of wealth or sex. That founding openness helped it grow into a world-leading research university, whose graduates would later seed the technology companies of nearby Silicon Valley.

evt-10-01-1906-simla-deputation.scenario: It's October 1906 at the Viceregal Lodge in Simla. You stand among 35 Muslim leaders led by the Aga Khan III, about to press Viceroy Lord Minto for political guarantees before upcoming constitutional reforms.
evt-10-01-1906-simla-deputation.prompt: What does the deputation ask Lord Minto to grant Indian Muslims?

choices.text: Separate electorates reserved for Muslim representation
Immediate independence from British rule
Formal union with the Ottoman Caliphate
Abolition of the provincial legislative councils

evt-10-01-1906-simla-deputation.butterflyEffect: The deputation secured a commitment to separate electorates for Muslims, later enshrined in the 1909 Morley-Minto reforms. The same year, the meeting's momentum helped found the All-India Muslim League, setting a political trajectory that would eventually lead toward the creation of Pakistan.

evt-10-01-1908-ford-model-t.scenario: It is October 1, 1908, and you are a Ford dealer unveiling the brand-new Model T to a crowd of curious, budget-conscious customers.
evt-10-01-1908-ford-model-t.prompt: What manufacturing innovation will Ford lean on over the coming years to keep slashing this car's price?

choices.text: Assembly-line mass production replacing handcrafted assembly
Importing cheaper parts from European workshops
Focusing on luxury features to raise per-unit profit
Custom-building each car to individual buyer specifications

evt-10-01-1908-ford-model-t.butterflyEffect: Ford's adoption of the moving assembly line in 1913 slashed production time and cost, dropping the price from $780 to just $290 by 1924. Over 15 million Model Ts were eventually sold, reshaping American life, suburban growth, and industrial manufacturing worldwide.

evt-10-01-1949-proclamation-of-the-peopl.scenario: You stand in Tiananmen Square on October 1, 1949, as Mao Zedong proclaims the founding of the People's Republic of China before a vast crowd and a newly raised red flag.
evt-10-01-1949-proclamation-of-the-peopl.prompt: Within weeks, what happens to the defeated Nationalist government and its forces?

choices.text: It forms a coalition government with the Communists
It surrenders unconditionally and dissolves
Its leadership flees into exile in the Soviet Union
It retreats to Taiwan and continues governing from there

evt-10-01-1949-proclamation-of-the-peopl.butterflyEffect: By December 1949 the Republic of China's government had retreated to the island of Taiwan, where it continued to claim to be China's legitimate government. This split produced two rival Chinese states whose unresolved status still shapes global politics and the Taiwan Strait's tensions today.

evt-10-01-1964-free-speech-movement.scenario: It's 1 October 1964 on Sproul Plaza at Berkeley. Campus police have just arrested former student Jack Weinberg for staffing a civil rights information table without authorization, and now hundreds of students are gathering around the squad car holding him.
evt-10-01-1964-free-speech-movement.prompt: What do the students do as police try to drive the car away with Weinberg inside?

choices.text: Help police load Weinberg into the car
Surround the car and refuse to let it move
Disperse quietly to avoid trouble
Ignore the arrest and continue classes

evt-10-01-1964-free-speech-movement.butterflyEffect: Students surrounded and immobilized the police car for roughly 32 hours, using it as an impromptu stage for speeches demanding free political speech on campus. The standoff launched the Free Speech Movement under leaders like Mario Savio, becoming a template for the wave of student activism that swept American campuses through the rest of the 1960s.

evt-10-01-1965-indonesian-national-armed.scenario: It is the early hours of 1 October 1965 in Jakarta. Word reaches you that six army generals have been seized and killed by a group calling itself the 30 September Movement, and that General Nasution narrowly escaped.
evt-10-01-1965-indonesian-national-armed.prompt: As Major General Suharto, what do you do next?

choices.text: Wait for President Sukarno to issue direct orders before acting
Assume command of the army and move to destroy the movement
Negotiate a truce with the movement's leaders
Flee Jakarta until the situation becomes clear

evt-10-01-1965-indonesian-national-armed.butterflyEffect: Suharto assumed command of the army, crushed the movement within days, and used the crisis to move against the Communist Party, launching a purge that killed hundreds of thousands and unraveling Sukarno's presidency. Within three years Suharto had taken power outright, beginning his three-decade New Order regime.

evt-10-01-1975-muhammad-ali.scenario: It is the 14th round of the 'Thrilla in Manila,' 1 October 1975. You are Eddie Futch, cornerman to Joe Frazier, whose eyes are swollen nearly shut and who can barely see Ali's punches coming.
evt-10-01-1975-muhammad-ali.prompt: What does Futch do before the 15th round?

choices.text: Demand the referee disqualify Ali for illegal blows
Throw in the towel immediately after round ten
Stop the fight to protect Frazier from further injury
Let Frazier answer the bell since he is willing to continue

evt-10-01-1975-muhammad-ali.butterflyEffect: Futch stopped the fight, telling Frazier 'It's enough, no more, sit down my son'—ending one of boxing's most brutal contests. Ali retained the heavyweight title, the trilogy with Frazier concluded forever, and both men's long-term health struggles afterward fueled lasting debate about the sport's toll on fighters.

evt-10-01-1990-rwandan-patriotic-front.scenario: It is October 1, 1990. You are a Rwandan Tutsi exile serving in the Ugandan Army, and fifty comrades around you are quietly organizing to abandon their posts as members of the Rwandan Patriotic Front.

choices.text: Report the plan to your Ugandan commanders
Desert your post and cross the border to fight for the RPF
Wait for United Nations peacekeepers to intervene first
Remain in the Ugandan Army and await a diplomatic solution

evt-10-01-1990-rwandan-patriotic-front.butterflyEffect: The deserters crossed into Rwanda that day, launching the RPF invasion that began the Rwandan Civil War. The unresolved tensions of that war fed directly into the horrors of 1994, and the RPF's eventual military victory brought Paul Kagame to power, where he remains today.

evt-10-01-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.scenario: It's 1 October 1991 and Yugoslav People's Army units are advancing on the hills above Dubrovnik, cutting the historic city off from land and sea. You're a resident of the walled Old Town watching artillery positions take shape in the surrounding hills.
evt-10-01-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.prompt: What can the city's defenders and civilians realistically do as the siege begins?

choices.text: Surrender the city at once to prevent any shelling
Request immediate NATO airstrikes on JNA positions
Evacuate the entire city by sea immediately
Organize local civil defense within the old walls and appeal for international attention

evt-10-01-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.butterflyEffect: Dubrovnik endured a seven-month siege, with shelling that damaged much of the UNESCO-listed Old Town and killed civilians. Televised images of the bombardment shocked international opinion, hardening support for Croatian independence and later contributing to war crimes prosecutions at the Hague tribunal.

evt-10-01-1998-europol.scenario: It is 1 October 1998 in The Hague. You are a justice ministry official watching as the last EU member state ratifies the convention that will finally let Europol begin its work.
evt-10-01-1998-europol.prompt: What does this ratification allow Europol to start doing?

choices.text: Coordinate cross-border criminal intelligence and support member states' investigations
Take direct command of national police forces
Conduct arrests independently of national authorities
Serve as the EU's unified military intelligence service

evt-10-01-1998-europol.butterflyEffect: With the convention in force, Europol began coordinating criminal intelligence and supporting national police across the EU on threats like drug trafficking and terrorism. Its powers expanded steadily after 2001, and in 2017 it was formally reconstituted as the European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation with broader authority.

evt-10-01-2012-2012-lamma-island-ferry-c.scenario: It is the evening of 1 October 2012, China's National Day. You are aboard one of two ferries converging in the dark waters off Lamma Island, both crowded with passengers heading to watch the harbour fireworks.
evt-10-01-2012-2012-lamma-island-ferry-c.prompt: What did investigators later find had caused the collision?

choices.text: Deliberate sabotage by a disgruntled crew member
A typhoon forced both vessels off their planned routes
A sudden engine failure left one vessel unable to steer
Poor lookout procedures and structural design flaws prevented timely evasive action

evt-10-01-2012-2012-lamma-island-ferry-c.butterflyEffect: Investigators found inadequate lookout practices and design flaws, including obstructed views from the wheelhouse and watertight doors that failed to hold back flooding, sealed the fate of the sinking vessel. The disaster, Hong Kong's deadliest maritime accident in decades, led to sweeping reforms in ferry design standards, lifejacket requirements, and crew training.

evt-10-02-1470-edward-iv.scenario: It is October 1470. The Earl of Warwick and the Duke of Clarence have risen against you, aiming to restore Henry VI to the throne, and their forces are closing in fast.
evt-10-02-1470-edward-iv.prompt: What does Edward IV choose to do as Warwick's forces close in?

choices.text: Surrender to Warwick and accept exile in the Tower
Sail to Ireland to rally Yorkist loyalists
Stand and fight Warwick's army at Doncaster
Flee by ship to Burgundy, seeking his brother-in-law's protection

evt-10-02-1470-edward-iv.butterflyEffect: Edward fled by ship to the Burgundian Netherlands, where Duke Charles the Bold gave him money and ships. Six months later he returned, crushed Warwick at Barnet and the Lancastrians at Tewkesbury, and reclaimed the crown he would hold until his death in 1483.

evt-10-02-1766-1766-food-riots.scenario: It is October 1766, and you are a laborer in Nottingham where bread and cheese prices have soared after poor harvests and grain exports abroad. A crowd is gathering at the market, furious at the traders.
evt-10-02-1766-1766-food-riots.prompt: What do the rioters do to force prices back down?

choices.text: Seize the goods and force merchants to sell at a lower, 'fair' price
Riot only against foreign merchants trading in the town
Boycott the market entirely and grow their own grain
Petition Parliament and wait quietly for a response

evt-10-02-1766-1766-food-riots.butterflyEffect: Across England that autumn, crowds seized grain, cheese, and other goods and compelled traders and farmers to sell at what they considered a fair "moral economy" price rather than looting for free. Around 131 such riots were recorded nationwide, pressuring local magistrates and shaping later debates over regulating the grain trade.

evt-10-02-1835-dragoon.scenario: It's October 2, 1835, in Gonzales, Mexican Texas. A detachment of Mexican dragoons has arrived demanding the return of a small cannon the government lent your town years ago for defense against Comanche raids, and the settlers are gathering with makeshift weapons.
evt-10-02-1835-dragoon.prompt: What do the Gonzales settlers decide to do when the dragoons demand the cannon?

choices.text: Hand over the cannon peacefully to avoid bloodshed
Defy the order, raise a flag over the cannon, and open fire
Abandon the town and flee toward San Antonio
Send a delegation to negotiate an extended loan of the cannon

evt-10-02-1835-dragoon.butterflyEffect: The Texians refused, raised a flag reading 'Come and Take It,' and fired the cannon at the approaching soldiers, driving them off in what became known as the Battle of Gonzales. It is remembered as the 'Lexington of Texas,' the first armed clash of the Texas Revolution that would end with Texan independence the following year.

evt-10-02-1879-qing-dynasty.scenario: It is 1879 in Livadia, Crimea. Your envoy Chonghou has just signed a treaty ceding key territory in Yili to Russia in exchange for the return of the rest of the region, and word has reached the Qing court in Beijing.
evt-10-02-1879-qing-dynasty.prompt: What should the Qing court do with this treaty?

choices.text: Reject the treaty and send a new envoy to renegotiate
Declare immediate war on Russia over Yili
Cede all of Yili outright without further talks
Ratify the treaty exactly as Chonghou signed it

evt-10-02-1879-qing-dynasty.butterflyEffect: The court refused to ratify the humiliating terms, initially condemning Chonghou to death before pardoning him, and dispatched the skilled diplomat Zeng Jize to renegotiate. His efforts produced the more favorable Treaty of St. Petersburg in 1881, one of the rare Qing diplomatic successes of the era.

evt-10-02-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is October 2, 1942, in the North Atlantic. You serve aboard the escort cruiser HMS Curacoa, guarding the liner RMS Queen Mary as she carries thousands of American troops toward Britain, both ships under strict wartime orders about evasive zigzagging.
evt-10-02-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: After Queen Mary's bow slices into Curacoa, what does the liner do next?

choices.text: Halt immediately and lower lifeboats for survivors
Continue at speed without stopping, per Admiralty anti-submarine orders
Radio for an immediate air-sea rescue and wait offshore
Turn back to the nearest port for repairs

evt-10-02-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Under standing orders never to stop for U-boat threats, Queen Mary continued on without pausing to rescue survivors, leaving other vessels to search the water. HMS Curacoa sank within minutes with the loss of most of her crew, a tragedy kept secret during the war and only fully disclosed afterward, prompting later scrutiny of wartime escort protocols.

evt-10-02-1958-guinea.scenario: It is September 1958, and you are a voter in French Guinea, handed a ballot asking whether your territory should join Charles de Gaulle's new French Community or strike out on its own.
evt-10-02-1958-guinea.prompt: What does Sékou Touré urge Guineans to choose?

choices.text: Abstain from voting entirely
Vote yes and remain within the French Community
Vote no and demand immediate full independence
Support a compromise of partial autonomy

evt-10-02-1958-guinea.butterflyEffect: Guinea voted overwhelmingly no, the only French African territory to reject the Community outright. France withdrew abruptly, and Guinea proclaimed full independence on October 2, 1958 under President Sékou Touré, a defiant precedent that emboldened other African independence movements.

evt-10-02-1967-thurgood-marshall.scenario: It is October 2, 1967, and you watch Thurgood Marshall take his oath as the newest justice of the US Supreme Court, the first African American to hold the seat.
evt-10-02-1967-thurgood-marshall.prompt: What defined Marshall's tenure on the Court in the years that followed?

choices.text: He focused primarily on international law cases
He became a reliable liberal voice, often dissenting as the Court grew more conservative
He resigned within two years citing age concerns
He shifted to a moderate swing vote for most of his career

evt-10-02-1967-thurgood-marshall.butterflyEffect: Marshall served on the Court until 1991, becoming one of its most consistently liberal voices. As the Court's composition shifted rightward through the 1970s and 80s, he was frequently found in dissent, and his eventual retirement opened the seat later filled by Clarence Thomas.

evt-10-02-1968-gustavo-diaz-ordaz.scenario: It is the evening of 2 October 1968, ten days before Mexico City opens the Olympic Games. Thousands of students rally in the Plaza de las Tres Culturas at Tlatelolco when army troops and plainclothes gunmen surround the square on President Díaz Ordaz's orders.
evt-10-02-1968-gustavo-diaz-ordaz.prompt: What did the government claim happened once the shooting stopped?

choices.text: The cabinet resigned en masse, taking responsibility
It blamed armed student agitators for the violence and minimized the death toll
It announced the Olympics were cancelled in response
It admitted troops fired first on unarmed civilians

evt-10-02-1968-gustavo-diaz-ordaz.butterflyEffect: Officials insisted only a handful had died and blamed armed student provocateurs, but witnesses and later investigations put the toll in the hundreds. The massacre became a defining wound in Mexican political memory, fueling decades-long demands for accountability from the ruling PRI.

evt-10-02-1970-wichita-state-university-.scenario: It's October 2, 1970, and you're the pilot of a chartered Martin 4-0-4 carrying Wichita State football staff and boosters through the Colorado Rockies. You've drifted off the filed flight plan to give passengers a scenic view of the mountains, and the terrain ahead is rising faster than your plane can climb.
evt-10-02-1970-wichita-state-university-.prompt: What should the pilot do the moment he realizes he can't clear the ridge?

choices.text: Immediately turn the aircraft away from the rising terrain and abandon the detour
Descend into the valley to fly beneath the cloud base
Radio air traffic control and wait for clearance before changing course
Push the throttles forward and try to climb directly over the ridge

evt-10-02-1970-wichita-state-university-.butterflyEffect: The pilot did not turn back in time, and the plane struck a mountainside west of Silver Plume, killing 31 of the 40 aboard, including much of the coaching staff and administration. Investigators blamed an unauthorized sightseeing detour into terrain the aircraft could not outclimb, and the tragedy pushed charter operators carrying sports teams toward stricter route and altitude oversight.

evt-10-02-1971-nguyen-van-thieu.scenario: It is October 1971, and South Vietnam prepares for a presidential election. Your rivals, generals Dương Văn Minh and Nguyễn Cao Kỳ, must decide whether to remain in the race against incumbent Nguyễn Văn Thiệu.
evt-10-02-1971-nguyen-van-thieu.prompt: What did Thiệu's opponents decide to do days before the vote?

choices.text: They formed a united opposition ticket
They stayed on the ballot but urged a boycott
They fled to North Vietnam in protest
They withdrew, calling the election rigged in Thiệu's favor

evt-10-02-1971-nguyen-van-thieu.butterflyEffect: With no rival left on the ballot, Thiệu won unopposed with over 90 percent of the vote, entrenching his one-man rule. The hollow result deepened doubts in Washington about South Vietnam's democratic legitimacy just as American troops were withdrawing under Vietnamization.

evt-10-02-1971-british-european-airways-.scenario: It is October 2, 1971. You are aboard a Vickers Vanguard cruising at 19,000 feet from London to Salzburg when a violent shudder runs through the rear of the cabin as the pressure bulkhead gives way.
evt-10-02-1971-british-european-airways-.prompt: What actually followed this structural failure?

choices.text: The tailplane surfaces separated, and the aircraft entered an uncontrollable dive
A fire broke out but the aircraft landed safely
Cabin depressurization alone caused casualties with no structural loss
The pilots regained control and made an emergency landing

evt-10-02-1971-british-european-airways-.butterflyEffect: The bulkhead failure tore away the tailplane surfaces, sending the Vanguard into an unrecoverable dive that killed all 63 aboard near Aarsele, Belgium. The disaster prompted urgent scrutiny of pressure bulkhead fatigue on aging Vanguard airframes across European fleets.

evt-10-02-1980-michael-myers-pennsylvani.scenario: You're a member of the House of Representatives in 1980, watching colleagues react to FBI videotapes showing Congressman Michael 'Ozzie' Myers accepting cash from agents posing as representatives of a wealthy Arab sheikh in the Abscam sting.
evt-10-02-1980-michael-myers-pennsylvani.prompt: What does the House vote to do with Myers after the tapes become public?

choices.text: Take no action and let voters decide in the next election
Expel him from the House by a formal vote
Quietly ask him to resign without a vote
Issue a formal censure but let him keep his seat

evt-10-02-1980-michael-myers-pennsylvani.butterflyEffect: The House expelled Myers by an overwhelming vote, the first expulsion of a member since the Civil War era and the first ever for corruption rather than disloyalty. He later served three years in federal prison, and the case set a precedent later invoked when Congress expelled Jim Traficant in 2002.

evt-10-02-1990-1990-guangzhou-baiyun-air.scenario: It is October 2, 1990, and you are the pilot of Xiamen Airlines Flight 8301. A hijacker aboard is demanding a diversion, but your fuel is running critically low as you approach Guangzhou Baiyun Airport.
evt-10-02-1990-1990-guangzhou-baiyun-air.prompt: With fuel nearly exhausted and the hijacker refusing to cooperate, what must the pilot attempt?

choices.text: Ditch the aircraft in open water instead
Continue on toward Taiwan as the hijacker demands
Circle indefinitely while awaiting a military escort
Attempt an emergency landing at Guangzhou despite the danger

evt-10-02-1990-1990-guangzhou-baiyun-air.butterflyEffect: The aircraft attempted an emergency landing at Guangzhou but collided with two parked planes on the runway, killing 128 people in what became the deadliest aircraft hijacking prior to the September 11 attacks. The disaster pushed Chinese aviation authorities to reassess hijack-response procedures and airport ground safety.

evt-10-02-1992-carandiru-massacre.scenario: It is 2 October 1992. A riot between rival prisoner factions has broken out inside Carandiru Penitentiary in São Paulo, and military police units are massing outside the pavilion, weighing how to respond.
evt-10-02-1992-carandiru-massacre.prompt: What decision does the military police make in response to the riot?

choices.text: Wait for a judge's order before entering
Storm the pavilion, opening fire on prisoners including many who had surrendered
Negotiate a peaceful surrender through prison chaplains
Withdraw and let prison staff regain control unaided

evt-10-02-1992-carandiru-massacre.butterflyEffect: The assault left 111 inmates dead, one of the deadliest prison massacres in modern history and a global symbol of Brazil's prison crisis. It spurred investigations and officer prosecutions, though most convictions were later overturned, and the pavilion itself was demolished in 2002.

evt-10-02-1996-freedom-of-information-ac.scenario: You run the records office of a federal agency in 1996. Congress has just passed amendments extending the Freedom of Information Act to cover records that only exist on computers, and citizens are now filing requests for data your office has never released in paper form.
evt-10-02-1996-freedom-of-information-ac.prompt: What are agencies now required to do under the new Electronic FOIA amendments?

choices.text: Provide records in electronic form and post frequently requested records online
Continue releasing only paper copies regardless of how records are stored
Charge requesters extra fees for any digital records
Refuse requests for records that exist only in computer databases

evt-10-02-1996-freedom-of-information-ac.butterflyEffect: The Electronic Freedom of Information Act Amendments, signed by President Clinton, required agencies to make many records available in electronic formats and searchable online reading rooms, not just on paper. It marked an early recognition that government transparency had to keep pace with computers, laying groundwork for later open-data and digital-government initiatives.

evt-10-02-2002-d-c-sniper-attacks.scenario: You're on the task force hunting the Beltway sniper in October 2002. Witnesses at several shooting scenes reported a white box truck or van fleeing the area, and your search has centered on that vehicle for weeks with no arrest.
evt-10-02-2002-d-c-sniper-attacks.prompt: What ultimately leads investigators to the actual shooters?

choices.text: The snipers surrender after sending a written confession
They are caught during an unrelated robbery
Police stop them at a roadblock while searching white vans
A tip locates their actual car, a blue sedan, at a highway rest stop

evt-10-02-2002-d-c-sniper-attacks.butterflyEffect: A trucker spotted the suspects' blue Chevrolet Caprice at a Maryland highway rest stop, and police arrested John Allen Muhammad and Lee Boyd Malvo there on October 24, ending the three-week wave of attacks that killed ten people. The case exposed how eyewitness fixation on the wrong vehicle type had slowed the manhunt, reshaping how police handle conflicting witness descriptions in later investigations.

evt-10-02-2004-parkrun.scenario: It is Saturday morning, 2 October 2004, in Bushy Park, London. Paul Sinton-Hewitt has gathered a handful of friends for a timed 5-kilometre run he is calling the Bushy Park Time Trial.
evt-10-02-2004-parkrun.prompt: What does Sinton-Hewitt hope this weekly time trial will achieve?

choices.text: Create a free, inclusive weekly running event open to anyone, not just competitive athletes
Qualify local runners for the London Marathon
Raise money for a single named charity
Launch a commercial gym franchise

evt-10-02-2004-parkrun.butterflyEffect: The informal Saturday run, started partly to keep Sinton-Hewitt fit after an injury and to stay connected with friends, grew into parkrun, now free weekly 5k events at thousands of locations worldwide. It is credited with getting millions of first-time and returning runners moving.

evt-10-02-2005-typhoon-longwang.scenario: It is October 1, 2005, and you live on Taiwan's east coast near Hualien. Radio reports say a powerful typhoon with winds over 170 km/h is bearing down on the island within hours.
evt-10-02-2005-typhoon-longwang.prompt: What is the safest response as Typhoon Longwang closes in on Hualien?

choices.text: Evacuate to a designated inland shelter before landfall
Head to the coast to watch the storm surge
Stay home and board up windows only
Drive inland to Taipei immediately without informing anyone

evt-10-02-2005-typhoon-longwang.butterflyEffect: Longwang struck near Hualien City early on October 2, crossed Taiwan's mountainous terrain in about six hours, then moved back offshore before making a second landfall in Fujian, China, where it rapidly weakened and dissipated by October 3.

evt-10-02-2016-2014-2016-oromo-protests.scenario: It is late 2015 in Ginchi, Oromia, and you join university students and farmers gathering to oppose the Addis Ababa Master Plan, which threatens to absorb Oromo farmland into the expanding capital.
evt-10-02-2016-2014-2016-oromo-protests.prompt: What actually happened to the Master Plan after the wave of protests it sparked?

choices.text: The plan was expanded to cover more Oromo territory
The plan was implemented immediately as scheduled
The government abandoned the plan, but protests continued over broader grievances
The protests ended the moment the plan was announced

evt-10-02-2016-2014-2016-oromo-protests.butterflyEffect: The government formally dropped the Addis Ababa Master Plan in January 2016, but the protests had already broadened into demands over land rights, marginalization, and political freedoms. The unrest continued for years and became a major pressure that contributed to leadership change in Ethiopia by 2018.

evt-10-02-2019-boeing-b-17-flying-fortre.scenario: You're a passenger aboard the vintage B-17 'Nine-O-Nine' as it lifts off from Bradley International Airport for a living-history flight experience on October 2, 2019. Almost immediately after takeoff, the crew reports a problem with one of the engines.
evt-10-02-2019-boeing-b-17-flying-fortre.prompt: What happens in the minutes after the crew declares the emergency?

choices.text: The pilot tries to bring the plane back to the runway but crashes short of it
The flight continues on to its planned route without incident
The crew shuts down all engines and glides to a soft landing in a field
The plane lands safely at a nearby diversion airport

evt-10-02-2019-boeing-b-17-flying-fortre.butterflyEffect: The pilot attempted an immediate return to the runway but the bomber came down short, crashing into airport de-icing equipment and killing seven of the thirteen people aboard. The disaster prompted renewed scrutiny of the FAA's oversight of vintage 'living history' flight programs and led operators to tighten maintenance and passenger-briefing standards for historic aircraft rides.

evt-10-03-1849-edgar-allan-poe.scenario: It's October 3, 1849, and you find writer Edgar Allan Poe collapsed outside a Baltimore tavern, incoherent, feverish, and dressed in clothes that are not his own.
evt-10-03-1849-edgar-allan-poe.prompt: What happens to Poe in the days that follow?

choices.text: He is jailed overnight for drunkenness and released unharmed
He recovers fully within a week and returns to New York
He finishes a final manuscript before dying peacefully at home
He is hospitalized and dies four days later, cause never definitively established

evt-10-03-1849-edgar-allan-poe.butterflyEffect: Poe was taken to Washington College Hospital and died on October 7, 1849, without ever explaining what had happened to him. The true cause of his death was never established, and the mystery of his final days has fueled speculation for over 170 years, becoming part of the gothic mythology that surrounds his legacy.

evt-10-03-1951-major-league-baseball.scenario: It is the bottom of the ninth in the deciding playoff game at the Polo Grounds, 3 October 1951. Your Brooklyn Dodgers lead 4-2, but the Giants have two men on and Bobby Thomson steps up against pitcher Ralph Branca.

choices.text: He strikes out to end the game
He is walked intentionally to load the bases
He hits a walk-off three-run home run
He grounds out into a game-ending double play

evt-10-03-1951-major-league-baseball.butterflyEffect: Thomson drove a three-run homer into the lower deck, and broadcaster Russ Hodges's cry of "The Giants win the pennant!" became one of the most famous calls in sports history. The "Shot Heard 'Round the World" completed a stunning late-season comeback over Brooklyn, though decades later some players admitted the Giants had been stealing opposing catchers' signs that season.

evt-10-03-1951-first-battle-of-maryang-s.scenario: It is October 1951 near the Imjin River. You are with the 3rd Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment, ordered to seize the ridge of Maryang-san from a numerically superior Chinese force during Operation Commando.
evt-10-03-1951-first-battle-of-maryang-s.prompt: How does the Australian battalion finally break the Chinese hold on the ridge crest?

choices.text: The battalion negotiates a local ceasefire with Chinese commanders
Tanks are brought up the ridge to crush the trench lines
A sustained naval bombardment forces the defenders to withdraw
A bayonet charge drives the defenders off the crest

evt-10-03-1951-first-battle-of-maryang-s.butterflyEffect: A Company pressed home a bayonet charge to take the summit, and 3RAR went on to hold the position against fierce counterattacks. The battle became one of the most celebrated actions in Australian military history and helped push the front to the Jamestown Line, where it largely stabilised for the rest of the war.

evt-10-03-1952-operation-hurricane.scenario: It is October 3, 1952, and you are a scientist aboard a support ship anchored off the Montebello Islands in Western Australia, watching a plutonium implosion device rigged inside a ship's hull, ready to fire Britain's first atomic test.
evt-10-03-1952-operation-hurricane.prompt: What happened when Operation Hurricane's device was detonated?

choices.text: It failed to detonate due to a wiring fault
It detonated prematurely, killing several technicians
The test was scrubbed and moved to mainland Australia
It detonated successfully, confirming Britain's nuclear capability

evt-10-03-1952-operation-hurricane.butterflyEffect: The device detonated successfully, making Britain the world's third nuclear power after the United States and Soviet Union. The test secured Britain's seat at the nuclear table and shaped Cold War strategy, though it also left lasting radioactive contamination on the Montebello Islands.

evt-10-03-1962-mercury-atlas-8.scenario: It is 3 October 1962, and you are astronaut Wally Schirra strapped into the Sigma 7 capsule atop an Atlas rocket, about to attempt the longest American orbital flight yet flown.
evt-10-03-1962-mercury-atlas-8.prompt: What is Schirra's main mission priority, unlike earlier Mercury flights?

choices.text: Testing a spacewalk outside the capsule
Rehearsing a docking manoeuvre with an Agena target vehicle
Conducting an extensive slate of scientific experiments
Conserving fuel and verifying the spacecraft's engineering systems

evt-10-03-1962-mercury-atlas-8.butterflyEffect: Schirra flew a deliberately conservative, fuel-sparing mission focused on proving the spacecraft's engineering reliability over nine hours and six orbits, rather than running scientific experiments. The flight's success gave NASA confidence to attempt the full one-day Mercury-Atlas 9 mission the following year, closing out the Mercury program on a high note.

evt-10-03-1963-oswaldo-lopez-arellano.scenario: It is early October 1963 in Tegucigalpa, days before a scheduled presidential election. You are an officer under Colonel Oswaldo López Arellano, and troops loyal to him are moving to seize the presidential palace from Ramón Villeda Morales.
evt-10-03-1963-oswaldo-lopez-arellano.prompt: What does the military do to the elected government?

choices.text: Overthrow the president in a violent coup before the election
Allow him to finish his term as scheduled
Negotiate a peaceful transfer of power after the vote
Call for international observers to oversee the election

evt-10-03-1963-oswaldo-lopez-arellano.butterflyEffect: López Arellano's forces overthrew Villeda Morales in a violent coup just before the vote, installing López Arellano as head of state. He would rule Honduras as a military strongman until 1971, then seize power again in 1972, entrenching military dominance over Honduran politics for years.

evt-10-03-1981-1981-irish-hunger-strike.scenario: It is March 1981 in H-Block 6 of the Maze Prison outside Belfast. You are among the republican prisoners who have spent years on the 'blanket protest,' and now IRA man Bobby Sands has begun refusing food to demand political status rather than criminal status.
evt-10-03-1981-1981-irish-hunger-strike.prompt: What ultimately happens to Bobby Sands during the strike?

choices.text: He resumes eating after last-minute negotiations succeed
He dies after 66 days without concession, having won a by-election as MP
The British government grants full political status and the protest ends
He is quietly released and the strike dissolves

evt-10-03-1981-1981-irish-hunger-strike.butterflyEffect: Sands died after 66 days without the government conceding, having been elected MP for Fermanagh and South Tyrone while starving. His death, and nine more that followed, drew global attention to the conflict and pushed Sinn Féin toward the electoral strategy that would eventually complement, and partly replace, armed struggle.

evt-10-03-1990-east-germany.scenario: It's October 3, 1990, and East Germany's parliament has just dissolved the state, formally joining the Federal Republic of Germany after months of negotiation following the fall of the Berlin Wall.
evt-10-03-1990-east-germany.prompt: What legal mechanism actually accomplishes this reunification?

choices.text: The two Germanys merge under a new treaty replacing both constitutions
East Germany accedes to West Germany's existing constitution
A brand new joint constitution is drafted and ratified by both states
The United Nations oversees a transitional joint government first

evt-10-03-1990-east-germany.butterflyEffect: East Germany acceded to the Federal Republic under Article 23 of West Germany's Basic Law, meaning it joined an existing state rather than forming a new one. This method avoided a lengthy constitutional convention but left many East Germans feeling they had been absorbed rather than truly unified as equals, a grievance still felt in eastern German politics today.

evt-10-03-1991-nadine-gordimer.scenario: It is October 1991 and you are a journalist in Stockholm awaiting the Swedish Academy's announcement. Nadine Gordimer, whose novels have long dissected apartheid South Africa from the inside, is about to become the first South African ever named.
evt-10-03-1991-nadine-gordimer.prompt: What does the Academy cite as the reason for honouring Gordimer?

choices.text: A collection of children's stories
A single celebrated volume of poetry
An epic body of writing of great benefit to humanity
Her memoir detailing life under apartheid

evt-10-03-1991-nadine-gordimer.butterflyEffect: The Academy praised writing that had 'been of very great benefit to humanity,' recognising decades of fiction that exposed apartheid's human cost. The award, coming as South Africa was dismantling apartheid, cemented Gordimer's international standing and encouraged continued attention to South African literature abroad.

evt-10-03-1992-sinead-o-connor.scenario: It is October 3, 1992, and you are watching Saturday Night Live live from home. Sinéad O'Connor has just finished an a cappella version of Bob Marley's "War," and she is holding up a photograph as the final note fades.
evt-10-03-1992-sinead-o-connor.prompt: What does Sinéad O'Connor do with the photograph on air?

choices.text: She sets it alight with a lighter
She hands it to an audience member in silence
She kisses it and blesses the audience
She tears it up, denouncing abuse within the Catholic Church

evt-10-03-1992-sinead-o-connor.butterflyEffect: She tore up a photo of Pope John Paul II while urging viewers to "fight the real enemy," protesting child abuse within the Catholic Church. The backlash nearly destroyed her American career at the time, but years later, as clergy abuse scandals surfaced worldwide, many recognized she had been years ahead of the reckoning.

evt-10-03-1993-battle-of-mogadishu-1993.scenario: It's October 3, 1993, and you're a U.S. Army Ranger pinned down in Mogadishu after two Black Hawk helicopters are shot down while trying to capture lieutenants of warlord Mohamed Farrah Aidid.
evt-10-03-1993-battle-of-mogadishu-1993.prompt: What follows this failed raid in the months ahead?

choices.text: Heavy casualties force a U.S. withdrawal from Somalia within months
The successful raid leads to an expanded UN peacekeeping mandate
Aidid surrenders to American forces the following week
The U.S. establishes a permanent military base in Mogadishu

evt-10-03-1993-battle-of-mogadishu-1993.butterflyEffect: Eighteen American soldiers died and images of a dead soldier dragged through the streets shocked the U.S. public. President Clinton announced a withdrawal of American forces from Somalia within months, and the debacle made Washington deeply wary of ground intervention in African conflicts, a hesitancy later cited in the muted U.S. response to the Rwandan genocide.

evt-10-03-1995-murder-trial-of-o-j-simps.scenario: It is October 3, 1995, in a packed Los Angeles courtroom. After eight months of televised testimony, you and eleven other jurors are about to deliver a verdict that the entire country is waiting to hear.
evt-10-03-1995-murder-trial-of-o-j-simps.prompt: What was the jury's verdict for O. J. Simpson?

choices.text: Guilty of the lesser charge of manslaughter
Guilty on both counts of murder
The jury deadlocked, forcing a mistrial
Not guilty on both counts of murder

evt-10-03-1995-murder-trial-of-o-j-simps.butterflyEffect: The jury acquitted Simpson of both murders after less than four hours of deliberation. A civil jury later found him liable for wrongful death, and the case became a flashpoint in American debates over race, celebrity, and the justice system that still echoes in true-crime coverage today.

evt-10-03-2003-siegfried-roy.scenario: It is October 3, 2003, and you are seated in the audience at the Mirage in Las Vegas, watching Roy Horn perform his signature act with the white tiger Mantecore during a sold-out Siegfried & Roy show.
evt-10-03-2003-siegfried-roy.prompt: What happens to Roy Horn during this performance?

choices.text: The tiger grabs him and drags him off stage, causing severe injuries
The performance concludes without any incident
Roy is nipped but finishes the act unharmed
The tiger briefly escapes into the audience before being recaptured

evt-10-03-2003-siegfried-roy.butterflyEffect: Mantecore seized Roy and dragged him offstage, inflicting injuries so severe he nearly died and never fully recovered, leaving him partially paralyzed. The long-running Las Vegas spectacle ended permanently, and the incident intensified public debate over using big cats and other exotic animals in live entertainment.

evt-10-03-2015-kunduz-hospital-airstrike.scenario: It is the night of 3 October 2015 in Kunduz, and a US AC-130 gunship is firing on the MSF trauma centre you know to be full of patients and staff, despite the coordinates having been shared with all warring parties weeks earlier.
evt-10-03-2015-kunduz-hospital-airstrike.prompt: What did the subsequent US military investigation conclude caused the strike?

choices.text: A combination of human and technical errors misidentified the building
MSF had given the coordinates of a different, nearby building
The crew deliberately targeted the hospital on orders from command
Taliban fighters had jammed the aircraft's targeting systems

evt-10-03-2015-kunduz-hospital-airstrike.butterflyEffect: The Pentagon's investigation found a combination of human error, equipment failure, and procedural mistakes led the crew to misidentify the hospital as a hostile target. Several personnel received administrative discipline rather than criminal charges, and MSF's demand for an independent international investigation was refused, fuelling lasting debate over accountability for wartime strikes on medical facilities.

evt-10-03-2022-svante-paabo.scenario: It is October 2022, and the Nobel committee is announcing the Physiology or Medicine laureate: a geneticist who spent decades coaxing readable DNA out of tens-of-thousands-year-old bone fragments.
evt-10-03-2022-svante-paabo.prompt: What discovery earned Svante Pääbo the Nobel Prize?

choices.text: Discovering the double-helix structure of DNA
Sequencing the Neanderthal genome and identifying the Denisovans
Developing the CRISPR gene-editing technique
Completing the first full sequencing of the human genome

evt-10-03-2022-svante-paabo.butterflyEffect: Pääbo's team sequenced the Neanderthal genome and identified a previously unknown hominin, the Denisovans, from a single finger bone. His work founded the field of paleogenomics and revealed that ancient interbreeding left modern humans carrying Neanderthal and Denisovan DNA still influencing traits like immune response today.

evt-10-03-2023-wab-kinew.scenario: It is election night 2023 in Manitoba. You are watching results come in as NDP leader Wab Kinew, who is Anishinaabe, closes in on victory over the incumbent Progressive Conservatives.
evt-10-03-2023-wab-kinew.prompt: What historic first does Kinew's win represent?

choices.text: First First Nations premier of a Canadian province
First female premier of Manitoba
First premier elected without a legislature seat
First Indigenous prime minister of Canada

evt-10-03-2023-wab-kinew.butterflyEffect: Kinew became the first First Nations person to serve as premier of a Canadian province, a milestone celebrated across Indigenous communities nationwide. His victory intensified discussion of Indigenous representation in Canadian politics and was cited as a benchmark for future provincial and federal candidates.

evt-10-04-1363-red-turban-rebellions.scenario: You command Zhu Yuanzhang's fleet on Lake Poyang in 1363, badly outnumbered by Chen Youliang's massive chained warships. A direct clash favors the larger fleet, but the wind is turning in your favor.
evt-10-04-1363-red-turban-rebellions.prompt: What tactic do you use to break the larger enemy fleet?

choices.text: Ram the enemy ships with siege towers
Launch fire ships into the enemy's linked fleet
Charge with cavalry across the lake ice
Withdraw and wait for reinforcements from the south

evt-10-04-1363-red-turban-rebellions.butterflyEffect: Zhu Yuanzhang's forces sent fire ships into the wind-driven current, igniting Chen Youliang's chained vessels in one of history's largest naval battles. The victory crushed his chief rival's power and cleared Zhu's path to found the Ming dynasty in 1368.

evt-10-04-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: You command a Union warship off Galveston, Texas, on 4 October 1862. Confederate defenses have thinned, and the city's mayor is signaling willingness to talk terms rather than face a bombardment.
evt-10-04-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: What do you do as the ranking Union officer demanding the port's surrender?

choices.text: Withdraw the fleet without engaging
Demand the mayor abolish slavery before accepting terms
Bombard the city regardless of the surrender offer
Accept the surrender and occupy the harbor

evt-10-04-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Galveston's authorities surrendered and Union forces occupied the port, but the victory proved short-lived: Confederate troops under John B. Magruder stormed back and retook the city in a surprise dawn attack on New Year's Day 1863. Galveston remained in Confederate hands for the rest of the war, one of the last major Southern ports to hold out.

evt-10-04-1918-world-war-i.scenario: It's October 4, 1918, in the seas off Ireland. The Japanese liner SS Hirano Maru is steaming toward Liverpool crowded with passengers when a German submarine's periscope slices the surface nearby.
evt-10-04-1918-world-war-i.prompt: What happened to the Hirano Maru moments later?

choices.text: British escort ships destroyed the submarine before it could fire
The liner outran the submarine and reached Liverpool safely
The submarine surfaced and let passengers evacuate before scuttling it
A torpedo struck the ship, sinking it with heavy loss of life

evt-10-04-1918-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: A German torpedo struck the liner, sinking it with heavy loss of life among the passengers and crew aboard. As one of the deadliest attacks on a Japanese vessel in the war, it deepened Japanese outrage at German unrestricted submarine warfare just weeks before the armistice ended the fighting.

evt-10-04-1925-great-syrian-revolt.scenario: You are a rebel fighter under Fawzi al-Qawuqji in October 1925, celebrating in the streets of newly captured Hama after driving out French colonial forces. French aircraft are already massing overhead.
evt-10-04-1925-great-syrian-revolt.prompt: What happens to Hama in the aftermath of the rebel capture?

choices.text: The League of Nations declares Hama an independent city-state
French forces recapture and bombard the city
Ottoman troops return to reclaim the city
The rebels hold Hama uncontested for the rest of the war

evt-10-04-1925-great-syrian-revolt.butterflyEffect: French forces regrouped and bombarded Hama to crush the rebellion, a tactic they would repeat against Damascus itself in 1925 and 1926. The brutal reprisals discredited French rule in the eyes of many Syrians and hardened nationalist resistance that continued until independence decades later.

evt-10-04-1927-gutzon-borglum.scenario: You are the lead sculptor standing before the granite face of Mount Rushmore in 1927. Removing hundreds of thousands of tons of rock by hand chisel alone would take lifetimes, and you need a faster way to rough out the presidents' features.
evt-10-04-1927-gutzon-borglum.prompt: What unconventional method do you choose to remove the bulk of the granite?

choices.text: Acid etching to dissolve the surface rock
Diamond-tipped rotary saws
Controlled dynamite blasting to rough out the shapes
Hand chisels and mallets exclusively

evt-10-04-1927-gutzon-borglum.butterflyEffect: Borglum's team used precision dynamite blasting to remove about 90% of the rock, leaving only fine finishing to jackhammers and hand tools. The technique let the memorial be completed in just 14 years despite its scale, and it remains one of the largest carved reliefs in the world.

evt-10-04-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It's October 4, 1943, off Bodø, Norway. Aircraft from USS Ranger, the only American carrier to strike German-held Europe during the war, are readying to launch against a German shipping convoy.
evt-10-04-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What was the outcome of this carrier strike, Operation Leader?

choices.text: The German battleship Tirpitz was sunk in her Norwegian anchorage
USS Ranger was torpedoed and sunk during the operation
Several German cargo ships were sunk before the strike force withdrew
The raid was cancelled before any aircraft could launch

evt-10-04-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Ranger's aircraft sank several German cargo ships and damaged port facilities near Bodø before withdrawing, though losses among the attacking aircraft to flak showed the risks of operating so close to occupied coastline. It remained a rare, one-off demonstration that US carrier air power could reach into European waters, but the Navy's carriers were needed in the Pacific and no similar raid followed.

evt-10-04-1957-sputnik-1.scenario: It is 4 October 1957 at the Baikonur launch site in Kazakh SSR. You are a Soviet engineer watching the R-7 rocket lift a polished metal sphere, Sputnik 1, toward orbit for the first time in history.
evt-10-04-1957-sputnik-1.prompt: What happens once Sputnik 1 reaches orbit?

choices.text: It transmits only within Soviet territory
It remains silent, its transmitter never activating
It transmits radio pulses detectable by receivers across the globe
It fails to separate from the rocket and burns up immediately

evt-10-04-1957-sputnik-1.butterflyEffect: Sputnik transmitted detectable radio pulses for three weeks before its batteries died, and its signal was picked up by amateur radio operators worldwide. Its unexpected success triggered the American 'Sputnik crisis,' spurring the creation of NASA and igniting the Space Race.

evt-10-04-1963-hurricane-flora.scenario: It is early October 1963. Hurricane Flora has stalled for days over eastern Cuba, unleashing catastrophic flooding. Fidel Castro travels personally into the flooded region to oversee the rescue effort.
evt-10-04-1963-hurricane-flora.prompt: What did Castro do that became emblematic of the government's response?

choices.text: He ordered the immediate evacuation of Havana as a precaution
He requested emergency relief aid directly from Washington
He delegated the entire relief effort to the Cuban Red Cross
He personally waded through floodwaters to direct rescue and evacuation efforts

evt-10-04-1963-hurricane-flora.butterflyEffect: Castro waded through floodwaters and continued in an amphibious vehicle after his jeep became stuck, personally directing evacuations in the hardest-hit areas. Images of him sharing the disaster with ordinary Cubans reinforced his image as a leader present in hardship, strengthening domestic loyalty to the revolution even as the storm's death toll made it one of the deadliest Atlantic hurricanes on record.

evt-10-04-1965-pope-paul-vi.scenario: You are a UN delegate on 4 October 1965 as Pope Paul VI, the first pope ever to set foot in the Americas, rises to address the General Assembly in New York with the world watching amid the Vietnam War.
evt-10-04-1965-pope-paul-vi.prompt: What is the central message of his historic address to the United Nations?

choices.text: A call for the canonization of new American saints
A declaration of Vatican neutrality in all future conflicts
An appeal for peace and an end to war
A private meeting agenda with the US president only

evt-10-04-1965-pope-paul-vi.butterflyEffect: Paul VI delivered his famous appeal 'no more war, war never again,' urging the UN toward peace and disarmament. The visit cemented the Vatican's engagement with international diplomacy and modern global institutions, a shift that continued through his successors' own UN appearances.

evt-10-04-1966-basutoland.scenario: It's October 4, 1966, in Maseru. The Union Jack is lowered for the last time as the small mountain kingdom prepares to raise its own flag over a newly sovereign nation.
evt-10-04-1966-basutoland.prompt: What did Basutoland become upon gaining independence from Britain?

choices.text: A province absorbed into South Africa
The independent Kingdom of Lesotho
A self-governing dominion still under the British monarch
A republic renamed Basotholand

evt-10-04-1966-basutoland.butterflyEffect: Basutoland became the independent Kingdom of Lesotho under King Moshoeshoe II, a constitutional monarchy still entirely enclosed by South Africa. That geography left Lesotho economically dependent on its apartheid-era neighbour for decades, shaping its politics through labour migration, trade routes, and later South African military intervention.

evt-10-04-1967-omar-ali-saifuddien-iii.scenario: You are a senior court official in Brunei in October 1967. The Sultan, who has ruled since 1950 and steered the sultanate through the transition from British protection toward self-government, calls you to discuss the succession.
evt-10-04-1967-omar-ali-saifuddien-iii.prompt: What did Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien III decide to do?

choices.text: Appoint a council of regents instead of naming an heir
Remain Sultan for life and name a co-ruler
Abdicate the throne in favour of his son, Hassanal Bolkiah
Dissolve the sultanate and merge with Malaysia

evt-10-04-1967-omar-ali-saifuddien-iii.butterflyEffect: He abdicated in favour of his 21-year-old son, Hassanal Bolkiah, who became Sultan and would go on to reign for decades, eventually becoming one of the world's longest-serving monarchs. Omar Ali Saifuddien retained the title Seri Begawan Sultan and continued to advise the government.

evt-10-04-1983-richard-noble.scenario: You are strapped into Thrust2 on the hard salt flats of Black Rock Desert, Nevada, in October 1983, chasing a new land speed record. The car's power comes from an aircraft-derived engine howling behind your seat.
evt-10-04-1983-richard-noble.prompt: What kind of engine drives your record-breaking car?

choices.text: An electric motor bank
A supercharged piston engine
A jet engine adapted from a fighter aircraft
A liquid-fuel rocket engine

evt-10-04-1983-richard-noble.butterflyEffect: Noble's Thrust2, powered by a Rolls-Royce Avon jet engine, hit 633.468 mph, the fastest speed ever driven on land at the time. The achievement launched his ThrustSSC project, which in 1997 became the first car to officially break the sound barrier on land.

evt-10-04-1992-el-al-flight-1862.scenario: You are an air traffic controller at Schiphol on 4 October 1992. El Al Flight 1862, a cargo 747, has just lost two engines on its right wing and the crew is trying to turn back for an emergency landing over the densely packed Bijlmermeer housing estate.
evt-10-04-1992-el-al-flight-1862.prompt: What happens as the crippled jumbo jet attempts its return to the runway?

choices.text: It lands safely on a shortened runway at Schiphol
It circles for an hour before making an emergency landing
It crashes into apartment towers in the Bijlmermeer before reaching the airport
It ditches successfully in a nearby lake

evt-10-04-1992-el-al-flight-1862.butterflyEffect: The 747 lost lift and slammed into the Groeneveen and Klein-Kruitberg apartment towers before it could reach Schiphol, killing everyone aboard and several residents on the ground. Years later, revelations that the cargo manifest included chemical precursors for nerve agents fuelled a long Dutch health-effects controversy and a parliamentary inquiry, and permanently damaged trust in El Al's cargo transparency.

evt-10-04-1993-battle-of-mogadishu-1993.scenario: You are a US Ranger in Mogadishu on 3–4 October 1993. A Black Hawk helicopter has just been shot down over the city during a raid to capture lieutenants of warlord Mohamed Farrah Aidid, and your convoy is pinned down under militia fire.
evt-10-04-1993-battle-of-mogadishu-1993.prompt: What does the task force do after the helicopter goes down?

choices.text: Negotiate directly with Aidid's militia for a ceasefire
Call in airstrikes to level the surrounding neighborhood
Push forward to rescue the downed crew despite heavy losses
Immediately abandon the mission and evacuate all forces

evt-10-04-1993-battle-of-mogadishu-1993.butterflyEffect: US forces fought through the night to reach the crash site and extract survivors, resulting in a brutal urban battle that killed 18 American soldiers and far more Somalis. The televised carnage shocked the American public and led President Clinton to withdraw US troops from Somalia within months, an outcome that shaped US reluctance to intervene during the Rwandan genocide the following year.

evt-10-04-1993-1993-russian-constitution.scenario: It's October 4, 1993, in Moscow. Tanks loyal to President Yeltsin have ringed the White House, where hardline parliamentary deputies remain barricaded after days of standoff following his dissolution of parliament.
evt-10-04-1993-1993-russian-constitution.prompt: What did Yeltsin order to finally end the standoff?

choices.text: Tank units to shell the parliament building until it surrendered
Special forces to storm the building using no heavy weapons
A ceasefire brokered by the Russian Orthodox Church
A national referendum to dissolve his own presidency

evt-10-04-1993-1993-russian-constitution.butterflyEffect: Yeltsin ordered tanks to shell the parliament building until the deputies inside surrendered, killing roughly 150 people in the deadliest street violence in Moscow since 1917. The victory let Yeltsin push through a new constitution that December, concentrating power in the presidency and shaping Russia's political system for decades afterward.

evt-10-04-2001-siberia-airlines-flight-1.scenario: It is 4 October 2001 over the Black Sea. Ukrainian and Russian forces are conducting joint air-defence exercises near Crimea as Siberia Airlines Flight 1812 crosses the region en route from Tel Aviv to Novosibirsk.
evt-10-04-2001-siberia-airlines-flight-1.prompt: What does Ukraine eventually admit caused the airliner's destruction?

choices.text: A mechanical failure in the Tupolev's engines
An errant S-200 missile fired during the military exercise
A bomb planted aboard the aircraft
Pilot error during a storm

evt-10-04-2001-siberia-airlines-flight-1.butterflyEffect: Ukraine later acknowledged that an S-200 missile fired during the live exercise had likely gone astray and struck the aircraft, killing all 78 aboard. Kyiv paid compensation to victims' families, and the disaster prompted lasting scrutiny of live-fire military exercises conducted near active civilian air corridors.

evt-10-04-2003-maxim-restaurant-suicide-.scenario: You sit on Israel's security cabinet on the morning after a suicide bomber struck the Maxim restaurant in Haifa on 4 October 2003, killing families gathered for a meal. Islamic Jihad has claimed responsibility, and ministers are weighing how to respond.
evt-10-04-2003-maxim-restaurant-suicide-.prompt: What retaliatory action does Israel take in the days that follow?

choices.text: Israel launches a full ground invasion of the Gaza Strip
Israel closes all border crossings but takes no military action
Israeli jets strike a militant training camp inside Syria
Israel opens direct negotiations with Islamic Jihad

evt-10-04-2003-maxim-restaurant-suicide-.butterflyEffect: On 5 October 2003, Israeli warplanes struck a Palestinian militant training camp near Ain es Saheb in Syria, the deepest strike into Syrian territory in three decades. The raid heightened tensions with Damascus but did not draw Syria into direct conflict, and it hardened Israel's policy of striking militant infrastructure beyond Palestinian territories.

evt-10-04-2004-spaceshipone.scenario: It's October 4, 2004, at Mojave Air and Space Port. Pilot Brian Binnie is strapped into SpaceShipOne for its second qualifying flight in two weeks, the final hurdle to claim a $10 million prize.
evt-10-04-2004-spaceshipone.prompt: What must this flight achieve to win the Ansari X Prize?

choices.text: Complete a full orbit of the Earth before returning
Carry the equivalent of three people above 100km altitude for the second time in two weeks
Dock with the International Space Station briefly
Reach 50km altitude while carrying a satellite payload

evt-10-04-2004-spaceshipone.butterflyEffect: SpaceShipOne reached over 100km altitude for the second time in two weeks, meeting the prize's requirement to carry the equivalent of three people to space twice within a fortnight. Its win proved private spaceflight was viable, and its design was licensed to build Virgin Galactic's SpaceShipTwo; the original craft now hangs in the Smithsonian.

evt-10-04-2010-ajka-alumina-plant-accide.scenario: You are a local official in Kolontár, Hungary, in October 2010 as a collapsed reservoir wall sends a wave of caustic red sludge toward nearby villages. Streets are already filling with toxic waste.
evt-10-04-2010-ajka-alumina-plant-accide.prompt: What should the immediate priority be for the response?

choices.text: Focus only on repairing the plant's containment wall
Notify international media before warning residents
Wait for a full damage assessment before acting
Evacuate residents downstream immediately

evt-10-04-2010-ajka-alumina-plant-accide.butterflyEffect: Authorities evacuated thousands from Kolontár and Devecser as the toxic red mud, containing heavy metals, swept through homes and reached tributaries of the Danube. The disaster killed several people, caused lasting environmental damage, and triggered stricter European Union regulation of mining waste storage.

evt-10-04-2017-united-states-army-specia.scenario: You are part of a joint U.S.-Nigerien Special Forces patrol near the village of Tongo Tongo in October 2017 when militants linked to the Islamic State open fire from all sides, catching your convoy without air support.
evt-10-04-2017-united-states-army-specia.prompt: What followed for the U.S. military in the aftermath of the ambush?

choices.text: Immediate withdrawal of all U.S. forces from Africa
Court-martial proceedings against the surviving soldiers
A Pentagon investigation into mission approval and support failures
Deployment of ten thousand additional troops to Niger
