evt-10-09-2024-hurricane-milton.scenario: It's 9 October 2024, and you're a resident of Siesta Key, Florida, watching Hurricane Milton churn toward the coast at Category 3 strength after having peaked as a rare Category 5 in the Gulf.
evt-10-09-2024-hurricane-milton.prompt: With landfall hours away, what's the safest choice?

choices.text: Move to a neighbor's second floor and ride it out
Evacuate inland immediately under the mandatory order
Board up the windows and shelter in your beachfront home
Wait to see the next radar update before deciding

evt-10-09-2024-hurricane-milton.butterflyEffect: Milton made landfall and spawned one of the most intense tornado outbreaks ever produced by a hurricane, compounding damage in areas Hurricane Helene had devastated weeks earlier. Total damages reached an estimated $34.3 billion, making it the ninth-costliest Atlantic hurricane on record.

evt-10-10-1846-william-lassell.scenario: It is October 1846 in Liverpool, just weeks after Neptune's discovery made headlines across Europe. You peer through your own hand-built reflecting telescope, hunting for anything orbiting the new planet.
evt-10-10-1846-william-lassell.prompt: How do you confirm the faint point of light near Neptune is truly a moon?

choices.text: Photograph it once and measure its brightness
Calculate its orbit from Newtonian theory alone
Track its position over several nights to see it move with Neptune
Wait for another astronomer to confirm it first

evt-10-10-1846-william-lassell.butterflyEffect: William Lassell tracked the tiny speck night after night and confirmed it was orbiting Neptune, naming it Triton. Its unusual retrograde orbit later convinced astronomers it was a captured object rather than formed alongside Neptune, an early clue toward understanding the icy bodies of the outer solar system.

evt-10-10-1903-emmeline-pankhurst.scenario: It is October 1903 in Manchester. You sit in a small parlour meeting with Emmeline Pankhurst and a handful of other women frustrated that decades of polite petitioning have won suffragists nothing.
evt-10-10-1903-emmeline-pankhurst.prompt: What motto does the new Women's Social and Political Union adopt to guide its tactics?

choices.text: Education Before Equality
Petition Before Protest
Patience and Persuasion
Deeds not Words

evt-10-10-1903-emmeline-pankhurst.butterflyEffect: The WSPU chose 'Deeds not Words' and turned to militancy: window-smashing, arson, and hunger strikes that shocked Edwardian Britain. The controversy over these tactics split the suffrage movement but kept the cause in headlines, and partial voting rights for women followed in 1918.

evt-10-10-1911-1911-revolution.scenario: It is the night of 10 October 1911 in Wuchang. Your revolutionary cell's bomb-making workshop has just been discovered by Qing authorities, and membership lists may already be in their hands.
evt-10-10-1911-1911-revolution.prompt: What should the exposed revolutionaries do next?

choices.text: Wait for reinforcements from revolutionaries in other provinces
Surrender to the authorities and cooperate
Launch the uprising immediately that night
Scatter and go into hiding until it is safe to regroup

evt-10-10-1911-1911-revolution.butterflyEffect: The conspirators launched their uprising that very night rather than wait for the crackdown to reach them. The revolt spread rapidly across provinces, forcing the abdication of the last Qing emperor by February 1912 and ending over two thousand years of imperial rule, ushering in the Republic of China.

evt-10-10-1963-partial-nuclear-test-ban-.scenario: It is 10 October 1963 in Moscow, and you are a junior diplomat watching the Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty formally enter into force between the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Soviet Union.
evt-10-10-1963-partial-nuclear-test-ban-.prompt: Which type of nuclear testing does the new treaty still permit?

choices.text: Testing in outer space
Underground testing
Underwater testing
Atmospheric testing

evt-10-10-1963-partial-nuclear-test-ban-.butterflyEffect: The treaty banned atmospheric, space, and underwater tests but left underground testing untouched, so the arms race continued beneath the surface. It nonetheless marked the first major Cold War arms-control agreement, setting a precedent that led toward the 1968 Non-Proliferation Treaty and later SALT negotiations.

evt-10-10-1973-spiro-agnew.scenario: It is October 1973. As Vice President, you face federal charges over kickbacks taken while governor of Maryland, and prosecutors have offered a deal in exchange for stepping down.

choices.text: Fight the charges in court and refuse to resign
Claim executive immunity from prosecution while in office
Ask Nixon to pardon him before any charges are filed
Resign and plead no contest to one tax evasion charge

evt-10-10-1973-spiro-agnew.butterflyEffect: Agnew resigned and pleaded no contest to a single charge of tax evasion, becoming only the second vice president in history to resign. His departure opened the vice presidency for Gerald Ford under the 25th Amendment, positioning Ford to become president without ever winning a national election when Nixon resigned less than a year later.

evt-10-10-1980-1980-el-asnam-earthquake.scenario: You are an engineer surveying El Asnam's shattered apartment blocks hours after the magnitude 7.1 quake on 10 October 1980, with a powerful aftershock already having struck.
evt-10-10-1980-1980-el-asnam-earthquake.prompt: What should Algerian authorities prioritize in rebuilding?

choices.text: Rebuild quickly without studying the newly exposed fault
Rebuild with stricter seismic codes and rename the town
Reconstruct every building exactly as it stood before
Abandon the site entirely and relocate the population permanently

evt-10-10-1980-1980-el-asnam-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The town was rebuilt with stricter seismic building codes and renamed Chlef. The disaster pushed Algeria to overhaul its national construction standards, though the same fault zone had also produced the destructive 1954 earthquake nearby.

evt-10-10-1980-farabundo-marti-national-.scenario: It is October 1980 in El Salvador. Five separate leftist guerrilla armies are fighting the military government alone, and you are among the commanders debating whether scattered resistance can survive a coordinated crackdown.
evt-10-10-1980-farabundo-marti-national-.prompt: What do the five guerrilla groups decide to do?

choices.text: Keep operating as five separate independent armies
Merge into a single united front, the FMLN, to coordinate the armed struggle
Disband and seek asylum abroad
Merge with the ruling party's youth wing

evt-10-10-1980-farabundo-marti-national-.butterflyEffect: The five factions united as the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front, launching a twelve-year civil war against the government. The 1992 Chapultepec Peace Accords ended the fighting and turned the FMLN into a legal political party, which went on to win the Salvadoran presidency in 2009.

evt-10-10-1985-achille-lauro-hijacking.scenario: It is 10 October 1985. You are flying a US Navy F-14 over the Mediterranean, ordered to intercept an EgyptAir jet carrying the four men who hijacked the Achille Lauro and murdered Leon Klinghoffer, now being flown out of Egypt.
evt-10-10-1985-achille-lauro-hijacking.prompt: What do you do with the intercepted airliner?

choices.text: Force it to land at the NATO base at Sigonella, Sicily
Escort it safely to its destination in Tunis
Shoot the airliner down over international waters
Allow it to continue on to Cairo unmolested

evt-10-10-1985-achille-lauro-hijacking.butterflyEffect: The fighters forced the airliner to land at the NATO base in Sigonella, Sicily, where US Delta Force operators and Italian carabinieri both surrounded the plane in a tense standoff. Italy ultimately took custody of the hijackers, straining US-Italian relations and contributing to political turmoil that helped bring down Prime Minister Bettino Craxi's government the following year.

evt-10-10-1986-1986-san-salvador-earthqu.scenario: It is 10 October 1986 and a violent shallow earthquake has just torn through San Salvador. You are part of a rescue team trying to reach survivors trapped in collapsed buildings downtown.
evt-10-10-1986-1986-san-salvador-earthqu.prompt: What ongoing conflict complicates the emergency response across the country?

choices.text: The Salvadoran Civil War
A border war with Honduras
A coup attempt in the capital
A general workers' strike

evt-10-10-1986-1986-san-salvador-earthqu.butterflyEffect: El Salvador's civil war, then in its sixth year, disrupted communications, strained already limited resources, and made some areas dangerous for rescue teams to reach. International aid still poured in, but the disaster deepened the hardship of a population already suffering the war's toll.

evt-10-10-1992-vidyasagar-setu.scenario: You are a Kolkata commuter in 1992, driving across the newly opened Vidyasagar Setu, India's first cable-stayed bridge, after two decades of construction over the Hooghly River.
evt-10-10-1992-vidyasagar-setu.prompt: What problem does this new bridge actually solve for the city?

choices.text: It becomes the very first bridge ever built across the Hooghly
It opens as a toll-free bridge funded entirely by the state
It relieves heavy traffic congestion on the old Howrah Bridge
It provides a direct road link between Kolkata and Mumbai

evt-10-10-1992-vidyasagar-setu.butterflyEffect: The bridge relieved chronic congestion on the aging Howrah Bridge by giving Kolkata and Howrah a second crossing. Its toll revenue and traffic capacity made it a model for later Indian infrastructure projects using public-private partnerships.

evt-10-10-2007-sheikh-muszaphar-shukor.scenario: It is 10 October 2007. You are Sheikh Muszaphar Shukor, a Malaysian doctor strapped into Soyuz TMA-11, about to become the first Malaysian in space under an agreement with Russia's space agency.
evt-10-10-2007-sheikh-muszaphar-shukor.prompt: How is his return to Earth arranged after the mission?

choices.text: He returns with the departing Expedition 15 crew on Soyuz TMA-10
He returns aboard a NASA Space Shuttle
He returns on the same Soyuz TMA-11 he launched in
He stays aboard the ISS for a full six-month rotation

evt-10-10-2007-sheikh-muszaphar-shukor.butterflyEffect: Muszaphar spent about ten days aboard the ISS before returning not on the craft he launched in, but on Soyuz TMA-10 with the departing Expedition 15 crew. This taxi-seat arrangement, paid for through Malaysia's Angkasawan program, became a template other nations later used to fly short-duration spaceflight participants to the station.

evt-10-10-2018-hurricane-michael.scenario: It is the night before landfall in October 2018. You live in Mexico Beach, Florida, and the storm off the coast has just exploded overnight from a moderate hurricane into a monster far stronger than forecasters predicted only a day earlier.
evt-10-10-2018-hurricane-michael.prompt: With landfall now only hours away, what is your best course of action?

choices.text: Move only to a neighbor's sturdier house nearby
Board up windows and shelter at home
Evacuate immediately, even at night
Wait until morning to decide

evt-10-10-2018-hurricane-michael.butterflyEffect: Michael's rapid intensification left little warning time, and it slammed into the Panhandle as the first Category 5 on record there, flattening Mexico Beach. The storm exposed gaps in forecasting fast-strengthening hurricanes, pushing the National Hurricane Center to invest further in rapid-intensification prediction models.

evt-10-11-1142-treaty-of-shaoxing.scenario: It is 1142 and you serve at the court of Emperor Gaozong of Song. The treaty ending decades of war with the Jin has just been ratified, but the emperor now turns his attention to the generals who wanted to keep fighting.
evt-10-11-1142-treaty-of-shaoxing.prompt: What happens to the outspoken anti-Jin general Yue Fei after the treaty?

choices.text: He is promoted to command the northern frontier
He retires peacefully to his estates
He defects to the Jin dynasty
He is executed on the emperor's orders

evt-10-11-1142-treaty-of-shaoxing.butterflyEffect: Yue Fei was arrested on trumped-up charges and executed in prison in early 1142, removing the most effective military voice against accommodation with the Jin. He was later exonerated and became a folk hero symbolizing loyalty and resistance, his tomb in Hangzhou still a pilgrimage site today.

evt-10-11-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 11 October 1776 on Lake Champlain. You serve under Benedict Arnold, whose hastily built fleet of gunboats blocks a much larger British force sailing south from Canada toward Fort Ticonderoga.
evt-10-11-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What should Arnold's fleet do against the superior British squadron?

choices.text: Sail out to attack the British fleet head-on in open water
Surrender the fleet to avoid needless bloodshed
Retreat immediately without engaging to preserve every vessel
Anchor in a defensive line and fight to delay the British advance as long as possible

evt-10-11-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Arnold's ships were battered and mostly destroyed at Valcour Island, but the fighting cost the British so much time that they called off the campaign until spring 1777. That delay let the Continental Army regroup and contributed to the British defeat at Saratoga the following year, a turning point that brought France into the war on the American side.

evt-10-11-1797-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: It is 11 October 1797 off the Dutch coast near Camperdown. Admiral Adam Duncan's Royal Navy fleet, still recovering from the year's mutinies, closes on a Dutch fleet under Admiral de Winter defending the Batavian Republic.
evt-10-11-1797-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What order does Duncan give to break the Dutch line of battle?

choices.text: Blockade the port instead of engaging directly
Offer the Dutch fleet terms of surrender before firing
Attack in two divisions, cutting through the Dutch line rather than forming a single traditional line
Retreat and wait for reinforcements from the Channel Fleet

evt-10-11-1797-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: Duncan's unconventional two-column attack shattered the Dutch fleet, capturing eleven ships without losing a single British vessel. The victory at Camperdown eliminated the Dutch navy as a threat, restored British public confidence after the Nore mutiny, and secured the North Sea for Britain for the rest of the wars.

evt-10-11-1840-bashir-shihab-ii.scenario: It is 1840 and you are Bashir Shihab II, Emir of Mount Lebanon for over fifty years. Ottoman troops and rebellious subjects, backed by European powers, now surround your position, and your decades of shrewd balancing between empires have finally run out of room.
evt-10-11-1840-bashir-shihab-ii.prompt: With his power collapsing, what does Bashir Shihab II do?

choices.text: He leads a final battle and dies fighting
He flees permanently to Egypt with Muhammad Ali's army
He surrenders and is exiled by the Ottomans
He declares Mount Lebanon fully independent

evt-10-11-1840-bashir-shihab-ii.butterflyEffect: Bashir surrendered to Ottoman authorities and was sent into exile, eventually dying in Istanbul in 1850. His fall ended nearly two centuries of Shihabi rule and led the Ottomans to impose new administrative arrangements over Mount Lebanon that reshaped the region's sectarian politics for decades.

evt-10-11-1865-morant-bay-rebellion.scenario: It is 11 October 1865 in Morant Bay, Jamaica. Preacher Paul Bogle leads hundreds of impoverished freedmen toward the courthouse to protest injustice, and the parish militia stands ready with rifles.
evt-10-11-1865-morant-bay-rebellion.prompt: What did colonial authorities do in the aftermath of the uprising?

choices.text: British troops withdrew and left the parish self-governing
Bogle was invited to negotiate directly with the Colonial Office
Governor Eyre declared martial law and led a brutal reprisal campaign, executing hundreds
The governor pardoned the protesters and reformed land laws

evt-10-11-1865-morant-bay-rebellion.butterflyEffect: Governor Edward Eyre's harsh crackdown killed far more people than the initial unrest and provoked fierce controversy in Britain, dividing intellectuals like John Stuart Mill and Thomas Carlyle. The scandal led to Eyre's recall and to Jamaica losing its elected assembly, becoming a Crown Colony directly ruled from London.

evt-10-11-1890-washington-d-c.scenario: It is 1890 in Washington, D.C. You can trace your lineage to a soldier of the Revolutionary War, but the all-male Sons of the American Revolution has just refused to admit women to its ranks.
evt-10-11-1890-washington-d-c.prompt: What do you and other excluded women do in response?

choices.text: Petition the Sons of the American Revolution to reverse the ban
Join the National Woman Suffrage Association instead
Found the Daughters of the American Revolution
Abandon genealogical societies altogether

evt-10-11-1890-washington-d-c.butterflyEffect: Excluded women founded the Daughters of the American Revolution that same year, creating a lineage society devoted to historic preservation, education, and patriotism. The DAR grew into one of America's most influential women's organizations, though it later drew controversy for barring Black contralto Marian Anderson from its concert hall in 1939.

evt-10-11-1937-edward-viii.scenario: It is October 1937 and you are the Duke of Windsor, arriving at Berlin's Friedrichstraße station with your wife Wallis on a tour of Nazi Germany, less than a year after abdicating the British throne.
evt-10-11-1937-edward-viii.prompt: What does the Duke of Windsor do during this controversial German visit?

choices.text: He publicly denounces Nazi policies before German officials
He tours Nazi facilities and meets privately with Hitler
He refuses all official engagements and returns home early
He secretly meets with German resistance figures

evt-10-11-1937-edward-viii.butterflyEffect: The Duke toured Nazi factories, military facilities, and met privately with Hitler at his Berchtesgaden retreat, gestures widely seen as sympathetic to the regime. The visit deepened British establishment distrust of him, reinforcing the government's decision to keep him away from any position of influence for the rest of his life.

evt-10-11-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 11 October 1942 off Guadalcanal. You command a U.S. cruiser-destroyer force under Rear Admiral Norman Scott, radar showing an unidentified Japanese column approaching Cape Esperance in the dark.
evt-10-11-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What should the American task force do with its radar contact?

choices.text: Hold fire and wait for the Japanese ships to identify themselves first
Withdraw to avoid a night engagement with an unknown force
Use the radar advantage to open fire first before the enemy can react
Request air support and delay any surface action until dawn

evt-10-11-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Scott's force opened fire first, sinking a cruiser and destroyer and killing Japanese commander Aritomo Goto, in one of the first U.S. night-surface victories of the Pacific War. The win boosted American confidence in radar-guided night fighting, though Japan continued costly reinforcement runs to Guadalcanal for months afterward.

evt-10-11-1950-cbs.scenario: It is 1950 and the FCC has just licensed CBS's field-sequential color television system as the official American color standard, over rival systems from RCA and others.
evt-10-11-1950-cbs.prompt: What ultimately happens to CBS's color standard in the years that follow?

choices.text: It is adopted by European broadcasters instead
It becomes the permanent worldwide color standard
It is abandoned in favor of RCA's compatible NTSC system
It merges seamlessly with existing black-and-white sets

evt-10-11-1950-cbs.butterflyEffect: CBS's system was incompatible with existing black-and-white sets and required a spinning color wheel inside the receiver, making it commercially impractical. Production was halted within a few years, and in 1953 the FCC adopted RCA's compatible NTSC color system instead, which became the American standard for decades.

evt-10-11-1968-apollo-7.scenario: It is October 1968 aboard Apollo 7 in Earth orbit. Commander Wally Schirra is nursing a bad head cold, and mission rules call for the crew to wear their helmets during the fiery, pressure-changing descent through the atmosphere.
evt-10-11-1968-apollo-7.prompt: Should Schirra order the crew to keep their helmets on for reentry despite his cold?

choices.text: Remove helmets for reentry to avoid the risk of eardrum injury from a blocked nose
Abort the mission early and return home immediately
Wear helmets exactly as mission rules specify, regardless of health concerns
Delay reentry until the cold clears completely

evt-10-11-1968-apollo-7.butterflyEffect: Schirra defied ground control and had the crew remove their helmets, reasoning a blocked nose could rupture eardrums during pressure changes; the descent went safely. His running friction with Houston over this and other decisions meant none of the Apollo 7 astronauts flew for NASA again, even as the mission's success cleared the way for Apollo 8's lunar orbit that December.

evt-10-11-1973-typhoon-nora-1973.scenario: It is early October 1973 over the western Pacific. Meteorologists watch a tropical depression explode in strength, its pressure plunging 77 millibars in a single day as it barrels toward the Philippines and China.
evt-10-11-1973-typhoon-nora-1973.prompt: What happened to Typhoon Nora after reaching its record-setting peak intensity?

choices.text: It curved north and struck Japan directly
It stalled and dissipated harmlessly over open ocean
It weakened as it brushed Luzon, then made landfall in China before dissipating
It maintained peak strength all the way to landfall

evt-10-11-1973-typhoon-nora-1973.butterflyEffect: Nora's peak pressure of 875 mb made it briefly the most intense tropical cyclone on record, a mark later tied and surpassed by storms like Tip and Patricia. Its weakening track before landfall in China spared the Philippines the full force of a storm that could otherwise have ranked among history's deadliest.

evt-10-11-1984-space-shuttle-challenger.scenario: You are astronaut Kathryn D. Sullivan aboard Space Shuttle Challenger on 11 October 1984, floating toward the airlock on mission STS-41-G, about to become part of spaceflight history.
evt-10-11-1984-space-shuttle-challenger.prompt: What milestone does Sullivan achieve on this spacewalk?

choices.text: First American woman to conduct a spacewalk
First woman ever to conduct a spacewalk
First person to conduct an untethered spacewalk
First American to conduct a spacewalk

evt-10-11-1984-space-shuttle-challenger.butterflyEffect: Sullivan became the first American woman to walk in space, months after Soviet cosmonaut Svetlana Savitskaya became the first woman ever to do so. Sullivan went on to become NASA's chief scientist and later led NOAA, and her flight helped open EVA assignments to more women astronauts in subsequent shuttle missions.

evt-10-11-1984-kathryn-d-sullivan.scenario: It is 11 October 1984, and you are astronaut Kathryn D. Sullivan aboard Space Shuttle Challenger, suited up and about to open the airlock hatch into the vacuum of space.
evt-10-11-1984-kathryn-d-sullivan.prompt: What historic first does Sullivan achieve on this mission?

choices.text: She becomes the first American woman to walk in space
She becomes the first person to repair a satellite in orbit
She becomes the first woman to command a shuttle mission
She becomes the first woman to fly in space

evt-10-11-1984-kathryn-d-sullivan.butterflyEffect: Sullivan became the first American woman to perform a spacewalk, working outside Challenger to demonstrate techniques for refueling satellites in orbit. Her feat, following Soviet cosmonaut Svetlana Savitskaya's spacewalk earlier that year, expanded the roles open to women in NASA's astronaut corps and paved the way for her later leadership as head of NOAA.

evt-10-11-1986-ronald-reagan.scenario: You're part of the American delegation inside Höfði House in Reykjavik on 11 October 1986, watching Reagan and Gorbachev edge astonishingly close to an agreement to eliminate nuclear arsenals entirely.
evt-10-11-1986-ronald-reagan.prompt: What causes the summit to collapse without a signed agreement?

choices.text: The two leaders cannot agree on a translator
Reagan refuses to abandon the Strategic Defense Initiative
Gorbachev refuses to discuss any arms control measures
The US Congress blocks any deal before it can be signed

evt-10-11-1986-ronald-reagan.butterflyEffect: Reagan refused to give up the Strategic Defense Initiative, and the talks broke down without a treaty, leaving both leaders visibly frustrated. Yet the near-agreement laid groundwork for the 1987 INF Treaty, marking a turning point that accelerated the end of the Cold War arms race.

evt-10-11-1987-sri-lankan-civil-war.scenario: You are an Indian Army officer with the Indian Peace Keeping Force in October 1987, ordered to launch Operation Pawan to disarm LTTE fighters and secure Jaffna under the terms of the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord.
evt-10-11-1987-sri-lankan-civil-war.prompt: What action does the IPKF take to try to seize control of Jaffna?

choices.text: Request Sri Lankan air force strikes on the city
Withdraw all Indian troops back to India
Negotiate an immediate ceasefire with LTTE leadership
Launch a full military assault into Jaffna city

evt-10-11-1987-sri-lankan-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The IPKF launched a direct assault into Jaffna, triggering intense urban fighting far bloodier than planners had expected. Though the LTTE was temporarily pushed out of the city, the IPKF became mired in a prolonged and costly counter-insurgency, ultimately withdrawing from Sri Lanka in 1990 without securing lasting peace.

evt-10-11-1987-second-national-march-on-.scenario: It is 11 October 1987 in Washington, D.C. You march with roughly 750,000 people demanding federal action on AIDS and equal rights, and organizers are planning a follow-up act of civil disobedience at the Supreme Court the next morning.
evt-10-11-1987-second-national-march-on-.prompt: Should activists proceed with mass arrests at the Supreme Court the following day?

choices.text: Cancel the protest to avoid confrontation with law enforcement
Shift the protest to a private meeting with senators instead
Proceed with civil disobedience to force national media attention on the cause
Wait for a more favorable political climate before acting

evt-10-11-1987-second-national-march-on-.butterflyEffect: On October 13, activists including many from ACT UP were arrested protesting the Court's 1986 Bowers v. Hardwick ruling upholding sodomy laws. The march and the arrests brought unprecedented national media coverage to AIDS activism and LGBT rights, energizing a movement that would push for the eventual overturning of sodomy laws in Lawrence v. Texas in 2003.

evt-10-11-1987-names-project-aids-memori.scenario: It is 11 October 1987 on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. Thousands of fabric panels, each stitched by grieving friends and family, are being unfolded across the grass for the first time as part of a national demonstration.
evt-10-11-1987-names-project-aids-memori.prompt: As an organizer, how do you want visitors to experience the quilt's first display?

choices.text: Limit viewing to family members of the deceased only
Display it quietly indoors to avoid drawing political attention
Lay it out publicly on the Mall with names read aloud so the scale of loss is impossible to ignore
Postpone the display until public opinion on AIDS improves

evt-10-11-1987-names-project-aids-memori.butterflyEffect: The quilt covered an area larger than a football field and drew roughly half a million visitors that weekend, forcing the AIDS crisis into public view at a time when many victims were denied funerals due to stigma. It grew into the largest piece of community folk art in the world and helped normalize public mourning and activism around HIV/AIDS.

evt-10-11-1991-anita-hill.scenario: It is 11 October 1991 and you sit on the Senate Judiciary Committee. Law professor Anita Hill has just testified on live television that Supreme Court nominee Clarence Thomas sexually harassed her when she worked for him.
evt-10-11-1991-anita-hill.prompt: How should the Senate proceed with Thomas's confirmation after this testimony?

choices.text: Postpone the confirmation vote indefinitely pending a criminal investigation
Hold the scheduled vote after weighing the testimony alongside Thomas's denial
Withdraw the nomination immediately without a further vote
Refer the matter to the Supreme Court for internal review

evt-10-11-1991-anita-hill.butterflyEffect: Despite Hill's testimony, the Senate confirmed Thomas by a narrow 52–48 vote, one of the closest Supreme Court confirmations in history. The hearings sparked national debate on workplace sexual harassment, contributed to a surge of women elected to Congress in 1992 dubbed the 'Year of the Woman,' and led many employers to adopt harassment policies.

evt-10-11-2001-polaroid-corporation.scenario: You're a longtime employee arriving at Polaroid's Massachusetts headquarters on 11 October 2001. Word has just spread that the once-dominant instant photography giant has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, crushed by debt and the rise of digital cameras.
evt-10-11-2001-polaroid-corporation.prompt: What happens to Polaroid in the aftermath of this filing?

choices.text: The US government nationalizes the company to save jobs
The company quickly emerges from bankruptcy unchanged
Its assets are sold off and the brand is later licensed to other manufacturers
Kodak purchases Polaroid outright and merges operations

evt-10-11-2001-polaroid-corporation.butterflyEffect: Polaroid's manufacturing operations were broken up and sold off in 2002, and its brand name was later licensed out for digital cameras, instant printers, and sunglasses rather than made by the original company. The Land-era Polaroid Corporation effectively ceased to exist, even as its name lived on as a licensed brand for decades.

evt-10-11-2002-myyrmanni-bombing.scenario: It is the afternoon of 11 October 2002 in the Myyrmanni shopping centre near Helsinki. A bomb hidden in a backpack has just exploded near a crowd gathered for a children's clown show, and investigators must work out who planted it.
evt-10-11-2002-myyrmanni-bombing.prompt: How did investigators ultimately identify the bomber?

choices.text: An anonymous tip named a former mall employee
A security camera caught him fleeing the mall before detonation
Forensic evidence linked one of the dead, initially assumed to be a bystander, to the explosive device
He was arrested days later trying to buy more chemicals

evt-10-11-2002-myyrmanni-bombing.butterflyEffect: Petri Gerdt, a young chemistry hobbyist who had experimented with explosives, was killed by his own device and was initially treated as a victim before forensics identified him as the bomber. The attack led Finland to tighten regulations on chemical purchases and sparked debate about monitoring online bomb-making forums.

evt-10-11-2018-soyuz-ms-10.scenario: You are aboard Soyuz MS-10 with your fellow cosmonaut, roughly two minutes after launch on 11 October 2018, when a booster failure suddenly throws your capsule off its planned trajectory toward the International Space Station.
evt-10-11-2018-soyuz-ms-10.prompt: What saves you and your crewmate in this emergency?

choices.text: The crew ejects using onboard ejection seats
The crew manually restarts the failed booster
The automatic abort system triggers a ballistic descent to safety
The capsule continues to orbit on its remaining engines

evt-10-11-2018-soyuz-ms-10.butterflyEffect: The automatic abort system triggered a ballistic descent, and both Alexey Ovchinin and Nick Hague landed safely in Kazakhstan under heavy g-forces. An investigation traced the failure to a bent sensor pin damaged during assembly, grounding crewed Soyuz-FG launches until the issue was fixed and flights resumed that December.

evt-10-12-1492-voyages-of-christopher-co.scenario: It is 2 a.m. on 12 October 1492. You are the lookout aboard the Pinta, weeks into the Atlantic crossing, when moonlight reveals a pale line on the horizon that could be land — or another false alarm.
evt-10-12-1492-voyages-of-christopher-co.prompt: What do you do the instant you're sure you see land?

choices.text: Report it only to the captain of your own ship and let him decide whether to tell Columbus
Say nothing until morning to be certain it isn't a cloud bank
Fire the signal cannon to alert the rest of the fleet, as agreed for the sighting reward
Turn the ship toward the shape immediately without waking the crew

evt-10-12-1492-voyages-of-christopher-co.butterflyEffect: The lookout, Rodrigo de Triana, fired the ship's gun to signal the fleet, and at dawn the expedition landed on an island in the Bahamas that Columbus named San Salvador. Columbus later insisted he had already sighted a light the night before and claimed the promised reward for himself, a dispute that foreshadowed the exploitation to come; the landfall itself opened sustained European contact with the Americas.

evt-10-12-1798-peasants-war-1798.scenario: It's October 1798 in the village of Overmere in the Southern Netherlands. French officials have just posted conscription lists under the new Jourdan Law, demanding your sons for armies of a Republic you never chose to obey.
evt-10-12-1798-peasants-war-1798.prompt: How do the peasants of Overmere respond to the conscription orders?

choices.text: They petition the French Directory for exemptions
They flee en masse across the border into Austrian territory
They comply and send their sons to be conscripted
They rise up and attack the French officials enforcing the law

evt-10-12-1798-peasants-war-1798.butterflyEffect: The villagers rose up and attacked French representatives, and the revolt spread rapidly across Flanders and Brabant as the Boerenkrijg, or Peasants' War. French troops crushed the uprising by December 1798 with mass executions, but the episode became a lasting symbol of local resistance to French rule and later fed into Belgian national memory.

evt-10-12-1799-jeanne-genevieve-garnerin.scenario: It is 12 October 1799, high above Paris. You are Jeanne Geneviève Garnerin, alone in a hydrogen balloon at 900 metres, your husband's experimental parachute rigged beneath the basket, and the crowd below is waiting.
evt-10-12-1799-jeanne-genevieve-garnerin.prompt: What do you do to become the first woman to descend by parachute?

choices.text: Release gas from the balloon and float down still attached to the basket
Cut loose and jump, trusting the parachute to open beneath you
Wait for your husband to jump first and follow only if he lands safely
Refuse to jump and order the balloon brought down gently instead

evt-10-12-1799-jeanne-genevieve-garnerin.butterflyEffect: She released the balloon and dropped beneath the canopy, landing safely and proving a woman could survive a parachute descent from altitude. Her feat, following her husband André-Jacques Garnerin's earlier jumps, helped establish parachuting as a serious pursuit rather than a mere circus stunt, inspiring generations of aeronauts and, eventually, military escape technology.

evt-10-12-1892-pledge-of-allegiance.scenario: It is 12 October 1892, the 400th anniversary of Columbus's landfall. You are a schoolteacher whose class is taking part in a nationwide public-school celebration built around a new verse by Francis Bellamy, printed for the occasion.
evt-10-12-1892-pledge-of-allegiance.prompt: What should your students do as part of the ceremony?

choices.text: Recite the newly written Pledge of Allegiance
Salute the flag in silence without words
Sing the national anthem instead
Read aloud from the Declaration of Independence

evt-10-12-1892-pledge-of-allegiance.butterflyEffect: Students across the country recited Bellamy's new Pledge of Allegiance for the first time, and it quickly became a daily classroom ritual. It was later amended by Congress, most notably adding the words 'under God' in 1954.

evt-10-12-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It is dawn on 12 October 1917 near Passchendaele. You command a New Zealand company ordered to advance across waterlogged ground, and reports are coming back that the artillery has failed to cut the German barbed wire ahead of you.
evt-10-12-1917-world-war-i.prompt: Do you press the attack as ordered despite the uncut wire?

choices.text: Withdraw to the starting trenches without authorisation
Advance as ordered, following the timetable despite the uncut wire
Order the men to dig in and wait for reinforcements before moving
Halt the company and send word up the line requesting a postponement

evt-10-12-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The New Zealand Division attacked as ordered into intact wire and murderous machine-gun fire, suffering more than 2,000 casualties in a single morning — still remembered as the deadliest day in New Zealand's military history. The failed assault on Bellevue Spur exposed the folly of attacking without proper artillery support and left a scar on New Zealand's national memory comparable to Gallipoli.

evt-10-12-1946-canto-degli-italiani.scenario: It is October 1946 in the newborn Italian Republic. The monarchy has just been abolished by referendum, and officials must choose a song to represent the nation at state occasions, since the old royal march no longer fits.
evt-10-12-1946-canto-degli-italiani.prompt: Which song should be adopted as the republic's provisional national anthem?

choices.text: Marcia Reale, the former royal march
Va, pensiero, the chorus from Verdi's Nabucco
Il Canto degli Italiani, Mameli's patriotic hymn
Giovinezza, the fascist party anthem

evt-10-12-1946-canto-degli-italiani.butterflyEffect: Il Canto degli Italiani, Mameli's 1847 patriotic hymn, was chosen as a provisional anthem. It remained only 'provisional' for over seventy years until Italian law formally confirmed it as the official national anthem in 2017.

evt-10-12-1960-nikita-khrushchev.scenario: It is 12 October 1960 at the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Filipino delegate Lorenzo Sumulong has just accused the Soviet Union of practicing colonialism in Eastern Europe, and Nikita Khrushchev, seated at the Soviet desk, is furious.
evt-10-12-1960-nikita-khrushchev.prompt: What does Khrushchev reportedly do to register his outrage?

choices.text: He demands the Filipino delegate be expelled from the UN
He storms out of the General Assembly hall
He calls for an immediate vote of censure against the Philippines
He pulls off his shoe and pounds it on the desk

evt-10-12-1960-nikita-khrushchev.butterflyEffect: According to widely repeated accounts, Khrushchev pulled off his shoe and pounded it on the desk in protest, though several eyewitnesses and later historians dispute whether this actually happened as described. True or exaggerated, the image became one of the defining, almost cartoonish symbols of Cold War brinkmanship and Khrushchev's combustible public style.

evt-10-12-1960-japan-socialist-party.scenario: It is 12 October 1960 in Tokyo, and you are in the studio audience for a live televised debate among party leaders. Suddenly a teenage ultranationalist bolts across the stage toward Japan Socialist Party leader Inejirō Asanuma.
evt-10-12-1960-japan-socialist-party.prompt: What does the attacker do as cameras keep rolling?

choices.text: He stabs Asanuma with a short sword
He shoots Asanuma with a pistol
He throws a smoke bomb onto the stage
He punches Asanuma and flees the studio

evt-10-12-1960-japan-socialist-party.butterflyEffect: Seventeen-year-old Otoya Yamaguchi stabbed Asanuma with a short sword, killing him live on air; Yamaguchi died in custody weeks later. Yasushi Nagao's photograph of the attack won a Pulitzer Prize and became one of the most famous news images of the twentieth century, and the killing deepened the era's bitter left-right political violence in Japan.

evt-10-12-1984-provisional-irish-republi.scenario: It is the early hours of 12 October 1984 in Brighton. A bomb planted by the Provisional IRA has just torn through the Grand Hotel during the Conservative Party conference, and you are advising Margaret Thatcher on what happens next.
evt-10-12-1984-provisional-irish-republi.prompt: What do you advise the Prime Minister to do about the conference?

choices.text: Postpone the speech indefinitely pending a full security review
Cancel the conference and evacuate everyone to London at once
Resign the leadership to protect the party from further attacks
Proceed with the conference as scheduled and deliver her speech that morning

evt-10-12-1984-provisional-irish-republi.butterflyEffect: Thatcher insisted the conference proceed on schedule and delivered her keynote speech that morning, an act of defiance that became one of the era's most enduring political images. Five people were killed and the Cabinet narrowly escaped, and the attack hardened British resolve against the IRA even as it later contributed to secret channels that eventually fed into the peace process.

evt-10-12-2002-2002-bali-bombings.scenario: In the hours after the nightclub bombings in Kuta, Bali, on 12 October 2002, you are among the Indonesian and Australian investigators sifting through the wreckage for any clue to who built the bombs.
evt-10-12-2002-2002-bali-bombings.prompt: What piece of forensic evidence helps investigators crack the case?

choices.text: A witness sketch of a suspect leaving the scene
Fingerprints lifted from an unexploded device
A chassis number traced from the bomb-carrying van's wreckage
CCTV footage from inside the nightclub

evt-10-12-2002-2002-bali-bombings.butterflyEffect: Investigators recovered a chassis number from the wreckage of the van used to carry the bomb, tracing it to Amrozi Nurhasyim, who had purchased the vehicle. His arrest exposed the wider Jemaah Islamiyah network, leading to the capture of Mukhlas and Imam Samudra, all later executed, and to deepened counter-terrorism cooperation between Indonesia and Australia.

evt-10-12-2005-shenzhou-6.scenario: You are Fei Junlong, strapped in beside Nie Haisheng aboard Shenzhou 6 at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center on 12 October 2005, about to fly China's most ambitious crewed mission yet.
evt-10-12-2005-shenzhou-6.prompt: What milestone does this flight achieve for China's crewed space program?

choices.text: China's first female astronaut in orbit
The first two-person, multi-day Chinese crewed spaceflight
The first Chinese docking with a space station
China's first spacewalk outside the capsule

evt-10-12-2005-shenzhou-6.butterflyEffect: Fei and Nie spent five days in orbit, far longer than Shenzhou 5's single-orbit flight, proving China could sustain a multi-person crew and manage in-flight operations over several days. The mission's success laid groundwork for Shenzhou 7's 2008 spacewalk and, eventually, China's Tiangong space station program.

evt-10-12-2012-european-union.scenario: It is October 2012 in Oslo. You sit on the Norwegian Nobel Committee while the eurozone is gripped by debt crises and street protests, and you must justify awarding this year's Peace Prize to the European Union.
evt-10-12-2012-european-union.prompt: What reasoning does the committee give for honoring the EU?

choices.text: Its historic role in advancing peace and reconciliation in Europe
Its handling of the eurozone debt crisis
The achievements of individual EU leaders
The success of the single currency, the euro

evt-10-12-2012-european-union.butterflyEffect: The committee cited the EU's six decades of advancing peace, reconciliation, democracy and human rights across a continent once torn by war. The choice drew criticism as tone-deaf given the ongoing crisis, fueling debate over the EU's purpose as Euroscepticism grew.

evt-10-12-2013-collapse-of-the-space-bui.scenario: It is the night of 12 October 2013 in Medellín. Tower 6 of the Space Building residential complex has just collapsed, killing residents inside, and cracks are visible in the neighboring towers.
evt-10-12-2013-collapse-of-the-space-bui.prompt: What should local authorities do about the rest of the complex immediately?

choices.text: Allow residents to stay but monitor the cracks
Wait for a full engineering report before acting
Reopen the building once the debris is cleared
Evacuate the remaining towers as a precaution

evt-10-12-2013-collapse-of-the-space-bui.butterflyEffect: Officials evacuated the remaining towers of the Space Building to prevent further loss of life, and the entire complex was later demolished. The disaster exposed construction defects and pushed Colombian authorities toward stricter enforcement of building codes.

evt-10-12-2017-unesco.scenario: It is 12 October 2017. The United States has just announced it will withdraw from UNESCO, citing anti-Israel bias and unpaid dues, and diplomats in Jerusalem are weighing how to respond.
evt-10-12-2017-unesco.prompt: What does Israel do in the hours after the US announcement?

choices.text: Condemns the US decision as premature
Stays neutral and takes no public position
Pledges to increase its own funding to UNESCO
Announces it will also withdraw from UNESCO

evt-10-12-2017-unesco.butterflyEffect: Israel announced its own withdrawal from UNESCO in solidarity with the US decision. Both countries formally left at the end of 2018, though the United States later rejoined the organization in 2023.

evt-10-12-2019-typhoon-hagibis.scenario: You are a Rugby World Cup organiser in Japan in October 2019. Typhoon Hagibis, one of the largest storms ever recorded, is bearing down on the country just as several pool-stage matches are due to kick off.
evt-10-12-2019-typhoon-hagibis.prompt: What do you decide to do with the endangered matches?

choices.text: Cancel the matches and record them as 0-0 draws
Postpone the matches to be replayed after the tournament
Proceed with the matches as scheduled regardless of the storm
Relocate the matches to stadiums untouched by the storm

evt-10-12-2019-typhoon-hagibis.butterflyEffect: Organisers cancelled the threatened fixtures outright and declared them 0-0 draws under tournament rules — the first cancellations in Rugby World Cup history. The decision affected qualification for Namibia, Canada, Italy and New Zealand, forcing the sport to confront how a single-elimination-style tournament handles a natural disaster mid-competition.

evt-10-12-2019-eliud-kipchoge.scenario: It's dawn in Vienna's Prater park on 12 October 2019. You're one of Eliud Kipchoge's rotating pacers, locked into a V-formation ahead of the laser-guided pace car, as he attempts to break the two-hour marathon barrier.
evt-10-12-2019-eliud-kipchoge.prompt: What does Kipchoge achieve minutes later, and how is it officially treated?

choices.text: He breaks the world record for the 5000 metres instead
He collapses just short of the two-hour mark
He runs under two hours, but it isn't eligible as an official world record
He sets a new official IAAF marathon world record

evt-10-12-2019-eliud-kipchoge.butterflyEffect: Kipchoge crossed the line in 1:59:40, the first human to run a marathon under two hours. Because the event used rotating pacers and wasn't an open competition, World Athletics did not recognize it as an official record, leaving his 2:01:39 from Berlin 2018 as the standing mark. The run reignited debate over shoe technology and pacing rules in elite distance running.

evt-10-12-2022-2022-bratislava-shooting.scenario: It is the morning after the shooting outside Tepláreň, Bratislava's best-known LGBTQ bar. You are a prosecutor with Slovakia's National Crime Agency deciding how to formally classify the attack that killed two people.
evt-10-12-2022-2022-bratislava-shooting.prompt: How do you classify the attack in the official case filing?

choices.text: Classify it solely as a hate-motivated double murder
Classify it as an unrelated act of random violence
Classify it as a private dispute between the victims and perpetrator
Classify it as domestic terrorism

evt-10-12-2022-2022-bratislava-shooting.butterflyEffect: Slovak authorities reclassified the shooting as an act of domestic terrorism rather than a hate-motivated murder, making it the first attack designated as terrorism in modern Slovak history. The killings of Juraj Vankulič and Matúš Horváth sparked national debate over hate-crime protections and the safety of LGBTQ Slovaks, pressuring lawmakers who had long resisted such legislation.

evt-10-13-1307-philip-iv-of-france.scenario: It is before dawn in Paris on 13 October 1307. Royal sergeants pound on the gate of your Templar commandery, presenting sealed warrants from King Philip IV accusing the entire order of heresy and secret vice.
evt-10-13-1307-philip-iv-of-france.prompt: As a Templar knight facing the royal agents at the door, what do you do?

choices.text: Flee at once into the countryside before dawn breaks
Produce a papal bull to claim immunity from French law
Submit peacefully to arrest, having no warning of the raid
Draw your sword and fight the royal sergeants

evt-10-13-1307-philip-iv-of-france.butterflyEffect: Most Templars across France were seized without resistance that morning, taken utterly by surprise. Under torture many confessed to fabricated charges; Pope Clement V, pressured by Philip, dissolved the order in 1312, and Grand Master Jacques de Molay was burned at the stake in 1314, ending the Templars and swelling the French crown's coffers.

evt-10-13-1710-queen-anne-s-war.scenario: You command the battered French garrison at Port Royal, Acadia, in October 1710. British colonial forces under Francis Nicholson have pounded your walls for weeks, and powder and food are nearly gone.
evt-10-13-1710-queen-anne-s-war.prompt: With the walls breached and no relief in sight, what does the garrison commander decide?

choices.text: Launch a desperate sortie to break the siege
Wait indefinitely for a French naval relief fleet
Negotiate terms of surrender with the besieging force
Fight on to the last man rather than surrender

evt-10-13-1710-queen-anne-s-war.butterflyEffect: The French and Wabanaki defenders surrendered on 13 October 1710, and Port Royal was renamed Annapolis Royal under British control. The Treaty of Utrecht in 1713 confirmed Britain's hold on Acadia, a shift that decades later set the stage for the forced expulsion of the Acadian population.

evt-10-13-1773-charles-messier.scenario: You are Charles Messier, scanning the night sky over Paris in October 1773, hunting for comets. Near the constellation Canes Venatici you spot a faint, fuzzy patch of light that does not move against the stars like a comet would.
evt-10-13-1773-charles-messier.prompt: What does Messier do with this newly spotted hazy object?

choices.text: He catalogues it as a fixed nebula, distinct from a comet
He announces the discovery of a new comet
He identifies it immediately as a new planet
He dismisses it as a flaw in his telescope lens

evt-10-13-1773-charles-messier.butterflyEffect: Messier recorded it as a nebula in his growing catalogue, meant to stop observers mistaking such fixed objects for comets. Centuries later this entry, M51, was recognized as the Whirlpool Galaxy, one of the first spiral galaxies whose structure astronomers could study, reshaping ideas about the scale of the universe.

evt-10-13-1908-suffragette.scenario: It is 13 October 1908 inside the House of Commons. Women are forbidden from speaking on the floor, but you, a suffragette, have just slipped past the attendants and burst into the chamber during a live debate.
evt-10-13-1908-suffragette.prompt: What do you do once you are standing on the floor of the House?

choices.text: Quietly take a seat in the public gallery instead
Shout 'Votes for Women' to interrupt the debate
Chain yourself to the nearest railing and wait to be arrested
Hand a written petition directly to the Speaker

evt-10-13-1908-suffragette.butterflyEffect: Margaret Travers Symons shouted her demand before startled MPs could remove her, becoming the first woman to speak within the chamber of the House of Commons, though not as an elected member. The stunt drew fresh press attention to the suffragettes' direct-action tactics and became one of many escalating protests that pushed the campaign for women's votes further into the public eye.

evt-10-13-1972-uruguayan-air-force-fligh.scenario: Your chartered flight has just crashed into the Andes at over 3,600 meters. Food is nearly gone, the cold is brutal, and rescue planes searching below cannot see your wreckage against the snow.
evt-10-13-1972-uruguayan-air-force-fligh.prompt: What difficult choice keeps survivors alive as the weeks stretch on?

choices.text: Melting snow into soup using seat cushions as fuel
Consuming the flesh of deceased passengers to survive
Rationing chocolate bars to last the full ten weeks
Sending a working radio distress signal from the wreck

evt-10-13-1972-uruguayan-air-force-fligh.butterflyEffect: With supplies exhausted and no rescue arriving, survivors made the wrenching decision to eat the flesh of those who had died in the crash. Ten weeks later two of them, Fernando Parrado and Roberto Canessa, trekked for ten days across the mountains to find help, leading rescuers back to save the remaining sixteen survivors.

evt-10-13-1994-the-troubles.scenario: You are a loyalist paramilitary commander in Belfast in October 1994. Two months earlier the IRA declared a ceasefire, and now your Combined Loyalist Military Command must decide how to respond at a press event held at Fernhill House.
evt-10-13-1994-the-troubles.prompt: What does the Combined Loyalist Military Command announce at Fernhill House?

choices.text: An announcement of a new political party contesting elections
A rejection of the IRA ceasefire and a call to escalate attacks
A reciprocal ceasefire ending loyalist paramilitary violence
A demand for the immediate withdrawal of British troops

evt-10-13-1994-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: The loyalist paramilitaries announced their own ceasefire, mirroring the IRA's move from August. With both republican and loyalist violence paused, the way was cleared for multi-party talks that eventually produced the Good Friday Agreement of 1998, formally ending the Troubles.

evt-10-13-2010-2010-copiapo-mining-accid.scenario: It is day 17 of your entrapment 700 meters underground in the collapsed San José mine. A narrow drill probe finally breaks through into your refuge, the first contact with the surface since the collapse.
evt-10-13-2010-2010-copiapo-mining-accid.prompt: What do the trapped miners send back up through the borehole?

choices.text: A list of demands for the mine's owners
A note confirming all 33 men are alive and well
Samples of rock to prove their location
A request to be left alone until they dig themselves out

evt-10-13-2010-2010-copiapo-mining-accid.butterflyEffect: The miners attached a note reading "Estamos bien en el refugio los 33" (We are well in the shelter, the 33 of us), proving for the first time that all had survived. The message triggered a massive rescue operation, Operation San Lorenzo, which drilled a rescue shaft and brought every miner up alive 69 days after the collapse.

evt-10-13-2011-king-of-bhutan.scenario: You stand among the crowds gathered at an ancient fortress-monastery in Bhutan in October 2011, watching the young Dragon King take a commoner, Jetsun Pema, as his queen in a ceremony steeped in centuries of tradition.
evt-10-13-2011-king-of-bhutan.prompt: Where does the king marry Jetsun Pema?

choices.text: Punakha Dzong
Paro Taktsang
Tashichho Dzong
Trongsa Dzong

evt-10-13-2011-king-of-bhutan.butterflyEffect: The wedding took place at Punakha Dzong, the fortress-monastery historically used for royal coronations. The marriage, broadcast to a nation embracing television and internet only a decade earlier, boosted global attention on Bhutan's monarchy and its "Gross National Happiness" philosophy, and Jetsun Pema went on to become the mother of the future king.

evt-10-13-2016-monarchy-of-thailand.scenario: You are a Thai government spokesperson on the night of 13 October 2016, informed that King Bhumibol Adulyadej has died after seventy years on the throne. The nation waits to learn who will lead it next.
evt-10-13-2016-monarchy-of-thailand.prompt: What official process follows to determine Thailand's new king?

choices.text: A regency council rules the country indefinitely
Princess Sirindhorn is named the new monarch
The Prime Minister becomes head of state
Crown Prince Vajiralongkorn is confirmed as the next king

evt-10-13-2016-monarchy-of-thailand.butterflyEffect: Crown Prince Vajiralongkorn was the designated heir but asked to delay formally ascending during the mourning period. He was officially proclaimed King Rama X on 1 December 2016, ending the reign of the world's then-longest-reigning monarch and reshaping the monarchy's relationship with Thai politics and the military.

evt-10-13-2016-maldives.scenario: You advise President Yameen's government in October 2016. The Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group is threatening suspension over the jailing of opposition leader Mohamed Nasheed and other democratic concerns.
evt-10-13-2016-maldives.prompt: What does the Maldivian government decide to do rather than face suspension?

choices.text: Ignore the warnings and make no formal response
Accept Commonwealth reform demands and remain a member
Appeal directly to the United Nations for mediation
Announce withdrawal from the Commonwealth entirely

evt-10-13-2016-maldives.butterflyEffect: On 13 October 2016 the Maldives announced its withdrawal from the Commonwealth, accusing the body of bias and "punitive" actions. It remained outside the organisation for nearly four years until Yameen lost power, and the new government under Ibrahim Solih applied to rejoin, restoring membership in 2020.

evt-10-13-2019-2019-chicago-marathon.scenario: You are pressed against the barricades at the finish line of the 2019 Chicago Marathon. Two exhausted runners come sprinting down the final stretch shoulder to shoulder, both desperate to lean for the tape first.
evt-10-13-2019-2019-chicago-marathon.prompt: What decides the outcome of this dramatic men's race finish?

choices.text: Officials declare a dead-heat tie between the two runners
One runner collapses from cramp just before the line
The leader trips and falls crossing the finish line
A photo finish separates the runners by a single second

evt-10-13-2019-2019-chicago-marathon.butterflyEffect: Lawrence Cherono won by a single second in one of the closest finishes in major marathon history, holding off his Ethiopian rival at the line. The same afternoon Brigid Kosgei shattered the women's world record, making the day a landmark for Kenyan distance running.

evt-10-14-1066-battle-of-hastings.scenario: It is the afternoon of 14 October 1066. You stand in the English shield wall atop Senlac Hill when the Norman cavalry below suddenly wheels around and flees downhill in apparent panic.
evt-10-14-1066-battle-of-hastings.prompt: What should you do as the Normans appear to flee?

choices.text: Send riders to negotiate a Norman surrender
Break ranks and chase the fleeing Normans
Fall back to regroup around Harold's banner
Hold the shield wall and let them retreat

evt-10-14-1066-battle-of-hastings.butterflyEffect: Many English housecarls broke ranks to chase what turned out to be a feigned retreat, a Norman tactic used more than once that day. The Norman cavalry turned back on the scattered pursuers, fatally thinning the shield wall and helping open the way to Harold's death and the Norman victory that began the Norman Conquest of England.

evt-10-14-1758-third-silesian-war.scenario: You are a Prussian officer camped at Hochkirch in October 1758, uneasy that Austrian forces under Field Marshal Daun are massing nearby while King Frederick delays reinforcing the camp's defenses.
evt-10-14-1758-third-silesian-war.prompt: What happens when Daun's Austrians strike at dawn?

choices.text: They achieve surprise and inflict a costly defeat on Frederick's army
Daun withdraws without engaging the Prussian camp
The two armies fight to an inconclusive stalemate
Frederick anticipates the attack and routs Daun's forces

evt-10-14-1758-third-silesian-war.butterflyEffect: The Austrians achieved near-total surprise, overrunning the Prussian camp and killing Field Marshal Keith among heavy losses. Yet Daun failed to press his advantage afterward, letting Frederick withdraw his battered army intact and continue the war for years more.

evt-10-14-1805-war-of-the-third-coalitio.scenario: You serve under Marshal Michel Ney on 14 October 1805 near Elchingen, ordered to storm a fortified abbey and bridge held by Austrian troops under General Riesch across the Danube.
evt-10-14-1805-war-of-the-third-coalitio.prompt: What must Ney's men do to break the Austrian position?

choices.text: Negotiate the Austrians' surrender before attacking
Flank the position via a river crossing further south
Wait for Napoleon's main army to arrive before attacking
Storm the bridge and abbey heights under fire

evt-10-14-1805-war-of-the-third-coalitio.butterflyEffect: Ney's soldiers stormed the bridge and abbey heights under heavy fire, shattering Austrian resistance and cutting off General Mack's escape routes. The victory helped seal the surrender of over 25,000 Austrian troops at Ulm days later, and Ney was later made Duke of Elchingen in honor of the assault.

evt-10-14-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: You are riding with Confederate Lieutenant General A.P. Hill on 14 October 1863 near Bristoe Station, Virginia, and you spot what looks like an exposed Union rearguard crossing an open field.
evt-10-14-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: What happens when Hill orders his lead division to charge without scouting the ground?

choices.text: His men charge into a hidden Union corps and are badly mauled
The surprise attack scatters the Union rearguard easily
Hill halts the advance and waits for artillery support
The Union troops retreat before any shots are fired

evt-10-14-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Hill attacked hastily without reconnoitering, and his men marched straight into a concealed Union II Corps hidden behind a railroad embankment. The Confederates suffered roughly 1,300 casualties in minutes, and Robert E. Lee later rebuked Hill sharply for the reckless assault.

evt-10-14-1888-louis-le-prince.scenario: You are visiting Oakwood Grange in Roundhay, Leeds, on 14 October 1888, watching inventor Louis Le Prince point his single-lens camera at family members strolling through the garden.
evt-10-14-1888-louis-le-prince.prompt: What does Le Prince capture that later grants him a claim to cinema history?

choices.text: The first known moving-picture footage recorded on film
The first motion picture with synchronized sound
The first color motion picture footage
The first film shown to a paying public audience

evt-10-14-1888-louis-le-prince.butterflyEffect: Roundhay Garden Scene is regarded by many historians as the earliest surviving motion picture footage. Le Prince mysteriously vanished in 1890 before he could patent or publicly demonstrate his camera, leaving Edison and the Lumière brothers to claim credit for popularizing cinema.

evt-10-14-1926-winnie-the-pooh-book.scenario: You are A. A. Milne in 1926, working with illustrator E. H. Shepard to turn your son Christopher Robin's nursery stories into a book for publication.
evt-10-14-1926-winnie-the-pooh-book.prompt: What choice shapes the characters that become world-famous?

choices.text: Invent wholly new creatures unrelated to any child's toys
Model the characters after zoo animals
Adapt characters from traditional English folklore
Base the characters directly on Christopher Robin's own stuffed toys

evt-10-14-1926-winnie-the-pooh-book.butterflyEffect: Shepard drew Pooh, Piglet, Eeyore and their friends directly from Christopher Robin Milne's real stuffed toys. The book's success led to a sequel, The House at Pooh Corner, and decades of adaptations that made Winnie-the-Pooh one of the most recognized franchises in children's literature, eventually acquired by Disney.

evt-10-14-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: You are a B-17 crewman on 14 October 1943, flying deep into Germany toward the ball-bearing factories of Schweinfurt. Your fighter escorts have already turned back, low on fuel, leaving your formation to face the Luftwaffe alone for hundreds of miles.
evt-10-14-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What happens to your bomber force on this mission?

choices.text: Destroy the factories with almost no losses thanks to surprise
Turn back before reaching Schweinfurt due to bad weather
Suffer catastrophic losses that force a halt to deep unescorted daylight raids
Receive full fighter escort all the way to the target and back

evt-10-14-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Sixty of the 291 attacking B-17s were shot down and many more badly damaged, a loss rate so severe that the USAAF called this raid 'Black Thursday' and suspended deep unescorted daylight raids into Germany. The disaster accelerated the push for long-range escort fighters, and once P-51 Mustangs arrived in early 1944, deep bombing campaigns resumed with far heavier fighter protection.

evt-10-14-1943-the-holocaust.scenario: You are a prisoner at Sobibor extermination camp on 14 October 1943. Word has quietly spread among the inmates that today, before the SS can select more of you for the gas chambers, a plan long prepared by Leon Feldhendler and Alexander Pechersky will be set in motion.
evt-10-14-1943-the-holocaust.prompt: What do you and your fellow prisoners do?

choices.text: Join the coordinated revolt, killing guards and rushing the perimeter fence
Sabotage the gas chambers alone without attempting to escape
Wait quietly in the barracks for the Red Army to liberate the camp
Petition the camp commandant for better treatment instead of revolting

evt-10-14-1943-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: Prisoners killed several SS officers and guards with hidden knives and axes, then stormed the fences under gunfire; roughly 300 of the camp's 600 inmates escaped into the surrounding forests, though most were later recaptured or killed. The uprising so alarmed Heinrich Himmler that he ordered Sobibor demolished within weeks, and the few survivors' testimony became crucial evidence of the camp's operation after the war.

evt-10-14-1949-smith-act-trials-of-commu.scenario: You sit on the jury in a New York City courtroom on 14 October 1949, after a nine-month trial of eleven leaders of the Communist Party USA accused of conspiring to advocate the violent overthrow of the government.
evt-10-14-1949-smith-act-trials-of-commu.prompt: What verdict do you and the jury reach?

choices.text: Convict them but recommend clemency for all
Deadlock, forcing the judge to declare a retrial
Acquit them on First Amendment free-speech grounds
Find all the defendants guilty of conspiracy under the Smith Act

evt-10-14-1949-smith-act-trials-of-commu.butterflyEffect: The jury convicted all eleven defendants under the Smith Act, and the conviction was upheld by the Supreme Court in Dennis v. United States (1951), enabling further prosecutions of Communist Party leaders through the 1950s. The Court later narrowed the Act's reach in Yates v. United States (1957), making it much harder to prosecute mere advocacy rather than concrete action.

evt-10-14-1956-b-r-ambedkar.scenario: You stand among hundreds of thousands gathered in Nagpur on 14 October 1956, watching B. R. Ambedkar prepare to renounce Hinduism before a vast crowd of his followers.
evt-10-14-1956-b-r-ambedkar.prompt: What does Ambedkar do next, and what does he ask the crowd to do?

choices.text: He calls for a nationwide boycott of upcoming elections
He asks followers to remain Hindu but reform caste customs
He formally converts to Buddhism and leads a mass conversion of followers
He announces his conversion to Sikhism instead

evt-10-14-1956-b-r-ambedkar.butterflyEffect: Ambedkar formally converted to Buddhism and led a mass conversion of hundreds of thousands of followers that same day, an event now marked as Dhammacakra Pravartan Din. It launched the modern Dalit Buddhist movement, reshaping Buddhism in India as a path to dignity and equality outside the caste system.

evt-10-14-1957-turia-river.scenario: It is after midnight on 14 October 1957, and after three days of relentless rain the Turia has burst its banks without warning, sweeping through the streets of Valencia around you.
evt-10-14-1957-turia-river.prompt: What should you do right now as the water rises?

choices.text: Wait for an official radio warning
Leave immediately for higher ground
Try to drive across the flooded bridges
Stay inside to protect your belongings

evt-10-14-1957-turia-river.butterflyEffect: The flood struck with little official warning and killed roughly 80 people, devastating central Valencia. In response, authorities launched the Plan Sur, diverting the Turia's course south of the city; the abandoned riverbed was later transformed into the Turia Gardens, now one of Europe's largest urban parks.

evt-10-14-1964-politburo-of-the-communis.scenario: You are a senior member of the Soviet Politburo meeting in Moscow on 14 October 1964, while Nikita Khrushchev remains away on holiday in the Crimea, unaware of what has been arranged in his absence.
evt-10-14-1964-politburo-of-the-communis.prompt: What does the Politburo vote to do about Khrushchev?

choices.text: Force him to share power equally with Brezhnev
Remove him from all his posts, citing old age and poor health
Exile him to a labor camp in Siberia
Put him on public trial for his policy failures

evt-10-14-1964-politburo-of-the-communis.butterflyEffect: The Politburo voted to strip Khrushchev of his posts, officially citing age and health, and replaced him with Leonid Brezhnev as First Secretary. Brezhnev's rise ushered in nearly two decades of political and economic stagnation, reversing many of Khrushchev's reforms and de-Stalinization efforts.

evt-10-14-1980-6th-congress-of-the-worke.scenario: You are a foreign delegate in Pyongyang's February 8 House of Culture in October 1980, watching Kim Il Sung's Workers' Party unveil its new leadership structure without foreign delegates being permitted to speak.
evt-10-14-1980-6th-congress-of-the-worke.prompt: What key succession move do delegates witness at this congress?

choices.text: The congress abolishes the office of General Secretary
Kim Jong Il is elevated to top party posts, confirming him as heir
Kim Il Sung names his younger brother as successor
Delegates elect a collective leadership excluding the Kim family

evt-10-14-1980-6th-congress-of-the-worke.butterflyEffect: Kim Jong Il was elevated to the Politburo Presidium, the Secretariat, and the Central Military Commission, publicly confirming him as heir apparent for the first time. This was the first hereditary succession staged within a communist state, setting the template later followed when Kim Jong Un succeeded his father in 2011.

evt-10-14-2012-felix-baumgartner.scenario: You stand at the open hatch of a capsule suspended nearly 39 kilometers above New Mexico, sealed inside a pressure suit, with nothing below you but curved earth and thin stratospheric air.
evt-10-14-2012-felix-baumgartner.prompt: As you step off the platform and fall, what happens?

choices.text: Your parachute deploys automatically at the moment you exit the capsule
You set an altitude record that stands unbroken to this day
You black out immediately and must be revived by ground crews
You break the sound barrier, becoming the first person to do so without engine power

evt-10-14-2012-felix-baumgartner.butterflyEffect: Felix Baumgartner became the first human to break the sound barrier without a vehicle, reaching roughly Mach 1.25 during his freefall before deploying his parachute over the New Mexico desert. His altitude record stood for two years until Alan Eustace surpassed it in 2014, but Baumgartner's speed and freefall-distance records remained his.

evt-10-14-2017-al-shabaab-militant-group.scenario: It is midday on 14 October 2017 near the crowded Zobe junction in Mogadishu when a truck packed with explosives detonates, becoming the deadliest single attack in Somalia's history.
evt-10-14-2017-al-shabaab-militant-group.prompt: What follows in the attack's immediate aftermath?

choices.text: The African Union withdraws its peacekeeping force
The government declares national mourning and appeals for aid
Al-Shabaab immediately claims responsibility
A ceasefire is declared with Al-Shabaab

evt-10-14-2017-al-shabaab-militant-group.butterflyEffect: Somalia's government declared three days of national mourning, and thousands of citizens lined up to donate blood while international aid poured in. Unusually, Al-Shabaab never claimed the attack, and the public outrage it provoked hardened resolve against the militant group in the months that followed.

evt-10-15-1529-ottoman-habsburg-wars.scenario: You are a defender inside Vienna's walls in mid-October 1529. Suleiman the Magnificent's massive army has besieged the city for weeks, but the assaults have stalled and the weather is turning bitterly cold.
evt-10-15-1529-ottoman-habsburg-wars.prompt: What should the outnumbered garrison do as the siege drags into autumn?

choices.text: Hold the walls and let the besiegers' supply lines and weather do the work
Sally out for a decisive open-field battle
Negotiate an immediate tribute payment to lift the siege
Surrender the city to spare the population

evt-10-15-1529-ottoman-habsburg-wars.butterflyEffect: The Ottomans, hampered by autumn rains, dwindling supplies, and failed breaches, abandoned the siege and withdrew. The failure marked the furthest reach of Ottoman expansion into Central Europe and set the Habsburg-Ottoman frontier for generations, with Vienna besieged again only in 1683.

evt-10-15-1815-napoleon.scenario: It is October 1815, and you are a British official deciding the fate of Napoleon after his final defeat at Waterloo. He escaped exile once before, from Elba, and returned to seize power for a hundred days.
evt-10-15-1815-napoleon.prompt: Where does Britain send Napoleon to prevent another escape and return to power?

choices.text: Return him to Elba under stricter guard
Imprison him in the Tower of London
Exile him to the remote, heavily guarded island of Saint Helena
Exile him to Corsica, his birthplace

evt-10-15-1815-napoleon.butterflyEffect: Napoleon was shipped to the remote South Atlantic island of Saint Helena, guarded closely by the Royal Navy, where he lived out his final years and died in 1821. His distance from Europe ended his political threat, but his memoirs and legend fed a Bonapartist myth his nephew later rode to power as Napoleon III.

evt-10-15-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: It is October 1864, and you command the small Union garrison at Glasgow, Missouri, as Confederate troops under Sterling Price's Missouri Expedition surround the town, seeking desperately needed supplies and weapons.
evt-10-15-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What does the outnumbered Union garrison at Glasgow do?

choices.text: Abandon the town and retreat toward Boonville before contact
Surrender after brief resistance to avoid needless casualties
Hold out for days awaiting reinforcements from St. Louis
Fight to the last man rather than yield the town

evt-10-15-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: After a sharp fight, the garrison surrendered, and Confederates seized badly needed arms and supplies. But Price's raid failed to rally lasting support in Missouri, and his army was decisively defeated later that month at the Battle of Westport, ending major Confederate operations in the state.

evt-10-15-1888-from-hell-letter.scenario: It is October 1888. You are George Lusk, head of the Whitechapel Vigilance Committee, when a small parcel arrives containing a piece of preserved human kidney and a crude letter boasting of murder and mutilation.
evt-10-15-1888-from-hell-letter.prompt: What does Lusk do with the grim package and letter?

choices.text: Publish its contents in the newspapers at once
Ignore it entirely as an obvious prank
Destroy it immediately, assuming it was a cruel hoax
Hand it over to the police for examination

evt-10-15-1888-from-hell-letter.butterflyEffect: Lusk turned the letter and kidney over to police and pathologists, who debated whether it matched wounds on victim Catherine Eddowes. Its authenticity was never proven, but the "From Hell" letter became one of the most infamous documents in the unsolved Jack the Ripper case, feeding decades of speculation about the killer's identity.

evt-10-15-1932-air-india.scenario: It is 15 October 1932. You are J.R.D. Tata, standing beside a single-engine de Havilland Puss Moth loaded with mail, about to launch India's first commercial airline service from Karachi to Bombay.
evt-10-15-1932-air-india.prompt: How do you prove to sceptics that commercial aviation can work in India?

choices.text: Pilot the inaugural mail flight yourself
Start with passenger routes instead of mail to attract more attention
Delay the launch until government subsidies are secured
Hire an experienced foreign pilot for the first flight

evt-10-15-1932-air-india.butterflyEffect: Tata piloted the flight himself, and Tata Airlines went on to become one of Asia's leading carriers. Nationalised in 1953 as Air India, it served as India's flag carrier for decades before returning to Tata Group ownership in 2022.

evt-10-15-1954-hurricane-hazel.scenario: It's the night of October 15, 1954, and the Humber River is rising fast through Toronto's west end. Forecasters had told residents Hazel would weaken harmlessly over land, so few evacuated before the floodwater swept through riverside neighborhoods.
evt-10-15-1954-hurricane-hazel.prompt: What lasting change did Toronto make after Hazel's flood devastated its river valleys?

choices.text: Canada immediately built a dedicated national hurricane forecasting agency
Toronto relocated its entire downtown core to higher ground
Governments expropriated flood-prone riverside land and turned it into permanent parkland
The city built high-rise concrete levees along every river in the region

evt-10-15-1954-hurricane-hazel.butterflyEffect: In Hazel's aftermath, Toronto's regional conservation authority expropriated hundreds of flood-prone properties along the Humber and other rivers, turning them into the permanent ravine parks that still line the city. The disaster also pushed Canada toward closer storm-warning cooperation with U.S. forecasters.

evt-10-15-1965-opposition-to-united-stat.scenario: You stand in a crowd at an anti-war rally in New York City on October 15, 1965. A young activist steps forward, having just received his new draft card, and organizers announce he intends to make a public statement against the war.
evt-10-15-1965-opposition-to-united-stat.prompt: What dramatic act of civil disobedience does he perform before the crowd?

choices.text: Announces he is fleeing to Canada that night
Chains himself to the induction center gates
Publicly burns his draft card
