Begins a hunger strike on the steps of City Hall

evt-10-15-1965-opposition-to-united-stat.butterflyEffect: David Miller burned his draft card, becoming the first person prosecuted under a new federal law that made destroying a draft card a felony. His arrest and conviction turned draft-card burning into a defining symbol of resistance, inspiring thousands of young men to follow suit as the anti-war movement grew.

evt-10-15-1979-carlos-humberto-romero.scenario: You are a junior Salvadoran army officer on October 15, 1979, as senior commanders move against President Carlos Humberto Romero, ending decades of military-dominated rule.
evt-10-15-1979-carlos-humberto-romero.prompt: What do the plotters install in place of Romero's government?

choices.text: A constitutional monarchy under exiled royalty
A restored Romero government with new advisers
A reform-minded civilian-military junta
A one-party socialist state under the guerrillas

evt-10-15-1979-carlos-humberto-romero.butterflyEffect: A civil-military junta took power promising land reform and an end to repression, but it failed to rein in death squads or satisfy leftist demands. Within months the country descended into the brutal Salvadoran Civil War, which lasted until 1992.

evt-10-15-1990-mikhail-gorbachev.scenario: It is October 1990. You are a Soviet citizen watching the news as Mikhail Gorbachev is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for reforms that have thawed the Cold War, even as shortages and unrest spread across the USSR itself.
evt-10-15-1990-mikhail-gorbachev.prompt: What did Gorbachev's reforms ultimately lead to within the Soviet Union?

choices.text: A renewed expansion of Soviet influence in Eastern Europe
The strengthening of the Warsaw Pact alliance
The dissolution of the Soviet Union within about a year
A return to strict Stalinist economic policy

evt-10-15-1990-mikhail-gorbachev.butterflyEffect: Gorbachev's policies of glasnost and perestroika, praised abroad, accelerated unrest at home. Within just over a year, the Soviet Union dissolved in December 1991, with Gorbachev resigning as its last leader and fifteen new independent states emerging.

evt-10-15-1996-criminal-assets-bureau.scenario: It is 1996 in Dublin. Journalist Veronica Guerin has just been murdered by a drug gang she was investigating, and public outrage demands the government hit organised crime where prosecution alone has failed.
evt-10-15-1996-criminal-assets-bureau.prompt: What new weapon should the state create to strike at crime bosses' wealth?

choices.text: A doubling of the national police force's budget
Mandatory minimum prison sentences for drug trafficking
New extradition treaties with neighbouring countries
A dedicated agency empowered to seize criminals' assets directly

evt-10-15-1996-criminal-assets-bureau.butterflyEffect: Ireland established the Criminal Assets Bureau, a multi-agency body of police, tax and welfare officials empowered under the Proceeds of Crime Act 1996 to seize criminally acquired assets even without a conviction. The model proved influential and was studied and partly copied by other European jurisdictions.

evt-10-15-1997-cassini-huygens.scenario: It's October 15, 1997, and you stand behind the barricades at Cape Canaveral as a Titan IV rocket ignites, carrying a probe fueled by nearly 33 kilograms of plutonium-238 toward Saturn. Anti-nuclear activists nearby have warned for months that a launch failure could scatter radioactive material across Florida.
evt-10-15-1997-cassini-huygens.prompt: What happens after the successful launch of Cassini–Huygens?

choices.text: The mission is aborted after protests force a last-minute launch delay
Cassini lands directly on Titan without ever entering Saturn orbit
The probe suffers a plutonium leak and is lost en route to Jupiter
Cassini reaches Saturn in 2004, becoming the first spacecraft to orbit the planet

evt-10-15-1997-cassini-huygens.butterflyEffect: Despite the protests, the launch succeeded with no radioactive release. Cassini spent seven years using Venus and Earth gravity-assist flybys before entering Saturn's orbit in 2004, and its Huygens lander touched down on Titan in 2005 — the most distant landing ever achieved by a human spacecraft.

evt-10-15-2003-shenzhou-5.scenario: It's October 15, 2003, and you are Yang Liwei, sealed inside the Shenzhou 5 capsule as a Long March 2F rocket carries you into orbit above China. No Chinese citizen has ever flown in space before, and the world is watching to see if the mission succeeds.
evt-10-15-2003-shenzhou-5.prompt: What did this flight establish for China's space program?

choices.text: China joined the International Space Station as a full partner nation
China became the third nation with independent human spaceflight capability
China became the first nation to land astronauts on the Moon
A multi-person Chinese crew orbited for a full week

evt-10-15-2003-shenzhou-5.butterflyEffect: Yang Liwei orbited Earth fourteen times in about twenty-one hours and returned safely, becoming a national hero. The success launched a rapid expansion of China's crewed program, leading to multi-astronaut missions, spacewalks, and eventually the construction of the Tiangong space station.

evt-10-15-2008-dow-jones-industrial-aver.scenario: It is October 15, 2008, on the trading floor. A week after Congress passed a $700 billion bailout, the Dow is plunging again as fresh fears of a deep global recession spook investors.
evt-10-15-2008-dow-jones-industrial-aver.prompt: What should traders have expected for the market in the months ahead?

choices.text: An immediate, sustained rebound in stock prices
Continued sharp swings and further steep declines into 2009
The Federal Reserve abandoning further intervention
A temporary closure of the New York Stock Exchange

evt-10-15-2008-dow-jones-industrial-aver.butterflyEffect: The volatility did not end that day. The Dow kept sliding through the winter, bottoming near 6,500 points in March 2009, the low point of the financial crisis, before a long recovery and bull market began.

evt-10-15-2011-15-october-2011-global-pr.scenario: It is 15 October 2011 and you stand among half a million people filling Madrid's Puerta del Sol, part of a coordinated day of demonstrations spreading across 82 countries under the banner 'United for Global Change.'
evt-10-15-2011-15-october-2011-global-pr.prompt: What grievance unites this global crowd of protesters?

choices.text: Opposition to a proposed increase in university tuition fees
Demands for Spain to leave the European Union
Calls for stricter immigration controls across Europe
Growing economic inequality and corporate influence over government

evt-10-15-2011-15-october-2011-global-pr.butterflyEffect: Roughly 950 cities took part, making it one of the largest coordinated protest days of the Occupy-era movement, born from Spain's Indignados and the earlier Arab Spring. The momentum helped sustain Occupy encampments worldwide for months and fed into new political movements, including Spain's Podemos party a few years later.

evt-10-15-2013-2013-bohol-earthquake.scenario: It is 8:12 a.m. on 15 October 2013. You are inside a centuries-old Spanish-era stone church in Bohol, Philippines, packed with morning worshippers, when the ground suddenly heaves beneath a magnitude 7.2 quake.
evt-10-15-2013-2013-bohol-earthquake.prompt: What should you tell the congregation to do right now?

choices.text: Have everyone kneel and pray beneath the altar for protection
Get everyone outside, away from the heavy stone walls and bell tower
Close the heavy wooden doors to keep the building from swaying open
Send people to shelter under the bell tower, the church's strongest point

evt-10-15-2013-2013-bohol-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The quake killed 222 people and severely damaged or collapsed several of Bohol and Cebu's oldest baroque churches, some standing since the 1600s. The disaster triggered a major national heritage-restoration campaign and renewed debate over retrofitting old masonry buildings against earthquakes.

evt-10-15-2016-montreal-protocol.scenario: It's October 2016 in Kigali, Rwanda, and you are among the negotiators debating whether to expand the decades-old Montreal Protocol beyond the ozone-depleting chemicals it originally targeted, to cover a class of widely used refrigerants that don't harm the ozone layer but trap enormous amounts of heat.
evt-10-15-2016-montreal-protocol.prompt: What do delegates agree to add to the Montreal Protocol's phase-down schedule at Kigali?

choices.text: Leaded additives in gasoline
Carbon dioxide emissions from coal-fired power plants
Methane emissions from livestock and agriculture
Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), potent greenhouse gases used as refrigerants

evt-10-15-2016-montreal-protocol.butterflyEffect: The Kigali Amendment committed nations to cut production and use of hydrofluorocarbons over the following decades. Because HFCs are extremely potent greenhouse gases, the deal is projected to avoid up to 0.5°C of global warming by 2100, turning the ozone treaty into a major climate tool as well.

evt-10-15-2018-kidnapping-of-jayme-closs.scenario: It is October 15, 2018, in Barron, Wisconsin. Investigators comb the countryside for 13-year-old Jayme Closs, missing since her parents were found dead in their home hours earlier.
evt-10-15-2018-kidnapping-of-jayme-closs.prompt: What ultimately happened to Jayme Closs after her disappearance?

choices.text: She was released by her captor after a ransom was paid
She was never located and the case remains unsolved
She was found by a police raid within days
She escaped captivity months later and got help from a stranger

evt-10-15-2018-kidnapping-of-jayme-closs.butterflyEffect: Jayme was held captive for 88 days at a remote cabin before escaping on January 10, 2019, and flagging down a woman walking her dog, who called police. Her escape led directly to the arrest of Jake Thomas Patterson and closed one of the most closely followed missing-child cases of the decade.

evt-10-16-1384-jadwiga-of-poland.scenario: You stand in Wawel Cathedral on 16 October 1384 as the young heiress Jadwiga is presented for coronation. Polish nobles debate exactly what title should be placed upon her to define her authority.
evt-10-16-1384-jadwiga-of-poland.prompt: Why do the nobles crown her as 'King' rather than 'Queen'?

choices.text: Because she was betrothed to a foreign king and took his title
Because Polish law forbade any female from ruling under any title
To make clear she held full sovereign royal authority, not consort status
To honor a promise made to her late father, Louis of Hungary

evt-10-16-1384-jadwiga-of-poland.butterflyEffect: The title emphasized that Jadwiga held full sovereign royal power in her own right, not merely the status of a queen consort. Two years later she married Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania, forging the Polish-Lithuanian union that reshaped Central European politics for centuries and brought Lithuania into Christendom.

evt-10-16-1834-palace-of-westminster.scenario: It is 16 October 1834, and you are a workman for the Office of Woods and Forests. Your job is to burn two cartloads of centuries-old wooden tally sticks in the House of Lords' underfloor stoves before the building closes for the day.
evt-10-16-1834-palace-of-westminster.prompt: How should you dispose of the tally sticks to avoid disaster?

choices.text: Feed the sticks in slowly, a few at a time, letting each batch burn down fully
Sell the old tallies to a local timber merchant instead of burning them
Load both furnaces to capacity at once to finish the job quickly
Stack the surplus sticks in the House of Commons for later burning

evt-10-16-1834-palace-of-westminster.butterflyEffect: Workers instead crammed the furnaces with far more sticks than intended, overheating the flues until wood panelling caught fire that night, destroying most of the medieval palace. The rebuilding, led by Charles Barry and Augustus Pugin, produced the Gothic Revival Houses of Parliament and Elizabeth Tower standing today.

evt-10-16-1875-brigham-young-university.scenario: It is 1875 in Provo, Utah. Church leader Brigham Young has asked your community to fund and staff a new academy for Latter-day Saint youth, to be built on principles combining secular learning with religious education.
evt-10-16-1875-brigham-young-university.prompt: What is the new institution originally named when it opens?

choices.text: Deseret College
Brigham Young Academy
Utah Territorial Institute
Provo University

evt-10-16-1875-brigham-young-university.butterflyEffect: It opened as Brigham Young Academy, only taking the name Brigham Young University in 1903. It grew from a small local school into the flagship university of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, now one of the largest private universities in the United States.

evt-10-16-1905-british-raj.scenario: You are Lord Curzon, Viceroy of India, weighing whether to proceed on 16 October 1905 with a plan to split the vast Bengal Presidency, despite fierce objections that the new boundary would divide communities along religious lines.
evt-10-16-1905-british-raj.prompt: What does Curzon's administration actually do with Bengal on this date?

choices.text: Merge Bengal and Assam into one unified province to simplify rule
Partition Bengal, separating a Muslim-majority east from a Hindu-majority west
Grant Bengal expanded self-governance instead of administrative division
Postpone any reorganization indefinitely due to local protests

evt-10-16-1905-british-raj.butterflyEffect: The partition created a Muslim-majority Eastern Bengal and Assam alongside a Hindu-majority western Bengal, provoking the mass Swadeshi movement of boycotts and protests against British goods. Public outrage forced Britain to reverse the partition in 1911, but the episode hardened communal political divisions that would echo decades later in the 1947 Partition of India.

evt-10-16-1934-long-march.scenario: You are a Red Army soldier at the Jiangxi Soviet in October 1934. Chiang Kai-shek's Fifth Encirclement Campaign has crushed the base's defenses, and your commanders must choose how to save the army.
evt-10-16-1934-long-march.prompt: What do the Communist leaders decide to do with the surrounded Red Army?

choices.text: Fortify Jiangxi and fight to the last man
Surrender the base to negotiate favorable terms
Break out and retreat westward through Kuomintang lines
Flee north to seek asylum in the Soviet Union

evt-10-16-1934-long-march.butterflyEffect: The Red Army broke out and began the Long March, a grueling year-long retreat of some 10,000 kilometers to Yan'an. Along the way the Zunyi Conference established Mao Zedong as the Communist Party's de facto leader, setting the course for his eventual victory in the Chinese Civil War.

evt-10-16-1943-the-holocaust.scenario: It is before dawn on 16 October 1943 in Rome's old Jewish quarter. German soldiers move house to house rounding up families, and you must decide where to seek refuge in the chaotic hours that follow.
evt-10-16-1943-the-holocaust.prompt: Where did many Roman Jews find shelter during and after this raid?

choices.text: Italian army barracks sympathetic to resistance fighters
Local Fascist Party headquarters, which offered protection papers
Convents, monasteries, and Vatican-affiliated buildings offering shelter
The ancient Coliseum, believed to be exempt from German searches

evt-10-16-1943-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: Vatican-owned buildings, convents, and monasteries across Rome sheltered thousands of Jews in the following months, even as over a thousand people seized that morning were deported to Auschwitz. This uneven pattern of local rescue amid catastrophic loss became a defining, still-debated feature of wartime Rome's history.

evt-10-16-1962-cuban-missile-crisis.scenario: You are an adviser in President Kennedy's EXCOMM meeting on October 16, 1962, just after U-2 photographs confirmed Soviet nuclear missile sites under construction in Cuba. Some generals are pushing for immediate air strikes or invasion.
evt-10-16-1962-cuban-missile-crisis.prompt: What initial response does Kennedy ultimately choose instead of a strike or invasion?

choices.text: A full-scale invasion of Cuba
An ultimatum threatening nuclear retaliation on Moscow
A naval blockade, or 'quarantine,' of Cuba
An immediate airstrike on the missile sites

evt-10-16-1962-cuban-missile-crisis.butterflyEffect: Kennedy imposed a naval quarantine of Cuba, buying time for tense negotiations with Khrushchev. The standoff ended with the Soviets withdrawing their missiles in exchange for a US pledge not to invade Cuba and the secret removal of American Jupiter missiles from Turkey, narrowly averting nuclear war.

evt-10-16-1964-project-596.scenario: It is 16 October 1964 at the Lop Nur test site in Xinjiang. You are a physicist on China's nuclear weapons team, watching final checks on an implosion device built from uranium enriched at Lanzhou.
evt-10-16-1964-project-596.prompt: What does the successful detonation of Project 596 achieve for China?

choices.text: The Soviet Union publicly congratulates China on the test
The test fails and sets the program back a decade
China joins the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty immediately
China becomes the world's fifth nuclear power

evt-10-16-1964-project-596.butterflyEffect: The test made China the world's fifth nuclear power, after the US, USSR, UK, and France. It reshaped Cold War geopolitics, hardened the Sino-Soviet split, and strengthened China's claim to a permanent UN Security Council seat with veto power.

evt-10-16-1975-balibo-five.scenario: It is 16 October 1975 in the border town of Balibo, East Timor. You are one of five foreign television journalists who have painted a large 'TV' on the wall of the house you are sheltering in, hoping it will mark you as press rather than combatants as Indonesian forces close in.
evt-10-16-1975-balibo-five.prompt: What happens when the Indonesian special forces reach the house?

choices.text: The sign is respected and troops withdraw without entering
They are allowed to keep filming and broadcast the assault live
They are captured, questioned, and released unharmed to Dili
They are killed despite identifying themselves as journalists

evt-10-16-1975-balibo-five.butterflyEffect: Despite the marking, the five journalists were killed, an act an Australian coroner ruled in 2007 was deliberate rather than crossfire as Indonesia claimed. The killings became a lasting point of tension between Australia and Indonesia, prompting decades of advocacy, a war crimes investigation that closed without charges in 2014, and the founding of the Balibo House Trust in their memory.

evt-10-16-1978-october-1978-conclave.scenario: You are a cardinal elector sealed inside the Sistine Chapel in mid-October 1978. The leading Italian candidates have deadlocked through several ballots, and attention turns to a relatively unknown archbishop from behind the Iron Curtain.
evt-10-16-1978-october-1978-conclave.prompt: Whom does the conclave elect on the eighth ballot to break the deadlock?

choices.text: Giuseppe Siri of Genoa
Sebastiano Baggio of the Curia
Giovanni Benelli of Florence
Karol Wojtyła of Kraków

evt-10-16-1978-october-1978-conclave.butterflyEffect: The cardinals chose Karol Wojtyła of Kraków, who became Pope John Paul II—the first non-Italian pope in 455 years. His papacy would galvanize opposition to communism, especially through his 1979 visit to Poland, which helped inspire the Solidarity movement.

evt-10-16-1991-luby-s-shooting.scenario: You survive the attack at the Killeen cafeteria, having left your handgun locked in your car because Texas law at the time barred concealed weapons in restaurants. In the years afterward, you decide to speak publicly about that choice.
evt-10-16-1991-luby-s-shooting.prompt: What change did survivors like Suzanna Hupp go on to campaign for in Texas?

choices.text: Mandatory 30-day waiting periods for all gun purchases
Legalizing concealed handgun carry for licensed citizens
A statewide ban on semi-automatic rifles
A federal firearms registry

evt-10-16-1991-luby-s-shooting.butterflyEffect: Hupp, who lost both parents in the massacre, became a prominent advocate for concealed carry rights, testifying that the law had left her unable to defend her family. Texas passed a concealed handgun licensing law in 1995, and the case became a touchstone in national gun-rights debates for decades afterward.

evt-10-16-1995-million-man-march.scenario: You are one of hundreds of thousands of Black men gathering on the National Mall on 16 October 1995, drawn by Louis Farrakhan's call for a day centered on atonement, unity, and responsibility rather than protest alone.
evt-10-16-1995-million-man-march.prompt: What was the central call urged upon attendees at the march?

choices.text: Demand Congress pass immediate reparations legislation that day
Launch an indefinite boycott of all American workplaces
Organize armed community self-defense units nationwide
Register to vote and commit to personal and community responsibility

evt-10-16-1995-million-man-march.butterflyEffect: The march's emphasis on personal responsibility and civic engagement helped drive a measurable surge in Black voter registration afterward and energized local community and mentoring organizations. It also reignited national debate over Farrakhan's leadership, a tension that shaped how the march's legacy is remembered in civil rights history.

evt-10-16-1995-skye-bridge.scenario: You live on the Isle of Skye as the new bridge opens on 16 October 1995, replacing the free ferry crossing. Almost immediately, you learn the toll is among the highest per-mile charges in Europe.
evt-10-16-1995-skye-bridge.prompt: How do many islanders respond to the new bridge tolls in the years that follow?

choices.text: Sued the construction firm for negligence
Petitioned to reinstate the old ferry as a free alternative
Organized a mass toll non-payment campaign
Boycotted crossing the bridge altogether

evt-10-16-1995-skye-bridge.butterflyEffect: Residents formed the campaign group SKAT (Skye and Kyle Against Tolls) and staged mass toll non-payment protests, with hundreds facing prosecution. The pressure eventually led the Scottish Government to buy out the bridge's private operator and abolish the tolls entirely in December 2004.

evt-10-16-1998-augusto-pinochet.scenario: It is 16 October 1998, and you are a British police officer in London. A Spanish judge has issued a warrant for the elderly former dictator recovering in a private clinic nearby, citing crimes committed against his own citizens years earlier.
evt-10-16-1998-augusto-pinochet.prompt: What does British authority do with the extradition warrant against Pinochet?

choices.text: Quietly allow him to fly home before the warrant is served
Refuse to act, citing diplomatic immunity
Deport him immediately to Chile without a hearing
Arrest him under the Spanish extradition request

evt-10-16-1998-augusto-pinochet.butterflyEffect: Pinochet was arrested and held under house arrest in Britain for over a year while courts weighed extradition. The House of Lords ruled he could face trial for post-1988 torture, but he was eventually deemed medically unfit and returned to Chile in 2000, where prosecutions continued. The case became a landmark for universal jurisdiction over human rights abuses.

evt-10-16-2013-lao-airlines-flight-301.scenario: You are the pilot of Flight 301, approaching Pakse on 16 October 2013 as a tropical storm batters southern Laos, cutting visibility over the Mekong River just as you begin your descent.
evt-10-16-2013-lao-airlines-flight-301.prompt: What ultimately brings down the aircraft during this stormy approach?

choices.text: Severe storm conditions during the landing approach
A mechanical failure in the landing gear before takeoff
A mid-air collision with another aircraft
A fire that broke out in the cargo hold

evt-10-16-2013-lao-airlines-flight-301.butterflyEffect: The ATR 72-600 crashed into the Mekong River near Pakse while attempting to land in severe weather, killing all 49 aboard. It remains Laos's deadliest aviation disaster and the first fatal crash of the ATR 72-600 variant, prompting scrutiny of approach procedures in poor tropical weather.

evt-10-16-2017-hurricane-ophelia-2017.scenario: It is 16 October 1917... no, 2017, and you step outside in Ireland as Storm Ophelia approaches. The sun overhead has turned an eerie deep red, and an orange haze hangs over the sky, unsettling residents who have never seen anything like it.
evt-10-16-2017-hurricane-ophelia-2017.prompt: What actually caused the strange red sky as Ophelia arrived?

choices.text: Saharan dust and wildfire smoke carried north by the storm's winds
Industrial pollution trapped beneath the storm system
Volcanic ash drifting from an Icelandic eruption
A rare solar eclipse coinciding with the storm

evt-10-16-2017-hurricane-ophelia-2017.butterflyEffect: Ophelia's southerly winds had swept up Saharan dust and smoke from severe wildfires burning in Portugal and Spain, scattering sunlight into deep red and orange hues. The phenomenon, combined with the storm's destructive winds and power outages, made 16 October 2017 one of the most talked-about days in recent Irish and British weather history.

evt-10-17-1346-hundred-years-war.scenario: It is 17 October 1346 near Durham, England. You ride with King David II of Scotland, who has invaded northern England to honor the Auld Alliance while Edward III campaigns in France after Crécy.
evt-10-17-1346-hundred-years-war.prompt: What happens to King David II at the Battle of Neville's Cross?

choices.text: He is killed in the fighting
He retreats safely back across the border
He wins a decisive victory and sacks Durham
He is captured and held prisoner in England

evt-10-17-1346-hundred-years-war.butterflyEffect: David II was wounded and captured by English forces, then held prisoner in England for eleven years until a huge ransom secured his release. The defeat crippled Scotland's ability to support France and weakened the Auld Alliance for years afterward.

evt-10-17-1604-johannes-kepler.scenario: It is October 1604 in Prague. You are Johannes Kepler, imperial mathematician, and word reaches you of an extraordinarily bright new star blazing in the constellation Ophiuchus, unlike anything predicted by the old astronomy.
evt-10-17-1604-johannes-kepler.prompt: What does Kepler do with this new star?

choices.text: Dismisses it as an atmospheric illusion
Concludes it confirms Aristotle's cosmology
Attributes it to a passing comet and moves on
Observes and documents it systematically, challenging the idea of unchanging heavens

evt-10-17-1604-johannes-kepler.butterflyEffect: Kepler tracked the star for over a year and published his findings in De Stella Nova, providing strong evidence against the Aristotelian belief that the heavens beyond the Moon were fixed and unchanging. It remains the last supernova confirmed to have been observed with the naked eye in the Milky Way.

evt-10-17-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 17 October 1777 near Saratoga, New York. You serve under British General John Burgoyne, whose army is surrounded, starving, and cut off from reinforcement after weeks of fighting the Continental Army.

choices.text: Holds out and waits for General Howe to relieve him
Breaks through the American lines and retreats to Canada
Surrenders his army to General Gates
Negotiates a truce and withdraws his forces to New York

evt-10-17-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Burgoyne surrendered his entire army to American General Horatio Gates, the first surrender of a British army in the war. The victory convinced France to formally ally with the United States, bringing crucial military and naval support that helped secure eventual independence.

evt-10-17-1931-al-capone.scenario: It is 1931 in Chicago, and federal agents have spent years chasing Al Capone for bootlegging and violence with no convictions sticking. You are one of the IRS investigators building the case that finally puts him away.
evt-10-17-1931-al-capone.prompt: What charge finally sends Al Capone to prison?

choices.text: Murder of rival gangsters
Income-tax evasion
Racketeering and extortion
Illegal liquor trafficking

evt-10-17-1931-al-capone.butterflyEffect: Capone was convicted on income-tax evasion, not murder or bootlegging, and sentenced to 11 years. The case proved federal tax law could jail mob bosses that violent-crime charges couldn't touch, a tactic later reused against organized crime nationwide.

evt-10-17-1952-indonesian-army.scenario: It is 17 October 1952, and army officers loyal to General Nasution have massed tanks and troops around the Merdeka Palace in Jakarta, demanding President Sukarno dissolve the fractious national parliament.
evt-10-17-1952-indonesian-army.prompt: What does Sukarno do when the crowd calls for him to act?

choices.text: He orders the immediate arrest of the officers
He flees the palace in secret
He dissolves parliament as demanded
He appears before the crowd and refuses their demand

evt-10-17-1952-indonesian-army.butterflyEffect: Sukarno walked out onto the palace steps, addressed the assembled troops directly, and refused to dissolve parliament, defusing the standoff without bloodshed. The failed pressure weakened the army's political leverage for the moment, but the underlying tension between military and civilian authority persisted into the later Guided Democracy era.

evt-10-17-1964-robert-menzies.scenario: It's 17 October 1964, and Canberra's dry Molonglo Valley is finally filling with water. Prime Minister Robert Menzies stands before the crowd at the ceremony marking the birth of the national capital's new landmark lake.
evt-10-17-1964-robert-menzies.prompt: Who does the new lake's name honour?

choices.text: Walter Burley Griffin, the American-born architect who designed Canberra
King George V, patron of the federal capital project
The Molonglo River that once ran through the valley
Robert Menzies himself, marking his long tenure as PM

evt-10-17-1964-robert-menzies.butterflyEffect: Menzies opened the floodgates that filled Lake Burley Griffin, finally realising the 1912 vision of architect Walter Burley Griffin for Canberra's design. The lake became the ceremonial and geographic heart of the capital, later framing Parliament House and the national institutions along its shores.

evt-10-17-1989-erich-honecker.scenario: It is 17 October 1989, and East Germany's Politburo has gathered behind closed doors. Mass protests are sweeping Leipzig and Berlin, and Erich Honecker's grip on power is the only item on the agenda.

choices.text: Reaffirm Honecker's leadership and denounce the protests as Western provocation
Postpone any decision until after planned November elections
Vote to remove Honecker and install Egon Krenz as General Secretary
Ask the Soviet Union to send troops to restore order

evt-10-17-1989-erich-honecker.butterflyEffect: Krenz took over but could not contain the unrest he inherited; within weeks the Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989, and Krenz himself resigned in December as the entire SED regime collapsed.

evt-10-17-1992-baton-rouge-louisiana.scenario: It is Halloween night, 1992, in a Baton Rouge suburb. You are 16-year-old Japanese exchange student Yoshihiro Hattori, dressed for a costume party, and you and a friend have knocked at the wrong address by mistake.
evt-10-17-1992-baton-rouge-louisiana.prompt: What follows when homeowner Rodney Peairs answers the door with a revolver?

choices.text: Peairs shoots and kills Hattori, who kept approaching despite being told to freeze
Hattori's host family intervenes and the visit ends without incident
Hattori immediately raises his hands and is let inside to explain the mix-up
Police arrive first and defuse the confrontation peacefully

evt-10-17-1992-baton-rouge-louisiana.butterflyEffect: Peairs shot and killed Hattori, then stood trial for manslaughter but was acquitted after invoking Louisiana's self-defense law. The case caused a diplomatic uproar between Japan and the United States and became a lasting touchstone in debates over American gun culture and armed self-defense against unarmed strangers.

evt-10-17-2001-rehavam-ze-evi.scenario: It is the morning of 17 October 2001 in Jerusalem, and word reaches the Israeli cabinet that Tourism Minister Rehavam Ze'evi has been shot dead in his hotel by PFLP gunmen in apparent retaliation for the killing of the group's leader.
evt-10-17-2001-rehavam-ze-evi.prompt: What does Israel do militarily in the days that follow?

choices.text: They withdraw all troops from the West Bank
They take no military action in response
They sign an immediate ceasefire with the PFLP
They reoccupy West Bank towns held by the Palestinian Authority

evt-10-17-2001-rehavam-ze-evi.butterflyEffect: Israeli forces reoccupied several West Bank towns previously under Palestinian Authority control, including Bethlehem and Jenin, marking a sharp escalation of the Second Intifada. The assassination and its aftermath further eroded the Oslo-era arrangements between Israel and the Palestinian Authority.

evt-10-17-2017-syrian-civil-war.scenario: It is 17 October 2017 in Raqqa, Syria. You advance with the Syrian Democratic Forces through the last blocks held by the Islamic State, the city that has served as the group's de facto capital.
evt-10-17-2017-syrian-civil-war.prompt: What does the fall of Raqqa mean for the Islamic State?

choices.text: The Syrian government reclaims full control of Raqqa
ISIS retakes the city within weeks
ISIS loses its de facto capital, hastening the caliphate's collapse
Turkey annexes Raqqa as part of a buffer zone

evt-10-17-2017-syrian-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Raqqa's capture stripped ISIS of its de facto capital and marked a decisive collapse of its territorial "caliphate," following the earlier loss of Mosul. The group would lose its last territorial holdings by 2019, though insurgent attacks and SDF-Turkey tensions over the city's control continued for years.

evt-10-17-2018-cannabis-act-canada.scenario: It is 17 October 2018, and you are opening the doors of a licensed cannabis shop in Canada for the first time as the Cannabis Act takes effect nationwide, ending decades of prohibition.
evt-10-17-2018-cannabis-act-canada.prompt: What historic distinction does Canada earn today?

choices.text: The first country ever to legalize cannabis
The second nation, after Uruguay, to legalize recreational cannabis nationwide
The first country to legalize only medical marijuana
The first G7 country to decriminalize all drugs

evt-10-17-2018-cannabis-act-canada.butterflyEffect: Canada became the second country in the world, after Uruguay, to legalize recreational cannabis nationwide. The move built a regulated legal industry and became a reference point for other jurisdictions debating legalization in the years that followed.

evt-10-17-2018-kerch-polytechnic-college.scenario: You are a Crimean lawmaker in the days after a student's bomb and gun attack tore through Kerch Polytechnic College, killing staff and students. Legislators in Moscow are debating how to respond.
evt-10-17-2018-kerch-polytechnic-college.prompt: What legislative change follows the attack?

choices.text: Russia raises the minimum legal age to buy firearms from 18 to 21
Crimea is placed under a new international peacekeeping mandate
Russia bans all private ownership of firearms nationwide
Metal detectors are installed in every Russian school within a week

evt-10-17-2018-kerch-polytechnic-college.butterflyEffect: In the attack's wake, Russia's State Duma tightened federal gun laws, raising the minimum purchase age for firearms to 21 and lengthening waiting periods. The massacre also reignited debate across Russia and Ukraine over school security, echoing the earlier Beslan tragedy.

evt-10-17-2019-culiacan.scenario: It's 17 October 2019 in Culiacán. Mexican security forces have just captured Ovidio Guzmán, son of jailed drug lord El Chapo, when Sinaloa Cartel gunmen flood the streets, torching vehicles and surrounding army barracks.
evt-10-17-2019-culiacan.prompt: What does President López Obrador's government decide to do?

choices.text: Impose martial law across Sinaloa state
Negotiate a prisoner swap for kidnapped soldiers
Deploy the army to storm cartel strongholds and retake the city
Release Ovidio Guzmán to stop the violence engulfing the city

evt-10-17-2019-culiacan.butterflyEffect: Officials freed Guzmán within hours, and the retreat—dubbed the 'Culiacanazo'—became a stark symbol of cartel power outmatching the state. It embarrassed López Obrador's 'hugs not bullets' security strategy; Guzmán was recaptured in 2023 and extradited to the United States.

evt-10-18-1081-byzantine-norman-wars.scenario: It is 18 October 1081, and you stand with Emperor Alexios I Komnenos's army outside the walls of Dyrrhachium, facing Robert Guiscard's Norman invaders in a fierce pitched battle on the coast.
evt-10-18-1081-byzantine-norman-wars.prompt: What follows this clash between the Byzantine army and the Norman invaders?

choices.text: The Normans rout the Byzantine army, destroying much of the elite Varangian Guard
Both sides negotiate a truce and withdraw without fighting
The Byzantines break the siege and drive the Normans back to Italy
The Norman garrison surrenders the city without a fight

evt-10-18-1081-byzantine-norman-wars.butterflyEffect: The Normans shattered the Byzantine army, cutting down much of the elite Varangian Guard, and went on to capture Dyrrhachium by early 1082, opening the road toward the Byzantine heartland. Robert Guiscard's death from illness in 1085 ended the immediate threat, but the campaign exposed Byzantine weakness that later Norman crusaders exploited when carving out the Principality of Antioch.

evt-10-18-1356-1356-basel-earthquake.scenario: It is the evening of 18 October 1356 in Basel. The ground has just convulsed violently, toppling towers and setting hearths ablaze across the wrecked city, and aftershocks keep rolling through.
evt-10-18-1356-1356-basel-earthquake.prompt: What should you do to survive the night?

choices.text: Take shelter inside the stone cathedral
Flee to open ground away from walls and buildings
Climb the city walls to watch for further tremors
Return inside to rescue valuables from your house

evt-10-18-1356-1356-basel-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Most survivors fled to open fields outside the walls as fires, sparked by overturned lamps and ovens in the ruins, burned for days. The quake, still the most powerful known to have struck Central Europe, destroyed Basel's castles and city walls and became a foundational case study for later European seismic-hazard research.

evt-10-18-1748-war-of-the-austrian-succe.scenario: You are a British negotiator at the congress in Aix-la-Chapelle in October 1748, tasked with ending eight years of inconclusive war among Europe's great powers. New England colonists are furious that their hard-won prize, the fortress of Louisbourg, is on the table.
evt-10-18-1748-war-of-the-austrian-succe.prompt: What should you agree to in order to secure the peace?

choices.text: Refuse any territorial exchanges and continue the war
Demand France cede Canada outright
Insist Prussia surrender Silesia back to Austria
Return Louisbourg to France in exchange for Madras

evt-10-18-1748-war-of-the-austrian-succe.butterflyEffect: Britain returned Louisbourg to France in exchange for France returning Madras, while the treaty largely confirmed Prussia's seizure of Silesia and recognized Maria Theresa's succession. The Louisbourg handover embittered New England colonists, and Prussia's unresolved rivalry with Austria over Silesia helped set the stage for the Seven Years' War.

evt-10-18-1887-johannes-brahms.scenario: It is 18 October 1887 in Cologne's Gürzenich Hall. You watch Johannes Brahms take the podium to conduct the premiere of his new Double Concerto, a work written in part to mend his broken friendship with violinist Joseph Joachim.
evt-10-18-1887-johannes-brahms.prompt: What role does this concerto play in Brahms and Joachim's estranged friendship?

choices.text: It further alienates the two men and they never speak again
It becomes the peace offering that reconciles Brahms and Joachim after years of silence
It is quietly withdrawn and never publicly performed
Joachim refuses to perform it and it goes unheard for years

evt-10-18-1887-johannes-brahms.butterflyEffect: The Double Concerto succeeded as a genuine peace offering: Joachim, who had cut off contact after a bitter dispute over his divorce, agreed to premiere the piece alongside cellist Robert Hausmann, and the two men's friendship was restored. It proved to be Brahms's last orchestral composition, closing his output with an act of reconciliation rather than rupture.

evt-10-18-1954-regency-tr-1.scenario: It is late 1954 and you are browsing a department store display of the new Regency TR-1, a radio no bigger than a deck of cards, priced at a steep $49.95. A large tabletop tube radio nearby costs less and sounds noticeably clearer.
evt-10-18-1954-regency-tr-1.prompt: Why do early buyers choose the TR-1 over the cheaper, better-sounding tube radio?

choices.text: Its compact, battery-powered portability you can carry in a pocket
Its clearer, richer sound compared to tube radios
Its lower price compared to tube radios
A government subsidy for buying new defense-related technology

evt-10-18-1954-regency-tr-1.butterflyEffect: Despite its high price and thin sound, the TR-1 sold roughly 150,000 units on the strength of its pocket-sized portability, proving there was consumer appetite for transistor electronics. Sony and other manufacturers soon raced to build cheaper transistor radios, igniting the personal electronics boom of the 1960s.

evt-10-18-1967-venera-4.scenario: You are a Soviet flight controller at Yevpatoria on 18 October 1967, watching Venera 4's telemetry as it parachutes into Venus's clouds. The pressure and temperature readings are climbing far faster than any pre-flight model predicted.
evt-10-18-1967-venera-4.prompt: What should mission control do as the readings blow past the probe's design limits?

choices.text: Switch off telemetry and declare the mission a failure
Order the probe to jettison its parachute early
Keep receiving data until the signal is lost
Command an emergency ascent burn

evt-10-18-1967-venera-4.butterflyEffect: Venera 4 kept transmitting until it was crushed by pressure roughly 25 km above the surface, but the data it sent proved Venus's atmosphere was over 90 times denser and far hotter than scientists had assumed. This forced Soviet engineers to build far tougher pressure vessels, leading to Venera 7's historic landing in 1970.

evt-10-18-1989-space-shuttle-atlantis.scenario: You are a flight controller in Houston as Atlantis lifts off on STS-34, carrying the Galileo probe on the first leg of its journey to Jupiter. Since the Challenger disaster grounded the powerful Centaur upper stage as too dangerous to fly on the shuttle, engineers have had to devise another way to get Galileo across the solar system.
evt-10-18-1989-space-shuttle-atlantis.prompt: What trajectory do mission planners use to send Galileo to Jupiter?

choices.text: A single Earth flyby followed by a straight run to Jupiter
Direct injection powered only by the probe's own onboard engine
A direct high-energy burn using the Shuttle-Centaur upper stage
A Venus-Earth-Earth Gravity Assist (VEEGA) trajectory using the Inertial Upper Stage

evt-10-18-1989-space-shuttle-atlantis.butterflyEffect: With the Shuttle-Centaur cancelled, Galileo relied on a slower Inertial Upper Stage and a Venus-Earth-Earth Gravity Assist (VEEGA) trajectory, stretching the trip to six years instead of two. The roundabout path let Galileo make historic flybys of asteroids Gaspra and Ida en route, before it finally reached Jupiter in 1995.

evt-10-18-1991-azerbaijan.scenario: You are a delegate in Baku's Supreme Council chamber on 18 October 1991, weeks after the failed Moscow coup shattered Soviet authority. War is already underway with Armenia over Nagorno-Karabakh as the council debates its final act.
evt-10-18-1991-azerbaijan.prompt: What does the Supreme Council vote to do?

choices.text: Delays any decision pending approval from Moscow
Adopts a full declaration of independence and restores the 1918 flag
Votes to remain part of a reformed Soviet Union
Calls only for a future referendum, taking no immediate action

evt-10-18-1991-azerbaijan.butterflyEffect: The council adopted a formal declaration of independence from the Soviet Union, restoring the flag and symbols of the short-lived 1918 Azerbaijani republic. Independence brought UN membership in 1992, but the unresolved war with Armenia over Nagorno-Karabakh would shape Azerbaijani politics for decades to come.

evt-10-18-2003-bolivian-gas-conflict.scenario: It is mid-October 2003 in La Paz. Weeks of protest against a plan to export natural gas through Chile have turned deadly, and pressure on President Gonzalo Sánchez de Lozada to step down is overwhelming.
evt-10-18-2003-bolivian-gas-conflict.prompt: What does Sánchez de Lozada do as the crisis reaches its peak?

choices.text: He orders a full military crackdown to remain in power
He resigns the presidency and leaves the country
He calls snap elections while staying in office
He immediately nationalizes the gas industry to end the protests

evt-10-18-2003-bolivian-gas-conflict.butterflyEffect: On 17 October 2003 Sánchez de Lozada resigned and fled to the United States, handing power to Vice President Carlos Mesa. The Gas War's unresolved demands over resource control fed directly into Evo Morales's rise to the presidency in 2005 and the later nationalization of Bolivia's gas industry.

evt-10-18-2019-santiago.scenario: It is 18 October 2019 and you are a resident of Santiago. Eleven days of fare-hike protests have exploded overnight: metro stations are burning and the streets are filled with tear gas and demonstrators clashing with police.
evt-10-18-2019-santiago.prompt: How does President Piñera respond to the escalating chaos?

choices.text: He resigns the presidency that same day
He immediately cancels the fare hike and calls for calm
He declares a state of emergency and deploys the military with a nightly curfew
He opens direct negotiations with student leaders before any security response

evt-10-18-2019-santiago.butterflyEffect: Piñera declared a state of emergency, deployed the army, and imposed a curfew for the first time since the Pinochet dictatorship. Far from ending the unrest, the crackdown fueled a year of mass protests demanding constitutional change, culminating in a 2020 referendum that approved drafting a new Chilean constitution.

evt-10-18-2019-nasa-astronaut-corps.scenario: You are the flight director on 18 October 2019, watching astronauts Christina Koch and Jessica Meir suit up for a spacewalk outside the International Space Station, the first ever conducted entirely by women.
evt-10-18-2019-nasa-astronaut-corps.prompt: What is the primary task the pair must complete during this spacewalk?

choices.text: Replace a failed power controller on the station's truss
Repair a leaking airlock hatch
Retrieve a malfunctioning satellite
Install a new set of solar panels

evt-10-18-2019-nasa-astronaut-corps.butterflyEffect: Koch and Meir successfully replaced a failed battery charge-discharge unit that had disrupted the station's power system. The spacewalk became a widely publicized milestone for women in spaceflight and highlighted NASA's growing number of female astronauts.

evt-10-18-2019-social-outburst-chile.scenario: It is 18 October 2019 in Santiago. What began as students hopping metro turnstiles over a fare hike has exploded into burning stations, looted stores, and clashes with police across the capital.
evt-10-18-2019-social-outburst-chile.prompt: What does President Sebastián Piñera do in response to the escalating unrest?

choices.text: Calls an emergency national referendum that same day
Cancels the fare hike and the unrest ends within days
Immediately resigns the presidency
Declares a state of emergency and deploys the military into the streets

evt-10-18-2019-social-outburst-chile.butterflyEffect: Piñera declared a state of emergency and sent soldiers onto Santiago's streets for the first time since the Pinochet dictatorship, but the unrest only spread nationwide and continued for months. The crisis eventually forced a 2020 plebiscite in which Chileans voted overwhelmingly to draft a new constitution.

evt-10-19-1579-entry-of-james-vi-into-ed.scenario: You stand among the crowds in Edinburgh on 19 October 1579, watching pageantry unfold as the 13-year-old King James VI, raised under regents at Stirling Castle, formally enters the city to begin his life as an adult monarch.
evt-10-19-1579-entry-of-james-vi-into-ed.prompt: What did James VI's ceremonial entry into Edinburgh actually signal for Scotland's governance?

choices.text: His abdication in favor of the Earl of Morton
A declaration of war against England
Immediate full and unchallenged royal authority
The symbolic start of his personal rule, though nobles still held real power

evt-10-19-1579-entry-of-james-vi-into-ed.butterflyEffect: Though the ceremony marked James's symbolic assumption of adult kingship, real power remained contested among rival nobles for years afterward. This tension culminated in the 1582 Ruthven Raid, when a faction of lords seized the young king, before James finally secured firm personal control of government later in the 1580s.

evt-10-19-1596-san-felipe-incident-1596.scenario: It is October 1596, and the Spanish galleon San Felipe has wrecked on the coast of Shikoku. As the ship's pilot, you are questioned by officials serving the taikō Toyotomi Hideyoshi about Spain's intentions in Asia.
evt-10-19-1596-san-felipe-incident-1596.prompt: What do you tell the Japanese authorities about Spanish missionaries and conquest?

choices.text: Offer to hand over the ship's cargo in exchange for silence
Insist the missionaries have no connection to the Spanish crown at all
Claim Spain has no interest in expanding into Japan
Warn that missionaries typically precede military conquest, as in the Americas and Philippines

evt-10-19-1596-san-felipe-incident-1596.butterflyEffect: Hideyoshi treated the pilot's remark as proof of a Christian plot and ordered the arrest of missionaries and converts. Twenty-six Christians were crucified in Nagasaki in February 1597, the first state-sponsored killing of Christians in Japan and a grim precedent for the persecutions that followed.

evt-10-19-1752-the-pennsylvania-gazette.scenario: October 1752, Philadelphia. You unfold the latest Pennsylvania Gazette and read Benjamin Franklin's account of flying a kite with a metal key attached during a thunderstorm.
evt-10-19-1752-the-pennsylvania-gazette.prompt: What did Franklin's kite experiment demonstrate about lightning?

choices.text: That lightning is caused by burning gases in clouds
That lightning is a form of electricity
That storms could be reliably predicted using kites
That electricity cannot travel through metal

evt-10-19-1752-the-pennsylvania-gazette.butterflyEffect: The experiment showed that lightning was a form of electricity, the same force studied in laboratories. This insight led Franklin to invent the lightning rod, which spread rapidly across Europe and America and dramatically reduced deaths and fires from lightning strikes on buildings and ships.

evt-10-19-1781-siege-of-yorktown.scenario: It is 19 October 1781 at Yorktown. Your army is surrounded by Washington's Continental forces and their French allies, and the British fleet that might have rescued you has already been turned back at sea by de Grasse.
evt-10-19-1781-siege-of-yorktown.prompt: As General Cornwallis, what should you do now?

choices.text: Wait indefinitely for naval relief
Launch a full counterattack at dawn
Attempt a breakout march to the north
Surrender your army to end the siege

evt-10-19-1781-siege-of-yorktown.butterflyEffect: Cornwallis surrendered his army, ending the last major land battle of the American Revolutionary War. The defeat broke Britain's political will to continue fighting, leading directly to peace negotiations and the 1783 Treaty of Paris that recognized American independence.

evt-10-19-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: It is dawn on October 19, 1864, at Cedar Creek, Virginia. Confederate troops under Jubal Early have just launched a surprise attack, routing two Union corps, and you are General Sheridan riding back from Winchester into the chaos of fleeing soldiers.
evt-10-19-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What do you do upon reaching your broken army?

choices.text: Rally the retreating men and organize a counterattack
Order a full retreat toward Washington
Wait for fresh reinforcements before engaging
Sue for a local ceasefire to reorganize

evt-10-19-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Sheridan rallied the fleeing troops and led a decisive afternoon counterattack that shattered Early's army, even though the Union suffered nearly twice the casualties of the Confederates. The victory ended major Confederate resistance in the Shenandoah Valley and gave a political boost to Lincoln weeks before his reelection.

evt-10-19-1914-world-war-i.scenario: It is late October 1914 near Ypres, Belgium. You are an officer with the British Expeditionary Force, and German divisions are pressing hard to break through to the Channel ports before winter.
evt-10-19-1914-world-war-i.prompt: What must the British line do to keep the Germans from reaching the coast?

choices.text: Negotiate a local truce to allow reinforcements to arrive
Hold the salient at all costs, even as casualties mount
Launch an immediate counteroffensive toward Brussels
Withdraw to the Channel ports to shorten the line

evt-10-19-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The British held Ypres despite catastrophic losses that nearly destroyed the old professional army, the so-called 'Old Contemptibles.' The battle closed the 'race to the sea,' and both sides dug in along a front that would remain locked in trench warfare for the next four years.

evt-10-19-1944-guatemalan-revolution.scenario: It is October 19, 1944, in Guatemala City. As one of the young officers backing Jacobo Árbenz, Francisco Arana, and Jorge Toriello, you face President Ponce Vaides's forces still loyal to the old Ubico regime.
evt-10-19-1944-guatemalan-revolution.prompt: What do you and your fellow officers do to break the old order's grip on power?

choices.text: Launch an armed uprising to overthrow the government
Push for a peaceful electoral transition instead
Negotiate a power-sharing deal with Ubico loyalists
Request direct U.S. military intervention

evt-10-19-1944-guatemalan-revolution.butterflyEffect: The officers' armed uprising toppled Ponce Vaides and installed a revolutionary junta, opening what Guatemalans call the 'Ten Years of Spring.' The following decade brought sweeping land and labor reforms under Árbenz, until a CIA-backed coup reversed them in 1954.

evt-10-19-1955-european-broadcasting-uni.scenario: You are a delegate at the European Broadcasting Union's General Assembly in October 1955, where a proposal is put forward for a new international televised singing competition uniting broadcasters across Europe, modeled on Italy's Sanremo festival.
evt-10-19-1955-european-broadcasting-uni.prompt: What should the assembly decide about the proposed international song contest?

choices.text: Reject it as too costly for member broadcasters
Approve it only as a radio-only competition
Approve the proposal, greenlighting the contest
Postpone the decision indefinitely over technical concerns

evt-10-19-1955-european-broadcasting-uni.butterflyEffect: The assembly approved the plan, leading to the first Eurovision Song Contest held in Lugano, Switzerland in 1956. It grew into the longest-running annual international televised music competition, later expanding participation far beyond Europe's borders.

evt-10-19-1965-vietnam-war.scenario: It is 19 October 1965, and you command the Special Forces camp at Plei Me in South Vietnam's Central Highlands. Hundreds of North Vietnamese Army regulars have encircled your CIDG defenders and cut the road to relief.
evt-10-19-1965-vietnam-war.prompt: What does the besieged garrison do to survive until help arrives?

choices.text: Call in continuous air strikes and artillery while holding the perimeter
Break out on foot under cover of darkness
Abandon the camp and retreat to Pleiku immediately
Negotiate a ceasefire with the besieging force

evt-10-19-1965-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: The garrison held with air support until an armored relief column broke the siege on 25 October. The NVA's withdrawal into the Ia Drang Valley drew in the U.S. 1st Cavalry Division weeks later, producing the war's first major helicopter-borne battle between American and North Vietnamese regulars.

evt-10-19-1987-dow-jones-industrial-aver.scenario: It is October 20, 1987, the morning after the Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 22.6 percent on Black Monday. As Federal Reserve Chairman, you watch markets teeter on the edge of further panic.
evt-10-19-1987-dow-jones-industrial-aver.prompt: What do you do to keep the financial system from seizing up?

choices.text: Publicly pledge the Fed's support to provide market liquidity
Order the stock exchanges closed indefinitely
Take no action and let the market self-correct
Raise interest rates to restore investor confidence

evt-10-19-1987-dow-jones-industrial-aver.butterflyEffect: Greenspan issued a brief statement affirming the Fed's readiness to serve as a source of liquidity, calming markets and helping banks keep credit flowing to brokers. The move set a precedent for central bank intervention during market crises that shaped Fed policy for decades afterward.

evt-10-19-1987-operation-nimble-archer.scenario: It is October 19, 1987, in the Persian Gulf. You command a U.S. Navy destroyer group ordered to respond after an Iranian missile struck the reflagged tanker Sea Isle City off Kuwait days earlier, and Iranian oil platforms sit within range.
evt-10-19-1987-operation-nimble-archer.prompt: What does your task force do to the Iranian platforms?

choices.text: Blockade the platforms without firing
Board the platforms and capture their crews
Use airstrikes exclusively, withholding surface ships
Destroy the platforms with naval gunfire

evt-10-19-1987-operation-nimble-archer.butterflyEffect: U.S. warships shelled and destroyed the Rakish and Rashadat oil platforms with naval gunfire, a direct retaliation for the missile strike. The attack escalated the 'Tanker War' within the Iran-Iraq conflict, setting the stage for further U.S.-Iran naval clashes, including the far larger Operation Praying Mantis the following spring.

evt-10-19-1988-1988-1994-british-broadca.scenario: It's October 1988 and you edit the evening news at the BBC. The Home Secretary's new order bans the broadcast of the actual voices of Sinn Féin and other named groups, though their words may still be shown or reported.
evt-10-19-1988-1988-1994-british-broadca.prompt: How do broadcasters get an IRA-linked spokesman's words on air without breaking the law?

choices.text: Show only silent footage with subtitles of the interview
Delay the broadcast by 24 hours to seek legal clearance
Refuse to broadcast any interview with the speaker at all
Hire an actor to voice the exact words over the footage

evt-10-19-1988-1988-1994-british-broadca.butterflyEffect: Broadcasters hired actors to dub the banned speakers' exact words, often visibly out of sync with their lips, a workaround that became a defining absurdity of British TV news. The ban lasted until September 1994, lifted after the IRA ceasefire, and is now cited as a case study in the limits of censoring speech to fight terrorism.

evt-10-19-2003-mother-teresa.scenario: It's 19 October 2003 and you stand among some 300,000 pilgrims in St Peter's Square as Pope John Paul II beatifies Mother Teresa just six years after her death, having taken the rare step of waiving the usual waiting period.
evt-10-19-2003-mother-teresa.prompt: What miraculous healing, credited to her intercession, was cited to qualify her for beatification?

choices.text: The cure of paralysis in a hospitalized child
The recovery of a soldier from fatal battlefield wounds
The restoration of sight to a blind pilgrim in Rome
The disappearance of a village woman's abdominal tumour

evt-10-19-2003-mother-teresa.butterflyEffect: The Vatican credited the sudden disappearance of a tumour in Monica Besra, an Indian villager, after prayer to Mother Teresa, though her own doctors insisted medical treatment explained the cure. The controversy did not stop her canonization as a saint by Pope Francis in September 2016.

evt-10-19-2004-corporate-airlines-flight.scenario: It is a foggy night at Kirksville Regional Airport on 19 October 2004. You are in the cockpit of Corporate Airlines Flight 5966, descending toward the runway on approach with no visual contact yet established and the minimum descent altitude fast approaching.
evt-10-19-2004-corporate-airlines-flight.prompt: What should the crew do upon reaching minimum descent altitude without seeing the runway?

choices.text: Continue descending further, hoping to spot the runway lights
Hand control to air traffic control for a remote landing
Execute a missed approach and climb back to a safe altitude
Immediately divert to another airport without attempting the approach

evt-10-19-2004-corporate-airlines-flight.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the pilots continued descending below the minimum descent altitude while engaged in non-pertinent conversation, violating the sterile cockpit rule, and struck trees short of the runway, killing 13 of 15 aboard. The crash prompted renewed federal emphasis on strict cockpit discipline during approach and landing.

evt-10-19-2005-hurricane-wilma.scenario: It is 19 October 2005, and Hurricane Wilma has just exploded into a Category 5 storm over the Caribbean, its pressure plunging faster than any Atlantic hurricane on record. You run emergency management for the Yucatán Peninsula's resort coast.
evt-10-19-2005-hurricane-wilma.prompt: What is the priority as the storm's record-small eye bears down on Cancún?

choices.text: Wait for the storm to weaken before issuing evacuation orders
Focus resources on protecting hotel property rather than moving people
Assume the storm will turn away and take no special action
Order mass evacuation of tourists and residents from low-lying coastal areas

evt-10-19-2005-hurricane-wilma.butterflyEffect: Wilma battered Cozumel and Cancún for over 24 hours, causing catastrophic damage before curving north to strike Florida. It became the costliest hurricane in Mexican history at the time and prompted major upgrades to the Yucatán tourism zone's evacuation planning and building codes.

evt-10-19-2005-saddam-hussein.scenario: It is 19 October 2005, and you sit in the reinforced Baghdad courtroom as Saddam Hussein appears before the Iraqi Special Tribunal, charged over the 1982 killings in the town of Dujail.
evt-10-19-2005-saddam-hussein.prompt: What charge anchors this first trial against the former president?

choices.text: Genocide charges from the Anfal campaign against the Kurds
Crimes against humanity linked to the Dujail massacre
Charges over the suppression of the 1991 uprisings
Charges related to the invasion of Kuwait in 1990

evt-10-19-2005-saddam-hussein.butterflyEffect: The Dujail trial ended in November 2006 with a death sentence, and Saddam was executed weeks later before the separate Anfal genocide trial could conclude. His swift execution left many of the broader crimes against Kurds and Shia Iraqis without a final legal reckoning in his own trial.

evt-10-19-2017-robert-weryk.scenario: It is 19 October 2017, and you are reviewing images from the Pan-STARRS telescope survey in Hawai'i when you spot a fast-moving point of light whose trajectory suggests it is not bound in orbit around the Sun.
evt-10-19-2017-robert-weryk.prompt: What should you do after noticing an object on a hyperbolic, sun-escaping trajectory?

choices.text: Assume it is a previously catalogued asteroid and ignore it
Report it to the Minor Planet Center for urgent confirmation and further observation
Classify it as an ordinary comet and move on without further checks
Wait several months to gather more data before telling anyone

evt-10-19-2017-robert-weryk.butterflyEffect: The object, soon named 'Oumuamua, was confirmed as the first interstellar object ever observed passing through our solar system. Its odd elongated shape and unexplained acceleration sparked years of scientific debate and inspired new dedicated survey programs to catch the next interstellar visitor.

evt-10-20-1740-pragmatic-sanction-of-171.scenario: You're an Austrian minister on October 20, 1740, as Emperor Charles VI dies and his daughter Maria Theresa inherits the Habsburg lands under the Pragmatic Sanction he spent years securing from Europe's powers.
evt-10-20-1740-pragmatic-sanction-of-171.prompt: What challenge immediately confronts her succession?

choices.text: She must immediately cede the crown to her husband
Neighboring rulers who had promised to honor the Sanction move to seize her territories instead
She is barred from ruling under Salic law and must abdicate
She is required to convert to Protestantism to keep the throne

evt-10-20-1740-pragmatic-sanction-of-171.butterflyEffect: Despite earlier guarantees, Frederick II of Prussia invaded Silesia within months, calculating that a young female ruler's realm was vulnerable. This triggered the War of the Austrian Succession, reshaping the European balance of power and beginning a long Habsburg-Hohenzollern rivalry that would recur in later conflicts.

evt-10-20-1939-pope-pius-xii.scenario: It's October 1939, weeks after Germany's invasion of Poland. You're an aide helping Pope Pius XII draft his first encyclical, and advisors are divided over how directly the document should name the aggressors of the new war.
evt-10-20-1939-pope-pius-xii.prompt: What approach did Pius XII actually take in Summi Pontificatus?

choices.text: He formally excommunicated Adolf Hitler by name
He condemned the invasion of Poland and appealed to natural law without naming Hitler or Nazi Germany directly
He called for a Vatican-organized military crusade against Germany
He avoided any reference to the war in Europe at all

evt-10-20-1939-pope-pius-xii.butterflyEffect: Pius condemned the invasion of Poland and defended human dignity and the unity of the human race under natural law, but stopped short of naming Hitler or Nazi Germany explicitly. This cautious diplomatic style set the pattern for his wartime papacy, a legacy still debated by historians weighing discretion against moral clarity in the face of the unfolding Holocaust.

evt-10-20-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is October 20, 1944, and you wade ashore at Leyte Gulf in the Philippines behind General Douglas MacArthur, who fled the islands under orders in 1942, vowing to return.
evt-10-20-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What does MacArthur do immediately after wading ashore at Leyte?

choices.text: He postpones any public statement until Leyte is fully secured
He meets privately with Filipino guerrilla leaders before any announcement
He delivers a radio broadcast declaring 'I have returned'
He orders an immediate assault on Manila

evt-10-20-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: MacArthur broadcast a radio address declaring 'People of the Philippines, I have returned,' fulfilling his 1942 promise and rallying Filipino resistance. The Leyte landing opened the campaign to retake the Philippines, a grueling fight that lasted into 1945 and was a major step toward Japan's eventual surrender.

evt-10-20-1951-college-football.scenario: You're a photographer on the sideline at Lewis Field on October 20, 1951, watching Drake's star Black halfback Johnny Bright take the field against Oklahoma A&M, amid rumors that opposing players intend to target him.
evt-10-20-1951-college-football.prompt: When Bright is elbowed hard on a play far from the ball, what should you do?

choices.text: Leave the sideline to avoid controversy
Look away and wait for the next play
Keep shooting to document the play
Stop shooting and report only to the referee

evt-10-20-1951-college-football.butterflyEffect: Photographers kept shooting, capturing a sequence showing Bright struck unprovoked and left with a broken jaw, images that later won a Pulitzer Prize and exposed the racially motivated attack nationally. Drake University left the Missouri Valley Conference in protest, and decades later Oklahoma State issued a formal apology and honored Bright's name at its stadium.

evt-10-20-1962-china.scenario: It's dawn on 20 October 1962 and you serve with an Indian Army unit strung thin along the disputed McMahon Line, when Chinese forces suddenly launch coordinated assaults here and in Ladakh at once, catching your unprepared garrison completely off guard.
evt-10-20-1962-china.prompt: After routing Indian forces in the weeks that followed, what did China do next?

choices.text: Allowed India to retake the lost ground through negotiation
Permanently annexed all the territory it had captured
Declared a unilateral ceasefire and withdrew its troops
Agreed to a UN-mediated settlement of the border

evt-10-20-1962-china.butterflyEffect: On 21 November 1962 China declared a unilateral ceasefire and withdrew to positions near the pre-war line in most sectors, a move that stunned India. The humiliating defeat spurred a major expansion and modernization of the Indian military, and the underlying border dispute remains unresolved, still flaring today such as in the 2020 Galwan clash.

evt-10-20-1967-patterson-gimlin-film.scenario: It's October 20, 1967, and you're riding horseback with Roger Patterson along Bluff Creek in Northern California when a large, upright, hair-covered figure strides across the creek bed ahead of you.
evt-10-20-1967-patterson-gimlin-film.prompt: What does Patterson do in this moment?

choices.text: Wait silently, assuming it is a bear, and do nothing
Dismount and approach the figure on foot to get a closer look
Ride back to town first to fetch more witnesses
Grab the camera and start filming immediately

evt-10-20-1967-patterson-gimlin-film.butterflyEffect: Patterson grabbed his 16mm camera and shot roughly a minute of footage, producing what became the most scrutinized purported evidence of Bigfoot ever recorded. Decades of frame-by-frame analysis, costume claims, and counter-claims followed, cementing the film as a centerpiece of American cryptozoology and pop culture.

evt-10-20-1969-slac-national-accelerator.scenario: You are a physicist analyzing data from the Stanford Linear Accelerator, where beams of high-energy electrons have been fired at protons and, unexpectedly, some scatter back at wide angles far more often than a smooth, uniform target would allow.
evt-10-20-1969-slac-national-accelerator.prompt: What do these deep inelastic scattering results reveal about the proton?

choices.text: The proton is a smooth, uniform sphere of charge
The proton contains point-like inner particles, later identified as quarks
The accelerator's beam energy is too weak to probe the proton
The electrons themselves are breaking apart during collision

evt-10-20-1969-slac-national-accelerator.butterflyEffect: The scattering pattern showed protons are not uniform blobs but contain small, hard, point-like constituents—confirming the quark model proposed by Gell-Mann and Zweig. This experimental evidence launched the parton model and quantum chromodynamics, and the discovery later earned Friedman, Kendall, and Taylor the 1990 Nobel Prize in Physics.

evt-10-20-1973-watergate-scandal.scenario: It's the evening of October 20, 1973, and as Attorney General you've just been ordered by President Nixon to fire Special Prosecutor Archibald Cox, who has subpoenaed the White House tapes.

choices.text: Comply and fire Cox as instructed
Resign rather than carry out the order
Leak the president's order to the press before deciding
Refuse the order but remain in office

evt-10-20-1973-watergate-scandal.butterflyEffect: Richardson resigned rather than comply, his deputy William Ruckelshaus also refused and was dismissed, and Solicitor General Robert Bork ultimately fired Cox in what became known as the Saturday Night Massacre. Public outrage intensified impeachment pressure on Nixon and led to the appointment of a new special prosecutor, accelerating the path to his resignation in August 1974.

evt-10-20-1973-sydney-opera-house.scenario: It's October 20, 1973, and you're standing among the crowds on Sydney Harbour's foreshore as Queen Elizabeth II steps up to formally declare the long-delayed Opera House open, fourteen years after construction began.
evt-10-20-1973-sydney-opera-house.prompt: What happens immediately after she declares it open?

choices.text: The Harbour Bridge is closed for a parade
Jørn Utzon takes the stage to accept applause
The building is immediately renamed in the Queen's honour
A fireworks display erupts over the harbour

evt-10-20-1973-sydney-opera-house.butterflyEffect: A fireworks display lit up the harbour as the building was finally unveiled to the public, though architect Jørn Utzon—who had resigned amid disputes years earlier—was notably absent from the ceremony. The Opera House went on to become an internationally recognized symbol of Australia, later inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.

evt-10-20-1977-lynyrd-skynyrd.scenario: It's the evening of 20 October 1977, and you are the pilot of Lynyrd Skynyrd's chartered Convair 240 approaching Baton Rouge when the fuel gauges plunge and the engines begin to sputter, with the nearest airport still miles off over dense Mississippi forest.
evt-10-20-1977-lynyrd-skynyrd.prompt: With fuel exhausted and no runway in reach, what must the pilot attempt?

choices.text: Attempt an emergency landing in an open forest clearing
Circle to burn off fuel before attempting a landing
Ditch the aircraft in a nearby river
Push on toward the nearest major commercial airport

evt-10-20-1977-lynyrd-skynyrd.butterflyEffect: The plane crash-landed in the forest, killing frontman Ronnie Van Zant, guitarist Steve Gaines, singer Cassie Gaines, and the flight crew, and seriously injuring the rest of the band. Lynyrd Skynyrd disbanded for a decade, reforming only in 1987 with Van Zant's brother Johnny as singer, and the crash remains one of rock's most cited air disasters.

evt-10-20-1981-brink-s.scenario: It's October 20, 1981, in Nyack, New York. You're a police officer manning a roadblock after a Brink's armored truck was robbed nearby, and a U-Haul truck matching the fleeing vehicle's description slows to a stop in front of you.
evt-10-20-1981-brink-s.prompt: What should you do as the truck approaches your checkpoint?

choices.text: Radio for SWAT and avoid approaching the vehicle at all
Check only the driver's identification and let the truck proceed
Wave it through since it doesn't match the getaway vehicle's color
Order the truck to stop and inspect it

evt-10-20-1981-brink-s.butterflyEffect: Officers stopped and approached the truck, which carried remnants of the Weather Underground and Black Liberation Army; gunfire erupted, killing two police officers and a Brink's guard. The arrests that followed, including Kathy Boudin and David Gilbert, effectively ended the fugitive activity of 1970s radical left groups and became a landmark case in that movement's history.

evt-10-20-1986-aeroflot-flight-6502.scenario: You are the co-pilot aboard Aeroflot Flight 6502 approaching Kurumoch Airport. The captain has curtained the cockpit windows to demonstrate an instrument-only landing, leaving the crew flying blind on final approach.
evt-10-20-1986-aeroflot-flight-6502.prompt: What should the crew do as the aircraft nears the runway with the windows deliberately blocked?

choices.text: Intervene and insist the windows be uncovered before landing
Trust the captain's experience and continue the demonstration
Request a diversion to another airport without objecting to the curtains
Increase airspeed to compensate for reduced visibility

evt-10-20-1986-aeroflot-flight-6502.butterflyEffect: The captain misjudged the aircraft's altitude with the windows curtained, and the Tu-134 struck the runway hard and overran it, killing 70 of the 94 aboard. Investigators ruled the crash pilot negligence, and it became a stark example cited in later Soviet aviation safety reviews of unauthorized cockpit procedures.

evt-10-20-1991-firestorm.scenario: It's midday on October 20, 1991, and you live on a wooded ridge above Oakland. A brush fire declared contained yesterday has flared back to life in fierce, dry winds, and smoke is pouring over your street.
evt-10-20-1991-firestorm.prompt: What should you do right now?

choices.text: Go door to door warning neighbors before leaving yourself
Stay and hose down your roof and yard to protect the house
Wait at home for an official evacuation notice before doing anything
Leave immediately and drive down the hill, without waiting for an official order

evt-10-20-1991-firestorm.butterflyEffect: The fire became one of the fastest-moving urban conflagrations on record, killing 25 people and destroying roughly 3,000 homes within hours. The disaster exposed fatal radio-frequency mismatches between Oakland and Berkeley fire crews, prompting statewide mutual-aid and building-code reforms for homes built against wildland brush.

evt-10-20-2003-sloan-great-wall.scenario: It's October 2003, and you're part of the Princeton team sifting through Sloan Digital Sky Survey data when you notice a filament of galaxies stretching far beyond any structure previously mapped.
evt-10-20-2003-sloan-great-wall.prompt: What do you and your colleagues decide to do?

choices.text: Attribute the structure to a known supercluster and stop investigating
Announce the discovery of a record-breaking galactic structure
Dismiss the pattern as a data-processing artifact and move on
Quietly file the result without publishing, pending years of review

evt-10-20-2003-sloan-great-wall.butterflyEffect: Gott, Jurić, and colleagues announced the discovery from Princeton on October 20, 2003, naming it the Sloan Great Wall, then the largest known cosmic structure at roughly 1.37 billion light-years across. It held that record for years until deeper surveys revealed even larger galaxy filaments, pushing cosmologists to keep mapping the universe's large-scale structure.

evt-10-20-2005-unesco.scenario: You are a delegate at UNESCO's General Conference in Paris on October 20, 2005, preparing to vote on a treaty meant to let nations protect local films, music, and media against the pressures of global free trade.
evt-10-20-2005-unesco.prompt: What treaty does the General Conference adopt on this day?

choices.text: A founding charter establishing UNESCO itself
The World Heritage Convention
The Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions
A resolution restricting American film imports worldwide
