evt-10-25-1997-republic-of-the-congo-civ.scenario: It is October 1997 in Brazzaville. Militias loyal to ousted president Denis Sassou Nguesso are closing in on the capital, but they cannot dislodge the government's forces alone.
evt-10-25-1997-republic-of-the-congo-civ.prompt: What finally broke the deadlock and returned Sassou Nguesso to power?

choices.text: A United Nations peacekeeping force disarmed all factions
Military intervention by Angola tipped the balance in his favor
French Foreign Legion troops seized Brazzaville on his behalf
A negotiated power-sharing deal ended the fighting without outside help

evt-10-25-1997-republic-of-the-congo-civ.butterflyEffect: Angolan troops crossed the border and intervened decisively on Sassou Nguesso's side, crushing the government forces and installing him as president by year's end. He has remained in power in the Republic of the Congo ever since, making this one of Africa's longest-running rules.

evt-10-25-1999-learjet-35.scenario: It is October 25, 1999. You are an Air Force F-16 pilot scrambled to intercept a Learjet flying erratically over the Midwest. Pulling alongside, you see its windows fogged with ice and no response comes over the radio.
evt-10-25-1999-learjet-35.prompt: What do you conclude has happened to everyone aboard the aircraft?

choices.text: The plane has been hijacked and the crew is being held at gunpoint
An electrical fire has knocked out the radio and cockpit instruments
A sudden loss of cabin pressure has incapacitated the passengers and crew
Contaminated fuel has caused the pilots to lose control of the aircraft

evt-10-25-1999-learjet-35.butterflyEffect: The Learjet had lost cabin pressure shortly after takeoff, and everyone aboard—including golfer Payne Stewart—lost consciousness from hypoxia. The plane flew on autopilot for nearly four hours before running out of fuel and crashing near Aberdeen, South Dakota, killing all six aboard and prompting renewed scrutiny of pressurization systems and pilot training.

evt-10-25-2001-microsoft.scenario: It is 2001 and you are a Microsoft product manager tasked with replacing the aging, crash-prone consumer line (Windows 9x/ME) and the more stable business-focused NT/2000 line with a single new operating system.
evt-10-25-2001-microsoft.prompt: What foundational approach does Microsoft take for Windows XP?

choices.text: Abandon backward compatibility with older Windows software entirely
Continue maintaining two separate consumer and business operating systems
Base the new system on a Unix-derived kernel instead of NT
Build XP on the stable NT kernel for both home and business users

evt-10-25-2001-microsoft.butterflyEffect: Microsoft unified consumer and business users on the stable NT kernel, ending the separate consumer OS line for good. Windows XP's reliability and longevity made it Microsoft's most enduring release, remaining widely used until official support ended in 2014 and shaping the architecture of every Windows version since.

evt-10-25-2010-mount-merapi.scenario: You live on the slopes of Mount Merapi as officials raise the alert level and order evacuations, warning that the volcano's activity is escalating rapidly.
evt-10-25-2010-mount-merapi.prompt: What should you do as authorities issue the evacuation order?

choices.text: Stay behind to protect livestock and property
Wait to see whether the activity worsens further
Evacuate immediately as instructed
Ignore the order since past alerts proved harmless

evt-10-25-2010-mount-merapi.butterflyEffect: The eruptions that followed became Merapi's deadliest since the 1930s, killing more than 300 people, including the volcano's revered gatekeeper who refused to leave his post. The disaster displaced over 350,000 residents and led Indonesia to overhaul its volcanic monitoring and evacuation protocols.

evt-10-25-2010-2010-mentawai-earthquake-.scenario: You live in a fishing village on the Mentawai Islands on the night of 25 October 2010. The ground has just shaken violently offshore, and no official tsunami warning has reached your remote coastline yet.
evt-10-25-2010-2010-mentawai-earthquake-.prompt: What should you do right now?

choices.text: Continue your evening as usual
Head immediately to higher ground without waiting
Go to the shore to check the sea level
Wait for an official tsunami warning before moving

evt-10-25-2010-2010-mentawai-earthquake-.butterflyEffect: Because warnings failed to reach many isolated Mentawai villages in time, a localized tsunami struck within minutes and caused heavy casualties. The disaster renewed pressure on Indonesia to extend its tsunami-warning network beyond major cities to remote outer islands.

evt-10-25-2023-2023-lewiston-shootings.scenario: It is the night of 25 October 2023 in Lewiston, Maine. A gunman has struck a bowling alley and a bar, killed and wounded dozens, and fled into the darkness still armed.
evt-10-25-2023-2023-lewiston-shootings.prompt: What do authorities tell Lewiston residents to do while the search continues?

choices.text: Gather at a downtown shelter
Shelter in place at home
Evacuate the city immediately
Continue normal activities since he fled the state

evt-10-25-2023-2023-lewiston-shootings.butterflyEffect: Lewiston and nearby towns were placed under an unprecedented shelter-in-place order lasting nearly two days. The manhunt ended when Robert Card was found dead of a self-inflicted wound near the Androscoggin River, and the tragedy reignited national debate over gun laws and military mental-health reporting.

evt-10-26-1520-charles-v-holy-roman-empe.scenario: It is 1519, and as a prince-elector of the Holy Roman Empire you must choose the next emperor. The young Habsburg King Charles I of Spain and King Francis I of France both court your vote with promises and gold.
evt-10-26-1520-charles-v-holy-roman-empe.prompt: Which candidate did the electors ultimately choose, crowned emperor in 1520?

choices.text: Frederick the Wise of Saxony
Henry VIII of England
Francis I of France
Charles V of the House of Habsburg

evt-10-26-1520-charles-v-holy-roman-empe.butterflyEffect: Charles V's election united Habsburg Spain, Austria, and the Holy Roman Empire under one ruler, forming a vast transcontinental power without precedent in Europe. His reign brought decades of rivalry with France and coincided with the eruption of Martin Luther's Reformation, which Charles spent much of his rule trying to contain.

evt-10-26-1597-imjin-war.scenario: It is 26 October 1597 in the Myeongnyang Strait off Korea's southwest coast. You serve aboard one of just thirteen ships under Admiral Yi Sun-sin, facing a Japanese fleet of well over a hundred warships bearing down on you.
evt-10-26-1597-imjin-war.prompt: How did Yi Sun-sin's tiny fleet overcome such overwhelming odds?

choices.text: He launched a surprise night raid using fire ships
He exploited the strait's narrow channel and tidal currents to fight the enemy piecemeal
He used newly built turtle ships in a massed frontal assault
He lured the fleet onto hidden underwater obstacles near shore

evt-10-26-1597-imjin-war.butterflyEffect: Yi used the strait's narrow width and violent tidal currents to fight the Japanese ships only a few at a time, then turned the tide against them at the critical moment, sinking dozens of enemy vessels without losing a single ship of his own. The victory blocked the Japanese fleet's advance up the coast, protecting Korean supply lines and becoming one of the most celebrated naval triumphs in Korean history.

evt-10-26-1813-war-of-1812.scenario: It is 26 October 1813 along the Châteauguay River. You serve under Charles de Salaberry, commanding a small force of Canadian militia and Mohawk allies dug into the forest as a far larger American army under General Hampton advances toward Montreal.
evt-10-26-1813-war-of-1812.prompt: What tactic helped the defenders turn back the much larger American force?

choices.text: Dispersed skirmishers and bugle calls made the force appear far larger than it was
A massed cavalry charge broke the American line
Naval gunboats bombarded the American column from the river
Fixed artillery batteries destroyed the advancing columns

evt-10-26-1813-war-of-1812.butterflyEffect: De Salaberry's men scattered through the woods, sounding bugles and shouting from multiple directions to make their tiny force seem enormous, and the confused Americans withdrew rather than push on. The failed advance ended the campaign against Montreal for the year and became a founding legend of Canadian military identity.

evt-10-26-1871-edward-james-roye.scenario: You sit on Liberia's cabinet in October 1871. President Roye stands accused of secretly extending his own term and mishandling a controversial £100,000 loan raised in London, and outrage is spreading through Monrovia.
evt-10-26-1871-edward-james-roye.prompt: What does the cabinet and legislature do about President Roye?

choices.text: Call new elections while Roye stays in office
Send the matter to Liberia's supreme court for a slow review
Depose him and place him under arrest
Ignore the allegations and let him finish his term

evt-10-26-1871-edward-james-roye.butterflyEffect: Roye was deposed and arrested in what is remembered as modern Africa's first coup d'état; he drowned soon after while trying to flee Monrovia by sea. Vice President James Skivring Smith took over, and the episode set an early precedent for the removal of Liberian leaders by force that would echo in the country's later 20th-century coups.

evt-10-26-1892-ida-b-wells.scenario: You are a Memphis newspaper editor in 1892. Three of your friends have just been lynched by a mob for daring to compete economically with white businessmen, and you have gathered evidence on dozens of similar killings across the South.
evt-10-26-1892-ida-b-wells.prompt: What did Ida B. Wells do with what she had uncovered?

choices.text: She petitioned Congress directly and stopped writing publicly
She published investigative articles exposing lynching as racial and economic terror
She organized an armed militia to retaliate against mobs
She quietly left journalism to avoid retaliation

evt-10-26-1892-ida-b-wells.butterflyEffect: Wells published her findings, arguing lynching was rarely about protecting white women but about eliminating Black economic competition and enforcing racial subordination. A mob destroyed her printing press in retaliation, forcing her north, where she continued the campaign that shaped the anti-lynching movement and led to her co-founding the NAACP.

evt-10-26-1905-saint-petersburg-soviet.scenario: You are a factory delegate in Saint Petersburg in October 1905, as a general strike grips the city and workers gather to decide how to organize their growing movement.
evt-10-26-1905-saint-petersburg-soviet.prompt: What do the assembled workers' delegates decide to create?

choices.text: An armed militia to seize government buildings immediately
A vote to end the strike and return to the factories
A petition committee to appeal directly to the Tsar
A workers' council, or soviet, to coordinate the strike

evt-10-26-1905-saint-petersburg-soviet.butterflyEffect: They formed the Saint Petersburg Soviet of Workers' Deputies, a council that coordinated strikes and voiced demands directly to the authorities, with Leon Trotsky soon rising to prominence within it. Though the Tsarist government crushed it within weeks, the soviet became the model revived in 1917, when the Petrograd Soviet helped drive the Russian Revolution.

evt-10-26-1921-chicago-theatre.scenario: It is opening night, October 26, 1921, and you join the crowds filing into Balaban and Katz's lavish new Chicago Theatre, its French Baroque lobby glittering with chandeliers and gilded plasterwork.
evt-10-26-1921-chicago-theatre.prompt: What made this new "movie palace" experience different from an ordinary neighborhood cinema?

choices.text: Films were shown alongside live orchestral music and elaborate stage performances
It showed only silent newsreels with no musical accompaniment
It screened exclusively foreign and imported films
It was built as America's first drive-in theater

evt-10-26-1921-chicago-theatre.butterflyEffect: The Chicago Theatre paired films with live orchestras and elaborate stage shows in a grand architectural setting, a formula that made Balaban & Katz the dominant Chicago theater chain by 1925. It became the flagship for the American "movie palace" era, shaping how millions experienced cinema through the 1940s.

evt-10-26-1955-ngo-dinh-diem.scenario: You are an election official in South Vietnam in October 1955, tallying ballots from a referendum pitting Prime Minister Ngô Đình Diệm against former emperor Bảo Đại for control of the new state.
evt-10-26-1955-ngo-dinh-diem.prompt: What happens with the referendum results?

choices.text: International observers void the referendum entirely
Diệm is declared the overwhelming winner amid fraud allegations
The vote is too close to call and a runoff is scheduled
Bảo Đại narrowly wins and remains head of state

evt-10-26-1955-ngo-dinh-diem.butterflyEffect: Diệm's supporters reported a suspiciously lopsided victory, with turnout and margins that outstripped the eligible population in some districts. He proclaimed the Republic of Vietnam and became its first president, a rule that lasted until his assassination in the 1963 CIA-backed coup, deepening America's commitment to the war that followed.

evt-10-26-1994-israel-jordan-peace-treat.scenario: You stand at Wadi Araba on 26 October 1994, where King Hussein of Jordan and Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin are about to sign a treaty ending decades of hostility between their nations, with US President Clinton looking on.
evt-10-26-1994-israel-jordan-peace-treat.prompt: What did the treaty the two leaders signed actually establish?

choices.text: Transfer of the West Bank to Jordanian administration
Formal peace and diplomatic relations ending the state of war
A joint military command over the Jordan Valley
A full economic and currency union between the two states

evt-10-26-1994-israel-jordan-peace-treat.butterflyEffect: The treaty ended the formal state of war dating to 1948, opened embassies in Amman and Tel Aviv, and settled disputes over land and shared water resources. Jordan became only the second Arab state, after Egypt, to formally recognize Israel, though the peace remained politically contested among ordinary Jordanians for years afterward.

evt-10-26-1995-mossad.scenario: It is 26 October 1995 in Sliema, Malta. You are part of an Israeli Mossad team tracking Palestinian Islamic Jihad leader Fathi Shaqaqi, who has just checked into a hotel under a false identity while traveling from Libya.
evt-10-26-1995-mossad.prompt: What does the Mossad team do to eliminate Shaqaqi?

choices.text: Plant a car bomb in the hotel parking lot
Shoot him at close range outside the hotel
Poison his food in the hotel restaurant
Abduct him and interrogate him in a safehouse

evt-10-26-1995-mossad.butterflyEffect: A motorcycle gunman shot Shaqaqi at close range outside the hotel, killing him instantly. Ramadan Shallah succeeded him as PIJ's leader, and the assassination fueled cycles of retaliatory violence between Israel and Palestinian militant groups in the years that followed.

evt-10-26-1995-flateyri.scenario: It is the night of 26 October 1995 in the fishing village of Flateyri, tucked beneath steep slopes in Iceland's Westfjords. A massive avalanche has just swept down onto the village without the warning system that later became standard.
evt-10-26-1995-flateyri.prompt: What lasting change did this disaster prompt in Iceland's approach to avalanche danger?

choices.text: Massive avalanche barriers were built into the mountain above the village
No changes were made due to the cost of construction
Only warning sirens were installed, with no physical defenses
The entire village was abandoned and never rebuilt

evt-10-26-1995-flateyri.butterflyEffect: The tragedy forced Iceland to confront how exposed its fjord villages were to avalanches. In the years after, massive earthen and steel barriers were built into the mountainside above Flateyri, and similar defenses and stricter hazard-zoning rules were adopted for other at-risk towns nationwide.

evt-10-26-1999-united-kingdom.scenario: It is October 1999, and you sit among the hereditary peers in the House of Lords as the government pushes a bill to strip almost all of you of your right to sit and vote by birthright alone.
evt-10-26-1999-united-kingdom.prompt: What compromise did the Lords accept to soften this sweeping reform?

choices.text: Ninety-two hereditary peers would be allowed to remain as an interim measure
The House of Lords would be abolished outright
All hereditary peers would keep their seats but lose voting rights
The Lords would be immediately replaced by an elected senate

evt-10-26-1999-united-kingdom.butterflyEffect: The House of Lords Act 1999 ended the automatic right of hereditary peers to sit, but a last-minute amendment let 92 of them remain as a transitional measure. That "temporary" fix was never resolved, and those 92 seats remain part of the Lords today, leaving reform of the chamber permanently unfinished.

evt-10-26-2000-robert-guei.scenario: It is 25 October 2000 in Abidjan. Military ruler Robert Guéï has just declared himself the winner of the presidential election despite results showing him losing badly, and crowds are pouring into the streets in fury.
evt-10-26-2000-robert-guei.prompt: What actually followed the mass protests against Guéï's claimed victory?

choices.text: The army reinstated former president Bédié
Guéï fled the country and Laurent Gbagbo became president
Guéï was arrested and put on trial for fraud
The election was peacefully rerun under UN supervision

evt-10-26-2000-robert-guei.butterflyEffect: Guéï fled the presidential palace as protesters and mutinying soldiers overran it, and Laurent Gbagbo was installed as president instead. The unresolved rivalry poisoned Ivorian politics for years, and Guéï himself was killed in September 2002 on the opening day of the civil war that followed.

evt-10-26-2001-patriot-act.scenario: You are a member of Congress on 26 October 2001, six weeks after the September 11 attacks. A sweeping anti-terrorism bill expanding surveillance and law enforcement powers is on your desk, and leadership wants a swift vote.
evt-10-26-2001-patriot-act.prompt: What does Congress do with the USA PATRIOT Act?

choices.text: Table it indefinitely for further study
Strip out all surveillance provisions before passing it
Pass it quickly with overwhelming bipartisan support
Vote it down over civil liberties concerns

evt-10-26-2001-patriot-act.butterflyEffect: Congress passed the act by overwhelming margins and President Bush signed it into law that day, granting agencies broad new surveillance and detention powers. The law reshaped American security policy for over a decade, sparking recurring civil-liberties battles that culminated in the 2013 Snowden revelations and its eventual replacement by the USA Freedom Act.

evt-10-26-2003-cedar-fire.scenario: It is October 25, 2003, and you are lost in the Cleveland National Forest as darkness falls. Hoping searchers will spot the smoke, you decide to light a small signal fire on a ridge.
evt-10-26-2003-cedar-fire.prompt: What followed from that decision to light a signal fire?

choices.text: The fire grew explosively into the deadly Cedar Fire
Rescuers spotted the smoke and reached him within the hour
It merged harmlessly with a nearby controlled burn
Rain extinguished the fire before it could spread

evt-10-26-2003-cedar-fire.butterflyEffect: Driven by fierce Santa Ana winds, the blaze exploded into the Cedar Fire, California's largest wildfire at the time, killing 15 people including a firefighter and destroying nearly 2,800 structures. Scrutiny over delayed nighttime aerial firefighting response afterward pushed California agencies to reassess wildfire response protocols.

evt-10-27-1674-franco-dutch-war.scenario: It's October 1674, and you command the French garrison inside the fortress town of Grave, besieged for months by a Dutch army under Prince William III of Orange, with food and ammunition nearly exhausted.
evt-10-27-1674-franco-dutch-war.prompt: What do you decide as the garrison's position becomes untenable?

choices.text: Hold out indefinitely awaiting French relief
Burn the fortress rather than yield it
Negotiate surrender and march out under agreed terms
Attempt a mass breakout under cover of night

evt-10-27-1674-franco-dutch-war.butterflyEffect: The garrison, under the Marquis de Chamilly, negotiated a surrender and marched out with honors after one of the war's longest sieges. The loss of Grave further weakened France's grip on captured Dutch territory and fed into the diplomatic pressures that eventually produced the Treaty of Nijmegen in 1678.

evt-10-27-1775-george-iii.scenario: It's 27 October 1775, and you sit in Parliament as King George III addresses both houses, expanding on his August Proclamation of Rebellion against the American colonies.
evt-10-27-1775-george-iii.prompt: What measure did the King propose to crush the colonial rebellion?

choices.text: Negotiating directly with the Continental Congress
Granting the colonies immediate self-governance
Hiring foreign mercenary troops to reinforce British forces in America
Withdrawing all British troops from America

evt-10-27-1775-george-iii.butterflyEffect: George III announced plans to enlarge the army and navy and to hire foreign troops, soon secured from Hesse-Kassel and other German states, to fight the rebellion. The speech convinced many wavering colonists that reconciliation was impossible, hardening support for the independence movement that culminated in July 1776.

evt-10-27-1904-early-history-of-the-irt-.scenario: It is opening day, 27 October 1904, in the City Hall station. You are the motorman assigned to the very first train, but Mayor George McClellan has climbed into the cab and taken hold of the controls himself.
evt-10-27-1904-early-history-of-the-irt-.prompt: What do you do when the mayor refuses to relinquish the controls?

choices.text: Let the mayor keep driving and stand by to assist
Insist on taking back the controls for safety
Refuse to move until the mayor steps aside
Stop the train and summon a supervisor

evt-10-27-1904-early-history-of-the-irt-.butterflyEffect: McClellan ended up driving much of the inaugural run himself, delighting the crowds who packed every platform to see the new underground railway. The IRT's opening triggered a subway-building boom that reshaped New York, pulling development northward into Upper Manhattan and the Bronx.

evt-10-27-1914-world-war-i.scenario: It's 27 October 1914, off the coast of County Donegal, Ireland. Your dreadnought HMS Audacious has struck a German mine during gunnery practice, and the Admiralty must decide how to handle the news.
evt-10-27-1914-world-war-i.prompt: How did the Admiralty respond to the loss of the Audacious?

choices.text: It publicly awarded medals to the crew that same week
It issued an immediate press release naming the ship
It blamed the sinking on a torpedo from a German U-boat
It suppressed the news, keeping the sinking secret from the public for the rest of the war

evt-10-27-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Every crew member survived, evacuated with help from the liner RMS Olympic, but the Admiralty censored the loss to hide the reduction in Britain's dreadnought strength from Germany. American passengers aboard the Olympic had already photographed the sinking ship, and their pictures reached the US press despite the official silence.

evt-10-27-1942-empire-of-japan.scenario: It is 26 October 1942 near the Santa Cruz Islands. You command Japanese carrier air groups that have already lost heavily locating and attacking the American task force, but a wounded U.S. carrier is still afloat below you.
evt-10-27-1942-empire-of-japan.prompt: Do you press the attack on the crippled American carrier despite crushing aircrew losses?

choices.text: Press the attack to finish off the carrier
Withdraw immediately to preserve remaining aircraft
Hold back and wait for reinforcing carriers to arrive
Divert the strike to the American escort ships instead

evt-10-27-1942-empire-of-japan.butterflyEffect: Japanese pilots pressed on and sank USS Hornet, but the battle cost Japan a huge share of its remaining veteran carrier aircrews. Unlike the Americans, Japan could not quickly replace such skilled pilots, and the resulting decline in carrier air quality helped doom Japanese naval aviation in later battles like the Philippine Sea.

evt-10-27-1964-ronald-reagan.scenario: It's October 27, 1964, and you're in the audience for a nationally televised address by actor Ronald Reagan, delivered on behalf of a Barry Goldwater campaign that polls suggest is heading for a landslide defeat.
evt-10-27-1964-ronald-reagan.prompt: What lasting effect does this speech have, even though Goldwater still loses badly?

choices.text: It secures a narrow win for Goldwater after all
It launches Reagan's own political career toward the California governorship
It prompts Reagan to switch to the Democratic Party
It ends Reagan's public career for good

evt-10-27-1964-ronald-reagan.butterflyEffect: "A Time for Choosing" raised over a million dollars for Goldwater's doomed campaign but did nothing to change the election outcome. What it did change was Reagan's own future: the speech's reception launched his political career, leading to his election as California governor in 1966 and eventually the presidency in 1980.

evt-10-27-1980-chun-doo-hwan.scenario: It's October 27, 1980, and you're a monk at a Jogye Order temple when soldiers under Chun Doo-hwan's martial law government arrive to search the grounds and detain clergy nationwide.
evt-10-27-1980-chun-doo-hwan.prompt: What justification does the junta give for the sweeping raids on Buddhist temples?

choices.text: A campaign to purge corruption and factionalism among the clergy
A response to an alleged monk-led plot against the government
An investigation into monks sheltering communist agents
A tax-evasion probe targeting wealthy temples

evt-10-27-1980-chun-doo-hwan.butterflyEffect: Framed as a "purification" against corruption within the clergy, the raids saw over 150 monks and lay leaders detained and many mistreated in custody. Coming soon after the Gwangju crackdown, it was widely understood as an effort to intimidate a community seen as sympathetic to dissent, and it left a lasting scar on Buddhist-state relations in South Korea.

evt-10-27-1981-cold-war.scenario: It's 27 October 1981. You are a Swedish naval officer near Karlskrona when you find a Soviet Whiskey-class submarine, S-363, wedged on the rocks deep inside a restricted military zone.
evt-10-27-1981-cold-war.prompt: What does the Swedish military do about the stranded Soviet submarine?

choices.text: Open fire and sink it where it lies
Ignore it as a routine navigational error
Quietly help tow it free overnight
Surround it, demand an explanation, and refuse to let it leave until Soviet officers are questioned

evt-10-27-1981-cold-war.butterflyEffect: Sweden held the sub for over a week, suspecting a spy mission and possibly nuclear weapons, before letting it depart after tense negotiations. The 'Whiskey on the Rocks' incident exposed a pattern of Soviet submarine incursions into Swedish waters and hardened Swedish defence policy for the rest of the Cold War.

evt-10-27-1986-big-bang-financial-market.scenario: It is 27 October 1986 on the floor of the London Stock Exchange. Overnight, fixed commissions have been scrapped and the old distinction between stockjobbers and stockbrokers has vanished under Margaret Thatcher's reforms.
evt-10-27-1986-big-bang-financial-market.prompt: What follows for how shares are actually traded in London?

choices.text: Fixed commissions are quietly reinstated within a year
Trading shifts to electronic screens and foreign banks buy up British firms
The exchange shuts down for a decade of restructuring
Trading permanently relocates to Edinburgh

evt-10-27-1986-big-bang-financial-market.butterflyEffect: Open-outcry floor trading was rapidly replaced by screen-based electronic dealing, and foreign banks moved in to buy up British brokerage firms almost overnight. The deregulation, nicknamed the "Big Bang," helped cement London's rise as one of the world's dominant financial centres in the decades that followed.

evt-10-27-1988-embassy-of-the-united-sta.scenario: It's 1988, and you're a State Department security officer reviewing the new US Embassy compound in Moscow when technicians confirm Soviet construction workers embedded listening devices throughout the building's structural steel.
evt-10-27-1988-embassy-of-the-united-sta.prompt: What does President Reagan order once the compromised building is confirmed?

choices.text: Halt construction until the building's security can be verified
Transfer the building to NATO for shared use
Demolish the entire compound immediately
Ignore the findings and move staff in as planned

evt-10-27-1988-embassy-of-the-united-sta.butterflyEffect: Reagan suspended construction, and the discovery forced years of costly redesign and reinforcement before American diplomats could safely occupy the building. The affair also hardened US suspicion of Soviet intelligence practices and led to reciprocal scrutiny of the Soviet embassy compound in Washington.

evt-10-27-1991-turkmenistan.scenario: It is 27 October 1991 in Ashgabat. The Soviet Union is disintegrating, and a referendum you held days earlier returned overwhelming support for leaving the USSR.
evt-10-27-1991-turkmenistan.prompt: What do you do as a delegate in the Turkmen Supreme Soviet?

choices.text: Propose remaining in a reformed Soviet union
Vote to ratify independence based on the referendum result
Wait to see what Russia decides first
Call for a second referendum before acting

evt-10-27-1991-turkmenistan.butterflyEffect: Turkmenistan formally declared independence, becoming one of the last Soviet republics to break away. Saparmurat Niyazov, already the republic's leader, entrenched himself as president and built one of the world's most isolated and personality-driven authoritarian states.

evt-10-27-1992-murder-of-allen-r-schindl.scenario: It's late October 1992 in Sasebo, Japan, where the body of Navy radioman Allen Schindler has just been found in a public restroom, killed for being gay.
evt-10-27-1992-murder-of-allen-r-schindl.prompt: What debate did the Schindler case help push to the center of American politics?

choices.text: Whether US bases in Japan should be closed
Whether the draft should be reinstated
Whether women should be allowed in combat roles
Whether gay men and lesbians should be allowed to serve openly in the military

evt-10-27-1992-murder-of-allen-r-schindl.butterflyEffect: Schindler's murder became a rallying point in the national debate over gay service members that Bill Clinton had promised to address. The following year, the administration adopted the compromise 'Don't Ask, Don't Tell' policy, which barred open service by gay troops until its repeal in 2011.

evt-10-27-1997-1997-asian-financial-cris.scenario: It's October 27, 1997, and you're a trader on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange as panic from Thailand and Hong Kong's currency turmoil rips through Wall Street, prices collapsing before your eyes.
evt-10-27-1997-1997-asian-financial-cris.prompt: What does the exchange do as the plunge accelerates?

choices.text: The Federal Reserve cuts interest rates within the hour
The SEC shuts every US exchange for a full week
Trading continues uninterrupted through the close
Circuit breakers halt trading and force an early close

evt-10-27-1997-1997-asian-financial-cris.butterflyEffect: The Dow fell over 550 points, about 7%, triggering the exchange's circuit-breaker rules for the first time and forcing an early close. The market rebounded sharply within days, and the episode became a textbook case for regulators studying how to manage contagion and panic-driven halts.

evt-10-27-1999-nairi-hunanyan.scenario: You are a prosecutor in Yerevan in the years following the October 1999 attack, building the case against Nairi Hunanyan and his accomplices for storming parliament and killing the Prime Minister, the Speaker, and six others.
evt-10-27-1999-nairi-hunanyan.prompt: What sentence does the court hand down to Hunanyan?

choices.text: Acquittal for lack of evidence
Life imprisonment
A short sentence for manslaughter
Execution by firing squad

evt-10-27-1999-nairi-hunanyan.butterflyEffect: Hunanyan and his co-conspirators were convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2003. Lingering questions about whether officials had foreknowledge of the plot were never fully resolved, and the killings continued to fuel conspiracy theories about the true motives behind Armenia's deadliest political attack.

evt-10-27-1999-armenian-parliament-shoot.scenario: It is the afternoon of 27 October 1999 in Yerevan. You are a member of Armenia's National Assembly, seated during a live televised session, when five armed men burst into the chamber and open fire on the government's leadership.
evt-10-27-1999-armenian-parliament-shoot.prompt: What happens in the hours after the attackers seize the chamber?

choices.text: The president immediately resigns to end the standoff
Parliament is dissolved and new elections called that same day
Special forces storm the building within the hour
Gunmen hold hostages overnight and surrender after negotiations

evt-10-27-1999-armenian-parliament-shoot.butterflyEffect: The gunmen held surviving deputies hostage overnight and surrendered the next morning after negotiations with President Robert Kocharyan. With Prime Minister Vazgen Sargsyan and Speaker Karen Demirchyan dead, the reformist coalition that had sidelined Kocharyan collapsed, letting him consolidate power over Armenian politics for years to come.

evt-10-27-2004-boston-red-sox.scenario: It is the ninth inning of Game 4 in St. Louis. The Red Sox lead the World Series 3-0 and are one out away from their first championship in generations.
evt-10-27-2004-boston-red-sox.prompt: What historic drought does this sweep of the Cardinals finally end?

choices.text: The franchise's longest single-season losing streak
A losing streak against the Yankees only
The Cardinals' modern dynasty run
The 86-year championship drought since 1918

evt-10-27-2004-boston-red-sox.butterflyEffect: The win ended the 86-year championship drought known as the Curse of the Bambino, Boston's first title since 1918. It launched a new Red Sox dynasty, with further championships in 2007, 2013, and 2018, and reshaped the team's identity from lovable losers to perennial contenders.

evt-10-27-2011-michael-d-higgins.scenario: It's October 2011, and you're an Irish voter marking your ballot in a crowded presidential race featuring Labour's Michael D. Higgins, businessman Seán Gallagher, Sinn Féin's Martin McGuinness, and independents David Norris and Gay Mitchell.
evt-10-27-2011-michael-d-higgins.prompt: How does the vote count play out for the presidency?

choices.text: Martin McGuinness rides Sinn Féin momentum to victory
Michael D. Higgins wins by a resounding margin after transfers
Seán Gallagher holds his early poll lead and wins comfortably
The result is so close it triggers a full recount and rerun

evt-10-27-2011-michael-d-higgins.butterflyEffect: Higgins topped the first-preference count and, after transfers, won by one of the widest margins in Irish presidential history. Frontrunner Gallagher's campaign collapsed in the final days after a damaging live-TV exchange over a fundraising controversy, handing Higgins a decisive victory that began his fourteen-year presidency.

evt-10-27-2017-catalonia.scenario: It is 27 October 1997... no, 2017, in the Catalan Parliament in Barcelona. Weeks earlier, a disputed referendum on independence was held despite the Spanish government declaring it illegal.
evt-10-27-2017-catalonia.prompt: As a Catalan lawmaker, what do you vote for in the chamber today?

choices.text: Vote for a unilateral declaration of independence
Vote to dissolve Parliament without acting
Call for a fresh, internationally supervised referendum
Vote to postpone any declaration pending talks with Madrid

evt-10-27-2017-catalonia.butterflyEffect: The Parliament voted to unilaterally declare independence. Madrid responded within hours by invoking Article 155, dissolving the Catalan government and imposing direct rule; several leaders were arrested and Carles Puigdemont fled into exile in Belgium.

evt-10-27-2018-pittsburgh-synagogue-shoo.scenario: It's the weeks after 27 October 2018, and federal prosecutors in Pittsburgh must decide how to charge Robert Bowers for his attack on the Tree of Life synagogue.
evt-10-27-2018-pittsburgh-synagogue-shoo.prompt: What charges did prosecutors ultimately pursue against the gunman?

choices.text: No charges, citing insanity
Extradition to face charges in another state
Federal hate crime charges eligible for the death penalty
State murder charges only, without a hate crime enhancement

evt-10-27-2018-pittsburgh-synagogue-shoo.butterflyEffect: Bowers was indicted on federal hate crime charges; in 2023 a jury convicted him and recommended a death sentence, the first federal death sentence imposed for a hate crime motivated by religion. The case intensified national debate over synagogue security and rising antisemitic violence in the United States.

evt-10-27-2019-the-mocking-of-christ-cim.scenario: You are an auction house expert called to survey the contents of a modest house in Compiègne, France, before an estate sale. Above the kitchen stove hangs a small, grime-darkened panel everyone has always assumed is just an old devotional icon.
evt-10-27-2019-the-mocking-of-christ-cim.prompt: What should you do with the panel before deciding how to sell it?

choices.text: Have it heavily cleaned and repainted to look newer
Send it for specialist authentication and research before the sale
List it as a minor decorative icon and sell it quickly
Donate it to the local parish church without appraisal

evt-10-27-2019-the-mocking-of-christ-cim.butterflyEffect: The panel was sent for expert study and identified as a lost 13th-century work by Cimabue, one of only a handful of his paintings known to survive. Re-catalogued as The Mocking of Christ, it sold at auction in October 2019 for €19.5 million, one of the highest prices ever paid for a medieval painting, and a reminder that masterpieces can hide in plain sight for generations.

evt-10-27-2019-islamic-state.scenario: It's the night of 26–27 October 2019. You are part of the US special forces team that has cornered ISIS leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi in a dead-end tunnel beneath his safe house in Barisha, Syria.
evt-10-27-2019-islamic-state.prompt: What does Baghdadi do as the raid closes in on him?

choices.text: He escapes through a hidden exit
He is shot dead by Kurdish fighters
He detonates a suicide vest, killing himself and two children
He surrenders and is taken into US custody

evt-10-27-2019-islamic-state.butterflyEffect: Baghdadi killed himself and two of his children by detonating a suicide vest as US forces closed in, confirmed by DNA testing. His death fractured ISIS's leadership; successor Abu Ibrahim al-Hashimi al-Qurashi could not restore the caliphate's former territory, and the group reverted to insurgency and clandestine attacks.

evt-10-28-312-civil-wars-of-the-tetrarch.scenario: It is the night before battle outside Rome, 27–28 October 312. Constantine's men whisper that their emperor has seen a sign in the sky promising victory over Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge.
evt-10-28-312-civil-wars-of-the-tetrarch.prompt: What does Constantine order his soldiers to do before the battle?

choices.text: Offer Maxentius a truce dividing the empire
Sacrifice to Jupiter and Mars before marching out
Paint the Chi-Rho, the first letters of Christ's name, on their shields
Retreat behind the walls of Rome and wait for reinforcements

evt-10-28-312-civil-wars-of-the-tetrarch.butterflyEffect: Constantine's forces marked their shields with the Chi-Rho and crushed Maxentius, who drowned fleeing across the Tiber. Constantine became master of the Western Empire and soon issued the Edict of Milan, ending Christian persecution and setting the empire on a path toward Christianization.

evt-10-28-1640-treaty-of-ripon.scenario: You advise Charles I in October 1640. His army has been beaten in the Second Bishops' War, a Scottish Covenanter army occupies Northumberland and Durham, and the crown's treasury is empty.
evt-10-28-1640-treaty-of-ripon.prompt: How must Charles raise the money the Treaty of Ripon obliges him to pay the Scots?

choices.text: Melt down church plate across England
Borrow the sum directly from Spanish bankers
Sell crown lands in Ireland to raise funds
Summon Parliament to grant new taxes

evt-10-28-1640-treaty-of-ripon.butterflyEffect: Unable to fund the occupying Scots any other way, Charles was forced to summon what became the Long Parliament in November 1640. That Parliament refused to be easily dissolved and its escalating conflict with the king led directly to the English Civil War.

evt-10-28-1707-1707-hoei-earthquake.scenario: It is 28 October 1707, and you live in a fishing village on Japan's Pacific coast. The ground has just stopped shaking violently after the longest, strongest earthquake anyone can remember.
evt-10-28-1707-1707-hoei-earthquake.prompt: What should you do in the minutes right after the shaking stops?

choices.text: Flee immediately to high ground, expecting a tsunami
Stay indoors and wait out any aftershocks
Head to the shore to check on the fishing boats
Return to the fields to finish the day's harvest

evt-10-28-1707-1707-hoei-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Coastal communities were struck by a massive tsunami that, together with the quake, killed more than 5,000 people across southwestern Japan. The Hōei earthquake remains the only known event to rupture the entire Nankai megathrust at once, and it may have triggered Mount Fuji's last eruption just 49 days later.

evt-10-28-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is October 28, 1776, near White Plains, New York. British and Hessian troops under General Howe have just seized Chatterton's Hill, outflanking your Continental Army positions. Washington must decide how to save his army.
evt-10-28-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What does Washington do after the fighting at White Plains?

choices.text: Surrender New York City outright to Howe
Withdraw the army northward to a stronger position, preserving it for future fighting
Launch an immediate counterattack to retake Chatterton's Hill
Disband the militia and march the whole army to Philadelphia at once

evt-10-28-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Washington withdrew his forces northward and later slipped across the Hudson into New Jersey, preserving the Continental Army rather than risking annihilation. Howe's failure to pursue aggressively gave Washington room to regroup, setting up the desperate Delaware crossing and the morale-saving victory at Trenton that Christmas.

evt-10-28-1886-new-york-harbor.scenario: You stand among the crowds packed into New York Harbor on October 28, 1886, watching French sculptor Bartholdi and President Grover Cleveland preside over the unveiling of a colossal gift from France.
evt-10-28-1886-new-york-harbor.prompt: What actually happened during the dedication ceremony?

choices.text: Crowds rioted over the cost of the French donation
Bartholdi released the veil over the statue's face prematurely during the speeches
The torch failed to light for the first time in front of the crowd
The ceremony was moved indoors due to a sudden storm

evt-10-28-1886-new-york-harbor.butterflyEffect: Fog blanketed the harbor, and Bartholdi, waiting atop the statue, released the veil covering its face early after mistaking a pause in Senator Chauncey Depew's long speech for its end, cutting the ceremony short. The Statue of Liberty went on to become the enduring symbol of American immigration, later paired with Emma Lazarus's poem "The New Colossus."

evt-10-28-1919-united-states-congress.scenario: It is late October 1919. President Wilson has just vetoed the National Prohibition Enforcement Act, questioning federal authority to police wartime liquor bans in peacetime. You are a member of Congress deciding how to vote on overriding him.
evt-10-28-1919-united-states-congress.prompt: Do you vote to override Wilson's veto of the Volstead Act?

choices.text: Vote to sustain the veto, killing the enforcement act
Delay the vote pending a Supreme Court review
Push for a weaker bill raising the legal alcohol threshold
Vote to override, enacting strict federal enforcement of Prohibition

evt-10-28-1919-united-states-congress.butterflyEffect: Congress overrode the veto by wide margins in both chambers, enacting the Volstead Act, which defined 'intoxicating liquors' at over 0.5% alcohol and gave Prohibition real teeth. The strict threshold fueled bootlegging and organized crime through the 1920s, pressures that eventually led to Prohibition's repeal via the 21st Amendment in 1933.

evt-10-28-1928-wage-rudolf-supratman.scenario: You're seated at the Youth Pledge Congress in Batavia on October 28, 1928, as young journalist and composer Wage Rudolf Supratman rises to play a new song on his violin for the assembled delegates.
evt-10-28-1928-wage-rudolf-supratman.prompt: What did this premiere of "Indonesia Raya" come to represent?

choices.text: It became the anthem of the Indonesian nationalist movement, later the national anthem
It was written to honor the Dutch queen's visit
It only gained popularity after World War II ended
It was immediately banned and never performed again

evt-10-28-1928-wage-rudolf-supratman.butterflyEffect: The song became the rallying anthem of the Indonesian nationalist movement, sung at gatherings despite wary Dutch colonial monitoring. When Indonesia declared independence in 1945, "Indonesia Raya" was formally adopted as the national anthem, cementing Supratman's status as a national hero.

evt-10-28-1965-st-louis.scenario: It is 28 October 1965, and you are part of the ironworker crew high above St. Louis, trying to lower the final stainless-steel section that will finally join the Gateway Arch's two towering legs.
evt-10-28-1965-st-louis.prompt: What must the crew do to close the last gap between the legs before the final piece can fit?

choices.text: Add heavy concrete counterweights at the base
Spray the sun-warmed leg with cold water to shrink it into alignment
Wait for a completely windless day and try again later
Weld extra steel bracing onto the legs overnight

evt-10-28-1965-st-louis.butterflyEffect: Workers sprayed the sun-warmed east leg with fire hoses to cool and shrink it just enough to align with the west leg, allowing the keystone section to be jacked into place. The completed Gateway Arch went on to become St. Louis's defining landmark, opening to the public in 1967 as a monument to westward expansion.

evt-10-28-1971-prospero-spacecraft.scenario: You're an engineer at the Woomera range in Australia on October 28, 1971, watching Britain's Black Arrow rocket lift off carrying the Prospero satellite into orbit.
evt-10-28-1971-prospero-spacecraft.prompt: What did this successful launch mean for Britain's space program?

choices.text: The launch secured new long-term funding for British rocketry
It won Britain a seat in NASA's Apollo program
It led to a joint British-Soviet satellite venture
Britain became one of the few nations to launch a satellite on its own rocket, even though the program had already been cancelled

evt-10-28-1971-prospero-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: Britain became the sixth nation to launch its own satellite on a domestically built rocket, but the government had already cancelled the Black Arrow program before the launch to save money. Britain never again launched a satellite on a home-built rocket, instead joining European cooperative efforts, while Prospero itself stayed operational into the 1970s and was periodically contacted for decades.

evt-10-28-2007-2007-argentine-general-el.scenario: It is October 28, 2007, election day across Argentina. Senator and First Lady Cristina Fernández de Kirchner faces Elisa Carrió and Roberto Lavagna, with polls showing her far ahead as her husband Néstor's chosen successor.
evt-10-28-2007-2007-argentine-general-el.prompt: What is the outcome of the vote?

choices.text: Carrió wins the presidency
Lavagna wins a plurality but falls short of a majority
Fernández wins outright in the first round with over 40 percent
The election goes to a runoff between Fernández and Carrió

evt-10-28-2007-2007-argentine-general-el.butterflyEffect: Fernández won outright in the first round with 45.28% of the vote, comfortably clearing the 40% threshold needed to avoid a runoff. Her victory made her the first woman directly elected president of Argentina, launching a presidency that would entrench Kirchnerism as a dominant political force for years afterward.

evt-10-28-2007-cristina-fernandez-de-kir.scenario: It is late October 2007, and First Lady Cristina Fernández de Kirchner has just won the presidency as her husband Néstor's chosen successor, addressing supporters in Buenos Aires.
evt-10-28-2007-cristina-fernandez-de-kir.prompt: What historic distinction does her win create for Argentina?

choices.text: She becomes the first directly elected female president of Argentina
She becomes the first Peronist president since Perón himself
She becomes the first female vice president of Argentina
She becomes the first female president of any South American nation

evt-10-28-2007-cristina-fernandez-de-kir.butterflyEffect: Fernández became Argentina's second female president after Isabel Perón, but the first ever directly elected to the office. She would serve two terms as president through 2015, and later returned to national power as vice president in 2019, cementing Kirchnerism as a defining force in Argentine politics for over a decade.

evt-10-28-2009-nasa.scenario: It is October 28, 2009, at Kennedy Space Center. Engineers watch the Ares I-X rocket, the first hardware built for NASA's post-Shuttle Constellation program, roar off the pad on a brief, uncrewed test flight.
evt-10-28-2009-nasa.prompt: What was the actual purpose of the Ares I-X test flight?

choices.text: To test the flight dynamics and stage-separation systems of a new crew rocket design
To carry astronauts to the International Space Station
To test Orion capsule re-entry heat shields
To deploy a satellite for lunar mapping

evt-10-28-2009-nasa.butterflyEffect: The uncrewed flight tested the aerodynamics and stage-separation systems for a new crew launch vehicle, gathering data NASA needed for its planned return to the Moon. Despite the test's success, the Obama administration cancelled the Constellation program in 2010, redirecting NASA toward commercial crew contracts and, eventually, the Artemis program.

evt-10-28-2009-barack-obama.scenario: It's October 28, 2009, and you're a civil rights advocate watching President Obama sign a bill in the White House, more than a decade after Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. were murdered in separate hate-fueled attacks.
evt-10-28-2009-barack-obama.prompt: What did the law Obama signed actually do?

choices.text: It established a national registry of hate crime offenders
It banned workplace discrimination nationwide
It expanded federal hate crime law to include sexual orientation, gender identity, and disability
It created a new federal police agency to investigate hate crimes

evt-10-28-2009-barack-obama.butterflyEffect: The Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act expanded federal hate crime law to cover sexual orientation, gender identity, and disability for the first time, and gave the Justice Department new power to prosecute such crimes. Attached to a defense spending bill, it became a landmark for LGBTQ civil rights and a model cited in later state-level legislation.

evt-10-28-2013-turkistan-islamic-party.scenario: You are a police officer stationed near Tiananmen Gate in Beijing on October 28, 2013, when an SUV suddenly veers off the road into the crowd and bursts into flames.
evt-10-28-2013-turkistan-islamic-party.prompt: What did Chinese authorities conclude had caused the crash?

choices.text: It was an economic protest that turned violent
A mechanical failure caused the SUV to crash
It was a deliberate attack tied to Uyghur separatist militants
A drunk driver had simply lost control of the vehicle

evt-10-28-2013-turkistan-islamic-party.butterflyEffect: Investigators determined it was a deliberate attack, later linked by authorities to Uyghur militants connected to separatist groups seeking independence for Xinjiang. Beijing responded with a sweeping security crackdown across Xinjiang, intensifying surveillance and detention policies that drew years of international scrutiny.

evt-10-28-2018-jair-bolsonaro.scenario: You're a voter in Brazil's presidential runoff on October 28, 2018, choosing between far-right congressman Jair Bolsonaro and leftist candidate Fernando Haddad.
evt-10-28-2018-jair-bolsonaro.prompt: What was the outcome of this runoff vote?

choices.text: A third round of voting was required to break a tie
Bolsonaro won with about 55% of the vote, becoming president-elect
The election was annulled over fraud allegations
Haddad narrowly won the runoff

evt-10-28-2018-jair-bolsonaro.butterflyEffect: Bolsonaro won with roughly 55% of the vote, becoming Brazil's first far-right president since the return of democracy. His presidency brought sharp policy shifts on the environment and security, and his contested 2022 defeat later triggered a riot by his supporters at Brazil's Congress in January 2023.

evt-10-28-2025-hurricane-melissa.scenario: It is October 28, 2025, and Hurricane Melissa, among the most powerful Atlantic hurricanes ever recorded, is making landfall near Black River, Jamaica. As officials assess the storm afterward, they look for what made it so extreme.
evt-10-28-2025-hurricane-melissa.prompt: What did scientific analysis identify as intensifying Melissa's destructive power?

choices.text: Volcanic ash from a nearby eruption
A rare alignment of lunar tides
Human-driven climate change warming the oceans
An unusually strong La Niña cooling pattern

evt-10-28-2025-hurricane-melissa.butterflyEffect: Climate scientists concluded that human-driven climate change, which raises ocean temperatures, intensified both Melissa's winds and its rainfall. The finding added the storm to a growing body of evidence tying hurricane intensification to global warming, sharpening debate over disaster preparedness and resilience funding across the Caribbean.

evt-10-29-1792-william-robert-broughton.scenario: It is late October 1792. As Lieutenant William Broughton, you row a small boat far up an unmapped river on the Pacific coast, sent by Captain Vancouver to see how far inland the waterway extends and to chart its course.
evt-10-29-1792-william-robert-broughton.prompt: What should Broughton do as his party pushes further upstream?

choices.text: Continue rowing upstream, charting the river and naming landmarks
Abandon the survey and sail directly back to England
Wait at the river mouth for Vancouver's ship to catch up
Turn back at once, fearing hostile encounters with local peoples

evt-10-29-1792-william-robert-broughton.butterflyEffect: Broughton continued roughly 100 miles upriver, becoming the first European to record and name Mount Hood after a British admiral. His detailed survey of the Columbia River later bolstered British claims during the 19th-century Oregon boundary dispute with the United States.

evt-10-29-1831-1831-bristol-riots.scenario: It is 29 October 1831, and anti-reform judge Charles Wetherell has just arrived in Bristol to open the assizes, drawing an angry crowd furious that the Reform Bill was defeated in the House of Lords. You are a civic magistrate watching the situation escalate.
evt-10-29-1831-1831-bristol-riots.prompt: How do the authorities actually handle the crowd as it turns violent?

choices.text: They immediately grant the crowd's demands
They deploy overwhelming, well-coordinated force at once
They arrest Wetherell to calm the crowd
They react with confused, disorganized policing

evt-10-29-1831-1831-bristol-riots.butterflyEffect: The civic and military response was confused and uncoordinated, and the city fell out of control for three days as rioters burned the bishop's palace, prisons, and toll houses. Order was only restored by troops and a hastily raised middle-class posse comitatus, and the chaos exposed corrupt, unaccountable city government, feeding pressure that led to the 1832 Reform Act and later municipal reforms.

evt-10-29-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It is the night of 28-29 October 1863 near Wauhatchie, Tennessee. You serve in Geary's Union division, camped to guard the newly opened supply line into besieged Chattanooga, when musket fire erupts out of the darkness as Confederate troops attack.
evt-10-29-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: What should Geary's division do to protect the vital supply line in the confusion of night combat?

choices.text: Launch an immediate counter-charge across the river in the dark
Abandon the camp and retreat toward Chattanooga immediately
Signal for a truce until visibility improves at dawn
Fix positions, hold ground, and wait for reinforcements at first light

evt-10-29-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Geary's men held their ground through the chaotic night fighting until Hooker's reinforcements arrived, securing the 'Cracker Line' into Chattanooga. The open supply route let Grant resupply and reinforce the besieged Union army, setting the stage for the decisive Union victories at Chattanooga weeks later.

evt-10-29-1929-wall-street-crash-of-1929.scenario: It is 29 October 1929 on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange. Prices are collapsing far faster than Black Thursday's panic, and many investors who bought shares on margin are getting frantic calls from their brokers.
evt-10-29-1929-wall-street-crash-of-1929.prompt: With margin calls piling up, what do most panicking investors end up doing?

choices.text: Buy more stock while prices are low
Refuse to sell and wait confidently for a rebound
Sell their shares immediately, even at steep losses, to cover margin calls
Ask the Federal Reserve to freeze the exchange

evt-10-29-1929-wall-street-crash-of-1929.butterflyEffect: Forced selling cascaded through the market, wiping out fortunes in hours and shattering confidence in American banks. The crash triggered credit contraction and bank failures that helped spiral into the Great Depression, eventually prompting New Deal banking and securities reforms.

evt-10-29-1956-suez-crisis.scenario: You are an Israeli paratroop officer on 29 October 1956, dropped near the Mitla Pass deep in the Sinai Peninsula as Israel launches its offensive against Egypt.
evt-10-29-1956-suez-crisis.prompt: What is the stated objective of Israel's advance across the Sinai?

choices.text: Break Egypt's blockade and secure passage through the Straits of Tiran
Seize the Aswan Dam construction site
Capture Cairo and depose President Nasser
Occupy the Suez Canal itself before the British and French arrive

evt-10-29-1956-suez-crisis.butterflyEffect: Israel's advance gave Britain and France their pretext to intervene, demanding both sides withdraw and then invading themselves to seize the Suez Canal. Fierce US and Soviet pressure forced a humiliating Anglo-French withdrawal, ending Britain's status as a leading global power and boosting Nasser's standing across the Arab world.

evt-10-29-1991-galileo-spacecraft.scenario: It's October 29, 1991, and you're a mission engineer at JPL watching the first images stream back as the Galileo probe sweeps past a small, cratered body on its way to Jupiter.
evt-10-29-1991-galileo-spacecraft.prompt: Which asteroid did Galileo photograph in history's first spacecraft asteroid flyby?

choices.text: 4 Vesta
243 Ida
951 Gaspra
1 Ceres

evt-10-29-1991-galileo-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: Galileo's flyby returned the first close-up images of an asteroid, revealing Gaspra as an irregular, heavily cratered body. Two years later Galileo also passed 243 Ida and discovered its tiny moon Dactyl, the first confirmed satellite of an asteroid, reshaping scientific understanding of how asteroid systems form.

evt-10-29-1998-john-glenn.scenario: It's October 29, 1998, and at age 77 you're strapped into Space Shuttle Discovery, about to become the oldest person ever to fly in space, 36 years after your first orbital flight.
evt-10-29-1998-john-glenn.prompt: What was Glenn's assigned role aboard this shuttle mission, STS-95?

choices.text: Engineer deploying a new space station module
Spacewalker repairing a satellite
Payload specialist studying the effects of spaceflight on aging
Mission commander piloting the shuttle to landing

evt-10-29-1998-john-glenn.butterflyEffect: Glenn flew as a payload specialist, serving as a research subject in studies on how spaceflight affects the aging body. His flight generated valuable data on senior physiology in orbit and became a symbolic bridge between the pioneering Mercury era and the Space Shuttle age, inspiring later research on older astronauts.

evt-10-29-2007-dai-hong-dan-incident.scenario: It is 29 October 2007, and you are among the 22 crew of the North Korean cargo ship Dai Hong Dan, just hijacked off Mogadishu by pirates posing as port security who now hold you at gunpoint in the engine room.
evt-10-29-2007-dai-hong-dan-incident.prompt: With a US warship shadowing the hijacked vessel, what do you and your crewmates do?

choices.text: Abandon ship in the lifeboats
Radio Pyongyang and await instructions before acting
Overpower the pirates with makeshift weapons
Pay the ransom quietly and wait to be released

evt-10-29-2007-dai-hong-dan-incident.butterflyEffect: The North Korean sailors fought back with axes, pipes, and their bare hands, killing two pirates and recapturing their own ship while the American destroyer USS James E. Williams stood by. It became a rare moment of tacit cooperation between the US Navy and a North Korean crew during otherwise frozen relations between the two states.

evt-10-29-2008-delta-air-lines.scenario: It is late October 2008. As a Delta Air Lines executive, you face soaring fuel costs and a shrinking market after the financial crisis, with Northwest Airlines open to a deal that could reshape the industry.
evt-10-29-2008-delta-air-lines.prompt: What should Delta's leadership decide about Northwest Airlines?

choices.text: File for bankruptcy protection independently
Pursue a merger with US Airways instead
Merge with Northwest to form the world's largest airline
Reject all merger talks and downsize alone

evt-10-29-2008-delta-air-lines.butterflyEffect: Delta completed the merger with Northwest, creating the world's largest airline by fleet size and traffic while keeping the Delta name and Atlanta hub. The deal triggered a wave of further consolidation, including the United-Continental and American-US Airways mergers, concentrating US air travel into a handful of giant carriers.

evt-10-29-2012-hurricane-sandy.scenario: It's October 29, 2012, and you're a city official in New York as Hurricane Sandy's storm surge bears down on the coastline, with forecasters warning of record flooding in low-lying neighborhoods.
evt-10-29-2012-hurricane-sandy.prompt: What emergency decision did New York authorities make ahead of the storm's landfall?

choices.text: Keep public transit running through the storm
Shut down the subway system and evacuate low-lying coastal zones
Cancel all evacuation orders to avoid panic
Open beaches for public storm-watching

evt-10-29-2012-hurricane-sandy.butterflyEffect: Officials shut down the subway system and ordered evacuations of coastal zones, yet the surge still flooded tunnels and cut power across Lower Manhattan, causing tens of billions in damage. Sandy exposed how vulnerable coastal infrastructure was to storm surge and spurred major investment in floodproofing and resilience projects across the region in the years that followed.

evt-10-29-2013-marmaray.scenario: It is 29 October 2013, and you are the chief engineer overseeing the final stage of a new commuter line meant to link Europe and Asia by rail for the first time, crossing the seabed beneath the Bosphorus.
evt-10-29-2013-marmaray.prompt: How do you get the tunnel safely across the strait floor?

choices.text: Bore entirely with a tunnel boring machine at surface level
Sink an immersed tube tunnel into a dredged seabed trench
Build a suspension bridge instead
Run trains on a temporary ferry shuttle

evt-10-29-2013-marmaray.butterflyEffect: Engineers sank prefabricated tube sections into a trench dredged across the Bosphorus, creating one of the world's deepest immersed-tube tunnels. The finished Marmaray line gave Istanbul its first standard-gauge rail link between two continents, and construction digs also uncovered a lost Byzantine harbor beneath the city.

evt-10-29-2015-china.scenario: You are a provincial family-planning official in China on 29 October 2015, reading the Communist Party's announcement that the one-child policy, enforced for 35 years, is ending.
evt-10-29-2015-china.prompt: What new nationwide policy does the Party announce to replace it?

choices.text: Complete abolition of all birth restrictions
A one-child policy retained only in rural areas
An immediate three-child policy for every couple
A universal two-child policy for all couples

evt-10-29-2015-china.butterflyEffect: China moved to a universal two-child policy starting in 2016, hoping to ease a rapidly aging population and shrinking workforce built up under decades of birth restrictions. Birth rates kept falling anyway, and by 2021 Beijing had to further relax the limit to three children per couple.

evt-10-29-2018-boeing-737-max.scenario: It's October 29, 2018. You're a pilot on a Boeing 737 MAX climbing out of Jakarta when the nose suddenly pitches down on its own, again and again, fighting your attempts to level off.
evt-10-29-2018-boeing-737-max.prompt: What did investigators later determine caused the plane's uncommanded dives?

choices.text: Pilot error while overriding the autopilot
Structural failure of the wing
A faulty sensor triggering the MCAS anti-stall system without pilot warning
A bird strike damaging an engine

evt-10-29-2018-boeing-737-max.butterflyEffect: Investigators traced the repeated nose-down commands to the MCAS anti-stall system reacting to a single faulty angle-of-attack sensor, a system pilots had not been told existed. Five months later an almost identical failure downed Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, and regulators worldwide grounded the entire 737 MAX fleet for nearly two years while Boeing redesigned the software.

evt-10-29-2020-jeremy-corbyn.scenario: It is 29 October 2020, and Jeremy Corbyn has just responded to the EHRC's damning report on antisemitism in the Labour Party by saying the scale of the problem was "dramatically overstated."
evt-10-29-2020-jeremy-corbyn.prompt: What does the Labour Party do in response to his statement?

choices.text: He is knighted for his service
He is promoted to the shadow cabinet
His party membership is suspended
The party takes no action at all

evt-10-29-2020-jeremy-corbyn.butterflyEffect: Labour's general secretary suspended Corbyn's party membership that day; though reinstated weeks later, Keir Starmer withheld the parliamentary whip, leaving Corbyn to sit as an independent MP. The rift never healed, leading to his formal expulsion in 2024 and his founding of a new left-wing party the following year.

evt-10-29-2022-seoul-halloween-crowd-cru.scenario: It's Halloween night, October 29, 2022, in Seoul's Itaewon district. You're packed into a narrow, sloping alley with costumed crowds when the mass of people suddenly stops moving and panic spreads.
evt-10-29-2022-seoul-halloween-crowd-cru.prompt: What civic failure did later investigations identify as a key contributing factor?

choices.text: A subway signal failure that trapped commuters underground
Collapse of a temporary stage structure
Lack of crowd-control planning and police presence for the organizer-less festival
A faulty fire alarm causing a stampede

evt-10-29-2022-seoul-halloween-crowd-cru.butterflyEffect: Investigations found no official organizer had been designated for the informal street festival, and police crowd-control deployment was inadequate for the narrow, sloped alley overwhelmed by revelers. The disaster led to new crowd-safety legislation in South Korea and resignation calls against senior police and disaster-response officials.

evt-10-29-2022-2022-somali-ministry-of-e.scenario: It's October 29, 2022, near Mogadishu's Ministry of Education complex. A vehicle explodes outside the gates, and as officials and rescuers rush to help, a second blast tears through the same junction.
evt-10-29-2022-2022-somali-ministry-of-e.prompt: Which group claimed responsibility for this double car bombing?

choices.text: Al-Shabaab
ISIS-Somalia
Ahlu Sunna Wal Jama'a
A breakaway clan militia

evt-10-29-2022-2022-somali-ministry-of-e.butterflyEffect: Al-Shabaab admitted responsibility for what became Somalia's deadliest attack since 2017. The bombing hardened public and international support for the Somali government's ongoing offensive against the group, which intensified with local militia and African Union backing in the following months.

evt-10-30-1806-war-of-the-fourth-coaliti.scenario: It's late October 1806. You command the Prussian garrison at the fortress of Stettin, thousands of troops and heavy artillery behind strong walls, when a small French cavalry force under General Lasalle appears demanding surrender.
evt-10-30-1806-war-of-the-fourth-coaliti.prompt: Convinced hidden French infantry vastly outnumber you, what do you do?

choices.text: Open artillery fire on the approaching cavalry
Surrender the fortress without firing a shot
Burn the supplies and retreat toward Prussian lines
Sortie out to attack before reinforcements arrive

evt-10-30-1806-war-of-the-fourth-coaliti.butterflyEffect: Governor Friedrich von Romberg surrendered Stettin's roughly 5,000 defenders and its cannons to a French cavalry brigade a fraction of that size, convinced overwhelming numbers lay hidden nearby. The bloodless capitulation became a byword for Prussian collapse after Jena-Auerstedt, helping spur the sweeping military reforms Prussia undertook in the years that followed.

evt-10-30-1863-athens.scenario: It's 1863 in Athens. King Otto has been deposed, and the Greek National Assembly is choosing a new monarch, hoping the right choice will secure Great Power backing for the fragile kingdom.
evt-10-30-1863-athens.prompt: Which young royal does the Assembly elect, betting on British goodwill?

choices.text: A Russian Romanov grand duke
Seventeen-year-old Prince Vilhelm of Denmark
An Ottoman-appointed Greek nobleman
A cousin of Emperor Napoleon III of France

evt-10-30-1863-athens.butterflyEffect: Vilhelm accepted the crown as George I, founding the Greek royal house that would reign, with interruptions, until 1974. Britain marked the choice by ceding the Ionian Islands to Greece as a gesture toward the new dynasty, expanding Greek territory for the first time since independence.

evt-10-30-1888-lobengula.scenario: You are King Lobengula of the Ndebele in Matabeleland in October 1888. Agents representing the mining magnate Cecil Rhodes press you to put your mark to a document granting exclusive mineral rights across your kingdom, offering rifles, ammunition, and a monthly payment in return.

choices.text: He granted mining rights but only for a single named mine
He signed the Rudd Concession granting Rhodes exclusive mineral rights
He refused outright and expelled Rhodes's agents from his court
He insisted on dealing directly with the British Colonial Office instead

evt-10-30-1888-lobengula.butterflyEffect: He signed the Rudd Concession, believing it granted only limited mining rights at a single site. Rhodes instead used it to secure a royal charter for the British South Africa Company in 1889, which invoked the concession to justify colonising Matabeleland and Mashonaland, leading to war with Lobengula's kingdom by 1893 and the founding of Rhodesia.

evt-10-30-1960-royal-infirmary-of-edinbu.scenario: It's October 1960 at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh. You are surgeon Michael Woodruff, preparing to attempt Britain's first successful kidney transplant, knowing rejection has doomed every previous attempt with unrelated donors.
evt-10-30-1960-royal-infirmary-of-edinbu.prompt: How do you sidestep the rejection problem that has defeated your predecessors?

choices.text: Wait until artificial immunosuppressive drugs are fully perfected first
Cross-match blood type only and proceed with any willing donor
Transplant a kidney between identical twins so the immune system won't reject it
Use a kidney from an unrelated deceased donor without any immunosuppression

evt-10-30-1960-royal-infirmary-of-edinbu.butterflyEffect: Woodruff transplanted a kidney between identical twins, since their genetic identity meant the recipient's immune system would not reject it — the same insight behind the world's first successful transplant in Boston in 1954. The operation's success established transplant surgery in Britain and pushed research toward immunosuppressive drugs that would later let doctors transplant organs between unrelated donors.

evt-10-30-1965-jean-shrimpton.scenario: It's Derby Day, 30 October 1965, at Flemington Racecourse in Melbourne. You watch British model Jean Shrimpton step out in a dress well above the knee, with no gloves, stockings, or hat — a shock at this famously formal event.
evt-10-30-1965-jean-shrimpton.prompt: What happened once photographs of Shrimpton's outfit spread worldwide?

choices.text: The Australian government banned short dresses at public events
She was arrested for indecent exposure
A media firestorm that helped push the miniskirt into mainstream fashion
British sponsors boycotted the race in protest

evt-10-30-1965-jean-shrimpton.butterflyEffect: The look sparked a global media storm, with older society figures calling it scandalous while younger audiences embraced it as daring and modern. The moment is widely credited with helping push the miniskirt from fringe fashion into mainstream style around the world, cementing Shrimpton's status as an icon of Swinging London.

evt-10-30-1968-korean-people-s-army.scenario: It's late October 1968, and you're a South Korean villager on the east coast when armed strangers speaking with northern accents appear near Uljin and Samcheok.
evt-10-30-1968-korean-people-s-army.prompt: What was the commandos' mission, and what actually happened to them?

choices.text: They successfully established a guerrilla base that lasted years
They were smugglers unrelated to the two Koreas' rivalry
They intended to assassinate South Korea's president in Seoul
They aimed to spark a local uprising, but were hunted down by the South Korean army

evt-10-30-1968-korean-people-s-army.butterflyEffect: Nearly all 120 infiltrators were killed or captured within weeks as South Korean forces mounted a massive manhunt. Coming soon after that year's Blue House Raid, the incident pushed Seoul to expand its reserve forces and civil defense, hardening South Korea's Cold War security posture.

evt-10-30-1983-national-reorganization-p.scenario: It's October 30, 1983, and you're a voter in Buenos Aires as Argentina holds its first free election since the 1976 coup.
evt-10-30-1983-national-reorganization-p.prompt: What followed the election Raúl Alfonsín won that day?

choices.text: The military annulled the results and stayed in power
The winning candidate resigned within a month under pressure
Argentina immediately rejoined a regional military alliance
Alfonsín took office and later put junta leaders on trial for human rights abuses

evt-10-30-1983-national-reorganization-p.butterflyEffect: Alfonsín's government carried out the 1985 Trial of the Juntas, convicting senior commanders of the dictatorship for crimes including forced disappearances. It was one of the first times a Latin American military regime's leaders faced justice in civilian courts, a model later cited across the region.

evt-10-30-1985-space-shuttle-challenger.scenario: It's October 30, 1985, and you're one of eight astronauts—the largest shuttle crew ever launched—aboard Challenger for the West German-sponsored Spacelab mission STS-61-A.
evt-10-30-1985-space-shuttle-challenger.prompt: What later happened to Challenger and its role in NASA's shuttle program?

choices.text: It was destroyed less than three months later, killing all seven crew of STS-51-L
It retired safely after over a decade of service
It completed ten more missions before decommissioning
It was mothballed and replaced by Endeavour immediately

evt-10-30-1985-space-shuttle-challenger.butterflyEffect: STS-61-A proved to be Challenger's last successful flight. On January 28, 1986, it broke apart 73 seconds after launch on mission STS-51-L, killing all seven aboard and grounding the shuttle program for over two years while NASA overhauled its safety culture.

evt-10-30-1991-madrid-conference-of-1991.scenario: It's 30 October 1991, and you are a delegate in Madrid's Royal Palace, where Israeli, Jordanian, Lebanese, Syrian, and Palestinian representatives sit down together under joint US-Soviet sponsorship for the first time in years.
evt-10-30-1991-madrid-conference-of-1991.prompt: How did organizers get Israel and the Palestinians into the same room?

choices.text: The PLO sent its own delegation headed by Yasser Arafat
The UN held separate talks with each Palestinian representative
Palestinians joined a joint delegation with Jordan
Egypt represented the Palestinians instead

evt-10-30-1991-madrid-conference-of-1991.butterflyEffect: Since Israel refused to negotiate directly with the PLO, Palestinians attended as part of a joint delegation with Jordan. Though Madrid produced no immediate deal, it opened bilateral tracks that led toward the 1993 Oslo Accords and the first direct Israeli-PLO negotiations in decades.

evt-10-30-1991-israeli-palestinian-confl.scenario: You are a Palestinian delegate in Madrid in late October 1991. Israel refuses to sit across the table from the PLO directly, yet the United States and Soviet Union have brought Israelis and Arabs together for the first face-to-face talks in decades.
evt-10-30-1991-israeli-palestinian-confl.prompt: How did Palestinians manage to take part in the talks despite Israel's objection to the PLO?

choices.text: The United Nations negotiated on their behalf without Israeli consent
Palestinian representatives boycotted the conference entirely
They joined as part of a joint delegation with Jordan
PLO officials attended the sessions in secret disguise

evt-10-30-1991-israeli-palestinian-confl.butterflyEffect: Palestinians joined as part of a joint Jordanian-Palestinian delegation, a workaround that let direct dialogue begin without Israel formally recognising the PLO.
