This opening helped enable the secret Oslo back-channel negotiations of 1992-93, culminating in the 1993 Oslo Accords and mutual recognition between Israel and the PLO.

evt-10-30-1993-the-troubles.scenario: It is Halloween night, 30 October 1993, in the Rising Sun Bar in Greysteel, County Londonderry. Armed men have just burst in shouting 'trick or treat' as the crowd celebrates in costume.
evt-10-30-1993-the-troubles.prompt: This Ulster Defence Association attack was revenge for which earlier bombing?

choices.text: The Shankill Road fish shop bombing
The Enniskillen Remembrance Day bombing
The Bloody Sunday shootings
The Omagh bombing

evt-10-30-1993-the-troubles.butterflyEffect: Loyalist gunmen killed civilians in the bar as revenge for the IRA's Shankill Road fish shop bombing days earlier, part of a deadly tit-for-tat cycle. The horror of these attacks added pressure that helped push both republican and loyalist paramilitaries toward the ceasefires of 1994, a crucial step on the road to the 1998 Good Friday Agreement.

evt-10-30-1995-quebec.scenario: It's 30 October 1995, and you're a Quebec voter standing before the referendum ballot, deciding whether the province should pursue sovereignty or remain part of Canada.
evt-10-30-1995-quebec.prompt: How does the province ultimately vote?

choices.text: Quebec votes to negotiate a new federal structure instead
The vote is nullified due to low turnout
A clear majority votes Yes for sovereignty
A razor-thin majority votes No, keeping Quebec in Canada

evt-10-30-1995-quebec.butterflyEffect: The No side won by just 50.58% to 49.42%, the closest margin in Quebec's referendum history. The scare pushed Ottawa to pass the Clarity Act in 2000, setting strict rules for any future secession vote, and the sovereignty movement never again came so close to winning.

evt-10-30-2001-michael-jackson.scenario: It's October 30, 2001, and you're a Sony executive reviewing the rollout for Michael Jackson's new album, Invincible — the most expensive album ever made.
evt-10-30-2001-michael-jackson.prompt: What actually happened to Jackson's studio career after Invincible's release?

choices.text: It became his last studio album before his 2009 death
Sony canceled promotion and shelved the album entirely
He immediately launched a stadium world tour to promote it
He released two more platinum albums before retiring

evt-10-30-2001-michael-jackson.butterflyEffect: Invincible turned out to be Jackson's final studio album. Disputes with Sony over promotion and cost soured their relationship, and no further studio album followed before his death in 2009, leaving fans anticipating a comeback that never arrived in album form.

evt-10-30-2002-warren-zevon.scenario: It's 30 October 2002. Terminally ill with cancer, you're on the Late Show set as David Letterman's only guest for the entire hour, guitar in hand, making your final television appearance.
evt-10-30-2002-warren-zevon.prompt: What do you tell Letterman you've learned since your diagnosis?

choices.text: "Fame was never worth the cost"
"Enjoy every sandwich"
"I wish I'd toured less and written more"
"Nothing changes until you're gone"

evt-10-30-2002-warren-zevon.butterflyEffect: Zevon's deadpan reply, telling viewers to "enjoy every sandwich," became one of the most quoted lines of his career, and the episode—where he played several songs instead of the usual one—was later ranked among Late Show's most memorable. He died less than a year later, in September 2003, shortly after releasing his final album, The Wind.

evt-10-30-2005-frauenkirche-dresden.scenario: It's 30 October 2005 in Dresden. You stand in the crowd as the Frauenkirche — reduced to rubble by Allied firebombing in 1945 — is formally reconsecrated after eleven years of painstaking reconstruction.
evt-10-30-2005-frauenkirche-dresden.prompt: What method did rebuilders use to reconstruct the ruined church?

choices.text: They imported stone-for-stone replicas from a sister church in Britain
They used only modern concrete cast to resemble the original
They reused thousands of the original blackened stones in the new structure
They built an entirely new church and preserved the ruins nearby as a memorial

evt-10-30-2005-frauenkirche-dresden.butterflyEffect: Thousands of the original blackened stones were catalogued, salvaged, and fitted back into the new structure, giving the facade its distinctive patchwork of dark and light stone. British donors, including descendants of the airmen who bombed Dresden, helped fund the rebuild and gave a new cross for the dome, turning the church into a lasting symbol of Anglo-German reconciliation.

evt-10-30-2010-jon-stewart.scenario: You're standing on the National Mall on October 30, 2010, among tens of thousands who've come at Jon Stewart's invitation just before the midterm elections.
evt-10-30-2010-jon-stewart.prompt: What was the stated purpose of the Rally to Restore Sanity and/or Fear?

choices.text: To launch Stewart's campaign for a Senate seat
To demand repeal of a new healthcare law
To endorse a specific presidential candidate for 2012
To push back against media hysteria and political extremism ahead of midterms

evt-10-30-2010-jon-stewart.butterflyEffect: The rally drew an estimated 200,000 people and was widely read as a satirical counter to that year's polarized midterm season and the earlier Glenn Beck rally. It became a touchstone for Stewart's media criticism and cemented The Daily Show's influence on political discourse.

evt-10-30-2014-european-union.scenario: You're Swedish Foreign Minister Margot Wallström on October 30, 2014, announcing the new government's decision to officially recognize the State of Palestine.
evt-10-30-2014-european-union.prompt: What did Sweden's decision provoke internationally?

choices.text: The EU immediately adopted the same recognition
Israel recalled its ambassador in protest
The UN Security Council voted to admit Palestine as a member state
The United States imposed sanctions on Sweden

evt-10-30-2014-european-union.butterflyEffect: Israel briefly withdrew its ambassador and called the move premature. Sweden became the first EU member to recognize Palestine while in government, fueling a wider European debate that saw several other parliaments pass symbolic recognition motions in the years that followed.

evt-10-30-2020-2020-aegean-sea-earthquak.scenario: It's 30 October 2020 in İzmir. The ground has just stopped shaking after a magnitude-7.0 quake off Samos, and several modern residential blocks lie collapsed while older buildings nearby stand untouched.
evt-10-30-2020-2020-aegean-sea-earthquak.prompt: What does this pattern of destruction prompt Turkish authorities to investigate?

choices.text: Whether Greek authorities delayed sharing seismic data with Turkey
Whether contractors bypassed Turkey's building codes during rapid urban construction
Whether offshore drilling triggered the earthquake
Whether the tsunami warning system failed to sound in time

evt-10-30-2020-2020-aegean-sea-earthquak.butterflyEffect: Investigators found that several of the collapsed buildings had been built recently in violation of Turkey's post-1999 seismic codes, and prosecutors pursued charges against contractors. The disaster also produced a rare moment of warmth between rival neighbors, as Greek and Turkish rescue teams and leaders exchanged support across the earthquake zone.

evt-10-30-2022-2022-morbi-bridge-collaps.scenario: You are a resident of Morbi, Gujarat, on the evening of 30 October 2022, joining crowds flocking onto the century-old suspension bridge over the Machchhu River during the festive season, just days after its reopening following private renovation work.
evt-10-30-2022-2022-morbi-bridge-collaps.prompt: What decision by the bridge's operator set the stage for the collapse?

choices.text: The bridge had been shut for scheduled maintenance that day
It closed the bridge for years of repairs before a certified reopening
It reopened the bridge without safety certification despite heavy crowding
Municipal engineers had approved strict visitor load limits beforehand

evt-10-30-2022-2022-morbi-bridge-collaps.butterflyEffect: The Oreva Group reopened the bridge to the public without an official structural fitness certificate, and it collapsed under a crowd far exceeding its safe capacity. The disaster led to negligence charges against company officials and triggered nationwide scrutiny of privately managed public infrastructure across India.

evt-10-30-2023-rescue-of-ori-megidish.scenario: It's 30 October 2023, and Israeli intelligence has just pinpointed a captured soldier's location inside Gaza during the ground invasion. You're part of the joint IDF-Shin Bet team moving in to bring her out.
evt-10-30-2023-rescue-of-ori-megidish.prompt: What was the outcome of this joint IDF-Shin Bet operation?

choices.text: The rescue failed and the hostage was killed in the crossfire
The operation was called off before troops entered Gaza
Megidish was rescued alive, the first hostage freed by military action in the war
She was released weeks later through a negotiated prisoner exchange

evt-10-30-2023-rescue-of-ori-megidish.butterflyEffect: Soldier Ori Megidish was rescued alive, becoming the first hostage freed by military action since the war began, after two Hamas militants guarding her were killed. The successful rescue boosted Israeli public morale and became an early reference point alongside the negotiated hostage releases that followed during later ceasefires.

evt-10-31-475-romulus-augustulus.scenario: It is 476 in Ravenna. The barbarian general Odoacer has just deposed the boy-emperor Romulus Augustulus, and as a Roman official you watch to see what he will do with the imperial title he now holds by force.
evt-10-31-475-romulus-augustulus.prompt: What does Odoacer do with the authority of the Western Roman throne?

choices.text: He crowns himself Western Roman Emperor
He divides the empire among rival barbarian generals
He sends the regalia east and rules Italy as king, naming no new Western emperor
He restores power to the exiled emperor Julius Nepos

evt-10-31-475-romulus-augustulus.butterflyEffect: Rather than crowning himself emperor, Odoacer sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople and ruled Italy as king, acknowledging nominal Eastern Roman authority. Historians traditionally mark this moment as the end of the Western Roman Empire and the beginning of the medieval period in Western Europe.

evt-10-31-1517-ninety-five-theses.scenario: You are a fellow professor at the University of Wittenberg on 31 October 1517. Martin Luther has just posted a list of ninety-five propositions on the church door, challenging a practice being promoted by traveling preachers across Germany.
evt-10-31-1517-ninety-five-theses.prompt: What was Luther's central target in the theses?

choices.text: The lack of a German translation of the Bible
The church's continued use of Latin in the mass
The sale of indulgences claiming to reduce punishment for sin
Rules forbidding clergy from marrying

evt-10-31-1517-ninety-five-theses.butterflyEffect: Luther attacked the sale of indulgences, certificates claiming to reduce punishment for sin, arguing they corrupted true repentance. Spread rapidly by the printing press, his theses ignited a movement that led to his excommunication in 1521 and launched the Protestant Reformation, permanently splitting Western Christianity.

evt-10-31-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It is late afternoon on 31 October 1917 outside Beersheba, and you command mounted troops of the Australian Light Horse. The town's wells must be seized before dark or your horses will die of thirst, and the Ottoman trenches lie open ahead across bare ground.
evt-10-31-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What do you order your mounted regiments to do to take the town before nightfall?

choices.text: Charge the trenches directly on horseback before the defenders can reload
Withdraw the brigade and search for water elsewhere
Wait until dawn for a coordinated artillery bombardment
Dismount the men and advance on foot with rifles

evt-10-31-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The Light Horse charged straight at the Ottoman trenches on horseback, overrunning the defenders and capturing Beersheba's wells intact — one of the last successful large-scale cavalry charges in history. The victory opened the road past the Gaza-Beersheba line, leading to the fall of Jerusalem to Allied forces that December.

evt-10-31-1941-bust-sculpture.scenario: It is 31 October 1941, high on the granite face of Mount Rushmore, and you are one of roughly 400 workers finishing the carving. Sculptor Gutzon Borglum died months earlier, and funding has grown scarce even as the original design called for far more than just faces.
evt-10-31-1941-bust-sculpture.prompt: What happens to the memorial's original plan to carve the presidents down to the waist?

choices.text: It is abandoned due to lack of funds and Borglum's death
A fifth president, Woodrow Wilson, is added to the design
Congress doubles funding to complete the full figures
The site is converted into a full working quarry

evt-10-31-1941-bust-sculpture.butterflyEffect: With Borglum dead and Depression-era funding exhausted, the ambitious full-torso design was abandoned, and work stopped with just the four 60-foot heads finished. What was meant as a grander monument became, by necessity, the iconic image of four presidential faces recognized worldwide today.

evt-10-31-1973-provisional-irish-republi.scenario: It is 31 October 1973, and you are a guard on duty in the exercise yard of Dublin's Mountjoy Prison when a hijacked helicopter suddenly drops out of the sky and touches down inside the walls.

choices.text: Guards open fire and force it to abort before touchdown
It drops weapons to start a mass riot
It is a decoy while prisoners tunnel out elsewhere
It lands, and three IRA prisoners climb aboard and escape

evt-10-31-1973-provisional-irish-republi.butterflyEffect: The helicopter, hijacked at gunpoint, picked up three IRA prisoners including senior figure Seamus Twomey and flew them to freedom in one of the most audacious prison escapes of the Troubles. The breakout deeply embarrassed Irish authorities, triggering tighter prison security reviews, while Twomey went on to become IRA Chief of Staff.

evt-10-31-1999-egyptair-flight-990.scenario: It is November 1999, and you are an NTSB analyst poring over the flight data and cockpit voice recorders recovered from the Atlantic seabed after EgyptAir Flight 990 plunged into the ocean, killing all 217 aboard. The final minutes show a strange, contested sequence of control inputs.
evt-10-31-1999-egyptair-flight-990.prompt: What did the U.S. investigation conclude was the most likely cause of the crash?

choices.text: Sudden explosive decompression of the cabin
Fuel starvation caused by a navigation error
Deliberate control input by the relief first officer
Mechanical failure of the elevator control system

evt-10-31-1999-egyptair-flight-990.butterflyEffect: The NTSB concluded the relief first officer deliberately put the aircraft into a dive while repeating a religious phrase, but Egyptian investigators rejected this, blaming mechanical failure instead. The unresolved dispute strained U.S.-Egyptian aviation cooperation and became a textbook case of how national narratives can diverge over the same evidence.

evt-10-31-1999-jesse-martin.scenario: It is October 31, 1999, and you are 18-year-old Jesse Martin, closing in on Port Phillip Bay after nearly eleven months alone at sea aboard your sloop Lionheart-Mistral. Crowds are gathering in Melbourne to see if you finish the way you started.
evt-10-31-1999-jesse-martin.prompt: To make your record official, what must Jesse do for the entire voyage?

choices.text: Sail the entire route himself, without stopping, refuelling, or outside help
Accept a tow from a support boat once land is in sight
Radio for a resupply drop near the finish to save time
Let a harbor pilot guide the boat in for the final approach

evt-10-31-1999-jesse-martin.butterflyEffect: Jesse Martin completed the circumnavigation entirely solo, non-stop and unassisted, becoming the youngest person ever to do so. His book and documentary inspired a wave of teenage sailors to attempt similar solo voyages, prompting debate about minimum ages for record attempts.

evt-10-31-2000-singapore-airlines-flight.scenario: It is late on 31 October 2000 at Chiang Kai-shek International Airport, Taiwan. Typhoon Xangsane is battering the runways with driving rain and near-zero visibility as you, the captain of Singapore Airlines Flight 006, line up for takeoff to Los Angeles.
evt-10-31-2000-singapore-airlines-flight.prompt: What should you do before advancing the throttles for takeoff?

choices.text: Proceed since air traffic control has already cleared the flight
Trust the first officer's prior landing at this airport as sufficient verification
Independently confirm you are on the correct, open runway before rolling
Accelerate quickly to minimize time exposed to crosswinds

evt-10-31-2000-singapore-airlines-flight.butterflyEffect: The crew mistakenly lined up on a closed, construction-obstructed runway instead of the active one and struck barriers during the roll, killing 83 of the 179 aboard. It was Boeing's first fatal 747-400 crash and Singapore Airlines' first fatal accident, prompting industry-wide reviews of runway identification procedures during low-visibility operations.

evt-10-31-2000-soyuz-tm-31.scenario: You are NASA astronaut Bill Shepherd, commanding the first resident crew as Soyuz TM-31 lifts off from Baikonur Cosmodrome. Mission planners want to know what radio call sign your new home in orbit should use.
evt-10-31-2000-soyuz-tm-31.prompt: What call sign does Shepherd choose for the station over the objections of some officials?

choices.text: "Unity Station"
"Freedom"
"Alpha"
"ISS-1"

evt-10-31-2000-soyuz-tm-31.butterflyEffect: Shepherd's insistence on the call sign "Alpha" caused friction with Russian space officials who preferred other names, but it stuck informally among crews for years. Expedition 1's arrival began an unbroken chain of human presence aboard the ISS that continues today.

evt-10-31-2002-houston.scenario: You are a federal prosecutor in Houston on 31 October 2002, presenting evidence to a grand jury against former Enron chief financial officer Andrew Fastow over a web of off-the-books partnerships he had used to hide the company's mounting debt.

choices.text: Securities fraud and conspiracy tied to hidden partnerships
Tax evasion unconnected to Enron's finances
Obstruction of justice for shredding company documents
Insider trading on Enron stock alone

evt-10-31-2002-houston.butterflyEffect: Fastow was indicted on securities fraud and conspiracy charges tied to the hidden partnerships that had inflated Enron's reported profits. He later pleaded guilty and cooperated with prosecutors, testimony that proved crucial in convicting former CEO Jeffrey Skilling and chairman Kenneth Lay in 2006.

evt-10-31-2003-mahathir-mohamad.scenario: It is 31 October 2003, and after 22 years running Malaysia, Mahathir Mohamad is stepping down as prime minister. As a senior UMNO figure, you watch him hand over the reins he has held since 1981.
evt-10-31-2003-mahathir-mohamad.prompt: Who did Mahathir choose as his successor to become the next prime minister?

choices.text: Abdullah Ahmad Badawi
Musa Hitam
Najib Razak
Anwar Ibrahim

evt-10-31-2003-mahathir-mohamad.butterflyEffect: Abdullah Ahmad Badawi took over as prime minister, initially promising reform but later drawing Mahathir's public criticism for straying from his policies. Mahathir's dissatisfaction with successive leaders eventually drove him back into frontline politics, and in 2018 he returned as prime minister for a second stint at age 92.

evt-10-31-2005-moons-of-pluto.scenario: You are part of the Hubble team led by Alan Stern, reviewing May 2005 images of Pluto in preparation for the New Horizons mission. Two faint points of light appear near the dwarf planet that were never catalogued before.
evt-10-31-2005-moons-of-pluto.prompt: Before telling the world you've found new moons, what should the team do?

choices.text: Dismiss the points as camera artifacts and move on
Assume they are passing asteroids unrelated to Pluto
Announce the discovery immediately in a press release
Take additional confirming images before making any announcement

evt-10-31-2005-moons-of-pluto.butterflyEffect: The team obtained follow-up Hubble observations confirming the objects were real, orbiting bodies, and announced the discovery of Nix and Hydra on October 31, 2005. Their existence forced NASA to plan New Horizons' 2015 flyby around potential debris hazards, and added fuel to the debate over Pluto's planetary status the following year.

evt-10-31-2014-vss-enterprise.scenario: You are co-pilot Michael Alsbury aboard VSS Enterprise's rocket-powered test flight over the Mojave Desert. As the spaceplane accelerates through the transonic region, procedure calls for unlocking the wing-feathering system only once a specific speed is reached.
evt-10-31-2014-vss-enterprise.prompt: What does Alsbury do with the feather lock during this critical phase of the flight?

choices.text: Wait for a manual signal from ground control before touching it
Disable the feather system for this test entirely
Leave the feather locked until reaching the specified speed
Unlock the feather early, ahead of the specified speed

evt-10-31-2014-vss-enterprise.butterflyEffect: Alsbury unlocked the feather early, and aerodynamic forces deployed it prematurely, tearing the spacecraft apart. He was killed and pilot Peter Siebold survived by parachute; the investigation led to a redesigned feather system with a mechanical inhibitor, delaying Virgin Galactic's commercial program by years.

evt-10-31-2015-metrojet-flight-9268.scenario: It is November 2015, days after Metrojet Flight 9268 broke apart over the Sinai Peninsula, killing all 224 aboard. As a Russian aviation official, you face mounting evidence of an onboard explosion, but acknowledging it carries serious political weight.
evt-10-31-2015-metrojet-flight-9268.prompt: What did Russian investigators eventually determine caused the crash?

choices.text: Pilot error while navigating severe turbulence
An explosive device hidden aboard the aircraft
Catastrophic engine failure during climb
A mid-air collision with an unidentified object

evt-10-31-2015-metrojet-flight-9268.butterflyEffect: Russia confirmed the explosion was caused by a bomb, which the Islamic State–affiliated Sinai Province claimed to have smuggled aboard. Russia suspended all flights to Egypt for years, dealing a severe blow to Egyptian tourism, and the attack hardened Moscow's resolve in its military campaign against Islamist militants in the region.

evt-10-31-2017-2017-new-york-city-truck-.scenario: You are the NYPD officer who has just watched a rented truck plow through cyclists along the Hudson River bike path before slamming into a school bus. The driver climbs out holding what look like a pistol and a paintball gun, shouting.
evt-10-31-2017-2017-new-york-city-truck-.prompt: With the driver ignoring commands and raising the objects toward you, what do you do?

choices.text: Retreat and call for a hostage negotiator
Attempt to tackle him unarmed
Fire, believing the objects to be real firearms
Order him to lie down and wait for backup to arrive

evt-10-31-2017-2017-new-york-city-truck-.butterflyEffect: Officer Ryan Nash shot and wounded the attacker, Sayfullo Saipov, ending the rampage that had killed eight people. The attack accelerated New York's rollout of protective bollards along bike paths and public routes, part of a wider global response to vehicle-ramming attacks in cities like Nice and London.

evt-10-31-2020-berlin-brandenburg-airpor.scenario: It is 31 October 2020, and you are a Berlin transport official watching the first flights finally land at a new airport that was originally supposed to open nearly a decade earlier, delayed for years by faulty fire-safety systems and mounting cost overruns.
evt-10-31-2020-berlin-brandenburg-airpor.prompt: After which former West German chancellor and Nobel Peace Prize laureate is the airport formally named?

choices.text: Willy Brandt
Angela Merkel
Konrad Adenauer
Helmut Kohl

evt-10-31-2020-berlin-brandenburg-airpor.butterflyEffect: The airport was officially named Berlin Brandenburg Willy Brandt Airport, honoring the chancellor famous for his Ostpolitik outreach to East Germany. Its opening finally closed Tegel Airport and consolidated Berlin's air traffic, though the decade of delays had already made BER a national symbol of troubled public infrastructure projects.

evt-11-01-1141-empress-matilda.scenario: You advise Empress Matilda in November 1141. Her forces hold her rival King Stephen captive, but the tables have turned: her own commander and half-brother, Robert of Gloucester, has just been captured by Stephen's queen.
evt-11-01-1141-empress-matilda.prompt: What do you advise Matilda to do to recover Robert of Gloucester?

choices.text: Keep Stephen imprisoned and abandon Robert
Execute Stephen to remove him as a threat
Trade Stephen's release for Robert's freedom
Offer Stephen's crown to Robert instead

evt-11-01-1141-empress-matilda.butterflyEffect: Matilda agreed to release Stephen in exchange for Robert of Gloucester, restoring Stephen to the throne he had lost. The civil war known as the Anarchy dragged on for another decade until the 1153 Treaty of Winchester recognized Stephen as king for life but named Matilda's son, the future Henry II, as his heir.

evt-11-01-1914-world-war-i.scenario: It is 1 November 1914, and you stand on the deck of a crowded troopship as the first convoy of the Australian Imperial Force pulls away from King George Sound at Albany, bound for a war on the other side of the world.
evt-11-01-1914-world-war-i.prompt: Where does your convoy first put you ashore for training before you see combat?

choices.text: German East Africa, to seize colonial territory
Egypt, for training before combat
Britain, to join a home defense garrison
Directly to the trenches in France

evt-11-01-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The convoy sailed to Egypt, where the Australians and New Zealanders trained before being thrown into the Gallipoli campaign in April 1915. That campaign, though a military failure, became the founding legend of Anzac identity in Australia and New Zealand.

evt-11-01-1941-ansel-adams.scenario: You are Ansel Adams driving south on Highway 84 near Hernandez, New Mexico, when you spot the rising moon glowing above a cemetery and adobe crosses in the fading autumn light. You have only seconds before the light changes, and you have just realized you cannot find your exposure meter.
evt-11-01-1941-ansel-adams.prompt: What do you do to correctly expose the shot before the light is gone?

choices.text: Switch to color film to capture the scene more accurately
Calculate exposure from the moon's known luminance using the Zone System
Wait for a better-lit moment later in the evening
Guess a fast shutter speed and bracket several random exposures

evt-11-01-1941-ansel-adams.butterflyEffect: Adams calculated the exposure from memory, using his Zone System to estimate the luminance of the moon itself since he had no meter reading. "Moonrise, Hernandez, New Mexico" became one of the most reproduced fine art photographs of the 20th century, and Adams later printed and sold it in countless variations that helped sustain his career and cement the Zone System's reputation.

evt-11-01-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 1 November 1944, and you are flying an American F-13 Superfortress on a long, lonely mission from Saipan toward the Japanese capital, the first Allied aircraft to approach it since the Doolittle Raid over two years earlier.
evt-11-01-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What is the primary purpose of your unarmed, high-altitude flight over Tokyo?

choices.text: To photograph the city and its industrial areas for future bombing targets
To scatter propaganda leaflets urging surrender
To drop the first incendiary bombs on Tokyo
To test a new long-range fighter escort tactic

evt-11-01-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The flight, flown by the aircraft nicknamed Tokyo Rose, photographed potential targets and returned safely with crucial intelligence. Those images helped plan the intensive B-29 firebombing campaign against Japanese cities that began weeks later and continued until the war's end.

evt-11-01-1959-hockey-puck.scenario: It is 1 November 1959. You are Montreal Canadiens goaltender Jacques Plante, bleeding after a shot from Andy Bathgate splits your face open. The trainers have patched the cut, but you refuse to skate back onto the ice under one condition.
evt-11-01-1959-hockey-puck.prompt: What do you insist on wearing before you return to the game?

choices.text: Extra padding on his chest only
A backup goaltender's jersey instead of returning
A protective face mask
A full metal cage helmet

evt-11-01-1959-hockey-puck.butterflyEffect: Plante returned wearing a fiberglass face mask he had been practicing with in secret, over his coach's objections, and the Canadiens won that night. His mask soon became a fixture, and within a decade masked goaltenders were the norm across the NHL, permanently changing the position's equipment and safety.

evt-11-01-1973-watergate-scandal.scenario: It is 1 November 1973, days after Nixon fired Special Prosecutor Archibald Cox in the 'Saturday Night Massacre,' triggering public outrage and the resignations of the Attorney General and his deputy. You are the newly named Special Prosecutor, Leon Jaworski, taking the job under intense scrutiny.
evt-11-01-1973-watergate-scandal.prompt: What does Jaworski do next in pursuing the Watergate investigation?

choices.text: Press forward and legally fight for access to the White House tapes
Resign in protest just as Cox had, refusing the compromised post
Negotiate a private immunity deal with Nixon to avoid further conflict
Quietly wind down the investigation to calm the political crisis

evt-11-01-1973-watergate-scandal.butterflyEffect: Jaworski subpoenaed Nixon's secret tapes and pushed the case to the Supreme Court, which ruled unanimously in United States v. Nixon (1974) that the president had to release them. The tapes proved the coverup, and Nixon resigned weeks later on 9 August 1974.

evt-11-01-1976-michel-micombero.scenario: It is November 1976 in Bujumbura. Micombero's decade of rule has grown erratic amid his declining health, and a group of army officers led by Lieutenant Colonel Jean-Baptiste Bagaza is moving to seize power without bloodshed.
evt-11-01-1976-michel-micombero.prompt: What is the outcome of the officers' coup against Micombero?

choices.text: The coup fails and Micombero crushes the plotters
Micombero is executed by the officers in a public trial
Micombero is removed and Bagaza takes power, sending him into exile
Hutu rebels seize the moment to launch a nationwide uprising

evt-11-01-1976-michel-micombero.butterflyEffect: Bagaza's Supreme Revolutionary Council removed Micombero peacefully, and he was sent into exile in Somalia. Bagaza ruled Burundi for the next decade, maintaining Tutsi-dominated one-party rule until he too was overthrown in a 1987 coup.

evt-11-01-1982-honda.scenario: You are a line manager at Honda's new Marysville, Ohio plant in November 1982, watching the first American-built Accord roll off the assembly line under the eyes of Ohio officials and skeptical American reporters.
evt-11-01-1982-honda.prompt: What does this moment represent for Honda in the U.S. market?

choices.text: The plant closes within a year due to poor sales
Toyota beats Honda to the milestone by opening its plant first
The plant is used only to assemble motorcycles, not cars
Honda becomes the first Asian automaker to build cars in the U.S.

evt-11-01-1982-honda.butterflyEffect: Honda became the first Asian automaker to manufacture cars in the United States, easing trade tensions from Japanese import quotas. The Marysville plant's success opened the door for Toyota, Nissan, and other Japanese automakers to build 'transplant' factories across America in the following years.

evt-11-01-1987-british-rail-class-43-hst.scenario: You are aboard a specially prepared InterCity 125 power car on the East Coast Main Line near Darlington in 1987, part of a record attempt to prove the diesel-powered HST's speed potential on ordinary track.
evt-11-01-1987-british-rail-class-43-hst.prompt: What does the test run achieve for the Class 43 power car?

choices.text: The attempt is abandoned after a mechanical failure
The record is disallowed for exceeding safety limits
It is beaten by a French TGV attempt the same week
It sets a world speed record for diesel-powered rail traction

evt-11-01-1987-british-rail-class-43-hst.butterflyEffect: The run set a world speed record for diesel traction at 238 km/h (148 mph), a mark that stood for decades. It cemented the InterCity 125's reputation as one of the most successful diesel train designs, with Class 43 power cars remaining in front-line UK service for over 40 years.

evt-11-01-1993-maastricht-treaty.scenario: It is 1 November 1993, and you work in a European Community government ministry. The Maastricht Treaty has just entered into force, and officials are scrambling to explain to the public what has actually changed.
evt-11-01-1993-maastricht-treaty.prompt: What concrete change takes effect for ordinary citizens of member states today?

choices.text: They are conscripted into a new joint European defense force
They begin using a single European currency the same day
They start paying a direct EU-wide income tax
They automatically become citizens of the new European Union

evt-11-01-1993-maastricht-treaty.butterflyEffect: The treaty created a legal citizenship of the European Union, alongside commitments to a future single currency and shared foreign and security policy, transforming the European Communities into the European Union. The debate over how "federal" this new Union should be continued through later treaties, culminating in the 2007 Treaty of Lisbon.

evt-11-01-2000-chhattisgarh.scenario: It is 1 November 2000, and after decades of campaigning by tribal and regional leaders, Madhya Pradesh's Chhattisgarhi-speaking districts are finally being carved into a new state. As officials finalize the paperwork, they must settle one last practical question.
evt-11-01-2000-chhattisgarh.prompt: Which city do the new state's founders designate as its capital?

choices.text: Ambikapur
Jagdalpur
Raipur
Bilaspur

evt-11-01-2000-chhattisgarh.butterflyEffect: Raipur was chosen as Chhattisgarh's capital, giving the young state its administrative and commercial center. Rapid urban growth followed as government offices, industry, and infrastructure investment concentrated there, while resource-rich but underdeveloped tribal areas elsewhere in the state remained a source of ongoing political tension.

evt-11-01-2011-mario-draghi.scenario: You are a bond trader on 1 November 2011, watching Italian and Greek government bond yields spike as Mario Draghi takes over as president of the European Central Bank amid a deepening eurozone debt crisis.
evt-11-01-2011-mario-draghi.prompt: What dramatic pledge would Draghi make less than a year later to calm the markets?

choices.text: That Italy and Greece should leave the eurozone
That the ECB would immediately launch quantitative easing
That interest rates would be raised to defend the currency
That the ECB would do "whatever it takes" to preserve the euro

evt-11-01-2011-mario-draghi.butterflyEffect: In July 2012, Draghi vowed the ECB would do "whatever it takes" to preserve the euro, a statement that preceded the Outright Monetary Transactions program. Borrowing costs for struggling eurozone states fell sharply, and the pledge is widely credited with halting the acute phase of the debt crisis.

evt-11-01-2024-novi-sad-railway-station-.scenario: It is the first week of November 2024, and you live in Novi Sad. A concrete canopy at the newly renovated railway station has just collapsed onto the pavement below, killing and injuring people who were sheltering there, and questions are swirling about the recent renovation work.
evt-11-01-2024-novi-sad-railway-station-.prompt: In the weeks that followed, what did the collapse actually trigger across Serbia?

choices.text: The station was quietly repaired and reopened within a week without controversy
Mass protests demanding accountability spread from Novi Sad across Serbia
The government immediately collapsed within days of the accident
The European Union imposed swift sanctions on Serbia

evt-11-01-2024-novi-sad-railway-station-.butterflyEffect: The collapse ignited sustained student-led protests in Novi Sad that spread nationwide, fueled by anger over the renovation, corruption, and media censorship. The unrest eventually forced the resignation of Prime Minister Miloš Vučević in January 2025, becoming one of the most significant political crises in Serbia since the 2000s.

evt-11-02-1880-james-a-garfield.scenario: It's November 1880. You've just won the presidency, but the Ohio legislature had already elected you to the U.S. Senate before your national campaign took off.
evt-11-02-1880-james-a-garfield.prompt: As president-elect, what do you do with the Senate seat you already hold?

choices.text: Keep the Senate seat and delay his inauguration
Decline the Senate seat and prepare to take the presidency
Resign the presidency and remain a senator
Ask Congress to let him hold both offices simultaneously

evt-11-02-1880-james-a-garfield.butterflyEffect: Garfield declined the Senate seat to take office as president in March 1881. Within months he was shot by a disappointed office-seeker, Charles Guiteau, and his death from the wound galvanized support for the Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act.

evt-11-02-1917-balfour-declaration.scenario: It is November 1917, and you are Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour finalizing a letter to Lord Rothschild on behalf of the British Cabinet, weighing wartime alliances and competing promises about the future of Palestine.
evt-11-02-1917-balfour-declaration.prompt: What does the declaration promise to support?

choices.text: Full independence for Palestine under Arab rule
A joint Ottoman-British administration of Jerusalem
British annexation of Palestine as a colony
A national home for the Jewish people in Palestine

evt-11-02-1917-balfour-declaration.butterflyEffect: The letter pledged British support for "a national home for the Jewish people" in Palestine. It became a cornerstone of British Mandate policy, encouraged Jewish immigration, and set in motion tensions that shaped the 1948 creation of Israel and the ongoing Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

evt-11-02-1932-australian-defence-force.scenario: It is November 1932, and you are Major Gwynydd Meredith, sent with soldiers and Lewis machine guns to Western Australia's wheat belt, where farmers say emus are trampling crops and fences by the thousand.
evt-11-02-1932-australian-defence-force.prompt: How does the military operation against the emus turn out?

choices.text: The army built emu-proof fences across the wheat belt
Farmers and soldiers negotiated a truce with the emus' migration routes
The emu population was exterminated within days
The operation was largely ineffective and quietly abandoned

evt-11-02-1932-australian-defence-force.butterflyEffect: The emus proved far more elusive than expected, scattering into small groups and absorbing bullets without dying in useful numbers, and the operation was withdrawn after a few weeks with little to show for it. The farce became known as the "Emu War," a lasting symbol of military overconfidence, and future emu control was left instead to bounty-hunting farmers.

evt-11-02-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It's the night of 1–2 November 1943 in Empress Augusta Bay off Bougainville. You command a US cruiser task force under Rear Admiral Merrill, standing guard as a Japanese cruiser squadron steams in to smash the transports that just landed Marines ashore.
evt-11-02-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What does the American task force do to protect the landing?

choices.text: Engage the Japanese force and force it to withdraw
Retreat to open sea and abandon the transports
Call in bombers instead of engaging directly
Surrender the bay to avoid losses

evt-11-02-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Merrill's ships engaged the Japanese force in a night action, sinking a light cruiser and a destroyer while losing none of their own, and forced the enemy squadron to withdraw. The victory secured the Bougainville beachhead and helped the Allies establish the air and naval dominance needed to isolate the major Japanese base at Rabaul.

evt-11-02-1949-dutch-indonesian-round-ta.scenario: It's 2 November 1949, and you sit at the negotiating table in The Hague as an Indonesian delegate. After months of talks, the Dutch will only agree to transfer sovereignty if one territory is carved out of the deal.
evt-11-02-1949-dutch-indonesian-round-ta.prompt: What compromise do you accept to finally conclude the conference?

choices.text: Reject the deal and continue the armed independence struggle
Agree Dutch sovereignty over most territory transfers now, but West New Guinea's status is deferred
Insist West New Guinea transfers immediately alongside everything else
Accept five more years of Dutch administration over all territories

evt-11-02-1949-dutch-indonesian-round-ta.butterflyEffect: The Netherlands transferred sovereignty over the rest of the archipelago but kept West New Guinea out of the settlement, promising further talks on its status. The dispute festered for over a decade, sparking armed confrontation before the territory was finally handed to Indonesia in the early 1960s.

evt-11-02-1959-1950s-quiz-show-scandals.scenario: It's November 1959. You are Charles Van Doren, once America's most celebrated quiz show champion, now sitting before a congressional subcommittee investigating whether Twenty-One was rigged.
evt-11-02-1959-1950s-quiz-show-scandals.prompt: What do you tell the committee about your winning streak?

choices.text: Refuse to testify, citing his Fifth Amendment rights
Blame only the network executives, denying personal involvement
Deny any wrongdoing and insist his wins were genuine
Admit that producers gave him the answers in advance

evt-11-02-1959-1950s-quiz-show-scandals.butterflyEffect: Van Doren admitted he had been fed answers by producers, ending his television career in disgrace. The scandal led to a 1960 amendment to the Communications Act banning rigged contests and permanently damaged public trust in early television.

evt-11-02-1959-m1-motorway.scenario: It's 2 November 1959, and you've just merged onto Britain's first inter-urban motorway, a wide new stretch running north from Watford toward Rugby. There are no speed cameras, no central reservation barriers, and crucially, no legal speed limit.
evt-11-02-1959-m1-motorway.prompt: Do you push your car to its top speed, since nothing in law stops you?

choices.text: No — stick to the old 30mph town limit out of caution
No — obey the existing 40mph trunk-road limit
No — wait for lane markings before speeding up
Yes — floor it, since there's no legal limit yet

evt-11-02-1959-m1-motorway.butterflyEffect: There genuinely was no speed limit on Britain's motorways at first, and drivers raced expensive cars to their limits. Rising accidents, including a notorious multi-car pile-up in fog, led the government to impose a temporary 70mph limit in 1965, made permanent in 1967 and still in force today.

evt-11-02-1963-ngo-dinh-diem.scenario: It's 2 November 1963 in Saigon. You are President Ngô Đình Diệm, hiding in a Catholic church in Cholon as coup forces close in and your palace guard has abandoned you.
evt-11-02-1963-ngo-dinh-diem.prompt: What happens after Diệm and his brother agree to surrender to the plotting generals?

choices.text: They fight their way out and escape across the border to Cambodia
They are promised safe exile, then killed inside an armored vehicle
They negotiate a power-sharing government with the coup leaders
They call in American airstrikes against the rebel generals

evt-11-02-1963-ngo-dinh-diem.butterflyEffect: Despite assurances of safe passage into exile, Diệm and his brother Ngô Đình Nhu were shot inside an armored personnel carrier shortly after surrendering. The coup, tacitly backed by Washington, plunged South Vietnam into years of political instability and deepened American military commitment to the war.

evt-11-02-1963-south-vietnam.scenario: It's November 1–2, 1963, in Saigon. You are among the generals who have just overthrown President Ngô Đình Diệm; he and his brother Nhu have surrendered after hiding in a Cholon church and are now in your custody, riding in an armored personnel carrier to headquarters.
evt-11-02-1963-south-vietnam.prompt: What happens to Diệm and Nhu in the APC on the way to headquarters?

choices.text: They are executed inside the vehicle
Send them into exile abroad
Restore Diệm to a ceremonial presidency
Hold them for a public trial

evt-11-02-1963-south-vietnam.butterflyEffect: Diệm and Nhu were shot and stabbed inside the vehicle on orders that remain disputed to this day. Their deaths stunned President Kennedy, who had tacitly backed the coup, and plunged South Vietnam into years of unstable governments, deepening the case for direct American military escalation.

evt-11-02-1964-saud-of-saudi-arabia.scenario: It's 1964 in Riyadh. You are a senior prince in the Al Saud family council, watching King Saud's erratic rule and financial mismanagement threaten the kingdom's stability.
evt-11-02-1964-saud-of-saudi-arabia.prompt: What does the royal family do to resolve the crisis?

choices.text: Force Saud's abdication in favor of Crown Prince Faisal
Split the kingdom between rival claimants
Invite British intervention to mediate the dispute
Reaffirm their loyalty to Saud and dismiss his critics

evt-11-02-1964-saud-of-saudi-arabia.butterflyEffect: The family council, backed by senior clerics, forced Saud to abdicate in favor of Crown Prince Faisal on November 2, 1964. Faisal went on to modernize Saudi institutions and steer oil policy through the 1970s, until his own assassination in 1975.

evt-11-02-1966-cuban-adjustment-act.scenario: It's November 1966. You fled Cuba after the 1959 revolution and have now lived in the United States for two years, uncertain about your legal status.
evt-11-02-1966-cuban-adjustment-act.prompt: What does the newly enacted Cuban Adjustment Act let you do?

choices.text: Qualify only for temporary asylum status
Apply for lawful permanent residency on an expedited basis
Be granted a work visa valid for five years
Receive automatic U.S. citizenship immediately

evt-11-02-1966-cuban-adjustment-act.butterflyEffect: The law let qualifying Cuban arrivals apply for expedited lawful permanent residency, bypassing the usual immigration process. It became the legal backbone of decades of Cuban migration policy, later shaping the 1990s 'wet foot, dry foot' rule before being ended in 2017.

evt-11-02-1967-vietnam-war.scenario: It's 2 November 1967 in Washington. President Johnson has summoned "The Wise Men," a group of senior foreign policy elders including Dean Acheson and McGeorge Bundy, to judge whether the Vietnam War can still be won as public doubt grows.
evt-11-02-1967-vietnam-war.prompt: What do the Wise Men advise Johnson to do?

choices.text: Launch a full invasion of North Vietnam
Begin immediate withdrawal of US troops
Hand the war entirely to South Vietnamese forces
Persevere with the current strategy

evt-11-02-1967-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: The group urged Johnson to persevere with the current strategy, reassuring him the war was being won. Just three months later the Tet Offensive shattered that confidence, and several of the same advisers reversed course, helping convince Johnson to seek negotiations and announce he would not run for reelection.

evt-11-02-1983-ronald-reagan.scenario: It is November 2, 1983. You stand on the White House lawn as President Reagan prepares to sign legislation after years of congressional resistance, with civil rights leaders and members of the King family watching.

choices.text: A constitutional amendment on voting rights
A federal holiday honoring Martin Luther King Jr.
A national civil rights museum in Atlanta
A federal commission to investigate King's assassination

evt-11-02-1983-ronald-reagan.butterflyEffect: The bill established Martin Luther King Jr. Day as a federal holiday, first observed in January 1986. It made King the only American besides George Washington to be honored with a federal holiday centered on his birth, cementing his legacy in the national calendar despite Reagan's earlier private doubts about the holiday.

evt-11-02-1984-capital-punishment.scenario: It's 2 November 1984 in Raleigh, North Carolina. Velma Barfield, convicted of poisoning her fiancé and others, has exhausted her final appeals as the state prepares to carry out her death sentence.
evt-11-02-1984-capital-punishment.prompt: What method does North Carolina use to execute her, making history?

choices.text: Hanging
Gas chamber
Electric chair
Lethal injection

evt-11-02-1984-capital-punishment.butterflyEffect: Barfield died by lethal injection, becoming the first woman executed in the US since the death penalty's reinstatement in 1976 and the first person of either sex put to death by that method. Her case intensified national debate over executing women and helped establish lethal injection as the dominant method used across the country in the decades that followed.

evt-11-02-1986-lebanon-hostage-crisis.scenario: It's late 1986 in Beirut. American hostage David Jacobsen has just been freed after 17 months in captivity, and you're a U.S. official trying to understand what secret channel made this release possible.
evt-11-02-1986-lebanon-hostage-crisis.prompt: What covert arrangement is quietly enabling hostage releases like this one?

choices.text: A direct ransom payment negotiated by the Red Cross
A prisoner exchange with the Palestine Liberation Organization
A covert U.S. military raid on the hostage-takers' hideout
Secret U.S. arms sales to Iran in exchange for influence over the captors

evt-11-02-1986-lebanon-hostage-crisis.butterflyEffect: The releases were tied to secret U.S. arms sales to Iran, meant to encourage Iranian influence over the kidnappers. When this became public weeks later, it ignited the Iran-Contra affair, badly damaging the Reagan administration's credibility.

evt-11-02-1997-tropical-storm-linda-1997.scenario: It's 2 November 1997 off Vietnam's Mekong Delta. You are a fisherman far from shore when a storm that strengthened faster than forecasters expected suddenly bears down on your boat and the coast beyond.
evt-11-02-1997-tropical-storm-linda-1997.prompt: What should coastal authorities have done differently as the storm approached?

choices.text: Rely solely on fishermen's own judgment
Do nothing, since the storm looked too weak to matter
Send all warnings to northern Vietnam instead
Issue earlier storm warnings to fleets far offshore

evt-11-02-1997-tropical-storm-linda-1997.butterflyEffect: Thousands of fishermen were caught unprepared far out to sea, and Linda became the deadliest storm to strike southern Vietnam in a century, killing thousands and destroying countless boats and homes. The disaster exposed serious gaps in storm warnings for the region's fishing fleets and pushed Vietnam to invest in better early-warning systems afterward.

evt-11-02-2000-expedition-1.scenario: It is November 2, 2000, and you are astronaut Bill Shepherd, commander of Expedition 1, floating through the hatch into the International Space Station for the first time, preparing to radio Mission Control.
evt-11-02-2000-expedition-1.prompt: What call sign do you request for the new station?

choices.text: Liberty Station
Freedom
Alpha
Mir 2

evt-11-02-2000-expedition-1.butterflyEffect: Shepherd requested the call sign "Alpha," which irritated Russian officials who felt it slighted the legacy of Mir. NASA nonetheless adopted it, and Expedition 1 began an unbroken human presence aboard the ISS that continues decades later.

evt-11-02-2016-chicago-cubs.scenario: It's Game 7 of the 2016 World Series at Cleveland's Progressive Field. Your Cubs have blown a late lead, the rain has just forced a delay before extra innings, and the whole season hangs in the balance.
evt-11-02-2016-chicago-cubs.prompt: What happens in that rain delay that becomes part of Cubs lore?

choices.text: Several players demand the game be postponed to the next day
Jason Heyward gives an emotional speech rallying the team
The front office threatens to trade underperforming players
The manager announces he is pulling the starting pitcher permanently

evt-11-02-2016-chicago-cubs.butterflyEffect: Outfielder Jason Heyward called a players-only meeting in the weight room, rallying a shaken clubhouse. The Cubs scored twice in the 10th, held on to win 8-7, and captured their first championship in 108 years, ending baseball's most famous title drought.

evt-11-02-2020-vienna.scenario: It's the evening of 2 November 2020 in Vienna's Innere Stadt, hours before Austria's second COVID-19 lockdown begins. Gunfire erupts near a synagogue as a lone gunman opens fire on people enjoying a last night out at bars and restaurants.
evt-11-02-2020-vienna.prompt: How do police end the attack?

choices.text: Wait for a specialist unit from Germany
Shoot him dead within minutes
Evacuate the district and let him escape
Negotiate his surrender through hostage talks

evt-11-02-2020-vienna.butterflyEffect: Officers tracked and shot the attacker dead within about nine minutes, though four bystanders had already been killed. He was a young man previously convicted of trying to join ISIL, and the attack pushed Austria to tighten monitoring of released jihadist offenders and deepen counterterrorism cooperation across Europe.

evt-11-02-2022-ethiopia-tigray-peace-agr.scenario: It is November 2, 2022, and you are part of the delegation in Pretoria representing the Tigray People's Liberation Front, two years into a devastating civil war, sitting down with Ethiopian government negotiators under African Union mediation.
evt-11-02-2022-ethiopia-tigray-peace-agr.prompt: What does the agreement require of Tigrayan forces?

choices.text: Indefinite ceasefire with no disarmament required
Cessation of hostilities and disarmament
Deployment of a permanent UN peacekeeping army
Immediate secession of Tigray as an independent state

evt-11-02-2022-ethiopia-tigray-peace-agr.butterflyEffect: The Pretoria Agreement mandated a permanent cessation of hostilities and disarmament of Tigrayan forces alongside restoration of federal authority in the region. It effectively ended a war that had killed and displaced enormous numbers of people, though disputes over contested territory like Western Tigray persisted afterward.

evt-11-03-1534-parliament-of-england.scenario: It is November 1534, and you sit among the members of the House of Commons as the Act of Supremacy comes to a vote. Henry VIII, having broken with a Rome that will not annul his first marriage, wants Parliament to declare him the supreme head of the Church in England.
evt-11-03-1534-parliament-of-england.prompt: How do you cast your vote on the Act of Supremacy?

choices.text: Abstain, hoping to avoid taking a side
Vote to approve, making the king supreme head of the Church of England
Vote to reject it and preserve the Pope's authority over England
Propose a compromise recognizing both Pope and king jointly

evt-11-03-1534-parliament-of-england.butterflyEffect: Parliament passed the Act, formally severing the English Church from papal authority and making the king its supreme head. The break enabled the dissolution of the monasteries and set England on a path toward Protestant reform that would fuel religious conflict for generations.

evt-11-03-1793-french-revolution.scenario: It is 3 November 1793, and you stand before the revolutionary tribunal in Paris. Weeks earlier you published a poster calling for the French people to vote in a referendum on the nation's form of government, a stance the Committee of Public Safety brands as treasonous.
evt-11-03-1793-french-revolution.prompt: What charge does the tribunal use to condemn Olympe de Gouges to the guillotine?

choices.text: Organizing an armed uprising of women in the streets of Paris
Being caught smuggling grain to hoard for profit
Acting as a paid informant for a foreign monarchy
Publishing a pamphlet calling for a referendum, seen as promoting federalism and treason

evt-11-03-1793-french-revolution.butterflyEffect: She was executed for publishing a pamphlet urging a popular referendum on the government's form, which the Terror's leaders treated as an attack on the sovereignty of the people and a sign of federalist sympathies. Her death silenced one of the Revolution's boldest feminist voices, but her earlier Declaration of the Rights of Woman would later become a founding text of modern feminist thought.

evt-11-03-1805-war-of-the-third-coalitio.scenario: It is November 3, 1805, and Tsar Alexander I has traveled to Potsdam to press you, King Frederick William III of Prussia, to abandon neutrality and join Austria and Russia against Napoleon.
evt-11-03-1805-war-of-the-third-coalitio.prompt: What do you agree to under the Treaty of Potsdam?

choices.text: Reaffirm strict neutrality and dismiss the Tsar's request
Sign a treaty conditionally committing Prussia to join the coalition against France
Declare war on France immediately and unconditionally
Refuse and formally ally Prussia with Napoleon instead

evt-11-03-1805-war-of-the-third-coalitio.butterflyEffect: You sign, conditionally committing Prussia to join the coalition if Napoleon rejects a peace ultimatum. But before the ultimatum was even delivered, Napoleon crushed Austria and Russia at Austerlitz, and Prussia's foreign minister quietly shelved the treaty, keeping the kingdom out of the war for another year.

evt-11-03-1812-french-invasion-of-russia.scenario: You march with Napoleon's Grande Armée as it begins its retreat from Moscow in late 1812, with winter closing in and Russian forces harassing your flanks. Napoleon must choose the road home.
evt-11-03-1812-french-invasion-of-russia.prompt: Which route did Napoleon choose for the retreat, and with what result?

choices.text: The same devastated road used on the advance, leaving no supplies
A northern route through allied Prussian territory
A sea evacuation from a captured Black Sea port
A southern route through untouched farmland

evt-11-03-1812-french-invasion-of-russia.butterflyEffect: Napoleon retreated along the same road his army had already stripped bare on the way in, rather than a southern route with untouched supplies. The devastated countryside offered no food or shelter, and starvation, cold, and Cossack raids destroyed most of the Grande Armée before it reached safety.

evt-11-03-1880-kimigayo.scenario: You sit on the Imperial Japanese Household Ministry's music committee in 1880, tasked with replacing the unpopular anthem melody composed by a foreign bandmaster a decade earlier. A new setting of the ancient Kimigayo poem is presented for approval.
evt-11-03-1880-kimigayo.prompt: What happened to this newly adopted melody in the decades that followed?

choices.text: It was banned after World War II and never used again
It was replaced immediately by a version with new lyrics
It became the enduring melody, only formally made law as the anthem in 1999
It was scrapped within a year for a Western-style march

evt-11-03-1880-kimigayo.butterflyEffect: The 1880 melody, arranged with help from German musician Franz Eckert, endured through imperial ceremonies, wartime nationalism, and postwar controversy over its ties to the emperor system. It was not formally codified as Japan's national anthem by law until 1999, over a century after its quiet adoption.

evt-11-03-1898-fashoda-incident.scenario: It is autumn 1898. You are part of a small French expedition that has just planted the tricolour at the remote outpost of Fashoda on the White Nile, only to see British-Egyptian gunboats under Kitchener arrive to challenge your claim.
evt-11-03-1898-fashoda-incident.prompt: Under mounting pressure from London and Paris, what does France ultimately decide to do?

choices.text: Withdraw its forces and abandon the claim
Reinforce the garrison and prepare for war
Propose an immediate partition of Sudan
Appeal to the Ottoman Sultan for arbitration

evt-11-03-1898-fashoda-incident.butterflyEffect: France withdrew its garrison from Fashoda under heavy diplomatic pressure, ceding the Upper Nile to British-Egyptian control. The crisis eased Anglo-French tensions and helped pave the way for the 1904 Entente Cordiale, reshaping the balance of European alliances before World War I.

evt-11-03-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is early November 1942 on Guadalcanal. You are a Marine officer ordered to help encircle a retreating Japanese force under Colonel Shoji near Koli Point before it can reach the rest of the Japanese garrison.
evt-11-03-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: Despite the encirclement effort, what happens to most of Shoji's trapped force?

choices.text: The entire force is captured intact
Most escape through the jungle despite heavy losses
They surrender en masse to Marine patrols
They are all killed in the encirclement

evt-11-03-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Difficult terrain, thick jungle, and coordination problems allowed a large portion of Shoji's force to slip through the American lines, though at heavy cost in men and equipment. The action still weakened Japanese strength on Guadalcanal, contributing to the eventual American victory in the campaign.

evt-11-03-1943-the-holocaust.scenario: It is 3 November 1943 in the Lublin district of occupied Poland. SS units begin a coordinated mass shooting operation at Majdanek and nearby camps, the deadliest single day of killing in the entire Holocaust.
evt-11-03-1943-the-holocaust.prompt: What led the SS to plan this massive, coordinated killing operation at this moment?

choices.text: A shortage of food supplies for prisoners
Fear of further camp uprisings after Sobibor and Treblinka revolts
Direct orders following Allied bombing raids nearby
An outbreak of typhus among the SS guards

evt-11-03-1943-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: Code-named Operation Harvest Festival (Aktion Erntefest), the killings followed the Sobibor uprising and earlier Treblinka revolt, as the SS moved to eliminate remaining Jewish prisoners they feared might resist. Roughly 42,000 people were murdered over two days, effectively ending the Jewish presence in the Lublin district.

evt-11-03-1954-godzilla-1954-film.scenario: You are a special effects technician on Ishirō Honda's 1954 film set at Toho Studios, tasked with bringing a nuclear-mutated monster to life without the budget for Hollywood-style stop-motion.
evt-11-03-1954-godzilla-1954-film.prompt: How did the crew actually create Godzilla's on-screen movement?

choices.text: Hand-drawn animation composited over live actors
A giant hydraulic puppet operated from beneath the set
An actor performed in a rubber suit destroying miniature sets
Frame-by-frame stop-motion animation of a small model

evt-11-03-1954-godzilla-1954-film.butterflyEffect: Eiji Tsuburaya pioneered "suitmation": an actor in a heavy rubber suit smashing through detailed miniature sets. The technique became the visual signature of Japanese kaiju cinema, launching a Godzilla franchise that has run for decades and shaped monster movies worldwide.

evt-11-03-1956-suez-crisis.scenario: You are an Israeli commander whose forces have just seized the Gaza Strip in late October 1956, as British and French bombers strike Egyptian targets under the joint ultimatum. Washington and Moscow are already reacting furiously to the invasion.
evt-11-03-1956-suez-crisis.prompt: What ultimately forced Britain, France, and Israel to withdraw from Egyptian territory?

choices.text: A decisive Egyptian military victory at the canal
An internal coup against Nasser that ended the crisis
Joint US–Soviet pressure and a UN peacekeeping deployment
NATO's refusal to support the operation from the outset

evt-11-03-1956-suez-crisis.butterflyEffect: Intense pressure from both the United States and the Soviet Union, alongside a UN resolution, compelled the withdrawal and led to the deployment of UNEF, the first UN peacekeeping force. The crisis humiliated Britain and France, ended Anthony Eden's premiership, and confirmed the decline of European imperial power in the Middle East.

evt-11-03-1957-sputnik-2.scenario: It is 3 November 1957 in Baikonur, and you are a Soviet engineer watching Sputnik 2 climb into orbit with the dog Laika sealed inside. Mission planners had no way to bring the capsule back down.
evt-11-03-1957-sputnik-2.prompt: What actually happened to Laika after reaching orbit?

choices.text: She never actually flew; a dummy was substituted for the launch
She died within hours from overheating caused by a thermal control failure
She was euthanized painlessly exactly as planned after ten days
She orbited safely for a week and was recovered by parachute

evt-11-03-1957-sputnik-2.butterflyEffect: Soviet officials initially claimed Laika survived several days and was painlessly euthanized, but in 2002 a scientist revealed she died within hours from overheating and stress due to a failed thermal control system. The revelation fueled international debate over animal testing in space and pushed later missions toward better life-support engineering.

evt-11-03-1969-richard-nixon.scenario: It is the evening of 3 November 1969. You sit before your television as President Nixon addresses the nation directly about the war in Vietnam, with anti-war protests mounting across the country.
evt-11-03-1969-richard-nixon.prompt: What does Nixon ask ordinary Americans to do in this address?

choices.text: Join nationwide protests demanding an immediate ceasefire
Support his gradual Vietnamization plan over immediate withdrawal
Back a full-scale invasion of North Vietnam
Support a unilateral declaration of victory

evt-11-03-1969-richard-nixon.butterflyEffect: Nixon appealed to the "great silent majority" of Americans to back his gradual Vietnamization policy rather than the antiwar movement's calls for withdrawal. The speech boosted his approval ratings and blunted momentum from the recent Moratorium protests, while the phrase itself entered lasting political vocabulary.

evt-11-03-1982-1982-salang-tunnel-fire.scenario: You are a Soviet officer on duty inside the Salang Tunnel when a collision between military vehicles ignites fuel and smoke floods the passage. Both entrances are sealed for security reasons, trapping traffic inside with the ventilation offline.
evt-11-03-1982-1982-salang-tunnel-fire.prompt: What critical decision worsened the disaster inside the tunnel?

choices.text: Sealing both entrances for security, trapping vehicles with no ventilation
Opening both entrances too early, letting smoke spread further into the mountains
Rerouting all traffic through a narrower side passage
Ordering an immediate demolition of the tunnel to stop the fire spreading

evt-11-03-1982-1982-salang-tunnel-fire.butterflyEffect: Soviet forces sealed both tunnel entrances fearing an ambush, trapping vehicles inside with no working ventilation. Carbon monoxide and smoke killed far more people than the fire itself, and the disaster became a grim symbol of the war's chaos and poor coordination between Soviet and Afghan forces.

evt-11-03-1986-iran-contra-affair.scenario: You work in the Reagan White House press office in early November 1986 when a small Lebanese magazine, Ash-Shiraa, publishes a story alleging secret US arms sales to Iran to fund Nicaraguan rebels.
evt-11-03-1986-iran-contra-affair.prompt: How did the Reagan administration initially respond to the revelation?

choices.text: Blamed the story entirely on Israeli intelligence leaks
Immediately confirmed every detail and Reagan resigned
Denied the story, then later admitted the operation under mounting pressure
Had the magazine's report legally suppressed in the US

evt-11-03-1986-iran-contra-affair.butterflyEffect: The White House first denied the reports, but mounting evidence forced Reagan to admit the arms sales weeks later and appoint the Tower Commission to investigate. The scandal led to congressional hearings, the conviction of Oliver North, and lasting damage to Reagan's foreign policy credibility even as he remained personally popular.

evt-11-03-1988-sri-lanka.scenario: It's 3 November 1988 in Malé. Armed Sri Lankan Tamil mercenaries have stormed government buildings and you, as President Gayoom, are hiding as they hunt for you.
evt-11-03-1988-sri-lanka.prompt: Who do you urgently call for military help to save your government?

choices.text: Pakistan, which dispatches naval vessels
The United States, which sends in Marines
The Soviet Union, which flies in military advisers
India, which airlifts paratroopers in to crush the coup

evt-11-03-1988-sri-lanka.butterflyEffect: India answered within hours, airlifting paratroopers into Hulhulé airport in what became known as Operation Cactus, and crushed the coup by the next morning. The swift intervention cemented India's role as the Indian Ocean's dominant security guarantor and deepened Malé's reliance on New Delhi.

evt-11-03-1992-arkansas.scenario: It's election night, 3 November 1992. You're watching returns come in across a tense three-way race between the sitting president, the Arkansas governor, and an outspoken Texas businessman running as an independent.
evt-11-03-1992-arkansas.prompt: Which candidate wins the presidency in this three-way contest?

choices.text: George H. W. Bush
Al Gore
Ross Perot
Bill Clinton

evt-11-03-1992-arkansas.butterflyEffect: Bill Clinton won a decisive Electoral College victory, ending twelve consecutive years of Republican control of the White House. His presidency brought NAFTA's ratification, welfare reform, and the first federal budget surpluses in decades, reshaping American politics for the rest of the 1990s.

evt-11-03-1994-space-shuttle-program.scenario: It is 3 November 1994. You are a mission specialist aboard Space Shuttle Atlantis on STS-66, preparing instruments to study Earth's atmosphere as part of the ATLAS-3 payload.
evt-11-03-1994-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What is the primary scientific goal of the ATLAS-3 instruments on this mission?

choices.text: Grow protein crystals in microgravity
Measure atmospheric ozone and solar radiation levels
Deploy a new communications satellite
Test in-orbit satellite repair techniques

evt-11-03-1994-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: ATLAS-3 measured atmospheric ozone, solar radiation, and trace gases, adding to a growing body of data on stratospheric ozone depletion. This research supported international monitoring efforts tied to the Montreal Protocol's push to phase out ozone-depleting substances.

evt-11-03-2002-2002-marib-airstrike.scenario: You are a CIA analyst on November 3, 2002, tracking a vehicle crossing Yemen's Marib desert that intelligence suggests carries Abu Ali al-Harithi, al-Qaeda's top commander in the country.

choices.text: Pass the intelligence to Yemen's government for a later raid
Call off surveillance due to civilian risk in the area
Wait for Yemeni ground forces to intercept the convoy
Authorize a drone strike on the vehicle

evt-11-03-2002-2002-marib-airstrike.butterflyEffect: A Predator drone struck the vehicle, killing al-Harithi and five others. It was the first US drone strike outside a conventional battlefield and the first targeted killing of the war on terror, establishing a template for the expanded drone campaigns of the following decades.

evt-11-03-2014-one-world-trade-center.scenario: It's 3 November 2014, and you step off the elevator into your new office on a high floor of the just-opened tower rising from the rebuilt World Trade Center site in Lower Manhattan.
evt-11-03-2014-one-world-trade-center.prompt: What symbolic height does the building's spire reach, tying it to a historic date?

choices.text: 1,945 feet, marking the end of the Second World War
1,001 feet, echoing the Arabian Nights
1,776 feet, echoing the year of American independence
2,001 feet, marking the year of the September 11 attacks

evt-11-03-2014-one-world-trade-center.butterflyEffect: The tower rises to exactly 1,776 feet, a deliberate reference to the year of the Declaration of Independence. Its completion anchored the redevelopment of Lower Manhattan and stood as the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere, a visible symbol of recovery at the former Ground Zero.

evt-11-03-2020-2020-united-states-presid.scenario: It is the night of November 3, 2020, and you are a campaign volunteer in a Pennsylvania county office, watching election workers continue counting a record wave of mail-in ballots cast during the pandemic.
evt-11-03-2020-2020-united-states-presid.prompt: What happens in the days that follow as counting continues?

choices.text: A prolonged count of mail ballots eventually delivers Biden the presidency days later
The Supreme Court immediately overturns the vote count
Trump concedes gracefully on election night itself
The result is certified for Biden within hours of polls closing

evt-11-03-2020-2020-united-states-presid.butterflyEffect: Biden was not declared the winner until November 7, after mail ballots swung several states his way. Trump refused to concede, launching legal challenges that culminated in the January 6, 2021 attack on the Capitol as Congress met to certify the result.

evt-11-04-1780-tupac-amaru-ii.scenario: It is 1780 in the Peruvian highlands. You are an Aymara or Quechua cacique, and Túpac Amaru II has just declared himself Sapa Inca, calling on you to rise against Spanish colonial rule.
evt-11-04-1780-tupac-amaru-ii.prompt: What ultimately happened to Túpac Amaru II after the rebellion he led?

choices.text: He negotiated a peace treaty and retired to his estate
He was captured and executed by the Spanish
He fled to Chile and continued the fight from exile
He successfully drove the Spanish out of Peru

evt-11-04-1780-tupac-amaru-ii.butterflyEffect: Túpac Amaru II was captured and executed by the Spanish in 1781, his body dismembered as a warning to other would-be rebels. Despite his death, he became a lasting symbol of indigenous resistance, later invoked by independence leaders and 20th-century indigenous rights movements across South America.

evt-11-04-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: On November 4, 1864, you command the Union supply depot at Johnsonville, Tennessee, as Nathan Bedford Forrest's cavalry and artillery suddenly appear across the Tennessee River, opening fire on your gunboats, transports, and warehouses.
evt-11-04-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: With the depot indefensible, what do you order to keep the supplies from Forrest's hands?

choices.text: Evacuate everything intact by rail before Forrest can advance
Surrender the depot and its supplies to Forrest's forces
Burn the gunboats and warehouses to deny them to Forrest
Ferry troops across the river to storm Forrest's artillery

evt-11-04-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Union officers set fire to their own gunboats, transports, and warehouses rather than let them be captured, destroying an estimated several million dollars in Union supplies. It stands as one of the war's most successful cavalry-and-artillery raids on a fixed base, though it did not stop Sherman's larger campaign toward Savannah.

evt-11-04-1890-city-and-south-london-rai.scenario: You stand on the platform at King William Street station in London, 1890, waiting for the maiden run of a new underground line built deep beneath the city streets.
evt-11-04-1890-city-and-south-london-rai.prompt: What technology actually powers these pioneering trains?

choices.text: Horse-drawn carriages
Electric locomotives
Cable-hauled carriages
Steam locomotives

evt-11-04-1890-city-and-south-london-rai.butterflyEffect: The line's cable contractor went bankrupt during construction, forcing engineers to adopt electric traction instead—an experimental technology at the time. The City and South London Railway became the world's first successful deep-level electric tube railway, setting the template for underground systems worldwide.

evt-11-04-1912-keel.scenario: On November 4, 1912, at the Fore River Shipyard in Massachusetts, workers lay the keel of a new U.S. Navy battleship, USS Nevada, designed around a radical new philosophy for protecting a warship's vitals.
evt-11-04-1912-keel.prompt: What revolutionary armor concept does Nevada introduce to American battleship design?

choices.text: An "all-or-nothing" scheme concentrating armor only over vital areas
A sloped "turtleback" armor deck copied from French designs
A continuous belt of uniform medium-thickness armor along the whole hull
No armor belt at all, relying purely on speed for protection

evt-11-04-1912-keel.butterflyEffect: Nevada's "all-or-nothing" armor scheme concentrated heavy protection only over vital areas—magazines, engines, turrets—leaving the rest of the hull thin, rather than spreading armor evenly. Combined with her new oil-fired boilers, the concept became the template for every subsequent U.S. battleship through World War II.

evt-11-04-1921-tomb-of-the-unknown-soldi.scenario: It is 1921 in Aquileia, Italy. You are Maria Bergamas, a mother who lost her son in the Great War and never recovered his body. Eleven identical caskets of unidentified soldiers stand before you, and you alone must choose one to represent all of Italy's fallen.
evt-11-04-1921-tomb-of-the-unknown-soldi.prompt: What did Maria Bergamas do, and what became of her choice?

choices.text: She selected one casket, which was buried at the Altare della Patria
She insisted all eleven bodies be buried together
She refused to choose, so officials selected one at random
She identified her own son among the remains

evt-11-04-1921-tomb-of-the-unknown-soldi.butterflyEffect: She collapsed before one casket, choosing it by instinct and grief rather than knowledge. That soldier's remains were carried to Rome and interred beneath the Altare della Patria, where an eternal flame still burns as a national monument to Italy's war dead.

evt-11-04-1922-tomb-of-tutankhamun.scenario: It is 4 November 1922 in the Valley of the Kings, and your workmen have just uncovered a hidden staircase leading to a sealed doorway bearing royal seals. Your financial backer, Lord Carnarvon, is still in England.
evt-11-04-1922-tomb-of-tutankhamun.prompt: What did Howard Carter do upon finding the sealed entrance?

choices.text: Broke the seal immediately and entered alone that night
Dynamited the doorway to speed up excavation
Reburied the staircase and waited for Lord Carnarvon to arrive from England
Alerted the Egyptian government, which sealed off the site for years

evt-11-04-1922-tomb-of-tutankhamun.butterflyEffect: Carter reburied the top of the staircase to protect it and sent word to Lord Carnarvon in England, waiting nearly three weeks before Carnarvon arrived so they could open the tomb together.
