The eventual discovery of Tutankhamun's largely intact treasures triggered a worldwide craze for Egyptian art and design that reshaped 1920s fashion, architecture, and film.

evt-11-04-1924-1924-wyoming-gubernatoria.scenario: It is November 4, 1924, in Wyoming. Governor William B. Ross died in office weeks ago, and now his widow, Nellie Tayloe Ross, is on the ballot against Republican E. J. Sullivan in the special election to finish his term.
evt-11-04-1924-1924-wyoming-gubernatoria.prompt: What does the electorate do, making history in the process?

choices.text: Elect Republican E. J. Sullivan by a comfortable margin
Reject both candidates and demand a new special election
Elect Nellie Tayloe Ross, making her the nation's first female governor
Split so evenly the legislature must decide the outcome

evt-11-04-1924-1924-wyoming-gubernatoria.butterflyEffect: Nellie Tayloe Ross defeated Sullivan and became the first woman ever to serve as governor of a U.S. state. She later became the first woman to head the U.S. Mint, and her win became a landmark reference point for women seeking executive office nationwide.

evt-11-04-1964-ruhollah-khomeini.scenario: You are an aide to Ayatollah Khomeini in Qom, November 1964. He has just been seized by SAVAK agents for denouncing the Shah's reforms and the law granting legal immunity to American personnel in Iran.
evt-11-04-1964-ruhollah-khomeini.prompt: What happens to Khomeini after his arrest?

choices.text: He is placed under house arrest in Qom
He is imprisoned in Tehran indefinitely
He is exiled to Turkey
He is executed for sedition

evt-11-04-1964-ruhollah-khomeini.butterflyEffect: He was exiled to Bursa, Turkey, then relocated in 1965 to Najaf, Iraq, where he spent over a decade developing his theory of Islamic governance and organizing opposition abroad. He returned to Iran in 1979 to lead the revolution that toppled the Shah.

evt-11-04-1970-feral-child.scenario: It is November 1970 in Los Angeles, and social workers have just found a 13-year-old girl who has spent most of her life confined and deprived of language. Linguists and psychologists quickly take an interest in her case.
evt-11-04-1970-feral-child.prompt: What scientific question did researchers hope her case would help answer?

choices.text: Whether children could survive without any human contact at all
Whether isolation permanently damaged a child's eyesight
Whether language could still be fully learned after the presumed critical period
Whether feral children retained memories of animal caregivers

evt-11-04-1970-feral-child.butterflyEffect: Researchers used her case to test the critical period hypothesis, the idea that language must be acquired before puberty or never fully mastered. She learned some vocabulary but never developed normal grammar, seeming to support the hypothesis, though later critics argued her prolonged abuse and shifting research team made the study scientifically and ethically flawed.

evt-11-04-1979-iran-hostage-crisis.scenario: It is 4 November 1979, and you are inside the U.S. Embassy in Tehran as hundreds of student militants scale the walls, chanting and demanding the return of the deposed Shah for trial.
evt-11-04-1979-iran-hostage-crisis.prompt: What did the United States attempt months later to free the hostages?

choices.text: Secured release within a week through direct UN mediation
Launched airstrikes on Tehran to force a release
Immediately traded the Shah for the hostages' release
Attempted a covert helicopter rescue mission that failed in the Iranian desert

evt-11-04-1979-iran-hostage-crisis.butterflyEffect: In April 1980 the U.S. launched Operation Eagle Claw, a covert helicopter rescue mission that collapsed in the desert after equipment failures and a fatal collision, killing eight servicemen and humiliating the Carter administration. The failure deepened the crisis, damaged Carter's re-election chances, and left the hostages held until January 1981.

evt-11-04-1995-yitzhak-rabin.scenario: It is the evening of 4 November 1995 in Tel Aviv's Kings of Israel Square. You have just watched Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin address a massive rally in support of the Oslo peace process before he heads toward his car.
evt-11-04-1995-yitzhak-rabin.prompt: What followed Rabin's departure from the rally that night?

choices.text: He signed a final peace agreement with Yasser Arafat
He was assassinated by a right-wing Israeli extremist
He announced his resignation from office
He survived an assassination attempt unharmed

evt-11-04-1995-yitzhak-rabin.butterflyEffect: Rabin was shot and killed by Yigal Amir, a far-right Israeli extremist opposed to the Oslo Accords. His death shocked Israel, stalled momentum for the peace process, and contributed to Benjamin Netanyahu's narrow election victory the following year.

evt-11-04-2008-barack-obama.scenario: It is the night of 4 November 2008. You are a volunteer in Chicago's Grant Park, watching a jumbotron as state results roll in from a tense, closely-watched presidential race.
evt-11-04-2008-barack-obama.prompt: What does the crowd learn as the final results come in?

choices.text: Obama wins but McCain contests the result in court
Obama wins, becoming the first African American president-elect
McCain wins a narrow victory
The election is too close to call and heads to recount

evt-11-04-2008-barack-obama.butterflyEffect: Obama defeated John McCain decisively, becoming the first African American president-elect in US history. His election, amid the 2008 financial crisis, reshaped American politics and inspired global attention to questions of race and representation in leadership.

evt-11-04-2015-2015-juba-antonov-an-12-c.scenario: At dawn on November 4, 2015, ground crew at Juba International Airport finish loading an aging Antonov An-12 cargo plane, already packed with freight and extra passengers, for a flight over the White Nile.
evt-11-04-2015-2015-juba-antonov-an-12-c.prompt: What factor investigators later pointed to in the plane's fatal loss of altitude after takeoff?

choices.text: A lightning strike set the fuel tanks alight mid-climb
An explosive device detonated in the cargo hold
The aircraft was loaded well beyond its safe weight limit
A bird strike disabled both engines on takeoff

evt-11-04-2015-2015-juba-antonov-an-12-c.butterflyEffect: The An-12, carrying far more weight than it was rated for, could not climb and crashed into the river shortly after liftoff, killing at least 37 people. The disaster drew fresh scrutiny to South Sudan's fragile aviation sector, still dependent on aging Soviet-era cargo aircraft and lax weight enforcement.

evt-11-04-2016-paris-agreement.scenario: It is 4 November 2016, and you are a UN climate official watching the Paris Agreement finally take legal force, more than a year after it was negotiated outside Paris.
evt-11-04-2016-paris-agreement.prompt: What condition had to be met before the agreement could enter into force?

choices.text: Unanimous ratification by every UN member state
Approval by the five permanent UN Security Council members only
A binding vote in the U.S. Senate ratifying the treaty
Ratification by 55 countries covering at least 55% of global emissions

evt-11-04-2016-paris-agreement.butterflyEffect: The treaty required ratification by at least 55 countries responsible for at least 55% of global greenhouse gas emissions, a threshold reached in October 2016 when the EU ratified. Barely a year later the newly elected U.S. president announced America's withdrawal, foreshadowing a pattern of U.S. exits and re-entries that would recur under later administrations.

evt-11-04-2020-tigray-war.scenario: You are a regional official in Mekelle, early November 2020. Relations between Tigray's government and Addis Ababa have collapsed after disputed elections and federal troop movements near the border.
evt-11-04-2020-tigray-war.prompt: What triggers the outbreak of full-scale war in these first days of November?

choices.text: The federal government launches airstrikes first
Eritrea invades Tigray unprovoked
UN peacekeepers withdraw from the region
Tigrayan forces attack federal army command centers

evt-11-04-2020-tigray-war.butterflyEffect: Tigrayan forces attacked federal army bases housing the Northern Command, prompting Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed to launch a full military offensive, soon joined by Eritrean troops. The resulting two-year civil war devastated the region before a peace agreement was signed in November 2022.

evt-11-05-1556-second-battle-of-panipat.scenario: It is 5 November 1556 at Panipat, and the wounded rival king Hemu has just been dragged before the young emperor Akbar and his regent Bairam Khan after the battle turns decisively against him.
evt-11-05-1556-second-battle-of-panipat.prompt: What did Bairam Khan urge, and what actually became of Hemu?

choices.text: Hemu was spared and made a Mughal vassal
Hemu escaped captivity and rebuilt his army
Hemu was executed after Bairam Khan urged Akbar to strike him down
Hemu was exchanged for Mughal prisoners

evt-11-05-1556-second-battle-of-panipat.butterflyEffect: Bairam Khan pressed Akbar to strike the killing blow himself; Akbar reportedly touched his sword to Hemu's neck, and Bairam Khan then beheaded him. Hemu's death ended his brief bid to restore Hindu rule in Delhi and secured the throne for Akbar, allowing the Mughal dynasty to dominate northern India for the next two centuries.

evt-11-05-1605-gunpowder-plot.scenario: It is 26 October 1605. You are William Parker, 4th Baron Monteagle, and an anonymous letter has just arrived warning you to stay away from Parliament's opening, hinting at a 'terrible blow' with no visible enemy.
evt-11-05-1605-gunpowder-plot.prompt: What did Monteagle do with the warning letter?

choices.text: He showed it to the authorities, triggering a search of Parliament
He fled London fearing he was the target
He burned it and told no one
He confronted Robert Catesby directly

evt-11-05-1605-gunpowder-plot.butterflyEffect: He handed it to the authorities, prompting a search of the House of Lords that uncovered Guy Fawkes guarding 36 barrels of gunpowder. The plot's failure led to the execution of the conspirators and gave England the enduring tradition of Bonfire Night, still marked every 5 November.

evt-11-05-1757-seven-years-war.scenario: It is 5 November 1757 near Rossbach, and you command a wing of the large Franco-Imperial army, watching what seems like a small, retreating Prussian force on the horizon.
evt-11-05-1757-seven-years-war.prompt: What actually happened when Frederick's cavalry struck your marching columns?

choices.text: The two armies fought to a costly draw
Prussian cavalry ambushed the marching columns and routed the much larger army
French artillery broke the Prussian line before infantry could engage
The Prussians retreated as expected, giving up the field

evt-11-05-1757-seven-years-war.butterflyEffect: Prussian cavalry under Friedrich von Seydlitz smashed into the Franco-Imperial army's flank while it was still marching in column, routing a force nearly three times Prussia's size in barely half an hour. The lopsided victory shattered French confidence in the campaign and cemented Frederick's reputation as Europe's most formidable tactical commander.

evt-11-05-1854-crimean-war.scenario: It is dawn on 5 November 1854 near Inkerman, and a thick fog blankets the heights above Sevastopol. A massive Russian force is pressing forward, and your understrength British division cannot see more than a few yards, let alone coordinate with neighboring units.
evt-11-05-1854-crimean-war.prompt: How do the outnumbered British and French troops manage to hold the line?

choices.text: French reinforcements arrive before dawn and turn the tide immediately
Naval gunfire from ships in the harbor disperses the Russian columns
A surprise cavalry charge from reserve breaks the Russian advance
Isolated groups of junior officers improvise attacks in the fog without central direction

evt-11-05-1854-crimean-war.butterflyEffect: The Battle of Inkerman became known as the 'Soldiers' Battle' because the fog made central command impossible, forcing small groups of officers and men to fight isolated, improvised actions that collectively repelled the much larger Russian assault. The costly Allied victory secured the siege of Sevastopol but exposed the exhausted, disease-ridden state of the armies, fueling public outrage back home over military mismanagement.

evt-11-05-1916-everett-massacre.scenario: It is 5 November 1916, and you stand aboard the steamer Verona, packed with IWW members sailing into Everett's harbor to support striking shingle workers, as armed men wait on the dock.
evt-11-05-1916-everett-massacre.prompt: What happened when the boat reached the dock and gunfire broke out?

choices.text: Local police escorted the Wobblies safely into town
The confrontation ended with no casualties on either side
The Wobblies surrendered peacefully before any shots were fired
Gunfire killed men on both sides, and the surviving Wobblies were later acquitted at trial

evt-11-05-1916-everett-massacre.butterflyEffect: Shots exchanged between deputies on the dock and Wobblies on the Verona left several men dead on both sides. Authorities charged 74 IWW members with murder, but a Seattle jury acquitted the lead defendant in 1917, and the case became a rallying point that strengthened labor organizing across the Pacific Northwest.

evt-11-05-1950-korean-war.scenario: It is 5 November 1950 near Pakchon, North Korea. Massive Chinese forces have entered the war and are pressing hard against retreating UN troops. You serve with the 27th British Commonwealth Brigade, ordered to hold a blocking position while other units withdraw.
evt-11-05-1950-korean-war.prompt: What does the brigade do to stop the Chinese advance from overwhelming the retreat?

choices.text: It launches an immediate counter-offensive deep into Chinese-held territory
It digs in and fights a stubborn defensive action to cover the withdrawal
It calls in a full-scale air strike and evacuates before Chinese troops arrive
It abandons its position and retreats without engaging

evt-11-05-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: The 27th British Commonwealth Brigade, including Australian and Scottish battalions, fought a fierce delaying action that blunted the Chinese assault and allowed other UN forces to withdraw in order. The action was one of several early clashes revealing the scale of Chinese intervention, forcing UN commanders to abandon hopes of a quick victory and rethink strategy for the rest of the war.

evt-11-05-1952-1952-severo-kurilsk-earth.scenario: It is just before 5am on 5 November 1952 in Severo-Kurilsk. The ground has just stopped shaking violently, and you can hear the sea beginning to roar and pull back from the shore in an unnatural way.
evt-11-05-1952-1952-severo-kurilsk-earth.prompt: What is the safest action to take right now?

choices.text: Go back to sleep since the worst has passed
Run inland and uphill to high ground immediately
Gather valuables and documents before leaving
Wait at home for an official siren or announcement

evt-11-05-1952-1952-severo-kurilsk-earth.butterflyEffect: Waves up to 18 meters high struck the town within half an hour, destroying it and killing thousands across the Kuril Islands and Kamchatka. Soviet authorities suppressed news of the disaster for decades, but it eventually led the USSR to build a Pacific tsunami warning network.

evt-11-05-1990-ultranationalism.scenario: It is the evening of 5 November 1990 in a Manhattan hotel ballroom. Rabbi Meir Kahane has just finished addressing a crowd of supporters when a man steps forward from the audience.

choices.text: A bomb hidden in the podium detonates
The man produces a pistol and shoots Kahane at close range
The man hands Kahane a threatening letter and flees
The man attempts to stab Kahane but is restrained by security

evt-11-05-1990-ultranationalism.butterflyEffect: El Sayyid Nosair shot Kahane dead at close range and was later acquitted of murder, though convicted of related weapons charges. Evidence found in Nosair's home linked him to a wider militant network, and he was later convicted for his role in the 1993 World Trade Center bombing conspiracy, making the Kahane assassination an early thread in the story of Islamist terrorism in the United States.

evt-11-05-1996-president-of-pakistan.scenario: You are a government official in Islamabad on 5 November 1996 as President Farooq Leghari goes on national radio to announce he is dissolving the National Assembly and dismissing Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government over corruption allegations.
evt-11-05-1996-president-of-pakistan.prompt: What constitutional power does the president invoke to dismiss the elected government?

choices.text: A parliamentary vote of no confidence
Article 58(2)(b) of the Eighth Amendment
A declaration of martial law by the army chief
An emergency ruling by the Supreme Court

evt-11-05-1996-president-of-pakistan.butterflyEffect: Leghari used Article 58(2)(b) of the Eighth Amendment, the same clause used twice before against elected governments in the early 1990s. A caretaker administration called fresh elections, bringing Nawaz Sharif to power in 1997, whose government soon repealed the clause via the Thirteenth Amendment.

evt-11-05-2006-saddam-hussein.scenario: You sit in the courtroom in Baghdad on 5 November 2006 as the Iraqi High Tribunal prepares to announce its verdict against former president Saddam Hussein for the 1982 killings in the town of Dujail.
evt-11-05-2006-saddam-hussein.prompt: What verdict and sentence does the tribunal hand down?

choices.text: Guilty, sentenced to life imprisonment
Acquitted of all charges
Sentenced to exile abroad
Guilty, sentenced to death by hanging

evt-11-05-2006-saddam-hussein.butterflyEffect: Saddam Hussein was sentenced to death by hanging and executed on 30 December 2006. The trial and execution drew international criticism over fairness and procedure, and deepened sectarian tensions in Iraq at the height of the insurgency following the US-led invasion.

evt-11-05-2007-chang-e-1.scenario: It is 5 November 2007, and you are a flight controller in Beijing tracking Chang'e 1 as it closes in on the Moon after a two-week journey from Earth.
evt-11-05-2007-chang-e-1.prompt: What must the probe do now to be captured into lunar orbit instead of flying past?

choices.text: Deploy a parachute to reduce its speed
Release a lander immediately while still moving at full speed
Accelerate further to escape into a higher solar orbit
Fire its main engine to slow down and be captured by lunar gravity

evt-11-05-2007-chang-e-1.butterflyEffect: Chang'e 1 fired its engine to brake and successfully entered lunar orbit, making China only the third nation to independently orbit the Moon. The mission's success launched the multi-phase Chinese Lunar Exploration Program, leading to the Chang'e 3 and 4 landers and the Chang'e 5 sample-return mission.

evt-11-05-2009-united-states-army.scenario: It is November 5, 2009, inside the Soldier Readiness Processing Center at Fort Hood, Texas. Soldiers preparing for deployment overseas are suddenly caught in gunfire from one of their own officers.
evt-11-05-2009-united-states-army.prompt: How did the Pentagon officially classify the attack in the years that followed, sparking controversy?

choices.text: Workplace violence
An isolated mental health incident
An act of terrorism
A hate crime

evt-11-05-2009-united-states-army.butterflyEffect: The Army labeled the shooting 'workplace violence' rather than terrorism, which denied wounded soldiers combat-related benefits and Purple Hearts for years. After sustained pressure, Congress and the Army reversed course in 2015, awarding Purple Hearts to victims. Nidal Hasan was convicted by court-martial in 2013 and sentenced to death.

evt-11-05-2009-nidal-hasan.scenario: It is 5 November 2009 at Fort Hood's Soldier Readiness Processing Center. An Army psychiatrist has just opened fire on fellow soldiers preparing for deployment, and the shooting is still ongoing when responders arrive.
evt-11-05-2009-nidal-hasan.prompt: What ultimately brings the attack to an end?

choices.text: He runs out of ammunition and surrenders
Police officers arrive and shoot him, ending the rampage
He is talked down by a chaplain called to the scene
He is overpowered unarmed by nearby soldiers

evt-11-05-2009-nidal-hasan.butterflyEffect: Civilian police officer Kimberly Munley and Sergeant Mark Todd engaged and wounded Hasan, ending the attack. Hasan survived, was later court-martialed and sentenced to death in 2013, and the case intensified scrutiny of the military's handling of warning signs and its screening for extremist ideology among service members.

evt-11-05-2013-mars-orbiter-mission.scenario: You are an ISRO engineer at Sriharikota on 5 November 2013, watching the PSLV rocket lift off carrying India's first interplanetary probe, nicknamed Mangalyaan, on a long journey toward the red planet.
evt-11-05-2013-mars-orbiter-mission.prompt: What historic milestone is this mission attempting to achieve for India?

choices.text: Become the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit
Launch India's first crewed spaceflight
Deploy India's first geostationary weather satellite
Land the first rover on the Martian surface

evt-11-05-2013-mars-orbiter-mission.butterflyEffect: Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit on 24 September 2014, making India the fourth space agency to succeed and the first nation to do so on its maiden attempt with an indigenous propulsion system. The mission's low cost and success boosted global confidence in ISRO, paving the way for later ambitions like Chandrayaan lunar landings.

evt-11-05-2015-iron-ore.scenario: It is 5 November 2015 in Bento Rodrigues, Minas Gerais, and a wall of mining waste is roaring down the valley toward your village after the Fundão tailings dam gives way upstream.
evt-11-05-2015-iron-ore.prompt: What did the collapse ultimately unleash downstream along the Rio Doce?

choices.text: The dam breach only affected mining company property, not nearby towns
The waste was contained within a few kilometers of the dam
The spill was cleaned up within days with no lasting effects
Toxic mining waste traveled the length of the Rio Doce to the ocean, causing lasting contamination

evt-11-05-2015-iron-ore.butterflyEffect: Roughly 40 million cubic meters of iron-ore waste buried Bento Rodrigues and killed 19 people, then travelled hundreds of kilometers down the Rio Doce to the Atlantic, poisoning water supplies and ecosystems along the way. It became Brazil's worst environmental disaster, forcing mining giant Samarco and its owners Vale and BHP into billions of dollars in reparations and stricter dam-safety regulation.

evt-11-05-2015-rona-ambrose.scenario: It is early November 2015, days after the Conservatives lost the federal election that ended nearly a decade of Stephen Harper's government. Harper has stepped down as party leader, leaving the caucus needing someone to steer them until a permanent successor is chosen.
evt-11-05-2015-rona-ambrose.prompt: What position does Rona Ambrose take on within the Conservative Party?

choices.text: Candidate in an immediate by-election for a new seat
Interim leader until a permanent leader is elected
Permanent leader elected outright by the caucus
Prime Minister in a caretaker government

evt-11-05-2015-rona-ambrose.butterflyEffect: Ambrose became interim leader of the Conservative Party, the first woman to hold the post, steering the opposition until Andrew Scheer won the permanent leadership in 2017. Her steady tenure helped stabilize the party after its election defeat and kept it competitive in Parliament during the transition.

evt-11-05-2021-astroworld-festival-crowd.scenario: It is November 5, 2021, and you are a fan pressed shoulder to shoulder near the front of the stage at NRG Park in Houston as Travis Scott performs, the crowd surging forward with nowhere to move.
evt-11-05-2021-astroworld-festival-crowd.prompt: What was the outcome of the criminal investigation into the festival's organizers and performer?

choices.text: Live Nation executives were criminally charged
Travis Scott was indicted for manslaughter
A grand jury declined to bring criminal charges against anyone involved
The festival's promoters were banned from producing events

evt-11-05-2021-astroworld-festival-crowd.butterflyEffect: A Harris County grand jury declined to indict Travis Scott, promoter Live Nation, or any other organizer, closing the criminal case in June 2023. Hundreds of civil lawsuits followed, resulting in settlements, and the tragedy prompted a wider industry reckoning over crowd density and festival safety planning.

evt-11-06-1217-henry-iii-of-england.scenario: You are a free tenant in an English shire in 1217, long burdened by harsh forest laws that criminalize gathering firewood or grazing livestock on royal land. Word spreads that the young king's regents have issued a new charter alongside Magna Carta.
evt-11-06-1217-henry-iii-of-england.prompt: What did the Charter of the Forest change for people like you?

choices.text: It imposes new taxes on anyone entering a royal forest
It grants trial by jury for all forest offences for the first time
It restores rights to graze animals and gather food and wood in royal forests
It abolishes the monarchy's ownership of all forests immediately

evt-11-06-1217-henry-iii-of-england.butterflyEffect: The Charter of the Forest rolled back Norman-era forest law, decriminalizing common activities like grazing and gathering wood and shrinking the royal forest's reach. Issued as a companion to Magna Carta, it became a cornerstone of English common law protecting shared land rights, and its principles echo in later ideas about the commons and public access.

evt-11-06-1856-scenes-of-clerical-life.scenario: It is 1857, and Mary Ann Evans has just finished 'The Sad Fortunes of the Reverend Amos Barton' for serialization in Blackwood's Magazine. As a woman writing fiction in a market skeptical of female novelists, she must decide how to present her name.
evt-11-06-1856-scenes-of-clerical-life.prompt: Under what name does she submit her first work of fiction for publication?

choices.text: Her own name, Mary Ann Evans
Her married name, Mrs. Lewes
The pseudonym George Eliot
No name at all, published fully anonymously with no attribution

evt-11-06-1856-scenes-of-clerical-life.butterflyEffect: She adopted the pseudonym 'George Eliot,' shielding her identity as a woman and avoiding scandal over her relationship with George Henry Lewes. The name stuck through Adam Bede, The Mill on the Floss, and Middlemarch, becoming one of the most famous pen names in English literature.

evt-11-06-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It's 6 November 1863 in the mountains of West Virginia. You lead a Union brigade under General William Averell, facing Confederate troops dug into the high, wooded slopes of Droop Mountain.
evt-11-06-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: Do you order a direct frontal assault or send troops to flank the Confederate line?

choices.text: Charge straight up the slope into the Confederate works
Attempt to negotiate the garrison's surrender
Send a column to turn the Confederate flank on the mountain
Withdraw and wait for reinforcements from Ohio

evt-11-06-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Averell's men flanked and broke the Confederate left, routing General Echols's force from the mountain. The victory shattered organized Confederate resistance in West Virginia for the rest of the war, cementing the state's hold for the Union.

evt-11-06-1868-red-cloud.scenario: It's 6 November 1868 at Fort Laramie. The US Army has abandoned its forts along the Bozeman Trail as you demanded, and officials now press you to put your mark on the treaty ending the war you have won.

choices.text: You demand the forts be rebuilt before signing
You sign but reject the reservation terms outright
You sign the Fort Laramie Treaty, ending Red Cloud's War
You refuse to sign and continue fighting

evt-11-06-1868-red-cloud.butterflyEffect: Red Cloud signed the Fort Laramie Treaty, ending the only war in which the United States formally conceded defeat to a Native nation and creating the Great Sioux Reservation, including the Black Hills. That peace unraveled after gold was discovered in the Black Hills in 1874, provoking the Great Sioux War of 1876.

evt-11-06-1900-william-mckinley.scenario: It's 1900 and you're a Republican strategist helping President McKinley shore up his re-election ticket after the death of his first vice president, weighing a bold but restless young New York governor as the new running mate.
evt-11-06-1900-william-mckinley.prompt: Which reform-minded governor joins McKinley's ticket and wins the vice presidency?

choices.text: Charles Fairbanks, senator from Indiana
Garret Hobart, the outgoing vice president
Mark Hanna, McKinley's chief political advisor
Theodore Roosevelt, governor of New York

evt-11-06-1900-william-mckinley.butterflyEffect: Theodore Roosevelt was chosen and elected vice president alongside McKinley. When McKinley was assassinated in September 1901, Roosevelt became the youngest president in U.S. history, launching the trust-busting, conservationist Progressive Era presidency that followed.

evt-11-06-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It's early November 1917 near Ypres. As commander of the Canadian Corps, you've been ordered to seize the shattered village of Passchendaele from its sea of mud and shell craters, though the cost in men has already been staggering.
evt-11-06-1917-world-war-i.prompt: Do you press the assault as ordered or press Haig to halt the offensive?

choices.text: Request that a fresh British division take over the attack
Negotiate a local truce with the German defenders
Press the costly assault using careful bite-and-hold tactics
Refuse the order and withdraw the Corps from the line

evt-11-06-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Currie pressed forward and Canadian troops captured Passchendaele village on 6 November 1917, finally securing Haig's objective and ending the Third Battle of Ypres. The horrific casualties for minimal strategic gain made the battle a lasting symbol of attritional warfare's futility.

evt-11-06-1936-spanish-civil-war.scenario: It's 6 November 1936 in Madrid. Franco's Nationalist columns are closing on the capital, and as a minister in the Republican government you must decide the seat of government's fate while militia and International Brigade volunteers dig in to defend the streets.
evt-11-06-1936-spanish-civil-war.prompt: Do you evacuate the government to Valencia and let Madrid's defenders fight on, or stay and lead the defense yourself?

choices.text: Remain in Madrid and personally command its defense
Surrender the capital to avoid further bloodshed
Relocate the government to Valencia while Madrid's defenders hold the line
Move the government north to Bilbao instead

evt-11-06-1936-spanish-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The government relocated to Valencia while General Miaja organized Madrid's defense, rallying behind the cry '¡No pasarán!'. The capital held out for the rest of 1936 and beyond, becoming an international symbol of anti-fascist resistance and prolonging the war for years.

evt-11-06-1939-intelligenzaktion.scenario: It is autumn 1939 in newly occupied western Poland, and you are a schoolteacher hearing that German occupation authorities are compiling lists of priests, professors, and officials for arrest.
evt-11-06-1939-intelligenzaktion.prompt: What is the Nazi occupiers' underlying goal behind these mass arrests of the intelligentsia?

choices.text: To relocate them to form a collaborationist Polish government
To conscript them as officers into the German army
To recruit skilled workers for German war factories
To eliminate Polish leadership and enable Germanization of the annexed lands

evt-11-06-1939-intelligenzaktion.butterflyEffect: The Intelligenzaktion aimed to destroy Poland's educated leadership class so the annexed territories could be more easily Germanized, with thousands of teachers, clergy, and officials murdered in mass shootings. The loss of this generation of leaders crippled organized resistance in the short term and left a lasting scar on Poland's postwar intellectual and professional class.

evt-11-06-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 6 November 1943. You march with the 1st Ukrainian Front toward Kyiv, the advance deliberately timed by Moscow to reach the city before the anniversary of the Bolshevik Revolution.
evt-11-06-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What happens as Soviet forces enter Kyiv?

choices.text: German forces retake the city within days
Kyiv remains besieged for another six months
The city surrenders without any prior fighting
Kyiv is liberated from German occupation

evt-11-06-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Kyiv was liberated from over two years of German occupation, a victory timed for maximum propaganda value on the eve of the revolution's anniversary. The recapture opened the way for further Soviet advances into western Ukraine, though the city bore the scars of occupation for years afterward.

evt-11-06-1944-b-reactor.scenario: It is September 1944 at the Hanford Site in Washington State. You are part of the crew bringing the newly built B Reactor to full power to begin producing plutonium for the Manhattan Project.
evt-11-06-1944-b-reactor.prompt: How do engineers keep the graphite-moderated reactor from overheating during operation?

choices.text: Cool it with large banks of electric fans
Continuously cool it with water drawn from the Columbia River
Circulate liquid sodium through the reactor core
Rely on natural convection with no active cooling

evt-11-06-1944-b-reactor.butterflyEffect: B Reactor ran on an open cooling loop drawing water from the Columbia River, and the plutonium it produced was used in the Trinity test and the bomb dropped on Nagasaki. The reactor's legacy also included decades of radioactive contamination that made Hanford one of the most polluted sites in the United States, driving a massive ongoing cleanup effort.

evt-11-06-1963-nguyen-ngoc-tho.scenario: It is 6 November 1963 in Saigon, two weeks after Diệm's assassination. General Dương Văn Minh's junta needs a civilian face for the new government, and as former vice president you are asked to head the cabinet.
evt-11-06-1963-nguyen-ngoc-tho.prompt: What follows your appointment as head of the civilian cabinet?

choices.text: The United States withdraws all support from the new government
You are overthrown within days of taking office
Real power stays with the military junta while your cabinet struggles for authority
You consolidate full civilian control and sideline the generals

evt-11-06-1963-nguyen-ngoc-tho.butterflyEffect: Real authority stayed with the Military Revolutionary Council, and Thơ's cabinet struggled against it in a period of confusion. In January 1964, General Nguyễn Khánh deposed Minh's junta in a coup, ending Thơ's brief tenure and beginning a cycle of coups that destabilized South Vietnam for years.

evt-11-06-1971-united-states-atomic-ener.scenario: It is 6 November 1971 on Amchitka Island, Alaska. Environmental groups have just exhausted their legal challenge, and the Atomic Energy Commission is set to detonate its largest underground hydrogen bomb test.
evt-11-06-1971-united-states-atomic-ener.prompt: What does the Supreme Court decide on the eve of the test?

choices.text: It halts the test indefinitely on environmental grounds
It allows the Cannikin test to proceed by a narrow vote
It requires new congressional approval before testing
It orders the test relocated to Nevada

evt-11-06-1971-united-states-atomic-ener.butterflyEffect: The Court allowed the roughly 5-megaton Cannikin test to proceed, the largest underground nuclear test the US ever conducted. The controversy over the blast's environmental risks helped galvanize the emerging anti-nuclear movement, feeding into organizations that grew directly out of opposition to Amchitka testing.

evt-11-06-1977-kelly-barnes-dam.scenario: It's early November 1977 outside Toccoa, Georgia. Days of relentless rain have soaked the aging earthen Kelly Barnes Dam sitting upstream of a Bible college campus, a structure that has never been formally inspected since it was patched decades earlier.
evt-11-06-1977-kelly-barnes-dam.prompt: What happened when the saturated dam finally gave way?

choices.text: It held, though the spillway overflowed harmlessly
Engineers reinforced it just before failure occurred
The water was safely diverted into nearby fields
It collapsed, unleashing a flash flood downstream

evt-11-06-1977-kelly-barnes-dam.butterflyEffect: The dam collapsed in the early hours, sending a flash flood crashing through the campus below and killing 39 people. The tragedy exposed how unregulated small dams were and helped push Georgia and other states toward stricter dam-safety inspection laws.

evt-11-06-1985-colombian-conflict.scenario: It is midday on 6 November 1985, and you are a court clerk trapped inside Bogotá's Palace of Justice as M-19 guerrillas storm the building and seize the Supreme Court's justices as hostages.
evt-11-06-1985-colombian-conflict.prompt: How does the Colombian government respond to the siege?

choices.text: The government agrees to put the president on trial as M-19 demands
The government orders a military assault to retake the building by force
The government negotiates the hostages' release in exchange for amnesty
The government evacuates the area and waits out a peaceful siege

evt-11-06-1985-colombian-conflict.butterflyEffect: President Belisario Betancur refused to negotiate and ordered the army to retake the Palace by force; the ensuing battle and fire killed roughly half the Supreme Court's justices along with many guerrillas and hostages. The siege devastated Colombia's judiciary, fueled lasting controversy over disappeared civilians, and deepened distrust between the state and left-wing insurgents.

evt-11-06-1986-1986-british-internationa.scenario: It's 6 November 1986. You're an offshore worker boarding a Boeing Chinook helicopter for the short hop from the Brent oilfield back to Sumburgh Airport, unaware the aircraft's tandem rotor system is about to fail catastrophically just short of the runway.
evt-11-06-1986-1986-british-internationa.prompt: What did the crash investigation find had caused the disaster?

choices.text: Pilot error while landing in dense fog
The helicopter ran out of fuel over open water
A bird strike disabled both engines
Catastrophic failure of the forward rotor transmission

evt-11-06-1986-1986-british-internationa.butterflyEffect: Investigators traced the crash to a forward transmission failure that let the tandem rotor blades collide, sending the helicopter into the sea and killing 45 of the 47 aboard. The inquiry led to tighter inspection and maintenance rules for offshore helicopter transport across the North Sea industry.

evt-11-06-2004-ufton-nervet-rail-crash.scenario: It is a dark evening on 6 November 2004, and you drive a First Great Western express approaching a level crossing near Ufton Nervet, Berkshire, unaware a car sits motionless across the tracks ahead.
evt-11-06-2004-ufton-nervet-rail-crash.prompt: What does the subsequent inquest determine caused the fatal crash?

choices.text: A signal failure let the train through with the crossing barriers still open
The level crossing barriers malfunctioned and failed to lower
The train driver misread the approach speed limit
The car's driver deliberately parked on the crossing to take his own life

evt-11-06-2004-ufton-nervet-rail-crash.butterflyEffect: Investigators found every signal, barrier and piece of track equipment had worked correctly; the crash was caused by the car driver's deliberate suicide on the crossing. The disaster renewed debate over level-crossing safety and driver support for train crews traumatized by such incidents, though it was ruled no one at the railway was at fault.

evt-11-06-2012-tammy-baldwin.scenario: It is election night, 6 November 2012, and you are watching Wisconsin's Senate returns as Democratic congresswoman Tammy Baldwin battles former governor Tommy Thompson for the seat.
evt-11-06-2012-tammy-baldwin.prompt: What LGBTQ milestone does Baldwin's Senate victory achieve that night?

choices.text: She becomes the first openly bisexual person elected to the U.S. Senate
She becomes the first openly gay person elected to the U.S. House of Representatives
She becomes the first openly gay or lesbian person elected to the U.S. Senate
She becomes the first openly transgender person elected to the U.S. Senate

evt-11-06-2012-tammy-baldwin.butterflyEffect: Baldwin became the first openly gay or lesbian person ever elected to the United States Senate, having already served in the House since 1999. Her win expanded visibility for LGBTQ candidates nationally and preceded further breakthroughs, including Kyrsten Sinema's election as the first openly bisexual senator in 2018.

evt-11-06-2016-syrian-civil-war.scenario: It's 6 November 2016 near Raqqa, Syria. You command Syrian Democratic Forces preparing to move against the Islamic State's de facto capital, backed by US-led coalition airstrikes.
evt-11-06-2016-syrian-civil-war.prompt: What operation do you launch that day?

choices.text: The evacuation of civilians from besieged Aleppo
A joint offensive with the Free Syrian Army against Damascus
Operation Wrath of Euphrates, the campaign to retake Raqqa
A ceasefire negotiation with the Assad government

evt-11-06-2016-syrian-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The SDF launched Operation Wrath of Euphrates, and with sustained coalition air support besieged and captured Raqqa by October 2017. The fall of ISIS's de facto capital marked a turning point in the group's territorial collapse and cemented Kurdish-led SDF control over much of northeastern Syria.

evt-11-07-680-third-council-of-constanti.scenario: It is 680 in Constantinople, and you are a bishop summoned by Emperor Constantine IV to settle a bitter dispute: did Christ possess a single divine will, or two distinct wills, human and divine, united in one person?
evt-11-07-680-third-council-of-constanti.prompt: What position does the council formally affirm?

choices.text: Christ has a single divine will alone
The question of Christ's will is left undefined
Christ has only a human will
Christ has two distinct wills and two energies

evt-11-07-680-third-council-of-constanti.butterflyEffect: The council condemned monothelitism and monoenergism, declaring that Christ has two wills and two energies, human and divine, united without division. It also posthumously condemned Pope Honorius I for supporting the heresy, a decision later cited in debates over papal infallibility.

evt-11-07-1811-tecumseh-s-war.scenario: It is before dawn near the Tippecanoe River, and warriors of Tecumseh's confederacy, led by the Prophet Tenskwatawa in Tecumseh's absence, suddenly rush your camp. You command Harrison's startled American force.
evt-11-07-1811-tecumseh-s-war.prompt: What order do you give as the surprise attack hits your lines?

choices.text: Send envoys to negotiate a truce mid-battle
Order an immediate cavalry charge into the darkness toward the enemy fires
Retreat the entire camp into the woods before dawn breaks
Hold the line and counterattack once the warriors' initial rush stalls

evt-11-07-1811-tecumseh-s-war.butterflyEffect: Harrison's men held their ground, repelled the assault, and burned the nearby village of Prophetstown in retaliation. The defeat discredited Tenskwatawa's spiritual leadership and pushed Tecumseh toward a formal alliance with the British once the War of 1812 began.

evt-11-07-1825-jereboam-o-beauchamp.scenario: It's the night of November 7, 1825, in Frankfort, Kentucky. You are Jereboam Beauchamp, having just confronted and fatally stabbed state legislator Solomon P. Sharp at his own home, convinced you were defending your wife Anna's honor.
evt-11-07-1825-jereboam-o-beauchamp.prompt: What follows for Beauchamp after the killing?

choices.text: Sharp's family publicly forgives him and drops charges
He is acquitted after pleading self-defense
He flees the state and is never captured
He is arrested, tried, and sentenced to hang

evt-11-07-1825-jereboam-o-beauchamp.butterflyEffect: Beauchamp was arrested, convicted, and sentenced to hang. Before the execution in 1826, he and Anna attempted a joint suicide in their cell; Anna died, but Jereboam survived just long enough to be hanged. The case, known as the Beauchamp–Sharp Tragedy or 'Kentucky Tragedy,' inspired numerous plays and novels, including works influenced by Edgar Allan Poe and Robert Penn Warren.

evt-11-07-1837-abolitionism-in-the-unite.scenario: It is the night of November 7, 1837, in Alton, Illinois. A pro-slavery mob surrounds the warehouse where your abolitionist newspaper's new printing press has just been delivered, determined to destroy it as they destroyed your previous three presses.
evt-11-07-1837-abolitionism-in-the-unite.prompt: What do you do to protect the press?

choices.text: Surrender the press peacefully to avoid bloodshed
Flee the city under cover of darkness
Arm yourself and your supporters to defend the warehouse
Negotiate a compromise to publish only non-abolitionist material

evt-11-07-1837-abolitionism-in-the-unite.butterflyEffect: Elijah Lovejoy and his armed supporters chose to defend the warehouse, and Lovejoy was shot and killed by the mob, becoming one of the abolitionist movement's first martyrs. His death galvanized northern opinion against mob violence and slavery, inspiring figures like John Brown and a young Abraham Lincoln to speak out against such lawlessness.

evt-11-07-1861-american-civil-war.scenario: You are Ulysses S. Grant at Belmont, Missouri, leading your first combat command. Your men have overrun the Confederate camp and, distracted by plunder, Confederate reinforcements are now crossing the river behind you.
evt-11-07-1861-american-civil-war.prompt: What do you order as the enemy closes in on your looting soldiers?

choices.text: Retreat immediately without re-engaging the enemy
Dig in and defend the captured camp at all costs
Surrender the position to avoid further casualties
Rally the troops and fight your way back to the transports

evt-11-07-1861-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Grant rallied his disorganized men and fought his way back to the transport boats, narrowly avoiding disaster. His composure under pressure at this first engagement helped build the reputation that led to greater commands and, eventually, overall command of Union forces.

evt-11-07-1893-liceu-bombing.scenario: You are a Barcelona police investigator called to the Grand Lyceum Theatre after an explosion tears through the audience during a performance, leaving the orchestra stalls in ruins.
evt-11-07-1893-liceu-bombing.prompt: What motive do investigators soon establish behind the bombing?

choices.text: Sabotage by a rival theatre seeking to close the Liceu
An accidental gas line explosion beneath the stalls
Revenge for the recent execution of the anarchist Paulí Pallàs
A personal vendetta against the theatre's owner

evt-11-07-1893-liceu-bombing.butterflyEffect: The attack was traced to anarchist Santiago Salvador, who acted in revenge for the recent execution of fellow anarchist Paulí Pallàs. The bombing intensified state repression of anarchism in Catalonia, feeding into the harsh Montjuïc trials and a continuing cycle of violence and reprisal in the years that followed.

evt-11-07-1916-1916-united-states-house-.scenario: It is November 7, 1916, and you are a Montana voter marking your ballot for one of the state's at-large seats in the U.S. House. One candidate, a longtime suffrage organizer, is on your ballot alongside the usual men.
evt-11-07-1916-1916-united-states-house-.prompt: What historic first results from this election in Montana?

choices.text: The first woman is elected governor of a U.S. state
The first woman is elected to the U.S. House of Representatives
The first woman is elected to the U.S. Senate
The first woman is nominated for U.S. vice president

evt-11-07-1916-1916-united-states-house-.butterflyEffect: Jeannette Rankin became the first woman elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, four years before the Nineteenth Amendment gave most American women the vote nationwide. In 1917 she cast a headline-making vote against U.S. entry into World War I, and in 1941 she was the only member of Congress to vote against declaring war on Japan.

evt-11-07-1917-october-revolution.scenario: It is late October 1917 in Petrograd. You are a soldier in the city garrison as the Bolshevik-led Military Revolutionary Committee calls on troops to rise against Kerensky's Provisional Government.
evt-11-07-1917-october-revolution.prompt: What should you do as the Bolsheviks call for insurrection?

choices.text: Join the Red Guards in seizing bridges, stations and government buildings
Join Cossack units seeking to restore the monarchy
Desert the city and return to the front lines
Rally to defend Kerensky's Provisional Government in the Winter Palace

evt-11-07-1917-october-revolution.butterflyEffect: Garrison soldiers and Red Guards seized key points across Petrograd with almost no bloodshed, and the Provisional Government collapsed within hours. Lenin's Bolsheviks took power, triggering the Russian Civil War and the eventual founding of the Soviet Union.

evt-11-07-1987-mass-rapid-transit-singap.scenario: You step onto the platform at one of five brand-new stations for the inaugural ride of Singapore's first Mass Rapid Transit line, a modest 6-kilometre stretch two decades in the planning.
evt-11-07-1987-mass-rapid-transit-singap.prompt: What does this small opening line eventually grow into?

choices.text: A nationwide rapid transit network spanning most of the island
A short tourist tram confined to the city centre
A monorail serving only the airport route
A freight line later converted for limited passenger use

evt-11-07-1987-mass-rapid-transit-singap.butterflyEffect: The initial 6 km stretch expanded over subsequent decades into a sprawling network covering most of Singapore's main island. It became the backbone of the country's public transport system, carrying millions of riders daily and shaping urban development around its stations.

evt-11-07-1987-zine-el-abidine-ben-ali.scenario: It is early morning on November 7, 1987, in Tunis. As prime minister, you have gathered physicians' statements declaring the elderly President Habib Bourguiba mentally unfit to govern, and troops are positioned around the palace.
evt-11-07-1987-zine-el-abidine-ben-ali.prompt: What do you do to take power?

choices.text: Declare the president medically unfit and assume the presidency
Dissolve the presidency and rule through a military council
Arrest the president and place him on trial
Call for immediate multiparty elections

evt-11-07-1987-zine-el-abidine-ben-ali.butterflyEffect: Ben Ali invoked Article 57 of the constitution, declared Bourguiba incapacitated, and assumed the presidency in a bloodless "medical coup." He would rule Tunisia for the next 24 years until mass protests, the Jasmine Revolution, drove him from power in January 2011, sparking the wider Arab Spring.

evt-11-07-1991-magic-johnson.scenario: It is November 7, 1991, and you are watching Magic Johnson announce his retirement from the Lakers after testing positive for HIV, a diagnosis many assume will end his public life entirely.
evt-11-07-1991-magic-johnson.prompt: What did Johnson defiantly do just months after this announcement?

choices.text: He immediately became a full-time head coach for the Lakers
He played in the 1992 NBA All-Star Game and won the MVP award
He withdrew completely from public life for the rest of the decade
He filed a lawsuit against the NBA for forcing his retirement

evt-11-07-1991-magic-johnson.butterflyEffect: Johnson returned to play in the 1992 NBA All-Star Game and won the MVP award, showing the world that a person with HIV could still compete at the highest level. His openness helped dismantle stigma around the virus and fueled his lasting advocacy work through the Magic Johnson Foundation.

evt-11-07-1996-nasa.scenario: It's the pre-dawn hours of November 7, 1996 at Cape Canaveral. You're part of the NASA team preparing to launch Mars Global Surveyor, the agency's first mission to the Red Planet since the Mars Observer disappeared in 1993.
evt-11-07-1996-nasa.prompt: What is Mars Global Surveyor primarily built to do once it reaches Mars?

choices.text: Land a rover to drill for subsurface ice samples
Orbit the planet and map its surface, atmosphere, and terrain in detail
Fly past Mars carrying a crew toward the outer planets
Collect Martian soil and return it to Earth

evt-11-07-1996-nasa.butterflyEffect: The spacecraft entered Mars orbit in 1997 and mapped the planet's surface, atmosphere, and magnetic field for nearly a decade, far outliving its planned mission. Its images of gully-like features suggesting possible liquid water reshaped scientific debate about the planet's history and set the stage for later rover missions.

evt-11-07-2000-hillary-clinton.scenario: It's election night, November 7, 2000, in New York. You're a campaign aide for Hillary Rodham Clinton, the sitting First Lady, as returns come in against Republican Rick Lazio in the race for an open Senate seat.
evt-11-07-2000-hillary-clinton.prompt: What historic distinction does a Clinton win in this race create?

choices.text: She becomes the youngest person ever elected to the Senate
She becomes the first sitting First Lady elected to public office
She becomes the first woman ever elected to the U.S. Senate
She becomes the first woman to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee

evt-11-07-2000-hillary-clinton.butterflyEffect: Clinton won the seat, becoming the first First Lady of the United States to be elected to public office. The victory launched a Senate career that led to her becoming Secretary of State and, in 2016, the first woman nominated for president by a major U.S. party.

evt-11-07-2000-2000-united-states-presid.scenario: It's election night, November 7, 2000. You're an aide to Al Gore, watching Florida's returns swing back and forth between too-close-to-call and a narrow Bush lead, with the presidency hanging on the outcome.
evt-11-07-2000-2000-united-states-presid.prompt: What should the Gore campaign push for in Florida in the days that follow?

choices.text: Demand that all of Florida hold a completely new vote
Request manual recounts in contested Florida counties
Ask Congress to decide the outcome directly
Concede the election immediately to avoid a constitutional crisis

evt-11-07-2000-2000-united-states-presid.butterflyEffect: Gore's campaign sought manual recounts in several Florida counties, triggering five weeks of legal battles that reached the Supreme Court. In Bush v. Gore, the Court halted the recount by a 5–4 vote, effectively handing Bush Florida's electoral votes and the presidency despite Gore winning the national popular vote.

evt-11-07-2004-iraq-war.scenario: It's November 7, 2004. You advise Iraq's interim Prime Minister Ayad Allawi as U.S. and Iraqi forces mass outside Fallujah, a city that has become an insurgent stronghold since the uprisings earlier that year.
evt-11-07-2004-iraq-war.prompt: What legal step does the interim government take to enable the coming offensive?

choices.text: It declares a 60-day nationwide state of emergency
It requests a United Nations peacekeeping force take over the city
It negotiates a permanent ceasefire with insurgent leaders
It dissolves itself and calls immediate elections

evt-11-07-2004-iraq-war.butterflyEffect: Allawi's government declared a 60-day state of emergency across most of Iraq, clearing the way for the Second Battle of Fallujah days later. The assault became one of the war's bloodiest urban battles, displacing most of the city's population and deepening Sunni Arab distrust of the new Iraqi government.

evt-11-07-2007-jokela-school-shooting.scenario: It is November 2007, and Finland is reeling from the shooting at Jokela High School. As officials and lawmakers examine how an 18-year-old legally obtained the pistol used in the attack, they weigh how to respond.
evt-11-07-2007-jokela-school-shooting.prompt: What did Finnish authorities change after the Jokela shooting?

choices.text: They made no changes to existing firearms laws
They banned all civilian firearm ownership nationwide
They raised the minimum age and tightened medical checks for handgun licences
They placed armed police officers permanently inside every school

evt-11-07-2007-jokela-school-shooting.butterflyEffect: Finland raised the minimum age for handgun licences and tightened requirements, including medical certification for applicants. The reform proved insufficient to prevent a strikingly similar attack at Kauhajoki less than a year later, which reignited national debate over gun culture and mental health screening.

evt-11-07-2020-joe-biden.scenario: It is the morning of November 7, 2020. Major networks have just projected Joe Biden as the winner of the presidential election, but the incumbent president has not conceded and is disputing the outcome.
evt-11-07-2020-joe-biden.prompt: What does the incumbent president do in the days that follow?

choices.text: He refuses to concede and pursues legal challenges to the results
He resigns immediately to allow a smooth transition
He calls for an immediate national re-vote
He concedes gracefully within days

evt-11-07-2020-joe-biden.butterflyEffect: Trump refused to concede, filed numerous lawsuits challenging results in key states, and pressured officials to overturn the outcome. The dispute culminated on January 6, 2021, when a mob stormed the U.S. Capitol during the certification of Biden's victory, a crisis that reshaped American politics for years.

evt-11-08-1291-venetian-glass.scenario: You are a master glassmaker in Venice in 1291, when the Republic orders that all glass furnaces be moved out of the crowded, wooden city center.

choices.text: Ignore the order and keep working in the city
Abandon glassmaking for another trade
Petition to move your furnace to the mainland city of Padua instead
Relocate your furnace and workshop to the island of Murano as ordered

evt-11-08-1291-venetian-glass.butterflyEffect: Glassmakers relocated their furnaces to the island of Murano, ostensibly to reduce fire risk. The move also let Venice tightly guard its glassmaking secrets, and over the following two centuries Murano's isolated workshops developed cristallo glass and dominated Europe's luxury glass trade.

evt-11-08-1644-shunzhi-emperor.scenario: It is November 1644, and you are a Manchu prince attending court in newly captured Beijing as five-year-old Fulin is enthroned as the Shunzhi Emperor.
evt-11-08-1644-shunzhi-emperor.prompt: Who actually wields power on behalf of the young emperor?

choices.text: Surviving Ming dynasty officials retained in office
Prince regent Dorgon
Co-regent Jirgalang, without Dorgon's involvement
The empress dowager acting alone

evt-11-08-1644-shunzhi-emperor.butterflyEffect: Prince regent Dorgon dominated the regency until his death in 1650, effectively ruling China in the young emperor's name and overseeing the Qing conquest of the rest of the country. After Shunzhi took personal control in 1651, Dorgon was posthumously stripped of his titles and honors.

evt-11-08-1895-wilhelm-rontgen.scenario: It is the evening of November 8, 1895, in your Würzburg laboratory. Working with a Crookes tube wrapped in black cardboard, you notice a nearby screen coated in barium platinocyanide glowing faintly, even though no visible light should be escaping the tube.
evt-11-08-1895-wilhelm-rontgen.prompt: What do you do about this unexplained glow?

choices.text: Dismiss it as a faulty tube and discard the experiment
Publish a paper immediately without further testing
Assume it is simply known cathode ray light and move on
Investigate the phenomenon systematically before announcing anything

evt-11-08-1895-wilhelm-rontgen.butterflyEffect: Röntgen spent weeks methodically investigating the mysterious rays, eventually producing the first X-ray image, a radiograph of his wife Anna's hand. His discovery transformed medical diagnosis almost overnight and earned him the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

evt-11-08-1932-australian-defence-force.scenario: You are Major G.P.W. Meredith, commanding Royal Australian Artillery soldiers armed with Lewis machine guns in Western Australia's wheat belt, sent to cull the emus trampling crops. After weeks of chasing fast, scattering birds with little success, headquarters asks for your recommendation.
evt-11-08-1932-australian-defence-force.prompt: What does the military ultimately decide to do about the 'war against emus'?

choices.text: Request RAAF biplanes to strafe the flocks from the air
Declare the emus successfully exterminated
Double the number of machine gun crews and continue
Withdraw the troops and hand the problem back to farmers

evt-11-08-1932-australian-defence-force.butterflyEffect: The army formally withdrew on 8 November 1932 having killed only a few hundred of the thousands of emus targeted. Responsibility passed back to farmers via a bounty system, and the episode became a lasting, often mocked, symbol of the limits of conventional force against wildlife.

evt-11-08-1940-greco-italian-war.scenario: It is before dawn on 28 October 1940. As Prime Minister of Greece, you are roused to receive an Italian ultimatum demanding free passage for Mussolini's troops through Greek territory.
evt-11-08-1940-greco-italian-war.prompt: How do you respond to the ultimatum?

choices.text: Refer the matter to the League of Nations without answering Rome
Accept the demand to avoid immediate conflict
Reject the ultimatum outright, accepting war with Italy
Offer a partial territorial concession to buy time

evt-11-08-1940-greco-italian-war.butterflyEffect: Ioannis Metaxas rejected the ultimatum, and Italy invaded that same day. Outnumbered Greek forces halted the Italians and drove them back into Albania within weeks, the first Allied land victory of the war, forcing Hitler to divert forces into the Balkans the following spring and delaying the invasion of the Soviet Union.

evt-11-08-1957-pan-am-flight-7.scenario: It is November 1957, and you are part of a Coast Guard search team scouring the Pacific after the Clipper Romance of the Skies, Pan Am Flight 7, vanishes en route from San Francisco to Honolulu.
evt-11-08-1957-pan-am-flight-7.prompt: What did investigators ultimately determine caused the crash?

choices.text: Pilot error was confirmed through air traffic recordings
The cause was never conclusively determined
Sabotage by a passenger seeking insurance money was proven
An engine fire was confirmed by flight recorder data

evt-11-08-1957-pan-am-flight-7.butterflyEffect: Wreckage and some remains were eventually recovered, but the Civil Aeronautics Board investigation could not conclusively determine what brought the aircraft down. The crash remains one of Pan Am's most enduring unsolved mysteries, and it fueled broader scrutiny of the Boeing 377 Stratocruiser's safety record.

evt-11-08-1966-massachusetts.scenario: You are a campaign strategist for the moderate Republican attorney general seeking Massachusetts's U.S. Senate seat on this Election Day in 1966, in a state dominated by Democratic voters.
evt-11-08-1966-massachusetts.prompt: What approach helps your candidate win over Democratic and independent voters?

choices.text: Run him as a hardline conservative in the Goldwater mold
Present him as a moderate on civil rights who can work across party lines
Focus the campaign exclusively on white working-class suburbs
Avoid any public discussion of racial issues entirely

evt-11-08-1966-massachusetts.butterflyEffect: Edward Brooke won as a racial moderate distancing himself from Goldwater-style conservatism, becoming the first African American senator elected by popular vote. He went on to chair Senate committees and author the Brooke Amendment limiting public housing rents, becoming a leading Republican voice on civil rights.

evt-11-08-1987-provisional-irish-republi.scenario: You stand in the crowd gathered at the war memorial in Enniskillen on Remembrance Sunday, 8 November 1987, waiting for the parade of veterans and civilians to reach the cenotaph.
evt-11-08-1987-provisional-irish-republi.prompt: What lasting political effect did the bombing that struck the crowd have?

choices.text: It significantly boosted IRA recruitment and sympathy
It led the IRA to declare an immediate ceasefire
It drew widespread condemnation and damaged the IRA's public support
It had little lasting political effect on either side

evt-11-08-1987-provisional-irish-republi.butterflyEffect: The bomb killed eleven civilians gathered to honor the war dead. The attack drew condemnation from across the political spectrum, including from some IRA sympathizers, and damaged the organization's public standing in a way that contributed to the long path toward the peace process of the following decade.

evt-11-08-1997-eritrea.scenario: You run a market stall in Asmara on 8 November 1997, the day Eritrea officially retires the Ethiopian birr in favor of its own new currency, six years after independence.
evt-11-08-1997-eritrea.prompt: What do you do with the birr notes still in your cash box?

choices.text: Keep accepting birr indefinitely alongside the new currency
Exchange them for nakfa at the official rate before the deadline
Destroy the birr notes as a political statement
Smuggle the notes into Ethiopia for full value

evt-11-08-1997-eritrea.butterflyEffect: Eritrea exchanged old birr for the new nakfa to assert full monetary independence from Ethiopia. The dispute over how the two currencies should be valued against each other became one of the frictions that fed into the devastating Eritrean–Ethiopian border war beginning in 1998.

evt-11-08-2004-iraq-war.scenario: It is early November 2004, and you are a Marine preparing to advance into Fallujah alongside more than 10,000 U.S. troops and Iraqi army units, tasked with retaking the city from entrenched insurgents.
evt-11-08-2004-iraq-war.prompt: How should coalition forces clear the city of dug-in insurgent fighters?

choices.text: Negotiate a ceasefire directly with insurgent commanders
Rely solely on airstrikes and avoid sending in ground troops
Encircle the city and wait for insurgents to surrender
Conduct methodical house-to-house clearing operations

evt-11-08-2004-iraq-war.butterflyEffect: The Second Battle of Fallujah involved brutal house-to-house urban combat that became the bloodiest engagement of the war for U.S. forces, leaving much of the city destroyed. It temporarily dispersed the insurgency but hardened resistance elsewhere and became a defining, controversial image of the occupation.

evt-11-08-2013-typhoon-haiyan.scenario: It is November 7, 2013, and you live in coastal Tacloban. Officials warn of an approaching 'storm surge' from Typhoon Haiyan, a term many in your community have never heard before.
evt-11-08-2013-typhoon-haiyan.prompt: What should you do to protect yourself from the coming storm surge?

choices.text: Evacuate immediately to higher ground away from the coast
Wait for local officials to issue further updates before acting
Move to the ground floor of your house for stability
Stay indoors and shutter your windows against the wind

evt-11-08-2013-typhoon-haiyan.butterflyEffect: Because the phrase 'storm surge' was unfamiliar to many Filipinos, thousands underestimated the danger and stayed in low-lying coastal homes, contributing to the catastrophic death toll. The disaster prompted the Philippine government to overhaul hazard communication, using clearer, more visual warnings in future typhoons.

evt-11-08-2016-donald-trump.scenario: It is the night of 8 November 2016. You are watching returns come in from Wisconsin, Michigan, and Pennsylvania, states pollsters had long assumed were safely Democratic.
evt-11-08-2016-donald-trump.prompt: What actually happens as the results come in from these battleground states?

choices.text: Trump wins the Electoral College despite losing the popular vote
Congress is forced to decide the outcome under the 12th Amendment
Clinton wins a comfortable Electoral College majority
The election is thrown to a contested recount for weeks

evt-11-08-2016-donald-trump.butterflyEffect: Donald Trump won the Electoral College while losing the national popular vote, defying most pre-election polling. The result upended assumptions about American politics, energized a populist realignment, and set the stage for his return to the presidency in 2024.

evt-11-08-2020-2020-myanmar-general-elec.scenario: It is 8 November 2020, and you are standing in line outside a Yangon polling station, aware that the military-aligned USDP fears a repeat of the 2015 landslide against it.
evt-11-08-2020-2020-myanmar-general-elec.prompt: What follows after Aung San Suu Kyi's NLD wins another sweeping victory?

choices.text: The military immediately deploys troops on election night to seize ballots
International observers annul the election results outright
The USDP accepts defeat and becomes a peaceful opposition party
The military stages a coup months later, alleging voter fraud

evt-11-08-2020-2020-myanmar-general-elec.butterflyEffect: The NLD's landslide was so decisive that the military, alleging unproven fraud, seized power in a coup in February 2021, arresting Aung San Suu Kyi and reversing a decade of democratic reform. The coup plunged Myanmar into ongoing armed resistance and civil conflict.

evt-11-09-1888-mary-jane-kelly.scenario: It is the morning of 9 November 1888 in Whitechapel. A rent collector has just discovered a horrifying scene inside a small room on Dorset Street and must decide what to do next.
evt-11-09-1888-mary-jane-kelly.prompt: What did the rent collector do upon making the discovery?

choices.text: He alerted the police immediately
He entered the room to check for survivors
He fetched a doctor before contacting police
He told the newspapers before informing authorities

evt-11-09-1888-mary-jane-kelly.butterflyEffect: He alerted the police rather than entering the room himself, and officers found the murder scene undisturbed. Kelly's murder, the most brutal of the Ripper's killings, was never solved, and the case has remained one of history's most enduring criminal mysteries.

evt-11-09-1913-great-lakes-storm-of-1913.scenario: It is 9 November 1913 and you captain a freighter on Lake Huron. The sky has turned ominous and reports of a strengthening storm are trickling in over the wireless.
evt-11-09-1913-great-lakes-storm-of-1913.prompt: What was the fateful decision many captains made as the storm intensified?

choices.text: They continued their voyages, trusting their ships to handle the weather
They anchored offshore and waited out the storm
They turned back to the nearest port at first warning
They radioed for naval escorts before proceeding

evt-11-09-1913-great-lakes-storm-of-1913.butterflyEffect: Many captains pressed on, underestimating a storm that reached hurricane-force winds and towering waves. It became the deadliest natural disaster ever to hit the Great Lakes, prompting major improvements in weather forecasting and ship-to-shore communication for the region.

evt-11-09-1914-world-war-i.scenario: It is 9 November 1914 in the Indian Ocean. You command HMAS Sydney, escorting a troop convoy, when a distress call crackles in: the wireless station on Direction Island has just been attacked by an unidentified warship.
evt-11-09-1914-world-war-i.prompt: Do you break off from the convoy to investigate and engage the raider?

choices.text: Retreat further out to sea to avoid contact
Ignore the signal and continue escorting the convoy
Break from the convoy to investigate and engage the raider
Radio for reinforcements before taking any action

evt-11-09-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Sydney detached, found the German cruiser SMS Emden, and destroyed her in the Battle of Cocos, ending a raiding career that had sunk or captured over twenty Allied ships. It became the young Royal Australian Navy's first major victory of the war, a point of national pride still celebrated today.

evt-11-09-1918-azerbaijan-democratic-rep.scenario: You sit on the Azerbaijani National Council in November 1918, months after declaring independence from the collapsed Transcaucasian federation. The council must choose a national flag to represent the new republic.
evt-11-09-1918-azerbaijan-democratic-rep.prompt: What design should the council adopt as the national flag?

choices.text: An Ottoman-style red flag with a single star
A plain green flag with a crescent moon
A red flag with a hammer and sickle
A blue-red-green tricolor with a crescent and star

evt-11-09-1918-azerbaijan-democratic-rep.butterflyEffect: The council adopted a blue, red, and green tricolor bearing a white crescent and eight-pointed star, blending Turkic, modernist, and Islamic symbolism. After decades of Soviet rule suppressed it, this same tricolor was restored in 1991 as the flag of independent Azerbaijan, directly linking the modern state to the 1918 republic.

evt-11-09-1938-kristallnacht.scenario: It is the night of 9 November 1938 in a German city. You watch mobs of SA and Hitler Youth smash the windows of Jewish-owned shops and set a synagogue alight, while police and firefighters stand nearby.
evt-11-09-1938-kristallnacht.prompt: What do the German authorities do as the violence unfolds?

choices.text: They stand by, intervening only to protect German-owned buildings
They evacuate Jewish families to protective custody for their safety
They arrest the rioters and disperse the crowds
They extinguish the synagogue fires and prosecute the attackers

evt-11-09-1938-kristallnacht.butterflyEffect: Authorities largely stood by, intervening mainly to stop fires spreading to non-Jewish property. In the following days some 30,000 Jewish men were arrested and sent to concentration camps, marking the shift from legal discrimination to open state-tolerated violence and foreshadowing the Holocaust.

evt-11-09-1939-world-war-ii.scenario: You are a British SIS officer near Venlo on the Dutch-German border in November 1939, arranging what you believe is a secret meeting with anti-Nazi conspirators inside the German military.
evt-11-09-1939-world-war-ii.prompt: What actually happens at this meeting?

choices.text: SD agents posing as resistance figures ambush and capture the British officers
The meeting is aborted and the officers return safely to Britain
The officers successfully meet genuine German resistance leaders
A Gestapo officer defects to the British during the meeting

evt-11-09-1939-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The contacts were Sicherheitsdienst agents running a deception, and they seized British officers Sigismund Payne Best and Richard Stevens in the Venlo Incident. Hitler used the capture to accuse British intelligence of orchestrating plots against Germany from Dutch soil, a claim exploited to help justify the invasion of the Netherlands months later, while the SD extracted intelligence that crippled SIS networks across occupied Europe.

evt-11-09-1985-garry-kasparov.scenario: It is November 1985 in Moscow. You are 22-year-old Garry Kasparov, sitting down for the final game of your World Championship match against reigning champion Anatoly Karpov, with the title within reach if you can seize the full point.
evt-11-09-1985-garry-kasparov.prompt: Do you play it safe for a draw, or push for an outright win?

choices.text: Offer Karpov a draw before the game begins
Play cautiously, aiming only for a safe draw
Request a postponement to rest before the deciding game
Push aggressively for a decisive win with the black pieces

evt-11-09-1985-garry-kasparov.butterflyEffect: Kasparov won the game and the match 13-11, becoming the youngest World Chess Champion in history at 22. It launched a legendary five-match rivalry with Karpov and a 255-month reign at world No. 1, and later fueled his second career as a pro-democracy dissident against the Kremlin.

evt-11-09-1989-fall-of-the-berlin-wall.scenario: You are a Berliner standing at the Bornholmer Strasse checkpoint on the evening of 9 November 1989. Rumours are spreading that East German officials have announced looser travel rules, and a crowd is gathering at the gate.
evt-11-09-1989-fall-of-the-berlin-wall.prompt: What do you and the crowd do at the checkpoint that night?

choices.text: Wait quietly at home for an official government announcement
Attempt to climb over the wall at an unguarded section instead
Disperse, fearing a violent crackdown like in past years
Push forward and cross as the overwhelmed guards open the gate

evt-11-09-1989-fall-of-the-berlin-wall.butterflyEffect: Overwhelmed and without clear orders, border guards opened the gates, and thousands streamed into West Berlin within hours. The breach triggered the rapid collapse of East German control, the fall of the wider Iron Curtain, and German reunification less than a year later.

evt-11-09-1993-bosnian-war.scenario: You command Croatian Defence Council artillery overlooking Mostar in November 1993. The centuries-old Ottoman bridge, Stari Most, links Bosniak-held districts across the Neretva River and sits squarely in your gun sights.
evt-11-09-1993-bosnian-war.prompt: What does the HVO command decide to do with the bridge?

choices.text: Negotiate a local ceasefire specifically to save the bridge
Use it as the main crossing point for advancing HVO troops
Preserve it as protected heritage and route troops elsewhere
Destroy the bridge as a symbolic and tactical target

evt-11-09-1993-bosnian-war.butterflyEffect: On 9 November 1993, HVO shelling brought Stari Most crashing into the river, an act that became a global symbol of the war's destruction of shared cultural heritage. After the war, UNESCO and international donors funded a careful reconstruction using original techniques, and the rebuilt bridge reopened in 2004 as a monument to reconciliation.

evt-11-09-1998-capital-punishment-in-the.scenario: It is 9 November 1998 in Westminster. You are a member of the House of Lords as the Human Rights Act receives Royal Assent, closing out decades of gradual retreat from the death penalty by striking the last capital offences from British law.
evt-11-09-1998-capital-punishment-in-the.prompt: What does this Act finally achieve for the death penalty in Britain?

choices.text: It leaves the death penalty in place for piracy only
It reinstates the death penalty for treason
It merely suspends executions temporarily
It abolishes the death penalty for the last remaining offences

evt-11-09-1998-capital-punishment-in-the.butterflyEffect: The Act incorporated the European Convention's Protocol 6, abolishing the death penalty for the remaining offences of treason and piracy, decades after it had already ended for murder in 1969. It completed Britain's long legal retreat from capital punishment and paved the way for ratifying Protocol 13, banning the death penalty even in wartime, the following year.
