evt-11-09-1999-taesa-flight-725.scenario: It is November 9, 1999, and you work in TAESA's operations office in Mexico City. Word arrives that Flight 725, en route from Tijuana with a stop in Uruapan, has crashed moments after departing Uruapan's airport.
evt-11-09-1999-taesa-flight-725.prompt: What consequence does this crash ultimately trigger for the airline?

choices.text: TAESA receives a national safety award
TAESA expands its route network in response
TAESA grounds its fleet and suspends operations within a year
TAESA merges with a larger international carrier

evt-11-09-1999-taesa-flight-725.butterflyEffect: All 18 people aboard were killed. The crash badly damaged TAESA's reputation and safety record, and within a year the airline grounded its entire fleet and suspended operations altogether, ending its run as a Mexican carrier.

evt-11-09-2000-uttarakhand.scenario: You are an activist who has spent years in the Uttarakhand movement, campaigning for a separate hill state carved out of Uttar Pradesh's mountainous districts.
evt-11-09-2000-uttarakhand.prompt: What actually happens on 9 November 2000 after decades of agitation?

choices.text: The movement fails and the region remains part of Uttar Pradesh
Uttarakhand is formally created as a separate state from Uttar Pradesh
The state is merged with neighbouring Himachal Pradesh
The region becomes a union territory instead of a full state

evt-11-09-2000-uttarakhand.butterflyEffect: Uttarakhand (initially named Uttaranchal) was formally created as India's 27th state, separated from Uttar Pradesh. The new state later reverted to its original name Uttarakhand in 2007, and its formation became a model cited by other regional statehood movements across India.

evt-11-09-2005-venus-express.scenario: You are an ESA mission engineer at the Baikonur Cosmodrome on 9 November 2005, watching a Soyuz-Fregat rocket lift the Venus Express orbiter toward its target planet.
evt-11-09-2005-venus-express.prompt: What is the probe's main scientific objective once it reaches orbit?

choices.text: Long-term observation of the Venusian atmosphere
Landing a rover to search for surface water
Testing crewed spacecraft life-support systems
Mapping Venus's moons for future missions

evt-11-09-2005-venus-express.butterflyEffect: Venus Express reached Venus in April 2006 and spent nearly nine years studying the planet's thick atmosphere from polar orbit, the longest continuous observation of Venus ever achieved. Its data revealed dynamic atmospheric circulation and hints of recent volcanic activity, shaping the design of later missions aimed at understanding Venus's runaway greenhouse effect.

evt-11-09-2005-2005-amman-bombings.scenario: It is the night of 9 November 2005 in Amman. Bombs have just torn through three hotel lobbies, and one blast struck the Radisson's Philadelphia Ballroom during a Palestinian wedding attended by hundreds of guests.
evt-11-09-2005-2005-amman-bombings.prompt: What did the attack on the wedding reception do to public opinion in Jordan?

choices.text: It turned Jordanian public opinion against al-Qaeda in Iraq
It rallied broad public support for Zarqawi's cause
It caused the Jordanian government to distance itself from the West
It had little effect on domestic opinion

evt-11-09-2005-2005-amman-bombings.butterflyEffect: Because the bombs killed ordinary Jordanians, including members of the wedding party, public revulsion turned sharply against al-Qaeda in Iraq and its leader Abu Musab al-Zarqawi, a Jordanian himself. Mass protests followed in Amman, and Jordan deepened its security cooperation with Western intelligence services, weakening AQI's support base in the kingdom.

evt-11-09-2014-2014-catalan-self-determi.scenario: It is November 2014 in Barcelona. Spain's Constitutional Court has just suspended the official independence referendum, and Catalan leaders must decide how to proceed without breaking the law.
evt-11-09-2014-2014-catalan-self-determi.prompt: How did the Catalan government respond to the court's suspension of the referendum?

choices.text: Declare independence immediately regardless of the ruling
Cancel the vote entirely to avoid legal conflict
Rebrand it as an informal, non-binding "participation process"
Delay the vote until the Spanish parliament approved it

evt-11-09-2014-2014-catalan-self-determi.butterflyEffect: They rebranded the vote as a non-binding "participation process" rather than an official referendum. Turnout was low but support for independence was overwhelming among those who voted, fueling tensions that erupted into the far larger 2017 independence referendum and crisis.

evt-11-09-2019-imran-khan.scenario: It is 9 November 2019, and you are a Sikh pilgrim gathered at the Pakistan-India border as Prime Minister Imran Khan prepares to open a new crossing linking Dera Baba Nanak to a sacred shrine deep inside Pakistan.
evt-11-09-2019-imran-khan.prompt: What historic opportunity does today's opening give you?

choices.text: Permanent resettlement rights in Pakistan
Visa-free pilgrimage across the corridor to the Kartarpur shrine
Duty-free trading rights along the border
Joint citizenship for residents of both border towns

evt-11-09-2019-imran-khan.butterflyEffect: Khan inaugurated the Kartarpur Corridor, letting Sikh pilgrims cross visa-free to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, the shrine where Guru Nanak spent his final years. It became a rare moment of cooperation between hostile neighbors, though it has repeatedly been suspended and reopened amid broader India-Pakistan tensions.

evt-11-09-2020-second-nagorno-karabakh-w.scenario: It is 9 November 2020, and you are Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan. Azerbaijani forces have just seized the strategic town of Shusha, and a Russian-brokered document ending the 44-day war sits on your desk.
evt-11-09-2020-second-nagorno-karabakh-w.prompt: Do you sign the armistice, ceding significant territory to stop the fighting?

choices.text: Request direct NATO military intervention
Appeal only to the UN Security Council for a ceasefire
Refuse and continue fighting despite the losses
Sign the Russian-brokered armistice, ceding territory to end the war

evt-11-09-2020-second-nagorno-karabakh-w.butterflyEffect: Pashinyan signed, ending the war but ceding Shusha and other territories, with Russian peacekeepers deployed to the remaining Armenian-held areas. The defeat triggered mass protests in Yerevan demanding his resignation, and set the stage for further clashes that led to Azerbaijan's full takeover of Nagorno-Karabakh in 2023.

evt-11-09-2023-nyu-langone-health.scenario: You are part of the NYU Langone surgical team in 2023, facing a patient who lost the left side of his face and his left eye in a high-voltage accident. Standard face transplant protocols do not include the eye itself.
evt-11-09-2023-nyu-langone-health.prompt: What should the surgical team attempt alongside the face transplant?

choices.text: Fit a glass prosthetic eye instead
Leave the eye socket untreated until later surgery
Transplant the whole donor eye along with the face
Perform only a corneal transplant on the remaining eye tissue

evt-11-09-2023-nyu-langone-health.butterflyEffect: Surgeons led by Eduardo Rodriguez performed the world's first combined face and whole-eye transplant on patient Aaron James. The eye did not regain sight, but it retained blood flow and pupil response, giving researchers a living model to study optic nerve regeneration for future vision-restoring transplants.

evt-11-10-1202-fourth-crusade.scenario: It's November 1202. You're a knight camped with the Crusader army before Zara, a Catholic city on the Adriatic. Doge Dandolo insists the army must help Venice seize it to settle the crusaders' massive debt for their ships.
evt-11-10-1202-fourth-crusade.prompt: With Zara a fellow Christian city and the Pope opposed to the attack, what does the army do?

choices.text: Abandon the crusade entirely and sail home
Petition Rome successfully for a formal exemption
Proceed with the siege despite the Pope's objection
Negotiate a ransom from Zara instead of attacking

evt-11-10-1202-fourth-crusade.butterflyEffect: Most of the army besieged and captured Zara anyway, defying Pope Innocent III's explicit prohibition and drawing threats of excommunication. The debts and diversions born at Zara set the pattern for the crusade's next detour, the catastrophic 1204 sack of Constantinople.

evt-11-10-1599-sigismund-iii-vasa.scenario: It's July 1599 at the Riksdag of Norrköping. You are a Swedish nobleman weighing the fate of King Sigismund III, defeated the previous year at Stångebro by the forces of his uncle, Duke Charles.
evt-11-10-1599-sigismund-iii-vasa.prompt: What does the Riksdag ultimately decide regarding Sigismund's crown?

choices.text: Exile Duke Charles and confirm Sigismund's rule
Reinstate Sigismund with new conditions
Depose Sigismund as King of Sweden
Establish a joint regency shared by both claimants

evt-11-10-1599-sigismund-iii-vasa.butterflyEffect: The Riksdag deposed Sigismund as King of Sweden, leaving Duke Charles as regent and later King Charles IX. The split ended the Polish-Swedish union and ignited decades of Polish-Swedish wars over the disputed succession.

evt-11-10-1865-henry-wirz.scenario: It's autumn 1865 in Washington, D.C. You serve on the military commission trying Captain Henry Wirz, the Confederate officer who commanded Andersonville Prison, where thousands of Union captives died.
evt-11-10-1865-henry-wirz.prompt: What verdict does the tribunal reach?

choices.text: Acquitted for lack of direct evidence
Case dismissed under a general amnesty
Guilty, sentenced to death by hanging
Guilty, but sentenced only to life imprisonment

evt-11-10-1865-henry-wirz.butterflyEffect: Wirz was found guilty and hanged on November 10, 1865, becoming the only Confederate officer executed specifically for war crimes committed during the Civil War. His trial set an early precedent for holding commanders accountable for conditions in prison camps under their control.

evt-11-10-1871-henry-morton-stanley.scenario: It is 10 November 1871, near Lake Tanganyika. You are a New York Herald journalist who has trekked hundreds of miles through East Africa searching for a missionary who vanished years ago. A gaunt, grey-bearded white man stands before a crowd in the village of Ujiji.
evt-11-10-1871-henry-morton-stanley.prompt: What do you say to confirm his identity?

choices.text: "Are you the missing British consul?"
"Dr. Livingstone, I presume?"
"I bring urgent word from the Royal Geographical Society."
"State your name and business here."

evt-11-10-1871-henry-morton-stanley.butterflyEffect: Stanley's greeting, "Dr. Livingstone, I presume?", became one of the most famous lines in exploration history once his account was published worldwide. The encounter made Stanley's career and later led him into the service of Belgium's King Leopold II, whose brutal colonization of the Congo Stanley helped make possible.

evt-11-10-1937-getulio-vargas.scenario: It is the night of 10 November 1937 in Rio de Janeiro. You are a congressman as President Getúlio Vargas announces over the radio that the constitution is suspended and a new order has begun.
evt-11-10-1937-getulio-vargas.prompt: What did Vargas do that night to seize full power?

choices.text: Negotiated a power-sharing deal with the opposition
Called immediate new elections to renew his mandate
Resigned in favor of a military junta
Dissolved Congress and suspended the constitution using a fabricated communist plot as pretext

evt-11-10-1937-getulio-vargas.butterflyEffect: Vargas dissolved Congress and suspended the 1934 constitution, citing a fabricated communist uprising plan known as the Cohen Plan as his justification. He then ruled as dictator under the corporatist Estado Novo for eight years, banning parties and censoring the press until his ouster in 1945.

evt-11-10-1945-indonesian-national-revol.scenario: It is dawn on 10 November 1945 in Surabaya. You are a pemuda fighter as the British ultimatum, issued after Brigadier Mallaby's killing, expires with no Indonesian surrender.
evt-11-10-1945-indonesian-national-revol.prompt: What did British and Indian forces do when the deadline passed?

choices.text: Withdrew to negotiate a new ceasefire
Called for United Nations mediation before acting
Handed the city over to Dutch administration without a fight
Launched a full naval, air, and land assault on the city

evt-11-10-1945-indonesian-national-revol.butterflyEffect: They launched a massive naval, air, and ground assault on Surabaya, triggering weeks of brutal urban fighting that became one of the bloodiest episodes of the revolution. The fierce resistance turned Surabaya into a national symbol, and 10 November is now marked in Indonesia as Hari Pahlawan, Heroes' Day.

evt-11-10-1969-sesame-street.scenario: It is November 10, 1969, and families across the United States tune in for the debut of a new educational program, developed by Joan Ganz Cooney and Lloyd Morrisett, that blends puppetry, live action, and animation to help prepare children for school.
evt-11-10-1969-sesame-street.prompt: What happens in the wake of the show's premiere?

choices.text: It earns positive reviews and high viewership despite some controversy
Rival networks sue to block its broadcast
It airs only in a few cities before going national years later
It is cancelled quickly due to poor ratings

evt-11-10-1969-sesame-street.butterflyEffect: Sesame Street drew positive reviews, some controversy over its pacing and content, and high viewership from its very first broadcast. It went on to run for decades on PBS, spawn adaptations in over 150 countries, and reshape expectations for educational children's television worldwide.

evt-11-10-1975-mpla.scenario: It is 10 November 1975, the eve of Angolan independence. You march north toward Luanda with FNLA and Zairian troops, backed by South African artillery, confident the capital will fall before midnight.
evt-11-10-1975-mpla.prompt: What stopped the FNLA-Zairian column just short of Luanda?

choices.text: An OAU peacekeeping force blocked the road into Luanda
Portuguese colonial troops rushed back to defend the city
Cuban-crewed rocket artillery devastated the advancing column
UNITA switched sides at the last moment to defend the capital

evt-11-10-1975-mpla.butterflyEffect: Cuban-crewed BM-21 rocket launchers, rushed in with Soviet backing, shattered the advancing column at Quifangondo. MPLA secured Luanda and declared Angola's independence the next day as the recognized government, while the FNLA never recovered, and the resulting civil war between MPLA, UNITA and foreign backers dragged on for 27 more years.

evt-11-10-1975-ss-edmund-fitzgerald.scenario: It is the night of November 10, 1975, and you are aboard the ore freighter Edmund Fitzgerald as she battles hurricane-force winds and towering waves crossing Lake Superior, the largest ship on the Great Lakes.
evt-11-10-1975-ss-edmund-fitzgerald.prompt: What ultimately happens to the ship that night?

choices.text: She rides out the storm and reaches port safely
She is abandoned at sea and later towed to shore
She sinks suddenly, and all hands are lost
She runs aground but the crew is rescued

evt-11-10-1975-ss-edmund-fitzgerald.butterflyEffect: The Fitzgerald sank suddenly without any distress call, and all 29 crew were lost. The wreck's sudden, unexplained nature spurred Coast Guard inquiries into Great Lakes shipping safety and inspired Gordon Lightfoot's ballad, keeping the disaster in public memory for decades.

evt-11-10-1989-people-s-republic-of-bulg.scenario: It is 10 November 1989 in Sofia, one day after the Berlin Wall fell. You sit on the Bulgarian Communist Party's Central Committee as an emergency session opens against Todor Zhivkov, who has ruled for 35 years.
evt-11-10-1989-people-s-republic-of-bulg.prompt: What actually ended Zhivkov's rule that day?

choices.text: Soviet tanks moved in to remove him
Crowds stormed the presidential palace in Sofia
The army staged a coup and arrested him
A Politburo vote inside the party forced his resignation

evt-11-10-1989-people-s-republic-of-bulg.butterflyEffect: The Politburo itself forced Zhivkov to resign, replacing him with Petar Mladenov rather than waiting for street revolution. This opened the door to Bulgaria's first multiparty elections in 1990 and the formal end of one-party rule, though Mladenov himself would be forced out within a year by continued pro-democracy protests.

evt-11-10-1989-fall-of-the-berlin-wall.scenario: It's the night of 9 November 1989. You command the Bornholmer Strasse checkpoint as thousands of East Berliners press against the barrier, having heard rumors that travel restrictions are being lifted.
evt-11-10-1989-fall-of-the-berlin-wall.prompt: With no clear orders from your superiors, what do you do?

choices.text: Order shots fired to disperse the crowd
Call in tanks to seal the checkpoint
Open the gate and let the crowd cross
Hold the line and wait for instructions

evt-11-10-1989-fall-of-the-berlin-wall.butterflyEffect: The guards opened the gate, and the crowd surged through within hours, an act that spread to other checkpoints and effectively ended the Wall's control over the city that same night. Formal deconstruction began the following year, and German reunification followed within twelve months.

evt-11-10-1995-nigeria.scenario: It is November 10, 1995, and you are a foreign diplomat in Lagos as a military tribunal under General Sani Abacha delivers its verdict on writer and Ogoni activist Ken Saro-Wiwa, convicted on disputed murder charges tied to his campaign against oil pollution in the Niger Delta.
evt-11-10-1995-nigeria.prompt: What does Nigeria's military government do despite worldwide appeals for clemency?

choices.text: It releases Saro-Wiwa under international pressure
It indefinitely postpones the executions
It executes Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni activists
It commutes the sentences to life imprisonment

evt-11-10-1995-nigeria.butterflyEffect: Saro-Wiwa and eight fellow Ogoni activists were hanged, provoking global outrage. Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth of Nations for years, and the case galvanized international environmental and human rights scrutiny of Shell's operations in the Niger Delta.

evt-11-10-1997-worldcom.scenario: It's October 1997. You sit on the board of MCI Communications, weighing a stunning all-stock offer from WorldCom that dwarfs the earlier bid from British Telecom.
evt-11-10-1997-worldcom.prompt: As a board member, what do you recommend to shareholders?

choices.text: Reject WorldCom and stick with the British Telecom deal
Accept WorldCom's higher all-stock offer over BT's bid
Solicit a counter-bid from GTE instead
Delay the vote indefinitely to seek better terms

evt-11-10-1997-worldcom.butterflyEffect: MCI's board accepted WorldCom's offer, creating MCI WorldCom in what was then the largest merger in US history. The combined giant collapsed in 2002 amid one of the largest accounting frauds ever uncovered, helping spur the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.

evt-11-10-1999-world-anti-doping-agency.scenario: It is 1999 in Lausanne. The Festina scandal has just exposed systematic drug use at the Tour de France, and Olympic officials fear the same rot runs through every sport. You are drafting the charter for a new body to police doping worldwide.
evt-11-10-1999-world-anti-doping-agency.prompt: What kind of organization do you create?

choices.text: A network of purely national anti-doping laboratories
A UN convention with no testing or enforcement powers
An independent international agency with government and IOC funding
An internal IOC committee reporting only to Olympic officials

evt-11-10-1999-world-anti-doping-agency.butterflyEffect: The World Anti-Doping Agency was founded as an independent body separate from the IOC, funded jointly by governments and sport. It went on to write the World Anti-Doping Code and later exposed the state-run Russian doping program, leading to Russia's ban from multiple Olympic Games.

evt-11-10-2002-2002-veterans-day-weekend.scenario: It is the evening of November 10, 2002, and you live near Van Wert, Ohio, as sirens sound warning of an approaching violent tornado during a widespread outbreak stretching across the eastern United States.
evt-11-10-2002-2002-veterans-day-weekend.prompt: What is the safest action to take right now?

choices.text: Seek shelter immediately in a basement or interior room away from windows
Drive your car away from the area at once
Go outside to watch and photograph the storm
Stand near a window to track the tornado's path

evt-11-10-2002-2002-veterans-day-weekend.butterflyEffect: The Van Wert tornado reached violent F4 intensity, the most powerful of 76 tornadoes over three days that killed 36 people, ranking among the largest November outbreaks on record. It renewed attention to issuing effective warnings for severe weather outside the traditional spring tornado season.

evt-11-10-2008-mars.scenario: It is November 10, 2008, at NASA mission control. Five months after touching down in the Martian arctic, the Phoenix lander has fallen silent as the encroaching Martian winter cuts off its solar power.
evt-11-10-2008-mars.prompt: What does NASA decide about the mission?

choices.text: It sends a repair rover to restore the lander
It extends the mission's funding for another year
It declares the mission concluded after the lander loses power
It declares the mission a failure due to a landing crash

evt-11-10-2008-mars.butterflyEffect: NASA declared the Phoenix mission concluded after confirming the lander could no longer generate power. During its short life, Phoenix confirmed water ice in the Martian arctic soil, a landmark finding that shaped later missions' focus on the planet's past and present habitability.

evt-11-10-2009-daecheong-incident.scenario: It is 10 November 2009 off Daecheong Island. You crew a South Korean patrol boat as a North Korean vessel crosses the Northern Limit Line into disputed waters.
evt-11-10-2009-daecheong-incident.prompt: How did the South Korean navy respond to the incursion?

choices.text: A diplomatic protest with no military response
Warning shots followed by direct fire that damaged the North Korean boat
A full naval blockade of North Korean ports
An immediate airstrike on the North Korean coast

evt-11-10-2009-daecheong-incident.butterflyEffect: South Korean ships fired warning shots and then direct fire, damaging the North Korean patrol boat and forcing its retreat. The clash added to rising tension along the NLL that would culminate in the sinking of the Cheonan in March 2010 and the shelling of Yeonpyeong Island later that year.

evt-11-10-2019-evo-morales.scenario: It is 10 November 2019 in La Paz. Nineteen days of protests have followed a disputed election you claimed to win outright, and the armed forces commander has just publicly suggested you step down to restore peace.

choices.text: Resign the presidency and leave the country
Declare martial law and deploy the military against protesters
Call for fresh elections while remaining in office
Dissolve congress and rule by decree

evt-11-10-2019-evo-morales.butterflyEffect: Morales resigned the presidency and fled the country, first to Mexico and then Argentina, while interim president Jeanine Áñez took power amid violent crackdowns on his supporters. His MAS party returned to power a year later when Luis Arce won the 2020 election decisively.

evt-11-10-2020-land-mines-in-the-falklan.scenario: It's the mid-1980s. You lead a British demining team on the Falkland Islands, but a string of accidents among your crews has just forced a halt to clearance work.
evt-11-10-2020-land-mines-in-the-falklan.prompt: What does the British government decide to do with the remaining minefields?

choices.text: Fence off the minefields and suspend clearance
Push through manual clearance despite the risk
Abandon the affected areas of the islands entirely
Use chemical defoliants to expose the mines

evt-11-10-2020-land-mines-in-the-falklan.butterflyEffect: The minefields were fenced off and left largely untouched for decades, inadvertently becoming havens for native penguins and flora protected from human disturbance. Ratifying the Ottawa Treaty in 1998 obligated Britain to resume clearance, a painstaking hand-operation not completed until November 2020.

evt-11-10-2020-armenia.scenario: It is 10 November 2020, and after 44 days of brutal fighting over Nagorno-Karabakh, Russia has brokered a deal to stop the bloodshed. You are Armenia's prime minister, facing a battlefield your forces are losing.
evt-11-10-2020-armenia.prompt: What do you agree to in order to end the fighting?

choices.text: Secure full international recognition of Nagorno-Karabakh's independence
Demand complete Azerbaijani withdrawal from all disputed territory
Establish a joint Armenian-Azerbaijani administration over Karabakh
Cede control of significant territories around Nagorno-Karabakh to Azerbaijan

evt-11-10-2020-armenia.butterflyEffect: Armenia agreed to withdraw from large surrounding territories it had held since the 1990s, and Russian peacekeepers moved into what remained of Karabakh. The deal triggered mass protests in Yerevan demanding Pashinyan's resignation, and set the stage for Azerbaijan's 2023 takeover of the enclave and the exodus of nearly its entire ethnic Armenian population.

evt-11-11-1778-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is dawn on 11 November 1778, and you are a Continental officer at the fort in Cherry Valley, New York, when Loyalist Rangers and Seneca and Cayuga warriors launch a surprise assault, despite earlier warnings of a coming raid.
evt-11-11-1778-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What decision by the fort's commander left civilians outside exposed to the attack?

choices.text: He ordered all civilians evacuated to Albany the night before
He surrendered the fort without a fight
He led a pre-emptive strike against the nearby Iroquois village
He dismissed warnings of an imminent raid and left houses outside the stockade unguarded

evt-11-11-1778-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Lt. Col. Ichabod Alden was killed along with dozens of soldiers and civilians in what became known as the Cherry Valley Massacre. Public outrage, coming after the earlier Wyoming Valley massacre, helped push Congress to authorize the Sullivan Expedition of 1779, which burned dozens of Iroquois towns and crops and permanently weakened the Iroquois Confederacy.

evt-11-11-1813-war-of-1812.scenario: It is 11 November 1813, and you are a British regular under Lieutenant Colonel Joseph Morrison, drawn up in open farmland near Crysler's Farm. A much larger American force under General James Wilkinson is pushing down the St. Lawrence toward Montreal, and your small mixed force of regulars, militia and Mohawk allies must hold the line.
evt-11-11-1813-war-of-1812.prompt: How do the outnumbered British-Canadian defenders repel the American advance?

choices.text: Disciplined volley fire in line formation halts the American columns
A scorched-earth retreat lures the Americans into a trap miles away
A surprise night ambush from the surrounding forest
Naval gunboats bombard the American flank from the river

evt-11-11-1813-war-of-1812.butterflyEffect: Disciplined volley fire from British regulars in line formation shattered the American attacks, and Wilkinson abandoned his advance on Montreal soon after. The defeat ended serious American hopes of conquering Canada that year and shifted the war's momentum toward the Niagara and Great Lakes fronts.

evt-11-11-1880-bushranger.scenario: It is the morning of 11 November 1880, and you stand with a restless crowd outside Old Melbourne Gaol. Inside, thousands of signatures on petitions for mercy have failed to move the colonial government, and Ned Kelly is due on the gallows within the hour.
evt-11-11-1880-bushranger.prompt: What does the Victorian government finally decide to do with Ned Kelly?

choices.text: Commute the sentence to life imprisonment
Grant a full reprieve and release him
Proceed with the hanging as scheduled
Pardon him in exchange for information on other bushrangers

evt-11-11-1880-bushranger.butterflyEffect: Despite a petition with over 30,000 signatures, the government proceeded with the hanging; Kelly reportedly said "Such is life" before he died. His execution turned him into an enduring folk figure, inspiring decades of Australian literature, art and film that recast the bushranger as a symbol of resistance to colonial authority.

evt-11-11-1918-armistice-of-11-november-.scenario: It is the morning of 11 November 1918 near Compiègne. You are a soldier in the trenches as word spreads that an armistice has just been signed in a railway carriage in the forest.
evt-11-11-1918-armistice-of-11-november-.prompt: At what hour did the armistice finally silence the guns?

choices.text: Noon, after final troop withdrawals
Midnight, the moment the papers were signed
6:00 p.m., at nightfall
11:00 a.m. Paris time

evt-11-11-1918-armistice-of-11-november-.butterflyEffect: Fighting continued right up until 11:00 a.m. Paris time, with 2,738 men dying on the war's final day. The armistice held through repeated extensions until the Treaty of Versailles took effect in 1920, whose harsh terms on Germany would help fuel the resentment that led to the Second World War.

evt-11-11-1920-the-cenotaph.scenario: It is 11 November 1920, and you stand in the crowd along Whitehall as King George V unveils Sir Edwin Lutyens' new stone monument. Behind you, a horse-drawn gun carriage bears a flag-draped coffin toward Westminster Abbey.
evt-11-11-1920-the-cenotaph.prompt: Where is the Unknown Warrior laid to rest that day?

choices.text: The Tower of London
St Paul's Cathedral
The grounds of Buckingham Palace
Westminster Abbey

evt-11-11-1920-the-cenotaph.butterflyEffect: The Unknown Warrior was buried in Westminster Abbey among Britain's kings, with soil brought from French battlefields poured over the coffin. The Cenotaph became the fixed site of the annual Remembrance Sunday service, and in 1946 it was rededicated to include the dead of the Second World War, cementing its role as Britain's central symbol of wartime loss.

evt-11-11-1926-united-states-numbered-hi.scenario: It is 11 November 1926, and you sit on a committee of state highway officials meeting under the American Association of State Highway Officials. Drivers currently rely on a confusing patchwork of privately marked "auto trails," and your task is to approve a single, logical grid for numbering the nation's roads.
evt-11-11-1926-united-states-numbered-hi.prompt: What numbering scheme do officials agree on for the new national highway grid?

choices.text: Even numbers for east-west routes, odd for north-south
Letters assigned by geographic region
Sequential numbers based on construction date
Numbers assigned according to state population

evt-11-11-1926-united-states-numbered-hi.butterflyEffect: The committee approved even numbers for east-west routes and odd numbers for north-south ones, replacing branded trails like the Lincoln Highway with a standardized federal grid. Route 66 soon became the system's most famous road, and the numbering logic later carried over into the Interstate Highway System.

evt-11-11-1934-shrine-of-remembrance.scenario: It is 11 November 1934, Armistice Day, and you stand among a vast crowd in Melbourne's Kings Domain as Victoria's new war memorial is formally dedicated.
evt-11-11-1934-shrine-of-remembrance.prompt: What annual observance will this Shrine become the focal point of for generations of Victorians?

choices.text: An annual harvest festival for rural Victoria
Anzac Day and Remembrance Day services
The opening ceremony of the Melbourne Cup
A coronation day parade

evt-11-11-1934-shrine-of-remembrance.butterflyEffect: The Shrine became the centre of Victoria's Anzac Day and Remembrance Day ceremonies, including the famous 'Ray of Light' effect when sunlight strikes the Stone of Remembrance each 11 November. It remains one of Australia's most visited war memorials, its role expanding from honouring World War I veterans to all who have served.

evt-11-11-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 11 November 1940. You pilot a Fairey Swordfish biplane launched from HMS Illustrious, closing in on the Italian battle fleet anchored in the harbour at Taranto.
evt-11-11-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: How do you and your fellow pilots strike the anchored battleships?

choices.text: A torpedo attack from carrier-launched aircraft
A coordinated submarine torpedo strike
A land-based long-range bomber raid
A close-range naval gunfire bombardment

evt-11-11-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Just 21 aircraft crippled three Italian battleships at anchor, proving that carrier-based air power alone could disable a battle fleet without a surface engagement. Japanese naval planners studied the raid closely, and many historians see it as a direct inspiration for the attack on Pearl Harbor thirteen months later.

evt-11-11-1960-1960-south-vietnamese-cou.scenario: It is 11 November 1960, and your paratroopers have ringed the presidential palace in Saigon. President Diệm's voice comes over the radio, promising to negotiate reform and even accept a coalition government if you hold your fire.
evt-11-11-1960-1960-south-vietnamese-cou.prompt: As a coup officer, what should you do with Diệm's offer to negotiate?

choices.text: Demand Diệm's live, unconditional resignation on national radio
Withdraw the paratroopers to regroup outside the city
Accept the offer and begin ceasefire talks
Press the attack immediately, before loyalist reinforcements arrive

evt-11-11-1960-1960-south-vietnamese-cou.butterflyEffect: Diệm used the stalled talks to summon loyalist troops from the Mekong Delta, then crushed the coup; its leaders, including Vương Văn Đông and Nguyễn Chánh Thi, fled into exile. The failed uprising exposed deep military discontent with Diệm and foreshadowed the successful, US-tolerated coup of November 1963 that killed him.

evt-11-11-1965-rhodesia.scenario: It is 11 November 1965, and you are a member of Southern Rhodesia's parliament as Prime Minister Ian Smith rises to read a declaration severing the colony's ties to the British Crown.
evt-11-11-1965-rhodesia.prompt: What does Smith's government declare that day?

choices.text: Rhodesia's annexation by South Africa
Unilateral independence from Britain, without agreeing to majority rule
A federation with Zambia and Malawi
Full transition to Black majority rule under British supervision

evt-11-11-1965-rhodesia.butterflyEffect: Britain and the United Nations refused to recognise Rhodesia's independence and imposed economic sanctions. The unrecognised state fought a fifteen-year guerrilla war against Black nationalist movements before the 1979 Lancaster House Agreement led to internationally recognised independence as Zimbabwe in 1980.

evt-11-11-1975-1975-australian-constitut.scenario: It is 11 November 1975 in Canberra. You are Prime Minister Gough Whitlam, summoned to Yarralumla by Governor-General Sir John Kerr as a Senate deadlock over supply bills paralyses the government.
evt-11-11-1975-1975-australian-constitut.prompt: What does Kerr do when Whitlam refuses to call an election to resolve the deadlock?

choices.text: Dissolves only the Senate, leaving Whitlam in office
Grants Whitlam emergency powers to bypass the Senate
Resigns his own position as Governor-General
Dismisses Whitlam and installs Fraser as caretaker prime minister

evt-11-11-1975-1975-australian-constitut.butterflyEffect: Kerr dismissed Whitlam and commissioned opposition leader Malcolm Fraser as caretaker prime minister on condition he call an immediate election, which Fraser's coalition then won decisively. The Dismissal remains the most contested use of vice-regal power in Australian history, still cited in debates over becoming a republic.

evt-11-11-1999-house-of-lords-act-1999.scenario: It is November 1999, and you are a hereditary peer in the House of Lords watching the Blair government's reform bill move toward royal assent, ending centuries of automatic inherited seats.
evt-11-11-1999-house-of-lords-act-1999.prompt: What compromise lets some hereditary peers keep their seats for now?

choices.text: Hereditary peerages are abolished with no transition period
Ninety-two hereditary peers remain as an interim arrangement
All hereditary peers keep their seats for their lifetimes
Hereditary peers must now stand for election to keep their seats

evt-11-11-1999-house-of-lords-act-1999.butterflyEffect: The Act stripped hereditary peers of their automatic right to sit, cutting their number from over 750 to just 92 as a temporary compromise. Full reform of the House of Lords remains unfinished a quarter-century later, with those 92 seats still occupied.

evt-11-11-2001-pierre-billaud.scenario: It is 11 November 2001, and you are travelling with a convoy of Northern Alliance fighters advancing on Taloqan alongside fellow correspondents covering the collapse of Taliban lines.
evt-11-11-2001-pierre-billaud.prompt: What deadly danger threatens journalists embedded with the advancing forces that day?

choices.text: Kidnapping for ransom by local militias
Landmines left over from the Soviet occupation
Ambush by retreating fighters along the road
Friendly fire from allied airstrikes

evt-11-11-2001-pierre-billaud.butterflyEffect: Pierre Billaud, Johanne Sutton, and Volker Handloik were killed when their convoy was caught in an ambush during the Northern Alliance advance. Their deaths, among several suffered by war correspondents that autumn, highlighted the extreme risks journalists faced covering the sudden collapse of Taliban-held territory.

evt-11-11-2002-grigori-perelman.scenario: It is 11 November 2002. Scanning the arXiv preprint server, you spot a paper titled 'The entropy formula for the Ricci flow and its geometric applications' posted by a little-known Russian geometer named Grigori Perelman.
evt-11-11-2002-grigori-perelman.prompt: What century-old mathematical problem does this preprint quietly begin to resolve?

choices.text: The Four Color Theorem
The Poincaré conjecture
The Riemann Hypothesis
Fermat's Last Theorem

evt-11-11-2002-grigori-perelman.butterflyEffect: Perelman's papers used Ricci flow to prove the Poincaré conjecture, solving one of mathematics' seven Millennium Prize Problems. He was awarded the Fields Medal in 2006 and later the Millennium Prize, but declined both and withdrew from mathematics entirely.

evt-11-11-2004-palestine-liberation-orga.scenario: It is 11 November 2004, in the lobby of a Paris military hospital crowded with journalists. Yasser Arafat has just died, and Palestinian officials must decide quickly who will speak for the movement he built.
evt-11-11-2004-palestine-liberation-orga.prompt: Who is named to succeed Arafat as PLO chairman in the following days?

choices.text: Mahmoud Abbas
Farouk Kaddoumi
Marwan Barghouti
Ahmed Qurei

evt-11-11-2004-palestine-liberation-orga.butterflyEffect: Mahmoud Abbas, already PLO secretary, was swiftly named chairman and went on to win the January 2005 presidential election. His preference for negotiation over armed struggle reshaped Palestinian politics for the next two decades.

evt-11-11-2020-typhoon-vamco.scenario: It is the night of 11 November 2020, and you are a resident of a low-lying Metro Manila neighbourhood as Typhoon Vamco's rains push the Marikina River over its banks.
evt-11-11-2020-typhoon-vamco.prompt: What should you do as floodwaters rise rapidly around your home?

choices.text: Move to higher ground or a rooftop immediately, rather than wait
Drive out through the flooded streets to reach relatives
Ignore evacuation warnings since the typhoon has already passed inland
Stay inside and wait for the water to recede naturally

evt-11-11-2020-typhoon-vamco.butterflyEffect: Vamco caused Metro Manila's worst flooding since Typhoon Ketsana in 2009, submerging entire neighbourhoods and forcing dramatic rooftop rescues. The disaster renewed criticism of upstream dam management and pushed the Philippine government to review flood-control and river-dredging programs in the years that followed.

evt-11-11-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.scenario: It is 11 November 2022, and you are a Ukrainian soldier advancing into Kherson city after weeks of Russian forces quietly withdrawing across the Dnipro River.
evt-11-11-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.prompt: What do Ukrainian troops find as they enter the city?

choices.text: Jubilant residents celebrating in the streets after Russian forces withdrew overnight
A city abandoned and destroyed by retreating Russian scorched-earth tactics
Fierce house-to-house fighting still underway
A Russian garrison still holding the city centre

evt-11-11-2022-russo-ukrainian-war.butterflyEffect: Kherson was the only regional capital Russia had captured in 2022, and its recapture was Ukraine's most significant success after the Kharkiv counteroffensive. The withdrawal shifted the front line to the Dnipro River, where it remained largely static for the rest of the war, and the victory strengthened Western resolve to keep supplying military aid to Kyiv.

evt-11-12-1330-voivode.scenario: It's November 1330, and you march with King Charles I of Hungary's army, withdrawing through a narrow forested gorge after a failed campaign to subdue the Wallachian voivode Basarab I.
evt-11-12-1330-voivode.prompt: What does Basarab do to the retreating Hungarian column?

choices.text: He ambushes it in the narrow pass, trapping and destroying much of the army
He challenges Charles to single combat to settle the war
He besieges the column's supply fortress instead
He offers a truce and lets it withdraw unmolested

evt-11-12-1330-voivode.butterflyEffect: Basarab's forces sprang an ambush at Posada, annihilating much of the retreating Hungarian army and nearly capturing King Charles himself. The victory secured Wallachia's effective independence from Hungarian overlordship, marking the emergence of the first lasting Romanian principality.

evt-11-12-1892-pudge-heffelfinger.scenario: It's 12 November 1892, and you play for the Allegheny Athletic Association against the rival Pittsburgh Athletic Club. Your club's officials, desperate to win, quietly offer a cash bonus to their star lineman for this single game.

choices.text: He refuses the money to preserve his amateur status
He turns the offer down and switches to boxing
He accepts $500 to play, becoming football's first documented professional
He demands a share of gate receipts instead of a flat fee

evt-11-12-1892-pudge-heffelfinger.butterflyEffect: Heffelfinger took the $500, later confirmed by a club expense ledger, making him the first athlete known to be paid to play American football. The precedent helped open the door to organized professional leagues, culminating decades later in the founding of the NFL.

evt-11-12-1912-terra-nova-expedition.scenario: It is November 12, 1912, on the Ross Ice Shelf. Your search party has trekked for days looking for Robert Falcon Scott's polar party, missing for eight months since their attempt on the South Pole.
evt-11-12-1912-terra-nova-expedition.prompt: What did the search party find, and what did they do?

choices.text: They found no trace of the party and presumed them lost at sea
They found the tent with the bodies and diaries, and left them under a cairn
They found the men alive but suffering from severe frostbite
They recovered the bodies and shipped them back to England for burial

evt-11-12-1912-terra-nova-expedition.butterflyEffect: They found a snow-covered tent containing the bodies of Scott, Wilson, and Bowers along with Scott's diaries and letters. Rather than attempt the impossible task of returning the bodies to Britain, they left them under a cairn of snow and ice, and the recovered diaries turned Scott's fatal failure into one of Britain's most enduring stories of heroism and sacrifice.

evt-11-12-1920-kingdom-of-italy.scenario: It is November 1920 in Rapallo, and you are among the diplomats hammering out the border between the Kingdom of Italy and the newly formed Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes after the collapse of Austria-Hungary.
evt-11-12-1920-kingdom-of-italy.prompt: What did the resulting Treaty of Rapallo grant to Italy?

choices.text: Trieste, Ljubljana, and full control of Montenegro
The entire Dalmatian coastline including Split and Dubrovnik
Istria, Zadar, and a number of Adriatic islands, but not Fiume
Nothing; the treaty confirmed the pre-war border unchanged

evt-11-12-1920-kingdom-of-italy.butterflyEffect: Italy secured Istria, Zadar, and several Adriatic islands, but the contested port of Fiume was left as an independent free state rather than annexed outright. The unresolved status of Fiume fed nationalist agitation, and Italy would seize it outright in 1924, deepening tensions with Yugoslavia that lingered into the Second World War.

evt-11-12-1932-government-of-western-aus.scenario: It is November 1932 in the Western Australian wheat belt. At the government's request, soldiers armed with Lewis machine guns have been sent to deal with tens of thousands of emus devastating farmers' crops.
evt-11-12-1932-government-of-western-aus.prompt: What was the outcome of this military operation against the emus?

choices.text: The government replaced the soldiers with a permanent army unit
The operation largely failed and was withdrawn after killing relatively few emus
The soldiers wiped out the regional emu population within days
The emus were successfully herded into a new reserve

evt-11-12-1932-government-of-western-aus.butterflyEffect: The so-called Emu War was a conspicuous failure: the emus proved fast, scattered, and hard to hit, and the operation was called off within weeks having killed only a small fraction of the birds. Farmers instead turned to bounty systems and exclusion fencing, and the episode became a famous, wry example of military force failing against wildlife.

evt-11-12-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the morning of 12 November 1944 over a Norwegian fjord near Tromsø. You are flying a Lancaster bomber with No. 617 Squadron, carrying a Tallboy bomb toward the German battleship Tirpitz, moored below as a last-ditch fleet-in-being.
evt-11-12-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What was the outcome of this raid, Operation Catechism, against the Tirpitz?

choices.text: A smoke screen hid the ship completely and no bombs found their target
Tirpitz shot down most of the attacking bombers and survived undamaged
Tirpitz was struck by Tallboy bombs and capsized, sinking in the fjord
Tirpitz escaped to open sea before the bombers arrived

evt-11-12-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Tallboy bombs struck the battleship, causing a massive explosion that capsized her with heavy loss of life among her crew. Her destruction removed the last major surface threat to Arctic convoys and freed Royal Navy resources to be redirected toward the Pacific theatre against Japan.

evt-11-12-1970-1970-bhola-cyclone.scenario: It is mid-November 1970 in East Pakistan. The Bhola cyclone has just torn through the Ganges Delta, and relief supplies from the central government in West Pakistan are arriving slowly, if at all, to the devastated coastal villages.
evt-11-12-1970-1970-bhola-cyclone.prompt: What political consequence followed from the government's slow disaster response?

choices.text: It prompted swift reconciliation between East and West Pakistan
It led the Pakistani president to resign within days of the storm
It fueled Bengali nationalist anger that helped drive the movement toward Bangladesh's independence
It caused the United Nations to permanently station a disaster agency in Dhaka

evt-11-12-1970-1970-bhola-cyclone.butterflyEffect: Anger over the sluggish, unequal relief effort deepened Bengali resentment toward the West Pakistan-dominated government and helped the Awami League sweep East Pakistan in December's elections. That grievance fed directly into the crisis of 1971, contributing to the Bangladesh Liberation War and the country's eventual independence.

evt-11-12-1991-santa-cruz-massacre.scenario: It is 12 November 1991 in Dili, East Timor. You march with hundreds of students toward Santa Cruz cemetery to honor a young independence activist killed weeks earlier, and Indonesian troops are massing at the gates.
evt-11-12-1991-santa-cruz-massacre.prompt: What happens when the procession reaches the cemetery?

choices.text: Police arrest only the demonstration's leaders
Troops disperse the marchers with tear gas only
Officials negotiate a peaceful truce with organizers
Soldiers open fire on the unarmed crowd

evt-11-12-1991-santa-cruz-massacre.butterflyEffect: Soldiers opened fire on the unarmed mourners, killing at least 250. Foreign journalists secretly filmed the killings, and the smuggled footage broadcast worldwide shattered Indonesia's official narrative, galvanizing international pressure that helped build the case for East Timor's 1999 independence referendum.

evt-11-12-1996-saudia.scenario: It's the evening of 12 November 1996 over Charkhi Dadri, India. A Saudia Boeing 747 climbs out of Delhi on a shared air corridor as a Kazakhstan Airlines Il-76 descends toward the same airspace at a conflicting altitude.
evt-11-12-1996-saudia.prompt: What change did this disaster force onto Indian civil aviation?

choices.text: India banned foreign carriers from its airspace
Delhi's airport was permanently closed to international traffic
Separate one-way corridors for arriving and departing aircraft were created
All flights over India were rerouted through Pakistan

evt-11-12-1996-saudia.butterflyEffect: The two aircraft collided head-on, killing all 349 people aboard in the deadliest mid-air collision in history. Investigators found the Il-76 had descended below its assigned level; India responded by separating inbound and outbound traffic into distinct corridors and accelerated the global push to make TCAS collision-avoidance systems mandatory on airliners.

evt-11-12-2001-american-airlines-flight-.scenario: It is 12 November 2001. Your Airbus A300 climbs out of JFK moments behind a Japan Airlines 747, and sudden wake turbulence jolts the cabin as the first officer fights the controls.
evt-11-12-2001-american-airlines-flight-.prompt: What control input did investigators later blame for the vertical stabilizer's failure?

choices.text: Excessive aileron input
Rapid, full rudder pedal reversals
Sudden autopilot disengagement
Manual override of the elevator trim

evt-11-12-2001-american-airlines-flight-.butterflyEffect: The NTSB concluded that rapid, full rudder pedal reversals by the first officer snapped the vertical stabilizer off in flight, not the turbulence itself. The finding triggered scrutiny of American Airlines' rudder training and led to industry-wide reviews of pilot instruction on wake turbulence recovery.

evt-11-12-2011-silvio-berlusconi.scenario: It is November 2011. Italy's bond yields are spiraling, parliament has just passed an austerity package, and Silvio Berlusconi is about to hand in his resignation as prime minister.
evt-11-12-2011-silvio-berlusconi.prompt: What followed Berlusconi's resignation as the debt crisis raged?

choices.text: Italy immediately called new general elections
Italy announced its withdrawal from the eurozone
Economist Mario Monti was appointed to lead a technocratic government
Berlusconi's coalition partner Umberto Bossi became prime minister

evt-11-12-2011-silvio-berlusconi.butterflyEffect: President Napolitano appointed economist Mario Monti to head a technocratic government tasked with pushing through austerity and reforms without facing elections. Monti's unelected cabinet steadied bond markets in the short term, but the resentment it generated helped fuel the populist backlash that reshaped Italian politics for a decade.

evt-11-12-2014-european-space-agency.scenario: It is 12 November 2014, and mission controllers watch anxiously as ESA's Philae lander, released from the Rosetta spacecraft, descends toward the surface of comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko.
evt-11-12-2014-european-space-agency.prompt: What happens in the crucial moments right after Philae's first touchdown?

choices.text: Its harpoons fail to fire and it bounces before settling in a shadowed spot
The lander crashes and is destroyed on impact
The harpoons fire perfectly and it anchors on the first attempt
It lands precisely on its intended target site in full sunlight

evt-11-12-2014-european-space-agency.butterflyEffect: Philae's anchoring harpoons failed to fire, and the lander bounced twice before settling in the shadow of a cliff, starving its solar panels of sunlight. It still returned unprecedented data on the comet's composition before its battery died within 60 hours, briefly reawakening in mid-2015 as the comet neared the sun.

evt-11-12-2014-philae-spacecraft.scenario: It is the afternoon of 12 November 2014 at ESA's control centre in Darmstadt. Your lander Philae is descending toward comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko after a ten-year journey, and its anchoring harpoons are supposed to fire on contact.
evt-11-12-2014-philae-spacecraft.prompt: What actually happened when Philae touched down on the comet?

choices.text: It anchored perfectly on the first attempt exactly as planned
It bounced off the surface twice before coming to rest in an unplanned, shadowed location
It missed the comet entirely and drifted into deep space
It collided with Rosetta during descent and was destroyed

evt-11-12-2014-philae-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: The harpoons failed to fire and a hold-down thruster did not activate, so Philae bounced twice before settling in a shadowed spot with poor sunlight for its solar panels. It still returned about 64 hours of data before its battery died, achieving the first soft landing on a comet nucleus and giving scientists rich chemical readings that reshaped theories about comets delivering organic molecules to early Earth.

evt-11-12-2014-mil-mi-24.scenario: It's 12 November 2014, and you patrol the tense line of contact separating Armenian and Azerbaijani forces in Nagorno-Karabakh. Ceasefire violations have been rising for weeks as your Mi-24 gunship banks over the front.
evt-11-12-2014-mil-mi-24.prompt: What actually happened to this Armenian helicopter that day?

choices.text: It was forced to land by a sudden mechanical failure
It was shot down by Azerbaijani forces, killing its crew and inflaming the ceasefire
It safely returned to base after a routine patrol
It intercepted and destroyed an Azerbaijani drone

evt-11-12-2014-mil-mi-24.butterflyEffect: Azerbaijani forces downed the helicopter with a man-portable missile, killing all three crew members. The incident triggered furious accusations on both sides and a spike in border skirmishes, foreshadowing the far larger clashes of the 2016 Four-Day War and the 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh War.

evt-11-12-2015-suicide-attack.scenario: It is 12 November 2015, in the busy market streets of Bourj el-Barajneh, a Shia neighborhood in southern Beirut, when two suicide bombers detonate their explosives minutes apart amid the evening crowds.
evt-11-12-2015-suicide-attack.prompt: Which group claims responsibility for the bombing?

choices.text: No group ever claims responsibility
The Islamic State (ISIS)
Hezbollah, in an internal purge
Al-Qaeda

evt-11-12-2015-suicide-attack.butterflyEffect: The Islamic State claimed the attack, its deadliest strike inside Lebanon in years. It struck a day before the coordinated Paris attacks of 13 November, and the far smaller global attention it received compared to Paris fueled lasting debate over disparities in how Western media cover attacks outside Europe.

evt-11-12-2020-playstation-5.scenario: It is November 12, 2020, launch day for the PlayStation 5 in North America, Japan, and Australia. You've been refreshing retailer websites for weeks trying to secure a unit.
evt-11-12-2020-playstation-5.prompt: What was the immediate reality for most buyers trying to get a PS5 at launch?

choices.text: Retailers sold consoles bundled only with unrelated hardware
Consoles were plentiful and prices were cut within weeks
Sony restricted sales to Japan only for the first year
Severe shortages meant most buyers couldn't find one in stores for months

evt-11-12-2020-playstation-5.butterflyEffect: A global semiconductor shortage combined with pandemic-driven demand and bot-driven scalpers left the PS5 in short supply for well over a year after launch. Sony's struggle to keep shelves stocked reshaped how retailers handled console drops, pushing many toward invite-only and lottery-style sales systems.

evt-11-12-2021-los-angeles-county-superi.scenario: It's 12 November 2021, and you sit in a packed Los Angeles courtroom as a judge reviews a long-running conservatorship that has controlled the finances and personal life of a pop superstar, amid a global #FreeBritney campaign outside.

choices.text: She terminates the conservatorship entirely, restoring the singer's legal rights
She extends the conservatorship for another five years
She transfers control to a court-appointed public administrator
She orders a new medical evaluation before any decision

evt-11-12-2021-los-angeles-county-superi.butterflyEffect: The judge ended Britney Spears's conservatorship outright, closing an arrangement that had controlled her earnings and daily life for over a decade. The case's publicity fueled a wave of state-level conservatorship reform bills aimed at preventing similar abuses of the guardianship system.

evt-11-12-2022-boeing-b-17-flying-fortre.scenario: It is November 12, 2022, at the Wings Over Dallas airshow. A vintage B-17 Flying Fortress and a Bell P-63 Kingcobra are flying a formation pass for the crowd below.
evt-11-12-2022-boeing-b-17-flying-fortre.prompt: What happened during this warbird display, and what changed afterward?

choices.text: The aircraft completed the pass safely and the show continued without incident
The two aircraft collided in mid-air, destroying both and killing all aboard
The B-17 made an emergency landing after an engine fire
The P-63 was grounded before the flight due to a mechanical fault

evt-11-12-2022-boeing-b-17-flying-fortre.butterflyEffect: The P-63 struck the B-17 during the pass, and both historic aircraft crashed, killing all six crew members aboard with no injuries on the ground. The NTSB investigation that followed led air show organizers to tighten separation and sequencing rules for formation flying by historic aircraft nationwide.

evt-11-13-1642-first-english-civil-war.scenario: It is 13 November 1642 and you ride with the Royalist army at Turnham Green, west of London, facing a Parliamentarian force roughly twice your size drawn up to block the road to the capital.
evt-11-13-1642-first-english-civil-war.prompt: What did the Royalist commanders decide to do?

choices.text: Withdraw without engaging and retreat toward Oxford
Split the army and attempt to encircle London from two sides
Open negotiations for an immediate surrender
Launch an immediate frontal assault on the larger army

evt-11-13-1642-first-english-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Rather than risk battle against the larger force, the Royalists withdrew without fighting and fell back to Oxford, which became Charles I's wartime capital for the rest of the conflict. The failure to seize London while it was vulnerable meant the war would grind on for years rather than end quickly.

evt-11-13-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 13 November 1775. You march with General Richard Montgomery's Continental Army column toward Montreal, fresh off the fall of Fort St. Jean, with the British garrison badly outnumbered inside the city.
evt-11-13-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What does the British garrison do as the Americans approach?

choices.text: It mounts a prolonged last stand inside the city
It burns the city rather than let it fall
It surrenders without significant resistance
It counterattacks Montgomery's column at the gates

evt-11-13-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Montreal surrendered without significant resistance, while British Governor Guy Carleton slipped away downriver to Quebec City. The victory gave Americans control of much of Canada, but their subsequent siege of Quebec that winter failed catastrophically, ending hopes of adding Canada as a fourteenth colony.

evt-11-13-1914-zaian-war.scenario: It is 13 November 1914 near El Herri in the Moroccan Atlas foothills. You are Colonel René Laverdure, marching a column of soldiers, wounded men, and civilians back toward Khénifra, and scouts warn that Zaian riders under Mouha ou Hammou Zayani are massing close by.
evt-11-13-1914-zaian-war.prompt: What does Laverdure decide to do with the column?

choices.text: Halt and dig in on defensible high ground
Turn back to Khénifra without the wounded
Press on with the march despite the risk
Send scouts ahead and wait for reinforcements before moving

evt-11-13-1914-zaian-war.butterflyEffect: Laverdure pressed on regardless, and the Zaians ambushed the strung-out column, killing him and inflicting one of France's heaviest colonial defeats, capturing artillery pieces that were paraded as trophies. The disaster forced France to adopt combined-arms "groupes mobiles" and prolonged the Zaian War until 1921.

evt-11-13-1927-holland-tunnel.scenario: It is 13 November 1927, and you are an engineer inspecting the newly finished tunnel beneath the Hudson River. Thousands of cars will soon pass through daily, and exhaust fumes trapped underwater could poison every driver inside.
evt-11-13-1927-holland-tunnel.prompt: What system was built into the tunnel to keep drivers from being asphyxiated?

choices.text: A mechanical ventilation system with giant fans
Open shafts relying on natural airflow
A rule allowing only electric vehicles through
Water sprays to scrub exhaust from the air

evt-11-13-1927-holland-tunnel.butterflyEffect: Giant fans in ventilation towers exchanged the tunnel's entire air supply roughly every 90 seconds, a design pioneered by chief engineer Clifford Holland, who died before its completion and for whom the tunnel was named. This forced-ventilation approach became the template for underwater vehicle tunnels built around the world afterward.

evt-11-13-1940-walt-disney.scenario: It is 13 November 1940 at the Broadway Theatre in New York, and you are a Disney sound engineer making last checks before the premiere of Fantasia. Dozens of speakers have been rigged around the auditorium instead of just behind the screen.
evt-11-13-1940-walt-disney.prompt: What made this Fantasia premiere a first for commercial cinema?

choices.text: Multiple speakers around the theater created directional, stereophonic sound
It used the first synchronized spoken dialogue track
It was screened with an early laugh-track audio overlay
It was the first film shown entirely in three-strip Technicolor

evt-11-13-1940-walt-disney.butterflyEffect: Fantasia debuted "Fantasound," a multi-channel directional sound system using extra speakers around the theater to create an immersive, stereophonic effect. It was costly to install and only a handful of theaters could show it that way, but the concept anticipated stereo and surround-sound formats that became standard decades later.

evt-11-13-1966-arab-israeli-conflict.scenario: It is dawn on 13 November 1966. You watch Israeli armored columns roll into the West Bank village of as-Samu in Jordan, retaliation for a Fatah landmine that killed Israeli soldiers days before.
evt-11-13-1966-arab-israeli-conflict.prompt: What does the Israeli operation do once it reaches the village?

choices.text: It strikes only a nearby Jordanian army barracks
It issues warnings and withdraws without engaging
It destroys homes and a school in a large raid
It negotiates directly with village elders

evt-11-13-1966-arab-israeli-conflict.butterflyEffect: Israeli forces demolished dozens of homes and a school in the largest cross-border raid since 1956. The attack humiliated Jordan's King Hussein for failing to defend the village, pushing Jordan closer to Egypt and Syria's defense pact and helping set the stage for the Six-Day War the following June.

evt-11-13-1974-amityville-murders.scenario: It is 13 November 1974 and you are a police officer arriving at a house on Ocean Avenue in Amityville, New York, after a report of gunfire. The sole survivor, 23-year-old Ronald DeFeo Jr., meets you at the door with an account of what happened to his family.
evt-11-13-1974-amityville-murders.prompt: What did DeFeo initially tell investigators had happened?

choices.text: That his family had been killed by the Mafia in a contract hit
That his father had killed the others before taking his own life
That his family died in an accidental gas explosion
That an unknown intruder had broken in and fled

evt-11-13-1974-amityville-murders.butterflyEffect: DeFeo first claimed his family had been killed by the Mafia in a contract hit before confessing he had shot all six himself. He was convicted on six counts of second-degree murder and sentenced to 25 years to life; the case later inspired the book and film "The Amityville Horror," turning the house into a lasting piece of American horror folklore.

evt-11-13-1985-nevado-del-ruiz.scenario: It is the evening of 13 November 1985. You are a civil defense official in Armero, Colombia, watching ash fall from Nevado del Ruiz as hazard maps warn that melting ice could send mudflows toward the town.
evt-11-13-1985-nevado-del-ruiz.prompt: What do local authorities decide about evacuating Armero?

choices.text: They decide conditions do not yet warrant evacuation
They order an immediate full evacuation
They call in the army to forcibly clear the town
They evacuate only the town's hospital patients

evt-11-13-1985-nevado-del-ruiz.butterflyEffect: Officials delayed, reassured by radio broadcasts that conditions were not yet critical. Hours later pyroclastic flows melted the summit's ice cap, sending lahars down the valley that buried Armero, killing more than 20,000 people. The disaster became a landmark case study in volcanic hazard communication, reshaping how nations issue and act on eruption warnings.

evt-11-13-1993-china-northern-airlines-f.scenario: It is 13 November 1993 and you are a passenger on China Northern Airlines Flight 6901, an MD-82 descending toward Ürümqi Diwopu International Airport after departing Beijing.
evt-11-13-1993-china-northern-airlines-f.prompt: What did investigators later determine caused the crash on approach?

choices.text: Pilot error during the landing approach
Severe unexpected turbulence over the airport
A miscommunication that sent the plane to the wrong runway
A mid-air engine explosion

evt-11-13-1993-china-northern-airlines-f.butterflyEffect: Investigators attributed the crash to pilot error during the approach; 12 of the 102 people aboard were killed. The accident added to scrutiny of crew training and approach procedures at Chinese domestic carriers during a period of rapid airline expansion.

evt-11-13-1995-nigeria-airways-flight-35.scenario: It is 13 November 1995 and you are aboard Nigeria Airways Flight 357 as it comes in to land at Kaduna International Airport on the second leg of its journey from Yola to Lagos.
evt-11-13-1995-nigeria-airways-flight-35.prompt: What happened as the Boeing 737 touched down at Kaduna?

choices.text: Hijackers seized control during the descent
The aircraft was struck by a flock of birds on final approach
It overran the runway, sparking a fire that destroyed the aircraft
An engine caught fire mid-flight before landing

evt-11-13-1995-nigeria-airways-flight-35.butterflyEffect: The aircraft overran the runway and caught fire, destroying the plane; all 14 crew survived but 11 of the 124 passengers died. The crash added to mounting safety concerns about Nigeria Airways, which struggled on for several more years before being liquidated in 2003.

evt-11-13-2000-philippines.scenario: It is 13 November 2000 in Manila. You sit in the House of Representatives as Speaker Manny Villar formally transmits the articles of impeachment against President Joseph Estrada over corruption and gambling payoff allegations.
evt-11-13-2000-philippines.prompt: What happens next in the constitutional process against Estrada?

choices.text: The Supreme Court immediately dismisses the charges
The Senate convenes to hold an impeachment trial
Estrada resigns the same day the articles are filed
Congress votes to remove Villar as Speaker instead

evt-11-13-2000-philippines.butterflyEffect: The Senate convened an impeachment trial in December, but in January 2001 senators voted to block opening a key evidence envelope, sparking mass "People Power II" protests. Estrada resigned days later and Vice President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo was sworn in as his successor.

evt-11-13-2015-november-2015-paris-attac.scenario: It is just after 9:40 PM on 13 November 2015. You command the French police unit surrounding the Bataclan theatre, where gunmen are holding hundreds of concertgoers hostage after a mass shooting.
evt-11-13-2015-november-2015-paris-attac.prompt: What decision by police ends the siege?

choices.text: Evacuate the surrounding streets and wait the attackers out
Negotiate for hours to secure a peaceful surrender
Cut power and gas to force the attackers outside
Storm the theatre in a tactical assault

evt-11-13-2015-november-2015-paris-attac.butterflyEffect: The BRI tactical unit stormed the theatre; the remaining attackers detonated their suicide vests as police closed in. France declared a nationwide state of emergency that night, extended repeatedly for nearly two years, reshaping French security law and European counterterrorism cooperation.

evt-11-14-1680-gottfried-kirch.scenario: It is the night of 14 November 1680, and through your telescope in Coburg you spot a faint smudge of light moving against the fixed stars, unlike anything catalogued before.
evt-11-14-1680-gottfried-kirch.prompt: As the discoverer, what should you do with this sighting?

choices.text: Report it only to church officials as a religious omen
Write to fellow astronomers across Europe so the object can be tracked and verified
Keep the sighting secret until you can claim sole credit
Assume it is a previously catalogued comet and ignore it

evt-11-14-1680-gottfried-kirch.butterflyEffect: Kirch's find was the first comet ever discovered by telescope, and its brilliant tail caused widespread public alarm across Europe that winter. Isaac Newton later used careful observations of this same comet to test his theory of gravity and confirm that comets follow elliptical orbits like planets.

evt-11-14-1851-moby-dick.scenario: It is November 14, 1851, and you are Herman Melville, watching the American edition of your whaling novel Moby-Dick reach booksellers after its earlier release in London.
evt-11-14-1851-moby-dick.prompt: How do critics and the reading public initially respond to the book?

choices.text: It is banned in several states for its content
It becomes an instant bestseller and critical triumph
It is ignored entirely, with no reviews published
It sells poorly and receives mixed reviews

evt-11-14-1851-moby-dick.butterflyEffect: The novel received mixed reviews and sold poorly, leaving it out of print by the time Melville died in 1891. Its reputation as a Great American Novel only took hold in the 20th century after a revival around the 1919 centennial of Melville's birth, influencing writers like William Faulkner and D. H. Lawrence.

evt-11-14-1910-eugene-burton-ely.scenario: You are strapped into a fragile biplane on a wooden platform bolted to the bow of the cruiser USS Birmingham, anchored in Hampton Roads, the deck sloping down toward the gray water just ahead.
evt-11-14-1910-eugene-burton-ely.prompt: How do you handle the launch as the runway runs out before you have enough lift?

choices.text: Wait for the ship to build forward speed before launching
Refuse to launch until the platform is lengthened
Dip the nose briefly to build airspeed, then climb away
Cut the engine and glide down to the water instead

evt-11-14-1910-eugene-burton-ely.butterflyEffect: Ely's plane dipped so low his propeller clipped the water before he pulled up and landed safely on a nearby Virginia beach. The flight proved aircraft could operate from warships, and within months Ely completed the first shipboard landing too, laying the groundwork for the modern aircraft carrier.

evt-11-14-2008-2008-g20-washington-summi.scenario: It is November 14, 2008, and you are a finance minister arriving in Washington, D.C. for the first-ever G20 leaders' summit, called together as the global financial crisis threatens banks and economies worldwide.
evt-11-14-2008-2008-g20-washington-summi.prompt: What core commitment do the assembled leaders agree to at this summit?

choices.text: Coordinate policy to stabilize markets and reject protectionism
Merge national central banks into one global institution
Adopt a single global currency to replace the dollar
Return the world's economies to the gold standard

evt-11-14-2008-2008-g20-washington-summi.butterflyEffect: Leaders pledged coordinated action to stabilize financial markets, reform regulation, and avoid protectionist trade measures during the crisis. The summit marked the G20's rise as the world's premier forum for economic coordination, setting up further meetings in 2009 that produced major stimulus and IMF funding commitments.

evt-11-14-2016-2016-kaikoura-earthquake.scenario: It is just after midnight on November 14, 2016, and you are driving along the coastal highway near Kaikōura, New Zealand, when the ground begins to heave violently and you feel the road buckle beneath your car.
evt-11-14-2016-2016-kaikoura-earthquake.prompt: With a tsunami possible along this coastline, what should you do once the shaking stops?

choices.text: Drive further along the coast to inspect the damage
Return home to check on your property first
Move immediately to high ground away from the coast
Stay in your car and wait for radio instructions

evt-11-14-2016-2016-kaikoura-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Coastal residents who moved to higher ground survived tsunami waves that struck parts of the shoreline within minutes. The quake ruptured multiple faults simultaneously, closed State Highway 1 for over a year, and became one of the most intensively studied earthquakes in the world for how it revealed faults can trigger one another in a single event.

evt-11-14-2017-rancho-tehama-shootings.scenario: It is the morning of November 14, 2017, and you are a teacher at an elementary school in Rancho Tehama, California. Gunfire erupts outside your classroom as a gunman moves between properties in the community, and you must protect the children in your care.
evt-11-14-2017-rancho-tehama-shootings.prompt: What finally stopped the gunman's rampage across the community?

choices.text: He ran out of ammunition and fled on foot
A SWAT team sniper shot him from a distance
A police officer rammed his vehicle to stop it
He surrendered after a lengthy standoff

evt-11-14-2017-rancho-tehama-shootings.butterflyEffect: A Corning police officer rammed the gunman's stolen vehicle, forcing a confrontation in which he took his own life. The attack, carried out by a man neighbors had reported for violent behavior, fueled renewed debate in California over gun violence restraining orders and background-check loopholes for homemade firearms.

evt-11-15-655-penda-of-mercia.scenario: You march with King Penda of Mercia in November 655, pursuing Oswiu of Northumbria's smaller retreating force. The trail leads toward the swollen River Winwaed, and your allies from East Anglia grow uneasy about crossing it.
evt-11-15-655-penda-of-mercia.prompt: What fatal decision leads to the destruction of Penda's army at the Winwaed?

choices.text: Pursuing Oswiu's army across the dangerously flooded river
Retreating to Mercia before engaging Oswiu at all
Agreeing to a truce and dividing Northumbria peacefully
Converting to Christianity to secure Oswiu's alliance

evt-11-15-655-penda-of-mercia.butterflyEffect: Penda pressed the pursuit across the flooded river, and when Oswiu turned to fight, the swollen waters drowned more of Penda's retreating men than the battle itself killed; Penda and Æthelhere were both slain. His death ended pagan resistance among the Anglo-Saxon kings and let Christianity spread further through Mercia, though the kingdom would rise again to power under his son Wulfhere.

evt-11-15-1859-evangelos-zappas.scenario: You are organizing Athens' revived Olympic Games in 1859, funded by the wealthy expatriate Evangelos Zappas. The city has no stadium fit for the ancient tradition, and King Otto's officials are lukewarm about the whole idea.
evt-11-15-1859-evangelos-zappas.prompt: How do you proceed with hosting the games?

choices.text: Postpone the games until a purpose-built stadium can be constructed
Cancel the athletic events and hold only the industrial exhibition
Move the games to Constantinople where facilities already exist
Hold events in a central public square, pairing athletics with an exhibition of Greek industry

evt-11-15-1859-evangelos-zappas.butterflyEffect: The games went ahead in the public Loudovikou Square, combining athletic contests with an agricultural and industrial exhibition, though critics mocked their disorganization. Zappas kept funding further Olympiads, and his bequest eventually paid to restore the Panathenaic Stadium, the venue for the first modern Olympics in 1896.

evt-11-15-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 15 November 1864 outside Atlanta. You serve under General Sherman as his army prepares to march toward Savannah, deliberately cutting itself off from its supply lines.
evt-11-15-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What strategy does Sherman order for the march ahead?

choices.text: Wait for reinforcements from Grant before beginning the march
Forage for supplies from the land while destroying railroads and war-supporting infrastructure
Maintain a secure supply line back to Chattanooga before advancing
Turn back to fortify and hold Atlanta instead of advancing further

evt-11-15-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Sherman's army lived off the countryside, destroying railroads, mills, and plantations as it cut a sixty-mile-wide swath to Savannah. The campaign broke the Confederacy's capacity to sustain the war, hastened Union victory, and left deep Southern resentment that shaped Reconstruction-era politics for generations.

evt-11-15-1889-pedro-ii-of-brazil.scenario: You are a minister at Emperor Pedro II's court in Rio de Janeiro on 15 November 1889. Word arrives that Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca has led troops into the streets and proclaimed a republic, ending six decades of imperial rule.
evt-11-15-1889-pedro-ii-of-brazil.prompt: How does Pedro II respond when told the monarchy has been overthrown?

choices.text: He refuses to resist and accepts exile in Europe
He flees south to establish a rival imperial government
He abdicates in favor of Princess Isabel to preserve the monarchy
He orders loyal troops to crush the uprising

evt-11-15-1889-pedro-ii-of-brazil.butterflyEffect: Pedro II refused to resist and accepted exile, sailing for Europe with his family days later; he would die in Paris in 1891. His fall ended the Empire of Brazil and ushered in the First Brazilian Republic, a change hastened by landowners' anger over his daughter Isabel's abolition of slavery the previous year.
