evt-11-15-1908-atrocities-in-the-congo-f.scenario: It is November 1908. You are a member of the Congo Reform Association, having spent years publicizing eyewitness accounts of forced-labor mutilations under King Leopold II's rubber regime. International outrage has finally reached a tipping point.
evt-11-15-1908-atrocities-in-the-congo-f.prompt: What happens to the Congo Free State as a result of this pressure?

choices.text: The League of Nations places the territory under international trusteeship
Leopold II voluntarily grants the Congolese population full citizenship rights
Britain intervenes militarily and adds the territory to its African colonies
Belgium formally annexes the territory as the Belgian Congo, ending Leopold's personal rule

evt-11-15-1908-atrocities-in-the-congo-f.butterflyEffect: Belgium's parliament voted to annex the territory, and on 15 November 1908 the Congo Free State became the Belgian Congo, ending Leopold II's personal rule. Forced-labor abuses eased but did not disappear under state colonial administration, and the campaign became a landmark in early international human-rights activism.

evt-11-15-1922-1922-guayaquil-general-st.scenario: It is 15 November 1922, the third day of a general strike in Guayaquil. Utility and transport workers have won wide public support for their demands, but army units are now massing to clear the streets.
evt-11-15-1922-1922-guayaquil-general-st.prompt: What do the strike leaders decide as troops move to disperse the crowd?

choices.text: Send a delegation to surrender unconditionally to military commanders
Immediately disband and send workers home to avoid confrontation
Remain gathered downtown to press their demands rather than disperse
Arm themselves and prepare to fight the approaching soldiers

evt-11-15-1922-1922-guayaquil-general-st.butterflyEffect: The strikers held their ground in the streets, and soldiers opened fire on the assembled crowd, a tragedy that shocked the nation. The massacre became a defining moment for Ecuador's labor movement, galvanizing organized labor and pushing later governments toward workplace protections.

evt-11-15-1959-clutter-family-murders.scenario: You are a Kansas Bureau of Investigation agent called to a remote farmhouse outside Holcomb, where four members of the Clutter family have been found dead and no clear motive or clue points to a suspect.
evt-11-15-1959-clutter-family-murders.prompt: Which lead should you pursue to identify the killers?

choices.text: Wait for the killers to come forward and confess voluntarily
Focus solely on local farmhands with old grudges against the family
Assume it was a random drifter and close the case quickly
Follow up on a former cellmate's tip about a rumored hidden safe

evt-11-15-1959-clutter-family-murders.butterflyEffect: A tip from Floyd Wells, a former cellmate of Richard Hickock who recalled him talking about a hidden safe at the Clutter farm, led investigators straight to Hickock and Perry Smith, both arrested within weeks. Their trial and 1965 executions were later chronicled by Truman Capote in "In Cold Blood," a book that helped pioneer the American true-crime genre.

evt-11-15-1988-buran-spacecraft.scenario: It is 15 November 1988 at Baikonur Cosmodrome. You watch the Soviet Union's Buran orbiter, mounted atop the giant Energia rocket, lift off on its first spaceflight — with no cosmonauts aboard.
evt-11-15-1988-buran-spacecraft.prompt: What made this flight historically distinct from NASA's Space Shuttle missions?

choices.text: Buran docked with the Mir space station before returning to Earth
Buran completed its entire orbital mission and landing fully autonomously without a crew
Buran was launched using strap-on solid rocket boosters like the Shuttle
Buran carried a crew of test cosmonauts who controlled its landing manually

evt-11-15-1988-buran-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: Buran completed its orbital mission and landed itself with no crew and no pilot input, a feat NASA's shuttles never matched. It proved the technology, but the Soviet collapse drained funding, the program was shelved, and this remained Buran's only flight before the orbiter was destroyed in a 2002 hangar collapse.

evt-11-15-2000-jharkhand.scenario: You are a tribal rights activist from the mineral-rich Chota Nagpur plateau, having spent decades demanding a homeland for Adivasi communities long overlooked by a distant Bihar government in Patna.
evt-11-15-2000-jharkhand.prompt: How do you respond as the Bihar Reorganisation Act finally takes effect on this date?

choices.text: Celebrate the birth of Jharkhand, with Ranchi as its capital
Boycott the ceremony over the choice of capital city
Push to merge the region into West Bengal instead
Reject the new state and demand full independence instead

evt-11-15-2000-jharkhand.butterflyEffect: Jharkhand became India's 28th state on 15 November 2000, its creation date chosen to honour tribal hero Birsa Munda's birthday. The new state inherited enormous mineral wealth but also years of political instability, cycling through many chief ministers in its first decade.

evt-11-15-2001-microsoft.scenario: It's November 15, 2001, and lines are forming outside electronics stores across North America. You're deciding whether to buy Microsoft's brand-new Xbox console, its first entry into a market dominated by Sony and Nintendo.
evt-11-15-2001-microsoft.prompt: What flagship launch title convinced many gamers the Xbox was worth buying?

choices.text: Halo: Combat Evolved
Gears of War
Halo 2
Fable

evt-11-15-2001-microsoft.butterflyEffect: Halo: Combat Evolved became the console's killer app, proving Microsoft could compete on gameplay, not just hardware muscle. Its success helped establish Xbox Live and turned Halo into Microsoft's signature franchise, anchoring the Xbox brand in the console market for the next two decades.

evt-11-15-2002-hu-jintao.scenario: You are a delegate at the 16th Communist Party Congress in Beijing, November 2002, watching Jiang Zemin hand the title of General Secretary to Hu Jintao in China's first orderly leadership succession.
evt-11-15-2002-hu-jintao.prompt: What happens to control of China's military as Hu takes the party's top post?

choices.text: Military command passes to Premier Wen Jiabao
Jiang Zemin retains the Central Military Commission chairmanship for two more years
Military authority is split evenly among the Politburo Standing Committee
Hu Jintao immediately assumes full command of the military

evt-11-15-2002-hu-jintao.butterflyEffect: Jiang Zemin kept the chairmanship of the Central Military Commission until 2004, showing that Hu's power was initially incomplete. This staggered handover became a notable feature of the transition, one Xi Jinping's own succession a decade later would deliberately avoid by taking full control immediately.

evt-11-15-2003-2003-istanbul-bombings.scenario: It is Saturday morning, 15 November 2003, and you are a Turkish counter-terrorism officer rushing to the smoking ruins outside two Istanbul synagogues, where truck bombs have just torn through Shabbat crowds. Intelligence chatter suggests this al-Qaeda-linked cell is not finished.
evt-11-15-2003-2003-istanbul-bombings.prompt: What target did the same terror cell strike just five days later, on 20 November?

choices.text: The Istanbul airport terminal
The British Consulate and HSBC's Istanbul headquarters
The Turkish parliament building
A third synagogue in Ankara

evt-11-15-2003-2003-istanbul-bombings.butterflyEffect: Despite the warnings, the cell detonated two more truck bombs on 20 November at the British Consulate and the HSBC Turkey headquarters, killing British Consul-General Roger Short. The attacks, traced to a network around Habib Akdas with links to al-Qaeda, deepened Turkish-Western intelligence cooperation and led to dozens of arrests and convictions in the following years.

evt-11-15-2007-cyclone-sidr.scenario: It is 14 November 2007, and Extremely Severe Cyclone Sidr is barreling toward Bangladesh's southwestern coast with winds over 250 km/h. You are a village leader responsible for hundreds of families near the Sundarbans.
evt-11-15-2007-cyclone-sidr.prompt: What is your best course of action as the storm approaches?

choices.text: Move everyone to the riverbank, believing the water will absorb the storm's force
Stay in your homes and reinforce the roofs against the wind
Wait until the storm makes landfall to assess whether evacuation is truly necessary
Lead your community to designated cyclone shelters immediately, heeding official warnings

evt-11-15-2007-cyclone-sidr.butterflyEffect: Bangladesh's government and volunteers carried out one of the largest evacuations in the country's history, moving millions to concrete cyclone shelters before landfall. The death toll, estimated between roughly 3,400 and 15,000, was still severe but far lower than the 1991 cyclone, and Sidr further strengthened the country's early-warning and shelter network.

evt-11-15-2010-2010-shanghai-fire.scenario: You supervise a hasty renovation on a 28-story Shanghai apartment tower on 15 November 2010, home mostly to retired teachers. Workers without proper welding permits are cutting metal near flammable insulation netting wrapped around the scaffolding to save time.
evt-11-15-2010-2010-shanghai-fire.prompt: What should you do before letting the welding continue?

choices.text: Let welders finish the section quickly since the deadline is close
Swap the flammable netting for cheaper material to cut costs, then proceed
Post a single fire extinguisher nearby and continue as scheduled
Halt all welding until proper permits, fireproof materials, and safety monitors are in place

evt-11-15-2010-2010-shanghai-fire.butterflyEffect: Sparks from unlicensed welders ignited the flammable netting, and the fire raced up the building, killing 58 people. The disaster exposed widespread illegal subcontracting in China's construction boom and triggered nationwide safety inspections and stricter fire codes for high-rise renovations.

evt-11-15-2012-xi-jinping.scenario: You are a delegate at the 18th Communist Party Congress in Beijing, November 2012, watching Hu Jintao step down and hand power to Xi Jinping in a transition being closely compared to Hu's own succession ten years earlier.
evt-11-15-2012-xi-jinping.prompt: What makes Xi's transfer of power notably different from Hu Jintao's in 2002?

choices.text: Hu retains the military chairmanship for two more years, as Jiang did
Power is split between Xi and Premier Li Keqiang
Xi delays becoming president for several years
Xi receives the Central Military Commission chairmanship immediately

evt-11-15-2012-xi-jinping.butterflyEffect: Unlike Jiang Zemin, who kept his military post for two more years, Hu Jintao relinquished the Central Military Commission chairmanship to Xi at once, giving Xi complete control from day one. This faster, fuller handover let Xi consolidate authority quickly, setting the stage for his sweeping anti-corruption campaign and the eventual removal of presidential term limits in 2018.

evt-11-15-2016-hong-kong-high-court.scenario: You are newly elected Legislative Council member Baggio Leung in October 2016. During your swearing-in you altered the oath and used language insulting to China, and Beijing's government swiftly demands your removal.
evt-11-15-2016-hong-kong-high-court.prompt: What does Hong Kong's High Court ultimately rule about your and Yau Wai-ching's seats?

choices.text: The court rules the government's challenge invalid
The court refers the matter to Beijing without a ruling
The court allows them to retake the oath and keep their seats
The court disqualifies them from the Legislative Council

evt-11-15-2016-hong-kong-high-court.butterflyEffect: On 15 November 2016 the High Court disqualified both lawmakers, upholding the government's legal challenge after Beijing's National People's Congress reinterpreted the Basic Law's oath requirements. The ruling opened the door to further disqualifications of pro-democracy legislators and deepened the rift between Beijing and Hong Kong's opposition ahead of the 2019 protests.

evt-11-15-2017-2017-west-attica-floods.scenario: It is early morning on 15 November 2017 in Mandra, west of Athens. A wall of water suddenly surges down the ravine through town after night-long torrential rain, and cars and people are being swept into the streets.
evt-11-15-2017-2017-west-attica-floods.prompt: Caught in the sudden flash flood, what is the safest action to take right now?

choices.text: Immediately abandon your car and move to higher ground on foot
Drive quickly through the flooded street to reach home
Stay inside your car and wait for the water to recede
Shelter in the basement of the nearest building

evt-11-15-2017-2017-west-attica-floods.butterflyEffect: The floods killed 24 people, Attica's third-deadliest on record. Investigations afterward pointed to illegal quarries and unregulated construction that had narrowed natural drainage channels for years, triggering prosecutions and renewed calls for stricter urban planning in the region.

evt-11-15-2022-world-population.scenario: It's November 15, 2022. You're a demographer at the United Nations watching the global population clock cross a historic threshold: eight billion people alive on Earth at once.
evt-11-15-2022-world-population.prompt: According to UN projections issued around this milestone, what did the future hold for global population growth?

choices.text: Growth would slow, with population peaking later this century before declining
The population would immediately begin shrinking due to falling birth rates
Growth would remain constant at the same pace seen throughout the 20th century
Population growth would accelerate sharply due to falling infant mortality

evt-11-15-2022-world-population.butterflyEffect: The UN projected growth would keep slowing, with world population peaking around the mid-2080s near 10.4 billion before gradually declining, driven by falling fertility rates worldwide. That projection reshaped policy debates from labor shortages to pension systems in aging societies.

evt-11-16-534-code-of-justinian.scenario: It's 534 in Constantinople. As one of Justinian's legal commissioners, you've spent months incorporating new imperial constitutions and correcting errors found in the original 529 Code.
evt-11-16-534-code-of-justinian.prompt: What must you do to give the revised code lasting legal authority?

choices.text: Leave the 529 edition standing unchanged
Issue it as an official second edition superseding the first
Merge it silently into the Digest without formal reissue
Let provincial courts interpret the law independently

evt-11-16-534-code-of-justinian.butterflyEffect: The revised Codex repetitae praelectionis replaced the 529 edition as the authoritative text. Bundled with the Digest, Institutes, and later Novellae into the Corpus Juris Civilis, it became the foundation of civil law across Europe for over a thousand years.

evt-11-16-1476-stephen-the-great.scenario: You are a Wallachian boyar in November 1476, watching Moldavian troops under Stephen the Great and Transylvanian forces under Stephen Báthory march in to depose the Ottoman-backed prince and install a new ruler.
evt-11-16-1476-stephen-the-great.prompt: Who did Stephen the Great and Stephen Báthory place on Wallachia's throne?

choices.text: Vlad III the Impaler (Dracula)
Mircea the Younger
Radu the Handsome
Basarab Laiotă

evt-11-16-1476-stephen-the-great.butterflyEffect: They restored Vlad III, known as the Impaler or Dracula, to the Wallachian throne. His triumph was brief: within weeks his Ottoman-backed rival Basarab Laiotă returned with Turkish support, and Vlad was killed in battle that December, ending the campaign almost as quickly as it began.

evt-11-16-1532-spanish-conquest-of-the-i.scenario: It's 16 November 1532 at Cajamarca. You are Atahualpa, marching toward the plaza to meet a small delegation of Spanish conquistadors, confident your thousands of retainers guarantee your safety.
evt-11-16-1532-spanish-conquest-of-the-i.prompt: How do you approach the meeting with Pizarro's men?

choices.text: Enter the square with an unarmed ceremonial retinue
Send envoys and refuse to attend in person
Withdraw and avoid the Spanish entirely
Bring your army fully armed for battle

evt-11-16-1532-spanish-conquest-of-the-i.butterflyEffect: Trusting his overwhelming numbers, Atahualpa entered the square largely unarmed. Pizarro's men ambushed the gathering, massacred his retinue, and captured him — a stunning victory that toppled the Inca Empire and opened South America to Spanish colonization.

evt-11-16-1632-gustavus-adolphus.scenario: You ride beside King Gustavus Adolphus at the Battle of Lützen on November 16, 1632, when thick gun smoke and fog swallow the battlefield and you suddenly lose sight of the king amid a cavalry charge.
evt-11-16-1632-gustavus-adolphus.prompt: What happens to the king during the battle?

choices.text: He retreats safely before the fighting ends
He is wounded but survives the battle
He is killed leading a cavalry charge
He is captured by imperial forces

evt-11-16-1632-gustavus-adolphus.butterflyEffect: Gustavus Adolphus was shot and killed leading his cavalry, though his Swedish forces still won the battle. His death ended Sweden's era of direct royal battlefield command; leadership passed to Chancellor Axel Oxenstierna and generals like Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar, shifting Swedish strategy in the Thirty Years' War toward more cautious, conciliar direction.

evt-11-16-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It's 16 November 1776, and you command the Patriot garrison of Fort Washington on Manhattan's Hudson bluffs as Hessian and British columns close in from three sides, vastly outnumbering your men.
evt-11-16-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What must Colonel Robert Magaw decide as the fort's defenses collapse?

choices.text: Evacuate every soldier by ferry to New Jersey under fire
Hold the fort indefinitely awaiting Washington's relief
Surrender the garrison once the outer defenses are overrun
Launch a counterattack down the bluffs into the assault columns

evt-11-16-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Magaw surrendered, and nearly 3,000 Continental soldiers along with vital cannon and supplies were captured—one of the war's worst American losses. The disaster forced Washington into a desperate retreat across New Jersey, bringing the Revolution to its lowest ebb before the Trenton counterstroke that December.

evt-11-16-1885-trial-of-louis-riel.scenario: It's July 1885 in a Regina courtroom, and you are Louis Riel, on trial for treason after leading the Métis and First Nations resistance in the North-West Rebellion, as your lawyers urge a defense that could spare your life.
evt-11-16-1885-trial-of-louis-riel.prompt: What did Riel insist on doing against his own lawyers' advice?

choices.text: Plead guilty and beg the court for mercy
Attempt to flee the courtroom before the verdict
Claim he had acted on secret orders from British officials
Reject the insanity plea and defend his own actions and beliefs

evt-11-16-1885-trial-of-louis-riel.butterflyEffect: Riel rejected the insanity defense and instead spoke in his own words to justify the rebellion and the Métis cause, sealing his conviction. He was hanged that November, and the execution became a lasting symbol of English-French division in Canada, fueling Quebec nationalism for generations.

evt-11-16-1914-world-war-i.scenario: You are a Serbian soldier holding a defensive line in November 1914, weeks after repelling an earlier Austro-Hungarian invasion, as enemy artillery signals a renewed assault along the Kolubara River.
evt-11-16-1914-world-war-i.prompt: What followed the Austro-Hungarian offensive that November?

choices.text: Serbia signed an armistice to end the fighting
Serbian forces were pushed back and Belgrade briefly fell
Serbian forces immediately routed the Austro-Hungarian army
Austro-Hungarian forces withdrew without engaging

evt-11-16-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The renewed attack pushed Serbian forces back, and Belgrade fell to Austro-Hungarian troops on December 2, 1914. But Serbian commander Radomir Putnik launched a dramatic counteroffensive, recapturing Belgrade by December 15 and inflicting heavy losses, a victory that boosted Serbian morale and Allied hopes early in the war.

evt-11-16-1938-albert-hofmann.scenario: It's November 1938 in your Sandoz lab in Basel. You've just synthesized the 25th compound in a series of lysergic acid derivatives meant to yield a new circulatory stimulant, but animal tests show nothing remarkable.
evt-11-16-1938-albert-hofmann.prompt: What do you do with this seemingly unremarkable compound, LSD-25?

choices.text: Test it on yourself immediately
Destroy the sample as a failed experiment
Set it aside and move on to other research
Publish the synthesis as a breakthrough drug

evt-11-16-1938-albert-hofmann.butterflyEffect: Hofmann shelved LSD-25 for five years. In April 1943 he resynthesized it on a hunch, accidentally absorbed some through his skin, and experienced the first LSD trip — launching decades of psychiatric research and later the 1960s psychedelic counterculture.

evt-11-16-1944-world-war-ii.scenario: You are a soldier of the U.S. First Army crouched near the Hürtgen Forest on November 16, 1944, as wave after wave of Allied bombers thunder overhead ahead of a planned ground assault toward the Rur River.
evt-11-16-1944-world-war-ii.prompt: What was Operation Queen meant to accomplish?

choices.text: Break through German lines and push toward the Rhine
Capture the port of Antwerp
Open a new supply route through the Ardennes
Relieve the besieged garrison at Bastogne

evt-11-16-1944-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Despite the massive bombardment, German defenses in the dense Hürtgen Forest held firm, and the ground offensive bogged down into some of the costliest fighting the U.S. Army faced in the West. The delay left American forces stretched thin along the front just weeks before Germany's surprise Ardennes counteroffensive, the Battle of the Bulge.

evt-11-16-1973-richard-nixon.scenario: It is November 16, 1973. The Arab oil embargo has triggered fuel shortages and long gas lines across America, and you are a congressional aide handing President Nixon a bill to sign that construction firms in Alaska have been waiting years for.
evt-11-16-1973-richard-nixon.prompt: What project does Nixon's signature authorize?

choices.text: Creation of the Strategic Petroleum Reserve
A national gasoline rationing program
Expansion of the Alaska Highway
Construction of the Trans-Alaska Pipeline

evt-11-16-1973-richard-nixon.butterflyEffect: Nixon signed the Trans-Alaska Pipeline Authorization Act, clearing legal hurdles that had stalled the project since its 1969 proposal. Built from 1974 to 1977, the 800-mile pipeline carried Prudhoe Bay oil to the port of Valdez and became a cornerstone of U.S. domestic oil supply for decades afterward.

evt-11-16-1988-supreme-soviet.scenario: You are a deputy in the Estonian Supreme Soviet in Tallinn. Nationalist sentiment is rising, and a resolution is on the floor asserting that Estonian law can override directives from Moscow.
evt-11-16-1988-supreme-soviet.prompt: What does the Estonian Supreme Soviet vote to do?

choices.text: Declare Estonian law supreme over Soviet law within the republic
Formally dissolve the Estonian Supreme Soviet
Request Soviet troops be permanently stationed in Tallinn
Declare full immediate independence from the USSR

evt-11-16-1988-supreme-soviet.butterflyEffect: Estonia became the first Soviet republic to pass a declaration of sovereignty, asserting the supremacy of its own laws over Soviet ones. Other Baltic and Soviet republics followed with similar declarations, accelerating the nationalist wave that led to the Baltic states' full independence by 1991.

evt-11-16-1989-1989-murders-of-jesuits-i.scenario: News reaches Washington that Salvadoran soldiers have murdered six Jesuit priests and two women at their university residence in San Salvador. You sit on a US congressional committee overseeing military aid to El Salvador's government.
evt-11-16-1989-1989-murders-of-jesuits-i.prompt: How does the US Congress respond to the killings?

choices.text: Increase military funding to help defeat the FMLN faster
Take no action, citing internal Salvadoran affairs
Significantly reduce military aid to El Salvador's armed forces
Send US combat troops to occupy San Salvador

evt-11-16-1989-1989-murders-of-jesuits-i.butterflyEffect: Congress cut US military assistance to El Salvador, and the killings became a turning point that pressured both sides toward negotiations, contributing to the 1992 Chapultepec Peace Accords ending the civil war. The case also spurred prosecutions decades later, including convictions in Spain of former Salvadoran officers.

evt-11-16-1992-suffolk.scenario: It's November 1992 near Hoxne, Suffolk. A friend has asked you to sweep a field with your metal detector for a lost hammer, and your machine suddenly signals something large and metallic buried in the plough soil.
evt-11-16-1992-suffolk.prompt: What do you do after unearthing a few gold coins and silver spoons?

choices.text: Sell the pieces quietly to a dealer
Dig up everything yourself to see what's there
Stop digging and report the find to archaeologists
Rebury it and tell no one

evt-11-16-1992-suffolk.butterflyEffect: Eric Lawes stopped digging and alerted the landowner and archaeologists, who excavated the site the next day, preserving crucial context. The result was the Hoxne Hoard, the largest hoard of Roman gold and silver ever found in Britain, later valued at over £1.75 million and shared with Lawes and the farmer.

evt-11-16-1992-hoxne-hoard.scenario: It's November 1992 and you're sweeping a Suffolk farmer's field near Hoxne with a metal detector, hoping to recover a lost hammer, when your machine screams over a mass of metal buried just beneath the plough soil.
evt-11-16-1992-hoxne-hoard.prompt: What should you do once you realise you've struck gold and silver Roman objects?

choices.text: Stop digging, mark the spot, and report it to the landowner and archaeological authorities
Sell the whole hoard privately to an antiques dealer
Dig up everything yourself and sell the coins to collectors
Keep the find secret and rebury it for later

evt-11-16-1992-hoxne-hoard.butterflyEffect: Eric Lawes stopped digging, marked the spot, and called in archaeologists, who excavated the hoard intact rather than letting it be scattered by amateur digging. The find—14,865 coins and 200 pieces of silver tableware and jewellery—became Britain's largest late-Roman hoard, was valued at £1.75 million, and now anchors a gallery at the British Museum.

evt-11-16-1997-wei-jingsheng.scenario: It's 16 November 1997, and you are a Chinese official reviewing the file of Wei Jingsheng, the Democracy Wall essayist who has now spent 18 years in and out of prison for his writings.
evt-11-16-1997-wei-jingsheng.prompt: What did the Chinese government do with Wei on this day?

choices.text: Released him quietly within Beijing
Transferred him to a labor camp for further sentencing
Deported him to the United States on medical parole
Placed him under permanent house arrest in Shanghai

evt-11-16-1997-wei-jingsheng.butterflyEffect: Wei was deported to the United States on medical parole rather than being released within China. From exile he founded the Wei Jingsheng Foundation in New York in 1998, becoming one of the most prominent international voices campaigning for human rights and democratic reform in China.

evt-11-16-2005-australia-men-s-national-.scenario: It is a tense night in Sydney. The scoreline against Uruguay is level after two legs, and the World Cup qualifying playoff has gone to a penalty shootout in front of a roaring home crowd.
evt-11-16-2005-australia-men-s-national-.prompt: What happens as Australia steps up to take the decisive penalty?

choices.text: Australia wins the shootout to qualify for the World Cup
The match is abandoned and replayed in Montevideo
Australia wins on away goals before penalties are needed
Uruguay wins the shootout and advances instead

evt-11-16-2005-australia-men-s-national-.butterflyEffect: John Aloisi buried the winning penalty and goalkeeper Mark Schwarzer's earlier save proved decisive, sending Australia to the 2006 World Cup for the first time since 1974. The result reinvigorated domestic interest in soccer and helped justify Australia's move from the Oceania confederation to Asia shortly after.

evt-11-16-2009-space-shuttle-program.scenario: You are a NASA ground controller at Kennedy Space Center on November 16, 2009, watching Space Shuttle Atlantis climb away on mission STS-129 toward the International Space Station, with the shuttle program's retirement looming.
evt-11-16-2009-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What was the main cargo purpose of this mission?

choices.text: Begin construction of the station's solar arrays
Test the first Ares rocket components
Conduct a repair mission on the Hubble Space Telescope
Deliver spare parts to sustain the station after shuttle retirement

evt-11-16-2009-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: Atlantis delivered two ExPRESS Logistics Carriers loaded with spare parts—gyroscopes, batteries, and other critical hardware—to stockpile supplies the station would need after the shuttle fleet retired in 2011. This foresight helped keep the ISS operational through years of relying solely on smaller resupply craft.

evt-11-16-2020-el-dorado-fire.scenario: It's 5 September 2020 in El Dorado Ranch Park, California. You watch a couple set up a pyrotechnic smoke-generating device to reveal their baby's gender, in brush parched by months of drought.
evt-11-16-2020-el-dorado-fire.prompt: What should you do to prevent a wildfire?

choices.text: Stop them and insist they use a safer alternative
Let them proceed since the device looks small
Only worry if you see actual open flame
Assume nearby vegetation is too green to burn

evt-11-16-2020-el-dorado-fire.butterflyEffect: The device ignited the dry brush, sparking the El Dorado Fire, which burned 22,744 acres over 71 days and killed a firefighter. The couple hosting the party were charged with involuntary manslaughter, and the disaster fueled a wider push to ban pyrotechnic gender-reveal devices.

evt-11-16-2022-artemis-program.scenario: It's the early morning of 16 November 2022 at Kennedy Space Center. After multiple scrubbed launch attempts due to hydrogen leaks, you're the flight director deciding whether Artemis I can finally fly.
evt-11-16-2022-artemis-program.prompt: What determines whether the uncrewed Space Launch System launches today?

choices.text: Confirm the hydrogen leak is fixed and proceed with launch
Cancel the Artemis program
Delay indefinitely pending a new investigation
Scrub again to fully redesign the rocket

evt-11-16-2022-artemis-program.butterflyEffect: Engineers resolved the leak and Artemis I launched successfully, sending an uncrewed Orion capsule on a 25-day journey around the Moon. Its success cleared the way for Artemis II's crewed lunar flyby and NASA's planned Artemis III landing.

evt-11-17-1558-elizabeth-i.scenario: It is 17 November 1558. Word reaches Hatfield House that Queen Mary I has died, and you are among the courtiers watching Elizabeth Tudor step forward as the new queen.
evt-11-17-1558-elizabeth-i.prompt: What is Elizabeth's most urgent task as she takes the throne?

choices.text: Declare war on Spain at once
Execute all surviving Catholic claimants to the throne
Settle the kingdom's religious future
Marry a foreign prince immediately to secure an heir

evt-11-17-1558-elizabeth-i.butterflyEffect: Elizabeth moved quickly to establish the Elizabethan Religious Settlement, restoring a moderate Protestant church and avoiding the violent swings of her predecessors' reigns. Her 45-year rule brought the defeat of the Spanish Armada, a flourishing of English literature under Shakespeare and Marlowe, and, since she never married, a succession crisis resolved only by James VI of Scotland's accession.

evt-11-17-1796-french-revolutionary-wars.scenario: It is 17 November 1796 near the marshes of Arcole in northern Italy. You serve under General Bonaparte, whose army has spent three days stalled trying to force a narrow bridge held by Austrian defenders.
evt-11-17-1796-french-revolutionary-wars.prompt: What move finally broke the Austrian line at Arcole?

choices.text: A flanking march through the marshes to cut off the Austrian retreat
A prolonged siege of a nearby fortress town
A massed cavalry charge straight across the bridge
A naval bombardment of the Austrian rear

evt-11-17-1796-french-revolutionary-wars.butterflyEffect: French troops under Augereau waded through the marshes to outflank the Austrians and threaten their line of retreat, forcing a withdrawal. The victory cemented Napoleon's reputation as a daring tactician and kept his Italian campaign alive, momentum that carried France to the favorable Treaty of Campo Formio in 1797.

evt-11-17-1950-14th-dalai-lama.scenario: Chinese troops have crossed into eastern Tibet, and you sit with the Tibetan National Assembly in Lhasa debating how to respond to the crisis, with the young 14th Dalai Lama still three years short of the traditional age for full authority.
evt-11-17-1950-14th-dalai-lama.prompt: What does the Assembly decide to do?

choices.text: Appeal to Britain to send troops to defend Lhasa
Enthrone the Dalai Lama early to assume full power
Send the government into exile in India immediately
Transfer authority entirely to the Panchen Lama

evt-11-17-1950-14th-dalai-lama.butterflyEffect: The Assembly enthroned the 15-year-old Dalai Lama with full temporal power to lead Tibet through the crisis. He governed under increasing Chinese pressure until the 1959 uprising forced him to flee to India, where he founded the Tibetan government-in-exile and became a global voice for Tibetan autonomy, later winning the 1989 Nobel Peace Prize.

evt-11-17-1973-watergate-scandal.scenario: You sit among 400 newspaper editors in Orlando as President Nixon takes the podium, facing questions about his taxes and the Watergate break-in.
evt-11-17-1973-watergate-scandal.prompt: What does Nixon famously insist to the assembled editors?

choices.text: "I accept full responsibility and will resign tonight"
"I will not answer any further questions about Watergate"
"The break-in was ordered by me personally"
"I am not a crook"

evt-11-17-1973-watergate-scandal.butterflyEffect: Nixon's declaration, 'I am not a crook,' became one of the most quoted lines of the scandal, a phrase that came to symbolize public doubt rather than reassurance. The remark deepened skepticism of his administration and became a lasting shorthand for the credibility collapse that ended in his resignation in August 1974.

evt-11-17-1973-athens-polytechnic-uprisi.scenario: It is the night of 16–17 November 1973 in Athens. You are a student barricaded inside the Polytechnic with hundreds of others, and army tanks have just pulled up outside the gates.
evt-11-17-1973-athens-polytechnic-uprisi.prompt: What did the students inside do when the army issued its ultimatum to leave?

choices.text: Immediately evacuate through the back streets
Set fire to the Polytechnic buildings themselves
Barricade the gates and refuse to leave the occupied campus
Negotiate a formal amnesty with the junta's officers

evt-11-17-1973-athens-polytechnic-uprisi.butterflyEffect: They refused, and before dawn a tank crashed through the gates; troops and police killed dozens in the crackdown that followed. The bloodshed discredited the junta so badly that it collapsed within months, paving the way for Greece's return to democracy in 1974.

evt-11-17-1989-velvet-revolution.scenario: It is 17 November 1989 in Prague. You march with thousands of students marking International Students' Day, and riot police lines have just moved to block your path on Národní Street.
evt-11-17-1989-velvet-revolution.prompt: What should the students do when police move to disperse the peaceful march?

choices.text: Fight back with improvised weapons against police lines
Disperse quietly and abandon further protest
Negotiate on the spot for immediate multi-party elections
Hold their ground peacefully and let public outrage build

evt-11-17-1989-velvet-revolution.butterflyEffect: The brutal police crackdown that evening outraged the public and ignited nationwide protests, culminating in a two-hour general strike on 27 November. Within days the Communist Party's leadership resigned, ending 41 years of one-party rule and opening the way to Václav Havel's presidency.

evt-11-17-1993-united-states-house-of-re.scenario: It is 17 November 1993 on the floor of the U.S. House of Representatives. President Clinton has spent weeks lobbying wavering members ahead of a knife-edge vote on the North American Free Trade Agreement.
evt-11-17-1993-united-states-house-of-re.prompt: What did the House do on this vote?

choices.text: Approved the agreement only with Canada, excluding Mexico
Voted down the NAFTA implementing legislation
Postponed the vote indefinitely under pressure from unions
Passed the NAFTA implementing legislation

evt-11-17-1993-united-states-house-of-re.butterflyEffect: The House passed the NAFTA implementing legislation by a bipartisan margin, clearing the way for the agreement to take effect on 1 January 1994. It reshaped North American trade by expanding cross-border manufacturing and investment, while fueling a lasting political debate over its effect on American manufacturing jobs.

evt-11-17-1997-luxor.scenario: It is the morning of 17 November 1997 at the Temple of Hatshepsut near Luxor. You are among foreign tourists visiting the ancient site when armed militants suddenly open fire on the crowd.
evt-11-17-1997-luxor.prompt: How did the Egyptian government respond in the aftermath of the massacre?

choices.text: Closed Luxor's temples permanently to all visitors
Opened negotiations offering the militants political concessions
Launched a sweeping security crackdown on Islamist militant networks
Publicly blamed foreign tour operators for the attack

evt-11-17-1997-luxor.butterflyEffect: The attack, carried out by militants of al-Gama'a al-Islamiyya, killed 62 people, mostly foreign tourists, and devastated Egypt's tourism economy for years. Public revulsion at the killings helped push the group toward renouncing violence by 1999, a turning point in Egypt's long fight against Islamist insurgency.

evt-11-17-2000-alberto-fujimori.scenario: It is November 2000. President Alberto Fujimori has fled Peru for Japan amid a corruption scandal and faxed his resignation to Congress from abroad.
evt-11-17-2000-alberto-fujimori.prompt: How did Peru's Congress respond to Fujimori's resignation letter?

choices.text: Accepted the resignation immediately without debate
Rejected the resignation and declared him removed for moral incapacity
Voted to reinstate him with expanded emergency powers
Ignored the fax and continued to recognize him as president

evt-11-17-2000-alberto-fujimori.butterflyEffect: Congress rejected the resignation and instead voted to remove Fujimori from office on grounds of "moral incapacity," a rare constitutional maneuver. He remained in Japan for years before his eventual extradition from Chile in 2007, leading to his 2009 conviction for human rights abuses and corruption.

evt-11-17-2013-tornado-outbreak-of-novem.scenario: It is midday on 17 November 2013 in Washington, Illinois. Sirens are wailing as an EF4 tornado bears down on your neighborhood with only minutes of warning.
evt-11-17-2013-tornado-outbreak-of-novem.prompt: What is the safest thing to do right now?

choices.text: Get in your car and try to outrun it
Stand near a window to watch the tornado's path
Go outside and shelter beneath a highway overpass
Take shelter in an interior room or basement away from windows

evt-11-17-2013-tornado-outbreak-of-novem.butterflyEffect: The Washington tornado tore through the town in minutes, destroying hundreds of homes as part of a 77-tornado outbreak across seven states. The rare, violent November outbreak pushed meteorologists to reexamine cold-season tornado warning systems across the Midwest.

evt-11-17-2013-tatarstan-airlines-flight.scenario: Investigators pore over flight data from a Boeing 737 that crashed nose-first at Kazan airport during a night-time go-around, killing everyone aboard.
evt-11-17-2013-tatarstan-airlines-flight.prompt: What did investigators conclude caused the crash?

choices.text: A bomb had been planted aboard the aircraft
The crew mishandled the aborted landing, stalling the aircraft
Both engines failed simultaneously due to fuel contamination
Severe icing on the wings caused loss of control

evt-11-17-2013-tatarstan-airlines-flight.butterflyEffect: The board found the crew mishandled the go-around, disengaging the autopilot and pulling the nose up too steeply, stalling the aircraft into the runway. The disaster, one of several fatal Russian airline crashes that decade, intensified scrutiny of pilot training and cockpit procedures at Russia's regional carriers, feeding regulatory reforms and consolidation of smaller airlines under Rosaviatsia.

evt-11-17-2019-covid-19.scenario: In Hubei province, a 55-year-old man falls ill with an unusual pneumonia. No one yet knows it, but doctors will later identify his case as the earliest known infection of a new coronavirus.
evt-11-17-2019-covid-19.prompt: What happens in the weeks that follow this first case?

choices.text: Health authorities dismiss it as ordinary seasonal flu with no follow-up
A cluster of similar pneumonia cases emerges, linked to a Wuhan market
The case remains isolated and no further infections occur
A vaccine is developed within days and the outbreak is contained

evt-11-17-2019-covid-19.butterflyEffect: By December, a cluster of similar pneumonia cases emerged around Wuhan's Huanan Seafood Market, prompting China to notify the WHO on 31 December 2019. The virus spread globally within months, leading the WHO to declare a pandemic in March 2020 and a global health emergency that lasted until May 2023.

evt-11-18-1583-siege-of-godesberg.scenario: It is 17 December 1583, and you command the garrison holding the fortress of Godesburg for Archbishop Gebhard von Waldburg. For weeks Bavarian engineers have tunneled beneath your walls, and their mine is now packed and ready to fire.
evt-11-18-1583-siege-of-godesberg.prompt: What follows when the Bavarian mine explodes beneath the walls?

choices.text: The garrison surrenders moments before the blast, securing safe passage.
The explosion breaches the walls, and the attackers storm the fortress, killing most defenders.
The mine misfires, and the siege is abandoned within days.
The garrison detonates a counter-mine, destroying the besiegers' works.

evt-11-18-1583-siege-of-godesberg.butterflyEffect: The blast breached the walls, and Ernst of Bavaria's soldiers stormed the fortress, killing most of the garrison despite pleas for surrender. The fall of Godesberg tipped the Cologne War toward the Catholic, Bavarian-backed candidate and helped secure Ernst's hold on the Archbishopric and its vote in the Holy Roman Empire.

evt-11-18-1865-the-celebrated-jumping-fr.scenario: You are a New York magazine editor in 1865 reviewing a submission from a little-known Western writer, a comic frontier tale about a gambler and his prize jumping frog told by a rambling bartender.
evt-11-18-1865-the-celebrated-jumping-fr.prompt: What do you decide to do with the manuscript?

choices.text: Hold it back for a specialized folklore journal instead
Reject it as too regional and crude for a national audience
Rewrite it in a more formal literary style before printing
Publish it as a humorous sketch for a wide readership

evt-11-18-1865-the-celebrated-jumping-fr.butterflyEffect: The story ran as "Jim Smiley and His Jumping Frog," quickly reprinted across the country, and gave Mark Twain his first taste of national fame. It later became the title piece of his first book and set him on the path to becoming America's leading literary humorist.

evt-11-18-1872-women-s-suffrage-in-the-u.scenario: You are Susan B. Anthony in Rochester, New York. You have just cast a ballot in the presidential election, knowing full well that state law forbids women from voting, and federal marshals are already asking questions.
evt-11-18-1872-women-s-suffrage-in-the-u.prompt: What happened to Anthony after she voted, and how did she respond?

choices.text: She fled the state before authorities could act
She was arrested, convicted, fined $100, and refused to pay it
Charges were quietly dropped to avoid publicity
She was acquitted after a sympathetic jury refused to convict her

evt-11-18-1872-women-s-suffrage-in-the-u.butterflyEffect: Anthony was arrested, tried, and fined $100 for illegal voting, but she refused to pay a cent of it. Her widely publicized trial turned her into a national symbol for the suffrage movement and helped build momentum toward the eventual 19th Amendment nearly fifty years later.

evt-11-18-1956-nikita-khrushchev.scenario: You are a Western ambassador at a reception in the Polish embassy in Moscow. Nikita Khrushchev, addressing the assembled diplomats, turns toward you and delivers a line that will be quoted around the world for decades.
evt-11-18-1956-nikita-khrushchev.prompt: What did Khrushchev say to the Western diplomats that became instantly infamous?

choices.text: "We will bury you"
"Capitalism will collapse on its own"
"Peaceful coexistence is our only path"
"History is on our side"

evt-11-18-1956-nikita-khrushchev.butterflyEffect: Khrushchev declared "We will bury you," widely taken in the West as a direct threat of Soviet military triumph over capitalism. Khrushchev later insisted he meant socialism would simply outlast capitalism economically, but the phrase became a lasting symbol of Cold War hostility and was repeated for years as proof of Soviet aggression.

evt-11-18-1978-jim-jones.scenario: It is 18 November 1978 at the Jonestown airstrip in Guyana. You are Congressman Leo Ryan, and several Peoples Temple members have just approached you privately, saying they want to leave the commune with your delegation.
evt-11-18-1978-jim-jones.prompt: How do you respond to their request to leave?

choices.text: Agree to escort them to the airstrip and take them with your delegation
Postpone any departure until the next scheduled visit
Refuse, citing the need to stay neutral during your visit
Tell them to discuss it with Jim Jones first

evt-11-18-1978-jim-jones.butterflyEffect: Ryan agreed to take them, and as the group prepared to fly out, Temple gunmen opened fire, killing him and four others. Jim Jones then led over 900 followers to their deaths at Jonestown that same day, an event that permanently reshaped public and legal scrutiny of religious communes and cult leadership.

evt-11-18-1987-king-s-cross-fire.scenario: It is the evening rush hour at King's Cross St Pancras station. A commuter reports smoke rising from beneath the wooden escalator, but trains are still running and the ticket hall above is packed with travelers.
evt-11-18-1987-king-s-cross-fire.prompt: What was the deadly mistake in how staff responded to reports of smoke?

choices.text: They flooded the escalator shaft with water straight away
They treated it as a minor smoulder and kept trains and passengers moving through the station
They evacuated the platforms immediately and shut the escalator down
They called the fire brigade and closed the entire station within minutes

evt-11-18-1987-king-s-cross-fire.butterflyEffect: Staff underestimated the fire and did not evacuate quickly, and a sudden flashover engulfed the ticket hall, killing 31 people. The Fennell Report that followed forced London Underground to replace wooden escalators and impose a total smoking ban across all stations and trains.

evt-11-18-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.scenario: After 87 days of siege and bombardment, you are among the exhausted Croatian defenders inside Vukovar as Yugoslav People's Army units close in on the last positions and the city's fall becomes unavoidable.
evt-11-18-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.prompt: What followed the JNA's capture of Vukovar that made the city infamous?

choices.text: Croatian forces recaptured the city a week later
Wounded and captured Croats from the hospital were taken to Ovčara and massacred
All prisoners were exchanged unharmed within days
The city was quickly rebuilt under a UN peacekeeping mandate

evt-11-18-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.butterflyEffect: After the city fell, JNA and Serb paramilitary forces removed patients and wounded from Vukovar hospital to the nearby Ovčara farm, where hundreds were massacred. The atrocity became a central case at the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, with JNA officer Mile Mrkšić later convicted for his role.

evt-11-18-1993-north-american-free-trade.scenario: It is November 1993, and you sit in the US House of Representatives as members debate ratifying the North American Free Trade Agreement, pushed hard by President Clinton despite opposition from labor unions and many in his own party.
evt-11-18-1993-north-american-free-trade.prompt: What does Congress ultimately do with the NAFTA implementation bill?

choices.text: Congress rejects it, forcing renegotiation of the treaty.
Congress approves it, and NAFTA takes effect on 1 January 1994.
Congress approves it only for Canada, excluding Mexico.
Congress delays the vote indefinitely amid union protests.

evt-11-18-1993-north-american-free-trade.butterflyEffect: Congress passed NAFTA with bipartisan support, and it took effect on 1 January 1994, creating one of the world's largest free-trade blocs. It reshaped North American manufacturing and agriculture while fueling a lasting political debate over job losses, one that echoed in later trade disputes and NAFTA's eventual replacement by the USMCA in 2020.

evt-11-18-2003-goodridge-v-department-of.scenario: It is 18 November 2003, and you are one of seven justices on the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court, reviewing a case brought by same-sex couples denied marriage licenses. Your ruling will decide whether the state constitution guarantees them the right to marry.
evt-11-18-2003-goodridge-v-department-of.prompt: How does the Court rule on the couples' claim?

choices.text: The Court rules 4-3 that the state constitution requires recognizing same-sex marriage.
The Court upholds the marriage ban, citing tradition and legislative authority.
The Court strikes down the law but delays any licensing indefinitely pending a referendum.
The Court sends the matter back to the legislature without a constitutional ruling.

evt-11-18-2003-goodridge-v-department-of.butterflyEffect: The 4-3 ruling made Massachusetts the first US state where the highest court recognized a constitutional right to same-sex marriage. Despite fierce political resistance, licenses began issuing on 17 May 2004, and the decision became a touchstone cited in later cases that eventually led to nationwide marriage equality in Obergefell v. Hodges (2015).

evt-11-18-2013-nasa.scenario: It is 18 November 2013 at Cape Canaveral, and you are a NASA mission planner watching the Atlas V rocket carrying the MAVEN probe climb toward Mars, tasked with answering a question that has puzzled scientists for decades.
evt-11-18-2013-nasa.prompt: What is MAVEN actually being sent to Mars to investigate?

choices.text: Whether microbial life is present in Martian soil
How to prepare a landing site for future astronauts
Whether liquid water currently exists on the surface
How the planet's upper atmosphere is escaping into space

evt-11-18-2013-nasa.butterflyEffect: MAVEN went on to confirm that solar wind had stripped away most of Mars's once-thick atmosphere over billions of years, explaining why the planet turned cold and dry. The mission remains in orbit, and its atmospheric data has shaped planning for later Mars exploration efforts.

evt-11-18-2014-2014-jerusalem-synagogue-.scenario: It is early morning on 18 November 2014 in Jerusalem's Har Nof neighborhood. You are a police officer racing to Kehilat Bnei Torah synagogue after reports that armed men are attacking worshippers inside.
evt-11-18-2014-2014-jerusalem-synagogue-.prompt: What must you do the moment you reach the synagogue?

choices.text: Wait outside for hostage negotiators to arrive
Seal the building and let the attack run its course
Withdraw and call for reinforcements before doing anything
Confront the attackers directly to stop the killing

evt-11-18-2014-2014-jerusalem-synagogue-.butterflyEffect: Responding officer Zidan Seif, a Druze member of the Israeli police, confronted and helped kill both attackers but was fatally wounded doing so. Four worshippers died at the scene and an eighth victim died of his injuries almost a year later, and the attack sharply raised security around synagogues across Israel.

evt-11-18-2017-cyclone-numa.scenario: It is 18 November 2017 and you are a civil protection official in western Greece as Medicane Numa, a rare Mediterranean cyclone, makes landfall and rivers begin overflowing into nearby towns.
evt-11-18-2017-cyclone-numa.prompt: What is your most urgent priority as the storm comes ashore?

choices.text: Focus resources on coastal areas only, since it is a cyclone
Wait until rainfall totals are confirmed before acting
Issue flood warnings and evacuate low-lying areas immediately
Delay warnings until the storm reaches peak intensity

evt-11-18-2017-cyclone-numa.butterflyEffect: Numa's flooding became Greece's worst weather event since 1977 and caused roughly $100 million in damage across the region. The storm added to growing scientific attention on Mediterranean "medicanes" and how a warming climate might make such hybrid storms more frequent.

evt-11-18-2020-utah-monolith.scenario: You are a Utah state wildlife biologist flying a helicopter survey over a remote red-rock canyon on 18 November 2020, counting bighorn sheep, when you spot a strange, gleaming metal object standing alone on the canyon floor.
evt-11-18-2020-utah-monolith.prompt: What do you do about the odd structure below?

choices.text: Assume it is old mining equipment and file no report
Land and remove it yourself before anyone else finds it
Ignore it and continue the sheep count
Report its location to state and land authorities

evt-11-18-2020-utah-monolith.butterflyEffect: The report went public and the object, a riveted metal monolith of unknown origin, became a viral sensation. It vanished within about ten days, and copycat monoliths began appearing in deserts and hillsides around the world, though who built the original has never been confirmed.

evt-11-19-1620-mayflower.scenario: It is November 1620, and the Mayflower has anchored off Cape Cod, far north of the Virginia Company's land grant that gave your voyage legal authority. Some passengers argue that without a charter for this territory, no one is bound to obey any government at all.
evt-11-19-1620-mayflower.prompt: What do the Pilgrim leaders do to prevent the colony from collapsing into lawlessness?

choices.text: Return to England to obtain a new charter before landing
Draft a compact binding all passengers to a self-governing civil body
Sail on immediately to reach the Virginia Company's chartered land
Wait offshore for a Crown official to arrive and take charge

evt-11-19-1620-mayflower.butterflyEffect: The passengers drafted and signed the Mayflower Compact, agreeing to govern themselves by majority rule until a royal charter could be secured. It became an early landmark of self-governance in the English colonies, later cited as a forerunner of American constitutional government.

evt-11-19-1794-jay-treaty.scenario: You are Alexander Hamilton advising President Washington in 1794. Britain still occupies forts in the Northwest and seizes American ships, but war would be ruinous for the young republic's finances and trade.
evt-11-19-1794-jay-treaty.prompt: Do you pursue a negotiated treaty with Britain instead of pressing for war?

choices.text: Ignore the disputes and let tensions fade on their own
Negotiate a treaty to avoid war and secure trade
Ally openly with France against Britain
Demand Congress declare war on Britain immediately

evt-11-19-1794-jay-treaty.butterflyEffect: Washington backed Hamilton's approach, and John Jay negotiated a treaty that secured British withdrawal from frontier forts and years of peaceful trade, though it ignored impressment and angered France. The treaty's unpopularity helped crystallize America's first party system, splitting Federalists from Democratic-Republicans.

evt-11-19-1863-gettysburg-address.scenario: It is the afternoon of 19 November 1863 in Gettysburg, Pennsylvania. The main orator has just finished a two-hour address to the crowd, and now it is your turn to speak over the fresh graves of the fallen.
evt-11-19-1863-gettysburg-address.prompt: What do you do with your brief turn at the podium?

choices.text: Read a prepared religious sermon instead of political remarks
Deliver a lengthy recounting of the three-day battle's tactics
Give a short speech reframing the war around the nation's founding principles
Postpone remarks until a more solemn occasion

evt-11-19-1863-gettysburg-address.butterflyEffect: Lincoln spoke for barely two minutes, framing the war as a test of whether a nation "conceived in liberty" could endure, and calling on listeners to ensure the dead had not died in vain. The 271-word speech became one of the most quoted texts in American history, reshaping how the Union understood the purpose of the war.

evt-11-19-1933-1933-spanish-general-elec.scenario: You are a Spanish woman voting for the first time under the new constitution, in a country whose left-wing Republican-Socialist coalition has just collapsed. A newly united right-wing coalition campaigns against the reforms of the past two years.
evt-11-19-1933-1933-spanish-general-elec.prompt: Given the fractured left, which way does the electorate swing in this election?

choices.text: Toward the incumbent left-wing Republican-Socialist bloc
Toward evenly split results with no clear winner
Toward the newly unified right-wing coalition
Toward a strong anarchist abstention movement

evt-11-19-1933-1933-spanish-general-elec.butterflyEffect: The united right, backed by the Radical Republican Party, won decisively over a divided left that had failed to form a similar alliance. The resulting conservative-led government rolled back earlier reforms, deepening polarization that contributed to the 1936 Popular Front victory and the slide toward civil war.

evt-11-19-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is dawn on 19 November 1942 on the frozen steppe northwest of Stalingrad. Massed Soviet artillery opens fire as your armies prepare to strike the weaker Romanian flanks guarding the German Sixth Army.
evt-11-19-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What is the strategic objective of this massive Soviet offensive?

choices.text: Withdraw further east to shorten the front line
Launch a naval assault down the Volga River
Encircle and trap the German Sixth Army inside Stalingrad
Push straight into Stalingrad to relieve trapped civilians

evt-11-19-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The pincers of Operation Uranus met at Kalach four days later, trapping roughly 250,000 Axis troops in the Stalingrad Pocket. Hitler forbade retreat, and the surrounded Sixth Army surrendered in February 1943, the first surrender of a German field marshal and a decisive turning point that put Germany permanently on the defensive in the East.

evt-11-19-1969-santos-fc.scenario: It is 19 November 1969, and you are among the crowd at the Maracanã as Santos face Vasco da Gama. Pelé steps up to take a penalty, one goal short of a milestone the whole country has been counting down to for weeks.
evt-11-19-1969-santos-fc.prompt: What does Pelé achieve with this penalty?

choices.text: He plays his final match before retirement
He breaks the world transfer fee record
He completes the fastest hat-trick in Brazilian league history
He scores his 1,000th career goal

evt-11-19-1969-santos-fc.butterflyEffect: Pelé scored his 1,000th career goal, a feat celebrated as a national event in Brazil, with the match briefly halted for the crowd to mob the pitch. "O Milésimo" cemented his status as football's first global superstar and became one of the sport's most enduring milestones.

evt-11-19-1985-geneva-summit-1985.scenario: You are an aide to President Reagan preparing for his first face-to-face meeting with Mikhail Gorbachev in Geneva. Advisers debate whether to focus strictly on arms control numbers or push for a broader personal rapport between the two leaders.
evt-11-19-1985-geneva-summit-1985.prompt: Do you encourage Reagan to build personal trust with Gorbachev beyond formal arms talks?

choices.text: No, keep the meeting strictly formal and technical
Yes, prioritize building a direct personal relationship
Avoid substantive talks until Gorbachev proves his intentions
Insist on public debates to score political points at home

evt-11-19-1985-geneva-summit-1985.butterflyEffect: Reagan and Gorbachev held private, informal fireside talks alongside the formal sessions, and the personal rapport they built became the foundation for the later INF Treaty and further summits. The Geneva meeting is widely seen as the turning point that began thawing the Cold War standoff.

evt-11-19-1985-cold-war.scenario: You are part of the American delegation at the Geneva summit. Reagan and Gorbachev have slipped away from their aides to talk privately by a fireside, meeting face to face for the first time as Cold War leaders.
evt-11-19-1985-cold-war.prompt: What comes out of this first Reagan–Gorbachev meeting?

choices.text: The Cold War is formally declared over
Talks collapse and both delegations withdraw their ambassadors
A full nuclear arms reduction treaty is signed on the spot
No treaty is signed, but the two agree to future summits and build personal rapport

evt-11-19-1985-cold-war.butterflyEffect: No treaty was signed at Geneva, but the two leaders built an unexpected personal rapport and agreed to hold further summits. That relationship laid the groundwork for the 1987 INF Treaty and the broader thaw that helped bring the Cold War to a close by the early 1990s.

evt-11-19-1991-luis-miguel.scenario: You are a young Mexican pop star known for upbeat ballads. Your producer suggests a full album of classic 1940s-style boleros instead of the youth-pop material that has built your career so far.
evt-11-19-1991-luis-miguel.prompt: Do you risk your teen-idol image by recording an album of old-fashioned boleros?

choices.text: Compromise by mixing boleros with English-language pop tracks
No, stick with contemporary pop to protect your teen fanbase
Delay the project until you can test it with a single first
Yes, record the bolero album and stake your career on it

evt-11-19-1991-luis-miguel.butterflyEffect: Luis Miguel recorded Romance, a collection of classic boleros, and it became a massive hit across Latin America and Spain. The album's success sparked a wave of bolero-revival records and led to three more Romance sequels, cementing his status as a crossover interpreter of traditional Latin song.

evt-11-19-1996-space-shuttle-program.scenario: Aboard Columbia on STS-80 in November 1996, you and your crewmate suit up for the mission's first scheduled spacewalk, only to find the airlock hatch will not open properly.
evt-11-19-1996-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What happens to the mission's two planned spacewalks?

choices.text: Both are canceled after the airlock hatch fails to open
Both are completed successfully ahead of schedule
Only one is completed due to bad weather
They are postponed to a later shuttle mission

evt-11-19-1996-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: A swollen handle mechanism jammed the airlock hatch, forcing NASA to scrub both EVAs entirely. The mission instead set a Space Shuttle endurance record at nearly 18 days, and engineers fixed the hardware issue before Columbia's next flight, STS-87, finally carried out its first-ever spacewalk.

evt-11-19-1997-sts-87.scenario: Aboard Space Shuttle Columbia in November 1997, you watch the SPARTAN-201 satellite you just released begin tumbling wildly instead of holding steady for its planned solar observations.
evt-11-19-1997-sts-87.prompt: What must the crew do to recover the out-of-control satellite?

choices.text: Use the robotic arm alone without any spacewalk
Abandon the satellite and return to Earth early
Conduct an unplanned spacewalk to grapple it by hand
Deploy a backup satellite in its place

evt-11-19-1997-sts-87.butterflyEffect: Astronauts Winston Scott and Takao Doi performed an unplanned spacewalk and captured the tumbling satellite by hand, an early example of manual orbital rescue. Doi became the first Japanese astronaut to complete a spacewalk, and the episode also marked the first EVA ever conducted from Columbia, since earlier attempts had been scrubbed on prior missions.

evt-11-19-1998-clinton-lewinsky-scandal.scenario: You sit on the House Judiciary Committee on 19 November 1998. Independent counsel Kenneth Starr has just taken his seat before you to defend his report on President Clinton's conduct.
evt-11-19-1998-clinton-lewinsky-scandal.prompt: What effect does Starr's testimony have on the process?

choices.text: Clinton resigns immediately afterward
It gives the committee grounds to move toward a full impeachment vote
Starr himself is censured by the committee
The committee drops its inquiry entirely

evt-11-19-1998-clinton-lewinsky-scandal.butterflyEffect: Starr's testimony helped the Judiciary Committee build its case, and the full House impeached Clinton the following month on charges of perjury and obstruction of justice. The Senate acquitted him on both counts in February 1999, and he served out his term.

evt-11-19-1999-shenzhou-1.scenario: You are an engineer at China's Jiuquan launch center on 19 November 1999, watching the uncrewed Shenzhou 1 lift off atop a Long March 2F rocket, a craft built without life support but with an emergency escape system.
evt-11-19-1999-shenzhou-1.prompt: What is the primary purpose of this uncrewed test flight?

choices.text: To test China's first reusable spaceplane
To validate the Shenzhou capsule and rocket ahead of crewed flight
To place a satellite into permanent geostationary orbit
To dock with the Russian Mir space station

evt-11-19-1999-shenzhou-1.butterflyEffect: After 14 orbits, Shenzhou 1 reentered and landed safely in Inner Mongolia, validating the spacecraft and rocket design. The success cleared the path for further uncrewed tests and, in 2003, Yang Liwei's Shenzhou 5 flight, making China only the third nation to independently launch a human into orbit.

evt-11-19-2001-aviation-and-transportati.scenario: It is November 2001, weeks after the September 11 attacks, and you are a Senate staffer helping draft legislation to overhaul how airport security is run across the United States.
evt-11-19-2001-aviation-and-transportati.prompt: What new federal agency does this act create to take over airport screening?

choices.text: The Department of Homeland Security
The National Counterterrorism Center
The Transportation Security Administration
The Federal Aviation Administration

evt-11-19-2001-aviation-and-transportati.butterflyEffect: The Act federalized airport security screening and created the TSA, mandating screening of all checked baggage. In 2002 the TSA was folded into the newly formed Department of Homeland Security, permanently reshaping US air travel with federalized screeners, reinforced cockpit doors, and expanded watchlists.

evt-11-19-2002-mv-prestige.scenario: It is 19 November 2002. The tanker Prestige, its hull cracked and leaking oil in a storm off Galicia, is being refused entry to a sheltered harbor by Spanish, Portuguese, and French authorities alike.
evt-11-19-2002-mv-prestige.prompt: What do Spanish authorities order for the crippled, leaking tanker?

choices.text: Tow it far out to sea, away from the coastline
Scuttle it immediately at its current position
Bring it into a sheltered port for emergency repairs
Transfer all its oil to another tanker at sea before towing

evt-11-19-2002-mv-prestige.butterflyEffect: Rather than let it shelter for repairs, Spain ordered tugs to tow the Prestige far out into the Atlantic, away from the coast. Days later it broke apart and sank, spilling tens of thousands of tons of oil that fouled thousands of kilometres of coastline and hastened EU rules phasing out single-hull tankers.

evt-11-19-2002-oil-tanker.scenario: You are a Spanish maritime official as the tanker Prestige, its hull cracked and leaking crude, drifts off the coast of Galicia in a storm. Officials must decide whether to bring it into a sheltered port or tow it away from shore.
evt-11-19-2002-oil-tanker.prompt: Do you order the crippled tanker towed out to open sea, away from the coast?

choices.text: Tow it away from the coast into open water
Attempt to offload the cargo at sea before towing
Bring it into the nearest sheltered harbor immediately
Abandon the ship and let it drift on its own

evt-11-19-2002-oil-tanker.butterflyEffect: Authorities had the Prestige towed further offshore rather than sheltered near a harbor, and days later it split apart and sank, spilling tens of thousands of tons of oil that fouled hundreds of miles of Spanish, Portuguese, and French coastline. The disaster triggered lasting reforms in EU maritime safety rules and single-hull tanker bans.

evt-11-19-2004-malice-at-the-palace.scenario: It is 19 November 2004 at the Palace of Auburn Hills. You are Ron Artest, lying on the scorer's table to cool off after a scuffle with the Pistons' Ben Wallace, when a fan hurls a cup of beer that hits you square in the chest.
evt-11-19-2004-malice-at-the-palace.prompt: What does Ron Artest do in response?

choices.text: He calls for a team timeout to calm down
He charges into the stands to confront the fan
He walks straight to the locker room
He apologizes to Ben Wallace on the spot

evt-11-19-2004-malice-at-the-palace.butterflyEffect: Artest charged into the stands after the fan, sparking a full-scale brawl between players and spectators that the AP called the most infamous fight in NBA history. The league handed down record suspensions, Artest lost roughly 86 games of pay, and the NBA overhauled arena security and alcohol sales policies afterward.

evt-11-19-2005-iraq-war.scenario: On 19 November 2005 in Haditha, Iraq, a roadside bomb kills one of your fellow Marines. In the hours that follow, Marines enter nearby houses and open fire, and 25 Iraqi civilians are killed.
evt-11-19-2005-iraq-war.prompt: What followed once the killings came to light the next year?

choices.text: The United Nations imposed sanctions on the United States
A military investigation and courts-martial were opened
The Iraqi government praised the unit's conduct
The incident was investigated and quietly closed with no charges

evt-11-19-2005-iraq-war.butterflyEffect: Time magazine's 2006 reporting forced a military investigation and courts-martial, though most charges against the Marines were later dropped and only one conviction, for dereliction of duty, resulted. Haditha became a defining symbol of civilian harm in the Iraq War, intensifying scrutiny of US rules of engagement and fueling opposition to the occupation.

evt-11-19-2013-2013-iranian-embassy-bomb.scenario: It is 19 November 2013, moments after two blasts have struck outside the Iranian embassy in Beirut. As investigators comb the wreckage, a statement circulates online claiming responsibility and issuing a demand tied to the war raging next door in Syria.
evt-11-19-2013-2013-iranian-embassy-bomb.prompt: Which group claims the bombing, and what does it demand?

choices.text: A Lebanese army faction, demanding new elections
The Free Syrian Army, demanding Assad's resignation
The Abdullah Azzam Brigades, demanding Hezbollah leave Syria
Hezbollah, demanding Israel withdraw from southern Lebanon

evt-11-19-2013-2013-iranian-embassy-bomb.butterflyEffect: The Abdullah Azzam Brigades, a Sunni jihadist group linked to al-Qaeda, claimed responsibility and demanded Hezbollah withdraw its fighters from Syria. The attack deepened the Sunni-Shia proxy struggle spilling from Syria into Lebanon and hardened security around Iranian and Hezbollah-linked sites in Beirut.

evt-11-19-2022-2022-colorado-springs-nig.scenario: It is just before midnight at Club Q in Colorado Springs. A gunman has opened fire inside the crowded bar, and for a moment there is no one between him and the rest of the room.
evt-11-19-2022-2022-colorado-springs-nig.prompt: What do patrons do in the chaos that follows?

choices.text: Patrons rush the gunman and wrestle him to the ground
Staff attempt to negotiate a ceasefire with the shooter
The crowd flees en masse through a single exit
Everyone hides and waits silently for police to arrive

evt-11-19-2022-2022-colorado-springs-nig.butterflyEffect: Several patrons, including a U.S. Army veteran, rushed the shooter and physically restrained him until police arrived, ending the attack. Their intervention was widely credited with limiting further casualties; the gunman was later convicted on state and federal hate crime charges and given multiple life sentences without parole.

evt-11-19-2023-2023-cricket-world-cup-fi.scenario: You are India's captain at the Narendra Modi Stadium, walking out for the toss of the World Cup final in front of over 100,000 fans. Australia is your opponent, just as they were in the 2003 final.
evt-11-19-2023-2023-cricket-world-cup-fi.prompt: You win the toss — do you bat first or bowl first on this pitch?

choices.text: Bowl first to exploit early moisture in the pitch
Bat first to set a target and use home crowd pressure
Bat first but aim for a very low, cautious total
Bowl first and rely on spin later in the Australian innings

evt-11-19-2023-2023-cricket-world-cup-fi.butterflyEffect: India chose to bat first and were bowled out for 240, a total that looked competitive but proved short. Travis Head's century powered Australia to victory with plenty of overs in hand, giving Australia their sixth World Cup title and denying India a home triumph.

evt-11-20-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is dawn on 20 November 1776 at Fort Lee, New Jersey. A scout bursts in with word that Cornwallis has ferried thousands of British and Hessian troops across the Hudson and is already climbing the Palisades toward your position.
evt-11-20-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What should the garrison do as the enemy column nears the fort?

choices.text: Open negotiations with Cornwallis for surrender terms
Man the walls and defend the fort to the last man
Launch a counterattack against the landing force before it reaches the top
Abandon the fort immediately, leaving equipment behind to save the army

evt-11-20-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: The garrison abandoned Fort Lee within hours, leaving behind tents, cannon, and supplies to save the men themselves. The narrow escape forced Washington into a grueling retreat across New Jersey, setting up his desperate Christmas crossing of the Delaware and the victory at Trenton that revived the flagging Revolution.

evt-11-20-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It is dawn on 20 November 1917 near Cambrai, and you sit inside a British tank as hundreds of others rumble forward across the German lines with no preliminary artillery bombardment to warn the enemy.
evt-11-20-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What tactic made this British assault different from earlier Western Front attacks?

choices.text: Infantry infiltrated at night before any armor was used
Poison gas cleared the trenches ahead of the tanks
A week-long artillery bombardment softened the line first
Massed tanks attacked without a preparatory artillery barrage

evt-11-20-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The mass tank assault achieved stunning early surprise, breaking through German lines and prompting church bells to ring across Britain in celebration. A German counterattack soon recovered much of the ground, but the battle proved tanks could break trench deadlock, shaping armored warfare doctrine for decades to come.

evt-11-20-1945-nuremberg-trials.scenario: It is 20 November 1945 in Nuremberg's Palace of Justice. You are one of the four Allied judges about to open the trial of 24 top Nazi leaders for offenses that no international court has ever prosecuted before.
evt-11-20-1945-nuremberg-trials.prompt: What novel charge do the prosecutors introduce alongside traditional war crimes?

choices.text: Crimes against humanity
Sedition against the German state
High treason against the Allied powers
Piracy on the high seas

evt-11-20-1945-nuremberg-trials.butterflyEffect: Prosecutors charged the defendants with 'crimes against humanity,' a category invented for this trial to cover atrocities against civilians that existing law did not clearly forbid. Twelve defendants were sentenced to death and the precedent became a cornerstone of international law, later underpinning the Geneva Conventions and the founding of the International Criminal Court.

evt-11-20-1969-native-americans-in-the-u.scenario: It is the night of 20 November 1969, and you are one of dozens of Native American activists paddling small boats out to the abandoned federal prison on Alcatraz Island, determined to occupy it in the name of Indians of All Tribes.
evt-11-20-1969-native-americans-in-the-u.prompt: What did the occupiers demand from the U.S. government once they landed?

choices.text: Cash reparations paid directly to individual tribal members
The release of Native American political prisoners nationwide
That the island be deeded to them for a Native American cultural center and university
Immediate statehood for all reservation lands

evt-11-20-1969-native-americans-in-the-u.butterflyEffect: The occupation lasted 19 months, drawing national attention to Native rights and grievances. Though the island was never deeded to the activists, the publicity helped end the federal termination policy and pushed the Nixon administration toward a new era of tribal self-determination.

evt-11-20-1977-egypt.scenario: It is 20 November 1977, and Anwar Sadat has just landed in Israel, the first Arab head of state ever to do so, defying the near-unanimous rejection of Israel by the Arab League.
evt-11-20-1977-egypt.prompt: What does Sadat do next that stuns both Israelis and the Arab world?

choices.text: He addresses the Israeli Knesset in person
He signs a peace treaty on arrival without negotiation
He demands immediate full withdrawal from Sinai before any talks
He refuses to meet Prime Minister Begin

evt-11-20-1977-egypt.butterflyEffect: Sadat addressed the Israeli Knesset directly, calling for peace and a full settlement of the conflict. The visit led to the Camp David Accords in 1978 and the Egypt-Israel peace treaty in 1979, but also to Egypt's suspension from the Arab League and, in 1981, to Sadat's assassination by Islamist militants opposed to the peace.

evt-11-20-1979-grand-mosque-seizure.scenario: It is 20 November 1979 outside the Grand Mosque in Mecca.
