Gunfire echoes from within, where Juhayman al-Otaybi's armed followers hold hundreds of pilgrims hostage and have proclaimed one of their own the Mahdi. As a Saudi official, you cannot simply storm Islam's holiest site.
evt-11-20-1979-grand-mosque-seizure.prompt: How did Saudi authorities justify using force to retake the mosque?

choices.text: Control of Mecca was temporarily ceded to a council of Islamic scholars
The Saudi air force bombed the mosque compound to end the siege
Ulama issued a fatwa authorizing force, and troops stormed the mosque with French commando assistance
Juhayman negotiated a peaceful surrender within days of the takeover

evt-11-20-1979-grand-mosque-seizure.butterflyEffect: Senior ulama issued a rare fatwa permitting armed force inside the Grand Mosque, and Saudi troops, assisted by French GIGN advisers, stormed the compound after a two-week siege. Sixty-three surviving militants were later publicly executed, and the crisis pushed the monarchy toward stricter religious enforcement, strengthening hardline clerics for decades.

evt-11-20-1994-angola.scenario: It is 20 November 1994 in Lusaka, Zambia. You represent the Angolan government at the negotiating table with Jonas Savimbi's UNITA delegation, both sides exhausted after nearly two years of renewed civil war since the disputed 1992 election.
evt-11-20-1994-angola.prompt: What did the Lusaka Protocol require to end the fighting?

choices.text: Angola is partitioned into separate UNITA and MPLA states
A NATO peacekeeping force is deployed to enforce the ceasefire
UNITA disarms its forces and joins a government of national unity
Immediate elections are held without any disarmament

evt-11-20-1994-angola.butterflyEffect: The protocol called for UNITA to demobilize its forces and join a government of national unity alongside the ruling MPLA, backed by UN peacekeepers. Implementation stalled for years as Savimbi resisted full disarmament, and the war reignited in 1998, dragging on until his death in combat in 2002 finally ended the conflict.

evt-11-20-1996-garley-building-fire.scenario: It is the night of 20 November 1996 on Nathan Road, Hong Kong. Fire has broken out low in the Garley Building and is racing upward through the elevator shaft, trapping office workers and residents on floors far above the flames.
evt-11-20-1996-garley-building-fire.prompt: What made this fire so much deadlier than a typical office blaze?

choices.text: Fire crews were delayed for hours by a citywide power outage
A gas explosion collapsed the building's central staircase instantly
The building's sprinkler system malfunctioned and flooded the lower floors
Flames and smoke spread upward rapidly through the elevator shaft, trapping people above

evt-11-20-1996-garley-building-fire.butterflyEffect: The fire spread rapidly through the building's elevator shaft, leaving the middle floors largely intact while trapping people at the top and bottom, and some victims died attempting to escape through smoke-filled stairwells. Forty-one people died in what was then Hong Kong's worst peacetime building fire, prompting tighter enforcement of fire safety codes and crackdowns on illegal structural alterations that blocked escape routes.

evt-11-20-1998-taliban.scenario: It is 20 November 1998 in Taliban-controlled Afghanistan, months after deadly bombings hit US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania. Washington demands Osama bin Laden be handed over, and a Taliban-appointed court now reviews the case.
evt-11-20-1998-taliban.prompt: How did the court rule on the US demand to extradite bin Laden?

choices.text: The court convicted him and ordered his execution under Islamic law
The court ordered his immediate extradition to the United States
The court found no proof of guilt and the Taliban refused to hand him over
The court sentenced him to permanent exile from Afghanistan

evt-11-20-1998-taliban.butterflyEffect: The court declared bin Laden a man without proven guilt and the Taliban refused to extradite him, deepening US sanctions and Afghanistan's isolation. Bin Laden remained under Taliban protection to plan further attacks, including the September 11, 2001 attacks, which triggered the US-led invasion that toppled the Taliban regime that same year.

evt-11-20-1998-zarya-iss-module.scenario: It is 20 November 1998 at the Baikonur Cosmodrome, and you watch a Proton-K rocket lift the newly built Zarya module skyward, the very first piece of what will become the International Space Station.
evt-11-20-1998-zarya-iss-module.prompt: What was Zarya designed to provide the fledgling space station in its earliest years?

choices.text: Crew sleeping quarters and life support
An airlock for spacewalks
Power, propulsion, and guidance for the station
A laboratory for microgravity experiments

evt-11-20-1998-zarya-iss-module.butterflyEffect: Zarya supplied power, propulsion, and guidance until later modules like Unity and Zvezda took over those roles. As the station grew, Zarya's job shifted mainly to storage, but it remains in orbit today as the foundation the entire ISS was built upon.

evt-11-20-2003-2003-istanbul-bombings.scenario: It is 20 November 2003 and you work near the British Consulate in Istanbul when a truck bomb detonates minutes after another explosion at the HSBC headquarters across the city.
evt-11-20-2003-2003-istanbul-bombings.prompt: Who was among the prominent victims killed in the consulate bombing?

choices.text: The Turkish Prime Minister
The United States Ambassador to Turkey
The CEO of HSBC worldwide
British Consul General Roger Short

evt-11-20-2003-2003-istanbul-bombings.butterflyEffect: British Consul General Roger Short was killed along with dozens of others in the coordinated al-Qaeda-linked attacks, which followed bombings of two synagogues five days earlier. The bombings pushed Turkey to intensify counterterrorism cooperation with Western allies and led to tightened security at diplomatic and financial targets worldwide.

evt-11-20-2015-radisson-blu-bamako-attac.scenario: It is 20 November 2015, and you are trapped inside the Radisson Blu hotel in Bamako, Mali, as Islamist gunmen hold guests and staff hostage while security forces gather outside.
evt-11-20-2015-radisson-blu-bamako-attac.prompt: How did the siege at the hotel come to an end?

choices.text: United Nations peacekeepers secured a hostage release deal
The attackers fled before security forces arrived
The gunmen negotiated a peaceful surrender
Malian special forces, backed by U.S. and French personnel, assaulted the hotel

evt-11-20-2015-radisson-blu-bamako-attac.butterflyEffect: Malian special forces, supported by U.S. and French personnel, stormed the hotel and ended the siege, though 20 people had already been killed. The attack underscored the growing reach of jihadist groups in the Sahel and spurred deeper French and international military engagement in the region.

evt-11-20-2016-jimmie-johnson.scenario: It is 20 November 2016 at Homestead-Miami Speedway, and you are Jimmie Johnson, one of four drivers racing head-to-head for the NASCAR Cup Series championship in the winner-take-all finale.
evt-11-20-2016-jimmie-johnson.prompt: What did Johnson need to do at Homestead to claim his seventh championship?

choices.text: Win the pole position for the final race
Win the race outright to guarantee the title
Simply finish in the top ten
Lead the most laps of the race

evt-11-20-2016-jimmie-johnson.butterflyEffect: Johnson won the race outright, clinching the title and tying Richard Petty and Dale Earnhardt for the most Cup championships ever. The victory cemented his reputation as one of NASCAR's all-time greats and intensified debate over who truly deserved the title of "greatest driver."

evt-11-21-1620-mayflower-compact.scenario: It is 21 November 1620. The Mayflower has anchored off Cape Cod, well outside the territory granted by the Virginia Company's charter. Some passengers argue that without a legal charter, no one aboard is bound to obey the colony's leaders.
evt-11-21-1620-mayflower-compact.prompt: What do the Pilgrim leaders ask the men aboard the ship to sign before anyone goes ashore?

choices.text: A private trading contract binding only the merchants aboard
An agreement to form a government and obey laws made for the colony's good
An oath of allegiance to Virginia's royal governor
A petition demanding the ship turn back to England

evt-11-21-1620-mayflower-compact.butterflyEffect: The Mayflower Compact bound the signers into a 'civil body politic' that would make and obey its own laws, creating self-government by mutual consent before any colony even existed on land. Later generations of Americans cited it as an early precedent for constitutional self-rule.

evt-11-21-1877-thomas-edison.scenario: It is 21 November 1877, and you are an editor who has just received a letter from Thomas Edison describing a strange tinfoil-cylinder machine he claims can capture the human voice and play it back exactly as spoken.
evt-11-21-1877-thomas-edison.prompt: What does Edison claim his new invention can do that so astonishes the press?

choices.text: Transmit a voice instantly over telegraph wires
Record human speech and reproduce it afterward
Convert spoken words automatically into printed text
Amplify a speaker's voice for a large hall

evt-11-21-1877-thomas-edison.butterflyEffect: Edison's announcement made him an overnight sensation and earned him the nickname 'Wizard of Menlo Park.' The phonograph became one of the era's most celebrated inventions, eventually spawning the recorded-sound industry, from wax cylinders to record players and the modern music business.

evt-11-21-1894-first-sino-japanese-war.scenario: It is 21 November 1894. Japanese forces have just captured the fortress port of Lüshunkou, known to Westerners as Port Arthur, from Qing troops. Foreign correspondents traveling with the Japanese army are filing dispatches on what soldiers are doing inside the captured city.
evt-11-21-1894-first-sino-japanese-war.prompt: What did foreign press dispatches from Port Arthur trigger back in Europe and America?

choices.text: An immediate Japanese withdrawal from the port
Outrage that briefly damaged Japan's reputation as a modern, civilized power
Japan's expulsion from further operations in Korea
A formal Russo-Chinese defense alliance signed that same week

evt-11-21-1894-first-sino-japanese-war.butterflyEffect: Correspondents' accounts of the massacre of Chinese civilians and disarmed soldiers at Port Arthur caused a wave of outrage in the Western press, briefly damaging Japan's carefully cultivated image as a modern, 'civilized' power. It did not, however, stop the great powers from dealing with Japan, and the war ended months later with the Treaty of Shimonoseki.

evt-11-21-1920-irish-war-of-independence.scenario: It is the early morning of November 21, 1920, in Dublin. As an IRA volunteer acting on Michael Collins's orders, you and other units fan out across the city to hit a coordinated list of addresses before breakfast.
evt-11-21-1920-irish-war-of-independence.prompt: Who are your assigned targets in the morning operation?

choices.text: Auxiliary Division patrol vehicles
Local Royal Irish Constabulary barracks
Dublin Castle's telegraph office
British intelligence officers living undercover in the city

evt-11-21-1920-irish-war-of-independence.butterflyEffect: The coordinated attacks killed more than a dozen British intelligence operatives, badly damaging British spy networks in Dublin. In reprisal that afternoon, Auxiliary and RIC forces opened fire on the crowd at a Gaelic football match at Croke Park, killing civilians, an atrocity that hardened Irish public opinion and helped push both sides toward the 1921 truce and Treaty negotiations.

evt-11-21-1945-manzanar.scenario: It is November 1945 and Manzanar is closing. You are among the last Japanese American families handed a train ticket and a small stipend, with nowhere confirmed to live back on the West Coast.
evt-11-21-1945-manzanar.prompt: What did many released internees find waiting for them when they returned home?

choices.text: Full restoration of their prewar property
Revocation of their American citizenship
Immediate government compensation for their losses
Their homes and businesses lost, and continued discrimination

evt-11-21-1945-manzanar.butterflyEffect: Most internees returned to find their houses, farms, and businesses sold, seized, or occupied by others, and many faced open hostility in their former communities. The injustice fueled a decades-long redress movement that culminated in the 1988 Civil Liberties Act, which issued a formal apology and reparations payments to survivors.

evt-11-21-1950-canoe-river-train-crash.scenario: It's the evening of November 21, 1950. You are the telegraph operator at a remote junction near Valemount, British Columbia, tasked with relaying an order telling a westbound troop train to take the siding so an eastbound passenger train can pass safely on the single track.
evt-11-21-1950-canoe-river-train-crash.prompt: What must you do before letting the troop train proceed on the order?

choices.text: Repeat the order back to the dispatcher word for word to confirm it before releasing the train
Flag down the train crew and give the instructions verbally instead of by telegraph
Log the order in the station book without checking it against the dispatcher's original message
Pass the order along immediately without confirming it, to keep the schedule on time

evt-11-21-1950-canoe-river-train-crash.butterflyEffect: An operator's mishandled order meant the troop train never took the siding, and it collided head-on with the passenger train, killing 21 people, including 17 soldiers bound for the Korean War. The disaster and the manslaughter trial that followed raised early Canadian legal questions about individual blame versus systemic failure, and prompted tighter verification rules for train orders.

evt-11-21-1959-disc-jockey.scenario: It's November 21, 1959, and as a radio executive at New York's WABC you're confronting DJ Alan Freed, the man credited with popularizing the term "rock and roll," over evidence he's taken undisclosed payments from record labels to play their songs.
evt-11-21-1959-disc-jockey.prompt: What does the station do after Freed refuses to sign a statement denying payola?

choices.text: WABC promotes him to program director
WABC ignores the allegations and keeps him on air unchanged
WABC gives him a raise to keep him quiet
WABC fires him immediately

evt-11-21-1959-disc-jockey.butterflyEffect: WABC fired Freed on the spot, making him the public face of the brewing payola scandal that led to congressional hearings on radio corruption. His career and reputation never recovered, and the scandal reshaped how record promotion and radio airplay were regulated in the following years.

evt-11-21-1964-verrazzano-narrows-bridge.scenario: It's November 21, 1964, and you're among the first drivers crossing the newly opened Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge, the first fixed link ever to join Staten Island directly to Brooklyn.
evt-11-21-1964-verrazzano-narrows-bridge.prompt: What real-world change followed the bridge's opening on Staten Island?

choices.text: The Staten Island Ferry is permanently shut down
Brooklyn's population declines sharply because of the new road
The bridge instantly becomes the busiest tunnel crossing in the city
Staten Island experiences a rapid population boom and suburban development

evt-11-21-1964-verrazzano-narrows-bridge.butterflyEffect: The bridge, briefly the world's longest suspension span, ended Staten Island's isolation and triggered a rapid population boom as suburban development spread across the borough in the following decades. It also reduced reliance on the Staten Island Ferry for vehicle traffic, reshaping the borough's growth pattern for generations.

evt-11-21-1970-vietnam-war.scenario: It's the night of November 21, 1970, and you're among the US Army Special Forces raiders landing by helicopter deep inside North Vietnam at the Son Tay prison camp, expecting to free dozens of American POWs held there.
evt-11-21-1970-vietnam-war.prompt: What do the raiders discover inside the camp?

choices.text: The raiders are ambushed and captured by North Vietnamese troops
The POWs are found and successfully rescued
Guards surrender and hand over the prisoners without resistance
The camp is empty; the POWs had been moved weeks earlier

evt-11-21-1970-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: The camp was empty; the POWs had been relocated weeks earlier due to flooding risk, unknown to US intelligence. The raid, though a flawless military operation, was a strategic disappointment, but it prompted North Vietnam to consolidate American prisoners into central Hanoi facilities, inadvertently improving their conditions and ability to communicate with each other.

evt-11-21-1977-god-defend-new-zealand.scenario: You're a New Zealand Member of Parliament in 1977, weighing a popular petition asking that "God Defend New Zealand" be given official recognition alongside "God Save the Queen."
evt-11-21-1977-god-defend-new-zealand.prompt: What official status does "God Defend New Zealand" receive?

choices.text: It replaces "God Save the Queen" entirely as the sole anthem
It is declared a second national anthem, equal in status to "God Save the Queen"
Parliament rejects the petition and it remains unofficial
It is adopted only in its Māori-language version

evt-11-21-1977-god-defend-new-zealand.butterflyEffect: Parliament declared it a second national anthem with equal legal status to "God Save the Queen," rather than replacing it. Over time "God Defend New Zealand" became the anthem heard far more often in practice, and by the late 1990s it became customary to sing its first verse in Māori followed by English at public events.

evt-11-21-1995-dayton-agreement.scenario: It is November 1995 at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio. You sit at the table with Serb, Croat, and Bosniak delegations, drawing borders that must end the Bosnian War without pleasing any side completely.
evt-11-21-1995-dayton-agreement.prompt: What governing structure do the negotiators agree Bosnia and Herzegovina will become?

choices.text: An indefinite United Nations trusteeship
Three fully independent nations
A single unitary state with no internal borders
One state split into Republika Srpska and the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina

evt-11-21-1995-dayton-agreement.butterflyEffect: The parties agreed to a single sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina split into two entities, Republika Srpska and the Bosniak-Croat Federation, under a weak central government. The deal stopped the killing but froze wartime ethnic divisions into permanent political structures still criticized today for near-paralyzing governance.

evt-11-21-2009-2009-heilongjiang-mine-ex.scenario: You are a work-safety official in Heilongjiang province in the hours after a gas explosion tears through the Xinxing coal mine near Hegang, killing 108 miners while hundreds more are trapped underground.
evt-11-21-2009-2009-heilongjiang-mine-ex.prompt: What action does the Chinese government take in the explosion's aftermath?

choices.text: Increases coal export quotas to offset production losses
Treats it as an isolated incident with no further action
Orders safety inspections and suspends operations at unsafe mines
Privatizes the mine immediately to attract foreign investment

evt-11-21-2009-2009-heilongjiang-mine-ex.butterflyEffect: Beijing ordered nationwide inspections of coal mines and temporary suspensions at sites with poor safety records, part of a recurring pattern after China's frequent mining disasters. The Xinxing disaster added pressure toward mine consolidation and stricter enforcement, though fatal accidents continued to plague the industry for years afterward.

evt-11-21-2012-2012-tel-aviv-bus-bombing.scenario: It's November 21, 2012, hours before a ceasefire ending Operation Pillar of Defense is due to take effect, when a remotely detonated bomb rips through a crowded Tel Aviv bus, injuring 28 civilians. You sit in Israel's security cabinet as the news arrives.
evt-11-21-2012-2012-tel-aviv-bus-bombing.prompt: What does Israel decide about the imminent ceasefire?

choices.text: Israel postpones the ceasefire indefinitely pending investigation
Israel launches an immediate ground invasion of Gaza
Israel proceeds with the ceasefire as planned
Israel cancels the ceasefire and resumes airstrikes on Gaza

evt-11-21-2012-2012-tel-aviv-bus-bombing.butterflyEffect: Israel proceeded with the ceasefire, which took effect just hours after the bombing, ending the eight-day operation. The attacker, an Israeli Arab citizen, was later arrested and convicted, and the bombing revived fears that bus bombings from the earlier intifada era might return.

evt-11-21-2015-2015-brussels-lockdown.scenario: It is 21 November 2015, a week after the Paris attacks. You run a small shop near Brussels' Grand Place, and authorities have just raised the terror alert to its highest level, warning that fugitive attacker Salah Abdeslam may be hiding in the city.
evt-11-21-2015-2015-brussels-lockdown.prompt: What do Belgian authorities order residents and businesses in Brussels to do?

choices.text: Evacuate the entire city immediately
Continue normal business since no formal warning was issued
Form armed citizen patrols to search buildings
Close shops and schools and avoid public gatherings

evt-11-21-2015-2015-brussels-lockdown.butterflyEffect: Brussels shut down schools, the metro, and shops for four days while police searched for Abdeslam, who nonetheless evaded capture in the city until March 2016. The lockdown exposed Brussels as a hub for the Paris attackers' network and pushed European governments toward tighter cross-border security cooperation.

evt-11-21-2017-robert-mugabe.scenario: It is 21 November 2017 in Harare. Parliament has begun impeachment proceedings against President Robert Mugabe, who has clung to office despite a military takeover and mass street protests. You are among the aides urging him to act before the vote concludes.
evt-11-21-2017-robert-mugabe.prompt: What does Mugabe do to avoid becoming the first Zimbabwean president removed by impeachment?

choices.text: He appeals to the Southern African Development Community to intervene militarily
He declares martial law and dissolves parliament
He calls a snap election to reaffirm his mandate
He submits his resignation before the impeachment vote is completed

evt-11-21-2017-robert-mugabe.butterflyEffect: Mugabe resigned that day in a letter read aloud to parliament, ending 37 years of rule. His former deputy Emmerson Mnangagwa took power promising reform, but many of the same ZANU-PF structures and practices persisted under his government.

evt-11-21-2019-benjamin-netanyahu.scenario: It's November 21, 2019, and you are Israel's Attorney General. Evidence from three separate investigations into the sitting prime minister's conduct sits on your desk, and Israeli law places no bar on indicting a prime minister while in office.
evt-11-21-2019-benjamin-netanyahu.prompt: What do you decide to do with the evidence?

choices.text: Refer the matter to the Knesset for an immunity vote before deciding
Close all three investigations for lack of evidence
Formally indict Netanyahu on charges of bribery, fraud, and breach of trust
Postpone any decision until after the next election

evt-11-21-2019-benjamin-netanyahu.butterflyEffect: The Attorney General indicted Netanyahu on charges of bribery, fraud, and breach of trust, making him the first sitting Israeli prime minister charged with a crime. The case fueled political deadlock through three elections and years of trial proceedings that ran alongside his continued time in office, deeply polarizing Israeli politics.

evt-11-21-2019-tesla-inc.scenario: It's November 21, 2019, at Tesla's design studio. Elon Musk has just unveiled the Cybertruck's supposedly unbreakable stainless steel body, and chief designer Franz von Holzhausen steps up to throw a metal ball at the truck's window in front of a live crowd and cameras.
evt-11-21-2019-tesla-inc.prompt: What happens when he throws the ball at the window?

choices.text: The window shatters, cracking on both throws
The ball bounces off without leaving a mark
The window flexes visibly but shows no damage
Musk stops the demonstration before the ball is thrown

evt-11-21-2019-tesla-inc.butterflyEffect: Both the front and rear windows cracked on stage in front of Musk and the crowd, instantly becoming a viral meme. Tesla's stock dropped roughly 6% the next trading day, yet the truck still drew hundreds of thousands of reservations within days, foreshadowing the vehicle's long and bumpy road to actual production years later.

evt-11-21-2021-waukesha-christmas-parade.scenario: It's the evening of November 21, 2021, in Waukesha, Wisconsin. Families line the street for the annual Christmas parade when a red SUV suddenly swerves past a barricade and speeds down the parade route.
evt-11-21-2021-waukesha-christmas-parade.prompt: What legal outcome followed for the driver, Darrell Brooks Jr.?

choices.text: He pleaded to a single misdemeanor reckless driving charge
He was found not guilty by reason of insanity
Charges against him were dropped for lack of evidence
He was convicted on six counts of first-degree intentional homicide

evt-11-21-2021-waukesha-christmas-parade.butterflyEffect: Brooks represented himself at a widely watched 2022 trial and was convicted on six counts of first-degree intentional homicide, later receiving six consecutive life sentences. The attack also pushed many U.S. cities to review vehicle barricades and security protocols for public parades and street events.

evt-11-21-2022-2022-west-java-earthquake.scenario: It is 21 November 2022, minutes after a sharp earthquake has flattened buildings around Cianjur, West Java. You lead a rescue team and reports are flooding in of collapsed schools and homes.
evt-11-21-2022-2022-west-java-earthquake.prompt: What should your team prioritize first in the chaotic hours after the quake?

choices.text: Distribute vaccines to affected villages
Evacuate coastal areas ahead of a tsunami
Search collapsed schools and homes for trapped survivors
Repair the regional power grid first

evt-11-21-2022-2022-west-java-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Rescue teams focused on pulling survivors, including many schoolchildren, from collapsed school buildings and homes, as the quake struck during class hours. It became Indonesia's deadliest earthquake since 2018, prompting renewed scrutiny of weak building codes in West Java's densely populated hill towns.

evt-11-22-1635-dutch-formosa.scenario: It is November 1635, and you march with Dutch soldiers and their Sinckan allies under Governor Hans Putmans toward the village of Mattau on Formosa, sent to punish the aborigines for killing Dutch troops years earlier.
evt-11-22-1635-dutch-formosa.prompt: What does this campaign achieve for the Dutch East India Company?

choices.text: It provokes direct Chinese military intervention
It secures a permanent peace treaty with all Formosan peoples
It ends in a Dutch defeat and withdrawal from Formosa
It destroys Mattau and forces widespread aboriginal submission

evt-11-22-1635-dutch-formosa.butterflyEffect: The Dutch force destroyed Mattau and forced its surrender, prompting many neighboring villages to submit to Company authority without further fighting. This began decades of Dutch pacification of Formosa's plains aborigines, a policy of control that lasted until the Company's expulsion in 1662.

evt-11-22-1718-blackbeard.scenario: It is 22 November 1718 off Ocracoke Island, and you command Lieutenant Robert Maynard's Royal Navy sloop closing in on Blackbeard's vessel for a final, bloody boarding fight.
evt-11-22-1718-blackbeard.prompt: What tactic does Maynard use to turn the tide in the close-quarters battle?

choices.text: Open a prolonged cannon barrage to sink the ship outright
Offer Blackbeard a pardon in exchange for peaceful surrender
Hide most of the crew below deck to lure the pirates aboard before ambushing them
Ram Blackbeard's ship head-on to disable it before boarding

evt-11-22-1718-blackbeard.butterflyEffect: Maynard hid most of his crew below deck to trick Blackbeard into thinking the sloop was undermanned, then sprang the ambush once the pirates boarded. Blackbeard was killed and beheaded, his head displayed as a warning, and the incident became a symbolic turning point in Britain's crackdown on Atlantic piracy.

evt-11-22-1873-ss-ville-du-havre.scenario: It's the middle of the night on November 22, 1873, far out in the mid-Atlantic. You are a crewman aboard the French steamship Ville du Havre when the lights of a Scottish iron clipper suddenly appear on a collision course in the darkness.
evt-11-22-1873-ss-ville-du-havre.prompt: What happens when the two ships meet?

choices.text: The clipper strikes Ville du Havre, which sinks within minutes
The two ships collide but both remain afloat until rescue arrives
Ville du Havre rams the clipper and sinks it instead
Both ships pass safely thanks to a last-second maneuver

evt-11-22-1873-ss-ville-du-havre.butterflyEffect: The clipper Loch Earn struck Ville du Havre, which sank within minutes, killing around 226 people. Among the dead were the four daughters of American lawyer Horatio Spafford, whose grief afterward inspired the hymn "It Is Well with My Soul," one of the disaster's most enduring cultural legacies.

evt-11-22-1971-cairngorm-plateau-disaste.scenario: It is November 1971 and you are one of two adult leaders on the Cairngorm Plateau with six teenage pupils. A blizzard has closed in, visibility is near zero, and the planned bothy is now unreachable in the dark.
evt-11-22-1971-cairngorm-plateau-disaste.prompt: What should the leaders do to give the group the best chance of survival?

choices.text: Split the group so some can move faster toward the bothy
Light distress flares and wait in the open for a helicopter
Keep walking in the direction of the last known path markers
Dig an emergency snow hole and shelter in place until the storm passes

evt-11-22-1971-cairngorm-plateau-disaste.butterflyEffect: The leaders dug an emergency snow hole near Feith Buidhe, but the shelter proved inadequate against the extreme cold. Five pupils and one leader died of hypothermia overnight before rescue arrived. Britain's worst mountaineering disaster led to lasting reforms in leadership training and supervision standards for school expeditions into Scotland's mountains.

evt-11-22-1975-francisco-franco.scenario: It is November 22, 1975, two days after Francisco Franco's death. You sit in the Cortes in Madrid as officials prepare to name Spain's new head of state.
evt-11-22-1975-francisco-franco.prompt: Who is proclaimed to lead Spain that day?

choices.text: Carlos Arias Navarro is named president for life
A military junta assumes control
Spain is declared a republic
Juan Carlos is proclaimed King of Spain

evt-11-22-1975-francisco-franco.butterflyEffect: Juan Carlos was proclaimed King of Spain, beginning a transition many expected to preserve Francoism but which instead opened the door to democracy. Within three years Spain adopted a democratic constitution, and the king's stand against the 1981 coup attempt cemented the new order.

evt-11-22-1986-mike-tyson.scenario: It is November 22, 1986, at the Las Vegas Hilton. You're ringside as 20-year-old Mike Tyson, unbeaten and ferocious, steps in against WBC champion Trevor Berbick.

choices.text: The fight is ruled a draw
Tyson knocks Berbick out in the second round
Tyson is disqualified for a low blow
Berbick wins a unanimous decision

evt-11-22-1986-mike-tyson.butterflyEffect: Tyson knocked Berbick out in the second round, becoming the youngest heavyweight champion in history at 20 years old. The win launched his rise to global superstardom and set up his brief reign as undisputed heavyweight champion.

evt-11-22-1987-max-headroom-signal-hijac.scenario: It is the night of 22 November 1987 in Chicago, and viewers of two television stations suddenly see their programming cut to a masked figure in a Max Headroom costume rambling gibberish before the signal returns to normal.
evt-11-22-1987-max-headroom-signal-hijac.prompt: What happens in the investigation that follows the broadcast hijacking?

choices.text: The perpetrators are never identified and the case remains unsolved
Investigators identify and arrest the hijackers within days
The FCC shuts down both stations for security failures
The hijack is traced to a European pirate broadcaster

evt-11-22-1987-max-headroom-signal-hijac.butterflyEffect: Despite an FCC and FBI investigation, the culprits were never identified or caught, and the case remains officially unsolved to this day. The incident exposed how vulnerable broadcast transmission signals were to outside interference, prompting stations to tighten security around their equipment.

evt-11-22-1990-prime-minister-of-the-uni.scenario: It is November 22, 1990, in Westminster. Margaret Thatcher has failed to win the first leadership ballot outright against Michael Heseltine, and her Cabinet colleagues are urging her to reconsider fighting on.
evt-11-22-1990-prime-minister-of-the-uni.prompt: What does Thatcher announce that morning?

choices.text: She withdraws and resigns as Prime Minister
She dissolves Parliament and calls a snap election
She sacks her Cabinet and refuses to step down
She contests the second ballot and wins comfortably

evt-11-22-1990-prime-minister-of-the-uni.butterflyEffect: Thatcher withdrew from the second ballot and announced her resignation as Prime Minister, ending eleven years in power. John Major won the subsequent contest and succeeded her, steering the party through the 1992 election.

evt-11-22-2003-2003-baghdad-dhl-attempte.scenario: It is November 22, 2003. Moments after your DHL cargo jet lifts off from Baghdad, a missile tears into the left wing, igniting a fire and severing every hydraulic line that controls the aircraft.
evt-11-22-2003-2003-baghdad-dhl-attempte.prompt: With no hydraulic flight controls left, how do the pilots bring the plane down?

choices.text: They order the crew to parachute out over the desert
They steer using differential engine thrust to reach the runway
They ditch the aircraft in the Tigris River
They radio for a military escort and abandon the aircraft mid-air

evt-11-22-2003-2003-baghdad-dhl-attempte.butterflyEffect: The crew steered using differential engine thrust alone and managed to land the crippled Airbus back at Baghdad, with all aboard surviving. The near-disaster pushed cargo carriers operating into Iraq to adopt missile-warning systems and armored fuel tanks.

evt-11-22-2004-orange-revolution.scenario: It's late November 2004 in Kyiv's Independence Square. Official results have just declared Viktor Yanukovych the winner of the presidential runoff, but exit polls and widespread reports of fraud have brought thousands of angry citizens into the freezing streets.
evt-11-22-2004-orange-revolution.prompt: What should the opposition and its supporters do to challenge the result?

choices.text: Accept the official result to avoid instability
Sustain daily peaceful protests, sit-ins, and general strikes
Request that the army seize the presidential administration
Call on Russia to mediate a new vote

evt-11-22-2004-orange-revolution.butterflyEffect: Ukrainians sustained weeks of peaceful mass protest, strikes, and sit-ins until the Supreme Court annulled the runoff and ordered a rerun, which Viktor Yushchenko won. The revolution became a defining moment of post-Soviet civic resistance and deepened Ukraine's tilt toward the West, setting the stage for later confrontations with Russia.

evt-11-22-2010-bon-om-touk.scenario: It is the final night of Bon Om Touk, November 22, 2010, on the crowded pedestrian bridge to Koh Pich in Phnom Penh, where hundreds of thousands of festival-goers are packed together.
evt-11-22-2010-bon-om-touk.prompt: In the aftermath of the deadly crush, what does the Cambodian government do?

choices.text: Cancels the water festival permanently
Suppresses all news of the incident
Blames foreign tourists and takes no further action
Declares a national day of mourning and investigates the disaster

evt-11-22-2010-bon-om-touk.butterflyEffect: The government declared a national day of mourning and launched an investigation into the causes of the crush, one of Cambodia's worst peacetime disasters. The tragedy led to lasting changes in crowd management for the festival in subsequent years.

evt-11-22-2013-magnus-carlsen.scenario: It's November 22, 2013, in Chennai. You are 22-year-old Magnus Carlsen, sitting down for game 10 of the World Chess Championship needing only a draw to overtake reigning champion Viswanathan Anand.
evt-11-22-2013-magnus-carlsen.prompt: What is the outcome of this decisive game?

choices.text: The game is postponed after a scoring dispute
Anand resigns the match before the game begins
Carlsen loses, forcing a tiebreak
Carlsen draws the game, sealing overall victory

evt-11-22-2013-magnus-carlsen.butterflyEffect: Carlsen drew the game to clinch the match 6.5–3.5, dethroning Anand and becoming World Chess Champion at 22. It launched a reign in which Carlsen held the No. 1 world ranking for over a decade and successfully defended the title multiple times before voluntarily relinquishing the classical crown in 2023.

evt-11-22-2014-african-americans.scenario: It's the afternoon of November 22, 2014, in a Cleveland recreation center park. A caller tells the 911 dispatcher a boy is waving a gun, adding twice that it is 'probably fake' and he's 'probably a juvenile' — but that caveat never reaches the officers racing to the scene.
evt-11-22-2014-african-americans.prompt: What happens when the patrol car pulls up to the boy in the park?

choices.text: The boy drops the toy and is safely taken into custody
The officers confiscate the toy gun and issue a warning
An officer shoots the boy within seconds of the car stopping
The officers observe from a distance and call for a hostage negotiator

evt-11-22-2014-african-americans.butterflyEffect: Twelve-year-old Tamir Rice was shot within two seconds of the officers' arrival; he died the next day. A grand jury declined to indict, but the killing became a national flashpoint in the Black Lives Matter movement, prompting a Justice Department review of Cleveland police and new rules on relaying 911 caller information to responding officers.

evt-11-22-2022-2022-chesapeake-shooting.scenario: It's the night of November 22, 2022, inside a Chesapeake, Virginia Walmart. Employees are gathering in the break room for a routine shift briefing when their night-shift supervisor arrives armed, having grown convinced his coworkers were harassing him.
evt-11-22-2022-2022-chesapeake-shooting.prompt: What happens in the break room that night?

choices.text: He barricades the room and takes hostages for negotiation
He confronts a manager verbally and is talked down by staff
He fires warning shots and flees the store
He opens fire on his coworkers before taking his own life

evt-11-22-2022-2022-chesapeake-shooting.butterflyEffect: Andre Bing opened fire during the briefing, killing six coworkers and wounding others before taking his own life; his note cited perceived workplace harassment and loneliness. The shooting renewed national debate over workplace violence prevention and Walmart's employee safety policies.

evt-11-23-1644-english-civil-war.scenario: You are a London printer in November 1644. Parliament's licensing order forbids publishing anything without prior approval, but you hold a manuscript by John Milton arguing that censorship itself is tyranny.
evt-11-23-1644-english-civil-war.prompt: What does Milton do with his unlicensed manuscript against censorship?

choices.text: Submit it to Parliament's censors for approval first
Print and distribute it unlicensed in open defiance of the order
Sell it anonymously through a foreign printer instead
Burn it rather than risk prosecution

evt-11-23-1644-english-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Milton published Areopagitica himself, defying the Licensing Order of 1643 outright rather than seeking approval. The pamphlet had little immediate legal effect, but it became a foundational text of free-press argument, later cited by framers of the US First Amendment and Enlightenment thinkers on liberty of expression.

evt-11-23-1700-1700-conclave.scenario: You are a cardinal elector locked in a Roman conclave that has dragged on for a month, split between a rising zelanti faction and moderates, when word arrives that the childless Charles II of Spain has just died, threatening a European war over his succession.
evt-11-23-1700-1700-conclave.prompt: With that alarming news, what does the conclave do to end the deadlock?

choices.text: Rally around a compromise candidate seen as non-partisan
Suspend the conclave until the succession crisis is resolved
Elect the outright leader of the zelanti faction
Ask the French crown to name the next pope directly

evt-11-23-1700-1700-conclave.butterflyEffect: The cardinals swiftly elected Giovanni Albani, seen as acceptably neutral, who took the name Clement XI. His papacy was almost immediately consumed by the War of the Spanish Succession, forcing him to balance the rival pressures of France and the Habsburgs for years afterward.

evt-11-23-1733-danish-west-indies.scenario: It is before dawn on 23 November 1733 on St. John. You are among the enslaved Akwamu men chosen to seize Fort Frederiksvaern, the Danish garrison guarding the harbor at Coral Bay.
evt-11-23-1733-danish-west-indies.prompt: How do the rebels get past the fort's guards to launch the uprising?

choices.text: They wait for a prisoner exchange to slip weapons inside
They scale the fort's walls using ropes under cover of a storm
They hide weapons inside bundles of firewood brought in as a routine delivery
They bribe the Danish commander to open the gates at night

evt-11-23-1733-danish-west-indies.butterflyEffect: The rebels smuggled cane knives into the fort hidden in bundles of firewood, then killed the soldiers and raised a cannon-fire signal that launched the revolt. The insurgents controlled most of St. John for about six months until French and Swiss troops from Martinique crushed the rebellion in 1734, but it remains one of the earliest and longest-sustained slave uprisings in the Americas.

evt-11-23-1867-manchester-martyrs.scenario: It is 23 November 1867 outside Salford Gaol, and a crowd gathers to watch the execution of William Allen, Michael Larkin, and Michael O'Brien, convicted after Sergeant Charles Brett was killed during a Fenian rescue of two imprisoned leaders.
evt-11-23-1867-manchester-martyrs.prompt: What effect does the execution of the three men have on Irish nationalism?

choices.text: It effectively ends the Fenian movement in Ireland
It galvanizes Irish nationalist sentiment and becomes a rallying symbol
It results in a general amnesty for other convicted Fenians
It leads the British government to grant immediate Home Rule

evt-11-23-1867-manchester-martyrs.butterflyEffect: Rather than crushing the movement, the hangings turned the three men into martyrs for Irish republicanism, inspiring the song 'God Save Ireland' and swelling support for the Fenian cause. Their memory endured for generations, cited by later republicans including leaders of the 1916 Easter Rising.

evt-11-23-1876-william-m-tweed.scenario: It is 23 November 1876. Having fled to Cuba and then Spain after escaping custody, William 'Boss' Tweed has just been recognized from a Thomas Nast cartoon and extradited back to New York.
evt-11-23-1876-william-m-tweed.prompt: What happens to Tweed once he is returned to the city he once controlled?

choices.text: He is imprisoned again and dies in custody without regaining freedom
He is acquitted at a new trial for lack of evidence
He is pardoned by the governor and resumes his political career
He escapes a second time and disappears permanently

evt-11-23-1876-william-m-tweed.butterflyEffect: Tweed was returned to prison in New York and died in the Ludlow Street Jail in 1878, having never regained his freedom. His downfall, driven partly by Nast's cartoons, became a symbol of the fight against political machine corruption and spurred later civil-service reform efforts.

evt-11-23-1976-jacques-mayol.scenario: It is November 23, 1976, off the coast of Elba, Italy. You are Jacques Mayol, gripping a weighted sled that will pull you down through the water on a 'no-limits' dive to a depth many physiologists believe the human body cannot survive.
evt-11-23-1976-jacques-mayol.prompt: What does Mayol accomplish on this attempt?

choices.text: He requires emergency rescue partway down
He sets a new record for longest breath-hold on land
He aborts the dive just short of the goal
He becomes the first person to freedive to 100 metres

evt-11-23-1976-jacques-mayol.butterflyEffect: Mayol became the first person to freedive to 100 metres, a feat that helped validate the theory of the mammalian diving reflex allowing the body to withstand extreme depths. His friendly rivalry with fellow diver Enzo Maiorca later inspired Luc Besson's 1988 film The Big Blue, which popularized freediving as a sport worldwide.

evt-11-23-1980-1980-irpinia-earthquake.scenario: It is the evening of November 23, 1980, in the Irpinia region of southern Italy. You are a local official as violent shaking collapses buildings across dozens of towns, leaving hundreds of thousands of people without shelter as winter approaches.
evt-11-23-1980-1980-irpinia-earthquake.prompt: What major criticism follows in the years after the disaster?

choices.text: International aid offers are turned away
The army rebuilds every affected town within weeks
The government's response is praised as swift and effective
Reconstruction funds are slowed by corruption and inefficiency

evt-11-23-1980-1980-irpinia-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Reconstruction funds were plagued by delays, mismanagement, and corruption, dragging the rebuilding effort out for decades and becoming a lasting symbol of state inefficiency in Italy. The disaster's chaotic response led directly to the creation of Italy's national Civil Protection Department in 1982 to better coordinate future emergencies.

evt-11-23-1991-queen-band.scenario: You read a press statement released on 23 November 1991 in which Freddie Mercury, after years of rumor, confirms he has AIDS, just a day before his death.
evt-11-23-1991-queen-band.prompt: What does Mercury's statement ask of the public?

choices.text: To expect Queen to resume touring immediately
To join him in the fight against the AIDS epidemic
To deny the rumors circulating about his health
To boycott media coverage of his illness

evt-11-23-1991-queen-band.butterflyEffect: Mercury died the following day, 24 November 1991. His disclosure and death brought AIDS into mainstream public conversation, led to the founding of the Mercury Phoenix Trust to fund HIV/AIDS charities, and encouraged greater openness from other public figures living with the virus.

evt-11-23-1992-ibm-simon.scenario: You are wandering the COMDEX show floor in Las Vegas in November 1992 when IBM unveils a strange grey slab: part telephone, part computer, with a screen you can tap with a pen.
evt-11-23-1992-ibm-simon.prompt: What can this device do that a standard 1992 mobile phone cannot?

choices.text: Take and store digital photographs
Browse the World Wide Web over a cellular connection
Play downloaded digital music files
Send and receive faxes and emails through a touchscreen with installable apps

evt-11-23-1992-ibm-simon.butterflyEffect: The IBM Simon, later released commercially in 1994, combined a touchscreen PDA with cellular calling, fax, and email, using a PCMCIA slot for extra software. Though a commercial footnote, it is now widely credited as the first true smartphone, predating the iPhone by fifteen years.

evt-11-23-1996-ethiopian-airlines-flight.scenario: You are the captain of Ethiopian Airlines Flight 961 on 23 November 1996. Hijackers demanding you fly to Australia have refused every request to land, and your fuel gauges are now reading empty over the Indian Ocean near the Comoros.
evt-11-23-1996-ethiopian-airlines-flight.prompt: With no fuel left and hijackers still refusing to let you land, what do you do?

choices.text: Turn back toward Kenya and hope to stretch the remaining fuel
Attempt a controlled ditching in the ocean near a visible beach
Circle over the water and wait for a rescue plan from the hijackers
Try to force an emergency landing at the nearest Comoros airport

evt-11-23-1996-ethiopian-airlines-flight.butterflyEffect: The captain attempted a controlled ditching near a Comoros beach, but a wingtip struck the water first and the plane broke apart and flipped; 125 of 175 aboard died, though about 50 survived. Filmed by tourists on the shore, it became the first recorded ditching of a wide-body jet and a case study still used in aviation survival training.

evt-11-23-2001-budapest-convention-on-cy.scenario: You are a Council of Europe delegate in Budapest in November 2001, about to sign a treaty drafted with input from the United States, Canada, and Japan to tackle a crime wave no single country's laws can reach.
evt-11-23-2001-budapest-convention-on-cy.prompt: What is the treaty's core purpose you are being asked to endorse?

choices.text: Harmonize national cybercrime laws and improve cross-border investigative cooperation
Ban all government surveillance of online communications
Create a permanent international court to try hackers
Establish a single global agency to govern the internet

evt-11-23-2001-budapest-convention-on-cy.butterflyEffect: The Budapest Convention became the first international treaty on cybercrime, pushing signatory nations to harmonize computer-crime laws and cooperate across borders on investigations. Russia and several other states refused to join, citing sovereignty concerns, a split that still shapes global debates over internet governance.

evt-11-23-2002-space-shuttle-endeavour.scenario: It is November 23, 2002, at Kennedy Space Center. You are strapped into Space Shuttle Endeavour, moments from launching on mission STS-113, carrying a fresh crew bound for the International Space Station.
evt-11-23-2002-space-shuttle-endeavour.prompt: What is a key objective of this mission besides the crew rotation?

choices.text: Delivering the Destiny laboratory module
Testing the Canadarm2 robotic arm for the first time
Installing the P1 truss segment on the space station
Deploying the Hubble Space Telescope

evt-11-23-2002-space-shuttle-endeavour.butterflyEffect: STS-113 delivered and installed the P1 truss segment, expanding the station's structural backbone and cooling capacity, while swapping in the Expedition 6 crew. It was the last shuttle flight to fly successfully before the Columbia disaster in February 2003 grounded the fleet for over two years.

evt-11-23-2003-rose-revolution.scenario: You stand among thousands on Tbilisi's Rustaveli Avenue in November 2003, furious over rigged election results, as Mikheil Saakashvili urges the crowd toward the Parliament building where Shevardnadze is speaking.
evt-11-23-2003-rose-revolution.prompt: What do you do as the crowd surges toward the parliament session?

choices.text: Boycott the parliament entirely and go home
Storm the building armed with rifles seized from police
March inside carrying roses, refusing to bring any weapons
Wait outside for international mediators to intervene

evt-11-23-2003-rose-revolution.butterflyEffect: Demonstrators stormed the chamber unarmed, carrying red roses, and Shevardnadze resigned days later, ending Soviet-era leadership in Georgia. The bloodless revolution became a template for later uprisings like Ukraine's Orange Revolution, and Georgia's subsequent pivot toward the West strained relations with Russia for years to come.

evt-11-23-2005-ellen-johnson-sirleaf.scenario: It is 23 November 2005 in Monrovia. You are a Liberian election official confirming the runoff results between Ellen Johnson Sirleaf and football star George Weah.
evt-11-23-2005-ellen-johnson-sirleaf.prompt: What historic milestone does the runoff's outcome achieve?

choices.text: George Weah becomes Liberia's youngest-ever president
The election is annulled amid fraud allegations
Ellen Johnson Sirleaf becomes Africa's first elected female head of state
A military council seizes power before results are announced

evt-11-23-2005-ellen-johnson-sirleaf.butterflyEffect: Sirleaf's victory made her Africa's first elected female head of state, and she governed Liberia until 2018. In 2011 she shared the Nobel Peace Prize for her work advancing women's rights and rebuilding the country after civil war.

evt-11-23-2007-mv-explorer-1969.scenario: It is November 23, 2007, and you are aboard MS Explorer, an Antarctic cruise ship navigating the Bransfield Strait near the South Shetland Islands, when the hull strikes something hard and unseen beneath the icy water.
evt-11-23-2007-mv-explorer-1969.prompt: What ultimately happens to the passengers and crew after the ship is holed?

choices.text: Rescue is delayed for days due to storms
The ship is towed to port and repaired
Several lifeboats are lost in the frigid water
All aboard are rescued safely before the ship sinks

evt-11-23-2007-mv-explorer-1969.butterflyEffect: Explorer took on water and sank the following day, becoming the first cruise ship lost in the Southern Ocean, but all 154 passengers and crew were rescued by a nearby vessel, the Nordnorge. The incident intensified scrutiny of polar tourism safety and contributed to stricter international guidelines for ships operating in ice-covered waters.

evt-11-23-2009-esmael-mangudadatu.scenario: It is November 23, 2009, in Maguindanao province, Philippines. Fearing assassination if he files it himself, Esmael Mangudadatu has sent his wife, female relatives, lawyers, and a group of local journalists to register his candidacy for governor on his behalf.
evt-11-23-2009-esmael-mangudadatu.prompt: What happens to the convoy as it travels the highway to the election office?

choices.text: It is escorted the entire way by the national military
It is briefly delayed at a checkpoint but proceeds unharmed
It is ambushed by gunmen and the passengers are massacred
It registers the candidacy safely and returns home

evt-11-23-2009-esmael-mangudadatu.butterflyEffect: The convoy was stopped and massacred by armed men linked to the rival Ampatuan clan; 58 people were killed, including 32 journalists, making it the deadliest single attack on the press in history. The atrocity led to martial law being declared in Maguindanao and a decade-long trial that ended in 2019 with murder convictions against members of the Ampatuan family.

evt-11-23-2009-maguindanao-massacre.scenario: It is November 2009 in Maguindanao. You are vice-mayor Esmael Mangudadatu, about to challenge the powerful Ampatuan clan for governor, but you fear an ambush if you personally file your candidacy papers.
evt-11-23-2009-maguindanao-massacre.prompt: Believing the clan won't harm women, what do you decide to do?

choices.text: Send his wife and female relatives with journalists to file the papers
Withdraw his candidacy to avoid confrontation
Postpone filing until after the election deadline passes
Go himself surrounded by a heavily armed escort

evt-11-23-2009-maguindanao-massacre.butterflyEffect: Mangudadatu sent his wife, sisters, and a convoy of journalists and lawyers to file the papers instead. The convoy was stopped and 58 people were slaughtered, the deadliest single attack on journalists in history, triggering a decade-long trial that ended in 2019 with the conviction of Andal Ampatuan Jr. and others.

evt-11-23-2010-2010-yeonpyeongdo-bombard.scenario: You are stationed with South Korean marines on Yeonpyeong Island on 23 November 2010, midway through a routine artillery drill, when North Korean shells suddenly begin striking military positions and nearby homes.
evt-11-23-2010-2010-yeonpyeongdo-bombard.prompt: What does the South Korean military do in response to the barrage?

choices.text: Suspend all further military exercises without responding
Immediately evacuate the island without returning fire
Return fire with artillery while raising the military alert level
Request an emergency United Nations airstrike

evt-11-23-2010-2010-yeonpyeongdo-bombard.butterflyEffect: South Korean forces returned fire with K9 self-propelled howitzers within minutes, and the country raised its military alert status across the region. The exchange drew international condemnation of North Korea and led Seoul to reinforce island defenses and revise its rules of engagement for future border incidents.

evt-11-23-2011-arab-spring.scenario: It is 23 November 2011 in Riyadh. You are President Ali Abdullah Saleh, having ruled Yemen for 33 years while nine months of mass protests have battered your government, and Gulf mediators now place a transition deal before you.
evt-11-23-2011-arab-spring.prompt: What do you do with the GCC initiative on the table?

choices.text: Dissolve parliament and call for immediate new elections himself
Flee the country into exile without any formal agreement
Refuse the deal and order a harsher crackdown on protesters
Sign the GCC initiative transferring power to his vice president

evt-11-23-2011-arab-spring.butterflyEffect: Saleh signed the deal, transferring power to Vice President Hadi in exchange for immunity from prosecution. The handover ended his long rule but left Yemen's fragile transition unresolved, a fragility that fed into the Houthi takeover and the devastating civil war that erupted within a few years.

evt-11-23-2018-dolce-gabbana.scenario: It is late November 2018 and you are an executive at Dolce & Gabbana. Ads mocking Chinese culture and leaked messages attributed to Domenico Dolce using racist slurs have gone viral days before your major Shanghai runway show, and Chinese celebrities and retailers are pulling out.
evt-11-23-2018-dolce-gabbana.prompt: With the boycott spreading fast, what does the brand do?

choices.text: Defend the ads publicly as harmless satire
Stay silent and let the controversy fade on its own
Proceed with the Shanghai show exactly as planned
Issue a video apology claiming the accounts were hacked

evt-11-23-2018-dolce-gabbana.butterflyEffect: The founders released a video apology on 23 November insisting their accounts had been hacked, but it failed to calm the storm. The Shanghai show was cancelled, Chinese e-commerce platforms pulled the brand's products, and Dolce & Gabbana's sales in China suffered for years afterward.

evt-11-24-1542-anglo-scottish-wars.scenario: It's 24 November 1542, and you ride with the Scottish force under Lord Maxwell that has crossed into England on King James V's orders, only to find an English army closing in as your men bog down in the marshy ground of Solway Moss.
evt-11-24-1542-anglo-scottish-wars.prompt: What happens to the Scottish force in the chaos that follows?

choices.text: They negotiate a truce and withdraw peacefully
They are routed and largely captured while trying to flee across the moss
They win a decisive victory over the English
They retreat safely and reach Edinburgh intact

evt-11-24-1542-anglo-scottish-wars.butterflyEffect: The Scots were routed while trying to flee across the moss, and English forces captured roughly 1,200 men with few killed outright. The humiliating defeat contributed to King James V's death weeks later, leaving the throne to his infant daughter Mary and plunging Scotland into the instability that led to the 'Rough Wooing.'

evt-11-24-1643-thirty-years-war.scenario: It is late November 1643 near Tuttlingen in southern Germany. You command the French army under Josias von Rantzau, settling into winter quarters as Bavarian and Spanish forces under Franz von Mercy approach unseen through the hills.
evt-11-24-1643-thirty-years-war.prompt: What should the French commander do to guard against surprise attack?

choices.text: Post strong outposts and scouts to give early warning
Launch a pre-emptive night attack on Mercy's camp
Retreat westward across the Rhine immediately
Send envoys to negotiate a local truce

evt-11-24-1643-thirty-years-war.butterflyEffect: Rantzau's army was caught almost entirely unprepared, its outposts overrun and much of the force captured or scattered in the ensuing Battle of Tuttlingen. The defeat crippled French momentum on the Rhine for the campaign season and gave the Bavarian-Spanish alliance a rare, morale-boosting victory late in the war.

evt-11-24-1859-on-the-origin-of-species.scenario: It is 24 November 1859 at a London bookshop. Charles Darwin's 'On the Origin of Species' has just gone on sale, and customers are lining up at the counter.
evt-11-24-1859-on-the-origin-of-species.prompt: What happens to the first print run on its opening day?

choices.text: The entire first print run sells out on the day of release
The publisher recalls the book after public protests
Sales are slow until a favorable royal endorsement months later
The book is banned by the Church of England before sale begins

evt-11-24-1859-on-the-origin-of-species.butterflyEffect: The entire first print run of 1,250 copies sold out on its first day. The book ignited fierce scientific, philosophical, and religious debate, and within two decades natural selection had become the dominant framework in biology, reshaping how humanity understood its place in nature.

evt-11-24-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 24 November 1863, and you march with Union General Joseph Hooker's men up the fog-shrouded slopes of Lookout Mountain outside Chattanooga, Tennessee, where Confederate defenders hold the heights above.
evt-11-24-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: How do Union troops manage to dislodge the entrenched Confederates above?

choices.text: Charge directly up the sheer cliff face in the open
Hold position and wait several days for reinforcements
Use the fog to conceal a flanking advance around the mountainside
Rely solely on artillery bombardment from the valley floor

evt-11-24-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Thick fog cloaked the Union advance, letting troops work around the Confederate flank in what became known as the 'Battle Above the Clouds.' The mountain's capture helped set up the decisive Union victory at Missionary Ridge the next day, breaking the Confederate siege of Chattanooga and opening the way for Sherman's later march into Georgia.

evt-11-24-1918-podgorica-assembly.scenario: It is 24 November 1918 in Podgorica. You are a delegate at the Great People's Assembly, called to decide whether Montenegro will unite unconditionally with the Kingdom of Serbia and depose King Nikola I.
evt-11-24-1918-podgorica-assembly.prompt: How do you cast your vote on the resolution before the assembly?

choices.text: Vote against union, insisting Montenegro remain independent under Nikola I
Walk out of the assembly in protest before any vote is taken
Vote in favor of unconditional union with Serbia and the king's removal
Propose a union that preserves the Montenegrin monarchy

evt-11-24-1918-podgorica-assembly.butterflyEffect: The assembly voted for unconditional union, deposing Nikola I and merging Montenegro into what became the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes just days later. Montenegrins who rejected the assembly's legitimacy launched the Christmas Uprising in protest, a split between "Whites" and "Greens" that shaped Montenegrin politics for generations and echoed in its eventual 2006 independence.

evt-11-24-1922-irish-civil-war.scenario: It is November 1922 in County Wicklow. You are Erskine Childers, novelist and former IRA intelligence officer, captured by Free State troops with a small pistol — a gift from Michael Collins — found in your pocket.
evt-11-24-1922-irish-civil-war.prompt: What sentence follows your trial by Free State military court?

choices.text: Sentenced to death and executed by firing squad
Sentenced to life imprisonment
Deported to Britain
Acquitted and released

evt-11-24-1922-irish-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Childers was convicted of possessing the pistol under the new Emergency Powers Resolution and executed by firing squad on 24 November 1922, even as his appeal was still pending. His calm death made him one of the Civil War's most debated executions. His son, Erskine Hamilton Childers, later became President of Ireland.

evt-11-24-1941-the-holocaust.scenario: It is late November 1941, and you are a Nazi administrator overseeing the new ghetto being established in the fortress town of Terezín in occupied Czechoslovakia. Officials want it to serve a dual purpose beyond simple confinement.
evt-11-24-1941-the-holocaust.prompt: How is the ghetto officially presented to the outside world?

choices.text: As a self-governing spa community for elderly and prominent Jews
As a quarantine hospital for infectious diseases
As a prisoner-of-war camp for captured Allied soldiers
As an armaments factory town for forced laborers

evt-11-24-1941-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: Theresienstadt was marketed as a 'model' Jewish settlement, later staged for a 1944 Red Cross visit to hide the truth of deportations. In reality it functioned as a transit point: the vast majority of its inmates were eventually sent onward to Auschwitz and other death camps, and the deception helped conceal the genocide from international scrutiny.

evt-11-24-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the morning of 24 November 1943, hours after Makin Atoll has fallen to American forces. You serve aboard the escort carrier USS Liscome Bay, standing offshore to support the landing.
evt-11-24-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What threat should the task force watch for most closely in these waters?

choices.text: Kamikaze air raid
Japanese submarine attack
An approaching typhoon
Land-based coastal artillery

evt-11-24-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: A Japanese submarine, I-175, torpedoed Liscome Bay that morning; her bomb magazine exploded and the carrier sank within minutes, killing over 640 sailors. The disaster exposed the vulnerability of thinly-escorted carriers during island landings and pushed the Navy toward tighter anti-submarine screening for future amphibious operations.

evt-11-24-1950-great-appalachian-storm-o.scenario: It's late November 1950, and as a utility dispatcher in the Appalachian region you watch barometric pressure plunge as a single monstrous storm threatens to bring blizzard conditions to the mountains and hurricane-force winds to the lowlands simultaneously.
evt-11-24-1950-great-appalachian-storm-o.prompt: What do you prioritize as the storm bears down on your service area?

choices.text: Concentrate solely on snow removal equipment
Pre-position repair crews for widespread power line failures
Preemptively shut down all rail travel in the region
Focus resources only on coastal evacuation

evt-11-24-1950-great-appalachian-storm-o.butterflyEffect: The storm's hurricane-force winds, gusting past 100 mph in places, knocked out power to roughly a million customers across the Eastern United States while heavy snow buried the mountains. The unprecedented combination of hazards from one system pushed the Weather Bureau toward better coordination in tracking storms that mixed winter and hurricane-strength conditions.

evt-11-24-1963-jack-ruby.scenario: It's Sunday morning, 24 November 1963, in the basement of Dallas police headquarters. Lee Harvey Oswald, accused of assassinating President Kennedy, is being walked through a crowd of reporters toward an armored car, and you have pushed close with a pistol hidden in your coat.
evt-11-24-1963-jack-ruby.prompt: What do you do as Oswald passes within reach?

choices.text: Hand reporters documents implicating Oswald
Wait quietly for the trial to proceed
Demand Oswald confess publicly before the cameras
Shoot Oswald at point-blank range

evt-11-24-1963-jack-ruby.butterflyEffect: Jack Ruby shot Oswald point-blank on live television, and Oswald died two days later without ever standing trial. His death denied investigators a courtroom accounting of the assassination, fueling decades of conspiracy theories; Ruby himself was convicted of murder and died in prison in 1967 before a retrial could take place.

evt-11-24-1971-d-b-cooper.scenario: It is the evening of 24 November 1971, and you are the hijacker known as Dan Cooper aboard Northwest Orient Flight 305, having just received $200,000 in cash and four parachutes as the Boeing 727 flies over the Pacific Northwest.
evt-11-24-1971-d-b-cooper.prompt: What do you do next to make your escape?

choices.text: Hide in the cargo hold until after landing
Order the pilot to land immediately and flee on foot
Jump from the aircraft's rear stairs while still airborne
Demand the plane divert to Cuba

evt-11-24-1971-d-b-cooper.butterflyEffect: Cooper lowered the plane's rear stairs and parachuted into a stormy night over southwest Washington, vanishing without a confirmed trace despite one of the largest manhunts in FBI history. The case remains unsolved to this day, and it prompted airlines to redesign the 727's aft stairway with a device preventing it from being opened mid-flight, later nicknamed the 'Cooper vane.'

evt-11-24-1976-1976-cald-ran-muradiye-ea.scenario: It is the afternoon of 24 November 1976. You are a Turkish army officer rushing toward Çaldıran and Muradiye after a violent magnitude-7.3 earthquake, with winter closing in on the mountainous Van countryside.
evt-11-24-1976-1976-cald-ran-muradiye-ea.prompt: What is your most urgent priority as rescue teams reach the ruined villages?

choices.text: Evacuate all survivors immediately to Ankara for permanent resettlement
Wait in place until international aid teams arrive before beginning any rescue
Search the rubble for survivors and set up emergency shelter before nightfall
Focus resources on rebuilding permanent housing before winter arrives

evt-11-24-1976-1976-cald-ran-muradiye-ea.butterflyEffect: Rescue and relief were badly hampered by the remote, mountainous terrain and onset of harsh winter weather, contributing to a death toll estimated between 4,000 and 5,000. The disaster exposed the fragility of rural Anatolian building practices, feeding into later, still-unfinished debates over construction standards that resurfaced after subsequent major Turkish earthquakes.

evt-11-24-2012-2012-dhaka-garment-factor.scenario: It is the evening of 24 November 2012 inside the Tazreen Fashion factory near Dhaka. Smoke is spreading through the building and the fire alarm sounds while workers are still at their sewing machines.
evt-11-24-2012-2012-dhaka-garment-factor.prompt: What do the factory's managers reportedly tell workers when the alarm goes off?

choices.text: They immediately evacuate the entire building floor by floor
They insist it is a false alarm and order everyone back to work
They lock the gates to prevent theft during the confusion
They call the fire department before telling any workers

evt-11-24-2012-2012-dhaka-garment-factor.butterflyEffect: Supervisors told workers it was a false alarm and ordered them to keep working, a decision that trapped many when the fire spread and exits proved inadequate. The disaster drew international attention to unsafe conditions in Bangladesh's garment industry and helped set the stage for broader safety reform campaigns in the years that followed.

evt-11-24-2013-iran.scenario: It is late November 2013 in Geneva. You are part of Iran's negotiating team, hours from sealing an interim deal with the US, UK, France, Russia, China and Germany over your nuclear program.
evt-11-24-2013-iran.prompt: What must Iran agree to do to secure this interim nuclear deal?

choices.text: Ship its entire uranium stockpile to Russia for permanent storage
Abandon its civilian nuclear program in exchange for full sanctions relief
Dismantle its entire uranium enrichment infrastructure immediately
Halt enrichment above 5%, neutralize its higher-grade stockpile, and allow more inspections

evt-11-24-2013-iran.butterflyEffect: Iran agreed to halt enrichment above 5%, neutralize its stockpile of near-20% enriched uranium, and accept expanded IAEA inspections, in exchange for limited sanctions relief. The Geneva accord became the foundation for the far more comprehensive 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, itself later abandoned when the US withdrew in 2018.

evt-11-24-2015-sukhoi-su-24.scenario: You are the pilot of a Russian Su-24 flying a bombing run over Syrian rebel-held territory near the Turkish border on 24 November 2015. Turkish air controllers have repeatedly warned over radio that you are drifting into their airspace.
evt-11-24-2015-sukhoi-su-24.prompt: Do you alter course away from the border or press on with the bombing run?

choices.text: Radio Moscow to request new orders before continuing
Immediately alter course away from the border
Abort the mission and return to base
Press on with the bombing run, ignoring the warnings

evt-11-24-2015-sukhoi-su-24.butterflyEffect: The pilot ignored the warnings and was shot down by a Turkish F-16; he was killed by rebels on the ground while parachuting down, and a Russian marine died in the rescue operation. Moscow imposed sweeping economic sanctions on Turkey, freezing relations until a rapprochement followed the failed 2016 coup against Erdoğan.

evt-11-24-2015-russian-air-force.scenario: You advise the Kremlin hours after a Turkish F-16 shot down a Russian Su-24 near the Syrian border on 24 November 2015. Putin is furious, and Turkey, a NATO member, insists the jet violated its airspace despite repeated warnings.
evt-11-24-2015-russian-air-force.prompt: How does the Kremlin choose to retaliate against Turkey?

choices.text: Sever all diplomatic relations with Turkey
Launch immediate airstrikes against Turkish military positions
Impose economic sanctions, including a tourism and food-import ban
Ignore the incident to avoid escalation with a NATO member

evt-11-24-2015-russian-air-force.butterflyEffect: Russia imposed sweeping economic sanctions, banning Turkish food imports and halting package tourism to Turkey, while stopping short of military retaliation. Relations stayed frozen for months until the failed 2016 coup against Erdoğan pushed the two leaders back toward cooperation, especially over Syria.

evt-11-24-2016-colombia.scenario: It is 24 November 2016 in Bogotá. Weeks after Colombian voters narrowly rejected the first peace deal with FARC in a referendum, President Juan Manuel Santos is about to sign a revised agreement.
evt-11-24-2016-colombia.prompt: How does the government secure approval for this new deal after the referendum defeat?

choices.text: A second referendum is held and passes by a landslide
The United Nations imposes the agreement without Colombian approval
The revised deal is sent to Congress for ratification instead of another referendum
FARC unilaterally declares the war over without a signed deal

evt-11-24-2016-colombia.butterflyEffect: Rather than risk another referendum, Santos sent the revised accord to Colombia's Congress, which ratified it. FARC fighters demobilized and the group transformed into a political party, though violence from other armed groups continued in parts of the country; Santos received the Nobel Peace Prize that year for the negotiations.

evt-11-24-2022-2022-malaysian-general-el.scenario: Five days after Malaysia's 19 November 2022 election left parliament hung with no coalition holding a majority, you stand before King Sultan Abdullah as rival coalition leaders press their claims to form a government.
evt-11-24-2022-2022-malaysian-general-el.prompt: Whom does the King appoint as prime minister to end the deadlock?

choices.text: Anwar Ibrahim
Muhyiddin Yassin
Mahathir Mohamad
Ismail Sabri Yaakob

evt-11-24-2022-2022-malaysian-general-el.butterflyEffect: The King appointed Anwar Ibrahim, who had spent decades pursuing the premiership through opposition, imprisonment and near-misses. Anwar formed a unity government with former rivals including UMNO, ending years of political instability that had toppled two previous prime ministers since 2018.

evt-11-25-1510-adil-shahi-portuguese-con.scenario: It is 25 November 1510. Having been driven out of Goa months earlier, you return with a reinforced fleet to find the Adil Shahi garrison entrenched behind the city's walls, and your officers await your order.
evt-11-25-1510-adil-shahi-portuguese-con.prompt: As Afonso de Albuquerque, what do you order?

choices.text: Blockade the harbor and starve the garrison into surrender
Withdraw the fleet and target a weaker port instead
Launch an immediate full assault on the fortifications
Negotiate terms with the Adil Shahi commander

evt-11-25-1510-adil-shahi-portuguese-con.butterflyEffect: Albuquerque launched a fierce assault and retook Goa, massacring much of the Muslim garrison in reprisal for the earlier defeat. Goa became the capital of the Portuguese Estado da Índia and remained under Portuguese rule for over 450 years, until its annexation by India in 1961.

evt-11-25-1678-trunajaya-rebellion.scenario: It is 25 November 1678. After weeks of grueling marches through eastern Java, your combined Mataram and Dutch East India Company forces finally stand before the rebel stronghold of Kediri.
evt-11-25-1678-trunajaya-rebellion.prompt: What should the allied commanders do?

choices.text: Offer Trunajaya a negotiated surrender with amnesty
Settle in for a prolonged siege to conserve troops
Withdraw to resupply before attempting the fortress
Launch a coordinated assault on the fortress before rebel reinforcements arrive

evt-11-25-1678-trunajaya-rebellion.butterflyEffect: The allied forces stormed and captured Kediri, breaking the back of Trunajaya's rebellion. The VOC's decisive military role deepened its influence over the Mataram court, a pattern that steadily expanded Dutch control across Java in the decades that followed.

evt-11-25-1795-stanis-aw-august-poniatow.scenario: It is 25 November 1795 in Grodno. Russian troops occupy the town, and officials place a document before you: your formal abdication as King of Poland, following the Third Partition that has erased your country from the map.
evt-11-25-1795-stanis-aw-august-poniatow.prompt: As Stanisław II Augustus, what do you do?

choices.text: Flee to raise a foreign army and reclaim the throne
Refuse to sign and call the Sejm into emergency session
Sign the abdication rather than provoke further bloodshed
Appeal directly to Napoleon for military intervention

evt-11-25-1795-stanis-aw-august-poniatow.butterflyEffect: Stanisław signed, ending both his reign and the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth's 800-year existence as an independent state. Poland vanished from the map for 123 years, its lands absorbed by Russia, Prussia, and Austria, until independence was restored in 1918.

evt-11-25-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 25 November 1863, and you stand with the Army of the Cumberland at the base of Missionary Ridge outside Chattanooga. Your orders are only to make a limited demonstration against the Confederate rifle pits below the ridge.
evt-11-25-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: What do you and the men around you do once you reach the base of the ridge?

choices.text: Wait in place for a full artillery bombardment first
Attempt a wide flanking march around the south end of the ridge
Press the charge straight up the steep slope beyond your orders
