Retreat back to camp as instructed after the demonstration

evt-11-25-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Without waiting for further orders, Union troops spontaneously surged up the steep slope and broke Bragg's center, routing the Confederate army. The victory secured Chattanooga as a Union base and set up Sherman's 1864 Atlanta Campaign.

evt-11-25-1885-banff-national-park.scenario: It's 1883, and you are a Canadian Pacific Railway worker who has just stumbled onto steaming hot springs at the foot of Sulphur Mountain. Rival prospectors quickly move to stake private claims to the site.
evt-11-25-1885-banff-national-park.prompt: How does the Canadian government resolve the dispute over the hot springs?

choices.text: It sells the springs to the highest private bidder
It grants exclusive rights to the Canadian Pacific Railway
It reserves the land as protected federal territory
It leaves the claims to be settled by local courts

evt-11-25-1885-banff-national-park.butterflyEffect: Ottawa set aside a small reserve around the springs in 1885 to keep them public, which grew into Rocky Mountains Park — Canada's first national park. The model spread, leading to the creation of Parks Canada in 1911, the world's first national park service.

evt-11-25-1901-gustav-mahler.scenario: It's 25 November 1901 in Munich. You sit in the concert hall as Gustav Mahler steps up to conduct the premiere of his Fourth Symphony, a work far gentler and more childlike than his earlier, darker symphonies.
evt-11-25-1901-gustav-mahler.prompt: How does the audience respond to this unexpectedly simple, sunny work?

choices.text: With official condemnation and a ban on further performances
With a mixed, puzzled reception from critics
With a unanimous, rapturous standing ovation
With a walkout and near-riot

evt-11-25-1901-gustav-mahler.butterflyEffect: The Munich audience and critics reacted with confusion and coolness, expecting the grand scale of his earlier symphonies rather than this pastoral simplicity. Mahler's music, including the Fourth, only found wide popularity decades later, especially after a post-1945 revival that made him one of the most performed composers of the 20th century.

evt-11-25-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It's late November 1917 in German East Africa. You serve under General Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck, whose small, cut-off force is running out of food, ammunition, and medicine.
evt-11-25-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What does the general do to keep his campaign alive?

choices.text: Surrenders immediately to British forces
Retreats into German South-West Africa
Invades Portuguese East Africa to seize supplies
Attempts to sail his men back to Germany

evt-11-25-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Lettow-Vorbeck led his men across the border into Portuguese East Africa, capturing Portuguese depots to resupply his force. Living off seized supplies, he kept fighting for another year, only surrendering on 25 November 1918 — over a week after the Armistice in Europe, making his the last German force to lay down arms in the war.

evt-11-25-1936-anti-comintern-pact.scenario: It's 25 November 1936 in Berlin. You watch German ambassador-at-large Joachim von Ribbentrop and Japanese ambassador Kintomo Mushanokōji sign a new pact framed publicly as a stand against communism.
evt-11-25-1936-anti-comintern-pact.prompt: Beyond its public anti-Comintern language, what does the pact actually contain?

choices.text: A full economic and currency union between Germany and Japan
A secret protocol aimed specifically at the Soviet Union
A binding mutual defense pact against Britain and France
A secret agreement to partition China between them

evt-11-25-1936-anti-comintern-pact.butterflyEffect: A secret protocol specifically targeted the Soviet Union, obliging both powers to consult if either were attacked by the USSR. Italy joined the following year, and the pact became the scaffolding for the wider Axis alliance, formalized in the 1940 Tripartite Pact between Germany, Italy, and Japan.

evt-11-25-1940-de-havilland-mosquito.scenario: It is 25 November 1940 at Hatfield aerodrome. You are chief test pilot Geoffrey de Havilland Jr., preparing for the first flight of a prototype fighter-bomber built almost entirely of wood.
evt-11-25-1940-de-havilland-mosquito.prompt: What practical wartime problem does building the aircraft from wood solve?

choices.text: It avoids straining scarce wartime supplies of aluminum and metalworkers
Wood makes the aircraft invisible to enemy radar
Wood is lighter than any metal alloy available in 1940
Wood is structurally stronger than aluminum at high speed

evt-11-25-1940-de-havilland-mosquito.butterflyEffect: Wood construction let furniture makers and cabinetmakers build the airframe, sidestepping the wartime shortage of strategic aluminum and skilled metalworkers. The Mosquito went on to serve as a bomber, night fighter, and reconnaissance aircraft, with over 7,000 built by war's end.

evt-11-25-1960-mirabal-sisters.scenario: It is 25 November 1960. You are Minerva Mirabal, driving with your sisters Patria and María Teresa along a remote mountain road after visiting your imprisoned husbands, knowing Trujillo's agents have long watched your family.
evt-11-25-1960-mirabal-sisters.prompt: Despite the danger, what do you and your sisters decide to do?

choices.text: Abandon the visit and flee the country that night
Disguise themselves and travel separately
Continue the journey home despite the known risk
Turn back and request a military escort

evt-11-25-1960-mirabal-sisters.butterflyEffect: The sisters were ambushed and killed on that road by Trujillo's agents. The killings provoked international outrage and fueled the underground resistance, contributing to Trujillo's own assassination less than a year later; the date is now the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

evt-11-25-1970-mishima-incident.scenario: It is 25 November 1970 at Japan Self-Defense Forces headquarters in Tokyo. You are one of Yukio Mishima's Tatenokai followers, and you have just helped him take the camp commandant hostage in his office.
evt-11-25-1970-mishima-incident.prompt: What does Mishima do next to try to achieve his aims?

choices.text: He steps onto the balcony to call on the assembled troops to stage a coup
He and his followers attempt to flee through a rear exit
He orders the hostage freed immediately and surrenders
He negotiates the commandant's release for safe passage out

evt-11-25-1970-mishima-incident.butterflyEffect: Mishima stepped onto the balcony and addressed the assembled soldiers, but they jeered and shouted him down. He returned inside and committed seppuku with a follower's assistance; the act shocked Japan and became a lasting symbol of resistance to the postwar pacifist order, though it sparked no coup.

evt-11-25-1999-elian-gonzalez.scenario: It is Thanksgiving morning, 25 November 1999, off the coast of Fort Lauderdale. You are a fisherman who has just spotted an inner tube bobbing in the waves with a five-year-old boy clinging to it, alone.

choices.text: Mark the coordinates and continue fishing before returning
Tow the inner tube to shore without boarding him
Pull him aboard and radio the Coast Guard
Wait for a larger vessel to arrive first

evt-11-25-1999-elian-gonzalez.butterflyEffect: The fishermen pulled the boy, Elián González, from the sea and turned him over to authorities, setting off a bitter international custody battle between his father in Cuba and relatives in Miami. The dispute strained U.S.–Cuba relations for months before federal agents removed him from his Miami relatives' home in April 2000 and he was returned to his father in Cuba.

evt-11-25-2009-2009-jeddah-floods.scenario: You are a resident of Jeddah on 25 November 2009, watching water rise over streets whose drainage system officials had promised to finish years earlier.
evt-11-25-2009-2009-jeddah-floods.prompt: What follows once investigators look into why the flooding was so catastrophic?

choices.text: The entire drainage system is rebuilt within weeks
No investigation is ever opened
Officials and contractors are prosecuted for corruption and negligence
The flooding is ruled an unavoidable natural event with no fault found

evt-11-25-2009-2009-jeddah-floods.butterflyEffect: Saudi authorities charged dozens of officials and contractors with corruption and negligence over unfinished drainage projects, with several later convicted. Yet the underlying infrastructure problems persisted, and Jeddah flooded again in 2011.

evt-11-26-1835-texas-revolution.scenario: It is 26 November 1835 near San Antonio de Bexar. You ride with James Bowie's scouts when word arrives that a Mexican pack train, rumored to be carrying a silver payroll, is approaching the besieged town.
evt-11-26-1835-texas-revolution.prompt: What do you and the other Texian riders do when you spot the mule train?

choices.text: Let the train pass unmolested into town
Attack the pack train, expecting to seize silver
Send a rider to negotiate its surrender first
Retreat to avoid contact with Mexican forces

evt-11-26-1835-texas-revolution.butterflyEffect: The Texians attacked, only to discover the mules were loaded with grass for the garrison's horses, not silver — earning the skirmish its lasting nickname, the "Grass Fight." Though anticlimactic, it boosted Texian morale and pressure on the besieged Mexican garrison just weeks before the town fell.

evt-11-26-1842-university-of-notre-dame.scenario: It is late November 1842 on the shore of a frozen lake in northern Indiana. You are Father Edward Sorin, a young French priest of the Congregation of Holy Cross, standing amid snow and unfinished log buildings with almost no money and only a handful of brothers.
evt-11-26-1842-university-of-notre-dame.prompt: What do you decide to do despite the harsh conditions and lack of resources?

choices.text: Postpone the founding until spring thaw
Found the school anyway, trusting Providence and hard work
Relocate the mission to a warmer southern state
Return to France and wait for better funding

evt-11-26-1842-university-of-notre-dame.butterflyEffect: Sorin pressed ahead and founded the University of Notre Dame du Lac that winter. The struggling frontier mission grew into a major Catholic research university, its Golden Dome and football program eventually making it one of the most recognized names in American higher education.

evt-11-26-1914-hms-bulwark-1899.scenario: It is the morning of 26 November 1914, and you are a sailor aboard the battleship HMS Bulwark, moored at Kethole Reach near Sheerness. Below decks, cordite charges are stacked near the ship's magazines ahead of an inspection.
evt-11-26-1914-hms-bulwark-1899.prompt: What causes the disaster that engulfs Bulwark this morning?

choices.text: A torpedo strike from a German U-boat
A collision with another vessel in the anchorage
A boiler explosion from faulty engine-room valves
An internal explosion in the ship's magazines, likely from overheated cordite

evt-11-26-1914-hms-bulwark-1899.butterflyEffect: A massive internal explosion tore Bulwark apart in seconds, killing more than 730 officers and men; only a dozen survived. It remains one of the Royal Navy's worst peacetime-anchorage losses, and after a near-identical explosion destroyed HMS Princess Irene months later, the fleet tightened its cordite storage and handling procedures.

evt-11-26-1917-eddie-livingstone.scenario: It is 26 November 1917 in a Montreal hotel room. You are an NHA team owner, and years of feuding with Toronto Blueshirts owner Eddie Livingstone have made the league unworkable.
evt-11-26-1917-eddie-livingstone.prompt: How did the owners resolve their impasse with Livingstone?

choices.text: Dissolved the NHA and formed the NHL without him
Bought out Livingstone's franchise at full price
Merged his team with a rival Toronto club he still controlled
Suspended the Blueshirts for one season only

evt-11-26-1917-eddie-livingstone.butterflyEffect: Rather than keep fighting Livingstone within the NHA, the other owners dissolved the association and formed a brand-new league, the National Hockey League, quietly leaving him without a club in it. The NHL went on to become the dominant professional ice hockey league in North America.

evt-11-26-1939-red-army.scenario: It is 26 November 1939. You are a Finnish diplomat in Helsinki when Moscow accuses Finland of shelling the Soviet border village of Mainila and demands an apology and troop withdrawal.
evt-11-26-1939-red-army.prompt: How does the Finnish government respond to the Soviet accusation?

choices.text: Immediately withdraw all troops as demanded
Declare war on the Soviet Union first
Deny responsibility and propose a joint investigation
Ignore the Soviet accusation entirely

evt-11-26-1939-red-army.butterflyEffect: Finland denied responsibility and proposed a joint investigation, but the Soviet Union used the incident as pretext to renounce its non-aggression pact. Four days later, on 30 November 1939, the Red Army invaded Finland, starting the Winter War.

evt-11-26-1940-iron-guard.scenario: It is late November 1940 in Romania. The Iron Guard now shares power with General Ion Antonescu and seeks revenge against former officials it blames for the 1938 killing of its founder, Corneliu Codreanu, whose bodies were held at Jilava prison near Bucharest.
evt-11-26-1940-iron-guard.prompt: What does the Iron Guard do to the detainees held responsible?

choices.text: Grant the detainees a pardon
Put the detainees on public trial
Exile the detainees from Romania
Storm the prison and kill the detainees in reprisal

evt-11-26-1940-iron-guard.butterflyEffect: Iron Guard members stormed Jilava and killed 64 political detainees in reprisal. The massacre deepened the rift between Antonescu and the Guard, a tension that exploded two months later when Antonescu crushed the Guard's Bucharest uprising in January 1941.

evt-11-26-1942-casablanca-film.scenario: You are Rick Blaine, standing on the fog-shrouded tarmac of Casablanca's airport, holding two letters of transit that could let you flee with the woman you love or send her away with her husband.
evt-11-26-1942-casablanca-film.prompt: What does Rick actually do with the letters of transit?

choices.text: He destroys the letters so no one can leave
He gives them to Ilsa and Victor, letting them fly to safety while he stays behind
He uses them to escape with Ilsa alone, abandoning Victor
He hands Victor over to the police and keeps Ilsa for himself

evt-11-26-1942-casablanca-film.butterflyEffect: Rick's sacrifice at the airport became one of cinema's most quoted endings, and Casablanca went on to win the Academy Award for Best Picture in 1944. Its blend of wartime romance and moral choice made it an enduring symbol of sacrifice for a larger cause, still referenced constantly in film and popular culture.

evt-11-26-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 26 November 1942 in the town of Bihać, and you are a delegate gathered by Josip Broz Tito to represent Yugoslavia's scattered anti-Axis resistance movements.
evt-11-26-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What does this first assembly actually decide to establish?

choices.text: An armistice with the occupying Axis forces
A political council to unite the anti-fascist resistance and govern liberated territory
A formal alliance with the royalist Chetniks under Draža Mihailović
A request for the exiled Yugoslav government to return immediately

evt-11-26-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: This meeting created the Anti-Fascist Council for the National Liberation of Yugoslavia (AVNOJ), which grew into the provisional government of a new socialist Yugoslavia. By war's end it had displaced the exiled monarchy entirely, and Tito used it as the constitutional basis for the federal state he led until 1980.

evt-11-26-1977-southern-television-broad.scenario: It is the evening of 26 November 1977, and you're the duty engineer at Southern Television when the audio abruptly cuts out mid-broadcast, replaced by a strange voice claiming to speak for an 'Intergalactic Association.'
evt-11-26-1977-southern-television-broad.prompt: What's your first move as the mysterious voice hijacks the transmission?

choices.text: Try to trace the point of intrusion while the fault is investigated
Broadcast a live on-air apology over the voice
Evacuate the studio, assuming a technical explosion
Immediately cut the transmitter to kill the signal

evt-11-26-1977-southern-television-broad.butterflyEffect: Engineers could not trace or stop the intrusion, which lasted five and a half minutes before the scheduled cartoon resumed on its own. No perpetrator was ever officially identified, and the incident remains a famous unsolved case, later cited as a landmark example of broadcast signal vulnerability.

evt-11-26-1979-pakistan-international-ai.scenario: It is 26 November 1979, and you're the captain of PIA Flight 740, climbing out of Jeddah toward Karachi, when a fire suddenly breaks out somewhere in the passenger cabin.
evt-11-26-1979-pakistan-international-ai.prompt: Facing an uncontrolled in-flight fire, what should the crew do?

choices.text: Attempt an emergency return to the nearest airport
Ask passengers to fight the fire themselves and carry on
Ditch the aircraft in the sea immediately
Continue on to Karachi as scheduled

evt-11-26-1979-pakistan-international-ai.butterflyEffect: The crew turned back toward Jeddah, but the Boeing 707 crashed near Taif before it could land, killing all 156 aboard. Investigators suspected the fire originated from cargo, prompting tighter screening of baggage and freight on Hajj-season charter flights.

evt-11-26-1983-brink-s.scenario: It is before dawn on 26 November 1983. You are a security guard at the Brink's-Mat warehouse near Heathrow when six armed men burst in, douse you with petrol, and demand you open the vault they expected to hold cash.
evt-11-26-1983-brink-s.prompt: What did the terrified guards ultimately do to save their lives?

choices.text: Reveal the vault combination under threat of being set alight
Overpower the robbers with a hidden weapon
Convince the robbers the vault was empty
Trigger a silent alarm and refuse to cooperate

evt-11-26-1983-brink-s.butterflyEffect: The guards revealed the vault combination, and the robbers discovered not cash but 6,800 gold bars worth about £26 million — Britain's largest robbery at the time. Laundering the gold drew in fences and financiers across London, and the fallout eventually led to further murders, including that of an undercover detective years later.

evt-11-26-2008-2008-mumbai-attacks.scenario: It's the night of 26 November 2008, and you're a Mumbai police officer as reports flood in of gunmen striking multiple sites at once — the Taj Hotel, the Oberoi, and CST railway station.
evt-11-26-2008-2008-mumbai-attacks.prompt: How should authorities respond to attacks unfolding simultaneously across the city?

choices.text: Wait for international forces before taking any action
Open immediate negotiations with the attackers
Send a single unit to the first reported site only
Coordinate police, NSG commandos, and hotel security together

evt-11-26-2008-2008-mumbai-attacks.butterflyEffect: The siege stretched over three days before National Security Guard commandos secured the last building. The attacks exposed major gaps in coastal surveillance and inter-agency coordination, leading India to establish new NSG regional hubs and overhaul its maritime security in the years that followed.

evt-11-26-2011-nasa.scenario: It is 26 November 2011, and NASA's Mars Science Laboratory has just lifted off from Cape Canaveral atop an Atlas V rocket, carrying a car-sized rover toward Mars.
evt-11-26-2011-nasa.prompt: What actually happens when the spacecraft reaches Mars nine months later?

choices.text: It burns up during an uncontrolled atmospheric entry
It lands safely using a rocket-powered "sky crane" that lowers the rover on cables
It crash-lands after its parachute fails to deploy
It misses Mars and enters an unplanned solar orbit

evt-11-26-2011-nasa.butterflyEffect: In August 2012, the untested rocket-powered "sky crane" maneuver worked perfectly, lowering the rover Curiosity safely into Gale Crater. Curiosity went on to find evidence of ancient habitable lakes and organic molecules on Mars, discoveries that helped justify NASA's later Perseverance mission and its search for signs of past microbial life.

evt-11-26-2011-2011-nato-attack-in-pakis.scenario: It is the night of 25–26 November 2011 at a Pakistani military checkpoint near the Afghan border. NATO aircraft open fire on your position in what becomes the Salala incident, killing soldiers on both sides of a confused firefight.
evt-11-26-2011-2011-nato-attack-in-pakis.prompt: How did Pakistan respond to the attack in the days that followed?

choices.text: Immediately declared war on the coalition forces
Closed NATO's overland supply routes into Afghanistan
Expelled all American diplomats from Islamabad
Requested more joint patrols with NATO troops

evt-11-26-2011-2011-nato-attack-in-pakis.butterflyEffect: Pakistan closed its border crossings to NATO supply convoys bound for Afghanistan and ordered the United States to vacate Shamsi Airfield, used for drone operations. The supply routes stayed shut for roughly seven months, straining the US–Pakistan alliance until Washington issued a formal apology.

evt-11-26-2011-mars-science-laboratory.scenario: It is 26 November 2011 at Cape Canaveral, and you're a NASA engineer watching the Atlas V rocket thunder skyward, carrying the car-sized rover Curiosity toward Mars.
evt-11-26-2011-mars-science-laboratory.prompt: What is Curiosity's primary scientific goal once it reaches the Martian surface?

choices.text: Build the first permanent human habitat
Collect samples for immediate return to Earth
Investigate whether Mars could have supported life and study its climate
Search only the Martian poles for ice caps

evt-11-26-2011-mars-science-laboratory.butterflyEffect: Curiosity landed successfully in Gale Crater in August 2012 using a novel rocket-powered 'sky crane,' then confirmed that Mars once had conditions suitable for microbial life. The rover far outlasted its planned two-year mission, still operating more than a decade later.

evt-11-26-2018-uncrewed-spacecraft.scenario: It is 26 November 2018 at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. The InSight lander is plunging toward Elysium Planitia on Mars, and the signal delay means Earth cannot send any commands during the final descent.
evt-11-26-2018-uncrewed-spacecraft.prompt: How must InSight survive its landing without help from mission control?

choices.text: Wait for real-time commands relayed from Earth
Abort descent and enter a holding orbit
Rely on an onboard astronaut to fly it manually
Follow its pre-programmed autonomous landing sequence

evt-11-26-2018-uncrewed-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: InSight executed its pre-programmed entry, descent, and landing sequence entirely on its own and touched down safely. Its seismometer went on to detect marsquakes, giving scientists their first direct data on the Red Planet's internal structure.

evt-11-26-2019-2019-albania-earthquake.scenario: It is the early hours of 26 November 2019 in Thumanë, Albania. A magnitude 6.4 earthquake has just collapsed several buildings, and you are among the first rescuers to arrive amid the dust and debris.
evt-11-26-2019-2019-albania-earthquake.prompt: What should rescue teams prioritize first?

choices.text: Search collapsed buildings immediately for trapped survivors
Evacuate the area entirely before any search begins
Focus first on restoring electricity and water service
Wait for international teams before starting search efforts

evt-11-26-2019-2019-albania-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Rescue crews focused on searching collapsed buildings for survivors trapped in the rubble, aided by international teams from across Europe. The disaster, Albania's deadliest earthquake in 99 years, prompted the government to declare a state of emergency and led to renewed scrutiny of substandard construction practices blamed for the scale of the collapses.

evt-11-26-2021-covid-19-pandemic.scenario: It is 26 November 2021, and you're a health ministry adviser reading the WHO's urgent bulletin: a newly detected variant from southern Africa, Omicron, has just been classified a 'variant of concern.'
evt-11-26-2021-covid-19-pandemic.prompt: What do governments rush to do in the days right after the announcement?

choices.text: Declare the pandemic officially over
Ignore the announcement as routine
Impose travel restrictions on southern African countries
Immediately lift all existing COVID restrictions worldwide

evt-11-26-2021-covid-19-pandemic.butterflyEffect: Dozens of countries imposed travel bans on southern African nations within days, a move the WHO and African leaders criticized as unfair since Omicron was merely detected there first. The variant nonetheless became globally dominant within weeks, driving a massive but comparatively less lethal wave of infections.

evt-11-26-2025-wang-fuk-court-fire.scenario: It is the evening of 26 November 2025, and flames are racing up bamboo scaffolding wrapped in green mesh outside your block at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, Hong Kong. Smoke is already seeping under your apartment door.
evt-11-26-2025-wang-fuk-court-fire.prompt: What is the safest immediate action as the fire spreads outside the building?

choices.text: Move to the rooftop and wait for helicopter rescue
Evacuate immediately down the stairwell, away from the burning side of the building
Wait inside your apartment for firefighters to reach you
Take the elevator down to the ground floor

evt-11-26-2025-wang-fuk-court-fire.butterflyEffect: Fueled by flammable scaffolding netting and foam sheeting left over from a renovation, the fire spread across seven of the complex's eight towers and burned for over 44 hours, killing 168 people, most of them trapped inside their homes. It became Hong Kong's deadliest fire since 1948, prompting arrests of contractors over substandard materials and a sweeping review of fire-safety rules for buildings under renovation.

evt-11-27-1095-council-of-clermont.scenario: It is 27 November 1095, the final day of the Council of Clermont. You stand in the crowd of clergy and knights as Pope Urban II rises to close the synod with an unexpected and urgent appeal.
evt-11-27-1095-council-of-clermont.prompt: What does Urban II call on the assembled Franks to do?

choices.text: Take up arms to aid Byzantium and reclaim Jerusalem
Submit to new taxes for church reform
Depose King Philip I of France immediately
End all private feuding under the Truce of God alone

evt-11-27-1095-council-of-clermont.butterflyEffect: Urban called for warriors to march east and aid the Byzantine Christians against the Seljuk Turks, promising remission of sins to those who took up the cross. The response launched the First Crusade, culminating in the capture of Jerusalem in 1099 and the founding of the Crusader states.

evt-11-27-1703-great-storm-of-1703.scenario: It is the night of 26 November 1703, and you captain a merchant vessel anchored off the treacherous Goodwin Sands as an unprecedented gale roars in from the Atlantic, straining your anchor cables to breaking point.
evt-11-27-1703-great-storm-of-1703.prompt: What should you do to give your ship and crew the best chance of survival?

choices.text: Lower the crew into small boats and row for the nearby shore
Stay anchored in place and wait for the storm to pass
Drop every spare anchor overboard and hope the extra weight holds the ship fast
Cut the anchor cables and attempt to run before the wind toward open sea

evt-11-27-1703-great-storm-of-1703.butterflyEffect: Many ships that stayed at anchor were driven onto the Goodwin Sands and wrecked, killing over a thousand sailors there alone. The storm devastated the Royal Navy's fleet and became England's deadliest recorded natural disaster, later immortalized in Daniel Defoe's pioneering journalistic account 'The Storm', which helped popularize systematic weather reporting.

evt-11-27-1895-alfred-nobel.scenario: You are Alfred Nobel, sitting in the Swedish-Norwegian Club in Paris on November 27, 1895. Your dynamite patents have made you wealthy, and you must decide what becomes of your fortune after death.
evt-11-27-1895-alfred-nobel.prompt: What does Nobel's will direct his fortune to fund?

choices.text: An endowment left entirely to his surviving relatives
A single chemistry research institute in Stockholm
A donation to the Swedish royal treasury
Prizes rewarding those who benefit humanity

evt-11-27-1895-alfred-nobel.butterflyEffect: The will established the Nobel Prizes in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature and Peace, first awarded in 1901 through the Nobel Foundation. It transformed Nobel's reputation from 'merchant of death' to patron of humanity's greatest achievements, and the prizes remain the most prestigious in their fields.

evt-11-27-1944-raf-fauld-explosion.scenario: It is 27 November 1944 and you work in the underground bomb store at RAF Fauld in Staffordshire, handling live ordnance among thousands of tonnes of high explosive. A routine task with a detonator is about to go wrong.
evt-11-27-1944-raf-fauld-explosion.prompt: What triggered the catastrophic explosion at the depot?

choices.text: Sabotage by enemy agents inside the facility
Lightning ignited the stored explosives
A German bombing raid struck the depot directly
A worker mishandling a detonator with the wrong tool caused a spark

evt-11-27-1944-raf-fauld-explosion.butterflyEffect: The improper removal of a detonator sparked a chain detonation of thousands of tonnes of stored munitions, gouging a crater over 300 feet wide and killing dozens of workers and villagers. It remains one of the largest non-nuclear explosions in history and prompted tighter safety protocols for underground munitions storage.

evt-11-27-1945-care-international.scenario: It is late 1945. Europe lies in ruins and millions face starvation through the coming winter. Twenty-two American charities have just pooled their resources into a new agency, and you must decide what to actually put in the hands of the hungry.
evt-11-27-1945-care-international.prompt: What did the new agency send to war-ravaged families across Europe?

choices.text: Medical teams with no food or supplies
Shipments of clothing and blankets only
Surplus U.S. Army food parcels repackaged for civilians
Cash grants wired directly to European governments

evt-11-27-1945-care-international.butterflyEffect: CARE repurposed surplus U.S. Army "10-in-1" food parcels into the first CARE Packages, sent directly to named individuals in Europe. The program became so iconic that "CARE package" entered everyday English, and the organization grew into one of the world's largest humanitarian and development agencies.

evt-11-27-1950-korean-war.scenario: It is November 27, 1950, near the Chosin Reservoir in North Korea. Waves of Chinese People's Volunteer Army soldiers pour out of the frozen mountains, encircling US and UN troops who had been pushing toward the Yalu River.
evt-11-27-1950-korean-war.prompt: What do the surrounded UN forces do next?

choices.text: Surrender en masse to Chinese forces
Fight their way south in a breakout toward the coast
Call for immediate use of nuclear weapons
Hold their position indefinitely awaiting reinforcements

evt-11-27-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: The trapped Marines and soldiers fought a grueling breakout south to Hungnam, later evacuated by sea in December 1950 in what became known as the 'Frozen Chosin.' The disaster ended any hope of reunifying Korea by force and pushed the war toward the long stalemate near the 38th parallel that would define the conflict's remaining years.

evt-11-27-1963-lyndon-b-johnson.scenario: It is 27 November 1963, five days after Kennedy's assassination. You sit in the chamber of a joint session of Congress as the new president rises to speak, invoking Kennedy's memory to press for unfinished business.
evt-11-27-1963-lyndon-b-johnson.prompt: What did Johnson urge Congress to pass in memory of Kennedy?

choices.text: A tax cut for defense industry workers
The civil rights bill Kennedy had proposed
A constitutional amendment on presidential succession
A declaration of war in Vietnam

evt-11-27-1963-lyndon-b-johnson.butterflyEffect: Johnson used the speech to demand swift passage of Kennedy's stalled civil rights bill, framing it as the best tribute to the fallen president. Congress passed the landmark Civil Rights Act of 1964 the following year, becoming a cornerstone of Johnson's Great Society and one of the most consequential laws of the century.

evt-11-27-1989-avianca-flight-203.scenario: It is 27 November 1989 and you board Avianca Flight 203 out of Bogotá. Unknown to passengers, Pablo Escobar's cartel has planted a bomb aboard, hoping to kill a rising political figure they believe is on this flight.
evt-11-27-1989-avianca-flight-203.prompt: Who was the cartel's intended target on Flight 203?

choices.text: A Colombian Supreme Court judge
Sitting President Virgilio Barco Vargas
A U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration agent
Presidential candidate César Gaviria

evt-11-27-1989-avianca-flight-203.butterflyEffect: Presidential candidate César Gaviria had booked a seat but canceled at the last moment, so he survived while all 107 people aboard and three on the ground were killed. Gaviria won the presidency in 1990 and intensified the war against Escobar's cartel, a campaign that ended with Escobar's death in 1993.

evt-11-27-1992-military.scenario: It is 27 November 1992 in Venezuela. Nine months after Hugo Chávez's failed coup, fellow officers approach you with a plan to strike again against President Carlos Andrés Pérez, using air force jets and army units this time.
evt-11-27-1992-military.prompt: What actually happened when the plotters launched their uprising?

choices.text: The coup succeeded and Pérez fled the country
The military refused to act and no coup was attempted
The United States intervened militarily to end it
Loyalist forces suppressed the coup and Pérez remained in power

evt-11-27-1992-military.butterflyEffect: Loyalist forces crushed the second coup within hours, but the attempt further exposed how fragile Pérez's authority had become. He was impeached on corruption charges in 1993, and the instability paved the way for Chávez's own election to the presidency in 1998.

evt-11-27-2004-pope-john-paul-ii.scenario: It is November 27, 2004, in a Vatican basilica. Pope John Paul II hands over ancient relics of Saint John Chrysostom, long housed in Rome since they were taken from Constantinople centuries earlier, to envoys of the Ecumenical Patriarchate.
evt-11-27-2004-pope-john-paul-ii.prompt: What was this gesture meant to advance?

choices.text: A trade of relics for Vatican Museum artifacts
Reconciliation between the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches
A military alliance against the Ottoman Empire's successors
The return of looted Byzantine art to the Greek state

evt-11-27-2004-pope-john-paul-ii.butterflyEffect: The relics had been carried west after the Fourth Crusade's 1204 sack of Constantinople. Returning them was a deliberate step in John Paul II's long campaign to heal the 1054 East-West Schism, easing centuries of tension between Rome and the Orthodox world and paving the way for further ecumenical exchanges.

evt-11-27-2004-blackwater-61-crash.scenario: It is 27 November 2004, and you are an investigator examining wreckage on Koh-i-Baba mountain, where a Blackwater-operated CASA 212 flying troops and supplies through Afghanistan went down with no survivors reaching help in time.
evt-11-27-2004-blackwater-61-crash.prompt: What did the investigation find had caused the crash?

choices.text: A mechanical engine failure at high altitude
Pilots flying a nonstandard low route for fun
Enemy ground fire striking the aircraft
A sudden and unpredictable mountain storm

evt-11-27-2004-blackwater-61-crash.butterflyEffect: The NTSB found the pilots had deliberately flown a nonstandard, low-altitude route through the valley for entertainment rather than following their filed flight plan, and the aircraft struck the mountain. The disaster intensified scrutiny of private military contractors' safety practices and fed into broader debates over accountability for contractors operating in war zones.

evt-11-27-2006-house-of-commons-of-canad.scenario: It is November 27, 2006, and you are a Member of Parliament in Ottawa. Prime Minister Stephen Harper has introduced a motion declaring that the Québécois form a nation within a united Canada, hours before the Bloc Québécois plans its own motion.
evt-11-27-2006-house-of-commons-of-canad.prompt: How did the House of Commons respond to Harper's motion?

choices.text: Rejected it after fierce debate
Passed it only in the Senate, not the Commons
Approved it overwhelmingly
Sent it to a national referendum

evt-11-27-2006-house-of-commons-of-canad.butterflyEffect: MPs approved the motion by a lopsided 266–16 vote, blunting the Bloc's separate push and offering symbolic recognition without any constitutional change. Cabinet minister Michael Chong resigned rather than support it, and the vote reignited debate over what Quebec's 'nationhood' actually meant within Canada.

evt-11-27-2008-xl-airways-germany-flight.scenario: It is 27 November 2008. You are part of the crew flying an acceptance test of a new Airbus A320 over the Mediterranean near the French-Spanish border, pushing the aircraft to its performance limits at low altitude.
evt-11-27-2008-xl-airways-germany-flight.prompt: What caused the aircraft's fatal loss of control during the test?

choices.text: A bird strike disabling both engines
Frozen, water-damaged angle-of-attack sensors from a maintenance error
Fuel contamination causing engine flameout
A structural failure of the wing spar

evt-11-27-2008-xl-airways-germany-flight.butterflyEffect: Water had entered the angle-of-attack sensors during earlier maintenance washing and froze at altitude, feeding false data to the flight computers just as the crew attempted a low-altitude stall test. All seven aboard died, and the investigation led Airbus to revise maintenance procedures for cleaning and protecting AOA sensors fleet-wide.

evt-11-27-2009-2009-nevsky-express-bombi.scenario: It is the evening of 27 November 2009 near Bologoye, Tver Oblast, as a bomb detonates beneath the high-speed Nevsky Express travelling from Moscow to Saint Petersburg, derailing the train.
evt-11-27-2009-2009-nevsky-express-bombi.prompt: Who claimed responsibility for the bombing in its aftermath?

choices.text: A far-right Russian nationalist group
Doku Umarov and the Caucasus insurgency
Ukrainian separatist militants
No group ever claimed the attack

evt-11-27-2009-2009-nevsky-express-bombi.butterflyEffect: Caucasus insurgent leader Doku Umarov claimed responsibility, signalling a shift by the North Caucasus insurgency toward striking targets deep inside Russia rather than only in the Caucasus region. The attack, along with a second bomb at the investigation site the next day, prompted a major tightening of Russian rail security.

evt-11-27-2020-mohsen-fakhrizadeh.scenario: It is late afternoon on 27 November 2020. You are part of the security detail riding with Iran's top nuclear scientist as his convoy passes through the small town of Absard outside Tehran.
evt-11-27-2020-mohsen-fakhrizadeh.prompt: What strikes the convoy moments later?

choices.text: A car bomb detonates alongside the road
A drone strike hits the lead vehicle
A remote-controlled machine gun opens fire from a parked pickup truck
Snipers fire from a nearby rooftop

evt-11-27-2020-mohsen-fakhrizadeh.butterflyEffect: Fakhrizadeh was killed by a remote-controlled machine gun mounted on a parked pickup truck, reportedly aided by facial-recognition targeting, in an operation widely attributed to Israel. Iran's parliament responded by passing a law to accelerate uranium enrichment, further straining nuclear diplomacy just before the incoming Biden administration.

evt-11-27-2020-utah-monolith.scenario: It is late November 2020, and you are one of thousands hiking into a remote San Juan County canyon in Utah, drawn by viral photos of a strange, gleaming metal monolith that appeared without explanation and has land managers scrambling to protect the fragile desert site.
evt-11-27-2020-utah-monolith.prompt: What ultimately happened to the monolith by the night of 27 November 2020?

choices.text: Shifting sand eventually buried it completely
It was removed and hauled away by unidentified visitors
A lightning strike destroyed the structure during a desert storm
Utah state officials dismantled it for public safety reasons

evt-11-27-2020-utah-monolith.butterflyEffect: A small group of local adventurers traveled to the canyon and dismantled the monolith themselves, citing 'leave no trace' principles and concern over the environmental damage caused by sudden crowds. Its mysterious removal only deepened public fascination, and near-identical monoliths began appearing in other countries in the following months, turning it into a lasting piece of internet-age folklore.

evt-11-28-1443-ottoman-empire.scenario: It is 1443, and you are Gjergj Kastrioti, an Albanian nobleman serving in the Ottoman army during the campaigns in the Balkans. Amid the chaos of battle near Niš, you see a chance to break from the Sultan's forces and reach your family's stronghold at Krujë.
evt-11-28-1443-ottoman-empire.prompt: What do you do with this opportunity?

choices.text: Desert and seize the fortress at Krujë
Remain loyal and report for further Ottoman service
Flee to Venice and abandon his claims
Join a Hungarian crusade without returning home

evt-11-28-1443-ottoman-empire.butterflyEffect: He deserted the Ottoman army, seized Krujë through a forged decree, and raised the banner of revolt, taking the name Skanderbeg. He went on to unite Albanian lords in the League of Lezhë and lead a resistance against the Ottomans for the next quarter century, becoming Albania's most celebrated national hero.

evt-11-28-1470-ai-viet.scenario: It is late 1470, and you march south with Emperor Lê Thánh Tông's army as it presses into the kingdom of Champa, aiming to break its power once and for all after generations of border wars.
evt-11-28-1470-ai-viet.prompt: What followed this Đại Việt invasion of Champa?

choices.text: Champa became independent under Ming Chinese protection
Champa repelled the invasion and pushed Đại Việt back to the border
The Cham capital Vijaya fell and the Cham king was captured
Both sides signed a lasting peace treaty with no territorial change

evt-11-28-1470-ai-viet.butterflyEffect: In 1471 Đại Việt forces stormed and sacked the Cham capital of Vijaya, capturing the Cham king and killing tens of thousands. The defeat shattered Champa as a major power, opening the way for centuries of Vietnamese expansion southward (the Nam tiến) that eventually absorbed most of former Cham territory.

evt-11-28-1660-robert-boyle.scenario: It is late November 1660, and you are among the scholars gathered at Gresham College after Christopher Wren's lecture. Robert Boyle, John Wilkins, and others agree that London needs a formal body to advance experimental knowledge through observation and testing.
evt-11-28-1660-robert-boyle.prompt: What do the assembled scholars decide to establish?

choices.text: A single university department at Gresham College
A private club with no lasting organization
A formal society dedicated to experimental philosophy
A petition demanding royal patronage before meeting again

evt-11-28-1660-robert-boyle.butterflyEffect: They founded what would become the Royal Society, chartered by Charles II in 1662 as one of the world's first scientific academies. It gave experimental philosophy an institutional home, publishing journals and hosting debates that shaped the modern scientific method for centuries afterward.

evt-11-28-1729-natchez-people.scenario: It is late 1729 near the French post of Fort Rosalie in the Lower Mississippi Valley. The French commandant has demanded that your people, the Natchez, abandon the fertile lands of the White Apple village so French colonists can expand their tobacco plantations.
evt-11-28-1729-natchez-people.prompt: How do the Natchez respond to the French demand for their land?

choices.text: Form an alliance with the British against the French
Attack Fort Rosalie and the surrounding French settlements
Petition the governor of Louisiana for a delay
Migrate west peacefully to avoid conflict

evt-11-28-1729-natchez-people.butterflyEffect: The Natchez launched a coordinated surprise attack, killing roughly 230 French settlers and soldiers around Fort Rosalie. France retaliated with a prolonged campaign, aided by Choctaw allies, that killed or enslaved most of the Natchez and scattered the survivors among other nations, effectively destroying the Natchez as an independent people.

evt-11-28-1811-ludwig-van-beethoven.scenario: It is November 1811 in Leipzig, and the Gewandhaus is preparing the public premiere of Beethoven's new piano concerto. Beethoven's worsening deafness makes it impossible for him to take the solo part himself, and the organizers must find someone else to sit at the keyboard.
evt-11-28-1811-ludwig-van-beethoven.prompt: Who should the organizers turn to for the solo piano part?

choices.text: Carl Czerny
Ferdinand Ries
Johann Nepomuk Hummel
Friedrich Schneider

evt-11-28-1811-ludwig-van-beethoven.butterflyEffect: They engaged the pianist and composer Friedrich Schneider, who gave the concerto its first public performance in Leipzig. The piece went on to become one of the most celebrated works in the piano repertoire, later nicknamed the "Emperor" concerto by an English publisher, and it helped establish the grand Romantic concerto style Beethoven pioneered.

evt-11-28-1912-all-albanian-congress.scenario: You are a delegate gathered in the port town of Vlorë on 28 November 1912, as Ottoman authority crumbles across the Balkans and the Balkan League armies advance. The assembled Albanian notables must decide how to respond.

choices.text: Declare independence and establish a provisional Albanian government
Renew Albania's loyalty to the Ottoman Sultan
Petition to be annexed by a Balkan League member state
Wait passively for the Great Powers to decide Albania's fate

evt-11-28-1912-all-albanian-congress.butterflyEffect: The delegates declared independence, formed a provisional government, and elected Ismail Kemal as its president. The new state was recognized by the Great Powers at the 1913 London Conference, but its borders excluded many Albanian-populated areas awarded to neighboring states, a grievance that still echoes in the region today.

evt-11-28-1925-grand-ole-opry.scenario: It is 28 November 1925. You are an announcer at radio station WSM in Nashville, about to introduce a new live music program devised by station director George D. Hay.
evt-11-28-1925-grand-ole-opry.prompt: What does Hay name this new weekly broadcast?

choices.text: The Grand Ole Opry
The WSM Barn Dance
The WSM Hayride
The National Barn Dance

evt-11-28-1925-grand-ole-opry.butterflyEffect: Hay launched it as the WSM Barn Dance; it was renamed the Grand Ole Opry in 1927. The show went on to become the longest continuously running radio broadcast in U.S. history and helped cement Nashville as the capital of country music.

evt-11-28-1966-michel-micombero.scenario: It is November 1966 in Bujumbura. As Prime Minister under the young King Ntare V, you command the loyalty of the army and see the monarchy as too weak to hold Burundi together after months of political turmoil.
evt-11-28-1966-michel-micombero.prompt: What do you do with the army behind you?

choices.text: Hand power to a civilian coalition government
Abolish the monarchy and declare a republic under his own presidency
Request Belgian military intervention to restore order
Restore full executive power to King Ntare V

evt-11-28-1966-michel-micombero.butterflyEffect: Micombero led a coup, abolished the monarchy, and declared Burundi a republic with himself as its first president. He ruled as military dictator for a decade, entrenching army and ethnic Tutsi dominance in politics, a pattern that fed later cycles of violence in Burundi.

evt-11-28-1967-jocelyn-bell-burnell.scenario: You are a PhD student at Cambridge in November 1967, hunched over yards of chart-paper printouts from a radio telescope you helped build, when you notice a strange, precisely regular pulse buried in the noise.
evt-11-28-1967-jocelyn-bell-burnell.prompt: What should you do with this puzzling repeating signal?

choices.text: Attribute it to a passing satellite and ignore it
Assume it is a fault in the telescope's wiring and move on
Dismiss it as stray radio interference from Earth
Investigate it seriously as a possible new astronomical phenomenon

evt-11-28-1967-jocelyn-bell-burnell.butterflyEffect: The signal was the first pulsar ever detected, a rapidly spinning neutron star. The 1974 Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery went to her supervisor Antony Hewish and Martin Ryle, not to Bell Burnell, and the omission became a landmark case in debates over recognition for women in science.

evt-11-28-1967-pulsar.scenario: It is 28 November 1967 in Cambridge, and you are Jocelyn Bell, poring over yards of chart-paper data from your radio telescope, staring at an oddly regular pulsing signal you and your supervisor have nicknamed "LGM-1."
evt-11-28-1967-pulsar.prompt: What did Bell and her supervisor half-jokingly suspect the strange, precise radio pulses might be?

choices.text: Radar echo from a nearby airbase
Interference from a Soviet satellite
A signal beamed by extraterrestrial intelligence
A fault in the telescope's receiver

evt-11-28-1967-pulsar.butterflyEffect: The nickname "LGM" stood for "Little Green Men," a half-serious guess that the signal might be an extraterrestrial beacon before the team identified it as a rapidly spinning neutron star: the first pulsar. The discovery opened an entire field of pulsar astrophysics, later used to test Einstein's general relativity and detect gravitational waves.

evt-11-28-1971-wasfi-tal.scenario: You are Jordanian Prime Minister Wasfi al-Tal, arriving at a Cairo hotel in November 1971 for an Arab League meeting. You do not know that Black September gunmen, seeking revenge for Jordan's 1970 crackdown on PLO fighters, are waiting outside.
evt-11-28-1971-wasfi-tal.prompt: What happens to him moments later?

choices.text: He is kidnapped and later released unharmed
He is detained by Egyptian security before any attack occurs
He narrowly escapes an assassination attempt
He is assassinated by Black September gunmen

evt-11-28-1971-wasfi-tal.butterflyEffect: Al-Tal was shot dead outside the hotel, one of Black September's most prominent assassinations. The killing signaled the group's growing reach and violence, and less than a year later they carried out the far more infamous Munich Olympics massacre in September 1972.

evt-11-28-1975-timor-leste.scenario: It is 28 November 1975 in Dili. You are among the Fretilin leadership, weeks after Portugal's abrupt withdrawal left the territory in chaos, preparing to declare independence unilaterally.
evt-11-28-1975-timor-leste.prompt: What happens just nine days after this declaration?

choices.text: Indonesia invades and occupies the territory
The United Nations sends peacekeepers to secure independence
Portugal returns to reassert colonial control
Australia formally annexes the territory

evt-11-28-1975-timor-leste.butterflyEffect: On 7 December 1975, Indonesia launched a full-scale invasion of East Timor, beginning a brutal 24-year occupation. Independence was not achieved until a 1999 UN-supervised referendum led to full sovereignty in 2002.

evt-11-28-1979-mount-erebus-disaster.scenario: It is 28 November 1979, and Air New Zealand Flight 901 descends over Antarctica for a low sightseeing pass, its crew believing they are safely over the flat expanse of McMurdo Sound near Mount Erebus.
evt-11-28-1979-mount-erebus-disaster.prompt: What did the official inquiry find had primarily caused the crash?

choices.text: Severe turbulence forcing the aircraft off course
Pilot fatigue after an unusually long overnight flight
An uncommunicated change to the programmed flight path combined with whiteout conditions
A mechanical failure in the aircraft's altimeter

evt-11-28-1979-mount-erebus-disaster.butterflyEffect: An inquiry led by Justice Peter Mahon found the aircraft's flight path coordinates had been altered the night before without the crew being told, while "sector whiteout" conditions made the ice-covered mountain visually indistinguishable from the sky. Mahon's report accused the airline of an "orchestrated litany of lies," and the case reshaped airline accountability and Antarctic tourism flight procedures.

evt-11-28-1983-space-shuttle-columbia.scenario: It is 28 November 1983, and you are one of six crew members aboard Columbia for STS-9, the largest shuttle crew flown to date, carrying a new European-built laboratory module in the cargo bay.
evt-11-28-1983-space-shuttle-columbia.prompt: What made this Columbia mission historically significant?

choices.text: It performed the first shuttle night landing
It docked with a space station for the first time
It carried the first flight of the Spacelab research module
It launched the first commercial satellite from a shuttle

evt-11-28-1983-space-shuttle-columbia.butterflyEffect: STS-9 carried Spacelab on its first flight, a reusable laboratory module built by the European Space Agency, and included Ulf Merbold, the first non-American to fly on the Space Shuttle. The mission proved international modules could support sustained orbital research, a concept later scaled up into the science segments of the International Space Station.

evt-11-28-1987-south-african-airways-fli.scenario: It is the night of 28 November 1987. You are in the cockpit of the Helderberg, a South African Airways 747 over the Indian Ocean, when smoke alarms trigger from the cargo hold below.
evt-11-28-1987-south-african-airways-fli.prompt: What does the captain attempt as the fire spreads?

choices.text: Turn back toward Taipei
Divert immediately toward Plaisance Airport in Mauritius
Descend to open cargo vents and clear the smoke
Continue on course to Johannesburg as planned

evt-11-28-1987-south-african-airways-fli.butterflyEffect: The crew tried to divert to Mauritius but lost control as the fire crippled the aircraft, and it broke apart before reaching land, killing all 159 aboard. The disaster, and the deep-sea recovery of its flight recorders, pushed aviation regulators to overhaul cargo-hold fire detection and suppression standards on wide-body jets.

evt-11-28-1989-cold-war.scenario: It is 28 November 1989, and you stand among the crowds still gathering in Prague's Wenceslas Square, weeks into mass protests against one-party rule, waiting to hear how the government will respond.
evt-11-28-1989-cold-war.prompt: What did the Communist Party of Czechoslovakia agree to that day?

choices.text: To declare martial law across the country
To relinquish its constitutional monopoly on political power
To arrest the leaders of Civic Forum
To dissolve parliament and hold elections within a week

evt-11-28-1989-cold-war.butterflyEffect: The party agreed to give up its constitutional monopoly on power and open negotiations with the opposition Civic Forum. Within weeks Václav Havel, a dissident playwright, was elected president, and Czechoslovakia's peaceful transition became a model for the term "Velvet Revolution."

evt-11-28-1990-prime-minister-of-the-uni.scenario: It is late November 1990 in Westminster. Margaret Thatcher failed to win outright in the first ballot of the Conservative leadership contest against Michael Heseltine, and after canvassing her Cabinet she has learned she no longer commands enough support to continue.
evt-11-28-1990-prime-minister-of-the-uni.prompt: What does Thatcher decide to do next?

choices.text: Call a snap general election
Force a second leadership ballot and fight on
Resign as party leader and Prime Minister
Dissolve Parliament to avoid the contest

evt-11-28-1990-prime-minister-of-the-uni.butterflyEffect: She resigned both as Conservative Party leader and as Prime Minister, ending eleven years in power. John Major succeeded her, and her departure marked the end of the Thatcherite era at the top of British government, though her policies continued to shape Conservative politics for decades.

evt-11-28-1991-south-ossetia.scenario: It is 28 November 1991, and you sit among the deputies of South Ossetia's Supreme Soviet in Tskhinvali, debating a response to years of rising tension with the Georgian government over language and autonomy.
evt-11-28-1991-south-ossetia.prompt: What did the South Ossetian legislature vote to do?

choices.text: Request an immediate United Nations peacekeeping deployment
Declare independence from Georgia
Vote to merge with North Ossetia inside Russia
Accept expanded autonomy within a new Georgian constitution

evt-11-28-1991-south-ossetia.butterflyEffect: The legislature declared independence from Georgia, a move Georgia refused to recognize. The declaration triggered the 1991–92 South Ossetia War and set the stage for decades of unresolved conflict, including the 2008 Russo-Georgian War, leaving South Ossetia's status only partially recognized to this day.

evt-11-28-2014-2014-kano-attack.scenario: It is Friday, 28 November 2014, and you are gathered with worshippers at Kano's Central Mosque, beside the Emir's palace, when explosions erupt in the courtyard.
evt-11-28-2014-2014-kano-attack.prompt: What had the Emir of Kano urged local civilians to do just before this attack?

choices.text: Evacuate the city entirely
Arm themselves to resist Boko Haram
Close all mosques until further notice
Appeal directly to the federal government for troops

evt-11-28-2014-2014-kano-attack.butterflyEffect: Two suicide bombers and gunmen killed around 120 people and wounded 260 at the mosque, a direct strike on a senior Muslim cleric who had spoken against Boko Haram. The attack deepened fears that traditional religious authorities who resisted the insurgency would themselves become targets, intensifying security crackdowns across northern Nigeria.

evt-11-28-2016-lamia-flight-2933.scenario: It is 28 November 2016. You are the co-pilot of a chartered jet carrying the Chapecoense football squad toward Medellín, and the fuel gauges are dropping faster than the flight plan allowed.
evt-11-28-2016-lamia-flight-2933.prompt: What should have been done before departure to prevent the coming crisis?

choices.text: Delay departure until the following morning
Request a more direct route from air traffic control
Stop to refuel at an intermediate airport in Bolivia
Reduce the plane's cruising altitude to save fuel

evt-11-28-2016-lamia-flight-2933.butterflyEffect: The aircraft ran out of fuel and crashed into a mountainside near Medellín, killing 71 of the 77 aboard, including most of the Chapecoense team. Investigators found the charter airline had skipped a mandatory refueling stop to save time and money; Bolivia revoked LaMia's operating license, and the tragedy drew global scrutiny of charter-flight fuel regulations.

evt-11-29-1781-slave-ship.scenario: It is 29 November 1781 aboard the slave ship Zong. Navigational errors have left the crew far off course with water supplies critically low, and the captain is weighing how to preserve what remains.
evt-11-29-1781-slave-ship.prompt: What does the crew resolve to do to conserve water and later file a claim for losses?

choices.text: Jettison non-human cargo to lighten the ship instead
Throw sick and weakened captives overboard to claim insurance for lost cargo
Ration remaining water equally among crew and captives
Divert immediately to the nearest port for fresh water

evt-11-29-1781-slave-ship.butterflyEffect: The crew threw more than 130 enslaved Africans overboard and then sought insurance payment for them as lost cargo. The resulting court case, Gregson v Gilbert, exposed the horror to the British public through abolitionists Granville Sharp and Olaudah Equiano, becoming a rallying point that helped build momentum toward the Slave Trade Act of 1807.

evt-11-29-1810-napoleonic-wars.scenario: It is November 29, 1810, and you are a British officer with troops massing at Grand Baie on the French island of Isle de France, preparing to march on the garrison at Port Louis.
evt-11-29-1810-napoleonic-wars.prompt: What follows in the days after the landing?

choices.text: A multi-year siege of Port Louis begins
A French relief fleet arrives and drives the British back to sea
The French garrison surrenders and Britain takes the island
Storms force Britain to abandon the invasion entirely

evt-11-29-1810-napoleonic-wars.butterflyEffect: The French garrison surrendered within days, and Britain seized Isle de France, renaming it Mauritius. The capture ended a major French privateering base that had long threatened British shipping to India, and Britain kept the island under the 1814 Treaty of Paris, ruling it until 1968.

evt-11-29-1854-eureka-flag.scenario: It is 29 November 1854 on Bakery Hill in Ballarat. You stand among thousands of gold miners, raising your hand to swear an oath beneath a newly sewn blue flag bearing the Southern Cross.
evt-11-29-1854-eureka-flag.prompt: What did the miners swear to do beneath the Eureka Flag?

choices.text: Disband peacefully and return to their claims
Pledge personal loyalty to Queen Victoria
Pay their mining licence fees promptly and without complaint
Stand together and resist the colonial licence system

evt-11-29-1854-eureka-flag.butterflyEffect: Days later, colonial troops stormed the stockade built beneath this same flag, and at least 27 people died in the fighting. The rebellion's aftermath brought reforms including the abolition of the hated licence fee and helped push forward the expansion of the vote in Victoria, making Eureka a founding moment in Australian democratic memory.

evt-11-29-1890-national-diet.scenario: It is 29 November 1890 in Tokyo, and you are one of the newly elected members taking your seat as Japan's Imperial Diet convenes for the very first time under the new Meiji Constitution.
evt-11-29-1890-national-diet.prompt: What real limit did this new legislature face under the Meiji Constitution?

choices.text: It could freely dismiss the Prime Minister at will
It was purely advisory and could not pass binding laws
It shared power with an Emperor who held supreme authority over the military and could dissolve it
It had full independent control over foreign policy

evt-11-29-1890-national-diet.butterflyEffect: The Meiji Constitution gave the Diet law-making power but kept sovereignty with the Emperor, who appointed the cabinet and controlled the military independent of parliamentary approval. This split authority let military and civilian leaders bypass elected representatives in later decades, feeding the rise of military dominance in the 1930s. Only in 1947 did a fully sovereign, popularly accountable Diet replace this arrangement.

evt-11-29-1947-united-nations-general-as.scenario: It is 29 November 1947 in the General Assembly hall at Flushing Meadows. You are a delegate about to cast your vote on the future of the British Mandate of Palestine after months of fierce debate.
evt-11-29-1947-united-nations-general-as.prompt: How does the General Assembly resolve to settle the fate of Palestine?

choices.text: Establish a single unified Arab state over all of Palestine
Place all of Palestine under permanent UN trusteeship
Adopt a plan partitioning Palestine into Jewish and Arab states
Reject partition and extend the British Mandate indefinitely

evt-11-29-1947-united-nations-general-as.butterflyEffect: Resolution 181 passed 33 to 13 with 10 abstentions, calling for separate Jewish and Arab states with Jerusalem under international control. Arab leaders rejected the plan, civil war erupted almost immediately, and when Britain withdrew in May 1948 Israel declared independence, triggering the first Arab-Israeli War.

evt-11-29-1952-dwight-d-eisenhower.scenario: It's December 1952. You are President-elect Eisenhower, having pledged during the campaign, 'I shall go to Korea,' to see the stalemated war firsthand before taking office.
evt-11-29-1952-dwight-d-eisenhower.prompt: What does Eisenhower do to fulfill this campaign pledge?

choices.text: He invites Korean leaders to Washington instead of traveling himself
He postpones any visit until after his inauguration in January
He flies secretly to Korea to inspect the front and meet with commanders
He sends Vice President-elect Nixon to Korea in his place

evt-11-29-1952-dwight-d-eisenhower.butterflyEffect: Eisenhower flew to Korea for a three-day visit, touring the front and meeting commanders, which convinced him the existing strategy could not win outright at an acceptable cost. This hardened his resolve to seek a negotiated end to the war, contributing to the armistice signed in July 1953 that still divides the peninsula today.

evt-11-29-1961-enos-chimpanzee.scenario: You are a NASA flight controller on November 29, 1961, watching Enos the chimpanzee's capsule malfunction midway through his second orbit, with a faulty valve triggering the wrong responses in his training panel.
evt-11-29-1961-enos-chimpanzee.prompt: What does Mission Control decide to do about the flight?

choices.text: Trigger an emergency capsule ejection immediately
End the mission early and bring Enos home after two orbits
Continue the full three orbits as originally planned
Leave him in orbit longer to gather extra data before landing

evt-11-29-1961-enos-chimpanzee.butterflyEffect: Controllers cut the mission short, bringing Enos down after two orbits instead of the planned three. He returned safely, proving the Mercury capsule and its systems could support orbital flight, clearing the way for John Glenn's historic three-orbit flight in February 1962.

evt-11-29-1963-montreal-trudeau-internat.scenario: You are a passenger boarding Trans-Canada Air Lines Flight 831 at Montréal–Dorval on the night of 29 November 1963. Minutes after takeoff, the pilots' cockpit instruments will begin feeding them false information about the aircraft's attitude.
evt-11-29-1963-montreal-trudeau-internat.prompt: What ultimately caused the crash minutes after takeoff?

choices.text: Ice buildup on the wings caused a sudden loss of control
A bomb had been planted aboard the aircraft
A faulty flight-director instrument gave the pilots false attitude readings
A bird strike disabled one of the engines on takeoff

evt-11-29-1963-montreal-trudeau-internat.butterflyEffect: All 118 people aboard the DC-8 died when it plunged into a swamp near Sainte-Thérèse, Quebec. Investigators traced the disaster to a malfunctioning flight-director instrument that misled the pilots about the plane's pitch, a finding that pushed the aviation industry toward stricter standards for instrument reliability and crew procedures.

evt-11-29-1963-lyndon-b-johnson.scenario: It's November 29, 1963, one week after President Kennedy's assassination in Dallas. Rumors of conspiracy swirl around Lee Harvey Oswald, and as the new president you need an inquiry the public will trust.
evt-11-29-1963-lyndon-b-johnson.prompt: What does Johnson do to settle doubts about the assassination?

choices.text: He calls for a joint congressional committee to investigate instead
He asks the state of Texas to lead the entire investigation
He creates a presidential commission chaired by Chief Justice Earl Warren
He hands the inquiry solely to the FBI under J. Edgar Hoover

evt-11-29-1963-lyndon-b-johnson.butterflyEffect: Johnson created a presidential commission chaired by Chief Justice Earl Warren, which concluded in 1964 that Oswald acted alone. Lingering doubts about the Commission's access to evidence fueled decades of conspiracy theories, prompting later congressional reinvestigations and ongoing fights over declassifying assassination files.

evt-11-29-1963-trans-canada-air-lines-fl.scenario: It is the evening of 29 November 1963. Word reaches Trans-Canada Air Lines headquarters that Flight 831, bound for Toronto, has gone down in poor weather just minutes after leaving Montreal-Dorval.
evt-11-29-1963-trans-canada-air-lines-fl.prompt: What made this crash historically significant at the time?

choices.text: It caused Trans-Canada Air Lines to permanently ground its fleet
It was the deadliest air crash in Canadian history to that date
It was the first jet airliner crash anywhere in North America
Investigators attributed it to a terrorist bombing

evt-11-29-1963-trans-canada-air-lines-fl.butterflyEffect: The disaster killed everyone aboard and stood as the deadliest air crash in Canadian history up to that point, as well as the deadliest DC-8 crash anywhere at the time. Its scale intensified scrutiny of jet operations in poor weather and icing conditions, feeding into the tighter procedures that later shaped Canadian aviation safety practice.

evt-11-29-1963-i-want-to-hold-your-hand.scenario: You run a record shop in London on 29 November 1963. Crates of a new single by a Liverpool quartet have just arrived, and a queue already stretches down the pavement outside.
evt-11-29-1963-i-want-to-hold-your-hand.prompt: What happens when this single is released across the Atlantic weeks later?

choices.text: It is banned from American radio for its lyrics
It becomes the Beatles' first US number-one single
Capitol Records declines to release it in America
It fails to chart outside the United Kingdom

evt-11-29-1963-i-want-to-hold-your-hand.butterflyEffect: Capitol Records rushed it out in the US in January 1964, and it became the Beatles' first American number one, selling over a million copies in ten days. Its success paved the way for their February 1964 Ed Sullivan Show appearance and launched the British Invasion of the American charts.

evt-11-29-1967-united-states-secretary-o.scenario: It is late November 1967. You have run the Pentagon for nearly seven years, but your private doubts about the strategy you built in Vietnam have grown impossible to reconcile with the war effort you are still expected to lead.
evt-11-29-1967-united-states-secretary-o.prompt: What did Robert McNamara announce on 29 November 1967?

choices.text: A plan to sharply escalate bombing of North Vietnam
His resignation as Secretary of Defense
His candidacy for the presidency
A ceasefire agreement with Hanoi

evt-11-29-1967-united-states-secretary-o.butterflyEffect: McNamara's resignation, driven by his mounting private disillusionment with the war he had overseen, paved the way for Clark Clifford's appointment as Secretary of Defense. Clifford's own growing doubts, sharpened months later by the Tet Offensive, helped push President Johnson toward de-escalation and his surprise decision not to seek re-election in 1968.

evt-11-29-1972-atari-inc.scenario: You are Atari co-founder Nolan Bushnell in late November 1972. The single test cabinet of your new game, Pong, placed in a Sunnyvale tavern, has jammed solid because its coin box overflowed with quarters within days.
evt-11-29-1972-atari-inc.prompt: What does Atari decide to do next?

choices.text: Build it only as a one-off novelty for that single tavern
Shelve the game, judging it too costly to build
License the design exclusively to Magnavox
Mass-produce Pong for wide commercial arcade release

evt-11-29-1972-atari-inc.butterflyEffect: Atari moved to mass-produce Pong for arcades, and its runaway popularity launched the commercial video arcade industry almost overnight. A home version followed in 1975 through Sears, helping spark the home video game boom of the following decade.

evt-11-29-1979-tellico-dam.scenario: It's 1979, and after decades of delay the Tennessee Valley Authority is close to completing the Tellico Dam, a project already halted once by a lawsuit over an endangered fish, the snail darter, found in the river.
evt-11-29-1979-tellico-dam.prompt: What lets the TVA finish flooding the valley despite the endangered species ruling?

choices.text: TVA relocates the snail darter and proceeds without any new legislation
The Supreme Court reverses its earlier ruling protecting the snail darter
Environmental groups voluntarily withdraw all their objections
Congress passes a specific exemption allowing the dam to proceed

evt-11-29-1979-tellico-dam.butterflyEffect: Congress attached a rider to an energy bill exempting Tellico from the Endangered Species Act, letting TVA complete the dam and flood the valley, submerging farmland and Cherokee sites like the town of Chota. The earlier Supreme Court case, TVA v. Hill, had already set a lasting precedent for strict enforcement of the Act, making Tellico a touchstone in development-versus-conservation debates.

evt-11-29-1982-michael-jackson.scenario: It's early 1983, and MTV has largely avoided videos by Black artists, branding itself a 'rock' channel. Epic Records executives lean hard on the network to add Michael Jackson's 'Billie Jean' video, riding the momentum of the freshly released Thriller album.
evt-11-29-1982-michael-jackson.prompt: Should MTV add 'Billie Jean' to rotation despite its unofficial color line?

choices.text: CBS pulls all its artists' videos from MTV in protest, and the channel loses viewers
MTV agrees to air it only during late-night hours to limit its visibility
MTV keeps refusing, so the video airs mainly on Soul Train instead
MTV puts 'Billie Jean' into rotation, becoming a turning point that opens the channel to Black artists

evt-11-29-1982-michael-jackson.butterflyEffect: MTV added 'Billie Jean' and then 'Beat It,' and the videos became must-see television, culminating in the blockbuster 14-minute 'Thriller' short film. The success forced MTV to broaden its playlist to more Black artists, reshaping the channel's identity while Thriller became history's best-selling album.

evt-11-29-1987-korean-air-flight-858.scenario: It is early December 1987. Investigators have traced two suspects from the doomed Korean Air Flight 858 to Bahrain, where security closes in on them before they can board a connecting flight out.
evt-11-29-1987-korean-air-flight-858.prompt: What do the two North Korean agents do as authorities move to arrest them?

choices.text: They attack the arresting officers and escape
They surrender immediately and cooperate fully
They attempt suicide by biting hidden cyanide capsules
They bribe local officials to let them flee to Libya

evt-11-29-1987-korean-air-flight-858.butterflyEffect: Kim Sung-il and Kim Hyon-hui bit cyanide capsules hidden in cigarettes; Kim Sung-il died, but Kim Hyon-hui survived and later confessed the bombing was ordered by Pyongyang to disrupt South Korea's upcoming election and the 1988 Seoul Olympics. Her testimony led the United States to designate North Korea a state sponsor of terrorism weeks later, a label that shaped decades of sanctions.

evt-11-29-2007-armed-forces-of-the-phili.scenario: It's November 29, 2007. Mutinous officers led by Senator Antonio Trillanes IV have walked out of their court hearing and barricaded themselves inside the Peninsula Manila hotel, demanding President Arroyo's resignation, while government troops surround the building.
evt-11-29-2007-armed-forces-of-the-phili.prompt: How does the military end the standoff at the hotel?

choices.text: Police simply cut off power and wait out the mutineers for weeks
Troops storm the hotel with armored vehicles, forcing the mutineers to surrender
The government grants immediate amnesty to end the siege peacefully
Negotiators persuade Trillanes to run for president instead

evt-11-29-2007-armed-forces-of-the-phili.butterflyEffect: An armored personnel carrier breached the hotel lobby that afternoon, and the mutineers surrendered within hours without major bloodshed. The episode burnished Trillanes's reputation as an anti-corruption dissident, and he later won a Senate seat, continuing to challenge Arroyo-era officials from within Congress.

evt-11-29-2012-united-nations-general-as.scenario: It is 29 November 2012 in the UN General Assembly chamber in New York. You are a delegate about to cast your vote on the Palestinian delegation's proposal to change its standing at the United Nations.
evt-11-29-2012-united-nations-general-as.prompt: What status did the resolution actually grant to Palestine?

choices.text: Full voting membership in the United Nations
A permanent seat on the Security Council
Non-member observer state status
Formal recognition as a UNESCO member state

evt-11-29-2012-united-nations-general-as.butterflyEffect: The resolution passed 138 to 9, elevating Palestine to non-member observer state status, the same tier held by the Holy See. This upgrade gave the Palestinian Authority firmer legal grounds to seek membership in bodies such as the International Criminal Court, sharpening the diplomatic standoff with Israel and the United States over Palestinian statehood in the years that followed.

evt-11-30-1700-great-northern-war.scenario: It is 30 November 1700 outside Narva, and you serve in Tsar Peter's siege lines. A blinding snowstorm sweeps in from the east, and somewhere in the whiteout, Charles XII's much smaller Swedish army is moving.
evt-11-30-1700-great-northern-war.prompt: What does the outnumbered Swedish army do under cover of the blizzard?

choices.text: They launch a surprise attack that shatters the Russian lines
They retreat across the border to regroup in Sweden
They open negotiations to surrender the siege peacefully
They wait several days for reinforcements before attacking

evt-11-30-1700-great-northern-war.butterflyEffect: Charles XII's roughly 10,000 Swedes used the storm to mask their approach and routed Peter's far larger, poorly-led army at Narva. The humiliation drove Peter to overhaul Russia's military, laying groundwork for his decisive reversal against Sweden at Poltava nine years later.

evt-11-30-1803-balmis-expedition.scenario: You are a physician aboard the Maria Pita, sailing from A Coruña with the vaccine that must survive weeks at sea to reach Spanish America before another smallpox epidemic strikes.
evt-11-30-1803-balmis-expedition.prompt: How do you keep the smallpox vaccine viable across the Atlantic crossing?

choices.text: Keep vaccine matter refrigerated in ice brought from Spain
Store dried lymph on sealed glass slides in the ship's hold
Expose sailors to smallpox patients along the route as living reservoirs
Pass it arm-to-arm through a relay of orphaned boys carried aboard the ship

evt-11-30-1803-balmis-expedition.butterflyEffect: Balmis carried the vaccine as a living chain, infecting orphan boys in relay so fresh cowpox matter was always available on arrival. The expedition vaccinated hundreds of thousands across Spanish America, the Philippines, and Macau, becoming one of history's first large-scale international public health campaigns.

evt-11-30-1853-pavel-nakhimov.scenario: You are Admiral Pavel Nakhimov, having cornered an Ottoman fleet anchored under the guns of Sinop's shore batteries. Your squadron carries new explosive shell guns rarely used in naval combat before.
evt-11-30-1853-pavel-nakhimov.prompt: How does Nakhimov destroy the anchored Ottoman fleet?

choices.text: Blockade the harbor and starve the fleet into surrender
