Withdraw and wait for reinforcements before engaging
Close to point-blank range and bombard with explosive shells
Launch a night raid using fireships

evt-11-30-1853-pavel-nakhimov.butterflyEffect: Nakhimov closed to point-blank range and unleashed explosive shells from Paixhans guns, annihilating the Ottoman fleet at anchor in hours. The scale of destruction alarmed Britain and France, who saw it as unprovoked aggression, and their subsequent intervention against Russia helped trigger the wider Crimean War.

evt-11-30-1872-1872-scotland-v-england-f.scenario: You're one of 4,000 spectators packed into Hamilton Crescent, Glasgow, watching Scotland take on England in a match organizers are calling the first official international football fixture.
evt-11-30-1872-1872-scotland-v-england-f.prompt: What was the final result of this historic match?

choices.text: A 0-0 draw
A 2-1 win for England
A 3-0 win for Scotland
A 1-0 win for Scotland

evt-11-30-1872-1872-scotland-v-england-f.butterflyEffect: The match ended scoreless, but its format set the template for future international fixtures. The Scotland-England rivalry became the world's oldest international football contest, helping establish the framework that would eventually grow into global competitions like the World Cup.

evt-11-30-1934-lner-class-a3-4472-flying.scenario: You are an LNER engineer aboard a test run near Little Bytham on November 30, 1934, watching the speedometer climb as Flying Scotsman races down a favorable stretch of track.
evt-11-30-1934-lner-class-a3-4472-flying.prompt: How do you make sure the 100 mph reading will be officially accepted as a record?

choices.text: Have trackside observers estimate speed by eye
Rely on the driver's personal stopwatch reading
Attach a dynamometer car to independently record and verify the speed
Remove carriages to lighten the train before the run

evt-11-30-1934-lner-class-a3-4472-flying.butterflyEffect: A dynamometer car coupled behind the locomotive recorded and verified the speed, making it the first authenticated 100 mph run by a steam locomotive. The feat cemented Flying Scotsman's fame and spurred LNER's pursuit of speed, culminating in sister engine Mallard's still-standing steam speed record in 1938.

evt-11-30-1936-alan-turing.scenario: You're a young Cambridge mathematician in 1936, wrestling with a deep problem in logic: can a fixed procedure ever decide whether any given mathematical statement is provable?
evt-11-30-1936-alan-turing.prompt: What abstract device did you introduce to resolve this problem?

choices.text: A mechanical calculating engine built from gears
An abstract computing device, later called the Turing machine
A code-breaking device for military ciphers
A stored-program electronic computer

evt-11-30-1936-alan-turing.butterflyEffect: Turing's paper 'On Computable Numbers' proved that some problems are fundamentally undecidable, and his abstract machine became the theoretical blueprint for all computation. It directly shaped the design of digital computers and earned Turing lasting recognition as a founder of computer science.

evt-11-30-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 30 November 1942 off Guadalcanal. You command a US Navy cruiser task force with a radar advantage, moving to intercept Japanese destroyers slipping supplies down 'The Slot.'
evt-11-30-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What happens when your ships engage Tanaka's destroyers in the darkness?

choices.text: Both forces withdraw without making contact
The Japanese destroyers surrender rather than engage
The US cruisers sink most of the Japanese destroyers
The Japanese destroyers inflict severe losses on the US cruisers

evt-11-30-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Despite being outgunned and outnumbered, Japanese destroyers under Raizo Tanaka used deadly Type 93 torpedoes to sink one US cruiser and cripple three others at the Battle of Tassafaronga. The lopsided result exposed flaws in US night-combat doctrine and forced a rethink of cruiser tactics and torpedo defense for the rest of the Pacific War.

evt-11-30-1947-united-nations-partition-.scenario: It's November 30, 1947, one day after the UN General Assembly voted to partition Mandatory Palestine into Arab and Jewish states. You hear reports of violence breaking out on the roads near Jerusalem.
evt-11-30-1947-united-nations-partition-.prompt: What happened in Palestine within a day of the UN vote?

choices.text: A joint Arab-Jewish government was formed the same day
British forces withdrew from Palestine immediately
Arab and Jewish leaders agreed to implement the plan peacefully together
Attacks on Jewish buses began, starting the civil war phase of the conflict

evt-11-30-1947-united-nations-partition-.butterflyEffect: Attacks on Jewish transport on 30 November 1947 marked the start of the civil war phase of the 1947–1949 Palestine war. The conflict escalated sharply after Israel's 1948 declaration of independence, drawing in neighboring Arab states and reshaping the political map of the Middle East for decades.

evt-11-30-1953-mutesa-ii-of-buganda.scenario: You are Kabaka Mutesa II of Buganda in 1953, facing Governor Andrew Cohen's demand that you accept constitutional changes folding your kingdom more tightly into a future unified Uganda.
evt-11-30-1953-mutesa-ii-of-buganda.prompt: What do you do when the governor threatens to withdraw recognition unless you comply?

choices.text: Appeal directly to the United Nations for intervention
Sign the reforms to preserve his throne
Refuse to cooperate and risk exile
Flee immediately to a neighboring kingdom

evt-11-30-1953-mutesa-ii-of-buganda.butterflyEffect: Mutesa refused to cooperate, and Cohen had him deposed and flown into exile in London. The crisis ignited Buganda nationalist agitation, forced his return in 1955 under a compromise agreement, and set the stage for his later, troubled tenure as Uganda's first president before his final exile in 1966.

evt-11-30-1954-sylacauga-meteorite.scenario: It's early afternoon on November 30, 1954, in Oak Grove, Alabama. You're resting on your couch when a grapefruit-sized rock tears through your roof and strikes your hip.
evt-11-30-1954-sylacauga-meteorite.prompt: What happened to the woman struck by this meteorite?

choices.text: She survived with a bruise, the first confirmed meteorite strike on a person
The meteorite missed her entirely
She suffered permanent paralysis from the impact
She was killed instantly by the impact

evt-11-30-1954-sylacauga-meteorite.butterflyEffect: Ann Hodges survived with only a large bruise, becoming the first documented person known to be struck by a meteorite. The event sparked a public legal dispute over who owned the rock—her or her landlord—and it remains one of history's only verified cases of a meteorite directly hitting a human being.

evt-11-30-1957-sukarno.scenario: It is November 30, 1957, in Jakarta. You are part of President Sukarno's security detail as he leaves his children's school, when grenades suddenly explode in the crowd around him.
evt-11-30-1957-sukarno.prompt: What lasting effect did this failed assassination attempt have on Sukarno's rule?

choices.text: It pushed Sukarno to crack down harder on political and Islamist opposition
It forced Sukarno to resign the presidency
It made him withdraw from public appearances for the rest of his presidency
It led him to open peace talks with the attackers' movement

evt-11-30-1957-sukarno.butterflyEffect: Sukarno escaped unharmed while several bystanders were killed, an attack later linked to Darul Islam rebels. The incident hardened Sukarno's resolve against his political and religious opponents, feeding into his push toward centralized 'Guided Democracy' and away from parliamentary politics within a few years.

evt-11-30-1999-1999-seattle-wto-protests.scenario: It is early morning on November 30, 1999, in downtown Seattle. Thousands of you have gathered to stop WTO delegates from reaching the Convention Center before the ministerial conference opens.
evt-11-30-1999-1999-seattle-wto-protests.prompt: What tactic do the protesters use to disrupt the opening ceremony?

choices.text: Form human blockades at intersections leading to the Convention Center
Occupy the conference floor disguised as delegates
Petition delegates individually at their hotels the night before
Stage a silent candlelight vigil outside city hall

evt-11-30-1999-1999-seattle-wto-protests.butterflyEffect: Protesters formed human blockades at key intersections, physically preventing delegates from reaching the venue and forcing the cancellation of the opening ceremony. Police responded with tear gas and rubber bullets, the mayor declared a civil emergency and curfew, and "the Battle of Seattle" became a defining symbol that reshaped anti-globalization activism worldwide.

evt-11-30-1999-exxonmobil.scenario: It is 30 November 1999 and you hold shares in Exxon as news breaks that the company has struck a deal worth tens of billions of dollars with its old rival Mobil.
evt-11-30-1999-exxonmobil.prompt: What does this agreement between Exxon and Mobil ultimately create?

choices.text: A joint venture that leaves both companies independent
A new company eventually renamed Chevron
ExxonMobil, the world's largest publicly traded oil company
A merger blocked outright by federal antitrust regulators

evt-11-30-1999-exxonmobil.butterflyEffect: The deal closed in 1999, forming ExxonMobil and reuniting two pieces of John D. Rockefeller's Standard Oil, split apart by antitrust action in 1911. Regulators forced some station divestitures, and the merger set off a wave of oil megamergers, including BP-Amoco and Chevron-Texaco.

evt-11-30-2000-sts-97.scenario: It's December 2000 and you're a spacewalking astronaut aboard Endeavour, tasked with attaching a massive new truss and solar array set to the still-small International Space Station.
evt-11-30-2000-sts-97.prompt: What did this critical spacewalk accomplish for the ISS?

choices.text: Retrieving a malfunctioning communications satellite
Testing the station's robotic arm for the very first time
Repairing a damaged thermal tile on the shuttle
Installing the first major solar arrays to power the station

evt-11-30-2000-sts-97.butterflyEffect: The newly installed P6 solar arrays gave the station its first major independent power source beyond the Russian segment. This enabled the station to support far more systems and crew, paving the way for the U.S. Destiny laboratory's arrival and continuous crewed operations in the years that followed.

evt-11-30-2007-atlasjet-flight-4203.scenario: It is just before dawn on 30 November 2007. You are in the cockpit of an MD-83 descending toward Isparta through dense fog, with hills hidden somewhere below and the runway lights nowhere in sight.
evt-11-30-2007-atlasjet-flight-4203.prompt: What should the crew do as the airport fails to appear through the fog?

choices.text: Circle at low altitude searching visually for the runway
Abort the approach and go around
Increase speed to break through the fog layer faster
Continue descending, trusting the instruments alone

evt-11-30-2007-atlasjet-flight-4203.butterflyEffect: Instead of aborting, the crew continued descending below a safe altitude and struck a hillside near Keçiborlu, killing all 57 people aboard. Investigators cited pilot error and poor decision-making in low visibility, adding pressure for wider terrain-warning technology and stricter approach discipline among Turkish carriers.

evt-11-30-2018-2018-anchorage-earthquake.scenario: It is 8:29 a.m. on November 30, 2018, and the ground beneath you in Anchorage, Alaska, suddenly lurches violently as a magnitude-7.1 earthquake strikes.
evt-11-30-2018-2018-anchorage-earthquake.prompt: What is the safest immediate action to take?

choices.text: Call 911 before taking any other action
Stand in a doorway until the shaking fully stops
Run outside immediately to escape the building
Drop to the ground, cover your head, and hold on to shelter

evt-11-30-2018-2018-anchorage-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Residents who dropped, covered, and held on avoided injury from falling debris as roads buckled and buildings cracked across the city. The quake caused widespread damage but no direct deaths, prompting Alaska to further strengthen its already strict seismic building codes.

evt-11-30-2021-barbados.scenario: It is midnight on 30 November 2021 in Bridgetown's National Heroes Square. The Royal Standard is lowered for the last time as Barbados sheds 396 years of ties to the British Crown.
evt-11-30-2021-barbados.prompt: Who is sworn in as Barbados's first president that night?

choices.text: Errol Barrow
Owen Arthur
Mia Mottley
Sandra Mason

evt-11-30-2021-barbados.butterflyEffect: Sandra Mason became Barbados's first president, and the island became a republic within the Commonwealth. Rihanna was named a National Hero the same night, and the move renewed debate across the Caribbean about other nations following suit.

evt-11-30-2021-2021-oxford-high-school-s.scenario: It is the morning of November 30, 2021, at Oxford High School in Michigan. School counselors have just met with a student and his parents after staff found a disturbing drawing at his desk.
evt-11-30-2021-2021-oxford-high-school-s.prompt: What decision do school officials make about the student?

choices.text: Suspend him immediately and search his locker
Send him back to class without searching his backpack
Call police to remove him from the building
Require the parents to take him home for the day

evt-11-30-2021-2021-oxford-high-school-s.butterflyEffect: The student was sent back to class without his backpack being searched, and he carried out the shooting hours later. His parents were subsequently convicted of involuntary manslaughter, a landmark ruling that held parents criminally responsible for failing to prevent their child's access to a gun.

evt-11-30-2022-chatgpt.scenario: You're on the OpenAI team in late November 2022, quietly launching a free chatbot as a low-key 'research preview,' unsure if it will attract any real attention.
evt-11-30-2022-chatgpt.prompt: What happened in the days immediately following ChatGPT's release?

choices.text: It required an expensive paid subscription from day one
It gained over a million users within a week
Major tech companies immediately banned it from workplaces
It attracted little interest and was quietly shelved

evt-11-30-2022-chatgpt.butterflyEffect: ChatGPT hit one million users within days, becoming the fastest-growing consumer application yet seen. The launch triggered an industry-wide AI boom, pushing Google, Microsoft, and others to race out competing chatbots and reshaping tech investment worldwide.

evt-12-01-1822-pedro-i-of-brazil.scenario: You stand among the crowd in Rio de Janeiro on 1 December 1822, weeks after Pedro declared Brazil's independence from Portugal at Ipiranga. Today he is being crowned in a grand ceremony.
evt-12-01-1822-pedro-i-of-brazil.prompt: What title is Pedro crowned with?

choices.text: Emperor of Brazil
King of Portugal and Brazil jointly
King of Brazil
President of the Brazilian Republic

evt-12-01-1822-pedro-i-of-brazil.butterflyEffect: Pedro was crowned Emperor of Brazil, establishing the country as a constitutional monarchy rather than a republic or a Portuguese colony. He would go on to briefly inherit the Portuguese throne in 1826, before Brazil's empire endured under his successors until the monarchy fell in 1889.

evt-12-01-1828-cisplatine-war.scenario: You march into Buenos Aires in late 1828 with the troops who fought Brazil over the Banda Oriental. The war has dragged on for years, draining both sides, and diplomats have been negotiating a settlement.
evt-12-01-1828-cisplatine-war.prompt: What outcome awaits the disputed Banda Oriental?

choices.text: The war continues without a settlement
It is formally annexed by the United Provinces
It remains a Brazilian province
It becomes the independent Oriental Republic of Uruguay

evt-12-01-1828-cisplatine-war.butterflyEffect: Under British mediation, the Treaty of Montevideo created the Banda Oriental as an independent buffer state, the Oriental Republic of Uruguay, rather than letting either Argentina or Brazil control it. Uruguay's independence, however, left it a fragile state contested by both powerful neighbors for decades afterward.

evt-12-01-1918-danish-icelandic-act-of-u.scenario: It is December 1, 1918, and you are an Icelandic negotiator signing the new Act of Union with Denmark, defining Iceland's status after centuries under the Danish crown.
evt-12-01-1918-danish-icelandic-act-of-u.prompt: What status does the Act actually grant Iceland?

choices.text: Continued status as a Danish colony
A fully sovereign kingdom in personal union with the Danish king
Union with Norway under a shared parliament
Complete independence with no ties to Denmark

evt-12-01-1918-danish-icelandic-act-of-u.butterflyEffect: Iceland became a fully sovereign kingdom joined to Denmark only through a shared monarch, while asking Denmark to handle its foreign affairs and defense. The agreement included a clause allowing revision after 1940, and Iceland used the chaos of the Danish occupation in World War II to declare full independence and become a republic in 1944.

evt-12-01-1923-gleno-dam.scenario: It is 1916 and you are a government engineer reviewing plans for a new dam above the Valle di Scalve. The approved design calls for a solid gravity dam, but you learn the contractor has quietly begun building a lighter multiple-arch structure with inferior rubble masonry to save time and money.
evt-12-01-1923-gleno-dam.prompt: As the inspector, what should you do?

choices.text: Approve the cheaper design without further review to save the contractor money
Report it only after construction is finished
Halt construction and demand the original approved design and materials be used
Ignore the change since the dam is far from any village

evt-12-01-1923-gleno-dam.butterflyEffect: The unauthorized change and shoddy materials went unchecked. The Gleno Dam's central section collapsed on 1 December 1923, just forty days after the reservoir was filled, sending a flood through the valley that killed at least 356 people. The disaster led to the builder's prosecution and tightened Italian dam-safety oversight.

evt-12-01-1934-sergei-kirov.scenario: It is 1 December 1934 at the Smolny Institute in Leningrad. You are a Communist Party official who has just learned that Sergei Kirov, Stalin's popular ally and head of the Leningrad party, has been shot dead in the corridor by a lone gunman.
evt-12-01-1934-sergei-kirov.prompt: What follows Kirov's assassination inside the Soviet leadership?

choices.text: Stalin uses the killing to justify mass arrests and show trials against alleged conspirators
The Politburo quietly investigates and finds no political significance to the murder
Kirov's death leads to an immediate loosening of internal party discipline
The assassin is publicly pardoned as mentally unfit and the case is closed

evt-12-01-1934-sergei-kirov.butterflyEffect: Stalin used Kirov's murder as the pretext to launch sweeping purges of the party, accusing rivals of conspiracy. The killing helped trigger the Great Terror of the late 1930s, and the guard who had been assigned to protect Kirov died in a suspicious accident before he could be questioned.

evt-12-01-1941-civil-air-patrol.scenario: It is 1 December 1941, days before Pearl Harbor, and you are a licensed civilian pilot in the United States deciding whether to join the newly chartered Civil Air Patrol, a volunteer force meant to put private aviation to use for home defense.
evt-12-01-1941-civil-air-patrol.prompt: What kind of wartime service will CAP volunteers actually perform?

choices.text: Train as combat pilots for immediate deployment overseas
Serve exclusively as ground crew mechanics on military airbases
Focus solely on delivering mail between domestic military installations
Fly coastal patrols in private aircraft to spot enemy submarines along U.S. shores

evt-12-01-1941-civil-air-patrol.butterflyEffect: CAP pilots flew unarmed civilian planes on coastal antisubmarine patrols, spotting German U-boats and even helping sink two of them, along with towing targets and ferrying aircraft for the military. The organization's wartime record secured its lasting role as the official civilian auxiliary of the U.S. Air Force.

evt-12-01-1948-somerton-man.scenario: It is 1 December 1948, and you are the detective called to Somerton Park beach in Adelaide, where a well-dressed man lies dead with no wallet, no ID, and every clothing label carefully cut away.
evt-12-01-1948-somerton-man.prompt: What is your best lead for identifying him?

choices.text: Publish his photo and wait for the public to respond before investigating further
Assume he is a foreign sailor and contact shipping lines only
Cremate the body immediately since no family has come forward
Check railway and hotel cloakrooms for a matching unclaimed suitcase

evt-12-01-1948-somerton-man.butterflyEffect: Police traced a brown suitcase checked into the Adelaide railway station cloakroom that matched his belongings, but its contents offered no name either. The case stayed unsolved for over 70 years until 2022, when DNA from exhumed remains finally identified him as Carl 'Charles' Webb, an engineer from Melbourne.

evt-12-01-1955-rosa-parks.scenario: It is December 1, 1955, on a Montgomery city bus. You are seated in the section reserved for Black passengers, but the driver orders you to give up your seat to a white rider.

choices.text: Refuse to move and stay in your seat
Quietly move to the back of the bus
Offer to switch seats with another passenger
Get off the bus without argument

evt-12-01-1955-rosa-parks.butterflyEffect: Rosa Parks refused to move and was arrested, an act that local NAACP leaders used to launch the Montgomery Bus Boycott. The 381-day boycott, organized in part by a young Martin Luther King Jr., ended with the Supreme Court's Browder v. Gayle ruling declaring bus segregation unconstitutional.

evt-12-01-1959-antarctic-treaty-system.scenario: It is 1 December 1959 in Washington, D.C. Delegates from twelve nations, several of which have made competing territorial claims to Antarctica, are about to sign a treaty governing the continent's future.
evt-12-01-1959-antarctic-treaty-system.prompt: What compromise allowed all twelve nations to sign the Antarctic Treaty?

choices.text: They agreed to set aside territorial claims without settling or dividing them
They agreed to divide the continent equally among the signatories
They permitted mining rights in exchange for dropping claims
They allowed military bases as long as they were unarmed

evt-12-01-1959-antarctic-treaty-system.butterflyEffect: The treaty froze existing territorial claims without requiring any nation to renounce or recognize them, while banning military activity and nuclear testing and guaranteeing freedom of scientific research. This became the first Cold War arms-control agreement and a model later echoed in the Outer Space Treaty, keeping Antarctica demilitarized and dedicated to science ever since.

evt-12-01-1966-gavle-goat.scenario: It is early December 1966 in Gävle, Sweden. Local businessmen have just erected a giant straw Yule goat in the central square, a novelty meant to draw shoppers downtown for the holidays.
evt-12-01-1966-gavle-goat.prompt: What happened to this very first Gävle Goat before the new year arrived?

choices.text: It was quietly dismantled after the holidays as planned
It collapsed in a winter storm
It was burned down by vandals
It was stolen and never recovered

evt-12-01-1966-gavle-goat.butterflyEffect: Vandals set the goat ablaze on New Year's Eve, destroying it within its first season. The arson became an annual tradition of its own, with the goat torched or attacked most years since despite escalating security measures, turning it into a global media spectacle and one of Sweden's best-known Christmas symbols.

evt-12-01-1971-croatian-spring.scenario: It is late 1971 and you are a reform-minded official in the League of Communists of Croatia. Josip Broz Tito has summoned Croatian leaders to Karađorđevo, unhappy with the growing push for economic and political liberalization tied to Matica hrvatska.
evt-12-01-1971-croatian-spring.prompt: What actually followed Tito's crackdown on the Croatian Spring?

choices.text: Croatia was granted full independence from Yugoslavia
The reformist leaders were purged from power
Yugoslavia adopted a fully free-market economy nationwide
Tito resigned in favor of a Croatian successor

evt-12-01-1971-croatian-spring.butterflyEffect: Tito purged the reformist leadership, including Savka Dabčević-Kučar and Miko Tripalo, replacing them with conservatives loyal to central authority. Yet some decentralizing reforms survived in the 1974 Yugoslav constitution, which granted republics greater autonomy—an arrangement that later fed the nationalist tensions of the 1990s breakup.

evt-12-01-1991-1991-ukrainian-independen.scenario: It is 1 December 1991 and you stand in a queue outside a Kyiv polling station. The Verkhovna Rada declared independence back in August, after the failed Moscow coup, and now the decision is yours to ratify.
evt-12-01-1991-1991-ukrainian-independen.prompt: What do you mark on the ballot?

choices.text: Abstain and wait for a new union treaty
Vote for autonomy within a reformed Soviet federation
Vote no to remain part of the USSR
Vote yes to ratify Ukraine's independence

evt-12-01-1991-1991-ukrainian-independen.butterflyEffect: Over 92% of voters approved independence. Days later, on 25 December 1991, the Soviet Union was formally dissolved, with Ukraine's vote a decisive factor in convincing Russia's leadership that the union could not survive.

evt-12-01-2005-perm-oblast.scenario: It is October 2004 and you are voting in a referendum that will decide whether Perm Oblast merges with the neighboring Komi-Permyak Autonomous Okrug into a single new region.
evt-12-01-2005-perm-oblast.prompt: How do you cast your vote on the merger?

choices.text: Vote no to keep the regions separate
Vote yes, merging into a new Perm Krai
Boycott the vote entirely
Push for the okrug to become fully independent

evt-12-01-2005-perm-oblast.butterflyEffect: Voters approved the merger, and Perm Krai officially came into existence on 1 December 2005. It became the first of several Putin-era mergers of federal subjects, a template later followed by other Russian regions consolidating their autonomous okrugs.

evt-12-01-2011-almaty-metro.scenario: It is December 1, 2011, and you finally board the first train of the Almaty Metro, a project first begun back in 1988 during the Soviet era.
evt-12-01-2011-almaty-metro.prompt: What caused the decades-long delay between the project's start and this opening day?

choices.text: The Soviet collapse cut off funding and stalled construction for years
The government redirected the project to Astana instead
An earthquake destroyed the completed tunnels
Local officials opposed having a metro at all

evt-12-01-2011-almaty-metro.butterflyEffect: The collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991 cut off funding and halted construction for years, leaving the half-built tunnels dormant through the 1990s. When the line finally opened in 2011, it became Kazakhstan's only metro system for over a decade, until Astana's own light metro opened in 2026.

evt-12-01-2019-vivianne-miedema.scenario: You are on the Arsenal Women's bench watching Vivianne Miedema tear apart the opposition defense on 1 December 2019, goal after goal piling up in a lopsided WSL fixture.
evt-12-01-2019-vivianne-miedema.prompt: What milestone does Miedema's six-goal display set?

choices.text: The most goals by one player in a WSL match
The first WSL player to score in every match of a season
The most assists by one player in WSL history
The fastest hat-trick in FA Cup history

evt-12-01-2019-vivianne-miedema.butterflyEffect: Miedema's six goals set a new record for the most goals scored by a single player in a Women's Super League match. The performance underlined her status as one of the league's most prolific strikers and helped fuel growing media attention on the women's game.

evt-12-01-2019-covid-19-pandemic.scenario: It is early December 2019, and you are a doctor in Wuhan, China, seeing several patients with an unusual pneumonia that isn't responding to normal treatment. Something about the pattern of illness worries you.
evt-12-01-2019-covid-19-pandemic.prompt: What should you do about these unexplained pneumonia cases?

choices.text: Wait for instructions from Beijing before taking any action
Warn fellow doctors privately and report the cluster up the chain regardless of pressure to stay quiet
Quietly discharge the patients to avoid drawing attention to the hospital
Treat the cases as an isolated local flu outbreak and say nothing further

evt-12-01-2019-covid-19-pandemic.butterflyEffect: Doctors including Li Wenliang tried to warn colleagues about the new illness and were reprimanded by local authorities for 'spreading rumors.' The delay in open reporting slowed the global response, and Li Wenliang himself died of the virus in February 2020, becoming a symbol of the pandemic's early cover-up.

evt-12-01-2020-arecibo-telescope.scenario: It is late 2020, and you are an engineer at the Arecibo Observatory. Cables supporting the massive receiver platform have already snapped twice, and the structure is now dangerously unstable.
evt-12-01-2020-arecibo-telescope.prompt: What does the National Science Foundation ultimately decide to do with the damaged telescope?

choices.text: Decommission the telescope rather than risk repairing it
Sell the observatory to a foreign space agency
Fund an emergency rebuild of all the support cables
Convert it immediately into a museum while still standing

evt-12-01-2020-arecibo-telescope.butterflyEffect: Engineers judged the structure too dangerous to repair safely, and the NSF announced plans to decommission it. Before any controlled demolition could take place, the remaining cables gave way and the platform crashed into the dish on December 1, 2020, ending 57 years of research that had included the Arecibo message and major pulsar discoveries.

evt-12-02-1805-battle-of-austerlitz.scenario: It is dawn on 2 December 1805 near Austerlitz. You serve under Napoleon, who has deliberately abandoned the dominant Pratzen Heights to lure the Russo-Austrian army into a trap, and now their forces are massing to seize it.
evt-12-02-1805-battle-of-austerlitz.prompt: What move does Napoleon order as the Allies commit to the heights?

choices.text: Hold a purely defensive line and wait for reinforcements
Order a full retreat toward Vienna
Counterattack to retake the Pratzen Heights and split the Allied army
Open immediate peace negotiations with the Tsar

evt-12-02-1805-battle-of-austerlitz.butterflyEffect: French troops surged back onto the Pratzen Heights, splitting the Allied army and routing it decisively. The victory ended the War of the Third Coalition, forced the Peace of Pressburg, and within a year contributed to the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire as Napoleon reshaped Central Europe.

evt-12-02-1823-james-monroe.scenario: It is December 1823. You are advising President Monroe as he prepares his annual message to Congress, worried that European powers restoring absolute monarchies might try to reclaim newly independent Latin American nations.
evt-12-02-1823-james-monroe.prompt: What does Monroe declare regarding European powers and the Americas?

choices.text: He calls for the annexation of the new Latin American republics
He warns Europe against colonizing or intervening in the Americas
He proposes a formal alliance with the European Holy Alliance
He asks Congress to declare war on Spain over its colonies

evt-12-02-1823-james-monroe.butterflyEffect: Monroe warned Europe against further colonization or intervention in the Western Hemisphere, threatening to treat such moves as hostile to the United States. Though weakly enforceable at the time, the Monroe Doctrine became a foundation of American foreign policy, later expanded by the Roosevelt Corollary to justify U.S. intervention across Latin America for a century.

evt-12-02-1899-philippine-american-war.scenario: It is December 2, 1899, at Tirad Pass in the Cordillera mountains. You command a mere sixty Filipino soldiers holding a narrow trail, buying time for President Aguinaldo's main force to escape advancing American troops below.
evt-12-02-1899-philippine-american-war.prompt: What happens to the rearguard holding the pass?

choices.text: They surrender the pass without resistance
They fight to the death, delaying the Americans and letting Aguinaldo flee
They retreat before any fighting begins
They repel the American force and hold the pass

evt-12-02-1899-philippine-american-war.butterflyEffect: General Gregorio del Pilar and nearly all his men were killed after fierce fighting, but their stand delayed the American column long enough for Aguinaldo to escape capture. The action, later dubbed the "Philippine Thermopylae," made del Pilar a lasting symbol of nationalist sacrifice in Philippine memory.

evt-12-02-1927-ford-motor-company.scenario: It is December 2, 1927. You run a Ford dealership whose showroom has sat nearly empty for months since the Model T stopped rolling off the line. Today, the long-secret successor finally goes on public display.
evt-12-02-1927-ford-motor-company.prompt: What happens when Ford unveils the new Model A to the public?

choices.text: Massive crowds flood dealerships nationwide just to see it
Sales are disappointing and dealers are left with unsold stock
Chevrolet forces Ford to slash prices before a single unit sells
Federal regulators order an immediate recall over safety flaws

evt-12-02-1927-ford-motor-company.butterflyEffect: Curiosity was so intense that an estimated 10 million people viewed the Model A in dealerships on its first day, temporarily restoring Ford's dominance after the aging Model T. The advantage was short-lived, though: within a few years Chevrolet's more modern engineering pulled ahead in sales.

evt-12-02-1942-chicago-pile-1.scenario: You are a physicist crouched in the squash court beneath Stagg Field's stands on 2 December 1942, watching neutron counters climb as George Weil slowly withdraws the last control rod from Fermi's uranium-graphite pile.
evt-12-02-1942-chicago-pile-1.prompt: What does Fermi's team do once the pile goes critical and sustains itself?

choices.text: Let it run indefinitely to study long-term behavior
Evacuate the building immediately without further testing
Add more uranium to push power output as high as possible
Let it run briefly to confirm the chain reaction, then deliberately shut it down

evt-12-02-1942-chicago-pile-1.butterflyEffect: Fermi let the pile run for about 28 minutes at roughly half a watt, then ordered the control rods reinserted to shut it down safely, proving a controlled chain reaction was possible. The achievement launched the Manhattan Project's plutonium-production effort at Hanford, directly enabling the bomb dropped on Nagasaki less than three years later.

evt-12-02-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 2 December 1943 in the harbor of Bari, Italy. German bombers strike without warning, sinking Allied ships including one secretly loaded with chemical weapons. You are treating sailors pulled from the oily water, but the ship's true cargo is being kept classified.
evt-12-02-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What does Allied command do as casualties show unexplained chemical burns?

choices.text: Order full evacuation and destruction of the gas stockpile
Immediately airlift victims to specialized chemical warfare units
Keep the presence of mustard gas classified, delaying proper treatment
Publicly disclose the mustard gas cargo to guide treatment

evt-12-02-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The SS John Harvey had secretly carried mustard gas bombs, and wartime secrecy meant doctors misdiagnosed the burns and blindness, worsening many casualties. American physician Stewart Alexander eventually identified the exposure, and his clinical observations on mustard's effect on white blood cells later helped inspire the development of nitrogen mustard chemotherapy, an early foundation of cancer treatment.

evt-12-02-1950-korean-war.scenario: You serve with the US Eighth Army in North Korea in early December 1950. Massive Chinese forces have just shattered friendly lines along the Ch'ongch'on River, threatening to cut off your entire unit.
evt-12-02-1950-korean-war.prompt: What order comes down from command?

choices.text: Retreat southward to avoid encirclement
Negotiate a local surrender to Chinese forces
Dig in and hold current positions at all costs
Push further north toward the Yalu River as planned

evt-12-02-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: Eighth Army was forced into a headlong retreat southward, eventually stabilizing near the 38th parallel. It became the longest retreat in US military history and locked the war into a grinding stalemate that lasted until the 1953 armistice.

evt-12-02-1954-united-states-senate.scenario: It is December 2, 1954. You are a senator on the floor as colleagues vote on a resolution condemning Joseph McCarthy's conduct, months after his combative, televised clash with the Army damaged his standing.
evt-12-02-1954-united-states-senate.prompt: How does the Senate vote on the resolution against McCarthy?

choices.text: The Senate acquits him by a wide margin
The Senate instead votes to expel him outright
The vote is tied and sent back to committee
The Senate votes 67 to 22 to condemn him

evt-12-02-1954-united-states-senate.butterflyEffect: The Senate approved the censure 67 to 22, formally condemning McCarthy's behavior toward colleagues and committees. The vote broke his grip on national politics almost overnight, and though he kept his seat until his death in 1957, his influence and the broader fever of McCarthyism rapidly faded.

evt-12-02-1956-cuban-revolution.scenario: It is December 2, 1956. You are aboard the overcrowded yacht Granma as it runs aground in a mangrove swamp near Playa Las Coloradas, two days behind schedule and far from the planned landing site.
evt-12-02-1956-cuban-revolution.prompt: What happens to Castro's rebel force in the days after this botched landing?

choices.text: They are captured en masse and imprisoned
They march triumphantly into Santiago unopposed
Batista's army ambushes and scatters them, leaving only a handful of survivors
They immediately link up with urban resistance cells

evt-12-02-1956-cuban-revolution.butterflyEffect: Alerted by the delay, Batista's army ambushed the rebels days later at Alegría de Pío, killing or capturing most of them. Fidel and Raúl Castro, Che Guevara, and only a handful of others escaped into the Sierra Maestra mountains, where they rebuilt the guerrilla movement that eventually overthrew Batista in 1959.

evt-12-02-1988-benazir-bhutto.scenario: It is December 2, 1988. You are Benazir Bhutto, taking the oath as Pakistan's first female prime minister after years of exile and imprisonment, aware that the presidency and military still hold sweeping constitutional powers.
evt-12-02-1988-benazir-bhutto.prompt: What real constraint limits her authority as she takes office?

choices.text: The president can dismiss her government under the Eighth Amendment
The military is fully removed from political affairs
The presidency is immediately abolished upon her inauguration
She holds unchecked authority with no presidential oversight

evt-12-02-1988-benazir-bhutto.butterflyEffect: Under the Eighth Amendment, President Ghulam Ishaq Khan retained the power to dismiss an elected government, and the military kept firm control over defense and foreign policy. That very power was used against her in 1990 when Ishaq Khan dismissed her government, though she returned to office in 1993.

evt-12-02-1989-malayan-communist-party.scenario: It is December 2, 1989, in Hat Yai, Thailand. You are a Malayan Communist Party negotiator after four decades of guerrilla insurgency, weighing whether to sign a peace accord with the Malaysian government.
evt-12-02-1989-malayan-communist-party.prompt: What does the peace accord actually require of the guerrillas?

choices.text: The MCP merges directly into the Malaysian armed forces
The MCP is recognized as an official political party in Malaysia
The insurgency continues but moves openly into Thailand
Fighters disarm and disband in exchange for amnesty and resettlement

evt-12-02-1989-malayan-communist-party.butterflyEffect: The Hat Yai Accords required MCP fighters to lay down their arms in exchange for amnesty and resettlement, ending one of Asia's longest-running communist insurgencies. Former guerrillas were resettled in "peace villages" along the Thai-Malaysian border, closing a chapter of Cold War conflict in Southeast Asia.

evt-12-02-1992-space-shuttle-discovery.scenario: It is December 2, 1992. You are a flight controller in Houston working the final Space Shuttle mission flown solely for the Department of Defense. Discovery's payload bay doors are about to open for a classified deployment, and mission communications are set to restricted mode.
evt-12-02-1992-space-shuttle-discovery.prompt: What do you do to protect operational security during the classified deployment?

choices.text: Cancel the deployment and abort the mission
Switch to encrypted, non-public communications during the classified operation
Broadcast live video of the satellite to the press
Continue normal public NASA commentary throughout the deployment

evt-12-02-1992-space-shuttle-discovery.butterflyEffect: Discovery deployed a classified payload believed to be part of the Satellite Data System, and STS-53 was the last shuttle flight flown exclusively for the Pentagon. After this, dedicated military shuttle missions ended, with the Air Force shifting toward expendable rockets for sensitive payloads while later shuttle flights carried mixed civilian and defense cargo.

evt-12-02-1993-colombia.scenario: It's 2 December 1993, and you're a Colombian National Police Search Bloc officer in Medellín's Los Olivos neighborhood, tracing a radio transmission to a rooftop where Pablo Escobar has been hiding since his escape from La Catedral prison.
evt-12-02-1993-colombia.prompt: What happens when the Search Bloc closes in on the rooftop?

choices.text: Escobar and a bodyguard are shot dead attempting to flee across the rooftops
Escobar escapes and disappears into hiding again
Escobar is captured alive and extradited to the United States
Escobar surrenders peacefully to negotiators

evt-12-02-1993-colombia.butterflyEffect: Escobar and a bodyguard were shot dead trying to flee across adjoining rooftops, ending a sixteen-month manhunt aided by US and Colombian forces. His death fractured the Medellín Cartel's dominance, opening the way for the Cali Cartel and later Mexican trafficking organizations to take over cocaine routes into the United States.

evt-12-02-1993-space-shuttle-program.scenario: It is December 2, 1993. You are part of the STS-61 crew aboard Space Shuttle Endeavour, preparing for the most complex series of spacewalks yet attempted, to fix the flawed vision of the Hubble Space Telescope.
evt-12-02-1993-space-shuttle-program.prompt: What corrective device do the astronauts install to fix Hubble's blurred images?

choices.text: A backup solar array
The COSTAR corrective optics package
A brand-new primary mirror
An external sunshade

evt-12-02-1993-space-shuttle-program.butterflyEffect: Over five spacewalks the crew installed COSTAR and new solar arrays, correcting the spherical aberration in Hubble's mirror and restoring the telescope to full scientific power. The daring repair proved astronauts could service orbiting observatories, and Hubble went on to produce decades of landmark astronomical discoveries.

evt-12-02-1999-northern-ireland.scenario: It's 2 December 1999 in Belfast, and you're a civil servant overseeing the formal handover of powers from Westminster to the newly formed Northern Ireland Executive under the Good Friday Agreement.
evt-12-02-1999-northern-ireland.prompt: What governing structure is established to share power between unionists and nationalists?

choices.text: Continuation of direct rule from Westminster
A single directly-elected leader with no assembly
A mandatory coalition Executive with a First Minister and deputy First Minister sharing power
Merger of Northern Ireland's governance into the Republic of Ireland's parliament

evt-12-02-1999-northern-ireland.butterflyEffect: A mandatory coalition took office with David Trimble as First Minister and Seamus Mallon as deputy First Minister, putting the Good Friday Agreement into practice. The Executive was suspended several times in the following years over disputes about IRA decommissioning, but the power-sharing framework created that day remains the basis of Northern Ireland's government.

evt-12-02-2001-enron-scandal.scenario: You are an Enron employee on December 2, 2001, watching your retirement savings evaporate as the company you believed was an unshakeable energy giant suddenly collapses.
evt-12-02-2001-enron-scandal.prompt: What does Enron do this day?

choices.text: Files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection
Merges with rival Dynegy to survive
Is nationalized by the federal government
Receives an emergency bailout from Congress

evt-12-02-2001-enron-scandal.butterflyEffect: Enron filed the largest corporate bankruptcy in US history to that point, revealing massive accounting fraud hidden by executives and auditors. The scandal destroyed accounting firm Arthur Andersen and led directly to the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, reshaping corporate financial oversight nationwide.

evt-12-02-2001-enron.scenario: It is December 2, 2001. You are an Enron employee watching your retirement savings, heavily invested in company stock, evaporate as the energy giant files for Chapter 11 amid revelations of hidden debt and accounting fraud.
evt-12-02-2001-enron.prompt: What does the Enron collapse trigger in Washington the following year?

choices.text: Passage of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act tightening corporate accounting oversight
Creation of the Securities and Exchange Commission
The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform Act
Repeal of the Glass-Steagall Act

evt-12-02-2001-enron.butterflyEffect: Enron's collapse, then the largest bankruptcy in US history, exposed massive accounting fraud and destroyed its auditor, Arthur Andersen. Congress responded in 2002 with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, imposing strict new financial reporting and corporate governance rules that reshaped American corporate auditing for decades.

evt-12-02-2015-san-bernardino-california.scenario: It's 2 December 2015, and you're a county employee at a holiday luncheon at the Inland Regional Center when a co-worker and his wife open fire on the gathering before fleeing in an SUV.
evt-12-02-2015-san-bernardino-california.prompt: What contentious legal fight followed as investigators sought evidence from the attack?

choices.text: The FBI and Apple clashed over unlocking the shooter's encrypted iPhone
Congress passed a new nationwide assault weapons ban
A new domestic terrorism statute was enacted immediately
The gun show loophole was closed by federal law

evt-12-02-2015-san-bernardino-california.butterflyEffect: The FBI demanded Apple build software to bypass the encryption on the shooter's iPhone, and Apple refused, igniting a national debate over privacy versus security that reached federal court before the FBI paid a third party to unlock the phone independently. The standoff reshaped public and corporate attitudes toward government access to encrypted devices.

evt-12-02-2016-ghost-ship-warehouse-fire.scenario: It's the night of 2 December 1916... wait, 2016, and you're at a packed electronic music show inside an Oakland warehouse converted into an artist collective, its narrow stairwells cluttered with wood, pianos, and RVs when fire breaks out.
evt-12-02-2016-ghost-ship-warehouse-fire.prompt: What was the wider consequence for illegal live/work warehouse spaces after this fire?

choices.text: DIY warehouse venues disappeared entirely across the country
No changes were made to fire codes anywhere
Cities nationwide launched inspections and crackdowns on illegal DIY venues
Only Oakland altered its building codes

evt-12-02-2016-ghost-ship-warehouse-fire.butterflyEffect: The Ghost Ship fire, the deadliest in Oakland's history, triggered inspections and crackdowns on unpermitted live/work and event spaces in cities across the country. It also sparked a fierce debate over balancing fire safety enforcement against the loss of affordable studio space for artists.

evt-12-02-2020-cannabis-drug.scenario: It is December 2, 2020, in Vienna. You are a delegate to the UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs, casting a vote on a World Health Organization recommendation about how cannabis should be classified under international drug treaties.
evt-12-02-2020-cannabis-drug.prompt: How do you vote on reclassifying cannabis under the 1961 Single Convention?

choices.text: Vote to keep cannabis in Schedule IV unchanged
Vote to move cannabis to Schedule III
Vote to remove cannabis from Schedule IV while keeping it in Schedule I
Vote to remove cannabis from all international scheduling entirely

evt-12-02-2020-cannabis-drug.butterflyEffect: The Commission voted 27–25 to remove cannabis and cannabis resin from Schedule IV, the most restrictive category reserved for drugs deemed to have no therapeutic value, while keeping it under Schedule I control. The move formally recognized cannabis's medical potential and gave momentum to countries expanding medical cannabis programs, though recreational use remained internationally restricted.

evt-12-03-1800-war-of-the-second-coaliti.scenario: It is 3 December 1800, and you march with General Moreau's French army through the snow-choked forest of Hohenlinden in Bavaria, converging columns against Archduke John's Austrian force.
evt-12-03-1800-war-of-the-second-coaliti.prompt: What tactic does Moreau use to break the Austrian army in the forest?

choices.text: A prolonged siege starves out a fortified town
Converging columns encircle and crush the Austrian center in the woods
Cavalry charges straight down an open plain at dawn
A naval bombardment clears the way for an amphibious landing

evt-12-03-1800-war-of-the-second-coaliti.butterflyEffect: The French victory at Hohenlinden shattered Austrian resistance and forced Vienna to seek terms, leading to the Treaty of Lunéville in 1801. That treaty effectively dissolved the Second Coalition, confirmed French dominance on the continent, and strengthened Napoleon's grip on power as First Consul.

evt-12-03-1910-freda-du-faur.scenario: It is early morning on 3 December 1910, high on the slopes of Aoraki / Mount Cook. You are guiding Freda Du Faur, an Australian climber determined to become the first woman to reach the summit, and the weather could turn at any hour.
evt-12-03-1910-freda-du-faur.prompt: What should the guiding party do about the summit attempt given the conditions?

choices.text: Turn back immediately and wait for a clearer day
Wait several days for a larger party to join them
Push on toward the summit while conditions still allowed it
Send Du Faur back and have the guides climb alone

evt-12-03-1910-freda-du-faur.butterflyEffect: Du Faur and her guides pushed on and reached the summit that day, making her the first woman to climb New Zealand's highest peak. The feat launched her career as a leading mountaineer, and she went on to complete New Zealand's first Grand Traverse of Mount Cook's three peaks in a single climb.

evt-12-03-1927-putting-pants-on-philip.scenario: You are directing a new Hal Roach comedy short in 1927, pairing British dandy Stan Laurel as a kilted Scotsman with Oliver Hardy as his mortified uncle sent to meet him at the pier.
evt-12-03-1927-putting-pants-on-philip.prompt: What running gag do you build the film's comedy around?

choices.text: Wind keeps lifting the kilt, scandalizing onlookers who gather to peer underneath
A ladder mishap traps both men on a rooftop for the whole film
The pair keep mistaking each other's hats in a crowded train station
A runaway pie cart chases the two men through the streets

evt-12-03-1927-putting-pants-on-philip.butterflyEffect: The finished short, built on gusts of wind lifting Laurel's kilt to shock passersby, is later identified by historians as Laurel and Hardy's first "official" film as a team. Hal Roach Studios began deliberately pairing them afterward, launching a partnership of over 100 films and defining a template for double-act slapstick comedy for decades.

evt-12-03-1959-flag-of-singapore.scenario: It's 1959, and you sit on the committee led by Toh Chin Chye tasked with designing a flag for newly self-governing Singapore.
evt-12-03-1959-flag-of-singapore.prompt: What symbol do you choose to represent the young nation's ideals?

choices.text: A golden lion's head on a blue field
A crescent moon and five stars on red and white
A single large white star on solid red
A British Union Jack retained in the canton

evt-12-03-1959-flag-of-singapore.butterflyEffect: The committee's design — red and white for brotherhood and purity, a crescent for a rising nation, five stars for democracy, peace, progress, justice and equality — survived Singapore's short union with Malaysia. It remains the national flag today, its symbolism recited in the national pledge.

evt-12-03-1967-cardiothoracic-surgery.scenario: You are part of Christiaan Barnard's surgical team in Cape Town on 3 December 1967, about to attempt the first human-to-human heart transplant on patient Louis Washkansky.
evt-12-03-1967-cardiothoracic-surgery.prompt: What critical step must the team take after the new heart is in place?

choices.text: Keep the patient in a hyperbaric oxygen chamber for a month
Administer immunosuppressive drugs to prevent the body rejecting the new heart
Withhold all medication to let the immune system adapt naturally
Perform a second transplant immediately as a backup

evt-12-03-1967-cardiothoracic-surgery.butterflyEffect: Washkansky survived eighteen days before dying of pneumonia brought on by the immunosuppressive drugs meant to stop rejection. Despite this, Barnard's operation proved heart transplantation was surgically possible, opening the door to the transplant programs and improved anti-rejection therapies that make the procedure routine today.

evt-12-03-1968-elvis-presley.scenario: It is December 1968, and NBC wants Elvis Presley to close his TV special with a saccharine Christmas medley to reassure sponsors. Director Steve Binder is pushing you, as his producer, to fight for something riskier.
evt-12-03-1968-elvis-presley.prompt: What format should the show use to relaunch Elvis's stalled career?

choices.text: Lip-synced footage of his 1950s film roles
A full hour of newly recorded Christmas carols
A silent instrumental set with no vocals at all
A stripped-down, live sit-down performance in leather before a small audience

evt-12-03-1968-elvis-presley.butterflyEffect: Elvis performed sitting on a small stage in black leather, surrounded by fans, doing raw, live versions of his early hits. The '68 Comeback Special reignited his career, leading directly to his Las Vegas residency and a string of hit records through the early 1970s.

evt-12-03-1971-pakistan-air-force.scenario: You are a Pakistani Air Force pilot on 3 December 1971, scrambling into the cockpit for a surprise strike against Indian airbases meant to cripple the Indian Air Force before it can respond.
evt-12-03-1971-pakistan-air-force.prompt: What followed Pakistan's pre-emptive air strikes that day?

choices.text: India declared war, and the conflict ended in Pakistan's swift defeat in the east and Bangladesh's independence
Both nations agreed to an immediate ceasefire brokered by the UN
India retaliated only with economic sanctions, avoiding direct combat
Pakistan's air force destroyed India's entire bomber fleet within hours

evt-12-03-1971-pakistan-air-force.butterflyEffect: The strikes failed to seriously damage Indian air power, and India responded by declaring full-scale war. Within thirteen days, Indian forces overwhelmed Pakistani positions in the east, leading to Pakistan's surrender in Dhaka and the birth of independent Bangladesh.

evt-12-03-1976-reggae.scenario: It is 3 December 1976, two days before the Smile Jamaica concert. Gunmen have just shot Bob Marley, his wife, and his manager at his Kingston home amid bitter political rivalry between Jamaica's two main parties.
evt-12-03-1976-reggae.prompt: What should Marley do about the upcoming Smile Jamaica concert?

choices.text: Cancel the concert and go into hiding indefinitely
Hold a press conference naming the political party responsible
Flee the country immediately without playing
Perform as planned to defy the attackers

evt-12-03-1976-reggae.butterflyEffect: Wounded but defiant, Marley performed at Smile Jamaica two days later before fleeing Jamaica for over a year, settling in London. In exile he recorded the album Exodus, which became a landmark of his international career.

evt-12-03-1979-1979-iranian-constitution.scenario: It is 2 December 1979 in Tehran. The Shah is gone, American hostages are held nearby at the embassy, and you are handed a ballot on a new Islamic constitution replacing the old order.
evt-12-03-1979-1979-iranian-constitution.prompt: What core institution did the new constitution establish that reshaped Iranian politics?

choices.text: A secular parliamentary republic with no clerical oversight
A constitutional monarchy retaining the Pahlavi line as figurehead
Rule of the jurist (velayat-e faqih), placing a senior cleric above elected government
A federal system granting broad autonomy to ethnic regions

evt-12-03-1979-1979-iranian-constitution.butterflyEffect: The constitution created the office of Supreme Leader (velayat-e faqih), giving ultimate authority to a senior cleric above elected officials. Ayatollah Khomeini became the first holder of this office, and it has remained the defining feature of Iran's political system into the present day.

evt-12-03-1979-the-who-concert-disaster.scenario: It is the evening of 3 December 1979 outside Riverfront Coliseum in Cincinnati. Thousands of ticket holders with unreserved festival seating are pressing against the doors, unsure if the Who have already started, and only a few entrances are unlocked.
evt-12-03-1979-the-who-concert-disaster.prompt: What should coliseum staff have done as the crowd surged against the few open doors?

choices.text: Direct everyone to a single main gate for ticket checks
Ask the crowd to form an orderly single-file line
Delay the concert until the crowd thinned naturally
Open every available entrance immediately to relieve pressure

evt-12-03-1979-the-who-concert-disaster.butterflyEffect: Only a handful of doors were open, and the crush killed eleven fans before the band even took the stage, unaware of the disaster until after the show. The tragedy prompted many US cities to ban festival (general-admission) seating and tightened crowd-management rules at large arena concerts.

evt-12-03-1990-mary-robinson.scenario: It's December 3, 1990, and you stand in the crowd as Mary Robinson is sworn in as Ireland's first female president, the first to win without Fianna Fáil's backing.
evt-12-03-1990-mary-robinson.prompt: What does Robinson do soon after taking office to symbolize her presidency?

choices.text: She places a lit candle in a window of Áras an Uachtaráin for emigrants
She abolishes the presidential veto
She refuses to meet with the British monarchy
She moves the presidential residence to Cork

evt-12-03-1990-mary-robinson.butterflyEffect: Robinson's candle became an enduring symbol of connection to the Irish diaspora and her broader push to modernize the presidency's moral voice. She went on to visit famine-stricken Somalia and war-torn Rwanda, and after leaving office became UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

evt-12-03-1994-sony-interactive-entertai.scenario: It's December 3, 1994, and you're a Sony executive in Tokyo watching the PlayStation go on sale against Sega's newly launched Saturn console.
evt-12-03-1994-sony-interactive-entertai.prompt: What price does Sony set to win over Japanese gamers?

choices.text: ¥39,800, undercutting the Saturn's ¥44,800 launch price
The same price as the Saturn, betting on brand loyalty
A price cut announced only after Saturn sales figures came in
A premium price reflecting its 3D graphics power

evt-12-03-1994-sony-interactive-entertai.butterflyEffect: The lower price helped PlayStation outsell the Saturn in Japan within months, launching Sony's rise as a console maker. PlayStation eventually became the first platform to ship over 100 million units, and Sega exited the hardware business altogether by 2001.

evt-12-03-1999-nasa.scenario: It's December 3, 1999, and you're a flight controller at JPL, waiting for Mars Polar Lander to phone home after its descent into the Martian south polar region.
evt-12-03-1999-nasa.prompt: What happens when the spacecraft's signal fails to arrive on schedule?

choices.text: Contact is never reestablished, and the lander is presumed lost
Engineers detect a garbled transmission and repair the antenna remotely
The lander pings back with full telemetry moments later
The signal arrives late but confirms a safe landing

evt-12-03-1999-nasa.butterflyEffect: No signal was ever received; investigators later concluded the descent engines likely shut off prematurely, causing a crash. The failure, following the loss of the Mars Climate Orbiter months earlier, triggered a review that ended NASA's 'faster, better, cheaper' approach and led to more rigorous testing for later missions like the Mars Exploration Rovers.

evt-12-03-2007-great-coastal-gale-of-200.scenario: It is early December 2007, and you live near the Chehalis River in Lewis County, Washington, as relentless Pacific storms push the river over its banks toward your home and the interstate beyond.
evt-12-03-2007-great-coastal-gale-of-200.prompt: With floodwaters rising fast, what is the safest immediate action?

choices.text: Evacuate to higher ground before roads become impassable
Drive through the flooded highway to reach town faster
Move valuables to the basement for safekeeping
Stay inside and wait for the water to recede on its own

evt-12-03-2007-great-coastal-gale-of-200.butterflyEffect: The flooding submerged long stretches of Interstate 5, shutting down the vital West Coast corridor for days and stranding freight traffic across the region. The disaster exposed the limits of the Chehalis basin's flood defenses and fueled years of debate over new flood-control projects for the valley.

evt-12-03-2009-2009-hotel-shamo-bombing.scenario: It is 3 December 2009 inside the Hotel Shamo in Mogadishu, where Somalia's Transitional Federal Government is holding a graduation ceremony for new medical students. A bomber disguised in women's clothing has slipped into the hall.
evt-12-03-2009-2009-hotel-shamo-bombing.prompt: What was the immediate consequence for Somalia's government after the bombing?

choices.text: Foreign peacekeepers withdrew entirely from Mogadishu the next day
The TFG immediately negotiated a lasting truce with insurgents
Three government ministers were among the dead, crippling the cabinet
The bombing had no effect on the transitional government's operations

evt-12-03-2009-2009-hotel-shamo-bombing.butterflyEffect: The blast killed 25 people, including three TFG ministers, striking a severe blow to an already fragile transitional government fighting insurgents for control of the capital. It became the deadliest attack in Somalia since the Beledweyne bombing months earlier, deepening the government's crisis of legitimacy.

evt-12-03-2012-typhoon-bopha.scenario: You lead a coastal village on Mindanao in early December 2012 as Typhoon Bopha, an unusually powerful storm for this normally typhoon-safe latitude, bears down with little warning.
evt-12-03-2012-typhoon-bopha.prompt: What must you decide for your community's safety?

choices.text: Wait for official government evacuation orders before moving anyone
Reinforce homes and shelter in place through the storm
Ignore the storm since typhoons rarely reach this latitude
Order immediate evacuation to higher ground despite the short warning

evt-12-03-2012-typhoon-bopha.butterflyEffect: Bopha's unprecedented southern track caught many Mindanao communities unprepared for a storm of Category 5 intensity, contributing to nearly 1,900 deaths. The disaster pushed the Philippines to overhaul early-warning systems for southern regions previously assumed to be beyond typhoon reach.

evt-12-03-2024-yoon-suk-yeol.scenario: It's just past midnight on December 3, 2024, and soldiers block the National Assembly's gates as President Yoon Suk Yeol declares martial law and bans political activity.
evt-12-03-2024-yoon-suk-yeol.prompt: What do lawmakers do after climbing the fences to reach the chamber?

choices.text: They hold an emergency vote demanding the martial law order be lifted
They comply with the decree and suspend the Assembly
They appeal directly to the military to stand down
They flee the country to avoid arrest

evt-12-03-2024-yoon-suk-yeol.butterflyEffect: 190 lawmakers unanimously voted to demand the decree's reversal, and Yoon rescinded it within six hours. The crisis led swiftly to his impeachment, removal from office, and eventual conviction and life sentence for insurrection.

evt-12-03-2024-2024-south-korean-martial.scenario: It is just after 10:27pm on 3 December 2024, and President Yoon Suk Yeol has declared martial law on live television, accusing the opposition of colluding with North Korea and ordering troops to the National Assembly.
evt-12-03-2024-2024-south-korean-martial.prompt: As a lawmaker, what do you do to stop the decree?

choices.text: Flee the country to avoid arrest
Rush past soldiers into the National Assembly to vote down the decree
Publicly endorse the president's declaration
Wait quietly for the military to stand down on its own

evt-12-03-2024-2024-south-korean-martial.butterflyEffect: Enough legislators scaled fences and pushed past soldiers to reach the chamber, voting 190-0 to overturn martial law within hours. Yoon rescinded the order that same night, but the episode triggered his impeachment weeks later.

evt-12-04-1639-jeremiah-horrocks.scenario: It is 4 December 1639 in Much Hoole, Lancashire. You are Jeremiah Horrocks, and your calculations say Venus will cross the face of the Sun this very afternoon, an event almost no one else on Earth expects.
evt-12-04-1639-jeremiah-horrocks.prompt: How do you observe the transit safely to record its timing?

choices.text: Measure the Sun's shadow length at intervals throughout the day
Observe only at sunset when the Sun's light is naturally dimmed
Project the Sun's image through a telescope onto paper to trace Venus's path
Stare directly at the Sun through smoked glass at the predicted moment

evt-12-04-1639-jeremiah-horrocks.butterflyEffect: Horrocks projected the Sun's image through a telescope onto a screen, allowing him and his friend William Crabtree to time Venus's transit precisely, the only two people known to have witnessed it. His method and data later underpinned efforts by astronomers, including Edmond Halley, to use transits of Venus to calculate the distance from Earth to the Sun.

evt-12-04-1872-brigantine.scenario: It is 4 December 1872 in the mid-Atlantic. You are captain of the brigantine Dei Gratia, and your lookout spots another ship, the Mary Celeste, drifting erratically with her sails set but no one visible on deck.
evt-12-04-1872-brigantine.prompt: What do you do after boarding and finding the ship abandoned with cargo and supplies intact?

choices.text: Leave it untouched and report its position to the nearest naval authority
Strip the cargo immediately and abandon the hull at sea
Burn the ship where it was found to prevent it drifting into shipping lanes
Claim the derelict ship as salvage and sail it to port for investigation

evt-12-04-1872-brigantine.butterflyEffect: The Dei Gratia's crew brought the Mary Celeste into port, and the fate of her missing captain, crew, and family was never definitively solved. The mystery became maritime legend, inspiring countless theories from mutiny to waterspouts, and fiction including a story by Arthur Conan Doyle that cemented the ship's name in popular imagination.

evt-12-04-1905-great-seimas-of-vilnius.scenario: It is 4 December 1905 in Vilnius. Over two thousand delegates have gathered amid the upheaval of the Russian Revolution to decide what Lithuania should demand from the Empire that rules it.
evt-12-04-1905-great-seimas-of-vilnius.prompt: What did the Great Seimas resolve to seek for Lithuania?

choices.text: The complete abolition of the Russian monarchy
Wide political autonomy within Russia, sought through peaceful means
A federal union merging Lithuania with Poland
Immediate armed uprising to seize independence outright

evt-12-04-1905-great-seimas-of-vilnius.butterflyEffect: The assembly demanded broad political autonomy within the Russian Empire, to be pursued through peaceful means rather than armed revolt. This first modern national congress in Lithuania laid groundwork that culminated, over a decade later, in the Act of Independence of Lithuania on 16 February 1918.

evt-12-04-1969-fred-hampton.scenario: It is before dawn on 4 December 1969 in a Chicago apartment. Illinois Black Panther chairman Fred Hampton is asleep as police, armed with an informant's floor plan, prepare to move in.
evt-12-04-1969-fred-hampton.prompt: What later came to light about the raid that ended Hampton's life?

choices.text: An FBI informant had given police a floor plan of the apartment in advance
Hampton had fired first, prompting a lawful police response
The raid was an unrelated narcotics operation that stumbled onto Hampton
Local police unions had publicly protested the operation beforehand

evt-12-04-1969-fred-hampton.butterflyEffect: It emerged that FBI informant William O'Neal had supplied Chicago police with a detailed floor plan of the apartment beforehand, part of the FBI's COINTELPRO program targeting Black activist leaders. A subsequent civil suit exposed collusion between the FBI, Chicago police, and prosecutors, leading to a landmark settlement and lasting scrutiny of domestic surveillance abuses.

evt-12-04-1978-assassinations-of-george-.scenario: It is the morning of 27 November 1978 inside San Francisco City Hall. Former supervisor Dan White has just climbed through a basement window, avoiding the metal detectors, to confront Mayor Moscone before an announcement he dreads.
evt-12-04-1978-assassinations-of-george-.prompt: What defense did White's lawyers use at trial after he killed Moscone and Milk?

choices.text: Diminished capacity from depression, blamed partly on junk food binges
Full insanity, arguing he could not distinguish right from wrong
Combat-related PTSD from prior military service
Self-defense, claiming Moscone attacked him first

evt-12-04-1978-assassinations-of-george-.butterflyEffect: White's lawyers argued diminished capacity, claiming binges on junk food worsened his depression — dubbed the "Twinkie defense" by the press. The jury convicted him only of voluntary manslaughter, and the lenient sentence ignited the White Night riots, galvanizing gay political activism for a generation.

evt-12-04-1980-led-zeppelin.scenario: It is December 1980, weeks after drummer John Bonham's sudden death. You are Robert Plant, Jimmy Page, or John Paul Jones, weighing whether the band can go on without him.
evt-12-04-1980-led-zeppelin.prompt: What do the surviving members decide about the band's future?

choices.text: Finish the current album using session drummers only
Officially disband the band
Recruit a new drummer and keep touring under the same name
Announce an indefinite hiatus but keep the name active

evt-12-04-1980-led-zeppelin.butterflyEffect: The three remaining members issued a statement announcing Led Zeppelin's dissolution, saying they could not continue as they were. Page and Plant later reunited for other projects, and Bonham's son Jason would go on to fill his father's drum stool at reunion performances.

evt-12-04-1992-george-h-w-bush.scenario: It is early December 1992. You are a Pentagon planner briefing President Bush on Somalia, where famine and warlord violence are blocking relief convoys from reaching starving civilians.
evt-12-04-1992-george-h-w-bush.prompt: What action does Bush order to break the humanitarian logjam?

choices.text: Fund Somali militias to escort aid shipments themselves
Send U.S. Marines to secure Mogadishu's port and airport for aid convoys
Impose a naval blockade to pressure warlords into a ceasefire
Airdrop supplies while avoiding any ground troop deployment

evt-12-04-1992-george-h-w-bush.butterflyEffect: Bush ordered U.S. troops into Somalia as the lead of a UN-sanctioned coalition, Operation Restore Hope, to secure ports and roads for food deliveries. The mission later expanded under UNOSOM II and escalated into direct conflict with Somali militias, culminating in the October 1993 Battle of Mogadishu that reshaped U.S. caution about humanitarian interventions for years afterward.

evt-12-04-1998-unity-iss-module.scenario: It is 4 December 1998, and you are part of the ground team watching Space Shuttle Endeavour lift off carrying Unity, the first American-built module meant to link up with Russia's orbiting Zarya module.
evt-12-04-1998-unity-iss-module.prompt: How will astronauts join Unity to the station once Endeavour reaches orbit?

choices.text: Wait for a future mission to attempt the connection with better equipment
Leave Unity attached to the shuttle permanently as a temporary lab
Use the shuttle's robotic arm to dock Unity to Zarya, followed by spacewalks to connect systems
Have Unity fly autonomously to dock itself with Zarya

evt-12-04-1998-unity-iss-module.butterflyEffect: Astronauts used the shuttle's robotic arm to mate Unity to Zarya, then completed spacewalks to hook up power and data connections between the two modules. This first successful joining of American and Russian hardware in orbit became the structural foundation for all subsequent assembly of the International Space Station.

evt-12-04-2005-december-2005-protest-for.scenario: It is 4 December 2005, and you march with tens of thousands through Hong Kong's streets, demanding the government allow direct election of the Chief Executive and the full Legislative Council.
evt-12-04-2005-december-2005-protest-for.prompt: What do the protesters press the government to do with its reform proposal?

choices.text: Boycott all future Legislative Council elections
Appeal directly to the central government in Beijing to intervene
Set a clear timetable toward full universal suffrage
Accept the limited reform package as a first step

evt-12-04-2005-december-2005-protest-for.butterflyEffect: The protests added pressure that helped sink the government's limited reform package, which the Legislative Council rejected weeks later for lacking a timetable toward universal suffrage. The unresolved demand for full democratic elections would resurface in later movements, including the 2014 Umbrella Movement.

evt-12-04-2012-canto-degli-italiani.scenario: It is 2012, and you sit in the Italian Parliament. For over sixty years, "Il Canto degli Italiani" has been played at state occasions purely by convention, never formally adopted into law as the nation's anthem.
evt-12-04-2012-canto-degli-italiani.prompt: What does Parliament finally do about the anthem's uncertain legal status?

choices.text: Vote to enshrine it in law as the official national anthem
Leave its status informal, as it has been for decades
Replace it with "Va, pensiero" from Verdi's Nabucco
Hold a national referendum to choose a new anthem

evt-12-04-2012-canto-degli-italiani.butterflyEffect: Parliament passed a law formally designating "Il Canto degli Italiani" as Italy's official national anthem, ending decades of informal use dating back to 1946. The vote closed off periodic proposals to replace it with alternatives like the chorus "Va, pensiero" from Verdi's Nabucco.

evt-12-04-2017-thomas-fire.scenario: It is early December 2017 near Santa Paula, California. Fierce Santa Ana winds are driving flames toward populated coastal communities, and you must decide how to protect thousands of residents in its path.
evt-12-04-2017-thomas-fire.prompt: What did fire crews and officials prioritize as the blaze raced toward Ventura and Santa Barbara?

choices.text: Focusing only on saving structures while ignoring evacuation orders
Letting the fire burn out naturally in the backcountry
Evacuating residents of Ventura and Santa Barbara ahead of the flames
Waiting for seasonal rains before committing resources

evt-12-04-2017-thomas-fire.butterflyEffect: Authorities ordered mass evacuations across Ventura and Santa Barbara counties as the fire grew into what was then the largest wildfire in modern California history. The scorched, denuded hillsides it left behind set the stage for the deadly Montecito debris flows just weeks later in January 2018.

evt-12-04-2021-semeru.scenario: It is early evening on 4 December 2021. Heavy monsoon rain has been battering the slopes of Mount Semeru for hours, and you are a village official in Lumajang district watching ash-grey clouds boil over the crater rim.
evt-12-04-2021-semeru.prompt: What should you do as the mountain shows signs of a major pyroclastic event?

choices.text: Advise residents to shelter indoors since ash rarely reaches populated areas
Order immediate evacuation of villages on the southeastern slope
Focus efforts on protecting farmland rather than moving people
Wait for an official eruption warning from the national volcanology center before acting

evt-12-04-2021-semeru.butterflyEffect: A large pyroclastic flow, triggered by the collapse of unstable crater material after heavy rain, swept down Semeru's slopes and buried villages including Curah Kobokan, killing at least 68 people. The disaster pushed Indonesian authorities to expand exclusion zones and invest further in volcanic early-warning systems for the densely populated slopes.

evt-12-05-1484-pope-innocent-viii.scenario: You are a papal secretary in Rome in 1484, drafting the text of Summis desiderantes affectibus at Pope Innocent VIII's request. Two Dominican inquisitors have complained that local authorities in Germany are obstructing their pursuit of alleged witches.
evt-12-05-1484-pope-innocent-viii.prompt: What does this new papal bull authorize the inquisitors to do?

choices.text: Pardon all those previously accused of witchcraft in the region
Ban all witchcraft trials pending further theological study
Transfer witchcraft cases entirely to secular civil courts
Hunt and prosecute suspected witches in Germany free from local interference

evt-12-05-1484-pope-innocent-viii.butterflyEffect: The bull gave papal sanction to inquisitors Heinrich Kramer and Jacob Sprenger to root out witchcraft without interference from local bishops. It was later printed as a preface to their 1486 treatise Malleus Maleficarum, lending papal authority to a text that fueled centuries of witch trials across Europe.
