evt-12-05-1757-seven-years-war.scenario: It is dawn on 5 December 1757 near the Silesian village of Leuthen. Your Prussian army, badly outnumbered, faces a much larger Austrian force arrayed across the open ground ahead.
evt-12-05-1757-seven-years-war.prompt: What tactic should Frederick the Great use to overcome the Austrians' numbers?

choices.text: Charge directly into the center of the Austrian line
Retreat and wait for reinforcements before engaging
Concentrate force in an oblique attack against one enemy flank
Divide his army evenly to attack both flanks at once

evt-12-05-1757-seven-years-war.butterflyEffect: Frederick used his famous oblique order, concentrating his forces to smash one Austrian flank before the rest of their line could react. The victory at Leuthen secured Silesia for Prussia and is still studied in military academies as a masterclass in maneuver against superior numbers.

evt-12-05-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 5 December 1775 and you are Colonel Henry Knox, arriving at the captured Fort Ticonderoga. Washington's army besieging Boston desperately needs heavy artillery, and dozens of cannons sit here for the taking.
evt-12-05-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What do you propose to do with the fort's guns?

choices.text: Sell the artillery to Continental sympathizers in New York for funds
Haul the heavy cannons overland by sledge to reinforce Washington near Boston
Leave the guns behind as too heavy to move in winter
Melt the cannons down for musket balls to save transport effort

evt-12-05-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Knox organized the legendary 'noble train of artillery,' hauling roughly 60 tons of cannon nearly 300 miles by ox-sled through winter to Boston. The guns, placed on Dorchester Heights in March 1776, forced the British to evacuate the city without a fight.

evt-12-05-1914-imperial-trans-antarctic-.scenario: It is 5 December 1914, and you stand on the deck of the Endurance as she departs South Georgia, the last outpost of civilization, bound south into the ice-choked Weddell Sea toward an unmapped Antarctic coast.
evt-12-05-1914-imperial-trans-antarctic-.prompt: What is Shackleton's expedition attempting to achieve on this voyage?

choices.text: Establish Britain's first permanent Antarctic research station
Reach the South Pole before rival expeditions
Chart a new sea route around Antarctica for whaling ships
Make the first land crossing of the Antarctic continent

evt-12-05-1914-imperial-trans-antarctic-.butterflyEffect: The Endurance became trapped and was eventually crushed by pack ice, stranding the crew for months on ice floes and in lifeboats. Shackleton's extraordinary effort to save every one of his men, culminating in an open-boat journey to South Georgia, became one of history's most celebrated survival stories even though the continental crossing was never made.

evt-12-05-1936-1936-constitution-of-the-.scenario: You are a delegate at the Extraordinary Eighth Congress of Soviets in Moscow on 5 December 1936, asked to approve a new constitution hailed as the most democratic in the world, guaranteeing universal suffrage and civil rights.
evt-12-05-1936-1936-constitution-of-the-.prompt: What actually followed the adoption of this celebrated document?

choices.text: It immediately introduced free multiparty elections
It coincided with the intensification of Stalin's Great Purge
It granted the Baltic states full independence
It ended forced collectivization of agriculture

evt-12-05-1936-1936-constitution-of-the-.butterflyEffect: Despite its promises of rights and elections, the Stalin Constitution coincided with the intensification of the Great Purge, in which hundreds of thousands were arrested or executed. The gap between its liberal text and brutal practice made it a lasting symbol of Soviet propaganda versus reality.

evt-12-05-1952-great-smog-of-london.scenario: It is early December 1952, and a thick, choking fog has swallowed London so completely that drivers and pedestrians alike can barely see their own hands. You are a bus conductor whose vehicle has ground to a halt in the gloom.
evt-12-05-1952-great-smog-of-london.prompt: What do you do to keep the bus moving safely through the fog?

choices.text: Switch off the headlights to conserve fuel
Walk ahead of the bus carrying a torch or flare to guide the driver
Follow the taillights of the vehicle ahead at full speed
Abandon the bus and let passengers find their own way

evt-12-05-1952-great-smog-of-london.butterflyEffect: Conductors and other volunteers walked ahead of buses carrying flares or torches to guide drivers through the near-zero visibility. The disaster's toll shocked Parliament into passing the Clean Air Act of 1956, which restricted the smoky coal fires that had caused it.

evt-12-05-1958-controlled-access-highway.scenario: It is 5 December 1958, and you are among the first motorists queuing to drive onto Britain's brand-new Preston Bypass, a stretch of road unlike anything built in the country before.
evt-12-05-1958-controlled-access-highway.prompt: What should you expect from this pioneering new type of road?

choices.text: A toll booth at every mile to fund its upkeep
A strict speed limit of 20 mph enforced throughout
Shared use with horse-drawn carts and cyclists as before
Continuous carriageways with no crossroads, junctions, or pedestrian crossings

evt-12-05-1958-controlled-access-highway.butterflyEffect: The Preston Bypass opened as Britain's first motorway, but frost damage forced its partial closure within weeks. It was soon absorbed into the M6 and became the template for the national motorway network that transformed British travel and freight over the following decades.

evt-12-05-1965-glasnost-meeting.scenario: It is 5 December 1965, Constitution Day, in Pushkin Square, Moscow. You stand with a small group of students and writers who have unfurled handmade banners, protesting the secret trial of writers Andrei Sinyavsky and Yuli Daniel.
evt-12-05-1965-glasnost-meeting.prompt: What do the demonstrators demand from the Soviet authorities?

choices.text: Political asylum for the writers abroad
Immediate release of the writers without any trial
Formation of a legal opposition party
An open, public trial as guaranteed by the Soviet constitution

evt-12-05-1965-glasnost-meeting.butterflyEffect: The KGB swiftly dispersed the crowd and detained several participants, but the protest is remembered as the birth of the Soviet human rights movement. Pushkin Square demonstrations became an annual tradition among dissidents in the years that followed.

evt-12-05-1972-gough-whitlam.scenario: It is December 1972 in Canberra. Gough Whitlam's Labor Party has just won government after 23 years in opposition, but the full cabinet cannot be sworn in for weeks.
evt-12-05-1972-gough-whitlam.prompt: How should Whitlam govern in the meantime, with no ministry yet appointed?

choices.text: Call an emergency second election to speed up the process
Ask the outgoing government to remain in caretaker roles
Form a temporary two-man ministry with his deputy to run all portfolios
Delay all government action until the full cabinet is sworn in

evt-12-05-1972-gough-whitlam.butterflyEffect: Whitlam and his deputy Lance Barnard formed a two-man ministry, dividing all 27 portfolios between themselves for a fortnight so reforms could begin immediately. This rapid start set the tone for Whitlam's ambitious and fast-moving legislative program over the next three years.

evt-12-05-1977-egypt.scenario: It is early December 1977. You are an aide to President Sadat, watching Syria, Libya, and Algeria sever diplomatic ties with Egypt in fury over his recent, unprecedented visit to Jerusalem.
evt-12-05-1977-egypt.prompt: How does Sadat respond to this coordinated Arab diplomatic backlash?

choices.text: Call an emergency Arab League summit to mediate the dispute
Sever diplomatic relations with the protesting states while continuing peace talks with Israel
Abandon the Jerusalem initiative to repair Arab unity
Offer economic concessions to the protesting states to reverse the break

evt-12-05-1977-egypt.butterflyEffect: Egypt broke relations with Syria, Libya, and Algeria in return, pressing ahead with its separate peace track with Israel despite growing Arab isolation. This rupture deepened over the following years, and after the 1979 Egypt-Israel treaty, Egypt was suspended from the Arab League entirely until the mid-1980s.

evt-12-05-1983-national-reorganization-p.scenario: It is December 1983 in Buenos Aires. Argentina's military dictatorship is dissolving after seven brutal years, and you are among the advisors shaping how the incoming civilian government should confront its legacy.
evt-12-05-1983-national-reorganization-p.prompt: What should the new government do about the military's human rights abuses?

choices.text: Investigate the disappearances and prosecute military commanders responsible
Leave the matter to future generations to address
Exile the former junta leaders without trial
Grant a blanket amnesty to preserve national stability

evt-12-05-1983-national-reorganization-p.butterflyEffect: Argentina's new government, under Raúl Alfonsín, established a truth commission and put the former junta leaders on trial in 1985. It was one of the first times a Latin American military regime faced criminal prosecution for its own atrocities, setting a precedent across the region.

evt-12-05-1991-leonid-kravchuk.scenario: It is 5 December 1991 in Kyiv, and you are a delegate watching Leonid Kravchuk take the oath as Ukraine's first president, days after a referendum saw over ninety percent of voters back independence from the Soviet Union.
evt-12-05-1991-leonid-kravchuk.prompt: What major challenge will Kravchuk's new presidency immediately face?

choices.text: Joining NATO immediately to secure Western military protection
Adopting the Russian ruble as Ukraine's sole national currency
Reuniting Ukraine with Russia under a new confederal treaty
Negotiating independence and the handover of Soviet nuclear weapons on Ukrainian soil

evt-12-05-1991-leonid-kravchuk.butterflyEffect: Kravchuk had to negotiate Ukraine's independence from the crumbling USSR while managing the fate of the Soviet nuclear arsenal stationed on Ukrainian soil. Within weeks he joined the leaders of Russia and Belarus in signing the Belovezha Accords, formally dissolving the Soviet Union.

evt-12-05-1994-budapest-memorandum.scenario: It is 5 December 1994 in Budapest. As a Ukrainian diplomat, you are about to sign a memorandum in which the United States, Britain, and Russia offer assurances to Ukraine in exchange for it giving up the nuclear arsenal it inherited from the Soviet Union.
evt-12-05-1994-budapest-memorandum.prompt: What do the signatories commit to in the memorandum?

choices.text: To provide automatic military intervention if Ukraine is attacked
To fund Ukraine's ongoing nuclear weapons program
To station NATO troops permanently on Ukrainian soil
To respect Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity and refrain from force

evt-12-05-1994-budapest-memorandum.butterflyEffect: Ukraine, Belarus, and Kazakhstan all surrendered their Soviet-era nuclear weapons under these assurances. The memorandum's promises proved contested when Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 and launched a full invasion in 2022, reigniting global debate over the value of such security guarantees.

evt-12-05-1995-sri-lankan-civil-war.scenario: It is early December 1995. You are a Sri Lankan Army soldier pushing into the streets of Jaffna, the LTTE's northern stronghold, after weeks of fighting in Operation Riviresa.
evt-12-05-1995-sri-lankan-civil-war.prompt: What does the government announce about Jaffna on 5 December 1995?

choices.text: The army has captured Jaffna city from the LTTE
Government forces are withdrawing from the north
LTTE leader Prabhakaran has been killed
A ceasefire has been signed with the LTTE

evt-12-05-1995-sri-lankan-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The fall of Jaffna forced the LTTE to abandon conventional territorial control there and retreat into jungle bases, shifting toward guerrilla and terror tactics elsewhere on the island. The war nonetheless dragged on for another fourteen years until the LTTE's final defeat in 2009.

evt-12-05-2001-space-shuttle-endeavour.scenario: It is 5 December 2001 at Kennedy Space Center. You watch Endeavour thunder off the pad on STS-108, carrying a fresh crew bound for the International Space Station to relieve the astronauts already aboard.
evt-12-05-2001-space-shuttle-endeavour.prompt: What is the main purpose of this shuttle flight?

choices.text: Service the Hubble Space Telescope
Test a new heat shield design for reentry
Deliver a new crew and swap out the current station residents
Launch the first module of the space station

evt-12-05-2001-space-shuttle-endeavour.butterflyEffect: STS-108 delivered the Expedition 4 crew to the ISS and brought Expedition 3 home, while also ferrying supplies in the Raffaello cargo module. Flying just months after 9/11, it underscored NASA's determination to keep station operations running under tightened security.

evt-12-05-2005-civil-partnership-act-200.scenario: It is 5 December 2005 and you are a same-sex couple in England who has waited years for legal recognition. Today the Civil Partnership Act finally comes into force, and you can register your relationship at a local register office.
evt-12-05-2005-civil-partnership-act-200.prompt: What rights does registering a civil partnership give you today?

choices.text: Only tax benefits, with no inheritance or hospital visitation rights
Recognition only if the couple also holds a religious ceremony
Full legal marriage status identical in every respect
Property, pension, and next-of-kin rights equivalent to civil marriage

evt-12-05-2005-civil-partnership-act-200.butterflyEffect: Civil partners gained rights nearly identical to marriage, including inheritance, pension, and next-of-kin protections, though the word 'marriage' itself remained withheld. The Act was a stepping stone toward full same-sex marriage, legalised in England and Wales in 2013 and extended to opposite-sex couples in 2019.

evt-12-05-2006-frank-bainimarama.scenario: It is the morning of 5 December 2006 in Suva. You serve in Prime Minister Laisenia Qarase's cabinet as Commodore Frank Bainimarama's soldiers take up positions around Parliament and government buildings, refusing to stand down.
evt-12-05-2006-frank-bainimarama.prompt: What does Bainimarama do to Qarase's government that day?

choices.text: He hands control to the Great Council of Chiefs
He resigns his military commission and stands for election
He seizes power, dissolving the elected government
He negotiates a power-sharing coalition with Qarase

evt-12-05-2006-frank-bainimarama.butterflyEffect: Bainimarama dissolved the government, declared a state of emergency, and installed himself as interim leader in Fiji's fourth coup since 1987. He later became prime minister after 2014 elections and ruled until 2022, while Fiji faced years of Commonwealth suspension over the takeover.

evt-12-05-2007-westroads-mall-shooting.scenario: You manage the Von Maur department store at Westroads Mall on 5 December 2007 when gunfire erupts on an upper floor. Customers are scattering and you have seconds to act.
evt-12-05-2007-westroads-mall-shooting.prompt: What is the right immediate action to protect shoppers in the store?

choices.text: Evacuate customers through emergency exits and initiate a store lockdown
Keep registers open and continue serving customers until police arrive
Attempt to approach and negotiate with the shooter directly
Wait for corporate headquarters to issue instructions before acting

evt-12-05-2007-westroads-mall-shooting.butterflyEffect: Robert Hawkins killed eight people and himself; he had left a suicide note referencing his troubled life and prior mental health struggles. The shooting, one of the deadliest in Nebraska history, pushed retailers and mall operators nationwide to review lockdown procedures and law enforcement active-shooter response protocols.

evt-12-05-2014-exploration-flight-test-1.scenario: It is 5 December 2014 at Cape Canaveral. You watch the uncrewed Orion capsule lift off atop a Delta IV Heavy rocket, bound for an altitude farther from Earth than any capsule built for astronauts since Apollo.
evt-12-05-2014-exploration-flight-test-1.prompt: What is the flight's key objective on reentry?

choices.text: Test life support systems for a crewed mission
Test the heat shield during a high-speed, high-altitude reentry
Practice docking with the International Space Station
Demonstrate a lunar surface landing

evt-12-05-2014-exploration-flight-test-1.butterflyEffect: EFT-1 tested Orion's heat shield and avionics during a high-speed reentry from roughly 3,600 miles up, far hotter and faster than an ISS return. The successful splashdown validated the capsule design NASA would build on for the crewed Artemis missions to the Moon.

evt-12-05-2017-international-olympic-com.scenario: You are a Russian speed skater in late 2017. The IOC has just announced a ban from the Sochi Games' successor after investigators found evidence of a state-run doping scheme at the 2014 Olympics you helped win medals in.
evt-12-05-2017-international-olympic-com.prompt: What must athletes like you do to compete at the 2018 Winter Olympics?

choices.text: Boycott the Games entirely alongside the Russian Olympic Committee
Compete for Russia as normal since the ban only affected officials
Compete under a neutral flag as an 'Olympic Athlete from Russia' after vetting
Switch national federations to compete for a different country

evt-12-05-2017-international-olympic-com.butterflyEffect: Clean Russian athletes were allowed to compete only as neutrals under the banner "Olympic Athletes from Russia," without their flag or anthem. The scandal deepened distrust between Russia and Western sporting bodies and led to years of further doping bans and legal battles at the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

evt-12-06-1060-bela-i-of-hungary.scenario: It is 1060 at Székesfehérvár. Having defeated your brother Andrew I for control of Hungary, you are about to be crowned king and must decide how to steady the kingdom's shaky economy.
evt-12-06-1060-bela-i-of-hungary.prompt: What reform do you announce to strengthen Hungary's currency?

choices.text: Adopt the Byzantine gold solidus as the kingdom's sole currency
Order that only Hungarian coinage be used in trade, banning foreign currency
Abolish all taxation across the kingdom for a decade
Introduce the German mark as Hungary's official currency

evt-12-06-1060-bela-i-of-hungary.butterflyEffect: Béla banned the use of foreign coin, ordering that only Hungarian denars circulate in trade. The reform unsettled nobles accustomed to foreign currency, feeding unrest, and within months Béla died after a throne collapsed beneath him at an assembly. His death opened the way for his nephew Solomon, backed by the Holy Roman Empire, to seize the crown and plunge Hungary into further succession conflict.

evt-12-06-1240-mongol-invasion-of-kievan.scenario: You are a boyar defending the walls of Kiev in early December 1240, watching Batu Khan's siege engines finally breach the city's fortifications after days of relentless bombardment.
evt-12-06-1240-mongol-invasion-of-kievan.prompt: What followed the fall of Kiev to the Mongols?

choices.text: The Mongols withdrew from Rus' territory entirely after taking Kiev.
Kiev was rebuilt immediately and remained the unchallenged capital of a unified Rus'.
The Byzantine Empire annexed Kiev to protect it from further Mongol raids.
Kievan Rus' effectively ended, and surviving principalities became tributaries of the Mongol-led Golden Horde.

evt-12-06-1240-mongol-invasion-of-kievan.butterflyEffect: Kiev's fall marked the effective end of Kievan Rus' as a political entity, though some western principalities like Galicia-Volhynia survived largely intact. Mongol overlordship through the Golden Horde would shape Russian political life for over two centuries, until Moscow's princes gradually asserted independence.

evt-12-06-1803-haitian-revolution.scenario: It is November 1803, and you serve aboard one of the last French vessels evacuating Saint-Domingue after General Rochambeau's surrender to Dessalines's army at Cap-Français. British warships, at war with France, wait offshore watching for French sails.
evt-12-06-1803-haitian-revolution.prompt: What happens to the French convoy as it tries to slip out to open water?

choices.text: Dessalines's forces burn the ships in harbor before they can sail
The Royal Navy intercepts and captures nearly all the ships
A hurricane scatters the fleet before the British can act
The convoy slips past unnoticed and reaches France safely

evt-12-06-1803-haitian-revolution.butterflyEffect: The Royal Navy intercepted and captured nearly all the fleeing French ships, crushing France's last hope of holding the colony. With French power broken, Jean-Jacques Dessalines proclaimed Haiti's independence on 1 January 1804, making it the first free Black republic and the only nation founded by a successful slave revolt.

evt-12-06-1865-slavery-in-the-united-sta.scenario: You are following the news in early December 1865 as Georgia becomes the state whose ratification pushes the Thirteenth Amendment past the required three-fourths threshold of states.
evt-12-06-1865-slavery-in-the-united-sta.prompt: What did this ratification actually achieve for the United States?

choices.text: It constitutionally abolished slavery except as punishment for crime
It formally ended sharecropping across the South
It granted citizenship to all people born in the United States
It gave Black men the constitutional right to vote

evt-12-06-1865-slavery-in-the-united-sta.butterflyEffect: The amendment constitutionally abolished slavery and involuntary servitude, except as punishment for crime. That exception clause was later exploited through convict leasing and mass incarceration, a legacy still debated in discussions of racial justice today.

evt-12-06-1904-theodore-roosevelt.scenario: You are drafting President Theodore Roosevelt's annual message to Congress in December 1904, searching for language that will justify American intervention in Latin American finances without provoking European powers.
evt-12-06-1904-theodore-roosevelt.prompt: What new policy did Roosevelt announce as an extension of the Monroe Doctrine?

choices.text: The U.S. would annex all Caribbean nations in default on European loans.
The U.S. would invite European powers to jointly police Latin America.
The U.S. would withdraw from all involvement in Latin American affairs.
The U.S. would act as an international policeman to preempt European intervention in the Americas.

evt-12-06-1904-theodore-roosevelt.butterflyEffect: The Roosevelt Corollary asserted a U.S. right to intervene in Latin American nations to preempt European powers, most immediately justifying American control over customs in the Dominican Republic. It set the template for decades of U.S. military and financial interventions in the Caribbean and Central America, a pattern only partially reversed by the later 'Good Neighbor' policy.

evt-12-06-1907-monongah-mining-disaster.scenario: It is the morning of December 6, 1907, and you are a mine inspector reviewing safety reports on the Fairmont Coal Company's Nos. 6 and 8 mines near Monongah, West Virginia, moments before an explosion tears through the shafts.
evt-12-06-1907-monongah-mining-disaster.prompt: What federal action followed the Monongah mining disaster?

choices.text: The United Mine Workers were outlawed nationwide.
Congress created the U.S. Bureau of Mines in 1910 to investigate mine safety.
The federal government nationalized all coal mines immediately.
West Virginia banned coal mining within the state.

evt-12-06-1907-monongah-mining-disaster.butterflyEffect: The explosion killed 362 miners, the deadliest mining disaster in U.S. history, and exposed the absence of federal oversight in coal mining. Public outcry pushed Congress to establish the U.S. Bureau of Mines in 1910, beginning a slow federal push toward mine safety regulation.

evt-12-06-1912-nefertiti-bust.scenario: You are archaeologist Ludwig Borchardt at Amarna on December 6, 1912, as your team's excavation uncovers a strikingly lifelike painted bust of Queen Nefertiti, and you must decide how to describe the find for the official division of antiquities with Egypt.
evt-12-06-1912-nefertiti-bust.prompt: How did Borchardt secure the bust for Germany rather than Egypt?

choices.text: Egypt formally gifted the bust to Germany as a diplomatic gesture.
He is alleged to have downplayed the bust's quality and value in the official documentation.
He purchased the bust outright from Egyptian officials at auction.
He smuggled the bust out of Egypt without informing any authorities.

evt-12-06-1912-nefertiti-bust.butterflyEffect: The bust went to Berlin under the era's antiquities-partition system, and Borchardt's description of it has long been criticized as misleading about its true value and quality. It became a lasting symbol of colonial-era archaeology, with Egypt repeatedly demanding its return—a dispute still unresolved today.

evt-12-06-1917-tnt.scenario: It is the morning of 6 December 1917 in Halifax Harbour. You are railway dispatcher Vince Coleman, and you've just learned the munitions ship Mont-Blanc, loaded with TNT, is on fire and drifting toward the pier — with an incoming passenger train due any minute.
evt-12-06-1917-tnt.prompt: Knowing the ship could explode at any moment, what do you do?

choices.text: Flee the telegraph office immediately to save yourself
Attempt to tow the burning ship away from the pier yourself
Assume it's a false alarm and continue your normal duties
Stay at your post and telegraph a warning to stop the train

evt-12-06-1917-tnt.butterflyEffect: Coleman stayed at his post and telegraphed a warning to stop the incoming train, ending his message "this will probably be the last message." He was killed when the ship exploded moments later, but the train stopped in time and its passengers survived. The explosion killed roughly 2,000 people and devastated Halifax; the disaster relief effort by Boston forged a bond still marked today by Nova Scotia's annual gift of a Christmas tree to the city.

evt-12-06-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It is 6 December 1917 off the coast of England. You are a sailor aboard the American destroyer USS Jacob Jones when a torpedo slams into the hull without warning, fired from a submerged U-boat.
evt-12-06-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What happens to Jacob Jones in the minutes after the torpedo strikes?

choices.text: She sinks within minutes, the first U.S. destroyer lost to enemy action
She rams and sinks the U-boat before going down herself
She limps to a British port for emergency repairs
She is towed to safety by a nearby merchant ship

evt-12-06-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: The ship sank within about eight minutes, becoming the first U.S. destroyer lost to enemy action, with most of the crew killed. In a striking act, the German U-boat commander radioed the ship's position to Allied forces so survivors could be rescued. The loss pushed the U.S. Navy to tighten anti-submarine tactics for its destroyer escorts for the rest of the war.

evt-12-06-1942-the-holocaust.scenario: It is 6 December 1942 in the Polish village of Stary Ciepielów. German Order Police have surrounded the settlement after learning that families here have been sheltering Jews in their homes and barns.
evt-12-06-1942-the-holocaust.prompt: What do the German police do to the villagers found hiding Jews?

choices.text: Fine them heavily and confiscate their farms
Execute the families who hid Jews along with those they sheltered
Relocate them to the nearest Jewish ghetto
Deport them to forced labor camps in Germany

evt-12-06-1942-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: The police shot the sheltering families, including children, alongside the Jews they had hidden, as collective punishment meant to terrorize other Poles into refusing aid. Despite the terror, rescue networks persisted elsewhere in occupied Poland; both rescuers and the Jews they hid from this era are today honored among the Righteous Among the Nations at Yad Vashem.

evt-12-06-1975-provisional-irish-republi.scenario: It is 6 December 1975 in London. Four IRA gunmen, cornered after a car chase, have just burst into a flat on Balcombe Street and seized a married couple as hostages, beginning a standoff with armed police outside.
evt-12-06-1975-provisional-irish-republi.prompt: How does the six-day Balcombe Street siege finally end?

choices.text: The hostages overpower their captors and escape
Police storm the flat and shoot the gunmen
The gunmen surrender peacefully after learning the SAS is being sent in
The gunmen detonate a bomb, killing everyone inside

evt-12-06-1975-provisional-irish-republi.butterflyEffect: After hearing radio reports that the SAS was being called in, the gunmen surrendered without firing a shot, and the hostages walked out unharmed. The captured men were later convicted for a string of bombings including Guildford and Woolwich, and their case became entangled in the scandal that eventually exposed the wrongful convictions of the Guildford Four.

evt-12-06-1992-babri-masjid.scenario: You are a state official in Ayodhya on 6 December 1992, watching kar sevaks climb the domes of the Babri Masjid despite prior assurances given to India's Supreme Court that the structure would be protected.
evt-12-06-1992-babri-masjid.prompt: What did the Uttar Pradesh government actually do as the demolition unfolded?

choices.text: It arrested all kar sevak leaders before the demolition began
It failed to stop the mob despite prior assurances to protect the mosque
It negotiated a peaceful handover of the site to Muslim leaders
It sent army units to disperse the crowd immediately

evt-12-06-1992-babri-masjid.butterflyEffect: The mosque was torn down within hours despite the court assurances, and the failure to intervene triggered communal riots across India that killed over two thousand people. The dispute over the site continued for decades until India's Supreme Court ruled in 2019 to allot the land for a Ram temple.

evt-12-06-1999-a-m-records-inc-v-napster.scenario: You are a Napster engineer in December 1999, watching news break that major record labels have filed suit against your company for enabling millions of users to trade music files for free.
evt-12-06-1999-a-m-records-inc-v-napster.prompt: How did the courts ultimately rule against Napster?

choices.text: Napster was held liable for contributory and vicarious copyright infringement.
Napster was found not liable because it never hosted any music files.
The Supreme Court dismissed the case for lack of jurisdiction.
Napster was ruled a legal library exempt from copyright law.

evt-12-06-1999-a-m-records-inc-v-napster.butterflyEffect: The Ninth Circuit's ruling forced Napster to shut down its free file-sharing service in 2001, establishing that platforms could be liable for infringement they enabled rather than committed directly. The decision reshaped the internet's approach to copyrighted content and helped pave the way for licensed digital music services like iTunes.

evt-12-06-2006-nasa.scenario: You are a NASA scientist in December 2006 comparing two Mars Global Surveyor photographs of the same gully, taken years apart, and noticing new bright deposits that suggest recent movement of material down the slope.
evt-12-06-2006-nasa.prompt: What did this photographic evidence suggest about present-day Mars?

choices.text: Mars's atmosphere could permanently sustain liquid water
The photos proved definitive evidence of microbial life
Liquid water may occasionally flow on Mars's surface today
Mars has vast confirmed underground oceans

evt-12-06-2006-nasa.butterflyEffect: The images suggested that liquid water might occasionally flow on Mars's surface even today, rather than only in its ancient past. This finding helped redirect NASA's Mars program toward searching for present-day water and habitability, influencing later missions like Phoenix, Curiosity, and the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.

evt-12-06-2017-donald-trump.scenario: You are a White House aide on December 6, 2017, reviewing the final draft of a presidential statement that will break with decades of U.S. diplomatic practice regarding one of the world's most contested cities.
evt-12-06-2017-donald-trump.prompt: What did President Trump announce that day?

choices.text: The U.S. recognized the Golan Heights as sovereign Israeli territory.
The U.S. formally recognized Jerusalem as the capital of Israel and moved to relocate its embassy there.
The U.S. cut all diplomatic relations with Israel.
The U.S. announced a two-state peace plan brokered with Palestinian leaders.

evt-12-06-2017-donald-trump.butterflyEffect: The recognition broke with decades of U.S. policy treating Jerusalem's status as unresolved, triggering protests across the Muslim world and condemnation from many U.S. allies. The embassy officially moved from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem in May 2018, cementing a shift in American Middle East policy still contested today.

evt-12-07-bce43-cicero.scenario: It is 7 December 43 BC near Formiae. Mark Antony's soldiers, sent under the Second Triumvirate's proscriptions, have caught up to your litter as your slaves urge you toward a waiting ship.
evt-12-07-bce43-cicero.prompt: What does Cicero do as the soldiers close in?

choices.text: He disguises himself as a slave to slip past them
He orders the litter to stop and faces his executioners without resistance
He offers the soldiers a large bribe to let him pass
He draws a hidden dagger and fights the soldiers

evt-12-07-bce43-cicero.butterflyEffect: Cicero ordered his bearers to halt and calmly bared his neck to the executioners rather than continue fleeing. Antony had his hands and head displayed on the Rostra in the Forum, a grim symbol that silenced Rome's most famous defender of the Republic and marked the Triumvirate's ruthless consolidation of power.

evt-12-07-574-justin-ii.scenario: It is 7 December 574 in Constantinople. Your mind has been failing for months, and the empire needs a steady hand to face wars on multiple frontiers while you can no longer reliably govern.
evt-12-07-574-justin-ii.prompt: What should Justin II do to secure the empire's leadership?

choices.text: Adopt the general Tiberius as Caesar and co-ruler
Appoint a council of senators to rule collectively
Name his infant son as sole heir
Abdicate the throne entirely to his wife Sophia

evt-12-07-574-justin-ii.butterflyEffect: Justin adopted his trusted general Tiberius as Caesar, effectively naming him regent and heir. Tiberius governed capably through Justin's decline and became Emperor Tiberius II Constantine in 578, continuing the empire's costly wars against Persia and the Avars.

evt-12-07-1837-william-lyon-mackenzie.scenario: It is 7 December 1837. You are one of William Lyon Mackenzie's poorly armed rebels, gathered at Montgomery's Tavern north of Toronto, as loyalist militia under Colonel FitzGibbon advance on your position.
evt-12-07-1837-william-lyon-mackenzie.prompt: After the rebels are swiftly routed, what happens to Mackenzie himself?

choices.text: He escapes to Britain to plead his case to Parliament
He surrenders and is granted an immediate pardon
He flees across the border into the United States
He is captured and publicly executed for treason

evt-12-07-1837-william-lyon-mackenzie.butterflyEffect: Mackenzie fled across the border into the United States, where he proclaimed a short-lived 'Republic of Canada' from Navy Island and helped provoke the Patriot War border raids. He was eventually pardoned, returned to Canada in 1849, and served again in the legislature, but the rebellion's failure accelerated British moves toward responsible government in Canada.

evt-12-07-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: You are Confederate General Thomas Hindman near Prairie Grove, Arkansas, on 7 December 1862, hoping to crush General James Blunt's isolated Union division before General Francis Herron's reinforcements can arrive.
evt-12-07-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: After a bloody day-long clash where the Union forces manage to unite, what do you do?

choices.text: Withdraw the army overnight, abandoning the field to Union forces
Press the attack at dawn and break through the Union line
Negotiate a local truce with General Blunt
Retreat immediately without engaging either Union force

evt-12-07-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Short on ammunition and supplies, Hindman withdrew his army overnight, ceding the field. The battle effectively ended major Confederate offensives in northwestern Arkansas, securing the region for Union control for the remainder of the war.

evt-12-07-1941-attack-on-pearl-harbor.scenario: It is the early morning of 7 December 1941, and you are a sailor aboard a battleship moored at Pearl Harbor when the drone of aircraft engines rises over the water and the first bombs begin to fall.
evt-12-07-1941-attack-on-pearl-harbor.prompt: What is actually unfolding above the harbor?

choices.text: An accidental munitions explosion aboard a nearby ship
A German U-boat shelling the harbor from offshore
A routine anti-aircraft drill scheduled for that morning
A surprise Japanese carrier-launched air raid on the fleet

evt-12-07-1941-attack-on-pearl-harbor.butterflyEffect: Japan had launched a coordinated surprise strike from six aircraft carriers, sinking or damaging every battleship in the harbor and killing over 2,300 Americans. The attack instantly ended U.S. neutrality, and Congress declared war on Japan the next day, drawing America fully into World War II.

evt-12-07-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 7 December 1942. You are one of ten Royal Marines launching two-man canoes from the submarine HMS Tuna off the French coast, tasked with striking deep into occupied territory.
evt-12-07-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: What is the marines' objective as they paddle toward the Gironde estuary?

choices.text: Scout the beaches of Normandy for a future invasion
Rescue downed Allied airmen sheltering with the French Resistance
Paddle up the Gironde to plant mines on blockade-runners in Bordeaux harbour
Sabotage rail lines feeding German coastal defences

evt-12-07-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The raiders paddled roughly 100 miles to Bordeaux and attached limpet mines to blockade-running ships, damaging several vessels. Only two of the ten men survived; others drowned or were captured and executed under Hitler's Commando Order, a sacrifice later commemorated in the film 'The Cockleshell Heroes' and credited with shaping future Royal Marine special operations.

evt-12-07-1972-martin-bormann.scenario: It is December 1972, and construction crews digging near Berlin's Lehrter Station uncover a skeleton believed to be Martin Bormann, Hitler's secretary who vanished amid the fall of Berlin in 1945.
evt-12-07-1972-martin-bormann.prompt: How should investigators confirm the skeleton's identity?

choices.text: Compare the skull's teeth against dental records from his former dentist
Wait for former Nazi colleagues to identify him by sight
Match fingerprints from wartime SS files
Run a DNA test against living relatives

evt-12-07-1972-martin-bormann.butterflyEffect: Forensic odontologists compared the skull's teeth to dental records held by Bormann's former dentist, and in 1973 West German authorities declared the remains his, officially closing a decades-long manhunt. A 1998 DNA test on remains later cremated and scattered at sea confirmed the match beyond doubt.

evt-12-07-1972-apollo-17.scenario: It is the early hours of 7 December 1972. You are aboard Apollo 17 after NASA's first crewed night launch, and through the window Earth hangs fully sunlit for the first time on a lunar trajectory.
evt-12-07-1972-apollo-17.prompt: What do you do with your camera as the whole illuminated Earth fills the window?

choices.text: Save the film exclusively for the lunar surface experiments
Photograph the Earth, producing what becomes the 'Blue Marble' image
Skip photography since NASA protocol forbids personal shots of Earth
Turn the camera toward the Moon instead, per mission priority

evt-12-07-1972-apollo-17.butterflyEffect: The photograph became known as 'The Blue Marble,' one of the most reproduced images ever taken, and helped galvanize the emerging environmental movement. As the last crewed mission to leave low Earth orbit, Apollo 17 also means no human has captured a similar full-Earth image firsthand since.

evt-12-07-1975-indonesian-occupation-of-.scenario: You are a Fretilin fighter in Dili on 7 December 1975 as Indonesian paratroopers and warships storm the city, only weeks after East Timor declared independence from Portugal.
evt-12-07-1975-indonesian-occupation-of-.prompt: With the capital falling, what do you and your comrades do?

choices.text: Await armed intervention from Portugal to restore the colony
Call for immediate UN peacekeepers to be deployed within days
Surrender the city immediately to avoid further conflict
Retreat to the mountains and wage a prolonged guerrilla resistance

evt-12-07-1975-indonesian-occupation-of-.butterflyEffect: Fretilin fighters retreated into the mountainous interior and waged a guerrilla resistance against Indonesian occupation for over two decades. The occupation, marked by mass suffering, ended only after a 1999 UN-supervised referendum, leading to full East Timorese independence in 2002.

evt-12-07-1982-texas.scenario: It is 7 December 1982 in the Texas execution chamber at Huntsville. You are a witness as officials strap Charles Brooks Jr. to a gurney and prepare to carry out his death sentence using a method never before applied in the United States.
evt-12-07-1982-texas.prompt: What method is used to carry out the execution?

choices.text: Lethal injection
Firing squad
The gas chamber
The electric chair

evt-12-07-1982-texas.butterflyEffect: Brooks was put to death by lethal injection, the first time the method had ever been used to execute a prisoner in the U.S. It rapidly displaced the electric chair and gas chamber as the standard American execution method, though its drug protocols would later face repeated legal and medical challenges.

evt-12-07-1993-long-island-rail-road-sho.scenario: It is evening rush hour on 7 December 1993 aboard a crowded Long Island Rail Road train pulling into Merillon Avenue station, moments after passengers have wrestled the gunman to the floor.
evt-12-07-1993-long-island-rail-road-sho.prompt: What follows in the legal aftermath of Colin Ferguson's attack?

choices.text: Charges against Ferguson are dropped for lack of evidence
Ferguson is extradited to face trial abroad
Ferguson is found not guilty by reason of insanity
Ferguson represents himself at trial and is convicted

evt-12-07-1993-long-island-rail-road-sho.butterflyEffect: Ferguson dismissed his lawyers and represented himself at trial, where he was convicted and sentenced to over 200 years in prison. Carolyn McCarthy, whose husband was killed, later ran for Congress on a gun-control platform and served for nearly two decades.

evt-12-07-1995-galileo-spacecraft.scenario: You are a flight controller at JPL on 7 December 1995, watching telemetry as Galileo's atmospheric probe plunges into Jupiter's crushing clouds while the main orbiter fires its engine to slow into orbit far above.
evt-12-07-1995-galileo-spacecraft.prompt: What ultimately happens to the descending atmospheric probe?

choices.text: It malfunctions and misses Jupiter entirely, drifting into deep space
It survives re-entry and transmits data for under an hour before being destroyed by pressure and heat
It burns up instantly on contact with the upper atmosphere
It successfully lands on the surface of Europa instead

evt-12-07-1995-galileo-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: The probe transmitted data for about 58 minutes before being crushed and vaporized by Jupiter's immense pressure and heat, having descended roughly 200 km into the atmosphere. Its readings on winds, composition, and lightning reshaped models of gas giant atmospheres, while the orbiter went on to study Jupiter's moons for nearly eight more years.

evt-12-07-1995-khabarovsk-united-air-gro.scenario: It is 7 December 1995, and you are in the cockpit of a domestic Russian airliner flying from Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk to Khabarovsk when the aircraft suddenly enters a steep, uncommanded spiral dive at high altitude.
evt-12-07-1995-khabarovsk-united-air-gro.prompt: What should the crew do the moment the autopilot sends the plane into an uncontrolled dive?

choices.text: Increase engine throttle and hold the current heading
Radio air traffic control and wait for instructions before acting
Immediately disengage the autopilot and manually recover the aircraft
Trust the autopilot to self-correct the dive

evt-12-07-1995-khabarovsk-united-air-gro.butterflyEffect: The crew failed to recover in time, and the airliner crashed into Bo-Dzhausa Mountain, killing all ninety-eight people aboard. The investigation pointed to an automated flight system malfunction compounded by a delayed manual response, prompting renewed scrutiny of automation reliability in Russian civil aviation.

evt-12-07-2011-al-anbar-governorate.scenario: It is December 2011 in Al Anbar, once the deadliest battleground of the Iraq War. You watch American soldiers hand the keys of their final base in the province over to Iraqi security forces and prepare to depart.
evt-12-07-2011-al-anbar-governorate.prompt: What does this handover signal for the U.S. military presence in Iraq?

choices.text: It signals the start of a new U.S. troop surge in the province
It marks the near-completion of the full U.S. withdrawal from Iraq
It extends the U.S. occupation for another decade
It confirms a permanent U.S. basing agreement in Anbar

evt-12-07-2011-al-anbar-governorate.butterflyEffect: The transfer marked the near-completion of the full U.S. withdrawal from Iraq, finished later that same month under the 2008 status of forces agreement. Anbar, scene of some of the war's fiercest fighting, was left to Iraqi forces who would struggle to hold it against a resurgent insurgency within a few years.

evt-12-07-2015-jaxa.scenario: It is 7 December 2015, and JAXA engineers are guiding the Akatsuki probe toward Venus for a second orbital insertion attempt, five years after the spacecraft's main engine was destroyed during its first try.
evt-12-07-2015-jaxa.prompt: How should engineers perform the orbit insertion burn without the damaged main engine?

choices.text: Fire the small reaction control thrusters for the insertion burn
Delay the burn until a repair mission could be launched
Attempt to relight the original ceramic main engine
Abandon orbit insertion and fly past Venus instead

evt-12-07-2015-jaxa.butterflyEffect: Engineers used Akatsuki's small attitude control thrusters instead of the ruined main engine, and the probe successfully entered Venus orbit. It became the first Japanese spacecraft to orbit another planet, going on to study Venus's atmosphere and its mysterious super-rotating winds for years afterward.

evt-12-07-2024-fall-of-damascus-2024.scenario: It is 7 December 2024, and you are a resident of Damascus as opposition fighters push to within 20 kilometers of the capital while government troops abandon their positions around the city.
evt-12-07-2024-fall-of-damascus-2024.prompt: What happens to President Bashar al-Assad in the hours that follow?

choices.text: He flees by air to Moscow, where he is granted asylum
He negotiates a power-sharing deal with the opposition
He is captured by rebel forces inside the presidential palace
He leads a personal counterattack to retake the capital

evt-12-07-2024-fall-of-damascus-2024.butterflyEffect: Assad fled Damascus by air to Moscow, where Russia granted him asylum, ending his family's decades-long rule of Syria. Opposition forces swept into the capital soon after, collapsing the regime and opening a chaotic new chapter in Syria's civil war.

evt-12-08-1660-margaret-hughes.scenario: It is 8 December 1660, and you take your seat in a London playhouse recently reopened after Puritan rule banned theatre. For the first time in living memory, the role of Desdemona is not being played by a boy in a wig.
evt-12-08-1660-margaret-hughes.prompt: What is about to happen on this stage for the first time in England?

choices.text: The theatre is closed again by order of Parliament
A woman plays a leading female role for the first time
The King himself performs a role on stage
A new translation of a French tragedy debuts

evt-12-08-1660-margaret-hughes.butterflyEffect: Margaret Hughes became the first woman to appear as a professional actress on the English public stage, likely in Othello. Charles II's decree permitting women to act ended the centuries-old convention of boy players in female roles and opened the profession to women, reshaping English theatre for good.

evt-12-08-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: You stand with Washington's Continental Army on the fortified heights at Whitemarsh on 8 December 1777, watching General Howe's redcoats probe your lines after marching out from Philadelphia.
evt-12-08-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What does Howe decide to do rather than storm your entrenched position?

choices.text: Launch a full frontal assault on the American lines
Withdraw his forces back to Philadelphia without attacking
Retreat entirely to New York City
Encircle Washington's army to cut off its supply lines

evt-12-08-1777-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Howe judged the American position too strong to assault and withdrew his army back to Philadelphia without a decisive battle. Washington then led his army into winter quarters at Valley Forge, where it survived a brutal winter and emerged retrained under Baron von Steuben.

evt-12-08-1854-pope-pius-ix.scenario: You are a bishop gathered in Rome on 8 December 1854, summoned by Pope Pius IX to witness a solemn proclamation about the mother of Jesus that he intends to bind on the whole Catholic Church.
evt-12-08-1854-pope-pius-ix.prompt: What doctrine is Pius IX about to formally declare?

choices.text: The Immaculate Conception of Mary
The perpetual virginity of Mary
Papal infallibility in matters of faith
The bodily Assumption of Mary into heaven

evt-12-08-1854-pope-pius-ix.butterflyEffect: Pius IX promulgated Ineffabilis Deus, defining the dogma of the Immaculate Conception—that Mary was conceived free from original sin. It was one of the first uses of papal authority to define doctrine independent of a council, foreshadowing his later declaration of papal infallibility in 1870.

evt-12-08-1880-boers.scenario: You stand among 10,000 Boers gathered at Paardekraal on 8 December 1880, watching Paul Kruger address the crowd after years of British annexation of the Transvaal.
evt-12-08-1880-boers.prompt: What did Kruger and the assembled Boers announce that day?

choices.text: A request for German colonial protection
Full acceptance of British annexation and taxation
Union with the Orange Free State under one flag
The restoration of Transvaal's independence from British rule

evt-12-08-1880-boers.butterflyEffect: They proclaimed the restoration of the independent South African Republic (Transvaal), rejecting British rule. Days later, on 16 December, fighting erupted at Bronkhorstspruit, igniting the First Boer War, which the Boers won, forcing Britain to restore Transvaal self-government under the 1881 Pretoria Convention.

evt-12-08-1941-the-holocaust.scenario: It is December 1941 in the Warthegau region of occupied Poland, where German occupation authorities have just put a new camp near the village of Chełmno into operation, using sealed vans rigged to pipe engine exhaust into the enclosed cargo space.
evt-12-08-1941-the-holocaust.prompt: What killing method does Chełmno pioneer that is later adopted at other camps?

choices.text: Forced labor until death in armaments factories
Execution exclusively by mass shooting in open pits
Mass murder by carbon monoxide gas vans
Death through prolonged starvation in sealed ghettos

evt-12-08-1941-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: Chełmno became the first stationary camp built specifically for mass murder, using gas vans to kill with carbon monoxide. The techniques tested there fed directly into the design of the fixed gas chambers later built at Auschwitz-Birkenau, Treblinka and other camps as part of the industrialized machinery of the Holocaust.

evt-12-08-1980-john-lennon.scenario: You are a doorman outside the Dakota building in New York City on the night of 8 December 1980, when gunshots suddenly ring out as John Lennon returns home.
evt-12-08-1980-john-lennon.prompt: What did fans later create in nearby Central Park to memorialize Lennon?

choices.text: The Strawberry Fields memorial with its 'Imagine' mosaic
The Lennon Wall in Prague
The Imagine Peace Tower in Iceland
A statue of the Beatles in Liverpool

evt-12-08-1980-john-lennon.butterflyEffect: In 1985, on the fifth anniversary of his death, the Strawberry Fields memorial opened in Central Park near the Dakota, featuring a mosaic reading 'Imagine,' donated by Yoko Ono. It became a global pilgrimage site for fans and a lasting symbol of Lennon's message of peace.

evt-12-08-1987-arab-israeli-conflict.scenario: You live in the Jabalia refugee camp in Gaza on 8 December 1987. News spreads that an Israeli tank transporter has collided with cars carrying Palestinian laborers home from work, killing four of your neighbors, and rumors claim it was deliberate revenge.
evt-12-08-1987-arab-israeli-conflict.prompt: What does the outrage over these deaths ignite in the days that follow?

choices.text: The dissolution of the Israeli government
Mass protests and unrest that grow into the First Intifada
A special session of the UN Security Council imposing sanctions on Israel
An immediate ceasefire agreement between Israel and the PLO

evt-12-08-1987-arab-israeli-conflict.butterflyEffect: The deaths at Jabalia triggered spontaneous protests and riots across Gaza and the West Bank that grew into the First Intifada, a sustained Palestinian uprising against Israeli occupation lasting into the early 1990s. It reshaped Palestinian politics, gave rise to Hamas, and pushed both sides toward the Oslo peace process.

evt-12-08-1988-united-states-air-force.scenario: You live in an apartment block in Remscheid, West Germany, on 8 December 1988, when a low-flying US Air Force A-10 suddenly plunges into buildings on your street during a training flight, the pilot having ejected moments before.
evt-12-08-1988-united-states-air-force.prompt: What follows for US low-level training flights over West German towns after the crash?

choices.text: The pilot is court-martialed and imprisoned for the crash
USAFE faces pressure and tightens restrictions on low-level flights over populated areas
The entire A-10 fleet in Europe is permanently retired within weeks
West Germany bans all American military flights outright

evt-12-08-1988-united-states-air-force.butterflyEffect: The crash killed several residents on the ground and set off widespread German public anger over low-altitude training flights near populated areas. USAFE faced mounting political pressure that led to tighter restrictions on where and how low American aircraft could fly over West Germany.

evt-12-08-1991-belovezha-accords.scenario: You are an aide inside the state dacha near Viskuli in Belarus on 8 December 1991, as Yeltsin, Kravchuk, and Shushkevich sign documents that will reshape a continent.
evt-12-08-1991-belovezha-accords.prompt: What did the leaders declare in the Belovezha Accords?

choices.text: That a new Soviet constitution would preserve the union
That the Warsaw Pact would be renewed under new leadership
That Ukraine would remain permanently within the USSR
That the USSR had ceased to exist, replaced by the Commonwealth of Independent States

evt-12-08-1991-belovezha-accords.butterflyEffect: The three leaders declared that the Soviet Union had effectively ceased to exist and established the Commonwealth of Independent States in its place. Days later, eight more former Soviet republics joined via the Alma-Ata Protocol, and on 25 December 1991 Gorbachev resigned, formally ending the USSR.

evt-12-08-1991-belarus.scenario: You are an aide waiting outside a hunting lodge in the Belovezhskaya Pushcha forest on 8 December 1991, as the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus meet in secret, bypassing Soviet President Gorbachev entirely.
evt-12-08-1991-belarus.prompt: What does the agreement signed inside actually declare?

choices.text: That the three republics will renegotiate a new union treaty with Gorbachev as president
That a nationwide referendum will decide the Union's fate
That Belarus alone will secede while Russia and Ukraine remain in the Union
That the Soviet Union no longer exists and a new Commonwealth of Independent States replaces it

evt-12-08-1991-belarus.butterflyEffect: The Belovezha Accords declared that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist and created the Commonwealth of Independent States in its place. Gorbachev resigned as Soviet president on 25 December, and within days the USSR formally dissolved into fifteen independent states.

evt-12-08-2004-columbus-nightclub-shooti.scenario: It is 8 December 2004 at the Alrosa Villa nightclub in Columbus, Ohio. During the opening song of Damageplan's set, a gunman has rushed the stage, shot several people, and is now holding a hostage as police arrive.
evt-12-08-2004-columbus-nightclub-shooti.prompt: What should the responding officer do to end the standoff and stop further harm?

choices.text: Evacuate the crowd and leave the gunman contained until SWAT arrives
Cut power to the venue to create confusion and retreat
Move in and use lethal force to stop the immediate threat to the hostage
Negotiate patiently and wait for the gunman to surrender

evt-12-08-2004-columbus-nightclub-shooti.butterflyEffect: Officer James Niggemeyer shot and killed the gunman, Nathan Gale, ending the attack that had already claimed four lives, including guitarist "Dimebag" Darrell Abbott. The shooting devastated the heavy metal community, ended any hope of a Pantera reunion, and pushed venues nationwide to tighten stage security.

evt-12-08-2010-ikaros.scenario: You are a JAXA engineer in Sagamihara, tracking IKAROS as it sails past Venus at 80,800 km on 8 December 2010. The craft's shimmering membrane is doing more than just catching sunlight for thrust.
evt-12-08-2010-ikaros.prompt: What second function did IKAROS's sail membrane perform besides propulsion?

choices.text: Acting as a radio communications dish
Shielding the craft from cosmic radiation
Serving as a mounting surface for cameras only
Generating electrical power through embedded thin-film solar cells

evt-12-08-2010-ikaros.butterflyEffect: IKAROS combined a photon-driven solar sail with thin-film solar cells embedded in the membrane, generating electricity while also providing thrust. This hybrid demonstration proved solar sails could power and propel deep-space probes simultaneously, influencing later sail concepts like NASA's proposed OKEANOS and other lightweight interplanetary designs.

evt-12-08-2013-little-india-singapore.scenario: You are a shopkeeper in Singapore's Little India on the evening of 8 December 2013, watching a crowd swell around a stalled private bus that has just struck and killed a construction worker.
evt-12-08-2013-little-india-singapore.prompt: What did the gathered crowd of migrant workers do in the aftermath?

choices.text: They organised a formal petition to the Ministry of Manpower
They held a silent candlelight vigil and dispersed peacefully
They assisted paramedics and went home quietly
They rioted, overturning and setting fire to vehicles including the bus

evt-12-08-2013-little-india-singapore.butterflyEffect: The crowd's anger boiled into Singapore's first riot in over four decades, with vehicles overturned and burned before police restored order. The unrest triggered a government inquiry, tighter alcohol-sale restrictions in the area, and a broader public reckoning with the living and working conditions of the city-state's migrant labour force.

evt-12-08-2024-fall-of-damascus-2024.scenario: You wake in Damascus on 8 December 2024 to find state television off the air and videos circulating of rebel fighters walking through the halls of the presidential palace.
evt-12-08-2024-fall-of-damascus-2024.prompt: What has just happened to end over five decades of Assad family rule?

choices.text: International peacekeepers arrive to enforce a truce before rebels advance
Assad flees to Moscow as rebel forces take the capital
Assad negotiates a power-sharing government with the opposition
The Syrian army launches a successful counteroffensive to retake the city

evt-12-08-2024-fall-of-damascus-2024.butterflyEffect: Rebel forces swept into Damascus as Syrian troops withdrew, and President Bashar al-Assad fled by air to Moscow, where Russia granted him asylum. His departure ended more than fifty years of Assad family rule and plunged Syria into an uncertain transition among rival armed factions.

evt-12-09-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is 9 December 1775 near Great Bridge, Virginia. You serve under Lord Dunmore, whose Loyalist force has just been routed by Patriot militia defending a narrow causeway south of Norfolk.
evt-12-09-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What did Dunmore's defeat here force him to do next?

choices.text: March inland to join Cornwallis's army
Abandon Norfolk and retreat to British ships
Negotiate a truce with the Virginia militia
Surrender his commission to the Continental Congress

evt-12-09-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: After the loss at Great Bridge, Dunmore evacuated Norfolk and took refuge with British forces aboard ships in the harbor, later bombarding and burning the town on New Year's Eve 1775. The defeat effectively ended royal government in Virginia and pushed the colony firmly toward the Patriot cause.

evt-12-09-1892-association-football.scenario: You sit on a football club committee in Newcastle in 1892, watching two rival local sides, East End and West End, struggle separately with debts and thin crowds while the city's footballing future hangs in the balance.
evt-12-09-1892-association-football.prompt: What do the two clubs decide to do to secure their survival?

choices.text: Form a new regional league to keep both clubs separate
Merge into a single club, Newcastle United
Merge with a Sunderland club instead
Both clubs disband and Newcastle goes without senior football

evt-12-09-1892-association-football.butterflyEffect: The two clubs merged to form Newcastle United, which soon moved into St James' Park and became one of England's dominant early clubs, winning multiple league titles and FA Cups in the following decades. The merger set the template for a single, unified football identity for the city that endures today.

evt-12-09-1897-marguerite-durand.scenario: You are Marguerite Durand, a former actress turned journalist, launching a daily Paris newspaper on 9 December 1897. You want it to prove women can run every part of a serious publication, not just write about fashion.
evt-12-09-1897-marguerite-durand.prompt: What did Durand do to make La Fronde unlike any paper before it?

choices.text: Staff the entire paper - writing, editing and printing - with women
Hire men to write under female pen names for credibility
Publish the paper anonymously to avoid public backlash
Focus the paper solely on fashion and high society gossip

evt-12-09-1897-marguerite-durand.butterflyEffect: La Fronde was staffed entirely by women, from reporters and editors down to the typesetters and printers, covering politics, labor, and economics as seriously as any male-run daily. It gave the French suffrage movement a powerful platform and proved women could operate a major newspaper end to end, inspiring later women-led press across Europe.

evt-12-09-1911-cross-mountain-mine-disas.scenario: It is 9 December 1911 near Briceville, Tennessee. A roof fall deep underground has just ignited coal dust and methane, and rescue crews from the newly formed federal mining bureau are rushing to organize a response.
evt-12-09-1911-cross-mountain-mine-disas.prompt: What made this disaster's rescue effort historically notable?

choices.text: It prompted the founding of the United Mine Workers union
It led to the immediate abolition of coal mining in Tennessee
It was the first mine disaster caught on film
It was the first rescue coordinated by the new federal Bureau of Mines

evt-12-09-1911-cross-mountain-mine-disas.butterflyEffect: Eighty-four miners died at Cross Mountain, but the rescue was led by the U.S. Bureau of Mines, created only months earlier in 1910. The disaster became an early test of the federal government's new role in mine safety, spurring further investigation into dust and gas hazards and open-flame lamps.

evt-12-09-1917-world-war-i.scenario: It is dawn on 9 December 1917. You are Hussein al-Husayni, Ottoman mayor of Jerusalem. Ottoman forces have withdrawn overnight, and British troops under Allenby are closing in on the city.
evt-12-09-1917-world-war-i.prompt: What should the mayor do to spare Jerusalem from a fight?

choices.text: Order the remaining garrison to defend the walls to the last man
Flee the city along with departing Ottoman officials
Appeal to German advisors for emergency reinforcements
Surrender the city peacefully to the advancing British troops

evt-12-09-1917-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Al-Husayni went out with a white flag and, after two British sergeants foraging for eggs twice declined to accept a city's surrender, an officer finally took it. Jerusalem fell without a shot; Allenby entered on foot two days later out of respect for the holy city, ending four centuries of Ottoman rule and setting the stage for the British Mandate of Palestine.

evt-12-09-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is early December 1940 in the Western Desert. You command British and Commonwealth forces facing a much larger Italian Tenth Army dug into fortified camps near Sidi Barrani, Egypt.
evt-12-09-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: Heavily outnumbered, what should you order to seize the initiative?

choices.text: Wait for the full Eighth Army to assemble before engaging
Launch a surprise attack through gaps between the Italian camps
Withdraw to fortify the defense of Alexandria
Negotiate a local truce to avoid heavy losses

evt-12-09-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: General O'Connor launched a surprise attack exploiting gaps between the isolated Italian camps, and what was meant as a five-day raid became a rout. British forces advanced hundreds of miles into Libya, capturing over 130,000 Italian prisoners. The collapse forced Hitler to dispatch Rommel's Afrika Korps, opening the seesaw desert campaign that would last until 1943.

evt-12-09-1948-united-nations-general-as.scenario: You are a delegate at the UN General Assembly in Paris in December 1948, only a few years removed from the revelations of the Holocaust, debating how the world should legally define and punish the deliberate destruction of a people.
evt-12-09-1948-united-nations-general-as.prompt: What treaty do you vote to adopt on this day?

choices.text: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
The Nuremberg Principles codification
The Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide
The Refugee Convention

evt-12-09-1948-united-nations-general-as.butterflyEffect: The General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, which entered into force in 1951 as the first human rights treaty adopted by the UN. It gave the world a legal definition of genocide, though full enforcement mechanisms only matured decades later with tribunals like the ICTY and ICTR.

evt-12-09-1961-tanganyika-territory.scenario: You stand in Dar es Salaam on 9 December 1961 as the Union Jack comes down after decades of British trusteeship, and a young leader named Julius Nyerere prepares to lead the new nation.
evt-12-09-1961-tanganyika-territory.prompt: What did Tanganyika's independence set in motion just a few years later?

choices.text: Union with Zanzibar to form Tanzania
A civil war with neighboring Kenya
Rejoining the British Commonwealth as a dependency
Partition into two separate republics

evt-12-09-1961-tanganyika-territory.butterflyEffect: Tanganyika became independent under Nyerere, and in 1964 it united with the islands of Zanzibar to form the United Republic of Tanzania. Nyerere went on to pursue his ujamaa policy of African socialism, shaping the country's politics for decades.

evt-12-09-1965-kecksburg-ufo-incident.scenario: It is the evening of 9 December 1965 in Kecksburg, Pennsylvania. Neighbors describe a blazing fireball streaking down into the woods behind your farm, and now military vehicles are rolling in to seal off the site.
evt-12-09-1965-kecksburg-ufo-incident.prompt: What did officials tell residents after searching the crash site in the woods?

choices.text: They confirmed it was a downed Soviet spacecraft and returned it to the USSR
They immediately released the object to independent scientists for study
They found nothing unusual, likely just a meteor burning up
They announced it was a classified American weather balloon

evt-12-09-1965-kecksburg-ufo-incident.butterflyEffect: The military removed something from the woods but publicly stated nothing was found, and astronomers suggested a meteor. Decades later NASA admitted debris was analyzed and possibly linked to the Soviet satellite Kosmos 96, but the records were lost. The unresolved mystery made Kecksburg famous in ufology as "Pennsylvania's Roswell."

evt-12-09-1968-douglas-engelbart.scenario: You sit in a packed San Francisco auditorium on 9 December 1968, watching Douglas Engelbart on a giant screen manipulate text and windows on a distant computer from his stage podium.
evt-12-09-1968-douglas-engelbart.prompt: What small handheld device does Engelbart use to control the on-screen cursor?

choices.text: A light pen touched directly to the screen
A voice-command microphone
A joystick borrowed from arcade games
A wired computer mouse

evt-12-09-1968-douglas-engelbart.butterflyEffect: The device was the computer mouse, demonstrated alongside hypertext, video conferencing, and windowed displays in what became known as the Mother of All Demos. It directly inspired Xerox PARC's Alto and, later, the graphical interfaces of the Apple Macintosh and Microsoft Windows. Personal computing's visual, point-and-click future was previewed that day, decades before it became standard.

evt-12-09-1969-william-p-rogers.scenario: You are U.S. Secretary of State William Rogers on 9 December 1969, unveiling a plan calling for Israel to withdraw from territories captured in the 1967 war in exchange for peace agreements with its Arab neighbors.
evt-12-09-1969-william-p-rogers.prompt: How did the parties in the region respond to the Rogers Plan?

choices.text: Both Israel and the Arab governments rejected the plan
Israel accepted it while every Arab government rejected it
Egypt and Israel both signed the plan within weeks
The United Nations adopted it as binding international law

evt-12-09-1969-william-p-rogers.butterflyEffect: Both Israel and the Arab states rejected the plan, Israel because it demanded withdrawal without guaranteed security, and Arab governments because accepting it implied recognizing Israel. Though it failed immediately, its 'land for peace' formula became the diplomatic template later used at Camp David and in subsequent Middle East negotiations.

evt-12-09-1979-world-health-organization.scenario: It is late 1979, and you sit on the international commission reviewing years of vaccination and surveillance records from across the globe, searching for any sign the virus still survives in the human population.
evt-12-09-1979-world-health-organization.prompt: What does the commission formally certify?

choices.text: That smallpox has been eradicated from the human population
That measles has been eradicated from the human population
That a new vaccine for smallpox has been approved
That polio has been eradicated from the human population

evt-12-09-1979-world-health-organization.butterflyEffect: The commission concluded that smallpox had been eradicated worldwide, and the WHO officially endorsed this in 1980. Smallpox remains the only human infectious disease ever eradicated, and the campaign's ring-vaccination strategy became a model for later efforts against polio and other diseases.

evt-12-09-2008-rod-blagojevich.scenario: It is the early hours of 9 December 2008 in Chicago. Federal investigators hold wiretap recordings of Governor Rod Blagojevich discussing how to profit from appointing Barack Obama's vacated U.S. Senate seat.
evt-12-09-2008-rod-blagojevich.prompt: What did federal prosecutors do with this evidence?

choices.text: Quietly refer the matter to the Illinois legislature only
Offer him immunity in exchange for immediate resignation
Wait until he left office voluntarily before filing charges
Arrest Blagojevich immediately on federal corruption charges

evt-12-09-2008-rod-blagojevich.butterflyEffect: Blagojevich was arrested and charged with corruption that morning. The Illinois legislature impeached and removed him from office weeks later, and he was ultimately convicted on multiple felony counts and sentenced to 14 years, making him a national symbol of Illinois political corruption before being granted clemency in 2020.

evt-12-09-2017-marriage-amendment-defini.scenario: It is 9 December 2017 in Canberra, and after months of a national postal survey and parliamentary debate, you and thousands of other Australians are waiting to hear whether the marriage law has finally changed.
evt-12-09-2017-marriage-amendment-defini.prompt: What happens the moment the bill receives royal assent?

choices.text: Same-sex marriage becomes legally recognised across Australia
The change must still be approved by a national referendum
Each state parliament must separately ratify the law
The High Court must first review the law before it takes effect

evt-12-09-2017-marriage-amendment-defini.butterflyEffect: Same-sex marriage became legal in Australia immediately upon royal assent, and the first weddings took place within weeks, in January 2018. Australia joined a growing list of nations recognising marriage equality, following a divisive but decisive national postal survey.

evt-12-09-2019-whakaari-white-island.scenario: You are a rescue helicopter pilot near Whakaari/White Island on 9 December 2019, minutes after the volcano erupts while tour groups are still on the crater floor.
evt-12-09-2019-whakaari-white-island.prompt: What did rescuers face as they moved to help those on the island?

choices.text: Find the volcano had already fully calmed with no ongoing danger
Weigh rescuing survivors against the risk of another eruption and toxic ash
Receive orders to abandon all rescue efforts and stay offshore
Discover the island had been evacuated hours before the eruption

evt-12-09-2019-whakaari-white-island.butterflyEffect: Responders had to weigh saving the injured against the real danger of a second eruption and toxic gases, delaying full recovery efforts. The disaster led New Zealand authorities to prosecute the island's owners and tour operators under workplace safety law, and prompted a wider reassessment of guided tourism to active volcanoes worldwide.

evt-12-10-1508-papal-states.scenario: You advise Pope Julius II in December 1508, as Rome joins old rivals France, Aragon, and the Holy Roman Empire in a startling new alliance against a common neighbor.
evt-12-10-1508-papal-states.prompt: What is the shared goal binding these unlikely allies together?

choices.text: To drive the Ottoman Turks out of the eastern Mediterranean
To unify the Italian peninsula under papal authority
To defend Venice against an Ottoman invasion
To partition the mainland territories of Venice among themselves

evt-12-10-1508-papal-states.butterflyEffect: The League of Cambrai aimed to dismember the Republic of Venice, and it succeeded spectacularly at the Battle of Agnadello in 1509. But Julius II, fearing French power more than Venetian, soon switched sides and formed the Holy League against France, plunging Italy into decades of shifting alliances and prolonged warfare.

evt-12-10-1684-edmond-halley.scenario: Months ago you rode to Cambridge and asked Isaac Newton what curve a planet would trace under an inverse-square force of gravity. He answered instantly: an ellipse. Now, in December 1684, you present his written proof, De motu corporum in gyrum, to the Royal Society.
evt-12-10-1684-edmond-halley.prompt: What do you urge Newton to do with this result?

choices.text: Publish it immediately in French for a wider readership
Expand it into a complete treatise on the laws of motion
Keep it secret to protect his claim to priority
Challenge Robert Hooke to a public debate over who discovered it first

evt-12-10-1684-edmond-halley.butterflyEffect: Halley pressed and financially backed Newton to expand the short tract into a full treatise. The result, published in 1687 as Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica, laid out the laws of motion and universal gravitation and became one of the foundational works of modern science.

evt-12-10-1768-first-edition-of-the-ency.scenario: It is 1768 in Edinburgh, and you are backing printer Colin Macfarquhar and engraver Andrew Bell's ambitious plan for a new three-volume reference work, but few readers can afford a bound encyclopedia outright.
evt-12-10-1768-first-edition-of-the-ency.prompt: How do Macfarquhar and Bell get the first edition into readers' hands?

choices.text: Fund the whole project through a royal subsidy
Offer only lavish bound sets priced for the aristocracy
Raise money through a public subscription lottery
Sell it unbound in cheap serial installments over several years

evt-12-10-1768-first-edition-of-the-ency.butterflyEffect: They sold the Encyclopædia Britannica unbound, in affordable weekly installments over three years, making the ambitious project financially viable. That format helped launch what became the longest continuously published encyclopedia in the English language, printed for over two centuries before moving fully online in 2012.

evt-12-10-1848-napoleon-iii.scenario: It is 10 December 1848 and you are casting your ballot in France's first-ever direct presidential election, choosing between General Cavaignac, the poet Lamartine, and the nephew of the old Emperor, Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte.
evt-12-10-1848-napoleon-iii.prompt: Who wins this historic election by an overwhelming margin?

choices.text: Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte
General Louis-Eugène Cavaignac
Alexandre Ledru-Rollin
Alphonse de Lamartine

evt-12-10-1848-napoleon-iii.butterflyEffect: Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte won roughly three-quarters of the vote on the strength of his family name. Within three years he staged a coup against the legislature, and in 1852 declared himself Emperor Napoleon III, ruling France for two decades and reshaping its cities and empire.
