evt-12-10-1861-nguyen-trung-truc.scenario: You fight alongside Nguyễn Trung Trực on the Nhật Tảo river on 10 December 1861, watching a French gunboat anchored nearby as darkness falls over the Mekong Delta.
evt-12-10-1861-nguyen-trung-truc.prompt: What tactic does the militia use to strike the French vessel?

choices.text: A night ambush that sets the gunboat ablaze
A direct assault using captured French rifles
Negotiating the gunboat's peaceful surrender
Poisoning the crew's water supply

evt-12-10-1861-nguyen-trung-truc.butterflyEffect: Nguyễn Trung Trực's men staged a night ambush and set fire to the French gunboat L'Espérance, one of the most celebrated acts of Vietnamese resistance to colonial conquest. Though he was eventually captured and executed in 1868, the raid made him a lasting symbol of anti-colonial defiance still honored in Vietnam today.

evt-12-10-1884-adventures-of-huckleberry.scenario: You are a librarian in Concord, Massachusetts, in early 1885, holding a freshly printed copy of Mark Twain's Adventures of Huckleberry Finn and deciding whether it belongs on your shelves.
evt-12-10-1884-adventures-of-huckleberry.prompt: What do you decide to do with the newly published novel?

choices.text: Immediately praise it as the great American novel
Ban it as unsuitable, coarse trash for young readers
Shelve it quietly as unremarkable children's fiction
Send it back to the publisher unread

evt-12-10-1884-adventures-of-huckleberry.butterflyEffect: The Concord Public Library banned the book in 1885, calling it "trash" fit only for the slums, due to Huck's vernacular grammar and morally ambiguous content. The controversy only fueled public curiosity and sales, and the novel went on to be hailed as one of the Great American Novels, while remaining a recurring flashpoint in debates over language, race, and censorship.

evt-12-10-1890-new-york-world-building.scenario: You are a reporter for Joseph Pulitzer's New York World in 1890, standing on Park Row as the paper's new headquarters opens, its gilded dome rising higher than anything else in the city.
evt-12-10-1890-new-york-world-building.prompt: What record does the New York World Building claim upon its completion?

choices.text: Tallest building in New York City
Tallest building on the entire East Coast for a century
First fully steel-framed skyscraper
First building with electric elevators anywhere

evt-12-10-1890-new-york-world-building.butterflyEffect: It became the tallest building in New York City, the first to surpass the spire of Trinity Church, and by some measures the tallest in the world. Its success fueled the skyscraper race on Newspaper Row, though it was eventually eclipsed and demolished in 1955 to widen an approach to the Brooklyn Bridge.

evt-12-10-1901-alfred-nobel.scenario: You stand in Stockholm on 10 December 1901, the fifth anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death, as the very first Nobel Prizes are awarded according to his will.
evt-12-10-1901-alfred-nobel.prompt: Who receives the first Nobel Peace Prize awarded this day?

choices.text: Theodore Roosevelt
Bertha von Suttner
Henry Dunant and Frédéric Passy
Woodrow Wilson

evt-12-10-1901-alfred-nobel.butterflyEffect: Henry Dunant, founder of the Red Cross, and Frédéric Passy, a leading pacifist, shared the inaugural Peace Prize. The ceremony launched an annual tradition that would grow into the world's most prestigious recognition across science, literature, and peace, permanently tying Nobel's dynamite fortune to humanitarian and intellectual achievement.

evt-12-10-1907-brown-dog-affair.scenario: You march through London in December 1907 with anti-vivisection protesters heading for the bronze statue of the Brown Dog, while hundreds of medical students converge from the opposite direction determined to tear it down.
evt-12-10-1907-brown-dog-affair.prompt: What happens when the two crowds meet?

choices.text: The statue is toppled without any police response
The two crowds merge peacefully and disperse
Police charge in to break up a violent clash
The students petition Parliament instead of protesting

evt-12-10-1907-brown-dog-affair.butterflyEffect: The confrontation erupted into what newspapers called the Brown Dog riots, with mounted police battling students and protesters through the streets and making dozens of arrests. The unrest pushed the government to establish a Royal Commission on vivisection, and the statue itself was quietly removed by the council in 1910 to end the disorder.

evt-12-10-1911-calbraith-perry-rodgers.scenario: You are Calbraith Perry Rodgers, having just landed your Vin Fiz biplane in California on 5 November 1911, completing the first flight across the continent after dozens of crashes and repairs along the way. Reporters swarm you, celebrating a new American hero of the air.
evt-12-10-1911-calbraith-perry-rodgers.prompt: What happens to Rodgers in the months following his triumphant flight?

choices.text: He becomes a test pilot for the U.S. Army Air Service
He attempts a transatlantic flight the following year
He dies in a crash during an exhibition flight in California
He retires from flying to write his memoirs

evt-12-10-1911-calbraith-perry-rodgers.butterflyEffect: Rodgers died in April 1912 when his plane crashed into the Pacific surf near Long Beach during an exhibition flight, only months after his transcontinental fame. His death underscored how dangerous early aviation remained even for its most celebrated pioneers, and his Vin Fiz flight nonetheless stood as a landmark proving cross-country air travel was possible.

evt-12-10-1932-emu-war.scenario: It's December 1932 in Western Australia. For weeks soldiers armed with Lewis guns have tried to drive off the emus trampling wheat farms, but the birds have scattered and proven almost impossible to hit in numbers.
evt-12-10-1932-emu-war.prompt: What does the Australian government ultimately decide?

choices.text: Negotiate a truce with farmers to abandon the affected crops
Deploy poison bait across the entire wheat belt
Withdraw the troops and end the military operation
Escalate the campaign with more machine guns and aircraft

evt-12-10-1932-emu-war.butterflyEffect: The army withdrew its troops, having expended thousands of rounds for a modest number of emus killed. Farmers later turned to exclusion fencing and a government bounty system, which proved far more effective at controlling the birds long-term.

evt-12-10-1936-edward-viii.scenario: It is 10 December 1936. As King, you have told the Cabinet you cannot continue your duties unless you may marry Wallis Simpson, a twice-divorced American the Church of England and government refuse to accept as queen.
evt-12-10-1936-edward-viii.prompt: What do you decide to do?

choices.text: Sign the instrument of abdication and step down as king
Renounce the marriage and remain on the throne
Marry Simpson secretly while remaining king
Dissolve Parliament and call a referendum on the marriage

evt-12-10-1936-edward-viii.butterflyEffect: Edward signed the instrument of abdication the next day and became Duke of Windsor. His brother, crowned George VI, led the monarchy through the Second World War, setting the family line that led to Elizabeth II's decades-long reign.

evt-12-10-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It is dawn on 10 December 1941 off the coast of Malaya. You are a lookout aboard HMS Repulse, watching wave after wave of Japanese aircraft approach, with no friendly fighters overhead to intercept them.
evt-12-10-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: What happens to the British capital ships in this attack?

choices.text: Anti-aircraft fire destroys most of the attacking planes
The ships outrun the bombers and reach Singapore safely
Japanese aircraft sink both ships with torpedoes and bombs
RAF fighters arrive in time to drive off the attack

evt-12-10-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Japanese torpedo bombers sank both HMS Prince of Wales and HMS Repulse, killing over 800 sailors including Admiral Tom Phillips. It was the first time capital ships had been sunk at sea by aircraft alone, proving air power's dominance over battleships and shocking Allied naval strategy for the rest of the war.

evt-12-10-1942-edward-bernard-raczynski.scenario: It is December 1942. As foreign minister of the Polish government-in-exile, you hold eyewitness reports of the mass deportation and murder of Jews under German occupation, and must decide how to bring this to the Allied governments' attention.
evt-12-10-1942-edward-bernard-raczynski.prompt: What formal step do you take?

choices.text: Request a private, unpublicized meeting with Churchill alone
Release the information only through the Polish underground press
Wait for further confirmation before informing any government
Issue a diplomatic note detailing the atrocities and appeal to the Allies for action

evt-12-10-1942-edward-bernard-raczynski.butterflyEffect: Raczyński's note of 10 December 1942 became the first official Allied document to describe the systematic extermination of Jews and to appeal for action. It helped prompt the joint Allied declaration of 17 December 1942 condemning the atrocities, though little concrete rescue effort followed.

evt-12-10-1948-universal-declaration-of-.scenario: It is 10 December 1948 at the Palais de Chaillot in Paris. You sit among delegates from the UN's 58 member states as Eleanor Roosevelt presents the finished Universal Declaration of Human Rights for a vote.
evt-12-10-1948-universal-declaration-of-.prompt: What is the result when the General Assembly votes on the Declaration?

choices.text: It is unanimously adopted without objection
It fails to reach the required majority
It passes 48–0 with 8 abstentions
The vote is postponed for further drafting

evt-12-10-1948-universal-declaration-of-.butterflyEffect: The Declaration passed 48 in favour, none against, with 8 abstentions (including the Soviet bloc and Saudi Arabia). Though not legally binding, it became the template for later binding treaties and national constitutions worldwide, and every UN member has since ratified at least one covenant it inspired.

evt-12-10-1967-otis-redding.scenario: It is the evening of December 10, 1967, and you are a member of the Bar-Kays boarding Otis Redding's twin-engine plane in dense fog, bound for a show in Madison, Wisconsin.

choices.text: The plane was grounded and the concert was rescheduled
The flight landed safely and the show went on as planned
The plane crashed into Lake Monona, killing Redding and most of the band
The plane made an emergency landing with no injuries

evt-12-10-1967-otis-redding.butterflyEffect: The plane crashed into icy Lake Monona, killing Redding and four of the Bar-Kays; only one bandmember survived. Weeks later his label released the song he had just finished recording, "(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay," which became his first and only number-one hit, posthumously cementing his legacy.

evt-12-10-1983-raul-alfonsin.scenario: It is December 10, 1983, and you have just been sworn in as Argentina's first freely elected president after years of brutal military rule. Thousands of citizens remain missing, and the outgoing generals warn against digging into the past.
evt-12-10-1983-raul-alfonsin.prompt: What is Alfonsín's most urgent move to confront the crimes of the military dictatorship?

choices.text: Quietly exile the generals without any public trial
Focus solely on economic recovery and leave the past uninvestigated
Establish a truth commission and prosecute the former junta leaders
Grant the military a blanket amnesty to secure a peaceful transition

evt-12-10-1983-raul-alfonsin.butterflyEffect: Alfonsín created CONADEP to document the disappeared and put the former junta leaders on trial in 1985, making Argentina the first Latin American nation to prosecute its own military rulers. The precedent later wavered under amnesty laws, but those laws were overturned in the 2000s, and the trials became a model for transitional justice worldwide.

evt-12-10-1989-tsakhiagiin-elbegdorj.scenario: It is the evening of 10 December 1989 in Sükhbaatar Square, Ulaanbaatar. You stand among a few hundred people at Mongolia's first open pro-democracy rally, listening to young journalist Tsakhiagiin Elbegdorj denounce seventy years of one-party rule.
evt-12-10-1989-tsakhiagiin-elbegdorj.prompt: What does the gathered crowd demand?

choices.text: Return to a Buddhist theocratic government
Restoration of the Mongolian monarchy
Multi-party elections and an end to the Communist Party's monopoly on power
Immediate independence from the Soviet Union

evt-12-10-1989-tsakhiagiin-elbegdorj.butterflyEffect: Within weeks the protesters formed the Mongolian Democratic Union; by March 1990 the ruling Politburo resigned, and that July Mongolia held its first multi-party elections, ending communist rule peacefully. Elbegdorj went on to serve as prime minister and later president.

evt-12-10-1992-zayed-bin-sultan-al-nahya.scenario: It is 1992, and as an adviser to Sheikh Zayed you report that rising wedding costs and a preference among Emirati men for marrying foreign brides are shrinking the number of citizen marriages.
evt-12-10-1992-zayed-bin-sultan-al-nahya.prompt: What does Sheikh Zayed do to address the trend?

choices.text: Ban Emirati citizens from marrying foreign nationals outright
Impose a tax on households with foreign-born spouses
Create a fund granting financial support to Emirati men marrying Emirati women
Launch a state-run matchmaking service for young Emiratis

evt-12-10-1992-zayed-bin-sultan-al-nahya.butterflyEffect: Zayed established the Marriage Fund, offering grants to Emirati men who married Emirati women to ease financial barriers to marriage. The fund later expanded into mass wedding ceremonies and housing support, becoming a lasting institution aimed at preserving Emirati family identity amid rapid modernization.

evt-12-10-2021-edwardsville-amazon-wareh.scenario: It is the evening of December 10, 2021, and as a shift supervisor at the Amazon Edwardsville warehouse, you hear tornado sirens while packages are still being processed for the holiday rush.
evt-12-10-2021-edwardsville-amazon-wareh.prompt: What should you do to protect the workers on your shift?

choices.text: Wait for corporate headquarters to confirm before acting
Direct everyone immediately to the designated storm shelter area
Move workers to the break room near the windows
Keep processing orders until the shift officially ends

evt-12-10-2021-edwardsville-amazon-wareh.butterflyEffect: An EF3 tornado struck the facility minutes later, and the roof collapsed, killing six workers who had sheltered away from the marked storm shelter. OSHA later cited inadequate training on shelter locations, and Amazon overhauled its severe-weather protocols across its warehouse network.

evt-12-10-2021-tornado-outbreak-of-decem.scenario: It is the night of December 10, 2021, and you are a shift manager at a candle factory in Mayfield, Kentucky, as sirens warn of a long-track tornado bearing down in the dark.
evt-12-10-2021-tornado-outbreak-of-decem.prompt: What consequence followed this outbreak for workplaces caught in its path?

choices.text: Investigations and calls for stronger workplace severe-weather protections followed
Overnight shift work was immediately banned nationwide
No policy discussions resulted from the outbreak
The outbreak was later reclassified as a non-tornadic wind event

evt-12-10-2021-tornado-outbreak-of-decem.butterflyEffect: The tornado's overnight timing and extraordinary track length devastated factories and warehouses where workers were still on shift, prompting investigations into whether employees had been allowed to leave. The disaster fueled a national push for stronger workplace protections and clearer shelter protocols during severe weather warnings.

evt-12-11-861-abbasid-caliphate.scenario: It is night in the Abbasid palace at Samarra in 861. You are among the Turkish guardsmen who have grown resentful of Caliph al-Mutawakkil for favoring a younger son as heir over al-Muntasir, and the plot to strike has reached its final hour.
evt-12-11-861-abbasid-caliphate.prompt: What did the conspiring guards do to al-Mutawakkil that night?

choices.text: They imprisoned him but kept him as a figurehead
They forced him into peaceful exile
They pressured him into abdicating in favor of a rival dynasty
They assassinated him

evt-12-11-861-abbasid-caliphate.butterflyEffect: The guards assassinated al-Mutawakkil, and al-Muntasir was swiftly installed as caliph in his place. The killing opened the so-called Anarchy at Samarra, a decade of chaos in which Turkic military commanders made and deposed caliphs at will, permanently weakening central Abbasid authority.

evt-12-11-1886-association-football.scenario: It is 1886, and you work alongside fellow laborers at the Royal Arsenal armaments factory in Woolwich, London. Your workmates want to form a football team and need a name for their new club.
evt-12-11-1886-association-football.prompt: What name do the Woolwich workers choose for their new football club?

choices.text: Woolwich United
Dial Square
Royal Arsenal
Arsenal Rovers

evt-12-11-1886-association-football.butterflyEffect: The workers named their club Dial Square after the factory workshop where they were employed. It was soon renamed Royal Arsenal, then Woolwich Arsenal, and finally simply Arsenal — growing from a factory works team into one of English football's most decorated clubs.

evt-12-11-1899-second-boer-war.scenario: It is dawn on 11 December 1899, and you march with the British Highland Brigade toward Magersfontein Hill, expecting the Boer defenders to be dug in along the heights above.
evt-12-11-1899-second-boer-war.prompt: What tactical surprise awaits the advancing British troops at Magersfontein?

choices.text: The British found the hill undefended entirely
The Boers had entrenched at the hill's base instead of its summit
The Boers attacked with artillery from the open plain
The Boer forces had abandoned the position overnight

evt-12-11-1899-second-boer-war.butterflyEffect: General Piet Cronjé had ordered trenches dug at the base of the hill rather than its summit, and the unsuspecting Highlanders walked into devastating close-range fire at dawn. The defeat was one of three in Britain's disastrous "Black Week," forcing London to send massive reinforcements and rethink its tactics for the rest of the war.

evt-12-11-1907-parliament-house-wellingt.scenario: It's the early hours of 11 December 1907, and fire is roaring through Wellington's wooden Parliament House. You're one of the few staff on site as flames spread rapidly from the debating chamber toward the rest of the complex.
evt-12-11-1907-parliament-house-wellingt.prompt: What is your best move to save Parliament's most valuable holdings from the blaze?

choices.text: Break into the basement to save land title deeds
Try to douse the burning debating chamber with buckets of water
Direct all efforts toward the adjoining General Assembly Library, built to be fireproof
Rush to rescue the ceremonial mace and speaker's chair first

evt-12-11-1907-parliament-house-wellingt.butterflyEffect: The fire gutted the original Parliament House, but the adjoining General Assembly Library survived intact thanks to its fireproof construction, self-closing doors, and firebreak wall. A grand new Parliament House was built between 1914 and 1922 to replace the lost chambers, and the historic library still stands as part of the complex today.

evt-12-11-1972-apollo-17.scenario: You are geologist Harrison Schmitt on the lunar surface on 11 December 1972, kneeling beside Shorty Crater during Apollo 17's final moonwalk when you notice strikingly orange soil beneath your boots.
evt-12-11-1972-apollo-17.prompt: What should you do about this unexpected discovery before time runs out?

choices.text: Photograph it but leave it untouched to save time for other tasks
Report it to Houston but continue without collecting a sample
Assume it's a camera or lighting artifact and move on
Collect samples immediately, recognizing it may be volcanic in origin

evt-12-11-1972-apollo-17.butterflyEffect: The orange soil turned out to be tiny beads of volcanic glass, evidence of ancient fire-fountain eruptions on the Moon billions of years ago. As the only professional geologist to walk on the Moon, Schmitt's find reshaped understanding of lunar volcanic history and remains central to lunar science research today.

evt-12-11-1997-kyoto-protocol.scenario: It's 11 December 1997 in Kyoto. After nearly two weeks of tense negotiation, delegates from around the world must settle on a final agreement to curb greenhouse gas emissions blamed for global warming.

choices.text: An immediate worldwide ban on new coal power plants
Legally binding emissions reduction targets for developed countries
Voluntary emissions targets applying equally to every nation
A global carbon tax imposed on all fossil fuel producers

evt-12-11-1997-kyoto-protocol.butterflyEffect: The Kyoto Protocol set legally binding emissions targets for developed nations and entered into force in 2005. The United States never ratified it and Canada later withdrew, and its uneven reach eventually led negotiators to replace it with the broader 2015 Paris Agreement.

evt-12-11-2001-world-trade-organization.scenario: You are a Chinese trade official on 11 December 2001, the day China formally joins the World Trade Organization after fifteen years of negotiations and sweeping promises of market reform.
evt-12-11-2001-world-trade-organization.prompt: What follows for China's economy in the years after this accession?

choices.text: China's economy stays largely closed, with WTO membership having little effect
Foreign companies immediately dominate China's domestic market
China withdraws from the WTO within a few years amid internal opposition
Explosive growth in exports and investment turns China into the world's factory

evt-12-11-2001-world-trade-organization.butterflyEffect: WTO membership unleashed explosive growth in Chinese exports and foreign investment, transforming the country into the world's leading manufacturing hub within a decade. The shift reshaped global supply chains and trade balances, eventually fueling trade tensions with the United States and other economies decades later.

evt-12-11-2005-buncefield-fire.scenario: It's just after 6am on 11 December 2005, and a massive explosion has rocked the Buncefield oil depot near Hemel Hempstead, shattering windows for miles and sending a huge fireball into the sky.
evt-12-11-2005-buncefield-fire.prompt: What should nearby residents and emergency crews do in response to the blast?

choices.text: Wait for the fire to burn out with no precautions needed
Evacuate the surrounding area immediately given the risk of smoke and further blasts
Return home right away since the fire poses no danger to nearby buildings
Ignore official warnings and go outside to watch the fire

evt-12-11-2005-buncefield-fire.butterflyEffect: Despite the explosion destroying storage tanks and damaging hundreds of nearby buildings in one of Europe's largest peacetime fires, remarkably no one was killed, though dozens were injured. The disaster prompted major reforms to UK and EU fuel storage regulations, including stricter tank bunding and safety standards.

evt-12-11-2005-2005-cronulla-riots.scenario: It's the afternoon of 11 December 2005 at Cronulla Beach. Text messages calling for a mass gathering to "reclaim the beach" have brought thousands of people together, and the mood is turning ugly.
evt-12-11-2005-2005-cronulla-riots.prompt: What did the crowd's anger, fanned by radio and text chains, actually lead to that night?

choices.text: It turned into a peaceful multicultural festival
It dispersed peacefully once police arrived
It was cancelled after organisers called it off
It erupted into mob violence that spread to neighbouring suburbs over following nights

evt-12-11-2005-2005-cronulla-riots.butterflyEffect: The gathering exploded into violent mob attacks on people of Middle Eastern appearance, and over the following nights retaliatory violence spread to nearby suburbs like Maroubra. The riots triggered a national debate on multiculturalism and policing, and NSW introduced tougher laws restricting large impromptu gatherings and alcohol on beaches.

evt-12-11-2006-mexican-drug-war.scenario: You are President Felipe Calderón in December 2006, just days into office, facing surging cartel violence and open gun battles in Michoacán that local police cannot control.
evt-12-11-2006-mexican-drug-war.prompt: What action do you order to confront the escalating cartel violence?

choices.text: Deploy thousands of federal troops and police in a major offensive against the cartels
Negotiate a truce directly with cartel leaders
Withdraw federal forces and leave the matter to local police
Legalize marijuana nationwide to undercut cartel profits

evt-12-11-2006-mexican-drug-war.butterflyEffect: Calderón's decision launched a massive military offensive against the cartels that became known as the Mexican drug war, a conflict still ongoing today. Rather than ending the violence, the crackdown fragmented cartels into smaller, more violent factions, and the death toll climbed into the tens of thousands within a few years.

evt-12-11-2006-felipe-calderon.scenario: It is December 11, 2006, just ten days into your presidency. Drug cartel violence is spiraling in your home state of Michoacán, and you must decide how to respond.
evt-12-11-2006-felipe-calderon.prompt: What does President Calderón do to confront the cartels in Michoacán?

choices.text: Negotiate a truce directly with cartel leaders
Rely solely on increased funding for local police
Request that the United States military intervene directly
Deploy thousands of federal troops in a military-led offensive

evt-12-11-2006-felipe-calderon.butterflyEffect: Calderón deployed thousands of federal troops to Michoacán, launching what became known as the Mexican Drug War. The militarized strategy continued for years under his successors, contributing to a death toll estimated in the hundreds of thousands and reshaping Mexico's security policy for a generation.

evt-12-11-2008-bernie-madoff.scenario: It's the morning of 11 December 2008 in a Manhattan apartment. FBI agents have arrived at Bernard Madoff's door just a day after his own sons reported his stunning confession that his investment business was "one big lie."
evt-12-11-2008-bernie-madoff.prompt: What happened to Madoff that day?

choices.text: He was released without charges pending a settlement
He voluntarily surrendered his assets and avoided arrest
He was arrested and charged with securities fraud
He fled the country before agents arrived

evt-12-11-2008-bernie-madoff.butterflyEffect: Madoff was arrested and charged with securities fraud, exposing what proved to be the largest Ponzi scheme in history, worth an estimated $65 billion. He pleaded guilty in 2009 and was sentenced to 150 years in prison, and the scandal spurred tighter SEC oversight of investment advisers.

evt-12-11-2009-rovio-entertainment.scenario: You're a developer at Rovio on 11 December 2009, preparing to launch your studio's 52nd game after more than fifty previous titles failed to break through on the new App Store.
evt-12-11-2009-rovio-entertainment.prompt: What approach do you take to finally make this one succeed?

choices.text: Build a simple, addictive physics game with charismatic characters designed for touchscreens
License a Hollywood movie tie-in as the game's basis
Develop a multiplayer online battle game for early smartphones
Port an existing PC strategy game directly to mobile

evt-12-11-2009-rovio-entertainment.butterflyEffect: Angry Birds became one of the best-selling mobile game franchises in history, spawning sequels, movies, and merchandise while helping establish Finland as a global hub for mobile game development. Its success also helped popularize the simple, addictive touchscreen game format that defined the smartphone gaming boom.

evt-12-11-2017-2017-new-york-city-subway.scenario: It's rush hour on 11 December 2017 in a crowded passageway near Times Square and the Port Authority Bus Terminal. A pipe bomb strapped to a man's body has just gone off, and commuters are scrambling for the exits.
evt-12-11-2017-2017-new-york-city-subway.prompt: What actually happened to the bomber in the chaos immediately after the blast?

choices.text: He detonated a second device before being stopped
He was killed instantly by the blast
He fled the station and evaded capture for days
He was subdued and arrested at the scene by police

evt-12-11-2017-2017-new-york-city-subway.butterflyEffect: The bomb only partially detonated, injuring the bomber, Akayed Ullah, and three bystanders but killing no one. Police officers in the station subdued and arrested him at the scene; he was convicted in 2018 and sentenced to life in prison in 2021, and security was increased at major NYC transit hubs afterward.

evt-12-11-2020-food-and-drug-administrat.scenario: It's 11 December 2020. An FDA advisory panel has just voted in favour of a COVID-19 vaccine, and as commissioner you must decide whether to authorize it for emergency use amid intense public pressure to speed vaccinations.
evt-12-11-2020-food-and-drug-administrat.prompt: What did the FDA authorize that day?

choices.text: Emergency Use Authorization for the Johnson & Johnson vaccine
A delay of all vaccine decisions pending further trials
Emergency Use Authorization for the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine
Full approval for the Moderna vaccine

evt-12-11-2020-food-and-drug-administrat.butterflyEffect: The FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, the first such authorization in the US. Vaccinations began within days, kicking off the largest immunization campaign in American history and setting the pace for the global vaccine rollout race.

evt-12-12-627-battle-of-nineveh-627.scenario: You ride with Emperor Heraclius outside the ruins of ancient Nineveh in December 627, having pushed deep into Persian territory after years of grinding war between Byzantium and the Sasanian Empire.
evt-12-12-627-battle-of-nineveh-627.prompt: What is the outcome when Heraclius's army meets the main Sasanian field force here?

choices.text: The Persians win a decisive victory
Heraclius is forced into a full retreat
The Byzantines rout the main Persian army
The battle ends in a costly stalemate

evt-12-12-627-battle-of-nineveh-627.butterflyEffect: Heraclius won a crushing victory that shattered the Sasanian field army and opened the road to the Persian heartland. The defeat triggered the overthrow and murder of Khosrow II, forcing a peace that restored Byzantine territory—but both empires emerged so exhausted that they could barely resist the Arab conquests just a few years later.

evt-12-12-1866-oaks-explosion.scenario: It is 12 December 1866 at the Oaks Colliery near Barnsley. A firedamp explosion has just torn through the workings, and rescue parties are gathering at the pit head, uncertain whether it is safe to go below.
evt-12-12-1866-oaks-explosion.prompt: What do the rescue teams decide to do?

choices.text: Descend immediately to search for survivors despite the risk of further blasts
Wait a full day for gas levels to clear before entering
Flood the mine shaft to smother any remaining fire
Evacuate the area and abandon any rescue attempt

evt-12-12-1866-oaks-explosion.butterflyEffect: Rescuers, including the colliery's chief engineer, descended to search for survivors despite the danger, and a second explosion killed many of them, pushing the final toll past 360 — England's worst mining disaster. The catastrophe helped drive later reforms in mine ventilation, gas testing, and rescue procedure.

evt-12-12-1936-republic-of-china-1912-19.scenario: It's December 12, 1936, in Xi'an, and Marshal Zhang Xueliang's troops have just seized Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek from his headquarters at gunpoint.
evt-12-12-1936-republic-of-china-1912-19.prompt: What did Zhang demand from Chiang before agreeing to release him?

choices.text: Surrender of Nationalist forces to Japanese command
An end to the civil war and a united front against Japan
Full independence for Manchuria
Chiang's immediate resignation as Nationalist leader

evt-12-12-1936-republic-of-china-1912-19.butterflyEffect: Chiang agreed to end the civil war against the Communists and form a united front with them against Japan. That alliance shaped Chinese resistance through World War II, though the truce collapsed after Japan's defeat, leading to renewed civil war and eventual Communist victory in 1949.

evt-12-12-1939-royal-navy.scenario: It is the early hours of 12 December 1939. You are a lookout aboard the destroyer HMS Duchess, screening the battleship HMS Barham through blacked-out, wartime waters off the Scottish coast.
evt-12-12-1939-royal-navy.prompt: What happens when the two warships lose their bearings in the darkness?

choices.text: Both ships collide but suffer only minor, repairable damage
Barham is struck and sinks while Duchess escapes damage
The ships spot each other in time and the collision is avoided
Duchess collides with Barham and sinks with heavy loss of life

evt-12-12-1939-royal-navy.butterflyEffect: Duchess collided with Barham and capsized, sinking with the loss of 124 of her crew — one of the Royal Navy's worst accidental losses of the early war. The tragedy highlighted the dangers of night navigation under strict blackout conditions and reinforced scrutiny of station-keeping procedures within escort groups.

evt-12-12-1939-hms-duchess-h64.scenario: It's before dawn on 12 December 1939, and thick fog has swallowed the sea off Scotland as your destroyer, HMS Duchess, escorts the battleship HMS Barham home to British waters.
evt-12-12-1939-hms-duchess-h64.prompt: What happened to Duchess in the fog during this escort?

choices.text: Duchess ran aground on rocks in the fog
Duchess safely guided Barham through the strait
A German U-boat torpedoed Duchess
Barham accidentally rammed Duchess, sinking her with heavy loss of life

evt-12-12-1939-hms-duchess-h64.butterflyEffect: Barham, unable to see clearly in the fog, accidentally rammed and sank Duchess, killing 124 of her crew. The tragedy underscored how deadly friendly warships could be to each other even without enemy action, prompting reviews of fleet navigation procedures in poor visibility.

evt-12-12-1941-the-holocaust.scenario: It's December 12, 1941, in Berlin's Reich Chancellery, days after Germany declared war on the United States. Hitler addresses the assembled Nazi Party Gauleiters.
evt-12-12-1941-the-holocaust.prompt: What did Hitler communicate to party leaders at this meeting?

choices.text: Plans to negotiate peace with the Allies
A new military alliance with the Soviet Union
His resolve to annihilate the Jewish people entirely
A halt to anti-Jewish measures for wartime unity

evt-12-12-1941-the-holocaust.butterflyEffect: According to Goebbels' diary, Hitler declared his 'prophecy' fulfilled and signaled his resolve to annihilate the Jewish people entirely. Historians regard this speech as a pivotal moment before the Wannsee Conference formalized the machinery of the genocide, after which deportations to death camps accelerated sharply.

evt-12-12-1942-world-war-ii.scenario: It is 12 December 1942. You are General Friedrich Paulus, commanding the German Sixth Army trapped inside Stalingrad, as Field Marshal von Manstein launches Operation Winter Storm to punch a corridor through to you.
evt-12-12-1942-world-war-ii.prompt: With Manstein's tanks pushing toward the encirclement, what do you do?

choices.text: Break out immediately toward Manstein without orders from Hitler
Surrender to Soviet forces before Manstein arrives
Retreat west toward Rostov, abandoning Stalingrad entirely
Hold position inside Stalingrad, awaiting Hitler's authorization to break out

evt-12-12-1942-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Hitler refused to authorize a breakout, so Paulus held his ground awaiting permission that never came. Manstein's relief drive stalled short of the pocket, and by early February 1943 the isolated Sixth Army was forced to surrender, marking the first major German battlefield capitulation of the war.

evt-12-12-1945-people-s-republic-of-kore.scenario: It is December 1945 in occupied Seoul. You command the US Army Military Government in Korea, and the People's Republic of Korea's local committees are running much of the day-to-day administration across the southern zone—but Washington views their leftist leanings with alarm.
evt-12-12-1945-people-s-republic-of-kore.prompt: As the American military governor, what do you decide to do about the PRK's committees?

choices.text: Declare the PRK's organizations illegal and order them dissolved
Absorb the PRK's committees directly into the military government's administration
Formally recognize the PRK as Korea's legitimate government
Let the committees keep operating but strip them of any judicial authority

evt-12-12-1945-people-s-republic-of-kore.butterflyEffect: USAMGIK declared the People's Republic of Korea and its committees illegal, driving many organizers underground or toward open resistance. The crackdown deepened the split between left and right in the South, fueling the polarization that erupted into the Korean War five years later.

evt-12-12-1946-united-nations-security-c.scenario: It is December 1946 and you are Siam's ambassador in New York, waiting anxiously as the UN Security Council prepares to vote on your country's bid to join the fledgling United Nations after its wartime alignment with Japan.
evt-12-12-1946-united-nations-security-c.prompt: What does the Security Council decide on Siam's membership bid?

choices.text: Postpone the vote pending fresh elections in Bangkok
Refer the matter to the Assembly with no recommendation at all
Unanimously recommend admitting Siam to the General Assembly
Reject the bid over Siam's wartime alliance with Japan

evt-12-12-1946-united-nations-security-c.butterflyEffect: The Council unanimously recommended admitting Siam, and the General Assembly approved it soon after. Membership helped Thailand shed its wartime Axis-aligned reputation and re-enter the postwar international order as a recognized, sovereign state.

evt-12-12-1963-kenya.scenario: It is just after midnight on 12 December 1963 in Nairobi's stadium. You stand in the crowd as the Union Flag comes down and a new flag is raised over an independent Kenya.
evt-12-12-1963-kenya.prompt: Who is sworn in as Kenya's first prime minister at independence?

choices.text: Daniel arap Moi
Oginga Odinga
Jomo Kenyatta
Tom Mboya

evt-12-12-1963-kenya.butterflyEffect: Jomo Kenyatta, released from colonial detention only a few years earlier, became Kenya's first prime minister that night. He went on to lead Kenya to full republic status in 1964 as its first president, shaping the country's politics for the next fifteen years.

evt-12-12-1964-jomo-kenyatta.scenario: It is 12 December 1964 in Nairobi. You are a KANU delegate in the National Assembly as Kenya formally becomes a republic within the Commonwealth, and the chamber must choose the nation's first head of state.
evt-12-12-1964-jomo-kenyatta.prompt: Whom does the newly independent republic install as its first president?

choices.text: Daniel Moi
Jomo Kenyatta
Oginga Odinga
Tom Mboya

evt-12-12-1964-jomo-kenyatta.butterflyEffect: Jomo Kenyatta became Kenya's first president, a post he held until his death in 1978. His conservative, pro-Western policies and consolidation of KANU power set the template for decades of one-party dominance and the political rise of his successor, Daniel Moi.

evt-12-12-1969-greek-junta.scenario: It is December 1969 and you serve in the Greek foreign ministry. The Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers is about to vote on expelling Greece after a damning report on the junta's torture and human rights abuses.
evt-12-12-1969-greek-junta.prompt: What does the Greek government do to head off a formal expulsion vote?

choices.text: Ignore the vote and remain a member regardless
Appeal to NATO to block the expulsion vote
Announce Greece's withdrawal from the Council of Europe first
Accept the Council's demanded human rights reforms

evt-12-12-1969-greek-junta.butterflyEffect: Greece announced its withdrawal from the Council of Europe rather than face expulsion, becoming the first member state ever to leave the organization. The move deepened the junta's diplomatic isolation in Western Europe until democracy was restored in 1974 and Greece rejoined the Council.

evt-12-12-1969-piazza-fontana-bombing.scenario: It is the evening of 12 December 1969. You are an Italian investigator in Milan, under intense political pressure to name culprits quickly after the bombing at Piazza Fontana.
evt-12-12-1969-piazza-fontana-bombing.prompt: Who do the authorities initially arrest and publicly blame for the attack?

choices.text: Left-wing Red Brigades militants
Anarchists, including Pietro Valpreda
Foreign intelligence agents acting for Moscow
Neo-fascist Ordine Nuovo members

evt-12-12-1969-piazza-fontana-bombing.butterflyEffect: Police blamed anarchists, arresting dancer Pietro Valpreda; fellow anarchist Giuseppe Pinelli died falling from a police station window during questioning. Years later investigations revealed the bombing was the work of the neo-fascist Ordine Nuovo, part of a covert 'strategy of tension' with links to sympathetic state actors, fueling Italy's turbulent Years of Lead.

evt-12-12-1985-arrow-air-flight-1285r.scenario: It is the aftermath of the 12 December 1985 crash at Gander, and you are part of the Canadian Aviation Safety Board team examining the wreckage of the DC-8 that carried American soldiers home for the holidays.
evt-12-12-1985-arrow-air-flight-1285r.prompt: What did the board's majority report identify as the probable cause of the crash?

choices.text: A bomb planted by terrorists
Catastrophic engine failure on takeoff
Ice contamination on the wings reducing lift
Pilot error during rotation

evt-12-12-1985-arrow-air-flight-1285r.butterflyEffect: The majority report concluded that ice contamination on the wings reduced lift during takeoff, though a minority of the board dissented, believing evidence pointed to an inflight explosion. The disaster, still Canada's deadliest aviation accident, led to closer scrutiny of winter deicing procedures for military charter flights.

evt-12-12-1988-clapham-junction-rail-cra.scenario: It is the morning of 12 December 1988, moments before a crowded commuter train slams into another stopped near Clapham Junction. Investigators will soon comb through the signalling equipment to find out why the danger signal was never shown.
evt-12-12-1988-clapham-junction-rail-cra.prompt: What does the subsequent inquiry find caused the fatal signal failure?

choices.text: Driver error in failing to observe a red signal
A mechanical brake failure on the leading train
Incomplete rewiring work left untested by an overworked signal technician
A broken rail causing the train to derail into the other line

evt-12-12-1988-clapham-junction-rail-cra.butterflyEffect: The Hidden Inquiry found that a signal technician, working without a proper day off in weeks, had left an old wire connected during rewiring work that was never independently tested. The report's recommendations pushed British Rail toward automatic train protection systems and stricter limits on technicians' working hours.

evt-12-12-2000-supreme-court-of-the-unit.scenario: It's December 12, 2000, five weeks after election night ended without a clear winner. The Supreme Court is about to rule on whether Florida's manual ballot recount can continue.
evt-12-12-2000-supreme-court-of-the-unit.prompt: What did the Supreme Court ultimately decide about the Florida recount?

choices.text: Halted the recount, effectively deciding the election for Bush
Sent the case back to the Florida Supreme Court indefinitely
Ordered a full hand recount of every ballot in Florida
Ordered the recount to continue under uniform statewide standards

evt-12-12-2000-supreme-court-of-the-unit.butterflyEffect: The 5-4 ruling in Bush v. Gore halted the recount, effectively awarding Florida's electoral votes—and the presidency—to George W. Bush despite Al Gore winning the national popular vote. The decision remains one of the most debated exercises of judicial power in American history, fueling later pushes for election reform.

evt-12-12-2012-north-korea.scenario: It's December 12, 2012, at the Sohae launch site, and North Korean engineers watch the Unha-3 rocket lift off, months after a failed attempt earlier that year.
evt-12-12-2012-north-korea.prompt: What did the international community conclude from this successful launch?

choices.text: It demonstrated progress toward long-range missile technology
China declared the launch an act of war
It proved North Korea had abandoned missile development
It led directly to North Korea rejoining the UN Security Council

evt-12-12-2012-north-korea.butterflyEffect: The launch placed North Korea's first satellite into orbit but was widely viewed as cover for testing long-range ballistic missile technology. It drew fresh UN Security Council sanctions and marked a step toward the intercontinental missile tests North Korea would conduct in later years.

evt-12-12-2015-paris-agreement.scenario: It is the early hours of 12 December 2015 in Le Bourget, outside Paris. You are a delegate at COP21, and after two weeks of talks the final text is about to be gaveled through.
evt-12-12-2015-paris-agreement.prompt: What temperature goal do the 196 parties agree to enshrine in the final text?

choices.text: A ceiling of 3°C above pre-industrial levels
A strict, legally binding cap of 1°C
Well below 2°C, with efforts to limit warming to 1.5°C
No numeric target, only voluntary pledges

evt-12-12-2015-paris-agreement.butterflyEffect: Delegates adopted a goal of keeping warming well below 2°C, with efforts to pursue 1.5°C, and the agreement entered into force in 2016. Despite the historic consensus, global emissions kept rising afterward, and the accord became a recurring political flashpoint as the United States later withdrew and rejoined it more than once.

evt-12-12-2021-2021-abu-dhabi-grand-prix.scenario: It is the final laps of the 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. As race director, a late safety car for Nicholas Latifi's crash has bunched the field, with Max Verstappen on fresh tyres right behind championship leader Lewis Hamilton, and several lapped cars sitting between other drivers.
evt-12-12-2021-2021-abu-dhabi-grand-prix.prompt: How do you handle the lapped cars before restarting the race?

choices.text: Red-flag the race and restart from a standing grid
End the race under the safety car with no further racing laps
Allow only the lapped cars between the leaders to unlap themselves
Let all lapped cars unlap themselves before the restart

evt-12-12-2021-2021-abu-dhabi-grand-prix.butterflyEffect: Race director Michael Masi let only the five lapped cars directly between Hamilton and Verstappen unlap themselves, setting up a one-lap sprint on fresh rubber. Verstappen passed Hamilton to snatch his first world title, and the controversial call led the FIA to overhaul race-control procedures and remove Masi from the role.

evt-12-12-2021-formula-one.scenario: It's the final lap of the 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. A controversial late safety car restart has bunched the field, putting Max Verstappen on fresh tyres right behind championship rival Lewis Hamilton.
evt-12-12-2021-formula-one.prompt: What happened on that decisive final lap?

choices.text: The race was red-flagged and the result voided
Hamilton held off Verstappen to secure his eighth title
Verstappen crashed out, handing Hamilton the title
Verstappen overtook Hamilton to win his first world championship

evt-12-12-2021-formula-one.butterflyEffect: Verstappen overtook Hamilton to win his first world championship by a single point, ending Mercedes' dominant title run. The chaotic handling of the safety car restart sparked such controversy that the FIA overhauled its race-director procedures and later replaced race director Michael Masi.

evt-12-13-1294-pope-celestine-v.scenario: It is 13 December 1294. You are a cardinal in the papal court, where the elderly hermit-pope Celestine V, elected only five months earlier, has grown overwhelmed by the politics and administration of Rome.
evt-12-13-1294-pope-celestine-v.prompt: What did Celestine V do that no pope had done for centuries?

choices.text: He declared a new crusade before dying of illness
He voluntarily resigned the papacy to return to monastic life
He moved the papal seat permanently from Rome to Naples
He excommunicated the cardinals who had elected him

evt-12-13-1294-pope-celestine-v.butterflyEffect: Celestine V formally abdicated the papacy, an almost unheard-of act, and tried to return to his hermitage. His successor, Boniface VIII, had him imprisoned to prevent any rival claim, and Celestine died in custody within a year. Dante later placed a figure widely read as Celestine in the vestibule of Hell for making, in his words, 'the great refusal.'

evt-12-13-1577-francis-drake.scenario: You stand on the quay at Plymouth on 13 December 1577 as Francis Drake's small fleet, sailing under Queen Elizabeth's secret commission, casts off. Officially the voyage is bound for the Mediterranean.
evt-12-13-1577-francis-drake.prompt: What was Drake's real, secret objective for this voyage?

choices.text: To deliver an English embassy to the Ottoman court
To establish England's first permanent colony in North America
To sail into the Pacific and raid Spanish colonies and treasure ships
To chart a Northwest Passage to Asia through the Arctic

evt-12-13-1577-francis-drake.butterflyEffect: Drake's true mission was to raid Spanish ports and shipping in the Pacific, waters the Spanish considered their private lake. He returned in 1580 having completed the second circumnavigation of the globe, laden with plunder, and Elizabeth knighted him aboard his ship the Golden Hind, deepening the rift with Spain that helped lead to the Armada.

evt-12-13-1643-first-english-civil-war.scenario: It is 13 December 1643 in the Hampshire town of Alton. You are a Parliamentarian soldier under Sir William Waller, storming the parish church where cornered Royalist troops under Colonel Richard Bolle have barricaded themselves for a last stand.
evt-12-13-1643-first-english-civil-war.prompt: What was the outcome of Waller's assault on the Royalist garrison at Alton?

choices.text: Parliamentarian troops stormed the church, killing the Royalist commander and taking the garrison
Both sides withdrew after agreeing to a local truce
A Royalist relief force arrived and drove Waller off
The Royalists broke out and escaped toward Winchester

evt-12-13-1643-first-english-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Waller's men stormed the church, killing Colonel Bolle and capturing several hundred Royalist prisoners, a decisive Parliamentarian victory. The win secured Hampshire for Parliament and blunted Royalist momentum in the south just as the war's balance was shifting after the autumn campaigns.

evt-12-13-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 13 December 1862 at Fredericksburg, Virginia. You are a Union infantryman in Ambrose Burnside's army, ordered to advance across open ground toward a stone wall lined with Confederate riflemen on Marye's Heights.
evt-12-13-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: What happened when wave after wave of Union troops charged the stone wall?

choices.text: Both sides agreed to a truce before the assault began
Repeated Union charges were repulsed with devastating losses
Union troops broke through and captured the heights
Confederate forces abandoned the wall and retreated south

evt-12-13-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Fourteen separate Union assaults were shattered by Confederate fire from the sunken road, producing over 12,000 Union casualties to the South's roughly 5,000. The catastrophic defeat shattered Union morale, led to Burnside's removal from command within weeks, and set the stage for his disastrous follow-up 'Mud March.'

evt-12-13-1937-second-sino-japanese-war.scenario: It is 13 December 1937 and Japanese forces have breached the walls of Nanjing. You are a foreign resident, part of a small group trying to shelter terrified Chinese civilians as the city falls.
evt-12-13-1937-second-sino-japanese-war.prompt: What did a group of foreign residents do to try to protect civilians as the city fell?

choices.text: They set up an International Safety Zone to shelter refugees
They negotiated a formal surrender that spared the population
They organized armed resistance alongside Chinese soldiers
They evacuated the entire city by river before the attack

evt-12-13-1937-second-sino-japanese-war.butterflyEffect: Foreigners including John Rabe established the Nanjing Safety Zone, sheltering roughly 200,000 civilians, though it could not stop the mass killing and atrocities that followed in the weeks after the city's capture. The massacre remains a defining and deeply contested wound in Chinese-Japanese relations to this day.

evt-12-13-1960-haile-selassie.scenario: It is December 1960 and Emperor Haile Selassie is on a state visit to Brazil. In Addis Ababa, officers of the Imperial Guard have seized the radio station and pressed Crown Prince Asfa Wossen to declare himself the new emperor.
evt-12-13-1960-haile-selassie.prompt: What did the Crown Prince do when the plotters pressed him to take the throne?

choices.text: He led loyalist troops in person to retake the radio station
He refused outright and was immediately arrested by the plotters
He fled the country to join his father in exile
He broadcast a hesitant declaration but did not fully break with his father

evt-12-13-1960-haile-selassie.butterflyEffect: Asfa Wossen made a radio broadcast under duress but avoided fully committing to the plotters' cause, while the army and police outside the capital stayed loyal to Haile Selassie. The Emperor flew home, the coup collapsed within days, and its ringleaders were later executed, but the unrest exposed deep grievances over land and reform that foreshadowed the revolution which finally toppled Selassie in 1974.

evt-12-13-1974-malta.scenario: It is 13 December 1974 in Valletta. Malta's parliament has just voted to end the monarchy while staying within the Commonwealth, and officials must decide who will take on the ceremonial duties of the departing Governor-General.
evt-12-13-1974-malta.prompt: What happens to Malta's head of state that day?

choices.text: Malta severs all ties with the Commonwealth immediately
The British monarch remains constitutional head of state
Malta merges its government with neighbouring Italy
A President replaces the Governor-General as head of state, within the Commonwealth

evt-12-13-1974-malta.butterflyEffect: Malta became a republic within the Commonwealth, with Sir Anthony Mamo sworn in as its first President while Maltese and English remained the official languages. Commonwealth membership was preserved, and the tiny island nation's political stability helped pave the way for full EU membership in 2004.

evt-12-13-1974-vietnam-war.scenario: It is December 1974 and you are a North Vietnamese commander weighing whether to test Washington's resolve after the 1973 peace accords by seizing Phước Long province in South Vietnam.
evt-12-13-1974-vietnam-war.prompt: What follows this opening attack on Phước Long?

choices.text: The U.S. does not intervene, and it emboldens a full offensive against the South
South Vietnamese forces decisively repel the attack
The U.S. launches a major air campaign to defend the province
China intervenes directly on behalf of South Vietnam

evt-12-13-1974-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: Phước Long fell in January 1975 without any American intervention, confirming to Hanoi that the U.S. would not return to the war. Emboldened, North Vietnam launched its full-scale offensive, and Saigon fell just months later in April 1975, ending the war.

evt-12-13-1977-air-indiana-flight-216.scenario: It is the evening of 13 December 1977 at Evansville Regional Airport. You are a ground crewman watching the University of Evansville Purple Aces board a chartered DC-3 bound for their game in Tennessee.
evt-12-13-1977-air-indiana-flight-216.prompt: What did investigators later cite as a key factor in the crash moments after takeoff?

choices.text: Improper weight distribution and maintenance lapses on the aircraft
A deliberate decision to fly through a hurricane
Sabotage by a rival university's fans
A collision with another aircraft on the runway

evt-12-13-1977-air-indiana-flight-216.butterflyEffect: The DC-3 lost control shortly after leaving the runway and crashed, killing all 29 aboard, wiping out virtually the entire Evansville basketball team, coaching staff, and boosters. Investigators pointed to improper weight distribution and inadequate maintenance oversight, and the tragedy led the university to rebuild its program from scratch for years afterward.

evt-12-13-1981-wojciech-jaruzelski.scenario: It is the night of 12–13 December 1981 in Warsaw. As leader of Poland's ruling party, you face a nationwide wave of Solidarity strikes and must decide whether to unleash the military to restore Party control.
evt-12-13-1981-wojciech-jaruzelski.prompt: What do you order that night?

choices.text: Request an open Soviet military invasion
Negotiate immediate power-sharing with Solidarity
Declare martial law, deploy troops, and arrest Solidarity leaders
Resign and call for free elections

evt-12-13-1981-wojciech-jaruzelski.butterflyEffect: Jaruzelski declared martial law, interning thousands of Solidarity activists including Lech Wałęsa and suspending civil liberties for over a year. Though the movement was crushed in the short term, Solidarity survived underground and returned in 1989 to negotiate Poland's peaceful transition to democracy.

evt-12-13-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.scenario: It's 13 December 1991, and Operation Whirlwind has just collapsed. You command a Croatian armored unit facing encirclement by advancing Yugoslav People's Army and Serb paramilitary forces, with no route to evacuate your tanks intact.
evt-12-13-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.prompt: What do you do with your tanks before pulling back?

choices.text: Surrender them in exchange for safe passage
Launch one last breakout attack with them
Abandon them intact and retreat on foot
Destroy them to keep them out of enemy hands

evt-12-13-1991-croatian-war-of-independe.butterflyEffect: Croatian crews blew up their own tanks rather than let them fall into enemy hands, accepting the material loss to deny the JNA a propaganda and equipment windfall. The failed offensive forced Croatia to rely more on diplomacy, contributing to the UN-brokered ceasefire of January 1992 that froze front lines until later operations like Storm in 1995.

evt-12-13-1994-flagship-airlines-flight-.scenario: It is 13 December 1994 aboard a Jetstream turboprop approaching Raleigh-Durham in poor conditions. The crew abandons the landing and begins a go-around after the approach becomes unstable.
evt-12-13-1994-flagship-airlines-flight-.prompt: What critical error follows during the go-around?

choices.text: The crew executes the go-around and lands safely
Air traffic control directs the plane into another aircraft
An unrelated engine failure causes the crash
The crew mishandles the maneuver, causing a stall

evt-12-13-1994-flagship-airlines-flight-.butterflyEffect: The mishandled go-around caused the aircraft to stall and crash short of the runway, killing both pilots and 13 of the 18 passengers. The NTSB's findings on stall recovery and crew coordination during go-arounds went on to shape later training standards for regional airline pilots.

evt-12-13-2001-2001-indian-parliament-at.scenario: It is midday on 13 December 2001. You are a security guard at Sansad Bhavan in New Delhi when a car rams through the perimeter gate and armed men leap out firing toward the building.
evt-12-13-2001-2001-indian-parliament-at.prompt: What happened to the five attackers who stormed India's Parliament?

choices.text: They detonated explosives inside the main chamber
They took several MPs hostage and negotiated their escape
They fled the compound and were never identified
All five were killed by security forces before reaching lawmakers

evt-12-13-2001-2001-indian-parliament-at.butterflyEffect: Security forces killed all five Jaish-e-Mohammed gunmen before they could enter the main chamber, but nine security and staff personnel died in the fighting. India blamed Pakistan-based militant groups and massed a million troops on the border in Operation Parakram, bringing the two nuclear-armed nations to the brink of war for months.

evt-12-13-2002-2004-enlargement-of-the-e.scenario: It's 13 December 2002, and you are a delegate at the Copenhagen European Council. The EU has just agreed accession terms with ten candidate countries from Central and Eastern Europe and the Mediterranean, ending decades of Cold War division on the continent.
evt-12-13-2002-2004-enlargement-of-the-e.prompt: What follows for these ten candidate nations after this announcement?

choices.text: They are given individual entry dates spread across the next decade
They join the EU together on 1 May 2004, the bloc's largest enlargement
All ten adopt the euro immediately upon entry
Three of the ten are rejected after final referendum votes

evt-12-13-2002-2004-enlargement-of-the-e.butterflyEffect: On 1 May 2004 the ten countries joined together in the EU's largest-ever single enlargement, taking membership to 25 states. It shifted the Union's geographic and political centre eastward, opened new labour markets, and set the template for further expansion into the Balkans in later years.

evt-12-13-2003-iraq-war.scenario: It is 13 December 2003 near ad-Dawr, Iraq. You are a U.S. soldier searching a rural compound during Operation Red Dawn, acting on intelligence about the fugitive former president's hiding place.
evt-12-13-2003-iraq-war.prompt: What do the troops discover at the farmhouse?

choices.text: Saddam Hussein hidden in a small underground hole
Saddam disguised as a farmer, shot while resisting
Evidence that Saddam had already fled to Syria
Saddam found dead by apparent suicide

evt-12-13-2003-iraq-war.butterflyEffect: Soldiers pulled a disheveled, bearded Saddam Hussein from a narrow underground hiding hole near his hometown of Tikrit, ending his nine-month manhunt. His capture deflated remnants of Ba'athist resistance and led to his 2006 trial and execution by the new Iraqi government.

evt-12-13-2013-beyonce.scenario: It is just after midnight on 13 December 2013. You open iTunes to find that Beyoncé has released an entire new album out of nowhere, no interviews, no lead single, no warning.
evt-12-13-2013-beyonce.prompt: What made this release strategy so disruptive to the music industry?

choices.text: She released it exclusively through a new streaming service she co-owned
She dropped the full album and videos with no advance announcement or promotion
She gave the album away for free to anyone who pre-ordered concert tickets
She premiered it as a one-night-only theatrical event before wide release

evt-12-13-2013-beyonce.butterflyEffect: Beyoncé's self-titled 'visual album,' with fourteen songs and seventeen videos, sold over 800,000 copies in three days with zero traditional promotion. The stunt upended standard release cycles and pushed rivals like Drake, Kanye West, and Rihanna toward their own surprise drops in the years that followed.

evt-12-13-2019-jo-swinson.scenario: It is the early hours of 13 December 2019. As the UK general election results roll in, you watch the Liberal Democrat leader Jo Swinson's own East Dunbartonshire count, hoping for a strong night for the party.
evt-12-13-2019-jo-swinson.prompt: What actually followed Swinson's shock loss of her own seat?

choices.text: She held her seat but the party still lost so many MPs that she resigned in solidarity
She lost her own seat and resigned as party leader that same day
She was re-elected but immediately called for a second Brexit referendum and quit over its rejection
She won her seat comfortably and remained leader into the new Parliament

evt-12-13-2019-jo-swinson.butterflyEffect: Swinson lost East Dunbartonshire to the SNP's Amy Callaghan by a razor-thin margin, becoming the first sitting party leader in the election to lose their seat. She resigned as Lib Dem leader that day, and the party installed joint interim leaders before Ed Davey won the subsequent leadership contest in 2020.

evt-12-14-1650-anne-greene.scenario: It is December 1650 in Oxford. Anne Greene has just been cut down from the gallows after her hanging for infanticide, and as her body lies in a coffin awaiting dissection, you notice her chest still moves.
evt-12-14-1650-anne-greene.prompt: As one of the attending physicians, what should you do upon seeing signs of life?

choices.text: Declare her legally dead and seal the coffin for burial
Attempt to revive her with warmth, rubbing, and medical care
Proceed with the planned anatomical dissection immediately
Notify the sheriff so the hanging can be completed

evt-12-14-1650-anne-greene.butterflyEffect: The Oxford doctors worked through the night to revive her with warmth, rubbing, and bloodletting, and she fully recovered. Many took her survival as a sign of divine intervention proving her innocence, and she was formally pardoned and later married and had children.

evt-12-14-1863-american-civil-war.scenario: It's 14 December 1863 near Bean's Station, Tennessee. You command a Union cavalry brigade as General Longstreet's Confederate infantry surge forward, trying to trap your division before it can slip back toward Knoxville.
evt-12-14-1863-american-civil-war.prompt: What is your best move to keep your division from being encircled and destroyed?

choices.text: Charge directly into Longstreet's main line to break the encirclement
Surrender the division to avoid further casualties
Fight a delaying action to cover the wagon train, then withdraw after dark
Scatter into small parties and flee individually toward Knoxville

evt-12-14-1863-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Union forces fought a stubborn delaying action to protect their wagons and men before withdrawing after nightfall, leaving the field technically to the Confederates but the trap unsprung. Worn down by the harsh winter and dwindling supplies, Longstreet abandoned East Tennessee entirely by spring 1864, freeing Union troops there for the coming campaigns.

evt-12-14-1911-roald-amundsen.scenario: It's 14 December 1911, and after months of man-hauling and dog-sledging across the Antarctic ice, your five-man Norwegian party's instruments confirm you have reached 90° South before anyone else.
evt-12-14-1911-roald-amundsen.prompt: What do you do to mark the feat and settle any future dispute over priority?

choices.text: Send a radio signal to Norway announcing the feat immediately
Build a stone cairn and turn back without any marker
Bury supplies and wait for the British team to arrive
Plant the flag and leave a letter for Scott to find

evt-12-14-1911-roald-amundsen.butterflyEffect: Amundsen's party planted the Norwegian flag, pitched a small tent named Polheim, and left a letter for Rival explorer Robert Falcon Scott confirming their arrival. Scott's team reached the pole 34 days later, found the tent and letter, and died on the return journey — cementing Amundsen's triumph and Scott's tragedy as the defining story of the Heroic Age of Antarctic exploration.

evt-12-14-1918-giacomo-puccini.scenario: It's the evening of 14 December 1918, and you watch from the wings as the curtain falls on the third and final piece of Puccini's new operatic triptych at the Metropolitan Opera in New York.
evt-12-14-1918-giacomo-puccini.prompt: Which of the three one-act operas earns the loudest, most enthusiastic response from the audience?

choices.text: The audience boos the entire triptych as too experimental
Gianni Schicchi, the comic finale about a scheming will-forger
Il tabarro, the tragic tale of a jealous barge owner
Suor Angelica, the tragedy set in a convent

evt-12-14-1918-giacomo-puccini.butterflyEffect: Gianni Schicchi, the comic finale, proved the runaway favorite that night, while the darker Il tabarro and Suor Angelica received a cooler reception. Ever since, Gianni Schicchi has been the most frequently staged panel of Il trittico, often performed alone, while the other two are usually paired with other short works.

evt-12-14-1925-wozzeck.scenario: You sit in the packed Berlin State Opera on 14 December 1925, watching Alban Berg's Wozzeck—built on atonal harmony rather than traditional melody—unfold before a startled audience.
evt-12-14-1925-wozzeck.prompt: What actually happens in the wake of this unsettling premiere?

choices.text: It sparks controversy but establishes Berg as a leading modern composer
The opera is booed off stage and never performed again
Prussian censors ban it outright before a second performance
The audience unanimously praises it with no dissent at all

evt-12-14-1925-wozzeck.butterflyEffect: Despite hisses from some quarters, Wozzeck was a critical triumph that made Berg one of the most performed living opera composers of the interwar years. The Nazis later banned it in 1933 as 'degenerate' music, and it did not return to German stages until after the Second World War.

evt-12-14-1948-thomas-t-goldsmith-jr.scenario: It is 1948, and you work alongside physicist Thomas T. Goldsmith Jr. at a television laboratory, testing a curious cathode-ray tube device that lets a player steer a glowing dot toward targets drawn on an overlay.
evt-12-14-1948-thomas-t-goldsmith-jr.prompt: What did Goldsmith and Mann's newly patented device let a user do?

choices.text: Record moving images onto magnetic tape for playback
Transmit compressed television broadcasts over long distances
Project three-dimensional images using early laser technology
Steer a simulated missile trajectory to hit targets on a CRT screen

evt-12-14-1948-thomas-t-goldsmith-jr.butterflyEffect: The patent covered a 'cathode-ray tube amusement device' letting players adjust a simulated missile's trajectory to hit targets on the screen. Though DuMont never mass-produced it, historians now consider it the earliest known interactive electronic game, decades before Pong or the arcade industry existed.

evt-12-14-1981-knesset.scenario: It is 14 December 1981 in Jerusalem. You sit in the Knesset chamber as members debate a bill concerning the territory captured from Syria in 1967, deciding how far Israeli law should reach.
evt-12-14-1981-knesset.prompt: What did the Knesset vote to do with the Golan Heights?

choices.text: Grant the Golan Heights full autonomous self-government
Return the Golan Heights to Syria under a negotiated treaty
Place the Golan Heights under permanent United Nations trusteeship
Extend Israeli civil law and administration over the Golan Heights

evt-12-14-1981-knesset.butterflyEffect: The Golan Heights Law extended Israeli civil law and administration over the territory, a move widely seen as de facto annexation. The UN Security Council declared the act null and void in Resolution 497, and the territory's status remained a major obstacle to any future Israeli-Syrian peace deal for decades.

evt-12-14-1981-arab-israeli-conflict.scenario: You sit in Israel's Knesset on 14 December 1981 as legislators debate a bill covering the Golan Heights, territory seized from Syria in the 1967 war and held under military occupation since.
evt-12-14-1981-arab-israeli-conflict.prompt: What did the Golan Heights Law that passed that day actually do?

choices.text: Returned the Golan Heights to Syrian control
Extended Israeli civil law and administration over the Golan Heights
Placed the Golan Heights under UN administration
Created a permanent demilitarized buffer zone there

evt-12-14-1981-arab-israeli-conflict.butterflyEffect: The law extended Israeli civil law, jurisdiction, and administration over the Golan Heights, a step widely seen as de facto annexation. The UN Security Council's Resolution 497 declared it null and void, and most of the world still does not recognize Israeli sovereignty there, though the US formally did so in 2019.

evt-12-14-1985-wilma-mankiller.scenario: You are among the Cherokee Nation on 14 December 1985 as Deputy Chief Wilma Mankiller takes the oath of office after Principal Chief Ross Swimmer departs to lead the Bureau of Indian Affairs.
evt-12-14-1985-wilma-mankiller.prompt: What made Mankiller's swearing-in as Principal Chief historic?

choices.text: She was the youngest person ever to become chief
She became the first woman to lead the Cherokee Nation
She was the first non-Cherokee to hold the office
She was directly appointed by the federal government

evt-12-14-1985-wilma-mankiller.butterflyEffect: She became the first woman ever to serve as Principal Chief of the Cherokee Nation. She went on to win reelection twice by large margins, expanded health, education, and community development programs, and was later awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom for her leadership.

evt-12-14-1994-three-gorges-dam.scenario: It's 14 December 1994, and you stand among officials at Sandouping as Premier Li Peng presides over the ceremony marking the start of construction on the Three Gorges Dam, a project long delayed by fierce debate.
evt-12-14-1994-three-gorges-dam.prompt: What justification does the government give for pushing ahead despite the controversy?

choices.text: Boosting international tourism revenue
Creating a strategic naval base on the Yangtze
Preserving ancient temples along the gorges
Flood control and hydroelectric power generation

evt-12-14-1994-three-gorges-dam.butterflyEffect: The dam was completed in 2006 and became the world's largest power station by capacity, taming devastating Yangtze floods and generating enormous hydroelectric output. But it also forced the resettlement of over a million people and submerged historic towns and archaeological sites, a cost still debated today.

evt-12-14-1995-yugoslav-wars.scenario: You watch in Paris on 14 December 1995 as the presidents of Bosnia, Croatia, and Serbia sign the Dayton Agreement, formally ending nearly four years of war in Bosnia after weeks of talks in Ohio.
evt-12-14-1995-yugoslav-wars.prompt: What governing structure did the Dayton Agreement establish for Bosnia and Herzegovina?

choices.text: Direct rule by a permanent UN trusteeship
Two ethnic entities under a weak shared central government
Partition into three fully independent countries
A single unitary centralized Bosnian state

evt-12-14-1995-yugoslav-wars.butterflyEffect: Dayton split Bosnia into two entities, the Bosniak-Croat Federation and Republika Srpska, joined by a weak central government, and brought in NATO-led peacekeepers. The deal stopped the killing but froze ethnic divisions into the constitution, a structure still blamed today for political paralysis in Bosnia.

evt-12-14-2003-pervez-musharraf.scenario: It's 14 December 2003, and you ride in the security escort of President Musharraf's motorcade as it crosses a bridge in Rawalpindi, unaware that explosives have been wired beneath it, timed to the convoy's passing.
evt-12-14-2003-pervez-musharraf.prompt: What saves the president's convoy in the final seconds?

choices.text: The attackers lose their nerve and abandon the plot
A signal-jamming device delays the bomb's detonation past the convoy
A decoy convoy takes the bridge instead of the real one
Security forces find and disarm the bomb hours earlier

evt-12-14-2003-pervez-musharraf.butterflyEffect: The bomb detonated moments after Musharraf's car had already crossed, sparing him by seconds. Eleven days later a second, more determined attempt using suicide bombers again narrowly failed, and both attacks—linked to militants opposed to his alliance with the US—only hardened his resolve to continue backing the war on terror.

evt-12-14-2008-baghdad.scenario: You are in the press room in Baghdad on 14 December 2008, watching President George W. Bush field questions beside Iraqi Prime Minister Maliki. Suddenly Iraqi journalist Muntadhar al-Zaidi rises, shouts "this is a farewell kiss, you dog," and hurls his shoe at Bush's head.
evt-12-14-2008-baghdad.prompt: What happened immediately after al-Zaidi threw both his shoes at Bush?

choices.text: He was tackled by security and hauled away for arrest
Secret Service agents shot him on the spot
He turned and threw the second shoe at Maliki instead
He was allowed to leave the press conference freely

evt-12-14-2008-baghdad.butterflyEffect: Bush ducked both throws unhurt, and security tackled al-Zaidi, who was beaten and jailed for nine months. He emerged a folk hero across the Arab world protesting the Iraq War, and shoe-throwing became a lasting global gesture of political protest and insult.

evt-12-14-2017-the-walt-disney-company.scenario: You read the headlines on 14 December 2017 as The Walt Disney Company announces a massive deal to acquire most of 21st Century Fox's entertainment assets, including its film studio and TV holdings.
evt-12-14-2017-the-walt-disney-company.prompt: What was Disney chiefly after in absorbing Fox's studio and franchises?

choices.text: An exit from the film production business entirely
A joint venture merger with Comcast's NBCUniversal
Franchises like X-Men and Avatar plus content to power a streaming service
Selling off its own studios to Fox in exchange

evt-12-14-2017-the-walt-disney-company.butterflyEffect: The deal closed in 2019 for $71.3 billion after a bidding war with Comcast, returning X-Men and Fantastic Four rights to Marvel and bringing Avatar under Disney's roof. The acquired content also fueled the launch of Disney+ later that year, reshaping the streaming landscape.

evt-12-15-533-belisarius.scenario: It is 15 December 533. You ride with Belisarius as his cavalry closes on King Gelimer's camp at Tricamarum, days after crushing the Vandals at Ad Decimum. Gelimer's brother Tzazon has arrived with reinforcements for one last stand to save the Vandal Kingdom.
evt-12-15-533-belisarius.prompt: What must Belisarius's cavalry do to break the Vandal line?

choices.text: Charge directly into the Vandal center before they can regroup
Wait for Byzantine infantry to arrive before engaging
Open negotiations with Gelimer for a peaceful surrender
Withdraw to consolidate gains already made at Carthage

evt-12-15-533-belisarius.butterflyEffect: Belisarius's repeated cavalry charges killed Tzazon and shattered Vandal morale, sending Gelimer fleeing into the mountains. The Vandal Kingdom collapsed within weeks, and North Africa was absorbed into the Byzantine Empire as the new Praetorian Prefecture of Africa.

evt-12-15-1025-constantine-viii.scenario: It is 15 December 1025 in Constantinople. Your brother, the great conqueror-emperor Basil II, has just died after a 66-year joint reign, leaving you, Constantine VIII, sole ruler at nearly sixty years old, having never independently commanded an army or run the empire's administration.
evt-12-15-1025-constantine-viii.prompt: What did Constantine VIII actually do once he became sole Byzantine emperor?

choices.text: He restored full legislative power to the old Roman Senate
He moved the imperial capital from Constantinople to Antioch
