He launched a major new campaign to conquer Fatimid Egypt
He devoted himself to leisure and left the empire's administration largely to court officials

evt-12-15-1025-constantine-viii.butterflyEffect: Constantine largely indulged in pleasure and delegated governance, doing little to sustain Basil's conquests or reforms. His neglect and his choice of the elderly Romanos III Argyros as successor for his daughter Zoe began a period of weak, short-lived emperors that eroded Macedonian-dynasty stability in the decades before Manzikert.

evt-12-15-1796-war-of-the-first-coalitio.scenario: You are aboard the French fleet anchored off Bantry Bay in December 1796, part of an expedition meant to land 15,000 troops in Ireland to spark rebellion among the United Irishmen. A fierce winter storm has scattered the ships and made the coastline impossible to approach.
evt-12-15-1796-war-of-the-first-coalitio.prompt: What must the French commanders do as storms prevent any troops from landing?

choices.text: Abandon the mission instantly and turn back for France
Wait offshore for the weather to clear, hoping to still land the troops
Sail south at once to try a different Irish port
Force a landing immediately despite the surf

evt-12-15-1796-war-of-the-first-coalitio.butterflyEffect: The fleet waited offshore for days hoping the weather would break, but the storm never relented and no troops ever landed. The expedition returned to France empty-handed, a lost chance that left the United Irishmen to rise alone in 1798, without the French support that might have changed the rebellion's outcome.

evt-12-15-1864-american-civil-war.scenario: It is dawn on 15 December 1864, outside Nashville. General George Thomas, criticized by Grant for weeks of delay, finally unleashes his Union army against John Bell Hood's exhausted Army of Tennessee.
evt-12-15-1864-american-civil-war.prompt: What did Thomas's Union forces achieve at the Battle of Nashville?

choices.text: They crushed Hood's Army of Tennessee, destroying it as an effective fighting force
They were repulsed and forced to retreat into Kentucky
They captured the city of Atlanta for the first time
They compelled Robert E. Lee's surrender at Appomattox

evt-12-15-1864-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Thomas's assault shattered Hood's Army of Tennessee as an organized fighting force, effectively ending major Confederate resistance in the western theater. The victory secured Thomas's reputation as "The Rock of Chickamauga" and hastened the Confederacy's collapse in the war's final months.

evt-12-15-1871-ella-stewart-udall.scenario: It is December 1871 at the remote Deseret Telegraph Company office in Pipe Spring. You are sixteen-year-old Ella Stewart, recently trained and stationed here, and the line to the rest of Arizona Territory has just been completed.
evt-12-15-1871-ella-stewart-udall.prompt: What must Ella do to make her mark on Arizona's new telegraph line?

choices.text: Wait for a more experienced male operator to arrive
Send the inaugural message herself from the Pipe Spring station
Delay transmission until the entire line is double-tested
Refuse the task, citing her lack of formal training

evt-12-15-1871-ella-stewart-udall.butterflyEffect: Ella sent the first telegraphed message from Arizona Territory, becoming its first telegraph operator at just sixteen. Her work helped link isolated frontier settlements into a wider communication network, and she went on to a long career as a telegraphist and entrepreneur.

evt-12-15-1890-sitting-bull.scenario: It is dawn on 15 December 1890 at Standing Rock Reservation. Indian agency police, backed by nearby U.S. troops, arrive at Sitting Bull's cabin to arrest him amid fears he will join the Ghost Dance movement, and his followers gather around the confrontation.
evt-12-15-1890-sitting-bull.prompt: What happens as police attempt to lead Sitting Bull away from his home?

choices.text: He flees the reservation before police arrive
He submits calmly and is escorted away without incident
His followers surround the police to stop the arrest, and violence erupts
Tribal elders negotiate a delay in the arrest

evt-12-15-1890-sitting-bull.butterflyEffect: His followers moved to stop the arrest, and in the ensuing struggle gunfire broke out, killing Sitting Bull. The killing deepened fear and grief among the Lakota, and within two weeks U.S. troops confronted Ghost Dance followers at Wounded Knee, effectively ending armed Native resistance on the Northern Plains.

evt-12-15-1939-epic-film.scenario: It's 15 December 1939 in Atlanta, Georgia. Crowds throng the streets for the glittering premiere of a sweeping Civil War epic adapted from Margaret Mitchell's bestselling novel, with stars arriving to a segregated Southern city.
evt-12-15-1939-epic-film.prompt: What happened at the Atlanta premiere involving the film's Black cast members?

choices.text: Black cast members, including Hattie McDaniel, were excluded from the segregated theater and festivities
The film was banned from release in the state of Georgia
The premiere was cancelled after NAACP protests shut it down
Clark Gable refused to attend and boycotted the event entirely

evt-12-15-1939-epic-film.butterflyEffect: Hattie McDaniel and her fellow Black cast members were barred from the whites-only theater and festivities under Jim Crow segregation. Weeks later McDaniel became the first African American to win an Academy Award for her role, though she still sat at a segregated table at the ceremony, exposing Hollywood's contradictions.

evt-12-15-1945-supreme-commander-for-the.scenario: It is 15 December 1945 in occupied Tokyo. General MacArthur's headquarters is preparing to issue a directive targeting an institution the Allies believe fueled Japan's wartime militarism and emperor-worship.
evt-12-15-1945-supreme-commander-for-the.prompt: What did SCAP order the Japanese government to do in this directive?

choices.text: Ban the practice of Buddhism throughout Japan
Nationalize all Shinto shrines as government property
Abolish the imperial institution entirely
End state financial support and official sponsorship of Shinto shrines

evt-12-15-1945-supreme-commander-for-the.butterflyEffect: The so-called Shinto Directive ended government funding and sponsorship of Shinto shrines, forcing a legal separation of religion from the state. It paved the way for Emperor Hirohito's 1946 renunciation of divine status and shaped the religious-freedom clauses of Japan's postwar constitution.

evt-12-15-1946-iran-crisis-of-1946.scenario: It is December 1946. Soviet troops have finally withdrawn from northern Iran under American pressure, and Iranian army columns are now advancing on Tabriz, capital of the Soviet-backed Azerbaijan People's Government.
evt-12-15-1946-iran-crisis-of-1946.prompt: What followed when Iranian government troops entered Tabriz?

choices.text: Tehran granted the region full autonomy in exchange for peace
Soviet forces returned to defend the separatist government
The separatist Azerbaijan People's Government collapsed and its leaders fled to the Soviet Union
The United Nations sent peacekeepers to administer the city

evt-12-15-1946-iran-crisis-of-1946.butterflyEffect: The Azerbaijan People's Government collapsed within days and its leaders fled across the border into the Soviet Union, ending the crisis. The episode became an early Cold War success story for the United States, later cited as an early demonstration of the containment strategy that would define the Truman Doctrine.

evt-12-15-1961-adolf-eichmann.scenario: It is 15 December 1961 in Jerusalem. You sit on the special tribunal of the Jerusalem District Court, about to deliver the verdict against Adolf Eichmann for his role in organizing the deportation of millions to Nazi camps.
evt-12-15-1961-adolf-eichmann.prompt: What did the tribunal decide regarding Eichmann's guilt and sentence?

choices.text: Found guilty on major counts and sentenced him to death
Convicted him only of minor administrative violations
Acquitted him on grounds that he was merely following orders
Found guilty but sentenced him to life imprisonment

evt-12-15-1961-adolf-eichmann.butterflyEffect: Eichmann was found guilty on charges including crimes against the Jewish people and crimes against humanity, and sentenced to death. His appeal was rejected by Israel's Supreme Court, and he was hanged in 1962, the only civil execution ever carried out in Israel; the trial's global coverage shaped postwar Holocaust memory and public understanding of bureaucratic complicity.

evt-12-15-1970-venera-7.scenario: It is 15 December 1970. Inside a Soviet control room, engineers strain over a faint, garbled signal from Venera 7, whose parachute failed to fully open and which now lies toppled on the Venusian surface.
evt-12-15-1970-venera-7.prompt: What must the ground team do to learn whether the lander survived?

choices.text: Declare the probe lost and end the mission
Send a radio command demanding a stronger retransmission
Wait for the next orbital pass to try again
Painstakingly filter the faint signal from noise to extract temperature data

evt-12-15-1970-venera-7.butterflyEffect: Painstaking analysis extracted temperature data from the weak signal, revealing a surface hotter than 470°C — the first data ever transmitted from another planet's surface. The result confirmed Venus as a hostile, superheated world and reshaped how future missions there were designed.

evt-12-15-2001-leaning-tower-of-pisa.scenario: It is 2001 in Pisa, and after a decade-long engineering project you must decide how to stabilize the famous leaning tower without erasing the tilt that made it world-famous.
evt-12-15-2001-leaning-tower-of-pisa.prompt: What method did engineers use to make the tower safe while preserving its lean?

choices.text: Attach permanent visible counterweights to the tower's summit
Inject concrete into the foundation to straighten the tower fully
Demolish and rebuild the tower on a new foundation
Extract soil from the north side to slightly reduce the lean

evt-12-15-2001-leaning-tower-of-pisa.butterflyEffect: Engineers extracted soil from beneath the tower's north side, gently reducing the lean by about 40 centimeters without straightening it fully. The tower reopened in December 2001 and was declared stable for at least two more centuries, becoming a model for heritage conservation worldwide.

evt-12-15-2010-refugee.scenario: It is 15 December 2010. You watch from the cliffs of Christmas Island as an overloaded wooden boat carrying dozens of asylum seekers is thrown against jagged rocks by heavy swell, its hull breaking apart before rescuers can reach everyone aboard.
evt-12-15-2010-refugee.prompt: What did this disaster trigger within Australian politics in the months that followed?

choices.text: The immediate closure of all offshore detention centres
A renewed, intense debate over Australia's border protection and asylum policies
Little public reaction, as the story received minimal coverage
A bipartisan decision to open borders to all asylum seekers by boat

evt-12-15-2010-refugee.butterflyEffect: Images of the wreck, filmed by horrified onlookers, became a rallying point in Australia's fierce national debate over asylum seeker policy. It intensified political pressure over border protection and offshore processing, shaping the harder line successive governments took toward boat arrivals in the years after.

evt-12-15-2017-2017-java-earthquake.scenario: It is late night on 15 December 2017 in West Java. Seismic instruments have just recorded a powerful shaking near Tasikmalaya, and officials must decide how to respond as initial readings suggest a very strong quake.
evt-12-15-2017-2017-java-earthquake.prompt: What did authorities do after first issuing an immediate tsunami warning?

choices.text: Cancel the warning once data showed the quake was too deep to trigger a tsunami
Order a mass evacuation of the entire Indonesian coastline
Escalate the warning to a nationwide state of emergency
Keep the warning active for a full week regardless of new data

evt-12-15-2017-2017-java-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Once data confirmed the quake originated at a deep 91 km, far too deep to displace enough seawater for a tsunami, the warning was cancelled. The episode underscored how earthquake depth, not just magnitude, determines tsunami risk, and it pushed Indonesian agencies to refine their rapid-assessment protocols.

evt-12-16-1653-oliver-cromwell.scenario: It is 16 December 1653, and you stand in Westminster Hall as Oliver Cromwell is installed under the new Instrument of Government. England has abolished its monarchy and House of Lords, and a single soldier-statesman is about to take an unfamiliar new office.
evt-12-16-1653-oliver-cromwell.prompt: What title does Cromwell assume as head of the Commonwealth?

choices.text: King of England
First Consul
Lord Protector
Lord High Admiral

evt-12-16-1653-oliver-cromwell.butterflyEffect: Cromwell became Lord Protector, ruling with near-monarchical power until his death in 1658. His son Richard briefly succeeded him, but the Protectorate collapsed within two years, paving the way for the Restoration of Charles II in 1660.

evt-12-16-1689-parliament-of-england.scenario: It is December 1689 and you sit in the English Parliament. Months earlier William and Mary accepted the crown on the condition they honour a Declaration of Rights, but that declaration is not yet binding law.
evt-12-16-1689-parliament-of-england.prompt: What does Parliament do to make the Declaration of Rights permanent?

choices.text: Leave it as an informal agreement with the monarchs
Grant William an absolute veto over Parliament instead
Pass the Declaration of Rights into statute law
Ask the Pope to arbitrate the succession question

evt-12-16-1689-parliament-of-england.butterflyEffect: Parliament enacted the Declaration as the Bill of Rights, a statute limiting the monarch's power, barring Catholics from the throne, and requiring regular parliaments and free elections. It became a cornerstone of English constitutional monarchy and a direct model for the American Bill of Rights a century later.

evt-12-16-1740-frederick-the-great.scenario: It is December 1740. You serve in the Prussian army as it crosses into the Habsburg province of Silesia, weeks after the death of Emperor Charles VI left his daughter Maria Theresa to inherit the Austrian lands.
evt-12-16-1740-frederick-the-great.prompt: What justification does Frederick give for seizing Silesia?

choices.text: Old Hohenzollern dynastic claims to Silesian duchies
Protection of Prussian trade routes through the region
Retaliation for an Austrian raid on Prussian territory
A treaty obligation to defend Silesian Protestants

evt-12-16-1740-frederick-the-great.butterflyEffect: Frederick invoked centuries-old Hohenzollern dynastic claims to Silesian duchies like Brieg and Liegnitz. The invasion ignited the First Silesian War within the wider War of the Austrian Succession, and Prussia's eventual annexation of most of Silesia by 1742 doubled its wealth and population, setting up decades of rivalry with Austria that culminated in the Seven Years' War.

evt-12-16-1761-seven-years-war.scenario: It is 16 December 1761 inside the besieged Prussian fortress of Kolberg. Russian forces have surrounded you for four months, your relief force has withdrawn, and your stores of food and powder are nearly gone.
evt-12-16-1761-seven-years-war.prompt: As the Prussian garrison commander, what do you decide to do?

choices.text: Negotiate a permanent ceasefire with Russia alone
Attempt a mass breakout under cover of night
Surrender the fortress once supplies are exhausted
Execute a scorched-earth retreat and burn the town

evt-12-16-1761-seven-years-war.butterflyEffect: The garrison surrendered, giving Russia its long-sought Baltic foothold and tightening the blockade around Frederick the Great's exhausted Prussia. Frederick's fortunes only recovered weeks later, when the death of Empress Elizabeth brought the pro-Prussian Peter III to the Russian throne, an event historians call the "Miracle of the House of Brandenburg," and Kolberg was later returned.

evt-12-16-1811-1811-1812-new-madrid-eart.scenario: It is the night of 16 December 1811. You are a boatman on the Mississippi River near New Madrid when the ground convulses violently, riverbanks begin caving into the water, and the current seems to reverse.
evt-12-16-1811-1811-1812-new-madrid-eart.prompt: What should you do to keep your boat safe?

choices.text: Keep navigating close to the bank where the current is calmer
Abandon the boat and swim for it
Row hard for the nearest shore immediately
Anchor in the middle of the river, away from the caving banks

evt-12-16-1811-1811-1812-new-madrid-eart.butterflyEffect: Survivors who steered toward the middle of the channel, away from the collapsing banks, fared best as landslides and newly formed sandbars swallowed stretches of shoreline. The quakes reshaped the landscape, creating Reelfoot Lake in Tennessee, and remain the most powerful ever recorded east of the Rockies, keeping the New Madrid Seismic Zone a subject of study and building-code concern today.

evt-12-16-1850-canterbury-association.scenario: It is 16 December 1850, and your ship, one of the First Four Ships, has just anchored at Lyttelton Harbour. Ahead lies the Canterbury Plains, where the Canterbury Association intends to found its new settlement of Christchurch.
evt-12-16-1850-canterbury-association.prompt: How do you and the other settlers reach the plains from the harbour?

choices.text: Cross the Port Hills on foot via the Bridle Path
Sail further around Banks Peninsula to a closer harbour
Travel by cart along an existing coastal road
Wait at Lyttelton until a road was built

evt-12-16-1850-canterbury-association.butterflyEffect: With no road yet built, settlers hauled their belongings over the steep Bridle Path across the Port Hills to reach the plains. The awkward overland link spurred later investment in a rail tunnel under the hills in 1867 and eventually a road tunnel in 1964, and Christchurch grew into New Zealand's third-largest city, long nicknamed 'the most English city outside England.'

evt-12-16-1893-antonin-dvorak.scenario: It is the evening of 16 December 1893 at Carnegie Hall in New York. Anton Seidl raises his baton for the world premiere of Antonín Dvořák's new symphony, written during his years directing the National Conservatory in America.
evt-12-16-1893-antonin-dvorak.prompt: What has Dvořák drawn on to give the symphony its distinctly American character?

choices.text: French impressionist harmonies
Themes from Italian grand opera
Traditional German lieder forms
African American spirituals and Native American melodies

evt-12-16-1893-antonin-dvorak.butterflyEffect: The symphony, soon known as "From the New World," wove in melodic ideas evoking African American spirituals and Native American music that Dvořák had come to admire in the United States, partly through his student Harry Burleigh. Its triumphant reception fueled a lasting debate among American composers about what a truly national American music should sound like.

evt-12-16-1901-beatrix-potter.scenario: It is December 1901. Publishers have turned down your little illustrated story about a mischievous rabbit named Peter, and you are determined not to let it disappear into a drawer.
evt-12-16-1901-beatrix-potter.prompt: What do you decide to do with your manuscript?

choices.text: Set the story aside and write about a different animal instead
Abandon writing and focus on scientific illustration
Submit it as a serial to a children's magazine
Pay for a small private printing yourself

evt-12-16-1901-beatrix-potter.butterflyEffect: Potter paid to have 250 copies of The Tale of Peter Rabbit privately printed. The small edition caught the eye of publisher Frederick Warne & Co., who issued it commercially in 1902; it became an instant bestseller, and by 1903 Peter Rabbit had become the first fictional character patented as a stuffed toy, launching Potter's career and a merchandising empire.

evt-12-16-1914-world-war-i.scenario: It is just before dawn on 16 December 1914. You live in Scarborough, on England's Yorkshire coast, and shells from unseen ships out at sea are suddenly crashing into the streets around you.
evt-12-16-1914-world-war-i.prompt: What should you do as the German battlecruisers open fire on your town?

choices.text: Take cover indoors, away from windows, until the shelling stops
Head to the beach to signal the Royal Navy
Ring the church bells to summon the Home Guard
Run toward the harbour to see the ships

evt-12-16-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: German battlecruisers shelled Scarborough, Hartlepool and Whitby that morning, killing well over a hundred civilians, the first time British soil had been attacked in this way. The raid enraged the British public, and "Remember Scarborough!" became a rallying cry on recruitment posters that helped swell volunteer enlistment in early 1915.

evt-12-16-1922-gabriel-narutowicz.scenario: It is 16 December 1922, five days after Gabriel Narutowicz's election as Poland's first president. Right-wing nationalists have denounced him bitterly for winning with support from minority deputies, and you are among the crowd at the opening of an art exhibition in Warsaw that he is attending.
evt-12-16-1922-gabriel-narutowicz.prompt: What happens to President Narutowicz at the exhibition?

choices.text: He resigns under political pressure
He dissolves the Polish parliament
He flees into exile
He is assassinated by a nationalist gunman

evt-12-16-1922-gabriel-narutowicz.butterflyEffect: A nationalist painter, Eligiusz Niewiadomski, shot Narutowicz dead just days into his presidency. The assassination shocked the young republic, deepened the divide between the left and the nationalist right, and the resulting instability helped set the stage for Józef Piłsudski's 1926 coup.

evt-12-16-1930-herman-lamm.scenario: It is 16 December 1930 near Clinton, Indiana. Your getaway car, swapped in haste, cannot outrun the farmers and police now chasing your gang after a bank job gone wrong, and the road ahead is blocked.
evt-12-16-1930-herman-lamm.prompt: As the pursuers close in, what does gang leader Herman Lamm do?

choices.text: Surrender and hope for a lenient sentence
Take a hostage to bargain for escape
Abandon the car and try to swim a nearby river
Shoot himself rather than be taken alive

evt-12-16-1930-herman-lamm.butterflyEffect: Cornered and wounded, Lamm shot himself rather than be captured, ending the career of the man who had pioneered meticulously "cased" bank robberies. His planning method, soon called the Lamm Technique, was studied by later robbers, including John Dillinger's gang, and by the FBI as it built modern bank-robbery investigation.

evt-12-16-1938-adolf-hitler.scenario: It is 16 December 1938 in Nazi Germany. The regime has just instituted the Cross of Honour of the German Mother, a state decoration for women who bear and raise large numbers of children as part of its racial and population policy.
evt-12-16-1938-adolf-hitler.prompt: What grade of the cross would a mother of eight or more children receive?

choices.text: An iron cross, the same as awarded to soldiers
The bronze cross
The silver cross
The gold cross

evt-12-16-1938-adolf-hitler.butterflyEffect: The gold Cross of Honour of the German Mother was reserved for mothers of eight or more children, with silver for six or seven and bronze for four or five. The award was central to Nazi pronatalist propaganda, publicly honouring 'Aryan' motherhood while excluding and persecuting women deemed racially or socially undesirable.

evt-12-16-2011-zhanaozen-massacre.scenario: It is 16 December 2011, Kazakhstan's Independence Day, and you are an oil worker in Zhanaozen who has spent months on strike over wages and working conditions. Police now surround the town square where you and your fellow strikers have gathered.
evt-12-16-2011-zhanaozen-massacre.prompt: What does the standoff between strikers and police become?

choices.text: A violent crackdown that kills at least 14 protesters
A nationwide referendum on oil wages
A peaceful negotiated wage settlement
A quiet truce that lasts through the winter

evt-12-16-2011-zhanaozen-massacre.butterflyEffect: Police opened fire on the crowd, killing at least 14 protesters and injuring many more, with unrest spreading to nearby towns. The massacre became a defining symbol of state repression under President Nazarbayev and drew sharp condemnation from international human rights groups.

evt-12-16-2014-lindt-cafe-siege.scenario: It is the morning of 15 December 2014, and you are working inside the Lindt Chocolate Café in Sydney's Martin Place when a gunman claiming a jihadist cause takes you and the other customers hostage, forcing a black flag into the window.
evt-12-16-2014-lindt-cafe-siege.prompt: How does the seventeen-hour siege come to an end?

choices.text: The government agrees to the gunman's political demands
Hostages negotiate the gunman's peaceful surrender
Police storm the café after hostages break free and shots are fired
The gunman releases everyone unharmed at dawn

evt-12-16-2014-lindt-cafe-siege.butterflyEffect: In the early hours, hostages made a desperate break for the door, prompting police to storm the café; the gunman and two hostages were killed in the chaos. The siege led to a major review of Australia's counter-terrorism and police response protocols.

evt-12-16-2014-pakistani-taliban.scenario: It is the morning of 16 December 2014. Gunmen from the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan have stormed the Army Public School in Peshawar, and the nation is reeling as news spreads of the massacre of students and staff.
evt-12-16-2014-pakistani-taliban.prompt: What major policy change followed this attack in Pakistan?

choices.text: Pakistan withdrew all troops from the tribal areas to negotiate a ceasefire
Pakistan closed its border with Afghanistan permanently
Pakistan lifted its moratorium on capital punishment and launched a national counter-terrorism plan
Pakistan abolished its military court system entirely

evt-12-16-2014-pakistani-taliban.butterflyEffect: The government lifted its moratorium on the death penalty for terrorism cases and launched the National Action Plan, a sweeping counter-terrorism strategy targeting militant financing, hate speech, and madrassa reform. Military operations against militant sanctuaries were also intensified in the attack's aftermath.

evt-12-17-942-william-longsword.scenario: It is 17 December 942 on an island in the Somme River near Picquigny. You accompany William Longsword, Count of Normandy, to a reconciliation meeting with Arnulf I of Flanders, unaware that Arnulf's men are waiting to strike.
evt-12-17-942-william-longsword.prompt: What actually followed William Longsword's assassination?

choices.text: His young son Richard succeeded him, backed by King Louis IV
His brother seized power and expelled all Norsemen
Flanders immediately annexed Normandy outright
Normandy dissolved into warring Viking warbands

evt-12-17-942-william-longsword.butterflyEffect: William's young son Richard, only about ten years old, was recognized as his heir with the backing of the West Frankish king Louis IV, though rival lords tried to exploit his minority to seize control of Normandy. Richard eventually secured his duchy as an adult, and the stability he built helped Normandy grow into the power base that would launch the conquest of England in 1066.

evt-12-17-1790-aztec-sun-stone.scenario: It is December 1790, and cathedral workers repaving the Zócalo in Mexico City have just uncovered a massive carved stone disc, buried since soon after the Conquest. You are a colonial official deciding its fate.
evt-12-17-1790-aztec-sun-stone.prompt: What did authorities decide to do with the newly unearthed Aztec sun stone?

choices.text: Break it apart for use as building stone in the cathedral
Mount it on an exterior wall of the cathedral for public viewing
Rebury it immediately, fearing it might encourage idolatry
Ship it to Madrid as a gift for the Spanish crown

evt-12-17-1790-aztec-sun-stone.butterflyEffect: The stone was mounted on an exterior wall of Mexico City Cathedral, where it remained on public view until 1885, when it was moved to a museum. It later became one of the most recognized symbols of Mexican national identity, reproduced on currency and in countless artworks.

evt-12-17-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: You are a Jewish cotton trader living within General Grant's military department in December 1862, when word spreads of a new order bearing his signature.
evt-12-17-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: What does General Order No. 11 demand of you and other Jewish residents of the district?

choices.text: Confiscation of all trading licenses
Relocation to army-supervised camps
Mandatory registration with Union military authorities
Expulsion from the district within 24 hours

evt-12-17-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The order commanded the expulsion of all Jews from Grant's department within 24 hours, alleging widespread cotton speculation. Jewish leaders appealed directly to Lincoln, who revoked the order within weeks, and the episode haunted Grant politically for years, resurfacing during his 1868 presidential campaign.

evt-12-17-1903-wright-flyer.scenario: It is 17 December 1903 on the windswept dunes near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. You and your brother have spent years testing gliders and a homemade engine, and this cold morning you ready your fragile biplane for another attempt at powered flight.
evt-12-17-1903-wright-flyer.prompt: What do you achieve with this flight attempt?

choices.text: The first successful unpowered glider flight
The first flight carrying a paying passenger
The first sustained powered, controlled flight by a manned aircraft
The first flight across the Atlantic

evt-12-17-1903-wright-flyer.butterflyEffect: The Flyer made the first sustained, controlled flight by a manned powered aircraft, covering 852 feet on its fourth attempt before a gust wrecked it on landing. It never flew again, but it launched the age of aviation and now hangs in the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum.

evt-12-17-1926-1926-lithuanian-coup-d-et.scenario: It is 17 December 1926 in Kaunas. You are an army officer who has just helped seize government buildings and detain President Kazys Grinius, ending Lithuania's parliamentary government.
evt-12-17-1926-1926-lithuanian-coup-d-et.prompt: What did the plotters do with the power they had just seized?

choices.text: Hand power to the Lithuanian Christian Democrats outright
Exile the deposed president to Poland
Restore the Seimas and call immediate new elections
Install Antanas Smetona as president under Nationalist Union rule

evt-12-17-1926-1926-lithuanian-coup-d-et.butterflyEffect: The military installed Antanas Smetona and the small Nationalist Union in power, ending democratic rule. Smetona governed as an increasingly authoritarian leader until the Soviet occupation of Lithuania in 1940.

evt-12-17-1939-world-war-ii.scenario: You are Captain Hans Langsdorff aboard the battle-damaged Admiral Graf Spee, anchored in neutral Montevideo harbour on 17 December 1939, convinced British warships are waiting just beyond the horizon.
evt-12-17-1939-world-war-ii.prompt: What do you order done with your ship rather than risk your crew in another battle?

choices.text: Scuttle the ship in the harbour
Surrender the ship to Uruguayan authorities
Attempt to break out and fight the waiting fleet
Sail for a German-friendly port in South America

evt-12-17-1939-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Langsdorff had the Graf Spee scuttled in the River Plate estuary that evening, then took his own life days later. The destruction of Germany's prized pocket battleship was an early propaganda triumph for the Allies and a blow to Hitler's surface-raider strategy.

evt-12-17-1967-harold-holt.scenario: It is the afternoon of 17 December 1967. Prime Minister Harold Holt wades into rough surf at Cheviot Beach near Portsea, a spot known for dangerous currents, ignoring friends who warn him the conditions are too dangerous.
evt-12-17-1967-harold-holt.prompt: What actually followed Holt's disappearance in the surf?

choices.text: He had resigned that morning and fled overseas
He was never found despite a massive search operation
His body washed ashore several days later
He was rescued by a passing fishing trawler

evt-12-17-1967-harold-holt.butterflyEffect: Despite one of the largest search operations in Australian history, no trace of Holt's body was ever recovered, and his death remains officially a presumed drowning. The mystery spawned enduring conspiracy theories, from shark attack to Chinese submarine abduction, while the Liberal Party moved swiftly to install John Gorton as the new prime minister.

evt-12-17-1970-december-1970-protests-in.scenario: You are a shipyard worker arriving by train in Gdynia on the morning of 17 December 1970, joining thousands protesting sudden price hikes on basic food.
evt-12-17-1970-december-1970-protests-in.prompt: What does the government do as workers step off the trains toward the shipyard gates?

choices.text: Soldiers open fire on the crowd
Police negotiate an immediate wage freeze
The government resigns on the spot
Workers are waved through to march peacefully

evt-12-17-1970-december-1970-protests-in.butterflyEffect: Soldiers opened fire on the crowds emerging from the trains, part of a crackdown that killed at least 44 people along the Baltic coast. The bloodshed forced the ouster of party leader Władysław Gomułka days later, and the massacre became a defining memory invoked by Solidarity a decade afterward.

evt-12-17-2002-second-congo-war.scenario: You are a delegate at the Inter-Congolese Dialogue talks, watching representatives of the government, former rebel movements, and civil society finally put pen to paper in Pretoria on 17 December 2002.
evt-12-17-2002-second-congo-war.prompt: What power-sharing structure does the peace agreement create for the transition?

choices.text: A United Nations trusteeship over the entire country
A rotating presidency shared with Rwanda
A transitional government with one president and four vice presidents
A federal system dividing Congo into ethnic regions

evt-12-17-2002-second-congo-war.butterflyEffect: The Global and All-Inclusive Agreement created a transitional government with President Kabila and four vice presidents drawn from the former warring factions. It paved the way for Congo's first multi-party elections in 2006, though fighting persisted in the eastern provinces for years afterward.

evt-12-17-2003-spaceshipone.scenario: It is 17 December 2003 above the Mojave Desert, exactly a century after the Wright brothers' first flight. You are pilot Brian Binnie, igniting SpaceShipOne's hybrid rocket motor for its first powered flight.
evt-12-17-2003-spaceshipone.prompt: What milestone did this flight achieve for the privately built craft?

choices.text: Its first powered flight, breaking the sound barrier
Its first fully orbital flight around the Earth
An unpowered glide test with the rocket motor left off
Its first crewed flight above 100 kilometres, reaching space

evt-12-17-2003-spaceshipone.butterflyEffect: SpaceShipOne became the first privately developed crewed vehicle to fly faster than the speed of sound. Less than a year later it reached space twice in quick succession, winning the Ansari X Prize and inspiring the commercial spaceflight ventures that followed, including Virgin Galactic.

evt-12-17-2003-international-day-to-end-.scenario: It is 2003 in Seattle. Sex worker rights activists have gathered for a vigil honoring victims of the Green River Killer, many of whom were sex workers whose deaths drew little public attention for years.
evt-12-17-2003-international-day-to-end-.prompt: What did the organizers decide to do with this local vigil going forward?

choices.text: Keep it as a single, one-time local memorial event
Establish it as an annual international day of awareness and remembrance
Focus it solely on lobbying for stricter policing of sex work
Limit it to a private gathering for victims' families only

evt-12-17-2003-international-day-to-end-.butterflyEffect: Activists turned the one-off vigil into an annual observance held every 17 December, now marked worldwide as the International Day to End Violence Against Sex Workers. It has become a recurring platform for demanding safer conditions and an end to the stigma that activists say enables violence against sex workers.

evt-12-17-2010-arab-spring.scenario: It is 17 December 2010 in Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia. A street vendor named Mohamed Bouazizi, humiliated after officials confiscated his goods, has just set himself on fire in front of a government building.
evt-12-17-2010-arab-spring.prompt: What followed Bouazizi's act in the weeks and months after?

choices.text: Unrest stayed confined to Sidi Bouzid for years afterward
Local police quickly contained the unrest with no lasting effect
The government paid Bouazizi's family and the protests dissolved
Protests spread nationwide and across the region, eventually toppling Ben Ali

evt-12-17-2010-arab-spring.butterflyEffect: Protests over Bouazizi's death spread rapidly across Tunisia and then the wider Arab world, toppling President Ben Ali within a month. The unrest cascaded into uprisings against long-ruling leaders in Egypt, Libya, Yemen and beyond, becoming known as the Arab Spring.

evt-12-17-2014-cuba-united-states-relati.scenario: You are a White House staffer on 17 December 2014, watching President Obama address the nation at the same hour Raúl Castro speaks to Cubans in Havana.
evt-12-17-2014-cuba-united-states-relati.prompt: What do the two leaders jointly announce that day?

choices.text: Withdrawal of US forces from Guantanamo Bay
A joint currency union between the two nations
Renewal of diplomatic relations alongside a prisoner exchange
Full and immediate lifting of the trade embargo

evt-12-17-2014-cuba-united-states-relati.butterflyEffect: The surprise announcement paired a prisoner exchange with a pledge to restore diplomatic ties, leading to reopened embassies in 2015 and Obama's historic 2016 visit to Havana. The trade embargo itself remained in place, and many of the thaw's gains were later rolled back under the Trump administration.

evt-12-18-1499-granada.scenario: It is 18 December 1499 in Granada's Albaicín quarter. Cardinal Cisneros's officials are carrying out forced baptisms of Muslim residents, breaking the surrender treaty that had promised religious freedom after the city fell in 1492.
evt-12-18-1499-granada.prompt: What did this uprising in Granada set in motion?

choices.text: Granada's Muslims were granted full religious freedom afterward
Cisneros was recalled to Rome and the policy reversed
It was crushed within days and forced conversions stopped
It sparked a wider revolt across the Alpujarras that took two years to suppress

evt-12-18-1499-granada.butterflyEffect: The revolt spread beyond Granada into the mountainous Alpujarras region, igniting a wider rebellion that took Castilian forces until 1501 to crush. Its suppression led to mass forced conversions across the former Emirate, creating Spain's Morisco population, who would ultimately be expelled from the country entirely between 1609 and 1614.

evt-12-18-1792-thomas-paine.scenario: You are in London on 18 December 1792, reading that Thomas Paine has been convicted in absentia of seditious libel for defending the French Revolution in Rights of Man, Part II. Paine himself is already across the Channel in France.
evt-12-18-1792-thomas-paine.prompt: What became of Paine after his conviction in Britain?

choices.text: He returned to London to stand trial in person
He immediately sailed for America to avoid arrest
He was extradited from France to face British justice
He stayed in France, serving in the National Convention

evt-12-18-1792-thomas-paine.butterflyEffect: Unable to safely return to England, Paine remained in France as an elected member of the National Convention. His British conviction permanently exiled him from his homeland, and within a year the same revolutionary politics that shielded him would land him in a French prison for opposing the execution of Louis XVI.

evt-12-18-1867-angola-new-york.scenario: You are riding in the rearmost car of a Lake Shore Railway train as it crosses the bridge over Big Sister Creek near Angola, New York, when the axle beneath your car snaps and it plunges from the tracks.
evt-12-18-1867-angola-new-york.prompt: What made this crash especially deadly for passengers trapped inside the wrecked cars?

choices.text: A boiler in the locomotive exploded on impact
Freight explosives in the baggage car detonated
The car's onboard stove set the wreckage ablaze
The car flooded instantly with icy creek water

evt-12-18-1867-angola-new-york.butterflyEffect: The wood-and-coal stoves used to heat the cars ignited the splintered wreckage, killing many who might otherwise have survived the fall itself. Public horror at these stove-caused deaths, remembered as the 'Angola Horror,' accelerated American railroads toward safer car heating and construction standards.

evt-12-18-1932-chicago-stadium.scenario: It is 18 December 1932, and a blizzard has forced the NFL playoff between your Chicago Bears and the Portsmouth Spartans indoors at Chicago Stadium, onto a cramped dirt field just 60 yards long with the arena boards serving as sidelines.
evt-12-18-1932-chicago-stadium.prompt: How did officials adapt play to the cramped indoor field?

choices.text: Punting was banned for the entire game
Halftime was extended to an hour to change equipment
The ball was moved inbounds toward the middle after plays near the boards
The field was widened to fit extra players per side

evt-12-18-1932-chicago-stadium.butterflyEffect: The improvised inbounds lines used to move the ball away from the boards directly inspired the NFL's adoption of hash marks the following season. The league also moved the goalposts to the goal line and loosened forward-pass restrictions in 1933, reforms traced back to this one snowbound indoor game.

evt-12-18-1939-world-war-ii.scenario: It's 18 December 1939. You pilot an RAF Wellington bomber, one of two dozen sent in broad daylight without fighter escort to strike German warships near Wilhelmshaven, when Messerschmitt fighters suddenly swarm your formation.
evt-12-18-1939-world-war-ii.prompt: What happens to the RAF's unescorted daylight bombers in this raid?

choices.text: The mission is recalled before making contact with the enemy
RAF fighters arrive in time to drive off the Luftwaffe
Heavy losses force the RAF to abandon unescorted daylight raids
The raid succeeds with minimal losses, sinking two battleships

evt-12-18-1939-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Nearly half the Wellingtons were shot down, exposing how vulnerable unescorted daylight bombers were to fighter defenses. The losses pushed RAF Bomber Command to abandon daylight raids in favor of night bombing, a doctrine that shaped Britain's entire strategic air war against Germany.

evt-12-18-1958-score-satellite.scenario: You are an engineer at Cape Canaveral in December 1958, watching the Atlas rocket carrying the world's first communications satellite, SCORE, lift off into orbit.
evt-12-18-1958-score-satellite.prompt: What historic first did SCORE achieve once it reached orbit?

choices.text: It transmitted the first live television signal from orbit
It sent only a repeating Morse code signal
It broadcast a recorded human voice message from space
It took the first photograph of Earth from space

evt-12-18-1958-score-satellite.butterflyEffect: SCORE relayed a recorded Christmas message from President Eisenhower, the first human voice broadcast from space. The mission proved satellites could store and relay communications, directly paving the way for later relay and broadcast satellites like Telstar.

evt-12-18-1966-epimetheus-moon.scenario: It is December 1966, and you are an astronomer reviewing fresh photographic plates of Saturn, having heard that a new moon called Janus was recently spotted near the rings. You notice another faint object close to where Janus should be.
evt-12-18-1966-epimetheus-moon.prompt: What conclusion do you draw about this second object near Janus?

choices.text: It is the same moon, Janus, observed at a different point in its orbit
It is a small comet passing near Saturn's rings
It is a reflection artifact caused by the telescope's optics
It is a completely separate moon with no relation to Janus

evt-12-18-1966-epimetheus-moon.butterflyEffect: The object was in fact a second moon, later named Epimetheus, but astronomers mistook the two for a single body seen at different points in its orbit. Only in 1978 did observers realize Janus and Epimetheus were separate moons sharing an almost identical orbit—a unique co-orbital pairing found nowhere else in the solar system.

evt-12-18-1999-nasa.scenario: It is December 18, 1999, and you're on NASA's launch team watching an Atlas rocket carry the newly built Terra spacecraft into polar orbit, its five instruments designed to keep watch over the planet for years to come.
evt-12-18-1999-nasa.prompt: What is Terra primarily built to observe from orbit?

choices.text: Earth's climate system, including atmosphere, land, oceans, and energy balance
Military installations of rival nations
Deep-space objects beyond the solar system
Solar flares and space weather near the Sun

evt-12-18-1999-nasa.butterflyEffect: Terra became the flagship of NASA's Earth Observing System, and instruments like MODIS produced decades of continuous data on clouds, vegetation, ice, and pollution. That long, uninterrupted record now underpins much of the world's climate-change science.

evt-12-18-2005-chadian-civil-war-2005-20.scenario: It's 18 December 2005. You are an aide to Chadian President Idriss Déby as reports arrive that rebel forces, allegedly armed and backed from across the border in Sudan, have struck towns in eastern Chad.
evt-12-18-2005-chadian-civil-war-2005-20.prompt: How does Déby's government respond to the rebel offensive?

choices.text: Déby immediately resigns and flees the country
It formally accuses Sudan and declares a state of war
It requests full French military occupation of Chad
It signs an unconditional ceasefire with the rebels

evt-12-18-2005-chadian-civil-war-2005-20.butterflyEffect: Chad publicly accused Sudan's government of arming the rebels and declared a state of war between the two countries, though a full interstate war never materialized. The conflict dragged on for years, entangled with the Darfur crisis next door, until Chad and Sudan signed a peace agreement in 2010.

evt-12-18-2006-2006-2007-southeast-asian.scenario: It's mid-December 2006 in Johor, Malaysia, and monsoon rains intensified by the remnants of Typhoon Utor have pushed rivers over their banks, stranding families on rooftops as water keeps rising.
evt-12-18-2006-2006-2007-southeast-asian.prompt: What does the Malaysian government do as the flooding worsens into January?

choices.text: Diverts the floodwaters directly into Singapore's reservoirs
Launches mass evacuations and declares affected areas disaster zones
Orders the permanent relocation of Johor's entire population
Bans international aid organizations from entering the country

evt-12-18-2006-2006-2007-southeast-asian.butterflyEffect: The floods, among the worst Johor had seen, displaced hundreds of thousands of people and were followed by a second major flood only weeks later. The scale of the disaster pushed Malaysia to invest heavily in flood-mitigation infrastructure and early-warning systems in the years afterward.

evt-12-18-2006-united-arab-emirates.scenario: It is December 2006, and you are among a small electoral college of UAE citizens hand-picked by the rulers to cast a vote in the country's first-ever election, choosing members for the Federal National Council.
evt-12-18-2006-united-arab-emirates.prompt: What did this historic vote actually decide?

choices.text: It created a fully sovereign elected parliament
It selected Dubai's next ruling successor
It chose half the Federal National Council's members, the rest still appointed
It directly elected the President of the UAE

evt-12-18-2006-united-arab-emirates.butterflyEffect: The election filled only 20 of the Federal National Council's 40 seats, with rulers still appointing the rest, and the electorate itself was a small hand-picked group rather than the general public. Subsequent elections in 2011 and beyond gradually widened the franchise, though the Council has remained an advisory body without full legislative power.

evt-12-18-2015-kellingley-colliery.scenario: You are a miner at Kellingley Colliery in North Yorkshire on 18 December 2015, riding the last coal wagon to the surface as the pit shuts its gates for good.
evt-12-18-2015-kellingley-colliery.prompt: What did the closure of Kellingley Colliery mark for Britain?

choices.text: The start of a national miners' strike
The opening of a new state-run coal mine
The end of deep coal mining in Great Britain
The nationalisation of the British coal industry

evt-12-18-2015-kellingley-colliery.butterflyEffect: Kellingley's closure ended deep coal mining in Great Britain entirely, a trade that had powered the Industrial Revolution for over two centuries. It symbolized the country's shift toward gas, nuclear, and renewable energy, while leaving former mining communities searching for new industries.

evt-12-19-1154-henry-ii-of-england.scenario: It is 19 December 1154 in Westminster Abbey. You are a baron watching the young Henry Plantagenet crowned king after two decades of civil war between Stephen and Empress Matilda left England's castles in private hands and royal authority in tatters.
evt-12-19-1154-henry-ii-of-england.prompt: What should the new king do first to restore royal power?

choices.text: Grant the barons permanent control of their wartime castles to keep the peace
Disband the royal army entirely to save money
Order the destruction of castles barons had built without royal license during the war
Divide England between the surviving supporters of Stephen and Matilda

evt-12-19-1154-henry-ii-of-england.butterflyEffect: Henry II demolished unlicensed 'adulterine' castles and reclaimed crown lands, then went further with legal reforms that created the foundations of English common law. His later clash with Thomas Becket and the vast Angevin Empire he built set the stage for centuries of Anglo-French conflict.

evt-12-19-1776-thomas-paine.scenario: It's 19 December 1776. Washington's army has just suffered defeats around New York, enlistments are about to expire, and morale is collapsing as Thomas Paine's new pamphlet begins circulating among the ranks and the public.
evt-12-19-1776-thomas-paine.prompt: What does Paine's pamphlet urge readers to do in this darkest hour of the Revolution?

choices.text: Urge the colonies to accept British terms of surrender
Call for immediate peace negotiations with Britain
Demand that France send troops before any further fighting
Rally support for continuing the war effort despite recent defeats

evt-12-19-1776-thomas-paine.butterflyEffect: Paine's famous opening, "These are the times that try men's souls," rallied support for continuing the fight despite recent losses. Washington had it read aloud to his exhausted troops just before they crossed the Delaware, helping steel them for the victory at Trenton days later.

evt-12-19-1828-nullification-crisis.scenario: It is late 1832. You are President Andrew Jackson, and South Carolina has just declared the federal tariff null and void within its borders, threatening secession if Washington tries to enforce it.
evt-12-19-1828-nullification-crisis.prompt: How do you respond to South Carolina's defiance?

choices.text: Accept South Carolina's right to nullify the law and repeal the tariff entirely
Ignore the ordinance and hope the controversy fades on its own
Immediately expel South Carolina from the Union
Threaten military enforcement while supporting a compromise tariff reduction

evt-12-19-1828-nullification-crisis.butterflyEffect: Jackson backed a Force Bill authorizing military enforcement while Congress passed a compromise tariff crafted by Henry Clay, and South Carolina backed down. The crisis was defused for the moment, but it hardened the states'-rights arguments that would resurface in the secession crisis of 1860–61.

evt-12-19-1843-a-christmas-carol.scenario: It is December 1843 in London, and you are Charles Dickens, determined to get your new ghost story about a miser named Scrooge into readers' hands before Christmas Day itself.
evt-12-19-1843-a-christmas-carol.prompt: What unusual step does Dickens take to guarantee the book reaches shelves in time?

choices.text: He delays publication a full year to add more illustrations
He releases it as a serialized story over twelve monthly installments
He pays for the printing and production himself to rush it out by Christmas
He publishes it anonymously to avoid damaging his reputation

evt-12-19-1843-a-christmas-carol.butterflyEffect: Dickens financed the printing and production of A Christmas Carol himself to control its quality and get it out by 19 December 1843, just days before Christmas. The gamble ate into his profits due to high production costs, but the book was an instant sensation that revived his reputation and helped popularize the modern spirit of Christmas generosity.

evt-12-19-1967-harold-holt.scenario: It is 17 December 1967 at Cheviot Beach near Melbourne. You are with Prime Minister Harold Holt, an experienced swimmer, as he prepares to enter rough, churning surf that local authorities have warned is dangerous that day.
evt-12-19-1967-harold-holt.prompt: What should you do as his companion?

choices.text: Urge him not to swim given the dangerous conditions
Leave him unattended and return to the car
Encourage him to swim further out to test the current
Suggest he swim at night when the water is calmer

evt-12-19-1967-harold-holt.butterflyEffect: Holt swam out into the heavy surf and vanished; despite one of Australia's largest search operations, no trace of him was ever found. He was officially declared dead without an inquest on 19 December, prompting decades of speculation and eventually a formal 2005 coronial inquiry confirming accidental drowning.

evt-12-19-1972-apollo-program.scenario: You are Eugene Cernan, standing on the lunar surface beside the Apollo 17 lander in December 1972, aware that no crewed mission is currently scheduled to follow yours to the Moon.
evt-12-19-1972-apollo-program.prompt: What made this mission distinct from every earlier Apollo landing?

choices.text: It was the first mission flown without a lunar module
It was the first Apollo flight to dock with a space station in orbit
It carried the first trained geologist to walk on the Moon and set records for sample return
It was the first mission to use a lunar rover on the surface

evt-12-19-1972-apollo-program.butterflyEffect: Apollo 17 included Harrison Schmitt, the only professional geologist to walk on the Moon, and returned the largest haul of lunar samples of the program. It also marked the last crewed lunar landing of the 20th century, as budget cuts ended Apollo and no human returned to the Moon for over fifty years.

evt-12-19-1974-nelson-rockefeller.scenario: It's 19 December 1974 in Washington. You watch Nelson Rockefeller take the oath of office to become Vice President under President Gerald Ford, less than a year and a half after Spiro Agnew's resignation.
evt-12-19-1974-nelson-rockefeller.prompt: How was Rockefeller placed into the vice presidency?

choices.text: Appointed unilaterally by the Senate Majority Leader
Elected alongside Ford in the 1972 general election
Nominated by Ford and confirmed by a majority vote in both houses of Congress
Chosen directly by the Electoral College after Agnew's resignation

evt-12-19-1974-nelson-rockefeller.butterflyEffect: Under the 25th Amendment, Ford nominated Rockefeller and Congress confirmed him by majority vote in both houses. It marked the first time in American history that both the president and vice president held office without being elected to it, a pairing that lasted until the 1976 election.

evt-12-19-1981-penlee-lifeboat-disaster.scenario: It is the night of 19 December 1981 off Cornwall. Hurricane-force winds batter the coast as you and your fellow volunteer crew launch the lifeboat Solomon Browne toward the disabled coaster Union Star.
evt-12-19-1981-penlee-lifeboat-disaster.prompt: What must the lifeboat crew attempt as they close on the stricken vessel?

choices.text: Return to port until the storm passed and conditions improved
Hold position offshore and wait for a helicopter to complete the rescue alone
Get alongside the coaster repeatedly to take survivors off by hand
Attempt to attach a tow line and pull the coaster to harbour

evt-12-19-1981-penlee-lifeboat-disaster.butterflyEffect: The Solomon Browne came alongside Union Star repeatedly in ferocious seas and succeeded in taking off four people before both vessels were lost with all hands, killing sixteen people including eight volunteer lifeboatmen. The disaster remains the RNLI's worst single loss of life and led to lasting reviews of small-boat rescue tactics and equipment.

evt-12-19-1984-sino-british-joint-declar.scenario: It is December 1984 and you are part of the British delegation finalizing the treaty that will hand Hong Kong's sovereignty to China in 1997. Hong Kong residents are anxious about their future under Communist rule.
evt-12-19-1984-sino-british-joint-declar.prompt: What guarantee must the declaration secure for Hong Kong's way of life?

choices.text: Immediate full democratic elections for Hong Kong's legislature
A promise of 50 years of autonomy and an unchanged way of life under 'one country, two systems'
Full independence for Hong Kong as a separate nation
Continued British sovereignty over Hong Kong Island indefinitely

evt-12-19-1984-sino-british-joint-declar.butterflyEffect: The treaty promised Hong Kong fifty years of autonomy under a 'one country, two systems' framework, later enshrined in the Basic Law. That autonomy was tested repeatedly, culminating in the 2019 protests and the 2020 National Security Law, which many argued undermined the pledge decades before it was due to expire in 2047.

evt-12-19-1997-silkair-flight-185.scenario: It's 19 December 1997. You are part of the international team examining wreckage pulled from Sumatra's Musi River after a Boeing 737 fell from cruising altitude nine minutes after its final radio contact.
evt-12-19-1997-silkair-flight-185.prompt: What did investigators ultimately conclude about the cause of the crash?

choices.text: A bomb planted aboard the aircraft was identified as the cause
A rudder mechanical fault, similar to other 737 incidents, was confirmed as the cause
Indonesian and U.S. investigators disagreed, and no cause was ever officially agreed upon
Both governments jointly confirmed engine failure caused the crash

evt-12-19-1997-silkair-flight-185.butterflyEffect: Indonesian investigators listed the cause as undetermined, while U.S. National Transportation Safety Board investigators believed the evidence pointed to deliberate control input by the pilot; the two sides never reached agreement. The unresolved dispute made it one of aviation history's most contested investigations, often compared to the later EgyptAir Flight 990 inquiry.

evt-12-19-1998-bill-clinton.scenario: It is 19 December 1998, and you are a member of the House of Representatives about to cast your vote on articles of impeachment against President Bill Clinton, stemming from his conduct in the Monica Lewinsky matter.
evt-12-19-1998-bill-clinton.prompt: What charges are contained in the articles the House is voting on?

choices.text: Abuse of pardon power and obstruction of Congress
Treason and bribery in foreign policy dealings
Tax evasion and campaign finance fraud
Perjury before a grand jury and obstruction of justice

evt-12-19-1998-bill-clinton.butterflyEffect: The House approved articles charging Clinton with perjury before a grand jury and obstruction of justice, making him only the second U.S. president impeached, after Andrew Johnson. The Senate acquitted him in February 1999 and he served out his term, but the episode set a precedent that shaped how later impeachment battles were fought along partisan lines.

evt-12-19-1999-space-shuttle-discovery.scenario: It is 19 December 1999, and you are an astronaut strapped into Space Shuttle Discovery on the STS-103 mission, a servicing call to a famous but ailing orbiting observatory.
evt-12-19-1999-space-shuttle-discovery.prompt: What is the primary task awaiting your crew once you reach the telescope?

choices.text: Replace failing gyroscopes and instruments on the Hubble Space Telescope
Deploy a brand-new communications satellite into orbit
Test a new docking system for the future International Space Station
Retrieve a failed weather satellite for return to Earth

evt-12-19-1999-space-shuttle-discovery.butterflyEffect: Discovery's crew replaced Hubble's failed gyroscopes, computer, and other components during a series of spacewalks, restoring the telescope to full operation after it had been shut down for safety. The repair kept Hubble producing landmark images and data for another decade-plus, cementing its legacy before later servicing missions extended it further.

evt-12-19-2001-1998-2002-argentine-great.scenario: It is 19 December 2001, and you stand among thousands of Argentines banging pots in the streets of Buenos Aires, furious that a freeze on bank withdrawals has locked away your savings while the economy collapses around you.
evt-12-19-2001-1998-2002-argentine-great.prompt: How did President Fernando de la Rúa respond to the escalating riots that night?

choices.text: He declared a state of siege to restore order
He resigned immediately without further action
He went out to negotiate directly with the crowds
He called for new elections within the week

evt-12-19-2001-1998-2002-argentine-great.butterflyEffect: De la Rúa declared a state of siege, hoping to restore order, but the move only enraged protesters further and triggered even larger demonstrations. He resigned the next day and fled the Casa Rosada by helicopter, opening a chaotic stretch in which Argentina had five presidents in two weeks and ultimately defaulted on its foreign debt.

evt-12-19-2005-chalk-s-ocean-airways-fli.scenario: It's 19 December 2005. You watch a Chalk's Ocean Airways Grumman Turbo Mallard, a seaplane design dating to the 1940s, lift off from Miami Beach bound for Bimini with 18 passengers and two crew aboard.
evt-12-19-2005-chalk-s-ocean-airways-fli.prompt: What caused the aircraft to break apart in flight moments after takeoff?

choices.text: A bird strike disabled both engines shortly after takeoff
An onboard fire spread from the cargo hold to the wing structure
The pilot lost control after a sudden storm squall
Metal fatigue caused the starboard wing to separate from the fuselage

evt-12-19-2005-chalk-s-ocean-airways-fli.butterflyEffect: Investigators traced the disaster to metal fatigue in the starboard wing, which separated from the fuselage. All 20 aboard died, and the crash led to intensified scrutiny of aging seaplane fleets; Chalk's, one of the world's oldest airlines, ceased operations soon after.

evt-12-19-2013-european-space-agency.scenario: It is 19 December 2013, and you are a mission engineer at the European Space Agency, watching a Soyuz rocket climb away from French Guiana carrying a satellite bound for the L2 point beyond Earth's orbit.
evt-12-19-2013-european-space-agency.prompt: What was this satellite, named Gaia, primarily designed to accomplish?

choices.text: Search for exoplanets by watching them cross in front of distant stars
Land on a comet to study its composition
Create a precise 3D map of over a billion stars in the Milky Way
Measure the cosmic microwave background radiation across the sky

evt-12-19-2013-european-space-agency.butterflyEffect: Gaia set out to build the most precise three-dimensional map ever made of the Milky Way, tracking the positions, distances, and motions of over a billion stars. Over the following decade its data reshaped astronomers' understanding of the galaxy's structure and history, and uncovered thousands of previously unknown asteroids and exoplanet candidates.

evt-12-19-2013-gaia-spacecraft.scenario: It is 19 December 2013 at Europe's Kourou spaceport, and you watch the Gaia spacecraft lift off atop a Soyuz rocket, bound for a vantage point beyond the Moon's orbit.
evt-12-19-2013-gaia-spacecraft.prompt: What is Gaia's core scientific mission once it reaches its observing position?

choices.text: Precisely map the positions and motions of about a billion stars in 3D
Photograph the surface of Mars in high resolution
Search for radio signals from extraterrestrial civilizations
Detect gravitational waves from colliding black holes

evt-12-19-2013-gaia-spacecraft.butterflyEffect: Gaia spent over a decade precisely measuring the positions, distances, and motions of roughly a billion stars, building the most detailed 3D map of the Milky Way ever made. Its data reshaped understanding of galactic structure, stellar populations, and even helped detect exoplanets and asteroids, with scientists still mining the catalogue after the mission ended in 2025.

evt-12-19-2016-andrei-karlov.scenario: It is 19 December 2016 at an art gallery in Ankara. Russian Ambassador Andrei Karlov is mid-speech at a photo exhibition when a man in a suit near the back, later revealed to be an off-duty police officer, begins shouting about Aleppo and Syria.
evt-12-19-2016-andrei-karlov.prompt: As security, what should this outburst prompt you to do?

choices.text: Immediately move to restrain or remove the shouting man before he can act further
Wait until the speech ends to ask him to leave quietly
Escort the ambassador closer to the man to calm the situation
Assume it is a scripted part of the exhibition and continue as planned

evt-12-19-2016-andrei-karlov.butterflyEffect: The assailant drew a concealed handgun and shot Karlov fatally before being killed by responding police. Many feared the assassination would rupture Russian-Turkish relations, but instead Moscow and Ankara drew closer, jointly sponsoring the Astana peace talks on Syria in the following months.

evt-12-19-2016-2016-berlin-truck-attack.scenario: It is the evening of 19 December 2016, and you are a shopper at the Christmas market beside Berlin's Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church when a heavy truck suddenly veers off the road and plows through the crowded stalls.
evt-12-19-2016-2016-berlin-truck-attack.prompt: What ultimately brought the truck's deadly run through the market to a halt?

choices.text: Police officers shot out the truck's tires
The truck's automatic braking system engaged and stopped it
A bystander climbed aboard and wrestled the wheel away
The truck simply ran out of fuel

evt-12-19-2016-2016-berlin-truck-attack.butterflyEffect: The truck's automatic emergency braking system stopped it before it could cause even greater harm. The attacker, Anis Amri, fled the scene and was killed four days later in a shootout with police near Milan, while the attack intensified Germany's national debate over asylum policy, deportation procedures, and security coordination between federal states.

evt-12-20-1951-experimental-breeder-reac.scenario: It is 1:50 p.m. on 20 December 1951, in the Idaho desert. You are an engineer at Experimental Breeder Reactor I, about to test whether a nuclear reactor can generate usable electricity for the very first time.
evt-12-20-1951-experimental-breeder-reac.prompt: What should the test aim to demonstrate?

choices.text: That the reactor can immediately power an entire town's grid
That the reactor can generate enough electricity to light a handful of bulbs
That the reactor can produce weapons-grade plutonium at scale
That the reactor can safely heat residential water supplies

evt-12-20-1951-experimental-breeder-reac.butterflyEffect: The reactor successfully lit four 200-watt light bulbs, making it one of the world's first nuclear plants to generate electricity. Within years EBR-I could power its own building and briefly the town of Arco, proving the concept behind the commercial nuclear power industry that followed.

evt-12-20-1970-koza-riot.scenario: It is the night of 20 December 1970 in Koza, Okinawa. You stand among thousands of Okinawans after a drunk US serviceman has struck a local man with his car, one incident too many in years of resentment toward the American military presence.
evt-12-20-1970-koza-riot.prompt: What actually follows as the crowd's anger boils over into riot?

choices.text: US forces immediately withdraw all troops from Okinawa
Japanese police disperse the crowd within minutes without incident
Crowds burn dozens of American vehicles and clash with military police at Kadena
The US grants Okinawa full independence the following week

evt-12-20-1970-koza-riot.butterflyEffect: Roughly 5,000 Okinawans clashed with US military police, burning some 80 vehicles and damaging buildings on Kadena Air Base before order was restored. The riot became a lasting symbol of Okinawan anger at US administration and intensified pressure that fed into the island's 1972 reversion to Japanese sovereignty and later debates over reducing the US base presence.

evt-12-20-1973-assassination-of-luis-car.scenario: It is 20 December 1973 in Madrid. You are walking near a quiet street when a massive explosion rips through the morning air, hurling a car high above the rooftops moments after Prime Minister Luis Carrero Blanco's vehicle passed by.
evt-12-20-1973-assassination-of-luis-car.prompt: What does the assassination mean for Franco's plans for Spain's political future?

choices.text: The Spanish military seizes power in a coup that day
It removes Franco's designated successor, disrupting his plan for continuity
Spain declares a republic within the week
Franco immediately abdicates in favor of Juan Carlos

evt-12-20-1973-assassination-of-luis-car.butterflyEffect: ETA's bombing killed Carrero Blanco, Franco's chosen hardline successor meant to preserve the regime unchanged after his death. His removal left a leadership vacuum that, after Franco died in 1975, helped open space for King Juan Carlos and reformers to steer Spain toward democracy rather than continued dictatorship.

evt-12-20-1984-summit-tunnel-fire.scenario: It's the afternoon of 20 December 1984. A freight train hauling tankers of petrol has derailed deep inside the Summit Tunnel and burst into flames, and you are the fire commander standing at the portal deciding how to fight it.
evt-12-20-1984-summit-tunnel-fire.prompt: What strategy do you order to tackle the blaze?

choices.text: Hold crews back and let the fire burn itself out under controlled conditions
Abandon the site and let the tunnel collapse rather than risk any firefighters
Send firefighters deep into the tunnel with breathing apparatus to douse the tankers directly
Blast open a new ventilation shaft immediately to vent the fumes

evt-12-20-1984-summit-tunnel-fire.butterflyEffect: Commanders held crews back at the portals and let the fire burn itself out under controlled conditions rather than risk sending firefighters into the toxic smoke. The fire raged for days, yet the tunnel's brick lining survived largely intact, and it reopened after repairs within a year — a case still studied for how tunnels can withstand extreme fire.

evt-12-20-1985-pope-john-paul-ii.scenario: It's December 1985 in Rome, and the crowds of young Catholics who gathered for the Holy Year celebrations have only just dispersed. You're a Vatican aide advising Pope John Paul II on how to keep their enthusiasm alive.
evt-12-20-1985-pope-john-paul-ii.prompt: What does the Pope announce to build on this momentum?

choices.text: The creation of an annual global World Youth Day
A papal encyclical focused on young people
A Vatican-run television network for youth
A new religious order dedicated to youth ministry

evt-12-20-1985-pope-john-paul-ii.butterflyEffect: John Paul II established World Youth Day as a recurring international gathering for Catholic youth. The first international edition drew crowds to Buenos Aires in 1987, and the event grew into a massive global fixture, drawing millions of young pilgrims to host cities for decades afterward.

evt-12-20-1987-mv-dona-paz.scenario: It is the night of 20 December 1987. You are among thousands packed aboard the ferry Doña Paz as it sails through the Tablas Strait, far more crowded than its official manifest shows, when a tanker looms out of the darkness.
evt-12-20-1987-mv-dona-paz.prompt: What turns this collision into the deadliest peacetime sea disaster in history?

choices.text: The ferry was struck by a second, unrelated vessel
The tanker was carrying gasoline, which ignited and set the ferry ablaze
A typhoon capsized both vessels moments after impact
The ferry's engines exploded independently of the collision

evt-12-20-1987-mv-dona-paz.butterflyEffect: The tanker Vector was carrying gasoline that ignited on impact, engulfing the overcrowded ferry in flames within minutes. Official records listed barely over 1,500 aboard, but the true toll was likely over 4,000, exposing chronic overloading in Philippine ferry travel and prompting later, if unevenly enforced, safety reforms.

evt-12-20-1989-united-states-invasion-of.scenario: It is the early hours of 20 December 1989, and you are a U.S. Army Ranger boarding a transport plane bound for Panama as Operation Just Cause begins.
evt-12-20-1989-united-states-invasion-of.prompt: What is the operation's primary objective?

choices.text: Depose General Manuel Noriega
Seize control of the Panama Canal Zone
Evacuate American citizens only
Support a coup led by rival Panamanian generals

evt-12-20-1989-united-states-invasion-of.butterflyEffect: U.S. forces overwhelmed the Panama Defense Forces within days, though Noriega evaded capture for weeks by taking refuge in the Vatican's embassy before surrendering in January 1990. He was later convicted on drug trafficking charges in a U.S. federal court, while Guillermo Endara was installed as president, reshaping Panama's political future.

evt-12-20-1995-dayton-agreement.scenario: It is 20 December 1995. You are a NATO officer in Bosnia as the UN peacekeeping mandate lapses and command formally passes to a new multinational force tasked with enforcing the peace just sealed at Dayton.
evt-12-20-1995-dayton-agreement.prompt: What happens as NATO's Implementation Force takes charge from the UN in Bosnia?

choices.text: The United Nations retains sole command of peacekeeping forces
The European Union takes over all military operations in Bosnia
Russian forces alone are given command of the peacekeeping mission
NATO's IFOR deploys tens of thousands of troops to enforce the ceasefire lines

evt-12-20-1995-dayton-agreement.butterflyEffect: IFOR deployed roughly 60,000 troops under NATO command, the alliance's first major ground operation, to separate former warring factions and enforce the Dayton ceasefire lines. It stabilized the country enough for reconstruction and elections to begin, later handing over to the smaller SFOR mission.

evt-12-20-1995-american-airlines-flight-.scenario: It's the night of 20 December 1995 and you're in the cockpit of Flight 965, descending toward Cali, Colombia. Air traffic control has just offered a shortcut, and you're reprogramming the flight computer's next waypoint under time pressure.
evt-12-20-1995-american-airlines-flight-.prompt: What error in the computer entry sends the aircraft off course toward the mountains?

choices.text: A fuel gauge malfunction forces an emergency descent
Entering "R" selects the wrong beacon, sending the plane off course
The crew misreads the altimeter and descends too early
The crew skips the pre-landing checklist entirely

evt-12-20-1995-american-airlines-flight-.butterflyEffect: The crew entered "R," intending the Rozo beacon, but the computer selected a different waypoint named Romeo far to the east, turning the aircraft toward high terrain in darkness. The crash killed 159 people and became a landmark case for cockpit automation risk, accelerating the aviation industry's push to mandate terrain awareness and warning systems (TAWS) on airliners.

evt-12-20-1999-handover-of-macau.scenario: It's midnight on 20 December 1999, and you stand in Macau's packed Cultural Centre as Portuguese officials prepare to lower their flag after 442 years of colonial rule, handing the territory to China.
evt-12-20-1999-handover-of-macau.prompt: What governing model does China promise to apply to Macau going forward?

choices.text: Temporary United Nations trusteeship pending a future referendum
Full and immediate integration into mainland China's legal and economic system
"One country, two systems," preserving Macau's own laws and economy for 50 years
Continued Portuguese administration of economic affairs alongside Chinese sovereignty

evt-12-20-1999-handover-of-macau.butterflyEffect: Macau became a Special Administrative Region under the "one country, two systems" model already used for Hong Kong, keeping its own currency, laws, and capitalist economy for fifty years. Freed from colonial constraints and boosted by loosened gambling licensing, Macau went on to become the world's largest gambling hub, dwarfing Las Vegas in revenue.

evt-12-20-1999-macau.scenario: It is 20 December 1999, and you stand in Macau's Cultural Center as the Portuguese flag is lowered for the last time after 442 years of colonial administration.
evt-12-20-1999-macau.prompt: What political status does Macau receive under Chinese sovereignty?

choices.text: Administration as a United Nations trust territory
Direct annexation as an ordinary Chinese city
Full independence as a new nation
A Special Administrative Region under 'one country, two systems'

evt-12-20-1999-macau.butterflyEffect: Macau became China's second Special Administrative Region after Hong Kong, keeping its own currency, legal system, and Portuguese as a co-official language for 50 years under 'one country, two systems.' Edmund Ho became its first Chief Executive, and the territory's casino industry soon grew to overtake Las Vegas as the world's largest gambling hub.

evt-12-20-2004-northern-bank-robbery.scenario: It is the evening of 20 December 2004, and you are a Northern Bank official whose family has just been taken hostage by armed men who then walk you into the Belfast headquarters after hours.
evt-12-20-2004-northern-bank-robbery.prompt: What do the robbers force bank staff to do once inside?

choices.text: Hand over confidential customer records
Open the vault and load sterling banknotes into a van
Wire millions electronically to overseas accounts
Reveal security codes to a rival bank

evt-12-20-2004-northern-bank-robbery.butterflyEffect: The gang escaped with £26.5 million in cash, one of the largest robberies in UK history. Suspicion quickly fell on the IRA, straining the fragile Northern Ireland peace process, and Northern Bank responded by withdrawing and redesigning all its banknotes to render the stolen currency worthless.
