evt-12-20-2007-pablo-picasso.scenario: It is 20 December 2007, and you are a guard at the São Paulo Museum of Art when two masked men walk in before closing time and pull out weapons in front of a gallery of European masterpieces.
evt-12-20-2007-pablo-picasso.prompt: Which Picasso work do the thieves cut from its frame and carry out?

choices.text: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
The Weeping Woman
Portrait of Suzanne Bloch
Guernica

evt-12-20-2007-pablo-picasso.butterflyEffect: The men also stole a Dalí painting before vanishing within seconds. Brazilian police recovered both works within weeks in early 2008, but the brazen daytime heist exposed serious gaps in the museum's security and forced a major overhaul of its protection systems.

evt-12-20-2007-elizabeth-ii.scenario: It's 20 December 2007, and royal correspondents are quietly checking their notes against the life of Queen Victoria. You're one of them, comparing dates as Buckingham Palace stays silent on the milestone.
evt-12-20-2007-elizabeth-ii.prompt: What record does Elizabeth II reach today, overtaking Victoria?

choices.text: She becomes the longest-reigning monarch in British history
She becomes the first British monarch to abdicate
She becomes the first female Head of the Commonwealth
She becomes the oldest monarch in British history by age

evt-12-20-2007-elizabeth-ii.butterflyEffect: Elizabeth II became the oldest monarch in British history by age, at 81 years and 243 days, surpassing Victoria's lifespan on the throne. She would not break Victoria's separate record for length of reign until 2015, when her 63-year, 216-day reign became the longest of any British sovereign.

evt-12-20-2016-aerosucre-flight-157.scenario: It is 20 December 2016 at Germán Olano Airport, Puerto Carreño. You are the pilot of an Aerosucre Boeing 727 cargo flight, throttling up for takeoff on a runway that suddenly feels too short as your speed lags behind expectations.
evt-12-20-2016-aerosucre-flight-157.prompt: What causes the aircraft to overrun the runway and crash?

choices.text: The aircraft was overloaded and failed to gain sufficient speed before the runway ended
Severe crosswinds pushed the aircraft off the runway centerline
A flock of birds struck the windshield during rotation
A sudden engine fire forced an aborted takeoff too late

evt-12-20-2016-aerosucre-flight-157.butterflyEffect: The heavily loaded 727 failed to reach safe takeoff speed in time, struck the perimeter fence and other obstacles, and crashed short of clearing the area, killing five of the six aboard. The investigation focused on cargo loading and weight practices, pushing Colombian regulators to tighten oversight of cargo carrier weight verification.

evt-12-20-2019-united-states-space-force.scenario: It's December 2019, and Congress has folded a long-debated proposal into the annual defense policy bill. You're a Pentagon planner watching a brand-new military branch take shape under the Department of the Air Force.
evt-12-20-2019-united-states-space-force.prompt: What historic distinction does the new Space Force receive today?

choices.text: It becomes the first new U.S. armed service branch since 1947
It fully replaces the U.S. Air Force
It becomes an independent Cabinet-level department
It merges NASA and the Pentagon into one agency

evt-12-20-2019-united-states-space-force.butterflyEffect: The Space Force became the first new U.S. armed service branch since the Air Force split from the Army in 1947. Organized like the Marine Corps under the Navy, it inherited satellite, missile-warning, and space-tracking missions from the Air Force, reshaping how the Pentagon budgets and plans for orbital warfare.

evt-12-20-2024-2024-magdeburg-car-attack.scenario: It is late December 2024, and you are part of the federal prosecutor's team in Germany deciding how to charge the driver who tore through Magdeburg's Christmas market with an SUV. Evidence shows an anti-Islam motive but no organized network behind him.
evt-12-20-2024-2024-magdeburg-car-attack.prompt: How do German prosecutors legally classify the attack?

choices.text: As an act of terrorism
As an accidental traffic collision
As a hate crime under new legislation
As a rampage, not terrorism

evt-12-20-2024-2024-magdeburg-car-attack.butterflyEffect: The Federal Prosecutor General ruled it a rampage (Amoktat) rather than an act of terrorism, since no organized extremist network was found. The driver, Taleb Al-Abdulmohsen, was convicted of six counts of murder and multiple attempted murders, receiving a life sentence in June 2026. The classification shaped debate in Germany over how to define lone-actor violence.

evt-12-21-1620-pilgrims-plymouth-colony.scenario: It is 21 December 1620. After weeks anchored in Cape Cod Bay searching for a defensible site, your Mayflower landing party finally steps ashore at a harbor with cleared fields and fresh water.
evt-12-21-1620-pilgrims-plymouth-colony.prompt: With winter already brutal, what should you do next to give the colony a chance at survival?

choices.text: Begin building shelters right away despite the cold
Move further south to a warmer coastline first
Sail back to England before winter worsens
Wait offshore on the Mayflower until spring

evt-12-21-1620-pilgrims-plymouth-colony.butterflyEffect: The Pilgrims began building shelters immediately, though nearly half the settlers died before spring from disease and exposure. The survivors' alliance with the Wampanoag and eventual harvest became the basis of the Plymouth Colony and the American Thanksgiving tradition.

evt-12-21-1826-mexican-texas.scenario: It is 21 December 1826 in Nacogdoches. You are Haden Edwards, an American land empresario locked in a dispute with Mexican authorities over settler land titles, and you have just declared the independent Republic of Fredonia.
evt-12-21-1826-mexican-texas.prompt: What do you do to try to defend your new republic against Mexican forces?

choices.text: Appeal directly to the government of Spain for support
Negotiate an autonomy agreement with the Mexican governor
Petition Stephen F. Austin's colonists to immediately join the rebellion
Ally with Cherokee leader Richard Fields against Mexican authority

evt-12-21-1826-mexican-texas.butterflyEffect: Edwards allied with Cherokee leader Richard Fields, but the alliance faltered and Stephen F. Austin's militia sided with Mexico. By January 1827 Mexican troops crushed the rebellion and Edwards fled to Louisiana, but the episode exposed the deep friction between Anglo settlers and Mexico City that would erupt again in the Texas Revolution a decade later.

evt-12-21-1872-hms-challenger-1858.scenario: It is December 1872 at Portsmouth. HMS Challenger, stripped of most of her guns and fitted with laboratories, is ready to depart on a Royal Society-organized voyage around the world's oceans.
evt-12-21-1872-hms-challenger-1858.prompt: What is the expedition's central scientific objective as you set sail?

choices.text: Chart new trade routes for merchant shipping
Search for sunken treasure along known wrecks
Map coastlines for future naval bases
Survey the ocean depths and catalogue marine life worldwide

evt-12-21-1872-hms-challenger-1858.butterflyEffect: Over nearly four years, the Challenger expedition surveyed ocean depths, currents, and marine life across the globe, discovering thousands of new species and measuring the deep trench later named the Challenger Deep. The voyage's findings founded the modern science of oceanography.

evt-12-21-1879-nora-helmer.scenario: You sit in the Royal Theatre in Copenhagen on 21 December 1879, watching Betty Hennings play Nora in the premiere of Ibsen's A Doll's House. As the final scene ends, Nora walks out on her husband and children, and the door slams shut on stage.
evt-12-21-1879-nora-helmer.prompt: How did theatres and audiences across Europe actually respond to that ending?

choices.text: The ending caused such an uproar that theatres pressed for a rewritten, happier version
Actresses refused further performances of the role of Nora
The play was hailed as a defense of traditional domestic life
Danish authorities banned the play outright

evt-12-21-1879-nora-helmer.butterflyEffect: The slammed door became one of the most debated moments in 19th-century theatre, igniting fierce arguments about marriage and women's independence. The scandal was so intense that some German productions pressured Ibsen into approving an altered, happier ending, which he later disowned. A Doll's House went on to become a founding text of modern realist drama and early feminist thought.

evt-12-21-1923-nepal-britain-treaty-of-1.scenario: It is 21 December 1923 at Singha Durbar. After decades of careful diplomacy under Chandra Shumsher, you finalize a treaty with British negotiators defining Nepal's place among nations.
evt-12-21-1923-nepal-britain-treaty-of-1.prompt: What key provision does this treaty formally grant Nepal?

choices.text: Protectorate status under the British Crown
Control over British Gurkha recruitment only
The right to conduct its own independent foreign policy
Full incorporation into British India

evt-12-21-1923-nepal-britain-treaty-of-1.butterflyEffect: The treaty was Britain's first formal acknowledgment that Nepal could conduct its own foreign policy as an independent nation. It was recorded with the League of Nations in 1925, cementing Nepal's sovereign status well before most Asian states achieved similar recognition.

evt-12-21-1934-lieutenant-kije-prokofiev.scenario: It is 1933 in Leningrad, and Belgoskino has offered you, Sergei Prokofiev, your very first film commission: music for the satirical comedy Lieutenant Kijé.
evt-12-21-1934-lieutenant-kije-prokofiev.prompt: How do you approach scoring a film satire about a fictitious officer invented by bureaucratic error?

choices.text: Compose only somber, funereal themes throughout
Decline and recommend another composer instead
Reuse an existing symphony without new composition
Write witty, folk-inflected music that satirizes military pomp

evt-12-21-1934-lieutenant-kije-prokofiev.butterflyEffect: Prokofiev wove witty, folk-tinged melodies through the score, mocking military pomp to match the film's satire of Tsarist bureaucracy. He later reworked the music into an orchestral suite that became one of his most beloved concert works, helping legitimize film scoring as serious composition.

evt-12-21-1937-snow-white-and-the-seven-.scenario: It is the evening of 21 December 1937 at the Carthay Circle Theatre in Los Angeles. Walt Disney watches nervously as the lights dim on his enormous gamble: the first full-length cel-animated feature ever attempted.
evt-12-21-1937-snow-white-and-the-seven-.prompt: How did the premiere audience and Hollywood react to Disney's risky feature-length cartoon?

choices.text: It received a standing ovation and became a massive box-office success
It flopped commercially and nearly bankrupted the Disney studio
Several states moved to ban the film's distribution
Critics dismissed it as a minor children's curiosity with no future

evt-12-21-1937-snow-white-and-the-seven-.butterflyEffect: The film received a standing ovation and went on to become the highest-grossing film of 1938, silencing skeptics who had mocked the project as 'Disney's Folly.' Its success bankrolled Disney's new Burbank studio and proved animated features were commercially viable, opening the door to Pinocchio, Fantasia, and Bambi in the years that followed.

evt-12-21-1963-greek-cypriots.scenario: It is 21 December 1963 at a police checkpoint in Nicosia. Greek Cypriot officers attempt to search Turkish Cypriot women, and the confrontation is spiraling into a wider standoff between the island's two communities.
evt-12-21-1963-greek-cypriots.prompt: What did this checkpoint incident trigger in the days that followed?

choices.text: It triggered an immediate Turkish military invasion of the island
UN peacekeepers were deployed to Nicosia within hours of the incident
It was resolved peacefully through same-day negotiation between both communities
It sparked intercommunal violence that collapsed the joint constitutional government

evt-12-21-1963-greek-cypriots.butterflyEffect: The incident ignited days of intercommunal violence remembered as 'Bloody Christmas,' shattering the fragile power-sharing government set up at independence in 1960. Turkish Cypriots withdrew from the constitutional arrangement and Nicosia was divided by the 'Green Line,' a partition that foreshadowed the island's permanent division after 1974.

evt-12-21-1965-united-nations.scenario: It is 21 December 1965 at the UN General Assembly. You are a delegate voting on a new convention meant to bind member states to a shared human rights standard.
evt-12-21-1965-united-nations.prompt: What does this newly adopted convention commit signatory states to do?

choices.text: Formally endorse existing systems of racial segregation
Work to eliminate racial discrimination in law and policy
Focus exclusively on religious rather than racial discrimination
Address discrimination only within colonial territories

evt-12-21-1965-united-nations.butterflyEffect: The International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination obligated states to outlaw discriminatory laws and promote equality, backed by a monitoring committee. It went on to become one of the most widely ratified UN human rights treaties, shaping national civil rights and anti-discrimination laws for decades.

evt-12-21-1968-apollo-8.scenario: It is 21 December 1968 at Kennedy Space Center. You are strapped into the Apollo 8 capsule with Frank Borman and Jim Lovell, moments from launch on the first crewed mission to leave Earth's orbit and travel to the Moon.
evt-12-21-1968-apollo-8.prompt: What did the crew famously do days later as they orbited the Moon on Christmas Eve?

choices.text: They planted a flag on the lunar surface
They broadcast a call for a Christmas truce in Vietnam
They read from the Book of Genesis and photographed Earthrise
They released an unmanned probe to land on the Moon

evt-12-21-1968-apollo-8.butterflyEffect: Borman, Lovell, and Anders read from the Book of Genesis live to what was then the largest television audience in history, and Anders captured the iconic Earthrise photograph. The mission's success proved lunar orbit and navigation were achievable, clearing the way for Apollo 11's landing just seven months later.

evt-12-21-1988-antonov-an-225-mriya.scenario: It's 21 December 1988 at Kyiv's Gostomel airfield. You are the test pilot preparing to fly the massive six-engined An-225 Mriya on its maiden flight.
evt-12-21-1988-antonov-an-225-mriya.prompt: What was this record-breaking aircraft originally built to carry?

choices.text: The Buran space shuttle orbiter
Airborne paratroop divisions
Bulk grain exports
Intercontinental ballistic missiles

evt-12-21-1988-antonov-an-225-mriya.butterflyEffect: Mriya was designed specifically to piggyback the Soviet Buran space shuttle orbiter and its boosters between factories and launch sites. When the Buran program collapsed with the USSR, the giant transport found new life hauling oversized commercial and humanitarian cargo worldwide, until it was destroyed by Russian forces at Hostomel in 2022.

evt-12-21-1994-popocatepetl.scenario: It's 21 December 1994, and Popocatépetl, quiet for 47 years, is suddenly venting ash and steam high into the sky above nearby villages. As a civil-protection official, you must decide how to respond to the reawakened volcano.
evt-12-21-1994-popocatepetl.prompt: What precaution do authorities take as the volcano stirs back to life?

choices.text: Dismiss the activity as harmless since major eruptions are considered impossible
Order a full evacuation of Mexico City as a precaution
Declare an exclusion zone around the crater and evacuate the nearest villages
Promote tourism to the crater rim so visitors can observe the eruption up close

evt-12-21-1994-popocatepetl.butterflyEffect: Officials declared a restricted zone around the crater and evacuated the closest communities as a precaution. This 1994 reawakening began a long era of intermittent activity that continues to this day, leading to permanent monitoring stations and larger evacuations in later years, including a major one in 2000.

evt-12-21-1995-oslo-ii-accord.scenario: It's 21 December 1995. Under the terms just signed in Oslo II, Israeli soldiers prepare to pull out of Bethlehem, handing security control to the newly formed Palestinian Authority just days before Christmas.
evt-12-21-1995-oslo-ii-accord.prompt: What administrative status does Bethlehem receive under the Oslo II Accord?

choices.text: Area C status, remaining under full Israeli control
Area B status, with joint Israeli-Palestinian security control
Area A status, with full Palestinian civil and security control
International status under a UN administrative mandate

evt-12-21-1995-oslo-ii-accord.butterflyEffect: Bethlehem became Area A, giving the Palestinian Authority full civil and security control, and Palestinians celebrated their first Christmas under self-rule there. The arrangement proved fragile, however — during the Second Intifada in 2002, Israeli forces reoccupied the city amid the siege of the Church of the Nativity.

evt-12-21-1995-bethlehem.scenario: It is 21 December 1995. Israeli troops have just withdrawn from Bethlehem under the Oslo II agreement, handing control to the Palestinian Authority just days before Christmas.
evt-12-21-1995-bethlehem.prompt: What did Yasser Arafat do to mark Palestinian control of the city that Christmas Eve?

choices.text: He attended Christmas Eve Midnight Mass at the Church of the Nativity
He declared Bethlehem the capital of a future Palestinian state
He evacuated Israeli settlers from the city by force
He ordered the closure of the Church of the Nativity to visitors

evt-12-21-1995-bethlehem.butterflyEffect: Arafat became the first Palestinian leader to attend Midnight Mass at the Church of the Nativity, a deliberately symbolic act asserting Palestinian stewardship over a Christian holy site. The moment captured the hopeful mood of the Oslo years, though Bethlehem would later see renewed conflict, including the 2002 siege of the same church during the Second Intifada.

evt-12-21-2004-iraq-war.scenario: It is midday on 21 December 2004 at Forward Operating Base Marez near Mosul. Hundreds of American soldiers and contractors are crowded into the dining tent for lunch when an attacker detonates explosives among them.
evt-12-21-2004-iraq-war.prompt: What security flaw did investigators later blame for letting the bomber inside?

choices.text: The bomber posed as a wounded American soldier needing medical aid
The bomber tunneled under the base's perimeter fence
The bomber wore an Iraqi security forces uniform, exploiting lax screening of local personnel
The bomber smuggled explosives in through the main supply gate hidden in cargo

evt-12-21-2004-iraq-war.butterflyEffect: The bomber, believed to be wearing an Iraqi security forces uniform, exploited lax screening of local personnel allowed onto U.S. bases. The attack, one of the deadliest against American forces in Iraq to that point, forced a sweeping review of force-protection procedures and tighter vetting of Iraqi contractors and interpreters on coalition bases.

evt-12-21-2012-maya-civilization.scenario: You stand among crowds gathered at Maya ruins across Mexico and Guatemala on 21 December 2012, the date many believed marked the end of the world according to the ancient Maya Long Count calendar.
evt-12-21-2012-maya-civilization.prompt: What actually happened when the calendar's 13th Baktun cycle completed that day?

choices.text: Astronomers confirmed an imminent planetary collision
The day passed without incident as a new calendar cycle simply began
Widespread disasters struck as predicted
Maya communities declared the start of a new war

evt-12-21-2012-maya-civilization.butterflyEffect: No catastrophe occurred; the Long Count simply rolled over into a new cycle, much like a calendar turning to a new century. The global "doomsday" hype drew huge media attention and tourism to Maya archaeological sites, fueling lasting public fascination with Maya astronomy and timekeeping.

evt-12-21-2012-2012-phenomenon.scenario: It is 21 December 2012. You stand among crowds at Chichén Itzá, where believers, tourists, and journalists have gathered to witness the supposed end of a 5,126-year Maya Long Count cycle.
evt-12-21-2012-2012-phenomenon.prompt: As the appointed hour arrives and passes, what actually happens?

choices.text: Nothing cataclysmic occurs and the festival celebrations continue
Governments declare a global state of emergency
A major earthquake strikes the region on schedule
The Maya calendar site is evacuated for safety

evt-12-21-2012-2012-phenomenon.butterflyEffect: No cataclysm occurred; the date simply marked the close of one Long Count cycle (a b'ak'tun) and the beginning of another, as Maya scholars had long explained. The episode spurred renewed public interest in Maya astronomy and calendar systems, while highlighting how apocalyptic rumors could spread rapidly through media.

evt-12-21-2018-special-boat-service.scenario: It's 21 December 2018. The cargo ship Grande Tema lies anchored off the Isle of Wight, its crew barricaded after being threatened by armed stowaways. You are among the Special Boat Service team about to storm the vessel.
evt-12-21-2018-special-boat-service.prompt: What happens when the SBS operators board the ship?

choices.text: They subdue the stowaways without firing a shot and hand them to police
The stowaways jump overboard and escape before capture
A firefight breaks out and several stowaways are killed
The operators discover the crew have already been killed

evt-12-21-2018-special-boat-service.butterflyEffect: The stowaways were subdued and restrained without a single shot being fired, and they were handed over to police once the ship reached port. The rare, publicly acknowledged operation drew attention to the SBS's counter-terrorism role in home waters and to the growing problem of stowaways on commercial shipping.

evt-12-21-2020-great-conjunction.scenario: You set up a telescope at dusk on 21 December 2020, hoping to catch Jupiter and Saturn appear closer together in the sky than they have since 1623.
evt-12-21-2020-great-conjunction.prompt: What did skywatchers actually see that evening?

choices.text: A total solar eclipse over the region
The first sighting of a newly discovered comet
Jupiter and Saturn nearly merging into a single point of light
An unusually intense meteor shower

evt-12-21-2020-great-conjunction.butterflyEffect: Jupiter and Saturn appeared so close they nearly merged into a single bright point, quickly dubbed the "Christmas Star" by the press and linked by many to the biblical Star of Bethlehem. The event reignited widespread public interest in amateur astronomy, and the next conjunction this close will not occur again until 2080.

evt-12-22-401-pope-innocent-i.scenario: You are Pope Innocent I in Rome. Bishops from the African synods of Carthage and Milevis have written to you, urging you to condemn the teachings of Pelagius and his followers on grace and free will.
evt-12-22-401-pope-innocent-i.prompt: What does Innocent I do with the African bishops' request?

choices.text: He dismisses the letter as a local dispute beneath papal concern
He sides with Pelagius against the African bishops
He confirms their decision, backing the condemnation of Pelagianism
He refers the matter to the Emperor for a political ruling

evt-12-22-401-pope-innocent-i.butterflyEffect: Innocent I upheld the African synods' condemnation of Pelagianism, lending Rome's authority to the campaign against it. His endorsement strengthened the papacy's role as final arbiter in doctrinal disputes and paved the way for Pelagius's eventual excommunication under his successor Zosimus.

evt-12-22-1937-lincoln-tunnel.scenario: It's 22 December 1937, and you are among the first drivers queuing at Weehawken to cross beneath the Hudson River through New York's newest tunnel.
evt-12-22-1937-lincoln-tunnel.prompt: Which president's name did this new Hudson River crossing bear?

choices.text: Theodore Roosevelt
Abraham Lincoln
George Washington
Ulysses S. Grant

evt-12-22-1937-lincoln-tunnel.butterflyEffect: Only the center tube opened in 1937; two more tubes followed in 1945 and 1957 as traffic exploded. Together with the Holland Tunnel and George Washington Bridge, it became one of the three vital road links tying New Jersey commuters to Manhattan, still carrying well over a hundred thousand vehicles daily.

evt-12-22-1939-all-india-muslim-league.scenario: It's 22 December 1939. You are a Muslim League supporter organizing celebrations after the Indian National Congress ordered its provincial ministries to resign in protest over Britain's wartime decisions.
evt-12-22-1939-all-india-muslim-league.prompt: What did the League call this day of celebration?

choices.text: Day of Partition
Day of Unity
Day of Independence
Day of Deliverance

evt-12-22-1939-all-india-muslim-league.butterflyEffect: Jinnah's League, joined by the Hindu Mahasabha and Ambedkar's Depressed Classes, framed Congress rule as Hindu domination over minorities. The rhetoric hardened communal politics and fed directly into the League's 1940 Lahore Resolution demanding a separate Muslim state, a key step toward Pakistan's creation in 1947.

evt-12-22-1948-sjafruddin-prawiranegara.scenario: It is 22 December 1948 in Bukittinggi, West Sumatra. Word has just reached you that Dutch paratroopers have seized Yogyakarta and captured President Sukarno and Vice President Hatta. As Finance Minister, you are the senior republican official still free.
evt-12-22-1948-sjafruddin-prawiranegara.prompt: What do you do to keep the Republic of Indonesia alive?

choices.text: Declare an emergency government to continue the Republic's sovereignty
Open immediate surrender talks with the Dutch to spare further bloodshed
Wait quietly for instructions from the captured leaders in Yogyakarta
Flee into exile abroad and lobby foreign governments from there

evt-12-22-1948-sjafruddin-prawiranegara.butterflyEffect: Sjafruddin Prawiranegara declared the Emergency Government of the Republic of Indonesia (PDRI), keeping a functioning republican authority in the field while Sukarno and Hatta were held. This kept Indonesia's claim to sovereignty credible internationally, strengthening its hand at the 1949 Round Table Conference that led to full Dutch recognition of independence.

evt-12-22-1984-new-york-city-subway.scenario: You are a passenger on a New York City Subway train. Four young men approach you and one demands five dollars, and you are carrying a concealed, unlicensed handgun.
evt-12-22-1984-new-york-city-subway.prompt: What does Bernhard Goetz do when confronted on the train?

choices.text: He hands over the money without resistance
He pulls the emergency brake to stop the train
He draws his gun and shoots the youths
He calls out to other passengers for help and waits for police

evt-12-22-1984-new-york-city-subway.butterflyEffect: Goetz drew his revolver and shot all four youths, then fled before eventually surfacing to police. The 'subway vigilante' case ignited a fierce national debate over self-defense, race, and crime in 1980s New York, and Goetz was acquitted of attempted murder but convicted only of illegal weapon possession.

evt-12-22-1990-lech-wa-esa.scenario: You are Lech Wałęsa, the electrician turned Solidarity leader, being sworn in as Poland's first popularly elected president since 1922. Communist rule has just ended and the country faces economic collapse.
evt-12-22-1990-lech-wa-esa.prompt: What challenge defines the start of Wałęsa's presidency?

choices.text: Steering Poland through a harsh economic shock-therapy transition
Rejoining the Warsaw Pact to stabilize regional relations
Reinstating the pre-war monarchy as a symbolic gesture
Negotiating Poland's entry into the European Union immediately

evt-12-22-1990-lech-wa-esa.butterflyEffect: Wałęsa took office as Poland pursued the painful 'Balcerowicz Plan' of rapid free-market reform. His presidency soon fractured from his old Solidarity allies over the pace and cost of change, and he lost re-election to Aleksander Kwaśniewski in 1995.

evt-12-22-1992-tripoli-international-air.scenario: You are an air traffic controller at Tripoli International Airport. A Libyan Arab Airlines jet is on final approach as a Libyan Air Force fighter enters the same airspace on a routine flight.
evt-12-22-1992-tripoli-international-air.prompt: What must controllers do to prevent the aircraft from colliding?

choices.text: Keep the fighter jet clear of the airliner's approach path
Hand control of the airliner to military air traffic command
Order both aircraft to land on parallel runways simultaneously
Instruct the airliner to circle indefinitely until the fighter lands

evt-12-22-1992-tripoli-international-air.butterflyEffect: The controllers failed to keep the two aircraft separated, and the Boeing 727 collided with the MiG-23 fighter jet, killing everyone aboard the airliner. The disaster exposed dangerous gaps in Libya's civil-military airspace coordination during a period of international isolation under sanctions.

evt-12-22-1997-acteal-massacre.scenario: You are a Mexican federal investigator arriving in Acteal after paramilitaries attacked a prayer meeting of the pacifist group Las Abejas. State police were reportedly stationed nearby during the attack.
evt-12-22-1997-acteal-massacre.prompt: What does the official investigation eventually establish about the killings?

choices.text: That no paramilitary group was ever identified or charged
That many convictions were later overturned on procedural grounds
That the victims themselves had instigated the violence
That the attack was an unplanned spontaneous brawl with no organizers

evt-12-22-1997-acteal-massacre.butterflyEffect: Dozens of paramilitary members were convicted, but in 2009 Mexico's Supreme Court ordered the release of many of them over due-process violations. The Mexican government did not formally acknowledge state responsibility for the massacre until September 2020.

evt-12-22-1997-somali-civil-war.scenario: It's 22 December 1997 in Cairo, where warring Somali faction leaders, including Hussein Farrah Aidid, have gathered for reconciliation talks brokered by Egypt.
evt-12-22-1997-somali-civil-war.prompt: What did Aidid agree to relinquish at this conference?

choices.text: Control of Mogadishu's seaport
Control over his militia's weapons stockpiles
His father's memorial legacy and name
His claim to the disputed title of President of Somalia

evt-12-22-1997-somali-civil-war.butterflyEffect: Aidid's renunciation was meant to open the way for a unified transitional government, but the Cairo agreement collapsed within months as rival factions refused to honor it. Somalia remained without an effective central government for years, deepening the state collapse that began with Siad Barre's fall in 1991.

evt-12-22-1999-london-stansted-airport.scenario: It is the night of 22 December 1999. You are flying a Korean Air Cargo Boeing 747 climbing out of Stansted, and your artificial horizon is silently feeding you false readings, making you feel the aircraft is banking when it is not.
evt-12-22-1999-london-stansted-airport.prompt: What should the crew do to prevent a fatal loss of control?

choices.text: Radio air traffic control and wait for their guidance before acting
Switch to autopilot and let the aircraft self-correct
Cross-check the other pilot's instruments and speak up immediately about the discrepancy
Trust the captain's display and follow his control inputs without comment

evt-12-22-1999-london-stansted-airport.butterflyEffect: The captain trusted his faulty instrument and rolled the aircraft into a steep spiral dive; the first officer and flight engineer, despite noticing the discrepancy, failed to challenge him in time, and the plane crashed killing all four crew. The disaster became a textbook case in crew resource management failures and pushed Korean Air into a sweeping safety overhaul with Boeing and Delta in the following years.

evt-12-22-2001-burhanuddin-rabbani.scenario: It's December 22, 2001, in Kabul. As outgoing president, you preside over a ceremony under the Bonn Agreement, formally transferring authority to Afghanistan's new interim government.
evt-12-22-2001-burhanuddin-rabbani.prompt: Who did Rabbani hand presidential power to that day?

choices.text: Hamid Karzai, head of the new Afghan Interim Administration
Ahmad Shah Massoud, the Northern Alliance's military commander
Zahir Shah, Afghanistan's former king
Mullah Omar, the exiled Taliban leader

evt-12-22-2001-burhanuddin-rabbani.butterflyEffect: Hamid Karzai took the reins of the Afghan Interim Administration, launching the Bonn-brokered political order that led to the 2004 constitution and his subsequent election as president. That US-backed framework shaped Afghan governance for two decades, until the Taliban's return to power in 2021.

evt-12-22-2001-richard-reid.scenario: You are a passenger on American Airlines Flight 63 from Paris to Miami. A man in the row ahead is struggling to light something in his shoe, and a flight attendant is trying to stop him.
evt-12-22-2001-richard-reid.prompt: What do passengers and crew do to stop Richard Reid?

choices.text: They physically subdue him and tie him up until landing
They negotiate with him for the remainder of the flight
They calmly ask him to move to another seat
They evacuate the cabin by opening emergency exits mid-flight

evt-12-22-2001-richard-reid.butterflyEffect: Passengers and crew wrestled Reid to the floor and restrained him with belts and headphone cords until the plane diverted to Boston. The failed attack, using explosives hidden in his shoe, led directly to mandatory shoe removal at airport security checkpoints worldwide.

evt-12-22-2008-kingston-fossil-plant-coa.scenario: It is early morning on 22 December 2008 near Kingston, Tennessee. You are a TVA engineer alerted that a containment dike holding decades of coal ash slurry has just failed, sending sludge toward the Emory River.
evt-12-22-2008-kingston-fossil-plant-coa.prompt: What lasting regulatory change did this disaster ultimately provoke?

choices.text: The EPA's first federal rule regulating coal ash disposal
An immediate nationwide ban on coal-fired power plants
Repeal of the Clean Water Act
The forced privatization of the Tennessee Valley Authority

evt-12-22-2008-kingston-fossil-plant-coa.butterflyEffect: The billion-gallon release, the largest industrial waste spill in US history, exposed the total absence of federal oversight for coal ash disposal. It pushed the EPA to issue the country's first national coal ash rule in 2015, forcing utilities nationwide to inspect and often close leaking ash ponds.

evt-12-22-2010-don-t-ask-don-t-tell-repe.scenario: It's December 22, 2010, and you're a gay service member watching President Obama sign the Don't Ask, Don't Tell Repeal Act. You still can't tell your commanding officer the truth just yet.
evt-12-22-2010-don-t-ask-don-t-tell-repe.prompt: What had to happen before the repeal actually took effect?

choices.text: The president, defense secretary, and Joint Chiefs chairman had to certify the military was ready
The repeal took effect immediately upon the president's signature
Each state's National Guard had to individually opt into the new policy
Congress had to hold a second ratification vote the following year

evt-12-22-2010-don-t-ask-don-t-tell-repe.butterflyEffect: The law required the President, Defense Secretary, and Joint Chiefs Chairman to certify the military was ready before repeal took effect. That certification came in July 2011, and DADT formally ended on September 20, 2011, letting gay and lesbian troops serve openly for the first time in modern US history.

evt-12-22-2012-bashir-ahmad-bilour.scenario: It's December 22, 2012, in Peshawar's Qissa Khwani Bazaar. Senior ANP minister Bashir Ahmad Bilour, a vocal opponent of the Taliban, has just finished addressing supporters when a suicide bomber strikes.
evt-12-22-2012-bashir-ahmad-bilour.prompt: What did this assassination signal for the party ahead of Pakistan's 2013 election?

choices.text: International peacekeepers would take over security for all Pakistani elections
Militants would keep targeting ANP candidates, crippling the party's campaign
ANP would negotiate a formal truce granting the Taliban seats in parliament
The government would postpone the national election indefinitely

evt-12-22-2012-bashir-ahmad-bilour.butterflyEffect: The Pakistani Taliban went on to systematically target ANP, PPP, and MQM candidates during the 2013 campaign, severely limiting their ability to hold public rallies. ANP suffered heavy losses in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, and PTI capitalized on the resulting security vacuum to sweep the province.

evt-12-22-2014-united-states-copyright-o.scenario: A macaque named Naruto has pressed the shutter on a wildlife photographer's unattended camera in Indonesia, producing a striking self-portrait. The photographer claims the copyright, but questions swirl about who, if anyone, owns the image.
evt-12-22-2014-united-states-copyright-o.prompt: What does the US Copyright Office say about registering a work like this?

choices.text: It cannot be copyrighted by anyone, since copyright requires human authorship
It belongs to the macaque under animal welfare copyright provisions
It automatically belongs to the photographer as owner of the camera
It must be registered jointly by the photographer and the wildlife park

evt-12-22-2014-united-states-copyright-o.butterflyEffect: On 22 December 2014 the Copyright Office stated that works lacking human authorship, including photos taken by animals, cannot be copyrighted. This set up the later Naruto v. Slater lawsuit, in which courts ruled animals cannot hold copyright, leaving the famous 'monkey selfie' in the public domain.

evt-12-22-2016-rvsv-zebov-vaccine.scenario: It is 2015 in Guinea, and Ebola is still spreading village to village. You are designing a trial for the experimental rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine, but a standard placebo-controlled study feels unethical while people are dying.
evt-12-22-2016-rvsv-zebov-vaccine.prompt: What trial design do researchers use to test the vaccine ethically and fast?

choices.text: Delay all human trials until animal testing was fully complete
Vaccinate rings of contacts around each new case, comparing immediate versus delayed dosing
Test the vaccine only on recovered survivors to avoid new exposure
Run a double-blind trial with a placebo group in an unaffected country

evt-12-22-2016-rvsv-zebov-vaccine.butterflyEffect: Researchers used a 'ring vaccination' design, immunizing the contacts of each new case immediately versus with a delay, rather than withholding the vaccine from a placebo group. The results, confirmed effective on 22 December 2016, led to the vaccine's eventual approval as Ervebo and its use in later Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

evt-12-22-2017-united-nations-security-c.scenario: It is 22 December 2017. North Korea has just tested its most powerful ICBM yet, the Hwasong-15, claimed capable of reaching the US mainland. You sit on the UN Security Council deciding how to respond.
evt-12-22-2017-united-nations-security-c.prompt: What action does the Council take against North Korea?

choices.text: Unanimously tighten sanctions on fuel imports and overseas labor
Lift existing sanctions to encourage North Korea back to talks
Expel North Korea from the United Nations entirely
Authorize military action to destroy North Korea's missile program

evt-12-22-2017-united-nations-security-c.butterflyEffect: The Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2397, tightening sanctions by capping fuel imports and pushing to repatriate North Korean workers abroad. Pyongyang called it an act of war, but the economic squeeze contributed to the diplomatic opening of 2018, including the inter-Korean and Trump-Kim summits.

evt-12-22-2018-2018-sunda-strait-tsunami.scenario: It is the night of 22 December 2018 along the coast of Banten. The sea suddenly surges ashore near Anyer with no warning siren, no felt earthquake, and no time to evacuate.
evt-12-22-2018-2018-sunda-strait-tsunami.prompt: Why did existing tsunami warning systems fail to alert coastal communities?

choices.text: The warning was issued but arrived too late due to power outages
The tsunami came from a volcanic collapse, which seismic warning systems could not detect
An earthquake occurred but was too small to trigger the alert threshold
Officials chose not to issue a warning to avoid panicking tourists

evt-12-22-2018-2018-sunda-strait-tsunami.butterflyEffect: The tsunami was caused by a partial flank collapse of Anak Krakatoa, not an earthquake, so Indonesia's seismic-based warning network never triggered an alert. The disaster exposed how reliant the country's tsunami detection was on quake-triggered systems, driving calls for volcano-monitoring and non-seismic tsunami sensors in vulnerable straits.

evt-12-23-1783-george-washington.scenario: It's December 23, 1783, in the Maryland State House at Annapolis. The Revolutionary War is won, and you, General Washington, stand before the Confederation Congress still holding supreme command of the Continental Army.
evt-12-23-1783-george-washington.prompt: What do you do with the military authority you have held for eight years of war?

choices.text: Formally resign your commission and return power to Congress
Accept the informal suggestions that you become king
March the army on Congress to secure soldiers' unpaid wages first
Retain command until the new government is fully established

evt-12-23-1783-george-washington.butterflyEffect: Washington voluntarily resigned his commission and returned to private life at Mount Vernon, stunning contemporaries including King George III, who reportedly called it the noblest act of his life. The precedent of a victorious general surrendering power set the template for civilian control that Washington reaffirmed when he later left the presidency after two terms.

evt-12-23-1815-jane-austen.scenario: You are working in publisher John Murray's London office in December 1815, preparing the title page for a new novel by an author who has insisted, as before, on keeping her name off the book.
evt-12-23-1815-jane-austen.prompt: How was the author of Emma credited on its title page?

choices.text: As "A Lady of Quality"
Under her full name, Jane Austen
Anonymously, as "By the Author of Pride and Prejudice"
Under a male pseudonym

evt-12-23-1815-jane-austen.butterflyEffect: Emma was published anonymously as "By the Author of Pride and Prejudice," continuing Austen's lifelong practice of concealing her identity in print. She died in 1817 still publicly unacknowledged as a novelist; her brother Henry first revealed her authorship in a biographical notice attached to her posthumously published novels.

evt-12-23-1916-world-war-i.scenario: It is 23 December 1916, and you ride with the ANZAC Mounted Division across the Sinai after an all-night march. Your canteen is nearly dry, and ahead lies an entrenched Ottoman garrison at Magdhaba.
evt-12-23-1916-world-war-i.prompt: With water critically low, what does General Chauvel ultimately decide?

choices.text: Press the attack despite the water shortage
Withdraw the whole force to preserve the horses
Halt and wait for water convoys to arrive
Offer the Ottoman garrison terms for surrender

evt-12-23-1916-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: Chauvel had drafted an order to withdraw, but pressed on after his commanders reported progress, and the New Zealand Mounted Rifles stormed the redoubts just before the recall could take effect. The garrison's fall secured vital wells and opened the route for the British advance toward Gaza and Palestine.

evt-12-23-1919-sex-disqualification-remo.scenario: You are a woman in England in early 1920, hoping to qualify as a solicitor or sit as a magistrate, doors that were closed to you until a new act received royal assent on 23 December 1919.
evt-12-23-1919-sex-disqualification-remo.prompt: What did the Sex Disqualification (Removal) Act newly allow women to do?

choices.text: Vote in general elections on the same terms as men
Keep their civil service jobs after marriage
Receive equal pay for equal work by law
Enter professions like law, sit on juries, and earn degrees

evt-12-23-1919-sex-disqualification-remo.butterflyEffect: The act let women enter professions such as law, sit on juries, and receive university degrees, but as a government compromise for a more radical bill, it left pay inequality and the marriage bar untouched. It marked incremental progress after partial suffrage in 1918, paving the way for Britain's first women barristers and magistrates in the early 1920s.

evt-12-23-1958-tokyo-tower.scenario: You stand in Shiba Park in Tokyo on December 23, 1958, watching engineers make final checks on a new lattice tower rising over the skyline, built at the request of the city's broadcasters.
evt-12-23-1958-tokyo-tower.prompt: What was the tower's primary practical purpose when it opened?

choices.text: To control air traffic over central Tokyo
To serve purely as a tourist observation deck
To serve as a shared broadcasting antenna for television and radio
To function as a civil defense watchtower

evt-12-23-1958-tokyo-tower.butterflyEffect: Tokyo Tower opened as Japan's tallest structure at 332.9 meters, built to carry the shared broadcast antennas for Tokyo's television and radio stations. It held that role for over half a century until Tokyo Skytree took over broadcasting duties in 2012, while Tokyo Tower endured as a beloved observation deck and cultural landmark.

evt-12-23-1972-immaculate-reception.scenario: It's December 23, 1972, in the final seconds of the AFC divisional playoff at Three Rivers Stadium. Your Pittsburgh Steelers trail the Raiders, and Terry Bradshaw's desperation pass ricochets off a violent collision near midfield, bouncing toward you as running back Franco Harris.
evt-12-23-1972-immaculate-reception.prompt: What do you do as the deflected ball drops toward your feet?

choices.text: Spike the ball immediately to stop the clock
Scoop the ball off your shoe tops and run it in for a touchdown
Signal for a fair catch to be safe
Let it fall to the ground, assuming it's incomplete

evt-12-23-1972-immaculate-reception.butterflyEffect: Harris scooped the ball off his shoe tops and sprinted 42 yards for a touchdown, giving Pittsburgh a stunning 13-7 win forever known as the "Immaculate Reception." The play became a cornerstone of Steelers lore as the franchise launched into its 1970s dynasty, and its legality is still debated by fans to this day.

evt-12-23-1979-soviet-afghan-war.scenario: It is 23 December 1979, and you watch Soviet armored columns and paratroopers pour into Kabul while President Hafizullah Amin's government scrambles to make sense of the buildup.
evt-12-23-1979-soviet-afghan-war.prompt: What is Moscow's real objective in massing troops in the Afghan capital?

choices.text: Reinforce Amin's regime against the mujahideen
Establish Afghanistan as a neutral buffer state
Negotiate a phased Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan
Depose Amin and install a more pliable communist government

evt-12-23-1979-soviet-afghan-war.butterflyEffect: Days later, Soviet special forces stormed the palace, killed Amin, and installed Babrak Karmal as a more compliant leader. The invasion dragged the USSR into a decade-long war against US- and Pakistan-backed mujahideen, a conflict whose costs are often cited among the pressures that hastened the Soviet collapse.

evt-12-23-1984-aeroflot-flight-3519.scenario: You are aboard a Tupolev Tu-154 climbing out of Krasnoyarsk toward Irkutsk on the night of December 23, 1984, when the crew reports a serious problem with one of the engines shortly after takeoff.
evt-12-23-1984-aeroflot-flight-3519.prompt: What critical failure led to the aircraft going down minutes after takeoff?

choices.text: The flight was hijacked and diverted
Severe wing icing caused loss of control
The aircraft ran out of fuel before reaching Irkutsk
An engine failure shortly after takeoff

evt-12-23-1984-aeroflot-flight-3519.butterflyEffect: An engine failure brought the Tu-154 down shortly after takeoff, killing 110 of the 111 people aboard; remarkably, one passenger survived. The crash stands as one of the deadliest aviation disasters in Soviet history from that year, a grim reminder of the risks in an era before modern engine-failure safeguards.

evt-12-23-1986-rutan-voyager.scenario: It's December 1986, and you and your co-pilot are nine days into an unrefueled flight around the world in the experimental Voyager aircraft. Near the very end of the journey, over California, your rear engine begins to run rough and finally quits.
evt-12-23-1986-rutan-voyager.prompt: With the finish line close and one engine dead, what do you do?

choices.text: Shut down the failing engine and continue on the remaining one
Jettison remaining fuel to reduce weight and glide down
Attempt an emergency landing at the nearest airstrip below
Radio for a mid-air rescue and prepare to bail out

evt-12-23-1986-rutan-voyager.butterflyEffect: The crew shut down the failing rear engine and flew the final stretch on the front engine alone, landing safely at Edwards Air Force Base on December 23. Voyager became the first aircraft to circle the globe non-stop without refueling, proving the viability of Burt Rutan's lightweight composite designs and inspiring later long-endurance aircraft like the GlobalFlyer.

evt-12-23-1990-history-of-slovenia.scenario: It is 23 December 1990, and you queue outside a polling station in Ljubljana. Yugoslavia is fracturing, and the ballot in your hand asks whether Slovenia should chart its own course.
evt-12-23-1990-history-of-slovenia.prompt: What does this referendum decide for Slovenia?

choices.text: A looser federal arrangement within Yugoslavia
Maintaining the existing status quo
Independence from Yugoslavia
Union with neighboring Austria

evt-12-23-1990-history-of-slovenia.butterflyEffect: 88.5% of voters backed independence, and Slovenia formally declared it on 25 June 1991. Belgrade responded with the brief Ten-Day War, but Slovenia held its ground, gained international recognition, and later joined the EU and NATO.

evt-12-23-1997-pioneer-helmet.scenario: It's March 1997 in Wollaston, Northamptonshire. Gravel-mining machinery is due on site any day, and your excavation team has just uncovered a corroded iron mass inside a young warrior's grave.
evt-12-23-1997-pioneer-helmet.prompt: What is the right way to handle the fragile iron mass before the miners arrive?

choices.text: Leave it in place and let the mining proceed around it
Scrub the corrosion off with a wire brush to see what's inside
Have specialists lift it intact in a soil block for lab conservation
Quietly sell the find to a private antiquities collector

evt-12-23-1997-pioneer-helmet.butterflyEffect: The corroded mass was carefully block-lifted and taken to conservators, who painstakingly revealed a complete boar-crested Anglo-Saxon helmet. It proved to be only the sixth such helmet ever found in Britain, now displayed as a centerpiece of Northamptonshire's archaeological heritage.

evt-12-23-2002-general-atomics-mq-1-pred.scenario: It's December 23, 2002, over southern Iraq's no-fly zone. You're monitoring an armed MQ-1 Predator drone when an Iraqi MiG-25 fighter locks onto it and opens fire.
evt-12-23-2002-general-atomics-mq-1-pred.prompt: What happened when the manned fighter and the armed drone exchanged fire?

choices.text: A backup pilot took remote control and won the engagement
The Predator evaded the missile and returned to base unharmed
The MiG was shot down by the Predator's missile
The Predator fired back but was shot down by the MiG's missile

evt-12-23-2002-general-atomics-mq-1-pred.butterflyEffect: The Predator fired a missile back at the MiG-25, but it missed while the MiG's missile struck and destroyed the drone, marking the first known air-to-air combat between a manned aircraft and an unmanned one. The engagement exposed the vulnerability of armed drones in contested airspace just months before the 2003 invasion of Iraq, spurring interest in better UAV self-defense.

evt-12-23-2007-kingdom-of-nepal.scenario: It's December 23, 2007, in Kathmandu. Nepal's interim parliament, seeking to end a decade of civil war and the king's discredited rule, debates the fate of the 240-year-old monarchy.
evt-12-23-2007-kingdom-of-nepal.prompt: What does the interim parliament agree Nepal should become?

choices.text: A federal democratic republic, abolishing the monarchy
A return to King Gyanendra's full executive powers
A referendum before any decision on the monarchy is made
A constitutional monarchy with the king as ceremonial head of state

evt-12-23-2007-kingdom-of-nepal.butterflyEffect: The agreement paved the way for the monarchy's formal abolition in May 2008, when the newly elected Constituent Assembly declared Nepal a federal democratic republic. It ended the Shah dynasty's 240-year reign, though the country's fragile coalition politics and the peace process with former Maoist rebels continued to unfold for years afterward.

evt-12-23-2008-republic-of-guinea-armed-.scenario: It is 23 December 2008, hours after the death of Guinea's longtime president Lansana Conté. You are a mid-ranking army officer watching the constitutional line of succession play out — or not.
evt-12-23-2008-republic-of-guinea-armed-.prompt: What did the junior officers led by Captain Moussa Dadis Camara actually do?

choices.text: Seized power in a coup, forming a military junta under Captain Camara
Called for elections within the constitutionally mandated 60 days
Deferred to the sitting prime minister to form a caretaker government
Backed the National Assembly president as interim leader per the constitution

evt-12-23-2008-republic-of-guinea-armed-.butterflyEffect: Camara's group seized power that night, suspended the constitution, and formed a military junta (the CNDD) instead of letting the National Assembly speaker take over as the constitution required. Camara ruled until he was shot by an aide in December 2009, triggering a transition that led to Alpha Condé's 2010 election — Guinea's first peaceful, democratic transfer of power.

evt-12-23-2008-2008-guinean-coup-d-etat.scenario: It's December 23, 2008, hours after President Lansana Conté's death ends his 24-year rule. You are Captain Moussa Dadis Camara, watching Guinea's constitutional succession process unfold with no army backing it yet.
evt-12-23-2008-2008-guinean-coup-d-etat.prompt: What do you do to seize control of the country before civilian succession takes hold?

choices.text: Announce a military junta and suspend the constitution
Call for an immediate election within days under existing law
Allow the National Assembly speaker to assume the interim presidency as written
Defer entirely to the army chief of staff's authority

evt-12-23-2008-2008-guinean-coup-d-etat.butterflyEffect: Camara's junta, the National Council for Democracy and Development, ruled Guinea by force for nearly two years, a period marred by a 2009 massacre of opposition demonstrators. After Camara was wounded in an assassination attempt, he stepped aside, and Alpha Condé's 2010 election victory finally restored civilian government.

evt-12-23-2023-2023-plateau-state-massac.scenario: In the days before Christmas 2023, armed groups strike at least seventeen rural farming communities in Bokkos and Barkin Ladi, Plateau State, over three days, leaving devastation across Berom villages.
evt-12-23-2023-2023-plateau-state-massac.prompt: Who did residents and authorities believe was behind the coordinated attacks?

choices.text: Boko Haram insurgents expanding south from the northeast
Fulani militias, tied to long-running farmer-herder land disputes
A rival political faction ahead of local elections
Bandit gangs with no connection to local land disputes

evt-12-23-2023-2023-plateau-state-massac.butterflyEffect: No group ever claimed responsibility, but suspicion fell on Fulani militias amid decades of tension between farming communities and herders over land and grazing rights in Nigeria's Middle Belt. The killings intensified calls for stronger security in Plateau State and renewed national debate over unresolved land and resource conflicts.

evt-12-24-1814-treaty-of-ghent.scenario: It is December 24, 1814, and you are among the American delegates at Ghent. Both London and Washington are exhausted by the War of 1812 and eager to stop fighting, but the borders and grievances that started the war remain unresolved.
evt-12-24-1814-treaty-of-ghent.prompt: What basis do the delegates agree on to end the war?

choices.text: Restore all pre-war borders and territory, changing nothing else
Grant the United States permanent control of Canada
Give Britain exclusive rights to the Great Lakes
Force the United States to cede the Louisiana Territory

evt-12-24-1814-treaty-of-ghent.butterflyEffect: The treaty restored the pre-war borders under status quo ante bellum, settling nothing about the impressment and trade disputes that had caused the war. News traveled so slowly that the Battle of New Orleans was fought after the treaty was signed, and the peace ushered in a long era of Anglo-American cooperation.

evt-12-24-1846-sultanate-of-brunei-1368-.scenario: You are Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddin II of Brunei in 1846, facing pressure from James Brooke and the British to secure protection against piracy and rival claimants to your throne.
evt-12-24-1846-sultanate-of-brunei-1368-.prompt: What do you decide to grant the British in exchange for their support?

choices.text: Grant Britain a temporary trading post only
Offer Britain a yearly tribute instead of territory
Cede the island of Labuan to the British Empire
Refuse all British demands and seek Dutch protection instead

evt-12-24-1846-sultanate-of-brunei-1368-.butterflyEffect: The Sultan ceded the island of Labuan outright to the British Empire, who developed it as a coaling station and free port to help suppress piracy in the region. Labuan remained under British control for over a century before eventually becoming part of Malaysia, now a federal territory off the coast of Sabah.

evt-12-24-1865-confederate-states-army.scenario: It's Christmas 1865 in Pulaski, Tennessee. You and five fellow Confederate veterans, restless after the war, decide to start a secret fraternal club with costumes, rituals, and a fanciful name.
evt-12-24-1865-confederate-states-army.prompt: What did the six founders name their new club?

choices.text: The White League
The Knights of the White Camellia
The Ku Klux Klan
The Red Shirts

evt-12-24-1865-confederate-states-army.butterflyEffect: They called it the Ku Klux Klan. What began as private theatrical fraternity quickly turned into a paramilitary campaign of terror against freed Black Americans across the Reconstruction South, before federal enforcement acts suppressed it in the 1870s — only for it to be revived in 1915 as a much larger movement.

evt-12-24-1913-italian-hall-disaster.scenario: It is Christmas Eve, 1913, in Calumet, Michigan. You are packed into the second-floor hall of the Italian Hall with striking copper miners and their families for a holiday party when someone near the stairs suddenly screams that the building is on fire.
evt-12-24-1913-italian-hall-disaster.prompt: What turns the resulting panic into a deadly crush on the stairway?

choices.text: The hall's only staircase collapses under the crowd's weight
A second stairway is found to be permanently locked from outside
The stairwell's exit door jams shut, blocked by the weight of the crowd
The building's lights fail, plunging the stairway into darkness

evt-12-24-1913-italian-hall-disaster.butterflyEffect: There was no fire—the alarm was false—but in the crush to escape, the door at the bottom of the narrow stairwell became jammed shut by the weight of bodies pressing against it, trapping dozens who suffocated or were crushed. The tragedy, striking families of striking miners, deepened bitterness in the ongoing Copper Country strike and was later memorialized in Woody Guthrie's song '1913 Massacre.' It also spurred later scrutiny of exit design in public assembly halls.

evt-12-24-1914-world-war-i.scenario: It is Christmas Eve, 1914, in a frozen trench on the Western Front. Across no-man's-land, you hear German soldiers singing carols, and some are lighting small candles on trees along their parapet.
evt-12-24-1914-world-war-i.prompt: What do many Allied soldiers do in response to this unofficial signal from the enemy trench?

choices.text: Ignore it entirely and report it to officers as enemy propaganda
Open fire immediately, suspecting a trick
Call for an artillery barrage to disrupt the singing
Climb out cautiously to meet, exchange small gifts, and briefly fraternise

evt-12-24-1914-world-war-i.butterflyEffect: In several sectors soldiers on both sides climbed out to exchange greetings, gifts, and even play impromptu football, one of the war's most famous unofficial truces. High command on both sides was alarmed by the fraternisation and moved to prevent any repeat, rotating units and threatening discipline so that nothing on this scale happened again in later Christmases of the war.

evt-12-24-1925-winnie-the-pooh.scenario: You are a child in London opening the Evening News on Christmas Eve, 1925, to find a new story commissioned specially for the holiday, about a stuffed bear based on a real toy from Harrods and a bear at London Zoo.
evt-12-24-1925-winnie-the-pooh.prompt: Which character makes his debut by name in this Christmas Eve newspaper story?

choices.text: Paddington Bear
Peter Rabbit
Winnie-the-Pooh
Rupert Bear

evt-12-24-1925-winnie-the-pooh.butterflyEffect: The story introduced Winnie-the-Pooh to the public for the first time; A. A. Milne would soon collect these tales into full books illustrated by E. H. Shepard. The character went on to become one of the best-known figures in children's literature and, decades later, a global media franchise after Disney acquired the rights.

evt-12-24-1953-north-island.scenario: It is 10:20pm on Christmas Eve, 1953, and you are motorist Cyril Ellis driving beside the Whangaehu River when you see the rail bridge ahead has just been swept away by a volcanic mudflow from Mount Ruapehu. The Wellington–Auckland express is minutes from reaching it.
evt-12-24-1953-north-island.prompt: With no phone nearby and the train approaching fast, what do you do to try to warn it?

choices.text: Run toward the train waving a lit torch to signal danger
Stand on the tracks and hope the driver sees you in the headlights
Wait at the riverbank for the train to pass, assuming it would see the gap
Drive back to the nearest station to raise the alarm

evt-12-24-1953-north-island.butterflyEffect: Ellis ran toward the train waving a torch, but the express could not stop in time and plunged into the river at Tangiwai, becoming New Zealand's worst rail disaster. The tragedy led to the installation of an early-warning system to monitor Ruapehu's crater lake for future lahars threatening the line.

evt-12-24-1955-norad-tracks-santa.scenario: It is Christmas Eve 1955 and you are the duty officer at the Continental Air Defense Command. The red phone rings, and instead of a general, a small child's voice asks if this is really Santa's number.
evt-12-24-1955-norad-tracks-santa.prompt: What do you do about the misdialed calls flooding in?

choices.text: Transfer every call to the base switchboard operator
Hang up immediately and report it as a prank line
Have the phone number disconnected for the rest of the night
Play along and give the children updates on Santa's location

evt-12-24-1955-norad-tracks-santa.butterflyEffect: A Sears ad had misprinted the hotline number, and Colonel Harry Shoup's staff decided to play along, giving callers cheerful updates on Santa's position. The stunt became an annual tradition, and NORAD has run a Santa-tracking program every Christmas Eve since, now reaching millions online worldwide.

evt-12-24-1964-viet-cong.scenario: It's Christmas Eve 1964, and you are a U.S. officer billeted at the Brink's Hotel in downtown Saigon, unaware that Viet Cong operatives have just placed a car bomb in the parking garage beneath the building.
evt-12-24-1964-viet-cong.prompt: What did the Viet Cong bombing of the Brink's Hotel accomplish?

choices.text: Destroyed the building with no casualties
Forced an immediate withdrawal of U.S. advisors
Killed two Americans and wounded dozens, exposing VC reach into central Saigon
Was discovered and defused before detonation

evt-12-24-1964-viet-cong.butterflyEffect: The blast killed two Americans and wounded dozens more, proving the Viet Cong could strike a guarded target in the heart of Saigon itself. The attack shook U.S. officials and sharpened the Washington debate over escalating America's military commitment, which expanded dramatically with combat troop deployments the following year.

evt-12-24-1968-jim-lovell.scenario: It is Christmas Eve, 1968. You are aboard Apollo 8, orbiting the Moon with Frank Borman and William Anders, and Mission Control has asked your crew to address an estimated billion people watching the live broadcast back on Earth.
evt-12-24-1968-jim-lovell.prompt: What do you and your crewmates choose to read aloud to the watching world?

choices.text: The lyrics to a popular Christmas carol, sung together
A passage from the U.S. Declaration of Independence
A poem by Walt Whitman about the frontier
The opening verses of the Book of Genesis

evt-12-24-1968-jim-lovell.butterflyEffect: The three astronauts took turns reading the opening verses of the Book of Genesis, ending with Borman's 'And from the crew of Apollo 8, good night, good luck, a Merry Christmas, and God bless all of you on the good Earth.' It became one of the most-watched broadcasts in history and prompted a lawsuit from atheist activist Madalyn Murray O'Hair, later dismissed for lack of standing. The mission's 'Earthrise' photograph, taken the same trip, went on to help inspire the modern environmental movement.

evt-12-24-1973-united-states-congress.scenario: You are a Washington, D.C. resident in December 1973, following Congress's debate over whether the capital's citizens should finally get a local government of their own.
evt-12-24-1973-united-states-congress.prompt: What new power did the District of Columbia Home Rule Act actually grant residents?

choices.text: A voting member in the U.S. House of Representatives
Full statehood for the District
Complete independence from congressional oversight
An elected mayor and city council for local governance

evt-12-24-1973-united-states-congress.butterflyEffect: The Act, signed by President Nixon on Christmas Eve 1973, gave D.C. its first elected mayor and city council since 1874; Walter Washington became the first elected mayor in 1975. Congress kept ultimate authority — including budget review and the power to overturn local laws — a tension that still fuels today's D.C. statehood debate.

evt-12-24-1974-cyclone-tracy.scenario: It is Christmas Eve, 1974, and you are a Darwin resident as radio warnings crackle about a cyclone that was supposed to pass the city by. Winds are rising fast and the storm has turned straight toward you.
evt-12-24-1974-cyclone-tracy.prompt: With the cyclone bearing down after dark, what is the safest immediate action?

choices.text: Shelter in the strongest, most interior part of the house, away from windows
Drive out of the city immediately along the highway
Take shelter in a parked car in the driveway
Stay on the veranda to watch for falling debris

evt-12-24-1974-cyclone-tracy.butterflyEffect: Tracy struck after 10pm, flattening most of Darwin with gusts over 217 km/h. More than 30,000 people—over half the city's population—were evacuated in the following days, the largest evacuation in Australian history, and Darwin was rebuilt to strict new cyclone-resistant building codes still used today.

evt-12-24-1979-soviet-afghan-war.scenario: It is December 1979 and you sit on the Soviet Politburo. The communist government in Kabul is collapsing under a mujahideen insurgency, and hardliners are pushing for direct military intervention to save it.
evt-12-24-1979-soviet-afghan-war.prompt: What does the Politburo decide to do?

choices.text: Limit involvement to money and weapons without deploying troops
Open negotiations with mujahideen commanders for a coalition government
Withdraw all support and let the Afghan communists fend for themselves
Send in the Soviet 40th Army to prop up the government by force

evt-12-24-1979-soviet-afghan-war.butterflyEffect: Soviet troops crossed into Afghanistan and stormed the palace, installing a new leader while fighting a nine-year war against US, Pakistani, and Gulf-backed mujahideen. The costly, unwinnable conflict drained Soviet resources and morale, becoming one of the pressures that helped bring down the USSR itself by 1991.

evt-12-24-1979-ariane-1.scenario: It is December 24, 1979, and you are an engineer watching the countdown at the Guiana Space Centre. Europe's newly formed space agency is betting its future on this untested rocket, designed with an unusual dual-payload capability.
evt-12-24-1979-ariane-1.prompt: What is Ariane 1 primarily built to do?

choices.text: Launch military reconnaissance satellites for NATO
Test intercontinental ballistic missile technology
Carry commercial satellites into geosynchronous orbit
Send crewed missions toward the Moon

evt-12-24-1979-ariane-1.butterflyEffect: The rocket successfully reached orbit, proving Europe could launch satellites independently of the US and USSR. Its dual-payload design let operators split launch costs between two satellites, and the program's success led directly to Arianespace, which came to dominate the commercial satellite launch market through the 1980s and 1990s.

evt-12-24-1999-jihadism.scenario: You are a passenger aboard Indian Airlines Flight 814, hijacked shortly after takeoff from Kathmandu on Christmas Eve 1999. The plane has been forced to land in Taliban-controlled Kandahar, and the hijackers are demanding the release of imprisoned militants.
evt-12-24-1999-jihadism.prompt: What did the Indian government ultimately do to end the week-long hijacking crisis?

choices.text: Paid a cash ransom while refusing to free any prisoners
Released Masood Azhar and two other militants in exchange for the hostages
Refused all demands, leading to a prolonged siege
Launched a special forces raid on the aircraft

evt-12-24-1999-jihadism.butterflyEffect: India released militants Masood Azhar, Ahmed Omar Saeed Sheikh, and Mushtaq Ahmed Zargar in exchange for the 176 hostages. Azhar went on to found Jaish-e-Mohammed, later responsible for major attacks in India, while Sheikh was convicted in the 2002 kidnapping and murder of journalist Daniel Pearl.

evt-12-24-2005-chad-sudan-relations.scenario: It is December 2005. You advise Chad's President Idriss Déby after rebels, whom his government says are backed by Sudan, strike the border town of Adré, killing Chadian troops and civilians.
evt-12-24-2005-chad-sudan-relations.prompt: What formal step does Chad's government take against Sudan in response?

choices.text: Launches a full-scale invasion into Sudan's Darfur region
Declares a formal 'state of belligerence' against Sudan
Requests immediate UN peacekeepers without confronting Sudan
Closes the border while maintaining full diplomatic relations

evt-12-24-2005-chad-sudan-relations.butterflyEffect: Chad declared a 'state of belligerence' against Sudan, accusing Khartoum of arming and directing the rebels, though it stopped short of a formal declaration of war. The move sharpened regional alarm over the Darfur conflict spilling across the border, fueling cross-border raids and a refugee crisis that drew in French forces and, eventually, a UN peacekeeping presence in eastern Chad.

evt-12-25-1046-henry-iii-holy-roman-empe.scenario: It is Christmas Day, 1046, in Rome. Weeks earlier at the Synod of Sutri you forced the deposition of rival claimants to the papacy, and now your handpicked pope, Clement II, stands ready to place a crown on your head.
evt-12-25-1046-henry-iii-holy-roman-empe.prompt: What happens to Henry at this Christmas ceremony in Rome?

choices.text: He is crowned King of Italy only
He abdicates in favor of his son
He is excommunicated for interfering in papal elections
He is crowned Holy Roman Emperor

evt-12-25-1046-henry-iii-holy-roman-empe.butterflyEffect: Henry III was crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Clement II, whose elevation he himself had engineered. The coronation marked the high point of imperial control over the papacy, a dominance that provoked reformist backlash and helped trigger the Investiture Controversy that convulsed church-state relations for the rest of the century.

evt-12-25-1066-norman-conquest.scenario: It is Christmas Day, 1066, inside Westminster Abbey. You stand among the assembled nobles as William, Duke of Normandy, kneels to receive the crown of England, ten weeks after his victory at Hastings.
evt-12-25-1066-norman-conquest.prompt: What happens outside that nearly turns the coronation into chaos?

choices.text: The Archbishop of Canterbury refuses to perform the ceremony
Saxon nobles storm the altar in protest
Norman soldiers outside mistake the cheering for a riot and set fire to nearby buildings
The crown slips and falls to the floor, seen as an ill omen

evt-12-25-1066-norman-conquest.butterflyEffect: According to the chronicler Orderic Vitalis, Norman guards outside heard shouts of acclamation in English and French, feared treachery, and set nearby houses ablaze, causing panic that emptied the abbey except for William and the clergy. The chaotic scene foreshadowed the fragile, often violent character of Norman rule over a conquered England.

evt-12-25-1100-baldwin-i-of-jerusalem.scenario: It is Christmas Day, 1100, in the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem. Your predecessor Godfrey of Bouillon refused the crown, calling himself only Advocate of the Holy Sepulchre, but you have decided the fledgling Crusader state needs a king.
evt-12-25-1100-baldwin-i-of-jerusalem.prompt: What title does Baldwin take as he is crowned in Bethlehem?

choices.text: Advocate of the Holy Sepulchre, like Godfrey before him
Duke of the Holy Land
Prince of Antioch
King of Jerusalem

evt-12-25-1100-baldwin-i-of-jerusalem.butterflyEffect: Baldwin I became the first King of Jerusalem, establishing a hereditary monarchy that outlasted Godfrey's more modest arrangement. His reign expanded the kingdom's borders through conquest of coastal cities, giving the Crusader states the political structure that would endure, in various forms, for nearly two centuries.

evt-12-25-1758-edmond-halley.scenario: It is the night of 25 December 1758 in Saxony. You are Johann Georg Palitzsch, a farmer and amateur astronomer, scanning the winter sky for a faint speck the late Edmond Halley calculated would return this very year.
evt-12-25-1758-edmond-halley.prompt: What does your sighting confirm to the scientific world?

choices.text: That comets are unpredictable omens with no fixed path
That comets follow predictable, calculable orbits governed by gravity
That the object was a newly discovered planet
That Halley's calculations were flawed and needed revision

evt-12-25-1758-edmond-halley.butterflyEffect: Palitzsch's sighting confirmed Halley's 1705 prediction that the comet seen in 1531, 1607, and 1682 would return on schedule, proving comets obey calculable, gravity-governed orbits rather than appearing at random. The confirmation, decades after Halley's death, cemented Newtonian physics and led the comet to be named in his honor.

evt-12-25-1809-ephraim-mcdowell.scenario: It is Christmas Day, 1809, in Danville, Kentucky. Jane Todd Crawford lies on your kitchen table, suffering from what you believe is a massive ovarian tumor, and no surgeon has ever attempted to remove one and had the patient live.
evt-12-25-1809-ephraim-mcdowell.prompt: What does Ephraim McDowell do, with no anesthesia and enormous risk?

choices.text: Sends her to a hospital in Philadelphia
Prescribes bed rest and refuses to operate
Attempts to shrink the tumor with medication first
Performs the surgery to remove the tumor

evt-12-25-1809-ephraim-mcdowell.butterflyEffect: McDowell successfully removed the 22-pound tumor while Crawford reportedly recited psalms to distract from the pain, and she recovered fully. The operation, performed without anesthesia or antiseptic technique decades before either existed, is credited as the birth of abdominal surgery and ovariotomy as a survivable procedure.

evt-12-25-1927-viet-nam-quoc-dan-ang.scenario: It is Hanoi, late December 1927. Your underground publishing house has just been shut down by French censors, and you and your fellow young intellectuals must decide what kind of movement to build to resist colonial rule.
evt-12-25-1927-viet-nam-quoc-dan-ang.prompt: Which foreign nationalist movement do the founders model their new party on?

choices.text: The Bolshevik Party
The Indian National Congress
The Comintern
Sun Yat-sen's Kuomintang

evt-12-25-1927-viet-nam-quoc-dan-ang.butterflyEffect: The VNQDĐ was founded on the Kuomintang model, complete with cells and a revolutionary program aimed at ousting the French. It later launched the failed 1930 Yên Bái mutiny, which brought brutal French reprisals and left the field open for Ho Chi Minh's communists to dominate Vietnamese nationalism.

evt-12-25-1941-world-war-ii.scenario: It is Christmas Day 1941. You are Governor Mark Aitchison Young in Hong Kong, and after eighteen days of fighting, your garrison is exhausted, water supplies are failing, and Japanese forces have broken through the last defensive lines.
evt-12-25-1941-world-war-ii.prompt: What does Governor Young decide to do?

choices.text: Evacuate the government to Chungking
Negotiate a neutral demilitarized zone
Surrender the colony to Japanese forces
Order a fight to the last man

evt-12-25-1941-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Young surrendered Hong Kong to the Japanese that afternoon, beginning what locals called the 'Three Years and Eight Months' of occupation. The harsh rule that followed, marked by shortages and internment of Allied civilians, shaped Hong Kong's postwar politics and its return to British administration in 1945.

evt-12-25-1968-tamil-nadu.scenario: It is Christmas 1968 in Kilvenmani, Tamil Nadu. Dalit agricultural laborers have been striking for fairer wages, and a landlord-backed gang has surrounded the village in retaliation.
evt-12-25-1968-tamil-nadu.prompt: What was the eventual judicial outcome of the case against the attackers?

choices.text: No suspects were ever identified or arrested
The case was dismissed before reaching trial
Convicted at trial, then acquitted on appeal
Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment, upheld on appeal

evt-12-25-1968-tamil-nadu.butterflyEffect: The men were convicted at trial but later acquitted on appeal for lack of direct evidence, a verdict that provoked national outrage.
