The massacre and its unjust aftermath galvanized Dalit rights movements and strengthened leftist agrarian organizing across Tamil Nadu.

evt-12-25-1990-tim-berners-lee.scenario: It is Christmas Day, 1990, at CERN. You and a colleague have spent the year building software on a NeXT workstation, and today you finally test whether a client program can fetch a page from a server across the network.
evt-12-25-1990-tim-berners-lee.prompt: What milestone does Berners-Lee achieve with this test?

choices.text: The first public website launch
The first successful web client-server exchange
The first internet search engine demo
The first email sent over the internet

evt-12-25-1990-tim-berners-lee.butterflyEffect: The first successful communication between an HTTP client and server took place, proving Berners-Lee's World Wide Web concept worked in practice. Within months the software was released publicly, and by the mid-1990s it had grown from a CERN research tool into the foundation of the modern internet.

evt-12-25-1991-mikhail-gorbachev.scenario: It is 25 December 1991. You sit before Soviet television cameras to address the nation for what everyone in the room knows will be the last time in your current role, as the republics you once governed have already declared independence.
evt-12-25-1991-mikhail-gorbachev.prompt: What does Gorbachev do in this address?

choices.text: Names Yeltsin as his successor as General Secretary
Announces a referendum to save the Union
Resigns as President of the Soviet Union
Declares a state of emergency

evt-12-25-1991-mikhail-gorbachev.butterflyEffect: Gorbachev resigned as President of the USSR, handing the nuclear launch codes to Russian President Boris Yeltsin. Within hours the Soviet flag over the Kremlin was lowered and replaced by the Russian tricolor, and the Soviet Union formally ceased to exist the next day, ending nearly seven decades of communist rule.

evt-12-25-2000-vladimir-putin.scenario: It is Christmas Day, 2000, in Moscow. As president you have decided Russia needs a new national anthem, and the choice you sign into law will revive a melody many citizens have not heard officially in nearly a decade.
evt-12-25-2000-vladimir-putin.prompt: Which anthem melody does Putin's new law restore, with fresh lyrics?

choices.text: Glinka's wordless 1990s anthem melody
The pre-revolutionary imperial anthem
A newly commissioned composition
The Soviet-era Alexandrov anthem melody

evt-12-25-2000-vladimir-putin.butterflyEffect: Putin restored the Soviet-era Alexandrov melody used since 1944, paired with new words by the same lyricist, Sergei Mikhalkov. The move drew criticism from reformers as nostalgic for the USSR, while supporters saw it as a bid to unite a fractured post-Soviet identity around a familiar, stirring tune.

evt-12-25-2007-san-francisco-zoo.scenario: It is Christmas Day 2007 at the San Francisco Zoo. Tatiana, a Siberian tiger, has escaped her enclosure and is attacking visitors near the Lion House as staff scramble to respond.
evt-12-25-2007-san-francisco-zoo.prompt: What do zoo staff do to stop the attack?

choices.text: Tranquilize it from a distance
Wait for animal control to arrive off-site
Shoot and kill the tiger
Lure it back with food into the enclosure

evt-12-25-2007-san-francisco-zoo.butterflyEffect: Staff shot and killed Tatiana, but visitor Carlos Sousa Jr. had already been fatally mauled. The investigation found the enclosure's barrier fell short of safety guidelines, prompting the zoo to rebuild the exhibit and spurring a wider review of big-cat enclosure standards at American zoos.

evt-12-25-2009-northwest-airlines-flight.scenario: You are a passenger on Northwest Flight 253 nearing Detroit on Christmas Day 2009, and you notice the man in seat 19A fumbling with something under a blanket moments before flames erupt.
evt-12-25-2009-northwest-airlines-flight.prompt: What stopped Abdulmutallab from detonating the explosive sewn into his underwear?

choices.text: The device simply failed to ignite on its own
Air marshals shot him before he could act
The pilot depressurized the cabin, extinguishing the flames
Passengers and crew tackled him and put out the fire

evt-12-25-2009-northwest-airlines-flight.butterflyEffect: Nearby passengers and a flight attendant tackled Abdulmutallab and smothered the flames before serious damage occurred; he suffered burns but the plane landed safely. The failed attack exposed watch-list failures and led to the rapid nationwide rollout of full-body airport security scanners.

evt-12-25-2016-ministry-of-defence-russi.scenario: You are aboard a Russian Defence Ministry Tu-154 lifting off from Sochi on Christmas Day 2016, carrying the Alexandrov Ensemble toward a New Year's concert for troops deployed in Syria.
evt-12-25-2016-ministry-of-defence-russi.prompt: What happened to the aircraft moments after it climbed away from Sochi?

choices.text: It suffered engine failure and made a safe emergency landing
It stalled and crashed into the Black Sea, killing everyone aboard
It caught fire on the runway before departure
It was struck by a missile and diverted to Turkey

evt-12-25-2016-ministry-of-defence-russi.butterflyEffect: The Tu-154 plunged into the Black Sea minutes after takeoff, killing all 92 aboard, including nearly the entire Alexandrov Ensemble choir and humanitarian doctor Elizaveta Glinka. Investigators attributed the crash to pilot error and disorientation in darkness, dealing a severe blow to Russia's military cultural corps and hastening the aging Tu-154's retirement from state service.

evt-12-25-2019-typhoon-phanfone.scenario: It is Christmas Eve, 2019, on Panay Island in the Philippines. Typhoon Phanfone, locally called Ursula, is bearing down as families finish holiday preparations, and local officials must decide how to respond.
evt-12-25-2019-typhoon-phanfone.prompt: What urgent action should disaster officials take as the storm approaches on Christmas?

choices.text: Postpone all warnings until after Christmas Day festivities conclude
Rely solely on church bells to alert residents
Evacuate coastal and low-lying communities despite the holiday
Advise residents to remain in coastal homes to protect their property

evt-12-25-2019-typhoon-phanfone.butterflyEffect: Despite warnings, the storm's holiday timing hampered evacuations and preparations, contributing to around 20 deaths and leaving thousands homeless just as families gathered for Christmas. The disaster renewed pressure on Philippine authorities to make evacuation protocols function even during major holidays, when compliance historically drops.

evt-12-25-2020-2020-nashville-bombing.scenario: It is 6:30 a.m. on Christmas Day 2020 in downtown Nashville. You are a police officer on Second Avenue when you notice a parked RV broadcasting a recorded warning and a countdown to detonation.
evt-12-25-2020-2020-nashville-bombing.prompt: What do you and fellow officers do before the countdown ends?

choices.text: Approach the RV to investigate the recording
Wait for the bomb squad without warning anyone
Evacuate nearby residents and buildings
Dismiss it as a prank and leave the scene

evt-12-25-2020-2020-nashville-bombing.butterflyEffect: Officers evacuated nearby buildings and residents just before the RV exploded, an act credited with preventing deaths despite extensive damage. The bomber, Anthony Quinn Warner, died in the blast, which also knocked out a regional AT&T facility, causing days of telecom outages and prompting scrutiny of infrastructure security.

evt-12-25-2021-james-webb-space-telescop.scenario: It is dawn on Christmas Day 2021 at the Kourou spaceport in French Guiana. You watch the Ariane 5 rocket carrying the James Webb Space Telescope climb into the sky, knowing the hardest part of the mission is still ahead.
evt-12-25-2021-james-webb-space-telescop.prompt: What critical process must Webb complete in the weeks after launch?

choices.text: Dock with the International Space Station
Deploy fully within minutes of separation
Broadcast first images the same day
Unfold its sunshield and mirror over several weeks

evt-12-25-2021-james-webb-space-telescop.butterflyEffect: Over the following weeks, Webb executed hundreds of single-point-failure deployments, unfolding its sunshield and unlatching its segmented mirror before settling into orbit around the Sun-Earth L2 point. Its success delivered unprecedented images of early galaxies and exoplanet atmospheres, reshaping astronomy.

evt-12-25-2024-azerbaijan-airlines-fligh.scenario: You are the captain of an Embraer E190 on approach to Grozny on 25 December 2024 when a shockwave tears through the fuselage, shredding your hydraulic lines and controls.
evt-12-25-2024-azerbaijan-airlines-fligh.prompt: What did the crew do to try to save the crippled aircraft and its passengers?

choices.text: Attempted to divert the damaged jet across the Caspian Sea toward Aktau
Turned back to Baku using a backup hydraulic system
Requested an emergency landing at the nearest Russian military airbase
Immediately ditched the aircraft in the sea near Grozny

evt-12-25-2024-azerbaijan-airlines-fligh.butterflyEffect: The pilots fought to keep the jet airborne across nearly 300 miles of the Caspian Sea before losing control on approach to Aktau, killing 38 of the 67 aboard. Investigators pointed to a Russian air-defense missile fired amid a drone alert, and Russia's president later apologized for the incident occurring in Russian airspace, straining ties with Azerbaijan.

evt-12-26-1606-king-lear.scenario: It is St Stephen's Day, 26 December 1606, and you sit among the court at Whitehall Palace as the King's Men prepare to perform a dark new tragedy for King James I.
evt-12-26-1606-king-lear.prompt: What becomes of Shakespeare's King Lear after this court performance?

choices.text: It is quickly forgotten and never performed again
It becomes one of the most enduring tragedies in English literature
The manuscript is lost and rediscovered centuries later
It is banned by the court for its dark themes

evt-12-26-1606-king-lear.butterflyEffect: The play was entered in the Stationers' Register in 1607 and printed in 1608. Restoration adapters later gave it a happy ending, but by the 19th century Shakespeare's original tragic text was restored, and King Lear is now regarded as one of his greatest works.

evt-12-26-1709-agrippina-opera.scenario: It's December 26, 1709, at Venice's Teatro San Giovanni Grisostomo, and you sit in the audience for the premiere of a new opera by a young German composer, satirizing the intrigues of ancient Rome.
evt-12-26-1709-agrippina-opera.prompt: What happens to this new opera in the weeks that follow?

choices.text: It is forgotten within days
Church censors ban it outright
It closes after a single disastrous night
It runs for an extraordinary 27 performances

evt-12-26-1709-agrippina-opera.butterflyEffect: Agrippina was a sensation, running for an unprecedented 27 performances and cementing the young George Frideric Handel's reputation in Italy, a triumph that helped launch the international career that would later carry him to London.

evt-12-26-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is dawn on 26 December 1776 near Trenton, New Jersey. You are one of Washington's soldiers, having just crossed the ice-choked Delaware River overnight, and the Hessian garrison ahead has not yet realized you are here.
evt-12-26-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What does Washington's army do with this surprise advantage?

choices.text: Wait several days for reinforcements from Congress
Attack the Hessian garrison at Trenton before it can rally
Retreat back across the Delaware to regroup
Open negotiations for a prisoner exchange

evt-12-26-1776-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: Washington's Continentals struck the Hessian garrison at Trenton before it could organize a defense, capturing nearly 900 prisoners in a stunning victory. Coming after months of defeats and desertions, the win restored American morale, renewed enlistments, and set up a follow-on victory at Princeton days later.

evt-12-26-1800-philip-gidley-king.scenario: It's 1800, and you have just become Governor of New South Wales, facing officers of the NSW Corps who control the colony's lucrative and disruptive rum trade.
evt-12-26-1800-philip-gidley-king.prompt: How do you handle the officers' rum monopoly?

choices.text: Let the officers keep their monopoly for peace
Crack down on the officers' rum trading
Resign immediately rather than confront them
Hand governing authority over to the military

evt-12-26-1800-philip-gidley-king.butterflyEffect: King's efforts to curb the rum trade provoked fierce resistance from the NSW Corps, which wore down his authority and helped force his resignation by 1806; the same officer resentment would erupt again against his successor, William Bligh, in the 1808 Rum Rebellion.

evt-12-26-1825-imperial-russian-army.scenario: It is 26 December 1825, and you stand with several thousand soldiers in St Petersburg's Senate Square, refusing to swear allegiance to Nicholas I in hopes of forcing a constitutional government.
evt-12-26-1825-imperial-russian-army.prompt: What happens when Nicholas I responds to the assembled rebels?

choices.text: He negotiates and grants a written constitution
He abdicates in favor of his brother
The soldiers successfully install a new tsar
He orders artillery to fire on the square, crushing the revolt

evt-12-26-1825-imperial-russian-army.butterflyEffect: Loyalist troops fired artillery into the square, crushing the uprising and killing many rebels. The failed Decembrist revolt led Nicholas I into decades of harsh repression, yet it became a founding legend for later generations of Russian revolutionaries.

evt-12-26-1862-american-civil-war.scenario: It is 27 December 1862, and you wade through the flooded cypress swamp of Chickasaw Bayou with Sherman's Union troops, ordered to storm the bluffs beyond and open the road to Vicksburg.
evt-12-26-1862-american-civil-war.prompt: What happens when the Union assault hits the Confederate defenses at Chickasaw Bayou?

choices.text: The Union attack is repulsed with heavy casualties
Confederate defenders surrender without resistance
Union gunboats destroy the bluffs before infantry attack
The assault breaks through and Vicksburg falls immediately

evt-12-26-1862-american-civil-war.butterflyEffect: The Union attack was bloodily repulsed by well-entrenched Confederates, and Sherman withdrew his battered force. The failure forced Grant to abandon his overland plan and eventually adopt the long river campaign that finally captured Vicksburg in July 1863.

evt-12-26-1871-thespis-opera.scenario: It's December 26, 1871, at London's Gaiety Theatre, and you watch the debut of a Christmas entertainment pairing playwright W. S. Gilbert with composer Arthur Sullivan for the very first time.
evt-12-26-1871-thespis-opera.prompt: What happens between these two collaborators after this debut?

choices.text: They don't collaborate again for four years
They immediately begin a decade-long partnership
They take the show on an international tour
Sullivan vows never to work with Gilbert again

evt-12-26-1871-thespis-opera.butterflyEffect: Thespis had only a modest run and its score was largely lost, and Gilbert and Sullivan did not work together again until Trial by Jury in 1875 — whose success finally launched the partnership that produced H.M.S. Pinafore, The Pirates of Penzance, and The Mikado.

evt-12-26-1898-french-academy-of-science.scenario: It is 26 December 1898, and you sit in the audience at the French Academy of Sciences as Pierre and Marie Curie present a paper on a fiercely radioactive new element they've isolated from tonnes of pitchblende ore.
evt-12-26-1898-french-academy-of-science.prompt: What does this announcement ultimately lead to for Marie Curie?

choices.text: Radium is immediately banned as too hazardous to study
The Academy dismisses the findings as fraudulent
She is knighted by the French government for the discovery
She becomes the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences

evt-12-26-1898-french-academy-of-science.butterflyEffect: The Curies' work on radium and radioactivity earned Marie Curie the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911, making her the only person to win Nobels in two different sciences. Radium therapy briefly became fashionable in medicine before its dangers were fully understood.

evt-12-26-1919-babe-ruth.scenario: It's December 26, 1919. You own the financially strained Boston Red Sox and have just received a hefty cash offer from the rival New York Yankees for your star pitcher-slugger, Babe Ruth.
evt-12-26-1919-babe-ruth.prompt: What do you do with Ruth?

choices.text: Retire him from professional baseball
Sell him to the Yankees for cash
Keep him and renegotiate his contract
Trade him to the Chicago White Sox instead

evt-12-26-1919-babe-ruth.butterflyEffect: Owner Harry Frazee sold Ruth to the Yankees, partly to fund a Broadway show, and Ruth's move sparked the Yankees' dynasty while the Red Sox endured an 86-year championship drought many fans blamed on the 'Curse of the Bambino.'

evt-12-26-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It's December 26, 1943. You lead a company of U.S. Marines wading ashore at Cape Gloucester on Japanese-held New Britain, tasked with seizing the island's two strategic airstrips.
evt-12-26-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: What is your unit's immediate objective after landing?

choices.text: Negotiate a local surrender
Capture the airfields
March directly on Rabaul
Establish a naval blockade offshore

evt-12-26-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The 1st Marine Division secured the Cape Gloucester airfields within weeks, denying Japan air cover over the Bismarck Sea and helping isolate the major Japanese base at Rabaul without a costly frontal assault on it.

evt-12-26-1946-bugsy-siegel.scenario: It is 26 December 1946, and you stand in the lobby of the newly opened Flamingo Hotel & Casino, watching Bugsy Siegel greet guests as his mob backers whisper about the casino's soaring construction costs.
evt-12-26-1946-bugsy-siegel.prompt: What happens to Siegel in the months after the Flamingo's troubled opening?

choices.text: He is convicted of tax fraud and imprisoned
He is murdered months later amid suspicion he skimmed funds
He becomes a respected Las Vegas businessman for decades
He sells his stake and retires to Europe

evt-12-26-1946-bugsy-siegel.butterflyEffect: The Flamingo lost money in its early weeks, fueling suspicion among mob partners that Siegel had skimmed construction funds. In June 1947 he was shot dead in Beverly Hills in an unsolved killing, but the Flamingo soon turned profitable, helping launch Las Vegas as a gambling capital.

evt-12-26-1991-dissolution-of-the-soviet.scenario: It is 26 December 1991 in Moscow. The Soviet of the Republics is about to vote on a declaration acknowledging that the union has already ceased to exist, one day after Gorbachev's resignation.
evt-12-26-1991-dissolution-of-the-soviet.prompt: What does this vote formally accomplish?

choices.text: It expels Russia from the union while preserving the USSR
It dissolves the Soviet Union as a sovereign state and subject of international law
It reinstates Gorbachev as head of a reformed union
It declares martial law to preserve the union by force

evt-12-26-1991-dissolution-of-the-soviet.butterflyEffect: The declaration ended nearly 70 years of Soviet statehood, leaving fifteen independent post-Soviet states and reshaping global geopolitics. Russia inherited the USSR's UN Security Council seat and nuclear arsenal, the Cold War's bipolar order dissolved, and the loosely structured Commonwealth of Independent States emerged as a successor framework.

evt-12-26-2003-2003-bam-earthquake.scenario: It is just before 2 a.m. on 26 December 2003 in Bam, Iran. The ground lurches violently, and around you the mudbrick walls of homes and the ancient citadel begin to crack and collapse in the darkness.
evt-12-26-2003-2003-bam-earthquake.prompt: What made this earthquake so catastrophic for the city of Bam?

choices.text: A dam upstream failing and flooding the city
A chemical plant explosion triggered by the tremor
Fires spreading through wooden-framed buildings
Widespread use of mud brick construction that ignored 1989 seismic codes

evt-12-26-2003-2003-bam-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Much of Bam was built from traditional mud brick that did not meet the earthquake-resistant building codes set in 1989, so structures collapsed en masse, killing roughly 34,000 people. The disaster prompted a major international reconstruction effort and renewed pressure on Iran to enforce seismic building standards.

evt-12-26-2004-2004-indian-ocean-earthqu.scenario: It is the morning of 26 December 2004 on a crowded beach in Aceh, Indonesia. Minutes after a distant rumble, the sea suddenly pulls far back from the shore, exposing the ocean floor and stranding fish, while curious onlookers begin walking out onto the wet sand.
evt-12-26-2004-2004-indian-ocean-earthqu.prompt: What should people on the beach do when the sea recedes like this?

choices.text: Gather belongings first, then decide what to do
Walk out to see the stranded fish up close
Wait for an official lifeguard signal before moving
Run immediately to high ground or inland

evt-12-26-2004-2004-indian-ocean-earthqu.butterflyEffect: The retreating sea was the warning sign of an incoming tsunami, and many who lingered or walked out to look were caught by the waves that followed within minutes. The catastrophe killed an estimated 227,898 people across 14 countries and led directly to the creation of the Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System to prevent a repeat.

evt-12-26-2006-2006-hengchun-earthquakes.scenario: It's the evening of December 26, 2006, and you manage international telecom traffic in Taiwan as two powerful earthquakes near the Luzon Strait sever several undersea fiber-optic cables.
evt-12-26-2006-2006-hengchun-earthquakes.prompt: How do you keep communications flowing across the region?

choices.text: Reroute traffic via satellite links and remaining cables
Rely solely on shortwave radio for all traffic
Wait for the cables to repair themselves
Shut down all international service until repairs finish

evt-12-26-2006-2006-hengchun-earthquakes.butterflyEffect: The quakes cut multiple submarine cables, crippling internet and phone service across East and Southeast Asia for days while repair ships worked to fix the lines; the crisis exposed how fragile the region's cable network was and pushed telecoms toward more redundant routing.

evt-12-26-2012-high-speed-rail-in-china.scenario: It's 26 December 2012, and you board the inaugural train pulling out of Beijing on a brand-new line stretching over 2,200 km to Guangzhou, officials proudly calling it the longest high-speed rail route ever built.
evt-12-26-2012-high-speed-rail-in-china.prompt: What follows this launch for China's high-speed rail ambitions?

choices.text: The government converts the line to freight-only operation
The line proves unprofitable and is scaled back within a decade
China's network becomes the world's longest and most heavily used
China halts further high-speed rail construction to focus on airports

evt-12-26-2012-high-speed-rail-in-china.butterflyEffect: The Beijing–Guangzhou line became a cornerstone of a rapidly expanding network. Within a decade China's HSR system exceeded 50,000 km, more than the rest of the world combined, reshaping domestic travel, business, and regional economies along its routes.

evt-12-26-2015-2015-garland-tornado.scenario: It is the night of 26 December 2015, and sirens wail across your Rowlett, Texas neighborhood as a violent tornado bears down in the darkness.
evt-12-26-2015-2015-garland-tornado.prompt: What is the safest action to take right now?

choices.text: Open all windows to equalize air pressure
Go outside to watch the storm's progress
Take shelter in an interior room away from windows
Drive away from the area immediately

evt-12-26-2015-2015-garland-tornado.butterflyEffect: The EF4 tornado killed 10 people and injured 468 across Garland, Rowlett, and Sunnyvale, making it the deadliest US tornado of 2015. The disaster's nighttime timing and severity prompted North Texas communities to push for improved warning systems and shelter requirements.

evt-12-27-537-hagia-sophia.scenario: It is 27 December 537, and you stand among the crowd as Emperor Justinian I enters the newly completed Hagia Sophia for its dedication, gazing up at a dome unlike anything built before in the Roman world.
evt-12-27-537-hagia-sophia.prompt: What happens to this original dome only about two decades later?

choices.text: It is converted into a mosque almost immediately
It partially collapses in an earthquake and is rebuilt taller
It burns down during a renewed round of riots
It remains completely unchanged for a thousand years

evt-12-27-537-hagia-sophia.butterflyEffect: An earthquake in 558 caused the dome to partially collapse. It was rebuilt taller and more stable by Isidore the Younger, completed in 562, giving Hagia Sophia the profile that endures today and influenced mosque and cathedral design for centuries.

evt-12-27-1521-wittenberg.scenario: It is late December 1521. Martin Luther is in hiding at Wartburg Castle, and three self-proclaimed prophets from Zwickau have arrived in Wittenberg preaching direct revelation while students smash images in the churches. Melanchthon does not know how to stop them.
evt-12-27-1521-wittenberg.prompt: What actually happened to restore order in Wittenberg?

choices.text: Luther secretly leaves hiding and returns to preach against the radicals
The city council adopts the prophets' teachings as official doctrine
Elector Frederick bans all religious preaching in the city
Melanchthon has the prophets arrested and executed

evt-12-27-1521-wittenberg.butterflyEffect: Luther defied the imperial ban and secretly returned to Wittenberg in March 1522, preaching against the radicals and reasserting his authority over the Reformation. This split set the template for later, sharper breaks between mainstream Lutheranism and radical movements like the Anabaptists.

evt-12-27-1657-new-netherland.scenario: It is December 1657 in the town of Flushing in New Netherland. Director-General Peter Stuyvesant has banned Quaker worship, and your neighbors are drafting a petition to send him defying the order.
evt-12-27-1657-new-netherland.prompt: What did the townspeople's petition assert?

choices.text: That the town should relocate entirely to Rhode Island
That the ban should be accepted without protest
That religious liberty should extend to Quakers and all residents
That only Dutch Reformed settlers deserved worship rights

evt-12-27-1657-new-netherland.butterflyEffect: The Flushing Remonstrance declared that all people, including Quakers, deserved freedom of conscience, and Stuyvesant initially jailed several signers for it. The document is now remembered as an early American statement of religious liberty, later echoed in the First Amendment.

evt-12-27-1831-hms-beagle.scenario: It's 27 December 1831, and you're a young naturalist boarding HMS Beagle at Plymouth, invited by Captain Robert FitzRoy on a survey voyage expected to last years and cover thousands of miles.
evt-12-27-1831-hms-beagle.prompt: What theory does this voyage's observations eventually lead you, Charles Darwin, to develop?

choices.text: The theory of evolution by natural selection
A treatise on ocean tides and currents
A new method of longitude calculation for the Royal Navy
A survey confirming the biblical age of the Earth

evt-12-27-1831-hms-beagle.butterflyEffect: Darwin's observations, especially of finches and tortoises in the Galápagos, fed directly into his theory of evolution by natural selection, published in 1859 as On the Origin of Species and transforming biology and humanity's understanding of life's diversity.

evt-12-27-1922-imperial-japanese-navy.scenario: It's December 27, 1922, at Yokosuka. You watch as the Imperial Japanese Navy commissions a new warship built from the keel up as a flat-top, unlike the converted vessels other navies are experimenting with.
evt-12-27-1922-imperial-japanese-navy.prompt: What makes this ship's commissioning historically significant?

choices.text: It sets a world speed record for surface warships
It's the first Japanese submarine capable of transoceanic voyages
It's Japan's largest battleship of the era
It's the world's first purpose-built aircraft carrier commissioned into service

evt-12-27-1922-imperial-japanese-navy.butterflyEffect: Hōshō became the world's first purpose-built aircraft carrier to enter service, ahead of similar British and American efforts. Its design shaped Japanese carrier doctrine that would later be used devastatingly at Pearl Harbor and Midway.

evt-12-27-1932-radio-city-music-hall.scenario: It's opening night, 27 December 1932, at the brand-new Radio City Music Hall. Impresario Samuel 'Roxy' Rothafel has booked an ambitious four-hour vaudeville-style variety show for the venue's debut.
evt-12-27-1932-radio-city-music-hall.prompt: What happened to Roxy's opening-night variety format?

choices.text: It was an instant smash and ran unchanged for years
It was replaced by a boxing arena
It flopped, and the hall quickly switched to a movie-and-stage-show format
The hall closed permanently within a week

evt-12-27-1932-radio-city-music-hall.butterflyEffect: The lavish variety show underwhelmed critics and audiences, and within weeks Radio City Music Hall pivoted to showing first-run movies paired with elaborate stage shows featuring the Rockettes. That formula made it the world's most successful movie theater for decades and cemented Rockefeller Center's reputation as an entertainment landmark.

evt-12-27-1949-indonesian-national-revol.scenario: It is 27 December 1949 in the Netherlands, and you stand beside Queen Juliana as she signs the papers ending four years of war and diplomacy over the Dutch East Indies.
evt-12-27-1949-indonesian-national-revol.prompt: What did the signed documents actually do?

choices.text: Transferred sovereignty over the Dutch East Indies to the new Republic of the United States of Indonesia
Annexed additional Indonesian territory to the Dutch crown
Refused to recognize Indonesian independence in any form
Declared a renewed Dutch military offensive against the Republic

evt-12-27-1949-indonesian-national-revol.butterflyEffect: The Netherlands formally transferred sovereignty over the Dutch East Indies to the Republic of the United States of Indonesia. Sukarno became president, and within a year Indonesia dissolved the federal structure into a unitary republic; disputes over Dutch-held West New Guinea would drag on until 1962.

evt-12-27-1979-soviet-afghan-war.scenario: It's the night of 27 December 1979 outside Kabul. Soviet special forces have surrounded Tajbeg Palace, where Afghan President Hafizullah Amin is holed up with his loyal guards.
evt-12-27-1979-soviet-afghan-war.prompt: What was the outcome of the Soviet assault on the palace?

choices.text: Amin negotiated a truce and remained in power
Amin was killed and a new Soviet-backed leader installed
Amin was captured and put on trial
The assault failed and Soviet troops withdrew

evt-12-27-1979-soviet-afghan-war.butterflyEffect: Soviet commandos killed Amin during the raid and installed Babrak Karmal as the new head of government, formally beginning the Soviet occupation of Afghanistan. The invasion triggered a decade-long insurgency backed by the US, Pakistan, and others, draining Soviet resources and contributing to the USSR's eventual collapse, while also seeding mujahideen networks that shaped later conflicts.

evt-12-27-1985-primatology.scenario: It is 27 December 1985 at the Karisoke Research Centre in Rwanda. You arrive to find primatologist Dian Fossey's cabin ransacked and discover she has been murdered, likely by an attacker wielding a panga.
evt-12-27-1985-primatology.prompt: What happened in the investigation that followed?

choices.text: Poachers were swiftly captured and convicted with clear evidence
No investigation was ever opened into her death
Rwandan authorities convicted an American researcher in absentia amid disputed evidence
The Rwandan government shut down the Karisoke Research Centre entirely

evt-12-27-1985-primatology.butterflyEffect: Rwandan authorities controversially convicted her American research assistant, Wayne McGuire, in absentia, though many believe local poachers or officials angered by her anti-poaching campaigns were responsible. The case remains officially unresolved, but her Karisoke research continued and helped anchor ongoing mountain gorilla conservation in the region.

evt-12-27-1997-loyalist-volunteer-force.scenario: It is 27 December 1997 inside HM Prison Maze. Billy Wright, leader of the breakaway Loyalist Volunteer Force, is being held in a segregated wing when INLA prisoners manage to reach him with smuggled weapons.
evt-12-27-1997-loyalist-volunteer-force.prompt: What followed Wright's assassination inside the prison?

choices.text: The LVF voluntarily disbanded in response
Loyalist gunmen carried out revenge killings, straining the peace process
The British government suspended all peace talks indefinitely
The INLA declared a full ceasefire following the killing

evt-12-27-1997-loyalist-volunteer-force.butterflyEffect: Loyalist paramilitaries retaliated with a wave of sectarian killings in early 1998, straining the fragile negotiations that led to the Good Friday Agreement that April. The violence exposed how prison security failures could threaten a peace process built outside the prison walls.

evt-12-27-1999-burger-king.scenario: It's 27 December 1999, and reports have surfaced that Burger King's popular Pokémon Poké Ball toys have suffocated infants who pressed the concave plastic halves over their mouths and noses.
evt-12-27-1999-burger-king.prompt: What does Burger King do in response to the reports?

choices.text: Sues the toy manufacturer without informing customers
Redesigns the toy quietly while continuing distribution
Ignores the reports and keeps the promotion running
Recalls millions of the toys nationwide

evt-12-27-1999-burger-king.butterflyEffect: Burger King and the CPSC recalled roughly 25 million Poké Ball toys, one of the largest recalls ever tied to a fast-food promotion. The incident sharpened industry-wide scrutiny of small-parts suffocation hazards in kids' meal giveaways.

evt-12-27-2002-human-cloning.scenario: It's 27 December 2002, and you're a reporter at a Florida press conference where Clonaid founder Dr. Brigitte Boisselier announces that a baby girl named 'Eve' has been born as the world's first human clone.
evt-12-27-2002-human-cloning.prompt: How did the scientific community and press respond to the claim?

choices.text: The claim was met with widespread skepticism since no verified proof was ever provided
Independent labs quickly confirmed the cloning with DNA tests
Boisselier won a Nobel Prize for the breakthrough
Governments immediately legalized human cloning research

evt-12-27-2002-human-cloning.butterflyEffect: Clonaid, founded by members of the Raëlian religious movement, never produced independent verification of the birth, and most scientists dismissed the claim as a hoax or publicity stunt. The episode intensified global debate over human cloning ethics and spurred several countries to tighten laws banning reproductive cloning research.

evt-12-27-2002-2002-grozny-truck-bombing.scenario: It's December 27, 2002, and you work inside the pro-Moscow Chechen government headquarters in Grozny when a truck races past the perimeter checkpoint toward the building.
evt-12-27-2002-2002-grozny-truck-bombing.prompt: What follows the truck's approach to the compound?

choices.text: Truck bombs detonate against the building in a catastrophic attack
Guards intercept and disable the truck before it reaches the compound
The building is evacuated in time and the truck is diverted away
The truck turns out to be delivering routine government supplies

evt-12-27-2002-2002-grozny-truck-bombing.butterflyEffect: Truck bombs detonated against the building in one of the deadliest attacks of the Second Chechen War, killing 72 people. The bombing hardened Moscow's resolve to maintain its military presence in Chechnya and marked an escalation in suicide bombing tactics used by separatist and Islamist insurgents in the years that followed.

evt-12-27-2004-radiation.scenario: It's December 27, 2004, and you're a satellite operator monitoring gamma-ray instruments when a burst of radiation from a magnetar 50,000 light-years away sweeps past Earth in milliseconds.
evt-12-27-2004-radiation.prompt: What happens to your detectors when the burst arrives?

choices.text: Earth's atmosphere absorbs the radiation before any instrument detects it
Detectors on multiple satellites saturate instantly, overwhelmed by the burst
Only ground-based telescopes detect the event
The signal is too faint to register on any instrument

evt-12-27-2004-radiation.butterflyEffect: The magnetar SGR 1806-20's giant flare was the brightest such burst ever recorded from beyond the solar system, saturating gamma-ray detectors on multiple orbiting satellites and measurably disturbing Earth's ionosphere. The event gave astronomers rare direct evidence of a magnetar's extreme power, reshaping models of these ultra-magnetized neutron stars.

evt-12-27-2007-mombasa.scenario: It's late December 2007 in Mombasa. Kenya's Electoral Commission has just declared Mwai Kibaki the winner of a bitterly contested presidential vote, and opposition supporters are pouring into the streets in fury over what they call a stolen election.
evt-12-27-2007-mombasa.prompt: What followed the disputed election announcement across Kenya?

choices.text: International observers declared the election fully free and fair
Nationwide violence and ethnic clashes killed over 1,000 people
The Electoral Commission reversed its decision within days
Kibaki resigned immediately to avoid unrest

evt-12-27-2007-mombasa.butterflyEffect: The violence, fueled by ethnic and political tensions, killed more than 1,000 Kenyans and displaced hundreds of thousands before former UN chief Kofi Annan brokered a power-sharing deal in February 2008. Kibaki remained president while rival Raila Odinga became prime minister in a coalition government, a compromise that reshaped Kenyan politics and later led to International Criminal Court indictments over the violence.

evt-12-27-2007-benazir-bhutto.scenario: It is 27 December 2007 in Rawalpindi. You are part of Benazir Bhutto's security detail as she stands through the sunroof of her vehicle, waving to supporters after a campaign rally, moments before gunfire and an explosion tear through the crowd.
evt-12-27-2007-benazir-bhutto.prompt: What happened to her party's leadership in the aftermath?

choices.text: The elections proceeded on schedule with no change in leadership
Leadership passed to her husband Asif Ali Zardari and son Bilawal
President Musharraf resigned within days of the assassination
Nawaz Sharif was immediately installed as PPP leader

evt-12-27-2007-benazir-bhutto.butterflyEffect: Leadership of the Pakistan People's Party passed to her widower, Asif Ali Zardari, and her teenage son Bilawal. Zardari went on to become President of Pakistan after the PPP won the delayed 2008 elections, while investigations pointed to militants linked to the Pakistani Taliban.

evt-12-27-2007-prime-minister.scenario: It's December 27, 2007, in Rawalpindi. You're part of Benazir Bhutto's security detail as she stands through the sunroof of her vehicle, waving to supporters after a campaign rally.

choices.text: A rival's car bomb misses her convoy entirely
She is whisked away safely by her bodyguards
She is shot and then a suicide bomber detonates, killing her
She collapses from heat exhaustion in the crowd

evt-12-27-2007-prime-minister.butterflyEffect: Bhutto was shot and then killed when a suicide bomber detonated near her vehicle, sparking nationwide riots. Elections were postponed to February 2008, and the sympathy vote helped her party win, ultimately installing her widower Asif Ali Zardari as Pakistan's president.

evt-12-27-2008-gaza-war-2008-2009.scenario: It is late December 2008. A six-month truce between Israel and Hamas has collapsed and rocket fire from Gaza has resumed. You sit in the Israeli security cabinet weighing how to respond.
evt-12-27-2008-gaza-war-2008-2009.prompt: What did Israel decide to do?

choices.text: Launch a major air and ground military operation against Gaza
Impose an economic blockade only, without military strikes
Request Egyptian mediation for a new truce without military action
Ask the UN to deploy peacekeepers along the border immediately

evt-12-27-2008-gaza-war-2008-2009.butterflyEffect: Israel launched Operation Cast Lead, a three-week air and ground offensive that ended in a unilateral ceasefire in January 2009. The operation drew intense international scrutiny, including the UN's Goldstone Report, and set the pattern for further large-scale Gaza operations in 2012 and 2014.

evt-12-27-2009-2009-iranian-presidential.scenario: It's Ashura, December 27, 2009, and you march with hundreds of thousands through Tehran chanting against Ahmadinejad's disputed re-election, defying the regime's ban on protest during this sacred day.
evt-12-27-2009-2009-iranian-presidential.prompt: How do security forces respond to the march?

choices.text: They allow the march to proceed without any intervention
They negotiate a truce directly with opposition leaders
They open fire and violently suppress the marchers, killing several
They arrest only foreign journalists covering the march

evt-12-27-2009-2009-iranian-presidential.butterflyEffect: Security forces opened fire and violently suppressed the demonstrators, killing several people, including a nephew of opposition leader Mir-Hossein Mousavi. The crackdown drew sharp international condemnation and became one of the bloodiest days of the Green Movement, though the uprising was ultimately contained through mass arrests over the following months.

evt-12-27-2019-bek-air-flight-2100.scenario: It's 27 December 2019 at Almaty International Airport. Bek Air Flight 2100's Fokker 100 has just crashed shortly after takeoff, and Kazakh aviation officials must decide how to respond to the disaster.
evt-12-27-2019-bek-air-flight-2100.prompt: What action followed the investigation into the crash?

choices.text: Bek Air's operating license was suspended and its fleet grounded
The airline expanded its Fokker 100 fleet the following year
No changes were made to Kazakhstan's aviation regulations
The airline was given a safety award for its response

evt-12-27-2019-bek-air-flight-2100.butterflyEffect: Kazakhstan's civil aviation authority grounded Bek Air's entire fleet and suspended its operating certificate over safety violations, effectively ending the airline. The crash also prompted a broader review of aging Fokker 100 aircraft and stricter oversight of domestic carriers in Kazakhstan.

evt-12-27-2024-president-of-south-korea.scenario: It's December 27, 2024, in Seoul. As acting president since Yoon Suk-yeol's impeachment, you've refused to fill vacant seats on the Constitutional Court, and the National Assembly is voting on your fate.
evt-12-27-2024-president-of-south-korea.prompt: What happens immediately after your impeachment?

choices.text: Yoon Suk-yeol is immediately reinstated as president
The National Assembly votes to dissolve itself
Finance Minister Choi Sang-mok becomes the new acting president
Han Duck-soo is arrested by prosecutors on the spot

evt-12-27-2024-president-of-south-korea.butterflyEffect: The National Assembly impeached Han Duck-soo, making him the second South Korean leader removed within weeks. Finance Minister Choi Sang-mok became the new acting president, deepening a political crisis as the Constitutional Court continued weighing Yoon Suk-yeol's fate.

evt-12-28-484-alaric-ii.scenario: It is 28 December 484 in Toulouse, and you are a Visigothic noble watching young Alaric II take his father Euric's throne, inheriting a kingdom stretching across Gaul and Hispania.
evt-12-28-484-alaric-ii.prompt: What rising power would come to threaten Alaric II's reign over the Visigothic kingdom?

choices.text: The Byzantine Empire under Justinian
The Vandal kingdom in North Africa
The Ostrogoths under Theodoric the Great
The Frankish kingdom under Clovis

evt-12-28-484-alaric-ii.butterflyEffect: The Frankish king Clovis steadily expanded his power and eventually crushed Alaric II at the Battle of Vouillé in 507, killing him and ending Visigothic rule in most of Gaul. The Visigoths retreated into Hispania, reshaping the political map of what would become medieval Spain and France.

evt-12-28-1065-westminster-abbey.scenario: It is 28 December 1065 and you stand among courtiers at the consecration of Westminster Abbey, though King Edward the Confessor, too ill to attend, remains absent from his own great church.
evt-12-28-1065-westminster-abbey.prompt: What happened only days after the abbey's consecration that reshaped English history?

choices.text: Edward crowned himself king again inside the new abbey
Harold Godwinson was crowned immediately at the ceremony itself
Edward the Confessor died, sparking a succession crisis and the Norman Conquest
William of Normandy personally attended the consecration

evt-12-28-1065-westminster-abbey.butterflyEffect: Edward the Confessor died on 5 January 1066, triggering a succession crisis. Harold Godwinson was crowned in the new abbey the next day, and later that year William the Conqueror was also crowned there after the Norman Conquest, beginning the abbey's enduring role as the site of English coronations.

evt-12-28-1612-galileo-galilei.scenario: You are Galileo Galilei in Padua, tracking Jupiter's moons through your telescope on the night of 28 December 1612. A faint, unfamiliar point of light sits near Jupiter, and you jot down its position in your notebook without giving it much more thought.
evt-12-28-1612-galileo-galilei.prompt: How does Galileo record this faint point of light in his notes?

choices.text: As an ordinary fixed background star
As a newly discovered moon of Jupiter
As a previously unknown planet
As a comet passing near Jupiter

evt-12-28-1612-galileo-galilei.butterflyEffect: Galileo logged the object as an ordinary fixed star, never suspecting it was the planet Neptune. The sighting went unrecognized for over two centuries, until astronomers re-examining his notebooks after Neptune's official 1846 discovery realized he had unknowingly observed it 234 years earlier.

evt-12-28-1767-taksin.scenario: It's December 1767, months after Ayutthaya's fall to Burmese forces. You are Taksin, just crowned king of the new Thonburi Kingdom, facing a fractured Siam with rival warlords and no unified defense.
evt-12-28-1767-taksin.prompt: What should Taksin do to secure his fledgling kingdom?

choices.text: Accept vassal status under Burma to avoid further war
Divide the realm among regional warlords for stability
Fortify Thonburi and campaign to reunify the fractured Siamese territories
Abandon the coast and retreat far inland for safety

evt-12-28-1767-taksin.butterflyEffect: Taksin fortified Thonburi as a river-based capital and launched military campaigns that reunified most of the former Siamese territories under his rule. His conquests restored Siamese sovereignty and laid the foundation for the Chakri dynasty, which later moved the capital across the river to Bangkok.

evt-12-28-1908-1908-messina-earthquake.scenario: It is the early hours of 28 December 1908 and you command a naval vessel that has just reached the ruined shoreline of the Strait of Messina, where entire cities lie in rubble.
evt-12-28-1908-1908-messina-earthquake.prompt: What did arriving naval crews from Italy and other nations prioritize in the earthquake's immediate aftermath?

choices.text: Refusing foreign assistance to protect Italian sovereignty
Immediately rebuilding the cities on the same foundations
Evacuating the entire region before any rescue attempts
Digging survivors out of collapsed buildings by hand

evt-12-28-1908-1908-messina-earthquake.butterflyEffect: Sailors from Italian, Russian, British and other ships worked alongside survivors to dig victims from the rubble in the days after the quake, one of the first large-scale international disaster responses. The catastrophe, which killed around 120,000 people, later spurred stricter Italian seismic building codes for reconstruction.

evt-12-28-1918-1918-united-kingdom-gener.scenario: It is December 1918 in a Dublin constituency, and the count confirms Constance Markievicz has won a seat in the House of Commons, becoming the first woman ever elected to it.
evt-12-28-1918-1918-united-kingdom-gener.prompt: In line with Sinn Féin policy, what did Markievicz do with her seat?

choices.text: Refused to take her seat, following Sinn Féin's abstentionist policy
Joined a coalition government at Westminster
Resigned the seat immediately after the count
Took her seat, becoming the first woman to sit in the Commons

evt-12-28-1918-1918-united-kingdom-gener.butterflyEffect: Markievicz refused to take her seat at Westminster, honoring Sinn Féin's abstentionist policy against British rule. She and other elected Sinn Féin MPs instead convened in Dublin in January 1919 as the First Dáil, declaring Irish independence and setting the revolutionary period in motion.

evt-12-28-1943-world-war-ii.scenario: It is late December 1943 and you are a Canadian infantryman fighting street by street through the shattered town of Ortona, Italy, where German paratroopers have turned every building into a fortress.
evt-12-28-1943-world-war-ii.prompt: How did Canadian troops advance through Ortona without being cut down in the exposed streets?

choices.text: Blowing mouseholes through connecting walls between buildings
Relying entirely on naval bombardment of the whole town
Marching in formation down the main street
Dropping paratroopers behind German lines

evt-12-28-1943-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: Canadian soldiers blasted holes through interior walls to move building-to-building without crossing open streets, a tactic later called 'mouseholing.' After eight brutal days the town fell on 28 December, earning Ortona the nickname 'Little Stalingrad' and cementing Canada's reputation as a hardened fighting force in the Italian campaign.

evt-12-28-1948-douglas-dc-3.scenario: It is 28 December 1948, and you are aboard a DC-3 flying from San Juan to Miami when radio contact with the aircraft goes silent roughly 50 miles short of the Florida coast.
evt-12-28-1948-douglas-dc-3.prompt: What did the ensuing search for the missing airliner find?

choices.text: No wreckage or survivors were ever found
Wreckage was located off the Bahamas within days
The aircraft was found to have been hijacked and landed in Cuba
The plane made an emergency landing on a remote airstrip

evt-12-28-1948-douglas-dc-3.butterflyEffect: No wreckage, debris, or survivors were ever recovered despite an extensive search, and the disappearance of NC16002 remains officially unsolved. The case became one of the founding stories cited in later Bermuda Triangle lore.

evt-12-28-1956-chin-peng.scenario: It's December 1956 in Baling, Malaya. You are Chin Peng, meeting Chief Minister David Marshall and Tunku Abdul Rahman, who will only grant amnesty if the Communist Party of Malaya disbands unconditionally and surrenders all arms.
evt-12-28-1956-chin-peng.prompt: What should Chin Peng do when offered amnesty only on terms of total surrender?

choices.text: Demand Tunku's resignation before further talks
Reject the terms and continue the armed insurgency
Accept the terms and surrender the movement immediately
Agree to disband publicly while hiding weapons for later use

evt-12-28-1956-chin-peng.butterflyEffect: Chin Peng rejected the terms, refusing to disband the CPM or surrender without political recognition. The talks collapsed, and the Malayan Emergency dragged on for decades until a formal peace accord was finally signed in 1989.

evt-12-28-1958-1958-nfl-championship-gam.scenario: It is sudden-death overtime at Yankee Stadium on 28 December 1958, and you carry the ball for the Baltimore Colts just yards from the Giants' goal line in the first title game ever decided this way.
evt-12-28-1958-1958-nfl-championship-gam.prompt: How did the Colts win the first sudden-death championship in NFL history?

choices.text: A field goal split the uprights as time expired
Alan Ameche scored on a short touchdown run
An interception was returned for a touchdown
A long touchdown pass was completed to the end zone

evt-12-28-1958-1958-nfl-championship-gam.butterflyEffect: Fullback Alan Ameche plunged in for the winning touchdown, sealing a 23–17 victory. The drama unfolded on national television and is widely credited with launching pro football's rise in American popularity, later voted the greatest game of the NFL's first century.

evt-12-28-1964-vietnam-war.scenario: It is 28 December 1964 near the village of Binh Gia, and Viet Cong regiments have breached the eastern perimeter as South Vietnamese reinforcements race toward the fighting.
evt-12-28-1964-vietnam-war.prompt: What followed for the South Vietnamese forces sent to relieve the village?

choices.text: The village was evacuated before any fighting occurred
They were ambushed and suffered a heavy defeat
US Marines landed directly to reinforce the village
They repelled the attack and relieved the village decisively

evt-12-28-1964-vietnam-war.butterflyEffect: The reinforcing ARVN units were ambushed and badly mauled, handing the Viet Cong one of its most significant conventional victories of the war. The battle shocked American advisers by showing Communist forces could now stand and defeat ARVN in open battle, accelerating the case for direct US ground intervention in 1965.

evt-12-28-1967-muriel-siebert.scenario: You are Muriel Siebert, a securities analyst determined to become the first woman to own a seat on the New York Stock Exchange. Exchange rules require every applicant to be formally nominated by two current members before purchase can even be considered.
evt-12-28-1967-muriel-siebert.prompt: What did Siebert need to secure before she could buy her NYSE seat?

choices.text: Approval from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
A unanimous vote of the full exchange membership
A personal endorsement from the NYSE chairman alone
Sponsorship from two existing exchange members

evt-12-28-1967-muriel-siebert.butterflyEffect: Siebert found two existing members willing to sponsor her and was admitted on December 28, 1967, joining 1,365 men as the exchange's 1,366th member. She went on to found her own discount brokerage and later became New York's Superintendent of Banking, remaining a symbol of women breaking into Wall Street's top ranks.

evt-12-28-1972-selective-service-system.scenario: It's December 28, 1972, and you've just received an induction notice for the U.S. military as this is the last day the Selective Service System has scheduled draft inductions.
evt-12-28-1972-selective-service-system.prompt: What actually followed this final scheduled induction day?

choices.text: Congress expanded the draft to cover more age groups
Draft calls ended and the U.S. moved toward an all-volunteer military
Induction quotas were doubled for the following year
The Vietnam War ended immediately as a result

evt-12-28-1972-selective-service-system.butterflyEffect: No further men were drafted after this date; conscription authority lapsed in mid-1973 as the U.S. formally shifted to an all-volunteer military. This ended nearly three decades of peacetime and wartime draft, reshaping American defense policy and recruitment for generations.

evt-12-28-1973-united-states.scenario: You are a White House aide on 28 December 1973, watching President Nixon sign a bill meant to halt the disappearance of wildlife across the country.
evt-12-28-1973-united-states.prompt: What did this new law require?

choices.text: Expansion of the National Park System into new wilderness areas
A nationwide ban on the pesticide DDT
Creation of a new federal agency to enforce all environmental law
Federal protection for threatened and endangered species and their critical habitats

evt-12-28-1973-united-states.butterflyEffect: The Endangered Species Act mandated federal protection for species at risk of extinction and the habitats they depend on. It became one of the most powerful conservation laws in the world, credited with helping recover the bald eagle, gray wolf, and American alligator, though it would also spark decades of land-use battles.

evt-12-28-1978-united-airlines-flight-17.scenario: You are the flight engineer aboard United 173, circling near Portland while the captain focuses on a landing gear indicator light that won't confirm the gear is down. Fuel gauges are dropping steadily, but no one has called out how little remains.
evt-12-28-1978-united-airlines-flight-17.prompt: What should the crew have done as fuel ran critically low?

choices.text: Land immediately on the fuel remaining, gear concerns aside
Circle until fuel is nearly exhausted to burn it off safely
Dump remaining fuel and prepare for a water landing
Continue troubleshooting until the gear light confirms safe

evt-12-28-1978-united-airlines-flight-17.butterflyEffect: The crew kept troubleshooting the gear problem until the DC-8 ran out of fuel and crashed in a Portland neighborhood, killing ten. The NTSB's findings on breakdowns in cockpit communication directly led airlines to adopt Crew Resource Management training, reshaping how flight crews are taught to speak up and manage workload under pressure.

evt-12-28-2006-war-in-somalia-2006-2009.scenario: It is late December 2006 and you serve Somalia's Transitional Federal Government, watching Ethiopian tanks and troops cross the border to help you retake Mogadishu from the Islamic Courts Union.
evt-12-28-2006-war-in-somalia-2006-2009.prompt: What did the Ethiopian intervention actually achieve for the TFG in the years that followed?

choices.text: Temporary victory over the ICU followed by a growing insurgency that reversed most gains
Direct American ground troops replacing Ethiopian forces within months
A swift, lasting peace under a stable TFG government
Complete failure to enter Mogadishu at all

evt-12-28-2006-war-in-somalia-2006-2009.butterflyEffect: Ethiopian forces quickly routed the ICU and installed the TFG in Mogadishu, but a fierce insurgency erupted almost immediately. By 2008 insurgents had reclaimed most of the lost territory, the conflict caused the second-largest displacement in Somalia since 1991, and the chaos fed the rise of al-Shabaab.

evt-12-28-2009-dhondup-wangchen.scenario: You are Tibetan filmmaker Dhondup Wangchen, held for over a year after smuggling out tapes of ordinary Tibetans speaking candidly about the Dalai Lama and Chinese rule. A closed court is about to deliver its verdict on charges tied to your documentary Leaving Fear Behind.
evt-12-28-2009-dhondup-wangchen.prompt: What sentence did the Chinese court hand down on this day in 2009?

choices.text: A fine and release with no prison term
A suspended sentence with house arrest
Immediate deportation from China
Six years in prison

evt-12-28-2009-dhondup-wangchen.butterflyEffect: Wangchen was sentenced to six years in prison for 'subversion of state power' and served the full term, released in 2014 in poor health. His documentary and imprisonment became a rallying point for international press-freedom and Tibetan rights advocacy, cited for years afterward in human rights reporting on China.

evt-12-28-2014-indonesia-airasia-flight-.scenario: It is early morning on 28 December 2014, and you are in the cockpit of an Airbus A320 climbing to skirt storm cells over the Java Sea when a rudder system fault triggers repeated alarms.
evt-12-28-2014-indonesia-airasia-flight-.prompt: What did investigators conclude followed the malfunction?

choices.text: A midair collision with another aircraft caused the crash
The pilots' handling of the fault led to a stall and loss of control of the aircraft
An engine failure forced a controlled ditching in the sea
The aircraft ran out of fuel after a diversion

evt-12-28-2014-indonesia-airasia-flight-.butterflyEffect: Investigators found the pilots' response to the rudder travel limiter fault led to loss of control and an aerodynamic stall from which they never recovered, killing all 162 aboard. The crash prompted new maintenance directives on the faulty component and renewed emphasis on manual flying skills for high-altitude upsets.

evt-12-29-1812-war-of-1812.scenario: It is 29 December 1812, off the coast of Brazil. You command USS Constitution, facing HMS Java in open water. Your gunners are ready, but Java's crew is eager to grapple and board.
evt-12-29-1812-war-of-1812.prompt: Do you close for boarding or keep firing from a distance to wreck Java's rigging?

choices.text: Signal for reinforcements before engaging further
Order an immediate boarding action to settle it hand-to-hand
Break off and retreat to preserve the ship for the squadron
Maintain distance and pound Java's rigging with sustained gunfire

evt-12-29-1812-war-of-1812.butterflyEffect: Constitution held her distance, shot away Java's masts and rigging, and forced her surrender after a fierce three-hour fight in which Java's captain was killed. It was Constitution's third frigate victory of the war, shattering British confidence in ship-to-ship duels and cementing the legend of 'Old Ironsides' in American memory.

evt-12-29-1845-republic-of-texas.scenario: It is late 1845, and as a delegate to the Texas Congress, you must decide whether to accept the United States' offer of annexation, knowing Mexico still claims Texas as its own territory and has warned of war.
evt-12-29-1845-republic-of-texas.prompt: What does the Texas Congress decide?

choices.text: Accept annexation and join the United States as a state
Delay the decision indefinitely pending Mexican recognition
Reject annexation and remain an independent republic
Seek annexation by Britain instead for protection

evt-12-29-1845-republic-of-texas.butterflyEffect: Texas was admitted as the 28th U.S. state, the very outcome Mexico had warned would mean war. Within months, disputes over the new state's southern border escalated into the Mexican-American War, which ended in 1848 with Mexico ceding vast territories that became the American Southwest.

evt-12-29-1860-french-navy.scenario: It is 29 December 1860 at Blackwall on the Thames. You watch as Britain's new warship, built to answer France's revolutionary ironclad Gloire, slides into the water for the first time.
evt-12-29-1860-french-navy.prompt: What did the launch of this new British ironclad mean for naval power?

choices.text: It was scrapped soon after due to construction flaws
It proved ironclads impractical and Britain returned to wooden ships
It rendered existing wooden warships obsolete and escalated the ironclad arms race
It ended naval competition between Britain and France entirely

evt-12-29-1860-french-navy.butterflyEffect: HMS Warrior, faster and more heavily armed than any ship afloat, instantly made existing wooden battlefleets obsolete and touched off an intense Anglo-French ironclad arms race. Within a generation, navies worldwide had abandoned wooden hulls entirely.

evt-12-29-1876-ashtabula-river-railroad-.scenario: It is the night of 29 December 1876, and the Pacific Express has just plunged through a collapsing iron bridge into the frozen Ashtabula River. Wooden cars, lit by oil lamps and heating stoves, are catching fire around trapped passengers.
evt-12-29-1876-ashtabula-river-railroad-.prompt: What do the arriving firefighters actually do as the wreck burns?

choices.text: They chop through the river ice to reach submerged cars first
They evacuate the town and let the wreck burn out untouched
They decline to fight the fire, leaving bystanders to pull out survivors
They pour water on the flames immediately to save trapped passengers

evt-12-29-1876-ashtabula-river-railroad-.butterflyEffect: Firefighters held back from dousing the flames, and many survivors of the initial crash burned to death in the wreckage while bystanders tried to pull others free. Public outrage over what was then the deadliest train wreck in U.S. history spurred investigations into the failed iron truss bridge and helped push forward stronger bridge engineering and rail safety standards in the decades that followed.

evt-12-29-1890-wounded-knee-massacre.scenario: It's the morning of December 29, 1890, at Wounded Knee Creek. You are a U.S. Army officer under orders to disarm Spotted Elk's band of Lakota, who are camped under guard after days of tension over the Ghost Dance movement.
evt-12-29-1890-wounded-knee-massacre.prompt: What decision by the army that morning set the tragedy in motion?

choices.text: Negotiate a peaceful surrender of weapons through the tribal council
Order soldiers to conduct forcible tent-by-tent weapon searches
Wait for reinforcements before attempting any disarmament
Withdraw troops and allow the band to leave unhindered

evt-12-29-1890-wounded-knee-massacre.butterflyEffect: Soldiers moved through the camp conducting forcible tent-by-tent weapon searches. A struggle broke out when Black Coyote resisted surrendering his rifle, a shot rang out, and the ensuing violence became one of the deadliest confrontations of the Indian Wars, marking the effective end of large-scale armed Native resistance on the Plains.

evt-12-29-1913-cecil-b-demille.scenario: It is 29 December 1913, and you are Cecil B. DeMille's assistant, standing outside a rented barn in a quiet citrus town called Hollywood. Bad weather has driven the production of The Squaw Man here instead of the originally planned Arizona location.
evt-12-29-1913-cecil-b-demille.prompt: What decision by DeMille shaped the future of this small town?

choices.text: He relocated the entire cast back to the original Arizona site
He continued filming in Hollywood using the barn as a makeshift studio
He abandoned the production and returned east to New York studios
He postponed filming until proper indoor stages could be built

evt-12-29-1913-cecil-b-demille.butterflyEffect: DeMille pressed on filming in the rented barn, and the finished feature's success proved Hollywood's reliable sunshine and varied scenery ideal for filmmaking. The choice helped draw studios west, establishing Hollywood as the center of American cinema.

evt-12-29-1928-northern-expedition.scenario: It is 29 December 1928, and you serve as an aide to Zhang Xueliang, the young warlord ruling Manchuria after his father's assassination. Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist forces have swept north, and you must advise Zhang on his next move.
evt-12-29-1928-northern-expedition.prompt: What should Zhang Xueliang do about the Nationalist government in Nanjing?

choices.text: Declare Manchuria's allegiance to the Nanjing government, raising its flag
Ally openly with Japan against the Nationalists
Remain an independent warlord and resist Nationalist authority
Seek Soviet backing to form a rival northern government

evt-12-29-1928-northern-expedition.butterflyEffect: Zhang formally submitted, raising the Nationalist flag over Manchuria and nominally completing China's reunification under the Kuomintang. The uneasy alliance masked deep regional tensions that Japan would later exploit, seizing Manchuria in the 1931 Mukden Incident.

evt-12-29-1940-world-war-ii.scenario: It is the night of 29 December 1940, and you are a fire warden on a rooftop in the City of London as Luftwaffe incendiary bombs fall in what will become known as the Second Great Fire of London.
evt-12-29-1940-world-war-ii.prompt: What should you do to stop the incendiary bombs from destroying the building?

choices.text: Douse the incendiaries immediately with a stirrup pump before fires spread
Ignore small incendiaries since only high explosives matter
Remove all sand buckets to prevent looting during the raid
Evacuate at once and wait for the professional fire brigade to arrive

evt-12-29-1940-world-war-ii.butterflyEffect: The raid gutted much of the historic City, destroying the Guildhall and eight Wren churches in a firestorm. It hardened Britain's civil defence doctrine around rooftop fire-watching and stirrup pumps, and stiffened public resolve through the ongoing Blitz.

evt-12-29-1975-1975-laguardia-airport-bo.scenario: It is 29 December 1975, and you are waiting near the TWA baggage claim at LaGuardia Airport in New York when an explosion suddenly tears through the terminal, killing and injuring dozens of travelers around you.
evt-12-29-1975-1975-laguardia-airport-bo.prompt: What happened in the investigation that followed this bombing?

choices.text: Investigators identified and convicted a lone bomber within months
A domestic anti-war group claimed responsibility and its leaders were arrested
No perpetrator was ever identified, and the case remains officially unsolved
The bombing was formally attributed to a foreign government and led to expulsions of diplomats

evt-12-29-1975-1975-laguardia-airport-bo.butterflyEffect: Despite theories pointing to anti-Yugoslav Croatian nationalists or Yugoslav agents seeking to discredit dissidents, no one was ever charged, and the case remains unsolved. The attack, amid a wave of 1970s domestic terrorism, pushed airports toward removing public storage lockers and tightening terminal security screening.

evt-12-29-1992-fernando-collor-de-mello.scenario: It is 29 December 1992, and you are a senator in Brasília. President Fernando Collor de Mello, facing an impeachment trial for corruption, has just submitted his resignation in hopes of halting the proceedings against him.
evt-12-29-1992-fernando-collor-de-mello.prompt: What did the Senate do after Collor's resignation attempt?

choices.text: Accept the resignation and dismiss all charges
Call for new elections and drop the impeachment entirely
Continue the trial anyway and convict him, banning him from office
Refer the matter to the Supreme Court to decide his fate

evt-12-29-1992-fernando-collor-de-mello.butterflyEffect: The Senate ruled his resignation did not end the trial, convicted him, and barred him from elected office for eight years. He was later acquitted on separate criminal charges, and the episode became a landmark in testing Brazil's young democratic institutions.

evt-12-29-1994-turkish-airlines-flight-2.scenario: It is 29 December 1994, and you are the captain of Turkish Airlines Flight 278, descending toward Van Ferit Melen Airport through heavy snow with visibility dropping fast on final approach.
evt-12-29-1994-turkish-airlines-flight-2.prompt: What did the crew do as the aircraft neared the runway in these conditions?

choices.text: They declared an emergency and made an unplanned water landing nearby
They aborted the landing and diverted to an alternate airport
They circled for an hour before conditions cleared and landed safely
They continued the approach and the aircraft crashed short of the runway

evt-12-29-1994-turkish-airlines-flight-2.butterflyEffect: The crew continued the approach rather than executing a go-around, and the aircraft crashed short of the runway, killing 57 of the 76 aboard. The accident renewed scrutiny of approach procedures and crew decision-making in poor-weather landings at Turkish regional airports.

evt-12-29-1996-guatemala.scenario: It is 29 December 1996 in the National Palace in Guatemala City. President Álvaro Arzú and URNG commander Rolando Morán are about to sign the Accord for a Firm and Lasting Peace, ending 36 years of civil war.
evt-12-29-1996-guatemala.prompt: What did signing this accord actually achieve?

choices.text: It merged Guatemala into a federation with neighboring states
It transferred Guatemala's capital to a newly built city
It established a new constitutional monarchy in Guatemala
It formally ended Guatemala's 36-year civil war between the government and URNG guerrillas

evt-12-29-1996-guatemala.butterflyEffect: The accord ended Central America's longest civil war, which had killed over 200,000 people, mostly Indigenous Maya. It created a UN-verified peace process, including a Historical Clarification Commission that documented atrocities, though implementation of land and justice reforms remained slow for decades.

evt-12-29-1998-khmer-rouge.scenario: It is December 1998 in Phnom Penh. Aging Khmer Rouge leaders, including Khieu Samphan, appear before cameras to express regret for the years of terror under Democratic Kampuchea. You are a journalist watching the government's response.
evt-12-29-1998-khmer-rouge.prompt: What actually followed the leaders' public expression of regret?

choices.text: The leaders fled Cambodia to avoid any accountability
UN peacekeepers were deployed to enforce immediate reparations
The government urged reconciliation, and prosecution was delayed for years
The leaders were arrested and tried within weeks by an international court

evt-12-29-1998-khmer-rouge.butterflyEffect: Prime Minister Hun Sen urged Cambodians to 'dig a hole and bury the past,' favoring reconciliation over immediate prosecution. It took until 2006 for the UN-backed Khmer Rouge Tribunal to begin, and only in 2014 were Nuon Chea and Khieu Samphan finally convicted of crimes against humanity.

evt-12-29-2003-akkala-sami.scenario: It is 29 December 2003 on Russia's Kola Peninsula. Marja Sergina, the last fluent speaker of Akkala Sámi, has just died, and the recordings and notes linguists made of her speech are now all that remain of her language's living sound.
evt-12-29-2003-akkala-sami.prompt: What became possible because linguists had recorded her before this day?

choices.text: Her recordings led to Akkala Sámi being adopted as an official state language
Her recordings allowed later scholars to reconstruct a written record of the language after it went extinct
Her recordings proved Akkala Sámi was simply a dialect of Russian
Her recordings were lost, leaving no trace of the language

evt-12-29-2003-akkala-sami.butterflyEffect: Because researchers had documented Sergina's speech, scholars were later able to compile dictionaries and grammatical descriptions of Akkala Sámi even after it became extinct as a spoken language. Her recordings remain the primary source for any modern study or revival attempt of this Sámi language.

evt-12-29-2006-anglo-american-loan.scenario: It is 1946, and as a British Treasury negotiator working alongside John Maynard Keynes, you are finalizing loan terms with American officials to keep postwar Britain solvent.
evt-12-29-2006-anglo-american-loan.prompt: What condition do you accept in exchange for the $3.75 billion loan?

choices.text: Transfer of British colonial trade preferences to the US
Immediate repayment within five years at 5% interest
A ban on further British borrowing from Canada
Convertibility of sterling into dollars within one year

evt-12-29-2006-anglo-american-loan.butterflyEffect: The convertibility clause backfired: when sterling became freely convertible in 1947 as required, a run on the pound forced Britain to suspend convertibility within weeks. The resulting crisis exposed Britain's fragile finances and helped justify the Marshall Plan's non-repayable aid the following year, while the original loan itself was not fully repaid until 2006.

evt-12-29-2013-december-2013-volgograd-b.scenario: It is 29 December 2013, and you are a security official in Volgograd, Russia, just after a suicide bomber has struck the city's main railway station, with the Sochi Winter Olympics only six weeks away.
evt-12-29-2013-december-2013-volgograd-b.prompt: What did Russian authorities do in response to this attack and the one that followed it the next day?

choices.text: They closed all rail travel in southern Russia indefinitely
They canceled the Sochi Olympics outright
They negotiated a public ceasefire with North Caucasus insurgent leaders
They imposed a massive security perimeter and lockdown around the upcoming Sochi Olympics

evt-12-29-2013-december-2013-volgograd-b.butterflyEffect: A second suicide bombing hit a Volgograd trolleybus the very next day, bringing the two-day toll to 34 dead. The attacks, blamed on North Caucasus insurgents, pushed Russia to impose an unprecedented security lockdown, the so-called 'ring of steel,' around Sochi for the Olympics.

evt-12-29-2013-formula-one.scenario: It is 29 December 2013 on a ski slope near Méribel, France. Seven-time world champion Michael Schumacher has just fallen while skiing off-piste and struck his head on a rock, despite wearing a helmet.
evt-12-29-2013-formula-one.prompt: What happened to Schumacher in the aftermath of the fall?

choices.text: He was flown to Paris for immediate surgery and returned to racing that season
He walked away with only minor bruising and no lasting injury
He was airlifted to hospital and placed in a medically induced coma
He was treated at the resort and skied again within days

evt-12-29-2013-formula-one.butterflyEffect: He was airlifted to a Grenoble hospital and placed in a medically induced coma to treat severe brain trauma. He survived but never returned to public life, and the accident renewed global debate over off-piste skiing safety and helmet standards.

evt-12-29-2020-2020-petrinja-earthquake.scenario: It is 29 December 2020, and you are a local official in Sisak-Moslavina County surveying the ruins after a magnitude 6.4 earthquake tore through Petrinja, a day after a strong foreshock had already rattled the region.
evt-12-29-2020-2020-petrinja-earthquake.prompt: What did Croatia's response to the disaster later face criticism for?

choices.text: Demolishing salvageable historic buildings too hastily
Slow and disorganized reconstruction and compensation for residents
Failing to declare any state of emergency
Refusing all international aid offered after the disaster

evt-12-29-2020-2020-petrinja-earthquake.butterflyEffect: The quake left widespread structural damage and displaced many families in and around Petrinja. In the following years, reconstruction was widely criticized as slow and bureaucratic, fueling public frustration and calls to reform how Croatia enforces building codes and manages disaster recovery.

evt-12-29-2024-jeju-air-flight-2216.scenario: It is 29 December 2024, and you are the captain of Jeju Air Flight 2216 on final approach to Muan. Both engines have ingested birds, you've declared a mayday, and now on your second attempt the landing gear refuses to extend.
evt-12-29-2024-jeju-air-flight-2216.prompt: What do you do as the runway rushes up with no gear deployed?

choices.text: Order passengers to brace for a water landing in the nearby estuary
Abort the landing and attempt a third go-around
Divert immediately to the nearest alternate airport
Attempt to land the aircraft on its belly rather than divert

evt-12-29-2024-jeju-air-flight-2216.butterflyEffect: The crew belly-landed well past the normal touchdown zone, overran the runway, and struck a concrete berm supporting the ILS antenna array, killing 179 of 181 aboard. The disaster triggered global scrutiny of rigid, non-frangible obstacles near runway ends and renewed debate over bird-strike mitigation at airports built near wetlands.
