evt-12-30-1460-wars-of-the-roses.scenario: It is 30 December 1460. You are Richard, Duke of York, holed up in Sandal Castle with a smaller force while a much larger Lancastrian army gathers outside during the Christmas truce. Reinforcements under the Earl of Warwick are still days away.
evt-12-30-1460-wars-of-the-roses.prompt: What does the Duke of York do?

choices.text: Sally out from the castle to engage the Lancastrian army in open battle
Negotiate a truce and withdraw north under safe passage
Abandon the castle by night and retreat to London
Hold the castle and wait for Warwick's reinforcements to arrive

evt-12-30-1460-wars-of-the-roses.butterflyEffect: York sallied out to fight in the open and was overwhelmed and killed at the Battle of Wakefield, along with his son Edmund. His eldest son, Edward, avenged him within months, seized the throne as Edward IV, and the Yorkist cause he died for ultimately triumphed.

evt-12-30-1702-queen-anne-s-war.scenario: It is late 1702 and you are Governor James Moore of Carolina, besieging the Spanish fortress at St. Augustine with English colonial troops and Native allies. The siege has stalled, and word arrives that Spanish reinforcements are approaching by sea.
evt-12-30-1702-queen-anne-s-war.prompt: What does Moore decide to do?

choices.text: Press the assault and storm the fortress before reinforcements land
Abandon the siege and retreat overland, burning the boats behind him
Fortify the siege lines and wait out the Spanish relief force
Negotiate a Spanish surrender in exchange for safe passage home

evt-12-30-1702-queen-anne-s-war.butterflyEffect: Moore abandoned the siege, burning his own boats and retreating overland after failing to breach the fort, though his men had already razed much of the town. The costly failure strained Carolina's treasury into issuing paper money and pushed English colonists toward harsher raids on Spanish Florida in the years that followed.

evt-12-30-1813-war-of-1812.scenario: It's late December 1813, and you're a militiaman defending Buffalo, New York, after American troops burned Newark, Upper Canada, prompting a British-led force to cross the frozen Niagara River in retaliation.
evt-12-30-1813-war-of-1812.prompt: What did the British and allied forces do to Buffalo?

choices.text: Negotiated a truce with the militia and withdrew peacefully
Captured the town and held it for ransom, sparing it
Burned Buffalo and nearby Black Rock to the ground
Bypassed Buffalo entirely to attack Fort Niagara instead

evt-12-30-1813-war-of-1812.butterflyEffect: On 30 December 1813, British and Native American forces captured and burned both Buffalo and the nearby village of Black Rock, devastating the frontier. The destruction deepened the cycle of retaliatory raids along the Niagara border that continued until the Treaty of Ghent restored the pre-war status quo in 1815.

evt-12-30-1902-discovery-expedition.scenario: It's 30 December 1902, and you're man-hauling a sledge across the Ross Ice Shelf with Scott and Shackleton, having just pushed the party's farthest south record deep into unmapped Antarctic territory.
evt-12-30-1902-discovery-expedition.prompt: What forces the three-man party to abandon the push south and turn back?

choices.text: Their sledge dogs all dying of exhaustion
Orders radioed back from the ship Discovery
Sighting a rival Norwegian expedition ahead
Shackleton's collapse from scurvy

evt-12-30-1902-discovery-expedition.butterflyEffect: Having reached 82°17'S, the furthest south yet recorded, the exhausted party turned for home as Shackleton grew dangerously ill with scurvy. The grueling retreat and Scott's harsh treatment of Shackleton afterward soured their relationship, a rivalry that later shaped the deadly race to the South Pole.

evt-12-30-1903-iroquois-theatre-fire.scenario: It's 30 December 1903, and you're an usher at Chicago's newly built, supposedly 'fireproof' Iroquois Theatre when sparks from a stage light ignite the curtain during a packed matinee of Mr. Bluebeard.
evt-12-30-1903-iroquois-theatre-fire.prompt: What lasting safety reform did this disaster force on public buildings nationwide?

choices.text: A requirement for asbestos curtains and nothing else
Compulsory fire insurance for all theatergoers
A nationwide ban on stage curtains
Mandatory unlocked, outward-swinging exit doors with panic bars

evt-12-30-1903-iroquois-theatre-fire.butterflyEffect: Investigators found exit doors bolted shut, hidden behind curtains, or opening inward, along with unfinished fire escapes and no alarm system, trapping hundreds inside. The catastrophe pushed cities across the country to mandate outward-swinging doors, illuminated exit signs, and the panic bar hardware still required in public buildings today.

evt-12-30-1906-all-india-muslim-league.scenario: It is December 1906 in Dacca. The Simla Deputation has just persuaded the Viceroy to consider separate political safeguards for Muslims, and delegates at the Muhammadan Educational Conference must decide how to build on that success.
evt-12-30-1906-all-india-muslim-league.prompt: What do the delegates decide to do?

choices.text: Dissolve the deputation and join the Indian National Congress outright
Found a separate political party to represent Muslim political interests
Focus purely on educational reform and avoid politics entirely
Petition the British to abolish separate communal representation

evt-12-30-1906-all-india-muslim-league.butterflyEffect: They founded the All-India Muslim League as a distinct political party to represent Muslim interests rather than working solely through the Congress. Over the following decades the League evolved from a loyalist body into the driving force behind the two-nation theory, culminating in the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

evt-12-30-1940-arroyo-seco-parkway.scenario: It is 1940 and you are a California highway engineer routing the new Arroyo Seco Parkway between Los Angeles and Pasadena, threading the road through the narrow, winding riverbed it is named for.
evt-12-30-1940-arroyo-seco-parkway.prompt: How do you route the new parkway?

choices.text: Tunnel beneath the arroyo to avoid altering its course
Bulldoze a straight route through the surrounding neighborhoods
Follow the arroyo's natural contours to keep the road within the narrow canyon
Elevate the entire roadway above the canyon on viaducts

evt-12-30-1940-arroyo-seco-parkway.butterflyEffect: Engineers followed the arroyo's natural curves to save cost and preserve the scenic canyon, producing tight bends and short entrance ramps. Those same curves, ideal for 1940s traffic, later made it one of America's most notoriously outdated freeways even as it became the template that shaped the coming Interstate Highway System.

evt-12-30-2004-cromanon-nightclub-fire.scenario: It's 30 December 2004, and you're packed into Buenos Aires' República Cromañón nightclub as pyrotechnics ignite the foam ceiling and smoke fills the room, but you find an emergency exit blocked.
evt-12-30-2004-cromanon-nightclub-fire.prompt: What safety failure trapped so many people inside during the fire?

choices.text: All fire extinguishers on site had expired years earlier
The building had only one narrow staircase by original design
Emergency exits had been chained shut to prevent gate-crashers
The venue had no smoke detectors installed anywhere

evt-12-30-2004-cromanon-nightclub-fire.butterflyEffect: Investigators found emergency exits had been chained shut to stop gate-crashers, turning the fire deadly. The venue's owner, city safety inspectors, and members of the band Callejeros were later convicted, and the disaster forced sweeping reform of Argentina's nightclub and building safety codes.

evt-12-30-2005-tropical-storm-zeta.scenario: It's 30 December 2005, more than a month after the Atlantic hurricane season officially ended, and forecasters watch an unexpected system far out at sea strengthen into a tropical depression.
evt-12-30-2005-tropical-storm-zeta.prompt: What made Tropical Storm Zeta so unusual among Atlantic storms?

choices.text: It formed in the Pacific rather than the Atlantic
It was the strongest hurricane of the 2005 season
It formed after the season's official end and lasted into the next year
It made a destructive landfall in Florida

evt-12-30-2005-tropical-storm-zeta.butterflyEffect: Zeta became only the second Atlantic tropical cyclone on record to persist across two calendar years, lingering into January 2006 without ever threatening land. Its bizarre late arrival capped the historically extreme 2005 season, which had already produced Katrina, Rita, and Wilma.

evt-12-30-2006-basque-nationalism.scenario: It's 30 December 2006, and you work in the parking garage of Madrid's Barajas Airport when a van packed with explosives detonates, months after ETA had declared a 'permanent' ceasefire.
evt-12-30-2006-basque-nationalism.prompt: What did the bombing do to the ceasefire ETA had announced earlier that year?

choices.text: It shattered the truce, ending the ceasefire
It had no real effect since ETA denied responsibility
The government had already voided the ceasefire a year earlier
It strengthened trust and extended the negotiations

evt-12-30-2006-basque-nationalism.butterflyEffect: The blast killed two people and shattered the ceasefire ETA had declared in March 2006, collapsing peace talks with Madrid. Spain returned to a hardline security stance, and ETA continued attacks for years before finally declaring a definitive end to violence in 2011 and dissolving in 2018.

evt-12-30-2006-saddam-hussein.scenario: It is the pre-dawn hours of 30 December 2006 in Baghdad. Saddam Hussein has been convicted and sentenced to death, but the date falls during Eid al-Adha and international voices are urging a delay.

choices.text: Transfer Hussein to an international tribunal for further appeal
Carry out the execution as scheduled that morning
Postpone the execution until after the Eid holiday
Commute the sentence to life imprisonment

evt-12-30-2006-saddam-hussein.butterflyEffect: The execution went ahead by hanging that morning, and a leaked cellphone video of the moment sparked global controversy over its conduct and timing. The episode deepened sectarian divisions in Iraq, with some regarding Hussein as a martyr and others celebrating the end of his rule.

evt-12-30-2006-madrid-barajas-airport.scenario: It's 30 December 2006, and you're waiting near Terminal 4 of Madrid–Barajas Airport when a massive car bomb detonates in the multi-storey car park, killing two men asleep nearby.
evt-12-30-2006-madrid-barajas-airport.prompt: What did this bombing bring to an abrupt end?

choices.text: ETA's ceasefire with the Spanish government
Spain's negotiations to join the European Union
The Good Friday peace process in Northern Ireland
Spain's referendum on the monarchy

evt-12-30-2006-madrid-barajas-airport.butterflyEffect: The bomb, planted by the Basque separatist group ETA, killed two Ecuadorian men and badly damaged the terminal, shattering the 'permanent' ceasefire ETA had declared nine months earlier. Peace talks collapsed and ETA resumed violence for years before finally disbanding in 2018.

evt-12-30-2006-president-of-iraq.scenario: It's the early hours of 30 December 2006 in Baghdad, and you are among the witnesses gathered as former president Saddam Hussein is led to the gallows after his conviction in the Al-Dujail massacre trial.
evt-12-30-2006-president-of-iraq.prompt: By what method was Saddam Hussein's death sentence carried out?

choices.text: Beheading
Firing squad
Lethal injection
Hanging

evt-12-30-2006-president-of-iraq.butterflyEffect: Saddam Hussein was hanged before dawn on 30 December 2006. A leaked cellphone video showing guards taunting him during the execution sparked international controversy over how it was conducted, and his death deepened sectarian tensions in Iraq without ending the ongoing insurgency.

evt-12-30-2009-2009-iranian-pro-governme.scenario: It's 30 December 2009 in Tehran, and crowds mobilized by the state pour into the streets one week after the deadly Ashura protests, chanting against the opposition Green Movement.
evt-12-30-2009-2009-iranian-pro-governme.prompt: What was the government's goal in staging these 'Dey 9' counter-rallies?

choices.text: To call for direct talks with the United States
To demand that new elections be held immediately
To rally support for opposition leader Mousavi
To display public support for the government and discredit the protesters

evt-12-30-2009-2009-iranian-pro-governme.butterflyEffect: State media and organizers used the rallies to brand Ashura protesters as enemies of Islam and to project an image of overwhelming public loyalty to the regime. The show of force helped justify a fresh wave of arrests that further weakened the Green Movement through 2010.

evt-12-30-2009-camp-chapman-attack.scenario: It is 30 December 2009 at Forward Operating Base Chapman. A Jordanian informant who claims to have located al-Zawahiri arrives at the gate, and your CIA team is eager for the breakthrough after months of cultivating him.
evt-12-30-2009-camp-chapman-attack.prompt: What actually happened when the informant reached the base?

choices.text: He was detained for hours of questioning before being cleared
He was turned away at the perimeter and never entered the base
He was thoroughly searched and a hidden weapon was found
He was let through the checkpoint without a search and detonated his vest

evt-12-30-2009-camp-chapman-attack.butterflyEffect: Humam al-Balawi was waved through without being searched and detonated a suicide vest, killing seven CIA officers and contractors, a Jordanian intelligence officer, and an Afghan asset. It was the deadliest attack on the CIA in over 25 years and forced sweeping reforms in how the agency vetted and handled informants.

evt-12-30-2013-december-2013-kinshasa-at.scenario: It's 30 December 2013, and armed followers of self-styled prophet Paul Joseph Mukungubila storm the state broadcaster, the airport, and a military camp in Kinshasa, convinced they are installing a new government.
evt-12-30-2013-december-2013-kinshasa-at.prompt: How did Congolese security forces respond to these coordinated attacks?

choices.text: President Kabila resigned in response
UN peacekeepers took direct control of the capital
They negotiated a power-sharing deal with Mukungubila
They put down the uprising by force across multiple cities

evt-12-30-2013-december-2013-kinshasa-at.butterflyEffect: Security forces crushed the uprising within hours in Kinshasa and in near-simultaneous clashes in Lubumbashi and Kolwezi, while Mukungubila fled into exile. The episode exposed how fragile state authority remained even in the capital, and the government later pursued his extradition over the attacks.

evt-12-31-1759-arthur-guinness.scenario: It's 31 December 1759, and you're a young Dublin brewer named Arthur Guinness standing before the owner of a disused brewery at St. James's Gate, weighing a commitment that will outlast your grandchildren.
evt-12-31-1759-arthur-guinness.prompt: What lease terms did Guinness sign for the site?

choices.text: A 900-year lease at £4 per year
A 99-year lease at £450 per year
Outright purchase of the site for £4,500
A 9,000-year lease at £45 per year

evt-12-31-1759-arthur-guinness.butterflyEffect: That extraordinary 9,000-year lease let the Guinness family build one of the world's most recognizable brewing empires on that single site for centuries. St. James's Gate remains Guinness's headquarters today, and the stout became a global symbol of Ireland.

evt-12-31-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.scenario: It is the night of December 31, 1775, and a blinding snowstorm masks your position outside the walls of Quebec City. General Montgomery and Colonel Arnold are preparing simultaneous columns to strike before dawn.
evt-12-31-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.prompt: What should the Patriot commanders do to seize Quebec before the garrison can react?

choices.text: Retreat south to Fort Ticonderoga
Wait for spring reinforcements before attacking
Negotiate a surrender with the garrison
Launch a surprise night assault under cover of the blizzard

evt-12-31-1775-american-revolutionary-wa.butterflyEffect: The assault went ahead in the storm, but Montgomery was killed leading his column and Arnold was wounded; Daniel Morgan's men were forced to surrender inside the city. The failed attack ended American hopes of seizing Canada and forced a costly Continental retreat the following spring.

evt-12-31-1857-queen-victoria.scenario: It is 1857, and the Province of Canada's rival cities—Quebec City, Montreal, Toronto, and Kingston—have failed to agree on a permanent seat of government. The dispute is referred to Queen Victoria for a final decision.
evt-12-31-1857-queen-victoria.prompt: Which small logging town does Victoria name as the new capital?

choices.text: Toronto
Kingston
Ottawa
Montreal

evt-12-31-1857-queen-victoria.butterflyEffect: Victoria chose Ottawa, then a modest lumber town far from the American border and roughly equidistant from English and French Canada. When the Dominion of Canada was formed in 1867, Ottawa's status as capital carried over and it remains the nation's capital today.

evt-12-31-1862-battle-of-stones-river.scenario: It is dawn on 31 December 1862 near Murfreesboro, Tennessee. Confederate troops under Braxton Bragg smash into your Union right flank in a surprise assault, and the line is buckling fast.
evt-12-31-1862-battle-of-stones-river.prompt: What must the Union right do to avoid total collapse?

choices.text: Launch an immediate counterattack on the Confederate center without regrouping
Hold the original position and wait for reinforcements from Nashville
Retreat entirely across Stones River and abandon the field
Fall back and re-form a new defensive line anchored by artillery along the Nashville Pike

evt-12-31-1862-battle-of-stones-river.butterflyEffect: Union troops fell back and reformed a new line along the Nashville Pike, anchored by massed artillery that broke repeated Confederate assaults. Bragg withdrew on 3 January, handing the Union a costly but badly needed victory that boosted morale after Fredericksburg and helped justify the Emancipation Proclamation.

evt-12-31-1907-times-square-ball.scenario: It is New Year's Eve 1907. Fire officials have banned the rooftop fireworks that used to mark midnight over Longacre Square, and the New York Times, whose new tower gives the square its name, needs a new spectacle to draw crowds.
evt-12-31-1907-times-square-ball.prompt: What does the paper's publisher arrange to replace the fireworks at midnight?

choices.text: Hold an indoor gala with no public spectacle
Lower an illuminated ball down the building's flagpole at midnight
Project searchlights onto passing clouds
Fire a cannon salute from the roof instead

evt-12-31-1907-times-square-ball.butterflyEffect: Adolph Ochs commissioned a 700-pound iron-and-wood ball, lit with 100 light bulbs, to be lowered down the flagpole atop One Times Square at midnight. The stunt was such a hit it became an annual ritual, evolving through material and technology changes into the televised ball drop watched by hundreds of millions worldwide today.

evt-12-31-1950-korean-war.scenario: It's New Year's Eve 1950. You're dug into a UN defensive position near the 38th parallel in Korea as scouts report massive Chinese and North Korean troop movements building for a night assault.
evt-12-31-1950-korean-war.prompt: What followed as communist forces launched their New Year's offensive?

choices.text: MacArthur ordered an immediate counter-invasion of China
Both sides declared a temporary New Year's ceasefire
Seoul fell to communist forces within days
UN forces held the line firmly along the 38th parallel

evt-12-31-1950-korean-war.butterflyEffect: The Third Phase Offensive drove UN forces out of Seoul on 4 January 1951, the lowest point of the war for the South. UN troops recaptured the city that March, but the front then stabilized near the 38th parallel, setting up two more years of grinding stalemate before the 1953 armistice.

evt-12-31-1961-rte.scenario: It is New Year's Eve, 1961, and you are gathered around a television set in Dublin as Ireland's first television service prepares to go on air for the very first time.
evt-12-31-1961-rte.prompt: What marks the centerpiece of this historic opening broadcast?

choices.text: A recorded American sitcom imported for the occasion
A live international football match broadcast from Britain
An address by President Éamon de Valera launching the service
A live broadcast of a Dáil Éireann debate

evt-12-31-1961-rte.butterflyEffect: President Éamon de Valera delivered an address formally launching the service, tying the new medium to the nation's identity from its first night. RTÉ went on to become Ireland's dominant broadcaster, shaping Irish language, culture and politics for decades.

evt-12-31-1972-roberto-clemente.scenario: It's the morning of December 31, 1972, at San Juan's airport, and the chartered DC-7 loaded with earthquake relief supplies for Nicaragua has a history of mechanical trouble and is dangerously overloaded.
evt-12-31-1972-roberto-clemente.prompt: What does Roberto Clemente decide to do about the flight?

choices.text: He sends the supplies without accompanying them
He cancels the flight until the aircraft is repaired
He hires a different, newer aircraft for the relief mission
He boards the plane himself to make sure the aid gets through

evt-12-31-1972-roberto-clemente.butterflyEffect: The overloaded DC-7 crashed into the ocean shortly after takeoff, killing Clemente instantly. His death prompted the Baseball Hall of Fame to waive its waiting period, and in 1973 he became the first Latino player inducted, cementing his legacy as a humanitarian as much as a ballplayer.

evt-12-31-1986-dupont-plaza-hotel-arson.scenario: It is early 1987, weeks after arson by disgruntled employees turned the Dupont Plaza Hotel into an inferno on New Year's Eve, killing dozens of guests trapped by smoke.
evt-12-31-1986-dupont-plaza-hotel-arson.prompt: What reform do fire safety officials push hardest for in hotels afterward?

choices.text: Voluntary fire drills left to each hotel's discretion
No significant changes to existing fire codes
Mandatory automatic sprinkler systems installed throughout hotel buildings
Removing fire alarms from casino and ballroom areas to avoid false alarms

evt-12-31-1986-dupont-plaza-hotel-arson.butterflyEffect: The disaster, alongside other major hotel fires, drove U.S. and international fire codes to require automatic sprinkler systems in hotels and other high-occupancy buildings. It remains one of the deadliest hotel fires in American history and a landmark case in fire-safety regulation.

evt-12-31-1999-vladimir-putin.scenario: It is New Year's Eve 1999 in Moscow. President Boris Yeltsin, weakened by ill health and scandal, addresses the nation with an unexpected announcement about his own future.
evt-12-31-1999-vladimir-putin.prompt: What does Yeltsin announce, and who does he name to take his place?

choices.text: Dissolve the Duma and call new elections immediately
Declare a state of emergency and remain in office
Step down without naming any successor
Resign and hand power to Prime Minister Vladimir Putin

evt-12-31-1999-vladimir-putin.butterflyEffect: Yeltsin resigned and named Prime Minister Vladimir Putin as acting president, giving Putin the advantage of incumbency ahead of the March 2000 election, which he won outright. Putin has dominated Russian politics ever since, as president or prime minister continuously from that day forward.

evt-12-31-1999-torrijos-carter-treaties.scenario: It is noon on 31 December 1999 at the Panama Canal. Under the terms signed by Carter and Torrijos more than two decades earlier, American officials must formally hand over the waterway they have run since 1903.
evt-12-31-1999-torrijos-carter-treaties.prompt: What happens to control of the Panama Canal on this day?

choices.text: Full control passes to Panama
The handover is postponed indefinitely
The canal is placed under United Nations administration
The U.S. retains permanent military bases along the canal

evt-12-31-1999-torrijos-carter-treaties.butterflyEffect: The United States transferred full control of the canal to Panama, ending 96 years of American administration. The Panama Canal Authority has run it since, later overseeing a major expansion completed in 2016 to accommodate larger ships.

evt-12-31-2004-taipei-101.scenario: You are a structural engineer inspecting Taipei 101 hours before its opening on 31 December 2004 as the world's tallest building, with typhoon winds forecast over the city.
evt-12-31-2004-taipei-101.prompt: What device do engineers rely on to keep the tower stable in storms and quakes?

choices.text: Hydraulic shock absorbers built into the ground-floor lobby
A 660-tonne tuned mass damper suspended near the top of the tower
A flexible glass curtain wall designed to flex with the wind
Deep foundation piles alone, with no upper-floor damping

evt-12-31-2004-taipei-101.butterflyEffect: A 660-tonne steel pendulum, suspended near the top floors as a tuned mass damper, sways to counteract wind and seismic motion. It became a famous engineering feature later opened to public viewing, and Taipei 101 held the tallest-building title until Burj Khalifa surpassed it in 2009.

evt-12-31-2011-nasa.scenario: It's New Year's Eve, 2011, and at mission control you watch the first of two identical GRAIL spacecraft approach the Moon after a three-month journey, its fuel tanks primed for a critical maneuver.
evt-12-31-2011-nasa.prompt: What must the spacecraft do to enter lunar orbit rather than fly past the Moon?

choices.text: Deploy a parachute to slow its descent
Release a lander to touch down on the surface
Fire its main engine to slow down and be captured into orbit
Fire thrusters to accelerate past the Moon into deep space

evt-12-31-2011-nasa.butterflyEffect: GRAIL-A's insertion burn succeeded, and its twin followed into orbit the next day; renamed Ebb and Flow by a student contest, the pair spent a year mapping the Moon's gravity field in unprecedented detail, revealing hidden basins and a fractured crust from ancient impacts.

evt-12-31-2014-2014-shanghai-stampede.scenario: It's New Year's Eve 2014, and you're a police officer stationed near Shanghai's Bund promenade as roughly 300,000 revelers pack the riverside walkway toward midnight.
evt-12-31-2014-2014-shanghai-stampede.prompt: What went wrong in the crowd, and what changed in the city afterward?

choices.text: A stairway bottleneck triggered a deadly crush, leading to a ban on future gatherings there
An explosive device was detonated in the crowd
A pedestrian bridge collapsed under the weight of celebrants
Fireworks ignited a fire that trapped the crowd

evt-12-31-2014-2014-shanghai-stampede.butterflyEffect: A fatal crush developed near a stairway leading down to the waterfront, killing 36 people and injuring dozens more. Shanghai authorities canceled the official Bund light show for future New Year's Eves and tightened crowd-control rules at large public gatherings across the country.

evt-12-31-2018-2018-magnitogorsk-buildin.scenario: It is the freezing morning of 31 December 2018 in Magnitogorsk. A suspected gas explosion has torn open a ten-story apartment block, and rescue crews must decide how long to keep searching the rubble as temperatures plunge and hope fades.
evt-12-31-2018-2018-magnitogorsk-buildin.prompt: What do rescuers do in the days after the collapse, despite the odds?

choices.text: Demolish the remaining structure immediately for safety
Wait for warmer weather before resuming the search
Call off the search after the first day
Continue the search past the point most victims could survive

evt-12-31-2018-2018-magnitogorsk-buildin.butterflyEffect: Crews kept digging through the freezing debris, and 35 hours after the collapse they pulled an 11-month-old boy alive from the wreckage, a survival that made national headlines. The disaster also intensified scrutiny of aging Soviet-era gas infrastructure across Russia's apartment blocks.

evt-12-31-2019-world-health-organization.scenario: It is 31 December 2019. The World Health Organization's China office receives word of a cluster of pneumonia cases in Wuhan with no identified cause, and officials must decide how seriously to treat the report.
evt-12-31-2019-world-health-organization.prompt: How does the WHO respond to this first report from Wuhan?

choices.text: Order international border closures at once
Dismiss the report as an isolated seasonal outbreak
Immediately declare a global pandemic
Begin monitoring the cluster and request further information

evt-12-31-2019-world-health-organization.butterflyEffect: The WHO began monitoring and requesting more information from Chinese authorities, the first formal step in tracking what would be identified weeks later as a novel coronavirus. Within months the organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic, triggering global lockdowns and reshaping public health policy worldwide.

evt-12-31-2020-covid-19-vaccine.scenario: It's 31 December 2020, and you're a WHO regulatory reviewer weighing months of trial data on a new mRNA vaccine as the pandemic rages worldwide.
evt-12-31-2020-covid-19-vaccine.prompt: Which vaccine received the WHO's first-ever emergency use validation that day?

choices.text: Oxford-AstraZeneca
Pfizer-BioNTech
Sinopharm
Moderna

evt-12-31-2020-covid-19-vaccine.butterflyEffect: WHO's emergency use listing for the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine allowed COVAX and lower-income countries to import and distribute it under the UN body's approval. This helped accelerate vaccine access beyond the wealthy nations that had already begun their own rollouts weeks earlier.
